title: Change in Grade and Size Requirements: Oranges, Grapefruit, Tangerines, and Pummelos Grown in Florida and Imported Grapefruit

units.obligation_text: No handler shall ship between the production area and any point outside thereof, in the 48 contiguous States and the District of Columbia of the United States, any variety of fruit listed in column (1) of Table I to paragraph (a), except for Ambersweet and Temple, unless such variety meets the applicable minimum grade and size (with tolerances for size as specified in paragraph (c) of this section) specified for such variety in columns (2) and (3) of Table I to paragraph (a).
units.action_summary: Handlers are prohibited from shipping listed varieties from the production area to points outside the production area within the contiguous U.S. and DC unless the fruit meets the specified minimum grade and size in Table I (with size tolerances in paragraph (c)).

units.obligation_text: Oranges — Minimum grade: U.S. No. 2; Minimum diameter: 2–4/16 inches.
units.action_summary: Oranges must meet U.S. No. 2 grade and minimum diameter 2-4/16 inches to be shipped under § 905.306(a).

units.obligation_text: Grapefruit, Seedless — Minimum grade: U.S. No. 1; Minimum diameter: 3 inches.
units.action_summary: Seedless grapefruit must meet U.S. No. 1 grade and minimum diameter 3 inches to be shipped under § 905.306(a).

units.obligation_text: Tangerines, Fallglo — Minimum grade: U.S. No. 2; Minimum diameter: 2–6/16 inches.
units.action_summary: Fallglo tangerines must meet U.S. No. 2 grade and minimum diameter 2-6/16 inches to be shipped under § 905.306(a).

units.obligation_text: Tangerines, Honey — Minimum grade: U.S. No. 2; Minimum diameter: 2–6/16 inches.

units.obligation_text: Tangerines, Sunburst — Minimum grade: U.S. No. 2; Minimum diameter: 2–6/16 inches.
units.action_summary: Sunburst tangerines must meet U.S. No. 2 grade and minimum diameter 2-6/16 inches to be shipped under § 905.306(a).

units.obligation_text: Tangelos — Minimum grade: U.S. No. 1; Minimum diameter: 2–8/16 inches.
units.action_summary: Tangelos must meet U.S. No. 1 grade and minimum diameter 2-8/16 inches to be shipped under § 905.306(a).

units.obligation_text: Except for Ambersweet and Temple.
units.action_summary: Ambersweet and Temple varieties are exceptions to the shipping restrictions in § 905.306(a).

units.obligation_text: Provided, That all grapefruit meet the minimum maturity requirements specified in paragraph (e) of this section.
units.action_summary: All grapefruit shipped under § 905.306(a) must meet the minimum maturity requirements in paragraph (e).

units.obligation_text: No handler shall ship to any destination outside the 48 contiguous States and the District of Columbia of the United States any variety of fruit listed in column (1) of Table II to paragraph (b), except for Ambersweet and Temple, unless such variety meets the applicable minimum grade and size (with tolerances for size as specified in paragraph (c) of this section) specified for such variety in columns (2) and (3) of Table II to paragraph (b).

units.obligation_text: Tangerines, Fallglo — Minimum grade: U.S. No. 2; Minimum diameter: 2–6/16 inches.
units.action_summary: Fallglo tangerines must meet U.S. No. 2 grade and minimum diameter 2-6/16 inches to be shipped to destinations outside the contiguous U.S. under § 905.306(b).

units.obligation_text: Tangerines, Honey — Minimum grade: U.S. No. 2; Minimum diameter: 2–6/16 inches.
units.action_summary: Honey tangerines must meet U.S. No. 2 grade and minimum diameter 2-6/16 inches to be shipped to destinations outside the contiguous U.S. under § 905.306(b).

units.action_summary: Sunburst tangerines must meet U.S. No. 2 grade and minimum diameter 2-6/16 inches to be shipped to destinations outside the contiguous U.S. under § 905.306(b).

units.obligation_text: Tangelos — Minimum grade: U.S. No. 1; Minimum diameter: 2–8/16 inches.
units.action_summary: Tangelos must meet U.S. No. 1 grade and minimum diameter 2-8/16 inches to be shipped to destinations outside the contiguous U.S. under § 905.306(b).

units.obligation_text: Except for Ambersweet and Temple.
units.action_summary: Ambersweet and Temple varieties are exceptions to the shipping restrictions in § 905.306(b).

units.obligation_text: Provided, That all grapefruit meet the minimum maturity requirements specified in paragraph (e) of this section.
units.action_summary: All grapefruit shipped under § 905.306(b) must meet the minimum maturity requirements in paragraph (e).

units.obligation_text: Terms and tolerances pertaining to grade and size requirements, which are defined in the United States Standards for Grades of Florida Grapefruit (7 CFR 51.750–51.784), and in Marketing Order No. 905 (7 CFR 905.18 and 905.306(a) through (d)), shall be applicable herein.

units.obligation_text: From the nominations submitted by the Board, the Secretary shall select the members of the Board;

title: AMS-SC-19-0015 Proposed Rule

units.obligation_text: There is hereby established a Softwood Lumber Board to administer the terms and provisions of this Order and promote the use of softwood lumber.
units.action_summary: Establish a Softwood Lumber Board to administer the Order and promote softwood lumber.

units.obligation_text: The Board shall be composed of manufacturers for the U.S. market who manufacture and domestically ship or import 15 million board feet or more of softwood lumber in the United States during a fiscal period.
units.action_summary: Board membership must consist of manufacturers for the U.S. market who domestically ship or import at least 15 million board feet per fiscal period.

units.obligation_text: Seats on the Board shall be apportioned based on the volume of softwood lumber production that is manufactured and shipped within the United States by domestic manufacturers and the volume of softwood lumber imported into the United States.
units.action_summary: Board seats must be apportioned according to domestic production volume and import volume.

units.obligation_text: Seats on the Board shall also be apportioned based on size of operation within each geographic region, as specified in paragraphs (b)(1)(i), (b)(1)(ii), (b)(2), and (b)(3) of this section.
units.action_summary: Board seats must also be apportioned by size of operation within geographic regions as specified in paragraph (b).

units.obligation_text: If there are no eligible nominees for a large or small seat within a region, that seat may be filled by a nominee representing an eligible manufacturer for the U.S. market of any size.
units.action_summary: If no eligible nominee of the specified size exists in a region, the seat may be filled by a nominee of any size.

units.obligation_text: Should the size of a manufacturer for the U.S. market change during a member’s term of office, that member may serve for the remainder of the term.
units.action_summary: A member whose size-category changes during the term may continue to serve for the remainder of the term.

units.action_summary: Set total number of Board members: 16 for 2020; 14 for 2021 and subsequent Boards.

units.obligation_text: Four members shall represent importers. Of these four members, two must represent large, one must represent small, and one may represent importers of any size.
units.actor: the Board (importer representation for 2021 and subsequent Boards)
units.action_summary: For 2021 and later, four Board members shall represent importers: two must be large, one must be small, and one may be any size.

units.obligation_text: At least three of these members must import softwood lumber from the following regions:
units.action_summary: At least three of the importer members must import from specified regions.

units.obligation_text: Two members must import softwood lumber from the Canadian West Region, as defined in paragraph (b)(2)(i) of this section;
units.action_summary: Two importer members must import from the Canadian West Region.

units.obligation_text: One member must import softwood lumber from the Canadian East Region, as defined in paragraph (b)(2)(ii) of this section.
units.action_summary: One importer member must import from the Canadian East Region.

units.obligation_text: In each five-year period, but not more frequently than once in each three-year period, the Board shall:
units.action_summary: Require the Board to perform specified periodic reviews within defined timing constraints.

units.obligation_text: Review, based on a three-year average, the geographical distribution of the volume of softwood lumber production that is manufactured and shipped within the United States by domestic manufacturers and the volume of softwood lumber imported into the United States;
units.action_summary: The Board must review geographic distribution of domestic production and imports using a three-year average.

units.obligation_text: Review, based on a three-year average, the distribution of the size of operations within each region;
units.action_summary: The Board must review regional distributions of operation sizes using a three-year average.

units.obligation_text: If warranted, recommend to the Secretary the reapportionment of the Board membership to reflect changes in the geographical distribution of the volume of softwood lumber production that is manufactured and shipped within the United States by domestic manufacturers and the volume of softwood lumber imported into the United States.
units.action_summary: If warranted, the Board must recommend reapportionment of membership to the Secretary to reflect distribution changes.

units.obligation_text: The distribution of volumes between regions and the distribution of the size of operations within regions shall also be considered.
units.actor: the Board (or those conducting the reapportionment)
units.action_summary: Distribution of volumes and size of operations must be considered in reapportionment deliberations.

units.obligation_text: The number of Board members may also be changed.
units.action_summary: The number of Board members may be changed as part of reapportionment.

units.obligation_text: Any changes in Board composition shall be implemented by the Secretary through rulemaking.
units.action_summary: The Secretary must implement changes in Board composition via rulemaking.

units.obligation_text: Nominations shall be conducted as follows:
units.action_summary: Directs that nominations must be conducted according to the following procedures.

units.obligation_text: The Board shall conduct outreach to all segments of the softwood lumber industry.
units.action_summary: The Board must conduct outreach to all segments of the industry.

units.obligation_text: Softwood lumber domestic manufacturers and importers may submit nominations to the Board.
units.action_summary: Domestic manufacturers and importers are permitted to submit nominations to the Board.

units.obligation_text: Nominees must domestically manufacture and/or import 15 million board feet or more of softwood lumber per fiscal year;
units.action_summary: Nominees are required to domestically manufacture or import at least 15 million board feet per fiscal year.

units.obligation_text: Domestic manufacturers and importer nominees may provide the Board a short background statement outlining their qualifications to serve on the Board;
units.action_summary: Nominees are permitted to provide a short background statement of qualifications.

units.obligation_text: Nominees may seek nomination to the Board for all open or vacant seats for which the nominees are eligible;
units.action_summary: Nominees may pursue nomination for any open seats for which they are eligible.

units.obligation_text: The Board will evaluate all eligible nominees and submit the name of one nominee for each open seat and the name of one additional nominee for each open seat to the Secretary.
units.action_summary: The Board is to evaluate nominees and submit one primary and one additional nominee name for each open seat to the Secretary.

units.obligation_text: Other qualified persons interested in serving in the open seats but not recommended by the Board will be designated by the Board as additional nominees for consideration by the Secretary;
units.action_summary: The Board will designate other qualified but not recommended persons as additional nominees for the Secretary's consideration.

units.obligation_text: The Board must submit nominations to the Secretary at least six months before the new Board term begins.
units.action_summary: The Board is required to send nominations to the Secretary at least six months before the new term.

units.obligation_text: From the nominations submitted by the Board, the Secretary shall select the members of the Board;
units.action_summary: The Secretary must select Board members from the nominations submitted by the Board.

units.obligation_text: No two members shall be employed by a single corporation, company, partnership, or any other legal entity. This includes subsidiaries and affiliates thereof;
units.action_summary: Prohibits two Board members from being employed by the same legal entity, including subsidiaries and affiliates.

units.obligation_text: The Board may recommend to the Secretary modifications to its nomination procedures as it deems appropriate.
units.action_summary: The Board is permitted to recommend modifications to its nomination procedures to the Secretary.

units.obligation_text: Any such modifications shall be implemented through rulemaking by the Secretary.
units.action_summary: The Secretary must implement any recommended nomination-procedure modifications via rulemaking.

units.obligation_text: A majority of Board members (exclusive of vacant seats) will constitute a quorum so long as at least two of the members present are importer members and five of the members present are domestic manufacturers.
units.action_summary: A quorum requires a majority of members, with at least two importers and five domestic manufacturers present.

units.obligation_text: If participation by telephone or other means is permitted, members participating by such means shall count as present in determining quorum or other voting requirements set forth in this section.
units.action_summary: Members participating by phone or other permitted means shall be counted as present for quorum and voting.

units.obligation_text: All votes at meetings of the Board, executive committee, and other committees will be cast in person or by electronic voting or other means as the Board and Secretary deem appropriate to allow members participating by telephone or other electronic means to cast votes.
units.actor: voting members / the Board and Secretary (methods)
units.action_summary: Votes must be cast in person or by electronic or other means the Board and Secretary deem appropriate to permit remote voting.

units.obligation_text: Voting by proxy will not be allowed.
units.action_summary: Prohibits voting by proxy.

units.obligation_text: Each member of the Board will be entitled to one vote on any matter put to the Board and the motion will carry if supported by a majority of Board members (exclusive of vacant seats), except for recommendations to change the assessment rate or to adopt a budget, both of which require affirmation by at least a majority of Board members plus two (exclusive of vacant seats).
units.action_summary: Each member has one vote; motions pass by majority, but changing assessment rates or adopting a budget require majority plus two.

units.obligation_text: The Board must give members and the Secretary timely notice of all Board, executive committee, and other committee meetings.
units.action_summary: The Board is required to give timely notice of all meetings to members and the Secretary.

units.obligation_text: In lieu of voting at a properly convened meeting, and when, in the opinion of the Board’s chairperson, such action is considered necessary, the Board may take action by mail, telephone, electronic mail, facsimile, or any other means of communication.
units.action_summary: The Board may act outside a convened meeting by mail, telephone, electronic means, or other communication when the chairperson deems necessary.

units.obligation_text: Any action taken under this procedure is valid only if: All members and the Secretary are notified, and the members are provided the opportunity to vote;
units.action_summary: For off-meeting actions to be valid, all members and the Secretary must be notified and members given an opportunity to vote.

units.obligation_text: Any action taken under this procedure is valid only if: A majority of Board members (exclusive of vacant seats) vote in favor of the action (unless a vote of a majority of Board members plus two (exclusive of vacant seats) is required under the Order);
units.action_summary: Off-meeting actions require a favorable vote of a majority of Board members, or majority plus two if so required by the Order.

units.obligation_text: Any action taken under this procedure is valid only if: All votes are promptly confirmed in writing and recorded in the Board minutes.
units.action_summary: All off-meeting votes must be promptly confirmed in writing and recorded in the minutes for the action to be valid.

units.obligation_text: A factor shall be used to determine the equivalent volume of softwood lumber in thousand board feet.
units.action_summary: A specified conversion factor must be used to determine equivalent volume in thousand board feet.

units.obligation_text: No later than seven years after this Order becomes effective and every seven years thereafter, to determine whether softwood lumber manufacturers for the U.S. market favor the continuation of the Order.
units.action_summary: A referendum to determine continuation of the Order must be held no later than seven years after effectiveness and every seven years thereafter.

units.obligation_text: The Order shall continue if it is favored by a majority of domestic manufacturers and importers voting in the referendum who also represent a majority of the volume of softwood lumber represented in the referendum who, during a representative period determined by the Secretary, have been engaged in the domestic manufacturing or importation of softwood lumber;
units.action_summary: The Order will remain in effect if a majority of voting domestic manufacturers and importers, representing a majority of volume, favor continuation.

units.obligation_text: Domestic product that cannot be categorized in the referenced HTSUS numbers if it were an import is not covered under this order.
units.action_summary: Domestic products not categorizable under the listed HTSUS numbers (if imported) are excluded from coverage under the Order.

units.obligation_text: Softwood lumber originating in the United States that is exported to another country and shipped back to the United States is also covered under this Order, provided it can be categorized in the referenced HTSUS numbers.
units.action_summary: U.S.-origin softwood lumber exported and returned is covered by the Order if it fits the referenced HTSUS categories.

units.obligation_text: Articles brought into the United States temporarily and for which an exemption is claimed under subchapter XIII of chapter 98 of the HTSUS are exempted from the SLA of 2008 and are not covered under this Order.
units.actor: articles temporarily imported with a subchapter XIII exemption
units.action_summary: Temporarily imported articles with a subchapter XIII HTSUS exemption are exempt from the SLA and excluded from this Order.

title: Reporting Requirements: Pecans Grown in the States of Alabama, Arkansas, Arizona, California, Florida, Georgia, Kansas, Louisiana, Missouri, Mississippi, North Carolina, New Mexico, Oklahoma, South Carolina, and Texas

units.obligation_text: Inter-handler transfers of inshell pecans, pursuant to § 986.62, shall be reported to the Council on APC Form 4.
units.action_summary: Report inter-handler transfers of inshell pecans to the Council using APC Form 4.

units.obligation_text: Handlers shall file reports by the tenth day of the month following the first transfer between two handlers.
units.action_summary: File the inter-handler transfer report by the 10th day of the month after the first transfer.

units.obligation_text: Should the tenth day of the month fall on a weekend or holiday, reports are due by the first business day following the tenth day of the month.
units.action_summary: If the 10th is a weekend/holiday, the report deadline moves to the next business day.

units.obligation_text: This report must be renewed each fiscal year.
units.action_summary: Renew the inter-handler transfer report each fiscal year.

units.obligation_text: The fiscal year covered by the report;
units.action_summary: Include the fiscal year covered by the report.

units.obligation_text: The names and signatures for both the transferring and receiving handler;
units.action_summary: Provide names and signatures of both transferring and receiving handlers.

units.obligation_text: Handler assuming the reporting and assessment obligations on the pecans transferred.
units.action_summary: Identify the handler who will assume reporting and assessment obligations for the transferred pecans.

units.obligation_text: Handlers shall submit to the Council a year-end inventory report following August 31 each fiscal year.
units.action_summary: Submit a year-end inventory report to the Council after August 31 each fiscal year.

units.obligation_text: Handlers shall file such reports by September 10.
units.action_summary: File the year-end inventory report by September 10.

units.obligation_text: Should September 10 fall on a weekend, reports are due by the first business day following September 10.
units.action_summary: If September 10 is a weekend, the report is due the next business day.

units.obligation_text: Such reports shall be reported to the Council on APC Form 5 and include:
units.action_summary: Use APC Form 5 to report year-end inventory and include required information.

units.obligation_text: Handlers shall submit to the Council, by the tenth day of the month, a summary report of inshell domestic pecans received, and all shipments, inventory, and committed inventory for pecans following the month of activity.
units.action_summary: Submit a monthly summary report (by the 10th) of inshell domestic pecans received, shipments, inventory, and committed inventory.

units.obligation_text: Should the tenth day of the month fall on a weekend or holiday, reports are due by the first business day following the tenth day of the month.
units.action_summary: If the 10th is a weekend/holiday, the monthly summary report is due the next business day.

units.obligation_text: The report shall be submitted to the Council on APC Form 1 and contain the following information:
units.action_summary: Submit the monthly summary report on APC Form 1 and include specified information.

units.obligation_text: The total weight and type of inshell pecans received during the reporting period;
units.action_summary: Provide the total weight and type of inshell pecans received during the reporting period.

units.obligation_text: The total weight and type of inshell pecans received year to date;
units.action_summary: Provide year-to-date total weight and type of inshell pecans received.

units.obligation_text: The weight of all shipments of pecans, inshell and shelled, and inter-handler transfers shipped and received during the reporting period;
units.action_summary: Report weights of all pecan shipments and inter-handler transfers during the reporting period.

units.obligation_text: The weight of all shipments of pecans, inshell and shelled, and inter-handler transfers shipped and received in the previous month and year to date;
units.action_summary: Provide weights of pecan shipments and inter-handler transfers for the previous month and year-to-date.

units.obligation_text: Total inventory held by handler;
units.action_summary: Report the total inventory held by the handler.

units.obligation_text: All the inventory committed (pecans not shipped, but sold or otherwise obligated) whether for domestic sale or export;
units.action_summary: Report all committed inventory (sold or otherwise obligated), for domestic sale or export.

units.obligation_text: The weight of all shelled or inshell pecans under contract for purchase from other handlers.
units.action_summary: Provide weights of shelled or inshell pecans under contract for purchase from other handlers.

units.obligation_text: Handlers shall submit to the Council, by the tenth day of the month following the month of activity, a summary report of shelled and inshell pecans imported during the preceding month.
units.action_summary: Submit, by the 10th of the following month, a summary report of shelled and inshell pecans imported in the preceding month.

units.obligation_text: Should the tenth day of the month fall on a weekend or holiday, reports are due by the first business day following the tenth day of the month.
units.action_summary: If the 10th is a weekend/holiday, the import summary report is due the next business day.

units.obligation_text: The report shall be submitted to the Council on APC Form 2 and contain the following information:
units.action_summary: Submit the import summary report on APC Form 2 and include specified information.

units.obligation_text: The weight of inshell pecans exported to Mexico for shelling;
units.action_summary: Report weight of inshell pecans exported to Mexico for shelling.

units.obligation_text: The date shelled pecans returned to the United States after shelling in Mexico;
units.action_summary: Provide the date shelled pecans returned to the U.S. after shelling in Mexico.

units.obligation_text: The weight of shelled pecans returned to the United States after shelling in Mexico;
units.action_summary: Report the weight of shelled pecans returned to the U.S. after shelling in Mexico.

units.obligation_text: The total weight of inshell pecans exported to Mexico for shelling, and shelled pecans returned from Mexico, year to date.
units.action_summary: Provide year-to-date totals for inshell pecans exported to Mexico for shelling and shelled pecans returned.

units.obligation_text: Handlers shall submit to the Council, by the tenth day of the month following the month of shipment, a report of exports.
units.action_summary: Submit an export report to the Council by the 10th of the month following shipment.

units.obligation_text: Should the tenth day of the month fall on a weekend or holiday, reports are due by the first business day following the tenth day of the month.
units.action_summary: If the 10th is a weekend/holiday, the export report is due the next business day.

units.obligation_text: The report shall be reported to the Council on APC Form 3 and contain the following information:
units.action_summary: Submit the export report on APC Form 3 and include specified information.

units.obligation_text: The name and address of the handler;
units.action_summary: Include the handler's name and address on the export report.

units.obligation_text: The month covered by the report;
units.action_summary: State the month covered by the export report.

units.obligation_text: The total weight of pecans shipped for export, whether inshell, shelled, or substandard during the reporting period;
units.action_summary: Report total weight of pecans shipped for export during the reporting period.

units.obligation_text: The total weight of pecans shipped for export, whether inshell, shelled, or substandard during the previous period and year to date;
units.action_summary: Provide export weights for the previous period and year-to-date.

units.obligation_text: The destination(s) of such exports.
units.action_summary: List the destination(s) for exported pecans.

title: Regulations and Procedures Under the Plant Variety Protection Act

units.obligation_text: Each certificate of plant variety protection certifies that the breeder has the right, during the term of the protection, to prevent others from selling the variety, offering it for sale, reproducing it, importing or exporting it, conditioning it, stocking it, or using it in producing a hybrid or different variety from it, as provided by the Act.
units.action_summary: Breeder is permitted to prevent others from selling, offering for sale, reproducing, importing/exporting, conditioning, stocking, or using the variety in producing hybrids or different varieties during the term of protection.

units.obligation_text: Application and exhibit forms shall be issued by the Commissioner.
units.action_summary: Commissioner must issue application and exhibit forms.

units.obligation_text: The fees for filing an application, examination, and certificate issuance shall be submitted with the application in accordance with §§ 97.175 through 97.178.
units.action_summary: Applicant must submit filing, examination, and certificate issuance fees with the application as specified in §§ 97.175-97.178.

units.obligation_text: With the application for a hybrid from self-incompatible parents, a declaration that a plot of vegetative material for each parent will be established in a public depository approved by the Commissioner and will be maintained for the duration of the certificate.
units.action_summary: Applicant must declare that vegetative plots for each parent will be established in a Commissioner-approved public depository and maintained for the certificate's duration.

units.obligation_text: With the application for an asexually propagated variety, a declaration that a deposit of propagating material in a public depository approved by the Commissioner will be made and maintained for the duration of the certificate.
units.action_summary: Applicant must declare that a deposit of propagating material in a Commissioner-approved public depository will be made and maintained for the certificate's duration.

units.obligation_text: Once a depository is recognized to be suitable by the Commissioner or has defaulted or discontinued its performance under this section, notice thereof will be published on the Plant Variety Protection Office website (https://www.ams.usda.gov/PVPO).
units.action_summary: When a depository is recognized or defaults/discontinues, the Office must publish notice on the PVPO website.

units.obligation_text: An original deposit of materials for seed-reproduced plants shall be made within three months of the filing date of the application or prior to issuance of the certificate, whichever occurs first.
units.action_summary: Applicant must make original deposit for seed-reproduced plants within three months of filing or before certificate issuance, whichever is earlier.

units.obligation_text: An original deposit of materials for tuber-propagated plants or asexually reproduced plants shall be made within three months from the notice of certificate issuance date.
units.action_summary: Applicant must make original deposit for tuber-propagated or asexually reproduced plants within three months of the notice of certificate issuance.

units.obligation_text: A waiver from these time requirements may be granted for good cause, such as delays in obtaining a phytosanitary certificate for the importation of voucher sample materials.
units.action_summary: Commissioner may grant a waiver of deposit time requirements for good cause (e.g., import phytosanitary delays).

units.obligation_text: When the original deposit is made, the applicant must promptly submit a statement from a person in a position to corroborate the fact, stating that the voucher specimen material which is deposited is the variety specifically identified in the application as filed.
units.action_summary: When original deposit is made, applicant must promptly submit a corroborating statement confirming the deposited voucher specimen is the variety identified in the application.

units.obligation_text: Such statement must be filed in the application and must contain the identifying information listed in paragraph (b) of this section and: (i) The name and address of the depository;
units.action_summary: The corroborating statement must include the depository's name and address.

units.obligation_text: (ii) The date of deposit;
units.action_summary: The corroborating statement must state the date of deposit.

units.obligation_text: (iii) The accession number given by the depository; and
units.action_summary: The corroborating statement must include the depository accession number.

units.obligation_text: (iv) A statement that the deposit is capable of reproduction.
units.action_summary: The corroborating statement must assert that the deposit is capable of reproduction.

units.obligation_text: When a delay waiver is granted due to technical difficulties with depositing propagating materials for asexually reproduced plants, the applicant is required to make a declaration that a voucher specimen will be provided within three months of a request by the Plant Variety Protection Office.
units.action_summary: If a delay waiver is granted for technical difficulties, applicant must declare that a voucher specimen will be provided within three months of PVPO's request.

units.obligation_text: Failure to provide a specimen as requested shall result in the certificate being regarded as abandoned.
units.action_summary: If applicant fails to provide the requested specimen, the certificate will be considered abandoned.

units.obligation_text: Drawings or photographs shall be in color when color is a distinguishing characteristic of the variety, and the color shall be described by use of Nickerson’s color fan, the Munsell Book of Color, the Royal Horticultural Society Colour Chart, or other recognized color chart.
units.action_summary: When color distinguishes the variety, drawings/photographs must be in color and the color must be described using a recognized color chart.

units.obligation_text: The color shall be described by use of Nickerson’s color fan, the Munsell Book of Color, the Royal Horticultural Society Colour Chart, or other recognized color chart.
units.action_summary: Applicant must describe color using one of the listed or other recognized color charts.

units.obligation_text: Drawings shall be sent flat, or may be sent in a suitable mailing tube, in accordance with instructions furnished by the Commissioner.
units.action_summary: Applicant must send drawings flat or, alternatively, may send them in a suitable mailing tube, following Commissioner's instructions.

units.obligation_text: Applications shall be numbered and dated in sequence in the order received by the Office.
units.action_summary: Office must number and date applications in sequence by receipt order.

units.obligation_text: Applicants will be informed in writing, by mail or email, as soon as practicable of the number and effective filing date of the application.
units.action_summary: Office must inform applicants in writing (mail or email) of the application number and effective filing date as soon as practicable.

units.obligation_text: If a joint owner refuses to join in an application or cannot be found after diligent effort, the remaining owner may file an application on behalf of him or herself and the missing owner.
units.action_summary: Remaining owner is permitted to file an application on behalf of themselves and the missing joint owner if the other owner refuses or cannot be located after diligent effort.

units.obligation_text: Such application shall be accompanied by a written explanation and shall state the last known address of the missing owner.
units.action_summary: The application filed by the remaining owner must include a written explanation and the missing owner's last known address.

units.obligation_text: Notice of the filing of the application shall be forwarded by the Office to the missing owner at the last known address.
units.action_summary: Office must forward notice of the filed application to the missing owner at the last known address.

units.obligation_text: If such notice is returned to the Office undelivered, or if the address of the missing owner is unknown, notice of the filing of the application shall be published once on the Plant Variety Protection Office website (https://www.ams.usda.gov/PVPO).
units.action_summary: If notice to the missing owner is undelivered or address unknown, the Office must publish notice of the application filing once on the PVPO website.

units.obligation_text: Prior to the issuance of the certificate, a missing owner may join in an application by filing a written explanation.
units.action_summary: A missing owner is permitted to join the application before certificate issuance by filing a written explanation.

units.obligation_text: Information relating to pending applications shall be published periodically as determined by the Commissioner to be necessary in the public interest.
units.action_summary: Office must publish information about pending applications periodically as the Commissioner deems necessary for the public interest.

units.obligation_text: With respect to each application, the Plant Variety Protection Office website shall show: (c) The name of the crop;
units.action_summary: PVPO website must display the name of the crop for each application.

units.obligation_text: Except as otherwise provided in § 97.104, if an applicant fails to advance actively his or her application within 30 days after the date when the last request for action was mailed to the applicant by the Office, or within such longer time as may be fixed by the Commissioner, the application shall be deemed abandoned.
units.action_summary: If applicant fails to actively advance the application within 30 days (or longer if fixed), the application will be deemed abandoned.

units.obligation_text: The filing and examination fees in such cases will not be refunded.
units.action_summary: When an application is deemed abandoned for failure to respond, filing and examination fees will not be refunded.

units.obligation_text: An original application which has been voluntarily withdrawn shall be returned to the applicant
units.action_summary: Office must return an original application that has been voluntarily withdrawn to the applicant.

units.obligation_text: An original application which has been voluntarily withdrawn ... may be reconsidered only by refiling and payment of new filing and examination fees.
units.action_summary: A voluntarily withdrawn original application can only be reconsidered if the applicant refiles and pays new filing and examination fees.

units.obligation_text: If, on examination, PVPO determines that the applicant is entitled to a certificate, a notice of allowance shall be sent to the applicant or his or her attorney or agent of record, if any, requesting verification of the variety name and of the name of the owner.
units.action_summary: If PVPO determines entitlement to a certificate, PVPO must send a notice of allowance requesting verification of the variety and owner names.

units.obligation_text: The notice will also provide an opportunity for withdrawal of the application before certificate issuance.
units.action_summary: The notice gives the applicant an opportunity to withdraw the application before certificate issuance.

units.obligation_text: The applicant must respond within 30 days from the date of the notice of allowance.
units.action_summary: Applicant is required to respond within 30 days of the notice of allowance.

units.obligation_text: Thereafter, a fee for delayed response shall be charged as specified in § 97.175(f).
units.action_summary: If applicant responds after 30 days, the Office will charge a delayed response fee as specified in §97.175(f).

units.obligation_text: After the notice of allowance has been issued and the applicant has clearly specified whether or not the variety shall be sold by variety name only as a class of certified seed, the certificate shall be promptly issued.
units.action_summary: Once notice of allowance is issued and the applicant has specified the variety's sale classification, the Office must promptly issue the certificate.

units.obligation_text: Once an election is made and a certificate issued specifying that seed of the variety shall be sold by variety name only as a class of certified seed, no waiver of such rights shall be permitted by amendment of the certificate.
units.action_summary: After electing sale by variety name as certified seed and issuance of the certificate, no waiver of those rights may be obtained by amending the certificate.

units.obligation_text: Upon request by the Office, the owner shall replenish the seed or propagating material of the variety and shall pay the handling fee for replenishment.
units.action_summary: When requested by the Office, the owner must replenish seed/propagating material and pay a handling fee.

units.obligation_text: Samples of seed or propagating material related to abandoned applications or certificates will be retained or destroyed by the depository.
units.action_summary: The depository will retain or destroy samples related to abandoned applications or certificates.

units.obligation_text: Failure to replenish seed or propagating material within 3 months from the date of request shall result in the certificate being regarded as abandoned.
units.action_summary: If the owner fails to replenish within 3 months of the Office's request, the certificate will be considered abandoned.

units.obligation_text: No sooner than 1 year after the date of such request, notices of abandoned certificates shall be published on the Plant Variety Protection Office website (https://www.ams.usda.gov/PVPO), indicating that the variety has become open for use by the public and, if previously specified to be sold by variety name as ‘‘certified seed only,’’ that such restriction no longer applies.
units.action_summary: At least one year after request, Commissioner must publish notices of abandoned certificates on PVPO website, noting the variety is open for public use and any prior 'certified seed only' restriction no longer applies.

units.obligation_text: If the seed or propagating material is submitted within 9 months of the final due date, it may be accepted by the Commissioner as though no abandonment had occurred.
units.action_summary: Commissioner may accept seed/propagating material submitted within 9 months of final due date and treat it as if abandonment did not occur.

units.obligation_text: For good cause, the Commissioner may extend for a reasonable time the period for submitting seed or propagating material before declaring the certificate abandoned.
units.action_summary: Commissioner may extend the submission period for good cause prior to declaring abandonment.

units.obligation_text: A certificate may be voluntarily abandoned by the applicant or his or her attorney or agent of record or the assignee of record by notifying the Commissioner in writing.
units.action_summary: Applicant (or attorney/agent/assignee) may voluntarily abandon a certificate by written notice to the Commissioner.

units.obligation_text: Upon receipt of such notice, the Commissioner shall publish a notice on the Plant Variety Protection Office website (https://www.ams.usda.gov/PVPO) that the variety has become open for use by the public, and if previously specified to be sold by variety name as ‘‘certified seed only,’’ that such restriction no longer applies.
units.action_summary: When Commissioner receives voluntary abandonment notice, Commissioner must publish notice on PVPO website that the variety is open for public use and any 'certified seed only' restriction no longer applies.

units.obligation_text: Upon issuance of a certificate, the owner of the variety, or his or her designee, may label the variety, propagating material of the variety, or containers of the seed of the variety or plants produced from such seed or propagating material substantially as follows: 'Unauthorized Propagation Prohibited—(Unauthorized Seed or Propagating Material Multiplication Prohibited)—U.S. Protected Variety.'
units.action_summary: Owner/designee is permitted to label the variety/material/containers with the specified 'Unauthorized Propagation Prohibited' notice upon certificate issuance.

units.obligation_text: Where applicable, 'PVPA 1994' or 'PVPA 1994—Unauthorized Sales for Reproductive Purposes Prohibited' may be added to the notice.
units.action_summary: Owner may add 'PVPA 1994' or related phrase to the notice where applicable.

units.obligation_text: An owner who contemplates filing an application and releases for testing or increase seed of the variety or propagating material or reproducible plant material of the variety may label such plant material or containers of the seed or plant material substantially as follows: 'Unauthorized Propagation Prohibited—For Testing (or Increase) Only.'
units.action_summary: An owner may label plant material/containers for testing or increase with the specified 'Unauthorized Propagation Prohibited—For Testing (or Increase) Only' notice.

units.obligation_text: The following fees and charges apply to the services and actions specified below:
units.action_summary: Specified fees and charges apply to users/applicants for the listed services and actions.

units.obligation_text: Field inspections or other services requiring travel by a representative of the Plant Variety Protection Office, made at the request of the applicant, shall be reimbursable in full (including travel, per diem or subsistence, salary, and administrative costs), in accordance with standardized government travel regulations.
units.action_summary: Applicant must reimburse in full the costs of PVPO travel-related inspections or services requested by the applicant, per government travel regulations.

units.obligation_text: Any other service not covered in this section ... will be charged for at rates prescribed by the Commissioner, but in no event shall they exceed $97 per employee hour.
units.action_summary: The Commissioner will charge for other services at prescribed rates but must not exceed $97 per employee hour.

units.obligation_text: Payments can be submitted through the electronic Plant Variety Protection system or pay.gov.
units.action_summary: Payer may submit payments electronically via PVPO system or pay.gov.

units.obligation_text: Checks or money orders shall be made payable to the Treasurer of the United States.
units.action_summary: Checks or money orders must be made payable to the Treasurer of the United States.

units.obligation_text: Remittances from foreign countries must be payable and immediately negotiable in the United States for the full amount of the prescribed fee.
units.action_summary: Foreign remittances must be payable and immediately negotiable in the U.S. for the full fee amount.

units.obligation_text: Money sent by mail to the Office shall be sent at the sender’s risk.
units.action_summary: Senders mailing money to the Office bear the risk of mailing.

units.obligation_text: Money paid by mistake or excess payments shall be refunded, but a mere change of plans after the payment of money, as when a party decides to withdraw an application or to withdraw an appeal, shall not entitle a party to a refund.
units.action_summary: Office must refund mistaken or excess payments, but will not refund merely because a party changes plans after payment.

units.obligation_text: However, the examination fee shall be refunded if an application is voluntarily withdrawn or abandoned pursuant to § 97.23(a) before the examination has begun.
units.action_summary: Office must refund the examination fee if the application is voluntarily withdrawn or abandoned under §97.23(a) before examination starts.

units.obligation_text: The certificate issuance fee shall be refunded if an application is voluntarily withdrawn or abandoned after an examination has been completed and before a certificate has been issued.
units.action_summary: Office must refund the certificate issuance fee if application is voluntarily withdrawn or abandoned after examination is complete but before certificate issuance.

units.obligation_text: Amounts of $1 or less shall not be refunded unless specifically demanded.
units.action_summary: Office will not refund amounts of $1 or less unless specifically requested.

units.obligation_text: Whenever it shall be found by the Commissioner or Secretary that none of the above modes of serving the paper is practicable, service may be by notice, published once on the Plant Variety Protection Office website (https://www.ams.usda.gov/PVPO).
units.action_summary: If other service modes are impracticable, Commissioner or Secretary may serve papers by publishing a notice once on the PVPO website.

units.obligation_text: Any applicant dissatisfied with the decision of the Secretary on appeal may appeal to the U.S. Courts of Appeals for the Federal Circuit, or institute a civil action in the U.S. District Court as set forth in the Act.
units.action_summary: Applicant dissatisfied with Secretary's decision may appeal to the Federal Circuit or file a civil action in U.S. District Court under the Act.

units.obligation_text: In such cases, the appellant or plaintiff shall give notice to the Secretary, state the reasons for appeal or civil action, and obtain a certified copy of the record.
units.action_summary: Appellant/plaintiff must notify the Secretary, state reasons for appeal/civil action, and obtain a certified copy of the record.

units.obligation_text: The certified copy of the record shall be forwarded to the Court by the Plant Variety Protection Office on order of, and at the expense of the appellant or plaintiff.
units.action_summary: PVPO must forward the certified record to the Court when ordered, and the appellant/plaintiff must bear the expense.

units.obligation_text: Voluntary submissions of varietal descriptions of 'public varieties' on forms obtainable from the Office will be accepted for publication on the Plant Variety Protection Office website (https://www.ams.usda.gov/PVPO).
units.action_summary: The Office will accept voluntary submissions of varietal descriptions of 'public varieties' for publication on the PVPO website.

title: Exceptions to Geographic Boundaries

units.obligation_text: Comments must be received by May 1, 2020.
units.action_summary: Comments responding to this ANPR must be received by May 1, 2020.

units.obligation_text: Comments must be submitted through the Federal e-rulemaking portal at http://www.regulations.gov
units.action_summary: Commenters are required to submit comments via the Federal e-rulemaking portal.

units.obligation_text: and should reference the document number and the date and page number of this issue of the Federal Register.
units.action_summary: Commenters should include the document number and the date and page number of this Federal Register issue with their submission.

units.obligation_text: All comments submitted in response to this notice will be included in the record and will be made available to the public.
units.action_summary: AMS will include all submitted comments in the public record and make them publicly available.

units.obligation_text: Please be advised that the identity of the individuals or entities submitting comments will be made public on the internet at the address provided above.
units.action_summary: AMS will disclose the identity of commenters on the internet.

units.obligation_text: Each official inspection agency (OA) in the United States is assigned a specific geographic area in which it performs all official grain inspection and weighing services for customers within that geographic area (7 U.S.C. 79(f)(2)(A)).
units.action_summary: Each OA is assigned a specific geographic area to perform official inspection and weighing services.

units.obligation_text: The USGSA also provides that customers may obtain services from other OAs under certain circumstances.
units.action_summary: Customers are permitted to obtain services from OAs other than their designated OA under specified circumstances.

units.obligation_text: OAs may cross geographic boundaries to provide services to requesting customers if the designated OA for the customer's geographic area is unable to provide necessary services on a timely basis.
units.action_summary: OAs are permitted to cross geographic boundaries to serve a customer when the customer's designated OA cannot provide necessary services in a timely manner.

units.obligation_text: OAs may cross geographic boundaries to provide services to requesting customers if the customer requires probe inspection on barge-lot basis.
units.action_summary: OAs are permitted to cross boundaries to provide requested probe inspections on a barge-lot basis.

units.obligation_text: OAs may cross geographic boundaries to provide services to requesting customers if the OA for the customer's geographic area agrees in writing with the adjacent official agency to waive the current geographic restriction at the customer's request.
units.action_summary: OAs may cross boundaries when the designated OA agrees in writing with the adjacent OA to waive the geographic restriction.

units.obligation_text: Exceptions must be approved on a case-by-case basis by AMS's Federal Grain Inspection Service (FGIS).
units.action_summary: FGIS is required to approve exceptions to geographic restrictions on a case-by-case basis.

units.obligation_text: The customer, the designated OA in the customer's geographic area, the OA that has been providing service under the exception, and FGIS must agree to terminate the exception.
units.actor: customer; designated OA; alternate OA; FGIS
units.action_summary: All listed parties are required to jointly agree to terminate a nonuse-of-service exception.

units.obligation_text: The requirement for all parties to jointly agree on termination of the "nonuse of service" exception does not apply if the designation of an official agency is terminated.
units.action_summary: The joint-agreement requirement for terminating a nonuse exception is excepted when the OA's designation is terminated.

units.obligation_text: If the designation of an official agency is renewed or restored after being terminated, the exceptions that were previously approved, under 7 U.S.C. 79(f)(2)(B), may be renewed or restored by requesting a determination from FGIS.
units.action_summary: Previously approved exceptions can be renewed/restored by requesting a determination from FGIS after an agency designation is renewed or restored.

units.obligation_text: The requesting facility would submit a verbal or written request for a "timely service" exception.
units.action_summary: A facility seeking a timely service exception would submit a verbal or written request.

units.obligation_text: The requesting facility would provide documentation that the designated OA cannot provide service within six (6) hours from the time of the request.
units.action_summary: The requesting facility would need to document that the designated OA cannot provide service within six hours of the request.

units.obligation_text: Valid documentation may include voice mail message, text message, or email which shows the date and time of the request.
units.action_summary: Acceptable proof of inability to provide service within six hours may include voicemail, text, or email showing date/time.

units.obligation_text: The services requested from the designated OA would be within the time frames established in the OA's approved fee schedule.
units.action_summary: Requested services must fall within timeframes in the designated OA's approved fee schedule.

units.obligation_text: The requesting facility would submit a written request for a "nonuse of service" exception.
units.action_summary: A facility seeking a nonuse-of-service exception would submit a written request.

units.obligation_text: The requesting facility would demonstrate it has not had official sample-lot inspection or weighing services for 90-consecutive days from its designated OA.
units.action_summary: The facility would need to show it has not received official sample-lot inspection or weighing services from its designated OA for 90 consecutive days.

units.obligation_text: The request would document, in writing, why the requesting facility has not received official sample-lot inspection or weighing services for 90-consecutive days from its designated OA.
units.action_summary: The request must include written documentation explaining why the facility did not receive services for the 90-day period.

units.obligation_text: Reasons would be based on data and facts regarding the designated OA's operational capacity to provide requested service.
units.action_summary: The written reasons should rely on data and facts about the designated OA's operational capacity.

units.obligation_text: Prior to finalizing a decision for a "nonuse of service" exception, AMS would take the following into consideration:
units.action_summary: AMS would consider several listed factors before finalizing a decision on a nonuse-of-service exception.

units.obligation_text: The location of the specified service point(s);
units.action_summary: Consider the location(s) of the service point(s).

units.obligation_text: Services offered/requested;
units.action_summary: Consider the services being offered or requested.

units.obligation_text: The ability of the alternate OA to take on additional customers;
units.action_summary: Consider whether the alternate OA can accommodate additional customers.

units.obligation_text: The ability to staff an onsite laboratory;
units.action_summary: Consider the ability to staff an onsite laboratory.

units.obligation_text: Impact of weather conditions on the designated OA's ability to provide service;
units.action_summary: Consider weather impacts on the designated OA's ability to provide service.

units.obligation_text: Whether the requesting facility has ever utilized the official system (i.e., facilities that have never used the official system before do not automatically qualify for "nonuse of service").
units.action_summary: AMS should consider whether the facility has ever used the official system; facilities that never have used it do not automatically qualify.

units.section: Additional Considerations for Comment - Comments submission
units.obligation_text: Comments in response to any or all of the above criteria and questions should be submitted to the address provided in the ADDRESSES section of this notice and must be received by May 1, 2020 to ensure consideration.
units.action_summary: Commenters should submit responses to the provided address and those comments must be received by May 1, 2020 to be considered.

title: Undue and Unreasonable Preferences and Advantages Under the Packers and Stockyards Act

units.obligation_text: The Secretary will consider one or more criteria when determining whether a packer, swine contractor, or live poultry dealer has made or given any undue or unreasonable preference or advantage to any particular person or locality in any respect in violation of section 202(b) of the Act.
units.action_summary: The Secretary must consider one or more criteria when determining whether a packer, swine contractor, or live poultry dealer gave an undue or unreasonable preference or advantage in violation of section 202(b).

units.obligation_text: Cannot be justified on the basis of a cost savings related to dealing with different producers, sellers, or growers;
units.actor: The Secretary (as a criterion in determining undue or unreasonable preference)
units.action_summary: The Secretary may consider that a preference/advantage is improper if it cannot be justified by cost savings from dealing with different producers, sellers, or growers.

units.obligation_text: Cannot be justified on the basis of meeting a competitor’s prices;
units.actor: The Secretary (as a criterion in determining undue or unreasonable preference)
units.action_summary: The Secretary may consider that a preference/advantage is improper if it cannot be justified by efforts to meet a competitor's prices.

units.obligation_text: Cannot be justified on the basis of meeting other terms offered by a competitor;
units.actor: The Secretary (as a criterion in determining undue or unreasonable preference)
units.action_summary: The Secretary may consider that a preference/advantage is improper if it cannot be justified by matching other terms offered by a competitor.

units.obligation_text: Cannot be justified as a reasonable business decision that would be customary in the industry.
units.actor: The Secretary (as a criterion in determining undue or unreasonable preference)
units.action_summary: The Secretary may consider that a preference/advantage is improper if it cannot be justified as a customary reasonable business decision in the industry.

title: Egg Research and Promotion; Reapportionment

units.obligation_text: Pursuant to § 1250.328 (d) and (e), the 48 contiguous States of the United States shall be grouped into three geographic areas, as follows:
units.actor: the 48 contiguous States (for purposes of Board membership grouping)
units.action_summary: Group the 48 contiguous States into three geographic areas for Board membership purposes.

units.obligation_text: Area I (East)—Connecticut, Delaware, Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, Vermont, Virginia, West Virginia, the District of Columbia, Alabama, Georgia, Florida, Louisiana, Mississippi, North Carolina, South Carolina and Texas;
units.action_summary: Specify that the listed states constitute Area I (East).

units.obligation_text: Area II (Central)—Arkansas, Oklahoma, Illinois, Indiana, Kentucky, Michigan, Missouri, Ohio, Tennessee, and Wisconsin;
units.action_summary: Specify that the listed states constitute Area II (Central).

units.obligation_text: Area III (West)—Arizona, California, Colorado, Idaho, Iowa, Kansas, Minnesota, Montana, Nebraska, Nevada, New Mexico, North Dakota, South Dakota, Utah, Washington, and Wyoming.
units.action_summary: Specify that the listed states constitute Area III (West).

units.obligation_text: Board representation among the three geographic areas is apportioned to reflect the percentages of United States egg production in each area times 18 (total Board membership).
units.actor: Board representation (as apportioned by the Board/Administrator)
units.action_summary: Apportion Board seats among the three areas based on each area's share of U.S. egg production multiplied by 18 total seats.

units.obligation_text: The distribution of members of the Board is: Area I–6, Area II–6, and Area III–6.
units.action_summary: Assign 6 Board members to each Area I, II, and III.

units.obligation_text: Each member will have an alternate appointed from the same area.
units.action_summary: Ensure each Board member has an alternate appointed from the same geographic area.

title: National Organic Program: Strengthening Organic Enforcement

units.obligation_text: Except for the exempt operations described in § 205.101, each operation, or portion of an operation, that produces or handles agricultural products that are intended to be sold, labeled, or represented as "100 percent organic," "organic," or "made with organic (specified ingredients or food group(s))" must be certified according to the provisions of subpart E of this part and must meet all other applicable requirements of this part.
units.actor: each operation or portion of an operation producing or handling products represented as organic
units.action_summary: Operations selling/handling products represented as organic must be certified under subpart E and meet all applicable part 205 requirements, unless exempt under §205.101.

units.obligation_text: The following operations in paragraphs (a) through (e) of this section are exempt from certification under subpart E of this part and from submitting an organic system plan for acceptance or approval under § 205.201 but must comply with the applicable organic production and handling requirements of subpart C of this part, including the provisions for prevention of contact of organic products with prohibited substances set forth in § 205.272, and the specific additional requirements stipulated in § 205.101(a) through (f).
units.action_summary: Specified small/retail/limited operations are exempt from certification and OSP submission but must comply with subpart C and specified additional requirements in §205.101(a)-(f).

units.obligation_text: The products from such operations must not be used as ingredients identified as organic in processed products produced by another handling operation.
units.actor: exempt production or handling operations (≤ $5,000 organic sales)
units.action_summary: Products from these exempt operations cannot be used as organic-identified ingredients in processed products made by other handlers.

units.obligation_text: Such operations must comply with the labeling provisions of § 205.310.
units.actor: exempt production or handling operations (≤ $5,000 organic sales)
units.action_summary: These exempt operations must follow the labeling provisions of §205.310.

units.obligation_text: A retail operation or a portion of a retail operation that sells, but does not process, organically produced agricultural products.
units.action_summary: Retail operations that only sell (not process) organic products are included in the exemptions described in this section.

units.obligation_text: Such operations must comply with the labeling provisions of § 205.310, and must maintain records sufficient to: (1) Prove that agricultural products identified as organic were organically produced and handled; and (2) Verify quantities produced or sold from such agricultural products.
units.actor: retail operations that process previously labeled organic products onsite at point of sale
units.action_summary: These retail operations must comply with §205.310 labeling and keep records proving organic origin and verifying quantities produced or sold.

units.obligation_text: Such operations must comply with the labeling provisions of §§ 205.305 and 205.310 and must maintain records sufficient to: (1) Prove that agricultural products identified as organic were organically produced and handled; and (2) Verify quantities produced or sold from such agricultural products.
units.actor: handling operations that only handle products with <70% organic ingredients or only identify organic ingredients on the information panel
units.action_summary: These handling operations must comply with §§205.305 and 205.310 labeling rules and keep records proving organic origin and quantities.

units.obligation_text: An operation that only stores, receives, and/or loads agricultural products, but does not process or alter such agricultural products.
units.action_summary: Operations that only store/receive/load (not process or alter) are included in the exemptions.

units.obligation_text: Records described in subparagraphs (a)–(d) of this section must be maintained for no less than 3 years beyond their creation, and the operations must allow representatives of the Secretary and the applicable State organic programs’ governing State official access to these records for inspection and copying during normal business hours to determine compliance with the applicable regulations set forth in this part.
units.action_summary: Exempt operations must retain required records for at least 3 years and allow access for inspection and copying by USDA and applicable State officials during normal business hours.

units.obligation_text: Fully disclose all activities and transactions of the certified operation in sufficient detail as to be readily understood and audited, including identification in records of products as "100% organic," "organic," or "made with organic (specified ingredients or food group(s))," as applicable;
units.action_summary: Certified operations must fully disclose activities and transactions in detailed, auditable records including product organic identification.

units.obligation_text: Include audit trail documentation for product handled or produced by the certified operation;
units.action_summary: Certified operations must include audit trail documentation for products they handle or produce.

units.obligation_text: A description of the monitoring practices and procedures to be performed and maintained, including the frequency with which they will be performed, to verify that the plan is effectively implemented. This must include a description of the monitoring practices and procedures to verify suppliers in the supply chain and organic status of products received, and to prevent organic fraud, as appropriate to the certified operation’s activities;
units.actor: applicant/certified operation (as part of organic system plan)
units.action_summary: Organic system plans must describe monitoring practices (including frequency), supplier verification, product organic status checks, and measures to prevent organic fraud.

units.obligation_text: In addition to paragraph (a) of this section, a grower group operation’s organic system plan must describe its internal control system.
units.actor: grower group operation (as part of organic system plan)
units.action_summary: Grower group organic system plans must include a description of the internal control system.

units.obligation_text: Define the organizational structure, roles, and responsibilities of all personnel;
units.actor: grower group operation (internal control system description)
units.action_summary: The internal control system description must define organizational structure and personnel roles/responsibilities.

units.obligation_text: Identify grower group production units and locations;
units.actor: grower group operation (internal control system description)
units.action_summary: The internal control system must identify production units and their locations.

units.obligation_text: Define geographical proximity criteria for grower group members and grower group production units;
units.actor: grower group operation (internal control system description)
units.action_summary: The internal control system must define geographical proximity criteria for members and production units.

units.obligation_text: Describe characteristics of high-risk grower group members and grower group production units;
units.actor: grower group operation (internal control system description)
units.action_summary: The internal control system must describe characteristics that identify high-risk members and production units.

units.obligation_text: Describe shared production practices and inputs;
units.actor: grower group operation (internal control system description)
units.action_summary: The internal control system must describe shared production practices and inputs used by the group.

units.obligation_text: Describe the internal monitoring, surveillance, and auditing methods used to assess the compliance of all grower group members;
units.actor: grower group operation (internal control system description)
units.action_summary: The internal control system must describe monitoring, surveillance, and auditing methods to assess member compliance.

units.obligation_text: Describe the system of sanctions for noncompliant grower group members, including procedures to address noncompliances detected among grower group members, impose sanctions, and remove grower group members when warranted, and procedures for reporting noncompliances to the certifying agent;
units.actor: grower group operation (internal control system description)
units.action_summary: The internal control system must describe sanctions and procedures for addressing, sanctioning, removing noncompliant members, and reporting noncompliances to the certifier.

units.obligation_text: Describe measures to protect against potential conflicts of interest;
units.actor: grower group operation (internal control system description)
units.action_summary: The internal control system must describe conflict-of-interest protections.

units.obligation_text: Describe how training, production and handling inputs, and other resources are procured and provided to all grower group members and personnel;
units.actor: grower group operation (internal control system description)
units.action_summary: The internal control system must explain procurement and distribution of training, inputs, and resources to members.

units.obligation_text: Have clear policies and procedures to verify the grower group operation’s and grower group members’ compliance with the USDA organic regulations;
units.actor: grower group operation (internal control system description)
units.action_summary: The internal control system must include policies and procedures to verify compliance with USDA organic regulations.

units.obligation_text: Address any other terms or conditions determined by the Administrator to be necessary to enforce compliance with the USDA organic regulations and the Act.
units.actor: grower group operation (internal control system description)
units.action_summary: The internal control system must include any additional terms or conditions the Administrator requires to enforce compliance.

units.obligation_text: Each shipment of organic products imported into the United States through U.S. Ports of Entry must be certified pursuant to subpart E of this part, labeled pursuant to subpart D of this part, be declared as organic to U.S. Customs and Border Protection, and be associated with a valid NOP Import Certificate (Form NOP 2110–1) or equivalent data source.
units.actor: each shipment of organic products imported into the United States
units.action_summary: Imported organic shipments must be certified, labeled, declared to CBP, and associated with a valid NOP Import Certificate or equivalent.

units.obligation_text: Persons exporting organic products to the United States must request an NOP Import Certificate, or provide data through an equivalent data source, from a certifying agent, for each physical shipment of certified organic products prior to their export.
units.actor: persons exporting organic products to the United States
units.action_summary: Exporters must request an NOP Import Certificate or provide equivalent data for each physical shipment before export.

units.obligation_text: Only certifying agents accredited by the USDA or foreign certifying agents authorized under an organic trade arrangement may issue an NOP Import Certificate or approve a listing in an equivalent data source (e.g., a third-party export system).
units.action_summary: Only USDA-accredited or authorized foreign certifying agents are permitted to issue NOP Import Certificates or approve equivalent listings.

units.obligation_text: The certifying agent must review an NOP Import Certificate request, determine whether the shipment complies with the USDA organic regulations, and issue the NOP Import Certificate or equivalent within 30 calendar days of receipt if the shipment complies with the USDA organic regulations.
units.action_summary: Certifying agents must review import certificate requests, determine compliance, and issue certificates or equivalent within 30 calendar days if compliant.

units.obligation_text: Each compliant organic shipment must be declared as organic to U.S. Customs and Border Protection through a U.S. Port of Entry by uploading the unique NOP Import Certificate, or equivalent electronic data entry, into the U.S. Customs and Border Protection’s Automated Commercial Environment system.
units.actor: the importer of record or declarant
units.action_summary: Compliant organic shipments must be declared to CBP by uploading the NOP Import Certificate or equivalent into ACE.

units.obligation_text: Upon receiving a shipment with organic products, the organic importer of record must ensure the shipment is accompanied by a verified NOP Import Certificate or equivalent; must verify that the shipment contains only the quantity and type of certified organic product specified on the NOP Import Certificate or equivalent; and must verify that the shipment has had no contact with prohibited substances pursuant to § 205.272 or exposure to ionizing radiation pursuant to § 205.105, since export.
units.action_summary: Importers of record must ensure shipments have verified import certificates, verify quantity/type matches the certificate, and verify no contact with prohibited substances or ionizing radiation since export.

units.obligation_text: Products produced in a foreign country and exported for sale in the United States must be certified pursuant to subpart E of this part, labeled pursuant to this subpart D, and must comply with the requirements in § 205.273, Imports to the United States.
units.actor: products produced in a foreign country (and their producers/exporters)
units.action_summary: Foreign-produced products exported for sale in the U.S. must be certified under subpart E, labeled under subpart D, and comply with §205.273 import requirements.

units.obligation_text: Be processed using ionizing radiation, pursuant to § 205.105(f);
units.action_summary: Organic products are prohibited from being processed using ionizing radiation (per §205.105(f)).

units.obligation_text: Be produced using sewage sludge, pursuant to § 205.105(g);
units.action_summary: Organic products are prohibited from being produced using sewage sludge (per §205.105(g)).

units.obligation_text: Dividing the total net weight (excluding water and salt) of combined organic ingredients at formulation by the total weight (excluding water and salt) of all ingredients.
units.action_summary: To calculate percentage of organic ingredients, divide the total net weight of organic ingredients (excl. water/salt) by total weight of all ingredients (excl. water/salt).

units.obligation_text: Dividing the fluid volume of all organic ingredients (excluding water and salt) at formulation by the fluid volume of all ingredients (excluding water and salt) if the product and ingredients are liquid. If the liquid product is identified on the principal display panel or information panel as being reconstituted from concentrates, the calculation should be made based on single-strength concentrations of the ingredients and all ingredients.
units.action_summary: For liquids, calculate organic percentage by dividing organic ingredient fluid volume by total fluid volume; if reconstituted from concentrates, base calculation on single-strength concentrations.

units.obligation_text: For products containing organically produced ingredients in both solid and liquid form, dividing the combined weight of the solid organic ingredients and the weight of the liquid organic ingredients (excluding water and salt) at formulation by the total weight (excluding water and salt) of all ingredients.
units.action_summary: For mixed solid/liquid products, calculate organic percentage by combining weights of solid and liquid organic ingredients (excl. water/salt) divided by total ingredients weight (excl. water/salt).
