units.obligation_text: Nonretail containers used to ship or store certified organic product must display the following: (1) The term, "100 percent organic," "organic," or "made with organic (specified ingredients or food group(s))," as applicable, to identify the product; (2) The statement, "Certified organic by (name of certifying agent)," or similar phrase, to identify the name of the certifying agent that certified the producer of the product, or, if processed, the certifying agent that certified the last handler that processed the product; and (3) The production lot number of the product, shipping identification, or other information needed to ensure traceability.
units.actor: handlers using nonretail containers to ship or store certified organic product
units.action_summary: Nonretail containers for certified organic products must display product organic term, certifier statement, and lot/shipping identification to ensure traceability.

units.obligation_text: Nonretail containers used to ship or store certified organic product may display the following: (1) Special handling instructions needed to maintain the organic integrity of the product; (2) The USDA seal. Use of the USDA seal must comply with § 205.311; (3) The name and contact information of the certified producer of the product, or if processed, the last certified handler that processed the product; (4) The seal, logo, or other identifying mark of the certifying agent that certified the producer of the product, or if processed, the last handler that processed the product; and/or (5) The business address, website, and/or contact information of the certifying agent.
units.actor: handlers using nonretail containers to ship or store certified organic product
units.action_summary: Handlers may display handling instructions, USDA seal (subject to §205.311), producer/contact info, certifier marks, and certifier contact details on nonretail containers.

units.obligation_text: Use of the USDA seal must comply with § 205.311;
units.actor: persons using the USDA seal on nonretail containers
units.action_summary: Any use of the USDA seal on nonretail containers must comply with §205.311.

units.obligation_text: Shipping containers of domestically produced product labeled as organic intended for export to international markets may be labeled in accordance with any shipping container labeling requirements of the foreign country of destination or the container labeling specifications of a foreign contract buyer: Provided, That, the shipping containers and shipping documents accompanying such organic products are clearly marked "For Export Only" and: Provided further, That, proof of such container marking and export must be maintained by the handler in accordance with recordkeeping requirements for exempt operations under § 205.101.
units.actor: handlers of domestically produced organic products intended for export
units.action_summary: Handlers may label export shipping containers per foreign requirements only if containers/docs are clearly marked 'For Export Only' and handlers maintain proof of marking and export per §205.101 recordkeeping.

units.obligation_text: The certifying agent must issue a certificate of organic operation. The certificate of organic operation must be generated from INTEGRITY and may be provided to certified operations electronically.
units.action_summary: Certifying agents must issue certificates of organic operation generated from INTEGRITY and may provide them electronically.

units.obligation_text: In addition to the certificate of organic operation provided for in § 205.404(b), a certifying agent may issue its own addenda to the certificate of organic operation. If issued, any addenda must include: (1) Name, address, and contact information for the certified operation; (2) The certified operation’s unique ID number/code that corresponds to the certified operation’s ID number/code in USDA Organic INTEGRITY; (3) A link to USDA Organic INTEGRITY or a link to the certified operation’s profile in USDA Organic INTEGRITY, along with a statement, "You may verify the certification of this operation at USDA Organic INTEGRITY," or a similar statement; (4) Name, address, and contact information of the certifying agent; (5) "Addendum issue date;" and (6) "Addendum expiration date," which must not exceed the expiration date of the certificate of organic operation.
units.action_summary: Certifying agents may issue addenda to certificates; if they do, addenda must include specified identifying and contact information, links, and issue/expiration dates (expiration not to exceed certificate expiration).

units.obligation_text: To continue certification, a certified operation must annually pay the certification fees and submit the following information to the certifying agent: (1) A summary statement, supported by documentation, detailing any deviations from, changes to, modifications to, or other amendments made to the organic system plan submitted during the previous year; and (2) Any additions or deletions to the previous year’s organic system plan, intended to be undertaken in the coming year, detailed pursuant to § 205.201; (3) Any additions to or deletions from the information required pursuant to § 205.401(b); and (4) Other information as deemed necessary by the certifying agent to determine compliance with the Act and the regulations in this part.
units.action_summary: To maintain certification, operations must annually pay fees and submit documentation about OSP changes, planned additions/deletions, §205.401(b) info changes, and other information requested by certifying agent.

units.obligation_text: The certifying agent must arrange and conduct an on-site inspection, pursuant to § 205.403, of the certified operation at least once per calendar year.
units.action_summary: Certifying agents must arrange and conduct at least one on-site inspection per calendar year for each certified operation.

units.obligation_text: Initial and annual on-site inspections of a grower group operation as defined in § 205.2 must: (i) Assess the compliance of the internal control system of the organic system plan, or its capability to comply, with the requirements of § 205.400(g)(8). This must include review of the internal inspections conducted by the internal control system. (ii) Conduct witness audits of internal control system inspectors performing inspections of the grower group operation. (iii) Individually inspect at least 1.4 times the square root of the total number of grower group members. This must include an inspection of all grower group members determined to be high risk according to criteria in 205.201(c)(4). At least one grower group member in each grower group production unit as defined in § 205.2 must be inspected. (iv) Inspect each handling facility.
units.actor: certifying agent conducting initial and annual on-site inspections of grower group operations
units.action_summary: Inspections of grower group operations must assess internal control system compliance, review internal inspections, conduct witness audits, inspect a statistical sample (at least 1.4×√N) including all high-risk members and at least one per production unit, and inspect each handling facility.

units.obligation_text: A certifying agent must, on an annual basis, conduct unannounced inspections of a minimum of five percent of the operations it certifies, rounded up to the nearest whole number.
units.action_summary: Certifying agents must annually conduct unannounced inspections of at least 5% of their certified operations (rounded up).

units.obligation_text: Certifying agents must be able to conduct unannounced inspections of any operation it certifies and must not accept applications or continue certification with operations located in areas where they are unable to conduct unannounced inspections.
units.action_summary: Certifying agents must be capable of conducting unannounced inspections of operations they certify and must not certify or continue certifying operations in areas where unannounced inspections cannot be performed.

units.obligation_text: That sufficient quantities of organic product and ingredients are produced or purchased to account for organic product sold or transported;
units.action_summary: Inspections must verify that sufficient organic product/ingredients are produced or purchased to account for organic product sold or transported.

units.obligation_text: That organic products and ingredients are traceable by the operation from the time of production or purchase to sale or transport; and that certifying agents can verify traceability back to the source per § 205.501(a)(21).
units.action_summary: Inspections must verify operations can trace organic products/ingredients from production/purchase to sale/transport and that certifiers can verify traceability back to source per §205.501(a)(21).

units.obligation_text: Continuously use a sufficient number of qualified and adequately trained personnel, including inspectors and persons who conduct certification review, to comply with and implement the USDA organic standards;
units.action_summary: Certifying agents must continuously employ sufficient qualified and trained personnel (inspectors and certification reviewers) to implement USDA organic standards.

units.obligation_text: Certifying agents must demonstrate that inspectors continuously maintain adequate knowledge and skills about the current USDA organic standards, production and handling practices, certification and inspection, import and/or export requirements, auditing practices and skills in written and oral communications, sample collection, investigation techniques, and preparation of technically accurate inspection documents;
units.action_summary: Certifying agents must demonstrate inspectors maintain up-to-date knowledge and skills across specified topics relevant to inspection and certification.

units.obligation_text: Initially and every year thereafter, inspectors must demonstrate successful completion of a minimum of 20 hours of training in topics that are relevant to inspection. Training may include material delivered via the NOP learning management system, certifying agents, or other relevant training provider;
units.action_summary: Inspectors must complete at least 20 hours of relevant training initially and annually thereafter.

units.obligation_text: Certifying agents must demonstrate that inspectors have a minimum of 1 year of field-based experience related to both the scope and scale of operations they will inspect before assigning inspection responsibilities;
units.action_summary: Certifying agents must ensure inspectors have at least one year of relevant field-based experience before assigning inspections.

units.obligation_text: Certifying agents must demonstrate that all persons who conduct certification review, including staff, volunteers, or contractors, have the knowledge, skills, and experience required to perform certification review of operations of the scope and scale assigned and to evaluate compliance with the applicable regulations of this part;
units.action_summary: Certifying agents must ensure certification reviewers have requisite knowledge, skills, and experience to perform reviews for operations assigned.

units.obligation_text: Initially and every year thereafter, all persons who conduct certification review activities must demonstrate successful completion of a minimum of 20 hours of training in topics that are relevant to certification review. Training may include material delivered via the NOP learning management system, certifying agents, or other relevant training provider;
units.action_summary: Certification review personnel must complete at least 20 hours of relevant training initially and annually thereafter.

units.obligation_text: Certifying agents must maintain current training requirements, training procedures, and training records for all inspectors and persons who conduct certification review activities.
units.action_summary: Certifying agents must maintain up-to-date training requirements, procedures, and records for inspectors and certification review personnel.

units.obligation_text: Demonstrate that all persons with inspection or certification review responsibilities have sufficient expertise in organic production or handling techniques to successfully perform the duties assigned; (i) Sufficient expertise must include knowledge of certification to USDA organic standards and evidence of formal education, training, or professional experience in the fields of agriculture, science, or organic production and handling that directly relates to assigned duties.
units.action_summary: Certifying agents must ensure and demonstrate that inspection/review personnel have sufficient expertise, including relevant education/training/experience.

units.obligation_text: Conduct an annual performance evaluation of all persons who conduct inspections, certification review, or implement measures to correct any deficiencies in certification services; (i) On-site evaluation of inspectors— Certifying agents must observe each inspector performing on-site inspections at least once every three years, or more frequently if warranted; and (A) On-site inspector evaluations must be performed by certifying agent personnel who are qualified to evaluate inspectors; (ii) Certifying agents must maintain documented policies, procedures, and records for annual performance evaluations and on-site inspector evaluations.
units.action_summary: Certifying agents must perform annual performance evaluations, observe each inspector on-site at least once every three years, ensure evaluations are conducted by qualified personnel, and maintain documented policies/procedures/records.

units.obligation_text: Maintain strict confidentiality with respect to its clients under the applicable organic certification program and not disclose to third parties (except for the Secretary or the applicable State organic programs’ governing State official or their authorized representatives) any business-related information concerning any client obtained while implementing the regulations in this part, except: (i) For information that must be made available to any member of the public, as provided for in § 205.504(b)(5); (ii) For enforcement purposes, certifying agents must exchange any compliance-related information that is credibly needed to certify, decertify, or investigate an operation, including for the purpose of verifying supply chain traceability and audit trail documentation; and (iii) If a certified operation’s proprietary business information is compliance-related and thus credibly needed to certify, decertify, or investigate that operation, certifying agents may exchange that information for the purposes of enforcing the Act, but the information in question still retains its proprietary character even after it is exchanged and all of the certifying agents that are involved in the exchange still have a duty to preserve the confidentiality of that information after the exchange.
units.action_summary: Certifying agents must maintain client confidentiality, except in specified public disclosure or enforcement-related circumstances where exchange of compliance-related information is permitted but confidentiality duties remain.

units.obligation_text: Accept the certification decisions made by another certifying agent accredited or accepted by USDA pursuant to § 205.500. Certifying agents must provide information to other certifying agents to ensure organic integrity or to enforce organic regulations, including to verify supply chain integrity, authenticate the organic status of certified products, and conduct investigations;
units.action_summary: Certifying agents must accept certification decisions by other USDA-accredited certifiers and must share information with other certifiers as necessary to ensure integrity and enforcement.

units.obligation_text: Maintain current and accurate data in INTEGRITY for each operation which it certifies;
units.action_summary: Certifying agents must keep current and accurate operation data in the INTEGRITY system for each operation they certify.

units.obligation_text: Annually, conduct risk-based supply chain audits to verify organic status of a product(s) of a certified operation(s) it certifies, back to the source(s).
units.action_summary: Certifying agents must annually conduct risk-based supply chain audits to verify organic product status back to the source.

units.obligation_text: Notify AMS not later than 90 calendar days after certification activities begin in a new certification office. The notification must include the countries where the certification activities are being provided, the nature of the certification activities, and the qualifications of the personnel providing the certification activities.
units.action_summary: Certifying agents must notify AMS within 90 days of beginning certification activities in a new office, providing specified details about countries, activities, and staff qualifications.

units.obligation_text: A copy of the procedures to be used for sharing information with other certifying agents and for maintaining the confidentiality of any business-related information as set forth in § 205.501(a)(10);
units.actor: applicant certifying agent (submitting evidence of expertise and ability)
units.action_summary: Applicants must submit procedures for sharing information with other certifying agents and for maintaining confidentiality as part of evidence of expertise.

units.obligation_text: A copy of the criteria to identify high-risk operations and products; and procedures to conduct risk-based supply chain audits, as required in § 205.501(a)(21); and procedures to report credible evidence of organic fraud to the Administrator.
units.actor: applicant certifying agent (submitting evidence of expertise and ability)
units.action_summary: Applicants must provide criteria for identifying high-risk operations/products, procedures for risk-based supply chain audits, and procedures to report credible organic fraud evidence to the Administrator.

units.obligation_text: Foreign product may be certified under the USDA organic regulations by a USDA-accredited certifying agent and imported for sale in the United States.
units.action_summary: Foreign products can be certified by USDA-accredited certifying agents and imported for sale in the U.S.

units.obligation_text: Countries desiring to establish eligibility of product certified under that country’s organic certification program to be sold, labeled or represented as organically produced in the United States may request an equivalence determination from AMS. A foreign government must maintain compliance and enforcement mechanisms to ensure that its organic certification program is fully meeting the terms and conditions of any equivalence determination provided by AMS pursuant to this section. To request this determination, the requesting country must submit documentation that fully describes its technical requirements and conformity assessment system.
units.action_summary: Countries may request an equivalence determination from AMS; foreign governments must maintain compliance and enforcement mechanisms and submit documentation describing technical requirements and conformity assessment system.

units.obligation_text: AMS will describe the scope of an equivalence determination. AMS will conduct reviews on a two-year cycle, beginning at the close of the prior review, to assess the effectiveness of the foreign government’s organic certification program. AMS will reassess a country’s organic certification program that AMS has recognized as equivalent every five years to verify that the foreign government’s technical requirements and conformity assessment program continue to be at least equivalent to the requirements of the Act and the regulations of this part, and will determine whether the equivalence determination should be continued.
units.action_summary: AMS will define equivalence scope, perform reviews every two years, and reassess recognized countries every five years to verify continued equivalence.

units.obligation_text: AMS may terminate an equivalence determination if the terms or conditions established under the determination are not met; if AMS determines that the country’s technical requirements and/or conformity assessment program are no longer equivalent; if AMS determines that the foreign government’s organic control system is inadequate to ensure that the country’s organic certification program is fully meeting the terms and conditions under the determination; or for other good cause.
units.action_summary: AMS has authority to terminate an equivalence determination for failure to meet terms, loss of equivalence, inadequate foreign control system, or other good cause.

units.obligation_text: The Program Manager may initiate enforcement action against any person who sells, labels, or provides other market information concerning an agricultural product if such label or information implies, directly or indirectly, that such product is produced or handled using organic methods, if the product was produced or handled in violation of the Organic Foods Production Act or the regulations in this part.
units.action_summary: Program Manager may initiate enforcement actions against persons who imply a product is organic when it was produced/handled in violation of the Act or regulations.

units.obligation_text: Within 3 business days of issuing a notification of suspension or revocation, or the effective date of an operation’s surrender, the certifying agent must update the operation’s status in INTEGRITY.
units.action_summary: Certifying agents must update an operation's status in INTEGRITY within 3 business days of issuing suspension/revocation notice or an operation's surrender effective date.

units.obligation_text: A certified operation or a person responsibly connected with an operation whose certification has been suspended may at any time, unless otherwise stated in the notification of suspension, submit a request to the Secretary for reinstatement of its certification, or submit a request for eligibility to be certified.
units.actor: certified operation or person responsibly connected with suspended operation
units.action_summary: Suspended operations or responsible persons may request reinstatement or eligibility to be certified, unless the suspension notice states otherwise.

units.obligation_text: Knowingly sells or labels a product as organic, except in accordance with the Act, shall be subject to a civil penalty of not more than the amount specified in § 3.91(b)(1)(xxxvii) of this title per violation.
units.actor: any person who knowingly sells or labels a product as organic except in accordance with the Act
units.action_summary: Persons who knowingly sell or label a product as organic contrary to the Act are subject to civil penalties up to the specified amount per violation.

units.obligation_text: A certifying agent must submit with its administrative policies and procedures provided in § 205.504(b): decision criteria for acceptance of mediation, and a process for identifying personnel conducting mediation and setting up mediation sessions.
units.action_summary: Certifying agents must include mediation acceptance criteria and processes for identifying mediators and arranging mediation in their administrative policies submitted under §205.504(b).

units.obligation_text: A certified operation or applicant for certification may request mediation to resolve a denial of certification or proposed suspension or proposed revocation of certification issued by a certifying agent or State organic program.
units.actor: certified operation or applicant for certification
units.action_summary: Certified operations or applicants may request mediation to resolve certification denial or proposed suspension/revocation.

title: Watermelon Research and Promotion Plan, Realignment

units.obligation_text: No State in a multi-State district shall have more than three producer and handler representatives concurrently on the Board.
units.actor: A State in a multi-State district
units.action_summary: A State in a multi-State district may not have more than three producer and handler representatives serving concurrently on the Board.

units.obligation_text: In multi-State districts, the convention chairperson will direct the eligible producer voters and handler voters from each State to caucus separately for the purpose of electing a State spokesperson for each group.
units.action_summary: The convention chairperson must direct eligible producer and handler voters from each State to caucus separately to elect a State spokesperson for each group.

units.obligation_text: Election of each State spokesperson shall be by simple majority of all individual voters in attendance.
units.actor: the election process / State spokesperson election
units.action_summary: Each State spokesperson must be elected by a simple majority of all individual voters in attendance.

units.obligation_text: In lieu of written ballots, a State spokesperson may be elected by voice vote or a show of hands.
units.actor: eligible producer and handler voters (electing a State spokesperson)
units.action_summary: Instead of written ballots, voters are permitted to elect a State spokesperson by voice vote or show of hands.

units.obligation_text: The role of the State spokesperson is to coordinate State voting and to cast all State votes.
units.action_summary: The State spokesperson must coordinate State voting and cast all State votes.

units.obligation_text: In accordance with § 1210.320(c) of the Plan, the districts shall be as follows:
units.actor: the Plan / the districts as established by the Plan
units.action_summary: The districts are required to be established as listed below.

units.obligation_text: District 1—The State of Florida.
units.action_summary: District 1 consists of the State of Florida.

units.obligation_text: District 2—The State of Georgia.
units.action_summary: District 2 consists of the State of Georgia.

units.obligation_text: District 3—The States of Alabama, Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi, North Carolina, Oklahoma, South Carolina, Tennessee, and Texas.
units.action_summary: District 3 consists of the listed States (Alabama, Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi, North Carolina, Oklahoma, South Carolina, Tennessee, and Texas).

units.obligation_text: District 4—The States of Connecticut, Delaware, Illinois, Indiana, Kentucky, Maryland, Massachusetts, Maine, Michigan, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, Vermont, Virginia, West Virginia, Wisconsin, and Washington, DC.
units.action_summary: District 4 consists of the listed States and Washington, DC.

units.obligation_text: District 5—The States of Alaska, Arizona, California, Colorado, Hawaii, Idaho, Iowa, Kansas, Minnesota, Missouri, Montana, Nebraska, Nevada, New Mexico, North Dakota, Oregon, South Dakota, Utah, Washington, and Wyoming.
units.action_summary: District 5 consists of the listed Western and Plains States.

units.obligation_text: The Board consists of 10 producers, 10 handlers, nine importers, and one public member appointed by the Secretary.
units.action_summary: The Board must be composed of 10 producers, 10 handlers, 9 importers, and one public member appointed by the Secretary.

title: Softwood Lumber Research, Promotion, Consumer Education and Industry Information Order: Assessment Rate Increase

units.obligation_text: Subject to the exemptions specified in § 1217.53, each manufacturer for the U.S. market shall pay an assessment to the Board at the rate of $0.41 per thousand board feet of softwood lumber
units.actor: each manufacturer for the U.S. market
units.action_summary: Pay an assessment to the Board at $0.41 per thousand board feet (subject to §1217.53 exemptions).

units.obligation_text: except that no person shall pay an assessment on the first 15 million board feet of softwood lumber otherwise subject to assessment in a fiscal year
units.action_summary: The first 15 million board feet of otherwise-assessable softwood lumber per fiscal year are exempt from assessment.

units.obligation_text: Domestic manufacturers shall pay assessments based on the volume of softwood lumber shipped within the United States
units.action_summary: Domestic manufacturers' assessments are calculated based on the volume shipped within the United States.

units.obligation_text: importers shall pay assessments based on the volume of softwood lumber imported to the United States
units.action_summary: Importers' assessments are calculated based on the volume of softwood lumber imported into the United States.

units.obligation_text: At least 24 months after the Order becomes effective and periodically thereafter, the Board shall review ... a change in the assessment rate
units.action_summary: The Board must review the assessment rate at least 24 months after the Order becomes effective and periodically thereafter.

units.obligation_text: the Board may recommend to the Secretary ... a change in the assessment rate
units.action_summary: The Board is permitted to recommend a change in the assessment rate to the Secretary.

units.obligation_text: upon an affirmative vote by at least a majority of Board members plus two (exclusive of vacant seats)
units.action_summary: A recommendation by the Board requires an affirmative vote of at least a majority of members plus two (excluding vacant seats).

units.obligation_text: In no event may the rate be less than $0.35 per thousand board feet nor more than $0.50 per thousand board feet
units.action_summary: The assessment rate cannot be set below $0.35 or above $0.50 per thousand board feet.

units.obligation_text: A change in the assessment rate is subject to rulemaking by the Secretary
units.action_summary: Any change to the assessment rate must be accomplished through rulemaking by the Secretary.

units.obligation_text: The assessment rates are computed using the following conversion factors: one cubic meter (m3) equals 0.423776001 thousand board feet, and one square meter (m2) equals 0.010763104 thousand board feet
units.action_summary: Conversion factors for computing assessment rates: 1 m3 = 0.423776001 MBF; 1 m2 = 0.010763104 MBF.

title: Exceptions to Geographic Boundaries

units.obligation_text: Under an exception, an official agency may provide service to a customer outside of their geographic area.
units.action_summary: Provide service to a customer outside their geographic area under an exception.

units.obligation_text: The applicant must request that the Service grant an exception.
units.action_summary: Request that the Service grant an exception.

units.obligation_text: As outlined below, the Service may grant an exceptions in instances when: The assigned official agency is unable to provide inspection services in a timely manner; a person requesting inspection services in that geographic area has not been receiving official inspection services from the official agency for that geographic area; a person requesting inspection services in that geographic area requests a probe inspection on a barge-lot basis; or, the assigned official agency for that geographic area agrees in writing with the adjacent official agency to waive the current geographic area restriction at the request of the applicant for service.
units.action_summary: Grant exceptions in specified instances (timely inability, nonuse, probe inspection on barge-lot basis, or written waiver by assigned agency).

units.obligation_text: The assigned official agency is unable to provide inspection services in a timely manner.
units.action_summary: Assigned agency cannot provide inspection services in a timely manner (grounds for exception).

units.obligation_text: A person requesting inspection services in that geographic area has not been receiving official inspection services from the official agency for that geographic area.
units.action_summary: Applicant has not received official inspection services from assigned agency (grounds for exception).

units.obligation_text: A person requesting inspection services in that geographic area requests a probe inspection on a barge-lot basis.
units.action_summary: Applicant requests a probe inspection on a barge-lot basis (grounds for exception).

units.obligation_text: The assigned official agency for that geographic area agrees in writing with the adjacent official agency to waive the current geographic area restriction at the request of the applicant for service.
units.action_summary: Assigned agency agrees in writing with adjacent agency to waive geographic restriction at applicant's request (grounds for exception).

units.obligation_text: The Service grants an exception when service is not timely as described in this section.
units.action_summary: Grant an exception when service is not timely according to the section's criteria.

units.obligation_text: Service is not timely when an official agency cannot provide requested official services within 6 hours or cannot provide results and certificate in accordance with 800.160(c).
units.action_summary: Defines 'not timely' as inability to provide services within 6 hours or to provide results and certificate per §800.160(c).

units.obligation_text: Applicants may also request timely service exceptions for delays caused by weather events or request a timely service exception for services that the assigned official agency does not offer.
units.action_summary: Applicants may request timely service exceptions for weather delays or for services the assigned agency does not offer.

units.obligation_text: The applicant must submit a request for a timely service exception to the Service.
units.action_summary: Submit a request for a timely service exception to the Service.

units.obligation_text: The applicant may make this request orally or in writing.
units.action_summary: Request may be made orally or in writing.

units.obligation_text: The applicant must clearly state and support the identified reason for the requested exception.
units.action_summary: Clearly state and support the reason for the requested exception.

units.obligation_text: There are three consecutive tiers of timely service exceptions: One-time, 90-day, and long-term. Applicants must progress through each tier.
units.action_summary: Applicants must progress through the one-time, then 90-day, then long-term tiers in order.

units.obligation_text: Applicants must apply for and the Service must approve a one-time exception before the Service considers a 90-day exception.
units.action_summary: Applicant must apply for a one-time exception and the Service must approve it before a 90-day exception will be considered.

units.obligation_text: Applicants must apply for and the Service must approve a 90-day exception before the Service will consider a long-term exception.
units.action_summary: Applicant must apply and Service must approve a 90-day exception before a long-term exception is considered.

units.obligation_text: The Service will review requests
units.action_summary: The Service will review exception requests.

units.obligation_text: The Service may contact the applicant, the assigned official agency, or potential gaining agency with questions during its review.
units.action_summary: Service may contact involved parties with questions during review.

units.obligation_text: The Service will provide its determination on the exception request to the customer in writing.
units.action_summary: Provide the exception determination in writing to the customer.

units.obligation_text: In the case of untimely service, the ability to use another official agency may be granted for the next service request, as applicable.
units.action_summary: The Service may grant the ability to use another official agency for the next service request in cases of untimely service.

units.obligation_text: If there is an occurrence of untimely service within 180 days of the date of the occurrence in paragraph (b)(1)(i) of this section, the applicant may request a 90-day exception.
units.action_summary: Applicant may request a 90-day exception if another untimely occurrence happens within 180 days of the one-time occurrence.

units.obligation_text: This 90-day window will begin the day the exception is granted.
units.action_summary: The 90-day period starts on the day the exception is granted.

units.obligation_text: If after a return to service following an exception granted under paragraph (b)(1)(ii) of this section there is another occurrence of untimely service within 365 days, the applicant may request a long-term exception.
units.action_summary: Applicant may request a long-term exception if another untimely occurrence happens within 365 days after return to service post-90-day exception.

units.obligation_text: When granting this exception, the Service may extend this exception up to the date of termination of the gaining agency’s designation term.
units.action_summary: Service may extend the long-term exception up to the gaining agency's designation termination date.

units.obligation_text: The applicant must submit a request for a timely service exception and associated supporting documentation to the Service.
units.action_summary: Submit a timely service exception request with supporting documentation to the Service.

units.obligation_text: The Service will give all parties an opportunity to provide information.
units.action_summary: Service will allow all parties to provide information related to the request.

units.obligation_text: The Service will request additional information if any is needed.
units.action_summary: Service will ask for additional information if necessary.

units.obligation_text: Prior to granting a timely service exception, the Service will review and validate all information submitted with the application.
units.action_summary: Service will review and validate all submitted information before granting a timely service exception.

units.obligation_text: If the request is urgent and made outside of the Service’s normal business hours, an official agency from outside the geographic area may provide service.
units.actor: an official agency from outside the geographic area
units.action_summary: An out-of-area official agency may provide service for urgent requests made outside Service business hours.

units.obligation_text: When providing an urgent service, the official agency must provide written notification to the Service within two business days after service.
units.actor: the official agency providing the urgent service
units.action_summary: Official agency must notify the Service in writing within two business days after providing urgent service.

units.obligation_text: The Service will review and validate the circumstances of the urgent request and the Service will verify that the request was not false or misleading.
units.action_summary: Service will review urgent request circumstances and verify they were not false or misleading.

units.obligation_text: If an applicant submits a request that the Service determines to be false or misleading, the Service will not grant the exception.
units.action_summary: Service will not grant exceptions based on requests it determines to be false or misleading.

units.obligation_text: If an urgent request was granted on the basis of a false and misleading request, the Service may deny the applicant from future urgent timely service exceptions for a period of up to 180 days.
units.action_summary: Service may deny the applicant future urgent timely service exceptions for up to 180 days if the prior urgent request was false or misleading.

units.obligation_text: The applicant maintains the option of returning to the assigned official agency at any time with a 60-day notification period to all parties.
units.action_summary: Applicant may return to the assigned official agency at any time by giving 60 days' notice to all parties.

units.obligation_text: The exception will be cancelled, and future exception requests will be considered at the beginning of successive-tiered system.
units.action_summary: When applicant returns, the exception will be cancelled and future requests will be treated starting at the first tier.

units.obligation_text: If the Service determines the original official agency’s inability to provide a specific service, limited due to weather events or service availability, has been resolved, the Service may terminate the long-term exception.
units.action_summary: Service may terminate a long-term exception when the original agency's inability to provide the service has been resolved.

units.obligation_text: If the exception was associated with the official agency’s inability to provide service in 6 hours or less, or timely issuance of the results and certificate, the Service may not terminate the exception.
units.action_summary: Service may not terminate a long-term exception if it was granted due to inability to provide service in 6 hours or to timely issue results and certificate.

units.obligation_text: If the Service terminates a long-term exception, all parties will be notified, and the applicant will resume service with the assigned official agency within 60 days of notification.
units.action_summary: If Service terminates a long-term exception, Service will notify all parties and the applicant will resume service with the assigned agency within 60 days.

units.obligation_text: If an applicant has not received service from the assigned official agency within the last 90 days, the applicant may request that the Service grant a nonuse of service exception.
units.action_summary: Applicant may request a nonuse of service exception if they haven't received service from assigned agency within last 90 days.

units.obligation_text: Requests must clearly state and support the following:
units.action_summary: Requests for nonuse exception must clearly state and support specified items.

units.obligation_text: The last date of service from assigned official agency;
units.action_summary: State the last date of service from the assigned official agency.

units.obligation_text: The reason service has not been received during this timeframe;
units.action_summary: State the reason service was not received during the specified timeframe.

units.obligation_text: The identified reason for the request.
units.action_summary: Provide the identified reason for requesting the nonuse exception.

units.obligation_text: Applicants may submit any relevant supporting information.
units.action_summary: Applicants may provide any relevant supporting information with their request.

units.obligation_text: The location of the specified service point(s);
units.action_summary: May submit the location of specified service points as supporting information.

units.obligation_text: The types of services requested by the applicant and offered by assigned official agency;
units.action_summary: May submit information on types of services requested and those offered by assigned agency.

units.obligation_text: The ability of the gaining official agency to take on additional customers;
units.action_summary: May include information about the gaining agency's ability to accept more customers.

units.obligation_text: The ability of the assigned official agency to provide the requested service;
units.action_summary: May include information on whether the assigned agency can provide the requested service.

units.obligation_text: Whether the requesting facility has ever used the official system.
units.action_summary: May submit whether the requesting facility has ever used the official system.

units.obligation_text: Included with the request for an exception, the applicant must submit supporting documentation to the Service.
units.action_summary: Applicant must include supporting documentation with the exception request to the Service.

units.obligation_text: After receipt of the request, the Service will give all parties an opportunity to provide additional supporting documentation.
units.action_summary: Service will allow all parties to provide additional supporting documentation after receiving the request.

units.obligation_text: The Service will request additional information if any is needed.
units.action_summary: Service will request further information if necessary.

units.obligation_text: Prior to granting an exception, the Service will review the application and all supporting documentation, and the Service will conduct any necessary analysis to estimate the exception’s impact.
units.action_summary: Service will review the application and documentation and conduct analyses before granting a nonuse exception.

units.obligation_text: The Service will notify the assigned official agency prior to granting an exception for nonuse of service.
units.action_summary: Service will notify the assigned official agency before granting a nonuse exception.

units.obligation_text: The assigned official agency may challenge a proposed exception for any reason.
units.action_summary: Assigned official agency may challenge a proposed nonuse exception.

units.obligation_text: To challenge a proposed exception, the assigned official agency must object in writing, and must submit supporting documents to the Service within 14 days after the date of notification.
units.action_summary: Assigned agency must object in writing and submit supporting documents within 14 days to challenge an exception.

units.obligation_text: Documents must clearly identify the objection and support the identified reason for the challenge.
units.action_summary: Submitted documents must clearly identify and support the objection.

units.obligation_text: The Service will consider impacts on the assigned official agency, the applicant, and the potential gaining agency when deciding whether to grant an exception.
units.action_summary: Service will consider impacts on relevant parties when deciding on granting the exception.

units.obligation_text: These impacts may include, but are not limited to, the viability of the assigned official agency given the loss of business.
units.action_summary: Service may consider impacts including the assigned agency's viability if it loses business.

units.obligation_text: The Service will also consider the impact on the integrity of the official system and confirm an exception would not undermine the congressional policies in section 2 of the United States Grain Standards Act.
units.action_summary: Service will consider system integrity and ensure exception won't undermine congressional policies in section 2 of the Act.

units.obligation_text: The Service will provide its decision in writing to the assigned official agency, the applicant, and the potential gaining agency.
units.action_summary: Service will provide written decision to assigned agency, applicant, and potential gaining agency.

units.obligation_text: If an applicant submits a request that the Service determines is false or misleading the Service may elect to limit them from submitting further requests for a period of up to 180 days.
units.action_summary: Service may limit an applicant from submitting further requests for up to 180 days if their request is false or misleading.

units.obligation_text: The nonuse of service exception is for the period of the gaining agency’s designation.
units.action_summary: The nonuse exception lasts for the gaining agency's designation period.

units.obligation_text: At the end of the designation, the Service will review the exception, and verify all criteria and information.
units.action_summary: Service will review and verify criteria and information at the end of the gaining agency's designation.

units.obligation_text: If the exception still meets the nonuse criteria, the Service will renew the exception for the new designation period.
units.action_summary: Service will renew the nonuse exception for the new designation period if criteria are still met.

units.obligation_text: In the event the gaining agency is no longer designated, the exception would automatically terminate and the customer would return to the assigned official agency.
units.action_summary: If gaining agency is no longer designated, exception terminates automatically and customer returns to assigned agency.

units.obligation_text: If all parties jointly agree to the termination of a nonuse of service exception, the Service will terminate the exception.
units.action_summary: Service will terminate the nonuse exception if all parties jointly agree to termination.

units.obligation_text: In this case, the assigned official agency must resume service within 60 days of notification.
units.action_summary: Assigned official agency must resume service within 60 days after notification of termination.

units.obligation_text: All nonuse of service exceptions, that were in place as of March 30, 2019, will be incorporated into geographic boundaries of the gaining agencies.
units.action_summary: Nonuse exceptions in place as of March 30, 2019, will be incorporated into the gaining agencies' geographic boundaries.
