units.obligation_text: The date the seller signed the agreement.
units.actor: the dealer (via the seller's written acknowledgement)
units.action_summary: The acknowledgement must include the date the seller signed the agreement.

units.obligation_text: The seller’s signature.
units.actor: the seller (as reflected in the written acknowledgement)
units.action_summary: The written acknowledgement must include the seller's signature.

units.obligation_text: The dealer retains the written acknowledgment, together with all other documents, if any, setting forth the terms of credit sales on which the purchaser and seller have agreed, and the dealer retains a copy thereof, in their records for such time as is required by any law, or by written notice served on the dealer by the Administrator, but not less than two calendar years from the date of expiration of the written agreement referred to in the acknowledgment.
units.action_summary: Dealer must retain the written acknowledgement and related documents in records for the time required by law or Administrator notice, but at least two years after the agreement's expiration.

units.obligation_text: Retain records for not less than two calendar years from the date of expiration of the written agreement referred to in the acknowledgment.
units.action_summary: Minimum statutory retention period: dealer must keep records at least two calendar years after agreement expiration.

units.obligation_text: The dealer provides a copy of the acknowledgment to the seller.
units.action_summary: Dealer must give the seller a copy of the written acknowledgement.

units.obligation_text: Purchasing livestock for which payment is to be made by a draft which is not a check shall constitute purchasing such livestock on credit within the meaning of paragraphs (a) and (b) of this section.
units.actor: a purchaser (person making such a purchase)
units.action_summary: A purchase paid by a draft that is not a check is treated as a purchase on credit for purposes of this section.

units.obligation_text: Within the times specified under sections 206(b), 207(d), and 318(b) of the Act, any livestock seller, live poultry seller or grower, to preserve their interest in the statutory trust, must give written notice to the appropriate packer, live poultry dealer, or livestock dealer and file such notice with the Secretary within the prescribed time by letter, fax, email, or other electronic transmission.
units.actor: any livestock seller, live poultry seller or grower
units.action_summary: Sellers/growers must give written notice to the appropriate packer/dealer and file that notice with the Secretary within the statutory timeframes and by permitted transmission methods to preserve trust interest.

units.obligation_text: Within the times specified under sections 206(b), 207(d), and 318(b) of the Act
units.action_summary: Time requirement: notices must be given within the times specified in the referenced statutory sections.

units.obligation_text: The written notice should provide:
units.actor: the livestock seller, live poultry seller, or grower
units.action_summary: Recommended content for the written notice that sellers/growers should include when providing notice to preserve trust benefits.

units.obligation_text: Notification to preserve trust benefits:
units.actor: the livestock seller, live poultry seller, or grower
units.action_summary: Notice should state that it is to preserve trust benefits.

units.obligation_text: Identification of packer, live poultry dealer, or livestock dealer;
units.actor: the livestock seller, live poultry seller, or grower
units.action_summary: Notice should identify the packer or dealer involved.

units.obligation_text: Identification of seller or poultry grower;
units.actor: the livestock seller, live poultry seller, or grower
units.action_summary: Notice should identify the seller or grower making the claim.

units.obligation_text: Date of the transaction;
units.actor: the livestock seller, live poultry seller, or grower
units.action_summary: Notice should include the transaction date.

units.obligation_text: Date of seller’s or poultry grower’s receipt of notice that payment instrument has been dishonored (if applicable);
units.actor: the livestock seller, live poultry seller, or grower
units.action_summary: If applicable, notice should state the date the seller/grower received notice of dishonored payment.

units.obligation_text: Amount of money due; and to make certain that a copy of such letter, fax, email, or other electronic transmission is filed with a PSD regional office or with the PSD headquarters office within the prescribed time.
units.actor: the livestock seller, live poultry seller, or grower
units.action_summary: Notice should state the amount due and the sender must ensure a copy of the notice is filed with a PSD regional or headquarters office within the prescribed time.

units.obligation_text: While the information in paragraphs (a)(1) through (6) of this section is desirable, any written notice which informs the packer, live poultry dealer, or livestock dealer, and the Secretary that the packer, live poultry dealer, or livestock dealer has failed to pay is sufficient to meet the statutory requirement in paragraph (a) of this section if it is given within the prescribed time.
units.actor: the livestock seller, live poultry seller, or grower
units.action_summary: Exception/alternative: a notice that informs the packer/dealer and the Secretary that payment was not made is sufficient to meet the statutory requirement if timely filed, even if it lacks the recommended details in (a)(1)-(6).

title: Transparency in Poultry Grower Contracting and Tournaments

units.obligation_text: Live Poultry Dealer Disclosure Document means the complete set of disclosures and statements that the live poultry dealer must provide to the poultry grower.
units.action_summary: Provide the complete set of disclosures and statements (the Disclosure Document) to the poultry grower.

units.obligation_text: A live poultry dealer must provide the documents described in this paragraph (a) to a prospective or current poultry grower.
units.action_summary: Provide the documents listed in paragraph (a) to prospective or current poultry growers.

units.obligation_text: Except as provided in paragraph (e) of this section, ... the live poultry dealer must provide the following documents at least seven days before the live poultry dealer executes the poultry growing arrangement: (i) A true, written copy of the renewed, revised, replacement, or new poultry growing arrangement;
units.action_summary: Provide a true, written copy of the poultry growing arrangement at least seven days before execution.

units.obligation_text: Except as provided in paragraph (e) of this section, ... the live poultry dealer must provide the following documents at least seven days before the live poultry dealer executes the poultry growing arrangement: (ii) The Live Poultry Dealer Disclosure Document, as described in paragraphs (b), (c), and (d) of this section.
units.action_summary: Provide the Live Poultry Dealer Disclosure Document at least seven days before executing the poultry growing arrangement.

units.obligation_text: When a live poultry dealer seeks to enter a poultry growing arrangement with a poultry grower or prospective poultry grower that will require an original capital investment, the live poultry dealer must provide the following to the poultry grower or prospective poultry grower simultaneously with the housing specifications:
units.action_summary: If original capital investment is required, provide specified documents simultaneously with housing specifications.

units.obligation_text: (a)(2)(i) A copy of the poultry growing arrangement that is affiliated with the current housing specifications,
units.action_summary: Provide a copy of the poultry growing arrangement affiliated with the current housing specifications.

units.obligation_text: (a)(2)(ii) The Live Poultry Dealer Disclosure Document, as described in paragraphs (b), (c), and (d) of this section, and
units.action_summary: Provide the Live Poultry Dealer Disclosure Document along with housing specifications.

units.obligation_text: (a)(2)(iii) A letter of intent that can be relied upon to obtain financing for the original capital investment.
units.action_summary: Provide a letter of intent suitable for obtaining financing for the original capital investment.

units.obligation_text: When a live poultry dealer seeks to offer or impose modifications to existing housing specifications that could reasonably require a poultry grower or prospective poultry grower to make an additional capital investment, the live poultry dealer must provide the following to the poultry grower or prospective poultry grower simultaneously with the modified housing specifications:
units.action_summary: If modified housing specifications could require additional capital investment, provide specified documents simultaneously with the modified specifications.

units.obligation_text: (a)(3)(i) A copy of the poultry growing arrangement that is affiliated with the modified housing specifications,
units.action_summary: Provide a copy of the poultry growing arrangement affiliated with the modified housing specifications.

units.obligation_text: (a)(3)(ii) The Live Poultry Dealer Disclosure Document, as described in paragraphs (b), (c), and (d) of this section, and
units.action_summary: Provide the Live Poultry Dealer Disclosure Document with the modified housing specifications.

units.obligation_text: (a)(3)(iii) A letter of intent that can be relied upon to obtain financing for the additional capital investment.
units.action_summary: Provide a letter of intent that can be used to obtain financing for the additional capital investment.

units.obligation_text: The Live Poultry Dealer Disclosure Document must include a cover page followed by additional disclosures as required in paragraphs (c) and (d) of this section. The order, form, and content of the cover page shall be and include:
units.action_summary: Ensure the Disclosure Document includes a cover page with specified order, form, and content followed by disclosures in (c) and (d).

units.obligation_text: (b)(1) The title 'LIVE POULTRY DEALER DISCLOSURE DOCUMENT' in capital letters and bold type;
units.action_summary: Include the specified title in capital letters and bold on the cover page.

units.obligation_text: (b)(2) The live poultry dealer’s name, type of business organization, principal business address, telephone number, email address, and, if applicable, primary internet web page address;
units.action_summary: Include contact and business identification information on the cover page.

units.obligation_text: (b)(3) The length of the term of the poultry growing arrangement;
units.action_summary: Include the term length of the poultry growing arrangement on the cover page.

units.obligation_text: (b)(4) The following statement: 'The income from your poultry farm may be significantly affected by the number of flocks the poultry company places on your farm each year, the density or number of birds placed with each flock, and the target weight at which poultry is caught. The poultry company may have full discretion and control over these and other factors. Please carefully review the information in this document.'
units.action_summary: Include specified cautionary statement about factors affecting farm income on the cover page.

units.obligation_text: (b)(5)(i) The minimum number of placements on the poultry grower’s farm annually under the terms of the poultry growing arrangement, and
units.action_summary: Disclose the minimum number of placements per year on the cover page.

units.obligation_text: (b)(5)(ii) The minimum stocking density for each flock to be placed on the poultry grower’s farm under the terms of the poultry growing arrangement.
units.action_summary: Disclose the minimum stocking density per flock on the cover page.

units.obligation_text: (b)(6) The applicable of the following two statements: (i) 'This disclosure document summarizes certain provisions of your poultry growing arrangement and other information. You have the right to read this disclosure document and all accompanying documents carefully. At least seven calendar days before the live poultry dealer executes the poultry growing arrangement, the poultry company is required to provide you with: (1) this disclosure document, and (2) a copy of the poultry growing arrangement.' OR (ii) 'This disclosure document summarizes certain provisions of your poultry growing arrangement and other information. You have the right to read this disclosure document and all accompanying documents carefully. The live poultry dealer is required to provide this disclosure document to you simultaneously with (a) a copy of the poultry growing arrangement, (b) any new or modified housing specifications that would require you to make an original or additional capital investment, and (c) a letter of intent.'
units.action_summary: Include one of the two specified statements on the cover page describing timing and accompanying documents the dealer must provide.

units.obligation_text: (b)(7) This statement: 'Even if the poultry growing arrangement contains a confidentiality provision, by law you still retain the right to discuss the terms of the poultry growing arrangement and the Live Poultry Dealer Disclosure Document with a Federal or State agency, your financial advisor or lender, your legal advisor, your accounting services representative, other growers for the same live poultry dealer, and your immediate family or business associates. A business associate is a person not employed by you, but with whom you have a valid business reason for consulting when entering into or operating under a poultry growing arrangement.'
units.action_summary: Include a statement on the cover page specifying the grower's right to discuss arrangement terms despite confidentiality provisions.

units.obligation_text: (b)(8) The following sentence in bold type: 'Note that USDA has not verified the information contained in this document. If this disclosure by the live poultry dealer contains any false or misleading statement or a material omission, a violation of federal and/or state law may have occurred.'
units.action_summary: Include the specified USDA disclaimer sentence in bold on the cover page.

units.obligation_text: The live poultry dealer shall disclose, in the Live Poultry Dealer Disclosure Document following the cover page, the following information:
units.action_summary: Disclose the listed information in the Disclosure Document after the cover page.

units.obligation_text: (c)(1) A summary of litigation over the prior six years between the live poultry dealer and any poultry grower; including the nature of the litigation, its location, the initiating party, a brief description of the controversy, and any resolution.
units.action_summary: Disclose a six-year summary of litigation involving the dealer and growers, with details.

units.obligation_text: (c)(2) A summary of all bankruptcy filings in the prior six years by the live poultry dealer and any parent, subsidiary, or related entity of the live poultry dealer;
units.action_summary: Disclose bankruptcy filings in the prior six years by the dealer and related entities.

units.obligation_text: (c)(3) A statement that describes the live poultry dealer’s policies and procedures regarding the potential sale of the poultry grower’s facility or assignment of the poultry growing arrangement to another party, including the circumstances under which the live poultry dealer will offer the successive buyer a poultry growing agreement.
units.action_summary: Describe policies/procedures regarding potential sale or assignment of grower facility/arrangement and conditions for offering agreement to buyer.

units.obligation_text: The live poultry dealer must include in the Live Poultry Dealer Disclosure Document the following information:
units.action_summary: Include the specified financial and cost-related information in the Disclosure Document.

units.obligation_text: (d)(1) A table showing average annual gross payments to poultry growers for the previous calendar year for all complexes owned or operated by the live poultry dealer, organized by housing specification, and expressing average payments on the basis of U.S. dollars per farm facility square foot.
units.action_summary: Provide a table of average annual gross payments per facility square foot for the previous year, organized by housing specification.

units.obligation_text: (d)(2) Tables showing average annual gross payments to poultry growers at the local complex for each of the five previous years. The tables should express average payments on the basis of U.S. dollars per farm facility square foot. The tables should be organized by year, housing specification tier (lowest to highest), and quintile (lowest to highest). The step-by-step process for calculating table values is:
units.action_summary: Provide five-year tables of average annual gross payments per facility square foot organized by year, housing specification tier, and quintile, calculated per specified process.

units.obligation_text: (d)(2)(i) Group growers according to the housing specification affiliated with their poultry growing arrangement;
units.action_summary: Group growers by the housing specification affiliated with their arrangement when computing table values.

units.obligation_text: (d)(2)(i)(A) Include all growers under contract for a complete calendar year and growers under flock-to-flock poultry growing arrangements during that year, and
units.action_summary: Include growers contracted for a full calendar year and flock-to-flock growers in the calculations.

units.obligation_text: (d)(2)(i)(B) Exclude growers whose housing specifications changed during the calendar year from the calculation for that year.
units.action_summary: Exclude growers whose housing specifications changed during the year from that year's calculations.

units.obligation_text: (d)(2)(ii) Sum all payments to each grower during the calendar year to determine each grower’s total annual payments;
units.action_summary: Sum all payments to each grower in the calendar year to get total annual payments.

units.obligation_text: (d)(2)(iii) Divide each grower’s total annual payments by the square footage of the grower’s farm facility to normalize annual payments to reflect dollars per farm facility square foot;
units.action_summary: Normalize each grower's annual payments by dividing by facility square footage to express dollars per square foot.

units.obligation_text: (d)(2)(iv) Sort normalized annual payments into quintiles (smallest to largest); and
units.action_summary: Sort normalized annual payments into quintiles from smallest to largest.

units.obligation_text: (d)(2)(v) Sum all normalized annual payments within each quintile and divide the result by the number of growers in the quintile to determine an average annual gross payment to poultry growers for that quintile.
units.action_summary: Compute average annual gross payment per quintile by summing normalized payments and dividing by number of growers in that quintile.

units.obligation_text: (d)(3) If poultry housing specifications for poultry growers under contract with the complex are modified such that an additional capital investment may be required, or if the five-year averages provided under paragraph (2) do not accurately represent projected grower gross annual payments under the terms of the applicable poultry growing arrangement for any reason, the live poultry dealer must provide the following additional information:
units.action_summary: If housing specs change or five-year averages are inaccurate, provide additional projected payment information and explanations.

units.obligation_text: (d)(3)(i) Tables providing projections of average annual gross payments to growers under contract with the complex with the same housing specifications for the term of the poultry growing arrangement at five quintile levels expressed as dollars per farm facility square foot, and
units.action_summary: Provide projection tables of average annual gross payments for five quintiles expressed as dollars per square foot.

units.obligation_text: (d)(3)(ii) An explanation of why the annual gross payment averages for the previous five years, as provided under (2), do not provide an accurate representation of projected future payments, including the basic assumptions underlying the projections provided under (i) of this paragraph.
units.action_summary: Provide an explanation and assumptions for why five-year averages are not accurate and for the provided projections.

units.obligation_text: (d)(4) A summary of information the live poultry dealer collects or maintains relating to grower variable costs inherent in poultry production.
units.action_summary: Summarize information collected/maintained about grower variable costs.

units.obligation_text: (d)(5) Current contact information for the State university extension service office or the county farm advisor’s office that can provide relevant information about poultry grower costs and poultry farm financial management in the poultry grower’s geographic area.
units.action_summary: Provide current contact information for local extension or county farm advisor offices for grower cost/financial information.

units.obligation_text: A live poultry dealer, including all parent and subsidiary companies, slaughtering fewer than 2 million live pounds of poultry weekly (104 million pounds annually) is exempt from the requirements in paragraph (a)(1) of this section.
units.actor: a live poultry dealer (and parent/subsidiaries) slaughtering fewer than 2 million live pounds weekly
units.action_summary: Dealers under the specified processing threshold are exempt from paragraph (a)(1) requirements.

units.obligation_text: (f)(1) The live poultry dealer must establish, maintain, and enforce a governance framework that is reasonably designed to—
units.action_summary: Establish, maintain, and enforce a governance framework designed to accomplish specified objectives.

units.obligation_text: (f)(1)(i) audit the accuracy and completeness of the disclosures required under (a), which shall include audits and testing, and which shall include reviews of an appropriate sampling of Live Poultry Dealer Disclosure Documents by the principal executive officer or officers;
units.actor: the live poultry dealer (including principal executive officer reviews)
units.action_summary: Conduct audits and testing to verify accuracy/completeness of disclosures and include CEO/principal officer review of a sample of Disclosure Documents.

units.obligation_text: (f)(1)(ii) ensure compliance with all obligations under the Packers and Stockyards Act and regulations thereunder.
units.action_summary: Ensure compliance with all obligations under the Packers and Stockyards Act and its regulations.

units.obligation_text: (f)(2) The principal executive officer or officers, or persons performing similar functions, shall certify in the Live Poultry Dealer Disclosure Document that the live poultry dealer has established, maintains, and enforces the governance framework and that based on the officer’s knowledge, the Live Poultry Dealer Disclosure Document does not contain any untrue statement of a material fact or omit to state a material fact which would render it misleading.
units.actor: the principal executive officer(s) or persons performing similar functions
units.action_summary: Certify in the Disclosure Document that the governance framework exists/is enforced and that, to officer knowledge, the document contains no material untrue statements or omissions.

units.obligation_text: (g)(1) The Live Poultry Dealer Disclosure Document must include a poultry grower’s signature page that contains the following statement: 'If the live poultry dealer does not deliver this disclosure document within the time frame specified herein, or if this disclosure document contains any false or misleading statement or a material omission (including any discrepancy with other oral or written statements made in connection with the poultry growing arrangement), a violation of federal and state law may have occurred. Violations of federal and state laws may be determined to be unfair, unjustly discriminatory, or deceptive and unlawful under the Packers and Stockyards Act, as amended. Allegations of such violations may be reported to the Packers and Stockyards Division of USDA’s Agricultural Marketing Service.'
units.action_summary: Include a signature page in the Disclosure Document containing the specified statement notifying growers of possible violations and reporting avenues.

units.obligation_text: (g)(2) The live poultry dealer must obtain the poultry grower’s or prospective poultry grower’s dated signature on the poultry grower’s signature page in paragraph (1) as evidence of receipt.
units.action_summary: Obtain the grower’s dated signature on the signature page as evidence of receipt.

units.obligation_text: The live poultry dealer must provide a copy of the dated signature page to the poultry grower or prospective poultry grower
units.action_summary: Provide the grower with a copy of the dated signature page.

units.obligation_text: The live poultry dealer must retain a copy of the dated signature page in the dealer’s records for three years following expiration, termination, or non-renewal of the poultry growing arrangement.
units.action_summary: Retain a copy of the dated signature page for three years after contract expiration, termination, or non-renewal.

units.obligation_text: A live poultry dealer, notwithstanding any confidentiality provision in the poultry growing arrangement, may not prohibit a poultry grower or prospective poultry grower from discussing the terms of a poultry growing arrangement offer or the accompanying Live Poultry Dealer Disclosure Document with: [list of persons].
units.action_summary: Do not prohibit growers from discussing arrangement terms or the Disclosure Document with specified persons despite confidentiality provisions.

units.obligation_text: (i)(2) The following variables controlled by the live poultry dealer: (i) The minimum number of placements of poultry at the poultry grower’s facility annually, and (ii) The minimum stocking density for each flock placed with the poultry grower under the poultry growing arrangement.
units.actor: the live poultry dealer (regarding items growers may discuss)
units.action_summary: Specify that the dealer controls the minimum number of placements and minimum stocking density — these are variables growers are permitted to discuss.

units.obligation_text: If a live poultry dealer uses a poultry grower ranking system to calculate grower payments, the live poultry dealer must produce records in accordance with paragraphs (b) and (c) of this section.
units.action_summary: If using a grower ranking system for payments, produce records as required in paragraphs (b) and (c).

units.obligation_text: The live poultry dealer must maintain such records for a period of five years.
units.action_summary: Maintain the ranking-system records for five years.

units.obligation_text: Within 24 hours of flock delivery to a poultry grower’s facility, a live poultry dealer must provide the following information to the grower regarding the placement:
units.action_summary: Within 24 hours of delivery, provide specified placement information to the grower.

units.obligation_text: (b)(1) The stocking density of the placement;
units.action_summary: Provide the stocking density for the placement within 24 hours of delivery.

units.obligation_text: (b)(2) Names and all ratios of breeds of the poultry delivered;
units.action_summary: Provide names and breed ratios of the delivered poultry within 24 hours.

units.obligation_text: (b)(3) If the live poultry dealer has determined the sex of the birds, all ratios of male and female poultry delivered;
units.action_summary: If sex has been determined, provide the male/female ratios of delivered birds within 24 hours.

units.obligation_text: (b)(4) The breeder facility identifier;
units.action_summary: Provide the breeder facility identifier within 24 hours of placement.

units.obligation_text: (b)(5) The breeder flock age;
units.action_summary: Provide the breeder flock age within 24 hours of placement.

units.obligation_text: (b)(6) Information regarding any known health impairments of the breeder flock or of the poultry delivered; and
units.action_summary: Provide information about any known health impairments of the breeder flock or delivered poultry within 24 hours.

units.obligation_text: (b)(7) Adjustments, if any, that the live poultry dealer may make to the calculation of the grower’s pay based on the inputs in (1) through (6) of this paragraph.
units.action_summary: Disclose any adjustments that may be made to grower pay calculations based on the provided placement inputs within 24 hours.

units.obligation_text: A live poultry dealer must provide ranking system settlement documents that include the following information:
units.action_summary: Provide settlement documents for ranking-system payments that include specified information.

units.obligation_text: (c)(1) Grouping, ranking, or comparison sheets. The live poultry dealer must furnish the poultry grower, at the time of settlement, a copy of a grouping or ranking sheet that shows the grower’s precise position in the grouping, ranking, or comparison sheet for that period. The grouping or ranking sheet need not show the names of other growers, but must show their housing specification and the actual figures upon which the grouping or ranking is based for each grower grouped or ranked during the specified period.
units.action_summary: At settlement, furnish the grower a grouping/ranking sheet showing the grower's precise position, housing specification for other growers, and the figures used in ranking.

units.obligation_text: The grouping or ranking sheet need not show the names of other growers, but must show their housing specification and the actual figures upon which the grouping or ranking is based for each grower grouped or ranked during the specified period.
units.action_summary: Ensure grouping/ranking sheets show housing specifications and the numerical figures underlying rankings for each grower (names not required).

units.obligation_text: (c)(2) Distribution of inputs. The distribution of inputs among participants must be reported to all poultry grower ranking system participants. The grouping or ranking sheets required in paragraph (1) must disclose the following information relating to live poultry dealer-controlled inputs provided to each grower participant:
units.action_summary: Report distribution of dealer-controlled inputs to all ranking system participants; ensure grouping/ranking sheets disclose specified input information for each participant.

units.obligation_text: (c)(2)(i) The stocking density for each placement;
units.action_summary: Disclose stocking density for each placement to ranking system participants.

units.obligation_text: (c)(2)(ii) The names and all ratios of breeds of the poultry delivered to each poultry grower’s facility;
units.action_summary: Disclose breed names and ratios delivered to each grower's facility.

units.obligation_text: (c)(2)(iii) If the live poultry dealer has determined the sex of the birds, all ratios of male and female poultry delivered to each poultry grower’s facility;
units.action_summary: If sex is determined, disclose male/female ratios delivered to each grower's facility.

units.obligation_text: (c)(2)(iv) All breeder facility identifiers;
units.action_summary: Disclose all breeder facility identifiers for poultry delivered to each grower.

units.obligation_text: (c)(2)(v) The breeder flock age(s); and
units.action_summary: Disclose breeder flock age(s) for birds delivered to each grower.

units.obligation_text: (c)(2)(vi) The number of feed disruptions each poultry grower endured during the growout period, where the grower was completely out of feed for 12 hours or more.
units.action_summary: Disclose number of feed disruptions (out of feed for 12+ hours) each grower experienced during the growout period.

title: Transparency in Poultry Grower Contracting and Tournaments

units.obligation_text: The comment period for the proposed rule published on June 8, 2022 (at 87 FR 34980) is extended.
units.action_summary: AMS extends the public comment period for the proposed rule published June 8, 2022.

units.obligation_text: We will consider all comments received on or before August 23, 2022.
units.action_summary: AMS will consider comments that are received by August 23, 2022.

units.obligation_text: Comments must be submitted on or before August 23, 2022.
units.action_summary: Interested persons must submit comments by August 23, 2022.

title: National Organic Program: National List of Allowed and Prohibited Substances per October 2020 and April 2021 National Organic Standards Board Recommendations (Handling, Crop)

units.obligation_text: Paper-based crop planting aid. A material that is comprised of at least 60% cellulose-based fiber by weight, including, but not limited to, pots, seed tape, and collars that are placed in or on the soil and later incorporated into the soil, excluding biodegradable mulch film.
units.action_summary: The material must be made of at least 60% cellulose-based fiber by weight and be suited to placement in or on the soil and later incorporation into the soil (excluding biodegradable mulch film).

units.obligation_text: Up to 40% of the ingredients can be nonsynthetic, other permitted synthetic ingredients at § 205.601(j), or synthetic strengthening fibers, adhesives, or resins.
units.actor: paper-based crop planting aid (the material) / its ingredients
units.action_summary: Up to 40% of the material's ingredients may be nonsynthetic or certain permitted synthetics or synthetic strengthening components.

units.obligation_text: Contains no less than 80% biobased content as verified by a qualified third-party assessment (e.g., laboratory test using ASTM D6866 or composition review by qualified personnel).
units.actor: paper-based crop planting aid (the material) / its producer or supplier
units.action_summary: The material must contain at least 80% biobased content, verified by a qualified third-party assessment or equivalent review.

units.obligation_text: Added nutrients must comply with §§ 205.105, 205.203, and 205.206.
units.actor: added nutrients / suppliers or producers adding nutrients
units.action_summary: Any nutrients added to the material must comply with the referenced regulatory sections.

units.obligation_text: Microcrystalline cheesewax (CAS #'s 64742–42–3, 8009–03–08, and 8002–74–2)—for use in log grown mushroom production.
units.action_summary: Microcrystalline cheesewax is allowed for use in log-grown mushroom production.

units.obligation_text: Must be made without either ethylene-propylene co-polymer or synthetic colors.
units.actor: microcrystalline cheesewax used in log grown mushroom production / its manufacturer
units.action_summary: The cheesewax used for log-grown mushroom production must not contain ethylene-propylene co-polymer or synthetic colors.

units.obligation_text: Paper-based crop planting aids as defined in § 205.2.
units.action_summary: Paper-based crop planting aids (as defined) are allowed for use as production aids in organic crop production.

units.obligation_text: Virgin or recycled paper without glossy paper or colored inks.
units.actor: paper used in paper-based crop planting aids / manufacturers
units.action_summary: The paper used must be virgin or recycled and must not be glossy paper or contain colored inks.

units.obligation_text: Waxes—nonsynthetic (Wood rosin).
units.action_summary: Nonsynthetic waxes (wood rosin) are allowed as nonagricultural ingredients in processed products labeled as 'organic' or 'made with organic.'

units.obligation_text: Low-acyl gellan gum.

title: United States Standards for Soybeans

units.obligation_text: TABLE 17 TO PARAGRAPH (c)(2)—GRADE LIMITS (GL) AND BREAKPOINTS (BP) FOR SOYBEANS
units.action_summary: Soybeans must meet the grade limits and breakpoints in Table 17 to be assigned grades U.S. No. 1 through U.S. No. 4.

units.obligation_text: U.S. No. 1 — Maximum limits: Damaged kernels (Heat (part of total)) 0.2; Damaged kernels (Total) 2.0; Foreign material 1.0; Splits 10.0; Total 0.2 (GL/BP values as listed).
units.action_summary: To be graded U.S. No. 1, soybeans must not exceed the specified maximum percentages for damaged kernels (heat and total), foreign material, splits, and total.

units.obligation_text: U.S. No. 2 — Maximum limits: Damaged kernels (Heat (part of total)) 0.5; Damaged kernels (Total) 3.0; Foreign material 2.0; Splits 20.0; Total 0.3 (GL/BP values as listed).
units.action_summary: To be graded U.S. No. 2, soybeans must not exceed the specified maximum percentages for damaged kernels (heat and total), foreign material, splits, and total.

units.obligation_text: U.S. No. 3 — Maximum limits: Damaged kernels (Heat (part of total)) 1.0; Damaged kernels (Total) 5.0; Foreign material 3.0; Splits 30.0; Total 0.5 (GL/BP values as listed).
units.action_summary: To be graded U.S. No. 3, soybeans must not exceed the specified maximum percentages for damaged kernels (heat and total), foreign material, splits, and total.

units.obligation_text: U.S. No. 4 — Maximum limits: Damaged kernels (Heat (part of total)) 3.0; Damaged kernels (Total) 8.0; Foreign material 5.0; Splits 40.0; Total 0.9 (GL/BP values as listed).
units.action_summary: To be graded U.S. No. 4, soybeans must not exceed the specified maximum percentages for damaged kernels (heat and total), foreign material, splits, and total.

units.obligation_text: Soybeans which are purple mottled or stained shall be graded not higher than U.S. No. 3.
units.action_summary: Soybeans that are purple mottled or stained must not be graded above U.S. No. 3.

units.obligation_text: Soybeans which are materially weathered shall be graded not higher than U.S. No. 4.
units.action_summary: Soybeans that are materially weathered must not be graded above U.S. No. 4.

units.obligation_text: Yellow soybeans... may include not more than 10.0 percent of soybeans of other colors.
units.action_summary: A lot classified as yellow soybeans is permitted to contain up to 10.0 percent soybeans of other colors.

units.obligation_text: The hilum of a soybean is not considered a part of the seed coat for this determination.
units.action_summary: When determining seed coat color for classification (e.g., yellow soybeans), the hilum must be excluded from consideration as part of the seed coat.

units.obligation_text: Each determination of class, heat-damaged kernels, damaged kernels, and splits is made on the basis of the grain when free from foreign material.
units.action_summary: Determinations of class, heat-damaged kernels, damaged kernels, and splits must be made based on grain that is free from foreign material.

units.obligation_text: Other determinations not specifically provided for under the general provisions are made on the basis of the grain as a whole.
units.action_summary: For determinations not specified under general provisions, graders must make those determinations based on the grain as a whole.

units.obligation_text: Grades and grade requirements for soybeans: Maximum percent limits and maximum count limits as listed for Grades U.S. Nos. 1–4.
units.action_summary: Soybeans must meet the listed maximum percent and count limits to qualify for Grades U.S. Nos. 1–4.

units.obligation_text: U.S. No. 1 — Maximum percent limits: Heat (part of total) 0.2; Total damaged kernels 2.0; Foreign material 1.0; Splits 10.0.
units.action_summary: To be graded U.S. No. 1, soybeans must not exceed these maximum percentages for heat-damaged kernels (part of total), total damaged kernels, foreign material, and splits.

units.obligation_text: U.S. No. 2 — Maximum percent limits: Heat (part of total) 0.5; Total damaged kernels 3.0; Foreign material 2.0; Splits 20.0.
units.action_summary: To be graded U.S. No. 2, soybeans must not exceed these maximum percentages for heat-damaged kernels (part of total), total damaged kernels, foreign material, and splits.

units.obligation_text: U.S. No. 3 — Maximum percent limits: Heat (part of total) 1.0; Total damaged kernels 5.0; Foreign material 3.0; Splits 30.0.
units.action_summary: To be graded U.S. No. 3, soybeans must not exceed these maximum percentages for heat-damaged kernels (part of total), total damaged kernels, foreign material, and splits.

units.obligation_text: U.S. No. 4 — Maximum percent limits: Heat (part of total) 3.0; Total damaged kernels 8.0; Foreign material 5.0; Splits 40.0.
units.action_summary: To be graded U.S. No. 4, soybeans must not exceed these maximum percentages for heat-damaged kernels (part of total), total damaged kernels, foreign material, and splits.

units.obligation_text: Maximum count limits of other materials: Animal filth 9; Castor beans 1; Crotalaria seeds 2; Glass 0; Stones 3; Unknown foreign substance 3; Total 10.
units.action_summary: To qualify for Grades U.S. Nos. 1–4, a sample must not exceed the listed maximum counts for specified other materials and the total count limit.

units.obligation_text: U.S. Sample grade are soybeans that: (a) Do not meet the requirements for U.S. Nos. 1, 2, 3, or 4; or (b) Have a musty, sour, or commercially objectionable foreign odor (except garlic odor); or (c) Are heating or otherwise of distinctly low quality.
units.action_summary: Soybeans are classified as U.S. Sample grade if they fail to meet U.S. Nos. 1–4 requirements, have certain objectionable odors, or are heating/low quality.

units.obligation_text: In addition to the maximum count limit, stones must exceed 0.1 percent of the sample weight.
units.action_summary: Stones are counted against the maximum count limit only if their weight exceeds 0.1 percent of the sample weight.

units.obligation_text: Includes any combination of animal filth, castor beans, crotalaria seeds, glass, stones, and unknown foreign substances. The weight of stones is not applicable for total other material.
units.action_summary: The total other material count may include any combination of the listed items, and when calculating total other material the weight of stones is not used.

Plant Pest Regulations

units.obligation_text: No person shall import, move interstate, transit, or release into the environment plant pests, biological control organisms, or associated articles, unless the importation, interstate movement, transit, or release into the environment of the plant pests, biological control organisms, or associated articles is: [authorized under an import, interstate movement, or continued curation permit issued in accordance with proposed § 330.201; authorized in accordance with other APHIS regulations in 7 CFR chapter III; explicitly granted an exception or exemption in the revised subpart from permitting requirements; authorized under a general permit issued by the Administrator].
units.action_summary: Persons are prohibited from importing, moving interstate, transiting through, or releasing into the environment plant pests, biological control organisms, or associated articles unless one of the listed authorizations or exceptions applies.

units.obligation_text: Authorized under an import, interstate movement, or continued curation permit issued in accordance with proposed § 330.201.
units.actor: persons seeking to import/move/transit/release regulated organisms or articles
units.action_summary: Importation/interstate movement/transit/release is permitted if authorized by an appropriate permit issued under § 330.201.

units.obligation_text: Authorized in accordance with other APHIS regulations in 7 CFR chapter III.
units.actor: persons seeking to import/move/transit/release regulated organisms or articles
units.action_summary: Importation/interstate movement/transit/release is permitted if authorized under other APHIS regulations in 7 CFR chapter III.

units.obligation_text: Explicitly granted an exception or exemption in the revised subpart from permitting requirements.
units.actor: persons seeking to import/move/transit/release regulated organisms or articles
units.action_summary: Importation/interstate movement/transit/release is permitted if an explicit exception or exemption in the subpart applies.

units.obligation_text: Authorized under a general permit issued by the Administrator.
units.actor: persons seeking to import/move/transit/release regulated organisms or articles
units.action_summary: Importation/interstate movement/transit/release is permitted if it is authorized under a general permit issued by the Administrator.

units.obligation_text: Pursuant to section 7711 of the PPA, the Administrator may also issue general permits, that is, general authorizations, for the importation or interstate movement of plant pests.
units.action_summary: The Administrator has authority to issue general permits authorizing importation or interstate movement of plant pests.

units.obligation_text: Other types of biological control organisms could be regulated under the revised subpart, as determined by APHIS. This determination would typically be on a case-by-case basis, and would be based on a permit application for movement of an organism which did not belong to any of the above types, but for which the Administrator determined it necessary to exercise a degree of regulatory oversight in order to prevent the introduction of a plant pest into the United States or the dissemination of a plant pest within the United States.
units.action_summary: APHIS may determine on a case-by-case basis to regulate other types of biological control organisms based on permit applications and risk concerns.

units.obligation_text: Paragraph (d) would exempt biological control organism products that EPA has issued experimental use permits for or that EPA has registered as microbial pesticide products having outdoor uses from regulatory oversight under the revised subpart.
units.actor: biological control organism products subject to EPA EUPs or EPA registration
units.action_summary: Biological control organism products authorized by EPA (EUPs or registered microbial pesticides with outdoor uses) are exempt from APHIS regulatory oversight under the revised subpart.

units.obligation_text: Paragraph (d) would ... allow for the importation and interstate movement of such unregistered pesticides without APHIS' oversight, because of EPA's oversight.
units.actor: persons importing or moving such unregistered pesticides
units.action_summary: Persons may import and interstate move certain EPA-regulated (including some unregistered) microbial pesticide products without APHIS oversight due to EPA oversight.

units.obligation_text: We issue import permits, interstate movement permits, continued curation permits, and transit permits.
units.action_summary: APHIS issues the listed types of permits for regulated movements and activities.

units.obligation_text: When import permits are issued to individuals, these individuals must be 18 years of age or older and have a physical address within the United States.
units.action_summary: Individuals issued import permits must be 18+ and have a U.S. physical address.

units.obligation_text: When import permits are issued to corporate persons, these persons must maintain an address or business office in the United States with a designated individual for service of process.
units.action_summary: Corporate permittees must maintain a U.S. address/business office and designate an individual for service of process.

units.obligation_text: When interstate movement permits are issued to individuals, these individuals must be 18 years of age or older and have a physical address within the United States.
units.actor: individual applicants for interstate movement permits
units.action_summary: Individuals issued interstate movement permits must be 18+ and have a U.S. physical address.

units.obligation_text: When interstate movement permits are issued to corporate persons, these persons must maintain an address or business office in the United States with a designated individual for service of process.
units.actor: corporate applicants for interstate movement permits
units.action_summary: Corporate interstate permittees must maintain a U.S. address/business office and designate an individual for service of process.

units.obligation_text: When continued curation permits are issued to individuals, these individuals must be 18 years of age or older and have a physical address within the United States.
units.actor: individual applicants for continued curation permits
units.action_summary: Individuals issued continued curation permits must be 18+ and have a U.S. physical address.

units.obligation_text: When continued curation permits are issued to corporate persons, these persons must maintain an address or business office in the United States with a designated individual for service of process.
units.actor: corporate applicants for continued curation permits
units.action_summary: Corporate continued curation permittees must maintain a U.S. address/business office and designate an individual for service of process.

units.obligation_text: Permit applications must be submitted by the applicant in writing or electronically through one of the methods specified at http://www.aphis.usda.gov/plant_health/permits/index.shtml, and must be submitted in advance of the action(s) proposed on the permit application.
units.action_summary: Applicants must submit permit applications in writing or electronically via specified methods and must submit them in advance of the proposed actions.

units.obligation_text: A permit application must be complete before we will evaluate it in order to determine whether to issue the permit requested.
units.action_summary: Applicants must submit complete permit applications for APHIS to evaluate them.

units.obligation_text: An application should be submitted at least 90 days before the actions proposed on the permit application are scheduled to take place, with additional time allotted for complex or novel applications, or applications for high-risk plant pests.
units.action_summary: Applicants are advised to submit applications at least 90 days in advance (more time for complex or high-risk applications).

units.obligation_text: APHIS reviews the information on the application to determine whether it is complete. In order to consider an application complete, APHIS may request additional information that we determine to be necessary in order to assess the risk to plants and plant products that may be posed by the actions proposed on the application. When it is determined that an application is complete, we commence review of the information provided. We share a copy of the permit application, and the proposed permit conditions, with the appropriate State or Tribal regulatory officials, and may share them with other persons or groups to provide comment.
units.action_summary: APHIS may request additional information to determine completeness and may share applications and proposed conditions with State/Tribal officials or others for comment.

units.obligation_text: All facilities would have to be determined by APHIS to be constructed and maintained in a manner that prevents the dissemination or dispersal of plant pests, biological control organisms, or associated articles from the facility.
units.action_summary: Facilities holding regulated organisms or articles must be constructed and maintained to prevent dissemination or dispersal of those organisms/articles.

units.obligation_text: The applicant would have to provide all information requested by APHIS regarding this assessment, and to allow all inspections requested by APHIS during normal business hours (8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday through Friday, excluding holidays).
units.action_summary: Applicants/permittees must provide requested facility/site assessment information and allow APHIS inspections during normal business hours.

units.obligation_text: Failure to do so would constitute grounds for denial of the permit application.
units.action_summary: If applicants/permittees fail to provide information or allow inspections, APHIS may deny the permit application.

units.obligation_text: APHIS may issue a permit to an applicant if APHIS concludes that the actions allowed under the permit would be highly unlikely to result in the introduction or dissemination of a plant pest, biological control organism, or noxious weed within the United States in a manner that presents an unacceptable risk to plants and plant products.
units.action_summary: APHIS may issue permits when the permitted actions are determined to pose a low (highly unlikely) risk of introduction or dissemination of regulated pests/weeds.

units.obligation_text: Prior to issuing the permit, APHIS would notify the applicant in writing or electronically of all proposed permit conditions. The applicant would have to agree in writing or electronically that he or she, and all his or her employees, agents, and/or officers, would comply with all permit conditions and all provisions of the regulations. If the organism or associated article will be contained in a private residence, the applicant would have to state in this agreement that he or she authorizes APHIS to conduct unscheduled assessments of the residence during normal business hours if a permit is issued. APHIS would issue the permit after it receives and reviews the applicant's agreement.
units.action_summary: APHIS will notify applicants of proposed permit conditions; applicants must agree in writing/electronically to comply (including authorizing unscheduled assessments for private-residence containment); APHIS issues the permit after receiving the agreement.

units.obligation_text: The permit would be valid for no more than 3 years.
units.action_summary: A permit's maximum validity period is three years.

units.obligation_text: During that period, the permittee would have to abide by all permitting conditions, and use of the organism or article would have to conform to the intended use on the permit.
units.action_summary: Permittee must comply with all permit conditions during the permit period and must use the organism/article only as specified on the permit.

units.obligation_text: The use of organisms derived from a regulated parent organism during that period would have to conform to the intended use specified on the permit for the parent organism.
units.action_summary: Any organisms derived from a regulated parent organism must be used only in ways that conform to the parent's permitted intended use.

units.obligation_text: The person to whom APHIS has issued a permit in accordance with this part and who must comply with the provisions of the permit and the regulations in this part.
units.action_summary: A permittee is required to comply with permit provisions and the regulations in this part.

units.obligation_text: For the duration of the permit, the individual must be physically present during normal business hours at or near the location specified on the permit as the ultimate destination of the plant pest, biological control organism, or associated article, and must serve as a primary contact for communication with APHIS. The responsible individual must be at least 18 years of age.
units.action_summary: The responsible individual must be at least 18 years old, be physically present during normal business hours at or near the permit-specified ultimate destination, and serve as the primary APHIS contact.

units.obligation_text: In accordance with section 7734 of the PPA, the act, omission, or failure of any responsible individual will also be deemed the act, omission, or failure of a permittee.
units.action_summary: Acts, omissions, or failures of a responsible individual are legally attributed to the permittee.

units.obligation_text: Persons contemplating the shipment of plant pests, biological control organisms, or associated articles to places outside the United States should make arrangements directly, or through the recipient, with the country of destination for the export of the plant pests, biological control organisms, or associated articles into that country.
units.action_summary: Persons planning to export regulated organisms/articles should coordinate with the destination country to meet that country's import/export requirements.

title: Importation of Fruit and Vegetable Into the Continental United States: Tree Tomatoes From Ecuador

units.obligation_text: Fresh tree tomatoes (Solanum betaceum Cavanilles) may be imported into the continental United States from Ecuador only under the conditions of this systems approach described in this section.
units.actor: importers of fresh tree tomatoes from Ecuador / NPPO of Ecuador
units.action_summary: Importation of tree tomatoes from Ecuador is permitted only if the systems-approach conditions in this section are met.

units.obligation_text: The national plant protection organization (NPPO) of Ecuador must provide an operational workplan to APHIS that details the activities that the NPPO of Ecuador will carry out to meet the requirements of this section.
units.action_summary: NPPO must provide an operational workplan to APHIS describing how it will meet the section's requirements.

units.obligation_text: The operational workplan must be approved by APHIS
units.action_summary: APHIS must approve the operational workplan.

units.obligation_text: The operational workplan must ... include and describe specific requirements as set forth in this section.
units.actor: NPPO of Ecuador (via the operational workplan)
units.action_summary: The workplan must include and describe the specific requirements of this section.

units.obligation_text: Tree tomatoes considered for export to the continental United States must be produced at places of production that are registered with the NPPO of Ecuador.
units.action_summary: Tree tomatoes for export must come from places of production registered with the NPPO of Ecuador.

units.obligation_text: Tree tomatoes must be packed for export to the continental United States in pest-exclusionary packinghouses that are registered with the NPPO of Ecuador.
units.action_summary: Exported tree tomatoes must be packed in pest-exclusionary packinghouses registered with the NPPO of Ecuador.

units.obligation_text: The NPPO of Ecuador must maintain all forms and documents related to export program activities in registered places of production and packinghouses for at least 1 year
units.action_summary: NPPO must retain all export-program records from registered places of production and packinghouses for at least one year.

units.obligation_text: The NPPO of Ecuador must ... provide them to APHIS upon request.
units.action_summary: NPPO must provide the maintained records to APHIS when requested.

units.obligation_text: The identity of each lot of tree tomatoes from Ecuador must be maintained throughout the export process, from the place of production until the tomatoes are released for entry into the continental United States.
units.action_summary: Each lot must retain identity information throughout export until release for entry to the U.S.

units.obligation_text: The means of identification ... must be described in the operational workplan.
units.actor: NPPO of Ecuador (via the operational workplan)
units.action_summary: The method used to identify and trace each lot must be described in the operational workplan.

units.obligation_text: Tree tomatoes from Ecuador may be imported in commercial consignments only.
units.action_summary: Importation from Ecuador is limited to commercial consignments.

units.obligation_text: Lots of tree tomatoes destined for export to the continental United States must be safeguarded during movement from registered places of production to registered packinghouses, and from registered packinghouses to arrival at the port of entry into the continental United States, as specified by the operational workplan.
units.action_summary: Lots must be safeguarded during movement between production, packing, and port of entry as specified in the workplan.

units.obligation_text: Registered places of production of tree tomatoes destined for export to the continental United States must be determined by APHIS and the NPPO of Ecuador to be free from A. fraterculus and C. capitata based on trapping conducted in accordance with the operational workplan.
units.action_summary: APHIS and the NPPO must determine, via trapping per the workplan, that registered production sites are free of specified fruit flies.

units.obligation_text: If the flies per trap per day exceed levels specified in the operational workplan, the place of production will be prohibited from exporting tree tomatoes to the continental United States until APHIS and the NPPO of Ecuador jointly agree that the risk has been mitigated.
units.action_summary: If trap counts exceed specified levels, that production site is prohibited from exporting until APHIS and NPPO jointly agree risk is mitigated.

units.obligation_text: The NPPO must keep records regarding the placement and monitoring of all traps, as well as records of all pest detections in these traps, for at least 1 year
units.action_summary: NPPO must retain trap placement, monitoring, and pest detection records for at least one year.

units.obligation_text: The NPPO must ... provide the records to APHIS, upon request.
units.action_summary: NPPO must provide trap records to APHIS on request.

units.obligation_text: Places of production must remove fallen tree tomato fruit in accordance with the operational workplan.
units.actor: places of production / producers / NPPO enforcement
units.action_summary: Production sites must remove fallen fruit per the operational workplan.

units.obligation_text: Fallen fruit may not be included in field containers of fruit brought to the packinghouse to be packed for export.
units.action_summary: Fallen fruit is prohibited from being placed in field containers for export packing.

units.obligation_text: The NPPO of Ecuador must inspect fields at registered places of production at least once during the growing season for Tamarillo mosaic virus.
units.action_summary: NPPO must inspect registered fields at least once per growing season for Tamarillo mosaic virus.

units.obligation_text: Sites must be determined by the NPPO to be free of the virus as a result of these inspections.
units.action_summary: NPPO must determine that sites are free of Tamarillo mosaic virus based on the inspections.

units.obligation_text: Starting 60 days before harvest and continuing throughout the shipping season, the NPPO of Ecuador must visit and inspect registered places of production monthly for signs of infestation.
units.action_summary: From 60 days before harvest through the shipping season, NPPO must conduct monthly inspections of registered production sites for infestation.

units.obligation_text: The NPPO of Ecuador must allow APHIS to monitor these inspections.
units.action_summary: NPPO must permit APHIS to monitor the monthly inspections.

units.obligation_text: The NPPO of Ecuador must also certify to APHIS that registered places of production have effective fruit fly trapping programs and control guidelines in place to reduce pest populations.
units.action_summary: NPPO must certify to APHIS that registered sites have effective trapping and control measures in place.

units.obligation_text: If APHIS or the NPPO of Ecuador determines that a registered place of production has failed to follow the requirements in this paragraph (b), the place of production will be excluded from the export program
units.action_summary: If a registered site fails to follow paragraph (b) requirements, it will be excluded from the export program.

units.obligation_text: the place of production will be excluded ... until APHIS and the NPPO of Ecuador jointly agree that the place of production has taken appropriate remedial measures to address the plant pest risk.
units.actor: place of production (for exclusion) / APHIS and NPPO (for reinstatement)
units.action_summary: Exclusion continues until APHIS and NPPO jointly agree that appropriate remedial measures have been taken.

units.obligation_text: During the time registered packinghouses are in use for packing tree tomatoes for export to the continental United States, the packinghouse can only accept tree tomatoes that are from registered places of production and that are produced in accordance with this section.
units.action_summary: Packinghouses may accept only tree tomatoes from registered production sites produced according to this section.

units.obligation_text: Tree tomatoes must be packed in insect-proof cartons or containers, or covered with insect-proof mesh or plastic tarpaulin, within 24 hours of harvest.
units.action_summary: Within 24 hours of harvest, tomatoes must be packed in insect-proof containers or covered with insect-proof mesh or tarpaulin.

units.obligation_text: These safeguards must remain intact until the tree tomatoes arrive in the United States
units.action_summary: The insect-proof packing or coverings must remain intact until arrival in the U.S.

units.obligation_text: or the consignment will not be allowed to enter the United States.
units.action_summary: If safeguards are not intact, the consignment will be denied entry into the United States.

units.obligation_text: All openings to the outside of the packinghouse must be covered by screening with openings of not more than 1.6 mm or by some other barrier that prevents pests from entering.
units.action_summary: Packinghouse openings must be screened to 1.6 mm or otherwise blocked to prevent pest entry.

units.obligation_text: The packinghouse must have double doors at the entrance to the facility and at the interior entrance to the area where the tree tomatoes are packed.
units.action_summary: Packinghouses must have double-door entries at facility and packing-area entrances.

units.obligation_text: A biometric sample of tree tomato fruit jointly agreed upon by the NPPO of Ecuador and APHIS must be inspected in Ecuador by the NPPO of Ecuador or officials authorized by the NPPO of Ecuador following post-harvest processing.
units.actor: NPPO of Ecuador or authorized officials
units.action_summary: An agreed biometric sample must be inspected in Ecuador by NPPO or its authorized officials after post-harvest processing.

units.obligation_text: The sample must be visually inspected for N. elegantalis and Tamarillo mosaic virus.
units.actor: NPPO of Ecuador or authorized officials
units.action_summary: The sample must be visually inspected for Neoleucinodes elegantalis and Tamarillo mosaic virus.

units.obligation_text: A portion of the fruit must then be cut open and inspected for A. fraterculus and C. capitata.
units.actor: NPPO of Ecuador or authorized officials
units.action_summary: Part of the sample must be cut open and inspected for Anastrepha fraterculus and Ceratitis capitata.

units.obligation_text: If N. elegantalis is found, the entire lot of fruit will be prohibited from import into the United States
units.action_summary: If N. elegantalis is detected, the entire lot is prohibited from import into the U.S.

units.obligation_text: unless it is treated with an approved quarantine treatment monitored by APHIS.
units.action_summary: An affected lot may be allowed if it receives an APHIS-monitored approved quarantine treatment.

units.obligation_text: If Tamarillo mosaic virus is found, the entire lot of fruit will be prohibited from importation into the United States.
units.action_summary: Detection of Tamarillo mosaic virus results in prohibition of the entire lot from importation.

units.obligation_text: If a single larva of A. fraterculus or C. capitata is found, the entire lot of fruit will be prohibited from importation to the United States
units.action_summary: If any single larva of the specified fruit flies is found, the entire lot is prohibited from import.

units.obligation_text: the place of production producing that fruit will be suspended from the export program until appropriate measures, as agreed upon by the NPPO of Ecuador and APHIS, have been taken.
units.actor: place of production (suspension); APHIS and NPPO (agreeing remedial measures)
units.action_summary: If a larva is found, the producing site will be suspended from the export program until NPPO and APHIS agree appropriate remedial measures have been taken.

units.obligation_text: Each consignment of fresh tree tomato fruit from Ecuador must be accompanied by a phytosanitary certificate, issued by the NPPO of Ecuador, that contains an additional declaration that the tomatoes were produced in accordance with the requirements of this section, and have been inspected and found free of A. fraterculus, C. capitata, N. elegantalis, and the Tamarillo mosaic virus.
units.action_summary: Each consignment must have a phytosanitary certificate from the NPPO that declares production in accordance with the section and inspection showing freedom from listed pests.

units.obligation_text: phytosanitary certificate, issued by the NPPO of Ecuador
units.action_summary: NPPO must issue the phytosanitary certificate accompanying each consignment.

units.obligation_text: that contains an additional declaration that the tomatoes were produced in accordance with the requirements of this section, and have been inspected and found free of A. fraterculus, C. capitata, N. elegantalis, and the Tamarillo mosaic virus.
units.actor: NPPO of Ecuador (via the phytosanitary certificate)
units.action_summary: The certificate must include an additional declaration that the tomatoes were produced as required and inspected free of the listed pests and virus.

title: Animal Welfare: Procedures for Applying for Licenses and Renewals
Extension of the Comment Period for "Animal Welfare: Procedures for Applying for Licenses and Renewals"
Lacey Act Implementation Plan: De Minimis Exception

units.obligation_text: The Lacey Act, as amended (16 U.S.C. 3371 et seq.), makes it unlawful to, among other things, import, export, transport, sell, receive, acquire, or purchase in interstate or foreign commerce any plant, with some limited exceptions, taken, possessed, transported or sold in violation of any Federal or Tribal law, or in violation of a State or foreign law that protects plants or that regulates certain specified plant-related activities.
units.action_summary: Prohibits importing, exporting, transporting, selling, receiving, acquiring, or purchasing in interstate or foreign commerce any plant that was taken/possessed/transported/sold in violation of applicable Federal, Tribal, State, or foreign plant-protecting laws.

units.obligation_text: The Lacey Act also makes it unlawful to make or submit any false record, account, or label for, or any false identification of, any plant covered by the Act.
units.action_summary: Prohibits making or submitting any false record, account, label, or false identification of any plant covered by the Act.

units.obligation_text: Any person importing any plant shall file upon importation a declaration that contains:
units.action_summary: Requires persons importing plants to file a declaration at importation containing specified information.

units.obligation_text: The scientific name of any plant (including the genus and species of the plant) contained in the importation;
units.action_summary: Declaration must include the scientific name (genus and species) of each plant in the importation.

units.obligation_text: A description of the value of the importation and the quantity, including the unit of measure, of the plant;
units.action_summary: Declaration must include a description of the importation's value and the quantity of the plant, including unit of measure.

units.obligation_text: The name of the country from which the plant was taken.
units.action_summary: Declaration must include the name of the country from which the plant was taken.

units.obligation_text: The declaration relating to a plant product shall also contain:
units.actor: any person importing a plant product
units.action_summary: Requires additional information on declarations for plant products as specified in subparagraphs.

units.obligation_text: If the species of plant used to produce the plant product that is the subject of the importation varies, and the species used to produce the plant product is unknown, the name of each species of plant that may have been used to produce the plant product;
units.actor: any person importing a plant product
units.action_summary: If species composition varies and the specific species is unknown, the declaration must list every species that may have been used to produce the plant product.

units.obligation_text: If the species of plant used to produce the plant product that is the subject of the importation is commonly taken from more than one country, and the country from which the plant was taken and used to produce the plant product is unknown, the name of each country from which the plant may have been taken;
units.actor: any person importing a plant product
units.action_summary: If a species is commonly sourced from multiple countries and the actual source is unknown, the declaration must list each possible source country.

units.obligation_text: If a paper or paperboard plant product includes recycled plant product, the average percent recycled content without regard for the species or country of origin of the recycled plant product, in addition to the information for the non-recycled plant content otherwise required by this section.
units.actor: any person importing a paper or paperboard plant product
units.action_summary: For paper/paperboard including recycled content, the declaration must state the average percent recycled content as well as the required non-recycled content information.

units.obligation_text: Plants and products containing plant materials are excepted from the declaration requirement if:
units.actor: persons importing plants and products containing plant materials
units.action_summary: Provides conditions under which plants and plant-containing products are exempted from the declaration requirement.

units.obligation_text: The plant is used exclusively as packaging material to support, protect, or carry another item, unless the packaging material itself is the item being imported;
units.actor: persons importing plants used as packaging
units.action_summary: Plant materials used solely as packaging are exempt from the declaration requirement, except when the packaging material itself is the imported item.

units.obligation_text: The plant material in a product represents no more than 5 percent of the total weight of the individual product unit, provided that the total weight of the plant material in [an entry of such products][a product unit] does not exceed [2.9 kilograms] [or other amount]; or, if the weight cannot be determined, the value of the plant material in the individual product unit represents no more than 10 percent of the declared value of the product, provided that the total quantity of plant material in [an entry of such products][a product unit] has a volume of less than [1 board foot (that is, 12 x 12 x 1 inches or 30.48 x 30.48 x 2.54 centimeters)] [or other amount].
units.actor: persons importing products containing plant material
units.action_summary: Sets quantitative thresholds under which products with plant material are exempt from declaration: either a weight-based threshold or, if weight cannot be determined, a value-and-volume-based threshold.

units.obligation_text: The plant material in a product represents no more than 5 percent of the total weight of the individual product unit, provided that the total weight of the plant material in [an entry of such products][a product unit] does not exceed [2.9 kilograms] [or other amount];
units.actor: persons importing products containing plant material
units.action_summary: Weight-based criterion for exception: plant material ≤5% of individual unit weight and total plant material weight per entry/unit does not exceed 2.9 kilograms (or other specified amount).

units.obligation_text: If the weight cannot be determined, the value of the plant material in the individual product unit represents no more than 10 percent of the declared value of the product, provided that the total quantity of plant material in [an entry of such products][a product unit] has a volume of less than [1 board foot (that is, 12 x 12 x 1 inches or 30.48 x 30.48 x 2.54 centimeters)] [or other amount].
units.actor: persons importing products containing plant material
units.action_summary: Alternative criterion for exception when weight is indeterminable: plant material value ≤10% of declared value and total plant material volume per entry/unit < 1 board foot (or other specified amount).

units.obligation_text: A product will not be eligible for an exception under paragraph (b) of this section if it contains plant material listed:
units.actor: products or persons importing those products
units.action_summary: Disqualifies products from the paragraph (b) exception if they contain plant material listed in specified endangered/CITES/State conservation listings.
units.modal_raw: will not be eligible for an exception

units.obligation_text: In an appendix to the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (27 UST 1087; TIAS 8249);
units.actor: products or persons importing those products
units.action_summary: If the plant material is listed in a CITES appendix, the product is not eligible for the paragraph (b) exception.
units.modal_raw: will not be eligible for an exception if

units.obligation_text: As an endangered or threatened species under the Endangered Species Act of 1973 (16 U.S.C. 1531 et seq.);
units.actor: products or persons importing those products
units.action_summary: If the plant material is listed as endangered or threatened under the ESA, the product is not eligible for the paragraph (b) exception.
units.modal_raw: will not be eligible for an exception if

units.obligation_text: Pursuant to any State law that provides for the conservation of species that are indigenous to the State and are threatened with extinction.
units.actor: products or persons importing those products
units.action_summary: If the plant material is listed under a State conservation law for indigenous, threatened-with-extinction species, the product is not eligible for the paragraph (b) exception.
units.modal_raw: will not be eligible for an exception if

units.obligation_text: In the case of commodities for which a plant declaration is required, the declaration must be submitted within 3 business days of importation.
units.actor: any person importing commodities for which a plant declaration is required
units.action_summary: Requires submission of required plant declarations within 3 business days of importation.

units.obligation_text: A plant is not eligible for these exclusions if it is listed:
