units.action_summary: Plants that are listed in specified endangered/CITES/State lists are not eligible for the categorical exclusions (common cultivar, common food crop, etc.).

units.obligation_text: In an appendix to the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (27 UST 1087; TIAS 8249);
units.action_summary: If a plant is listed in a CITES appendix, it is not eligible for the categorical exclusions.

units.obligation_text: As an endangered or threatened species under the Endangered Species Act of 1973 (16 U.S.C. 1531 et seq.);
units.action_summary: If a plant is listed as endangered or threatened under the ESA, it is not eligible for the categorical exclusions.

units.obligation_text: Pursuant to any State law that provides for the conservation of species that are indigenous to the State and are threatened with extinction.
units.action_summary: If a plant is listed under a State conservation law for indigenous, threatened species, it is not eligible for the categorical exclusions.

title: Regulated Areas, Regulated Establishments, and Testing Protocols: Phytophthora ramorum

units.obligation_text: No person may move interstate from any regulated establishment any regulated, restricted, or associated articles except in accordance with this subpart.
units.action_summary: Prohibits moving regulated/restricted/associated articles interstate from a regulated establishment except as allowed by this subpart.

units.obligation_text: The Administrator will designate as a quarantined area in paragraph (a)(3) of this section each State, or each portion of a State, in which Phytophthora ramorum has been confirmed by an inspector to be established in the natural environment, in which the Administrator has reason to believe that Phytophthora ramorum is present in the natural environment, or that the Administrator considers it necessary to quarantine because of its inseparability for quarantine enforcement purposes from localities in which Phytophthora ramorum has been found in the natural environment.
units.action_summary: Requires the Administrator to designate States or portions as quarantined areas when P. ramorum is confirmed, reasonably believed present, or inseparable for enforcement.

units.obligation_text: Less than an entire area will be designated as a quarantined area only if the Administrator determines that: (i) The State has adopted and is enforcing restrictions on the intrastate movement of regulated, restricted, and associated articles that are substantially the same as those imposed by this subpart on the interstate movement of regulated, restricted, and associated articles;
units.action_summary: Administrator may designate part of a State as quarantined only if the State has adopted and enforces intrastate movement restrictions substantially the same as the subpart's interstate rules.
units.modal_raw: will / has adopted and is enforcing

units.obligation_text: Less than an entire area will be designated as a quarantined area only if the Administrator determines that: (ii) The designation of less than the entire State as a quarantined area will prevent the interstate spread of Phytophthora ramorum.
units.action_summary: Administrator must determine that designating less than the entire State will prevent interstate spread of P. ramorum before doing so.

units.obligation_text: The Administrator or an inspector may temporarily designate any nonquaratined area as a quarantined area in accordance with paragraph (a)(1) of this section.
units.action_summary: Permits the Administrator or an inspector to temporarily designate nonquarantined areas as quarantined areas.

units.obligation_text: The Administrator will give a copy of this regulation along with a written notice for the temporary designation to the owner or person in possession of the nonquarantined area.
units.action_summary: Requires the Administrator to provide the owner/person in possession with the regulation and written notice when temporarily designating an area quarantined.

units.obligation_text: Thereafter, the interstate movement of any regulated, restricted, or associated article from an area temporarily designated as a quarantined area will be subject to this subpart.
units.actor: persons moving regulated, restricted, or associated articles
units.action_summary: After temporary designation, interstate movement of regulated articles from that area must comply with this subpart.

units.obligation_text: As soon as practicable, this area will be added to the list in paragraph (a)(3) of this section or the designation will be terminated by the Administrator or an inspector.
units.action_summary: Requires the Administrator or inspector to either add the temporarily designated area to the official list or terminate the designation as soon as practicable.

units.obligation_text: The owner or person in possession of an area for which designation is terminated will be given notice of the termination as soon as practicable.
units.action_summary: Requires notice to be given to the owner/person in possession when a temporary quarantine designation is terminated.

units.obligation_text: The Administrator will designate a nursery that is not located in a quarantined area for Phytophthora ramorum as a regulated establishment for Phytophthora ramorum if the nursery ships regulated, restricted, or associated articles interstate and sources of Phytophthora ramorum are detected on nursery stock, or in soil, growing media, pots used for nursery stock, standing water, drainage water, water used for irrigation, or any other regulated, restricted, or associated articles at the nursery.
units.action_summary: Administrator must designate out-of-quarantine nurseries as regulated establishments if they ship interstate and P. ramorum sources are detected on-site or in associated media.

units.obligation_text: The Administrator will withdraw regulation of a regulated establishment if, for 3 consecutive years, each time the nursery is inspected by an inspector, it is found free of sources of Phytophthora ramorum inoculum.
units.action_summary: Requires the Administrator to deregulate an establishment if inspections over 3 consecutive years find it free of P. ramorum inoculum each time.

units.obligation_text: The regulated article or associated article originated outside the quarantined area and the point of origin of the article is indicated on the waybill of the vehicle transporting the article; and the regulated or associated article is moved from outside of the quarantined area through the quarantined area without stopping except for refueling or for traffic conditions, such as traffic lights or stop signs, and the article is not unpacked or unloaded in the quarantined area.
units.actor: person moving the regulated or associated article
units.action_summary: Allows interstate movement without a certificate if the article originated outside, the origin is on the waybill, it only transits the quarantined area without stopping except for refueling/traffic, and is not unpacked/unloaded there.

units.obligation_text: Soil samples may be moved from a quarantined area for Phytophthora ramorum for chemical or physical (compositional) analysis provided that they are moved to a laboratory; and that laboratory: (A) Has entered into and is operating under a compliance agreement with APHIS in accordance with § 301.92–6; (B) Is abiding by all terms and conditions of that compliance agreement; and (C) Is approved by APHIS to test and/or analyze such samples.
units.actor: person moving soil samples / the laboratory
units.action_summary: Permits movement of soil samples out of a quarantined area to a laboratory for analysis only if the lab has a compliance agreement, abides by it, and is APHIS-approved.

units.obligation_text: That laboratory has entered into and is operating under a compliance agreement with APHIS in accordance with § 301.92–6.
units.action_summary: Requires the laboratory to enter into and operate under a compliance agreement with APHIS to receive soil samples.
units.modal_raw: has entered into and is operating under

units.obligation_text: That laboratory is abiding by all terms and conditions of that compliance agreement.
units.action_summary: Requires the laboratory to abide by all terms of its compliance agreement with APHIS.

units.obligation_text: That laboratory is approved by APHIS to test and/or analyze such samples.
units.action_summary: Requires the laboratory to be APHIS-approved to test/analyze soil samples moved from quarantined areas.

units.obligation_text: Regulated, restricted, and associated articles may be moved interstate from a regulated establishment if the regulated establishment has entered into a compliance agreement with APHIS in accordance with § 301.92–6, and the articles are accompanied by a certificate issued in accordance with § 301.92–5.
units.action_summary: Permits interstate movement from a regulated establishment only if the establishment has a compliance agreement with APHIS and the articles are accompanied by an APHIS-issued certificate.

units.obligation_text: Are shipped from a nursery that has been inspected in accordance with the inspection and sampling protocol described in § 301.92–11(a)(1), and the nursery is free of evidence of Phytophthora ramorum infestation;
units.action_summary: One criterion for qualifying shipments: nursery inspected per §301.92–11(a)(1) and found free of P. ramorum evidence.

units.obligation_text: Shipments qualify if they meet one of the specified conditions under § 301.92–5(a)(1)(iv)(A).
units.action_summary: Sets that certificates may be issued for shipments that meet any of the listed inspection/testing conditions.

units.obligation_text: Are shipped from a nursery that has been inspected in accordance with the inspection and sampling protocol described in § 301.92–11(a)(2), and the nursery is free of evidence of Phytophthora ramorum infestation;
units.action_summary: Alternative criterion: nursery inspected per §301.92–11(a)(2) and found free of P. ramorum evidence.

units.obligation_text: Are shipped from a nursery that has been inspected in accordance with the inspection and sampling protocol described in § 301.92–11(a)(2), is not free of evidence of Phytophthora ramorum infestation, but has entered into and is operating under a compliance agreement with APHIS, and is determined by an inspector to be abiding by all terms and conditions of that agreement;
units.action_summary: Alternative criterion: even if nursery has evidence of infestation, it may qualify for shipments if it has a compliance agreement and an inspector determines it is abiding by the agreement's terms.
units.modal_raw: has entered into and is operating under / is determined to be

units.obligation_text: An inspector may issue a certificate for the movement of regulated, restricted, and/or associated articles from a regulated establishment if the inspector determines that: (1) The nursery has entered into a compliance agreement APHIS in accordance with § 301.92–6 and is abiding by all terms and conditions of that agreement; and (2) The nursery has been inspected in accordance with § 301.92–11(c); and (3) The articles to be shipped interstate are free from Phytophthora ramorum inoculum; and (4) The movement of the articles is not subject to additional restriction under section 414 of the Plant Protection Act (7 U.S.C. 7714) or other Federal domestic plant quarantines and regulations.
units.action_summary: Permits an inspector to issue certificates for movements from regulated establishments only if four specified conditions are met (compliance agreement, inspection, articles free of inoculum, and no other restrictions).

units.obligation_text: Nurseries that are located in quarantined areas, that move regulated articles ... interstate, and in which Phytophthora ramorum has not been detected since March 31, 2011, must meet the following requirements.
units.actor: nurseries located in quarantined areas (with no detections since 3/31/2011)
units.action_summary: Requires such nurseries to meet the specified annual inspection, sampling, testing, and certification requirements; failure prohibits interstate movement of regulated/associated articles.

units.obligation_text: The nursery must be inspected annually for symptoms of Phytophthora ramorum by an inspector.
units.action_summary: Requires annual inspection by an inspector for P. ramorum symptoms at the nursery.

units.obligation_text: A minimum number of plant samples must be tested per nursery location. The minimum number will be determined by APHIS on a nursery-by-nursery basis, based on the number of regulated, restricted, and associated articles contained in the nursery. Each sample may contain more than one leaf, and may come from more than one plant, but all plants in the sample must be from the same lot. Asymptomatic samples, if collected, must be taken from regulated and associated articles and nearby plants.
units.action_summary: Requires a minimum number of samples (set by APHIS), allows samples to contain multiple leaves/plants from same lot, and requires asymptomatic samples be taken from regulated/associated and nearby plants if collected.
units.modal_raw: must / will be determined / may / must

units.obligation_text: Inspectors must conduct inspections at times when the best expression of symptoms is anticipated and must take nursery fungicide programs into consideration.
units.action_summary: Requires inspectors to time inspections to when symptoms are most likely visible and to consider nursery fungicide programs.

units.obligation_text: Nursery owners must keep records of fungicide applications for 2 years and must make them available to inspectors upon request.
units.action_summary: Requires nursery owners to retain fungicide application records for 2 years and provide them to inspectors on request.

units.obligation_text: Samples must be labeled and sent for testing to a laboratory approved by APHIS and must be tested using a test method approved by APHIS, in accordance with § 301.92–12.
units.action_summary: Requires samples to be labeled, sent to APHIS-approved labs, and tested using APHIS-approved methods per §301.92–12.

units.obligation_text: If all plant samples tested in accordance with this section and § 301.92–12 return negative results for Phytophthora ramorum, an inspector may certify that the nursery is free of evidence of Phytophthora ramorum infestation at the time of the inspection, and the nursery is eligible to enter into or maintain its compliance agreement in accordance with § 301.92–6.
units.action_summary: Allows an inspector to certify the nursery is free of P. ramorum if all samples test negative, enabling eligibility to enter/maintain a compliance agreement.

units.obligation_text: During the 30 days prior to interstate movement from a nursery in a quarantined area, regulated articles or associated articles intended for interstate movement must be inspected for symptoms of Phytophthora ramorum by an inspector.
units.action_summary: Requires pre-shipment inspection by an inspector within 30 days prior to interstate movement for regulated/associated articles from quarantined-area nurseries.

units.obligation_text: No inspections of shipments will be conducted unless the nursery from which the shipment originates has a current and valid annual certification in accordance with this section.
units.action_summary: Prohibits shipment inspections for nurseries that do not have a current valid annual certification.

units.obligation_text: If no symptomatic plants are found upon inspection, the shipment may be considered free from evidence of Phytophthora ramorum and is eligible for interstate movement, provided that the nursery is operating under a compliance agreement with APHIS in accordance with § 301.92–6.
units.actor: the shipment / person moving the shipment (conditional)
units.action_summary: Allows a shipment to be considered free and eligible for interstate movement if pre-shipment inspection finds no symptomatic plants and the nursery has a compliance agreement.

units.obligation_text: If symptomatic plants are found upon inspection, the inspector will collect at least one sample per symptomatic plant, and one sample per regulated article or associated article that is in close proximity to, or that has had physical contact with, a symptomatic plant.
units.action_summary: Requires inspectors to collect at least one sample per symptomatic plant and samples from nearby or contacting regulated/associated articles when symptoms are found.

units.obligation_text: Samples taken in accordance with this paragraph (a)(1) must be labeled and sent for testing to a laboratory approved by APHIS and must be tested using a test method approved by APHIS, in accordance with § 301.92–12. The interstate movement of plants in the shipment is prohibited until the plants in the shipment are determined to be free of evidence of Phytophthora ramorum infection in accordance with § 301.92–12.
units.actor: inspectors / person responsible for shipment / persons moving the plants
units.action_summary: Requires samples to be sent to APHIS-approved labs using approved methods and prohibits interstate movement of shipment plants until they are determined free of P. ramorum per §301.92–12.

units.obligation_text: The nursery must be inspected at least twice annually for symptoms of Phytophthora ramorum infestation by an inspector.
units.action_summary: Requires at least two inspections per year by an inspector for nurseries where P. ramorum has been detected since March 31, 2011.

units.obligation_text: Samples must be taken from host plants, soil, standing water, drainage water, water for irrigation, and any other articles determined by the inspector to be possible sources of Phytophthora ramorum inoculum.
units.action_summary: Requires sampling from host plants, soil, waters, irrigation water, and any other inspector-identified possible inoculum sources.

units.obligation_text: Samples must be labeled and sent for testing to a laboratory approved by APHIS and must be tested using a test method approved by APHIS in accordance with § 301.92–12.
units.action_summary: Requires labeling and testing of samples at APHIS-approved labs using APHIS-approved methods.

units.obligation_text: If all samples tested in accordance with this section and § 301.92–12 return negative results for Phytophthora ramorum, an inspector may certify that the nursery is free of Phytophthora ramorum at the time of the inspection.
units.action_summary: Allows an inspector to certify the nursery is free of P. ramorum if all samples test negative.

units.obligation_text: If the nursery is inspected and determined by an inspector to be free of Phytophthora ramorum inoculum each time it is inspected for 3 consecutive years, the nursery will thereafter be inspected in accordance with paragraph (a)(1) of this section.
units.action_summary: Provides that nurseries free of inoculum at each inspection for 3 consecutive years will thereafter follow the less-frequent inspection schedule of paragraph (a)(1).

units.obligation_text: If any samples tested in accordance with this section and § 301.92–12 return positive results for Phytophthora ramorum, the nursery may ship lots of regulated, restricted, and associated articles interstate pursuant to § 301.92–5(b) only if the lot is determined to be free from Phytophthora ramorum inoculum. The method for this determination will be specified in the nursery’s compliance agreement with APHIS.
units.action_summary: Permits shipping of lots from a nursery with positive results only under §301.92–5(b) and only if the lot is determined free of inoculum by a method specified in the nursery's compliance agreement.

units.obligation_text: The nursery must be visually inspected annually for symptoms of Phytophthora ramorum. Inspections and determinations of freedom from evidence of Phytophthora ramorum infestation must occur at the time when the best expression of symptoms is anticipated.
units.action_summary: Requires annual visual inspections timed to when symptoms are most likely to be expressed to determine freedom from P. ramorum.

units.obligation_text: All plants showing symptoms of infection with Phytophthora ramorum upon inspection will be sampled and tested in accordance with § 301.92–12. If symptomatic plants are found upon inspection, the following plants must be withheld from interstate shipment until testing is completed and the nursery is found free of evidence of Phytophthora ramorum in accordance with this paragraph and § 301.92–12: All symptomatic plants, any plants located in the same lot as the suspect plant, and any plants located within 2 meters of this lot of plants.
units.actor: nursery owners / persons moving plants / inspectors
units.action_summary: Requires sampling and testing of symptomatic plants and mandates withholding symptomatic plants, same-lot plants, and plants within 2 meters from interstate shipment until testing clears them.
units.modal_raw: will be sampled / must be withheld

units.obligation_text: If all plant samples tested in accordance with this section and § 301.92–12 return negative results for Phytophthora ramorum, or if an inspector at the nursery determines that plants in a nursery exhibit no signs of infection with Phytophthora ramorum, the inspector may certify that the nursery [is] free of evidence of Phytophthora ramorum infestation at the time of inspection. Certification is valid for 1 year and must be renewed each year to continue shipping plants interstate.
units.action_summary: Allows an inspector to certify nursery freedom if tests are negative or no signs observed; certification lasts 1 year and must be renewed annually to continue interstate shipments.

units.obligation_text: To meet the conditions of § 301.92–5(b), the regulated establishment must be inspected at least twice annually for symptoms of Phytophthora ramorum infestation by an inspector.
units.action_summary: Requires at least two annual inspections by an inspector for regulated establishments to meet §301.92–5(b) conditions.

units.obligation_text: Samples must be taken from host plants, soil, standing water, drainage water, water for irrigation, growing media, and any other articles determined by the inspector to be possible sources of Phytophthora ramorum inoculum.
units.action_summary: Requires sampling from various potential inoculum sources at regulated establishments as determined by the inspector.

units.obligation_text: Samples must be labeled and sent for testing to a laboratory approved by APHIS and must be tested using a test method approved by APHIS in accordance with § 301.92–12.
units.action_summary: Requires regulated-establishment samples to be labeled, sent to APHIS-approved labs, and tested via APHIS-approved methods.

units.obligation_text: If all samples tested in accordance with this section and § 301.92–12 return negative results for Phytophthora ramorum, an inspector may certify that the nursery is free of Phytophthora ramorum at the time of the inspection.
units.action_summary: Allows an inspector to certify a regulated establishment is free of P. ramorum when all samples test negative.

units.obligation_text: If any samples tested in accordance with this section and § 301.92–12 return positive results for Phytophthora ramorum, the nursery may ship lots of regulated, restricted, and associated articles interstate pursuant to § 301.92–5(b) only if the lot is determined to be free from Phytophthora ramorum inoculum. The method for this determination will be specified in the nursery’s compliance agreement with APHIS.
units.action_summary: Permits interstate shipment of lots from a regulated establishment with positive samples only under §301.92–5(b) and only if the lot is determined free of inoculum by a method specified in the compliance agreement.

title: Importation of Pummelo From Thailand Into the Continental United States

units.obligation_text: Fresh pummelo fruit (Citrus maxima (Burm.) Merr.) (Rutaceae) may be imported into the continental United States from Thailand under the following conditions:
units.actor: importers/consignors of fresh pummelo fruit from Thailand
units.action_summary: Importation of fresh pummelo fruit from Thailand into the continental United States is permitted, subject to stated conditions.

units.obligation_text: The fresh pummelo fruit must be shipped in commercial consignments only.
units.action_summary: Shipments must be commercial consignments only (no noncommercial consignments).

units.obligation_text: The fresh pummelo fruit must be treated with irradiation in accordance with part 305 of this chapter.
units.actor: handlers/packers/importers (treatment providers) of the fresh pummelo fruit
units.action_summary: Fruit must receive irradiation treatment as specified in 7 CFR part 305.

units.obligation_text: Prior to packing, the fresh pummelo fruit must be washed, brushed, disinfested, submerged in surfactant, treated for Xanthomonas citri Gabriel et al. with an APHIS-approved surface disinfectant, and treated for Phyllosticta citriasiana and Phyllosticta citricarpa with an APHIS-approved fungicide.
units.actor: packinghouse operators / handlers of fresh pummelo fruit prior to packing
units.action_summary: Before packing, packinghouse operators must perform specified washing, brushing, disinfestation, surfactant submersion, and APHIS-approved surface disinfectant and fungicide treatments.

units.obligation_text: Prior to packing, the fresh pummelo fruit must be washed.
units.actor: packinghouse operators / handlers of fresh pummelo fruit
units.action_summary: Fruit must be washed before packing.

units.obligation_text: Prior to packing, the fresh pummelo fruit must be brushed.
units.actor: packinghouse operators / handlers of fresh pummelo fruit
units.action_summary: Fruit must be brushed before packing.

units.obligation_text: Prior to packing, the fresh pummelo fruit must be disinfested.
units.actor: packinghouse operators / handlers of fresh pummelo fruit
units.action_summary: Fruit must be disinfested before packing.

units.obligation_text: Prior to packing, the fresh pummelo fruit must be submerged in surfactant.
units.actor: packinghouse operators / handlers of fresh pummelo fruit
units.action_summary: Fruit must be submerged in a surfactant prior to packing.

units.obligation_text: Prior to packing, the fresh pummelo fruit must be treated for Xanthomonas citri Gabriel et al. with an APHIS-approved surface disinfectant.
units.actor: packinghouse operators / handlers of fresh pummelo fruit
units.action_summary: Fruit must be treated for Xanthomonas citri using an APHIS-approved surface disinfectant before packing.

units.obligation_text: Prior to packing, the fresh pummelo fruit must be treated for Phyllosticta citriasiana and Phyllosticta citricarpa with an APHIS-approved fungicide.
units.actor: packinghouse operators / handlers of fresh pummelo fruit
units.action_summary: Fruit must be treated for Phyllosticta citriasiana and Phyllosticta citricarpa using an APHIS-approved fungicide before packing.

units.obligation_text: Each shipment of fresh pummelo fruit must be accompanied by a phytosanitary certificate issued by the national plant protection organization (NPPO) of Thailand.
units.actor: consignors/importers and the NPPO of Thailand
units.action_summary: Each shipment must be accompanied by a phytosanitary certificate issued by Thailand's NPPO.

units.obligation_text: If the fresh pummelo fruit was irradiated in Thailand, each consignment of fruit must be inspected jointly in Thailand by APHIS and the NPPO of Thailand, and the phytosanitary certificate must contain an additional declaration attesting to irradiation of the fresh pummelo fruit in accordance with part 305 of this chapter.
units.actor: APHIS and the NPPO of Thailand; consignors (for the phytosanitary certificate content)
units.action_summary: When fruit is irradiated in Thailand, APHIS and Thailand's NPPO must jointly inspect consignments in Thailand and the phytosanitary certificate must include an additional declaration attesting to irradiation per part 305.

units.obligation_text: If the fresh pummelo fruit will be irradiated upon arrival into the continental United States, joint inspection in Thailand and an additional declaration on the phytosanitary certificate are not required.
units.actor: APHIS and the NPPO of Thailand; consignors (regarding certificate contents)
units.action_summary: If irradiation occurs upon arrival in the U.S., then joint inspection in Thailand and the additional phytosanitary certificate declaration are not required.

units.obligation_text: Consignments of fresh pummelo fruit from Thailand are subject to inspection at ports of entry in the continental United States.
units.actor: consignments/importers/APHIS (inspection will be performed at ports of entry)
units.action_summary: Shipments will be inspected at U.S. ports of entry.

title: Branding Requirements for Bovines Imported Into the United States from Mexico

units.obligation_text: Each steer or spayed heifer imported into the United States from Mexico shall be identified with a distinct, permanent, and legible "M" mark applied with a freeze brand, hot iron, or other method prior to arrival at a port of entry, unless the steer or spayed heifer is imported for slaughter in accordance with § 93.429.
units.actor: each steer or spayed heifer imported into the United States from Mexico
units.action_summary: Animals imported from Mexico must be identified prior to arrival at a port of entry with a distinct, permanent, legible 'M' mark applied by freeze brand, hot iron, or other method, unless imported for slaughter under § 93.429.

units.obligation_text: The "M" mark shall be between 3 inches (7.5 cm) and 5 inches (12.5 cm) high and wide.
units.actor: the 'M' mark on each such animal
units.action_summary: The 'M' mark must be between 3 and 5 inches high and wide.

units.obligation_text: and shall be applied to each animal’s right hip, within 4 inches (10 cm) of the midline of the tailhead (that is, the top of the brand should be within 4 inches (10 cm) of the midline of the tailhead, and placed above the hook and pin bones).
units.actor: the 'M' mark on each such animal / the person applying the mark
units.action_summary: The mark must be applied to the animal's right hip, with the top of the brand within 4 inches of the midline of the tailhead and placed above the hook and pin bones.

units.obligation_text: The brand should also be within 18 inches (45.7 cm) of the anus.
units.actor: the 'M' mark on each such animal / the person applying the mark
units.action_summary: It is recommended that the brand also be within 18 inches of the anus.

units.obligation_text: unless the steer or spayed heifer is imported for slaughter in accordance with § 93.429.
units.actor: a steer or spayed heifer imported for slaughter in accordance with § 93.429
units.action_summary: Animals imported for slaughter under § 93.429 are exempt from the marking requirement.

units.obligation_text: An "M" mark properly applied with a freeze brand, hot iron, or other method, and easily visible on the live animal and on the carcass before skinning.
units.actor: the 'M' mark on each animal / the person applying the mark
units.action_summary: An acceptable 'M' mark must be properly applied by freeze brand, hot iron, or other method and be easily visible on the live animal and on the carcass before skinning.

units.obligation_text: Such a mark must be between 3 inches (7.5 cm) and 5 inches (12.5 cm) high and wide.
units.actor: the 'M' mark on each such animal
units.action_summary: The mark must be between 3 and 5 inches high and wide.

units.obligation_text: and must be applied to the upper right front shoulder of each animal;
units.actor: the 'M' mark on each such animal / the person applying the mark
units.action_summary: The mark must be applied to the upper right front shoulder of each animal.

units.obligation_text: applied with a freeze brand, hot iron, or other method
units.action_summary: The mark must be applied using a freeze brand, hot iron, or other method.

units.obligation_text: easily visible on the live animal and on the carcass before skinning.
units.actor: the 'M' mark on each such animal / the person applying the mark
units.action_summary: The mark must be easily visible on the live animal and on the carcass before skinning.

title: Importation of Fresh Avocado Fruit from Continental Ecuador Into the Continental United States

units.obligation_text: Fresh avocados (Persea americana Miller), may be imported into the continental United States from continental Ecuador only under the conditions described in this section.
units.actor: importers of fresh avocados from continental Ecuador
units.action_summary: Importation of fresh avocados from continental Ecuador is permitted only under the conditions in this section.

units.obligation_text: The national plant protection organization (NPPO) of Ecuador must provide an operational workplan to APHIS that details the activities that the NPPO of Ecuador will, subject to APHIS' approval of the workplan, carry out to meet the requirements of this section.
units.action_summary: Provide an operational workplan to APHIS detailing activities to meet the section's requirements, subject to APHIS approval.

units.obligation_text: The operational workplan must include and describe the quarantine pest survey intervals and other specific requirements as set forth in this section.
units.action_summary: Include and describe quarantine pest survey intervals and other specific requirements in the operational workplan.

units.obligation_text: Avocados from continental Ecuador may be imported in commercial consignments only.
units.actor: importers of avocados from continental Ecuador
units.action_summary: Importation is permitted only in commercial consignments.

units.obligation_text: All production sites that participate in the export program must be approved by and registered with the NPPO of Ecuador in accordance with the requirements of the operational workplan.
units.actor: production sites participating in the export program
units.action_summary: Be approved by and registered with the NPPO of Ecuador per the operational workplan.

units.obligation_text: The NPPO of Ecuador will visit and inspect the production sites monthly starting 2 months before harvest and continue until the end of the shipping season.
units.action_summary: Visit and inspect production sites monthly beginning 2 months before harvest through the shipping season.

units.obligation_text: APHIS may also monitor the places of production if necessary.
units.action_summary: APHIS is permitted to monitor places of production if necessary.

units.obligation_text: If APHIS or the NPPO of Ecuador finds that a place of production is not complying with the requirements of this section, no fruit from the place of production will be eligible for export to the United States until APHIS and the NPPO of Ecuador conduct an investigation and appropriate remedial actions have been implemented.
units.action_summary: Fruit from noncomplying production sites will be ineligible for export until investigation and remedial actions are completed and agreed.

units.obligation_text: Fallen avocado fruit must be removed from the production site at least once every 7 days, starting 2 months before harvest and continuing through the end of the harvest,
units.action_summary: Remove fallen avocado fruit from the production site at least once every 7 days from 2 months before harvest through the end of harvest.

units.obligation_text: fallen fruit may not be included in field containers of fruit to be packed for export.
units.action_summary: Fallen fruit cannot be included in field containers destined for export packing.

units.obligation_text: At each non-Hass avocado production site, no other host of A. fraterculus, A. serpentina, A. striata, or C. capitata can be grown within 100 meters of the edge of the place of production.
units.action_summary: May not grow other hosts of specified fruit flies within 100 meters of the production site edge.

units.obligation_text: At each non-Hass avocado production site, the NPPO of Ecuador must conduct a fruit fly trapping program beginning at least 2 months before the beginning of harvest and continuing for the duration of the harvest period for the detection of A. fraterculus, A. serpentina, A. striata, and C. capitata in accordance with the operational workplan.
units.action_summary: Conduct a fruit fly trapping program at non-Hass production sites from at least 2 months before harvest through the harvest period per the operational workplan.

units.obligation_text: The NPPO of Ecuador must maintain records of fruit fly detections for each trap in a non-Hass avocado production site and update the records each time the traps are checked.
units.action_summary: Maintain and update records of fruit fly detections for each trap each time traps are checked.

units.obligation_text: The trapping records must be maintained for at least 1 year and provided for APHIS’ review, if requested.
units.action_summary: Keep trapping records for at least one year and provide them to APHIS upon request.

units.obligation_text: If the number of flies per trap per day exceeds levels specified in the operational workplan for more than 2 consecutive weeks, the place of production will be prohibited from exporting avocados to the continental United States until APHIS and the NPPO of Ecuador jointly agree that the risk has been mitigated.
units.action_summary: If fly trap thresholds are exceeded for over 2 weeks, the production site is prohibited from exporting to the U.S. until APHIS and NPPO jointly agree the risk is mitigated.

units.obligation_text: All avocados must be placed in field cartons or containers that are marked to identify the production site from which the consignment of fruit originated.
units.action_summary: Place avocados in field cartons/containers marked to identify the production site of origin.

units.obligation_text: The fruit must either be moved to the packinghouse within 3 hours of harvest or protected from fruit fly infestation until moved.
units.action_summary: Either move the fruit to the packinghouse within 3 hours of harvest or protect it from fruit fly infestation until it is moved.

units.obligation_text: Avocados must be packed for export to the continental United States in pest-exclusionary packinghouses that are approved by and registered with the NPPO of Ecuador in accordance with the requirements of the operational workplan.
units.action_summary: Pack avocados for export in pest-exclusionary packinghouses approved and registered with the NPPO of Ecuador per the operational workplan.

units.obligation_text: The avocados must be packed within 24 hours of harvest in a pest-exclusionary packinghouse in accordance with the requirements of the operational workplan.
units.action_summary: Pack avocados within 24 hours of harvest in a pest-exclusionary packinghouse per the operational workplan.

units.obligation_text: The avocados must be safeguarded by an insect-proof mesh screen or plastic tarpaulin while in transit to the packinghouse and while awaiting packing.
units.action_summary: Safeguard avocados with insect-proof mesh or plastic tarpaulin during transit to the packinghouse and while awaiting packing.

units.obligation_text: The avocados must be packed in insect-proof cartons or containers, or covered with insect-proof mesh or plastic tarpaulin, for transit into the continental United States.
units.action_summary: Pack avocados in insect-proof cartons/containers or cover with insect-proof mesh/tarpaulin for transit to the United States.

units.obligation_text: These safeguards must remain intact until arrival at the port of entry into the continental United States
units.action_summary: Maintain insect-proof safeguards intact until arrival at the U.S. port of entry.

units.obligation_text: or the consignment will be denied entry into the continental United States.
units.action_summary: Consignments for which safeguards are not intact will be denied entry into the United States.

units.obligation_text: All openings to the outside of the packinghouse must be covered by screening with openings of not more than 1.6 mm or by some other barrier that prevents pests from entering.
units.action_summary: Cover all packinghouse openings with screening ≤1.6 mm or another pest-excluding barrier.

units.obligation_text: The packinghouse must have double doors at the entrance to the facility and at the interior entrance to the area where the avocados are packed.
units.action_summary: Maintain double doors at the facility entrance and at the interior entrance to the packing area.

units.obligation_text: During the time the packinghouse is in use for exporting avocados to the continental United States, the packinghouse may only accept avocados from registered approved production sites
units.action_summary: May accept avocados for U.S. export only from registered, approved production sites.

units.obligation_text: the fruit must be segregated from fruit intended for other markets.
units.action_summary: Segregate fruit intended for U.S. export from fruit intended for other markets.

units.obligation_text: The identity and origin of the fruit must be maintained from the packinghouse through export of consignments to the United States.
units.action_summary: Maintain identity and origin information of the fruit from packinghouse through export to the U.S.

units.obligation_text: If the non-Hass variety avocados are ineligible for export under the systems approach due to the place of production exceeding the trapping threshold for fruit flies as established in the operational workplan, they may still be exported, but only after undergoing an APHIS approved treatment in accordance with part 305 of this chapter.
units.action_summary: If ineligible under the systems approach due to exceeding trap thresholds, avocados may still be exported only after APHIS-approved treatment per part 305.

units.obligation_text: Inspectors from the NPPO of Ecuador must inspect a biometric sample of the fruit from each avocado consignment jointly agreed upon by APHIS and the NPPO of Ecuador, following post-harvest processing.
units.actor: inspectors from the NPPO of Ecuador
units.action_summary: Inspect a biometric sample of fruit from each consignment (sample agreed with APHIS) after post-harvest processing.

units.obligation_text: The inspectors must visually inspect for quarantine pests listed in the operational workplan required by paragraph (a) of this section and must cut fruit if signs of quarantine pests that are internal feeders are observed.
units.actor: inspectors from the NPPO of Ecuador
units.action_summary: Visually inspect for listed quarantine pests and cut fruit if signs of internal-feeding quarantine pests are observed.

units.obligation_text: If quarantine pests are detected in this inspection, the consignment will be prohibited entry into the United States unless it is treated with an APHIS-approved quarantine treatment in accordance with part 305 of this chapter.
units.action_summary: Consignments with detected quarantine pests will be denied entry unless treated with an APHIS-approved quarantine treatment per part 305.

units.obligation_text: Fruit presented for inspection at a U.S. port of entry must be identified in the shipping documents accompanying each consignment of fruit that specify the place of production in which the fruit was produced and the packinghouse in which the fruit was processed.
units.action_summary: Provide shipping documents identifying the place of production and the packinghouse for each consignment presented for inspection at a U.S. port.

units.obligation_text: This identification must be maintained until the fruit is released for entry into the continental United States.
units.action_summary: Maintain the identification in shipping documents until the fruit is released for entry into the U.S.

units.obligation_text: Each consignment of avocado fruit must be accompanied by a phytosanitary certificate of inspection issued by the NPPO of Ecuador that states that the fruit in the consignment was produced in accordance with the requirements of § 319.56–84.
units.action_summary: Accompany each consignment with a phytosanitary certificate issued by the NPPO of Ecuador stating production in accordance with § 319.56–84.

title: Approval of Laboratories to Conduct Official Testing; Consolidation of Regulations

units.obligation_text: State, university, and private laboratories must obtain APHIS approval to conduct official testing for those diseases covered by subchapters B, C, and D of this chapter.
units.action_summary: Laboratories must obtain APHIS approval before conducting official testing for covered diseases.

units.obligation_text: Laboratories seeking approval must meet the requirements of this section.
units.action_summary: Applicants for approval must comply with the requirements in § 71.22.

units.obligation_text: Official testing must be performed in laboratory facilities with controlled conditions, instrumentation appropriate for the testing being conducted, and biosecurity measures commensurate with the disease of diagnostic concern.
units.action_summary: Testing must occur in facilities with controlled conditions, appropriate instruments, and commensurate biosecurity.

units.obligation_text: Approved laboratories must agree to periodic, unannounced inspection by APHIS personnel or other APHIS-approved inspectors following an APHIS-approved checklist.
units.action_summary: Approved labs must allow periodic unannounced inspections by APHIS or APHIS-approved inspectors using an APHIS checklist.

units.obligation_text: Laboratories must operate under a quality system acceptable to APHIS.
units.action_summary: Laboratories are required to operate under an APHIS-acceptable quality system.

units.obligation_text: Adherence to certain nationally or internationally established and quality systems recognized by APHIS may be used to meet all or part of this requirement.
units.action_summary: Labs may use recognized national or international quality systems to satisfy the quality system requirement.

units.obligation_text: Quality system records are subject to review during facility inspections.
units.action_summary: Quality system records can be reviewed by inspectors during facility inspections.

units.obligation_text: All official testing must be conducted using APHIS-approved assay methods.
units.action_summary: Official tests must use APHIS-approved assay methods.

units.obligation_text: APHIS-approved assay methods may include standard operating procedures recognized by the National Veterinary Services Laboratories (NVSL) or National Animal Health Laboratory Network, and/or diagnostic test kits licensed by the USDA.
units.action_summary: Acceptable APHIS-approved methods can include NVSL/NAHLN-recognized SOPs or USDA-licensed diagnostic kits.

units.obligation_text: Official testing must be conducted only by those individuals who have completed APHIS-approved training and have passed proficiency tests administered by APHIS or its official designee.
units.actor: Individuals conducting official testing / Laboratories ensuring personnel
units.action_summary: Only individuals with APHIS-approved training and passed APHIS-administered proficiency tests may perform official testing.

units.obligation_text: These tests will be administered annually or as necessary at an interval stipulated by APHIS.
units.action_summary: Proficiency tests will be administered annually or at intervals set by APHIS.

units.obligation_text: Supervisory oversight of official testing must be performed by qualified individuals, as determined by APHIS.
units.action_summary: Supervisory oversight must be provided by individuals determined qualified by APHIS.

units.obligation_text: Approved laboratories must report test results to APHIS and State animal health officials using an individualized (by disease) timeline established by APHIS at the time of laboratory approval.
units.action_summary: Approved labs must report test results to APHIS and State officials on a disease-specific timeline set by APHIS.

units.obligation_text: Laboratories must use APHIS application forms, including an agreement to meet the obligations to APHIS listed in this section, and submit completed forms to the NVSL Director.
units.action_summary: Applicants must use APHIS forms, include an agreement to meet the section's obligations, and submit completed forms to the NVSL Director.

units.obligation_text: If positive, applicants will then be able to request a facility inspection and personnel training, conducted in accordance with this section.
units.action_summary: Applicants with a positive preliminary determination may request facility inspection and personnel training per § 71.22.

units.obligation_text: If negative, APHIS will provide a rationale for the denial.
units.action_summary: If an application is preliminarily denied, APHIS must provide a rationale for the denial.

units.obligation_text: Denied applicants may appeal any denials in accordance with the regulations in paragraph (j) of this section.
units.action_summary: Applicants denied preliminary approval may appeal the denial under paragraph (j).

units.obligation_text: When all requirements in this section have been met, the NVSL Director will issue a final approval.
units.action_summary: The NVSL Director will issue final approval once all section requirements are met.

units.obligation_text: Previously approved laboratories that wish to maintain their approved status must reapply for APHIS approval at least 1 month before their approval term expires, or at least every 2 years, whichever comes first.
units.action_summary: Previously approved labs must reapply at least 1 month before expiration or at least every 2 years to maintain approved status.

units.obligation_text: Laboratories wishing to maintain approved status must submit a renewal application form, as supplied by APHIS, to the NVSL Director.
units.actor: Laboratories wishing to maintain approved status
units.action_summary: Labs must submit APHIS-supplied renewal application forms to the NVSL Director to maintain approved status.

units.obligation_text: Approved laboratories must have at least one individual with the required training and unexpired proficiency certification in their employ at all times.
units.action_summary: Approved labs must always employ at least one person with required training and unexpired proficiency certification.

units.obligation_text: Approved laboratories must perform the minimum number of tests to maintain proficiency, as stipulated by APHIS in the guidance documents developed for individual test types.
units.action_summary: Approved labs must perform the minimum number of tests specified by APHIS guidance to maintain proficiency.

units.obligation_text: Laboratories not conducting the minimum number of tests as required by paragraph (h)(3) of this section during a single reporting period will be assigned probationary status.
units.action_summary: If a lab fails to do the minimum tests in one reporting period, it will be placed on probationary status.

units.obligation_text: Laboratories on probation may continue to conduct official testing.
units.action_summary: Labs placed on probation are permitted to continue conducting official testing.

units.obligation_text: If the minimum required number of tests are not performed during two consecutive reporting periods, the laboratory will not be eligible for renewal of APHIS approval.
units.action_summary: Failure to meet minimum test numbers for two consecutive reporting periods makes a lab ineligible for renewal.

units.obligation_text: Exceptions to this requirement may be granted by the NVSL Director upon request.
units.action_summary: The NVSL Director may grant exceptions to the minimum-test requirement upon request.

units.obligation_text: Approval to conduct official testing will be suspended in the event that a laboratory experiences changes that may impact its ability to provide quality testing services.
units.action_summary: Approval may be suspended if a lab undergoes changes that impact its ability to provide quality testing services.

units.obligation_text: These changes include: No longer employing an individual approved to conduct official testing, a move to different facilities, or a natural disaster that impacts power or water systems.
units.action_summary: Examples of changes triggering suspension include loss of approved personnel, facility relocation, or disaster affecting utilities.

units.obligation_text: Laboratories with suspended status will not be approved to conduct official testing.
units.action_summary: Labs whose approval is suspended are not authorized to conduct official testing.

units.obligation_text: Laboratories will be restored to approved status upon training and/or testing new personnel, successful inspection of new facilities, and/or correction of noncompliance issues.
units.action_summary: A lab's approved status will be reinstated after required training/testing of personnel, successful facility inspection, or correcting noncompliance.

units.obligation_text: Reapproval will involve resubmitting those sections of the application materials required by the NVSL Director.
units.action_summary: Reapproval requires resubmission of specified sections of application materials as required by the NVSL Director.

units.obligation_text: Approval may be rescinded at any time, at the discretion of the NVSL Director, if a laboratory fails to meet its obligations to APHIS, as listed in the agreement signed by the laboratory during the application process.
units.action_summary: The NVSL Director may rescind a lab's approval if the lab fails to meet its agreed obligations.

units.obligation_text: The NVSL Director will issue a notice to the laboratory, providing the justification for the proposed removal.
units.action_summary: The NVSL Director must provide a notice explaining the reasons for proposed removal of approval.

units.obligation_text: Laboratories will have 30 days to respond in writing to the concerns provided before the NVSL Director finalizes the removal decision.
units.action_summary: Labs are given 30 days to submit a written response to concerns before removal is finalized.

units.obligation_text: Appeal of any denial, probation, suspension, or rescission of laboratory approval must be made in writing to the APHIS Administrator or the Administrator’s official designee within 30 days of the laboratory’s receipt of the NVSL Director’s decision.
units.action_summary: Appeals of denials, probation, suspension, or rescission must be submitted in writing to the APHIS Administrator or designee within 30 days of receipt of the NVSL Director's decision.

units.obligation_text: Responses to these appeals will be provided within 60 days of receipt by APHIS.
units.action_summary: APHIS will provide responses to appeals within 60 days of receipt.

title: Animal Welfare; Amendments to Licensing Provisions and to Requirements for Dogs

units.obligation_text: Business hours means a reasonable number of hours between 7 a.m. and 7 p.m. each week of the year, during which inspections by APHIS may be made.
units.action_summary: APHIS may make inspections during defined business hours (7 a.m. to 7 p.m.).

units.obligation_text: No person shall operate as a dealer, exhibitor, or operator of an auction sale, without a valid license, except persons who are exempt from the licensing requirements under paragraph (a)(3) of this section.
units.action_summary: Operating as a dealer/exhibitor/auction operator without a valid license is prohibited, except for exempt persons.

units.obligation_text: A person must be 18 years of age or older to obtain a license.
units.action_summary: Applicants must be at least 18 years old to obtain a license.

units.obligation_text: A person seeking a license shall apply on a form which will be furnished by the Deputy Administrator.
units.action_summary: Applicants must apply using the form provided by the Deputy Administrator.

units.obligation_text: The applicant shall provide the information requested on the application form, including, but not limited to:
units.action_summary: Applicants must provide the requested information on the application form.

units.obligation_text: The name of the person applying for the license;
units.action_summary: Applicant must provide their name on the application.

units.obligation_text: A valid mailing address through which the applicant can be reached at all times;
units.action_summary: Applicant must provide a valid mailing address for contact.

units.obligation_text: A valid address for all premises, facilities, or locations where animals, animal facilities, equipment, and records are held, kept, or maintained;
units.action_summary: Applicant must provide addresses for all premises where animals or related items are kept.

units.obligation_text: The anticipated maximum number of animals on hand at any one time during the period of licensure;
units.action_summary: Applicant must state the maximum number of animals expected at any one time.

units.obligation_text: The anticipated type of animals to be owned, held, maintained, sold, or exhibited, including those animals leased, during the period of licensure, and if the anticipated type of animals includes exotic or wild animals, information and records demonstrating that the applicant has adequate knowledge of and experience with those animals;
units.action_summary: Applicant must list types of animals and, for exotic/wild animals, provide records showing adequate knowledge and experience.

units.obligation_text: If the person is seeking a license as an exhibitor, whether the person intends to exhibit any animal at any location other than the person’s location(s) listed pursuant to paragraph (a)(1)(iii) of this section;
units.action_summary: Exhibitor applicants must disclose intent to exhibit at locations other than their listed premises.

units.obligation_text: Disclosure of any plea of nolo contendere (no contest) or finding of violation of Federal, State, or local laws or regulations pertaining to animal cruelty or the transportation, ownership, neglect, or welfare of animals.
units.action_summary: Applicant must disclose any relevant pleas or findings related to animal laws or welfare.

units.obligation_text: The completed application form, along with a $120 license fee, shall be submitted to the appropriate Animal Care office.
units.action_summary: Applicants must submit the completed form and $120 fee to the appropriate Animal Care office.

units.obligation_text: No person shall have more than one license.
units.action_summary: A person is prohibited from holding more than one license.

units.obligation_text: Licenses are not valid upon change of ownership, location, activities, or animals, and a new license must be obtained.
units.action_summary: When ownership, location, activities, or animals change, the existing license is invalid and a new license must be obtained.

units.obligation_text: A licensee shall notify Animal Care no fewer than 90 days, and obtain a new license, before any change in the name, address, management, substantial control or ownership of his business or operation, locations, activities, and number or type of animals described in paragraph (b)(2) of this section.
units.action_summary: Licensees must notify Animal Care at least 90 days in advance and obtain a new license before specified changes.

units.obligation_text: Any person who is subject to the regulations in this subchapter and who intends to exhibit any animal at any location other than the person’s approved site must provide that information on their application form in accordance with paragraph (a) of this section and submit written itineraries in accordance with § 2.126.
units.action_summary: Persons who will exhibit animals off-site must disclose it on the application and submit written itineraries per §2.126.

units.obligation_text: Licenses authorize increments of 50 animals on hand at any single point in time during the period of licensure. A licensee must obtain a new license before any change resulting in more than the authorized number of animals on hand at any single point in time during the period of licensure.
units.action_summary: Licenses authorize animals in increments of 50; licensees must obtain a new license before exceeding the authorized number.

units.obligation_text: Licenses authorize increments of 50 animals on hand at any single point in time during the period of licensure.
units.action_summary: Licenses are issued in increments authorizing 50 animals each.

units.obligation_text: Licenses authorize the use of animals subject to subparts A through F in part 3 of this subchapter, except that, for animals subject to subparts D and F, licenses must specifically authorize the use of each of the following groups of animals: Group 5 and 6 nonhuman primates, big cats or large felids (lions, tigers, leopards, cheetahs, jaguars, cougars, and any hybrid cross thereof), wolves, bears, and mega-herbivores (elephants, rhinoceroses, hippopotamuses, and giraffes). A licensee must obtain a new license before using any animal beyond those animals authorized under the existing license.
units.actor: license issuer/Deputy Administrator (for authorizations) ; licensee (for obtaining new license)
units.action_summary: Licenses authorize animals per subparts; for certain species the license must specifically authorize them; licensees must obtain a new license before using animals beyond those authorized.

units.obligation_text: A license will be issued to any applicant, except as provided in §§ 2.9 through 2.11, when:
units.action_summary: Licenses are issued when the listed conditions are satisfied (unless exceptions apply).

units.obligation_text: The applicant has met the requirements of this section and §§ 2.2 and 2.3;
units.action_summary: Applicant must meet requirements of §2.1 and §§2.2–2.3 as a condition for license issuance.

units.obligation_text: The applicant has paid a $120 license fee to the appropriate Animal Care office. The applicant may pay the fee by certified check, cashier’s check, personal check, money order, or credit card. An applicant whose check is returned by a bank will be charged a fee of $20 for each returned check. If an applicant’s check is returned, subsequent fees must be paid by certified check, cashier’s check, or money order.
units.action_summary: Applicant must pay the $120 fee; allowed payment methods listed; returned checks incur $20 fee; subsequent fees after a returned check must be paid by certain instruments.
units.modal_raw: has paid / may / will be charged / must

units.obligation_text: The failure of any person to comply with any provision of the Act, or any of the provisions of the regulations or standards in this subchapter, shall constitute grounds for denial of a license or for its suspension or revocation by the Secretary, as provided in the Act.
units.action_summary: Failure to comply with the Act/regulations is grounds for denial, suspension, or revocation of a license.

units.obligation_text: Signing the application form is an acknowledgement that the applicant has reviewed the Act and the regulations and standards and agrees to comply with them.
units.action_summary: By signing the application, the applicant acknowledges review and agrees to comply with the Act and regulations.

units.obligation_text: Each applicant for a license must demonstrate that his or her location(s) and any animals, facilities, vehicles, equipment, or other locations used or intended for use in the business comply with the Act and the regulations and standards set forth in parts 2 and 3 of this subchapter.
units.action_summary: Applicants must demonstrate that their premises, animals, and equipment comply with the Act and regulations.

units.obligation_text: Each applicant must make his or her animals, locations, facilities, vehicles, equipment, and records available for inspection during business hours and at other times mutually agreeable to the applicant and APHIS, to ascertain the applicant’s compliance with the Act and the regulations and standards.
units.action_summary: Applicants must make animals, premises, equipment, and records available for inspection during business hours or other mutually agreeable times.

units.obligation_text: Each applicant for a license must be inspected by APHIS and demonstrate compliance with the Act and the regulations and standards ... before APHIS will issue a license.
units.action_summary: Applicants must undergo APHIS inspection and demonstrate compliance before a license will be issued.

units.obligation_text: If the first inspection reveals that the applicant’s animals, premises, facilities, vehicles, equipment, locations, or records do not meet the applicable requirements of this subchapter, APHIS will advise the applicant of existing deficiencies and the corrective measures that must be completed to come into compliance with the regulations and standards.
units.actor: APHIS (will advise); applicant (must complete corrective measures)
units.action_summary: If deficiencies are found, APHIS will inform the applicant of deficiencies and required corrective measures, which the applicant must complete to achieve compliance.

units.obligation_text: An applicant who fails the first inspection may request up to two more inspections by APHIS to demonstrate his or her compliance with the Act and the regulations and standards. The applicant must request the second inspection, and if applicable, the third inspection, within 60 days following the first inspection.
units.action_summary: Applicants who fail the first inspection may request up to two re-inspections but must request subsequent inspections within 60 days of the first inspection.

units.obligation_text: Any applicant who fails the third and final pre-license inspection may appeal all or part of the inspection findings to the Deputy Administrator. To appeal, the applicant must send a written statement contesting the inspection finding(s) and include any documentation or other information in support of the appeal. To receive consideration, the appeal must be received by the Deputy Administrator within 7 days of the date the applicant received the third pre-license inspection report.
units.action_summary: Applicants who fail the third inspection may appeal by sending a written statement with supporting documentation; the appeal must be received within 7 days of receipt of the inspection report.

units.obligation_text: Within 7 days of receiving a timely appeal, the Deputy Administrator will issue a written response to notify the applicant whether APHIS will issue a license or deny the application.
units.action_summary: Deputy Administrator must issue a written response within 7 days of a timely appeal indicating whether a license will be issued or the application denied.

units.obligation_text: If an applicant fails inspection or fails to request reinspections within the 60-day period, or fails to submit a timely appeal of the third pre-license inspection report as described in paragraph (c) of this section, the applicant will forfeit the application fee and cannot reapply for a license for a period of 6 months from the date of the failed third inspection or the expiration of the time to request a third inspection.
units.action_summary: Failure to request re-inspection or timely appeal results in forfeiture of fee and prohibition from reapplying for 6 months.

units.obligation_text: No license will be issued until the applicant demonstrates upon inspection that the animals, premises, facilities, vehicles, equipment, locations, and records are in compliance with all applicable requirements in the Act and the regulations and standards in this subchapter.
units.action_summary: Licenses will not be issued until APHIS inspection shows full compliance.

units.obligation_text: A license issued under this part shall be valid and effective for 3 years unless: (1) The license has been revoked or suspended pursuant to section 19 of the Act. (2) The license is voluntarily terminated upon request of the licensee, in writing, to the Deputy Administrator. (3) The license has expired, except that: (i) The Deputy Administrator may issue a temporary license that automatically expires after 120 days to an applicant whose immediately preceding 3-year license has expired if: (A) The applicant submits the appropriate application form before the expiration date of a preceding license; and (B) The applicant had no noncompliances ... documented in an inspection report during the preceding period of licensure. (ii) For expedited hearings occurring under § 2.11(b)(2), a license will remain valid and effective until the administrative law judge issues his or her initial decision. Should the administrative law judge’s initial decision affirm the denial of the license application, the applicant’s license shall terminate immediately. (4) There will not be a refund of the license fee if a license is denied, terminated, suspended, or revoked prior to its expiration date.
units.action_summary: License generally valid for 3 years except under listed circumstances: revocation/suspension, voluntary termination, expiration (with possible temporary license issued by Deputy Administrator under conditions), validity during expedited hearing until ALJ decision, and no refund if license ends early.

units.obligation_text: The license is voluntarily terminated upon request of the licensee, in writing, to the Deputy Administrator.
units.action_summary: A licensee may voluntarily terminate a license by submitting a written request to the Deputy Administrator.

units.obligation_text: The Deputy Administrator may issue a temporary license that automatically expires after 120 days ... if: (A) The applicant submits the appropriate application form before the expiration date of a preceding license; and (B) The applicant had no noncompliances ... documented in an inspection report during the preceding period of licensure.
units.actor: Deputy Administrator (may issue temporary license); applicant (must submit application and have no noncompliances)
units.action_summary: Deputy Administrator may issue a 120-day temporary license if applicant applies before expiration and had no documented noncompliances during prior licensure.

units.obligation_text: The applicant submits the appropriate application form before the expiration date of a preceding license;
units.action_summary: Applicant must submit the application before the previous license expires to qualify for a temporary license.

units.obligation_text: The applicant had no noncompliances with the Act and the regulations and standards in parts 2 and 3 of this subchapter documented in an inspection report during the preceding period of licensure.
units.action_summary: To qualify for a temporary license, the applicant must have had no documented noncompliances during the prior licensure period.

units.obligation_text: For expedited hearings occurring under § 2.11(b)(2), a license will remain valid and effective until the administrative law judge issues his or her initial decision. Should the administrative law judge’s initial decision affirm the denial of the license application, the applicant’s license shall terminate immediately.
units.action_summary: During expedited hearings, the applicant's license remains valid until the ALJ's initial decision; if the ALJ affirms denial, the license terminates immediately.

units.obligation_text: There will not be a refund of the license fee if a license is denied, terminated, suspended, or revoked prior to its expiration date.
units.action_summary: No refund of license fee if license ends before expiration due to denial, termination, suspension, or revocation.

units.obligation_text: Any person who seeks the reinstatement of a license that has expired or been terminated must follow the procedure applicable to new applicants for a license set forth in § 2.1.
units.action_summary: To reinstate an expired or terminated license, the person must follow the new applicant procedures in §2.1.

units.obligation_text: A license which is invalid under this part shall be surrendered to the Deputy Administrator. If the license cannot be found, the licensee shall provide a written statement so stating to the Deputy Administrator.
units.action_summary: Invalid licenses must be surrendered to the Deputy Administrator; if lost, the licensee must provide a written statement stating so.

units.obligation_text: Any person who has been or is an officer, agent, or employee of a licensee whose license has been suspended or revoked and who was responsible for or participated in the activity upon which the order of suspension or revocation was based will not be licensed, or registered as a carrier, intermediate handler, exhibitor, or research facility within the period during which the order of suspension or revocation is in effect.
units.actor: person who was officer/agent/employee involved in suspension/revocation activity
units.action_summary: Persons who participated in conduct causing a license suspension/revocation are prohibited from being licensed or registered in relevant roles during the suspension/revocation period.

units.obligation_text: Any person whose license has been suspended for any reason shall not be licensed, or registered, in his or her own name or in any other manner, within the period during which the order of suspension is in effect.
units.action_summary: Persons with suspended licenses are prohibited from being licensed or registered in any manner during the suspension period.

units.obligation_text: No partnership, firm, corporation, or other legal entity in which any such person has a substantial interest, financial or otherwise, will be licensed or registered during that period.
units.actor: partnerships/firms/corporations/other entities with substantial interest by suspended person
units.action_summary: Entities in which a suspended person has substantial interest are prohibited from being licensed or registered during the suspension period.

units.obligation_text: Any person whose license has been suspended for any reason may apply to the Deputy Administrator, in writing, for reinstatement of his or her license.
units.action_summary: Suspended persons may apply in writing to the Deputy Administrator for reinstatement.

units.obligation_text: Any person whose license has been revoked shall not be licensed or registered, in his or her own name or in any other manner, and no partnership, firm, corporation, or other legal entity in which any such person has a substantial interest, financial or otherwise, will be licensed or registered.
units.actor: person whose license is revoked; entities with substantial interest
units.action_summary: Persons with revoked licenses and entities in which they have substantial interest are prohibited from being licensed or registered.

units.obligation_text: Any person whose license has been suspended or revoked shall not buy, sell, transport, exhibit, or deliver for transportation, any animal during the period of suspension or revocation, under any circumstances, whether on his or her behalf or on the behalf another licensee or registrant.
units.actor: person whose license is suspended or revoked
units.action_summary: Persons with suspended or revoked licenses are prohibited from transacting in animals in any manner during suspension or revocation.

units.obligation_text: A license will not be issued to any applicant who:
units.action_summary: General prohibition: licenses will be denied to applicants meeting any of the listed disqualifying conditions.

units.obligation_text: Has not complied with the requirements of §§ 2.1 through 2.4 and has not paid the fees indicated in § 2.1;
units.action_summary: Applicants failing to comply with §§2.1–2.4 or not paying fees will be denied a license.
units.modal_raw: has not complied / has not paid

units.obligation_text: Is not in compliance with the Act or any of the regulations or standards in this subchapter;
units.action_summary: Noncompliant applicants will be denied a license.

units.obligation_text: Has had a license revoked or whose license is suspended, as set forth in § 2.10;
units.action_summary: Applicants who previously had licenses revoked or suspended will be denied a new license under specified rules.

units.obligation_text: Was an officer, agent, or employee of a licensee whose license has been suspended or revoked and who was responsible for or participated in the activity upon which the order of suspension or revocation was based, as set forth in § 2.9;
units.action_summary: Applicants who participated in actions causing a prior suspension/revocation are disqualified from licensing.

units.obligation_text: Has pled nolo contendere (no contest) or has been found to have violated any Federal, State, or local laws or regulations pertaining to animal cruelty within 3 years of application, or after 3 years if the Administrator determines that the circumstances render the applicant unfit to be licensed;
units.action_summary: Applicants with certain convictions/findings within 3 years (or later if Administrator deems unfit) will be denied a license.

units.obligation_text: After 3 years if the Administrator determines that the circumstances render the applicant unfit to be licensed
units.action_summary: Administrator may determine that, even after 3 years, circumstances make the applicant unfit, resulting in denial.

units.obligation_text: Is or would be operating in violation or circumvention of any Federal, State, or local laws;
units.action_summary: Applicants operating (or who would operate) in violation or circumvention of laws will be denied a license.

units.obligation_text: Has made any false or fraudulent statements or provided any false or fraudulent records to the Department or other government agencies, or has pled nolo contendere (no contest) or has been found to have violated any Federal, State, or local laws or regulations pertaining to the transportation, ownership, neglect, or welfare of animals, or is otherwise unfit to be licensed and the Administrator determines that the issuance of a license would be contrary to the purposes of the Act.
units.action_summary: Applicants who made false statements, provided false records, have certain pleas/findings, or are otherwise unfit (per Administrator) will be denied a license.

units.obligation_text: An applicant whose initial license application has been denied may request a hearing in accordance with the applicable rules of practice for the purpose of showing why the application for license should not be denied.
units.action_summary: Applicants denied initially may request a hearing under applicable rules to contest the denial.

units.obligation_text: The denial of an initial license application shall remain in effect until the final legal decision has been rendered.
units.action_summary: License denial remains in effect until a final legal decision is made.
