title: National Poultry Improvement Plan and Auxiliary Provisions

units.obligation_text: The Administrator may pay indemnity and/or compensation for the activities listed in this paragraph (a), as provided in paragraph (b) of this section:
units.action_summary: Administrator may pay indemnity and/or compensation for the listed activities as provided in paragraph (b).

units.obligation_text: Except for poultry that are described by the categories in this paragraph (b), the Administrator is authorized to pay 100 percent of the costs and/or compensation, as determined in accordance with § 56.4, of the activities described in paragraphs (a)(1) through (3) of this section, regardless of whether the infected or exposed poultry participate in the Plan.
units.action_summary: Administrator is authorized to pay 100% of costs/compensation for the listed activities except for certain categorized poultry.

units.obligation_text: For infected or exposed poultry that are described by the categories in this paragraph (b), the Administrator is authorized to pay 25 percent of the costs of the activities described in paragraphs (a)(1) through (3) of this section:
units.action_summary: Administrator is authorized to pay 25% of costs for activities for poultry that meet the specified categories.

units.obligation_text: The poultry are from a breeding flock, commercial flock, or slaughter plant that participates in any Plan program in part 145 or 146 of this chapter but that does not participate in the U.S. Avian Influenza Clean, U.S. H5/H7 Avian Influenza Clean, or U.S. H5/H7 Avian Influenza Monitored program of the Plan available to the flock in part 145 or 146 of this chapter;
units.action_summary: Poultry from flocks that participate in some Plan programs but not the specified Clean/Monitored programs qualify for the 25% payment category.

units.obligation_text: A commercial table-egg laying premises with at least 75,000 birds;
units.action_summary: Premises with at least 75,000 table-egg layers meet a threshold for the 25% payment category.

units.obligation_text: A meat-type chicken slaughter plant that slaughters at least 200,000 meat-type chickens in an operating week;
units.action_summary: Plants slaughtering at least 200,000 chickens in a week meet the threshold for the 25% payment category.

units.obligation_text: A meat-type turkey slaughter plant that slaughters at least 2 million meat-type turkeys in a 12 month period;
units.action_summary: Plants slaughtering at least 2 million turkeys annually meet the threshold for the 25% payment category.

units.obligation_text: A commercial waterfowl and commercial upland game bird slaughter plant that slaughters at least 50,000 birds annually;
units.actor: Commercial waterfowl/upland game bird slaughter plant
units.action_summary: Plants slaughtering at least 50,000 birds annually meet the threshold for the 25% payment category.

units.obligation_text: A raised-for-release upland game bird premises, raised-for-release waterfowl premises, and commercial upland game bird or commercial waterfowl producing eggs for human consumption premises that raise at least 25,000 birds annually;
units.action_summary: Premises raising at least 25,000 birds annually meet the threshold for the 25% payment category.

units.obligation_text: A breeder flock premises with at least 5,000 birds.
units.action_summary: Breeder flock premises with at least 5,000 birds meet the threshold for the 25% payment category.

units.obligation_text: The poultry are located in a State that does not participate in the diagnostic surveillance program for H5/H7 LPAI, as described in § 146.14 of this chapter, or that does not have an initial State response and containment plan for H5/H7 LPAI that is approved by APHIS under § 56.10, unless such poultry participate in the Plan with another State that does participate in the diagnostic surveillance program for H5/H7 LPAI, as described in § 146.14 of this chapter, and has an initial State response and containment plan for H5/H7 LPAI that is approved by APHIS under § 56.10.
units.action_summary: Poultry located in States that do not participate in surveillance or lack an approved response plan (unless covered by another participating State) qualify for the 25% payment category.

units.obligation_text: If the recipient of indemnity and/or compensation for any of the activities listed in paragraphs (a)(1) through (3) of this section also receives payment for any of those activities from a State or from other sources, the indemnity and/or compensation provided under this part may be reduced by the total amount of payment received from the State or other sources to the extent that total payments do not exceed 100 percent of total reimbursable indemnity and/or compensation amounts.
units.action_summary: APHIS may reduce indemnity/compensation by amounts received from other sources so total reimbursements do not exceed 100% of reimbursable amounts.

units.obligation_text: Indemnity for the destruction of poultry and/or eggs infected with or exposed to H5/H7 LPAI will be based on the fair market value of the poultry and/or eggs, as determined by an appraisal.
units.action_summary: Indemnity amounts must be based on fair market value determined by appraisal.

units.obligation_text: The appraisal will use the current APHIS appraisal calculator values; if no such calculator value exists, an APHIS official appraiser will provide an appraisal of fair market value.
units.action_summary: Appraisals must use APHIS calculator values when available; otherwise an APHIS appraiser will provide an appraisal.

units.obligation_text: An indemnity request form must be signed by the owners and grower (if applicable) of the poultry and received by APHIS prior to the destruction of the poultry and eggs, unless the owners, grower, APHIS, and the Cooperating State Agency agree in writing that the poultry may be destroyed immediately.
units.action_summary: Owners/growers must sign and submit an indemnity request form to APHIS before destruction, unless parties agree in writing to immediate destruction.

units.obligation_text: Unless the owners, grower, APHIS, and the Cooperating State Agency agree in writing that the poultry may be destroyed immediately.
units.actor: Owners, grower, APHIS, and the Cooperating State Agency
units.action_summary: If these parties agree in writing, the poultry may be destroyed immediately without prior receipt of the indemnity request form.

units.obligation_text: Reports of appraisals must show the number of birds and the value per head.
units.action_summary: Appraisal reports are required to show number of birds and value per head.

units.obligation_text: Complete inventory records of all birds and/or eggs on the premises must be provided to APHIS prior to the start of depopulation.
units.action_summary: Owners/growers must provide complete inventory records to APHIS before depopulation begins.

units.obligation_text: Compensation for disposal of poultry and/or eggs infected with or exposed to H5/H7 LPAI will be based on receipts or other documentation maintained by the claimant verifying expenditures for disposal activities authorized by this part.
units.action_summary: Compensation for disposal is determined based on claimant's receipts/documentation of authorized disposal expenditures.

units.obligation_text: Any disposal of poultry infected with or exposed to H5/H7 LPAI for which compensation is requested must be performed under a compliance agreement between the claimant and APHIS.
units.action_summary: Disposal for which compensation is requested must be performed under a compliance agreement with APHIS.

units.obligation_text: APHIS will review claims for compensation for disposal to ensure that all expenditures relate directly to activities described in § 56.5 and in the initial State response and containment plan described in § 56.10.
units.action_summary: APHIS will review disposal compensation claims to ensure expenditures relate to authorized activities and approved plans.

units.obligation_text: If disposal is performed by the Cooperating State Agency, APHIS will compensate the Cooperating State Agency for disposal under a cooperative agreement.
units.action_summary: If the Cooperating State Agency performs disposal, APHIS will compensate it under a cooperative agreement.

units.obligation_text: The destruction and disposal of the poultry and/or eggs must be conducted in accordance with the initial State response and containment plan for H5/H7 LPAI, as described in § 56.10.
units.actor: Owners, contractors, and agencies conducting destruction/disposal
units.action_summary: Destruction and disposal must follow the initial State response and containment plan described in §56.10.

units.obligation_text: Compensation for cleaning and disinfection (virus elimination) of premises, conveyances, and materials that came into contact with poultry that are infected with or exposed to H5/H7 LPAI will be determined using the current APHIS flat-rate virus elimination (VE) calculator in effect at the time of the infection.
units.action_summary: Compensation for cleaning/disinfection will be determined using the APHIS flat-rate VE calculator when available.

units.obligation_text: For premises types for which a flat-rate VE calculator is not available, reimbursement will be based on receipts or other documentation maintained by the claimant verifying expenditures for cleaning and disinfection (virus elimination) activities authorized by this part.
units.action_summary: When no flat-rate exists, reimbursement is based on claimant's receipts/documentation of authorized cleaning/disinfection expenditures.

units.obligation_text: Any cleaning and disinfection (virus elimination) of premises, conveyances, and materials for which compensation is requested must be performed under a compliance agreement between the claimant, the Cooperating State Agency, and APHIS.
units.actor: Claimant (and Cooperating State Agency where applicable)
units.action_summary: Cleaning/disinfection for which compensation is requested must be performed under a compliance agreement with APHIS and the Cooperating State Agency.

units.obligation_text: APHIS will review claims for compensation for cleaning and disinfection (virus elimination) to ensure that all expenditures relate directly to activities described in § 56.5 and in the initial State response and containment plan described in § 56.10.
units.action_summary: APHIS will review cleaning/disinfection compensation claims to ensure expenses relate to authorized activities and approved plans.

units.obligation_text: In the case of materials, if the cost of cleaning and disinfection (virus elimination) would exceed the value of the materials or cleaning and disinfection (virus elimination) would be impracticable for any reason, compensation for the destruction of the materials will be based on the fair market value (depreciated value) of those materials, as determined by an appraisal.
units.action_summary: If cleaning is impracticable or costs exceed value, compensation for destruction of materials will be based on fair market (depreciated) value via appraisal.

units.obligation_text: Materials will be appraised by an APHIS official appraiser.
units.action_summary: APHIS official appraiser will appraise materials.

units.obligation_text: Compensation for disposal of the materials will be based on receipts or other documentation maintained by the claimant verifying expenditures for disposal activities authorized by this part.
units.action_summary: Compensation for disposal of materials is determined based on claimant's receipts/documentation.

units.obligation_text: Appraisals of materials must be reported on forms furnished by APHIS and must be signed by the appraisers and by the owners of the materials to indicate agreement with the appraisal amount.
units.action_summary: Appraisals must be reported on APHIS forms and signed by appraisers and owners to indicate agreement.

units.obligation_text: Appraisals of materials must be signed and received by APHIS prior to the disassembly or destruction of the materials, unless the owners, APHIS, and the Cooperating State Agency agree in writing that the materials may be disassembled and/or destroyed immediately.
units.action_summary: Appraisals must be signed and received by APHIS before disassembly/destruction unless parties agree in writing to immediate disassembly/destruction.

units.obligation_text: Unless the owners, APHIS, and the Cooperating State Agency agree in writing that the materials may be disassembled and/or destroyed immediately.
units.actor: Owners, APHIS, and the Cooperating State Agency
units.action_summary: If these parties agree in writing, materials may be disassembled/destroyed immediately without prior receipt of appraisals by APHIS.

units.obligation_text: Any disposal of materials for which compensation is requested must be performed under a compliance agreement between the claimant, the Cooperating State Agency, and APHIS.
units.actor: Claimant (and Cooperating State Agency where applicable)
units.action_summary: Disposal of materials for which compensation is requested must be performed under a compliance agreement with APHIS and the Cooperating State Agency.

units.obligation_text: APHIS will review claims for compensation for disposal to ensure that all expenditures relate directly to activities described in § 56.5 and in the initial State response and containment plan described in § 56.10.
units.action_summary: APHIS will review material disposal compensation claims to ensure expenditures relate to authorized activities and approved plans.

units.obligation_text: The compliance agreement is a comprehensive document that describes the depopulation, disposal, and cleaning and disinfection (virus elimination) plans for poultry that were infected with or exposed to H5/H7 LPAI, or a premises that contained such poultry. The compliance agreement must set out cost estimates that include labor, materials, supplies, equipment, personal protective equipment, and any additional information deemed necessary by APHIS.
units.action_summary: Compliance agreements must set out cost estimates including labor, materials, equipment, PPE, and any additional APHIS-deemed necessary information.

units.obligation_text: A compliance agreement must indicate what tasks will be completed, who will be responsible for each task, and how much the work is expected to cost.
units.action_summary: Compliance agreements must identify tasks, responsible parties, and estimated costs.

units.obligation_text: Once work associated with the compliance agreement is completed, receipts and documentation detailing the activities specified in the agreement should be forwarded to APHIS for review, approval, and final payment.
units.action_summary: After completing work under a compliance agreement, receipts and documentation should be forwarded to APHIS for review, approval, and payment.

units.obligation_text: This documentation should be submitted to APHIS no later than 30 days after the quarantine release of the affected or exposed premises.
units.action_summary: Documentation should be submitted to APHIS within 30 days after quarantine release.

units.obligation_text: Poultry moved for controlled marketing will not be eligible for indemnity under § 56.3.
units.actor: Poultry moved for controlled marketing / their owners
units.action_summary: Poultry moved for controlled marketing are ineligible for indemnity under §56.3.

units.obligation_text: However, any costs related to cleaning and disinfection (virus elimination) of premises, conveyances, and materials that came into contact with poultry that are moved for controlled marketing will be eligible for compensation under § 56.3.
units.action_summary: Cleaning/disinfection costs for premises/conveyances/materials associated with poultry moved for controlled marketing are eligible for compensation under §56.3.

units.obligation_text: Premises, conveyances, and materials that came into contact with poultry infected with or exposed to H5/H7 LPAI must be cleaned and disinfected;
units.actor: Owners, operators, or responsible parties of premises/conveyances/materials
units.action_summary: Premises, conveyances, and materials exposed to infected or exposed poultry must be cleaned and disinfected.

units.obligation_text: Provided, that materials for which the cost of cleaning and disinfection would exceed the value of the materials or for which cleaning and disinfection would be impracticable for any reason may be destroyed and disposed.
units.action_summary: Materials for which cleaning is impracticable or costs exceed value may be destroyed and disposed.

units.obligation_text: Cleaning and disinfection must be performed in accordance with the initial State response and containment plan described in § 56.10, which must be approved by APHIS.
units.actor: Owners, operators, and those performing cleaning/disinfection; APHIS for approval
units.action_summary: Cleaning/disinfection must follow the initial State response and containment plan, and that plan must be approved by APHIS.

units.obligation_text: Cleaning and disinfection must also be performed in accordance with any applicable State and local environmental regulations.
units.actor: Owners, operators, and those performing cleaning/disinfection
units.action_summary: Cleaning/disinfection must comply with applicable State and local environmental regulations.

units.obligation_text: If indemnity for the destroyed poultry or eggs is being provided for 100 percent of eligible costs under § 56.3(b), the Administrator may pay contractors eligible for indemnity under this section 100 percent of the amount determined in paragraph (a) of this section.
units.action_summary: If indemnity covers 100% of eligible costs, Administrator may pay eligible contractors 100% of the amount determined under paragraph (a).

units.obligation_text: If indemnity for the destroyed poultry or eggs is being provided for 25 percent of eligible costs under § 56.3(b), the Administrator may pay contractors eligible for indemnity 25 percent of the amount determined in paragraph (a) of this section.
units.action_summary: If indemnity covers 25% of eligible costs, Administrator may pay eligible contractors 25% of the amount determined under paragraph (a).

units.obligation_text: Dealers in hatching eggs, newly hatched poultry, or started poultry shall comply with the provisions in this part (within the NPIP Program Standards document, Program Standard C applies to hatcheries; alternatives to the program standards may also be approved by the Administrator under § 147.53).
units.actor: Dealers in hatching eggs, newly hatched poultry, or started poultry
units.action_summary: Dealers must comply with the provisions of this part and applicable NPIP Program Standards (with possible Administrator-approved alternatives).

units.obligation_text: The ELISA test must be conducted using test kits approved by the Department and the Official State Agency and must be conducted in accordance with the recommendations of the producer or manufacturer.
units.action_summary: ELISA testing must use Department- and Official State Agency-approved kits and follow manufacturer/producer recommendations.

units.obligation_text: When positive ELISA samples are identified, an AGID test must be conducted within 48 hours.
units.action_summary: An AGID test must be conducted within 48 hours when ELISA samples are positive.

units.obligation_text: The AGID test must be conducted using reagents approved by the Department and the Official State Agency.
units.action_summary: AGID tests must use Department- and Official State Agency-approved reagents.

units.obligation_text: The AGID test for avian influenza must be conducted in accordance with this section (within the NPIP Program Standards document, Program Standard A applies to blood and yolk testing procedures; alternatives to the program standards may also be approved by the Administrator under § 147.53) for the avian influenza agar gel immunodiffusion (AGID) test.
units.action_summary: AGID testing for avian influenza must be conducted in accordance with the specified section and applicable NPIP Program Standards.

units.obligation_text: Positive tests for the AGID must be further tested by Federal Reference Laboratories using appropriate tests for confirmation.
units.action_summary: Federal Reference Laboratories must further test positive AGID results with appropriate confirmatory tests.

units.obligation_text: Final judgment may be based upon further sampling and appropriate tests for confirmation.
units.action_summary: Final determination may consider further sampling and confirmatory tests.

units.obligation_text: Agent detection tests may be used to detect influenza A virus but not to determine hemagglutinin or neuraminidase subtypes.
units.action_summary: Agent detection tests are permitted for detecting influenza A but not for determining HA or NA subtypes.

units.obligation_text: Samples for agent detection testing should be collected from naturally occurring flock mortality or clinically ill birds.
units.action_summary: Samples for agent detection testing should preferably come from mortality events or clinically ill birds.

units.obligation_text: During each 90-day period, all multiplier spent fowl, up to a maximum of 30, must be tested and found negative for avian influenza within 21 days prior to movement to slaughter.
units.action_summary: Up to 30 multiplier spent fowl per 90-day period must be tested and found negative for AI within 21 days before movement to slaughter.

units.obligation_text: A flock and the hatching eggs and poults produced from it will qualify for the classification in this paragraph (h) when the Official State Agency determines that they have met the following requirements:
units.actor: Official State Agency (and flock owners to meet requirements)
units.action_summary: Flocks qualify for U.S. Newcastle Disease Clean classification when the Official State Agency determines they meet the enumerated requirements.

units.obligation_text: It is a primary breeding flock that is either: (i) Vaccinated for Newcastle disease using USDA-licensed vaccines and response to vaccination is serologically monitored using an approved test as described in § 145.14 when more than 4 months of age, and meets the criteria in paragraph (h)(2) of this section to retain classification;
units.action_summary: Primary breeding flocks may qualify if vaccinated with USDA-licensed vaccines and serologically monitored using approved tests, and they meet retention criteria.
units.modal_raw: must be vaccinated / must be monitored

units.obligation_text: (ii) Unvaccinated for Newcastle disease, in which a minimum of 30 birds have tested negative to ND using an approved test as described in § 145.14 when more than 4 months of age and meets the criteria in paragraph (h)(3) of this section to retain classification.
units.action_summary: Unvaccinated primary breeding flocks may qualify if at least 30 birds test negative on approved ND tests when >4 months old and meet retention criteria.

units.obligation_text: Vaccines for ND must be USDA-licensed vaccines administered during early stages of development through rearing, and inactivated vaccines as final vaccination prior to the onset of egg production;
units.action_summary: ND vaccines must be USDA-licensed and administered during development through rearing, with inactivated vaccine as final vaccination before egg production.

units.obligation_text: The flock has been monitored for antibody response using approved serological tests as listed in § 145.14 and the results are compatible with immunological response against ND vaccination;
units.action_summary: Flocks must be monitored for antibody response using approved serological tests and show results compatible with vaccination response.

units.obligation_text: Testing must include a minimum of 30 birds with a serologic monitoring program when more than 4 months of age and prior to the onset of production and not longer than every 90 days thereafter.
units.action_summary: Serologic monitoring must include at least 30 birds when >4 months old and prior to production, and testing interval must be no longer than every 90 days.

units.obligation_text: A minimum of 30 birds per flock must test negative using an approved test in § 145.14 at intervals of 90 days;
units.action_summary: Unvaccinated flocks must have at least 30 birds test negative on approved tests every 90 days.

units.obligation_text: A sample of fewer than 30 birds may be tested, and found negative, at any one time if all pens are equally represented and a total of 30 birds is tested within each 90-day period;
units.action_summary: Owners may test fewer than 30 birds at one time if all pens are equally represented and a total of 30 birds is tested within each 90-day period.

units.obligation_text: During each 90-day period, all primary spent fowl, up to a maximum of 30, must test negative to ND within 21 days prior to movement to slaughter.
units.action_summary: All primary spent fowl (up to 30) must test negative to ND within 21 days before movement to slaughter during each 90-day period.

units.obligation_text: Newcastle disease must be a disease reportable to the responsible State authority (State veterinarian, etc.) by all licensed veterinarians.
units.action_summary: Licensed veterinarians must report ND to the responsible State authority.

units.obligation_text: All laboratories (private, State, and university laboratories) that perform diagnostic procedures on poultry must examine all submitted cases of unexplained respiratory disease, egg production drops, and mortality for ND.
units.action_summary: Laboratories must examine all submitted cases of unexplained respiratory disease, egg production drops, and mortality for Newcastle disease.

units.obligation_text: Participating flocks of hobbyist and exhibition poultry, raised-for-release waterfowl, and the eggs, chicks, started, and mature poultry produced from them shall comply with the applicable general provisions of subpart A of this part and the special provisions of this subpart.
units.action_summary: Participating flocks must comply with the general provisions of subpart A and the special provisions of this subpart.

units.obligation_text: All participating raised-for-release waterfowl flocks, regardless of whether they are breeders or non-breeders, shall be enrolled under this subpart.
units.actor: Participating raised-for-release waterfowl flocks / their owners
units.action_summary: All participating raised-for-release waterfowl flocks must be enrolled under this subpart regardless of breeder status.

units.obligation_text: Hatcheries must be kept in a sanitary condition as applicable and as outlined in § 145.6 (within the NPIP Program Standards document, Program Standard C applies to hatcheries; alternatives to the program standards may also be approved by the Administrator under § 147.53).
units.action_summary: Hatcheries must be maintained in a sanitary condition as applicable and as outlined in §145.6 and relevant NPIP Program Standards.

units.obligation_text: An Authorized Agent shall collect and submit to an authorized laboratory: A minimum of five samples from the hatchery at least every 30 days while in operation.
units.action_summary: An Authorized Agent must collect and submit at least five hatchery samples to an authorized laboratory every 30 days while the hatchery is operating.

units.obligation_text: These samples may include: Hatchery debris, swabs from hatchers, setters, hatchery environment, hatchery equipment, sexing tables and belts, meconium, chick box papers, hatching trays, or chick transfer devices. Samples will be examined bacteriologically at an authorized laboratory for Salmonella;
units.actor: Authorized laboratories (and Authorized Agent for sample selection)
units.action_summary: Collected hatchery samples will be examined bacteriologically for Salmonella at an authorized laboratory; sample types are listed.

units.obligation_text: Annual environmental samples from each pullet and breeder farm in accordance with this section ... Samples will be examined bacteriologically at an authorized laboratory for Salmonella.
units.action_summary: Authorized Agent must collect annual environmental samples from each pullet/breeder farm; authorized labs will examine them bacteriologically for Salmonella.

units.obligation_text: A qualified poultry health professional knowledgeable with the operation will be consulted and will: (A) Review test results to evaluate the Salmonella monitoring program.
units.action_summary: A qualified poultry health professional will be consulted to review Salmonella test results and evaluate the monitoring program.

units.obligation_text: (B) Use the Salmonella monitoring program test results to develop appropriate and practical Salmonella intervention measures.
units.action_summary: The qualified poultry health professional will use test results to develop appropriate Salmonella intervention measures.

units.obligation_text: To claim products are of the classification in this paragraph (f), all products shall be derived from a farm or hatchery that meets the requirements of the classification.
units.action_summary: Products claiming the U.S. Salmonella Monitored classification must come from farms/hatcheries that meet the classification requirements.

units.obligation_text: A flock and the hatching eggs and chicks produced from it will qualify for the classification in this paragraph (h) when the Official State Agency determines that they have met the following requirements:
units.actor: Official State Agency (and flock owners to meet requirements)
units.action_summary: Flocks qualify for U.S. Newcastle Disease Clean classification for chickens when the Official State Agency determines they meet the enumerated requirements.

units.obligation_text: It is a primary breeding flock that is either: (i) Vaccinated for Newcastle disease using USDA-licensed vaccines and response to vaccination is serologically monitored using an approved test as described in § 145.14 when more than 4 months of age and meets the criteria in paragraph (h)(2) of this section to retain classification; or
units.action_summary: Primary breeding flocks may qualify if vaccinated with USDA-licensed vaccines and serologically monitored using approved tests and meet retention criteria.
units.modal_raw: must be vaccinated / must be monitored

units.obligation_text: (ii) Unvaccinated for Newcastle disease, in which a minimum of 30 birds have tested negative to ND using an approved test as described in § 145.14 when more than 4 months of age and meets criteria in paragraph (h)(3) of this section to retain classification.
units.action_summary: Unvaccinated primary breeding flocks may qualify if at least 30 birds test negative on approved ND tests when >4 months old and meet retention criteria.

units.obligation_text: Vaccines for ND must be USDA-licensed vaccines administered during early stages of development through rearing, and inactivated vaccines as final vaccination prior to the onset of egg production;
units.action_summary: ND vaccines must be USDA-licensed and administered during development through rearing, with inactivated vaccine as final vaccination before egg production for vaccinated flocks.

units.obligation_text: The flock has been monitored for antibody response using approved serological tests as listed in § 145.14 and the results are compatible with immunological response against ND vaccination; and
units.action_summary: Flocks must be monitored for antibody response with approved serological tests and show compatible results.

units.obligation_text: Testing must include a minimum of 30 birds with a serologic monitoring program when more than 4 months of age and prior to the onset of production and not longer than every 90 days thereafter.
units.action_summary: Serologic monitoring must include at least 30 birds when >4 months old and prior to production, and occur at intervals not longer than 90 days.

units.obligation_text: A minimum of 30 birds per flock must test negative using an approved test as described in § 145.14 at intervals of 90 days; or
units.action_summary: Unvaccinated flocks must have at least 30 birds test negative on approved tests every 90 days.

units.obligation_text: A sample of fewer than 30 birds may be tested, and found negative, at any one time if all pens are equally represented and a total of 30 birds is tested within each 90-day period; and
units.action_summary: Owners may test fewer than 30 birds at once if pens are equally represented, provided 30 birds are tested within each 90-day period.

units.obligation_text: During each 90-day period, all primary spent fowl, up to a maximum of 30, must test negative to ND within 21 days prior to movement to slaughter.
units.action_summary: During each 90-day period, up to 30 primary spent fowl must test negative to ND within 21 days prior to slaughter movement.

units.obligation_text: Newcastle disease must be a disease reportable to the responsible State authority (State veterinarian, etc.) by all licensed veterinarians. To accomplish this, all laboratories (private, State, and university laboratories) that perform diagnostic procedures on poultry must examine all submitted cases of unexplained respiratory disease, egg production drops, and mortality for ND.
units.actor: Licensed veterinarians and laboratories performing diagnostic procedures
units.action_summary: Licensed veterinarians must report ND to State authorities, and laboratories must examine relevant submitted cases for ND.

title: Amendments to the Pale Cyst Nematode Regulations

units.obligation_text: You may submit comments by either of the following methods: Federal eRulemaking Portal; Postal Mail/Commercial Delivery
units.action_summary: Persons are permitted to submit comments via the Federal eRulemaking Portal or by postal mail/commercial delivery.

units.obligation_text: Federal eRulemaking Portal: Go to http://www.regulations.gov/#!docketDetail;D=APHIS-2018-0041
units.action_summary: Commenters may use the Federal eRulemaking Portal to submit comments to Docket APHIS-2018-0041.

units.obligation_text: Postal Mail/Commercial Delivery: Send your comment to Docket No. APHIS-2018-0041, Regulatory Analysis and Development, PPD, APHIS, Station 3A-03.8, 4700 River Road, Unit 118, Riverdale, MD 20737-1238
units.action_summary: Commenters may submit comments by postal mail or commercial delivery to the specified APHIS address.

units.obligation_text: We will consider all comments that we receive on or before July 6, 2020
units.action_summary: APHIS will consider all comments received by July 6, 2020.

units.obligation_text: The PCN program protocols include requirements for pressure washing or using steam to clean all farm equipment, vehicles, or other conveyances that have been in a PCN infested or associated field
units.actor: owners/operators of farm equipment and vehicles
units.action_summary: Equipment, vehicles, and other conveyances that have been in PCN-infested or associated fields must be cleaned by pressure washing or steam.

units.obligation_text: Pressure washing sanitation requirements ... are implemented for all equipment in contact with field soil
units.action_summary: Sanitation requirements (pressure washing) must be applied to all equipment that contacts field soil.

units.obligation_text: Specimens from a soil sample must be definitively identified and confirmed by an APHIS-approved laboratory using morphological and molecular DNA-based methods
units.action_summary: APHS-approved labs are required to definitively identify and confirm soil sample specimens using morphological and DNA methods.

units.obligation_text: The technical minimum threshold for declaring a field infested/positive for PCN is met by detecting a minimum of two cysts from two samples that were identified as PCN by morphological/morphometric analysis, and at least one of the cysts was viable and confirmed as PCN by molecular (DNA) analysis
units.action_summary: A field is considered infested if at least two cysts are detected from two samples identified morphologically, with at least one cyst viability confirmed by DNA analysis.

units.obligation_text: Associated fields are required to undergo two surveys at the delimiting rate, each following a host crop
units.action_summary: Associated fields must undergo two delimiting-rate surveys, each conducted after a host crop harvest.

units.obligation_text: A series of two negative delimiting surveys, each following harvest of two host crops grown on the field, is required to deregulate an associated field
units.action_summary: An associated field must have two consecutive negative delimiting surveys (each after a host crop harvest) to be deregulated.

units.obligation_text: Fields that APHIS has determined to be infested with PCN are eligible for release under a deregulation protocol if the field is used for host crop production
units.action_summary: Infested fields used for host crop production may be released under a deregulation protocol (subject to protocol conditions).

units.obligation_text: A field is eligible for full deregulation if no viable cysts are detected after each of three host crops are harvested
units.action_summary: To achieve full deregulation, a field must show no viable cysts after harvest of each of three consecutive host crops.

units.obligation_text: In the Infested Field Deregulation Protocol, APHIS conducts an initial full field survey in a fixed grid pattern at an 80,000 cc of soil per acre sampling rate
units.action_summary: APHIS will perform an initial full-field fixed-grid survey at 80,000 cc/acre sampling rate for infested fields.

units.obligation_text: The infested field monitoring survey rate is 80,000 cc/ac
units.action_summary: The monitoring survey rate for infested fields is specified as 80,000 cc per acre.

units.obligation_text: The infested field in-field bioassay rate is 20,000 cc/ac
units.action_summary: The in-field bioassay sampling rate for infested fields is specified as 20,000 cc per acre.

units.obligation_text: After sampling results are determined, a field may undergo a series of optional, PCN program-sponsored eradication treatments, which are monitored according to initial grid survey results
units.action_summary: Fields may receive optional PCN program-sponsored eradication treatments, monitored based on initial grid survey outcomes.

units.obligation_text: These treatments are conducted at the discretion of the grower
units.action_summary: Growers have discretion to decide whether to undertake eradication treatments.
units.modal_raw: are conducted at the discretion of

units.obligation_text: To become deregulated, fields no longer in host crop production must complete a two-step process
units.action_summary: Fields out of host crop production must complete a specified two-step process to be deregulated.

units.obligation_text: Records must be made available to APHIS to demonstrate that the land has been out of host crop production for the last 30 years
units.action_summary: Owners must provide records to APHIS showing the land has not had host crop production for 30 years.

units.obligation_text: APHIS then surveys the entire field at a rate of 8,000 cc soil per acre
units.action_summary: APHIS will survey the entire field at 8,000 cc per acre as part of deregulation for lands out of host production.

units.obligation_text: To become deregulated, fields converted to non-agricultural uses must have records available to determine the land has been out of agricultural use for at least the last 20 years and will not return to production, or construction for non-agricultural purposes has rendered the land non-tillable and is not likely to return to agricultural production
units.action_summary: Owners of lands converted to non-agricultural uses must provide records showing at least 20 years out of agricultural use and that the land will not return to production (or that construction makes it non-tillable).

units.obligation_text: A deregulation option exists for regulated fields where agriculture still occurs but where all host crop production was prohibited or has ceased for a minimum of 30 years
units.action_summary: Fields where host crop production has been prohibited or ceased for 30 years may be eligible for a deregulation option.

units.obligation_text: A deregulation option also exists for regulated fields that have been converted to non-agricultural uses
units.action_summary: Regulated fields converted to non-agricultural use may qualify for deregulation under specified conditions.

units.obligation_text: Every precaution should be taken to prevent the spread of potato cyst nematodes
units.actor: persons working in the fields / stakeholders
units.action_summary: Field workers and stakeholders are advised to take all reasonable precautions to prevent spreading PCN.

title: Animal Welfare Act Research Facility Registration Updates, Reviews, and Reports

units.obligation_text: Each research facility, other than a Federal research facility, shall register with the Secretary by completing and filing a properly executed form which will be furnished, upon request, by the Deputy Administrator.
units.actor: each research facility (other than a Federal research facility)
units.action_summary: Register with the Secretary by completing and filing the prescribed form furnished by the Deputy Administrator.

units.obligation_text: The registration form shall be filed with the Deputy Administrator.
units.action_summary: File the registration form with the Deputy Administrator.

units.obligation_text: Except as provided in paragraph (a)(2) of this section, where a school or department of a university or college uses or intends to use live animals for research, tests, experiments, or teaching, the university or college rather than the school or department will be considered the research facility and will be required to register with the Secretary.
units.actor: university or college (when a school/department uses or intends to use live animals)
units.action_summary: Be considered the research facility and register with the Secretary (in cases where a school/department of a university uses or intends to use live animals).

units.obligation_text: An official who has the legal authority to bind the parent organization shall sign the registration form.
units.actor: an official who has the legal authority to bind the parent organization
units.action_summary: Sign the registration form.

units.obligation_text: A research facility shall notify the Deputy Administrator by certified mail of any change in the name, address, or ownership, or other change in operations affecting its status as a research facility, within 10 days after making such change.
units.action_summary: Notify the Deputy Administrator by certified mail of any change in name, address, ownership, or other operational changes affecting facility status within 10 days of the change.

units.obligation_text: The Notification of Change form (APHIS Form 7033) may be used to provide the information.
units.actor: research facilities or persons providing notification
units.action_summary: May use APHIS Form 7033 to provide the required change-of-operation information.

units.obligation_text: A research facility that goes out of business or ceases to function as a research facility, or that changes its method of operation so that it no longer uses, handles, or transports animals, and does not plan to use, handle, or transport animals at any time in the future, may have its registration canceled by making a written request to the Deputy Administrator.
units.actor: a research facility that meets the described conditions
units.action_summary: May have its registration canceled by submitting a written request to the Deputy Administrator if it ceases operations or no longer uses/handles/transports animals and does not plan to in the future.

units.obligation_text: The Deputy Administrator may cancel the registration on its own, without a written request from the research facility.
units.action_summary: May cancel a facility's registration on the Deputy Administrator's own initiative without a written request.

units.obligation_text: If the Deputy Administrator has reason to believe that a research facility has ceased to function as a research facility, then the Deputy Administrator may cancel the registration on its own, without a written request from the research facility.
units.action_summary: If the Deputy Administrator has reason to believe a facility has ceased functioning, the Deputy Administrator may cancel its registration without a written request.

units.obligation_text: The facility is responsible for submitting a form to reregister at least 10 days prior to it using, handling, or transporting animals.
units.actor: the facility (research facility that resumes operation or wishes to conduct regulated activities)
units.action_summary: Submit a reregistration form at least 10 days before resuming use, handling, or transportation of animals.

units.obligation_text: If a research facility resumes operation or otherwise wishes to conduct regulated activities in the future, the facility is responsible for submitting a form to reregister at least 10 days prior to it using, handling, or transporting animals.
units.actor: the facility (research facility that resumes operation or wishes to conduct regulated activities)
units.action_summary: When the facility resumes operations or wishes to conduct regulated activities, it must reregister at least 10 days before using/handling/transporting animals.

units.obligation_text: The IACUC shall conduct complete reviews of activities covered by this subchapter at appropriate intervals as determined by the IACUC, but not less than every 3 years.
units.actor: the Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC)
units.action_summary: Conduct complete reviews of covered activities at intervals determined by the IACUC, at least once every 3 years.

units.obligation_text: The IACUC shall be provided a written description of all proposed activities that involve the care and use of animals for review and approval at the end of the term;
units.actor: persons proposing activities / the research facility (implied providers of proposed-activity information)
units.action_summary: Provide the IACUC with a written description of all proposed activities involving animal care and use for review and approval at the end of the term.

units.obligation_text: The reporting facility shall be that segment of the research facility, or that department, agency, or instrumentality of the United States that uses or intends to use live animals in research, tests, experiments, or for teaching.
units.action_summary: Be defined as the segment/department/agency/instrumentality of the entity that uses or intends to use live animals for research/testing/teaching.

units.obligation_text: Each reporting facility shall submit an annual report to the Deputy Administrator on or before December 1 of each calendar year.
units.action_summary: Submit an annual report to the Deputy Administrator by December 1 each calendar year.

units.obligation_text: The report shall cover the previous Federal fiscal year.
units.actor: each reporting facility (as preparer of the report)
units.action_summary: Ensure the annual report covers the previous Federal fiscal year.

units.obligation_text: The Annual Report of Research Facility (APHIS Form 7023), Continuation Sheet for Annual Report of Research Facility (APHIS Form 7023A), and Annual Report of Research Facility Column E Explanation (APHIS Form 7023B) are forms which may be used to submit the information required by paragraph (b) of this section.
units.actor: reporting facilities or persons submitting the report
units.action_summary: May use APHIS Forms 7023, 7023A, and 7023B to submit the information required by paragraph (b).

title: Horse Protection: Licensing of Designated Qualified Persons and Other Amendments

units.obligation_text: The Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service is withdrawing the proposed rule published July 26, 2016 (81 FR 49112-49137) as of December 13, 2021.
units.actor: Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service (APHIS)
units.action_summary: APHIS withdraws the July 26, 2016 proposed rule effective December 13, 2021.

units.obligation_text: We are withdrawing the July 26, 2016 proposed rule referenced above, and will issue a new proposed rule that incorporates more recent findings and recommendations, including the NAS report.
units.actor: Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service (APHIS) / we
units.action_summary: APHIS will issue a new proposed rule that incorporates recent findings and recommendations (including the NAS report).

title: Import Regulations for Horses

units.obligation_text: Shipping containers used to transport live equine(s) to the United States must meet the following requirements:
units.actor: shipping containers used to transport live equine(s) / persons arranging transport
units.action_summary: Shipping containers for live equines must comply with the listed requirements.

units.obligation_text: Containers must be new or cleaned and disinfected in a manner that sufficiently reduces the risk of introduction or dissemination of any pests or diseases of livestock into the United States.
units.action_summary: Containers must be new or properly cleaned and disinfected to reduce disease/pest risk.

units.obligation_text: Containers must be of sufficient size and construction to reasonably assure that live equine(s) are transported safely.
units.action_summary: Containers must be appropriately sized and constructed to transport horses safely.

units.obligation_text: Stocking density of live equine(s) must not be to an extent that impinges on the animals’ safety during transportation.
units.action_summary: Stocking density must not compromise the animals' safety.

units.obligation_text: Guidance on how to meet these requirements may be found in the Live Animal Regulations (LAR), as amended, published by the International Air Transport Association (IATA). The Administrator may also approve alternative guidance than that described in the LAR.
units.action_summary: Guidance may be found in the IATA LAR; the Administrator may approve alternative guidance.

units.obligation_text: No litter or manure, fodder or other aliment, nor any equipment such as boxes, buckets, ropes, chains, blankets, or other things used for or about horses governed under any law or regulation administered by the Secretary of Agriculture for prevention of the introduction or dissemination of any pests or diseases of livestock, shall be landed from any conveyance except under such restrictions as the inspector in charge at the port of entry shall direct.
units.action_summary: Landing of horse-related articles from conveyances is prohibited except under restrictions directed by the port inspector.

units.obligation_text: except under such restrictions as the inspector in charge at the port of entry shall direct.
units.actor: inspector in charge at the port of entry
units.action_summary: Inspector may direct restrictions under which such articles may be landed.

units.obligation_text: For Spanish Pure Breed horses, the horses have been in Spain for a minimum of 60 days immediately prior to export; for racing thoroughbreds residing in France, Germany, Ireland and/or the United Kingdom, the horses have been in one or a combination of these countries for a minimum of 60 days immediately prior to export;
units.action_summary: Horses must have been in specified country(ies) for at least 60 days immediately prior to export.

units.obligation_text: Horses offered for importation from any part of the world shall be accompanied by an original certificate endorsed by a salaried veterinary officer of the national government of the region of origin ... and shows that:
units.action_summary: Horses must be accompanied by an original certificate endorsed by a salaried veterinary officer of the exporting national government.

units.obligation_text: The certificate shall specify the name and address of the importer; the species, breed, number or quantity of horses or horse test specimens to be imported; the purpose of the importation; individual horse identification which requires a description of the horse, name, age, markings and, when present, registration number, tattoo, microchip, eartag, brand, if any; the region and premises of origin; the name and address of the exporter; and the destination address for release into the United States;
units.actor: issuing authority / certificate issuer (national government salaried veterinary officer)
units.action_summary: The certificate must include importer/exporter details, horse identification, origin, destination, and purpose.

units.obligation_text: The horses described in the certificate have been in said region during the 60 days preceding exportation, or, for horses described in § 93.301(g), for the duration of their temporary exportation to each CEM-affected region;
units.action_summary: The certificate must show horses were in the stated region for 60 days preceding export (or for duration of temporary export under §93.301(g)).

units.obligation_text: The horse, if applicable, has not been gelded during the 14 days preceding exportation. If gelded, the horse is accompanied by certificate of castration including date of completion and removal of both testicles;
units.action_summary: If gelded within 14 days prior to export, the horse must be accompanied by a certificate of castration; otherwise the horse must not have been gelded during the 14 days preceding export.

units.obligation_text: The horse will be accompanied by documentation of pre-export examination occurring within 48 hours of export endorsed by a salaried veterinary medical officer;
units.action_summary: Horses must have documentation of a pre-export exam within 48 hours endorsed by a salaried veterinary medical officer.

units.obligation_text: The horses, except horses described in § 93.301(f), have not been in any region listed in accordance with § 93.301(c)(1) on the APHIS website as affected with CEM during the 12 months immediately prior to their importation into the United States;
units.action_summary: Except as provided, horses must not have been in regions listed as CEM-affected during the 12 months before importation.

units.obligation_text: Any declaration, permit, or other required document for horses may be issued and presented using a United States Government electronic information exchange system or other method authorized by APHIS.
units.actor: issuing authorities / national government of region of origin
units.action_summary: Required documents may be issued and presented electronically or by other APHIS-authorized methods.

units.obligation_text: Except as provided in paragraph (d) of this section, horses from Canada shall be accompanied by a certificate as required by § 93.314, which shall include evidence of a negative test for equine infectious anemia for which blood samples were drawn during the 180 days preceding exportation to the United States and which test was conducted in a laboratory approved by the Canada Department of Agriculture or the United States Department of Agriculture.
units.action_summary: Horses from Canada must be accompanied by a certificate that includes evidence of a negative EIA test with blood drawn within 180 days and tested in an approved laboratory.

units.obligation_text: evidence of a negative test for equine infectious anemia for which blood samples were drawn during the 180 days preceding exportation
units.action_summary: Blood samples for EIA testing must have been drawn during the 180 days preceding export.

units.obligation_text: the test was conducted in a laboratory approved by the Canada Department of Agriculture or the United States Department of Agriculture.
units.action_summary: The EIA test must have been conducted in a laboratory approved by the Canadian Department of Agriculture or the USDA.

units.obligation_text: Certificates required for horses from Canada must be issued and endorsed by a salaried veterinarian of the Canadian Government.
units.action_summary: Certificates for horses from Canada must be issued and endorsed by a salaried Canadian Government veterinarian.

units.obligation_text: For all horses offered for importation from or transiting through regions of Central America or of the West Indies, the importer or his or her agent shall have obtained an import permit under § 93.304
units.actor: importer or his or her agent
units.action_summary: Importers/agents must obtain an import permit under §93.304 for horses from/transiting through Central America or the West Indies.

units.obligation_text: and shall present two copies of a declaration as provided in § 93.305.
units.actor: importer or his or her agent
units.action_summary: Importers/agents must present two copies of the required declaration under §93.305.

units.obligation_text: Horses quarantined at a U.S. facility designated in § 93.303 must obtain an import permit under § 93.304.
units.actor: horses quarantined at a U.S. facility / owner/importer
units.action_summary: Horses quarantined at designated U.S. facilities must obtain an import permit under §93.304.

units.obligation_text: Except as provided in §§ 93.317 (horses from Canada) and 93.324 (horses from Mexico), horses intended for importation from regions that APHIS considers to be affected with Venezuelan equine encephalomyelitis shall be quarantined at a port designated in § 93.303 to be evaluated for signs of Venezuelan equine encephalomyelitis.
units.action_summary: Horses from APHIS-designated VEE-affected regions must be quarantined at designated ports for evaluation.

units.obligation_text: Each horse must be accompanied at the time of importation by an import permit in accordance with § 93.304.
units.action_summary: Each imported horse must have an import permit under §93.304 at time of importation.

units.obligation_text: A list of regions that APHIS considers affected with Venezuelan equine encephalomyelitis is maintained on the APHIS website at https://www.aphis.usda.gov/aphis/ourfocus/animalhealth/animal-and-animal-product-import-information/animal-health-status-of-regions. Copies of the list can be obtained via postal mail or email upon request to Regionalization Evaluation Services, Strategy and Policy, Veterinary Services, Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service, 4700 River Road, Unit 38, Riverdale, Maryland 20737; AskRegionalization@usda.gov.
units.action_summary: APHIS maintains a list of VEE-affected regions on its website and provides copies on request.

units.obligation_text: APHIS will add a region to the list upon determining that the disease exists in the region based on reports APHIS receives of outbreaks of the disease from veterinary officials of the exporting country, from the World Organization for Animal Health (OIE), or from other sources the Administrator determines to be reliable.
units.action_summary: APHIS will add regions to the VEE-affected list when it determines disease exists based on reliable reports.

units.obligation_text: APHIS will remove a region from the list after conducting an evaluation of the region in accordance with § 92.2 of this subchapter and finding that the disease is not present in the region.
units.action_summary: APHIS will remove regions from the VEE-affected list after evaluation finds disease absent.

units.obligation_text: Horses from regions where APHIS considers screwworm to exist may be imported into the United States only if they meet the requirements in paragraphs (a)(3)(i) through (vii) of this section, obtain an import permit in accordance with § 93.304, and meet all other applicable requirements of this part.
units.action_summary: Importation of horses from screwworm regions is permitted only if they meet specified requirements, obtain an import permit, and meet other applicable parts.

units.obligation_text: A veterinarian must treat horses with ivermectin 3 to 5 days prior to the date of export to the United States according to the recommended dose prescribed on the product’s label.
units.action_summary: A veterinarian must treat horses with ivermectin 3–5 days before export per label dosing.

units.obligation_text: Horses must be examined for screwworm by a full-time salaried veterinary official of the exporting country within 24 hours prior to shipment to the United States. The official must fully examine the horses, including their external genitalia.
units.actor: full-time salaried veterinary official of the exporting country
units.action_summary: A full-time salaried veterinary official must examine horses within 24 hours before shipment, including external genitalia.

units.obligation_text: If horses are found to be infested with screwworm, they must be treated until free from infestation.
units.actor: exporting-country veterinary officials / veterinarians treating horses
units.action_summary: If screwworm infestation is detected, horses must be treated until infestation is eliminated.

units.obligation_text: At the time horses are loaded onto a means of conveyance for export, a veterinarian must treat any visible wounds on the animals with a solution of coumaphos dust at a concentration of 5 percent active ingredient.
units.action_summary: Visible wounds must be treated with 5% coumaphos dust at loading for export.

units.obligation_text: Horses must be accompanied to the United States by a certificate signed by a full-time salaried veterinary official of the exporting country. The certificate must state that the horses, including their external genitalia, have been thoroughly examined and found free of screwworm and that the horses have been treated in accordance with paragraphs (a)(3)(i) and (iii) of this section.
units.action_summary: Horses must be accompanied by a certificate signed by a full-time salaried veterinary official stating they were examined free of screwworm and treated per paragraphs (i) and (iii).

units.obligation_text: Horses must be quarantined upon arrival in the United States at a port designated in § 93.303 for at least 7 days.
units.action_summary: Horses from screwworm regions must be quarantined at designated ports for at least 7 days upon arrival.

units.obligation_text: Horses must be examined for screwworm by a veterinarian within 24 hours after arrival at a port designated in § 93.303. The examining veterinarian must examine horses, including their external genitalia, to determine whether the horse is infested with screwworm.
units.actor: a veterinarian at the designated port
units.action_summary: Within 24 hours after arrival, a veterinarian must examine horses for screwworm, including external genitalia.

units.obligation_text: Horses must be held at the animal import center for a minimum of 7 days.
units.action_summary: Horses must be held at the animal import center for at least 7 days.

units.obligation_text: On day 7, prior to the horses’ release, the horses must be examined by a veterinarian at the expense of the owner or broker.
units.actor: a veterinarian; owner or broker (to pay examination costs)
units.action_summary: Before release on day 7, horses must be examined by a veterinarian; owner/broker bears the cost.

units.obligation_text: For this examination, male horses must be tranquilized or sedated so that the external genitalia of the horses can be thoroughly examined.
units.action_summary: Male horses must be tranquilized or sedated for thorough examination of external genitalia.

units.obligation_text: If screwworm is found during this examination, the horses must be held in quarantine and treated until free of infestation.
units.action_summary: If screwworm is detected during the day-7 exam, horses must remain in quarantine and be treated until free of infestation.

units.obligation_text: Mares to be used to test stallions for CEM shall be permanently identified before the mares are used for such testing with the letter "T" or other permanent identification approved by APHIS on a case-by-case basis.
units.action_summary: Mares used to test stallions for CEM must be permanently identified (e.g., with 'T' or APHIS-approved identification) before testing.

units.obligation_text: The marking shall be permanently applied by an inspector, a State inspector, or an accredited veterinarian
units.actor: inspector, State inspector, or accredited veterinarian
units.action_summary: The permanent identification must be applied by an inspector, State inspector, or accredited veterinarian.

units.obligation_text: who shall use a hot iron, freezemarking, a lip tattoo, or other APHIS-approved method.
units.actor: inspector, State inspector, or accredited veterinarian (applicator)
units.action_summary: Appointed applicators must use hot iron, freezemarking, lip tattoo, or other APHIS-approved method.

units.obligation_text: If a hot iron or freezemarking is used, the marking shall not be less than 2 inches (5.08 cm) high and shall be applied to the left shoulder or left side of the neck of the mare.
units.actor: inspector, State inspector, or accredited veterinarian (applicator)
units.action_summary: If hot iron/freezemarking used, marking must be at least 2 inches high and applied to left shoulder or left side of neck.

units.obligation_text: If a lip tattoo is used, the marking shall not be less than 1 inch (2.54 cm) high and 0.75 inch (1.9 cm) wide and shall be applied to the inside surface of the upper lip of the test mare.
units.actor: inspector, State inspector, or accredited veterinarian (applicator)
units.action_summary: If lip tattoo used, it must be at least 1 inch high and 0.75 inch wide and applied inside upper lip.

units.obligation_text: The State must agree to provide oversight during the test breeding of quarantined stallions.
units.action_summary: The State is required to provide oversight during test breeding of quarantined stallions.

units.obligation_text: A list of States approved by APHIS to receive stallions over 731 days of age imported under paragraph (e) of this section is maintained on the APHIS website at [ADDRESS TO BE ADDED IN FINAL RULE].
units.action_summary: APHIS maintains a list on its website of States approved to receive stallions over 731 days of age.

units.obligation_text: Copies of the list will also be available via postal mail, fax, or email upon request to the Regionalization Evaluation Services, Veterinary Services, Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service, 4700 River Road, Unit 38, Riverdale, MD 20737.
units.action_summary: APHIS will provide copies of the approved-States list via mail, fax, or email upon request.

units.obligation_text: A list of States approved by APHIS to receive mares over 731 days of age imported under paragraph (e) of this section is maintained on the APHIS website at [ADDRESS TO BE ADDED IN FINAL RULE].
units.action_summary: APHIS maintains a list on its website of States approved to receive mares over 731 days of age.

units.obligation_text: Copies of the list will also be available via postal mail, fax, or email upon request to Live Animal Imports, Veterinary Services, Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service, 4700 River Road, Unit 38, Riverdale, MD 20737.
units.action_summary: APHIS will provide copies of the approved-States-for-mares list via mail, fax, or email upon request.

units.obligation_text: A list of regions where screwworm is considered to exist is maintained on the APHIS website at https://www.aphis.usda.gov/animalhealth/disease-status-of-regions. Copies of the list will also be available via postal mail, fax, or email upon request to the Regionalization Evaluation Services, Strategy and Policy, Veterinary Services, Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service, 4700 River Road, Unit 38, Riverdale, MD 20737; AskRegionalization@usda.gov.
units.action_summary: APHIS maintains a screwworm-affected regions list on its website and provides copies on request.

units.obligation_text: APHIS will add a region to the list upon determining that screwworm exists in the region based on reports APHIS receives of detections of the pest from veterinary officials of the exporting country, from the World Organization for Animal Health (OIE), or from other sources the Administrator determines to be reliable.
units.action_summary: APHIS will add regions to the screwworm list when it determines screwworm exists based on reliable detections/reports.

units.obligation_text: APHIS will remove a region from the list after conducting an evaluation of the region in accordance with § 92.2 of this subchapter and finding that screwworm is not present in the region.
units.action_summary: APHIS will remove regions from the screwworm list after evaluation finds the pest is not present.

title: Imports: Fresh Avocado Fruit From Continental Ecuador Into the Continental United States

units.obligation_text: Based on the findings of the revised PRA, we are proposing that commercial fresh avocado fruit may be imported into the continental United States from continental Ecuador subject to the conditions outlined in the June 2018 proposed rule, as well as additional conditions designed to safeguard against Stenoma catenifer.
units.actor: importers/National Plant Protection Organization (NPPO) of Ecuador/places of production
units.action_summary: Commercial fresh avocados from continental Ecuador may be imported into the continental United States if they meet specified conditions to mitigate Stenoma catenifer risk.

units.obligation_text: Avocados must be grown in pest free places of production for the avocado seed pest Stenoma catenifer that are established and maintained in accordance with international standards.
units.actor: avocado producers/places of production (NPPO of Ecuador)
units.action_summary: Avocados must be produced in pest-free places of production established and maintained per international standards.

units.obligation_text: APHIS must approve the survey protocol used by the National Plant Protection Organization (NPPO) of Ecuador to determine and maintain pest free status.
units.action_summary: APHIS is required to approve the NPPO of Ecuador's survey protocol for determining and maintaining pest-free status.

units.obligation_text: If the avocados are grown in a municipality free of Stenoma catenifer, the municipality must be surveyed every 6 months (twice a year) for the pest.
units.action_summary: Municipalities declared free of the pest must be surveyed twice a year for Stenoma catenifer.

units.obligation_text: Representative areas of the municipality where there are avocado trees, including production sites and urban areas, must be sampled.
units.action_summary: Surveys must sample representative areas of municipalities with avocado trees, including production sites and urban areas.

units.obligation_text: If the avocados are grown in a municipality not completely free of Stenoma catenifer, the NPPO of Ecuador can certify individual places of production as pest free.
units.action_summary: The NPPO may certify individual production sites as pest-free even if the municipality is not entirely free of the pest.

units.obligation_text: The surveys for pest free places of production must include representative areas from all parts of each registered place of production and a buffer zone of 1 kilometer.
units.action_summary: Surveys to certify pest-free places must cover all parts of the production site and include a 1-kilometer buffer zone.

units.obligation_text: The places of production and buffer zone must be surveyed monthly for Stenoma catenifer from 2 months before harvest until harvest is completed.
units.action_summary: Monthly surveys of the production site and its 1-kilometer buffer must be conducted from two months before harvest through completion of harvest.

units.obligation_text: If one or more Stenoma catenifer are detected during a survey or during any other monitoring or inspection activity, the place of production will be prohibited from exporting avocados to the continental United States until APHIS and the NPPO of Ecuador jointly agree that the risk has been mitigated.
units.action_summary: Detection of one or more Stenoma catenifer prohibits the production site from exporting avocados to the continental U.S. until APHIS and the NPPO jointly determine the risk is mitigated.

units.obligation_text: until APHIS and the NPPO of Ecuador jointly agree that the risk has been mitigated.
units.actor: APHIS and the NPPO of Ecuador
units.action_summary: Export prohibition remains in place until APHIS and the NPPO jointly agree the risk is mitigated.

units.obligation_text: The NPPO of Ecuador must keep records of Stenoma catenifer detections for each place of production, and update the records each time the places of production are surveyed.
units.action_summary: The NPPO must record and update detections of Stenoma catenifer for each production site whenever surveys occur.

units.obligation_text: The records must be maintained for at least 1 year and provided for APHIS’ review, if requested.
units.action_summary: NPPO must keep detection records for at least one year and provide them to APHIS upon request.

units.obligation_text: The NPPO of Ecuador would also have to enter into an operational work plan with APHIS that details the daily procedures the NPPO will take to meet these and all conditions.
units.action_summary: The NPPO must enter into an operational work plan with APHIS detailing daily procedures to meet all conditions.

units.obligation_text: The facility must provide training for its personnel regarding their roles and responsibilities as outlined in the plan.
units.action_summary: Provide training for personnel on their roles and responsibilities as described in the contingency plan.

units.obligation_text: For current registrants, training of facility personnel must be completed within 60 days of the research facility putting their plan in place;

units.obligation_text: for research facilities registered after [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER EFFECTIVE DATE OF FINAL RULE] training of facility personnel must be completed within 60 days of the facility putting its contingency plan in place.
