title: Horse Protection; Licensing of Designated Qualified Persons and Other Amendments

units.obligation_text: OPM or a delegated examining unit (DEU) will use one of the mechanisms identified below to refer a sufficient number of candidates for consideration, in accordance with this section and the agency’s delegated examining policies.
units.action_summary: Use one of the listed mechanisms to refer a sufficient number of candidates for consideration pursuant to the section and agency policies.

units.obligation_text: Agencies must establish a policy on the use of these procedures.
units.action_summary: Establish a policy governing use of the procedures described in this section.

units.obligation_text: OPM or a DEU may determine, based on the position to be filled, which of the following mechanisms will best meet the hiring needs of the agency and result in at least three names for consideration.
units.action_summary: May choose which referral mechanism to use to meet hiring needs and obtain at least three names.

units.obligation_text: OPM or a DEU may establish a cut-off score based on the assessment(s) used, supported by job analysis data;
units.action_summary: May establish a cut-off score based on assessments and job analysis data.

units.obligation_text: OPM or a DEU may establish a cut-off score based on business necessity;
units.action_summary: May establish a cut-off score justified by business necessity.

units.obligation_text: OPM or a DEU may use a set number of the highest ranked eligible applicants to certify;
units.action_summary: May certify a set number of highest-ranked eligible applicants.

units.obligation_text: OPM or a DEU may use a set percentage of the highest ranked eligible applicants to certify.
units.action_summary: May certify a set percentage of highest-ranked eligible applicants.

units.obligation_text: When using a set number of candidates or top percentage of eligible applicants, all applicants with the same score and veterans’ preference category as the last candidate in the cut, will also be referred.
units.action_summary: If tie at the cut, also refer all applicants with same score and veterans' preference category as the last candidate.

units.obligation_text: In selecting an appropriate mechanism, agencies should consider the number of positions to be filled, the assessment(s) used, historical applicant data, current labor market conditions, and other factors appropriate for the hiring action.
units.action_summary: Consider listed factors when selecting an appropriate referral mechanism.

units.obligation_text: The mechanism, or approach, used must be determined before announcing the vacancy and must be stated in the job opportunity announcement.
units.action_summary: Decide on the mechanism before announcing the vacancy and state it in the job announcement.

units.obligation_text: The approach used must be clearly documented in the examining case file and available for reconstruction or third-party review.
units.action_summary: Document the approach in the case file and make it available for reconstruction or review.

units.obligation_text: Hiring managers will receive sufficient names, when available, to allow them to consider at least three candidates for each vacancy.
units.action_summary: Provide hiring managers, when possible, with enough names to consider at least three candidates per vacancy.

units.obligation_text: In instances when a certificate of eligibles results in fewer than three eligible and available candidates per vacancy and an agency needs to issue a supplemental certification, OPM or a DEU must have decided, before announcing the vacancy, how to expand the group of candidates for whichever of the referral mechanisms used in accordance with the guidance in the Delegated Examining Operations Handbook.
units.action_summary: Decide before announcing how to expand candidates (per the handbook) if certificate yields fewer than three and supplemental certification is needed.

units.obligation_text: OPM or a DEU will refer candidates for consideration by simultaneously listing a candidate on all certificates for which the candidate is interested, eligible, and within reach,
units.action_summary: Refer candidates by listing them simultaneously on all applicable certificates when interested, eligible, and within reach.

units.obligation_text: except that, when it is deemed in the interest of good administration and candidates have been so notified, OPM or a DEU may choose to refer candidates for only one vacancy at a time.
units.action_summary: May, as an exception when in interest of good administration and candidates notified, refer candidates for only one vacancy at a time.

units.obligation_text: A hiring manager, with sole regard to merit and fitness, shall select any eligible candidate certified for appointment on a certificate of eligibles,
units.action_summary: Select any eligible candidate certified on a certificate of eligibles based solely on merit and fitness.

units.obligation_text: the hiring manager may not pass over a preference eligible to select a lower standing non-preference eligible on the certificate unless the agency complies with pass over procedures in accordance with § 332.406.
units.actor: A hiring manager (subject to agency compliance)
units.action_summary: May not pass over a preference eligible in favor of a lower-standing non-preference eligible unless agency follows pass-over procedures in § 332.406.

units.obligation_text: An appointing officer is not required to consider an eligible who has been considered by one or more hiring managers for three separate appointments from the same or different certificates for the same position (i.e., the same title, series, and grade).
units.action_summary: May decline to consider an eligible who has been considered for three separate appointments for the same position.

units.obligation_text: In order to remove a candidate from consideration, one or more hiring managers must have made three valid selections and given bona fide consideration to the candidate during this process.
units.action_summary: Before removing a candidate, hiring managers must have made three valid selections and provided bona fide consideration.

units.obligation_text: To use this provision, a hiring manager must consider the candidate’s application material and interview the candidate for the position.
units.action_summary: Consider the candidate's application materials and interview the candidate to use the three-consideration provision.

units.obligation_text: The interview must have been of the same rigor and thoroughness as those conducted with other candidates interviewed for the position.
units.action_summary: Conduct interviews with the same rigor and thoroughness as for other candidates.

units.obligation_text: The agency must document in the case file the bona fide consideration a candidate received and its reason(s) for removing the candidate from consideration, including a description of why the candidate is not receiving additional consideration, such as the candidate’s lack of a specific skill(s) or attribute(s).
units.action_summary: Document in the case file the bona fide consideration and reasons for removing a candidate, including explanatory descriptions.

units.obligation_text: An agency may use the three consideration provision to remove one candidate from further consideration starting with the fourth selection, i.e., after three valid selections have been made, and may remove one candidate for each subsequent selection made from a certificate of eligibles as long as bona fide consideration has been given and documented as required by this section.
units.action_summary: May remove one candidate starting with the fourth selection (and one per subsequent selection) provided bona fide consideration was given and documented.

units.obligation_text: Veterans’ preference must be applied as prescribed in 5 U.S.C. 3319(b) and (c)(6);
units.action_summary: Apply veterans' preference as prescribed in the cited statutory provisions.

units.obligation_text: Veterans’ preference points as prescribed in § 337.101 are not applied in category rating;
units.action_summary: Do not apply veterans' preference points (per § 337.101) when using category rating.

units.obligation_text: Sections 3319(b) and 3319(c)(6) of title 5 U.S.C. constitute veterans’ preference requirements for purposes of 5 U.S.C. 2302(b)(11)(A) and (B).
units.action_summary: Designate the cited statutory sections as the veterans' preference requirements for purposes of the referenced 5 U.S.C. provisions.

title: Procedures To Adjust Customs COBRA User Fees To Reflect Inflation

units.obligation_text: CBP will determine annually whether an adjustment to the fees and limitations is necessary
units.action_summary: CBP must decide each year if fee/limitation adjustments are needed.

units.obligation_text: a notice specifying the amount of the fees and limitations will be published in the Federal Register annually for each fiscal year at least 30 days prior to the effective date of the new fees and limitations
units.action_summary: CBP must publish a Federal Register notice with adjusted fee amounts at least 30 days before they take effect each fiscal year.

units.obligation_text: The fees and the limitations will also be maintained for the public's convenience on the CBP Web site at www.cbp.gov
units.action_summary: CBP must post the fees and limitations on its website.

units.obligation_text: If a customs user has pre-paid or met the calendar year limit prior to the effective date of the new fees and limitations, no additional fees will be required for that calendar year
units.action_summary: No further fees are required that calendar year for users who prepaid or already met the limit before new fees take effect.

units.obligation_text: If the customs user has not pre-paid or met the calendar year limit prior to the effective date of the new fees and limitations, the customs user will be subject to the adjusted limitation or prepayment amount
units.action_summary: Users who haven't prepaid or met the limit by the effective date are subject to the adjusted fees/limits.

units.obligation_text: Upon arrival at a CBP port of entry, the driver or other person in charge of a commercial truck must tender the fees to CBP unless they have been prepaid as provided for in paragraph (c)(3) of this section
units.actor: the driver or other person in charge of a commercial truck
units.action_summary: Truck drivers/persons in charge must pay CBP the applicable fees on arrival unless prepaid per paragraph (c)(3).

units.obligation_text: The fees will not apply to any commercial truck which, at the time of arrival, is being transported by any vessel other than a ferry
units.action_summary: No fees apply to commercial trucks that are being transported by a vessel other than a ferry at arrival.

units.obligation_text: No CBP fee will be collected under paragraph (c)(1) of this section for the arrival of a commercial truck during any calendar year once a prepayment of $100, as adjusted by the terms of paragraph (k) of this section, has been made and a transponder has been affixed to the vehicle windshield as provided in paragraph (c)(3) of this section
units.action_summary: Once the specified prepayment is made and a transponder affixed, CBP will not collect additional CBP fees for that truck in the calendar year.

units.obligation_text: a fee of $5.50, as adjusted by the terms of paragraph (k) of this section, must be collected and remitted to CBP for services provided in connection with the arrival of each passenger aboard a commercial vessel or commercial aircraft from a place outside the United States except: (A) When the journey ... originates in a territory or possession ...; or (B) When the journey ... originates in the United States and was not limited to the territories and possessions
units.action_summary: A $5.50 (adjusted) fee must be collected and remitted to CBP for each arriving international passenger, except specified origin exceptions.

units.obligation_text: a fee of $1.93, as adjusted by the terms of paragraph (k) of this section, must be collected and remitted to CBP for services provided in connection with the arrival of each passenger aboard a commercial vessel whose journey originated in a territory or possession of the United States or whose journey originated in the United States and was limited to the territories and possessions of the United States
units.action_summary: A $1.93 (adjusted) fee must be collected/remitted to CBP for passengers from territories/limited domestic journeys as specified.

units.obligation_text: Customs brokers are subject to an annual user fee of $138, as adjusted by the terms of paragraph (k) of this section, for each district permit and for a national permit held by an individual, partnership, association, or corporation
units.action_summary: Customs brokers must pay an annual user fee (base $138 adjusted) for each district and national permit.

units.obligation_text: The annual user fee for each district permit must be submitted to the port through which the broker was granted the permit
units.action_summary: Brokers must submit each district permit's annual fee to the port that granted the permit.

units.obligation_text: The annual user fee for a national permit must be submitted to the port through which the broker's license is delivered
units.action_summary: Brokers must submit national permit annual fees to the port where their license is delivered.

units.obligation_text: CBP will determine annually whether an adjustment to the fees and limitations is necessary and a notice specifying the amount of the fees and limitations, as adjusted, will be published in the Federal Register annually for each fiscal year at least 30 days prior to the effective date of the new fees and limitations
units.action_summary: CBP must annually decide on adjustments and publish an adjusted-fee notice at least 30 days before the effective date.

units.obligation_text: CBP will determine the adjustments, if any, by making the following calculations
units.action_summary: CBP must compute adjustments using the listed calculation steps.

units.obligation_text: Calculate the arithmetic average of the Consumer Price Index--All Urban Consumers, U.S. All items, 1982-84 = 100 (CPI-U) for the current year based on the most recent June-May period
units.action_summary: CBP must compute the CPI-U arithmetic average for the current year (June-May).

units.obligation_text: Use the figure 236.009 which is the arithmetic average of the CPI-U for FY 2014
units.action_summary: CBP must use 236.009 as the FY2014 CPI-U average in calculations.

units.obligation_text: State the arithmetic average of CPI-U for the comparison year which will be either (B) if the fees have never been adjusted in accordance with this paragraph (k), or the arithmetic average of the CPI-U for the last year in which fees were adjusted in accordance with this paragraph (k) as set forth in the Federal Register notice that last adjusted the fee
units.action_summary: CBP must identify the appropriate comparison-year CPI-U average (either FY2014 figure or last adjusted year).

units.obligation_text: Calculate the difference between the arithmetic averages of the CPI-U of the comparison year (C) and the current year (A). (D) = (A)-(C)
units.action_summary: CBP must compute difference D = A - C between current and comparison CPI-U averages.

units.obligation_text: Round the difference (D) to the nearest whole number
units.action_summary: CBP must round the computed difference to the nearest whole number (E).

units.obligation_text: Calculate the percentage change in the arithmetic averages of the CPI-U of the comparison year (C) and the current year (A) which is referred to as (F). (F) = ((E)/(C)) x 100%
units.action_summary: CBP must compute percentage change F = (E/C)*100%.

units.obligation_text: If (F) is one percent or more, proceed to the next step (viii). If (F) is less than one percent, no adjustment will be made
units.action_summary: CBP must proceed with adjustment steps only when F >= 1%; otherwise make no adjustment.

units.obligation_text: Calculate the difference in the arithmetic average of the CPI-U between the current year (the most recent June through May period) and the base year (FY 2014). (G) = (A)-(B)
units.action_summary: CBP must compute G = A - B as the CPI-U difference from base year to current year.

units.obligation_text: Calculate the percentage change in the CPI-U from the base year to the current year. (H) = ((G)/(B)) x 100%
units.action_summary: CBP must calculate percentage change H = (G/B)*100%.

units.obligation_text: Increase the fees and limitations that are subject to the rules of this paragraph by (H), calculating fees and limitations to the second decimal
units.action_summary: CBP must raise applicable fees/limits by percentage H, rounding to two decimal places.

units.obligation_text: Each carrier or operator using an express consignment carrier facility or a centralized hub facility must pay to CBP a fee in the amount of $1.00, as adjusted in accordance with the terms of paragraph (k) of Sec. 24.22 of this chapter, per individual air waybill or individual bill of lading for the processing of airway bills for shipments arriving in the United States
units.actor: each carrier or operator using an express consignment carrier facility or a centralized hub facility
units.action_summary: Carriers/operators using such facilities must pay a per-waybill/bill fee (adjusted $1.00) to CBP for processing.

units.obligation_text: In addition, if merchandise is formally entered and valued at $2,500 or less, the importer of record must pay to CBP the ad valorem fee specified in paragraph (b)(1) of this section, if applicable
units.action_summary: Importers of record must pay the ad valorem fee for formally entered merchandise valued at $2,500 or less, when applicable.

units.obligation_text: Payment must be made to CBP on a quarterly basis and must cover the individual fees for all subject transactions that occurred during a calendar quarter
units.action_summary: Carriers/operators must pay quarterly to CBP and cover fees for all transactions in that quarter.

units.obligation_text: The quarterly payment must conform to the requirements of Sec. 24.1, must be submitted electronically via Fedwire or pay.gov, or mailed to ... and must be received by CBP no later than the last day of the month that follows the close of the calendar quarter to which the payment relates
units.action_summary: Quarterly payments must meet Sec. 24.1 requirements, be sent by specified methods, and be received by CBP by the deadline (last day of following month).

units.obligation_text: The following information must be included with the quarterly payment: (1) The identity of the calendar quarter to which the payment relates; (2) The identity of the facility ... and the port code ... and portion ...; and (3) The total number of individual air waybills and individual bills of lading covered by the payment, and a breakdown ...
units.action_summary: Quarterly payments must include quarter ID, facility/port codes and allocation, and counts of waybills/bills with breakdowns.

units.obligation_text: In the case of an overpayment, the carrier or operator may request a refund by writing to Customs and Border Protection, Revenue Division/Attention: Reimbursables, 6650 Telecom Drive, Suite 100, Indianapolis, Indiana 46278
units.action_summary: Carriers/operators may seek a refund for overpayments by writing to CBP at the specified address.

units.obligation_text: The refund request must specify the grounds for the refund and must be received by CBP within one year of the date the fee for which the refund is sought was paid to CBP
units.action_summary: Refund requests must state grounds and be received by CBP within one year of the fee payment date.

units.obligation_text: In the case of an underpayment, interest will accrue on the amount not paid from the date payment was initially due to the date that payment to CBP is made
units.action_summary: Underpayments accrue interest from the due date until paid.

units.obligation_text: The underpayment or failure of a carrier or operator using an express consignment carrier facility or a centralized hub facility to pay all applicable fees owed to CBP pursuant to paragraph (b)(4) of this section may result in the assessment of penalties under 19 U.S.C. 1592, liquidated damages, and any other action authorized by law
units.action_summary: Failure to pay required fees can lead to penalties, liquidated damages, and other lawful actions.

units.obligation_text: The total number of individual air waybills and individual bills of lading covered by the payment, and a breakdown of that total for each facility covered by the payment according to the number covered by formal entry procedures, the number covered by informal entry procedures specified in Sec. Sec. 128.24(e) and 143.23(j) of this chapter, and the number covered by other informal entry procedures
units.action_summary: Payers must include counts and breakdowns of waybills/bills by entry procedure with quarterly payments.

units.obligation_text: The refund request must be received by CBP within one year of the date the fee for which the refund is sought was paid to CBP
units.action_summary: Refund requests must be filed within one year of the fee payment date.

title: Modernization of the Customs Brokers Regulations

units.obligation_text: Customs business must be conducted within the customs territory of the United States as defined in Sec. 101.1 of this chapter.
units.action_summary: Customs business must be conducted within the U.S. customs territory.

units.obligation_text: A licensed customs broker, or partnership, association, or corporation, conducting customs business under a national permit must designate a knowledgeable point of contact to be available to CBP during and outside of normal operating hours to respond to customs business issues.
units.actor: licensed customs broker, or partnership, association, or corporation conducting business under a national permit
units.action_summary: Designate a knowledgeable point of contact available to CBP during and outside normal hours.

units.obligation_text: The licensed customs broker, or partnership, association, or corporation, must maintain accurate and current point of contact information in a CBP-authorized electronic data interchange (EDI) system.
units.actor: licensed customs broker, or partnership, association, or corporation
units.action_summary: Maintain accurate and current point-of-contact information in a CBP-authorized EDI system.

units.obligation_text: If a CBP-authorized EDI system is not available, then the information must be provided in writing to the director of the designated Center.
units.actor: licensed customs broker, or partnership, association, or corporation
units.action_summary: If EDI unavailable, provide point-of-contact information in writing to the designated Center director.

units.obligation_text: An application for a broker's license must be timely submitted to the director of the Center identified by CBP after the applicant attains a passing grade on the examination.
units.action_summary: Submit the broker license application timely to the CBP-identified Center director after passing the exam.

units.obligation_text: The application must be executed on CBP Form 3124.
units.action_summary: Complete the application on CBP Form 3124.

units.obligation_text: The application must be accompanied by the application fee prescribed in Sec. 111.96(a) and one copy of the appropriate attachment required by the application form (Articles of Agreement or an affidavit signed by all partners, Articles of Agreement of the association, or the Articles of Incorporation).
units.action_summary: Include required fee and specified attachment(s) with the application.

units.obligation_text: If the applicant proposes to operate under a trade or fictitious name in one or more States, evidence of the applicant's authority to use the name in each of those States must accompany the application.
units.action_summary: Provide state-authority evidence if operating under a trade or fictitious name.

units.obligation_text: An application for an individual license must be submitted within the 3-year period after the applicant took and passed the examination referred to in Sec. 111.11(a)(4) and Sec. 111.13.
units.actor: individual applicant for a broker's license
units.action_summary: Submit individual license application within 3 years of passing the exam.

units.obligation_text: The Center director may require an individual applicant to provide a copy of the notification that the applicant passed the examination and will require the applicant to submit fingerprints at the time of the interview.
units.action_summary: Center director can require proof of exam passage and will require fingerprints at interview.

units.obligation_text: The Center director may reject an application as improperly filed if the application is incomplete or, if on its face, the application demonstrates that one or more of the basic requirements set forth in Sec. 111.11 has not been met at the time of filing; in either case the application and fee will be returned to the filer without further action.
units.action_summary: Center director may reject incomplete or noncompliant applications and return application and fee.

units.obligation_text: If the appropriate Executive Director, Office of Trade, finds that the applicant is qualified and has paid all applicable fees prescribed in Sec. 111.96(a), the Executive Assistant Commissioner will issue a license.
units.action_summary: Issue a license when applicant is found qualified and applicable fees are paid.

units.obligation_text: If the appropriate Executive Director, Office of Trade, determines that the application for a license should be denied for any reason, notice of denial will be given by him or her to the applicant and to the director of the designated Center.
units.actor: appropriate Executive Director, Office of Trade
units.action_summary: Provide notice of license denial to applicant and designated Center director.

units.obligation_text: Upon the denial of an application for a license, the applicant may file with the appropriate Executive Director, Office of Trade, in writing, additional information or arguments in support of the application and may request to appear in person, by telephone, or by other acceptable means of communication.
units.action_summary: Applicant may file additional written information and request to appear following a denial.

units.obligation_text: This filing and request must be received by the appropriate Executive Director, Office of Trade within sixty (60) calendar days of the denial.
units.action_summary: Submit filing/request to appropriate Executive Director within 60 days of denial.

units.obligation_text: Upon the decision of the appropriate Executive Director, Office of Trade, affirming the denial of an application for a license, the applicant may file with the Executive Assistant Commissioner, in writing, a request for any additional review that the Executive Assistant Commissioner deems appropriate.
units.action_summary: Applicant may request additional review by the Executive Assistant Commissioner after affirmation of denial.

units.obligation_text: This request must be received by the Executive Assistant Commissioner within sixty (60) calendar days of the affirmation by the appropriate Executive Director, Office of Trade, of the denial of the application for a license.
units.action_summary: File the request for additional review with the Executive Assistant Commissioner within 60 days of affirmation.

units.obligation_text: Upon a decision of the Executive Assistant Commissioner affirming the denial of an application for a license, the applicant may appeal the decision to the Court of International Trade, provided that the appeal action is commenced within sixty (60) calendar days after the date of entry of the Executive Assistant Commissioner's decision.
units.action_summary: Applicant may appeal to the Court of International Trade within 60 days of the Executive Assistant Commissioner's decision.

units.obligation_text: Add the phrase 'and addressing how deficiencies have been remedied' after the term 'Sec. 111.12'.
units.actor: applicants following Sec. 111.12 (implicit: applicant or reviewer)
units.action_summary: When referencing Sec. 111.12, include information addressing how deficiencies have been remedied.

units.obligation_text: A national permit is required for the purpose of transacting customs business throughout the customs territory of the United States as defined in Sec. 101.1 of this chapter.
units.actor: persons transacting customs business throughout the customs territory
units.action_summary: A national permit is required to transact customs business nationwide.

units.obligation_text: An applicant who obtains a passing grade on the examination for an individual broker's license may apply for a national permit.
units.actor: applicant who passes the individual broker exam
units.action_summary: Applicants who pass the exam are permitted to apply for a national permit.

units.obligation_text: The applicant will exercise responsible supervision and control (as described in Sec. 111.28 of this part) over the activities conducted under that national permit.
units.actor: applicant granted a national permit (individual broker)
units.action_summary: The national permit holder must exercise responsible supervision and control over activities under the permit.

units.obligation_text: The national permit application may be submitted concurrently with or after the submission of an application for a broker's license.
units.action_summary: Applicant may submit national permit application at the same time as or after the broker license application.

units.obligation_text: An application for a national permit under this paragraph must be in the form of a letter or CBP-approved electronic submission to the director of the designated Center.
units.action_summary: Submit national permit application as a letter or CBP-approved electronic submission to the designated Center director.

units.obligation_text: The application must set forth or attach the following: (1) broker license number and date of issuance if available; (2)-(11) [various required items including office of record, point of contact, employee lists, supervision plan, records location, receipt of fees].
units.action_summary: Provide the enumerated information and attachments (license number, organization info, office of record, point of contact, employee list, supervision plan, records location, fee receipt) with the national permit application.

units.obligation_text: The director of the designated Center who receives the application will review to determine whether the applicant meets the requirements of paragraphs (a) and (b) of this section.
units.action_summary: Designated Center director will review national permit applications for compliance with requirements.

units.obligation_text: If the director of the designated Center is of the opinion that the national permit should not be issued, he or she will submit his or her written reasons for that opinion to the appropriate Executive Director, Office of Trade, CBP Headquarters, for appropriate instructions on whether to grant or deny the national permit.
units.action_summary: If recommending denial, designated Center director must submit written reasons to the appropriate Executive Director for instructions.

units.obligation_text: The appropriate Executive Director, Office of Trade, CBP Headquarters, will notify the applicant if his or her application is denied.
units.actor: appropriate Executive Director, Office of Trade
units.action_summary: Notify applicants of national permit denial.

units.obligation_text: CBP will issue a national permit to an applicant who meets the requirements of paragraphs (a) and (b) of this section.
units.action_summary: CBP will grant a national permit to applicants meeting the section's requirements.

units.obligation_text: CBP will maintain and make available to the public an alphabetical list of permitted brokers.
units.action_summary: CBP must maintain and publicly provide an alphabetical list of permitted brokers.

units.obligation_text: Upon the denial of an application for a national permit under this section, the applicant may file with the Executive Assistant Commissioner, in writing, additional information or arguments in support of the denied application and may request to appear in person, by telephone, or by other acceptable means of communication.
units.action_summary: Applicant may submit additional written information and request to appear before the Executive Assistant Commissioner after denial of a national permit.

units.obligation_text: This filing and request must be received by the Executive Assistant Commissioner within sixty (60) calendar days of the denial.
units.action_summary: Submit filing/request to the Executive Assistant Commissioner within 60 days of denial.

units.obligation_text: Upon a decision of the Executive Assistant Commissioner affirming the denial of an application for a national permit under this section, the applicant may appeal the decision to the Court of International Trade, provided that the appeal action is commenced within sixty (60) calendar days after the date of entry of the decision by the Executive Assistant Commissioner.
units.action_summary: Applicant may appeal to the Court of International Trade within 60 days of the Executive Assistant Commissioner's decision.

units.obligation_text: The individual broker who qualifies for the national permit will exercise responsible supervision and control (as described in Sec. 111.28 of this part) over the activities conducted under that national permit.
units.actor: individual broker who qualifies for the national permit
units.action_summary: The qualifying individual broker must exercise responsible supervision and control over permit activities.

units.obligation_text: Each broker must provide notification to the broker's designated Center of any known breach of electronic or physical records relating to the broker's customs business.
units.action_summary: Notify the designated Center of any known breach of electronic or physical records relating to customs business.

units.obligation_text: Notification to CBP must be provided within 72 hours of the discovery of the breach with a list of all compromised importer identification numbers (see 19 CFR 24.5).
units.action_summary: Provide breach notification to CBP within 72 hours including list of compromised importer IDs.

units.obligation_text: Each broker must designate a knowledgeable employee as the party responsible for brokerage-wide recordkeeping requirements.
units.action_summary: Designate a knowledgeable employee responsible for brokerage-wide recordkeeping.

units.obligation_text: Each broker must maintain accurate and current point of contact information in a CBP-authorized electronic data interchange (EDI) system.
units.action_summary: Maintain accurate/current point-of-contact information in a CBP-authorized EDI.

units.obligation_text: If a CBP-authorized EDI system is not available, then the information must be provided in writing to the director of the designated Center.
units.action_summary: If EDI unavailable, provide point-of-contact information in writing to designated Center director.

units.obligation_text: A licensed customs broker must maintain the records referred to in this part, including any records stored in electronic formats, within the customs territory of the United States and in accordance with the provisions of this part and part 163 of this chapter.
units.action_summary: Maintain required records (including electronic) within U.S. customs territory in accordance with this part and part 163.

units.obligation_text: The records referred to in this part and pertaining to the business of the clients serviced by the broker are to be considered confidential, and the broker must not disclose their contents or any information connected with the records to any persons other than those clients, their surety on a particular entry, and representatives of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), or other duly accredited officers or agents of the United States, except on subpoena or court order by a court of competent jurisdiction, or when authorized in writing by the client.
units.action_summary: Treat client records as confidential and do not disclose them except to specified parties or under subpoena/court order or written client authorization.

units.obligation_text: This confidentiality provision does not apply to information that properly is available from a source open to the public.
units.action_summary: Confidentiality rule excludes information available from public sources.

units.obligation_text: During the period of retention, the broker must maintain the records referred to in this part in such a manner that they may readily be examined.
units.action_summary: Keep records during retention period so they can be readily examined.

units.obligation_text: Records required to be maintained under the provisions of this part must be made available upon reasonable notice for inspection, copying, reproduction or other official use by representatives of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) within the prescribed period of retention or within any longer period of time during which they remain in the possession of the broker.
units.action_summary: Make records available upon reasonable notice to DHS representatives for inspection or official use during retention period (or longer if retained).

units.obligation_text: Upon request by DHS to examine records, the designated recordkeeping contact (see Sec. 111.21(d)), must make all records available to DHS within thirty (30) calendar days, or such longer time as specified by DHS, at the location specified by DHS.
units.action_summary: Provide all requested records to DHS within 30 days (or longer if DHS specifies) at DHS-specified location.

units.obligation_text: Records subject to the requirements of part 163 of this chapter must be made available to DHS in accordance with the provisions of that part.
units.action_summary: Make records subject to part 163 available to DHS as required by part 163.

units.obligation_text: Replace 'the port director and other proper officials of the Treasury Department' with 'DHS, or other duly accredited officers or agents of the United States.'
units.actor: regulatory text (affects who may inspect/receive records)
units.action_summary: Authorized recipients are DHS or other duly accredited officers/agents of the United States.

units.obligation_text: Every individual broker operating as a sole proprietor, every licensed member of a partnership that is a broker, and every licensed officer of an association or corporation that is a broker must exercise responsible supervision and control over the transaction of the customs business of the sole proprietorship, partnership, association, or corporation.
units.actor: every individual broker (sole proprietor), licensed member of partnership, licensed officer of association/corporation
units.action_summary: Exercise responsible supervision and control over the entity's customs business.

units.obligation_text: A sole proprietorship, partnership, association, or corporation must employ a sufficient number of licensed brokers relative to the job complexity, similarity of subordinate tasks, physical proximity of subordinates, abilities and skills of employees, and abilities and skills of the managers.
units.actor: sole proprietorship, partnership, association, or corporation (brokerage)
units.action_summary: Employ a sufficient number of licensed brokers considering listed factors to ensure responsible supervision and control.

units.obligation_text: Each national permit holder must submit to the director of the designated Center, a list of the names of persons currently employed by the broker.
units.action_summary: Submit list of currently employed persons to designated Center director.

units.obligation_text: The list of employees must be submitted prior to issuance of a national permit under Sec. 111.19 and before the broker begins to transact customs business.
units.action_summary: Provide employee list before permit issuance and before transacting customs business.

units.obligation_text: For each employee, the broker must provide the name, social security number, date and place of birth, date of hire, and current home address.
units.action_summary: Provide specified personal and employment information for each employee.

units.obligation_text: After the initial submission, an updated list must be submitted to a CBP-authorized electronic data interchange (EDI) system if any of the information required by this paragraph changes.
units.action_summary: Submit updated employee lists via CBP-authorized EDI when required information changes.

units.obligation_text: If a CBP-authorized EDI system is not available, then the information must be provided in writing to the director of the designated Center.
units.action_summary: If EDI unavailable, provide employee information in writing to the designated Center director.

units.obligation_text: The update must be submitted within thirty (30) calendar days of the change.
units.action_summary: Submit updates within 30 calendar days of the change.

units.obligation_text: Within thirty (30) calendar days of the start of employment of a new employee(s), the broker must submit a list of new employee(s) with the information required under paragraph (b)(1) of this section to a CBP-authorized EDI system.
units.action_summary: Within 30 days of hiring, submit new employee list with required information via EDI.

units.obligation_text: The broker may submit a list of the new employees or an updated list of all employees, specifically noting the new employee(s).
units.action_summary: Broker is permitted to submit only new employees or an updated full employee list (not both required).

units.obligation_text: If a CBP-authorized EDI system is not available, then the information must be provided in writing to the director of the designated Center.
units.action_summary: If EDI unavailable, provide new employee information in writing to designated Center director.

units.obligation_text: Within thirty (30) calendar days after the termination of employment of an employee, the broker must submit a list of terminated employee(s) to a CBP-authorized EDI system.
units.action_summary: Within 30 days of termination, submit terminated employee list via EDI.

units.obligation_text: The broker may submit a list of the terminated employees or an updated list of all employees, specifically noting the terminated employee(s).
units.action_summary: Broker may submit only terminated employees or an updated full employee list.

units.obligation_text: If a CBP-authorized EDI system is not available, then the information must be provided in writing to the director of the designated Center.
units.action_summary: If EDI unavailable, provide terminated-employee information in writing to the designated Center director.

units.obligation_text: Notwithstanding a broker's responsibility for providing the information required in paragraph (b) of this section, in the absence of culpability by the broker, CBP will not hold the broker responsible for the accuracy of any information that is provided to the broker by the employee.
units.action_summary: CBP will not hold broker responsible for accuracy of employee-provided information absent broker culpability.

units.obligation_text: If the ownership of a broker changes and ownership shares in the broker are not publicly traded, the broker must immediately provide written notice of that fact to the appropriate Executive Director, Office of Trade, and must send a copy of the written notice to the director of the designated Center.
units.action_summary: Immediately provide written notice of non-public-traded ownership change to appropriate Executive Director and copy to designated Center director.

units.obligation_text: When a change in ownership results in the addition of a new principal to the organization, CBP reserves the right to conduct a background investigation on the new principal.
units.action_summary: CBP may conduct a background investigation on a new principal resulting from ownership change.

units.obligation_text: The director of the designated Center will notify the broker if CBP objects to the new principal, and the broker will be given a reasonable period of time to remedy the situation.
units.actor: director of the designated Center / broker
units.action_summary: Designated Center director will notify broker of objections to new principal and broker will have reasonable time to remedy.

units.obligation_text: If the background investigation uncovers information which would have been the basis for a denial of an application for a broker's license and the principal's interest in the broker is not terminated to the satisfaction of the director of the designated Center, suspension or revocation proceedings may be initiated under subpart D of this part.
units.action_summary: CBP may initiate suspension or revocation proceedings if investigation reveals disqualifying information and principal interest is not terminated to the director's satisfaction.

units.obligation_text: A broker is responsible for providing CBP with the broker's current addresses, which include the broker's office of record address as defined in Sec. 111.1 and, if the broker is not actively engaged in transacting business as a broker, the broker's non-business address.
units.action_summary: Provide CBP with current office of record and non-business addresses as applicable.

units.obligation_text: If a broker does not receive mail at the broker's office of record or non-business address, the broker must also provide CBP with a valid address at which he or she receives mail.
units.action_summary: Provide an alternate valid mailing address if broker does not receive mail at listed addresses.

units.obligation_text: When address information changes, or the broker is no longer actively engaged in transacting business as a broker, he or she must update his or her address information within ten (10) calendar days through a CBP-authorized electronic data interchange (EDI) system.
units.action_summary: Update address information within 10 calendar days via CBP-authorized EDI when addresses change or broker ceases active engagement.

units.obligation_text: If a CBP-authorized EDI system is not available, then address updates must be provided in writing within ten (10) calendar days to the director of the designated Center.
units.action_summary: If EDI unavailable, provide address updates in writing within 10 days to designated Center director.

units.obligation_text: A partnership, association, or corporation broker must update within ten (10) calendar days in writing to the director of the designated Center any of the following: (1) date a licensed member or officer ceases to be the qualifying member or officer and name of successor; (2) date a licensed employee ceases to be the national permit qualifier and name of successor; and (3) any change in the Articles or legal nature of the organization.
units.action_summary: Provide written updates within 10 days to the designated Center director for specified organizational/personnel/legal changes.

units.obligation_text: Each broker must file a triennial status report with CBP on February 1 of each third year after 1985.
units.action_summary: File a triennial status report with CBP every three years on Feb 1.

units.obligation_text: The report must be filed through the CBP-authorized EDI system and accompanied by payment or valid proof of payment of the triennial status report fee prescribed in Sec. 111.96(d).
units.action_summary: File the triennial report via CBP-authorized EDI and include payment or proof of payment of the fee.

units.obligation_text: If a CBP-authorized EDI system is not available, the triennial status report must be filed with the director of the designated Center.
units.action_summary: If EDI unavailable, file the triennial report with the designated Center director.

units.obligation_text: Each individual broker must state in the report whether he or she is actively engaged in transacting business as a broker and, if so, provide specified information: (A) business name and address if sole proprietor; (B) name and address of employer if employed by another broker (with exceptions); and (C) state whether he or she still meets applicable requirements of Sec. 111.11 and Sec. 111.19 and has not engaged in conduct constituting grounds for suspension or revocation.
units.action_summary: State active engagement, provide business/employer information as applicable, and state continued compliance with Sec. 111.11 and 111.19 and absence of disqualifying conduct.

units.obligation_text: A broker must not file or procure or assist in the filing of any claim, or of any document, affidavit, or other papers, known by such broker to be false.
units.action_summary: Do not file or assist in filing claims or documents known to be false.

units.obligation_text: A broker must not give, or solicit or procure the giving of, any information or testimony that the broker knew or should have known was false or misleading in any matter pending before the Department of Homeland Security or to any representative of the Department of Homeland Security.
units.action_summary: Do not give or solicit information or testimony that is known or should have been known to be false or misleading to DHS or its representatives.

units.obligation_text: A broker also must document and report to CBP when the broker separates from or cancels representation of a client as a result of determining the client is intentionally attempting to use the broker to defraud or otherwise commit any criminal act against the U.S. Government.
units.action_summary: Document and report to CBP when terminating representation due to client intent to defraud or commit criminal acts against the U.S. Government.

units.obligation_text: The broker must obtain a customs power of attorney directly from the importer of record or drawback claimant, and not via a freight forwarder, to transact customs business for that importer of record or drawback claimant.
units.action_summary: Obtain customs power of attorney directly from the importer of record or drawback claimant, not through a freight forwarder.

units.obligation_text: No part of the agreement of compensation between the broker and the forwarder, nor any action taken pursuant to the agreement, can forbid or prevent direct communication between the importer of record, drawback claimant, or other party in interest and the broker;
units.action_summary: Agreements or actions may not forbid or prevent direct communication between importer/drawback claimant/other party and the broker.

title: Coal Workers' Health Surveillance Program: B Reader Decertification and Autopsy Payment

units.obligation_text: Any interested party may make a complaint to the NIOSH Coal Workers’ Health Surveillance Program against any B Reader who routinely provides chest radiograph classifications in practice that are believed to be unreasonably inaccurate.
units.action_summary: May file a complaint with the NIOSH Program against a B Reader believed to provide unreasonably inaccurate classifications.

units.obligation_text: A valid complaint must be submitted to the NIOSH Coal Workers’ Health Surveillance Program, Respiratory Health Division, and include the chest radiographs and ILO classifications being contested as well as a letter of support from a medical professional.
units.action_summary: Complaint must be submitted to NIOSH RHD and include radiographs, ILO classifications, and a supporting medical professional letter.

units.obligation_text: A complaint that demonstrates more than a reasonable difference of opinion will be considered valid.
units.actor: NIOSH Coal Workers’ Health Surveillance Program
units.action_summary: NIOSH will deem a complaint valid if it shows more than a reasonable difference of opinion.

units.obligation_text: A complaint that fails to include any required element will be considered invalid, and the NIOSH Respiratory Health Division will notify the complainant that no further investigation will occur.
units.action_summary: NIOSH will deem incomplete complaints invalid and will notify the complainant that no further investigation will occur.

units.obligation_text: Investigations may be initiated at NIOSH’s discretion or in response to a valid complaint, pursuant to paragraph (d)(1) of this section, to determine whether a B Reader has provided chest radiograph classifications in practice that are unreasonably inaccurate.
units.action_summary: NIOSH may initiate investigations, at its discretion or in response to valid complaints, to determine if a B Reader's classifications are unreasonably inaccurate.

units.obligation_text: The NIOSH Respiratory Health Division will choose a panel of at least four B Readers who will independently review the information provided in each valid complaint.
units.action_summary: NIOSH RHD will select a panel of at least four B Readers to independently review each valid complaint.

units.obligation_text: If one or more of the B Readers on the panel independently determines that the classification being contested is reasonable, the NIOSH Respiratory Health Division will conclude that the classification being contested is reasonable. The complainant will be notified of the finding and no further action will be conducted.
units.action_summary: If any panelist finds the contested classification reasonable, NIOSH RHD will conclude it is reasonable, notify the complainant, and take no further action.

units.obligation_text: If the B Readers on the panel independently and unanimously concur that the classification being contested is unreasonable, remedial actions will be taken by the NIOSH Respiratory Health Division pursuant to paragraphs (d)(2)(ii) through (v) of this section, accordingly.
units.action_summary: If the panel unanimously finds the contested classification unreasonable, NIOSH RHD will take remedial actions as described in paragraphs (d)(2)(ii)-(v).

units.obligation_text: If, after an investigation, a panel of B Readers unanimously finds that the classification contested in a complaint is unreasonably inaccurate, the Program will issue an initial report to the B Reader under review.
units.action_summary: If the panel unanimously finds an unreasonably inaccurate classification, the Program will issue an initial report to the B Reader under review.

units.obligation_text: If the B Reader chooses not to challenge the initial report within 30 days, the initial report becomes a final determination.
units.action_summary: If not challenged within 30 days, the initial report automatically becomes a final determination.

units.obligation_text: If the B Reader chooses to challenge the initial report, the Coal Workers’ Health Surveillance Program will respond within 90 days; the Program’s decision is final.
units.action_summary: If the B Reader challenges, the Program will respond within 90 days; the Program's decision is final.

units.obligation_text: The first final report may be considered a warning that further misclassification of small or large opacities or other types of pleural abnormalities will result in suspension or revocation of the B Reader’s certification.
units.actor: Coal Workers’ Health Surveillance Program / regulatory effect
units.action_summary: The first final report may serve as a warning that further misclassification will lead to suspension or revocation of the B Reader's certification.

units.obligation_text: If, after an investigation, a panel of B Readers unanimously finds that the classification contested in a second complaint is unreasonably inaccurate, the Program will issue an initial report to the B Reader under review.
units.action_summary: If the panel unanimously finds an unreasonably inaccurate classification in a second complaint, the Program will issue an initial report to the B Reader.

units.obligation_text: If the B Reader chooses not to challenge the initial report within 30 days, the initial report becomes a final determination.
units.action_summary: If the second initial report is not challenged within 30 days, it becomes a final determination.

units.obligation_text: If the B Reader chooses to challenge the initial report, the Coal Workers’ Health Surveillance Program will respond within 90 days, during which time the B Reader’s certification will remain in good standing; the Program’s decision is final and may result in the 1-year suspension of the B Reader’s certification with the 1-year period beginning on the date the Program issues the final decision letter.
units.action_summary: If the B Reader challenges the second report, the Program will respond within 90 days; certification remains in good standing during that time; the Program's final decision may result in a 1-year suspension beginning on the date of the final decision letter.
units.modal_raw: will respond / will remain / is final / may result

units.obligation_text: The suspended B Reader must take and pass the certification examination at the conclusion of the suspension period in order to be reinstated.
units.action_summary: A B Reader suspended for one year must take and pass the certification exam at the end of suspension to be reinstated.

units.obligation_text: If, after an investigation, a panel of B Readers unanimously finds that the classification contested in a third complaint is unreasonably inaccurate, the Program will issue an initial report to the B Reader under review.
units.action_summary: If the panel unanimously finds an unreasonably inaccurate classification in a third complaint, the Program will issue an initial report to the B Reader.

units.obligation_text: If the B Reader chooses not to challenge the initial report within 30 days, the initial report becomes a final determination.
units.action_summary: If the third initial report is not challenged within 30 days, it becomes a final determination.

units.obligation_text: If the B Reader chooses to challenge the initial report, the Coal Workers’ Health Surveillance Program will respond within 90 days, during which time the B Reader’s certification will remain in good standing; the Program’s decision is final, unless the B Reader successfully appeals the decision pursuant to § 37.52(d)(3), and will result in permanent revocation of the B Reader’s certification beginning on the date the Program issues the final decision letter.
units.action_summary: If the B Reader challenges the third report, the Program will respond within 90 days; certification remains in good standing during that time; the Program's decision is final unless successfully appealed and will result in permanent revocation effective on the date of the final decision letter.
units.modal_raw: will respond / will remain / is final / will result

units.obligation_text: If the first complaint is found to be valid and to demonstrate a pattern of inaccurate chest radiograph classifications, the Program will issue an initial report to the B Reader under review and immediately apply the procedures in paragraph (d)(2)(iv) of this section.
units.action_summary: If the first complaint proves a pattern of inaccurate classifications, the Program will issue an initial report and immediately apply the third-complaint procedures (d)(2)(iv).

units.obligation_text: To demonstrate a pattern of inaccurate classifications, the valid complaint must provide radiographs from three or more patients conducted within a one-year period that are determined by the Program to be inaccurate.
units.action_summary: A valid complaint demonstrating a pattern must include radiographs from three or more patients within one year that the Program determines are inaccurate.

units.obligation_text: A B Reader whose certification is revoked after three final adverse determinations is no longer a certified B Reader.
units.action_summary: A B Reader revoked after three final adverse determinations ceases to be a certified B Reader.

units.obligation_text: Such B Reader may appeal the Coal Workers’ Health Surveillance Program’s decision to revoke the B Reader’s certification.
units.action_summary: A B Reader whose certification is revoked may appeal the revocation decision.

units.obligation_text: An appeal request must be submitted in writing to the NIOSH Respiratory Health Division Director, signed and postmarked within 30 calendar days of the date of the letter notifying the B Reader of the decertification decision. Electronic versions of the signed appeal request letter will also be accepted.
units.action_summary: Appeal request must be signed, postmarked, and submitted in writing to the NIOSH RHD Director within 30 days; electronic signed versions will also be accepted.

units.obligation_text: The appeal request must state the reason(s) the B Reader believes the decertification decision is incorrect and should be reversed. The appeal request may include scientific or medical information correcting factual errors, any information demonstrating that the decertification decision was not reasonable, and/or relevant new information not previously considered by the Coal Workers’ Health Surveillance Program.
units.action_summary: Appeal must state reasons for reversal; may include scientific/medical information, evidence of unreasonableness, or new relevant information.

units.obligation_text: The appeal request must be sent to the NIOSH Respiratory Health Division Director at the address specified in the decertification letter.
units.action_summary: Appeal request must be sent to the NIOSH RHD Director at the address given in the decertification letter.

units.obligation_text: The NIOSH Respiratory Health Division Director will review the Coal Workers’ Health Surveillance Program decision and any relevant information provided by the B Reader and make a final decision on the appeal.
units.action_summary: The Director will review the Program decision and any relevant materials and make a final decision on the appeal.

units.obligation_text: The Director will notify the B Reader of the following in writing: (A) The Director’s final decision on the appeal; (B) An explanation of the reason(s) for the Director’s final decision on the appeal; and (C) Any administrative actions taken by the Coal Workers’ Health Surveillance Program.
units.action_summary: The Director will notify the B Reader in writing of the final decision, explanation of reasons, and any administrative actions taken.

units.obligation_text: NIOSH may, at its discretion, pay any pathologist who has received prior authorization from NIOSH pursuant to § 37.204(a), and with legal consent: (1) Performs an autopsy on a miner in accordance with this subpart; and (2) Submits the findings and other materials to NIOSH in accordance with this subpart within 180 calendar days after having performed the autopsy.
units.action_summary: NIOSH may pay a pathologist (with prior authorization and legal consent) who performs an autopsy per this subpart and submits findings and materials within 180 days.

units.obligation_text: Pathologist has received prior authorization from NIOSH pursuant to § 37.204(a), and with legal consent (condition for payment).
units.action_summary: To be eligible for NIOSH payment, the pathologist must have received prior authorization from NIOSH and have legal consent.

units.obligation_text: Performs an autopsy on a miner in accordance with this subpart (condition for payment).
units.action_summary: To be paid by NIOSH, the pathologist must perform the autopsy in accordance with this subpart.

units.obligation_text: Submits the findings and other materials to NIOSH in accordance with this subpart within 180 calendar days after having performed the autopsy.
units.action_summary: Pathologist must submit findings and materials to NIOSH within 180 days after performing the autopsy to be eligible for payment.

units.obligation_text: More than one type of chest radiographic image may be submitted.
units.action_summary: Submitters may submit more than one type of chest radiographic image.

units.obligation_text: Pathologists will be compensated in accordance with the ordinary, usual, or customary fee charged by other pathologists for the same services, at the discretion of NIOSH.
units.action_summary: NIOSH will compensate pathologists based on ordinary customary fees, at NIOSH's discretion.

units.obligation_text: NIOSH will additionally compensate a pathologist for the submission of chest radiographic images made of the subject of the autopsy within 5 years prior to his/her death together with copies of any interpretations made.
units.action_summary: NIOSH will also compensate for submission of chest images from within 5 years before death plus any interpretation copies.

units.obligation_text: A pathologist who receives any other specific payment, fee, or reimbursement in connection with the autopsy from the miner’s widow/widower, his/her family, his/her estate, or any other Federal agency will not receive compensation from NIOSH.
units.action_summary: If the pathologist receives other specific payment related to the autopsy, the pathologist will not receive compensation from NIOSH.

units.obligation_text: Each autopsy for which a claim for payment is submitted pursuant to this subpart must be performed in a manner consistent with standard autopsy procedures such as those, for example, set forth in Autopsy Performance & Reporting, third edition (Kim A. Collins, ed., College of American Pathologists, 2017).
units.action_summary: Autopsies claimed for payment must be performed consistent with specified standard autopsy procedures.

units.obligation_text: Copies of this document may be borrowed from NIOSH.
units.action_summary: Copies of the referenced autopsy performance document may be borrowed from NIOSH.

units.obligation_text: Each autopsy must include: (list of required examinations, measurements, specimens, and submissions).
units.action_summary: Each autopsy claimed must include specified examinations, measurements, and specimen submissions as listed in paragraphs (b)(1)-(7).

units.obligation_text: Gross and microscopic examination of the lungs, pulmonary pleura, and tracheobronchial lymph nodes.
units.action_summary: Must perform gross and microscopic examination of lungs, pleura, and tracheobronchial lymph nodes.

units.obligation_text: Weights of the heart and each lung (these and all other measurements required under this subparagraph must be in the metric system).
units.action_summary: Must record weights of the heart and each lung, with all measurements in metric units.

units.obligation_text: Circumference of each cardiac valve when opened.
units.action_summary: Must measure and report the circumference of each cardiac valve when opened.

units.obligation_text: Thickness of right and left ventricles; these measurements must be made perpendicular to the ventricular surface and must not include trabeculations or pericardial fat. The right ventricle must be measured at a point midway between the tricuspid valve and the apex, and the left ventricle must be measured directly above the insertion of the anterior papillary muscle.
units.action_summary: Must measure ventricle thickness perpendicular to the surface excluding trabeculations/pericardial fat; measure right and left ventricles at specified anatomical points.

units.obligation_text: Size, number, consistency, location, description and other relevant details of all lesions of the lungs.
units.action_summary: Must document size, number, consistency, location, description, and other relevant details of all lung lesions.

units.obligation_text: Level of the diaphragm.
units.action_summary: Must record the level of the diaphragm.

units.obligation_text: From each type of suspected pneumoconiotic lesion, representative microscopic slides stained with hematoxylin eosin or other appropriate stain, and one formalin fixed, paraffin-impregnated block of tissue; a minimum of three stained slides and three blocks of tissue must be submitted.
units.action_summary: For each suspected pneumoconiotic lesion, must submit representative stained slides and one block of tissue, with a minimum of three stained slides and three blocks.

units.obligation_text: When no such lesion is recognized, similar material must be submitted from three separate areas of the lungs selected at random; a minimum of three stained slides and three formalin fixed, paraffin-impregnated blocks of tissue must be submitted.
units.action_summary: If no lesion is recognized, must submit similar material from three separate random lung areas and at least three stained slides and three blocks.

units.obligation_text: Needle biopsy techniques will not be accepted.
units.action_summary: Needle biopsy techniques are not acceptable for autopsies submitted for payment.

units.obligation_text: Prior to performing an autopsy, the pathologist must obtain written authorization from NIOSH and agreement regarding payment amount for services specified in § 37.202(a) by submitting an Authorization for Payment of Autopsy (form CDC #0.1585).
units.action_summary: Before performing the autopsy, the pathologist must obtain written authorization and payment agreement from NIOSH by submitting the specified form.

units.obligation_text: NIOSH will maintain up-to-date information about the availability of payments on its website. If payments are not available, the online Authorization of Payment for Autopsy form will not be active and available for completion on the NIOSH website.
units.action_summary: NIOSH will keep payment availability info current on its website; if payments are unavailable, the online authorization form will be inactive.

units.obligation_text: After receiving a completed authorization request form, NIOSH will reply in writing with an authorization determination within 3 working days.
units.action_summary: NIOSH will respond in writing with an authorization determination within 3 working days after receiving a completed authorization request.

units.obligation_text: After performance of an autopsy, each claim for payment under this subpart must be submitted to NIOSH and must include:
units.action_summary: After the autopsy, each payment claim must be submitted to NIOSH and include specified documents and materials.

units.obligation_text: An invoice (in duplicate) on the pathologist’s letterhead or billhead indicating the date of autopsy, the amount of the claim and a signed statement that the pathologist is not receiving any other specific compensation for the autopsy from the miner’s widow/widower, his/her surviving next-of-kin, the estate of the miner, or any other source.
units.action_summary: Claim must include a duplicate invoice with autopsy date, claim amount, and a signed statement that no other specific compensation is being received.

units.obligation_text: Completed Consent, Release and History Form for Autopsy (CDC/NIOSH (M)2.6). This form may be completed with the assistance of the pathologist, attending physician, family physician, or any other responsible person who can provide reliable information.
units.action_summary: Claim must include the completed Consent, Release and History Form; that form may be completed with assistance from specified persons.

units.obligation_text: The information, slides, and blocks of tissue required by this subpart.
units.action_summary: Claim must include the information, slides, and tissue blocks required elsewhere in this subpart.

units.obligation_text: Clinical abstract of terminal illness and other data that the pathologist determines is relevant.
units.action_summary: Claim must include a clinical abstract of the terminal illness and other relevant data determined by the pathologist.

units.obligation_text: Final summary, including final anatomical diagnoses, indicating presence or absence of simple and complicated pneumoconiosis, and correlation with clinical history if indicated.
units.action_summary: Claim must include a final summary with final anatomical diagnoses indicating presence/absence of pneumoconiosis and correlate with clinical history if indicated.

title: CMS-5517-P Display Version  Medicare Program; Merit-Based Incentive Payment System (MIPS) and Alternative Payment Model (APM) Incentive under the Physician Fee Schedule and Criteria for Physician -Focused Payment Models

units.obligation_text: MIPS applies to payments for items and services furnished by MIPS eligible clinicians on or after January 1, 2019.
units.actor: Payments for items and services furnished by MIPS eligible clinicians / CMS program
units.action_summary: The MIPS program applies to payments for items and services furnished by MIPS eligible clinicians beginning 1/1/2019.

units.obligation_text: For a year, a MIPS eligible clinician does not include an eligible clinician who:
units.actor: MIPS program / CMS (definition of who is a MIPS eligible clinician)
units.action_summary: Establishes exclusions for who is considered a MIPS eligible clinician for a year.

units.obligation_text: Is a Qualifying APM Participant as defined at §414.1305;
units.action_summary: Being a Qualifying APM Participant excludes an eligible clinician from being a MIPS eligible clinician for a year.

units.obligation_text: Is a Partial Qualifying APM Participant (as defined at §414.1305) for the most recent period for which data are available and who, for the performance period for the year, elects to not have measures and activities reported that are otherwise required to be reported by such professional under the MIPS;
units.action_summary: Partial QPs who elect not to report measures and activities are excluded from being MIPS eligible clinicians for a year.

units.obligation_text: For the performance period with respect to a year, does not exceed the low-volume threshold as defined at §414.1305.
units.action_summary: Clinicians below the low-volume threshold are excluded from being MIPS eligible clinicians for a year.

units.obligation_text: New Medicare-enrolled eligible clinicians, as defined at §414.1305, must not be treated as a MIPS eligible clinician until the subsequent year and the performance period for such subsequent year.
units.actor: CMS / the MIPS program (treatment of new Medicare-enrolled clinicians)
units.action_summary: New Medicare-enrolled clinicians are not treated as MIPS eligible clinicians until the following year and performance period.

units.obligation_text: In no case will a MIPS adjustment factor (or additional MIPS adjustment factor) apply to the items and services furnished by individuals who are not MIPS eligible clinicians, including the MIPS eligible clinicians described in paragraphs (b) and (c) of this section.
units.action_summary: MIPS adjustment factors cannot be applied to items/services furnished by individuals who are not MIPS eligible clinicians.

units.obligation_text: A group must meet the definition of a group at all times during the performance period for the MIPS payment year in order to have its performance assessed as a group.
units.action_summary: Groups must continuously meet the group definition during the performance period to be assessed as a group.

units.obligation_text: Individuals MIPS eligible clinicians within a group must aggregate their performance data across the TIN.
units.actor: Individual MIPS eligible clinicians within a group
units.action_summary: Clinicians in a group must aggregate performance data across the group's TIN.

units.obligation_text: A group that elects to have its performance assessed as a group will be assessed as a group across all four MIPS performance categories.
