title: Medicare Program: Merit-Based Incentive Payment System and Alternative Payment Model Incentive under the Physician Fee Schedule, and Criteria for Physician-Focused Payment Models

units.obligation_text: MIPS applies to payments for items and services furnished by MIPS eligible clinicians on or after January 1, 2019.
units.action_summary: The MIPS program applies to payments for items and services furnished by MIPS eligible clinicians beginning January 1, 2019.

units.obligation_text: For a year, a MIPS eligible clinician does not include an eligible clinician who:
units.action_summary: Certain eligible clinicians are excluded from being MIPS eligible clinicians for a year.

units.obligation_text: Is a Qualifying APM Participant as defined at Sec. 414.1305;
units.action_summary: An eligible clinician who is a Qualifying APM Participant is excluded from being a MIPS eligible clinician.

units.obligation_text: Is a Partial Qualifying APM Participant (as defined at Sec. 414.1305) for the most recent period for which data are available and who, for the performance period for the year, elects to not have measures and activities reported that are otherwise required to be reported by such professional under the MIPS;
units.action_summary: An eligible clinician who is a Partial QP and elects not to report required MIPS measures/activities is excluded from MIPS for that year.

units.obligation_text: For the performance period with respect to a year, does not exceed the low-volume threshold as defined at Sec. 414.1305.
units.action_summary: An eligible clinician whose billing/activity is at or below the low-volume threshold is excluded from being a MIPS eligible clinician for that year.

units.obligation_text: New Medicare-enrolled eligible clinicians, as defined at Sec. 414.1305, must not be treated as a MIPS eligible clinician until the subsequent year and the performance period for such subsequent year.
units.action_summary: Newly Medicare-enrolled eligible clinicians are not treated as MIPS eligible clinicians until the next year and its performance period.

units.obligation_text: In no case will a MIPS adjustment factor (or additional MIPS adjustment factor) apply to the items and services furnished by individuals who are not MIPS eligible clinicians, including the MIPS eligible clinicians described in paragraphs (b) and (c) of this section.
units.action_summary: MIPS adjustment factors will not be applied to items and services furnished by individuals who are not MIPS eligible clinicians (including those excluded under (b) and (c)).

units.obligation_text: The following way is for individual MIPS eligible clinicians to have their performance assessed as a group:
units.action_summary: Introductory statement describing how clinicians may have performance assessed as a group.

units.obligation_text: As part of a single TIN associated with two or more MIPS eligible clinicians, as identified by a NPI, that have their Medicare billing rights reassigned to the TIN.
units.action_summary: Clinicians are assessed as a group when they are part of a single TIN with reassigned Medicare billing rights and two or more clinicians.

units.obligation_text: A group must meet the definition of a group at all times during the performance period for the MIPS payment year in order to have its performance assessed as a group.
units.action_summary: A group must continuously meet the regulatory definition of a group during the performance period to be assessed as a group.

units.obligation_text: Individuals MIPS eligible clinicians within a group must aggregate their performance data across the TIN.
units.actor: individual MIPS eligible clinicians within a group
units.action_summary: Clinicians in a group are required to aggregate performance data across the group's TIN.

units.obligation_text: A group that elects to have its performance assessed as a group will be assessed as a group across all four MIPS performance categories.
units.action_summary: A group electing group assessment will be evaluated across all four MIPS performance categories.

units.obligation_text: A group must adhere to an election process established and required by CMS.
units.action_summary: Groups are required to follow the CMS-established election process to be assessed as a group.

units.obligation_text: MIPS eligible clinicians and groups must submit measures, objectives, and activities for the quality, CPIA, and advancing care information performance categories.
units.action_summary: Clinicians and groups are required to submit specified measures/objectives/activities for the listed performance categories.

units.obligation_text: An individual MIPS eligible clinician may elect to submit their MIPS data using:
units.action_summary: Individual clinicians are permitted to choose among specified data submission mechanisms.

units.obligation_text: A qualified registry for the quality, CPIA, or advancing care information performance categories;
units.action_summary: Clinicians may submit data via a qualified registry for the listed performance categories.

units.obligation_text: The EHR submission mechanism (which includes submission of data by health IT vendors on behalf of MIPS eligible clinicians) for the quality, CPIA, or advancing care information performance categories;
units.actor: individual MIPS eligible clinician / health IT vendors
units.action_summary: Clinicians (or their health IT vendors) may submit data via the EHR submission mechanism for the listed categories.

units.obligation_text: A QCDR for the quality, CPIA, or advancing care information performance categories;
units.action_summary: Clinicians may submit data via a QCDR for the listed performance categories.

units.obligation_text: Medicare Part B claims for the quality performance category; or
units.action_summary: Clinicians may submit quality performance category data via Medicare Part B claims.

units.obligation_text: Attestation for the CPIA and advancing care information performance categories.
units.action_summary: Clinicians may submit CPIA and advancing care information data via attestation.

units.obligation_text: Groups may submit their MIPS data using:
units.action_summary: Groups are permitted to choose among specified data submission mechanisms.

units.obligation_text: A CMS Web Interface (for groups comprised of at least 25 MIPS eligible clinicians) for the quality, CPIA, and advancing care information performance categories;
units.actor: groups of 25 or more MIPS eligible clinicians
units.action_summary: Groups of 25+ clinicians may submit via the CMS Web Interface for the listed categories.

units.obligation_text: A CMS-approved survey vendor for groups that elect to include the CAHPS for MIPS survey as a quality measure. units.action_summary: Groups may use a CMS-approved survey vendor to submit CAHPS data if they elect that survey, and such groups must use one of the other listed mechanisms to submit other quality information.

units.obligation_text: Except as described in paragraph (c)(6) of this section, MIPS eligible clinicians and groups may elect to submit information via multiple mechanisms; however, they must use the same identifier for all performance categories and they may only use one submission mechanism per performance category.
units.action_summary: Clinicians/groups may elect multiple submission mechanisms overall but are required to use the same identifier across categories and are limited to one submission mechanism per category.

units.obligation_text: There are no data submission requirements for the resource use performance category and for certain quality measures used to assess performance on the quality performance category and for certain activities in the CPIA performance category.
units.action_summary: No data submissions are required for the resource use category and certain specified measures/activities; CMS will calculate performance using claims data.

units.obligation_text: For the qualified registry, QCDR, EHR, and attestation submission mechanisms shall be March 31 following the close of the performance period.

units.obligation_text: For Medicare Part B claims, shall be on claims with dates of service during the performance period that must be processed no later than 90 days following the close of the performance period.

units.obligation_text: For the CMS Web Interface, shall be an eight-week period following the close of the performance period. The period shall begin no earlier than January 1 and end no later than March 31.

units.obligation_text: Performance in the quality performance category will comprise: 50 percent of a MIPS eligible clinician's composite performance score for 2019.

units.action_summary: For 2020, the quality category accounts for 45% of the composite performance score.

units.obligation_text: Performance in the quality performance category will comprise: 30 percent of a MIPS eligible clinician's composite performance score for each year thereafter.
units.action_summary: From 2021 onward, the quality category accounts for 30% of the composite performance score.

If fewer than six measures apply to the MIPS eligible clinician or group, report on each measure that is applicable.
units.action_summary: For a 12-month period, clinicians/groups must report at least six measures (including cross-cutting and outcome measures), or alternatives if fewer measures apply.

units.obligation_text: Subject to paragraph (a)(1)(i) of this section, MIPS eligible clinicians and groups can either select their measures from the complete MIPS final measure list or a subset of that list, MIPS specialty-specific measure sets, as designated by CMS.

units.obligation_text: Groups that elect this reporting mechanism must select an additional group data submission mechanism in order to meet the data submission criteria for the MIPS quality performance category.
units.action_summary: Groups using CAHPS must also choose another submission mechanism to meet overall quality data submission criteria.

units.obligation_text: MIPS eligible clinicians who are non-patient-facing eligible clinicians, as defined at Sec. 414.1305, are not required to submit data on a cross-cutting measure.
units.action_summary: Non-patient-facing clinicians are exempt from the cross-cutting measure submission requirement.

units.obligation_text: MIPS eligible clinicians and groups submitting quality measures data using the QCDR, qualified registry, or EHR submission mechanism must submit data on at least 90 percent of the MIPS eligible clinician or group's patients that meet the measure's denominator criteria, regardless of payer.

units.action_summary: These submitters must include at least 90% of eligible patients meeting denominator criteria when submitting quality measure data.

units.obligation_text: MIPS eligible clinicians submitting quality measures data using Medicare Part B claims, must submit data on at least 80 percent of the applicable Medicare Part B patients.

units.obligation_text: Groups submitting quality measures data using the CMS Web Interface or a CMS-approved survey vendor to submit the CAHPS for MIPS survey must meet the data submission requirement on the sample of the Medicare Part B patients CMS provides.
units.actor: groups using CMS Web Interface or CMS-approved survey vendor
units.action_summary: Such groups must meet data submission requirements based on the CMS-provided sample of Medicare Part B patients.

units.obligation_text: Performance in the resource use performance category comprises: 10 percent of a MIPS eligible clinician's composite performance score for MIPS payment year 2019.
units.action_summary: For 2019, resource use makes up 10% of the composite performance score.

units.obligation_text: Performance in the resource use performance category comprises: 15 percent of a MIPS eligible clinician's composite performance score for MIPS payment year 2020.
units.action_summary: For 2020, resource use makes up 15% of the composite performance score.

units.obligation_text: Performance in the resource use performance category comprises: 30 percent of a MIPS eligible clinician's composite performance score for each year thereafter.
units.action_summary: From 2021 onward, resource use makes up 30% of the composite performance score.

units.obligation_text: Subject to CMS's authority to reweight performance category weights under section 1848(q)(5)(F) of the Act, performance in the CPIA performance category comprises: 15 percent of an MIPS eligible clinician's composite performance score for MIPS payment year 2019 and for each year thereafter.
units.action_summary: CPIA accounts for 15% of the composite performance score for 2019 and thereafter (subject to CMS reweighting authority).

units.obligation_text: The CPIA inventory shall include one or more of the following criteria (in any order):
units.action_summary: The CPIA inventory is required to include one or more of the listed criteria.

units.obligation_text: Relevant to an existing CPIA subcategory (or a proposed new subcategory).
units.action_summary: One CPIA inclusion criterion is that the activity be relevant to an existing or proposed CPIA subcategory.

units.obligation_text: Importance of activity toward achieving improved beneficiary health outcome.
units.action_summary: A CPIA inclusion criterion is importance toward improving beneficiary health outcomes.

units.obligation_text: Importance of activity that could lead to improvement in practice to reduce healthcare disparities.
units.action_summary: A CPIA inclusion criterion is potential to reduce healthcare disparities.

units.obligation_text: Aligned with patient-centered medical home.
units.action_summary: A CPIA inclusion criterion is alignment with patient-centered medical home principles.

units.obligation_text: Representative of activities that multiple providers could perform (for example, primary care, specialty care).
units.action_summary: A CPIA inclusion criterion is that activities be performable by multiple provider types.

units.obligation_text: Feasible to implement, recognizing importance in minimizing provider burden, especially for small (consisting of 15 or fewer clinicians), practices located in rural areas, and geographic HPSAs designated by HRSA.
units.action_summary: A CPIA inclusion criterion is feasibility and minimizing provider burden, especially for small/rural/HPSA practices.

units.obligation_text: CMS is able to be validate the activity; or
units.action_summary: A CPIA inclusion criterion is that CMS can validate the activity.

units.obligation_text: Evidence supports that an activity has a high probability of contributing to improved beneficiary health outcomes.
units.action_summary: A CPIA inclusion criterion is supporting evidence that the activity likely improves beneficiary outcomes.

title: Display Version CMS-1648-P  Medicare and Medicaid Program;  CY 2017 Home Health Prospective Payment System Rate Update; Home Health Value -Based Purchasing Model; and Home Health Quality Reporting Requirements

units.obligation_text: The coinsurance liability of the beneficiary or other person for DME or applicable disposable devices (as defined in section 1834(s)(2)) furnished as a home health service is 20 percent of the customary (insofar as reasonable) charge for the services.
units.action_summary: Pay coinsurance equal to 20% of the customary charge for DME and applicable disposable devices furnished as a home health service.

units.obligation_text: CMS imputes the cost for each episode by multiplying the national per-15 minute unit amount of each discipline by the number of 15 minute units in the discipline and computing the total imputed cost for all disciplines.
units.action_summary: Compute (impute) episode costs by multiplying national per-15-minute unit amounts by number of 15-minute units per discipline and summing across disciplines.

units.obligation_text: Competing home health agencies will be evaluated using a set of quality measures.
units.action_summary: Competing HHAs are subject to evaluation using a set of quality measures.

units.obligation_text: Subject to the limitations on review under section 1115A of the Act, a HHA may submit a request for recalculation under this section if it wishes to dispute the calculation of the following:
units.action_summary: May submit a request to recalculate specified calculations if disputing them (subject to statutory limitations).

units.obligation_text: A recalculation request must be submitted in writing within 15 calendar days after CMS posts the HHA-specific information on the HHVBP Secure Portal, in a time and manner specified by CMS.
units.action_summary: Submit recalculation requests in writing within 15 calendar days after CMS posts HHA-specific information on the HHVBP Secure Portal, in the specified time and manner.

units.obligation_text: (i) The provider’s name, address associated with the services delivered, and CMS Certification Number (CCN).
units.action_summary: Include provider name, service address, and CMS Certification Number (CCN) in the recalculation request.

units.obligation_text: (ii) The basis for requesting recalculation to include the specific quality measure data that the HHA believes is inaccurate or the calculation the HHA believes is incorrect.
units.action_summary: Provide the basis for requesting recalculation, specifying which quality measure data or calculation is believed inaccurate.

units.obligation_text: (iii) Contact information for a person at the HHA with whom CMS or its agent can communicate about this request, including name, e-mail address, telephone number, and mailing address (must include physical address, not just a post office box).
units.action_summary: Provide contact information (name, email, phone, physical mailing address) for a person at the HHA for communications about the request.

units.obligation_text: (iv) The HHA may include in the request for reconsideration additional documentary evidence that CMS should consider.
units.action_summary: May include additional documentary evidence for CMS to consider in the request.

units.obligation_text: Such documents may not include data that was to have been filed by the applicable data submission deadline, but may include evidence of timely submission.
units.action_summary: May not include data that should have been filed by the submission deadline; may include evidence that submission was timely.

units.obligation_text: In conducting the recalculation, CMS will review the applicable measures and performance scores, the evidence and findings upon which the determination was based, and any additional documentary evidence submitted by the home health agency.
units.action_summary: CMS will review specified measures, performance scores, evidence, findings, and any documentary evidence submitted by the HHA during recalculation.

units.obligation_text: CMS may also review any other evidence it believes to be relevant to the recalculation.
units.action_summary: CMS may review any other evidence it deems relevant to the recalculation.

units.obligation_text: CMS will issue a written notification of findings.
units.action_summary: CMS will provide a written notification of the recalculation findings.

units.obligation_text: A recalculation decision is subject to the request for reconsideration process in accordance with paragraph (b) of this section.
units.action_summary: A recalculation decision can be reconsidered through the reconsideration process described in paragraph (b).

units.obligation_text: A home health agency may request reconsideration of the recalculation of the annual total performance score and payment adjustment percentage following a recalculation request submitted under §484.335(a) or the decision to deny a HHA’s recalculation request submitted under paragraph (a) of this section.
units.action_summary: May request reconsideration of the recalculation of annual total performance score and payment adjustment percentage following a recalculation request or denial.

units.obligation_text: The request for reconsideration must be submitted via the HHVBP Secure Portal within 15 calendar days from CMS’ notification to the HHA contact of the outcome of the recalculation process.
units.action_summary: Submit reconsideration requests via the HHVBP Secure Portal within 15 calendar days from CMS' notification of recalculation outcome.

units.obligation_text: (i) The name of the HHA, address associated with the services delivered, and CMS Certification Number (CCN).
units.action_summary: Include HHA name, service address, and CMS Certification Number (CCN) in the reconsideration request.

units.obligation_text: (ii) The basis for requesting reconsideration to include the specific quality measure data that the HHA believes is inaccurate or the calculation the HHA believes is incorrect.
units.action_summary: Provide the basis for requesting reconsideration, specifying which quality measure data or calculation is believed inaccurate.

units.obligation_text: (iii) Contact information for a person at the HHA with whom CMS or its agent can communicate about this request, including name, e-mail address, telephone number, and mailing address (must include physical address, not just a post office box).
units.action_summary: Provide contact information (name, email, phone, physical mailing address) for a person at the HHA for communications about the reconsideration request.

units.obligation_text: (iv) The HHA may include in the request for reconsideration additional documentary evidence that CMS should consider.
units.action_summary: May include additional documentary evidence in the reconsideration request for CMS to consider.

units.obligation_text: Such documents may not include data that was to have been filed by the applicable data submission deadline,
units.action_summary: May not include data that should have been filed by the applicable data submission deadline as part of the documentary evidence.

units.obligation_text: but may include evidence of timely submission.
units.action_summary: May include evidence demonstrating timely submission.

units.obligation_text: In conducting the reconsideration review, CMS will review the applicable measures and performance scores, the evidence and findings upon which the determination was based, and any additional documentary evidence submitted by the HHA.
units.action_summary: CMS will review specified measures, performance scores, evidence, findings, and any documentary evidence submitted by the HHA in the reconsideration review.

units.obligation_text: CMS may also review any other evidence it believes to be relevant to the reconsideration.
units.action_summary: CMS may review any other evidence it considers relevant to the reconsideration.

units.obligation_text: The HHA must prove its case by a preponderance of the evidence with respect to issues of fact
units.action_summary: HHA has the burden to prove factual issues by a preponderance of the evidence in the reconsideration.

units.obligation_text: CMS reconsideration officials will issue a written determination.
units.action_summary: CMS reconsideration officials will issue a written determination on the reconsideration.

title: CY 2017 Hospital Outpatient PPS Policy Changes and Payment Rate and Ambulatory Surgical Center Payment System Policy Changes and Payment Rates.  CMS-1656-P OFR Display

units.obligation_text: Beginning with the CY 2017 payment determination year, data collected must be submitted during the time period of January 1 to May 15 in the year prior to the payment determination year.
units.actor: entities submitting quality measure data via a CMS online data submission tool (e.g., ASCs)
units.action_summary: Submit collected quality measure data between January 1 and May 15 in the year prior to the payment determination year.

units.obligation_text: ASCs may request an extension or exemption within 90 days of the date that the extraordinary circumstance occurred.
units.action_summary: ASCs may request an extension or exemption within 90 days after an extraordinary circumstance.

units.obligation_text: Ambulatory surgical centers must use an approved OAS CAHPS survey vendor to administer and submit OAS CAHPS data to CMS.
units.action_summary: Use an approved OAS CAHPS survey vendor to administer and submit OAS CAHPS data to CMS.

units.obligation_text: CMS approves an application for an entity to administer the OAS CAHPS survey as a vendor on behalf of one or more ambulatory surgical centers when the applicant has met the Minimum Survey Requirements and Rules of Participation ... and agrees to comply with the current survey administration protocols ...
units.actor: CMS and OAS CAHPS survey vendor applicants
units.action_summary: CMS will approve an entity as an OAS CAHPS vendor only if the applicant meets Minimum Survey Requirements and Rules and agrees to comply with current protocols.
units.modal_raw: approves when / has met / agrees to comply

units.obligation_text: Applicant has met the Minimum Survey Requirements and Rules of Participation that can be found on the official OAS CAHPS Web site.
units.actor: Applicant entity seeking OAS CAHPS vendor approval
units.action_summary: Meet the Minimum Survey Requirements and Rules of Participation as listed on the OAS CAHPS website as a condition for approval.

units.obligation_text: Applicant ... agrees to comply with the current survey administration protocols that can be found on the official OAS CAHPS Web site.
units.actor: Applicant entity seeking OAS CAHPS vendor approval
units.action_summary: Agree to comply with current OAS CAHPS survey administration protocols as a condition for approval.

units.obligation_text: Effective January 1, 2017, for cost reporting periods beginning on or after January 1, 2017, items and services that are provided by an off-campus provider-based department ... that do not meet the definition of excepted items and services under § 419.48(a).
units.actor: Items and services provided by off-campus provider-based departments (and payers/CMS in payment determination)
units.action_summary: Items and services provided by an off-campus provider-based department that do not meet 'excepted' criteria are excluded from payment under the hospital outpatient prospective payment system effective Jan 1, 2017.

units.obligation_text: Outlier payments made to CMHCs for services provided on or after January 1, 2017 are subject to a cap ... so that each CMHC’s total outlier payments for the calendar year do not exceed 8 percent of that CMHC’s total per diem payments for the calendar year.
units.actor: Community mental health centers (CMHCs) / outlier payment program
units.action_summary: Cap outlier payments to each CMHC so total outlier payments for the year do not exceed 8% of that CMHC's total per diem payments.
units.modal_raw: are subject to / do not exceed

units.obligation_text: For all device-intensive procedures (defined as having a device offset of greater than 40 percent), the device offset portion of the device-intensive procedure payment is subtracted prior to determining the program payment and beneficiary copayment amounts identified in paragraph (b)(1)(ii) of this section.
units.action_summary: Subtract the device offset portion from the device-intensive procedure payment before calculating program payment and beneficiary copayment amounts.

units.obligation_text: Hospital outpatient departments must use an approved OAS CAHPS survey vendor to administer and submit OAS CAHPS data to CMS.
units.action_summary: Use an approved OAS CAHPS survey vendor to administer and submit OAS CAHPS data to CMS.

units.obligation_text: CMS approves an application for an entity to administer the OAS CAHPS Survey as a vendor ... when the applicant has met the Minimum Survey Requirements and Rules of Participation ... and agrees to comply with the current survey administration protocols ...
units.action_summary: CMS will approve an entity as an OAS CAHPS vendor only if the applicant meets Minimum Survey Requirements and Rules and agrees to comply with current protocols.
units.modal_raw: approves when / has met / agrees to comply

units.obligation_text: An entity must be an approved OAS CAHPS Survey vendor in order to administer and submit OAS CAHPS Survey data to CMS on behalf of one or more hospital outpatient departments.
units.actor: Entities wishing to administer and submit OAS CAHPS Survey data on behalf of hospital outpatient departments
units.action_summary: Be an approved OAS CAHPS Survey vendor to administer and submit OAS CAHPS Survey data for hospital outpatient departments.

units.obligation_text: Excepted items and services are items or services that are furnished on or after January 1, 2017— (1) In a dedicated emergency department ...; or (2) By an off-campus provider-based department that submitted a bill for a covered OPD service prior to November 2, 2015, are furnished at the same location that the department was furnishing such services as of November 1, 2015, and are in the same clinical family of services as the services that the department furnished prior to November 2, 2015.
units.actor: Items and services / off-campus provider-based departments
units.action_summary: Define 'excepted' items/services as those furnished on/after Jan 1, 2017 either in a dedicated ED or by off-campus provider-based departments meeting the specified billing/location/clinical-family criteria.

units.obligation_text: For the purpose of this section, “off-campus provider-based department” means a department of a provider ... that is not located on the campus ... or within the distance described in such definition from a remote location of a hospital ... that meets the requirements for provider-based status under § 413.65 of this chapter.
units.action_summary: Define 'off-campus provider-based department' as a department not on campus or within the specified distance that meets provider-based status requirements under § 413.65.

units.obligation_text: CMS limits the eligibility of a pass-through payment established under this section to a period of at least 2 years, but not more than 3 years, beginning on the first date on which pass-through payment is made.
units.action_summary: Limit pass-through payment eligibility to a minimum of 2 years and a maximum of 3 years from the first pass-through payment date.

units.obligation_text: The number of observed events divided by the number of expected events is greater than 1.85.
units.actor: Transplant center performance metric (observed/expected events ratio)
units.action_summary: Set a threshold where an observed-to-expected events ratio greater than 1.85 is the specified criterion in this context.

units.obligation_text: The number of observed events divided by the number of expected events is greater than 1.85.
units.actor: Transplant center performance metric (observed/expected events ratio) for re-approval
units.action_summary: Set a threshold where an observed-to-expected events ratio greater than 1.85 is the specified criterion for re-approval context.

units.obligation_text: If a deceased person meets the criteria specified in paragraphs (1) through (5) of this definition, the death of the person would be classified as an eligible death, unless the donor meets any of the following criteria: ...
units.actor: Classification of a deceased person as an 'eligible death' for organ donation
units.action_summary: Classify a deceased person as an eligible death for organ donation if criteria (1)-(5) are met, unless disqualifying criteria apply.

units.obligation_text: Who is 75 years old or younger;
units.action_summary: Deceased must be 75 years old or younger to meet eligible-death criterion.

units.obligation_text: Who is legally declared dead by neurologic criteria in accordance with State or local law;
units.action_summary: Deceased must be legally declared dead by neurologic criteria per state or local law.

units.obligation_text: Whose body weight is 5 kg or greater;
units.action_summary: Deceased must weigh at least 5 kg to meet eligible-death criterion.

units.obligation_text: Whose body mass Index (BMI) is 50 kg/m2 or less;
units.action_summary: Deceased must have BMI of 50 kg/m2 or less to meet eligible-death criterion.

units.obligation_text: Who had at least one kidney, liver, heart, or lung that is deemed to meet the eligible data definition as follows: (i)-(iv) ...
units.action_summary: At least one of the major organs must be initially deemed to meet eligible data definitions, subject to organ-specific exceptions.

units.obligation_text: The kidney would be initially deemed to meet the eligible data definition unless the donor meets one of the following: (A) Is more than 70 years of age; (B) Is age 50-69 years with history of Type 1 diabetes for more than 20 years; (C) Has polycystic kidney disease; (D) Has glomerulosclerosis equal to or more than 20 percent by kidney biopsy; (E) Has terminal serum creatinine greater than 4/0 mg/dl; (F) Has chronic renal failure; or (G) Has no urine output for at least or more than 24 hours;
units.actor: Kidney organ initial deeming / donor characteristics
units.action_summary: Kidney is initially deemed eligible unless donor meets any listed disqualifying kidney-specific criteria (age >70, specified diseases, labs, etc.).
units.modal_raw: would be initially deemed unless / has

units.obligation_text: The liver would be initially deemed to meet the eligible data definition unless the donor has one of the following: (A) Cirrhosis; (B) Terminal total bilirubin equal to or more than 4 mg/dl; (C) Portal hypertension; (D) Macrosteatosis equal to or more than 50 percent or fibrosis equal to or more than stage II; (E) Fulminant hepatic failure; or (F) Terminal AST/ALT of more than 700 U/L.
units.actor: Liver organ initial deeming / donor characteristics
units.action_summary: Liver is initially deemed eligible unless donor has any listed liver-specific disqualifying conditions.
units.modal_raw: would be initially deemed unless / has

units.obligation_text: The heart would be initially deemed to meet the eligible data definition unless the donor meets one of the following: (A) Is more than 60 years of age; (B) Is at least or more than 45 years of age with a history of at least or more than 10 years of HTN or at least or more than 10 years of type 1 diabetes; (C) Has a history of Coronary Artery Bypass Graft (CABG); (D) Has a history of coronary stent/intervention; (E) Has a current or past medical history of myocardial infarction (MI); (F) Has a severe vessel diagnosis ... ; (G) Has acute myocarditis and/or endocarditis; (H) Has heart failure due to cardiomyopathy; (I) Has an internal defibrillator or pacemaker; (J) Has moderate to severe single valve or 2-valve disease ...; (K) Has serial echo results showing severe global hypokinesis; (L) Has myxoma; or (M) Has congenital defects ... .
units.actor: Heart organ initial deeming / donor characteristics
units.action_summary: Heart is initially deemed eligible unless donor meets any listed heart-specific disqualifying conditions.
units.modal_raw: would be initially deemed unless / has

units.obligation_text: The lung would be initially deemed to meet the eligible data definition unless the donor meets one of the following: (A) Is more than 65 years of age; (B) Is diagnosed with COPD; (C) Has terminal PaO2/FiO2 less than 250 mmHg; (D) Has asthma (with daily prescription); (E) Asthma is the cause of death; (F) Has pulmonary fibrosis; (G) Has previous lobectomy; (H) Has multiple blebs documented on CAT Scan; (I) Has pneumonia as indicated on CT, X-ray, bronchoscopy, or cultures; (J) Has bilateral severe pulmonary contusions as per CT
units.actor: Lung organ initial deeming / donor characteristics
units.action_summary: Lung is initially deemed eligible unless donor meets any listed lung-specific disqualifying conditions.
units.modal_raw: would be initially deemed unless / has

units.obligation_text: The donor was taken to the operating room with the intent for the OPO to recover organs for transplant and all organs were deemed not medically suitable for transplantation;
units.action_summary: If donor was taken to OR with intent to recover organs and all organs were deemed not medically suitable, donor is disqualified from eligible death classification.

units.obligation_text: The donor exhibits any of the following active infections (specific diagnoses) of-- (A) Bacterial: Tuberculosis, Gangrenous bowel or perforated bowel or intra-abdominal sepsis; (B) Viral: HIV infection ... (see text for full list); (C) Fungal: Active infection with Cryptococcus, Aspergillus, Histoplasma, Coccidioides, Active candidemia or invasive yeast infection; (D) Parasites: Active infection with Trypanosoma cruzi (Chagas'), Leishmania, Strongyloides, or Malaria (Plasmodium sp.); or (E) Prion: Creutzfeldt-Jacob Disease.
units.action_summary: Donor with any listed active infections (bacterial, viral, fungal, parasitic, prion) is disqualified from eligible death classification, subject to specified exceptions.

units.obligation_text: The following are general exclusions: (i) Aplastic anemia, Agranulocytosis; (ii) Current malignant neoplasms except non-melanoma skin cancers ...; (iii) Previous malignant neoplasms with current evident metastatic disease; (iv) A history of melanoma; (v) Hematologic malignancies ...; (vi) Active Fungal, Parasitic, Viral, or Bacterial Meningitis or Encephalitis; and (vii) No discernable cause of death.
units.action_summary: Donors with any listed general exclusions (certain malignancies, infections, no discernable cause of death, etc.) are excluded from eligible death classification.

units.obligation_text: Notwithstanding paragraph (6)(ii)(B) of this definition, an HIV positive organ procured for the purpose of transplantation into an HIV positive recipient would be an exception to an active infection rule out.
units.actor: Donor and transplant recipient (HIV positive organ into HIV positive recipient)
units.action_summary: An HIV-positive organ intended for transplantation into an HIV-positive recipient is an exception to the active infection rule-out.

units.obligation_text: At least 2 of the 3 yield measures specified in paragraph (a)(3)(i) of this section are no more than 1 standard deviation below the national mean, averaged over the 4 years of the recertification cycle, and the OPO data reports must meet the rules and requirements of the most current OPTN aggregate donor yield measure:
units.action_summary: OPOs must have at least 2 of 3 yield measures within 1 standard deviation below the national mean (averaged over 4-year recertification) and must meet OPTN aggregate donor yield reporting rules.

units.obligation_text: A difference of at least 11 fewer observed organs per 100 donors than expected yield (Observed per 100 donors-Expected per 100 donors < -10);
units.actor: OPO performance metric (observed per 100 donors minus expected per 100 donors)
units.action_summary: One initial criterion is a deficit of at least 11 observed organs per 100 donors compared to expected yield (i.e., < -10).

units.obligation_text: A ratio of observed to expected yield less than 0.90;
units.action_summary: One initial criterion is an observed-to-expected yield ratio less than 0.90.

units.obligation_text: A two-sided p-value is less than 0.05.
units.action_summary: One initial criterion is a two-sided p-value less than 0.05.

units.obligation_text: The yield measures include pancreata used for islet cell transplantation as required by section 371(c) of the Public Health Service Act (42 U.S.C. 273(c)).
units.action_summary: Yield measures must include pancreata used for islet cell transplantation as required by statute.

units.obligation_text: At least 2 out of the 3 following yield measures specified in paragraph (b)(3)(i) of this section are no more than 1 standard deviation below the national mean, averaged over the 4 years of the recertification cycle, and the OPO data reports must meet the rules and requirements of the most current OPTN aggregate donor yield measure:
units.action_summary: OPOs must have at least 2 of 3 yield measures (per paragraph (b)(3)(i)) within 1 standard deviation below the national mean (averaged over 4 years) and meet OPTN reporting rules.

units.obligation_text: More than 10 fewer observed organs per 100 donors than expected yield (Observed per 100 donors-Expected per 100 donors < -10);
units.action_summary: One criterion is more than 10 fewer observed organs per 100 donors than expected (< -10).

units.obligation_text: A ratio of observed to expected yield less than 0.90;
units.action_summary: One criterion is observed-to-expected yield ratio less than 0.90.

units.obligation_text: A two-sided p-value is less than 0.05.
units.action_summary: One criterion is a two-sided p-value less than 0.05.

units.obligation_text: The yield measures include pancreata used for islet cell transplantation as required by section 371(c) of the Public Health Service Act (42 U.S.C. 273(c)).
units.action_summary: Yield measures must include pancreata used for islet cell transplantation as required by statute (alternate set).

units.obligation_text: The OPO must send complete documentation of donor information to the transplant center with the organ, including donor evaluation, the complete record of the donor’s management, documentation of consent, documentation of the pronouncement of death, and documentation for determining organ quality.
units.action_summary: Send complete donor documentation (evaluation, management record, consent, pronouncement of death, organ quality documentation) with the organ to the transplant center.

units.obligation_text: The OPO must physically send a paper copy of the following documentation with each organ: (i) Blood type; (ii) Blood subtype, if used for allocation; and (iii) Infectious disease testing results available at the time of organ packaging.
units.action_summary: Physically send paper copy of blood type, blood subtype (if used), and available infectious disease testing results with each organ.

units.obligation_text: The source documentation must be placed in a watertight container in either of the following: (i) A location specifically designed for documentation; or (ii) Between the inner and external transport materials.
units.actor: Organ Procurement Organization (OPO) / organ transport agents
units.action_summary: Place source documentation in a watertight container either in a documentation-specific location or between inner and external transport materials.

units.obligation_text: Two individuals, one of whom must be an OPO employee, must verify that the documentation that accompanies an organ to a transplant center is correct.
units.action_summary: Require verification by two individuals (one OPO employee) that accompanying organ documentation is correct.

units.obligation_text: Except for situations of immediate jeopardy or deficiencies other than failure to meet requirements of § 482.80 or § 482.82 of this chapter, CMS will consider such mitigating factors as may be appropriate ... in making a decision of initial and re-approval of a transplant center that does not meet the data submission, clinical experience, or outcome requirements:
units.action_summary: CMS will consider mitigating factors (except in immediate jeopardy or other specified situations) when deciding initial/re-approval for transplant centers that do not meet certain requirements.

units.obligation_text: Within 14 calendar days after CMS has issued formal written notice of a condition-level deficiency to the program, CMS must receive notification of the program's intent to seek mitigating factors approval or re-approval, and receive all information for consideration of mitigating factors within 120 calendar days of the CMS written notification for a deficiency due to data submission, clinical experience or outcomes at § 482.80 or § 482.82 of this chapter.
units.actor: Transplant program (applicant seeking mitigating factors) / CMS receiving party
units.action_summary: Program must notify CMS of intent to seek mitigating factors within 14 days and must submit all information for consideration within 120 days of CMS's written notification.

units.obligation_text: Failure to meet these timeframes may be the basis for denial of mitigating factors. However, CMS may permit an extension of the timeline for good cause, such as a declared public health emergency.
units.action_summary: Missing timeframes can lead to denial; CMS may permit extensions for good cause.

units.obligation_text: A Systems Improvement Agreement will be established for up to a 12-month period, subject to CMS’ discretion to determine if a shorter timeframe may suffice.
units.action_summary: CMS will establish a Systems Improvement Agreement for up to 12 months, but may set a shorter timeframe at its discretion.

units.obligation_text: At the hospital’s request, CMS may extend the agreement for up to an additional 6-month period.
units.action_summary: Upon hospital request, CMS may extend a Systems Improvement Agreement by up to 6 additional months.

units.obligation_text: A signed Systems Improvement Agreement remains in force even if a subsequent SRTR report indicates that the program has restored compliance with the CMS conditions of participation, except that CMS in its sole discretion may shorten the timeframe or allow modification to any portion of the elements of the Agreement in such a case.
units.actor: CMS and hospital (Systems Improvement Agreement parties)
units.action_summary: A signed Systems Improvement Agreement remains in effect despite later restored compliance, although CMS may shorten or modify it at its discretion.

units.obligation_text: Subject to the provisions of paragraph (a)(2) of this section, the criteria specified in this section are applicable for EPs, eligible hospitals and CAHs for 2015 through 2017.
units.actor: Eligible Professionals (EPs), eligible hospitals, and CAHs
units.action_summary: The meaningful use criteria in this section apply to EPs, eligible hospitals, and CAHs for 2015-2017, subject to paragraph (a)(2).

units.obligation_text: For 2017 only, EPs, eligible hospitals and CAHs that have successfully demonstrated meaningful use in a prior year have the option to use the criteria specified for 2018 in § 495.24 instead of the criteria specified for 2017 under paragraphs (e) and (f) of this section.
units.actor: EPs, eligible hospitals, and CAHs with prior-year meaningful use
units.action_summary: For 2017 only, entities that previously demonstrated meaningful use may choose to use 2018 criteria (§495.24) instead of 2017 criteria under paragraphs (e) and (f).

units.obligation_text: Eligible hospitals and CAHs attesting under the Medicare EHR Incentive Program must meet all objectives and associated measures of the meaningful use criteria specified under paragraph (e) of this section to meet the definition of a meaningful EHR user in 2015 and 2016 and must meet all objectives and associated measures of the meaningful use criteria specified under paragraph (f) of this section to meet the definition of a meaningful EHR user in 2017.
units.actor: Eligible hospitals and CAHs attesting under the Medicare EHR Incentive Program
units.action_summary: Meet all objectives and measures in paragraph (e) for 2015-2016 and paragraph (f) for 2017 to be a meaningful EHR user under Medicare.

units.obligation_text: Eligible hospitals and CAHs attesting under a State’s Medicaid EHR Incentive Program must meet all objectives and associated measures of the meaningful use criteria specified under paragraph (e) of this section to meet the definition of a meaningful EHR user in 2015 through 2017.
units.actor: Eligible hospitals and CAHs attesting under a State's Medicaid EHR Incentive Program
units.action_summary: Meet all objectives and measures in paragraph (e) for 2015-2017 to be a meaningful EHR user under a State Medicaid program.

units.obligation_text: If a measure (or associated objective) in paragraph (e) or (f) of this section references paragraph (d) of this section, the measure may be calculated by reviewing only the actions for patients whose records are maintained using CEHRT.
units.actor: Eligible hospitals and CAHs / measure calculators
units.action_summary: When referenced, measures may be calculated using only actions for patients whose records are maintained using CEHRT.

units.obligation_text: Conduct or review a security risk analysis in accordance with the requirements under 45 CFR 164.308(a)(1), including addressing the security (to include encryption) of ePHI created or maintained in CEHRT ... and implement security updates as necessary, and correct identified security deficiencies as part of the eligible hospital’s or CAH’s risk management process.
units.action_summary: Conduct or review a security risk analysis per 45 CFR, address security of ePHI (including encryption), implement security updates, and correct identified security deficiencies within the risk management process.

units.obligation_text: Subject to the provisions of paragraph (d) of this section, more than 10 percent of hospital discharge medication orders for permissible prescriptions are queried for a drug formulary and transmitted electronically using CEHRT.
units.action_summary: Ensure that more than 10% of discharge medication orders are queried for drug formulary and transmitted electronically using CEHRT.

units.obligation_text: Exclusion for nonapplicable objectives. ... any eligible hospital or CAH that does not have an internal pharmacy that can accept electronic prescriptions and is not located within 10 miles of any pharmacy that accepts electronic prescriptions at the start of their EHR reporting period.
units.action_summary: Hospitals/CAHs without an internal pharmacy and not located within 10 miles of an e-prescribing-capable pharmacy may be excluded from the e-prescribing objective.

units.obligation_text: The eligible hospital or CAH that transitions or refers their patient to another setting of care or provider of care must do the following: (A) Use CEHRT to create a summary of care record; and (B) Electronically transmit such summary to a receiving provider for more than 10 percent of transitions of care and referrals.
units.action_summary: When transitioning/referring patients, use CEHRT to create a summary of care and electronically transmit it for more than 10% of transitions/referrals.

units.obligation_text: More than 10 percent of all unique patients admitted to the eligible hospital’s or CAH’s inpatient or emergency department (POS 21 or 23) are provided patient specific education resources identified by CEHRT.
units.action_summary: Provide CEHRT-identified patient-specific education resources to more than 10% of unique admitted patients.

units.obligation_text: Subject to the provisions of paragraph (d) of this section, the eligible hospital or CAH performs medication reconciliation for more than 50 percent of transitions of care in which the patient is admitted to the eligible hospital’s or CAH’s inpatient or emergency department (POS 21 or 23).
units.action_summary: Perform medication reconciliation for more than 50% of relevant transitions of care where the patient is admitted to inpatient or ED.

units.obligation_text: More than 50 percent of all unique patients who are discharged from the inpatient or emergency department (POS 21 or 23) of an eligible hospital or CAH have timely access to view online, download, and transmit to a third party their health information.
units.action_summary: Ensure more than 50% of discharged patients have timely online access to view, download, and transmit their health information.

units.obligation_text: At least 1 patient (or patient-authorized representative) who is discharged from the inpatient or emergency department ... during the EHR reporting period views, downloads, or transmits to a third party his or her information during the EHR reporting period.
units.actor: Eligible hospital or CAH / discharged patients
units.action_summary: Ensure at least one discharged patient views, downloads, or transmits their health information during the EHR reporting period.

units.obligation_text: Any eligible hospital or CAH that is located in a county that does not have 50 percent or more of its housing units with 4Mbps broadband availability ... is excluded from paragraph (f)(8)(ii)(B) of this section.
units.actor: Eligible hospital or CAH located in low-broadband counties
units.action_summary: Hospitals/CAHs located in counties with less than 50% housing units at 4Mbps broadband are excluded from the VDT (view/download/transmit) measure requiring at least one patient action.

units.obligation_text: The eligible hospital or CAH is in active engagement with a public health agency to submit electronic public health data from CEHRT, except where prohibited, and in accordance with applicable law and practice.
units.action_summary: Be in active engagement with a public health agency to submit electronic public health data from CEHRT, except where prohibited and consistent with law.

units.obligation_text: In order to meet the objective under paragraph (f)(9)(i) of this section, an eligible hospital or CAH must choose from measures 1 through 4 (as described in paragraphs (f)(9)(ii)(A) through (D) of this section).
units.action_summary: Choose from one of the four specified public health engagement measures to meet the public health reporting objective.

units.obligation_text: Immunization measure. The eligible hospital or CAH is in active engagement with a public health agency to submit immunization data.
units.action_summary: Be in active engagement to submit immunization data to a public health agency.

units.obligation_text: Syndromic surveillance measure. The eligible hospital or CAH is in active engagement with a public health agency to submit syndromic surveillance data.
units.action_summary: Be in active engagement to submit syndromic surveillance data to a public health agency.

units.obligation_text: Specialized registry measure. The eligible hospital or CAH is in active engagement to submit data to a specialized registry.
units.action_summary: Be in active engagement to submit data to a specialized registry.

units.obligation_text: Electronic reportable laboratory result reporting measure. The eligible hospital or CAH is in active engagement with a public health agency to submit electronic reportable laboratory results.
units.action_summary: Be in active engagement to submit electronic reportable laboratory results to public health agencies.

units.obligation_text: Does not administer any immunizations to any of the populations for which data is collected by its jurisdiction’s immunization registry or immunization information system during the EHR reporting period.
units.actor: Eligible hospital or CAH (criterion for immunization exclusion)
units.action_summary: If a hospital/CAH does not administer immunizations to the relevant populations, it may be excluded from the immunization measure.

units.obligation_text: Operates in a jurisdiction for which no immunization registry or immunization information system is capable of accepting the specific standards required to meet the CEHRT definition at the start of the EHR reporting period.
units.actor: Eligible hospital or CAH (jurisdictional readiness criterion)
units.action_summary: Hospitals/CAHs in jurisdictions without registries capable of CEHRT standards may be excluded from the immunization measure.

units.obligation_text: Operates in a jurisdiction where no immunization registry or immunization information system has declared readiness to receive immunization data from the eligible hospital or CAH at the start of the EHR reporting period.
units.actor: Eligible hospital or CAH (jurisdictional readiness criterion)
units.action_summary: Hospitals/CAHs in jurisdictions where registries have not declared readiness may be excluded from the immunization measure.

units.obligation_text: Except as specified in paragraphs (a)(2) and (3) of this section, EPs must meet all objectives and associated measures of the Stage 3 criteria specified in paragraph (d) of this section to meet the definition of a meaningful EHR user.
units.action_summary: EPs must meet all Stage 3 objectives and measures in paragraph (d) to be considered meaningful EHR users, except as specified.

units.obligation_text: An EP may meet the criteria for 2 out of the 3 measures associated with an objective, rather than meeting the criteria for all 3 of the measures, if the EP meets all of the following requirements:
units.action_summary: EPs are permitted to satisfy an objective by meeting 2 of 3 associated measures if they meet the listed requirements.

units.obligation_text: Must ensure that the objective in paragraph (d) of this section includes an option to meet 2 out of the 3 associated measures.
units.action_summary: EP must ensure the objective provides an option to meet 2 of 3 measures (i.e., that such an option is available for that objective).

units.obligation_text: Meets the threshold for 2 out of the 3 measures for that objective.
units.action_summary: EP must meet the performance threshold for two of the three measures associated with the objective.

units.obligation_text: Attests to all 3 of the measures for that objective
units.action_summary: EP must attest to all three measures for the objective even if meeting only two thresholds.

units.obligation_text: An EP may exclude a particular objective ... if the EP meets all of the following requirements: (A) Meets the criteria in the applicable objective that would permit the exclusion. (B) Attests to the exclusion.
units.action_summary: EP may exclude an objective only if they meet the objective's exclusion criteria and attest to the exclusion.

units.obligation_text: An EP may exclude a measure within an objective ... by (1) Meets the criteria in the applicable measure or measures that would permit the exclusion; and (2) Attests to the exclusion or exclusions.
units.action_summary: EP may exclude a specific measure if they meet the measure's exclusion criteria and attest to the exclusion.

units.obligation_text: (B)(1) Meets the threshold; and (2) Attests to any remaining measure or measures.
units.action_summary: For measure-exclusion options, EP must meet required thresholds and attest to any remaining measures.

units.obligation_text: For Medicaid EPs who adopt, implement, or upgrade its CEHRT in their first payment year, the meaningful use objectives and associated measures of the Stage 3 criteria specified in paragraph (d) of this section apply beginning with the second payment year, and do not apply to the first payment year.
units.actor: Medicaid Eligible Professionals (EPs) who adopt/implement/upgrade CEHRT in first payment year
units.action_summary: Stage 3 objectives/measures do not apply in the first payment year for Medicaid EPs who adopt/implement/upgrade CEHRT; they apply beginning in the second payment year.

units.obligation_text: If a measure (or associated objective) in paragraph (d) of this section references paragraph (a)(5) of this section, the measure may be calculated by reviewing only the actions for patients whose records are maintained using CEHRT.
units.action_summary: When referenced, Stage 3 measures may be calculated using only actions for patients whose records are maintained using CEHRT.

title: Medicare Program: Hospital Outpatient Prospective Payment and Ambulatory Surgical Center Payment Systems and Quality Reporting Programs; Organ Procurement Organization Reporting and Communication; Transplant Outcome Measures and Documentation Requirements; etc.

units.obligation_text: For purposes of this paragraph (d), subject to applicable State law, an issuer is not considered to have discontinued offering all health insurance coverage in a market if—
units.action_summary: An issuer will not be treated as having discontinued offering all coverage in a market if one of the qualifying conditions below is met.

units.obligation_text: The issuer or a member of the issuer’s controlled group continues to offer and make available in the applicable market in the State at least one product of the issuer that is considered to be the same product as a product the issuer had been offering (as defined in §144.103 of this subchapter).
units.actor: the issuer or a member of the issuer’s controlled group
units.action_summary: Continue to offer at least one product that is considered the same as a previously offered product in the applicable market.
units.modal_raw: continues to offer and make available

units.obligation_text: The issuer continues to offer and make available at least one product in the applicable market in the State, even if such product is not considered to be the same product as a product the issuer had been offering (as defined in §144.103 of this subchapter), provided the issuer subjects that product to the rate review requirements under part 154 of this title (to the extent otherwise applicable to coverage of the same type and in the same market) as if that part applied to that product, and reasonably identifies a discontinued product that corresponds to the new product for purposes of such rate review.
units.action_summary: Continue to offer at least one product and, to qualify, subject that product to applicable rate review requirements and reasonably identify a corresponding discontinued product for rate review purposes.
units.modal_raw: continues to offer and make available; provided (must) subject

units.obligation_text: The product is offered by the same health insurance issuer (within the meaning of section 2791(b)(2) of the PHS Act), or a member of the issuer’s controlled group (as defined in paragraph (d) of this section);
units.actor: the product issuer or member of the issuer’s controlled group
units.action_summary: Condition specifying that the product is offered by the same issuer or a member of the issuer's controlled group for renewability purposes.

units.obligation_text: A health insurance issuer in the individual market must provide a limited open enrollment period for the events described in §155.420(d) of this subchapter, excluding §§155.420(d)(3) of this subchapter (concerning citizenship status), 155.420(d)(8) of this subchapter (concerning Indians), 155.420(d)(9) of this subchapter (concerning exceptional circumstances), and 155.420(d)(13) of this subchapter (concerning eligibility for insurance affordability programs or enrollment in the Exchange).
units.actor: a health insurance issuer in the individual market
units.action_summary: Provide a limited open enrollment period for the events listed in §155.420(d), with specified exclusions.

units.obligation_text: For purposes of this paragraph (d), subject to applicable State law, an issuer is not considered to have discontinued offering all health insurance coverage in a market if—

units.action_summary: Continue to offer at least one product and, to qualify, subject that product to rate review requirements and reasonably identify a corresponding discontinued product.

units.action_summary: Condition specifying that the product is offered by the same issuer or a member of the issuer's controlled group for purposes of the provision.

units.obligation_text: For purposes of this paragraph (e), subject to applicable State law, an issuer is not considered to have discontinued offering all health insurance coverage in a market if—
units.action_summary: Issuer will not be treated as having discontinued offering all coverage in a market if qualifying conditions are met (individual market).

units.obligation_text: The issuer or a member of the issuer’s controlled group continues to offer and make available in the applicable market in the State at least one product of the issuer that is considered to be the same product as a product the issuer had been offering (as defined in §144.103 of this subchapter).
