units.actor: the product issuer or member of the issuer’s controlled group
units.action_summary: Condition specifying that the product is offered by the same issuer or a member of the issuer's controlled group for the referenced provision.

units.obligation_text: The risk adjustment methodology is developed by HHS and published in advance of the benefit year in rulemaking; or
units.action_summary: HHS must develop and publish the risk adjustment methodology in advance of the benefit year through rulemaking.

units.obligation_text: Draft factors to be employed in the model, including but not limited to demographic factors, diagnostic factors, and utilization factors, if any, the dataset(s) to be used to calculate final coefficients, and the date by which final coefficients will be released in guidance;
units.action_summary: Include draft factors, datasets to calculate final coefficients, and the date for release of final coefficients in draft materials.

units.obligation_text: Remit to HHS an amount equal to the product of its monthly billable enrollment in the risk adjustment covered plan multiplied by the per-enrollee-per-month risk adjustment user fee specified in the annual HHS notice of benefit and payment parameters for the applicable benefit year.
units.action_summary: Remit monthly risk adjustment user fees to HHS equal to monthly billable enrollment times per-enrollee-per-month fee.

units.obligation_text: Beginning in the 2018 benefit year, validating enrollee health status through review of all relevant paid pharmacy claims;
units.action_summary: Validate enrollee health status by reviewing all relevant paid pharmacy claims beginning 2018 benefit year.

units.obligation_text: Within 15 calendar days of notification of the initial validation audit sample determined by HHS, in the manner set forth by HHS, an issuer must confirm the sample or file a discrepancy report to dispute the initial validation audit sample determined by HHS.
units.action_summary: Within 15 days of HHS notification of the initial validation audit sample, confirm the sample or file a discrepancy report to dispute it.

units.obligation_text: Within 30 calendar days of notification of the findings of a second validation audit or the calculation of a risk score error rate, in the manner set forth by HHS, an issuer must confirm the audit or error rate, or file a discrepancy report to dispute the findings of a second validation audit or the calculation of a risk score error rate as result of risk adjustment data validation.
units.action_summary: Within 30 days of notification of second audit findings or risk score error rate, confirm the audit/error rate or file a discrepancy report.

units.obligation_text: An issuer may appeal the findings of a second validation audit or the calculation of a risk score error rate as result of risk adjustment data validation, under the process set forth in §156.1220 of this subchapter.
units.action_summary: An issuer may appeal the second audit findings or calculated risk score error rate under §156.1220.

units.obligation_text: A State Exchange on the Federal platform that utilizes the Federal platform for certain SHOP functions, as set forth in paragraphs (f)(4)(i) through (vii), must—
units.actor: A State Exchange on the Federal platform
units.action_summary: State Exchanges using the Federal platform for SHOP functions must meet the following specific requirements.

units.obligation_text: If utilizing the Federal platform for SHOP eligibility, enrollment, or premium aggregation functions, establish standard processes for premium calculation, premium payment, and premium collection that are consistent with the requirements applicable in a Federally-facilitated SHOP under §155.705(b)(4);
units.actor: State Exchange on the Federal platform
units.action_summary: Establish standard processes for premium calculation, payment, and collection consistent with Federally-facilitated SHOP requirements when using the Federal platform for specified functions.

units.obligation_text: If utilizing the Federal platform for SHOP enrollment or premium aggregation functions, require its QHP issuers to make any changes to rates in accordance with the timeline applicable in a Federally-facilitated SHOP under §155.705(b)(6)(i)(A);
units.actor: State Exchange on the Federal platform
units.action_summary: Require QHP issuers to make rate changes according to the Federally-facilitated SHOP timeline when using Federal platform for enrollment or premium aggregation.

units.obligation_text: If utilizing the Federal platform for SHOP enrollment functions, establish minimum participation rate requirements and calculation methodologies that are consistent with those applicable in a Federally-facilitated SHOP under §155.705(b)(10);
units.actor: State Exchange on the Federal platform
units.action_summary: Establish minimum participation rate requirements and calculation methodologies consistent with Federally-facilitated SHOP when using Federal platform for enrollment.

units.obligation_text: If utilizing the Federal platform for SHOP enrollment or premium aggregation functions, establish employer contribution methodologies that are consistent with the methodologies applicable in a Federally-facilitated SHOP under §155.705(b)(11)(ii);
units.actor: State Exchange on the Federal platform
units.action_summary: Establish employer contribution methodologies consistent with Federally-facilitated SHOP when using the Federal platform for enrollment or premium aggregation.

units.obligation_text: If utilizing the Federal platform for SHOP enrollment functions, establish annual employee open enrollment period requirements that are consistent with §155.725(e)(2);
units.actor: State Exchange on the Federal platform
units.action_summary: Set annual employee open enrollment requirements consistent with §155.725(e)(2) when using Federal platform for enrollment.

units.obligation_text: If utilizing the Federal platform for SHOP enrollment functions, establish effective dates of coverage for an initial group enrollment or a group renewal that are consistent with the effective dates of coverage applicable in a Federally-facilitated SHOP under §155.725(h)(2);
units.actor: State Exchange on the Federal platform
units.action_summary: Establish effective dates of coverage for initial group enrollments or renewals consistent with Federally-facilitated SHOP rules when using Federal platform.

units.obligation_text: If utilizing the Federal platform for SHOP eligibility, enrollment, or premium aggregation functions, establish policies for the termination of SHOP coverage or enrollment that are consistent with the requirements applicable in a Federally-facilitated SHOP under §155.735.
units.actor: State Exchange on the Federal platform
units.action_summary: Establish termination policies for SHOP coverage/enrollment consistent with Federally-facilitated SHOP when using Federal platform.

units.obligation_text: For Exchanges and QHP issuers, beginning no later than the first day of the individual market open enrollment period for the 2017 benefit year, this standard also includes taglines on Web site content and any document that is critical for obtaining health insurance coverage or access to health care services through a QHP for qualified individuals, applicants, qualified employers, qualified employees, or enrollees.
units.action_summary: Exchanges and QHP issuers must include taglines on website content and critical documents by the specified date.

units.obligation_text: Such taglines must indicate the availability of language services in at least the top 15 languages spoken by the limited English proficient population of the relevant State or States, as determined in guidance published by the Secretary.
units.action_summary: Taglines must indicate availability of language services in at least the top 15 LEP languages for the State(s) as determined by HHS guidance.

units.obligation_text: If an Exchange is operated by an entity operating multiple Exchanges, or relies on an eligibility or enrollment platform that is relied on by multiple Exchanges, the Exchange may aggregate the limited English proficient populations across all the States served by the entity that operates the Exchange or its eligibility or enrollment platform to determine the top 15 languages required for taglines.
units.actor: an Exchange operated by a multi-Exchange entity
units.action_summary: Such Exchanges may aggregate LEP populations across served States to determine the top 15 languages for taglines.

units.obligation_text: A QHP issuer may aggregate the limited English proficient populations across all States served by the health insurance issuers within the issuer’s controlled group (as defined under §147.106(d)(3) of this subchapter), whether or not those health insurance issuers offer plans through the Exchange in each of those States, to determine the top 15 languages required for taglines.
units.action_summary: QHP issuers may aggregate LEP populations across States served by issuers in their controlled group to determine top 15 languages.

units.obligation_text: Exchanges and QHP issuers may satisfy tagline requirements with respect to Web site content if they post a Web link prominently on their home page that directs individuals to the full text of the taglines indicating how individuals may obtain language assistance services, and if they also include taglines on any critical standalone document linked to or embedded in the Web site.
units.action_summary: Exchanges and QHP issuers may comply with tagline requirements by posting a prominent link to the full taglines and including taglines on critical standalone documents.

units.obligation_text: For an agent or broker subject to §155.220(c)(3)(i), beginning on the first day of the individual market open enrollment period for the 2017 benefit year, or when such entity has been registered with the Exchange for at least 1 year, whichever is later, this standard also includes taglines on Web site content and any document that is critical for obtaining health insurance coverage or access to health care services through a QHP for qualified individuals, applicants, qualified employers, qualified employees, or enrollees.
units.actor: an agent or broker subject to §155.220(c)(3)(i)
units.action_summary: Covered agents and brokers must include taglines on website content and critical documents beginning on the specified date.

units.obligation_text: Such taglines must indicate the availability of language services in at least the top 15 languages spoken by the limited English proficient population of the relevant State or States, as determined in guidance published by the Secretary.
units.actor: an agent or broker subject to §155.220(c)(3)(i)
units.action_summary: Taglines must indicate availability of language services in at least the top 15 LEP languages as determined by HHS guidance.

units.obligation_text: An agent or broker subject to §155.220(c)(3)(i) that is licensed in and serving multiple States may aggregate the limited English populations in the States it serves to determine the top 15 languages required for taglines.
units.actor: an agent or broker subject to §155.220(c)(3)(i)
units.action_summary: Licensed multi-state agents/brokers may aggregate LEP populations across States they serve to determine top 15 languages for taglines.

units.obligation_text: An agent or broker subject to §155.220(c)(3)(i) may satisfy tagline requirements with respect to Web site content if it posts a Web link prominently on its home page that directs individuals to the full text of the taglines indicating how individuals may obtain language assistance services, and if it also includes taglines on any critical standalone document linked to or embedded in the Web site.
units.actor: an agent or broker subject to §155.220(c)(3)(i)
units.action_summary: Agents/brokers may comply with tagline requirements by posting a prominent link to full taglines and including taglines on critical standalone documents.

units.obligation_text: Maintain audit trails and records in an electronic format for a minimum of ten years and cooperate with any audit under this section;
units.action_summary: Maintain electronic audit trails and records for at least ten years and cooperate with audits under the section.

units.obligation_text: Differentially display all standardized options in accordance with the requirements under §155.205(b)(1) in a manner consistent with that adopted by HHS for display on the Federally-facilitated Exchange Web site, unless HHS approves a deviation;
units.action_summary: Display all standardized options in a manner consistent with HHS Federally-facilitated Exchange display requirements, unless HHS approves a deviation.

units.obligation_text: Prominently display information provided by HHS pertaining to a consumer’s eligibility for advance payments of the premium tax credit or cost-sharing reductions;
units.action_summary: Prominently display HHS-provided information about consumer eligibility for advance premium tax credits or cost-sharing reductions.

units.obligation_text: Allow the consumer to select an amount for advance payments of the premium tax credit, if applicable, and make related attestations in accordance with §155.310(d)(2);
units.action_summary: Allow consumers to select the amount for advance premium tax credits and make the related attestations per §155.310(d)(2).

units.obligation_text: Support post-enrollment activities necessary for the consumer to effectuate his or her coverage or resolve issues related to his or her enrollment, including discrepancies related to eligibility;
units.action_summary: Support post-enrollment activities needed to effectuate coverage or resolve enrollment issues, including eligibility discrepancies.

units.obligation_text: Demonstrate operational readiness and compliance with applicable requirements prior to the agent or broker’s Internet Web site being used to complete the QHP selection;
units.action_summary: Demonstrate operational readiness and compliance before using agent/broker website to complete QHP selections.

units.obligation_text: HHS may immediately suspend the agent or broker’s ability to transact information with the Exchange if HHS discovers circumstances that pose unacceptable risk to Exchange operations or Exchange information technology systems until the incident or breach is remedied or sufficiently mitigated to HHS’s satisfaction.
units.action_summary: HHS may immediately suspend an agent or broker's ability to transact with the Exchange if unacceptable risks to operations or IT systems are discovered, until remedied to HHS's satisfaction.

units.obligation_text: Report to HHS and applicable State departments of insurance any potential material breach of the standards in paragraphs (c) and (d) of this section, or the agreement entered into under §155.260(b), by the agent or broker accessing the Internet Web site, should it become aware of any such potential breach. An agent or broker that provides access to its Web site or ability to transact information with HHS to another agent or broker Web site is responsible for ensuring that the other agent’s or broker’s Web site is in compliance with this section;
units.action_summary: Report any potential material breaches to HHS and State insurance departments and ensure that third-party agent/broker websites accessing HHS are compliant.
units.modal_raw: must (report) and is responsible for ensuring

units.obligation_text: Provide consumers with correct information, without omission of material fact, regarding the Federally-facilitated Exchanges, QHPs offered through the Federally-facilitated Exchanges, and insurance affordability programs,
units.action_summary: Provide consumers accurate, complete information about Federally-facilitated Exchanges, QHPs, and insurance affordability programs.

units.obligation_text: and refrain from marketing or conduct that is misleading (including by having a direct enrollment Web site that HHS determines could mislead a consumer into believing they are visiting HealthCare.gov), coercive, or discriminates based on race, color, national origin, disability, age, sex, gender identity, or sexual orientation;
units.action_summary: Do not engage in marketing or conduct that is misleading, coercive, or discriminatory on listed bases.

units.obligation_text: Unless otherwise required by Federal or State law, the SHOP must provide required notices electronically or, if an employer or employee elects, through standard mail.
units.action_summary: Provide required notices electronically or by standard mail if elected, unless law requires otherwise.

units.obligation_text: If notices are provided electronically, the SHOP must comply with the requirements for electronic notices in 42 CFR 435.918(b)(2) through (5) for the employer or employee.
units.action_summary: Comply with specified 42 CFR electronic notice requirements when notices are provided electronically.

units.obligation_text: In the event that an individual market Exchange or SHOP is unable to send select required notices electronically due to technical limitations, it may instead send these notices through standard mail, even if an election has been made to receive such notices electronically.
units.actor: an individual market Exchange or SHOP
units.action_summary: If unable to send notices electronically due to technical limits, may send notices via standard mail despite electronic election.

units.obligation_text: Except as provided in paragraph (e)(2)(iii) of this section, if the Exchange identifies updated information regarding death, in accordance with paragraph (d)(1)(i) of this section, or regarding any factor of eligibility not regarding income, family size, or family composition, or tax filing status, the Exchange must—
units.action_summary: When the Exchange identifies updated non-income eligibility information, it must follow the listed redetermination procedures (subject to exceptions in (e)(2)(iii)).

units.obligation_text: If the Exchange identifies updated information that the tax filer for the enrollee’s household or the tax filer’s spouse did not comply with the requirements described in §155.305(f)(4), the Exchange when redetermining and providing notification of eligibility for advance payments of the premium tax credit must:
units.action_summary: When the Exchange identifies that the tax filer did not comply with specified requirements, the Exchange must follow one of the listed procedures in redetermination and notification for advance premium tax credits.

units.obligation_text: Follow the procedures specified in paragraph (e)(2)(i) of this section;
units.action_summary: Follow the procedures set out in paragraph (e)(2)(i).

units.obligation_text: Follow the procedures in guidance published by the Secretary; or
units.action_summary: Follow Secretary-published guidance procedures as an alternative approach.

units.obligation_text: Follow alternative procedures approved by the Secretary based on a showing by the Exchange that the alternative procedures would facilitate continued enrollment in coverage with financial assistance for which the enrollee remains eligible, provide appropriate information about the process to the enrollee (including regarding any action by the enrollee necessary to obtain the most accurate redetermination of eligibility), and provide adequate program integrity protections and safeguards for Federal tax information under section 6103 of the Internal Revenue Code with respect to the confidentiality, disclosure, maintenance, or use of such information.
units.action_summary: Follow Secretary-approved alternative procedures if Exchange shows they meet specified criteria including facilitating continued enrollment and protecting tax information confidentiality.

units.obligation_text: When an eligibility redetermination in accordance with this section results in a change in the amount of advance payments of the premium tax credit for the benefit year, the Exchange must:
units.action_summary: When redetermination changes the amount of advance premium tax credit, the Exchange must recalculate advance payments using specified methods.

units.obligation_text: Recalculate the amount of advance payments of the premium tax credit in such a manner as to account for any advance payments already made on behalf of the tax filer for the benefit year for which information is available to the Exchange, such that the recalculated advance payment amount is projected to result in total advance payments for the benefit year that correspond to the tax filer's total projected premium tax credit for the benefit year, calculated in accordance with 26 CFR 1.36B-3 (or, if less than zero, be set at zero);
units.action_summary: Recalculate advance payments to account for payments already made so projected total advance payments match the tax filer's projected premium tax credit (or set to zero if negative).

units.obligation_text: For benefit years through 2023, recalculate advance payments of the premium tax credit using an alternate method that has been approved by the Secretary.
units.action_summary: For benefit years through 2023, the Exchange may use a Secretary-approved alternate method to recalculate advance payments.

units.obligation_text: Premium payment deadline extension. Exchanges may, and the Federally-facilitated Exchange will, allow issuers experiencing billing or enrollment problems due to high volume or technical errors to implement a reasonable extension of the binder payment deadlines in paragraph (e)(1) of this section.
units.action_summary: Exchanges may (and the Federally-facilitated Exchange will) allow issuers experiencing billing or enrollment problems to implement reasonable extensions of binder payment deadlines.

units.obligation_text: In the case of a qualified individual or enrollee eligible for a special enrollment period as described in paragraph (d)(4), (5), (9), (11), (12), or (13) of this section, the Exchange must ensure that coverage is effective on an appropriate date based on the circumstances of the special enrollment period.
units.action_summary: Ensure that coverage is effective on an appropriate date determined by the circumstances of the SEPs listed.

units.obligation_text: Who gains or maintains status as an Indian, as defined by section 4 of the Indian Health Care Improvement Act, may enroll in a QHP or change from one QHP to another one time per month;
units.actor: a qualified individual who gains or maintains status as an Indian
units.action_summary: May enroll in a QHP or change QHP one time per month.

units.obligation_text: The qualified individual—
units.action_summary: Parent for permissions related to Indians and dependents regarding monthly enrollment/change.

units.obligation_text: Who is or becomes a dependent of an Indian, as defined by section 4 of the Indian Health Care Improvement Act and is enrolled or is enrolling in a QHP through an Exchange on the same application as the Indian, may change from one QHP to another one time per month, at the same time as the Indian;
units.actor: a dependent of an Indian enrolled/enrolling on same application
units.action_summary: May change QHP one time per month at the same time as the Indian.

units.obligation_text: Is a dependent of a victim of domestic abuse or spousal abandonment, on the same application as the victim, may enroll in coverage at the same time as the victim;
units.actor: a dependent of a victim of domestic abuse or spousal abandonment
units.action_summary: May enroll in coverage at the same time as the victim.

units.obligation_text: At the option of the Exchange, the qualified individual provides satisfactory documentary evidence to verify his or her eligibility for an insurance affordability program or enrollment in a qualified health plan through the Exchange following termination of Exchange enrollment due to a failure to verify such status within the time period specified in §155.315 or is under 100 percent of the Federal poverty level and did not enroll in coverage while waiting for HHS to verify his or her citizenship, status as a national, or lawful presence.
units.action_summary: Exchange may allow provision of documentary evidence to verify eligibility for affordability programs or QHP enrollment following termination for failure to verify or if enrollee under 100% FPL did not enroll while awaiting HHS verification.
units.modal_raw: may (at the option of the Exchange)

units.obligation_text: The enrollee's coverage is rescinded in accordance with §147.128 of this subchapter, after a QHP issuer demonstrates, to the reasonable satisfaction of the Exchange, if required by the Exchange, that the rescission is appropriate;
units.action_summary: Coverage may be rescinded only after the QHP issuer demonstrates to the Exchange's reasonable satisfaction (if required) that rescission is appropriate under §147.128.

units.obligation_text: If the Exchange appeals entity cannot fulfill the electronic requirements of subparts C, D, F, and H of this part related to acceptance of telephone- or Internet-based appeal requests, the provision of appeals notices electronically, or the secure electronic transfer of eligibility and appeal records between appeals entities and Exchanges or Medicaid or CHIP agencies, the Exchange appeals entity may fulfill those requirements that it cannot fulfill electronically using a secure and expedient paper-based process.
units.action_summary: If unable to meet electronic requirements, the Exchange appeals entity may use a secure, expedient paper-based process to fulfill those requirements.

units.obligation_text: An Exchange may establish an employer appeals process in accordance with the requirements of this section and §§155.505(f) through (h) and 155.510(a)(1) and (2) and (c).
units.action_summary: An Exchange may establish an employer appeals process that complies with specified requirements.

units.obligation_text: Where an Exchange has not established an employer appeals process, HHS will provide an employer appeals process that meets the requirements of this section and §§155.505(f) through (h) and 155.510(a)(1) and (2) and (c).
units.action_summary: If an Exchange does not establish an employer appeals process, HHS will provide one meeting the specified requirements.

units.obligation_text: The SHOP must provide an employee who becomes a qualified employee outside of the initial or annual open enrollment period with a 30-day enrollment period beginning on the date the qualified employer notifies the SHOP about the newly qualified employee.
units.action_summary: Provide a 30-day enrollment period for newly qualified employees beginning on the date the employer notifies the SHOP.

units.obligation_text: Qualified employers must notify the SHOP about a newly qualified employee on or before the thirtieth day after the day that the employee becomes eligible for coverage.
units.action_summary: Notify the SHOP about newly qualified employees no later than 30 days after the employee becomes eligible for coverage.

units.obligation_text: If a qualified employer with variable hour employees makes regularly having a specified number of hours of service per period, or working full-time, a condition of employee eligibility for coverage offered through a SHOP, any measurement period that the qualified employer elects to use under §147.116(c)(3)(i) to determine whether an employee meets the applicable eligibility conditions with respect to coverage offered through the SHOP must not exceed 10 months, beginning on any date between the employee’s start date and the first day of the first calendar month following the employee’s start date.
units.action_summary: Any measurement period elected to determine eligibility for variable-hour employees must not exceed 10 months and must begin within the specified timeframe.

units.obligation_text: Waiting periods in a SHOP are calculated beginning on the date the employee becomes eligible for coverage, regardless of when a qualified employer notifies the SHOP about the newly qualified employee, and must not exceed 60 days in length.
units.actor: the SHOP and qualified employers (with respect to waiting periods)
units.action_summary: Waiting periods must be calculated from the employee's eligibility date and must not exceed 60 days.

title: Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act: Benefit and Payment Parameters for 2018

units.obligation_text: For purposes of this paragraph (d), subject to applicable State law, an issuer is not considered to have discontinued offering all health insurance coverage in a market if the issuer or a member of the issuer's controlled group continues to offer and make available in the applicable market in the State at least one product of the issuer that is considered to be the same product as a product the issuer had been offering (as defined in Sec. 144.103 of this subchapter).
units.actor: issuer or a member of the issuer's controlled group
units.action_summary: An issuer (or controlled-group member) that continues to offer at least one product that is the same as a previously offered product will not be considered to have discontinued offering all coverage in the market.

units.obligation_text: The issuer continues to offer and make available at least one product in the applicable market in the State, even if such product is not considered to be the same product as a product the issuer had been offering (as defined in Sec. 144.103 of this subchapter), provided the issuer subjects that product to the rate review requirements under part 154 of this title (to the extent otherwise applicable to coverage of the same type and in the same market) as if that part applied to that product, and reasonably identifies a discontinued product that corresponds to the new product for purposes of such rate review.
units.action_summary: An issuer that offers a new, non-identical product will not be considered to have discontinued offering coverage if it subjects the product to applicable rate review requirements and reasonably identifies a corresponding discontinued product.

units.obligation_text: The product is offered by the same health insurance issuer (within the meaning of section 2791(b)(2) of the PHS Act), or a member of the issuer's controlled group (as defined in paragraph (d) of this section);
units.actor: health insurance issuer or member of the issuer's controlled group
units.action_summary: Specification that the product must be offered by the same issuer or a controlled-group member.

units.obligation_text: A single age band for individuals age 0 through 14.
units.action_summary: Age rating must use a single age band covering ages 0–14.

units.obligation_text: One-year age bands for individuals age 15 through 20.
units.action_summary: Age rating must use one-year age bands for ages 15–20.

units.obligation_text: Each State may establish a uniform age rating curve in the individual or small group market, or both markets, for rating purposes under paragraph (a)(1)(iii) of this section.
units.action_summary: States are permitted to establish a uniform age rating curve for individual and/or small group markets.

units.obligation_text: If a State does not establish a uniform age rating curve or provide information on such age curve in accordance with Sec. 147.103, a default uniform age rating curve specified in guidance by the Secretary ... will apply in that State
units.action_summary: A Secretary-specified default age rating curve applies in States that do not establish or provide required information about an age rating curve.

units.obligation_text: A health insurance issuer in the individual market must provide a limited open enrollment period for the events described in Sec. 155.420(d) of this subchapter, excluding ...
units.actor: health insurance issuer in the individual market
units.action_summary: Individual-market issuers are required to provide limited open enrollment periods for events listed in Sec. 155.420(d), with specified exclusions.

units.obligation_text: For purposes of this paragraph (d), subject to applicable State law, an issuer is not considered to have discontinued offering all health insurance coverage in a market if the issuer or a member of the issuer's controlled group continues to offer and make available in the applicable market in the State at least one product of the issuer that is considered to be the same product as a product the issuer had been offering (as defined in Sec. 144.103 of this subchapter).
units.actor: issuer or a member of the issuer's controlled group
units.action_summary: Issuer (or controlled-group member) continuing to offer at least one same product will not be treated as having discontinued offering all coverage.

units.obligation_text: The issuer continues to offer and make available at least one product in the applicable market in the State, even if such product is not considered to be the same product as a product the issuer had been offering, provided the issuer subjects that product to the rate review requirements under part 154 ... and reasonably identifies a discontinued product that corresponds to the new product for purposes of such rate review.
units.action_summary: An issuer offering a new product will not be deemed to have discontinued offering if it subjects the product to rate review and reasonably identifies a corresponding discontinued product.

units.obligation_text: The product is offered by the same health insurance issuer (within the meaning of section 2791(b)(2) of the PHS Act) or member of the issuer's controlled group (as defined in paragraph (d) of this section);
units.actor: health insurance issuer or member of issuer's controlled group
units.action_summary: Product must be offered by the same issuer or a controlled-group member for the provision to apply.

units.obligation_text: For purposes of this paragraph (e), subject to applicable State law, an issuer is not considered to have discontinued offering all health insurance coverage in a market if the issuer or a member of the issuer's controlled group continues to offer and make available in the applicable market in the State at least one product of the issuer that is considered to be the same product as a product the issuer had been offering (as defined in Sec. 144.103 of this subchapter).
units.actor: issuer or member of issuer's controlled group
units.action_summary: An issuer that continues to offer at least one same product will not be considered to have discontinued offering all coverage in the market.

units.obligation_text: The issuer continues to offer and make available at least one product in the applicable market in the State, even if such product is not considered to be the same product as a product the issuer had been offering, provided the issuer subjects that product to the rate review requirements under part 154 ... and reasonably identifies a discontinued product that corresponds to the new product for purposes of such rate review.
units.action_summary: An issuer offering a new product will not be treated as having discontinued coverage if it subjects the product to rate review and reasonably identifies a corresponding discontinued product.

units.obligation_text: The risk adjustment methodology is developed by HHS and published in advance of the benefit year in rulemaking;
units.action_summary: HHS must develop and publish the risk adjustment methodology in advance of the benefit year through rulemaking.

units.obligation_text: Draft factors to be employed in the model, including but not limited to demographic factors, diagnostic factors, and utilization factors, if any, the dataset(s) to be used to calculate final coefficients, and the date by which final coefficients will be released in guidance;
units.action_summary: HHS must include specified draft factors, datasets, and target date for final coefficients when publishing draft methodology.

units.obligation_text: Remit to HHS an amount equal to the product of its monthly billable enrollment in the risk adjustment covered plan multiplied by the per-enrollee-per-month risk adjustment user fee specified in the annual HHS notice of benefit and payment parameters for the applicable benefit year.
units.action_summary: Issuers must remit to HHS the calculated monthly risk adjustment user fee based on billable enrollment.

units.obligation_text: Beginning in the 2018 benefit year, validating enrollee health status through review of all relevant paid pharmacy claims;
units.action_summary: Starting 2018, validation must include review of all relevant paid pharmacy claims.

units.obligation_text: Within 15 calendar days of notification of the initial validation audit sample determined by HHS, in the manner set forth by HHS, an issuer must confirm the sample or file a discrepancy report to dispute the initial validation audit sample determined by HHS.
units.action_summary: Issuers must confirm the initial validation audit sample or file a discrepancy report within 15 calendar days of notification.

units.obligation_text: Within 30 calendar days of notification of the findings of a second validation audit or the calculation of a risk score error rate, in the manner set forth by HHS, an issuer must confirm the audit or error rate, or file a discrepancy report to dispute the findings of a second validation audit or the calculation of a risk score error rate as result of risk adjustment data validation.
units.action_summary: Issuers must confirm or dispute the second validation audit findings or risk score error rate within 30 calendar days.

units.obligation_text: An issuer may appeal the findings of a second validation audit or the calculation of a risk score error rate as result of risk adjustment data validation, under the process set forth in Sec. 156.1220 of this subchapter.
units.action_summary: Issuers are permitted to appeal second-audit findings or risk score error rate calculations under Sec. 156.1220.

units.obligation_text: If utilizing the Federal platform for SHOP eligibility, enrollment, or premium aggregation functions, establish standard processes for premium calculation, premium payment, and premium collection that are consistent with the requirements applicable in a Federally-facilitated SHOP under Sec. 155.705(b)(4);
units.actor: State Exchange on the Federal platform
units.action_summary: State Exchanges using the Federal platform for SHOP functions must establish standard processes for premium calculation, payment, and collection consistent with Federally-facilitated SHOP requirements.

units.obligation_text: If utilizing the Federal platform for SHOP enrollment or premium aggregation functions, require its QHP issuers to make any changes to rates in accordance with the timeline applicable in a Federally-facilitated SHOP under Sec. 155.705(b)(6)(i)(A);
units.actor: State Exchange on the Federal platform
units.action_summary: State Exchanges using the Federal platform must require their QHP issuers to change rates according to Federally-facilitated SHOP timelines.

units.obligation_text: If utilizing the Federal platform for SHOP enrollment functions, establish minimum participation rate requirements and calculation methodologies that are consistent with those applicable in a Federally-facilitated SHOP under Sec. 155.705(b)(10);
units.actor: State Exchange on the Federal platform
units.action_summary: State Exchanges must set minimum participation rate requirements and calculation methods consistent with Federally-facilitated SHOP rules.

units.obligation_text: If utilizing the Federal platform for SHOP enrollment or premium aggregation functions, establish employer contribution methodologies that are consistent with the methodologies applicable in a Federally-facilitated SHOP under Sec. 155.705(b)(11)(ii);
units.actor: State Exchange on the Federal platform
units.action_summary: State Exchanges must establish employer contribution methodologies consistent with Federally-facilitated SHOP methodologies.

units.obligation_text: If utilizing the Federal platform for SHOP enrollment functions, establish annual employee open enrollment period requirements that are consistent with Sec. 155.725(e)(2);
units.actor: State Exchange on the Federal platform
units.action_summary: State Exchanges must set annual employee open enrollment period requirements consistent with Sec. 155.725(e)(2).

units.obligation_text: If utilizing the Federal platform for SHOP enrollment functions, establish effective dates of coverage for an initial group enrollment or a group renewal that are consistent with the effective dates of coverage applicable in a Federally-facilitated SHOP under Sec. 155.725(h)(2);
units.actor: State Exchange on the Federal platform
units.action_summary: State Exchanges must set effective dates of coverage for initial group enrollments and renewals consistent with Federally-facilitated SHOP rules.

units.obligation_text: If utilizing the Federal platform for SHOP eligibility, enrollment, or premium aggregation functions, establish policies for the termination of SHOP coverage or enrollment that are consistent with the requirements applicable in a Federally-facilitated SHOP under Sec. 155.735.
units.actor: State Exchange on the Federal platform
units.action_summary: State Exchanges must establish termination policies for SHOP coverage consistent with Federally-facilitated SHOP requirements.

units.obligation_text: For Exchanges and QHP issuers, beginning no later than the first day of the individual market open enrollment period for the 2017 benefit year, this standard also includes taglines on Web site content and any document that is critical for obtaining health insurance coverage or access to health care services ... Such taglines must indicate the availability of language services in at least the top 15 languages spoken by the limited English proficient population of the relevant State or States ...
units.action_summary: Exchanges and QHP issuers must include taglines on specified web content/documents indicating availability of language services in at least the top 15 LEP languages.

units.obligation_text: If an Exchange is operated by an entity operating multiple Exchanges, or relies on an eligibility or enrollment platform that is relied on by multiple Exchanges, the Exchange may aggregate the limited English proficient populations across all the States served by the entity ... to determine the top 15 languages required for taglines.
units.action_summary: Such Exchanges may aggregate LEP populations across states served to determine required top 15 languages for taglines.

units.obligation_text: A QHP issuer may aggregate the limited English proficient populations across all States served by the health insurance issuers within the issuer's controlled group ... to determine the top 15 languages required for taglines.
units.action_summary: QHP issuers may aggregate LEP populations across states served by issuers in their controlled group to determine top 15 languages.

units.obligation_text: Exchanges and QHP issuers may satisfy tagline requirements with respect to Web site content if they post a Web link prominently on their home page that directs individuals to the full text of the taglines ... and if they also include taglines on any critical standalone document linked to or embedded in the Web site.
units.action_summary: Exchanges and QHP issuers may meet tagline requirements by posting a prominent link to full taglines plus including taglines on critical standalone documents.

units.obligation_text: For an agent or broker subject to Sec. 155.220(c)(3)(i), beginning on the first day of the individual market open enrollment period for the 2017 benefit year, or when such entity has been registered with the Exchange for at least 1 year, whichever is later, this standard also includes taglines on Web site content and any document that is critical ... Such taglines must indicate the availability of language services in at least the top 15 languages ...
units.actor: agent or broker subject to Sec. 155.220(c)(3)(i)
units.action_summary: Agents/brokers subject to sec.155.220(c)(3)(i) must include taglines indicating availability of language services in at least the top 15 LEP languages on specified web content/documents after the stated start date.

units.obligation_text: An agent or broker subject to Sec. 155.220(c)(3)(i) that is licensed in and serving multiple States may aggregate the limited English populations in the States it serves to determine the top 15 languages required for taglines.
units.actor: agent or broker subject to Sec.155.220(c)(3)(i)
units.action_summary: Multi-state agents/brokers may aggregate LEP populations across states they serve to determine required top 15 languages.

units.obligation_text: An agent or broker subject to Sec. 155.220(c)(3)(i) may satisfy tagline requirements with respect to Web site content if it posts a Web link prominently on its home page that directs individuals to the full text of the taglines ... and if it also includes taglines on any critical standalone document linked to or embedded in the Web site.
units.actor: agent or broker subject to Sec.155.220(c)(3)(i)
units.action_summary: Agents/brokers may meet tagline requirements by posting a prominent link to full taglines and including taglines on critical standalone documents.

units.obligation_text: Maintain audit trails and records in an electronic format for a minimum of ten years and cooperate with any audit under this section;
units.action_summary: Agents/brokers must keep electronic audit trails/records for at least ten years and cooperate with audits.

units.obligation_text: Differentially display all standardized options in accordance with the requirements under Sec. 155.205(b)(1) in a manner consistent with that adopted by HHS for display on the Federally-facilitated Exchange Web site, unless HHS approves a deviation;
units.action_summary: Agents/brokers must display standardized options consistent with HHS's Federally-facilitated Exchange display unless HHS approves a deviation.

units.obligation_text: Prominently display information provided by HHS pertaining to a consumer's eligibility for advance payments of the premium tax credit or cost-sharing reductions;
units.action_summary: Agents/brokers must prominently display HHS-provided information about consumers' eligibility for advance premium tax credits or cost-sharing reductions.

units.obligation_text: Allow the consumer to select an amount for advance payments of the premium tax credit, if applicable, and make related attestations in accordance with Sec. 155.310(d)(2);
units.action_summary: Agents/brokers must allow consumers to select advance premium tax credit amounts and make related attestations per Sec.155.310(d)(2).

units.obligation_text: Support post-enrollment activities necessary for the consumer to effectuate his or her coverage or resolve issues related to his or her enrollment, including discrepancies related to eligibility;
units.action_summary: Agents/brokers must support post-enrollment activities to help consumers effectuate coverage and resolve enrollment/eligibility issues.

units.obligation_text: Demonstrate operational readiness and compliance with applicable requirements prior to the agent or broker's Internet Web site being used to complete the QHP selection;
units.action_summary: Agents/brokers must demonstrate operational readiness and compliance before their websites can be used to complete QHP selection.

units.obligation_text: HHS may immediately suspend the agent or broker's ability to transact information with the Exchange if HHS discovers circumstances that pose unacceptable risk to Exchange operations or Exchange information technology systems until the incident or breach is remedied or sufficiently mitigated to HHS's satisfaction.
units.action_summary: HHS is permitted to immediately suspend an agent/broker's Exchange access if risks to Exchange operations/IT are discovered, until mitigated.

units.obligation_text: Report to HHS and applicable State departments of insurance any potential material breach of the standards in paragraphs (c) and (d) of this section, or the agreement entered into under Sec. 155.260(b), by the agent or broker accessing the Internet Web site, should it become aware of any such potential breach.
units.actor: agent or broker accessing the Internet Web site
units.action_summary: Agents/brokers must report potential material breaches of standards or agreements to HHS and State insurance departments if they become aware.

units.obligation_text: An agent or broker that provides access to its Web site or ability to transact information with HHS to another agent or broker Web site is responsible for ensuring that the other agent's or broker's Web site is in compliance with this section;
units.actor: agent or broker that provides access
units.action_summary: An agent/broker that allows another agent/broker to use its Web site must ensure that the other site complies with the section's requirements.

units.obligation_text: Provide consumers with correct information, without omission of material fact, regarding the Federally-facilitated Exchanges, QHPs offered through the Federally-facilitated Exchanges, and insurance affordability programs, and refrain from marketing or conduct that is misleading ... coercive, or discriminates based on race, color, national origin, disability, age, sex, gender identity, or sexual orientation;
units.action_summary: Agents/brokers must give accurate information and must not engage in misleading, coercive, or discriminatory marketing or conduct.

units.obligation_text: Unless otherwise required by Federal or State law, the SHOP must provide required notices electronically or, if an employer or employee elects, through standard mail. If notices are provided electronically, the SHOP must comply with the requirements for electronic notices in 42 CFR 435.918(b)(2) through (5) for the employer or employee.
units.action_summary: The SHOP is required to provide required notices electronically (or by mail if elected) and must comply with electronic notice requirements in 42 CFR 435.918(b)(2)-(5) when notices are electronic.

units.obligation_text: In the event that an individual market Exchange or SHOP is unable to send select required notices electronically due to technical limitations, it may instead send these notices through standard mail, even if an election has been made to receive such notices electronically.
units.action_summary: If unable to send certain notices electronically due to technical limits, the Exchange or SHOP may send them by standard mail despite prior elections for electronic notices.

units.obligation_text: If the Exchange identifies updated information that the tax filer for the enrollee's household or the tax filer's spouse did not comply with the requirements described in Sec. 155.305(f)(4), the Exchange when redetermining and providing notification of eligibility for advance payments of the premium tax credit must: (A) Follow the procedures specified in paragraph (e)(2)(i) of this section; (B) Follow the procedures in guidance published by the Secretary; or (C) Follow alternative procedures approved by the Secretary based on a showing by the Exchange that the alternative procedures would facilitate continued enrollment in coverage with financial assistance for which the enrollee remains eligible, provide appropriate information about the process to the enrollee ..., and provide adequate program integrity protections and safeguards for Federal tax information under section 6103 ...
units.action_summary: If the tax filer failed to comply with specified requirements, the Exchange must, when redetermining eligibility for advance payments, either follow paragraph (e)(2)(i), follow Secretary guidance, or follow Secretary-approved alternative procedures that meet specified criteria.

units.obligation_text: Recalculate the amount of advance payments of the premium tax credit in such a manner as to account for any advance payments already made on behalf of the tax filer for the benefit year for which information is available to the Exchange, such that the recalculated advance payment amount is projected to result in total advance payments for the benefit year that correspond to the tax filer's total projected premium tax credit for the benefit year, calculated in accordance with 26 CFR 1.36B-3 (or, if less than zero, be set at zero);
units.action_summary: When redetermination changes advance payment amounts, the Exchange must recalculate advance payments to reflect prior payments and project total advance payments to match the tax filer's projected premium tax credit (or set to zero if negative).

units.obligation_text: When an eligibility redetermination in accordance with this section results in a change in the amount of advance payments of the premium tax credit for the benefit year, the Exchange must:
units.action_summary: If eligibility redetermination changes advance payment amounts, the Exchange must take specified recalculation actions.

units.obligation_text: For benefit years through 2023, recalculate advance payments of the premium tax credit using an alternate method that has been approved by the Secretary.
units.action_summary: For benefit years through 2023, the Exchange may use a Secretary-approved alternate method to recalculate advance payments.

units.obligation_text: Exchanges may, and the Federally-facilitated Exchange will, allow issuers experiencing billing or enrollment problems due to high volume or technical errors to implement a reasonable extension of the binder payment deadlines in paragraph (e)(1) of this section.
units.action_summary: Exchanges may allow issuers to extend binder payment deadlines for billing/enrollment problems; the Federally-facilitated Exchange will allow such extensions.

units.obligation_text: In the case of a qualified individual or enrollee eligible for a special enrollment period as described in paragraph (d)(4), (5), (9), (11), (12), or (13) of this section, the Exchange must ensure that coverage is effective on an appropriate date based on the circumstances of the special enrollment period.
units.action_summary: The Exchange must ensure coverage takes effect on an appropriate date for SEPs described in specified paragraphs.

units.obligation_text: Who gains or maintains status as an Indian, as defined by section 4 of the Indian Health Care Improvement Act, may enroll in a QHP or change from one QHP to another one time per month;
units.actor: qualified individual who gains or maintains Indian status
units.action_summary: Individuals who gain or maintain Indian status may enroll in or change QHPs once per month.

units.obligation_text: Who is or becomes a dependent of an Indian ... may change from one QHP to another one time per month, at the same time as the Indian;
units.action_summary: Dependents of Indians may change QHPs once per month concurrently with the Indian.

units.obligation_text: A qualified individual or enrollee who is a victim of domestic abuse or spousal abandonment ... is enrolled in minimum essential coverage and seeks to enroll in coverage separate from the perpetrator of the abuse or abandonment;
units.action_summary: Victims of domestic abuse/spousal abandonment who are enrolled in MEC and seek separate coverage are eligible for enrollment (special enrollment period).

units.obligation_text: The enrollee's coverage is rescinded in accordance with Sec. 147.128 of this subchapter, after a QHP issuer demonstrates, to the reasonable satisfaction of the Exchange, if required by the Exchange, that the rescission is appropriate;
units.actor: the Exchange (coverage rescission action upon demonstration by QHP issuer)
units.action_summary: Coverage will be rescinded in accordance with Sec.147.128 after a QHP issuer demonstrates to the Exchange that rescission is appropriate, if required by the Exchange.

units.obligation_text: If the Exchange appeals entity cannot fulfill the electronic requirements ... the Exchange appeals entity may fulfill those requirements that it cannot fulfill electronically using a secure and expedient paper-based process.
units.action_summary: If unable to meet electronic requirements, the Exchange appeals entity may use a secure paper-based process to fulfill them.

units.obligation_text: An Exchange may establish an employer appeals process in accordance with the requirements of this section and Sec. Sec. 155.505(f) through (h) and 155.510(a)(1) and (2) and (c). Where an Exchange has not established an employer appeals process, HHS will provide an employer appeals process that meets the requirements of this section and Sec. Sec. 155.505(f) through (h) and 155.510(a)(1) and (2) and (c).
units.actor: Exchange; HHS (if Exchange has not established process)
units.action_summary: An Exchange may set up an employer appeals process per specified requirements; if it does not, HHS will provide one meeting those requirements.

units.obligation_text: The SHOP must provide an employee who becomes a qualified employee outside of the initial or annual open enrollment period with a 30-day enrollment period beginning on the date the qualified employer notifies the SHOP about the newly qualified employee.
units.action_summary: SHOPs must give newly qualified employees a 30-day enrollment period starting when the employer notifies the SHOP.

units.obligation_text: Qualified employers must notify the SHOP about a newly qualified employee on or before the thirtieth day after the day that the employee becomes eligible for coverage.
units.action_summary: Qualified employers are required to notify the SHOP of newly qualified employees within 30 days of their eligibility for coverage.

units.obligation_text: If a newly qualified employee's waiting period ends on the first day of a month and the employee has already made a plan selection by that date, coverage must take effect on that date. If a newly qualified employee makes a plan selection on the first day of a month and any applicable waiting period has ended by that date, coverage must be effective on that date.
units.actor: the SHOP and QHP issuers (for effective date processing)
units.action_summary: Coverage must take effect on the first day of the month when the waiting period has ended and a plan selection has been made by that date.

units.obligation_text: If a qualified employer ... any measurement period that the qualified employer elects to use under Sec. 147.116(c)(3)(i) to determine whether an employee meets the applicable eligibility conditions with respect to coverage offered through the SHOP must not exceed 10 months, beginning on any date between the employee's start date and the first day of the first calendar month following the employee's start date.
units.action_summary: Measurement periods chosen by qualified employers for determining eligibility through SHOP cannot exceed 10 months and must begin within the specified date range.

units.obligation_text: Waiting periods in a SHOP are calculated beginning on the date the employee becomes eligible for coverage, regardless of when a qualified employer notifies the SHOP about the newly qualified employee, and must not exceed 60 days in length. Waiting periods in a Federally-facilitated SHOP or a State-based SHOP that uses the Federal platform for SHOP eligibility or enrollment functions must be 0, 15, 30, 45 or 60 days in length.
units.action_summary: SHOP waiting periods start on employee eligibility date, cannot exceed 60 days, and if Federally-facilitated or using the Federal platform must be one of the specified durations (0,15,30,45,60 days).

title: Medicare and Medicaid Programs: Conditions of Participation for Home Health Agencies; Delay of Effective Date CMS-3819-P2

units.obligation_text: In § 484.65, amend paragraph (d) by removing the date "January 13, 2018" and adding in its place "July 13, 2018".
units.actor: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) / codifier
units.action_summary: Change the date in §484.65(d) from January 13, 2018 to July 13, 2018.

units.obligation_text: In § 484.115, amend paragraphs (a)(1) and (2) by removing the date "July 13, 2017" and adding in its place "January 13, 2018".
units.actor: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) / codifier
units.action_summary: Change the dates in §484.115(a)(1) and (a)(2) from July 13, 2017 to January 13, 2018.

units.obligation_text: Pursuant to sections 1.415 and 1.419 of the Commission’s rules, 47 CFR 1.415, 1.419, interested parties may file comments and reply comments on or before the dates indicated on the first page of this document.
units.action_summary: Interested parties are permitted to file comments and reply comments by the stated deadlines.

units.obligation_text: Comments are due on or before April 17, 2017.
units.action_summary: Comments must be submitted by April 17, 2017.

units.obligation_text: Reply comments are due on or before April 24, 2017.
units.action_summary: Reply comments must be submitted by April 24, 2017.

units.obligation_text: Comments may be filed using the Commission’s Electronic Comment Filing System (ECFS).
units.action_summary: Comments may be submitted electronically via the Commission's ECFS.

units.obligation_text: Electronic Filers: Comments may be filed electronically using the Internet by accessing the ECFS: http://fjallfoss.fcc.gov/ecfs2/.
units.action_summary: Electronic filers may file comments online through the ECFS URL provided.

units.obligation_text: Filings can be sent by hand or messenger delivery, by commercial overnight courier, or by first-class or overnight U.S. Postal Service mail.
units.action_summary: Filers are permitted to submit filings by hand/messenger, commercial overnight courier, or by first-class/overnight USPS mail.

units.obligation_text: Paper Filers: Parties who choose to file by paper must file an original and one copy of each filing.
units.actor: paper filers / parties who file by paper
units.action_summary: Paper filers are required to submit an original plus one copy of each filing.

units.obligation_text: If more than one docket or rulemaking number appears in the caption of this proceeding, filers must submit two additional copies for each additional docket or rulemaking number.
units.action_summary: Filers must submit two extra copies for each additional docket/rulemaking number in the caption.

units.obligation_text: All filings must be addressed to the Commission’s Secretary, Office of the Secretary, Federal Communications Commission.
units.action_summary: All filings are required to be addressed to the Commission's Secretary at the Office of the Secretary.

units.obligation_text: All hand-delivered or messenger-delivered paper filings for the Commission’s Secretary must be delivered to FCC Headquarters at 445 12th St. SW., Room TW–A325, Washington, DC 20554.
units.action_summary: Hand-delivered or messenger-delivered paper filings for the Secretary must be delivered to the specified FCC Headquarters address and room.

units.obligation_text: The filing hours are 8:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m.
units.action_summary: Hand-delivered or messenger-delivered filings must be delivered during the stated filing hours (8:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m.).

units.obligation_text: All hand deliveries must be held together with rubber bands or fasteners.
units.action_summary: Hand-delivered filings are required to be held together with rubber bands or fasteners.

units.obligation_text: Any envelopes and boxes must be disposed of before entering the building.
units.action_summary: Envelopes and boxes must be disposed of before entry into the building.

units.obligation_text: Commercial overnight mail (other than U.S. Postal Service Express Mail and Priority Mail) must be sent to 9300 East Hampton Drive, Capitol Heights, MD 20743.
units.action_summary: Commercial overnight mail (excluding USPS Express and Priority Mail) must be sent to the specified Capitol Heights address.

units.obligation_text: Subject to §155.420(a)(4) and (5) of this subchapter, a health insurance issuer in the individual market must provide a limited open enrollment period for the triggering events described in §155.420(d) of this subchapter, excluding the following:
units.actor: a health insurance issuer in the individual market
units.action_summary: Provide a limited open enrollment period for the triggering events in §155.420(d) (with specified exclusions).

units.obligation_text: For the benefit years beginning on January 1, 2016 and January 1, 2017, the annual open enrollment period begins on November 1 of the calendar year preceding the benefit year, and extends through January 31 of the benefit year.
units.action_summary: Set the annual open enrollment period for the 2016 and 2017 benefit years from November 1 through January 31.

units.obligation_text: For the benefit years beginning on January 1, 2018 and beyond, the annual open enrollment period begins on November 1 and extends through December 15 of the calendar year preceding the benefit year.
units.action_summary: Set the annual open enrollment period for 2018 and later benefit years from November 1 through December 15 of the preceding calendar year.

units.obligation_text: The Exchange must allow a qualified individual, and when specified in paragraph (d) of this section, his or her dependent, who are not enrolled in a QHP through the Exchange, to enroll in a QHP if one of the triggering events specified in paragraph (d) of this section occur.
units.action_summary: Allow qualified individuals (and specified dependents) not enrolled through the Exchange to enroll in a QHP when a triggering event occurs.

units.obligation_text: If an enrollee has gained a dependent in accordance with paragraph (d)(2)(i) of this section, the Exchange must allow the enrollee to add the dependent to his or her current QHP, or, if the QHP’s business rules do not allow the dependent to enroll, the Exchange must allow the enrollee and his or her dependents to change to another QHP within the same level of coverage (or one metal level higher or lower, if no such QHP is available), as outlined in §156.140(b) of this subchapter, or enroll the dependent in a separate QHP.
units.action_summary: When an enrollee gains a dependent per (d)(2)(i), allow adding the dependent to the current QHP or, if business rules prevent that, allow changing to another QHP within the same (or adjacent) metal level or enrolling the dependent in a separate QHP.

units.obligation_text: the Exchange must allow the enrollee to add the dependent to his or her current QHP
units.action_summary: Permit the enrollee to add the gained dependent to the enrollee's current QHP.

units.obligation_text: if the QHP’s business rules do not allow the dependent to enroll, the Exchange must allow the enrollee and his or her dependents to change to another QHP within the same level of coverage (or one metal level higher or lower, if no such QHP is available)
units.action_summary: If business rules prevent adding the dependent to the current QHP, allow changing to another QHP within the same metal level (or one level up/down if necessary).

units.obligation_text: or enroll the dependent in a separate QHP
units.action_summary: Alternatively, allow enrollment of the dependent in a separate QHP.

units.obligation_text: If an enrollee and his or her dependents become newly eligible for cost-sharing reductions in accordance with paragraph (d)(6)(i) or (ii) and are not enrolled in a silver-level QHP, the Exchange must allow the enrollee and his or her dependents to change to a silver-level QHP if they elect to change their QHP enrollment.
units.action_summary: Allow enrollees and dependents who newly become eligible for cost-sharing reductions and are not in a silver QHP to change to a silver-level QHP if they elect to change enrollment.

units.obligation_text: If an enrollee qualifies for a special enrollment period through another triggering event specified in paragraph (d) of this section, except for paragraph (d)(4), (d)(8), (d)(9), and (d)(10), the Exchange must allow the enrollee and his or her dependents to make changes to their enrollment in the same QHP or to change to another QHP within the same level of coverage, as outlined in §156.140(b) of this subchapter, provided that other QHPs at that metal level are available.
units.action_summary: When an enrollee qualifies for certain triggering events (excluding specified paragraphs), allow changes to the same QHP or to another QHP within the same metal level, if other QHPs at that level are available.

units.obligation_text: except for paragraph (d)(4), (d)(8), (d)(9), and (d)(10)
units.action_summary: Excludes triggering events listed in paragraphs (d)(4), (d)(8), (d)(9), and (d)(10) from the allowance to change QHPs under this provision.

units.obligation_text: provided that other QHPs at that metal level are available
units.action_summary: The Exchange's allowance to change QHPs is conditioned on availability of other QHPs at that metal level.

units.obligation_text: Qualified individuals who are required to demonstrate coverage in the 60 days prior to a qualifying event can either demonstrate that they had minimum essential coverage as described in 26 CFR 1.5000A-1(b) for 1 or more days during the 60 days preceding the date of the qualifying event or that they lived outside of the United States or in a United States territory for 1 or more days during the 60 days preceding the date of the qualifying event.
units.actor: Qualified individuals who are required to demonstrate coverage
units.action_summary: Permits qualified individuals to demonstrate prior coverage either by showing minimum essential coverage for 1+ days in the prior 60 days or by showing they lived outside the U.S./territory for 1+ days in that period.

units.obligation_text: At the option of the consumer, the Exchange must provide for a coverage effective date that is no more than 1 month later than the effective date specified in this paragraph (b) if a consumer’s enrollment is delayed until after the verification of the consumer’s eligibility for a special enrollment period, and the assignment of a coverage effective date consistent with this paragraph (b) would result in the consumer being required to pay 2 or more months of retroactive premium to effectuate coverage or avoid termination for non-payment.
units.action_summary: At the consumer's option, provide a coverage effective date up to 1 month later where verification delays would otherwise require the consumer to pay 2+ months of retroactive premium.

units.obligation_text: a coverage effective date that is no more than 1 month later than the effective date specified in this paragraph (b)
units.action_summary: The later coverage effective date provided may be no more than one month after the specified effective date.

units.obligation_text: if a consumer’s enrollment is delayed until after the verification of the consumer’s eligibility for a special enrollment period
units.action_summary: Condition triggering the Exchange's obligation: the consumer's enrollment must be delayed until after eligibility verification.

units.obligation_text: and the assignment of a coverage effective date consistent with this paragraph (b) would result in the consumer being required to pay 2 or more months of retroactive premium to effectuate coverage or avoid termination for non-payment
units.action_summary: Additional condition: the standard effective date would cause the consumer to owe 2 or more months of retroactive premium.

units.obligation_text: Subject to paragraphs (a)(3) through (5) of this section, the Exchange must allow a qualified individual or enrollee, and, when specified below, his or her dependent, to enroll in or change from QHP to another if one of the triggering events occur:
units.action_summary: Allow qualified individuals/enrollees (and specified dependents) to enroll in or change QHPs when a triggering event occurs, subject to (a)(3)-(5).

units.obligation_text: In the case of marriage, at least one spouse must demonstrate having minimum essential coverage as described in 26 CFR 1.5000A-1(b) for 1 or more days during the 60 days preceding the date of marriage.
units.action_summary: Require that at least one spouse demonstrate minimum essential coverage for 1+ days in the 60 days before the marriage for the marriage triggering event.

units.obligation_text: The allowable variation in the AV of a health plan that does not result in a material difference in the true dollar value of the health plan is – 4 percentage points and + 2 percentage points, except if a health plan under paragraph (b)(1) of this section (a bronze health plan) either covers and pays for at least one major service, other than preventive services, before the deductible or meets the requirements to be a high deductible health plan within the meaning of 26 U.S.C. 223(c)(2), in which case the allowable variation in AV for such plan is −4 percentage points and +5 percentage points.
units.actor: a health plan (or health insurance issuer offering the plan)
units.action_summary: Specify allowable AV variation: generally -4/+2 percentage points; for certain bronze plans meeting criteria, -4/+5 percentage points.

title: Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act; Market Stabilization

units.obligation_text: Subject to § 155.420(a)(4) and (5) of this subchapter, a health insurance issuer in the individual market must provide a limited open enrollment period for the triggering events described in § 155.420(d) of this subchapter, excluding the following:
units.actor: a health insurance issuer in the individual market
units.action_summary: Provide a limited open enrollment period for specified triggering events.

units.obligation_text: For the benefit years beginning on January 1, 2016 and January 1, 2017, the annual open enrollment period begins on November 1 of the calendar year preceding the benefit year, and extends through January 31 of the benefit year.
units.action_summary: Set the annual open enrollment period from November 1 through January 31 for 2016 and 2017 benefit years.

units.obligation_text: For the benefit years beginning on January 1, 2018 and beyond, the annual open enrollment period begins on November 1 and extends through December 15 of the calendar year preceding the benefit year.
units.action_summary: Set the annual open enrollment period from November 1 through December 15 for benefit years beginning January 1, 2018 and beyond.

units.obligation_text: The Exchange must allow a qualified individual, and when specified in paragraph (d) of this section, his or her dependent, who are not enrolled in a QHP through the Exchange, to enroll in a QHP if one of the triggering events specified in paragraph (d) of this section occur.
units.action_summary: Allow qualified individuals (and specified dependents not already enrolled through the Exchange) to enroll in a QHP when a triggering event occurs.

units.obligation_text: If an enrollee has gained a dependent in accordance with paragraph (d)(2)(i) of this section, the Exchange must allow the enrollee to add the dependent to his or her current QHP, or, if the QHP’s business rules do not allow the dependent to enroll, the Exchange must allow the enrollee and his or her dependents to change to another QHP within the same level of coverage (or one metal level higher or lower, if no such QHP is available), as outlined in § 156.140(b) of this subchapter, or enroll the dependent in a separate QHP.
units.action_summary: When an enrollee gains a dependent as specified, allow adding the dependent to the current QHP or, if business rules prevent that, allow changing QHPs within specified metal levels or enrolling the dependent in a separate QHP.

units.obligation_text: The Exchange must allow the enrollee to add the dependent to his or her current QHP.
units.action_summary: Allow the enrollee to add the gained dependent to the enrollee's current QHP.

units.obligation_text: If the QHP’s business rules do not allow the dependent to enroll, the Exchange must allow the enrollee and his or her dependents to change to another QHP within the same level of coverage (or one metal level higher or lower, if no such QHP is available), or enroll the dependent in a separate QHP.
units.action_summary: If the current QHP won't accept the dependent, allow changing to another QHP within same or adjacent metal level, or permit enrolling the dependent in a separate QHP.

units.obligation_text: Allow the enrollee and his or her dependents to change to another QHP within the same level of coverage.
units.action_summary: Permit changing to another QHP within the same metal level.

units.obligation_text: Allow the enrollee and his or her dependents to change to another QHP one metal level higher or lower if no such QHP within the same level is available.
units.action_summary: If no same-level QHP is available, permit changing to a QHP one metal level higher or lower.

units.obligation_text: Enroll the dependent in a separate QHP.
units.action_summary: Permit enrolling the dependent in a separate QHP as an alternative.

units.obligation_text: If an enrollee and his or her dependents become newly eligible for cost-sharing reductions in accordance with paragraph (d)(6)(i) or (ii) and are not enrolled in a silver-level QHP, the Exchange must allow the enrollee and his or her dependents to change to a silver-level QHP if they elect to change their QHP enrollment.
units.action_summary: If newly eligible for cost-sharing reductions and not in a silver QHP, allow enrollee/dependents to change to a silver-level QHP if they choose to change enrollment.

units.obligation_text: If an enrollee qualifies for a special enrollment period through another triggering event specified in paragraph (d) of this section, except for paragraph (d)(4), (d)(8), (d)(9), and (d)(10), the Exchange must allow the enrollee and his or her dependents to make changes to their enrollment in the same QHP or to change to another QHP within the same level of coverage, as outlined in § 156.140(b) of this subchapter, provided that other QHPs at that metal level are available.
units.action_summary: When qualifying through certain triggering events, allow enrollee/dependents to modify enrollment in the same QHP or switch to another QHP within the same metal level, if other QHPs at that level are available.

units.obligation_text: Qualified individuals who are required to demonstrate coverage in the 60 days prior to a qualifying event can either demonstrate that they had minimum essential coverage as described in 26 CFR 1.5000A–1(b) for 1 or more days during the 60 days preceding the date of the qualifying event or that they lived outside of the United States or in a United States territory for 1 or more days during the 60 days preceding the date of the qualifying event.
units.action_summary: Permits qualified individuals required to show prior coverage to demonstrate either minimum essential coverage for 1+ days in the prior 60 days or residence outside the U.S./territory for 1+ days in that period.
