units.obligation_text: The allowable variation in the AV of a health plan that does not result in a material difference in the true dollar value of the health plan is ¥4 percentage points and + 2 percentage points, except if a health plan under paragraph (b)(1) of this section (a bronze health plan) either covers and pays for at least one major service, other than preventive services, before the deductible or meets the requirements to be a high deductible health plan within the meaning of 26 U.S.C. 223(c)(2), in which case the allowable variation in AV for such plan is ¥4 percentage points and +5 percentage points.

units.action_summary: Provide increased allowable AV variation (-4/+5) for bronze plans that pay for at least one major service pre-deductible or qualify as high deductible plans under 26 U.S.C. 223(c)(2).

units.obligation_text: A solo practitioner or a group of 10 or fewer eligible clinicians must make their election prior to the start of the applicable performance period
units.actor: a solo practitioner or a group of 10 or fewer eligible clinicians
units.action_summary: Elect to participate in a virtual group before the performance period starts

units.obligation_text: and cannot change their election during the performance period.
units.actor: a solo practitioner or a group of 10 or fewer eligible clinicians
units.action_summary: May not change their virtual group election during the performance period

units.obligation_text: Virtual group participants may elect to be in no more than one virtual group for a performance period
units.actor: virtual group participants (solo practitioners or groups)
units.action_summary: Permitted to join at most one virtual group per performance period

units.obligation_text: in the case of a group, the election applies to all MIPS eligible clinicians in the group.
units.actor: groups (that elect to be a virtual group)
units.action_summary: A group's election binds all MIPS eligible clinicians in that group

units.obligation_text: A virtual group representative must make an election, on behalf of the members of a virtual group, regarding the formation of a virtual group for an applicable performance period, by December 1 of the calendar year preceding the applicable performance year.
units.action_summary: Submit the virtual group election by December 1 of the preceding calendar year

units.obligation_text: Solo practitioners and groups with 10 or fewer eligible clinicians interested in forming or joining a virtual group have the option to contact their designated technical assistance representative or the Quality Payment Program Service Center ... in order to obtain information pertaining to virtual groups and/or determine whether or not they are eligible ... to participate in MIPS as a virtual group.
units.actor: solo practitioners and groups with 10 or fewer eligible clinicians
units.action_summary: May contact designated assistance or the Service Center to obtain info and determine eligibility for forming/joining a virtual group

units.obligation_text: TINs comprising a virtual group must establish a written formal agreement between each member of a virtual group prior to an election.
units.action_summary: Execute a written formal agreement among members before making a virtual group election

units.obligation_text: On behalf of a virtual group, the official designated virtual group representative must submit an election by December 1 of the calendar year prior to the start of the applicable performance period.
units.action_summary: Submit the virtual group election by December 1 on behalf of the group

units.obligation_text: The submission of a virtual group election must include, at a minimum, information pertaining to each TIN and NPI associated with the virtual group and contact information for the virtual group representative.
units.action_summary: Include TIN and NPI information and contact info in the virtual group election submission

units.obligation_text: Once an election is made, the virtual group representative must contact their designated CMS contact to update any election information that changed during a performance period one time prior to the start of an applicable submission period.
units.action_summary: Notify CMS one time prior to submission period of any election information changes that occurred during the performance period

units.obligation_text: Virtual groups must execute a written formal and contractual agreement between each member of a virtual group that includes the following elements:
units.action_summary: Execute a written formal contractual agreement among members that includes specified elements

units.obligation_text: Expressly state the only parties to the agreement are the TINs and NPIs of the virtual group.
units.actor: the written formal agreement (executed by virtual groups)
units.action_summary: Agreement must state parties are only the virtual group's TINs and NPIs

units.obligation_text: Be executed on behalf of the TINs and the NPIs by individuals who are authorized to bind the TINs and the NPIs, respectively.
units.actor: the written formal agreement (and signatories of virtual groups)
units.action_summary: Agreement must be signed by individuals authorized to bind the TINs and NPIs

units.obligation_text: Expressly require each member of the virtual group (including each NPI under each TIN) to agree to participate in the MIPS as a virtual group and comply with the requirements of the MIPS and all other applicable laws and regulations ...
units.actor: each member of the virtual group (including each NPI)
units.action_summary: Members must agree to participate as a virtual group and comply with MIPS and applicable laws

units.actor: each TIN within a virtual group
units.action_summary: TINs must notify their NPIs about participation in the virtual group

units.action_summary: Agreement must describe NPIs' rights, obligations, reporting duties, and effects on outside participation

units.obligation_text: Describe how the opportunity to receive payment adjustments will encourage each member of the virtual group ... to adhere to quality assurance and improvement.
units.actor: the written formal agreement (executed by virtual groups)
units.action_summary: Agreement must describe how payment adjustments incentivize quality assurance and improvement

units.obligation_text: Require each member of the virtual group to update its Medicare enrollment information, including the addition and deletion of NPIs billing through a TIN that is part of a virtual group, on a timely basis in accordance with Medicare program requirements and to notify the virtual group of any such changes within 30 days after the change.
units.actor: each member of the virtual group
units.action_summary: Members must timely update Medicare enrollment info and notify the virtual group within 30 days of changes

units.obligation_text: Be for a term of at least one performance period as specified in the formal written agreement.

units.action_summary: Permitted to submit measures via multiple mechanisms when available and applicable

units.obligation_text: The mental or behavioral health assessment should be signed by the provider and submitted with an attestation that the provider is prohibited from furnishing a complete medical record by applicable State or Federal privacy laws.
units.action_summary: Assessment should be signed and submitted with an attestation that the provider is prohibited from furnishing the complete record due to privacy laws.

units.obligation_text: The initial validation auditor must measure and report to the issuer and HHS, in a manner and timeframe specified by HHS, its inter-rater reliability rates among its reviewers.
units.action_summary: Must measure and report inter-rater reliability rates to the issuer and HHS as specified by HHS.

units.obligation_text: The initial validation auditor must achieve a consistency measure of at least 95 percent for his or her review outcomes, except that for validation of risk adjustment data for the 2015 and 2016 benefit years, the initial validation auditor may meet an inter-rater reliability standard of 85 percent for review outcomes.
units.action_summary: Must achieve 95% consistency in review outcomes; for 2015 and 2016, may meet an 85% standard instead.

units.obligation_text: HHS may impose civil money penalties in accordance with the procedures set forth in § 156.805(b) through (e) of this subchapter if an issuer of a risk adjustment covered plan—(i) Fails to engage an initial validation auditor; (ii) Fails to submit the results of an initial validation audit to HHS; (iii) Engages in misconduct or substantial non-compliance with the risk adjustment data validation standards and requirements applicable to issuers of risk adjustment covered plans; or (iv) Intentionally or recklessly misrepresents or falsifies information that it furnishes to HHS.
units.action_summary: HHS may impose civil money penalties if an issuer fails to engage/submits results, engages in misconduct/non-compliance, or intentionally/recklessly falsifies information.

units.obligation_text: Fails to engage an initial validation auditor;
units.actor: an issuer of a risk adjustment covered plan
units.action_summary: Failure to engage an initial validation auditor is a trigger for HHS to impose penalties.

units.obligation_text: Fails to submit the results of an initial validation audit to HHS;
units.actor: an issuer of a risk adjustment covered plan
units.action_summary: Failure to submit initial validation audit results to HHS is a trigger for penalties.

units.obligation_text: Engages in misconduct or substantial non-compliance with the risk adjustment data validation standards and requirements applicable to issuers of risk adjustment covered plans;
units.actor: an issuer of a risk adjustment covered plan
units.action_summary: Misconduct or substantial non-compliance by an issuer is a trigger for penalties.

units.obligation_text: Intentionally or recklessly misrepresents or falsifies information that it furnishes to HHS.
units.actor: an issuer of a risk adjustment covered plan
units.action_summary: Intentional or reckless misrepresentation or falsification by an issuer is a trigger for penalties.

units.obligation_text: The requirements of this part do not apply to—(1) Grandfathered health plan coverage as defined in § 147.140 of this subchapter; (2) Excepted benefits as described in section 2791(c) of the PHS Act; and (3) For plan years beginning on or after January 1, 2019, student health insurance coverage as defined in § 147.145 of this subchapter.
units.actor: the requirements of this part / regulated entities
units.action_summary: Exempts specified categories (grandfathered plans, excepted benefits, and certain student health insurance coverage) from the part's requirements.

units.obligation_text: A rate increase filed in a State, or effective in a State that does not require a rate increase to be filed, is subject to review if: (1) The rate increase is 15 percent or more applicable to a 12-month period that begins on January 1, as calculated under paragraph (b) of this section; or (2) The rate increase meets or exceeds a State-specific threshold applicable to a 12-month period that begins on January 1, as calculated under paragraph (b) of this section, determined by the Secretary.
units.actor: a rate increase filed in a State
units.action_summary: Rate increases meeting a 15% federal threshold or a Secretary-determined State-specific threshold are subject to review.

units.obligation_text: States interested in proposing a State-specific threshold greater than the Federal default stated in paragraph (a)(1) of this section are required to submit a proposal for approval of such threshold to the Secretary by August 1 of the preceding year.
units.action_summary: States must submit proposals to the Secretary by Aug 1 of the preceding year to set a higher State-specific threshold.

units.obligation_text: A rate increase meets or exceeds the applicable threshold set forth in paragraph (a) of this section if the average increase, including premium rating factors described in § 147.102 of this subchapter, for all enrollees weighted by premium volume for any plan within the product meets or exceeds the applicable threshold.
units.action_summary: Defines how to calculate whether a rate increase meets the applicable threshold (premium-weighted average increase for enrollees).

units.obligation_text: If a rate increase that does not otherwise meet or exceed the threshold under paragraph (b) of this section meets or exceeds the threshold when combined with a previous increase or increases during the 12-month period preceding the date on which the rate increase would become effective, then the rate increase must be considered to meet or exceed the threshold and is subject to review under § 154.210, and such review shall include a review of the aggregate rate increases during the applicable 12-month period.
units.action_summary: If combined increases in a 12-month period meet/exceed the threshold, the rate increase must be considered to meet the threshold and be reviewed, including aggregate increases.

units.obligation_text: CMS will make available to the public on its Web site the information contained in Parts I and III of each Rate Filing Justification that is not a trade secret or confidential commercial or financial information as defined in HHS’s Freedom of Information Act regulations, 45 CFR 5.31(d).
units.action_summary: CMS will publish on its website Parts I and III of each Rate Filing Justification that are not confidential.

units.obligation_text: If a State intends to make the information in paragraph (b)(1)(i) of this section available to the public prior to the date specified by the Secretary, or if it intends to make the information in paragraph (b)(1)(ii) of this section available to the public prior to the first day of the annual open enrollment period in the individual market for the applicable calendar year, the State must notify CMS in writing, no later than five (5) business days prior to the date it intends to make the information public, of its intent to do so and the date it intends to make the information public.
units.action_summary: State must notify CMS in writing at least 5 business days before making certain information public earlier than specified dates.

units.obligation_text: States may seek approval to operate a State Exchange utilizing the Federal platform for only the individual market.
units.action_summary: States are permitted to seek approval to operate a State Exchange using the Federal platform for the individual market only.

units.obligation_text: A State seeking approval to operate a State Exchange utilizing the Federal platform for the individual market to support select functions through a Federal platform agreement under § 155.200(f) must:
units.action_summary: States seeking such approval must follow required (listed) steps to operate a State Exchange on the Federal platform.

units.obligation_text: A State Exchange on the Federal platform that utilizes the Federal platform for SHOP functions, for plan years beginning on or after January 1, 2018, must require its QHP issuers to make any changes to rates in accordance with the timeline applicable in a Federally-facilitated SHOP under § 155.706(b)(6)(i)(A).
units.actor: a State Exchange on the Federal platform
units.action_summary: Must require QHP issuers to make rate changes according to the Federally-facilitated SHOP timeline.

units.obligation_text: The Exchange must include an entity from at least one of the following categories for receipt of a Navigator grant:
units.action_summary: Must include at least one entity from specified categories as Navigator grant recipients.

units.obligation_text: In a Federally-facilitated Exchange, no individual or entity shall be ineligible to operate as a Navigator solely because its principal place of business is outside of the Exchange service area;
units.action_summary: Prohibits deeming an individual/entity ineligible to be a Navigator solely due to its principal place of business being outside the service area.

units.obligation_text: In a Federally-facilitated Exchange, no individual or entity shall be ineligible to operate as a non-Navigator entity or as non-Navigator assistance personnel solely because its principal place of business is outside of the Exchange service area.
units.action_summary: Prohibits making an individual/entity ineligible to operate as non-Navigator assistance personnel solely due to its principal place of business being outside the Exchange service area.

units.obligation_text: An agent, broker, or issuer participating in direct enrollment must engage a third-party entity to conduct an annual review to demonstrate operational readiness in accordance with § 155.220(c)(3)(i)(K) and with § 156.1230(b)(2) of this subchapter.
units.actor: an agent, broker, or issuer participating in direct enrollment
units.action_summary: Must engage a third-party entity to conduct an annual operational readiness review per referenced requirements.

units.obligation_text: The third-party entity will be a downstream or delegated entity of the agent, broker or issuer that participates or wishes to participate in direct enrollment.
units.actor: the third-party entity / agent, broker, or issuer
units.action_summary: The annual reviewer must be a downstream or delegated entity of the agent, broker, or issuer.

units.obligation_text: An agent, broker, or issuer participating in direct enrollment must satisfy the requirement to demonstrate operational readiness under paragraph (a) of this section by engaging a third-party entity that meets each of the following standards:
units.actor: an agent, broker, or issuer participating in direct enrollment
units.action_summary: Must engage a third-party entity that meets specified standards to demonstrate operational readiness.

units.obligation_text: Has experience conducting audits or similar services, including experience with relevant privacy and security standards;
units.action_summary: Third-party entity must have relevant audit and privacy/security experience.

units.obligation_text: Adheres to HHS specifications for content, format, privacy, and security in the conduct of an operational readiness review, which includes ensuring that agents, brokers, and issuers are in compliance with the applicable privacy and security standards and other applicable requirements;
units.action_summary: Must follow HHS specifications for operational readiness reviews and ensure compliance by agents/brokers/issuers.

units.obligation_text: Collects, stores, and shares with HHS all data related to the third-party entity’s audit of agents, brokers, and issuers in a manner, format, and frequency specified by HHS until 10 years from the date of creation, and complies with the privacy and security standards HHS adopts for agents, brokers, and issuers as required in accordance with § 155.260;
units.action_summary: Must collect, store, and share audit data with HHS as specified and retain it for 10 years, complying with HHS privacy/security standards.

units.obligation_text: Discloses to HHS any financial relationships between the entity and individuals who own or are employed by an agent, broker, or issuer for which it is conducting an operational readiness review.
units.action_summary: Must disclose to HHS any financial relationships with owners/employees of the agent/broker/issuer being reviewed.

units.obligation_text: Complies with all applicable Federal and State requirements;
units.action_summary: Must comply with all applicable federal and state laws and requirements.

units.obligation_text: Ensures, on an annual basis, that appropriate staff successfully complete operational readiness review training as established by HHS prior to conducting audits under paragraph (a) of this section;
units.action_summary: Must ensure staff annually complete HHS-established operational readiness review training before conducting audits.

units.obligation_text: Permits access by the Secretary and the Office of the Inspector General (OIG) or their designees ... to the third-party entity’s books, contracts, computers, or other electronic systems, relating to the third-party entity’s audits ... until 10 years from the date of creation;
units.action_summary: Must permit Secretary and OIG access to relevant books, contracts, and systems related to audits for 10 years.

units.obligation_text: Complies with other minimum business criteria as specified in guidance by HHS.
units.action_summary: Must meet other minimum business criteria as specified by HHS guidance.

units.obligation_text: An agent, broker or issuer may engage multiple third-party entities to conduct the audit under paragraph (a) of this section and each third-party entity must satisfy the standards outlined under paragraph (b) of this section.
units.actor: an agent, broker or issuer; each third-party entity
units.action_summary: Agents/brokers/issuers may engage multiple third-party entities for audits; each engaged third-party must meet the standards in paragraph (b).

units.obligation_text: The Exchange may not determine a tax filer eligible for APTC if HHS notifies the Exchange ... that APTC were made on behalf of the tax filer ... and the tax filer or his or her spouse did not comply with the requirement to file an income tax return for that year ... and reconcile the advance payments of the premium tax credit for that period.
units.action_summary: Exchange shall not determine a tax filer eligible for APTC when HHS notifies it that APTC were made and the filer/spouse did not file required tax returns and reconcile advance premium tax credits.

units.obligation_text: the Exchange must accept the applicant’s attestation regarding a tax filer’s annual household income without further verification.
units.action_summary: Exchange must accept attestations of increased or expected increased annual household income without further verification when conditions apply.

units.obligation_text: If an applicant’s attestation to projected annual household income ... is greater than or equal to 100 percent but not more than 400 percent of the FPL ... and is more than a reasonable threshold above the annual household income computed ... the Exchange must proceed in accordance with § 155.315(f)(1) through (4).
units.action_summary: If attested projected income is between 100%-400% FPL and significantly above computed income, the Exchange must follow verification procedures §155.315(f)(1)-(4).

units.obligation_text: For the purposes of this paragraph, a reasonable threshold is established by the Exchange in guidance and approved by HHS, but must not be less than 10 percent, and can also include a threshold dollar amount.
units.action_summary: Exchange must establish a reasonable threshold (approved by HHS) that is not less than 10%; it may include a dollar amount.

units.obligation_text: Applicants that would otherwise be eligible for APTC based on § 155.305(f)(2) are not subject to the verification described in this paragraph.
units.action_summary: Applicants eligible for APTC per §155.305(f)(2) are exempt from this verification requirement.

units.obligation_text: If, at the conclusion of the period specified in § 155.315(f)(2)(ii), the Exchange remains unable to verify the applicant’s attestation, the Exchange must determine the applicant’s eligibility based on the information described in paragraph (c)(3)(ii)(A) of this section, notify the applicant of such determination in accordance with the notice requirements specified in § 155.310(g), and implement such determination in accordance with the effective dates specified in § 155.330(f).
units.action_summary: If unable to verify by the deadline, Exchange must determine eligibility based on available information, notify the applicant per §155.310(g), and implement the determination per §155.330(f).

units.obligation_text: If, at the conclusion of the period specified in § 155.315(f)(2)(ii), the Exchange remains unable to verify the applicant’s attestation and the information described in paragraph (c)(3)(ii)(A) of this section is unavailable, the Exchange must determine the tax filer ineligible for advance payments of the premium tax credit and cost-sharing reductions, notify the applicant of such determination in accordance with the notice requirements specified in § 155.310(g), and discontinue any advance payments of the premium tax credit and cost-sharing reductions in accordance with the effective dates specified in § 155.330(f).
units.action_summary: If unable to verify and baseline info is unavailable, Exchange must determine filer ineligible for APTC/CSRs, notify the applicant, and discontinue advance payments per effective dates.

units.obligation_text: the Exchange must accept the applicant’s attestation for the tax filer’s family without further verification, unless: (1) The Exchange finds that an applicant’s attestation ... is not reasonably compatible with other information provided ...; or (2) The data ... indicates that projected annual household income is under 100 percent FPL and the applicant’s attestation ... is greater than or equal to 100 percent but not more than 400 percent ... and is more than a reasonable threshold ... in which case the Exchange must follow the procedures specified in § 155.315(f)(1) through (4).
units.action_summary: Exchange must accept attestations of increased income without further verification unless attestation is incompatible with other info or triggers the >reasonable threshold condition, in which case Exchange must follow verification procedures.

units.obligation_text: The Exchange finds that an applicant’s attestation of a tax filer’s annual household income is not reasonably compatible with other information provided by the application filer,
units.action_summary: If Exchange finds attestation not reasonably compatible with other provided information, this is an exception triggering further verification.

units.obligation_text: The data described in paragraph (c)(3)(vi)(A) of this section indicates that projected annual household income is under 100 percent FPL and the applicant’s attestation to projected household income ... is greater than or equal to 100 percent but not more than 400 percent ... and is more than a reasonable threshold above the annual household income ... in which case the Exchange must follow the procedures specified in § 155.315(f)(1) through (4).
units.action_summary: If data shows projected income <100% FPL but applicant attests 100%-400% and exceeds the reasonable threshold, Exchange must follow specified verification procedures.

units.obligation_text: If electronic data are unavailable or an applicant’s attestation to projected annual household income ... is more than a reasonable threshold below the annual household income as computed using data sources described ... the Exchange must follow the procedures specified in § 155.315(f)(1) through (4).
units.action_summary: If electronic data is unavailable or attested income is significantly below computed income, Exchange must follow verification procedures in §155.315(f)(1)-(4).

units.obligation_text: If, at the conclusion of the period specified in § 155.315(f)(2)(ii), the Exchange remains unable to verify the applicant’s attestation, the Exchange must determine the applicant’s eligibility based on the information described in paragraph (c)(3)(ii)(A) of this section, notify the applicant ... and implement such determination in accordance with the effective dates specified in § 155.330(f).
units.action_summary: If unable to verify by deadline, Exchange must determine eligibility based on available info, notify applicant, and implement per effective dates.

units.obligation_text: If, at the conclusion of the period specified in § 155.315(f)(2)(ii), the Exchange remains unable to verify the applicant’s attestation for the tax filer and the information described in paragraph (c)(3)(ii)(A) of this section is unavailable, the Exchange must determine the tax filer ineligible for advance payments of the premium tax credit and cost-sharing reductions, notify the applicant ... and discontinue any advance payments of the premium tax credit and cost-sharing reductions in accordance with the effective dates specified in § 155.330(f).
units.action_summary: If unable to verify and baseline info is unavailable for tax filer, Exchange must determine filer ineligible for APTC/CSRs, notify, and discontinue advance payments per effective dates.

units.obligation_text: For any benefit year for which it does not reasonably expect to obtain sufficient verification data ... the Exchange must follow the procedures specified in paragraph (d)(4)(i) of this section or, for benefit years 2016 through 2019, the Exchange may follow the procedures specified in paragraph (d)(4)(ii) of this section.
units.action_summary: Exchange must follow specified alternate procedures when it does not expect to obtain sufficient verification data; for 2016-2019 may follow different procedures.

units.obligation_text: If an enrollee qualifies for a special enrollment period, the Exchange must allow the enrollee and his or her dependents to change to another QHP within the same level of coverage (or one metal level higher or lower, if no such QHP is available), as outlined in § 156.140(b) of this subchapter;
units.action_summary: When an enrollee qualifies for SEP, Exchange must allow enrollee and dependents to switch to another QHP within same metal level (or adjacent metal level if needed).

units.obligation_text: If a dependent qualifies for a special enrollment period, and an enrollee is adding the dependent to his or her QHP, the Exchange must allow the enrollee to add the dependent to his or her current QHP; or, if the QHP’s business rules do not allow the dependent to enroll, the Exchange must allow the enrollee and his or her dependents to change to another QHP within the same level of coverage (or one metal level higher or lower, if no such QHP is available), as outlined in § 156.140(b) of this subchapter, or enroll the new qualified individual in a separate QHP.
units.action_summary: If dependent qualifies for SEP, Exchange must allow adding the dependent to current QHP; if not possible, must allow change to another QHP or enroll the dependent in a separate QHP.

units.obligation_text: Qualified individuals who are required to demonstrate coverage in the 60 days prior to a qualifying event can either demonstrate that they had minimum essential coverage ...; lived in a foreign country or in a United States territory ...; are an Indian ...; or lived in a service area ... where no qualified health plan was offered through the Exchange.
units.action_summary: Qualified individuals may satisfy the 60-day prior coverage requirement by one of several alternatives (MEC for 1+ days, foreign residence, Indian status, or residence in an area with no QHP offered).

units.obligation_text: In the case of birth, adoption, placement for adoption, placement in foster care, or child support or other court order as described in paragraph (d)(2)(i) of this section, the Exchange must ensure that coverage is effective for a qualified individual or enrollee on the date of birth, adoption, placement for adoption, placement in foster care, or effective date of court order; or it may permit the qualified individual or enrollee to elect a coverage effective date of the first of the month following plan selection; or in accordance with paragraph (b)(1) of this section. If the Exchange permits the qualified individual or enrollee to elect a coverage effective date of either the first of the month following the date of plan selection or in accordance with paragraph (b)(1) of this section, the Exchange must ensure coverage is effective on the date duly selected by the qualified individual or enrollee.
units.action_summary: For specified events (birth, adoption, etc.), Exchange must ensure coverage is effective on the event date or may permit the enrollee to choose a later effective date; if permitted, must ensure coverage is effective on the selected date.

units.obligation_text: For purposes of this section, changes in eligibility for advance payments of the premium tax credit and cost sharing reductions, including terminations, must adhere to the effective dates specified in § 155.330(f).
units.action_summary: Changes in eligibility for APTC and CSRs, including terminations, must follow the effective dates in §155.330(f).

units.obligation_text: For an individual who is ineligible to purchase coverage under an eligible employer-sponsored plan, the Exchange determines the required contribution for coverage in accordance with section 5000A(e)(1)(B)(ii) of the Code, inclusive of all members of the family ... If there is not a bronze level plan offered through the Exchange in the individual’s rating area, the Exchange must use the annual premium for the lowest cost Exchange metal level plan available in the individual market through the Exchange in the State in the rating area in which the individual resides to determine whether coverage exceeds the affordability threshold specified in section 5000A(e)(1) of the Code;
units.action_summary: Exchange must determine required contribution per the Code; if no bronze plan exists in the rating area, it must use the annual premium of the lowest cost metal level plan to assess affordability.

units.obligation_text: The Exchange will only accept an application for an exemption described in § 155.605(d)(1) during one of the 3 calendar years after the month or months during which the applicant attests that the hardship occurred.
units.action_summary: Exchange will accept hardship exemption applications only within the three calendar years after the month(s) the hardship occurred.

units.obligation_text: For plan years beginning before January 1, 2018, an Exchange must provide for the establishment of a SHOP that meets the requirements of this subpart and is designed to assist qualified employers and facilitate the enrollment of qualified employees into qualified health plans.
units.action_summary: For plan years before 2018, Exchange must establish a SHOP meeting subpart requirements to assist employers and facilitate employee enrollment in QHPs.

units.obligation_text: For plan years beginning on or after January 1, 2018, an Exchange must provide for the establishment of a SHOP that meets the requirements of this subpart and is designed to assist qualified employers in facilitating the enrollment of their employees in qualified health plans.
units.action_summary: For plan years on/after 2018, Exchange must establish a SHOP to assist employers in facilitating employee enrollment in QHPs.

units.obligation_text: The SHOP must carry out all the required functions of an Exchange described in this subpart and in subparts C, E, K, and M of this part, except: (1) Requirements related to individual eligibility determinations in subpart D of this part; (2) Requirements related to enrollment of qualified individuals described in subpart E of this part; (3) The requirement to issue certificates of exemption in accordance with § 155.200(b); and (4) Requirements related to the payment of premiums by individuals, Indian tribes, tribal organizations and urban Indian organizations under § 155.240.
units.action_summary: SHOP must perform all required Exchange functions in referenced subparts, except for the listed exceptions.

units.obligation_text: Requirements related to individual eligibility determinations in subpart D of this part (are excepted).
units.action_summary: Shop is not required to carry out individual eligibility determination requirements from subpart D.

units.obligation_text: Requirements related to enrollment of qualified individuals described in subpart E of this part (are excepted).
units.action_summary: SHOP is not required to carry out enrollment requirements for qualified individuals from subpart E.

units.obligation_text: The requirement to issue certificates of exemption in accordance with § 155.200(b) (is excepted).
units.action_summary: SHOP is not required to issue certificates of exemption under §155.200(b).

units.obligation_text: Requirements related to the payment of premiums by individuals, Indian tribes, tribal organizations and urban Indian organizations under § 155.240 (are excepted).
units.action_summary: SHOP is not required to perform functions related to premium payments by individuals/tribal entities under §155.240.

units.obligation_text: The SHOP must adhere to the requirements outlined in subpart H.
units.action_summary: SHOP must comply with the requirements in subpart H.

units.obligation_text: The SHOP must allow a qualified employer to select a level of coverage as described in section 1302(d)(1) of the Affordable Care Act, in which all QHPs within that level are made available to the qualified employees of the employer.
units.action_summary: SHOP must let a qualified employer select a coverage level whereby all QHPs at that level are made available to the employer's qualified employees.

units.obligation_text: For plan years beginning on or after January 1, 2018, SHOP: (A) Must allow an employer to make available to qualified employees all QHPs at the level of coverage selected by the employer as described in paragraph (b)(2) of this section,
units.action_summary: For plan years on/after 2018, SHOP must allow employers to make all QHPs at the selected level available to employees.

units.obligation_text: (B) May allow an employer to make one or more QHPs available to qualified employees by a method other than the method described in paragraph (b)(2) of this section.
units.action_summary: SHOP may permit employers to make one or more specific QHPs available using a method other than selecting a coverage level.

units.obligation_text: For plan years beginning on or after January 1, 2018, a Federally-facilitated SHOP will provide a qualified employer a choice of two methods to make QHPs available to qualified employees: (A) The employer may choose a level of coverage as described in paragraph (b)(2) of this section, or (B) The employer may choose a single QHP.
units.action_summary: Federally-facilitated SHOP will offer employers a choice: select a coverage level (making all QHPs at that level available) or choose a single QHP.

title: Policy and Technical Changes to the Medicare Advantage and the Medicare Prescription Drug Benefit Programs for Contract Year 2019 CMS-4182-P

units.obligation_text: The application form must comply with CMS instructions regarding content and format and be approved by CMS as described in § 422.2262 of this chapter.
units.actor: the application form (i.e., the applicant/MA organization/HMO or CMP eligible individual)
units.action_summary: Ensure the application form complies with CMS instructions on content/format and is approved by CMS.

units.obligation_text: The application must be completed by an HMO or CMP eligible (or soon to become eligible) individual and include authorization for disclosure between HHS and its designees and the HMO or CMP.
units.actor: an HMO or CMP eligible (or soon to become eligible) individual (the applicant)
units.action_summary: The applicant must complete the application and include authorization for disclosure between HHS (and designees) and the HMO or CMP.

units.obligation_text: All cost contracts under section 1876 of the Act must agree to be rated under the quality rating system specified at subpart D of part 422, and for cost plans that provide the Part D prescription benefit, under the quality rating system specified at part 423 subpart D, of this chapter.
units.actor: all cost contracts under section 1876 of the Act
units.action_summary: Cost contracts must agree to be rated under the specified MA (and Part D where applicable) quality rating systems.

units.obligation_text: Cost contacts are not required to submit data on or be rated on specific measures determined by CMS to be inapplicable to their contract or for which data are not available, including hospital readmission and call center measures.
units.action_summary: Cost contracts need not submit data on or be rated on measures CMS deems inapplicable or lacking available data (e.g., readmission, call center).

units.obligation_text: The prohibitions, procedures and requirements relating to payment to individuals and entities on the preclusion list, defined in §422.2 of this chapter, apply to HMOs and CMPs that contract with CMS under section 1876 of the Act.
units.actor: HMOs and CMPs that contract with CMS under section 1876
units.action_summary: HMOs and CMPs contracting under section 1876 are subject to the payment prohibitions, procedures, and requirements related to the preclusion list.

units.obligation_text: In applying the provisions of §§ 422.2, 422.222, and 422.224 of this chapter under paragraph (e)(1) of this section, references to part 422 of this chapter must be read as references to this part, and references to MA organizations as references to HMOs and CMPs.
units.actor: persons applying the provisions of §§ 422.2, 422.222, and 422.224 under paragraph (e)(1)
units.action_summary: When applying those provisions under (e)(1), read references to part 422 as references to part 417 and MA organizations as HMOs and CMPs.

units.obligation_text: That payments must not be made to individuals and entities included on the preclusion list, defined in § 422.2 of this chapter.
units.action_summary: Payments are prohibited to individuals and entities on the CMS preclusion list.

units.obligation_text: Obtain CMS's approval of the continuation area, the communication materials that describe the option, and the MA organization's assurances of access to services.
units.actor: the MA organization (or entity implementing continuation of enrollment)
units.action_summary: MA organization must obtain CMS approval for the continuation area, related communication materials, and assurances of access to services.

units.obligation_text: Organizations that require enrollees to give advance notice of intent to use the continuation of enrollment option, must stipulate the notification process in the communication materials.
units.actor: organizations that require advance notice (MA organizations)
units.action_summary: If an organization requires advance notice for continuation of enrollment, it must describe the notification process in its communication materials.

units.obligation_text: CMS may implement passive enrollment procedures in any of the following situations:
units.action_summary: CMS is permitted to implement passive enrollment procedures under specified circumstances.

units.obligation_text: CMS may implement passive enrollment described in paragraph (g)(1)(iii) only into MA-PD plans that meet all the following requirements:
units.actor: CMS (with respect to which plans may receive passive enrollment)
units.action_summary: CMS may implement passive enrollment into MA-PD plans, but only into plans that meet the listed requirements.

units.obligation_text: Operate as a fully integrated dual eligible special needs plan as defined in § 422.2, or a specialized MA plan for special needs individuals that meets a high standard of integration, as described in § 422.102(e).
units.actor: MA-PD plans seeking to receive passive enrollments
units.action_summary: Plans must operate as fully integrated dual-eligible SNPs or meet a high standard of integration to be eligible for passive enrollment.
units.modal_raw: must (as a requirement to receive passive enrollments)

units.obligation_text: Have substantially similar provider and facility networks and Medicare- and Medicaid-covered benefits as the plan (or plans) from which the beneficiaries are passively enrolled.
units.action_summary: Plans must have provider/facility networks and Medicare/Medicaid-covered benefits substantially similar to the plan(s) beneficiaries are being passively enrolled from.

units.obligation_text: Have an overall quality rating of at least 3 stars under the rating system described in § 422.160 through § 422.166 for the year prior to the plan year passive enrollments take effect or is a low enrollment contract or new MA plan as defined in § 422.252.
units.action_summary: Plans must have a ≥3-star overall quality rating for the prior year, or qualify as a low-enrollment contract or new MA plan to receive passive enrollments.

units.obligation_text: Not have any prohibition on new enrollment imposed by CMS.
units.action_summary: Plans must not be subject to any CMS-imposed prohibition on new enrollment to be eligible for passive enrollment.

units.obligation_text: Have limits on premiums and cost-sharing appropriate to full-benefit dual eligible beneficiaries.
units.action_summary: Plans must have premiums and cost-sharing limits appropriate to full-benefit dual eligible beneficiaries.

units.obligation_text: Have the operational capacity to passively enroll beneficiaries and agree to receive the enrollments.
units.action_summary: Plans must have the operational capacity to perform passive enrollments and must agree to receive passively enrolled beneficiaries.

units.obligation_text: Decline the plan selected by CMS, in a form and manner determined by CMS,
units.actor: individuals who are potential passive enrollees
units.action_summary: To avoid passive enrollment, individuals must decline the CMS-selected plan using the form and manner CMS specifies.

units.obligation_text: Request enrollment in another plan.
units.actor: individuals who are potential passive enrollees
units.action_summary: Individuals may request enrollment in a different plan to avoid being passively enrolled in the CMS-selected plan.

units.obligation_text: The MA organization that receives the passive enrollment must provide to the enrollee a notice that describes the costs and benefits of the plan and the process for accessing care under the plan and clearly explains the beneficiary’s ability to decline the enrollment or choose another plan.
units.actor: the MA organization that receives the passive enrollment
units.action_summary: MA organization receiving passive enrollments must provide enrollees a notice describing plan costs/benefits, access procedures, and how to decline or choose another plan.

units.obligation_text: Such notice must be provided to all potential passively enrolled enrollees prior to the enrollment effective date (or as soon as possible after the effective date if prior notice is not practical), in a form and manner determined by CMS.
units.actor: the MA organization that receives the passive enrollment
units.action_summary: The notice must be given to all potential passively enrolled enrollees before the enrollment effective date (or promptly after if prior notice impractical), in CMS-specified form and manner.

units.obligation_text: Individuals not otherwise eligible for a special election period at the time of passive enrollment will be provided with a special election period, in accordance with § 422.62(b)(4).
units.actor: CMS (or the enrollment/plan process as administered by CMS)
units.action_summary: Individuals passively enrolled who otherwise lack a special election period will be given a special election period per § 422.62(b)(4).

units.obligation_text: Except as provided in paragraphs (a)(3)(ii) and (iii) and (a)(4) of this section, an individual who is enrolled in an MA plan may make an election once during the first 3 months of the year to enroll in another MA plan or disenroll to obtain Original Medicare.
units.actor: an individual who is enrolled in an MA plan
units.action_summary: Enrollees may, once during the first three months of the year, switch to another MA plan or disenroll to Original Medicare (subject to exceptions).

units.obligation_text: An individual who chooses to exercise this election may also make a coordinating election to enroll in or disenroll from Part D, as specified in § 423.38(e).
units.action_summary: Individuals exercising this MA election may also elect to enroll in or disenroll from Part D as specified.

units.obligation_text: For 2019 and subsequent years, a newly MA eligible individual who is enrolled in a MA plan may change his or her election once during the period that begins the month the individual is entitled to both Part A and Part B and ends on the last day of the third month of the entitlement.
units.actor: a newly MA eligible individual who is enrolled in a MA plan
units.action_summary: Newly MA-eligible enrollees may change their election once during the three-month period starting with entitlement to Part A and Part B.

units.obligation_text: The limitation to one election or change in paragraphs (a)(3)(i) and (ii) of this section does not apply to elections or changes made during the annual coordinated election period specified in paragraph (a)(2) of this section, or during a special election period specified in paragraph (b) of this section.
units.action_summary: The single-election limitation does not apply to elections during the annual coordinated election period or applicable special election periods.

units.obligation_text: Subject to the MA plan being open to enrollees as provided under § 422.60(a)(2), an MA eligible institutionalized individual may at any time elect an MA plan or change his or her election from an MA plan to Original Medicare, to a different MA plan, or from original Medicare to an MA plan.
units.action_summary: Institutionalized MA-eligible individuals may at any time elect or change MA/Original Medicare elections, provided the MA plan is open to enrollees as specified.

units.obligation_text: Through 2018, at any time from January 1 through February 14, an individual who is enrolled in an MA plan may elect Original Medicare once during this 45-day period.
units.actor: individuals enrolled in an MA plan (through 2018)
units.action_summary: Through 2018, enrollees could elect Original Medicare once during Jan 1–Feb 14 each year.

units.obligation_text: Subject to paragraph (c)(2) of this section, an individual who fails to make an election during the initial coverage election period is deemed to have elected original Medicare.
units.actor: individuals who fail to make an election during the initial coverage election period
units.action_summary: If an individual does not elect during the initial coverage election period (subject to c(2)), they are treated as having elected Original Medicare.

units.obligation_text: During an individual’s initial coverage election period, an individual may be deemed to have elected a MA special needs plan for individuals entitled to medical assistance under a State plan under Title XIX offered by the organization provided all the following conditions are met:
units.action_summary: An individual may be default-enrolled into a specified MA special needs plan during the initial coverage election period if all enumerated conditions are met.

units.obligation_text: At the time of the deemed election, the individual remains enrolled in an affiliated Medicaid managed care plan.
units.action_summary: A condition for default enrollment is that the individual remains enrolled in an affiliated Medicaid managed care plan at the time of deemed election.

units.obligation_text: The state has approved the use of the default enrollment process in the contract described in § 422.107 and provides the information that is necessary for the MA organization to identify individuals who are in their initial coverage election period;
units.actor: the State and MA organization (as condition)
units.action_summary: A condition is state approval of the default enrollment process in the contract and provision of necessary information to identify eligible individuals.
units.modal_raw: must (state must approve and provide information)

units.obligation_text: The MA organization offering the MA special needs plan has issued the notice described in paragraph (c)(2)(iv) of this section to the individual;
units.actor: the MA organization offering the MA special needs plan
units.action_summary: A condition for default enrollment is that the MA organization has issued the required notice to the individual.

units.obligation_text: Prior to the effective date described in paragraph (c)(2)(iii) of this section, the individual does not decline the default enrollment and does not elect to receive coverage other than through the MA organization;
units.action_summary: A condition is that the individual does not decline default enrollment or choose other coverage prior to the effective date.

units.obligation_text: CMS has approved the MA organization to use default enrollment under paragraph (c)(2)(ii) of this section.
units.actor: CMS (approval) and MA organization (to have approval)
units.action_summary: A condition is that CMS has approved the MA organization to implement the default enrollment process.

units.obligation_text: An MA organization must obtain approval from CMS before implementing any default enrollment as described in this section. CMS may suspend or rescind approval when CMS determines the MA organization is not in compliance with the requirements of this section.
units.actor: MA organization (first sentence) and CMS (second sentence)
units.action_summary: MA organizations must obtain CMS approval before implementing default enrollment; CMS may suspend or rescind that approval for noncompliance.

units.obligation_text: The MA organization must provide notification that describes the costs and benefits of the MA plan and the process for accessing care under the plan and clearly explains the individual's ability to decline the enrollment, up to and including the day prior to the enrollment effective date, and either enroll in Original Medicare or choose another plan. Such notification must be provided to all individuals who qualify for default enrollment under paragraph (c)(2) of this section no fewer than 60 calendar days prior to the enrollment effective date described in paragraph (c)(2)(iii) of this section.
units.action_summary: MA organizations must provide detailed notification about costs, benefits, access, and how to decline, to qualifying individuals at least 60 days before the default enrollment effective date.

units.obligation_text: An MA plan offered by an MA organization must accept any individual (regardless of whether the individual has end-stage renal disease) who requests enrollment during his or her Initial Coverage Election Period and is enrolled in a health plan offered by the MA organization during the month immediately preceding the MA plan enrollment effective date, and who meets the eligibility requirements at § 422.50.
units.actor: an MA plan offered by an MA organization
units.action_summary: MA plans must accept any individual meeting the described enrollment-period and eligibility conditions who requests enrollment.

units.obligation_text: An individual who requests seamless continuation of coverage as described in paragraph (d)(1) of this section may complete a simplified election, in a form and manner approved by CMS that meets the requirements in § 422.60(c)(1).
units.actor: an individual who requests seamless continuation of coverage
units.action_summary: Such individuals may use a CMS-approved simplified election process that meets § 422.60(c)(1) requirements.

units.obligation_text: Except as provided in paragraph (f)(5) of this section, MA local plans (as defined in § 422.2) must have an out-of pocket maximum for Medicare Parts A and B services that is no greater than the annual limit set by CMS using Medicare Fee-for-Service data.
units.action_summary: MA local plans must set an out-of-pocket maximum for Parts A and B no greater than the CMS annual limit (using FFS data), except as provided in f(5).

units.obligation_text: With respect to a local PPO plan, the limit specified under paragraph (f)(4) of this section applies only to use of network providers. Such local PPO plans must include a total catastrophic limit annually determined by CMS using Medicare Fee-for-Service and to establish appropriate beneficiary out-of-pocket expenditures for both in-network and out-of-network Parts A and B services that is—
units.action_summary: Local PPOs must include a CMS-determined total catastrophic limit for in-network and out-of-network Parts A and B services; the f(4) limit applies only to network provider use.

units.obligation_text: Not greater than the annual limit set by CMS using Medicare Fee-for-Service data to establish appropriate beneficiary out-of-pocket expenditures.
units.actor: local PPO plans (with respect to their total catastrophic limit)
units.action_summary: The total catastrophic limit must not exceed the annual limit set by CMS using Medicare FFS data.

units.obligation_text: Cost sharing for Medicare Part A and B services specified by CMS does not exceed levels annually determined by CMS to be discriminatory for such services. CMS may use Medicare Fee-for-Service data to evaluate the possibility of discrimination and to establish non-discriminatory out-of-pocket limits and also use MA encounter data to inform patient utilization scenarios used to help identify MA plan cost sharing standards and thresholds that are not discriminatory.
units.actor: MA plans (cost-sharing specified by CMS) and CMS (data use)
units.action_summary: MA plans' cost sharing for Part A/B (as specified by CMS) must not exceed CMS-determined discriminatory thresholds; CMS may use FFS and MA encounter data to evaluate and set non-discriminatory limits.

units.obligation_text: Catastrophic limit. MA regional plans are required to establish a catastrophic limit on beneficiary out-of-pocket expenditures for in-network benefits under the Medicare Fee-for-Service program (Part A and Part B benefits) that is no greater than the annual limit set by CMS using Medicare Fee-for-Service data to establish appropriate out-of-pocket limits.
units.action_summary: MA regional plans must set an in-network catastrophic out-of-pocket limit no greater than the CMS annual limit determined using Medicare FFS data.

units.obligation_text: Total catastrophic limit. MA regional plans are required to establish a total catastrophic limit on beneficiary out-of-pocket expenditures for in-network and out-of-network benefits under the Medicare Fee-for-Service program (Part A and Part B benefits).
units.action_summary: MA regional plans must establish a total catastrophic out-of-pocket limit covering both in-network and out-of-network benefits.

units.obligation_text: This total out-of-pocket catastrophic limit, which would apply to both in-network and out-of-network benefits under Medicare Fee-for-Service, may be higher than the in-network catastrophic limit in paragraph (d)(2) of this section, but may not increase the limit described in paragraph (d)(2) of this section and may be no greater than the annual limit set by CMS using Medicare Fee-for-Service data.
units.action_summary: The total out-of-pocket catastrophic limit may exceed the in-network limit but cannot increase the in-network limit described in (d)(2) and must be no greater than CMS's annual FFS-based limit.

units.obligation_text: Supplemental benefits packaging. MA organizations may offer enrollees a group of services as one optional supplemental benefit, offer services individually, or offer a combination of groups and individual services.
units.action_summary: MA organizations are permitted to package supplemental benefits as groups, offer them individually, or mix both approaches.

units.obligation_text: An MA organization must disclose the information specified in paragraph (b) of this section in the manner specified by CMS—
units.action_summary: MA organizations must disclose the information listed in paragraph (b) in the manner CMS specifies.

units.obligation_text: At the time of enrollment and at least annually thereafter, by the first day of the annual coordinated election period.
units.actor: MA organization (with respect to disclosure timing)
units.action_summary: MA organizations must make the required disclosures at enrollment and at least annually by the first day of the annual coordinated election period.

units.obligation_text: Copies of its evidence of coverage, summary of benefits, and information (names, addresses, phone numbers, and specialty) on the network of contracted providers. Posting does not relieve the MA organization of its responsibility under paragraph (a) of this section to provide hard copies to enrollees upon request.
units.action_summary: MA organizations must provide hard copies of evidence of coverage, summary of benefits, and network information upon enrollee request, even if posted online.

units.obligation_text: MA organizations are required to collect, analyze, and report data that permit measurement of health outcomes and other indices of quality.
units.action_summary: MA organizations must collect, analyze, and report data enabling measurement of health outcomes and quality indices.

units.obligation_text: MA organizations must provide unbiased, accurate, and complete quality data described in paragraph (c)(1) of this section to CMS on a timely basis as requested by CMS.
units.action_summary: MA organizations must timely provide unbiased, accurate, and complete quality data to CMS when requested.

units.obligation_text: CMS adds, updates, and removes measures used to calculate the Star Ratings as provided in this section. CMS lists the measures used for a particular Star Rating each year in the Technical Notes or similar guidance document with publication of the Star Ratings.
units.action_summary: CMS will add, update, or remove measures for Star Ratings and annually list measures used for each Star Rating in Technical Notes or similar guidance.

units.obligation_text: CMS reviews the quality of the data on which performance, scoring and rating of a measure is based before using the data to score and rate performance or in calculating a Star Rating.
units.action_summary: CMS must review data quality (accuracy, reliability, validity, variation) before using those data to score or rate measures or calculate Star Ratings.

title: Medicare Program; Contract Year 2019 Policy and Technical Changes to the Medicare Advantage, Medicare Cost Plan, Medicare Fee-for-Service, the Medicare Prescription Drug Benefit Programs, and the PACE Program

units.obligation_text: The application form must comply with CMS instructions regarding chapter.
units.actor: HMO or CMP applicant / application form
units.action_summary: Application form must follow CMS instructions.

units.obligation_text: The application must be completed by an HMO or CMP eligible (or soon to become eligible) individual
units.action_summary: Applicant must complete the application.

units.obligation_text: The application must ... include authorization for disclosure between HHS and its designees and the HMO or CMP.
units.action_summary: Application must include authorization for disclosure between HHS/designees and the HMO/CMP.

units.obligation_text: All cost contracts under section 1876 of the Act must agree to be rated under the quality rating system specified at subpart D of part 422, and for cost plans that provide the Part D prescription benefit, under the quality rating system specified at part 423 subpart D, of this chapter.
units.action_summary: Cost contracts must agree to be rated under specified quality rating systems.

units.obligation_text: Cost contracts are not required to submit data on or be rated on specific measures determined by CMS to be inapplicable to their contract or for which data are not available, including hospital readmission and call center measures.
units.action_summary: Cost contracts are exempt from submitting or being rated on measures CMS deems inapplicable or lacking data for.

units.obligation_text: The prohibitions, procedures and requirements relating to payment to individuals and entities on the preclusion list, defined in § 422.2 of this chapter, apply to HMOs and CMPs that contract with CMS under section 1876 of the Act.
units.actor: HMOs and CMPs that contract under section 1876
units.action_summary: HMOs and CMPs are subject to payment prohibitions/procedures applicable to preclusion list entities.

units.obligation_text: In applying the provisions of §§ 422.2, 422.222, and 422.224 ... references to part 422 of this chapter must be read as references to this part, and references to MA organizations as references to HMOs and CMPs.
units.action_summary: When applying those provisions, read references to part 422 and MA organizations as referring to this part and to HMOs/CMPs respectively.

units.obligation_text: That payments must not be made to individuals and entities included on the preclusion list, defined in § 422.2 of this chapter.
units.action_summary: Payments must not be made to individuals/entities on the preclusion list.

units.obligation_text: Have substantially similar provider and facility networks and Medicare- and Medicaid-covered benefits as the plan (or plans) from which the beneficiaries are passively enrolled.
units.action_summary: Continuation area/MA organization must have networks and benefits substantially similar to the originating plan(s).

units.obligation_text: Obtain CMS’s approval of the continuation area, the communication materials that describe the option, and the MA organization’s assurances of access to services.
units.action_summary: MA organization must obtain CMS approval for the continuation area, communications, and assurances of access.

units.obligation_text: Organizations that require enrollees to give advance notice of enrollment option, must stipulate the notification process in the communication materials.
units.action_summary: If an organization requires advance notice, it must describe the notification process in its communications.

units.obligation_text: CMS may implement passive enrollment procedures in any of the following situations:
units.action_summary: CMS is permitted to use passive enrollment in specified situations.

units.obligation_text: CMS may implement passive enrollment in circumstances including immediate terminations (§ 422.510(b)(2)(i)(B)), when remaining in a plan poses potential harm, or when passive enrollment will promote integrated care for certain dual eligible beneficiaries after consulting the State Medicaid agency.
units.action_summary: CMS may apply passive enrollment for immediate terminations, harm to members, or to promote integrated care for qualifying dual eligibles.

units.obligation_text: CMS may implement passive enrollment described in paragraph (g)(1)(iii) only into MA–PD plans that meet all the following requirements:
units.actor: CMS (as to where passive enrollment may be implemented) / MA–PD plans (as eligible recipients)
units.action_summary: Passive enrollment under (g)(1)(iii) may only be applied to MA–PD plans that satisfy the listed requirements.

units.obligation_text: Have an overall quality rating of at least 3 stars under the rating system described in § 422.160 through § 422.166 for the year prior to the plan year passive enrollments take effect or is a low enrollment contract or new MA plan as defined in § 422.252.
units.action_summary: MA–PD plans must have at least a 3-star rating (or be a low enrollment/new plan) to receive passive enrollments under this provision.

units.obligation_text: Not have any prohibition on new enrollment imposed by CMS.
units.action_summary: Plan must have no CMS-imposed prohibition on new enrollments to be eligible for passive enrollment.

units.obligation_text: Have limits on premiums and cost-sharing appropriate to full-benefit dual eligible beneficiaries.
units.action_summary: Plan must have premiums and cost-sharing limits suitable for full-benefit dual eligibles.

units.obligation_text: Have the operational capacity to passively enroll beneficiaries and agree to receive the enrollments.
units.action_summary: Plan must be operationally able and willing to accept passive enrollments.

units.obligation_text: Individuals will be considered to have elected the plan selected by CMS unless they—
units.action_summary: By default, individuals are deemed to have elected the CMS-selected plan unless they take specified actions.

units.obligation_text: Decline the plan selected by CMS, in a form and manner determined by CMS,
units.action_summary: Individuals may decline the CMS-selected plan by following CMS-determined form and manner.

units.obligation_text: Request enrollment in another plan.
units.action_summary: Individuals may request enrollment in a different plan to avoid default enrollment.

units.obligation_text: The MA organization that receives the passive enrollment must provide to the enrollee a notice that describes the costs and benefits of the plan and the process for accessing care under the plan and clearly explains the beneficiary’s ability to decline the enrollment or choose another plan.
units.action_summary: MA organization must notify enrollees about plan costs/benefits, access process, and options to decline or choose another plan.

units.obligation_text: Such notice must be provided to all potential passively enrolled enrollees prior to the enrollment effective date (or as soon as possible after the effective date if prior notice is not practical), in a form and manner determined by CMS.
units.action_summary: MA organization must provide the notice before the enrollment effective date (or ASAP after if not practical) in a CMS-determined form/manner.

units.obligation_text: Individuals not otherwise eligible for a special election period at the time of passive enrollment will be provided with a special election period, in accordance with § 422.62(b)(4).
units.actor: CMS / MA program (provider of election period)
units.action_summary: Individuals passively enrolled will be given a special election period if they weren't already eligible for one.

units.obligation_text: An individual who is enrolled in an MA plan may make an election once during the first 3 months of the year to enroll in another MA plan or disenroll to obtain Original Medicare.
units.actor: Individuals enrolled in an MA plan
units.action_summary: Enrollees may make one election in the first three months to change plans or disenroll to Original Medicare.

units.obligation_text: Subject to paragraph (c)(2) of this section, an individual who fails to make an election during the initial coverage election period is deemed to have elected original Medicare.
units.action_summary: If an individual does not elect during the initial coverage period, they are deemed to have elected Original Medicare.

units.obligation_text: A newly MA eligible individual who is enrolled in a MA plan may change his or her election once during the period that begins the month the individual is entitled to both Part A and Part B and ends on the last day of the third month of the entitlement.
units.action_summary: Newly eligible individuals may change their MA election once during the specified entitlement period.

units.obligation_text: During an individual’s initial coverage election period, an individual may be deemed to have elected a MA special needs plan for individuals entitled to medical assistance under Title XIX ... provided all the following conditions are met: (A) At the time of the deemed election, the individual remains enrolled in an affiliated Medicaid managed care plan; (B) The state has approved the use of the default enrollment process ...; (C) The MA organization offering the MA special needs plan has issued the notice ...; (D) Prior to the effective date, the individual does not decline the default enrollment and does not elect to receive coverage other than through the MA organization; and (E) CMS has approved the MA organization to use default enrollment under paragraph (c)(2)(ii) of this section.
units.actor: MA organization / state / CMS as applicable; effect on individual
units.action_summary: An individual may be default-enrolled into an MA-SNP during initial coverage period if all listed conditions (A–E) are satisfied (relating to Medicaid enrollment, state approval, notice, no decline, and CMS approval).

units.obligation_text: An MA organization must obtain approval from CMS before implementing any default enrollment as described in this section. CMS may suspend or rescind approval when CMS determines the MA organization is not in compliance with the requirements of this section.
units.action_summary: MA organizations must obtain CMS approval for default enrollment; CMS may suspend or rescind approval for noncompliance.

units.obligation_text: The MA organization must provide notification that describes the costs and benefits of the MA plan and the process for accessing care under the plan and clearly explains the individual's ability to decline the enrollment, up to and including the day prior to the enrollment effective date, and either enroll in Original Medicare or choose another plan. Such notification must be provided to all individuals who qualify for default enrollment ... no fewer than 60 calendar days prior to the enrollment effective date.
units.action_summary: MA organization must provide a notice describing costs/benefits, access, and ability to decline, delivered at least 60 days before the enrollment effective date.

units.obligation_text: An MA plan offered by an MA organization must accept any individual ... who requests enrollment during his or her Initial Coverage Election Period and is enrolled in a health plan offered by the MA organization during the month immediately preceding the MA plan enrollment effective date, and who meets the eligibility requirements at § 422.50.
units.action_summary: MA plans must accept any eligible individual requesting enrollment during their Initial Coverage Election Period provided they meet eligibility and prior enrollment criteria.

units.obligation_text: An individual who requests seamless continuation of coverage as described in paragraph (d)(1) of this section may complete a simplified election, in a form and manner approved by CMS that meets the requirements in § 422.60(c)(1).
units.action_summary: Individuals requesting seamless continuation may use a simplified election in a CMS-approved form/manner.

units.obligation_text: An election made during an initial coverage election period ... If made prior to the month of entitlement ... it is effective as of the first day of the month of entitlement ... If made during or after the month of entitlement ... it is effective the first day of the calendar month following the month in which the election is made.
units.action_summary: Specifies when elections during initial coverage periods become effective depending on timing of election relative to entitlement.

units.obligation_text: MA regional plans are required to establish a catastrophic limit on beneficiary out-of-pocket expenditures for in-network benefits under the Medicare Fee-for-Service program ... that is no greater than the annual limit set by CMS using Medicare Fee-for-Service data.
units.action_summary: MA regional plans must set an in-network catastrophic out-of-pocket limit not greater than CMS's annual limit.

units.obligation_text: MA regional plans are required to establish a total catastrophic limit on beneficiary out-of-pocket expenditures for in-network and out-of-network benefits ... this total out-of-pocket catastrophic limit ... may not increase the limit described in paragraph (d)(2) of this section.
units.action_summary: MA regional plans must set a total catastrophic limit for all benefits and that total limit may not exceed the in-network annual limit set by CMS.

units.obligation_text: With respect to a local PPO plan, the limit specified under paragraph (f)(4) of this section applies only to use of network providers. Such local PPO plans must include a total catastrophic limit annually determined by CMS ...
units.action_summary: Local PPOs must include a total catastrophic limit (annually determined by CMS) with the network-use limit applying only to network providers.

units.obligation_text: Cost sharing for Medicare Part A and B services specified by CMS does not exceed levels annually determined by CMS to be discriminatory for such services.
units.actor: MA plans / plan sponsors (as to cost-sharing)
units.action_summary: Cost-sharing for Part A and B services must not exceed CMS-determined discriminatory thresholds.

units.obligation_text: MA organizations may offer enrollees a group of services as one optional supplemental benefit, offer services individually, or offer a combination of groups and individual services.
units.action_summary: MA organizations are permitted to package supplemental benefits in group or individual formats or both.

units.obligation_text: An MA organization must disclose the information specified in paragraph (b) of this section in the manner specified by CMS ... At the time of enrollment and at least annually thereafter, by the first day of the annual coordinated election period.
units.action_summary: MA organizations must disclose specified information in CMS-specified manner at enrollment and at least annually by a specified date.

units.obligation_text: Posting does not relieve the MA organization of its responsibility under paragraph (a) of this section to provide hard copies to enrollees upon request.
units.action_summary: MA organizations must provide hard copies of evidence of coverage/summary of benefits and network information upon enrollee request, even if posted online.

units.obligation_text: MA organizations are required to collect, analyze, and report data that permit measurement of health outcomes and other indices of quality.
units.action_summary: MA organizations must collect, analyze, and report quality and health outcomes data.

units.obligation_text: MA organizations must provide unbiased, accurate, and complete quality data that will still exist under a consolidation, and all of the beneficiaries enrolled in the consumed contract(s) are moved to the surviving contracts.
units.action_summary: MA organizations must supply unbiased, accurate, complete quality data that reflect enrollment post-consolidation.

units.obligation_text: For consolidations, CMS will determine QBP status of a contract using enrollment-weighted means of the surviving and consumed contracts for the first year after consolidation and will determine QBP/status in subsequent years based on the consolidated entity's Star Ratings displayed on Medicare Plan Finder.
units.action_summary: CMS will calculate QBP status for consolidated contracts using enrollment-weighted methods in year one and consolidated Star Ratings in later years.
