title: Display version 042718  Inpatient Rehabilitation Facility Prospective Payment system for Federal Fiscal Year 2019 (CMS-1688-P)

units.obligation_text: Requires physician supervision by a rehabilitation physician, defined as a licensed physician with specialized training and experience in inpatient rehabilitation.
units.action_summary: IRFs must ensure physician supervision by a rehabilitation physician (licensed physician with specialized training/experience in inpatient rehabilitation).

units.obligation_text: The requirement for medical supervision means that the rehabilitation physician must conduct face-to-face visits with the patient at least 3 days per week throughout the patient's stay in the IRF to assess the patient both medically and functionally, as well as to modify the course of treatment as needed to maximize the patient's capacity to benefit from the rehabilitation process.
units.action_summary: The rehabilitation physician must conduct face-to-face visits with the patient at least 3 days per week during the IRF stay to assess and modify treatment.

units.obligation_text: For CY 2010 through CY 2018, the update is the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (U.S. city average) as estimated by the Secretary for the 12-month period ending with the midpoint of the year involved.

units.obligation_text: For CY 2014 through CY 2018, the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers update determined under paragraph (a)(2)(ii) of this section is reduced by 2.0 percentage points for an ASC that fails to meet the standards for reporting of ASC quality measures as established by the Secretary for the corresponding calendar year.

units.obligation_text: For CY 2019 through CY 2023, the hospital inpatient market basket update determined under paragraph (a)(2)(iii) of this section is reduced by 2.0 percentage points for an ASC that fails to meet the standards for reporting of ASC quality measures as established by the Secretary for the corresponding calendar year.

units.obligation_text: For CY 2011 through CY 2018, the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers determined under paragraph (a)(2)(ii) of this section, after application of any reduction under paragraph (a)(2)(iv) of this section, is reduced by the productivity adjustment described in section 1886(b)(3)(B)(xi)(II) of the Act.

units.action_summary: CMS will not individually acknowledge or respond to the large number of public comments it receives.

title: Medicare Program: Changes to the Medicare Claims and Medicare Prescription Drug Coverage Determination Appeals Procedures

units.obligation_text: If CMS or a contractor elects to participate before receipt of a notice of hearing, or when a notice of hearing is not required, it must send written notice of its intent to participate to—
units.action_summary: Send written notice of intent to participate when electing to participate before receipt of a notice of hearing or when a notice is not required.

units.obligation_text: The assigned ALJ or attorney adjudicator, or a designee of the Chief ALJ if the request for hearing is not yet assigned to an ALJ or attorney adjudicator;
units.action_summary: Specify that written notice of intent to participate must be sent to the assigned ALJ or attorney adjudicator or designee.

units.obligation_text: The parties who were sent a copy of the notice of reconsideration or, for escalated requests for reconsideration, any party that filed a request for reconsideration or was found liable for the services at issue subsequent to the initial determination.
units.action_summary: Specify that written notice of intent to participate must be sent to the parties who received the notice of reconsideration or relevant parties in escalated requests.

units.obligation_text: If a hearing is scheduled, no later than 10 calendar days after receipt of the notice of hearing by the QIC or another contractor designated by CMS to receive the notice of hearing.
units.actor: CMS or a contractor (sending the notice of intent to participate)
units.action_summary: When a hearing is scheduled, send the written notice of intent to participate no later than 10 calendar days after the QIC or designated contractor receives the notice of hearing.

units.obligation_text: Unless the ALJ or attorney adjudicator grants additional time to submit the position paper or written testimony, a position paper or written testimony must be submitted within 14 calendar days of an election to participate if no hearing has been scheduled, or no later than 5 calendar days prior to the hearing if a hearing is scheduled.
units.action_summary: Submit position paper or written testimony within 14 days of electing to participate (if no hearing scheduled) or no later than 5 days before the hearing (if scheduled), unless additional time is granted.

units.obligation_text: The parties that are required to be sent a copy of the notice of intent to participate in accordance with paragraph (b)(1) of this section, if the position paper or written testimony is being submitted before receipt of a notice of hearing for the appeal;
units.actor: Parties submitting position paper or written testimony (recipient specification)
units.action_summary: When submitting position papers before receipt of a notice of hearing, send them to the parties required to be sent a copy of the notice of intent to participate under paragraph (b)(1).

units.obligation_text: A notice of hearing is sent to all parties that filed an appeal or participated in the reconsideration; any party who was found liable for the services at issue subsequent to the initial determination or may be found liable based on a review of the record; the QIC that issued the reconsideration or from which the request for reconsideration was escalated, or another contractor designated to receive the notice of hearing by CMS; and CMS or a contractor that elected to participate in the proceedings in accordance with § 405.1010(b) or that the ALJ believes would be beneficial to the hearing, advising them of the proposed time and place of the hearing.
units.actor: OMHA or the ALJ (entity sending the notice)
units.action_summary: Send a notice of hearing advising the proposed time and place to all listed parties and entities.

units.obligation_text: If the party’s objection to the place of the hearing includes a request for an in-person or VTC hearing, the objection and request are considered in paragraph (i) of this section.
units.action_summary: Consider objections that include requests for in-person or VTC hearings under paragraph (i).

units.obligation_text: The ALJ may grant the request, with the concurrence of the Chief ALJ or designee if the request was for an in-person hearing, upon a finding of good cause and will reschedule the hearing for a time and place when the party may appear in person or by VTC before the ALJ.
units.action_summary: The ALJ may grant a party's request for an in-person or VTC hearing (requiring Chief ALJ concurrence for in-person), and will reschedule the hearing upon finding good cause.

units.obligation_text: with the concurrence of the Chief ALJ or designee if the request was for an in-person hearing
units.action_summary: Concurrence of the Chief ALJ or designee is required when the ALJ grants an in-person hearing request.

units.obligation_text: upon a finding of good cause
units.action_summary: A finding of good cause by the ALJ is required to grant and reschedule the hearing for in-person requests (except where noted).

units.obligation_text: will reschedule the hearing for a time and place when the party may appear in person or by VTC before the ALJ.
units.action_summary: Reschedule the hearing to a time and place where the party can appear in person or by VTC.

units.obligation_text: Good cause is not required for a request for VTC hearing made by an unrepresented beneficiary who filed the request for hearing and objects to an ALJ’s offer to conduct a hearing by telephone.
units.actor: Unrepresented beneficiary (requesting party) / ALJ (treatment of request)
units.action_summary: Do not require a showing of good cause for a VTC hearing request made by an unrepresented beneficiary who objects to a telephone hearing.

units.obligation_text: Official copies of redeterminations and reconsiderations that were conducted on the appealed claims, and official copies of dismissals of a request for redetermination or reconsideration, can be provided only by CMS or its contractors.
units.actor: CMS or its contractors (exclusive providers of official copies)
units.action_summary: Only CMS or its contractors may provide official copies of certain adjudicative documents.

units.obligation_text: Prior to issuing a request for information to the QIC, OMHA will confirm whether an electronic copy of the redetermination, reconsideration, or dismissal is available in the official system of record, and if so will accept the electronic copy as an official copy.
units.action_summary: OMHA must check for an electronic copy in the official record before requesting information from the QIC and accept it as an official copy if available.

units.obligation_text: The ALJ dismisses a hearing request entirely or refuses to consider any one or more of the issues because a QIC, an ALJ or attorney adjudicator, or the Council has made a previous determination or decision under this subpart about the appellant’s rights on the same facts and on the same issue(s) or claim(s), and this previous determination or decision has become binding by either administrative or judicial action.
units.action_summary: Dismiss or refuse to consider hearing requests or issues when there is a previously binding determination on the same facts and issues.

units.obligation_text: An ALJ may conclude that an appellant has abandoned a request for hearing when OMHA attempts to schedule a hearing and is unable to contact the appellant after making reasonable efforts to do so.
units.action_summary: The ALJ may determine that an appellant has abandoned a hearing request if OMHA cannot contact the appellant after reasonable efforts.

units.obligation_text: OMHA mails or otherwise transmits a written notice of the dismissal of the hearing or review request to the appellant, all parties who were sent a copy of the request for hearing or review at their last known address, and to CMS or a CMS contractor that is a party to the proceedings on a request for hearing. The notice states that there is a right to request that the ALJ or attorney adjudicator vacate the dismissal action.
units.action_summary: OMHA must send written notice of dismissal to listed recipients and include that there is a right to request vacatur of the dismissal.

units.obligation_text: If good and sufficient cause is established, the ALJ or attorney adjudicator may vacate his or her dismissal of a request for hearing or review within 180 calendar days of the date of the notice of dismissal.
units.action_summary: The ALJ or attorney adjudicator may vacate a dismissal within 180 calendar days if good and sufficient cause is shown.

units.obligation_text: within 180 calendar days of the date of the notice of dismissal
units.action_summary: The vacatur may be performed within a 180-calendar-day timeframe from the dismissal notice date.

units.obligation_text: Consistent with § 405.1004(b), an ALJ or attorney adjudicator will remand a case to the appropriate QIC if the ALJ or attorney adjudicator determines that a QIC’s dismissal of a request for reconsideration was in error.
units.action_summary: Remand the case to the QIC when the ALJ/attorney adjudicator determines the QIC's dismissal was in error.

units.obligation_text: If an official copy of the notice of dismissal or case file cannot be obtained from the QIC, an ALJ or attorney adjudicator may also remand a request for review of a dismissal in accordance with the procedures in paragraph (a) of this section.
units.action_summary: If an official copy cannot be obtained from the QIC, the ALJ/attorney adjudicator may remand the request for review following paragraph (a) procedures.

units.obligation_text: OMHA mails or otherwise transmits a written notice of the remand of the request for hearing or request for review to the appellant, all of the parties who were sent a copy of the request at their last known address, and CMS or a contractor that elected to be a participant in the proceedings or party to the hearing. The notice states that there is a right to request that the Chief ALJ or a designee review the remand, unless the remand was issued under paragraph (d)(1) of this section.
units.action_summary: OMHA must transmit written notice of remand to listed recipients and state the right to request Chief ALJ review, except for remands under paragraph (d)(1).

units.obligation_text: Upon a request by a party or CMS or one of its contractors filed within 30 calendar days of receiving a notice of remand, the Chief ALJ or designee will review the remand, and if the remand is not authorized by this section, vacate the remand order. The determination on a request to review a remand order is binding and not subject to further review. The review of remand procedures provided for in this paragraph are not available for and do not apply to remands that are issued under paragraph (d)(1) of this section.
units.action_summary: Chief ALJ/designee will review remand upon timely request and vacate unauthorized remands; that determination is final; review procedures do not apply to remands under paragraph (d)(1).

units.obligation_text: For purposes of this section, the date of receipt of the ALJ’s or attorney adjudicator’s decision or dismissal is presumed to be 5 calendar days after the date of the notice of the decision or dismissal, unless there is evidence to the contrary.
units.action_summary: Presume date of receipt of decision or dismissal is 5 calendar days after the notice date unless contrary evidence exists.

units.obligation_text: An enrollee who is dissatisfied with the IRE reconsideration determination has a right to a hearing before an ALJ if— (2) An enrollee meets the amount in controversy requirements of § 423.2006.
units.action_summary: An enrollee has the right to an ALJ hearing if the enrollee meets the amount in controversy requirements.

units.obligation_text: To be entitled to a hearing before an ALJ, an enrollee must meet the amount in controversy requirements of this section.
units.action_summary: Enrollees must meet the section's amount in controversy requirements to be entitled to an ALJ hearing.

units.obligation_text: For ALJ hearing requests, the required amount remaining in controversy must be $100, increased by the percentage increase in the medical care component of the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (U.S. city average) as measured from July 2003 to the July preceding the current year involved.
units.action_summary: The minimum amount in controversy for ALJ hearings is $100 adjusted by the medical care CPI increase from July 2003 to the July before the current year.

units.obligation_text: If the figure in paragraph (a)(1) of this section is not a multiple of $10, it is rounded to the nearest multiple of $10. The Secretary will publish changes to the amount in controversy requirement in the Federal Register when necessary.
units.action_summary: Round non-multiples of $10 to the nearest $10; the Secretary will publish changes to the amount in controversy requirement when necessary.

units.obligation_text: To be entitled to judicial review, the enrollee must meet the amount in controversy requirements of this subpart at the time it requests judicial review. For review requests, the required amount remaining in controversy must be $1,000 or more, adjusted as specified in paragraphs (a)(1) and (2) of this section.
units.action_summary: Enrollees seeking judicial review must meet the amount-in-controversy requirement of $1,000 (adjusted as specified).

units.obligation_text: If the basis for the appeal is the refusal by the Part D plan sponsor to provide drug benefits, the projected value of those benefits is used to compute the amount remaining in controversy. The projected value of a Part D drug or drugs must include any costs the enrollee could incur based on the number of refills prescribed for the drug(s) in dispute during the plan year.
units.action_summary: When appeal basis is Part D plan refusal, use the projected value of benefits (including costs from prescribed refills) to compute amount in controversy.

units.obligation_text: If the basis for the appeal is an at-risk determination made under a drug management program in accordance with § 423.153(f), the projected value of the drugs subject to the drug management program is used to compute the amount remaining in controversy. The projected value of the drugs subject to the drug management program shall include the value of any refills prescribed for the drug(s) in dispute during the plan year.
units.action_summary: When appeal is based on an at-risk determination, compute amount in controversy using projected value of drugs including refills.

units.obligation_text: Two or more appeals may be aggregated by an enrollee to meet the amount in controversy for an ALJ hearing if—
units.action_summary: An enrollee may aggregate two or more appeals to meet the amount in controversy requirement for an ALJ hearing if specified conditions are met.

units.obligation_text: The appeals have previously been reconsidered by an IRE;
units.action_summary: Appeals to be aggregated must have been previously reconsidered by an IRE.

units.obligation_text: The enrollee requests aggregation at the same time the requests for hearing are filed, and the request for aggregation and requests for hearing are filed within 60 calendar days after receipt of the notice of reconsideration for each of the reconsiderations being appealed, unless the deadline to file one or more of the requests for hearing has been extended in accordance with § 423.2014(d);
units.action_summary: To aggregate appeals, the enrollee must request aggregation when filing for hearing and must file within 60 days of receiving each reconsideration notice, unless extended per §423.2014(d).

units.obligation_text: The appeals the enrollee seeks to aggregate involve the delivery of prescription drugs to a single enrollee, as determined by an ALJ or attorney adjudicator.
units.action_summary: Aggregated appeals must involve delivery of prescription drugs to a single enrollee as determined by an ALJ or attorney adjudicator.

units.obligation_text: Two or more appeals may be aggregated by multiple enrollees to meet the amount in controversy for an ALJ hearing if—
units.action_summary: Multiple enrollees may aggregate appeals to meet the amount in controversy if specified conditions are met.

units.obligation_text: The appeals have previously been reconsidered by an IRE;
units.action_summary: Appeals aggregated by multiple enrollees must have been previously reconsidered by an IRE.

units.obligation_text: The enrollees request aggregation at the same time the requests for hearing are filed, and the request for aggregation and requests for hearing are filed within 60 calendar days after receipt of the notice of reconsideration for each of the reconsiderations being appealed, unless the deadline to file one or more of the requests for hearing has been extended in accordance with § 423.2014(d);
units.action_summary: Multiple enrollees seeking aggregation must request it when filing for hearing and must file within 60 days of each reconsideration notice unless extended per §423.2014(d).

units.obligation_text: The appeals the enrollees seek to aggregate involve the same prescription drugs, as determined by an ALJ or attorney adjudicator.
units.actor: Multiple enrollees / ALJ or attorney adjudicator (determination)
units.action_summary: Aggregated appeals by multiple enrollees must involve the same prescription drugs as determined by an ALJ or attorney adjudicator.

units.obligation_text: If the request for hearing or review is not filed within 60 calendar days of receipt of the written IRE’s reconsideration or dismissal, an enrollee may request an extension for good cause.
units.action_summary: An enrollee may request a good-cause extension if they missed the 60-day filing deadline.

units.obligation_text: The request must be filed with the office specified in the notice of reconsideration or dismissal, must give the reasons why the request for a hearing or review was not filed within the stated time period, and must be filed with the request for hearing or request for review of an IRE dismissal, or upon notice that the request may be dismissed because it was not timely filed.
units.action_summary: When requesting an extension, file it with the specified office, state reasons for late filing, and file it with the hearing or review request (or upon notice of potential dismissal).

units.obligation_text: The ALJ sets the time and place for the hearing, and may change the time and place, if necessary.
units.action_summary: ALJ must set the hearing time and place and may change them if necessary.

units.obligation_text: and may change the time and place, if necessary.
units.action_summary: ALJ has discretion to change the hearing time and place when necessary.

units.obligation_text: If the enrollee’s objection to the place of the hearing includes a request for an in-person or video-teleconferencing hearing, the objection and request are considered in paragraph (i) of this section.
units.action_summary: Consider objections that include requests for in-person or video-teleconferencing hearings under paragraph (i).

units.obligation_text: The ALJ may grant the request, with the concurrence of the Chief ALJ or designee if the request was for an in-person hearing, upon a finding of good cause and will reschedule the hearing for a time and place when the enrollee may appear in person or by video-teleconference before the ALJ.
units.action_summary: ALJ may grant in-person or VTC hearing requests (requiring Chief ALJ concurrence for in-person), and will reschedule the hearing upon finding good cause.

units.obligation_text: Good cause is not required for a request for video-teleconferencing hearing made by an unrepresented enrollee who filed the request for hearing and objects to an ALJ’s offer to conduct a hearing by telephone.
units.action_summary: Do not require good cause for a VTC hearing request made by an unrepresented enrollee who objects to a telephone hearing.

units.obligation_text: Official copies of redeterminations and reconsiderations that were conducted on the appealed issues, and official copies of dismissals of a request for redetermination or reconsideration, can be provided only by CMS, the IRE, and/or the Part D plan sponsor.
units.actor: CMS, the IRE, and/or the Part D plan sponsor
units.action_summary: Only CMS, the IRE, and/or the Part D plan sponsor may provide official copies of certain adjudicative documents.

units.obligation_text: Prior to issuing a request for information to the IRE, OMHA will confirm whether an electronic copy of the missing redetermination, reconsideration, or dismissal is available in the official system of record, and if so will accept the electronic copy as an official copy.
units.action_summary: OMHA must check for an electronic copy in the official record before requesting information from the IRE and accept it as official if available.

units.obligation_text: If an ALJ or attorney adjudicator finds that the IRE issued a reconsideration and no redetermination was made with respect to the issue under appeal or the request for redetermination was dismissed, the reconsideration will be remanded to the IRE, or its successor, to readjudicate the request for reconsideration, unless the request for redetermination was forwarded to the IRE in accordance with § 423.590(c) or (e) without a redetermination having been conducted.
units.action_summary: Remand reconsiderations to the IRE for readjudication when no redetermination was made, unless the request was forwarded without redetermination.

units.obligation_text: Consistent with § 423.2004(b), an ALJ or attorney adjudicator will remand a case to the appropriate IRE if the ALJ or attorney adjudicator determines that an IRE’s dismissal of a request for reconsideration was in error.
units.action_summary: Remand cases to the IRE when the ALJ/attorney adjudicator determines the IRE's dismissal was erroneous.

units.obligation_text: OMHA mails or otherwise transmits a written notice of the remand of the request for hearing or request for review to the enrollee at his or her last known address, and CMS, the IRE, and/or the Part D plan sponsor if a request to be a participant was granted by the ALJ or attorney adjudicator. The notice states that there is a right to request that the Chief ALJ or a designee review the remand, unless the remand was issued under paragraph (d)(1) of this section.
units.action_summary: OMHA must notify the enrollee and relevant parties of remand and state the right to request Chief ALJ review, except for remands issued under paragraph (d)(1).

units.obligation_text: Upon a request by the enrollee or CMS, the IRE, or the Part D plan sponsor filed within 30 calendar days of receiving a notice of remand, the Chief ALJ or designee will review the remand, and if the remand is not authorized by this section, vacate the remand order. The determination on a request to review a remand order is binding and not subject to further review. The review of remand procedures provided for in this paragraph are not available for and do not apply to remands that are issued in paragraph (d)(1) of this section.
units.action_summary: Chief ALJ/designee will review remands upon timely request and vacate unauthorized remands; that determination is final; review procedures do not apply to remands under paragraph (d)(1).

units.obligation_text: An enrollee who is dissatisfied with an ALJ’s or attorney adjudicator’s decision or dismissal may request that the Council review the ALJ’s or attorney adjudicator’s decision or dismissal.
units.action_summary: An enrollee may request Council review of an ALJ's or attorney adjudicator's decision or dismissal if dissatisfied.

units.obligation_text: For purposes of this section, the date of receipt of the ALJ’s or attorney adjudicator’s decision or dismissal is presumed to be 5 calendar days after the date of the notice of the decision or dismissal, unless there is evidence to the contrary.
units.action_summary: Presume receipt of decision or dismissal is 5 calendar days after the notice date unless contrary evidence exists.

units.obligation_text: To the extent authorized by sections 1876(c)(5)(B) and 1860D–4(h) of the Act, an enrollee may obtain a court review of a Council decision if— (i) It is a final decision of the Secretary; and (ii) The amount in controversy meets the threshold requirements of § 423.2006.
units.action_summary: An enrollee may seek court review of a Council decision if it's a final Secretary decision and the amount in controversy meets the threshold.

units.obligation_text: To the extent authorized by sections 1876(c)(5)(B) and 1860D–4(h) of the Act, the enrollee may request judicial review of an ALJ’s or attorney adjudicator’s decision if— (i) The Council denied the enrollee’s request for review; and (ii) The amount in controversy meets the threshold requirements of § 423.2006.
units.action_summary: An enrollee may request judicial review of an ALJ's decision if the Council denied review and the amount in controversy meets the threshold.

units.obligation_text: Any civil action described in paragraph (a) of this section must be filed in the District Court of the United States for the judicial district in which the enrollee resides.
units.action_summary: File civil actions for judicial review in the U.S. District Court for the district where the enrollee resides.

title: Medicare and Medicaid Programs: Drug Pricing Transparency CMS-4187-P

units.obligation_text: Any advertisement for any prescription drug or biological product on television (including broadcast, cable, streaming, or satellite) must contain a textual statement indicating the current list price for a typical 30-day regimen or for a typical course of treatment, whichever is most appropriate, as determined on the first day of quarter during which the advertisement is being aired or otherwise broadcast, as follows: "The list price for a [30-day supply of] [typical course of treatment with] [name of prescription drug or biological product] is [insert list price]. If you have health insurance that covers drugs, your cost may be different."
units.actor: Advertisers of prescription drug or biological product television advertisements
units.action_summary: Require television advertisements to include a textual statement showing the current list price for a typical 30-day supply or course of treatment, using the specified wording and insurance disclaimer.

units.obligation_text: as determined on the first day of quarter during which the advertisement is being aired or otherwise broadcast
units.actor: Advertisers of prescription drug or biological product television advertisements
units.action_summary: The current list price must be the price as determined on the first day of the quarter when the ad is aired or broadcast.

units.obligation_text: Where the price is related to the "typical course of treatment" and that course of treatment varies depending on the indication for which a drug is prescribed, the list price to be used is the one for the "course of treatment" associated with the primary indication addressed in the advertisement.
units.actor: Advertisers of prescription drug or biological product television advertisements
units.action_summary: If typical course of treatment varies by indication, use the list price for the course associated with the primary indication in the ad.

units.obligation_text: The textual statement described in § 403.1202 shall be presented at the end of an advertisement in a legible manner
units.actor: Advertisers of prescription drug or biological product advertisements
units.action_summary: Require that the required textual list-price statement appear at the end of the advertisement and be legible.

units.obligation_text: meaning that it is placed appropriately
units.actor: Advertisers of prescription drug or biological product advertisements
units.action_summary: The statement must be placed appropriately within the ad.

units.obligation_text: and is presented against a contrasting background
units.actor: Advertisers of prescription drug or biological product advertisements
units.action_summary: The statement must be shown against a contrasting background.

units.obligation_text: for sufficient duration
units.actor: Advertisers of prescription drug or biological product advertisements
units.action_summary: The statement must be displayed for a sufficient amount of time to be read.

units.obligation_text: and in a size and style of font that allows the information to be read easily.
units.actor: Advertisers of prescription drug or biological product advertisements
units.action_summary: The statement must use font size and style that permit easy reading.
units.modal_raw: in a size and style ... that allows

units.obligation_text: The Secretary shall maintain a public list that will include the drugs and biological products identified by the Secretary to be advertised in violation of this subpart.
units.actor: The Secretary (Department of Health and Human Services / CMS)
units.action_summary: Require the Secretary to keep a public list of drugs and biological products identified as being advertised in violation of this subpart.

units.obligation_text: No State or political subdivision of any State may establish or continue in effect any requirement that depends in whole or in part on any pricing statement required by this subpart.
units.actor: States and political subdivisions of States
units.action_summary: Prohibits states and their subdivisions from creating or maintaining any requirement that relies in whole or in part on the pricing statement required by this subpart.

units.obligation_text: An advertisement for any prescription drug or biological product that has a list price, as defined in § 403.1201, less than $35 per month for a 30-day supply or typical course of treatment shall be exempt from the requirements of this subpart.
units.actor: Advertisements for prescription drugs or biological products with a list price less than $35 per month
units.action_summary: Provides an exemption: advertisements for products with list price under $35/month are exempt from the subpart's requirements.

title: Medicare Programs: International Pricing Index Model for Medicare Part B Drugs  (CMS-5528-ANPRM)

Medicare and Medicaid Programs: Medicare Advantage, Medicare Prescription Drug Benefit, Program of All-inclusive Care for the Elderly, Medicaid Fee-For-Service, and Medicaid Managed Care Programs for Years 2020 and 2021; Policy and Technical Changes CMS-4185-P

units.obligation_text: Such a plan must have a contract with the State Medicaid agency consistent with § 422.107 that meets the minimum requirements in § 422.107(c); and, beginning January 1, 2021, must satisfy one or more of the following criteria for the integration of Medicare and Medicaid benefits:
units.action_summary: The plan must have a contract with the State Medicaid agency meeting §422.107(c) and, beginning 1/1/2021, must satisfy one or more specified integration criteria.

units.obligation_text: (1) Meets the additional requirement specified in § 422.107(d) in its contract with the State Medicaid agency;
units.action_summary: One way to satisfy integration criteria is to meet the additional requirement of §422.107(d) in the State contract.

units.obligation_text: (2) Is a highly integrated dual eligible special needs plan;
units.action_summary: One way to satisfy integration criteria is to be a highly integrated D-SNP.

units.obligation_text: (3) Is a fully integrated dual eligible special needs plan.
units.action_summary: One way to satisfy integration criteria is to be a fully integrated D-SNP.

units.obligation_text: (1) That provides dual eligible individuals access to Medicare and Medicaid benefits under a single entity that holds both an MA contract with CMS and a Medicaid managed care organization contract under section 1903(m) of the Act with the applicable State;
units.actor: fully integrated dual eligible special needs plan
units.action_summary: The plan must provide access to Medicare and Medicaid benefits under a single entity that holds both MA and Medicaid managed care contracts.

units.obligation_text: (2) Whose capitated contract with the State Medicaid agency includes coverage of specified primary care, acute care, behavioral health, and long-term services and supports, consistent with State policy, and provides coverage of nursing facility services for a period of at least 180 days during the plan year;
units.actor: fully integrated dual eligible special needs plan
units.action_summary: The plan's capitated contract must include coverage of primary, acute, behavioral health, long-term services and supports, and at least 180 days of nursing facility services per plan year.

units.obligation_text: (3) That coordinates the delivery of covered Medicare and Medicaid services using aligned care management and specialty care network methods for high-risk beneficiaries;
units.actor: fully integrated dual eligible special needs plan
units.action_summary: The plan must coordinate Medicare and Medicaid services using aligned care management and specialty care networks for high-risk beneficiaries.

units.obligation_text: (4) That employs policies and procedures approved by CMS and the State to coordinate or integrate beneficiary communication materials, enrollment, communications, grievance and appeals, and quality improvement.
units.actor: fully integrated dual eligible special needs plan
units.action_summary: The plan must have CMS- and State-approved policies and procedures to coordinate communications, enrollment, grievances/appeals, and quality improvement.

units.obligation_text: Highly integrated dual eligible special needs plan means a dual eligible special needs plan offered by an MA organization that also has, or whose parent organization or another entity that is owned and controlled by its parent organization has, a capitated contract with the Medicaid agency in the State in which the dual eligible special needs plan operates that includes coverage of long-term services and supports, behavioral health services, or both, consistent with State policy.
units.actor: MA organization / D-SNP (for designation as highly integrated)
units.action_summary: To be a highly integrated D-SNP, the MA organization (or its parent/related entity) must have a capitated Medicaid contract that includes coverage of long-term services and supports, behavioral health, or both, per State policy.

units.obligation_text: Subject to CMS approval, fully integrated dual eligible special needs plans and highly integrated dual eligible special needs plans that meet minimum performance and quality-based standards may offer additional supplemental benefits, consistent with the requirements of this part, where CMS finds that the offering of such benefits could better integrate care for the dual eligible population provided that the special needs plan—
units.actor: fully integrated and highly integrated dual eligible special needs plans
units.action_summary: Such D-SNPs may offer additional supplemental benefits, subject to CMS approval and meeting minimum performance/quality standards and other requirements.

units.obligation_text: MA organizations seeking to offer a dual eligible special needs plan must have a contract consistent with this section with the State Medicaid agency.
units.actor: MA organizations seeking to offer a dual eligible special needs plan
units.action_summary: MA organizations must have a contract with the State Medicaid agency consistent with this section to offer a D‑SNP.

units.obligation_text: The MA organization’s responsibility to provide, as applicable, and coordinate the delivery of Medicaid benefits, including long-term services and supports and behavioral health services, for individuals who are eligible for such services.
units.action_summary: The contract must specify the MA organization's responsibility to provide and coordinate Medicaid benefits including LTSS and behavioral health for eligible individuals.

units.obligation_text: The category(ies) and criteria for eligibility for dual eligible individuals to be enrolled under the SNP, including as described in the Act at sections 1902(a), 1902(f), 1902(p), and 1905.
units.action_summary: The contract must include the categories and criteria for eligibility of dual eligible individuals for enrollment under the SNP.

units.obligation_text: The Medicaid benefits covered by the MA organization offering the SNP under a capitated contract with the State Medicaid agency or covered for the SNP’s enrollees under a risk contract as defined in § 438.2 of this chapter with a Medicaid managed care organization, as defined in section 1903(m) of the Act, offered by the SNP’s parent organization or another entity that is owned and controlled by its parent organization.
units.action_summary: The contract must specify which Medicaid benefits are covered by the MA organization under a capitated contract or via risk contract arrangements by affiliated managed care organizations.

units.obligation_text: For any dual eligible special needs plan that is not a fully integrated or highly integrated dual eligible special needs plan, the contract must also stipulate that, for the purpose of coordinating Medicare and Medicaid-covered services between settings of care, the SNP will notify or authorize another entity or entities to notify the State Medicaid agency and/or individuals or entities designated by the State Medicaid agency of hospital and skilled nursing facility admissions for at least one group of high-risk full-benefit dual eligible individuals, identified by the State Medicaid agency.
units.action_summary: For non-fully/highly integrated D‑SNPs, the contract must stipulate that the SNP will notify (or authorize others to notify) the State and designated entities of hospital and SNF admissions for at least one group of high‑risk full‑benefit dual eligibles.
units.modal_raw: must stipulate / will notify or authorize

units.obligation_text: The State Medicaid agency must establish the timeframe(s) and method(s) by which notice is provided.
units.action_summary: The State Medicaid agency must set the timeframes and methods for the required notices of admissions.

units.obligation_text: In the event that a SNP authorizes another entity or entities to perform this notification, the SNP must retain responsibility for complying with this requirement.
units.action_summary: If an SNP authorizes others to perform the notice, the SNP remains responsible for complying with the notification requirement.

units.obligation_text: MA organizations offering a dual eligible SNP must comply with paragraph (d) of this section beginning January 1, 2021.
units.actor: MA organizations offering a dual eligible SNP
units.action_summary: MA organizations offering D‑SNPs must comply with the paragraph (d) notification/stipulation requirements beginning 1/1/2021.

units.obligation_text: By a dual eligible special needs plan, prior to enrollment, for each prospective enrollee, a comprehensive written statement describing cost sharing protections and benefits that the individual is entitled to under title XVIII and the State Medicaid program under title XIX.
units.action_summary: Prior to enrollment, the D‑SNP must provide each prospective enrollee a comprehensive written statement describing cost‑sharing protections and Medicare and Medicaid benefits.

units.obligation_text: An MA plan may treat additional telehealth benefits as basic benefits covered under the original Medicare fee-for-service program for purposes of this part 422 provided that the requirements of this section are met.
units.action_summary: An MA plan may treat clinically appropriate additional telehealth services as basic Medicare Part B benefits for Part C purposes if it meets the section's requirements.

units.obligation_text: If the MA plan fails to comply with the requirements of this section, then the MA plan may not treat the benefits provided through electronic exchange as additional telehealth benefits, but may treat them as supplemental benefits as described in § 422.102, subject to CMS approval.
units.action_summary: If requirements are not met, the MA plan may not classify those electronic-exchange services as additional telehealth (basic) benefits, but may instead offer them as supplemental benefits subject to CMS approval.

units.obligation_text: An MA plan furnishing additional telehealth benefits must:
units.actor: MA plan furnishing additional telehealth benefits
units.action_summary: General obligation: MA plans that furnish additional telehealth benefits are subject to the following required actions.

units.obligation_text: (1) Furnish in-person access to the specified Part B service(s) at the election of the enrollee.
units.actor: MA plan furnishing additional telehealth benefits
units.action_summary: The plan must provide an in‑person option for the specified Part B services if the enrollee chooses.

units.obligation_text: (2) Advise each enrollee, at a minimum in the MA plan’s Evidence of Coverage required at § 422.111(b), that the enrollee may receive the specified Part B service(s) through an in-person visit or through electronic exchange.
units.actor: MA plan furnishing additional telehealth benefits
units.action_summary: The plan must inform enrollees in the Evidence of Coverage that services may be received in person or via electronic exchange.

units.obligation_text: (3) Identify, in the MA plan’s provider directory required at § 422.111(b)(3)(i), any providers offering services for additional telehealth benefits and in-person visits or offering services exclusively for additional telehealth benefits.
units.actor: MA plan furnishing additional telehealth benefits
units.action_summary: The plan must identify in its provider directory which providers offer additional telehealth services and whether they offer in-person or telehealth-only services.

units.obligation_text: (4) Comply with the provider selection and credentialing requirements provided in § 422.204, and, when providing additional telehealth benefits, ensure through its contract with the provider that the provider meet and comply with applicable state licensing requirements and other applicable laws for the state in which the enrollee is located and receiving the service.
units.actor: MA plan furnishing additional telehealth benefits
units.action_summary: The plan must follow §422.204 credentialing/selection rules and require providers to meet state licensing and other applicable laws where enrollee is located.

units.obligation_text: (5) Make information about coverage of additional telehealth benefits available to CMS upon request. Information may include, but is not limited to, statistics on use or cost, manner(s) or method of electronic exchange, evaluations of effectiveness, and demonstration of compliance with the requirements of this section.
units.actor: MA plan furnishing additional telehealth benefits
units.action_summary: The plan must provide CMS, upon request, information about coverage and use of additional telehealth benefits, including stats, methods, evaluations, and compliance evidence.

units.obligation_text: An MA plan furnishing additional telehealth benefits may only do so using contracted providers.
units.actor: MA plan furnishing additional telehealth benefits
units.action_summary: The plan may provide additional telehealth benefits as basic benefits only through contracted providers.

units.obligation_text: Coverage of benefits furnished by a non-contracted provider through electronic exchange may only be covered as a supplemental benefit.
units.action_summary: Benefits furnished via electronic exchange by non-contracted providers can only be covered as supplemental benefits (not as basic additional telehealth benefits).

units.obligation_text: An MA plan that fully complies with this section may include additional telehealth benefits in its bid for basic benefits in accordance with § 422.254.
units.action_summary: If the plan complies with §422.135, it may include additional telehealth benefits in its basic benefits bid per §422.254.

units.obligation_text: MA plans offering additional telehealth benefits may maintain different cost sharing for the specified Part B service(s) furnished through an in-person visit and the specified Part B service(s) furnished through electronic exchange.
units.actor: MA plans offering additional telehealth benefits
units.action_summary: Plans may set different cost sharing for services delivered in-person versus via electronic exchange.

units.obligation_text: CMS will exclude any measure that receives a measure-level Star Rating reduction for data integrity concerns for either the current or prior year from the improvement measure(s).
units.action_summary: CMS will exclude measures reduced for data integrity concerns from improvement measures.

units.obligation_text: CMS will reduce a measure rating to 1 star for the applicable appeals measure(s) if a contract fails to submit Timeliness Monitoring Project data for CMS’s review to ensure the completeness of the contract’s IRE data.
units.action_summary: If a contract fails to submit required Timeliness Monitoring Project data, CMS will reduce the applicable appeals measure rating to 1 star.

units.obligation_text: A request for CMS or the IRE to review a contract’s appeals data must be received no later than June 30 of the following year.
units.action_summary: Requests for CMS or IRE review of appeals data must be submitted by June 30 of the following year.

units.obligation_text: A request for CMS to review a contract’s Complaints Tracking Module (CTM) data must be received no later than June 30 of the following year.
units.action_summary: Requests for CMS review of CTM data must be received by June 30 of the following year.

units.obligation_text: In the event of extreme and uncontrollable circumstances that may negatively impact operational and clinical systems and contracts’ abilities to conduct surveys needed for accurate performance measurement, CMS will calculate the Star Ratings as specified in paragraphs (i)(2) through (10) of this section for each contract that is an affected contract during the performance period for the applicable measures.
units.action_summary: Under extreme circumstances affecting measurement, CMS will calculate Star Ratings according to the specified special procedures for affected contracts.

units.obligation_text: A contract, even if an affected contract, must administer the CAHPS survey unless exempt under paragraph (i)(2)(ii) of this section.
units.action_summary: Contracts must administer the CAHPS survey unless they qualify for an exemption as specified.

units.obligation_text: An affected contract will be exempt from administering the CAHPS survey if the contract completes both of the following: (A) Demonstrates to CMS that the required sample for the survey cannot be contacted because a substantial number of the contract’s enrollees are displaced due to the FEMA-designated disaster identified in paragraph (i)(1)(iii) of this section in the prior calendar year. (B) Requests and receives a CMS approved exception.
units.action_summary: An affected contract may be exempt from CAHPS administration if it demonstrates the required sample cannot be contacted due to disaster displacement and requests and receives a CMS-approved exception.
units.modal_raw: will be exempt if / demonstrates / requests

units.obligation_text: An affected contract with an exception defined in paragraph (i)(2)(ii) of this section will receive the contract’s CAHPS measure stars and corresponding measure scores from the prior year.
units.action_summary: Contracts granted the CAHPS exemption will receive their prior-year CAHPS measure stars and scores.

units.obligation_text: For an affected contract with at least 25 percent of enrollees in FEMA-designated Individual Assistance areas at the time of the extreme and uncontrollable circumstance, the contract will receive the higher of the previous year’s Star Rating or the current year’s Star Rating (and corresponding measure score) for each CAHPS measure.
units.action_summary: If at least 25% of enrollees were in FEMA IA areas at the time, the contract will be assigned the higher of prior- or current-year CAHPS measure ratings/scores.

units.obligation_text: An affected contract must administer the HOS survey unless exempt under paragraph (i)(3)(ii) of this section.
units.action_summary: Affected contracts must administer the HOS survey unless they qualify for the specified exemption.

units.obligation_text: An affected contract will be exempt from administering the HOS survey if the contract completes the following: (A) Demonstrates to CMS that the required sample for the survey cannot be contacted because a substantial number of the contract’s enrollees are displaced due to the FEMA-designated disaster identified in (i)(1)(iii) of this section during the measurement period. (B) Requests and receives a CMS approved exception.
units.action_summary: An affected contract is exempt from HOS survey administration if it demonstrates displaced enrollees prevent contact and it requests and obtains a CMS-approved exception.
units.modal_raw: will be exempt if / demonstrates / requests

units.obligation_text: Affected contracts with an exception defined in paragraph (i)(3)(ii) of this section will receive the prior year’s HOS and Healthcare Effectiveness Data and Information Set (HEDIS)-HOS measure stars and corresponding measure scores.
units.action_summary: Contracts with a HOS exemption will receive prior-year HOS and HEDIS-HOS measure stars and scores.

units.obligation_text: For an affected contract with at least 25 percent of enrollees in FEMA-designated Individual Assistance areas at the time of the extreme and uncontrollable circumstance, the affected contract will receive the higher of the previous year’s Star Rating or the current year’s Star Rating (and corresponding measure score) for each HOS and HEDIS–HOS measure.
units.action_summary: If at least 25% of enrollees were in FEMA IA areas, the affected contract will receive the higher of prior or current year ratings for HOS and HEDIS-HOS measures.

units.obligation_text: An affected contract must report HEDIS data unless exempted under paragraph (i)(4)(ii) of this section.
units.action_summary: Affected contracts must report HEDIS data unless they qualify for a specific exemption.

units.obligation_text: An affected contract will be exempt from reporting HEDIS data if the contract completes the following: (A) Demonstrates an inability to obtain both administrative and medical record data that are required for reporting HEDIS measures due to a FEMA-designated disaster in the prior calendar year. (B) Requests and receives a CMS approved exception.
units.action_summary: An affected contract may be exempt from HEDIS reporting if it demonstrates inability to obtain required data due to a FEMA disaster and it requests and receives a CMS exception.
units.modal_raw: will be exempt if / demonstrates / requests

units.obligation_text: Affected contracts with an exception defined in paragraph (i)(4)(ii) of this section will receive the prior year’s HEDIS measure stars and corresponding measure scores.
units.action_summary: Contracts granted the HEDIS reporting exemption will receive prior-year HEDIS measure stars and scores.

units.obligation_text: Affected contracts that do not have an exception defined in paragraph (i)(4)(ii) of this section may contact National Committee for Quality Assurance (NCQA) to request modifications to the samples for measures that require medical record review.
units.action_summary: Contracts without a HEDIS exemption may contact NCQA to request sample modifications for measures requiring medical record review.

units.obligation_text: For an affected contract with at least 25 percent of enrollees in FEMA-designated Individual Assistance areas at the time of the extreme and uncontrollable circumstance, the affected contract will receive the higher of the previous year’s Star Rating or the current year’s Star Rating (and corresponding measure score) for each HEDIS measure.
units.action_summary: If at least 25% of enrollees were in FEMA IA areas, affected contracts will receive the higher of prior or current year HEDIS measure ratings/scores.

units.obligation_text: For affected contracts with at least 25 percent of enrollees in a FEMA-designated Individual Assistance area at the time of the extreme and uncontrollable circumstance, CMS will apply a hold harmless provision by comparing the result of the contract’s summary and/or overall rating with and without including all of the applicable new measures. If the "with" result is lower than the "without" result, then CMS will use the "without" result as the final rating.
units.action_summary: CMS will apply a hold-harmless comparison for affected contracts with ≥25% enrollees in FEMA IA areas and use the higher ('without new measures') result if 'with' is lower.

units.obligation_text: For all other measures except those measures identified in this paragraph (i)(6)(ii) of this section, affected contracts with at least 25 percent of enrollees in a FEMA-designated Individual Assistance area at the time of the extreme and uncontrollable circumstance will receive the higher of the previous or current year’s measure Star Rating and then use the corresponding measure score.
units.action_summary: CMS will assign affected contracts (with ≥25% enrollees in FEMA IA areas) the higher of prior or current year measure star ratings for most measures and use corresponding scores.

units.obligation_text: CMS will not adjust the scores or Star Ratings for the following measures, unless the exception in paragraph (i)(6)(iii) of this section applies. (A) Part C Call Center—Foreign Language Interpreter and TTY Availability. (B) Part D Call Center—Foreign Language Interpreter and TTY Availability.
units.action_summary: CMS will not adjust scores or Star Ratings for specified call center measures, except in limited communications-exception circumstances.

units.obligation_text: CMS will adjust the measures listed in paragraph (i)(6)(ii) of this section using the adjustments listed in paragraph (i)(6)(i) of this section for contracts affected by extreme and uncontrollable circumstances where there are continuing communications issues related to loss of electricity and damage to infrastructure during the call center study.
units.action_summary: CMS will adjust the specified call center measures for contracts that have continuing communications issues (loss of electricity, infrastructure damage) during the call center study.

units.obligation_text: Any measure that reverts back to the data underlying the previous year’s Star Rating due to the adjustments made in paragraph (i) of this section will be excluded from both the count of measures and the applicable improvement measures for the current and next year’s Star Ratings for the affected contract.
units.action_summary: Measures that revert to prior-year data because of these adjustments will be excluded from measure counts and improvement calculations for current and following year.

units.obligation_text: For an affected contract that has missing data in the current or previous year, the final measure rating will come from the current year unless any of the exceptions described in paragraphs (i)(2)(ii), (i)(3)(ii), and (i)(4)(ii) of this section apply.
units.action_summary: If data are missing, CMS will use current year data for final measure ratings unless specified exemptions apply.

units.obligation_text: CMS will exclude the numeric values for affected contracts with 60 percent or more of their enrollees in the FEMA-designated Individual Assistance area at the time of the extreme and uncontrollable circumstance from the clustering algorithms described in paragraph (a)(2) of this section.
units.action_summary: CMS will exclude numeric values from clustering for affected contracts with ≥60% of enrollees in FEMA IA areas.

units.obligation_text: The cut points calculated as described in paragraph (i)(9)(i) of this section will be used to assess all affected contracts’ measure Star Ratings.
units.action_summary: Cut points computed excluding affected contracts' numeric values will be used to assess all affected contracts' measure Star Ratings.

units.obligation_text: CMS will exclude the numeric values for affected contracts with 60 percent or more of their enrollees in the FEMA-designated Individual Assistance area at the time of the extreme and uncontrollable circumstance from the determination of the performance summary and variance thresholds for the Reward Factor described in paragraph (f)(1) of this section.
units.action_summary: CMS will exclude numeric values for affected contracts (≥60% in FEMA IA areas) when determining performance summary and variance thresholds for the Reward Factor.

units.obligation_text: All affected contracts will be eligible for the Reward Factor based on the calculations described in paragraph (i)(10)(i) of this section.
units.action_summary: All affected contracts will be eligible for the Reward Factor based on the specified calculations.

units.obligation_text: Except as provided in paragraph (a)(1)(ii) of this section, an MA organization must not make payment for a health care item or service furnished by an individual or entity that is included on the preclusion list, defined in § 422.2.
units.action_summary: MA organizations are prohibited from making payments for items or services furnished by individuals or entities on the preclusion list, except as provided.

units.obligation_text: With respect to MA providers that have been added to an updated preclusion list, the MA organization must do all of the following:
units.action_summary: For providers newly added to an updated preclusion list, the MA organization must perform specified actions (see subitems).

units.obligation_text: (A) No later than 30 days after the posting of this updated preclusion list, must provide an advance written notice to any beneficiary who has received an MA service or item from the individual or entity added to the preclusion list in this update;
units.action_summary: Within 30 days of posting an updated preclusion list, the MA organization must provide advance written notice to beneficiaries who received services from newly added individuals/entities.

units.obligation_text: (B) Must ensure that reasonable efforts are made to notify the individual or entity described in paragraph (a)(1)(ii) of this section of a beneficiary who was sent a notice under paragraph (a)(1)(ii)(A) of this section;
units.action_summary: The MA organization must make reasonable efforts to notify the individual/entity that a beneficiary was sent the advance notice.

units.obligation_text: (C) Must not deny payment for a service or item furnished by the newly added individual or entity, solely on the ground that they have been included in the updated preclusion list, in the 60-day period after the date it sent the notice described in paragraph (a)(1)(ii)(A) of this section.
units.action_summary: The MA organization must not deny payment solely because a provider was newly added to the preclusion list during the 60-day period after sending the beneficiary notice.

units.obligation_text: CMS sends written notice to the individual or entity via letter of their inclusion on the preclusion list. The notice must contain the reason for the inclusion and inform the individual or entity of their appeal rights. An individual or entity may appeal their inclusion on the preclusion list, defined in § 422.2, in accordance with part 498 of this chapter.
units.action_summary: CMS must send written notice explaining reasons and appeal rights; the individual/entity may appeal inclusion under part 498.

units.obligation_text: The notice described in paragraph (a)(2)(i) of this section must also include notice of the revocation, the reason(s) for the revocation, and a description of the individual’s or entity’s appeal rights concerning the revocation.
units.action_summary: If preclusion is based on contemporaneous Medicare revocation, CMS must include revocation notice, reasons, and appeal rights in the notice.

units.obligation_text: The appeals of the individual’s or entity’s inclusion on the preclusion list and the individual’s or entity’s revocation shall be filed jointly by the individual or entity and, as applicable, considered jointly by CMS under part 498 of this chapter.
units.action_summary: Appeals of preclusion-list inclusion and Medicare revocation must be filed and considered jointly under part 498.

units.obligation_text: (A) If the individual or entity does not file a reconsideration request under § 498.5(n)(1) of this chapter, the individual or entity will be added to the preclusion list upon the expiration of the 60-day period in which the individual or entity may request a reconsideration;
units.action_summary: If no reconsideration request is filed, the individual/entity will be added to the preclusion list after the 60‑day reconsideration period expires.

units.obligation_text: (B) If the individual or entity files a reconsideration request under § 498.5(n)(1) of this chapter, the individual or entity will be added to the preclusion list effective on the date on which CMS, if applicable, denies the individual’s or entity’s reconsideration.
units.action_summary: If a reconsideration is filed, the individual/entity is added to the preclusion list when CMS denies the reconsideration (if applicable).

units.obligation_text: An OIG excluded individual or entity is added to the preclusion list effective on the date of the exclusion.
units.actor: CMS / OIG excluded individual or entity
units.action_summary: An individual/entity excluded by OIG is added to the CMS preclusion list effective on the OIG exclusion date.

units.obligation_text: Payment denials based upon an individual’s or entity’s inclusion on the preclusion list are not appealable by beneficiaries.
units.action_summary: Beneficiaries may not appeal payment denials that are based on a provider's inclusion on the preclusion list.

units.obligation_text: Except as provided in paragraphs (a)(5)(iii) and (iv) of this section, an individual or entity that is revoked under § 424.535 of this chapter will be included on the preclusion list for the same length of time as the individual’s or entity’s reenrollment bar.
units.action_summary: Individuals/entities revoked under §424.535 will be included on the preclusion list for the same duration as their reenrollment bar, subject to exceptions.

units.obligation_text: Except as provided in paragraphs (a)(5)(iii) and (iv) of this section, an individual or entity that is not enrolled in Medicare will be included on the preclusion list for the same length of time as the reenrollment bar that CMS could have imposed on the individual or entity had they been enrolled and then revoked.
units.action_summary: Individuals/entities not enrolled in Medicare will be included on the preclusion list for the same length as the reenrollment bar that could have been imposed had they been enrolled and revoked.

units.obligation_text: An individual or entity, regardless of whether they are or were enrolled in Medicare, that is included on the preclusion list because of a felony conviction will remain on the preclusion list for a 10-year period, beginning on the date of the felony conviction, unless CMS determines that a shorter length of time is warranted. Factors that CMS considers in making such a determination are: (A) The severity of the offense. (B) When the offense occurred. (C) Any other information that CMS deems relevant to its determination.
units.action_summary: Individuals/entities placed on the preclusion list for a felony conviction will remain for 10 years from the conviction date unless CMS determines a shorter period is appropriate, considering specified factors.

units.obligation_text: In cases where an individual or entity is excluded by the OIG, the individual or entity shall remain on the preclusion list until the expiration of the CMS-imposed preclusion list period or reinstatement by the OIG, whichever occurs later.
units.action_summary: If excluded by OIG, the individual/entity remains on the CMS preclusion list until either the CMS preclusion period expires or OIG reinstates them, whichever is later.

units.obligation_text: MA plans offering additional telehealth benefits as defined in § 422.135(a) must exclude any capital and infrastructure costs and investments relating to such benefits from their bid submission.
units.actor: MA plans offering additional telehealth benefits
units.action_summary: MA plans that offer additional telehealth benefits must exclude capital and infrastructure costs related to those benefits from their bid submissions.

units.obligation_text: The bid amount is for plan payments only but must be based on plan assumptions about the amount of revenue required from enrollee cost-sharing. The estimate of plan cost-sharing for the unadjusted MA statutory non-drug monthly bid amount for coverage of basic benefits as defined in § 422.100(c)(1) must reflect the requirement that the level of cost sharing MA plans charge to enrollees must be actuarially equivalent to the level of cost sharing (deductible, copayments, or coinsurance) charged to beneficiaries under the original Medicare fee-for-service program option.
units.action_summary: Bids must be based on plan assumptions about revenue from enrollee cost-sharing, and estimates must reflect that plan cost-sharing levels are actuarially equivalent to original Medicare fee-for-service cost-sharing.

units.obligation_text: The actuarially equivalent level of cost sharing reflected in a regional plan’s unadjusted MA statutory non-drug monthly bid amount does not include cost sharing for out-of-network Medicare benefits, as described at § 422.101(d).
units.action_summary: When reflecting actuarially equivalent cost sharing in regional plan bids, out‑of‑network Medicare benefit cost sharing is excluded.

units.obligation_text: MA organizations and their providers and practitioners will be required to submit a sample of medical records for the validation of risk adjustment data, as required by CMS.
units.actor: MA organizations and their providers and practitioners
units.action_summary: MA organizations and their providers/practitioners must submit medical record samples for validation of risk adjustment data upon CMS requirement.

units.obligation_text: There may be penalties for submission of false data.
units.action_summary: Submission of false data may result in penalties.

units.obligation_text: MA organizations must remit improper payments based on RADV audits and established in accordance with stated methodology, in a manner specified by CMS.
units.action_summary: MA organizations are required to remit improper payments identified by RADV audits using CMS-specified methodology and manner.

units.obligation_text: For RADV audits, CMS may extrapolate RADV Contract-Level audit findings to Payment Year 2011 forward.
units.action_summary: CMS may extrapolate RADV contract-level audit findings to payment years from 2011 onward.

units.obligation_text: In accordance with §§ 422.2 and 422.310(e), the Secretary annually conducts RADV audits to ensure risk adjusted payment integrity and accuracy.
units.action_summary: The Secretary conducts annual RADV audits to ensure risk-adjusted payment integrity and accuracy.

units.obligation_text: Recovery of improper payments from MA organizations will be conducted according to the Secretary’s payment error extrapolation and recovery methodologies.
units.action_summary: Recovery of improper payments will follow the Secretary's extrapolation and recovery methodologies.

units.obligation_text: CMS will apply extrapolation to plan year audits for payment year 2011 forward.
units.action_summary: CMS will apply extrapolation to plan-year RADV audits for payment years from 2011 forward.

units.obligation_text: The enrollee shall not have any financial liability for services or items furnished to the enrollee by an MA contracted individual or entit
units.action_summary: The enrollee must not bear financial liability for services/items furnished by an MA contracted individual or entity (text truncated in source).

title: Medicare and Medicaid Programs: Risk Adjustment Data Validation

units.obligation_text: the comment period for RADV provisions ... is extended to 5 p.m. on April 30, 2019
units.action_summary: CMS extends the public comment period for the RADV provisions until 5 p.m. on April 30, 2019.

units.obligation_text: The comment period for all other provisions of the November 1, 2018 proposed rule ends on December 31, 2018
units.action_summary: The comment period for all other provisions of the November 1, 2018 proposed rule ends on December 31, 2018.

units.obligation_text: Comments, including mass comment submissions, must be submitted in one of the following three ways (please choose only one of the ways listed)
units.action_summary: Commenters are required to submit comments by one of the specified methods and to choose only one method.

units.obligation_text: Because of staff and resource limitations, we cannot accept comments by facsimile (FAX) transmission
units.action_summary: CMS will not accept comments submitted by facsimile (FAX).

units.obligation_text: You may submit electronic comments on this regulation to http://www.regulations.gov. Follow the "Submit a comment" instructions
units.action_summary: Commenters are permitted to submit comments electronically via regulations.gov following that site's instructions.

units.obligation_text: You may mail written comments to the following address ONLY: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, Department of Health and Human Services, Attention: CMS-4185-P, P.O. Box 8013, Baltimore, MD 21244-8013
units.action_summary: Commenters are permitted to mail written comments to the specified P.O. Box address only.

units.obligation_text: You may send written comments to the following address ONLY: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, Department of Health and Human Services, Attention: CMS-4185-P, Mail Stop C4-26-05, 7500 Security Boulevard, Baltimore, MD 21244-1850
units.action_summary: Commenters are permitted to send written comments by express or overnight mail to the specified address only.

title: Medicare Program: Modernizing and Clarifying the Physician Self-Referral Regulations

units.obligation_text: Notwithstanding paragraph (g) of this section, a physician in the group practice may be paid a share of overall profits of the group that is indirectly related to the volume or value of the physician’s referrals.
units.actor: a physician in the group practice
units.action_summary: Physicians in a group practice are permitted to receive a share of group overall profits even if indirectly related to their referral volume or value.

units.obligation_text: Overall profits must be divided in a reasonable and verifiable manner.
units.actor: the group practice (or the entity dividing overall profits)
units.action_summary: Overall profits must be allocated in a manner that is reasonable and verifiable.

units.obligation_text: Overall profits are divided per capita (for example, per member of the group or per physician in the group).
units.action_summary: One permissible method is per-capita division of overall profits.

units.obligation_text: Overall profits derived from designated health services are distributed based on the distribution of the group’s revenues attributed to services that are not designated health services and would not be considered designated health services if they were payable by Medicare.
units.action_summary: Another permissible method ties distribution to revenues from non-DHS services.

units.obligation_text: Revenues derived from designated health services constitute less than 5 percent of the group’s total revenues, and the portion of those revenues distributed to each physician in the group constitutes 5 percent or less of his or her total compensation from the group.
units.actor: the group practice and its physicians
units.action_summary: A small-DHS-revenue threshold qualifies distributions as not relating to referrals.

units.obligation_text: Notwithstanding paragraph (g) of this section, a physician in the group may be paid a productivity bonus based on services that he or she has personally performed, or services "incident to" such personally performed services, that is indirectly related to the volume or value of the physician’s referrals (except that the bonus may directly relate to the volume or value of referrals by the physician if the referrals are for services "incident to" the physician’s personally performed services).
units.action_summary: Physicians may receive productivity bonuses that are indirectly related to referrals; bonuses for 'incident to' services may directly relate to referrals.

units.obligation_text: A productivity bonus must be calculated in a reasonable and verifiable manner.
units.actor: the group practice or entity calculating the bonus
units.action_summary: Productivity bonuses must be determined using reasonable, verifiable methods.

units.obligation_text: The productivity bonus is based on the physician’s total patient encounters or the relative value units (RVUs) personally performed by the physician.
units.action_summary: A permitted basis for bonuses is total patient encounters or physician RVUs.

units.obligation_text: The services on which the productivity bonus is based are not designated health services and would not be considered designated health services if they were payable by Medicare.
units.action_summary: Bonuses can be based on services that are not DHS.

units.obligation_text: Revenues derived from designated health services are less than 5 percent of the group’s total revenues, and the portion of those revenues distributed to each physician in the group constitutes 5 percent or less of his or her total compensation from the group.
units.actor: the group practice and its physicians
units.action_summary: A revenue-threshold condition qualifies bonuses as not relating to referrals.

units.obligation_text: Profits from designated health services that are directly attributable to a physician’s participation in a value-based enterprise, as defined in § 411.351, are distributed to the participating physician.
units.actor: the value-based enterprise or entity distributing profits
units.action_summary: Profits directly attributable to a physician's VBE participation are distributed to that physician.

units.obligation_text: Supporting documentation verifying the method used to calculate the profit share or productivity bonus under paragraphs (i)(1), (2), and (3) of this section, and the resulting amount of compensation, must be made available to the Secretary upon request.
units.actor: the group practice or entity that calculated the profit share or bonus
units.action_summary: Entities must provide supporting documentation of profit-share/bonus calculations to the Secretary on request.

units.obligation_text: Except as provided in paragraph (e) of this section, no Medicare payment may be made for a designated health service that is furnished pursuant to a prohibited referral.
units.action_summary: Medicare must not pay for DHS provided pursuant to a prohibited referral, except as allowed in paragraph (e).

units.obligation_text: Except as provided in this paragraph (c)(4) of this section, only the exceptions at §§ 411.355 and 411.357(p) are applicable to indirect compensation arrangements.
units.action_summary: Generally, only §§ 411.355 and 411.357(p) exceptions apply to indirect compensation arrangements, unless this paragraph provides otherwise.

units.obligation_text: When an unbroken chain described in paragraph (c)(2)(i) of this section includes a value-based arrangement to which the physician (or the physician organization in whose shoes the physician stands under this paragraph) is a direct party, only the exceptions at §§ 411.355, 411.357(p), and 411.357(aa) are applicable to the indirect compensation arrangement.
units.actor: indirect compensation arrangements that include a value-based arrangement
units.action_summary: If the chain includes a value-based arrangement to which the physician is a direct party, only the listed exceptions apply.

units.obligation_text: Unit-based compensation (including time-based or per-unit of service-based compensation) is deemed not to take into account the volume or value of referrals if the compensation is fair market value for items or services actually provided and does not vary during the course of the compensation arrangement in any manner that takes into account referrals.
