units.action_summary: Unit-based compensation will be treated as not taking referrals into account if it is FMV and does not vary based on referrals.

units.obligation_text: Unit-based compensation (including time-based or per-unit of service-based compensation) is deemed not to take into account other business generated between the parties or other business generated by the referring physician if the compensation is fair market value for items or services actually provided and does not vary during the course of the compensation arrangement in any manner that takes into account referrals or other business generated by the referring physician, including private pay health care business (except for services personally performed by the physician, which are not considered 'other business generated' by the physician).
units.action_summary: Unit-based compensation will be treated as not taking other business into account if FMV and not variable based on referrals or other business.

units.obligation_text: If a physician’s compensation under a bona fide employment relationship, personal service arrangement, or managed care contract is conditioned on the physician’s referrals to a particular provider, practitioner, or supplier, all of the following conditions must be met.
units.action_summary: When compensation is conditioned on referrals to a particular provider, a set of requirements must be satisfied.

units.obligation_text: The compensation, or a formula for determining the compensation, is set in advance for the duration of the arrangement. Any changes to the compensation (or the formula for determining the compensation) must be made prospectively.
units.actor: the parties to the compensation arrangement
units.action_summary: Compensation/formula must be set in advance and any changes must be prospective.

units.obligation_text: The compensation is consistent with the fair market value of the physician’s services.
units.actor: the parties to the compensation arrangement
units.action_summary: Compensation must be consistent with fair market value.

units.obligation_text: The compensation arrangement otherwise complies with an applicable exception at §§ 411.355 or 411.357.
units.action_summary: Arrangement must comply with an applicable exception at §411.355 or §411.357.

units.obligation_text: The requirement to make referrals to a particular provider, practitioner, or supplier is set out in writing and signed by the parties.
units.action_summary: Referral requirements must be documented in writing and signed by the parties.

units.obligation_text: The requirement to make referrals to a particular provider, practitioner, or supplier does not apply if the patient expresses a preference for a different provider, practitioner, or supplier; the patient’s insurer determines the provider, practitioner, or supplier; or the referral is not in the patient’s best medical interests in the physician’s judgment.
units.actor: the referral requirement / the parties to the arrangement
units.action_summary: Referral requirement is inapplicable when patient preference, insurer choice, or physician judgment (best medical interest) dictates otherwise.

units.obligation_text: The required referrals relate solely to the physician’s services covered by the scope of the employment, personal service arrangement, or managed care contract, and the referral requirement is reasonably necessary to effectuate the legitimate business purposes of the compensation arrangement. In no event may the physician be required to make referrals that relate to services that are not provided by the physician under the scope of his or her employment, personal service arrangement, or managed care contract.
units.actor: the parties to the arrangement / the physician
units.action_summary: Referral requirements must be limited to services within the physician's scope and be reasonably necessary for legitimate business purposes; physicians cannot be required to refer for out-of-scope services.

units.obligation_text: Compensation from an entity furnishing designated health services to a physician (or immediate family member of the physician) takes into account the volume or value of referrals only if—
units.actor: compensation from an entity furnishing DHS to a physician
units.action_summary: Defines the conditions under which such compensation is considered to take into account referral volume or value.

units.obligation_text: The formula used to calculate the physician’s (or immediate family member’s) compensation includes the physician’s referrals to the entity as a variable, resulting in an increase or decrease in the physician’s (or immediate family member’s) compensation that positively correlates with the number or value of the physician’s referrals to the entity.
units.actor: the formula / the entity setting compensation
units.action_summary: Compensation takes referrals into account if the formula uses referrals as a variable that positively correlates with compensation.

units.obligation_text: There is a predetermined, direct correlation between the physician’s prior referrals to the entity and the prospective rate of compensation to be paid over the entire duration of the arrangement for which the compensation is determined.
units.actor: the entity or parties to the arrangement
units.action_summary: Compensation takes referrals into account if there is a predetermined direct correlation between past referrals and future compensation rate.

units.obligation_text: Compensation from an entity furnishing designated health services to a physician (or immediate family member of the physician) takes into account the volume or value of other business generated only if—
units.actor: compensation from an entity furnishing DHS to a physician
units.action_summary: Defines conditions under which compensation is deemed to take into account other business generated.

units.obligation_text: The formula used to calculate the physician’s (or immediate family member’s) compensation includes other business generated by the physician for the entity as a variable, resulting in an increase or decrease in the physician’s (or immediate family member’s) compensation that positively correlates with the physician’s generation of other business for the entity.
units.actor: the formula / the entity setting compensation
units.action_summary: Compensation takes other business into account if the formula uses that business as a variable positively correlating with compensation.

units.obligation_text: There is a predetermined, direct correlation between the other business previously generated by the physician for the entity and the prospective rate of compensation to be paid over the entire duration of the arrangement for which the compensation is determined.
units.actor: the entity or parties to the arrangement
units.action_summary: Compensation takes other business into account if there is a predetermined direct correlation between past business and prospective compensation.

units.obligation_text: Compensation from a physician (or immediate family member of the physician) to an entity furnishing designated health services takes into account the volume or value of referrals only if—
units.actor: compensation from a physician to an entity furnishing DHS
units.action_summary: Specifies when physician-to-entity compensation is considered to take into account referrals.

units.obligation_text: The formula used to calculate the entity’s compensation includes the physician’s referrals to the entity as a variable, resulting in an increase or decrease in the entity’s compensation that negatively correlates with the number or value of the physician’s referrals to the entity.
units.actor: the formula / the entity receiving compensation
units.action_summary: Physician-to-entity compensation takes referrals into account if the formula uses referrals as a variable that negatively correlates with entity compensation.

units.obligation_text: There is a predetermined, direct correlation between the physician’s prior referrals to the entity and the prospective rate of compensation to be paid over the entire duration of the arrangement for which the compensation is determined.
units.actor: the entity or parties to the arrangement
units.action_summary: A predetermined direct correlation between past referrals and compensation rate causes the compensation to take referrals into account.

units.obligation_text: Compensation from a physician (or immediate family member of the physician) to an entity furnishing designated health services takes into account the volume or value of other business generated only if—
units.actor: compensation from a physician to an entity furnishing DHS
units.action_summary: Specifies when physician-to-entity compensation is considered to take into account other business generated.

units.obligation_text: The formula used to calculate the entity’s compensation includes other business generated by the physician for the entity as a variable, resulting in an increase or decrease in the entity’s compensation that negatively correlates with the physician’s generation of other business for the entity.
units.actor: the formula / the entity receiving compensation
units.action_summary: Entity compensation takes other business into account if the formula uses it as a variable negatively correlating with compensation.

units.obligation_text: There is a predetermined, direct correlation between the other business previously generated by the physician for the entity and the prospective rate of compensation to be paid over the entire duration of the arrangement for which the compensation is determined.
units.actor: the entity or parties to the arrangement
units.action_summary: A predetermined direct correlation between prior other business and compensation rate means compensation takes other business into account.

units.obligation_text: In the case of any requirement in this subpart for a compensation arrangement to be in writing and signed by the parties, the writing requirement or the signature requirement is satisfied if—
units.actor: the parties to the compensation arrangement
units.action_summary: Sets conditions under which a writing/signature requirement is considered satisfied for a compensation arrangement.

units.obligation_text: The compensation arrangement between the entity and the referring physician fully complies with an applicable exception in this subpart except with respect to the writing or signature requirement of the exception;
units.actor: the compensation arrangement and the parties
units.action_summary: If the arrangement otherwise complies with an applicable exception except for the writing/signature requirement, that requirement may be considered satisfied under this rule.

units.obligation_text: The parties obtain the required writing(s) or signature(s) within 90 consecutive calendar days immediately following the date on which the compensation arrangement became noncompliant with the requirements of the applicable exception.
units.actor: the parties to the compensation arrangement
units.action_summary: Parties must obtain the required writing/signatures within 90 days after noncompliance to satisfy the writing/signature requirement.

units.obligation_text: A coordinated care plan (within the meaning of section 1851(a)(2)(A) of the Act) offered by a Medicare Advantage organization in accordance with a contract with CMS under section 1857 of the Act and part 422 of this chapter.
units.action_summary: Coordinated care plans offered by Medicare Advantage organizations under the specified authorities qualify under this exception.

units.obligation_text: The total compensation paid by each academic medical center component is not determined in any manner that takes into account the volume or value of referrals or other business generated by the referring physician within the academic medical center.
units.action_summary: Academic medical center components' total compensation must not be determined based on referral volume or other business generated by the referring physician.

units.obligation_text: If any compensation paid to the referring physician is conditioned on the physician’s referrals to a particular provider, practitioner, or supplier, the arrangement satisfies the requirements of § 411.354(d)(4).
units.action_summary: Compensation conditioned on referrals must meet the requirements set out in §411.354(d)(4).

units.obligation_text: The space rented or leased does not exceed that which is reasonable and necessary for the legitimate business purposes of the lease arrangement and is used exclusively by the lessee when being used by the lessee (and is not shared with or used by the lessor or any person or entity related to the lessor).
units.action_summary: Leased space must be reasonable in size/necessity and exclusively used by the lessee when in use.

units.obligation_text: The lessee may make payments for the use of space consisting of common areas if the payments do not exceed the lessee’s pro rata share of expenses for the space based upon the ratio of the space used exclusively by the lessee to the total amount of space (other than common areas) occupied by all persons using the common areas.
units.action_summary: Lessee is permitted to pay for common-area use provided payments do not exceed the lessee's pro rata share of expenses.

units.obligation_text: The lessor (or any person or entity related to the lessor) may not be an invitee of the lessee to use the office space.
units.action_summary: Lessor and related parties are prohibited from being invitees of the lessee to use the leased office space.

units.obligation_text: The equipment leased does not exceed that which is reasonable and necessary for the legitimate business purposes of the lease arrangement and is used exclusively by the lessee when being used by the lessee (and is not shared with or used by the lessor or any person or entity related to the lessor).
units.action_summary: Leased equipment must be reasonable in amount/necessity and exclusively used by the lessee when in use.

units.obligation_text: The lessor (or any person or entity related to the lessor) may not be an invitee of the lessee to use the equipment.
units.action_summary: Lessor and related parties are prohibited from being invitees of the lessee to use the leased equipment.

units.obligation_text: Except as provided in paragraph (c)(4) of this section, is not determined in any manner that takes into account the volume or value of referrals by the referring physician.
units.actor: the amount of remuneration under the arrangement (or the arrangement itself)
units.action_summary: Remuneration must not be determined in a way that takes into account referrals by the referring physician, except as specified in (c)(4).

units.obligation_text: If remuneration to the physician is conditioned on the physician’s referrals to a particular provider, practitioner, or supplier, the arrangement satisfies the requirements of § 411.354(d)(4).
units.action_summary: Remuneration conditioned on physician referrals must meet the §411.354(d)(4) requirements.

units.obligation_text: The compensation to be paid over the term of each arrangement is set in advance, does not exceed fair market value, and, except in the case of a physician incentive plan (as defined in § 411.351), is not determined in any manner that takes into account the volume or value of referrals or other business generated between the parties.
units.action_summary: Compensation must be preset, not exceed FMV, and generally not be determined by referrals or other business (with a physician incentive plan exception).
units.modal_raw: is set / does not exceed / is not determined

units.obligation_text: If remuneration to the physician is conditioned on the physician’s referrals to a particular provider, practitioner, or supplier, the arrangement satisfies the requirements of § 411.354(d)(4).
units.action_summary: Remuneration conditioned on referrals must meet the requirements set in §411.354(d)(4).

units.obligation_text: In the case of a physician incentive plan (as defined at § 411.351) between a physician and an entity (or downstream contractor), the compensation may be determined in any manner (through a withhold, capitation, bonus, or otherwise) that takes into account the volume or value of referrals or other business generated between the parties, if the plan meets the following requirements:
units.actor: the physician incentive plan parties / the entity
units.action_summary: A physician incentive plan may base compensation on referral volume/value or other business if it meets the listed requirements.

units.obligation_text: If remuneration to the physician is conditioned on the physician’s referrals to a particular provider, practitioner, or supplier, the arrangement satisfies the requirements of § 411.354(d)(4).
units.action_summary: Physician incentive plans that condition remuneration on referrals must meet §411.354(d)(4).

units.obligation_text: The amount of remuneration under the arrangement is not determined in any manner that takes into account the volume or value of actual or anticipated referrals by the physician or other business generated between the parties;
units.actor: the party setting remuneration under the arrangement
units.action_summary: Remuneration amount must not be based on actual or anticipated referrals or other business generated between the parties.

units.obligation_text: The writing in paragraph (e)(1) of this section is also signed by the physician practice if the remuneration is provided indirectly to the physician through payments made to the physician practice and the physician practice does not pass directly through to the physician all of the remuneration from the hospital.
units.action_summary: If remuneration is passed indirectly through a physician practice that does not fully pass it through to the physician, the physician practice must also sign the writing.

units.obligation_text: The remuneration from the hospital under the arrangement is not determined in any manner that takes into account the volume or value of actual or anticipated referrals by the recruited physician or the physician practice (or any physician affiliated with the physician practice) receiving the direct payments from the hospital.
units.actor: the hospital (or the party determining remuneration)
units.action_summary: Hospital remuneration must not be determined based on referrals by the recruited physician or physician practice.

units.obligation_text: This paragraph (e) applies to remuneration provided by a federally qualified health center or a rural health clinic in the same manner as it applies to remuneration provided by a hospital.
units.action_summary: The rules in paragraph (e) apply equally to federally qualified health centers and rural health clinics as they do to hospitals.

units.obligation_text: The amount of remuneration under the isolated financial transaction is consistent with the fair market value of the isolated financial transaction;
units.actor: the parties to the isolated financial transaction
units.action_summary: Remuneration in an isolated financial transaction must be consistent with that transaction's fair market value.

units.obligation_text: The amount of remuneration under the isolated financial transaction is not determined in any manner that takes into account the volume or value of referrals by the referring physician or other business generated between the parties.
units.actor: the parties to the isolated financial transaction
units.action_summary: Isolated transaction remuneration must not be determined by physician referrals or other business generated between the parties.

units.obligation_text: There are no additional transactions between the parties for 6 months after the isolated financial transaction, except for transactions that are specifically excepted under the other provisions in §§ 411.355 through 411.357 and except for commercially reasonable post-closing adjustments that do not take into account the volume or value of referrals or other business generated by the referring physician.
units.actor: the parties to the isolated financial transaction
units.action_summary: No additional transactions between the parties are permitted for six months after an isolated financial transaction, except for specified exceptions and permitted adjustments that do not take referrals into account.

units.obligation_text: The remuneration is not determined in any manner that takes into account the volume or value of the physician’s referrals;
units.action_summary: Remuneration unrelated to DHS must not be determined by the physician's referral volume or value.

units.obligation_text: The remuneration is for an item or service that is not related to the provision of patient care services.
units.action_summary: Remuneration must be for items/services not related to patient care.

units.obligation_text: The compensation paid over the term of the agreement is consistent with fair market value, and the compensation per unit of service is fixed in advance and is not determined in any manner that takes into account the volume or value of referrals or other business generated between the parties.
units.action_summary: Compensation must be FMV, per-unit compensation fixed in advance, and not based on referrals or other business.
units.modal_raw: is consistent / is fixed / is not determined

units.obligation_text: If remuneration to the physician is conditioned on the physician’s referrals to a particular provider, practitioner, or supplier, the arrangement satisfies the requirements of § 411.354(d)(4).
units.action_summary: Remuneration conditioned on referrals must meet §411.354(d)(4)'s requirements.

units.obligation_text: To an entity as compensation for any other items or services that are furnished at a price that is consistent with fair market value;
units.action_summary: Compensation for other items/services must be furnished at prices consistent with FMV.
units.modal_raw: are furnished at a price that is consistent with

units.obligation_text: To an entity as compensation for any other items or services to which the exceptions in paragraphs (a) through (h) of this section are not applicable.
units.action_summary: This covers compensation for items/services not covered by the exceptions in paragraphs (a) through (h).

units.obligation_text: Compensation resulting from an arrangement between an entity and a physician (or an immediate family member) or any group of physicians for the provision of items or services or for the use of office space or equipment, if the arrangement meets the following conditions:
units.action_summary: Sets out conditions that an arrangement must meet to be considered fair market value compensation.

units.obligation_text: The arrangement is in writing, signed by the parties, and covers only identifiable items, services, office space, or equipment, all of which are specified in writing.
units.action_summary: Arrangement must be written, signed, and specify identifiable items/services/space/equipment.

units.obligation_text: The writing specifies the timeframe for the arrangement, which can be for any period of time and contain a termination clause, provided that the parties enter into only one arrangement for the same items, services, office space, or equipment during the course of a year. An arrangement may be renewed any number of times if the terms of the arrangement and the compensation for the same items, services, office space, or equipment do not change.
units.action_summary: Agreement must specify timeframe; only one arrangement per item per year unless renewed without changes.

units.obligation_text: The writing specifies the compensation that will be provided under the arrangement. The compensation must be set in advance, consistent with fair market value, and not determined in any manner that takes into account the volume or value of referrals or other business generated by the referring physician. Compensation for the rental of office space or equipment may not be determined using a formula based on—
units.action_summary: Compensation must be set in advance, be FMV, not reflect referrals or other generated business; rental compensation cannot be based on certain formulas.
units.modal_raw: must be / may not be determined

units.obligation_text: A percentage of the revenue raised, earned, billed, collected, or otherwise attributable to the services performed or business generated in the office space or to the services performed on or business generated through the use of the equipment;
units.action_summary: Rental compensation may not be calculated as a percentage of revenue generated in the space or via the equipment.

units.obligation_text: Per-unit of service rental charges, to the extent that such charges reflect services provided to patients referred by the lessor to the lessee.
units.action_summary: Rental compensation may not be per-unit charges to the extent they reflect services for patients referred by the lessor.

units.obligation_text: The arrangement is commercially reasonable (taking into account the nature and scope of the transaction).
units.action_summary: Arrangement must be commercially reasonable given nature and scope.

units.obligation_text: The services to be performed under the arrangement do not involve the counseling or promotion of a business arrangement or other act
units.actor: the parties to the arrangement / service providers
units.action_summary: Services under the arrangement must not involve counseling or promotion of business arrangements (text truncated in source).

title: Medicare Program: Release of Data Underlying Risk Adjustment Data Validation Provisions CMS-4185-N2

units.obligation_text: Persons or entities requesting the data must complete and submit a Limited Data Set (LDS) Data Use Agreement (DUA) along with the required fee to CMS.
units.actor: Persons or entities requesting the data
units.action_summary: Requesters must complete and submit an LDS Data Use Agreement and pay the required fee to CMS to obtain the data.

title: Medicare and Medicaid Programs: Risk Adjustment Data Validation

units.obligation_text: The comment period for the RADV provision of this proposed rule... is extended by 120 days until August 28, 2019.
units.action_summary: The RADV comment period is extended 120 days, now ending August 28, 2019 (5 p.m.).

units.obligation_text: This document also announces that CMS will be releasing additional data underlying the FFS Adjuster Study released October 26, 2018.
units.action_summary: CMS will release additional data underlying the October 26, 2018 FFS Adjuster Study.

units.obligation_text: Updates to existing documentation related to the study data, as well as additional data without Personally Identifiable Information, were posted on the CPI Private Plans Team website on April 25, 2019.
units.action_summary: CMS posted updates and additional non-PII data for the study on April 25, 2019.

units.obligation_text: Additional data containing Protected Health Information are being made available by CMS to all parties who have entered into an applicable data use agreement and to those parties who can request this information if they agree to enter into an applicable data use agreement.
units.action_summary: CMS will make PHI-containing data available to parties that have or will enter into an applicable data use agreement.

units.obligation_text: CMS expects to release that data by June 14th.
units.action_summary: CMS expects to release the PHI-containing additional data by June 14.

units.obligation_text: This will be the final release of data from the October 26, 2018 FFS Adjuster Study.
units.action_summary: CMS states this release will be the final data release from that study.

units.obligation_text: CMS intends to replicate that study, publish the results, and release associated data.
units.action_summary: CMS plans to replicate the FFS Adjuster Study, publish the replication results, and release the associated data.

title: Medicare and Medicaid Programs: Risk Adjustment Data Validation
Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments of 1988 (CLIA) Proficiency Testing Regulations Related to Analytes and Acceptable Performance

units.obligation_text: Peer group is a group of laboratories whose testing process utilizes similar instruments, methodologies, and/or reagent systems and is not to be assigned using the reagent lot number level.
units.actor: person or entity assigning peer groups (proficiency testing program)
units.action_summary: Peer groups must not be assigned based on reagent lot number level.

units.obligation_text: Target value for quantitative tests is: (1) If the peer group consists of 10 participants or greater:
units.action_summary: Defines when the following target value rules apply (peer group size ≥ 10).

units.obligation_text: (i) The mean of all participant responses after removal of outliers (that is, those responses greater than three standard deviations from the original mean, as applicable);
units.action_summary: For peer groups of ≥10, target value may be the mean of participant responses after removing outliers.

units.obligation_text: (ii) The mean established by a definitive method or reference methods; or
units.action_summary: For peer groups of ≥10, target value may be the mean established by a definitive or reference method.

units.obligation_text: (iii) The mean of a peer group, in instances when a definitive method or reference methods are not available;
units.action_summary: For peer groups of ≥10, when definitive methods aren't available, target value may be the mean of a peer group.

units.obligation_text: (iv) If the peer group consists of fewer than 10 participants, "target value" means the overall mean after outlier removal (as defined in paragraph (1) of this definition) unless acceptable scientific reasons are available to indicate that such an evaluation is not appropriate.
units.action_summary: For peer groups <10, target value normally is overall mean after outlier removal, unless acceptable scientific reasons justify otherwise.

units.obligation_text: If the laboratory also performs waived tests, compliance with § 493.801(a) and (b)(7) and subparts J, K, and M of this part is not applicable to the waived tests.
units.action_summary: Specified CLIA requirements do not apply to waived tests performed by the laboratory.

units.obligation_text: However, the laboratory must comply with the requirements in § 493.15(e), §§ 493.801(b)(1) through (6), 493.1771, 493.1773, and 493.1775.
units.action_summary: Laboratories performing waived tests must comply with the listed CLIA requirements.

units.obligation_text: If the laboratory also performs waived tests, compliance with §§ 493.801(a) and 493.801(b)(7) and subparts J, K, and M of this part are not applicable to the waived tests.
units.action_summary: Specified CLIA requirements do not apply to waived tests performed by the laboratory.

units.obligation_text: However, the laboratory must comply with the requirements in §§ 493.15(e), 493.801(b)(1) through (6), 493.1771, 493.1773, and 493.1775.
units.action_summary: Laboratories performing waived tests must comply with the listed CLIA requirements.

units.obligation_text: The laboratory must report PT results for microbiology organism identification to the highest level that it reports results on patient specimens.
units.action_summary: Laboratories must report PT organism identifications at the highest reporting level they use for patient specimens.

units.obligation_text: Require a minimum of ten laboratory participants before offering a proficiency testing analyte;
units.actor: proficiency testing program (as a criterion for approval)
units.action_summary: Programs must have at least ten laboratory participants before offering an analyte.

units.obligation_text: For those results submitted electronically, a mechanism to track changes to any result reported to the proficiency testing program and the reason for the change;
units.action_summary: PT programs must have a mechanism to track electronic result changes and reasons.

units.obligation_text: A process to resolve technical, administrative, and scientific problems about program operations;
units.action_summary: PT programs must have a process to resolve technical, administrative, and scientific operational problems.

units.obligation_text: A contractor performing administrative responsibilities as described in this section and § 493.903 must be a private nonprofit organization or a Federal or State agency, or an entity acting as a designated agent for the Federal or State agency.
units.action_summary: Contractors performing administrative responsibilities must be a private nonprofit, a Federal/State agency, or that agency's designated agent.

units.obligation_text: HHS may require on-site visits for all initial proficiency testing program applications for CMS approval and periodically or when problems are encountered for previously HHS-approved proficiency testing programs either during the reapproval process or as necessary to review and verify the policies and procedures represented in its application and other information, including, but not limited to, review and examination of documents and interviews of staff.
units.action_summary: HHS has authority to require on-site visits for initial applications, reapproval, or when problems arise.

units.obligation_text: HHS may require a proficiency testing program to reapply for approval using the process for initial applications if significant problems are encountered during the reapproval process.
units.action_summary: HHS may compel a PT program to reapply using the initial-application process if major problems occur during reapproval.

units.obligation_text: Not change submitted laboratory data and results for any proficiency testing event;
units.action_summary: PT programs must not alter laboratory-submitted data/results for PT events.

units.obligation_text: If a proficiency testing program is determined by HHS to fail to meet any criteria contained in §§ 493.901 through 493.959 for approval of the proficiency testing program, CMS will notify the program and the program must notify all laboratories enrolled of the nonapproval and the reasons for nonapproval within 30 days of the notification.
units.action_summary: CMS will notify unapproved programs; the program must notify its enrolled labs and reasons within 30 days.

units.obligation_text: CMS may disapprove any proficiency testing program that provides false or misleading information with respect to any information that is necessary to meet any criteria contained in §§ 493.901 through 493.959 for approval of the proficiency testing program.
units.action_summary: CMS may disapprove PT programs that provide false or misleading information relevant to approval criteria.

units.obligation_text: Any PT program that is dissatisfied with a determination to disapprove the program, as applicable, may request that CMS reconsider the determination, in accordance with subpart D of part 488 of this chapter.
units.action_summary: Disapproved PT programs may request CMS reconsideration following the specified appeal provisions.

units.obligation_text: To be approved for proficiency testing for bacteriology, the annual program must provide a minimum of five samples per testing event. There must be at least three testing events provided to the laboratory at approximately equal intervals per year.
units.action_summary: Bacteriology PT programs must provide ≥5 samples per event and at least 3 events per year at roughly equal intervals.

units.obligation_text: The samples may be provided to the laboratory through mailed shipments.
units.action_summary: PT program may use mailed shipments to provide samples.

units.obligation_text: The annual program must include, as applicable, samples for: (i) Gram stain including bacterial morphology; (ii) Direct bacterial antigen detection; (iii) Bacterial toxin detection; and, (iv) Detection and identification of bacteria which includes one of the following: (A) Detection of growth or no growth in culture media; (B) Identification of bacteria; and (v) Antimicrobial susceptibility or resistance testing.
units.action_summary: Bacteriology PT programs must include samples for listed test types (Gram stain, antigen detection, toxin detection, detection/identification, and antimicrobial susceptibility).

units.obligation_text: An approved program must furnish HHS and its agents with a description of samples that it plans to include in its annual program no later than 6 months before each calendar year.
units.action_summary: Approved PT programs must submit a description of planned annual samples to HHS at least 6 months before the calendar year.

units.obligation_text: At least 25 percent of the samples must be mixtures of the principal organism and appropriate normal flora.
units.action_summary: At least 25% of bacteriology PT samples must be mixed cultures of principal organism plus normal flora.

units.obligation_text: Samples that require laboratories to report only organisms that the testing laboratory considers to be a principal pathogen that is clearly responsible for a described illness (excluding immunocompromised patients). The program determines the reportable isolates, including antimicrobial susceptibility or resistance for any designated isolate;
units.action_summary: Program determines which isolates are reportable for samples where labs report only principal pathogen(s).

units.obligation_text: Samples that require laboratories to report all organisms present. Samples must contain multiple organisms frequently found in specimens where multiple isolates are clearly significant or where specimens are derived from immuno-compromised patients. The program determines the reportable isolates.
units.action_summary: Program must provide samples requiring labs to report all organisms present and program determines reportable isolates.

units.obligation_text: To determine the accuracy of each of the laboratory’s responses, the program must compare each response with the response which reflects agreement of either 80 percent or more of ten or more referee laboratories or 80 percent or more of all participating laboratories. Both methods must be attempted before the program can choose to not grade a PT sample.
units.action_summary: Programs must compare each lab response to a consensus defined by two alternative 80% rules, and must attempt both methods before choosing to not grade a PT sample.

units.obligation_text: A laboratory must identify the organisms to highest level that it performs these procedures on patient specimens.
units.action_summary: Labs must identify organisms in PT to the highest level they identify in patient testing.

units.obligation_text: For antimicrobial susceptibility or resistance testing, a laboratory must indicate which drugs are routinely included in its test panel when testing patient samples.
units.action_summary: Labs must state which antimicrobial drugs are routinely included in their patient test panels.

units.obligation_text: The score for a testing event in bacteriology is the average of the scores determined under paragraphs (b)(4) through (8) of this section based on the type of service offered by the laboratory.
units.action_summary: Bacteriology testing event score is determined as the average of the component scores described in paragraphs (b)(4)-(8).

units.obligation_text: To be approved for proficiency testing for mycobacteriology, the annual program must provide a minimum of five samples per testing event. There must be at least two testing events provided to the laboratory at approximately equal intervals per year.
units.action_summary: Mycobacteriology PT programs must provide ≥5 samples per event and at least 2 events per year.

units.obligation_text: An approved program must furnish HHS and its agents with a description of the samples it plans to include in its annual program no later than 6 months before each calendar year.
units.action_summary: Approved mycobacteriology PT programs must submit planned sample descriptions to HHS at least 6 months before the year.

units.obligation_text: The program must provide at least five samples per testing event that include challenges that are acid-fast and challenges which do not contain acid-fast organisms.
units.action_summary: Programs must include at least five samples per event that include both acid-fast and non–acid-fast challenges.

units.obligation_text: To determine the accuracy of each of the laboratory’s responses, the program must compare each response with the response that reflects agreement of either 80 percent or more of ten or more referee laboratories or 80 percent or more of all participating laboratories. Both methods must be attempted before the program can choose to not grade a PT sample.
units.action_summary: Mycobacteriology PT programs must use the specified 80% consensus rules and attempt both methods before choosing not to grade a sample.

units.obligation_text: To be approved for proficiency testing for mycology, the annual program must provide a minimum of five samples per testing event. There must be at least three testing events provided to the laboratory at approximately equal intervals per year.
units.action_summary: Mycology PT programs must provide ≥5 samples per event and at least 3 events per year.

units.obligation_text: An approved program must furnish HHS and its agents with a description of the samples it plans to include in its annual program no later than 6 months before each calendar year.
units.action_summary: Approved mycology PT programs must submit planned sample descriptions to HHS at least 6 months before the year.

units.obligation_text: For antifungal susceptibility or resistance testing, the program must provide at least two challenges per testing event that include fungi that have a predetermined pattern of susceptibility or resistance to the common antifungal agents.
units.action_summary: Programs must include at least two antifungal susceptibility challenges per testing event with predetermined patterns.

units.obligation_text: To determine the accuracy of a laboratory’s responses, the program must compare each response with the response reflects agreement of either 80 percent or more of ten or more referee laboratories or 80 percent or more of all participating laboratories. Both methods must be attempted before the program can choose to not grade a PT sample.
units.action_summary: Mycology PT programs must apply the 80% consensus rules and attempt both methods before not grading a sample.

units.obligation_text: To be approved for proficiency testing in parasitology, the annual program must provide a minimum of five samples per testing event. There must be at least three testing events provided to the laboratory at approximately equal intervals per year.
units.action_summary: Parasitology PT programs must provide ≥5 samples per event and at least 3 events per year.

units.obligation_text: An approved program must furnish HHS and its agents with a description of the samples it plans to include in its annual program no later than 6 months before each calendar year.
units.action_summary: Approved parasitology PT programs must submit planned sample descriptions to HHS at least 6 months before the year.

units.obligation_text: To determine the accuracy of a laboratory’s response, the program must compare each response with the response which reflects agreement of either 80 percent or more of ten or more referee laboratories or 80 percent or more of all participating laboratories. Both methods must be attempted before the program can choose to not grade a PT sample.
units.action_summary: Parasitology PT programs must use the 80% consensus rules and attempt both methods before choosing not to grade a sample.

units.obligation_text: To be approved for proficiency testing in virology, a program must provide a minimum of five samples per testing event. There must be at least three testing events at approximately equal intervals per year.
units.action_summary: Virology PT programs must provide ≥5 samples per event and at least 3 events per year.

units.obligation_text: An approved program must furnish HHS and its agents with a description of the samples it plans to include in its annual program no later than 6 months before each calendar year.
units.action_summary: Approved virology PT programs must submit planned sample descriptions to HHS at least 6 months before the year.

units.obligation_text: To determine the accuracy of a laboratory’s response, the program must compare each response with the response which reflects agreement of either 80 percent or more of ten or more referee laboratories or 80 percent or more of all participating laboratories. Both methods must be attempted before the program can choose to not grade a PT sample.
units.action_summary: Virology PT programs must apply the 80% consensus rules and attempt both methods before deciding not to grade a sample.

units.obligation_text: To be approved for proficiency testing in syphilis serology, a program must provide a minimum of five samples per testing event. There must be at least three testing events at approximately equal intervals per year.
units.action_summary: Syphilis serology PT programs must provide ≥5 samples per event and at least 3 events per year.

units.obligation_text: An annual program must include samples that cover the full range of reactivity from highly reactive to non-reactive.
units.action_summary: Syphilis PT programs must include samples covering the full reactivity range.

units.obligation_text: To determine the accuracy of a laboratory’s response for qualitative and quantitative syphilis tests, the program must compare the laboratory’s response with the response that reflects agreement of either 80 percent or more of ten or more referee laboratories or 80 percent or more of all participating laboratories. Both methods must be attempted before the program can choose to not grade a PT sample.
units.action_summary: Syphilis PT programs must use the two 80% consensus methods and attempt both before electing not to grade a sample.

title: Inpatient Rehabilitation Facility Prospective Payment System for Federal Fiscal Year 2020 and Updates to the IRF Quality Reporting Program CMS-1710-P Display Version

units.obligation_text: Requires physician supervision by a rehabilitation physician.
units.action_summary: The IRF must ensure physician supervision is provided by a rehabilitation physician.

units.obligation_text: The requirement for medical supervision means that the rehabilitation physician must conduct face-to-face visits with the patient at least 3 days per week throughout the patient’s stay in the IRF to assess the patient both medically and functionally, as well as to modify the course of treatment as needed to maximize the patient’s capacity to benefit from the rehabilitation process.
units.action_summary: The rehabilitation physician must conduct face-to-face visits at least 3 days per week throughout the patient's IRF stay to assess and modify treatment.

units.obligation_text: The post-admission physician evaluation described in paragraph (a)(4)(ii) of this section may count as one of the face-to-face visits.
units.action_summary: The post-admission physician evaluation is permitted to be counted as one of the required face-to-face visits.

units.obligation_text: It is conducted by a licensed or certified clinician(s) designated by a rehabilitation physician within the 48 hours immediately preceding the IRF admission.
units.actor: licensed or certified clinician(s) designated by a rehabilitation physician
units.action_summary: The preadmission screening must be conducted by a licensed/certified clinician designated by a rehabilitation physician within 48 hours before IRF admission.

units.obligation_text: A preadmission screening that includes all of the required elements, but that is conducted more than 48 hours immediately preceding the IRF admission, will be accepted as long as an update is conducted in person or by telephone to update the patient's medical and functional status within the 48 hours immediately preceding the IRF admission and is documented in the patient's medical record.
units.action_summary: CMS will accept a preadmission screening done more than 48 hours before admission only if an update is performed within 48 hours before admission and documented.

units.obligation_text: An update is conducted in person or by telephone to update the patient's medical and functional status within the 48 hours immediately preceding the IRF admission and is documented in the patient's medical record.
units.actor: licensed or certified clinician(s) designated by a rehabilitation physician / the IRF
units.action_summary: If preadmission screening was done >48 hours before admission, an in-person or telephone update of medical and functional status must be done within 48 hours before admission and documented in the medical record.

units.obligation_text: It is developed by a rehabilitation physician with input from the interdisciplinary team within 4 days of the patient's admission to the IRF.
units.action_summary: A required plan (or similar item) must be developed by a rehabilitation physician with interdisciplinary team input within 4 days of admission.

units.obligation_text: The team meetings are led by a rehabilitation physician and further consist of a registered nurse with specialized training or experience in rehabilitation; a social worker or case manager (or both); and a licensed or certified therapist from each therapy discipline involved in treating the patient.
units.action_summary: Interdisciplinary team meetings must be led by a rehabilitation physician and must include specified team members (specialized RN, social worker or case manager, and a licensed/certified therapist from each therapy discipline treating the patient).

units.obligation_text: All team members must have current knowledge of the patient's medical and functional status.
units.action_summary: Every team member must maintain current knowledge of the patient's medical and functional status.

units.obligation_text: The rehabilitation physician may lead the interdisciplinary team meeting remotely via a mode of communication such as video or telephone conferencing.
units.action_summary: The rehabilitation physician is permitted to lead the interdisciplinary team meeting remotely (e.g., by video or telephone).

units.obligation_text: For the FY 2018 payment determination and subsequent years, an IRF must begin reporting data under the IRF QRP requirements no later than the first day of the calendar quarter subsequent to 30 days after the date on its CMS Certification Number (CCN) notification letter, which designates the IRF as operating in the CMS designated data submission system.
units.action_summary: IRFs must begin reporting IRF QRP data by the first day of the calendar quarter following 30 days after the CCN notification date (for FY2018 and later).

units.obligation_text: IRFs that do not meet the requirement in paragraph (b) of this section for a program year will receive a written notification of non-compliance through at least one of the following methods: the CMS designated data submission system, the United States Postal Service, or via an email from the Medicare Administrative Contractor (MAC).
units.action_summary: CMS will provide written notification of non-compliance to IRFs that fail to meet paragraph (b) requirements, using at least one listed method (data system, USPS, or MAC email).

units.obligation_text: CMS will notify IRFs, in writing, of its final decision regarding any reconsideration request through at least one of the following methods: the CMS designated data submission system, the United States Postal Service, or via an email from the Medicare Administrative Contractor (MAC).
units.action_summary: CMS will notify IRFs in writing of its final decision on any reconsideration request using at least one of the specified methods.

units.obligation_text: IRFs must meet or exceed two separate data completeness thresholds:
units.action_summary: IRFs are required to meet or exceed two specified data completeness thresholds.

units.obligation_text: One threshold set at 95 percent for completion of required quality measures data and standardized patient assessment data collected using the IRF-PAI submitted through the CMS designated data submission system;
units.action_summary: IRFs must achieve at least 95% completeness for required quality measures and standardized patient assessment data submitted via the IRF-PAI through the CMS data submission system.

units.obligation_text: a second threshold set at 100 percent for measures data collected and submitted using the CDC NHSN.
units.action_summary: IRFs must achieve 100% completeness for measures data collected and submitted using the CDC NHSN.

units.obligation_text: In accordance with the general regulations in this part, the regulated area shall be closed immediately prior to, during and immediately after the event to all persons and vessels not participating in the event and authorized by the event sponsor.
units.actor: persons and vessels not participating in the event and not authorized by the event sponsor
units.action_summary: Prohibit persons and vessels not participating in the event and not authorized by the event sponsor from being in the regulated area immediately before, during, and immediately after the event.

units.obligation_text: All persons or vessels who desire to enter the designated area created in this section while it is enforced must obtain permission from the on-scene patrol craft on VHF Ch 9.
units.actor: persons or vessels who desire to enter the designated area while it is enforced
units.action_summary: Require entrants to obtain permission from the on-scene patrol craft on VHF Channel 9 before entering the designated area while enforced.

title: FY 2020 Inpatient Psychiatric Facilities Prospective Payment System - Rate Update CMS-1712-P Display

units.obligation_text: IPFs must include a valid procedure code for ECT services provided to IPF beneficiaries in order to bill for ECT services, as described in our Medicare Claims Processing Manual, Chapter 3, Section 190.7.3.
units.action_summary: IPFs are required to include a valid ECT procedure code on claims to bill for ECT services.

units.obligation_text: In accordance with the ICD–10–CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting, when a primary (psychiatric) diagnosis code has a 'code first' note, the provider would follow the instructions in the ICD–10–CM text.
units.action_summary: When a primary diagnosis has a 'code first' note, providers must follow the ICD-10-CM instructions for sequencing (etiology first, manifestation second).

units.obligation_text: Diagnoses that relate to an earlier episode of care and have no bearing on the current hospital stay are excluded and must not be reported on IPF claims.
units.action_summary: Do not report diagnoses on IPF claims that relate only to prior episodes and do not affect the current stay.

units.obligation_text: For each claim, an IPF may receive only one comorbidity adjustment within a comorbidity category.
units.action_summary: An IPF's claim can receive at most one comorbidity adjustment from any single comorbidity category.

units.obligation_text: An IPF may receive an adjustment for more than one comorbidity category.
units.action_summary: A claim may receive comorbidity adjustments from multiple different comorbidity categories.

units.obligation_text: Current billing instructions for discharge claims, on or after October 1, 2015, require IPFs to enter the complete ICD-10-CM codes for up to 24 additional diagnoses if they co-exist at the time of admission, or develop subsequently and impact the treatment provided.
units.action_summary: On discharge claims (on/after Oct 1, 2015), IPFs must record up to 24 additional complete ICD-10-CM diagnosis codes that coexist at admission or develop later and affect treatment.

units.obligation_text: Comorbid conditions must exist at the time of admission or develop subsequently, and affect the treatment received, length of stay (LOS), or both treatment and LOS.
units.action_summary: To qualify for a comorbidity adjustment, the comorbid condition must be present at admission or arise during the stay and must affect treatment or length of stay.

units.obligation_text: We established variable per diem adjustments that begin on day 1 and decline gradually until day 21 of a patient's stay.
units.action_summary: The payment system applies higher per-diem adjustments early in the stay that decline through day 21.

units.obligation_text: If an IPF has a qualifying ED, it receives a 1.31 adjustment factor for day 1 of each stay.
units.action_summary: IPFs with a qualifying ED get a 1.31 multiplier applied to day 1 per diem.

units.obligation_text: If an IPF does not have a qualifying ED, it receives a 1.19 adjustment factor for day 1 of the stay.
units.action_summary: IPFs without a qualifying ED get a 1.19 multiplier applied to day 1 per diem.

units.obligation_text: Section 1886(s)(4)(A)(i) of the Act requires that for RY 2014 and each subsequent RY, in the case of an IPF that fails to report required quality data with respect to such rate year, the Secretary shall reduce any annual update to a standard federal rate for discharges during the RY by 2.0 percentage points.
units.action_summary: If an IPF fails to report required quality data for a rate year, the Secretary must reduce any annual update to the federal rate for that year's discharges by 2 percentage points.

units.obligation_text: For IPFs that fail requirements under the Inpatient Psychiatric Facilities Quality Reporting (IPFQR) Program, we applied a -0.15 percent payment rate update ... and the wage index budget-neutrality factor of 1.0078 to the FY 2019 federal per diem base rate of $782.78, yielding a federal per diem base rate of $787.70 for FY 2020.
units.action_summary: CMS reduced the annual update and applied the budget-neutrality factor to produce a reduced federal per diem base rate for IPFs failing IPFQR requirements.

units.obligation_text: For IPFs that fail to meet requirements under the IPFQR Program, we applied the -0.15 percent annual payment rate update and the 1.0078 wage index budget-neutrality factor to the FY 2019 ECT payment per treatment of $337.00, yielding an ECT payment per treatment of $339.12 for FY 2020.
units.action_summary: CMS applied the reduced update and budget-neutrality factor to the ECT per-treatment payment for IPFs failing IPFQR requirements.

units.obligation_text: Psychiatric principal diagnoses that do not group to one of the 17 designated MS-DRGs will still receive the federal per diem base rate and all other applicable adjustments, but the payment will not include an MS-DRG adjustment.
units.action_summary: If a psychiatric principal diagnosis does not map to one of the 17 MS-DRGs, the claim gets the federal per diem and other applicable adjustments but no MS-DRG adjustment.

units.obligation_text: Our wage index policy was put into regulation at 42 CFR 412.424(a)(2), and requires us to use the best Medicare data available to estimate costs per day, including an appropriate wage index to adjust for wage differences.
units.action_summary: CMS must use the best available Medicare data and an appropriate wage index to estimate per-day costs and adjust for wage differences.

units.obligation_text: The submitted claim goes through the CMS processing system, which will identify the primary diagnosis code as non-psychiatric and search the secondary codes for a psychiatric code to assign a DRG code for adjustment.
units.action_summary: The CMS claims processing system will treat primary non-psychiatric code with a 'code first' situation by finding secondary psychiatric codes for DRG assignment and comorbidity adjustments.

title: Medicare Program: Fiscal Year 2020 Inpatient Psychiatric Facilities Prospective Payment System and Quality Reporting Updates for Fiscal Year Beginning October 1, 2019

units.obligation_text: IPFs must include a valid procedure code for ECT services provided to IPF beneficiaries in order to bill for ECT services, as described in our Medicare Claims Processing Manual, Chapter 3, Section 190.7.3.

units.obligation_text: Section 1886(s)(4)(A)(i) of the Act requires that for RY 2014 and each subsequent RY, in the case of an IPF that fails to report required quality data with respect to such rate year, the Secretary shall reduce any annual update to a standard federal rate for discharges during the RY by 2.0 percentage points.
units.action_summary: If an IPF fails to report required quality data for a rate year, the Secretary must reduce that year's annual update to the federal rate by 2 percentage points.

units.obligation_text: Diagnoses that relate to an earlier episode of care and have no bearing on the current hospital stay are excluded and must not be reported on IPF claims.
units.action_summary: Do not report diagnoses on IPF claims that relate to an earlier episode of care and have no bearing on the current stay.

units.obligation_text: Comorbid conditions must exist at the time of admission or develop subsequently, and affect the treatment received, length of stay (LOS), or both treatment and LOS.
units.action_summary: To qualify as a comorbidity for IPF PPS adjustments, a condition must be present at admission or develop thereafter and must affect treatment or length of stay.

units.obligation_text: For each claim, an IPF may receive only one comorbidity adjustment within a comorbidity category, but it may receive an adjustment for more than one comorbidity category.
units.action_summary: Per claim, IPFs are limited to one comorbidity adjustment per comorbidity category but may receive adjustments for multiple different comorbidity categories.

units.obligation_text: For each claim, an IPF may receive only one comorbidity adjustment within a comorbidity category.
units.action_summary: An IPF can receive at most one comorbidity adjustment from any single comorbidity category for a claim.

units.obligation_text: For each claim, an IPF may receive an adjustment for more than one comorbidity category.
units.action_summary: An IPF may receive comorbidity adjustments from multiple different comorbidity categories on the same claim.

units.obligation_text: Current billing instructions for discharge claims, on or after October 1, 2015, require IPFs to enter the complete ICD–10–CM codes for up to 24 additional diagnoses if they co-exist at the time of admission, or develop subsequently and impact the treatment provided.
units.action_summary: For discharge claims on/after Oct 1, 2015, IPFs must record up to 24 complete ICD-10-CM additional diagnosis codes that co-exist at admission or develop later and affect treatment.

units.obligation_text: For such conditions, the ICD–10–CM has a coding convention that requires the underlying condition be sequenced first followed by the manifestation.
units.action_summary: When a condition has an underlying etiology and manifestations, coders must sequence the underlying condition first, then the manifestation per ICD-10-CM convention.

units.obligation_text: In accordance with the ICD–10–CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting, when a primary (psychiatric) diagnosis code has a 'code first' note, the provider would follow the instructions in the ICD–10–CM text.
units.action_summary: When a primary diagnosis code carries a 'code first' note, providers must follow the sequencing/instruction guidance in the ICD-10-CM guidelines.

units.obligation_text: In accordance with the methodology described in §413.337(c) related to the adjustment of the Federal rates for case-mix, SNFs must submit assessments according to an assessment schedule.
units.action_summary: SNFs are required to submit resident assessments according to an assessment schedule.

units.obligation_text: This schedule must include performance of an initial patient assessment no later than the 8th day of posthospital SNF care
units.action_summary: The assessment schedule must include an initial patient assessment by the 8th day of posthospital SNF care.

units.obligation_text: and such other interim payment assessments as the SNF determines are necessary to account for changes in patient care needs.
units.action_summary: SNFs may perform additional interim payment assessments as they determine necessary to account for changes in patient care needs.

units.obligation_text: Beginning with the FY 2018 program year, a SNF must begin reporting data in accordance with paragraph (b) of this section no later than the first day of the calendar quarter subsequent to 30 days after the date on its CMS Certification Number (CCN) notification letter, which designates the SNF as operating in the CMS designated data submission system.
units.action_summary: SNFs must begin reporting required data (per paragraph (b)) by the first day of the calendar quarter that is at least 30 days after their CCN notification letter.

units.obligation_text: For purposes of this section, a program year is the fiscal year in which the market basket percentage described in §413.337(d) is reduced by two percentage points if the SNF does not report data in accordance with paragraph (b) of this section.
units.action_summary: If a SNF does not report data per paragraph (b), the market basket percentage will be reduced by two percentage points in that fiscal year.

units.obligation_text: SNFs that do not meet the requirements in paragraph (b) of this section for a program year will receive a notification of non-compliance sent through at least one of the following methods: the CMS designated data submission system, the United States Postal Service, or via an email from the Medicare Administrative Contractor (MAC).
units.action_summary: CMS or its MAC will send a notification of non-compliance to SNFs that fail to meet paragraph (b) requirements, using at least one specified method.

units.obligation_text: A SNF may request reconsideration no later than 30 calendar days after the date identified on the letter of non-compliance.
units.action_summary: A SNF has the option to request reconsideration within 30 calendar days after the non-compliance letter date.

units.obligation_text: CMS will notify SNFs, in writing, of its final decision regarding any reconsideration request through at least one of the following methods: CMS designated data submission system, the United States Postal Service, or via email from the CMS Medicare Administrative Contractor (MAC).
units.action_summary: CMS is required to provide written notice to SNFs of its final decision on any reconsideration request using at least one specified method.
