units.action_summary: Provide a written acknowledgement to CMS containing the following specified statements.

units.obligation_text: If the application for the transfer of the existing CMS-approval for the accreditation program(s) to be transferred in the change of ownership transaction is approved by CMS, said purchaser/buyer/transferee must assume complete responsibility for the operations (that is, managerial, financial, and legal) of the CMS-approved accreditation programs transferred, immediately upon the finalization of the change of ownership transaction.
units.action_summary: Assume full managerial, financial, and legal responsibility for the transferred CMS-approved accreditation programs immediately upon finalization if CMS approves the transfer.

units.obligation_text: The purchaser/buyer/transferee agrees to operate the transferred CMS-approved accreditation program(s) under all of the CMS imposed terms and conditions, to include program reviews and probationary status terms, currently approved by CMS;
units.action_summary: Operate the transferred CMS-approved accreditation programs under all CMS-imposed terms and conditions, including program reviews and probationary terms.

units.obligation_text: The purchaser/buyer/transferee must not operate the accreditation program(s) it acquired in the change in ownership transaction as CMS approved accreditation programs, until the effective date set forth within the notice of approval from CMS.
units.action_summary: Do not operate the acquired accreditation programs as CMS-approved programs until the effective date specified in CMS's notice of approval.

units.obligation_text: The purchaser/buyer/transferee agrees to operate the transferred CMS-approved accreditation program(s) under all of the terms and conditions found at §§ 488.5 through 488.9.
units.action_summary: Operate the transferred accreditation programs in accordance with all terms and conditions in §§ 488.5–488.9.

units.obligation_text: The following written notifications are required after the change of ownership transaction has been approved by CMS:
units.actor: parties to the change of ownership transaction
units.action_summary: After CMS approves the transfer, specified written notifications must be provided.

units.obligation_text: All parties to the change of ownership transaction must notify the providers and suppliers affected by such change within 15 calendar days after being notified of CMS’s approval of the transfer of the existing CMS-approval for the accreditation programs to be transferred in the change of ownership transaction.
units.actor: all parties to the change of ownership transaction
units.action_summary: Notify affected providers and suppliers within 15 calendar days after being notified of CMS's approval of the transfer.

units.obligation_text: If applicable, the purchaser/buyer/transferee must acknowledge in writing to CMS that the accrediting organization or accreditation program(s) being acquired through a purchase or transfer of ownership was under a performance review or under probationary status at the time the change of ownership notice was submitted.
units.action_summary: If applicable, provide written acknowledgment to CMS that the acquired accrediting organization/program was under performance review or probation at the time of the change-of-ownership notice.

units.obligation_text: CMS will publish a notice of approval in the Federal Register of the transfer of the existing CMS approval for the accreditation program(s) to be transferred to the new owner, only after CMS receives written confirmation from the new owner that the change of ownership has taken place.
units.action_summary: CMS will publish a Federal Register notice of approval of the transfer only after receiving written confirmation from the new owner that the change of ownership has occurred.

units.obligation_text: In the event that CMS does not approve the transfer of the existing CMS approval for the accreditation program(s) to be transferred in the change of ownership transaction, CMS will notify all parties to the change of ownership transaction of such in writing.
units.action_summary: If CMS disapproves the transfer, CMS will notify all parties in writing.

units.obligation_text: Withdrawal of CMS approval for transferred accreditation programs due to failure to notify CMS of intent to transfer accreditation programs. In the event that CMS was not made aware of or did not approve the transfer of the existing CMS-approval for the accreditation program(s) to be transferred under a change of ownership:
units.action_summary: Describes outcomes if CMS was not notified of or did not approve the transfer of CMS approval.

units.obligation_text: The existing AO would be permitted to continue operating their existing CMS-approved accreditation programs, if the change of ownership transaction was not completed, unless our review of the transaction revealed issues with the AO that were the subject of the un-finalized change of ownership transaction that was previously unknown to CMS.
units.action_summary: If the change of ownership was not completed and no new issues are revealed, the existing AO may continue operating its CMS-approved programs.

units.obligation_text: If a change of ownership transaction was completed without notice to CMS or the approval of CMS, CMS would be able to withdraw the existing approval of the AO’s accreditation programs in accordance with § 488.8(c)(3)(ii) and (iii) of this section.
units.action_summary: If a transfer was completed without CMS notice or approval, CMS may withdraw the AO's existing program approvals under the specified procedures.

units.obligation_text: In the event that the parties complete the change of ownership transaction, notwithstanding CMS disapproval and the purchaser/buyer/transferee attempts to operate the transferred accreditation program(s) under the CMS-approval granted to the previous owner, CMS will withdraw the existing approval of the transferred accreditation program(s) in accordance with the procedures set out at § 488.8(c)(3)(ii) and (iii).
units.action_summary: If parties complete a transfer despite CMS disapproval and attempt to operate under the previous owner's approval, CMS will withdraw the transferred program's CMS approval under specified procedures.

units.obligation_text: Requirements for continuation of a deemed status accreditation of Medicare-certified providers and suppliers after CMS withdraws the existing approval of the transferred accreditation program(s). If CMS withdraws the existing approval of the transferred accreditation program(s) because the change of ownership transaction was completed without notice to CMS or the approval of CMS, an affected Medicare-Certified provider or supplier’s deemed status will continue in effect for 180 calendar days if the Medicare-Certified provider or supplier takes the following steps set forth is § 488.8(g).
units.actor: an affected Medicare-certified provider or supplier
units.action_summary: If CMS withdraws approval due to an unapproved change of ownership, an affected Medicare-certified provider/supplier can retain deemed status for 180 days by meeting specified steps.

units.obligation_text: The Medicare-certified provider or supplier must submit an application to another CMS-approved accreditation program within 60 calendar days from the date of publication of the removal notice in the Federal Register;
units.action_summary: Submit an application to another CMS-approved accreditation program within 60 calendar days of the removal notice publication.

units.obligation_text: The Medicare-certified provider or supplier must provide written notice to the SA that it has submitted an application for accreditation under another CMS-approved accreditation program within this same 60-calendar day timeframe in accordance with § 488.8(g).
units.action_summary: Provide written notice to the State Agency that an application to another CMS-approved accreditation program has been submitted within the same 60-day timeframe.

units.obligation_text: Failure to comply with the timeframe requirements specified in § 488.8(g) will place the provider or supplier under the SA’s authority for continued participation in Medicare and on-going monitoring.
units.actor: the State Agency (SA) / the provider or supplier as affected
units.action_summary: If the provider/supplier fails to meet the timeframe requirements, they will be placed under the State Agency's authority for continued Medicare participation and monitoring.

units.obligation_text: Requirements for continuation of accreditation for non-certified suppliers when CMS withdraws the existing approval of the transferred accreditation program(s). If CMS withdraws its existing approval from a transferred non-certified accreditation program for Advanced Diagnostic Imaging (ADI) suppliers; Home Infusion Therapy (HIT) suppliers; Diabetic Self-Management Training (DSMT) entities; Durable Medical Equipment Prosthetics, Orthotics and Supplies (DMEPOS) suppliers; or clinical laboratories, because a change of ownership transaction was completed without notice to or the approval of CMS, such affected non-certified supplier’s deemed status would continue in effect for 1 year after the removal of the existing CMS accreditation approval, if such non-certified supplier take the steps specified paragraphs (f)(10)(i) and (ii) of this section—
units.actor: an affected non-certified supplier (ADI, HIT, DSMT, DMEPOS, or clinical laboratory)
units.action_summary: If CMS withdraws its approval due to an unapproved change of ownership, affected non-certified suppliers can retain deemed status for one year by taking specified steps.

units.obligation_text: The non-certified supplier must submit an application to another CMS-approved accreditation program within 60 calendar days from the date of publication of the removal notice in the Federal Register;
units.action_summary: Submit an application to another CMS-approved accreditation program within 60 calendar days of the removal notice publication.

units.obligation_text: The non-certified supplier must provide written notice to CMS stating that it has submitted an application for accreditation under another CMS-approved accreditation program within the 60-calendar days from the date of publication of the removal notice in the Federal Register.
units.action_summary: Provide written notice to CMS that an application to another CMS-approved accreditation program was submitted within the 60-day timeframe.

units.obligation_text: Failure to comply with the above-stated timeframe requirements will result in de-recognition of such provider or supplier’s accreditation.
units.actor: CMS / the provider or supplier as affected
units.action_summary: If the supplier fails to meet the timeframe requirements, CMS will de-recognize the provider's or supplier's accreditation.

units.obligation_text: An accrediting organization that wishes to undergo a change of ownership is subject to the requirements set out at § 488.5(f).
units.actor: an accrediting organization that wishes to undergo a change of ownership
units.action_summary: Such accrediting organizations must comply with the requirements in § 488.5(f) when undergoing a change of ownership.

units.obligation_text: An accrediting organization that wishes to undergo a change of ownership is subject to the requirements set out at § 488.5(f) of this chapter.
units.actor: an accrediting organization that wishes to undergo a change of ownership
units.action_summary: Such accrediting organizations must comply with the requirements in § 488.5(f) when undergoing a change of ownership.

title: Medicare Program: Secure Electronic Prior Authorization for Medicare Part D CMS-4189-P

units.obligation_text: Beginning January 1, 2021, Part D sponsors and prescribers must comply with the National Council for Prescription Drug Programs SCRIPT standard, Implementation Guide Version 2017071 approved July 28, 2017 (incorporated by reference in paragraph (c)(1)(vii) of this section), to provide for the communication of a prescription or related prescription-related information between prescribers and dispensers for the following transactions:
units.action_summary: Starting Jan 1, 2021, Part D sponsors and prescribers are required to comply with the NCPDP SCRIPT Implementation Guide (Version 2017071) to enable electronic communication of prescriptions and related information between prescribers and dispensers for specified prior authorization transactions.

units.obligation_text: (i) PAInitiationRequest and PAInitiationResponse
units.action_summary: Require support for PAInitiationRequest and PAInitiationResponse transactions under the required SCRIPT standard.

units.obligation_text: (ii) PARequest and PAResponse
units.action_summary: Require support for PARequest and PAResponse transactions under the required SCRIPT standard.

units.obligation_text: (iii) PAAppealRequest and PAAppealResponse
units.action_summary: Require support for PAAppealRequest and PAAppealResponse transactions under the required SCRIPT standard.

units.obligation_text: (iv) PACancelRequest and PACancelResponse
units.action_summary: Require support for PACancelRequest and PACancelResponse transactions under the required SCRIPT standard.

title: Medicare and Medicaid Programs: Organ Procurement Organizations Conditions for Coverage: Revisions to the Outcome Measure Requirements for Organ Procurement Organization

units.obligation_text: If an OPO does not meet the performance requirements of the outcome measures as described in paragraph (a)(1) of this section at the final assessment prior to the end of the re-certification cycle or the requirements described in paragraph (a)(2) of this section the OPO is de-certified.
units.action_summary: If an OPO fails to meet specified performance or certification requirements at final assessment, it will be de-certified.

units.obligation_text: If the OPO does not appeal or the OPO appeals and the reconsideration official and CMS hearing officer uphold the de-certification, the OPO’s service area is opened for competition from other OPOs.
units.action_summary: If de-certification is not overturned on appeal, the de-certified OPO's service area will be opened for competition by other OPOs.

units.obligation_text: The de-certified OPO is not permitted to compete for its open area or any other open area.
units.action_summary: A de-certified OPO is prohibited from competing for its former service area or any other open area.

units.obligation_text: An OPO competing for an open service area must submit information and data that describe the barriers in its service area, how they affected organ donation, what steps the OPO took to overcome them, and the results.
units.actor: an OPO competing for an open service area
units.action_summary: An OPO that seeks to compete for an open service area must submit descriptive information and data about barriers, effects, corrective steps, and results.

units.obligation_text: To compete for an open service area, an OPO must meet the performance requirements of the outcome measures at § 486.318 and the requirements for certification at § 486.303, including the conditions for coverage at §§ 486.320 through 486.360.
units.action_summary: An OPO must satisfy the outcome measure performance and certification requirements to be eligible to compete for an open service area.

units.obligation_text: The OPO must compete for the entire service area.
units.actor: the OPO (competing for an open service area)
units.action_summary: An OPO competing for an open service area is required to bid for the entire service area, not part of it.

units.obligation_text: The numerator of donors and organs transplanted is based on the data submitted to the OPTN as required in § 486.328 and/or 42 CFR 121.11.
units.action_summary: Data submitted to the OPTN (as required by referenced provisions) form the numerator for the outcome measures.

units.obligation_text: An OPO must demonstrate a success rate on the outcome measures in accordance with the following parameters and requirements:
units.action_summary: An OPO is required to meet success-rate performance on specified outcome measures according to the listed parameters.

units.obligation_text: For the assessment period, a threshold rate will be established based on the lowest rate among the top 25 percent of donation rates during the 12-month period immediately prior to the period being evaluated.
units.action_summary: The threshold for donation rates will be set as the lowest rate among the top 25% of donation rates from the prior 12-month period.

units.obligation_text: For the assessment period, a threshold rate will be established based on the lowest rate among the top 25 percent of organ transplantation rates during the 12-month period prior to the period being evaluated.
units.action_summary: The threshold for organ transplantation rates will be set as the lowest rate among the top 25% of organ transplantation rates from the prior 12-month period.

units.obligation_text: The 95 percent confidence interval for each OPO will be calculated using a one-sided test.
units.action_summary: Each OPO's 95% confidence interval for outcome measures will be computed using a one-sided statistical test.

units.obligation_text: OPOs whose upper limit of the one-sided 95 percent confidence interval is less than the threshold rate established will be flagged.
units.action_summary: If an OPO's upper one-sided 95% confidence interval limit is below the threshold, that OPO will be flagged.

units.obligation_text: An OPO’s performance on the outcome measures is based on an assessment at least every 12 months with the most recent 12 months of data from the OPTN and state death certificates, beginning December 31 of the first year of the re-certification cycle and ending December 31, prior to the end of the re-certification cycle.
units.action_summary: OPO performance will be assessed at least annually using the most recent 12 months of OPTN and state death certificate data covering specified dates.

units.obligation_text: If an OPO’s performance falls below the outcome measure described in paragraph (b) of this section prior to the last cycle before the end of the certification period, the OPO must meet the requirements of § 486.348(d)(3).
units.action_summary: If performance falls below the specified outcome measures before the final certification cycle, the OPO is required to meet the actions in §486.348(d)(3).

units.obligation_text: If an OPO takes over another OPO’s service area on a date later than January 1 of the first year of the re-certification cycle so that 12 months of data are not available to evaluate the OPO’s performance in its new service area, we will not hold the OPO accountable for its performance in the new area until 12 months of data are available.
units.actor: the OPO (and CMS as assessing authority)
units.action_summary: If an OPO assumes a new service area after Jan 1 and lacks 12 months of data, CMS will not hold the OPO accountable for that new area until 12 months of data exist.

units.obligation_text: An OPO must include a process to review its performance on the outcome measure requirements at § 486.318.
units.action_summary: An OPO is required to have a process in place to review its performance on the outcome measures.

units.obligation_text: The process must be a continuous activity to improve performance.
units.action_summary: The review process must be continuous and aimed at improving performance.

units.obligation_text: An OPO must incorporate data on the outcome measures into their QAPI program.
units.action_summary: An OPO must incorporate outcome measure data into its Quality Assessment and Performance Improvement program.

units.obligation_text: If the outcome measure at each assessment cycle, except the final assessment before re-certification, is statistically significantly lower than the top 25 percent of donation rates or organ transplantation rates, the OPO must identify opportunities for improvement and implement changes that lead to improvement in these measures.
units.action_summary: If an OPO's outcome measures are statistically significantly below the top 25% (except at final pre-recertification assessment), the OPO must identify improvement opportunities and implement changes to improve those measures.

title: Medicare Program: Medicare Secondary Payer and Certain Civil Money Penalties

units.obligation_text: Any entity that has a reporting obligation under section 1862(b)(7) of the Act ("reporting entity") reports, but fails to comply with the reporting instructions in the following situations:
units.action_summary: Comply with reporting instructions under section 1862(b)(7); failure to comply in listed situations constitutes a report violation triggering CMPs.

units.obligation_text: Fails to report any beneficiary record within 1 year from the group health plan (GHP) coverage effective date or the Medicare beneficiary’s entitlement date.
units.action_summary: Report each beneficiary record within 1 year of the GHP coverage effective date or the beneficiary's entitlement date.

units.obligation_text: Contradicts its reporting under section 1862(b)(7) of the Act in response to CMS recovery efforts.
units.action_summary: Do not contradict prior reporting when responding to CMS recovery efforts.

units.obligation_text: Has reported and exceeds any error tolerance(s) threshold established by the Secretary in any 4 out of 8 consecutive reporting periods.
units.action_summary: Maintain reporting error rates at or below Secretary-established error tolerance thresholds (not exceed in 4 of 8 periods).

units.obligation_text: A civil money penalty (CMP) is not imposed if— (A) It is associated with a specific policy or procedural change is not imposed for a minimum of two reporting periods following the implementation of that policy or procedural change;
units.action_summary: CMP will not be imposed for at least two reporting periods after implementation of a specific policy or procedural change associated with the failure.

units.obligation_text: A civil money penalty (CMP) is not imposed if— (B) The entity complies with any reporting thresholds or any other reporting exclusions.
units.action_summary: Comply with applicable reporting thresholds or exclusions to avoid imposition of a CMP.

units.obligation_text: An applicable plan has a reporting obligation under section 1862(b)(8) of the Act ("applicable plan"), but fails to comply with the reporting instructions in the following situations:
units.action_summary: Comply with reporting instructions under section 1862(b)(8); listed failures constitute violations triggering CMPs.

units.obligation_text: Except for the situations described in paragraphs (c)(22)(iv)(A) through (C) of this section, fails to report any beneficiary record within 1 year from the date of the settlement, judgment, award, or other payment.
units.action_summary: Report NGHP beneficiary records within 1 year of the settlement/judgment/award/other payment date (TPOC date), subject to exceptions.

units.obligation_text: Contradicts its reporting under section 1862(b)(8) of the Act in response to CMS recovery efforts.
units.action_summary: Do not contradict prior reporting when responding to CMS recovery efforts.

units.obligation_text: Has reported, and exceeds any error tolerance(s) threshold established by the Secretary (not to exceed 20 percent) in any 4 out of 8 (or less) consecutive reporting periods.
units.action_summary: Keep reported error rates at or below Secretary-established thresholds (not to exceed 20%) to avoid violation (no more than 3 of 8 periods over tolerance).

units.obligation_text: A CMP is not imposed in the following situations: (A) If a non-group health plan (NGHP) applicable plan fails to report required information as a result of the applicable plan’s inability to obtain an individual’s last name, first name, date of birth, gender, Medicare Beneficiary Identifier (MBI), Social Security Number (SSN), or the last 5 digits of the SSN, and the applicable plan has made a good faith effort to obtain this information by meeting all of the following:
units.action_summary: CMP will not be imposed if NGHP cannot obtain required identifying information and has made specified good faith efforts to obtain it.

units.obligation_text: Communicating the need for this information to the individual and his or her attorney or other representative.
units.action_summary: Communicate to the individual and their attorney/representative the need for the identifying information.

units.obligation_text: Requesting the information from the individual and his or her attorney or other representative at least twice by mail and at least once by phone or other means of contact.
units.action_summary: Make at least two mail requests and at least one phone/other contact request to obtain the identifying information.

units.obligation_text: Has not received a response or has received a response in writing that the individual refuses to provide his or her MBI or SSN or a truncated form of the MBI or SSN.
units.action_summary: Document that there was no response or a written refusal to provide MBI/SSN (or truncated forms) as a condition for the CMP exception.

units.obligation_text: Has documented its efforts to obtain the MBI or SSN (or the last 5 digits of the SSN).
units.action_summary: Document all efforts made to obtain the MBI/SSN (including last 5 digits) to qualify for the CMP exception.

units.obligation_text: A CMP is not imposed if an NGHP applicable plan complies with any reporting thresholds or any other reporting exclusions.
units.action_summary: If the NGHP meets reporting thresholds or other reporting exclusions, CMPs will not be imposed.

units.obligation_text: A CMP associated with a specific policy or procedural change is not imposed for a minimum of two reporting periods following the implementation of that policy or procedural change.
units.action_summary: CMP tied to a specific policy or procedural change will not be imposed for at least two reporting periods after implementation.

units.obligation_text: For entities with reporting obligations under section 1862(b)(7) of the Act ("reporting entity") as follows:
units.action_summary: Entities with reporting obligations under 1862(b)(7) must meet the reporting requirements described below or incur specified penalties.

units.obligation_text: A reporting entity fails to report any beneficiary record within the specified period from the latter of the GHP coverage effective date or the Medicare beneficiary’s entitlement date. The penalty is—
units.action_summary: Report beneficiary records within the specified period (generally within 1 year) or be subject to penalties calculated below.

units.obligation_text: Calculated on a daily basis, based on the actual number of beneficiary records that the entity submitted more than 1 year after the GHP Medicare Secondary Payer (MSP) effective date;
units.action_summary: Penalty is calculated daily based on the number of records submitted more than 1 year late.

units.obligation_text: $1,000 as adjusted annually under 45 CFR part 102 for each calendar day of noncompliance for each individual for which the required information should have been submitted, up to a maximum penalty of $365,000 as adjusted annually under 45 CFR part 102 per individual per year.
units.action_summary: Penalty amount up to $1,000 per calendar day per individual (adjusted annually), capped at $365,000 per individual per year (adjusted).

units.obligation_text: A reporting entity’s response to CMS recovery efforts contradicts the entity’s reporting under section 1862(b)(7) of the Act. The penalty is—
units.action_summary: Do not provide responses to CMS recovery efforts that contradict earlier reporting; such contradictions trigger penalties.

units.obligation_text: Calculated based on the number of calendar days that the entity failed to appropriately report updates to beneficiary records, as required for accurate and timely reporting;
units.action_summary: Penalty is calculated based on calendar days the entity failed to report required updates.

units.obligation_text: $1,000 as adjusted annually under 45 CFR part 102 for each calendar day of noncompliance for each individual for which the required information should have been submitted.
units.action_summary: Penalty amount is $1,000 per calendar day (adjusted annually) per individual for failure to report required updates.

units.obligation_text: A reporting entity has reported, and exceeds any error tolerance(s) threshold established by the Secretary (not to exceed 20 percent) in any 4 out of 8 (or less) consecutive reporting periods. The penalty is—
units.action_summary: Maintain error rates within Secretary-established tolerances; exceeding in 4 of 8 periods triggers penalties described below.

units.obligation_text: Based upon the number of beneficiary records on the fourth submission that exceed any such error tolerance(s); and
units.action_summary: Penalty is based on count of beneficiary records on the fourth submission that exceed error tolerances.

units.obligation_text: $1,000 as adjusted annually under 45 CFR part 102 for each calendar day of noncompliance for each individual for which the required information should have been submitted.
units.action_summary: Penalty amount is $1,000 per calendar day per individual (adjusted annually) for records exceeding error tolerances.

units.obligation_text: For entities with reporting obligations under section 1862(b)(8) ("applicable plan") of the Act as follows:
units.action_summary: Applicable plans with reporting obligations under 1862(b)(8) must meet reporting requirements or be subject to specified penalties.

units.obligation_text: An applicable plan fails to report any NGHP beneficiary record within the specified period from the date of the settlement, judgment, award, or other payment. The penalty is—
units.action_summary: Report NGHP beneficiary records within the specified period (from TPOC date) or be subject to penalties described below.

units.obligation_text: Calculated on a daily basis, based on the actual number of beneficiary records that the entity submitted more than 1 year after the Total Payment Obligation to Claimant (TPOC) date;
units.action_summary: Penalty is calculated daily based on the number of records submitted more than 1 year after the TPOC date.

units.obligation_text: Up to $1,000 as adjusted annually under 45 CFR part 102 for each calendar day of noncompliance for each individual for which the required information should have been submitted, up to a maximum penalty of $365,000 as adjusted annually under 45 CFR part 102 per individual per year.
units.action_summary: Penalty up to $1,000 per calendar day per individual (adjusted), capped at $365,000 per individual per year (adjusted).

units.obligation_text: An applicable plan’s response to CMS recovery efforts contradicts the entity’s reporting under section 1862(b)(8) of the Act. The penalty is—
units.action_summary: Do not contradict prior reporting when responding to CMS recovery efforts; contradictions trigger penalties.

units.obligation_text: Calculated based on the number of calendar days that the entity failed to appropriately report updates to beneficiary records, as required for accurate and timely reporting;
units.action_summary: Penalty is calculated based on number of calendar days the applicable plan failed to report required updates.

units.obligation_text: Up to $1,000 as adjusted annually under 45 CFR part 102 per calendar day of noncompliance, for a maximum penalty of $365,000 as adjusted annually under 45 CFR part 102.
units.action_summary: Penalty amount up to $1,000 per calendar day (adjusted), maximum $365,000 (adjusted).

units.obligation_text: An applicable plan has reported, and exceeds any error tolerance(s) threshold established by the Secretary (not to exceed 20 percent) in any 4 out of 8 consecutive reporting periods. The penalty is calculated using the following tiered approach, based on the number of calendar days that the applicable plan exceeded the error tolerance(s) in the entity’s fourth above-tolerance submission.
units.action_summary: If an applicable plan exceeds error tolerance thresholds in 4 of 8 periods, penalties are imposed under a tiered approach described below.

units.obligation_text: Initial penalty amount. For the first penalty, CMS imposes a penalty of one-quarter (25 percent) of the maximum penalty per beneficiary per calendar day of non-compliance after the required date of submission (last calendar day of the applicable plan’s reporting period), based upon the number of beneficiaries whose records exceeded any error tolerance(s) established by the Secretary.
units.action_summary: First penalty equals 25% of maximum penalty per beneficiary per calendar day for beneficiaries exceeding error tolerances on the fourth above-tolerance submission.

units.obligation_text: Subsequent penalty amounts. For the second and subsequent penalties, CMS increases the penalty specified in paragraph (b)(3)(iii)(A) of this section in increments of one-quarter (25 percent) of the maximum penalty for applicable plans that fail to comply in consecutive reporting periods to a maximum of $1,000 as adjusted annually under 45 CFR part 102 per beneficiary per calendar day of non-compliance.
units.action_summary: Penalties increase by 25% of the maximum penalty for subsequent penalties up to the $1,000 per beneficiary per day (adjusted) cap.

units.obligation_text: Reduction in penalty amount. If the applicable plan reports after the assessment of a penalty and the entity remains below any error tolerances, the penalty amount for the next penalty eligible file is reduced by increments of one-quarter (25 percent) of the maximum penalty per beneficiary per calendar day of non-compliance per consecutive subsequent quarter of compliance, to the minimum penalty of one-quarter (25 percent) of the maximum penalty per beneficiary per calendar day of non-compliance.
units.action_summary: If plan returns to compliance after a penalty, future penalty amounts are reduced in 25% increments per compliant quarter down to a 25% minimum of the maximum penalty.

units.obligation_text: Penalty for any person or entity who knowingly and willfully bills or collects for any outpatient therapy services or comprehensive outpatient rehabilitation services on other than an as-assignment-related basis.
units.action_summary: Do not knowingly and willfully bill or collect for outpatient therapy or comprehensive outpatient rehab services on other than an assignment-related basis.

units.obligation_text: Penalty for any supplier of ambulance services who knowingly and willfully fills or collects for any services on other than an assignment-related basis.
units.action_summary: Do not knowingly and willfully bill or collect for ambulance services on other than an assignment-related basis.

units.obligation_text: Penalty for any entity that knowingly, willfully, and repeatedly fails to complete a claim form relating to the availability of other health benefits in accordance with statute or provides inaccurate information relating to such on the claim form.
units.actor: any entity required to complete claim form
units.action_summary: Complete claim forms accurately regarding availability of other health benefits; do not knowingly, willfully, and repeatedly fail to complete or provide inaccurate information.

units.obligation_text: Penalty for any entity serving as insurer, third party administrator, or fiduciary for a group health plan that fails to provide information that identifies situations where the group health plan is or was a primary plan to Medicare to the HHS Secretary.
units.actor: entity serving as insurer, third party administrator, or fiduciary for a group health plan
units.action_summary: Provide information identifying situations where the group health plan is or was primary to Medicare to the HHS Secretary.

units.obligation_text: Penalty for any entity serving as insurer, third party administrator, or fiduciary for a non-group health plan that fails to provide information that identifies situations where the group health plan is or was a primary plan to Medicare to the HHS Secretary.
units.actor: entity serving as insurer, third party administrator, or fiduciary for a non-group health plan (NGHP applicable plan)
units.action_summary: Provide information to HHS identifying when the non-group health plan is or was primary to Medicare; failure to do so may result in penalty.

title: Basic Health Program; Federal Funding Methodology for Program Year 2021

units.obligation_text: States operating a State-based Exchange in the individual market, however, must provide certain data, including premiums for second lowest cost silver plans, by geographic area, for CMS to calculate the federal BHP payment rates in those states.
units.action_summary: State-based Exchanges must provide specified data (including second-lowest-cost silver plan premiums) by geographic area so CMS can calculate federal BHP payment rates.

units.obligation_text: We propose that a State-based Exchange interested in obtaining the applicable 2021 program year federal BHP payment rates for its state must submit such data accurately, completely, and as specified by CMS, by no later than October 15, 2020.
units.action_summary: State-based Exchanges seeking 2021 federal BHP payment rates must submit the required data accurately, completely, and as specified by CMS by October 15, 2020.

units.obligation_text: If additional state data (that is, in addition to the second lowest cost silver plan premium data) are needed to determine the federal BHP payment rate, such data must be submitted in a timely manner, and in a format specified by us to support the development and timely release of annual BHP payment notices.
units.action_summary: States must submit any additional data needed to determine federal BHP payment rates promptly and in a CMS-specified format.

units.obligation_text: States operating a BHP must submit enrollment data to us on a quarterly basis
units.action_summary: States running a BHP are required to submit enrollment data to CMS every quarter.

units.obligation_text: and should be technologically prepared to begin submitting data at the start of their BHP, starting with the beginning of the first program year.
units.action_summary: States should have the technical ability to begin submitting enrollment data at the start of their BHP's first program year.

units.obligation_text: We propose that in states that have BHP enrollees who do not file federal tax returns (non-filers), the state must develop a methodology to determine the enrollees’ household income and household size consistently with Marketplace requirements.
units.action_summary: States with BHP non-filers must create a methodology consistent with Marketplace requirements to determine household income and size.

units.obligation_text: The state must submit this methodology to us at the time of their Blueprint submission.
units.action_summary: States must submit the non-filer methodology to CMS when they submit their Blueprint.

units.obligation_text: We reserve the right to approve or disapprove the state’s methodology to determine household income and household size for non-filers if the household composition and/or household income resulting from application of the methodology are different than what typically would be expected to result if the individual or head of household in the family were to file a tax return.
units.action_summary: CMS may approve or disapprove a state's non-filer methodology if the results differ from expected tax-filing outcomes.
units.modal_raw: reserve the right to approve or disapprove

units.obligation_text: States currently operating a BHP that wish to change the methodology for non-filers must submit a revised Blueprint outlining the revisions to its methodology, consistent with § 600.125.
units.action_summary: Existing BHP states that change their non-filer methodology must submit a revised Blueprint describing those changes in accordance with § 600.125.

units.obligation_text: The states must maintain data that are consistent with CMS’ verification requirements, including auditable records for each individual enrolled, indicating an eligibility determination and a determination of income and other criteria relevant to the payment methodology as of the beginning of each quarter.
units.action_summary: States must keep verification-consistent, auditable records for each enrolled individual showing eligibility, income, and other payment-relevant criteria as of each quarter's start.

units.obligation_text: Consistent with § 600.610 (Secretarial determination of BHP payment amount), the state is required to submit certain data in accordance with this notice. We require that this data be collected and validated by states operating a BHP, and that this data be submitted to CMS.
units.action_summary: States operating a BHP are required to collect, validate, and submit specified data to CMS as set out in this notice and § 600.610.

units.obligation_text: We propose that the quarterly payment would be based on the characteristics of the enrollee at the beginning of the quarter (or their first month of enrollment in the BHP in each quarter).
units.action_summary: CMS proposes to base quarterly payments on enrollee characteristics as of the quarter's start (or their first month enrolled in that quarter).

units.obligation_text: Payments would still be made only for months that the person is enrolled in and eligible for the BHP.
units.action_summary: CMS will make payments only for months when the person is enrolled and eligible for the BHP.

units.obligation_text: We propose to publish separate rate cells for household sizes of 1 through 10.
units.action_summary: CMS proposes to publish federal payment rate cells for household sizes 1–10.

units.obligation_text: These rate cells would only be used to calculate the federal BHP payment amount. A state implementing a BHP would not be required to use these rate cells or any of the factors in these rate cells as part of the state payment to the standard health plans participating in the BHP or to help define BHP enrollees’ covered benefits, premium costs, or out-of-pocket cost-sharing levels.
units.action_summary: States implementing a BHP are not required to use the federal rate cells or their factors for state payments, benefits, premiums, or cost-sharing settings.

units.obligation_text: Consistent with the policy set forth in 26 CFR 1.36B–3(f)(6), to calculate the PTC for those enrolled in a QHP through an Exchange, we propose not to update the payment methodology, and subsequently the federal BHP payment rates, in the event that the second lowest cost silver plan used as the RP, or the lowest cost silver plan, changes (that is, terminates or closes enrollment during the year).
units.action_summary: CMS proposes not to change the payment methodology or federal BHP payment rates during the year if the reference silver plan changes or closes.

units.obligation_text: We propose to include the PAF in the 2021 payment methodology and to calculate it in the same manner as in the Final Administrative Order.
units.action_summary: CMS proposes to include the Premium Adjustment Factor (PAF) in the 2021 methodology and compute it as before.

units.obligation_text: Given these analytic challenges and the limited data about Exchange coverage and the characteristics of BHP-eligible consumers, we propose that the PHF continue to be 1.00 for program year 2021.
units.action_summary: CMS proposes to set the Population Health Factor (PHF) at 1.00 for program year 2021.

units.obligation_text: In previous years BHP payment methodologies, we included an option for states to include a retrospective population health status adjustment. We propose that states be provided with the same option for 2021 to include a retrospective population health status adjustment in the certified methodology, which is subject to our review and approval.
units.action_summary: States may choose to include a retrospective population health status adjustment in their certified methodology for 2021, subject to CMS review and approval.

units.obligation_text: While the statute requires consideration of risk adjustment payments and reinsurance payments insofar as they would have affected the PTC ..., we are not proposing to require that a BHP’s standard health plans receive such payments.
units.action_summary: CMS is not proposing to require that BHP standard health plans receive risk adjustment or reinsurance payments.

units.obligation_text: We propose to use geographic areas based on the rating areas used in the Exchanges.

units.obligation_text: When the RP varies within a rating area, we propose defining geographic areas as aggregations of counties with the same RP.

units.obligation_text: We propose that no geographic area, for purposes of defining BHP payment rate cells, will be smaller than a county.
units.action_summary: Do not define BHP payment geographic areas smaller than a county.

units.obligation_text: We propose that federal payment rates only recognize self-only and two-adult coverage, with exceptions that account for children who are potentially eligible for the BHP.

units.action_summary: CMS applies a reduced payment rate update (0.6%) to the federal per diem base rate for IPFs that fail IPFQR requirements, resulting in the specified FY2021 base rate.

units.obligation_text: For IPFs that fail to meet requirements under the IPFQR Program, we applied the 0.6 percent annual payment rate update and the 0.9979 wage index budget-neutrality factor to the FY 2020 ECT payment per treatment of $343.79, yielding an ECT payment per treatment of $345.13 for FY 2021.
units.action_summary: CMS applies the reduced update and wage index factor to calculate a reduced FY2021 ECT payment per treatment for IPFs failing IPFQR requirements.

units.obligation_text: Diagnoses that relate to an earlier episode of care and have no bearing on the current hospital stay are excluded and must not be reported on IPF claims.
units.action_summary: Providers must not report diagnoses on IPF claims that relate only to prior episodes and do not affect the current stay.

units.obligation_text: Comorbid conditions must exist at the time of admission or develop subsequently, and affect the treatment received, length of stay (LOS), or both treatment and LOS.
units.actor: providers/IPFs (for purposes of coding and claiming comorbid conditions)
units.action_summary: Only comorbid conditions that exist on admission or develop during the stay and that affect treatment or LOS qualify for comorbidity adjustment.

units.obligation_text: For each claim, an IPF may receive only one comorbidity adjustment within a comorbidity category, but it may receive an adjustment for more than one comorbidity category.
units.action_summary: An IPF claim can get at most one adjustment per comorbidity category but may receive adjustments for multiple different comorbidity categories.

units.obligation_text: Current billing instructions for discharge claims, on or after October 1, 2015, require IPFs to enter the complete ICD–10–CM codes for up to 24 additional diagnoses if they co-exist at the time of admission, or develop subsequently and impact the treatment provided.
units.action_summary: IPFs must report up to 24 additional full ICD-10-CM diagnosis codes on discharge claims when those diagnoses co-exist on admission or develop and impact treatment.

units.obligation_text: In accordance with the ICD–10–CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting, when a primary (psychiatric) diagnosis code has a "code first" note, the provider would follow the instructions in the ICD–10–CM text.
units.action_summary: When a primary diagnosis has a 'code first' note, providers must follow the sequencing instructions in the ICD‑10‑CM guidelines.

units.obligation_text: Psychiatric principal diagnoses that do not group to one of the 17 designated MS–DRGs would still receive the federal per diem base rate and all other applicable adjustments, but the payment would not include an MS–DRG adjustment.
units.action_summary: If a psychiatric principal diagnosis does not map to one of the 17 MS‑DRGs, the claim still gets the federal per diem base rate and other adjustments, but no MS‑DRG adjustment.

units.obligation_text: The diagnoses for each IPF MS–DRG would be updated as of October 1, 2020, using the final IPPS FY 2021 ICD–10–CM/PCS code sets.
units.action_summary: CMS will update the diagnoses that define each IPF MS‑DRG effective October 1, 2020, using the FY2021 ICD‑10‑CM/PCS code sets.

units.obligation_text: For FY 2021, we are proposing to continue to use the patient age adjustments currently in effect in FY 2020, as shown in Addendum A of this rule.
units.action_summary: CMS proposes to retain the current patient age adjustment factors for FY2021.
units.modal_raw: are proposing to continue to use

units.obligation_text: The variable per diem adjustments begin on day 1 and decline gradually until day 21 of a patient's stay. For day 22 and thereafter, the variable per diem adjustment remains the same each day for the remainder of the stay. However, the adjustment applied to day 1 depends upon whether the IPF has a qualifying ED.
units.action_summary: Variable per diem adjustments are applied by day of stay (declining through day 21, constant thereafter), and day‑1 adjustment varies based on whether the IPF has a qualifying ED.

units.obligation_text: If an IPF has a qualifying ED, it receives a 1.31 adjustment factor for day 1 of each stay.
units.action_summary: IPFs that have a qualifying emergency department receive a 1.31 day‑1 per diem adjustment factor.

units.obligation_text: If an IPF does not have a qualifying ED, it receives a 1.19 adjustment factor for day 1 of the stay.
units.action_summary: IPFs without a qualifying emergency department receive a 1.19 day‑1 per diem adjustment factor.

units.obligation_text: For FY 2021, we are proposing to continue to use the variable per diem adjustment factors currently in effect, as shown in Addendum A of this rule.
units.action_summary: CMS proposes to continue the current variable per diem adjustment schedule for FY2021.
units.modal_raw: are proposing to continue to use

units.obligation_text: Our wage index policy at § 412.424(a)(2), requires us to use the best Medicare data available to estimate costs per day, including an appropriate wage index to adjust for wage differences.
units.action_summary: CMS is required to use the best available Medicare data, including an appropriate wage index, to estimate per‑day costs.

units.obligation_text: For FY 2021, we are proposing to continue to use the concurrent pre-floor, pre-reclassified IPPS hospital wage index as the basis for the IPF wage index.
units.action_summary: CMS proposes to base the FY2021 IPF wage index on the concurrent pre‑floor, pre‑reclassified IPPS hospital wage index.
units.modal_raw: are proposing to continue to use

units.obligation_text: We would apply the IPF wage index adjustment to the labor-related share of the national base rate and ECT payment per treatment. The labor-related share of the national rate and ECT payment per treatment would change from 76.9 percent in FY 2020 to 77.2 percent in FY 2021.
units.action_summary: CMS will apply the IPF wage index adjustment to the labor‑related portion of the national base rate and ECT payment, with the labor share moving to 77.2% for FY2021.

units.obligation_text: We are proposing to implement the new OMB delineations as described in the September 14, 2018 OMB Bulletin No. 18–04, effective beginning with the FY 2021 IPF PPS wage index.
units.action_summary: CMS proposes adopting the OMB Bulletin No.18‑04 labor market delineations for use in the FY2021 IPF wage index.

units.obligation_text: We are proposing to implement a wage index transition policy that would be applicable to all IPFs that may experience negative impacts due to the proposed implementation of the revised OMB delineations.
units.action_summary: CMS proposes a transition policy to mitigate negative impacts on IPFs from adopting the revised OMB delineations.

units.obligation_text: OMB defines a "Micropolitan Statistical Area" as a CBSA associated with at least one urban cluster that has a population of at least 10,000, but less than 50,000 ... we determined the best course of action would be to treat Micropolitan Areas as "rural" and include them in the calculation of each state's IPF PPS rural wage index.
units.action_summary: CMS will treat Micropolitan Areas as rural and include them in state rural wage index calculations for the IPF PPS.

units.obligation_text: We are proposing that the wage data for all providers located in the counties listed above would now be considered rural, beginning in FY 2021, when calculating their respective state's rural wage index. This rural wage index value would also be used under the IPF PPS.
units.action_summary: CMS proposes to treat wage data from specified counties as rural for state rural wage index calculations beginning FY2021, and to use that value in the IPF PPS.

units.obligation_text: We are proposing that when calculating the area wage index, beginning with FY 2021, the wage data for providers located in these counties would be included in their new respective urban CBSAs.
units.action_summary: CMS proposes to include wage data for certain counties within their newly assigned urban CBSA when calculating area wage indices starting FY2021.

units.obligation_text: We finalized in the FY 2015 IPF PPS rule, that we would remove site "unspecified" codes from the IPF PPS ICD–10–CM/PCS codes in instances when laterality codes (site specified codes) are available.
units.action_summary: CMS will remove 'site unspecified' ICD‑10‑CM/PCS codes from IPF PPS code lists when more specific laterality codes exist.

units.obligation_text: None of the proposed additions to the FY 2021 ICD–10–CM/PCS codes were site "unspecified" by laterality, therefore we are not removing any of the new codes.
units.action_summary: Because no new FY2021 ICD‑10‑CM/PCS additions were site‑unspecified, CMS will not remove any of the new codes (exception to removal policy).

units.obligation_text: For FY 2021, we are proposing to continue to use the same comorbidity adjustment factors in effect in FY 2020, which are found in Addendum A.
units.action_summary: CMS proposes to retain the FY2020 comorbidity adjustment factors for FY2021.
units.modal_raw: are proposing to continue to use

units.obligation_text: We would include any updates from this bulletin in any changes that would be adopted in the FY 2021 IPF PPS final rule.
units.action_summary: CMS will incorporate relevant OMB bulletin updates into any changes adopted in the FY2021 IPF PPS final rule if needed.

units.obligation_text: The wage index used for the IPF PPS is calculated using the unadjusted, pre-reclassified and pre-floor inpatient PPS (IPPS) wage index data and is assigned to the IPF on the basis of the labor market area in which the IPF is geographically located.
units.action_summary: CMS calculates the IPF wage index using unadjusted pre‑floor/pre‑reclassified IPPS wage index data and assigns it based on the IPF's labor market area.

units.obligation_text: IPF labor market areas are delineated based on the CBSAs established by the OMB.
units.actor: CMS (for delineation of labor market areas)
units.action_summary: Labor market areas for IPFs are determined based on OMB-established Core Based Statistical Areas (CBSAs).

title: Prospective Payment System and Consolidated Billing for Skilled Nursing Facilities and Updates to the Value-Based Purchasing Program for Federal Fiscal Year 2021 (CMS-1737-P) Display

units.obligation_text: In making a “practical matter” determination, as required by §409.31(b)(3), consideration must be given to the patient's condition and to the availability and feasibility of using more economical alternative facilities and services.
units.actor: the person making the 'practical matter' determination
units.action_summary: When making a 'practical matter' determination, the decisionmaker must consider the patient's condition and whether more economical alternative facilities/services are available and feasible.

units.obligation_text: However, in making that determination, the availability of Medicare payment for those services may not be a factor.
units.actor: the person making the 'practical matter' determination
units.action_summary: The decisionmaker may not consider whether Medicare will pay for alternative services when making the determination.

units.obligation_text: For example, if a beneficiary can obtain daily physical therapy services on an outpatient basis, the unavailability of Medicare payment for those alternative services due to the beneficiary’s non-enrollment in Part B may not be a basis for finding that the needed care can only be provided in a SNF.
units.actor: the person making the 'practical matter' determination
units.action_summary: The lack of Medicare payment (e.g., due to non-enrollment in Part B) cannot be used as the reason to conclude care can only be provided in a SNF.

units.obligation_text: Performance standards are the levels of performance that SNFs must meet or exceed to earn points under the SNF VBP Program for a fiscal year
units.action_summary: SNFs are required to meet or exceed specified performance levels to earn points under the SNF VBP Program.

units.obligation_text: Performance standards ... are announced no later than 60 days prior to the start of the performance period that applies to the SNF readmission measure for that fiscal year.
units.action_summary: CMS must announce the performance standards at least 60 days before the start of the applicable performance period.

units.obligation_text: Beginning with the performance standards that apply to FY 2021, if CMS discovers an error in the performance standard calculations subsequent to publishing their numerical values for a fiscal year, CMS will update the numerical values to correct the error.
units.action_summary: If CMS finds an error after publishing performance standard numerical values (starting with FY2021 standards), CMS will update the numerical values to correct that error.

units.obligation_text: If CMS subsequently discovers one or more other errors with respect to the same fiscal year, CMS will not further update the numerical values for that fiscal year.
units.action_summary: If additional errors are discovered for the same fiscal year after an initial correction, CMS will not make further updates for that fiscal year.

units.obligation_text: Beginning October 1, 2016, CMS will provide quarterly confidential feedback reports to SNFs on their performance on the SNF readmission measure.
units.action_summary: CMS will provide quarterly confidential feedback reports to SNFs about their SNF readmission measure performance.

units.obligation_text: SNFs will have the opportunity to review and submit corrections for these data by March 31st following the date that CMS provides the reports, for reports issued prior to October 1, 2019.
units.action_summary: For reports issued before Oct 1, 2019, SNFs are permitted to review and submit corrections to the data by the following March 31.

units.obligation_text: Beginning with the performance period quality measure quarterly report issued on or after October 1, 2019 ... SNFs will have 30 days following the date that CMS provides these reports to review and submit corrections for the data contained in these reports.
units.action_summary: For performance period reports issued on/after Oct 1, 2019, SNFs have 30 days from report date to review and submit corrections.

units.obligation_text: Beginning with the baseline period quality measure quarterly report issued on or after October 1, 2020 ... SNFs will have 30 days following the date that CMS provides these reports to review and submit corrections for the data contained in these reports.
units.action_summary: For baseline period reports issued on/after Oct 1, 2020, SNFs have 30 days from report date to review and submit corrections.

units.obligation_text: Any such correction requests must be accompanied by appropriate evidence showing the basis for the correction.
units.action_summary: When SNFs submit correction requests, they must include appropriate evidence supporting the requested correction.

units.obligation_text: CMS will publicly report the information described in paragraphs (e)(1) and (2) of this section on the Nursing Home Compare Website or a successor Website.
units.action_summary: CMS will publicly post the information from paragraphs (e)(1) and (e)(2) on Nursing Home Compare (or successor) website.

units.obligation_text: If CMS determines that a SNF has fewer than 25 eligible stays during the baseline period for a fiscal year but has 25 or more eligible stays during the performance period for that fiscal year, CMS will not publicly report the SNF’s baseline period SNF readmission measure rate and improvement score for that fiscal year;
units.action_summary: If a SNF has <25 eligible baseline stays but ≥25 in the performance period, CMS will not publicly report the SNF's baseline readmission rate and improvement score for that fiscal year.

units.obligation_text: If CMS determines that a SNF is a low-volume SNF with respect to a fiscal year and assigns a performance score to the SNF under paragraph (d)(3) of this section, CMS will not publicly report the SNF’s performance period SNF readmission measure rate, achievement score or improvement score for the fiscal year;
units.action_summary: If CMS classifies a SNF as low-volume for a fiscal year and assigns a performance score under paragraph (d)(3), CMS will not publicly report that SNF's performance period readmission rate, achievement score, or improvement score for that year.

units.obligation_text: If CMS determines that a SNF has zero eligible cases during the performance period with respect to a fiscal year, CMS will not publicly report any information for that SNF for that fiscal year.
units.action_summary: If a SNF has zero eligible cases in the performance period for a fiscal year, CMS will not publicly report any information for that SNF for that year.

units.obligation_text: Generally requires and can reasonably be expected to actively participate in, and benefit from, an intensive rehabilitation therapy program.
units.action_summary: Patient must require and be able to actively participate in and benefit from an intensive rehabilitation therapy program as a condition for IRF care.
units.modal_raw: requires and can reasonably be expected to

units.obligation_text: Under current industry standards, this intensive rehabilitation therapy program generally consists of at least 3 hours of therapy (physical therapy, occupational therapy, speech-language pathology, or prosthetics/orthotics therapy) per day at least 5 days per week.
units.action_summary: The intensive rehabilitation therapy program generally must provide at least 3 hours of specified therapies per day, at least 5 days per week.

units.obligation_text: In certain well-documented cases, this intensive rehabilitation therapy program might instead consist of at least 15 hours of intensive rehabilitation therapy per week.
units.action_summary: As an alternative in well-documented cases, the program may consist of at least 15 hours of intensive rehabilitation therapy per week.

units.obligation_text: Benefit from this intensive rehabilitation therapy program is demonstrated by measurable improvement that will be of practical value to the patient in improving the patient’s functional capacity or adaptation to impairments.
units.action_summary: Benefit must be shown by measurable improvement that has practical value in improving functional capacity or adaptation to impairments.

units.obligation_text: The required therapy treatments must begin within 36 hours from midnight of the day of admission to the IRF.
units.actor: the required therapy treatments / the treating provider
units.action_summary: Therapy treatments required for the program must commence within 36 hours from midnight of the day of IRF admission.

units.obligation_text: Requires physician supervision by a rehabilitation physician.
units.actor: the patient (as a condition of IRF care)
units.action_summary: Patient care requires medical supervision by a rehabilitation physician.

units.obligation_text: The requirement for medical supervision means that the rehabilitation physician must conduct face-to-face visits with the patient at least 3 days per week throughout the patient's stay in the IRF to assess the patient both medically and functionally, as well as to modify the course of treatment as needed to maximize the patient's capacity to benefit from the rehabilitation process.
units.action_summary: Rehabilitation physician must conduct face-to-face visits at least 3 days per week throughout the patient's IRF stay to assess medically and functionally and modify treatment as needed.

units.obligation_text: Except that during a Public Health Emergency, as defined in § 400.200 of this chapter, such visits may be conducted using telehealth services (as defined in section 1834(m)(4)(F) of the Act).

units.obligation_text: Except for subpoena requests being sent to a nonparty under § 405.1857(c), the reviewing entity may prescribe the method(s) by which a party must make a submission, including the requirement to use an electronic filing system for submission of documents.
units.action_summary: The reviewing entity may set methods for submissions and can require parties to use specified methods, including electronic filing; parties are required to use the prescribed method.

units.obligation_text: Such methods or instructions apply to any period of time or deadline prescribed or allowed under this subpart (for example, requests for appeal under §§ 405.1811(b), 405.1835(b), and 405.1837(c) and (e)) or authorized by a reviewing entity.
units.action_summary: Submission methods prescribed by the reviewing entity apply to any deadlines or periods under this subpart; parties must follow them.

units.obligation_text: All parties to a Board appeal are to familiarize themselves with the instructions for handling a Provider Reimbursement Review Board (PRRB) appeal, including any and all requirements related to the electronic/online filing of documents.
units.actor: all parties to a Board appeal
units.action_summary: Parties must familiarize themselves with PRRB appeal handling instructions and electronic filing requirements.

units.obligation_text: The requesting party must send any subpoena request submitted to the Board promptly to the party or nonparty subject to the subpoena, and to any other party to the Board appeal.
units.action_summary: The requesting party must promptly send subpoena requests to the subpoenaed party/nonparty and to other parties to the appeal.

units.obligation_text: If the subpoena request is being sent to a nonparty subject to the subpoena, then the subpoena request must be sent by certified mail.
units.action_summary: Subpoena requests sent to nonparties must be sent by certified mail.

units.obligation_text: The request must—
units.action_summary: The subpoena request must meet whatever additional requirements follow (placeholder indicating further required elements).

units.obligation_text: Under either prospective payment system, a hospital may keep the difference between its prospective payment rate and its operating or capital-related costs incurred in furnishing inpatient services...
units.action_summary: Hospitals are permitted to retain any amount by which payment exceeds their incurred costs.

units.obligation_text: CMS makes an adjustment to the standardized amount to ensure that the reasonable cost based payments for allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell acquisition costs are made in a manner so that aggregate payments to hospitals are not affected.
units.action_summary: CMS will adjust the standardized amount so reasonable cost-based payments for stem cell acquisition do not affect aggregate hospital payments.

units.obligation_text: For discharges occurring on or after October 1, 2020, the amount of payment for a discharge described in paragraph (b) of this section is adjusted as described in paragraph (c) of this section.
units.action_summary: For qualifying discharges on/after Oct 1, 2020, payment amounts must be adjusted per paragraph (c).

units.obligation_text: Except as provided for in paragraph (e)(3) of this section, CMS only considers, for add-on payments for a particular fiscal year, an application for which the new medical service or technology has received FDA marketing authorization by July 1 prior to the particular fiscal year.
units.action_summary: CMS will consider add-on payment applications only if the technology had FDA marketing authorization by July 1 prior to the fiscal year, unless paragraph (e)(3) applies.

units.obligation_text: A technology ... that does not receive FDA marketing authorization by the July 1 deadline ... may be conditionally approved for the new technology add-on payment for a particular fiscal year ... provided that FDA marketing authorization is granted before July 1 of the fiscal year for which the applicant applied for new technology add-on payments.
units.action_summary: CMS may conditionally approve an add-on payment for certain antimicrobial technologies that miss the July 1 deadline, provided FDA authorizes them before the fiscal year's July 1.

units.obligation_text: Unless a discharge case qualifies for outlier payment under § 412.84, Medicare will not pay any additional amount beyond the DRG payment plus -- (i) 65 percent ...; (ii) ... 75 percent ...; (iii) ... 75 percent ...
units.action_summary: Medicare is prohibited from paying amounts beyond specified DRG payment plus specified percentages unless outlier payment applies.

units.obligation_text: If the hospital’s cost reporting period ... is for less than 12 months or longer than 12 months, the hospital’s number of discharges for that cost reporting period will be annualized to estimate the total number of discharges for a 12-month cost reporting period.
units.action_summary: Hospitals must annualize discharge counts for cost reporting periods that are not 12 months to estimate a 12-month total.

units.obligation_text: CMS provides an additional payment to a hospital ... if the hospital has established that ESRD beneficiary discharges ... constitute 10 percent or more of its total Medicare discharges.
units.action_summary: CMS will give an additional payment when a hospital demonstrates ESRD discharges are 10%+ of its Medicare discharges; hospitals must establish this fact to qualify.

units.obligation_text: A subsection (d) hospital that furnishes allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplants is required to formulate a standard acquisition charge that approximates the hospital’s average cost of acquiring hematopoietic stem cells for all of its allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplants.
units.action_summary: Hospitals providing these transplants must set a standard acquisition charge approximating their average acquisition cost.

units.obligation_text: The hospital’s Medicare share of the allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell acquisition costs is based on the ratio ... which is applied to reasonable cost.
units.action_summary: The hospital's Medicare share is determined by applying the Medicare proportion of transplants to reasonable costs.

units.obligation_text: A subsection (d) hospital must maintain an itemized statement that identifies the services furnished in collecting hematopoietic stem cells, the charges, the person receiving the service (donor/recipient; if donor the provider must identify the prospective recipient), and the prospective recipient’s health care insurance number.
units.action_summary: Hospitals must keep an itemized statement with specified details for stem cell collection services.

units.obligation_text: An additional payment is made to a hospital in accordance with § 476.78 of this chapter for the costs of sending requested patient records to the QIO in electronic format, by facsimile, or by photocopying and mailing.
units.action_summary: CMS will make additional payments to hospitals for costs of sending requested patient records to the QIO in specified formats.

units.obligation_text: For hospital-specific data, the hospital must provide a weighted 3-year average of its average hourly wages using data from the CMS hospital wage survey used to construct the wage index in effect for prospective payment purposes.
units.action_summary: Hospitals must provide a weighted 3-year average of average hourly wages using CMS hospital wage survey data for reclassification purposes.

units.obligation_text: The hospital's request for review must be in writing and sent to the Administrator, in care of the Office of the Attorney Advisor. The request must be received by the Administrator within 15 days after the date the MGCRB issues its decision. The hospital must also submit an electronic copy of its request for review to CMS's Hospital and Ambulatory Policy Group.
units.action_summary: Hospitals must submit a written request for review to the Administrator within 15 days and also submit an electronic copy to CMS's Hospital and Ambulatory Policy Group.

units.obligation_text: For discharges occurring on or after October 1, 2020, in determining the payment amount under this section for certain clinical trial cases as described in § 412.85(b), the DRG weighting factor described in paragraph (b)(1) of this section is adjusted as described in § 412.85(c).
units.action_summary: For certain clinical trial cases on/after Oct 1, 2020, CMS must adjust the DRG weighting factor as specified.

units.obligation_text: The long-term care hospital prospective payment system standard Federal payment rate for a long-term care prospective payment system fiscal year is the standard Federal payment rate for the previous fiscal year updated by the percentage increase in the market basket index ... less a multifactor productivity adjustment ..., and further adjusted, as appropriate, as described in paragraph (d) of this section.
units.action_summary: CMS will set the LTCH standard Federal payment rate by updating the prior year's rate by market basket increase, subtracting a productivity adjustment, and applying other adjustments as appropriate.

units.obligation_text: The provider must furnish the contractor— Upon request, copies of patient service charge schedules and changes thereto as they are put into effect; and its median payer-specific negotiated charge by MS-DRG for payers that are Medicare Advantage (MA) organizations, and its median payer-specific negotiated charge by MS-DRG for all third party payers, as applicable, and changes thereto as they are put into effect.
units.action_summary: Providers must furnish the contractor, upon request, copies of patient service charge schedules and the median payer-specific negotiated charges by MS-DRG and changes as they take effect.

units.obligation_text: The contractor evaluates the charge schedules as specified in paragraph (d)(3)(i) of this section to determine the extent to which they may be used for determining program payment.
units.action_summary: The contractor must evaluate submitted charge schedules to determine their use in program payment calculations.

units.obligation_text: Effective for cost reporting periods beginning on or after October 1, 2020, Medicare bad debts must not be written off to a contractual allowance account but must be charged to an expense account for uncollectible accounts.
units.action_summary: Providers are prohibited from writing Medicare bad debts to contractual allowance accounts and must instead charge them to an uncollectible accounts expense account.

units.obligation_text: The provider must be able to establish that reasonable collection efforts were made.
units.action_summary: Providers are required to demonstrate they made reasonable collection efforts to collect debts.

units.obligation_text: A provider’s collection effort ... to collect Medicare deductible or coinsurance amounts must consist of all of the following: (1) Be similar to the collection effort put forth to collect comparable amounts from non-Medicare patients. (2) For cost reporting periods beginning before October 1, 2020, involve the issuance of a bill ... on or shortly after discharge or death. (3) For cost reporting periods beginning on or after October 1, 2020, involve the issuance of a bill ... on or before 120 days after the latter of the date of the Medicare remittance advice or the date of remittance advice from the beneficiary’s secondary payer. (4) Include other actions such as subsequent billings, collection letters and telephone calls or personal contacts ... constituting a genuine collection effort. (5)(i) Last at least 120 days after paragraph (e)(2)(i)(A)(2) or (3) ... before being written off as uncollectible ... (ii) Start a new 120-day collection period each time a partial payment is received within a 120-day collection period until the ...
units.action_summary: Providers' collection efforts must meet all listed elements: be comparable to non-Medicare collection efforts; issue bills within specified times; include follow-up actions; continue for at least 120 days before write-off; and restart the 120-day period after partial payments.

units.obligation_text: For purposes of a contractor hearing, if no contractor hearing officer is appointed (or none is currently presiding), the date of receipt of materials sent to the contractor hearing officer (as permitted under paragraph (d) of this section) is presumed to be, as applicable, the date that the contractor stamps "Received" on the materials, or the date of electronic delivery.

units.obligation_text: Under either prospective payment system, a hospital may keep the difference between its prospective payment rate and its operating or capital-related costs incurred in furnishing inpatient services...
units.action_summary: Permits hospitals to retain any surplus when prospective payments exceed incurred operating or capital costs.
