units.action_summary: Establishes that hospitals bear the financial risk for costs exceeding the prospective payment rate.

units.obligation_text: CMS makes an adjustment to the standardized amount to ensure that the reasonable cost based payments for allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell acquisition costs are made in a manner so that aggregate payments to hospitals are not affected.
units.action_summary: Requires CMS to adjust the standardized amount so reasonable-cost payments for allogeneic stem cell acquisition do not affect aggregate hospital payments.

units.obligation_text: For discharges occurring on or after October 1, 2020, the amount of payment for a discharge described in paragraph (b) of this section is adjusted as described in paragraph (c) of this section.
units.action_summary: States that payment amounts for specified discharges occurring on/after Oct 1, 2020, will be adjusted per §412.85(c).

units.obligation_text: Payment is adjusted in accordance with paragraph (c) of this section for discharges assigned to MS–DRG 018 that are part of a clinical trial as determined by CMS based on the reporting of a diagnosis code indicating the encounter is part of a clinical research program on the claim for the discharge.
units.action_summary: Specifies that discharges assigned to MS-DRG 018 that are part of clinical trials will have payments adjusted per paragraph (c).

units.obligation_text: The DRG weighting factor determined under § 412.60(b) is adjusted by a factor that reflects the average cost for cases to be assigned to MS–DRG 018 that are part of a clinical trial to the average cost for cases to be assigned to MS–DRG 018 that are not part of a clinical trial.
units.action_summary: Requires adjustment of the DRG weighting factor by a cost-ratio reflecting clinical-trial vs non-clinical-trial MS-DRG 018 cases.

units.obligation_text: Except as provided for in paragraph (e)(3) of this section, CMS only considers, for add-on payments for a particular fiscal year, an application for which the new medical service or technology has received FDA marketing authorization by July 1 prior to the particular fiscal year.
units.action_summary: Conditions CMS consideration for add-on payments on FDA marketing authorization being received by July 1 before the fiscal year, except as provided in (e)(3).

units.obligation_text: A technology for which an application is submitted under an alternative pathway for certain antimicrobial products under paragraph (d) of this section that does not receive FDA marketing authorization by the July 1 deadline specified in paragraph (e)(2) of this section may be conditionally approved for the new technology add-on payment for a particular fiscal year, effective for discharges beginning in the first quarter after FDA marketing authorization is granted...
units.action_summary: Permits CMS to conditionally approve certain antimicrobial technologies for add-on payments even if FDA authorization missed the July 1 deadline, subject to conditions.

units.obligation_text: ...provided that FDA marketing authorization is granted before July 1 of the fiscal year for which the applicant applied for new technology add-on payments.
units.action_summary: Condition for conditional approval: FDA authorization must be granted before July 1 of the fiscal year for which application was made.

units.obligation_text: For cost reporting periods beginning on or after October 1, 2020, in the case of a subsection (d) hospital that furnishes an allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant to an individual, payment to such hospital for hematopoietic stem cell acquisition costs is made on a reasonable cost basis.
units.action_summary: Requires that payment for allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell acquisition costs be made on a reasonable cost basis for applicable hospitals and periods.

units.obligation_text: Allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell acquisition costs recognized under this paragraph (e) are costs of acquiring hematopoietic stem cells from a donor. These costs are as follows: (i) Registry fees from a national donor registry described in 42 U.S.C. 274k, if applicable, for stem cells from an unrelated donor. (ii) Tissue typing of donor and recipient. (iii) Donor evaluation. (iv) Physician pre-admission/pre-procedure donor evaluation services. (v) Costs associated with the collection procedure (for example, general routine and special care services, procedure/operating room and other ancillary services, apheresis services). (vi) Post-operative/post-procedure evaluation of donor. (vii) Preparation and processing of peripheral blood stem cells, or cord blood (but not including embryonic stem cells).
units.actor: subsection (d) hospital; CMS (as payer defining covered costs)
units.action_summary: Specifies the categories of donor acquisition costs that are recognized as allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell acquisition costs for payment on a reasonable cost basis.

units.obligation_text: The hospital’s Medicare share of the allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell acquisition costs is based on the ratio of the number of its allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplants furnished to Medicare beneficiaries to the total number of its allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplants furnished to all patients, regardless of payer, which is applied to reasonable cost.
units.action_summary: Specifies how to calculate the Medicare share of acquisition costs (ratio of Medicare-transplants to total transplants applied to reasonable cost).

units.obligation_text: A subsection (d) hospital must maintain an itemized statement that identifies the services furnished in collecting hematopoietic stem cells, the charges, the person receiving the service (donor/recipient; if donor the provider must identify the prospective recipient), and the prospective recipient’s health care insurance number.
units.action_summary: Requires hospitals that furnish allogeneic transplants to keep an itemized statement identifying services, charges, donor/recipient info, and prospective recipient insurance number.

units.obligation_text: The hospital must also submit an electronic copy of its request for review to CMS’s Hospital and Ambulatory Policy Group.
units.action_summary: Requires hospitals to also submit an electronic copy of the request for review to CMS's specified group.

units.obligation_text: For discharges occurring on or after October 1, 2020, in determining the payment amount under this section for certain clinical trial cases as described in § 412.85(b), the DRG weighting factor described in paragraph (b)(1) of this section is adjusted as described in § 412.85(c).
units.action_summary: Requires adjustment of the DRG weighting factor when determining payment for certain clinical trial cases per §412.85(c).

units.obligation_text: An additional payment is made to a hospital in accordance with § 476.78 of this chapter for the costs of sending requested patient records to the QIO in electronic format, by facsimile, or by photocopying and mailing.
units.action_summary: Provides that an additional payment will be made to hospitals for costs of sending requested patient records to the QIO in specified formats.

units.action_summary: Requires providers to furnish specified information to the contractor upon request.

units.obligation_text: Upon request, copies of patient service charge schedules and changes thereto as they are put into effect;

units.obligation_text: Its median payer-specific negotiated charge by MS–DRG for payers that are Medicare Advantage (MA) organizations, and its median payer-specific negotiated charge by MS–DRG for all third party payers, as applicable, and changes thereto as they are put into effect.
units.action_summary: Requires providers to furnish median payer-specific negotiated charges by MS–DRG for MA and third-party payers and updates when effective.

units.obligation_text: For cost reporting periods beginning on or after October 1, 2020, bad debts are amounts considered to be uncollectible from patient accounts that were created or acquired in providing services and are categorized as implicit price concessions for cost reporting purposes and are recorded in the provider’s accounting records as a component of net patient revenue.
units.action_summary: Requires that, for specified cost reporting periods, bad debts be treated as implicit price concessions and recorded in accounting records as part of net patient revenue.

units.obligation_text: For child support enforcement services beginning February 9, 2018, the provider certifies that before billing Medicaid, if the provider has billed a third party, the provider has waited 100 days from the date of the service and has not received payment from the third party.
units.action_summary: Provider must certify that, before billing Medicaid for child support enforcement services (if they billed a third party), they waited 100 days and did not receive payment from the third party.

units.obligation_text: Contracts that obligate MCOs, MCEs, PIHPs or PAHPs to provide coverage of covered outpatient drugs must include the following requirements:

units.obligation_text: The MCO, MCE, PIHP or PAHP must operate a drug utilization review program that complies with the requirements described in section 1927(g) of the Act and part 456, subpart K of this chapter, as if such requirement applied to the MCO, MCE, PIHP, or PAHP instead of the State.

units.action_summary: MCO/MCE/PIHP/PAHP must annually give the State a detailed description of its DUR program activities.

units.obligation_text: The primary manufacturer must exclude from its calculation of AMP any sales of authorized generic drugs to wholesalers for drugs distributed to retail community pharmacies when reporting the AMP of the brand name drug of that authorized generic drug.
units.action_summary: Primary manufacturer is required to exclude sales of authorized generics to wholesalers for retail community pharmacy distribution when calculating AMP for the brand name drug.

units.obligation_text: Limit on rebate. In no case will the total rebate amount exceed 100 percent of the AMP of the single source or multiple source innovator drug.
units.actor: the total rebate amount (as applied by rebate calculation parties)
units.action_summary: The total rebate amount cannot exceed 100% of the AMP for single source or innovator multiple source drugs.

units.obligation_text: Additional rebate for noninnovator multiple source drugs. In addition to the basic rebate described in paragraph (a)(6) of this section, for each dosage form and strength of a noninnovator multiple source drug, the rebate amount will be increased by an amount equal to the product of the following:
units.actor: the rebate calculation (parties responsible for rebate computation)
units.action_summary: For each dosage form/strength of a noninnovator multiple source drug, the rebate amount must be increased by a calculated product specified in subparts.

units.obligation_text: The total number of units of such dosage form and strength paid for under the State plan in the rebate period.
units.actor: the rebate calculation (parties responsible for rebate computation)
units.action_summary: One factor of the additional rebate calculation is the total number of units of that dosage form/strength paid under the State plan during the rebate period.

units.obligation_text: The amount, if any, by which: (A) The AMP for the dosage form and strength of the drug for the period exceeds: (B) The base date AMP for such dosage form and strength, increased by the percentage by which the consumer price index for all urban consumers (United States city average) for the month before the month in which the rebate period begins exceeds such index associated with the base date AMP of the drug.
units.actor: the rebate calculation (parties responsible for rebate computation)
units.action_summary: The other factor of the additional rebate is the amount by which current AMP exceeds the CPI-adjusted base date AMP for that dosage/strength.

units.obligation_text: The AMP for the dosage form and strength of the drug for the period.
units.actor: the rebate calculation (parties responsible for rebate computation)
units.action_summary: Part (A) of the calculation specifies using the current AMP for the dosage form and strength.

units.obligation_text: The base date AMP for such dosage form and strength, increased by the percentage by which the consumer price index for all urban consumers (United States city average) for the month before the month in which the rebate period begins exceeds such index associated with the base date AMP of the drug.
units.actor: the rebate calculation (parties responsible for rebate computation)
units.action_summary: Part (B) of the calculation specifies the CPI-inflation-adjusted base date AMP to be used in the comparison.

units.obligation_text: Total rebate. The total rebate amount for noninnovator multiple source drugs is equal to the basic rebate amount plus the additional rebate amount, if any.
units.actor: the rebate calculation (parties responsible for rebate computation)
units.action_summary: Total rebate for noninnovator multiple source drugs must be calculated as basic rebate plus any additional rebate.

units.obligation_text: Limit on rebate. In no case will the total rebate amount exceed 100 percent of the AMP for the noninnovator multiple source drug.
units.actor: the total rebate amount (as applied by rebate calculation parties)
units.action_summary: The total rebate for a noninnovator multiple source drug cannot exceed 100% of its AMP.

units.obligation_text: The change is a result of a VBP arrangement, as defined in § 447.502, requiring the manufacturer to make changes outside of the 12-quarter rule, when the outcome must be evaluated outside of the 12-quarter period.
units.action_summary: A manufacturer is required to make changes outside the 12-quarter rule when a VBP arrangement necessitates evaluating outcomes outside the 12-quarter period.

units.obligation_text: On a quarterly basis, the State must submit drug utilization data to CMS, which will be the same information as submitted to the manufacturers on the CMS–R–144, as specified in paragraph (a) of this section. The state data submission will be due no later than 60 days after the end of each rebate period.
units.action_summary: State must submit quarterly drug utilization data to CMS (same as CMS–R–144), and submissions are due no later than 60 days after the end of each rebate period.

units.obligation_text: The state data submission will be due no later than 60 days after the end of each rebate period.
units.action_summary: State submissions of drug utilization data must be submitted within 60 days after each rebate period ends.
units.modal_raw: will be due no later than

units.obligation_text: In the event that a due date falls on a weekend or Federal holiday, the submission will be due on the first business day following that weekend or Federal holiday.
units.action_summary: If the due date is a weekend or Federal holiday, the State's submission deadline is the next business day.

units.obligation_text: Any adjustments to previously submitted data will be transmitted to the manufacturer and CMS in the same reporting period.
units.action_summary: State must transmit any adjustments to previously submitted data to manufacturers and CMS within the same reporting period.

units.obligation_text: Each data submission in this section must be certified by one of the following:
units.action_summary: Every data submission must be certified by an eligible official or delegated authority listed in the following subparts.

units.obligation_text: The State Medicaid Director (SMD).
units.action_summary: An SMD is an authorized person to certify the state's data submission.

units.obligation_text: The Deputy State Medicaid Director (DSMD).
units.action_summary: A DSMD is an authorized person to certify the state's data submission.

units.obligation_text: An individual other than the SMD or DSMD, who has authority equivalent to an SMD or DSMD.
units.actor: an individual with authority equivalent to SMD/DSMD
units.action_summary: An individual with authority equivalent to SMD or DSMD may certify the state's data submission.

units.obligation_text: An individual with the directly delegated authority to perform the certification on behalf of an individual described in paragraphs (d)(1) through (3) of this section.
units.actor: an individual with directly delegated authority
units.action_summary: An individual delegated authority by the SMD/DSMD or equivalent may certify the state's data submission.

units.obligation_text: Each data submission by a state must include the following certification language: "I hereby certify, to the best of my knowledge, that the state’s data submission is complete and accurate at the time of this submission, and was prepared in accordance with the state’s good faith, reasonable efforts based on existing guidance from CMS, section 1927 of the Act and applicable federal regulations. I further certify that the state has transmitted data to CMS, including any adjustments to previous rebate periods, in the same reporting period as provided to the manufacturer. Further, the state certifies that it has applied any necessary edits to the data for both CMS and the labeler to avoid inaccuracies at both the NDC/line item and file/aggregate level. Such edits are to be applied in the same manner and in the same reporting period to both CMS and the manufacturer."
units.action_summary: Each state data submission must include the specified certification language attesting to completeness, accuracy, adherence to guidance, timely transmission of adjustments, and application of necessary edits.

units.obligation_text: A State participating in value-based purchasing arrangements must report data described in paragraph (d)(2) of this section on an annual basis.
units.actor: a State participating in VBP arrangements
units.action_summary: States in VBP arrangements are required to annually report the data specified in paragraph (d)(2).

units.obligation_text: Within 60 days of the end of each year, the State must submit all of the following data:
units.action_summary: States must submit specified VBP-related data within 60 days after year end.

units.obligation_text: State.
units.action_summary: The submission must include the State identifier.

units.obligation_text: National drug code(s) (for drugs covered under the VBP).
units.action_summary: The submission must include NDC(s) for drugs covered under the VBP.

units.obligation_text: Product FDA list name.
units.action_summary: The submission must include the product's FDA list name.

units.obligation_text: Number of prescriptions.
units.action_summary: The submission must include the number of prescriptions.

units.obligation_text: Cost to the State to administer VBP (for example, systems changes, tracking outcomes, etc.).
units.action_summary: The submission must include the State's administrative costs to implement VBP.

units.obligation_text: Total savings generated by the supplemental rebate due to VBP.
units.action_summary: The submission must include total savings generated by supplemental rebate attributable to VBP.

units.obligation_text: Minimum standards. In operating their DUR programs, states must include the following minimum standards:
units.action_summary: States are required to include specified minimum standards when operating their DUR programs.

units.obligation_text: Prospective safety edit limitations for opioid prescriptions, as specified by the State, on:
units.action_summary: States must establish prospective safety edit limits for opioid prescriptions as specified, covering several sub-elements.

units.obligation_text: Days’ supply for patients not currently receiving opioid therapy for initial prescription fills;
units.action_summary: States must set prospective safety edits limiting days' supply for initial opioid prescriptions to patients not currently receiving opioid therapy.

units.obligation_text: Quantity of prescription dispensed for initial and subsequent prescription fills;
units.action_summary: States must set prospective safety edits limiting the quantity dispensed for initial and subsequent opioid fills.

units.obligation_text: Therapeutically-duplicative initial and subsequent opioid prescription fills; and
units.action_summary: States must set prospective safety edits to prevent therapeutically duplicative opioid prescriptions.

units.obligation_text: Early refills, for subsequent prescription fills.
units.action_summary: States must set prospective safety edits addressing early refills for subsequent opioid fills.

units.obligation_text: Prospective safety edit limitations for opioid prescriptions, as specified by the State, on the maximum daily morphine milligram equivalent for treatment of chronic pain, for initial and subsequent prescription fills.
units.action_summary: States must set prospective safety edit limits on maximum daily morphine milligram equivalents for chronic pain for initial and subsequent opioid fills.

units.obligation_text: A retrospective claims review automated process that indicates prescription fills of opioids in excess of the prospective safety edit limitations specified by the state under paragraphs (h)(1)(i) or (ii) of this section to provide for the ongoing review of opioid claims data to identify patterns of fraud, abuse, excessive utilization, inappropriate or medically unnecessary care, or prescribing or billing practices that indicate abuse or provision of inappropriate or medically unnecessary care among prescribers, pharmacists and individuals receiving Medicaid benefits.
units.action_summary: States must implement an automated retrospective claims review process to flag opioid fills exceeding prospective safety edits and to identify patterns of fraud, abuse, excessive or inappropriate utilization.

units.obligation_text: A retrospective claims review automated process and, at the option of the state, prospective safety edits that monitor when an individual is concurrently prescribed opioids and: (A) Benzodiazepines; or (B) Antipsychotics.
units.action_summary: States must have a retrospective claims review (and may add prospective edits) to monitor concurrent prescribing of opioids with benzodiazepines or antipsychotics.

units.obligation_text: Benzodiazepines;
units.action_summary: States must monitor concurrent opioid and benzodiazepine prescriptions.

units.obligation_text: Antipsychotics.
units.action_summary: States must monitor concurrent opioid and antipsychotic prescriptions.

units.obligation_text: A program to monitor and manage the appropriate use of antipsychotic medications by children enrolled under the State plan, including any Medicaid expansion groups for the Children’s Health Insurance Program (CHIP).
units.action_summary: States must implement a program to monitor and manage appropriate antipsychotic use among children enrolled in the State plan and CHIP expansion groups.

units.obligation_text: A process to identify potential fraud or abuse of controlled substances by individuals enrolled under the State plan, health care providers prescribing drugs to individuals so enrolled, and pharmacies dispensing drugs to individuals so enrolled.
units.action_summary: States must have a process to identify potential controlled-substance fraud or abuse by enrollees, prescribers, and dispensing pharmacies.

units.obligation_text: Prospective safety edits, retrospective claims review automated processes, or a combination of these approaches as determined by the state, to identify when: (A) A beneficiary is prescribed an opioid after the beneficiary has been prescribed one or more drugs used for Medication Assisted Treatment (MAT) of an opioid use disorder or has been diagnosed with an opioid use disorder, within a timeframe specified by the state, in the absence of a new indication to support utilization of opioids (such as new cancer diagnosis or entry into hospice care); and (B) A beneficiary could be at high risk of opioid overdose and should be considered for co-prescription or co-dispensing of naloxone.
units.action_summary: States must use prospective edits, retrospective review, or both to identify beneficiaries prescribed opioids under concerning circumstances (post-MAT or opioid use disorder diagnoses) and those at high overdose risk for naloxone consideration.

units.obligation_text: A beneficiary is prescribed an opioid after the beneficiary has been prescribed one or more drugs used for Medication Assisted Treatment (MAT) of an opioid use disorder or has been diagnosed with an opioid use disorder, within a timeframe specified by the state, in the absence of a new indication to support utilization of opioids (such as new cancer diagnosis or entry into hospice care);
units.action_summary: States must identify beneficiaries who receive opioids after MAT drugs or an opioid use disorder diagnosis within a state-specified timeframe absent a new justification.

units.obligation_text: A beneficiary could be at high risk of opioid overdose and should be considered for co-prescription or co-dispensing of naloxone.
units.action_summary: States must identify beneficiaries at high overdose risk and consider co-prescribing or co-dispensing naloxone.

units.obligation_text: The requirements in paragraphs (h)(1)(i) through (vii) of this section do not apply with respect to individuals receiving hospice or palliative care or treatment for cancer; individuals who are residents of long-term care facilities, intermediate care facilities for the intellectually disabled, or facilities that dispense frequently abused drugs through a contract with a single pharmacy; or other individuals the state elects to exempt.
units.action_summary: The minimum DUR requirements in (h)(1)(i)-(vii) do not apply to specified exempt categories of individuals.

units.obligation_text: While States are not required to apply these requirements with respect to these individuals, States may elect to do so.
units.action_summary: States have the option to apply the requirements to exempted individuals even though they are not required to.

units.obligation_text: Individuals receiving hospice or palliative care or treatment for cancer.
units.action_summary: Individuals in hospice/palliative care or receiving cancer treatment are exempt from the (h)(1)(i)-(vii) requirements unless the State elects otherwise.

units.obligation_text: Individuals who are residents of long-term care facilities, intermediate care facilities for the intellectually disabled, or facilities that dispense frequently abused drugs through a contract with a single pharmacy.
units.action_summary: Residents of specified facilities are exempt from the (h)(1)(i)-(vii) requirements unless the State elects otherwise.

units.obligation_text: Other individuals the state elects to exempt.
units.action_summary: States may choose to exempt other categories of individuals from the (h)(1)(i)-(vii) requirements.

units.obligation_text: All FFS and managed care DUR reports received by CMS under paragraph (b) of this section and, as applicable, pursuant to § 438.3(s) of this chapter, will be publicly posted on a website maintained by CMS for the sharing of reports and other information concerning Medicaid DUR programs.
units.action_summary: CMS will publicly post all received FFS and managed care DUR reports (and applicable reports under § 438.3(s)) on a CMS-maintained website.

title: CY 2021 Home Health Prospective Payment System Rate Update Quality Reporting Requirements (CMS-1730-P)

units.obligation_text: An individualized plan of care must be established and periodically reviewed by the certifying physician or allowed practitioner.
units.action_summary: Establish and periodically review an individualized plan of care.

units.obligation_text: The HHA must be acting upon a plan of care that meets the requirements of this section for HHA services to be covered.
units.action_summary: HHAs must act on a compliant plan of care for services to be covered.

units.obligation_text: The plan of care must include all of the following:
units.actor: plan of care / certifying clinician / HHA
units.action_summary: The plan of care must include the specified elements listed in subparagraphs (A)–(C).

units.obligation_text: The identification of the responsible discipline(s) and the frequency and duration of all visits as well as those items listed in § 484.60(a) of this chapter that establish the need for such services.
units.actor: plan of care / certifying clinician / HHA
units.action_summary: Include responsible disciplines and visit frequency/duration and items from § 484.60(a) that establish need.

units.obligation_text: Any provision of remote patient monitoring or other services furnished via a telecommunications system and such services must be tied to the patient-specific needs as identified in the comprehensive assessment, cannot substitute for a home visit ordered as part of the plan of care, and cannot be considered a home visit for the purposes of patient eligibility or payment.
units.actor: plan of care / certifying clinician / HHA / providers furnishing telecommunication services
units.action_summary: Remote patient monitoring/telehealth services included on the plan must be tied to patient-specific needs, may not substitute for ordered home visits, and may not be considered a home visit for eligibility/payment.

units.obligation_text: Such services must be tied to the patient-specific needs as identified in the comprehensive assessment.
units.actor: providers furnishing remote patient monitoring/telecommunications services
units.action_summary: Tie remote patient monitoring/telecommunications services to patient-specific needs identified in the comprehensive assessment.

units.obligation_text: Such services cannot substitute for a home visit ordered as part of the plan of care.
units.action_summary: Remote/telecommunications services may not be used in place of an ordered home visit.

units.obligation_text: Such services cannot be considered a home visit for the purposes of patient eligibility or payment.
units.actor: providers/home health agencies / Medicare payment/eligibility determinations
units.action_summary: Remote/telecommunications services cannot count as a home visit for eligibility or payment.

units.obligation_text: A description of how the use of such technology will help to achieve the goals outlined on the plan of care.
units.actor: plan of care / certifying clinician / HHA
units.action_summary: Include a description of how the technology use will help achieve plan of care goals.

units.obligation_text: All care provided must be in accordance with the plan of care.
units.action_summary: All provided care must follow the established plan of care.

units.obligation_text: Telecommunications technology, as indicated on the plan of care, can include: remote patient monitoring, defined as the collection of physiologic data (for example, ECG, blood pressure, glucose monitoring) digitally stored and/or transmitted by the patient or caregiver or both to the home health agency; teletypewriter (TTY) technology; and 2-way audio-video telecommunications technology that allows for real-time interaction between the patient and clinician.
units.actor: home health agencies / providers furnishing telecommunications technology
units.action_summary: Telecommunications technology indicated on the plan may include remote monitoring, TTY, and 2-way audio-video allowing real-time patient-clinician interaction.

units.obligation_text: The costs of any equipment, set-up, and service related to the technology are allowable only as administrative costs.
units.actor: home health agencies / Medicare billing entities
units.action_summary: Costs for equipment, setup, and related services for telecommunications technology are allowed only as administrative costs.

units.obligation_text: Visits to a beneficiary's home for the sole purpose of supplying, connecting, or training the patient on the technology, without the provision of a skilled service, are not separately billable.
units.action_summary: Home visits solely for supplying/connecting/training on technology (without skilled service) may not be billed separately.

units.obligation_text: Services that are covered under the home infusion therapy benefit as outlined at § 486.525 of this chapter, including any home infusion therapy services furnished to a Medicare beneficiary that is under a home health plan of care, are excluded from coverage under the Medicare home health benefit.
units.action_summary: Services covered under the home infusion therapy benefit are excluded from Medicare home health benefit coverage.

units.obligation_text: Services for the provision of drugs and biologicals not covered under this definition may continue to be provided under the Medicare home health benefit.
units.action_summary: Providers may continue to provide drugs/biologicals not covered by the home infusion definition under the Medicare home health benefit.

units.obligation_text: The home infusion therapy supplier must be enrolled in Medicare consistent with the provisions of § 424.68 and part 424, subpart P of this chapter.
units.action_summary: Home infusion therapy suppliers must be enrolled in Medicare consistent with § 424.68 and part 424 subpart P to qualify for payment.

units.obligation_text: For purposes of this section, a home infusion therapy supplier means a supplier of home infusion therapy that meets all of the following requirements:
units.actor: supplier seeking designation as home infusion therapy supplier
units.action_summary: To be considered a home infusion therapy supplier, a supplier must meet the listed requirements.

units.obligation_text: Furnishes infusion therapy to individuals with acute or chronic conditions requiring administration of home infusion drugs.
units.action_summary: Supplier must furnish infusion therapy to individuals with acute or chronic conditions requiring home infusion drugs.

units.obligation_text: Ensures the safe and effective provision and administration of home infusion therapy on a 7-day-a-week, 24-hour-a-day basis.
units.action_summary: Supplier must ensure safe and effective home infusion therapy provision 24/7.

units.obligation_text: Is accredited by an organization designated by the Secretary in accordance with section 1834(u)(5) of the Act.
units.action_summary: Supplier must be accredited by a Secretary-designated organization per section 1834(u)(5).

units.obligation_text: Is enrolled in Medicare as a home infusion therapy supplier consistent with the provisions of this section and of part 424, subpart P of this chapter.
units.action_summary: Supplier must be enrolled in Medicare consistent with § 424.68 and part 424 subpart P.

units.obligation_text: For a supplier to receive Medicare payment for the provision of home infusion therapy supplier services, the supplier must qualify as a home infusion therapy supplier (as defined in this section) and be in compliance with all applicable provisions of this section and of part 424, subpart P of this chapter.
units.action_summary: Supplier must qualify as a home infusion therapy supplier and comply with applicable provisions to receive Medicare payment.

units.obligation_text: To enroll in the Medicare program as a home infusion therapy supplier, a home infusion therapy supplier must meet all of the following requirements:
units.action_summary: Suppliers must meet the following specific enrollment requirements.

units.obligation_text: Fully complete and submit the Form CMS-855B application (or its electronic or successor application) to its applicable Medicare contractor.
units.action_summary: Fully complete and submit Form CMS-855B to the applicable Medicare contractor.

units.obligation_text: Certify via the Form CMS-855B that the home infusion therapy supplier meets and will continue to meet the specific requirements and standards for enrollment described in this section and in part 424, subpart P of this chapter.
units.action_summary: Certify on Form CMS-855B that the supplier meets and will continue to meet enrollment requirements and standards.

units.obligation_text: Comply with the application fee requirements in § 424.514.
units.action_summary: Comply with the application fee requirements in § 424.514.

units.obligation_text: Be currently and validly accredited as a home infusion therapy supplier by a CMS-recognized home infusion therapy supplier accreditation organization.
units.action_summary: Be currently and validly accredited by a CMS-recognized accreditation organization.

units.obligation_text: Comply with § 414.1515 of this chapter and all provisions of part 486, subpart I of this chapter.
units.action_summary: Comply with § 414.1515 and all provisions of part 486, subpart I.

units.obligation_text: Successfully complete the limited categorical risk level of screening under § 424.518 of this title.
units.action_summary: Successfully complete limited categorical risk level screening under § 424.518.

units.obligation_text: CMS may deny a supplier’s enrollment application as a home infusion therapy supplier on either of the following grounds:
units.action_summary: CMS may deny enrollment applications for home infusion therapy suppliers on specified grounds.

units.obligation_text: The supplier does not meet all of the requirements for enrollment outlined in § 424.68 and in part 424, subpart P of this chapter.
units.action_summary: Failure to meet enrollment requirements is a ground for CMS to deny enrollment.

units.obligation_text: Any of the applicable denial reasons in § 424.530.
units.action_summary: Any applicable denial reason in § 424.530 is a ground for denying enrollment.

units.obligation_text: A supplier may appeal the denial of its enrollment application as a home infusion therapy supplier under part 498 of this chapter.
units.action_summary: Suppliers may appeal enrollment denials under part 498.

units.obligation_text: Upon and after enrollment, a home infusion therapy supplier --
units.action_summary: Upon and after enrollment, the home infusion therapy supplier is subject to the following continuing obligations.

units.obligation_text: Must remain currently and validly accredited as described in paragraph (c)(3) of this section.
units.action_summary: Remain currently and validly accredited as required under paragraph (c)(3).

units.obligation_text: Remains subject to, and must remain in full compliance with, all of the provisions of-- (A) This section; (B) Part 424, subpart P of this chapter; (C) Section 414.1515 of this chapter; and (D) Part 486, subpart I of this chapter.
units.action_summary: Remain subject to and in full compliance with specified provisions (this section, part 424 subpart P, § 414.1515, part 486 subpart I).

units.obligation_text: This section.
units.action_summary: Comply with the requirements of § 424.68.

units.obligation_text: Part 424, subpart P of this chapter.
units.action_summary: Comply with part 424, subpart P.

units.obligation_text: Section 414.1515 of this chapter.
units.action_summary: Comply with § 414.1515.

units.obligation_text: Part 486, subpart I of this chapter.
units.action_summary: Comply with part 486, subpart I.

units.obligation_text: CMS may revoke a home infusion therapy supplier’s enrollment on any of the following grounds:
units.action_summary: CMS may revoke enrollment for specified grounds.

units.obligation_text: The supplier does not meet the accreditation requirements as described in paragraph (c)(3) of this section.
units.action_summary: Failure to meet accreditation requirements is a ground for CMS to revoke enrollment.

units.obligation_text: The supplier does not comply with all of the provisions of-- (A) This section; (B) Part 424, subpart P of this chapter; (C) Section 414.1515 of this chapter; and (D) Part 486, subpart I of this chapter.
units.action_summary: Noncompliance with the listed provisions is a ground for CMS to revoke enrollment.

units.obligation_text: This section.
units.action_summary: Compliance with § 424.68 is required; failure is ground for revocation.

units.obligation_text: Part 424, subpart P of this chapter.
units.action_summary: Compliance with part 424 subpart P is required; failure is ground for revocation.

units.obligation_text: Section 414.1515 of this chapter.
units.action_summary: Compliance with § 414.1515 is required; failure is ground for revocation.

units.obligation_text: Part 486, subpart I of this chapter.
units.action_summary: Compliance with part 486 subpart I is required; failure is ground for revocation.

units.obligation_text: Any of the revocation reasons in § 424.535 applies.
units.action_summary: Application of any revocation reasons in § 424.535 is a ground for CMS to revoke enrollment.

units.obligation_text: A home infusion therapy supplier may appeal the revocation of its enrollment under part 498 of this chapter.
units.action_summary: Suppliers may appeal enrollment revocations under part 498.

units.obligation_text: Home infusion therapy suppliers.
units.action_summary: Identifies home infusion therapy suppliers within the screening levels list.

units.obligation_text: Physicians, non-physician practitioners, physician and non-physician practitioner organizations, ambulance suppliers, opioid treatment programs, and home infusion therapy suppliers may retrospectively bill for services when the physician, non-physician practitioner, physician or non-physician organization, ambulance supplier, opioid treatment program, or home infusion therapy supplier has met all program requirements, including State licensure requirements, and services were provided at the enrolled practice location for up to --

units.obligation_text: Except as provided in paragraph (f) of this section and unless extraordinary circumstances justify an exception, to receive the low-volume adjustment an ESRD facility must provide an attestation statement, by November 1st of each year preceding the payment year, to its Medicare Administrative Contractor (MAC) that the facility meets all the criteria established in this section, except that:
units.action_summary: Provide an attestation to its MAC by November 1 each year preceding the payment year that it meets all criteria for the low-volume adjustment.

units.obligation_text: For payment year 2012, the attestation must be provided by January 3, 2012;
units.action_summary: Provide the attestation by January 3, 2012 for payment year 2012.

units.obligation_text: For payment year 2015, the attestation must be provided by December 31, 2014;
units.action_summary: Provide the attestation by December 31, 2014 for payment year 2015.

units.obligation_text: For payment year 2016, the attestation must be provided by December 31, 2015;
units.action_summary: Provide the attestation by December 31, 2015 for payment year 2016.

units.obligation_text: For payment year 2021, the attestation must be provided by December 31, 2020.
units.action_summary: Provide the attestation by December 31, 2020 for payment year 2021.

units.obligation_text: To receive the low-volume adjustment, an ESRD facility must include in their attestation provided pursuant to paragraph (e) of this section a statement that the ESRD facility meets the definition of a low-volume facility in paragraph (b) of this section.
units.action_summary: Include in the attestation a statement that the facility meets the low-volume definition in paragraph (b).

units.obligation_text: Furnished less than 4,000 treatments in each of the 3 cost reporting years (based on as-filed or final settled 12-consecutive month cost reports, whichever is most recent, except as specified in paragraph (g)(4) of this section) preceding the payment year;
units.actor: the ESRD facility (as the entity defined as low-volume)
units.action_summary: To meet the low-volume definition, the facility must have furnished fewer than 4,000 treatments in each of the three prior cost reporting years.

units.obligation_text: For payment years 2021, 2022, and 2023, the attestation specified in paragraph (e)(4) of this section must indicate that the ESRD facility meets all the criteria specified in this section, except that, for a facility that would not otherwise meet the number of treatments criterion specified in paragraph (b)(1) of this section because of the COVID-19 PHE, the facility may attest that it furnished less than 2,000 treatments in any six months during the cost-reporting period ending in 2020.
units.action_summary: For PYs 2021–2023, the attestation must state the facility meets all criteria; facilities affected by the COVID-19 PHE may instead attest they furnished <2,000 treatments in any six months during the 2020 cost-reporting period.

units.obligation_text: For a facility that would not otherwise meet the number of treatments criterion specified in paragraph (b)(1) of this section because of the COVID-19 PHE, the facility may attest that it furnished less than 2,000 treatments in any six months during the cost-reporting period ending in 2020.
units.action_summary: Permits a facility affected by the COVID-19 PHE to attest it furnished fewer than 2,000 treatments in any six-month period in 2020 as an alternative to meeting the 4,000-treatment criterion.

units.obligation_text: The facility must also attest that it furnished treatments equal to or in excess of 4,000 in the payment year due to temporary patient shifting as a result of the COVID-19 PHE;
units.actor: an ESRD facility that so attests under the COVID-19 exception
units.action_summary: If using the COVID-19 exception, the facility must also attest that it furnished ≥4,000 treatments in the payment year because of temporary patient shifting due to the PHE.

units.obligation_text: The MAC relies on the attestation and multiplies the total number of treatments for the 6 months period by 2.
units.action_summary: When a facility attests under the COVID-19 exception, the MAC will rely on that attestation and multiply the total treatments in the six-month period by 2 for eligibility verification.

units.obligation_text: When an ESRD facility provides an attestation in accordance with paragraph (e) of this section, for the third eligibility year, the MAC verifies the as-filed cost report and takes one of the following actions:
units.action_summary: Upon receipt of the attestation for the third eligibility year, the MAC must verify the as-filed cost report and then take the appropriate action based on its determination.

units.obligation_text: If the MAC determines an ESRD facility meets the definition of a low-volume facility as described in paragraph (b) of this section, CMS adjusts the low-volume facility’s base rate for the entire payment year;
units.action_summary: If MAC determines facility meets low-volume definition, CMS will adjust the facility's base rate for the entire payment year.

units.obligation_text: If the MAC determines an ESRD facility does not meet the definition of a low-volume facility as described in paragraph (b) of this section, the MAC reprocesses claims and recoups low-volume adjustments paid during the payment year.
units.action_summary: If MAC determines facility does not meet the low-volume definition, the MAC must reprocess claims and recoup low-volume adjustments paid during that year.

units.obligation_text: Methodology for modifying the ESRD PPS base rate to account for the costs of calcimimetics in the ESRD PPS bundled payment. Beginning January 1, 2021, payment for calcimimetics are included in the ESRD PPS base rate using the following data sources and methodology:
units.action_summary: Beginning Jan 1, 2021, CMS will include payment for calcimimetics in the ESRD PPS base rate using specified data sources and methodology.

units.obligation_text: Total units of oral and injectable calcimimetics and total number of paid hemodialysis-equivalent dialysis treatments furnished, as derived from Medicare ESRD facility claims, that is, the 837-institutional form with bill type 072X, for calendar years 2018 and 2019.
units.action_summary: Use Medicare ESRD facility claims (837-institutional bill type 072X) for 2018 and 2019 to obtain total units of calcimimetics and total number of paid hemodialysis-equivalent treatments.

units.obligation_text: The weighted average ASP based on the most recent determinations by CMS.
units.action_summary: Use the weighted average ASP based on CMS' most recent determinations as a data source for pricing calcimimetics.

units.obligation_text: CMS uses the following methodology to calculate the average per treatment payment amount for calcimimetics that is added to the ESRD PPS base rate:
units.action_summary: CMS must follow a specified methodology to calculate the average per-treatment payment amount for calcimimetics to add to the ESRD PPS base rate.

units.obligation_text: Determines utilization of oral and injectable calcimimetics by aggregating the total units of oral and injectable calcimimetics in paragraph (f)(1) of this section.
units.action_summary: Determine utilization by aggregating total units of oral and injectable calcimimetics from specified data sources.

units.obligation_text: Determines a price for each form of the drug by calculating 100 percent of the values from the most recent calendar quarter ASP calculations available to the public for the oral and injectable calcimimetic.
units.action_summary: Determine a price for each form of calcimimetic by using 100% of the most recent calendar quarter ASP values available to the public.

units.obligation_text: Calculates the total calcimimetic expenditure amount by multiplying the utilization of the oral and injectable calcimimetics determined in paragraph (f)(2)(i) of this section by their respective prices determined in paragraph (f)(2)(ii) of this section and adding the expenditure amount for both forms.
units.action_summary: Calculate total calcimimetic expenditures by multiplying utilization by price for each form and summing them.

units.obligation_text: Calculates the average per treatment payment amount by dividing the total calcimimetic expenditure amount determined in paragraph (f)(2)(iii) of this section by the total number of paid hemodialysis-equivalent dialysis treatments in calendar years 2018 and 2019.
units.action_summary: Compute the average per-treatment payment by dividing total calcimimetic expenditures by total paid hemodialysis-equivalent treatments in 2018–2019.

units.obligation_text: Calculates the amount added to the ESRD PPS base rate by reducing the average per treatment payment amount determined in paragraph (f)(2)(iv) of this section by 1 percent to account for the outlier policy under § 413.237.
units.action_summary: Reduce the average per-treatment payment amount by 1% to account for the outlier policy, and add that amount to the ESRD PPS base rate.

units.obligation_text: CMS provides for a transitional add-on payment adjustment for new and innovative equipment and supplies (as specified in paragraph (d) of this section) to an ESRD facility for furnishing a covered equipment or supply only if the item:

units.action_summary: An item is eligible for the transitional add-on payment only if it meets the criteria listed in the following subparagraphs.

units.obligation_text: Is new, meaning within 3 years beginning on the date of the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) marketing authorization;
units.actor: the item (new renal dialysis equipment or supply)
units.action_summary: To be eligible, the item must be new — within 3 years from FDA marketing authorization.

units.obligation_text: Has a complete Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS) Level II code application submitted, in accordance with the HCPCS Level II coding procedures on the CMS website, by the HCPCS Level II code application deadline for biannual Coding Cycle 2 for durable medical equipment, orthotics, prosthetics and supplies (DMEPOS) and services as specified in the HCPCS Level II coding guidance on the CMS website prior to the particular calendar year;
units.action_summary: A complete HCPCS Level II code application must be submitted according to CMS procedures by the specified Coding Cycle 2 application deadline prior to the calendar year for consideration.

units.obligation_text: Is innovative, meaning it meets the criteria specified in § 412.87(b)(1) of this chapter;
units.actor: the item (new renal dialysis equipment or supply)
units.action_summary: To be eligible, the item must be 'innovative' as defined by meeting criteria in § 412.87(b)(1).

units.obligation_text: Is not a capital-related asset, except for capital-related assets that are home dialysis machines.
units.actor: the item (new renal dialysis equipment or supply)
units.action_summary: The item generally must not be a capital-related asset, except capital-related assets that are home dialysis machines are allowed.

units.obligation_text: CMS will only consider a complete application received by CMS by February 1 prior to the particular calendar year.
units.actor: the applicant (manufacturer or entity submitting the HCPCS Level II application)
units.action_summary: CMS will consider only complete applications received by February 1 prior to the particular calendar year.

units.obligation_text: FDA marketing authorization for the equipment or supply must occur by the HCPCS Level II code application deadline for biannual Coding Cycle 2 for DMEPOS items and services as specified in the HCPCS Level II coding guidance on the CMS website prior to the particular calendar year.
units.actor: the equipment/supply (manufacturer/applicant in securing FDA authorization)
units.action_summary: FDA marketing authorization must occur by the HCPCS Level II code application deadline for Coding Cycle 2 prior to the calendar year to be considered.

units.obligation_text: A new and innovative renal dialysis equipment or supply will be paid for using a transitional add-on payment adjustment for new and innovative equipment and supplies based on 65 percent of the MAC-determined price, as specified in paragraph (e) of this section.
units.action_summary: Payment for eligible new and innovative items will be made as a transitional add-on equal to 65% of the MAC-determined price.

units.obligation_text: For capital-related assets that are home dialysis machines, payment is based on 65 percent of the pre-adjusted per treatment amount, as specified in paragraph (f)(1)(ii) of this section.
units.action_summary: For capital-related home dialysis machines, the transitional add-on payment is 65% of the pre-adjusted per-treatment amount (per paragraph (f)(1)(ii)).

units.obligation_text: Following payment of the transitional add-on payment adjustment for new and innovative equipment and supplies, the ESRD PPS base rate will not be modified
units.action_summary: After payment of the transitional add-on, CMS will not modify the ESRD PPS base rate.

units.obligation_text: the new and innovative renal dialysis equipment or supply will be an eligible outlier service as provided in § 413.237,
units.action_summary: A new and innovative item that received the transitional add-on payment will be an eligible outlier service under § 413.237.

units.obligation_text: except a capital-related asset that is a home dialysis machine will not be an eligible outlier service as provided in § 413.237.
units.actor: capital-related assets that are home dialysis machines
units.action_summary: Capital-related home dialysis machines are not eligible outlier services under § 413.237 despite receiving the transitional add-on payment.

units.obligation_text: The MACs calculate a pre-adjusted per treatment amount, using the prices they establish under paragraph (e) of this section for a capital-related asset that is a home dialysis machine, as defined in paragraph (a)(2) of this section, as follows:
units.action_summary: MACs must calculate a pre-adjusted per-treatment amount for capital-related home dialysis machines using prices established under paragraph (e).

units.obligation_text: Calculate an annual allowance to determine the amount that represents the portion of the cost allocable to 1 year for use in calculating the pre-adjusted per treatment amount, using the straight-line depreciation method, by dividing the MAC-determined price by its useful life of 5 years.
units.action_summary: MACs must calculate an annual allowance by dividing the MAC-determined price by a 5-year useful life using straight-line depreciation.

units.obligation_text: Calculate a pre-adjusted per treatment amount to determine the amount that is adjusted by the 65 percent under paragraph (d) of this section, by dividing the annual allowance, as determined in paragraph (f)(1)(i) of this section, by the expected number of treatments.
units.action_summary: MACs must calculate the pre-adjusted per-treatment amount by dividing the annual allowance by the expected number of treatments.

units.obligation_text: CMS will consider whether a new renal dialysis supply or equipment meets the eligibility criteria specified in paragraph (b) of this section and announce the results in the Federal Register as part of its annual updates and changes to the ESRD prospective payment system.
units.action_summary: CMS will review applications for eligibility and announce determinations in the Federal Register as part of annual ESRD PPS updates.
