units.action_summary: CMS must use total units of oral and injectable calcimimetics and total paid hemodialysis-equivalent treatments from specified Medicare ESRD facility claims for 2018 and 2019 as data sources.

units.obligation_text: The weighted average ASP based on the most recent determinations by CMS.
units.action_summary: CMS must use the weighted average ASP based on its most recent determinations as a data source.

units.obligation_text: CMS uses the following methodology to calculate the average per treatment payment amount for calcimimetics that is added to the ESRD PPS base rate:
units.action_summary: CMS shall use the specified multi-step methodology to calculate the average per treatment payment amount for calcimimetics to add to the ESRD PPS base rate.

units.obligation_text: Determines utilization of oral and injectable calcimimetics by aggregating the total units of oral and injectable calcimimetics in paragraph (f)(1) of this section.
units.action_summary: CMS shall determine calcimimetic utilization by aggregating total units of oral and injectable formulations from the data sources.

units.obligation_text: Determines a price for each form of the drug by calculating 100 percent of the values from the most recent calendar quarter ASP calculations available to the public for the oral and injectable calcimimetic.
units.action_summary: CMS shall determine a price for each drug form by using 100% of the most recent calendar quarter ASP values available to the public.

units.obligation_text: Calculates the total calcimimetic expenditure amount by multiplying the utilization of the oral and injectable calcimimetics determined in paragraph (f)(2)(i) of this section by their respective prices determined in paragraph (f)(2)(ii) of this section and adding the expenditure amount for both forms.
units.action_summary: CMS shall calculate total expenditure by multiplying utilization by respective prices and summing expenditures for oral and injectable forms.

units.obligation_text: Calculates the average per treatment payment amount by dividing the total calcimimetic expenditure amount determined in paragraph (f)(2)(iii) of this section by the total number of paid hemodialysis-equivalent dialysis treatments in calendar years 2018 and 2019.
units.action_summary: CMS shall compute the average per-treatment payment by dividing total expenditure by total paid hemodialysis-equivalent treatments for 2018 and 2019.

units.obligation_text: Calculates the amount added to the ESRD PPS base rate by reducing the average per treatment payment amount determined in paragraph (f)(2)(iv) of this section by 1 percent to account for the outlier policy under § 413.237.
units.action_summary: CMS shall reduce the average per-treatment amount by 1% to account for the outlier policy and add that amount to the ESRD PPS base rate.

units.obligation_text: CMS provides for a transitional add-on payment adjustment for new and innovative equipment and supplies (as specified in paragraph (d) of this section) to an ESRD facility for furnishing a covered equipment or supply only if the item:
units.actor: a renal dialysis equipment or supply (item)
units.action_summary: An item is eligible for the transitional add-on payment adjustment only if it meets the listed criteria.

units.obligation_text: Is new, meaning within 3 years beginning on the date of the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) marketing authorization;
units.action_summary: The item must be new, defined as within 3 years from the date of FDA marketing authorization.

units.obligation_text: Has a complete Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS) Level II code application submitted, in accordance with the HCPCS Level II coding procedures on the CMS website, by the HCPCS Level II code application deadline for biannual Coding Cycle 2 for durable medical equipment, orthotics, prosthetics and supplies (DMEPOS) and services as specified in the HCPCS Level II coding guidance on the CMS website prior to the particular calendar year;
units.action_summary: The applicant must submit a complete HCPCS Level II code application by the specified HCPCS application deadline and in accordance with CMS procedures.

units.obligation_text: Is innovative, meaning it meets the criteria specified in § 412.87(b)(1) of this chapter;
units.action_summary: The item must meet the innovation criteria set forth in § 412.87(b)(1).

units.obligation_text: Is not a capital-related asset, except for capital-related assets that are home dialysis machines.
units.action_summary: The item must not be a capital-related asset, except capital-related assets that are home dialysis machines are allowed.

units.obligation_text: CMS will consider whether a new renal dialysis supply or equipment meets the eligibility criteria specified in paragraph (b) of this section and announce the results in the Federal Register as part of its annual updates and changes to the ESRD prospective payment system.
units.action_summary: CMS will review applications to determine eligibility and will announce determinations in the Federal Register as part of annual ESRD PPS updates.

units.obligation_text: CMS will only consider a complete application received by CMS by February 1 prior to the particular calendar year.
units.actor: the applicant (submission of a complete application)
units.action_summary: CMS will consider only complete applications received by February 1 prior to the particular calendar year; applicants must ensure timely complete submissions.

units.obligation_text: FDA marketing authorization for the equipment or supply must occur by the HCPCS Level II code application deadline for biannual Coding Cycle 2 for DMEPOS items and services as specified in the HCPCS Level II coding guidance on the CMS website prior to the particular calendar year.
units.action_summary: The equipment or supply must have FDA marketing authorization by the HCPCS Level II code application deadline specified in CMS guidance prior to the calendar year.

units.obligation_text: A new and innovative renal dialysis equipment or supply will be paid for using a transitional add-on payment adjustment for new and innovative equipment and supplies based on 65 percent of the MAC-determined price, as specified in paragraph (e) of this section.
units.action_summary: New and innovative equipment or supplies will be paid via a transitional add-on adjustment equal to 65% of the MAC-determined price.

units.obligation_text: For capital-related assets that are home dialysis machines, payment is based on 65 percent of the pre-adjusted per treatment amount, as specified in paragraph (f)(1)(ii) of this section.
units.action_summary: For home dialysis machines that are capital-related assets, payment will be 65% of the pre-adjusted per-treatment amount (special pricing rule).

units.obligation_text: Following payment of the transitional add-on payment adjustment for new and innovative equipment and supplies, the ESRD PPS base rate will not be modified and the new and innovative renal dialysis equipment or supply will be an eligible outlier service as provided in § 413.237,
units.action_summary: After payment of the transitional add-on, CMS will not modify the ESRD PPS base rate and the new and innovative item will be considered an eligible outlier service under §413.237.

units.obligation_text: except a capital-related asset that is a home dialysis machine will not be an eligible outlier service as provided in § 413.237.
units.actor: a capital-related asset that is a home dialysis machine
units.action_summary: Capital-related assets that are home dialysis machines are excluded and will not be treated as eligible outlier services under §413.237.

units.obligation_text: The MACs calculate a pre-adjusted per treatment amount, using the prices they establish under paragraph (e) of this section for a capital-related asset that is a home dialysis machine, as defined in paragraph (a)(2) of this section, as follows:
units.action_summary: MACs must calculate a pre-adjusted per-treatment amount for home dialysis machines using prices established under paragraph (e) according to the following steps.

units.obligation_text: Calculate an annual allowance to determine the amount that represents the portion of the cost allocable to 1 year for use in calculating the pre-adjusted per treatment amount, using the straight-line depreciation method, by dividing the MAC-determined price by its useful life of 5 years.
units.action_summary: MACs shall calculate an annual allowance by dividing the MAC-determined price by a useful life of 5 years using straight-line depreciation.

units.obligation_text: Calculate a pre-adjusted per treatment amount to determine the amount that is adjusted by the 65 percent under paragraph (d) of this section, by dividing the annual allowance, as determined in paragraph (f)(1)(i) of this section, by the expected number of treatments.
units.action_summary: MACs shall calculate the pre-adjusted per-treatment amount by dividing the annual allowance by the expected number of treatments.

units.obligation_text: Renal dialysis equipment and supplies, except for capital-related assets that are home dialysis machines (as defined in § 413.236(a)(2)), that receive the transitional add-on payment adjustment as specified in § 413.236, after the payment period has ended.
units.actor: renal dialysis equipment and supplies receiving the transitional add-on adjustment
units.action_summary: Renal dialysis equipment and supplies that received the transitional add-on payment adjustment (excluding home dialysis capital assets) are treated under the outlier provisions after the payment period ends.

title: Basic Health Program: Federal Funding Methodology for Program Year 2022

units.obligation_text: States currently operating a BHP that wish to change the methodology for non-filers must submit a revised Blueprint outlining the revisions to its methodology, consistent with § 600.125.
units.actor: States currently operating a BHP that wish to change the methodology for non-filers
units.action_summary: Submit a revised Blueprint outlining methodology revisions consistent with § 600.125.

units.obligation_text: Payments would still be made only for months that the person is enrolled in and eligible for the BHP.
units.action_summary: Federal BHP payments are limited to months when the person is enrolled and eligible.

units.obligation_text: The states must maintain data that are consistent with CMS’ verification requirements, including auditable records for each individual enrolled, indicating an eligibility determination and a determination of income and other criteria relevant to the payment methodology as of the beginning of each quarter.
units.action_summary: Maintain data consistent with CMS verification requirements, including auditable individual records reflecting eligibility and income as of the start of each quarter.

units.obligation_text: including auditable records for each individual enrolled, indicating an eligibility determination and a determination of income and other criteria relevant to the payment methodology as of the beginning of each quarter.
units.action_summary: Maintain auditable individual-level records showing eligibility determinations, income, and other criteria as of the beginning of each quarter.

units.obligation_text: Consistent with § 600.610 (Secretarial determination of BHP payment amount), the state is required to submit certain data in accordance with this methodology.
units.action_summary: Submit certain data in accordance with the BHP payment methodology per § 600.610.

units.obligation_text: We require that this data be collected and validated by states operating a BHP.
units.action_summary: Collect and validate the data required by the BHP methodology.

units.obligation_text: We require that this data be ... submitted to CMS.
units.action_summary: Submit the collected and validated data to CMS.

units.obligation_text: Despite the discontinuance of Federal payments for CSRs, QHP issuers are required to provide CSRs to eligible enrollees.
units.action_summary: Provide cost-sharing reductions (CSRs) to eligible enrollees even though Federal CSR payments were discontinued.

units.obligation_text: Although plans are allowed to serve geographic areas smaller than counties after obtaining our approval, we propose that no geographic area, for purposes of defining BHP payment rate cells, will be smaller than a county.
units.action_summary: May serve geographic areas smaller than counties only after obtaining CMS approval (permission).

units.obligation_text: We propose that no geographic area, for purposes of defining BHP payment rate cells, will be smaller than a county.
units.action_summary: Geographic areas used to define BHP payment rate cells must be at least county-sized.

units.obligation_text: There will be an annual reconciliation following the end of the year to compare the APTC to the correct amount of PTC based on household circumstances shown on the Federal income tax return.
units.action_summary: Conduct an annual reconciliation comparing APTC paid to the correct PTC determined from federal tax returns.

units.obligation_text: If too little APTC was paid, the difference would be paid to the taxpayer.
units.action_summary: Pay taxpayers any underpayment of APTC identified in the annual reconciliation.

units.obligation_text: If too much APTC was paid, the difference would be charged to the taxpayer as additional tax (if too much APTC was paid, subject to any limitations in statute or regulation).
units.action_summary: Charge taxpayers additional tax for any overpayment of APTC, subject to statutory/regulatory limitations.

units.section: Section 1331(e)(2) of the Affordable Care Act
units.obligation_text: Section 1331(e)(2) of the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act specifies that an individual eligible for the BHP may not be treated as a "qualified individual" under section 1312 of the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act who is eligible for enrollment in a QHP offered through an Exchange.
units.actor: Exchanges/Administrators (those who would otherwise treat individuals as "qualified individuals")
units.action_summary: Do not treat individuals eligible for the BHP as 'qualified individuals' eligible to enroll in Exchange QHPs.

units.obligation_text: To the extent that a state operating a BHP determines that, because of the distinctive risk profile of BHP-eligible consumers, BHP standard health plans should be included in mechanisms that share risk with other plans in the state’s individual market, the state would need to use other methods for achieving this goal.
units.action_summary: If the state elects to include BHP standard plans in state risk-sharing mechanisms, the state must use alternative methods to achieve inclusion.

units.obligation_text: To calculate the estimated PTC that would be paid if BHP-eligible individuals enrolled in QHPs through an Exchange, we must calculate a RP because the PTC is based, in part, on the premiums for the applicable second lowest cost silver plan.
units.action_summary: Calculate a reference premium (RP) to estimate the premium tax credit (PTC).

units.obligation_text: The applicable second lowest cost silver plan premium will be included in the BHP payment methodology by age range (if applicable), geographic area, and self-only or applicable category of family coverage obtained through the BHP.
units.action_summary: Include the second-lowest cost silver plan premium in BHP payment calculations across age ranges, geographic areas, and coverage categories.

units.obligation_text: The PTC amount provided for a person enrolled in a QHP through an Exchange is calculated in accordance with the methodology described in 26 U.S.C. 36B(b)(2). The amount is equal to the lesser of the premium for the plan in which the person or household enrolls, or the adjusted premium for the applicable second lowest cost silver plan minus the contribution amount.
units.action_summary: Compute PTC as the lesser of the enrolled plan premium or the adjusted second-lowest silver premium minus the contribution amount, per 26 U.S.C. 36B(b)(2).

units.section: Section 1331(d)(3) of the Affordable Care Act
units.obligation_text: We do not believe it is appropriate to adjust the payment for an assumption that some BHP enrollees would not have enrolled in QHPs for purposes of calculating the BHP payment rates, since section 1331(d)(3)(A)(ii) of the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act requires the calculation of such rates as if the enrollee had enrolled in a QHP through an Exchange.
units.action_summary: Calculate BHP payment rates as if enrollees had enrolled in QHPs through an Exchange, per section 1331(d)(3)(A)(ii).

title: Medicare Program: Durable Medical Equipment, Prosthetics, Orthotics, and Supplies Policy Issues and Level II of the Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System

units.obligation_text: Coding cycles begin no less frequently than—
units.action_summary: CMS must run HCPCS Level II coding cycles at least as frequently as specified.

units.obligation_text: Bi-annually for non-drug, non-biological items and services;
units.action_summary: Coding cycles for non-drug, non-biological items and services must occur bi-annually.

units.obligation_text: Quarterly for drug or biological products.
units.action_summary: Coding cycles for drug or biological products must occur quarterly.

units.obligation_text: HCPCS Level II code application submission deadlines are established on the CMS website or in another manner
units.action_summary: CMS must establish and publish code application submission deadlines on its website or otherwise.

units.obligation_text: In or around January and June of each year for non-drug, non-biological items and services;
units.action_summary: Deadlines for non-drug, non-biological items are approximately in January and June each year.

units.obligation_text: In or around January, April, June, and September each year, for drug or biological products.
units.action_summary: Deadlines for drug or biological products are approximately January, April, June, and September each year.

units.obligation_text: Public meetings are held to provide the public with notice of, and the opportunity for public input on code applications and preliminary recommendations ... and for CMS to gather public input regarding these applications and preliminary recommendations.
units.action_summary: CMS must hold public meetings to notify the public and gather input on code applications and preliminary recommendations.

units.obligation_text: Public meetings are held during each bi-annual coding cycle.
units.action_summary: CMS must hold public meetings during each bi-annual coding cycle.

units.obligation_text: Subject to paragraph (e)(3) of this section, public meetings are held for all code applications for non-drug, non-biological items and services.
units.action_summary: CMS must hold public meetings for all non-drug, non-biological code applications, subject to delay provisions in e(3).

units.obligation_text: Subject to paragraph (e)(3) of this section, public meetings are held for drug or biological product code applications only under the following circumstances:
units.action_summary: CMS holds public meetings for drug/biological product code applications only in specified circumstances, subject to e(3).

units.obligation_text: The code application is one that was resubmitted for reevaluation as provided in § 414.9(b).
units.action_summary: A resubmitted code application (per §414.9(b)) is a circumstance under which CMS holds a public meeting for drug/biological applications.

units.obligation_text: A decision on the code application is delayed under paragraph (e)(3) of this section, and CMS determines it presents program, policy, or implementation concerns or complexities, or otherwise raises questions that public input could help to address.
units.action_summary: If a decision is delayed and CMS finds the application raises concerns public input could address, CMS holds a public meeting for drug/biological applications.

units.obligation_text: CMS issues preliminary recommendations ... on code applications for items and services included in the public meeting agenda. ... preliminary recommendations are posted on the CMS website or issued in another manner, prior to the public meetings described in paragraph (d) of this section.
units.action_summary: CMS must issue preliminary recommendations for agenda items and post them (unless delayed under e(3)) prior to the public meetings.
units.modal_raw: is required to issue and post

units.obligation_text: CMS may delay a preliminary recommendation and therefore a final decision, or delay a final decision alone, one or more times into a subsequent coding cycle where a code application raises complex or significant issues or considerations and CMS determines that additional time is needed to evaluate the code application.
units.action_summary: CMS may delay issuing preliminary and/or final recommendations into a subsequent coding cycle when additional evaluation time is needed due to complexity or significance.

units.obligation_text: Final decisions ... are posted on the CMS website or issued in another manner within approximately— (i) Six months of the application deadline for non-drug, non-biological items and services; and (ii) Three months of the application deadline for drug or biological products.
units.action_summary: CMS must post final decisions within approximately six months for non-drug items and three months for drug items after the application deadline, subject to e(3).

units.obligation_text: Six months of the application deadline for non-drug, non-biological items and services;
units.action_summary: Final decisions for non-drug, non-biological items must be posted approximately six months after the application deadline.

units.obligation_text: Three months of the application deadline for drug or biological products.
units.action_summary: Final decisions for drug or biological products must be posted approximately three months after the application deadline.

units.obligation_text: For code applications (including code applications for drug or biological products) that are resubmitted for reevaluation and placed on a public meeting agenda in accordance with § 414.9(b)(3), CMS may also delay issuing a preliminary recommendation, a final decision, or both into a subsequent quarterly coding cycle.
units.action_summary: CMS may delay preliminary recommendations and/or final decisions into a subsequent quarterly cycle for resubmitted applications placed on a public meeting agenda.

units.obligation_text: Decisions to delay a preliminary recommendation or final decision are issued by CMS, either on the CMS website or in another manner, at the same time that CMS issues the preliminary recommendations or final decisions, as applicable, for other applications during a coding cycle.
units.action_summary: If CMS decides to delay recommendations/decisions, it must publish those delay decisions simultaneously with other recommendations/decisions for the coding cycle.

units.obligation_text: Coding changes are effective approximately 3 months after the issuance of the final coding decision.
units.action_summary: Coding changes take effect approximately three months after CMS issues the final coding decision.

units.obligation_text: To be considered in a given HCPCS Level II coding cycle specified in § 414.8(b), a code application must be timely and complete.
units.action_summary: Applicants must submit timely and complete code applications to be considered in a coding cycle.

units.obligation_text: Code applications that are not timely and complete are declined by CMS but may be submitted by the applicant in a subsequent coding cycle.
units.action_summary: CMS must decline applications that are not timely and complete.

units.obligation_text: Code applications that are not timely and complete ... may be submitted by the applicant in a subsequent coding cycle.
units.action_summary: Applicants are permitted to resubmit declined applications in a subsequent coding cycle.

units.obligation_text: All applicable information and documentation specified in this section, and meet all administrative elements specified by the application instructions issued by CMS and posted on the CMS website.
units.action_summary: Applicants must include all specified information/documentation and meet administrative elements per CMS application instructions.

units.obligation_text: FDA documentation of the item’s current classification, as applicable, as well as FDA marketing authorization documentation, or the regulation number under 21 CFR parts 862 through 892 for a device exempted from the premarket notification requirement ... If a device exceeds the limitations to the exemptions ... the appropriate marketing authorization documentation must be submitted as part of the application.
units.action_summary: Applicants must provide applicable FDA classification and marketing authorization documentation (or regulation number for exempt devices); if not exempt, submit appropriate marketing authorization.

units.obligation_text: For applications for non-drug, non-biological items or services that are not subject to marketing authorization under the FD&C Act or PHSA to be considered complete, evidence that the item or service is available in the United States market for use and purchase at the time of the relevant HCPCS Level II code application submission deadline specified by CMS.
units.action_summary: Applicants for non-drug/non-biological items without marketing authorization must provide evidence the item is available in the U.S. market at the submission deadline.

units.obligation_text: For biosimilar biological products, CMS allows a 10-business day extension past the code application deadline to provide a complete application as specified in paragraph (a)(2) of this section.
units.action_summary: CMS permits a 10-business-day extension for biosimilar biological product applicants to provide a complete application under specified criteria.

units.obligation_text: The marketing authorization documentation is dated between the first day of the extension period and no later than the last day of the extension period.
units.action_summary: To qualify for the biosimilar extension, the marketing authorization documentation must be dated within the extension period.

units.obligation_text: The applicant submits a complete application to CMS by the last day of the extension period.
units.action_summary: Applicants using the biosimilar extension must submit a complete application by the extension's last day.

units.obligation_text: An applicant who is dissatisfied with a final coding decision on an initial code application may resubmit their application for reevaluation by CMS no more than two times.
units.action_summary: Applicants may resubmit their application for reevaluation up to two times if dissatisfied with the final decision.

units.obligation_text: Any application resubmitted for reevaluation by CMS must be timely and complete in accordance with paragraph (a) of this section and must include the following:
units.action_summary: Resubmitted applications must be timely and complete and must include specified supporting materials.

units.obligation_text: A description of the previous application submission(s).
units.action_summary: Applicants must include a description of prior application submissions when resubmitting for reevaluation.

units.obligation_text: A copy of the prior final code decision(s) with respect to the application.
units.action_summary: Applicants must include copies of prior final coding decisions in resubmissions.

units.obligation_text: An explanation of the reason for disagreement with the prior final coding decision(s).
units.action_summary: Applicants must explain why they disagree with the prior final coding decision(s) when resubmitting.

units.obligation_text: For applications resubmitted a second time for reevaluation ... the application must include any significant new information as described in paragraphs (b)(1)(i) and (ii) of this section.
units.action_summary: A second resubmission must include any significant new information addressing reasons for the prior decision.

units.obligation_text: Any significant new information which would include information that was not previously submitted to CMS with respect to the application that directly relates to the reason for the prior final coding decision(s) and could potentially change the final coding decision.
units.action_summary: Applicants must provide any significant new information not previously submitted that directly relates to prior reasons and could change the decision.

units.obligation_text: An explanation of how the significant new information addresses and directly relates to the reason(s) for the prior final coding decision(s) and supports the request for a different coding decision.
units.action_summary: Applicants must explain how the new information addresses prior reasons and supports requesting a different decision.

units.obligation_text: An application that is resubmitted for reevaluation under this paragraph (b) is included on an agenda for a public meeting as described in § 414.8(d) and receives a preliminary recommendation as described in § 414.8(e)(1).
units.action_summary: CMS must include resubmitted applications on a public meeting agenda and provide a preliminary recommendation.

units.obligation_text: An application for a drug or biological product that is resubmitted for reevaluation will not be included in a public meeting or receive a final decision in the quarterly cycle in which the application is submitted.
units.action_summary: Resubmitted drug or biological product applications shall not be included in a public meeting nor receive a final decision in the same quarterly cycle they are submitted.

units.obligation_text: Preliminary recommendations and final decisions for applications that are resubmitted for reevaluation may be delayed as described in § 414.8(e)(3).
units.action_summary: CMS may delay preliminary recommendations and final decisions for resubmitted applications as permitted under §414.8(e)(3).

units.obligation_text: An applicant may submit an external HCPCS Level II code application to request the addition of a code, revision of an existing code, or discontinuation of an existing code.
units.action_summary: Applicants are permitted to submit external HCPCS Level II code applications to add, revise, or discontinue codes.

units.obligation_text: CMS’ evaluation of a code application is based on information contained in the application and supporting material, any comments received through the public meeting process as applicable, any information obtained from and evaluations conducted by federal employees or CMS contractors, and any additional research or information obtained independently by CMS ...
units.action_summary: CMS must base its evaluation on application materials, public comments, federal evaluations, contractor evaluations, and any additional research it obtains.

units.obligation_text: Except as provided in paragraph (d)(2) of this section, a request to add a code is further evaluated under paragraph (d)(4) of this section if CMS determines the following—
units.action_summary: CMS must determine whether certain factors are met to decide if a request to add a code should be further evaluated under d(4).

units.obligation_text: The item or service is not appropriate for inclusion in or already coded in a different HIPAA standard medical data code set, such as CPT®, ICD, or CDT®;
units.action_summary: CMS must determine whether the item/service is not appropriate for another HIPAA code set or not already coded elsewhere.

units.obligation_text: The item or service is primarily medical in nature;
units.action_summary: CMS must determine whether the item/service is primarily medical in nature.

units.obligation_text: If applicable, the item has the appropriate marketing authorization from FDA, or is exempt from premarket notification requirements;
units.action_summary: CMS must determine whether, where applicable, the item has appropriate FDA marketing authorization or is exempt from premarket notification.

units.obligation_text: There is a claims processing need on the part of Medicare to identify the item or service in the HCPCS Level II code set.
units.action_summary: CMS must determine whether Medicare has a claims processing need to identify the item/service in the HCPCS Level II code set.

units.obligation_text: If paragraphs (d)(1)(i), (ii), or (iii) of this section are not met, but paragraph (d)(1)(iv) of this section is met, a request to add a code is further evaluated under paragraph (d)(4).
units.action_summary: Even if some factors are not met, CMS must further evaluate a request under d(4) if there is a claims processing need.

units.obligation_text: If neither paragraph (d)(1) nor (2) of this section is met, CMS does not further evaluate the application under paragraph (d)(4) and does not modify the HCPCS Level II code set.
units.action_summary: If neither set of conditions is met, CMS shall not further evaluate the request under d(4) and shall not modify the HCPCS Level II code set.

units.obligation_text: If paragraph (d)(1) or (d)(2) of this section is met, CMS determines if the item or service that is the subject of the code application— (i) Performs a significantly different clinical function ...; or (ii) Results in a significant therapeutic distinction ...
units.action_summary: If preliminary conditions are met, CMS must determine whether the item/service performs a different clinical function or results in a significant therapeutic distinction.

units.obligation_text: Performs a significantly different clinical function compared to other items or services described in the HCPCS Level II code set.
units.action_summary: CMS must evaluate whether the item/service performs a clinical function not performed by any other item/service in the HCPCS Level II set.

units.obligation_text: Results in a significant therapeutic distinction compared to the use of other similar items or services described in the HCPCS Level II code set.
units.action_summary: CMS must evaluate whether use of the item/service yields a significantly improved or different medical benefit versus similar items/services.

units.obligation_text: The item or service offers a treatment option for a patient population unresponsive to, or ineligible for, currently available treatments.
units.action_summary: CMS may consider offering a treatment option for previously unresponsive/ineligible populations as evidence of significant therapeutic distinction.

units.obligation_text: The item or service offers the ability to diagnose a medical condition in a patient population where that medical condition is currently undetectable, or offers the ability to diagnose a medical condition earlier ... and there must also be evidence that use of the item or service to make a diagnosis affects the management of the patient.
units.action_summary: CMS may treat improved or earlier diagnostic ability (that affects patient management) as evidence of significant therapeutic distinction.

units.obligation_text: A reduction in at least one clinically significant adverse event, including a reduction in mortality or a clinically significant complication.
units.action_summary: CMS may consider reduction in significant adverse events (including mortality) as evidence of significant therapeutic distinction.

units.obligation_text: A decreased rate of at least one subsequent diagnostic or therapeutic intervention.
units.action_summary: CMS may consider lower rates of subsequent diagnostic/therapeutic interventions as evidence of significant therapeutic distinction.

units.obligation_text: A decreased number of future hospitalizations or physician visits.
units.action_summary: CMS may consider reductions in future hospitalizations or physician visits as evidence of significant therapeutic distinction.

units.obligation_text: A more rapid beneficial resolution of the disease process treatment including, but not limited to, a reduced length of stay or recovery time.
units.action_summary: CMS may consider faster beneficial resolution or reduced length of stay/recovery time as evidence of significant therapeutic distinction.

units.obligation_text: An improvement in one or more activities of daily living.
units.action_summary: CMS may consider improvements in activities of daily living as evidence of significant therapeutic distinction.

units.obligation_text: An improved quality of life.
units.action_summary: CMS may consider improved quality of life as evidence of significant therapeutic distinction.

units.obligation_text: A demonstrated greater medication adherence or compliance.
units.action_summary: CMS may consider demonstrated greater medication adherence/compliance as evidence of significant therapeutic distinction.

units.obligation_text: The totality of the information otherwise demonstrates that the use of the item or service results in a significantly improved or a significantly different medical benefit when compared with the use of other similar items or services described in the HCPCS Level II code set.
units.action_summary: CMS may consider the totality of information to determine if the item/service yields a significantly improved/different medical benefit.

units.obligation_text: CMS may consider instances where the use of the item or service may substantially improve or substantially change the medical benefit realized by a specific subpopulation of patients ...
units.action_summary: CMS may consider substantial improvements in specific patient subpopulations as part of the determination of therapeutic distinction.

units.obligation_text: CMS makes this determination without regard to the prevalence among Medicare beneficiaries of the underlying medical condition treated or diagnosed by the item or service that is the subject of the code application.
units.action_summary: CMS must make the therapeutic distinction determination without regard to how prevalent the underlying medical condition is among Medicare beneficiaries.

units.obligation_text: An item’s designation under the FDA Breakthrough Devices Program and marketing authorization for the indication covered by the FDA Breakthrough Devices designation are given substantial weight in determining whether the item meets the significant therapeutic distinction factor ...
units.action_summary: CMS must give substantial weight to FDA Breakthrough Device designation and corresponding marketing authorization when assessing significant therapeutic distinction.

units.obligation_text: An application must contain sufficient information and supporting documentation to support a claim of significant therapeutic distinction.
units.action_summary: Applicants must provide sufficient information and documentation to support claims of significant therapeutic distinction.

units.obligation_text: If the item or service ... meets either of the two factors set forth in paragraph (d)(4)(i) or (ii) ... and CMS determines there is a claims processing need ... then CMS creates a new code.
units.action_summary: If conditions and a claims processing need are met, CMS must create a new HCPCS Level II code to identify the item/service.

units.obligation_text: If the conditions in paragraph (d)(5)(i) of this section are not met, CMS does not create a new code.
units.action_summary: If the specified conditions and claims processing need are not met, CMS shall not create a new code.

units.obligation_text: If CMS finds that revisions to the descriptor of an existing code category are appropriate to account for minor distinctions ... then CMS revises the descriptor rather than add a new code.
units.action_summary: CMS must revise an existing code descriptor (rather than add a new code) when such a revision appropriately accounts for minor distinctions and clarifies inclusion.

units.obligation_text: When evaluating a request to add a code for a drug or biological product, CMS first determines if— (i)-(iv)
units.action_summary: For drug/biological product code requests, CMS must first determine whether specified factors (inclusion in other code sets, medical nature, FDA authorization if applicable, and claims processing need) are met.

units.obligation_text: If CMS determines that the factors set forth in paragraph (e)(1) of this section are met, then CMS next determines ... whether an existing code adequately describes a product, or whether a revision to the descriptor ... is appropriate, or whether a new code is necessary. In making the determination ... CMS considers applicable Medicare Part B statutory and regulatory payment requirements ... and information such as the following: (i)-(iv).
units.action_summary: CMS must consider statutory/regulatory payment requirements, program instructions, and relevant information sources when deciding whether to add, revise, or take no coding action for a drug/biological product.

units.obligation_text: When evaluating a request to add a code for a drug or biological product, CMS determines if the product that is the subject of the code application — (i) Is separately payable under Medicare Part B as a drug or biological product; and (ii) Is a single source drug, multiple source drug, biological, or biosimilar biological product under section 1847A of the Act, or if other specific payment provisions ... apply.
units.action_summary: CMS must determine Part B payability and the product's sourcing/classification under section 1847A or applicability of other payment provisions.

units.obligation_text: After reviewing an application to add a code for a drug or biological product ... CMS will then make a determination about whether the appropriate action is to add a code, revise a code, or take no coding action, in response to the application for that product.
units.action_summary: CMS must make a determination to add, revise, or take no coding action after reviewing a drug/biological product application.

units.obligation_text: CMS may assign code descriptors with drug amounts that correspond to smaller quantities of the product to facilitate more accurate billing.
units.action_summary: CMS is permitted to assign code descriptors that include drug amounts for smaller quantities to improve billing accuracy.

units.obligation_text: If CMS determines that the revised descriptor suggested by the applicant would provide a more appropriate description of the category of items or services, CMS revises the descriptor accordingly.
units.action_summary: CMS must revise an existing code descriptor if it determines the applicant's suggested revision better describes the category.

units.obligation_text: If CMS determines that an existing code is duplicative of another code, or has become obsolete and CMS has no further expectation that the same or similar item or service will be marketed at a later date, CMS discontinues the code.
units.action_summary: CMS must discontinue codes found to be duplicative or obsolete with no expectation of future marketing.

units.obligation_text: Any coding action taken on an applicant’s coding request is set forth in the final coding decision.
units.action_summary: CMS must state any coding action taken on an applicant's request in the final coding decision.

units.obligation_text: At the start of a HCPCS coding cycle, CMS performs an analysis to determine if the item or service is statutorily excluded from coverage under Medicare under section 1862 of the Act, and, if not excluded by statute, whether the item or service is parenteral or enteral nutrients, supplies, and equipment covered under the prosthetic device benefit, splints and casts or other devices used for reductions of fractures or dislocations, or IOLs inserted in a physician’s office covered under the prosthetic device benefit.
units.action_summary: At each coding cycle start, CMS must analyze whether items/services are statutorily excluded or fall under specified prosthetic/splint/IOL categories.

units.obligation_text: If a preliminary determination is made that the item or service is parenteral or enteral nutrients, supplies, and equipment covered under the prosthetic device benefit, splints and casts or other devices used for reductions of fractures or dislocations, or IOLs inserted in a physician’s office covered under the prosthetic device benefit, CMS makes a preliminary payment determination for the item or service.
units.action_summary: If a preliminary benefit-category determination is made for listed items/services, CMS must make a preliminary payment determination.

units.obligation_text: CMS posts preliminary benefit category determinations and payment determinations on CMS.gov approximately 2 weeks prior to a public meeting described under § 414.8(d).
units.action_summary: CMS must post preliminary benefit category and payment determinations on CMS.gov about two weeks before the related public meeting.

units.obligation_text: After consideration of public consultation provided at a public meeting described under § 414.8(d) on preliminary benefit category determinations and payment determinations for items and services, CMS establishes the benefit category determinations and payment determinations for items and services through program instructions.
units.action_summary: Following public consultation, CMS must establish final benefit category and payment determinations via program instructions.

units.obligation_text: For accounting years that end on or before September 30, 2016 and end on or after October 1, 2030, the cap amount is adjusted for inflation by using the percentage change in the medical care expenditure category of the Consumer Price Index (CPI) for urban consumers that is published by the Bureau of Labor Statistics.

units.obligation_text: CMS will not calculate a performance score for any SNF using the methodology described in paragraphs (d)(1) and (2) of this section.

units.section: § 422.2 (Fully integrated dual eligible special needs plan)(2)(i)
units.obligation_text: Whose capitated contract with the State Medicaid agency requires coverage of ... Primary care and acute care, including Medicare cost-sharing as defined in section 1905(p)(3)(B), (C), and (D) of the Act, without regard to the limitation of that definition to qualified Medicare beneficiaries.
units.actor: capitated contract with the State Medicaid agency / FIDE SNP
units.action_summary: The capitated contract must provide coverage of primary and acute care, including Medicare cost-sharing.

units.section: § 422.2 (Fully integrated dual eligible special needs plan)(2)(ii)
units.obligation_text: Whose capitated contract with the State Medicaid agency requires coverage of ... Long-term services and supports, including coverage of nursing facility services for a period of at least 180 days during the plan year.
units.actor: capitated contract with the State Medicaid agency / FIDE SNP
units.action_summary: The capitated contract must cover long-term services and supports, including at least 180 days of nursing facility services during the plan year.

units.section: § 422.2 (Fully integrated dual eligible special needs plan)(2)(iii)
units.obligation_text: Whose capitated contract with the State Medicaid agency requires coverage of ... For plan year 2025 and subsequent years, behavioral health services.
units.actor: capitated contract with the State Medicaid agency / FIDE SNP
units.action_summary: Beginning 2025, the capitated contract must cover behavioral health services.

units.section: § 422.2 (Fully integrated dual eligible special needs plan)(2)(iv)
units.obligation_text: Whose capitated contract with the State Medicaid agency requires coverage of ... For plan year 2025 and subsequent years, home health services as defined in § 440.70.
units.actor: capitated contract with the State Medicaid agency / FIDE SNP
units.action_summary: Beginning 2025, the capitated contract must include home health services as defined in § 440.70.

units.section: § 422.2 (Fully integrated dual eligible special needs plan)(2)(v)
units.obligation_text: Whose capitated contract with the State Medicaid agency requires coverage of ... For plan year 2025 and subsequent years, durable medical equipment as defined in § 440.70(b)(3);
units.actor: capitated contract with the State Medicaid agency / FIDE SNP
units.action_summary: Beginning 2025, the capitated contract must cover durable medical equipment per § 440.70(b)(3).

units.section: § 422.2 (Fully integrated dual eligible special needs plan)(3)
units.obligation_text: That coordinates the delivery of covered Medicare and Medicaid services using aligned care management and specialty care network methods for high-risk beneficiaries;
units.action_summary: The plan must coordinate Medicare and Medicaid service delivery using aligned care management and specialty care networks for high-risk beneficiaries.

units.section: § 422.2 (Fully integrated dual eligible special needs plan)(5)
units.obligation_text: For plan year 2025 and subsequent years, that has exclusively aligned enrollment;
units.action_summary: Beginning 2025, the plan must have exclusively aligned enrollment.

units.section: § 422.2 (Fully integrated dual eligible special needs plan)(6)
units.obligation_text: For plan year 2025 and subsequent years, whose capitated contract with the State Medicaid agency covers the entire service area for the dual eligible special needs plan.
units.actor: capitated contract with the State Medicaid agency / FIDE SNP
units.action_summary: Beginning 2025, the capitated contract must cover the entire service area for the plan.

units.section: § 422.2 (Highly integrated dual eligible special needs plan)(1)
units.obligation_text: The capitated contract is between the State Medicaid agency and— (i) The MA organization; or (ii) The MA organization’s parent organization, or another entity that is owned and controlled by its parent organization.
units.action_summary: The capitated contract must be between the State Medicaid agency and the MA organization or its parent/controlled entity.

units.section: § 422.2 (Highly integrated dual eligible special needs plan)(2)(i-ii)
units.obligation_text: The capitated contract requires coverage of the following benefits ... (i) Long-term services and supports, including community-based long-term services and supports and some days of coverage of nursing facility services during the plan year; or (ii) Behavioral health services;
units.actor: capitated contract with the State Medicaid agency / HIDE SNP
units.action_summary: The capitated contract must cover either long-term services and supports (including some nursing facility days) or behavioral health services, as applicable.

units.section: § 422.2 (Highly integrated dual eligible special needs plan)(3)
units.obligation_text: For plan year 2025 and subsequent years, the capitated contract covers the entire service area for the dual eligible special needs plan.
units.actor: capitated contract with the State Medicaid agency / HIDE SNP
units.action_summary: Beginning 2025, the capitated contract must cover the entire service area for the plan.

units.obligation_text: MA plans are required to track the maximum out-of-pocket limit described in paragraph (f)(4) of this section based on accrued out-of-pocket beneficiary costs for original Medicare covered services, and are also required to notify members and health care providers when the limit has been reached.
units.action_summary: MA plans must track the OOP maximum (based on accrued costs) and notify members and providers when it's reached.

units.obligation_text: MA plans are required to track the maximum out-of-pocket limit described in paragraph (f)(5) of this section based on accrued out-of-pocket beneficiary costs for original Medicare covered services, and are also required to notify members and health care providers when the limit has been reached.
units.action_summary: MA plans must track the OOP maximum per paragraph (f)(5) and notify members and providers when reached.

units.obligation_text: When a disaster or emergency is declared ... an MA organization offering an MA plan must, until one of the conditions described in paragraph (m)(3) of this section occurs, ensure access to covered benefits in the following manner:
units.actor: MA organization offering an MA plan
units.action_summary: During declared disasters/emergencies and until specified conditions occur, the MA organization must ensure enrollees' access to covered benefits.

units.obligation_text: An MA organization must continue furnishing access to benefits as specified in paragraphs (m)(1)(i) through (iv) of this section for 30 days after the conditions described in paragraph (m)(3)(i) or (ii) of this section occur ... or after the condition described in paragraph (m)(3)(iii) of this section occurs, whichever is earlier:
units.action_summary: After certain end-of-emergency conditions, the MA organization must continue providing access to benefits for 30 days or until disruptions end, as specified.

units.obligation_text: An MA plan that cannot resume normal operations by the end of the disaster or emergency as described in paragraph (m)(3)(i) or (ii) of this section must notify CMS.
units.action_summary: If an MA plan cannot resume normal operations by the end of the disaster/emergency, it must notify CMS.

units.obligation_text: Conduct a comprehensive initial health risk assessment of the individual’s physical, psychosocial, and functional needs as well as annual health risk reassessment, using a comprehensive risk assessment tool that CMS may review during oversight activities, and ensure that the results from the initial assessment and annual reassessment conducted for each individual enrolled in the plan are addressed in the individuals’ individualized care plan as required under paragraph (f)(1)(ii) of this section.
units.action_summary: Plans must conduct comprehensive initial and annual health risk assessments using a tool (subject to CMS review) and ensure results are addressed in individualized care plans.

units.obligation_text: Beginning in 2024, the comprehensive risk assessment tool must include standardized questions specified by CMS in subregulatory guidance as follows:
units.actor: comprehensive risk assessment tool / MA plan
units.action_summary: Starting 2024, the risk assessment tool must include CMS-specified standardized questions.

units.obligation_text: (A) One or more questions on housing stability. (B) One or more questions on food security. (C) One or more questions on access to transportation.
units.actor: comprehensive risk assessment tool / MA plan
units.action_summary: The tool must include questions on housing stability, food security, and transportation access.

units.obligation_text: The verification of an enrollee’s Medicaid eligibility.
units.actor: dual eligible special needs plan / contract
units.action_summary: Plans/contracts must verify an enrollee's Medicaid eligibility.

units.obligation_text: The contract must also stipulate that ... the SNP notifies, or arranges for another entity or entities to notify, the State Medicaid agency, individuals or entities designated by the State Medicaid agency, or both, of hospital and skilled nursing facility admissions for at least one group of high-risk full-benefit dual eligible individuals, identified by the State Medicaid agency.
units.action_summary: Contracts must require the SNP to notify (or arrange notification to) state entities of hospital and SNF admissions for at least one group of high-risk full-benefit dual eligibles.

units.obligation_text: The State Medicaid agency must establish the timeframe(s) and method(s) by which notice is provided.
units.action_summary: The State Medicaid agency must set the timeframes and methods for the required notifications.

units.obligation_text: In the event that a SNP authorizes another entity or entities to perform this notification, the SNP must retain responsibility for complying with the requirement in this paragraph (d)(1).
units.action_summary: Even if the SNP delegates notification, the SNP remains responsible for complying with the notification requirement.

units.obligation_text: For a dual eligible special needs plan that ... only enrolls beneficiaries who are not entitled to full medical assistance ... paragraph (d)(1) of this section does not apply if the SNP operates under the same parent organization and in the same service area as a dual eligible special needs plan limited to beneficiaries with full medical assistance ... that meets the requirements at paragraph (d)(1) of this section.
units.action_summary: Paragraph (d)(1)'s notification requirement does not apply to certain SNPs if they operate under the same parent org and service area as a qualifying plan that meets the requirement.

units.obligation_text: Apply for, and seek CMS approval to establish and maintain, one or more MA contracts that only include one or more dual eligible special needs plans with a service area limited to that State.
units.actor: MA organizations (when required by State Medicaid agency)
units.action_summary: If the State requires, MA organizations must apply to CMS to establish/maintain MA contracts limited to that State for D-SNPs.

units.obligation_text: Use required materials that integrate Medicare and Medicaid content, including at a minimum the Summary of Benefits, Formulary, and combined Provider and Pharmacy Directory that meets MA requirements consistent with § 422.2267(e) and §§ 423.2267(e) and 438.10(h) of this chapter.
units.actor: MA organizations (when required by State Medicaid agency)
units.action_summary: If the State requires, MA organizations must use integrated Medicare-Medicaid materials (Summary of Benefits, Formulary, combined Provider and Pharmacy Directory) meeting specified requirements.

units.obligation_text: The requirements, processes, and procedures applicable to dual eligible special needs plans and the MA program ... remain applicable. ... CMS begins good faith work following receipt of a letter from the State Medicaid agency indicating intent to include the provisions described in paragraph (e)(1) of this section in a future contract year and collaborate with CMS on implementation.
units.action_summary: Upon receiving a letter of intent from the State, CMS will begin good faith work to collaborate on implementing the provisions described in (e)(1).

units.obligation_text: Following a State request, CMS grants access for State Medicaid agency officials to the Health Plan Management System (HPMS) ... as long as State Medicaid agency officials agree to protect the proprietary nature of information ...
units.action_summary: CMS will grant HPMS access to State officials upon request, conditioned on the State officials agreeing to protect proprietary information.

units.obligation_text: CMS may terminate a State official’s access to the Health Plan Management System (or its successor) if any policy is violated or if information is not adequately protected;
units.action_summary: CMS has authority to terminate State officials' HPMS access if policies are violated or information is not protected.

units.obligation_text: CMS coordinates with States on program audits, including information-sharing on major audit findings and coordination of audits schedules for the D–SNPs subject to paragraph (e)(1) of this section.
units.action_summary: CMS will coordinate with States on program audits and information-sharing for affected D-SNPs.

units.obligation_text: Any MA organization offering one or more D–SNPs in a State must establish and maintain one or more enrollee advisory committees that serve the D–SNPs offered by the MA organization in that State.
units.action_summary: MA organizations offering D-SNPs in a State must establish and maintain enrollee advisory committee(s) serving those D-SNPs.

units.obligation_text: The enrollee advisory committee must include at least a reasonably representative sample of the population enrolled in the dual eligible special needs plan or plans, or other individuals representing those enrollees, and solicit input on, among other topics, ways to improve access to covered services, coordination of services, and health equity for underserved populations.
units.action_summary: The committee must be reasonably representative and solicit input on access, coordination, and health equity.

units.obligation_text: The enrollee advisory committee may also advise managed care plans that serve D–SNP enrollees under title XIX of the Act offered by the same parent organization as the MA organization offering the D–SNP.
units.action_summary: The committee is permitted to advise affiliated managed care plans that serve D-SNP enrollees.

units.obligation_text: A plan meets the FIDE SNP or HIDE SNP definition at § 422.2, even if its contract with the State Medicaid agency ... has carve-outs of long-term services and supports, as approved by CMS, that apply primarily to a minority ... or constitute a small part of the total scope ...
units.action_summary: Plans may still qualify as FIDE/HIDE SNPs despite CMS-approved carve-outs of LTSS if the carve-outs meet specified minority/small-part conditions.

units.obligation_text: A plan meets the FIDE SNP or HIDE SNP definition at § 422.2, even if its contract ... has carve-outs of behavioral health services, as approved by CMS, that apply primarily to a minority ... or constitute a small part of the total scope ...
units.action_summary: Plans may still qualify as FIDE/HIDE SNPs despite CMS-approved carve-outs of behavioral health services if carve-outs meet specified conditions.

units.obligation_text: Beginning with contract year 2024, an applicant for a new or expanding service area must demonstrate compliance with this section as part of its application for a new or expanding service area and CMS may deny an application on the basis of an evaluation of the applicant’s network for the new or expanding service area.
units.actor: applicant for a new or expanding service area; CMS
units.action_summary: From 2024, applicants must demonstrate compliance with network adequacy; CMS may deny applications based on network evaluation.

units.obligation_text: Beginning with contract year 2024, an applicant for a new or expanding service area receives a 10-percentage point credit ... at the time of application and for the duration of the application review. At the beginning of the applicable contract year, this credit no longer applies and if the application is approved, the MA organization must be in full compliance with this section.
units.action_summary: From 2024, applicants get a 10-point network credit during application review; if approved, the MA organization must be fully compliant at start of contract year.

units.obligation_text: For the 2023 Star Ratings only, for measures derived from the Health Outcomes Survey only, CMS does not apply the provisions in paragraph (i)(9) or (10) of this section and CMS does not exclude the numeric values for affected contracts with 60 percent or more of their enrollees in the FEMA-designated Individual Assistance area ... from the clustering algorithms or from the determination of the performance summary and variance thresholds for the Reward Factor.
units.action_summary: For 2023 HOS-derived measures, CMS will not apply certain provisions and will not exclude affected contracts' numeric values from clustering or threshold determination.

units.obligation_text: If an MA organization fails during the 12 months preceding the deadline ... to comply with the requirements of the Part C program ... CMS may deny an application based on the applicant’s failure to comply with the requirements of the Part C program under any current or prior contract with CMS even if the applicant currently meets all of the requirements of this part.
units.action_summary: CMS may deny a contract qualification application if the applicant failed to comply with Part C program requirements during the prior 12 months, even if current requirements are met.

units.obligation_text: An applicant may be considered to have failed to comply with a contract for purposes of an application denial ... if during the applicable review period the applicant does any of the following: (A) Was subject to the imposition of an intermediate sanction ... (B) Failed to maintain a fiscally sound operation ... (C) Filed for or is currently in State bankruptcy proceedings. (D) Received 2.5 or less on CMS Star Ratings ... (E) Met or exceeded 13 points for compliance actions.
units.action_summary: CMS may consider an applicant noncompliant for application denial if any listed criteria (A-E) occur during the review period.

units.obligation_text: CMS determines the number of points each MA organization accumulated during the performance period for compliance actions based on the following point values: (i) Each corrective action plan ... counts for 6 points. (ii) Each warning letter ... counts for 3 points. (iii) Each notice of noncompliance ... counts for 1 point.
units.action_summary: CMS assigns points for compliance actions (CAP=6, warning=3, notice=1) to determine if an organization meets the threshold.

units.obligation_text: Not accept, or share a corporate parent organization owning a controlling interest in an entity that accepts, new enrollees under a section 1876 reasonable cost contract in any area in which it seeks to offer an MA plan that is not a dual eligible special needs plan.
units.action_summary: An MA organization (or its corporate parent) must not accept new enrollees under a section 1876 reasonable cost contract in any area where it seeks to offer a non-D-SNP MA plan.

units.obligation_text: Not accept, or be either the parent organization owning a controlling interest of or subsidiary of an entity that accepts, new enrollees under a section 1876 reasonable cost contract in any area in which it seeks to offer an MA plan that is not a dual eligible special needs plan.
units.action_summary: An MA organization, or its parent/subsidiary, must not accept new enrollees under a section 1876 reasonable cost contract in areas where it seeks to offer a non-D-SNP MA plan.

units.obligation_text: The MA organization acknowledges that CMS may take compliance actions ... CMS may take compliance actions as described ... if it determines that the MA organization has not complied with the terms of a current or prior Part C contract with CMS.
units.action_summary: CMS may take compliance actions when it determines an MA organization has failed to comply with Part C contract terms.

units.obligation_text: CMS may determine that an MA organization is out of compliance ... when the organization fails to meet performance standards ... or when its performance ... represents an outlier relative to the performance of other MA organizations.
units.action_summary: CMS can determine noncompliance based on failure to meet standards or outlier performance, even absent a specific measure.

units.obligation_text: CMS bases its decision on whether to issue a compliance action and what level of compliance action to take on an assessment ... including the nature of the conduct; the degree of culpability; adverse effect to beneficiaries; history of prior offenses; whether noncompliance was self-reported; other factors.
units.action_summary: CMS will consider listed factors when deciding whether and what level of compliance action to issue.

units.obligation_text: CMS may take one of three types of compliance actions ... (i) Notice of non-compliance ... (ii) Warning letter ... (iii) Corrective action plan ...
units.action_summary: CMS may issue a notice of non-compliance, a warning letter, or request/issue a corrective action plan depending on the noncompliance.

units.obligation_text: CMS issues a corrective action plan if CMS determines that the MA organization has repeated or not corrected noncompliance identified in prior compliance actions, has substantially impacted beneficiaries or the program with its noncompliance, or must implement a detailed plan to correct the underlying causes of the noncompliance.
units.action_summary: CMS will issue a corrective action plan if the MA organization has repeated/unremedied noncompliance, substantially impacted beneficiaries/program, or needs to implement a corrective plan.

units.obligation_text: When a renewing D–SNP has another new or renewing D–SNP, and the two D–SNPs are offered to different populations, enrollees who are no longer eligible for their current D–SNP may be moved into the other new or renewing D–SNP offered by the same MA organization if they meet the eligibility criteria for the new or renewing D–SNP and CMS determines it is in the best interest of the enrollees to move to the new or renewing D–SNP in order to promote access to and continuity of care ...
units.action_summary: Enrollees may be moved between a renewing and another new/renewing D-SNP offered by same MA org if they meet eligibility and CMS determines the move is in their best interest to promote access/continuity.

units.obligation_text: For the crosswalk exception in this paragraph (c)(4), CMS does not permit enrollees to be moved between different contracts;
units.action_summary: CMS prohibits moving enrollees between different contracts under the crosswalk exception.

units.obligation_text: An MA organization creates a new MA contract when required by a State ... eligible enrollees may be moved from the existing D–SNP that is non-renewing, reducing its service area, or has its eligible population newly restricted by a State, to a D–SNP offered under the D–SNP-only contract, which must be of the same plan type operated by the same parent organization.
units.action_summary: If required by a State to create a new MA contract, eligible enrollees may be moved to the D-SNP under the D-SNP-only contract, which must be same plan type and parent organization.

units.obligation_text: The applicable integrated plan must provide the enrollee a reasonable opportunity, in person and in writing, to present evidence and testimony and make legal and factual arguments for integrated grievances, and integrated reconsiderations; and must provide information on how evidence and testimony should be presented to the plan.
units.action_summary: The integrated plan must give enrollees reasonable opportunities (in person and in writing) to present evidence/testimony and must provide instructions on how to present them.

units.obligation_text: Inform the enrollee of the limited time available for presenting evidence sufficiently in advance of the resolution timeframe for appeals as specified in this section if the case is being considered under an expedited timeframe for the integrated grievance or integrated reconsideration.
units.action_summary: If the case is expedited, the plan must inform the enrollee in advance about limited time for presenting evidence.

units.obligation_text: The following individuals or entities can request an integrated grievance, integrated organization determination, and integrated reconsideration, and are parties to the case: (i) The enrollee. (ii) The enrollee’s representative, including any person authorized under State law.
units.action_summary: Enrollees and their representatives may request integrated grievances/determinations/reconsiderations and are parties to the case.

units.obligation_text: The following individuals or entities may request an integrated reconsideration and are parties to the case: (i) An assignee of the enrollee ... (ii) Any other provider or entity (other than the applicable integrated plan) who has an appealable interest in the proceeding.
units.actor: assignee of enrollee; other providers/entities with appealable interest
units.action_summary: Assignees and other providers/entities with an appealable interest may request integrated reconsiderations and are parties.

units.obligation_text: The applicable integrated plan must process requests for payment according to the 'prompt payment' provisions set forth in § 422.520.
units.action_summary: Integrated plans must process payment requests per § 422.520 prompt payment rules.

units.obligation_text: Applicable integrated plans must accept requests to expedite integrated reconsiderations from either of the following: (i) An enrollee. (ii) A provider, making the request on behalf of an enrollee, that is not a request for expedited payment.
units.action_summary: Integrated plans must accept expedite requests for integrated reconsiderations from enrollees or providers acting on their behalf (except expedited payment requests).

units.obligation_text: The applicable integrated plan may extend the timeframe for resolving any integrated reconsideration other than those concerning Part B drugs by 14 calendar days if—
units.action_summary: The integrated plan is permitted to extend reconsideration timeframes (except for Part B drugs) by 14 days when specified conditions are met.

units.obligation_text: If an applicable integrated plan reverses its decision to deny, limit, or delay services that were not furnished while the appeal was pending, the applicable integrated plan must authorize or provide the disputed services promptly and as expeditiously as the enrollee’s health condition requires but no later than the earlier of: (i) 72 hours from the date it reverses its decision; or (ii)(A) ... 30 calendar days ... (B) For a Part B drug, 7 calendar days ... For a Medicaid benefit, if a State fair hearing officer reverses ... the applicable integrated plan must authorize or provide the disputed services ... no later than 72 hours from the date it receives notice reversing the determination.
units.action_summary: If the plan reverses a denial/limit/delay (or a state hearing reverses), it must promptly provide/authorize disputed services within specified shorter timelines (72 hours, 30 days, or 7 days for Part B drugs).

units.obligation_text: Reversals by the Part C independent review entity, an administrative law judge or attorney adjudicator at the Office of Medicare Hearings and Appeals, or the Medicare Appeals Council must be effectuated under same timelines applicable to other MA plans as specified in §§ 422.618 and 422.619.
units.action_summary: Reversals by review/appeals entities must be implemented according to the timelines in §§ 422.618 and 422.619.

units.obligation_text: Websites must include instructions on how to appoint a representative including a link to the downloadable CMS Appointment of Representative Form (CMS Form–1696); and Enrollment instructions and forms.
units.action_summary: Plan websites are required to provide instructions/link for appointing a representative and include enrollment instructions and forms.

units.obligation_text: The member ID card is a model communications material that plans must provide to enrollees as required under § 422.111(i). The member ID card— (i) Must be provided to new enrollees within ten calendar days from receipt of CMS confirmation of enrollment or by last day of month prior to effective date, whichever is later; (ii) Must include the plan’s website address; customer service number; and contract/PBP number; (iii) Must include, if issued for a PPO and PFFS plan, the phrase 'Medicare limiting charges apply.'; (iv) May not use a member’s Social Security number (SSN), in whole or in part; (v) Must be updated whenever information on a member’s existing card changes; in such cases an updated card must be provided to the member; and (vi) Is excluded from the translation requirement under paragraph (a)(2) of this section.
units.action_summary: Plans must provide member ID cards to new enrollees on a specified timeline, include required information, not use SSNs, update cards when information changes, and the card is excluded from translation requirements.

units.obligation_text: The Multi-language insert (MLI) ... (i) Additional languages that meet the 5-percent service area threshold ... must be added to the MLI used in that service area. A plan may also opt to include ... additional language that do not meet the 5-percent threshold ... (ii) The MLI must be provided with all required materials under paragraph (e) of this section. (iii) The MLI may be included as a part of the required material or as a standalone material ... (iv) When used as a standalone, the MLI may include organization name and logo. (v) When mailing multiple required materials together, only one MLI is required. (vi) The MLI may be provided electronically when a required material is provided electronically as permitted under paragraph (d)(2) of this section.
units.action_summary: Plans must include languages meeting the 5% threshold in the MLI; must provide the MLI with required materials; may include it as part of or separate from required materials; may include name/logo when standalone; only one MLI is required when mailing multiple materials; may provide MLI electronically when allowed.

units.obligation_text: Third-party marketing organization disclaimer ... The MA organization must ensure that the disclaimer is as follows: (i) Used by any TPMO ... that sells plans on behalf of more than one MA organization unless the TPMO sells all commercially available MA plans in a given service area. (ii) Verbally conveyed within the first minute of a sales call. (iii) Electronically conveyed when communicating with a beneficiary through email, online chat, or other electronic means. (iv) Prominently displayed on TPMO websites. (v) Included in any marketing materials, including print materials and television advertisements, developed, used or distributed by the TPMO.
units.action_summary: MA organizations must ensure TPMOs use a standardized disclaimer and convey/display/include it as specified (verbal in first minute, electronic, on websites, in marketing materials).

units.obligation_text: When a TPMO is not otherwise an FDR, the MA organization is responsible for ensuring that the TPMO adheres to any requirements that apply to the MA plan.
units.action_summary: If TPMO is not an FDR, the MA organization must ensure the TPMO complies with MA plan requirements.

units.obligation_text: Contracts, written arrangements, and agreements between the TPMO and an MA plan, or between the TPMO and an MA plan’s FDR, must ensure the TPMO: (i) Discloses to the MA organization any subcontracted relationships used for marketing, lead generation, and enrollment. (ii) Records all calls with beneficiaries in their entirety, including the enrollment process. (iii) Reports to plans monthly any staff disciplinary actions associated with beneficiary interaction to the plan. (iv) Uses the TPMO disclaimer as required under § 422.2267(e)(41).
units.action_summary: MA plan contracts must require TPMOs to disclose subcontractors, record beneficiary calls entirely, report monthly staff disciplinary actions, and use the required TPMO disclaimer.

units.obligation_text: Ensure that the TPMO, when conducting lead generating activities ... must, when applicable: (i) Disclose to the beneficiary that his or her information will be provided to a licensed agent for future contact.
units.action_summary: MA organizations must ensure TPMOs disclose to beneficiaries, when generating leads, that their information will be provided to a licensed agent for future contact.
