title: Medicare Program: Contract Year 2023 Policy and Technical Changes to the Medicare Advantage and Medicare Prescription Drug Benefit Programs; Correction

units.obligation_text: This document corrects technical errors that appeared in the proposed rule published in the Federal Register on January 12, 2022 entitled "Medicare Program; Contract Year 2023 Policy and Technical Changes to the Medicare Advantage and Medicare Prescription Drug Benefit Programs."
units.action_summary: CMS corrects technical errors in the referenced proposed rule.

units.obligation_text: On page 1899, first column, first full paragraph, line 3, the reference "Sec.  422.505(n)" is corrected to read "Sec.  423.505(n)".
units.action_summary: CMS corrects a regulatory citation from Sec. 422.505(n) to Sec. 423.505(n).

units.obligation_text: On page 1925, first column, after the first full paragraph that begins with the phrase "The burden for an initial Part D", the text is corrected by adding the following paragraph to read as follows: "While we anticipate changes to the number of respondents and our active time estimates for the Part C and Part D applications, if this proposal is finalized we would revise control numbers 0938-0935 (CMS-10237) and 0938-0936 (CMS-10137) for the 2025 plan year application and prior to the effective date of the requirement."
units.action_summary: CMS corrects the text by adding a paragraph stating that, if finalized, CMS would revise specified control numbers for the 2025 plan year application prior to the effective date.

units.obligation_text: "If this proposal is finalized we would revise control numbers 0938-0935 (CMS-10237) and 0938-0936 (CMS-10137) for the 2025 plan year application and prior to the effective date of the requirement."
units.action_summary: Conditional on finalization of the proposal, CMS will revise the specified control numbers for the 2025 plan year prior to the requirement's effective date.

units.obligation_text: "The CMS-10237 and CMS-10137 collection of information materials would be made available to the public for review/comment under the standard PRA process which includes the publication of 60- and 30-day Federal Register notices and the posting of the collection of information documents on our PRA website."
units.action_summary: Conditional on the proposal, CMS will make the CMS-10237 and CMS-10137 information collection materials available to the public under the standard PRA process (including 60- and 30-day notices and posting on the PRA website).

title: Medicare Program: FY 2023 Hospice Wage Index and Payment Rate Update and Hospice Quality Reporting Requirements. CMS-1773-P Display

units.obligation_text: Each hospice's labor market is determined based on definitions of Metropolitan Statistical Areas (MSAs) issued by OMB.
units.action_summary: CMS must determine each hospice's labor market using OMB definitions of Metropolitan Statistical Areas (MSAs).

units.obligation_text: CMS will issue annually, in the Federal Register, a hospice wage index based on the most current available CMS hospital wage data, including changes to the definition of MSAs.
units.action_summary: CMS must publish annually in the Federal Register a hospice wage index based on the most current available CMS hospital wage data, including MSA definition changes.

units.obligation_text: The payment rates established by CMS are adjusted by the Medicare contractor to reflect local differences in wages according to the revised wage data.
units.action_summary: The Medicare contractor must adjust CMS-established payment rates to reflect local wage differences according to the revised wage data.

units.obligation_text: Beginning on October 1, 2022, CMS applies a cap on decreases to the hospice wage index.
units.action_summary: Starting October 1, 2022, CMS must apply a cap on decreases to the hospice wage index.

units.obligation_text: The wage index applied to a geographic area is not less than 95 percent of the wage index applied to that geographic area in the prior fiscal year.
units.action_summary: The wage index applied to any geographic area must be at least 95 percent of that area's wage index from the prior fiscal year.

title: Medicare Program: FY 2023 Hospice Wage Index and Payment Rate Update and Hospice Quality Reporting Requirements

units.obligation_text: Each hospice’s labor market is determined based on definitions of Metropolitan Statistical Areas (MSAs) issued by OMB.
units.actor: CMS (the entity determining each hospice's labor market)
units.action_summary: Determine each hospice's labor market using OMB MSA definitions.

units.obligation_text: CMS will issue annually, in the Federal Register, a hospice wage index based on the most current available CMS hospital wage data, including changes to the definition of MSAs.
units.action_summary: Annually publish in the Federal Register a hospice wage index using the most current CMS hospital wage data and any MSA definition changes.

units.obligation_text: The payment rates established by CMS are adjusted by the Medicare contractor to reflect local differences in wages according to the revised wage data.
units.action_summary: Adjust CMS-established payment rates to reflect local wage differences using the revised wage data.

units.obligation_text: Beginning on October 1, 2022, CMS applies a cap on decreases to the hospice wage index such that the wage index applied to a geographic area is not less than 95 percent of the wage index applied to that geographic area in the prior fiscal year.
units.action_summary: Starting 10/1/2022, apply a cap on decreases so an area's hospice wage index is not reduced below 95% of the prior fiscal year value.

units.obligation_text: the wage index applied to a geographic area is not less than 95 percent of the wage index applied to that geographic area in the prior fiscal year.
units.action_summary: Ensure the wage index for a geographic area is at least 95% of that area's prior fiscal year wage index (i.e., prohibit reductions below 95%).

title: CMS-1767-P

units.obligation_text: Completion of patient assessment instrument. For each Medicare part A fee-for-service patient admitted to or discharged from an IRF on or after January 1, 2002, the inpatient rehabilitation facility must complete a patient assessment instrument in accordance with § 412.606.
units.action_summary: Complete a patient assessment instrument for each Medicare Part A fee-for-service patient admitted to or discharged on or after Jan 1, 2002.

units.obligation_text: IRFs must also complete a patient assessment instrument in accordance with § 412.606 for each Medicare Part C (Medicare Advantage) patient admitted to or discharged from an IRF on or after October 1, 2009.
units.action_summary: Complete a patient assessment instrument for each Medicare Part C (Medicare Advantage) patient admitted to or discharged on or after Oct 1, 2009.

units.obligation_text: In addition, IRFs must complete a patient assessment instrument in accordance with § 412.606 for all other patients, regardless of payer, admitted to or discharged from an IRF on or after October 1, 2023.
units.action_summary: Complete a patient assessment instrument for all other patients (regardless of payer) admitted to or discharged on or after Oct 1, 2023.

units.obligation_text: Patient assessment instrument. An inpatient rehabilitation facility must use the CMS inpatient rehabilitation facility patient assessment instrument to assess Medicare Part A fee-for-service and Medicare Part C (Medicare Advantage) inpatients who are admitted on or after January 1, 2002, or were admitted before January 1, 2002, and are still inpatients as of January 1, 2002.
units.action_summary: Use the CMS IRF patient assessment instrument to assess Medicare Part A and Part C inpatients admitted on or after Jan 1, 2002 or admitted before and still inpatients as of that date.

units.obligation_text: Starting on October 1, 2023, inpatient rehabilitation facilities must use the CMS inpatient rehabilitation facility patient assessment instrument to assess all inpatients, regardless of payer, who are admitted on or after October 1, 2023, or who were admitted before October 1, 2023 and are still inpatients as of October 1, 2023.
units.action_summary: Beginning Oct 1, 2023, use the CMS IRF patient assessment instrument to assess all inpatients regardless of payer admitted on or after Oct 1, 2023 or admitted earlier and still inpatients on that date.

units.obligation_text: A clinician of the inpatient rehabilitation facility must perform a comprehensive, accurate, standardized, and reproducible assessment of each Medicare Part A fee-for-service inpatient using the inpatient rehabilitation facility patient assessment instrument specified in paragraph (b) of this section as part of his or her patient assessment in accordance with the schedule described in § 412.610.
units.actor: a clinician of the inpatient rehabilitation facility
units.action_summary: A clinician must perform a comprehensive, accurate, standardized, reproducible assessment of each Medicare Part A fee-for-service inpatient using the IRF patient assessment instrument according to the schedule in §412.610.

units.obligation_text: IRFs must also complete a patient assessment instrument in accordance with §412.606 for each Medicare Part C (Medicare Advantage) patient admitted to or discharged from an IRF on or after October 1, 2009.
units.action_summary: Complete the IRF patient assessment instrument for each Medicare Part C patient admitted or discharged on or after Oct 1, 2009.

units.obligation_text: In addition, IRFs must complete a patient assessment instrument in accordance with § 412.606 for all other patients, regardless of payer, admitted to or discharged from an IRF on or after October 1, 2023.
units.action_summary: Complete the IRF patient assessment instrument for all other patients (regardless of payer) admitted or discharged on or after Oct 1, 2023.

units.obligation_text: For each inpatient, an inpatient rehabilitation facility must complete a patient assessment instrument as specified in § 412.606 that covers a time period that is in accordance with the assessment schedule specified in paragraph (c) of this section.
units.action_summary: For each inpatient, complete an IRF patient assessment instrument covering the time period in accordance with the assessment schedule in §412.610(c).

units.obligation_text: The first day that the inpatient is furnished services during his or her current inpatient rehabilitation facility hospital stay is counted as day one of the patient assessment schedule.
units.actor: the inpatient rehabilitation facility (IRF) (for purposes of counting assessment days)
units.action_summary: Count the first day the patient receives services during current IRF stay as day one of the assessment schedule.

units.obligation_text: The inpatient rehabilitation facility must complete a patient assessment instrument upon the patient’s admission and discharge as specified in paragraphs (c)(1) and (2) of this section.
units.action_summary: Complete the patient assessment instrument at admission and discharge as specified in §412.610(c)(1) and (2).

units.obligation_text: General. Time period is a span of time that covers calendar days 1 through 3 of the patient’s current hospitalization.
units.actor: the inpatient rehabilitation facility (IRF) (for defining time period)
units.action_summary: Define the time period to cover calendar days 1 through 3 of the current hospitalization.

units.obligation_text: The patient stops being furnished inpatient rehabilitation services.
units.actor: the inpatient rehabilitation facility (IRF) (as trigger for discharge assessment)
units.action_summary: Treat cessation of furnishing inpatient rehabilitation services as a trigger (condition) for completion of a discharge patient assessment instrument.

units.obligation_text: Patient assessment instrument record retention. An inpatient rehabilitation facility must maintain all patient assessment data sets completed on all Medicare Part A fee-for-service patients within the previous 5 years, on Medicare Part C (Medicare Advantage) patients within the previous 10 years, and all other patients within the previous 5 years either in a paper format in the patient’s clinical record or in an electronic computer file format that the inpatient rehabilitation facility can easily obtain and produce upon request to CMS or its contractors.
units.action_summary: Maintain patient assessment data sets for specified retention periods and in paper or readily producible electronic format so they can be produced upon request to CMS or contractors.

units.obligation_text: Maintain all patient assessment data sets completed on all Medicare Part A fee-for-service patients within the previous 5 years.
units.action_summary: Retain Medicare Part A patient assessment data sets for 5 years.

units.obligation_text: Maintain all patient assessment data sets completed on Medicare Part C (Medicare Advantage) patients within the previous 10 years.
units.action_summary: Retain Medicare Part C patient assessment data sets for 10 years.

units.obligation_text: Maintain all patient assessment data sets completed on all other patients within the previous 5 years either in a paper format in the patient’s clinical record or in an electronic computer file format that the inpatient rehabilitation facility can easily obtain and produce upon request to CMS or its contractors.
units.action_summary: Retain all other patients' assessment data sets for 5 years in paper or readily producible electronic format.

units.obligation_text: The inpatient rehabilitation facility must encode and transmit data for each inpatient –
units.action_summary: Encode and transmit patient assessment data for each inpatient.

units.obligation_text: Electronically transmit complete, accurate, and encoded data from the patient assessment instrument for each inpatient to our patient data system in accordance with the data format specified in paragraph (a) of this section;
units.action_summary: Electronically transmit complete, accurate, encoded PAI data for each inpatient to CMS's patient data system in the required format.

units.obligation_text: Failure of the inpatient rehabilitation facility to transmit all of the required patient assessment instrument data for its Medicare Part C (Medicare Advantage) patients to our patient data system in accordance with the transmission timeline in paragraph (c) of this section will result in a forfeiture of the facility's ability to have any of its Medicare Part C (Medicare Advantage) data used in the calculations for determining the facility's compliance with the regulations in § 412.29(b)(1).
units.action_summary: If an IRF fails to timely transmit required Medicare Part C PAI data, it forfeits the ability to have any Medicare Part C data used in calculations determining compliance with §412.29(b)(1).

units.obligation_text: Failure of the inpatient rehabilitation facility to transmit all of the required patient assessment instrument data for all other patients, regardless of payer, to our patient data system in accordance with the transmission timeline in paragraph (c) of this section will result in a forfeiture of the facility's ability to have any of its other payer data used in the calculations for determining the facility's compliance with the regulations in § 412.29(b)(1).
units.action_summary: If an IRF fails to timely transmit required PAI data for other payers, it forfeits ability to have any other payer data used in compliance calculations under §412.29(b)(1).

units.obligation_text: CMS may waive the consequences of failure to submit complete and timely IRF-PAI data specified in paragraph (d) of this section when, due to an extraordinary situation that is beyond the control of an inpatient rehabilitation facility, the inpatient rehabilitation facility is unable to transmit the patient assessment data in accordance with paragraph (c) of this section.
units.action_summary: CMS may waive the forfeiture consequences for failure to timely submit IRF-PAI data when an extraordinary situation beyond the facility's control prevents timely transmission.

units.obligation_text: Only CMS can determine if a situation encountered by an inpatient rehabilitation facility is extraordinary and qualifies as a situation for waiver of the forfeiture specified in paragraphs (d)(2) or (3) of this section.
units.action_summary: Only CMS has the authority to determine whether a situation qualifies as extraordinary for waiver purposes.

units.obligation_text: An extraordinary situation must be fully documented by the inpatient rehabilitation facility.
units.action_summary: Fully document any extraordinary situation if seeking a waiver from CMS.

units.obligation_text: Adjustment for area wage levels. The labor portion of a facility's Federal prospective payment is adjusted to account for geographical differences in the area wage levels using an appropriate wage index.
units.action_summary: Adjust the labor portion of Federal prospective payment using an appropriate wage index to reflect geographic wage differences.

units.obligation_text: The application of the wage index is made on the basis of the location of the facility in an urban or rural area as defined in § 412.602.
units.actor: CMS (in applying the wage index) / the wage index application
units.action_summary: Apply the wage index based on whether the facility is located in an urban or rural area as defined in §412.602.

units.obligation_text: Starting on October 1, 2022, CMS applies a cap on decreases to the wage index such that the wage index applied to an IRF is not less than 95 percent of the wage index applied to that IRF in the prior FY.
units.action_summary: Beginning Oct 1, 2022, CMS must cap wage index decreases so an IRF's wage index is at least 95% of the prior fiscal year's wage index.

units.obligation_text: Adjustments or updates to the wage data used to adjust a facility's Federal prospective payment rate under paragraph (e)(1) of this section will be made in a budget neutral manner. CMS determines a budget neutral wage adjustment factor, based on any adjustment or update to the wage data, to apply to the standard payment conversion factor.
units.action_summary: Make adjustments or updates to wage data in a budget-neutral manner; CMS will determine and apply a budget-neutral wage adjustment factor to the payment conversion factor.

units.obligation_text: For discharges on or after October 1, 2005, CMS adjusts the Federal prospective payment on a facility basis by a factor as specified by CMS for facilities that are teaching institutions or units of teaching institutions.
units.action_summary: For discharges on or after Oct 1, 2005, CMS will adjust Federal prospective payments for teaching facilities by a CMS-specified factor.

units.obligation_text: An IRF’s teaching adjustment is based on the ratio of the number of full-time equivalent residents training in the IRF divided by the facility’s average daily census.
units.actor: CMS / inpatient rehabilitation facility (for calculation basis)
units.action_summary: Calculate the teaching adjustment using the ratio of FTE residents to the facility's average daily census.

units.obligation_text: As described in § 412.105(f)(1)(iii)(A), residents with less than full-time status are counted as partial full time equivalent based on the proportion of time assigned to the inpatient rehabilitation facility compared to the total time necessary to fill a residency slot. Residents rotating to more than one hospital or non-hospital setting will be counted in proportion to the time they are assigned to inpatient rehabilitation facility compared to the total time worked in all locations.
units.actor: the inpatient rehabilitation facility (in reporting/counting residents)
units.action_summary: Count residents with less-than-full-time status as partial FTEs proportional to time assigned to the IRF; prorate residents who rotate across settings.

units.obligation_text: An inpatient rehabilitation facility cannot claim time spent by the resident at another inpatient rehabilitation facility or hospital.
units.action_summary: Prohibits an IRF from claiming resident time spent at another IRF or hospital for purposes of the teaching adjustment.

units.obligation_text: Except as described in paragraph (e)(4)(i)(D) of this section, the actual number of current year full-time equivalent residents used in calculating the teaching adjustment is limited to the number of full-time equivalent residents in the IRF’s final settled cost report for the most recent cost reporting period ending on or before November 15, 2004 (base year).
units.actor: the inpatient rehabilitation facility (for reporting) / CMS (for calculation)
units.action_summary: Limit the number of FTE residents used in the teaching adjustment to the number reported in the IRF's final settled cost report for the most recent cost reporting period ending on or before Nov 15, 2004, except as provided in (D).

units.obligation_text: If the inpatient rehabilitation facility first begins training residents in a new approved graduate medical education program after November 15, 2004, the number of full-time equivalent residents determined under paragraph (e)(4)(i)(C) of this section may be adjusted using the method described in § 413.79(e)(1)(i).
units.actor: CMS (in applying adjustments) / the IRF (as subject to adjustment)
units.action_summary: If an IRF begins training in a new approved GME program after Nov 15, 2004, the FTE count used for the teaching adjustment may be adjusted using the method in §413.79(e)(1)(i).

units.obligation_text: The teaching adjustment is made on a claim basis as an interim payment, and the final payment in full for the claim is made during the final settlement of the cost report.
units.action_summary: Apply the teaching adjustment as an interim claim payment; finalize payment during the cost report settlement.

units.obligation_text: For cost reporting periods beginning on or after October 1, 2011, an IRF may receive a temporary adjustment to its FTE cap to reflect displaced residents added because of another IRF's closure if the IRF meets the following criteria:
units.actor: the inpatient rehabilitation facility (IRF) / CMS (as granter of adjustment)
units.action_summary: For cost reporting periods beginning Oct 1, 2011, an IRF may be eligible to receive a temporary FTE cap adjustment to account for displaced residents from another IRF's closure if it meets specified criteria.

units.obligation_text: The IRF is training additional displaced residents from an IRF that closed on or after October 1, 2011.
units.actor: the inpatient rehabilitation facility (IRF) (as eligibility condition)
units.action_summary: Eligibility condition: IRF must be training displaced residents from an IRF that closed on or after Oct 1, 2011.

units.obligation_text: No later than 60 days after the IRF begins to train the displaced residents, the IRF submits a request to its Medicare contractor for a temporary adjustment by identifying the displaced residents who have come from the closed IRF and have caused the IRF to exceed its cap, and specifies the length of time the adjustment is needed.
units.action_summary: Within 60 days of beginning to train displaced residents, submit to Medicare contractor a request identifying displaced residents who caused cap exceedance and specifying the needed adjustment duration.

units.obligation_text: If an IRF that closes its residency training program on or after October 1, 2011, agrees to temporarily reduce its FTE cap according to the criteria specified in paragraph (e)(4)(ii)(A)(2) of this section, another IRF(s) may receive a temporary adjustment to its FTE cap to reflect displaced residents added because of the closure of the residency training program if the criteria specified in paragraph (e)(4)(ii)(A)(1) of this section are met.
units.actor: other IRF(s); CMS (as granter of adjustment)
units.action_summary: If an IRF that closed its residency program agrees to temporarily reduce its FTE cap per criteria, other IRFs may receive temporary FTE cap adjustments to reflect displaced residents if other eligibility criteria are met.

units.obligation_text: For cost reporting periods beginning on or after October 1, 2011, an IRF may receive a temporary adjustment to its FTE cap to reflect displaced residents added because of the closure of another IRF’s residency training program if the IRF is training additional displaced residents from the residency training program of an IRF that closed a program; and if no later than 60 days after the IRF begins to train the displaced residents the IRF submits to its Medicare Contractor a request for a temporary adjustment to its FTE cap, documents that it is eligible for this temporary adjustment by identifying the displaced residents who have come from another IRF’s closed program and have caused the IRF to exceed its cap, specifies the length of time the adjustment is needed, and submits to its Medicare Contractor a copy of the FTE reduction statement by the hospital that closed its program, as specified in paragraph (ii)(A)(2) of this section.
units.action_summary: Receiving IRF may obtain a temporary FTE cap adjustment for displaced residents if training such residents and, within 60 days, submits a request to its Medicare Contractor documenting eligibility, identifying displaced residents, specifying duration, and providing a copy of the closed program's FTE reduction statement.

units.obligation_text: The IRF is training additional displaced residents from the residency training program of an IRF that closed a program.
units.action_summary: Condition: the receiving IRF must be training displaced residents from a closed IRF's residency program.

units.obligation_text: No later than 60 days after the IRF begins to train the displaced residents the IRF submits to its Medicare Contractor a request for a temporary adjustment to its FTE cap
units.action_summary: Submit a request to Medicare Contractor for temporary FTE cap adjustment within 60 days of beginning to train displaced residents.

units.obligation_text: documents that it is eligible for this temporary adjustment by identifying the displaced residents who have come from another IRF’s closed program and have caused the IRF to exceed its cap, specifies the length of time the adjustment is needed,
units.action_summary: Document eligibility by identifying displaced residents causing cap exceedance and specify how long the adjustment is needed.

units.obligation_text: and submits to its Medicare Contractor a copy of the FTE reduction statement by the hospital that closed its program, as specified in paragraph (ii)(A)(2) of this section.
units.action_summary: Submit to Medicare Contractor a copy of the FTE reduction statement from the hospital that closed its program.

units.obligation_text: An IRF that agrees to train displaced residents who have been displaced by the closure of another IRF’s program may receive a temporary FTE cap adjustment only if the hospital with the closed program temporarily reduces its FTE cap based on the FTE of displaced residents in each program year training in the program at the time of the program's closure.
units.actor: the inpatient rehabilitation facility (IRF) that agrees to train displaced residents; the hospital with the closed program
units.action_summary: An IRF training displaced residents may receive a temporary FTE cap adjustment only if the closed-program hospital temporarily reduces its FTE cap based on displaced residents for each program year at time of closure.

units.obligation_text: This yearly reduction in the FTE cap will be determined based on the number of those displaced residents who would have been training in the program during that year had the program not closed.
units.actor: the hospital with the closed program / Medicare Contractor (for determination)
units.action_summary: Determine yearly FTE cap reductions based on the number of displaced residents who would have been training during each program year if the program had not closed.

units.obligation_text: No later than 60 days after the displaced residents who were in the hospital that closed its program(s) begin training at another hospital must submit to its Medicare Contractor a statement signed and dated by its representative that specifies that it agrees to the temporary reduction in its FTE cap to allow the IRF training the displaced residents to obtain a temporary adjustment to its cap; identifies the displaced residents who were in the training at the time of the program’s closure; identifies the IRFs to which the displaced residents are transferring once the program closes; and specifies the reduction for the applicable program years.
units.actor: the hospital that closed its program (or the IRF that closed its program)
units.action_summary: Within 60 days after displaced residents begin training elsewhere, submit to Medicare Contractor a signed, dated statement agreeing to the temporary FTE cap reduction, identifying displaced residents and receiving IRFs, and specifying the reduction for applicable program years.

title: Medicare Program: Inpatient Rehabilitation Facility Prospective Payment System for Federal Fiscal Year 2023 and Updates to the Inpatient Rehabilitation Facility Quality Reporting Program

units.obligation_text: For each Medicare part A fee-for-service patient admitted to or discharged from an IRF on or after January 1, 2002, the inpatient rehabilitation facility must complete a patient assessment instrument in accordance with § 412.606.
units.action_summary: Complete a patient assessment instrument for each Medicare Part A fee-for-service patient admitted to or discharged from the IRF on or after Jan 1, 2002, in accordance with §412.606.

units.obligation_text: IRFs must also complete a patient assessment instrument in accordance with § 412.606 for each Medicare Part C (Medicare Advantage) patient admitted to or discharged from an IRF on or after October 1, 2009.
units.action_summary: Complete a patient assessment instrument for each Medicare Part C (Medicare Advantage) patient admitted to or discharged from the IRF on or after Oct 1, 2009, per §412.606.

units.obligation_text: In addition, IRFs must complete a patient assessment instrument in accordance with § 412.606 for all other patients, regardless of payer, admitted to or discharged from an IRF on or after October 1, 2023.
units.action_summary: Complete a patient assessment instrument for all other patients (regardless of payer) admitted to or discharged from the IRF on or after Oct 1, 2023, per §412.606.

units.obligation_text: An inpatient rehabilitation facility must use the CMS inpatient rehabilitation facility patient assessment instrument to assess Medicare Part A fee-for-service and Medicare Part C (Medicare Advantage) inpatients who are admitted on or after January 1, 2002, or were admitted before January 1, 2002, and are still inpatients as of January 1, 2002.
units.action_summary: Use the CMS IRF patient assessment instrument to assess Medicare Part A and Part C inpatients admitted on or after Jan 1, 2002, or admitted earlier and still inpatients on that date.

units.obligation_text: Starting on October 1, 2023, inpatient rehabilitation facilities must use the CMS inpatient rehabilitation facility patient assessment instrument to assess all inpatients, regardless of payer, who are admitted on or after October 1, 2023, or who were admitted before October 1, 2023 and are still inpatients as of October 1, 2023.
units.action_summary: Beginning Oct 1, 2023, use the CMS IRF patient assessment instrument to assess all inpatients regardless of payer admitted on or after Oct 1, 2023, or admitted earlier and still inpatients on that date.

units.obligation_text: A clinician of the inpatient rehabilitation facility must perform a comprehensive, accurate, standardized, and reproducible assessment of each Medicare Part A fee-for-service inpatient using the inpatient rehabilitation facility patient assessment instrument specified in paragraph (b) of this section as part of his or her patient assessment in accordance with the schedule described in § 412.610.
units.actor: a clinician of the inpatient rehabilitation facility
units.action_summary: Clinicians must perform a comprehensive, accurate, standardized, reproducible assessment of each Medicare Part A inpatient using the IRF patient assessment instrument per the schedule in §412.610.

units.obligation_text: IRFs must also complete a patient assessment instrument in accordance with § 412.606 for each Medicare Part C (Medicare Advantage) patient admitted to or discharged from an IRF on or after October 1, 2009.
units.action_summary: Complete the IRF patient assessment instrument for each Medicare Part C patient admitted to or discharged from the IRF on or after Oct 1, 2009.

units.obligation_text: In addition, IRFs must complete a patient assessment instrument in accordance with § 412.606 for all other patients, regardless of payer, admitted to or discharged from an IRF on or after October 1, 2023.
units.action_summary: Complete the IRF patient assessment instrument for all other patients (regardless of payer) admitted to or discharged from the IRF on or after Oct 1, 2023.

units.obligation_text: For each inpatient, an inpatient rehabilitation facility must complete a patient assessment instrument as specified in § 412.606 that covers a time period that is in accordance with the assessment schedule specified in paragraph (c) of this section.
units.action_summary: For each inpatient, complete the patient assessment instrument specified in §412.606 covering the time period per the assessment schedule in paragraph (c).

units.obligation_text: The inpatient rehabilitation facility must complete a patient assessment instrument upon the patient’s admission and discharge as specified in paragraphs (c)(1) and (2) of this section.
units.action_summary: Complete a patient assessment instrument at patient admission and at discharge as specified in the assessment schedule.

units.obligation_text: An inpatient rehabilitation facility must maintain all patient assessment data sets completed on all Medicare Part A fee-for-service patients within the previous 5 years, on Medicare Part C (Medicare Advantage) patients within the previous 10 years, and all other patients within the previous 5 years either in a paper format in the patient’s clinical record or in an electronic computer file format that the inpatient rehabilitation facility can easily obtain and produce upon request to CMS or its contractors.
units.action_summary: Maintain patient assessment data sets for specified retention periods by payer and keep them in a producible paper or electronic format.

units.obligation_text: Maintain patient assessment data sets completed on Medicare Part A fee-for-service patients within the previous 5 years.
units.action_summary: Retain Medicare Part A patient assessment data sets for 5 years.

units.obligation_text: Maintain patient assessment data sets completed on Medicare Part C (Medicare Advantage) patients within the previous 10 years.
units.action_summary: Retain Medicare Part C patient assessment data sets for 10 years.

units.obligation_text: Maintain patient assessment data sets completed on all other patients within the previous 5 years.
units.action_summary: Retain patient assessment data sets for all other patients for 5 years.

units.obligation_text: The inpatient rehabilitation facility must encode and transmit data for each inpatient—
units.action_summary: Encode and transmit patient assessment data for each inpatient (general rule).

units.obligation_text: Electronically transmit complete, accurate, and encoded data from the patient assessment instrument for each inpatient to our patient data system in accordance with the data format specified in paragraph (a) of this section;
units.action_summary: Electronically transmit complete, accurate, encoded patient assessment instrument data for each inpatient to CMS's patient data system in the specified format.

units.obligation_text: Failure of the inpatient rehabilitation facility to transmit all of the required patient assessment instrument data for its Medicare Part C (Medicare Advantage) patients to our patient data system in accordance with the transmission timeline in paragraph (c) of this section will result in a forfeiture of the facility’s ability to have any of its Medicare Part C (Medicare Advantage) data used in the calculations for determining the facility’s compliance with the regulations in § 412.29(b)(1).
units.action_summary: If the IRF fails to timely transmit required Medicare Part C patient assessment data, it forfeits the ability to have its Medicare Part C data used in compliance calculations under §412.29(b)(1).

units.obligation_text: Failure of the inpatient rehabilitation facility to transmit all of the required patient assessment instrument data for all other patients, regardless of payer, to our patient data system in accordance with the transmission timeline in paragraph (c) of this section will result in a forfeiture of the facility’s ability to have any of its other payer data used in the calculations for determining the facility’s compliance with the regulations in § 412.29(b)(1).
units.action_summary: If the IRF fails to timely transmit required patient assessment data for all other patients, it forfeits the ability to have that other-payer data used in compliance calculations under §412.29(b)(1).

units.obligation_text: CMS may waive the consequences of failure to submit complete and timely IRF–PAI data specified in paragraph (d) of this section when, due to an extraordinary situation that is beyond the control of an inpatient rehabilitation facility, the inpatient rehabilitation facility is unable to transmit the patient assessment data in accordance with paragraph (c) of this section.
units.action_summary: CMS has discretion to waive the forfeiture consequences for late or incomplete IRF–PAI submissions when an extraordinary situation beyond the IRF's control prevents timely transmission.

units.obligation_text: Only CMS can determine if a situation encountered by an inpatient rehabilitation facility is extraordinary and qualifies as a situation for waiver of the forfeiture specified in paragraphs (d)(2) or (3) of this section.
units.action_summary: Only CMS has the authority to decide whether a situation is extraordinary and qualifies for a waiver of forfeiture.

units.obligation_text: An extraordinary situation must be fully documented by the inpatient rehabilitation facility.
units.action_summary: The IRF must fully document any extraordinary situation when seeking a waiver of forfeiture.

units.obligation_text: The labor portion of a facility’s Federal prospective payment is adjusted to account for geographical differences in the area wage levels using an appropriate wage index.
units.actor: CMS (applies adjustment to Federal prospective payment)
units.action_summary: Adjust the labor portion of Federal prospective payments using an appropriate wage index to account for geographical wage differences.

units.obligation_text: The application of the wage index is made on the basis of the location of the facility in an urban or rural area as defined in § 412.602.
units.action_summary: Apply the wage index based on whether the facility's location is urban or rural as defined in §412.602.

units.obligation_text: Starting on October 1, 2022, CMS applies a cap on decreases to the wage index such that the wage index applied to an IRF is not less than 95 percent of the wage index applied to that IRF in the prior FY.
units.action_summary: Beginning Oct 1, 2022, cap decreases to the wage index so it cannot be less than 95% of the prior fiscal year's wage index for the same IRF.

units.obligation_text: Adjustments or updates to the wage data used to adjust a facility’s Federal prospective payment rate under paragraph (e)(1) of this section will be made in a budget neutral manner. CMS determines a budget neutral wage adjustment factor, based on any adjustment or update to the wage data, to apply to the standard payment conversion factor.
units.action_summary: Make wage data adjustments/updates in a budget-neutral manner and determine a budget-neutral wage adjustment factor to apply to the standard payment conversion factor.

units.obligation_text: For discharges on or after October 1, 2005, CMS adjusts the Federal prospective payment on a facility basis by a factor as specified by CMS for facilities that are teaching institutions or units of teaching institutions.
units.action_summary: CMS adjusts Federal prospective payments for teaching IRFs by a facility-level teaching factor for discharges on or after Oct 1, 2005.

units.obligation_text: An IRF’s teaching adjustment is based on the ratio of the number of full-time equivalent residents training in the IRF divided by the facility’s average daily census.
units.action_summary: Calculate the IRF teaching adjustment based on the FTE residents divided by the facility's average daily census.

units.obligation_text: Residents with less than full-time status are counted as partial full time equivalent based on the proportion of time assigned to the inpatient rehabilitation facility compared to the total time necessary to fill a residency slot. Residents rotating to more than one hospital or non-hospital setting will be counted in proportion to the time they are assigned to inpatient rehabilitation facility compared to the total time worked in all locations. An inpatient rehabilitation facility cannot claim time spent by the resident at another inpatient rehabilitation facility or hospital.
units.action_summary: Count part-time and rotating residents as proportional FTEs based on time assigned to the IRF; do not claim time residents spend at other facilities.

units.obligation_text: Except as described in paragraph (e)(4)(i)(D) of this section, the actual number of current year full-time equivalent residents used in calculating the teaching adjustment is limited to the number of full-time equivalent residents in the IRF’s final settled cost report for the most recent cost reporting period ending on or before November 15, 2004 (base year).
units.actor: the inpatient rehabilitation facility (IRF) / CMS (for calculation limit)
units.action_summary: Limit the FTE resident count used for teaching adjustment to the number reported in the IRF's final settled cost report for the base year (period ending on or before Nov 15, 2004), except as provided in (D).

units.obligation_text: If the inpatient rehabilitation facility first begins training residents in a new approved graduate medical education program after November 15, 2004, the number of full-time equivalent residents determined under paragraph (e)(4)(i)(C) of this section may be adjusted using the method described in § 413.79(e)(1)(i).
units.actor: the inpatient rehabilitation facility (IRF) / CMS (for adjustment)
units.action_summary: If the IRF starts training residents in a new approved GME program after Nov 15, 2004, the FTE resident count may be adjusted using the method in §413.79(e)(1)(i).

units.obligation_text: The teaching adjustment is made on a claim basis as an interim payment, and the final payment in full for the claim is made during the final settlement of the cost report.
units.action_summary: Make the teaching adjustment as an interim claim payment; finalize full payment during final cost report settlement.

units.obligation_text: For cost reporting periods beginning on or after October 1, 2011, an IRF may receive a temporary adjustment to its FTE cap to reflect displaced residents added because of another IRFs closure if the IRF meets the following criteria:
units.action_summary: An IRF may receive a temporary FTE cap adjustment for displaced residents from a closed IRF for cost reporting periods beginning on or after Oct 1, 2011, if specified criteria are met.

units.obligation_text: The IRF is training additional displaced residents from an IRF that closed on or after October 1, 2011.
units.action_summary: Criterion: IRF must be training displaced residents from an IRF that closed on or after Oct 1, 2011.

units.obligation_text: No later than 60 days after the IRF begins to train the displaced residents, the IRF submits a request to its Medicare contractor for a temporary adjustment by identifying the displaced residents who have come from the closed IRF and have caused the IRF to exceed its cap, and specifies the length of time the adjustment is needed.
units.action_summary: Within 60 days of beginning to train displaced residents, submit a request to the Medicare contractor identifying the displaced residents, the cap exceedance, and the length of the temporary adjustment needed.

units.obligation_text: If an IRF that closes its residency training program on or after October 1, 2011, agrees to temporarily reduce its FTE cap according to the criteria specified in paragraph (e)(4)(ii)(A)(2) of this section, another IRF(s) may receive a temporary adjustment to its FTE cap to reflect displaced residents added because of the closure of the residency training program if the criteria specified in paragraph (e)(4)(ii)(A)(1) of this section are met.
units.actor: receiving IRF(s) and the IRF that closed its residency program
units.action_summary: If the closed IRF agrees to temporarily reduce its FTE cap per criteria, other IRFs may receive temporary FTE cap adjustments to reflect displaced residents if qualifying criteria are met.

units.obligation_text: For cost reporting periods beginning on or after October 1, 2011, an IRF may receive a temporary adjustment to its FTE cap to reflect displaced residents added because of the closure of another IRF’s residency training program if the IRF is training additional displaced residents from the residency training program of an IRF that closed a program; and if no later than 60 days after the IRF begins to train the displaced residents the IRF submits to its Medicare Contractor a request for a temporary adjustment to its FTE cap, documents that it is eligible for this temporary adjustment by identifying the displaced residents who have come from another IRF’s closed program and have caused the IRF to exceed its cap, specifies the length of time the adjustment is needed, and submits to its Medicare Contractor a copy of the FTE reduction statement by the hospital that closed its program, as specified in paragraph (ii)(A)(2) of this section.
units.action_summary: Receiving IRF may get a temporary FTE cap adjustment for displaced residents from a closed residency program if it submits a request within 60 days identifying displaced residents, documents eligibility, specifies length of adjustment, and provides a copy of the closed hospital's FTE reduction statement.

units.obligation_text: An IRF that agrees to train displaced residents who have been displaced by the closure of another IRF’s program may receive a temporary FTE cap adjustment only if the hospital with the closed program temporarily reduces its FTE cap based on the FTE of displaced residents in each program year training in the program at the time of the programs closure.
units.actor: IRF that closed its program (hospital with closed program) and receiving IRF
units.action_summary: Receiving IRF's eligibility for temporary FTE cap adjustment depends on the closed program hospital temporarily reducing its FTE cap based on displaced residents for each program year at closure.

units.obligation_text: No later than 60 days after the displaced residents who were in the hospital that closed its program(s) begin training at another hospital must submit to its Medicare Contractor a statement signed and dated by its representative that specifies that it agrees to the temporary reduction in its FTE cap to allow the IRF training the displaced residents to obtain a temporary adjustment to its cap; identifies the displaced residents who were in the training at the time of the program’s closure; identifies the IRFs to which the displaced residents are transferring once the program closes; and specifies the reduction for the applicable program years.
units.actor: the hospital with the closed residency program (the closed IRF)
units.action_summary: Within 60 days after displaced residents begin training elsewhere, the closed-hospital must submit a signed and dated statement to its Medicare Contractor agreeing to the temporary FTE cap reduction, identifying displaced residents and receiving IRFs, and specifying the yearly cap reductions.

title: Medicare Program; FY 2023 Inpatient Psychiatric Facilities Prospective Payment System – Rate Update. CMS-1769-P

units.obligation_text: CMS adjusts the labor portion of the Federal per diem base rate to account for geographic differences in the area wage levels using an appropriate wage index.
units.action_summary: Adjust the labor portion of the Federal per diem base rate using an appropriate wage index to account for geographic wage differences.

units.obligation_text: The application of the wage index is made on the basis of the location of the inpatient psychiatric facility in an urban or rural area as defined in § 412.402.
units.action_summary: Apply the wage index based on whether the inpatient psychiatric facility is located in an urban or rural area as defined in § 412.402.

units.obligation_text: Beginning October 1, 2022, CMS applies a cap on decreases to the wage index, such that the wage index applied to an inpatient psychiatric facility is not less than 95 percent of the wage index applied to that inpatient psychiatric facility in the prior fiscal year.
units.action_summary: Beginning Oct 1, 2022, apply a cap on decreases so the wage index for an inpatient psychiatric facility is not reduced below 95 percent of the prior fiscal year value.

units.obligation_text: The wage index applied to an inpatient psychiatric facility is not less than 95 percent of the wage index applied to that inpatient psychiatric facility in the prior fiscal year.
units.action_summary: Ensure the wage index applied to a facility is at least 95 percent of the wage index that facility had in the prior fiscal year.

title: Medicare Program: Fiscal Year 2023 Inpatient Psychiatric Facilities Prospective Payment System-Rate Update and Quality Reporting

units.obligation_text: Adjustment for wages. CMS adjusts the labor portion of the Federal per diem base rate to account for geographic differences in the area wage levels using an appropriate wage index.
units.action_summary: CMS must adjust the labor portion of the Federal per diem base rate using an appropriate wage index to account for geographic differences in area wage levels.

units.obligation_text: The application of the wage index is made on the basis of the location of the inpatient psychiatric facility in an urban or rural area as defined in § 412.402.
units.action_summary: Apply the wage index based on whether the inpatient psychiatric facility is located in an urban or rural area as defined in § 412.402.

units.obligation_text: Beginning October 1, 2022, CMS applies a cap on decreases to the wage index, such that the wage index applied to an inpatient psychiatric facility is not less than 95 percent of the wage index applied to that inpatient psychiatric facility in the prior fiscal year.
units.action_summary: Starting October 1, 2022, CMS must cap decreases so a facility's wage index is at least 95% of the wage index applied to that facility in the prior fiscal year.

title: CMS-1765-P

units.obligation_text: The cost data are standardized for geographic variation in wage levels using the wage index. The application of the wage index is made on the basis of the location of the facility in an urban or rural area as defined in §413.333.
units.action_summary: Standardize cost data for geographic wage variation using the wage index applied based on facility urban/rural location.

units.obligation_text: Starting on October 1, 2022, CMS applies a cap on decreases to the wage index such that the wage index applied to a SNF is not less than 95 percent of the wage index applied to that SNF in the prior FY.
units.action_summary: Apply a cap on wage index decreases so a SNF's wage index is at least 95% of prior FY's wage index, effective Oct 1, 2022.

units.obligation_text: The cost data are standardized for facility variation in case-mix using the case-mix indices and other data that indicate facility case-mix.
units.action_summary: Standardize cost data for facility case-mix variation using case-mix indices and other facility case-mix data.

units.obligation_text: The SNF VBP Program applies to SNFs, including facilities described in section 1888(e)(7)(B) of the Act.
units.actor: SNFs (are subject to the SNF VBP Program)
units.action_summary: The SNF Value-Based Purchasing Program is applicable to SNFs, including specified facilities.

units.obligation_text: Beginning with fiscal year 2023, the SNF VBP Program does not include a SNF, with respect to a fiscal year, if the SNF does not have the minimum number of cases that applies to each measure for the fiscal year, as specified by CMS.
units.action_summary: Exclude a SNF from the SNF VBP Program for a fiscal year if it lacks the minimum number of cases for each measure as specified by CMS.

units.obligation_text: Beginning with fiscal year 2023, the SNF VBP Program does not include a SNF, with respect to a fiscal year, if the SNF does not have the minimum number of measures for the fiscal year, as specified by CMS.
units.action_summary: Exclude a SNF from the SNF VBP Program for a fiscal year if it does not have the minimum number of measures specified by CMS.

units.obligation_text: The total amount available for value-based incentive payments for a fiscal year is at least 60 percent of the total amount of the reduction to the adjusted SNF PPS payments for that fiscal year, as estimated by CMS, and will be increased as appropriate for each fiscal year to account for the assignment of a performance score to low-volume SNFs under paragraph (d)(3) of this section. Beginning with the FY 2023 SNF VBP, the total amount for value-based incentive payments for a fiscal year is 60 percent of the total amount of the reduction to the adjusted SNF PPS payments for that fiscal year, as estimated by CMS.
units.action_summary: Set aside at least 60% of the reduction to adjusted SNF PPS payments for value-based incentive payments each fiscal year; for FY2023 specifically set at 60%, and increase as appropriate to account for low-volume SNFs.

units.obligation_text: and will be increased as appropriate for each fiscal year to account for the assignment of a performance score to low-volume SNFs under paragraph (d)(3) of this section.
units.action_summary: Increase the total amount for value-based incentive payments as appropriate to account for assigning performance scores to low-volume SNFs.

units.obligation_text: Beginning with the FY 2023 SNF VBP, the total amount for value-based incentive payments for a fiscal year is 60 percent of the total amount of the reduction to the adjusted SNF PPS payments for that fiscal year, as estimated by CMS.
units.action_summary: For FY2023, set the total amount for value-based incentive payments at 60% of the reduction to adjusted SNF PPS payments.

units.obligation_text: If, with respect to a fiscal year beginning with fiscal year 2019 through and including fiscal year 2022, CMS determines that a SNF is a low-volume SNF, CMS will assign a performance score to the SNF for the fiscal year that, when used to calculate the value-based incentive payment amount (as defined in paragraph (a)(17) of this section), results in a value-based incentive payment amount that is equal to the adjusted Federal per diem rate (as defined in paragraph (a)(2) of this section) that would apply to the SNF for the fiscal year without application of § 413.337(f).
units.action_summary: Assign a performance score to low-volume SNFs for FY2019–FY2022 that yields a value-based incentive payment amount equal to the adjusted Federal per diem rate without applying §413.337(f).

units.obligation_text: CMS will specify the measures for application in the SNF VBP Program for a given fiscal year.
units.action_summary: CMS will designate which measures apply in the SNF VBP Program for each fiscal year.

units.obligation_text: Performance standards are announced no later than 60 days prior to the start of the performance period that applies to that measure for that fiscal year.
units.action_summary: Announce performance standards at least 60 days before the start of the performance period for the measure.

units.obligation_text: Beginning with the performance standards that apply to FY 2021, if CMS discovers an error in the performance standard calculations subsequent to publishing their numerical values for a fiscal year, CMS will update the numerical values to correct the error.
units.action_summary: If CMS finds an error in published performance standard calculations (starting with FY2021), it will update the numerical values to correct the error.

units.obligation_text: If CMS subsequently discovers one or more other errors with respect to the same fiscal year, CMS will not further update the numerical values for that fiscal year.
units.action_summary: If additional errors are discovered for the same fiscal year, CMS will not make further updates to the numerical values for that year.

units.obligation_text: CMS will award points to SNFs based on their performance on each measure for which the SNF reports the applicable minimum number of cases during the performance period applicable to that fiscal year as follows:
units.action_summary: CMS will award performance points to SNFs for each applicable measure when the SNF reports the minimum number of cases.

units.obligation_text: CMS will award from 1 to 9 points for achievement to each SNF whose performance on a measure during the applicable performance period meets or exceeds the achievement threshold for that measure but is less than the benchmark for that measure.
units.action_summary: Award 1–9 achievement points to SNFs whose measure performance meets/exceeds the achievement threshold but is below the benchmark.

units.obligation_text: CMS will award 10 points for achievement to a SNF whose performance on a measure during the applicable performance period meets or exceeds the benchmark for that measure.
units.action_summary: Award 10 achievement points to SNFs whose measure performance meets or exceeds the benchmark.

units.obligation_text: CMS will award from 0 to 9 points for improvement to each SNF whose performance on a measure during the applicable performance period exceeds the improvement threshold but is less than the benchmark for that measure.
units.action_summary: Award 0–9 improvement points to SNFs whose measure performance exceeds the improvement threshold but is below the benchmark.

units.obligation_text: CMS will not award points for improvement to a SNF that does not meet the case minimum for a measure for the applicable baseline period.
units.action_summary: Do not award improvement points to SNFs that fail to meet the case minimum for the measure in the applicable baseline period.

units.obligation_text: The highest of the SNF’s achievement and improvement score for a given measure will be the SNF’s score on that measure for the applicable fiscal year.
units.action_summary: Use the higher of achievement and improvement scores as the SNF's score for each measure for the fiscal year.

units.obligation_text: The SNF performance score for a fiscal year is calculated as follows:
units.action_summary: Defines the method for calculating the SNF performance score for a fiscal year.

units.obligation_text: CMS will sum all points awarded to a SNF as described in paragraph (e) of this section for each measure applicable to a fiscal year to calculate the SNF’s point total.
units.action_summary: Sum all points awarded across measures to calculate each SNF's point total for the fiscal year.

units.obligation_text: CMS will normalize the point total such that the resulting SNF performance score is expressed as a number of points earned out of a total of 100.
units.action_summary: Normalize the SNF point total to produce a performance score expressed out of 100.

units.obligation_text: CMS will provide quarterly confidential feedback reports to SNFs on their performance on each measure specified for the fiscal year. Beginning with the baseline period and performance period quality measure quarterly reports issued on or after October 1, 2021, which contain the baseline period and performance period measure rates, respectively, SNFs will have 30 days following the date CMS provides each of these reports to review and submit corrections to the measure rates contained in that report. The administrative claims data used to calculate measure rates are not subject to review and correction under paragraph (e)(1) of this section. All correction requests must be accompanied by appropriate evidence showing the basis for the correction to each of the applicable measure rates.
units.action_summary: CMS must provide quarterly confidential feedback reports; SNFs have 30 days to review and submit corrections; administrative claims data are not subject to review/correction; correction requests must include evidence.
units.modal_raw: will provide / will have / are not subject / must be accompanied

units.obligation_text: SNFs will have 30 days following the date CMS provides each of these reports to review and submit corrections to the measure rates contained in that report.
units.action_summary: SNFs may review and submit corrections to the report's measure rates within 30 days after CMS provides the reports.

units.obligation_text: The administrative claims data used to calculate measure rates are not subject to review and correction under paragraph (e)(1) of this section.
units.action_summary: Administrative claims data cannot be reviewed or corrected by SNFs under the specified paragraph.

units.obligation_text: All correction requests must be accompanied by appropriate evidence showing the basis for the correction to each of the applicable measure rates.
units.action_summary: SNFs must include appropriate evidence with any correction requests to measure rates.

units.obligation_text: CMS will publicly report the information described in paragraphs (f)(1) and (2) of this section on the Nursing Home Compare website or a successor website.
units.action_summary: CMS will publicly report the information from paragraphs (f)(1) and (f)(2) on Nursing Home Compare or successor.

units.obligation_text: If a SNF does not have the minimum number of cases during the baseline period that applies to a measure for a fiscal year, CMS will not publicly report the SNF’s baseline period measure rate for that particular measure,
units.action_summary: Do not publicly report a SNF's baseline period measure rate for a measure if the SNF lacks the minimum number of baseline cases.

units.obligation_text: although CMS will publicly report the SNF’s performance period measure rate and achievement score if the SNF had the minimum number of cases for the measure during the performance period of the same program year;
units.action_summary: If the SNF met the minimum number of performance-period cases, CMS will publicly report the SNF's performance period measure rate and achievement score even if baseline rate is not reported.

units.obligation_text: If a SNF does not have the minimum number of cases during the performance period that applies to a measure for a fiscal year, CMS will not publicly report any information with respect to the SNF’s performance on that measure for the fiscal year;
units.action_summary: If a SNF lacks the minimum number of performance-period cases for a measure, CMS will not publicly report any information about that SNF's performance on that measure for the fiscal year.

units.obligation_text: If a SNF does not have the minimum number of measures during the performance period for a fiscal year, CMS will not publicly report any data for that SNF for the fiscal year.
units.action_summary: If a SNF does not have the minimum number of measures during the performance period, CMS will not publicly report any data for that SNF for that fiscal year.

units.obligation_text: Special rules for the FY 2023 SNF VBP Program.
units.action_summary: Header indicating special rules applicable to the FY2023 SNF VBP Program (details follow in (i)(1)-(4)).

units.obligation_text: CMS will calculate a SNF readmission measure rate for each SNF based on its performance on the SNF readmission measure during the performance period specified by CMS for fiscal year 2023,
units.action_summary: Calculate a SNF readmission measure rate for each SNF using their FY2023 performance period data.

units.obligation_text: If ... CMS determines that a SNF is a low-volume SNF, CMS will assign a performance score to the SNF for the fiscal year that ... results in a value-based incentive payment amount that is equal to the adjusted Federal per diem rate ... that would apply to the SNF for the fiscal year without application of § 413.337(f).

units.obligation_text: Beginning with the performance standards that apply to FY 2021, if CMS discovers an error in the performance standard calculations subsequent to publishing their numerical values for a fiscal year, CMS will update the numerical values to correct the error.

units.obligation_text: If CMS subsequently discovers one or more other errors with respect to the same fiscal year, CMS will not further update the numerical values for that fiscal year.

units.obligation_text: CMS will award points to SNFs based on their performance on each measure for which the SNF reports the applicable minimum number of cases during the performance period applicable to that fiscal year as follows:

units.obligation_text: CMS will award from 1 to 9 points for achievement to each SNF whose performance on a measure during the applicable performance period meets or exceeds the achievement threshold for that measure but is less than the benchmark for that measure.
units.action_summary: CMS will award 1–9 achievement points to SNFs whose performance is between the achievement threshold and the benchmark.

units.obligation_text: CMS will award 10 points for achievement to a SNF whose performance on a measure during the applicable performance period meets or exceeds the benchmark for that measure.
units.action_summary: CMS will award 10 achievement points to SNFs that meet or exceed the benchmark for a measure.

units.obligation_text: CMS will award from 0 to 9 points for improvement to each SNF whose performance on a measure during the applicable performance period exceeds the improvement threshold but is less than the benchmark for that measure.
units.action_summary: CMS will award 0–9 improvement points to SNFs whose performance exceeds the improvement threshold but is below the benchmark.

units.obligation_text: CMS will not award points for improvement to a SNF that does not meet the case minimum for a measure for the applicable baseline period.
units.action_summary: CMS will not give improvement points to SNFs that fail to meet the case minimum for the measure's baseline period.

units.obligation_text: The highest of the SNF’s achievement and improvement score for a given measure will be the SNF’s score on that measure for the applicable fiscal year.
units.action_summary: CMS will use the higher of a SNF's achievement or improvement score as its score for a measure for the fiscal year.

units.obligation_text: The SNF performance score for a fiscal year is calculated as follows:
units.action_summary: CMS will calculate each SNF's performance score for the fiscal year according to the following steps.

units.obligation_text: CMS will sum all points awarded to a SNF as described in paragraph (e) of this section for each measure applicable to a fiscal year to calculate the SNF’s point total.
units.action_summary: CMS will add up all points awarded across measures to get a SNF's point total.

units.obligation_text: CMS will normalize the point total such that the resulting SNF performance score is expressed as a number of points earned out of a total of 100.
units.action_summary: CMS will normalize the SNF's point total to a 0–100 scale to produce the performance score.

title: Medicare Program: End-Stage Renal Disease Prospective Payment System, Payment for Renal Dialysis Services Furnished to Individuals With Acute Kidney Injury, etc.

units.obligation_text: For purposes of paragraph (d)(1) of this section, the baseline period that applies to each of payment year 2023 and payment year 2024 is calendar year 2019 for purposes of calculating the achievement threshold, benchmark and minimum total performance score, and calendar year 2019 for purposes of calculating the improvement threshold.
units.actor: the baseline period applicable to payment years 2023 and 2024 / CMS (for calculation purposes)
units.action_summary: The baseline period for payment years 2023 and 2024 is calendar year 2019 for calculating achievement threshold, benchmark, minimum total performance score, and improvement threshold.

units.obligation_text: The baseline period that applies to payment year 2025 is calendar year 2021 for purposes of calculating the achievement threshold, benchmark and minimum total performance score, and calendar year 2022 for purposes of calculating the improvement threshold, and the performance period that applies to payment year 2025 is calendar year 2023.
units.actor: the baseline and performance periods applicable to payment year 2025 / CMS (for calculation purposes)
units.action_summary: For payment year 2025, the baseline period for achievement/benchmark/mTPS is calendar year 2021, the baseline period for the improvement threshold is calendar year 2022, and the performance period is calendar year 2023.

units.obligation_text: Beginning with payment year 2026, the performance period and corresponding baseline periods are each advanced 1 year for each successive payment year.
units.actor: the performance period and baseline periods / CMS (for calculation purposes)
units.action_summary: Starting with payment year 2026, for each successive payment year the performance and corresponding baseline periods advance by one year.

units.obligation_text: CMS will calculate a measure rate for, but will not score facility performance on or include in the TPS for any facility under paragraph (e) of this section, the following measures: Standardized Hospitalization Ratio (SHR) clinical measure, Standardized Readmission Ratio (SRR) clinical measure, Long-Term Catheter Rate clinical measure, ICH CAHPS clinical measure, Percentage of Prevalent Patients Waitlisted (PPPW) clinical measure, and Kt/V Dialysis Adequacy clinical measure.
units.action_summary: CMS will calculate measure rates for the listed measures but will not score facility performance on them or include them in the TPS for any facility under paragraph (e).

units.obligation_text: Standardized Hospitalization Ratio (SHR) clinical measure.
units.actor: CMS (specification of measures to which the calculation/no-score/no-include rule applies)
units.action_summary: Specifies that the SHR clinical measure is subject to CMS calculating the measure rate but not scoring or including it in the TPS.

units.obligation_text: Standardized Readmission Ratio (SRR) clinical measure.
units.actor: CMS (specification of measures to which the calculation/no-score/no-include rule applies)
units.action_summary: Specifies that the SRR clinical measure is subject to CMS calculating the measure rate but not scoring or including it in the TPS.

units.obligation_text: Long-Term Catheter Rate clinical measure.
units.actor: CMS (specification of measures to which the calculation/no-score/no-include rule applies)
units.action_summary: Specifies that the Long-Term Catheter Rate clinical measure is subject to CMS calculating the measure rate but not scoring or including it in the TPS.

units.obligation_text: ICH CAHPS clinical measure.
units.actor: CMS (specification of measures to which the calculation/no-score/no-include rule applies)
units.action_summary: Specifies that the ICH CAHPS clinical measure is subject to CMS calculating the measure rate but not scoring or including it in the TPS.

units.obligation_text: Percentage of Prevalent Patients Waitlisted (PPPW) clinical measure.
units.actor: CMS (specification of measures to which the calculation/no-score/no-include rule applies)
units.action_summary: Specifies that the PPPW clinical measure is subject to CMS calculating the measure rate but not scoring or including it in the TPS.

units.obligation_text: Kt/V Dialysis Adequacy clinical measure.
units.actor: CMS (specification of measures to which the calculation/no-score/no-include rule applies)
units.action_summary: Specifies that the Kt/V Dialysis Adequacy clinical measure is subject to CMS calculating the measure rate but not scoring or including it in the TPS.

units.obligation_text: Beginning January 1, 2023, CMS applies a cap on decreases to the wage index, such that the wage index applied to an ESRD facility is not less than 95 percent of the wage index applied to that ESRD facility in the prior calendar year.
units.action_summary: Starting Jan 1, 2023, CMS must limit decreases to an ESRD facility's wage index so it is at least 95% of the wage index from the prior year.

units.obligation_text: The wage index applied to an ESRD facility is not less than 95 percent of the wage index applied to that ESRD facility in the prior calendar year.
units.actor: the wage index applied to an ESRD facility / CMS (for implementation)
units.action_summary: The wage index for an ESRD facility must be no less than 95% of its prior-year wage index.

units.obligation_text: Beginning January 1, 2023, CMS applies a floor of 0.6000 to the wage index, such that the wage index applied to an ESRD facility is not less than 0.6000.
units.action_summary: Starting Jan 1, 2023, CMS must ensure the wage index for an ESRD facility is no less than 0.6000.

units.obligation_text: The wage index applied to an ESRD facility is not less than 0.6000.
units.actor: the wage index applied to an ESRD facility / CMS (for implementation)
units.action_summary: The wage index for an ESRD facility must be at least 0.6000.

units.obligation_text: For MY5 through MY10, CMS will assign an achievement score to an ETC Participant for the home dialysis rate or the transplant rate only if the ETC Participant’s aggregation group has a home dialysis rate or a transplant rate greater than zero for the MY.
units.action_summary: For MY5–MY10, CMS will assign an achievement score for home dialysis or transplant rate only when the ETC Participant's aggregation group has a corresponding rate greater than zero for that performance year.

units.obligation_text: The ETC Participant’s aggregation group has a home dialysis rate or a transplant rate greater than zero for the MY.
units.action_summary: The aggregation group must have a home dialysis or transplant rate > 0 in the performance year for CMS to assign an achievement score.

units.obligation_text: CMS waives the requirement under section 1861(ggg)(2)(A)(i) of the Act and § 410.48(a) of this chapter that only doctors, physician assistants, nurse practitioners, and clinical nurse specialists can furnish kidney disease patient education services to allow kidney disease patient education services to be provided by clinical staff (as defined at § 512.310) under the direction of and incident to the services of the Managing Clinician who is an ETC Participant.
units.actor: CMS (action: waiver); clinical staff (effect: permitted providers)
units.action_summary: CMS waives the statutory requirement limiting who may furnish kidney disease patient education services, permitting clinical staff (as defined) to provide those services under the direction of the Managing Clinician who is an ETC Participant.

units.obligation_text: The kidney disease patient education services may be furnished only by qualified staff (as defined at § 512.310).
units.action_summary: Kidney disease patient education services may be provided only by staff who meet the definition of qualified staff in § 512.310.

units.obligation_text: Beginning MY5, only clinical staff that are not leased from or otherwise provided by an ESRD facility or related entity may furnish kidney disease patient education services pursuant to the waiver described in this section.
units.actor: clinical staff not leased from or otherwise provided by an ESRD facility or related entity
units.action_summary: Starting in MY5, only clinical staff who are not leased from or provided by an ESRD facility or related entity may provide kidney disease patient education services under this waiver.

title: Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments Fees: Histocompatibility, Personnel, and Alternative Sanctions for Certificate of Waiver Laboratories

units.obligation_text: The CE credit hours must cover the applicable laboratory director responsibilities and be obtained prior to qualifying as a laboratory director.
units.action_summary: CE credit hours covering director responsibilities must be obtained before qualifying as a laboratory director.

units.obligation_text: Experience directing or supervising means that the director or supervisory experience must be obtained in a facility that meets the definition of a laboratory under this section and is not excepted under § 493.3(b).
units.action_summary: Director/supervisory experience must be obtained in a facility that qualifies as a laboratory and is not excepted under §493.3(b).

units.obligation_text: Laboratory training or experience means that the training or experience must be obtained in a facility that meets the definition of a laboratory under this section and is not excepted under § 493.3(b).
units.action_summary: Laboratory training/experience must be obtained in a facility that meets the definition of a laboratory and is not excepted under §493.3(b).

units.obligation_text: Laboratories must pay a fee that covers the costs incurred for the issuance, renewal, change in certificate type, or reinstatement of a terminated certificate with a gap in service, and other direct administrative costs, as applicable.
units.action_summary: Laboratories are required to pay fees covering various certificate-related and administrative costs.

units.obligation_text: For registration certificates, the fee is a flat fee that includes the costs for issuing the certificates, collecting the fees, and evaluating whether the procedures, tests, or examinations listed on the application fall within the testing allowed for the requested certificate.
units.action_summary: Registration certificate fee is flat and includes issuing, collecting, and evaluating application test scope costs.

units.obligation_text: For a certificate of waiver, the fee includes the costs for issuing the certificate; collecting the fees; evaluating whether the procedures, tests, or examinations listed on the application fall within the testing appropriate for the requested certificate; and determining whether a laboratory test meets the criteria for a waived test.
