units.action_summary: Waiver certificate fee covers issuance, collection, evaluation of test appropriateness, and determination of waived test criteria.

units.obligation_text: For a certificate for PPM procedures, the fee includes the costs for issuing the certificate, collecting the fees; and evaluating whether the procedures, tests, or examinations listed on the application meet the criteria for inclusion in the subcategory of PPM procedures.
units.action_summary: PPM certificate fee covers issuance, collection, and evaluation of PPM procedure criteria.

units.obligation_text: For a certificate of accreditation, the fee includes the costs for issuing the certificate, collecting the fees, evaluating the programs of accrediting bodies, and evaluating whether the procedures, tests, or examinations listed on the application fall within the testing appropriate for the requested certificate.
units.action_summary: Accreditation certificate fee includes issuance, collection, accreditor program evaluation, and test appropriateness evaluation costs.

units.obligation_text: For a certificate of compliance, the fee includes the costs for issuing the certificates, collecting the fees, evaluating and monitoring proficiency testing programs, and evaluating whether the procedures, tests or examinations listed on the application fall within the testing appropriate for the requested certificate.
units.action_summary: Compliance certificate fee covers issuance, collection, proficiency testing evaluation/monitoring, and test appropriateness evaluation costs.

units.obligation_text: The certificate fee amount is set biennially by HHS.
units.action_summary: HHS establishes certificate fee amounts every two years.

units.obligation_text: CMS will publish a notice in the Federal Register biennially with any adjustments to the fee amounts, including any adjustments due to inflation, in accordance with § 493.680.
units.action_summary: CMS will publish a biennial Federal Register notice with fee adjustments and inflation adjustments.

units.obligation_text: Certificate fees are assessed and payable at least biennially.
units.action_summary: Laboratories must pay assessed certificate fees at least every two years.

units.obligation_text: The amount of the fee payable by the laboratory is the amount listed in the most recent notice published in the Federal Register at the time the application, renewal, change in certificate type, or reinstatement is processed by HHS or its designee.
units.action_summary: Laboratories owe the fee amount shown in the most recent Federal Register notice when their transaction is processed.

units.obligation_text: After processing an application for an issuance, renewal, change in certificate type, or reinstatement of a terminated certificate with a gap in service, HHS or its designee notifies the laboratory of the applicable fee amount.
units.action_summary: HHS notifies laboratories of the applicable fee amount after processing their application.

units.obligation_text: If, after a laboratory is issued a certificate, it requests a revised certificate, the laboratory must pay a fee to cover the cost of issuing a revised certificate.
units.action_summary: Laboratories requesting revised certificates must pay a fee to cover reissuance costs.

units.obligation_text: The fee must be paid in full before the revised certificate will be issued.
units.action_summary: Payment in full is required before issuance of a revised certificate.

units.obligation_text: If laboratory services are added to a certificate of compliance, the laboratory must pay an additional fee if required under § 493.643(d)(2).
units.action_summary: Labs adding services to a compliance certificate must pay an additional fee if §493.643(d)(2) requires it.

units.obligation_text: If, after a laboratory is issued a certificate, it requests a replacement certificate, the laboratory must pay a fee to cover the cost of issuing a replacement certificate.
units.action_summary: Laboratories requesting replacement certificates must pay a fee to cover reissuance costs.

units.obligation_text: The fee must be paid in full before issuing the replacement certificate.
units.action_summary: Payment in full is required before issuance of a replacement certificate.

units.obligation_text: In addition to the fee required under § 493.638, a laboratory subject to routine inspections must pay a fee to cover the cost of determining program compliance.
units.actor: Laboratory subject to routine inspections (certificate of compliance)
units.action_summary: Labs subject to routine inspections (certificate of compliance) must pay a program compliance determination fee in addition to certificate fees.

units.obligation_text: Laboratories issued a certificate for PPM procedures, certificate of waiver, or a certificate of accreditation are not subject to this fee for routine inspections.
units.actor: Laboratories with certificate for PPM, waiver, or accreditation
units.action_summary: PPM, waiver, and accredited laboratories are exempt from the routine inspection program compliance fee.

units.obligation_text: The fee is assessed and payable biennially.
units.actor: Laboratories subject to program compliance fee
units.action_summary: Program compliance fees are assessed and must be paid every two years.

units.obligation_text: If a laboratory issued a certificate of compliance has been inspected and follow-up visits are necessary because of identified deficiencies, HHS assesses the laboratory a fee to cover the cost of these visits.
units.action_summary: HHS assesses a fee on the compliance certificate laboratory to cover follow-up visit costs when inspections identify deficiencies.

units.obligation_text: HHS revokes the laboratory’s certificate of compliance for failure to pay the assessed fee.
units.action_summary: HHS may revoke a laboratory's compliance certificate if it fails to pay assessed follow-up visit fees.

units.obligation_text: If, after a certificate of compliance is issued, a laboratory adds services and requests that its certificate be upgraded, the laboratory must pay an additional fee if, to determine compliance with additional requirements, it is necessary to conduct an inspection, evaluate personnel, or monitor proficiency testing performance.
units.action_summary: Laboratories requesting an upgrade after adding services must pay additional fees if compliance determination requires inspection, personnel evaluation, or proficiency monitoring.

units.obligation_text: HHS revokes the laboratory’s certificate for failure to pay the compliance determination fee.
units.action_summary: HHS may revoke a laboratory's certificate for failure to pay fees assessed for compliance determinations relating to upgrades.

units.obligation_text: If it is necessary to conduct a complaint investigation, impose sanctions, or conduct a hearing, HHS assesses the laboratory holding a certificate of compliance a fee to cover the cost of these activities.
units.action_summary: HHS may assess a fee on compliance certificate laboratories to cover complaint investigations, sanctions, or hearings when necessary.

units.obligation_text: If a complaint investigation results in a complaint being unsubstantiated, or if an HHS adverse action is overturned at the conclusion of the administrative appeals process, the Government’s costs of these activities are not imposed upon the laboratory.
units.action_summary: Government costs for complaint investigations, sanctions, or hearings are not imposed on the laboratory if the complaint is unsubstantiated or an adverse action is overturned.

units.obligation_text: Costs for these activities are based on the actual resources and time necessary to perform the activities and are not assessed until after the laboratory concedes the existence of deficiencies or an ALJ rules in favor of HHS.
units.action_summary: Fees for investigations/hearings are based on actual resources and are only assessed after the laboratory concedes deficiencies or an ALJ rules for HHS.

units.obligation_text: HHS revokes the laboratory’s certificate of compliance for failure to pay the assessed costs.
units.action_summary: HHS may revoke a lab's certificate of compliance for failure to pay assessed costs from investigations, sanctions, or hearings.

units.obligation_text: Laboratories with a certificate of compliance must pay a fee if the laboratory fails to perform successfully in proficiency testing for one or more specialties, subspecialties, analytes, or tests specified in subpart I of this part, and it is necessary to conduct a desk review of the unsuccessful performance.
units.action_summary: Compliance certificate laboratories must pay a fee for desk reviews when they fail proficiency testing and a desk review is necessary.

units.obligation_text: The additional fee is based on the actual resources and time necessary to perform the desk review. HHS revokes the laboratory’s certificate of compliance for failure to pay the assessed costs.
units.action_summary: Desk review fees are based on actual resources/time; HHS may revoke the compliance certificate for failure to pay these costs.

units.obligation_text: A laboratory that is issued a certificate of accreditation is assessed an additional fee to cover the cost of performing validation inspections described at § 493.563. All accredited laboratories share in the cost of these inspections.
units.action_summary: Accredited labs are assessed an additional fee (shared among accredited labs) to cover validation inspections.

units.obligation_text: These costs are five percent of the same costs as those that are incurred when inspecting nonaccredited laboratories of the same schedule (or range) and are paid biennially by each accredited laboratory whether the accredited laboratory has a validation inspection or not.
units.action_summary: Accredited labs must pay, biennially, shared validation inspection costs equal to 5% of comparable nonaccredited inspection costs.

units.obligation_text: HHS revokes the laboratory’s certificate of accreditation for failure to pay the fee.
units.action_summary: HHS may revoke an accredited laboratory's certificate for failure to pay the shared validation inspection fee.

units.obligation_text: If a laboratory issued a certificate of accreditation has been inspected and follow-up visits are necessary because of identified deficiencies, HHS assesses the laboratory an additional fee to cover the cost of these visits.
units.action_summary: HHS may assess accredited labs additional fees for follow-up visits resulting from inspections identifying deficiencies.

units.obligation_text: The fee is based on the actual resources and time necessary to perform the follow-up visits. HHS revokes the laboratory’s certificate of accreditation for failure to pay the fee.
units.action_summary: Follow-up visit fees are based on actual resources/time; HHS may revoke accreditation for failure to pay.

units.obligation_text: State laboratory programs approved by HHS are assessed a fee for the following: Costs of Federal inspections of laboratories in that State; Costs incurred for investigations of complaints against the State’s CLIA-exempt laboratories if the complaint is substantiated; The State’s pro rata share of general overhead to administer the laboratory certification program under section 353 of the PHS Act.
units.actor: State laboratory programs approved by HHS
units.action_summary: Approved State lab programs are assessed fees for federal inspection costs, substantiated complaint investigations, and pro rata overhead to administer CLIA program.

units.obligation_text: Except for laboratories covered by approved State laboratory programs, all laboratories are notified in writing by HHS or its designee of the appropriate fee(s) and instructions for submitting the fee(s), including the due date for payment and where to make payment.
units.action_summary: HHS (or designee) must notify laboratories in writing of applicable fees and submission instructions (due date, where to pay), except approved State program labs.

units.obligation_text: The appropriate certificate is not issued until the applicable fees have been paid.
units.action_summary: HHS will withhold issuance of the applicable certificate until the laboratory has paid the required fees.

units.obligation_text: For approved State laboratory programs, HHS estimates the cost of conducting validation inspections as described at § 493.563 within the State on at least a biennial period.
units.action_summary: HHS must estimate validation inspection costs in approved States at least every two years.

units.obligation_text: HHS or its designee notifies the State by mail of the appropriate fees, including the due date for payment and the address of the United States Department of Treasury designated commercial bank to which payment must be made.
units.action_summary: HHS must mail approved States notice of appropriate fees, due date, and designated payment bank address.

units.obligation_text: If complaint investigations are conducted in laboratories within these States and are substantiated, HHS bills the State(s) the costs of the complaint investigations.
units.action_summary: HHS will bill approved State programs for costs of substantiated complaint investigations in their laboratories.

units.obligation_text: CMS calculates the inflation rate using the compounded CPI–U over 2 years and, provided that the calculated rate is greater than zero, applies an increase to all fee amounts equal to the calculated rate.
units.action_summary: CMS must compute a two-year compounded CPI–U inflation rate and increase all fee amounts by that rate if it is greater than zero.

units.obligation_text: If the total fee amounts, including any increase applied under paragraph (a)(1) of this section, do not match or exceed actual program obligations based on a review of the previous 2 years’ obligations, CMS applies an additional across the board increase to each laboratory’s fees by calculating the difference between the total fee amounts and actual program obligations.
units.action_summary: If fee revenue (after CPI increase) is insufficient to cover program obligations, CMS applies an additional across-the-board fee increase equal to the shortfall.

units.obligation_text: Any increase applied under paragraph (a) of this section is incorporated into the baseline fee amounts for any subsequent biennial increase.
units.action_summary: Fee increases applied are rolled into the baseline for future biennial increases.

units.obligation_text: Any increase applied under paragraph (a) of this section, including the calculation thereof, will be published as a notice in the Federal Register.
units.action_summary: CMS must publish a Federal Register notice detailing any applied fee increase and its calculation.

units.obligation_text: Use a continuous monitoring system and alert system to monitor the storage temperature of specimens (donor and recipient) and reagents and notify laboratory personnel when temperature limits are exceeded.
units.action_summary: Laboratory must monitor specimen and reagent storage temperatures with continuous monitoring/alert systems and notify personnel if limits are exceeded.

units.obligation_text: Establish and follow written policies and procedures for the storage and retention of specimens based on the specific type of specimen.
units.action_summary: Laboratory must have and follow written storage and retention policies tailored to specimen type.

units.obligation_text: All specimens must be easily retrievable.
units.action_summary: Specimens must be stored so they can be readily retrieved.

units.obligation_text: The laboratory must have an emergency plan for alternate storage.
units.action_summary: Laboratory must maintain an emergency alternate storage plan for specimens.

units.obligation_text: If the laboratory uses immunologic reagents to facilitate or enhance the isolation or identification of lymphocytes or lymphocyte subsets, the efficacy of the methods must be monitored with appropriate quality control procedures.
units.action_summary: When using immunologic reagents for lymphocyte isolation/identification, laboratories must monitor method efficacy with quality control procedures.

units.obligation_text: Have available and follow written criteria for determining when antigen and allele typing are required.
units.action_summary: Laboratory must maintain and follow written criteria to determine when antigen and allele typing is required.

units.obligation_text: The laboratory must make a reasonable effort to have available monthly serum specimens for all potential transplant recipients for periodic antibody screening, identification, and crossmatch.
units.action_summary: Laboratory must reasonably attempt to have monthly serum specimens for transplant recipients for screening and crossmatch purposes.

units.obligation_text: For each type of crossmatch that a laboratory performs, the laboratory must do the following, as applicable: Establish and follow written policies and procedures for performing a crossmatch; Have available and follow written criteria ...; The test report must specify the type of crossmatch performed.
units.action_summary: For each crossmatch type performed, labs must establish/follow written procedures and criteria and specify crossmatch type on the report.

units.obligation_text: Defining donor and recipient human leukocyte antigen (HLA) antigens, alleles, and antibodies to be tested;
units.action_summary: Laboratory must have written criteria defining which donor and recipient HLA antigens, alleles, and antibodies are to be tested.

units.obligation_text: Defining the criteria necessary to assess a recipient’s alloantibody status;
units.action_summary: Laboratory must have written criteria for assessing recipient alloantibody status.

units.obligation_text: Assessing recipient antibody presence or absence on an ongoing basis;
units.action_summary: Laboratory must have written criteria to assess recipient antibody presence or absence on an ongoing basis.

units.obligation_text: Typing the donor at the serologic level to include those HLA antigens to which antibodies have been identified in the potential recipient, as applicable;
units.action_summary: Donors must be serologically typed for HLA antigens identified in potential recipients where applicable.

units.obligation_text: Describing the circumstances in which pre- and post-transplant confirmation testing of donor and recipient specimens is required;
units.action_summary: Laboratory must have written criteria describing when pre- and post-transplant confirmation testing is required.

units.obligation_text: Making available all applicable donor and recipient test results to the transplant team;
units.action_summary: Laboratory must make applicable donor and recipient test results available to the transplant team.

units.obligation_text: Ensuring immunologic assessments are based on test results obtained from a test report from a CLIA-certified laboratory;
units.action_summary: Laboratory must ensure immunologic assessments rely on test results from CLIA-certified laboratory test reports.

units.obligation_text: Defining time limits between recipient testing and the performance of a crossmatch.
units.action_summary: Laboratory must define time limits between recipient testing and performing crossmatch.

units.obligation_text: The test report must specify the type of crossmatch performed.
units.action_summary: Laboratory must specify the crossmatch type on the test report.

units.obligation_text: Laboratories performing histocompatibility testing for infusion and transplantation purposes must establish and follow written policies and procedures specifying the histocompatibility testing ... to be performed for each type of cell, tissue, or organ to be infused or transplanted.
units.actor: Laboratories performing histocompatibility testing for infusion and transplantation
units.action_summary: Transplant histocompatibility labs must have written policies specifying testing to be performed for each transplant type.

units.obligation_text: Testing protocols that address: Transplant type (organ, tissue, cell); Donor (living, deceased, or paired); and Recipient (high risk vs. unsensitized);
units.action_summary: Laboratory policies must include testing protocols addressing transplant type, donor type, and recipient risk status.

units.obligation_text: Type and frequency of testing required to support clinical transplant protocols;
units.action_summary: Laboratory policies must specify the types and frequencies of testing needed to support transplant protocols.

units.obligation_text: Process to obtain a recipient specimen, if possible, for crossmatch that is collected on the day of the transplant. If the laboratory is unable to obtain a recipient specimen on the day of the transplant, the laboratory must have a process to document its efforts to obtain the specimen.
units.action_summary: Laboratory must have a process to obtain same-day recipient specimens for crossmatch and must document efforts if unable to obtain one.

units.obligation_text: The laboratory must document all control procedures performed, as specified in this section.
units.action_summary: Laboratory must document all control procedures performed as required by the section.

units.obligation_text: Evaluate the competency of all testing personnel and ensure that the staff maintains their competency to perform test procedures and report test results promptly, accurately, and proficiently.
units.action_summary: The PPM laboratory director must evaluate and ensure testing personnel competency for accurate and timely testing and reporting.

units.obligation_text: Direct observations of routine patient test performance, including, if applicable, specimen handling, processing, and testing;
units.action_summary: Competency evaluation procedures must include direct observation of routine patient test performance.

units.obligation_text: Monitoring the recording and reporting of test results;
units.action_summary: Competency evaluations must include monitoring how tests are recorded and results reported.

units.obligation_text: Review of test results or worksheets;
units.action_summary: Competency evaluations must include review of test results or worksheets.

units.obligation_text: Assessment of test performance through testing internal blind testing samples or external proficiency testing samples;
units.action_summary: Competency evaluations must include assessment via internal blind samples or external proficiency testing.

units.obligation_text: Assessment of problem solving skills;
units.action_summary: Competency evaluations must include assessment of staff problem-solving skills.

units.obligation_text: Evaluating and documenting the performance of individuals responsible for PPM testing at least semiannually during the first year the individual tests patient specimens. Thereafter, evaluations and documentation must be performed at least annually.
units.action_summary: PPM testing personnel must be evaluated/documented semiannually in their first year and at least annually thereafter.

units.obligation_text: The laboratory director must— (various alternative qualification paths are described in paragraphs (b)(1) through (b)(6)).
units.action_summary: Laboratory directors must meet one of the specified qualification pathways enumerated in §493.1405(b).

units.obligation_text: (1) Be a doctor of medicine or doctor of osteopathy licensed to practice medicine or osteopathy in the State in which the laboratory is located; and be certified in anatomic or clinical pathology, or both, by the American Board of Pathology or the American Osteopathic Board of Pathology;
units.action_summary: Laboratory director option: MD or DO licensed in-state and certified in anatomic or clinical pathology by an approved board.

units.obligation_text: (2) Be a doctor of medicine, doctor of osteopathy, or doctor of podiatric medicine licensed to practice medicine, osteopathy, or podiatry in the State in which the laboratory is located; and have had laboratory training or experience consisting of: at least 1 year directing or supervising nonwaived laboratory testing; and have at least 20 CE credit hours in laboratory practice that cover the laboratory director responsibilities defined in § 493.1407;
units.action_summary: Laboratory director option: MD/DO/DPod licensed in-state with ≥1 year directing/supervising nonwaived testing and ≥20 CE hours covering director responsibilities.

units.obligation_text: Notwithstanding any other provision of this section, an individual is considered qualified as a laboratory director of moderate complexity testing under this section if they were qualified and serving as a laboratory director of moderate complexity testing in a CLIA-certified laboratory as of [effective date of the final rule], and have done so continuously since [effective date of the final rule].
units.actor: Individuals already serving as laboratory director of moderate complexity testing as of effective date
units.action_summary: Individuals who were qualified and serving as moderate complexity lab directors on the effective date and have continued to serve are considered qualified.

units.obligation_text: Be onsite at least once every 6 months, with at least 4 months between the minimum two on-site visits. Laboratory directors may elect to be on-site more frequently and must continue to be accessible to the laboratory to provide telephone or electronic consultation as needed;
units.action_summary: Laboratory directors must be on-site at least twice per year (min 4 months apart), may be more often, and must remain accessible for consultation.

units.obligation_text: Provide documentation of these visits, including evidence of performing activities that are part of the laboratory director responsibilities.
units.action_summary: Laboratory directors must document on-site visits and provide evidence of activities performed as part of their responsibilities.

units.obligation_text: The technical consultant must— (various alternative qualification paths are described in paragraphs (b)(1) through (b)(7)).
units.action_summary: Technical consultants must meet one of the specified qualification pathways set out in §493.1411(b).

units.obligation_text: (1) Be a doctor of medicine or doctor of osteopathy licensed to practice medicine or osteopathy in the State in which the laboratory is located; and be certified in anatomic or clinical pathology, or both, by the American Board of Pathology or the American Osteopathic Board of Pathology;
units.action_summary: Technical consultant option: MD or DO licensed in-state and certified in anatomic or clinical pathology by an approved board.

units.obligation_text: (2) Be a doctor of medicine, doctor of osteopathy, or doctor of podiatric medicine licensed to practice medicine, osteopathy, or podiatry in the State in which the laboratory is located; and have at least 1 year of laboratory training or experience, or both, in nonwaived testing, in the designated specialty or subspecialty areas of service for which the technical consultant is responsible;
units.action_summary: Technical consultant option: MD/DO/DPod licensed in-state and ≥1 year lab training/experience in nonwaived testing in the specialty they cover.

units.obligation_text: For blood gas analysis, the individual must— (i) Be qualified under paragraph (b)(1), (2), (3), or (4) of this section; or (ii) Have earned a bachelor’s degree in respiratory therapy or cardiovascular technology from an accredited institution; and have at least 2 years of laboratory training or experience, or both, in blood gas analysis;
units.action_summary: Technical consultants for blood gas analysis must meet standard consultant qualifications OR hold a relevant bachelor's degree plus ≥2 years blood gas lab experience.

units.obligation_text: Notwithstanding any other provision of this section, an individual is considered qualified as a technical consultant under this section if they were qualified and serving as a technical consultant for moderate complexity testing in a CLIA-certified laboratory as of [effective date of the final rule], and have done so continuously since [effective date of the final rule].
units.actor: Individuals serving as technical consultants for moderate complexity testing as of effective date
units.action_summary: Individuals who were qualified and serving as technical consultants for moderate complexity testing on the effective date and have continued are considered qualified.

units.obligation_text: Meet one of the following requirements: (various alternative educational/training/experience pathways listed in paragraphs (b)(1) through (b)(7)).
units.action_summary: Testing personnel must meet one of the enumerated qualification pathways in §493.1423(b).

units.obligation_text: Have documentation of training appropriate for the testing performed prior to analyzing patient specimens. Such training must ensure that the individual has— (A) The skills required for proper specimen collection ... (H) The skills required to assess and verify the validity of patient test results through the evaluation of quality control sample values prior to reporting patient test results.
units.actor: Testing personnel (with high school diploma/equivalent pathway)
units.action_summary: Personnel with a high school diploma/equivalent must have documented training ensuring skills for specimen collection, lab procedures, instrument use, maintenance, reagent knowledge, QC implementation, awareness of test influences, and result verification.

units.obligation_text: For blood gas analysis, the individual must— (i) Be qualified under paragraph (b)(1), (2), (3), or (4) of this section; or (ii) ... have at least 1 year of laboratory training or experience, or both, in blood gas analysis; or (C) have an associate’s degree related to pulmonary function and at least 2 years of training or experience in blood gas analysis.
units.action_summary: Personnel performing blood gas analysis must meet standard qualification pathways or have specified degree plus required years of blood gas experience.

units.obligation_text: (1) Be a doctor of medicine or doctor of osteopathy licensed to practice medicine or osteopathy in the State in which the laboratory is located; and be certified in anatomic or clinical pathology, or both, by the American Board of Pathology or the American Osteopathic Board of Pathology;
units.action_summary: High-complexity laboratory director option: MD/DO licensed in-state and certified in anatomic or clinical pathology by an approved board.

units.obligation_text: (2) Be a doctor of medicine, a doctor of osteopathy, or doctor of podiatric medicine licensed to practice medicine, osteopathy, or podiatry in the State in which the laboratory is located; and (i) Have at least 2 years of experience directing or supervising high complexity testing; and (ii) Have at least 20 CE credit hours in laboratory practice that cover the director responsibilities defined in § 493.1445;
units.action_summary: High-complexity lab director option: MD/DO/DPod licensed in-state with ≥2 years directing/supervising high complexity testing and ≥20 CE hours covering director responsibilities.

title: Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments Fees; Histocompatibility, Personnel, and Alternative Sanctions for Certificate of Waiver Laboratories; Extension of Comment Period

units.obligation_text: The comment period for the proposed rule published July 26, 2022 (87 FR 44896), is extended through September 26, 2022.
units.action_summary: CMS and CDC extend the comment period for the referenced proposed rule through September 26, 2022.

title: Medicare Program: Contract Year 2024 Policy and Technical Changes to the Medicare Advantage Program, Medicare Prescription Drug Benefit Program, Medicare Cost Plan Program, etc.

units.obligation_text: CMS (or a third party to which CMS has assigned this responsibility, such as an HMO or CMP) may reinstate enrollment in the plan, without interruption of coverage, if the individual submits a request for reinstatement for good cause within 60 calendar days of the disenrollment effective date, has not previously requested reinstatement for good cause during the same 60 day period following the involuntary disenrollment, shows good cause for failure to pay, and pays all overdue premiums or other charges within 3 calendar months after the disenrollment date.
units.actor: CMS or a third party to which CMS has assigned this responsibility (such as an HMO or CMP)
units.action_summary: May reinstate enrollment without interruption if the individual meets listed conditions (timely request, not previously requested, shows good cause, pays overdue amounts within 3 months).

units.obligation_text: the individual submits a request for reinstatement for good cause within 60 calendar days of the disenrollment effective date
units.action_summary: Submit a reinstatement request for good cause within 60 calendar days of disenrollment.

units.obligation_text: has not previously requested reinstatement for good cause during the same 60 day period following the involuntary disenrollment
units.action_summary: May not have previously requested reinstatement for good cause during the same 60-day period.

units.obligation_text: shows good cause for failure to pay
units.action_summary: Demonstrate good cause for failing to pay.

units.obligation_text: pays all overdue premiums or other charges within 3 calendar months after the disenrollment date
units.action_summary: Pay all overdue premiums/charges within 3 calendar months after disenrollment.

units.obligation_text: The individual must establish by a credible statement that failure to pay premiums or other charges was due to circumstances for which the individual had no control, or which the individual could not reasonably have been expected to foresee.
units.action_summary: Provide a credible statement that payment failure was due to circumstances beyond the individual's control or not reasonably foreseeable.

units.obligation_text: The HMO or CMP must make a serious effort to resolve the problem presented by the enrollee, including the use (or attempted use) of internal grievance procedures, and including providing reasonable accommodations, as determined by CMS, for individuals with mental or cognitive conditions, including mental illness and developmental disabilities.
units.action_summary: Make a serious effort to resolve the enrollee's problem, including using grievance procedures and providing reasonable accommodations for mental/cognitive conditions.

units.obligation_text: including the use (or attempted use) of internal grievance procedures
units.action_summary: Include using or attempting to use internal grievance procedures as part of efforts to resolve problems.

units.obligation_text: including providing reasonable accommodations, as determined by CMS, for individuals with mental or cognitive conditions, including mental illness and developmental disabilities
units.action_summary: Provide reasonable accommodations for individuals with mental or cognitive conditions as part of efforts to resolve problems.

units.obligation_text: The HMO or CMP must inform the individual of the right to use the organization’s grievance procedures, through the notices described in paragraph (e)(7) of this section.
units.action_summary: Inform the individual of the right to use the organization's grievance procedures via the notices described in §417.460(e)(7).

units.obligation_text: The HMO or CMP must document the problems, efforts, and medical conditions as described in paragraphs (e)(1) through (3) of this section.
units.action_summary: Document the enrollee's problems, the organization's efforts, and relevant medical conditions.

units.obligation_text: Dated copies of the notices required in paragraph (d)(2)(iv) of this section must also be submitted to CMS.
units.action_summary: Submit dated copies of the notices required in paragraph (d)(2)(iv) to CMS.

units.obligation_text: The HMO or CMP must provide the individual two notices prior to submitting the request for disenrollment to CMS.
units.action_summary: Provide two notices to the individual before submitting a disenrollment request to CMS.

units.obligation_text: If the disruptive behavior ceases after the enrollee receives the advance notice and then later resumes, the HMO or CMP must begin the process again.
units.action_summary: Restart the notice/process if disruptive behavior ceases and later resumes.

units.obligation_text: The HMO or CMP must wait at least 30 days after sending the advance notice before sending the second notice
units.action_summary: Wait at least 30 days after the advance notice before sending the second notice.

units.obligation_text: The second notice ... notifies the enrollee that the HMO or CMP will request CMS permission to involuntarily disenroll the enrollee. This notice must be provided prior to submission of the request to CMS.
units.action_summary: Provide the second notice (notice of intent) to the enrollee prior to submitting the disenrollment request to CMS.

units.obligation_text: FI–SNP ... must own or have a contractual arrangement with each institutionalized facility serving enrollees in the plan.
units.actor: FI–SNP (the MA organization operating the FI–SNP)
units.action_summary: Own or have contractual arrangements with each institutionalized facility serving plan enrollees.

units.obligation_text: HI–SNPs must meet the standards specified in the definitions of FI–SNP and IE–SNP.
units.actor: HI–SNP (the MA organization operating the HI–SNP)
units.action_summary: Meet the standards specified for FI–SNP and IE–SNP.

units.obligation_text: A C–SNP may focus on one severe or disabling chronic condition, as defined in § 422.2, or on a grouping of severe or disabling chronic conditions.
units.actor: a C–SNP / MA organization offering a C–SNP
units.action_summary: May focus enrollment on one severe/disabling chronic condition or a grouping of such conditions.

units.obligation_text: Upon CMS approval, an MA organization may offer a C–SNP that focuses on multiple commonly co-morbid and clinically-linked conditions from the following list of groupings: ...
units.action_summary: May offer a C–SNP focusing on multiple co-morbid, clinically-linked conditions if CMS approves.

units.obligation_text: For C–SNPs that use a group of multiple severe or disabling chronic conditions as described in § 422.4(a)(1)(iv) of this chapter, special needs individuals need only have one of the qualifying severe or disabling chronic conditions in order to be eligible to enroll.
units.action_summary: To be eligible for enrollment in these C–SNPs, an individual only needs one of the qualifying conditions.

units.obligation_text: When an individual is disenrolled from an MA plan due to the election of a new plan, the MA organization must reinstate the individual’s enrollment in that plan if the individual cancels the election in the new plan within timeframes established by CMS.
units.action_summary: Must reinstate enrollment when the individual cancels the new plan election within CMS-established timeframes.

units.obligation_text: The MA organization offering the plan from which the individual was disenrolled must send the member notification of the reinstatement within 10 calendar days of receiving confirmation of the individual’s reinstatement.
units.actor: the MA organization offering the original plan
units.action_summary: Send notification of reinstatement to the member within 10 calendar days of receiving confirmation.

units.obligation_text: Individuals affected by an emergency or major disaster declared by a Federal, State or local government entity are eligible for a SEP to make a MA enrollment or disenrollment election. The SEP starts as of the date the declaration is made, the incident start date or, if different, the start date identified in the declaration, whichever is earlier. The SEP ends 2 full calendar months following the end date identified in the declaration or, if different, the date the end of the incident is announced, the date the incident automatically ends under applicable State or local law, or, if incident end date is not otherwise identified, the incident end date specified in paragraph (b)(18)(i) of this section.
units.actor: individuals affected by an emergency or major disaster
units.action_summary: Eligible for a special enrollment period (SEP) to make MA enrollment/disenrollment elections, with start and end tied to the emergency declaration dates.

units.obligation_text: If the incident end date of an emergency or major disaster is not otherwise identified, the incident end date will be one year after the SEP start date or, if applicable, the date of a renewal or extension of the emergency or disaster declaration, whichever is later. Therefore, the maximum length of this SEP, if the incident end date is not otherwise identified, is 14 full calendar months after the SEP start date or, if applicable, the date of a renewal or extension of the emergency or disaster declaration.
units.action_summary: If no incident end date is identified, the incident end date defaults to one year after SEP start (max SEP length 14 full calendar months).

units.obligation_text: Document its efforts to obtain information to complete the disenrollment request;
units.action_summary: Document efforts to obtain missing information necessary to complete a disenrollment request.

units.obligation_text: Notify the individual (in writing or verbally) within 10 calendar days of receipt of the disenrollment request.
units.action_summary: Notify the individual (in writing or verbally) within 10 calendar days after receiving the disenrollment request.

units.obligation_text: The organization must deny the request if any additional information needed to make the disenrollment request "complete" is not received within the following timeframes: (1) For disenrollment requests received during the AEP, by December 7, or within 21 calendar days of the request for additional information, whichever is later; and (2) For disenrollment requests received during all other election periods, by the end of the month in which the disenrollment request was initially received, or within 21 calendar days of the request for additional information, whichever is later.
units.action_summary: Deny the disenrollment request if required additional information is not received within specified timeframes depending on the election period.

units.obligation_text: For disenrollment requests received during the AEP, by December 7, or within 21 calendar days of the request for additional information, whichever is later;
units.action_summary: For AEP disenrollment requests, deny if additional info not received by December 7 or within 21 calendar days of the request, whichever is later.

units.obligation_text: For disenrollment requests received during all other election periods, by the end of the month in which the disenrollment request was initially received, or within 21 calendar days of the request for additional information, whichever is later.
units.action_summary: For non-AEP periods, deny if additional info not received by the end of the month of initial receipt or within 21 calendar days of the request, whichever is later.

units.obligation_text: A disenrollment request is considered to be incomplete if the required but missing information is not received by the MA organization within the timeframe specified in paragraph (b)(3)(v)(C) of this section.
units.actor: a disenrollment request / the MA organization (classification)
units.action_summary: Defines a disenrollment request as incomplete if missing information is not received within the specified timeframe.

units.obligation_text: the MA organization must give the individual a written notice of the disenrollment with an explanation of why the MA organization is planning to disenroll the individual.
units.action_summary: Provide written notice explaining the reason for planned disenrollment.

units.obligation_text: Be provided to the individual before submission of the disenrollment to CMS;
units.action_summary: Provide the written disenrollment notice to the individual before submitting the disenrollment to CMS.

units.obligation_text: Include an explanation of the individual’s right to submit a grievance under the MA organization’s grievance procedures.
units.action_summary: Include an explanation of the individual's right to submit a grievance in the notice.

units.obligation_text: When an individual is disenrolled for failure to pay the plan premium, CMS (or a third party to which CMS has assigned this responsibility, such as an MA organization) may reinstate enrollment in the MA plan, without interruption of coverage, if the individual—
units.actor: CMS (or a third party to which CMS has assigned this responsibility, such as an MA organization)
units.action_summary: May reinstate enrollment without interruption if the individual meets the listed conditions for good cause reinstatement after premium nonpayment.

units.obligation_text: Submits a request for reinstatement for good cause within 60 calendar days of the disenrollment effective date;
units.action_summary: Submit a reinstatement request for good cause within 60 calendar days of disenrollment.

units.obligation_text: Has not previously requested reinstatement for good cause during the same 60 day period following the involuntary disenrollment;
units.action_summary: Must not have previously requested reinstatement for good cause during the same 60-day period.

units.obligation_text: Shows good cause for failure to pay within the initial grace period;
units.action_summary: Show good cause for failing to pay within the initial grace period.

units.obligation_text: Pays all overdue premiums within 3 calendar months after the disenrollment date;
units.action_summary: Pay all overdue premiums within 3 calendar months after disenrollment.

units.obligation_text: Establishes by a credible statement that failure to pay premiums within the initial grace period was due to circumstances for which the individual had no control, or which the individual could not reasonably have been expected to foresee.
units.action_summary: Provide a credible statement that payment failure was due to uncontrollable or unforeseeable circumstances.

units.obligation_text: The MA organization must make a serious effort to resolve the problems presented by the individual, including providing reasonable accommodations, as determined by CMS, for individuals with mental or cognitive conditions, including mental illness and developmental disabilities.
units.action_summary: Make a serious effort to resolve problems raised by the individual, including providing CMS-determined reasonable accommodations for mental/cognitive conditions.

units.obligation_text: including providing reasonable accommodations, as determined by CMS, for individuals with mental or cognitive conditions, including mental illness and developmental disabilities.
units.action_summary: Provide reasonable accommodations for individuals with mental or cognitive conditions as part of efforts to resolve problems.

units.obligation_text: In addition, the MA organization must inform the individual of the right to use the organization’s grievance procedures, through the notices described in paragraph (d)(2)(vii) of this section.
units.action_summary: Inform individuals of the right to use the organization's grievance procedures via the notices described in paragraph (d)(2)(vii).

units.obligation_text: The MA organization must document the enrollee’s behavior, its own efforts to resolve any problems, as described in paragraph (d)(2)(iii) of this section, and any extenuating circumstances.
units.action_summary: Document the enrollee's behavior, the organization's efforts to resolve problems, and any extenuating circumstances.

units.obligation_text: The MA organization may request from CMS the ability to decline future enrollment by the individual.
units.action_summary: May request CMS permission to decline the individual's future enrollment.

units.obligation_text: The MA organization must submit this information and any documentation received by the beneficiary to CMS.
units.action_summary: Submit documented information and any beneficiary documentation to CMS.

units.obligation_text: Dated copies of the notices required in paragraph (d)(2)(vii) of this section must also be submitted to CMS.
units.action_summary: Submit dated copies of notices required in paragraph (d)(2)(vii) to CMS.

units.obligation_text: The MA organization must provide the individual two notices prior to submitting the request for disenrollment to CMS.
units.action_summary: Provide two notices to the individual before submitting the disenrollment request to CMS.

units.obligation_text: If the disruptive behavior ceases after the member receives the advance notice and then later resumes, the organization must begin the process again.
units.action_summary: If disruptive behavior stops after the advance notice and later resumes, restart the notice/process.

units.obligation_text: The organization must wait at least 30 days after sending the advance notice before sending the second notice, during which 30-day period the individual has the opportunity to cease their behavior.
units.action_summary: Wait at least 30 days after the advance notice before sending the second notice to give the individual an opportunity to cease behavior.

units.obligation_text: The second notice ... notifies the member that the MA organization will request CMS permission to involuntarily disenroll the member. This notice must be provided prior to submission of the request to CMS.
units.action_summary: Provide the second notice (notice of intent) prior to submitting the disenrollment request to CMS.

units.obligation_text: Unless continuation of enrollment is elected under § 422.54, the MA organization must disenroll an individual, and must document the basis for such action, if the MA organization establishes, on the basis of a written statement from the individual or other evidence acceptable to CMS, that the individual has permanently moved—
units.action_summary: Must disenroll an individual and document the basis if it establishes the individual has permanently moved (unless continuation elected).

units.obligation_text: The MA organization must document the basis for such action
units.action_summary: Document the basis for disenrollment when disenrolling for permanent move.

units.obligation_text: The MA organization must give the individual a written notice of the disenrollment that meets the requirements set forth in paragraph (c) of this section within 10 calendar days of the plan’s confirmation of the individual’s residence outside of the plan service area or within the first 10 calendar days of the sixth month of an individual’s temporary absence from the plan service area or, for individuals using a visitor/traveler benefit, within the first 10 calendar days of the last month of the allowable absence. If the plan learns of an individual’s temporary absence from the plan service area after the expiration of the allowable period, the plan must send this notice within 10 calendar days of the plan learning of the absence.
units.action_summary: Provide written disenrollment notice meeting paragraph (c) requirements within specified 10-day periods tied to confirmation of residence or temporary absence; if learned later, send within 10 days of learning.

units.obligation_text: If an enrollee loses special needs status and must be disenrolled under paragraph (b)(2)(iv) of this section, the SNP must provide the enrollee with a minimum of 30 days advance notice of disenrollment, regardless of the date of loss of special needs status.
units.action_summary: Provide at least 30 days advance notice of disenrollment when an enrollee loses special needs status and must be disenrolled.

units.obligation_text: The advance notice must be provided to the enrollee within 10 calendar days of the plan learning of the loss of special needs status and must afford the enrollee an opportunity to prove that they are still eligible to remain in the plan.
units.action_summary: Provide the advance notice within 10 calendar days of learning of loss of special needs status and allow the enrollee to prove continued eligibility.

units.obligation_text: The advance notice must include the disenrollment effective date, a description of eligibility for the SEP described in § 422.62(b)(11), and, if applicable, information regarding the period of deemed continued eligibility, the duration of the period of deemed continued eligibility, and the consequences of not regaining special needs status within the period of deemed continued eligibility.
units.action_summary: Advance notice must include disenrollment effective date, SEP eligibility description, and applicable information on deemed continued eligibility and consequences.

units.obligation_text: A final involuntary disenrollment notice must be sent within 3 business days following the disenrollment effective date, which is either the last day of the period of deemed continued eligibility, if applicable, or a minimum of 30 days after providing the advance notice of disenrollment. The final involuntary disenrollment notice must be sent before submission of the disenrollment to CMS.
units.action_summary: Send the final involuntary disenrollment notice within 3 business days following the disenrollment effective date and before submitting the disenrollment to CMS.

units.obligation_text: The final involuntary disenrollment notice must include an explanation of the enrollee’s right to file a grievance under the MA organization’s grievance procedures that are required by § 422.564.
units.action_summary: Final involuntary disenrollment notice must explain the enrollee's right to file a grievance under required grievance procedures.

units.obligation_text: When coverage criteria are not fully established in applicable Medicare statute, regulation, NCD or LCD, MA organizations may create internal coverage criteria that are based on current evidence in widely used treatment guidelines or clinical literature that is made publicly available.
units.action_summary: May create internal coverage criteria based on current evidence when coverage criteria are not fully established elsewhere.

units.obligation_text: A publicly accessible summary of evidence that was considered during the development of the internal coverage criteria used to make medical necessity determinations;
units.action_summary: Provide a publicly accessible summary of evidence considered when developing internal coverage criteria.

units.obligation_text: A list of the sources of such evidence;
units.action_summary: Provide a list of sources used as evidence for internal coverage criteria.

units.obligation_text: Include an explanation of the rationale that supports the adoption of the coverage criteria used to make a medical necessity determination.
units.action_summary: Include an explanation of the rationale supporting adoption of internal coverage criteria.

units.obligation_text: MA organizations must make medical necessity determinations based on: (A) Coverage and benefit criteria as specified at paragraphs (b) and (c) of this section and may not deny coverage for basic benefits based on coverage criteria not specified in paragraph (b) or (c) of this section; (B) Whether the provision of items or services is reasonable and necessary under section 1862(a)(1) of the Act; (C) The enrollee’s medical history (for example, diagnoses, conditions, functional status), physician recommendations, and clinical notes; and (D) Where appropriate, involvement of the organization’s medical director as required at § 422.562(a)(4).
units.action_summary: Make medical necessity determinations based on specified criteria (coverage criteria, reasonableness/necessity under section 1862(a)(1), patient medical history, and involvement of medical director when appropriate).

units.obligation_text: Coverage and benefit criteria as specified at paragraphs (b) and (c) of this section
units.action_summary: Base medical necessity determinations on the coverage and benefit criteria specified in paragraphs (b) and (c).

units.obligation_text: may not deny coverage for basic benefits based on coverage criteria not specified in paragraph (b) or (c) of this section
units.action_summary: Prohibited from denying basic benefits based on coverage criteria not specified in paragraphs (b) or (c).

units.obligation_text: Whether the provision of items or services is reasonable and necessary under section 1862(a)(1) of the Act;
units.action_summary: Consider whether items/services are reasonable and necessary under section 1862(a)(1).

units.obligation_text: The enrollee’s medical history (for example, diagnoses, conditions, functional status), physician recommendations, and clinical notes;
units.action_summary: Consider the enrollee's medical history, physician recommendations, and clinical notes in determinations.

units.obligation_text: Where appropriate, involvement of the organization’s medical director as required at § 422.562(a)(4).
units.action_summary: When appropriate, involve the organization's medical director as required by § 422.562(a)(4).

units.obligation_text: MA organizations may elect to furnish, as part of their Medicare covered benefits, coverage of posthospital SNF care as described in subparts C and D of this part, in the absence of the prior qualifying hospital stay that would otherwise be required for coverage of this care.
units.action_summary: May elect to provide covered posthospital SNF care without a prior qualifying hospital stay.

units.obligation_text: For I–SNPs, ensure that contracts with long-term care institutions (listed in the definition of the term institutionalized in § 422.2) contain requirements allowing I–SNP clinical and care coordination staff access to enrollees of the I–SNP who are institutionalized.
units.action_summary: Ensure contracts with long-term care institutions include requirements allowing I–SNP clinical and care coordination staff access to institutionalized enrollees.

units.obligation_text: Each element of the model of care of a plan must meet a minimum benchmark score of 50 percent and each MOC must meet an aggregate minimum benchmark of 70 percent, and a plan’s model of care will only be approved if each element of the model of care meets the minimum benchmark and the model of care meets aggregate minimum benchmark.
units.action_summary: Each model-of-care element must meet at least 50% and the aggregate MOC must meet at least 70% for approval.

units.obligation_text: An MOC for a C–SNP that receives a passing score is approved for 1 year.
units.action_summary: A passing C–SNP MOC is approved for one year.

units.obligation_text: An MOC for an I–SNP or D–SNP that receives an aggregate minimum benchmark score of 85 percent or greater is approved for 3 years. An MOC for an I–SNP or D–SNP that receives a score of 75 percent to 84 percent is approved for 2 years. An MOC for an I–SNP or D–SNP that receives a score of 70 percent to 74 percent is approved for 1 year.
units.action_summary: Approval duration for I–SNP/D–SNP MOCs depends on aggregate benchmark score: ≥85% = 3 years; 75–84% = 2 years; 70–74% = 1 year.

units.obligation_text: For an MOC that fails to meet a minimum element benchmark score of 50 percent or an MOC that fails to meet the aggregate minimum benchmark of 70 percent, the MA organization is permitted a one-time opportunity to resubmit the corrected MOC for reevaluation; and an MOC that is corrected and resubmitted using this cure period is approved for only 1 year.
units.action_summary: If MOC fails benchmarks, the MA organization may resubmit corrected MOC one time for reevaluation; corrected resubmission is approved for 1 year.

units.obligation_text: SNPs may not implement any changes to a MOC until NCQA has approved the changes and the MOC is not rescored during the off-cycle review of changes to the MOC.
units.action_summary: Cannot implement MOC changes until NCQA approves them and the MOC is not rescored during the off-cycle review.

units.obligation_text: D–SNPs and I–SNPs may submit updates and corrections to their NCQA-approved MOC any number of times between June 1st and November 30th of each calendar year or when CMS requires an off-cycle submission to ensure compliance with applicable law.
units.action_summary: May submit MOC updates/corrections between June 1 and November 30 (or when CMS requires off-cycle submission).

units.obligation_text: D–SNPs and I–SNPs are required to submit updates or corrections as part of an off-cycle submissions based on: (1) Substantial changes in policies or procedures pertinent to: the health risk assessment (HRA) process; revising processes to develop and update the Individualized Care Plan (ICP); the integrated care team process; risk stratification methodology; or care transition protocols; (2) Target population changes that warrant modifications to care management approaches; (3) Changes in a SNP’s plan benefit package between consecutive contract years that can considerably impact critical functions necessary to maintain member well-being and are related SNP operations; (4) Changes in level of authority or oversight for personnel conducting care coordination activities (for example, medical provider to non-medical provider, clinical vs. non-clinical personnel); or (5) Changes to quality metrics used to measure performance.
units.action_summary: Required to submit off-cycle updates/corrections when specified substantial changes or triggers occur.

units.obligation_text: When a deficiency identified in the off-cycle revisions to a MOC, the SNP may cure the deficiency a single time between June 1st and November 30th of each calendar year.
units.action_summary: May cure an identified off-cycle MOC deficiency one time between June 1 and November 30 each year.

units.obligation_text: With the exception specified in paragraph (e)(3) of this section, original Medicare is responsible for coverage of MA enrollees participating in CMS-approved clinical trials to include routine costs, as specified in NCD 310.1, and any coverage for the diagnosis or treatment of complications related to the clinical trial.
units.action_summary: Original Medicare covers routine costs and costs for diagnosis/treatment of complications for MA enrollees in CMS-approved clinical trials (subject to exceptions).

units.obligation_text: MA enrollees are not charged traditional Medicare Part A and B deductibles for clinical trial coverage.
units.action_summary: Prohibits charging MA enrollees traditional Medicare Part A and B deductibles for clinical trial coverage.

units.obligation_text: MA plans are responsible for paying the difference between traditional Medicare cost-sharing incurred for qualifying clinical trial items and services and the MA plan’s in-network cost-sharing for the same category of items and services.
units.action_summary: MA plans must pay the difference between traditional Medicare cost-sharing and the plan's in-network cost-sharing for qualifying clinical trial items/services.

units.obligation_text: An enrollee’s in-network cost-sharing portion must be included in the MA plan’s maximum out-of-pocket calculation.
units.action_summary: Include enrollee's in-network cost-sharing for clinical trial services in the plan's maximum out-of-pocket calculation.

units.obligation_text: MA plans may not require prior authorization for participation in a Medicare-qualified clinical trial not sponsored by the plan, nor may it create impediments to an enrollee’s participation in a non-plan-sponsored clinical trial.
units.action_summary: May not require prior authorization or create impediments to an enrollee's participation in non-plan-sponsored Medicare-qualified clinical trials.

units.obligation_text: MA plans are responsible for payment of routine care items and services in CMS-approved Category A and Category B IDE studies that are covered under § 405.211(a) of this chapter.
units.action_summary: MA plans must pay for routine care items/services in CMS-approved Category A and B IDE studies covered under §405.211(a).

units.obligation_text: MA plans are responsible for coverage of CMS-approved Category B devices that are covered under § 405.211(b) of this chapter.
units.action_summary: MA plans must cover CMS-approved Category B devices as specified under §405.211(b).

units.obligation_text: The number, mix, and distribution (addresses) of providers from whom enrollees may reasonably be expected to obtain services; each provider’s cultural and linguistic capabilities, including languages (including American Sign Language) offered by the provider or a skilled medical interpreter at the provider’s office; notations for MOUD-Waivered Providers as defined in § 422.116(b)(1)(xxx) who are listed on the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration’s Buprenorphine Practitioner Locator; any out-of network coverage; any point-of-service option, including the supplemental premium for that option; and how the MA organization meets the requirements of §§ 422.112 and 422.114 for access to services offered under the plan.
units.action_summary: Disclose detailed provider network information (number, mix, addresses, language capabilities, MOUD notations, out-of-network coverage, point-of-service options, and access compliance).

units.obligation_text: The MA organization must provide enrollees notice of a termination of a contracted provider, irrespective of whether the termination was for cause or without cause, in accordance with § 422.2267(e)(12).
units.action_summary: Provide enrollees notice of a contracted provider's termination (for-cause or without-cause) per § 422.2267(e)(12).

units.obligation_text: The MA organization must make a good faith effort to provide enrollees notice of a for-cause termination of a contracted provider within the timeframes required by this paragraph (e).
units.action_summary: Make a good faith effort to notify enrollees of for-cause provider terminations within required timeframes.

units.obligation_text: Provide both written and telephonic notice
units.action_summary: For primary care or behavioral health provider terminations, provide both written and telephonic notice to affected enrollees.

units.obligation_text: At least 45 calendar days before the termination effective date
units.action_summary: Provide notice at least 45 calendar days before the termination effective date for primary care or behavioral health providers.

units.obligation_text: To all enrollees who have ever been patients of that primary care or behavioral health provider.
units.action_summary: Notify all enrollees who have ever been patients of the terminating primary care or behavioral health provider.

units.obligation_text: Provide written notice
units.action_summary: For specialty provider terminations (other than primary care/behavioral health), provide written notice to affected enrollees.

units.obligation_text: At least 30 calendar days before the termination effective date
units.action_summary: Provide notice at least 30 calendar days before the termination effective date for specialty provider terminations.

units.obligation_text: To all enrollees who are patients seen on a regular basis by the provider whose contract is terminating.
units.action_summary: Notify enrollees who are regular patients of the terminating specialty provider (defined by assignment, current care, or care within past three months).

title: Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act: Benefit and Payment Parameters for 2024

units.obligation_text: For the 2020 through 2023 benefit years, States can request to reduce risk adjustment transfers in the State’s individual catastrophic, individual non-catastrophic, small group, or merged market risk pool by up to 50 percent in States where HHS operates the risk adjustment program.
units.action_summary: States may request up to a 50% reduction in risk adjustment transfers (2020-2023) in HHS-operated programs.

units.obligation_text: For the 2024 benefit year, only prior participants, as defined in paragraph (d)(5) of this section, may request to reduce risk adjustment transfers in the State’s individual catastrophic, individual non-catastrophic, small group, or merged market risk pool by up to 50 percent in States where HHS operates the risk adjustment program.
units.action_summary: Only prior participants may request up to a 50% reduction in risk adjustment transfers for 2024 in HHS-operated programs.

units.obligation_text: For the 2024 benefit year only, a justification for the requested reduction demonstrating the requested reduction would have de minimis impact on the necessary premium increase to cover the transfers for issuers that would receive reduced transfer payments.
units.action_summary: Requesters for 2024 must provide a justification showing the reduction would have de minimis impact on necessary premium increases for affected issuers.

units.obligation_text: For the 2024 benefit year only, that the requested reduction would have de minimis impact on the necessary premium increase to cover the transfers for issuers that would receive reduced transfer payments.
units.action_summary: Requesters for 2024 must demonstrate the reduction would have de minimis impact on necessary premium increases for affected issuers.

units.obligation_text: Within 15 calendar days of the notification of the findings of a second validation audit (if applicable) by HHS, in the manner set forth by HHS, an issuer must confirm the findings of the second validation audit (if applicable), or file a discrepancy report to dispute the findings of a second validation audit (if applicable).
units.action_summary: Issuers must confirm or dispute (file a discrepancy report) second validation audit findings within 15 calendar days of notification.

units.obligation_text: Within 30 calendar days of the notification by HHS of the calculation of a risk score error rate, in the manner set forth by HHS, an issuer must confirm the calculation of the risk score error rate as a result of risk adjustment data validation, or file a discrepancy report to dispute the calculation of a risk score error rate as a result of risk adjustment data validation.
units.action_summary: Issuers must confirm or dispute the calculated risk score error rate within 30 calendar days of HHS notification.

units.obligation_text: Notwithstanding any discrepancy report made under paragraph (d)(2) of this section, any discrepancy filed under § 153.630(d)(2) or (3), or any request for reconsideration under § 156.1220(a) of this subchapter with respect to any risk adjustment payment or charge... an issuer must report, for purposes of the risk corridors and MLR programs:
units.action_summary: Issuers must report specified disputed or reconsidered risk adjustment/reinsurance/other payment or charge items for risk corridors and MLR programs unless dispute resolved.

units.obligation_text: Have in effect an approved, or conditionally approved, Exchange Blueprint and operational readiness assessment prior to the date on which the Exchange would begin open enrollment as a State Exchange;
units.action_summary: State Exchanges must have an approved or conditionally approved Blueprint and operational readiness assessment before beginning open enrollment as a State Exchange.

units.obligation_text: Have in effect an approved, or conditionally approved, Exchange Blueprint and operational readiness assessment prior to the date on which the Exchange proposes to begin open enrollment as an SBE–FP, in accordance with HHS rules, as a State Exchange utilizing the Federal platform;
units.actor: Exchange (SBE–FP proposing to begin open enrollment)
units.action_summary: An Exchange proposing to operate as an SBE–FP must have an approved or conditionally approved Blueprint and operational readiness assessment before starting open enrollment.

units.obligation_text: The agent, broker, or web-broker may submit evidence in a form and manner to be specified by HHS, to rebut the allegation during this 90-day period.
units.action_summary: Agents/brokers/web-brokers are permitted to submit rebuttal evidence during the 90-day suspension period.

units.obligation_text: If the agent, broker, or web-broker submits such evidence during the suspension period, HHS will review the evidence and make a determination whether to lift the suspension within 45 calendar days of receipt of such evidence.
units.action_summary: HHS will review rebuttal evidence and decide whether to lift a suspension within 45 days of receiving it.
units.modal_raw: will review and make a determination

units.obligation_text: If the rebuttal evidence does not persuade HHS to lift the suspension, or if the agent, broker, or web-broker fails to submit rebuttal evidence during the suspension period, HHS may terminate the agent’s, broker’s, or web-broker’s agreements required under paragraph (d) of this section and under § 155.260(b) for cause under paragraph (g)(5)(ii) of this section.
units.action_summary: HHS may terminate agent/broker/web-broker agreements for cause if rebuttal evidence fails or is not submitted.

units.obligation_text: The HHS reconsideration entity will provide the agent, broker, or web-broker with a written notice of the reconsideration decision within 60 calendar days of the date it receives the request for reconsideration. This decision will constitute HHS' final determination.
units.action_summary: HHS reconsideration entity will send written reconsideration decisions within 60 days; that decision is final.

units.obligation_text: Provide the Federally-facilitated Exchanges with correct information, and document that eligibility application information has been reviewed by and confirmed to be accurate by the consumer, or the consumer’s authorized representative designated in compliance with § 155.227, prior to the submission of information under section 1411(b) of the Affordable Care Act...
units.action_summary: Agents/brokers/web-brokers must provide correct information to Federally-facilitated Exchanges and document that the consumer (or authorized rep) has reviewed and confirmed eligibility information before submission.

units.obligation_text: Documenting that eligibility application information has been reviewed by and confirmed to be accurate by the consumer or the consumer’s authorized representative must require the consumer or their authorized representative to take an action that produces a record that can be maintained by the individual or entity described in paragraph (j)(1) of this section and produced to confirm the consumer or their authorized representative has reviewed and confirmed the accuracy of the eligibility application information.
units.action_summary: Agents/brokers/web-brokers must require the consumer (or authorized rep) to take an action that generates a maintainable record confirming review and accuracy of eligibility information.

units.obligation_text: The documentation required under paragraph (j)(2)(ii)(A) of this section must include the date the information was reviewed, the name of the consumer or their authorized representative, an explanation of the attestations at the end of the eligibility application, and the name of the assisting agent, broker, or web-broker.
units.actor: individual or entity described in paragraph (j)(1)
units.action_summary: Required documentation must include review date, consumer/rep name, explanation of attestations, and name of assisting agent/broker/web-broker.

units.obligation_text: An individual or entity described in paragraph (j)(1) of this section must maintain the documentation described in paragraph (j)(2)(ii)(A) of this section for a minimum of ten years, and produce the documentation upon request in response to monitoring, audit, and enforcement activities conducted consistent with paragraphs (c)(5), (g), (h), and (k) of this section.
units.actor: individual or entity described in paragraph (j)(1)
units.action_summary: Those individuals/entities must retain the documentation for at least 10 years and produce it upon request for monitoring, audit, or enforcement.

units.obligation_text: Obtain and document the receipt of consent of the consumer or their authorized representative designated in compliance with § 155.227, employer, or employee prior to assisting with or facilitating enrollment through a Federally-facilitated Exchange or assisting the individual in applying for advance payments of the premium tax credit and cost-sharing reductions for QHPs;
units.action_summary: Agents/brokers/web-brokers must obtain and document consumer (or authorized rep) consent before assisting with enrollment or subsidy applications.

units.obligation_text: Obtaining and documenting the receipt of consent must require the consumer, or the consumer’s authorized representative designated in compliance with § 155.227, to take an action that produces a record that can be maintained and produced by an individual or entity described in paragraph (j)(1) of this section to confirm the consumer’s or their authorized representative’s consent has been provided. Non-exhaustive examples of acceptable documentation of consent include obtaining the signature of the consumer or their authorized representative (electronically or otherwise), verbal confirmation by the consumer or their authorized representative that is captured in an audio recording, a response from the consumer or their authorized representative to an electronic or other communication sent by the agent, broker, or web-broker.
units.action_summary: Consent documentation must require an action by the consumer/rep that produces a record (e.g., signature, recorded verbal confirmation, written response) to confirm consent.

units.obligation_text: The documentation required under paragraph (j)(2)(iii)(A) of this section must include a description of the scope, purpose, and duration of the consent provided by the consumer or their authorized representative designated in compliance with § 155.227, the date consent was given, name of the consumer or their authorized representative, and the name of the agent, broker, web-broker, or agency being granted consent, as well as a process through which the consumer or their authorized representative may rescind the consent.
units.action_summary: Consent documentation must state scope, purpose, duration, date given, consumer/rep name, agent/broker name, and a rescission process.

units.obligation_text: An individual or entity described in paragraph (j)(1) of this section must maintain the documentation described in paragraph (j)(2)(iii)(A) of this section for a minimum of 10 years, and produce the documentation upon request in response to monitoring, audit, and enforcement activities conducted consistent with paragraphs (c)(5), (g), (h), and (k) of this section.
units.actor: individual or entity described in paragraph (j)(1)
units.action_summary: Entities must retain consent documentation for at least 10 years and provide it upon request for monitoring, audit, or enforcement.
