units.obligation_text: Beginning January 1, 2024, the Exchange may not determine a tax filer eligible for APTC if the IRS notifies HHS and HHS notifies the Exchange ... that APTC payments were made on behalf of the tax filer or either spouse ... for two consecutive years ... and the tax filer or his or her spouse did not comply with the requirement to file an income tax return for that year and for the previous year ... and reconcile APTC for that period.
units.action_summary: Beginning Jan 1, 2024, Exchanges must not determine a tax filer eligible for APTC when IRS/HHS notify of two consecutive years of APTC payments and the filer (or spouse) failed to file required returns and reconcile APTC for those years.

units.obligation_text: Must extend the period described in paragraph (f)(2)(ii) of this section by a period of 60 days for an applicant if the applicant is required to present satisfactory documentary evidence to verify household income.
units.action_summary: The Exchange must extend the specified verification period by 60 days when an applicant is required to present satisfactory documentary evidence of household income.

units.obligation_text: Notwithstanding any other requirement described in this paragraph (c) to the contrary, when the Exchange requests tax return data and family size from the Secretary of Treasury as described in § 155.320(c)(1)(i)(A) but no such data is returned for an applicant, the Exchange will accept that applicant’s attestation of income and family size without further verification.
units.action_summary: If requested tax return data is not returned by Treasury, the Exchange will accept the applicant's attestation of income and family size without further verification.

units.obligation_text: If the enrollee’s current QHP is available through the Exchange and – the Exchange will re-enroll the enrollee in accordance with the following subparagraphs.
units.action_summary: When an enrollee's current QHP remains available, the Exchange will re-enroll the enrollee according to CSR eligibility and plan metal level conditions.

units.obligation_text: The Exchange will re-enroll the enrollee in the same plan as the enrollee’s current QHP when the enrollee is not CSR-eligible, in accordance with § 155.305(g).
units.action_summary: If not CSR-eligible, the Exchange will re-enroll the enrollee in the same plan.

units.obligation_text: The Exchange will re-enroll the enrollee either in the same plan as the enrollee’s current QHP, or, at the option of the Exchange, in a silver level QHP within the same product that has a lower or equivalent premium after APTC and that has the most similar network compared to the enrollee’s current QHP, when the enrollee is CSR-eligible and the enrollee’s current QHP is a bronze level plan.
units.action_summary: If CSR-eligible and currently in a bronze plan, the Exchange will re-enroll the enrollee in the same plan or may choose a silver plan in same product with similar network and not higher premium after APTC.

units.obligation_text: The Exchange will re-enroll the enrollee in the same plan as the enrollee’s current QHP when the enrollee is CSR-eligible and the enrollee’s current QHP is not a bronze level plan.
units.action_summary: If CSR-eligible and not in a bronze plan, the Exchange will re-enroll the enrollee in the same plan.

units.obligation_text: If the enrollee’s current QHP is not available through the Exchange the Exchange will re-enroll the enrollee in accordance with the following subparagraphs.
units.action_summary: When the enrollee's current QHP is not available, the Exchange will re-enroll the enrollee based on CSR eligibility, metal level, and most similar network rules.

units.obligation_text: If the enrollee is not CSR-eligible, in accordance with § 155.305(g), the Exchange will re-enroll the enrollee in a QHP within the same product, at the same metal level and that has the most similar network compared to the enrollee’s current QHP.
units.action_summary: If not CSR-eligible and current QHP not available, the Exchange will re-enroll the enrollee in a same-product QHP at the same metal level with the most similar network.

units.obligation_text: If the enrollee is CSR-eligible, and the enrollee’s current QHP is a bronze level plan, the Exchange will re-enroll the enrollee either in a bronze level QHP within the same product, or, at the option of Exchange, in a silver level QHP within the same product that has a lower or equivalent premium after APTC and that has the most similar network compared to the enrollee’s current QHP.
units.action_summary: If CSR-eligible and current QHP was bronze but unavailable, the Exchange will re-enroll in a bronze QHP or may choose a silver QHP in same product with similar network and not higher premium after APTC.

units.obligation_text: If the enrollee is CSR-eligible, and the enrollee’s current QHP is not a bronze level plan, the Exchange will re-enroll the enrollee in a QHP within the same product at the same metal level and that has the most similar network compared to the enrollee’s current QHP.
units.action_summary: If CSR-eligible and current QHP not bronze and unavailable, Exchange will re-enroll in same-product QHP at same metal level with most similar network.

units.obligation_text: If the enrollee’s current QHP is a silver level plan, the Exchange will re-enroll the enrollee in a silver level QHP under a different product offered by the same QHP issuer that is most similar to and that has the most similar network compared to the enrollee’s current product. If no such silver level QHP is available for enrollment through the Exchange, the Exchange will re-enroll the enrollee in a QHP under the same product that is one metal level higher or lower than the enrollee’s current QHP and that has the most similar network compared to the enrollee’s current QHP;
units.action_summary: If current QHP is silver, Exchange will re-enroll in most similar silver QHP under different product by same issuer, or if none, in same product one metal level higher or lower with similar network.

units.obligation_text: If the enrollee’s current QHP is not a silver level plan, the Exchange will re-enroll the enrollee under the same product that is one metal level higher or lower than the enrollee’s current QHP and that has the most similar network compared to the enrollee’s current QHP.
units.action_summary: If current QHP is not silver, Exchange will re-enroll in same product at one metal level higher or lower with most similar network.

units.obligation_text: If the enrollee’s current QHP is not available through the Exchange and the enrollee’s product no longer includes a QHP that is at the same metal level as, or one metal level higher or lower than the enrollee’s current QHP, the Exchange will re-enroll the enrollee in any other QHP offered under the product in which the enrollee’s current QHP is offered in which the enrollee is eligible to enroll that has the most similar network compared to the enrollee’s current QHP.
units.action_summary: If no QHP at same/adjacent metal level is available in the product, the Exchange will re-enroll the enrollee in another eligible QHP in that product with the most similar network.

units.obligation_text: When re-enrolling an enrollee as part of annual redetermination in circumstances described in this paragraph, the Exchange will apply the following issuer-same-product requirements.
units.action_summary: Exchange will re-enroll enrollees according to issuer-product similarity rules described in subparagraphs (i)-(v).

units.obligation_text: If the enrollee is not CSR eligible, the Exchange will re-enroll the enrollee in a QHP in the product offered by the same issuer that is the most similar to the enrollee’s current product at the same metal level as and with the most similar network compared to the enrollee’s current QHP;
units.action_summary: If not CSR-eligible, Exchange will re-enroll the enrollee in the most similar same-issuer product at the same metal level with most similar network.

units.obligation_text: If the enrollee is CSR-eligible, and the enrollee’s current QHP is a bronze level plan, the Exchange will re-enroll the enrollee either in a bronze level QHP, or, at the option of the Exchange, in a silver level QHP that has a lower or equivalent premium after APTC and that has the most similar network compared to the enrollee’s current QHP in the product offered by the same issuer through the Exchange that is most similar to the enrollee’s current product;
units.action_summary: If CSR-eligible and current QHP was bronze, the Exchange will re-enroll in a bronze QHP or may choose a silver QHP in same-issuer product with similar network and not higher premium after APTC.

units.obligation_text: If the enrollee is CSR-eligible, and the enrollee’s current QHP is not a bronze level plan, the Exchange will re-enroll the enrollee in a QHP at the same metal level that has the most similar network compared to the enrollee’s current QHP in the product offered by the same issuer that is the most similar to the enrollee’s current product;
units.action_summary: If CSR-eligible and current QHP not bronze, Exchange will re-enroll in same metal level QHP by same issuer with the most similar network.

units.obligation_text: If the issuer does not offer another QHP at the same metal level as the enrollee’s current QHP, the Exchange will re-enroll the enrollee in a QHP that is one metal level higher or lower than the enrollee’s current QHP and that has the most similar network compared to the enrollee’s current QHP in the product offered by the same issuer through the Exchange that is the most similar to the enrollee’s current product;
units.action_summary: If issuer lacks same-metal-level QHP, Exchange will re-enroll the enrollee in a QHP one metal level higher or lower with the most similar network from same issuer in the most similar product.

units.obligation_text: If the issuer does not offer another QHP through the Exchange at the same metal level as, or one metal level higher or lower than the enrollee’s current QHP, the Exchange will re-enroll the enrollee in any other QHP offered by the same issuer in which the enrollee is eligible to enroll in the product that is most similar to the enrollee’s current product and in a QHP within that product that has the most similar network to the enrollee’s current QHP.
units.action_summary: If issuer offers no QHP at same or adjacent metal level through the Exchange, Exchange will re-enroll the enrollee in any other eligible QHP by same issuer in the most similar product and with most similar network.

units.obligation_text: If an enrollee or his or her dependents become newly eligible for cost-sharing reductions ... and the enrollee or his or her dependents are not enrolled in a silver-level QHP, the Exchange must allow the enrollee and his or her dependents to change to a silver-level QHP if they elect to change their QHP enrollment;
units.action_summary: When someone becomes newly eligible for CSRs and is not enrolled in a silver plan, the Exchange must allow them to change to a silver-level QHP if they choose.

units.obligation_text: Beginning January 2022, if an enrollee or his or her dependents become newly ineligible for cost-sharing reductions ... and the enrollee or his or her dependents are enrolled in a silver-level QHP, the Exchange must allow the enrollee and his or her dependents to change to a QHP one metal level higher or lower if they elect to change their QHP enrollment;
units.action_summary: Starting Jan 2022, if someone becomes newly ineligible for CSRs and is enrolled in a silver plan, the Exchange must allow them to change to a plan one metal level higher or lower if they choose.

units.obligation_text: If the plan selection is made on or before the day of the triggering event, the Exchange must ensure that the coverage effective date is the first day of the month following the date of the triggering event.
units.action_summary: If plan selected on/before the day of the triggering event, the Exchange must set coverage to begin the first day of the following month.

units.obligation_text: If the plan selection is made after the date of the triggering event, the Exchange must ensure that coverage is effective in accordance with paragraph (b)(1) of this section or on the first day of the following month, at the option of the Exchange.
units.action_summary: If plan selected after triggering event, the Exchange must make coverage effective per (b)(1) or on the first day of the next month, at its option.

units.obligation_text: Notwithstanding the requirements of this paragraph (b)(2)(iv), and at the option of the Exchange, if the plan selection is made on or before the last day of the month preceding the triggering event, the Exchange must ensure that the coverage effective date is the first of the month in which the triggering event occurs for losses of coverage as described in paragraphs (d)(1), (d)(6)(iii), and (d)(15) of this section.
units.action_summary: At the Exchange's option, if plan selected on or before last day of month before triggering event, the Exchange must make coverage effective the first day of the month in which the triggering event occurs for certain loss-of-coverage situations.

units.obligation_text: A qualified individual or his or her dependent who is described in paragraph (d)(1), (d)(6)(iii), or (d)(15) of this section has 60 days before and, unless the Exchange exercises the option in paragraph (c)(6) of this section, 60 days after the triggering event to select a QHP.
units.action_summary: Qualified individuals/dependents generally have 60 days before and 60 days after the triggering event to select a QHP unless the Exchange limits via (c)(6).

units.obligation_text: At the option of the Exchange, a qualified individual or his or her dependent who is described in paragraph (d)(7) of this section; who is described in paragraph (d)(6)(iv) of this section becomes newly eligible for advance payments ... has 60 days before or after the triggering event to select a QHP.
units.action_summary: At the Exchange's option, certain qualified individuals/dependents may have 60 days before or after the triggering event to select a QHP (Exchange may choose one-sided timing).

units.obligation_text: Beginning January 1, 2024, at the option of the Exchange, a qualified individual or his or her dependent(s) who is described in paragraph (d)(1)(i) of this section and whose loss of coverage is a loss of Medicaid or CHIP coverage shall have 90 days after the triggering event to select a QHP.
units.action_summary: Beginning Jan 1, 2024, Exchange may allow individuals losing Medicaid/CHIP 90 days after the triggering event to select a QHP.

units.obligation_text: Exchanges on the Federal platform must ... prohibit QHP issuers from terminating dependent coverage of a child before the end of the plan year in which the child attains age 26, or before the end of the plan year in which the child attains the maximum age a QHP issuer is required to make available dependent coverage of children under applicable State law, on the basis of the child’s age, unless otherwise permitted.
units.action_summary: Federal platform Exchanges are required to prohibit QHP issuers from terminating dependent coverage of children based on age before the end of the applicable plan year.

units.obligation_text: State Exchanges using their own platform may prohibit QHP issuers from terminating dependent coverage of a child before the end of the plan year ... on the basis of the child’s age, unless otherwise permitted.
units.actor: State Exchanges using their own platform
units.action_summary: State Exchanges on their own platforms are permitted (but not required) to prohibit issuers from terminating dependent child coverage based on age before the end of the applicable plan year.

units.obligation_text: Prohibit QHP issuers from terminating dependent coverage of a child before the end of the plan year ... on the basis of the child’s age, unless otherwise permitted.
units.action_summary: QHP issuers are prohibited (where Exchanges impose prohibition) from terminating dependent child coverage before the end of the plan year due to the child's age, unless otherwise permitted.
units.modal_raw: are prohibited from (functional prohibition where Exchanges prohibit)

units.obligation_text: Within 14 calendar days of the date of the Exchange eligibility appeal decision issued by an impartial official as described in § 155.535(c)(4), a party to the appeal may request review of the Exchange eligibility appeal decision by the CMS Administrator.
units.action_summary: A party may request CMS Administrator review of an Exchange eligibility appeal decision within 14 calendar days of issuance.

units.obligation_text: Within 30 days of the date of the party’s request for administrative review, the CMS Administrator may decline to review the Exchange eligibility appeal decision;
units.action_summary: Within 30 days of a party's request, the CMS Administrator may decline to review the appeal decision.

units.obligation_text: Within 30 days of the date of the party’s request for administrative review, the CMS Administrator may render a final decision as described in § 155.545 (a)(1) based on their review of the eligibility appeal decision;
units.action_summary: Within 30 days of a request, the CMS Administrator may render a final decision based on review.

units.obligation_text: Within 30 days of the date of the party’s request for administrative review, the CMS Administrator may choose to take no action on the request for review.
units.action_summary: Within 30 days, the CMS Administrator may decide not to act on the request for review.
units.modal_raw: may choose to take no action

units.obligation_text: Within 14 calendar days of the date of the Exchange eligibility appeal decision issued by an impartial official as described in § 155.535(c)(4), the CMS Administrator may initiate a review of an eligibility appeal decision at their discretion.
units.action_summary: CMS Administrator may initiate review of an eligibility appeal decision within 14 days at their discretion.

units.obligation_text: Within 30 days of the date the CMS Administrator initiates a review, the CMS Administrator may decline to review the Exchange eligibility appeal decision;
units.action_summary: After initiating review, CMS Administrator may decline to review within 30 days.

units.obligation_text: Within 30 days of the date the CMS Administrator initiates a review, the CMS Administrator may render a final decision as described in § 155.545 (a)(1) based on their review of the eligibility appeal decision;
units.action_summary: Within 30 days of initiating review, CMS Administrator may render a final decision based on their review.

units.obligation_text: Within 30 days of the date the CMS Administrator initiates a review, the CMS Administrator may choose to take no action on the Exchange eligibility appeal decision.
units.action_summary: CMS Administrator may choose to take no action on the appeal decision within 30 days of initiating review.

units.obligation_text: For purposes of the IPPTA, a State Exchange must submit the following information in a form and manner specified by HHS:
units.action_summary: State Exchanges must submit specified IPPTA information to HHS in the form and manner HHS specifies.

units.obligation_text: The State Exchange must provide to HHS the following data documentation: The State Exchange’s data dictionary including attribute name, data type, allowable values, and description;
units.action_summary: State Exchanges must provide a data dictionary (attribute names, types, allowable values, descriptions) to HHS.

units.obligation_text: The State Exchange must provide to HHS an entity relationship diagram, which shall include the structure of the data tables and the residing data elements that identify the relationships between the data tables;
units.action_summary: State Exchanges must provide an entity relationship diagram showing data table structure and relationships.

units.obligation_text: The State Exchange must provide to HHS business rules and related calculations.
units.action_summary: State Exchanges must provide business rules and related calculations to HHS.

units.obligation_text: The State Exchange must use the pre-testing and assessment data request form, or other method as specified by HHS, to submit to HHS the application data associated with no fewer than 10 tax household identification numbers and the associated policy identification numbers that address scenarios specified by HHS to allow HHS to test all of the pre-testing and assessment processes and procedures.
units.action_summary: State Exchanges must submit application data for at least 10 tax households (and associated policy IDs) using HHS-specified forms/methods to allow testing of procedures.

units.obligation_text: The State Exchange must submit the information specified in paragraph (a) of this section within the timelines in the pre-testing and assessment plan specified in § 155.1515.
units.action_summary: State Exchanges must submit required IPPTA information according to timelines specified in the pre-testing and assessment plan.

units.obligation_text: The State Exchanges are required to participate in the IPPTA for a period of one calendar year. The State Exchange and HHS will execute the pre-testing and assessment procedures in this section within the timelines in the pre-testing and assessment plan.
units.action_summary: State Exchanges must participate in the IPPTA for one calendar year and execute procedures within the plan's timelines.

units.obligation_text: As a part of the orientation process, HHS will provide State Exchanges with an overview of the pre-testing and assessment procedures and identify documentation that a State Exchange must provide to HHS for pre-testing and assessment.
units.action_summary: HHS will give State Exchanges an overview of procedures and identify required documentation for pre-testing and assessment.

units.obligation_text: HHS, in collaboration with each State Exchange, will develop a pre-testing and assessment plan that takes into consideration relevant activities, if any, that were completed during a prior, voluntary State engagement. The pre-testing and assessment plan will include the pre-testing and assessment checklist.
units.actor: HHS (in collaboration with each State Exchange)
units.action_summary: HHS (with each State Exchange) will develop a pre-testing and assessment plan including the checklist, considering prior voluntary activities.

units.obligation_text: At the conclusion of the pre-testing and assessment planning process, HHS will issue the pre-testing and assessment plan specific to that State Exchange. The pre-testing and assessment plan will be for HHS and State Exchange internal use only and will not be made available to the public by HHS unless otherwise required by law.
units.action_summary: HHS will issue the State-specific plan and will keep it for internal use (not public) unless required by law.

units.obligation_text: As needed throughout the pre-testing and assessment period, HHS will issue notifications to State Exchanges concerning information related to the pre-testing and assessment processes and procedures.

units.obligation_text: Throughout the pre-testing and assessment period, the State Exchange must provide HHS with information regarding any operational, policy, business rules, information technology, or other changes that may impact the ability of the State Exchange to satisfy the requirements of the pre-testing and assessment.
units.action_summary: State Exchanges must inform HHS of any operational, policy, business rule, IT, or other changes that might affect their ability to meet pre-testing requirements.

units.obligation_text: As specified in § 155.1510, HHS will inform State Exchanges about the form and manner for State Exchanges to submit required data and data documentation to HHS in accordance with the pre-testing and assessment plan.

units.obligation_text: HHS will coordinate with each State Exchange to track and manage the data and data documentation submitted by a State Exchange as specified in § 155.1510(a)(1) and (2).
units.action_summary: HHS will coordinate with State Exchanges to track and manage submitted data and documentation.

units.obligation_text: HHS will coordinate with each State Exchange to provide assistance in aligning the data specified in § 155.1510(a)(2) from the State Exchange’s existing data structure to the standardized set of data elements.

units.obligation_text: HHS will coordinate with each State Exchange to interpret and validate the data specified in § 155.1510(a)(2).

units.obligation_text: HHS will use the data and data documentation submitted by the State Exchange to execute the pre-testing and assessment procedures.
units.action_summary: HHS will use State Exchanges' submitted data and documentation to carry out pre-testing and assessment procedures.

units.obligation_text: HHS will issue the pre-testing and assessment checklist as part of the pre-testing and assessment plan.
units.action_summary: HHS will issue a checklist as part of the pre-testing and assessment plan.

units.obligation_text: A State Exchange’s submission of the data documentation as specified in § 155.1510(a)(1).
units.action_summary: The checklist includes submission of required data documentation as a criterion; State Exchanges must submit such documentation.

units.obligation_text: A State Exchange’s submission of the data for processing and testing as specified in § 155.1510(a)(2);
units.action_summary: The checklist includes submission of processing and testing data (as specified) as a criterion; State Exchanges must provide it.

units.obligation_text: A State Exchange’s completion of the pre-testing and assessment processes and procedures related to the IPPTA program.
units.action_summary: The checklist includes completion of IPPTA processes and procedures as a criterion; State Exchanges must complete them.

units.obligation_text: Subsequent to the completion of a State Exchange’s pre-testing and assessment period, HHS will issue a pre-testing and assessment report specific to that State Exchange. title: Medicare Secondary Payer and Certain Civil Money Penalties; Extension of Timeline for Publication of Final Rule

units.section: Section 1871(a)(3)(A) of the Social Security Act
units.obligation_text: Section 1871(a)(3)(A) of the Social Security Act ... requires us to establish and publish a regular timeline for the publication of final regulations based on the previous publication of a proposed regulation.
units.action_summary: Establish and publish a regular timeline for publishing final regulations based on a previously published proposed regulation.

units.section: Section 1871(a)(3)(B) of the Social Security Act
units.obligation_text: Section 1871(a)(3)(B) of the Act allows us to extend the timeline for publication of the final rule by publishing a Federal Register document which includes a brief explanation of the justification for the variation in the timeline.
units.action_summary: Permits CMS/Secretary to extend the timeline for publishing a final rule by issuing a Federal Register document that includes a brief justification for the change.

units.section: Section 1871(a)(3) of the Social Security Act
units.obligation_text: The initial targeted timeline for a rule cannot exceed 3 years from the date of publishing the proposed regulation, absent exceptional circumstances.
units.actor: the Secretary / CMS (as to the initial targeted timeline)
units.action_summary: Prohibits the initial targeted timeline for a rule from exceeding three years from the date the proposed regulation was published, unless exceptional circumstances exist.

units.section: Section 1871(a)(3) of the Social Security Act
units.obligation_text: The Secretary may extend the initial targeted publication date of the final regulation if the Secretary provides public notice, including a brief explanation of the justification for the variation, no later than the regulation’s previously established proposed publication date.
units.action_summary: Permits the Secretary to extend the initial targeted publication date provided the Secretary gives public notice with a brief justification no later than the previously established proposed publication date.

units.section: Section 1871(a)(3)(B) of the Social Security Act
units.obligation_text: Section 1871(a)(3)(B) of the Act allows the regular timeline for publishing Medicare final regulations to vary based on the complexity of the regulation, number and scope of comments received, and other related factors.
units.action_summary: Permits the timeline for publishing Medicare final regulations to be varied based on factors such as regulatory complexity, comments received, and related factors.

units.obligation_text: As of February 22, 2023, the timeline for the publication of the final rule ... is extended until February 18, 2024.
units.action_summary: Officially extends the deadline for publishing the final rule until February 18, 2024.

title: Medicare and Medicaid Programs: Disclosures of Ownership and Additional Disclosable Parties Information for Skilled Nursing Facilities and Nursing Facilities

units.obligation_text: In addition to all other applicable reporting requirements in this subpart, a skilled nursing facility (as defined in section 1819(a) of the Act) must disclose upon initial enrollment (which, for purposes of this paragraph (g), also includes a change of ownership under 42 CFR 489.18) and revalidation the following information:
units.action_summary: Disclose specified ownership, governance, and related party information upon initial enrollment and revalidation (including COOs under 42 CFR 489.18).

units.obligation_text: Each member of the governing body of the facility, including the name, title, and period of service for each such member.
units.action_summary: Provide names, titles, and service periods for each governing body member.

units.obligation_text: Each person or entity who is an officer, director, member, partner, trustee, or managing employee (as defined in § 424.502) of the facility, including the name, title, and period of service of each such person or entity.
units.action_summary: Identify each officer, director, member, partner, trustee, or managing employee and provide their name, title, and service period.

units.obligation_text: Each person or entity who is an additional disclosable party of the facility (as defined in § 424.502).
units.action_summary: Identify each additional disclosable party associated with the facility.

units.obligation_text: The organizational structure (as defined in § 424.502) of each additional disclosable party of the facility and a description of the relationship of each such additional disclosable party to the facility and to one another.
units.action_summary: Provide the organizational structure of each additional disclosable party and describe their relationships to the facility and to each other.

units.obligation_text: The skilled nursing facility need not disclose the same information described in paragraph (g)(1) of this section more than once on the same enrollment application submission.
units.action_summary: Is not required to repeat the same disclosure information more than once on the same enrollment application submission.

units.obligation_text: The skilled nursing facility must report any change to any of the information described in paragraph (g)(1) of this section consistent with the applicable timeframes in paragraph (e) of this section.
units.action_summary: Report changes to any disclosed information within the applicable timeframes in paragraph (e).

units.obligation_text: In addition to all other applicable reporting requirements in this subpart, a nursing facility (as defined in section 1919(a) of the Act) must disclose upon initial enrollment and revalidation the following information:
units.action_summary: Disclose specified ownership, governance, and related party information upon initial enrollment and revalidation.

units.obligation_text: Each member of the governing body of the facility, including the name, title, and period of service for each such member.
units.action_summary: Provide names, titles, and service periods for each governing body member.

units.obligation_text: Each person or entity who is an officer, director, member, partner, trustee, or managing employee (as defined in § 455.101) of the facility, including the name, title, and period of service of each such person or entity.
units.action_summary: Identify each officer, director, member, partner, trustee, or managing employee and provide their name, title, and service period.

units.obligation_text: Each person or entity who is an additional disclosable party of the facility (as defined in § 455.101).
units.action_summary: Identify each additional disclosable party associated with the facility.

units.obligation_text: The organizational structure (as defined in § 455.101) of each additional disclosable party of the facility and a description of the relationship of each such additional disclosable party to the facility and to one another.
units.action_summary: Provide the organizational structure of each additional disclosable party and describe their relationships to the facility and to each other.

units.obligation_text: The State need not require the facility to disclose the same information described in this paragraph (e) more than once on the same enrollment application submission.
units.action_summary: State agencies are not required to demand that a facility repeat the same disclosure information more than once on the same enrollment application.

units.obligation_text: Total amount available for a fiscal year. The total amount available for value-based incentive payments for a fiscal year is at least 60 percent of the total amount of the reduction to the adjusted SNF PPS payments for that fiscal year, as estimated by CMS, and will be increased as appropriate for each fiscal year to account for the assignment of a performance score to low-volume SNFs under paragraph (d)(3) of this section.
units.action_summary: CMS must set the total amount available for value-based incentive payments at least 60% of the reduction to adjusted SNF PPS payments and increase it as appropriate to account for assignment of scores to low-volume SNFs.

units.obligation_text: Beginning with the FY 2023 SNF VBP, the total amount available for value-based incentive payments for a fiscal year is 60 percent of the total amount of the reduction to the adjusted SNF PPS payments for that fiscal year, as estimated by CMS.
units.action_summary: For FY2023, CMS sets the total amount available for incentive payments equal to 60% of the reduction to adjusted SNF PPS payments.

units.obligation_text: Beginning with the FY 2027 SNF VBP, the total amount available for value-based incentive payments for a fiscal year is at least 60 percent of the total amount of the reduction to the adjusted SNF PPS payments for that fiscal year, as estimated by CMS, and will be increased as appropriate for each fiscal year to account for the application of the Health Equity Adjustment described at paragraph (k) of this section.
units.action_summary: Beginning FY2027, CMS must set the total amount available at least 60% of the reduction and increase it as appropriate to account for application of the Health Equity Adjustment.

units.obligation_text: CMS will calculate a SNF Performance Score for a fiscal year for a SNF for which it has granted an exception request that does not include its performance on a quality measure during the calendar months affected by the extraordinary circumstance.
units.action_summary: CMS will compute a SNF Performance Score for SNFs granted an exception that excludes performance during months affected by an extraordinary circumstance.

units.obligation_text: (3) Calculation of the SNF performance score beginning with fiscal year 2027. The SNF performance score for a fiscal year is calculated as follows:
units.action_summary: CMS must calculate the SNF performance score for each fiscal year beginning FY2027 according to the following steps.

units.obligation_text: CMS will sum all points awarded to a SNF as described in paragraph (e)(1) of this section for each measure applicable to a fiscal year.
units.action_summary: CMS will add together all points awarded to a SNF for each applicable measure.

units.obligation_text: CMS will normalize the SNF’s point total such that the resulting point total is expressed as a number of points earned out of a total of 100.
units.action_summary: CMS will scale the SNF's point total to a 0-100 point scale.

units.obligation_text: CMS will add to the SNF’s point total under paragraph (e)(3)(ii) of this section any applicable health equity adjustment bonus points calculated under paragraph (k) of this section such that the resulting point total is the SNF Performance Score for the fiscal year, except that no SNF Performance Score may exceed 100 points.
units.action_summary: CMS will add any applicable Health Equity Adjustment bonus points to the normalized total to form the SNF Performance Score, which cannot exceed 100 points.

units.obligation_text: Validation. Beginning with the FY 2023 Program year, for the SNFRM measure, and beginning with the FY 2026 Program year for all other claims-based measures, the information reported through claims are validated for accuracy by Medicare Administrative Contractors (MACs). Beginning with the FY 2026 Program year, for all measures that are calculated using Payroll-Based Journal System data, information reported through the Payroll-Based Journal system is validated for accuracy by CMS and its contractors through quarterly audits. Beginning with the FY 2027 program year, for all measure that are calculated using Minimum Data Set (MDS) information, such information is validated for accuracy by CMS and its contractors through periodic audits not to exceed 1,500 SNFs per calendar year.

units.obligation_text: Beginning with the FY 2026 Program year, for all measures that are calculated using Payroll-Based Journal System data, information reported through the Payroll-Based Journal system is validated for accuracy by CMS and its contractors through quarterly audits.
units.action_summary: Beginning FY2026, CMS and its contractors must validate PBJ-reported information via quarterly audits.

units.obligation_text: Calculation of the Health Equity Adjustment (HEA) bonus points. CMS calculates the number of HEA bonus points that are added to a SNF’s point total calculated under paragraph (e)(3)(iii) of this section by:
units.action_summary: CMS must calculate HEA bonus points to add to a SNF's point total by following the listed steps.

units.obligation_text: Determining for each measure whether the SNF is a top tier performing SNF and assigning two points to the SNF for each such measure;
units.action_summary: CMS must determine if a SNF is top tier on each measure and assign two points for each such measure.

units.obligation_text: Summing the points calculated under paragraph (k)(1) of this section to calculate the measure performance scaler;
units.action_summary: CMS must sum the assigned points to compute the measure performance scaler.

units.obligation_text: Calculating the underserved multiplier for the SNF; and
units.action_summary: CMS must calculate the SNF's underserved multiplier.

units.obligation_text: Multiplying the measure performance scaler calculated under paragraph (k)(2) of this section by the underserved multiplier calculated under paragraph (k)(3) of this section.
units.action_summary: CMS must multiply the measure performance scaler by the underserved multiplier to compute HEA bonus points.

units.action_summary: CMS will approve an entity's application to administer the questionnaire when the applicant meets minimum business requirements and agrees to comply with current survey protocols.

units.obligation_text: An entity must be a CMS-approved survey vendor in order to administer and submit the resident satisfaction survey data to CMS on behalf of one or more SNFs.

units.obligation_text: SNFs and CMS-approved survey vendors must fully comply with resident satisfaction measure oversight activities, including allowing CMS to perform site visits at the survey vendors’ company locations.

units.obligation_text: SNFs must meet or exceed the following data completeness thresholds with respect to a calendar year:
units.action_summary: SNFs are required to meet or exceed the listed data completeness thresholds each calendar year.

units.obligation_text: The threshold set at 100 percent completion of measures data and standardized patient assessment data collected using the Minimum Data Set (MDS) on at least 80 percent of the assessments SNFs submit through the CMS designated data submission system for FY 2018 through FY 2025.
units.action_summary: For FY2018–FY2025, SNFs must have 100% completion of MDS measures on at least 80% of submitted assessments.

units.obligation_text: The threshold set at 100 percent completion of measures data and standardized patient assessment data collected using the MDS on at least 90 percent of the assessments SNFs submit through the CMS designated data submission system beginning with the FY 2026 program year.
units.action_summary: Beginning FY2026, SNFs must have 100% completion of MDS measures on at least 90% of submitted assessments.

units.obligation_text: The threshold set at 100 percent for measures data collected and submitted through the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention’s (CDC) National Healthcare Safety Network (NHSN) for FY 2023 and for all subsequent payment updates.
units.action_summary: For FY2023 and thereafter, SNFs must submit 100% of measures data collected through NHSN.

units.obligation_text: The threshold set at 75 percent of the weeks in a reporting year for submission of resident information files and 90 percent completion of the data required in resident information files for the resident satisfaction measure for FY 2026 and for all subsequent payment updates.
units.action_summary: Beginning FY2026, SNFs must submit resident information files for at least 75% of weeks and achieve 90% completion of required data for the resident satisfaction measure.

units.obligation_text: These thresholds apply to all measures and standardized patient assessment data requirements adopted into the SNF QRP.
units.action_summary: The listed thresholds apply to all measures and standardized patient assessment data requirements adopted into the SNF Quality Reporting Program.

units.action_summary: CMS will compute a SNF Performance Score for SNFs granted exception requests excluding months affected by the extraordinary circumstance.

units.obligation_text: Calculation of the SNF performance score beginning with fiscal year 2027. The SNF performance score for a fiscal year is calculated as follows:
units.action_summary: The SNF performance score for FY2027 and later must be calculated according to the specified steps.

units.obligation_text: CMS will sum all points awarded to a SNF as described in paragraph (e)(1) of this section for each measure applicable to a fiscal year.
units.action_summary: CMS will add together all points awarded to a SNF for applicable measures for the fiscal year.

units.obligation_text: CMS will normalize the SNF’s point total such that the resulting point total is expressed as a number of points earned out of a total of 100.
units.action_summary: CMS will convert the SNF's raw point total to a 0–100 scale.

units.obligation_text: CMS will add to the SNF’s point total under paragraph (e)(3)(ii) of this section any applicable health equity adjustment bonus points calculated under paragraph (k) of this section such that the resulting point total is the SNF Performance Score for the fiscal year.
units.action_summary: CMS will add any applicable HEA bonus points to the normalized point total to produce the SNF Performance Score.

units.obligation_text: except that no SNF Performance Score may exceed 100 points.
units.action_summary: The SNF Performance Score is capped at 100 points; it cannot exceed 100.

units.obligation_text: Beginning with the FY 2023 Program year, for the SNFRM measure, and beginning with the FY 2026 Program year for all other claims-based measures, the information reported through claims are validated for accuracy by Medicare Administrative Contractors (MACs).
units.action_summary: MACs validate the accuracy of claims-reported information for specified measures in the stated program years.

units.obligation_text: Beginning with the FY 2026 Program year, for all measures that are calculated using Payroll-Based Journal System data, information reported through the Payroll-Based Journal system is validated for accuracy by CMS and its contractors through quarterly audits.
units.action_summary: CMS and its contractors must validate PBJ-reported information via quarterly audits starting FY2026.

units.obligation_text: Beginning with the FY 2027 program year, for all measure that are calculated using Minimum Data Set (MDS) information, such information is validated for accuracy by CMS and its contractors through periodic audits not to exceed 1,500 SNFs per calendar year.
units.action_summary: CMS and its contractors validate MDS-based measure information through periodic audits starting FY2027.

units.obligation_text: such information is validated for accuracy by CMS and its contractors through periodic audits not to exceed 1,500 SNFs per calendar year.
units.action_summary: The periodic audits of MDS information are limited to auditing no more than 1,500 SNFs per calendar year.

units.obligation_text: Calculation of the Health Equity Adjustment (HEA) bonus points. CMS calculates the number of HEA bonus points that are added to a SNF’s point total calculated under paragraph (e)(3)(iii) of this section by:
units.action_summary: CMS must calculate HEA bonus points according to the following steps.

units.obligation_text: Determining for each measure whether the SNF is a top tier performing SNF and assigning two points to the SNF for each such measure;
units.action_summary: CMS determines if a SNF is top-tier on each measure and assigns two points per such measure.

units.obligation_text: Summing the points calculated under paragraph (k)(1) of this section to calculate the measure performance scaler;
units.action_summary: CMS sums the points from k(1) to compute the measure performance scaler.

units.obligation_text: Calculating the underserved multiplier for the SNF; and
units.action_summary: CMS calculates the underserved multiplier for the SNF.

units.obligation_text: Multiplying the measure performance scaler calculated under paragraph (k)(2) of this section by the underserved multiplier calculated under paragraph (k)(3) of this section.
units.action_summary: CMS multiplies the measure performance scaler by the underserved multiplier to produce HEA bonus points.

units.obligation_text: Resident satisfaction data. A SNF must submit to CMS data regarding resident satisfaction after a short-stay discharge in the form and manner, and at a time, specified by CMS.
units.action_summary: SNFs must submit resident satisfaction data after short-stay discharge in the form, manner, and timing specified by CMS.

units.obligation_text: Requirements. A SNF must contract with an independent survey vendor, approved by CMS in accordance with paragraph (b)(2)(ii) of this section, to administer the resident satisfaction questionnaire on its behalf.
units.action_summary: SNFs must contract with a CMS-approved independent survey vendor to administer the resident satisfaction questionnaire.

units.obligation_text: CMS approves an application for an entity to administer the resident satisfaction questionnaire on behalf of one or more SNFs when an applicant has met the resident satisfaction survey’s Protocols and Guidelines minimum business requirements that can be found on the official resident satisfaction measure website, and agrees to comply with the current survey administration protocols that can be found on the resident satisfaction measure website.
units.action_summary: An applicant must meet the survey's minimum business requirements and agree to comply with current survey administration protocols for CMS to approve it as a vendor.

units.obligation_text: An entity must be a CMS-approved survey vendor in order to administer and submit the resident satisfaction survey data to CMS on behalf of one or more SNFs.
units.actor: Entity seeking to administer/submit resident satisfaction survey data
units.action_summary: An entity must obtain CMS approval as a survey vendor before administering or submitting resident satisfaction data on behalf of SNFs.

units.obligation_text: Compliance with oversight activities. SNFs and CMS-approved survey vendors must fully comply with resident satisfaction measure oversight activities, including allowing CMS to perform site visits at the survey vendors’ company locations.
units.action_summary: SNFs and approved vendors must comply with oversight activities, including permitting CMS site visits at vendor locations.

units.obligation_text: SNFs must meet or exceed the following data completeness thresholds with respect to a calendar year:
units.action_summary: SNFs are required to meet or exceed specified annual data completeness thresholds.

units.obligation_text: The threshold set at 100 percent completion of measures data and standardized patient assessment data collected using the Minimum Data Set (MDS) on at least 80 percent of the assessments SNFs submit through the CMS designated data submission system for FY 2018 through FY 2025.
units.action_summary: For FY2018–FY2025, SNFs must have 100% completion of measures and MDS data on at least 80% of assessments submitted.

units.obligation_text: The threshold set at 100 percent completion of measures data and standardized patient assessment data collected using the MDS on at least 90 percent of the assessments SNFs submit through the CMS designated data submission system beginning with the FY 2026 program year.
units.action_summary: Beginning FY2026, SNFs must achieve 100% completion of measures and MDS data on at least 90% of assessments submitted.

units.obligation_text: The threshold set at 100 percent for measures data collected and submitted through the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention’s (CDC) National Healthcare Safety Network (NHSN) for FY 2023 and for all subsequent payment updates.
units.action_summary: For FY2023 and after, SNHs must submit 100% of specified measures data collected via NHSN.

units.obligation_text: The threshold set at 75 percent of the weeks in a reporting year for submission of resident information files and 90 percent completion of the data required in resident information files for the resident satisfaction measure for FY 2026 and for all subsequent payment updates.
units.action_summary: Beginning FY2026, SNFs must submit resident information files for 75% of weeks and have 90% completion of required resident satisfaction data.

units.obligation_text: These thresholds apply to all measures and standardized patient assessment data requirements adopted into the SNF QRP.
units.actor: SNF Quality Reporting Program (requirements applicable to SNFs)
units.action_summary: The listed thresholds apply broadly to all measures and standardized assessment data adopted into the SNF QRP.

units.obligation_text: If a facility waives its right to a hearing as specified in § 488.436, the State initiates collection of civil money penalty imposed per day of noncompliance after 60 days from the date of the notice imposing the penalty and the State has not received a timely request for a hearing.
units.action_summary: If the facility waives hearing rights and no timely request is received, the State will start collecting per-day civil money penalties after 60 days from notice.

units.obligation_text: If a facility waives its right to a hearing as specified in § 488.436, the State initiates collection of civil money penalty imposed per instance of noncompliance after 60 days from the date of the notice imposing the penalty and the State has not received a timely request for a hearing.
units.action_summary: If the facility waives hearing rights and no timely request is received, the State will start collecting per-instance civil money penalties after 60 days from notice.

units.obligation_text: Constructive waiver of a hearing. A facility is deemed to have waived its right to a hearing after 60 days from the date of the notice imposing the civil money penalty if CMS has not received a request for a hearing from the facility.
units.action_summary: If CMS does not receive a hearing request within 60 days of the penalty notice, the facility is deemed to have waived its right to a hearing.

units.obligation_text: Except as provided for in § 488.431, a civil money penalty is due 75 days after the notice of the penalty in accordance with § 488.436 and a hearing request was not received when:
units.action_summary: A civil money penalty becomes due 75 days after the penalty notice if no hearing request was received, subject to § 488.431 exceptions.

units.actor: an IPF (as defined under § 412.402) that is paid under the IPF PPS

units.action_summary: A withdrawn IPF will have its annual payment update reduced as specified in paragraph (a).

units.action_summary: A withdrawn IPF must renew participation per paragraph (b) to participate in future years of the IPFQR Program.

units.obligation_text: Except as provided in paragraph (f) of this section, IPFs that participate in the IPFQR Program must submit to CMS data on measures selected under section 1886(s)(4)(D) of the Act and specified non-measure data in a form and manner, and at a time specified by CMS

units.action_summary: CMS will use the rulemaking process to make substantive updates to measure specifications for the IPFQR Program.

units.obligation_text: Quality measures adopted for the IPFQR Program measure set for a previous payment determination year are retained for use in subsequent payment determination years, except when they are removed, suspended, or modified as set forth in paragraph (3) of this section
units.action_summary: Quality measures from prior payment determination years are retained for subsequent years unless removed/suspended/modified per paragraph (3).

units.obligation_text: CMS will use the regular rulemaking process to remove, suspend, or modify quality measures in the IPFQR Program to allow for public comment
units.action_summary: CMS will use the regular rulemaking process (with opportunity for public comment) to remove, suspend, or modify quality measures.

units.obligation_text: Factors for consideration in removal or replacement of quality measures.  CMS will weigh whether to remove or modify measures based on the following factors:
units.action_summary: CMS will consider the following factors when deciding whether to remove or modify quality measures.

units.obligation_text: Factor 1:  Measure performance among IPFs is so high and unvarying that meaningful distinctions and improvements in performance can no longer be made
units.action_summary: Consider removing/modifying a measure if performance is uniformly high and unvarying so distinctions/improvements are no longer possible.

units.obligation_text: Factor 2:  Measure does not align with current clinical guidelines or practice
units.action_summary: Consider removal/modification if the measure does not align with current clinical guidelines or practice.

units.obligation_text: Factor 3:  Measure can be replaced by a more broadly applicable measure (across settings or populations) or a measure that is more proximal in time to desired patient outcomes for the particular topic
units.action_summary: Consider replacement if a more broadly applicable or more proximate-to-outcomes measure is available.

units.obligation_text: Factor 4:  Measure performance or improvement does not result in better patient outcomes
units.action_summary: Consider removal/modification if measure performance/improvement does not lead to better patient outcomes.

units.obligation_text: Factor 5:  Measure can be replaced by a measure that is more strongly associated with desired patient outcomes for the particular topic
units.action_summary: Consider replacement if a measure more strongly associated with desired outcomes exists.

units.obligation_text: Factor 6:  Measure collection or public reporting leads to negative unintended consequences other than patient harm
units.action_summary: Consider removal/modification if collection or public reporting of the measure causes negative unintended consequences (other than patient harm).

units.obligation_text: Factor 7:  Measure is not feasible to implement as specified
units.action_summary: Consider removal/modification if the measure is not feasible to implement as specified.

units.obligation_text: Factor 8:  The costs associated with a measure outweigh the benefit of its continued use in the program
units.action_summary: Consider removal/modification if the costs of a measure outweigh its benefits to the program.

units.obligation_text: Retention. CMS may retain a quality measure that meets one or more of the measure removal factors described in paragraph (i) of this subsection if the continued collection of data on the quality measure would align with other CMS and HHS policy goals, align with other CMS programs, or support efforts to move IPFs toward reporting electronic measures
units.action_summary: CMS may retain a measure that meets removal factors if continued collection aligns with CMS/HHS policy goals, other CMS programs, or supports movement to electronic measures.

units.obligation_text: if the continued collection of data on the quality measure would align with other CMS and HHS policy goals, align with other CMS programs, or support efforts to move IPFs toward reporting electronic measures

units.action_summary: CMS may, at its discretion, grant exceptions to IPFs that did not request them when CMS determines an extraordinary circumstance has occurred.

units.obligation_text: Except as provided in paragraph (f) of this section, IPFs that participate in the IPFQR Program must submit to CMS data on measures selected under section 1886(s)(4)(D) of the Act and specified non-measure data in a form and manner, and at a time specified by CMS.
units.actor: IPFs that participate in the IPFQR Program
units.action_summary: Participating IPFs must submit specified measure and non-measure data to CMS in the form, manner, and time CMS specifies, subject to paragraph (f) exceptions.

units.obligation_text: Except as provided in paragraph (f) of this section
units.actor: IPFs that participate in the IPFQR Program
units.action_summary: The data submission obligation is subject to the exceptions described in paragraph (f).

units.obligation_text: CMS uses rulemaking to make substantive updates to the specifications of measures used in the IPFQR Program
units.action_summary: CMS will use rulemaking to make substantive updates to measure specifications.

units.obligation_text: Quality measures adopted for the IPFQR Program measure set for a previous payment determination year are retained for use in subsequent payment determination years, except when they are removed, suspended, or modified as set forth in paragraph (3) of this section.
units.action_summary: Quality measures adopted in prior years are retained for subsequent years unless removed, suspended, or modified under paragraph (3).

units.obligation_text: CMS will use the regular rulemaking process to remove, suspend, or modify quality measures in the IPFQR Program to allow for public comment.
units.action_summary: CMS will use the rulemaking process (allowing public comment) to remove, suspend, or modify measures.

units.obligation_text: CMS will weigh whether to remove or modify measures based on the following factors:
units.action_summary: CMS will consider specified factors when deciding whether to remove or modify measures.

units.obligation_text: Factor 1: Measure performance among IPFs is so high and unvarying that meaningful distinctions and improvements in performance can no longer be made;
units.action_summary: A removal/modification factor is that measure performance is uniformly high so distinctions/improvements can't be made.

units.obligation_text: Factor 2: Measure does not align with current clinical guidelines or practice;
units.action_summary: A factor is that the measure does not align with current clinical guidelines/practice.

units.obligation_text: Factor 3: Measure can be replaced by a more broadly applicable measure (across settings or populations) or a measure that is more proximal in time to desired patient outcomes for the particular topic;
units.action_summary: A factor is that the measure can be replaced by a more broadly applicable or more proximal measure.

units.obligation_text: Factor 4: Measure performance or improvement does not result in better patient outcomes;
units.action_summary: A factor is that performance/improvement on the measure does not lead to better patient outcomes.

units.obligation_text: Factor 5: Measure can be replaced by a measure that is more strongly associated with desired patient outcomes for the particular topic;
units.action_summary: A factor is that the measure can be replaced by one more strongly associated with desired patient outcomes.

units.obligation_text: Factor 6: Measure collection or public reporting leads to negative unintended consequences other than patient harm;
units.action_summary: A factor is that collecting or publicly reporting the measure causes negative unintended consequences (not including patient harm).

units.obligation_text: Factor 7: Measure is not feasible to implement as specified; and
units.action_summary: A factor is that the measure is not feasible to implement as specified.

units.obligation_text: Factor 8: The costs associated with a measure outweigh the benefit of its continued use in the program.
units.action_summary: A factor is that the costs of a measure outweigh the benefits of continued use.

units.obligation_text: CMS may retain a quality measure that meets one or more of the measure removal factors described in paragraph (i) of this subsection if the continued collection of data on the quality measure would align with other CMS and HHS policy goals, align with other CMS programs, or support efforts to move IPFs toward reporting electronic measures.
units.action_summary: CMS may retain a measure that meets removal factors if continued collection aligns with CMS/HHS policy goals, other CMS programs, or supports electronic reporting efforts.

units.obligation_text: if the continued collection of data on the quality measure would align with other CMS and HHS policy goals, align with other CMS programs, or support efforts to move IPFs toward reporting electronic measures
units.action_summary: Condition under which CMS may retain a measure: continued collection aligns with policy goals/programs or supports electronic reporting.

units.obligation_text: CMS may grant an exception to one or more data submissions deadlines and requirements in the event of extraordinary circumstances beyond the control of the IPF, such as when an act of nature affects an entire region or locale or a systemic problem with one of CMS’s data collection systems directly or indirectly affects data submission.
units.action_summary: CMS may grant exceptions to data submission deadlines/requirements when extraordinary circumstances beyond the IPF's control occur.

units.obligation_text: Upon request by the IPF.
units.action_summary: An exception under paragraph (f) may be granted upon the IPF's request.

units.obligation_text: At the discretion of CMS. CMS may grant exceptions to IPFs that have not requested them when CMS determines that an extraordinary circumstance has occurred.
units.action_summary: CMS may, at its discretion and upon determining extraordinary circumstances, grant exceptions even without an IPF request.

units.obligation_text: Data that an IPF submits to CMS for the IPFQR Program will be made publicly available on a CMS website after providing the IPF an opportunity to review the data to be made public.
units.action_summary: CMS will publish IPF-submitted data on a CMS website after giving the IPF an opportunity to review the data before publication.

units.obligation_text: IPFs will have a period of 30 days to review and submit corrections to errors resulting from CMS calculations prior to the data being made public.
units.action_summary: IPFs are afforded a 30-day period to review submitted data and submit corrections to errors from CMS calculations before public posting.

units.obligation_text: Beginning in calendar year 2025, a multifactor productivity adjustment (as determined by CMS) and 0.5 percentage point, except that the 0.5 percentage point reduction shall not apply to hospital outpatient items and services, not including separately payable drugs, furnished by a hospital with a CMS certification number (CCN) effective date of January 2, 2018, or later.
units.action_summary: Beginning in 2025, apply a multifactor productivity adjustment and a 0.5 percentage point reduction to prospective payment rates (subject to the specified exception).

units.obligation_text: the 0.5 percentage point reduction shall not apply to hospital outpatient items and services, not including separately payable drugs, furnished by a hospital with a CMS certification number (CCN) effective date of January 2, 2018, or later.

title: CMS-2447-IFC  Medicaid: Enforcement of State Compliance with Reporting and Federal Medicaid Renewal Requirements under the Social Security Act

units.obligation_text: Disputes that pertain to CMS’ imposition of suspensions of procedural disenrollments and civil money penalties under § 430.49(c) of this part are heard by the Board in accordance with procedures set forth in 45 CFR part 16.
units.action_summary: The Board will hear disputes about CMS's imposition of suspensions of procedural disenrollments and civil money penalties under §430.49(c) following 45 CFR part 16.

units.obligation_text: After consideration of any mitigating circumstances in accordance with paragraph (d) of this section and notwithstanding whether an FMAP reduction has been imposed under § 435.928 of this subchapter, CMS will determine whether to require the State to submit a corrective action plan if CMS finds that the State is not in compliance during the period beginning on April 1, 2023, through June 30, 2024, with either of the following requirements:
units.action_summary: If CMS finds certain noncompliance in the specified period, CMS will determine whether to require the State to submit a corrective action plan.

units.obligation_text: If, after considering mitigating circumstances as described in paragraph (d) of this section, the Administrator decides to require the State to submit and implement a corrective action plan for noncompliance described in paragraph (b)(1) of this section or to revise or resubmit such a plan, the Administrator will provide the State with a written notice directing the State to submit a corrective action plan to correct the identified areas of noncompliance.
units.action_summary: If the Administrator requires a corrective action plan, the Administrator must give the State a written notice directing submission of a CAP to address the noncompliance.

units.obligation_text: Such notice will – (i) Explain the violation of Federal redetermination or reporting requirements that CMS has identified and the basis for CMS’ finding;
units.action_summary: The notice must explain the identified violation and the basis for CMS's finding.

units.obligation_text: Such notice will – (ii) Inform the State of the requirement to submit and implement a corrective action plan;
units.action_summary: The notice must inform the State that it is required to submit and implement a corrective action plan.

units.obligation_text: Such notice will – (iii) Include instructions on the method and deadline by which the State must submit a corrective action plan to CMS;
units.action_summary: The notice must include how and when the State must submit the CAP to CMS.

units.obligation_text: Such notice will – (iv) Explain the enforcement actions that CMS may pursue if the State fails to submit or implement an approved corrective action plan, including if CMS disapproves the State’s submitted CAP or if the State fails to meet the requirements set forth in the approved CAP, in accordance with this section.
units.action_summary: The notice must explain potential enforcement actions CMS may take if the State fails to submit or implement an approvable CAP.

units.obligation_text: A State that receives a notice described in paragraph (b)(2) of this section must submit a corrective action plan, including the elements in paragraph (b)(3) of this section, not later than 14 calendar days from the date of the notice of noncompliance.
units.action_summary: A State receiving the notice must submit a CAP with required elements within 14 calendar days.

units.obligation_text: A corrective action plan must describe in detail— (i) The actions the State will take immediately, if needed to prevent further harm or risk of harm to beneficiaries while it implements the corrective action plan, including to prevent increased burden for beneficiaries in completing the renewal process, loss of coverage at renewal for individuals who continue to meet the substantive eligibility criteria and whose eligibility should otherwise be retained but for failure to meet a procedural requirement, and delays in access to coverage or care;
units.action_summary: The CAP must detail immediate actions the State will take to prevent harm or increased burden to beneficiaries.

units.obligation_text: A corrective action plan must describe in detail— (ii) The steps the State will take to ensure compliance with Federal requirements, including but not limited to new policies, procedures, operational processes or systems changes it will implement;
units.action_summary: The CAP must describe steps the State will take to achieve compliance, including new policies or system changes.

units.obligation_text: A corrective action plan must describe in detail— (iii) Key milestones and a detailed timeline for achieving compliance;
units.action_summary: The CAP must include key milestones and a detailed timeline for achieving compliance.

units.obligation_text: A corrective action plan must describe in detail— (iv) A plan for communicating the steps the State will take to prevent actual harm or risk of harm to beneficiaries and to ensure compliance with Federal requirements per paragraphs (b)(3)(i) and (ii) of this section to State staff, including staff of non-Medicaid agencies or entities to which the agency has delegated authority to conduct redeterminations of eligibility in accordance with § 431.10(c)(1)(i) of this subchapter; CMS; and beneficiaries, as applicable.
units.action_summary: The CAP must include a communication plan to inform relevant staff, CMS, and beneficiaries about steps to prevent harm and ensure compliance.

units.obligation_text: CMS must approve or disapprove a corrective action plan submitted by the State within 21 calendar days of the date it is submitted. If CMS does not approve or disapprove the corrective action plan within 21 calendar days of submission, the corrective action plan will be deemed approved.
units.action_summary: CMS must approve or disapprove a submitted CAP within 21 days; failure to act within 21 days results in deemed approval.

units.obligation_text: A State must begin implementation of the corrective action plan not later than 14 calendar days after the date that either the State receives CMS approval, or the corrective action plan is deemed approved.
units.action_summary: The State must start implementing an approved or deemed-approved CAP within 14 days of approval or deemed approval.

units.obligation_text: A corrective action plan will be approved if CMS determines that the plan– (i) Meets the requirements at paragraph (b)(3) of this section; (ii) Promptly eliminates or minimizes any harm or risk of harm to beneficiaries ...; and (iii) Results in the State achieving compliance in a reasonable time, taking into account systems challenges and circumstances faced by the agencies involved.
units.action_summary: CMS will approve a CAP if it meets the CAP-content requirements, promptly addresses harm or risk, and leads to compliance within a reasonable time.
units.modal_raw: will be approved if CMS determines

units.obligation_text: (i) Meets the requirements at paragraph (b)(3) of this section;
units.action_summary: The CAP must meet the content requirements listed in paragraph (b)(3).

units.obligation_text: (ii) Promptly eliminates or minimizes any harm or risk of harm to beneficiaries, including increased burden for beneficiaries in completing the renewal process, loss of coverage at renewal for individuals who continue to meet the substantive eligibility criteria ... and delays in access to coverage or care due to the noncompliance to be addressed by the plan;
units.action_summary: The CAP must promptly eliminate or minimize harm or risk of harm to beneficiaries caused by the noncompliance.

units.obligation_text: (iii) Results in the State achieving compliance in a reasonable time, taking into account systems challenges and circumstances faced by the agencies involved.
units.action_summary: The CAP must lead to the State achieving compliance within a reasonable timeframe considering challenges.

units.obligation_text: After considering any applicable mitigating circumstances in accordance with paragraph (d) of this section and notwithstanding whether the State is subject to an FMAP reduction under § 435.928 of this subchapter, CMS may take one or both of the following actions if the State fails to submit or implement an approved corrective action plan ... :
units.action_summary: If a State fails to submit or implement an approved CAP, CMS may take enforcement actions described below.

units.obligation_text: (i) Require the State to suspend some or all procedural disenrollments, in accordance with paragraph (c)(3)(i) of this section;
units.action_summary: CMS may require the State to suspend some or all procedural disenrollments.

units.obligation_text: (ii) Impose civil money penalties in accordance with paragraph (c)(3)(ii) of this section.
units.action_summary: CMS may impose civil money penalties on the State for failure to submit or implement an approved CAP.

units.obligation_text: Prior to requiring the State to suspend procedural disenrollments of Medicaid eligibility or imposing civil money penalties, CMS will issue a notice to the State.
units.action_summary: Before requiring suspensions or imposing penalties, CMS will issue a notice to the State.

units.obligation_text: Such notice will include – (A) A description of the enforcement action(s) CMS is taking and the basis for such action(s);
units.action_summary: The notice must describe the enforcement actions CMS is taking and the basis for them.

units.obligation_text: Such notice will include – (B) Whether CMS is requiring the State to suspend some or all procedural disenrollments and, in the case of a partial suspension, the affected populations;
units.action_summary: The notice must state whether CMS is requiring suspension of some or all procedural disenrollments and identify affected populations for partial suspensions.

units.obligation_text: Such notice will include – (C) The date on which the State must begin suspending procedural disenrollments, if applicable;
units.action_summary: The notice must include the date the State must begin suspending procedural disenrollments, if applicable.

units.obligation_text: Such notice will include – (D) The daily amount owed for any civil money penalties imposed, the date the penalties will begin to be charged, the timeline for payment (including information on how the timeline for payment would be affected by an appeal), and instructions on how to submit payment;
units.action_summary: The notice must include penalty daily amount, when charges begin, payment timeline and appeal effects, and payment instructions.

units.obligation_text: Such notice will include – (E) The steps the State must take to cure its noncompliance and for CMS to lift the enforcement action(s);
units.action_summary: The notice must list steps the State must take to correct noncompliance and obtain lifting of enforcement actions.

units.obligation_text: Such notice will include – (F) Information on the State’s appeal rights as described in paragraph (f) of this section, including the deadline to submit an appeal request, and the effect of requesting an appeal on the applicability of any enforcement actions pending the decision in such appeal. The notice must also provide that the decision outlined in the notice is final unless it is timely appealed as described in paragraph (f) of this section.
units.action_summary: The notice must inform the State of appeal rights, appeal deadline, effect of appeal on enforcement actions, and that the decision is final unless timely appealed.

units.obligation_text: CMS may issue additional notices requiring a State to take additional actions (including paying increased civil money penalties or implementing or broadening the scope of a required suspension of procedural disenrollments) if CMS identifies additional violations of corrective action plan provisions. Such notices will meet the requirements outlined in paragraph (c)(2)(i) of this section.
units.action_summary: CMS may issue additional notices requiring further actions or increased penalties if additional violations are found; such notices must meet the specified content requirements.

units.obligation_text: (A) If the noncompliance determined by CMS under paragraph (b)(1) of this section impacts a substantial number of (meaning all or nearly all) individuals who are or should have been found eligible for Medicaid, CMS will require the State to suspend all procedural disenrollments.
units.action_summary: If noncompliance affects a substantial number of individuals, CMS will require the State to suspend all procedural disenrollments.

units.obligation_text: (B) If the impact of the noncompliance is limited (for example, to a specific population or geographic area), CMS may limit the suspension of procedural disenrollments to the impacted population(s). After requiring a limited suspension of procedural disenrollments, CMS may later opt to require the State to suspend all procedural disenrollments if CMS subsequently determines that the impact of the noncompliance is greater than was initially determined, or if the State fails to comply with the initial requirement to suspend some procedural disenrollments in accordance with the notice issued under paragraph (c)(2) of this section. In these circumstances, CMS will issue a subsequent notice under paragraph (c)(2).
units.action_summary: CMS may limit suspensions to impacted populations, may later require full suspension if impact is greater or State fails to comply, and will issue a subsequent notice in such cases.
