units.modal_raw: may limit / may later opt / will issue

units.obligation_text: CMS may require the State to pay a civil money penalty of not more than $100,000, as adjusted annually under 45 CFR part 102, for each day that the State has not submitted or implemented an approved corrective action plan in accordance with the requirements described in paragraph (b) of this section or has failed to meet the requirements of the approved plan, until the penalty is lifted due to the State meeting the conditions described in paragraph (e) of this section.
units.action_summary: CMS may require the State to pay daily civil money penalties (up to the stated maximum, adjusted annually) for failure to submit or implement an approved CAP until the penalty is lifted under specified conditions.

units.obligation_text: Civil money penalties will start accruing five (5) calendar days after the date of the initial notice described in paragraph (c)(2) of this section and become payable 60 calendar days after the date of the notice, if not timely appealed, or 60 calendar days after issuance of a final determination at the conclusion of any appeal pursuant to paragraph (f) of this section.
units.action_summary: Penalties begin accruing 5 days after initial notice and become payable 60 days after notice (if not appealed) or 60 days after final appeal determination.

units.obligation_text: The amount of any applicable civil money penalties ... will be determined according to the following formula ...: Days 1-30 of noncompliance: $25,000/day; Days 31-60 of noncompliance: $50,000/day; and Days 61 or more of noncompliance until lifted ...: $100,000/day. Each of these amounts is adjusted annually under 45 CFR part 102.
units.action_summary: Penalty amounts follow a tiered daily formula: $25k/day for days 1-30; $50k/day for days 31-60; $100k/day for day 61 onward (subject to annual adjustment).

units.obligation_text: Consistent with paragraph (c)(2)(ii) of this section, if CMS identifies additional violations of corrective action plan provisions, CMS may issue additional notices to increase civil money penalties more quickly than provided for by the formula in paragraph (c)(3)(ii)(B) of this section.
units.action_summary: If additional violations are identified, CMS may issue notices to increase penalties more quickly than the tiered formula.

units.obligation_text: If the State fails to suspend procedural disenrollments as required pursuant to a notice described in paragraph (c)(2) of this section, or to pay civil money penalties as specified in that notice, or both, CMS may issue an additional notice pursuant to paragraph (c)(2) of this section to increase the civil money penalties to the maximum allowable daily amount, if not already reached, or may pursue additional enforcement action under section 1904 of the Act and § 430.35 of this subpart, including withholding some or all Federal financial participation.
units.action_summary: If the State fails to comply with suspension or payment requirements, CMS may increase penalties to the maximum and may pursue further enforcement actions, including withholding federal funds.

units.obligation_text: In the case of noncompliance relating to a violation of Federal redetermination requirements, CMS may delay requiring, or determine not to require, a State to submit a corrective action plan under paragraph (b) of this section if — (i) The noncompliance caused neither actual harm nor a substantial risk of harm to beneficiaries ...; or (ii) CMS determines that there is an emergency or other extraordinary circumstances preventing the State’s compliance.
units.action_summary: For redetermination-related noncompliance, CMS may delay or choose not to require a CAP if there's no harm/risk or if extraordinary circumstances prevent compliance.
units.modal_raw: may delay or determine not to require

units.obligation_text: (i) The noncompliance caused neither actual harm nor a substantial risk of harm to beneficiaries, including increased burden for beneficiaries in completing the renewal process, loss of coverage at renewal for individuals who continue to meet the substantive eligibility criteria and whose eligibility should otherwise be retained but for failure to meet a procedural requirement, and delays in access to coverage or care to beneficiaries;
units.action_summary: Noncompliance that caused no actual harm or substantial risk may justify delaying or not requiring a CAP.

units.obligation_text: (ii) CMS determines that there is an emergency or other extraordinary circumstances preventing the State’s compliance.
units.action_summary: If CMS finds emergency or extraordinary circumstances prevented compliance, it may delay or not require a CAP.

units.obligation_text: In the case of noncompliance relating to a violation of the reporting requirements under § 435.927 of this subchapter, CMS may delay requiring, or determine not to require, a State to submit a corrective action plan under paragraph (b) of this section if – (i) CMS has determined that the State implementing a corrective action plan is not necessary to ensure that the noncompliance is remedied; or (ii) CMS determines that there is an emergency or other extraordinary circumstances preventing the State’s compliance.
units.action_summary: For reporting-related noncompliance, CMS may delay or not require a CAP if a CAP is unnecessary to remedy the issue or extraordinary circumstances prevented compliance.
units.modal_raw: may delay or determine not to require

units.obligation_text: (i) CMS has determined that the State implementing a corrective action plan is not necessary to ensure that the noncompliance is remedied;
units.action_summary: CMS may decide a CAP is unnecessary to remedy the reporting noncompliance, and therefore delay or not require a CAP.

units.obligation_text: (ii) CMS determines that there is an emergency or other extraordinary circumstances preventing the State’s compliance.
units.action_summary: Extraordinary circumstances preventing compliance can justify delaying or not requiring a CAP for reporting noncompliance.

units.obligation_text: (i) In the case of a State that has failed to submit or implement an approved corrective action plan relating to a violation of either the reporting requirements under § 435.927 of this subchapter or Federal redetermination requirements, CMS may delay or forgo imposing civil money penalties if CMS determines that the State faces an emergency or other extraordinary circumstances that – (A) Occurred after the violation resulting in CMS’ requirement of a CAP ...; and (B) Has significantly impeded the State’s ability to submit or implement a corrective action plan.
units.action_summary: If extraordinary circumstances occurred after the violation and significantly impeded the State's ability to submit/implement a CAP, CMS may delay or forgo imposing penalties.

units.obligation_text: (A) Occurred after the violation resulting in CMS’ requirement of a CAP for noncompliance with Federal redetermination requirements or reporting requirements under § 435.927;
units.action_summary: The circumstance must have occurred after the violation that led to the CAP requirement.

units.obligation_text: (B) Has significantly impeded the State’s ability to submit or implement a corrective action plan.
units.action_summary: The extraordinary circumstance must significantly impede the State's ability to submit or implement a CAP.

units.obligation_text: (ii) In the case of a State’s failure to submit or implement a corrective action plan relating to a violation of the reporting requirements under § 435.927 of this subchapter in which the underlying reporting violation does not impede CMS’ oversight of the State’s procedural disenrollments, CMS will: (A) Delay suspension of procedural disenrollments for 1 month; and (B) Impose civil money penalties, except in cases where there are also extraordinary circumstances as described in paragraph (d)(3)(i) of this section.
units.action_summary: If the reporting violation doesn't impede oversight of procedural disenrollments, CMS will delay suspension for one month and impose civil money penalties unless extraordinary circumstances exist.

units.obligation_text: (A) Delay suspension of procedural disenrollments for 1 month;
units.action_summary: CMS will delay suspending procedural disenrollments for one month in the specified reporting-violation circumstances.

units.obligation_text: (B) Impose civil money penalties, except in cases where there are also extraordinary circumstances as described in paragraph (d)(3)(i) of this section.
units.action_summary: CMS will impose civil money penalties in these circumstances unless extraordinary circumstances justify otherwise.

units.obligation_text: (i) The State will be required to continue any suspension of procedural disenrollments required pursuant to such notice, and any civil money penalties imposed in accordance with the terms of such notice will continue to be charged, until– (A) For a State that failed to submit a corrective action plan, the State submits a corrective action plan that CMS determines is approvable consistent with paragraph (b)(5) of this section. (B) For a State that failed to implement an approved corrective action plan, the State has implemented or resumed implementation of such plan.
units.action_summary: When CMS has issued a notice, the State must continue any required suspension, and penalties will continue to accrue until the State submits an approvable CAP or implements/resumes implementation of an approved CAP.

units.obligation_text: (A) For a State that failed to submit a corrective action plan, the State submits a corrective action plan that CMS determines is approvable consistent with paragraph (b)(5) of this section.
units.action_summary: The State must submit an approvable CAP to end suspensions/penalties for failure to submit.

units.obligation_text: (B) For a State that failed to implement an approved corrective action plan, the State has implemented or resumed implementation of such plan.
units.action_summary: The State must implement or resume implementation of an approved CAP to end suspensions/penalties for failure to implement.

units.obligation_text: CMS will continue the accrual of civil money penalties from the date specified in the original notice provided to the State under paragraph (c)(2) of this section until CMS determines whether the plan is approvable. If CMS determines that the plan is approvable, CMS will retroactively end the accrual of the civil money penalties on the day the CAP was submitted and cease charging civil money penalties prospectively. If CMS determines that the plan is not approvable, CMS will continue charging civil money penalties imposed under the terms of the enforcement notice without interruption until the State submits an approvable plan.
units.actor: CMS (charging/accrual actions) and the State (to stop penalties)
units.action_summary: CMS will continue penalty accrual until it determines whether the CAP is approvable; if approvable, CMS will end accrual retroactively and stop future charges; if not, CMS will continue charging until an approvable plan is submitted.
units.modal_raw: will continue / will retroactively end / will continue charging

units.obligation_text: Where a State has met the conditions under paragraph (e)(1)(i) of this section, CMS will notify the State that the enforcement actions are being lifted. For States that were required to suspend procedural disenrollments, such notice will include the date on which the State may resume such disenrollments. For States that were subject to civil money penalties, such notice will include the date on which such civil money penalties stopped accruing, the total number of days for which civil money penalties accrued and the amount(s) of such civil money penalties, and the total amount of civil money penalties owed.
units.action_summary: CMS will notify the State when enforcement actions are lifted and include details about resume date for disenrollments and penalty accruals and amounts.

units.obligation_text: For States that were required to suspend procedural disenrollments, such notice will include the date on which the State may resume such disenrollments.
units.action_summary: CMS's notice must state the date when the State may resume procedural disenrollments.

units.obligation_text: For States that were subject to civil money penalties, such notice will include the date on which such civil money penalties stopped accruing, the total number of days for which civil money penalties accrued and the amount(s) of such civil money penalties, and the total amount of civil money penalties owed.
units.action_summary: CMS's notice must provide the date penalties stopped accruing, total days and amounts accrued, and total amount owed.

units.obligation_text: A State that is dissatisfied with CMS’s determination under paragraph (c) of this section that the State must suspend procedural disenrollments or pay civil money penalties ... may appeal, pursuant to 45 CFR part 16, the imposition of such suspensions of procedural disenrollments or civil money penalties to the Departmental Appeals Board ... within 30 days after receipt of a notice described in paragraph (c)(2) of this section.
units.action_summary: A State may appeal CMS's determination to suspend disenrollments or impose penalties to the Departmental Appeals Board within 30 days of receiving the notice.

units.obligation_text: The appeal request must comply with 45 CFR 16.7, and the process for counting days to submit an appeal will follow the provisions under 45 CFR 16.19. The appeals process is governed by 45 CFR part 16.
units.action_summary: An appeal request must follow 45 CFR 16.7 and day-counting rules in 45 CFR 16.19; appeals are governed by 45 CFR part 16.

units.obligation_text: If the State does not submit an appeal request within the 30-day timeframe provided for an appeal to the Board, then the decision described in the notice received by the State under paragraph (c)(2) of this section is the final decision of the Secretary and is final agency action within the meaning of 5 U.S.C. 704.
units.action_summary: If the State fails to appeal within 30 days, the notice decision becomes the Secretary's final agency action.

units.obligation_text: If any party to the appeal is dissatisfied with the Board’s decision under paragraph (f)(1) of this section, it may seek the Administrator’s reconsideration of that decision within 15 calendar days of receiving notice of the decision pursuant to 45 CFR 16.21.
units.action_summary: A party dissatisfied with the Board's decision may seek the Administrator's reconsideration within 15 days of notice of the decision.

units.obligation_text: The request for reconsideration must be filed with the Administrator and must include a copy of the Board’s decision, a brief statement of why the party believes the decision was wrong, and a statement of the amount of any civil money penalties in dispute.
units.action_summary: A reconsideration request must be filed with the Administrator and include the Board's decision, reasons it's wrong, and amounts of penalties in dispute.

units.obligation_text: The party requesting reconsideration must send a copy of the request described in paragraph (f)(2)(i)(A) of this section to all other parties to the appeal and other participants in the appeal (as described in 45 CFR 16.16) at the same time that the request is filed with the Administrator.
units.action_summary: The requesting party must serve all other parties and participants with the reconsideration request at the time of filing with the Administrator.

units.obligation_text: Any other party to the appeal, or other participant in the appeal, may respond to the request for reconsideration in writing and file their response with the Administrator within 15 calendar days of the date the request for reconsideration is filed with the Administrator.
units.action_summary: Other parties or participants may file written responses to a reconsideration request within 15 days of its filing.

units.obligation_text: The Administrator will review the Board’s decision and any additional information submitted by the parties and other participants under paragraphs (f)(2)(i)(A) or (C) of this section and, within 60 calendar days after the Board issues notice of its decision under 45 CFR 16.21, will either affirm the Board’s decision or issue a new decision.
units.action_summary: The Administrator will review the Board's decision and materials and will affirm or issue a new decision within 60 days of the Board's notice.
units.modal_raw: will review / will either affirm or issue

units.obligation_text: Within the 60-day period that is described in paragraph (f)(2)(i)(D) of this section, the Administrator may also modify or reverse the Board’s decision even if no party to the appeal has requested reconsideration of that decision.
units.action_summary: During the 60-day review period, the Administrator may modify or reverse the Board's decision even without a reconsideration request.

units.obligation_text: If no request for reconsideration is filed under paragraph (f)(2)(i) of this section and the Administrator does not modify or reverse the Board’s decision within the 60-day period described in paragraph (f)(2)(ii) of this section, then the decision of the Board is the final determination of the Secretary and is final agency action, ... and the Administrator will provide notice to all parties and other participants of such decision as described in paragraph (f)(2)(iv) of this section.
units.actor: the Administrator / the Board / the Secretary
units.action_summary: If no reconsideration is requested and the Administrator does not act within 60 days, the Board's decision becomes the Secretary's final agency action and the Administrator will notify all parties.

units.obligation_text: The Administrator will provide a notice to all parties and other participants of the final decision together with a notice indicating that this is the final determination of the Secretary and is final agency action, as described in paragraph (f)(2)(v) of this section.
units.action_summary: The Administrator will notify all parties and participants of the final decision and that it is the Secretary's final agency action.

units.obligation_text: The determination of the Administrator pursuant to paragraph (f)(2)(i)(D) or (f)(2)(ii) of this section is the final determination of the Secretary and is final agency action within the meaning of 5 U.S.C. 704.
units.action_summary: The Administrator's determination under the specified paragraphs is the Secretary's final determination and final agency action under 5 U.S.C. 704.

units.obligation_text: For data representing activities conducted by a State during the time period beginning April 1, 2023, and ending June 30, 2024, each State must submit to CMS the data described in paragraph (d) of this section, and those data must be timely, complete, and of sufficient quality (as those terms are defined in paragraph (b) of this section). To meet this requirement, a State must:
units.action_summary: States must submit specified redetermination data for April 1, 2023 through June 30, 2024; submissions must be timely, complete, and of sufficient quality.

units.obligation_text: Submit data via existing CMS-approved processes;
units.action_summary: A State may meet the reporting requirement by submitting data through existing CMS-approved processes.

units.obligation_text: Submit data through alternative processes approved by CMS, under the circumstances specified in paragraph (b)(4) of this section.
units.action_summary: Alternatively, a State may submit data through CMS-approved alternative processes when CMS has approved such alternatives.

units.obligation_text: States must submit the following data to CMS in accordance with paragraph (c) of this section:
units.action_summary: States are required to submit the enumerated data elements to CMS as specified.

units.obligation_text: Total number of Medicaid and Children’s Health Insurance Program (CHIP) beneficiaries for whom a renewal was initiated.
units.action_summary: Report the total number of Medicaid and CHIP beneficiaries for whom a renewal was initiated.

units.obligation_text: Total number of Medicaid and CHIP beneficiaries whose Medicaid or CHIP coverage is renewed.
units.action_summary: Report the total number of beneficiaries whose coverage was renewed.

units.obligation_text: Of the Medicaid and CHIP beneficiaries whose Medicaid or CHIP coverage is renewed, the total number whose coverage is renewed on an ex parte basis.
units.action_summary: Report how many renewed coverage on an ex parte basis.

units.obligation_text: Total number of individuals whose coverage for Medicaid or CHIP was terminated.
units.action_summary: Report the total number of individuals whose coverage was terminated.

units.obligation_text: Total number of individuals whose coverage for Medicaid or CHIP was terminated for procedural reasons.
units.action_summary: Report the number of terminations that were for procedural reasons.

units.obligation_text: Total number of beneficiaries who were enrolled in a separate CHIP.
units.action_summary: Report the count of beneficiaries enrolled in a separate CHIP.

units.obligation_text: For each State call center, total call center volume.
units.action_summary: Report total call center volume for each State call center.

units.obligation_text: For each State call center, average wait times.
units.action_summary: Report average wait times for each State call center.

units.obligation_text: For each State call center, average abandonment rate.
units.action_summary: Report average abandonment rates for each State call center.

units.obligation_text: For States with State-based Exchanges (SBEs) using a Non-Integrated Eligibility System and not using the Federal Exchange eligibility and enrollment platform:
units.actor: the States (with SBEs using Non-Integrated Eligibility Systems)
units.action_summary: States with SBEs using a Non-Integrated Eligibility System must submit the following specific data elements.

units.obligation_text: (i) Total number of individuals whose accounts are received by the SBE or Basic Health Program (BHP) due to a Medicaid/CHIP redetermination.
units.actor: the States (with SBEs using Non-Integrated Systems)
units.action_summary: Report number of individuals whose accounts are received by SBE or BHP due to Medicaid/CHIP redetermination.

units.obligation_text: (ii) Total number of individuals who apply for coverage due to a Medicaid/CHIP redetermination who are determined eligible for a QHP or a BHP.
units.actor: the States (with SBEs using Non-Integrated Systems)
units.action_summary: Report number of individuals who applied due to redetermination and were determined eligible for a QHP or BHP.

units.obligation_text: (iii) Total number of individuals who apply for coverage due to a Medicaid/CHIP redetermination who are determined eligible for a QHP or a BHP, and who make a QHP plan selection or are enrolled in a BHP.
units.actor: the States (with SBEs using Non-Integrated Systems)
units.action_summary: Report number of such applicants who are determined eligible and who select a QHP plan or enroll in a BHP.

units.obligation_text: For States with SBEs with an Integrated Eligibility System and not using the Federal Exchange eligibility and enrollment platform:
units.actor: the States (with SBEs with Integrated Eligibility Systems)
units.action_summary: States with SBEs using an Integrated Eligibility System must submit the following specific data elements.

units.obligation_text: (i) Total number of individuals who apply for coverage due to a Medicaid/CHIP redetermination who are determined eligible for a QHP or a BHP.
units.actor: the States (with SBEs with Integrated Systems)
units.action_summary: Report the number of applicants due to redetermination who were determined eligible for a QHP or BHP.

units.obligation_text: (ii) Total number of individuals who apply for coverage due to a Medicaid/CHIP redetermination who are determined eligible for a QHP or BHP, and who make a QHP plan selection or are enrolled in a BHP.
units.actor: the States (with SBEs with Integrated Systems)
units.action_summary: Report the number of such applicants who are determined eligible and who select a QHP plan or enroll in a BHP.

units.obligation_text: If CMS finds that, for a fiscal quarter in the period beginning on July 1, 2023, and ending on June 30, 2024, the State was noncompliant with the requirements of § 435.927, CMS will reduce the State’s Federal medical assistance percentage (FMAP) for that fiscal quarter as described in paragraph (b)(4) of this section.
units.action_summary: CMS will reduce a State's FMAP for any fiscal quarter in which the State is found noncompliant with §435.927.

units.obligation_text: A State is noncompliant in a fiscal quarter if it has failed to comply with the reporting requirements described in § 435.927 for one or more months of the quarter.
units.action_summary: A State is noncompliant in a quarter if it failed to comply with §435.927 in one or more months of that quarter.

units.obligation_text: The FMAP reduction under paragraph (b)(2) of this section will equal the product of 0.25 percentage points and the number of the fiscal quarters during the period from July 1, 2023, through June 30, 2024, in which the State is noncompliant with the reporting requirements described in § 435.927. When States are noncompliant in multiple quarters during that period, the FMAP reduction will increase by 0.25 percentage points for each successive quarter of noncompliance, even if nonconsecutive, but in no case will the reduction for any single quarter exceed 1 percentage point.
units.action_summary: FMAP reduction equals 0.25 percentage points times the number of noncompliant fiscal quarters in the period, increasing by 0.25 points per quarter but capped at 1 percentage point per quarter.
units.modal_raw: will equal / will increase / will not exceed

units.obligation_text: The FMAP reduction ... will equal the product of 0.25 percentage points and the number of the fiscal quarters ... in which the State is noncompliant with the reporting requirements described in § 435.927.
units.action_summary: FMAP reduction = 0.25 percentage points × number of noncompliant fiscal quarters in the specified period.

units.obligation_text: When States are noncompliant in multiple quarters during that period, the FMAP reduction will increase by 0.25 percentage points for each successive quarter of noncompliance, even if nonconsecutive,
units.action_summary: For each quarter of noncompliance during the period, the FMAP reduction increases by 0.25 percentage points, even if quarters are nonconsecutive.

units.obligation_text: but in no case will the reduction for any single quarter exceed 1 percentage point.
units.action_summary: The FMAP reduction for any single quarter is capped at 1 percentage point.

units.obligation_text: In programs listed in appendix A, B.(a)(1), to this part implement a decision to disallow Federal financial participation claimed in expenditures reported on a statement of expenditures, by recovering, withholding or offsetting payments, if the decision is issued before the reported expenditures are included in the calculation of a subsequent grant;
units.actor: programs listed in appendix A, B.(a)(1) to this part
units.action_summary: Programs identified may implement a decision to disallow federal financial participation by recovering, withholding, or offsetting payments if the decision is timely issued.

units.obligation_text: Take other action to recover, withhold, or offset funds if specifically authorized by statute or regulation;
units.actor: programs listed in appendix A, B.(a)(1) to this part
units.action_summary: Programs may take other statutorily or regulatorily authorized actions to recover, withhold, or offset funds.

units.obligation_text: Take action to require a State to suspend procedural disenrollments, as defined at 42 CFR 430.5, or continue the accrual of the civil money penalties a State owes under 42 CFR 430.49(c).
units.actor: programs listed in appendix A, B.(a)(1) to this part
units.action_summary: Programs may take action to require suspension of procedural disenrollments or to continue accrual of civil money penalties owed by a State under §430.49(c).

units.obligation_text: Decisions relating to suspensions of procedural disenrollments and civil money penalties under 42 CFR 430.49(c).
units.action_summary: The Board reviews disputes concerning suspensions of procedural disenrollments and civil money penalties under §430.49(c).

title: CMS-1808-P

units.obligation_text: The Board consists of five members appointed by the Secretary.
units.action_summary: Secretary must appoint a Board of five members.

units.obligation_text: All members must be knowledgeable in the field of payment of providers under Medicare Part A.
units.action_summary: Board members are required to have knowledge of Medicare Part A provider payment.

units.obligation_text: At least one member must be a certified public accountant.
units.action_summary: At least one Board member is required to be a certified public accountant.

units.obligation_text: At least two Board members must be representative of providers of services.
units.action_summary: At least two Board members must represent providers of services.

units.obligation_text: The term of office for Board members must be 3 years, except that initial appointments may be for such shorter terms as the Secretary may designate to permit staggered terms of office.
units.action_summary: Board member terms are generally 3 years; Secretary may designate shorter initial terms for staggering.

units.obligation_text: No member may serve more than three consecutive terms of office, except a Board member who, in their second or third consecutive term, is designated as Chairperson, as described in paragraph (c) of this section, may serve a maximum of four consecutive terms, provided that the Member continues to serve as Chairperson once so designated.
units.action_summary: Members generally may not serve more than three consecutive terms; a member designated Chairperson in 2nd or 3rd consecutive term may serve up to four consecutive terms if they continue as Chairperson.

units.obligation_text: The Secretary has the authority to terminate a Board member's term of office for good cause.
units.action_summary: Secretary may terminate a Board member's term for good cause.

units.obligation_text: Additional payments are made for outlier cases, bad debts, indirect medical education costs, for serving a disproportionate share of low-income patients, for the additional resource costs of domestic National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health approved surgical N95 respirators, and for the additional resource costs for small, independent hospitals to establish and maintain access to buffer stocks of essential medicines.
units.action_summary: CMS provides additional payments for listed categories, including buffer stock costs for small independent hospitals.

units.obligation_text: A payment adjustment for small, independent hospitals for the additional resource costs of establishing and maintaining access to buffer stocks of essential medicines as specified in § 412.113.
units.action_summary: A payment adjustment is provided for small independent hospitals for buffer stock resource costs, per § 412.113.

units.obligation_text: Subject to the provisions of paragraphs (e)(3)(ii) through (vii) of this section and paragraphs (e)(4)(iv) and (v) of this section as applicable, the average Medicare inpatient length of stay specified under paragraph (e)(2)(i) of this section is calculated by dividing the total number of covered and noncovered days of stay of Medicare inpatients (less leave or pass days) by the number of total Medicare discharges for the hospital's most recent complete cost reporting period.
units.actor: the entity calculating the average inpatient length of stay (hospital/CMS)
units.action_summary: The average Medicare inpatient length of stay must be calculated by dividing total inpatient days by total Medicare discharges for the recent cost reporting period, subject to listed provisions.

units.obligation_text: If a change in a hospital's average length of stay specified under paragraph (e)(2)(i) or (e)(2)(ii) of this section would result in the hospital not maintaining an average Medicare inpatient length of stay of greater than 25 days, the calculation is made by the same method for the period of at least 5 months of the immediately preceding 6-month period.
units.actor: the entity calculating the average inpatient length of stay (hospital/CMS)
units.action_summary: If a change would drop the average below 25 days, the average is calculated using at least 5 months of the prior 6-month period using the same method.

units.obligation_text: a satellite facility ... that voluntarily reorganizes as a separate Medicare participating hospital ... and that seeks to qualify as a new long-term care hospital for Medicare payment purposes must demonstrate through documentation that it meets the average length of stay requirement as specified under paragraphs (e)(2)(i) or (e)(2)(ii) of this section based on discharges that occur on or after the effective date of its participation under Medicare as a separate hospital.
units.actor: satellite facility or remote location seeking LTCH status
units.action_summary: A reorganized satellite or remote hospital seeking LTCH status must document that it meets the average length of stay requirement based on discharges after it begins participation as a separate hospital.

units.obligation_text: Satellite facilities and remote locations of hospitals ... may submit to the fiscal intermediary discharge data gathered during 5 months of the immediate 6 months preceding the facility's separation from the main hospital for calculation of the average length of stay specified under paragraph (e)(2)(i) or paragraph (e)(2)(ii) of this section.
units.actor: satellite facilities and remote locations seeking LTCH qualification
units.action_summary: Certain satellite facilities/remote locations may submit 5 months of discharge data from the 6 months before separation for average length of stay calculation.

units.obligation_text: A hospital may be classified as a long-term care hospital after a 6-month qualifying period, provided that the average length of stay during at least 5 consecutive months of that 6-month qualifying period, calculated under paragraph (e)(2) of this section, is greater than 25 days.
units.action_summary: A hospital can be classified as an LTCH after a 6-month qualifying period if its average length of stay during at least 5 consecutive months exceeds 25 days.

units.obligation_text: If a hospital seeks exclusion from the inpatient prospective payment system as a long-term care hospital and a change of ownership occurs within the period of at least 5 months of the 6-month period preceding its petition for long-term care hospital status, the hospital may be excluded from the inpatient prospective payment system as a long-term care hospital for the next cost reporting period if ... the hospital has met the required average length of stay, has continuously operated as a hospital, and has continuously participated as a hospital in Medicare.
units.action_summary: A hospital with a qualifying change in ownership may be excluded from IPPS as an LTCH for the next cost reporting period if it met average length, continuous operation, and continuous Medicare participation requirements.

units.obligation_text: For a medical product that is a gene therapy ... for discharges occurring on or after October 1, 2024, if the costs of the discharge ... exceed the full DRG payment, an additional amount equal to the lesser of— (1) 75 percent of the costs of the new medical service or technology; or (2) 75 percent of the amount by which the costs of the case exceed the standard DRG payment.
units.action_summary: CMS will pay an additional amount for certain gene therapies for sickle cell disease equal to the lesser of two 75%-based calculations when discharge costs exceed the DRG payment.
units.modal_raw: an additional amount equal to the lesser of

units.obligation_text: 75 percent of the costs of the new medical service or technology.
units.action_summary: One payment alternative is 75% of the costs of the new medical service or technology.

units.obligation_text: 75 percent of the amount by which the costs of the case exceed the standard DRG payment.
units.action_summary: Alternate payment calculation is 75% of the amount by which case costs exceed the DRG payment.

units.obligation_text: For discharges occurring on or after October 1, 2024, for a medical product that is a gene therapy ... 75 percent of the estimated costs of the new medical service or technology.
units.action_summary: Estimated payment amount for such discharges is 75% of estimated costs of the new medical service or technology.

units.obligation_text: CMS adjusts the prospective payment rates for inpatient operating costs determined under subparts D and E of this part if a hospital is classified as a Medicare-dependent, small rural hospital.
units.action_summary: CMS must adjust prospective payment rates for inpatient operating costs when a hospital is classified as Medicare-dependent, small rural.

units.obligation_text: An osteopathic hospital ... that is located in a rural area must have at least 3,000 discharges during its cost reporting period ... to meet the number of discharges criterion. A hospital applying for rural referral center status under the number of discharges criterion in this paragraph must demonstrate its status as an osteopathic hospital.
units.action_summary: A rural osteopathic hospital must have at least 3,000 discharges and must demonstrate its osteopathic status to qualify for rural referral center status under the discharge criterion.

units.obligation_text: For FY 2005 through FY 2010, the portion of FY 2025 beginning on January 1, 2025 and subsequent fiscal years, a hospital must have fewer than 200 total discharges ... during the fiscal year, based on the hospital's most recently submitted cost report, and be located more than 25 road miles ... from the nearest 'subsection (d)' hospital.
units.action_summary: To qualify for low-volume adjustment in specified years, a hospital must have fewer than 200 total discharges and be located more than 25 road miles from the nearest subsection (d) hospital.

units.obligation_text: For FY 2019 through FY 2024 and the portion of FY 2025 beginning on October 1, 2024, and ending on December 31, 2024, a hospital must have fewer than 3,800 total discharges ... during the fiscal year ... and be located more than 15 road miles ... from the nearest 'subsection (d)' hospital.
units.action_summary: To qualify for low-volume adjustment in specified years, a hospital must have fewer than 3,800 discharges and be more than 15 road miles from the nearest subsection (d) hospital.

units.obligation_text: For FY 2005 through FY 2010, the portion of FY 2025 beginning on January 1, 2025 and subsequent fiscal years, the adjustment is an additional 25 percent for each Medicare discharge.
units.action_summary: CMS payment adjustment equals an additional 25% per Medicare discharge for specified periods.

units.obligation_text: Effective for cost reporting periods beginning before October 1, 2024, the estimated weekly cost of dialysis is the average number of dialysis sessions furnished per week during the 12-month period that ended June 30, 1983, multiplied by the average cost of dialysis for the same period.
units.action_summary: For cost periods before Oct 1, 2024, estimated weekly dialysis cost is computed using historical 1983 sessions per week multiplied by the average cost for that period.

units.obligation_text: Effective for cost reporting periods beginning on or after October 1, 2024, the estimated weekly cost of dialysis is calculated as 3 dialysis sessions per week multiplied by the applicable ESRD prospective payment system (PPS) base rate ... that corresponds with the fiscal year in which the cost reporting period begins.
units.action_summary: For cost periods on/after Oct 1, 2024, estimated weekly dialysis cost is 3 sessions/week times the applicable ESRD PPS base rate.

units.obligation_text: The average cost of dialysis used for purposes of determining the estimated weekly cost of dialysis for cost reporting periods beginning before October 1, 2024, includes only those costs determined to be directly related to the renal dialysis services.
units.action_summary: Only costs directly related to renal dialysis services may be included in the average cost used for estimating weekly dialysis cost for periods before Oct 1, 2024.

units.obligation_text: Effective for cost reporting periods beginning before October 1, 2024, the average cost of dialysis is reviewed and adjusted, if appropriate, at the time the composite rate reimbursement for outpatient dialysis is reviewed.
units.action_summary: For periods before Oct 1, 2024, the average cost of dialysis must be reviewed and adjusted as appropriate when composite rate reimbursement is reviewed.

units.obligation_text: Effective for portions of cost reporting periods beginning on or after July 1, 2026, a hospital may qualify to receive an increase in its otherwise applicable FTE resident cap if the criteria specified in § 413.79(q) of this subchapter are met.
units.action_summary: Hospitals may qualify for an increase in their FTE resident cap for portions of cost reporting periods beginning on/after July 1, 2026, if they meet § 413.79(q) criteria.

units.obligation_text: Interim payments are made during the payment year to each hospital that is estimated to be eligible for payments under this section at the time of the annual final rule for the hospital inpatient prospective payment system, subject to the final determination of eligibility at the time of cost report settlement for each hospital. For FY 2025 and subsequent fiscal years, interim uncompensated care payments are calculated based on an average of the most recent 3 years of available historical discharge data.
units.action_summary: CMS makes interim payments to hospitals estimated eligible (subject to final settlement) and calculates FY2025+ interim uncompensated care payments based on an average of the most recent three years of discharge data.

units.obligation_text: For cost reporting periods beginning on or after October 1, 2024, a payment adjustment to a small, independent hospital for the additional resource costs of establishing and maintaining access to buffer stocks of essential medicines is made as described in paragraph (g)(4) of this section.
units.action_summary: CMS will provide a payment adjustment to small, independent hospitals for buffer stock resource costs for cost reporting periods starting on/after Oct 1, 2024, as described in (g)(4).

units.obligation_text: The payment adjustment is based on the estimated reasonable cost incurred by the hospital for establishing and maintaining access to buffer stocks of essential medicines during the cost reporting period.
units.action_summary: The payment adjustment will be based on the hospital's estimated reasonable costs for establishing and maintaining buffer stocks during the cost reporting period.

units.obligation_text: Prior to the FY 2028 payment determination, a hospital meets the eCQM validation requirement with respect to a fiscal year if it submits 100 percent of sampled eCQM measure medical records in a timely and complete manner, as determined by CMS.
units.action_summary: Before FY2028, hospitals meet the eCQM validation requirement by submitting 100% of sampled eCQM medical records timely and completely as determined by CMS.

units.obligation_text: For the FY 2028 payment determination and later years, a hospital meets the eCQM validation requirement with respect to a fiscal year if it achieves a 75-percent score, as determined by CMS.
units.action_summary: For FY2028 and later, hospitals meet eCQM validation by achieving a 75% score as determined by CMS.

units.obligation_text: If the hospital has requested reconsideration on the basis that CMS concluded it did not meet the validation requirement set forth in paragraph (d) of this section, the reconsideration request must contain a detailed explanation identifying which data the hospital believes was improperly validated by CMS and why the hospital believes that such data are correct.
units.action_summary: A hospital requesting reconsideration must provide a detailed explanation identifying data it believes were improperly validated and explain why the data are correct.

units.obligation_text: After the MGCRB issues a decision, provided that the request for withdrawal is received by the MCGRB within 45 days of the date of filing for public inspection of the proposed rule at the website of the Office of the Federal Register, or within 7 calendar days of receiving a decision of the Administrator’s in accordance with § 412.278, whichever is later ...
units.action_summary: A request for withdrawal must be received by the MGCRB within 45 days of public inspection filing or within 7 days of receiving the Administrator's decision, whichever is later.

units.obligation_text: A request for termination must be received by the MGCRB within 45 days of the date of filing for public inspection of the proposed rule at the website of the Office of the Federal Register, or within 7 calendar days of receiving a decision of the Administrator’s in accordance with § 412.278, whichever is later ...
units.action_summary: A request for termination must be received by the MGCRB within the stated 45-day or 7-day deadlines, whichever is later.

units.obligation_text: FTE residents who are displaced by the closure of either another hospital or another hospital's program are added to the FTE count after applying the averaging rules in this paragraph (d), for the receiving hospital for the duration of the time that the displaced residents are training at the receiving hospital.
units.actor: receiving hospital / FTE count administrator (as applied by CMS)
units.action_summary: Displaced FTE residents must be added to the receiving hospital's FTE count (after averaging) for the duration of their training at the receiving hospital.

units.obligation_text: FTE resident cap slots added under section 126 of Pub. L. 116–260 and section 4122 of Pub. L. 117-328 may be used in a Medicare GME affiliation agreement beginning in the fifth year after the effective date of those FTE resident cap slots.
units.actor: entities entering Medicare GME affiliation agreements
units.action_summary: FTE resident cap slots may be used in Medicare GME affiliation agreements starting in the fifth year after their effective date.

units.obligation_text: For rural track programs started before October 1, 2012, for the first 3 years of the rural track’s existence, the rural track FTE limitation for each urban hospital will be the actual number of FTE residents, subject to the rolling average specified in paragraph (d)(7) of this section, training in the rural track at the urban hospital and the rural nonprovider site(s).
units.action_summary: For specified rural track programs, the rural track FTE limitation for an urban hospital equals the actual number of FTE residents (subject to the rolling average) training in the rural track.

units.obligation_text: For rural track programs started on or after October 1, 2012, and before October 1, 2022, prior to the start of the urban hospital’s cost reporting period that coincides with or follows the start of the sixth program year of the rural track’s existence, the rural track FTE limitation for each urban hospital will be the actual number of FTE residents, subject to the rolling average specified in paragraph (d)(7) of this section, training in the rural track at the urban hospital and the rural nonprovider site(s).
units.action_summary: For specified rural track programs, the rural track FTE limitation equals the actual number of FTE residents (subject to rolling average) prior to the start of the relevant cost reporting period.

units.obligation_text: For cost reporting periods beginning on or after October 1, 2022, before the start of the urban or rural hospital’s cost reporting period that coincides with or follows the start of the sixth program year of the Rural Track Program’s existence, the rural track FTE limitation for each hospital will be the actual number of FTE residents training in the Rural Track Program at the urban or rural hospital and subject to the requirements under § 413.78(g), at the rural nonprovider site(s).
units.actor: each hospital participating in Rural Track Program
units.action_summary: For cost reporting periods beginning on/after Oct 1, 2022, the rural track FTE limitation equals the actual number of FTE residents training in the program and is subject to § 413.78(g) requirements.

units.obligation_text: For portions of cost reporting periods beginning on or after July 1, 2026, a hospital may receive an increase in its otherwise applicable FTE resident cap (as determined by CMS) if the hospital meets the requirements and qualifying criteria under section 1886(h)(10) of the Act and if the hospital submits an application to CMS within the timeframe specified by CMS.
units.action_summary: Hospitals may receive an increase in their FTE resident cap for portions of cost reporting periods beginning on/after July 1, 2026, if they meet statutory requirements and submit a timely application to CMS.

units.obligation_text: The hospital must electronically report information on acute respiratory illnesses, including influenza, SARS-CoV-2/COVID-19, and RSV.
units.action_summary: Hospitals are required to electronically report information on acute respiratory illnesses.

units.obligation_text: The report must be in a standardized format and frequency specified by the Secretary.
units.action_summary: Hospitals must use the Secretary-specified standardized format and frequency for reports.

units.obligation_text: To the extent as required by the Secretary, this report must include all of the following data elements: (A) Confirmed infections ... (B) Total bed census and capacity ... (C) Limited patient demographic information, including but not limited to age.
units.action_summary: Hospitals must include specified data elements in reports to the extent required by the Secretary: confirmed infections, bed census/capacity, and limited demographics.

units.obligation_text: In the event that the Secretary has declared a national, state, or local PHE for an acute infectious illness or determined that a significant threat for one exists, the hospital must also electronically the report the following data elements in a standardized format and frequency specified by the Secretary: (i) Supply inventory shortages. (ii) Staffing shortages. (iii) Relevant medical countermeasures and therapeutic inventories, usage, or both. (iv) Facility structure and operating status, including hospital/ED diversion status.
units.action_summary: During a declared or determined PHE, hospitals must electronically report additional data elements (supply and staffing shortages, medical countermeasures, facility status) in Secretary-specified format and frequency.

units.obligation_text: The CAH must electronically report information on acute respiratory illnesses, including influenza, SARS-CoV-2/COVID-19, and RSV.
units.action_summary: CAHs are required to electronically report information on acute respiratory illnesses.

units.obligation_text: The report must be in a standardized format and frequency specified by the Secretary.
units.action_summary: CAHs must use the Secretary-specified standardized format and frequency for reports.

units.obligation_text: To the extent as required by the Secretary, the report must include the following data elements: (A) Confirmed infections ... (B) Total bed census and capacity ... (C) Limited patient demographic information, including but not limited to age.
units.action_summary: CAHs must include specified data elements in reports to the extent required by the Secretary: confirmed infections, bed census/capacity, and limited demographics.

units.obligation_text: In the event that the Secretary has declared a national, state, or local PHE for an acute infectious illness or determined that a significant threat for one exists, the CAH must also electronically the report the following data elements in a standardized format and frequency specified by the Secretary: (i) Supply inventory shortages. (ii) Staffing shortages. (iii) Relevant medical countermeasures and therapeutic inventories, usage, or both. (iv) Facility structure and operating status, including CAH/ED diversion status.
units.action_summary: During a declared or determined PHE, CAHs must electronically report additional data elements (supply and staffing shortages, medical countermeasures, facility status) in Secretary-specified format and frequency.

units.obligation_text: In 2025 and subsequent years, earn a total score of at least 80 points.
units.action_summary: Eligible professionals, hospitals, and CAHs must earn at least 80 points in 2025 and subsequent years for the Stage 3 meaningful use objective.

title: Medicare and Medicaid Programs and the Children's Health Insurance Program: Hospital Inpatient Prospective Payment Systems for Acute Care Hospitals and the Long Term Care Hospital Prospective Payment System, etc.

units.obligation_text: All members must be knowledgeable in the field of payment of providers under Medicare Part A.
units.action_summary: Board members are required to have knowledge of Medicare Part A provider payment.

units.obligation_text: At least one member must be a certified public accountant.
units.action_summary: At least one Board member is required to be a certified public accountant.

units.obligation_text: At least two Board members must be representative of providers of services.
units.action_summary: At least two Board members are required to represent service providers.

units.obligation_text: The term of office for Board members must be 3 years, except that initial appointments may be for such shorter terms as the Secretary may designate to permit staggered terms of office.
units.action_summary: Board members' terms are required to be 3 years, with the Secretary authorized to set shorter initial terms to stagger them.

units.obligation_text: No member may serve more than three consecutive terms of office, except a Board member who, in their second or third consecutive term, is designated as Chairperson, as described in paragraph (c) of this section, may serve a maximum of four consecutive terms, provided that the Member continues to serve as Chairperson once so designated.
units.action_summary: Members generally are prohibited from serving more than three consecutive terms; an exception allows a member designated Chairperson in 2nd/3rd term to serve up to four consecutive terms if they remain Chairperson.

units.obligation_text: a Board member who, in their second or third consecutive term, is designated as Chairperson ... may serve a maximum of four consecutive terms, provided that the Member continues to serve as Chairperson once so designated.
units.action_summary: Chairperson-designated members are permitted to serve up to four consecutive terms if they continue as Chairperson.

units.obligation_text: The Secretary has the authority to terminate a Board member's term of office for good cause.
units.action_summary: The Secretary is authorized to terminate a Board member's term for good cause.

units.obligation_text: Additional payments are made for outlier cases, bad debts, indirect medical education costs, for serving a disproportionate share of low-income patients, for the additional resource costs of domestic National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health approved surgical N95 respirators, and for the additional resource costs for small, independent hospitals to establish and maintain access to buffer stocks of essential medicines.
units.action_summary: CMS provides additional payments for listed items including outliers, bad debts, IME, DSH, certain respirator costs, and buffer-stock medicine costs for small independent hospitals.

units.obligation_text: A payment adjustment for small, independent hospitals for the additional resource costs of establishing and maintaining access to buffer stocks of essential medicines as specified in Sec. 412.113.
units.action_summary: CMS provides a payment adjustment to small, independent hospitals for additional resource costs to establish and maintain buffer stocks of essential medicines, as specified in §412.113.

units.obligation_text: the average Medicare inpatient length of stay specified under paragraph (e)(2)(i) of this section is calculated by dividing the total number of covered and noncovered days of stay of Medicare inpatients (less leave or pass days) by the number of total Medicare discharges for the hospital's most recent complete cost reporting period. Subject to the provisions of paragraphs (e)(3)(ii) through (vii) of this section, the average inpatient length of stay specified under paragraph (e)(2)(ii) of this section is calculated by dividing the total number of days for all patients, including both Medicare and non-Medicare inpatients (less leave or pass days) by the number of total discharges for the hospital's most recent complete cost reporting period.
units.action_summary: The rule prescribes how to calculate average Medicare and overall inpatient length of stay by dividing days by discharges for the hospital's most recent complete cost reporting period.

units.obligation_text: If a change in a hospital's average length of stay ... the calculation is made by the same method for the period of at least 5 months of the immediately preceding 6-month period.
units.action_summary: When a hospital's average length of stay changes such that it would not maintain >25 days, the average is calculated using the same method applied to at least 5 months of the immediately preceding 6-month period.

units.obligation_text: a satellite facility ... that seeks to qualify as a new long-term care hospital for Medicare payment purposes must demonstrate through documentation that it meets the average length of stay requirement as specified under paragraphs (e)(2)(i) or (e)(2)(ii) of this section based on discharges that occur on or after the effective date of its participation under Medicare as a separate hospital.
units.actor: Satellite facility/remote location seeking LTCH status
units.action_summary: Satellite facilities or remote locations seeking new LTCH classification must document that they meet the average length of stay requirement based on discharges after they begin Medicare participation as a separate hospital.

units.obligation_text: Satellite facilities and remote locations ... may submit to the fiscal intermediary discharge data gathered during 5 months of the immediate 6 months preceding the facility's separation from the main hospital for calculation of the average length of stay specified under paragraph (e)(2)(i) or paragraph (e)(2)(ii) of this section.
units.action_summary: Such facilities are permitted to submit five months of discharge data from the immediate preceding six months for average length of stay calculations when separating from the main hospital.

units.obligation_text: A hospital may be classified as a long-term care hospital after a 6-month qualifying period, provided that the average length of stay during at least 5 consecutive months of that 6-month qualifying period, calculated under paragraph (e)(2) of this section, is greater than 25 days.
units.action_summary: A hospital can be classified as an LTCH after a 6-month qualifying period if its average length of stay exceeds 25 days for at least 5 consecutive months.

units.obligation_text: If a hospital seeks exclusion from the inpatient prospective payment system as a long-term care hospital and a change of ownership ... occurs within the period of at least 5 months of the 6-month period preceding its petition for long-term care hospital status, the hospital may be excluded ... for the next cost reporting period if, for the period of at least 5 months of the 6 months immediately preceding the start of the cost reporting period ... the hospital has met the required average length of stay, has continuously operated as a hospital, and has continuously participated as a hospital in Medicare.
units.action_summary: A hospital experiencing a change of ownership may be excluded as an LTCH for the next cost reporting period if it met the average length of stay requirement for at least 5 of the prior 6 months and continuously operated and participated in Medicare.

units.obligation_text: the hospital has met the required average length of stay; has continuously operated as a hospital; and has continuously participated as a hospital in Medicare.
units.action_summary: Conditions required for exclusion: met average length of stay, continuous operation as a hospital, and continuous Medicare participation.

units.obligation_text: an additional amount equal to the lesser of-- (1) 75 percent of the costs of the new medical service or technology; or (2) 75 percent of the amount by which the costs of the case exceed the standard DRG payment.
units.action_summary: For eligible gene therapy discharges, CMS provides an add-on payment equal to the lesser of two 75%-based amounts.

units.obligation_text: 75 percent of the costs of the new medical service or technology.
units.action_summary: One possible cap for the add-on payment is 75% of the new service's costs.

units.obligation_text: 75 percent of the amount by which the costs of the case exceed the standard DRG payment.
units.action_summary: The second cap is 75% of the excess of case costs over the DRG payment.

units.obligation_text: For discharges occurring on or after October 1, 2024, for a medical product that is a gene therapy ... 75 percent of the estimated costs of the new medical service or technology.
units.action_summary: For specified gene therapy discharges, CMS uses 75% of estimated costs for payment calculation.

units.obligation_text: CMS adjusts the prospective payment rates for inpatient operating costs ... if a hospital is classified as a Medicare-dependent, small rural hospital.
units.action_summary: CMS will adjust IPPS prospective payment rates for hospitals classified as Medicare-dependent, small rural hospitals.

units.obligation_text: an osteopathic hospital ... that is located in a rural area must have at least 3,000 discharges during its cost reporting period ... to meet the number of discharges criterion. A hospital applying for rural referral center status under the number of discharges criterion in this paragraph must demonstrate its status as an osteopathic hospital.
units.actor: Osteopathic hospital / hospital applying for rural referral center status
units.action_summary: To meet the referral center discharge criterion, eligible rural osteopathic hospitals must have at least 3,000 discharges in the cost reporting period and must demonstrate their osteopathic status when applying.

units.obligation_text: a hospital must have fewer than 200 total discharges ... during the fiscal year, based on the hospital's most recently submitted cost report, and be located more than 25 road miles ... from the nearest 'subsection (d)' hospital.
units.action_summary: To qualify for low-volume adjustment (for specified years), a hospital must have under 200 discharges and be more than 25 road miles from the nearest subsection (d) hospital.

units.obligation_text: a hospital must have fewer than 3,800 total discharges ... during the fiscal year, based on the hospital's most recently submitted cost report, and be located more than 15 road miles ... from the nearest 'subsection (d)' hospital.
units.action_summary: For FY2019-FY2024 and part of FY2025, a hospital must have fewer than 3,800 discharges and be more than 15 road miles from the nearest subsection (d) hospital to qualify.

units.obligation_text: For FY 2005 through FY 2010, the portion of FY 2025 beginning on January 1, 2025 and subsequent fiscal years, the adjustment is an additional 25 percent for each Medicare discharge.
units.action_summary: The low-volume hospital payment adjustment is an additional 25% per Medicare discharge for the specified years.

units.obligation_text: Effective for cost reporting periods beginning on or after October 1, 2024, the estimated weekly cost of dialysis is calculated as 3 dialysis sessions per week multiplied by the applicable ESRD prospective payment system (PPS) base rate ...
units.action_summary: For cost reporting periods starting on/after Oct 1, 2024, dialysis weekly cost is calculated as 3 sessions/week times the applicable ESRD PPS base rate.

units.obligation_text: The average cost of dialysis used for purposes of determining the estimated weekly cost of dialysis for cost reporting periods beginning before October 1, 2024, includes only those costs determined to be directly related to the renal dialysis services.
units.action_summary: When determining estimated weekly dialysis cost for earlier periods, only costs directly related to renal dialysis services are included.

units.obligation_text: Effective for cost reporting periods beginning before October 1, 2024, the average cost of dialysis is reviewed and adjusted, if appropriate, at the time the composite rate reimbursement for outpatient dialysis is reviewed.
units.action_summary: CMS reviews and adjusts, if appropriate, the average dialysis cost during composite rate reimbursement reviews for outpatient dialysis for applicable reporting periods.

units.obligation_text: Effective for portions of cost reporting periods beginning on or after July 1, 2026, a hospital may qualify to receive an increase in its otherwise applicable FTE resident cap if the criteria specified in Sec. 413.79(q) of this subchapter are met.
units.action_summary: Hospitals may qualify for an increase in their FTE resident cap for portions of cost reporting periods starting on/after July 1, 2026 if they meet §413.79(q) criteria.

units.obligation_text: For portions of cost reporting periods beginning on or after July 1, 2026, a hospital may receive an increase in its otherwise applicable FTE resident cap (as determined by CMS) if the hospital meets the requirements and qualifying criteria under section 1886(h)(10) of the Act and if the hospital submits an application to CMS within the timeframe specified by CMS.
units.action_summary: Hospitals may receive an FTE resident cap increase for applicable periods if they satisfy statutory qualifying criteria and submit a timely application to CMS.

units.obligation_text: Interim payments are made during the payment year to each hospital that is estimated to be eligible for payments under this section at the time of the annual final rule for the hospital inpatient prospective payment system, subject to the final determination of eligibility at the time of cost report settlement for each hospital. For FY 2025 and subsequent fiscal years, interim uncompensated care payments are calculated based on an average of the most recent 3 years of available historical discharge data.
units.action_summary: CMS issues interim uncompensated care payments to hospitals estimated eligible, subject to final eligibility at cost report settlement; for FY2025+, calculations use the average of the most recent 3 years' discharge data.

units.obligation_text: For discharges occurring during cost reporting periods ... 75 percent of the amount that the Federal rate determined under paragraph (c)(1) of this section is exceeded by the highest of the following:
units.action_summary: Payment calculations for certain Medicare-dependent small rural hospitals use 75% of the amount by which the Federal rate is exceeded by the highest listed comparator.

units.obligation_text: For cost reporting periods beginning on or after October 1, 2024, a payment adjustment to a small, independent hospital for the additional resource costs of establishing and maintaining access to buffer stocks of essential medicines is made as described in paragraph (g)(4) of this section.
units.action_summary: CMS provides a payment adjustment to small, independent hospitals for additional resource costs to establish/maintain buffer stocks of essential medicines for cost reporting periods starting Oct 1, 2024, as described in (g)(4).

units.obligation_text: The payment adjustment is based on the estimated reasonable cost incurred by the hospital for establishing and maintaining access to buffer stocks of essential medicines during the cost reporting period.
units.action_summary: The payment adjustment amount is determined based on the hospital's estimated reasonable costs for establishing/maintaining buffer stocks during the cost reporting period.

units.obligation_text: Prior to the FY 2028 payment determination, a hospital meets the eCQM validation requirement with respect to a fiscal year if it submits 100 percent of sampled eCQM measure medical records in a timely and complete manner, as determined by CMS.
units.action_summary: Before FY2028 payment determination, a hospital meets eCQM validation if it timely and completely submits 100% of sampled eCQM medical records as determined by CMS.

units.obligation_text: For the FY 2028 payment determination and later years, a hospital meets the eCQM validation requirement with respect to a fiscal year if it achieves a 75-percent score, as determined by CMS.
units.action_summary: For FY2028 and later, a hospital must achieve a CMS-determined 75% score to meet the eCQM validation requirement.

units.obligation_text: If the hospital has requested reconsideration on the basis that CMS concluded it did not meet the validation requirement set forth in paragraph (d) of this section, the reconsideration request must contain a detailed explanation identifying which data the hospital believes was improperly validated by CMS and why the hospital believes that such data are correct.
units.action_summary: A hospital requesting reconsideration must provide a detailed explanation identifying allegedly improperly validated data and reasons it believes the data are correct.

units.obligation_text: After the MGCRB issues a decision, provided that the request for withdrawal is received by the MCGRB within 45 days of the date of filing for public inspection of the proposed rule at the website of the Office of the Federal Register, or within 7 calendar days of receiving a decision of the Administrator's in accordance with Sec. 412.278, whichever is later ...
units.action_summary: A request for withdrawal must be received by the MGCRB within the specified 45-day or 7-day timeframe after notice or the Administrator's decision, whichever is later.

units.obligation_text: A request for termination must be received by the MGCRB within 45 days of the date of filing for public inspection of the proposed rule at the website of the Office of the Federal Register, or within 7 calendar days of receiving a decision of the Administrator's in accordance with Sec. 412.278, whichever is later ...
units.action_summary: To terminate an approved reclassification, the requester must submit the termination request to the MGCRB within the specified 45-day or 7-day timeframe.

units.obligation_text: The hospital must electronically report information on acute respiratory illnesses, including influenza, SARS-CoV-2/COVID-19, and RSV.
units.action_summary: Hospitals are required to electronically report information on acute respiratory illnesses (influenza, COVID-19, RSV).

units.obligation_text: The report must be in a standardized format and frequency specified by the Secretary.
units.action_summary: Hospitals must submit reports in a standardized format and frequency as specified by the Secretary.

units.obligation_text: To the extent as required by the Secretary, this report must include ... Confirmed infections for a limited set of respiratory illnesses, including but not limited to influenza, SARS-CoV-2/COVID-19, and RSV, among newly admitted and hospitalized patients.
units.action_summary: Hospitals must include confirmed infections for listed respiratory illnesses among newly admitted and hospitalized patients when required by the Secretary.

units.obligation_text: To the extent as required by the Secretary, this report must include ... Total bed census and capacity, including for critical hospital units and age groups.
units.action_summary: Hospitals must include total bed census and capacity details when required by the Secretary.

units.obligation_text: To the extent as required by the Secretary, this report must include ... Limited patient demographic information, including but not limited to age.
units.action_summary: Hospitals must include limited patient demographics (e.g., age) in reports when required by the Secretary.

units.obligation_text: In the event that the Secretary has declared a national, state, or local PHE ... the hospital must also electronically the report the following data elements in a standardized format and frequency specified by the Secretary:
units.action_summary: If the Secretary declares a relevant PHE or determines a significant threat exists, hospitals must also electronically report additional specified data elements in a standardized format/frequency.

units.obligation_text: Supply inventory shortages.
units.action_summary: Hospitals must report supply inventory shortages during a declared relevant PHE.

units.obligation_text: Staffing shortages.
units.action_summary: Hospitals must report staffing shortages during a declared relevant PHE.

units.obligation_text: Relevant medical countermeasures and therapeutic inventories, usage, or both.
units.action_summary: Hospitals must report inventories and usage of relevant medical countermeasures and therapeutics during a declared relevant PHE.

units.obligation_text: Facility structure and operating status, including hospital/ED diversion status.
units.action_summary: Hospitals must report facility structure and operating status, including diversion status, during a declared relevant PHE.

units.obligation_text: The CAH must electronically report information on acute respiratory illnesses, including influenza, SARS-CoV-2/COVID-19, and RSV.
units.action_summary: CAHs are required to electronically report information on acute respiratory illnesses including influenza, COVID-19, and RSV.

units.obligation_text: The report must be in a standardized format and frequency specified by the Secretary.
units.action_summary: CAHs must submit reports in the standardized format and frequency specified by the Secretary.

units.obligation_text: To the extent as required by the Secretary, the report must include ... Confirmed infections for a limited set of respiratory illnesses ... among newly admitted and hospitalized patients.
units.action_summary: CAHs must include confirmed infections for specified respiratory illnesses among newly admitted and hospitalized patients when required by the Secretary.

units.obligation_text: To the extent as required by the Secretary, the report must include ... Total bed census and capacity, including for critical hospital units and age groups.
units.action_summary: CAHs must include total bed census and capacity details when required by the Secretary.

units.obligation_text: To the extent as required by the Secretary, the report must include ... Limited patient demographic information, including but not limited to age.
units.action_summary: CAHs must include limited patient demographic information when required by the Secretary.

units.obligation_text: In the event that the Secretary has declared a national, state, or local PHE ... the CAH must also electronically the report the following data elements in a standardized format and frequency specified by the Secretary:
units.action_summary: If a relevant PHE is declared, CAHs must also electronically report additional specified data elements in a standardized format/frequency.

units.obligation_text: Supply inventory shortages.
units.action_summary: CAHs must report supply inventory shortages during a declared relevant PHE.

units.obligation_text: Staffing shortages.
units.action_summary: CAHs must report staffing shortages during a declared relevant PHE.

units.obligation_text: Relevant medical countermeasures and therapeutic inventories, usage, or both.
units.action_summary: CAHs must report inventories and usage of relevant medical countermeasures and therapeutics during a declared relevant PHE.

units.obligation_text: Facility structure and operating status, including CAH/ED diversion status.
units.action_summary: CAHs must report facility structure and operating status, including diversion status, during a declared relevant PHE.

units.obligation_text: In 2025 and subsequent years, earn a total score of at least 80 points.
units.actor: Eligible professionals (EPs), eligible hospitals, and CAHs
units.action_summary: In 2025 and later, EPs, eligible hospitals, and CAHs must earn at least 80 points (total score) under the Stage 3 meaningful use objectives/measures.

title: Medicare and Medicaid Programs and the Children's Health Insurance Program: Hospital Inpatient Prospective Payment Systems for Acute Care Hospitals and theLong Term Care Hospital Prospective Payment System, etc.; Correction
CY 2026 Hospital Outpatient PPS Policy Changes and Payment Rates and Ambulatory Surgical Center Payment System Policy Changes and Payment Rates. CMS-1834-P Display.

units.obligation_text: For purposes of this section, direct supervision means that the physician or nonphysician practitioner must be immediately available to furnish assistance and direction throughout the performance of the procedure.
units.action_summary: Be immediately available to furnish assistance and direction throughout the performance of the procedure (direct supervision).

units.obligation_text: It does not mean that the physician or nonphysician practitioner must be present in the room when the procedure is performed.
units.action_summary: The physician or nonphysician practitioner is not required to be physically present in the room during the procedure.

units.obligation_text: For pulmonary rehabilitation, cardiac rehabilitation, and intensive cardiac rehabilitation services, direct supervision must be furnished as specified in §§ 410.47 and 410.49, respectively.
units.actor: the physician or nonphysician practitioner / CMS (as specifying)
units.action_summary: Direct supervision for pulmonary, cardiac, and intensive cardiac rehabilitation must be furnished according to the specifications in §§ 410.47 and 410.49.

units.obligation_text: The presence of the physician or nonphysician practitioner for the purpose of the supervision of pulmonary rehabilitation, cardiac rehabilitation, and intensive cardiac rehabilitation services includes virtual presence through audio/video real-time communications technology (excluding audio-only).
