units.action_summary: Supervision may be satisfied by virtual presence using real-time audio/video communications (not audio-only) for specified rehabilitation services.

units.obligation_text: The presence of the physician or nonphysician practitioner under paragraphs (e)(2)(i) and (ii) of this section includes virtual presence through audio/video real-time communications technology (excluding audio-only) for services without a 010 or 090 global surgery indicator.
units.action_summary: For certain outpatient diagnostic services (without a 010 or 090 global surgery indicator), the physician's presence may be virtual via real-time audio/video communications (excluding audio-only).

units.obligation_text: An inpatient admission for a surgical procedure specified by Medicare as inpatient only under § 419.22(n) of this chapter is generally appropriate for payment under Medicare Part A regardless of the expected duration of care.
units.actor: an inpatient admission for a surgical procedure specified by Medicare as inpatient only
units.action_summary: Such inpatient admissions qualify for Medicare Part A payment regardless of expected duration.

units.obligation_text: Procedures no longer specified as inpatient only under § 419.22(n) of this chapter are appropriate for payment under Medicare Part A in accordance with paragraph (d)(1) or (3) of this section.
units.actor: procedures no longer specified as inpatient only
units.action_summary: Procedures removed from the inpatient-only list may be paid under Medicare Part A according to the rules in paragraph (d)(1) or (3).

units.obligation_text: Claims for services and procedures removed from the inpatient only list under § 419.22 of this chapter on or after January 1, 2021 are exempt from certain medical review activities until the Secretary determines that the service or procedure is more commonly performed in the outpatient setting than the inpatient setting.
units.actor: claims for services and procedures removed from the inpatient only list
units.action_summary: Such claims are exempt from certain medical review activities until the Secretary determines outpatient predominance.

units.obligation_text: Is approved by one of the national organizations listed in § 415.152 of this chapter, provided that the national organization does not use accreditation criteria that promote or emphasize diversity, equity, inclusion, or awareness based on race, color, sex, sexual orientation or identity, national origin, or any other characteristic which serves as a proxy to achieve the same ends.
units.actor: the national organization (as condition for program approval)
units.action_summary: The national organization must not use accreditation criteria that promote or emphasize DEI characteristics as a condition for program approval.

units.obligation_text: May count towards certification of the participant in a specialty or subspecialty listed in the current edition of either of the following publications: (1) The Directory of Graduate Medical Education Programs published by the American Medical Association. (2) The Annual Report and Reference Handbook published by the American Board of Medical Specialties.
units.action_summary: The program may count toward participant certification if listed in the specified publications.

units.obligation_text: Provided that listing in either of those publications, or in successor information sources, does not require the program to promote or emphasize diversity, equity, inclusion, or awareness based on race, color, sex, sexual orientation or identity, national origin, or any other characteristic which serves as a proxy to achieve the same ends.
units.actor: the listing in the publications (as condition)
units.action_summary: Listing in the publications must not require the program to promote or emphasize DEI characteristics.

units.obligation_text: Is approved by the Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education (ACGME), or other organization designated by the Secretary, as a fellowship program in geriatric medicine, provided that the Council or other organization does not use accreditation criteria that promote or emphasize diversity, equity, inclusion, or awareness based on race, color, sex, sexual orientation or identity, national origin, or any other characteristic which serves as a proxy to achieve the same ends.
units.actor: the ACGME or other organization designated by the Secretary
units.action_summary: The accrediting organization must not use accreditation criteria that promote or emphasize DEI characteristics to approve geriatric fellowship programs.

units.obligation_text: Is a program that would be accredited except for the accrediting agency's reliance upon an accreditation standard that requires an entity to promote or emphasize diversity, equity, inclusion, or awareness based on race, color, sex, sexual orientation or identity, national origin, or any other characteristic which serves as a proxy to achieve the same ends.
units.action_summary: A program qualifies if it would be accredited except that the accrediting agency relies on a standard requiring promotion/emphasis of DEI characteristics.

units.obligation_text: Apply a 4-star cap for hospitals in the lowest quartile of the Safety of Care measure group performance in Calendar Year 2026. Any hospital that is assigned 5 stars in step eight but has a lowest quartile Safety of Care score (based on at least three Safety of Care measures) would be reassigned to 4 stars.
units.action_summary: CMS will cap ratings at 4 stars for hospitals in the lowest Safety of Care quartile in CY 2026, reassigning any 5-star hospitals with lowest-quartile Safety scores to 4 stars.

units.obligation_text: Apply a blanket 1-Star reduction for hospitals in the lowest quartile of Safety of Care measure group performance beginning in Calendar Year 2027 and later years. Any hospital assigned a 2, 3, 4, or 5-star rating in step eight, but with a lowest quartile Safety of Care score (based on at least three Safety of Care measures) would be reduced to 1, 2, 3, or 4 stars, respectively.
units.action_summary: Beginning CY 2027 CMS will reduce hospitals in the lowest Safety of Care quartile by one star (shifting ratings down one level as specified).

units.obligation_text: CMS provides hospitals the opportunity to preview their Overall Hospital Quality Star Rating prior to publication.
units.action_summary: CMS must give hospitals an opportunity to preview their Star Ratings before publication.

units.obligation_text: Hospitals have at least 30 days to preview their results
units.actor: hospitals / CMS (as provider of preview period)
units.action_summary: Hospitals are afforded a minimum 30-day preview period to review their Star Ratings.

units.obligation_text: If necessary, [hospitals] can reach out to CMS with questions.
units.action_summary: Hospitals are permitted to contact CMS with questions during the preview period.

units.obligation_text: CMS may consider suppressing Overall Hospital Quality Star Rating for subsection (d) hospitals only under extenuating circumstances that affect numerous hospitals (as in, not an individualized or localized issue) as determined by CMS, or when CMS is at fault, including but not limited to when: (i) There is an Overall Hospital Quality Star Rating calculation error by CMS; (ii) There is a systemic error at the CMS quality program level that substantively affects the Overall Hospital Quality Star Rating calculation; or (iii) If a Public Health Emergency substantially affects the underlying measure data.
units.action_summary: CMS is permitted to suppress Star Ratings for subsection (d) hospitals only under broad extenuating circumstances or when CMS is at fault, with specified examples.

units.obligation_text: There is an Overall Hospital Quality Star Rating calculation error by CMS.
units.action_summary: A calculation error by CMS is a qualifying condition under which CMS may consider suppressing ratings.

units.obligation_text: There is a systemic error at the CMS quality program level that substantively affects the Overall Hospital Quality Star Rating calculation.
units.action_summary: A systemic error at the CMS quality program level that substantively affects the calculation is a qualifying condition for suppression.

units.obligation_text: If a Public Health Emergency substantially affects the underlying measure data.
units.action_summary: A Public Health Emergency that substantially affects underlying data is a qualifying condition for suppression of ratings.

units.obligation_text: CAHs may request to withhold their Overall Hospital Quality Star Rating from publication on Care Compare on Medicare.gov so long as the request for withholding is made, at the latest, during the Overall Hospital Quality Star Rating preview period.
units.action_summary: CAHs are permitted to request withholding of their Star Rating from publication if they make the request during the preview period.

units.obligation_text: CAHs may request to have their Overall Hospital Quality Star Rating withheld from publication on Care Compare on Medicare.gov, as well as their data from the public input file, so long as the request is made during the CMS quality program-level 30-day confidential preview period for the Care Compare refresh data used to calculate the Overall Hospital Quality Ratings.
units.action_summary: CAHs may request withholding of both their Star Rating and their public input file data if requested during the CMS program-level 30-day confidential preview period.

units.obligation_text: The provider must furnish the contractor— Upon request, copies of patient service charge schedules and changes thereto as they are put into effect;
units.action_summary: Upon contractor request, the provider must furnish copies of patient service charge schedules and any changes as they take effect.

units.obligation_text: The provider must furnish the contractor— Its median payer-specific negotiated charge by MS-DRG for payers that are Medicare Advantage (MA) organizations, as applicable, and changes thereto as they are put into effect.
units.action_summary: The provider must furnish the contractor its median payer-specific negotiated charge by MS-DRG for applicable MA payers and any changes as they take effect.

units.obligation_text: The contractor evaluates the charge schedules as specified in paragraph (d)(3)(i) of this section to determine the extent to which they may be used for determining program payment.
units.action_summary: The contractor must evaluate submitted charge schedules to determine their usability for program payment determinations.

units.obligation_text: Approved geriatric program means a fellowship program ... that is approved by one of the national organizations listed in § 415.152 of this chapter under that respective organization's criteria for geriatric fellowship programs, provided that the national organization does not use accreditation criteria that promote or emphasize diversity, equity, inclusion, or awareness ...
units.action_summary: To qualify as an approved geriatric program, the approving national organization must not use accreditation criteria that promote or emphasize DEI characteristics.

units.obligation_text: Is approved by one of the national organizations listed in § 415.152 of this chapter, provided that the national organization does not use accreditation criteria that promote or emphasize diversity, equity, inclusion, or awareness based on race, color, sex, sexual orientation or identity, national origin, or any other characteristic which serves as a proxy to achieve the same ends.
units.action_summary: An approving national organization must not use accreditation criteria that promote or emphasize DEI characteristics for approval of medical residency programs.

units.obligation_text: May count towards certification of the participant in a specialty or subspecialty listed in the current edition of either of the following publications: (i) The Directory of Graduate Medical Education Programs ...; or (ii) The Annual Report and Reference Handbook ...
units.action_summary: The program may be recognized as counting toward participant certification if listed in the specified publications.

units.obligation_text: Provided that listing in either of those publications, or in successor information sources, does not require the program to promote or emphasize diversity, equity, inclusion, or awareness based on race, color, sex, sexual orientation or identity, national origin, or any other characteristic which serves as a proxy to achieve the same ends.
units.action_summary: Listing in the publications must not require the program to promote or emphasize DEI characteristics.

units.obligation_text: Is approved by the Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education (ACGME), or other organization designated by the Secretary, as a fellowship program in geriatric medicine ... provided that the Council or other organization does not use accreditation criteria that promote or emphasize diversity, equity, inclusion, or awareness based on race, color, sex, sexual orientation or identity, national origin, or any other characteristic which serves as a proxy to achieve the same ends.
units.actor: ACGME or other organization designated by the Secretary
units.action_summary: The accrediting council or organization must not use accreditation criteria that promote or emphasize DEI characteristics to approve the fellowship program.

units.obligation_text: Is a program that would be accredited except for the accrediting agency's reliance upon an accreditation standard that requires an entity to promote or emphasize diversity, equity, inclusion, or awareness ...
units.action_summary: Programs that would otherwise be accredited except for the accrediting agency's reliance on DEI-promoting standards qualify under this provision.

units.obligation_text: A residency program approved by the Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education, by the American Osteopathic Association, by the Commission on Dental Accreditation of the American Dental Association, or by the Council on Podiatric Medical Education of the American Podiatric Medical Association, or other organization determined by the Secretary, provided that the applicable organization does not use accreditation criteria that promote or emphasize diversity, equity, inclusion, or awareness based on race, color, sex, sexual orientation or identity, national origin, or any other characteristic which serves as a proxy to achieve the same ends.
units.action_summary: An accrediting organization must not use accreditation criteria that promote or emphasize DEI characteristics for a residency program to be considered approved.

units.obligation_text: Physicians consider the following safety factors as to a specific beneficiary when determining whether to perform a covered surgical procedure.
units.action_summary: Physicians must consider enumerated safety factors for each beneficiary when deciding whether to perform a covered surgical procedure.

units.obligation_text: The covered procedure is not expected to pose a significant safety risk when performed in an ASC.
units.actor: the covered procedure (as factor considered by physicians)
units.action_summary: One safety factor physicians must consider is that the procedure is not expected to pose a significant safety risk in an ASC.

units.obligation_text: The covered procedure is one of which standard medical practice dictates the beneficiary would not typically be expected to required active medical monitoring and care at midnight following the procedure.
units.action_summary: Physicians must consider whether the procedure typically does not require active medical monitoring at midnight post-procedure.

units.obligation_text: The covered procedure generally results in extensive blood loss.
units.action_summary: Physicians must consider whether the procedure generally results in extensive blood loss.

units.obligation_text: The covered procedure requires major or prolonged invasion of body cavities.
units.action_summary: Physicians must consider whether the procedure requires major or prolonged invasion of body cavities.

units.obligation_text: The covered procedure directly involves major blood vessels.
units.action_summary: Physicians must consider whether the procedure directly involves major blood vessels.

units.obligation_text: The covered procedure is generally emergent or life-threatening in nature.
units.action_summary: Physicians must consider whether the procedure is generally emergent or life-threatening.

units.obligation_text: The covered procedure commonly requires systemic thrombolytic therapy.
units.action_summary: Physicians must consider whether the procedure commonly requires systemic thrombolytic therapy.

units.obligation_text: On or after January 1, 2026, CMS adds surgical procedures to the list of ASC covered procedures as follows:
units.action_summary: CMS will add surgical procedures to the ASC covered procedures list on or after Jan 1, 2026 following the specified process.

units.obligation_text: CMS identifies a surgical procedure that meets the requirements at paragraph (b)(2) of this section.
units.action_summary: CMS may identify a surgical procedure that satisfies the requirements in paragraph (b)(2) for addition to the ASC list.

units.obligation_text: CMS is notified of a surgical procedure that could meet the requirements at paragraph (b)(2) of this section and CMS confirms that such surgical procedure meets those requirements.
units.action_summary: Upon notification, CMS must confirm that the surgical procedure meets required criteria before adding it to the ASC list.

units.obligation_text: For CY 2014 through CY 2018, the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers update determined under paragraph (a)(2)(ii) of this section is reduced by 2.0 percentage points for an ASC that fails to meet the standards for reporting of ASC quality measures as established by the Secretary for the corresponding calendar year.
units.action_summary: For CY2014-2018 an ASC failing to meet reporting standards will have its CPI-U update reduced by 2.0 percentage points.

units.obligation_text: For CY 2019 through CY 2026, the hospital inpatient market basket percentage increase determined under paragraph (a)(2)(iii) of this section is reduced by 2.0 percentage points for an ASC that fails to meet the standards for reporting of ASC quality measures as established by the Secretary for the corresponding calendar year.
units.action_summary: For CY2019-2026 an ASC failing to meet required ASC quality reporting standards will have its market-basket update reduced by 2.0 percentage points.

units.obligation_text: For CY 2027 and subsequent years, the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers update determined under paragraph (a)(2)(iv) of this section is reduced by 2.0 percentage points for an ASC that fails to meet the standards for reporting of ASC quality measures as established by the Secretary for the corresponding calendar year.
units.action_summary: Beginning CY2027, an ASC that fails to meet ASC quality reporting standards will have its CPI-U update reduced by 2.0 percentage points.

units.obligation_text: For a qualifying medical device as defined in paragraph (b) of this section, the amount of payment is the amount of the hospital's charges for the device, adjusted to cost, that exceeds the portion of the otherwise applicable Medicare OPD fee schedule amount, subject to paragraph (c)(3) of this section.
units.action_summary: Payment for a qualifying medical device equals the hospital's cost-adjusted charges exceeding the applicable Medicare OPD fee schedule amount, subject to further rules.

units.obligation_text: CMS may grant an ECE with respect to the reporting requirements under this section in the event of extraordinary circumstances beyond the control of the ASC.
units.action_summary: CMS is permitted to grant an extraordinary circumstance exception (ECE) to ASC reporting requirements when extraordinary circumstances beyond the ASC's control occur.

units.obligation_text: An ASC may request an ECE within 30 calendar days of the date that the extraordinary circumstance occurred by submitting the information specified by CMS at QualityNet or a successor website.
units.action_summary: An ASC may request an extraordinary circumstance exception within 30 days of the event by submitting required information at QualityNet or successor.

units.obligation_text: CMS notifies the ASC of its decision on the request, in writing, via email. In the event that CMS grants an ECE to the ASC, the written decision specifies whether the ASC is exempted from one or more reporting requirements or whether CMS has granted the ASC an extension of time to comply with one or more reporting requirements.
units.action_summary: CMS must notify the ASC in writing of its ECE determination and, if granted, specify whether the ASC is exempted from reporting requirements or granted an extension.

units.obligation_text: CMS may grant an ECE to one or more ASCs that have not requested an ECE if CMS determines that— (i) A systemic problem with a CMS data collection system directly impacted the ability of the ASC to comply with a quality data reporting requirement; or (ii) An extraordinary circumstance has affected an entire region or locale. Any ECE granted under this paragraph (d)(3) specifies whether the affected ASCs are exempted from one or more reporting requirements or whether CMS has granted the ASCs an extension of time to comply with one or more reporting requirements.
units.action_summary: CMS may proactively grant ECEs to ASCs that did not request them if a systemic data collection problem or regional extraordinary circumstance affected compliance; CMS must specify the scope of exemption or extensions in such decisions.

units.obligation_text: A systemic problem with a CMS data collection system directly impacted the ability of the ASC to comply with a quality data reporting requirement;
units.actor: a systemic CMS data collection problem (as condition)
units.action_summary: A systemic CMS data collection problem is a qualifying condition under which CMS may grant an ECE to ASCs that did not request one.

units.obligation_text: An extraordinary circumstance has affected an entire region or locale.
units.action_summary: A region- or locale-wide extraordinary circumstance is a qualifying condition for CMS to grant ECEs to ASCs that did not request one.

units.obligation_text: Effective beginning on January 1, 2026, the Secretary shall eliminate the list of services and procedures designated as requiring inpatient care through a 3-year transition, with the list eliminated in its entirety by January 1, 2029.
units.action_summary: Beginning Jan 1, 2026 the Secretary is obligated to eliminate the inpatient-only list over a 3-year transition, completing elimination by Jan 1, 2029.

units.obligation_text: Beginning in calendar year 2026, a multifactor productivity adjustment (as determined by CMS), and 2.0-percentage point reduction, [applies],
units.action_summary: Beginning CY2026, CMS will apply a multifactor productivity adjustment and a 2.0-percentage-point reduction in calculating payment rates.

units.obligation_text: Except that the 2.0-percentage point reduction shall not apply to hospital outpatient items and services furnished by a hospital with a CMS certification number (CCN) effective date of January 2, 2018, or later.
units.actor: hospitals with a CCN effective date of January 2, 2018 or later (as exception)
units.action_summary: The 2.0-percentage-point reduction does not apply to outpatient items/services furnished by hospitals whose CCN effective date is Jan 2, 2018 or later.

units.obligation_text: CMS may grant an ECE with respect to the reporting requirements under this section in the event of extraordinary circumstances beyond the control of the hospital.
units.action_summary: CMS is permitted to grant an extraordinary circumstance exception to hospital reporting requirements when extraordinary circumstances beyond a hospital's control occur.

units.obligation_text: A hospital may request an ECE within 30 calendar days of the date that the extraordinary circumstance occurred by submitting the information specified by CMS at QualityNet or a successor website.
units.action_summary: Hospitals may request an extraordinary circumstance exception within 30 days of the event by submitting required information at QualityNet or successor.

units.obligation_text: CMS notifies the hospital of its decision on the request, in writing, via email. In the event that CMS grants an ECE to the hospital, the written decision specifies whether the hospital is exempted from one or more reporting requirements or whether CMS has granted the hospital an extension of time to comply with one or more reporting requirements.
units.action_summary: CMS must notify hospitals in writing of its ECE decision and, if granted, specify whether the hospital is exempted from reporting requirements or granted an extension.

units.obligation_text: A systemic problem with a CMS data collection system directly impacted the ability of the hospital to comply with a quality data reporting requirement;
units.actor: a systemic CMS data collection problem (as condition)
units.action_summary: A systemic CMS data collection problem that directly impacted compliance is a qualifying condition for CMS to grant an ECE to hospitals that did not request one.

units.obligation_text: An extraordinary circumstance has affected an entire region or locale.
units.action_summary: A region- or locale-wide extraordinary circumstance is a qualifying condition for CMS to grant ECEs to hospitals that did not request one.

units.obligation_text: CMS provides for an additional payment (as specified in this section § 419.49) beyond the standard payment to a hospital for a dose of Tc-99m derived from Mo-99, if at least 50 percent of the Mo-99 in the Tc-99m generator that produced the dose was both irradiated and processed in the United States.
units.action_summary: CMS will make an additional payment to hospitals for Tc-99m doses when at least 50% of the Mo-99 in the generator was irradiated and processed in the United States.

units.obligation_text: A dose of Tc-99m does not qualify for the add-on payment if more than 50 percent of the Mo-99 in the Tc-99m generator was irradiated or processed outside the United States, even if the Mo-99 has been loaded into a Tc-99m generator in the United States or if the Tc-99m has been eluted at a radiopharmacy in the United States.
units.actor: a dose of Tc-99m / the hospital seeking add-on payment
units.action_summary: Tc-99m doses where over 50% of Mo-99 was irradiated or processed outside the U.S. are excluded from the add-on payment.

units.obligation_text: CMS may grant an ECE with respect to the reporting requirements under this section in the event of extraordinary circumstances beyond the control of the REH.
units.action_summary: CMS is permitted to grant an extraordinary circumstance exception to REH reporting requirements when extraordinary circumstances beyond the REH's control occur.

units.obligation_text: An REH may request an ECE within 30 calendar days of the date that the extraordinary circumstance occurred by submitting the information specified by CMS at QualityNet or a successor website.
units.action_summary: REHs may request an ECE within 30 days of the extraordinary event by submitting required information at QualityNet or successor.

units.obligation_text: CMS notifies the REH of its decision on the request, in writing, via email. In the event that CMS grants an ECE to the REH, the written decision specifies whether the REH is exempted from one or more reporting requirements or whether CMS has granted the REH an extension of time to comply with one or more reporting requirements.
units.action_summary: CMS must notify REHs in writing of its ECE decision and, if granted, specify exemptions or extensions.

units.obligation_text: A systemic problem with a CMS data collection system directly impacted the ability of the REH to comply with a quality data reporting requirement;
units.actor: a systemic CMS data collection problem (as condition)
units.action_summary: A systemic CMS data collection problem is a qualifying condition for CMS to grant an ECE to REHs that did not request one.

units.obligation_text: An extraordinary circumstance has affected an entire region or locale.
units.action_summary: A region- or locale-wide extraordinary circumstance is a qualifying condition for CMS to grant ECEs to REHs that did not request one.

units.obligation_text: When reporting eCQMs under the REHQR Program, REHs must adhere to the following requirements:
units.action_summary: REHs that report electronic clinical quality measures under the REHQR Program are required to follow specified technical and reporting requirements.

units.obligation_text: REHs must utilize technology certified to the Office of the National Coordinator for Health Information Technology's (ONC’s) health information technology (IT) certification criteria, as adopted and updated in 45 CFR 170.315, for reporting eCQMs under the REHQR Program.
units.action_summary: REHs must use ONC-certified health IT technology (per 45 CFR 170.315) for eCQM reporting under the REHQR Program.

units.obligation_text: REHs must use health IT certified to all eCQMs that are available to report under the REHQR Program.
units.action_summary: REHs must use health IT that is certified to support all eCQMs available for reporting under the program.

units.obligation_text: REHs must use the most recent version of the eCQM electronic measure specifications for the applicable reporting period available on the Electronic Clinical Quality Improvement Resource Center website ... or another website as designated by CMS.
units.action_summary: REHs must use the most recent eCQM specifications for the applicable reporting period as published on the designated resource site.

units.obligation_text: The requirements set forth in paragraphs (h)(1) through (3) of this section apply only where an REH opts to report an eCQM.
units.action_summary: The eCQM technical and specification requirements apply to REHs only if the REH chooses to report an eCQM.

units.obligation_text: Prior to January 1, 2026, make a good faith effort to ensure that the standard charge information encoded in the machine-readable file is true, accurate, and complete as of the date indicated in the machine-readable file.
units.action_summary: Before Jan 1, 2026, hospitals must make a good faith effort to ensure their machine-readable file's standard charge information is true, accurate, and complete as of the file date.

units.obligation_text: Prior to January 1, 2026, affirm in its machine-readable file that, to the best of its knowledge and belief, the hospital has included all applicable standard charge information in accordance with the requirements of this section, and that the information encoded is true, accurate, and complete as of the date indicated in the machine-readable file.
units.action_summary: Before Jan 1, 2026 hospitals must affirm in their machine-readable file that they have included all applicable standard charge information and that it is true, accurate, and complete.

units.obligation_text: Beginning January 1, 2026, attest in its machine-readable file the following: This hospital has included all applicable standard charge information in accordance with the requirements of 45 CFR 180.50, and the information encoded is true, accurate, and complete as of the date in the file. This hospital has included all payer-specific negotiated charges in dollars that can be expressed as a dollar amount. For payer-specific negotiated charges that cannot be expressed as a dollar amount in the machine-readable file or not knowable in advance, the hospital attests that the payer-specific negotiated charge is based on a contractual algorithm, percentage or formula that precludes the provision of a dollar amount and has provided all necessary information available to the hospital for the public to be able to derive the dollar amount, including, but not limited to, the specific fee schedule or components referenced in such percentage, algorithm or formula.
units.action_summary: Beginning Jan 1, 2026 hospitals must attest in their machine-readable file to inclusion and accuracy of standard charge information, include payer-specific negotiated charges where expressible in dollars, and for charges not expressible as dollars attest to the algorithm/percentage/formula basis and provide derivation information.

units.obligation_text: Beginning January 1, 2026, encode the name of the hospital chief executive officer, president or senior official designated to oversee the encoding of true, accurate, and complete data as directed in paragraph (a)(3)(iii) of this section.
units.action_summary: Beginning Jan 1, 2026 hospitals must encode the name of the CEO/president or senior official designated to oversee the accuracy of the machine-readable file data.

units.obligation_text: Hospital name, license number, location name(s) and address(es) under the single hospital license to which the list of standard charges applies, and beginning January 1, 2026, Type 2 (organizational) National Provider Identifier(s) (NPI). Location name(s) and address(es) must include, at minimum, all inpatient facilities and stand-alone emergency departments;
units.action_summary: Hospitals must include in the machine-readable file the hospital name, license number, location names/addresses (including all inpatient facilities and standalone EDs), and beginning Jan 1, 2026 Type 2 NPIs.

units.obligation_text: Whether the standard charge indicated should be interpreted by the user as a dollar amount, or if the standard charge is based on a percentage or algorithm. If the standard charge is based on a percentage or algorithm, the machine-readable file (MRF) must also describe the percentage or algorithm that determines the dollar amount for the item or service, and (1) Beginning January 1, 2025 through December 31, 2025, calculate and encode an estimated allowed amount in dollars for that item or service; and (2) Beginning January 1, 2026, calculate and encode the tenth (10th) percentile allowed amount, the median allowed amount, and the ninetieth (90th) percentile allowed amount in dollars for that item or service. Hospitals must also calculate and encode the total number of allowed amount remittances that were used to calculate the 10th percentile allowed amount, median allowed amount, and 90th percentile allowed amount.
units.action_summary: Hospitals must indicate whether a standard charge is a dollar amount or based on a percentage/algorithm; if the latter, the MRF must describe the algorithm and hospitals must calculate and encode estimated allowed amounts (2025) and the 10th, median, and 90th percentile allowed amounts and the count of remittances (beginning 2026).

units.obligation_text: Beginning January 1, 2025 through December 31, 2025, calculate and encode an estimated allowed amount in dollars for that item or service;
units.action_summary: For 2025 hospitals must calculate and encode an estimated allowed amount in dollars for items/services where the standard charge is based on a percentage or algorithm.

units.obligation_text: Beginning January 1, 2026, calculate and encode the tenth (10th) percentile allowed amount, the median allowed amount, and the ninetieth (90th) percentile allowed amount in dollars for that item or service. Hospitals must also calculate and encode the total number of allowed amount remittances that were used to calculate the 10th percentile allowed amount, median allowed amount, and 90th percentile allowed amount.
units.action_summary: Beginning Jan 1, 2026 hospitals must calculate and encode the 10th percentile, median, and 90th percentile allowed amounts in dollars for items/services and report the number of remittances used to compute them.

units.obligation_text: Except as provided in this paragraph, the amount of a civil monetary penalty is reduced by 35 percent if the hospital submits a written notice to CMS requesting to waive its right to a hearing under § 180.100 within 30-calendar days of the date of the notice of imposition of the civil monetary penalty.
units.action_summary: A hospital may obtain a 35% reduction in a civil monetary penalty by submitting a written notice to CMS waiving its right to a hearing within 30 days of the penalty notice.

units.obligation_text: A hospital that receives a 35 percent reduction in a civil monetary penalty under this paragraph is not eligible to receive a 35 percent reduction for any civil monetary penalties imposed pursuant to continuing violations according to § 180.90(f) and also waives its right to appeal under § 180.100 any civil monet[ary penalty].
units.actor: the hospital that received the reduction
units.action_summary: A hospital that accepts the 35% reduction becomes ineligible for further 35% reductions for continuing violations and waives its right to appeal the civil monetary penalty.

title: Medicare and Medicaid Programs: Hospital Outpatient Prospective Payment and Ambulatory Surgical Center Payment Systems; Quality Reporting Programs; Overall Hospital Quality Star Ratings; and Hospital Price Transparency CMS-1834-P

units.obligation_text: the physician or nonphysician practitioner must be immediately available to furnish assistance and direction throughout the performance of the procedure
units.action_summary: Physicians/NPPs must be immediately available to provide assistance and direction for the procedure.

units.obligation_text: For pulmonary rehabilitation, cardiac rehabilitation, and intensive cardiac rehabilitation services, direct supervision must be furnished as specified in Sec. Sec. 410.47 and 410.49, respectively
units.actor: physician or nonphysician practitioner / CMS (as specified in referenced sections)
units.action_summary: Direct supervision for specified rehabilitation services must be furnished according to the rules in §§410.47 and 410.49.

units.obligation_text: The presence of the physician or nonphysician practitioner for the purpose of the supervision of pulmonary rehabilitation, cardiac rehabilitation, and intensive cardiac rehabilitation services includes virtual presence through audio/video real-time communications technology (excluding audio-only)
units.action_summary: Virtual presence by audio/video real-time communications (not audio-only) counts as physician/NPP presence for supervision of specified rehabilitation services.

units.obligation_text: The presence of the physician or nonphysician practitioner under paragraphs (e)(2)(i) and (ii) of this section includes virtual presence through audio/video real-time communications technology (excluding audio-only) for services without a 010 or 090 global surgery indicator
units.action_summary: For certain diagnostic services, virtual audio/video presence (excluding audio-only) satisfies presence requirements.

units.obligation_text: An inpatient admission for a surgical procedure specified by Medicare as inpatient only under Sec. 419.22(n) of this chapter is generally appropriate for payment under Medicare Part A regardless of the expected duration of care
units.action_summary: Admissions for procedures listed as inpatient-only under §419.22(n) are generally appropriate for Medicare Part A payment regardless of expected duration.

units.obligation_text: Claims for services and procedures removed from the inpatient only list under Sec. 419.22 of this chapter on or after January 1, 2021 are exempt from certain medical review activities until the Secretary determines that the service or procedure is more commonly performed in the outpatient setting than the inpatient setting
units.actor: claims for services and procedures removed from the inpatient-only list / Secretary
units.action_summary: Claims for procedures removed from the inpatient-only list (on/after 1/1/2021) are exempt from certain medical reviews until the Secretary finds they are more commonly outpatient.

units.obligation_text: Is approved by one of the national organizations listed in Sec. 415.152 of this chapter, provided that the national organization does not use accreditation criteria that promote or emphasize diversity, equity, inclusion, or awareness based on race, color, sex, sexual orientation or identity, national origin, or any other characteristic which serves as a proxy to achieve the same ends
units.actor: program seeking special treatment / national organization
units.action_summary: To qualify, a program must be approved by a listed national organization that does not employ accreditation criteria promoting or emphasizing specified diversity/equity characteristics.

units.obligation_text: May count towards certification of the participant in a specialty or subspecialty listed in the current edition of either the Directory of Graduate Medical Education Programs or the Annual Report and Reference Handbook, provided that listing does not require the program to promote or emphasize diversity, equity, inclusion, or awareness based on race, color, sex, sexual orientation or identity, national origin, or any other characteristic which serves as a proxy to achieve the same ends
units.action_summary: Listing in specified publications may count toward participant certification, provided listing does not require promotion/emphasis of specified diversity/equity characteristics.

units.obligation_text: Is approved by the Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education (ACGME), or other organization designated by the Secretary, as a fellowship program in geriatric medicine, provided that the Council or other organization does not use accreditation criteria that promote or emphasize diversity, equity, inclusion, or awareness based on race, color, sex, sexual orientation or identity, national origin, or any other characteristic which serves as a proxy to achieve the same ends
units.actor: fellowship program / ACGME or other designated organization
units.action_summary: A geriatric fellowship must be approved by ACGME or Secretary-designated organization that does not use accreditation criteria emphasizing specified diversity/equity characteristics.

units.obligation_text: Is a program that would be accredited except for the accrediting agency's reliance upon an accreditation standard that requires an entity to promote or emphasize diversity, equity, inclusion, or awareness based on race, color, sex, sexual orientation or identity, national origin, or any other characteristic which serves as a proxy to achieve the same ends
units.action_summary: Programs that would otherwise be accredited but for accrediting agency standards requiring promotion/emphasis of specified diversity/equity characteristics qualify under this provision.

units.obligation_text: Apply a 4-star cap for hospitals in the lowest quartile of the Safety of Care measure group performance in Calendar Year 2026
units.action_summary: CMS will cap ratings at 4 stars for hospitals in the lowest Safety of Care quartile in CY2026.

units.obligation_text: Any hospital that is assigned 5 stars in step eight but has a lowest quartile Safety of Care score (based on at least three Safety of Care measures) would be reassigned to 4 stars
units.action_summary: Hospitals assigned 5 stars but in lowest Safety of Care quartile (≥3 measures) will be reassigned to 4 stars.

units.obligation_text: Apply a blanket 1-Star reduction for hospitals in the lowest quartile of Safety of Care measure group performance beginning in Calendar Year 2027 and later years
units.action_summary: Beginning CY2027, CMS will reduce Overall Hospital Quality Star Ratings by one star for hospitals in the lowest Safety of Care quartile.

units.obligation_text: Any hospital assigned a 2, 3, 4, or 5-star rating in step eight, but with a lowest quartile Safety of Care score (based on at least three Safety of Care measures) would be reduced to 1, 2, 3, or 4 stars, respectively
units.action_summary: CMS will lower assigned star ratings by one step for hospitals in the lowest Safety of Care quartile (with ≥3 measures) beginning CY2027.

units.obligation_text: CMS provides hospitals the opportunity to preview their Overall Hospital Quality Star Rating prior to publication
units.action_summary: CMS will give hospitals an opportunity to preview their star rating before publication.

units.obligation_text: Hospitals have at least 30 days to preview their results
units.action_summary: Hospitals are provided a minimum 30-day preview period for their star rating results.

units.obligation_text: CMS may consider suppressing Overall Hospital Quality Star Rating for subsection (d) hospitals only under extenuating circumstances ... as determined by CMS, or when CMS is at fault
units.action_summary: CMS may suppress star ratings for subsection (d) hospitals only in extenuating circumstances or when CMS is at fault.

units.obligation_text: CMS may suppress when: (i) There is an Overall Hospital Quality Star Rating calculation error by CMS; (ii) there is a systemic error at the CMS quality program level that substantively affects the calculation; or (iii) if a Public Health Emergency substantially affects the underlying measure data
units.action_summary: CMS may suppress star ratings for calculation errors, systemic program errors, or substantial effects from a Public Health Emergency.

units.obligation_text: CAHs may request to withhold their Overall Hospital Quality Star Rating from publication on Care Compare on Medicare.gov so long as the request for withholding is made, at the latest, during the Overall Hospital Quality Star Rating preview period
units.action_summary: CAHs may request to withhold their star rating from publication if they request during the preview period.

units.obligation_text: CAHs may request to have their Overall Hospital Quality Star Rating withheld from publication ... as well as their data from the public input file, so long as the request is made during the CMS quality program-level 30-day confidential preview period for the Care Compare refresh data used to calculate the Overall Hospital Quality Star Ratings
units.action_summary: CAHs may request withholding of both their star rating and related data if requested during the specified 30-day confidential preview period.

units.obligation_text: The provider must furnish the contractor upon request, copies of patient service charge schedules and changes thereto as they are put into effect; and its median payer-specific negotiated charge by MS-DRG for payers that are Medicare Advantage organizations, as applicable, and changes thereto as they are put into effect
units.action_summary: Providers must give contractors, upon request, patient service charge schedules (and changes) and median payer-specific negotiated MS-DRG charges (and changes) as they take effect.

units.obligation_text: The contractor evaluates the charge schedules as specified in paragraph (d)(3)(i) of this section to determine the extent to which they may be used for determining program payment
units.action_summary: Contractor must evaluate submitted charge schedules to determine their use for program payment.

units.obligation_text: approved geriatric program means ... approved by one of the national organizations listed in Sec. 415.152 ... provided that the national organization does not use accreditation criteria that promote or emphasize diversity, equity, inclusion, or awareness based on ... characteristics
units.action_summary: To be an approved geriatric program, the approving national organization must not use accreditation criteria promoting/emphasizing specified diversity/equity characteristics.

units.obligation_text: An approved medical residency program is one that (1) is approved by a listed national organization provided that the national organization does not use accreditation criteria that promote or emphasize diversity, equity, inclusion, or awareness based on specified characteristics; (2) may count towards certification in listed publications provided that listing does not require program to promote or emphasize such characteristics; (3) is approved by ACGME or other designated organization provided that organization does not use such accreditation criteria; (5) is a program that would be accredited except for the accrediting agency's reliance upon an accreditation standard that requires promotion or emphasis of such characteristics
units.action_summary: Sets multiple alternative criteria for approval of medical residency programs and prohibits approving organizations from using accreditation criteria that promote/emphasize specified diversity/equity characteristics; also allows programs excluded solely because of such standards to qualify.

units.obligation_text: A residency program approved by [listed organizations] or other organization determined by the Secretary, provided that the applicable organization does not use accreditation criteria that promote or emphasize diversity, equity, inclusion, or awareness based on specified characteristics
units.action_summary: To qualify as an approved GME program, the approving organization must not use accreditation criteria promoting/emphasizing specified diversity/equity characteristics.

units.obligation_text: Covered surgical procedures are those procedures that meet the general standards described in paragraph (b)(1) for services through 12/31/2025 and the requirements described in paragraph (b)(2) beginning 1/1/2026
units.action_summary: Defines which surgical procedures qualify as covered surgical procedures over specified effective dates based on standards or requirements in paragraph (b).

units.obligation_text: Effective for services furnished on or after January 1, 2026, covered surgical procedures are not: (A) Currently designated as requiring inpatient care under Sec. 419.22(n); (B) Only able to be reported using a CPT unlisted surgical procedure code; or (C) Otherwise excluded under Sec. 411.15
units.action_summary: From 1/1/2026, covered procedures exclude those designated inpatient-only, those only reportable with unlisted CPT codes, or those excluded under §411.15.

units.obligation_text: Covered surgical procedures do not include those surgical procedures that: (1) generally result in extensive blood loss; (2) require major or prolonged invasion of body cavities; (3) directly involve major blood vessels; (4) are generally emergent or life-threatening; (5) commonly require systemic thrombolytic therapy; (6) are designated as requiring inpatient care under Sec. 419.22(n); (7) can only be reported using a CPT unlisted surgical procedure code; or (8) are otherwise excluded under Sec. 411.15
units.action_summary: Lists categories of procedures that are excluded from being ASC covered surgical procedures (general exclusions).

units.obligation_text: Physicians consider the following safety factors as to a specific beneficiary when determining whether to perform a covered surgical procedure
units.action_summary: Physicians must consider listed safety factors when deciding whether to perform a covered surgical procedure on a beneficiary.

units.obligation_text: The covered procedure: (1) is not expected to pose a significant safety risk when performed in an ASC; (2) is one of which standard medical practice dictates the beneficiary would not typically be expected to require active medical monitoring and care at midnight following the procedure; (3) generally results in extensive blood loss; (4) requires major or prolonged invasion of body cavities; (5) directly involves major blood vessels; (6) is generally emergent or life-threatening in nature; and (7) commonly requires systemic thrombolytic therapy
units.action_summary: Enumerates safety considerations physicians must weigh regarding the covered procedure (both inclusion/exclusion-type characteristics).
units.modal_raw: is / would not be expected / generally results / requires / directly involves / is / commonly requires

units.obligation_text: On or after January 1, 2026, CMS adds surgical procedures to the list of ASC covered procedures as follows: (1) CMS identifies a surgical procedure that meets the requirements at paragraph (b)(2); (2) CMS is notified of a surgical procedure that could meet the requirements at paragraph (b)(2) and CMS confirms that such surgical procedure meets those requirements
units.action_summary: CMS will add procedures to the ASC list by identifying qualifying procedures or confirming notified procedures meet the paragraph (b)(2) requirements.

units.obligation_text: For specified CYs, the update is reduced by 2.0 percentage points for an ASC that fails to meet the standards for reporting of ASC quality measures as established by the Secretary for the corresponding calendar year
units.actor: ASC (if fails to meet reporting standards)
units.action_summary: An ASC that fails reporting standards will have its annual update reduced by 2.0 percentage points in specified years.

units.obligation_text: For specified CY ranges, after application of any reduction, the applicable update is reduced by the productivity adjustment described in section 1886(b)(3)(B)(xi)(II) of the Act
units.action_summary: After applying any applicable reductions, CMS will apply a statutory productivity adjustment to the update in specified years.

units.obligation_text: CMS may grant an ECE with respect to the reporting requirements under this section in the event of extraordinary circumstances beyond the control of the ASC
units.action_summary: CMS may grant an Extraordinary Circumstance Exception for ASC reporting requirements when extraordinary events beyond the ASC's control occur.

units.obligation_text: An ASC may request an ECE within 30 calendar days of the date that the extraordinary circumstance occurred by submitting the information specified by CMS at QualityNet or a successor website
units.action_summary: An ASC may request an ECE within 30 days of the event by submitting required information on QualityNet or successor site.

units.obligation_text: CMS notifies the ASC of its decision on the request, in writing, via email; the written decision specifies whether the ASC is exempted from one or more reporting requirements or whether CMS has granted the ASC an extension of time to comply with one or more reporting requirements
units.action_summary: CMS must notify ASCs in writing by email about ECE decisions and must state whether exemptions or extensions are granted.

units.obligation_text: CMS may grant an ECE to one or more ASCs that have not requested an ECE if CMS determines that (i) a systemic problem with a CMS data collection system directly impacted the ability of the ASC to comply; or (ii) an extraordinary circumstance has affected an entire region or locale
units.action_summary: CMS may proactively grant ECEs to ASCs (even without requests) if systemic data collection problems or widespread extraordinary circumstances affected compliance.

units.obligation_text: Effective beginning on January 1, 2026, the Secretary shall eliminate the list of services and procedures designated as requiring inpatient care through a 3-year transition, with the list eliminated in its entirety by January 1, 2029
units.action_summary: Secretary is required to phase out the inpatient-only list over a three-year transition starting 1/1/2026 and complete elimination by 1/1/2029.

units.obligation_text: Beginning in calendar year 2026, a multifactor productivity adjustment (as determined by CMS), and 2.0-percentage point reduction, except that the 2.0-percentage point reduction shall not apply to hospital outpatient items and services furnished by a hospital with a CMS certification number (CCN) effective date of January 2, 2018, or later
units.actor: CMS / hospital outpatient items and services
units.action_summary: Starting CY2026, CMS applies a multifactor productivity adjustment and a 2.0 percentage-point reduction to payments, but the 2.0-point reduction does not apply to hospitals with CCN effective on/after Jan 2, 2018.

units.obligation_text: the 2.0-percentage point reduction shall not apply to hospital outpatient items and services furnished by a hospital with a CMS certification number (CCN) effective date of January 2, 2018, or later
units.actor: hospitals with CCN effective date Jan 2, 2018 or later
units.action_summary: Hospitals with CCNs effective Jan 2, 2018 or later are exempt from the 2.0-percentage-point reduction.

units.obligation_text: CMS provides for an additional payment beyond the standard payment to a hospital for a dose of Tc-99m derived from Mo-99, if at least 50 percent of the Mo-99 in the Tc-99m generator that produced the dose was both irradiated and processed in the United States
units.action_summary: CMS will pay an add-on for Tc-99m doses when at least 50% of the Mo-99 in the generator was irradiated and processed in the U.S.

units.obligation_text: A dose of Tc-99m does not qualify for the add-on payment if more than 50 percent of the Mo-99 in the Tc-99m generator was irradiated or processed outside the United States, even if the Mo-99 has been loaded into a Tc-99m generator in the United States or if the Tc-99m has been eluted at a radiopharmacy in the United States
units.actor: dose of Tc-99m / hospitals seeking add-on payment
units.action_summary: Tc-99m doses where >50% of Mo-99 was irradiated/processed outside the U.S. are ineligible for the add-on payment.

units.obligation_text: CMS may grant an ECE with respect to the reporting requirements under this section in the event of extraordinary circumstances beyond the control of the REH; an REH may request an ECE within 30 calendar days of the date that the extraordinary circumstance occurred; CMS notifies the REH of its decision in writing via email and specifies whether the REH is exempted or granted an extension; CMS may grant an ECE to one or more REHs that have not requested an ECE if CMS determines a systemic problem or regional extraordinary circumstance
units.action_summary: ECE process for REHs: REHs may request ECEs within 30 days; CMS may grant ECEs (including proactively), must notify decisions in writing and specify exemptions or extensions when granted.
units.modal_raw: may grant / may request / notifies / specifies / determines

units.obligation_text: REHs must utilize technology certified to the Office of the National Coordinator for Health Information Technology's (ONC's) health IT certification criteria, as adopted and updated in 45 CFR 170.315, for reporting eCQMs under the REHQR Program
units.action_summary: REHs are required to use ONC-certified health IT (per 45 CFR 170.315) to report eCQMs under REHQR.

units.obligation_text: REHs must use health IT certified to all eCQMs that are available to report under the REHQR Program
units.action_summary: REHs must use health IT certified to support all eCQMs available for reporting under REHQR.

units.obligation_text: REHs must use the most recent version of the eCQM electronic measure specifications for the applicable reporting period available on the Electronic Clinical Quality Improvement Resource Center website or another website as designated by CMS
units.action_summary: REHs must use the latest eCQM specifications for the reporting period from the designated website.

units.obligation_text: The requirements set forth in paragraphs (h)(1) through (3) of this section apply only where an REH opts to report an eCQM
units.action_summary: The eCQM technology and specification requirements apply only if an REH chooses to report eCQMs.

units.obligation_text: Prior to January 1, 2026, make a good faith effort to ensure that the standard charge information encoded in the machine-readable file is true, accurate, and complete as of the date indicated in the machine-readable file
units.action_summary: Before 1/1/2026, hospitals must make a good-faith effort to ensure machine-readable standard charge information is true, accurate, and complete as of the file date.

units.obligation_text: Prior to January 1, 2026, affirm in its machine-readable file that, to the best of its knowledge and belief, the hospital has included all applicable standard charge information in accordance with the requirements of this section, and that the information encoded is true, accurate, and complete as of the date indicated in the machine-readable file
units.action_summary: Before 1/1/2026, hospitals must affirm in their machine-readable file that they have included all applicable standard charge information and that it is true, accurate, and complete as of the file date.

units.obligation_text: Beginning January 1, 2026, attest in its machine-readable file the following: This hospital has included all applicable standard charge information in accordance with the requirements of 45 CFR 180.50, and the information encoded is true, accurate, and complete as of the date in the file. This hospital has included all payer-specific negotiated charges in dollars that can be expressed as a dollar amount. For payer-specific negotiated charges that cannot be expressed as a dollar amount ... the hospital attests that the payer-specific negotiated charge is based on a contractual algorithm, percentage or formula ... and has provided all necessary information available to the hospital for the public to be able to derive the dollar amount
units.action_summary: Starting 1/1/2026, hospitals must make a detailed attestation in their machine-readable file about inclusion and format of standard charges and payer-specific negotiated charges, and provide necessary information when dollar amounts cannot be directly provided.

units.obligation_text: Beginning January 1, 2026, encode the name of the hospital chief executive officer, president or senior official designated to oversee the encoding of true, accurate, and complete data as directed in paragraph (a)(3)(iii) of this section
units.action_summary: From 1/1/2026, hospitals must include the name of the CEO/president/senior official responsible for encoding the machine-readable file data.

units.obligation_text: Location name(s) and address(es) must include, at minimum, all inpatient facilities and stand-alone emergency departments; and beginning January 1, 2026, Type 2 (organizational) National Provider Identifier(s) (NPI)
units.action_summary: Hospitals must include location names/addresses for all inpatient facilities and stand-alone EDs and, starting 1/1/2026, include Type 2 organizational NPIs in the machine-readable file.

units.obligation_text: Beginning January 1, 2025 through December 31, 2025, calculate and encode an estimated allowed amount in dollars for that item or service
units.action_summary: Hospitals must calculate and include an estimated allowed amount in dollars for items/services during 1/1/2025–12/31/2025 when the standard charge is based on a percentage or algorithm.

units.obligation_text: Beginning January 1, 2026, calculate and encode the tenth (10th) percentile allowed amount, the median allowed amount, and the ninetieth (90th) percentile allowed amount in dollars for that item or service
units.action_summary: Starting 1/1/2026, hospitals must calculate and include the 10th percentile, median, and 90th percentile allowed amounts in dollars for items/services when required.

title: Homeland Security Acquisition Regulation (HSAR); Safeguarding of Controlled Unclassified Information (HSAR Case 2015–001)

units.obligation_text: DHS requires that CUI be safeguarded wherever such information resides. Compliance with these policies and procedures, as amended, is required.
units.actor: holders of Controlled Unclassified Information (including government and contractor information systems, contractor and subcontractor employees)
units.action_summary: CUI must be safeguarded wherever it resides; applicable DHS policies and procedures must be complied with.

units.obligation_text: DHS requires contractor employees that require recurring access to Government facilities or access to CUI to complete such forms as may be necessary for security or other reasons, including the conduct of background investigations to determine fitness.
units.actor: contractor employees requiring recurring access to Government facilities or access to CUI
units.action_summary: Contractor employees with recurring access must complete required security forms and undergo background investigations as necessary.

units.obligation_text: Compliance with these policies and procedures, as amended, is required.
units.actor: contractors and contractor employees subject to DHS policies and procedures
units.action_summary: Contractors and relevant employees must comply with DHS policies and procedures referenced.

units.obligation_text: Contracting officers shall insert the basic clause at (HSAR) 48 CFR 3052.204–71, Contractor Employee Access, in solicitations and contracts when contractor and/or subcontractor employees require recurring access to Government facilities or access to CUI.
units.action_summary: Insert HSAR clause 3052.204–71 in solicitations/contracts when employees require recurring access to Government facilities or CUI.

units.obligation_text: Contracting officers shall insert the basic clause with its Alternate I for acquisitions requiring contractor access to Government information resources.
units.action_summary: Use Alternate I of the basic clause when acquisition requires contractor access to Government information resources.

units.obligation_text: For acquisitions in which contractor and/or subcontractor employees will not have access to Government information resources, but the Department has determined contractor and/or subcontractor employee access to CUI or Government facilities must be limited to U.S. citizens and lawful permanent residents, the contracting officer shall insert the clause with its Alternate II.
units.action_summary: Use Alternate II of the basic clause when access must be limited to U.S. citizens and lawful permanent residents and employees won't access Government information resources.

units.obligation_text: Neither the basic clause nor its alternates shall be used unless contractor and/or subcontractor employees will require recurring access to Government facilities or access to CUI.
units.action_summary: Do not use the basic clause or alternates unless employees will require recurring access to Government facilities or CUI.

units.obligation_text: Neither the basic clause nor its alternates should ordinarily be used in contracts with educational institutions.
units.action_summary: Ordinarily avoid using the basic clause or its alternates in contracts with educational institutions.

units.obligation_text: Contracting officers shall insert the clause at (HSAR) 48 CFR 3052.204–7X, Safeguarding of Controlled Unclassified Information, in solicitations and contracts where:
units.action_summary: Insert HSAR clause 3052.204–7X in solicitations/contracts when specified conditions apply.

units.obligation_text: Contracting officers shall insert the clause where contractor and/or subcontractor employees will have access to CUI.
units.action_summary: Condition triggering insertion: employees will have access to CUI.

units.obligation_text: Contracting officers shall insert the clause where CUI will be collected or maintained on behalf of the agency.
units.action_summary: Condition triggering insertion: CUI will be collected or maintained on behalf of the agency.

units.obligation_text: Contracting officers shall insert the clause where Federal information systems, which include contractor information systems operated on behalf of the agency, are used to collect, process, store, or transmit CUI.
units.action_summary: Condition triggering insertion: Federal information systems are used to handle CUI.

units.obligation_text: If the clauses prescribed in subsections (a) and/or (b) are included in a prime contract, the prime contractor shall include the clauses in subsections (a) and/or (b), in its contract(s) with subcontractors.
units.action_summary: Prime contractors must flow down the specified clauses to their subcontractors when included in the prime contract.

units.obligation_text: If a subcontract includes the clauses prescribed in subsections (a) and/or (b) and the subcontractor has contracts with lower-tier subcontractors, the lower-tier subcontracts shall include the clauses in subsections (a) and/or (b).
units.action_summary: Lower-tier subcontracts must include the same clauses if flowed down to a subcontractor with further subcontracting.

units.obligation_text: Contractors and subcontractors must provide adequate security to protect CUI from unauthorized access and disclosure. Adequate security includes compliance with DHS policies and procedures in effect at the time of contract award.
units.action_summary: Provide adequate security for CUI, including complying with current DHS policies and procedures.

units.obligation_text: The Contractor shall not use or redistribute any CUI handled, collected, processed, stored, or transmitted by the Contractor except as specified in the contract.
units.action_summary: Contractor is prohibited from using or redistributing CUI except as contractually specified.

units.obligation_text: The Contractor shall not maintain SPII in its invoicing, billing, and other recordkeeping systems maintained to support financial or other administrative functions.
units.action_summary: Contractor prohibited from storing Sensitive PII in financial/administrative recordkeeping systems.

units.obligation_text: It is acceptable to maintain in these systems the names, titles and contact information for the Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR) or other Government personnel associated with the administration of the contract, as needed.
units.action_summary: Contractor may store COR or Government personnel contact details in administrative systems as needed.

units.obligation_text: Any Government data provided, developed, obtained under the contract, or otherwise under the control of the contractor, shall not become part of the bankruptcy estate in the event a contractor and/or subcontractor enters into bankruptcy proceedings.
units.action_summary: Government data under contract control must not be treated as part of a contractor's bankruptcy estate.

units.obligation_text: The Contractor shall not collect, process, store or transmit CUI within a Federal information system until an Authority to Operate (ATO) has been accepted and signed by the Component or Headquarters CIO, or designee.
units.action_summary: Contractor may not handle CUI in a Federal information system until a signed ATO is accepted by the appropriate CIO.

units.obligation_text: Once the ATO has been accepted and signed by the Government, the Contracting Officer shall incorporate the ATO into the contract as a compliance document.
units.action_summary: CO must incorporate the accepted ATO into the contract as a compliance document.

units.obligation_text: Complete the Security Authorization process.
units.action_summary: Contractor must complete the DHS Security Authorization process.

units.obligation_text: SA package shall be developed using the Government provided Requirements Traceability Matrix and SA templates.
units.action_summary: Develop the Security Authorization package using government-provided templates and traceability matrix.

units.obligation_text: The Contractor shall submit a signed copy of the SA package, validated by an independent third party, to the COR for acceptance by the Headquarters or Component CIO, or designee, at least thirty (30) days prior to the date of operation of the information system.
units.action_summary: Submit a third-party-validated signed SA package to the COR at least 30 days before the system's operation date for CIO acceptance.

units.obligation_text: Contractors shall have an independent third party validate the security and privacy controls in place for the information system(s).
units.action_summary: Contractors must obtain independent third-party validation of security and privacy controls.

units.obligation_text: The Contractor shall address all deficiencies before submitting the SA package to the COR for acceptance.
units.action_summary: Fix all identified deficiencies prior to submitting the SA package to the COR.

units.obligation_text: The Contractor is required to update its SA package as part of the ATO renewal process for review and verification of security controls.
units.action_summary: Contractor must update the SA package during ATO renewal to review and verify security controls.

units.obligation_text: The updated SA package shall be submitted for acceptance by the Headquarters or Component CIO, or designee, at least 90 days before the ATO expiration date.
units.action_summary: Submit the updated SA package to the CIO at least 90 days before ATO expiration for acceptance.

units.obligation_text: The Contractor shall update its SA package by one of the following methods: (i) Updating the SA package in the DHS Information Assurance Compliance System; or (ii) Submitting the updated SA package directly to the COR.
units.action_summary: Update the SA package either via the DHS compliance system or by submitting it directly to the COR.

units.obligation_text: Updating the SA package in the DHS Information Assurance Compliance System.
units.action_summary: One permitted method: update the SA package within DHS's Information Assurance Compliance System.

units.obligation_text: Submitting the updated SA package directly to the COR.
units.action_summary: Alternative method: submit updated SA package directly to the COR.

units.obligation_text: The Government may elect to conduct random periodic reviews to ensure that the security requirements contained in this contract are being implemented and enforced.
units.action_summary: Government may perform random periodic reviews of contractor security implementation.

units.obligation_text: The Government, at its sole discretion, may obtain the assistance from other Federal agencies and/or third-party firms to aid in security review activities.
units.action_summary: Government may seek assistance from other agencies or third parties for security reviews.

units.obligation_text: The Contractor shall afford access to DHS, the Office of the Inspector General, other Government organizations, and contractors working in support of the Government access to the Contractor’s facilities, installations, operations, documentation, databases, networks, systems, and personnel used in the performance of this contract.
units.action_summary: Contractor must provide access to facilities, systems, personnel, and relevant materials to DHS/OIG/other government orgs and supporting contractors.

units.obligation_text: The Contractor shall, through the Contracting Officer and COR, contact the Headquarters or Component CIO, or designee, to coordinate and participate in review and inspection activity by Government organizations external to the DHS.
units.action_summary: Contractor must coordinate with CO/COR to contact CIO for participation in external government review/inspection activities.

units.obligation_text: Access shall be provided, to the extent necessary as determined by the Government (including providing all requested images), for the Government to carry out a program of inspection, investigation, and audit to safeguard against threats and hazards to the integrity, availability and confidentiality of Government data or the function of computer systems used in performance of this contract and to preserve evidence of computer crime.
units.action_summary: Contractor must provide necessary access, including images, to support government inspection, investigation, audit, and evidence preservation.

units.obligation_text: Contractors operating information systems on behalf of the Government shall comply with Federal reporting and information system continuous monitoring requirements.
units.actor: Contractors operating information systems on behalf of the Government
units.action_summary: Contractors must comply with federal reporting and continuous monitoring requirements.

units.obligation_text: The Contractor shall provide the Government with all information to fully satisfy Federal reporting requirements for information systems.
units.action_summary: Provide all information needed to meet federal reporting requirements for information systems.

units.obligation_text: The Contractor shall provide the COR with requested information within three (3) business days of receipt of the request.
units.action_summary: Provide requested information to the COR within 3 business days of request.

units.obligation_text: Unless otherwise specified in the contract, monthly continuous monitoring data shall be stored at the Contractor’s location for a period not less than one year from the date the data is created.
units.action_summary: Store monthly continuous monitoring data locally for at least one year unless contract specifies otherwise.

units.obligation_text: The Government may elect to perform information system continuous monitoring and IT security scanning of information systems from Government tools and infrastructure.
units.action_summary: Government may perform continuous monitoring and security scanning using Government tools/infrastructure.

units.obligation_text: All known or suspected incidents shall be reported to the Component Security Operations Center (SOC) in accordance with 4300A Sensitive Systems Handbook Attachment F Incident Response. If the Component SOC is not available, the Contractor shall report to the DHS Enterprise SOC.
units.action_summary: Report all known or suspected incidents to the Component SOC per handbook; if unavailable, report to DHS Enterprise SOC.

units.obligation_text: The Contractor shall also notify the Contracting Officer and COR using the contact information identified in the contract.
units.action_summary: Also notify the Contracting Officer and COR using contract-specified contact info.

units.obligation_text: If the report is made by phone, or the email address for the Contracting Officer or COR is not immediately available, the Contractor shall contact the Contracting Officer immediately after reporting to the Component or DHS Enterprise SOC.
units.action_summary: If initial report was by phone or CO/COR email not available, contact the Contracting Officer immediately after SOC reporting.

units.obligation_text: All known or suspected incidents involving PII or SPII shall be reported within one hour of discovery. All other incidents shall be reported within eight hours of discovery.
units.action_summary: Report PII/SPII incidents within 1 hour of discovery; all other incidents within 8 hours.

units.obligation_text: The Contractor shall not include any CUI in the subject or body of any email.
units.action_summary: Do not include CUI in email subject or body.

units.obligation_text: The Contractor shall transmit CUI using FIPS 140–2 Security Requirements for Cryptographic Modules compliant encryption methods ... to protect CUI in attachments to email.
units.action_summary: Transmit CUI in email attachments only using FIPS 140–2 compliant encryption methods.

units.obligation_text: Passwords shall not be communicated in the same email as the attachment.
units.action_summary: Do not send passwords in the same email as the encrypted attachment.
