units.obligation_text: If an incident involves PII or SPII, in addition to the incident reporting guidelines in 4300A Sensitive Systems Handbook Attachment F Incident Response, Contractors shall also provide as many of the following data elements that are available at the time the incident is reported, with any remaining data elements provided within 24 hours of submission of the initial incident report:
units.action_summary: When PII/SPII incidents occur, contractors must provide available specified data elements with any remainder within 24 hours.

units.obligation_text: Data Universal Numbering System (DUNS).
units.action_summary: Provide DUNS number when reporting a PII/SPII incident.

units.obligation_text: Contract numbers affected unless all contracts by the company are affected.
units.action_summary: Provide affected contract numbers (unless all company contracts are affected).

units.obligation_text: Facility CAGE code if the location of the event is different than the prime contractor location.
units.action_summary: Provide facility CAGE code when event location differs from prime contractor location.

units.obligation_text: Point of contact (POC) if different than the POC recorded in the System for Award Management (address, position, telephone, email).
units.action_summary: Provide POC details if different than SAM-recorded POC.

units.obligation_text: Contracting Officer POC (address, telephone, email).
units.action_summary: Provide Contracting Officer point of contact information.

units.obligation_text: Contract clearance level.
units.action_summary: Provide contract clearance level relevant to the incident.

units.obligation_text: Name of subcontractor and CAGE code if this was an incident on a subcontractor network.
units.action_summary: Provide subcontractor name and CAGE code if incident occurred on subcontractor network.

units.obligation_text: Government programs, platforms or systems involved.
units.action_summary: Identify government programs, platforms, or systems involved in the incident.

units.obligation_text: Location(s) of incident.
units.action_summary: Provide incident locations.

units.obligation_text: Date and time the incident was discovered.
units.action_summary: Provide date and time when incident was discovered.

units.obligation_text: Server names where CUI resided at the time of the incident, both at the Contractor and subcontractor level.
units.action_summary: Provide server names at contractor and subcontractor levels where CUI resided.

units.obligation_text: Description of the Government PII or SPII contained within the system.
units.action_summary: Describe the Government PII or SPII present in the system.

units.obligation_text: Any additional information relevant to the incident.
units.action_summary: Provide any other information relevant to the incident.

units.obligation_text: All determinations by the Department related to incidents, including response activities, notifications to affected individuals and/or Federal agencies, and related services (e.g., credit monitoring) will be made in writing by the Contracting Officer.
units.action_summary: The Contracting Officer will make written determinations regarding incident responses, notifications, and related services.

units.obligation_text: The Contractor shall provide full access and cooperation for all activities determined by the Government to be required to ensure an effective incident response, including providing all requested images, log files, and event information to facilitate rapid resolution of incidents.
units.action_summary: Contractor must fully cooperate and provide requested images, logs, and event information for incident response.

units.obligation_text: Incident response activities determined to be required by the Government may include, but are not limited to, the following: (i) Inspections, (ii) Investigations, (iii) Forensic reviews, (iv) Data analyses and processing, and (v) Revocation of the Authority to Operate.
units.action_summary: The Government may require various incident response activities including inspections, investigations, forensic reviews, data analysis, and revocation of ATO.

units.obligation_text: Inspections.
units.action_summary: Inspections may be required as part of incident response.

units.obligation_text: Investigations.
units.action_summary: Investigations may be required as part of incident response.

units.obligation_text: Forensic reviews.
units.action_summary: Forensic reviews may be required as part of incident response.

units.obligation_text: Data analyses and processing.
units.action_summary: Data analyses and processing may be required as part of incident response.

units.obligation_text: Revocation of the Authority to Operate.
units.action_summary: The Government may revoke an Authority to Operate as part of incident response.

units.obligation_text: The contractor shall preserve and protect images of known affected information systems identified in paragraph (b) of this section and all relevant monitoring/packet capture data for at least 90 days from submission of the incident report to allow DHS to request the media or decline interest.
units.action_summary: Preserve and protect images and monitoring/packet capture data for at least 90 days after incident report submission.

units.obligation_text: The Government, at its sole discretion, may obtain assistance from other Federal agencies and/or third-party firms to aid in incident response activities.
units.action_summary: Government may obtain assistance from other agencies or third-party firms for incident response.

units.obligation_text: The Contractor shall have in place procedures and the capability to notify any individual whose PII and/or SPII was under the control of the Contractor or resided in the information system at the time of the incident not later than 5 business days after being directed to notify individuals, unless otherwise approved by the Contracting Officer.
units.action_summary: Contractor must have procedures and be able to notify affected individuals within 5 business days after being directed, unless CO approves otherwise.

units.obligation_text: The method and content of any notification by the Contractor shall be coordinated with, and subject to prior written approval by the Contracting Officer utilizing the DHS Privacy Incident Handling Guidance. The Contractor shall not proceed with notification unless directed in writing by the Contracting Officer.
units.action_summary: Coordinate notification method/content with CO and obtain prior written approval; do not notify unless directed in writing by CO.

units.obligation_text: Subject to Government analysis of the incident and the terms of its instructions to the Contractor regarding any resulting notification, the notification method may consist of letters to affected individuals sent by first class mail, electronic means, or general public notice, as approved by the Government. Notification may require the Contractor’s use of address verification and/or address location services.
units.action_summary: Notification method may be letters, electronic means, or public notice as approved by Government; contractor may be required to use address verification services.

units.obligation_text: At a minimum, the notification shall include: (i) A brief description of the incident; (ii) A description of the types of PII or SPII involved; (iii) A statement as to whether the PII or SPII was encrypted or protected by other means; (iv) Steps individuals may take to protect themselves; (v) What the Contractor and/or the Government are doing to investigate the incident, to mitigate the incident, and to protect against any future incidents; and (vi) Information identifying who individuals may contact for additional information.
units.action_summary: Notifications must include specified minimum content about the incident, data involved, protections, mitigation steps, investigation actions, and contact information.

units.obligation_text: A brief description of the incident.
units.action_summary: Include a brief incident description in notifications.

units.obligation_text: A description of the types of PII or SPII involved.
units.action_summary: Describe the types of PII/SPII involved in the notification.

units.obligation_text: A statement as to whether the PII or SPII was encrypted or protected by other means.
units.action_summary: State whether the PII/SPII was encrypted or otherwise protected.

units.obligation_text: Steps individuals may take to protect themselves.
units.action_summary: Include recommended steps individuals can take to protect themselves.

units.obligation_text: What the Contractor and/or the Government are doing to investigate the incident, to mitigate the incident, and to protect against any future incidents.
units.action_summary: Describe actions taken by contractor and/or government to investigate, mitigate, and prevent future incidents.

units.obligation_text: Information identifying who individuals may contact for additional information.
units.action_summary: Provide contact information for further inquiries.

units.obligation_text: In the event that an incident involves PII or SPII, the Contractor may be directed by the Contracting Officer to: (1) Provide notification to affected individuals
units.action_summary: Contracting Officer may direct the contractor to provide notification to affected individuals in PII/SPII incidents.

title: Homeland Security Acquisition Regulation (HSAR); Safeguarding of Controlled Unclassified Information (HSAR Case 2015–001); Information Technology Security Awareness Training (HSAR Case 2015–002); Privacy Training (HSAR Case 2015- 003)- Extension of Comment Periods

units.obligation_text: Comments on the proposed rules should be submitted in writing to one of the addresses shown below on or before April 19, 2017.
units.action_summary: Submit written comments on the proposed rules by April 19, 2017.

units.obligation_text: Submit comments identified by HSAR Case 2015–001, Safeguarding of Controlled Unclassified Information; HSAR Case 2015–002, Information Technology Security Awareness Training; and HSAR Case 2015–003, Privacy Training using any of the following methods: Regulations.gov: http://www.regulations.gov.
units.action_summary: Submit comments via Regulations.gov for the identified HSAR cases.

units.obligation_text: Submit comments identified by HSAR Case 2015–001, ... using any of the following methods: Fax: (202) 447–0520.
units.action_summary: Submit comments by fax to (202) 447–0520 for the identified HSAR cases.

units.obligation_text: Submit comments identified by HSAR Case 2015–001, ... using any of the following methods: Mail: Department of Homeland Security, Office of the Chief Procurement Officer, Acquisition Policy and Legislation, ATTN: Ms. Candace Lightfoot, 245 Murray Drive, Bldg. 410 (RDS), Washington, DC 20528.
units.action_summary: Submit comments by mail to the DHS Office of the Chief Procurement Officer at the listed postal address for the identified HSAR cases.

units.obligation_text: To avoid duplication, please use only one of these three methods.
units.action_summary: Use only one of the three listed submission methods to avoid duplicate comments.

units.obligation_text: Comments received generally will be posted without change to http://www.regulations.gov, including any personal information provided. To confirm receipt of your comment(s), please check www.regulations.gov, approximately two to three days after submission to verify posting (except allow 30 days for posting of comments submitted by mail).
units.action_summary: Check regulations.gov about 2–3 days after submission (30 days for mailed comments) to verify that your comment was posted.

units.obligation_text: If you submit a comment, please include the docket number for the applicable rulemaking (DHS–2017–0006, DHS–2017–0007, or DHS–2017–0008), indicate the specific section of each document to which each comment applies, and provide a reason for each suggestion or recommendation.
units.action_summary: Include the applicable docket number, the specific section your comment addresses, and a reason for each suggestion when submitting a comment.

units.obligation_text: When using email, include HSAR Case 2015–001, HSAR Case 2015–002, or HSAR Case 2015–003 in the "Subject" line.
units.action_summary: Include the applicable HSAR case identifier in the email subject line when submitting comments by email.

units.obligation_text: We recommend that you include your name and a mailing address, an email address, or a phone number in the body of your document so that we can contact you if we have questions regarding your submission.
units.action_summary: Provide contact information (name and mailing address, email, or phone) in your comment so DHS can contact you if needed.

units.obligation_text: To submit your comment online, go to http://www.regulations.gov and insert the applicable docket number (DHS–2017–0006, DHS–2017–0007, or DHS–2017–0008) in the "Search" box. Click on "Submit a Comment" in the "Actions" column.
units.action_summary: To submit online, go to regulations.gov, enter the docket number, and click 'Submit a Comment' in the Actions column.

units.obligation_text: If you submit comments by mail, submit them in an unbound format, no larger than 81/2 by 11 inches, suitable for copying and electronic filing.
units.action_summary: When mailing comments, provide them unbound and no larger than 8.5 x 11 inches so they are suitable for copying and electronic filing.

units.obligation_text: If you submit comments by mail and would like to know that they reached the Facility, please enclose a stamped, self-addressed postcard or envelope.
units.action_summary: Optionally enclose a stamped, self-addressed postcard or envelope with mailed comments to receive confirmation of receipt.

units.obligation_text: To view comments, as well as documents mentioned in this preamble as being available in the docket, go to http://www.regulations.gov and insert the applicable docket number (DHS–2017–0006, DHS–2017–0007, or DHS–2017–0008) in the "Search" box. Click "Search." Click the "Open Docket Folder" in the "Actions" column.
units.action_summary: To view docketed comments and documents, go to regulations.gov, enter the docket number, search, and open the docket folder in the Actions column.

title: Equal Participation of Faith- Based Organizations in DHS's Programs and Activities: Implementation of Executive Order 13831

units.obligation_text: All organizations that participate in DHS social service programs, including faith-based organizations, must carry out eligible activities in accordance with all program requirements, subject to any reasonable religious accommodation, and other applicable requirements governing the conduct of DHS-funded activities, including those prohibiting the use of direct financial assistance from DHS to engage in explicitly religious activities.
units.actor: All organizations that participate in DHS social service programs, including faith-based organizations
units.action_summary: Carry out eligible activities in accordance with all program requirements and other applicable requirements, subject to reasonable religious accommodations.

units.obligation_text: No grant document, agreement, covenant, memorandum of understanding, policy, or regulation that is used by DHS or an intermediary in administering financial assistance from DHS shall disqualify a faith-based organization from participating in DHS’s social service programs because such organization is motivated or influenced by religious faith to provide social services or because of its religious exercise or affiliation.
units.actor: DHS or an intermediary when using grant documents, agreements, covenants, memoranda of understanding, policies, or regulations to administer DHS financial assistance
units.action_summary: May not disqualify a faith-based organization from DHS social service programs for being motivated by religion or for its religious exercise or affiliation.

units.obligation_text: No grant document, agreement, covenant, memorandum of understanding, policy, or regulation used by DHS or an intermediary in administering financial assistance from DHS shall require faith-based organizations to provide assurances or notices where they are not required of non-faith-based organizations.
units.actor: DHS or an intermediary when using grant documents, agreements, covenants, memoranda of understanding, policies, or regulations to administer DHS financial assistance
units.action_summary: May not require faith-based organizations to provide assurances or notices that are not required of non-faith-based organizations.

units.obligation_text: Any restrictions on the use of grant funds shall apply equally to faith-based and non-faith-based organizations.
units.actor: DHS and intermediaries administering grant funds
units.action_summary: Ensure that any restrictions on grant fund use apply equally to faith-based and non-faith-based organizations.

units.obligation_text: Participation in explicitly religious activities must be voluntary for beneficiaries of the programs or services funded with such assistance.
units.actor: Providers/organizations of explicitly religious activities funded with DHS direct assistance
units.action_summary: Ensure that beneficiary participation in explicitly religious activities funded with DHS direct assistance is voluntary.

units.obligation_text: All organizations that participate in DHS social service programs, including faith-based organizations, must carry out eligible activities in accordance with all program requirements, subject to any religious accommodations appropriate under the Constitution or other provisions of federal law ... and in accordance with all other applicable requirements governing the conduct of DHS-funded activities, including those prohibiting the use of direct financial assistance from DHS to engage in explicitly religious activities.
units.actor: All organizations that participate in DHS social service programs, including faith-based organizations
units.action_summary: Carry out eligible activities consistent with program requirements and applicable religious accommodation laws, and obey prohibitions on using DHS direct assistance for explicitly religious activities.

units.obligation_text: No grant document, agreement, covenant, memorandum of understanding, policy, or regulation that is used by DHS or a State or local government in administering financial assistance from DHS shall disqualify a faith-based organization from participating in DHS’s social service programs because such organization is motivated or influenced by religious faith to provide social services or because of its religious exercise or affiliation.
units.actor: DHS or a State or local government when using grant documents, agreements, covenants, memoranda of understanding, policies, or regulations to administer DHS financial assistance
units.action_summary: May not disqualify faith-based organizations from participation for being motivated by religion or for their religious exercise or affiliation.

units.obligation_text: May require attendance at all activities that are fundamental to the program.
units.action_summary: Organizations may require attendance at program activities that are fundamental to the program.

units.obligation_text: In general, DHS does not require that a recipient, including a faith-based organization, obtain tax-exempt status under section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code to be eligible for funding under DHS social service programs.
units.action_summary: Recipients are not generally required by DHS to have 501(c)(3) tax-exempt status to be eligible for funding.
units.modal_raw: does not require / is not required to

units.obligation_text: Funding announcements and other grant application solicitations that require organizations to have nonprofit status will specifically so indicate in the eligibility section of the solicitation.
units.actor: Funding announcements and other grant application solicitations (DHS or grant-making entity)
units.action_summary: Explicitly indicate in the eligibility section when nonprofit status is required.

units.obligation_text: Any solicitation that requires an organization to maintain tax-exempt status will expressly state the statutory authority for requiring such status.
units.action_summary: State the statutory authority when a solicitation requires tax-exempt status.

units.obligation_text: Recipients are free to engage in explicitly religious activities.
units.action_summary: Recipients may engage in explicitly religious activities (subject to other constraints).

units.obligation_text: Such activities must be offered separately, in time or location, from the programs or services funded with direct financial assistance from DHS.
units.action_summary: Offer explicitly religious activities separately in time or location from DHS-funded programs or services.

units.obligation_text: An applicant that must show it is a nonprofit organization may do so by any of the following means:
units.action_summary: Applicants may prove nonprofit status by any of the listed methods.

units.obligation_text: Proof that the Internal Revenue Service currently recognizes the applicant as an organization to which contributions are tax deductible under section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code;
units.action_summary: Provide proof of IRS 501(c)(3) recognition as a means of demonstrating nonprofit status.

units.obligation_text: A statement from a State or other governmental taxing body or the State secretary of State certifying that: (1) The organization is a nonprofit organization operating within the State; and (2) No part of its net earnings may benefit any private shareholder or individual;
units.action_summary: Provide a state or taxing-body certification that the organization is a nonprofit and no earnings benefit private individuals.

units.obligation_text: The organization is a nonprofit organization operating within the State;
units.actor: State or other governmental taxing body (as certifier)
units.action_summary: Certification must state the organization operates as a nonprofit within the State.
units.modal_raw: shall be certified / is to be certified

units.obligation_text: No part of its net earnings may benefit any private shareholder or individual;
units.actor: State or other governmental taxing body (as certifier)
units.action_summary: Certification must state that no net earnings benefit private shareholders or individuals.
units.modal_raw: shall be certified / is to be certified

units.obligation_text: A certified copy of the applicant’s certificate of incorporation or similar document that clearly establishes the nonprofit status of the applicant;
units.action_summary: Provide a certified copy of the certificate of incorporation or similar document to demonstrate nonprofit status.

units.obligation_text: Any item described in paragraphs (a) through (c) of this section if that item applies to a State or national parent organization, together with a statement by the State or parent organization that the applicant is a local nonprofit affiliate;
units.actor: Applicant (by providing parent organization documents and statement)
units.action_summary: Provide documentation for a parent organization plus a statement that the applicant is a local nonprofit affiliate.

units.obligation_text: For an entity that holds a sincerely-held religious belief that it cannot apply for a determination as an entity that is tax-exempt under section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code, evidence sufficient to establish that the entity would otherwise qualify as a nonprofit organization under paragraphs (a) through (d) of this section.
units.actor: Applicant that holds a sincerely-held religious belief preventing 501(c)(3) application
units.action_summary: Provide other evidence sufficient to establish that the entity would otherwise qualify as a nonprofit.

units.obligation_text: A faith-based organization that applies for, or participates in, a social service program supported with Federal financial assistance will retain its autonomy; right of expression; religious character; authority over its governance; and independence from Federal, State, and local governments;
units.actor: Faith-based organization that applies for or participates in DHS-supported social service programs
units.action_summary: Retain autonomy, right of expression, religious character, governance authority, and independence from government.

units.obligation_text: A faith-based organization ... may continue to carry out its mission, including the definition, development, practice, and expression of its religious beliefs, provided that it does not use direct Federal financial assistance contrary to § 19.4.
units.actor: Faith-based organization that applies for or participates in DHS-supported social service programs
units.action_summary: May continue to carry out its religious mission, subject to the condition that it does not use DHS direct assistance in ways contrary to §19.4.

units.obligation_text: Provided that it does not use direct Federal financial assistance contrary to § 19.4.
units.action_summary: Condition limiting the permission to continue religious mission: must not use DHS direct assistance contrary to §19.4.

units.obligation_text: Faith-based organizations may use space in their facilities to provide social services using financial assistance from DHS without removing, concealing, or altering religious articles, texts, art, or symbols.
units.actor: Faith-based organizations using DHS financial assistance
units.action_summary: May use their facilities to provide DHS-funded social services and may keep religious articles, texts, art, or symbols in those spaces.

units.obligation_text: A faith-based organization using financial assistance from DHS for social service programs retains its authority over its internal governance.
units.actor: Faith-based organization using DHS financial assistance
units.action_summary: Retain authority over internal governance while using DHS financial assistance.

units.obligation_text: It may retain religious terms in its organization's name.
units.actor: Faith-based organization using DHS financial assistance
units.action_summary: May keep religious terms in the organization's name.

units.obligation_text: It may select its board members on the basis of their acceptance of or adherence to the religious tenets of the organization.
units.actor: Faith-based organization using DHS financial assistance
units.action_summary: May select board members based on acceptance or adherence to the organization's religious tenets.

units.obligation_text: It may include religious references in its organization's mission statements and other governing documents.
units.actor: Faith-based organization using DHS financial assistance
units.action_summary: May include religious references in mission statements and governing documents.

units.obligation_text: Neither DHS nor any State or local government or other intermediary receiving funds under any DHS social service program shall construe these provisions in such a way as to advantage or disadvantage faith-based organizations affiliated with historic or well-established religions or sects in comparison with other religions or sects.
units.actor: DHS and any State or local government or other intermediary receiving funds under any DHS social service program
units.action_summary: May not interpret these provisions so as to advantage or disadvantage faith-based organizations affiliated with historic or well-established religions compared to other religions or sects.

units.obligation_text: Faith-based organizations may apply for this award on the same basis as any other organization, as set forth at and subject to the protections and requirements of part 19 of Title 6 of the CFR and 42 U.S.C. 2000bb et seq.
units.action_summary: May apply for awards on the same basis as any other organization, subject to part 19 protections and requirements.

units.obligation_text: DHS will not, in the selection of recipients, discriminate against an organization on the basis of the organization's religious exercise or affiliation.
units.action_summary: May not discriminate in recipient selection on the basis of religious exercise or affiliation.

units.obligation_text: A faith-based organization that participates in this program will retain its independence from the government
units.actor: Faith-based organization participating in the program
units.action_summary: Retain independence from the government while participating in the program.

units.obligation_text: A faith-based organization ... may continue to carry out its mission consistent with religious freedom protections in federal law.
units.actor: Faith-based organization participating in the program
units.action_summary: May continue to carry out its religious mission consistent with federal religious freedom protections.

units.obligation_text: Religious accommodations may also be sought under many of these religious freedom protection laws.
units.action_summary: May seek religious accommodations under applicable religious freedom laws.

units.obligation_text: A faith-based organization may not use direct financial assistance from DHS to support or engage in any explicitly religious activities except where consistent with the Establishment Clause and any other applicable requirements.
units.actor: Faith-based organization receiving DHS direct financial assistance
units.action_summary: May not use DHS direct funds to support explicitly religious activities, except to the extent allowed by the Establishment Clause and other applicable requirements.

units.obligation_text: Exception: where consistent with the Establishment Clause and any other applicable requirements.
units.action_summary: Exception allowing use of funds for explicitly religious activities if consistent with the Establishment Clause and other applicable requirements.

units.obligation_text: Such an organization also may not, in providing services funded by DHS, discriminate against a program beneficiary or prospective program beneficiary on the basis of religion, a religious belief, a refusal to hold a religious belief, or a refusal to attend or participate in a religious practice.
units.actor: Faith-based organization providing services funded by DHS
units.action_summary: May not discriminate against program beneficiaries or prospective beneficiaries on the basis of religion, religious belief, or refusal to participate in religious practice.

title: Privacy Act of 1974

units.obligation_text: An individual may make a request for access to a Department of Homeland Security record about that individual covered by a DHS or Component system of records notice (SORN) by writing directly to the Department component that maintains the record at the address listed in appendix A to this part or via the internet at http://www.dhs.gov/dhs-foia-request-submission-form.
units.action_summary: Requesters may submit Privacy Act access requests by writing to the DHS component maintaining the record or via the specified internet form.

units.obligation_text: The head of a component or designee thereof is authorized to make written requests under subsection (b)(7) of the Privacy Act for records maintained by other agencies that are necessary to carry out an authorized law enforcement activity.
units.actor: the head of a component or the component head's designee
units.action_summary: Component heads/designees may request records from other agencies for authorized law enforcement purposes.

units.obligation_text: When applying the (b)(1) exception for authorized disclosures within an agency on a need to know basis, the Department will consider itself a single entity, meaning that information may be disclosed between components of the Department under the (b)(1) exception.
units.action_summary: Information may be disclosed between DHS components under the (b)(1) exception because DHS will treat itself as a single entity.

units.obligation_text: All agencies and components under the Department will retain the necessary authority from their original purpose in order to conduct these necessary activities.
units.actor: all agencies and components under the Department
units.action_summary: Components must retain their original authorities to conduct necessary Privacy Act activities during the transition period.

units.obligation_text: If records are held by a field office of U.S. Customs and Border Protection, the U.S. Coast Guard, or other Department components with field offices other than the U.S. Secret Service, the requester must write directly to that U.S. Customs and Border Protection, Coast Guard, or other field office address, which can be found by calling the component’s central FOIA office.
units.action_summary: Requesters must send requests directly to the relevant field office address when records are held by component field offices.

units.obligation_text: Requests for records held by the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) should be sent to the DHS Privacy Office.
units.action_summary: Requesters are advised to send CISA-held records requests to the DHS Privacy Office.

units.obligation_text: DHS and components will ordinarily use the most efficient and least expensive method for processing requested records.
units.action_summary: DHS/components must normally use the most efficient and least costly method to process record requests.

units.obligation_text: DHS ordinarily will collect all applicable fees before sending copies of records to a requester.
units.action_summary: DHS will usually require payment of applicable fees before providing copies of records.

units.obligation_text: When an individual makes a request for access to records about that individual, he or she must verify his or her identity.
units.action_summary: Requesters must verify their identity when seeking access to their records.

units.obligation_text: The individual must state his or her full name, current address, date and place of birth, and country of citizenship or residency.
units.action_summary: Requesters must provide full name, address, birth details, and citizenship/residency as part of identity verification.

units.obligation_text: The individual must sign his or her request and provide a signature that must either be notarized or submitted by the requester under 28 U.S.C. 1746.
units.action_summary: Requesters must sign their request and provide a notarized signature or a signature under 28 U.S.C. 1746.

units.obligation_text: If a third party requests records about a subject individual, the third party requester must provide verification of the subject individual’s identity in the manner provided in paragraph (e) along with the subject individual’s written consent authorizing disclosure of the records to the third party requester, or by submitting proof by the requester that the subject individual is deceased.
units.action_summary: Third-party requesters must verify the subject's identity and provide consent or proof of death to obtain records.

units.obligation_text: As an exercise of its administrative discretion, each component can require a third-party requester to supply additional information to verify that the subject individual has consented to disclosure or is deceased.
units.action_summary: Components may require extra verification from third-party requesters to confirm consent or death.

units.obligation_text: DHS and components shall charge for processing requests under the Privacy Act or JRA.
units.action_summary: DHS and its components must charge fees to process Privacy Act or JRA requests.

units.obligation_text: An individual may also send a request to the Privacy Office, Mail Stop 0655, U.S. Department of Homeland Security ... or via the internet at http://www.dhs.gov/dhs-foia-request-submission-form, or via fax to (202) 343–4011.
units.action_summary: Individuals may submit requests to the DHS Privacy Office by mail, online form, or fax.

units.obligation_text: The Privacy Office will forward the request to the component(s) that it determines to be most likely to maintain the records that are sought.
units.action_summary: The DHS Privacy Office must forward forwarded requests to the component(s) most likely to have the records.

units.obligation_text: The component that first receives a request for access to a record, and has possession of that record, is the component responsible for responding to the request.
units.actor: the component that first receives and possesses the record
units.action_summary: The component that first receives and possesses the record must respond to the access request.

units.obligation_text: If any other date is used, the component will inform the requester of that date.
units.action_summary: If a component uses a date other than when it began its search, it must inform the requester of that alternate date.

units.obligation_text: DHS may at its discretion either administratively close the request or seek additional information from the requester.
units.action_summary: DHS may either administratively close a request or ask the requester for additional information at its discretion.

units.obligation_text: A component making an adverse determination denying a request for access in any respect will notify the requester of that determination in writing.
units.actor: the component making an adverse determination
units.action_summary: If a component denies an access request (in whole or in part), it must notify the requester in writing.

units.obligation_text: The denial letter will be signed by the head of the first component or agency, not any later component, or the component head’s designee, and will include: (1) The name and title or position of the person responsible for the denial; (2) A brief statement of the reason(s) for the denial, including any Privacy Act exemption(s) applied by the component in denying the request; and (3) A statement that the denial may be appealed under 6 CFR 5.25(a) and a description of the requirements of 6 CFR 5.25(a).
units.action_summary: Denial letters must be signed by the appropriate component head/designee and must include the responsible person's identity, reasons/exemptions, and appeal instructions.

units.obligation_text: Whenever a component refers all or any part of the responsibility for responding to a request to another component or agency, it ordinarily will notify the requester of the referral and inform the requester of the name of each component or agency to which the request has been referred and of the part of the request that has been referred.
units.action_summary: If a component refers a request (or part of it) to another component/agency, it must notify the requester of the referral and identify where it was sent and which parts were referred.

units.obligation_text: All consultations, coordination, and referrals received by DHS will be handled according to the date the Privacy Act or JRA access request was initially received by the first component.
units.action_summary: Consultations and referrals must be processed based on the date the first component initially received the access request.

units.obligation_text: Components may establish agreements with other components or agencies to eliminate the need for consultations or referrals with respect to types of records.
units.action_summary: Components are permitted to make agreements to avoid consultations/referrals for certain record types.

units.obligation_text: Components should, to the extent practicable, communicate with requesters having access to the internet using electronic means, such as email or web portal.
units.action_summary: Components are advised to use electronic communication with internet-capable requesters when practicable.

units.obligation_text: A component will acknowledge the request and assign it an individualized tracking number if it will take longer than ten (10) working days to process.
units.action_summary: If processing will exceed 10 working days, the component must acknowledge the request and assign a tracking number.

units.obligation_text: Components will include in the acknowledgement a brief description of the records sought to allow requesters to more easily keep track of their requests.
units.action_summary: Acknowledgements must include a brief description of the records sought.

units.obligation_text: In the acknowledgment letter, the component will confirm the requester’s agreement to pay fees under 6 CFR 5.21(d) and 5.29.
units.action_summary: Acknowledgement letters must confirm the requester's agreement to pay applicable fees.

units.obligation_text: A component will have twenty (20) working days from when a request is received to determine whether to grant or deny the request unless there are unusual or exceptional circumstances as defined by the FOIA and set out in 6 CFR 5.5(c).
units.action_summary: Components generally must decide to grant or deny requests within 20 working days unless FOIA-specified exceptions apply.

units.obligation_text: Once a component decides to grant a request for access to record(s) in whole or in part, it will notify the requester in writing.
units.action_summary: If a request is granted (in whole or part), the component must notify the requester in writing.

units.obligation_text: The component will inform the requester of the availability of its FOIA Public Liaison to offer assistance.
units.action_summary: Components must inform requesters about FOIA Public Liaison availability to assist.

units.obligation_text: On receipt of any request involving classified information, the component will determine whether information is currently and properly classified and take appropriate action to ensure compliance with 6 CFR part 7.
units.action_summary: Components must determine classification status and take actions to ensure compliance with part 7 when requests involve classified information.

units.obligation_text: Whenever a record contains information that has been derivatively classified by a component or agency because it contains information classified by another component or agency, the component will consult the component or agency that classified the underlying information.
units.actor: the component that received the request
units.action_summary: If records include derivatively classified information, the receiving component must consult the agency/component that originally classified the underlying information.

units.obligation_text: Information determined to no longer require classification will not be withheld from a requester based on exemption (k)(1) of the Privacy Act.
units.action_summary: Components cannot withhold information no longer requiring classification based on Privacy Act exemption (k)(1).

units.obligation_text: On receipt of any appeal involving classified information, the DHS Office of the General Counsel or its designee, shall take appropriate action to ensure compliance with part 7 of this title.
units.actor: DHS Office of the General Counsel or its designee
units.action_summary: The DHS OGC (or designee) must take actions to ensure part 7 compliance when appeals involve classified information.

units.obligation_text: An individual may appeal an adverse determination denying his or her request for access in any respect to the appropriate component Appeals Officer.
units.action_summary: Requesters may appeal adverse determinations to the component Appeals Officer.

units.obligation_text: An appeal must be in writing, and to be considered timely it must be postmarked or, in the case of electronic submissions, transmitted to the Appeals Officer within 90 working days.
units.action_summary: Appeals must be written and submitted within 90 working days (postmark or electronic transmission) to be timely.

units.obligation_text: The DHS Office of the General Counsel or its designee is the authorized appeals authority for DHS.
units.actor: DHS Office of the General Counsel or its designee
units.action_summary: The DHS OGC (or designee) serves as DHS's authorized appeals authority.

units.obligation_text: On receipt of any appeal involving classified information, the Appeals Officer will consult with the Chief Security Officer and take appropriate action to ensure compliance with 6 CFR part 7.
units.action_summary: Appeals Officers must consult the Chief Security Officer and ensure part 7 compliance on appeals involving classified information.

units.obligation_text: The decision on an appeal will be made in writing generally twenty (20) working days after receipt.
units.actor: the Appeals Officer / DHS Office of the General Counsel or its designee
units.action_summary: Appeals decisions must generally be issued in writing within 20 working days of receipt.

units.obligation_text: If an individual wishes to seek review by a court of any adverse determination or denial of a request by DHS ... that individual must first appeal it under this subpart.
units.action_summary: Individuals must first exhaust administrative appeals under this subpart before seeking court review.

units.obligation_text: Unless the record is not subject to amendment or correction as stated in paragraph (f) of this section, an individual may make a request for amendment or correction of a record of the Department about that individual by writing directly to the component that maintains the record, following the procedures in section 5.21.
units.action_summary: Individuals may request amendment or correction of their records by writing to the component that maintains the record, per §5.21 procedures.

units.obligation_text: Within ten working days of receiving a request for amendment or correction of records, a component will send the requester a written acknowledgment of its receipt of the request.
units.action_summary: Components must acknowledge receipt of amendment/correction requests in writing within ten working days.

units.obligation_text: The component will request additional information if an outstanding fee has not been paid; the request will be considered not to have been received until the outstanding fee has been paid in full to the agency.
units.action_summary: If fees are outstanding, the component will request additional information and will treat the amendment request as not received until fees are paid.

units.obligation_text: A requester may appeal a denial of a request for an amendment or correction to the Component Appeals Officer or the DHS Office of the General Counsel or its designee in the same manner as a denial of a request for access to records (see § 5.25 of this part) and the same procedures will be followed.
units.action_summary: Requesters may appeal amendment/correction denials to the component Appeals Officer or DHS OGC and the access-appeal procedures apply.

units.obligation_text: If an individual’s appeal under this section is denied in whole or in part, that individual has the right to file a Statement of Disagreement, unless exempt, that states his or her reason(s) for disagreeing with the Department’s denial of his or her request for amendment or correction.
units.action_summary: If an amendment/correction appeal is denied, the individual may file a Statement of Disagreement stating reasons for disagreement.

units.obligation_text: Statements of Disagreement must be concise, must clearly identify each part of any record that is disputed, and should be no longer than one typed page for each fact disputed.
units.actor: the individual filing the Statement of Disagreement
units.action_summary: Statements of Disagreement must be concise, identify disputed record parts, and generally be limited to one typed page per disputed fact.

units.obligation_text: The individual’s Statement of Disagreement must be sent to the component involved, which will place it in the system of records in which the disputed record is maintained and will mark the disputed record to indicate that a Statement of Disagreement has been filed and where in the system of records it may be found.
units.action_summary: Individuals must send the Statement to the component; the component must place and mark the disputed record and note where the Statement is located.

units.obligation_text: Within 30 working days of the amendment or correction of a record, the component that maintains the record will, unless exempt, notify all persons, organizations, or agencies to which it previously disclosed the record, if an accounting of that disclosure was made or should have been made, that the record has been amended or corrected.
units.actor: the component that maintains the record
units.action_summary: Components must notify prior recipients (where an accounting was/should have been made) within 30 working days when a record is amended or corrected, unless exempt.

units.obligation_text: If an individual has filed a Statement of Disagreement, the component will append a copy of it to the disputed record whenever the record is disclosed and may also append a concise statement of its reason(s) for denying the request to amend or correct the record.
units.action_summary: If a Statement of Disagreement exists, components must append it to the disputed record on disclosure and may append their concise rationale for denial.

units.obligation_text: The following records are not subject to amendment or correction: (1) Transcripts of testimony given under oath or written statements made under oath; (2) Transcripts of grand jury proceedings, judicial proceedings, or quasi-judicial proceedings, which are the official record of those proceedings; (3) Presentence records that originated with the courts; and (4) Records in systems of records that have been exempted from amendment and correction under the Privacy Act (5 U.S.C. 552a(j) or (k)) pursuant to a Final Rule published in the Federal Register.
units.action_summary: Certain categories of records (oath transcripts, official court/grand jury transcripts, presentence court records, and records in exempted systems) cannot be amended or corrected.

units.obligation_text: An individual may make a request for an accounting of any disclosure that has been made by the Department to another person, organization, or agency of any record about the requester, except to the extent the records are covered by the JRA.
units.action_summary: Individuals may request an accounting of departmental disclosures of their records, subject to JRA limitations.

units.obligation_text: Components are not required to provide accountings to the requester where they relate to: (1) Disclosures for which accountings are, by statute (5 U.S.C. 552a(c)(1)), not required to be kept, such as disclosures that are made to officers and employees within the agency and disclosures that are required to be made under the FOIA; (2) Disclosures made to law enforcement agencies for authorized law enforcement activities in response to written requests from those law enforcement agencies specifying the law enforcement activities for which the disclosures are sought; or (3) Disclosures made from systems of records that have been exempted from accounting requirements by a rulemaking pursuant to 5 U.S.C. 552a(j) or (k).
units.action_summary: Components need not provide accountings in specified situations: certain statutory exceptions, law enforcement requests, or records in systems exempted from accounting requirements.

units.obligation_text: Each component will preserve all correspondence pertaining to the requests that it receives under this subpart, as well as copies of all requested records, until disposition or destruction is authorized by title 44 of the United States Code or the National Archives and Records Administration’s General Records Schedule 4.2.
units.action_summary: Components must preserve request-related correspondence and copies of requested records until official disposition/destruction is authorized.

units.obligation_text: Records will not be disposed of while they are the subject of a pending request, appeal, lawsuit, or litigation or audit hold under the Act.
units.action_summary: Components must not dispose of records that are the subject of pending requests, appeals, litigation, or audit holds.

units.obligation_text: Fees for access requests granted in full under the Privacy Act are limited to duplication fees.
units.action_summary: When access requests are granted in full under the Privacy Act, fees charged may be limited only to duplication costs.

title: Critical Electric Infrastructure Information: Administrative Procedures

units.obligation_text: The Secretary has the authority to designate information as CEII, in accordance with FPA section 215A.
units.action_summary: Secretary may designate information as CEII under FPA §215A.

units.obligation_text: The Secretary may delegate the authority to designate information as CEII to any DOE Office.
units.action_summary: Secretary may delegate CEII designation authority to any DOE Office.

units.obligation_text: The DOE CEII Coordinator shall be the primary point of contact for the submission of all requests for designation of information as CEII by DOE, as well as for requests made to DOE by organizations or individuals for information that may be protected, in whole or in part, as CEII.
units.action_summary: CEII Coordinator must serve as the primary contact for CEII designation submissions and related requests.

units.obligation_text: The CEII Coordinator or Coordinator’s designee shall:
units.actor: The CEII Coordinator or Coordinator’s designee
units.action_summary: Establish delegated duties to be performed by the CEII Coordinator or designee (see sub-items).

units.obligation_text: Receive and review all incoming requests for CEII as defined in § 1004.13(c) and in accordance with § 1004.13(g);
units.actor: The CEII Coordinator or Coordinator’s designee
units.action_summary: Receive and review all incoming CEII designation requests.

units.obligation_text: Make initial determinations as to whether particular information fits within the definition of CEII found at § 1004.13(c), including but not limited to those considerations related to pre-designation of information related to Defense Critical Electric Infrastructure as defined in § 1004.13(c), NTIA-managed Federal agency spectrum use information, and/or accident and emergency information provided to DOE through Form OE–417;
units.actor: The CEII Coordinator or Coordinator’s designee
units.action_summary: Make initial determinations whether information meets the CEII definition, including specific categories.

units.obligation_text: Assist any DOE Offices with delegated CEII designation authority to make determinations as to whether a particular requester’s need for and ability and willingness to protect CEII warrants limited disclosure of the information to the requester;
units.actor: The CEII Coordinator or Coordinator’s designee
units.action_summary: Assist DOE Offices in assessing whether to disclose CEII to requesters based on need and protective ability.

units.obligation_text: Establish reasonable conditions for considering requests for release of CEII-designated material in accordance with § 1004.13(g)(5) through (6);
units.actor: The CEII Coordinator or Coordinator’s designee
units.action_summary: Set reasonable conditions for considering release requests for CEII-designated material.

units.obligation_text: Make the Department’s final determination regarding request by any non-Federal entity (organization or individual) for CEII-designated materials, in consultation with the appropriate DOE Office(s);
units.actor: The CEII Coordinator or Coordinator’s designee
units.action_summary: Make final determinations on non-Federal entity requests for CEII materials, consulting appropriate DOE Offices.

units.obligation_text: Notify a CEII submitter of a request for such information by a non-Federal entity;
units.actor: The CEII Coordinator or Coordinator’s designee
units.action_summary: Notify CEII submitter when a non-Federal entity requests their CEII.

units.obligation_text: Convene a conference call within no more than five (5) business days between an affected DOE Office and a CEII submitter to discuss concerns related to a non-Federal entity requesting release of CEII;
units.actor: The CEII Coordinator or Coordinator’s designee
units.action_summary: Within 5 business days convene a call between affected DOE Office and submitter to discuss release concerns.

units.obligation_text: Perform oversight of the DOE CEII program and establish guidance for the treatment, handling, and storage of all CEII materials in the Department in accordance with § 1004.13(g)(6), including those related to CEII international sharing protocols.
units.actor: The CEII Coordinator or Coordinator’s designee
units.action_summary: Oversee DOE CEII program and set guidance for treatment, handling, storage, and international sharing protocols as applicable.

units.obligation_text: DOE Offices with delegated authority to designate CEII in accordance with § 1004.13(d), as well as any CEII Coordinator designee(s) from the Bonneville Power Administration, the Energy Information Administration, the Southeastern Power Administration, the Southwestern Power Administration, and the Western Area Power Administration, will meet regularly, at the discretion of the CEII Coordinator, but not less than once per year, to ensure coordinated implementation of DOE’s CEII designation authority.
units.actor: DOE Offices with delegated CEII designation authority and CEII Coordinator designees
units.action_summary: These DOE Offices/designees must meet regularly, at least annually, to coordinate CEII designation implementation.

units.obligation_text: DOE, at the discretion of the CEII Coordinator, shall meet with representatives from FERC semi-annually (or more often, as necessary) to ensure that both agencies are applying CEII designation criteria consistently and to share best practices.
units.actor: DOE (at the discretion of the CEII Coordinator)
units.action_summary: DOE must meet with FERC semi-annually (or more often) to align CEII designation criteria and share best practices.

units.obligation_text: DOE, at the discretion of the CEII Coordinator, shall meet annually with representatives from Department of Commerce, NTIA, or other Federal agencies, as needed, to ensure shared understanding and consistent communication among Federal agencies that collect, maintain and potentially release information that DOE may consider designating as CEII as defined in § 1004.13(c).
units.actor: DOE (at the discretion of the CEII Coordinator)
units.action_summary: DOE must meet annually with Commerce, NTIA, or other agencies as needed to ensure consistent CEII understanding and communication.

units.obligation_text: Any person or entity requesting that information submitted to DOE be designated as CEII must submit such request to the DOE CEII Coordinator or Coordinator’s designee according to the following procedures:
units.actor: Any person or entity requesting CEII designation for information submitted to DOE
units.action_summary: Requesters of CEII designation for information submitted to DOE must submit their requests to the CEII Coordinator or designee following specified procedures.

units.obligation_text: The submitter must clearly label the cover page and pages or portions of the information for which CEII treatment is requested in bold, capital lettering, indicating that it contains CEII, as appropriate, and marked "CEII—DO NOT RELEASE."
units.actor: The submitter (person or entity requesting CEII designation)
units.action_summary: Submitter must label CEII portions prominently and mark them 'CEII—DO NOT RELEASE.'

units.obligation_text: The submitter must also clearly indicate the DOE Office(s) from which the CEII designation is being requested in bold, capital lettering on the cover page.
units.action_summary: Submitter must indicate on the cover page the DOE Office(s) from which CEII designation is requested.

units.obligation_text: The submitter must also segregate those portions of the information that contain CEII (or information that reasonably could be expected to lead to the disclosure of the CEII) wherever feasible.
units.action_summary: Submitter must segregate CEII portions of the submission where feasible.

units.obligation_text: The submitter must submit a public version of the information where information designated CEII and information for which CEII designation is requested is redacted or otherwise protected through extraction from the non-CEII to the DOE CEII Coordinator and the Coordinator’s designee in an appropriate DOE Office.
units.action_summary: Submitter must provide a public (redacted) version of materials to the CEII Coordinator and designee.

units.obligation_text: Any DOE employees, DOE contractors, or agents of DOE requesting that information generated by the Department be designated as CEII must submit such request to the DOE CEII Coordinator and the Coordinator’s designee in an appropriate DOE Office according to the following procedures:
units.actor: DOE employees, DOE contractors, or agents of DOE
units.action_summary: DOE personnel/contractors/agents requesting CEII designation for DOE-generated information must submit requests to the CEII Coordinator/designee following specified procedures.

units.obligation_text: The submitter must clearly label the cover page and pages or portions of the information for which CEII treatment is requested in bold, capital lettering, indicating that it contains CEII, as appropriate, and marked "CEII—DO NOT RELEASE."
units.action_summary: DOE submitter must label DOE-generated CEII portions and mark them 'CEII—DO NOT RELEASE.'

units.obligation_text: The submitter must also segregate those portions of the information that contain CEII (or information that reasonably could be expected to lead to the disclosure of the CEII) wherever feasible.
units.action_summary: DOE submitter must segregate CEII portions wherever feasible.

units.obligation_text: The submitter must submit to DOE a public version of the information where information designated CEII and information for which CEII designation is requested is redacted or otherwise protected through extraction from non-CEII to the DOE CEII Coordinator and Coordinator’s designee.
units.action_summary: DOE submitter must provide a public/redacted version of DOE-generated information to CEII Coordinator/designee.

units.obligation_text: CEII designation for information generated by DOE, to include, all organizational entities that are a part of the Executive Department created by Title II of the DOE Organization Act, may be executed at any time, regardless of when such information was generated.
units.action_summary: DOE may designate internally-generated information as CEII at any time, regardless of when it was created.

units.obligation_text: Upon receiving a request for CEII designation of information submitted to DOE, the DOE CEII Coordinator or Coordinator’s designee shall review the submission made in accordance with § 1004.13(g)(2) for information about "Defense Critical Electric Infrastructure," as defined by section 215A(a)(4) of the FPA; information on electric incidents and emergencies reported to DOE through Form OE–417; and/or Federal spectrum information managed by the NTIA, for immediate pre-designation as CEII. If the CEII Coordinator determines that the information submitted does not qualify for immediate pre-designation, such information shall be evaluated for designation as CEII under this part.
units.actor: The DOE CEII Coordinator or Coordinator’s designee
units.action_summary: Upon receipt of a CEII designation request, CEII Coordinator/designee must review submission for immediate pre-designation for specified categories; if not, evaluate under the part.

units.obligation_text: Information for which CEII treatment is requested will be maintained by the CEII Coordinator or Coordinator’s designee in DOE’s files as non-public unless and until DOE completes its determination that the information is not entitled to CEII treatment. The interim treatment of the information as CEII does not mean that DOE has made a determination regarding CEII designation. DOE will endeavor to make a determination as soon as practicable. The Department retains the right to make determinations about any request for CEII designation at any time, including the removal of a previously granted CEII designation.
units.actor: The CEII Coordinator or Coordinator’s designee; DOE
units.action_summary: Submissions for CEII will be kept non-public while DOE determines designation; DOE will endeavor to decide promptly and retains authority to determine or remove CEII at any time.
units.modal_raw: will (will be maintained / will endeavor / retains the right)

units.obligation_text: When a requester seeks information for which CEII status has been requested but not designated, or when DOE itself is considering release of such information, DOE will render a decision on designation before responding to the requester or releasing such information.
units.action_summary: DOE must decide designation status before responding to requests or releasing information that has pending CEII status.

units.obligation_text: The DOE CEII Coordinator, or a Coordinator’s designee, will execute the Department’s evaluation as to whether the submitted information or portions of the information meets the definition of CEII, as described at section (c)(2) of this Part, with the appropriate DOE Office with delegated CEII designation authority.
units.actor: The DOE CEII Coordinator or Coordinator’s designee
units.action_summary: CEII Coordinator/designee will carry out evaluation with appropriate DOE Office to determine whether submitted information meets CEII definition.

units.obligation_text: The Secretary or delegated DOE Office will make a determination regarding CEII designation after considering the information against the criteria for CEII designation.
units.actor: The Secretary or delegated DOE Office
units.action_summary: Secretary or delegated DOE Office will decide whether submitted information qualifies as CEII based on criteria.

units.obligation_text: Upon making the determination, the DOE CEII Coordinator or Coordinator’s designee shall communicate the decision to the submitter.
units.actor: The DOE CEII Coordinator or Coordinator’s designee
units.action_summary: After determination, CEII Coordinator/designee must notify the submitter of the decision.

units.obligation_text: DOE reserves the right to review at any time information designated by DOE as CEII to determine whether the information is properly designated.
units.action_summary: DOE may review CEII designations at any time to check appropriateness.

units.obligation_text: The designation of information as CEII, or the removal of such designation, must be reviewed when: A FOIA request is submitted for the information under section 1004.10,
units.action_summary: DOE must review CEII designation when a FOIA request for that information is submitted.

units.obligation_text: The designation of information as CEII, or the removal of such designation, must be reviewed when: A request is made for reconsideration of the designation or removal of the designation under § 1004.13(i)(1).
units.action_summary: DOE must review CEII designation when a reconsideration request is made under §1004.13(i)(1).

units.obligation_text: If the submitter voluntarily provided the information to DOE, at the request of the submitter, DOE will return or destroy information for which CEII designation was requested but not granted, and will attempt to remove all copies of such information from DOE files, both physical and electronic.
units.action_summary: If submitter voluntarily provided info and designation not granted, DOE will return/destroy it and attempt to remove copies from files upon request.

units.obligation_text: DOE shall not remove electronic files in the ordinary course of business.
units.action_summary: DOE must not remove electronic files in ordinary business operations.

units.obligation_text: If a submitter is required to provide information and DOE denies CEII designation, the submitter may file a request for review under the procedures.
units.action_summary: A required submitter may request review if DOE denies CEII designation.

units.obligation_text: All information designated by DOE as CEII, whether submitted to or generated by DOE, shall be clearly labeled as such, and shall include the date on which the information was designated as CEII.
units.actor: Information designated by DOE as CEII / DOE
units.action_summary: All CEII must be clearly labeled and include the date of designation.

units.obligation_text: For information that meets the definition of CEII but cannot be physically labeled, such as electronic information, the information shall be stored in a secure electronic environment that identifies the stored information as CEII.
units.action_summary: CEII that cannot be physically labeled must be stored in secure electronic environments identified as CEII.

units.obligation_text: All information designated by DOE as CEII: (A) Shall be exempt from disclosure under the FOIA exemption codified at 5 U.S.C. 552(b)(3);
units.actor: Information designated by DOE as CEII / DOE
units.action_summary: CEII is exempt from disclosure under FOIA exemption (b)(3).

units.obligation_text: All information designated by DOE as CEII: (B) Shall not be made available by any Federal, State, political subdivision or tribal authority under any Federal, State, political subdivision or tribal law requiring public disclosure of information or records, in accordance with FPA section 215A(d)(1).
units.actor: All Federal, State, political subdivision or tribal authorities; DOE
units.action_summary: CEII must not be disclosed under laws requiring public disclosure by Federal, State, local, or tribal authorities.

units.obligation_text: Secure Storage. DOE will store information for which CEII treatment is requested in a secure place in a manner that would prevent unauthorized access.
units.action_summary: DOE must store requested-CEII information securely to prevent unauthorized access.

units.obligation_text: Designation of information as CEII may last up to a five-year period, unless re-designated.
units.action_summary: CEII designations may remain in effect up to five years unless redesignated.

units.obligation_text: The Secretary or delegated DOE Office will determine the duration of designation at the time of designation.
units.actor: The Secretary or delegated DOE Office
units.action_summary: The Secretary or delegated office must decide how long CEII designation will last when designating.

units.obligation_text: A submitter may re-apply for CEII designation no earlier than one year prior to the date of expiration of the prior designation or re-designation in accordance with the application procedures in § 1004.13(g)(1).
units.action_summary: A submitter may re-apply for CEII designation starting one year before expiration using specified procedures.

units.obligation_text: The designation of information as CEII may be removed at any time, by the Secretary or the DOE CEII Coordinator in consultation with the DOE Office to which the Secretary has delegated the authority, in whole or in part, upon determination that the unauthorized disclosure of such information could no longer be used to impair the security or reliability of the bulk-power system or distribution facilities or any other form of energy infrastructure.
units.actor: The Secretary or the DOE CEII Coordinator (in consultation with delegated DOE Office)
units.action_summary: Secretary or CEII Coordinator may remove CEII designation any time if disclosure would no longer impair infrastructure security or reliability.

units.obligation_text: If the CEII designation is to be removed, the submitter and the DOE Office that produced or maintains the CEII will receive notice and an opportunity to comment.
units.actor: The CEII Coordinator or Coordinator’s designee (acting for DOE)
units.action_summary: If DOE intends to remove CEII designation, submitter and maintaining DOE Office must be notified and given opportunity to comment.

units.obligation_text: The CEII Coordinator or Coordinator’s designee will notify the submitter and the DOE Office that produced or maintains the CEII, and will give the submitter an opportunity (at least ten (10) business days) in which to comment in writing prior to the removal of the designation.
units.actor: The CEII Coordinator or Coordinator’s designee
units.action_summary: CEII Coordinator/designee must notify submitter and DOE Office and give at least 10 business days to comment in writing before removal.

units.obligation_text: The CEII Coordinator or Coordinator’s designee will provide notice of a removal decision to any submitter claiming that the information is CEII no less than twenty (20) business days before disclosure.
units.actor: The CEII Coordinator or Coordinator’s designee
units.action_summary: CEII Coordinator/designee must give at least 20 business days' notice to submitter before disclosing information for which removal decision was made.

units.obligation_text: The notice will briefly explain DOE’s determination of why the submitter’s objections do not support a decision to retain the CEII designation.
units.actor: The CEII Coordinator or Coordinator’s designee
units.action_summary: Notice of removal decision must explain briefly why submitter's objections don't justify retaining CEII designation.

units.obligation_text: At the request of the submitter, DOE will return or destroy information for which CEII designation has expired or has been removed and will attempt to remove all copies of it from DOE files, both physical and electronic; however, DOE shall not remove electronic files that have been backed up in the ordinary course of business.
units.action_summary: Upon submitter request, DOE will return/destroy expired/removed CEII and try to remove copies, but will not remove routine backup electronic files.

units.obligation_text: Such backed up electronic files shall be treated as CEII until they are destroyed under the normal electronic backup retention schedules.
units.action_summary: Backed-up electronic files remain treated as CEII until destroyed per backup retention schedule.

units.obligation_text: If a FOIA request is received for the non-CEII prior to its return or destruction, DOE will work with the submitter to review whether the information is subject to other FOIA exemptions.
units.action_summary: If FOIA request arrives before return/destruction, DOE will consult submitter to assess other FOIA exemptions.

units.obligation_text: Any person who has submitted information and requested such information to be designated as CEII may request reconsideration of a DOE decision not to designate that information as CEII or to remove an existing CEII designation.
units.actor: A person who submitted information and requested CEII designation
units.action_summary: Submitter may request reconsideration of DOE decision denying CEII designation or removing designation.

units.obligation_text: Within ten (10) business days of notification by DOE of its CEII decision, the person must file a request for reconsideration.
units.action_summary: Person must file reconsideration request within 10 business days of DOE notification.

units.obligation_text: The request must be sent to the DOE CEII Coordinator and Coordinator’s designee in electronic format at: CEII COORDINATOR MAILBOX. The request must also be sent to the DOE Office that made the decision at issue and to DOE’s Office of General Counsel in Washington, DC, according to the instructions at 10 CFR 205.12.
units.action_summary: Reconsideration request must be sent electronically to CEII Coordinator/designee and also to the decision-making DOE Office and Office of General Counsel per instructions.

units.obligation_text: A statement in support of the request for reconsideration must be submitted within twenty (20) business days of the date of the determination.
units.action_summary: A supporting statement must be submitted within 20 business days of the determination.

units.obligation_text: The request and the supporting statement will be considered submitted upon receipt by the Office of General Counsel.
units.actor: Office of General Counsel / The person seeking reconsideration
units.action_summary: Reconsideration request/supporting statement are considered submitted when received by Office of General Counsel.

units.obligation_text: Any person who has received a decision denying a request for the release of CEII, in whole or in part, or a decision denying a request to change the designation of CEII, may request reconsideration of that decision. A statement in support of the request for reconsideration must be submitted to the Office of General Counsel within twenty (20) business days of the date of the determination.
units.actor: Person who received denial for release/change of designation
units.action_summary: Person may request reconsideration of denial; must submit supporting statement to Office of General Counsel within 20 business days.

units.obligation_text: The Secretary or the DOE Office that made the decision at issue will make a determination, in coordination with the DOE CEII Coordinator or Coordinator’s designee, with respect to any request for reconsideration within twenty (20) business days after the receipt of the request and will notify the person submitting the request of the determination and the availability of judicial review.
units.actor: The Secretary or the DOE Office that made the decision (in coordination with CEII Coordinator/designee)
units.action_summary: Secretary or decision-making DOE Office must decide reconsideration requests within 20 business days and notify requester, including judicial review availability.

units.obligation_text: Before seeking judicial review in Federal District Court under section 215A(d)(11) of the Federal Power Act, a person who received a determination from DOE concerning a CEII designation must first request reconsideration of that determination.
units.action_summary: Person must first request reconsideration before seeking judicial review in federal district court under FPA §215A(d)(11).

units.obligation_text: A request for reconsideration triggers a stay of the underlying decision, except in instances where voluntary sharing of the disputed information is necessary for law enforcement purposes, to ensure reliable operation or maintenance of electric or energy infrastructure, to maintain infrastructure security, to address potential threats, or to address an urgent need to disseminate the information quickly due to an emergency or other unforeseen circumstance.
units.action_summary: Filing reconsideration automatically stays the underlying decision, except in specified emergency or necessary-sharing circumstances.

units.obligation_text: Exception: voluntary sharing of the disputed information is necessary for law enforcement purposes.
units.action_summary: If voluntary sharing is necessary for law enforcement, the stay does not apply.

units.obligation_text: Exception: voluntary sharing of the disputed information is necessary to ensure reliable operation or maintenance of electric or energy infrastructure.
