units.action_summary: If voluntary sharing is necessary to ensure reliable operation/maintenance, the stay does not apply.

units.obligation_text: Exception: voluntary sharing of the disputed information is necessary to maintain infrastructure security, to address potential threats, or to address an urgent need to disseminate the information quickly due to an emergency or other unforeseen circumstance.
units.action_summary: If voluntary sharing is necessary to maintain infrastructure security or address threats/emergencies, the stay does not apply.

units.obligation_text: DOE will require those Federal entities requesting CEII to follow the procedures specified in § 1004.13(k).
units.action_summary: DOE must require Federal entities requesting CEII to follow the procedures in §1004.13(k).

units.obligation_text: DOE may share CEII with affected agencies for those agencies to carry out their specific jurisdictional responsibilities, but may impose additional restrictions on how the information may be used and maintained, if shared.
units.action_summary: DOE may share CEII with affected agencies for jurisdictional responsibilities and may impose additional use/maintenance restrictions.

units.obligation_text: The Secretary or the DOE Coordinator shall make a final determination whether to share CEII materials requested by non-Federal entities that are within the categories specified in section 215A(d)(2)(D) of the FPA.
units.actor: The Secretary or the DOE Coordinator
units.action_summary: Secretary or CEII Coordinator must decide whether to share CEII with eligible non-Federal entities within specified FPA categories.

units.obligation_text: A request by such a non-Federal entity shall not be entertained unless the requesting non-Federal entity has entered into a Non-Disclosure Agreement with DOE that ensures, at a minimum:
units.action_summary: DOE will not consider non-Federal CEII requests unless requester has executed an NDA containing minimum requirements.

units.obligation_text: Use of the information only for authorized purposes and by authorized recipients and under the conditions prescribed by the Secretary or CEII Coordinator;
units.actor: Requesting non-Federal entity (as bound by NDA)
units.action_summary: Requester must ensure information is used only for authorized purposes by authorized recipients under Secretary/Coordinator-prescribed conditions.

units.obligation_text: Protection of the information in a secure manner to prevent unauthorized access;
units.actor: Requesting non-Federal entity (as bound by NDA)
units.action_summary: Requester must protect CEII securely to prevent unauthorized access.

units.obligation_text: Destruction or return of the information after the intended purposes of receiving the information have been fulfilled;
units.actor: Requesting non-Federal entity (as bound by NDA)
units.action_summary: Requester must destroy or return CEII after intended use is complete.

units.obligation_text: Prevention of viewing or access by individuals or organizations that have been prohibited or restricted by the United States or the Department from viewing or accessing CEII;
units.actor: Requesting non-Federal entity (as bound by NDA)
units.action_summary: Requester must prevent access to CEII by persons or organizations prohibited by the U.S. or Department.

units.obligation_text: Compliance with the provisions of the Non-Disclosure Agreement, subject to DOE audit;
units.actor: Requesting non-Federal entity (as bound by NDA)
units.action_summary: Requester must comply with NDA terms and is subject to DOE audit.

units.obligation_text: No further sharing of the information without DOE’s permission.
units.actor: Requesting non-Federal entity (as bound by NDA)
units.action_summary: Requester must not share CEII further unless DOE permits it.
units.modal_raw: no further sharing without DOE's permission (prohibition/condition)

units.obligation_text: All entities receiving CEII must execute either a Non-Disclosure Agreement or an Acknowledgement and Agreement or participate in an Electric Reliability Organization or Regional Entity information sharing program that ensures the protection of CEII.
units.action_summary: Entities receiving CEII must sign an NDA/Acknowledgement or participate in an approved sharing program that protects CEII.

units.obligation_text: A copy of each agreement or program will be maintained by the DOE Office with a copy to the CEII Coordinator or the Coordinator’s designee.
units.action_summary: DOE Office must maintain a copy of each NDA/agreeing program and provide a copy to the CEII Coordinator/designee.

units.obligation_text: If DOE facilitates voluntary sharing of CEII under this subsection, DOE may impose additional restrictions on how the information may be used and maintained.
units.action_summary: If DOE facilitates voluntary CEII sharing, it may impose extra restrictions on use and maintenance.

units.obligation_text: The Secretary may delegate authority to DOE Offices to develop, after consultation with Canadian and Mexican authorities, protocols for the voluntary sharing of CEII with Canadian and Mexican authorities and owners, operators, and users of the bulk-power system outside the United States.
units.action_summary: Secretary may delegate authority for developing voluntary international CEII sharing protocols after consultation with Canada and Mexico.

units.obligation_text: The DOE CEII Coordinator or Coordinator’s designee would provide assistance and advice to DOE Offices in the development of the international sharing protocols.
units.actor: The DOE CEII Coordinator or Coordinator’s designee
units.action_summary: CEII Coordinator/designee would provide assistance and advice to DOE Offices developing international sharing protocols.

units.obligation_text: The DOE CEII Coordinator or Coordinator’s designee will provide electronic notice to the CEII submitter no less than ten (10) business days before DOE releases CEII submitted to and not generated by DOE, except in instances where voluntary sharing is necessary for law enforcement purposes, to ensure reliable operation or maintenance of electric or energy infrastructure, to maintain infrastructure security, or to address potential threats; where there is an urgent need to quickly disseminate the information; or where prior notice is not practicable due to an emergency or other unforeseen circumstance.
units.actor: The DOE CEII Coordinator or Coordinator’s designee
units.action_summary: CEII Coordinator/designee must give electronic notice to submitter at least 10 business days before releasing CEII not generated by DOE, except in specified emergency or necessary-sharing cases.

units.obligation_text: If prior notice is not given, DOE will provide notice as soon as practicable.
units.actor: DOE / The CEII Coordinator or Coordinator’s designee
units.action_summary: If prior notice cannot be provided, DOE must give notice as soon as practicable.

units.obligation_text: The DOE CEII Coordinator or Coordinator’s designee would convene a phone call, within five (5) days of electronic notice with the CEII submitter, to discuss concerns about the proposed release of CEII-designated materials to the requester.
units.actor: The DOE CEII Coordinator or Coordinator’s designee
units.action_summary: Within 5 days of electronic notice, CEII Coordinator/designee would convene a call with submitter to discuss release concerns.

units.obligation_text: DOE would make the final determination as to whether to share CEII not generated by DOE.
units.action_summary: DOE has final authority to decide whether to share CEII not generated by DOE.

units.obligation_text: Any person requesting CEII must include the following material with the request:
units.action_summary: Requesters must include specified materials with their CEII request.

units.obligation_text: Provide your name, title and employer, work address, work phone number, and work email. If you are requesting the information on behalf of a person or entity other than yourself, you must also list that person’s or entity’s work contact information, including name, title, address, phone number, and email.
units.action_summary: Requester must provide personal/work contact information and, if requesting for another, that person's/entity's contact info as well.

units.obligation_text: Provide a detailed statement explaining the particular need for and intended use of the information.
units.action_summary: Requester must provide a detailed explanation of need and intended use for the CEII.

units.obligation_text: Provide an executed Non-Disclosure Acknowledgement (if the requester is a Federal entity) or an executed Non-Disclosure Agreement (if the requester is not a Federal entity) requiring adherence to limitations on the use and disclosure of the information requested.
units.action_summary: Requester must submit an executed NDA/Acknowledgement requiring adherence to use/disclosure limits.

units.obligation_text: Upon receiving a request for CEII, the CEII Coordinator shall contact the DOE Office or Federal agency that created or maintains the CEII. In consultation with the DOE Office, the CEII Coordinator shall determine if the need for CEII and the protection afforded to the CEII should result in sharing CEII for the limited purpose made in the request. In the event the CEII Coordinator or Coordinator’s designee denies the request, the requestor may seek request for reconsideration, as provided in § 1004.13(i).
units.actor: The CEII Coordinator or Coordinator’s designee; The requester
units.action_summary: CEII Coordinator must contact maintaining office and determine whether to share CEII per request; if denied, requester may seek reconsideration under §1004.13(i).

units.obligation_text: If the submitter of information discloses to the public information that has received a CEII designation, then the Department reserves the right to remove its CEII designation.
units.action_summary: If a submitter publicly discloses CEII, DOE may remove its CEII designation.

units.obligation_text: DOE employees or contractors who knowingly or willfully disclose CEII in an unauthorized manner will be subject to appropriate sanctions, including disciplinary action under DOE or DOE Office personnel rules or referral to the DOE Inspector General.
units.action_summary: Employees/contractors who knowingly or willfully disclose CEII unauthorized face sanctions, including discipline or IG referral.

title: Elemental Mercury Storage Fees

units.obligation_text: DOE will not accept elemental mercury in environmental media or consumer products (fluorescent lamps, batteries, etc.) or elemental mercury in manufactured items (manometers, thermometers, switches, etc.).
units.action_summary: DOE is prohibited from accepting elemental mercury that is in environmental media, consumer products, or manufactured items.

units.obligation_text: The form acceptable to DOE is at least 99.5% elemental mercury by volume.
units.actor: persons delivering elemental mercury to the DOE facility
units.action_summary: Delivered elemental mercury must be at least 99.5% elemental mercury by volume to be acceptable to DOE.

units.obligation_text: Fees are payable upon delivery of elemental mercury to the DOE facility.
units.actor: persons delivering elemental mercury to the DOE facility
units.action_summary: Pay fees when delivering elemental mercury to the DOE facility.

units.obligation_text: All fee payments are to be made payable to the U.S. Department of Energy.
units.actor: persons delivering elemental mercury to the DOE facility (payers)
units.action_summary: Fee payments must be made payable to the U.S. Department of Energy.

units.obligation_text: The payments are to be made in U.S. funds by electronic funds transfer such as ACH (Automated Clearing House) using E.D.I. (Electronic Data Interchange), check, draft, money order, or credit card.
units.actor: persons delivering elemental mercury to the DOE facility (payers)
units.action_summary: Payments must be in U.S. funds and may be made by ACH (using EDI), check, draft, money order, or credit card.

units.obligation_text: Persons delivering elemental mercury to the DOE facility for long-term management and storage of elemental mercury shall pay fees in accordance with paragraph (b) of this section.
units.actor: persons delivering elemental mercury to the DOE facility
units.action_summary: Deliverers must pay fees as specified in paragraph (b).

units.obligation_text: The sum of the receiving charge, the cost of storage per metric ton for the number of years escalating costs according to the published escalation rate in storage, the cost per metric ton to transport elemental mercury to a treatment facility in the year following the number of years stored and cost per metric ton to treat and dispose of elemental mercury in the year following the number of years stored.
units.action_summary: The fee is comprised of the receiving charge, storage cost per metric ton (escalated per published rate) for the years stored, transport cost per metric ton in the year after storage, and treatment/disposal cost per metric ton in the year after storage.
units.modal_raw: shall (as the specified components of the fee)

units.obligation_text: These values may be updated annually.
units.action_summary: DOE may update the fee component values on an annual basis.

units.obligation_text: These values are posted to the DOE Long-Term Management and Storage of Elemental Mercury website (https://www.energy.gov/em/services/waste-management/waste-and-materials-disposition-information/long-term-management-and).
units.action_summary: DOE posts the fee component values to the specified DOE Long-Term Management and Storage of Elemental Mercury website.

units.obligation_text: DOE will publish notice in the Federal Register when the values are updated to inform the public of the updates.
units.action_summary: When the values are updated, DOE will publish a notice in the Federal Register to inform the public.

title: National Environmental Policy Act Implementing Procedures

units.section: Appendix B to subpart D of part 1021
units.obligation_text: Appendix B to subpart D of part 1021 is amended by: a. Revising section B5.7; and b. Removing and reserving section B5.8.
units.action_summary: DOE must amend Appendix B by revising section B5.7 and removing and reserving section B5.8.

units.obligation_text: Revising section B5.7.
units.action_summary: DOE must revise section B5.7 of Appendix B to subpart D.

units.obligation_text: Removing and reserving section B5.8.
units.action_summary: DOE must remove and reserve section B5.8 of Appendix B to subpart D.

units.obligation_text: Approvals or disapprovals of new authorizations or amendments of existing authorizations to export natural gas under section 3 of the Natural Gas Act and any associated transportation of natural gas by marine vessel.
units.action_summary: DOE may treat approvals or disapprovals of new authorizations or amendments to export natural gas under NGA section 3 and associated marine transportation as a categorical exclusion (i.e., not require further NEPA review).

units.action_summary: Specifies that approvals or disapprovals of new authorizations or amendments to existing export authorizations under NGA section 3 fall within the categorical exclusion.

units.action_summary: DOE must remove and reserve section C13 in Appendix C to subpart D of part 1021.

units.section: Appendix D to subpart D of part 1021, sections D8 and D9

title: Procedures for the Issuance of Guidance Documents

units.obligation_text: All new or revised DOE guidance documents must meet the following content requirements.
units.actor: All new or revised DOE guidance documents
units.action_summary: Guidance documents must satisfy the content requirements listed in paragraph (a).

units.obligation_text: Must comply with all relevant statutes and regulations;
units.actor: All new or revised DOE guidance documents
units.action_summary: Guidance documents must comply with all applicable statutes and regulations.

units.obligation_text: Must include a clear and prominent statement declaring that:
units.actor: All new or revised DOE guidance documents
units.action_summary: Guidance documents must include a clear prominent declaration stating the following items.

units.obligation_text: (i) The contents of the document do not have the force and effect of law and are not meant to bind the public in any way;
units.actor: All new or revised DOE guidance documents (must include statement)
units.action_summary: Include a statement that the document does not have the force of law and does not bind the public.

units.obligation_text: (ii) The document is intended only to provide clarity to the public regarding existing requirements under the law or agency policies, except as authorized by law or as incorporated into a contract;
units.actor: All new or revised DOE guidance documents (must include statement)
units.action_summary: Include a statement that the document only provides clarity about existing legal or policy requirements, unless authorized by law or in a contract.

units.obligation_text: (iii) DOE will not rely upon the document as an independent basis for an enforcement action or other administrative penalty.
units.actor: All new or revised DOE guidance documents (must include statement)
units.action_summary: Include a statement that DOE will not use the document alone as the basis for enforcement or penalties.

units.obligation_text: Must avoid using mandatory language such as 'shall,' 'must,' 'required,' or 'requirement,' unless the language is describing an established statutory or regulatory requirement, or is directed solely to DOE personnel and is not intended to have a substantial future effect on the behavior of regulated parties;
units.actor: All new or revised DOE guidance documents
units.action_summary: Guidance documents should not use mandatory wording except in specified circumstances.

units.obligation_text: Unless the language is describing an established statutory or regulatory requirement, or is directed solely to DOE personnel and is not intended to have a substantial future effect on the behavior of regulated parties.
units.action_summary: Exception permitting mandatory language when describing established statutory/regulatory requirements or when directed solely to DOE personnel and not impacting regulated parties.

units.obligation_text: Must be written in plain and understandable language;
units.actor: All new or revised DOE guidance documents
units.action_summary: Guidance documents must be drafted in clear, plain language.

units.obligation_text: Must include the following attributes:
units.actor: All new or revised DOE guidance documents
units.action_summary: Guidance documents must contain the listed attributes.

units.obligation_text: The term 'guidance';
units.actor: All new or revised DOE guidance documents
units.action_summary: Include the term 'guidance' in the document.

units.obligation_text: a title;
units.actor: All new or revised DOE guidance documents
units.action_summary: Include a title.

units.obligation_text: identify the issuing agency or office;
units.actor: All new or revised DOE guidance documents
units.action_summary: Identify the issuing agency or office.

units.obligation_text: identify activities to which and the persons to whom the document applies;
units.actor: All new or revised DOE guidance documents
units.action_summary: Specify the activities and persons to which the guidance applies.

units.obligation_text: the date of issuance;
units.actor: All new or revised DOE guidance documents
units.action_summary: Include the issuance date.

units.obligation_text: the relation to previous guidance (if applicable);
units.actor: All new or revised DOE guidance documents
units.action_summary: State the relation to prior guidance, where applicable.

units.obligation_text: a citation to the statutory provision or regulation to which applies;
units.actor: All new or revised DOE guidance documents
units.action_summary: Provide a citation to the relevant statute or regulation.

units.obligation_text: and a short summary of the subject matter.
units.actor: All new or revised DOE guidance documents
units.action_summary: Include a brief summary of the subject matter.

units.obligation_text: All new or revised DOE guidance documents must be reviewed by the Office of the Assistant General Counsel for Legislation, Regulation and Energy Efficiency prior to issuance to:
units.actor: All new or revised DOE guidance documents / DOE
units.action_summary: Guidance documents must undergo review by the specified Office before issuance.

units.obligation_text: Ensure compliance with this part and Executive Order 13891;
units.actor: Office of the Assistant General Counsel for Legislation, Regulation and Energy Efficiency (via review)
units.action_summary: Review must ensure the document complies with this part and EO 13891.

units.obligation_text: Obtain a determination from the Administrator as to whether the guidance document is significant, as defined in this part;
units.actor: Office of the Assistant General Counsel for Legislation, Regulation and Energy Efficiency (via review)
units.action_summary: Review must obtain a determination from the Administrator on whether the guidance is 'significant'.

units.obligation_text: If the guidance document is determined to be significant, coordinate efforts with the Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs within the Office of Management and Budget as prescribed in paragraph (c) of this section.
units.actor: Office of the Assistant General Counsel for Legislation, Regulation and Energy Efficiency / DOE
units.action_summary: If determined significant, coordinate with OIRA per paragraph (c).

units.obligation_text: For any guidance document deemed to be a significant guidance document by the Administrator, DOE shall:
units.action_summary: If Administrator deems guidance 'significant', DOE has the following obligations.

units.obligation_text: Publish notice of the guidance document in the Federal Register and on DOE’s guidance website, and provide a public notice and comment period of not less than 30 days prior to the issuance of the final significant guidance document;
units.action_summary: DOE must publish notice and provide at least 30 days for public comment before issuing a final significant guidance document.

units.obligation_text: Provide publicly available responses to major and relevant concerns raised in comments;
units.action_summary: DOE must publicly respond to major relevant comments.

units.obligation_text: Obtain approval of the significant guidance document by the Secretary of Energy or DOE component head appointed by the President prior to issuance of the final significant guidance document;
units.action_summary: DOE must obtain approval from the Secretary or component head before issuing the final significant guidance document.

units.obligation_text: In accordance with the procedures of Executive Order 12866, obtain review of the significant guidance document by the Administrator prior to issuance of the final significant guidance document;
units.action_summary: DOE must obtain Administrator review per EO 12866 before issuing final significant guidance document.

units.obligation_text: Comply with applicable requirements of Executive Orders 12866, 13563, 13609, 13771, and 13777.
units.action_summary: DOE must comply with the listed Executive Order requirements for significant guidance documents.

units.obligation_text: DOE may dispense with the requirements of paragraphs (c)(1) and (2) of this section where DOE finds for good cause that notice and public comment for a significant guidance document are impracticable, unnecessary, or contrary to the public interest.
units.action_summary: DOE is permitted to skip notice and comment requirements for significant guidance documents if it finds good cause.

units.obligation_text: DOE shall incorporate such finding and a brief statement of the reasons for such finding into the significant guidance document.
units.action_summary: If DOE dispenses with notice/comment for good cause, DOE must include that finding and reasons in the guidance document.

units.obligation_text: The procedural requirements of paragraph (c) of this section shall not apply, in whole or in part, when:
units.action_summary: Paragraph (c) procedures do not apply in the following situations.

units.obligation_text: DOE and the Administrator agree that exigency, safety, health, or other compelling cause warrants an exemption from the relevant requirement or requirements;
units.action_summary: If DOE and the Administrator agree exigent or compelling causes exist, the paragraph (c) requirements may be exempted.

units.obligation_text: The significant guidance document is of a kind for which DOE and the Administrator have developed a categorical exception from the relevant requirement or requirements, as approved by the Administrator.
units.action_summary: If a categorical exception approved by the Administrator exists for that kind of guidance, paragraph (c) may not apply.

units.obligation_text: DOE will:
units.action_summary: DOE has the following obligations regarding electronic availability of guidance.

units.obligation_text: Ensure that all guidance documents, as defined in this part, are available to the public on the DOE website through a single web page portal;
units.action_summary: DOE must make all guidance documents available on a single web portal.

units.obligation_text: State clearly and prominently on its web page portal that guidance documents lack the force and effect of law, except as authorized by law or as incorporated into a contract.
units.action_summary: DOE must clearly state on the portal that guidance documents are not legally binding except as authorized or incorporated into contracts.

units.obligation_text: All guidance documents, as defined in this part, that are not posted on DOE’s website portal as described in paragraph (a) of this section shall be deemed rescinded, unless and until DOE subjects such guidance documents to the procedures of this section.
units.action_summary: Guidance documents not posted on the DOE portal are deemed rescinded until they undergo the procedures in this section.

units.obligation_text: Except for the purposes of establishing historical facts, DOE will not cite, use, or rely upon rescinded guidance documents unless and until DOE subjects such guidance documents to the procedures of this section.
units.action_summary: DOE is prohibited from citing, using, or relying on rescinded guidance documents except to establish historical facts or until they are resubmitted to procedures.

units.obligation_text: Any person may petition DOE to withdraw or modify a guidance document.
units.action_summary: Anyone is permitted to petition DOE to withdraw or modify a guidance document.

units.obligation_text: The petition must be addressed to the Assistant General Counsel for Legislation, Regulation, and Energy Efficiency, Attention: Petition for Modification or Withdrawal of Guidance Document, and either:
units.action_summary: Petitions must be addressed to the specified Assistant General Counsel and submitted by one of the listed methods.

units.obligation_text: Sent by mail addressed to: Forrestal Building, U.S. Department of Energy, 1000 Independence Avenue SW, Washington, DC 20585;
units.action_summary: One acceptable method is to send the petition by mail to the listed postal address.

units.obligation_text: Sent by email to Guidance@hq.doe.gov;
units.action_summary: One acceptable method is to send the petition by email to Guidance@hq.doe.gov.

units.obligation_text: Hand delivered to DOE at 1000 Independence Avenue SW, Washington, DC 20585.
units.action_summary: One acceptable method is to hand deliver the petition to the listed DOE address.

units.obligation_text: For each petition filed under this section, the petitioner must:
units.action_summary: Petitioner has the following mandatory content requirements for each petition.

units.obligation_text: Specify the petitioner’s:
units.action_summary: Petitioner must specify identifying information as listed.

units.obligation_text: (i) Name, or if the petitioner is an organization, the name of the organization and the name and authority of the individual who signed the petition on behalf of the organizational or corporate petitioner;
units.action_summary: Provide name (or organization name and signatory's name and authority).

units.obligation_text: (ii) Telephone number;
units.action_summary: Provide a telephone number.

units.obligation_text: (iii) Mailing address; and
units.action_summary: Provide a mailing address.

units.obligation_text: (iv) Email address (if available).
units.action_summary: Provide an email address if available.

units.obligation_text: Identify the guidance document to be withdrawn or modified;
units.action_summary: Identify which guidance document is the subject of the petition.

units.obligation_text: Be signed by the petitioner or authorized representative.
units.action_summary: Petition must be signed by the petitioner or an authorized representative.

units.obligation_text: To assist DOE in responding appropriately to the petition, a petitioner should also:
units.action_summary: Petitioners are urged to provide the following additional information to assist DOE.

units.obligation_text: Present any specific problems or issues that the petitioner believes are associated with the guidance document, including any specific circumstances in which the guidance document is incorrect, incomplete, obsolete, or inadequate;
units.action_summary: Describe specific problems or contexts where the guidance is flawed or inadequate.

units.obligation_text: Present any proposed solution to either modify or withdraw the guidance document, including a discussion of how the petitioner’s proposed solution resolves the issues identified under paragraph (c)(1) of this section;
units.action_summary: Provide proposed modifications or withdrawal solutions and explain how they resolve identified issues.

units.obligation_text: In the case of a petition for modification of a guidance document, specify any modifications to the text of the document that petitioner seeks;
units.action_summary: If seeking modification, specify the exact textual changes requested.

units.obligation_text: Cite, enclose, or reference technical, scientific, or other data or information supporting the petitioner’s assertions under paragraphs (c)(1) and (2) of this section.
units.action_summary: Provide supporting technical, scientific, or other data for assertions and proposed solutions.

units.obligation_text: DOE will publish a petition for modification or withdrawal of a guidance document and supporting documentation in the Federal Register, and provide opportunity for public comment.
units.action_summary: DOE must publish petitions and supporting documents in the Federal Register and allow public comment.

units.obligation_text: DOE may dispense with the notice and comment procedures in this paragraph where DOE finds for good cause that notice and public comment are impracticable, unnecessary, or contrary to the public interest, or where exigency, safety, health, or other compelling cause warrants an exemption from the notice and comment procedures in this paragraph.
units.action_summary: DOE may waive the notice-and-comment requirement for petitions if it finds good cause or exigent circumstances.

units.obligation_text: DOE shall incorporate such finding and a brief statement of the reasons for such finding into its decision on the petition.
units.action_summary: If DOE dispenses with notice/comment, it must include the finding and reasons in its decision on the petition.

units.obligation_text: In accordance with the provisions set forth in 10 CFR 1004.11, any request for confidential treatment of any information contained in a petition for modifying or withdrawing a guidance document, or in supporting documentation, must be accompanied by a copy of the petition or supporting documentation from which the information claimed to be confidential has been deleted.
units.action_summary: Requests for confidential treatment must include a redacted copy of the petition or supporting documents.

units.obligation_text: DOE will publish in the Federal Register the petition and supporting documents from which confidential information, as determined by DOE, has been deleted in accordance with 10 CFR 1004.11.
units.action_summary: DOE will publish the petition and supporting documents with confidential information deleted per 10 CFR 1004.11.

units.obligation_text: DOE shall determine the appropriate disposition of a petition after consideration of the petition and any supporting documents received, as well as any public comment received on the petition, within 90 days of DOE’s publication in the Federal Register of such petition, to the maximum extent practicable.
units.action_summary: DOE must decide on the petition (considering materials and comments) within 90 days of publishing the petition, to the maximum extent practicable.

units.obligation_text: Before any DOE action under this part is final, a person must exhaust his or her administrative remedies.
units.action_summary: Individuals must exhaust administrative remedies before any DOE action under this part becomes final.

units.obligation_text: To exhaust administrative remedies under this part, a person must:
units.action_summary: To exhaust remedies one must complete the following steps.

units.obligation_text: Avail himself or herself of the procedures in this section;
units.action_summary: Use the procedures in this section.

units.obligation_text: Receive a final disposition from DOE in accordance with paragraph (f) of this section.
units.action_summary: Obtain a final disposition from DOE per paragraph (f).

title: Procedures for the Issuance of Guidance Documents

units.obligation_text: the undersigned DOE Federal Register Liaison Officer has been authorized to sign and submit the document in electronic format for publication, as an official document of the Department of Energy
units.actor: the undersigned DOE Federal Register Liaison Officer
units.action_summary: The DOE Federal Register Liaison Officer is permitted to sign and electronically submit the document for publication as an official DOE document.

units.obligation_text: That document with the original signature and date is maintained by DOE
units.action_summary: DOE maintains the document containing the original signature and date.

title: Proposed Administrative Priority and Definitions for Discretionary Grant Programs

units.obligation_text: an applicant must propose a project that is designed to address one or more of the following priority areas:
units.action_summary: Applicants must propose projects that address one or more listed priority areas.

units.obligation_text: Adopting and supporting models that leverage technology (e.g., universal design for learning, competency-based education (as defined in this notice), or hybrid/blended learning) and provide high-quality digital learning content, applications, and tools.
units.action_summary: Applicants must adopt/support technology-leveraging models and provide high-quality digital learning content, apps, and tools.

units.obligation_text: Providing personalized and job-embedded professional learning to build the capacity of educators to effectively use technology to create remote learning experiences that advance student engagement and learning (e.g., synchronous and asynchronous professional learning, professional learning networks or communities, and coaching).
units.action_summary: Applicants must provide personalized, job-embedded professional learning to help educators use technology for remote learning.

units.obligation_text: Providing access to any of the following, in particular to serve learners without access to such technologies: Reliable, high-speed internet, learning devices, and software applications that meet all students’ and educators’ remote learning needs while inside the school building and in remote learning environments.
units.action_summary: Applicants must provide access to reliable high-speed internet, devices, and software to meet remote learning needs.

units.obligation_text: These technology costs cannot exceed 10 percent of the overall costs for all activities of the project.
units.action_summary: Technology costs funded by the project are limited to no more than 10% of total project activity costs.

units.obligation_text: Developing performance-based assessments that promote competency-based education that can be delivered remotely or in-person to students and obtain valid and reliable results that accurately document students’ skills (e.g., inquiry/game-based assessment or data visualization tools for monitoring ongoing learning).
units.action_summary: Applicants must develop valid, reliable performance-based assessments for competency-based education deliverable remotely or in-person.

units.obligation_text: Supporting the development of digital interoperable credentials (as defined in this notice) that make transparent the competencies achieved through remote learning experiences and allow students to access, control, and share their achievements across a variety of education and training processes (formal or informal, classroom-based, remote, or workplace-based).
units.action_summary: Applicants must support developing interoperable digital credentials that transparently record competencies and allow students to control/share achievements.

units.obligation_text: Information on these credentials must be publicly accessible using linked open data formats to ensure their transferability and the continuity of learning for students.
units.action_summary: Information about interoperable credentials must be publicly accessible in linked open data formats to ensure transferability and continuity.

units.obligation_text: Providing high-quality remote learning or competency-based education specifically for one or more of the following student subgroups: Students from low-income families, students with disabilities, English learners, Native American students, homeless students, and students attending schools in rural areas.
units.action_summary: Applicants must provide high-quality remote or competency-based education targeted to one or more specified underserved student subgroups.

units.obligation_text: The remote learning environment must be accessible to individuals with disabilities in accordance with Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 and Title II of the Americans with Disabilities Act, as applicable.
units.action_summary: Remote learning environments funded must comply with Section 504 and Title II accessibility requirements.

units.obligation_text: The remote learning environment must also provide appropriate remote learning language assistance services to English learners.
units.action_summary: Remote learning environments must provide appropriate language assistance services for English learners.

units.obligation_text: The Secretary may choose to include the entire priority within a grant program or merely one or more of the priority’s component parts.
units.action_summary: The Secretary may include the whole priority or only selected component parts in a grant program.

units.obligation_text: Proposed component part (f) of the priority would only be used in conjunction with another component part of the priority.
units.action_summary: Component (f) may be used only together with at least one other component part of the priority.

units.obligation_text: When inviting applications for a competition using one or more priorities, we designate the type of each priority as absolute, competitive preference, or invitational through a notice in the Federal Register.
units.action_summary: When inviting applications, the Department will designate each priority's type (absolute, competitive preference, or invitational) via Federal Register notice.

units.obligation_text: Under an absolute priority, we consider only applications that meet the priority (34 CFR 75.105(c)(3)).
units.action_summary: For absolute priorities, the Department will consider only applications that meet the priority.

units.section: Types of Priorities - Competitive preference priority
units.obligation_text: Under a competitive preference priority, we give competitive preference to an application by (1) awarding additional points, depending on the extent to which the application meets the priority; or (2) selecting an application that meets the priority over an application of comparable merit that does not meet the priority (34 CFR 75.105(c)(2)(i) and (ii)).
units.action_summary: For competitive preference priorities, the Department gives applications that meet the priority a competitive advantage either via additional points or selection over comparable applications that do not meet the priority.

units.section: Types of Priorities - Competitive preference priority (1)
units.obligation_text: (1) awarding additional points, depending on the extent to which the application meets the priority (34 CFR 75.105(c)(2)(i)).
units.action_summary: The Department may award additional points to applications based on the extent they meet the competitive preference priority.

units.section: Types of Priorities - Competitive preference priority (2)
units.obligation_text: (2) selecting an application that meets the priority over an application of comparable merit that does not meet the priority (34 CFR 75.105(c)(2)(ii)).
units.action_summary: The Department may select an application that meets the priority over a comparably meritorious application that does not.

units.obligation_text: Under an invitational priority we are particularly interested in applications that meet the priority.
units.action_summary: The Department expresses interest in applications that meet an invitational priority but does not give them a preference.

units.section: Types of Priorities - Invitational priority prohibition
units.obligation_text: However, we do not give an application that meets the priority a preference over other applications (34 CFR 75.105(c)(1)).
units.action_summary: The Department will not give preferential treatment to applications that meet an invitational priority.

units.obligation_text: We will announce the final priority and definitions in a document in the Federal Register.
units.action_summary: The Department will publish the final priority and definitions in the Federal Register.

units.section: Final Priority and Definitions - determination condition
units.obligation_text: We will determine the final priority and definitions after considering responses to the proposed priority and definitions and other information available to the Department.
units.action_summary: The Department will finalize the priority and definitions after considering public comments and other information.

units.obligation_text: This document does not preclude us from proposing additional priorities, requirements, definitions, or selection criteria, subject to meeting applicable rulemaking requirements.
units.action_summary: The Department retains the authority to propose additional priorities, requirements, definitions, or selection criteria in the future.

units.section: Final Priority and Definitions - application invitation
units.obligation_text: In any year in which we choose to use the priority and definitions, we invite applications through a notice in the Federal Register.
units.action_summary: If the Department uses the priority and definitions in a given year, it will invite applications via Federal Register notice.

title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutant Emissions: Petroleum Refinery Sector Amendments

units.obligation_text: the owner or operator shall not discharge or cause the discharge of any gases containing SO2 into the atmosphere in excess of the emission limit calculated using Equation 1 of this section.
units.action_summary: Prohibits owners/operators from discharging SO2 gases in excess of the emission limit calculated by Equation 1.

units.obligation_text: An owner or operator may designate a process vent as a maintenance vent if the vent is only used as a result of startup, shutdown, maintenance, or inspection of equipment where equipment is emptied, depressurized, degassed or placed into service.
units.action_summary: Permits owners/operators to designate a process vent as a maintenance vent when used only during startup/shutdown/maintenance/inspection involving emptying or depressurizing equipment.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator does not need to designate a maintenance vent as a Group 1 or Group 2 miscellaneous process vent.
units.action_summary: Owners/operators are not required to categorize a maintenance vent as Group 1 or Group 2.

units.obligation_text: The owner of operator must comply with the applicable requirements in paragraphs (c)(1) through (3) of this section for each maintenance vent according to the compliance dates specified in table 11 of this subpart, unless an extension is requested in accordance with the provisions in Sec. 63.6(i).
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must meet the specified requirements for each maintenance vent by the Table 11 compliance dates, unless they obtain an approved extension under Sec. 63.6(i).

units.obligation_text: After February 1, 2016 and prior to the date of compliance with the maintenance vent provisions in paragraph (c) of this section, the owner or operator must comply with the requirements in Sec. 63.642(n) for each maintenance venting event and maintain records necessary to demonstrate compliance with the requirements in Sec. 63.642(n) including, if appropriate, records of existing standard site procedures used to deinventory equipment for safety purposes.
units.action_summary: Between Feb 1, 2016 and compliance with paragraph (c), owners/operators must follow Sec.63.642(n) for each maintenance venting event and keep records showing compliance (including safety deinventory procedures when appropriate).

units.obligation_text: Each owner or operator of an existing source subject to the provisions of this subpart shall comply with the provisions of 40 CFR part 60, subpart VV, and paragraph (b) of this section except as provided in paragraphs (a)(1) and (2), (c) through (i), and (j)(1) and (2) of this section.
units.actor: each owner or operator of an existing source
units.action_summary: Existing-source owners/operators must comply with 40 CFR part 60, subpart VV and paragraph (b), except as the listed exceptions provide.

units.obligation_text: Each owner or operator of a new source subject to the provisions of this subpart shall comply with subpart H of this part except as provided in paragraphs (c) through (i) and (j)(1) and (2) of this section.
units.actor: each owner or operator of a new source
units.action_summary: New-source owners/operators must comply with subpart H, except as provided in the listed paragraphs.

units.obligation_text: For fenceline monitoring systems subject to Sec. 63.658, within 45 calendar days after the end of each reporting period, each owner or operator shall submit the following information to the EPA's Compliance and Emissions Data Reporting Interface (CEDRI).
units.action_summary: Owners/operators with fenceline monitoring must submit specified information to EPA's CEDRI within 45 days after each reporting period.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator need not transmit these data prior to obtaining 12 months of data.
units.action_summary: Owners/operators are not required to submit the fenceline monitoring data until they have collected 12 months of data.

units.obligation_text: Implementation of prevention measures listed for pressure relief devices in Sec. 63.648(j)(5) for each pressure relief device that can discharge to the flare.
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must implement the prevention measures in Sec.63.648(j)(5) for any pressure relief device that can discharge to the flare.

units.obligation_text: Then the owner or operator must comply with requirements for new sources in Sec. 63.643(a) and (b); 63.644, 63.645, and 63.647; 63.648(a) through (i) and (j)(1) and (2); 63.649 through 63.651; and 63.654 through 63.656.
units.action_summary: Owners/operators of sources constructed after June 30, 2014 must comply with the listed new-source requirements.

units.obligation_text: Then the owner or operator must comply with requirements for new sources in Sec. 63.642(n), 63.643(c), 63.648(j)(3), (6) and (7); and 63.657 through 63.660.
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must comply with these additional new-source requirements upon initial startup or Feb 1, 2016, whichever is later.

units.obligation_text: Then the owner or operator must comply with requirements for new sources in Sec. 63.643(a) and (b); 63.644, 63.645, and 63.647; 63.648(a) through (i) and (j)(1) and (2); and 63.649 through 63.651, 63.655 and 63.656.
units.action_summary: Owners/operators with construction between Sept 4, 2007 and June 30, 2014 must comply with the listed new-source requirements upon initial startup.

units.obligation_text: Then the owner or operator must comply with requirements for new sources in Sec. 63.654 upon initial startup or October 28, 2009, whichever is later.
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must meet Sec.63.654 by initial startup or Oct 28, 2009, whichever occurs later.

units.obligation_text: Then the owner or operator must comply with requirements for new sources in either Sec. 63.646 or Sec. 63.660, with transition to comply only with Sec. 63.660 on or before April 29, 2016.
units.action_summary: Owners/operators electing either Sec.63.646 or 63.660 must transition to only Sec.63.660 by April 29, 2016.

units.obligation_text: Then the owner or operator must comply with requirements for existing sources in Sec. 63.643(c) on or before August 1, 2017.
units.action_summary: Existing-source owners/operators must meet Sec.63.643(c) by Aug 1, 2017.

units.obligation_text: Then the owner or operator must comply with requirements for existing sources in Sec. 63.658 on or before January 30, 2018.
units.action_summary: Existing-source owners/operators must meet Sec.63.658 by Jan 30, 2018.

units.obligation_text: Then the owner or operator must comply with requirements for existing sources in Sec. 63.648 (j)(3), (6) and (7) and Sec. 63.657 on or before January 30, 2019.
units.action_summary: Existing-source owners/operators must meet these provisions by Jan 30, 2019.

units.obligation_text: If you startup your affected source before April 11, 2002, then you must comply with the emission limitations and work practice standards for new and reconstructed sources in this subpart no later than April 11, 2002 except as provided in paragraph (d) of this section.
units.action_summary: Sources started up before April 11, 2002 had to comply with new/reconstructed source standards by April 11, 2002, except as paragraph (d) provides.

units.obligation_text: If you startup your affected source after April 11, 2002, you must comply with the emission limitations and work practice standards for new and reconstructed sources in this subpart upon startup of your affected source except as provided in paragraph (d) of this section.
units.action_summary: Sources starting up after April 11, 2002 must comply with new/reconstructed standards upon startup, except as paragraph (d) provides.

units.obligation_text: If you have an existing affected source, you must comply with the emission limitations and work practice standards for existing affected sources in this subpart by no later than April 11, 2005 except as specified in paragraphs (c) and (d) of this section.
units.action_summary: Existing affected sources must meet existing-source standards by April 11, 2005, except as paragraphs (c) and (d) provide.

units.obligation_text: For sources which commenced construction or reconstruction before June 30, 2014, you must comply with the applicable requirements in Sec. Sec. 63.1564(a)(5), 63.1565(a)(5) and 63.1568(a)(4) on or before August 1, 2017 unless an extension is requested and approved in accordance with the provisions in Sec. 63.6(i).
units.action_summary: Sources started before June 30, 2014 must meet the listed requirements by Aug 1, 2017 unless they get an approved extension under Sec.63.6(i).

units.obligation_text: After February 1, 2016 and prior to the date of compliance with the provisions in Sec. Sec. 63.1564(a)(5), 63.1565(a)(5) and 63.1568(a)(4), you must comply with the requirements in Sec. 63.1570(c) and (d).
units.action_summary: Between Feb 1, 2016 and the compliance date, sources must follow Sec.63.1570(c) and (d).

units.obligation_text: For sources which commenced construction or reconstruction on or after June 30, 2014, you must comply with the applicable requirements in Sec. Sec. 63.1564(a)(5), 63.1565(a)(5) and 63.1568(a)(4) on or before February 1, 2016 or upon startup, whichever is later.
units.action_summary: Sources started on/after June 30, 2014 must meet the listed requirements by Feb 1, 2016 or upon startup, whichever is later.

units.obligation_text: You can elect to comply with the PM per coke burn-off emission limit of this chapter (Option 2);
units.action_summary: Sources may choose to meet the PM per coke burn-off emission limit option (Option 2).

units.obligation_text: On or before the date specified in Sec. 63.1563(d), you must comply with one of the two options in paragraphs (a)(5)(i) and (ii) of this section during periods of startup, shutdown and hot standby:
units.action_summary: By the Sec.63.1563(d) date, sources must follow one of two specified options during startup/shutdown/hot standby.

units.obligation_text: If you elect to comply with the alternative limit in paragraph (a)(5)(ii) of this section during periods of startup, shutdown and hot standby, demonstrate continuous compliance on or before the date specified in Sec. 63.1563(d) by:
units.action_summary: If electing the alternative limit in (a)(5)(ii), sources must demonstrate continuous compliance by the Sec.63.1563(d) date by following the prescribed means.

units.obligation_text: On or before the date specified in Sec. 63.1563(d), you must comply with one of the two options in paragraphs (a)(5)(i) and (ii) of this section during periods of startup, shutdown and hot standby:
units.action_summary: By the Sec.63.1563(d) date, sources must follow one of two specified options for organic HAP emissions during startup/shutdown/hot standby.

units.obligation_text: The emission limitations in Tables 15 and 16 of this subpart do not apply to emissions from process vents during passive depressuring when the reactor vent pressure is 5 pounds per square inch gauge (psig) or less or during active depressuring or purging prior to January 30, 2019, when the reactor vent pressure is 5 psig or less.
units.action_summary: Emission limits in Tables 15 and 16 are not applicable to process vent emissions during passive depressuring at ≤5 psig, and before Jan 30, 2019, also during active depressuring/purging at ≤5 psig.

units.obligation_text: On and after January 30, 2019, the emission limitations in Tables 15 and 16 of this subpart do apply to emissions from process vents during active purging operations ... or active depressuring ... regardless of the reactor vent pressure.
units.action_summary: From Jan 30, 2019 onward, emission limits apply to process vent emissions during active purging or active depressuring regardless of vent pressure.

units.obligation_text: On or before the date specified in Sec. 63.1563(d), you must comply with one of the three options in paragraphs (a)(4)(i) through (iii) of this section during periods of startup and shutdown.
units.action_summary: By the Sec.63.1563(d) date, sources must follow one of three options for sulfur recovery unit organic HAP emissions during startup/shutdown.

units.obligation_text: On and after August 1, 2017, maintain the 3-hour rolling average opacity of emissions from your catalyst regenerator vent no higher than 20 percent.
units.action_summary: From Aug 1, 2017, keep the 3-hour rolling average opacity from catalyst regenerator vents at or below 20%.

units.obligation_text: You shall install, operate, and maintain a continuous parameter monitoring system to measure and record the gas flow rate exiting the catalyst regenerator.
units.action_summary: Owners/operators electing the operating limits must install/operate/maintain a continuous monitoring system for gas flow rate from the catalyst regenerator.

units.obligation_text: If applicable, you can use the alternative in Sec. 63.1573(a)(1) instead of a continuous parameter monitoring system for gas flow rate.
units.action_summary: Where applicable, owners/operators may use the Sec.63.1573(a)(1) alternative in place of a continuous gas flow monitoring system.

units.obligation_text: PM emissions must not exceed 1.0 g/kg (1.0 lb PM/1,000 lb) of coke burn-off.
units.action_summary: PM emissions from the catalyst regenerator vent cannot exceed 1.0 g/kg of coke burn-off.

units.obligation_text: You have already conducted a performance test to demonstrate initial compliance with the NSPS and the measured PM emission rate is less than or equal to 1.0 g/kg ... As part of the Notification of Compliance Status, you must certify that your vent meets the PM limit.
units.action_summary: If you performed a qualifying performance test showing compliance, you must certify in the Notification of Compliance Status that the vent meets the PM limit.

units.obligation_text: You are not required to do another performance test to demonstrate initial compliance.
units.action_summary: Owners/operators meeting the specified performance-test conditions need not perform an additional performance test for initial compliance.

units.obligation_text: As part of your Notification of Compliance Status, you certify that your BLD; CO2, O2, or CO monitor; or continuous opacity monitoring system meets the requirements in Sec. 63.1572.
units.action_summary: In the Notification of Compliance Status, owners/operators must certify that their monitoring equipment meets Sec.63.1572 requirements.

title: National Emission Standards: Hazardous Air Pollutant Emissions: Petroleum Refinery Sector

units.obligation_text: Equipment leaks that are also subject to the provisions of 40 CFR part 60, subpart GGGa, are required to comply only with the provisions specified in 40 CFR part 60, subpart GGGa
units.actor: equipment leaks that are also subject to 40 CFR part 60, subpart GGGa
units.action_summary: Equipment leaks subject to 40 CFR part 60, subpart GGGa must comply only with that subpart's provisions.

units.obligation_text: pressure relief devices in organic HAP service must only comply with the requirements in Sec. 63.648(j)
units.actor: pressure relief devices in organic HAP service
units.action_summary: Pressure relief devices in organic HAP service are required to comply only with the requirements in § 63.648(j).

units.obligation_text: the owner or operator must comply with the requirements specified in paragraphs (j)(1) and (2) of this section for pressure relief devices, such as relief valves or rupture disks, in organic HAP gas or vapor service instead of the pressure relief device requirements of Sec. 60.482-4 of this chapter, Sec. 60.482-4a of this chapter, or Sec. 63.165, as applicable
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must follow the § 63.648(j)(1) and (j)(2) requirements for pressure relief devices in organic HAP gas/vapor service rather than the referenced alternate PRD requirements.

units.obligation_text: Except as specified in paragraphs (j)(4) and (5) of this section, the owner or operator must also comply with the requirements specified in paragraph (j)(3) of this section for all pressure relief devices
units.action_summary: Unless paragraphs (j)(4) or (j)(5) apply, owners/operators must comply with the § 63.648(j)(3) requirements for all pressure relief devices.

units.obligation_text: If the pressure relief device does not consist of or include a rupture disk, conduct instrument monitoring, as specified in Sec. 60.485(c) of this chapter, Sec. 60.485a(c) of this chapter, or Sec. 63.180(c), as applicable, no later than 5 calendar days after the pressure relief device returns to organic HAP gas or vapor service following a pressure release to verify that the pressure relief device is operating with an instrument reading of less than 500 ppm
units.action_summary: If a PRD has no rupture disk, the owner/operator must perform specified instrument monitoring within 5 days after it returns to service to verify readings are under 500 ppm.

units.obligation_text: If the pressure relief device includes a rupture disk, either comply with the requirements in paragraph (j)(2)(i) of this section (not replacing the rupture disk) or install a replacement disk as soon as practicable after a pressure release, but no later than 5 calendar days after the pressure release
units.action_summary: If a PRD includes a rupture disk, the owner/operator must either follow the monitoring procedure in (j)(2)(i) without replacing the disk, or install a replacement disk as soon as practicable but within 5 days.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator must conduct instrument monitoring, as specified in Sec. 60.485(c) of this chapter, Sec. 60.485a(c) of this chapter, or Sec. 63.180(c), as applicable, no later than 5 calendar days after the pressure relief device returns to organic HAP gas or vapor service following a pressure release to verify that the pressure relief device is operating with an instrument reading of less than 500 ppm
units.action_summary: After a pressure release for a PRD that includes a rupture disk, the owner/operator must perform specified instrument monitoring within 5 days after it returns to service to verify <500 ppm.

units.obligation_text: If the pressure relief device consists only of a rupture disk, install a replacement disk as soon as practicable after a pressure release, but no later than 5 calendar days after the pressure release
units.action_summary: If a PRD is only a rupture disk, the owner/operator must install a replacement disk as soon as practicable and within 5 days after a pressure release.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator may not initiate startup of the equipment served by the rupture disk until the rupture disc is replaced
units.action_summary: Owners/operators are prohibited from starting up equipment served by a rupture disk until the disk has been replaced.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator must conduct instrument monitoring, as specified in Sec. 60.485(c) of this chapter, Sec. 60.485a(c) of this chapter, or Sec. 63.180(c), as applicable, no later than 5 calendar days after the pressure relief device returns to organic HAP gas or vapor service following a pressure release to verify that the pressure relief device is operating with an instrument reading of less than 500 ppm
units.action_summary: After replacement of a rupture-disk-only PRD and its return to service following a pressure release, the owner/operator must perform specified instrument monitoring within 5 days to verify <500 ppm.

units.obligation_text: Implementation of prevention measures listed for pressure relief devices in Sec. 63.648(j)(3)(ii) for each pressure relief valve that can discharge to the flare
units.actor: owner or operator (responsible for flare control devices)
units.action_summary: Owners/operators of flare control devices must implement the prevention measures listed in § 63.648(j)(3)(ii) for every pressure relief valve that can discharge to the flare.

title: National Emission Standards: Hazardous Air Pollutant Emissions; Petroleum Refinery Sector
Greenhouse Gas Emissions and Fuel Efficiency Standards: Medium- and Heavy-Duty Engines and Vehicles Phase 2

units.obligation_text: Comments must be received on or before April 1, 2016.
units.action_summary: Commenters are required to submit comments by April 1, 2016.

units.obligation_text: Submit your comments, identified by Docket ID No. EPA-HQ-OAR-2014-0827 (for EPA's docket) and NHTSA-2014-0132 (for NHTSA's docket), by one of the following methods:
units.action_summary: Commenters must submit comments identified by the specified docket ID numbers using one of the listed methods.

units.obligation_text: Online: www.regulations.gov: Follow the on-line instructions for submitting comments.
units.action_summary: Commenters may submit comments online via regulations.gov and must follow the online instructions.

units.obligation_text: Email: a-and-r-docket@epa.gov.
units.action_summary: Commenters may submit comments by email to the specified EPA address.

units.obligation_text: Mail: EPA: Air and Radiation Docket and Information Center, Environmental Protection Agency, Mailcode: 28221T, 1200 Pennsylvania Ave. NW., Washington, DC 20460. NHTSA: Docket Management Facility, M-30, U.S. Department of Transportation, West Building, Ground Floor, Rm. W12-140, 1200 New Jersey Avenue SE., Washington, DC 20590.
units.action_summary: Commenters may submit comments by mail to the specified EPA or NHTSA docket addresses.

units.obligation_text: Hand Delivery: EPA: EPA Docket Center, EPA WJC West Building, Room 3334, 1301 Constitution Ave. NW., Washington, DC 20460. Such deliveries are only accepted during the Docket's normal hours of operation, and special arrangements should be made for deliveries of boxed information. NHTSA: West Building, Ground Floor, Rm. W12-140, 1200 New Jersey Avenue SE., Washington, DC 20590, between 9 a.m. and 4 p.m. Eastern Time, Monday through Friday, except Federal Holidays.
units.action_summary: Commenters may hand-deliver comments to the specified docket centers during stated hours; special arrangements should be made for boxed deliveries.

units.obligation_text: Comments that are submitted for consideration by one agency should be identified as such, and comments that are submitted for consideration by both agencies should be identified as such.
units.action_summary: Commenters must identify whether their comments are for EPA, NHTSA, or both.

units.obligation_text: Comments submitted to the EPA docket will be considered comments submitted to the NHTSA docket, and vice versa. Therefore, a commenter only needs to submit comments to either of the agency dockets (or choose to submit a comment to both).
units.action_summary: Commenters may submit comments to either agency docket and that submission will be treated as filed with both agencies.

units.obligation_text: When submitting comments, please remember to: Identify the rulemaking by docket number and other identifying information (subject heading, Federal Register date and page number).
units.action_summary: Commenters should identify the rulemaking by docket number and other identifying details when submitting comments.

units.obligation_text: NHTSA: Your comments must be written and in English.
units.action_summary: Comments submitted to NHTSA must be written in English.

units.obligation_text: To ensure that your comments are correctly filed in the Docket, please include the Docket number NHTSA-2014-0132 in your comments.
units.action_summary: Commenters should include the NHTSA docket number to ensure proper filing.

units.obligation_text: Your comments must not be more than 15 pages long.
units.action_summary: Comments submitted to NHTSA must be limited to 15 pages (attachments allowed separately).

units.obligation_text: If you submit an electronic comment, EPA recommends that you include your name and other contact information in the body of your comment and with any disk or CD-ROM you submit.
units.action_summary: EPA recommends including name and contact information with electronic submissions.

units.obligation_text: Electronic files should avoid the use of special characters, any form of encryption, and be free of any defects or viruses.
units.action_summary: Electronic submissions to EPA should not use special characters or encryption and should be free of defects or viruses.

units.obligation_text: If you submit your comments by mail and wish Docket Management to notify you upon its receipt of your comments, enclose a self-addressed, stamped postcard in the envelope containing your comments.
units.actor: commenters who submit by mail and wish receipt notification
units.action_summary: Mailing commenters who want notification must include a self-addressed stamped postcard.

units.section: B. Public Participation (4) EPA CBI instructions
units.obligation_text: EPA: Do not submit CBI to EPA through www.regulations.gov or email.
units.action_summary: Submitters must not send confidential business information to EPA via regulations.gov or email.

units.section: B. Public Participation (4) EPA CBI instructions
units.obligation_text: Clearly mark the part or all of the information that you claim to be CBI.
units.action_summary: Submitters claiming CBI must clearly mark the specific information as confidential.

units.section: B. Public Participation (4) EPA CBI instructions
units.obligation_text: For CBI information in a disk or CD ROM that you mail to EPA, mark the outside of the disk or CD ROM as CBI and then identify electronically within the disk or CD ROM the specific information that is claimed as CBI.
units.action_summary: When mailing CBI on disk/CD, submitters must label the disk/CD as CBI and identify the specific CBI electronically inside.

units.section: B. Public Participation (4) EPA CBI instructions
units.obligation_text: In addition to one complete version of the comment that includes information claimed as CBI, a copy of the comment that does not contain the information claimed as CBI must be submitted for inclusion in the public docket.
units.action_summary: Submitters must provide both a full version containing CBI and a redacted version without CBI for the public docket.

units.section: B. Public Participation (4) NHTSA CBI instructions
units.obligation_text: NHTSA: If you wish to submit any information under a claim of confidentiality, you should submit three copies of your complete submission, including the information you claim to be confidential business information, to the Chief Counsel, NHTSA, at the address given above under FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT.
units.action_summary: Submitters claiming confidentiality to NHTSA should submit three copies of their complete submission, including the CBI, to NHTSA Chief Counsel.

units.section: B. Public Participation (4) NHTSA CBI instructions
units.obligation_text: When you send a comment containing confidential business information, you should include a cover letter setting forth the information specified in our confidential business information regulation.
units.action_summary: Submitters should include a cover letter with required details when sending CBI to NHTSA.

units.section: B. Public Participation (4) NHTSA CBI instructions
units.obligation_text: In addition, you should submit a copy from which you have deleted the claimed confidential business information to the Docket by one of the methods set forth above.
units.action_summary: Submitters should also provide a redacted copy with claimed CBI removed for the public docket.

units.obligation_text: Make sure to submit your comments by the comment period deadline identified in the DATES section above.
units.action_summary: Commenters are instructed to ensure their comments arrive by the deadline stated in DATES.

title: Accidental Release Prevention Requirements: Risk Management Programs under the Clean Air Act

units.obligation_text: an owner or operator of a stationary source that has more than a threshold quantity of a regulated substance in a process, as determined under Sec. 68.115, shall comply with the requirements of this part no later than the latest of the following dates
units.actor: owner or operator of a stationary source
units.action_summary: Owners/operators with threshold quantities must comply with this part by the latest applicable date listed.

units.obligation_text: Three years after the date on which a regulated substance is first listed under Sec. 68.130
units.actor: owner or operator of a stationary source
units.action_summary: One of the alternative compliance dates is three years after a substance is listed.

units.obligation_text: The date on which a regulated substance is first present above a threshold quantity in a process
units.actor: owner or operator of a stationary source
units.action_summary: One of the alternative compliance dates is the date the substance first exceeds the threshold in a process.

units.obligation_text: For any revisions to this part, the effective date of the final rule
units.actor: owner or operator of a stationary source
units.action_summary: One of the alternative compliance dates is the effective date of any revisions.

units.obligation_text: Within 1 year of [DATE 1 YEAR AFTER THE EFFECTIVE DATE OF THE FINAL RULE] the owner or operator of a stationary source shall comply with the emergency response coordination activities in Sec. 68.93(a) and (b)
units.actor: owner or operator of a stationary source
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must comply with emergency response coordination activities in §68.93(a) and (b) within 1 year after the final rule's effective date.

units.obligation_text: Within 3 years of the LEPC or equivalent requesting in writing, pursuant to Sec. 68.90(b)(2), the owner or operator must develop and implement an emergency response program in accordance with Sec. 68.95
units.action_summary: If the LEPC requests in writing, the owner/operator must develop and implement an emergency response program within 3 years.

units.obligation_text: By [DATE 4 YEARS AFTER THE EFFECTIVE DATE OF THE FINAL RULE], the owner or operator shall comply with the following provisions promulgated on [PUBLICATION DATE OF FINAL RULE]
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must comply by 4 years after effective date with listed provisions (third-party audits, root cause provisions, safer technology analysis, emergency response exercises, information availability).

units.obligation_text: Third-party audit provisions in Sec. Sec. 68.58(f), 68.58(g), 68.58(h), 68.59, 68.79(f), 68.79(g), 68.79(h), and 68.80
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must comply with the listed third-party audit provisions by the specified date.

units.obligation_text: Incident investigation root cause analysis provisions in Sec. Sec. 68.60(d)(7) and 68.81(d)(7) and the incident root cause category information provision in Sec. 68.42(b)(10)
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must comply with incident investigation root cause analysis and reporting provisions by the specified date.

units.obligation_text: Safer technology and alternative analysis provisions in Sec. 68.67(c)(8)
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must comply with safer technology and alternative analysis provisions by the specified date.

units.obligation_text: Emergency response exercise provisions of Sec. 68.96
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must comply with emergency response exercise provisions by the specified date.

units.obligation_text: Availability of information provisions in Sec. Sec. 68.205, 68.210(b), 68.210(c), and 68.210(d)
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must comply with information availability provisions by the specified date.

units.obligation_text: By [DATE 5 YEARS AFTER EFFECTIVE DATE OF THE FINAL RULE], the owner or operator shall comply with the risk management plan provisions of subpart G promulgated on [PUBLICATION DATE OF FINAL RULE]
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must comply with subpart G RMP provisions within 5 years after effective date.

units.obligation_text: Coordinate response actions with local emergency planning and response agencies as provided in Sec. 68.93
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must coordinate response actions with local emergency planning and response agencies per §68.93.

units.obligation_text: Develop and implement an emergency response program, and conduct exercises, as provided in Sec. Sec. 68.90 to 68.96
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must develop, implement, and exercise an emergency response program as specified.

units.obligation_text: Submit as part of the RMP the data on prevention program elements for Program 2 processes as provided in Sec. 68.170
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must submit Program 2 prevention program element data as part of the RMP.

units.obligation_text: Coordinate response actions with local emergency planning and response agencies as provided in Sec. 68.93
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must coordinate response actions with local emergency planning and response agencies per §68.93 (for paragraph d).

units.obligation_text: Develop and implement an emergency response program, and conduct exercises, as provided in Sec. Sec. 68.90 to 68.95 96 of this part
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must develop, implement, and exercise an emergency response program as specified (for paragraph d).

units.obligation_text: Submit as part of the RMP the data on prevention program elements for Program 3 processes as provided in Sec. 68.175
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must submit Program 3 prevention program element data as part of the RMP.

units.obligation_text: Categories of root causes identified based on the root cause analysis required in the incident investigation in accordance with Sec. 68.60(d)(7) or Sec. 68.81(d)(7)
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must include categories of root causes identified by incident root cause analysis in the five-year accident history.

units.obligation_text: Safety Data Sheets (SDS) that meet the requirements of 29 CFR 1910.1200(g)
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must include SDS that meet OSHA requirements as part of safety information.

units.obligation_text: Opportunities for equipment malfunctions or human errors that could cause an accidental release, including findings from incident investigations
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must include potential equipment malfunction or human error opportunities, including incident investigation findings, in hazard review.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator shall ensure that each employee presently involved in operating a process, and each employee newly assigned to a covered process have been trained or tested competent in the operating procedures provided in Sec. 68.52 that pertain to their duties
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must ensure current and newly assigned process employees are trained or shown competent in applicable operating procedures.

units.obligation_text: For those employees already operating a process on June 21, 1999, the owner or operator may certify in writing that the employee has the required knowledge, skills, and abilities to safely carry out the duties and responsibilities as provided in the operating procedures
units.action_summary: Owners/operators may certify in writing that pre-1999 employees are competent instead of training/testing.
