units.obligation_text: Refresher training shall be provided at least every three years, and more often if necessary, to each employee involved in operating a process to ensure that the employee understands and adheres to the current operating procedures of the process
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must provide refresher training at least every three years, or more often if needed, to process operators.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator, in consultation with the employees operating the process, shall determine the appropriate frequency of refresher training
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must, with employee consultation, set appropriate refresher training frequency.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator shall ensure that employees involved in operating a process are trained in any updated or new procedures prior to startup of a process after a major change
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must train process employees on updated/new procedures before restarting after major changes.

units.obligation_text: For the purposes of this section, the term employee also includes supervisors responsible for directing process operations
units.action_summary: Supervisors with process responsibilities are treated as employees for training requirements.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator shall certify that they have evaluated compliance with the provisions of this subpart for each covered process, at least every three years to verify that the procedures and practices developed under the rule are adequate and are being followed
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must certify they've evaluated compliance for each covered process at least every three years.

units.obligation_text: When required as set forth in paragraph (f), the compliance audit shall be a third-party audit
units.action_summary: If paragraph (f) applies, the required compliance audit must be a third-party audit.

units.obligation_text: An accidental release meeting the criteria in Sec. 68.42(a) from a covered process at a stationary source has occurred
units.action_summary: An accidental release meeting §68.42(a) is a condition that makes the next audit a third-party audit.

units.obligation_text: An implementing agency requires a third-party audit based on non-compliance with the requirements of this subpart, including when a previous third-party audit failed to meet the competency, independence, or impartiality criteria of Sec. 68.59(b)
units.actor: implementing agency (makes determination); owner or operator (subject to audit)
units.action_summary: If the implementing agency requires it (e.g., for non-compliance or prior audit deficiencies), the next audit must be a third-party audit.

units.obligation_text: If an implementing agency makes a preliminary determination that a third-party audit is necessary pursuant to paragraph (f)(2) of this section, the implementing agency will provide written notice to the owner or operator stating the reasons for the implementing agency's determination
units.action_summary: Implementing agency must provide written notice explaining reasons when preliminarily determining a third-party audit is necessary under (f)(2).

units.obligation_text: Within 30 days of receipt of such written notice, the owner or operator may provide information and data to, and may consult with, the implementing agency on the determination. Thereafter, the implementing agency will provide a final determination to the owner or operator
units.actor: owner or operator (may provide), implementing agency (will provide final determination)
units.action_summary: Owners/operators may submit info and consult within 30 days; then implementing agency will issue a final determination.

units.obligation_text: If the final determination requires a third-party audit, the owner or operator shall comply with the requirements of Sec. 68.59, pursuant to the schedule in paragraph (h) of this section
units.action_summary: If required by final determination, owners/operators must comply with §68.59 on the schedule in (h).

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator may appeal a final determination made by an implementing agency under paragraph (g)(2) of this section within 30 days of receipt of the final determination
units.action_summary: Owners/operators may appeal an implementing agency's final determination within 30 days.

units.obligation_text: Within 12 months of when any third-party audit is required pursuant to paragraphs (f) and/or (g) of this section
units.actor: owner or operator (to ensure audit/report submitted) / auditor
units.action_summary: The audit and audit report must be completed and submitted within 12 months of when a third-party audit is required.

units.obligation_text: Within three years of completion of the previous compliance audit, whichever is sooner
units.actor: owner or operator (to ensure audit/report submitted) / auditor
units.action_summary: Alternatively, the audit/report must be completed within three years of the previous compliance audit, whichever is sooner.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator shall engage a third-party auditor to evaluate compliance with the provisions of this subpart in accordance with the requirements of this section when either criterion of Sec. 68.58(f) is met
units.action_summary: When §68.58(f) criteria are met, owners/operators must engage a third-party auditor per §68.59.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator shall determine and document that the auditor and/or audit team are independent and impartial, and that the auditor's or audit team's credentials address the following competency requirements
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must determine and document auditor independence, impartiality, and competencies.

units.obligation_text: Knowledgeable with the requirements of this part
units.action_summary: Auditors must be knowledgeable about the part's requirements.

units.obligation_text: Experienced with the stationary source type and processes being audited and applicable recognized and generally accepted good engineering practices
units.action_summary: Auditors must have experience with the source type, processes, and accepted good engineering practices.

units.obligation_text: Trained or certified in proper auditing techniques
units.action_summary: Auditors must be trained or certified in auditing techniques.

units.obligation_text: A licensed Professional Engineer (PE), or shall include a licensed PE on the audit team
units.action_summary: Audit teams must include or be a licensed PE.

units.obligation_text: Act impartially when performing all activities under this section
units.action_summary: Auditors must act impartially in all audit activities.

units.obligation_text: Receive no financial benefit from the outcome of the audit, apart from payment for the auditing services
units.action_summary: Auditors must not receive financial benefit from audit outcomes beyond payment for services.

units.obligation_text: Not have conducted past research, development, design, construction services, or consulting for the owner or operator within the last 3 years
units.action_summary: Auditors must not have provided certain services to the owner/operator in the prior 3 years.

units.obligation_text: Not provide other business or consulting services to the owner or operator, including advice or assistance to implement the findings or recommendations in an audit report, for a period of at least 3 years following submission of the final audit report
units.action_summary: Auditors must not provide business/consulting services to the audited owner/operator for at least 3 years after the final audit report.

units.obligation_text: Ensure that all personnel involved in the audit sign and date the conflict of interest statement in Sec. 68.59(c)(1)(v)
units.action_summary: Audit personnel must sign and date the conflict of interest statement.

units.obligation_text: Ensure that all personnel involved in the audit do not accept future employment with the owner or operator of the stationary source for a period of at least 3 years following submission of the final audit report
units.action_summary: Audit personnel must not accept employment with the audited owner/operator for 3 years after the final audit report.

units.obligation_text: The auditor shall have written policies and procedures to ensure that all personnel comply with the competency, independence, and impartiality requirements of this section
units.action_summary: Auditor must maintain written policies/procedures to ensure personnel meet competency/independence/impartiality requirements.

units.obligation_text: The scope and content of each audit report shall: identify lead auditor and participants; document evaluation of compliance for each covered process; document findings including deficiencies; include summary of owner's comments and adjustments; and include the signed certification by the auditor or supervising manager
units.action_summary: Auditors must prepare audit reports with required scope/content including identification, evaluations, findings, owner's comments, and a signed certification.

units.obligation_text: The auditor shall retain copies of all audit reports and related records for a period of five years, and make them available if directed by the owner or operator, to the owner or operator and/or the implementing agency
units.action_summary: Auditor must keep audit reports/records for five years and make them available when directed.

units.obligation_text: The auditor shall submit the audit report to the implementing agency at the same time, or before, it provides it to the owner or operator
units.action_summary: Auditor must submit the audit report to the implementing agency concurrently with or before providing it to the owner/operator.

units.obligation_text: The audit report and related records shall not be privileged as attorney-client communications or attorney work products, even if written for or reviewed by legal staff
units.action_summary: Audit reports/records are not privileged as attorney-client or work product.

units.obligation_text: As soon as possible, but no later than 90 days after receiving the final audit report, the owner or operator shall determine an appropriate response to each of the findings in the audit report, and develop and provide to the implementing agency a findings response report that includes: (i) A copy of the final audit report; (ii) An appropriate response to each of the audit report findings; (iii) A schedule for promptly addressing deficiencies; and (iv) A certification, signed and dated by a senior corporate officer ...
units.action_summary: Within 90 days of the final audit report, owners/operators must prepare and submit a findings response report with specified contents and certification.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator shall implement the schedule to address deficiencies identified in the audit findings response report in paragraph (d)(1)(iii) of this section and document the action taken to address each deficiency, along with the date completed
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must carry out the schedule to correct deficiencies and document actions and completion dates.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator shall immediately provide a copy of each document required under paragraphs (d)(1) and (d)(2) of this section, when completed, to the owner or operator's audit committee of the Board of Directors, or other comparable committee, if one exists
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must promptly provide completed audit-related documents to their board audit committee or comparable committee.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator shall retain at the stationary source the two most recent third-party audit reports, related findings response reports, documentation of actions taken to address deficiencies, and related records
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must keep the two most recent third-party audit reports and related documentation at the source.

units.obligation_text: Copies of all draft third-party audit reports. The owner or operator shall provide draft third-party audit reports to the implementing agency upon request
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must keep copies of draft third-party audit reports and provide them to implementing agency on request.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator shall investigate each incident that: (1) Resulted in a catastrophic release ...; or (2) Could reasonably have resulted in a catastrophic release (i.e., was a near miss)
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must investigate incidents that resulted in or could have resulted in a catastrophic release.

units.obligation_text: An incident investigation team shall be established and consist of at least one person knowledgeable in the process involved and other persons with appropriate knowledge and experience to thoroughly investigate and analyze the incident
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must establish an investigation team with required knowledge and experience.

units.obligation_text: A report shall be prepared at the conclusion of the investigation. The report shall be completed within 12 months of the incident, unless the implementing agency approves, in writing, an extension of time. The report shall include: (1) Date, time, and location of incident; (2) Date investigation began; (3) A description ...; (4) The name and amount ...; (5) The consequences ...; (6) Emergency response actions taken; (7) The factors that contributed ... Root causes shall be determined by conducting an analysis for each incident using a recognized method; and (8) Any recommendations resulting from the investigation and a schedule for addressing them
units.actor: owner or operator (to ensure report prepared)
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must prepare and complete an incident investigation report within 12 months containing specified required elements, including root cause analysis and recommendations.

units.obligation_text: Incident investigation reports shall be retained for five years
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must retain incident investigation reports for five years.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator shall complete a compilation of written process safety information before conducting any process hazard analysis required by the rule, and shall keep process safety information up-to-date
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must compile written process safety information before PHA and keep it updated.

units.obligation_text: For processes in NAICS 322, 324, and 325, safer technology and alternative risk management measures applicable to eliminating or reducing risk from process hazards
units.action_summary: Owners/operators of processes in specified NAICS codes must address safer technology and alternative measures.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator shall consider, in the following order of preference, inherently safer technology or design, passive measures, active measures, and procedural measures. A combination of risk management measures may be used to achieve the desired risk reduction
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must consider risk reduction measures in order: inherently safer design, passive, active, then procedural; combinations allowed.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator shall determine the feasibility of the inherently safer technologies and designs considered
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must determine feasibility of considered inherently safer technologies/designs.

units.obligation_text: For the purposes of this section, the term employee also includes supervisors with process operational responsibilities
units.action_summary: Supervisors with operational responsibilities are included in 'employee' for training obligations.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator shall certify that they have evaluated compliance with the provisions of this subpart for each covered process, at least every three years to verify that the procedures and practices developed under the rule are adequate and are being followed
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must certify compliance evaluations for each covered process at least every three years (subpart D mirror of §68.58).

units.obligation_text: When required as set forth in paragraph (f), the compliance audit shall be a third-party audit
units.action_summary: If paragraph (f) applies, the required compliance audit must be a third-party audit (subpart D).

units.obligation_text: An accidental release meeting the criteria in Sec. 68.42(a) from a covered process at a stationary source has occurred
units.action_summary: An accidental release meeting §68.42(a) triggers the next audit to be third-party (subpart D).

units.obligation_text: An implementing agency requires a third-party audit based on non-compliance with the requirements of this subpart, including when a previous third-party audit failed to meet the competency, independence, or impartiality criteria of Sec. 68.80(b)
units.actor: implementing agency (makes determination); owner or operator (subject)
units.action_summary: Implementing agency can require a third-party audit for non-compliance or prior audit deficiencies (subpart D).

units.obligation_text: If an implementing agency makes a preliminary determination ... the implementing agency will provide written notice ... Within 30 days ... the owner or operator may provide information ... Thereafter, the implementing agency will provide a final determination ... If the final determination requires a third-party audit, the owner or operator shall comply with the requirements of Sec. 68.80, pursuant to the schedule in paragraph (h) ... The owner or operator may appeal a final determination ... within 30 days ...
units.action_summary: Implementing agency must notify owners/operators of preliminary determinations; owners/operators may respond and appeal; if required, owners/operators must comply with §68.80 per schedule.

units.obligation_text: The audit and audit report shall be completed, and the audit report submitted to the implementing agency pursuant to Sec. 68.80(c)(3) as follows: (1) Within 12 months of when any third-party audit is required pursuant to paragraphs (f) and/or (g) of this section; or (2) Within three years of completion of the previous compliance audit, whichever is sooner
units.action_summary: Audits/reports must be completed and submitted within specified timeframes (12 months after requirement or within three years of prior audit).

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator shall engage a third-party auditor to evaluate compliance with the provisions of this subpart in accordance with the requirements of this section when either criterion of Sec. 68.79(f) is met
units.action_summary: When §68.79(f) criteria are met, owners/operators must engage a third-party auditor per §68.80.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator shall determine and document that the auditor and/or audit team are independent and impartial, and that the auditor's or audit team's credentials address competency requirements (knowledgeable, experienced, trained/certified, licensed PE) and independence/impartiality requirements (act impartially; no financial benefit beyond payment; no prohibited past services within 3 years; not provide other consulting services for 3 years; sign conflict statement; not accept employment for 3 years)
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must ensure and document auditor independence/competency; auditors must meet specified independence and competence criteria and associated prohibitions.

units.obligation_text: The auditor shall have written policies and procedures to ensure that all personnel comply with the competency, independence, and impartiality requirements of this section
units.action_summary: Auditor must maintain written policies/procedures to ensure personnel comply with competency/independence/impartiality rules.

units.obligation_text: The scope and content of each audit report shall: identify lead auditor and participants; document evaluation of compliance for each covered process; document findings including deficiencies; include a summary of owner's comments and adjustments; and include the auditor's signed certification
units.action_summary: Auditors must prepare audit reports with specified scope/content and include a signed certification.

units.obligation_text: The auditor shall retain copies of all audit reports and related records for a period of five years, and make them available if directed by the owner or operator, to the owner or operator and/or the implementing agency
units.action_summary: Auditor must retain audit reports/records for five years and make them available when directed.

units.obligation_text: The auditor shall submit the audit report to the implementing agency at the same time, or before, it provides it to the owner or operator
units.action_summary: Auditor must submit the audit report to implementing agency concurrently with or before providing it to owner/operator.

units.obligation_text: The audit report and related records shall not be privileged as attorney-client communications or attorney work products, even if written for or reviewed by legal staff
units.action_summary: Audit reports/records are not privileged as attorney-client communications or work product.

units.obligation_text: As soon as possible, but no later than 90 days after receiving the final audit report, the owner or operator shall determine an appropriate response to each of the findings in the audit report, and develop and provide to the implementing agency a findings response report that includes specified items and a senior officer certification
units.action_summary: Within 90 days of final audit report, owners/operators must produce and submit a findings response report with required contents and certification.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator shall implement the schedule to address deficiencies identified in the audit findings response report in paragraph (d)(1)(iii) of this section and document the action taken to address each deficiency, along with the date completed
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must implement and document the schedule to correct audit-identified deficiencies and record completion dates.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator shall immediately provide a copy of each document required under paragraphs (d)(1) and (d)(2) of this section, when completed, to the owner or operator's audit committee of the Board of Directors, or other comparable committee, if one exists
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must promptly give completed audit-related documents to their board audit committee or comparable committee.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator shall retain at the stationary source, the two most recent third-party audit reports, related findings response reports, documentation of actions taken to address deficiencies, and related records
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must keep the two most recent third-party audit reports and related documentation at the stationary source.

units.obligation_text: Copies of all draft third-party audit reports. The owner or operator shall provide draft third-party audit reports to the implementing agency upon request
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must keep copies of draft third-party audit reports and provide them to implementing agency when requested.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator shall investigate each incident that: (1) Resulted in a catastrophic release ...; or (2) Could reasonably have resulted in a catastrophic release (i.e., was a near miss)
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must investigate incidents that resulted or could have resulted in catastrophic releases (mirror of §68.60 for other subpart).

units.obligation_text: A report shall be prepared at the conclusion of the investigation. The report shall be completed within 12 months of the incident, unless the implementing agency approves, in writing, an extension of time. The report shall include: (1) Date, time, and location of incident; (3) A description ...; (4) The name and amount ...; (5) The consequences ...; (6) Emergency response actions taken; (7) The factors that contributed ... Root causes shall be determined by conducting an analysis for each incident using a recognized method; and (8) Any recommendations resulting from the investigation and a schedule for addressing them
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must prepare an incident investigation report within 12 months containing specified elements including root cause analysis and recommendations (subpart equivalent).

units.obligation_text: The coordination activities required under Sec. 68.93 indicate that adequate local public emergency response capabilities are available to appropriately respond to any accidental release of the regulated substances at the stationary source
units.action_summary: If coordination under §68.93 shows local response capabilities are adequate, the source may be non-responding (condition).

units.obligation_text: Appropriate mechanisms are in place to notify emergency responders when there is a need for a response
units.action_summary: Having appropriate notification mechanisms is a condition allowing non-compliance with §68.95.

units.obligation_text: The LEPC or equivalent has not requested in writing that the owner or operator comply with the requirements of Sec. 68.95
units.action_summary: If LEPC has not requested in writing compliance with §68.95, that is a condition for non-responding sources.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator of a stationary source shall coordinate response activities as described in Sec. 68.93. The owner or operator shall also comply with the requirements of Sec. 68.95 when: (1) The outcome of the response coordination activities demonstrates that local public emergency response capabilities are not adequate ...; or (2) The LEPC or equivalent requests in writing that the owner or operator of the stationary source comply with the requirements of Sec. 68.95
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must coordinate response activities per §68.93 and must comply with §68.95 when local capabilities are inadequate or LEPC requests in writing.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator of a stationary source shall coordinate response needs with local emergency planning and response organizations to ensure resources and capabilities are in place to respond to an accidental release of a regulated substance
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must coordinate response needs with local emergency planning and response organizations to ensure response resources/capabilities exist.

units.obligation_text: Coordination shall occur at least annually, and more frequently if necessary, to address changes: At the source; in the source's emergency action plan; in local authorities' response resources and capabilities; or in the local community emergency response plan
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must coordinate at least annually (or more often as needed) to address changes in source, plans, or local response capabilities.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator shall document coordination with local authorities, including: The names of individuals involved and their contact information (phone number, email address, and organizational affiliations); dates of coordination activities; and nature of coordination activities
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must document coordination with local authorities including participants, contact info, dates, and nature of activities.
