units.obligation_text: A direction to use a respirator with an Assigned Protection Factor (APF) of 10. Refer to § 751.205(c)(3)(ii) for respirators having an APF of 10 or greater;
units.action_summary: Label must direct use of a respirator with APF of 10 and reference authorized respirators.

units.obligation_text: Each person or company engaged in any commercial NMP paint and coating removal activities [date 180 calendar days after the date of publication of the final rule] is prohibited from using paint and coating removal products or formulations that contain more than 35 percent by weight of NMP and must institute a worker protection program that includes the requirements of § 751.205(c) and (e) except for product formulations destined to be used for paint and coating removal from critical corrosion-sensitive components of military aviation and vessels as defined in § 751.203.
units.actor: Each person or company engaged in commercial NMP paint and coating removal activities
units.action_summary: Prohibits commercial use of >35% NMP formulations after 180 days and requires a worker protection program including specified requirements, with DOD exception.

units.obligation_text: After [date 10 years after the date of publication of the final rule], all persons are prohibited from using paint and coating removal products or formulations that contain more than 35 percent by weight of NMP and must institute a worker protection program that includes the requirements of § 751.205(c) and (e).
units.action_summary: After 10 years, prohibits use of >35% NMP formulations and requires institute of worker protection program for all persons.

units.obligation_text: Exception: product formulations destined to be used for paint and coating removal from critical corrosion-sensitive components of military aviation and vessels as defined in § 751.203 are excepted from the prohibition and worker protection program requirement in this paragraph.
units.actor: persons using product formulations destined for critical corrosion-sensitive military components
units.action_summary: Exempts DOD-destined formulations for critical components from the >35% prohibition and worker protection program requirement.

units.obligation_text: Any paint and coating removal from critical corrosion-sensitive components of military aviation and vessels must be conducted under the following restrictions:
units.actor: persons conducting paint and coating removal from critical corrosion-sensitive components of military aviation and vessels
units.action_summary: Requires paint and coating removal from critical components to follow specified restrictions.

units.obligation_text: All paint and coating removal from critical corrosion-sensitive components of military aviation and vessels using NMP must be conducted at DOD installations; or at government owned, contractor operated locations; or at contractor owned and contractor operated locations performing paint and coating removal from critical corrosion-sensitive components of military aviation and vessels for DOD.
units.actor: persons conducting paint and coating removal from critical corrosion-sensitive military components using NMP
units.action_summary: Requires such NMP-based paint removal to occur only at specified DOD or contractor locations.

units.obligation_text: Protective equipment that is of safe design and construction for the work to be performed must be provided, used, and maintained in a sanitary, reliable, and undamaged condition. The employer must select PPE that properly fits each affected employee and communicate PPE selections to each affected employee.
units.action_summary: Employers must provide, maintain, and select appropriately fitting PPE and communicate selections to affected employees.
units.modal_raw: must be provided, used, and maintained / must select

units.obligation_text: The employer must provide training to each employee required to use PPE.
units.action_summary: Employer must train every employee required to use PPE.

units.obligation_text: Each affected employee must be trained to know at least the following: (1) When PPE is necessary. (2) What PPE is necessary. (3) How to properly don, doff, adjust, and wear PPE. (4) The limitations of the PPE. (5) The proper care, maintenance, useful life and disposal of the PPE.
units.actor: the employer / each affected employee (training requirement)
units.action_summary: Requires training content for employees on necessity, selection, use, limitations, care, and disposal of PPE.

units.obligation_text: Each affected employee must demonstrate an understanding of these elements and the ability to use PPE properly before being allowed to perform work requiring the use of PPE.
units.action_summary: Employees must demonstrate understanding and ability to use PPE before performing PPE-required work.

units.obligation_text: Retraining is required when previous training is rendered obsolete, whether due to changes in the workplace or the type of PPE, or when the employer has reason to believe that a previously-trained employee does not have the understanding and skill required by this subparagraph.
units.action_summary: Requires retraining when training is obsolete or when employer doubts employee competence.

units.obligation_text: Each person who is reasonably likely to be dermally exposed in the work area to an NMP paint and coating removal product ... must be provided with, and required to wear, personal protective equipment that provides a barrier to prevent dermal exposure in the specific work area where it is selected for use.
units.actor: persons reasonably likely to be dermally exposed / the employer
units.action_summary: Requires provision and mandatory wear of dermal-protective PPE for persons likely to have dermal exposure.
units.modal_raw: must be provided with, and required to wear

units.obligation_text: Formulation-specific gloves as indicated on the NMP paint and coating removal product label. A new pair must be supplied and worn each time the NMP product is used.
units.actor: the employer / persons using the product
units.action_summary: Requires provision and use of formulation-specific gloves, with a new pair for each use.

units.obligation_text: Impervious clothing covering the exposed areas of the body (e.g. long pants, long shirt).
units.actor: the employer / persons using the product
units.action_summary: Requires impervious clothing covering exposed skin.
units.modal_raw: must be provided / required to wear

units.obligation_text: Testing the material used to make the chemical protective clothing and the construction of the clothing to establish that the protective clothing will be impervious for the expected duration and conditions of exposure. The testing must subject the chemical protective clothing to the expected conditions of exposure, including the likely combinations of chemical substances to which the clothing may be exposed in the work area.
units.action_summary: Employer must test protective clothing materials and construction under expected exposure conditions to demonstrate imperviousness.

units.obligation_text: Evaluating the specifications from the manufacturer or supplier of the chemical protective clothing, or of the material used in construction of the clothing, to establish that the chemical protective clothing will be impervious to the chemical substance alone and in likely combination with other chemical substances in the work area.
units.action_summary: Employer may establish imperviousness by evaluating manufacturer specifications of clothing or materials.

units.obligation_text: Each person who is reasonably likely to be exposed in the workplace to the use of NMP in paint and coating removal products must be provided with and is required to wear, at a minimum, a NIOSH-certified respirator with an APF of 10.
units.actor: persons reasonably likely to be exposed in the workplace / the employer (provision)
units.action_summary: Requires provision and mandatory wearing of at least a NIOSH-certified respirator with APF of 10 for persons likely exposed to NMP.
units.modal_raw: must be provided with and is required to wear

units.obligation_text: All respirators must be issued, used, and maintained in accordance with an appropriate written respiratory protection program that is specific to the workplace and that includes procedures for selecting respirators; medical evaluations; fit testing; procedures for proper use; procedures and schedules for cleaning, disinfecting, storing, inspecting, repairing, discarding, and otherwise maintaining respirators; procedures to ensure adequate air quality, quantity, and flow of breathing air for atmosphere-supplying respirators; procedures for regularly evaluating the effectiveness of the program; and recordkeeping.
units.action_summary: Requires a written workplace-specific respiratory protection program with detailed procedures and recordkeeping.
units.modal_raw: must be issued, used, and maintained / must include

units.obligation_text: Any NIOSH-certified air-purifying elastomeric half-mask respirator equipped with N100 (if oil aerosols absent), R100, or P100 filters meets the minimum requirements of this section.
units.actor: NIOSH-certified respirator types / employers selecting respirators
units.action_summary: Specifies an authorized respirator type that satisfies minimum requirements.

units.obligation_text: Any appropriate NIOSH-certified N100 (if oil aerosols absent), R100, or P100 filtering facepiece respirator meets the minimum requirements of this section.
units.actor: NIOSH-certified filtering facepiece respirator types / employers selecting respirators
units.action_summary: Specifies another authorized respirator option that satisfies minimum requirements.

units.obligation_text: Any NIOSH-certified air-purifying full facepiece respirator equipped with N100 (if oil aerosols absent), R100, or P100 filters. A full facepiece air-purifying respirator, although it has a higher APF of 50, is required to provide full face protection because the PMN substance presents significant exposure concern for mucous membranes, eyes, or skin.
units.actor: NIOSH-certified full facepiece respirator types / employers selecting respirators
units.action_summary: Specifies full facepiece respirators as authorized and explains when full face protection is required.
units.modal_raw: meet the minimum requirements / is required to provide

units.obligation_text: Any NIOSH-certified negative pressure (demand) supplied-air respirator equipped with a half-mask meets the minimum requirements of this section.
units.actor: NIOSH-certified supplied-air respirator types / employers selecting respirators
units.action_summary: Specifies supplied-air respirators with half-mask as meeting minimum requirements.

units.obligation_text: Any NIOSH-certified negative pressure (demand) self-contained breathing apparatus (SCBA) equipped with a half mask meets the minimum requirements of this section.
units.actor: NIOSH-certified SCBA types / employers selecting respirators
units.action_summary: Specifies SCBA equipped with a half mask as meeting minimum requirements.

units.obligation_text: Commercial users of NMP products for paint and coating removal may use an existing chemical exposure limit (ECEL) as a means of controlling inhalation exposures whenever practicable rather than respirators.
units.action_summary: Permits commercial users to use an existing ECEL to control inhalation exposures instead of respirators when practicable.

units.obligation_text: The employer must ensure that no person is exposed to an airborne concentration of NMP in excess of 20 mg/m3 (the ECEL) as an 8-hour time-weighted average (TWA) without using a respirator.
units.action_summary: Employer must ensure exposures do not exceed ECEL without respirator protection.

units.obligation_text: An independent accredited reference laboratory must verify the validity of the analytical method for NMP in paint and coating removal products.
units.action_summary: Requires independent lab verification of the validity of analytical methods for NMP.

units.obligation_text: The employer must collect samples that are representative of the potential exposure of each person who is reasonably likely to be exposed to airborne concentrations of NMP.
units.action_summary: Employer must perform representative exposure sampling for potentially exposed individuals.

units.obligation_text: Initial monitoring: Before the employer may deviate from the respirator requirements in subsection (d) of this section, the employer must conduct initial exposure monitoring to accurately determine the airborne concentration of NMP for each exposure group in which persons are reasonably likely to be exposed.
units.action_summary: Employer must conduct initial exposure monitoring before deviating from respirator requirements.

units.obligation_text: Employees whose exposures are represented by initial monitoring results below the ECEL need not wear the respirators required in subsection (d) of this section.
units.actor: employees represented by initial monitoring results below the ECEL
units.action_summary: Permits employees with initial exposures below ECEL to forgo respirators.

units.obligation_text: Employees whose exposures are represented by initial monitoring results above the ECEL must continue to wear the respirators required in subsection (d) of this section until such time as two monitoring results below the ECEL, sampled at least 24 hours apart, are obtained.
units.actor: employees represented by initial monitoring results above the ECEL / the employer to ensure
units.action_summary: Requires employees with initial exposures above ECEL to continue wearing respirators until two qualifying below-ECEL results are obtained.

units.obligation_text: Within 15 days of the date exposure monitoring results are received, the employer must provide the results to each person whose exposure is represented by the monitoring. If the result is above the ECEL, the employer must also provide the employee with information on the actions the employer will take to reduce employee exposures to the ECEL or below.
units.action_summary: Employer must provide monitoring results within 15 days and, if above ECEL, inform employees of corrective actions to reduce exposure.

units.obligation_text: Periodic monitoring: The employer must repeat exposure monitoring every 6 months for those employees whose initial monitoring results are between 0.5 ECEL and the ECEL, until such time as 2 results below 0.5 ECEL, from samples collected at least 24 hours apart, are obtained.
units.action_summary: Requires employers to repeat monitoring every 6 months for employees with intermediate initial results until criteria met.

units.obligation_text: Periodic monitoring: The employer must repeat exposure monitoring every 3 months for those employees whose initial monitoring results are at or above the ECEL. If 2 results below the ECEL, from samples collected at least 24 hours apart, are obtained, then frequency may be reduced to every 6 months. If 2 results below 0.5 ECEL, from samples collected at least 24 hours apart, are obtained, then exposure monitoring under this subsection need not be repeated unless there is a process, equipment, environment, or personnel change.
units.action_summary: Requires quarterly monitoring for high exposures and provides conditions for reducing or stopping monitoring.
units.modal_raw: must repeat / may be reduced / need not be repeated

units.obligation_text: The employer must repeat exposure monitoring at any time when process, equipment, environment, or personnel changes may reasonably cause new or additional exposures to NMP.
units.action_summary: Requires monitoring whenever workplace changes may cause new or increased exposures.

units.obligation_text: Each employer that performs commercial NMP paint and coating removal activities must develop and implement a written hazard communication program for the substance in each workplace.
units.actor: each employer that performs commercial NMP paint and coating removal activities
units.action_summary: Requires employers to develop and implement a written hazard communication program for NMP in each workplace.

units.obligation_text: The written program will, at a minimum, describe how the requirements of this section for labels, SDSs, other forms of warning material, and employee information and training will be satisfied. The employer must make the written hazard communication program available, upon request, to all employees, contractor employees, and their designated representatives.
units.action_summary: Written program must describe compliance with labeling/SDS/training requirements and must be made available on request to employees and representatives.

units.obligation_text: The employer may rely on an existing hazard communication program that satisfies the requirements of this paragraph.
units.action_summary: Permits employers to use an existing hazard communication program if it meets the requirements.

units.obligation_text: The written program must include a list of each NMP paint and coating removal product present in the work area. The list must be maintained in the work area and must use the identity provided on the appropriate SDS.
units.action_summary: Written program must list NMP products present and maintain the list in the work area using SDS identities.

units.obligation_text: The methods the employer will use to inform contractors of the presence of NMP paint and coating removal products in the employer’s workplace and of the provisions of this part applicable to the NMP products if employees of the contractor work in the employer’s workplace and are reasonably likely to be exposed to the NMP products while in the employer’s workplace.
units.action_summary: Written program must describe methods to inform contractors about NMP presence and applicable provisions when contractors' employees may be exposed.

units.obligation_text: Each employer must ensure that employees are provided with information and training on NMP paint and coating removal products. This information and training must be provided at the time of each employee’s initial assignment to using an NMP paint and coating removal product.
units.action_summary: Requires employers to provide information and training about NMP products at initial assignment.

units.obligation_text: Information provided to employees under this paragraph must include the requirements of this section.
units.action_summary: Employer-provided information must include the section's requirements.

units.obligation_text: Information provided to employees under this paragraph must include the location and availability of the written hazard communication program.
units.action_summary: Information must include where the written hazard communication program is located and how to access it.

units.obligation_text: Training provided to employees must include the potential human health hazards of the NMP paint and coating removal products as specified on the label.
units.action_summary: Training must cover potential human health hazards specified on labels.

units.obligation_text: Training provided to employees must include the measures employees can take to protect themselves from the NMP paint and coating removal products, including specific procedures the employer has implemented to protect employees from exposure to the substance, including appropriate work practices, emergency procedures, personal protective equipment, engineering controls, and other measures to control worker exposure.
units.action_summary: Training must explain protective measures employees can take and employer-implemented controls and procedures.

units.obligation_text: The employer need not take additional actions if existing programs and procedures satisfy the requirements of this section.
units.action_summary: Permits employers to rely on existing programs if they already meet the requirements.

units.obligation_text: Each person who manufactures, processes, or distributes in commerce NMP for any use after [date 45 calendar days after the date of publication of the final rule] must, prior to or concurrent with the shipment, notify companies to whom NMP is shipped, in writing, of the restrictions described in this subpart.
units.actor: Each person who manufactures, processes, or distributes in commerce NMP for any use after [date 45 calendar days after the date of publication of the final rule]
units.action_summary: Requires written downstream notification of subpart restrictions for NMP shipments after 45 days (Option 2).

units.obligation_text: Each person who manufactures, processes, or distributes in commerce any NMP after [date 45 calendar days after the date of publication of final rule] must retain in one location at the headquarters of the company documentation showing:
units.actor: Each person who manufactures, processes, or distributes in commerce any NMP after [date 45 calendar days after the date of publication of final rule]
units.action_summary: Requires companies to retain specified documentation at company headquarters for NMP shipped after 45 days (Option 2).

units.obligation_text: The name, address, contact, and telephone number of companies to whom NMP was shipped.
units.actor: Each person who manufactures, processes, or distributes in commerce any NMP after [date 45 calendar days after the date of publication of final rule]
units.action_summary: Requires retaining recipient contact information for NMP shipments.

units.obligation_text: A copy of the notification provided under § 751.209.
units.actor: Each person who manufactures, processes, or distributes in commerce any NMP after [date 45 calendar days after the date of publication of final rule]
units.action_summary: Requires retaining a copy of the downstream notification required under § 751.209.

units.obligation_text: The amount of NMP shipped.
units.actor: Each person who manufactures, processes, or distributes in commerce any NMP after [date 45 calendar days after the date of publication of final rule]
units.action_summary: Requires retaining records of the amount shipped.

units.obligation_text: The documentation in (a) must be retained for 3 years from the date of shipment.
units.actor: Each person who manufactures, processes, or distributes in commerce any NMP after [date 45 calendar days after the date of publication of final rule]
units.action_summary: Requires that the documentation be kept for 3 years from shipment.

ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION AGENCY

40 CFR Part 751

[EPA-HQ-OPPT-2016-0387; EPA-HQ-OPPT-2016-0231; FRL-9961-66]
RIN 2070-AK11 and RIN 2070-AK07

Trichloroethylene; Regulation of Vapor Degreasing Under TSCA 
Section 6(a); Methylene Chloride and N-Methylpyrrolidone; Regulation of 
Certain Uses Under TSCA Section 6(a); Reopening of Comment Periods

AGENCY: Environmental Protection Agency (EPA).

ACTION: Notice; Reopening of comment periods.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------

SUMMARY: In the Federal Register of January 19, 2017, EPA issued two 
proposed rules under section 6 of the Toxic Substances Control Act 
(TSCA). The first action proposed to prohibit the manufacture 
(including import), processing, and distribution in commerce of 
trichloroethylene (TCE) for use in vapor degreasing; to prohibit the 
use of TCE in vapor degreasing; to require manufacturers (including 
importers), processors, and distributors, except for retailers, of TCE 
for any use to provide downstream notification of these prohibitions 
throughout the supply chain; and to require limited recordkeeping. The 
second action proposed to prohibit the manufacture (including import), 
processing, and distribution in commerce of methylene chloride and N-
methylpyrrolidone (NMP) for consumer and most types of commercial paint 
and coating removal; to prohibit the use of methylene chloride and NMP 
in these commercial uses; to require manufacturers (including 
importers), processors, and distributors, except for retailers, of 
methylene chloride and NMP for any use to provide downstream 
notification of these prohibitions throughout the supply chain; and to 
require

[[Page 20311]]

recordkeeping. This document reopens and extends the comment periods 
for each proposed rule for an additional 30 days. Commenters requested 
additional time to submit written comments for the proposed rules.

DATES: Comments, identified by docket identification (ID) number EPA-
HQ-OPPT-2016-0387 and by docket identification (ID) number EPA-HQ-OPPT-
2016-0231 must be received on or before May 19, 2017.

ADDRESSES: Follow the detailed instructions provided under ADDRESSES in 
the Federal Register documents of January 19, 2017, (82 FR 7432) (FRL-
9950-08) or (82 FR 7464) (FRL-9958-57).

FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT: 
    For technical information contact: Cindy Wheeler, Chemical Control 
Division (7405M), Office of Pollution Prevention and Toxics, 
Environmental Protection Agency, 1200 Pennsylvania Ave. NW., 
Washington, DC 20460-0001; telephone number: 202-566-0484; email 
address: 
wheeler.cindy@epa.gov
 or Ana Corado, Chemical Control Division 
(7405M), Office of Pollution Prevention and Toxics, Environmental 
Protection Agency, 1200 Pennsylvania Ave. NW., Washington, DC 20460-
0001; telephone number: 202-564-0140; email address: 

corado.ana@epa.gov
.
    For general information contact: The TSCA-Hotline, ABVI-Goodwill, 
422 South Clinton Ave., Rochester, NY 14620; telephone number: (202) 
554-1404; email address: 
TSCA-Hotline@epa.gov
.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: This document reopens public comment periods 
established in the two proposed rules issued in the Federal Register of 
January 19, 2017 (82 FR 7432) (FRL-9950-08) and (82 FR 7464) (FRL-9958-
57). In the first action, EPA proposed a rule under section 6 of the 
Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA) to prohibit the manufacture 
(including import), processing, and distribution in commerce of 
trichloroethylene (TCE) for use in vapor degreasing; to prohibit the 
use of TCE in vapor degreasing; to require manufacturers (including 
importers), processors, and distributors, except for retailers, of TCE 
for any use to provide downstream notification of these prohibitions 
throughout the supply chain; and to require limited recordkeeping. In 
the second notice, EPA proposed a rule under section 6 of TSCA to 
prohibit the manufacture (including import), processing, and 
distribution in commerce of methylene chloride and N-methylpyrrolidone 
(NMP) for consumer and most types of commercial paint and coating 
removal; to prohibit the use of methylene chloride and NMP in these 
commercial uses; to require manufacturers (including importers), 
processors, and distributors, except for retailers, of methylene 
chloride and NMP for any use to provide downstream notification of 
these prohibitions throughout the supply chain; and to require 
recordkeeping. EPA is hereby reopening the comment periods for 30 days, 
to May 19, 2017.
    Even though EPA received requests for a lengthier extension of the 
comment periods, the Agency has concluded that a 30-day reopening of 
the comment period is sufficient. EPA has already provided for a 
substantial comment period, now totaling 90 days, for each of the two 
proposals. EPA has already extended the original 60-day comment period 
for the proposed rule in TCE in vapor degreasing for 30 days, from 
March 20, 2017, to April 19, 2017 (82 FR 10732, February 15, 2017). 
This notice provides the second extension of the comment period for 
that proposed rule. EPA proposed the rule on methylene chloride and NMP 
in paint and coating removal with a 90-day comment period, ending on 
April 19, 2017. Additionally, much of the technical bases for the 
proposals has been available to the public since the risk assessments 
for methylene chloride and TCE were published in 2014 and the risk 
assessment for NMP was published in 2015, and the commenters' expressed 
need for further extension was general in nature (e.g., the complexity 
and importance of the subject matter, and prospective commenters' 
desire to continue conferring and reviewing the technical basis for 
EPA's proposal). The Agency, therefore, is extending the comment period 
at its own discretion, in the interest of receiving comprehensive 
public comment for the benefit of the current rules.
    To submit comments, or access a docket, please follow the detailed 
instructions provided under ADDRESSES in the Federal Register documents 
of January 19, 2017, (82 FR 7432) (FRL-9950-08) or (82 FR 7464) (FRL-
9958-57). If you have questions, consult the technical person listed 
under FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT.

List of Subjects in 40 CFR Part 751

    Environmental protection, Chemicals, Export notification, Hazardous 
substances, Import certification, Methylene Chloride, N-
Methylpyrrolidone, Trichloroethylene, Recordkeeping.

    Dated: April 18, 2017.
Wendy Cleland-Hamnett,
Acting Assistant Administrator for Chemical Safety and Pollution 
Prevention.

title: TSCA Inventory Notification (Active-Inactive) Requirements

units.obligation_text: Any person who manufactured a chemical substance subject to commercial activity designation or who manufactured an interim active substance that is on the confidential portion of the TSCA Inventory, at any time during the lookback period, except as provided in § 710.27, must submit a Notice of Activity Form A as specified under § 710.29 and § 710.30.
units.actor: Any person who manufactured a chemical substance subject to commercial activity designation or an interim active substance on the confidential portion of the TSCA Inventory during the lookback period
units.action_summary: Submit a Notice of Activity Form A as specified in §§ 710.29 and 710.30

units.obligation_text: Any person who processed a chemical substance subject to commercial activity designation, at any time during the lookback period, except as provided in § 710.27, may submit a Notice of Activity Form A as specified under § 710.29 and § 710.30.
units.actor: Any person who processed a chemical substance subject to commercial activity designation during the lookback period
units.action_summary: May submit a Notice of Activity Form A as specified in §§ 710.29 and 710.30

units.obligation_text: Any person who intends to manufacture or process an inactive chemical substance, except as provided in § 710.27, after the effective date of the Administrator’s designation of such chemical substance as an inactive substance, must submit a Notice of Activity Form B as specified under § 710.29 and § 710.30.
units.actor: Any person who intends to manufacture or process an inactive chemical substance after designation as inactive
units.action_summary: Submit a Notice of Activity Form B as specified in §§ 710.29 and 710.30 prior to manufacturing or processing

units.obligation_text: The following activities do not trigger notification requirements under this subpart:
units.actor: Persons engaging in the listed activities
units.action_summary: Lists activities that are excepted from notification requirements

units.obligation_text: The manufacturing or processing of a chemical substance solely in small quantities for research and development.
units.actor: Persons manufacturing or processing solely in small quantities for R&D
units.action_summary: Such manufacturing/processing does not trigger notification requirements

units.obligation_text: The import of a chemical substance as part of an article.
units.actor: Persons importing chemical substances as part of an article
units.action_summary: Import as part of an article does not trigger notification requirements

units.obligation_text: The manufacturing or processing of a chemical substance as described in § 720.30(g) or (h).
units.actor: Persons manufacturing or processing as described in § 720.30(g) or (h)
units.action_summary: Manufacturing/processing described in §720.30(g) or (h) does not trigger notification requirements

units.obligation_text: Manufacturing or processing naturally occurring chemical substances. The following activities do not trigger notification requirements under this subpart:
units.actor: Persons manufacturing or processing naturally occurring chemical substances as described
units.action_summary: Lists exemptions for manufacturing/processing naturally occurring chemical substances

units.obligation_text: The manufacture of a naturally occurring chemical substance, as described in § 710.4(b). Some chemical substances can be manufactured both as described in § 710.4(b) and by means other than those described in § 710.4(b). If a person manufactures a chemical substance by means other than those described in § 710.4(b), this exemption is inapplicable, regardless of whether the chemical substance also could have been produced as described in § 710.4(b). This exemption does not cover the manufacture of a chemical substance from a naturally occurring chemical substance.
units.actor: Persons manufacturing naturally occurring chemical substances as described in § 710.4(b)
units.action_summary: Manufacture as described in § 710.4(b) is exempt from notification unless manufactured by other means or made from a naturally occurring chemical substance

units.obligation_text: The processing of a naturally occurring chemical substance only by manual, mechanical, or gravitational means; by dissolution in water; by flotation; or by heating solely to remove water.
units.actor: Persons processing naturally occurring chemical substances by listed means
units.action_summary: Processing by these limited means does not trigger notification requirements

units.obligation_text: Any person who reports information to EPA, including post-notification substantiation of confidentiality claims under § 710.37(b), must do so using the e-NOA software module, the CISS reporting tool, and the CDX electronic reporting portal provided by EPA at the addresses set forth in § 710.39.
units.actor: Any person who reports information to EPA under this part
units.action_summary: Use e-NOA, CISS, and CDX to report information to EPA

units.obligation_text: For notices of activity under § 710.25(a) and § 710.25(b), the submission must include all information described in paragraph (b) of this section. For a Notice of Activity under § 710.25(c), the submission must include all information described in paragraph (c) of this section.
units.action_summary: Include the specified information in submissions: paragraph (b) for Forms A and paragraph (c) for Form B

units.obligation_text: A person must submit a separate form for each chemical substance that the person is required to report.
units.actor: A person required to report chemical substances
units.action_summary: Submit a separate form for each chemical substance required to be reported

units.obligation_text: CDX, CISS, and e-NOA allow a person to report multiple chemical substances in one session that will be transmitted to EPA on separate forms.
units.action_summary: May report multiple substances in one session though transmitted as separate forms

units.obligation_text: Any person submitting a Notice of Activity Form A under § 710.25(a) or § 710.25(b) must submit the information described in this paragraph for each reportable chemical substance during the submission period specified in § 710.30(a).
units.actor: Any person submitting a Notice of Activity Form A under § 710.25(a) or § 710.25(b)
units.action_summary: Submit the listed information for each reportable chemical substance during the specified submission period

units.obligation_text: Information specified in § 710.29(d).
units.actor: Persons submitting Notice of Activity Form A
units.action_summary: Provide the information required by § 710.29(d)

units.obligation_text: The type of commercial activity for each reportable chemical substance: Whether the chemical substance was domestically manufactured in the United States, imported into the United States, or both domestically manufactured in the United States and imported into the United States during the lookback period.
units.actor: Persons submitting Notice of Activity Form A
units.action_summary: Report whether each substance was manufactured domestically, imported, or both during the lookback period

units.obligation_text: The first date and the last date that each reportable chemical substance was domestically manufactured in the United States, imported into the United States, or both domestically manufactured in the United States and imported into the United States during the lookback period.
units.actor: Persons submitting Notice of Activity Form A
units.action_summary: Report the first and last dates of manufacture/import during the lookback period for each substance

units.obligation_text: Any person submitting a Notice of Activity Form B under § 710.25(c) must provide the information described in this paragraph for each inactive chemical substance intended to be manufactured or processed at the time specified in § 710.30(b).
units.actor: Any person submitting a Notice of Activity Form B under § 710.25(c)
units.action_summary: Provide the listed information for each inactive substance intended to be manufactured or processed at the specified time

units.obligation_text: Information specified in § 710.29(d).
units.actor: Persons submitting Notice of Activity Form B
units.action_summary: Provide the information required by § 710.29(d)

units.obligation_text: The type of intended commercial activity for the inactive substance: Whether the inactive substance is intended to be domestically manufactured in the United States, imported into the United States, processed in the United States, or a particular combination of these.
units.actor: Persons submitting Notice of Activity Form B
units.action_summary: Report the intended commercial activity (manufacture, import, process, or combination) for the inactive substance

units.obligation_text: The actual date by which the inactive substance is to be domestically manufactured in the United States, imported into the United States, or processed in the United States.
units.actor: Persons submitting Notice of Activity Form B
units.action_summary: Provide the actual date by which the inactive substance will be manufactured, imported, or processed

units.obligation_text: Information to be reported on either the Notice of Activity Form A or Form B.
units.actor: Persons submitting either Form A or Form B
units.action_summary: Provide the listed company, contact, and chemical-specific information on either form

units.obligation_text: Company. The name of the submitting company.
units.action_summary: Provide the name of the submitting company on the form

units.obligation_text: Authorized official. The name and address of the authorized official for the submitting company.
units.action_summary: Provide the name and address of the authorized official for the submitting company

units.obligation_text: Technical contact. The name and telephone number of a person who will serve as technical contact for the submitting company and who will be able to answer questions about the information submitted by the company to EPA.
units.action_summary: Provide a technical contact name and telephone number able to answer questions about submitted information

units.obligation_text: Chemical-specific information. The correct CA Index name as used to list the chemical substance on the Inventory and the correct corresponding CASRN must be submitted for each reportable chemical substance. Persons who wish to report chemical substances listed on the confidential portion of the TSCA Inventory must report the chemical substances using a TSCA Accession Number and generic name.
units.actor: Persons submitting either Form A or Form B
units.action_summary: Provide correct CA Index name and CASRN for each reportable substance; confidential-list substances must be reported using TSCA Accession Number and generic name

units.obligation_text: If an importer submitting a notice cannot provide the information specified in § 710.29(d)(4) because it is unknown to the importer and claimed as confidential by the supplier of the chemical substance or mixture, the importer must ask the supplier to provide the specific chemical identity information directly to EPA in a joint submission using the same e-NOA software module used for commercial activity reporting. Such request must include instructions for submitting chemical identity information electronically, using e-NOA, CISS, and CDX (see § 710.39), and for clearly referencing the importer’s submission. Contact information for the supplier, a trade name or other name for the chemical substance or mixture, and a copy of the request to the supplier must be included with the importer’s submission with respect to the chemical substance.
units.actor: Importer submitting a notice who cannot provide chemical identity information
units.action_summary: Ask the supplier to submit specific chemical identity directly to EPA via joint electronic submission and include supplier contact info, trade name, and copy of the request with the importer's submission

units.obligation_text: If a manufacturer or processor submitting a notice cannot provide the information specified in § 710.29(d)(4) because the reportable chemical substance is manufactured or processed using a reactant having a specific chemical identity that is unknown to the manufacturer or processor and claimed as confidential by its supplier, the manufacturer or processor must ask the supplier of the confidential reactant to provide the specific chemical identity of the confidential reactant directly to EPA in a joint submission using the same e-NOA software module used for commercial activity reporting. Such request must include instructions for submitting chemical identity information electronically using e-NOA, CISS, and CDX (see § 710.39), and for clearly referencing the manufacturer’s or processor’s submission. Contact information for the supplier, a trade name or other name for the chemical substance, and a copy of the request to the supplier must be included with the manufacturer’s or processor’s submission with respect to the chemical substance.
units.actor: Manufacturer or processor who cannot provide chemical identity information due to supplier confidentiality
units.action_summary: Request the supplier to submit the confidential reactant identity directly to EPA via joint electronic submission and include supplier contact info, trade name, and copy of the request with the submission

units.obligation_text: EPA will only accept joint submissions that are submitted electronically using e-NOA, CISS, and CDX (see § 710.39) and that clearly reference the primary submission to which they refer.
units.actor: Submitters of joint submissions to EPA
units.action_summary: Joint submissions must be submitted electronically via e-NOA, CISS, and CDX and clearly reference the primary submission to be accepted by EPA

units.obligation_text: Certification statement. The authorized official must certify that the submitted information has been completed in compliance with the requirements of this part and that the confidentiality claims made on the form are true and correct using the certification statement in this paragraph.
units.actor: Authorized official of the submitting company
units.action_summary: Certify that the submission is complete and that confidentiality claims are true and correct, using the required certification statement

units.obligation_text: The certification must be signed and dated by the authorized official for the submitting company.
units.actor: Authorized official of the submitting company
units.action_summary: Sign and date the certification statement

units.obligation_text: The following is the required certification language: "I certify under penalty of law that this document and all attachments were prepared under my direction or supervision and the information contained therein, to the best of my knowledge is, true, accurate, and complete. I am aware there are significant penalties for submitting incomplete, false and/or misleading information, including the possibility of fine and imprisonment for knowing violations."
units.actor: Authorized official of the submitting company
units.action_summary: Use the specified certification language when certifying submissions

units.obligation_text: The Notice of Activity Form A required to be submitted under § 710.25(a) must be submitted during the applicable submission period.
units.actor: Persons required to submit Notice of Activity Form A
units.action_summary: Submit Form A within the applicable submission period

units.obligation_text: Manufacturers. The submission period for manufacturers under § 710.25(a) begins on [date on which the final rule is published in the Federal Register] and ends on [180 days after the date on which the final rule is published in the Federal Register].
units.action_summary: Defines the submission period start and end dates for manufacturers (publication date to 180 days after)

units.obligation_text: Processors. The submission period for processors under § 710.25(b) begins on [date on which the final rule is published in the Federal Register] and ends on [360 days after the date on which the final rule is published in the Federal Register].
units.action_summary: Defines the submission period start and end dates for processors (publication date to 360 days after)

units.obligation_text: The Notice of Activity Form B required to be submitted under § 710.25(c) must be submitted before a person manufactures or processes the inactive substance, but not more than 30 days prior to the actual date of manufacturing or processing.
units.actor: Persons required to submit Notice of Activity Form B
units.action_summary: Submit Form B before manufacturing or processing an inactive substance, but no more than 30 days prior to the actual date

units.obligation_text: When, in a single instance of manufacturing or importing a particular volume of a chemical substance during the lookback period, two or more persons qualify as the manufacturer or importer of that volume, they may determine among themselves who should make the required submission under § 710.25(a).
units.actor: Two or more persons who qualify as manufacturer or importer for the same volume
units.action_summary: May decide among themselves who will submit the required Form A

units.obligation_text: If no notice is submitted as required under this subpart, EPA will hold each such person liable for failure to submit a notice.
units.action_summary: EPA will hold each person who qualified as manufacturer/importer liable if no required notice is submitted

units.obligation_text: If two or more persons intend to manufacture, import, or process a particular volume of an inactive substance, such that multiple persons would qualify as the manufacturer, importer, or processor of that volume, they may determine among themselves who will submit the required notice under § 710.25(c).
units.actor: Two or more prospective co-manufacturers or co-processors
units.action_summary: May decide among themselves who will submit the required Form B

units.obligation_text: If no notice is submitted as required under this subpart, all of the persons remain subject to the reporting requirements, and EPA will hold each such person liable for a failure to submit a notice prior to the date of manufacturing, importing, or processing.
units.actor: All persons who would qualify as manufacturer/importer/processor; EPA (enforcement)
units.action_summary: All persons remain subject to reporting requirements and EPA will hold each liable if no notice is submitted prior to manufacturing/importing/processing

units.obligation_text: Each person who is subject to the notification requirements of this part must retain records that document any information reported to EPA.
units.actor: Each person subject to the notification requirements
units.action_summary: Retain records documenting any information reported to EPA

units.obligation_text: Records relevant to a notice of activity under § 710.25(a) and § 710.25(b) must be retained for a period of 5 years beginning on the last day of the submission period.
units.actor: Each person subject to the notification requirements for Notices under §§ 710.25(a) and 710.25(b)
units.action_summary: Retain records relevant to Forms A for 5 years starting the last day of the submission period

units.obligation_text: Records relevant to a notice of activity under § 710.25(c) must be retained for a period of 5 years beginning on the day that the notice was submitted.
units.actor: Each person subject to the notification requirements for Notices under § 710.25(c)
units.action_summary: Retain records relevant to Form B for 5 years starting the day the notice was submitted

units.obligation_text: Any persons submitting information under this part may request to maintain an existing claim of confidentiality for the specific chemical identity of a reportable chemical substance only if the identity of the chemical substance is listed on the confidential portion of the TSCA Inventory as of the time the notice is submitted for that chemical substance under this part.
units.actor: Persons submitting information under this part
units.action_summary: May request to maintain an existing confidentiality claim for specific chemical identity only if the identity is listed as confidential on the Inventory at time of submission

units.obligation_text: Any such requests to maintain an existing claim of confidentiality must be made at the time the information is submitted.
units.actor: Persons submitting information and requesting confidentiality
units.action_summary: Make requests to maintain confidentiality at the time of submission

units.obligation_text: If no person submitting the information specified in § 710.29(d)(4) for a particular chemical substance requests that the claim be maintained, EPA will treat the specific chemical identity of that chemical substance as not subject to a confidentiality claim and will move the chemical substance to the public portion of the TSCA Inventory.
units.action_summary: If no request to maintain confidentiality is made for a particular chemical identity, EPA will treat it as not confidential and move it to the public Inventory

units.obligation_text: The following steps must be taken to maintain an existing claim of confidentiality for the specific chemical identity of a reportable chemical substance.
units.action_summary: Follow the listed steps to maintain an existing confidentiality claim for specific chemical identity

units.obligation_text: A person requesting to maintain an existing claim of confidentiality for specific chemical identity may submit with the notice detailed written answers to the questions in paragraph (1)(iii) of this section, signed and dated by an authorized official.
units.actor: Person requesting to maintain confidentiality on Form A
units.action_summary: May submit early detailed written answers to specified substantiation questions with the notice, signed and dated by an authorized official

units.obligation_text: If these early answers are received less than five years before the date on which substantiation is due pursuant to TSCA Section 8(b)(4)(D)(i) the early answers will be deemed to be substantiations made under TSCA Section (8)(b)(4)(D)(i) and the person will be exempt from further substantiation requirements under Section (8)(b)(4)(D)(i). Early answers that do not include the answers to questions in paragraph (1)(iii) of this section will not be deemed to be substantiations made under the TSCA section (8)(b)(4)(D)(i) requirement.
units.actor: EPA (in determining sufficiency of early answers); person submitting early answers (effect)
units.action_summary: Early answers received within five years of substantiation due date will be deemed substantiations and exempt the person from further substantiation; early answers lacking required detail will not be deemed substantiation
units.modal_raw: will be deemed / will not be deemed

units.obligation_text: A person requesting to maintain an existing claim of confidentiality for specific chemical identity must submit detailed written answers to the questions in paragraph (1)(iii) of this section within 30 days of submitting the notice, signed and dated by an authorized official.
units.actor: Person requesting to maintain confidentiality on Form B
units.action_summary: Submit detailed written substantiation answers within 30 days of submitting Form B, signed and dated by an authorized official

units.obligation_text: If this information is not submitted within 30 days of submitting the notice, EPA will consider the specific chemical identity as not subject to a confidentiality claim and may make the information public without further notice.
units.action_summary: If substantiation is not provided within 30 days, EPA will treat the chemical identity as not confidential and may make it public

units.obligation_text: If any of the information contained in the answers to the questions listed in paragraph (a)(1)(iii) of this section is asserted to be confidential, the submitter must clearly identify the information that is claimed as confidential by marking the specific information on each page with a label such as 'confidential business information,' 'proprietary,' or 'trade secret.'
units.actor: Submitter asserting confidentiality for information in substantiation answers
units.action_summary: Clearly identify and mark with appropriate labels any information asserted confidential in the substantiation answers

units.obligation_text: Any persons submitting information under this part may assert a claim of confidentiality for information other than specific chemical identity. Any such confidentiality claims must be made at the time the information is submitted.
units.actor: Persons submitting information under this part
units.action_summary: May assert confidentiality claims for non-identity information, but must make such claims at time of submission

units.obligation_text: Confidentiality claims cannot be made when a response field on a reporting form is left blank or designated as not known or reasonably ascertainable.
units.actor: Persons submitting information under this part
units.action_summary: Prohibits making confidentiality claims for response fields left blank or marked unknown/not reasonably ascertainable

units.obligation_text: The following steps must be taken to assert a claim of confidentiality for information other than specific chemical identity. If no claim is asserted at the time the information is submitted, or if the following steps are not taken, EPA will consider the information as not subject to a confidentiality claim and may make the information public without further notice.
units.actor: Persons seeking to assert confidentiality for non-identity information; EPA (consequence)
units.action_summary: Follow the listed substantiation steps at time of submission, or EPA will treat the information as not confidential and may publish it

units.obligation_text: A person asserting a claim of confidentiality for information other than specific chemical identity must submit detailed written answers to the following questions at the time of submission, signed and dated by an authorized official.
units.actor: Person asserting a claim of confidentiality for non-identity information
units.action_summary: Submit detailed written substantiation answers at time of submission, signed and dated by an authorized official

title: Procedures for Prioritization of Chemicals for Risk Evaluation under Toxic Substances Control Act

units.obligation_text: EPA will make priority designations pursuant to these procedures for a chemical substance, not for a specific condition or conditions of use of a chemical substance.
units.action_summary: EPA must make priority designations for an entire chemical substance, not for specific conditions of use.

units.obligation_text: The Agency will publish a final priority designation for a chemical substance in no fewer than 9 months and no longer than 1 year following initiation of prioritization pursuant to 40 CFR 702.9.
units.action_summary: EPA must publish a final priority designation between 9 months and 1 year after initiation of prioritization.

units.obligation_text: in no fewer than 9 months
units.action_summary: Minimum timeframe: at least 9 months after initiation to publish final designation.

units.obligation_text: and no longer than 1 year following initiation of prioritization pursuant to 40 CFR 702.9.
units.action_summary: Maximum timeframe: no more than 1 year after initiation to publish final designation.

units.obligation_text: In identifying priorities for chemical substances that are metals or metal compounds, EPA will, as appropriate, refer to relevant considerations from the Framework for Metals Assessment of the Office of the Science Advisor, Risk Assessment Forum, dated March 2007, or a successor document that addresses metals risk assessment and is peer reviewed by the Science Advisory Board.
units.action_summary: When prioritizing metals or metal compounds, EPA should refer as appropriate to the Framework for Metals Assessment or successor peer-reviewed document.

units.obligation_text: These regulations do not apply to any chemical substance for which a manufacturer requests a risk evaluation under TSCA section 6(b)(4)(C) (15 U.S.C. 2605(b)(4)(C)).
units.action_summary: The rules in this subpart do not apply to substances for which a manufacturer requests a risk evaluation under the specified TSCA provision.

units.obligation_text: In identifying potential candidates for High-Priority Substances, EPA will generally consider whether information available to the Agency suggests there is hazard and exposure under a condition or conditions of use, and whether a risk evaluation would be needed to determine whether there is an unreasonable risk of injury to health or the environment.
units.action_summary: EPA should generally consider available information about hazard and exposure and whether a risk evaluation is needed when identifying High-Priority candidates.

units.obligation_text: In identifying potential candidates for Low-Priority Substances, EPA will generally consider whether information available to the EPA suggests such low hazard and/or exposure under all conditions of use that EPA is confident the chemical substances does not present an unreasonable risk of injury to health or the environment, including an unreasonable risk to potentially exposed or susceptible subpopulations identified as relevant by EPA, even in the absence of a risk evaluation.
units.action_summary: EPA should generally consider whether available information indicates very low hazard/exposure across all uses when identifying Low-Priority candidates.

units.obligation_text: In identifying potential candidates for prioritization, EPA will generally evaluate whether or not the chemical substance meets one or more of the following exposure or hazard considerations:
units.action_summary: EPA should generally evaluate whether the substance meets one or more listed exposure or hazard considerations when identifying prioritization candidates.

units.obligation_text: Persistent, bioaccumulative, and toxic;
units.action_summary: Consider whether the substance is persistent, bioaccumulative, and toxic.

units.obligation_text: Used in children’s products;
units.action_summary: Consider whether the substance is used in children's products.

units.obligation_text: Used in consumer products;
units.action_summary: Consider whether the substance is used in consumer products.

units.obligation_text: Detected in human and/or ecological biomonitoring programs;
units.action_summary: Consider whether the substance is detected in human or ecological biomonitoring programs.

units.obligation_text: Potentially of concern for children’s health;
units.action_summary: Consider whether the substance is potentially of concern for children's health.

units.obligation_text: High acute and chronic toxicity;
units.action_summary: Consider whether the substance has high acute and chronic toxicity.

units.obligation_text: Probable or known carcinogen;
units.action_summary: Consider whether the substance is a probable or known carcinogen.

units.obligation_text: Neurotoxicity;
units.action_summary: Consider whether the substance exhibits neurotoxicity.

units.obligation_text: Other emerging exposure and hazard concerns to human health or the environment, as determined by the Agency.
units.action_summary: Consider other emerging exposure or hazard concerns as determined by EPA.

units.obligation_text: Therefore, EPA will generally review and analyze the information necessary for both prioritization and risk evaluation prior to initiating the prioritization process for a chemical substance pursuant to 40 CFR 702.9.
units.action_summary: EPA generally will review and analyze information needed for prioritization and risk evaluation before initiating prioritization.

units.obligation_text: The availability of information and resources necessary and sufficient to support a priority designation pursuant to 40 CFR 702.11, a risk evaluation pursuant to 40 CFR 702, subpart B, or other such action as determined by the Administrator;
units.action_summary: EPA should consider whether information and resources are available to support a priority designation or risk evaluation.

units.obligation_text: The ability of EPA to timely develop or require development of information necessary and sufficient to support a priority designation pursuant to 40 CFR 702.11; a risk evaluation pursuant to 40 CFR 702, subpart B; or other such action as determined by the Agency.
units.action_summary: EPA should consider its ability to timely develop or require development of necessary information.

units.obligation_text: In the absence of sufficient information to support a priority designation pursuant to 40 CFR 702.11, a risk evaluation pursuant to 40 CFR 702, subpart B, or other such action as determined by the Agency, EPA may use its authorities under the Act, and other information gathering authorities, to gather or require the generation of the needed information on a chemical substance before initiating the prioritization process for that chemical substance.
units.action_summary: If information is insufficient, EPA may use its authorities to gather or require generation of information before initiating prioritization.

units.obligation_text: In selecting a candidate for prioritization as a High-Priority Substance, EPA will: (1) Give preference to: (A) Chemical substances that are listed in the 2014 update of the TSCA Work Plan for Chemical Assessments as having a persistence and bioaccumulation score of 3, and (B) Chemical substances that are listed in the 2014 update of the TSCA Work Plan for Chemical Assessments that are known human carcinogens and have high acute and chronic toxicity; and (2) Identify a sufficient number of candidates from the 2014 update of the TSCA Work Plan for Chemical Assessments to ensure that, at any given time, at least 50 percent of risk evaluations being conducted by EPA are drawn from that list until all substances on the list have been designated as either a High-Priority Substance or Low-Priority Substance pursuant to 40 CFR 702.13.
units.action_summary: When selecting High-Priority candidates, EPA must give specified preferences and identify enough candidates so that at least 50% of ongoing risk evaluations come from the TSCA Work Plan list until all listed substances are designated.

units.obligation_text: Give preference to chemical substances that are listed in the 2014 update of the TSCA Work Plan for Chemical Assessments as having a persistence and bioaccumulation score of 3.
units.action_summary: EPA should prefer substances on the 2014 Work Plan list with a persistence and bioaccumulation score of 3.

units.obligation_text: Give preference to chemical substances that are listed in the 2014 update of the TSCA Work Plan for Chemical Assessments that are known human carcinogens and have high acute and chronic toxicity.
units.action_summary: EPA should prefer substances on the 2014 Work Plan list that are known human carcinogens with high toxicity.

units.obligation_text: Identify a sufficient number of candidates from the 2014 update of the TSCA Work Plan for Chemical Assessments to ensure that, at any given time, at least 50 percent of risk evaluations being conducted by EPA are drawn from that list until all substances on the list have been designated as either a High-Priority Substance or Low-Priority Substance pursuant to 40 CFR 702.13.
units.action_summary: EPA must select enough candidates from the Work Plan list so that at least 50% of ongoing risk evaluations are from that list until all listed substances are designated.

units.obligation_text: EPA is not required to select candidates or initiate prioritization pursuant to 40 CFR 702.9 in any ranked or hierarchical order.
units.action_summary: EPA is not obligated to select candidates or begin prioritization in ranked or hierarchical order.

units.obligation_text: Following selection of a candidate chemical substance, EPA will generally use available information to screen the candidate chemical substance against the following criteria and considerations:
units.action_summary: EPA generally will screen a selected candidate using available information against listed criteria.

units.obligation_text: The chemical substance’s hazard and exposure potential;
units.action_summary: Consider hazard and exposure potential in screening.

units.obligation_text: The chemical substance’s persistence and bioaccumulation;
units.action_summary: Consider persistence and bioaccumulation in screening.

units.obligation_text: Potentially exposed or susceptible subpopulations;
units.action_summary: Consider potentially exposed or susceptible subpopulations in screening.

units.obligation_text: Storage of the chemical substance near significant sources of drinking water;
units.action_summary: Consider storage near drinking water sources in screening.

units.obligation_text: The chemical substance’s conditions of use or significant changes in conditions of use;
units.action_summary: Consider conditions of use or significant changes thereto in screening.

units.obligation_text: The chemical substance’s production volume or significant changes in production volume; and
units.action_summary: Consider production volume or significant changes in production volume in screening.

units.obligation_text: Any other risk-based criteria relevant to the designation of the chemical substance’s priority, in EPA’s discretion.
units.action_summary: Consider other risk-based criteria relevant to priority designation, at EPA's discretion.

units.obligation_text: In conducting the screening review in paragraph (c) of this section, EPA expects to consider sources of information relevant to the listed criteria, including, as appropriate, sources for hazard and exposure data listed in Appendices A and B of the TSCA Work Plan Chemicals: Methods Document (February 2012).
units.action_summary: EPA expects to consider appropriate information sources, including specified appendices, when conducting the screening review.

units.obligation_text: EPA generally expects to initiate the prioritization process for a chemical substance only when it believes that all or most of the information necessary to prioritize and perform a risk evaluation on the substance already exists.
units.action_summary: EPA generally will initiate prioritization only when most or all necessary information already exists.

units.obligation_text: EPA will initiate prioritization by publishing a notice in the Federal Register identifying a chemical substance for prioritization and the results of the screening review conducted pursuant to 40 CFR 702.7(c).
units.action_summary: EPA must publish a Federal Register notice identifying the chemical and screening review results to initiate prioritization.

units.obligation_text: The prioritization timeframe in 40 CFR 702.1(d) begins upon EPA’s publication of the notice described in paragraph (b) of this section.
units.action_summary: The timeframe for prioritization (9 months to 1 year) starts when EPA publishes the Federal Register notice.

units.obligation_text: The results of the screening review published pursuant to paragraph (b) of this section will identify, in a form and manner that EPA deems appropriate, the information analysis and basis used in conducting the screening process. Subject to 15 U.S.C. 2613, copies of the information will also be placed in a public docket established for each chemical substance.
units.action_summary: EPA must identify the information, analysis, and basis used in the screening and, subject to confidentiality law, place copies in a public docket for each chemical.

units.obligation_text: Publication of a notice in the Federal Register pursuant to paragraph (b) of this section will initiate a period of 90 days during which interested persons may submit relevant information on that chemical substance.
units.action_summary: After EPA's notice, interested persons are permitted to submit relevant information during a 90-day comment period.

units.obligation_text: EPA may, in its discretion, extend the public comment period in paragraph (b) of this section for up to three months in order to receive or evaluate information submitted under 15 U.S.C. 2603(a)(2)(B).
units.action_summary: EPA may extend the public comment period at its discretion to receive or evaluate certain submitted information.

units.obligation_text: for up to three months
units.action_summary: The extension period may be up to three months.

units.obligation_text: Based on the results of the screening review in 40 CFR 702.7(c), relevant information received from the public as described in 40 CFR 702.9(e), and other information as appropriate and in EPA’s discretion, EPA will propose to designate the chemical substance as either a High-Priority Substance or Low-Priority Substance.
units.action_summary: EPA will propose to designate the chemical as High- or Low-Priority based on screening, public comments, and other information.

units.obligation_text: EPA will not consider costs or other non-risk factors in making a proposed priority designation.
units.action_summary: EPA is prohibited from considering costs or other non-risk factors when making a proposed priority designation.

units.obligation_text: If information available to EPA remains insufficient to enable the proposed designation of the chemical substance as a Low-Priority Substance, including after any extension of the initial public comment period pursuant to 40 CFR 702.9(f), EPA will propose to designate the chemical substance as a High-Priority Substance.
units.action_summary: If EPA lacks sufficient information to propose Low-Priority designation (even after comment extension), it must propose High-Priority designation.

units.obligation_text: EPA may propose to designate a chemical substance as a High-Priority Substance based on the proposed conclusion that the chemical substance satisfies the definition of High-Priority Substance in 40 CFR 702.3 under any one or more uses that the Agency determines constitute conditions of use as defined in 15 U.S.C. 2602.
units.action_summary: EPA may propose a High-Priority designation based on a conclusion that the chemical meets the High-Priority definition for one or more uses.

units.obligation_text: EPA will propose to designate a chemical substance as a Low-Priority Substance based only on the proposed conclusion that the chemical substance satisfies the definition of Low-Priority Substance in 40 CFR 702.3 under all uses that the Agency determines constitute conditions of use as defined in 15 U.S.C. 2602.
units.action_summary: EPA may propose a Low-Priority designation only if it concludes the chemical meets the Low-Priority definition across all uses.

units.obligation_text: EPA will publish the proposed designation in the Federal Register, along with an identification of the information, analysis and basis used to support a proposed designation, in a form and manner that EPA deems appropriate, and provide a comment period of 90 days, during which time the public may submit comment on EPA’s proposed designation.
units.action_summary: EPA must publish the proposed designation with supporting information and provide a 90-day public comment period during which the public may comment.

units.obligation_text: during which time the public may submit comment on EPA’s proposed designation.
units.action_summary: The public is permitted to submit comments on the proposed designation within the 90-day period.

units.obligation_text: For chemical substances that EPA proposes to designate as Low-Priority Substances, EPA will specify in the notice published pursuant to paragraph (e) of this section that all comments that could be raised on the issues in the proposed designation must be presented during this comment period.

Mercury; Reporting Requirements for the TSCA Mercury Inventory; 
Extension of Comment Period

AGENCY: Environmental Protection Agency (EPA).

ACTION: Proposed rule; extension of comment period.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------

SUMMARY: EPA issued a document in the Federal Register of October 26, 
2017, concerning proposed reporting requirements for applicable persons 
to provide information to assist in the preparation of an ``inventory 
of mercury supply, use, and trade in the United States.'' This document 
extends the comment period for 16 days, from December 26, 2017 to 
January 11, 2018. EPA received requests to extend the comment period 
and believes it is appropriate to do so in order to give stakeholders 
additional time to assess the impacts of the proposal, review technical 
documents in the docket, and prepare comments.

DATES: Comments, identified by docket identification number EPA-HQ-
OPPT-2017-0421, must be received on or before January 11, 2018.

ADDRESSES: Follow the detailed instructions provided under ADDRESSES in 
the Federal Register document of October 26, 2017 (82 FR 49564) (FRL-
9970-07).

FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT: 
    For technical information contact: Thomas Groeneveld, National 
Program Chemicals Division, Office of Pollution Prevention and Toxics, 
Environmental Protection Agency, 1200 Pennsylvania Ave. NW, Washington, 
DC 20460-0001; telephone number: (202) 566-1188; email address: 

[email protected]
.
    For general information contact: The TSCA-Hotline, ABVI-Goodwill, 
422 South Clinton Ave., Rochester, NY 14620; telephone number: (202) 
554-1404; email address: 
[email protected]
.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: This document extends the public comment 
period established in the Federal Register document of October 26, 2017 
(82 FR 49564) (FRL-9970-07). EPA is hereby extending the comment 
period, which was set to end on December 26, 2017, to January 11, 2018.
    To submit comments, or access the docket, please follow the 
detailed instructions provided under ADDRESSES in the Federal Register 
document of October 26, 2017 (82 FR 49564) (FRL-9970-07). If you have 
questions, consult the technical person listed under FOR FURTHER 
INFORMATION CONTACT.

compounds, Inventory, Supply, Use, Trade, Manufacture, Import, Export.
