units.obligation_text: For lead content of materials that are provided as a range, the maximum content of the range must be used.
units.actor: person determining lead content (e.g., manufacturer, tester)
units.action_summary: Use the maximum value of any provided range when calculating lead content.

units.obligation_text: If a coating ... is applied to the internal surfaces of a pipe, fitting or fixture component, the maximum lead content of both the coating and the alloy must be used to calculate the lead content of the component.
units.actor: person determining lead content (e.g., manufacturer, tester)
units.action_summary: Include the maximum lead content of both coating and alloy when calculating component lead content.

units.obligation_text: If a liner ... is manufactured into a pipe, fitting or fixture, the maximum lead content of the liner must be used to calculate the lead content of the component.
units.actor: person determining lead content (e.g., manufacturer, tester)
units.action_summary: Use the liner's maximum lead content in component lead calculations.

units.obligation_text: No person may use any pipe, any pipe or plumbing fitting or fixture, any solder or any flux that is not lead free as defined in § 143.12 in the installation or repair of:
units.action_summary: Prohibits use of non-lead-free pipes, fittings, fixtures, solder or flux in specified installations or repairs.

units.obligation_text: Any public water system.
units.action_summary: Specifies that the prohibition in §143.13(a) applies to public water systems (use prohibited).

units.obligation_text: Any plumbing in a residential or nonresidential facility providing water for human consumption.
units.action_summary: Specifies that the prohibition in §143.13(a) applies to plumbing providing water for human consumption (use prohibited).

units.obligation_text: Paragraph (a) of this section shall not apply to leaded joints necessary for the repair of cast iron pipes.
units.actor: persons performing repairs on cast iron pipes
units.action_summary: Allows use of leaded joints when necessary to repair cast iron pipes (exception to §143.13(a)).

units.obligation_text: As a condition of receiving a full allotment of Public Water System Supervision grants under section 1443(a) of the Safe Drinking Water Act, states must enforce the requirements of section 1417(a)(1) of Safe Drinking Water Act and § 143.13 through state or local plumbing codes, or such other means of enforcement as the state may determine to be appropriate.
units.action_summary: States must enforce section 1417(a)(1) and §143.13 by codes or other appropriate means as a condition for receiving full grant allotments.

units.obligation_text: It shall be unlawful for any person to introduce into commerce any pipe, or any pipe or plumbing fitting or fixture, that is not lead free, except for a pipe that is used in manufacturing or industrial processing;
units.action_summary: Prohibits introducing into commerce any non-lead-free pipe or fitting, with an exception for pipes used in manufacturing/industrial processing.

units.obligation_text: Except for a pipe that is used in manufacturing or industrial processing.
units.actor: persons introducing pipes used in manufacturing/industrial processing
units.action_summary: Allows introduction into commerce of non-lead-free pipes when used in manufacturing or industrial processing (exception to §143.15(a)).

units.obligation_text: It shall be unlawful for any person engaged in the business of selling plumbing supplies in the United States, except manufacturers, to sell solder or flux that is not lead free;
units.actor: persons engaged in the business of selling plumbing supplies in the United States, except manufacturers
units.action_summary: Prohibits sellers (other than manufacturers) of plumbing supplies from selling non-lead-free solder or flux.

units.obligation_text: It shall be unlawful for any person to introduce into commerce any solder or flux that is not lead free unless the solder or flux bears a prominent label stating that it is illegal to use the solder or flux in the installation or repair of any plumbing providing water for human consumption.
units.action_summary: Prohibits introducing non-lead-free solder or flux into commerce unless it bears a prominent label stating it is illegal to use for plumbing providing water for human consumption.

units.obligation_text: Unless the solder or flux bears a prominent label stating that it is illegal to use the solder or flux in the installation or repair of any plumbing providing water for human consumption.
units.actor: any person introducing solder or flux into commerce
units.action_summary: Condition allowing introduction into commerce of non-lead-free solder/flux only if it bears the required prominent illegal-to-use label.

units.obligation_text: The prohibitions in §§ 143.13 and 143.15 shall not apply to the products listed in paragraphs (a) through (c) of this section:
units.actor: persons dealing with the listed products
units.action_summary: States that prohibitions in §§143.13 and 143.15 do not apply to listed exempt products.

units.obligation_text: Pipes, pipe fittings, plumbing fittings, or fixtures, including backflow preventers, that are used exclusively for nonpotable services such as manufacturing, industrial processing, irrigation, outdoor watering, or any other uses where the water is not anticipated to be used for human consumption.
units.actor: persons dealing with products used exclusively for nonpotable services
units.action_summary: Exempts listed products used exclusively for nonpotable services from the prohibitions.

units.obligation_text: The product is incapable of use in potable services (e.g., physically incompatible with other products that would be needed to convey water for potable uses);
units.actor: persons asserting product is used exclusively for nonpotable services
units.action_summary: Specifies that a product is 'used exclusively for nonpotable services' if it is incapable of use in potable services.

units.obligation_text: The product is clearly labeled, on the product, package, container, or tag with a phrase such as: 'Not for use with water for human consumption' or another phrase that conveys the same meaning in plain language.
units.actor: persons asserting product is used exclusively for nonpotable services (manufacturers/importers/sellers)
units.action_summary: Specifies that a product is 'used exclusively for nonpotable services' if it is clearly labeled as not for use with water for human consumption.

units.obligation_text: Toilets, bidets, urinals, fill valves, flushometer valves, tub fillers, shower valves, fire hydrants, service saddles, water distribution main gate valves that are 2 inches in diameter or larger.
units.action_summary: Exempts these specific listed products from the prohibitions in §§143.13 and 143.15.

units.obligation_text: Clothes washing machines, fire suppression sprinklers, eyewash devices, sump pumps, and emergency drench showers.
units.action_summary: Exempts these specific listed products from the prohibitions in §§143.13 and 143.15.

units.obligation_text: Persons that introduce into commerce products that must meet the lead free requirements of section 1417(a)(3)(A) of the Safe Drinking Water Act and § 143.12 must label such products to indicate that it is in compliance with those requirements. Such labeling must occur by [DATE 3 YEARS AFTER PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE Federal Register] or prior to introduction into commerce, whichever occurs later.
units.actor: persons that introduce into commerce applicable products
units.action_summary: Requires persons introducing covered products into commerce to label them as compliant with lead-free requirements, by the specified deadline or prior to introduction.

units.obligation_text: Such labeling must occur by [DATE 3 YEARS AFTER PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE Federal Register] or prior to introduction into commerce, whichever occurs later.
units.actor: persons that introduce into commerce applicable products
units.action_summary: Sets the deadline/threshold for when labeling must occur (3 years after final rule or before introduction into commerce).

units.obligation_text: Labeling or marking as specified in paragraph (a) of this section must be in accordance with paragraphs (b)(1), (b)(2), and (c) of this section:
units.action_summary: Requires that labeling/marking follow the specific rules set out in (b)(1), (b)(2), and (c).

units.obligation_text: Packaged, containerized or tagged products must be labeled or marked on the package, container, or tag with a phrase such as: 'Conforms with the lead free requirements of the federal Safe Drinking Water Act,' 'Lead Free,' or similar terms that clearly convey to users that the product is in compliance with the applicable requirements. Products that are not packaged, containerized or tagged are only required to be marked consistent with requirements in paragraph (b)(2) of this section. Shrink wrapping of bulk products solely for the purpose of shipping or storage does not constitute being packaged, containerized, or tagged.
units.action_summary: Requires packaged/containerized/tagged products to bear clear compliance labeling; non-packaged products must follow marking rules in (b)(2); shrink wrap alone does not count as packaging.

units.obligation_text: Shrink wrapping of bulk products solely for the purpose of shipping or storage does not constitute being packaged, containerized, or tagged.
units.actor: persons who ship or store bulk products
units.action_summary: Clarifies that shrink wrapping for shipping/storage does not make bulk products 'packaged' for labeling obligations.

units.obligation_text: Products must be directly marked by physically stamping, forging, or printing with indelible ink, except as provided in (b)(2)(i) or (b)(2)(ii) of this section. The marking must clearly convey to consumers that the product is lead free, such as 'Lead Free,' 'LF,' or certification marks. If the marking is 'LF' or another abbreviation, symbol or acronym, the product package, container, or tag must associate that marking with a phrase such as 'lead free' or 'meets lead free requirements.' Product markings should be located where they are visible after product installation when practical.
units.action_summary: Requires direct marking of products to indicate lead-free status using durable marking; abbreviations require association with full phrase; markings should be visible after installation when practical; exceptions in (i) and (ii) apply.

units.obligation_text: If the product is too small for a legible marking in a type face ranging from approximately 8 point to 14 point depending on the method of marking and roughness of product surface, only a product package, container or tag must be labeled or marked.
units.action_summary: If product is too small for legible marking, labeling on package/container/tag suffices.

units.obligation_text: If the visible marking on installed products will adversely impact the visual appeal to consumers of the finished product, the product may be marked in a location not visible after installation.
units.action_summary: Allows marking in a non-visible after-installation location if visible marking would adversely affect visual appeal.

units.obligation_text: For products certified by accredited third party certification bodies, labeling or marking on the product, package, container, tag or some combination of these locations must include:
units.action_summary: Requires certified products to include specified certification information in labeling/marking.

units.obligation_text: The logo or name of the certification body as specified by the specific certification body;
units.action_summary: Labeling must include the certification body's logo or name.

units.obligation_text: The specific certification body’s required identifier text to convey lead free or low lead content.
units.action_summary: Labeling must include the certification body's identifier text indicating lead-free/low-lead content.

units.obligation_text: Solder and flux that is not 'lead free' as defined in § 143.12(a)(1) must bear a prominent label stating that it is illegal to use the solder or flux in the installation or repair of any plumbing providing water for human consumption.
units.actor: manufacturers, importers, distributors, or sellers of solder and flux
units.action_summary: Requires non-lead-free solder and flux to bear a prominent label indicating it is illegal to use for plumbing providing water for human consumption.

units.obligation_text: Manufacturers or importers that introduce into commerce products that must meet the lead free requirements of section 1417 of the Safe Drinking Water Act and § 143.12 must ensure that the products are certified to be in compliance as specified in paragraphs (b) and (c) of this section by [DATE 3 YEARS AFTER PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE Federal Register] or prior to product introduction into commerce, whichever occurs later. Such manufacturers or importers must maintain documentation to substantiate the certification.
units.actor: manufacturers or importers that introduce into commerce applicable products
units.action_summary: Requires manufacturers/importers to ensure products are certified by the deadline or before introduction into commerce and to maintain documentation substantiating certification.

units.obligation_text: must ensure that the products are certified ... by [DATE 3 YEARS AFTER PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE Federal Register] or prior to product introduction into commerce, whichever occurs later.
units.action_summary: Sets the deadline/threshold for when certification must be obtained (3 years after final rule or before introduction into commerce).

units.obligation_text: Such manufacturers or importers must maintain documentation to substantiate the certification.
units.action_summary: Requires maintenance of documentation supporting product certification.

units.obligation_text: Certification of products must be obtained by manufacturers or importers from an accredited third party certification body, except as provided in paragraph (c) of this section.
units.action_summary: Requires certification from an accredited third-party certification body, except as allowed in paragraph (c).

units.obligation_text: Products certified by an accredited third party certification body must be labeled or marked as specified in § 143.17(c).
units.actor: manufacturers or importers of certified products
units.action_summary: Requires labeling/marking of products certified by accredited bodies in accordance with §143.17(c).

units.obligation_text: The manufacturer or importers must keep records for all products certified by an accredited third party certification body that include at a minimum: Documentation of certification, dates of certification and expiration. This documentation must be provided upon request to the Administrator as specified in § 143.20(b).
units.action_summary: Requires manufacturers/importers to keep records of certification (including dates and expiration) and to provide documentation to the Administrator upon request.

units.obligation_text: Manufacturers having fewer than 100 employees or importers sourcing products from or representing manufacturers having fewer than 100 employees may elect to self-certify products in lieu of obtaining certification from an accredited third party certification body.
units.actor: manufacturers with fewer than 100 employees and qualifying importers
units.action_summary: Permits small manufacturers or qualifying importers to self-certify products instead of using an accredited third-party certification body.

units.obligation_text: Such manufacturers or importers electing to self-certify products must comply with paragraphs (d) through (g) of this section.
units.actor: manufacturers or importers electing to self-certify
units.action_summary: Requires that entities electing self-certification comply with the detailed requirements in paragraphs (d) through (g).

units.obligation_text: In order for eligible manufacturers or importers to self-certify products, such manufacturers or importers must attest that products are in compliance by developing and maintaining a 'certificate of conformity.' The certificate of conformity must be: (1) Signed by a responsible corporate officer, a general partner or proprietor, or an authorized representative of a responsible corporate officer, general partner or proprietor; and (2) Posted to a Web page with continuing public access in the United States.
units.actor: eligible manufacturers or importers electing to self-certify
units.action_summary: Self-certifying entities must develop and maintain a certificate of conformity, which must be signed by an authorized officer and posted to a publicly accessible U.S. web page.

units.obligation_text: Signed by a responsible corporate officer, a general partner or proprietor, or an authorized representative of a responsible corporate officer, general partner or proprietor;
units.action_summary: Requires the certificate of conformity to be signed by a responsible corporate officer, general partner, proprietor, or authorized representative.

units.obligation_text: Posted to a Web page with continuing public access in the United States.
units.action_summary: Requires the certificate of conformity to be posted to a U.S.-accessible web page for public access.

units.obligation_text: The certificate of conformity must be in English and include: (1) Contact information for the manufacturer or importer to include: (i) The entity or proprietor name, (ii) Street and mailing addresses, (iii) Phone number, and (iv) Email address. For products imported into the United States, the contact information must also be included for the manufacturer; (2) A brief listing of the products to include, when applicable, unique identifying information such as model names and numbers; (3) A statement attesting that the products meet the lead free requirements of the Safe Drinking Water Act and 40 CFR part 143, subpart B and also that the manufacturer or importer is eligible to self-certify the product consistent with this regulation; (4) A statement indicating how the manufacturer or importer verified conformance with the Safe Drinking Water Act and 40 CFR part 143, subpart B; and (5) The signature, date, name and position of the signatory; and if the signatory is an authorized representative of a responsible corporate officer, a general partner or proprietor, the name and position of the responsible corporate officer, a general partner or proprietor.
units.actor: eligible manufacturers or importers preparing a certificate of conformity
units.action_summary: Sets content and language requirements for the certificate of conformity, including contact info, product listing, attestation statements, verification method, and signatory details.

units.obligation_text: Contact information for the manufacturer or importer to include: (i) The entity or proprietor name, (ii) Street and mailing addresses, (iii) Phone number, and (iv) Email address.
units.action_summary: Requires inclusion of contact information (name, addresses, phone, email) on the certificate of conformity.

units.obligation_text: The entity or proprietor name.
units.action_summary: Certificate must include the entity or proprietor name.

units.obligation_text: Street and mailing addresses.
units.action_summary: Certificate must include street and mailing addresses.

units.obligation_text: Phone number.
units.action_summary: Certificate must include a phone number.

units.obligation_text: Email address.
units.action_summary: Certificate must include an email address.

units.obligation_text: For products imported into the United States, the contact information must also be included for the manufacturer;
units.action_summary: Requires importers to include the manufacturer's contact information on the certificate for imported products.

units.obligation_text: A brief listing of the products to include, when applicable, unique identifying information such as model names and numbers;
units.action_summary: Certificate must include a brief product listing with unique identifiers where applicable.

units.obligation_text: A statement attesting that the products meet the lead free requirements of the Safe Drinking Water Act and 40 CFR part 143, subpart B and also that the manufacturer or importer is eligible to self-certify the product consistent with this regulation;
units.action_summary: Requires an attestation statement that the products meet lead-free requirements and that the entity is eligible to self-certify.

units.obligation_text: A statement indicating how the manufacturer or importer verified conformance with the Safe Drinking Water Act and 40 CFR part 143, subpart B;
units.action_summary: Certificate must state how conformance with lead-free requirements was verified.

units.obligation_text: The signature, date, name and position of the signatory; and if the signatory is an authorized representative of a responsible corporate officer, a general partner or proprietor, the name and position of the responsible corporate officer, a general partner or proprietor.
units.actor: eligible manufacturers or importers (signatory and responsible officers)
units.action_summary: Certificate must include signature, date, name and position of the signatory and, if applicable, the name/position of the responsible officer represented.

units.obligation_text: Manufacturers or importers that self-certify products must maintain, at a primary place of business within the United States, certificates of conformity and sufficient documentation to confirm that products meet the lead free requirements of this subpart. Sufficient documentation may include: Detailed schematic drawings of the products indicating dimensions, calculations of the weighted average lead content of the product, lead content of materials used in manufacture and other documentation used in verifying the lead content of a plumbing device. This documentation and certificates of conformity must be provided upon request to the Administrator as specified in § 143.20(b).
units.action_summary: Requires self-certifying entities to maintain certificates and sufficient supporting documentation at a U.S. primary place of business and to provide them to the Administrator upon request.

units.obligation_text: Sufficient documentation may include: Detailed schematic drawings of the products indicating dimensions, calculations of the weighted average lead content of the product, lead content of materials used in manufacture and other documentation used in verifying the lead content of a plumbing device.
units.action_summary: Provides examples of acceptable supporting documentation to confirm compliance.

units.obligation_text: This documentation and certificates of conformity must be provided upon request to the Administrator as specified in § 143.20(b).
units.action_summary: Requires providing certificates and documentation to the Administrator upon request.

units.obligation_text: The certificate of conformity and documentation must be completed prior to a product’s introduction into commerce.
units.action_summary: Requires that certificate and supporting documentation be completed before introducing the product into commerce.

units.obligation_text: Noncompliance with the Safe Drinking Water Act or this subpart may be subject to enforcement. Enforcement actions may include seeking injunctive relief, civil or criminal penalties.
units.action_summary: Allows enforcement actions, including injunctive relief and civil or criminal penalties, for noncompliance.

units.obligation_text: The Administrator may, on a case-by-case basis, request any information deemed necessary to determine whether a person has acted or is acting in compliance with section 1417 of the Safe Drinking Water Act and this subpart.
units.action_summary: Permits the Administrator to request information necessary to determine compliance.

units.obligation_text: Such information requested must be provided to the Administrator at a time and in a format as may be reasonably determined by the Administrator.
units.actor: any person from whom information is requested
units.action_summary: Requires persons to provide requested information to the Administrator in the time and format reasonably determined by the Administrator.

units.obligation_text: At a time and in a format as may be reasonably determined by the Administrator.
units.actor: any person from whom information is requested
units.action_summary: Specifies that the timing and format for providing requested information will be reasonably determined by the Administrator.

title: Use of Lead Free Pipes, Fittings, Fixtures, Solder and Flux for Drinking Water

units.action_summary: Submit comments by May 17, 2017.

units.action_summary: Submit comments to Regulations.gov and identify them by the specified Docket ID.

units.obligation_text: identified by Docket ID No. EPA–HQ–OW–2015–0680
units.action_summary: Ensure submissions include the specified Docket ID.

units.obligation_text: Follow the online instructions for submitting comments.
units.action_summary: Comply with the online submission instructions on Regulations.gov when submitting comments.

units.obligation_text: Once submitted, comments cannot be edited or removed from Regulations.gov.
units.action_summary: You cannot edit or remove comments once submitted to Regulations.gov.

units.obligation_text: EPA may publish any comment received to its public docket.
units.action_summary: EPA is permitted to publish submitted comments to the public docket.

units.obligation_text: Do not submit electronically any information you consider to be Confidential Business Information (CBI) or other information whose disclosure is restricted by statute.

units.obligation_text: Multimedia submissions (audio, video, etc.) must be accompanied by a written comment.

units.action_summary: EPA generally will not consider comments that are submitted or located outside the primary submission system.

units.action_summary: File oppositions to the petitions by April 26, 2017.

units.obligation_text: Replies to an opposition must be filed on or before May 8, 2017.

units.action_summary: The public may access the Petition online via the FCC's Electronic Comment Filing System.

units.obligation_text: The Commission will not send a copy of this document pursuant to the Congressional Review Act, 5 U.S.C. 801(a)(1)(A), because this document does not have an impact on any rules of particular applicability.
units.action_summary: The Commission will not mail/send a copy of this document under the Congressional Review Act.

title: Public Notification Requirements for Combined Sewer Overflows to the Great Lakes Basin

units.obligation_text: Each applicant that discharges a combined sewer overflow to the Great Lakes Basin as defined in § 122.2 must submit a public notification plan developed in accordance with § 122.38 as part of its permit application.
units.actor: Each applicant that discharges a CSO to the Great Lakes Basin
units.action_summary: Submit a public notification plan (per §122.38) with permit application.

units.obligation_text: The public notification plan shall describe any significant updates to the plan that may have occurred since the last plan submission.
units.actor: Each applicant (via the public notification plan)
units.action_summary: Include any significant updates since last submission in the plan.

units.obligation_text: All permittees authorized to discharge a combined sewer overflow (CSO) to the Great Lakes Basin ("Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee") must provide public notification of CSO discharges as described in this paragraph after [date 6 months after publication of final rule]. Public notification shall consist of:
units.actor: All permittees authorized to discharge a CSO to the Great Lakes Basin (Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee)
units.action_summary: Provide public notification of CSO discharges after specified date; notification shall consist of the listed elements.

units.obligation_text: The Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee shall ensure that there is adequate signage where signage is feasible at CSO outfalls and potentially impacted public access areas.
units.action_summary: Ensure adequate signage at feasible CSO outfalls and impacted public access areas.

units.obligation_text: At a minimum, signs shall include: The name of the Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee,
units.actor: Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee (via signage)
units.action_summary: Signage must include the permittee's name.

units.obligation_text: At a minimum, signs shall include: A description of the discharge (e.g., untreated human sewage, treated wastewater) and notice that sewage may be present in the water,
units.actor: Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee (via signage)
units.action_summary: Signage must describe the discharge and warn that sewage may be present.

units.obligation_text: At a minimum, signs shall include: The Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee contact information, including a telephone number, NPDES permit number and outfall number as identified in the NPDES permit.
units.actor: Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee (via signage)
units.action_summary: Signage must include contact info, phone, NPDES permit number, and outfall number.

units.obligation_text: The Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee shall perform periodic maintenance of signs to ensure that they are legible, visible and factually correct.
units.action_summary: Perform periodic maintenance so signs remain legible, visible, and accurate.

units.obligation_text: Where a permittee has before [date 6 months after publication of final rule] installed a sign at a CSO outfall or potentially impacted public access area that is consistent with state requirements, the sign is not required to meet the minimum requirements specified in paragraph (a)(1)(i) of this section until the sign is replaced or reset.
units.action_summary: Pre-existing state-compliant signs need not meet the new minimum requirements until replaced or reset.

units.obligation_text: As soon as possible, but no later than four (4) hours after becoming aware by monitoring, modeling or other means that a CSO discharge has occurred, the Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee shall provide initial notice of the CSO discharge to the local public health department (or if there is no local health department, to the state health department), any potentially affected public entities ..., and Indian Tribes whose waters may be affected.
units.action_summary: Provide initial notice to local/state health department, affected public entities, and Indian Tribes within 4 hours of awareness of a CSO discharge.

units.obligation_text: Such initial notice shall, at a minimum, include the following information: The water body that received the discharge(s);
units.actor: Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee (in initial notice)
units.action_summary: Initial notice must identify the water body that received the discharge.

units.obligation_text: Such initial notice shall, at a minimum, include the following information: The location of the discharge(s). Where CSO discharges from the same system occur at multiple locations at the same time, the Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee may provide a description of the area in the waterbody where discharges are occurring and identification of the public access areas potentially impacted by the discharge, and the permittee is not required to identify the specific location of each discharge;
units.actor: Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee (in initial notice)
units.action_summary: Initial notice must include the discharge location; if multiple simultaneous locations occur, permittee may give an area description and is not required to identify each exact location.

units.obligation_text: Such initial notice shall, at a minimum, include the following information: The date(s) and time(s) that the discharge(s) commenced or the time the permittee became aware of the discharge(s) or when discharges are expected to occur;
units.actor: Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee (in initial notice)
units.action_summary: Initial notice must include dates/times when discharge began, when permittee became aware, or when discharges are expected.

units.obligation_text: Such initial notice shall, at a minimum, include the following information: Whether, at the time of the notification, the discharge(s) is continuing or has ended. If the discharge(s) has ended, the approximate time that the discharge ended;
units.actor: Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee (in initial notice)
units.action_summary: Initial notice must state whether the discharge is ongoing or ended, and if ended, approximate end time.

units.obligation_text: Such initial notice shall, at a minimum, include the following information: A point of contact for the CSO permittee.
units.actor: Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee (in initial notice)
units.action_summary: Initial notice must include a permittee point of contact.

units.obligation_text: Within twenty-four (24) hours after becoming aware by monitoring, modeling or other means that the CSO discharge(s) has ended, the Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee shall provide the following supplemental information to the public health department and affected public entities and Indian Tribes receiving the initial notice under paragraph (a)(2)(i) of this section unless the information had been provided in an earlier notice:
units.action_summary: Within 24 hours after awareness that discharge ended, provide supplemental information to those who received initial notice unless already provided.

units.obligation_text: The measured or estimated volume of the discharge(s). Where CSO discharges from the same system occur at multiple locations at the same time, the Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee may provide an estimate of the cumulative volume discharged to a given waterbody;
units.actor: Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee (in supplemental information)
units.action_summary: Supplemental notice must include measured or estimated discharge volume; for multiple locations, may provide cumulative estimate.

units.obligation_text: The approximate time that the discharge(s) ended.
units.actor: Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee (in supplemental information)
units.action_summary: Supplemental notice must include approximate end time of discharge.

units.obligation_text: As soon as possible, but no later than four (4) hours after becoming aware by monitoring, modeling or other means that a CSO discharge has occurred, the Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee shall provide public notification of CSO discharges. The Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee shall provide public notification of CSO discharges electronically, such as by text, email, social media alerts to subscribers or by posting a notice on its public access Web site, and by other appropriate means (e.g. newspaper, radio, television).
units.action_summary: Notify the public of CSO discharges within 4 hours of awareness using electronic means and other appropriate media.

units.obligation_text: At a minimum, the notice shall include: The water body that received the discharge(s);
units.actor: Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee (in public notice)
units.action_summary: Public notice must identify the water body receiving the discharge.

units.obligation_text: At a minimum, the notice shall include: The location of the discharge(s). Where CSO discharges from the same system occur at multiple locations at the same time, the Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee may provide a description of the area in the waterbody where discharges are occurring and identification of the public access areas potentially impacted by the discharge, and the permittee is not required to identify the specific location of each discharge;
units.actor: Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee (in public notice)
units.action_summary: Public notice must include discharge location; for multiple simultaneous locations, permittee may describe area and need not identify each specific location.

units.obligation_text: At a minimum, the notice shall include: The date(s) and time(s) that the discharge(s) commenced or the time the permittee became aware of the discharge(s);
units.actor: Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee (in public notice)
units.action_summary: Public notice must include dates/times the discharge began or when permittee became aware.

units.obligation_text: At a minimum, the notice shall include: Whether, at the time of the notification, the discharge(s) is continuing or has ended. If the discharge(s) has ended, the approximate time that the discharge(s) ended.
units.actor: Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee (in public notice)
units.action_summary: Public notice must state if discharge is ongoing or ended, and if ended, approximate end time.

units.obligation_text: Within twenty-four (24) hours after becoming aware by monitoring, modeling or other means that the CSO discharge(s) has ended, the Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee shall update the electronic notice with the following information unless the information had been provided in an earlier notice:
units.action_summary: Within 24 hours after knowing discharge ended, update electronic notice with specified information unless already provided.

units.obligation_text: The measured or estimated volume of the discharge(s). Where CSO discharges from the same system occur at multiple locations at the same time, the Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee may provide an estimate of the cumulative volume discharged to a given waterbody;
units.actor: Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee (in electronic update)
units.action_summary: Electronic update must include measured or estimated discharge volume; cumulative estimate acceptable for multiple locations.

units.obligation_text: The approximate time that the discharge(s) ended, unless this information was provided in an earlier notice.
units.actor: Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee (in electronic update)
units.action_summary: Electronic update must include approximate end time of discharge unless already provided.

units.obligation_text: By May 1 of each calendar year (or an earlier date specified by the Director), all permittees authorized to discharge a CSO to the Great Lakes Basin shall make available to the public an annual notice describing the CSO discharges from its outfall(s) that occurred in the previous calendar year and shall provide the Director with notice of how the annual notice is available.
units.actor: All permittees authorized to discharge a CSO to the Great Lakes Basin
units.action_summary: By May 1 each year, make an annual notice public describing prior year's CSO discharges and inform the Director how the notice is available.

units.obligation_text: Permittees that are owners or operators of a satellite collection system with one or more CSO outfalls shall provide the annual notice to the public and a copy of the annual notice to the operator of the POTW treatment plant providing treatment for its wastewater.
units.actor: Permittees that are owners or operators of a satellite collection system with CSO outfalls
units.action_summary: Satellite system owners/operators must provide the annual notice to the public and send a copy to the POTW operator.

units.obligation_text: At a minimum, the annual notice shall include: Information on the availability of the permittee’s public notification plan and a summary of significant modifications to the plan that were made in the past year;
units.actor: Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee (in annual notice)
units.action_summary: Annual notice must state where the public notification plan is available and summarize significant modifications in the past year.

units.obligation_text: At a minimum, the annual notice shall include: A description of the location, treatment provided and receiving water for each CSO outfall;
units.actor: Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee (in annual notice)
units.action_summary: Annual notice must describe location, treatment, and receiving water for each CSO outfall.

units.obligation_text: At a minimum, the annual notice shall include: The date, location, duration, and volume of each wet weather CSO discharge that occurred during the past calendar year. Where CSO discharges from the same system occur at multiple locations at the same time, the Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee may provide an estimate of the cumulative volume discharged to a given waterbody;
units.actor: Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee (in annual notice)
units.action_summary: Annual notice must include date, location, duration, and volume of each wet weather discharge; may provide cumulative volume estimate for multiple locations.

units.obligation_text: At a minimum, the annual notice shall include: The date, location, duration, and volume of each dry weather CSO discharge that occurred during the past calendar year;
units.actor: Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee (in annual notice)
units.action_summary: Annual notice must include date, location, duration, and volume of each dry weather discharge from the prior year.

units.obligation_text: At a minimum, the annual notice shall include: A summary of available monitoring data for CSO discharges from the past calendar year;
units.actor: Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee (in annual notice)
units.action_summary: Annual notice must include a summary of monitoring data for CSO discharges from the prior year.

units.obligation_text: At a minimum, the annual notice shall include: A description of any public access areas impacted by each CSO discharge;
units.actor: Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee (in annual notice)
units.action_summary: Annual notice must describe public access areas impacted by each CSO discharge.

units.obligation_text: At a minimum, the annual notice shall include: Representative rain gauge data in total inches to the nearest 0.1 inch that resulted in a CSO discharge;
units.actor: Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee (in annual notice)
units.action_summary: Annual notice must include representative rain gauge data (total inches to nearest 0.1) that resulted in CSO discharge.

units.obligation_text: At a minimum, the annual notice shall include: A point of contact;
units.actor: Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee (in annual notice)
units.action_summary: Annual notice must include a point of contact.

units.obligation_text: At a minimum, the annual notice shall include: A concise summary of implementation of the nine minimum controls and the status of implementation of the long-term CSO control plan (or other plans to reduce or prevent CSO discharges), including:
units.actor: Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee (in annual notice)
units.action_summary: Annual notice must include summary of implementation status for minimum controls and long-term CSO control plan, including specified elements.

units.obligation_text: A description of key milestones remaining to complete implementation of the plan;
units.actor: Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee (in annual notice)
units.action_summary: Annual notice must describe key remaining milestones to complete plan implementation.

units.obligation_text: A description of the average annual number of CSO discharges anticipated after implementation of the long-term control plan (or other plan relevant to reduction of CSO overflows) is completed.
units.actor: Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee (in annual notice)
units.action_summary: Annual notice must describe the anticipated average annual number of CSO discharges after plan completion.

units.obligation_text: By May 1 of each calendar year (or an earlier date specified by the Director), all permittees authorized to discharge a CSO to the Great Lakes Basin shall electronically report any CSO discharge that occurred during the past calendar year that has not been previously reported pursuant to a permit requirement to the initial recipient, as defined in 40 CFR 127.2(b), in compliance with 40 CFR 127 using the discharge monitoring report (NPDES Data Group 3, Appendix A to 40 CFR 127) or the Sewer Overflow Event Report (NPDES Data Group 9, Appendix A to 40 CFR 127).
units.actor: All permittees authorized to discharge a CSO to the Great Lakes Basin
units.action_summary: By May 1 each year, electronically report any CSO discharge from prior year not previously reported, using specified reporting forms in compliance with 40 CFR 127.

units.obligation_text: The Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee shall develop a public notification plan that describes how the Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee will ensure that the public receives adequate notification of CSO occurrences and CSO impacts.
units.action_summary: Develop a public notification plan explaining how the public will be adequately notified of CSO events and impacts.

units.obligation_text: The Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee must provide notice of the availability of the plan on the permittee’s Web site (if it has a Web site), and periodically provide information in bill mailings and by other appropriate means on how to view the notification plan.
units.action_summary: Inform the public about the availability of the notification plan on the permittee's website and by bill mailings and other means.

units.obligation_text: The Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee must submit its public notification plan to the Director by [date 6 months after publication of a final rule] and as part of a permit application under § 122.21(j)(8)(iii).
units.action_summary: Submit the public notification plan to the Director by specified date and include it with permit application.

units.obligation_text: The plan must: Identify the location of signs required under paragraph (a)(1) of this section and the location of any CSO outfall where a sign is not feasible. Where a sign has not been provided at an outfall, the plan shall explain why a sign at that location is not feasible.
units.actor: Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee (in public notification plan)
units.action_summary: Plan must identify sign locations and explain where signs are not feasible.

units.obligation_text: The plan must: Describe the message used on signs required under paragraph (a)(1) of this section;
units.actor: Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee (in public notification plan)
units.action_summary: Plan must describe the sign messages.

units.obligation_text: The plan must: Describe protocols for maintaining signage (e.g., inspections at set intervals);
units.actor: Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee (in public notification plan)
units.action_summary: Plan must describe signage maintenance protocols such as inspection intervals.

units.obligation_text: The plan must: Identify (with points of contact) the municipalities, public drinking water supplies, public parks with water access, Indian Tribe(s), and describe other sensitive area(s) identified in the permittee’s long-term CSO control plan, that may be affected by the permittee’s CSO discharges;
units.actor: Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee (in public notification plan)
units.action_summary: Plan must identify potentially affected municipalities, water supplies, parks, Tribes, and other sensitive areas, with contacts.

units.obligation_text: The plan must: Summarize significant comments and recommendations raised by the local public health department under paragraph (e) of this section;
units.actor: Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee (in public notification plan)
units.action_summary: Plan must summarize significant comments/recommendations from local public health department.

units.obligation_text: The plan must: Identify other affected public entities and Indian Tribes whose waters may be affected by a CSO discharge that were contacted under paragraph (e) of this section and provide a summary of their significant comments and recommendations;
units.actor: Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee (in public notification plan)
units.action_summary: Plan must identify other affected entities and Tribes contacted and summarize their significant comments/recommendations.

units.obligation_text: The plan must: Describe protocols for the initial and supplemental notice to public health departments and other public entities;
units.actor: Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee (in public notification plan)
units.action_summary: Plan must describe protocols for initial/supplemental notices to health departments and other entities.

units.obligation_text: The plan must: Describe protocols for the initial and supplemental notice to the public;
units.actor: Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee (in public notification plan)
units.action_summary: Plan must describe protocols for initial/supplemental public notice.

units.obligation_text: The plan must: Describe, for each outfall, how the volume and duration of CSO discharges shall be either measured or estimated for the purposes of complying with paragraphs (a)(2)(B)(i), (a)(3)(C)(i), (b)(2), and (b)(3) of this section. If the Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee intends to use a model to estimate discharge volumes and durations, the plan must summarize the model and describe how the model was or will be calibrated. CSO permittees that are a municipality or sewer district with a population of 75,000 or more must calibrate their model at least once every 5 years;
units.actor: Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee (in public notification plan)
units.action_summary: Plan must describe how outfall volume/duration will be measured or estimated; if using a model, summarize and describe calibration; municipalities/sewer districts with population ≥75,000 must calibrate at least every 5 years.

units.obligation_text: The plan must: Describe protocols for making the annual notice described in paragraph (b) of this section available to the public and to the Director.
units.actor: Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee (in public notification plan)
units.action_summary: Plan must describe how the annual notice will be made available to the public and the Director.

units.obligation_text: Prior to submitting the public notification plan, or resubmitting under § 122.21(j)(8)(iii), the Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee must:
units.action_summary: Before submitting or resubmitting the plan, the permittee must take the listed steps (seek input, consider recommendations).

units.obligation_text: Seek input from the local public health department (or if there is no local health department, the state health department), to:
units.action_summary: Obtain input from local (or state) public health department prior to plan submission.

units.obligation_text: Develop recommended protocols for providing notification of CSO discharges to the public health department. The protocols will specify which CSO discharges are subject to notification, the means of notification, timing of notification and other relevant factors;
units.actor: Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee (in consultation with public health department)
units.action_summary: Work with public health department to develop protocols specifying which discharges to notify about, how, timing, and other factors.

units.obligation_text: Develop recommendations for providing notice to the general public of CSO discharges electronically and by other appropriate means.
units.actor: Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee (in consultation with public health department)
units.action_summary: Work with public health department to develop recommendations for notifying the general public electronically and by other means.

units.obligation_text: Seek input from other potentially affected public entities and Indian Tribes whose waters may be affected by a CSO discharge.
units.action_summary: Obtain input from other potentially affected public entities and Tribes prior to plan submission.

units.obligation_text: Consider the recommendations of the public health department and other potentially affected entities in developing protocols in its public notification plan for providing notification of CSO discharges to the public health department and potentially affected public entities and Indian Tribes.
units.action_summary: Consider recommendations received when developing notification protocols in the plan.

units.obligation_text: The Director may extend the compliance dates in paragraphs (a), (b), and (d) of this section for individual communities if the Director determines the community needs additional time to comply in order to avoid undue economic hardship.
units.action_summary: Director may grant extensions to compliance dates for individual communities to avoid undue economic hardship.

units.obligation_text: Where the Director extends the compliance date of any of these requirements for a community, the Director shall notify the Regional Administrator of the extension and the reason for the extension.
units.action_summary: If Director extends a compliance date, notify Regional Administrator and provide reason.

units.obligation_text: The Director shall post on its Web site a notice that includes the name of the community and the new compliance date(s).
units.action_summary: Post a notice on the Director's website with community name and new compliance dates when extension is granted.

units.obligation_text: The notice shall remain on the Director’s Web site until the new compliance date.
units.action_summary: Keep the posted notice on the Director's website until the new compliance date.

units.obligation_text: Any permit issued for combined sewer overflow (CSO) discharges to the Great Lakes Basin must:
units.actor: Permitting authority / NPDES permits issued for CSO discharges to the Great Lakes Basin
units.action_summary: Permits for CSO discharges to the Great Lakes Basin must include the following specified elements.

units.obligation_text: Require implementation of the public notification requirements in § 122.38(a);
units.actor: Permits issued for CSO discharges to the Great Lakes Basin (via permitting authority)
units.action_summary: Permit must require implementation of the public notification requirements in §122.38(a).

units.obligation_text: Specify the information that must be included on outfall signage, which, at a minimum, must include those elements in § 122.38(a)(1)(i);
units.actor: Permits issued for CSO discharges to the Great Lakes Basin (via permitting authority)
units.action_summary: Permit must specify required outfall signage information, at minimum the elements in §122.38(a)(1)(i).

units.obligation_text: Specify outfalls and public access areas where signs are required pursuant to § 122.38(a)(1)(i);
units.actor: Permits issued for CSO discharges to the Great Lakes Basin (via permitting authority)
units.action_summary: Permit must specify the outfalls and public access areas where signs are required.

units.obligation_text: Specify the timing and minimum information required for providing initial and supplemental notification to: Local public health department and other potentially affected entities under § 122.38(a)(2);
units.actor: Permits issued for CSO discharges to the Great Lakes Basin (via permitting authority)
units.action_summary: Permit must specify timing and minimum content for initial and supplemental notifications to public health departments and affected entities.

units.obligation_text: Specify the timing and minimum information required for providing initial and supplemental notification to: The public under § 122.38(a)(3).
units.actor: Permits issued for CSO discharges to the Great Lakes Basin (via permitting authority)
units.action_summary: Permit must specify timing and minimum content for initial and supplemental public notifications.

units.obligation_text: Specify the location of CSO discharges that must be monitored for volume and discharge duration and the location of CSO discharges where CSO volume and duration may be estimated;
units.actor: Permits issued for CSO discharges to the Great Lakes Basin (via permitting authority)
units.action_summary: Permit must specify which CSO locations require monitoring for volume/duration and which may have estimates.

units.obligation_text: Require submittal of an annual notice in accordance with § 122.38(b);
units.actor: Permits issued for CSO discharges to the Great Lakes Basin (via permitting authority)
units.action_summary: Permit must require submittal of the annual notice as described in §122.38(b).

units.obligation_text: Specify protocols for making the annual notice under § 122.38(b) available to the public;
units.actor: Permits issued for CSO discharges to the Great Lakes Basin (via permitting authority)
units.action_summary: Permit must specify protocols for making the annual notice available to the public.

units.obligation_text: Require all CSO discharges be electronically reported in a discharge monitoring report or a sewer overflow event report pursuant to 40 CFR 122.41(l)(6) or (7).
units.actor: Permits issued for CSO discharges to the Great Lakes Basin (via permitting authority) / CSO permittees (as obligated by permits)
units.action_summary: Permit must require electronic reporting of all CSO discharges via specified report forms under 40 CFR 122.41(l)(6) or (7).

title:
Definition of Waters of United States - Recodification of Pre-Existing
Rules

units.obligation_text: Waters of the United States do not include prior converted cropland.
units.action_summary: Prior converted cropland is excluded from the definition of waters of the United States.

units.obligation_text: Notwithstanding the determination of an area's status as prior converted cropland by any other Federal agency, for the purposes of the Clean Water Act, the final authority regarding Clean Water Act jurisdiction remains with EPA.
units.action_summary: EPA retains final authority to determine Clean Water Act jurisdiction regardless of other agencies' determinations of prior converted cropland status.

units.obligation_text: Waste treatment systems, including treatment ponds or lagoons designed to meet the requirements of CWA (other than cooling ponds as defined in 40 CFR 423.11(m) which also meet the criteria of this definition) are not waters of the United States.
units.actor: Waste treatment systems (including treatment ponds or lagoons designed to meet the requirements of the CWA)
units.action_summary: Waste treatment systems (with an exception for certain cooling ponds) are excluded from being waters of the United States.

units.obligation_text: Navigable waters do not include prior converted cropland.
units.action_summary: Prior converted cropland is excluded from the definition of navigable waters.

units.obligation_text: Notwithstanding the determination of an area's status as prior converted cropland by any other federal agency, for the purposes of the Clean Water Act, the final authority regarding Clean Water Act jurisdiction remains with EPA.
units.action_summary: EPA retains final authority to determine Clean Water Act jurisdiction despite other agencies' determinations about prior converted cropland.

units.obligation_text: Waste treatment systems, including treatment ponds or lagoons designed to meet the requirements of CWA (other than cooling ponds as defined in 40 CFR 423.11(m) which also meet the criteria of this definition) are not waters of the United States.
units.actor: Waste treatment systems (including treatment ponds or lagoons designed to meet the requirements of the CWA)
units.action_summary: Waste treatment systems are excluded from the definition of waters of the United States, except certain cooling ponds.

units.obligation_text: This exclusion applies only to manmade bodies of water which neither were originally created in waters of the United States (such as disposal area in wetlands) nor resulted from the impoundment of waters of the United States.
units.actor: This exclusion (the exclusion of waste treatment systems)
units.action_summary: The exclusion of waste treatment systems from waters of the United States is limited to manmade bodies of water not originally created in or resulting from impoundment of waters of the United States.

units.obligation_text: This revision continues that suspension.
units.action_summary: EPA continues the prior suspension of the last sentence in Sec. 122.2 that had been suspended until further notice.

units.obligation_text: Waters of the United States do not include prior converted cropland.
units.action_summary: Prior converted cropland is excluded from the definition of waters of the United States.

units.obligation_text: Waste treatment systems, including treatment ponds or lagoons designed to meet the requirements of CWA (other than cooling ponds as defined in 40 CFR 423.11(m) which also meet the criteria of this definition) are not waters of the United States.
units.actor: Waste treatment systems (including treatment ponds or lagoons designed to meet the requirements of the CWA)
units.action_summary: Waste treatment systems are excluded from being waters of the United States, except certain cooling ponds.

units.obligation_text: Waste treatment systems, including treatment ponds or lagoons designed to meet the requirements of the Act (other than cooling ponds as defined in 40 CFR 123.11(m) which also meet the criteria of this definition) are not waters of the United States.
units.actor: Waste treatment systems (including treatment ponds or lagoons designed to meet the requirements of the Act)
units.action_summary: Waste treatment systems are excluded from the definition of waters of the United States, with an exception for certain cooling ponds.

units.obligation_text: Wetlands adjacent to waters identified in paragraphs (a) through (e) of this definition: Provided, that waste treatment systems (other than cooling ponds meeting the criteria of this paragraph) are not waters of the United States.
units.action_summary: Affirms that waste treatment systems (excluding certain cooling ponds) are not waters of the United States in the context of Oil Spill Response definitions.

units.obligation_text: Waters of the United States do not include prior converted cropland. Notwithstanding the determination of an area's status as prior converted cropland by any other federal agency, for the purposes of the Clean Water Act, the final authority regarding Clean Water Act jurisdiction remains with EPA.
units.action_summary: Declares that prior converted cropland is excluded from waters of the United States and that EPA retains final authority over Clean Water Act jurisdiction determinations.

units.obligation_text: Navigable waters do not include prior converted cropland. Notwithstanding the determination of an area's status as prior converted cropland by any other federal agency, for the purposes of the Clean Water Act, the final authority regarding Clean Water Act jurisdiction remains with EPA.
units.action_summary: States prior converted cropland is not included in navigable waters and that EPA has final authority for Clean Water Act jurisdiction determinations.

units.obligation_text: Comments must be received on or before September 27, 2017.

units.obligation_text: Submit your comments, identified by Docket ID No. EPA–HQ–OW–2017–0203, at http://www.regulations.gov. Follow the online instructions for submitting comments.
units.action_summary: Submit comments at Regulations.gov using the online instructions and identify by the docket ID.

units.obligation_text: Once submitted, comments cannot be edited or removed from Regulations.gov.
units.action_summary: You cannot edit or remove comments after submission on Regulations.gov.

units.obligation_text: The agencies may publish any comment received to the public docket.
units.action_summary: Agencies may publish submitted comments to the public docket.

units.obligation_text: Do not submit electronically any information you consider to be Confidential Business Information (CBI) or other information whose disclosure is restricted by statute.
units.action_summary: Do not electronically submit CBI or other statutorily restricted information.

units.obligation_text: Multimedia submissions (audio, video, etc.) must be accompanied by a written comment.
units.action_summary: Any multimedia submission must include an accompanying written comment.

units.obligation_text: The written comment is considered the official comment and should include discussion of all points you wish to make.
units.action_summary: The written comment is the official record and should discuss all points you want to make.

units.obligation_text: The agencies will generally not consider comments or comment contents located outside of the primary submission (i.e. on the web, cloud, or other file sharing system).
units.action_summary: Agencies generally will not consider comments that are located outside the primary submission.

Addition of Natural Gas Processing Facilities to the Toxics 
Release Inventory (TRI); Extension of Comment Period

AGENCY: Environmental Protection Agency (EPA).

ACTION: Proposed rule; extension of comment period.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------

SUMMARY: EPA issued a proposed rule in the Federal Register of Friday, 
January 6, 2017, concerning the Agency's addition of natural gas 
processing facilities to the Toxics Release Inventory (TRI). This 
document extends the comment period for 60 days, from March 7, 2017 to 
May 6, 2017. This action is in response to stakeholders' requests to 
extend the comment period.

DATES: The comment period on the proposed rule published January 6, 
2016 (82 FR 1651, identified by docket identification (ID) number EPA-
HQ-TRI-2016-0390, is extended to May 6, 2017.

ADDRESSES: Follow the detailed instructions provided under ADDRESSES in 
the Federal Register document of January 6, 2017 (82 FR 1651) (FRL-
9953-68).

Inventory Program Division, Office of Pollution Prevention and Toxics, 
Environmental Protection Agency, 1200 Pennsylvania Ave. NW., 
Washington, DC 20460-0001; telephone number: 202-566-0310; email 
address:  koehrn.kara@epa.gov .
    For general information contact: The Emergency Planning and 
Community Right-to-Know Hotline; telephone numbers: toll free at (800) 
424-9346 (select menu option 3) or (703) 412-9810 in the Washington, DC 
Area and International; or toll free, TDD (800) 553-7672; or go to 
 https://www.epa.gov/home/epa-hotlines#HotlinesServiceLines4SpecificTopics .

period established in the Federal Register document of January 6, 2017. 
In that document, the Agency proposes to add natural gas processing 
facilities to TRI. EPA is hereby extending the comment period, which 
was set to end on March 7, 2017, to May 6, 2017.

detailed instructions provided under ADDRESSES in the Federal Register

Air Plan Approval; Michigan Minor New Source Review

AGENCY: Environmental Protection Agency (EPA).

ACTION: Proposed rule.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------

SUMMARY: The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is proposing to 
approve certain changes to the Michigan State Implementation Plan 
(SIP). This action relates to changes to the Permit to Install (PTI) 
requirements of the Michigan Rules submitted on November 12, 1993; May 
16, 1996; April 3, 1998; September 2, 2003; March 24, 2009; and 
February 28, 2017.

DATES: Comments must be received on or before September 14, 2017.

ADDRESSES: Submit your comments, identified by Docket ID No. EPA-R05-
OAR-2007-1092 at 
http://www.regulations.gov
, or via email to 

damico.genvieve@epa.gov
. For comments submitted at 
Regulations.gov
, 
follow the online instructions for submitting comments. Once submitted, 
comments cannot be edited or removed from 
Regulations.gov
. For either 
manner of submission, EPA may publish any comment received to its

visit 
http://www2.epa.gov/dockets/commenting-epa-dockets
.

FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT: Rachel Rineheart, Environmental 
Engineer, Air Permits Section, Air Programs Branch (AR-18J), 
Environmental Protection Agency, Region 5, 77 West Jackson Boulevard,

[[Page 38652]]

Chicago, Illinois 60604, (312) 886-7017, 
Rineheart.rachel@epa.gov
.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: Throughout this document whenever ``we,'' 
``us,'' or ``our'' is used, we mean EPA. This supplementary information 
section is arranged as follows:

I. Background
II. Review of State Submittals
III. What action is EPA taking?
IV. Incorporation by Reference
V. Statutory and Executive Order Reviews

I. Background

    Section 110(a)(2)(C) of the Clean Air Act (CAA) requires that the 
SIP include a program to provide for the ``regulation of the 
modification and construction of any stationary source within the areas 
covered by the plan as necessary to assure that national ambient air 
quality standards are achieved.'' This includes a program for 
permitting construction and modification of both major sources and 
minor sources that the State deems necessary to protect air quality. 
The State of Michigan's minor source PTI rules are contained in Part 2 
of the Michigan Administrative Code. EPA last approved changes to the 
Part 2 rules in 1982. The Michigan Department of Environmental Quality 
(MDEQ) has submitted several Part 2 revision packages since that time; 
however, EPA has not taken a final action on any of the submittals. The 
following table provides a summary of the various state submittals with 
the most recent version of each section of the Michigan Rule 
highlighted in bold.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

                            date         date            336.1xxx
