units.obligation_text: Modified steam generating unit or IGCC: A unit-specific emission limit determined by the unit’s best historical annual CO2 emission rate (from 2002 to the date of the modification); the emission limit will be no more stringent than: 1. 910 kg CO2/MWh (2,000 lb CO2/MWh) of gross energy output; or 980 kg CO2/MWh (2,160 lb CO2/MWh) of net energy output for units with a base load rating of 2,100 GJ/h (2,000 MMBtu/h) or less.
units.actor: owner or operator of modified unit
units.action_summary: For modified units (<=2,100 GJ/h), unit-specific limit not more stringent than listed gross or net values.
units.modal_raw: will be no more stringent than

units.obligation_text: Modified steam generating unit or IGCC: ... no more stringent than: 2. 870 kg CO2/MWh (1,900 lb CO2/MWh) of gross energy output; or 940 kg CO2/MWh (2,070 lb CO2/MWh) of net energy output for units with a base load rating of greater than 2,100 GJ/h (2,000 MMBtu/h).
units.actor: owner or operator of modified unit
units.action_summary: For modified units (>2,100 GJ/h), unit-specific limit not more stringent than listed gross or net values.
units.modal_raw: will be no more stringent than

units.obligation_text: Modified steam generating unit or IGCC: ... no more stringent than: 3. 1,000 kg CO2/MWh (2,200 lb CO2/MWh) of gross energy output; or 1,080 kg CO2/MWh (2,380 lb CO2/MWh) of net energy output for units that burn 75 percent or more (by heat input) coal refuse on a 12-operating month rolling average basis.
units.actor: owner or operator of modified unit
units.action_summary: For modified units burning >=75% coal refuse, unit-specific limit not more stringent than listed gross or net values.
units.modal_raw: will be no more stringent than

units.obligation_text: As an alternate to meeting the requirements in paragraph (b) of this section, an owner or operator of an EGU may petition the Administrator in writing to comply with the alternate applicable net energy output standard.
units.actor: owner or operator of an EGU
units.action_summary: Permittee may petition EPA to use a net energy output–based standard instead of the paragraph (b) requirements.

units.obligation_text: If the Administrator grants the petition, beginning on the date the Administrator grants the petition, the affected EGU must comply with the applicable net energy output-based standard included in this subpart.
units.actor: owner or operator of the affected EGU
units.action_summary: If petition is granted, the affected EGU is required to comply with the net energy output–based standard.

units.obligation_text: Your operating permit must include monitoring, recordkeeping, and reporting methodologies based on the applicable net energy output standard.
units.action_summary: Operating permit must include monitoring, recordkeeping, and reporting methods tied to the net energy output standard.

units.obligation_text: For the remainder of this subpart, where the term "gross or net energy output" is used, the term that applies to you is "net energy output."
units.actor: owner or operator to whom petition applies
units.action_summary: For affected parties under the petition, references to 'gross or net energy output' mean 'net energy output.'

units.obligation_text: Owners or operators complying with the net output-based standard must petition the Administrator to switch back to complying with the gross energy output-based standard.
units.actor: owners or operators complying with the net output-based standard
units.action_summary: If currently complying with net output standard, owners/operators are required to petition EPA to switch back to gross output standard.

units.obligation_text: Combustion turbines qualifying under § 60.5520(d)(1) are not subject to any requirements in this section other than the requirement to maintain fuel purchase records for permitted fuel(s).
units.actor: combustion turbines qualifying under § 60.5520(d)(1) / their owners/operators
units.action_summary: Qualifying combustion turbines are exempt from this section except they must maintain fuel purchase records for permitted fuels.

units.obligation_text: Requirement to maintain fuel purchase records for permitted fuel(s).
units.actor: owners or operators of qualifying combustion turbines
units.action_summary: Maintain records of fuel purchases for permitted fuels.

units.obligation_text: For all other affected sources, compliance with the applicable CO2 emission standard of this subpart shall be determined on a 12-operating-month rolling average basis.
units.actor: owners or operators of affected sources
units.action_summary: Compliance is determined using a 12-operating-month rolling average.

units.obligation_text: Within 30 days after the end of the initial compliance period (i.e., no more than 30 days after the first 12-operating-month compliance period), you must make an initial compliance determination for your affected EGU(s) with respect to the applicable emissions standard in Table 1, 2, or 3 of this subpart, in accordance with the requirements in this subpart.
units.actor: owner or operator of affected EGU(s)
units.action_summary: Make an initial compliance determination within 30 days after the initial 12-month compliance period ends.

units.obligation_text: The first operating month included in the initial 12-operating-month compliance period shall be determined by Section 60.5555(c)(3)(i), for units subject to the Acid Rain Program.
units.actor: owner or operator (determining first operating month)
units.action_summary: If in Acid Rain Program, determine first operating month per § 60.5555(c)(3)(i).

units.obligation_text: The first operating month included in the initial 12-operating-month compliance period shall be determined by Section 60.5555(c)(3)(ii)(A), for units that are not in the Acid Rain Program.
units.actor: owner or operator (determining first operating month)
units.action_summary: If not in Acid Rain Program, determine first operating month per § 60.5555(c)(3)(ii)(A).

units.obligation_text: For an affected EGU that has commenced commercial operation prior to October 23, 2015: If the date on which emissions reporting is required to begin under § 75.64(a) of this chapter has passed prior to October 23, 2015, emissions reporting shall begin according to § 60.5555(c)(3)(i) (for Acid Rain program units), or according to § 60.5555(c)(3)(ii)(B) (for units that are not subject to the Acid Rain Program). The first month of the initial compliance period shall be the first operating month (as defined in § 60.5580) after the calendar month in which the rule becomes effective;
units.actor: owner or operator of affected EGU
units.action_summary: If reporting was required to begin before Oct 23, 2015, begin emissions reporting per cited provisions; first compliance month is first operating month after rule effective calendar month.

units.obligation_text: For an affected EGU that has commenced commercial operation prior to October 23, 2015: If the date on which emissions reporting is required to begin under § 75.64(a) of this chapter occurs on or after October 23, 2015, then the first month of the initial compliance period shall be the first operating month (as defined in § 60.5580) after the calendar month in which emissions reporting is required to begin under § 60.5555(c)(3)(ii)(A).
units.actor: owner or operator of affected EGU
units.action_summary: If emissions reporting requirement begins on or after Oct 23, 2015, the first compliance month is the first operating month after the calendar month when reporting is required to begin under the cited provision.

units.obligation_text: For a modified or reconstructed EGU that becomes subject to this subpart, the first month of the initial compliance period shall be the first operating month (as defined in § 60.5580) after the calendar month in which emissions reporting is required to begin under § 60.5555(c)(3)(iii).
units.actor: owner or operator of modified or reconstructed EGU
units.action_summary: For newly covered modified/reconstructed EGUs, first compliance month is first operating month after month when emissions reporting is required under cited provision.

units.obligation_text: In accordance with §§ 60.13(g) and 60.5520, if two or more affected EGUs that implement the continuous emission monitoring provisions in paragraph (b) of this section share a common exhaust gas stack and are subject to the same emissions standard in Table 1, 2, or 3 of this subpart, you may monitor the hourly CO2 mass emissions at the common stack in lieu of monitoring each EGU separately.
units.actor: owner or operator of affected EGUs
units.action_summary: If multiple affected EGUs share a common stack and same standard, the owner/operator may monitor at the common stack instead of each unit separately.

units.obligation_text: If you choose this option, the hourly gross or net energy output (electric, thermal, and/or mechanical, as applicable) must be the sum of the hourly loads for the individual affected EGUs and you must express the operating time as 'stack operating hours' (as defined in § 72.2 of this chapter).
units.actor: owner or operator who chooses common stack monitoring
units.action_summary: When monitoring at a common stack, sum hourly outputs of individual EGUs and express operating time as 'stack operating hours.'

units.obligation_text: In accordance with §§ 60.13(g) and 60.5520 if the exhaust gases from an affected EGU that implements the continuous emission monitoring provisions in paragraph (b) of this section are emitted to the atmosphere through multiple stacks (or if the exhaust gases are routed to a common stack through multiple ducts and you elect to monitor in the ducts), you must monitor the hourly CO2 mass emissions and the 'stack operating time' (as defined in § 72.2 of this chapter) at each stack or duct separately.
units.actor: owner or operator of affected EGU
units.action_summary: If emissions go through multiple stacks/ducts, monitor hourly CO2 mass emissions and stack operating time at each stack/duct separately.

units.obligation_text: You must determine compliance with the applicable emissions standard in Table 1, 2, or 3 of this subpart by summing the CO2 mass emissions measured at the individual stacks or ducts and dividing by the total gross or net energy output for the affected EGU.
units.actor: owner or operator of affected EGU
units.action_summary: Determine compliance by summing CO2 from each stack/duct and dividing by total gross or net energy output.

units.obligation_text: In accordance with § 60.5520, if you are subject to an output-based emission standard or you burn non-uniform fuels as specified in § 60.5520(d)(2), you must demonstrate compliance with the applicable CO2 emission standard in Table 1, 2, or 3 of this subpart as required in this section. For the initial and each subsequent 12-operating-month rolling average compliance period, you must follow the procedures in paragraphs (a)(1) through (7) of this section to calculate the CO2 mass emissions rate for your affected EGU(s) in units of the applicable emissions standard (i.e., either kg/MWh or lb/MMBtu).
units.actor: owner or operator of affected EGU
units.action_summary: Demonstrate compliance and follow specified procedures to calculate CO2 mass emissions rate for each 12-month rolling period.

units.obligation_text: You must use the hourly CO2 mass emissions calculated under § 60.5535(b) or (c), as applicable, and either the generating load data from § 60.5535(d)(1) for output-based calculations or the heat input data from § 60.5535(d)(2) for heat-input-based calculations.
units.actor: owner or operator performing compliance calculations
units.action_summary: Use specified hourly CO2 measurements and appropriate load or heat input data when calculating CO2 mass emissions rate.

units.obligation_text: Combustion turbines firing non-uniform fuels that contain CO2 prior to combustion (e.g., blast furnace gas or landfill gas) may sample the fuel stream to determine the quantity of CO2 present in the fuel prior to combustion and exclude this portion of the CO2 mass emissions from compliance determinations.
units.actor: owner or operator of combustion turbine firing non-uniform fuels
units.action_summary: Such turbines may sample fuel CO2 and exclude pre-combustion CO2 from compliance calculations.

units.obligation_text: To demonstrate compliance with the applicable CO2 emission standard, for the initial and each subsequent 12-operating-month compliance period, the CO2 mass emissions rate for your affected EGU must be determined according to the procedures specified in paragraph (a)(1) through (7) of this section and must be less than or equal to the applicable CO2 emissions standard in Table 1, 2, or 3 of this part, or the emissions standard calculated in accordance with § 60.5525(a)(2).
units.actor: owner or operator of affected EGU
units.action_summary: CO2 mass emissions rate must be calculated per procedures and be ≤ applicable CO2 standard or calculated alternative standard.

units.obligation_text: Consistent with § 60.5520, the CO2 emissions standard (as identified in Table 1, 2, or 3 of this part) with which your affected EGU must comply;
units.action_summary: Include in required reports the applicable CO2 emissions standard that the affected EGU must comply with.
units.modal_raw: must (implied by context of required report contents)

units.obligation_text: You must keep records of the calculations you performed to assess compliance with each applicable CO2 mass emissions standard in Table 1, 2, or 3 of this subpart.
units.action_summary: Retain records of calculations used to assess compliance with applicable CO2 standards.

units.obligation_text: Design efficiency shall be determined using one of the following methods: ASME PTC 22 Gas Turbines, ASME PTC 46 Overall Plant Performance, ISO 2314 Gas turbines—acceptance tests, or an alternative approved by the Administrator.
units.actor: owner or operator (or party responsible for determining design efficiency)
units.action_summary: Determine design efficiency using one of the listed standardized methods or an Administrator-approved alternative.

units.obligation_text: Design efficiency shall be determined using ASME PTC 22 Gas Turbines (incorporated by reference, see § 60.17).
units.actor: owner or operator (or party responsible for determining design efficiency)
units.action_summary: One accepted method for determining design efficiency is ASME PTC 22.

units.obligation_text: Design efficiency shall be determined using ASME PTC 46 Overall Plant Performance (incorporated by reference, see § 60.17).
units.actor: owner or operator (or party responsible for determining design efficiency)
units.action_summary: One accepted method for determining design efficiency is ASME PTC 46.

units.obligation_text: Design efficiency shall be determined using ISO 2314 Gas turbines—acceptance tests (incorporated by reference, see § 60.17).
units.actor: owner or operator (or party responsible for determining design efficiency)
units.action_summary: One accepted method for determining design efficiency is ISO 2314.

units.obligation_text: Design efficiency shall be determined using an alternative approved by the Administrator.
units.actor: owner or operator (or party responsible for determining design efficiency)
units.action_summary: Design efficiency may be determined by an alternative method if the Administrator approves it.

title: Review of Standards of Performance for Greenhouse Gas Emissions From New, Modified, and Reconstructed Stationary Sources: Electric Utility Generating Units; Notice of Public Hearing

units.obligation_text: In an exceptional case, the Copyright Office may waive the online filing requirement set forth in paragraph (j)(6) of this section or may grant special relief from the deposit requirement under § 202.20(d), subject to such conditions as the Associate Register of Copyrights and Director of the Office of Registration Policy and Practice may impose on the applicant.
units.action_summary: May waive the online filing requirement or grant special relief from the deposit requirement in exceptional cases, subject to conditions imposed by the Associate Register and Director.

units.obligation_text: subject to such conditions as the Associate Register of Copyrights and Director of the Office of Registration Policy and Practice may impose on the applicant.
units.actor: Associate Register of Copyrights and Director of the Office of Registration Policy and Practice
units.action_summary: May impose conditions on an applicant as a condition of waiving online filing or granting special relief from the deposit requirement.

title: Revisions to Testing Regulations for Air Emission Sources

units.obligation_text: You must use the preliminary velocity traverse data.
units.actor: the tester / person performing the traverse
units.action_summary: Use the preliminary velocity traverse data for calculations.

units.obligation_text: The NEAR must be ≤0.05.
units.actor: the measured NEAR / the monitoring system (implicit: the tester/operator)
units.action_summary: Ensure the NEAR value is less than or equal to 0.05.

units.obligation_text: The gas dilution system shall be recalibrated once per calendar year using NIST-traceable flow standards with an uncertainty ≤0.25 percent.
units.actor: the owner/operator or person responsible for the gas dilution system
units.action_summary: Recalibrate the gas dilution system annually with NIST-traceable flow standards (uncertainty ≤0.25%).

units.obligation_text: You shall report the results of the calibration by the person or manufacturer who carried out the calibration whenever the dilution system is used, listing the date of the most recent calibration, the due date for the next calibration, calibration point, reference flow device (ID, S/N), and acceptance criteria.
units.action_summary: Report calibration results and specified calibration details whenever the dilution system is used.

units.obligation_text: Follow the manufacturer’s instructions for the operation and use of the gas dilution system.
units.action_summary: Use and operate the gas dilution system according to the manufacturer's instructions.

units.obligation_text: A copy of the manufacturer’s instructions for the operation of the instrument, as well as the most recent calibration documentation shall be made available for inspection at the test site.
units.action_summary: Make available the manufacturer's instructions and most recent calibration documentation for inspection at the test site.

units.obligation_text: The sampling time and sample volume for each run shall be at least 60 minutes and 0.85 dscm (30 dscf).
units.action_summary: Ensure each run's sampling time is at least 60 minutes and sample volume at least 0.85 dscm.

units.obligation_text: The probe and filter holder heating systems in the sampling train shall be set to provide an average gas temperature of 160 ±5 °C (320 ±9 °F).
units.action_summary: Set probe and filter holder heating to provide average gas temperature of 160 ±5 °C.

units.obligation_text: The sampling time and sample volume for each run shall be at least 120 minutes and 1.70 dscm (60 dscf).
units.action_summary: Ensure each run samples for at least 120 minutes and 1.70 dscm volume.

units.obligation_text: The probe and filter holder heating system in the sampling train may be set to provide an average gas temperature of no greater than 160 ±5 °C (320 ±9 °F).
units.action_summary: Optionally set heating system to provide gas temperature not greater than 160 ±5 °C.

units.obligation_text: For Method 5 of appendix A of this part, the temperature of the sample gas in the probe and filter holder is monitored and is maintained at 160 ±5 °C (320 ±9 °F).
units.action_summary: Monitor and maintain sample gas temperature in probe and filter holder at 160 ±5 °C when using Method 5.

units.obligation_text: For Method 5 or 5B of appendix A of this part, the temperature of the sample gas in the probe and filter holder shall be monitored and maintained at 160 ±5 °C (320 ±9 °F).
units.action_summary: Monitor and maintain probe and filter holder sample gas temperature at 160 ±5 °C for Method 5 or 5B.

units.obligation_text: Method 5 shall be used for determining compliance with the particulate matter emission limit.
units.action_summary: Use Method 5 to determine compliance with PM emission limit.

units.obligation_text: The minimum sample volume shall be 1.7 cubic meters (60 cubic feet).
units.action_summary: Collect at least 1.7 m3 (60 ft3) sample volume for each run.

units.obligation_text: The probe and filter holder heating systems in the sample train shall be set to provide a gas temperature of 160° ±5 °C (320° ±9 °F).
units.action_summary: Set heating systems to provide 160 ±5 °C gas temperature in sample train.

units.obligation_text: An oxygen or carbon dioxide measurement shall be obtained simultaneously with each Method 5 run.
units.action_summary: Obtain O2 or CO2 measurement simultaneously during each Method 5 run.

units.obligation_text: Test methods and procedures as specified in § 60.296 shall be used to determine compliance with this section
units.action_summary: Use the test methods in §60.296 to determine compliance.

units.obligation_text: except that to determine compliance for any glass melting furnace using modified processes and fired with either a gaseous fuel or a liquid fuel containing less than 0.50 weight percent sulfur, Method 5 shall be used with the probe and filter holder heating system in the sampling train set to provide a gas temperature of 120 ±5 °C (248 ±9 °F).
units.action_summary: For specified glass melting furnaces, use Method 5 with probe/filter heating set to 120 ±5 °C.

units.obligation_text: Method 5 shall be used to determine the particulate matter concentration (cs) and volumetric flow rate (Qsd) of the effluent gas.
units.action_summary: Use Method 5 to measure particulate concentration and flow rate of the effluent gas.

units.obligation_text: The sampling time and sample volume for each run shall be at least 60 minutes and 0.90 dscm (31.8 dscf).
units.action_summary: Ensure each Method 5 run lasts at least 60 minutes and collects at least 0.90 dscm.

units.obligation_text: The probe and filter holder heating system may be set to provide a gas temperature no greater than 177 ±5 °C (350 ±9 °F), except under the conditions specified in § 60.293(e).
units.action_summary: You may set probe/filter heating up to 177 ±5 °C, unless §60.293(e) applies.

units.obligation_text: (CO2)a = Ambient carbon dioxide concentration, ppm (if not measured during the test period, may be assumed to equal the global monthly mean CO2 concentration posted at http://www.esrl.noaa.gov/gmd/ccgg/trends/global.html#global_data).
units.action_summary: If ambient CO2 not measured, you may assume it equals the global monthly mean CO2 concentration from the referenced source.

units.obligation_text: Particulate matter is withdrawn isokinetically from the source and collected on a glass fiber filter maintained at a temperature of 120 ±5 °C (248 ±9 °F) or such other temperature as specified by an applicable subpart of the standards or approved by the Administrator for a particular application.
units.action_summary: Collect PM isokinetically on a filter maintained at 120 ±5 °C unless another temperature is specified or approved.

units.obligation_text: Borosilicate or quartz glass tubing with a heating system capable of maintaining a probe gas temperature during sampling of 120 ±5 °C (248 ±9 °F), or such other temperature as specified by an applicable subpart of the standards or as approved by the Administrator for a particular application.
units.action_summary: Use borosilicate or quartz probe liners with heating capable of maintaining probe gas temperature at 120 ±5 °C (unless other temp specified/approved).

units.obligation_text: Either borosilicate or quartz glass probe liners may be used for stack temperatures up to about 480 °C (900 °F); quartz glass liners shall be used for temperatures between 480 and 900 °C (900 and 1,650 °F).
units.action_summary: Allow borosilicate or quartz liners up to ~480 °C; require quartz liners for 480–900 °C stack temps.

units.obligation_text: Both types of liners may be used at higher temperatures than specified for short periods of time, subject to the approval of the Administrator.
units.action_summary: You may use either liner above specified temps for short periods if Administrator approves.

units.obligation_text: Alternatively, metal liners (e.g., 316 stainless steel, Incoloy 825 or other corrosion resistant metals) made of seamless tubing may be used, subject to the approval of the Administrator.
units.action_summary: Metal liners may be used as an alternative if Administrator approves.

units.obligation_text: Any heating system capable of monitoring and maintaining temperature around the filter shall be used to ensure the sample gas temperature exiting the filter of 120 ± 5 °C (248 ±9 °F) during sampling or such other temperature as specified by an applicable subpart of the standards or approved by the Administrator for a particular application.
units.action_summary: Use a heating system that monitors and maintains filter temperature to yield 120 ±5 °C sample gas exiting the filter (unless other temp specified/approved).

units.obligation_text: A temperature sensor capable of measuring temperature to within ±3 °C (5.4 °F) shall be installed so that the sensing tip of the temperature sensor is in direct contact with the sample gas exiting the filter.
units.action_summary: Install a temperature sensor with ±3 °C accuracy with its sensing tip in direct contact with the sample gas exiting the filter.

units.obligation_text: The sensing tip of the sensor may be encased in glass, Teflon, or metal and must protrude at least 1/2 in. into the sample gas exiting the filter.
units.action_summary: Ensure sensor tip protrudes at least 1/2 inch into sample gas; may be encased in specified materials.

units.obligation_text: The filter temperature sensor must be monitored and recorded during sampling to ensure a sample gas temperature exiting the filter of 120 ±5 °C (248 ±9 °F), or such other temperature as specified by an applicable subpart of the standards or approved by the Administrator for a particular application.
units.action_summary: Monitor and record filter temperature sensor during sampling to ensure sample gas temp exiting filter is 120 ±5 °C (or other specified/approved).

units.obligation_text: Metering System. Vacuum gauge, leak-free pump, calibrated temperature sensors, dry gas meter (DGM) capable of measuring volume to within 2 percent, and related equipment, as shown in Figure 5–1.
units.action_summary: Use a metering system including vacuum gauge, leak-free pump, calibrated temp sensors, and a DGM capable of ±2% volume measurement.

units.obligation_text: Other metering systems capable of maintaining sampling rates within 10 percent of isokinetic and of determining sample volumes to within 2 percent may be used, subject to the approval of the Administrator.
units.action_summary: Alternative metering systems with required performance may be used if Administrator approves.

units.obligation_text: When the metering system is used in conjunction with a pitot tube, the system shall allow periodic checks of isokinetic rates.
units.action_summary: Ensure metering system allows periodic checks of isokinetic sampling when used with a pitot tube.

units.obligation_text: During the sampling run, maintain an isokinetic sampling rate (within 10 percent of true isokinetic unless otherwise specified by the Administrator) and a sample gas temperature through the filter of 120 ±5 °C (248 ±9 °F) or such other temperature as specified by an applicable subpart of the standards or approved by the Administrator.
units.action_summary: Maintain isokinetic sampling rate within 10% and sample gas temperature through filter at 120 ±5 °C (unless other specified/approved).

units.obligation_text: The probe liner heating system and filter heating system must be capable of maintaining a sample gas temperature of 160 ±5 °C (320 ±9 °F).
units.action_summary: Ensure probe liner and filter heating systems can maintain 160 ±5 °C sample gas temperature.

units.obligation_text: Maintain the probe outlet and filter temperatures at 160 ±5 °C (320 ±9 °F).
units.action_summary: Keep probe outlet and filter temperatures at 160 ±5 °C during sampling.

units.obligation_text: Record and report the data required on a sheet such as the one shown in Figure 5B–1.
units.action_summary: Record and report required data on the specified data sheet format.

units.obligation_text: Leave the contents in the shipping container or transfer the filter and any loose PM from the sample container to a tared glass weighing dish. Oven dry the filter sample at a temperature of 160 ±5 °C (320 ±9 °F) for 6 hours. Cool in a desiccator for 2 hours, and weigh to constant weight. Report the results to the nearest 0.1 mg.
units.action_summary: Handle Container No.1 by leaving or transferring contents, oven-drying at 160 ±5 °C for 6 hours, desiccating 2 hours, weigh to constant weight, and report to 0.1 mg.

units.obligation_text: Note the level of liquid in the container, and confirm on the analysis sheet whether leakage occurred during transport. If a noticeable amount of leakage has occurred, either void the sample or use methods, subject to the approval of the Administrator, to correct the final results.
units.action_summary: Record liquid level and leakage; if leakage occurred, either void sample or correct results using Administrator-approved methods.
units.modal_raw: shall / may (void or use approved methods)

units.obligation_text: Weigh the spent silica gel (or silica gel plus impinger) to the nearest 0.5 g using a balance.
units.action_summary: Weigh spent silica gel to nearest 0.5 g.

units.obligation_text: Measure the acetone in this container either volumetrically or gravimetrically. Transfer the acetone to a tared 250 ml beaker, and evaporate to dryness at ambient temperature and pressure. Desiccate for 24 hours, and weigh to a constant weight. Report the results to the nearest 0.1 mg.
units.action_summary: Measure acetone, transfer to tared beaker, evaporate to dryness, desiccate 24 hours, weigh to constant weight, report to 0.1 mg.

units.obligation_text: Care should be taken to maintain the filter box temperature of the paired trains as close as possible to the Method required temperature of 120 ±5 °C (248 ±9 °F). If separate ovens are being used for simultaneously operated trains, it is recommended that the oven temperature of each train be maintained within ±5 °C (±9 °F) of each other.
units.action_summary: Maintain paired train filter box temperatures close to 120 ±5 °C and, if using separate ovens, keep oven temps within ±5 °C of each other.

units.obligation_text: This calibration procedure must be repeated on each day that samples are analyzed.
units.action_summary: Repeat the calibration procedure daily when samples are analyzed.

units.obligation_text: Mix the contents of the flask thoroughly, and measure the absorbance at the optimum wavelength used for the standards ... Dilute the sample and the blank with equal volumes of water if the absorbance exceeds A4.
units.action_summary: Thoroughly mix, measure absorbance at optimum wavelength, and dilute sample/blank if absorbance exceeds specified standard.

units.obligation_text: When the stack temperature exceeds 210 °C (410 °F), a leak-free ground glass fitting or other leak free, non-contaminating fitting must be used to couple the nozzle to the probe liner.
units.action_summary: Use a leak-free ground glass or equivalent fitting to couple nozzle to probe liner when stack temp >210 °C.

units.obligation_text: The probe nozzle shall be of the button-hook or elbow design, unless otherwise specified by the Administrator.
units.action_summary: Use a button-hook or elbow design probe nozzle unless Administrator specifies otherwise.

units.obligation_text: Probe Liner. Borosilicate or quartz glass, with a heating system to prevent visible condensation during sampling. Do not use metal probe liners.
units.action_summary: Use borosilicate or quartz probe liners with heating to prevent condensation; do not use metal probe liners.

units.obligation_text: The holder design shall provide a positive seal against leakage from the outside or around the filter. The filter holder shall be placed between the first and second impingers. Do not heat the filter holder.
units.action_summary: Ensure filter holder provides positive seal, place it between first and second impingers, and do not heat it.

units.obligation_text: The first and third impingers must have standard tips. The second and fourth impingers must be modified by replacing the insert with an approximately 13-mm (1/2-in.) ID glass tube, having an unconstricted tip located 13 mm (1/2 in.) from the bottom of the impinger.
units.action_summary: Equip impingers with specified tip configurations: first/third standard, second/fourth modified with specified tube.

units.obligation_text: Thermometer, or equivalent, to measure the temperature of the gas leaving the impinger train to within 1 °C (2 °F).
units.action_summary: Use a thermometer or equivalent to measure impinger effluent gas temperature to within 1 °C accuracy.

units.obligation_text: After developing an appropriate sampling and analytical system for the pollutants of interest, conduct the procedure in section 8.4. Conduct the appropriate recovery study in section 8.4 at each sampling point where the method is being applied. Submit the data and results of the recovery procedure with the reporting of results under section 8.3.
units.action_summary: Conduct the procedure and recovery study at each sampling point and submit the recovery data with reports.

units.obligation_text: Outdoor Location. Record the following information on the field data sheet ... Record also the estimated wind speed, wind direction, and sky condition. Sketch the process unit being observed, and note the observer location relative to the source and the sun. Indicate the potential and actual emission points on the sketch.
units.action_summary: Record specified identification, meteorological and positional information and sketch emission points for outdoor observations.

units.obligation_text: Alternatively, digital photography as described in Section 11.2.3 may be used for a subset of the recordkeeping requirements of this section.
units.action_summary: You may use digital photography as an alternative for part of the recordkeeping requirements.

units.obligation_text: Indoor Location. Record the following information on the field data sheet ... Indicate the potential and actual fugitive emission points on the sketch.
units.action_summary: Record specified identification and lighting info and sketch emission points for indoor observations.

units.obligation_text: Digital photographs, annotated or unaltered, may be used to record and report sky conditions, observer’s location relative to the source, observer’s location relative to the sun, process unit being observed, potential emission points and actual emission points for the requirements in Sections 11.2.1 and 11.2.2.
units.action_summary: You may use digital photographs to record and report required observational details.

units.obligation_text: The image must have the proper lighting, field of view and depth of field to properly distinguish the sky condition (if applicable), process unit, potential emission point and actual emission point.
units.action_summary: Ensure digital photographs have appropriate lighting, field of view, and depth of field to distinguish required elements.

units.obligation_text: At least one digital photograph must be from the point of the view of the observer.
units.action_summary: Include at least one photo taken from the observer's point of view.

units.obligation_text: The photograph(s) representing the environmental conditions must be taken within reasonable time of the observation (i.e., 15 mins).
units.action_summary: Take photos representing environmental conditions within about 15 minutes of the observation.

units.obligation_text: Any photographs altered or annotated must be retained in an unaltered format for recordkeeping purposes.
units.action_summary: Retain unaltered originals of any altered or annotated photographs for records.

units.obligation_text: Storage Bottles. 100- or 250-ml, high-density polyethylene or glass sample storage containers with Teflon screw cap liners to store impinger samples.
units.action_summary: Use 100- or 250-ml HDPE or glass containers with Teflon screw cap liners for impinger samples.

units.obligation_text: Probe-Liner and Probe-Nozzle Brushes, Wash Bottles, Petri Dishes, Graduated Cylinder and/or Balance, and Rubber Policeman. Same as Method 5, sections 6.2.1, 6.2.2, 6.2.4, 6.2.5, and 6.2.7.
units.action_summary: Provide and use the same set of sampling tools/equipment as required in Method 5 sections referenced.

units.obligation_text: Sample Storage Containers. High-density polyethylene or glass sample storage containers with Teflon screw cap liners to store impinger samples.
units.action_summary: Use HDPE or glass sample storage containers with Teflon liners for impinger samples.

units.section: Appendix B to Part 60, Performance Specification 1, 2.1
units.obligation_text: The opacity monitor manufacturer must periodically select and test an opacity monitor, that is representative of a group of monitors produced during a specified period or lot, for conformance with the design specifications in ASTM D6216–12.
units.action_summary: Manufacturer must periodically select and test representative monitors for conformance with ASTM D6216–12 design specs.

units.section: Appendix B to Part 60, Performance Specification 1, 2.1
units.obligation_text: The opacity monitor manufacturer must test each opacity monitor for conformance with the manufacturer’s performance specifications in ASTM D6216–12.
units.action_summary: Manufacturer must test every monitor to ensure conformance with its performance specifications.

units.section: Appendix B to Part 60, Performance Specification 1, 6.1
units.obligation_text: You, as owner or operator, are responsible for purchasing an opacity monitor that meets the specifications of ASTM D6216–12, including a suitable data recorder or automated data acquisition handling system.
units.action_summary: Owner/operator must purchase an opacity monitor that meets ASTM D6216–12 specs and include suitable data recorder or DAHS.

units.section: Appendix B to Part 60, Performance Specification 1, 8.1(1)
units.obligation_text: You must purchase an opacity monitor that complies with ASTM D6216–12 and obtain a certificate of conformance from the opacity monitor manufacturer.
units.action_summary: Purchase a monitor that complies with ASTM D6216–12 and obtain its certificate of conformance from the manufacturer.

units.section: Appendix B to Part 60, Performance Specification 1, 8.1(3)(ii)
units.obligation_text: Conduct a three-point calibration error test using three calibration attenuators ... Make a total of five nonconsecutive readings for each attenuator. At the end of the test, correlate each attenuator insertion to the corresponding value from the data recorder. ... Calculate the calibration error ... Report the calibration error test results for each of the three attenuators.
units.action_summary: Perform three-point calibration error test with specified procedure, take five readings per attenuator, correlate readings, calculate calibration error and report results.

units.section: Appendix B to Part 60, Performance Specification 1, 8.2(1)
units.obligation_text: Conduct the verification procedures for design specifications in section 6 of ASTM D6216–12.
units.action_summary: Perform verification procedures for design specifications per ASTM section 6.

units.section: Appendix B to Part 60, Performance Specification 1, 8.2(2)
units.obligation_text: Conduct the verification procedures for performance specifications in section 7 of ASTM D6216–12.
units.action_summary: Perform verification procedures for performance specifications per ASTM section 7.

units.section: Appendix B to Part 60, Performance Specification 1, 8.2(3)
units.obligation_text: Provide to the owner or operator, a report of the opacity monitor’s conformance to the design and performance specifications required in sections 6 and 7 of ASTM D6216–12 in accordance with the reporting requirements of section 9 in ASTM D6216–12.
units.action_summary: Deliver a conformance report to the owner/operator consistent with ASTM reporting requirements.

units.section: Appendix B to Part 60, Performance Specification 1, 9.0
units.obligation_text: Opacity monitor manufacturers must initiate a quality program following the requirements of ASTM D6216–12, section 8. The quality program must include (1) a quality system and (2) a corrective action program.
units.action_summary: Manufacturers must start a quality program per ASTM section 8, including a quality system and corrective action program.

units.section: Appendix B to Part 60, Performance Specification 1, 13.1
units.obligation_text: Design Specifications. The opacity monitoring equipment must comply with the design specifications of ASTM D6216–12.
units.action_summary: Ensure opacity monitoring equipment complies with ASTM D6216–12 design specifications.

units.section: Appendix B to Part 60, Performance Specification 1, 13.2
units.obligation_text: Manufacturer’s Performance Specifications. The opacity monitor must comply with the manufacturer’s performance specifications of ASTM D6216–12.
units.action_summary: Opacity monitor must meet manufacturer's performance specs in ASTM D6216–12.

units.section: Appendix B to Part 60, Performance Specification 2, 13.2
units.obligation_text: Relative Accuracy Performance Specification. [RA criteria rows specifying percent limits under specified conditions].
units.action_summary: Ensure the CEMS relative accuracy meets the specified percentage limits depending on average emissions and emission standard ranges.

units.section: Appendix B to Part 60, Performance Specification 3, 12.0
units.obligation_text: Calculations and Data Analysis. Summarize the results on a data sheet similar to that shown in Figure 2.2 of PS2.
units.action_summary: Summarize calculation and analysis results on a data sheet similar to the referenced figure.

units.section: Appendix B to Part 60, Performance Specification 3, 13.2
units.obligation_text: The RA of the CEMS must be no greater than 20.0 percent of the mean value of the reference method (RM) data when calculated using equation 3–1. The results are also acceptable if the result of Equation 3–2 is less than or equal to 1.0 percent O2 (or CO2).
units.action_summary: Ensure CEMS relative accuracy is ≤20% of RM mean (per Eq.3-1), or meet alternative Eq.3-2 threshold of ≤1.0% O2 (or CO2).

units.section: Appendix B to Part 60, Performance Specification 11, 13.1
units.obligation_text: Your daily PM CEMS internal drift checks must demonstrate that the daily drift of your PM CEMS does not deviate from the value of the reference light, optical filter, Beta attenuation signal, or other technology-suitable reference standard by more than 2 percent of the response range.
units.action_summary: Daily internal drift checks must show PM CEMS drift ≤2% of response range relative to reference standard.

units.section: Appendix B to Part 60, Performance Specification 11, 13.1
units.obligation_text: If your CEMS includes diluent and/or auxiliary monitors ... you must determine the calibration drift separately for each ancillary monitor in terms of its respective output. None of the calibration drifts may exceed their individual specification.
units.action_summary: Determine calibration drift separately for each ancillary monitor and ensure none exceed their individual specifications.

units.section: Appendix B to Part 60, Performance Specification 18, 11.8.7
units.obligation_text: The zero-level and mid-level CD for each day must be less than 5.0 percent of the span value as specified in section 13.2 of this PS. You must meet this criterion for 7 consecutive operating days.
units.action_summary: Ensure daily zero- and mid-level calibration drift <5% of span, and meet this for 7 consecutive operating days.

units.section: Appendix B to Part 60, Performance Specification 18, TABLE 1 note 1
units.obligation_text: Any of these specific gases can be tested at a lower level if the manufacturer has provided reliable means for limiting or scrubbing that gas to a specified level in CEMS field installations.
units.action_summary: You may test certain interferent gases at lower concentrations if manufacturer provides means to limit or scrub them.

units.section: Appendix B to Part 60, Performance Specification 18, TABLE 1 note 2
units.obligation_text: Gases for short path IP cell interference tests cannot be added above 100 percent stack equivalent concentration.
units.action_summary: Do not add gases above 100% stack equivalent concentration during short path IP cell interference tests.

title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Surface Coating of Wood Building Products Residual Risk and Technology Review

units.obligation_text: For a new or reconstructed affected source, the compliance date is the applicable date in paragraph (a)(1), (2) or (3) of this section:
units.actor: owner or operator of a new or reconstructed affected source
units.action_summary: New or reconstructed affected sources must comply by the applicable date identified in (a)(1)-(3).

units.obligation_text: If the initial startup of your new or reconstructed affected source is before May 28, 2003, the compliance date is May 28, 2003; except that the compliance date for the revised requirements promulgated at §§ 63.4683, 63.4700, 63.4710, 63.4720, 63.4730, 63.4741, 63.4751, 63.4761, 63.4763, 63.4764, 63.4766, 63.4781, Table 4 of this subpart QQQQ, and Appendix A of this subpart QQQQ published on [DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER] is [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER THE DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER].
units.actor: owner or operator of a new or reconstructed affected source
units.action_summary: If initial startup before May 28, 2003, compliance date is May 28, 2003, except certain revised requirements have a compliance date 180 days after final rule publication.

units.obligation_text: If the initial startup of your new or reconstructed affected source occurs after May 28, 2003, the compliance date is the date of initial startup of your affected source; except that if the initial startup of your new or reconstructed affected source occurs after May 28, 2003, but on or before May 16, 2018, the compliance date for the revised requirements promulgated at [list of sections] published on [DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER] is [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER THE DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER].
units.actor: owner or operator of a new or reconstructed affected source
units.action_summary: If initial startup after May 28, 2003, compliance date is startup date; but for startups after May 28, 2003 and on/before May 16, 2018 certain revised requirements have compliance date 180 days after final rule publication.

units.obligation_text: If the initial startup of your new or reconstructed affected source occurs after May 16, 2018, the compliance date is [DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER] or the date of startup, whichever is later.
units.actor: owner or operator of a new or reconstructed affected source
units.action_summary: For startups after May 16, 2018, compliance date is final rule publication date or startup date, whichever is later.

units.obligation_text: For an existing affected source, the compliance date is the date 3 years after May 28, 2003, except that the compliance date for the revised requirements promulgated at [list of sections] published on [DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER] is [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER THE DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER].
units.actor: owner or operator of an existing affected source
units.action_summary: Existing affected sources must comply by 3 years after May 28, 2003, except revised requirements have compliance date 180 days after final rule publication.

units.obligation_text: Any coating operation(s) at existing sources for which you use the emission rate with add-on controls option, as specified in § 63.4691(c), must be in compliance with the applicable emission limitations as specified in paragraphs (a)(2)(i) through (iii) of this section.
units.actor: owner or operator of existing sources using the emission rate with add-on controls option
units.action_summary: Coating operations using the emission-rate-with-add-on-controls option at existing sources must meet the applicable emission limits and related provisions in (a)(2)(i)-(iii).

units.obligation_text: Prior to [DATE 181 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], the coating operation(s) must be in compliance with the applicable emission limit in § 63.4690 at all times, except during periods of startup, shutdown, and malfunction (SSM). After [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], the coating operation(s) must be in compliance with the applicable emission limit in § 63.4690 at all times.
units.actor: owner or operator of coating operations at existing sources
units.action_summary: Coating operations must comply with §63.4690 emission limits at all times; prior to a specified date SSM periods are excepted, after the later date compliance is required at all times.

units.obligation_text: Prior to [DATE 181 DAYS AFTER PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], the coating operation(s) must be in compliance with the applicable operating limits for emission capture systems and add-on control devices required by § 63.4692 at all times, except during periods of SSM, and except for solvent recovery systems for which you conduct liquid-liquid material balances according to § 63.4761(j). After [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], the coating operation(s) must be in compliance with the operating limits for emission capture systems and add-on control devices required by § 63.4692 at all times, except for solvent recovery systems for which you conduct liquid-liquid material balances according to § 63.4761(j).
units.actor: owner or operator of coating operations at existing sources
units.action_summary: Coating operations must meet operating limits for capture systems and add-on controls at all times, with SSM exceptions before a date and specified exception for solvent recovery liquid-liquid material balances.

units.obligation_text: For new or reconstructed sources with initial startup after May 16, 2018, any coating operation(s) for which you use the emission rate with add-on controls option, as specified in § 63.4691(c), must be in compliance with the applicable emission limitations and work practice standards as specified in paragraphs (a)(3)(i) through (iii) of this section.
units.actor: owner or operator of new or reconstructed sources
units.action_summary: New/reconstructed sources using the emission-rate-with-add-on-controls option must meet specified emission limits and work practice standards in (a)(3)(i)-(iii).

units.obligation_text: The coating operation(s) must be in compliance with the applicable emission limit in § 63.4690 at all times.
units.actor: owner or operator of coating operations at new or reconstructed sources
units.action_summary: Coating operations at new/reconstructed sources must continuously meet the §63.4690 emission limits.

units.obligation_text: The coating operation(s) must be in compliance with the operating limits for emission capture systems and add-on control devices required by § 63.4692 at all times, except for solvent recovery systems for which you conduct liquid-liquid material balances according to § 63.4761(j).
units.actor: owner or operator of coating operations at new or reconstructed sources
units.action_summary: Coating operations must continuously meet operating limits for capture systems and add-on controls, with specified exception for certain solvent recovery systems.

units.obligation_text: The coating operation(s) must be in compliance with the work practice standards in § 63.4693 at all times.
units.actor: owner or operator of coating operations at new or reconstructed sources
units.action_summary: Coating operations must continuously follow the work practice standards in §63.4693.

units.obligation_text: For existing sources as of May 16, 2018, prior to [DATE 181 DAYS AFTER PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], you must always operate and maintain your affected source, including all air pollution control and monitoring equipment you use for purposes of complying with this subpart, according to the provisions in § 63.6(e)(1)(i). After [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER] for such existing sources and after [DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER] for new or reconstructed sources, you must always operate and maintain your affected source, including associated air pollution control equipment and monitoring equipment, in a manner consistent with safety and good air pollution control practices for minimizing emissions.
units.action_summary: Operators must operate and maintain affected sources and associated control/monitoring equipment per §63.6(e)(1)(i) before a date, and thereafter in accordance with safety and good practices to minimize emissions.

units.obligation_text: The general duty to minimize emissions does not require you to make any further efforts to reduce emissions if levels required by the applicable standard have been achieved.
units.action_summary: Operators are not required to take further emission reductions beyond meeting applicable standards.

units.obligation_text: Determination of whether a source is operating in compliance with operation and maintenance requirements will be based on information available to the Administrator which may include, but is not limited to, monitoring results, review of operation and maintenance procedures, review of operation and maintenance records, and inspection of the source.
units.action_summary: Administrator's compliance determinations will be based on available information such as monitoring results, records, procedures, and inspections.

units.obligation_text: For existing sources until [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], if your affected source uses an emission capture system and add-on control device, you must develop a written startup, shutdown, and malfunction plan (SSMP) according to the provisions in § 63.6(e)(3).
units.actor: you (owner or operator) of existing sources using emission capture systems and add-on controls
units.action_summary: Existing sources using capture systems and add-on controls must develop an SSMP meeting §63.6(e)(3) requirements during the specified period.

units.obligation_text: The SSMP must address startup, shutdown, and corrective actions in the event of a malfunction of the emission capture system or the add-on control device.
units.action_summary: The SSMP must include procedures for startup, shutdown, and corrective actions for malfunctions of capture systems or add-on controls.

units.obligation_text: The SSMP must also address any coating operation equipment that may cause increased emissions or that would affect capture efficiency if the process equipment malfunctions, such as conveyors that move parts among enclosures.
units.action_summary: The SSMP must cover any equipment that could increase emissions or affect capture efficiency if it malfunctions.

units.obligation_text: For the emission rate without add-on controls option, provide the calculation of the total mass of organic HAP emissions for each month; the calculation of the total volume of coating solids used each month; and the calculation of the 12-month organic HAP emission rate, using Equations 1 and 1A (or 1A-alt) through 1C, 2, and 3, respectively, of § 63.4751.
units.actor: you (owner or operator) using the emission rate without add-on controls option
units.action_summary: Operators using the emission-rate-without-add-on-controls option must provide monthly calculations of organic HAP mass, coating solids volume, and the 12-month emission rate using specified equations.

units.obligation_text: The calculations used to determine the 12-month organic HAP emission rate for the compliance period in which the deviation occurred. You must provide the calculations for Equations 1, 1A (or 1A-alt) through 1C, 2, and 3 in § 63.4751; and if applicable, the calculation used to determine mass of organic HAP in waste materials according to § 63.4751(e)(4). You do not need to submit background data supporting these calculations (e.g., information provided by materials suppliers or manufacturers, or test reports).
units.action_summary: Operators must provide the calculations used to determine the 12-month organic HAP emission rate (and certain waste mass calculations), but are not required to submit background supporting data.

units.obligation_text: Deviations: emission rate with add-on controls option. You must be in compliance with the emission limitations in this subpart as specified in paragraphs (7)(i) and (ii) of this section.
units.action_summary: Operators using emission-rate-with-add-on-controls option must comply with emission limitations and reporting provisions described in (7)(i) and (ii).

units.obligation_text: For existing sources until [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], if you used the emission rate with add-on controls option and there was a deviation from an emission limitation (including any periods when emissions bypassed the add-on control device and were diverted to the atmosphere), the semiannual compliance report must contain the information in paragraphs (a)(7)(i)(A) through (N) of this section. This includes periods of SSM during which deviations occurred.
units.actor: you (owner or operator) at existing sources
units.action_summary: Existing sources must include specified information (A-N) in semiannual compliance reports if deviations occurred while using emission-rate-with-add-on-controls option.

units.obligation_text: After [DATES], if you used the emission rate with add-on controls option and there was a deviation from an emission limitation (including any periods when emissions bypassed the add-on control device and were diverted to the atmosphere), the semiannual compliance report must contain the information in paragraphs (a)(7)(ii)(A) through (M) of this section.
units.action_summary: For new/reconstructed sources (after specific dates) and after specified date for existing sources, semiannual reports must include specified information A-M when deviations occurred.

units.obligation_text: The beginning and ending dates of each compliance period during which the 12-month organic HAP emission rate exceeded the applicable emission limit in § 63.4690.
units.action_summary: Reports must include start and end dates of compliance periods when the 12-month emission rate exceeded the limit.

units.obligation_text: The calculations used to determine the 12-month organic HAP emission rate for each compliance period in which a deviation occurred. You must provide the calculation of the total mass of organic HAP emissions for the coatings, thinners, and cleaning materials used each month, using Equations 1 and 1A through 1C of § 63.4751; and, if applicable, the calculation used to determine mass of organic HAP in waste materials according to § 63.4751(e)(4); the calculation of the total volume of coating solids used each month, using Equation 2 of § 63.4751; the calculation of the mass of organic HAP emission reduction each month by emission capture systems and add-on control devices, using Equations 1 and 1A through 1D of § 63.4761, and Equations 2, 3, and 3A through 3C of § 63.4761, as applicable; the calculation of the total mass of organic HAP emissions each month, using Equation 4 of § 63.4761; and the calculation of the 12-month organic HAP emission rate, using Equation 5 of § 63.4761. You do not need to submit the background data supporting these calculations (e.g., information provided by materials suppliers or manufacturers, or test reports).
units.action_summary: Reports must include detailed calculations for monthly and 12-month emission rates and reductions using specified equations; background supporting data is not required to be submitted.

units.obligation_text: A brief description of the CPMS.
units.action_summary: Reports must include a brief description of the Continuous Parameter Monitoring System (CPMS).

units.obligation_text: The date of the latest CPMS certification or audit.
units.action_summary: Reports must state the date of the most recent CPMS certification or audit.

units.obligation_text: The date and time that each CPMS was inoperative, except for zero (low-level) and high-level checks.
units.action_summary: Reports must list dates and times each CPMS was inoperative, excluding certain checks.

units.obligation_text: The date, time, and duration that each CPMS was out-of-control, including the information in § 63.8(c)(8).
units.action_summary: Reports must include details on CPMS out-of-control events including date, time, duration and required §63.8(c)(8) information.

units.obligation_text: The date and time period of each deviation from an operating limit in Table 3 to this subpart, date and time period of any bypass of the add-on control device.
units.action_summary: Reports must record dates and time periods for deviations from Table 3 operating limits and any bypasses of add-on control devices.

units.obligation_text: A summary of the total duration of each deviation from an operating limit in Table 3 to this subpart, each bypass of the add-on control device during the semiannual reporting period, and the total duration as a percent of the total source operating time during that semiannual reporting period.
units.action_summary: Reports must summarize total durations of deviations and bypasses and express these as a percent of operating time for the reporting period.

units.obligation_text: A breakdown of the total duration of the deviations from the operating limits in Table 3 to this subpart and bypasses of the add-on control device during the semiannual reporting period by identifying deviations due to control equipment problems, process problems, other known causes, and other unknown causes; a list of the affected source or equipment, an estimate of the quantity of each regulated pollutant emitted over any emission limit, and a description of the method used to estimate the emissions.
units.action_summary: Reports must break down deviation durations by cause, list affected equipment, estimate pollutant quantities over limits, and describe estimation methods.

units.obligation_text: A summary of the total duration of CPMS downtime during the semiannual reporting period and the total duration of CPMS downtime as a percent of the total source operating time during that semiannual reporting period.
units.action_summary: Reports must summarize CPMS downtime duration and express it as a percentage of operating time.

units.obligation_text: A description of any changes in the CPMS, coating operation, emission capture system, or add-on control device since the last semiannual reporting period.
units.action_summary: Reports must describe any changes to CPMS, coating operations, capture systems, or add-on controls since the last report.

units.obligation_text: For each deviation from the work practice standards, a description of the deviation, the date and time period of the deviation, and the actions you took to correct the deviation.
units.action_summary: Reports must include details for each deviation from work practice standards and corrective actions taken.

units.obligation_text: A statement of the cause of each deviation.
units.action_summary: Reports must state the cause for each deviation.

units.obligation_text: For existing sources until [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], if you used the emission rate with add-on controls option and you had an SSM during the semiannual reporting period, you must submit the reports specified in paragraphs (c)(1) and (2) of this section.
units.actor: you (owner or operator) at existing sources
units.action_summary: Existing sources with SSM events must submit the specified SSM reports during the semiannual reporting period.

units.obligation_text: Within 60 days after the date of completing each performance test (as defined in § 63.2) required by this subpart, the owner or operator must submit the results of the performance test following the procedure specified in either paragraph (d)(1)(i) or (ii) of this section.
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must submit performance test results within 60 days following the procedures in (d)(1)(i) or (ii).

units.obligation_text: For data collected using test methods supported by the EPA’s Electronic Reporting Tool (ERT) ... the owner or operator must submit the results of the performance test to the EPA via CEDRI. Performance test data must be submitted in a file format generated using the EPA’s ERT or an alternate electronic file format consistent with the XML schema listed on the EPA’s ERT website. If the owner or operator claims that some of the performance test information being submitted is confidential business information (CBI), the owner or operator must submit a complete file generated through the use of the EPA’s ERT or an alternate electronic file consistent with the XML schema listed on the EPA’s ERT website, including information claimed to be CBI, on a compact disc, flash drive, or other commonly used electronic storage media to the EPA. The same ERT or alternate file with the CBI omitted must be submitted to the EPA via the EPA’s CDX as described earlier in this paragraph.
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must submit ERT-supported performance test results via CEDRI in specified file formats; if claiming CBI, submit complete file on physical media to EPA and submit CBI-omitted file via CDX.

units.obligation_text: For data collected using test methods that are not supported by the EPA’s ERT ... the owner or operator must submit the results of the performance test to the Administrator at the appropriate address listed in § 63.13 unless the Administrator agrees to or specifies an alternative reporting method.
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must submit non-ERT performance test results to the Administrator at the address in §63.13 unless alternative reporting is specified.

units.obligation_text: You must submit notifications and semiannual compliance reports to the EPA via the CEDRI. You must use the appropriate electronic report in CEDRI for this subpart or an alternative electronic file format consistent with the XML schema listed on the CEDRI website. If the reporting form specific to this subpart is not available in CEDRI at the time that the report is due, you must submit the report to the Administrator at all the appropriate addresses listed in § 63.13. Once the reporting template has been available in CEDRI for 1 year, you must begin submitting all subsequent reports via CEDRI. The reports must be submitted by the deadlines specified in this subpart, regardless of the method in which the reports are submitted.
units.action_summary: Operators must submit notifications and semiannual reports via CEDRI in specified formats, use Administrator addresses if template unavailable, begin CEDRI submissions after template available for 1 year, and meet all reporting deadlines.

units.obligation_text: If you are required to electronically submit a report through CEDRI ... and due to a planned or actual outage ... you may assert a claim of EPA system outage for failure to timely comply with the reporting requirement. You must submit notification to the Administrator in writing as soon as possible following the date you first knew ... You must provide to the Administrator a written description identifying the date, time and length of the outage; a rationale for attributing the delay in reporting beyond the regulatory deadline to the EPA system outage; describe the measures taken or to be taken to minimize the delay in reporting; and identify a date by which you propose to report, or if you have already met the reporting requirement at the time of the notification, the date you reported. In any circumstance, the report must be submitted electronically as soon as possible after the outage is resolved. The decision to accept the claim of EPA system outage and allow an extension to the reporting deadline is solely within the discretion of the Administrator.
units.action_summary: Operators may assert an EPA system outage claim; they must notify the Administrator in writing promptly with details and proposed reporting date; must submit report electronically ASAP after outage resolution; Administrator has sole discretion to accept the claim and extend deadlines.
units.modal_raw: may / must / must / is solely within the discretion

units.obligation_text: If you are required to electronically submit a report through CEDRI ... and a force majeure event is about to occur, occurs, or has occurred ... the owner or operator may assert a claim of force majeure for failure to timely comply with the reporting requirement. ... you must submit notification to the Administrator in writing as soon as possible ... You must provide to the Administrator a written description of the force majeure event and a rationale for attributing the delay in reporting beyond the regulatory deadline to the force majeure event; describe the measures taken or to be taken to minimize the delay in reporting; and identify a date by which you propose to report, or if you have already met the reporting requirement at the time of the notification, the date you reported. In any circumstance, the reporting must occur as soon as possible after the force majeure event occurs. The decision to accept the claim of force majeure and allow an extension to the reporting deadline is solely within the discretion of the Administrator.
units.action_summary: Operators may claim force majeure for late electronic reporting; must notify Administrator promptly with description, rationale, mitigation measures, and proposed report date; must report ASAP after event; Administrator decides whether to accept claim and extend deadline.
units.modal_raw: may / must / is solely within the discretion

units.obligation_text: For the emission rate without add-on controls option, a record of the calculation of the total mass of organic HAP emissions for the coatings, thinners, and cleaning materials used each month, using Equations 1, 1A (or 1A-alt) through 1C, and 2 of § 63.4751; and, if applicable, the calculation used to determine mass of organic HAP in waste materials according to § 63.4751(e)(4); the calculation of the total volume of coating solids used each month, using Equation 2 of § 63.4751; and the calculation of each 12-month organic HAP emission rate, using Equation 3 of § 63.4751.
units.actor: you (owner or operator) using the emission rate without add-on controls option
units.action_summary: Operators must keep monthly and 12-month calculation records for organic HAP mass, coating solids volume, and any waste material HAP mass calculations as specified.

units.obligation_text: If you use the emission rate with add-on controls option, you must keep the records specified in paragraphs (k)(1) through (2) of this section.
units.actor: you (owner or operator) using the emission rate with add-on controls option
units.action_summary: Operators using the emission-rate-with-add-on-controls option must retain the records listed in (k)(1)-(2).

units.obligation_text: For each capture system that is not a PTE, the data and documentation you used to determine capture efficiency according to the requirements specified in §§ 63.4764 and 63.4765(b) through (e), including the records specified in paragraphs (k)(1)(v)(A) through (C) of this section that apply to you.
units.action_summary: For non-PTE capture systems, operators must keep data and documentation used to determine capture efficiency per specified requirements, including applicable records A-C.

units.obligation_text: The records specified in paragraphs (k)(1)(vi)(A) and (B) of this section for each add-on control device organic HAP destruction or removal efficiency determination as specified in § 63.4766.
units.action_summary: Operators must retain records specified in (k)(1)(vi)(A)-(B) for each add-on control device efficiency determination under §63.4766.

units.obligation_text: The records required to show continuous compliance with each operating limit specified in Table 3 to this subpart that applies to you.
units.actor: you (owner or operator) (new/reconstructed after publication and existing after specified date)
units.action_summary: Operators must keep records demonstrating continuous compliance with applicable operating limits in Table 3.

units.obligation_text: For each capture system that is a PTE, the data and documentation you used to support a determination that the capture system meets the criteria in Method 204 of appendix M to 40 CFR part 51 for a PTE and has a capture efficiency of 100 percent, as specified in § 63.4765(a).
units.action_summary: For capture systems designated as PTE, operators must retain data and documentation showing they meet Method 204 criteria and have 100% capture efficiency per §63.4765(a).

units.obligation_text: For each capture system that is not a PTE, the data and documentation you used to determine capture efficiency according to the requirements specified in §§ 63.4764 and 63.4765(b) through (e), including the records specified in paragraphs (k)(2)(iii)(A) through (C) of this section that apply to you.
units.action_summary: For non-PTE capture systems after specified dates, operators must keep data/documentation to determine capture efficiency per §§63.4764 and 63.4765(b)-(e), including applicable records A-C.

units.obligation_text: Records for a liquid-to-uncaptured-gas protocol using a temporary total enclosure or building enclosure. Records of the mass of total volatile hydrocarbon (TVH) as measured by Method 204A or F of appendix M to 40 CFR part 51 for each material used in the coating operation, and the total TVH for all materials used during each capture efficiency test run, including a copy of the test report. Records of the mass of TVH emissions not captured by the capture system that exited the temporary total enclosure or building enclosure during each capture efficiency test run as measured by Method 204D or E of appendix M to 40 CFR part 51, including a copy of the test report. Records documenting that the enclosure used for the capture efficiency test met the criteria in Method 204 of appendix M to 40 CFR part 51 for either a temporary total enclosure or a building enclosure.
units.action_summary: Operators must keep specific test records and documentation for liquid-to-uncaptured-gas capture efficiency tests including TVH measurements, test reports, and enclosure compliance documentation.

units.obligation_text: Records for a gas-to-gas protocol using a temporary total enclosure or a building enclosure. Records of the mass of TVH emissions captured by the emission capture system as measured by Method 204B or C ... including a copy of the test report. Records of the mass of TVH emissions not captured ... as measured by Method 204D or E ... including a copy of the test report. Records documenting that the enclosure used ... met the criteria in Method 204 ...
units.action_summary: Operators must retain records for gas-to-gas capture efficiency tests including inlet and escaped TVH measurements, test reports, and enclosure compliance documentation.

units.obligation_text: Records for an alternative protocol. Records needed to document a capture efficiency determination using an alternative method or protocol as specified in § 63.4765(e), if applicable.
units.action_summary: Operators using alternative capture-efficiency protocols must keep records documenting the alternative method per §63.4765(e).

units.obligation_text: Records of each add-on control device performance test conducted according to §§ 63.4764 and 63.4766.
units.action_summary: Operators must retain records of add-on control device performance tests conducted under §§63.4764 and 63.4766.

units.obligation_text: Records of the coating operation conditions during the add-on control device performance test showing that the performance test was conducted under representative operating conditions.
units.action_summary: Operators must keep records demonstrating that performance tests were conducted under representative coating operation conditions.

units.obligation_text: Records of the data and calculations you used to establish the emission capture and add-on control device operating limits as specified in § 63.4767 and to document compliance with the operating limits as specified in Table 3 to this subpart.
units.action_summary: Operators must retain data and calculations used to set operating limits and to document compliance with Table 3 operating limits.

units.obligation_text: A record of the work practice plan required by § 63.4693, and documentation that you are implementing the plan on a continuous basis.
units.action_summary: Operators must keep the work practice plan required by §63.4693 and documentation showing continuous implementation.

units.obligation_text: Method 24 (appendix A–7 to 40 CFR part 60). For coatings, you may use Method 24 to determine the mass fraction of nonaqueous volatile matter and use that value as a substitute for mass fraction of organic HAP. One of the voluntary consensus standards in paragraphs (a)(2)(i) through (v) may be used as an alternative to using Method 24.
units.action_summary: Operators may use Method 24 to determine nonaqueous volatile matter as a substitute for organic HAP mass fraction, or may use one of the listed voluntary consensus standards as an alternative.

units.obligation_text: ASTM Methods listed in (i) through (v) may be used as alternatives to Method 24 for determining mass fraction of nonaqueous volatile matter.
units.action_summary: Operators may use the specified ASTM methods as alternatives to Method 24 for coatings testing.

units.obligation_text: If there is disagreement between ASTM Method D1475–90 test results and other information sources, the test results will take precedence.
units.action_summary: When density information conflicts, ASTM D1475–90 test results override other information sources.

units.obligation_text: Determine the density of each coating. Determine the density of each coating used during the compliance period from test results using ASTM Method D1475–90 ... or information from the supplier or manufacturer of the material.
