If there is disagreement between ASTM Method D1475–90 test results and the supplier’s or manufacturer’s information, the test results will take precedence.
units.action_summary: Operators must determine each coating's density using ASTM D1475–90 test results or supplier data; test results override supplier info if they disagree.

units.obligation_text: Determine the density of each coating, thinner, and cleaning material used during each month from test results using ASTM Method D1475–90 ... or information from the supplier or manufacturer of the material. If there is disagreement between ASTM Method D1475–90 test results and such other information sources, the test results will take precedence.
units.action_summary: Operators must determine monthly densities for coatings, thinners, and cleaning materials using ASTM D1475–90 or supplier info; test results take precedence if conflict exists.

units.obligation_text: As an alternative to paragraph (h) of this section, you may demonstrate initial compliance by conducting a performance test using Method 25A of appendix A–7 to 40 CFR part 60 or Method 320 or 326 of appendix A to 40 CFR part 63 for formaldehyde or isocyanates respectively to obtain an organic HAP emission factor (EF).
units.action_summary: Operators may alternatively demonstrate initial compliance by conducting specified performance tests to obtain an organic HAP emission factor.

units.obligation_text: You must also calculate the mass of organic HAP emitted from the coatings used during the month using Equation 1A-alt of this section.
units.actor: you (owner or operator) using alternative compliance demonstration
units.action_summary: If using alternative compliance, operators must calculate monthly mass of organic HAP emitted using Equation 1A-alt.

units.obligation_text: Calculate the organic HAP emission rate for the 12-month compliance period, grams organic HAP per liter coating solids used, using Equation 3 of this section.
units.action_summary: Operators must calculate the 12-month organic HAP emission rate using Equation 3.

units.obligation_text: The organic HAP emission rate for the initial 12-month compliance period, calculated using Equation 3 of this section, must be less than or equal to the applicable emission limit in § 63.4690. You must keep all records as required by §§ 63.4730 and 63.4731. As part of the Notification of Compliance Status required by § 63.4710, you must identify the coating operation(s) for which you used the emission rate without add-on controls option and submit a statement that the coating operation(s) was (were) in compliance with the emission limitations during the initial compliance period because the organic HAP emission rate was less than or equal to the applicable emission limit in § 63.4690, determined according to this section.
units.action_summary: The calculated 12-month emission rate must meet the §63.4690 limit; operators must retain required records and include identification and compliance statement in the Notification of Compliance Status.

units.obligation_text: Test plan preparation and implementation in the Annexes to ASTM D6348–03, sections A1 through A8 are mandatory.
units.actor: you (owner or operator) performing ASTM D6348–03 testing
units.action_summary: Operators using ASTM D6348–03 must prepare and implement test plans in Annexes A1-A8.

units.obligation_text: In ASTM D6348–03 Annex A5 (Analyte Spiking Technique), the percent (%) R must be determined for each target analyte (Equation A5.5 of ASTM D6348–03). In order for the test data to be acceptable for a compound, %R must be between 70 and 130 percent. If the %R value does not meet this criterion for a target compound, the test data are not acceptable for that compound, and the test must be repeated for that analyte following adjustment of the sampling and/or analytical procedure before the retest. The %R value for each compound must be reported in the test report, and all field measurements must be corrected with the calculated %R value for that compound using the following equation: Reported Result = (Measured Concentration in the Stack × 100)/%R.
units.actor: you (owner or operator) using ASTM D6348–03
units.action_summary: Operators must determine %R for each analyte, ensure %R between 70-130% or repeat the test, report %R in test report, and correct field measurements using the specified equation.
units.modal_raw: must / must be / must be reported

units.obligation_text: For purposes of evaluating attainment pollutants, the source was capable of accommodating before January 6, 1975, unless such change would be prohibited under any federally enforceable permit condition which was established after January 6, 1975 pursuant to 40 CFR 52.21 or under regulations approved pursuant to subpart I of this part;

units.obligation_text: For purposes of evaluating nonattainment pollutants, the source was capable of accommodating before December 21, 1976, unless such change would be prohibited under any federally enforceable permit condition which was established after December 21, 1976 pursuant to 40 CFR 52.21 or under regulations approved pursuant to subpart I of this part;

units.obligation_text: Emissions increase test. For each regulated NSR pollutant for which you have hourly average CEMS or PEMS emissions data with corresponding fuel heat input data, compare the pre-change maximum actual hourly emissions rate in pounds per hour (lb/hr) to a projection of the post-change maximum actual hourly emissions rate in lb/hr, subject to the provisions in paragraphs (f)(1)(i) through (iii) of this section.
units.action_summary: Using hourly CEMS or PEMS data with heat input, you must compare pre-change maximum actual hourly emissions to projected post-change maximum actual hourly emissions.

units.obligation_text: Select a period of 365 consecutive days within the 5-year period immediately preceding when you begin actual construction of the physical or operational change. Compile a data set (for example, in a spreadsheet) with the hourly average CEMS or PEMS (as applicable) measured emissions rates and corresponding heat input data for all of the hours of operation for that 365-day period for the pollutant of interest.
units.action_summary: Select a 365-day period within the prior 5 years and compile hourly emissions and heat input data for that period.

units.obligation_text: Delete any unacceptable hourly data from this 365-day period in accordance with the data limitations in paragraph (f)(2) of this section.

units.obligation_text: Extract the hourly data for the 10 percent of the remaining data set corresponding to the highest heat input rates for the selected period.
units.action_summary: From remaining data, extract the top 10% of hours by heat input.

units.obligation_text: Calculate the average emissions rate from the extracted (i.e., highest 10 percent heat input rates) data set, using Equation 1.
units.action_summary: Compute the average emissions rate from the extracted top 10% heat-input hourly data using the specified equation.

units.obligation_text: Calculate the standard deviation of the data set using Equation 2.
units.action_summary: Compute the data set's standard deviation using the specified equation.

units.obligation_text: Calculate the Upper Tolerance Limit of the data set using Equation 3.
units.action_summary: Compute the Upper Tolerance Limit (UTL) for the data set using the specified equation.

units.obligation_text: Use the UTL calculated in paragraph (f)(1)(i)(F) of this section as the pre-change maximum actual hourly emissions rate.
units.action_summary: Adopt the calculated UTL as the pre-change maximum actual hourly emission rate.

units.obligation_text: Regardless of any preconstruction projections, an emissions increase has occurred if the hourly emissions rate actually achieved in the 5 years after the change exceeds the pre-change maximum actual hourly emissions rate.
units.action_summary: If actual hourly emissions in the 5 years post-change exceed the pre-change maximum actual hourly rate, an emissions increase has occurred irrespective of projections.

units.obligation_text: Emissions increase test. units.obligation_text: You must determine the highest pre-change hourly emissions rate for each regulated NSR pollutant using the best data available to you. units.obligation_text: Regardless of any preconstruction projections, an emissions increase has occurred if the hourly emissions rate actually achieved in the 5 years after the change exceeds the pre-change maximum actual hourly emissions rate.

title: Environmental Protection Agency Acquisition Regulation; Scientific Integrity

units.obligation_text: Contracting Officers shall insert the contract clause at 1552.203–72—Scientific Integrity, in solicitations and contracts when the Contractor may be required to perform, communicate, or supervise scientific activities, or use scientific information to perform advisory and assistance services.
units.action_summary: Insert the Scientific Integrity contract clause (1552.203–72) into solicitations and contracts when contractor work may involve scientific activities or information.

units.obligation_text: When performing, communicating, supervising, or utilizing scientific activities or scientific information, the Contractor shall adhere to EPA’s Scientific Integrity Policy.
units.action_summary: Follow EPA's Scientific Integrity Policy when conducting or using scientific activities or information under the contract.

units.obligation_text: Prior to beginning performance under this contract, the Contractor shall ensure that all personnel within their organization, including subcontractors and consultants, that perform, communicate, or supervise scientific activities, or use scientific information to perform advisory and assistance services under this contract, have read and understand their compliance responsibilities with EPA’s Scientific Integrity Policy.
units.action_summary: Before starting work, ensure all personnel (including subcontractors/consultants) who will perform/scientific tasks have read and understand compliance responsibilities under EPA's Scientific Integrity Policy.

units.obligation_text: Consistent with the objective of promoting a culture of scientific integrity and transparency, as discussed in EPA’s Scientific Integrity Policy, the Contractor agrees to:
units.action_summary: Commit to a set of practices promoting scientific integrity and transparency described in the following sub-items.

units.obligation_text: Produce scientific products of the highest quality, rigor, and objectivity, by adhering to applicable EPA information quality policy, quality assurance policy, and peer review policy;
units.action_summary: Produce high-quality, rigorous, objective scientific products by following applicable EPA information quality, quality assurance, and peer review policies.

units.obligation_text: Prohibit the suppression, alteration, or otherwise impede the timely release of scientific findings or conclusions;
units.action_summary: Prevent suppression, alteration, or other actions that would impede timely release of scientific findings or conclusions.

units.obligation_text: Adhere to the Peer Review Handbook, current edition, for the peer review of scientific and technical work products generated through this contract;
units.action_summary: Follow the current Peer Review Handbook for peer review of scientific/technical work products under the contract.

units.obligation_text: Act honestly and refrain from acts of research misconduct, including publication or reporting, as described in EPA Order 3120.5 Policy and Procedures for Addressing Research Misconduct.
units.action_summary: Behave honestly and avoid research misconduct as defined in EPA Order 3120.5 (misconduct excludes honest error or differences of opinion).

units.obligation_text: Require that reviews of the content of a scientific product be based only on scientific quality considerations, e.g., the methods used are clear and appropriate, the presentation of results and conclusions is impartial;
units.action_summary: Ensure content reviews focus solely on scientific quality considerations (methods, impartial presentation of results/conclusions).

units.obligation_text: Ensure scientific findings are generated and disseminated in a timely and transparent manner, including scientific research performed by subcontractors and consultants who assist with developing or applying the results of scientific activities;
units.action_summary: Make sure scientific findings (including those from subcontractors/consultants) are generated and shared promptly and transparently.

units.obligation_text: Include an explication of underlying assumptions, accurate contextualization of uncertainties, and a description of the probabilities associated with both optimistic and pessimistic projections when communicating scientific findings, if applicable;
units.action_summary: When communicating findings (if applicable), explain assumptions, contextualize uncertainties, and describe probabilities of optimistic/pessimistic projections.

units.obligation_text: Document the use of independent validation of scientific methods;
units.action_summary: Record and document any use of independent validation for scientific methods.

units.obligation_text: Document any independent review of the Contractor’s scientific facilities and testing activities, as occurs with accreditation by a nationally or internationally recognized sanctioning body;
units.action_summary: Document independent reviews of scientific facilities and testing activities (e.g., accreditation reviews).

units.obligation_text: Make scientific information available online in open formats in a timely manner, including access to data and non-proprietary models.
units.action_summary: Provide scientific information online in open formats promptly, including access to data and non-proprietary models.

units.obligation_text: To assure protection of staff supported by this contract, consistent with the objectives described in the Scientific Integrity Policy, the Contractor agrees to:
units.action_summary: Commit to measures protecting staff under the contract, as detailed in the following sub-items.

units.obligation_text: Prohibit intimidation or coercion of scientists to alter scientific data, findings, or professional opinions or non-scientific influence of scientific advisory boards.
units.action_summary: Prevent intimidation or coercion aimed at altering scientific data, findings, opinions, or exerting non-scientific influence on advisory boards.

units.obligation_text: Employees, subcontractors, and consultants, including scientists, managers, and other leadership, shall not knowingly misrepresent, exaggerate, or downplay areas of scientific uncertainty;
units.actor: employees, subcontractors, and consultants (including scientists, managers, and leadership)
units.action_summary: Prohibit contractor employees/subcontractors/consultants and leadership from knowingly misrepresenting, exaggerating, or downplaying scientific uncertainty.

units.obligation_text: Prohibit retaliation or other punitive actions toward employees who uncover or report allegations of scientific and research misconduct, or who express a differing scientific opinion.
units.action_summary: Prevent retaliation or punitive actions against employees who report misconduct or express differing scientific opinions.

units.obligation_text: Employees who have allegedly engaged in scientific or research misconduct shall be afforded the due process protections provided by law, regulation, and applicable collective bargaining agreements, prior to any action.
units.action_summary: Ensure that employees accused of misconduct receive the due process protections required by law, regulation, and applicable collective bargaining agreements before any action.

units.obligation_text: The Contractor shall ensure that all employees, subcontractors, and consultants shall be familiar with these protections and avoid the appearance of retaliatory actions.
units.action_summary: Ensure all employees, subcontractors, and consultants know about due process protections and avoid actions that appear retaliatory.

units.obligation_text: If during performance of this contract the Contractor becomes aware of an actual or potential loss of scientific integrity, the Contractor shall immediately inform the Contracting Officer and Contracting Officer’s Representative with a description of the issue and any corrective action the contractor will take to mitigate the issue.
units.action_summary: Immediately notify the Contracting Officer and COR of any actual or potential loss of scientific integrity, describing the issue and corrective actions to mitigate it.

units.obligation_text: The Contracting Officer and Contracting Officer’s Representative will consult with the Agency’s Scientific Integrity Official on all issues related to the loss of scientific integrity under this contract.
units.actor: Contracting Officer and Contracting Officer’s Representative
units.action_summary: Consult with the Agency's Scientific Integrity Official on all contract issues related to loss of scientific integrity.

units.obligation_text: The Agency’s Scientific Integrity Official will advise the Contracting Officer and Contracting Officer’s Representative on the appropriate remedy for any actual or potential loss of scientific integrity.
units.action_summary: Advise the Contracting Officer and COR on appropriate remedies for actual or potential losses of scientific integrity.

units.obligation_text: The Contractor bears the primary responsibility for prevention and detection of research misconduct and for the inquiry, investigation, and adjudication of research misconduct alleged to have occurred in association with its own institution.
units.action_summary: Hold primary responsibility for preventing, detecting, and handling inquiries/investigations/adjudication of research misconduct associated with its institution.

units.obligation_text: The Contractor shall take the actions required as described in EPA Order 3120.5 Policy and Procedures for Addressing Research Misconduct when research misconduct is suspected or found.
units.action_summary: Follow the actions and procedures in EPA Order 3120.5 when research misconduct is suspected or found.

units.obligation_text: The Contracting Officer will make the final decision on any remedy to an actual or potential loss of scientific integrity.
units.action_summary: The Contracting Officer has final decision authority on remedies for actual or potential losses of scientific integrity.

units.obligation_text: Acceptance of the Contractor’s proposed mitigation plan to the scientific integrity issue;
units.action_summary: Accept the contractor's proposed mitigation plan as a remedy.

units.obligation_text: Acceptance of an alternate mitigation plan negotiated by the parties;
units.action_summary: Accept an alternate mitigation plan negotiated between the parties.

units.obligation_text: Termination for convenience, in whole or in part, if no mitigation plan will adequately resolve the actual or potential loss of scientific integrity;
units.action_summary: Terminate the contract for convenience (whole or in part) if no mitigation plan can adequately resolve the integrity issue.

units.obligation_text: Termination for default or cause, in whole or in part, if the Contractor was aware of an actual or potential loss of scientific integrity under this contract and did not disclose it or misrepresented relevant information to the Contracting Officer.
units.action_summary: Terminate the contract for default or cause (whole or in part) if the contractor knew of a loss of scientific integrity and failed to disclose it or misrepresented information.

units.obligation_text: Additionally, the Government may debar the Contractor from Government contracting, or pursue other remedies as may be permitted by law or this contract.
units.action_summary: The Government may debar the contractor or pursue other legal or contractual remedies.

units.obligation_text: The Contractor agrees to insert in any subcontract or consultant agreement placed hereunder which shall conform substantially to the language of this clause, including this paragraph (g), unless otherwise authorized by the Contracting Officer.
units.action_summary: Insert a subcontract clause substantially conforming to this Scientific Integrity clause into subcontracts/consultant agreements, unless authorized otherwise by the Contracting Officer.

units.obligation_text: unless otherwise authorized by the Contracting Officer.
units.action_summary: Exception allowing subcontracts to deviate from substantially conforming clause if Contracting Officer authorizes.

title: Accidental Release Prevention Requirements: Risk Management Programs Under the Clean Air Act

units.obligation_text: By [DATE 1 YEAR AFTER THE EFFECTIVE DATE OF THE FINAL RULE], the owner or operator of a stationary source shall comply with the emergency response coordination activities in § 68.93.
units.actor: the owner or operator of a stationary source
units.action_summary: Comply with the emergency response coordination activities in § 68.93 by the specified date.

units.obligation_text: By [DATE 4 YEARS AFTER THE EFFECTIVE DATE OF THE FINAL RULE], the owner or operator shall have developed plans for conducting emergency response exercises in accordance with provisions of § 68.96.
units.action_summary: Develop plans for conducting emergency response exercises per § 68.96 by the specified date.

units.obligation_text: After [DATE 2 YEARS AFTER THE EFFECTIVE DATE OF THE FINAL RULE] the owner or operator of a stationary source shall comply with the public meeting requirement in § 68.210(b) for any accident meeting the five-year accident history requirements of § 68.42 that occurs after [DATE 2 YEARS AFTER THE EFFECTIVE DATE OF THE FINAL RULE].
units.actor: the owner or operator of a stationary source
units.action_summary: Comply with the public meeting requirement in § 68.210(b) for qualifying accidents occurring after the specified date.

units.obligation_text: By [DATE 5 YEARS AFTER THE EFFECTIVE DATE OF THE FINAL RULE], the owner or operator shall comply with § 68.160 (b)(21) of the risk management plan provisions of subpart G of this part promulgated on [PUBLICATION DATE OF FINAL RULE] and with § 68.180 of the risk management plan provisions of subpart G of this part promulgated on January 13, 2017.
units.action_summary: Comply with specified RMP provisions (§ 68.160(b)(21) and § 68.180) by the specified date.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator shall ensure that each employee presently operating a process, and each employee newly assigned to a covered process have been trained or tested competent in the operating procedures provided in § 68.52 that pertain to their duties.
units.action_summary: Ensure current and newly assigned process employees are trained or tested competent in applicable operating procedures.

units.obligation_text: Refresher training shall be provided at least every three years, and more often if necessary, to each employee operating a process to ensure that the employee understands and adheres to the current operating procedures of the process.
units.action_summary: Provide refresher training to each process operator at least every three years, or more often if necessary.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator shall ensure that operators are trained in any updated or new procedures prior to startup of a process after a major change.
units.action_summary: Ensure operators receive training on updated/new procedures before startup after a major change.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator shall certify that they have evaluated compliance with the provisions of this subpart at least every three years to verify that the procedures and practices developed under this subpart are adequate and are being followed.
units.action_summary: Certify that compliance evaluations of the subpart were conducted at least every three years and that procedures/practices are adequate and followed.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator shall investigate each incident which resulted in, or could reasonably have resulted in a catastrophic release.
units.action_summary: Investigate each incident that resulted in, or could have reasonably resulted in, a catastrophic release.

units.obligation_text: A summary shall be prepared at the conclusion of the investigation which includes at a minimum:
units.actor: the owner or operator (or investigation preparer)
units.action_summary: Prepare a summary at the conclusion of the investigation that includes specified minimum content.

units.obligation_text: Date of incident;
units.actor: the owner or operator (preparer of the investigation summary)
units.action_summary: Include the date of the incident in the investigation summary.

units.obligation_text: A description of the incident;
units.actor: the owner or operator (preparer of the investigation summary)
units.action_summary: Include a description of the incident in the investigation summary.

units.obligation_text: The factors that contributed to the incident;
units.actor: the owner or operator (preparer of the investigation summary)
units.action_summary: Include contributing factors to the incident in the investigation summary.

units.obligation_text: Any recommendations resulting from the investigation.
units.actor: the owner or operator (preparer of the investigation summary)
units.action_summary: Include any recommendations resulting from the investigation in the summary.

units.obligation_text: Investigation summaries shall be retained for five years.
units.action_summary: Retain investigation summaries for five years.

units.obligation_text: In accordance with the schedule set forth in § 68.67, the owner or operator shall complete a compilation of written process safety information before conducting any process hazard analysis required by the rule.
units.action_summary: Complete written process safety information, per schedule, before conducting any required process hazard analysis.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator shall certify that they have evaluated compliance with the provisions of this subpart at least every three years to verify that procedures and practices developed under this subpart are adequate and are being followed.
units.action_summary: Certify that compliance evaluations of the subpart were conducted at least every three years and that procedures/practices are adequate and followed.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator shall investigate each incident which resulted in, or could reasonably have resulted in a catastrophic release.
units.action_summary: Investigate each incident that resulted in, or could have reasonably resulted in, a catastrophic release.

units.obligation_text: A report shall be prepared at the conclusion of the investigation which includes at a minimum:
units.actor: the owner or operator (preparer of the investigation report)
units.action_summary: Prepare a report at the conclusion of the investigation that includes specified minimum content.

units.obligation_text: Date of incident;
units.action_summary: Include the date of the incident in the investigation report.

units.obligation_text: Date investigation began;
units.action_summary: Include the date the investigation began in the report.

units.obligation_text: A description of the incident;
units.action_summary: Include a description of the incident in the report.

units.obligation_text: The factors that contributed to the incident;
units.action_summary: Include factors that contributed to the incident in the report.

units.obligation_text: Any recommendations resulting from the investigation.
units.action_summary: Include any recommendations resulting from the investigation in the report.

units.obligation_text: Coordination shall include providing to the local emergency planning and response organizations: The stationary source’s emergency response plan if one exists; emergency action plan; and updated emergency contact information.
units.actor: the owner or operator (responsible for coordination)
units.action_summary: Provide the local emergency planning and response organizations with the source's emergency response plan (if one exists), emergency action plan, and updated emergency contact information as part of coordination.

units.obligation_text: The stationary source’s emergency response plan if one exists;
units.action_summary: Provide the stationary source's emergency response plan (if one exists) to local emergency planning and response organizations.

units.obligation_text: Emergency action plan;
units.action_summary: Provide the emergency action plan to local emergency planning and response organizations.

units.obligation_text: Updated emergency contact information.
units.action_summary: Provide updated emergency contact information to local emergency planning and response organizations.

units.obligation_text: For responding stationary sources, coordination shall also include consulting with local emergency response officials to establish appropriate schedules and plans for field and tabletop exercises required under § 68.96(b).
units.actor: the owner or operator of responding stationary sources
units.action_summary: Consult with local emergency response officials to establish schedules and plans for field and tabletop exercises required under § 68.96(b).

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator shall request an opportunity to meet with the local emergency planning committee (or equivalent) and/or local fire department as appropriate to review and discuss those materials.
units.action_summary: Request an opportunity to meet with local emergency planning committee and/or local fire department to review and discuss emergency materials.

units.obligation_text: The disclosure of information classified by the Department of Defense or other Federal agencies or contractors of such agencies shall be controlled by applicable laws, regulations, or executive orders concerning the release of classified information.
units.actor: persons or entities disclosing classified information
units.action_summary: Ensure disclosure of classified information is controlled by applicable laws, regulations, or executive orders.

units.obligation_text: An owner or operator asserting CBI for information required under this section shall provide a sanitized version to the local emergency planning and response organizations.
units.actor: an owner or operator asserting CBI
units.action_summary: Provide a sanitized version of information claimed as CBI to local emergency planning and response organizations.

units.obligation_text: Assertion of claims of CBI and substantiation of CBI claims shall be in the same manner as required in §§ 68.151 and 68.152 for information contained in the RMP required under subpart G.
units.actor: an owner or operator asserting CBI
units.action_summary: Assert and substantiate CBI claims in the same manner required by §§ 68.151 and 68.152 for RMP information.

units.obligation_text: As provided under § 68.151(b)(3), an owner or operator of a stationary source may not claim five-year accident history information as CBI.

units.action_summary: May not claim five-year accident history information as CBI.

units.obligation_text: As provided in § 68.151(c)(2), an owner or operator of a stationary source asserting that a chemical name is CBI shall provide a generic category or class name as a substitute.

units.action_summary: Provide a generic category or class name when asserting a chemical name is CBI.

units.obligation_text: At least once each calendar year, the owner or operator of a stationary source with any Program 2 or Program 3 process shall conduct an exercise of the source’s emergency response notification mechanisms required under § 68.90(b)(3) or § 68.95(a)(1)(i), as appropriate, before [DATE 5 YEARS AFTER EFFECTIVE DATE OF FINAL RULE] and annually thereafter.
units.actor: the owner or operator of a stationary source with any Program 2 or Program 3 process
units.action_summary: Conduct an exercise of emergency response notification mechanisms at least annually (and before specified date), for Program 2 or 3 processes.

units.obligation_text: As part of coordination with local emergency response officials required by § 68.93, the owner or operator shall consult with these officials to establish an appropriate frequency for field exercises.
units.action_summary: Consult with local emergency response officials to establish appropriate frequency for field exercises.

units.obligation_text: Field exercises should include: Tests of procedures to notify the public and the appropriate Federal, state, and local emergency response agencies about an accidental release; tests of procedures and measures for emergency response actions including evacuations and medical treatment; tests of communications systems; mobilization of facility emergency response personnel, including contractors, as appropriate; coordination with local emergency responders; emergency response equipment deployment; and any other action identified in the emergency response program, as appropriate.
units.actor: the owner or operator (organizing field exercises)
units.action_summary: Field exercises are expected to include specified tests and activities related to notification, response actions, communications, personnel mobilization, coordination, equipment deployment, and other identified actions.

units.obligation_text: Tests of procedures to notify the public and the appropriate Federal, state, and local emergency response agencies about an accidental release;

units.section: I.D How are sites listed on the NPL? (mechanism 1)
units.obligation_text: A site may be included on the NPL if it scores sufficiently high on the HRS, which the EPA promulgated as appendix A of the NCP (40 CFR part 300).
units.action_summary: Sites that score high enough on the Hazard Ranking System may be listed on the NPL.

units.section: I.D How are sites listed on the NPL? (policy threshold)
units.obligation_text: As a matter of agency policy, those sites that score 28.50 or greater on the HRS are eligible for the NPL.
units.action_summary: Sites scoring 28.50 or above on the HRS are eligible for NPL listing.

units.section: I.D How are sites listed on the NPL? (mechanism 2)
units.obligation_text: Pursuant to 42 U.S.C. 9605(a)(8)(B), each state may designate a single site as its top priority to be listed on the NPL, without any HRS score.
units.action_summary: Each state may select one site as its top priority for NPL listing without an HRS score.

units.section: I.D How are sites listed on the NPL? (mechanism 3) (parent)
units.obligation_text: The third mechanism for listing, included in the NCP at 40 CFR 300.425(c)(3), allows certain sites to be listed without any HRS score, if all of the following conditions are met:
units.action_summary: EPA may list certain sites without an HRS score if specified conditions are satisfied.

units.section: I.D How are sites listed on the NPL? (mechanism 3) (condition i)
units.obligation_text: The Agency for Toxic Substances and Disease Registry (ATSDR) of the U.S. Public Health Service has issued a health advisory that recommends dissociation of individuals from the release.
units.action_summary: A qualifying condition is that ATSDR has issued a health advisory recommending dissociation from the release.

units.section: I.D How are sites listed on the NPL? (mechanism 3) (condition ii)
units.obligation_text: The EPA determines that the release poses a significant threat to public health.
units.action_summary: A qualifying condition is EPA's determination that the release poses a significant public health threat.

units.section: I.D How are sites listed on the NPL? (mechanism 3) (condition iii)
units.obligation_text: The EPA anticipates that it will be more cost-effective to use its remedial authority than to use its removal authority to respond to the release.
units.action_summary: A qualifying condition is EPA's anticipation that remedial authority will be more cost-effective than removal authority.

units.section: I.E What happens to sites on the NPL?
units.obligation_text: A site may undergo remedial action financed by the Trust Fund established under CERCLA only after it is placed on the NPL, as provided in the NCP at 40 CFR 300.425(b)(1).
units.action_summary: Remedial actions financed by the Trust Fund may be taken at a site only after the site is placed on the NPL.

units.section: I.E What happens to sites on the NPL?
units.obligation_text: The EPA may pursue other appropriate authorities to respond to the releases, including enforcement action under CERCLA and other laws.
units.action_summary: EPA may use other authorities, including enforcement under CERCLA, to respond to releases.

units.action_summary: EPA has the authority to delete sites from the NPL when no further Superfund response is appropriate.

units.section: I.G How are sites removed from the NPL? (parent)
units.obligation_text: This section also provides that the EPA shall consult with states on proposed deletions and shall consider whether any of the following criteria have been met:
units.action_summary: EPA is required to consult with states on proposed deletions and consider whether listed criteria are met.

units.section: I.G How are sites removed from the NPL? (criterion i)
units.obligation_text: Responsible parties or other persons have implemented all appropriate response actions required;
units.action_summary: One criterion for deletion is that responsible parties or others have implemented all required appropriate response actions.

units.section: I.G How are sites removed from the NPL? (criterion ii)
units.obligation_text: All appropriate Superfund-financed response has been implemented and no further response action is required;
units.action_summary: Another deletion criterion is that all Superfund-financed responses are complete and no further response is required.

units.section: I.G How are sites removed from the NPL? (criterion iii)
units.obligation_text: The remedial investigation has shown the release poses no significant threat to public health or the environment, and taking of remedial measures is not appropriate.
units.action_summary: A deletion criterion is that RI shows no significant threat and remedial measures are inappropriate.

units.section: I.I What is the Construction Completion List (CCL)? (parent)
units.obligation_text: Sites qualify for the CCL when: (1) Any necessary physical construction is complete, whether or not final cleanup levels or other requirements have been achieved; (2) the EPA has determined that the response action should be limited to measures that do not involve construction (e.g., institutional controls); or (3) the site qualifies for deletion from the NPL.
units.action_summary: Sites become eligible for the CCL when any of three listed conditions are satisfied.

units.section: I.I What is the Construction Completion List (CCL)? (condition 1)
units.obligation_text: Any necessary physical construction is complete, whether or not final cleanup levels or other requirements have been achieved;
units.action_summary: Condition for CCL: necessary physical construction is complete.

units.section: I.I What is the Construction Completion List (CCL)? (condition 2)
units.obligation_text: The EPA has determined that the response action should be limited to measures that do not involve construction (e.g., institutional controls);
units.action_summary: Condition for CCL: EPA determines that response action will be non-construction measures.

units.section: I.I What is the Construction Completion List (CCL)? (condition 3)

ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION AGENCY

40 CFR Part 721

[EPA-HQ-OPPT-2017-0414; FRL-9981-82]
RIN 2070-AB27

Significant New Use Rules on Certain Chemical Substances

AGENCY: Environmental Protection Agency (EPA).

ACTION: Proposed rule.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------

SUMMARY: EPA is proposing significant new use rules (SNURs) under the 
Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA) for 27 chemical substances which 
were the subject of premanufacture notices (PMNs). The chemical 
substances are subject to Orders issued by EPA pursuant to section 5(e) 
of TSCA. This action would require persons who intend to manufacture 
(defined by statute to include import) or process any of these 27 
chemical substances for an activity that is designated as a significant 
new use by these rules to notify EPA at least 90 days before commencing 
that activity. The required notification initiates EPA's evaluation of 
the intended use within the applicable review period. Persons may not 
commence manufacture or processing for the significant new use until 
EPA has conducted a review of the notice, made an appropriate 
determination on the notification, and has taken such actions as are 
required with that determination. In addition to this notice of 
proposed rulemaking, EPA is issuing the action as a direct final rule 
elsewhere in this issue of the Federal Register.

DATES: Comments must be received on or before September 17, 2018.

ADDRESSES: Submit your comments, identified by docket identification 
(ID) number EPA-HQ-OPPT-2017-0414, by one of the following methods:
    
 Federal eRulemaking Portal: 
http://www.regulations.gov
. 
Follow the online instructions for submitting comments. Do not submit 
electronically any information you consider to be Confidential Business 
Information (CBI) or other information whose disclosure is restricted 
by statute.
    
 Mail: Document Control Office (7407M), Office of Pollution 
Prevention and Toxics (OPPT), Environmental Protection Agency, 1200 
Pennsylvania Ave. NW, Washington, DC 20460-0001.
    
 Hand Delivery: To make special arrangements for hand 
delivery or delivery of boxed information, please follow the 
instructions at 
http://www.epa.gov/dockets/contacts.html
.
    Additional instructions on commenting or visiting the docket, along 
with more information about dockets generally, is available at 
http://www.epa.gov/dockets
.

FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:
    For technical information contact: Kenneth Moss, Chemical Control 
Division (7405M), Office of Pollution Prevention and Toxics, 
Environmental Protection Agency, 1200 Pennsylvania Ave. NW, Washington, 
DC 20460-0001; telephone number: (202) 564-9232; email address: 

[email protected]
.
    For general information contact: The TSCA-Hotline, ABVI-Goodwill, 
422 South Clinton Ave., Rochester, NY 14620; telephone number: (202) 
554-1404; email address: 
[email protected]
.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: In addition to this Notice of Proposed 
Rulemaking, EPA is issuing the action as a direct final rule elsewhere 
in this issue of the Federal Register. For further information about 
the proposed significant new use rules, please see the information 
provided in the direct final action, with the same title, that is 
located in the ``Rules and Regulations'' section of this issue of the 
Federal Register.

List of Subjects in 40 CFR Part 721

    Environmental protection, Chemicals, Hazardous substances, 
Reporting and recordkeeping requirements.

title: Technical Issues-Formaldehyde Emission Standards for Composite Wood Products

units.obligation_text: Beginning June 1, 2018, all manufacturers (including importers), fabricators, suppliers, distributors, and retailers of composite wood products, and component parts or finished goods containing these materials, must comply with this part, subject to the following:
units.actor: all manufacturers (including importers), fabricators, suppliers, distributors, and retailers of composite wood products and component parts or finished goods containing these materials
units.action_summary: Must comply with the requirements of this part beginning June 1, 2018.

units.obligation_text: Beginning June 1, 2018, laminated product producers must comply with the requirements of this part that are applicable to fabricators.
units.action_summary: Laminated product producers must follow the requirements applicable to fabricators beginning June 1, 2018.

units.obligation_text: Composite wood products manufactured (including imported) before June 1, 2018 may be sold, supplied, offered for sale, or used to fabricate component parts or finished goods at any time.
units.actor: any person (sellers, suppliers, distributors, retailers, or users of pre-June 1, 2018 composite wood products)
units.action_summary: Products manufactured before June 1, 2018 may be sold, supplied, offered for sale, or used to fabricate component parts or finished goods at any time.

units.obligation_text: The TPC must notify a panel producer exceeding its established QCL for three consecutive quality control tests within 72 hours of the time that the TPC becomes aware of the third exceedance.
units.action_summary: TPC must notify the panel producer within 72 hours after learning of a third consecutive QCL exceedance.

units.obligation_text: The notice must include the product type, dates of the quality control tests that exceeded the QCL, quality control test results, ASTM E1333–14 or ASTM D6007–14 correlative equivalent values in accordance with § 770.20(d), the established QCL value(s) and the quality control method used.
units.action_summary: Notification must contain the product type, dates, test results, correlative values, established QCL values, and the quality control method used.

units.obligation_text: Except as otherwise provided in this part, the emission standards in this section apply to composite wood products sold, supplied, offered for sale, or manufactured (including imported) on or after June 1, 2018 in the United States. These emission standards apply regardless of whether the composite wood product is in the form of a panel, a component part, or incorporated into a finished good.
units.actor: composite wood products sold, supplied, offered for sale, or manufactured (including imported) on or after June 1, 2018 (and their sellers/manufacturers)
units.action_summary: The emission standards in this section govern composite wood products sold, supplied, offered for sale, or manufactured on or after June 1, 2018, in any form.

units.obligation_text: The sale of stockpiled inventory of composite wood products, whether in the form of panels or incorporated into component parts or finished goods, is prohibited after June 1, 2018.
units.action_summary: Sale of stockpiled inventory of composite wood products is prohibited after June 1, 2018.

units.obligation_text: Beginning June 1, 2018, only certified composite wood products, whether in the form of panels or incorporated into component parts or finished goods, are permitted to be sold, supplied, offered for sale, or manufactured (including imported) in the United States, unless the product is specifically exempted by this part.
units.actor: persons who sell, supply, offer for sale, or manufacture (including import) composite wood products in the United States
units.action_summary: Only certified composite wood products may be sold, supplied, offered for sale, or manufactured (including imported) in the U.S. beginning June 1, 2018, unless specifically exempted.

units.obligation_text: Correlation data and linear regression equation (or, under the threshold approach, the correlation data and the upper limit);
units.action_summary: Must provide correlation data and linear regression equation (or correlation data and upper limit if threshold approach used) as part of certification.

units.obligation_text: Correlation data and linear regression equation (or, under the threshold approach, the correlation data and the upper limit);
units.action_summary: Must provide correlation data and linear regression equation (or correlation data and upper limit under threshold approach) as required for certification.

units.obligation_text: Three months of routine quality control tests under § 770.20, including a showing of correlation in accordance with § 770.20(d)(2), totaling not less than thirteen quality control tests.
units.actor: panel producers/manufacturers seeking certification under § 770.17 (No-added formaldehyde based resin)
units.action_summary: Must perform three months of routine QC tests, including correlation, totaling at least 13 quality control tests.

units.obligation_text: Six months of routine quality control tests under § 770.20, including a showing of correlation in accordance with § 770.20(d)(2), totaling not less than twenty-six quality control tests.
units.actor: panel producers/manufacturers seeking certification under § 770.18 (Ultra low-emitting formaldehyde based resins)
units.action_summary: Must perform six months of routine QC tests, including correlation, totaling at least 26 quality control tests.

units.obligation_text: Test results may represent a single chamber value or, the average value of testing nine specimens representing evenly distributed portions of an entire panel.
units.actor: testing laboratories / TPCs / panel producers performing quality control testing
units.action_summary: Test results can be either a single chamber value or the average of nine specimens representing the panel.

units.obligation_text: The nine specimens must be tested in groups of three specimens, resulting in three test values, which must be averaged to represent one data point for the panel those specimens represent.
units.actor: testing laboratories / TPCs / panel producers performing quality control testing
units.action_summary: When using nine specimens, they must be tested in three groups of three; the three resulting values must be averaged to form one data point for the panel.

units.obligation_text: Equivalence between ASTM E1333–14 and ASTM D6007–14 must be demonstrated by EPA TSCA Title VI TPCs at least once each year or whenever there is a significant change in equipment, procedure, or the qualifications of testing personnel, or reason to believe that the equivalence is no longer valid.
units.actor: EPA TSCA Title VI TPCs (testing laboratories accredited under TSCA Title VI)
units.action_summary: TPCs must demonstrate equivalence between ASTM E1333–14 and ASTM D6007–14 at least annually or upon significant change or reason to doubt equivalence.

units.obligation_text: Equivalence may be demonstrated between several similar model or size and construction ASTM E1333–14 and ASTM D6007–14 apparatuses located in the same EPA TSCA Title VI TPC laboratory.
units.action_summary: TPCs may demonstrate equivalence across several similar apparatuses within the same laboratory.

units.obligation_text: Once equivalence has been established for three consecutive years, equivalence must be demonstrated every two years or whenever there is a significant change in equipment, procedure, or the qualifications of testing personnel.
units.action_summary: After three consecutive years of established equivalence, TPCs must re-demonstrate equivalence every two years or upon significant change.

units.obligation_text: Correlation between ASTM E1333–14 or, upon a showing of equivalence in accordance with paragraph (d) of this section, ASTM D6007–14, and any other test method used for quality control testing must be demonstrated by EPA TSCA Title VI TPCs or panel producers, respectively, before the certification of composite wood products, and then whenever there is a significant change in equipment, procedure, the qualifications of testing personnel, or reason to believe that the correlation is no longer valid.
units.actor: EPA TSCA Title VI TPCs (for TPC methods) and panel producers (for their quality control methods)
units.action_summary: TPCs and panel producers must demonstrate correlation between ASTM methods and any other QC method before certification and upon significant changes or doubts.

units.obligation_text: Correlation may be established between several similar model or size and construction mill quality control test methods defined in § 770.20(b)(1) located at any one physical mill quality control testing laboratory to the EPA TSCA Title VI TPC’s laboratory’s ASTM E1333–14 and/or ASTM D6007–14 apparatus.
units.actor: panel producers / mill quality control testing laboratories
units.action_summary: Correlation may be established between similar mill QC test methods at one mill QC lab and the TPC laboratory's ASTM apparatus.

units.obligation_text: If the TPC laboratory’s ASTM E1333–14 or equivalent ASTM D6007–14 test chamber is used for panel producer quality control testing, no correlation as determined in § 770.20(d)(2) would be required.
units.action_summary: If the TPC's ASTM test chamber is used for panel producer QC testing, the correlation requirement in § 770.20(d)(2) does not apply.

units.obligation_text: Equivalence must be demonstrated for at least five comparison sample sets in each range tested by the TPC, which compare the results of the two methods.
units.action_summary: TPCs must demonstrate equivalence with at least five comparison sample sets in each tested range.

units.obligation_text: EPA TSCA Title VI TPCs must demonstrate equivalence in at least two of the three formaldehyde emission ranges listed in (d)(1)(iv)(A) through (C) of this section unless the EPA TSCA Title VI TPC will only certify products in one range.
units.action_summary: TPCs must demonstrate equivalence in at least two of the three specified emission ranges unless they only certify products in a single range.

units.obligation_text: If the EPA TSCA Title VI TPC will only certify products in one range, the EPA TSCA Title VI TPC may demonstrate equivalence in only that one range and would then be restricted to only certifying composite wood products in that range.
units.action_summary: If a TPC only certifies in one range, it may demonstrate equivalence in that one range but will be limited to certifying products only in that range.

units.obligation_text: Equivalence in one range must be demonstrated for at least five comparison sample sets in that range which compare the two methods.
units.action_summary: If demonstrating equivalence in one range, TPCs must use at least five comparison sample sets in that range.

units.obligation_text: Lower Range: Less than, or equal to 0.05 ppm.
units.actor: EPA TSCA Title VI TPCs (for purposes of defining equivalence ranges)
units.action_summary: Defines the Lower Range for equivalence as ≤ 0.05 ppm.

units.obligation_text: Intermediate Range: Greater than 0.05 ppm to less than or equal to 0.15 ppm.
units.actor: EPA TSCA Title VI TPCs (for purposes of defining equivalence ranges)
units.action_summary: Defines the Intermediate Range for equivalence as >0.05 to ≤0.15 ppm.

units.obligation_text: Upper Range: Greater than 0.15 to 0.25 ppm.
units.actor: EPA TSCA Title VI TPCs (for purposes of defining equivalence ranges)
units.action_summary: Defines the Upper Range for equivalence as >0.15 to 0.25 ppm.

units.obligation_text: Correlation must be demonstrated by establishing an acceptable correlation coefficient ("r" value) or following the threshold approach at § 770.20(d)(2)(i)(B).
units.actor: EPA TSCA Title VI TPCs and panel producers (respectively)
units.action_summary: Correlation must be shown either by achieving an acceptable r-value or by using the threshold approach.

units.obligation_text: The correlation must be based on a minimum sample size of five data pairs and a simple linear regression (unless the threshold approach at § 770.20(d)(2)(i)(B) is used) where the dependent variable (Y-axis) is the quality control test value and the independent variable (X-axis) is the ASTM E1333–14 test value or, upon a showing of equivalence in accordance with paragraph (d) of this section, the equivalent ASTM D6007–14 test value.
units.actor: EPA TSCA Title VI TPCs and panel producers
units.action_summary: Correlation must use at least five data pairs and simple linear regression (unless threshold approach used), with QC test as dependent and ASTM E1333 (or equivalent) as independent variable.

units.obligation_text: Either composite wood products or formaldehyde emissions reference materials can be used to establish the correlation.
units.actor: EPA TSCA Title VI TPCs and panel producers establishing correlation
units.action_summary: Either composite wood products or reference materials may be used to establish the correlation.

units.obligation_text: A panel producer may work with its EPA TSCA Title VI TPC to develop a correlation and linear regression between the TPC’s ASTM E1333–14 or equivalent ASTM D6007–14 test method and the panel producer’s quality control method under § 770.20(b).
units.actor: panel producers (in conjunction with their EPA TSCA Title VI TPC)
units.action_summary: Panel producers may collaborate with their TPC to develop a correlation and linear regression between the TPC test method and the producer's QC method.

units.obligation_text: As an alternative to the linear regression and cluster approaches, a panel producer may use the average value of the clustered data pairs from the EPA TSCA Title VI TPC’s ASTM E1333–14 or equivalent ASTM D6007–14 test method and the panel producer’s quality control method under § 770.20(b) as the quality control limit for the product.
units.actor: panel producers (in conjunction with their EPA TSCA Title VI TPC)
units.action_summary: Panel producers may use the average of clustered data pairs as the QC limit instead of fitting a linear regression.

units.obligation_text: This value, established as the quality control limit, must be below the applicable emission standard.
units.actor: panel producers establishing a quality control limit under the threshold approach
units.action_summary: The QC limit established under the threshold approach must be below the applicable emission standard.

units.obligation_text: At least one test panel must be randomly selected so that it is representative of the entire non-complying lot and is not the top or bottom panel of a bundle.
units.actor: panel producers / testing personnel selecting panels for retest
units.action_summary: At least one representative test panel must be randomly selected and cannot be the top or bottom panel of a bundle.

units.obligation_text: Panel sampling shall be conducted according to the quarterly testing procedure at § 770.20(c)(2)(iv).
units.action_summary: Panel sampling must follow the quarterly testing procedure specified in § 770.20(c)(2)(iv).

units.obligation_text: The panel may be selected from properly stored samples set aside by the panel producer for retest in the event of a failure.
units.action_summary: The selected panel may be chosen from properly stored samples set aside for retest.

units.obligation_text: If a fabricator, importer, distributor, or retailer is notified that they have been supplied a non-complying lot after those composite wood products have been fabricated into component parts or finished goods, the notification requirement at paragraph (d)(1) of this section does not apply.
units.action_summary: If notified after products have been fabricated into component parts or finished goods, the notification requirement at paragraph (d)(1) does not apply to these entities.

units.obligation_text: Importers must demonstrate that they have taken reasonable precautions by maintaining, for three years, bills of lading, invoices, or comparable documents that include a written statement from the supplier that the composite wood products, component parts, or finished goods are TSCA Title VI compliant or were produced before June 1, 2018 and by ensuring the following records are made available to EPA within 30 calendar days of request:
units.action_summary: Importers must maintain specified records for three years and ensure those records can be provided to EPA within 30 calendar days upon request.

units.obligation_text: maintaining, for three years, bills of lading, invoices, or comparable documents that include a written statement from the supplier that the composite wood products, component parts, or finished goods are TSCA Title VI compliant or were produced before June 1, 2018
units.action_summary: Must keep bills of lading, invoices, or comparable documents including supplier written statements for three years.

units.obligation_text: ensuring the following records are made available to EPA within 30 calendar days of request
units.action_summary: Must make records available to EPA within 30 calendar days of request.

units.obligation_text: Fabricators, distributors, and retailers must demonstrate that they have taken reasonable precautions by obtaining bills of lading, invoices, or comparable documents that include a written statement from the supplier that the composite wood products, component parts, or finished goods are TSCA Title VI compliant or that the composite wood products were produced before June 1, 2018.
units.action_summary: Fabricators, distributors, and retailers must obtain bills of lading, invoices, or comparable documents with supplier written statements showing compliance or pre-June 1, 2018 production.

units.obligation_text: Panels or bundles of panels that are imported, sold, supplied, or offered for sale in the United States must be labeled with the panel producer’s name, the lot number, the number of the EPA TSCA Title VI TPC, and a statement that the products are TSCA Title VI certified (or, for products exempt from certain testing and certification pursuant to §§ 770.17 or 770.18, a statement that the products are TSCA Title VI compliant).
units.actor: persons importing, selling, supplying, or offering for sale panels or bundles of panels in the United States (panel producers, importers, distributors, fabricators, retailers)
units.action_summary: Panels or bundles must carry a label with producer name, lot number, TPC number, and appropriate TSCA Title VI certification/compliance statement.

units.obligation_text: If a composite wood panel is not individually labeled, the panel producer, importer, distributor, fabricator, or retailer must have a method (e.g., color-coded edge marking) sufficient to identify the supplier of the panel and linking the information on the label to the products.
units.actor: panel producer, importer, distributor, fabricator, or retailer
units.action_summary: If panels are not individually labeled, the responsible parties must have an identification method linking products to the supplier and label information.

units.obligation_text: This information must be made available to potential customers upon request.
units.actor: panel producer, importer, distributor, fabricator, or retailer
units.action_summary: Supplier and label information must be provided to potential customers upon request.

units.obligation_text: The label may be applied as a stamp, tag, or sticker.
units.actor: panel producer, importer, distributor, fabricator, or retailer
units.action_summary: Labels may be applied by stamp, tag, or sticker.

units.obligation_text: All panels (or bundles of panels) and finished goods (or boxes or bundles containing finished goods) must be properly labeled pursuant to paragraphs (a), (b), and (c) of this section before being imported into the United States, except as provided in paragraph (e) of this section.
units.actor: persons importing panels, bundles, finished goods, or boxes/bundles containing finished goods into the United States (importers, panel producers, etc.)
units.action_summary: All panels and finished goods must be properly labeled according to paragraphs (a)–(c) before importation into the U.S., except as provided in paragraph (e).

Clean Air Plans; 2008 8-Hour Ozone Nonattainment Area 
Requirements; San Joaquin Valley, California

AGENCY: Environmental Protection Agency (EPA).

ACTION: Proposed rule.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------

SUMMARY: The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is proposing to 
approve portions of three state implementation plan (SIP) revisions 
submitted by the State of California to meet Clean Air Act (CAA or 
``the Act'') requirements for the 2008 8-hour ozone national ambient 
air quality standards (NAAQS or ``standards'') in the San Joaquin 
Valley, California ozone nonattainment area. First, the EPA is 
proposing to approve the portions of the 2016 Ozone Plan for the 2008 
8-Hour Ozone Standard (``2016 Ozone Plan'') that address the 
requirements to demonstrate attainment by the applicable attainment 
date and implementation of reasonably available control measures, among 
other requirements. Second, the EPA is proposing to approve the 
portions of the Revised Proposed 2016 State Strategy for the State 
Implementation Plan (``2016 State Strategy'') related to the ozone 
control strategy for San Joaquin Valley for the 2008 ozone standards, 
including a specific aggregate emissions reduction commitment. Lastly, 
the EPA is proposing to approve an air district rule addressing the 
emission statement requirement for ozone nonattainment areas. The EPA 
is not taking action at this time on the portions of the San Joaquin 
Valley 2016 Ozone Plan that address the requirements for a reasonable 
further progress (RFP) demonstration, motor vehicle emissions budgets 
(MVEBs), a base year emissions inventory, and contingency measures for 
failure to attain or to meet reasonable further progress milestones. We 
intend to address these remaining elements in a forthcoming proposal.

I. Regulatory Context

A. Ozone Standards, Area Designations and SIPs

    Ground-level ozone pollution is formed from the reaction of 
volatile organic compounds (VOC) and oxides of nitrogen 
(NO
X
) in the presence of sunlight.\1\ These two pollutants, 
referred

[[Page 44529]]

to as ozone precursors, are emitted by many types of sources, including 
on-and off-road motor vehicles and engines, power plants and industrial 
facilities, and smaller area sources such as lawn and garden equipment 
and paints.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    \1\ The State of California typically refers to reactive organic 
gases (ROG) in its ozone-related submissions since VOC in general 
can include both reactive and unreactive gases. However, since ROG 
and VOC inventories pertain to common chemical species (e.g., 
benzene, xylene, etc.), we refer to this set of gases as VOC in this 
proposed rule.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    Scientific evidence indicates that adverse public health effects 
occur following exposure to ozone, particularly in children and adults 
with lung disease. Breathing air containing ozone can reduce lung 
function and inflame airways, which can increase respiratory symptoms 
and aggravate asthma or other lung diseases.\2\
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    \2\ See ``Fact Sheet--2008 Final Revisions to the National 
Ambient Air Quality Standards for Ozone'' dated March 2008.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    Under section 109 of the CAA, the EPA promulgates NAAQS for 
pervasive air pollutants, such as ozone. The EPA has previously 
promulgated NAAQS for ozone in 1979 and 1997.\3\ In 2008, the EPA 
revised and further strengthened the ozone NAAQS by setting the 
acceptable level of ozone in the ambient air at 0.075 parts per million 
(ppm) averaged over an 8-hour period.\4\ Although the EPA further 
tightened the 8-hour ozone NAAQS to 0.070 ppm in 2015, this action 
relates to the requirements for the 2008 ozone NAAQS.\5\
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    \3\ The ozone NAAQS promulgated in 1979 was 0.12 parts per 
million (ppm) averaged over a 1-hour period. See 44 FR 8202 
(February 8, 1979). The ozone NAAQS promulgated in 1997 was 0.08 ppm 
averaged over an 8-hour period. See 62 FR 38856 (July 18, 1997).
    \4\ See 73 FR 16436 (March 27, 2008).
    \5\ Information on the 2015 ozone NAAQS is available at 80 FR 
65292 (October 26, 2015).
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    Following promulgation of a new or revised NAAQS, the EPA is 
required under CAA section 107(d) to designate areas throughout the 
country as attaining or not attaining the NAAQS. The San Joaquin Valley 
was designated as nonattainment for the 2008 ozone standards on May 21, 
2012, and classified as Extreme.\6\
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    \6\ See 77 FR 30088 (May 21, 2012).
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    Under the CAA, after the EPA designates areas as nonattainment for 
a NAAQS, states with nonattainment areas are required to submit SIP 
revisions that provide for, among other things, attainment of the NAAQS 
within certain prescribed periods that vary depending on the severity 
of nonattainment. Areas classified as Extreme must attain the NAAQS 
within 20 years of the effective date of the nonattainment 
designation.\7\
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    \7\ See CAA section 181(a)(1), 40 CFR 51.1102 and 51.1103(a).
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    In California, the California Air Resources Board (CARB or 
``State'') is the state agency responsible for the adoption and 
submission to the EPA of California SIPs and SIP revisions, and it has 
broad authority to establish emissions standards and other requirements 
for mobile sources. Local and regional air pollution control districts 
in California are responsible for the regulation of stationary sources 
and are generally responsible for the development of regional air 
quality plans. In the San Joaquin Valley, the San Joaquin Valley Air 
Pollution Control District (SJVAPCD or ``District'') develops and 
adopts air quality management plans to address CAA planning 
requirements applicable to that region. Such plans are then submitted 
to CARB for adoption and submittal to the EPA as revisions to the 
California SIP.

B. The San Joaquin Valley Ozone Nonattainment Area

    The San Joaquin Valley nonattainment area for the 2008 ozone 
standards consists of San Joaquin, Stanislaus, Merced, Madera, Fresno, 
Tulare, and Kings counties, and the western portion of Kern County. The 
San Joaquin Valley nonattainment area stretches over 250 miles from 
north to south, averages a width of 80 miles, and encompasses over 
23,000 square miles. It is partially enclosed by the Coast Mountain 
range to the west, the Tehachapi Mountains to the south, and the Sierra 
Nevada range to the east.\8\
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    \8\ For a precise definition of the boundaries of the San 
Joaquin Valley 2008 ozone nonattainment area, see 40 CFR 81.305.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    The population of the San Joaquin Valley in 2015 was estimated to 
be nearly 4.2 million people, and is projected to increase by 25.3 
percent in 2030 to over 5.2 million people.\9\ Ambient 8-hour ozone 
concentrations in the San Joaquin Valley are above the level of the 
2008 8-hour ozone NAAQS. The maximum design value for the area, based

C. CAA and Regulatory Requirements for 2008 8-Hour Ozone Nonattainment 
Area SIPs

    States must implement the 2008 ozone standards under Title 1, part 
D of the CAA, which includes section 172 (``Nonattainment plan 
provisions in general'') and sections 181-185 of subpart 2 
(``Additional Provisions for Ozone Nonattainment Areas''). To assist 
states in developing effective plans to address ozone nonattainment 
problems, in 2015 the EPA issued a SIP Requirements Rule (SRR) for the 
2008 ozone standards (``2008 Ozone SRR'') that addresses e.g., 
attainment dates, requirements for emissions inventories, attainment 
and RFP demonstrations, and the transition from the 1997 8-hour ozone 
standards to the 2008 8-hour ozone standards and associated anti-
backsliding requirements.\11\ The 2008 Ozone SRR is codified at 40 CFR 
part 51, subpart AA. We discuss each of the CAA and regulatory 
requirements for 2008 8-hour ozone plans in more detail below.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    \11\ See 80 FR 12264, March 6, 2015.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    The EPA's 2008 Ozone SRR was challenged, and on February 16, 2018, 
the U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit (``D.C. Circuit'') 
published its decision in South Coast Air Quality Management. District 
v. EPA \12\ vacating portions of the 2008 Ozone SRR. The 2008 Ozone SRR 
required the baseline emissions inventory for RFP plans to be the 
emissions inventory for the most recent calendar year for which a 
triennial inventory is required to be submitted to the EPA under 
subpart A (``Air Emissions Reporting Requirements'') of 40 CFR part 51, 
and it allowed states to use an alternative year, between 2008 and 
2012, for the baseline emissions inventory provided the state 
demonstrates why the alternative baseline year is appropriate. In the 
South Coast decision, the D.C. Circuit vacated the provisions of the 
2008 Ozone SRR that allowed states to justify and use an alternative 
baseline year for demonstrating RFP. The RFP demonstrations in several 
California ozone plans developed to address nonattainment area 
requirements for the 2008 ozone standards, including the ozone plan for 
the South Coast Air Basin and San Joaquin Valley, are based on the 
alternative baseline year of 2012. In response to the South Coast 
decision regarding alternative baseline years, the South Coast Air 
Quality Management District filed a petition in the D.C. Circuit 
requesting rehearing on the RFP

[[Page 44530]]

baseline year issue to clarify that nonattainment areas may use the 
year of the nonattainment designation (i.e., 2012 for the 2008 ozone 
standards) as the baseline year for calculating RFP.\13\ Because the 
D.C. Circuit has not yet issued a response to the petitions filed for 
rehearing, the EPA is not proposing action at this time on the San 
Joaquin Valley's RFP demonstration for the 2008 ozone standards.\14\ 
Several required attainment plan elements are related to the RFP 
demonstration, namely the MVEBs, the base year emissions inventory, and 
contingency measures. Therefore, the EPA is also not proposing action 
at this time on these three elements. For completeness, however, in 
this proposed action, we provide a summary of all the required 
elements, including those for which we will be proposing action at a 
later time.

III. Evaluation of the 2016 Ozone Plan

A. Emissions Inventories

1. Statutory and Regulatory Requirements
    CAA sections 172(c)(3) and 182(a)(1) require states to submit for 
each ozone nonattainment area a ``base year inventory'' that is a 
comprehensive, accurate, current inventory of actual emissions from all 
sources of the relevant pollutant or pollutants in the area. In 
addition, the 2008 Ozone SRR requires that the inventory year be 
selected consistent with the baseline year for the RFP demonstration, 
which is usually the most recent calendar year for which a complete 
triennial inventory is required to be submitted to the EPA under the 
Air Emissions Reporting Requirements.\26\ The EPA has issued guidance 
on the development of base year and future year emissions inventories 
for 8-hour ozone and other pollutants.\27\ Emissions inventories for 
ozone must include emissions of VOC and NO
X
 and represent 
emissions for a typical ozone season weekday.\28\ States should include 
documentation explaining how the emissions data were calculated. In 
estimating mobile source emissions, states should use the latest 
emissions models and planning assumptions available at the time the SIP 
is developed.\29\

3. The EPA's Review of the State's Submission
    As described elsewhere, the 2008 Ozone SRR requires the base year 
inventory to be consistent with the RFP baseline year inventory; 
accordingly, the 2016 Ozone Plan uses the year 2012 for the base year 
inventory and the RFP baseline year inventory. The EPA has evaluated 
the 2012 base year inventory and the methodologies used by the District 
and CARB, and we find them to be comprehensive, accurate, and current. 
However, as discussed elsewhere, we are not taking action at this time 
to approve the base year emissions inventory or the emissions 
inventories for any of the RFP milestone years in the 2016 Ozone Plan. 
We intend to take action on the base year emissions inventory at a 
later time, together with the RFP demonstration, and other elements 
affected by the South Coast decision.
    However, we note that the attainment demonstration and VMT offset 
demonstration rely on the 2012 base year inventory. As discussed in 
section III.D of this proposed action, the EPA's draft modeling 
guidance states that the EPA does not require a particular year to be 
used for the base year for modeling purposes. The most appropriate base 
year may be the most recent year of the National Emissions Inventory, 
or it may be selected in view of unusual meteorology, transport 
patterns, or other factors that may vary from year to year.\33\ Based 
on our review of the emissions inventories provided in the 2016 Ozone 
Plan, we find that the 2012 base year emissions inventory and future 
year emissions inventories that are derived therefrom provide an 
acceptable basis for the attainment demonstration and VMT offset 
demonstration in the 2016 Ozone Plan.
