units.action_summary: Provide the Administrator records necessary to determine performance test conditions upon request.

units.obligation_text: Prior to [DATE 181 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE Federal Register], you may not conduct performance tests during periods of startup, shutdown, or malfunction, as specified in § 63.7(e)(1).
units.action_summary: Before the specified date, do not conduct performance tests during startup, shutdown, or malfunction.

units.obligation_text: After [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE Federal Register], during startup and shutdown, you must follow the requirements in § 63.7090(c).
units.action_summary: During startup and shutdown after the specified date, follow the requirements of §63.7090(c).

units.obligation_text: The observer conducting the VE checks need not be certified to conduct EPA Method 9 ... but must meet the training requirements as described in EPA Method 22 ...
units.action_summary: Observer need not be Method 9 certified but must meet training requirements under EPA Method 22.

units.obligation_text: When determining compliance with the opacity standards for fugitive emissions from PSH operations in item 8 of Table 1 to this subpart, you must conduct EPA Method 9 ... and in accordance with paragraphs (l)(1) through (3) of this section.
units.action_summary: Use EPA Method 9 and follow specified subparagraphs to determine compliance with fugitive emissions opacity standards for PSH operations.

units.obligation_text: After [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE Federal Register], for kilns and coolers equipped with an ESP, the run average temperature must be calculated for each run, and the average of the run average temperatures must be determined and included in the performance test report and will be used to determine compliance with § 63.7090(c)(5).
units.actor: owners/operators of kilns and coolers equipped with an ESP
units.action_summary: Calculate run-average temperatures for each run, compute their average, include in performance test report to determine compliance with §63.7090(c)(5).

units.obligation_text: For each bag leak detection system (BLDS), you must meet any applicable requirements in paragraphs (a)(1) through (5) and (d)(1) through (9) of this section.
units.action_summary: Ensure each BLDS complies with applicable requirements listed in the section.

units.obligation_text: The BLDS must be equipped with a device to continuously record the output signal from the sensor.
units.action_summary: Equip bag leak detection systems with a device that continuously records sensor output.

units.obligation_text: Each triboelectric BLDS must be installed, calibrated, operated, and maintained according to EPA–454/R–98–015. Other types of bag leak detection systems must be installed, operated, calibrated, and maintained according to the manufacturer’s written specifications and recommendations. Standard operating procedures must be incorporated into the OM&M plan.
units.action_summary: Install, calibrate, operate, and maintain triboelectric BLDS per EPA guidance; other BLDS per manufacturer's specs; incorporate SOPs into OM&M plan.

units.obligation_text: At a minimum, initial adjustment of the system must consist of establishing the baseline output in both of the following ways, according to section 5.0 of the EPA–454/R–98–015.
units.action_summary: During initial adjustment, establish baseline output in required ways per EPA guidance.

units.obligation_text: After initial adjustment, the sensitivity or range, averaging period, alarm set points, or alarm delay time may not be adjusted except as specified in the OM&M plan required by § 63.7100(d). In no event may the range be increased by more than 100 percent or decreased by more than 50 percent over a 365-day period unless such adjustment follows a complete FF inspection that demonstrates that the FF is in good operating condition. Record each adjustment.
units.action_summary: Do not adjust specified BLDS settings except as in OM&M plan; range adjustments limited to +100%/-50% over 365 days unless preceded by a complete FF inspection showing good condition; record every adjustment.

units.obligation_text: Record the results of each inspection, calibration, and validation check.
units.action_summary: Keep records of every inspection, calibration, and validation check of BLDS.

units.obligation_text: After [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE Federal Register], for kilns and coolers equipped with an ESP, you must demonstrate compliance with the startup requirements in § 63.7090(c)(5) by meeting the requirements of paragraphs (h)(1) through (5) of this section.
units.actor: owners/operators of kilns and coolers equipped with an ESP
units.action_summary: Demonstrate compliance with §63.7090(c)(5) by meeting §63.7113(h)(1)-(5) requirements after the specified date.

units.obligation_text: You must install, calibrate, maintain, and continuously operate a CMS to record the temperature of the exhaust gases at the inlet to, or upstream of, the ESP.
units.action_summary: Install, calibrate, maintain, and continuously operate a continuous monitoring system to record exhaust gas temperature at/near ESP inlet.

units.obligation_text: The temperature recorder response range must include zero and 1.5 times the average temperature established during your performance test according to the requirements in § 63.7112(m).
units.action_summary: Ensure temperature recorder range includes zero and 1.5× the average test-established temperature.

units.obligation_text: The calibration reference for the temperature measurement must be a National Institute of Standards and Technology calibrated reference thermocouple-potentiometer system or alternate reference, subject to approval by the Administrator.
units.action_summary: Use NIST-calibrated thermocouple-potentiometer reference or an Administrator-approved alternate for temperature calibration.

units.obligation_text: The calibration of all thermocouples and other temperature sensors must be verified at least once every three months.
units.action_summary: Verify calibration of thermocouples and temperature sensors at least quarterly.

units.obligation_text: You must monitor and continuously record the temperature of the exhaust gases from the kiln and cooler, if applicable, at the inlet to the kiln and/or cooler ESP.
units.action_summary: Continuously monitor and record exhaust gas temperatures at inlet to kiln and/or cooler ESP.

units.obligation_text: You must report each instance in which you did not meet each operating limit, work practice, opacity limit, and VE limit in Tables 2 and 6 to this subpart that applies to you. This includes periods of startup, shutdown, and malfunction. These deviations must be reported according to the requirements in § 63.7131.
units.action_summary: Report every instance of noncompliance with operating, work practice, opacity, and VE limits (including during S/S/M) per §63.7131 requirements.

units.obligation_text: Deviations that occur during a period of startup, shutdown, or malfunction are not violations if you demonstrate to the Administrator’s satisfaction that you were operating in accordance with § 63.6(e)(1).
units.action_summary: To avoid a violation for deviations during S/S/M, demonstrate to the Administrator that you operated in accordance with §63.6(e)(1).

units.obligation_text: If you are required to conduct a performance test, design evaluation, opacity observation, VE observation, or other initial compliance demonstration as specified in Table 3 or 4 to this subpart, you must submit a Notification of Compliance Status according to § 63.9(h)(2)(ii).
units.actor: you (owner/operator required to conduct initial compliance demonstrations)
units.action_summary: Submit a Notification of Compliance Status per §63.9(h)(2)(ii) if an initial compliance demonstration is required.

units.obligation_text: Beginning on [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE Federal Register], submit all subsequent Notification of Compliance Status following the procedure specified in § 63.7131(h).
units.action_summary: After the specified date, submit subsequent Notifications of Compliance Status following §63.7131(h) procedures.

units.obligation_text: Unless the Administrator has approved a different schedule for submission of reports under § 63.10(a), you must submit each report by the date specified in Table 7 to this subpart and according to the requirements in paragraphs (b)(1) through (6) of this section.
units.action_summary: Submit required reports by the Table 7 dates and per listed requirements unless an alternative schedule is approved.

units.obligation_text: Beginning on [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE Federal Register], submit all subsequent compliance reports following the procedure specified in paragraph (h) of this section.
units.action_summary: After the specified date, submit compliance reports via the procedure in paragraph (h).

units.obligation_text: Prior to [DATE 181 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE Federal Register], if you had a startup, shutdown, or malfunction during the reporting period and you took actions consistent with your SSMP, the compliance report must include the information in § 63.10(d)(5)(i).
units.action_summary: If S/S/M occurred and you followed your SSMP, include §63.10(d)(5)(i) information in the compliance report before the specified date.

units.obligation_text: If there were no deviations from any emission limitations that apply to you, the compliance report must include a statement that there were no deviations from the emission limitations during the reporting period.
units.action_summary: Include a statement of 'no deviations' in the compliance report when applicable.

units.obligation_text: If there were no periods during which the continuous monitoring systems (CMS), including CPMS, were out-of-control as specified in § 63.8(c)(7), a statement that there were no periods during which the CMS were out-of-control during the reporting period.
units.action_summary: Report that CMS were never out-of-control during the reporting period if that is the case.

units.obligation_text: For each deviation from an emission limitation that occurs at an affected source where you are not using a CMS to comply with the emission limitations in this subpart, the compliance report must contain the information specified in paragraphs (c)(1) through (4) and (d)(1) and (2) of this section.
units.action_summary: Include specified information elements when reporting deviations for units not using a CMS.

units.obligation_text: The total operating time of each emission unit during the reporting period.
units.action_summary: Report total operating time of each emission unit during the reporting period.

units.obligation_text: Information on the number, duration, and cause of deviations (including unknown cause, if applicable), and the corrective action taken.
units.action_summary: Provide details on number, duration, cause of deviations and corrective actions taken.

units.obligation_text: An estimate of the quantity of each regulated pollutant emitted over any emission limit, and a description of the method used to estimate the emissions.
units.action_summary: Estimate pollutant quantities emitted over limits and describe the estimation method.

units.obligation_text: For each deviation from an emission limitation occurring at an affected source where you are using a CMS to comply with the emission limitation in this subpart, you must include the information specified in paragraphs (c)(1) through (4) and (e)(1) through (11) of this section, except that after [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE Federal Register] the semiannual compliance report must also include the information included in paragraph (e)(12) of this section.
units.action_summary: When using a CMS, include specified information for deviations; after the specified date also include (e)(12) in semiannual reports.

units.obligation_text: The date, time, and duration that each CMS was inoperative, except for zero (low-level) and high-level checks.
units.action_summary: Report date, time, and duration of CMS inoperative periods (excluding certain checks).

units.obligation_text: An estimate of the quantity of each regulated pollutant emitted over any emission limit, and a description of the method used to estimate the emissions.
units.action_summary: Include an estimate of pollutant emissions over limits and describe the estimation method in the semiannual compliance report after the specified date.

units.obligation_text: Each facility that has obtained a title V operating permit pursuant to part 70 or part 71 of this chapter must report all deviations as defined in this subpart in the semiannual monitoring report required by §§ 70.6(a)(3)(iii)(A) or 71.6(a)(3)(iii)(A) of this chapter.
units.actor: facilities with a title V operating permit
units.action_summary: Title V permit facilities must report all deviations in the semiannual monitoring report required by the permit rules.

units.obligation_text: If you are required to submit reports following the procedure specified in this paragraph, you must submit reports to the EPA via the Compliance and Emissions Data Reporting Interface (CEDRI), which can be accessed through the EPA’s Central Data Exchange (CDX). You must use the appropriate electronic report template on the CEDRI website for this subpart.
units.actor: you (owner/operator required to submit reports electronically)
units.action_summary: Submit required reports via CEDRI using the specified electronic report template on the CEDRI/CDX system.

units.obligation_text: The report must be submitted by the deadline specified in this subpart, regardless of the method in which the report is submitted.
units.action_summary: Submit reports by the subpart-specified deadline irrespective of submission method.

units.obligation_text: If you claim some of the information required to be submitted via CEDRI is confidential business information (CBI), submit a complete report, including information claimed to be CBI, to the EPA. The report must be generated using the appropriate form on the CEDRI website. Submit the file on a compact disc, flash drive, or other commonly used electronic storage medium and clearly mark the medium as CBI. Mail the electronic medium to U.S. EPA/OAQPS/CORE CBI Office ... The same file with the CBI omitted must be submitted to the EPA via the EPA’s CDX as described earlier in this paragraph.
units.action_summary: If claiming CBI, submit a complete CBI-containing file on physical media to EPA's CBI office and submit a redacted file via CDX/CEDRI as described.

units.obligation_text: Performance Tests. Within 60 days after the date of completing each performance test required by this subpart, you must submit the results of the performance test following the procedures specified in paragraphs (h)(1) through (3) of this section.
units.action_summary: Submit performance test results within 60 days using the procedures in (h)(1)-(3).

units.obligation_text: Data collected using test methods supported by the EPA’s Electronic Reporting Tool (ERT) ... Submit the results of the performance test to the EPA via CEDRI ... The data must be submitted in a file format generated through the use of the EPA’s ERT. Alternatively, you may submit an electronic file consistent with the XML schema listed on the EPA’s ERT website.
units.actor: you (owner/operator conducting performance tests using ERT-supported methods)
units.action_summary: Submit performance test data collected with ERT-supported methods to EPA via CEDRI in the ERT-generated format or in a compliant XML file.

units.obligation_text: Data collected using test methods that are not supported by the EPA’s ERT ... The results of the performance test must be included as an attachment in the ERT or an alternate electronic file consistent with the XML schema listed on the EPA’s ERT website. Submit the ERT generated package or alternative file to the EPA via CEDRI.
units.actor: you (owner/operator conducting performance tests using non-ERT-supported methods)
units.action_summary: Attach results from non-ERT-supported methods in the ERT or as an alternate XML-compliant electronic file and submit via CEDRI.

units.obligation_text: If you claim some of the information submitted under paragraph (i) of this section is CBI, you must submit a complete file, including information claimed to be CBI, to the EPA. The file must be generated through the use of the EPA’s ERT or an alternate electronic file consistent with the XML schema listed on the EPA’s ERT website. Submit the file on a compact disc, flash drive, or other commonly used electronic storage medium and clearly mark the medium as CBI. Mail the electronic medium to U.S. EPA/OAQPS/CORE CBI Office ... The same file with the CBI omitted must be submitted to the EPA via the EPA’s CDX.
units.actor: you (owner/operator claiming CBI for performance test submissions)
units.action_summary: When claiming CBI for performance test submissions, submit a complete CBI-containing file on physical media to the EPA CBI office and a redacted file via CDX.

units.obligation_text: You must submit notification to the Administrator in writing as soon as possible following the date you first knew, or through due diligence should have known, that the event may cause or has caused a delay in reporting.
units.actor: you (entity asserting an EPA system outage claim)
units.action_summary: Notify the Administrator in writing as soon as possible when you first knew an EPA system outage may have caused a reporting delay.

units.obligation_text: You must provide to the Administrator a written description identifying: (i) The date(s) and time(s) when CDX or CEDRI was accessed and the system was unavailable; (ii) A rationale for attributing the delay in reporting beyond the regulatory deadline to EPA system outage; (iii) Measures taken or to be taken to minimize the delay in reporting; and (iv) The date by which you propose to report, or if you have already met the reporting requirement at the time of the notification, the date you reported.
units.actor: you (entity asserting an EPA system outage claim)
units.action_summary: Provide the Administrator with a written description containing specific details about the outage timing, rationale, mitigation measures, and proposed reporting date.

units.obligation_text: In any circumstance, the report must be submitted electronically as soon as possible after the outage is resolved.
units.action_summary: Submit the report electronically as soon as possible after the EPA system outage is resolved.

units.obligation_text: You must submit notification to the Administrator in writing as soon as possible following the date you first knew, or through due diligence should have known, that the event may cause or has caused a delay in reporting (for force majeure claims).
units.actor: you (entity asserting a force majeure claim)
units.action_summary: Notify the Administrator in writing as soon as possible when a force majeure event may have caused a reporting delay.

units.obligation_text: You must provide to the Administrator: (i) A written description of the force majeure event; (ii) A rationale for attributing the delay in reporting beyond the regulatory deadline to the force majeure event; (iii) Measures taken or to be taken to minimize the delay in reporting; and (iv) The date by which you propose to report, or if you have already met the reporting requirement at the time of the notification, the date you reported.
units.actor: you (entity asserting a force majeure claim)
units.action_summary: Provide the Administrator with a written description of the force majeure event, rationale, mitigation measures, and proposed or actual reporting date.

units.obligation_text: In any circumstance, the reporting must occur as soon as possible after the force majeure event occurs.
units.action_summary: Report as soon as possible following a force majeure event.

units.obligation_text: You must keep records of the date, time and duration of each startup and/or shutdown period for any affected source that is subject to a standard during startup or shutdown that differs from the standard applicable at other times.
units.action_summary: Record date, time, and duration of each startup/shutdown period for affected sources with different startup/shutdown standards.

units.obligation_text: You must keep records of the date, time, cause and duration of each malfunction that causes an affected source to fail to meet an applicable standard; if there was also a monitoring malfunction, the date, time, cause, and duration of the monitoring malfunction; the record must list the affected source or equipment, an estimate of the volume of each regulated pollutant emitted over the standard for which the source failed to meet a standard, and a description of the method used to estimate the emissions.
units.action_summary: Keep records of malfunctions including date/time/cause/duration, list affected equipment, estimate pollutant volumes over standards, and describe estimation methods.

units.obligation_text: For kilns and coolers equipped with an ESP, the average of the run average temperatures determined in accordance with § 63.7112(m) must be recorded.
units.actor: owners/operators of kilns and coolers equipped with an ESP
units.action_summary: Record the average of run-average temperatures as determined per §63.7112(m).

units.obligation_text: Any records required to be maintained by this part that are submitted electronically via the EPA’s CEDRI may be maintained in electronic format.
units.action_summary: You may keep CEDRI-submitted records in electronic format.

units.obligation_text: This ability to maintain electronic copies does not affect the requirement for facilities to make records, data, and reports available upon request to a delegated air agency or the EPA as part of an on-site compliance evaluation.
units.action_summary: Make records, data, and reports available upon request for on-site compliance evaluations despite ability to maintain electronic copies.

units.obligation_text: The test plan preparation and implementation in the Annexes to ASTM D 6348–12e1, Sections A1 through A8 are mandatory.
units.action_summary: Follow and implement the Annexes A1–A8 of ASTM D6348–12e1 in test plan preparation and implementation.

units.obligation_text: In ASTM D6348–12e1 Annex A5 (Analyte Spiking Technique), the percent recovery (%R) must be determined for each target analyte (Equation A5.5). In order for the test data to be acceptable for a compound, %R must be greater than or equal to 70 percent and less than or equal to 130 percent. If the %R value does not meet this criterion for a target compound, the test data are not acceptable for that compound and the test must be repeated for that analyte. The %R value for each compound must be reported in the test report, and all field measurements must be corrected with the calculated %R value for that compound by using the following equation: Reported Results = ((Measured Concentration in the Stack)) / (%R) × 100;
units.action_summary: Determine %R for each analyte; accept data only if %R between 70% and 130%; if not, repeat test; report %R and correct field measurements using the %R value.

units.obligation_text: A test must include three or more runs in which a pair of samples is obtained simultaneously for each run according to section 11.2.6 of ASTM Method D6735–01.
units.action_summary: Conduct tests with at least three runs, obtaining simultaneous paired samples each run per ASTM D6735–01 section 11.2.6.

units.obligation_text: The post-test analyte spike procedure of section 11.2.7 of ASTM Method D6735–01 is conducted, and the percent recovery is calculated according to section 12.6 of ASTM Method D6735–01.
units.action_summary: Conduct post-test analyte spike procedure and calculate percent recovery as specified in ASTM D6735–01.

units.obligation_text: The test plan preparation and implementation in the Annexes to ASTM D 6348–12e1, Sections A1 through A8 are mandatory.
units.actor: you (testers/owners/operators using ASTM D6348 as alternative)
units.action_summary: Mandatory use of Annexes A1–A8 for test plan prep/implementation when using ASTM D6348 as an alternative.

units.obligation_text: In ASTM D6348–12e1 Annex A5 ... the percent recovery (%R) must be determined for each target analyte ... %R must be greater than or equal to 70 percent and less than or equal to 130 percent. If the %R value does not meet this criterion ... the test must be repeated ... The %R value for each compound must be reported in the test report, and all field measurements must be corrected with the calculated %R value for that compound by using the following equation: Reported Results = ((Measured Concentration in the Stack)) / (%R) × 100;
units.actor: you (testers/owners/operators using ASTM D6348 as alternative)
units.action_summary: When using ASTM D6348 as alternative, determine %R for each analyte, require %R between 70–130% for acceptability, repeat tests if outside range, report %R and correct field measurements.

units.obligation_text: The target compound(s) are those listed in section 1.1 of ASTM D6420–99 (Reapproved 2010) as measurable.
units.action_summary: Limit target compounds to those listed as measurable in ASTM D6420–99 section 1.1.

units.obligation_text: This ASTM should not be used for methane and ethane because their atomic mass is less than 35.
units.action_summary: Do not use ASTM D6420 to measure methane and ethane because their atomic mass is <35.

units.obligation_text: ASTM D6420 (Reapproved 2010) should never be specified as a total VOC.
units.action_summary: Do not specify ASTM D6420 as a method for total volatile organic compounds (VOCs).

title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Generic Maximum Achievable Control Technology Standards Residual Risk and Technology Review for Ethylene Production

units.obligation_text: To determine compliance with a parts per million by volume total organic regulated material or TOC limit, the owner or operator shall use Method 18 or 25A of 40 CFR part 60, appendix A, as applicable.
units.action_summary: Use Method 18 or 25A to determine compliance with ppmv TOC limits.

units.obligation_text: The ASTM D6420–18 (Incorporated by reference, see § 63.14) may be used in lieu of Method 18 of 40 CFR part 60, appendix A, under the conditions specified in paragraphs (e)(2)(iii)(D)(1) through (3) of this section.
units.action_summary: May use ASTM D6420–18 instead of Method 18 under specified conditions.

units.obligation_text: Alternatively, any other method or data that have been validated according to the applicable procedures in Method 301 of appendix A of 40 CFR part 63 may be used.
units.action_summary: May use other validated methods or data per Method 301 as alternatives.

units.obligation_text: The procedures specified in paragraphs (e)(2)(iii)(A), (B), (D), and (E) of this section shall be used to calculate parts per million by volume concentration.
units.action_summary: Use the specified procedures to calculate ppmv concentrations.

units.obligation_text: The calculated concentration shall be corrected to 3 percent oxygen using the procedures specified in paragraph (e)(2)(iii)(C) of this section if a combustion device is the control device and supplemental combustion air is used to combust the emissions.
units.action_summary: If combustion control device with supplemental air, correct calculated concentration to 3% oxygen using specified procedures.

units.obligation_text: The emission rate correction factor (or excess air), integrated sampling and analysis procedures of Method 3B of 40 CFR part 60, appendix A, or the manual method in ANSI/ASME PTC 19–10–1981—Part 10 (Incorporated by reference, see § 63.14)), shall be used to determine the oxygen concentration.
units.action_summary: Use Method 3B or ANSI/ASME PTC 19–10–1981 Part 10 procedures to determine oxygen concentration.

units.obligation_text: The sampling site shall be the same as that of the organic regulated material or organic compound samples, and the samples shall be taken during the same time that the organic regulated material or organic compound samples are taken.
units.action_summary: Take oxygen samples at same site and time as organic samples.

units.obligation_text: To measure the total organic regulated material concentration at the outlet of a control device, use Method 18 of 40 CFR part 60, appendix A, or ASTM D6420–18.
units.action_summary: Measure outlet total organic regulated material concentration using Method 18 or ASTM D6420–18.

units.obligation_text: If you have a combustion control device, you must first determine which regulated material compounds are present in the inlet gas stream using process knowledge or the screening procedure described in Method 18.
units.action_summary: For combustion control devices, determine inlet regulated compounds using process knowledge or Method 18 screening.

units.obligation_text: In conducting the performance test, analyze samples collected at the outlet of the combustion control device as specified in Method 18 or ASTM D6420–18 for the regulated material compounds present at the inlet of the control device.
units.action_summary: Analyze outlet samples per Method 18 or ASTM D6420–18 for compounds identified at inlet.

units.obligation_text: The method ASTM D6420–18 may be used only under the conditions specified in paragraphs (e)(2)(iii)(D)(1) through (3) of this section.
units.action_summary: ASTM D6420–18 permitted only under specified conditions.

units.obligation_text: If the target compounds are all known and are all listed in Section 1.1 of ASTM D6420–18 as measurable.
units.action_summary: Condition: ASTM D6420–18 usable if all target compounds are known and listed as measurable.

units.obligation_text: ASTM D6420–18 may not be used for methane and ethane.
units.action_summary: Prohibits using ASTM D6420–18 for methane and ethane.

units.obligation_text: ASTM D6420–18 may not be used as a total VOC method.
units.action_summary: Prohibits using ASTM D6420–18 as a total VOC method.

units.obligation_text: To determine compliance with a percent reduction requirement, the owner or operator shall use Method 18, 25, or 25A of 40 CFR part 60, appendix A, as applicable.
units.action_summary: Use Method 18, 25, or 25A to determine percent reduction compliance.

units.obligation_text: The method ASTM D6420–18 may be used in lieu of Method 18 of 40 CFR part 60, appendix A, under the conditions specified in paragraphs (e)(2)(iii)(D)(1) through (3) of this section.
units.action_summary: May use ASTM D6420–18 instead of Method 18 for percent reduction under specified conditions.

units.obligation_text: Alternatively, any other method or data that have been validated according to the applicable procedures in Method 301 of appendix A of 40 CFR part 63 may be used.
units.action_summary: May use other validated methods or data per Method 301 as an alternative for percent reduction.

units.obligation_text: The procedures specified in paragraphs (e)(2)(iv)(A) through (I) of this section shall be used to calculate percent reduction efficiency.
units.action_summary: Use the listed procedures to calculate percent reduction efficiency.

units.obligation_text: To measure inlet and outlet concentrations of total organic regulated material, use Method 18 of 40 CFR part 60, appendix A, or ASTM D6420–18, under the conditions specified in paragraphs (e)(2)(iii)(D)(1) through (3) of this section. In conducting the performance test, collect and analyze samples as specified in Method 18 or ASTM D6420–18.
units.action_summary: Measure inlet and outlet concentrations using Method 18 or ASTM D6420–18 and analyze samples per those methods.

units.obligation_text: You must collect samples simultaneously at the inlet and outlet of the control device.
units.action_summary: Collect inlet and outlet samples simultaneously during testing.

units.obligation_text: If the performance test is for a combustion control device, you must first determine which regulated material compounds are present in the inlet gas stream (i.e., uncontrolled emissions) using process knowledge or the screening procedure described in Method 18.
units.action_summary: For combustion control device tests, identify inlet regulated compounds using process knowledge or Method 18 screening.

units.obligation_text: Quantify the emissions for the regulated material compounds present in the inlet gas stream for both the inlet and outlet gas streams for the combustion device.
units.action_summary: Quantify emissions of identified regulated compounds at both inlet and outlet.

units.obligation_text: If the uncontrolled or inlet gas stream to the control device contains formaldehyde, you must conduct emissions testing according to paragraphs (e)(2)(iv)(I)(1) through (3) of this section.
units.action_summary: If inlet contains formaldehyde, conduct emissions testing per specified paragraphs.

units.obligation_text: Except as specified in paragraph (e)(2)(iv)(I)(3) of this section, if you elect to comply with a percent reduction requirement and formaldehyde is the principal regulated material compound (i.e., greater than 50 percent of the regulated material compounds in the stream by volume), you must use Method 316 or 320 of 40 CFR part 63, appendix A, to measure formaldehyde at the inlet and outlet of the control device. Use the percent reduction in formaldehyde as a surrogate for the percent reduction in total regulated material emissions.
units.action_summary: When formaldehyde >50% and complying with percent reduction, use Method 316 or 320 for inlet/outlet formaldehyde and use its percent reduction as surrogate.

units.obligation_text: Except as specified in paragraph (e)(2)(iv)(I)(3) of this section, if you elect to comply with an outlet total organic regulated material concentration or TOC concentration limit, and the uncontrolled or inlet gas stream to the control device contains greater than 10 percent (by volume) formaldehyde, you must use Method 316 or 320 of 40 CFR part 63, appendix A, to separately determine the formaldehyde concentration. Calculate the total organic regulated material concentration or TOC concentration by totaling the formaldehyde emissions measured using Method 316 or 320 and the other regulated material compound emissions measured using Method 18 or 25/25A.
units.action_summary: If inlet >10% formaldehyde and complying with outlet TOC limit, measure formaldehyde with Method 316/320 and sum with other compounds measured by Method 18/25/25A.

units.obligation_text: You may elect to use ASTM D6348–12e1 (Incorporated by reference, § 63.14) in lieu of Method 316 or 320 of 40 CFR part 63, appendix A as specified in paragraph (e)(2)(iv)(I)(1) or (2) of this section.
units.action_summary: May choose ASTM D6348–12e1 instead of Method 316/320 under specified situations.

units.obligation_text: To comply with this paragraph, the test plan preparation and implementation in the Annexes to ASTM D 6348–03 (Incorporated by reference, see § 63.14) Sections A1 through A8 are mandatory; the percent (%) R must be determined for each target analyte using Equation A5.5 of ASTM D6348–03 Annex A5 (Analyte Spiking Technique); and in order for the test data to be acceptable for a compound, the %R must be 70% ≥ R ≤ 130%.
units.action_summary: If using ASTM D6348–12e1, must follow Annexes A1–A8, determine %R per Equation A5.5, and ensure %R between 70% and 130% for acceptability.

units.obligation_text: If the %R value does not meet this criterion for a target compound, then the test data is not acceptable for that compound and the test must be repeated for that analyte (i.e., the sampling and/or analytical procedure should be adjusted before a retest).
units.action_summary: If %R is outside 70–130%, the test data for that compound is unacceptable and the test must be repeated after adjustments.

units.obligation_text: The %R value for each compound must be reported in the test report, and all field measurements must be corrected with the calculated %R value for that compound by using the following equation: Reported Results = (Measured Concentration in the Stack × 100)/%R.
units.action_summary: Report %R for each compound and correct field measurements by the given equation.

units.obligation_text: Except as specified in paragraphs (a) and (b) of this section, you must comply with the requirements of this subpart according to the schedule specified in § 63.1102(a).
units.action_summary: Comply with the subpart requirements according to schedule in §63.1102(a), unless (a) or (b) apply.

units.obligation_text: Each heat exchange system at an ethylene production affected source that commenced construction or reconstruction on or before October 9, 2019, must be in compliance with the heat exchange system requirements specified in § 63.1084(f), § 63.1085(e) and (f), § 63.1086(e), § 63.1087(c) and (d), § 63.1088(d), § 63.1089(d), and § 63.1089(d) upon initial startup or [date 3 years after date of publication of final rule in the Federal Register], whichever is later.
units.action_summary: Heat exchange systems constructed on or before Oct 9, 2019 must comply with listed heat exchange system provisions by initial startup or specified deadline, whichever is later.

units.obligation_text: Each heat exchange system at an ethylene production affected source that commences construction or reconstruction after October 9, 2019, must be in compliance with the heat exchange system requirements specified in §§ 63.1084(f), 63.1085(e) and (f), 63.1086(e), 63.1087(c) and (d), 63.1088(d), 63.1089(d), and 63.1089(d) upon initial startup, or [date of publication of final rule in the Federal Register], whichever is later.
units.action_summary: Heat exchange systems built after Oct 9, 2019 must comply with listed provisions upon initial startup or specified publication date, whichever is later.

units.obligation_text: Each waste stream at an ethylene production affected source that commenced construction or reconstruction on or before October 9, 2019, must be in compliance with the flare requirements specified in § 63.1095(a)(1)(vi) and (b)(3) upon initial startup or [date 3 years after date of publication of final rule in the Federal Register], whichever is later.
units.action_summary: Waste streams from sources constructed on/before Oct 9, 2019 must comply with specific flare requirements by initial startup or specified deadline.

units.obligation_text: Each waste stream at an ethylene production affected source that commences construction or reconstruction after October 9, 2019, must be in compliance with the flare requirements specified in § 63.1095(a)(1)(vi) and (b)(3) upon initial startup, or [date of publication of final rule in the Federal Register], whichever is later.
units.action_summary: Waste streams from sources constructed after Oct 9, 2019 must comply with specific flare requirements upon initial startup or publication date.

units.obligation_text: Except as specified in paragraph (f) of this section, your heat exchange system is exempt from the requirements in §§ 63.1085 and 63.1086 if it meets any one of the criteria in paragraphs (a) through (e) of this section.
units.action_summary: Heat exchange systems meeting any criteria (a)-(e) are exempt from §§63.1085 and 63.1086, unless (f) applies.

units.obligation_text: Beginning no later than the compliance dates specified in § 63.1081(a), your heat exchange system is no longer exempt from the requirements in §§ 63.1085 and 63.1086 if it meets the criteria in paragraphs (c) or (d) of this section; instead, your heat exchange system is exempt from the requirements in §§ 63.1085 and 63.1086 if it meets any one of the criteria in paragraphs (a), (b), or (e) of this section.
units.action_summary: Changes exemption criteria as of compliance date: systems meeting (c) or (d) lose exemption; systems meeting (a), (b), or (e) remain exempt.
units.modal_raw: is no longer exempt / is exempt

units.obligation_text: Unless you meet one of the requirements for exemptions in § 63.1084, you must meet the requirements in paragraphs (a) through (f) of this section.
units.action_summary: If not exempt per §63.1084, you must comply with requirements (a)-(f) of §63.1085.

units.obligation_text: Except as specified in paragraph (e) of this section, you must monitor the cooling water for the presence of substances that indicate a leak according to § 63.1086(a) through (d).
units.action_summary: Monitor cooling water for leak-indicating substances per §63.1086(a)-(d), unless paragraph (e) applies.

units.obligation_text: Except as specified in paragraph (f) of this section, if you detect a leak, then you must repair it according to § 63.1087(a) and (b) unless repair is delayed according to § 63.1088(a) through (c).
units.action_summary: If a leak is detected, repair per §63.1087(a)-(b) unless delay of repair provisions apply.

units.obligation_text: Beginning no later than the compliance dates specified in § 63.1081(a), the requirements specified in § 63.1086(a) through (d) no longer apply; instead, you must monitor the cooling water for the presence of total strippable hydrocarbon concentration (as methane) that indicate a leak according to § 63.1086(e). At any time before the compliance dates specified in § 63.1081(a), you may choose to comply with the requirements in this paragraph in lieu of the requirements in paragraph (a) of this section.
units.action_summary: As of compliance date, must monitor for total strippable hydrocarbons per §63.1086(e); before that date, may opt into this method in lieu of §63.1086(a)-(d).

units.obligation_text: Beginning no later than the compliance dates specified in § 63.1081(a), the requirements specified in § 63.1087(a) and (b), and § 63.1088(a) through (c), no longer apply; instead, if you detect a leak, then you must repair it according to § 63.1087(c) and (d), unless repair is delayed according to § 63.1088(d). At any time before the compliance dates specified in § 63.1081(a), you may choose to comply with the requirements in this paragraph in lieu of the requirements in paragraph (b) of this section.
units.action_summary: As of compliance date, follow repair requirements in §63.1087(c)-(d) and delay rules in §63.1088(d); before that date, may opt into this approach instead of §63.1087(a)-(b)/§63.1088(a)-(c).

units.obligation_text: Except as specified in § 63.1085(e) and paragraph (e) of this section, you must monitor for leaks to cooling water by monitoring each heat exchange system according to the requirements of paragraph (a) of this section, monitoring each heat exchanger according to the requirements of paragraph (b) of this section, or monitoring a surrogate parameter according to the requirements of paragraph (c) of this section. Except as specified in § 63.1085(e) and paragraph (e) of this section, if you elect to comply with the requirements of paragraph (a) or (b) of this section, you may use alternatives in paragraph (d)(1) or (2) of this section for determining the mean entrance concentration.
units.action_summary: Monitor for leaks by one of the specified methods (a),(b),(c); if choosing (a) or (b), may use alternatives in (d)(1) or (2) to determine mean entrance concentration.

units.obligation_text: Beginning no later than the compliance dates specified in § 63.1081(a), you must perform monitoring to identify leaks of total strippable hydrocarbon concentration (as methane) from each heat exchange system subject to the requirements of this subpart according to the procedures in paragraphs (e)(1) through (5) of this section.
units.action_summary: As of compliance date, perform monitoring for total strippable hydrocarbons per procedures (e)(1)-(5).

units.obligation_text: For each closed loop recirculating heat exchange system, you must collect and analyze a sample from the location(s) described in either paragraph (e)(1)(i) or (ii) of this section.
units.action_summary: For closed-loop systems, collect and analyze samples from specified monitoring locations (either option i or ii).

units.obligation_text: Each cooling tower return line or any representative riser within the cooling tower prior to exposure to air for each heat exchange system.
units.action_summary: Monitor at each cooling tower return line or representative riser prior to air exposure.

units.obligation_text: Selected heat exchanger exit line(s), so that each heat exchanger or group of heat exchangers within a heat exchange system is covered by the selected monitoring location(s).
units.action_summary: Or monitor at selected heat exchanger exit lines covering each exchanger or group.

units.obligation_text: For each once-through heat exchange system, you must collect and analyze a sample from the location(s) described in paragraph (e)(2)(i) of this section. You may also elect to collect and analyze an additional sample from the location(s) described in paragraph (e)(2)(ii) of this section.
units.action_summary: For once-through systems, must sample at specified exit locations; may also sample inlet water feed prior to any heat exchanger as additional sample.

units.obligation_text: Selected heat exchanger exit line(s), so that each heat exchanger or group of heat exchangers within a heat exchange system is covered by the selected monitoring location(s). The selected monitoring location may be at a point where discharges from multiple heat exchange systems are combined provided that the combined cooling water flow rate at the monitoring location does not exceed 40,000 gallons per minute.
units.action_summary: Monitor at selected exit lines; combined monitoring allowed if combined flow ≤ 40,000 gpm.

units.obligation_text: The inlet water feed line for a once-through heat exchange system prior to any heat exchanger. If multiple heat exchange systems use the same water feed (i.e., inlet water from the same primary water source), you may monitor at one representative location and use the monitoring results for that sampling location for all heat exchange systems that use that same water feed.
units.action_summary: May monitor inlet water feed prior to any exchanger; representative monitoring allowed for multiple systems sharing same feed.

units.obligation_text: You must determine the total strippable hydrocarbon concentration (in parts per million by volume (ppmv) as methane) at each monitoring location using the 'Air Stripping Method (Modified El Paso Method) for Determination of Volatile Organic Compound Emissions from Water Sources' (incorporated by reference, see § 63.14) using a flame ionization detector (FID) analyzer for on-site determination as described in Section 6.1 of the Modified El Paso Method.
units.action_summary: Determine total strippable hydrocarbon concentration as methane at each monitoring location using the Modified El Paso Method with FID per Section 6.1.

units.obligation_text: For each heat exchange system, you must comply with the applicable monitoring frequency and leak action level, as defined in paragraphs (e)(4)(i) through (iii) of this section.
units.action_summary: Comply with the specified monitoring frequencies and leak action levels per (e)(4)(i)-(iii).

units.obligation_text: For each heat exchange system at an ethylene production affected source that commenced construction or reconstruction on or before December 6, 2000, you must monitor quarterly using a leak action level defined as a total strippable hydrocarbon concentration (as methane) in the stripping gas of 6.2 ppmv. If a leak is detected as specified in paragraph (e)(5) of this section, then you must monitor monthly until the leak has been repaired according to the requirements in § 63.1087(c) or (d). Once the leak has been repaired according to the requirements in § 63.1087(c) or (d), quarterly monitoring for the heat exchange system may resume.
units.action_summary: Systems constructed on/before Dec 6, 2000: monitor quarterly at 6.2 ppmv action level; if leak detected, monitor monthly until repaired; resume quarterly after repair.

units.obligation_text: If you have completed the initial weekly monitoring for 6-months of the heat exchange system as specified in § 63.1086(a)(2)(ii) or (b)(1)(ii) then you must monitor monthly. If a leak is detected as specified in paragraph (e)(5) of this section, then you must monitor weekly until the leak has been repaired according to the requirements in § 63.1087(c) or (d). Once the leak has been repaired according to the requirements in § 63.1087(c) or (d), monthly monitoring for the heat exchange system may resume.
units.action_summary: For systems with completed initial weekly monitoring for 6 months: monitor monthly thereafter; if leak detected, monitor weekly until repaired, then resume monthly.

units.obligation_text: If you have not completed the initial weekly monitoring for 6-months of the heat exchange system as specified in § 63.1086(a)(2)(ii) or (b)(1)(ii), or if you elect to comply with paragraph (e) of this section rather than paragraphs (a) through (d) of this section upon startup, then you must initially monitor weekly for 6-months beginning upon startup and monitor monthly thereafter. If a leak is detected as specified in paragraph (e)(5) of this section, then you must monitor weekly until the leak has been repaired according to the requirements in § 63.1087(c) or (d). Once the leak has been repaired according to the requirements in § 63.1087(c) or (d), monthly monitoring for the heat exchange system may resume.
units.action_summary: If initial weekly monitoring hasn't been completed or if electing paragraph (e) at startup: monitor weekly for first 6 months, then monthly; if leak detected, monitor weekly until repaired; then monthly.

units.obligation_text: For each heat exchange system at an ethylene production affected source that commences construction or reconstruction after October 9, 2019, you must initially monitor weekly for 6-months beginning upon startup and monitor monthly thereafter using a leak action level defined as a total strippable hydrocarbon concentration (as methane) in the stripping gas of 6.2 ppmv. If a leak is detected as specified in paragraph (e)(5) of this section, then you must monitor weekly until the leak has been repaired according to the requirements in § 63.1087(c) or (d). Once the leak has been repaired according to the requirements in § 63.1087(c) or (d), monthly monitoring for the heat exchange system may resume.
units.action_summary: Systems commencing after Oct 9, 2019: monitor weekly for first 6 months upon startup then monthly, with 6.2 ppmv action level; if leak detected, monitor weekly until repaired.

units.obligation_text: For once-through heat exchange systems for which the inlet water feed is monitored as described in paragraph (e)(2)(ii) of this section, a leak is detected if the difference in the measurement value of the sample taken from a location specified in paragraph (e)(2)(i) of this section and the measurement value of the corresponding sample taken from the location specified in paragraph (e)(2)(ii) of this section equals or exceeds the leak action level.
units.action_summary: For once-through systems with inlet monitoring, a leak is detected when the difference between exit and inlet sample values ≥ leak action level.

units.obligation_text: For all other heat exchange systems, a leak is detected if a measurement value of the sample taken from a location specified in paragraph (e)(1)(i), (ii), or (e)(2)(i) of this section equals or exceeds the leak action level.
units.action_summary: For other systems, a leak is detected if a sample measurement at specified locations ≥ leak action level.

units.obligation_text: Except as specified in § 63.1085(f) and paragraphs (c) and (d) of this section, if a leak is detected, you must comply with the requirements in paragraphs (a) and (b) of this section unless repair is delayed according to § 63.1088.
units.action_summary: If a leak is detected, comply with §63.1087(a)-(b) unless repair is delayed per §63.1088 or unless (c) or (d) apply.

units.obligation_text: Beginning no later than the compliance dates specified in § 63.1081(a), if a leak is detected using the methods described in § 63.1086(e), you must repair the leak to reduce the measured concentration to below the applicable leak action level as soon as practicable, but no later than 45 days after identifying the leak, except as specified in § 63.1088(d).
units.action_summary: If leak detected using §63.1086(e) methods, repair to below leak action level as soon as practicable and no later than 45 days after identification, unless §63.1088(d) applies.

units.obligation_text: Repair must include re-monitoring at the monitoring location where the leak was identified according to the method specified in § 63.1086(e)(3) to verify that the measured total strippable hydrocarbon concentration is below the applicable leak action level.
units.action_summary: After repair, re-monitor at the original monitoring location per §63.1086(e)(3) to verify concentration is below action level.

units.obligation_text: Repair may also include performing the additional monitoring in paragraph (d) of this section to verify that the total strippable hydrocarbon concentration is below the applicable leak action level.
units.action_summary: May perform additional monitoring per paragraph (d) to verify repair effectiveness.

units.obligation_text: Physical modifications to the leaking heat exchanger, such as welding the leak or replacing a tube;
units.action_summary: May repair by physical modifications like welding or tube replacement.

units.obligation_text: Blocking the leaking tube within the heat exchanger;
units.action_summary: May repair by blocking the leaking tube.

units.obligation_text: Changing the pressure so that water flows into the process fluid;
units.action_summary: May change pressures so water flows into process to address leak.

units.obligation_text: Replacing the heat exchanger or heat exchanger bundle;
units.action_summary: May replace the heat exchanger or bundle to repair the leak.

units.obligation_text: Isolating, bypassing, or otherwise removing the leaking heat exchanger from service until it is otherwise repaired.
units.action_summary: May isolate, bypass, or remove leaking exchanger from service until repaired.

units.obligation_text: Beginning no later than the compliance dates specified in § 63.1081(a), if you detect a leak when monitoring a cooling tower return line according to § 63.1086(e)(1)(i), you may conduct additional monitoring of each heat exchanger or group of heat exchangers associated with the heat exchange system for which the leak was detected, as provided in § 63.1086(e)(1)(ii). If no leaks are detected when monitoring according to the requirements of § 63.1086(e)(1)(ii), the heat exchange system is considered to have met the repair requirements through re-monitoring of the heat exchange system, as provided in paragraph (c) of this section.
units.action_summary: If a leak is detected at a cooling tower return line, may do additional monitoring of associated exchangers; if no leaks found then re-monitoring satisfies repair requirement.

units.obligation_text: You may delay the repair of heat exchange systems if the leaking equipment is isolated from the process. At any time before the compliance dates specified in § 63.1081(a), you may also delay repair if repair is technically infeasible without a shutdown, and you meet one of the conditions in paragraphs (a) through (c) of this section. Beginning no later than the compliance dates specified in § 63.1081(a), paragraphs (a) through (c) of this section no longer apply; instead, you may delay repair if the conditions in paragraph (d) of this section are met.
units.action_summary: May delay repair under specified conditions (isolated equipment; infeasibility; or paragraph (d) conditions after compliance date).

units.obligation_text: Beginning no later than the compliance dates specified in § 63.1081(a), you may delay repair when one of the conditions in paragraph (d)(1) or (2) of this section is met and the leak is less than the delay of repair action level specified in paragraph (d)(3) of this section. You must determine if a delay of repair is necessary as soon as practicable, but no later than 45 days after first identifying the leak.
units.action_summary: May delay repair under (d)(1) or (2) if leak is below delay action level; must determine need for delay within 45 days of identifying leak.

units.obligation_text: If the repair is technically infeasible without a shutdown and the total strippable hydrocarbon concentration is initially and remains less than the delay of repair action level for all monitoring periods during the delay of repair, then you may delay repair until the next scheduled shutdown of the heat exchange system. If, during subsequent monitoring, the delay of repair action level is exceeded, then you must repair the leak within 30 days of the monitoring event in which the leak was equal to or exceeded the delay of repair action level.
units.action_summary: If repair infeasible without shutdown and concentration remains below delay action level, may delay until next scheduled shutdown; if level later exceeded, must repair within 30 days of that monitoring event.

units.obligation_text: If the necessary equipment, parts, or personnel are not available and the total strippable hydrocarbon concentration is initially and remains less than the delay of repair action level for all monitoring periods during the delay of repair, then you may delay the repair for a maximum of 120 calendar days. You must demonstrate that the necessary equipment, parts, or personnel were not available. If, during subsequent monitoring, the delay of repair action level is exceeded, then you must repair the leak within 30 days of the monitoring event in which the leak was equal to or exceeded the delay of repair action level.
units.action_summary: If parts/equipment/personnel unavailable and concentration remains below delay level, may delay repair up to 120 days and must demonstrate unavailability; if level exceeded later, must repair within 30 days.

units.obligation_text: The delay of repair action level is a total strippable hydrocarbon concentration (as methane) in the stripping gas of 62 ppmv. The delay of repair action level is assessed as described in paragraph (d)(3)(i) or (ii) of this section, as applicable.
units.action_summary: Defines delay of repair action level as 62 ppmv and states assessment methods in (i) and (ii).

units.obligation_text: For once-through heat exchange systems for which the inlet water feed is monitored as described in § 63.1086(e)(2)(ii), the delay of repair action level is exceeded if the difference in the measurement value of the sample taken from a location specified in § 63.1086(e)(2)(i) and the measurement value of the corresponding sample taken from the location specified in § 63.1086(e)(2)(ii) equals or exceeds the delay of repair action level.
units.action_summary: For once-through with inlet monitoring, the delay action level is exceeded when exit minus inlet sample difference ≥ 62 ppmv.

units.obligation_text: For all other heat exchange systems, the delay of repair action level is exceeded if a measurement value of the sample taken from a location specified in § 63.1086(e)(1)(i) and (ii) or § 63.1086(e)(2)(i) equals or exceeds the delay of repair action level.
units.action_summary: For other systems, delay action level is exceeded when a sample measurement at specified locations ≥ 62 ppmv.

units.obligation_text: At any time before the compliance dates specified in § 63.1081(a), you must keep documentation of delay of repair as specified in § 63.1088(a) through (c). Beginning no later than the compliance dates specified in § 63.1081(a), the requirement to keep documentation of delay of repair as specified in § 63.1088(a) through (c) no longer applies; instead, you must keep documentation of delay of repair as specified in paragraphs (d)(1) through (4) of this section.
units.action_summary: Keep documentation of delay of repair per §63.1088(a)-(c) before compliance date; as of compliance date, keep documentation per §63.1089(d)(1)-(4).

units.obligation_text: The reason(s) for delaying repair.
units.action_summary: Record the reasons for delaying repair.

units.obligation_text: A schedule for completing the repair as soon as practical.
units.action_summary: Record a schedule for completing the repair as soon as practical.

units.obligation_text: The date and concentration of the leak as first identified and the results of all subsequent monitoring events during the delay of repair.
units.action_summary: Record date and concentration when leak first identified and results of subsequent monitoring during delay.

units.obligation_text: An estimate of the potential strippable hydrocarbon emissions from the leaking heat exchange system or heat exchanger for each required delay of repair monitoring interval following the procedures in paragraphs (d)(4)(i) through (iv) of this section.
units.action_summary: Estimate potential strippable hydrocarbon emissions for each delay monitoring interval following specified procedures.

units.obligation_text: Determine the leak concentration as specified in § 63.1086(e) and convert the stripping gas leak concentration (in ppmv as methane) to an equivalent liquid concentration, in parts per million by weight (ppmw), using equation 7–1 from 'Air Stripping Method (Modified El Paso Method) for Determination of Volatile Organic Compound Emissions from Water Sources' and the molecular weight of 16 grams per mole (g/mol) for methane.
units.action_summary: Determine leak concentration per §63.1086(e) and convert ppmv methane to ppmw using specified equation and molecular weight.

units.obligation_text: Determine the mass flow rate of the cooling water at the monitoring location where the leak was detected. ... Volumetric flow measurements may be used and converted to mass flow rates using the density of water at the specific monitoring location temperature or using the default density of water at 25 degrees Celsius, which is 997 kilograms per cubic meter or 8.32 pounds per gallon.
units.action_summary: Determine cooling water mass flow rate at the monitoring location, using permitted measurement or conversion methods.

units.obligation_text: For delay of repair monitoring intervals prior to repair of the leak, calculate the potential strippable hydrocarbon emissions for the leaking heat exchange system or heat exchanger for the monitoring interval by multiplying the leak concentration in the cooling water, ppmw, determined in (d)(4)(i) of this section, by the mass flow rate of the cooling water determined in (d)(4)(ii) of this section and by the duration of the delay of repair monitoring interval.
units.action_summary: Calculate potential emissions for each pre-repair interval by multiplying ppmw concentration × mass flow rate × duration.

units.obligation_text: For delay of repair monitoring intervals ending with a repaired leak, calculate the potential strippable hydrocarbon emissions for the leaking heat exchange system or heat exchanger for the final delay of repair monitoring interval by multiplying the duration of the final delay of repair monitoring interval by the leak concentration and cooling water flow rates determined for the last monitoring event prior to the re-monitoring event used to verify the leak was repaired.
units.action_summary: For final interval ending with repair, calculate emissions by duration × leak concentration × cooling water flow rates from last pre-repair monitoring event.

units.obligation_text: At any time before the compliance dates specified in § 63.1081(a), if you validate a 40 CFR part 136 method for the HAP listed in Table 1 to this subpart according to the procedures in appendix D to this part, then you must keep a record of the test data and calculations used in the validation. On the compliance dates specified in § 63.1081(a), this requirement no longer applies.
units.action_summary: If you validate a 40 CFR part 136 method for listed HAP before compliance date, you must keep the test data and calculations; requirement ends on compliance date.

units.obligation_text: If you delay repair for your heat exchange system, you must report the delay of repair in the semiannual report required by § 63.1110(e). If the leak remains unrepaired, you must continue to report the delay of repair in semiannual reports until you repair the leak. Except as provided in paragraph (f) of this section, you must include the information in paragraphs (a) through (e) of this section in the semiannual report.
units.action_summary: Report any delayed repair in semiannual reports per §63.1110(e) and continue reporting until repair; include information (a)-(e) unless (f) applies.

units.obligation_text: For heat exchange systems subject to § 63.1085(e) and (f), Periodic Reports must include the information specified in paragraphs (f)(1) through (5) of this section, in lieu of the information specified in paragraphs (a) through (e) of this section.
units.action_summary: For systems subject to §63.1085(e) and (f), periodic reports must include specified information (f)(1)-(5) instead of (a)-(e).

units.obligation_text: The number of heat exchange systems at the plant site subject to the monitoring requirements in § 63.1085(e) and (f).
units.action_summary: Report the number of heat exchange systems subject to §63.1085(e) and (f).

units.obligation_text: The number of heat exchange systems at the plant site found to be leaking.
units.action_summary: Report the number of heat exchange systems found leaking.

units.obligation_text: For each monitoring location where the total strippable hydrocarbon concentration was determined to be equal to or greater than the applicable leak definitions specified in § 63.1086(e)(5), identification of the monitoring location (e.g., unique monitoring location or heat exchange system ID number), the measured total strippable hydrocarbon concentration, the date the leak was first identified, and, if applicable, the date the source of the leak was identified;
units.action_summary: For each monitoring location meeting leak definitions, report location ID, measured concentration, date first identified, and date source identified if applicable.

units.obligation_text: For leaks that were repaired during the reporting period (including delayed repairs), identification of the monitoring location associated with the repaired leak, the total strippable hydrocarbon concentration measured during re-monitoring to verify repair, and the re-monitoring date (i.e., the effective date of repair); and
units.action_summary: For leaks repaired during reporting period, report monitoring location, concentration measured during re-monitoring, and re-monitoring date.

units.obligation_text: For each delayed repair, identification of the monitoring location associated with the leak for which repair is delayed, the date when the delay of repair began, the date the repair is expected to be completed (if the leak is not repaired during the reporting period), the total strippable hydrocarbon concentration and date of each monitoring event conducted on the ...
units.action_summary: For each delayed repair, report monitoring location, date delay began, expected completion date (if not repaired), and concentration and date of each monitoring event during delay.

title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Generic Maximum Achievable Control Technology Standards Residual Risk and Technology Review for Ethylene Production

units.obligation_text: Under the general safety zone regulations in subpart C of this part, you may not enter the safety zone described in paragraph (a) of this section unless authorized by the COTP or the COTP’s designated representative.
units.action_summary: Prohibits entering the safety zone unless authorized by the Captain of the Port or designated representative.

units.obligation_text: All vessels underway within this safety zone at the time it is activated are to depart the zone.
units.actor: all vessels underway within the safety zone
units.action_summary: Requires vessels underway inside the zone at activation to depart the zone.

units.obligation_text: To seek permission to enter, contact the COTP or the COTP’s designated representative by telephone at 410–576–2693 or on Marine Band Radio VHF–FM channel 16 (156.8 MHz).
units.actor: persons seeking permission to enter the safety zone
units.action_summary: Requires those seeking permission to enter the zone to contact the Captain of the Port or designated representative by the specified phone number or radio channel.

units.obligation_text: The Coast Guard vessels enforcing this section can be contacted on Marine Band Radio VHF–FM channel 16 (156.8 MHz).
units.actor: the public/persons seeking to contact enforcement vessels
units.action_summary: Permits/contact information indicating the Coast Guard enforcing vessels are reachable on VHF–FM channel 16.

units.obligation_text: Those in the safety zone must comply with all lawful orders or directions given to them by the COTP or the COTP’s designated representative.
units.action_summary: Requires persons/vessels in the safety zone to comply with lawful orders or directions from the Captain of the Port or designated representative.

units.obligation_text: The U.S. Coast Guard may be assisted in the patrol and enforcement of the safety zone by Federal, State, and local agencies.
units.action_summary: Permits the Coast Guard to be assisted by Federal, State, and local agencies in patrolling and enforcing the safety zone.

units.obligation_text: This safety zone will be enforced during the periods described in paragraph (f) of this section.
units.action_summary: States that the safety zone will be enforced during specified periods.

units.obligation_text: A "FIREWORKS—DANGER—STAY AWAY" sign will be posted on the port and starboard sides of the barge on-scene near the location described in paragraph (a) of this section.
units.actor: on-scene personnel (e.g., Coast Guard/on-scene barge personnel)
units.action_summary: Requires posting a 'FIREWORKS—DANGER—STAY AWAY' sign on both sides of the on-scene barge near the specified location.

units.obligation_text: This section will be enforced from 11:00 p.m. on December 31, 2019 to 1:00 a.m. on January 1, 2020.
units.action_summary: Specifies the time period during which the safety zone will be enforced.

title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Asphalt Processing and Asphalt Roofing Manufacturing Residual Risk and Technology Review

units.obligation_text: You are subject to this subpart if you own or operate an asphalt processing facility or an asphalt roofing manufacturing facility, as defined in § 63.8698, that is a major source as defined in § 63.2, or is located at, or is part of a major source as defined in § 63.2.
units.actor: owner or operator of an asphalt processing facility or asphalt roofing manufacturing facility
units.action_summary: Establishes which facilities are covered by the subpart (those that are or are part of a major source).

units.obligation_text: You must meet the notification requirements in § 63.8692 according to the schedules in §§ 63.8692 and 63.9(a) through (f) and (h).
units.action_summary: Submit required notifications according to the listed schedules.

units.obligation_text: Before [DATE 181 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE Federal Register], you must be in compliance with the emission limitations (including operating limits) in this subpart at all times, except during periods of startup, shutdown, and malfunction. On and after [DATE 181 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE Federal Register], you must be in compliance with the emission limitations (including operating limits) in this subpart at all times, except during periods of nonoperation of the affected source (or specific portion thereof) resulting in cessation of the emissions to which this subpart applies.
units.action_summary: Maintain continuous compliance with emission and operating limits, with specified exceptions that differ before and after the stated date.

units.obligation_text: Exception: Before [DATE ...], compliance need not be maintained during periods of startup, shutdown, and malfunction.
units.action_summary: Before the specified date, startup/shutdown/malfunction periods are exceptions to continuous compliance.

units.obligation_text: Exception: On and after [DATE ...], compliance exceptions apply only during periods of nonoperation of the affected source resulting in cessation of the emissions to which this subpart applies.
units.action_summary: After the specified date, only periods when the affected source is nonoperational (and emissions have ceased) are exceptions to compliance.

units.obligation_text: Before [DATE ...], you must always operate and maintain your affected source, including air pollution control and monitoring equipment, according to the provisions in § 63.6(e)(1)(i).
units.action_summary: Prior to the specified date, operate and maintain the affected source per §63.6(e)(1)(i).

units.obligation_text: On and after [DATE ...], at all times, you must operate and maintain any affected source, including associated air pollution control equipment and monitoring equipment, in a manner consistent with safety and good air pollution control practices for minimizing emissions.
units.action_summary: After the specified date, operate and maintain affected sources consistent with safety and good pollution-control practices to minimize emissions.

units.obligation_text: The general duty to minimize emissions does not require you to make any further efforts to reduce emissions if levels required by the applicable standard have been achieved.
units.action_summary: You are not required to take extra measures beyond what the applicable standard already requires.

units.obligation_text: Before [DATE ...], you must develop a written startup, shutdown, and malfunction plan (SSMP) according to the provisions in § 63.6(e)(3).
units.action_summary: Prepare a written SSMP in accordance with §63.6(e)(3) before the specified date.

units.obligation_text: On and after [DATE ...], a startup, shutdown, and malfunction plan is not required.
units.action_summary: After the specified date, the SSMP requirement is removed.

units.obligation_text: For existing affected sources, you must conduct initial performance tests no later than 180 days after the compliance date that is specified for your source in § 63.8683 and according to the provisions in § 63.7(a)(2).
units.action_summary: Existing affected sources must perform initial performance tests within 180 days after their compliance date following §63.7(a)(2).

units.obligation_text: As an alternative to the requirement specified in paragraph (a) of this section, you may use the results of a previously-conducted emission test to demonstrate compliance with the emission limitations in this subpart if you demonstrate to the Administrator’s satisfaction that: ...
units.action_summary: You may use a prior emission test to demonstrate compliance instead of conducting a new initial test if you meet Administrator-approved conditions.

units.obligation_text: The control device and process parameter values established during the previously-conducted emission test are used to demonstrate continuous compliance with this subpart;
units.action_summary: Condition of the alternative: prior test's control device and process parameters must be used to demonstrate continuous compliance.

units.obligation_text: The previously-conducted emission test was completed within the last 5 years.
units.action_summary: Condition of the alternative: the prior test must have been completed within 5 years.

units.obligation_text: Each performance test must be conducted under normal operating conditions and under the conditions specified in Table 3 to this subpart.
units.action_summary: Performance tests must be run under normal operations and per conditions in Table 3.

units.obligation_text: Operations during periods of startup, shutdown, or nonoperation do not constitute representative conditions for purposes of conducting a performance test.
units.action_summary: Startup, shutdown, and nonoperation are not representative for performance testing.

units.obligation_text: You may not conduct performance tests during periods of malfunction.
units.action_summary: Performance tests are prohibited during malfunctions.

units.obligation_text: You must record the process information that is necessary to document operating conditions during the test and explain why the conditions represent normal operation.
units.action_summary: Record and document operating conditions during performance tests and justify representativeness.

units.obligation_text: Upon request, you must make available to the Administrator such records as may be necessary to determine the conditions of performance tests.
units.action_summary: Provide test records to the Administrator on request to verify test conditions.

units.obligation_text: As an option to installing the CPMS specified in paragraph (a) of this section, you may install a continuous emissions monitoring system (CEMS) or a continuous opacity monitoring system (COMS) that meets the applicable requirements in § 63.8 according to Table 7 to this subpart and the applicable performance specifications of 40 CFR part 60, appendix B.
units.action_summary: You may choose to install a CEMS or COMS instead of the specified CPMS if it meets referenced requirements.

units.obligation_text: In your site-specific monitoring plan, you must also address the following:
units.action_summary: Require specific topics to be addressed in the site-specific monitoring plan.

units.obligation_text: Ongoing operation and maintenance procedures in accordance with the general requirements of § 63.8(c)(1)(ii), (c)(3), (c)(4)(ii), (c)(7), and (c)(8);
units.action_summary: Include ongoing O&M procedures per specified §63.8 provisions in the monitoring plan.

units.obligation_text: Ongoing data quality assurance procedures in accordance with the general requirements of § 63.8(d);
units.action_summary: Include ongoing data quality assurance procedures per §63.8(d) in the monitoring plan.

units.obligation_text: Ongoing recordkeeping and reporting procedures in accordance with §§ 63.8693, 63.8694, and the general requirements of § 63.10(e)(1) and (e)(2)(i).
units.action_summary: Include recordkeeping and reporting procedures consistent with referenced sections in the monitoring plan.

units.obligation_text: Except as specified in paragraph (d) of this section, you must establish each site-specific operating limit in Table 2 to this subpart that applies to you according to the requirements in § 63.8687 and Table 3 to this subpart.
units.action_summary: Establish site-specific operating limits in Table 2 per the referenced procedures, unless paragraph (d) allows an alternative.
