units.obligation_text: For control devices used to comply with the particulate matter standards, you may establish the pressure drop across the control device operating limit using manufacturers’ specifications in lieu of complying with paragraph (b) of this section.
units.action_summary: You may use manufacturer specifications to set pressure drop operating limits for PM control devices as an alternative to paragraph (b).

units.obligation_text: Before [DATE ...], except for monitor malfunctions, associated repairs, and required quality assurance or control activities (including, as applicable, calibration checks and required zero and span adjustments), you must monitor continuously (or collect data at all required intervals) at all times that the affected source is operating including periods of startup, shutdown, and malfunction when the affected source is operating.
units.action_summary: Prior to the specified date, continuously monitor or collect required data whenever the affected source is operating, with limited exceptions for monitor malfunctions and maintenance.

units.obligation_text: Exception: Before [DATE ...], monitoring need not be continuous during monitor malfunctions, associated repairs, and required quality assurance or control activities.
units.action_summary: Before the specified date, monitor malfunctions and certain maintenance activities are exceptions to continuous monitoring.

units.obligation_text: On and after [DATE ...], you must monitor and collect data at all times in accordance with § 63.8685(b), except during periods of nonoperation of the affected source (or specific portion thereof) resulting in cessation of the emissions to which this subpart applies.
units.action_summary: After the specified date, monitor and collect data per §63.8685(b), with exception for periods when the source is nonoperational and emissions have ceased.

units.obligation_text: You must demonstrate continuous compliance with each operating limit in Table 2 to this subpart that applies to you according to the procedures specified in Table 5 to this subpart, and you must conduct performance tests as specified in paragraph (e) of this section.
units.action_summary: Demonstrate continuous compliance with applicable operating limits per Table 5 and conduct periodic performance tests as required by paragraph (e).

units.obligation_text: Before [DATE ...], you must report each instance in which you did not meet each operating limit in Table 5 to this subpart that applies to you. ... On and after [DATE ...], you must report each instance in which you did not meet each operating limit in Table 5 to this subpart that applies to you, except during periods of nonoperation of the affected source (or specific portion thereof) resulting in cessation of the emissions to which this subpart applies.
units.action_summary: Report all instances of noncompliance with operating limits, with temporal exception for nonoperation after the specified date.

units.obligation_text: Before [DATE ...], deviations that occur during a period of startup, shutdown, or malfunction are not violations if you demonstrate to the Administrator’s satisfaction that you were operating in accordance with § 63.6(e)(1). The Administrator will determine whether deviations that occur during a period of startup, shutdown, or malfunction are violations, according to the provisions in § 63.6(e). On and after [date ...], this paragraph no longer applies.
units.action_summary: Prior to the specified date, deviations during startup/shutdown/malfunction may not be violations if you can demonstrate compliance with §63.6(e)(1); the Administrator decides. After the specified date this exception no longer applies.
units.modal_raw: are not violations if / will determine

units.obligation_text: For each control device used to comply with the PM, THC, opacity, or visible emission standards of this subpart, you must conduct periodic performance tests using the applicable procedures specified in § 63.8687 and Table 4 to this subpart to demonstrate compliance with § 63.8684(a), and to confirm or reestablish the operating limits required by § 63.8684(b). You must conduct periodic performance tests according to the schedule specified in paragraphs (e)(1) through (3) of this section.
units.action_summary: Conduct periodic performance tests for each relevant control device per referenced procedures and schedules to demonstrate compliance and (re)establish operating limits.

units.obligation_text: For each existing affected source, and for each new and reconstructed affected source that commences construction or reconstruction after November 21, 2001 and on or before [DATE ...], you must conduct the first periodic performance test on or before [DATE 3 YEARS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE Federal Register] and conduct subsequent periodic performance tests no later than 60 months thereafter following the previous performance test.
units.action_summary: Existing and certain new/reconstructed sources must conduct first periodic test by specified date and then every 60 months.

units.obligation_text: For each new and reconstructed affected source that commences construction or reconstruction after [DATE ...], you must conduct the first periodic performance no later than 60 months following the initial performance test required by § 63.8689 and conduct subsequent periodic performance tests no later than 60 months thereafter following the previous performance test. If you used the alternative compliance option specified in § 63.8686(b) to comply with the initial performance test, then you must conduct the first periodic performance no later than 60 months following the date you demonstrated to the Administrator that the requirements of § 63.8686(b) had been met.
units.action_summary: New/reconstructed sources post-publication must conduct first periodic test within 60 months after initial test (or 60 months after demonstrating alternative compliance), and every 60 months thereafter.

units.obligation_text: If an affected source is not operating on the dates the periodic performance test is required to be conducted as specified in paragraph (e)(1) or (2) of this section, then you are not required to restart the affected source for the sole purpose of complying with paragraph (e)(1) or (2) of this section. Instead, upon restart of the affected source, you must conduct the first periodic performance test within 60 days of achieving normal operating conditions but no later than 180 days from startup. You must conduct subsequent periodic performance tests no later than 60 months thereafter following the previous performance test.
units.action_summary: If the source isn't operating on the scheduled test date, you don't have to restart just to test; instead test within 60 days of normal operations (no later than 180 days), and then every 60 months.

units.obligation_text: You must submit all the notifications in §§ 63.6(h)(4) and (5), 63.7(b) and (c), 63.8(f), and 63.9(b) through (f) and (h) that apply to you by the dates specified.
units.action_summary: Submit all applicable notifications listed in the referenced sections by their specified deadlines.

units.obligation_text: If you are required to conduct a performance test, design evaluation, opacity observation, visible emission observation, or other compliance demonstration as specified in Table 3 or 4 to this subpart, you must submit a Notification of Compliance Status according to § 63.9(h)(2)(ii). You must submit the Notification of Compliance Status, including the performance test results, before the close of business on the 60th calendar day following the completion of the performance test according to § 63.10(d)(2).
units.action_summary: If required to perform specified compliance demonstrations, submit a Notification of Compliance Status including test results within 60 days after test completion.

units.obligation_text: On and after [DATE ...], you must submit all subsequent Notification of Compliance Status reports to EPA via the Compliance and Emissions Data Reporting Interface (CEDRI), which can be accessed through EPA’s Central Data Exchange (CDX).
units.action_summary: After the specified date, submit subsequent Notifications of Compliance Status electronically via CEDRI/CDX.

units.obligation_text: If you claim some of the information required to be submitted via CEDRI is confidential business information (CBI), then submit a complete report, including information claimed to be CBI, to EPA. Submit the file on a compact disc, flash drive, or other commonly used electronic storage medium and clearly mark the medium as CBI. Mail the electronic medium to U.S. EPA/OAQPS/CORE CBI Office ... The same file with the CBI omitted must be submitted to EPA via EPA’s CDX as described earlier in this paragraph.
units.action_summary: If claiming CBI, submit a complete CBI-including report to EPA on physical media and submit the redacted file via CDX.

units.obligation_text: You may assert a claim of EPA system outage or force majeure for failure to timely comply with this reporting requirement provided you meet the requirements outlined in §§ 63.8693(h) or (i), as applicable.
units.action_summary: You may claim EPA system outage or force majeure to excuse late reporting if you satisfy the conditions in §63.8693(h) or (i).

units.obligation_text: If you are using data from a previously-conducted emission test to serve as documentation of conformance with the emission standards and operating limits of this subpart as specified in § 63.8686(b), you must submit the test data in lieu of the initial performance test results with the Notification of Compliance Status required under paragraph (e) of this section.
units.action_summary: If relying on prior test data per §63.8686(b), submit that data with the Notification of Compliance Status instead of initial test results.

units.obligation_text: On and after [DATE ...], you must submit all compliance reports to EPA via the CEDRI, which can be accessed through EPA’s CDX. You must use the appropriate electronic report template on the CEDRI website for this subpart.
units.action_summary: After the specified date, submit compliance reports electronically via CEDRI using the appropriate templates.

units.obligation_text: If you claim some of the information required to be submitted via CEDRI is CBI, submit a complete report, including information claimed to be CBI, to EPA. The report must be generated using the appropriate form on the CEDRI website or an alternate electronic file consistent with the XML schema ... Submit the file on a compact disc, flash drive, or other commonly used electronic storage medium and clearly mark the medium as CBI. Mail the electronic medium to U.S. EPA/OAQPS/CORE CBI Office ... The same file with the CBI omitted must be submitted to EPA via EPA’s CDX as described earlier in this paragraph.
units.action_summary: If claiming CBI for electronically submitted reports, submit full CBI-containing file to EPA on physical media and a redacted file via CDX in the specified formats.

units.obligation_text: Before [DATE ...], if you had a startup, shutdown or malfunction during the reporting period and you took actions consistent with your SSMP, the compliance report must include the information in § 63.10(d)(5)(i). On and after [DATE ...], this paragraph no longer applies.
units.action_summary: Prior to the specified date, include SSMP-related information per §63.10(d)(5)(i) in reports if relevant; after the date this requirement ends.

units.obligation_text: For each reporting period, you must include in the compliance report the total number of deviations that occurred during the reporting period. If there are no deviations ... then you must include a statement that there were no deviations from the emission limitations during the reporting period.
units.action_summary: Include the total number of deviations (or a statement of none) for each reporting period.

units.obligation_text: The start date, start time, and duration of each malfunction.
units.action_summary: Report the start date, time, and duration for each malfunction in the compliance report.

units.obligation_text: For each instance that the CPMS, CEMS, or COMS was inoperative, except for zero (low-level) and high-level checks, the start date, start time, and duration that the CPMS, CEMS, or COMS was inoperative; the cause (including unknown cause) for the CPMS, CEMS, or COMS being inoperative; and descriptions of corrective actions taken.
units.action_summary: Report dates, durations, causes, and corrective actions for instances of monitor inoperability (excluding certain checks).

units.obligation_text: For each instance that the CPMS, CEMS, or COMS was out-of-control as specified in § 63.8(c)(7), the start date, start time, and duration that the CPMS, CEMS, or COMS was out-of-control, including the information in § 63.8(c)(8).
units.action_summary: Report dates, durations, and required details for monitor out-of-control events as specified.

units.obligation_text: On and after [DATE ...], the start date, start time, and duration of the deviation including a description of the deviation and the actions you took to minimize emissions in accordance with § 63.8685(b). You must also include: (i) A list of the affected sources or equipment for which the deviation occurred; (ii) The cause of the deviation (including unknown cause, if applicable); and (iii) Any corrective actions taken to return the affected unit to its normal or usual manner of operation.
units.action_summary: After the specified date, report start date/time/duration for deviations plus description, emission-minimizing actions, list of affected equipment, cause, and corrective actions.

units.obligation_text: A list of the affected sources or equipment for which the deviation occurred;
units.action_summary: Include a list of affected sources/equipment for each deviation.

units.obligation_text: The cause of the deviation (including unknown cause, if applicable);
units.action_summary: Include the cause (or unknown) of each deviation.

units.obligation_text: Any corrective actions taken to return the affected unit to its normal or usual manner of operation.
units.action_summary: Report corrective actions taken for each deviation.

units.obligation_text: On and after [DATE ...], a breakdown of the total duration of the deviations during the reporting period into those that are due to control equipment problems, process problems, other known causes, and other unknown causes.
units.action_summary: Provide a categorized breakdown of total deviation durations by cause categories for each reporting period after the specified date.

units.obligation_text: On and after [DATE ...], for each deviation from an emission limitation in § 63.8684, you must include an estimate of the quantity of each regulated pollutant emitted over any emission limitation in § 63.8684, and a description of the method used to estimate the emissions.
units.action_summary: After the specified date, for each deviation include estimated pollutant quantities over limits and the estimation method.

units.obligation_text: On and after [DATE ...], within 60 days after the date of completing each performance test required by this subpart, you must submit the results of the performance test following the procedures specified in paragraphs (f)(1) through (3) of this section.
units.action_summary: Submit performance test results within 60 days following test completion using specified procedures.

units.obligation_text: Data collected using test methods supported by EPA’s Electronic Reporting Tool (ERT) ... Submit the results of the performance test to EPA via the CEDRI ... The data must be submitted in a file format generated through the use of EPA’s ERT. Alternatively, you may submit an electronic file consistent with the XML schema listed on EPA’s ERT website.
units.action_summary: When using ERT-supported methods, submit test data via CEDRI in ERT-generated format or an acceptable XML file.

units.obligation_text: Data collected using test methods that are not supported by EPA’s ERT ... The results of the performance test must be included as an attachment in the ERT or an alternate electronic file consistent with the XML schema ... Submit the ERT generated package or alternative file to EPA via CEDRI.
units.action_summary: For non-ERT-supported methods, include results as an ERT attachment or XML-compatible file and submit via CEDRI.

units.obligation_text: If you claim some of the information submitted under paragraph (a)(1) of this section is CBI, you must submit a complete file, including information claimed to be CBI, to EPA. The file must be generated through the use of EPA’s ERT or an alternate electronic file ... Submit the file on a compact disc, flash drive, or other commonly used electronic storage medium and clearly mark the medium as CBI. Mail the electronic medium to U.S. EPA/OAQPS/CORE CBI Office ... The same file with the CBI omitted must be submitted to EPA via EPA’s CDX as described in paragraph (f)(1) of this section.
units.action_summary: If claiming CBI, submit a full CBI file to EPA on physical media and a redacted file via CDX in specified formats.

units.obligation_text: On and after [DATE ...], within 60 days after the date of completing each continuous monitoring system (CMS) performance evaluation ... you must submit the results of the performance evaluation following the procedures specified in paragraphs (g)(1) through (3) of this section.
units.action_summary: Submit CMS performance evaluation results within 60 days using specified procedures.

units.obligation_text: Performance evaluations of CMS measuring RATA pollutants that are supported by EPA’s ERT ... Submit the results of the performance evaluation to EPA via CEDRI ... The data must be submitted in a file format generated through the use of EPA’s ERT. Alternatively, you may submit an electronic file consistent with the XML schema listed on EPA’s ERT website.
units.action_summary: For ERT-supported CMS RATA evaluations, submit results via CEDRI in ERT format or acceptable XML.

units.obligation_text: Performance evaluations of CMS measuring RATA pollutants that are not supported by EPA’s ERT ... The results ... must be included as an attachment in the ERT or an alternate electronic file consistent with the XML schema ... Submit the ERT generated package or alternative file to EPA via CEDRI.
units.action_summary: For non-ERT-supported CMS RATA evaluations, include results as an ERT attachment or XML-compatible file and submit via CEDRI.

units.obligation_text: If you claim some of the information submitted under paragraph (g)(1) of this section is CBI, you must submit a complete file, including information claimed to be CBI, to EPA. The file must be generated ... Submit the file on a compact disc, flash drive, or other commonly used electronic storage medium and clearly mark the medium as CBI. Mail the electronic medium to U.S. EPA/OAQPS/CORE CBI Office ... The same file with the CBI omitted must be submitted to EPA via EPA’s CDX as described in paragraph (g)(1) of this section.
units.action_summary: If claiming CBI for CMS evaluation data, submit full file on physical media to EPA and a redacted file via CDX per specifications.

units.obligation_text: If you are required to electronically submit a report through CEDRI in EPA’s CDX, you may assert a claim of EPA system outage for failure to timely comply with the reporting requirement. To assert a claim of EPA system outage, you must meet the requirements outlined in paragraphs (h)(1) through (7) of this section.
units.action_summary: You may claim EPA system outage to excuse late electronic submissions if you meet the listed requirements.

units.obligation_text: You must have been or will be precluded from accessing CEDRI and submitting a required report within the time prescribed due to an outage of either EPA’s CEDRI or CDX systems.
units.action_summary: To assert outage, you must have been prevented from accessing CEDRI/CDX during the submission window due to EPA system outage.

units.obligation_text: The outage must have occurred within the period of time beginning five business days prior to the date that the submission is due.
units.action_summary: Outage must fall within 5 business days before the submission due date to qualify.

units.obligation_text: You must submit notification to the Administrator in writing as soon as possible following the date you first knew, or through due diligence should have known, that the event may cause or has caused a delay in reporting.
units.action_summary: Notify the Administrator in writing promptly when you learn the outage may cause or has caused a reporting delay.

units.obligation_text: You must provide to the Administrator a written description identifying: (i) The date(s) and time(s) when CDX or CEDRI was accessed and the system was unavailable; (ii) A rationale for attributing the delay in reporting beyond the regulatory deadline to EPA system outage; (iii) Measures taken or to be taken to minimize the delay in reporting; and (iv) The date by which you propose to report, or if you have already met the reporting requirement at the time of the notification, the date you reported.
units.action_summary: Provide detailed written information about the outage incident, its impact, mitigation measures, and proposed reporting date.

units.obligation_text: The decision to accept the claim of EPA system outage and allow an extension to the reporting deadline is solely within the discretion of the Administrator.
units.action_summary: Administrator has sole discretion to accept an outage claim and grant an extension.
units.modal_raw: is solely within the discretion of

units.obligation_text: In any circumstance, the report must be submitted electronically as soon as possible after the outage is resolved.
units.action_summary: Submit the delayed report electronically as soon as the outage ends.

units.obligation_text: If you are required to electronically submit a report through CEDRI in EPA’s CDX, you may assert a claim of force majeure for failure to timely comply with the reporting requirement. To assert a claim of force majeure, you must meet the requirements outlined in paragraphs (i)(1) through (5) of this section.
units.action_summary: You may claim force majeure to excuse late electronic submissions if you satisfy the listed requirements.

units.obligation_text: You must submit notification to the Administrator in writing as soon as possible following the date you first knew, or through due diligence should have known, that the event may cause or has caused a delay in reporting.
units.action_summary: Notify the Administrator promptly in writing when a force majeure event may cause or has caused a reporting delay.

units.obligation_text: You must provide to the Administrator: (i) A written description of the force majeure event; (ii) A rationale for attributing the delay in reporting beyond the regulatory deadline to the force majeure event; (iii) Measures taken or to be taken to minimize the delay in reporting; and (iv) The date by which you propose to report, or if you have already met the reporting requirement at the time of the notification, the date you reported.
units.action_summary: Provide a written description of the force majeure event, rationale, mitigation measures, and proposed reporting date (or actual report date).

units.obligation_text: The decision to accept the claim of force majeure and allow an extension to the reporting deadline is solely within the discretion of the Administrator.
units.action_summary: Administrator has sole discretion to accept a force majeure claim and grant an extension.
units.modal_raw: is solely within the discretion of

units.obligation_text: In any circumstance, the reporting must occur as soon as possible after the force majeure event occurs.
units.action_summary: Submit the delayed report as soon as reasonably possible after the force majeure event.

units.obligation_text: Before [DATE ...], the records in § 63.6(e)(3)(iii) through (v) related to startup, shutdown, and malfunction. On and after [DATE ...], this paragraph no longer applies.
units.action_summary: Maintain SSMP-related records per §63.6(e)(3)(iii)-(v) until the specified date; requirement ends thereafter.
units.modal_raw: (must keep) before [date]; no longer applies after [date]

units.obligation_text: Any records required to be maintained by this part that are submitted electronically via EPA’s CEDRI may be maintained in electronic format. This ability to maintain electronic copies does not affect the requirement for facilities to make records, data, and reports available upon request to a delegated air agency or EPA as part of an on-site compliance evaluation.
units.action_summary: Records submitted via CEDRI may be kept electronically, but facilities must still provide records/data/reports upon request during on-site evaluations.

units.obligation_text: Facilities must make records, data, and reports available upon request to a delegated air agency or EPA as part of an on-site compliance evaluation.
units.action_summary: Provide records, data, and reports to delegated agencies or EPA on request during on-site evaluations.

units.obligation_text: Each blowing still, Group 1 asphalt loading rack, and Group 1 asphalt storage tank ... You must meet the following emission limitation—
units.actor: owner or operator of listed equipment
units.action_summary: Owners/operators of the listed units must meet the following emission control options/limits.

units.obligation_text: Reduce total hydrocarbon mass emissions by 95 percent, or to a concentration of 20 ppmv, on a dry basis corrected to 3 percent oxygen;
units.actor: owner or operator of listed equipment
units.action_summary: Reduce total hydrocarbon emissions by 95% or to 20 ppmv (dry, corrected to 3% O2).

units.obligation_text: Route the emissions to a combustion device achieving a combustion efficiency of 99.5 percent;
units.actor: owner or operator of listed equipment
units.action_summary: Route emissions to a combustion device with 99.5% combustion efficiency.

units.obligation_text: Route the emissions to a combustion device that does not use auxiliary fuel achieving a total hydrocarbon (THC) destruction efficiency of 95.8 percent;
units.actor: owner or operator of listed equipment
units.action_summary: Route emissions to a combustion device without auxiliary fuel that achieves 95.8% THC destruction efficiency.

units.obligation_text: Route the emissions to a boiler or process heater with a design heat input capacity of 44 megawatts (MW) or greater;
units.actor: owner or operator of listed equipment
units.action_summary: Route emissions to a boiler/process heater with design heat input >= 44 MW.

units.obligation_text: Introduce the emissions into the flame zone of a boiler or process heater;
units.actor: owner or operator of listed equipment
units.action_summary: Introduce emissions into the flame zone of a boiler or process heater as a compliance option.

units.obligation_text: Route emissions to a flare meeting the requirements of § 63.11(b).
units.actor: owner or operator of listed equipment
units.action_summary: Route emissions to a flare that meets the requirements of §63.11(b) as a compliance option.

units.obligation_text: The opacity limit can be exceeded for one consecutive 15-minute period in any 24-hour period when the storage tank transfer lines are being cleared.
units.actor: owner or operator of the storage tank
units.action_summary: Permits one consecutive 15-minute exceedance of the opacity limit during clearing of storage tank transfer lines in any 24-hour period.

units.obligation_text: During this 15-minute period, the control device must not be bypassed.
units.action_summary: Prohibits bypassing the control device during the 15-minute permitted opacity exceedance.

units.obligation_text: If the emissions from the asphalt storage tank are ducted to the saturator control device, the combined emissions from the saturator and storage tank must meet the 20 percent opacity limit (specified in 3.a of Table 1 to this subpart) during this 15-minute period.
units.action_summary: If storage tank emissions are ducted to saturator, combined emissions must meet 20% opacity during the permitted 15-minute period.

units.obligation_text: Maintain the 3-hour average inlet gas temperature at or below the operating limit established during the performance test;
units.action_summary: Keep the 3-hour average inlet gas temperature at or below the test-established operating limit.

units.obligation_text: Maintain the 3-hour average pressure drop across the device at or below either the operating limit established during the performance test, or as an alternative, according to manufacturer’s specifications.
units.action_summary: Keep the 3-hour average pressure drop at or below the test-established limit or, alternatively, per manufacturer's specs.

units.obligation_text: As an alternative to monitoring the pressure drop across the control device, owners or operators using an ESP to achieve compliance with the emission limits ... can monitor the voltage to the ESP. If this option is selected, the ESP voltage must be maintained at or above the operating limit established during the performance test.
units.action_summary: ESP users may monitor voltage instead of pressure drop; if chosen, maintain ESP voltage at or above test-established operating limit.

units.obligation_text: Other control devices that are neither a combustion device or a control device used to comply with the particulate matter emission standards: Maintain the approved monitoring parameters within the operating limits established during the performance test.
units.action_summary: Keep approved monitoring parameters within the operating limits established during performance testing for other control devices.

units.obligation_text: The inlet gas temperature operating limit is set at +20 percent of the test run average inlet gas temperature measured during the performance test.
units.action_summary: Defines the inlet gas temperature operating limit as test-run average plus 20%.

units.obligation_text: All particulate matter, total hydrocarbon, carbon monoxide, and carbon dioxide emission tests. a. Select sampling port’s location and the number of traverse points. i. EPA test method 1 or 1A in appendix A to part 60 of this chapter.
units.action_summary: For listed emission tests, select sampling port location and number of traverse points using EPA Test Method 1 or 1A.

units.obligation_text: For demonstrating compliance with the total hydrocarbon percent reduction standard, the sampling sites must be located at the inlet and outlet of the control device prior to any releases to the atmosphere.
units.action_summary: For THC percent reduction tests, locate sampling sites at inlet and outlet of the control device before atmospheric release.

units.obligation_text: For demonstrating compliance with the particulate matter mass emission rate, THC destruction efficiency, THC outlet concentration, or combustion efficiency standards, the sampling sites must be located at the outlet of the control device prior to any releases to the atmosphere.
units.action_summary: For PM mass rate, THC destruction, THC outlet concentration, or combustion efficiency tests, locate sampling sites at the outlet of the control device before atmospheric release.

units.obligation_text: All opacity tests. Conduct opacity observations. EPA test method 9 in appendix A to part 60 of this chapter, or ASTM D7520–2013 (incorporated by reference, see § 63.14). Conduct opacity observations for at least 3 hours and obtain 30, 6-minute averages.
units.action_summary: Conduct opacity observations per EPA Method 9 or ASTM D7520–2013 for at least 3 hours, obtaining 30 six-minute averages.

units.obligation_text: Each combustion device. Establish a site-specific combustion zone temperature limit.
units.action_summary: Set a site-specific combustion zone temperature limit for each combustion device.

title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Taconite Iron Ore Processing Residual Risk and Technology Review

units.obligation_text: If you have an affected source the construction or reconstruction of which is commenced before December 18, 2002, you must comply with each emission limitation, work practice standard, and operation and maintenance requirement in this subpart that applies to you no later than October 30, 2006, except as provided in paragraphs (f)(1) and (2) of this section.
units.actor: you (owner or operator of the affected source)
units.action_summary: Comply with all applicable emission limits, work practice standards, and O&M requirements by Oct 30, 2006.

units.obligation_text: If you have an affected source the construction or reconstruction of which is commenced on or after December 18, 2002, and its initial startup date is on or before October 30, 2003, you must comply with each emission limitation, work practice standard, and operation and maintenance requirement in this subpart that applies to you by October 30, 2003, except as noted in paragraphs (f)(1) and (2) of this section.
units.actor: you (owner or operator of the affected source)
units.action_summary: Comply with all applicable emission limits, work practice standards, and O&M requirements by Oct 30, 2003.

units.obligation_text: If you have an affected source and its initial startup date is after October 30, 2003, you must comply with each emission limitation, work practice standard, and operation and maintenance requirement in this subpart that applies to you upon initial startup, except as noted in paragraphs (f)(1) and (2) of this section.
units.actor: you (owner or operator of the affected source)
units.action_summary: Comply with all applicable emission limits, work practice standards, and O&M requirements upon initial startup.

units.obligation_text: Any portion of the taconite iron ore processing plant that is a new affected source or a new reconstructed source must be in compliance with this subpart upon startup, except as noted in paragraphs (f)(1) and (2) of this section.
units.actor: you (owner or operator of the plant)
units.action_summary: New or reconstructed portions of the plant must comply with the subpart upon startup.

units.obligation_text: All other parts of the taconite iron ore processing plant must be in compliance with this subpart no later than 3 years after the plant becomes a major source, except as noted in paragraphs (f)(1) and (2) of this section.
units.actor: you (owner or operator of the plant)
units.action_summary: All other plant parts must comply within 3 years after the plant becomes a major source.

units.obligation_text: You must meet the notification and schedule requirements in § 63.9640. Several of these notifications must be submitted before the compliance date for your affected source.
units.action_summary: Meet the notification and schedule requirements in §63.9640, with some notifications due before the compliance date.

units.obligation_text: If you have an affected source the construction or reconstruction of which is commenced before September 25, 2019, you must comply with the following requirements of this subpart by [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER]: § 63.9590(b)(2); § 63.9600(a); § 63.9610(a) introductory text; § 63.9621(a); § 63.9622(b) introductory text, (b)(1) and (2) and (d)(2); § 63.9623(b)(2); § 63.9631(c); § 63.9632(a)(3); § 63.9634(b)(3), (f) introductory text, and (f)(1), (3), and (4); § 63.9637; § 63.9641(b)(7)(ii), (b)(8)(ii) and (iv), (c), (e), (g), (h), (i), and (j); § 63.9642(a)(4), (5), and (6) and (b)(3); § 63.9643(d); Table 2 to this subpart.
units.actor: you (owner or operator of affected source commenced before Sept 25, 2019)
units.action_summary: Comply with the listed subpart requirements by the specified date (180 days after final rule publication).

units.obligation_text: If you have an affected source the construction or reconstruction of which is commenced on or after September 25, 2019, you must comply with all the requirements of this subpart by [DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER] or the date of startup, whichever is later.
units.actor: you (owner or operator of affected source commenced on or after Sept 25, 2019)
units.action_summary: Comply with all subpart requirements by the publication date of the final rule or by startup, whichever is later.

units.obligation_text: For each dynamic wet scrubber applied to meet any particulate matter emission limit in Table 1 to this subpart, you must maintain the daily average scrubber water flow rate and the daily average fan amperage (a surrogate for fan speed as revolutions per minute) at or above the minimum levels established during the initial performance test.
units.actor: you (owner or operator of dynamic wet scrubber)
units.action_summary: Maintain daily average scrubber water flow rate and fan amperage at or above the minimums established during initial performance test.

units.obligation_text: For dynamic wet scrubbers subject to performance testing in § 63.9620 and operating limits for scrubber water flow rate and fan amperage in § 63.9590(b)(2), you must establish site-specific operating limits according to the procedures in paragraphs (b)(1) and (2) of this section.
units.actor: you (owner or operator of dynamic wet scrubber)
units.action_summary: Establish site-specific operating limits for scrubber water flow rate and fan amperage using the procedures in paragraphs (b)(1) and (2).

units.obligation_text: Using the CPMS required in § 63.9631(b), measure and record the scrubber water flow rate and the fan amperage every 15 minutes during each run of the particulate matter performance test.
units.action_summary: Measure and record scrubber water flow rate and fan amperage every 15 minutes during each performance test run using the CPMS.

units.obligation_text: Calculate and record the average scrubber water flow rate and the average fan amperage for each individual test run. Your operating limits are established as the lowest average scrubber water flow rate and the lowest average fan amperage value corresponding to any of the three test runs.
units.action_summary: Calculate the average flow rate and fan amperage for each run; set operating limits as the lowest average values from the runs.

units.obligation_text: You must always operate and maintain any affected source, including associated air pollution control equipment and monitoring equipment, in a manner consistent with safety and good air pollution control practices for minimizing emissions.
units.action_summary: Always operate and maintain affected sources and associated control and monitoring equipment consistent with safety and good air pollution control practices to minimize emissions.

units.obligation_text: The general duty to minimize emissions does not require the owner or operator to make any further efforts to reduce emissions if levels required by the applicable standard have been achieved.
units.action_summary: Owner/operator is not required to take further emission reduction efforts once applicable standard levels are achieved.

units.obligation_text: In the event a bag leak detection system alarm is triggered, you must initiate corrective action to determine the cause of the alarm within 1 hour of the alarm, initiate corrective action to correct the cause of the problem within 24 hours of the alarm, and complete the corrective action as soon as practicable.
units.action_summary: If a bag leak detection alarm triggers, determine cause within 1 hour, begin corrective action to fix cause within 24 hours, and complete corrective action as soon as practicable.

units.obligation_text: Corrective actions may include, but are not limited to, the actions listed in paragraphs (b)(2)(i) through (vi) of this section.
units.action_summary: Permits the use of listed corrective actions (and others) in response to bag leak detection alarms.

units.obligation_text: You must be in compliance with the requirements in paragraphs (a)(1) through (6) of this section at all times.
units.action_summary: Remain in compliance with the section's listed requirements at all times.

units.obligation_text: If you elect to test representative emission units as provided in paragraph (e) of this section, the units that are grouped together as similar units must meet the criteria in paragraphs (f)(1) and (2) of this section.
units.action_summary: Units grouped as similar for representative testing must meet the specified criteria in (f)(1) and (f)(2).

units.obligation_text: You must conduct each performance test that applies to your affected source under normal maximum operating conditions of the affected source.
units.action_summary: Conduct applicable performance tests under normal maximum operating conditions.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator may not conduct performance tests during periods of malfunction.
units.action_summary: Do not conduct performance tests during malfunctions.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator must record the process information that is necessary to document operating conditions during the test and include in such record an explanation to support that such conditions represent normal operation.
units.action_summary: Record necessary process information and an explanation documenting that test conditions represent normal operation.

units.obligation_text: Upon request, the owner or operator shall make available to the Administrator such records as may be necessary to determine the conditions of performance tests.
units.action_summary: Provide records related to performance tests to the Administrator upon request.

units.obligation_text: You must also conduct each performance test that applies to your affected source according to the requirements in paragraphs (b) and (c) of this section.
units.action_summary: Conduct performance tests in accordance with the procedures and methods specified in paragraphs (b) and (c).

units.obligation_text: Except as provided in § 63.9620(e), determine the concentration of particulate matter in the stack gas for each emission unit according to the test methods listed in paragraphs (b)(1)(i) through (v) of this section.
units.action_summary: Determine particulate matter concentration in stack gas using the listed test methods.

units.obligation_text: Method 1 or 1A in appendix A–1 to part 60 of this chapter to select sampling port locations and the number of traverse points. Sampling ports must be located at the outlet of the control device and prior to any releases to the atmosphere.
units.action_summary: Use Method 1/1A to select sampling port locations and traverse points, and locate sampling ports at the control device outlet before atmospheric release.

units.obligation_text: Method 2, 2A, 2C, 2D, or 2F in appendix A–1 to part 60 of this chapter or Method 2G in appendix A–2 to part 60 of this chapter, as applicable, to determine the volumetric flow rate of the stack gas.
units.action_summary: Determine stack gas volumetric flow rate using the applicable Method 2 series or Method 2G.

units.obligation_text: Method 3A or 3B in appendix A–2 to part 60 of this chapter to determine the dry molecular weight of the stack gas.
units.action_summary: Use Method 3A or 3B to determine the dry molecular weight of stack gas.

units.obligation_text: The voluntary consensus standard ANSI/ASME PTC 19.10–1981—Part 10 (incorporated by reference—see § 63.14) may be used as an alternative to the manual procedures (but not instrumental procedures) in Method 3B.
units.action_summary: You may use ANSI/ASME PTC 19.10–1981 Part 10 as an alternative to Method 3B's manual procedures (not instrumental procedures).

units.obligation_text: Method 4 in appendix A–3 to part 60 of this chapter to determine the moisture content of the stack gas.
units.action_summary: Use Method 4 to determine stack gas moisture content.

units.obligation_text: Method 5 or 5D in appendix A–3 to part 60 of this chapter or Method 17 in appendix A–6 to part 60 of this chapter to determine the concentration of particulate matter.
units.action_summary: Use Method 5, 5D, or 17 to determine particulate matter concentration.

units.obligation_text: Each Method 5, 5D, or 17 performance test must consist of three separate runs. Each run must be conducted for a minimum of 1 hour. If any measurement result is reported as below the method detection limit, use the method detection limit for that value when calculating the average particulate matter concentration. The average particulate matter concentration from the three runs will be used to determine compliance.
units.action_summary: Method 5/5D/17 tests require three runs of at least 1 hour each; use detection limits for below-detection results and average the three runs to determine compliance.

units.obligation_text: Determine the concentration of particulate matter for each stack according to the test methods listed in paragraphs (c)(1)(i) through (v) of this section.
units.action_summary: Determine stack particulate concentration using the listed test methods for stacks.

units.obligation_text: Method 1 or 1A in appendix A–1 to part 60 of this chapter to select sampling port locations and the number of traverse points. Sampling ports must be located at the outlet of the control device and prior to any releases to the atmosphere.
units.action_summary: For stack tests use Method 1/1A to select sampling port locations and traverse points; locate sampling ports at control device outlet prior to atmospheric release.

units.obligation_text: Method 2, 2A, 2C, 2D, or 2F in appendix A–1 to part 60 of this chapter or Method 2G in appendix A–2 to part 60 of this chapter, as applicable, to determine the volumetric flow rate of the stack gas.
units.action_summary: Use the applicable Method 2 series or Method 2G to determine stack gas volumetric flow rate for stack tests.

units.obligation_text: Method 3A or 3B in appendix A–2 to part 60 of this chapter to determine the dry molecular weight of the stack gas.
units.action_summary: Use Method 3A or 3B to determine dry molecular weight for stack tests.

units.obligation_text: The voluntary consensus standard ANSI/ASME PTC 19.10–1981—Part 10 (incorporated by reference—see § 63.14) may be used as an alternative to the manual procedures (but not instrumental procedures) in Method 3B.
units.action_summary: You may use the ANSI/ASME standard as an alternative to Method 3B's manual procedures for stack tests (not instrumental procedures).

units.obligation_text: Method 4 in appendix A–3 to part 60 of this chapter to determine the moisture content of the stack gas.
units.action_summary: Use Method 4 to determine moisture content for stack tests.

units.obligation_text: Method 5 or 5D in appendix A–3 to part 60 of this chapter to determine the concentration of particulate matter.
units.action_summary: Use Method 5 or 5D to determine particulate matter concentration for stack tests.

units.obligation_text: Each Method 5 or 5D performance test must consist of three separate runs. Each run must be conducted for a minimum of 1 hour. If any measurement result is reported as below the method detection limit, use the method detection limit for that value when calculating the average particulate matter concentration. The average particulate matter concentration from the three runs will be used to determine compliance.
units.action_summary: Method 5/5D stack tests require three runs of at least 1 hour each; use detection limits for below-detection results and average to determine compliance.

units.obligation_text: For each dynamic wet scrubber subject to performance testing in § 63.9620 and operating limits for scrubber water flow rate and fan amperage in § 63.9590(b)(2), you have established appropriate site-specific operating limits and have a record of the scrubber water flow rate and the fan amperage value, measured during the performance test in accordance with § 63.9622(b).
units.action_summary: Have established site-specific operating limits and maintain records of scrubber water flow and fan amperage measured during performance testing per §63.9622(b).

units.obligation_text: For each air pollution control device subject to operating limits in § 63.9590(b), you have demonstrated initial compliance with the operation and maintenance requirements if you meet all of the requirements in paragraphs (a) through (d) of this section.
units.action_summary: To demonstrate initial compliance for control devices subject to §63.9590(b), meet all requirements in paragraphs (a) through (d) of §63.9625.

units.obligation_text: For each baghouse applied to meet any particulate matter emission limit in Table 1 to this subpart, you must install, operate, and maintain a bag leak detection system to monitor the relative change in particulate matter loadings according to the requirements in § 63.9632(a), and conduct inspections at their specified frequencies according to the requirements in paragraphs (a)(1) through (6) and (8) of this section.
units.action_summary: Install, operate, and maintain a bag leak detection system for each baghouse meeting particulate limits, and conduct inspections at required frequencies per §63.9632(a).

units.obligation_text: For each baghouse applied to meet any particulate matter emission limit in Table 1 to this subpart that is not required by § 63.9632(a) to be equipped with a bag leak detection system, you must conduct inspections at their specified frequencies according to the requirements in paragraphs (a)(1) through (8) of this section.
units.action_summary: If a baghouse is not required to have a bag leak detection system, conduct inspections at specified frequencies per the section.

units.obligation_text: For each dynamic wet scrubber subject to the scrubber water flow rate and the fan amperage operating limits in § 63.9590(b)(2), you must install, operate, and maintain a CPMS according to the requirements in § 63.9632(b) through (e) and monitor the daily average scrubber water flow rate and the daily average fan amperage according to the requirements in § 63.9633.
units.action_summary: Install, operate, and maintain a CPMS for each applicable dynamic wet scrubber and monitor daily average flow rate and fan amperage as required.

units.obligation_text: For each negative pressure baghouse or positive pressure baghouse equipped with a stack, applied to meet any particulate emission limit in Table 1 to this subpart, you must install, operate, and maintain a bag leak detection system for each exhaust stack according to the requirements in paragraphs (a)(1) through (9) of this section.
units.action_summary: Install, operate, and maintain a bag leak detection system for each exhaust stack of baghouses meeting particulate limits according to the listed requirements.

units.obligation_text: A bag leak detection system installed before September 25, 2019, must be certified by the manufacturer to be capable of detecting emissions of particulate matter at concentrations of 10 milligrams per actual cubic meter (0.0044 grains per actual cubic foot) or less. A bag leak detection system installed after September 25, 2019, must be certified by the manufacturer to be capable of detecting emissions of particulate matter at concentrations of 1 milligram per actual cubic meter (0.00044 grains per actual cubic foot) or less.
units.action_summary: Ensure bag leak detection systems are manufacturer-certified to detect PM at <=10 mg/m3 for pre-9/25/2019 installations and <=1 mg/m3 for post-9/25/2019 installations.

units.obligation_text: The bag leak detection system must be equipped with a device to continuously record the output signal from the sensor.
units.action_summary: Equip the bag leak detection system with continuous recording of the sensor output signal.

units.obligation_text: The system must be equipped with an alarm that will sound when an increase in relative particulate loadings is detected over the alarm level set point established according to paragraph (a)(5) of this section. The alarm must be located such that it can be heard by the appropriate plant personnel.
units.action_summary: Provide an alarm that sounds upon increased particulate loading above set point, and locate it so appropriate plant personnel can hear it.

units.obligation_text: For each bag leak detection system, you must develop and submit to the Administrator for approval, a site-specific monitoring plan that addresses the items identified in paragraphs (a)(5)(i) through (v) of this section. You must operate and maintain the bag leak detection system according to the site-specific monitoring plan at all times.
units.action_summary: Develop and submit a site-specific monitoring plan for each bag leak detection system and operate/maintain the system in accordance with that approved plan at all times.

units.obligation_text: The monitoring plan shall be consistent with the manufacturer's specifications and recommendations contained in the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency guidance document, 'Fabric Filter Bag Leak Detection Guidance' (EPA–454/R–98–015) (incorporated by reference—see § 63.14).
units.action_summary: Ensure the site-specific monitoring plan is consistent with manufacturer specifications and the EPA Fabric Filter Bag Leak Detection Guidance.

units.obligation_text: Following initial adjustment, do not adjust sensitivity or range, averaging period, alarm set point, or alarm delay time, without approval from the Administrator except as provided for in paragraph (a)(7)(i) of this section. In no event may the sensitivity be increased more than 100 percent or decreased by more than 50 percent over a 365-day period unless such adjustment follows a complete baghouse inspection that demonstrates the baghouse is in good operating condition.
units.action_summary: Do not adjust BLDS sensitivity, range, averaging period, alarm set point, or delay time without Administrator approval; sensitivity may not increase >100% or decrease >50% over 365 days unless following a complete inspection that shows good condition.

units.obligation_text: Once per quarter, you may adjust the sensitivity or range of the bag leak detection system to account for seasonal effects, including temperature and humidity, according to the procedures identified in the site-specific monitoring plan required under paragraph (a)(5) of this section.
units.action_summary: You may adjust BLDS sensitivity or range once per quarter for seasonal effects, following procedures in the site-specific monitoring plan.

units.obligation_text: Performance evaluation procedures, a schedule for performing such procedures, and acceptance criteria (e.g., calibrations), as well as corrective action to be taken if a performance evaluation does not meet the acceptance criteria. If a CPMS calibration fails, the CPMS is considered to be inoperative until you take corrective action and the system passes calibration.
units.action_summary: Include performance evaluation procedures, schedule, acceptance criteria and corrective actions in the plan; if CPMS calibration fails, treat CPMS as inoperative until corrective action and passing calibration.
units.modal_raw: must (implied as required plan content); 'is considered' (status)

units.obligation_text: Ongoing operation and maintenance procedures and a schedule for preventative maintenance procedures, in a manner consistent with good air pollution control practices and in accordance with the general requirements of § 63.8(c)(1)(ii), (c)(3), (c)(4)(ii), and (c)(7) and (8).
units.action_summary: Include ongoing operation and preventive maintenance procedures and schedule in the plan consistent with good practices and §63.8 general requirements.

units.obligation_text: Ongoing data quality assurance procedures in accordance with the general requirements of § 63.8(d)(1) and (2). The owner or operator shall keep these written procedures on record for the life of the affected source or until the affected source is no longer subject to the provisions of this part, to be made available for inspection, upon request, by the Administrator. If the performance evaluation plan is revised, the owner or operator shall keep previous (i.e., superseded) versions of the performance evaluation plan on record to be made available for inspection, upon request, by the Administrator, for a period of 5 years after each revision to the plan.
units.action_summary: Include data quality assurance procedures in the plan; retain written procedures for the life of the source and keep superseded plan versions for 5 years after each revision, available for inspection upon request.

units.obligation_text: Ongoing recordkeeping and reporting procedures in accordance with the general requirements of § 63.10(c)(1) through (14), (e)(1), and (e)(2)(i).
units.action_summary: Include ongoing recordkeeping and reporting procedures in the plan per §63.10 general requirements.

units.obligation_text: You must develop and implement a quality control program for operating and maintaining each COMS according to § 63.8(a) and (b), (c)(1)(ii), (c)(2) through (8), (d)(1) and (2), and (e) through (g) and Procedure 3 in appendix F to 40 CFR part 60. At a minimum, the quality control program must include a daily calibration drift assessment, quarterly performance audit, and annual zero alignment of each COMS.
units.action_summary: Develop and implement a COMS quality control program per §63.8 and appendix F, including daily calibration drift checks, quarterly audits, and annual zero alignment.

units.obligation_text: You must determine and record the 6-minute average opacity for periods during which the COMS is not out of control. All COMS must complete a minimum of one cycle of sampling and analyzing for each successive 10-second period and one cycle of data recording for each successive 6-minute period.
units.action_summary: Determine and record 6-minute average opacity when COMS is in control; ensure COMS completes required sampling/analyzing and data recording cycles.

units.obligation_text: Except for monitoring malfunctions, out of control periods, associated repairs, and required quality assurance or control activities (including as applicable, calibration checks and required zero and span adjustments), you must monitor continuously (or collect data at all required intervals) at all times an affected source is operating.
units.action_summary: Continuously monitor or collect required data at all times the affected source is operating, except for specified exceptions.

units.obligation_text: You may not use data recorded during monitoring malfunctions, out of control periods, associated repairs, and required quality assurance or control activities in data averages and calculations used to report emission or operating levels, or to fulfill a minimum data availability requirement. You must use all the data collected during all other periods in assessing compliance.
units.action_summary: Do not use data from malfunctions/out-of-control/repairs/QA activities in averages/required calculations; use all other collected data to assess compliance.

units.obligation_text: For ore crushing and handling and finished pellet handling emission units not selected for initial performance testing and defined within a group of similar emission units in accordance with § 63.9620(e), the site-specific operating limits established for the emission unit selected as representative of a group of similar emission units will be used as the operating limit for each emission unit within the group. The operating limit established for the representative unit must be met by each emission unit within the group.
units.action_summary: When representative testing is used, apply the representative unit's site-specific operating limits to all units in the similar group, and meet those limits for each unit.

units.obligation_text: For each baghouse applied to meet any particulate emission limit in Table 1 to this subpart, you must demonstrate continuous compliance by completing the requirements in paragraphs (d)(1) through (3) of this section.
units.action_summary: Demonstrate continuous compliance for each baghouse by completing the specified requirements in (d)(1)-(3).

units.obligation_text: Inspecting and maintaining each baghouse according to the requirements in § 63.9631(a) and recording all information needed to document conformance with the requirements in § 63.9631(a). If you increase or decrease the sensitivity of the bag leak detection system beyond the limits specified in your site-specific monitoring plan, you must include a copy of the required written certification by a responsible official in the next semiannual compliance report.
units.action_summary: Inspect and maintain each baghouse per §63.9631(a), record documentation of conformance; if you adjust BLDS sensitivity beyond plan limits, include a written certification by a responsible official in the next semiannual compliance report.

units.obligation_text: Each bag leak detection system must be operated and maintained such that the alarm does not sound more than 5 percent of the operating time during a 6-month period. Calculate the alarm time as specified in paragraphs (d)(3)(i) through (iii) of this section.
units.action_summary: Operate and maintain BLDS so alarms sound no more than 5% of operating time in a 6-month period; calculate alarm time per specified rules.

units.obligation_text: If inspection of the fabric filter demonstrates that no corrective action is required, no alarm time is counted.
units.action_summary: If inspection shows no corrective action needed, do not count alarm time.

units.obligation_text: If corrective action is required, each alarm time (i.e., time that the alarm sounds) is counted as a minimum of 1 hour.
units.action_summary: If corrective action is required, count each alarm time as at least 1 hour.

units.obligation_text: If it takes longer than 1 hour to initiate corrective action, each alarm time is counted as the actual amount of time taken to initiate corrective action.
units.action_summary: If initiation of corrective action takes longer than 1 hour, count alarm time as the actual time taken to initiate corrective action.

units.obligation_text: For each dynamic wet scrubber subject to the operating limits for scrubber water flow rate and the fan amperage in § 63.9590(b)(2), you must demonstrate continuous compliance by completing the requirements of paragraphs (f)(1) through (4) of this section.
units.action_summary: Demonstrate continuous compliance for each applicable dynamic wet scrubber by completing requirements in (f)(1)-(4).

units.obligation_text: Maintaining the daily average scrubber water flow rate and the daily average fan amperage at or above the minimum levels established during the initial or subsequent performance test.
units.action_summary: Keep daily average scrubber water flow rate and fan amperage at or above minimum levels established during testing.

units.obligation_text: Collecting and reducing monitoring data for scrubber water flow rate and fan amperage according to § 63.9632(c) and recording all information needed to document conformance with the requirements in § 63.9632(c).
units.action_summary: Collect, reduce, and record monitoring data for scrubber flow rate and fan amperage per §63.9632(c) to document conformance.

units.obligation_text: If the daily average scrubber water flow rate or daily average fan amperage, is below the operating limits established for a corresponding emission unit or group of similar emission units, you must then follow the corrective action procedures in paragraph (j) of this section.
units.action_summary: If daily averages fall below operating limits, follow the corrective action procedures in paragraph (j).

units.obligation_text: You must initiate and complete initial corrective action within 10 calendar days and demonstrate that the initial corrective action was successful. During any period of corrective action, you must continue to monitor and record all required operating parameters for equipment that remains in operation.
units.action_summary: Initiate and complete initial corrective action within 10 days and demonstrate success; continue monitoring and recording during corrective action.

units.obligation_text: If the initial corrective action required in paragraph (j)(1) of this section was not successful, then you must complete additional corrective action within 10 calendar days and demonstrate that the subsequent corrective action was successful. During any period of corrective action, you must continue to monitor and record all required operating parameters for equipment that remains in operation.
units.action_summary: If initial corrective action fails, complete additional corrective action within 10 days and demonstrate success; continue monitoring and recording during corrective actions.

units.obligation_text: You must report each instance in which you did not meet each emission limitation in Table 1 to this subpart that applies to you. You also must report each instance in which you did not meet the work practice standards in § 63.9591 and each instance in which you did not meet each operation and maintenance requirement in § 63.9600 that applies to you. These deviations must be reported in accordance with the requirements in § 63.9641.
units.action_summary: Report all deviations from emission limitations, work practice standards, and O&M requirements that apply, in accordance with §63.9641.

units.obligation_text: For each initial compliance demonstration that does include a performance test, you must submit the notification of compliance status, including the performance test results, before the close of business on the 60th calendar day following the completion of the performance test according to § 63.10(d)(2). If the performance test results have been submitted electronically in accordance with § 63.9641(f), the process unit(s) tested, the pollutant(s) tested, and the date that such performance test was conducted may be submitted in the notification of compliance status report in lieu of the performance test results. The performance test results must be submitted to the Compliance and Emissions Data Reporting Interface (CEDRI) by the date the notification of compliance status report is submitted.
units.action_summary: Submit notification of compliance status (including performance test results) within 60 days of test completion; if results were already submitted electronically, include process/pollutant/date in notification and ensure results are in CEDRI by the notification submission date.

units.obligation_text: The first compliance report must be electronically submitted, postmarked or delivered no later than July 31 or January 31, whichever date comes first after your first compliance report is due.
units.action_summary: Submit the first compliance report by the earlier of July 31 or January 31 following the due date, via electronic submission, postmark, or delivery.

units.obligation_text: Each subsequent compliance report must be electronically submitted, postmarked or delivered no later than July 31 or January 31, whichever date comes first after the end of the semiannual reporting period.
units.action_summary: Submit each subsequent semiannual compliance report by the earlier of July 31 or January 31 after the reporting period, via electronic submission, postmark, or delivery.

units.obligation_text: Each compliance report must include the information in paragraphs (b)(1) through (8) of this section, as applicable.
units.action_summary: Include the applicable information listed in paragraphs (b)(1)-(8) in each compliance report.

units.obligation_text: Statement by a responsible official, with the official’s name, title, and signature, certifying the truth, accuracy, and completeness of the content of the report. If your report is submitted via CEDRI, the certifier’s electronic signature during the submission process replaces the requirement in this paragraph (b)(2).
units.action_summary: Include a certified statement by a responsible official in the report, unless submitted via CEDRI where an electronic signature suffices.

units.obligation_text: Date of report and beginning and ending dates of the reporting period. You are no longer required to provide the date of report when the report is submitted via CEDRI.
units.action_summary: Include report date and reporting period start/end dates unless submitting via CEDRI, in which case report date is not required.

units.obligation_text: The total operating time in hours of each affected source during the reporting period.
units.action_summary: Report the total operating time (hours) of each affected source during the reporting period for deviations when not using a CMS.
units.modal_raw: must (as part of required compliance report content)

units.obligation_text: Information on the affected sources or equipment, the emission limited deviation from, the start date, start time, duration in hours, and cause of each deviation (including unknown cause) as applicable, an estimate of the quantity in pounds of each regulated pollutant emitted over an emission limit and a description of the method used to estimate the emissions, and the corrective action taken.
units.action_summary: For deviations when not using a CMS, report details including equipment affected, deviation description, start/stop times, duration, cause, emission estimate and estimation method, and corrective action taken.
units.modal_raw: must (as part of required compliance report content)

units.obligation_text: The start date, start time, and duration in hours (or minutes for COMS) that each continuous monitoring system was inoperative, except for zero (low-level) and high-level checks.
units.action_summary: Report start date/time and duration that each CMS was inoperative (excluding routine zero/high-level checks).
units.modal_raw: must (as part of required compliance report content)

units.obligation_text: The start date, start time, and duration in hours (or minutes for COMS) that each continuous monitoring system was out-of-control, including the information in § 63.8(c)(8).
units.action_summary: Report start date/time and duration each CMS was out-of-control, including required §63.8(c)(8) information.

units.obligation_text: For each affected source or equipment, the date, the time that each deviation started and stopped, the cause of the deviation, and whether each deviation occurred during a period of malfunction or during another period.
units.action_summary: For each affected source/equipment, report date/time each deviation started/stopped, cause, and whether it occurred during malfunction or another period.

units.obligation_text: The total duration in hours (or minutes for COMS) of all deviations for each CMS during the reporting period, the total operating time in hours of the affected source during the reporting period, and the total duration as a percent of the total source operating time during that reporting period.
units.action_summary: Report total duration of CMS deviations, total operating time of the source, and the deviations as a percent of operating time.

units.obligation_text: A breakdown of the total duration in hours (or minutes for COMS) of the deviations during the reporting period including those that are due to control equipment problems, process problems, other known causes, and other unknown causes.
units.action_summary: Provide breakdown of deviation durations by cause categories (control equipment, process, other known, unknown).

units.obligation_text: The total duration in hours (or minutes for COMS) of continuous monitoring system downtime for each continuous monitoring system during the reporting period, the total operating time in hours of the affected source during the reporting period, and the total duration of continuous monitoring system downtime as a percent of the total source operating time during the reporting period.
units.action_summary: Report total CMS downtime, total source operating time, and downtime as a percent of operating time.

units.obligation_text: The monitoring equipment manufacturer and model number and the pollutant or parameter monitored.
units.action_summary: Report monitoring equipment manufacturer and model and the pollutant or parameter being monitored.

units.obligation_text: Beginning on [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], submit all subsequent compliance reports to the EPA via CEDRI, which can be accessed through the EPA's Central Data Exchange (CDX). You must use the appropriate electronic report template on the CEDRI website for this subpart. The report must be submitted by the deadline specified in this subpart, regardless of the method in which the report is submitted. If you claim some of the information required to be submitted via CEDRI is confidential business information (CBI), submit a complete report, including information claimed to be CBI, to the EPA. The report must be generated using the appropriate form on the CEDRI website. Submit the file on a compact disc, flash drive, or other commonly used electronic storage medium and clearly mark the medium as CBI. Mail the electronic medium to U.S. EPA/OAQPS/SPPD/CORE CBI Office, Attention: Taconite Iron Ore Processing Sector Lead, MD C404–02, 4930 Old Page Rd., Durham, NC 27703. The same file with the CBI omitted must be submitted to the EPA via the EPA's CDX as described earlier in this paragraph (c).
units.action_summary: Beginning on the specified date, submit all subsequent compliance reports via CEDRI using the appropriate template and by the subpart deadlines; if claiming CBI, also provide a complete CBI-containing file on physical media to EPA and submit a redacted file via CDX.

units.obligation_text: Within 60 days after the date of completing each performance test required by this subpart, you must submit the results of the performance test following the procedures specified in paragraphs (f)(1) through (3) of this section.
units.action_summary: Submit performance test results within 60 days following the procedures in paragraphs (f)(1)-(3).

units.obligation_text: Data collected using test methods supported by the EPA’s Electronic Reporting Tool (ERT) as listed on the EPA’s ERT website at the time of the test. Submit the results of the performance test to the EPA via CEDRI, which can be accessed through the EPA’s CDX. The data must be submitted in a file format generated through the use of the EPA’s ERT. Alternatively, you may submit an electronic file consistent with the extensible markup language (XML) schema listed on the EPA’s ERT website.
units.action_summary: For tests using ERT-supported methods, submit results via CEDRI in ERT-generated format or an XML file consistent with the ERT schema.

units.obligation_text: Data collected using test methods that are not supported by the EPA’s ERT as listed on the EPA’s ERT website at the time of the test. The results of the performance test must be included as an attachment in the ERT or an alternate electronic file consistent with the XML schema listed on the EPA’s ERT website. Submit the ERT generated package or alternative file to the EPA via CEDRI.
units.action_summary: For tests using methods not supported by ERT, include results as an attachment in ERT or alternate XML-consistent file and submit to EPA via CEDRI.

units.obligation_text: Confidential business information (CBI). If you claim some of the information submitted under paragraph (f)(1) or (2) of this section is CBI, you must submit a complete file, including information claimed to be CBI, to the EPA. The file must be generated through the use of the EPA’s ERT or an alternate electronic file consistent with the XML schema listed on the EPA’s ERT website. Submit the file on a compact disc, flash drive, or other commonly used electronic storage medium and clearly mark the medium as CBI. Mail the electronic medium to U.S. EPA/ OAQPS/CORE CBI Office, Attention: Group Leader, Measurement Policy Group, MD C404–02, 4930 Old Page Rd., Durham, NC 27703. The same file with the CBI omitted must be submitted to the EPA via the EPA’s CDX.
units.action_summary: If claiming CBI for performance test submissions, send a complete CBI-containing file on physical media to EPA and also submit a CBI‑omitted file via CDX, using ERT or XML-consistent format.

title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Stationary Combustion Turbines Residual Risk and Technology Review

units.obligation_text: You must be in compliance with the emission limitations and operating limitations which apply to you at all times.
units.actor: you (owner or operator of affected source)
units.action_summary: Be in compliance with applicable emission and operating limitations at all times.

units.obligation_text: Before [DATE 181 DAYS AFTER PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE Federal Register], you must be in compliance with the emission limitations and operating limitations which apply to you at all times except during startup, shutdown, and malfunctions.
units.actor: you (owner or operator of affected source)
units.action_summary: Prior to specified date, comply with applicable emission and operating limits at all times except during startup, shutdown, and malfunctions.

units.obligation_text: After [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE Federal Register], you must be in compliance with the emission limitations, operating limitations, and other requirements in this subpart which apply to you at all times.
units.actor: you (owner or operator of affected source)
units.action_summary: After specified date, comply at all times with emission, operating, and other requirements in the subpart.

units.obligation_text: Before [DATE 181 DAYS AFTER PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE Federal Register], if you must comply with emission and operating limitations, you must operate and maintain your stationary combustion turbine, oxidation catalyst emission control device or other air pollution control equipment, and monitoring equipment in a manner consistent with good air pollution control practices for minimizing emissions at all times including during startup, shutdown, and malfunction.
units.action_summary: Prior to specified date, operate and maintain turbines, control equipment, and monitoring equipment following good practices to minimize emissions, including during SSM.

units.obligation_text: After [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE Federal Register], at all times, the owner or operator must operate and maintain any affected source, including associated air pollution control equipment and monitoring equipment, in a manner consistent with safety and good air pollution control practices for minimizing emissions.
units.action_summary: After specified date, owner/operator must operate and maintain affected source and associated equipment consistent with safety and good pollution-control practices to minimize emissions.

units.obligation_text: The general duty to minimize emissions does not require the owner or operator to make any further efforts to reduce emissions if levels required by the applicable standard have been achieved.
