units.action_summary: Limitation: owner/operator is not required to make further emission-reduction efforts once applicable standard levels are achieved.

units.obligation_text: Determination of whether a source is operating in compliance with operation and maintenance requirements will be based on information available to the Administrator which may include, but is not limited to, monitoring results, review of operation and maintenance procedures, review of operation and maintenance records, and inspection of the source.
units.action_summary: Administrator will base compliance determinations on available information such as monitoring results, procedure/record reviews, and inspections.

units.obligation_text: You must conduct the initial performance tests or other initial compliance demonstrations in Table 4 of this subpart that apply to you within 180 calendar days after the compliance date that is specified for your stationary combustion turbine in § 63.6095 and according to the provisions in § 63.7(a)(2).
units.action_summary: Conduct applicable initial performance tests or compliance demonstrations within 180 days after your compliance date and per §63.7(a)(2).

units.obligation_text: New or reconstructed stationary combustion turbines that are lean premix gas-fired stationary combustion turbines or diffusion flame gas-fired stationary combustion turbines that commenced construction before April 12, 2019 and were subject to the stay of the standards for gas-fired subcategories in § 63.6095(d) that was finalized on August 18, 2004, must conduct the initial performance test within 180 calendar days after the date the stay in § 63.6095(d) is removed from this subpart.
units.actor: owners/operators of new or reconstructed specified turbines
units.action_summary: Specified new/reconstructed turbines that were subject to stay must conduct initial performance test within 180 days after the stay is removed.

units.obligation_text: Each performance test must be conducted according to the requirements in Table 3 of this subpart.
units.action_summary: Conduct each performance test per the requirements in Table 3 of the subpart.

units.obligation_text: Before [DATE 181 DAYS AFTER PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE Federal Register], each performance test must be conducted according to the requirements of the General Provisions at § 63.7(e)(1).
units.action_summary: Prior to specified date, conduct performance tests according to §63.7(e)(1) General Provisions.

units.obligation_text: Performance tests must be conducted at high load, defined as 100 percent plus or minus 10 percent.
units.action_summary: Conduct performance tests at high load (100% ± 10%).

units.obligation_text: Before [DATE 181 DAYS AFTER PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE Federal Register], do not conduct performance tests or compliance evaluations during periods of startup, shutdown, or malfunction.
units.action_summary: Prior to specified date, performance tests and compliance evaluations are prohibited during startup, shutdown, or malfunction.

units.obligation_text: After [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE Federal Register], performance tests shall be conducted under such conditions based on representative performance of the affected source for the period being tested.
units.action_summary: After specified date, conduct performance tests under conditions representative of the source's performance during the test period.

units.obligation_text: Representative conditions exclude periods of startup and shutdown.
units.action_summary: Representative testing conditions must not include startup or shutdown periods.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator may not conduct performance tests during periods of malfunction.
units.action_summary: Performance tests are prohibited during malfunctions.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator must record the process information that is necessary to document operating conditions during the test and include in such record an explanation to support that such conditions represent normal operation.
units.action_summary: Record process information during the test and include explanation supporting that conditions represent normal operation.

units.obligation_text: Upon request, the owner or operator shall make available to the Administrator such records as may be necessary to determine the conditions of performance tests.
units.action_summary: Provide records necessary to determine test conditions to the Administrator upon request.

units.obligation_text: After [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE Federal Register], if you are required to use a continuous monitoring system (CMS), you must develop and implement a CMS quality control program that included written procedures for CMS according to § 63.8(d)(1)–(2).
units.actor: you (owner or operator required to use CMS)
units.action_summary: If required to use a CMS after specified date, develop and implement a CMS quality control program with written procedures per §63.8(d)(1)-(2).

units.obligation_text: You must keep these written procedures on record for the life of the affected source or until the affected source is no longer subject to the provisions of this part, to be made available for inspection, upon request, by the Administrator.
units.action_summary: Keep CMS written procedures on record for the life of the source (or until no longer subject) and make them available for inspection upon Administrator request.

units.obligation_text: If the performance evaluation plan is revised, the owner or operator shall keep previous (i.e., superseded) versions of the performance evaluation plan on record to be made available for inspection, upon request, by the Administrator, for a period of 5 years after each revision to the plan.
units.action_summary: When performance evaluation plan is revised, keep previous versions on record for 5 years and make them available upon Administrator request.

units.obligation_text: The program of corrective action should be included in the plan required under § 63.8(d)(2).
units.action_summary: Recommendation that corrective action program be included in required plan under §63.8(d)(2).

units.obligation_text: Before [DATE 181 DAYS AFTER PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE Federal Register], consistent with §§ 63.6(e) and 63.7(e)(1), deviations that occur during a period of startup, shutdown, and malfunction are not violations if you have operated your stationary combustion turbine in accordance with § 63.6(e)(1)(i).
units.action_summary: Prior to specified date, deviations during SSM are not violations if turbine was operated per §63.6(e)(1)(i).

units.obligation_text: Anyone who owns or operates a stationary combustion turbine which must meet the emission limitation for formaldehyde must submit a semiannual compliance report according to Table 6 of this subpart.
units.actor: anyone who owns or operates a stationary combustion turbine subject to the formaldehyde limit
units.action_summary: Submit a semiannual compliance report per Table 6 if subject to the formaldehyde emission limitation.

units.obligation_text: The semiannual compliance report must contain the information described in paragraphs (a)(1) through (5) of this section.
units.action_summary: Include specified information (paragraphs a(1)-a(5)) in the semiannual compliance report.

units.obligation_text: The semiannual compliance report must be submitted by the dates specified in paragraphs (b)(1) through (5) of this section, unless the Administrator has approved a different schedule.
units.action_summary: Submit semiannual compliance report by specified dates unless Administrator approves an alternative schedule.

units.obligation_text: After [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE Federal Register], you must submit all subsequent reports to the EPA following the procedure specified in paragraph (g) of this section.
units.action_summary: After specified date, submit all subsequent reports to EPA following procedures in paragraph (g).

units.obligation_text: Before [DATE 181 DAYS AFTER PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE Federal Register], for each deviation from an emission limitation, the compliance report must contain the information in paragraphs (a)(4)(i) through (iii) of this section.
units.action_summary: Prior to specified date, include specified information for each deviation from an emission limitation in the compliance report.

units.obligation_text: After [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE Federal Register], if a source fails to meet an applicable standard, report such events in the semiannual compliance report. Report the information specified in paragraphs (a)(5)(i) through (iv) of this section.
units.action_summary: After specified date, report failures to meet applicable standard in the semiannual compliance report and provide specified information.

units.obligation_text: Report the number of failures to meet an applicable standard. For each instance, report the start date, start time, duration, and cause of each failure, and the corrective action taken.
units.action_summary: Report count of failures and for each failure provide start date/time, duration, cause, and corrective action.

units.obligation_text: For each failure, the report must include a list of the affected sources or equipment, an estimate of the quantity of each regulated pollutant emitted over any emission limit, a description of the method used to estimate the emissions.
units.action_summary: Include list of affected sources/equipment, estimated quantity of each pollutant emitted over the limit, and method used to estimate emissions for each failure.

units.obligation_text: Information on the number, duration, and cause for monitor downtime incidents (including unknown cause, if applicable), as applicable, and the corrective action taken.
units.action_summary: Provide information on monitor downtime incidents (number, duration, cause) and corrective actions taken.

units.obligation_text: Report the total operating time of the affected source during the reporting period.
units.action_summary: Report total operating time of the affected source during the reporting period.

units.obligation_text: If you are operating as a stationary combustion turbine which fires landfill gas or digester gas equivalent to 10 percent or more of the gross heat input on an annual basis, or a stationary combustion turbine where gasified MSW is used to generate 10 percent or more of the gross heat input on an annual basis, you must submit an annual report according to Table 6 of this subpart by the date specified unless the Administrator has approved a different schedule. You must report the data specified in (c)(1) through (3) of this section.
units.actor: you (owner or operator of turbines using specified fuels ≥10%)
units.action_summary: If turbine fires specified fuels at or above 10% gross heat input annually, submit annual report per Table 6 and include specified data.

units.obligation_text: If you are operating a lean premix gas-fired stationary combustion turbine or a diffusion flame gas-fired stationary combustion turbine as defined by this subpart, and you use any quantity of distillate oil to fire any new or existing stationary combustion turbine which is located at the same major source, you must submit an annual report according to Table 6 of this subpart by the date specified unless the Administrator has approved a different schedule. You must report the data specified in (e)(1) through (3) of this section.
units.actor: you (owner or operator meeting fuel-use condition)
units.action_summary: If specified turbines use any distillate oil at same major source, submit annual report per Table 6 including specified data.

units.obligation_text: After [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE Federal Register], within 60 days after the date of completing each performance test required by this subpart, you must submit the results of the performance test (as specified in § 63.6145(f)) following the procedures specified in paragraphs (f)(1) through (3) of this section.
units.action_summary: Within 60 days after completing required performance tests, submit test results as specified, following procedures in (f)(1)-(3).

units.obligation_text: Data collected using test methods supported by the EPA’s Electronic Reporting Tool (ERT) as listed on the EPA’s ERT website at the time of the test. Submit the results of the performance test to the EPA via the Compliance and Emissions Data Reporting Interface (CEDRI), which can be accessed through the EPA’s Central Data Exchange (CDX). The data must be submitted in a file format generated through the use of the EPA’s ERT. Alternatively, you may submit an electronic file consistent with the extensible markup language (XML) schema listed on the EPA’s ERT website.
units.actor: you (owner or operator using ERT-supported test methods)
units.action_summary: For tests using ERT-supported methods, submit test results via CEDRI in ERT-generated file format or alternate XML file per ERT schema.

units.obligation_text: Data collected using test methods that are not supported by the EPA’s ERT as listed on the EPA’s ERT website at the time of the test. The results of the performance test must be included as an attachment in the ERT or an alternate electronic file consistent with the XML schema listed on the EPA’s ERT website. Submit the ERT generated package or alternative file to the EPA via CEDRI.
units.actor: you (owner or operator using non-ERT-supported methods)
units.action_summary: For tests not supported by ERT, include results as attachment in ERT or an alternate XML file and submit the package to EPA via CEDRI.

units.obligation_text: If you claim some of the information submitted under paragraph (f)(1) of this section is CBI, you must submit a complete file, including information claimed to be CBI, to the EPA. The file must be generated through the use of the EPA’s ERT or an alternate electronic file consistent with the XML schema listed on the EPA’s ERT website. Submit the file on a compact disc, flash drive, or other commonly used electronic storage medium and clearly mark the medium as CBI. Mail the electronic medium to U.S. EPA/OAQPS/CORE CBI Office, Attention: Group Leader, Measurement Policy Group, MD C404–02, 4930 Old Page Rd., Durham, NC 27703. The same file with the CBI omitted must be submitted to the EPA via the EPA’s CDX as described in paragraph (f)(1) of this section.
units.action_summary: If claiming CBI, submit complete file including CBI on physical medium marked as CBI to EPA CBI Office; also submit same file with CBI omitted via CDX per paragraph (f)(1).

units.obligation_text: If you are required to submit reports following the procedure specified in this paragraph, you must submit reports to the EPA via CEDRI, which can be accessed through the EPA’s (CDX). You must use the appropriate electronic report template on the CEDRI website (https://www.epa.gov/electronic-reporting-air-emissions/compliance-and-emissions-data-reporting-interface-cedri) for this subpart. The date report templates become available will be listed on the CEDRI website. The report must be submitted by the deadline specified in this subpart, regardless of the method in which the report is submitted.
units.actor: you (owner or operator required to submit reports electronically)
units.action_summary: Submit required reports via CEDRI using the appropriate CEDRI template and meet the report deadlines regardless of submission method.

units.obligation_text: If you claim some of the information required to be submitted via CEDRI is confidential business information (CBI), submit a complete report, including information claimed to be CBI, to the EPA. The report must be generated using the appropriate form on the CEDRI website. Submit the file on a compact disc, flash drive, or other commonly used electronic storage medium and clearly mark the medium as CBI. Mail the electronic medium to U.S. EPA/OAQPS/CORE CBI Office, Attention: Group Leader, Measurement Policy Group, MD C404–02, 4930 Old Page Rd., Durham, NC 27703. The same file with the CBI omitted must be submitted to the EPA via the EPA’s CDX as described earlier in this paragraph.
units.action_summary: If claiming CBI for reports, submit complete CBI-including file on physical medium to EPA CBI Office and also submit CBI-omitted file via CDX using appropriate CEDRI form.

units.obligation_text: If you are required to electronically submit a report through CEDRI in the EPA’s CDX, you may assert a claim of EPA system outage for failure to timely comply with the reporting requirement.
units.actor: you (owner or operator required to submit electronically)
units.action_summary: You may assert an EPA system outage claim for failure to timely submit reports electronically under specified conditions.

units.obligation_text: You must have been or will be precluded from accessing CEDRI and submitting a required report within the time prescribed due to an outage of either the EPA’s CEDRI or CDX systems.
units.action_summary: To assert an outage claim, you must have been or will be unable to access CEDRI/CDX within the prescribed submission time due to outage.

units.obligation_text: The outage must have occurred within the period of time beginning five business days prior to the date that the submission is due.
units.actor: you (owner or operator asserting outage claim)
units.action_summary: Outage must have occurred within five business days before the submission due date to qualify for outage claim.

units.obligation_text: The outage may be planned or unplanned.
units.action_summary: Outage eligible for claim can be either planned or unplanned.

units.obligation_text: You must submit notification to the Administrator in writing as soon as possible following the date you first knew, or through due diligence should have known, that the event may cause or has caused a delay in reporting.
units.action_summary: Promptly notify the Administrator in writing when you know or should have known an event may cause or caused a reporting delay.

units.obligation_text: You must provide to the Administrator a written description identifying: (i) The date(s) and time(s) when CDX or CEDRI was accessed and the system was unavailable; (ii) A rationale for attributing the delay in reporting beyond the regulatory deadline to EPA system outage; (iii) Measures taken or to be taken to minimize the delay in reporting; and (iv) The date by which you propose to report, or if you have already met the reporting requirement at the time of the notification, the date you reported.
units.action_summary: Provide Administrator with written description including outage dates/times, rationale attributing delay to EPA outage, mitigation measures, and proposed or actual reporting date.

units.obligation_text: The decision to accept the claim of EPA system outage and allow an extension to the reporting deadline is solely within the discretion of the Administrator.
units.action_summary: Administrator has sole discretion to accept outage claims and grant extensions.
units.modal_raw: is solely within the discretion of

units.obligation_text: In any circumstance, the report must be submitted electronically as soon as possible after the outage is resolved.
units.action_summary: Submit the report electronically as soon as possible after the EPA outage is resolved.

units.obligation_text: If you are required to electronically submit a report through CEDRI in the EPA’s CDX, you may assert a claim of force majeure for failure to timely comply with the reporting requirement.
units.actor: you (owner or operator required to submit electronically)
units.action_summary: You may assert a force majeure claim for failure to timely submit electronic reports under specified conditions.

units.obligation_text: You may submit a claim if a force majeure event is about to occur, occurs, or has occurred or there are lingering effects from such an event within the period of time beginning five business days prior to the date the submission is due. For the purposes of this section, a force majeure event is defined as an event that will be or has been caused by circumstances beyond the control of the affected facility, its contractors, or any entity controlled by the affected facility that prevents you from complying with the requirement to submit a report electronically within the time period prescribed. Examples of such events are acts of nature (e.g., hurricanes, earthquakes, or floods), acts of war or terrorism, or equipment failure or safety hazard beyond the control of the affected facility (e.g., large scale power outage).
units.action_summary: Permission to submit force majeure claim if qualifying event occurs within five business days before due date; defines force majeure and examples.

units.obligation_text: You must submit notification to the Administrator in writing as soon as possible following the date you first knew, or through due diligence should have known, that the event may cause or has caused a delay in reporting.
units.action_summary: Promptly notify Administrator in writing when you know or should have known a force majeure event may cause or caused a reporting delay.

units.obligation_text: You must provide to the Administrator: (i) A written description of the force majeure event; (ii) A rationale for attributing the delay in reporting beyond the regulatory deadline to the force majeure event; (iii) Measures taken or to be taken to minimize the delay in reporting; and (iv) The date by which you propose to report, or if you have already met the reporting requirement at the time of the notification, the date you reported.
units.action_summary: Provide Administrator with written description of event, rationale linking delay to event, mitigation measures, and proposed or actual reporting date.

units.obligation_text: The decision to accept the claim of force majeure and allow an extension to the reporting deadline is solely within the discretion of the Administrator.
units.action_summary: Administrator has sole discretion to accept force majeure claims and grant extensions.
units.modal_raw: is solely within the discretion of

units.obligation_text: In any circumstance, the reporting must occur as soon as possible after the force majeure event occurs.
units.action_summary: Report as soon as possible after the force majeure event.

units.obligation_text: You must keep the records as described in paragraphs (a)(1) through (7) of this section.
units.action_summary: Maintain the records specified in paragraphs (a)(1)-(7).

units.obligation_text: Before [DATE 181 DAYS AFTER PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE Federal Register], records of the occurrence and duration of each startup, shutdown, or malfunction as required in § 63.10(b)(2)(i).
units.action_summary: Prior to specified date, keep records of occurrence and duration of each startup, shutdown, or malfunction per §63.10(b)(2)(i).

units.obligation_text: Before [DATE 181 DAYS AFTER PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE Federal Register], records of the occurrence and duration of each malfunction of the air pollution control equipment, if applicable, as required in § 63.10(b)(2)(ii).
units.action_summary: Prior to specified date, keep records of occurrence and duration of each malfunction of air pollution control equipment as required.

units.obligation_text: Records of all maintenance on the air pollution control equipment as required in § 63.10(b)(2)(iii).
units.action_summary: Keep records of all maintenance on air pollution control equipment as required.

units.obligation_text: After [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE Federal Register], records of the date, time, and duration of each startup period, recording the periods when the affected source was subject to the standard applicable to startup.
units.action_summary: After specified date, record date, time, and duration of each startup period and when the source was subject to startup standard.

units.obligation_text: In the event that an affected unit fails to meet an applicable standard, record the number of failures. For each failure record the date, time, cause, and duration of each failure.
units.action_summary: If unit fails to meet a standard, record number of failures and for each failure the date, time, cause, and duration.

units.obligation_text: For each failure to meet an applicable standard, record and retain a list of the affected sources or equipment, an estimate of the quantity of each regulated pollutant emitted over any emission limit and a description of the method used to estimate the emissions.
units.action_summary: For each failure, record affected sources/equipment, estimate pollutant quantities emitted over limits, and describe estimation method.

units.obligation_text: Record actions taken to minimize emissions in accordance with § 63.6105(c), and any corrective actions taken to return the affected unit to its normal or usual manner of operation.
units.action_summary: Record actions taken to minimize emissions per §63.6105(c) and corrective actions to return unit to normal operation.

units.obligation_text: Any records required to be maintained by this part that are submitted electronically via the EPA’s CEDRI may be maintained in electronic format.
units.action_summary: Records submitted electronically via CEDRI may be maintained electronically.

units.obligation_text: This ability to maintain electronic copies does not affect the requirement for facilities to make records, data, and reports available upon request to a delegated air agency or the EPA as part of an on-site compliance evaluation.
units.action_summary: Facilities remain required to make records, data, and reports available upon request during on-site compliance evaluations despite electronic record-keeping permission.
units.modal_raw: does not affect the requirement to

units.obligation_text: You must meet the following emission limitations ... limit the concentration of formaldehyde to 91 ppbvd or less at 15-percent O2, except during turbine startup.
units.actor: you (owner or operator of new or reconstructed stationary combustion turbine described)
units.action_summary: Limit formaldehyde concentration to ≤91 ppbvd at 15% O2 (except during startup).

units.obligation_text: During turbine startup, you must minimize the turbine’s time spent at idle or holding at low load levels and minimize the turbine’s startup time to a period needed for appropriate and safe loading of the turbine, not to exceed 1 hour for simple cycle stationary combustion turbines and 3 hours for combined cycle stationary combustion turbines, after which time the formaldehyde emission limitation of 91 ppbvd or less at 15 percent O2 applies.
units.action_summary: During startup, minimize idle/low-load time and keep startup duration to necessary safe loading time, not exceeding 1 hour (simple) or 3 hours (combined), after which the formaldehyde limit applies.

units.obligation_text: Demonstrate formaldehyde emissions meet the emission limitations specified in Table 1 by a performance test initially and on an annual basis.
units.action_summary: Perform initial and annual performance tests to demonstrate formaldehyde emissions meet Table 1 limits.

units.obligation_text: Using Test Method 320 of 40 CFR part 63, appendix A; ASTM D6348–12e1 provided that the test plan preparation and implementation provisions of Annexes A1 through A8 are followed and the %R as determined in Annex A5 is equal or greater than 70% and less than or equal to 130%; or other methods approved by the Administrator.
units.action_summary: Use specified test methods (Test Method 320 or ASTM D6348–12e1 meeting Annex criteria) or other Administrator-approved methods for formaldehyde testing.
units.modal_raw: must / or other methods approved by the Administrator

units.obligation_text: Formaldehyde concentration must be corrected to 15 percent O2, dry basis.
units.action_summary: Correct measured formaldehyde concentration to dry basis at 15% O2.

units.obligation_text: Results of this test consist of the average of the three 1 hour runs.
units.action_summary: Report test results as the average of three one-hour runs.

units.obligation_text: Test must be conducted within 10 percent of 100 percent load.
units.action_summary: Conduct the test at load within ±10% of 100% load.

units.obligation_text: Select the sampling port location and the number of traverse points using Method 1 or 1A of 40 CFR part 60, appendix A; if using an air pollution control device, the sampling site must be located at the outlet of the air pollution control device.
units.action_summary: Choose sampling port location and traverse points per Method 1 or 1A; if testing after a control device, locate sampling at the device outlet.

units.obligation_text: Determine the O2 concentration at the sampling port location using Method 3A or 3B of 40 CFR part 60, appendix A; ANSI/ASME PTC 19–10–1981 (Part 10) manual portion only; ASTM D6522–11 if the turbine is fueled by natural gas. Measurements to determine O2 concentration must be made at the same time as the performance test.
units.action_summary: Measure O2 concentration at the sampling port using specified methods concurrently with the performance test.

units.obligation_text: Determine the moisture content at the sampling port location for the purposes of correcting the formaldehyde concentration to a dry basis using Method 4 of 40 CFR part 60, appendix A or Test Method 320 of 40 CFR part 63, appendix A, or ASTM D6348–12e1. Measurements to determine moisture content must be made at the same time as the performance test.
units.action_summary: Measure moisture content at the sampling port using specified methods concurrently with the performance test to correct formaldehyde to dry basis.

title: Oil and Natural Gas Sector: Emission Standards for New, Reconstructed, and Modified Sources Review; Notice of Public Hearing on October 17, 2019

units.obligation_text: individuals planning to attend the hearing should be prepared to show valid picture identification to the security staff to gain access to the meeting room
units.actor: individuals planning to attend the hearing
units.action_summary: Attendees should bring valid photo ID to gain access to the hearing facility.

units.obligation_text: The EPA will accept government-issued IDs, including driver's licenses from the District of Columbia and all states and territories
units.action_summary: EPA will accept government-issued IDs (including state/DC driver's licenses) for entry.

units.obligation_text: Acceptable alternative forms of identification include: Federal employee badges, passports, enhanced driver's licenses, and military identification cards
units.action_summary: Attendees may use listed alternative IDs for entry.

units.obligation_text: Any objects brought into the building need to fit through the security screening system, such as a purse, laptop bag, or small backpack
units.action_summary: Items brought in must be small enough to fit through security screening.

units.obligation_text: Demonstrations will not be allowed on federal property for security reasons
units.action_summary: Demonstrations are prohibited on the federal property where the hearing is held.

units.obligation_text: The EPA will begin pre-registering speakers for the hearing upon publication of this document in the Federal Register
units.action_summary: EPA will start pre-registering speakers once the document is published.

units.obligation_text: To register to speak at the October 17, 2019, hearing, please use the online registration form ... or contact Virginia Hunt at (919) 541-0832 to register to speak at the hearing
units.action_summary: Prospective speakers must register using the online form or by contacting Virginia Hunt to speak.

units.obligation_text: The last day to pre-register to speak at the hearing will be October 14, 2019
units.action_summary: Prospective speakers must pre-register by October 14, 2019.

units.obligation_text: If the EPA receives a high volume of requests, we may continue the public hearing on October 18, 2019, at the location described above
units.action_summary: EPA may extend the hearing to October 18, 2019 if there are many registration requests.

units.obligation_text: We encourage the public to register to speak as soon as possible after this document publishes in order to inform that decision
units.action_summary: Public is urged to register early so EPA can decide about extending the hearing.

units.obligation_text: The EPA does not intend to publish a document in the Federal Register announcing the potential addition of a second day for the public hearing or any updates to the information on the hearing described in this document
units.action_summary: EPA does not plan to publish a Federal Register notice if a second hearing day is added or information is updated.

units.obligation_text: Please monitor [EPA website] or contact Virginia Hunt at (919) 541-0832 to determine if there are any updates to the information on the hearing
units.action_summary: Interested parties should check the EPA website or contact Virginia Hunt for hearing updates.

units.obligation_text: If a second day of the public hearing is scheduled, we will update the website with this information by October 10, 2019
units.action_summary: EPA will post an update on the website by October 10 if a second hearing day is scheduled.

units.obligation_text: On October 15, 2019, the EPA will post ... a general agenda for the hearing that will list pre-registered speakers in approximate order
units.action_summary: EPA will post a general agenda listing pre-registered speakers on October 15, 2019.

units.obligation_text: The EPA will make every effort to follow the schedule as closely as possible on the day of the hearing; however, please plan for the hearing to run either ahead of schedule or behind schedule
units.action_summary: EPA will try to follow the agenda; attendees should expect possible schedule changes.
units.modal_raw: will make every effort / please plan

units.obligation_text: Additionally, requests to speak will be taken the day of the hearing at the hearing registration desk
units.action_summary: On the hearing day, the registration desk will accept additional requests to speak.

units.obligation_text: The EPA will make every effort to accommodate all speakers who arrive and register, although preferences on speaking times may not be able to be fulfilled
units.action_summary: EPA will try to accommodate all registered speakers but may not honor specific time preferences.

units.obligation_text: Each commenter will have 5 minutes to provide oral testimony
units.action_summary: Speakers are allotted 5 minutes for oral testimony.

units.obligation_text: If there are no additional registered speakers, the EPA will end the hearing 2 hours after the last registered speaker has concluded their comments
units.action_summary: If no more speakers are registered, EPA will end the hearing two hours after the last speaker finishes.

units.obligation_text: The EPA may ask clarifying questions during the oral presentations but will not respond to the presentations at that time
units.action_summary: EPA may ask clarifying questions during presentations but will not provide responses at that time.

units.obligation_text: Written statements and supporting information submitted during the comment period will be considered with the same weight as oral comments and supporting information presented at the public hearing
units.action_summary: EPA will treat written submissions received during the comment period the same as oral comments from the hearing.

units.obligation_text: Verbatim transcripts of the hearings and written statements will be included in the docket for the rulemaking
units.action_summary: EPA will place hearing transcripts and written statements into the rulemaking docket.

units.obligation_text: The EPA also encourages commenters to provide the EPA with a copy of their oral testimony electronically (via email) or in hard copy form
units.action_summary: Commenters are encouraged to provide a copy of oral testimony electronically or in hard copy.

units.obligation_text: If you require the service of a translator or special accommodations such as audio description, please pre-register for the hearing and describe your needs by October 14, 2019
units.actor: persons requiring translator or special accommodations
units.action_summary: People needing translation or special accommodations must pre-register and state needs by October 14, 2019.

units.obligation_text: We may not be able to arrange accommodations without advanced notice
units.action_summary: EPA might be unable to provide accommodations if not given advanced notice.

units.obligation_text: The EPA will not provide audiovisual equipment for presentations
units.action_summary: EPA will not supply audiovisual equipment for hearing presentations.

units.obligation_text: Any media presentations should be submitted to the public docket at https://www.regulations.gov/, identified by Docket ID No. EPA-HQ-OAR-2017-0757
units.action_summary: Media presentations must be submitted to the public docket at Regulations.gov with the specified docket ID.

units.obligation_text: The EPA must receive comments on the proposed action no later than 60 days after it publishes in the Federal Register
units.action_summary: Commenters must submit comments so EPA receives them within 60 days of publication.

title: Oil and Natural Gas Sector: Emission Standards for New, Reconstructed, and Modified  Sources Review

units.obligation_text: The potential for VOC emissions must be calculated using a generally accepted model or calculation methodology, based on the maximum average daily throughput determined for a 30-day period of production prior to the applicable emission determination deadline specified in this section.
units.actor: owner or operator (party determining potential VOC emissions)
units.action_summary: Calculate potential VOC emissions using a generally accepted model/method based on maximum average daily throughput for a 30-day production period before the applicable deadline.

units.obligation_text: For storage vessels that are skid-mounted or permanently attached to something that is mobile (such as trucks, railcars, barges or ships), records indicating the number of consecutive days that the vessel is located between the wellhead and the point of custody transfer to the natural gas transmission and storage segment.
units.action_summary: Maintain records showing the number of consecutive days a skid-mounted or permanently attached storage vessel is located between the wellhead and custody transfer to the transmission and storage segment.

units.obligation_text: If a storage vessel is removed from a site and, within 30 days, is either returned to or replaced by another storage vessel at the site to serve the same or similar function, then the entire period since the original storage vessel was first located at the site, including the days when the storage vessel was removed, will be added to the count towards the number of consecutive days.
units.action_summary: If a storage vessel is removed and returned or replaced within 30 days, include the entire original period (including removal days) in the count of consecutive days.

units.obligation_text: The potential for VOC emissions must be calculated using a generally accepted model or calculation methodology, based on the maximum average daily throughput, as defined in § 60.5430a, determined for a 30-day period of production prior to the applicable emission determination deadline specified in this subsection.
units.actor: owner or operator (party determining potential VOC emissions)
units.action_summary: Calculate potential VOC emissions with a generally accepted method based on maximum average daily throughput for a 30-day period before the applicable deadline.

units.obligation_text: For purposes of § 60.5397a, a 'modification' to a compressor station occurs when: (1) An additional compressor is installed at a compressor station;
units.actor: compressor station owner or operator / compressor station
units.action_summary: Installing an additional compressor at a compressor station constitutes a 'modification' for § 60.5397a purposes.

units.obligation_text: For purposes of § 60.5397a, a 'modification' to a compressor station occurs when: (2) One or more compressors at a compressor station is replaced by one or more compressors of greater total horsepower than the compressor(s) being replaced.
units.actor: compressor station owner or operator / compressor station
units.action_summary: Replacing one or more compressors with compressors of greater total horsepower constitutes a 'modification'.

units.obligation_text: When one or more compressors is replaced by one or more compressors of an equal or smaller total horsepower than the compressor(s) being replaced, installation of the replacement compressor(s) does not trigger a modification of the compressor station for purposes of § 60.5397a.
units.actor: compressor station owner or operator / installation of replacement compressors
units.action_summary: Replacing compressors with equal or smaller total horsepower does not constitute a 'modification'.

units.obligation_text: If you are the owner or operator of a well affected facility as described in § 60.5365a(a) that also meets the criteria for a well affected facility in § 60.5365(a) of subpart OOOO of this part, you must reduce VOC emissions by complying with paragraphs (a) through (g) of this section.
units.action_summary: Owners/operators of qualifying well affected facilities must reduce VOC emissions by complying with paragraphs (a)-(g) of § 60.5375a.

units.obligation_text: If you own or operate a well affected facility as described in § 60.5365a(a) that does not meet the criteria for a well affected facility in § 60.5365(a) of subpart OOOO of this part, you must reduce VOC emissions by complying with paragraphs (f)(3), (f)(4) or (g) of this section for each well completion operation with hydraulic fracturing prior to November 30, 2016, and you must comply with paragraphs (a) through (g) of this section for each well completion operation with hydraulic fracturing on or after November 30, 2016.
units.action_summary: Owners/operators of well affected facilities that do not meet the other criteria must follow specified paragraphs for well completions with hydraulic fracturing before Nov 30, 2016, and comply with paragraphs (a)-(g) on/after that date.

units.obligation_text: You must comply with the VOC standards in paragraphs (a) through (d) of this section for each centrifugal compressor affected facility.
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must follow the VOC standards in paragraphs (a)-(d) for each centrifugal compressor affected facility.

units.obligation_text: You must reduce VOC emissions from each centrifugal compressor wet seal fluid degassing system by 95.0 percent.
units.action_summary: Reduce VOC emissions from each centrifugal compressor wet seal fluid degassing system by 95%.

units.obligation_text: You must reduce VOC emissions by complying with the standards in paragraphs (a) through (d) of this section for each reciprocating compressor affected facility.
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must meet the VOC standards in paragraphs (a)-(d) for each reciprocating compressor affected facility.

units.obligation_text: Collect the VOC emissions from the rod packing using a rod packing emissions collection system that operates under negative pressure and route the rod packing emissions to a process through a closed vent system that meets the requirements of § 60.5411a(a) and (d).
units.action_summary: Collect rod packing VOC emissions with a negative-pressure collection system and route them through a closed vent system meeting § 60.5411a(a) and (d).

units.obligation_text: For each pneumatic controller affected facility you must comply with the VOC standards, based on natural gas as a surrogate for VOC, in either paragraph (b)(1) or (c)(1) of this section, as applicable.
units.action_summary: Owners/operators of pneumatic controller affected facilities must meet the VOC standards in either paragraph (b)(1) or (c)(1), using natural gas as a surrogate for VOC.

units.obligation_text: Pneumatic controllers meeting the conditions in paragraph (a) of this section are exempt from this requirement.
units.actor: pneumatic controllers meeting the conditions in paragraph (a)
units.action_summary: Pneumatic controllers that meet the specified paragraph (a) conditions are exempt from the VOC standards requirement.

units.obligation_text: For each pneumatic pump affected facility you must comply with the VOC standards, based on natural gas as a surrogate for VOC, in either paragraph (a) or (b) of this section, as applicable, on or after November 30, 2016.
units.action_summary: Owners/operators of pneumatic pump affected facilities must meet the VOC standards in either paragraph (a) or (b) on or after Nov 30, 2016.

units.obligation_text: For each affected facility under § 60.5365a(i) and (j), you must reduce VOC emissions by complying with the requirements of paragraphs (a) through (j) of this section.
units.action_summary: Owners/operators of affected facilities under § 60.5365a(i) and (j) must comply with paragraphs (a)-(j) of § 60.5397a to reduce VOC emissions.

units.obligation_text: If, in the Administrator’s judgment, an alternative means of emission limitation will achieve a reduction in VOC emissions at least equivalent to the reduction in VOC emissions achieved under § 60.5375a, § 60.5385a, and § 60.5397a, the Administrator will publish, in the Federal Register, a notice permitting the use of that alternative means for the purpose of compliance with § 60.5375a, § 60.5385a, and § 60.5397a. The notice may condition permission on requirements related to the operation and maintenance of the alternative means.
units.action_summary: Administrator may publish a Federal Register notice permitting an alternative means of emission limitation if it achieves equivalent VOC reductions; the notice may impose operation and maintenance conditions.

units.obligation_text: Operation and maintenance procedures and other provisions necessary to ensure reduction in VOC emissions at least equivalent to the reduction in VOC emissions achieved under § 60.5397a.
units.actor: applicant for alternative means / holder of the alternative means permission
units.action_summary: Include operation and maintenance procedures and other provisions necessary to ensure VOC reductions at least equivalent to those under § 60.5397a in the application or as required by the notice.

units.obligation_text: After notice and opportunity for public comment, the Administrator will determine whether the requested alternative fugitive emissions standard will achieve at least equivalent emission reduction(s) in VOC emissions as the reduction(s) achieved under the applicable requirement(s) for which an alternative is being requested, and will publish the determination in the Federal Register.
units.action_summary: Administrator will decide, after notice and comment, whether a requested alternative fugitive emissions standard achieves equivalent VOC reductions and will publish the decision in the Federal Register.

units.obligation_text: You may apply to the Administrator for permission to use an alternative means of emission limitation that achieves a reduction in emissions of VOC at least equivalent to that achieved by the controls required in this subpart according to the requirements of § 60.5402a.
units.action_summary: Owners/operators may apply to the Administrator for permission to use an alternative emission control approach that achieves equivalent VOC reductions, following § 60.5402a.

units.obligation_text: If, in the Administrator’s judgment, an alternative means of emission limitation will achieve a reduction in VOC emissions at least equivalent to the reduction in VOC emissions achieved under any design, equipment, work practice or operational standard, the Administrator will publish, in the Federal Register, a notice permitting the use of that alternative means for the purpose of compliance with that standard. The notice may condition permission on requirements related to the operation and maintenance of the alternative means.
units.action_summary: Administrator may publish a notice permitting use of an alternative means for compliance if it achieves equivalent VOC reductions; the notice may impose operation/maintenance conditions.

units.obligation_text: The application must include operation, maintenance and other provisions necessary to assure reduction in VOC emissions at least equivalent to the reduction in VOC emissions achieved under the design, equipment, work practice or operational standard in paragraph (a) of this section by including the information specified in paragraphs (d)(1)(i) through (x) of this section.
units.actor: applicant for alternative means / owner or operator
units.action_summary: An application for an alternative means must include operation, maintenance, and other provisions and the information listed in paragraphs (d)(1)(i)-(x) to ensure equivalent VOC reductions.

units.obligation_text: To achieve initial compliance with the VOC standards for each well completion operation conducted at your well affected facility you must comply with paragraphs (a)(1) through (4) of this section.
units.action_summary: To demonstrate initial compliance for well completions, follow paragraphs (a)(1)-(4) of § 60.5410a.

units.obligation_text: To achieve initial compliance with standards for your centrifugal compressor affected facility you must reduce VOC emissions from each centrifugal compressor wet seal fluid degassing system by 95.0 percent or greater as required by § 60.5380a(a) and as demonstrated by the requirements of § 60.5413a.
units.action_summary: To achieve initial compliance for centrifugal compressors, reduce VOCs from each wet seal fluid degassing system by 95% or greater and demonstrate per § 60.5413a.

units.obligation_text: To achieve initial compliance with VOC emission standards for your pneumatic controller affected facility you must comply with the requirements specified in paragraphs (d)(1) through (6) of this section, as applicable.
units.action_summary: To achieve initial compliance for pneumatic controllers, follow the applicable requirements in paragraphs (d)(1)-(6) of § 60.5410a.

units.obligation_text: For affected facilities at onshore natural gas processing plants, initial compliance with the VOC standards is demonstrated if you are in compliance with the requirements of § 60.5400a.
units.action_summary: Initial compliance is demonstrated by complying with the requirements of § 60.5400a for affected facilities at onshore natural gas processing plants.

units.obligation_text: You must reduce the mass content of VOC in the gases vented to the device by 95.0 percent by weight or greater as determined in accordance with the requirements of § 60.5413a(b), with the exceptions noted in § 60.5413a(a).
units.action_summary: Reduce VOC mass content in gases vented to control devices by 95% by weight or greater as determined per § 60.5413a(b), subject to noted exceptions.

units.obligation_text: Each vapor recovery device (e.g., carbon adsorption system or condenser) or other non-destructive control device must be designed and operated to reduce the mass content of VOC in the gases vented to the device by 95.0 percent by weight or greater as determined in accordance with the requirements of § 60.5413a(b).
units.actor: owner or operator / designer/operator of vapor recovery devices
units.action_summary: Vapor recovery and other non-destructive control devices must be designed and operated to achieve at least 95% VOC mass reduction as determined per § 60.5413a(b).

units.obligation_text: As an alternative to the performance testing requirements, you may demonstrate initial compliance by conducting a design analysis for vapor recovery devices according to the requirements of § 60.5413a(c).
units.action_summary: As an alternative to performance testing, owners/operators may demonstrate initial compliance for vapor recovery devices via a design analysis per § 60.5413a(c).

units.obligation_text: A manufacturer must demonstrate a destruction efficiency of at least 95 percent for THC, as propane.
units.action_summary: Manufacturers must demonstrate at least 95% THC (as propane) destruction efficiency for control devices.

units.obligation_text: You must reduce VOC emissions from the wet seal fluid degassing system by 95.0 percent or greater.
units.action_summary: Continuously reduce VOC emissions from wet seal fluid degassing systems by at least 95%.

units.obligation_text: For affected facilities at onshore natural gas processing plants, continuous compliance with VOC requirements is demonstrated if you are in compliance with the requirements of § 60.5400a.
units.action_summary: Continuous compliance is demonstrated by complying with § 60.5400a for affected facilities at onshore natural gas processing plants.

units.obligation_text: For storage vessels that are skid-mounted or permanently attached to something that is mobile (such as trucks, railcars, barges or ships), records indicating the number of consecutive days that the vessel is located at a site in the oil and natural gas production segment or natural gas processing segment.
units.action_summary: Maintain records of the number of consecutive days a skid-mounted or permanently attached storage vessel is located at a site in the oil/natural gas production or natural gas processing segment.

units.obligation_text: If a storage vessel is removed from a site and, within 30 days, is either returned to the site or replaced by another storage vessel at the site to serve the same or similar function, then the entire period since the original storage vessel was first located at the site, including the days when the storage vessel was removed, will be added to the count towards the number of consecutive days.
units.action_summary: If a storage vessel is removed and returned or replaced within 30 days, count the entire original period (including removal days) toward consecutive days at the site.

title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Organic Liquids Distribution (Non-Gasoline) Residual Risk and Technology Review

units.obligation_text: To enforce any edition other than that specified in this section, the EPA must publish a document in the Federal Register
units.action_summary: Publish a Federal Register document to enforce an edition other than that specified

units.obligation_text: To enforce any edition other than that specified in this section, ... and the material must be available to the public.
units.action_summary: Ensure the incorporated material is available to the public when enforcing a different edition

units.obligation_text: Except as specified in paragraph (e) of this section, if you have a new or reconstructed affected source, you must comply with this subpart according to the schedule identified in paragraph (a)(1), (2), or (3) of this section, as applicable.
units.actor: owner/operator of a new or reconstructed affected source (you)
units.action_summary: Comply with this subpart on the schedule in (a)(1)-(3)

units.obligation_text: Except as specified in paragraph (e) of this section, if you have an existing affected source, you must comply with this subpart according to the schedule identified in paragraph (b)(1), (2), or (3) of this section, as applicable.
units.actor: owner/operator of an existing affected source (you)
units.action_summary: Comply with this subpart on the schedule in (b)(1)-(3)

units.obligation_text: You must meet the notification requirements in §§ 63.2343 and 63.2382(a), as applicable, according to the schedules in § 63.2382(a) and (b)(1) through (2) and in subpart A of this part.
units.action_summary: Meet notification requirements in specified sections according to their schedules

units.obligation_text: An affected source that commenced construction or reconstruction on or before October 21, 2019, must be in compliance with the requirements listed in paragraphs (e)(1) through (7) of this section upon initial startup or [date 3 years after date of publication of final rule in the Federal Register], whichever is later. An affected source that commenced construction or reconstruction after October 21, 2019, must be in compliance with the requirements listed in paragraphs (e)(1) through (7) of this section upon initial startup.
units.action_summary: Be in compliance with the subset of requirements (e)(1)-(7) by initial startup or specified dates

units.obligation_text: The requirements for storage tanks not requiring control specified in § 63.2343(b)(4) through (7).
units.action_summary: Comply with §63.2343(b)(4)-(7) requirements for storage tanks not requiring control

units.obligation_text: The requirements for storage tanks at an existing affected source specified in § 63.2346(a)(5) and (6), § 63.2386(d)(3)(iii), § 63.2396(a)(4), Table 2 to this subpart, footnote (2), and Table 2b to this subpart.
units.action_summary: Comply with listed storage tank requirements for existing affected sources

units.obligation_text: The equipment leak requirements specified in § 63.2346(l), Table 4 to this subpart, item 7, and footnote (1), Table 10 to this subpart, item 5.b.i and footnote (1).
units.action_summary: Comply with specified equipment leak requirements

units.obligation_text: The fenceline monitoring requirements specified in § 63.2348, § 63.2386(k), and § 63.2390(i) according to the compliance dates specified in paragraph (f) of this section.
units.action_summary: Comply with fenceline monitoring requirements in listed sections per §63.2342(f) schedule

units.obligation_text: The flare requirements specified in § 63.2346(k), § 63.2382(d)(2)(ix), § 63.2386(d)(5), § 63.2390(h), Table 2 to this subpart, footnote (1), Table 3 to this subpart, item 7.d, Table 8 to this subpart, items 1.a.iii and 2.a.iii, and Table 9 to this subpart, item 7.e.
units.action_summary: Comply with the listed flare-related requirements

units.obligation_text: The requirements specified in § 63.2346(m), § 63.2350(d), § 63.2366(c), § 63.2390(f) and (g), § 63.2386(c)(11) and (12), § 63.2386(d)(1)(xiii) and (f) through (j), § 63.2378(e), Table 9 to this subpart, footnote (1), and Table 10 to this subpart, items 1.a.i and 2.a.ii.
units.action_summary: Comply with listed miscellaneous requirements

units.obligation_text: The performance testing requirements specified in § 63.2354(b)(6).
units.action_summary: Comply with the performance testing requirements in §63.2354(b)(6)

units.obligation_text: For each OLD operation complying with the requirements in § 63.2348:
units.action_summary: Introductory parent for obligations related to OLD operations complying via §63.2348

units.obligation_text: An affected source that commenced construction or reconstruction on or before October 21, 2019, must submit modeling results, proposed analytes, and action levels according to the requirements of § 63.2348(b) upon initial startup or [date 1 year after date of publication of final rule in the Federal Register], whichever is later. All affected sources that commenced construction or reconstruction after October 21, 2019, must submit modeling results, proposed analytes and action levels according to the requirements of § 63.2348(b) as part of your permit application for the new OLD operations.
units.action_summary: Submit modeling results, proposed analytes, and action levels per §63.2348(b) by specified deadlines or with permit application

units.obligation_text: An affected source that commenced construction or reconstruction on or before October 21, 2019, must obtain approval of the modeling results, proposed analytes, and action levels submitted in paragraph (f)(1) of this section and be in compliance with all requirements of § 63.2348 upon initial startup or [date 2 years after date of publication of final rule in the Federal Register], whichever is later. An affected source that commenced construction or reconstruction after October 21, 2019, must obtain approval of the modeling results, proposed analytes, and action levels submitted in paragraph (f)(1) of this section and must be in compliance with all requirements listed in § 63.2348 by initial startup.
units.action_summary: Obtain approval of modeling/analytes/action levels and be in compliance with §63.2348 by specified deadlines

units.obligation_text: For each storage tank subject to this subpart having a capacity of less than 18.9 cubic meters (5,000 gallons), you must comply with paragraph (e) of this section.
units.actor: owner/operator (you) of each storage tank < 18.9 m3
units.action_summary: For small storage tanks (<5,000 gal) comply with §63.2343(e)

units.obligation_text: Also, for each storage tank subject to this subpart having a capacity of less than 18.9 cubic meters (5,000 gallons) and for each transfer rack subject to this subpart that only unloads organic liquids (i.e., no organic liquids are loaded at any of the transfer racks), you must keep documentation that verifies that each storage tank and transfer rack identified in paragraph (a) of this section is not required to be controlled. The documentation must be kept up-to-date ... and must be in a form suitable and readily available for expeditious inspection and review according to § 63.10(b)(1), including records stored in electronic form in a separate location.
units.action_summary: Keep up-to-date documentation verifying that small storage tanks and certain transfer racks are not required to be controlled, and keep it available in a suitable form

units.obligation_text: The documentation may consist of identification of the tanks and transfer racks identified in paragraph (a) of this section on a plant site plan or process and instrumentation diagram (P&ID).
units.action_summary: Allow the documentation to consist of site plan or P&ID identification

units.obligation_text: Except as specified in paragraph (b)(7) of this section, for each storage tank subject to this subpart having a capacity of 18.9 cubic meters (5,000 gallons) or more that is not subject to control based on the criteria specified in Table 2 to this subpart, items 1 through 6, you must comply with the requirements specified in paragraphs (b)(1) through (6) of this section.
units.actor: owner/operator (you) of storage tanks ≥ 18.9 m3 not subject to control per Table 2
units.action_summary: Comply with the requirements in (b)(1)-(6) for larger storage tanks not subject to control per Table 2

units.obligation_text: Beginning no later than the compliance dates specified in § 63.2342(e), you must monitor each potential source of vapor leakage from each fixed roof storage tank and its closure devices for leaks as specified in paragraphs (b)(4)(i) through (iii) of this section.
units.action_summary: Monitor potential vapor leakage sources from fixed roof tanks per specified procedures and schedule

units.obligation_text: Conduct monitoring using Method 21 of part 60, appendix A–7 of this chapter within 90 days after the initial fill. You must conduct subsequent monitoring no later than 1 year after previous monitoring is performed, provided the fixed roof storage tank contains organic liquid.
units.action_summary: Use Method 21 within 90 days after initial fill and annually thereafter (if tank contains organic liquid)

units.obligation_text: Calibrate the instrument before use on the day of its use according to the procedures in Method 21 of 40 CFR part 60, appendix A–7 of this chapter. Calibration gases must be zero air and a mixture of methane in air at a concentration of no greater than 2,000 parts per million.
units.action_summary: Calibrate monitoring instrument each day of use per Method 21 and use specified calibration gases

units.obligation_text: Perform a calibration drift assessment, at a minimum, at the end of each monitoring day using the same calibration gas that was used to calibrate the instrument before use. Follow the procedures in Section 10.1 of Method 21 of part 60, appendix A–7 to this chapter, except do not adjust the meter readout to correspond to the calibration gas value. Divide the arithmetic difference of the initial and post-test calibration response by the corresponding calibration gas value and multiply by 100 to express the calibration drift as a percentage.
units.action_summary: Perform end-of-day calibration drift assessment per Method 21 procedures (without adjusting readout) and calculate drift percentage

units.obligation_text: If the calibration drift assessment shows a negative drift of more than 10 percent from the initial calibration response, you must re-monitor all equipment monitored since the last calibration with instrument readings below the appropriate leak definition and above the leak definition multiplied by (100 minus the percent of negative drift/divided by 100).
units.action_summary: Re-monitor equipment if calibration drift shows >10% negative drift

units.obligation_text: An instrument reading of 500 parts per million by volume (ppmv) or greater defines a leak.
units.action_summary: Treat instrument readings ≥500 ppmv as a leak threshold

units.obligation_text: When a leak is identified, you must either complete repairs or completely empty the fixed roof storage tank within 45 days.
units.action_summary: Repair or empty the fixed roof storage tank within 45 days after identifying a leak

units.obligation_text: If a repair cannot be completed or the fixed roof storage tank cannot be completely emptied within 45 days, you may use up to two extensions of up to 30 additional days each.
units.action_summary: Permit up to two 30-day extensions if repair or emptying cannot be completed within 45 days

units.obligation_text: Keep records documenting each decision to use an extension, as specified in paragraphs (b)(4)(iii)(A) through (C) of this section.
units.action_summary: Maintain records documenting each decision to use an extension and supporting details per (A)-(C)

units.obligation_text: If you do not empty or repair leaks before the end of the second extension period, report the date when the fixed roof storage tank was emptied or repaired in your compliance report.
units.action_summary: Report the date of emptying or repair in the compliance report if not completed before end of second extension

units.obligation_text: Records for a first extension must include a description of the defect, documentation that alternative storage capacity was unavailable in the 45-day period after the inspection and a schedule of actions that you took in an effort to either repair or completely empty the fixed roof storage tank during the extension period.
units.action_summary: Maintain specified content in records for the first extension

units.obligation_text: For a second extension, if needed, you must maintain records documenting that alternative storage capacity was unavailable during the first extension period and a schedule of the actions you took to ensure that the fixed roof storage tank was completely emptied or repaired by the end of the second extension period.
units.action_summary: Maintain specified records documenting unavailability of alternative storage and actions taken for second extension

units.obligation_text: Record the date on which the fixed roof storage tank was completely emptied, if applicable.
units.action_summary: Record the date the tank was completely emptied

units.obligation_text: Beginning no later than the compliance dates specified in § 63.2342(e), you must conduct periodic vapor pressure analyses or obtain vapor pressure analysis data from the organic liquid supplier according to the schedule specified in paragraphs (b)(5)(i) and (ii) of this section to demonstrate that the annual average true vapor pressure of the organic liquid associated with each storage tank is below control thresholds.
units.action_summary: Conduct or obtain periodic vapor pressure analyses to show annual average true vapor pressure is below control thresholds

units.obligation_text: For each periodic vapor pressure analysis, you must use ASTM D6378–18a (incorporated by reference, see § 63.14), a vapor to liquid ratio of 4:1, and the actual annual average temperature as defined in this subpart. Maintain records of each periodic annual average true vapor pressure analysis according to the requirements of § 63.2394.
units.action_summary: Use ASTM D6378–18a, 4:1 vapor-liquid ratio, and actual annual average temperature; maintain records per §63.2394

units.obligation_text: For each existing affected source, and for each new and reconstructed affected source that commences construction or reconstruction after April 2, 2002, and on or before October 21, 2019, you must obtain analysis data or conduct the first periodic vapor pressure analysis on or before [date 3 years after date of publication of final rule in the Federal Register] and obtain analysis data or conduct subsequent periodic vapor pressure analyses no later than 60 months thereafter following the previous analysis, or if the contents of storage tank are a different commodity since the previous analysis, whichever occurs first.
units.action_summary: Obtain first and subsequent vapor pressure analyses by specified deadlines (initial by specified date; subsequent every 60 months or upon commodity change)

units.obligation_text: For each new and reconstructed affected source that commences construction or reconstruction after October 21, 2019, you must obtain analysis data or conduct the first periodic vapor pressure analysis no later than 60 months following the initial analysis required by § 63.2358 and obtain analysis data or conduct subsequent periodic vapor pressure analyses no later than 60 months thereafter following the previous analysis, or if the contents of storage tank are a different commodity since the previous analysis, whichever occurs first.
units.actor: owner/operator (you) of new/reconstructed affected sources after Oct 21, 2019
units.action_summary: Obtain first vapor pressure analysis within 60 months after initial §63.2358 requirement and then every 60 months or upon commodity change

units.obligation_text: Beginning no later than the compliance dates specified in § 63.2342(e), you must conduct periodic HAP content analyses or obtain HAP content analysis data from the organic liquid supplier according to the schedule specified in paragraphs (b)(6)(i) and (ii) of this section to demonstrate that the HAP content of the organic liquid associated with each storage tank is below control thresholds.
units.action_summary: Conduct or obtain periodic HAP content analyses to demonstrate HAP content is below control thresholds

units.obligation_text: For each periodic HAP content analysis, you must use the procedures specified in § 63.2354(c), except you may not use voluntary consensus standards, safety data sheets (SDS), or certified product data sheets. Maintain records of each periodic HAP content analysis according to the requirements of § 63.2394.
units.action_summary: Use §63.2354(c) procedures for HAP analyses; do not use voluntary consensus standards, SDS, or certified product data sheets; maintain records per §63.2394

units.obligation_text: For each existing affected source, and for each new and reconstructed affected source that commences construction or reconstruction after April 2, 2002, and on or before October 21, 2019, you must obtain analysis data or conduct the first periodic HAP content analysis on or before [date 3 years after date of publication of final rule in the Federal Register] and obtain analysis data or conduct subsequent periodic HAP content analyses no later than 60 months thereafter following the previous analysis, or if the contents of storage tank have changed significantly since the previous analysis, whichever occurs first.
units.action_summary: Obtain initial and subsequent HAP content analyses by specified deadlines (initial by specified date; every 60 months or upon significant contents change)

units.obligation_text: For each new and reconstructed affected source that commences construction or reconstruction after October 21, 2019, you must obtain analysis data or conduct the first periodic HAP content analysis no later than 60 months following the initial analysis required by § 63.2358 and obtain analysis data or conduct subsequent periodic HAP content analyses no later than 60 months thereafter following the previous analysis, or if the contents of storage tank have changed significantly since the previous analysis, whichever occurs first.
units.actor: owner/operator (you) of new/reconstructed affected sources after Oct 21, 2019
units.action_summary: Obtain first HAP content analysis within 60 months after initial §63.2358 requirement; subsequent analyses every 60 months or upon significant change

units.obligation_text: Except as specified in paragraph (b)(7)(ii) of this section, the requirements specified in paragraphs (b)(1) through (6) of this section apply to the following storage tanks: (A) Storage tanks at an existing affected source subject to this subpart having a capacity of 18.9 cubic meters (5,000 gallons) or more that are not subject to control based on the criteria specified in Table 2b of this subpart, items 1 through 3. (B) Storage tanks at a reconstructed or new affected source subject to this subpart having a capacity of 18.9 cubic meters (5,000 gallons) or more that are not subject to control based on the criteria specified in Table 2 to this subpart, items 3 through 6.
units.action_summary: Apply requirements (b)(1)-(6) to the listed categories of storage tanks

units.obligation_text: If you choose to meet the fenceline monitoring requirements specified in § 63.2348, then you are not required to comply with paragraphs (b)(4) and (b)(7)(i) of this section. Instead, you may continue to comply with paragraphs (b)(1) through (3) of this section for each storage tank subject to this subpart having a capacity of 18.9 cubic meters (5,000 gallons) or more that is not subject to control based on the criteria specified in Table 2 to this subpart, items 1 through 6.
units.action_summary: Option to use fenceline monitoring to avoid complying with (b)(4) and (b)(7)(i) and instead comply with (b)(1)-(3)

units.obligation_text: If you are already submitting a Notification of Compliance Status or a first Compliance report under § 63.2386(c), you do not need to submit a separate Notification of Compliance Status or first Compliance report for each transfer rack that meets the conditions identified in paragraph (c) of this section (i.e., a single Notification of Compliance Status or first Compliance report should be submitted).
units.action_summary: If already submitting required report under §63.2386(c), you need not submit separate reports for each qualifying transfer rack; one report suffices

units.obligation_text: Beginning no later than the compliance dates specified in § 63.2342(e), for each fixed roof storage tank having a capacity less than 18.9 cubic meters (5,000 gallons) but greater than 3.8 cubic meters (1,000 gallons) storing an organic liquid with an annual average true vapor pressure greater than 10.3 kilopascals (1.5 psia), you must monitor each closure device and potential source of vapor leakage as specified in paragraphs (e)(1) through (3) of this section.
units.action_summary: Monitor closure devices and potential vapor leakage sources on specified small fixed roof tanks with vapor pressure >10.3 kPa per (e)(1)-(3)

units.obligation_text: Conduct monitoring using Method 21 of part 60, appendix A–7 of this chapter within 90 days after the initial fill. You must conduct subsequent monitoring no later than 1 year after the previous monitoring is performed, provided the fixed roof storage tank contains organic liquid.
units.action_summary: Use Method 21 for monitoring within 90 days after initial fill and annually thereafter if tank contains organic liquids

units.obligation_text: Calibrate the instrument before use on the day of its use according to the procedures in Method 21 of 40 CFR part 60, appendix A–7 of this chapter. Calibration gases must be zero air and a mixture of methane in air at a concentration of no greater than 2,000 parts per million.
units.action_summary: Calibrate monitoring instruments per Method 21 daily and use specified calibration gases

units.obligation_text: Perform a calibration drift assessment, at a minimum, at the end of each monitoring day using the same calibration gas that was used to calibrate the instrument before use. Follow the procedures in Section 10.1 of Method 21 of part 60, appendix A–7 to this chapter, except do not adjust the meter readout to correspond to the calibration gas value. Divide the arithmetic difference of the initial and post-test calibration response by the corresponding calibration gas value and multiply by 100 to express the calibration drift as a percentage.
units.action_summary: Perform end-of-day calibration drift assessment per Method 21 and calculate drift percentage (without adjusting meter readout)

units.obligation_text: If the calibration drift assessment shows a negative drift of more than 10 percent, you must re-monitor all equipment monitored since the last calibration.
units.action_summary: Re-monitor equipment if calibration drift exceeds 10% negative

units.obligation_text: An instrument reading of 500 ppmv or greater defines a leak.
units.action_summary: Treat instrument readings ≥500 ppmv as a leak threshold for small tanks described in (e)

units.obligation_text: When a leak is identified, you must either complete repairs or completely empty the fixed roof storage tank within 45 days.
units.action_summary: Repair or empty the tank within 45 days when a leak is identified

units.obligation_text: If a repair cannot be completed or the fixed roof storage tank cannot be completely emptied within 45 days, you may use up to two extensions of up to 30 additional days each.
units.action_summary: Allow up to two 30-day extensions if repair or emptying cannot be completed in 45 days

units.obligation_text: Keep records documenting each decision to use an extension, as specified in paragraphs (e)(3)(i) through (iii) of this section.
units.action_summary: Maintain records documenting each decision to use an extension and specified details

units.obligation_text: If you do not empty or repair leaks before the end of the second extension period, report the date when the fixed roof storage tank was emptied or repaired in your compliance report.
units.action_summary: Report the date of emptying or repair in compliance report if not completed before end of second extension

units.obligation_text: Records for a first extension must include a description of the defect, documentation that alternative storage capacity was unavailable in the 45-day period after the inspection and a schedule of actions that you took in an effort to either repair or completely empty the fixed roof storage tank during the extension period.
units.action_summary: Maintain specified record contents for first extension
