units.obligation_text: For a second extension, if needed, you must maintain records documenting that alternative storage capacity was unavailable during the first extension period and a schedule of the actions you took to ensure that the fixed roof storage tank was completely emptied or repaired by the end of the second extension period.
units.action_summary: Maintain specified record contents for second extension

units.obligation_text: Record the date on which the fixed roof storage tank was completely emptied, if applicable.
units.action_summary: Record the date the tank was completely emptied

units.obligation_text: Storage tanks. Except as specified in paragraph (a)(5) and (m) of this section, for each storage tank storing organic liquids that meets the tank capacity and liquid vapor pressure criteria for control in Table 2 to this subpart, items 1 through 5, you must comply with paragraph (a)(1), (2), (3), or (4) of this section. For each storage tank storing organic liquids that meets the tank capacity and liquid vapor pressure criteria for control in Table 2 to this subpart, item 6, you must comply with paragraph (a)(1), (2), or (4) of this section.
units.actor: owner/operator (you) of storage tanks meeting control criteria
units.action_summary: Comply with specified paragraphs (a)(1)-(4) depending on table criteria for storage tanks

units.obligation_text: Meet the emission limits specified in Table 2 or 2b to this subpart and comply with paragraph (m) of this section and the applicable requirements specified in 40 CFR part 63, subpart SS, for meeting emission limits, except substitute the term ‘‘storage tank’’ at each occurrence of the term ‘‘storage vessel’’ in subpart SS.
units.action_summary: Meet emission limits in Table 2/2b, comply with paragraph (m) and applicable subpart SS requirements (substituting 'storage tank')

units.obligation_text: Route emissions to fuel gas systems or back into a process as specified in 40 CFR part 63, subpart SS. If you comply with this paragraph, then you must also comply with the requirements specified in paragraph (m) of this section.
units.action_summary: Route emissions to fuel gas systems or back to process per subpart SS; if chosen, also comply with paragraph (m)

units.obligation_text: Transport vehicles must have a current certification in accordance with the United States Department of Transportation (U.S. DOT) qualification and maintenance requirements of 49 CFR part 180, subpart E for cargo tanks and subpart F for tank cars.
units.action_summary: Ensure transport vehicles have current U.S. DOT certifications as specified

units.obligation_text: No pressure relief device on the storage tank, on the vapor return line, or on the cargo tank or tank car, shall open during loading or as a result of diurnal temperature changes (breathing losses).
units.action_summary: Prohibit pressure relief devices from opening during loading or due to diurnal breathing losses

units.obligation_text: Pressure relief devices must be set to no less than 2.5 pounds per square inch gauge (psig) at all times to prevent breathing losses.
units.action_summary: Set pressure relief devices to >=2.5 psig to prevent breathing losses

units.obligation_text: Pressure relief devices may be set at values less than 2.5 psig if the owner or operator provides rationale in the notification of compliance status report explaining why the alternative value is sufficient to prevent breathing losses at all times.
units.action_summary: Permit setting relief devices below 2.5 psig if rationale is provided in the compliance notification

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator shall comply with paragraphs (a)(4)(v)(A) through (C) of this section for each relief valve.
units.action_summary: Comply with monitoring and record requirements (A)-(C) for each relief valve

units.obligation_text: The relief valve shall be monitored quarterly using the method described in § 63.180(b).
units.action_summary: Monitor each relief valve quarterly per §63.180(b)

units.obligation_text: Except as specified in paragraph (a)(6) of this section, beginning no later than the compliance dates specified in § 63.2342(e), the tank capacity criteria, liquid vapor pressure criteria, and emission limits specified for storage tanks at an existing affected source in Table 2 of this subpart, item 1 no longer apply. Instead, for each storage tank at an existing affected source storing organic liquids that meets the tank capacity and liquid vapor pressure criteria for control in Table 2b to this subpart, items 1 through 3, you must comply with paragraph (a)(1), (2), (3), or (4) of this section.
units.action_summary: Change applicability: tanks meeting Table 2b items 1-3 must comply with paragraphs (a)(1)-(4) beginning by specified compliance dates

units.obligation_text: If you choose to meet the fenceline monitoring requirements specified in § 63.2348, then you are not required to comply with paragraph (a)(5) of this section. Instead, you may continue to comply with the tank capacity and liquid vapor pressure criteria and the emission limits specified for storage tanks at an existing affected source in Table 2 of this subpart, item 1.
units.action_summary: Optionally use fenceline monitoring instead of complying with (a)(5); otherwise continue to comply with Table 2 item 1 criteria

units.obligation_text: Meet the emission limits specified in Table 2 to this subpart and comply with paragraph (m) of this section and the applicable requirements for transfer racks specified in 40 CFR part 63, subpart SS, for meeting emission limits.
units.action_summary: Meet emission limits in Table 2 for transfer racks and comply with paragraph (m) and subpart SS applicable requirements

units.obligation_text: Route emissions to fuel gas systems or back into a process as specified in 40 CFR part 63, subpart SS. If you comply with this paragraph, then you must also comply with the requirements specified in paragraph (m) of this section.
units.action_summary: Route emissions to fuel gas systems or back into process per subpart SS; if chosen, comply with paragraph (m)

units.obligation_text: Except as specified in paragraph (l) of this section, for each pump, valve, and sampling connection that operates in organic liquids service for at least 300 hours per year, you must comply with paragraph (m) of this section and the applicable requirements under 40 CFR part 63, subpart TT (control level 1), subpart UU (control level 2), or subpart H.
units.action_summary: For components operating ≥300 hours/year, comply with paragraph (m) and applicable control-level subpart requirements

units.obligation_text: Ensure that organic liquids are loaded only into transport vehicles that have a current certification in accordance with the U.S. DOT qualification and maintenance requirements in 49 CFR part 180, subpart E for cargo tanks and subpart F for tank cars.
units.action_summary: Load organic liquids only into transport vehicles certified per U.S. DOT requirements

units.obligation_text: Operating limits. For each high throughput transfer rack, you must meet each operating limit in Table 3 to this subpart for each control device used to comply with the provisions of this subpart whenever emissions from the loading of organic liquids are routed to the control device. Except as specified in paragraph (k) of this section, for each storage tank and low throughput transfer rack, you must comply with paragraph (m) of this section and the requirements for monitored parameters as specified in 40 CFR part 63, subpart SS, for storage vessels and, during the loading of organic liquids, for low throughput transfer racks, respectively. Alternatively, you may comply with the operating limits in Table 3 to this subpart.
units.action_summary: Meet Table 3 operating limits for high throughput racks; for storage tanks and low throughput racks follow paragraph (m) and subpart SS monitored parameter requirements or alternatively comply with Table 3

units.obligation_text: For noncombustion devices, if you elect to demonstrate compliance with a percent reduction requirement in Table 2 or 2b to this subpart using total organic compounds (TOC) rather than organic HAP, you must first demonstrate, subject to the approval of the Administrator, that TOC is an appropriate surrogate for organic HAP in your case; that is, for your storage tank(s) and/or transfer rack(s), the percent destruction of organic HAP is equal to or higher than the percent destruction of TOC. This demonstration must be conducted prior to or during the initial compliance test.
units.action_summary: If electing TOC as surrogate for organic HAP, demonstrate (with Administrator approval) that TOC is appropriate before or during initial compliance test

units.obligation_text: Safety device. Opening of a safety device is allowed at any time that it is required to avoid unsafe operating conditions.
units.action_summary: Permit opening safety devices when required to avoid unsafe conditions

units.obligation_text: Beginning no later than [date 3 years after date of publication of final rule in the Federal Register], this paragraph no longer applies.
units.action_summary: Indicates the permission to open safety devices will expire on a specified date

units.obligation_text: Beginning no later than the compliance dates specified in § 63.2342(e), for each storage tank and low throughput transfer rack, if you vent emissions through a closed vent system to a flare then you must comply with the requirements specified in § 63.2380 instead of the requirements in § 63.987 and the provisions regarding flare compliance assessments at § 63.997(a), (b), and (c).
units.action_summary: If venting to a flare via closed vent system, comply with §63.2380 rather than §63.987 or certain §63.997 provisions

units.obligation_text: Equipment leak components. Beginning no later than the compliance dates specified in § 63.2342(e), paragraph (c) of this section no longer applies. Instead, you must comply with paragraph (l)(1) or (2) of this section.
units.action_summary: Paragraph (c) is superseded and you must comply with either (l)(1) or (l)(2) beginning by specified dates

units.obligation_text: Except as specified in paragraph (l)(2) of this section, for each connector, pump, valve, and sampling connection that operates in organic liquids service for at least 300 hours per year, you must comply with paragraph (m) of this section and the applicable requirements under 40 CFR part 63, subpart UU (control level 2), or subpart H.
units.action_summary: For components operating ≥300 hours/year, comply with paragraph (m) and subpart UU or H requirements unless (l)(2) chosen

units.obligation_text: If you choose to meet the fenceline monitoring requirements specified in § 63.2348, then you may choose to comply with this paragraph instead of paragraph (l)(1) of this section. For each pump, valve, and sampling connection that operates in organic liquids service for at least 300 hours per year, you must comply with paragraph (m) of this section and the applicable requirements under 40 CFR part 63, subpart TT (control level 1), subpart UU (control level 2), or subpart H.
units.action_summary: Option to elect fenceline monitoring and comply with (l)(2) requirements (paragraph (m) and subpart TT/UU/H) instead of (l)(1)

units.obligation_text: Start-up, shutdown, and malfunction. Beginning no later than the compliance dates specified in § 63.2342(e), the referenced provisions specified in paragraphs (m)(1) through (19) of this section do not apply when demonstrating compliance with 40 CFR part 63, subpart H, subpart SS, and subpart UU.
units.action_summary: The listed start-up/shutdown/malfunction provisions cannot be used when demonstrating compliance with subparts H, SS, and UU beginning by specified dates

units.obligation_text: If you own or operate a facility that is not required to conduct fenceline monitoring pursuant to § 63.658, then you may opt to conduct fenceline monitoring pursuant to this section.
units.action_summary: Optionally elect to conduct fenceline monitoring under this section if not required by §63.658

units.obligation_text: Beginning no later than the compliance dates specified in § 63.2342(f), if you choose to comply with the requirements specified in § 63.2343(b)(7)(ii) and § 63.2346(a)(6) and (l)(2), then you must conduct sampling along the facility property boundary and analyze the samples in accordance with Methods 325A and 325B of appendix A of this part and paragraphs (b) through (k) of this section.
units.action_summary: If opting into fenceline monitoring per referenced sections, conduct boundary sampling and analyze using Methods 325A/325B and follow (b)-(k)

units.obligation_text: You must determine your target analytes for monitoring and site-specific action level for each analyte as specified in paragraphs (b)(1) through (5) of this section.
units.action_summary: Determine target analytes and action levels per subsections (b)(1)-(5)

units.obligation_text: You must use EPA’s Guidance on Determination of Analytes and Action Levels for Fenceline Monitoring of Organic Liquids Distribution Sources to develop your HAP emissions inventory and conduct your modeling.
units.action_summary: Use EPA guidance to develop HAP emissions inventory and modeling

units.obligation_text: The HAP emissions inventory is set at allowable emissions from all equipment at the source under common control of the owner and operator of the OLD operation.
units.action_summary: Set the HAP emissions inventory at allowable emissions from all equipment under common control

units.obligation_text: For this modeling effort, modeled allowable emissions from storage tanks and equipment leaks must be adjusted to take into account the requirements at §§ 63.2343(b)(4), 63.2346(a)(5), and (l)(1) for the purpose of setting the analytes and action level of the fenceline monitoring program.
units.action_summary: Adjust modeled allowable emissions to reflect requirements in specified sections when setting analytes and action levels

units.obligation_text: You must determine at least one target analyte as prescribed in paragraphs (b)(2)(i) through (iv) of this section.
units.action_summary: Determine at least one target analyte following (b)(2)(i)-(iv)

units.obligation_text: Each analyte must have an available uptake rate at Table 12.1 of Method 325B of appendix A to this part or must have an uptake rate for the selected sorbent validated using Addendum A of Method 325B of appendix A to this part.
units.action_summary: Select analytes that have uptake rate in Table 12.1 or validate uptake rate for selected sorbent using Addendum A

units.obligation_text: A HAP cannot be used to meet the fenceline monitoring requirements of this section unless the corresponding action level is at least five times the method detection limit for the HAP.
units.action_summary: Do not use a HAP as an analyte unless its action level is ≥5× method detection limit

units.obligation_text: The first analyte is the Table 1 HAP with the most allowable emissions from OLD operations at the facility on an annual basis.
units.action_summary: Select as the first analyte the Table 1 HAP with the highest annual allowable emissions at the facility

title: Standards of Performance for New Residential Wood Heaters, New Residential Hydronic Heaters and Forced-Air Furnaces; Reopen Comment Period
National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Paper and Other Web Coating Residual Risk and Technology Review

units.obligation_text: Any web coating line that coats both paper or a web, and another substrate such as fabric, must comply with the subpart of this part that applies to the predominant activity conducted on the affected source.
units.actor: owner or operator of the web coating line
units.action_summary: If a web coating line coats paper and another substrate, the owner/operator must apply the subpart applicable to the predominant activity

units.obligation_text: Any web coating line subject to this part that is modified to include printing activities, may continue to demonstrate compliance with this part, in lieu of demonstrating compliance with subpart KK of this part.
units.actor: owner or operator of the web coating line
units.action_summary: A web coating line modified to include printing may keep demonstrating compliance under this subpart instead of subpart KK

units.obligation_text: You must limit organic HAP emissions to the level specified in paragraph (b)(1), (2), (3), or (4) of this section for all periods of operation, including startup, shutdown, and malfunction.
units.action_summary: You are required to limit organic HAP emissions to the specified levels at all times, including SSM

units.obligation_text: If you use an oxidizer to control organic HAP emissions, operate the oxidizer such that an outlet organic HAP concentration of no greater than 20 parts per million by volume (ppmv) on a dry basis is achieved and the efficiency of the capture system is 100 percent.
units.actor: owner or operator (you) using an oxidizer
units.action_summary: When using an oxidizer, operate it to achieve ≤20 ppmv outlet organic HAP and ensure capture system efficiency is 100%

units.obligation_text: Before [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE Federal Register], the affected coating operation(s) must be in compliance with the applicable emission limit in § 63.3320 at all times, except during periods of startup, shutdown, and malfunction (SSM).
units.actor: owner or operator (you) of affected coating operation(s)
units.action_summary: Prior to the specified date, affected coating operations must comply with emission limits at all times except during SSM

units.obligation_text: On and after [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE Federal Register] the affected coating operation(s) must be in compliance with the applicable emission limit in § 63.3320 at all times, including periods of startup, shutdown, and malfunction.
units.actor: owner or operator (you) of affected coating operation(s)
units.action_summary: On and after the specified date, affected coating operations must comply with emission limits at all times including SSM

units.obligation_text: A periodic performance test must be performed by [DATE 3 YEARS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION IN THE Federal Register], and subsequent tests no later than 60 months thereafter, as required in § 63.3360.
units.action_summary: Conduct an initial periodic performance test by the specified date and repeat tests at least every 60 months

units.obligation_text: After [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE Federal Register], you must electronically submit initial notifications, semiannual compliance reports, and performance test reports, as required in § 63.3400.
units.action_summary: Electronically submit required initial notifications, semiannual reports, and performance test reports after the specified date

units.obligation_text: The coating operation(s) must be in compliance with the applicable emission limit in § 63.3320 at all times, including periods of startup, shutdown, and malfunction, immediately upon startup.
units.actor: owner or operator (you) of new affected sources
units.action_summary: New affected sources must meet emission limits at all times, including SSM, immediately when starting operation

units.obligation_text: You must complete any initial performance test required in § 63.3360 within the time limits specified in § 63.7(a)(2), and subsequent tests no later than 60 months thereafter.
units.actor: owner or operator (you) of new affected sources
units.action_summary: Complete initial performance tests within §63.7(a)(2) time limits and repeat no less frequently than every 60 months

units.obligation_text: You must electronically submit initial notifications and performance test reports as required in § 63.3400.
units.actor: owner or operator (you) of new affected sources
units.action_summary: Electronically submit required initial notifications and performance test reports

units.obligation_text: After [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE Federal Register], you must electronically submit semiannual compliance reports as required in § 63.3400.
units.actor: owner or operator (you) of new affected sources
units.action_summary: After the specified date, electronically submit semiannual compliance reports as required

units.obligation_text: Before [DATE 181 DAYS AFTER PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE Federal Register], for each existing source, and for each new or reconstructed source for which construction or reconstruction commenced after September 13, 2000, but on or before September 19, 2019, you must be in compliance with the emission limits and operating limits in this subpart at all times, except during periods of startup, shutdown, and malfunction.
units.action_summary: Prior to the specified date, applicable sources must meet emission and operating limits at all times except during SSM

units.obligation_text: After [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE Federal Register], for each such source you must be in compliance with the emission limits and operating limits in this subpart at all times.
units.action_summary: On and after the specified date, applicable sources must comply with emission and operating limits at all times

units.obligation_text: For new and reconstructed sources for which construction or reconstruction commenced after September 19, 2019, you must be in compliance with the emission limits and operating limits in this subpart at all times, immediately upon startup.
units.actor: owner or operator (you) of new or reconstructed sources
units.action_summary: New/reconstructed sources after Sept 19, 2019 must comply with emission and operating limits immediately upon startup

units.obligation_text: For affected sources as of September 19, 2019, before [DATE 181 DAYS AFTER PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE Federal Register], you must always operate and maintain your affected source, including all air pollution control and monitoring equipment you use for purposes of complying with this subpart, according to the provisions in § 63.6(e)(1)(i).
units.action_summary: Operate and maintain affected source and control/monitoring equipment per §63.6(e)(1)(i) prior to the specified date

units.obligation_text: On and after [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE Federal Register] for such sources and after September 19, 2019 for new or reconstructed affected sources, you must always operate and maintain your affected source, including associated air pollution control equipment and monitoring equipment, in a manner consistent with safety and good air pollution control practices for minimizing emissions.
units.action_summary: On/after the dates, operate and maintain affected sources and equipment consistent with safety and good air pollution control practices to minimize emissions

units.obligation_text: You must conduct each performance test required by § 63.3360 according to the requirements in § 63.3360(e)(2) and under the conditions in this section unless you obtain a waiver of the performance test according to the provisions in § 63.7(h).
units.action_summary: Conduct required performance tests per §63.3360(e)(2) and this section unless you obtain a waiver under §63.7(h)

units.obligation_text: You must conduct the performance test under representative operating conditions for the coating operation. Operations during periods of startup, shutdown, and nonoperation do not constitute representative conditions.
units.action_summary: Performance tests must be conducted under representative operating conditions; SSM and nonoperation are not representative

units.obligation_text: You may not conduct performance tests during periods of malfunction.
units.action_summary: Performance tests are prohibited during malfunctions

units.obligation_text: You must record the process information that is necessary to document operating conditions during the test and explain why the conditions represent normal operation.
units.action_summary: Record and document process information during tests and justify that conditions were normal

units.obligation_text: Upon request, you shall make available to the Administrator such records as may be necessary to determine the conditions of performance tests.
units.action_summary: Provide records related to performance test conditions to the Administrator upon request

units.obligation_text: You must conduct the performance test when the emission capture system and add-on control device are operating at a representative flow rate, and the add-on control device is operating at a representative inlet concentration.
units.action_summary: Conduct performance tests when capture system and control device operate at representative flow rates and inlet concentrations

units.obligation_text: You may not conduct performance tests during periods of malfunction.
units.action_summary: Performance tests are prohibited during malfunctions (capture/control device context)

units.obligation_text: You must record information that is necessary to document emission capture system and add-on control device operating conditions during the test and explain why the conditions represent normal operation.
units.action_summary: Record capture system and control device operating data during tests and justify normal operation

units.obligation_text: Upon request, you shall make available to the Administrator such records as may be necessary to determine the conditions of performance tests.
units.action_summary: Provide capture/control test records to the Administrator upon request

units.obligation_text: Following the date on which the initial or periodic performance test of a control device is completed to demonstrate continuing compliance with the standards, you must monitor and inspect each capture system and each control device used to comply with § 63.3320. You must install and operate the monitoring equipment as specified in paragraphs (c) and (f) of this section.
units.action_summary: After performance testing, monitor and inspect each capture and control device and install/operate monitoring equipment per specified paragraphs

units.obligation_text: If you own or operate web coating lines with intermittently-controlled work stations, you must monitor bypasses of the control device and the mass of each coating material applied at the work station during any such bypass.
units.actor: owner or operator (you) of web coating lines with intermittently-controlled work stations
units.action_summary: Monitor control device bypasses and the mass of coating material applied during bypass for intermittently-controlled work stations

units.obligation_text: If using a control device for complying with the requirements of this subpart, you must demonstrate that any coating material applied on a never-controlled work station or an intermittently-controlled work station operated in bypass mode is allowed in your compliance demonstration according to § 63.3370(o) and (p).
units.actor: owner or operator (you) using a control device
units.action_summary: Demonstrate that coatings applied on never-controlled or bypassed intermittently-controlled stations are allowable in compliance demonstrations per §63.3370(o) and (p)

units.obligation_text: The bypass monitoring must be conducted using at least one of the procedures in paragraphs (c)(1) through (4) of this section for each work station and associated dryer.
units.action_summary: Conduct bypass monitoring by using at least one of the listed procedures for each work station/dryer

units.obligation_text: You must have valid data from at least 90 percent of the hours when the process is operated. Invalid or missing data should be reported as a deviation in the semiannual compliance report.
units.action_summary: Maintain valid monitoring data for at least 90% of operating hours and report invalid/missing data as deviations in semiannual reports

units.obligation_text: If you are using a control device to comply with the emission standards in § 63.3320, you must install, operate, and maintain each CPMS specified in paragraphs (e)(10) and (11) and (f) of this section according to the requirements in paragraphs (e)(1) through (9) of this section. You must install, operate, and maintain each CPMS specified in paragraph (c) of this section according to paragraphs (e)(5) through (8) of this section.
units.actor: owner or operator (you) using a control device
units.action_summary: Install, operate, and maintain required CPMS per specified paragraph requirements

units.obligation_text: You must have valid data from at least 90 percent of the hours when the process is operated. Invalid or missing data should be reported as a deviation in the semiannual compliance report.
units.action_summary: Ensure CPMS yields valid data for at least 90% of operating hours and report deviations in semiannual reports

units.obligation_text: You must determine the block 3-hour average of all recorded readings for each operating period. To calculate the average for each 3-hour averaging period, you must have at least two of three of the hourly averages for that period using only average values that are based on valid data (i.e., not from out-of-control periods).
units.action_summary: Calculate 3-hour block averages using at least two valid hourly averages per block

units.obligation_text: You must develop a quality control program, as required in § 63.8(d).
units.action_summary: Develop a quality control program per §63.8(d)

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator shall keep these written procedures on record for the life of the affected source or until the affected source is no longer subject to the provisions of this part, to be made available for inspection, upon request, by the Administrator.
units.action_summary: Keep written QC procedures on record for life of the affected source and make them available to the Administrator upon request

units.obligation_text: If the performance evaluation plan is revised, the owner or operator shall keep previous (i.e., superseded) versions of the performance evaluation plan on record to be made available for inspection, upon request, by the Administrator, for a period of 5 years after each revision to the plan.
units.action_summary: Retain superseded performance evaluation plan versions and make them available to the Administrator for 5 years after each revision

units.obligation_text: The program of corrective action should be included in the plan required under § 63.8(d)(2).
units.action_summary: Recommend including corrective action program in the performance evaluation plan

units.obligation_text: Oxidizer. If you are using an oxidizer to comply with the emission standards, you must comply with paragraphs (e)(10)(i) through (vi) of this section.
units.actor: owner or operator (you) using an oxidizer
units.action_summary: When using an oxidizer, comply with the specified temperature monitoring and inspection requirements (e)(10)(i)-(vi)

units.obligation_text: Install, maintain, and operate temperature monitoring equipment according to the manufacturer’s specifications. Calibrate the chart recorder or data logger at least quarterly.
units.actor: owner or operator (you) using an oxidizer
units.action_summary: Install/maintain/operate temperature monitors per manufacturer; calibrate chart recorder/data logger quarterly

units.obligation_text: For an oxidizer other than a catalytic oxidizer, install, operate, and maintain a temperature monitoring device equipped with a continuous recorder. The device must have an accuracy of ±1 percent of the temperature being monitored in degrees Fahrenheit, or ±1.8 degree Fahrenheit, whichever is greater. The temperature sensor must be installed in the combustion chamber at a location in the combustion zone.
units.actor: owner or operator (you) using a non-catalytic oxidizer
units.action_summary: For non-catalytic oxidizers, install and maintain a continuous-recording temperature monitor with specified accuracy and sensor placement in combustion zone

units.obligation_text: For a catalytic oxidizer, install, operate, and maintain a temperature monitoring device equipped with a continuous recorder. The device must be capable of monitoring temperature with an accuracy of ±1 percent of the temperature being monitored in degrees Fahrenheit or ±1.8 degree Fahrenheit, whichever is greater. The temperature sensor must be installed in the vent stream at the nearest feasible point to the inlet and outlet of the catalyst bed. Calculate the temperature rise across the catalyst.
units.actor: owner or operator (you) using a catalytic oxidizer
units.action_summary: For catalytic oxidizers, install and maintain an accurate continuous-recording temperature monitor with sensor placement near catalyst inlet/outlet and calculate temperature rise across catalyst

units.obligation_text: Validate the temperature sensor at least quarterly using method (iv)(A), (B), (C), (D), or (E):
units.action_summary: Quarterly validate the temperature sensor using one of the listed methods

units.obligation_text: Compare measured readings to a National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) traceable temperature measurement device or simulate a typical operating temperature using a NIST traceable temperature simulation device. When the temperature measurement device method is used, the sensor of the calibrated device must be placed as close as practicable to the process sensor, and both devices must be subjected to the same environmental conditions. The accuracy of the temperature measured must be 2.5% of the temperature measured by the NIST traceable device or 5 °F whichever is greater.
units.action_summary: Validation may be done by comparing readings to a NIST-traceable device with specified placement and accuracy requirements

units.obligation_text: Follow applicable procedures in the manufacturer owner’s manual.
units.action_summary: Validation may be done by following procedures in the manufacturer's manual

units.obligation_text: Request the temperature sensor manufacturer to certify or re-certify electromotive force (electrical properties) of the thermocouple.
units.action_summary: Validation may be performed by obtaining manufacturer certification/re-certification of the thermocouple electrical properties

units.obligation_text: Replace the temperature sensor with a new certified temperature sensor in lieu of validation.
units.action_summary: Validation may be satisfied by replacing the sensor with a new certified sensor

units.obligation_text: Permanently install a redundant temperature sensor as close as practicable to the process temperature sensor. The sensors must yield a reading within 25 °F of each other for thermal oxidizers and catalytic oxidizers.
units.action_summary: Validation may be done by installing a redundant sensor near the process sensor; both sensors must read within 25°F for the specified oxidizers

units.obligation_text: Conduct calibration and validation checks any time the temperature sensor exceeds the manufacturer’s specified maximum operating temperature range or install a new temperature sensor.
units.action_summary: Do calibration/validation checks whenever sensor exceeds manufacturer's max temperature range or when installing a new sensor

units.obligation_text: At least quarterly, inspect all components for integrity and all electrical connections for continuity, oxidation, and galvanic corrosion.
units.action_summary: Quarterly inspect oxidizer components and electrical connections for integrity and specified conditions

units.obligation_text: Determine the organic HAP or volatile matter and coating solids content of coating materials according to procedures in paragraphs (c) and (d) of this section. If applicable, determine the mass of volatile matter retained in the coated web or otherwise not emitted to the atmosphere according to paragraph (g) of this section.
units.action_summary: Determine organic HAP/volatile matter and coating solids per specified procedures and determine retained volatile matter if applicable

units.obligation_text: Initially, conduct a performance test for each capture and control system to determine: the destruction or removal efficiency of each control device other than solvent recovery according to paragraph (e) of this section, and the capture efficiency of each capture system according to paragraph (f) of this section. If applicable, determine the mass of volatile matter retained in the coated web or otherwise not emitted to the atmosphere according to paragraph (g) of this section.
units.action_summary: Perform initial performance tests for each capture/control system to determine destruction/removal efficiency and capture efficiency, and retained volatile matter if applicable

units.obligation_text: Perform a periodic test once every 5 years for each non-recovery control device to determine the destruction or removal efficiency according to paragraph (e) of this section. If applicable, perform a periodic test once every 5 years to determine the mass of volatile matter retained in the coated web or otherwise not emitted to the atmosphere according to paragraph (g) of this section.
units.action_summary: Every 5 years, test non-recovery control devices for destruction/removal efficiency and retained volatile matter if applicable

units.obligation_text: If you are using a control device to comply with the emission standards in § 63.3320, you are not required to conduct a performance test to demonstrate compliance if one or more of the criteria in paragraphs (b)(1) through (3) of this section are met.
units.actor: owner or operator (you) using a control device
units.action_summary: You may be exempt from performance testing if one or more specified criteria are met

units.obligation_text: The control device is equipped with continuous emission monitoring systems (CEMS) for determining inlet and outlet total organic volatile matter concentration and meeting the requirements of Performance Specification 6, 8, or 9 in Appendix B to 40 CFR part 60 and capture efficiency has been determined in accordance with the requirements of this subpart such that an overall organic HAP control efficiency can be calculated, and the CEMS are used to demonstrate continuous compliance in accordance with § 63.3350;
units.action_summary: Exemption condition: control device has specified CEMS, capture efficiency determined, and CEMS used for continuous compliance per §63.3350

units.obligation_text: You have met the requirements of § 63.7(h) (for waiver of performance testing);
units.action_summary: Exemption condition: you obtained a waiver of performance testing under §63.7(h)

units.obligation_text: The control device is a solvent recovery system and you comply by means of a monthly liquid-liquid material balance.
units.actor: owner or operator (you) using a solvent recovery system
units.action_summary: Exemption condition: control device is solvent recovery and compliance demonstrated via monthly liquid-liquid material balance

units.obligation_text: Include each organic HAP in Table 3 to this subpart determined to be present at greater than or equal to 0.1 mass percent and greater than or equal to 1.0 mass percent for other organic HAP compounds.
units.action_summary: Include organic HAPs meeting specified mass percent thresholds when determining constituents

units.obligation_text: Method 24. For coatings, determine the volatile organic content as mass fraction of nonaqueous volatile matter and use it as a substitute for organic HAP using Method 24 of appendix A–7 to 40 CFR part 60. The Method 24 determination may be performed by the manufacturer of the coating and the results provided to you. One of the voluntary consensus standards in paragraphs (c)(2)(i) through (v) of this section may be used as an alternative to using Method 24.
units.action_summary: Determine VOC content using Method 24 (manufacturer may perform) or use one of listed consensus standards as an alternative

units.obligation_text: ASTM D1963–85 (1996), (incorporated by reference, see § 63.14);
units.action_summary: ASTM D1963–85 may be used as an alternative to Method 24

units.obligation_text: ASTM D2111–10 (Reapproved 2015), (incorporated by reference, see § 63.14);
units.action_summary: ASTM D2111–10 may be used as an alternative to Method 24

units.obligation_text: ASTM D2369–10 (Reapproved 2015)e, (incorporated by reference, see § 63.14);
units.action_summary: ASTM D2369–10 may be used as an alternative to Method 24

units.obligation_text: ASTM D2697–03 (2014), (incorporated by reference, see § 63.14);
units.action_summary: ASTM D2697–03 may be used as an alternative to Method 24

units.obligation_text: ASTM D6093–97 (Reapproved 2016), (incorporated by reference, see § 63.14).
units.action_summary: ASTM D6093–97 may be used as an alternative to Method 24

units.obligation_text: Formulation data. You may use formulation data to determine the organic HAP mass fraction of a coating material. Formulation data may be provided to the owner or operator by the manufacturer of the material. In the event of an inconsistency between Method 311 (appendix A to 40 CFR part 63) test data and a facility’s formulation data, and the Method 311 test value is higher, the Method 311 data will govern. Formulation data may be used provided that the information represents all organic HAP present at a level equal to or greater than 0.1 percent for the organic HAP specified in Table 3 to this subpart and equal to or greater than 1.0 percent for other organic HAP compounds in any raw material used.
units.action_summary: Permitted to use manufacturer-provided formulation data to determine organic HAP mass fraction if it represents constituents at specified thresholds; Method 311 governs if higher

units.obligation_text: As-applied organic HAP mass fraction. If the as-purchased coating material is applied to the web without any solvent or other material added, then the as-applied organic HAP mass fraction is equal to the as-purchased organic HAP mass fraction. Otherwise, the as-applied organic HAP mass fraction must be calculated using Equation 4 of § 63.3370.
units.action_summary: If coating is applied without additions, use as-purchased HAP fraction; otherwise calculate as-applied HAP fraction using Equation 4

units.obligation_text: Method 24. You may determine the volatile organic and coating solids mass fraction of each coating applied using Method 24 (appendix A–7 to 40 CFR part 60). The Method 24 determination may be performed by the manufacturer of the material and the results provided to you. When using volatile organic compound content as a surrogate for HAP, you may also use ASTM D3960–98, (incorporated by reference, see § 63.14) as an alternative to Method 24. If these values cannot be determined using either of these methods, you must submit an alternative technique for determining their values for approval by the Administrator.
units.action_summary: You may use Method 24 (or ASTM D3960) to determine VOC and solids; if not possible, submit alternative technique to Administrator for approval

units.obligation_text: Formulation data. You may determine the volatile organic content and coating solids content of a coating material based on formulation data and may rely on volatile organic content data provided by the manufacturer of the material. In the event of any inconsistency between the formulation data and the results of Method 24 of appendix A–7 to 40 CFR part 60 and the Method 24 results are higher, the results of Method 24 will govern.
units.action_summary: You may use formulation data or manufacturer-provided VOC data to determine VOC and solids, but Method 24 governs if it yields higher values

units.obligation_text: As-applied volatile organic content and coating solids content. If the as-purchased coating material is applied to the web without any solvent or other material added, then the as-applied volatile organic content is equal to the as-purchased volatile content and the as-applied coating solids content is equal to the as-purchased coating solids content. Otherwise, the as-applied volatile organic content must be calculated using Equation 5 of § 63.3370 and the as-applied coating solids content must be calculated using Equation 6 of § 63.3370.
units.action_summary: Use as-purchased VOC and solids when applied without additions; otherwise calculate as-applied VOC and solids using Equations 5 and 6

units.obligation_text: Initial performance test. An initial performance test to establish the destruction or removal efficiency of the control device must be conducted such that control device inlet and outlet testing is conducted simultaneously, and the data are reduced in accordance with the test methods and procedures in paragraphs (e)(1)(i) through (ix) of this section. You must conduct three test runs as specified in § 63.7(e)(3), and each test run must last at least 1 hour.
units.action_summary: Conduct initial performance test with simultaneous inlet/outlet testing per specified methods; run three tests each at least one hour

units.obligation_text: Method 1 or 1A of appendix A–1 to 40 CFR part 60 must be used for sample and velocity traverses to determine sampling locations.
units.action_summary: Use Method 1 or 1A for sample/velocity traverses to determine sampling locations

units.obligation_text: Method 2, 2A, 2C, 2D, or 2F of appendix A–1 to 40 CFR part 60, or Method 2G of appendix A–2 to 40 CFR part 60 must be used to determine gas volumetric flow rate.
units.action_summary: Use specified Method 2-series or 2G to determine gas volumetric flow rate

units.obligation_text: Method 3, 3A, or 3B of appendix A–2 to 40 CFR part 60 must be used for gas analysis to determine dry molecular weight. You may also use as an alternative to Method 3B the manual method for measuring the oxygen, carbon dioxide, and carbon monoxide content of exhaust gas in ANSI/ASME PTC 19.10–1981 Part 10 (2010).
units.action_summary: Use Method 3/3A/3B for gas analysis to determine dry molecular weight; ANSI/ASME PTC 19.10–1981 Part 10 may be used as an alternative to Method 3B

units.obligation_text: Method 4 of appendix A–3 to 40 CFR part 60 must be used to determine stack gas moisture.
units.action_summary: Use Method 4 to determine stack gas moisture

units.obligation_text: Methods for determining the gas volumetric flow rate, dry molecular weight, and stack gas moisture must be performed, as applicable, during each test run.
units.action_summary: Perform applicable methods for flow rate, molecular weight, and moisture during each test run

units.obligation_text: Method 25 or 25A of appendix A–7 to 40 CFR part 60 must be used to determine total gaseous non-methane organic matter concentration. Use the same test method for both the inlet and outlet measurements which must be conducted simultaneously. You must submit notice of the intended test method to the Administrator for approval along with notification of the performance test required under § 63.7(b). You must use Method 25A if any of the conditions described in paragraphs (e)(1)(vi)(A) through (D) of this section apply to the control device.
units.action_summary: Use Method 25 or 25A for measuring total gaseous non-methane organic matter; use same method inlet/outlet, notify Administrator of intended method, and use Method 25A under specified conditions

units.obligation_text: The control device is not an oxidizer.
units.action_summary: Condition: if control device is not an oxidizer, Method 25A must be used

units.obligation_text: The control device is an oxidizer but an exhaust gas volatile organic matter concentration of 50 ppmv or less is required to comply with the emission standards in § 63.3320;
units.action_summary: Condition: if oxidizer and required exhaust VOC ≤50 ppmv, Method 25A must be used

units.obligation_text: The control device is an oxidizer but the volatile organic matter concentration at the inlet to the control system and the required level of control are such that they result in exhaust gas volatile organic matter concentrations of 50 ppmv or less;
units.action_summary: Condition: if oxidizer and inlet and required control produce exhaust VOC ≤50 ppmv, Method 25A must be used

units.obligation_text: The control device is an oxidizer but because of the high efficiency of the control device the anticipated volatile organic matter concentration at the control device exhaust is 50 ppmv or less, regardless of inlet concentration.
units.action_summary: Condition: if oxidizer and expected exhaust VOC ≤50 ppmv due to high efficiency, Method 25A must be used

units.obligation_text: Except as provided in § 63.7(e)(3), each performance test must consist of three separate runs with each run conducted for at least 1 hour under the conditions that exist when the affected source is operating under normal operating conditions. You may not conduct performance tests during periods of malfunction.
units.action_summary: Performance tests must include three ≥1-hour runs under normal conditions; tests prohibited during malfunctions

units.obligation_text: Volatile organic matter mass flow rates must be determined for each run specified in paragraph (e)(1)(vii) of this section using Equation 1.
units.action_summary: Calculate VOC mass flow rates for each test run using Equation 1

units.obligation_text: For each run, emission control device destruction or removal efficiency must be determined using Equation 2.
units.action_summary: Determine destruction/removal efficiency for each run using Equation 2

units.obligation_text: The control device destruction or removal efficiency is determined as the average of the efficiencies determined in the test runs and calculated in Equation 2.
units.action_summary: Determine the device's destruction/removal efficiency as the average of run efficiencies computed by Equation 2

units.obligation_text: Process information. You must record such process information as may be necessary to determine the conditions in existence at the time of the performance test. Representative conditions exclude periods of startup and shutdown. You may not conduct performance tests during periods of malfunction. You must record the process information that is necessary to document operating conditions during the test and include in such record an explanation to support that such conditions represent normal operation. Upon request, you shall make available to the Administrator such records as may be necessary to determine the conditions of performance tests.
units.action_summary: Record necessary process information to document test conditions and normal operation; tests prohibited during malfunction; provide records to Administrator upon request

units.obligation_text: Capture efficiency. If you demonstrate compliance by meeting the requirements of § 63.3370(f) through (i), (j)(2), (l), (o)(2) or (3), or (q), you must determine capture efficiency using the procedures in paragraph (f)(1), (2), or (3) of this section, as applicable.
units.action_summary: If demonstrating compliance via specified §63.3370 provisions, determine capture efficiency using the applicable procedures in §63.3360(f)(1)-(3)

units.obligation_text: Volatile matter retained in the coated web or otherwise not emitted to the atmosphere. You may choose to take into account the mass of volatile matter retained in the coated web after curing or drying or otherwise not emitted to the atmosphere when determining compliance with the emission standards in § 63.3320.
units.action_summary: You may elect to account for volatile matter retained in the web when determining compliance with emission standards

units.obligation_text: If you choose this option, you must develop a site- and product-specific emission factor (EF) and determine the amount of volatile matter retained in the web using Equation 3.
units.actor: owner or operator (you) choosing to account for retained volatile matter
units.action_summary: If you choose to account for retained volatile matter, develop a site/product-specific EF and calculate retained mass using Equation 3

units.obligation_text: The EF must be developed by conducting a performance test using Method 25A of Appendix A–7 to 40 CFR part 60 and be determined by obtaining the average of a three-run test.
units.action_summary: Develop the EF via a three-run performance test using Method 25A and use the average result

units.obligation_text: You may use the EF in your compliance calculations only for periods that the work station(s) was (were) used to make the product, or a similar product, corresponding to that produced during the performance test.
units.action_summary: You can only apply the EF to compliance calculations for periods producing the same or similar product as during the EF test

units.obligation_text: You must develop a separate EF for each group of different products that you choose to utilize an EF for calculating emissions by conducting a separate performance test for that product.
units.action_summary: Develop separate EF by product group via separate performance tests if using EF to calculate emissions

units.obligation_text: Calculate the mass of volatile organics retained in the web for the month from each group of similar products using Equation 3.
units.action_summary: Compute monthly retained volatile organics per product group using Equation 3

units.obligation_text: You must demonstrate compliance each month with the emission limitations in § 63.3320(b)(1) through (4). For each monthly demonstration, you may apply any combination of the emission limitations to each of your web coating lines individually, to each of one or more groupings of your lines (including a single grouping encompassing all lines of your affected source), or to any combination of individual and grouped lines, so long as each web coating line is included in the compliance demonstration for the month.
units.action_summary: Monthly demonstrate compliance with §63.3320(b)(1)-(4); you may apply limitations per line or grouped lines as long as each line is included

units.obligation_text: Each coating material used at an existing affected source does not exceed 0.04 kg organic HAP per kg coating material, and each coating material used at a new affected source does not exceed 0.016 kg organic HAP per kg coating material as-purchased; or Follow the procedures set out in § 63.3370(b).
units.action_summary: As-purchased coating HAP limits: existing ≤0.04 kg/kg; new ≤0.016 kg/kg; alternatively follow §63.3370(b) procedures

units.obligation_text: Each coating material used at an existing affected source does not exceed 0.2 kg organic HAP per kg coating solids, and each coating material used at a new affected source does not exceed 0.08 kg organic HAP per kg coating solids as-purchased.
units.action_summary: As-purchased HAP per coating solids limits: existing ≤0.2 kg/kg solids; new ≤0.08 kg/kg solids

units.obligation_text: Each coating material used at an existing affected source does not exceed 0.04 kg organic HAP per kg coating material, and each coating material used at a new affected source does not exceed 0.016 kg organic HAP per kg coating material as-applied; or Follow the procedures set out in § 63.3370(c)(1).
units.action_summary: As-applied HAP limits per coating material: existing ≤0.04 kg/kg; new ≤0.016 kg/kg; follow §63.3370(c)(1) procedures

units.obligation_text: Each coating material used at an existing affected source does not exceed 0.2 kg organic HAP per kg coating solids, and each coating material used at a new affected source does not exceed 0.08 kg organic HAP per kg coating solids as-applied; or Follow the procedures set out in § 63.3370(c)(2).
units.action_summary: As-applied HAP per coating solids limits: existing ≤0.2 kg/kg solids; new ≤0.08 kg/kg solids; follow §63.3370(c)(2) procedures

title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Hydrochloric Acid Production Residual Risk and Technology Review

units.obligation_text: An HCl production facility is not subject to this subpart if all of the gaseous streams containing HCl and chlorine (Cl2) from HCl process vents, HCl storage tanks, and HCl transfer operations are recycled or routed to another process for process purpose, prior to being discharged to the atmosphere.
units.action_summary: If all gaseous streams containing HCl and Cl2 from process vents, storage tanks, and transfers are recycled or routed for process purpose before discharge, the facility is not subject to this subpart.

units.obligation_text: Before [DATE 181 DAYS AFTER PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], for each existing source, and for each new or reconstructed source for which construction or reconstruction commenced after April 17, 2003, but before February 5, 2019, you must be in compliance with the emission limitations and work practice standards in this subpart at all times, except during periods of startup, shutdown, and malfunction.
units.action_summary: Before the specified date, existing sources and certain new/reconstructed sources must comply at all times with the subpart's emission limitations and work practice standards, except during startup/shutdown/malfunction periods.

units.obligation_text: After [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], for each such source, you must be in compliance with the emission limitations in this subpart at all times.
units.action_summary: After the specified date, those sources must comply at all times with the emission limitations in the subpart.

units.obligation_text: For new and reconstructed sources for which construction or reconstruction commenced after February 4, 2019, you must be in compliance with the emissions limitations in this subpart at all times.
units.action_summary: New/reconstructed sources with construction commencing after Feb 4, 2019 must comply at all times with the subpart emission limitations.

units.obligation_text: Before [DATE 181 DAYS AFTER PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], for each existing source, and for each new or reconstructed source for which construction or reconstruction commenced after April 17, 2003, but before February 5, 2019, you must always operate and maintain your affected source, including air pollution control and monitoring equipment, according to the provisions in § 63.6(e)(1)(i).
units.action_summary: Before the specified date, affected sources must be operated and maintained according to §63.6(e)(1)(i), including control and monitoring equipment.

units.obligation_text: After [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER] for each such source, and after [DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER] for new and reconstructed sources for which construction or reconstruction commenced after February 4, 2019, at all times you must operate and maintain any affected source, including associated air pollution control equipment and monitoring equipment, in a manner consistent with safety and good air pollution control practices for minimizing emissions.
units.action_summary: After the applicable dates, affected sources must be operated and maintained at all times consistent with safety and good practices to minimize emissions.

units.obligation_text: Before [DATE 181 DAYS AFTER PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], for each existing source, and for each new or reconstructed source for which construction or reconstruction commenced after April 17, 2003, but before February 5, 2019, you must develop a written startup, shutdown, and malfunction plan according to the provisions in § 63.6(e)(3).
units.action_summary: Before the specified date, applicable sources must develop a written SSM plan per §63.6(e)(3).

units.obligation_text: For each such source, a startup, shutdown, and malfunction plan is not required after [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER].
units.action_summary: After the specified date, those sources are not required to have a SSM plan.

units.obligation_text: No startup, shutdown, and malfunction plan is required for any new or reconstructed source for which construction or reconstruction commenced after February 4, 2019.
units.action_summary: New/reconstructed sources with construction after Feb 4, 2019 do not need a SSM plan.

units.obligation_text: Before [DATE 181 DAYS AFTER PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], for each existing source, and for each new or reconstructed source for which construction or reconstruction commenced after April 17, 2003, but before February 5, 2019, ongoing operation and maintenance (O&M) procedures in accordance with the general requirements of §§ 63.8(c)(1), (3), (4)(ii), (7), and (8), and 63.9025.
units.action_summary: Before the date, applicable sources must have ongoing O&M procedures meeting the listed general requirements and §63.9025.

units.obligation_text: After [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER] for each such source, and after [DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER] for new and reconstructed sources for which construction or reconstruction commenced after February 4, 2019, ongoing operation and maintenance (O&M) procedures in accordance with the general requirements of §§ 63.8(c)(1)(ii), (3), (4)(ii), (7), and (8), and 63.9025.
units.action_summary: After the specified dates, applicable sources must have O&M procedures meeting the listed (slightly different) general requirements and §63.9025.

units.obligation_text: Before [DATE 181 DAYS AFTER PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], for each existing source, and for each new or reconstructed source for which construction or reconstruction commenced after April 17, 2003, but before February 5, 2019, ongoing data quality assurance procedures in accordance with the general requirements of § 63.8(d).
units.action_summary: Before the date, applicable sources must have ongoing data QA procedures per §63.8(d).

units.obligation_text: After [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER] for each such source, and after [DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER] for new and reconstructed sources for which construction or reconstruction commenced after [February 4, 2019, ongoing data quality assurance procedures in accordance with the general requirements of § 63.8(d) except for the requirements related to startup, shutdown, and malfunction plans referenced in § 63.8(d)(3).
units.action_summary: After the specified dates, applicable sources must follow data QA procedures per §63.8(d) except for requirements tied to SSM plans in §63.8(d)(3).

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator shall keep these written procedures on record for the life of the affected source or until the affected source is no longer subject to the provisions of this part, to be made available for inspection, upon request, by the Administrator.
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must retain written data QA procedures for the life of the affected source (or until no longer subject) and make them available for EPA inspection upon request.

units.obligation_text: If the performance evaluation plan is revised, the owner or operator shall keep previous (i.e., superseded) versions of the performance evaluation plan on record to be made available for inspection, upon request, by the Administrator, for a period of 5 years after each revision to the plan.
units.action_summary: If the performance evaluation plan is revised, owners/operators must retain superseded versions for 5 years and make them available to the Administrator on request.

units.obligation_text: The program of corrective action should be included in the plan required under § 63.8(d)(2).
units.action_summary: Owners/operators are advised to include a corrective action program in the performance evaluation plan required under §63.8(d)(2).

units.obligation_text: Before [DATE 181 DAYS AFTER PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], for each existing source, and for each new or reconstructed source for which construction or reconstruction commenced after April 17, 2003, but before February 5, 2019, ongoing recordkeeping and reporting procedures in accordance with the general requirements of § 63.10(c) and (e)(1) and (2)(i).
units.action_summary: Before the specified date, applicable sources must follow recordkeeping and reporting procedures per §63.10(c) and (e)(1) and (2)(i).

units.obligation_text: After [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER] for each such source, and after [DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER] for new and reconstructed sources for which construction or reconstruction commenced after February 4, 2019, ongoing recordkeeping and reporting procedures in accordance with the general requirements of § 63.10(c)(1) through (c)(14), and (e)(1) and (2)(i).
units.action_summary: After the specified dates, applicable sources must follow the expanded recordkeeping and reporting requirements in §63.10(c)(1)-(14) and (e)(1) and (2)(i).

units.obligation_text: Before [DATE 181 DAYS AFTER PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], for each existing source, and for each new or reconstructed source for which construction or reconstruction commenced after April 17, 2003, but before February 5, 2019, you must conduct each performance test under representative conditions according to the requirements in § 63.7(e)(1) and under the specific conditions that this subpart specifies in Table 3.
units.action_summary: Before the date, applicable sources must perform performance tests under representative conditions per §63.7(e)(1) and Table 3.

units.obligation_text: After [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER] for each such source, and after [DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER] for new and reconstructed sources for which construction or reconstruction commenced after February 4, 2019, you must conduct each performance test under conditions representative of normal operations.
units.action_summary: After the dates, sources must conduct performance tests under conditions representative of normal operations.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator must record the process information that is necessary to document operating conditions during the test and include in such record an explanation to support that such conditions represent normal operation.
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must record process information during performance tests and explain how conditions represent normal operation.

units.obligation_text: Upon request, the owner or operator shall make available to the Administrator such records as may be necessary to determine the conditions of performance tests.
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must provide test condition records to the Administrator upon request.

units.obligation_text: You may not conduct performance tests during periods of startup, shutdown, or malfunction.
units.action_summary: Performance tests are prohibited during startup, shutdown, or malfunction periods.

units.obligation_text: For at least 75 percent of the operating hours in a 24-hour period, you must have valid data (as defined in your site-specific monitoring plan) for at least 4 equally spaced periods each hour.
units.action_summary: Operators must obtain valid monitoring data for at least 75% of operating hours per day, with at least 4 equally spaced valid periods each hour.

units.obligation_text: 75 percent of the operating hours in a 24-hour period
units.action_summary: Threshold: valid data must be present for at least 75% of operating hours in a day.

units.obligation_text: for at least 4 equally spaced periods each hour
units.action_summary: Specification: valid data must cover at least 4 equally spaced periods every hour.

units.obligation_text: For existing sources and for new or reconstructed sources which commenced construction or reconstruction after April 17, 2003, but before February 5, 2019, before [DATE 181 DAYS AFTER PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], You must submit the Notification of Compliance Status containing the results of the initial compliance demonstration according to the requirements in § 63.9045(f)-(g).
units.action_summary: Before the specified date, applicable sources must submit a Notification of Compliance Status (NOCS) containing initial compliance demonstration results per §63.9045(f)-(g).

units.obligation_text: After [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER] for such sources, and after [DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER] for new or reconstructed sources which commence construction or reconstruction after February 4, 2019, you must submit the Notification of Compliance Status containing the results of the initial compliance demonstration according to the requirements in § 63.9045(f)–(g) and § 63.9050(d).
units.action_summary: After the dates, applicable sources must submit NOCS with initial demonstration results per §63.9045(f)-(g) and §63.9050(d).

units.obligation_text: For existing sources and for new or reconstructed sources which commenced construction or reconstruction after April 17, 2003, but before February 5, 2019, before [DATE 181 DAYS AFTER PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], consistent with §§ 63.6(e) and 63.7(e)(1), deviations that occur during a period of startup, shutdown, or malfunction are not violations if you demonstrate to the Administrator’s satisfaction that you were operating in accordance with § 63.6(e)(1).
units.action_summary: Before the date, deviations during SSM are not violations provided the owner/operator demonstrates compliance with §63.6(e)(1) to the Administrator's satisfaction.

units.obligation_text: After [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER] for such sources, and after [DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER] for new and reconstructed sources which commence construction or reconstruction after February 4, 2019, the exemptions for periods of startup, shutdown, and malfunction in § 63.6(e) no longer apply.
units.action_summary: After the specified dates, exemptions for deviations during SSM in §63.6(e) are removed and cannot be claimed.

units.obligation_text: You must submit the Notification of Compliance Status, including the performance test results, within 180 calendar days after the applicable compliance dates specified in § 63.8995.
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must submit NOCS with performance test results within 180 days after the applicable compliance dates in §63.8995.

units.obligation_text: You must submit a compliance report that includes the information in § 63.9050(c) through (e), as applicable, as specified in Table 6 to this subpart.
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must submit a compliance report containing the specified information in §63.9050(c)-(e) and Table 6.

units.obligation_text: If you had a startup, shutdown, or malfunction during the reporting period and you took actions consistent with your startup, shutdown, and malfunction plan, the compliance report must include the information in § 63.10(d)(5)(i).
units.action_summary: If an SSM occurred and actions were consistent with the SSM plan, the compliance report must include the information specified in §63.10(d)(5)(i).

units.obligation_text: A startup, shutdown, and malfunction plan and the information in § 63.10(d)(5)(i) is not required after [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER].
units.action_summary: After the specified date, a SSM plan and the related reporting information in §63.10(d)(5)(i) are not required.

units.obligation_text: If there are no deviations from any emission limitations that apply to you, a statement that there were no deviations from the emission limitations during the reporting period.
units.action_summary: If no deviations occurred, include a statement in the compliance report that there were no deviations during the reporting period.

units.obligation_text: For each deviation from an emission limitation occurring at an affected source where you are using a CMS to comply with the emission limitation in this subpart, you must include the information in paragraphs (c)(1) through (6) of this section and the following information in paragraphs (d)(1) through (9) of this section and § 63.10(e)(3)(vi).
units.action_summary: When using a CMS, for each deviation you must include the listed information from (c)(1)-(6), (d)(1)-(9), and §63.10(e)(3)(vi) in reports (including SSM periods).

units.obligation_text: For each startup, shutdown, or malfunction during the reporting period that is not consistent with your startup, shutdown, and malfunction plan you must submit an immediate startup, shutdown and malfunction report.
units.action_summary: If an SSM occurred that is not consistent with your SSM plan, you must submit an immediate SSM report.

units.obligation_text: Unless the Administrator has approved a different schedule for submission of reports under § 63.10(a), you must submit each report according to paragraphs (f)(1) and (2) of this section.
units.action_summary: Reports must be submitted according to the timing in (f)(1) and (f)(2) unless the Administrator approves a different schedule.

units.obligation_text: An immediate startup, shutdown, and malfunction report is not required after [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER].
units.action_summary: After the specified date, immediate SSM reports are not required.

units.obligation_text: Within 60 days after the date of completing each performance test required by this subpart, you must submit the results of the performance test following the procedures specified in paragraphs (g)(1) through (3) of this section.
units.action_summary: Performance test results must be submitted within 60 days following the specified procedures.

units.obligation_text: Data collected using test methods supported by the EPA’s Electronic Reporting Tool (ERT) ... Submit the results of the performance test to the EPA via the Compliance and Emissions Data Reporting Interface (CEDRI) ... The data must be submitted in a file format generated through the use of the EPA’s ERT. Alternatively, you may submit an electronic file consistent with the extensible markup language (XML) schema listed on the EPA’s ERT website.
units.action_summary: If test methods are supported by ERT, submit test results via CEDRI in ERT-generated format or an XML schema-compliant electronic file.

units.obligation_text: Data collected using test methods that are not supported by the EPA’s ERT ... Submit the results of the performance test as an attachment in the ERT.
units.action_summary: If test methods are not supported by ERT, submit performance test results as an attachment in the ERT.

units.obligation_text: If you claim some of the information submitted under paragraph (a)(1) is CBI, you must submit a complete file, including information claimed to be CBI, to the EPA. The file must be generated through the use of the EPA’s ERT or an alternate electronic file consistent with the XML schema listed on the EPA’s ERT website. Submit the file on a compact disc, flash drive or other commonly used electronic storage medium and clearly mark the medium as CBI. Mail the electronic medium to U.S. EPA/OAQPS/CORE CBI Office ... The same file with the CBI omitted must be submitted to the EPA via the EPA’s CDX as described in paragraph (a)(1) of this section.
units.action_summary: If claiming CBI, submit a complete file including CBI via ERT/XML on physical media marked CBI to the EPA CBI Office, and also submit the non-CBI version via CDX/CEDRI.

units.obligation_text: Within 60 days after the date of completing each continuous monitoring system (CMS) performance evaluation (as defined in § 63.2), you must submit the results of the performance evaluation following the procedures specified in paragraphs (h)(1) through (3) of this section.
units.action_summary: CMS performance evaluation results must be submitted within 60 days according to the specified procedures.

units.obligation_text: Performance evaluations of CMS measuring relative accuracy test audit (RATA) pollutants that are supported by the EPA’s ERT ... Submit the results of the performance evaluation to the EPA via CEDRI ... The data must be submitted in a file format generated through the use of the EPA’s ERT. Alternatively, you may submit an electronic file consistent with the XML schema listed on the EPA’s ERT website.
units.action_summary: If CMS RATA pollutants are supported by ERT, submit evaluation results via CEDRI in ERT format or XML schema-compliant file.

units.obligation_text: Performance evaluations of CMS measuring RATA pollutants that are not supported by the EPA’s ERT ... Submit the results of the performance evaluation as an attachment in the ERT.
units.action_summary: If CMS RATA pollutants are not supported by ERT, submit evaluation results as an attachment in the ERT.

units.obligation_text: If you claim some of the information submitted under paragraph (a)(1) is CBI, you must submit a complete file, including information claimed to be CBI, to the EPA. The file must be generated through the use of the EPA’s ERT or an alternate electronic file consistent with the XML schema listed on the EPA’s ERT website. Submit the file on a compact disc, flash drive or other commonly used electronic storage medium and clearly mark the medium as CBI. Mail the electronic medium to U.S. EPA/OAQPS/CORE CBI Office ... The same file with the CBI omitted must be submitted to the EPA via the EPA’s CDX as described in paragraph (a)(1) of this section.
units.action_summary: If claiming CBI for CMS evaluation submissions, submit complete CBI file on physical media marked CBI to EPA CBI Office and submit non-CBI file via CDX/CEDRI.

units.obligation_text: You must submit to the Administrator compliance reports. Beginning on [DATE 181 DAYS AFTER PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], submit all subsequent reports following the procedure specified in paragraph (l) of this section.
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must submit compliance reports to the Administrator and, beginning on the specified date, must follow the electronic submission procedure in (l) for subsequent reports.

units.obligation_text: You must submit to the Administrator performance evaluations. Beginning on [DATE 181 DAYS AFTER PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], submit all subsequent reports following the procedure specified in paragraph (l) of this section.
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must submit performance evaluations to the Administrator and, starting on the specified date, must use the procedure in (l) for subsequent submissions.

units.obligation_text: You must submit to the Administrator a Notification of Compliance Status. Beginning on [DATE 181 DAYS AFTER PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], submit all subsequent reports following the procedure specified in paragraph (l) of this section.
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must submit a Notification of Compliance Status to the Administrator and, after the specified date, use the procedure in (l) for subsequent submissions.
