units.obligation_text: If you are required to submit reports following the procedure specified in this paragraph, you must submit reports to the EPA via CEDRI. ... You must use the appropriate electronic report template on the CEDRI website ... The report must be submitted by the deadline specified in this subpart, regardless of the method in which the report is submitted. If you claim some of the information required to be submitted via CEDRI is confidential business information (CBI), submit a complete report, including information claimed to be CBI, to the EPA. The report must be generated using the appropriate form on the CEDRI website. Submit the file on a compact disc, flash drive, or other commonly used electronic storage medium and clearly mark the medium as CBI. Mail the electronic medium to U.S. EPA/OAQPS/CORE CBI Office ... The same file with the CBI omitted must be submitted to the EPA via the EPA’s CDX as described earlier in this paragraph.
units.action_summary: When required, reports must be submitted via CEDRI using the appropriate template, by the subpart deadline; if claiming CBI, submit a complete CBI file to the EPA CBI Office on physical media and submit the non-CBI file via CDX/CEDRI.

units.obligation_text: If you are required to electronically submit a report through CEDRI in the EPA’s CDX, you may assert a claim of EPA system outage for failure to timely comply with the reporting requirement. To assert a claim of EPA system outage, you must meet the requirements outlined in paragraphs (m)(1) through (7) of this section.
units.action_summary: You may assert an EPA system outage claim for late reporting if you meet the listed requirements (m)(1)-(7).

units.obligation_text: You must have been or will be precluded from accessing CEDRI and submitting a required report within the time prescribed due to an outage of either the EPA’s CEDRI or CDX systems.
units.action_summary: To claim outage, you must have been or will be prevented from accessing CEDRI/CDX during the reporting period due to system outage.
units.modal_raw: must have been or will be

units.obligation_text: The outage must have occurred within the period of time beginning 5 business days prior to the date that the submission is due.
units.action_summary: The outage must have taken place within 5 business days before the submission due date to claim outage.

units.obligation_text: The outage may be planned or unplanned.
units.action_summary: The outage for which a claim is asserted can be either planned or unplanned.

units.obligation_text: You must submit notification to the Administrator in writing as soon as possible following the date you first knew, or through due diligence should have known, that the event may cause or caused a delay in reporting.
units.action_summary: You must promptly notify the Administrator in writing when you first knew (or should have known) an event may cause or caused a reporting delay.

units.obligation_text: You must provide to the Administrator a written description identifying: (i) The date, time and length of the outage; (ii) A rationale for attributing the delay in reporting beyond the regulatory deadline to EPA system outage; (iii) Measures taken or to be taken to minimize the delay in reporting; and (iv) The date by which you propose to report, or if you have already met the reporting requirement at the time of the notification, the date you reported.
units.action_summary: You must provide a written description to the Administrator containing outage details, rationale, mitigation measures, and proposed or actual reporting date.

units.obligation_text: The decision to accept the claim of EPA system outage and allow an extension to the reporting deadline is solely within the discretion of the Administrator.
units.action_summary: Acceptance of an EPA system outage claim and granting of an extension is solely at the Administrator's discretion.

units.obligation_text: In any circumstance, the report must be submitted electronically as soon as possible after the outage is resolved.
units.action_summary: After an outage, the report must be submitted electronically as soon as possible.

units.obligation_text: If you are required to electronically submit a report through CEDRI in the EPA’s CDX, you may assert a claim of force majeure for failure to timely comply with the reporting requirement. To assert a claim of force majeure, you must meet the requirements outlined in paragraphs (n)(1) through (5) of this section.
units.action_summary: You may assert a force majeure claim for late electronic reporting if you meet the specified (n)(1)-(5) requirements.

units.obligation_text: You may submit a claim if a force majeure event is about to occur, occurs, or has occurred or there are lingering effects from such an event within the period of time beginning 5 business days prior to the date the submission is due.
units.action_summary: You may submit a force majeure claim if the event occurs or has lingering effects within 5 business days before the submission due date.

units.obligation_text: You must submit notification to the Administrator in writing as soon as possible following the date you first knew, or through due diligence should have known, that the event may cause or caused a delay in reporting.
units.action_summary: You must notify the Administrator in writing promptly when aware (or should have been aware) that a force majeure event may cause a reporting delay.

units.obligation_text: You must provide to the Administrator: (i) A written description of the force majeure event; (ii) A rationale for attributing the delay in reporting beyond the regulatory deadline to the force majeure event; (iii) Measures taken or to be taken to minimize the delay in reporting; and (iv) The date by which you propose to report, or if you have already met the reporting requirement at the time of the notification, the date you reported.
units.action_summary: You must provide a written description of the force majeure event, rationale, mitigation measures, and proposed or actual reporting date to the Administrator.

units.obligation_text: The decision to accept the claim of force majeure and allow an extension to the reporting deadline is solely within the discretion of the Administrator.
units.action_summary: Acceptance of force majeure claims and granting extensions is at the Administrator's sole discretion.

units.obligation_text: In any circumstance, the reporting must occur as soon as possible after the force majeure event occurs.
units.action_summary: Reports must be submitted as soon as possible after the force majeure event.

units.obligation_text: For existing sources and for new or reconstructed sources which commenced construction or reconstruction after April 17, 2003, but before February 5, 2019, before [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], the records in § 63.6(e)(3)(iii) through (v) related to startup, shutdown, and malfunction. for a period of five years.
units.action_summary: Before the specified date, applicable sources must retain records specified in §63.6(e)(3)(iii)-(v) related to SSM for five years.

units.obligation_text: A startup, shutdown, and malfunction plan is not required after [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER].
units.action_summary: After the specified date, SSM plans are not required.

units.obligation_text: After [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], you must keep records of each deviation specified in paragraphs (c)(1) through (3) of this section.
units.action_summary: After the date, owners/operators must keep records for each deviation as specified in (c)(1)-(3).

units.obligation_text: For each deviation record the date, time and duration of each deviation.
units.action_summary: Record date, time, and duration for each deviation.

units.obligation_text: For each deviation, record and retain a list of the affected sources or equipment, an estimate of the quantity of each regulated pollutant emitted over any emission limit and a description of the method used to estimate the emissions.
units.action_summary: For each deviation, record affected equipment, estimate pollutant quantities over the limit, and describe the estimation method; retain these records.

units.obligation_text: Record actions taken to minimize emissions in accordance with 63.9005(b), and any corrective actions taken to return the affected unit to its normal or usual manner of operation.
units.action_summary: Record actions taken to minimize emissions per §63.9005(b) and any corrective actions to return units to normal operation.

units.obligation_text: Any records required to be maintained by this part that are submitted electronically via the EPA’s CEDRI may be maintained in electronic format.
units.action_summary: Records submitted via CEDRI may be kept electronically.

units.obligation_text: This ability to maintain electronic copies does not affect the requirement for facilities to make records, data, and reports available upon request to a delegated air agency or the EPA as part of an on-site compliance evaluation.
units.action_summary: Regardless of electronic maintenance, facilities must make records, data, and reports available upon request for on-site compliance evaluations.

title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Hydrochloric Acid Production Residual Risk and Technology Review

units.obligation_text: The EPA will hold a public hearing on March 27, 2019, in Washington, DC
units.action_summary: EPA will hold a public hearing on March 27, 2019 in Washington, DC.

units.obligation_text: The deadline for accepting written comments is being extended by 36 days, to April 26, 2019
units.action_summary: The public comment deadline is extended to April 26, 2019.

units.obligation_text: Because this hearing is being held at a U.S. government facility, individuals planning to attend the hearing should be prepared to show valid picture identification to the security staff to gain access to the meeting room
units.action_summary: Attendees should be prepared to show valid photo ID to security to access the meeting room.

units.obligation_text: For purposes of the REAL ID Act, the EPA will accept government-issued IDs, including driver's licenses from the District of Columbia and all states and territories
units.action_summary: EPA will accept government-issued IDs (including state/DC driver's licenses) for REAL ID Act purposes.

units.obligation_text: Acceptable alternative forms of identification include: Federal employee badges, passports, enhanced driver's licenses, and military identification cards
units.action_summary: Attendees may use listed alternative forms of identification to gain access.

units.obligation_text: Any objects brought into the building need to fit through the security screening system, such as a purse, laptop bag, or small backpack
units.actor: individuals bringing objects into the building
units.action_summary: Objects brought into the building must fit through the security screening system.

units.obligation_text: Demonstrations will not be allowed on federal property for security reasons
units.action_summary: Demonstrations are prohibited on federal property at the hearing.

units.obligation_text: The last day to pre-register to speak at the hearing will be March 25, 2019
units.action_summary: Prospective speakers must pre-register by March 25, 2019 if they want to pre-register.

units.obligation_text: Additionally, requests to speak will be taken the day of the hearing at the hearing registration desk
units.action_summary: Requests to speak may be submitted in person at the registration desk on the day of the hearing.

units.obligation_text: The hearing will convene at 9:00 a.m. (local time) and will conclude at 5:00 p.m.
units.action_summary: The hearing is scheduled to start at 9:00 a.m. and end at 5:00 p.m.

units.obligation_text: If there are no additional registered speakers, the EPA will end the hearing 2 hours after the last registered speaker has concluded their comments
units.action_summary: If no additional registered speakers exist, EPA will end the hearing two hours after the last registered speaker finishes.

units.obligation_text: The EPA will begin pre-registering speakers for the hearing upon publication of this document in the Federal Register
units.action_summary: EPA will start pre-registration for speakers upon publication.

units.obligation_text: On March 26, 2019, the EPA will post ... a general agenda for the hearing that will list pre-registered speakers in approximate order
units.action_summary: EPA will post a general agenda listing pre-registered speakers on March 26, 2019.

units.obligation_text: The EPA will make every effort to follow the schedule as closely as possible on the day of the hearing; however, please plan for the hearing to run either ahead of schedule or behind schedule
units.action_summary: EPA will attempt to follow the schedule; attendees should plan for possible schedule changes.

units.obligation_text: Each commenter will have 5 minutes to provide oral testimony
units.action_summary: Each commenter is allotted 5 minutes for oral testimony at the hearing.

units.obligation_text: The EPA encourages commenters to provide the EPA with a copy of their oral testimony electronically (via email) or in hard copy form
units.action_summary: EPA asks commenters to provide copies of their oral testimony electronically or in hard copy.

units.obligation_text: The EPA may ask clarifying questions during the oral presentations
units.action_summary: EPA may ask clarifying questions of presenters during oral presentations.

units.obligation_text: Written statements and supporting information submitted during the comment period will be considered with the same weight as oral comments and supporting information presented at the public hearing
units.action_summary: EPA will give written statements submitted during the comment period equal consideration to oral comments from the hearing.

units.obligation_text: Commenters should notify Nancy Perry if they will need specific equipment or if there are other special needs related to providing comments at the hearings
units.action_summary: Commenters needing specific equipment or special accommodations should notify Nancy Perry in advance.

units.obligation_text: Verbatim transcripts of the hearings and written statements will be included in the docket for the rulemaking
units.action_summary: EPA will include hearing transcripts and written statements in the rulemaking docket.

units.obligation_text: Please note that any updates made to any aspect of the hearing will be posted online at [EPA website]
units.action_summary: EPA will post any updates about the hearing on its website.

units.obligation_text: The EPA does not intend to publish a document in the Federal Register announcing updates
units.action_summary: EPA does not plan to publish Federal Register notices announcing hearing updates.

units.obligation_text: The EPA will not provide audiovisual equipment
units.action_summary: EPA will not supply audiovisual equipment for commenters at the hearing.

units.obligation_text: Commenters should notify Nancy Perry when they pre-register to speak that they will require the service of a translator or special accommodations such as audio description
units.action_summary: Commenters needing translators or special accommodations should notify Nancy Perry when pre-registering.

units.obligation_text: The EPA may not be able to arrange accommodations without advanced notice
units.action_summary: EPA might be unable to arrange accommodations if not given advanced notice.

units.obligation_text: Global marine fuel. "For use only in steamships or Category 3 marine vessels outside of an Emission Control Area (ECA), consistent with MARPOL Annex VI."

units.action_summary: Include the specified global marine fuel usage statement in the product transfer document.

units.obligation_text: Beginning June 1, 2007, or June 1, 2006, if that is the first period credits are generated under § 80.535, any person who produces, imports, sells, offers for sale, dispenses, distributes, supplies, offers for supply, stores, or transports nonroad, locomotive or marine diesel fuel, or ECA marine fuel (beginning June 1, 2014) subject to the provisions of this subpart, must keep all the records specified in this paragraph (a). These recordkeeping requirements for global marine fuel start January 1, 2020.

units.action_summary: Maintain all records specified in paragraph (a) for covered fuels; recordkeeping for global marine fuel begins Jan 1, 2020.

units.obligation_text: The applicable product transfer documents required under §§ 80.590 and 80.591.
units.actor: any person subject to the recordkeeping requirements in § 80.602(a)
units.action_summary: Keep copies of the applicable product transfer documents required by §§ 80.590 and 80.591.

units.obligation_text: The location, date, time and storage tank or truck identification for each sample collected;
units.actor: any person conducting sampling/testing and subject to the recordkeeping requirements
units.action_summary: Record location, date, time, and storage tank/truck ID for each sample collected.

units.obligation_text: The name and title of the person who collected the sample and the person who performed the testing;
units.actor: any person conducting sampling/testing and subject to the recordkeeping requirements
units.action_summary: Record the names and titles of the sampler and tester for each sample.

units.obligation_text: The results of the tests for sulfur content (including, where applicable, the test results with and without application of the adjustment factor under § 80.580(d)), for cetane index or aromatics content, dye solvent red 164, marker solvent yellow 124 (as applicable), and the volume of product in the storage tank or container from which the sample was taken.
units.actor: any person conducting sampling/testing and subject to the recordkeeping requirements
units.action_summary: Record test results for specified fuel properties and the sampled product volume.

units.obligation_text: The actions the party has taken, if any, to stop the sale or distribution of any NRLM diesel fuel, global marine fuel, or ECA marine fuel found not to be in compliance with the sulfur standards specified in this subpart, and the actions the party has taken, if any, to identify the cause of any noncompliance and prevent future instances of noncompliance.
units.actor: any person subject to the recordkeeping requirements
units.action_summary: Document and keep records of any actions taken to stop noncompliant fuel sales/distribution and to identify and prevent causes of noncompliance.

units.obligation_text: These recordkeeping requirements for global marine fuel start January 1, 2020.
units.action_summary: Recordkeeping obligations for global marine fuel become effective Jan 1, 2020.

units.obligation_text: NRLM diesel fuel, NR diesel fuel, LM diesel fuel, global marine fuel, ECA marine fuel, or heating oil, as applicable.
units.actor: entities required to keep records under § 80.602(b)
units.action_summary: Include records pertaining to the applicable fuel types specified.

units.obligation_text: Exempt distillate fuels such as global marine fuels under § 80.605, fuels that are covered by a national security exemption under § 80.606, fuels that are used for purposes of research and development pursuant to § 80.607, and fuels used in the U.S. Territories pursuant to § 80.608 (including additional identifying information).
units.actor: refiners, importers, and distributors (when providing designations)
units.action_summary: Include identification of exempt distillate fuels (including global marine fuels and listed exemptions) and additional identifying information in designation documentation.

units.obligation_text: Exempt distillate fuels such as global marine fuels under § 80.605, fuels that are covered by a national security exemption under § 80.606, fuels that are used for purposes of research and development pursuant to § 80.607, and fuels used in the U.S. Territories pursuant to § 80.608 (including additional identifying information).
units.actor: refiners, importers, and distributors (when providing designations)
units.action_summary: Provide the listed identification information for exempt distillate fuels as part of designation procedures.

units.obligation_text: The standards of this subpart I do not apply to global marine fuel that is produced, imported, sold, offered for sale, supplied, offered for supply, stored, dispensed, or transported for use in steamships or Category 3 marine vessels when operating outside of ECA boundaries.
units.actor: global marine fuel produced, imported, sold, supplied, stored, dispensed, or transported for use in steamships or Category 3 vessels outside ECAs (and the persons handling such fuel)
units.action_summary: Grant an exemption from the subpart's standards for global marine fuel used in specified vessels outside ECAs.

units.obligation_text: The exempt fuel must meet all the following conditions:
units.actor: exempt global marine fuel (and persons handling it)
units.action_summary: Before qualifying for the exemption, exempt global marine fuel must satisfy the listed conditions.

units.obligation_text: It must not exceed 0.50 weight percent sulfur (5.0·103 ppm).
units.actor: exempt global marine fuel (and persons producing/importing/supplying it)
units.action_summary: Ensure sulfur content does not exceed 0.50 weight percent (5,000 ppm).

units.obligation_text: It must be accompanied by product transfer documents as required under § 80.590.
units.actor: exempt global marine fuel (and persons transferring it)
units.action_summary: Accompany the exempt fuel with the product transfer documents required by § 80.590.

units.obligation_text: It must be designated as specified under § 80.598.
units.actor: exempt global marine fuel (and persons designating it)
units.action_summary: Designate the fuel consistent with the requirements of § 80.598.

units.obligation_text: It must be segregated from non-exempt fuel at all points in the distribution system.
units.actor: persons handling exempt global marine fuel
units.action_summary: Keep exempt fuel physically segregated from non-exempt fuel throughout distribution.

units.obligation_text: It may not be used in any vehicles, engines, or equipment other than those referred to in paragraph (a) of this section.
units.actor: users/handlers of exempt global marine fuel
units.action_summary: Prohibit use of the exempt fuel in vehicles, engines, or equipment other than steamships or Category 3 marine vessels outside ECAs.

units.obligation_text: Fuel not meeting the conditions specified in paragraph (b) of this section is subject to the standards, requirements, and prohibitions that apply for MVNRLM diesel fuel.
units.actor: fuel failing to meet the paragraph (b) conditions (and persons handling it)
units.action_summary: If fuel fails to meet the exemption conditions, it becomes subject to MVNRLM diesel fuel standards and requirements.

units.obligation_text: Any person who produces, imports, sells, offers for sale, supplies, offers for supply, stores, dispenses, or transports global marine fuel without meeting the recordkeeping requirements under § 80.602 may not claim the fuel is exempt from the standards, requirements, and prohibitions that apply for MVNRLM diesel fuel.
units.actor: any person who produces, imports, sells, offers for sale, supplies, offers for supply, stores, dispenses, or transports global marine fuel
units.action_summary: Prohibit claiming the exemption for global marine fuel if the recordkeeping requirements of § 80.602 are not met.

units.obligation_text: Engines and vessels may qualify for delaying the Tier 4 standards specified in § 1042.101 as follows:
units.action_summary: Engines and vessels that meet specified criteria may be eligible to delay Tier 4 standards.

units.obligation_text: Category 1 propulsion engines with specific power density above 35.0 kW/liter, up to maximum engine power of 1,400 kW.
units.action_summary: Engine must be Category 1 with power density >35.0 kW/liter and max power up to 1,400 kW to qualify for the delay (MY2021 and earlier).

units.obligation_text: Vessels have total propulsion power at or below 2,800 kW.
units.action_summary: Vessel total propulsion power must be ≤ 2,800 kW to qualify for the delay (MY2021 and earlier).

units.obligation_text: Vessel length is at or below 65 feet.
units.action_summary: Vessel length must be ≤ 65 feet to qualify for the delay (MY2021 and earlier).

units.obligation_text: Vessels qualify as uninspected vessels under 46 CFR 2.01–7.
units.action_summary: Vessel must qualify as an uninspected vessel under 46 CFR 2.01–7 to be eligible for the delay (MY2021 and earlier).

units.obligation_text: Vessels have a maximum speed (in knots) at or above 3.0 • L1/2, where L is the vessel’s waterline length, in feet.
units.action_summary: Vessel maximum speed must meet or exceed 3.0 * sqrt(L) knots to qualify for the delay (MY2021 and earlier).

units.obligation_text: Category 1 propulsion engines with specific power density above 40.0 kW/liter, up to maximum engine power of 1,000 kW.
units.action_summary: Engine must be Category 1 with power density >40.0 kW/liter and max power up to 1,000 kW to qualify for the delay (MY2022–2023).

units.obligation_text: Vessels have total propulsion power at or below 1,000 kW.
units.action_summary: Vessel total propulsion power must be ≤ 1,000 kW to qualify for the delay (MY2022–2023).

units.obligation_text: Vessel length is at or below 50 feet.
units.action_summary: Vessel length must be ≤ 50 feet to qualify for the delay (MY2022–2023).

units.obligation_text: Vessels qualify as uninspected vessels under 46 CFR 2.01–7.
units.action_summary: Vessel must qualify as an uninspected vessel under 46 CFR 2.01–7 to be eligible for the delay (MY2022–2023).

units.obligation_text: Vessels have a maximum speed (in knots) at or above 3.0 • L1/2, where L is the vessel’s waterline length, in feet.
units.action_summary: Vessel maximum speed must meet or exceed 3.0 * sqrt(L) knots to qualify for the delay (MY2022–2023).

units.obligation_text: Vessels have fiberglass or other nonmetal hulls.
units.action_summary: Vessel hull must be fiberglass or other nonmetal to qualify for the delay (MY2022–2023).

units.obligation_text: Affected engines must instead be certified to the appropriate Tier 3 emission standards specified in § 1042.101.
units.action_summary: Engines qualifying for the delay must be certified to the Tier 3 emission standards in § 1042.101.

units.obligation_text: Engine manufacturers may include engine configurations with maximum engine power below 600 kW in the same engine family even if the power density is below the value specified in paragraph (k)(1) or (2) of this section.
units.action_summary: Manufacturers are permitted to include sub-600 kW configurations in the same engine family despite lower power density for qualifying purposes.

units.obligation_text: If you introduce an engine into U.S. commerce under this section, you must meet the labeling requirements in § 1042.135, but add the following statement instead of the compliance statement in § 1042.135(c)(10): THIS MARINE ENGINE COMPLIES WITH U.S. EPA TIER 3 EMISSION STANDARDS UNDER 40 CFR 1042.145(k). ANY OTHER INSTALLATION OR USE OF THIS ENGINE MAY BE A VIOLATION OF FEDERAL LAW SUBJECT TO CIVIL PENALTY.
units.actor: you (those who introduce an engine into U.S. commerce under this section)
units.action_summary: Meet §1042.135 labeling requirements and include the specified Tier 3 compliance statement in place of the standard compliance statement when introducing an engine under this section.

units.obligation_text: THIS MARINE ENGINE COMPLIES WITH U.S. EPA TIER 3 EMISSION STANDARDS UNDER 40 CFR 1042.145(k). ANY OTHER INSTALLATION OR USE OF THIS ENGINE MAY BE A VIOLATION OF FEDERAL LAW SUBJECT TO CIVIL PENALTY.
units.action_summary: Include the exact specified compliance statement on the engine label.

units.obligation_text: Starting in model year 2024, vessel manufacturers may request an exemption from the Tier 4 standards as follows:
units.action_summary: Vessel manufacturers are permitted to request Tier 4 exemptions beginning in model year 2024 under the specified procedures.

units.obligation_text: The subject vessels and engines must meet the qualifications of paragraph (k)(2) of this section.
units.actor: the subject vessels and engines (and vessel manufacturers)
units.action_summary: Vessels and engines for which an exemption is requested must meet the criteria listed in §1042.145(k)(2).

units.obligation_text: Vessel manufacturers must send a written request for the exemption to the Designated Compliance Officer.
units.action_summary: Submit a written exemption request to the Designated Compliance Officer.

units.obligation_text: The request must describe efforts taken to identify available engines certified to the Tier 4 standards and design efforts for installing engines in the subject vessels.
units.action_summary: Explain efforts to find Tier 4 certified engines and design efforts for installation in the exemption request.

units.obligation_text: The request must also identify the number of vessels needing exempt engines.
units.action_summary: State the number of vessels that would need exempt engines in the exemption request.

units.obligation_text: Engine manufacturers may ship exempt engines under this paragraph (m) only after receiving a written request from a vessel manufacturer who has received our approval to build a specific number of vessels.
units.action_summary: Engine manufacturers are permitted to ship exempt engines only after a vessel manufacturer's approved written request has been received.

units.obligation_text: The prohibitions in § 1068.101(a)(1) do not apply to a new engine that is subject to Tier 4 standards, subject to the following conditions:
units.actor: a new engine that is subject to Tier 4 standards (and engine manufacturers)
units.action_summary: Relax the prohibitions in §1068.101(a)(1) for certain new Tier 4 engines, provided the following conditions are met.

units.obligation_text: The engine meets the appropriate Tier 3 emission standards in § 1042.101 consistent with the provisions specified in § 1068.265 of this chapter.
units.action_summary: Ensure the engine complies with the appropriate Tier 3 emissions standards per §1042.101 and §1068.265.

units.obligation_text: The engine is installed on a vessel consistent with the conditions of this paragraph (m).
units.action_summary: Install the engine only in vessels consistent with the conditions set forth in paragraph (m).

units.obligation_text: The engine meets the labeling requirements in § 1042.135, with the following statement instead of the compliance statement in § 1042.135(c)(10): THIS MARINE ENGINE DOES NOT COMPLY WITH CURRENT U.S. EPA EMISSION STANDARDS UNDER 40 CFR 1042.145(m). ANY OTHER INSTALLATION OR USE OF THIS ENGINE MAY BE A VIOLATION OF FEDERAL LAW SUBJECT TO CIVIL PENALTY.
units.action_summary: Apply the §1042.135 labeling requirements and include the specified noncompliance statement on exempt engines.

units.obligation_text: THIS MARINE ENGINE DOES NOT COMPLY WITH CURRENT U.S. EPA EMISSION STANDARDS UNDER 40 CFR 1042.145(m). ANY OTHER INSTALLATION OR USE OF THIS ENGINE MAY BE A VIOLATION OF FEDERAL LAW SUBJECT TO CIVIL PENALTY.
units.action_summary: Include the exact specified noncompliance statement on the engine label in place of the standard compliance statement.

units.obligation_text: Engine manufacturers may use assigned deterioration factors for certifying Tier 4 engines with maximum power up to 1,400 kW, as follows:
units.action_summary: Manufacturers are permitted to use assigned deterioration factors for certifying certain Tier 4 engines within specified power limits.

units.obligation_text: For engine families that have at least one configuration with maximum engine power at or below 1,400 kW and power density above 40.0 kW/liter, you may use assigned deterioration factors through model year 2023.
units.action_summary: Eligible engine families may use assigned deterioration factors through model year 2023.

units.obligation_text: For engine families that have at least one configuration with maximum engine power at or below 1,000 kW and power density above 35.0 kW/liter, you may use assigned deterioration factors through model year 2025.
units.action_summary: Eligible engine families may use assigned deterioration factors through model year 2025.

units.obligation_text: The assigned deterioration factors are multiplicative values of 1.1 for NOX and 1.4 for HC and CO, and an additive value of 0.003 g/kW-hr for PM, unless we approve your request to use different values.
units.actor: assigned deterioration factors for certification (and engine manufacturers seeking alternatives)
units.action_summary: Default assigned deterioration factors and PM additive value apply; different values require EPA approval.

units.obligation_text: We will approve your proposed values if you demonstrate that they better represent your engines based on data from similar engines you have certified.
units.action_summary: EPA will approve requested alternative deterioration factor values if the manufacturer demonstrates they better represent the engines using data from similar certified engines.

units.obligation_text: Commercial Category 1 engines at or above 600 kW with power density above 50.0 kW/liter are subject to the exhaust emission standards of this part over a full useful life of 10 years or 5,000 hours of operation instead of the useful-life values specified in § 1042.101(e).
units.actor: Commercial Category 1 engines at or above 600 kW with power density above 50.0 kW/liter (and their manufacturers)
units.action_summary: Such engines must meet the exhaust emission standards over a useful life of 10 years or 5,000 hours instead of the values in §1042.101(e).

units.obligation_text: The EPA will hold a public hearing on March 18, 2019, in Washington, DC.
units.action_summary: EPA will conduct a public hearing on March 18, 2019 in Washington, DC.

units.obligation_text: The hearing will be held at the EPA WJC East Building, 1201 Constitution Avenue NW, Room 1153, Washington, DC 20004
units.action_summary: The hearing location is at the EPA WJC East Building, Room 1153, Washington, DC.

units.obligation_text: The hearing will convene at 8:00 a.m. (local time) and will conclude at 6:00 p.m.
units.action_summary: The hearing start time is 8:00 a.m. and end time is 6:00 p.m.

units.obligation_text: There will be a lunch break from noon to 1 p.m.
units.action_summary: A lunch break is scheduled from 12:00 to 13:00.

units.obligation_text: The deadline for accepting written comments is being extended by 9 days, to April 17, 2019.
units.action_summary: EPA extended the deadline for written comments to April 17, 2019.

units.obligation_text: The EPA will begin pre-registering speakers for the hearing upon publication of this document in the Federal Register.
units.action_summary: EPA will start pre-registration of speakers once this notice is published.

units.obligation_text: On March 15, 2019, the EPA will post ... a general agenda for the hearing that will list pre-registered speakers in approximate order.
units.action_summary: EPA will publish a general agenda listing pre-registered speakers on March 15, 2019.

units.obligation_text: Additionally, requests to speak will be taken the day of the hearing at the hearing registration desk.
units.action_summary: On the hearing day, additional requests to speak may be made at the registration desk.

units.obligation_text: Each commenter will have 5 minutes to provide oral testimony.
units.action_summary: Each person providing oral testimony is limited to 5 minutes.

units.obligation_text: The EPA encourages commenters to provide the EPA with a copy of their oral testimony electronically (via email) or in hard copy form.
units.action_summary: EPA requests commenters also submit copies of oral testimony electronically or in hard copy.

units.obligation_text: The EPA may ask clarifying questions during the oral presentations, but will not respond to the presentations at that time.
units.action_summary: EPA may ask clarification questions during presentations but will not respond at that time.

units.obligation_text: Written statements and supporting information submitted during the comment period will be considered with the same weight as oral comments and supporting information presented at the public hearing.
units.action_summary: EPA will treat written statements submitted during the comment period as having the same weight as oral comments.

units.obligation_text: Commenters should notify Adrian Gates if they will need specific equipment or if there are other special needs related to providing comments at the hearing.
units.action_summary: Commenters needing equipment or special accommodations should notify Adrian Gates in advance.

units.obligation_text: We may not be able to arrange accommodations without advanced notice.
units.action_summary: EPA may be unable to provide accommodations if not notified in advance.

units.obligation_text: Because this hearing is being held at a U.S. government facility, individuals planning to attend the hearing should be prepared to show valid picture identification to the security staff to gain access to the meeting room.
units.action_summary: Attendees should be prepared to show valid photo ID at security to enter the meeting room.

units.obligation_text: For purposes of the REAL ID Act, the EPA will accept government-issued IDs, including driver's licenses from the District of Columbia and all states and territories.
units.action_summary: EPA will accept government-issued IDs including state and DC driver's licenses for entry.

units.obligation_text: Acceptable alternative forms of identification include: Federal employee badges, passports, enhanced driver's licenses, and military identification cards.
units.action_summary: Acceptable alternate IDs for entry include federal badges, passports, enhanced licenses, and military IDs.

units.obligation_text: Any objects brought into the building need to fit through the security screening system, such as a purse, laptop bag, or small backpack.

units.obligation_text: Demonstrations will not be allowed on federal property for security reasons.
units.action_summary: Demonstrations are prohibited on federal property.

units.obligation_text: The EPA will not provide audiovisual equipment.
units.action_summary: EPA will not supply audiovisual equipment for the hearing.

units.obligation_text: Commenters should notify Adrian Gates when they pre-register to speak that they will require the service of a translator or special accommodations such as audio description.
units.action_summary: Commenters needing translators or special accommodations should notify Adrian Gates when pre-registering.

units.obligation_text: Verbatim transcripts of the hearing and written statements will be included in the docket for the rulemaking.
units.action_summary: EPA will include hearing transcripts and written statements in the rulemaking docket.

units.obligation_text: Please refer to the proposal (84 FR 2670) for the addresses and detailed instructions [for submitting written comments].
units.action_summary: Commenters must consult the proposal notice for addresses and detailed submission instructions.

units.obligation_text: Please note that any updates made to any aspect of the hearing will be posted online at [EPA website].

title: Test Methods and Performance Specifications for Air Emission Sources

units.obligation_text: You can use this method to measure filterable PM from stationary sources only.
units.action_summary: May use this method to measure filterable particulate matter from stationary sources only.

units.obligation_text: If the gas filtration temperature exceeds 29.4 °C (85 °F), then you may use the procedures in this method to measure only filterable PM (material that does not pass through a filter or a cyclone/filter combination).
units.action_summary: Permits use of the method to measure only filterable PM when gas filtration temperature > 29.4 °C.

units.obligation_text: If the gas filtration temperature exceeds 29.4 °C (85 °F), and you must measure both the filterable and condensable components of total primary (direct) PM emissions to the atmosphere, then you must combine the procedures in this method with the procedures in Method 202 of appendix M to this part for measuring condensable PM.
units.action_summary: Requires combining Method 201A with Method 202 to measure both filterable and condensable PM when filtration temperature > 29.4 °C and both components must be measured.

units.obligation_text: However, if the gas filtration temperature never exceeds 29.4 °C (85 °F), then use of Method 202 of appendix M to this part is not required to measure total primary PM.
units.action_summary: If filtration temperature never exceeds 29.4 °C, Method 202 is not required to measure total primary PM.

units.obligation_text: You can use this method to obtain particle sizing at 10 micrometers and or 2.5 micrometers if you sample within 80 and 120 percent of isokinetic flow.
units.action_summary: May use method for particle sizing at PM10/PM2.5 provided sampling is within 80–120% isokinetic flow.

units.obligation_text: sample within 80 and 120 percent of isokinetic flow.
units.action_summary: Sampling must be within 80–120% of isokinetic flow to obtain particle sizing.

units.obligation_text: You can also use this method to obtain total filterable particulate if you sample within 90 to 110 percent of isokinetic flow, the number of sampling points is the same as required by Method 5 of appendix A–3 to part 60 or Method 17 of appendix A–6 to part 60, and the filter temperature is within an acceptable range for these methods.
units.action_summary: May use method to obtain total filterable particulate provided sampling meets flow, sampling-point, and filter-temperature conditions.

units.obligation_text: sample within 90 to 110 percent of isokinetic flow.
units.action_summary: Sampling must be within 90–110% of isokinetic flow to obtain total filterable particulate.

units.obligation_text: the number of sampling points is the same as required by Method 5 of appendix A–3 to part 60 or Method 17 of appendix A–6 to part 60.
units.action_summary: Number of sampling points must match those required by Method 5 or Method 17.

units.obligation_text: the filter temperature is within an acceptable range for these methods.
units.action_summary: Filter temperature must be within the acceptable range for the referenced methods.

units.obligation_text: For Method 5, the acceptable range for the filter temperature is generally 120 °C (248 °F) unless a higher or lower temperature is specified.
units.action_summary: Specifies that for Method 5, acceptable filter temperature is generally 120 °C unless otherwise specified.

units.obligation_text: To satisfy Method 5 criteria, you may need to remove the in-stack filter and use an out-of-stack filter and recover the PM in the probe between the PM2.5 particle sizer and the filter.
units.action_summary: May need to remove in-stack filter and use out-of-stack filter and recover PM to satisfy Method 5 criteria.

units.obligation_text: to satisfy Method 5 and Method 17 criteria, you may need to sample from more than 12 traverse points.
units.action_summary: May need to sample from >12 traverse points to satisfy Method 5 and 17 criteria.

units.obligation_text: this method determines in-stack PM10 and PM2.5 filterable emissions by sampling from a required maximum of 12 sample points, at a constant flow rate through the train (the constant flow is necessary to maintain the size cuts of the cyclones), and with a filter that is at the stack temperature.
units.action_summary: Method requires in-stack sampling using a maximum of 12 sample points, constant flow, and filter at stack temperature.

units.obligation_text: sampling from a required maximum of 12 sample points.
units.action_summary: Must sample from no more than 12 sample points.

units.obligation_text: sampling at a constant flow rate through the train (the constant flow is necessary to maintain the size cuts of the cyclones).
units.action_summary: Must operate sampling train at a constant flow rate to maintain cyclone size cuts.

units.obligation_text: with a filter that is at the stack temperature.
units.action_summary: Filter must be at stack temperature during sampling.

units.obligation_text: to use this method in place of Method 5 or Method 17, you must extend the sampling time so that you collect the minimum mass necessary for weighing each portion of this sampling train.
units.action_summary: Requires extending sampling time to collect minimum mass when using this method in place of Method 5 or 17.

units.obligation_text: if you are using this method as an alternative to a test method specified in a regulatory requirement (e.g., a requirement to conduct a compliance or performance test), then you must receive approval from the authority that established the regulatory requirement before you conduct the test.
units.action_summary: If using the method as an alternative to a regulatory test method, you must obtain approval from the establishing authority before conducting the test.

units.obligation_text: Petri dishes. For filter samples; glass, polystyrene, or polyethylene, unless otherwise specified by the Administrator.
units.action_summary: Petri dishes for filter samples must be made of glass, polystyrene, or polyethylene unless the Administrator specifies otherwise.

units.obligation_text: You must preheat the combined sampling head to the stack temperature of the gas stream at the test location (±28 °C, ±50 °F).
units.action_summary: Requires preheating the combined sampling head to stack temperature (±28 °C).

units.obligation_text: The approved test laboratory must allow the manufacturer, the manufacturer’s approved third-party certifier, the EPA and delegated state regulatory agencies to observe certification testing.
units.action_summary: Test labs must allow manufacturer, certifier, EPA, and delegated state agencies to observe certification testing.

units.obligation_text: manufacturers must not involve themselves in the conduct of the test after the pretest burn has begun.
units.action_summary: Prohibits manufacturers from participating in test conduct after the pretest burn begins.

units.obligation_text: Communications between the manufacturer and laboratory or third-party certifier personnel regarding operation of the wood heater must be limited to written communications transmitted prior to the first pretest burn of the certification test series.
units.actor: manufacturer and laboratory or third-party certifier personnel
units.action_summary: Requires that operational communications be written and transmitted prior to the first pretest burn.

units.obligation_text: During certification tests, the manufacturer may communicate with the third-party certifier, and only in writing to notify them that the manufacturer has observed a deviation from proper test procedures by the laboratory.
units.action_summary: Manufacturer may communicate in writing with third-party certifier during tests to notify observed deviations by the laboratory.

units.obligation_text: All communications must be included in the test documentation required to be submitted pursuant to § 60.533(b)(5) and must be consistent with instructions provided in the owner’s manual required under § 60.536(g).
units.action_summary: All communications must be included in required test documentation and conform to owner’s manual instructions.

units.obligation_text: Monitor temperature of the landfill gas on a monthly basis as provided in 60.765(a)(5).
units.action_summary: Requires monthly monitoring of landfill gas temperature.

units.obligation_text: The temperature measuring device must be calibrated annually using the procedure in 40 CFR part 60, appendix A–1, Method 2, Section 10.3 such that a minimum of two temperature points, bracket within 10 percent of all landfill absolute temperature measurements or two fixed points of ice bath and boiling water, corrected for barometric pressure, are used.
units.action_summary: Requires annual calibration of the temperature measuring device using specified procedures and calibration points.

units.obligation_text: a minimum of two temperature points, bracket within 10 percent of all landfill absolute temperature measurements.
units.action_summary: Calibration must use at least two temperature points that bracket within 10% of landfill absolute temperatures.

units.obligation_text: or two fixed points of ice bath and boiling water, corrected for barometric pressure, are used.
units.action_summary: Alternatively, calibration may use ice-bath and boiling-water fixed points corrected for barometric pressure.

units.obligation_text: If you use a PM CPMS to demonstrate continuing compliance, you must establish your PM CPMS operating limit and determine compliance with it according to paragraphs (i)(1) through (5) of this section:
units.action_summary: Requires establishment and determination of a PM CPMS operating limit according to specified procedures if PM CPMS is used for continuing compliance.

units.obligation_text: Determine your operating limit as the average PM CPMS output value recorded during the performance test or at a PM CPMS output value corresponding to 75 percent of the emission limit if your PM performance test demonstrates compliance below 75 percent of the emission limit.
units.action_summary: Operating limit must be set as either the average PM CPMS output during the performance test or the output corresponding to 75% of the emission limit if tests are below 75%.

units.obligation_text: You must verify an existing or establish a new operating limit after each repeated performance test.
units.action_summary: Must verify or establish a new operating limit after each repeated performance test.

units.obligation_text: You must repeat the performance test annually and reassess and adjust the site-specific operating limit in accordance with the results of the performance test.
units.action_summary: Requires annual performance tests and reassessment/adjustment of site-specific operating limit based on results.

units.obligation_text: Your PM CPMS must provide a 4–20 milliamp output, or digital equivalent, and the establishment of its relationship to manual reference method measurements must be determined in units of milliamps;
units.actor: the affected source operator / equipment installer
units.action_summary: PM CPMS must provide 4–20 mA (or digital equivalent) and its relationship to manual reference methods must be determined in milliamps.

units.obligation_text: Your PM CPMS operating range must be capable of reading PM concentrations from zero to a level equivalent to at least two times your allowable emission limit. If your PM CPMS is an auto-ranging instrument capable of multiple scales, the primary range of the instrument must be capable of reading PM concentration from zero to a level equivalent to two times your allowable emission limit;
units.actor: the affected source operator / equipment installer
units.action_summary: PM CPMS must read from zero up to at least two times the allowable emission limit; auto-ranging instruments must have primary range covering that span.

units.obligation_text: During the initial performance test or any such subsequent performance test that demonstrates compliance with the PM limit, record and average all milliamp output values, or their digital equivalent, from the PM CPMS for the periods corresponding to the compliance test runs (e.g., average all your PM CPMS output values for three corresponding Method 5 or Method 29 test runs).
units.action_summary: During performance tests, must record and average all PM CPMS outputs corresponding to compliance test runs.

units.obligation_text: If the average of your three PM performance test runs are below 75 percent of your PM emission limit, you must calculate an operating limit by establishing a relationship of PM CPMS signal to PM concentration using the PM CPMS instrument zero, the average PM CPMS output values corresponding to the three compliance test runs, and the average PM concentration from the Method 5 or Method 29 performance test with the procedures in (i)(1) through (5) of this section:
units.action_summary: When average of three PM runs is below 75% of limit, must calculate operating limit by relating CPMS signal to PM concentration using specified data.

units.obligation_text: For waste-burning kilns, you must conduct an annual performance test for particulate matter, cadmium, lead, carbon monoxide, dioxins/furans and hydrogen chloride as listed in table 7 of this subpart, unless you choose to demonstrate initial and continuous compliance using CEMS, as allowed in paragraph (u) of this section.

units.obligation_text: unless you choose to demonstrate initial and continuous compliance using CEMS, as allowed in paragraph (u) of this section.

units.obligation_text: If you do not use an acid gas wet scrubber or dry scrubber, you must determine compliance with the hydrogen chloride emissions limit using a HCl CEMS according to the requirements in paragraph (j)(1) of this section.
units.action_summary: If no acid gas wet/dry scrubber, must use HCl CEMS to determine HCl compliance per paragraph (j)(1).

units.obligation_text: You must determine compliance with the mercury emissions limit using a mercury CEMS or an integrated sorbent trap monitoring system according to paragraph (j)(2) of this section.

units.obligation_text: You must determine compliance with nitrogen oxides and sulfur dioxide using CEMS.

units.obligation_text: You must determine continuing compliance with the particulate matter emissions limit using a PM CPMS according to paragraph (x) of this section.
units.action_summary: Requires use of PM CPMS per paragraph (x) to demonstrate continuing PM compliance.

units.obligation_text: instead of installing a CEMS or PM CPMS on the alkali bypass stack or in-line coal mill stack, the results of the initial and subsequent performance test can be used to demonstrate compliance with the relevant emissions limit.

units.obligation_text: A performance test must be conducted on an annual basis (no later than 13 calendar months following the previous performance test).

units.obligation_text: You must conduct annual performance tests no later than 13 calendar months following the previous performance test.
units.action_summary: Requires annual performance tests within 13 months of the prior test.

units.obligation_text: The annual report required under § 60.2205 must include the items listed in paragraphs (a) through (p) of this section.
units.action_summary: Annual report must include items listed in paragraphs (a) through (p).

units.obligation_text: If you have a deviation from the operating limits or the emission limitations, you must also submit deviation reports as specified in §§ 60.2215, 60.2220, and 60.2225:

title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Solvent Extraction for Vegetable Oil Production Residual Risk and Technology Review

units.obligation_text: For each facility meeting the applicability criteria in § 63.2832, you must comply with either the requirements specified in paragraphs (a) through (d) of this section, or the requirements in paragraph (e) of this section.
units.actor: each facility meeting the applicability criteria in § 63.2832
units.action_summary: Choose and comply with either requirements in (a)-(d) or requirements in (e).

units.obligation_text: You must also comply with the requirements in paragraph (g) of this section.
units.actor: each facility meeting the applicability criteria in § 63.2832
units.action_summary: Also comply with paragraph (g) requirements.

units.obligation_text: You must comply with the work practice standard provided in paragraph (h) of this section, if you choose to operate your source under an initial startup period subject to § 63.2850(c)(2) or (d)(2).
units.action_summary: If operating under an initial startup period, comply with the work practice standard in (h).

units.obligation_text: For each operating month, as defined in § 63.2872, you must calculate a compliance ratio which compares your actual HAP loss to your allowable HAP loss for the previous 12 operating months as shown in Equation 1 of this section.
units.action_summary: Calculate a 12-month compliance ratio each operating month comparing actual vs allowable HAP loss.

units.obligation_text: When your source has processed listed oilseed for 12 operating months, calculate the compliance ratio by the end of each calendar month following an operating month, as defined in § 63.2872, using Equation 2 of this section.
units.action_summary: After 12 operating months, calculate compliance ratio by end of each calendar month following an operating month using Equation 2.

units.obligation_text: If your source shuts down and processes no listed oilseed for an entire calendar or accounting month, then you must categorize the month as a nonoperating month, as defined in § 63.2872.
units.action_summary: If shut down for a month, categorize that month as a nonoperating month.

units.obligation_text: Exclude any nonoperating months from the compliance ratio determination.
units.action_summary: Do not include nonoperating months in the compliance ratio calculation.

units.obligation_text: If your source is subject to an initial startup period as defined in § 63.2872, you may exclude from the compliance ratio determination any solvent and oilseed information recorded for the initial startup period, provided you meet the work practice standard in § 63.2850(c)(2) or (d)(2).
units.action_summary: May exclude initial startup period data from compliance ratio if you meet the specified work practice standard.

units.obligation_text: Before [date 181 days after date of publication of final rule in the Federal Register], if your source is subject to a malfunction period as defined in § 63.2872, exclude from the compliance ratio determination any solvent and oilseed information recorded for the malfunction period.
units.action_summary: Before the listed date, you may exclude data recorded during a malfunction period from the compliance ratio.

units.obligation_text: The provisions of this paragraph (e) do not apply on and after [date 181 days after date of publication of final rule in the Federal Register].
units.action_summary: Paragraph allowing exclusion for malfunction periods ceases to apply on and after the specified date.

units.obligation_text: On or after [date 181 days after date of publication of final rule in the Federal Register], you must operate and maintain any affected source, including associated air pollution control equipment and monitoring equipment, at all times in a manner consistent with safety and good air pollution control practices for minimizing emissions.
units.actor: owner or operator of any affected source
units.action_summary: Operate and maintain source and associated control/monitoring equipment consistent with safety and good practices to minimize emissions.

units.obligation_text: On and after [date 181 days after date of publication of final rule in the Federal Register], you must meet the requirements in paragraphs (h)(1) through (3) of this section if you choose to operate your source under an initial startup period subject to § 63.2850(c)(2) or (d)(2).
units.actor: owner or operator of source operating under an initial startup period
units.action_summary: If operating under an initial startup period on/after the date, meet requirements (h)(1)-(3).

units.obligation_text: You must operate the mineral oil absorption system at all times during the initial startup period unless doing so is not possible due to safety considerations;
units.action_summary: Run the mineral oil absorption system continuously during initial startup unless unsafe.

units.obligation_text: You must operate the solvent condensers at all times during the initial startup period unless doing so is not possible due to safety considerations;
units.action_summary: Operate solvent condensers continuously during initial startup unless unsafe.

units.obligation_text: You must follow site-specific operating limits, established according to the requirements in paragraphs (h)(3)(i) and (ii) of this section, for temperature and pressure for the desolventizing and oil distillation units associated with solvent recovery at all times, unless doing so is not possible due to safety considerations.
units.action_summary: Adhere to site-specific temperature and pressure operating limits for desolventizing and oil distillation units during initial startup, unless safety prevents it.

units.obligation_text: Your site-specific operating limits may be based on equipment design, manufacturer’s recommendations, or other site-specific operating values established for normal operating periods.
units.action_summary: You may base site-specific operating limits on equipment design, manufacturer recommendations, or other site-specific values.

units.obligation_text: The operating limits may be in the form of a minimum, maximum, or operating range.
units.action_summary: Operating limits may be expressed as min, max, or range.

units.obligation_text: Develop a written startup, shutdown and malfunction (SSM) plan in accordance with the provisions in § 63.2852. On and after [date 181 days after date of publication of final rule in the Federal Register], an SSM plan is not required.
units.action_summary: Prepare a written SSM plan per §63.2852 (required before date); after date SSM plan not required.

units.obligation_text: Submit the reports in paragraphs (a)(5)(i) through (iv) of this section, as applicable:
units.action_summary: Submit the listed reports as applicable.

units.obligation_text: Initial startup period reports in accordance with § 63.2861(e).
units.action_summary: Submit initial startup period reports as required in §63.2861(e).

units.obligation_text: You must meet all of the requirements listed in paragraph (a) of this section and Table 1 of this section for sources under normal operation, and the schedules for demonstrating compliance for existing sources under normal operation in Table 2 of this section.
units.action_summary: Existing sources under normal operation must meet paragraph (a), Table 1, and Table 2 schedules.

units.obligation_text: Upon initial startup of your new source, you must meet all of the requirements listed in § 63.2850(a) and Table 1 of this section for sources under normal operation, and the schedules for demonstrating compliance for new sources under normal operation in Table 2 of this section.
units.action_summary: New sources upon initial startup must meet paragraph (a), Table 1, and Table 2 schedules for normal operation.

units.obligation_text: For up to 6 calendar months after the startup date of your new source, you must meet all of the requirements listed in paragraph (a) of this section and Table 1 of this section for sources operating under an initial startup period, and the schedules for demonstrating compliance for new sources operating under an initial startup period in Table 2 of this section.
units.action_summary: For up to 6 months after startup, new sources must meet paragraph (a) and Table 1 requirements for initial startup period and related schedules.

units.obligation_text: On and after [date 181 days after date of publication of final rule in the Federal Register], you must also comply with the work practice standard in § 63.2840(h) for the duration of the initial startup period.
units.action_summary: On/after the specified date, new sources must follow the work practice standard in §63.2840(h) during the initial startup period.

units.obligation_text: At the end of the initial startup period (as defined in § 63.2872), your new source must then meet all of the requirements listed in Table 1 of this section for sources under normal operation.
units.action_summary: After initial startup period ends, new sources must meet Table 1 normal operation requirements.

units.obligation_text: Upon initial startup of your significantly modified existing or new source, you must meet all of the requirements listed in paragraph (a) of this section and Table 1 of this section for sources under normal operation, and the schedules for demonstrating compliance for an existing or new source that has been significantly modified in Table 2 of this section.
units.actor: owner or operator of significantly modified source
units.action_summary: Upon initial startup after significant modification, meet paragraph (a), Table 1, and Table 2 schedules.

units.obligation_text: For up to 3 calendar months after the startup date of your significantly modified existing or new source, you must meet all of the requirements listed in paragraph (a) of this section and Table 1 of this section for sources operating under an initial startup period, and the schedules for demonstrating compliance for a significantly modified existing or new source operating under an initial startup period in Table 2 of this section.
units.actor: owner or operator of significantly modified source
units.action_summary: For up to 3 months after startup of significantly modified source, meet initial startup period requirements and schedules.

units.obligation_text: On and after [date 181 days after date of publication of final rule in the Federal Register], you must also comply with the work practice standard in § 63.2840(h) for the duration of the initial startup period.
units.actor: owner or operator of significantly modified source
units.action_summary: On/after date, significantly modified sources must comply with §63.2840(h) during initial startup.

units.obligation_text: At the end of the initial startup period (as defined in § 63.2872), your new or existing source must meet all of the requirements listed in Table 1 of this section for sources under normal operation.
units.actor: owner or operator of new or modified existing source
units.action_summary: After initial startup ends, the source must meet normal operation Table 1 requirements.

units.obligation_text: Within 15 days of the beginning date of the malfunction, you must choose to comply with one of the options listed in paragraphs (e)(1) and (2) of this section.
units.actor: existing or new source owner or operator experiencing a malfunction
units.action_summary: Within 15 days of a malfunction's start, choose one of the compliance options (e)(1) or (e)(2).

units.obligation_text: Throughout the malfunction period, you must meet all of the requirements listed in paragraph (a) of this section and Table 1 of this section for sources operating during a malfunction period. At the end of the malfunction period, your source must then meet all of the requirements listed in Table 1 of this section for sources under normal operation.
units.actor: owner or operator experiencing a malfunction
units.action_summary: During malfunction, meet paragraph (a) and Table 1 requirements for malfunction; after malfunction, meet normal operation requirements.

units.obligation_text: Operate and maintain your source in accordance with general duty provisions of § 63.6(e) before [date 181 days after date of publication of final rule in the Federal Register].
units.action_summary: Before the specified date, operate and maintain in accordance with §63.6(e).

units.obligation_text: On and after [date 181 days after date of publication of final rule in the Federal Register], you must meet the requirements of § 62.2840(g).
units.action_summary: On/after the date, meet the requirements of § 63.2840(g) (text shows §62.2840(g) but implies §63.2840(g)).

units.obligation_text: Determine and record the extraction solvent loss in gallons from your source as described in § 63.2853.
units.action_summary: Measure and record extraction solvent loss per §63.2853.

units.obligation_text: Record the volume fraction of HAP present at greater than 1 percent by volume and gallons of extraction solvent in shipment received.
units.action_summary: Record HAP volume fraction (>1%) and gallons of extraction solvent in shipments received.

units.obligation_text: Determine and record the tons of each oilseed type processed by your source (for periods of normal operation).
units.action_summary: Measure and record tons of each oilseed type processed during normal operation.

units.obligation_text: Determine the weighted average volume fraction of HAP in extraction solvent received as described in § 63.2854 by the end of the following calendar month (for normal operation).
units.action_summary: Compute weighted average HAP volume fraction in solvent received by the end of the following calendar month during normal operation.

units.obligation_text: Determine and record the actual solvent loss, weighted average volume fraction HAP, oilseed processed and compliance ratio for each 12 operating month period as described in § 63.2840 by the end of the following calendar month.
units.action_summary: Calculate and record solvent loss, weighted average HAP fraction, oilseed processed, and compliance ratio for each 12 operating month period by the next calendar month.

units.obligation_text: Submit a Notification of Compliance Status or Annual Compliance Certification as appropriate as described in §§ 63.2860(d) and 63.2861(a).
units.action_summary: Submit NOCS or annual compliance certification per referenced sections.

units.obligation_text: Submit a Deviation Notification Report by the end of the calendar month following the month in which you determined that the compliance ratio exceeds 1.00 as described in § 63.2861(b) (for normal operation before the specified date).
units.action_summary: If compliance ratio >1.00, submit a deviation report by end of following calendar month (for normal operation pre-date).

units.obligation_text: Submit a Deviation Notification Report as described in § 63.2861(b) on and after [date 181 days after date of publication of final rule in the Federal Register].
units.action_summary: On/after the date, submit deviation notification reports per §63.2861(b).

units.obligation_text: Submit a Periodic SSM Report as described in § 63.2861(c) when applicable (e.g., for initial startup periods before [date] and for malfunction periods).
units.action_summary: When applicable, submit periodic SSM reports per §63.2861(c).

units.obligation_text: Submit an Immediate SSM Report as described in § 63.2861(d) if you handle a SSM differently from the SSM plan or the source does not follow the SSM plan (as applicable).
units.action_summary: If SSM handled differently or SSM plan not followed, submit immediate SSM report per §63.2861(d).

units.obligation_text: Submit an Initial Startup Report as described in § 63.2861(e) on and after [date 181 days after date of publication of final rule in the Federal Register] if applicable.
units.action_summary: On/after the date, submit initial startup report per §63.2861(e) when applicable.

units.obligation_text: You must develop and implement a written plan for demonstrating compliance that provides the detailed procedures you will follow to monitor and record data necessary for demonstrating compliance with this subpart.
units.action_summary: Create and implement a written compliance demonstration plan detailing monitoring and recording procedures.

units.obligation_text: You must also incorporate the plan for demonstrating compliance by reference in the source’s title V permit and keep the plan on-site and readily available as long as the source is operational.
units.action_summary: Incorporate the compliance plan into the Title V permit and keep it on-site and accessible while source operates.

units.obligation_text: If you make any changes to the plan for demonstrating compliance, then you must keep all previous versions of the plan and make them readily available for inspection for at least 5 years after each revision.
units.action_summary: Retain prior versions of the compliance plan and make them available for 5 years after revision.

units.obligation_text: The plan for demonstrating compliance must include the items in paragraphs (a)(1) through (8) of this section.
units.action_summary: Ensure the compliance plan contains the enumerated items (a)(1)-(8).

units.obligation_text: On and after [date 181 days after date of publication of final rule in the Federal Register], if you choose to operate your source under an initial start-up period subject to § 63.2850(c)(2) or (d)(2), the items in paragraphs (c)(8)(i) and (ii) of this section must be included.
units.action_summary: If operating under initial startup on/after date, include the specified items (c)(8)(i)-(ii) in the plan.

units.obligation_text: Your site-specific operating limits, and their basis, for temperature and pressure for the desolventizing and oil distillation units associated with solvent recovery.
units.action_summary: Include site-specific operating limits and their basis for temperature and pressure of desolventizing and distillation units in the plan.

units.obligation_text: A detailed description of all methods of measurement your source will use to measure temperature and pressure, including the measurement frequency.
units.action_summary: Include detailed descriptions of measurement methods and frequencies for temperature and pressure in the plan.

units.obligation_text: Before [date 181 days after date of publication of final rule in the Federal Register], you must develop a written SSM plan in accordance with § 63.6(e)(3). You must complete the SSM plan before the compliance date for your source.
units.action_summary: Develop and complete a written SSM plan per §63.6(e)(3) before the compliance date (required before the date).

units.obligation_text: You must also keep the SSM plan on-site and readily available as long as the source is operational.
units.action_summary: Maintain the SSM plan on-site and accessible while the source operates.

units.obligation_text: The SSM plan must specify a program of corrective action for malfunctioning process and air pollution control equipment and reflect the best practices now in use by the industry to minimize emissions.
units.action_summary: SSM plan must include corrective action program and reflect industry's best practices to minimize emissions.

units.obligation_text: To qualify as a SSM plan, other such plans must meet all the applicable requirements of these NESHAP.
units.actor: owner or operator (submitting other plans as SSM)
units.action_summary: Any other plan used to qualify as an SSM plan must meet all applicable NESHAP requirements.

units.obligation_text: The provisions of this section do not apply on and after [date 181 days after date of publication of final rule in the Federal Register].
units.action_summary: Section's requirements (SSM plan obligations) cease to apply on and after the specified date.

units.obligation_text: You must categorize the operating status of your source for each recorded time interval in accordance with criteria in Table 1 or Table 2 of this section.
units.action_summary: For each recorded interval, categorize operating status per Table 1 or Table 2 criteria.

units.obligation_text: You are required to measure and record the solvent inventory on the beginning and ending dates of each normal operating period that occurs during an operating month.
units.action_summary: Measure and record solvent inventory at beginning and end of each normal operating period during an operating month.

units.obligation_text: You may use a control device to reduce solvent emissions to meet the emission standard.
units.action_summary: You are permitted to use control devices (e.g., incinerators, boilers, flares) to reduce solvent emissions.

units.obligation_text: If you use a control device that reduces solvent emissions through destruction of the solvent instead of recovery, then determine the gallons of solvent that enter the control device and are destroyed there during each normal operating period.
units.actor: owner or operator using a destructive control device
units.action_summary: If using destructive control device, quantify gallons entering and destroyed during each normal operating period.

units.obligation_text: All solvent destroyed in a control device during a normal operating period can be subtracted from the total solvent loss.
units.action_summary: You may subtract solvent destroyed in a control device from total solvent loss.

units.obligation_text: Identify and describe, in your plan for demonstrating compliance, each type of reasonable and sound measurement method that you use to quantify the gallons of solvent entering and exiting the control device and to determine the destruction efficiency of the control device.
units.action_summary: Document measurement methods and destruction efficiency calculations for control devices in the compliance plan.

units.obligation_text: You may use design evaluations to document the gallons of solvent destroyed or removed by the control device instead of performance testing under § 63.7. The design evaluations must be based on the procedures and options described in § 63.985(b)(1)(i)(A) through (C) or § 63.11, as appropriate. All data, assumptions, and procedures used in such evaluations must be documented and available for inspection.
units.action_summary: You may use design evaluations instead of performance testing, but such evaluations must follow specified procedures and be documented and available for inspection.

units.obligation_text: If you use performance testing to determine solvent flow rate to the control device or destruction efficiency of the device, follow the procedures as outlined in § 63.997(e)(1) and (2) and the requirements in paragraph (a)(5)(i)(A) of this section.
units.actor: owner or operator conducting performance testing
units.action_summary: If using performance testing, follow specified procedures and requirements in referenced paragraphs.

units.obligation_text: Instead of periodic performance testing to demonstrate continued good operation of the control device, you may develop a monitoring plan, following the procedures outlined in § 63.988(c) and using operational parametric measurement devices.
units.action_summary: You may substitute a monitoring plan using parametric devices instead of periodic performance testing, following §63.988(c).

units.obligation_text: On or after [date 181 days after date of publication of final rule in the Federal Register], you must conduct all performance tests under such conditions as the Administrator specifies to you based on representative performance of the affected source for the period being tested.
units.actor: owner or operator conducting performance tests
units.action_summary: Conduct performance tests under Administrator-specified representative conditions on/after the specified date.

units.obligation_text: You may not conduct performance tests during periods of malfunction.
units.action_summary: Do not perform performance tests during malfunction periods.
