units.obligation_text: You must record the process information that is necessary to document operating conditions during the test and include in such record an explanation to support that such conditions represent normal operation.
units.action_summary: Record process information and an explanation showing test conditions reflect normal operation.

units.obligation_text: Upon request, you shall make available to the Administrator such records as may be necessary to determine the conditions of performance tests.
units.action_summary: Provide records to the Administrator upon request to determine test conditions.

units.obligation_text: You are required to measure and record the oilseed inventory on the beginning and ending dates of each normal operating period that occurs during an operating month.
units.action_summary: Measure and record oilseed inventory at the start and end of each normal operating period during operating months.

units.obligation_text: You must consistently follow the procedures described in your plan for demonstrating compliance, as specified in § 63.2851, to determine the oilseed inventory on an as received basis and maintain readily available records of the oilseed inventory as described by § 63.2862(c)(3).
units.action_summary: Follow the plan's procedures to determine oilseed inventory and keep records as specified.

units.obligation_text: Submit a deviation report for each compliance determination you make in which the compliance ratio exceeds 1.00 as determined under § 63.2840(c) or if you deviate from the work practice standard for an initial startup period subject to § 63.2850(c)(2) or (d)(2). Submit the deviation report by the end of the month following the calendar month in which you determined the deviation.
units.action_summary: When compliance ratio >1.00 or you deviate from the startup work practice standard, submit a deviation report by the end of the following month.

units.obligation_text: The deviation notification report must include the items in paragraphs (b)(1) through (7) of this section if you exceed the compliance ratio, and must include the items in paragraphs (b)(1), (2), and (5) through (8) of this section if you deviate from the work practice standard.
units.action_summary: Deviation reports must contain specified items depending on whether the deviation is compliance-ratio exceedance or work-practice deviation.

units.obligation_text: Beginning on [date 181 days after date of publication of final rule in the Federal Register], the number of deviations and for each deviation the date, time, and duration of each deviation.
units.action_summary: Include number, date, time, and duration for each deviation in the deviation report (on/after the date).

units.obligation_text: Beginning on [date 181 days after date of publication of final rule in the Federal Register], a statement of the cause of each deviation (including unknown cause, if applicable).
units.action_summary: Provide a cause statement (or 'unknown') for each deviation in the deviation report (on/after the date).

units.obligation_text: Beginning on [date 181 days after date of publication of final rule in the Federal Register], for each deviation, a list of the affected sources or equipment, an estimate of the quantity of HAP emitted over the emission requirements of § 63.2840, and a description of the method used to estimate the emissions.
units.action_summary: For each deviation, list affected sources/equipment, estimate excess HAP emissions, and describe estimation method (on/after date).

units.obligation_text: A description of the deviation from the work practice standard during the initial startup period, including the records of § 63.2862(f) for the deviation.
units.action_summary: Describe any deviation from the startup work practice standard and include §63.2862(f) records.

units.obligation_text: Before [date 181 days after date of publication of final rule in the Federal Register], if you choose to operate your source under an initial startup period subject to § 63.2850(c)(2) or (d)(2) or a malfunction period subject to § 63.2850(e)(2), you must submit a periodic SSM report by the end of the calendar month following each month in which the initial startup period or malfunction period occurred. The periodic SSM report must include the items in paragraphs (c)(1) through (3) of this section.
units.action_summary: Before the date, if operating under initial startup or malfunction, submit periodic SSM reports monthly including specified items.

units.obligation_text: Before [date 181 days after date of publication of final rule in the Federal Register], if you handle a SSM during an initial startup period subject to § 63.2850(c)(2) or (d)(2) or a malfunction period subject to § 63.2850(e)(2) differently from procedures in the SSM plan and the relevant emission requirements in § 63.2840 are exceeded, then you must submit an immediate SSM report.
units.action_summary: Before the date, if you deviate from the SSM plan and emission limits are exceeded, submit an immediate SSM report.

units.obligation_text: Immediate SSM reports consist of a telephone call or facsimile transmission to the responsible agency within 2 working days after starting actions inconsistent with the SSM plan, followed by a letter within 7 working days after the end of the event. The letter must include the items in paragraphs (d)(1) through (3) of this section.
units.action_summary: Provide immediate SSM notification by phone/fax within 2 working days and follow-up letter within 7 working days including specified items.

units.obligation_text: If you choose to operate your source under an initial startup period subject to § 63.2850(c)(2) or (d)(2) on and after [date 181 days after date of publication of final rule in the Federal Register], you must submit an initial startup period report within 30 days after the initial startup period ends.
units.action_summary: On/after the date, if operating under initial startup, submit an initial startup report within 30 days after that period ends.

units.obligation_text: The name and address of the owner or operator (must be included in the initial startup period report).
units.action_summary: Include owner/operator name and address in the initial startup period report.

units.obligation_text: The physical address of the vegetable oil production process (must be included in the initial startup period report).
units.action_summary: Include the physical address of the process in the initial startup report.

units.obligation_text: A compliance certification indicating whether the source was in compliance with the work practice standard of § 63.2840(h) (must be included in the initial startup period report).
units.action_summary: Include a certification stating compliance status with §63.2840(h) in the initial startup report.

units.obligation_text: On and after [date 181 days after date of publication of final rule in the Federal Register], if you conduct performance tests to determine solvent flow rate to a control device or destruction efficiency of a control device according to the requirements of § 63.2853(a)(5)(i), within 60 days after the date of completing each performance test, you must submit the results of the performance test following the procedures specified in paragraphs (f)(1) and (2) of this section.
units.actor: owner or operator conducting performance tests
units.action_summary: On/after date, if conducting specified performance tests, submit test results within 60 days following procedures in (f)(1)-(2).

units.obligation_text: Data collected using test methods supported by EPA’s Electronic Reporting Tool (ERT) ... Submit the results of the performance test to EPA via the Compliance and Emissions Data Reporting Interface (CEDRI) ... The data must be submitted in a file format generated through the use of EPA’s ERT. Alternatively, you may submit an electronic file consistent with the XML schema listed on EPA’s ERT website.
units.actor: owner or operator submitting test data
units.action_summary: Submit ERT-supported test data via CEDRI in ERT-generated format or an XML schema-consistent file.

units.obligation_text: Data collected using test methods that are not supported by EPA’s ERT ... The results of the performance test must be included as an attachment in the ERT or an alternate electronic file consistent with the XML schema listed on EPA’s ERT website. Submit the ERT generated package or alternative file to EPA via CEDRI.
units.actor: owner or operator submitting test data
units.action_summary: For non-ERT-supported test methods, attach results in ERT or alternate XML file and submit via CEDRI.

units.obligation_text: If you claim some of the information submitted under paragraph (f) or (g) of this section is CBI, you must submit a complete file, including information claimed to be CBI, to EPA. The file must be generated through the use of EPA’s ERT or an alternate electronic file consistent with the XML schema listed on EPA’s ERT website. Submit the file on a compact disc, flash drive, or other commonly used electronic storage medium and clearly mark the medium as CBI. Mail the electronic medium to U.S. EPA/OAQPS/CORE CBI Office ... The same file with the CBI omitted must be submitted to EPA via EPA’s CDX as described in paragraph (f)(1) of this section.
units.action_summary: If claiming CBI, submit a complete electronic CBI file to EPA by physical media marked CBI and also submit the redacted file via CDX per instructions.

units.obligation_text: On and after [date 181 days after date of publication of final rule in the Federal Register], you must submit the initial notification required in § 63.2860(b) and the annual compliance certification, deviation report, and initial startup report required in § 63.2861(a), (b), and (e) to the EPA via CEDRI, which can be accessed through the EPA’s CDX. The owner or operator must upload to CEDRI an electronic copy of each applicable notification in portable document format (PDF). The applicable notification must be submitted by the deadline specified in this subpart, regardless of the method in which the reports are submitted. You must use the appropriate electronic report template on the CEDRI website.
units.action_summary: On/after date, submit specified notifications and reports via CEDRI/CDX using required templates and upload a PDF of each notification by the applicable deadlines.

units.obligation_text: If you claim some of the information required to be submitted via CEDRI is confidential business information (CBI), submit a complete report, including information claimed to be CBI, to EPA. The report must be generated using the appropriate form on the CEDRI website. Submit the file on a compact disc, flash drive, or other commonly used electronic storage medium and clearly mark the medium as CBI. Mail the electronic medium to U.S. EPA/OAQPS/CORE CBI Office ... The same file with the CBI omitted must be submitted to EPA via EPA’s CDX.
units.action_summary: If asserting CBI, submit a complete CBI file on physical media to the EPA CBI office and submit the redacted file via CDX.

units.obligation_text: If you are required to electronically submit a report through CEDRI in EPA’s CDX, you may assert a claim of EPA system outage for failure to timely comply with the reporting requirement. To assert a claim of EPA system outage, you must meet the requirements outlined in paragraphs (h)(1) through (7) of this section.
units.actor: owner or operator required to submit electronically
units.action_summary: You may claim EPA system outage as excuse for late electronic submission, but to do so you must meet the listed requirements in (h)(1)-(7).

units.obligation_text: You must have been or will be precluded from accessing CEDRI and submitting a required report within the time prescribed due to an outage of either EPA’s CEDRI or CDX systems.
units.actor: owner or operator seeking to assert an EPA system outage claim
units.action_summary: To assert an outage claim you must have been or be prevented from accessing CEDRI/CDX during the submission period due to an EPA outage.

units.obligation_text: The outage must have occurred within the period of time beginning five business days prior to the date that the submission is due.
units.actor: owner or operator seeking to assert an EPA system outage claim
units.action_summary: The EPA outage must have taken place within the specified five-business-day window before the submission due date for the claim to apply.

units.obligation_text: You must submit notification to the Administrator in writing as soon as possible following the date you first knew, or through due diligence should have known, of the outage (truncated in source).
units.actor: owner or operator asserting EPA system outage
units.action_summary: If asserting EPA outage, notify the Administrator in writing as soon as possible after learning of the outage.

title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Surface Coating of Automobiles and Light-Duty Trucks; Surface Coating of Miscellaneous Metal Parts and Products; Surface Coating of Plastic Parts and Products; Surface Coating of Large Appliances; Printing, Coating, and Dyeing of Fabrics and Other Textiles; and Surface Coating of Metal Furniture Residual Risk and Technology Reviews

units.obligation_text: 0.10 percent by weight of any organic HAP in Table 5 of this subpart.
units.actor: owner or operator (you) of the electrodeposition primer system
units.action_summary: Limit organic HAP in the electrodeposition primer system to 0.10 percent by weight (per Table 5).

units.obligation_text: Except as provided in paragraph (d) of this section, for any controlled coating operation(s), you must meet the operating limits specified in Table 1 to this subpart.
units.action_summary: Comply with the operating limits in Table 1 for any controlled coating operations, subject to paragraph (d).

units.obligation_text: These operating limits apply to the emission capture and add-on control systems on the coating operation(s) for which you use this option.
units.action_summary: Operating limits are applicable to emission capture and add-on control systems for the covered coating operations.

units.obligation_text: You must establish the operating limits during performance tests according to the requirements in § 63.3167.
units.action_summary: Set the operating limits through performance testing per §63.3167.

units.obligation_text: You must meet the operating limits at all times after you establish them.
units.action_summary: Maintain compliance with established operating limits continuously after establishment.

units.obligation_text: Before [date 181 days after date of publication of final rule in the Federal Register], the coating operations must be in compliance with the operating limits for emission capture systems and add-on control devices required by § 63.3093 at all times except during periods of startup, shutdown, and malfunction. On and after [date 181 days after date of publication of final rule in the Federal Register], the coating operations must be in compliance with the operating limits for emission capture systems and add-on control devices required by § 63.3093 at all times.
units.action_summary: Ensure coating operations comply with §63.3093 operating limits; before the specified date compliance may exclude startup/shutdown/malfunction, and on/after the date compliance is required at all times.

units.obligation_text: Before [date ...], the coating operations must be in compliance ... at all times except during periods of startup, shutdown, and malfunction.
units.action_summary: Prior to the specified date, maintain compliance with operating limits except during startup, shutdown, and malfunction periods.

units.obligation_text: On and after [date ...], the coating operations must be in compliance with the operating limits for emission capture systems and add-on control devices required by § 63.3093 at all times.
units.action_summary: After the specified date, coating operations must continuously meet the operating limits with no startup/shutdown/malfunction exception.

units.obligation_text: Before [date ...], you must always operate and maintain your affected source including all air pollution control and monitoring equipment you use for purposes of complying with this subpart according to the provisions in § 63.6(e)(1)(i). On and after [date ...], at all times, the owner or operator must operate and maintain any affected source, including associated air pollution control equipment and monitoring equipment, in a manner consistent with safety and good air pollution control practices for minimizing emissions.
units.action_summary: Operate and maintain affected sources and control/monitoring equipment per §63.6(e)(1)(i) before the date; thereafter operate and maintain in a manner consistent with safety and good air pollution control practices to minimize emissions.

units.obligation_text: Before [date ...], you must always operate and maintain your affected source ... according to the provisions in § 63.6(e)(1)(i).
units.action_summary: Prior to the specified date, operate and maintain affected source and equipment in accordance with §63.6(e)(1)(i).

units.obligation_text: On and after [date ...], at all times, the owner or operator must operate and maintain any affected source ... in a manner consistent with safety and good air pollution control practices for minimizing emissions.
units.action_summary: After the date, operate and maintain affected source consistent with safety and good air pollution control practices to minimize emissions.

units.obligation_text: The general duty to minimize emissions does not require the owner or operator to make any further efforts to reduce emissions if levels required by the applicable standard have been achieved.
units.action_summary: Once applicable standard emission levels are achieved, the owner/operator is not required to make further emission reductions under the general duty to minimize emissions.

units.obligation_text: Before [date ...], if your affected source uses emission capture systems and add-on control devices, you must develop a written startup, shutdown, and malfunction plan (SSMP) according to the provisions in § 63.6(e)(3). On and after [date ...], the SSMP is not required.
units.action_summary: Prior to the date, develop a written SSMP per §63.6(e)(3) if using capture systems/add-on devices; after the date the SSMP requirement is discontinued.

units.obligation_text: You must develop a written startup, shutdown, and malfunction plan (SSMP) according to the provisions in § 63.6(e)(3).
units.action_summary: Create a written SSMP following §63.6(e)(3) requirements.

units.obligation_text: The SSMP must address startup, shutdown, and corrective actions in the event of a malfunction of the emission capture system or the add-on control devices.
units.action_summary: SSMP must include procedures for startup, shutdown, and corrective actions for malfunctions of capture/control equipment.

units.obligation_text: On and after [date ...], the SSMP is not required.
units.action_summary: After the specified date, facilities are no longer required to maintain an SSMP for this subpart.

units.obligation_text: If there were no deviations from the emission limits, operating limits, or work practices ... the semiannual compliance report must include a statement that there were no deviations from the applicable emission limitations during the reporting period.
units.action_summary: Include a statement in the semiannual compliance report indicating there were no deviations during the reporting period if none occurred.

units.obligation_text: If you used control devices to comply with the emission limits, and there were no periods during which the CPMS were out of control as specified in § 63.8(c)(7), the semiannual compliance report must include a statement that there were no periods during which the CPMS were out of control during the reporting period.
units.action_summary: If control devices were used and CPMS were never out-of-control, include a statement to that effect in the semiannual report.

units.obligation_text: Before [date ...], if there was a deviation from the applicable emission limits in § 63.3090(c) and (d) or § 63.3091(c) and (d), the semiannual compliance report must contain the information in paragraphs (a)(5)(i) through (iv) of this section. On and after [date ...], if there was a deviation ... the semiannual compliance report must contain the information in paragraphs (a)(5)(i) through (v) of this section.
units.action_summary: When deviations from specified adhesive/sealer/deadener emission limits occur, include enumerated information in the semiannual report; after the date, an additional data element (v) is required.

units.obligation_text: The reason for the deviation (including unknown cause, if applicable).
units.action_summary: Report the reason or cause (or unknown) for each deviation.

units.obligation_text: On and after [date ...], the number of deviations and, for each deviation, a list of the affected source or equipment, an estimate of the quantity of each regulated pollutant emitted over the applicable emission limit ... and a description of the method used to estimate the emissions.
units.action_summary: After the date, for each deviation provide count, affected equipment, estimated excess emissions, and estimation method.

units.obligation_text: Before [date ...], if there was a deviation from the applicable emission limits in § 63.3090(a) or (b) or § 63.3091(a) or (b) or the applicable operating limit(s) in Table 1 to this subpart, the semiannual compliance report must contain the information in paragraphs (a)(6)(i) through (xiv) of this section. On and after [date ...], ... the semiannual compliance report must contain the information in paragraphs (a)(6)(i) through (xv) of this section.
units.action_summary: When deviations from combined coating emission limits or Table 1 operating limits occur, include the specified information in the semiannual compliance report; after the date an additional item (xv) is required.

units.obligation_text: The date and time that each malfunction of the capture system or add-on control devices used to control emissions from these operations started and stopped.
units.action_summary: Report start and stop date/time for each malfunction of capture or add-on control devices.

units.obligation_text: Before [date ...], the date and time that each CPMS was inoperative, except for zero (low-level) and high-level checks. On and after [date ...], for each instance that the CPMS was inoperative, except for zero (low-level) and high-level checks, the date, time, and duration that the CPMS was inoperative; the cause (including unknown cause) for the CPMS being inoperative; and descriptions of corrective actions taken.
units.action_summary: Record and report CPMS inoperative events: before the date report date/time (except checks); after the date report date/time/duration, cause, and corrective actions.

units.obligation_text: Before [date ...], the date, time, and time period that each CPMS was out of control, including the information in § 63.8(c)(8). On and after [date ...], for each instance that the CPMS was out of control, as specified in § 63.8(c)(7), the date, time, and duration that the CPMS was out-of-control; the cause (including unknown cause) for the CPMS being out-of-control; and descriptions of corrective actions taken.
units.action_summary: Report CPMS out-of-control events: before the date report date/time period and §63.8(c)(8) info; after the date report date/time/duration, cause, and corrective actions.

units.obligation_text: Before [date ...], The date and time period of each deviation from an operating limit in Table 1 to this subpart; date and time period of each bypass of an add-on control device; and whether each deviation occurred during a period of startup, shutdown, or malfunction or during another period. On and after [date ...], the date, time, and duration of each deviation from an operating limit in Table 1 to this subpart; and the date, time, and duration of each bypass of an add-on control device.
units.action_summary: Report each deviation from Table 1 operating limits and each bypass of add-on control devices, including timing and whether it occurred during startup/shutdown/malfunction (before date) and include durations (after date).

units.obligation_text: Before [date ...], a breakdown of the total duration of the deviations from each operating limit in Table 1 to this subpart and bypasses of each add-on control device during the semiannual reporting period into those that were due to startup, shutdown, control equipment problems, process problems, other known causes, and other unknown causes. On and after [date ...], a breakdown of the total duration ... into those that were due to control equipment problems, process problems, other known causes, and other unknown causes.
units.action_summary: Provide a categorized breakdown of total duration of deviations and bypasses by cause categories; categories differ before and after the date.

units.obligation_text: Before [date ...], for each deviation from the work practice standards a description of the deviation, the date and time period of the deviation, and the actions you took to correct the deviation. On and after [date ...], for deviations from the work practice standards, the number of deviations, and, for each deviation, the information in paragraphs (a)(6)(xiii)(A) and (B) of this section.
units.action_summary: Report deviations from work practice standards, including descriptive, timing, and corrective information; after the date, include counts and specified details for each deviation.

units.obligation_text: A description of the deviation, the date, time, and duration of the deviation; and the actions you took to minimize emissions in accordance with § 63.3100(d).
units.action_summary: Describe each deviation with date/time/duration and actions taken to minimize emissions per §63.3100(d).

units.obligation_text: A list of the affected sources or equipment for which a deviation occurred, the cause of the deviation (including unknown cause, if applicable), and any corrective actions taken to return the affected unit to its normal or usual manner of operation.
units.action_summary: List affected sources/equipment, causes (including unknown), and corrective actions taken to return units to normal operation for each deviation.

units.obligation_text: Before [date ...], a statement of the cause of each deviation. On and after [date ...], for deviations from an emission limitation ... or operating limit in Table 1 of this subpart, a statement of the cause of each deviation (including unknown cause, if applicable).
units.action_summary: Provide a statement of the cause for each deviation (including unknown cause after the date) related to emission limitations or operating limits.

units.obligation_text: On and after [date ...], for each deviation from an emission limitation in § 63.3090(a) or (b), or § 63.3091(a) or (b), or operating limit in Table 1 to this subpart, a list of the affected sources or equipment for which a deviation occurred, an estimate of the quantity of each regulated pollutant emitted over any emission limit ... and a description of the method used to estimate the emissions.
units.action_summary: After the date, for each deviation provide affected equipment list, estimated excess emissions, and estimation method.

units.obligation_text: Before [date ...], if you used the separate electrodeposition primer organic HAP content limits in § 63.3092(a), and there was a deviation from these limits, the semiannual compliance report must contain the information in paragraphs (a)(7)(i) through (iii) of this section. On and after [date ...], ... the semiannual compliance report must contain the information in paragraphs (a)(7)(i) through (iv) of this section.
units.action_summary: When deviating from electrodeposition primer organic HAP content limits, include specified information in the semiannual compliance report; after the date an additional item (iv) is required.

units.obligation_text: Identification of each material used that deviated from the emission limit, and the date, time, and duration each was used.
units.action_summary: Identify materials that exceeded emission limits and report when and how long each was used.

units.obligation_text: A statement of the cause of each deviation (including unknown case, if applicable).
units.action_summary: Provide the cause for each deviation, including 'unknown' if applicable.

units.obligation_text: On and after [date ...], the number of deviations, a list of the affected source or equipment, an estimate of the quantity of each regulated pollutant emitted over any emission limit in § 63.3092(a), and a description of the method used to estimate the emissions.
units.action_summary: After the date, report the count of deviations, affected equipment, estimated excess emissions, and the method used to estimate emissions for each deviation.

units.obligation_text: Before [date ...], if you used the separate electrodeposition primer bake oven capture and control limitations in § 63.3092(b), and there was a deviation from the limitations in § 63.3092(b) or the applicable operating limit in Table 1 to this subpart, the semiannual compliance report must contain the information in paragraphs (a)(8)(i) through (xii) of this section. On and after [date ...], ... the semiannual compliance report must contain the information in paragraphs (a)(8)(i) through (xiv) of this section.
units.action_summary: When deviating from electrodeposition primer bake oven capture/control limitations or applicable operating limits, include specified information in the semiannual report; additional items required after the date.

units.obligation_text: The date and time that each malfunction of the capture systems or control devices used to control emissions from the electrodeposition primer bake oven started and stopped.
units.action_summary: Report start and stop date/time for malfunctions of capture systems or control devices for electrodeposition primer bake ovens.

units.obligation_text: Before [date ...], the date and time that each CPMS was inoperative, except for zero (low-level) and high-level checks. On and after [date ...], for each instance that the CPMS was inoperative, except for zero (low-level) and high-level checks, the date, time, and duration that the CPMS was inoperative; the cause (including unknown cause) for the CPMS being inoperative; and descriptions of corrective actions taken.
units.action_summary: Report CPMS inoperative events for electrodeposition primer bake oven controls: timing (before date) and timing/duration/cause/corrective actions (after date).

units.obligation_text: Before [date ...], the date, time, and duration that each CPMS was out of control, including the information in § 63.8(c)(8). On and after [date ...], for each instance that the CPMS was out of control, as specified in § 63.8(c)(7), the date, time, and duration that the CPMS was out-of-control; the cause (including unknown cause) for the CPMS being out-of-control; and descriptions of corrective actions taken.
units.action_summary: Report CPMS out-of-control events for electrodeposition primer bake ovens including timing and required supplemental info and, after the date, cause and corrective actions.

units.obligation_text: Before [date ...], the date and time period of each deviation from an operating limit in Table 1 ... date and time period of each bypass of an add-on control device; and whether each deviation occurred during a period of startup, shutdown, or malfunction or during another period. On and after [date ...], the date, time, and duration of each deviation ... and the date, time, and duration of each bypass of an add-on control device.
units.action_summary: Report deviations from Table 1 operating limits and bypasses of add-on controls for electrodeposition primer bake ovens, including timing and context (startup/shutdown/malfunction) before the date and durations after the date.

units.obligation_text: Before [date ...], a breakdown of the total duration of the deviations from each operating limit in Table 1 to this subpart and bypasses of each add-on control device during the semiannual reporting period into those that were due to startup, shutdown, control equipment problems, process problems, other known causes, and other unknown causes. On and after [date ...], a breakdown ... into those that were due to control equipment problems, process problems, other known causes, and other unknown causes.
units.action_summary: Provide categorized breakdown of total duration of deviations and bypasses by cause for electrodeposition primer bake oven operations; categories change after the date.

units.obligation_text: A statement of the cause of each deviation (including unknown cause, if applicable).
units.action_summary: State the cause for each deviation, including 'unknown' if applicable, for electrodeposition primer bake oven deviations.

units.obligation_text: Before [date ...], if there was a deviation from an applicable work practice plan developed in accordance with § 63.3094(b) or (c), the semiannual compliance report must contain the information in paragraphs (a)(9)(i) through (iii) of this section. On and after [date ...], if there were deviations from an applicable work practice plan developed in accordance with § 63.3094(b) or (c), the semiannual compliance report must contain the number of deviations, and, for each deviation, the information in paragraphs (a)(9)(i) through (iii) of this section.
units.action_summary: For deviations from work practice plans, include specified time/nature/cause/affected equipment info in semiannual report; after the date include counts and details for each deviation.

units.obligation_text: Before [date ...], the time period during which each deviation occurred. On and after [date ...], the date, time, and duration of the deviation.
units.action_summary: Report timing of each work practice plan deviation; format differs before and after the date.

units.obligation_text: Before [date ...], the nature of each deviation. On and after [date ...], the nature of the deviation, including a list of the affected sources or equipment for which the deviation occurred, and the cause of the deviation (including unknown cause, if applicable).
units.action_summary: Describe the nature of each deviation; after the date include affected equipment list and cause (including unknown).

units.obligation_text: Before [date ...], if you used add-on control devices and you had a startup, shutdown, or malfunction during the semiannual reporting period, you must submit the reports specified in paragraph (c)(1) and (2) of this section. On and after [date ...], the reports specified in paragraph (c)(1) and (2) of this section are not required.
units.action_summary: Prior to the date, submit specified startup/shutdown/malfunction reports if you used add-on control devices and had such events; after the date those reports are not required.

units.obligation_text: On and after [date ...], you must submit the results of the performance test required in paragraph (b) of this section following the procedure specified in paragraphs (d)(1) through (3) of this section.
units.action_summary: After the date, submit performance test results as specified in paragraphs (d)(1)-(3).

units.obligation_text: For data collected using test methods supported by the EPA’s Electronic Reporting Tool (ERT) ... you must submit the results of the performance test to the EPA via the Compliance and Emissions Data Reporting Interface (CEDRI). Performance test data must be submitted in a file format generated through the use of the EPA’s ERT or an alternate electronic file format consistent with the XML schema listed on the EPA’s ERT website.
units.action_summary: If test methods are supported by EPA ERT, submit performance test results to EPA via CEDRI in ERT-generated or XML-schema-consistent electronic file format.

units.obligation_text: For data collected using test methods that are not supported by the EPA’s ERT ... you must submit the results of the performance test to the Administrator at the appropriate address listed in § 63.13, unless the Administrator agrees to or specifies an alternate reporting method.
units.action_summary: If test methods are not supported by EPA ERT, submit performance test results to the Administrator at the address in §63.13 unless an alternate method is specified/allowed.

units.obligation_text: If you claim that some of the performance test information being submitted under paragraph (c)(1) of this section is confidential business information (CBI), you must submit a complete file ... including information claimed to be CBI, on a compact disc, flash drive, or other commonly used electronic storage medium to the EPA ... The same ERT or alternate file with the CBI omitted must be submitted to the EPA via the EPA’s CDX.
units.action_summary: If claiming CBI, submit a complete electronic file including CBI on a physical medium to EPA CBI Office and also submit the file with CBI omitted via CDX/CEDRI.

units.obligation_text: On and after [date ...], the owner or operator shall submit the initial notifications required in § 63.9(b) and the notification of compliance status required in § 63.9(h) and § 63.3110(c) to the EPA via the CEDRI. The owner or operator must upload to CEDRI an electronic copy of each applicable notification in portable document format (PDF). The applicable notification must be submitted by the deadline specified in this subpart, regardless of the method in which the reports are submitted.
units.action_summary: After the date, submit initial notifications and notification of compliance status via CEDRI and upload each notification as a PDF by the specified deadlines.

units.obligation_text: Owners or operators who claim that some of the information required to be submitted via CEDRI is CBI shall submit a complete report ... including information claimed to be CBI, on a compact disc, flash drive, or other commonly used electronic storage medium to the EPA ... The same file with the CBI omitted shall be submitted to the EPA via the EPA’s CDX.
units.action_summary: If claiming CBI for notifications, send a complete electronic file including CBI on physical media to the EPA CBI Office and submit a CBI-omitted file via CDX.

units.obligation_text: On and after [date ...], or once the reporting template has been available on the CEDRI website for 1 year, whichever date is later, the owner or operator shall submit the semiannual compliance report required in paragraph (a) of this section to the EPA via the CEDRI.
units.action_summary: After the date (or once template has been in CEDRI for 1 year), submit the semiannual compliance report via CEDRI.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator must use the appropriate electronic template on the CEDRI Web for this subpart or an alternate electronic file format consistent with the XML schema listed on the CEDRI website.
units.action_summary: Use the CEDRI web template for the subpart or an XML-schema-consistent alternate file format when submitting reports.

units.obligation_text: If the reporting form for the semiannual compliance report specific to this subpart is not available in CEDRI at the time that the report is due, you must submit the report to the Administrator at the appropriate addresses listed in § 63.13.
units.action_summary: If CEDRI form isn't available when due, submit the semiannual report to the Administrator at the addresses in §63.13.

units.obligation_text: Once the form has been available in CEDRI for 1 year, you must begin submitting all subsequent reports via CEDRI.
units.action_summary: After the CEDRI form has been available for one year, all subsequent semiannual reports must be submitted via CEDRI.

units.obligation_text: The reports must be submitted by the deadlines specified in this subpart, regardless of the method in which the reports are submitted.
units.action_summary: Submit reports by the regulatory deadlines irrespective of submission method.

units.obligation_text: Owners or operators who claim that some of the information required to be submitted via CEDRI is CBI shall submit a complete report ... including information claimed to be CBI, on a compact disc, flash drive, or other commonly used electronic storage medium to the EPA ... The same file with the CBI omitted shall be submitted to the EPA via the EPA’s CDX.
units.action_summary: If claiming CBI for semiannual reports, provide a complete file including CBI on physical media to EPA and submit a CBI-omitted file via CDX.

units.obligation_text: If you are required to electronically submit a report through the CEDRI in the EPA’s CDX, and due to a planned or actual outage ... you may assert a claim of EPA system outage for failure to timely comply with the reporting requirement. You must submit notification to the Administrator in writing as soon as possible ... You must provide ... a written description identifying the date, time and length of the outage; a rationale ...; describe the measures taken or to be taken to minimize the delay in reporting; and identify a date by which you propose to report, or if you have already met the reporting requirement ... the date you reported. In any circumstance, the report must be submitted electronically as soon as possible after the outage is resolved. The decision to accept the claim of EPA system outage and allow an extension to the reporting deadline is solely within the discretion of the Administrator.
units.action_summary: If EPA CEDRI/CDX outage prevents timely electronic submission, you may claim an EPA system outage but must notify Administrator with details and submit the report as soon as possible after the outage; acceptance is at Administrator's discretion.

units.obligation_text: You may assert a claim of EPA system outage for failure to timely comply with the reporting requirement.
units.action_summary: Permit to assert an EPA system outage claim to explain late reporting due to EPA system outage.

units.obligation_text: You must submit notification to the Administrator in writing as soon as possible following the date you first knew, or through due diligence should have known, that the event may cause or caused a delay in reporting.
units.action_summary: If asserting an EPA system outage claim, promptly notify the Administrator in writing when you first knew (or should have known) of the outage causing reporting delay.

units.obligation_text: You must provide to the Administrator a written description identifying the date, time and length of the outage; a rationale for attributing the delay ...; describe the measures taken or to be taken to minimize the delay in reporting; and identify a date by which you propose to report, or if you have already met the reporting requirement ... the date you reported.
units.action_summary: Include detailed outage description, rationale attributing delay, mitigation measures, and proposed reporting date (or actual date reported) in the notification to Administrator.

units.obligation_text: In any circumstance, the report must be submitted electronically as soon as possible after the outage is resolved.
units.action_summary: Submit the required report electronically as soon as feasible after the EPA system outage ends.

units.obligation_text: If you are required to electronically submit a report through CEDRI in the EPA’s CDX and a force majeure event ... the owner or operator may assert a claim of force majeure for failure to timely comply with the reporting requirement. If you intend to assert a claim of force majeure, you must submit notification to the Administrator in writing as soon as possible ... You must provide ... a written description of the force majeure event and a rationale ...; describe the measures taken or to be taken to minimize the delay in reporting; and identify a date by which you propose to report, or if you have already met the reporting requirement ... the date you reported. In any circumstance, the reporting must occur as soon as possible after the force majeure event occurs. The decision to accept the claim of force majeure and allow an extension to the reporting deadline is solely within the discretion of the Administrator.
units.action_summary: If a force majeure prevents timely electronic submission, you may claim force majeure but must promptly notify Administrator with details and mitigation; report as soon as possible after the event; acceptance is at Administrator's discretion.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator may assert a claim of force majeure for failure to timely comply with the reporting requirement.
units.action_summary: Allows assertion of a force majeure claim to justify delayed reporting due to events beyond control.

units.obligation_text: If you intend to assert a claim of force majeure, you must submit notification to the Administrator in writing as soon as possible following the date you first knew ...
units.action_summary: Promptly notify Administrator in writing if you intend to claim force majeure.

units.obligation_text: You must provide to the Administrator a written description of the force majeure event and a rationale for attributing the delay ...; describe the measures taken or to be taken to minimize the delay in reporting; and identify a date by which you propose to report, or if you have already met the reporting requirement ... the date you reported.
units.action_summary: Provide detailed description of the force majeure, rationale for delay, mitigation measures, and proposed reporting date (or actual reporting date) to Administrator.

units.obligation_text: In any circumstance, the reporting must occur as soon as possible after the force majeure event occurs.
units.action_summary: Even if claiming force majeure, submit the required report as soon as possible after the event.

units.obligation_text: Before [date ...], a record of the date, time, and duration of each deviation, and for each deviation, a record of whether the deviation occurred during a period of startup, shutdown, or malfunction. On and after [date ...], for each deviation from an emission limitation, operating limit, or work practice plan reported under § 63.3120(a)(5) through (9), a record of the information specified in paragraphs (g)(1) through (4) of this section, as applicable.
units.action_summary: Keep records of deviations with timing and startup/shutdown/malfunction info before the date; after the date retain specified detailed records for each reported deviation.

units.obligation_text: The date, time, and duration of the deviation, and for each deviation, the information as reported under § 63.3120(a)(5) through (9).
units.action_summary: Maintain records of deviation timing and the information reported under §63.3120(a)(5)-(9).

units.obligation_text: A list of the affected sources or equipment for which the deviation occurred and the cause of the deviation, as reported under § 63.3120(a)(5) through (9).
units.action_summary: Keep records listing affected sources/equipment and causes for each deviation matching report information.

units.obligation_text: An estimate of the quantity of each regulated pollutant emitted over any applicable emission limit ... and a description of the method used to calculate the estimate, as reported under § 63.3120(a)(5) through (9).
units.action_summary: Maintain records estimating excess emissions and describing the estimation method for each deviation.

units.obligation_text: A record of actions taken to minimize emissions in accordance with § 63.3100(d) and any corrective actions taken to return the affected unit to its normal or usual manner of operation.
units.action_summary: Keep records of emissions-minimization actions per §63.3100(d) and any corrective actions taken to restore normal operation.

units.obligation_text: Before [date ...], the records required by § 63.6(e)(3)(iii) through (v) related to startup, shutdown, and malfunction. On and after [date ...], the provisions of this paragraph no longer apply.
units.action_summary: Prior to the date, maintain records required by §63.6(e)(3)(iii)-(v) for startup/shutdown/malfunction; after the date this paragraph no longer applies.

units.obligation_text: On and after [date ...], any records required to be maintained by this subpart that are submitted electronically via the EPA’s CEDRI may be maintained in electronic format. This ability to maintain electronic copies does not affect the requirement for facilities to make records, data, and reports available upon request to a delegated air agency or the EPA as part of an on-site compliance evaluation.
units.action_summary: After the date, records submitted via CEDRI may be kept electronically; however, facilities must still make records available on request for on-site compliance evaluations.

units.obligation_text: Facilities must make records, data, and reports available upon request to a delegated air agency or the EPA as part of an on-site compliance evaluation.
units.action_summary: Ensure records, data, and reports are accessible to delegated agencies or EPA during on-site evaluations, even if maintained electronically.

units.obligation_text: Your records must be in a form suitable and readily available for expeditious review according to § 63.10(b)(1).
units.action_summary: Maintain records in a form that is suitable and readily available for prompt review under §63.10(b)(1).

units.obligation_text: Where appropriate, the records may be maintained as electronic spreadsheets or as a database.
units.action_summary: Records may be kept as electronic spreadsheets or databases where appropriate.

units.obligation_text: On and after [date ...], any records required to be maintained by this subpart that are submitted electronically via the EPA’s CEDRI may be maintained in electronic format.
units.action_summary: After the date, records submitted via CEDRI can be kept electronically.

units.obligation_text: This ability to maintain electronic copies does not affect the requirement for facilities to make records, data, and reports available upon request to a delegated air agency or the EPA as part of an on-site compliance evaluation.
units.action_summary: Even if records are electronic, facilities must provide them upon request for on-site compliance checks.

units.obligation_text: Count each organic HAP in Table 5 to this subpart that is present at 0.1 percent by mass or more and at 1.0 percent by mass or more for other compounds. Express the mass fraction of each organic HAP you count as a value truncated to four places after the decimal point (e.g., 0.3791).
units.action_summary: Identify and count organic HAPs meeting specified thresholds and report each mass fraction truncated to four decimal places.

units.obligation_text: For coatings, you may use EPA Method 24 to determine the mass fraction of nonaqueous volatile matter and use that value as a substitute for mass fraction of organic HAP. As an alternative to using EPA Method 24, you may use ASTM D2369–10 (2015)e (incorporated by reference, see § 63.14).
units.action_summary: Permit to use EPA Method 24 or ASTM D2369–10 as alternatives to determine mass fraction of nonaqueous volatile matter to substitute for organic HAP mass fraction for coatings.

units.obligation_text: You may rely on information other than that generated by the test methods specified in paragraphs (a)(1) through (3) of this section, such as manufacturer’s formulation data, if it represents each organic HAP in Table 5 to this subpart that is present at 0.1 percent by mass or more and at 1.0 percent by mass or more for other compounds. If there is a disagreement between such information and results of a test conducted according to paragraphs (a)(1) through (3) of this section, then the test method results will take precedence, unless after consultation, the facility demonstrates to the satisfaction of the enforcement authority that the facility’s data are correct.
units.action_summary: You may rely on supplier/manufacturer formulation data (subject to thresholds); if supplier data conflicts with test results, test results prevail unless facility convinces enforcement authority otherwise.

units.obligation_text: Determine the density of each material used. Determine the density of each material used during the compliance period from test results using ASTM D1475–13 (incorporated by reference, see § 63.14).
units.action_summary: Determine each material's density during the compliance period using test results from ASTM D1475–13.

title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Iron and Steel Foundries Residual Risk and Technology Review

units.obligation_text: You must always operate and maintain your iron and steel foundry, including air pollution control and monitoring equipment, in a manner consistent with good air pollution control practices for minimizing emissions at least to the levels required by this subpart.
units.actor: You (owner/operator of the iron and steel foundry)
units.action_summary: Operate and maintain the foundry and its control/monitoring equipment according to good air pollution control practices to minimize emissions to required levels.

units.obligation_text: You must be in compliance with the emission limitations, work practice standards, and operation and maintenance requirements in this subpart at all times.
units.action_summary: Remain in compliance with all emission limits, work practice standards, and O&M requirements at all times.

units.obligation_text: You must conduct each performance test that applies to your iron and steel foundry based on your selected compliance alternative, if applicable, according to the requirements in paragraphs (b) through (i) of this section.
units.action_summary: Conduct all applicable performance tests per the specified procedures and chosen compliance alternative.

units.obligation_text: Each performance test must be conducted under conditions representative of normal operations.
units.action_summary: Run performance tests under normal operating conditions.

units.obligation_text: Normal operating conditions exclude periods of startup and shutdown.
units.action_summary: Do not consider startup/shutdown as normal operating conditions for tests.

units.obligation_text: You may not conduct performance tests during periods of malfunction.
units.action_summary: Prohibits conducting performance tests during malfunctions.

units.obligation_text: You must record the process information that is necessary to document operating conditions during the test and include in such record an explanation to support that such conditions represent normal operation.
units.action_summary: Record process information and explanation showing test conditions were normal.

units.obligation_text: Upon request, you shall make available to the Administrator such records as may be necessary to determine the conditions of performance tests.
units.action_summary: Provide records to Administrator upon request to verify test conditions.

units.obligation_text: Determine the VOHAP concentration for each test run according to the test methods in 40 CFR part 60, appendix A, that are specified in paragraphs (e)(1)(i) through (v) of this section.
units.action_summary: Measure VOHAP concentration for each test run using specified test methods.

units.obligation_text: If there were no periods during which a continuous monitoring system (including a CPMS or CEMS) was inoperable or out-of-control as specified by § 63.8(c)(7), a statement that there were no periods during which the CPMS was inoperable or out-of-control during the reporting period.
units.action_summary: Include a statement in the report declaring no CPMS inoperable/out-of-control periods if none occurred.

units.obligation_text: For each affected source or equipment for which there was a deviation from an emissions limitation ... during the reporting period, the compliance report must contain the information specified in paragraphs (b)(7)(i) through (iii) of this section.
units.action_summary: Include specified information in compliance report for each deviation from emissions limits.

units.obligation_text: A list of the affected source or equipment and the total operating time of each emissions source during the reporting period.
units.action_summary: List affected sources/equipment and their operating time in the report.

units.obligation_text: The date, start time, duration (in hours), and cause of each deviation (characterized as either startup, shutdown, control equipment problem, process problem, other known cause, or unknown cause, as applicable) and the corrective action taken;
units.action_summary: Report date/time, duration, cause, and corrective action for each deviation.

units.obligation_text: An estimate of the quantity of each regulated pollutant emitted over any emission limit and a description of the method used to estimate the emissions.
units.action_summary: Provide estimated pollutant quantities above limits and describe estimation method.

units.obligation_text: A summary of the total duration (in hours) of the deviations that occurred during the reporting period by cause ... and the cumulative duration of deviations during the reporting period across all causes both in hours and as a percent of the total source operating time during the reporting period.
units.action_summary: Provide a summary by cause and cumulative duration (hours and percent) of deviations.

units.obligation_text: For each continuous monitoring system (including a CPMS or CEMS) used to comply ... that was inoperable or out-of-control during any portion of the reporting period, you must include the information specified in paragraphs (b)(8)(i) through (vi) of this section.
units.action_summary: Include specified information for each CMS that was inoperable or out-of-control.

units.obligation_text: A brief description of the continuous monitoring system, including manufacturer and model number.
units.action_summary: Provide brief CMS description and manufacturer/model number.

units.obligation_text: The date of the latest continuous monitoring system certification or audit.
units.action_summary: Report date of most recent CMS certification/audit.

units.obligation_text: A brief description and the total operating time of the affected source or equipment that is monitored by the continuous monitoring system during the reporting period.
units.action_summary: Describe monitored source/equipment and report its operating time.

units.obligation_text: A description of any changes in continuous monitoring systems, processes, or controls since the last reporting period.
units.action_summary: Describe any changes to monitoring systems, processes, or controls since last report.

units.obligation_text: For each period for which the continuous monitoring system was inoperable or out-of-control during the reporting period, report: (A) The date, start time, and duration (in hours) of the deviation;
units.action_summary: Report date, start time, and duration for each CMS deviation.

units.obligation_text: (B) The type of deviation (inoperable or out-of-control);
units.action_summary: Report type of deviation (inoperable or out-of-control).

units.obligation_text: (C) The cause of deviation (characterized as monitoring system malfunctions, non-monitoring equipment malfunctions, quality assurance/quality control calibrations, other known causes, and unknown causes, as applicable) and the corrective action taken.
units.action_summary: Report cause of deviation (characterized) and corrective action taken.

units.obligation_text: A summary of the total duration (in hours) of the deviations that occurred during the reporting period by cause ... and the cumulative duration of deviations during the reporting period across all causes both in hours and as a percent of the total source operating time during the reporting period.
units.action_summary: Provide summary of total and cumulative deviation durations by cause in hours and percent.

units.obligation_text: Prior to [DATE 6 MONTHS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF THE FINAL RULE IN THE Federal Register], you must submit semiannual compliance reports to the Administrator as specified in § 63.13.
units.action_summary: Submit semiannual compliance reports to the Administrator before the specified date.

units.obligation_text: Beginning on [DATE 6 MONTHS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF THE FINAL RULE IN THE Federal Register], you must submit all subsequent semiannual compliance reports to the EPA via the Compliance and Emissions Data Reporting Interface (CEDRI) ... You must use the appropriate electronic report template on the CEDRI website for this subpart.
units.action_summary: Submit all subsequent semiannual reports via CEDRI using the appropriate electronic template.

units.obligation_text: The report must be submitted by the deadline specified in this subpart, regardless of the method in which the report is submitted.
units.action_summary: Submit reports by the regulatory deadline regardless of submission method.

units.obligation_text: If you claim some of the information required to be submitted via CEDRI is confidential business information (CBI), submit a complete report, including information claimed to be CBI, to the EPA.
units.action_summary: If claiming CBI, submit a complete report including CBI to the EPA.

units.obligation_text: The report must be generated using the appropriate form on the CEDRI website or an alternate electronic file consistent with the extensible markup language (XML) schema listed on the CEDRI website.
units.action_summary: Generate the report using the CEDRI form or an XML-consistent electronic file.

units.obligation_text: Submit the file on a compact disc, flash drive, or other commonly used electronic storage medium and clearly mark the medium as CBI. Mail the electronic medium to U.S. EPA/OAQPS/CORE CBI Office, Attention: Group Leader, Measurement Policy Group, MD C404–02, 4930 Old Page Rd., Durham, NC 27703.
units.action_summary: Submit the full CBI-containing file on physical electronic media, clearly marked as CBI, and mail to the EPA CBI Office at the specified address.

units.obligation_text: The same file with the CBI omitted must be submitted to the EPA via the EPA’s CDX as described earlier in this paragraph.
units.action_summary: Submit the non-CBI version of the file electronically via EPA's CDX.

units.obligation_text: Within 60 days after the date of completing each performance test required by this subpart, you must submit the results of the performance test following the procedures specified in paragraphs (f)(1) through (3) of this section.
units.action_summary: Submit performance test results within 60 days according to specified procedures.

units.obligation_text: Data collected using test methods supported by the EPA’s Electronic Reporting Tool (ERT) ... Submit the results of the performance test to the EPA via the CEDRI ... The data must be submitted in a file format generated through the use of the EPA’s ERT. Alternatively, you may submit an electronic file consistent with the XML schema listed on the EPA’s ERT website.
units.action_summary: Submit ERT-supported test data to EPA via CEDRI in ERT-generated format or as an XML-consistent electronic file.

units.obligation_text: Data collected using test methods that are not supported by the EPA’s ERT ... The results of the performance test must be included as an attachment in the ERT or an alternate electronic file consistent with the XML schema listed on the EPA’s ERT website. Submit the ERT generated package or alternative file to the EPA via CEDRI.
units.action_summary: For non-ERT-supported methods, include results as ERT attachment or XML-consistent file and submit to EPA via CEDRI.

units.obligation_text: Confidential business information (CBI). If you claim some of the information submitted under paragraph (e)(1) of this section is CBI, you must submit a complete file, including information claimed to be CBI, to the EPA. The file must be generated through the use of the EPA’s ERT or an alternate electronic file consistent with the XML schema listed on the EPA’s ERT website. Submit the file on a compact disc, flash drive, or other commonly used electronic storage medium and clearly mark the medium as CBI. Mail the electronic medium to U.S. EPA/ OAQPS/CORE CBI Office ... The same file with the CBI omitted must be submitted to the EPA via the EPA’s CDX as described in paragraph (f)(1) of this section.
units.action_summary: For CBI, submit complete ERT/XML file to EPA on physical media marked CBI and also submit a CBI-omitted version via CDX.

units.obligation_text: Within 60 days after the date of completing each continuous monitoring system (CMS) performance evaluation (as defined in § 63.2), you must submit the results of the performance evaluation following the procedures specified in paragraphs (g)(1) through (3) of this section.
units.action_summary: Submit CMS performance evaluation results within 60 days according to specified procedures.

units.obligation_text: Performance evaluations of CMS measuring RATA pollutants that are supported by the EPA’s ERT ... Submit the results of the performance evaluation to the EPA via CEDRI ... The data must be submitted in a file format generated through the use of the EPA’s ERT. Alternatively, you may submit an electronic file consistent with the XML schema listed on the EPA’s ERT website.
units.action_summary: Submit RATA-supported CMS evaluation results via CEDRI in ERT format or XML-consistent file.

units.obligation_text: Performance evaluations of CMS measuring RATA pollutants that are not supported by the EPA’s ERT ... The results of the performance evaluation must be included as an attachment in the ERT or an alternate electronic file consistent with the XML schema listed on the EPA’s ERT website. Submit the ERT generated package or alternative file to the EPA via CEDRI.
units.action_summary: For non-ERT-supported CMS evaluations, include results as ERT attachment or XML file and submit via CEDRI.

units.obligation_text: Confidential business information (CBI). If you claim some of the information submitted under paragraph (f)(1) of this section is CBI, you must submit a complete file, including information claimed to be CBI, to the EPA. The file must be generated through the use of the EPA’s ERT or an alternate electronic file consistent with the XML schema listed on the EPA’s ERT website. Submit the file on a compact disc, flash drive, or other commonly used electronic storage medium and clearly mark the medium as CBI. Mail the electronic medium to U.S. EPA/ OAQPS/CORE CBI Office ... The same file with the CBI omitted must be submitted to the EPA via the EPA’s CDX as described in paragraph (g)(1) of this section.
units.action_summary: For CBI in CMS evaluations, submit complete ERT/XML file on physical media marked CBI and submit a non-CBI file via CDX.

units.obligation_text: If you are required to electronically submit a report through CEDRI in the EPA’s CDX, you may assert a claim of EPA system outage for failure to timely comply with the reporting requirement. To assert a claim of EPA system outage, you must meet the requirements outlined in paragraphs (h)(1) through (7) of this section.
units.action_summary: You may assert an EPA system outage claim but must meet the listed requirements to do so.

units.obligation_text: You must have been or will be precluded from accessing CEDRI and submitting a required report within the time prescribed due to an outage of either the EPA’s CEDRI or CDX systems.
units.action_summary: To claim outage, you must have been or will be prevented from accessing CEDRI/CDX during the submission period.

units.obligation_text: The outage must have occurred within the period of time beginning five business days prior to the date that the submission is due.
units.action_summary: The outage must have happened within five business days before the submission due date to qualify.

units.obligation_text: The outage may be planned or unplanned.
units.action_summary: Outages eligible for claim can be either planned or unplanned.

units.obligation_text: You must submit notification to the Administrator in writing as soon as possible following the date you first knew, or through due diligence should have known, that the event may cause or has caused a delay in reporting.
units.action_summary: Promptly notify the Administrator in writing upon learning the event may delay reporting.

units.obligation_text: You must provide to the Administrator a written description identifying: (i) The date(s) and time(s) when CDX or CEDRI was accessed and the system was unavailable; (ii) A rationale for attributing the delay in reporting beyond the regulatory deadline to EPA system outage; (iii) Measures taken or to be taken to minimize the delay in reporting; and (iv) The date by which you propose to report, or if you have already met the reporting requirement at the time of the notification, the date you reported.
units.action_summary: Provide a written description to the Administrator including specified information about the outage and reporting plan.

units.obligation_text: Provide the date(s) and time(s) when CDX or CEDRI was accessed and the system was unavailable.
units.action_summary: Report specific dates/times of attempted access and unavailability.

units.obligation_text: Provide a rationale for attributing the delay in reporting beyond the regulatory deadline to EPA system outage.
units.action_summary: Explain why the outage caused the delay past the deadline.

units.obligation_text: Provide measures taken or to be taken to minimize the delay in reporting.
units.action_summary: Describe steps taken or planned to reduce reporting delay.

units.obligation_text: Provide the date by which you propose to report, or if you have already met the reporting requirement at the time of the notification, the date you reported.
units.action_summary: State the proposed reporting date or the date already reported.

units.obligation_text: In any circumstance, the report must be submitted electronically as soon as possible after the outage is resolved.
units.action_summary: Submit the report electronically as soon as possible after the outage ends.

units.obligation_text: If you are required to electronically submit a report through CEDRI in the EPA’s CDX, you may assert a claim of force majeure for failure to timely comply with the reporting requirement. To assert a claim of force majeure, you must meet the requirements outlined in paragraphs (i)(1) through (5) of this section.
units.action_summary: You may claim force majeure but must meet the listed requirements to do so.

units.obligation_text: You may submit a claim if a force majeure event is about to occur, occurs, or has occurred or there are lingering effects from such an event within the period of time beginning five business days prior to the date the submission is due.
units.action_summary: Permission to submit a force majeure claim under the specified timing conditions.

units.obligation_text: You must submit notification to the Administrator in writing as soon as possible following the date you first knew, or through due diligence should have known, that the event may cause or has caused a delay in reporting.
units.action_summary: Promptly notify the Administrator in writing upon learning the force majeure event may delay reporting.

units.obligation_text: You must provide to the Administrator: (i) A written description of the force majeure event; (ii) A rationale for attributing the delay in reporting beyond the regulatory deadline to the force majeure event; (iii) Measures taken or to be taken to minimize the delay in reporting; and (iv) The date by which you propose to report, or if you have already met the reporting requirement at the time of the notification, the date you reported.
units.action_summary: Provide specified documentation and explanations to support a force majeure claim, including proposed reporting date.

units.obligation_text: A written description of the force majeure event.
units.action_summary: Provide a written description of the event causing the delay.

units.obligation_text: A rationale for attributing the delay in reporting beyond the regulatory deadline to the force majeure event.
units.action_summary: Explain why the force majeure caused the reporting delay.

units.obligation_text: Measures taken or to be taken to minimize the delay in reporting.
units.action_summary: Describe steps taken or planned to minimize reporting delay from the force majeure event.

units.obligation_text: The date by which you propose to report, or if you have already met the reporting requirement at the time of the notification, the date you reported.
units.action_summary: Provide proposed reporting date or the date already reported for the force majeure claim.

units.obligation_text: In any circumstance, the reporting must occur as soon as possible after the force majeure event occurs.
units.action_summary: Report as soon as practicable after the force majeure event.

units.obligation_text: Records of required maintenance performed on the air pollution control and monitoring equipment as required by § 63.10(b)(2)(iii).
units.action_summary: Keep records of required maintenance on air pollution control and monitoring equipment.
units.modal_raw: must (implied by section title 'What records must I keep?')

units.obligation_text: Records of the site-specific performance evaluation test plan required under § 63.8(d)(2) for the life of the affected source or until the affected source is no longer subject to the provisions of this part, to be made available for inspection, upon request, by the Administrator.
units.action_summary: Keep the site-specific performance evaluation test plan records for the life of the source and make them available for inspection upon request.

units.obligation_text: If the performance evaluation plan is revised, you shall keep previous (i.e., superseded) versions of the performance evaluation plan on record to be made available for inspection, upon request, by the Administrator, for a period of 5 years after each revision to the plan.
units.action_summary: Retain superseded versions of the performance evaluation plan for 5 years after each revision and make them available on request.

units.obligation_text: Records of the date and time that each deviation started and stopped.
units.action_summary: Keep records of start and stop date/time for each deviation.

units.obligation_text: You must keep the following records for each failure to meet an emissions limitation (including operating limit), work practice standard, or operation and maintenance requirement in this subpart.
units.action_summary: Maintain specified records for each failure to meet emissions/work practice/O&M requirements.

units.obligation_text: Date, start time and duration of each failure.
units.action_summary: Record date, start time, and duration for each failure to meet requirements.

units.obligation_text: List of the affected sources or equipment for each failure, an estimate of the quantity of each regulated pollutant emitted over any emission limit and a description of the method used to estimate the emissions.
units.action_summary: Record affected sources/equipment, estimated pollutant quantities over limits, and estimation method for each failure.

units.obligation_text: Actions taken to minimize emissions in accordance with § 63.7710(a), and any corrective actions taken to return the affected unit to its normal or usual manner of operation.
units.action_summary: Record actions taken to minimize emissions and corrective actions to restore normal operation for each failure.

units.obligation_text: Any records required to be maintained by this part that are submitted electronically via the EPA’s CEDRI may be maintained in electronic format. This ability to maintain electronic copies does not affect the requirement for facilities to make records, data, and reports available upon request to a delegated air agency or the EPA as part of an on-site compliance evaluation.
units.action_summary: You may keep records submitted via CEDRI in electronic format, but must still make records available upon request for inspections.

units.obligation_text: Restricted metallic scrap. You must prepare and operate at all times according to written material specifications for the purchase and use of only metal ingots, pig iron, slitter, or other materials that do not include post-consumer automotive body scrap, post-consumer engine blocks, post-consumer oil filters, oily turnings, lead components, chlorinated plastics, or free liquids.
units.actor: You (owner/operator of affected source / small foundry subject to this subpart)
units.action_summary: Only purchase/use specified clean feedstock per written material specifications; exclude listed contaminated scrap and free liquids.

units.obligation_text: The requirements for no free liquids do not apply if the owner or operator can demonstrate that the free liquid is water that resulted from scrap exposure to rain.
units.action_summary: Exception: free liquids rule doesn't apply if the free liquid is water from rain as demonstrated by the owner/operator.

units.obligation_text: Any post-consumer engine blocks, post-consumer oil filters, or oily turnings that are processed and/or cleaned to the extent practicable such that the materials do not include lead components, mercury switches, chlorinated plastics, or free organic liquids can be included in this certification.
units.action_summary: Materials processed/cleaned as practicable and free of listed contaminants may be included in certification.

units.obligation_text: You must submit a notification of compliance status according to § 63.9(h)(2)(i). You must send the notification of compliance status before the close of business on the 30th day after the applicable compliance date specified in § 63.10881. The notification must include the following compliance certifications, as applicable:
units.action_summary: Submit a notification of compliance status by the 30th day after the compliance date including required certifications.

units.obligation_text: As required by § 63.10(b)(1), you must maintain files of all information (including all reports and notifications) for at least 5 years following the date of each occurrence, measurement, maintenance, corrective action, report, or record. At a minimum, the most recent 2 years of data shall be retained on site. The remaining 3 years of data may be retained off site. Such files may be maintained on microfilm, on a computer, on computer floppy disks, on magnetic tape disks, or on microfiche. Any records required to be maintained by this part that are submitted electronically via the EPA’s CEDRI may be maintained in electronic format. This ability to maintain electronic copies does not affect the requirement for facilities to make records, data, and reports available upon request to a delegated air agency or the EPA as part of an on-site compliance evaluation.
