units.action_summary: Retain records for 5 years, keep most recent 2 years on site, other 3 may be off site; materials can be kept in specified formats; electronic retention via CEDRI allowed but records must be available on request.

units.obligation_text: If you are subject to the requirements for a site-specific plan for mercury switch removal under § 63.10885(b)(1), you must maintain records of the number of mercury switches removed or the weight of mercury recovered from the switches and properly managed, the estimated number of vehicles processed, and an estimate of the percent of mercury switches recovered.
units.action_summary: Keep records of mercury switches removed or mercury recovered, vehicles processed, and estimated recovery percent.

units.obligation_text: You must submit semiannual compliance reports to the Administrator according to the requirements in § 63.10899(c), (f), and (g), except that § 63.10899(c)(5) and (7) do not apply.
units.action_summary: Submit semiannual compliance reports to the Administrator per specified requirements with noted exceptions.

units.obligation_text: At all times, you must operate and maintain any affected source, including associated air pollution control equipment and monitoring equipment, in a manner consistent with safety and good air pollution control practices for minimizing emissions.
units.action_summary: Continuously operate and maintain affected sources and control/monitoring equipment in a safe manner consistent with good air pollution control practices to minimize emissions.

units.obligation_text: You must comply with the following requirements of the General Provisions (40 CFR part 63, subpart A): §§ 63.1 through 63.5; § 63.6(a), (b), and (c); § 63.9; § 63.10(a), (b)(1), (b)(2)(xiv), (b)(3), (d)(1), (d)(4), and (f); and §§ 63.13 through 63.16.
units.actor: You (owner/operator of a new or existing affected source classified as a small foundry)
units.action_summary: Comply with the listed General Provisions sections; unlisted General Provisions do not apply to small foundries.

units.obligation_text: At all times, you must operate and maintain any affected source, including associated air pollution control equipment and monitoring equipment, in a manner consistent with safety and good air pollution control practices for minimizing emissions.
units.action_summary: Continuously operate and maintain affected sources and control/monitoring equipment in a safe manner consistent with good air pollution control practices to minimize emissions.

units.obligation_text: In the event that a bag leak detection system alarm is triggered, you must initiate corrective action to determine the cause of the alarm within 1 hour of the alarm, initiate corrective action to correct the cause of the problem within 24 hours of the alarm, and complete corrective action as soon as practicable, but no later than 10 calendar days from the date of the alarm. You must record the date and time of each valid alarm, the time you initiated corrective action, the corrective action taken, and the date on which corrective action was completed.
units.action_summary: On bag leak alarm, take corrective actions within specified timeframes and record alarm and corrective action details.

units.obligation_text: Initiate corrective action to determine the cause of the alarm within 1 hour of the alarm.
units.action_summary: Begin actions to determine cause within 1 hour of bag leak alarm.

units.obligation_text: Initiate corrective action to correct the cause of the problem within 24 hours of the alarm.
units.action_summary: Start corrective action to fix the cause within 24 hours of alarm.

units.obligation_text: Complete corrective action as soon as practicable, but no later than 10 calendar days from the date of the alarm.
units.action_summary: Finish corrective actions within 10 calendar days of the alarm at the latest.

units.obligation_text: You must record the date and time of each valid alarm, the time you initiated corrective action, the corrective action taken, and the date on which corrective action was completed.
units.action_summary: Keep records of alarm timestamps, times corrective action was initiated, actions taken, and completion dates.

units.obligation_text: In the event of an exceedance of an established emissions limitation (including an operating limit), you must restore operation of the emissions source (including the control device and associated capture system) to its normal or usual manner of operation as expeditiously as practicable in accordance with good air pollution control practices for minimizing emissions. The response shall include taking any necessary corrective actions to restore normal operation and prevent the likely recurrence of the exceedance. You must record the date and time corrective action was initiated, the corrective action taken, and the date corrective action was completed.
units.action_summary: On emissions exceedance, promptly restore normal operation, take corrective actions to prevent recurrence, and record corrective actions and timing.

units.obligation_text: You must conduct each performance test under conditions representative of normal operations according to the requirements in Table 1 to this subpart and paragraphs (d) through (g) of this section. Normal operating conditions exclude periods of startup and shutdown. You may not conduct performance tests during periods of malfunction. You must record the process information that is necessary to document operating conditions during the test and include in such record an explanation to support that such conditions represent normal operation. Upon request, you shall make available to the Administrator such records as may be necessary to determine the conditions of performance tests.
units.action_summary: Conduct performance tests under normal conditions (excluding startup/shutdown), not during malfunctions; record process info and make records available upon request.

units.obligation_text: As required by § 63.10(b)(1), you must maintain files of all information (including all reports and notifications) for at least 5 years following the date of each occurrence, measurement, maintenance, corrective action, report, or record. At a minimum, the most recent 2 years of data shall be retained on site. The remaining 3 years of data may be retained off site. Such files may be maintained on microfilm, on a computer, on computer floppy disks or flash drives, on magnetic tape disks, or on microfiche. Any records required to be maintained by this part that are submitted electronically via the EPA’s CEDRI may be maintained in electronic format. This ability to maintain electronic copies does not affect the requirement for facilities to make records, data, and reports available upon request to a delegated air agency or the EPA as part of an on-site compliance evaluation.
units.action_summary: Maintain records for 5 years, keep recent 2 years on site; electronic maintenance via CEDRI allowed but records must be available on request.

units.obligation_text: If you are subject to the requirements for a site-specific plan for mercury under § 63.10885(b)(1), you must maintain records of the number of mercury switches removed or the weight of mercury recovered from the switches and properly managed, the estimated number of vehicles processed, and an estimate of the percent of mercury switches recovered.
units.actor: You (owner/operator subject to site-specific mercury plan)
units.action_summary: Keep records of mercury switches removed or mercury recovered, vehicles processed, and estimated recovery percentage.

units.obligation_text: You must keep records of the site-specific performance evaluation test plan required under § 63.8(d)(2) for the life of the affected source or until the affected source is no longer subject to the provisions of this part, to be made available for inspection, upon request, by the Administrator. If the performance evaluation plan is revised, you shall keep previous (i.e., superseded) versions of the performance evaluation plan on record to be made available for inspection, upon request, by the Administrator, for a period of 5 years after each revision to the plan.
units.action_summary: Retain the site-specific performance evaluation plan for life of source and keep prior versions for 5 years after each revision; make available on request.

units.obligation_text: You must keep the following records for each failure to meet an emissions limitation (including operating limit), work practice standard, or operation and maintenance requirement in this subpart.
units.action_summary: Maintain records for each failure to meet emissions, work practice, or O&M requirements (specifics follow in subparagraphs).

units.obligation_text: Date, start time, and duration of each failure;
units.action_summary: Record date, start time, and duration for each failure.

units.obligation_text: List of the affected sources or equipment for each failure, a
units.action_summary: Record list of affected sources/equipment for each failure (text truncated in source).

units.obligation_text: Before [DATE 181 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], you must be in compliance with the applicable emission limitations specified in Tables 1 through 4 to this subpart at all times, except during periods of startup, shutdown, and malfunction if you are using a control device to comply with an emission limit.
units.actor: you (owner or operator of the affected source)
units.action_summary: Be in compliance at all times with emission limits in Tables 1–4 (prior to specified date).

units.obligation_text: except during periods of startup, shutdown, and malfunction if you are using a control device to comply with an emission limit.
units.actor: you (owner or operator of the affected source)
units.action_summary: Exempts compliance requirement during SSM periods if using a control device.

units.obligation_text: After [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], you must be in compliance with the applicable emission limitations specified in Tables 1 through 4 to this subpart at all times
units.actor: you (owner or operator of the affected source)
units.action_summary: Be in compliance at all times with emission limits in Tables 1–4 (after specified date).

units.obligation_text: Before [DATE 181 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], except as provided in § 63.5982(b)(4), you must always operate and maintain your affected source, including air pollution control and monitoring equipment, according to the provisions in § 63.6(e)(1)(i).
units.actor: you (owner or operator of the affected source)
units.action_summary: Operate and maintain the affected source and associated control/monitoring equipment per §63.6(e)(1)(i) (prior to specified date).

units.obligation_text: After [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], at all times, you must operate and maintain any affected source, including associated air pollution control equipment and monitoring equipment, in a manner consistent with safety and good air pollution control practices for minimizing emissions.
units.actor: you (owner or operator of the affected source)
units.action_summary: Continuously operate and maintain affected source and control/monitoring equipment using safety and good practices to minimize emissions (after specified date).

units.obligation_text: The general duty to minimize emissions does not require you to make any further efforts to reduce emissions if levels required by the applicable standard have been achieved.
units.actor: you (owner or operator of the affected source)
units.action_summary: No obligation to make further emission reductions beyond applicable standard levels.

units.obligation_text: Before [DATE 181 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], for each affected source that complies with the emission limits in Tables 1 through 3 to this subpart using a control device, you must develop a written startup, shutdown, and malfunction plan according to the provisions in § 63.6(e)(3).
units.actor: you (owner or operator of the affected source)
units.action_summary: Develop a written startup, shutdown, and malfunction plan (SSMP) for affected sources using a control device (prior to specified date).

units.obligation_text: After [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], a startup, shutdown, and malfunction plan is not required.
units.actor: you (owner or operator of the affected source)
units.action_summary: SSMP is no longer required after the specified date.

units.obligation_text: Before [DATE 181 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], in your site-specific monitoring plan, you must also address the ongoing procedures specified in paragraphs (f)(1) through (3) of this section as follows.
units.actor: you (owner or operator of the affected source)
units.action_summary: Address the specified ongoing monitoring procedures in the site-specific monitoring plan (prior to specified date).

units.obligation_text: After [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], in your site-specific monitoring plan, you must also address the ongoing procedures specified in paragraphs (f)(1) through (4) of this section as follows.
units.actor: you (owner or operator of the affected source)
units.action_summary: Address the specified ongoing monitoring procedures including (f)(4) in the site-specific monitoring plan (after specified date).

units.obligation_text: Before [DATE 181 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], ongoing data quality assurance procedures in accordance with the general requirements of § 63.8(d).
units.actor: you (owner or operator of the affected source)
units.action_summary: Include ongoing data quality assurance procedures conforming to §63.8(d) in the monitoring plan (prior to specified date).

units.obligation_text: After [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], ongoing data quality assurance procedures in accordance with the general requirements of § 63.8(d)(1) and (2).
units.actor: you (owner or operator of the affected source)
units.action_summary: Include ongoing data quality assurance procedures conforming to §63.8(d)(1) and (2) in the monitoring plan (after specified date).

units.obligation_text: Before [DATE 181 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], ongoing recordkeeping and reporting procedures in accordance with the general requirements of § 63.10(c), (e)(1), and (e)(2)(i).
units.actor: you (owner or operator of the affected source)
units.action_summary: Include ongoing recordkeeping and reporting procedures per §63.10(c),(e)(1),(e)(2)(i) in the monitoring plan (prior to specified date).

units.obligation_text: After [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], the owner or operator shall keep these written procedures on record for the life of the affected source or until the affected source is no longer subject to the provisions of this part, to be made available for inspection, upon request, by the Administrator.
units.action_summary: Keep written monitoring/recordkeeping procedures on record for the life of the source or until no longer subject, and make them available for Administrator inspection (after specified date).

units.obligation_text: If the performance evaluation plan is revised, the owner or operator shall keep previous (i.e., superseded) versions of the performance evaluation plan on record to be made available for inspection, upon request, by the Administrator, for a period of 5 years after each revision to the plan.
units.action_summary: Retain superseded versions of the performance evaluation plan for 5 years after each revision and make them available to the Administrator on request.

units.obligation_text: The program of corrective action should be included in the plan required under § 63.8(d)(2);
units.action_summary: Recommend inclusion of a program of corrective action in the plan under §63.8(d)(2).

units.obligation_text: After [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], Ongoing recordkeeping and reporting procedures in accordance with the general requirements of § 63.10(c), (e)(1), and (e)(2)(i).
units.action_summary: Include ongoing recordkeeping and reporting procedures per §63.10(c),(e)(1),(e)(2)(i) in the monitoring plan (after specified date).

units.obligation_text: After [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], performance tests shall be conducted under such conditions as the Administrator specifies to the owner or operator based on representative performance of the affected source for the period being tested.
units.action_summary: Conduct performance tests under conditions specified by the Administrator that represent normal performance (after specified date).

units.obligation_text: Before [DATE 181 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], you may not conduct performance tests during periods of startup, shutdown, or malfunction, as specified in § 63.7(e)(1).
units.action_summary: Prohibits conducting performance tests during startup, shutdown, or malfunction periods (prior to specified date).

units.obligation_text: Representative conditions exclude periods of startup and shutdown unless specified by the Administrator or an applicable subpart.
units.action_summary: Representative test conditions should exclude startup and shutdown periods unless Administrator or subpart specifies otherwise.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator may not conduct performance tests during periods of malfunction.
units.action_summary: Prohibits conducting performance tests during malfunctions.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator must record the process information that is necessary to document operating conditions during the test and include in such record an explanation to support that such conditions represent normal operation.
units.action_summary: Record process information and explanation to document that test conditions represent normal operation.

units.obligation_text: Upon request, the owner or operator shall make available to the Administrator such records as may be necessary to determine the conditions of performance tests.
units.action_summary: Provide records necessary to determine performance test conditions to the Administrator upon request.

units.obligation_text: Before [DATE 181 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], You must conduct three separate test runs for each performance test required in this section, as specified in § 63.7(e)(1) unless otherwise specified in the test method. Each test run must last at least 1 hour.
units.action_summary: Conduct three separate test runs for each performance test, each lasting at least 1 hour (prior to specified date).

units.obligation_text: After [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], you must conduct three separate test runs for each performance test required in this section, as specified in § 63.5993(c) above, unless otherwise specified in the test method. Each test run must last at least 1 hour.
units.action_summary: Conduct three separate test runs for each performance test, each lasting at least 1 hour, as specified by §63.5993(c) (after specified date).

units.obligation_text: For any other control device, or for other capture systems, ensure that the CPMS is operated according to a monitoring plan submitted to the Administrator with the Notification of Compliance Status report required by § 63.9(h).
units.action_summary: Operate CPMS per a monitoring plan that is submitted to the Administrator with the Notification of Compliance Status.

units.obligation_text: The monitoring plan must meet the requirements in paragraphs (a) and (d)(1) through (3) of this section.
units.action_summary: Ensure the monitoring plan complies with specified requirements in the section.

units.obligation_text: Conduct monitoring in accordance with the plan submitted to the Administrator unless comments received from the Administrator require an alternate monitoring scheme.
units.action_summary: Perform monitoring per the submitted plan unless Administrator requires an alternate scheme.

units.obligation_text: Before [DATE 181 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], for each initial compliance demonstration required in tables 6 through 8 to this subpart that includes a performance test conducted according to the requirements in table 5 to this subpart, you must submit the Notification of Compliance Status, including the performance test results, before the close of business on the 60th calendar day following the completion of the performance test according to § 63.10(d)(2).
units.action_summary: Submit Notification of Compliance Status and performance test results within 60 days after test completion (prior to specified date).

units.obligation_text: After [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], For each initial compliance demonstration required in tables 6 through 8 to this subpart that includes a performance test conducted according to the requirements in table 5 to this subpart, you must submit the Notification of Compliance Status, including the performance test results, before the close of business on the 60th calendar day following the completion of the performance test according to § 63.10(d)(2) and § 63.6010(h)(1) through (3).
units.action_summary: Submit Notification of Compliance Status and performance test results within 60 days after test completion, complying with additional submission procedures (after specified date).

units.obligation_text: You must submit to the Administrator notification reports of the following recorded information. Beginning on [DATE 181 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER] or once the reporting form has been available on the CEDRI website for 1 year, whichever date is later, you must submit all subsequent notification of compliance status reports required in § 63.9(h) and § 63.6009(d) through (i) to the EPA via the Compliance and Emissions Data Reporting Interface (CEDRI).
units.action_summary: Submit Notification of Compliance Status reports to EPA via CEDRI beginning on the specified date or after the CEDRI form has been available for one year.

units.obligation_text: You must use the appropriate electronic report form (i.e., template) on the CEDRI website (https://www.epa.gov/electronic-reporting-air-emissions/compliance-and-emissions-data-reporting-interface-cedri) for this subpart.
units.action_summary: Use the designated electronic report template on the CEDRI website for submissions.

units.obligation_text: If the reporting form for the notification of compliance status report specific to this subpart is not available in CEDRI at the time that the report is due, you must submit the report to the Administrator at the appropriate addresses listed in § 63.13.
units.action_summary: If CEDRI form is unavailable when due, submit the report to the Administrator at addresses in §63.13.

units.obligation_text: Once the form has been available in CEDRI for 1 year, you must begin submitting all subsequent notification of compliance status reports via CEDRI.
units.action_summary: Begin electronic submissions via CEDRI after the form has been available for one year.

units.obligation_text: The applicable notification must be submitted by the deadline specified in this subpart, regardless of the method in which the report is submitted.
units.action_summary: Submit notifications by the specified deadlines regardless of submission method.

units.obligation_text: If you claim that some of the information required to be submitted via CEDRI is confidential business information (CBI), submit a complete report, including information claimed to be CBI, to the EPA. The report must be generated using the appropriate electronic reporting form found on the CEDRI website. Submit the file on a compact disc, flash drive, or other commonly used electronic storage medium and clearly mark the medium as CBI. Mail the electronic medium to U.S. EPA/OAQPS/CORE CBI Office, Attention: Group Leader, Measurement Policy Group, MD C404–02, 4930 Old Page Rd., Durham, NC 27703. The same file with the CBI omitted shall be submitted to the EPA via the EPA’s CDX as described earlier in this paragraph.
units.action_summary: If claiming CBI, submit complete CBI-containing file to EPA's CBI office on physical medium and submit a redacted file via CDX.

units.obligation_text: Where applicable, you may assert a claim of EPA system outage, in accordance with § 63.6010(i), or force majeure, in accordance with § 63.6010(j), for failure to timely comply with this requirement.
units.action_summary: You may claim EPA system outage or force majeure as reasons for late compliance with reporting requirements, following specified procedures.

units.obligation_text: Before [DATE 181 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], the first semiannual compliance report must be postmarked or delivered no later than July 31 or January 31, whichever date follows the end of the first calendar half after the compliance date that is specified for your affected source in § 63.5983.
units.action_summary: Timely postmark or deliver first semiannual compliance report by specified July 31 or January 31 deadline (prior to specified date).

units.obligation_text: After [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], the first semiannual compliance report must be submitted electronically via CEDRI no later than July 31 or January 31, whichever date follows the end of the first calendar half after the compliance date that is specified for your affected source in § 63.5983.
units.action_summary: Submit the first semiannual compliance report electronically via CEDRI by the specified deadlines (after specified date).

units.obligation_text: Before [DATE 181 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], each subsequent semiannual compliance report must be postmarked or delivered no later than July 31 or January 31, whichever date is the first date following the end of the semiannual reporting period.
units.action_summary: Timely postmark or deliver each subsequent semiannual compliance report by the specified July 31 or January 31 deadlines (prior to specified date).

units.obligation_text: After [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], each subsequent semiannual compliance report must be submitted electronically via CEDRI no later than July 31 or January 31, whichever date is the first date following the end of the semiannual reporting period.
units.action_summary: Submit subsequent semiannual compliance reports electronically via CEDRI by the specified deadlines (after specified date).

units.obligation_text: Before [DATE 181 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], if you had a startup, shutdown or malfunction during the reporting period and you took actions consistent with your startup, shutdown, and malfunction plan, the compliance report must include the information in § 63.10(d)(5)(i).
units.action_summary: If SSM occurred and actions were consistent with SSMP, include specified information in compliance report (prior to specified date).

units.obligation_text: After [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], a startup, shutdown, and malfunction plan is not required.
units.action_summary: SSMP is no longer required after the specified date.

units.obligation_text: Before [DATE 181 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], for each deviation from an emission limitation (emission limit or operating limit) that occurs at an affected source, the compliance report must contain the information in paragraphs (c)(1) through (4) and paragraphs (d)(1) and (2) of this section.
units.action_summary: Include specified information in the compliance report for each deviation from an emission or operating limit (prior to specified date).

units.obligation_text: After [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], for each deviation from an emission limitation (emission limit or operating limit) that occurs at an affected source, the compliance report must contain the information in paragraphs (c)(1) through (3) and (d)(1) through (3) of this section.
units.action_summary: Include the updated specified information in the compliance report for each deviation (after specified date).

units.obligation_text: Before [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER] the total operating time of each affected source during the reporting period.
units.action_summary: Record the total operating time of each affected source during the reporting period (prior to specified date).

units.obligation_text: After [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], in the event that an affected unit fails to meet an applicable standard, record the number of failures. For each failure record the date, time and duration of each failure.
units.action_summary: If an affected unit fails an applicable standard, record the number of failures and for each failure record its date, time, and duration (after specified date).

units.obligation_text: Before [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER] information on the starting date, starting time, duration, and cause of each deviation (including unknown cause, if applicable) and the corrective action taken.
units.action_summary: Report start date, start time, duration, cause of each deviation, and corrective action taken (prior to specified date).

units.obligation_text: After [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], for each failure to meet an applicable standard, record and retain a list of the affected sources or equipment, an estimate of the quantity of each regulated pollutant emitted over any emission limit and a description of the method used to estimate the emissions.
units.action_summary: For each failure, record and retain list of affected sources/equipment, estimate excess pollutant emissions, and describe estimation method (after specified date).

units.obligation_text: After [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], record actions taken to minimize emissions in accordance with § 63.5990, and any corrective actions taken to return the affected unit to its normal or usual manner of operation.
units.action_summary: Record actions taken to minimize emissions per §63.5990 and corrective actions to return unit to normal operation (after specified date).

units.obligation_text: Before [DATE 1 YEAR AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], or once the reporting form has been available on the CEDRI website for 1 year, whichever date is later, if acceptable to both the Administrator and you, you may submit reports and notifications electronically.
units.action_summary: You may submit reports electronically if acceptable to both you and the Administrator (prior to mandatory date).

units.obligation_text: Beginning on [DATE 1 YEAR AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], or once the reporting form has been available on the CEDRI website for 1 year, whichever date is later, you must submit the semiannual compliance report required in § 63.6010(c)(1) through (10), as applicable, to the EPA via the CEDRI.
units.action_summary: Begin mandatory submission of semiannual compliance reports via CEDRI starting on the specified date or after the CEDRI form has been available for one year.

units.obligation_text: You must use the appropriate electronic report form on the CEDRI website for this subpart.
units.action_summary: Use the specified electronic report form on CEDRI for submissions.

units.obligation_text: If the reporting form for the semiannual compliance report specific to this subpart is not available in CEDRI at the time that the report is due, you must submit the report to the Administrator at the appropriate addresses listed in § 63.13.
units.action_summary: If the CEDRI form is unavailable when due, submit the semiannual report to the Administrator at the addresses in §63.13.

units.obligation_text: Once the form has been available in CEDRI for 1 year, you must begin submitting all subsequent reports via CEDRI.
units.action_summary: After the form is available in CEDRI for one year, all subsequent reports must be submitted via CEDRI.

units.obligation_text: The reports must be submitted by the deadlines specified in this subpart, regardless of the method in which the reports are submitted.
units.action_summary: Submit reports by the specified deadlines regardless of submission method.

units.obligation_text: If you claim that some of the information required to be submitted via CEDRI is CBI, submit a complete report, including information claimed to be CBI, to the EPA. The report must be generated using the appropriate electronic reporting form found on the CEDRI website. Submit the file on a compact disc, flash drive, or other commonly used electronic storage medium and clearly mark the medium as CBI. Mail the electronic medium to U.S. EPA/OAQPS/CORE CBI Office, Attention: Group Leader, Measurement Policy Group, MD C404–02, 4930 Old Page Rd., Durham, NC 27703. The same file with the CBI omitted shall be submitted to the EPA via the EPA’s CDX as described earlier in this paragraph.
units.action_summary: If claiming CBI, submit complete CBI-containing file to EPA CBI office on physical medium and submit redacted file via CDX.

units.obligation_text: After [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], if you use a control system (add-on control device and capture system) to meet the emission limitations, you must also conduct a performance test at least once every 5 years following your initial compliance demonstration to verify control system performance and reestablish operating parameters or operating limits for control systems used to comply with the emissions limits.
units.action_summary: If using a control system to comply, conduct a performance test at least every 5 years after initial compliance demonstration to verify performance and reestablish operating parameters.

units.obligation_text: Within 60 days after the date of completing each performance test required by this subpart, you must submit the results of the performance test following the procedures specified in paragraphs (h)(1) through (3) of this section.
units.action_summary: Submit performance test results within 60 days using specified procedures.

units.obligation_text: Data collected using test methods supported by the EPA’s Electronic Reporting Tool (ERT) ... Submit the results of the performance test to the EPA via the CEDRI ... The data must be submitted in a file format generated through the use of the EPA’s ERT. Alternatively, you may submit an electronic file consistent with the extensible markup language (XML) schema listed on the EPA’s ERT website.
units.action_summary: Submit ERT-supported test method data via CEDRI in ERT-generated file format or XML schema.

units.obligation_text: Data collected using test methods that are not supported by the EPA’s ERT ... The results of the performance test must be included as an attachment in the ERT or an alternate electronic file consistent with the XML schema listed on the EPA’s ERT website. Submit the ERT generated package or alternative file to the EPA via CEDRI.
units.action_summary: Submit results from non-ERT-supported test methods as an attachment in ERT or alternate electronic file consistent with XML schema and submit via CEDRI.

units.obligation_text: If you claim some of the information submitted under paragraph (h) of this section is CBI, you must submit a complete file, including information claimed to be CBI, to the EPA. The file must be generated through the use of the EPA’s ERT or an alternate electronic file consistent with the XML schema listed on the EPA’s ERT website. Submit the file on a compact disc, flash drive, or other commonly used electronic storage medium and clearly mark the medium as CBI. Mail the electronic medium to U.S. EPA/OAQPS/CORE CBI Office ... The same file with the CBI omitted must be submitted to the EPA via the EPA’s CDX as described in paragraph (h) of this section.
units.action_summary: If claiming CBI for performance test submissions, submit full CBI file to EPA CBI office on physical medium and submit redacted file via CDX in required formats.

units.obligation_text: After [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER] if you are required to electronically submit a report or notification (i.e., Notification of Compliance Status Report) through CEDRI in the EPA’s CDX, you may assert a claim of EPA system outage for failure to timely comply with the reporting requirement.
units.action_summary: You may assert an EPA system outage claim to explain a late electronic submission, subject to conditions.

units.obligation_text: You must have been or will be precluded from accessing CEDRI and submitting a required report or notification within the time prescribed due to an outage of either the EPA’s CEDRI or CDX systems.
units.action_summary: Demonstrate that you were or will be prevented from accessing CEDRI/CDX due to an outage within the prescribed submission time.

units.obligation_text: The outage must have occurred within the period of time beginning 5 business days prior to the date that the submission is due.
units.action_summary: The outage relied upon must have occurred within 5 business days before the submission due date.

units.obligation_text: The outage may be planned or unplanned.
units.action_summary: Outage relied on for the claim can be either planned or unplanned.

units.obligation_text: You must submit notification to the Administrator in writing as soon as possible following the date you first knew, or through due diligence should have known, that the event may cause or has caused a delay in reporting.
units.action_summary: Promptly notify the Administrator in writing when you first know (or should have known) the outage may cause a delay.

units.obligation_text: You must provide to the Administrator a written description identifying: (i) The date(s) and time(s) when CDX or CEDRI was accessed and the system was unavailable; (ii) A rationale for attributing the delay in reporting beyond the regulatory deadline to EPA system outage; (iii) Measures taken or to be taken to minimize the delay in reporting; and (iv) The date by which you propose to report, or if you have already met the reporting requirement at the time of the notification, the date you reported.
units.action_summary: Provide a written description to the Administrator with specified details about the outage, rationale, mitigation measures, and proposed reporting date (or actual reporting date).

units.obligation_text: The decision to accept the claim of EPA system outage and allow an extension to the reporting deadline is solely within the discretion of the Administrator.
units.action_summary: The Administrator alone has discretion to accept outage claims and grant deadline extensions.
units.modal_raw: is solely within the discretion of

units.obligation_text: In any circumstance, the report or notification must be submitted electronically as soon as possible after the outage is resolved.
units.action_summary: Submit the report electronically as soon as possible after the outage is resolved.

units.obligation_text: After [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER] if you are required to electronically submit a report or notification (i.e., Notification of Compliance Status Report) through CEDRI in the EPA’s CDX, you may assert a claim of force majeure for failure to timely comply with the reporting requirement.
units.action_summary: You may assert a force majeure claim to excuse late electronic submissions, subject to conditions and procedures.

units.obligation_text: You may submit a claim if a force majeure event is about to occur, occurs, or has occurred or there are lingering effects from such an event within the period of time beginning five business days prior to the date the submission is due.
units.action_summary: You may submit a force majeure claim if the event occurs or has effects within five business days before the submission due date.

units.obligation_text: You must submit notification to the Administrator in writing as soon as possible following the date you first knew, or through due diligence should have known, that the event may cause or has caused a delay in reporting.
units.action_summary: Promptly notify the Administrator in writing when you learn (or should have learned) the force majeure event may cause a reporting delay.

units.obligation_text: You must provide to the Administrator: (i) A written description of the force majeure event; (ii) A rationale for attributing the delay in reporting beyond the regulatory deadline to the force majeure event; (iii) Measures taken or to be taken to minimize the delay in reporting; and (iv) The date by which you propose to report, or if you have already met the reporting requirement at the time of the notification, the date you reported.
units.action_summary: Provide detailed written information about the force majeure event, rationale for delay, mitigation measures, and proposed or actual reporting date to the Administrator.

units.obligation_text: The decision to accept the claim of force majeure and allow an extension to the reporting deadline is solely within the discretion of the Administrator.
units.action_summary: The Administrator has sole discretion to accept force majeure claims and grant reporting deadline extensions.
units.modal_raw: is solely within the discretion of

units.obligation_text: In any circumstance, the reporting must occur as soon as possible after the force majeure event occurs.
units.action_summary: Submit the required report as soon as possible after the force majeure event.

units.obligation_text: Before [DATE 181 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], the records in § 63.6(e)(3)(iii) through (v) related to startup, shutdown, and malfunction.
units.action_summary: Retain records specified in §63.6(e)(3)(iii)-(v) related to startup, shutdown, and malfunction (prior to specified date).

units.obligation_text: After [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], it is not required to keep records in § 63.6(e)(3)(iii) through (v) related to startup, shutdown, or malfunction.
units.action_summary: Recordkeeping requirements in §63.6(e)(3)(iii)-(v) for SSM are no longer required after the specified date.

units.obligation_text: After [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER] any records required to be maintained by this subpart that are submitted electronically via the EPA’s CEDRI may be maintained in electronic format.
units.action_summary: You may maintain records submitted via CEDRI in electronic format after the specified date.

units.obligation_text: This ability to maintain electronic copies does not affect the requirement for facilities to make records, data, and reports available upon request to a delegated air agency or the EPA as part of an on-site compliance evaluation.
units.action_summary: Make records, data, and reports available upon request to delegated air agencies or EPA during on-site compliance evaluations, even if maintained electronically.

units.obligation_text: [As stated in § 63.6010, you must submit each report that applies to you according to the following table]
units.action_summary: Submit each applicable report according to the schedule and content requirements in the table and §63.6010.

units.obligation_text: Before [DATE 181 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], immediate startup, shutdown, and malfunction report if you had a startup, shutdown, or malfunction during the reporting period that is not consistent with your startup, shutdown, and malfunction plan. After [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], this report is no longer required.
units.action_summary: Prior to specified date, immediately report SSM events inconsistent with your SSMP; after specified date, this immediate report is no longer required.

units.obligation_text: If you use a control system (add-on control device and capture system) to meet the emission limitations. Conduct a performance test at least once every 5 years following your initial compliance demonstration according to the requirements in § 63.5993.
units.action_summary: If using a control system to meet emission limits, conduct a performance test at least every 5 years following initial compliance demonstration per §63.5993.

title: Environmental Protection Agency Acquisition Regulation (EPAAR); Open Source Software

units.obligation_text: Contracting Officers shall use clause 1552.239–71, Open Source Software, for all procurements where open-source software development/custom development of software will be required; including, but not limited to, multi-agency contracts, Federal Supply Schedule orders, Governmentwide Acquisition Contracts, interagency agreements, cooperative agreements and student services contracts.
units.action_summary: Use clause 1552.239-71 for all procurements requiring open-source or custom software development.

units.obligation_text: In addition to clause 1552.239–71, Contracting Officers must also select the appropriate version* of Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) clause 52.227–14, Rights in Data—General, to include in the subject procurement in accordance with FAR 27.409.
units.action_summary: Select and include the appropriate version of FAR clause 52.227-14 in the procurement per FAR 27.409.

units.obligation_text: Alternate IV of clause 52.227–14 is NOT suitable for open-source software procurement use because it gives the contractor blanket permission to assert copyright.
units.action_summary: Do not use Alternate IV of FAR clause 52.227-14 for open-source software procurements.

units.obligation_text: It is the EPA policy that new custom-developed code be made broadly available for reuse across the federal government, subject to the exceptions provided in (b)(3) of this section.
units.action_summary: New custom-developed code should be made broadly available for reuse across the federal government, subject to listed exceptions.

units.obligation_text: The policy does not apply retroactively so it does not require existing custom-developed code also be made available for Government-wide reuse or as OSS. However, making such code available for government-wide reuse or as OSS, to the extent practicable, is strongly encouraged.
units.action_summary: Making existing custom-developed code available for government-wide reuse or as OSS is strongly encouraged but not required.

units.obligation_text: Providing an enterprise code inventory (e.g., code.json file) that lists new and applicable custom-developed code for, or by, the EPA;
units.action_summary: Provide an enterprise code inventory listing new and applicable custom-developed code.

units.obligation_text: Indicating whether the code is available for Federal reuse;
units.action_summary: Indicate whether code is available for Federal reuse.

units.obligation_text: Indicating if the code is available publicly as OSS.
units.action_summary: Indicate whether code is available publicly as open source software.

units.obligation_text: Source code developed for National Security Systems (NSS), as defined in 40 U.S.C. 11103, is exempt from the requirements herein.
units.action_summary: Source code developed for National Security Systems is exempt from these requirements.

units.obligation_text: Exceptions may be applied in specific instances to exempt EPA from sharing custom-developed code with other government agencies.
units.action_summary: EPA may apply exceptions in specific cases to avoid sharing custom-developed code with other agencies.

units.obligation_text: Any exceptions used must be approved and documented by the Chief Information Officer (CIO) or his or her designee for the purposes of ensuring effective oversight and management of IT resources.
units.action_summary: CIO or designee must approve and document any exceptions used to exempt sharing code.

units.obligation_text: For excepted software, EPA must provide OMB a brief narrative justification for each exception, with redactions as appropriate.
units.action_summary: EPA must provide OMB a brief narrative justification for each exception for excepted software.

units.obligation_text: The sharing of the source code is restricted by law or regulation, including—but not limited to—patent or intellectual property law, the Export Asset Regulations, the International Traffic in Arms Regulation and the federal laws and regulations governing classified information.
units.action_summary: Exception applies if sharing is restricted by law or regulation (e.g., IP, export, ITAR, classified info).

units.obligation_text: The sharing of the source code would create an identifiable risk to the detriment of national security, confidentiality of government information or individual privacy.
units.action_summary: Exception applies if sharing would create identifiable risk to national security, confidentiality, or privacy.

units.obligation_text: The sharing of the source code would create an identifiable risk to the stability, security or integrity of EPA’s systems or personnel.
units.action_summary: Exception applies if sharing risks stability, security, or integrity of EPA systems or personnel.

units.obligation_text: The sharing of the source code would create an identifiable risk to EPA mission, programs or operations.
units.action_summary: Exception applies if sharing risks EPA mission, programs, or operations.

units.obligation_text: The CIO believes it is in the national interest to exempt sharing the source code.
units.action_summary: Exception may be applied if the CIO determines exemption is in the national interest.

units.obligation_text: The Contractor shall deliver to the Contracting Officer (CO) or Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR) the underlying source code, license file, related files, build instructions, software user’s guides, automated test suites, and other associated documentation as applicable.

units.obligation_text: In accordance with OMB Memorandum M–16–21 the Government asserts its unlimited rights—including rights to reproduction, reuse, modification and distribution of the custom source code, associated documentation, and related files— for reuse across the federal government and as open source software for the public.
units.action_summary: The Government asserts unlimited rights to reproduce, reuse, modify, and distribute custom source code and related materials for government reuse and public OSS.

units.obligation_text: These unlimited rights described above attach to all code furnished in the performance of the contract, unless the parties expressly agree otherwise in the contract.
units.action_summary: Unlimited rights attach to all code furnished under the contract unless the parties expressly agree otherwise.

units.obligation_text: The Contractor is prohibited from reselling code developed under this contract without express written consent of the EPA Contracting Officer.
units.action_summary: Contractor may not resell code developed under the contract without express written consent of the EPA Contracting Officer.

units.obligation_text: The Contractor must provide at least 30 days advance notice if it intends to resell code developed under this contract.
units.action_summary: Provide at least 30 days advance notice if intending to resell contract-developed code.

units.action_summary: Technical guidance should conform to EPA's Open Source Code Guidance maintained by OMS.

title: Hazardous and Solid Waste Management System: Disposal of Coal Combustion Residuals from Electric Utilities; A Holistic Approach to Closure Part A: Deadline to Initiate Closure

units.obligation_text: Except as provided by paragraph (a)(3) of this section, no later than August 31, 2020, an owner or operator of an existing unlined CCR surface impoundment must cease placing CCR and non-CCR wastestreams into such CCR surface impoundment and either retrofit or close the CCR unit in accordance with the requirements of § 257.102.
units.actor: the owner or operator of an existing unlined CCR surface impoundment
units.action_summary: By Aug 31, 2020, stop placing CCR and non-CCR wastes into the unlined impoundment and either retrofit or close it per §257.102.

units.obligation_text: Except as provided by paragraph (b)(4) of this section, the owner or operator of an existing CCR surface impoundment that has not demonstrated compliance with the location standard specified in § 257.60(a) must cease placing CCR and non-CCR wastestreams into such CCR unit no later than August 31, 2020 and close the CCR unit in accordance with the requirements of § 257.102.
units.actor: the owner or operator of an existing CCR surface impoundment that has not demonstrated compliance with §257.60(a)
units.action_summary: If the unit hasn't shown compliance with the location standard, stop placing wastes by Aug 31, 2020 and close per §257.102.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator of a CCR landfill, CCR surface impoundment, or any lateral expansion of a CCR unit that is subject to closure pursuant to § 257.101(a), (b)(1), or (d) may continue to receive CCR and/or non-CCR wastestreams in the unit provided the owner or operator meets the requirements of either paragraph (a), (b), (e), or (f) of this section.
units.actor: the owner or operator of a CCR landfill, CCR surface impoundment, or lateral expansion subject to closure under §257.101(a),(b)(1), or (d)
units.action_summary: May continue receiving CCR/non-CCR in the unit only if the owner/operator meets requirements in (a), (b), (e), or (f).

units.obligation_text: Notwithstanding the provisions of § 257.101(d), a CCR landfill may continue to receive CCR if the owner or operator of the CCR landfill certifies that the CCR must continue to be managed in that CCR landfill due to the absence of alternative disposal capacity both on-site and off-site of the facility. To qualify under this paragraph, the owner or operator of the CCR landfill must document that all of the following conditions have been met:
units.actor: the owner or operator of the CCR landfill
units.action_summary: Permission to continue receiving CCR if owner certifies need due to lack of alternative capacity and documents required conditions.
units.modal_raw: may / must (certify and document to qualify)

units.obligation_text: Once alternative capacity is available, the CCR landfill must cease receiving CCR and initiate closure following the timeframes in § 257.102(e) and (f).
units.actor: the owner or operator of the CCR landfill
units.action_summary: When alternative capacity becomes available, stop receiving CCR and begin closure per §257.102(e),(f).

units.obligation_text: If no alternative capacity is identified within five years after the initial certification, the CCR landfill must cease receiving CCR and close in accordance with the timeframes in § 257.102(e) and (f).
units.actor: the owner or operator of the CCR landfill
units.action_summary: If no alternative capacity within five years of initial certification, stop receiving CCR and close per §257.102(e),(f).

units.obligation_text: Notwithstanding the provisions of § 257.101(d), a CCR landfill may continue to receive CCR if the owner or operator certifies that the facility will cease operation of the coal-fired boilers within the timeframes specified in paragraphs (b)(2) through (4) of this section, but in the interim period (prior to closure of the coal-fired boiler), the facility must continue to use the CCR unit due to the absence of alternative disposal capacity both on-site and off-site of the facility. To qualify under this paragraph, the owner or operator of the CCR unit must document that all of the following conditions have been met:
units.actor: the owner or operator of the CCR landfill/CCR unit
units.action_summary: May continue receiving CCR if owner certifies boilers will cease within specified timeframes and documents conditions; in interim must continue to use the CCR unit due to lack of alternative capacity.
units.modal_raw: may / must (certify and document; must continue to use in interim)

units.obligation_text: In the interim period (prior to closure of the coal-fired boiler), the facility must continue to use the CCR unit due to the absence of alternative disposal capacity both on-site and off-site of the facility.
units.action_summary: During the interim before boiler closure, the facility must continue to use the CCR unit because no alternative capacity exists.

units.obligation_text: To qualify under this paragraph, the owner or operator of the CCR unit must document that all of the following conditions have been met:
units.actor: the owner or operator of the CCR unit
units.action_summary: Must document that the specified qualifying conditions have been met to continue receiving CCR under this paragraph.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator must prepare and place in the facility’s operating record a notification of intent to comply with the alternative closure requirements of this section. The notification must describe why the CCR unit qualifies for the alternative closure provisions under either paragraph (a) or (b) of this section, in addition to providing the documentation and certifications required by paragraph (a) or (b) of this section.
units.action_summary: Prepare and put in the operating record a notification of intent to comply with alternative closure requirements, describing qualification and providing required documentation/certifications.

units.obligation_text: If the CCR unit is closing pursuant to § 257.101(a)(1), the owner or operator must prepare the notification no later than August 31, 2020.
units.action_summary: If closing under §257.101(a)(1), prepare and place the notification in the operating record by Aug 31, 2020.

units.obligation_text: If the CCR unit is closing pursuant to § 257.101(b)(1), the owner or operator must prepare the notification no later than August 31, 2020.
units.action_summary: If closing under §257.101(b)(1), prepare and place the notification in the operating record by Aug 31, 2020.

units.obligation_text: If the CCR unit is closing pursuant to § 257.101(d)(1), the owner or operator must prepare the notification no later than six months after the date it is determined that the CCR unit is not in compliance with the requirements of § 257.64(a).
units.action_summary: If closing under §257.101(d)(1), prepare and place the notification in the operating record within six months after noncompliance determination under §257.64(a).

units.obligation_text: Notwithstanding the provisions of § 257.101(a), or (b)(1), a CCR surface impoundment may continue to receive CCR and/or non-CCR wastestreams if the owner or operator of the CCR surface impoundment certifies that the CCR and/or non-CCR wastestreams must continue to be managed in that CCR surface impoundment to allow the facility to complete the measures necessary to provide alternative disposal capacity, either on-site or off-site of the facility. Qualification under this paragraph lasts only until alternative capacity is available or until November 30, 2020, whichever is sooner. To qualify under this paragraph, the owner or operator of the CCR surface impoundment must document that all of the following conditions have been met:
units.actor: the owner or operator of the CCR surface impoundment
units.action_summary: Short-term permission to continue receiving wastes if owner certifies necessity and documents conditions; authorization lasts until alt capacity is available or Nov 30, 2020.
units.modal_raw: may / must (certify and document to qualify)

units.obligation_text: No alternative disposal capacity is available on-site or off-site. An increase in costs or the inconvenience of existing capacity is not sufficient to support qualification under this section;
units.actor: the owner or operator (as to qualification)
units.action_summary: To qualify, there must be no alternative disposal capacity available; higher costs/inconvenience alone do not qualify.
units.modal_raw: must (as a qualifying condition to document)

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator has made, and continues to make, efforts to obtain additional capacity that will become available no later than November 30, 2020.
units.action_summary: Owner must have made and continue making efforts to obtain additional capacity available by Nov 30, 2020.

units.obligation_text: Once alternative capacity is identified, the owner or operator must arrange to use such capacity as soon as feasible;
units.action_summary: When alternative capacity is identified, the owner must arrange to use it as soon as feasible.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator must remain in compliance with all other requirements of this subpart, including the requirement to conduct any necessary corrective action. The owner or operator at all times bears responsibility for demonstrating qualification under this section. Failure to remain in compliance with any of the requirements of this subpart could result in the automatic loss of authorization under this section.
units.action_summary: Owner must remain in compliance with the subpart and is responsible for demonstrating qualification; noncompliance can result in loss of authorization.

units.obligation_text: Once alternative capacity is available, the CCR surface impoundment must cease receiving CCR and non-CCR wastestreams and initiate closure following the timeframes in § 257.102(e) and (f).
units.actor: the owner or operator of the CCR surface impoundment
units.action_summary: When alternative capacity is available, cease receiving wastes and start closure per §257.102(e),(f).

units.obligation_text: If no alternative capacity is identified by November 30, 2020, the CCR surface impoundment must cease receiving CCR and non-CCR wastestreams and close in accordance with the timeframes in § 257.102(e) and (f).
units.actor: the owner or operator of the CCR surface impoundment
units.action_summary: If no alternative capacity by Nov 30, 2020, stop receiving wastes and close per §257.102(e),(f).

units.obligation_text: An owner or operator of a CCR surface impoundment that closes in accordance with paragraphs (e) of this section must complete the notices as specified in paragraphs (d) and (e)(4)(i) through (ii) of this section.
units.actor: the owner or operator of the CCR surface impoundment
units.action_summary: If closing under paragraph (e), the owner/operator must complete the specified notices.

units.obligation_text: No later than August 31, 2020 the owner or operator must prepare and place in the facility’s operating record a notification of intent to comply with alternative closure requirements of this section. The notification must describe the factual basis to support the facility’s conclusion that the CCR unit qualifies for the alternative closure provisions under this paragraph, in addition to providing the documentation and certifications required by this paragraph.
units.action_summary: By Aug 31, 2020, prepare and place in operating record a notification of intent to comply with the alternative closure provisions, including factual basis and required documentation/certifications.

units.obligation_text: An owner or operator of a CCR surface impoundment must also prepare the notification of intent to close a CCR unit as required by § 257.102(g).
units.action_summary: Must prepare the notification of intent to close required by §257.102(g).

units.obligation_text: Notwithstanding the provisions of § 257.101(a), and (b)(1), a CCR surface impoundment may continue to recieve CCR and/or non-CCR wastestreams if the owner or operator of the CCR surface impoundment demonstrates to the Administrator or the Participating State Director that the CCR and/or non-CCR wastestreams must continue to be managed in that CCR surface impoundment either: Because it was infeasible to complete the measures necessary to provide alternative disposal capacity on-site or off-site of the facility by November 30, 2020; or because the owner or operator certifies that the facility will permanently cease operation of the coal-fired boilers within the timeframes specified in paragraph (f)(2)(ii) of this section. Authorization under this paragraph is not available for units that have continued operation pursuant to § 257.103(e). The demonstration must be submitted to the Administrator or the Participating State Director no later than the relevant deadline in paragraph (f)(3) of this section and will act on the submission in accordance with the procedures in paragraph (f)(3) of this section.
units.actor: the owner or operator of the CCR surface impoundment
units.action_summary: Site-specific permission to continue receiving wastes if owner demonstrates infeasibility of obtaining alternative capacity by Nov 30, 2020, or certifies permanent cessation of boilers within specified timeframes; must submit demonstration by relevant deadlines.

units.obligation_text: To obtain approval under this paragraph, the owner or operator of the CCR surface impoundment must submit a demonstration that includes documents all of the following:
units.actor: the owner or operator of the CCR surface impoundment
units.action_summary: Must submit a demonstration including required documents to obtain approval under the site-specific infeasibility provision.

units.obligation_text: Documentation that no alternative disposal capacity is available on-site or off-site. An increase in costs or the inconvenience of existing capacity is not sufficient to support qualification under this section;
units.actor: the owner or operator (as part of the demonstration)
units.action_summary: Include documentation showing no alternative disposal capacity exists; cost/inconvenience alone insufficient.

units.obligation_text: A certification from the owner or operator of the CCR surface impoundment that CCR and/or non-CCR wastestreams must continue to be managed in that CCR surface impoundment because it was infeasible to complete the measures necessary to obtain alternative disposal capacity either on-site or off-site of the facility by November 30, 2020;
units.action_summary: Provide a certification that managing wastes in the impoundment is necessary because obtaining alternative capacity by Nov 30, 2020 was infeasible.

units.obligation_text: A certification from the owner or operator of the CCR surface impoundment that the facility is in compliance with all of the requirements of this Subpart;
units.action_summary: Provide certification that the facility complies with all requirements of this Subpart.

units.obligation_text: A workplan that contains the following elements:
units.action_summary: Submit a workplan containing specified elements as part of the demonstration.

units.obligation_text: A narrative discussing the approach selected to obtain alternative capacity for CCR and/or non-CCR wastestreams;
units.action_summary: Include a narrative describing the selected approach to obtain alternative capacity.

units.obligation_text: A detailed schedule of the fastest feasible time to complete the measures necessary for alternate capacity to be available including a visual timeline representation;
units.action_summary: Include a detailed schedule and visual timeline showing the fastest feasible completion of measures to obtain alternative capacity.

units.obligation_text: A narrative discussion of the schedule and visual timeline representation;
units.action_summary: Include a narrative explaining the schedule and visual timeline.

units.obligation_text: A narrative discussion of the progress the owner or operator has made to obtain alternative capacity for the CCR and/or non-CCR wastestreams;
units.action_summary: Include a narrative describing progress already made to obtain alternative capacity.

units.obligation_text: A narrative discussion of the strategy the owner or operator will utilize to remain in compliance with all other requirements of this subpart, including the requirement to conduct any necessary corrective action;
units.action_summary: Include a narrative of the strategy to remain in compliance with the subpart and carry out any necessary corrective action.

units.obligation_text: Once alternative capacity for a CCR or non-CCR wastestream is available, the existing CCR surface impoundment must cease receiving that CCR or non-CCR wastestream. The new alternate capacity must be utilized as soon as available. Once the existing CCR surface impoundment ceases receipt of all CCR and/or non-CCR wastestreams, the existing CCR surface impoundment must initiate closure following the timeframes in 257.102(e) and (f).
units.actor: the owner or operator of the existing CCR surface impoundment
units.action_summary: When alternative capacity becomes available, cease receipt of that wastestream, use the new capacity immediately, and when all receipts stop initiate closure per §257.102.

units.obligation_text: An owner or operator may seek additional time beyond the time granted in the initial approval by making the showing in paragraph (f)(1)(i) of this section, provided that no facility may be granted time to operate the impoundment beyond October 15, 2023.
units.actor: the owner or operator / the Administrator
units.action_summary: Owner may request additional time by making the required showing, but no facility may be granted authorization to operate past Oct 15, 2023.

units.obligation_text: No later than October 15, 2023, all CCR surface impoundments covered by this section must cease receiving CCR and non-CCR wastestreams and close in accordance with the timeframes in § 257.102(e) and (f).
units.actor: the owner or operator of CCR surface impoundments covered by this section
units.action_summary: By Oct 15, 2023, all covered impoundments must stop receiving wastes and close per §257.102(e),(f).

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator at all times bears responsibility for demonstrating qualification under this section. Failure to remain in compliance with any of the requirements of this subpart will result in the automatic loss of authorization under this section.
units.action_summary: Owner/operator must at all times demonstrate qualification; noncompliance leads to automatic loss of authorization.

units.obligation_text: An owner or operator of a CCR surface impoundment that closes in accordance with paragraph (f)(1) of this section must complete the notices and progress reports as specified in paragraphs (d) and (f)(1)(vi) through (xi) of this section.
units.action_summary: If closing under paragraph (f)(1), owner must complete the specified notices and progress reports.

units.obligation_text: Upon submission of the demonstration to the Administrator or the Participating State Director the owner or operator must prepare and place in the facility’s operating record a notification of submitting the demonstration.
units.action_summary: Upon submitting the demonstration, prepare and put a notification of submission in the facility operating record.

units.obligation_text: Upon approval or denial from the Administrator or the Participating State Director the owner or operator must prepare and place in the facility’s operating record the notification of approval or denial and the approved or denied demonstration required by paragraph (f)(1) of this section.
units.action_summary: After approval or denial, prepare and place in the operating record the notice of approval/denial and the approved/denied demonstration.

units.obligation_text: If at any time after approval, the owner or operator discovers the need to seek additional time due to infeasibility to achieve cease receipt of waste prior to the granted alternative deadline under paragraph (f)(1)(iii) of this section, the owner or operator must submit a notification to the Administrator or the Participating State Director as soon as possible. The owner or operator must prepare and place the notification in the facility’s operating record.
units.action_summary: If after approval the owner needs more time due to infeasibility, promptly notify the Administrator or Participating State Director and place the notification in the operating record.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator must prepare semi-annual progress reports. The semi-annual progress reports are to contain the following: (A) Discussion on progress obtaining alternative capacity, including: (1) Discussion on the current stage of obtaining the capacity in reference to the timeline required under paragraph (f)(1)(i)(D)(2) of this section; (2) Discussion on if the owner or operator is on schedule for obtaining alternative capacity; (3) Discussion of any problems encountered, and a description of the actions taken to resolve the problems; and (4) Discussion of the goals for the next 6 months and major milestones to be achieve for obtaining alternative capacity; and (B) Discussion of any planned operational changes at the facility.
units.action_summary: Prepare semi-annual progress reports containing specified discussions of progress, schedule, problems and plans, and any planned operational changes.

units.obligation_text: Discussion on the current stage of obtaining the capacity in reference to the timeline required under paragraph (f)(1)(i)(D)(2) of this section;
units.actor: the owner or operator (in the semi-annual report)
units.action_summary: Include discussion of current stage relative to the workplan timeline in the semi-annual report.

units.obligation_text: Discussion on if the owner or operator is on schedule for obtaining alternative capacity;
units.actor: the owner or operator (in the semi-annual report)
units.action_summary: Report whether the owner/operator is on schedule to obtain alternative capacity.

units.obligation_text: Discussion of any problems encountered, and a description of the actions taken to resolve the problems;
units.actor: the owner or operator (in the semi-annual report)
units.action_summary: Describe problems encountered and actions taken to resolve them in the semi-annual report.

units.obligation_text: Discussion of the goals for the next 6 months and major milestones to be achieve for obtaining alternative capacity;
units.actor: the owner or operator (in the semi-annual report)
units.action_summary: Include goals and major milestones for the next six months in the semi-annual report.

units.obligation_text: Discussion of any planned operational changes at the facility.
units.actor: the owner or operator (in the semi-annual report)
units.action_summary: Report any planned operational changes in the semi-annual progress report.

units.obligation_text: The semi-annual progress reports are to be prepared and posted on April 1 and October 1 of each year for the duration of the alternate cease receipt of waste deadline.
units.action_summary: Prepare and post semi-annual progress reports on April 1 and October 1 each year while alternate cease-receipt deadline applies.

units.obligation_text: The first semi-annual progress report is to be prepared and posted by whichever date, April 1 or October 1, is soonest after receiving approval from the Administrator or the Participating State Director;
units.action_summary: Prepare and post the first semi-annual report by the next April 1 or October 1 following approval.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator has completed the progress reports specified in paragraph (f)(1)(ix) of this section when the reports are placed in the facility’s operating record as required by § 257.105(i)(17).
units.action_summary: Progress reports are completed when placed in the facility's operating record per §257.105(i)(17).

units.obligation_text: An owner or operator of a CCR surface impoundment must also prepare the notification of intent to close a CCR unit as required by § 257.102(g).
units.action_summary: Prepare the notification of intent to close required by §257.102(g).

units.obligation_text: Notwithstanding the provisions of § 257.101(a), and (b)(1), a CCR surface impoundment may continue to receive CCR and non-CCR wastestreams if the owner or operator certifies that the facility will cease operation of the coal-fired boilers and complete closure of the impoundment within the timeframes specified in paragraphs (f)(2)(ii) of this section, but in the interim period (prior to closure of the coal-fired boiler), the facility must continue to use the CCR unit due to the absence of alternative disposal capacity both on-site and off-site of the facility. To qualify under this paragraph, the owner or operator of the CCR unit must submit a demonstration to the Administrator or Participating State Director that contains all of the following:
units.actor: the owner or operator of the CCR surface impoundment
units.action_summary: Permission to continue receiving wastes if owner certifies boilers will cease and closure completed within specified timeframes and submits a demonstration with required elements; interim use required due to lack of alternative capacity.
