units.actor: the owner or operator (as part of the demonstration)
units.action_summary: Provide documentation showing no alternative disposal capacity is available; cost/inconvenience alone is insufficient.

units.obligation_text: A plan to mitigate potential risks to human health and the environment from the CCR surface impoundment;
units.actor: the owner or operator (as part of the demonstration)
units.action_summary: Include a plan to mitigate potential human health and environmental risks from the impoundment.

units.obligation_text: Certification that the owner or operator remains in compliance with all other requirements of this subpart, including the requirement to conduct any necessary corrective action;
units.actor: the owner or operator (as part of the demonstration)
units.action_summary: Certify ongoing compliance with the Subpart, including corrective actions.

units.obligation_text: Documentation that the coal-fired boilers and closure of the impoundment will be completed within the timeframes specified in paragraphs (f)(2)(ii) of this section.
units.actor: the owner or operator (as part of the demonstration)
units.action_summary: Provide documentation showing the boilers' cessation and impoundment closure will be completed within specified timeframes.

units.obligation_text: For a CCR surface impoundment that is 40 acres or smaller, the coal-fired boiler must cease operation and the CCR surface impoundment must have completed closure no later than October 17, 2023.
units.actor: the owner or operator of a CCR surface impoundment 40 acres or smaller
units.action_summary: For impoundments ≤40 acres, boilers must stop and closure completed by Oct 17, 2023.

units.obligation_text: For a CCR surface impoundment that is larger than 40 acres, the coal-fired boiler must cease operation, and the CCR surface impoundment must complete closure no later than October 17, 2028.
units.actor: the owner or operator of a CCR surface impoundment larger than 40 acres
units.action_summary: For impoundments >40 acres, boilers must stop and closure completed by Oct 17, 2028.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator at all times bears responsibility for demonstrating qualification for authorization under section. Failure to remain in compliance with any of the requirements of this subpart will result in the automatic loss of authorization under this section.
units.action_summary: Owner/operator must demonstrate qualification at all times; noncompliance results in automatic loss of authorization.

units.obligation_text: An owner or operator of a CCR surface impoundment that closes in accordance with paragraph (f)(2) of this section must complete the notices and progress reports as specified in paragraphs (d) and (f)(2)(v) through (vii) of this section.
units.action_summary: If closing under paragraph (f)(2), complete specified notices and progress reports.

units.obligation_text: Upon approval or denial from the Administrator or the Participating State Director the owner or operator must prepare and place in the facility’s operating record the notification of approval or denial and the approved or denied demonstration required by paragraph (f)(2) of this section.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator must prepare an annual progress report documenting the continued lack of alternative capacity and the progress towards the closure of the CCR surface impoundment.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator must submit the demonstration required under paragraph (f)(1)(i) of this section, for an alternative cease receipt of waste deadline for a CCR surface impoundment pursuant to paragraph (f)(1) of this section, to EPA for approval no later than 2 months prior to the unit’s deadline to cease receiving waste.
units.action_summary: Submit the f(1)(i) demonstration to EPA for approval at least 2 months before the unit's cease-receiving deadline.

units.obligation_text: An owner or operator may seek additional time beyond the time granted in the initial approval, as allowed under paragraph (f)(1)(iii) of this section, by submitting a new demonstration, as required under paragraph (f)(1)(i) of this section, to EPA for approval. units.actor: the owner or operator / EPA (granting time)
units.action_summary: Owner may request additional time by submitting a new demonstration; however, no facility may be authorized to operate past Oct 15, 2023.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator must submit the demonstration required under paragraph (f)(2)(i) of this section, for an alternative cease receipt of waste deadline for a CCR surface impoundment under paragraph (f)(2) of this section, to EPA for approval no later than May 15, 2020.

units.obligation_text: EPA will evaluate the demonstration and may request additional information to complete its review.

units.obligation_text: Submission of a complete demonstration will toll the facility’s deadline to cease receipt of waste until issuance of a final decision under paragraph (f)(3)(iv) of this section. Incomplete submissions will not toll the facility’s deadline.

units.obligation_text: EPA will publish a proposed decision on EPA’s website for a 15-day comment period. If the demonstration is particularly complex, EPA will provide a comment period of 20 to 30 days.
units.action_summary: EPA will publish its proposed decision online for a 15-day comment period (20-30 days if complex).

units.obligation_text: After consideration of the comments, EPA will issue its decision on the alternate compliance deadline within 4 months of receiving a complete demonstration. title: Tolerance Crop Grouping Program V

units.obligation_text: Therefore, it is proposed that 40 CFR chapter I be amended as follows:
units.action_summary: EPA proposes to amend 40 CFR chapter I as described below.

units.obligation_text: The authority citation for part 180 continues to read as follows: Authority: 21 U.S.C. 321 (q), 346a and 371.
units.action_summary: The existing authority citation for part 180 remains as stated.

units.obligation_text: Add alphabetically the entries for "Basil"; "Flowers, edible, multiple species"; and "Mint" to the table in paragraph (g).
units.action_summary: EPA must add entries for Basil; Flowers, edible, multiple species; and Mint to the §180.1(g) table, in alphabetical order.

units.obligation_text: Revise the entry for "Marjoram" in the table in paragraph (g).
units.action_summary: EPA must revise the Marjoram entry in the §180.1(g) table.

units.obligation_text: Amend Sec. 180.40 by revising paragraph (j) to read as follows:
units.action_summary: EPA must revise paragraph (j) of §180.40 as provided.

units.obligation_text: When EPA amends a crop group in a manner that expands or contracts the commodities that are covered by the group, EPA will initially retain the pre-existing as well as the revised crop group in the CFR.
units.action_summary: If EPA amends a crop group by expanding or contracting covered commodities, EPA must initially keep both the pre-existing and revised crop groups in the CFR.

units.obligation_text: Where the revised crop group has the same number as the pre-existing crop group, the revised crop group number will be followed by a hyphen and the final two digits of the year in which it was established (e.g., if Crop Group 1 is amended in 2007, the revised group will be designated as Crop Group 1-07). If the pre-existing crop group had crop subgroups, these subgroups will be numbered in a similar fashion in the revised crop group. The name of the revised crop group will not be changed from the pre-existing crop group unless the revision so changes the composition of the crop group that the pre-existing name is no longer accurate.
units.action_summary: If a revised crop group keeps the same number, EPA must append -YY (final two digits of year) to the revised group number; similarly number subgroups; and EPA must keep the pre-existing name unless the composition change makes it inaccurate.

units.obligation_text: Where EPA amends a crop group by creating one or more different crop groups, the revised crop groups will have different numbers and names (e.g., the amendment of Crop Group 19 through the creation of Crop Groups 25 and 26). The pre-existing crop group will be amended to identify the revised crop group(s).
units.action_summary: If EPA splits a crop group into new groups, the new groups must have different numbers and names, and the pre-existing group's entry must be amended to identify the new group(s).

units.obligation_text: Once a revised crop group is established, EPA will no longer establish tolerances under the pre-existing crop group. At appropriate times, EPA will amend tolerances for crop groups that have been superseded by revised crop groups to conform the pre-existing crop group to the revised crop group. Once all of the tolerances for the pre-existing crop group have been updated, the pre-existing crop group will be removed from the CFR.
units.action_summary: After establishing a revised crop group, EPA must stop creating tolerances under the old group, update tolerances as appropriate to conform to the revised group, and then remove the pre-existing group from the CFR once updates are complete.

units.obligation_text: In Sec. 180.41: Add a new paragraph (c)(28)(iv) after the table in paragraph (iii). Add new paragraphs (c)(34) and (35).
units.action_summary: EPA must add specified new paragraphs to §180.41: (c)(28)(iv) and (c)(34) and (c)(35).

units.obligation_text: After [date of publication of final rule], new herb crop group and subgroup tolerances will be established as Crop Group 25 or subgroups 25A and 25B, and new spice crop group tolerances will be established as Crop Group 26.
units.action_summary: After the final rule's publication date, EPA will establish new herb crop group tolerances as Crop Group 25 (with subgroups 25A and 25B) and new spice crop group tolerances as Crop Group 26.

units.obligation_text: at least 60 days before signing it in proposed form for publication in the Federal Register.

units.obligation_text: The draft regulatory document is not available to the public until after it has been signed and made available by EPA.
units.action_summary: The public is prohibited from accessing the draft regulatory document until EPA signs and makes it available.

units.section: I. What action is EPA taking?
units.obligation_text: If the Secretary of USDA comments in writing regarding the draft proposed rule within 30 days after receiving it, the EPA Administrator shall include the comments of the Secretary of USDA and the EPA Administrator’s response to those comments with the proposed rule that publishes in the Federal Register.
units.action_summary: If the Secretary of USDA submits written comments within 30 days, the EPA Administrator must include those comments and EPA's response with the proposed rule when published.

units.section: I. What action is EPA taking?
units.obligation_text: The Secretary of USDA comments in writing regarding the draft proposed rule within 30 days after receiving it.
units.action_summary: The Secretary of USDA may submit written comments on the draft proposed rule within 30 days of receipt.

units.section: I. What action is EPA taking?
units.obligation_text: If the Secretary of USDA does not comment in writing within 30 days after receiving the draft proposed rule, the EPA Administrator may sign the proposed rule for publication in the Federal Register any time after the 30-day period.
units.action_summary: If the Secretary does not submit written comments within 30 days, the EPA Administrator is permitted to sign the proposed rule for publication any time after that 30-day period.

units.section: I. What action is EPA taking?
units.obligation_text: The Secretary of USDA does not comment in writing within 30 days after receiving the draft proposed rule.
units.action_summary: Condition that the Secretary of USDA fails to submit written comments within 30 days of receiving the draft.

units.obligation_text: Comments must be received by August 21, 2019.

units.action_summary: Agricultural employers are prohibited from allowing or directing anyone to enter or remain in the treated area or an application exclusion zone within the establishment during outdoor pesticide application until the application is complete.

units.actor: appropriately trained and equipped handler involved in the application
units.action_summary: Appropriately trained and equipped handlers involved in the application are excepted from the prohibition in § 170.405(a)(2).

units.obligation_text: The person reports to EPA the submission date; submission type; and case number, transaction ID, or equivalent identifier for the previous submission that contained the substantiation, not later than the deadline specified in § 710.47.
units.action_summary: Report the prior submission's date, type, and identifier to EPA by the § 710.47 deadline.

units.obligation_text: A person substantiating a confidentiality claim for a specific chemical identity must submit answers to the questions in § 710.37(c)(1) and (2), signed and dated by an authorized official, and complete the certification statement in § 710.37(e).
units.actor: A person substantiating a confidentiality claim
units.action_summary: Submit signed and dated answers to § 710.37(c)(1) and (2) and complete the certification statement in § 710.37(e).

units.obligation_text: If any of the information contained in the answers to the questions listed in § 710.37(c)(1) or (2) is claimed as confidential, the submitter must clearly indicate such by marking the substantiation as confidential business information.
units.action_summary: Mark any information claimed confidential in the substantiation as confidential business information.

units.obligation_text: All persons required to substantiate a confidentiality claim pursuant to § 710.43(a) must submit their substantiation not later than [insert date that is 90 days after effective date of final rule].
units.actor: All persons required to substantiate under § 710.43(a)
units.action_summary: Submit substantiation by the specified deadline (90 days after the effective date).

units.obligation_text: All persons who seek an exemption under § 710.43(b)(2) must submit the information specified in § 710.43(b)(2)(iii) not later than [date that is 90 days after effective date of final rule].
units.actor: All persons seeking an exemption under § 710.43(b)(2)
units.action_summary: Submit the information required for the exemption by the specified deadline.

units.obligation_text: If substantiation required under § 710.43(a) is not submitted to EPA in accordance with the provisions of this subpart, and no exemption under § 710.43(b) applies, EPA will consider the confidentiality claim as deficient, so that the specific chemical identity is not subject to a confidentiality claim.
units.action_summary: If required substantiation is not submitted and no exemption applies, EPA will treat the confidentiality claim as deficient and the chemical identity will not be treated as confidential.

units.obligation_text: EPA may make the information public without further notice to the Notice of Activity Form A submitter.
units.action_summary: EPA is permitted to disclose the information publicly without further notice if substantiation is not submitted and no exemption applies.

units.obligation_text: EPA will accept information submitted under this subpart only if submitted in accordance with § 710.39.
units.actor: Persons submitting information under this subpart
units.action_summary: Submit information in accordance with § 710.39 for EPA to accept it under this subpart.

units.obligation_text: Each person who is subject to this part must retain records that document any information reported to EPA.
units.actor: Each person who is subject to this part
units.action_summary: Retain records documenting information reported to EPA.

units.obligation_text: Records must be retained for a period of 5 years beginning on the last day of the submission period.
units.actor: Each person who is subject to this part
units.action_summary: Keep records for 5 years starting on the last day of the submission period.

units.obligation_text: Except as set forth in this subpart, confidentiality claims for specific chemical identities asserted in Notices of Activity Form A will be reviewed and approved or denied in accordance with the criteria and procedures in 40 CFR part 2, subpart B.
units.action_summary: Review and either approve or deny confidentiality claims according to 40 CFR part 2, subpart B.

units.obligation_text: Except as provided in 40 CFR part 2, subpart B, and section 14 of TSCA, a specific chemical identity that is the subject of an approved confidentiality claim under this subpart will be protected from disclosure for a period of 10 years from the date on which the confidentiality claim was first asserted by any submitter after June 22, 2016.
units.action_summary: Protect approved specific chemical identities from disclosure for 10 years from the first asserted date (subject to cited exceptions).

units.obligation_text: Prior to the expiration of the period, the claimant notifies EPA that the person is withdrawing the confidentiality claim, in which case EPA will not protect the information from disclosure.
units.action_summary: If the claimant notifies EPA they are withdrawing the claim before expiration, EPA will cease to protect the information.

units.obligation_text: If EPA otherwise becomes aware that the information does not qualify for protection from disclosure, in which case EPA will take the actions described in TSCA section 14(g)(2) to notify the claimant of EPA’s intent to disclose the information.
units.action_summary: If EPA determines the information does not qualify for protection, EPA will follow TSCA section 14(g)(2) procedures to notify the claimant of intent to disclose.

units.obligation_text: EPA will periodically update the TSCA Inventory based on the results of the reviews of the confidentiality claims asserted in Notices of Activity Form A.
units.action_summary: Periodically update the TSCA Inventory to reflect review results of confidentiality claims.

units.obligation_text: At the beginning of each calendar year, EPA will publish an annual goal for reviews and the number of reviews completed in the prior year on the Agency website.
units.action_summary: Publish each year an annual review goal and the prior year's number of completed reviews on the Agency website.

units.obligation_text: Determination of annual review goals will take into consideration the number of claims needing review, available resources, and a target completion date for all reviews under this subpart not later than February 19, 2024.
units.action_summary: When setting annual review goals, consider claims needing review, available resources, and aim for completion of all reviews by Feb 19, 2024.

units.obligation_text: If EPA determines that the target completion date in paragraph (d) of this section cannot be met based on the number of claims needing review and the available resources, then EPA will publish a document in the Federal Register announcing the extension of the deadline to complete its review of all confidentiality claims under this subpart for not more than two additional years, together with an explanation of the reasons for the extension.
units.action_summary: If the target completion date cannot be met, publish a Federal Register notice extending the deadline by up to two years and explain the reasons.

title: Procedures for Review of CBI Claims for the Identity of Chemicals on the TSCA Inventory: Revisions to the CBI Substantiation Requirements

units.obligation_text: Comments must be received on or before December 9, 2019.
units.action_summary: Submit comments by December 9, 2019.

units.obligation_text: Submit your comments, identified by docket identification (ID) number EPA–HQ–OPPT–2018–0320, by one of the following methods:
units.action_summary: Submit comments using one of the specified methods and include the docket ID.

units.obligation_text: Federal eRulemaking Portal: https://www.regulations.gov. Follow the online instructions for submitting comments.
units.action_summary: Use the regulations.gov portal and follow its online submission instructions.

units.obligation_text: Do not submit electronically any information you consider to be Confidential Business Information (CBI) or other information whose disclosure is restricted by statute.
units.action_summary: Do not submit CBI or legally restricted information via electronic methods (e.g., regulations.gov or email).

units.obligation_text: Mail: Document Control Office (7407M), Office of Pollution Prevention and Toxics (OPPT), Environmental Protection Agency, 1200 Pennsylvania Ave. NW, Washington, DC 20460–0001.
units.action_summary: Submit comments by mail to the specified EPA Document Control Office address.

units.obligation_text: Hand Delivery: To make special arrangements for hand delivery or delivery of boxed information, please follow the instructions at https://www.epa.gov/dockets/where-send-comments-epa-dockets.
units.action_summary: For hand or boxed deliveries, follow the specified EPA docket instructions to make arrangements.

units.obligation_text: Clearly mark the part or all of the information that you claim to be CBI.
units.action_summary: Identify and mark any portion of submissions claimed as Confidential Business Information.

units.obligation_text: For CBI in a CD–ROM or other electronic media that you mail to EPA, mark the outside of the media as CBI and then identify electronically within the media the specific information that is claimed as CBI.
units.action_summary: When mailing electronic media containing CBI, label the media externally and electronically identify the CBI inside.

units.obligation_text: In addition to one complete version of the comment that includes information claimed as CBI, a copy of the comment that does not contain the information claimed as CBI must be submitted for inclusion in the public docket.
units.action_summary: Provide both a full CBI-containing version and a redacted non-CBI version of comments for the public docket.

units.obligation_text: Information so marked will not be disclosed except in accordance with procedures set forth in 40 CFR part 2, subpart B.
units.action_summary: EPA will not disclose information marked as CBI except pursuant to the procedures in 40 CFR part 2, subpart B.

units.obligation_text: EPA is proposing two additional questions that manufacturers and processors would be required to answer to substantiate certain CBI claims for specific chemical identities.
units.action_summary: Answer two additional substantiation questions regarding reverse engineering when claiming CBI for specific chemical identities.

units.obligation_text: EPA is proposing to require any manufacturer or processor who has already submitted answers to the substantiation questions currently listed in the Active-Inactive Rule at 40 CFR 710.37(c) to supplement their submission by adding answers to the newly proposed questions relating to reverse engineering.
units.actor: manufacturers and processors who previously submitted substantiation
units.action_summary: Supplement previously submitted substantiations by adding answers to the new reverse-engineering questions.
units.modal_raw: is proposing to require (would be required to)

units.obligation_text: Under this supplemental proposed rule, Groups (1) and (3) would be required to submit responses to the two proposed additional substantiation questions.
units.actor: Group (1) and Group (3) reporters (as defined in the preamble)
units.action_summary: Reporters in Groups 1 and 3 must submit responses to the two additional substantiation questions.

units.obligation_text: There would be no additional requirements for Group (2).
units.action_summary: Reporters in Group 2 are not required to submit additional information related to the two new questions.

units.section: 40 CFR part 710 (as proposed to be amended)
units.obligation_text: Under the requirements of the Active-Inactive Rule, as proposed to be amended by this supplemental proposed rule, all reporters who assert a CBI claim for specific chemical identity in their NOA Form B would be required to address the two proposed additional substantiation questions.
units.actor: reporters asserting a CBI claim in NOA Form B
units.action_summary: NOA Form B reporters must answer the two new substantiation questions when asserting CBI for specific chemical identities.

units.obligation_text: Manufacturers and processors who have not yet submitted any substantiation to EPA would be required to submit answers to the two newly proposed substantiation questions at the same time as they submit the rest of their required substantiation.
units.actor: manufacturers and processors who have not yet submitted substantiation
units.action_summary: When submitting substantiation for CBI claims, include answers to the two new reverse-engineering questions together with the rest of the substantiation.

units.obligation_text: For persons substantiating a chemical identity CBI claim asserted in an NOA Form A, if finalized as proposed, EPA’s 2019 Proposed Rule would require that all substantiations be filed not later than 90 days after the effective date of the final rule.
units.actor: persons substantiating CBI claims in NOA Form A
units.action_summary: File all substantiations for NOA Form A within 90 days after the final rule's effective date.
units.modal_raw: would require ... be filed not later than

units.obligation_text: For persons substantiating a chemical identity CBI claim asserted in an NOA Form B, the Active-Inactive Rule requires that all substantiations be submitted within 30 days of submitting the NOA Form B.
units.action_summary: Submit substantiation for NOA Form B within 30 days of the NOA Form B submission.

units.obligation_text: Manufacturers and processors who have already voluntarily submitted substantiation to EPA with an NOA Form A, or who will have submitted substantiation for a chemical identity CBI claim asserted in an NOA Form B before the revisions to 40 CFR 710.37(c) are finalized and go into effect, would be required to supplement their earlier submission with answers to the two new substantiation questions.
units.actor: manufacturers and processors with prior substantiation (NOA Form A or B)
units.action_summary: Supplement previously submitted substantiations with answers to the two new questions when the rule is finalized.

units.obligation_text: EPA is proposing to require submission of the supplemental substantiation by not later than 90 days after the effective date of the final rule.
units.actor: persons with NOA Form A prior substantiations (to be supplemented)
units.action_summary: Submit the supplemental (amended) substantiation for NOA Form A reporters within 90 days after the final rule's effective date.
units.modal_raw: is proposing to require ... by not later than

units.obligation_text: For persons substantiating a chemical identity CBI claim asserted in an NOA Form B, EPA is proposing to require submission of the supplemental substantiation by not later than 30 days after the effective date of the final rule.
units.actor: persons with NOA Form B prior substantiations (to be supplemented)
units.action_summary: Submit the supplemental (amended) substantiation for NOA Form B reporters within 30 days after the final rule's effective date.
units.modal_raw: is proposing to require ... by not later than

units.obligation_text: A previously submitted substantiation must contain information that is responsive to all substantiation questions in the final rule to relieve the submitter of the requirement to submit a new substantiation.
units.actor: previous submitters seeking exemption from new substantiation
units.action_summary: To qualify for the exemption, an earlier substantiation must fully respond to all substantiation questions in the final rule.

units.obligation_text: Substantiations of specific chemical identity CBI claims that were submitted with CDR submissions in accordance with the substantiation procedures at 40 CFR 711.30(b)(1), or with NOCs in accordance with the substantiation procedures at 40 CFR 720.85(b)(3)(iv), would be deemed by EPA as responsive to all substantiation questions in the amended 40 CFR 710.37(c), and could therefore serve as a basis for the proposed exemption.
units.actor: submitters of CDR submissions and NOCs
units.action_summary: CDR- or NOC-based substantiations will be treated as responsive to the amended 710.37(c) questions and may qualify for exemption from new substantiation.

title: Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA) Chemical Data Reporting Revisions and Small Manufacturer Definition Update for Reporting and Recordkeeping Requirements Under TSCA Section 8(a)

units.obligation_text: A manufacturer (including importer) of a substance is small if its total annual sales, when combined with those of its parent company (if any), are less than $110 million.
units.action_summary: A manufacturer qualifies as a small manufacturer if combined annual sales are under $110 million.

units.obligation_text: However, if the annual production or importation volume of a particular substance at any individual site owned or controlled by the manufacturer or importer is greater than 45,400 kilograms (100,000 lbs), the manufacturer (including importer) will not qualify as small for purposes of reporting on the production or importation of that substance at that site, unless the manufacturer (including importer) qualifies as small under standard (2) of this definition.
units.action_summary: If production/import of a substance at a site exceeds 45,400 kg, the manufacturer does not qualify as small for reporting on that substance at that site, unless it meets standard (2).

units.obligation_text: A manufacturer (including importer) of a substance is small if its total annual sales, when combined with those of its parent company (if any), are less than $11million, regardless of the quantity of substances produced or imported by that manufacturer (including importer).
units.action_summary: A manufacturer qualifies as small if combined annual sales are under $11 million, regardless of production/import quantity.

units.obligation_text: EPA will make use of the Gross Domestic Product deflators, as compiled by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, for purposes of determining the need to adjust the total annual sales values and for determining new sales values when adjustments are made.
units.action_summary: EPA will use GDP deflators to decide when to adjust total annual sales thresholds and to determine new values when adjustments occur.

units.obligation_text: EPA may adjust the total annual sales values whenever the Agency deems it necessary to do so, provided that the Gross Domestic Product deflator has changed more than 20 percent since either the most recent previous change in sales values or the date of promulgation of this rule, whichever is later.
units.action_summary: EPA is permitted to adjust the sales thresholds when the GDP deflator has changed by more than 20% since the last change or promulgation.

units.obligation_text: EPA will provide notification in the Federal Register when changing the total annual sales values.
units.action_summary: When EPA changes sales threshold values it will notify the public in the Federal Register.

units.obligation_text: TSCA section 15(3) makes it unlawful for any person to fail or refuse to submit information required under this part.
units.action_summary: Persons must submit information required under this part; failure or refusal is unlawful.
units.modal_raw: is unlawful to fail or refuse

units.obligation_text: TSCA section 15(3) makes it unlawful for any person to fail to keep, and permit access to, records required by this part.
units.action_summary: Persons must keep and permit access to records required by this part; failing to do so is unlawful.

units.obligation_text: TSCA section 11 allows for inspections to assure compliance.
units.action_summary: Inspections are permitted to ensure compliance with TSCA reporting requirements.

units.obligation_text: The Administrator may by subpoena require the attendance and testimony of witnesses and the production of reports, papers, documents, answers to questions, and other information that the Administrator deems necessary.
units.action_summary: The Administrator is authorized to compel witnesses and the production of documents by subpoena.

units.obligation_text: The following groups or categories of chemical substances are exempted from some or all of the reporting requirements of this part
units.actor: chemical substances in the listed groups or categories
units.action_summary: Specified groups/categories of chemical substances are exempt from some or all reporting requirements.

units.obligation_text: A chemical substance described in paragraph (a)(1), (a)(2), or (a)(4), or (b) of this section is not exempted from any of the reporting requirements of this part if that chemical substance is the subject of a rule proposed or promulgated under TSCA sections 4, 5(a)(2), 5(b)(4), or 6, or is the subject of an enforceable consent agreement (ECA) ... or is the subject of an order issued under TSCA sections 4, 5(e), or 5(f), or is the subject of relief that has been granted under a civil action under TSCA sections 5 or 7.
units.actor: chemical substances described in those paragraphs
units.action_summary: Even if nominally exempt, a chemical substance is not exempt from reporting if it is subject to specified TSCA rules, orders, agreements, or court-granted relief.

units.obligation_text: Any person who manufactured (including imported) for commercial purposes 25,000 lb (11,340 kg) or more of a chemical substance described in § 711.5 at any single site owned or controlled by that person during any calendar year since the last principal reporting year.
units.action_summary: Persons who manufactured or imported 25,000 lb or more of a listed chemical substance at a single site during a calendar year are subject to recurring reporting.

units.obligation_text: Any person who manufactured (including imported) for commercial purposes any chemical substance that is the subject of a rule proposed or promulgated under TSCA sections 5(a)(2), 5(b)(4), or 6, or is the subject of an order in effect under TSCA sections 4, 5(e) or 5(f), or is the subject of relief that has been granted under a civil action under TSCA sections 5 or 7 is subject to reporting as described in § 711.8(a), except that the applicable production volume threshold is 2,500 lb (1,134 kg).
units.actor: any person manufacturing/importing substances subject to specified rules/orders/actions
units.action_summary: For substances subject to certain TSCA actions, reporting applies but the production threshold is lowered to 2,500 lb.

units.obligation_text: A person described in § 711.8 is not subject to the requirements of this part if that person qualifies as a small manufacturer or small government as those terms are defined in 40 CFR 704.3.
units.action_summary: Persons meeting § 711.8 are exempt from this part if they qualify as a small manufacturer or small government per 40 CFR 704.3.

units.obligation_text: Notwithstanding this exclusion, a person who qualifies as a small manufacturer or small government is subject to this part with respect to any chemical substance that is the subject of a rule proposed or promulgated under TSCA sections 4, 5(b)(4), or 6, or is the subject of an order in effect under TSCA sections 4 or 5(e), or is the subject of relief that has been granted under a civil action under TSCA sections 5 or 7.
units.actor: a person who qualifies as a small manufacturer or small government
units.action_summary: Small manufacturers/governments are still subject to reporting for chemical substances that are subject to specified TSCA rules, orders, or court-granted relief.

units.obligation_text: A person described in § 711.8 is not subject to the requirements of this part with respect to any chemical substance described in § 711.5, when: (then enumerated conditions apply).
units.action_summary: Persons meeting § 711.8 are exempt from reporting for substances in § 711.5 under certain enumerated circumstances.

units.obligation_text: The person manufactured or imported the chemical substance solely in small quantities for research and development.
units.action_summary: Reporting is not required if the substance was made/imported only in small quantities for R&D.

units.obligation_text: The person imported the chemical substance as part of an article.
units.action_summary: Reporting is not required for chemical substances imported as part of an article.

units.obligation_text: Any byproduct if its only commercial purpose is for use by public or private organizations that (i) burn it as a fuel, (ii) dispose of it as a waste, including in a landfill or for enriching soil, or (iii) extract component chemical substances from it for commercial purposes. (This exclusion only applies to the byproduct; it does not apply to the component substances extracted from the byproduct.)
units.action_summary: Byproducts intended only for burning, disposal, or component extraction are exempt from reporting; extracted components are not exempt.

units.obligation_text: Byproduct substances listed in subparagraph (i) for the following manufacturing processes, when recycled or otherwise used within a site-limited, physically enclosed system that is part of the same overall manufacturing process from which the byproduct substance was generated, and when the site is reporting the byproduct or a different chemical substance that was manufactured from the recycled byproduct or manufactured in the same overall manufacturing process.
units.action_summary: Certain listed byproduct substances are exempt from reporting when recycled/used within an enclosed, site-limited system and reported appropriately.

units.obligation_text: Any person may request that EPA amend the chemical substance list in paragraph (c)(2)(i) of this section. Your request must be in writing and must be submitted to the address provided in 40 CFR 700.17(a). Please label your request as follows: Attention: TSCA Chemical Data Reporting—Byproduct Exemption Request. Requests must identify the manufacturing process and byproduct chemical substance in question, as well as its CASRN or other chemical identification number as identified in § 711.15(b)(3)(i), and must contain a written rationale for the request that provides sufficient specific information, addressing the considerations listed in (c)(2)(ii)(B) of this section, including cites and relevant documents, to demonstrate to EPA that the byproduct substance and process in question either does or does not meet the criteria explained in paragraph (c)(2) of this section. If a request related to a particular byproduct substance and process is resubmitted, any subsequent request must clearly identify new information contained in the request. EPA may request other information that it believes necessary to evaluate the request. EPA will issue a written response to each request within 120 days of receipt of the request and will maintain copies of these responses in a docket that will be established for each reporting cycle.
units.action_summary: Any person may request EPA amend the byproduct exemption list; requests must be written, include specified information, and follow labeling; EPA may request more info, will respond within 120 days and maintain responses in a docket.

units.obligation_text: In making its determination of whether this exemption should apply to a particular manufacturing process and related byproduct substance, EPA will consider the totality of information available for the process and related byproduct substance in question, including but not limited to, one or more of the following considerations:
units.action_summary: EPA will consider the totality of available information and listed considerations when deciding on byproduct exemption requests.

units.obligation_text: Whether the byproduct substance is recycled or otherwise used to manufacture another chemical substance within an enclosed system, within the same overall manufacturing process, and on the same site as that byproduct was originally manufactured.
units.action_summary: EPA will consider if the byproduct is recycled/used within an enclosed, same-process, same-site system.

units.obligation_text: Whether the site is reporting under CDR other chemical substances, in particular a chemical substance other than the byproduct substance that was manufactured from the byproduct or manufactured in the same overall manufacturing process.
units.action_summary: EPA will consider if the site reports other chemical substances, especially those made from the byproduct or in the same process.

units.obligation_text: Whether EPA has a current interest in the byproduct substance.
units.action_summary: EPA will consider whether it currently has an interest in the byproduct substance.

units.obligation_text: That the byproduct substance must have already been reported under CDR or would be expected to be reported if not exempted by this exemption.
units.action_summary: EPA will consider whether the byproduct has already been or would be reported under CDR absent the exemption.

units.obligation_text: As needed, the Agency will initiate rulemaking to make revisions to the list of substances in paragraph (c)(2)(i) of this section.
units.action_summary: EPA may initiate rulemaking to revise the list of exempted byproduct substances when needed.

units.obligation_text: To assist EPA in reaching a decision regarding a particular request prior to a given principal reporting year, requests must be submitted to EPA no later than 12 months prior to the start of the next principal reporting year.
units.action_summary: Requests to amend the byproduct exemption list must be submitted at least 12 months before the next principal reporting year.

units.obligation_text: A quantity of the byproduct that is manufactured solely in the following equipment when it is not integral to the chemical manufacturing processes of the site:
units.action_summary: Byproducts manufactured solely in certain non-integral equipment are exempt from reporting.

units.obligation_text: Pollution control equipment.
units.action_summary: Byproduct made solely in pollution control equipment is exempt from reporting.
units.modal_raw: is exempt when manufactured solely in

units.obligation_text: Boilers used to generate heat or electricity for that site.
units.action_summary: Byproduct manufactured solely in boilers used to generate heat/electricity for the site is exempt.
units.modal_raw: is exempt when manufactured solely in

units.obligation_text: Any impurity.
units.action_summary: Impurities are exempt from reporting.

units.obligation_text: Any byproduct which is not used for commercial purposes.
units.action_summary: Byproducts not used for commercial purposes are exempt from reporting.

units.obligation_text: Any chemical substance which results from a chemical reaction that occurs incidental to exposure of another chemical substance, mixture, or article to environmental factors such as air, moisture, microbial organisms, or sunlight.
units.action_summary: Substances formed incidentally by environmental exposure are exempt from reporting.

units.obligation_text: Any chemical substance which results from a chemical reaction that occurs incidental to storage or disposal of another chemical substance, mixture, or article.
units.action_summary: Substances formed incidentally during storage or disposal are exempt from reporting.

units.obligation_text: Any chemical substance which results from a chemical reaction that occurs upon end use of another chemical substance, mixture, or article ... and which is not itself manufactured or imported for distribution in commerce or for use as an intermediate.
units.action_summary: Substances formed upon end use that are not themselves distributed in commerce are exempt from reporting.

units.obligation_text: Any chemical substance which results from a chemical reaction that occurs upon use of curable plastic or rubber molding compounds, inks, drying oils, metal finishing compounds, adhesives, or paints, or any other chemical substance formed during the manufacture of an article destined for the marketplace without further chemical change of the chemical substance except for those chemical changes that occur as described elsewhere in this paragraph.
units.action_summary: Certain substances formed during manufacture of articles that are not further chemically changed are exempt from reporting.

units.obligation_text: Any chemical substance which results from a chemical reaction that occurs when (A) a stabilizer, colorant, odorant, ... functions as intended, or (B) a chemical substance, which is intended solely to impart a specific physiochemical characteristic, functions as intended.
units.action_summary: Substances formed when additives/functioning-intended chemicals perform their intended role are exempt from reporting.

units.obligation_text: Any nonisolated intermediate.
units.action_summary: Nonisolated intermediates are exempt from reporting.

units.obligation_text: Any person who must report under this part, as described in § 711.8, must submit the information described in this section for each chemical substance described in § 711.5 that the person manufactured (including imported) for commercial purposes in an amount of 25,000 lb (11,340 kg) or more (or in an amount of 2,500 lb (1,134 kg) or more for chemical substances subject to the rules, orders, or actions described in § 711.8(b)) at any one site during any calendar year since the last principal reporting year.
units.actor: any person who must report under this part
units.action_summary: Persons subject to reporting must submit specified information for each chemical substance meeting the production/import thresholds at a site during the reporting period.

units.obligation_text: For all submission periods, a separate report must be submitted for each chemical substance at each site for which the submitter is required to report.
units.action_summary: A separate report is required for each chemical substance at each site.

units.obligation_text: Any person who reports information to EPA must complete a Form U using the e-CDRweb reporting tool provided by EPA at the address set forth in § 711.35.
units.actor: any person who reports information to EPA
units.action_summary: Reporters are required to complete a Form U via the e-CDRweb tool at the specified address.

units.obligation_text: The submission must include all information described in paragraph (b) of this section.
units.action_summary: Submissions must contain all information required in paragraph (b).

units.obligation_text: Persons must submit the chemical reports on a separate single Form U for each site for which the person is required to report.
units.action_summary: Each site requires its own single Form U submission for each chemical report.

units.obligation_text: A submitter of information under this part must report information as described in this section to the extent that such information is known to or reasonably ascertainable by that person.
units.action_summary: Submitters must provide information known or reasonably ascertainable to them.

units.obligation_text: The information described in paragraphs (b)(1), (b)(2), (b)(3), and (b)(4) of this section must be reported for each chemical substance manufactured (including imported) in an amount of 25,000 lb (11,340 kg) or more (or in an amount of 2,500 lb (1,134 kg) or more for chemical substances subject to the rules, orders, or actions described in § 711.8(b)) at any one site during any calendar year since the last principal reporting year.
units.action_summary: Reporters must provide the specific categories of information listed in (b)(1)-(b)(4) when thresholds are met.

units.obligation_text: The requirement to report information described in paragraph (b)(4) of this section is subject to exemption as described in § 711.6.
units.action_summary: Reporting of (b)(4) processing/use information may be exempted per § 711.6.

units.obligation_text: A certification statement signed and dated by an authorized official of the submitter company. The authorized official must certify that the submitted information has been completed in compliance with the requirements of this part and that the confidentiality claims made on the Form U are true and correct. The certification must be signed and dated by the authorized official for the submitter company, and provide that person’s name, official title, and email address.
units.actor: authorized official of the submitter company
units.action_summary: An authorized official must sign and date a certification affirming compliance and correctness of confidentiality claims and provide name, title, and email.

units.obligation_text: The following currently correct company and site information must be reported for each site at which a reportable chemical substance is manufactured (including imported) above the applicable production volume threshold...
units.action_summary: Submitters must report correct company and site information for each affected site.

units.obligation_text: The legal name, address, and Dun and Bradstreet D–U–N–S® (D&B) number for the highest-level parent company located in the United States and, if one exists, the highest-level foreign-based parent company. A submitter under this part must obtain a D&B number for the parent company if none exists and must report using the standardized conventions for the naming of a parent company as provided in the CDR Instructions for Reporting identified in § 711.35.
units.action_summary: Submitters must report parent company name/address/D&B number and obtain a D&B number if none exists, following naming conventions.

units.obligation_text: The name of a person who will serve as technical contact for the submitter company who will be able to answer questions about the information submitted by the company to EPA, and that technical contact person’s full mailing address, telephone number, and email address.
units.action_summary: Submitters must provide a technical contact's name and full contact information.

units.obligation_text: The legal name and full street address of each site. A submitter under this part must include the appropriate D&B number for each site reported, and the county or parish (or other jurisdictional indicator) in which the site is located. A submitter under this part must obtain a D&B number for the site reported if none exists. For a co-manufacturing situation, the contracting company must report both the site controlling the contract and the producing company’s site information.
units.action_summary: Submitters must report each site's legal name/address, D&B number and jurisdiction; obtain D&B if absent; contracting company must report both controlling and producing site info in co-manufacturing situations.

units.obligation_text: The six-digit NAICS code for the site. A submitter under this part must include the appropriate six-digit NAICS code for each site reported.
units.action_summary: Submitters must provide the six-digit NAICS code for each reported site.

units.obligation_text: The following chemical-specific information must be reported for each reportable chemical substance manufactured (including imported) above the applicable production volume threshold...
units.action_summary: Submitters must provide specified chemical-specific information for each reportable chemical substance meeting the thresholds.

units.obligation_text: The specific, currently correct CA Index name as used to list the chemical substance on the TSCA Inventory and the correct corresponding CASRN for each reportable chemical substance at each site. Submitters ... must specify the type of number they are reporting by selecting from among the codes in Table 3 of this paragraph.
units.action_summary: Submitters must report the chemical's CA Index name and CASRN and indicate the type of identifying number using Table 3 codes.

units.obligation_text: Alternately, a submitter under this part may report an inorganic byproduct chemical substance using a designated metal compound category, unless the chemical substance is excluded from reporting in categories.
units.action_summary: Submitters may, as an alternative, report certain inorganic byproduct substances using metal compound category codes unless excluded.

units.obligation_text: For purposes of determining whether any of the thresholds specified in § 711.8 are met for a metal compound category, a submitter must make the threshold determination based on the total amount of all members of the metal compound category manufactured at the site.
units.action_summary: When using a metal compound category, the submitter must determine thresholds based on the total amount of all members of that category at the site.

units.obligation_text: If an importer submitting a report cannot provide the information specified in § 711.15(b)(3)(i) because it is unknown to the importer and claimed as confidential by the supplier of the chemical substance or mixture, the importer must use e-CDRweb to ask the supplier to provide the correct chemical identity and, in the case of a mixture, chemical function information directly to EPA in a joint submission. Such request must include instructions for submitting chemical identity information electronically, using e-CDRweb and CDX (see § 711.35), and for clearly referencing the importer’s submission. Contact information for the supplier, a trade name or other designation for the chemical substance or mixture, and a copy of the request to the supplier must be included with the importer’s submission.
units.action_summary: If importer cannot provide chemical identity because supplier claims confidentiality, importer must request supplier to submit identity via e-CDRweb as a joint submission and include specified instructions and contact info with its submission.

units.obligation_text: If a manufacturer submitting a report cannot provide the information specified in § 711.15(b)(3)(i) because the reportable chemical substance is manufactured using a reactant having a specific chemical identity that is unknown to the manufacturer and claimed as confidential by its supplier, the manufacturer must use e-CDRweb to ask the supplier of the confidential reactant to provide the correct chemical identity of the confidential reactant directly to EPA in a joint submission. Such request must include instructions for submitting chemical identity information electronically using e-CDRweb and CDX (see § 711.35), and for clearly referencing the manufacturer’s submission. Contact information for the supplier, a trade name or other designation for the chemical substance, and a copy of the request to the supplier must be included with the importer’s submission.
units.action_summary: If a manufacturer lacks identity of a confidential reactant, it must use e-CDRweb to request the supplier to submit the identity directly to EPA, including specified instructions and contact info.

units.obligation_text: EPA will only accept joint submissions that are submitted electronically using e-CDRweb and CDX (see § 711.35) and that clearly reference the primary submission to which they refer.
units.action_summary: EPA will accept joint submissions only if submitted electronically via e-CDRweb/CDX and clearly reference the primary submission.

units.obligation_text: For the principal reporting year only, a statement indicating, for each reportable chemical substance at each site, whether the chemical substance is manufactured in the United States, imported into the United States, or both manufactured in the United States and imported into the United States.
units.action_summary: For the principal reporting year, submitters must state whether each chemical substance is manufactured domestically, imported, or both.

units.obligation_text: For the principal reporting year, the total annual volume (in pounds) of each reportable chemical substance domestically manufactured or imported at each site. The total annual domestically manufactured volume (not including imported volume) and the total annual imported volume must be separately reported. These amounts must be reported to two significant figures of accuracy. In addition, the total annual volume (domestically manufactured plus imported volumes in pounds) of each reportable chemical substance at each site for each complete calendar year since the last principal reporting year.
units.action_summary: Submitters must report total annual domestic and imported volumes for the principal reporting year (separately) to two significant figures and total annual volumes for each complete calendar year since the last principal reporting year.

units.obligation_text: For the principal reporting year only, the volume used on site and the volume directly exported of each reportable chemical substance domestically manufactured or imported at each site. These amounts must be reported to two significant figures of accuracy.
units.action_summary: Submitters must report volumes used on-site and directly exported for the principal reporting year to two significant figures.

units.obligation_text: For the principal reporting year only, a designation indicating, for each imported reportable chemical substance at each site, whether the imported chemical substance is physically present at the reporting site.
units.action_summary: For imported substances, submitters must indicate whether the imported substance is physically present at the reporting site for the principal reporting year.

units.obligation_text: For the principal reporting year only, the percentage, rounded off to the closest 10 percent, of total production volume of the reportable chemical substance, for each reportable chemical substance at each site, that is manufactured as a byproduct at the site. Where this percentage accounts for less than 5 percent of the total production volume of the reportable chemical substance, submitters instead must report the percentage, rounded off to the closest 1 percent.
units.action_summary: Submitters must report the percent of production that is byproduct, rounded to nearest 10% (or to nearest 1% if under 5%).

units.obligation_text: For the principal reporting year only, a designation indicating, for each reportable chemical substance at each site, whether the chemical substance is being recycled or otherwise used for a commercial purpose instead of being disposed of as a waste or included in a waste stream.
units.action_summary: Submitters must indicate whether each chemical is being recycled/used commercially rather than disposed.

units.obligation_text: For the principal reporting year only, the total number of workers reasonably likely to be exposed to each reportable chemical substance at each site. For each reportable chemical substance at each site, the submitter must select from among the ranges of workers listed in Table 5 of this paragraph and report the corresponding code (i.e., W1 through W8).
units.action_summary: Submitters must report the number-of-workers-exposed using codes W1-W8 for each reportable chemical at each site for the principal reporting year.

units.obligation_text: For the principal reporting year only, the maximum concentration, measured by percentage of weight, of each reportable chemical substance at the time it is sent off-site from each site. ... For each chemical substance at each site, select the maximum concentration of the chemical substance from among the ranges listed in Table 6 of this paragraph and report the corresponding code (i.e., M1 through M5).
units.action_summary: Submitters must report maximum concentration by weight for each chemical when sent off-site and report corresponding code M1-M5.

units.obligation_text: For the principal reporting year only, the physical form(s) of the reportable chemical substance as it is sent off-site from each site. ... For each chemical substance at each site, the submitter must report as many physical forms as applicable from among the physical forms listed in this unit.
units.action_summary: Submitters must report applicable physical forms (e.g., dry powder, liquid, gas) for each chemical when sent off-site for the principal reporting year.

units.obligation_text: For the principal reporting year only, submitters must report the percentage, rounded off to the closest 10 percent, of total production volume of the reportable chemical substance, reported in response to paragraph (b)(3)(iv) of this section, that is associated with each physical form reported under paragraph (b)(3)(x) of this section.
units.action_summary: Submitters must report percentages of production associated with each physical form, rounded to nearest 10%.

units.obligation_text: Chemical-specific information related to processing and use. The following chemical-specific information must be reported for each reportable chemical substance manufactured (including imported) above the applicable production volume threshold, as described in this section. Persons subject to paragraph (b)(4) of this section must report the information described in paragraphs (b)(4)(i) and (b)(4)(ii) of this section for each reportable chemical substance at sites under their control and at sites that receive a reportable chemical substance from the submitter directly or indirectly (including through a broker/distributor, from a customer of the submitter, etc.). Information reported in response to this paragraph must be reported for the principal reporting year only and only to the extent that it is known to or reasonably ascertainable by the submitter. If information responsive to a given data requirement under this paragraph, including information in the form of an estimate, is not known or reasonably ascertainable, the submitter is not required to respond to the requirement. Information required to be reported under this paragraph is limited to domestic (i.e., within the customs territory of the United States) processing and use activities.
units.action_summary: Submitters must report processing/use information for each reportable chemical at controlled sites and recipient sites for the principal reporting year, but only to the extent known or reasonably ascertainable; if not known, they are not required to respond.
units.modal_raw: must / is not required (if not known)

units.obligation_text: A designation indicating the type of industrial processing or use operation(s) at each site that receives a reportable chemical substance from the submitter site directly or indirectly ... For each chemical substance, report the letters which correspond to the appropriate processing or use operation(s) listed in Table 7 of this paragraph.
units.action_summary: Submitters must designate the type(s) of industrial processing or use operations for recipient sites by reporting the corresponding Table 7 letter codes for each chemical.

units.obligation_text: Requests must identify the manufacturing process and byproduct chemical substance in question, as well as its CASRN or other chemical identification number as identified in § 711.15(b)(3)(i), and must contain a written rationale for the request that provides sufficient specific information, addressing the considerations listed in (c)(2)(ii)(B) of this section, including cites and relevant documents, to demonstrate to EPA that the byproduct substance and process in question either does or does not meet the criteria explained in paragraph (c)(2) of this section.
units.action_summary: Requests to amend the byproduct exemption list must identify process and byproduct (including CASRN) and include a written rationale addressing specified considerations and supporting documents.

ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION AGENCY

RIN 2070-AK34

Regulation of Persistent, Bioaccumulative, and Toxic Chemicals 
Under TSCA Section 6(h); Extension of Comment Period

AGENCY: Environmental Protection Agency (EPA).

ACTION: Notice; extension of comment period.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------

SUMMARY: In the Federal Register of July 29, 2019, EPA proposed a rule 
concerning certain persistent, bioaccumulative, and toxic chemicals 
identified pursuant to section 6(h) of the Toxic Substances Control Act 
(TSCA). These five chemicals are: decabromodiphenyl ether; phenol, 
isopropylated phosphate (3:1), also known as tris(4-isopropylphenyl) 
phosphate; 2,4,6-tris(tert-butyl)phenol; hexachlorobutadiene; and 
pentachlorothiophenol. The proposed rule, if finalized, would restrict 
or prohibit manufacture (including import), processing, and 
distribution in commerce for many uses of four of these five chemical 
substances. EPA evaluated the uses of hexachlorobutadiene and proposed 
no regulatory action. For the other four, the proposal included 
recordkeeping requirements. Additional downstream notification 
requirements were proposed for phenol, isopropylated phosphate (3:1). 
This document extends the comment period for 31 days, from September 
27, 2019, to October 28, 2019.

DATES: Comments, identified by docket identification (ID) number EPA-
HQ-OPPT-2019-0080 must be received on or before October 28, 2019.

ADDRESSES: Follow the detailed instructions provided under ADDRESSES in 
the Federal Register document of July 29, 2019 (84 FR 36728) (FRL-9995-
76).

FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT: For technical information contact: 
Cindy Wheeler, Chemical Control Division (7405M), Office of Pollution 
Prevention and Toxics, Environmental Protection Agency, 1200 
Pennsylvania Ave. NW, Washington, DC 20460-0001; telephone number: 202-
566-0484; email address: 
wheeler.cindy@epa.gov
; or Peter Gimlin, 
National Program Chemicals Division, Office of Pollution Prevention and 
Toxics, Environmental Protection Agency, 1200 Pennsylvania Ave. NW, 
Washington, DC 20460-0001; telephone number: 202-566-0515; email 
address: 
gimlin.peter@epa.gov
.
    For general information contact: The TSCA-Hotline, ABVI-Goodwill, 
422 South Clinton Ave., Rochester, NY 14620; telephone number: (202) 
554-1404; email address: 
TSCA-Hotline@epa.gov
.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: This document extends the public comment 
period established in the Federal Register document of July 29, 2019 
(84 FR 36728) (FRL-9995-76). In that document, EPA proposed a rule 
concerning certain persistent, bioaccumulative, and toxic chemicals 
identified pursuant to section 6(h) of the Toxic Substances Control Act 
(TSCA). These five chemicals are: decabromodiphenyl ether; phenol, 
isopropylated phosphate (3:1), also known as tris(4-isopropylphenyl) 
phosphate; 2,4,6-tris(tert-butyl)phenol; hexachlorobutadiene; and 
pentachlorothiophenol. The proposed rule, if finalized, would restrict 
or prohibit manufacture (including import), processing, and 
distribution in commerce for many uses of four of these five chemical 
substances. EPA evaluated the uses of hexachlorobutadiene and proposed 
no regulatory action. For the other four, the proposal included 
recordkeeping requirements. Additional downstream notification 
requirements were proposed for phenol, isopropylated phosphate (3:1). 
More information on EPA's proposal can be found in the July 29, 2019 
Federal Register document (84 FR 36728) (FRL-9995-76).
    This document extends the comment period for 31 days, from 
September 27, 2019, to October 28, 2019. A lengthier extension of the 
comment period was requested. EPA agrees that an extension of the 
comment period is warranted, given the fact that the proposal and the 
extensive supporting materials address five separate chemical 
substances. However, in view of the statutory deadline requiring final 
action 18 months after issuance of the proposal and the considerable 
outreach EPA

a 31-day extension is sufficient.
