units.obligation_text: CWA section 303(c) directs states to adopt WQS for their waters subject to the CWA.
units.action_summary: Requires states to adopt water quality standards for waters subject to the Clean Water Act.

units.obligation_text: CWA section 303(c)(2)(A) provides that WQS shall consist of the designated uses of the waters and water quality criteria based on those uses.
units.action_summary: Requires states' water quality standards to include designated uses and criteria based on those uses.

units.obligation_text: Such criteria must be based on sound scientific rationale and must contain sufficient parameters or constituents to protect the designated use; for waters with multiple use designations, the criteria shall support the most sensitive use.
units.action_summary: Requires criteria be scientifically justified, include sufficient parameters to protect designated uses, and support the most sensitive use where multiple uses exist.

units.obligation_text: In designating uses of a water body and the appropriate criteria for those uses, the state shall take into consideration the water quality standards of downstream waters and shall ensure that its water quality standards provide for the attainment and maintenance of the water quality standards of downstream waters.
units.action_summary: Requires the state to consider downstream water quality standards and ensure its standards allow attainment and maintenance of downstream standards.

units.obligation_text: States are required to review applicable WQS at least once every three years and, if appropriate, revise or adopt new WQS.
units.action_summary: Obligates states to review water quality standards at least once every three years and revise/adopt as appropriate.

units.obligation_text: Any new or revised WQS must be submitted to the EPA for review and approval or disapproval.
units.action_summary: Requires states to submit new or revised water quality standards to EPA for review.

units.obligation_text: If the EPA disapproves a state's new or revised WQS, the CWA provides the state 90 days to adopt a revised WQS that meets CWA requirements.
units.action_summary: Requires the state to adopt revised water quality standards that meet CWA requirements within 90 days after EPA disapproval.

units.obligation_text: If the state fails to adopt revised WQS within 90 days after notification, the Administrator shall promptly prepare and publish proposed regulations setting forth a revised or new water quality standard and shall promulgate any revised or new standard not later than ninety days after he publishes such proposed standards, unless the State adopts a replacement standard first.
units.action_summary: Obligates the Administrator to propose and, if necessary, promulgate federal WQS within specified timelines when a state fails to timely adopt approved revisions.

units.obligation_text: Where the EPA has published recommended criteria, states should establish numeric water quality criteria based on the Agency’s CWA section 304(a) recommended criteria, CWA section 304(a) recommended criteria modified to reflect site-specific conditions, or other scientifically defensible methods.
units.action_summary: Advises states to use EPA 304(a) recommendations, modifications for site-specific conditions, or other scientifically defensible methods in establishing numeric criteria.

units.obligation_text: In all cases criteria must be sufficient to protect the designated use and be based on sound scientific rationale.
units.action_summary: Requires that criteria be protective of designated uses and grounded in sound science.

units.obligation_text: Neither value (CMC or CCC) is to be exceeded more than once in three years.
units.action_summary: Prohibits exceeding the acute (CMC) or chronic (CCC) criterion more than once every three years.

units.section: III.B (Proposed Acute and Chronic Aluminum Criteria for Oregon’s Fresh Waters)
units.obligation_text: The proposed CMC and CCC freshwater aluminum criteria values for a site shall be calculated using the 2018 Aluminum Criteria Calculator V.2.0 (Aluminum Criteria Calculator V.2.0.xlsx) or a calculator in R or other software package using the same 1985 Guidelines calculation approach and underlying model equations as in the Aluminum Criteria Calculator V.2.0.xlsx as established in the final 2018 recommended national criteria.
units.actor: the State of Oregon or other users calculating site-specific criteria
units.action_summary: Requires site-specific CMC and CCC values to be calculated using the specified Aluminum Criteria Calculator or equivalent software implementing the same models and approach.

units.obligation_text: The EPA proposes to express the CMC as a one-hour average total recoverable aluminum concentration (in mg/L) and the CCC as a four-day average total recoverable aluminum concentration (in mg/L).
units.action_summary: Specifies how the CMC and CCC should be expressed temporally and in units (one-hour average for CMC; four-day average for CCC; mg/L total recoverable).

units.obligation_text: The CMC and CCC are not to be exceeded more than once every three years.
units.action_summary: Specifies the allowable exceedance frequency for the CMC and CCC (no more than once every three years).

units.obligation_text: Oregon will need to use ambient water chemistry data (i.e., pH, DOC, total hardness) as inputs to the model in order to determine protective aluminum criteria values for specific sites, unless the State develops default values to be used in implementation.
units.action_summary: Requires the State to use ambient pH, DOC, and total hardness data as model inputs to determine site-specific protective criteria unless default values are adopted.

units.obligation_text: Oregon has the discretion to select the appropriate method to reconcile model outputs and calculate the final criteria values for each circumstance
units.action_summary: Permits Oregon to choose how to reconcile model outputs and calculate final criteria values for different circumstances.

units.obligation_text: as long as the resulting calculated criteria values shall protect aquatic life throughout the site and throughout the range of spatial and temporal variability, including when aluminum is most toxic.
units.actor: State of Oregon (and those calculating criteria)
units.action_summary: Requires that any resulting calculated criteria values provide protection for aquatic life across the full spatial and temporal variability, including worst-case toxicity conditions.

units.obligation_text: The EPA strongly recommends that the State develop implementation materials to outline its approach.
units.action_summary: Recommends that the State prepare implementation materials describing its approach to calculating and implementing criteria.

units.obligation_text: The EPA suggests three methods that the State could use to reconcile model outputs and calculate criteria values; alternatively, the State may use its own alternate methods to reconcile outputs to generate protective criteria values.
units.action_summary: Permits the State to use the EPA-suggested methods or other alternate methods to reconcile model outputs to generate protective criteria.

title: National Primary Drinking Water Regulations: Lead and Copper Rule Revisions

units.obligation_text: Find-and-Fix means the requirement in 141.82(j) that water systems must perform at every sampling site that yielded a lead result above the action level (0.015 mg/L).
units.action_summary: Perform Find-and-Fix at every sampling site with lead > 0.015 mg/L.

units.obligation_text: Follow-up sampling results must be provided to the consumer in accordance with § 141.85(d).
units.action_summary: Provide follow-up sampling results to consumers per §141.85(d).

units.obligation_text: Tap sampling protocols may not include any instructions or recommendations for pre-stagnation flushing or removal or cleaning of faucet aerators prior to sample collection.
units.actor: authors of tap sampling protocols (e.g., water systems)
units.action_summary: Tap sampling protocols must not instruct or recommend pre-stagnation flushing or aerator removal/cleaning before sample collection.

units.obligation_text: Wide-mouth bottles for the purpose of subpart I of this part only means bottles configured with a mouth that is at least 55 mm wide, required to be used for lead and copper tap sampling collection to optimize capturing accurate lead measurements.
units.action_summary: Use wide-mouth (≥55 mm) bottles for lead and copper tap sampling.

units.obligation_text: The public water system, within 10 days of completing the public notification requirements under subpart Q of this part for the initial public notice and any repeat notices, must submit to the primacy agency a certification that it has fully complied with the public notification regulations.
units.action_summary: Within 10 days after completing public notification (initial and repeats), submit to the primacy agency a certification of full compliance with public notification rules.

units.obligation_text: For Tier 2 and 3 notices, the public water system must include with this certification a representative copy of each type of notice distributed, published, posted, and made available to the persons served by the system and to the media.
units.action_summary: Include representative copies of each type of Tier 2 and 3 notice with the certification sent to the primacy agency.

units.obligation_text: For Tier 1 notices public water systems must provide a copy of any Tier 1 notice to the Administrator and the head of the Primacy Agency as soon as practicable, but not later than 24 hours after the public water system learns of the violation or exceedance.
units.action_summary: Provide a copy of any Tier 1 notice to the EPA Administrator and the head of the Primacy Agency as soon as practicable and within 24 hours of learning of the violation/exceedance.

units.obligation_text: Community water systems and non-transient, non-community water systems must comply with the requirements of this subpart no later than [DATE THREE YEARS AFTER PUBLICATION OF THE FINAL RULE IN THE Federal Register], except where otherwise specified at §§ 141.81, 141.84, 141.85, 141.86, and 141.90, or where an exemption in accordance with 40 CFR 142 at subpart C or F has been established by the Administrator.
units.actor: community water systems and non-transient, non-community water systems
units.action_summary: Comply with the subpart's requirements by the specified three-year compliance date, subject to listed exceptions and exemptions.

units.obligation_text: Between [DATE 60 DAYS AFTER PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE Federal Register] and [DATE 3 YEARS AFTER PUBLICATION OF THE FINAL RULE IN THE Federal Register], community water systems and non-transient, non-community water systems must comply with 40 CFR 141.80 through 141.90 as promulgated in 56 FR 26548, June 7, 1991; 57 FR 28788, June 29, 1992; 59 FR 33862, June 30, 1994; 65 FR 2004, January 12, 2000; 72 FR 57814, October 10, 2007.
units.actor: community water systems and non-transient, non-community water systems
units.action_summary: During the transition period, comply with 40 CFR 141.80-141.90 as previously promulgated in listed FR publications.

units.obligation_text: If an exemption from Subpart I has been issued in accordance with 40 CFR 142 subpart C or F, then the water systems must comply with 40 CFR 141.80 through 141.90 as promulgated in [earlier FR citations] until the expiration of that exemption.
units.actor: water systems with such an exemption
units.action_summary: Systems with an exemption must comply with the previously promulgated versions of 40 CFR 141.80-141.90 until the exemption expires.

units.obligation_text: All community water systems are subject to sampling for lead in schools and child care facilities and public education requirements regardless of the results of the compliance tap sampling.
units.action_summary: Collect lead samples in schools and child care facilities and comply with public education requirements regardless of compliance sample results.

units.obligation_text: Trigger levels and action levels must be determined based on tap water samples collected in accordance with the monitoring requirements of § 141.86 and tested using the analytical methods specified in § 141.89.
units.action_summary: Determine trigger and action levels using tap samples collected per §141.86 and analyzed using methods in §141.89.

units.obligation_text: For a public water system that has been allowed by the State to collect fewer than five samples in accordance with § 141.86(c), the sample result with the highest concentration is considered the 90th percentile value.
units.action_summary: If the State allows fewer than five samples, treat the highest sample result as the 90th percentile.

units.obligation_text: All water systems shall install and operate corrosion control treatment in accordance with §§ 141.81 and 141.82, and that meets the definition of optimal corrosion control treatment at § 141.2 of this chapter.
units.action_summary: Install and operate corrosion control treatment meeting the definition of optimal corrosion control treatment per §§141.81 and 141.82.

units.obligation_text: Any small water system that complies with the applicable small system compliance flexibility requirements specified by the State under § 141.81 and § 141.93 shall be deemed in compliance with the treatment requirement in paragraph (d)(1) of this section.
units.action_summary: Small systems that comply with State-specified small system flexibilities are deemed in compliance with the corrosion control treatment requirement of paragraph (d)(1).

units.obligation_text: Any water system exceeding the lead action level specified at (c) of this section must complete mandatory lead service line replacement. Lead service line replacement must be conducted in accordance with § 141.84 and must include public education pursuant to § 141.85.
units.actor: water systems exceeding the lead action level
units.action_summary: Complete mandatory lead service line replacement per §141.84 and include public education per §141.85 if the lead action level is exceeded.

units.obligation_text: Any water system exceeding the lead trigger level specified at (c) of this section must complete goal-based lead service line replacement pursuant to § 141.84 and public education pursuant to § 141.85.
units.actor: water systems exceeding the lead trigger level
units.action_summary: Complete goal-based lead service line replacement per §141.84 and public education per §141.85 if the lead trigger level is exceeded.

units.obligation_text: All water systems must prepare an inventory of service lines connected to its distribution system, whether or not they are owned or controlled by the water system, to identify those service lines that are made of lead or of unknown material. The inventory must be prepared in accordance with § 141.84(a).
units.action_summary: Prepare a service line inventory (including privately owned lines) to identify lead or unknown-material lines, per §141.84(a).

units.obligation_text: Pursuant to § 141.85(d), all water systems must provide notification of lead tap water monitoring results to persons served at the sites (taps) that are tested.
units.action_summary: Notify persons served at tested taps of lead tap water monitoring results per §141.85(d).

units.obligation_text: Any water system exceeding the lead action level specified at (c) of this section shall implement the public education requirements in accordance with § 141.85(a) and (b).
units.actor: water systems exceeding the lead action level
units.action_summary: Implement public education requirements per §141.85(a) and (b) when the lead action level is exceeded.

units.obligation_text: Any water system exceeding the lead trigger level specified at (c) of this section shall provide notification to all customers with a lead service line in accordance with § 141.85(f).
units.actor: water systems exceeding the lead trigger level
units.action_summary: Notify all customers with lead service lines per §141.85(f) if the lead trigger level is exceeded.

units.obligation_text: Any water system exceeding the lead action level specified at (c) of this section shall notify the public in accordance with the public notification requirements in subpart Q of this part.
units.actor: water systems exceeding the lead action level
units.action_summary: Provide public notification per subpart Q when the lead action level is exceeded.

units.obligation_text: All water systems must collect samples from all schools and child care facilities within its distribution system in accordance with § 141.92.
units.action_summary: Collect lead samples from all schools and child care facilities per §141.92.

units.obligation_text: Failure to comply with the applicable requirements of §§ 141.80 through 141.93, including requirements established by the State pursuant to these provisions, shall constitute a violation of the national primary drinking water regulations for lead and/or copper.
units.action_summary: Noncompliance with §§141.80–141.93 constitutes a violation of the lead and/or copper national primary drinking water regulations.

units.obligation_text: Corrosion control treatment. Water systems shall complete the applicable corrosion control treatment requirements described in § 141.82 by the deadline established in this section.
units.action_summary: Complete applicable corrosion control treatment requirements in §141.82 by the deadlines in §141.81.

units.obligation_text: Large water systems with corrosion control treatment that exceed either the lead trigger level or copper action level shall complete the corrosion control treatment steps specified in paragraph (d) of this section.
units.actor: large water systems with corrosion control treatment
units.action_summary: Complete the corrosion control treatment steps in §141.81(d) if either the lead trigger or copper action level is exceeded.

units.obligation_text: Large water systems without corrosion control treatment that exceed either the lead trigger level or the copper action level shall complete the corrosion control treatment steps specified in paragraph (e) of this section.
units.actor: large water systems without corrosion control treatment
units.action_summary: Complete the corrosion control steps in §141.81(e) if either the lead trigger or copper action level is exceeded.

units.obligation_text: Large water systems with corrosion control treatment that do not exceed the lead trigger level and copper action level but are not deemed to have optimized corrosion control under paragraph (b)(3) of this section may be required by the State to complete the corrosion control treatment steps in paragraph (d) of this section.
units.actor: State (with respect to large water systems)
units.action_summary: The State may require large systems that are not deemed optimized to complete the §141.81(d) corrosion control steps even if they do not exceed trigger/action levels.

units.obligation_text: Large water systems without corrosion control treatment that do not exceed the lead trigger level and copper action level but are not deemed to have optimized corrosion control under paragraph (b)(3) of this section may be required by the State to complete the corrosion control treatment steps in paragraph (e) of this section.
units.actor: State (with respect to large water systems)
units.action_summary: The State may require large systems without treatment that are not deemed optimized to complete §141.81(e) steps even if they do not exceed trigger/action levels.

units.obligation_text: Medium-size water systems with corrosion control treatment that exceed either the lead trigger level or copper action level shall complete the corrosion control treatment steps specified in paragraph (d) of this section.
units.actor: medium-size water systems with corrosion control treatment
units.action_summary: If either lead trigger or copper action level is exceeded, medium-size systems with treatment must complete the §141.81(d) steps.

units.obligation_text: Medium-size water systems without corrosion control treatment that exceed either the lead or copper action level shall complete the corrosion control treatment steps specified in paragraph (e) of this section.
units.actor: medium-size water systems without corrosion control treatment
units.action_summary: Medium-size systems without treatment that exceed action levels must complete §141.81(e) steps.

units.obligation_text: Medium-size water systems without corrosion control treatment that exceed the lead trigger level shall complete the treatment recommendation steps specified in paragraph (e) of this section.
units.actor: medium-size water systems without corrosion control treatment
units.action_summary: Complete the treatment recommendation steps in §141.81(e) when the lead trigger level is exceeded.

units.obligation_text: The water system shall complete the remaining steps in paragraph (e) of this section if it subsequently exceeds either the lead or copper action level.
units.action_summary: If the system subsequently exceeds either action level, it must complete the remaining §141.81(e) steps.

units.obligation_text: Small water systems with corrosion control treatment that exceed either the lead trigger level or copper action level shall complete the corrosion control treatment steps specified in paragraph (d) of this section.
units.actor: small water systems with corrosion control treatment
units.action_summary: Small systems with treatment that exceed trigger or action levels must complete §141.81(d) steps.

units.obligation_text: Small water systems without corrosion control treatment that exceed either the lead or copper action level shall complete the corrosion control treatment steps specified in paragraph (e) of this section.
units.actor: small water systems without corrosion control treatment
units.action_summary: Small systems without treatment that exceed action levels must complete §141.81(e) steps.

units.obligation_text: Small water systems without corrosion control treatment that exceed the lead trigger level shall complete the treatment recommendation steps specified in paragraph (e) of this section.
units.actor: small water systems without corrosion control treatment
units.action_summary: Small systems without treatment that exceed the lead trigger must complete treatment recommendation steps in §141.81(e).

units.obligation_text: The water system shall complete the remaining steps in paragraph (e) of this section, if it subsequently exceeds either the lead or copper action level.
units.action_summary: If the small system later exceeds either action level, it must complete the remaining §141.81(e) steps.

units.obligation_text: Any such system deemed to have optimized corrosion control under this paragraph and which has treatment in place shall continue to operate and maintain optimal corrosion control treatment and meet any requirements that the State determines to be appropriate to ensure optimal corrosion control treatment is maintained.
units.actor: systems deemed to have optimized corrosion control and which have treatment in place
units.action_summary: Continue to operate and maintain optimal corrosion control treatment and meet State-required measures to ensure maintenance.

units.obligation_text: Any small community water system or Non-transient Non-community water system selecting a small system option under paragraph (b)(4) of this section shall follow the schedule for that small system option under § 141.81(f).
units.actor: small community water systems or non-transient non-community water systems selecting a small system option
units.action_summary: Follow the schedule for the selected small system option under §141.81(f).

units.obligation_text: Water systems without corrosion control treatment must complete the treatment recommendation step to be deemed optimized under this section.
units.actor: water systems without corrosion control treatment
units.action_summary: Complete the treatment recommendation step to achieve 'deemed optimized' status.

units.obligation_text: Water systems with corrosion control treatment are deemed optimized or re-optimized if the system meets the requirements of this section and the State has not required the system to meet optimal water quality parameters and monitor under § 141.87(d).
units.actor: water systems with corrosion control treatment
units.action_summary: Systems meeting the section's requirements and not required by the State to meet §141.87(d) parameters are deemed optimized or re-optimized.

units.obligation_text: Any water system deemed to have optimized or re-optimized corrosion control in accordance with this paragraph shall continue monitoring for lead and copper at the tap no less frequently than once every three calendar years using the reduced number of sites specified in § 141.86(c) and collecting samples at times and locations specified in § 141.86(d)(4)(iv).
units.actor: water systems deemed to have optimized or re-optimized
units.action_summary: Continue tap monitoring for lead/copper at least once every three years using reduced sites and specified sampling times/locations.

units.obligation_text: Any water system deemed to have optimized or re-optimized corrosion control pursuant to this paragraph shall notify the State in writing pursuant to § 141.90(a)(3) of any upcoming long-term change in treatment or addition of a new source as described in § 141.90.
units.actor: water systems deemed to have optimized or re-optimized
units.action_summary: Notify the State in writing of any upcoming long-term treatment changes or addition of a new source per §141.90(a)(3).

units.obligation_text: The State must review and approve the addition of a new source or long-term change in water treatment before it is implemented by the water system.
units.action_summary: Review and approve proposed new sources or long-term treatment changes before implementation.

units.obligation_text: The State may require any such water system to conduct additional monitoring or to take other action the State deems appropriate to ensure that such water system maintains minimal levels of corrosion control in its distribution system.
units.action_summary: State may require additional monitoring or other actions to ensure continued corrosion control when approving changes.

units.obligation_text: A water system is not deemed to have optimized or re-optimized corrosion control under this paragraph and shall implement corrosion control treatment pursuant to (b)(3)(v) of this section unless it meets the copper action level.
units.action_summary: If the system does not meet the copper action level, it is not deemed optimized and must implement corrosion control treatment per (b)(3)(v).

units.obligation_text: Any water system triggered into corrosion control because it is no longer deemed to have optimized or re-optimized corrosion control under this paragraph shall implement corrosion control treatment in accordance with the deadlines in paragraph (d) or (e) of this section. The time period for completing each step shall be triggered by the date the sampling was conducted showing that the water system no longer meets the requirements to be deemed to have optimized or re-optimized corrosion control under this paragraph.
units.action_summary: Implement corrosion control treatment according to the deadlines in §141.81(d) or (e) when no longer deemed optimized; timelines start from the sample date showing loss of deemed status.

units.obligation_text: Any small system selecting a small system compliance option shall monitor and follow the small system option steps described in § 141.93.
units.actor: small systems selecting a small system compliance option
units.action_summary: Monitor and follow the small system option steps in §141.93.

units.obligation_text: Any small or medium-size water system that is required to complete the corrosion control steps in paragraph (e) of this section due to its exceedance of the lead or copper action level may cease completing the treatment steps after paragraph (e), Step 2 of this section, when the water system meets both action levels during each to two consecutive 6-month monitoring periods conducted pursuant to § 141.86 and submits the results to the State.
units.action_summary: May stop treatment steps after §141.81(e) Step 2 if meeting both action levels for two consecutive 6-month monitoring periods and submitting results to the State.

units.obligation_text: Any such system required to conduct a corrosion control treatment study under paragraph (e), Step 3 of this section, shall complete the study and paragraph (e), Step 4 of this section, unless the water system meets both action levels during each of two consecutive six-month monitoring periods prior to the start of the study.
units.actor: small or medium-size water systems required to conduct the study
units.action_summary: Complete the required corrosion control treatment study and Step 4 unless the system had already met both action levels for two consecutive 6-month periods before the study.

units.obligation_text: If any such water system thereafter exceeds the lead or copper action level during any monitoring period, the water system (or the State) shall recommence completion of the applicable treatment steps, beginning with the first treatment step which was not previously completed in its entirety, and complete all the steps through installation of optimal corrosion control treatment (paragraph (e), Step 5 of this section).
units.action_summary: If the system later exceeds an action level, the system or State must restart and complete the applicable treatment steps through installation of optimal corrosion control treatment.

units.obligation_text: The State may require a water system to repeat treatment steps previously completed by the water system when the State determines that this is necessary to implement the treatment requirements of this section.
units.action_summary: State may require repetition of previously completed treatment steps if necessary to implement treatment requirements.

units.obligation_text: The State shall notify the system in writing of such a determination and explain the basis for its decision.
units.action_summary: If the State requires repetition of steps, it must notify the system in writing and explain the basis.

units.obligation_text: Any small or medium-size water system that is required to complete the corrosion control steps in paragraph (e) of this section due to its exceedance of the lead trigger level may cease completing the treatment steps after paragraph (e), Step 2 of this section.
units.action_summary: Systems required to complete §141.81(e) steps due to a lead trigger exceedance may stop after Step 2 in certain circumstances.

units.obligation_text: Any such system required to conduct a corrosion control treatment study under paragraph (e), Step 3 of this section, shall complete the study and paragraph (e), Step 4 of this section.
units.actor: small or medium-size water systems required to do the study
units.action_summary: If required to perform the treatment study under §141.81(e) Step 3, complete the study and Step 4.

units.obligation_text: If any such water system thereafter exceeds the lead or copper action level during any monitoring period, the water system (or the State) shall recommence completion of the applicable treatment steps, beginning with the first treatment step which was not previously completed in its entirety and complete all the steps through installation of optimal corrosion control treatment paragraph (e), (Step 5) of this section.
units.action_summary: If the system later exceeds an action level, the system or State must restart and finish all applicable treatment steps through installation of optimal corrosion control treatment.

units.obligation_text: Step 1. The water system shall complete the initial tap sampling (§ 141.86(d)(1) and § 141.87(b)) until the water system either exceeds the lead trigger level or copper action level or becomes eligible for reduced monitoring under § 141.86(d)(4)(ii)(A).
units.action_summary: Complete initial tap sampling per §141.86(d)(1) and §141.87(b) until exceeding trigger/action level or qualifying for reduced monitoring.

units.obligation_text: A water system exceeding the lead trigger level or copper action level shall recommend optimal corrosion control treatment (§ 141.82(a)(5) or (6) or (7)) within six months after the end of the monitoring period during which it exceeds either the lead trigger level or copper action level.
units.actor: water system exceeding the lead trigger level or copper action level
units.action_summary: Within six months after the monitoring period when a trigger/action exceedance occurs, recommend optimal corrosion control treatment per §141.82.

units.obligation_text: Large water systems that exceed the lead trigger level or copper action level shall conduct the corrosion control studies for re-optimization under paragraph (d), Step 3 of this section.
units.action_summary: Conduct corrosion control re-optimization studies as described in Step 3 if trigger/action levels are exceeded.

units.obligation_text: Within 12 months after the end of the monitoring period during which a small or medium-size water system with corrosion control treatment exceeds the lead trigger level or copper action level, the State may require the water system to perform corrosion control studies for re-optimization (§ 141.81(d)(2) or (3)).
units.action_summary: Within 12 months after the relevant monitoring period, the State may require small/medium systems with treatment that exceeded trigger/action levels to perform re-optimization studies.

units.obligation_text: If the State does not require the system to perform such studies, the State shall specify re-optimized corrosion control treatment (§ 141.82(d)(3) or (4)) within the following timeframes: For medium-size water systems, within 12 months after the end of the monitoring period during which such water system exceeds the lead trigger level or copper action level.
units.action_summary: If the State does not require studies, it must specify re-optimized corrosion control for medium-size systems within 12 months after the monitoring period in which they exceeded the trigger/action level.

units.obligation_text: If the State does not require the system to perform such studies, the State shall specify re-optimized corrosion control treatment within the following timeframes: For small water systems, within 18 months after the end of the monitoring period during which such water system exceeds the lead trigger level or copper action level.
units.action_summary: If the State does not require studies, it must specify re-optimized corrosion control for small systems within 18 months after the monitoring period in which they exceeded the trigger/action level.

units.obligation_text: Large water systems that exceed the lead trigger level or copper action level shall complete the corrosion control treatment studies for re-optimization within 18 months.
units.action_summary: Complete re-optimization corrosion control studies within 18 months after exceeding trigger/action levels.

units.obligation_text: If the State requires a water system to perform corrosion control studies under paragraph (d), Step 2 of this section, the water system shall complete the studies (§ 141.82(c)(1)) within 18 months after the State requires that such studies be conducted.
units.action_summary: If required by the State, complete the corrosion control studies within 18 months of the State's requirement.

units.obligation_text: The State shall designate re-optimized corrosion control treatment (§ 141.82(d)(3)) within six months after completion of paragraph (d)(3)(i), Step 3 of this section.
units.action_summary: Designate re-optimized corrosion control treatment within six months after completion of the Step 3 studies for large systems.

units.obligation_text: If the water system has performed corrosion control studies under paragraph (d), Step 2 of this section, the State shall designate re-optimized corrosion control treatment (§ 141.82(d)(3) or (4)) within six months after completion of paragraph (d), Step 3(ii) of this section.
units.action_summary: When systems have performed required studies, the State must designate re-optimized corrosion control treatment within six months after the studies are completed.

units.obligation_text: Large water systems shall complete modifications to corrosion control treatment to have re-optimized corrosion control treatment installed within 12 months after completion of paragraph (d), Step 4(i) of this section.
units.action_summary: Complete modifications to install re-optimized corrosion control within 12 months after State designation (Step 4(i)).

units.obligation_text: Small or medium-size water systems that exceed the lead trigger level or copper action level shall install re-optimized corrosion control treatment (§ 141.82(e)(3) or (4)) within 12 months after completion of paragraph (d), Step 4(ii) of this section.
units.actor: small or medium-size water systems that exceed the lead trigger level or copper action level
units.action_summary: Install re-optimized corrosion control treatment within 12 months after State designation for small/medium systems that exceeded trigger/action levels.

units.obligation_text: Water systems shall complete follow-up sampling (§ 141.86(d)(2) and § 141.87(c)) within 12 months after completion of paragraph (d), Step 5(i) or (ii) of this section.
units.action_summary: Complete follow-up sampling within 12 months after installing re-optimized corrosion control treatment.

units.obligation_text: The State shall review the water system’s installation of treatment and designate optimal water quality control parameters (§ 141.82(f)(1)) within six months of completion of paragraph (d)(6), Step 6 of this section.
units.action_summary: Review the system's installed treatment and designate optimal water quality control parameters within six months after follow-up sampling.

units.obligation_text: The water system shall operate in compliance with the State-designated optimal water quality control parameters (§ 141.82(g)(1)) and continue to conduct tap sampling (§ 141.86(d)(3) and water quality parameter monitoring under § 141.87(d)).
units.action_summary: Operate in compliance with State-designated optimal parameters and continue required tap and water quality monitoring.

units.obligation_text: Step 1. The water system shall complete the initial tap sampling (§ 141.86(d)(1) and § 141.87(b)) until the water system either exceeds the lead trigger level or copper action level or becomes eligible for reduced monitoring under § 141.86(d)(4)(i)(A) or (B). A water system exceeding the lead trigger level or copper action level shall recommend optimal corrosion control treatment (§ 141.82(a)(1) or (2) or (3) or (4)) within six months after the end of the monitoring period during which it exceeds either the lead trigger level or copper action level.
units.actor: small and medium-size water systems without corrosion control treatment
units.action_summary: Complete initial tap sampling until exceedance or eligibility for reduced monitoring; if exceedance occurs, recommend optimal corrosion control within six months.

units.obligation_text: Within 12 months after the end of the monitoring period during which a water system exceeds the lead trigger level or copper action level, the State may require the water system to perform corrosion control studies (§ 141.82(b)(1)); the State shall notify the system in writing of this requirement.
units.action_summary: Within 12 months after exceedance, State may require corrosion control studies and must notify the system in writing if it does so.

units.obligation_text: If the State does not require the system to perform such studies, the State shall specify optimal corrosion control treatment (§ 141.82(d)(1) or (2)) within the following timeframes: For medium-size water systems, within 18 months after the end of the monitoring period during which such water system exceeds the lead trigger level or copper action level.
units.action_summary: If the State does not require studies, it must specify optimal corrosion control for medium-size systems within 18 months after the monitoring period in which they exceeded the trigger/action level.

units.obligation_text: If the State does not require the system to perform such studies, the State shall specify optimal corrosion control treatment within the following timeframes: For small water systems, within 24 months after the end of the monitoring period during which such water system exceeds the lead trigger level or copper action level.
units.action_summary: If the State does not require studies, it must specify optimal corrosion control for small systems within 24 months after the monitoring period in which they exceeded the trigger/action level.

units.obligation_text: If the State requires a water system to perform corrosion control studies under paragraph (e), Step 2 of this section, the water system shall complete the studies (§ 141.82(c)(1)) within 18 months after the State notifies the system in writing that such studies must be conducted.
units.action_summary: When the State requires studies and notifies the system in writing, complete the studies within 18 months.

units.obligation_text: If the water system has performed corrosion control studies under paragraph (e), Step 2 of this section, the State shall designate optimal corrosion ...
units.action_summary: When the system has performed the required studies, the State must designate optimal corrosion control treatment (text continues in the regulation).

title: National Primary Drinking Water Regulations: Lead and Copper
Public Hearings: Revised Definition of "Waters of the United States"

units.obligation_text: All submissions received must include the Docket ID No. for this rulemaking.
units.action_summary: Submitters must include the docket identification number with their submissions.

units.obligation_text: Comments received may be posted without change to https://www.regulations.gov/, including any personal information provided.
units.action_summary: The agencies may post received comments publicly, without changes, including personal information.

units.obligation_text: The public is invited to speak during the public hearing on February 27 and 28, 2019.
units.action_summary: Members of the public are permitted/invited to speak at the public hearing on the listed dates.

units.obligation_text: Those interested in speaking at the hearing can sign up for a three-minute speaking slot within an identified 45-minute timeframe.
units.action_summary: Interested speakers may register for a three-minute speaking slot during designated 45-minute periods.

units.obligation_text: To register to speak at the hearing, please use the online registration form available at https://www.epa.gov/wotus-rule/proposed-revised-definition-wotus-public-hearing.
units.action_summary: Prospective speakers are asked to use the specified online registration form to register to speak.

units.obligation_text: The last day to pre-register to speak at the hearing will be February 21, 2019.
units.action_summary: The deadline to pre-register to speak is February 21, 2019.

units.obligation_text: Requests to speak will be taken the day of the hearing at the hearing registration desk.
units.action_summary: Attendees may request to speak on the day of the hearing by registering at the registration desk.

units.obligation_text: Each commenter will have three minutes to provide oral testimony.
units.action_summary: Oral presenters are allotted three minutes each for testimony.

units.obligation_text: Written comments must be received by the last day of the comment period, as specified in the notice of proposed rulemaking.
units.action_summary: Commenters are required to submit written comments by the close of the comment period specified in the NPRM.

units.obligation_text: Verbatim transcripts of the hearing and written statements will be included in the docket for the rulemaking.
units.action_summary: The agencies will place transcripts and written statements into the rulemaking docket.

units.obligation_text: Any updates made to any aspect of the hearing will be posted online at https://www.epa.gov/wotus-rule/proposed-revised-definition-wotus-public-hearing.
units.action_summary: The agencies will post any hearing updates to the specified website.

units.obligation_text: The agencies will not provide audiovisual equipment for presentations.
units.action_summary: The agencies will not supply audiovisual equipment for use during presentations.

units.obligation_text: Any media presentations should be submitted to the public docket at https://www.regulations.gov/, identified by Docket ID No. EPA-HQ-OW-2018-0149.
units.action_summary: Media presentation files are requested/submitted to the public docket identified by the docket ID.

units.obligation_text: A sign language interpreter will be available for the hearing.
units.action_summary: A sign language interpreter will be provided at the hearing.

units.obligation_text: If you require the service of a translator or other special accommodations such as audio description, please pre-register for the hearing and describe your needs by February 20, 2019.
units.actor: attendees who require translator or special accommodations
units.action_summary: Attendees needing translation or other special accommodations should pre-register and describe their needs by February 20, 2019.

units.obligation_text: The agencies may ask clarifying questions during the oral presentations but will not respond to the presentations at that time.
units.action_summary: The agencies may ask clarifying questions of presenters but will not provide responses during the presentations.

title: Revised Definition of Waters of the United States

units.obligation_text: The high tide line may be determined, in the absence of actual data, by a line of oil or scum along shore objects, a more or less continuous deposit of fine shell or debris on the foreshore or berm, other physical markings or characteristics, vegetation lines, tidal gages, or other suitable means that delineate the general height reached by a rising tide.
units.action_summary: Permits the Corps/determining authority to use listed physical indicators or other suitable means to determine the high tide line when actual data are absent.

units.obligation_text: EPA and the Corps will recognize designations of prior converted cropland made by the Secretary of Agriculture.

units.obligation_text: For the purposes of the Clean Water Act, the EPA Administrator shall have the final authority to determine whether prior converted cropland has been abandoned.

title: Clean Water Act Methods Update Rule for the Analysis of Effluent

units.obligation_text: The method must be specified when results are reported.
units.actor: the person or entity reporting results (e.g., testing laboratory or permittee)
units.action_summary: When reporting test results, the reporting entity must specify the analytical method used.

units.obligation_text: Because the MF technique usually yields low and variable recovery from chlorinated wastewaters, the Most Probable Number method will be required to resolve any controversies.
units.actor: the testing laboratory or responsible analyst
units.action_summary: If there is a controversy (e.g., disputed results) involving MF technique performance on chlorinated wastewaters, the Most Probable Number (MPN) method must be used to resolve it.

units.obligation_text: Tests must be conducted to provide organism enumeration (density).
units.action_summary: Laboratories must perform tests that provide organism enumeration (density).

units.obligation_text: Select the appropriate configuration of tubes/filtrations and dilutions/volumes to account for the quality, character, consistency, and anticipated organism density of the water sample.
units.action_summary: Laboratories must select appropriate tube/filtration configurations and dilutions/volumes based on sample quality and expected organism density.

units.obligation_text: When the MF method has been used previously to test waters with high turbidity, large numbers of noncoliform bacteria, or samples that may contain organisms stressed by chlorine, a parallel test should be conducted with a multiple-tube technique to demonstrate applicability and comparability of results.
units.action_summary: If MF has been used on problematic samples (high turbidity, many noncoliforms, chlorine-stressed organisms), labs should run a parallel multiple-tube test to show applicability and comparable results.

units.obligation_text: Lactose broth may be used in lieu of lauryl tryptose broth (LTB), if at least 25 parallel tests are conducted between this broth and LTB using the water samples normally tested, and this comparison demonstrates that the false-positive rate and false-negative rate for total coliform using lactose broth is less than 10 percent.
units.action_summary: Laboratories may substitute lactose broth for LTB only after conducting at least 25 parallel tests showing false-positive and false-negative rates under 10% for the routine sample set.

units.obligation_text: After prior enrichment in a presumptive medium for total coliform using 9221B.2–2014, all presumptive tubes or bottles showing any amount of gas, growth or acidity within 48 h ± 3 h of incubation shall be submitted to 9221F–2014.
units.action_summary: Following enrichment, any presumptive coliform tubes/bottles with gas, growth, or acidity within the specified incubation time must be forwarded for analysis under method 9221F–2014.

units.obligation_text: Samples shall be enumerated by the multiple-tube or multiple-well procedure.
units.action_summary: Samples must be enumerated using multiple-tube or multiple-well procedures.

units.obligation_text: Using multiple-tube procedures, employ an appropriate tube and dilution configuration of the sample as needed and report the Most Probable Number (MPN).
units.action_summary: When using multiple-tube procedures, labs must use appropriate tube/dilution configurations and must report the Most Probable Number (MPN).

units.obligation_text: To use Colilert-18® to assay for fecal coliforms, the incubation temperature is 44.5 ± 0.2 °C, and a water bath incubator is used.
units.action_summary: When using Colilert-18® for fecal coliform assay, laboratories must incubate at 44.5 ± 0.2 °C and use a water-bath incubator.

units.obligation_text: On a monthly basis, at least ten blue colonies from positive samples must be verified using Lauryl Tryptose Broth and EC broth, followed by count adjustment based on these results;
units.action_summary: Each month, labs must verify at least ten blue colonies from positive samples using specified broths and adjust counts based on verification results.

units.obligation_text: Representative non-blue colonies should be verified using Lauryl Tryptose Broth.
units.action_summary: Labs should verify representative non-blue colonies with Lauryl Tryptose Broth.

units.obligation_text: Where possible, verifications should be done from randomized sample sources.
units.action_summary: When performing verifications, labs should, where possible, use randomized sample sources.

units.obligation_text: On a monthly basis, at least ten sheen colonies from positive samples must be verified using lauryl tryptose broth and brilliant green lactose bile broth, followed by count adjustment based on these results;
units.action_summary: Each month, labs must verify at least ten sheen colonies from positive samples using specified broths and adjust counts based on verification results.

units.obligation_text: Representative non-sheen colonies should be verified using lauryl tryptose broth.
units.action_summary: Labs should verify representative non-sheen colonies with lauryl tryptose broth.

units.obligation_text: Where possible, verifications should be done from randomized sample sources.
units.action_summary: When performing these verifications, labs should, where possible, use randomized sample sources.

units.obligation_text: Subject coliform positive samples determined by 9222 B–2015 or other membrane filter procedure to 9222 I–2015 using NA–MUG media.
units.action_summary: Coliform-positive samples identified by method 9222B–2015 or other MF procedures must be subjected to method 9222I–2015 using NA–MUG media.

units.obligation_text: Verification of colonies by incubation of BHI agar at 10 ± 0.5 °C for 48 ± 3 h is optional.
units.action_summary: Laboratories may optionally verify colonies by incubating BHI agar at 10 ± 0.5 °C for 48 ± 3 h.

title: Hearing: Water Quality Certification
Water Quality Certification

units.obligation_text: Any applicant for a license or permit to conduct any activity which may result in a discharge shall provide the Federal agency a certification from the certifying authority in accordance with this part.
units.actor: Any applicant for a license or permit (project proponent)
units.action_summary: Applicant must provide the Federal agency a Clean Water Act section 401 certification from the certifying authority.

units.obligation_text: The Federal agency shall establish the reasonable period of time categorically or on a case by case basis, which shall not exceed one year from receipt.
units.action_summary: Federal agency must set the reasonable period of time (not exceeding one year) for certifying authority to act.

units.obligation_text: Upon submittal of a certification request, the project proponent shall contact the Federal agency in writing to provide notice of the certification request.
units.action_summary: Project proponent must notify the Federal agency in writing when submitting a certification request.

units.obligation_text: Within 15 days of receiving notice of the certification request from the project proponent, the Federal agency shall provide, in writing, the following information to the certifying authority:
units.action_summary: Federal agency must, within 15 days of notice, provide specified written information to the certifying authority.

units.obligation_text: The applicable reasonable period of time to act on the certification request;
units.action_summary: Provide the applicable reasonable period of time to act on the certification request.

units.obligation_text: The date of receipt of the certification request;
units.action_summary: Provide the date the certification request was received.

units.obligation_text: The date upon which waiver will occur if the certifying authority fails or refuses to act on the certification request.
units.action_summary: Provide the date on which waiver will occur if the certifying authority fails or refuses to act.

units.obligation_text: In establishing the reasonable period of time, Federal agencies shall consider:
units.action_summary: Federal agencies must consider specified factors when setting the reasonable period of time.

units.obligation_text: The complexity of the proposed project;
units.action_summary: Consider the complexity of the proposed project when establishing the reasonable period.

units.obligation_text: The potential for any discharge;
units.action_summary: Consider the potential for any discharge when establishing the reasonable period.

units.obligation_text: The potential need for additional study or evaluation of water quality effects from the discharge.
units.action_summary: Consider whether additional study or evaluation of water quality effects may be needed.

units.obligation_text: The Federal agency may modify an established reasonable period of time, but in no case shall it exceed one year from receipt.
units.action_summary: Federal agency may modify the reasonable period of time, but it must never exceed one year from receipt.

units.obligation_text: but in no case shall it exceed one year from receipt.
units.action_summary: The reasonable period of time may not exceed one year from receipt.

units.obligation_text: Any request by a certifying authority or project proponent to the Federal agency to extend the reasonable period of time shall be in writing.
units.action_summary: Requests to extend the reasonable period must be in writing.

units.obligation_text: If the Federal agency agrees to modify the reasonable period of time, it shall notify the certifying authority and project proponent in writing.
units.action_summary: If the Federal agency modifies the period, it must notify the certifying authority and project proponent in writing.

units.obligation_text: The certifying authority is not authorized to request the project proponent to withdraw a certification request or to take any other action for the purpose of modifying or restarting the established reasonable period of time.
units.action_summary: Certifying authority is prohibited from asking the project proponent to withdraw or otherwise restart/modify the established reasonable period.

units.obligation_text: Any action to grant, grant with conditions, or deny a certification request must be within the scope of certification and completed within the established reasonable period of time.
units.actor: The certifying authority (actions to grant/grant with conditions/deny)
units.action_summary: Certification decisions must be within scope and completed within the established reasonable period.

units.obligation_text: Alternatively, a certifying authority may expressly waive the certification requirement.
units.action_summary: Certifying authority is permitted to expressly waive the certification requirement.

units.obligation_text: If the certifying authority determines that the discharge from a proposed project will comply with water quality requirements it may issue a certification. If the certifying authority cannot certify that the discharge from a proposed project will comply with water quality requirements, it may deny or waive certification.
units.action_summary: Certifying authority may issue certification if compliance is determined; may deny or waive if it cannot certify compliance.

units.obligation_text: Any grant of certification shall be in writing and shall include a statement that the discharge from the proposed project will comply with water quality requirements.
units.action_summary: Grants of certification must be written and include a statement that the discharge will comply with water quality requirements.

units.obligation_text: Any grant of certification with conditions shall be in writing and shall for each condition include, at a minimum:
units.actor: The certifying authority (when granting certification with conditions)
units.action_summary: Grants with conditions must be written and include specified elements for each condition.

units.obligation_text: A statement explaining why the condition is necessary to assure that the discharge from the proposed project will comply with water quality requirements;
units.action_summary: Include an explanation why the condition is necessary to assure compliance.

units.obligation_text: A citation to federal, state, or tribal law that authorizes the condition;
units.action_summary: Provide a legal citation authorizing the condition.

units.obligation_text: A statement of whether and to what extent a less stringent condition could satisfy applicable water quality requirements.
units.action_summary: State whether a less stringent condition could satisfy the requirements and to what extent.

units.obligation_text: Any denial of certification shall be in writing and shall include:
units.action_summary: Denials must be written and include specified items.

units.obligation_text: The specific water quality requirements with which the proposed project will not comply;
units.action_summary: Identify the specific water quality requirements the project will not comply with.

units.obligation_text: A statement explaining why the proposed project will not comply with the identified water quality requirements;
units.action_summary: Explain why the project will not comply with the identified requirements.

units.obligation_text: The specific water quality data or information, if any, that would be needed to assure that the discharge from the proposed project complies with water quality requirements.
units.action_summary: Identify the data or information needed to assure compliance.

units.obligation_text: If the certifying authority determines that no water quality requirements are applicable to the waters receiving the discharge from the proposed project, the certifying authority shall grant or waive certification.
units.action_summary: If no water quality requirements apply, the certifying authority must grant or waive certification.

units.obligation_text: A certification denial shall not preclude a project proponent from submitting a new certification request, in accordance with the substantive and procedural requirements of this part.
units.action_summary: Denial does not prevent the project proponent from submitting a new certification request under the part's requirements.

units.obligation_text: Where a Federal agency determines that a certifying authority’s denial satisfies the requirements of Clean Water Act section 401 and §§ 121.3 and 121.5(e), the Federal agency must provide written notice of such determination to the certifying authority and project proponent,
units.action_summary: If Federal agency determines denial satisfies requirements, it must provide written notice to certifying authority and project proponent.

units.obligation_text: the license or permit shall not be granted.
units.action_summary: If the Federal agency finds the denial satisfies requirements, the license or permit must not be granted.

units.obligation_text: Where a Federal agency determines that a certifying authority’s denial did not satisfy the requirements of Clean Water Act section 401 and §§ 121.3 and 121.5(e), the Federal agency must provide written notice of such determination to the certifying authority and indicate which provision(s) of Clean Water Act section 401 and this part the certifying authority failed to satisfy.
units.action_summary: If the Federal agency finds the denial insufficient, it must notify the certifying authority in writing and identify the provisions not satisfied.

units.obligation_text: If the Federal agency receives the certifying authority’s certification decision prior to the end of the reasonable period of time, the Federal agency may offer the certifying authority the opportunity to remedy the identified deficiencies in the remaining period of time.
units.action_summary: Federal agency may offer the certifying authority an opportunity to remedy deficiencies if decision is received before period ends.

units.obligation_text: If the certifying authority does not provide a certification decision that satisfies the requirements of Clean Water Act section 401 and this part by the end of the reasonable period of time, the Federal agency shall treat the certification in a similar manner as waiver.
units.action_summary: If no satisfactory decision by period end, Federal agency must treat the certification similarly to a waiver.

units.obligation_text: The certification requirement for a license or permit shall be waived upon:
units.action_summary: Certification requirement will be waived upon specified events listed in (a)(1) and (a)(2).

units.obligation_text: Written notification from the certifying authority to the project proponent and the Federal agency that it expressly waives its authority to act on a certification request;
units.actor: The certifying authority (by providing written notification)
units.action_summary: Waiver occurs upon express written notification from the certifying authority that it waives authority to act.

units.obligation_text: The certifying authority’s failure or refusal to act on a certification request.
units.actor: The certifying authority (by failing or refusing to act)
units.action_summary: Waiver occurs if certifying authority fails or refuses to act on the certification request.

units.obligation_text: If the certifying authority fails or refuses to act, the Federal agency shall provide written notice to the Administrator, certifying agency, and project proponent that waiver has occurred. This notice must be in writing and include the notice that the Federal agency provided to the certifying authority pursuant to § 121.4(c).
units.action_summary: If certifying authority fails/refuses to act, Federal agency must provide written notice of waiver to specified parties and include the §121.4(c) notice.

units.obligation_text: A written notice of waiver from the Federal agency shall satisfy the project proponent’s requirement to obtain a certification.
units.actor: The Federal agency (issuing written notice of waiver)
units.action_summary: A Federal agency's written notice of waiver fulfills the project proponent's certification requirement.

units.obligation_text: Upon issuance of a written notice of waiver, the Federal agency may issue the license or permit.
units.action_summary: After issuing a written notice of waiver, the Federal agency is permitted to issue the license or permit.

units.obligation_text: All conditions that satisfy the definition of § 121.1(f) and meet the requirements of § 121.5(d) shall be incorporated into the license or permit and shall be federally enforceable.
units.action_summary: Conditions that meet the definition and requirements must be incorporated into the license/permit and are federally enforceable.

units.obligation_text: If the Federal agency determines that a condition does not satisfy the definition of § 121.1(f) and meet the requirements of § 121.5(d), such condition shall not be incorporated into the license or permit. The Federal agency must provide written notice of such determination to the certifying authority and indicate which conditions are deficient and why they do not satisfy provisions of this part.
units.action_summary: If a condition is deficient, the Federal agency must not incorporate it and must notify the certifying authority in writing explaining deficiencies.

units.obligation_text: If the Federal agency receives a certification with conditions that do not satisfy the definition of § 121.1(f) and the requirements of § 121.5(d) prior to the end of the reasonable period of time, the Federal agency may notify the certifying authority and provide an opportunity in the remaining period of time for the certifying authority to remedy the deficient conditions. If the certifying authority does not remedy the deficient conditions by the end of the reasonable period of time, the Federal agency shall not incorporate them in the license or permit.
units.actor: The Federal agency (and certifying authority as responder)
units.action_summary: Federal agency may notify and give opportunity to remedy deficient conditions; if not remedied by period end, it must not incorporate them.

units.obligation_text: The license or permit must clearly identify any conditions that are based on the certification.
units.actor: The Federal agency (issuing the license or permit)
units.action_summary: License/permit must clearly identify conditions that are based on the certification.

units.obligation_text: The certifying authority, prior to the initial operation of a certified project, shall be afforded the opportunity to inspect the proposed discharge location for the purpose of determining if the discharge from the certified project will comply with the certification.
units.actor: The certifying authority (shall be afforded the opportunity by the Federal agency/licensee)
units.action_summary: Certifying authority must be given an opportunity to inspect the discharge location before initial operation to determine compliance.

units.obligation_text: If the certifying authority, after an inspection, determines that the discharge from the certified project will violate the certification, the certifying authority shall notify the project proponent and the Federal agency in writing, and recommend remedial measures necessary to bring the certified project into compliance with the certification.
units.action_summary: If inspection shows likely violation, certifying authority must notify project proponent and Federal agency in writing and recommend remedial measures.

units.obligation_text: The Federal agency shall be responsible for enforcing certification conditions that are incorporated into a federal license or permit.
units.action_summary: Federal agency is responsible for enforcing certification conditions included in federal licenses/permits.

units.obligation_text: Upon receipt of a federal license or permit application and the related certification, the Federal agency shall notify the Administrator.
units.action_summary: Federal agency must notify the Administrator upon receipt of the federal application and related certification.

units.obligation_text: Within 30 days of receipt of the notice provided by the Federal agency, the Administrator at his or her discretion may determine that the discharge from the certified project may affect water quality in a neighboring jurisdiction. In making this determination and in accordance with applicable law, the Administrator may request copies of the certification and the federal license or permit application.
units.action_summary: Administrator may determine within 30 days that discharge may affect neighboring jurisdiction and may request copies of certification and application.

units.obligation_text: If the Administrator determines that the discharge from the certified project may affect water quality in a neighboring jurisdiction, the Administrator shall notify the affected neighboring jurisdiction, the certifying authority, the Federal agency, and the project proponent, and the federal license or permit may not be issued pending the conclusion of the processes in this paragraph and paragraph (d) of this section.
units.action_summary: Administrator must notify specified parties if discharge may affect neighboring jurisdiction; federal license/permit may not be issued pending resolution.

units.obligation_text: Notification from the Administrator shall be in writing, dated, identify the materials provided by the Federal agency, and inform the affected neighboring jurisdiction that it has 60 days to notify the Administrator and the Federal agency, in writing, whether it has determined that the discharge will violate any of its water quality requirements, object to the issuance of the federal license or permit, and request a public hearing from the Federal agency.
units.actor: The Administrator (in providing notification); the affected neighboring jurisdiction (receiving 60-day period)
units.action_summary: Administrator's notification must be written, dated, identify materials, and inform the neighboring jurisdiction it has 60 days to respond with determinations, objections, or hearing requests.

units.obligation_text: Inform the affected neighboring jurisdiction that it has 60 days to notify the Administrator and the Federal agency, in writing, whether it has determined that the discharge will violate any of its water quality requirements, object to the issuance of the federal license or permit, and request a public hearing from the Federal agency.
units.action_summary: Affected neighboring jurisdiction has 60 days to notify, object, and/or request a public hearing in writing.

units.obligation_text: Notification of objection from the neighboring jurisdiction shall be in writing, shall identify the receiving waters it determined will be affected by the discharge and the specific water quality requirements it determines will be violated by the certified project, and state whether the neighboring jurisdiction requests a hearing.
units.action_summary: Neighboring jurisdiction's objection must be written and identify affected receiving waters, the specific water quality requirements alleged to be violated, and whether it requests a hearing.

units.obligation_text: If the affected neighboring jurisdiction requests a hearing in accordance with this paragraph, the Federal agency shall hold a public hearing on the affected neighboring jurisdiction’s objection to the license or permit.
units.action_summary: If a neighboring jurisdiction requests a hearing, the Federal agency must hold a public hearing on the objection.

units.obligation_text: The Federal agency shall provide the hearing notice to the Administrator at least 30 days before the hearing takes place.
units.action_summary: Federal agency must provide the Administrator with hearing notice at least 30 days before the hearing.

units.obligation_text: At the hearing, the Administrator shall submit to the Federal agency its evaluation and recommendation(s) concerning the objection.
units.action_summary: Administrator must submit its evaluation and recommendations to the Federal agency at the hearing.

units.obligation_text: The Federal agency shall consider recommendations from the neighboring jurisdiction and the Administrator, and any additional evidence presented to the Federal agency at the hearing and determine if additional conditions are necessary to assure that the discharge from the certified project will comply with water quality requirements.
units.action_summary: Federal agency must consider recommendations and evidence and determine if additional conditions are needed to ensure compliance.

units.obligation_text: If additional conditions cannot assure that the discharge from the certified project will comply with water quality requirements, the Federal agency shall not issue the license or permit.
units.action_summary: If additional conditions cannot assure compliance, the Federal agency must not issue the license or permit.

units.obligation_text: Certification by the Administrator that the discharge from a proposed project will comply with water quality requirements will be required where no state, tribe, or interstate agency has authority to give such a certification.
units.actor: The Administrator (when no state/tribe/interstate agency has authority)
units.action_summary: Where no other entity has certification authority, the Administrator's certification is required.

units.obligation_text: In taking action pursuant to this paragraph, the Administrator shall comply with the requirements of the Clean Water Act section 401 and this part.
units.action_summary: Administrator must comply with Clean Water Act section 401 and this part when taking action under this subpart.

units.obligation_text: At least 30 days prior to submitting a certification request, the project proponent shall request a pre-filing meeting with the certifying authority.
units.action_summary: Project proponent must request a pre-filing meeting at least 30 days before submitting a certification request.

units.obligation_text: The certifying authority shall timely grant the pre-filing meeting request or provide written notice to the project proponent that a pre-filing meeting is not necessary.
units.action_summary: Certifying authority must timely grant the pre-filing meeting or provide written notice that it is unnecessary.

units.obligation_text: At the pre-filing meeting, the project proponent and the certifying authority shall discuss the nature of the proposed project and potential water quality effects.
units.actor: Project proponent and the certifying authority
units.action_summary: Both parties must discuss the project nature and potential water quality effects at the pre-filing meeting.

units.obligation_text: The project proponent shall provide a list of applicable state and federal licenses and permits and describe the anticipated timeline for construction and operation.
units.action_summary: Project proponent must provide a list of applicable licenses/permits and the anticipated construction/operation timeline.

units.obligation_text: After the pre-filing meeting, the certifying authority shall contact the Federal agency and identify points of contact at each agency to facilitate information sharing throughout the certification process.
units.action_summary: Certifying authority must contact the Federal agency and identify points of contact following the pre-filing meeting.

units.obligation_text: The certifying authority shall have 30 days from receipt to request additional information from the project proponent.
units.action_summary: Certifying authority has 30 days from receipt to request additional information from the project proponent.

units.obligation_text: The certifying authority shall only request additional information that is within the scope of certification and directly related to the discharge from the proposed project and its potential effect on the receiving waters.
units.action_summary: Certifying authority may request only information within the scope and directly related to the discharge and its effects.

units.obligation_text: The certifying authority shall only request information that can be collected or generated within the established reasonable period of time.
units.action_summary: Certifying authority may only request information that can be produced within the established reasonable period.

units.obligation_text: In any request for additional information, a certifying authority shall include a deadline for the project proponent to respond.
units.action_summary: Requests for additional information must include a response deadline for the project proponent.

units.obligation_text: Project proponents shall comply with deadlines established by the certifying authority.
units.action_summary: Project proponents must comply with deadlines set by the certifying authority.
