units.obligation_text: Section 110(a)(2)(C) of the Clean Air Act requires that the SIP include a program to provide for the "regulation of the modification and construction of any stationary source within the areas covered by the plan as necessary to assure that national ambient air quality standards are achieved."
units.action_summary: The SIP must include a permitting program regulating construction and modification of stationary sources as needed to assure attainment of NAAQS.

units.obligation_text: The provisions of rule 205 require a permit to install that includes limitations which restrict the potential to emit from a stationary source, process, or process equipment to a quantity below that which would otherwise constitute a major source or major modification under any part of the Part 2 air permit rules.
units.action_summary: Permits to install must include limitations that restrict potential to emit below major source/major modification thresholds.

units.obligation_text: The permit to install must contain adequate emission limits that are enforceable as a practical matter; with a consideration to the time-period, production, emission, usage and/or operational limits that restrict the source’s potential to emit in order to demonstrate compliance.
units.action_summary: Permits must include adequate, practically enforceable emission limits and related operational constraints to demonstrate compliance.

units.obligation_text: Rule 205 specifies that the draft permit is subject to the public participation process specified in section 324.5511(3) of Michigan Act 451.
units.action_summary: Draft permits must undergo the public participation process described in section 324.5511(3).

units.obligation_text: Michigan, at its discretion, may approve a permit to install that includes limitations restricting the potential to emit of the stationary source without meeting the requirements of section 324.5511(3) if the emission limitations restrict the potential to emit of the source to less than 90% of the quantity referenced in the applicable requirement.
units.action_summary: MDEQ may approve a permit without following section 324.5511(3)'s public participation if permit limits restrict potential to emit to less than 90% of the applicable threshold.

units.obligation_text: The Michigan rule sets a deminimus level for these 'synthetic minor' sources at 50% of the applicable emission threshold.
units.action_summary: Michigan establishes a de minimis threshold of 50% of the applicable emission threshold for synthetic minor sources.

units.obligation_text: Section 324.5511(3), paragraphs (a), (b), and (c) specify the requirements for permit notification and sets the public comment period to at least 30 days with an opportunity for a public hearing with at least a 30-day notice.
units.action_summary: Requires permit notifications include at least a 30-day public comment period and an opportunity for a public hearing with at least 30-day notice.

units.obligation_text: Sets the public comment period to at least 30 days.
units.action_summary: Public comment periods must be at least 30 days long.

units.obligation_text: Provides an opportunity for a public hearing with at least a 30-day notice.

units.obligation_text: EPA requires that major sources and major modifications to major sources subject to the Prevention of Significant Deterioration of air quality and those sources impacting nonattainment areas be subject to public participation requirements, including a public comment period and opportunity for a public hearing.

units.obligation_text: To attain the 2008 ozone NAAQS, the three-year average of the annual fourth-highest daily maximum 8-hour average ozone concentrations (ozone design values) at each monitor must not exceed 0.075 ppm.
units.actor: areas / monitoring sites / responsible air agencies
units.action_summary: An area's three-year design value at each monitor must be 0.075 ppm or less to be considered attaining the 2008 ozone NAAQS.

units.obligation_text: The air quality data must be collected and quality-assured in accordance with 40 CFR part 58 and recorded in EPA’s Air Quality System (AQS).
units.action_summary: Collect and quality-assure air quality data per 40 CFR part 58 and record it in AQS.

units.obligation_text: Ambient air quality monitoring data for the three-year period must also meet data completeness requirements.
units.action_summary: Ensure three-year monitoring data meet completeness requirements.

units.section: B. Clean Data Determination (design value validity specification)
units.obligation_text: An ozone design value is valid if daily maximum 8-hour average concentrations are available for at least 90% of the days within the ozone monitoring seasons, on average, for the three-year period, with a minimum data completeness of 75% during the ozone monitoring season of any year during the three-year period.
units.action_summary: Design values are valid only if data completeness averages at least 90% over three years and at least 75% in any single season year.

units.obligation_text: EPA will not take final action to determine that the proposed separate Inland Sheboygan area is attaining the 2008 ozone NAAQS if the design value of a monitoring site in the area exceeds the 2008 ozone NAAQS after proposal but prior to final approval of the clean data determination.
units.action_summary: EPA will not finalize the attainment determination if any monitor's design value exceeds the standard after proposal and before final approval.

units.obligation_text: EPA will not finalize this clean data determination unless and until EPA takes final action to split the Sheboygan nonattainment area into two separate areas, as proposed.
units.action_summary: EPA will not finalize the clean data determination until it finalizes the split of the nonattainment area into two areas.

units.section: B. Clean Data Determination (WDNR planning requirements)

units.action_summary: WDNR is required to submit attainment demonstrations, RACM, RFP plans, contingency measures, and other planning requirements related to attainment of the 2008 ozone NAAQS.

units.section: B. Clean Data Determination (suspension if finalized and attaining)
units.obligation_text: Should this action be finalized, the requirements for WDNR to submit attainment demonstrations, and associated reasonably available control measures (RACM), reasonable further progress (RFP) plans, contingency measures, and any other planning requirements related to attainment of the 2008 ozone NAAQS for the proposed Inland Sheboygan area, would be suspended for as long as the area continues to attain the 2008 ozone NAAQS.

units.obligation_text: Once an area is reclassified as Serious, the state must submit to the EPA the SIP revisions for the area that satisfy the statutory and regulatory requirements applicable to Serious areas established in CAA section 182(c) and in the 2008 Ozone NAAQS SIP Requirements Rule.
units.action_summary: After reclassification to Serious, the State must submit SIP revisions satisfying Serious-area statutory and regulatory requirements.

units.obligation_text: Consistent with the final national notice, we are proposing for the Denver Area the same August 3, 2020 due date to submit Serious area SIP revisions, including RACT measures the State determines necessary for meeting reasonable further progress (RFP) or demonstrating timely attainment in the area, and to implement those RACT measures that are tied to timely attainment.
units.action_summary: Proposed due date (Aug 3, 2020) to submit Serious-area SIP revisions and to implement RACT measures tied to timely attainment.

units.obligation_text: For the Denver Area, we are proposing the same due date for submitting SIP revisions for any RACT provisions not otherwise needed for attainment purposes as the date finalized in the August 2019 national rulemaking for other areas: 18 months from the effective date of that national rulemaking.
units.action_summary: Proposed due date to submit SIP revisions for RACT not tied to attainment: 18 months from the effective date of the national rulemaking.

units.obligation_text: We propose for the Denver Area the deadline of July 20, 2021 for implementation of any new RACT requirements not otherwise needed for RFP or timely attainment purposes.
units.action_summary: Proposed implementation deadline for RACT not tied to attainment: July 20, 2021.

units.obligation_text: For Serious areas reclassified from Moderate, the requirement for RACT expands to include all sources that emit, or have the potential to emit, 50 tons per year of volatile organic compounds (VOC) or nitrogen oxides (NOX).
units.action_summary: RACT requirements will cover all sources emitting or with potential to emit 50 tpy VOC or NOX.

units.obligation_text: The reclassified area will then be subject to the Serious area requirement to attain the 2008 ozone NAAQS as expeditiously as practicable, but not later than 9 years from the date of original designation, or July 20, 2021.
units.action_summary: After reclassification to Serious, the area must attain the 2008 ozone NAAQS as expeditiously as practicable and no later than July 20, 2021.

units.obligation_text: The Administrator may adjust applicable deadlines (other than attainment dates) to the extent such adjustment is "necessary or appropriate to assure consistency among the required submissions."
units.action_summary: Administrator may adjust applicable (non-attainment) deadlines when necessary or appropriate to assure consistency among submissions.

units.obligation_text: Send written comments by September 16, 2019.
units.action_summary: Submit written comments by September 16, 2019 (Montana UST proposed rule docket).

units.obligation_text: The EPA’s policy is that all comments received will be included in the public docket without change and may be available online at https://www.regulations.gov, including any personal information provided, unless the comment includes information claimed to be Confidential Business Information (CBI) or other information whose disclosure is restricted by statute.
units.action_summary: EPA will include received comments in the public docket and they may be made available online, except for information claimed as CBI or otherwise restricted.

units.obligation_text: If you submit an electronic comment, the EPA recommends that you include your name and other contact information in the body of your comment and with any disk or CD–ROM you submit.
units.action_summary: Include name and contact information in electronic comments to help EPA process them.

title: Strengthening Transparency in Regulatory Science

units.obligation_text: The provisions of this part apply to data and models, underlying pivotal science supporting influential scientific information and/or underlying pivotal regulatory science used to justify significant regulatory decisions regardless of the source of funding or identity of the party conducting the science.
units.actor: the provisions of this part / EPA
units.action_summary: This part applies to data and models underlying pivotal science and pivotal regulatory science used to support influential scientific information or significant regulatory decisions, regardless of funding or who conducted the science.

units.obligation_text: The provisions of this section do not apply to physical objects (like laboratory samples), drafts, and preliminary analyses.
units.actor: the provisions of this part / EPA
units.action_summary: The part does not apply to physical objects, drafts, or preliminary analyses.

units.obligation_text: In the event the procedures outlined in this part conflict with statutes that EPA administers, or their implementing regulations, the statutes and regulations will control.
units.action_summary: If these procedures conflict with governing statutes or their implementing regulations, the statutes and regulations control.

units.obligation_text: Except where explicitly stated otherwise, the provisions of this part do not apply to any other type of agency action, including individual party adjudications, enforcement activities, or permit proceedings.
units.actor: the provisions of this part / EPA
units.action_summary: Unless explicitly stated, the part does not apply to other agency actions such as adjudications, enforcement, or permits.

units.obligation_text: When promulgating significant regulatory decisions or finalizing influential scientific information, the Agency will only use pivotal regulatory science and/or pivotal science ... if there is tiered access to these data and models in a manner sufficient for independent validation, and [will only use] studies that do not include restricted data and models if the data and models are publicly available in a manner sufficient for independent validation.
units.action_summary: EPA will only use pivotal science for significant regulatory decisions or influential scientific information if restricted-data studies have tiered access sufficient for independent validation, and non-restricted studies have publicly available data/models sufficient for independent validation.

units.obligation_text: Restricted data and models ... only [may be used] if there is tiered access to these data and models in a manner sufficient for independent validation.
units.action_summary: Restricted-data studies may be used only when there is tiered access sufficient for independent validation.

units.obligation_text: Studies that do not include restricted data and models [will be used] if the data and models are publicly available in a manner sufficient for independent validation.
units.action_summary: Non-restricted studies may be used only if their data and models are publicly available enough for independent validation.

units.obligation_text: Where the Agency is making data or models publicly available, it shall do so in a manner that is consistent with law, protects privacy, confidentiality, confidential business information, and is sensitive to national and homeland security.
units.action_summary: When EPA makes data or models public, it must do so consistent with law and protecting privacy, confidentiality, CBI, and national/homeland security.

units.obligation_text: Information is considered 'available in a manner sufficient for independent validation' when it includes the information necessary to understand, assess, and reanalyze findings.
units.action_summary: Defines when information counts as available for independent validation: it must enable understanding, assessment, and reanalysis of findings.

units.obligation_text: (a) Data (where necessary, data would be made available subject to access and use restrictions); (b) Associated protocols necessary to understand, assess, and extend conclusions; (c) Computer codes and models involved in the creation and analysis of such information; (d) Recorded factual materials; and (e) Detailed descriptions of how to access and use such information.
units.action_summary: Examples of what 'available in a manner sufficient for independent validation' may include: data (possibly restricted), protocols, computer codes/models, recorded factual materials, and descriptions of access/use.

units.obligation_text: The agency shall make reasonable efforts to explore methodologies, technologies, and institutional arrangements for making such data and models available before it concludes that doing so in a manner consistent with law and protection of privacy, confidentiality, national and homeland security is not possible.
units.action_summary: EPA must reasonably explore methods and arrangements to make data and models available before deciding it's impossible due to legal or privacy/security constraints.

units.obligation_text: Where data and models are controlled by third parties, EPA may work with those parties to endeavor to make the data and models available in a manner that complies with this section.
units.action_summary: EPA may collaborate with third parties controlling data/models to try to make them available consistent with the section.

units.obligation_text: When promulgating significant regulatory decisions or finalizing influential scientific information, the Agency will, other things equal, give greater consideration to studies where the underlying data and models are publicly available in a manner sufficient for independent validation.
units.action_summary: EPA will generally give greater consideration to studies whose underlying data and models are publicly available for independent validation.

units.obligation_text: The Agency will also give greater consideration to studies based on data and models that include confidential business information, proprietary information or personally identifiable information if these data and models were available through restricted access, such as through a secure data enclave, in a manner sufficient for independent validation.
units.action_summary: EPA will give greater consideration to studies with restricted-sensitive data if those data/models were available via restricted access (e.g., secure enclave) sufficient for independent validation.

units.obligation_text: Where there is no access to data and models, or access is limited, the Agency may still consider these studies, depending on the other attributes of the studies.
units.action_summary: EPA may still consider studies lacking data/model access or with limited access, based on other study attributes.

units.obligation_text: The Agency will identify those studies that are given greater consideration and provide a short description of why greater consideration was given.
units.action_summary: EPA must identify which studies received greater consideration and briefly explain why.

units.obligation_text: Where the Agency is making data or models publicly available, it shall do so in a manner that is consistent with law, protects privacy, confidentiality, confidential business information, and is sensitive to national and homeland security.
units.action_summary: When making data/models public, EPA must comply with law and protect privacy, confidentiality, CBI, and national/homeland security.

units.obligation_text: (1) Data (where necessary, data would be made available subject to access and use restrictions); (2) Associated protocols necessary to understand, assess, and extend conclusions; (3) Computer codes and models involved in the creation and analysis of such information; (4) Recorded factual materials; and (5) Detailed descriptions of how to access and use such information.
units.action_summary: Examples of information constituting availability for independent validation: data (possibly restricted), protocols, codes/models, recorded factual materials, and access/use descriptions.

units.obligation_text: The agency shall make reasonable efforts to explore methodologies, technologies, and institutional arrangements for making such data and models available before it concludes that doing so in a manner consistent with law and protection of privacy, confidentiality, national and homeland security is not possible.
units.action_summary: EPA must reasonably explore ways to make data/models available before determining it's impossible due to legal or privacy/security concerns.

units.obligation_text: Where data and models are controlled by third parties, EPA may work with those parties to endeavor to make the data and models available in a manner that complies with this section.
units.action_summary: EPA may collaborate with third-party controllers to try to make data/models available consistent with the section.

units.obligation_text: EPA shall describe and document any assumptions and methods used and shall describe variability and uncertainty.
units.action_summary: EPA must describe and document the assumptions and methods used and describe variability and uncertainty in analyses.

units.obligation_text: EPA shall evaluate the appropriateness of using default assumptions on a case-by-case basis.
units.action_summary: EPA must assess whether default assumptions are appropriate in each case.

units.obligation_text: EPA shall clearly explain the scientific basis for critical assumptions used in the analysis that drove the analytical results and subsequent decisions and shall present analyses showing the sensitivity of the modeled results to alternative assumptions.
units.action_summary: EPA must explain the scientific basis for critical assumptions and present sensitivity analyses showing how results change under alternative assumptions.

units.obligation_text: When available, EPA shall give explicit consideration to high quality studies, including but not limited to those that explore: A broad class of parametric dose-response or concentration-response models; a robust set of potential confounding variables; nonparametric models that incorporate fewer assumptions; various threshold models across the dose or exposure range; and models that investigate factors that might account for spatial heterogeneity.
units.action_summary: When available, EPA must explicitly consider high-quality studies, including various model types and studies addressing confounding, thresholds, and spatial heterogeneity.

units.obligation_text: EPA shall conduct independent peer review on all pivotal regulatory science used to justify significant regulatory decisions and on all pivotal science underlying influential scientific information, consistent with the requirements of the OMB Final Information Quality Bulletin for Peer Review and the exemptions described therein.
units.action_summary: EPA must conduct independent peer review of all pivotal regulatory science and pivotal science underlying influential scientific information, consistent with OMB peer review Bulletin and exemptions.

units.obligation_text: EPA shall ask peer reviewers to articulate the strengths and weaknesses of EPA's justification for the assumptions applied and the implications of those assumptions for the results.
units.action_summary: EPA must instruct peer reviewers to evaluate and articulate strengths/weaknesses of EPA's assumption justifications and implications for results.

units.obligation_text: The Administrator may grant an exemption to this part on a case-by case basis if he or she determines that compliance is impracticable because technological barriers render sharing of the data or models infeasible, the development of the data or model was completed or updated before [EFFECTIVE DATE OF FINAL RULE] or making the data and models publicly available would conflict with laws governing privacy, confidentiality, confidential business information, or national and homeland security.
units.action_summary: The Administrator may grant case-by-case exemptions to the part if compliance is impracticable due to technological barriers, pre-effective-date development, or legal/privacy/confidentiality/national security conflicts.

units.obligation_text: An exemption may be granted if technological barriers render sharing of the data or models infeasible.
units.action_summary: Administrator may exempt when technological barriers make sharing infeasible.

units.obligation_text: An exemption may be granted if the development of the data or model was completed or updated before [EFFECTIVE DATE OF FINAL RULE].
units.action_summary: Administrator may exempt studies whose data/models were developed or updated before the rule's effective date.

units.obligation_text: An exemption may be granted if making the data and models publicly available would conflict with laws governing privacy, confidentiality, confidential business information, or national and homeland security.
units.action_summary: Administrator may exempt when public disclosure would conflict with privacy, confidentiality, CBI, or national/homeland security laws.

title: Guidance: Administrative Procedures for Issuance and Public Petitions

units.obligation_text: The Captain of the Port Sector Ohio Valley (COTP) or a designated representative will inform the public through broadcast notice to mariners of the enforcement period for the special local regulation.
units.actor: The Captain of the Port Sector Ohio Valley (COTP) or a designated representative
units.action_summary: COTP or its representative must inform the public by broadcast notice to mariners of the enforcement period.

units.obligation_text: In accordance with the general regulations in § 100 of this part, entry into this area is prohibited unless authorized by the COTP or a designated representative.
units.actor: All persons and vessels (those seeking to enter the regulated area)
units.action_summary: Entering the regulated area is prohibited unless authorized by the COTP or designated representative.

units.obligation_text: Recreational vessels may be permitted to transit the regulated area, but are restricted to the Indiana side of the navigation channel.
units.action_summary: Recreational vessels may be allowed to transit the area, subject to restrictions.

units.obligation_text: Recreational vessels ... are restricted to the Indiana side of the navigation channel.
units.action_summary: If permitted, recreational vessels must stay on the Indiana side of the navigation channel.

units.obligation_text: There shall be no anchoring or loitering in the navigation channel.
units.actor: All vessels and persons in the regulated area
units.action_summary: Anchoring or loitering in the navigation channel is prohibited.

units.obligation_text: There is a no-entry zone starting at Ohio River MM 602.7 through MM 607.0.
units.action_summary: A no-entry zone is established from MM 602.7 through MM 607.0; entry is prohibited in that zone.

units.obligation_text: Recreational vessels transiting into and away from this area are restricted to the slowest safe speed creating minimum wake.
units.actor: Recreational vessels transiting into and away from the area
units.action_summary: Recreational vessels must transit at the slowest safe speed that creates a minimum wake.

units.obligation_text: The COTP may terminate the event or the operation of any vessel at any time it is deemed necessary for the protection of life or property.
units.actor: The Captain of the Port Sector Ohio Valley (COTP)
units.action_summary: COTP is authorized to terminate the event or the operation of any vessel when necessary to protect life or property.

units.obligation_text: All other persons or vessels desiring entry into or passage through the area must request permission from the COTP or a designated representative.
units.actor: All other persons or vessels desiring entry or passage
units.action_summary: Anyone else seeking entry or passage must request permission from the COTP or designated representative.

units.obligation_text: Section 3(a) of E.O. 13891 directs agencies to establish and maintain a website guidance portal that contains or links to guidance documents that are "active".
units.actor: EPA (as an agency directed by E.O. 13891)
units.action_summary: EPA must establish and maintain an online guidance portal containing or linking to active guidance documents.

units.obligation_text: The E.O. requires that all active guidance documents issued by an agency be included on the agency’s guidance portal and that any guidance document excluded from the portal does not represent the final guidance of the agency and will have no effect.
units.action_summary: All active guidance documents must be included on the guidance portal; documents excluded from the portal do not represent final agency guidance and have no effect.
units.modal_raw: are required / will have no effect

units.obligation_text: The EPA Guidance Portal [will include the following] information for each guidance document:
units.action_summary: The Guidance Portal must provide specified information for each guidance document.

units.obligation_text: A concise name for the guidance document;
units.action_summary: Portal entries must include a concise name for each guidance document.

units.obligation_text: The date on which the guidance document was issued;
units.action_summary: Portal must show the issuance date of each guidance document.

units.obligation_text: The date on which the guidance document was posted to the Guidance Portal;
units.action_summary: Portal must record the date each guidance document was posted to the portal.

units.obligation_text: An EPA unique identifier;
units.action_summary: Portal entries must include a unique EPA identifier for each guidance document.

units.obligation_text: A hyperlink to the guidance document and any supporting or ancillary documents;
units.action_summary: Portal must include hyperlinks to the guidance document and supporting materials.

units.obligation_text: The general topic, program, and/or statute addressed by the guidance document;
units.action_summary: Portal must state the general topic, program, or statute the guidance addresses.

units.obligation_text: A brief summary of the guidance document’s content.
units.action_summary: Portal must include a brief summary of each guidance document's content.

units.obligation_text: The EPA proposes to require that each guidance document would satisfy the following standard elements:
units.action_summary: Each guidance document must include standard elements specified in the rule.

units.obligation_text: Include the term "guidance;"
units.actor: Issuer of the guidance document (EPA office issuing the document)
units.action_summary: Guidance documents must include the term 'guidance'.

units.obligation_text: Identify the office issuing the document;
units.actor: Issuer of the guidance document (EPA office)
units.action_summary: Guidance must identify the issuing office.

units.obligation_text: Provide the title of the guidance;
units.action_summary: Guidance must provide its title.

units.obligation_text: Provide the unique document identification number;
units.action_summary: Guidance must include a unique document identification number.

units.obligation_text: Include the date of issuance;
units.action_summary: Guidance must include its issuance date.

units.obligation_text: When practicable, identify the general activities to which and the persons to whom the document applies;
units.action_summary: Guidance should, when practicable, state the activities and persons to which it applies.

units.obligation_text: Include the citation to the statutory provision (including the U.S.C. citation) or regulation (in CFR format) to which the guidance document applies or which it interprets;
units.action_summary: Guidance must cite the statute or regulation it applies to or interprets.

units.obligation_text: Note if the guidance document is a revision to a previously issued guidance document and, if so, identify the guidance document that it modifies or replaces;
units.action_summary: Guidance must state if it revises a prior guidance and identify the prior document.

units.obligation_text: Include a short summary of the subject matter covered in the guidance document at the beginning of the document;
units.action_summary: Guidance must begin with a short summary of its subject matter.

units.obligation_text: Include a disclaimer stating that the contents of the guidance document do not have the force and effect of law and that the Agency does not intend to bind the public in any way and intends only to provide clarity to the public regarding existing requirements under the law or Agency policies.
units.action_summary: Guidance must include a disclaimer that it does not have the force of law and is not intended to bind the public.

units.obligation_text: When a new guidance document has been issued, or an active guidance document has been modified, or an active guidance document has been withdrawn, the EPA proposes to inform the public via the EPA Guidance Portal or other Agency website.
units.action_summary: EPA will inform the public via the Guidance Portal or other website when guidance is issued, modified, or withdrawn.

units.obligation_text: Given their legally nonbinding nature, guidance documents will avoid including mandatory language such as "shall," "must," "required" or "requirement," unless these words are used to describe a statutory or regulatory requirement, or the language is addressed to EPA staff and will not foreclose consideration by the EPA of positions advanced by affected private parties.
units.action_summary: Guidance should avoid mandatory terms like 'shall' or 'must' unless describing statutory/regulatory requirements or directed to EPA staff.

units.obligation_text: Before issuing a new guidance document covered by this rule that is developed by an EPA Regional Office, the EPA Regional Office must receive concurrence from the corresponding Presidentially-appointed EPA official ... at EPA headquarters who is responsible for administering the national program to which the guidance document pertains.
units.action_summary: Regional Offices must obtain concurrence from the relevant Headquarters official before issuing covered guidance developed by the Regional Office.

units.obligation_text: The EPA will seek significance determinations from OIRA for certain guidance documents, as appropriate, in the same manner as for rulemakings.
units.action_summary: EPA will request significance determinations from OIRA for certain guidance documents as appropriate.

units.obligation_text: This proposed rule would establish a public review and comment opportunity for all significant guidance documents, whether that document is new or a modification or withdrawal of an active guidance document.
units.action_summary: Significant guidance documents will be subject to a public review and comment opportunity.

units.obligation_text: The EPA ... generally require the EPA to publish a Notice in the Federal Register to announce the availability of a new draft significant guidance document and provide a 30-day public comment opportunity prior to issuing the final significant guidance document.
units.action_summary: EPA must publish a Federal Register notice announcing a draft significant guidance document and provide a 30-day public comment period before finalizing it.

units.obligation_text: Publish a Notice in the Federal Register announcing the proposed modification or withdrawal of an active significant guidance document and provide a 30-day public comment opportunity before finalizing the modification or withdrawal of such a document.
units.action_summary: EPA must publish a Federal Register notice and provide 30 days for comment before finalizing modifications or withdrawals of active significant guidance documents.

units.obligation_text: The draft significant guidance document itself (including a link to any supporting documents) would be posted on the EPA’s website concurrently and labeled appropriately.
units.action_summary: EPA must post the draft significant guidance document and supporting documents on its website concurrently with the Federal Register notice.

units.obligation_text: Public comments on draft significant guidance documents and draft modifications or withdrawals of significant active guidance documents should be submitted using the methods specified in the Notice in the Federal Register announcing the availability of the draft significant guidance document or its withdrawal.
units.action_summary: Public comments should be submitted by the methods specified in the Federal Register notice.

units.obligation_text: All comments received on a draft significant guidance document, or draft modification or withdrawal of an active significant guidance document, would be made available to the public either through the Federal eRulemaking Portal (i.e., https://www.regulations.gov/) or on the EPA website.
units.action_summary: EPA will make all comments on draft significant guidance documents publicly available through regulations.gov or the EPA website.

units.obligation_text: The EPA is proposing to publish a Notice in the Federal Register announcing when the issuance of a new or modified active significant guidance document or withdrawal of an active significant guidance document is finalized.
units.action_summary: EPA will publish a Federal Register notice announcing that a significant guidance document issuance, modification, or withdrawal is finalized.

units.obligation_text: The proposed regulations would also require the EPA ... to respond to major public comments and identify in the required Notice in the Federal Register how the public may access the comments received and the Agency’s response.
units.action_summary: EPA must respond to major public comments and explain in the Federal Register notice how to access the comments and responses.

units.obligation_text: The EPA proposes limited exceptions to the significant guidance document notice and comment process.
units.action_summary: EPA may apply limited exceptions to the notice-and-comment requirements for significant guidance documents under specified circumstances.

units.obligation_text: The EPA would not seek or respond to public comment before it implements a significant guidance document ... if exigent circumstances, as determined by the Administrator, (e.g., a public health, safety, environment or other emergency) make it impracticable to delay issuance of the guidance document, or there is a statutory or judicial requirement that compels the EPA to immediately issue the document.
units.action_summary: EPA may forgo seeking or responding to public comment before implementing a significant guidance document when exigent circumstances or statutory/judicial compulsion require immediate issuance.

units.obligation_text: The EPA would not seek or respond to public comment when it finds good cause that notice and public comment is impracticable, unnecessary, or contrary to public interest.
units.action_summary: EPA may omit notice-and-comment if it finds good cause that notice and public comment are impracticable, unnecessary, or contrary to the public interest.

units.obligation_text: The EPA would present the good cause finding in the guidance document or notice of availability in the Federal Register.
units.action_summary: If EPA invokes good cause to omit comment, it must state the good-cause finding in the guidance document or Federal Register notice.

units.obligation_text: The EPA Administrator or other Presidentially-appointed EPA official, or an official who is serving in an acting capacity of either of the foregoing, would approve each significant guidance document before it is issued and posted on the EPA Guidance Portal.
units.actor: EPA Administrator or other Presidentially-appointed EPA official (or acting official)
units.action_summary: A Presidentially-appointed (or acting) official must approve each significant guidance document before issuance and posting on the Guidance Portal.

units.obligation_text: Accordingly, the EPA would comply with the requirements of Executive Orders 12866, 13563, 13609, and 13891 when issuing significant guidance documents.
units.action_summary: EPA must comply with the applicable requirements of specified Executive Orders when issuing significant guidance documents.

units.obligation_text: The EPA would assess the potential impacts of the significant guidance document if those effects may reasonably be anticipated to lead to an annual effect on the economy of $100 million.
units.action_summary: EPA must assess potential economic impacts when a significant guidance document may have $100 million+ annual effects.

units.obligation_text: The analysis (Regulatory Impact Analysis (RIA) or Economic Analysis (EA)) would focus on how that economically significant guidance document affects the incentives of regulated parties and would conform to OMB Circular A–4 on Regulatory Analysis and EPA Guidelines for Preparing Economic Analyses.
units.action_summary: Economic analyses for economically significant guidance must assess effects on regulated-party incentives and conform to OMB Circular A–4 and EPA economic guidelines.

units.obligation_text: The EPA is proposing procedures to allow the public to petition the EPA for the modification or withdrawal of an active guidance document posted on the EPA Guidance Portal.
units.action_summary: The public is permitted to petition EPA to modify or withdraw active guidance documents on the Guidance Portal.
units.modal_raw: to allow the public to petition / may petition

units.obligation_text: The EPA Guidance Portal will provide clear and specific instructions to the public regarding how to request the modification or withdrawal of an active guidance document.
units.action_summary: The Guidance Portal must provide clear instructions on how the public can request modification or withdrawal of active guidance documents.

units.obligation_text: The public may submit petitions using one of the two following methods described on the EPA Guidance Portal: (1) An electronic submission through the EPA’s designated submission system ... or, (2) a paper submission to the EPA’s designated mailing address listed on the EPA Guidance Portal.
units.action_summary: Petitioners may submit petitions either electronically via the designated submission system or by paper to the designated mailing address listed on the Guidance Portal.

units.obligation_text: Electronic submission through the EPA’s designated submission system identified on the EPA Guidance Portal (i.e., using a link labeled 'Submit a petition for Agency modification or withdrawal of guidance documents').
units.action_summary: Petitioners may submit petitions electronically via the designated portal link.

units.obligation_text: A paper submission to the EPA’s designated mailing address listed on the EPA Guidance Portal.
units.action_summary: Petitioners may submit petitions by paper to the designated mailing address on the Guidance Portal.

units.obligation_text: The EPA is proposing the following formatting elements for petitions:
units.action_summary: EPA proposes required formatting elements that petitions should include.

units.obligation_text: The petitioner’s name and a means for the EPA to contact the petitioner such as an email address or mailing address, in addition to any other contact information (such as telephone number) that the petitioner chooses to include;
units.action_summary: Petitions should include the petitioner's name and contact information so EPA can reach them.

units.obligation_text: A heading, preceding its text that states, either 'Petition to Modify a Guidance Document' or 'Petition to Withdraw a Guidance Document.'
units.action_summary: Petitions should include a heading stating whether it requests modification or withdrawal.

units.obligation_text: The EPA is proposing that a petition should include the following content elements:
units.action_summary: EPA proposes content elements that petitions should contain to be evaluated.

units.obligation_text: Identification of the specific title and the EPA unique identifier of the guidance document that the petitioner is requesting be modified or withdrawn;
units.action_summary: Petitions should identify the guidance document by title and EPA unique identifier.

units.obligation_text: The nature of the relief sought (i.e., modification or withdrawal);
units.action_summary: Petitions should state whether they seek modification or withdrawal.

units.obligation_text: An explanation of the interest of the petitioner in the requested action;
units.action_summary: Petitions should explain the petitioner's interest in the requested modification or withdrawal.

units.obligation_text: If practicable, specification of the text that the petitioner request be modified or withdrawn, and, where possible, suggested text for the Agency to consider;
units.action_summary: Petitions should, if practicable, specify the exact text to be modified/withdrawn and may suggest replacement text.

units.obligation_text: A rationale for the requested modification or withdrawal.
units.action_summary: Petitions should provide a rationale for the requested modification or withdrawal.

units.obligation_text: Although the EPA may be able to consider incomplete petitions, petitions that omit the specified information may impede the EPA from fully evaluating the merits of the requested action.
units.action_summary: EPA may consider incomplete petitions, but missing information may limit evaluation.

units.obligation_text: A petition that is not submitted using one of the two methods described above (as well as on the EPA Guidance Portal), but that includes the required formatting and content elements, will be treated as a properly filed petition, received as of the time it is discovered and identified.
units.action_summary: If a petition is not submitted by the specified methods but contains required format/content, EPA will treat it as a properly filed petition upon discovery.

units.obligation_text: If a document does not include all of the format and content elements described above, the EPA may be unable to identify the document as a petition. These will instead be treated according to the existing correspondence or other appropriate procedures of the EPA, and any suggestions contained in it will be considered at the discretion of the Administrator.
units.action_summary: Documents lacking required elements may not be identified as petitions; EPA may treat them as correspondence and consider suggestions at the Administrator's discretion.
units.modal_raw: may be unable / will be treated / will be considered at the discretion

units.obligation_text: The EPA would respond to petitions in a timely manner, but no later than 90 calendar days after receipt of the petition.
units.action_summary: EPA will respond to petitions within 90 calendar days of receipt.
units.modal_raw: would respond / no later than 90 calendar days

units.obligation_text: If the EPA requires more than 90 calendar days to consider a petition, the EPA would inform the petitioner that more time is required and indicate the reason why and provide an estimated decision date.
units.action_summary: If EPA needs more than 90 days, it must notify the petitioner, state the reason, and give an estimated decision date.

units.obligation_text: The EPA will only extend the response date one time for a period not to exceed 90 calendar days before providing a response.
units.action_summary: EPA may extend the response deadline only once and by no more than 90 calendar days.

units.obligation_text: Duplicative petitions and petitions submitted as part of a mass petitioning effort may be responded to in a single response to ensure an efficient and consistent response to the petitions.
units.action_summary: EPA may answer duplicative or mass-submitted petitions with a single, consolidated response.
units.modal_raw: may be responded to in a single response

units.obligation_text: Petitions that request a change to the underlying statute or promulgated rules, rather than specific text in the guidance document, will not be considered valid petitions under this process because they are not petitions to modify or withdraw a guidance document.
units.action_summary: Petitions seeking changes to statutes or promulgated rules are not valid under this guidance-petition process and will not be considered here.

title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Major Sources: Industrial, Commercial, and Institutional Boilers and Process Heaters; Amendments

units.obligation_text: You must meet the requirements in paragraphs (a)(1) through (3) of this section, except as provided in paragraphs (b) through (e) of this section. You must meet these requirements at all times the affected unit is operating, except as provided in paragraph (f) of this section.
units.action_summary: Comply with the listed requirements in (a)(1)-(3) whenever the affected unit is operating, subject to stated exceptions.

units.obligation_text: You must meet each emission limit and work practice standard in Tables 1 through 3, and 11 through 15 to this subpart that applies to your boiler or process heater, for each boiler or process heater at your source, except as provided under § 63.7522.
units.action_summary: Meet all applicable emission limits and work practice standards in the referenced tables for each boiler/process heater at the source, unless emissions averaging under §63.7522 applies.

units.obligation_text: The output-based emission limits, in units of pounds per million Btu of steam output, in Tables 1 or 2 to this subpart are an alternative applicable only to boilers and process heaters that generate either steam, cogenerate steam with electricity, or both.
units.actor: boiler or process heater that generate steam or cogenerate
units.action_summary: Output-based emission limits (lb/MMBtu steam output) are available only for boilers/process heaters that generate or cogenerate steam.
units.modal_raw: are an alternative applicable only to

units.obligation_text: The output-based emission limits, in units of pounds per megawatt-hour, in Tables 1 or 2 to this subpart are an alternative applicable only to boilers that generate only electricity.
units.action_summary: Output-based emission limits (lb/MWh) are available only for boilers that generate only electricity.
units.modal_raw: are an alternative applicable only to

units.obligation_text: Boilers that perform multiple functions (cogeneration and electricity generation) or supply steam to common headers would calculate a total steam energy output using equation 21 of § 63.7575 to demonstrate compliance with the output-based emission limits, in units of pounds per million Btu of steam output, in Tables 1 or 2 to this subpart.
units.actor: multi-function boilers or boilers supplying steam to common headers
units.action_summary: Calculate total steam energy output using Equation 21 of §63.7575 to show compliance with output-based limits.

units.obligation_text: If your boiler or process heater commenced construction or reconstruction after June 4, 2010, and before May 20, 2011, you may comply with the emission limits in Table 11 or 14 to this subpart until January 31, 2016.
units.actor: owner or operator of boilers/process heaters commenced construction/reconstruction in specified period
units.action_summary: Optionally comply with Table 11 or 14 limits until Jan 31, 2016 for units constructed/reconstructed in that date range.

units.obligation_text: If your boiler or process heater commenced construction or reconstruction on or after May 20, 2011, and before December 23, 2011, you may comply with the emission limits in Table 12 or 14 to this subpart until January 31, 2016.
units.actor: owner or operator of boilers/process heaters commenced construction/reconstruction in specified period
units.action_summary: Optionally comply with Table 12 or 14 limits until Jan 31, 2016 for units constructed/reconstructed in that date range.

units.obligation_text: If your boiler or process heater commenced construction or reconstruction on or after December 23, 2011, and before April 1, 2013, you may comply with the emission limits in Table 13 or 14 to this subpart until January 31, 2016.
units.actor: owner or operator of boilers/process heaters commenced construction/reconstruction in specified period
units.action_summary: Optionally comply with Table 13 or 14 limits until Jan 31, 2016 for units constructed/reconstructed in that date range.

units.obligation_text: If you operate a new boiler or process heater, you may comply with the emission limits in Table 1 or 14 until you must comply with the emission limits in Table 1 to this subpart.
units.actor: owner or operator of new boilers/process heaters
units.action_summary: New units may temporarily comply with Table 1 or 14 limits until the required Table 1 compliance date.

units.obligation_text: If you operate an existing boiler or process heater, you may comply with the emission limits in Table 2 or 15 until you must comply with the emission limits in Table 2 to this subpart.
units.actor: owner or operator of existing boilers/process heaters
units.action_summary: Existing units may temporarily comply with Table 2 or 15 limits until required Table 2 compliance date.

units.obligation_text: Limited-use boilers and process heaters must complete a tune-up every 5 years as specified in § 63.7540.
units.actor: owner or operator of limited-use boilers and process heaters
units.action_summary: Complete a tune-up every 5 years per §63.7540.

units.obligation_text: They are not subject to the emission limits in Tables 1 and 2 or 11 through 15 to this subpart, the annual tune-up, or the energy assessment requirements in Table 3 to this subpart, or the operating limits in Table 4 to this subpart.
units.action_summary: Limited-use units are exempt from the listed emission limits, annual tune-up, energy assessment, and operating limits.

units.obligation_text: Boilers and process heaters in the units designed to burn gas 1 fuels subcategory with a heat input capacity of less than or equal to 5 million Btu per hour must complete a tune-up every 5 years as specified in § 63.7540.
units.actor: owner or operator of gas 1 boilers/process heaters ≤5 MMBtu/hr
units.action_summary: Complete a tune-up every 5 years for units ≤5 MMBtu/hr in gas 1 subcategory.

units.obligation_text: Boilers and process heaters in the units designed to burn gas 1 fuels subcategory with a heat input capacity greater than 5 million Btu per hour and less than 10 million Btu per hour must complete a tune-up every 2 years as specified in § 63.7540.
units.actor: owner or operator of gas 1 boilers/process heaters >5 and <10 MMBtu/hr
units.action_summary: Complete a tune-up every 2 years for units >5 and <10 MMBtu/hr in gas 1 subcategory.

units.obligation_text: Boilers and process heaters in the units designed to burn gas 1 fuels subcategory are not subject to the emission limits in Tables 1 and 2 or 11 through 15 to this subpart, or the operating limits in Table 4 to this subpart.
units.action_summary: Units in the gas 1 subcategory are exempt from the listed emission and operating limits.

units.obligation_text: You must demonstrate compliance with all applicable emission limits using performance stack testing, fuel analysis, or continuous monitoring systems (CMS), including a continuous emission monitoring system (CEMS), continuous opacity monitoring system (COMS), continuous parameter monitoring system (CPMS), or particulate matter continuous parameter monitoring system (PM CPMS), where applicable.
units.action_summary: Demonstrate compliance via performance testing, fuel analysis, or applicable continuous monitoring systems.

units.obligation_text: You may demonstrate compliance with the applicable emission limit for hydrogen chloride (HCl), mercury, or total selected metals (TSM) using fuel analysis if the emission rate calculated according to § 63.7530(c) is less than the applicable emission limit.
units.action_summary: May use fuel analysis to demonstrate compliance for HCl, mercury, or TSM if the calculated emission rate is below the applicable limit.

units.obligation_text: For gaseous fuels, you may not use fuel analyses to comply with the TSM alternative standard or the HCl standard.
units.actor: owner or operator burning gaseous fuels
units.action_summary: Prohibits use of fuel analysis for TSM alternative standard or HCl standard when burning gaseous fuels.

units.obligation_text: Otherwise, you must demonstrate compliance for HCl, mercury, or TSM using performance stack testing, if subject to an applicable emission limit listed in Tables 1, 2, or 11 through 15 to this subpart.
units.action_summary: If fuel analysis is not allowed or applicable, use performance stack testing to demonstrate compliance for HCl, mercury, or TSM.

units.obligation_text: For each boiler or process heater that is required or that you elect to demonstrate compliance with any of the applicable emission limits in Tables 1 or 2 or 11 through 15 of this subpart through performance (stack) testing, your initial compliance requirements include all the following:
units.action_summary: Initiate and complete the listed initial compliance requirements for boilers/process heaters that will use performance (stack) testing.

units.obligation_text: For each boiler or process heater that you elect to demonstrate compliance with the applicable emission limits in Tables 1 or 2 or 11 through 15 to this subpart for HCl, mercury, or TSM through fuel analysis, your initial compliance requirement is to conduct a fuel analysis for each type of fuel burned in your boiler or process heater according to § 63.7521 and Table 6 to this subpart and establish operating limits according to § 63.7530 and Table 8 to this subpart.
units.action_summary: If using fuel analysis for HCl/mercury/TSM, conduct fuel analysis for each fuel type per §63.7521/Table 6 and set operating limits per §63.7530/Table 8.

units.obligation_text: The fuels described in paragraph (a)(2)(i) and (ii) of this section are exempt from these fuel analysis and operating limit requirements.
units.actor: owner or operator (you) for fuels described in §63.7510(a)(2)(i) and (ii)
units.action_summary: Specified fuels are exempt from fuel analysis and operating limit requirements.

units.obligation_text: The fuels described in paragraph (a)(2)(ii) of this section are exempt from the chloride fuel analysis and operating limit requirements.
units.actor: owner or operator (you) for fuels described in §63.7510(a)(2)(ii)
units.action_summary: Specific fuels are exempt from chloride fuel analysis and operating limits.

units.obligation_text: Boilers and process heaters that use a CEMS for mercury or HCl are exempt from the performance testing and operating limit requirements specified in paragraph (a) of this section for the HAP for which CEMS are used.
units.actor: owner or operator using CEMS for mercury or HCl
units.action_summary: Using a mercury or HCl CEMS exempts the source from performance testing and operating limit requirements for that HAP specified in paragraph (a).

units.obligation_text: If your boiler or process heater is subject to a carbon monoxide (CO) limit, your initial compliance demonstration for CO is to conduct a performance test for CO according to Table 5 to this subpart or conduct a performance evaluation of your continuous CO monitor, if applicable, according to § 63.7525(a).
units.action_summary: If subject to CO limit, conduct CO performance test per Table 5 or perform CO monitor evaluation under §63.7525(a) as initial compliance.

units.obligation_text: Boilers and process heaters that use a CO CEMS to comply with the applicable alternative CO CEMS emission standard listed in Tables 1, 2, or 11 through 15 to this subpart, as specified in § 63.7525(a), are exempt from the initial CO performance testing and oxygen concentration operating limit requirements specified in paragraph (a) of this section.
units.actor: owner or operator using CO CEMS
units.action_summary: Using a qualifying CO CEMS exempts the source from initial CO performance testing and oxygen operating limit requirements in paragraph (a).

units.obligation_text: For new or reconstructed affected sources (as defined in § 63.7490), you must complete the initial compliance demonstration with the emission limits no later than July 30, 2013, or within 180 days after startup of the source, whichever is later.
units.actor: owner or operator of new or reconstructed affected sources
units.action_summary: Complete initial compliance demonstration by July 30, 2013 or within 180 days after startup (whichever is later).

units.obligation_text: If you are demonstrating compliance with an emission limit in Tables 11 through 13 to this subpart that is less stringent (that is, higher) than the applicable emission limit in Table 14 to this subpart, you must demonstrate compliance with the applicable emission limit in Table 14 no later than July 29, 2016.
units.actor: owner or operator demonstrating with Tables 11-13 limits
units.action_summary: If initially complying with less stringent limits in Tables 11-13, demonstrate compliance with Table 14 by July 29, 2016.

units.obligation_text: If you are demonstrating compliance with an emission limit in Table 14 to this subpart that is less stringent (that is, higher) than the applicable emission limit in Table 1 to this subpart, you must demonstrate compliance with the applicable emission limit in Table 1 to this subpart no later than [date 3 years after date of publication of final rule in the Federal Register].
units.actor: owner or operator demonstrating with Table 14 limits
units.action_summary: If initially complying with less stringent Table 14 limits, demonstrate compliance with Table 1 by the specified 3-year date.

units.obligation_text: For existing affected sources (as defined in § 63.7490) that have not operated between the effective date of the rule and the compliance date that is specified for your source in § 63.7495, you must complete the initial compliance demonstration, if subject to the emission limits in Tables 2 or 14, to this subpart, as applicable, as specified in paragraphs (a) through (d) of this section, no later than 180 days after the re-start of the affected source and according to the applicable provisions in § 63.7(a)(2) as cited in Table 10 to this subpart.
units.actor: owner or operator of existing affected sources that were not operating between dates
units.action_summary: If the source was not operating during specified period, complete initial compliance demonstration within 180 days after restart and per cited provisions.

units.obligation_text: You must complete an initial tune-up by following the procedures described in § 63.7540(a)(10)(i) through (vi) no later than 30 days after the re-start of the affected source and, if applicable, complete the one-time energy assessment specified in Table 3 to this subpart, no later than the compliance date specified in § 63.7495.
units.actor: owner or operator of existing affected sources restarting
units.action_summary: Complete initial tune-up within 30 days after restart per §63.7540(a)(10)(i)-(vi), and complete one-time energy assessment by compliance date if applicable.

units.obligation_text: If your performance tests for a given pollutant for at least 2 consecutive years show that your emissions are at or below 75 percent of the emission limit (or, in limited instances as specified in Tables 1 and 2 or 11 through 15 to this subpart, at or below the emission limit) for the pollutant, and if there are no changes in the operation of the individual boiler or process heater or air pollution control equipment that could increase emissions, you may choose to conduct performance tests for the pollutant every third year.
units.action_summary: If emissions have been ≤75% of limit for 2 years and operations haven't changed, you may elect to test every third year for that pollutant.

units.obligation_text: Each such performance test must be conducted no more than 37 months after the previous performance test.
units.actor: owner or operator (you) electing triennial testing
units.action_summary: If testing every third year, each test must occur within 37 months of the previous test.

units.obligation_text: If you elect to demonstrate compliance using emission averaging under § 63.7522, you must continue to conduct performance tests annually.
units.actor: owner or operator electing emissions averaging
units.action_summary: Electing emissions averaging requires you to continue annual performance testing.

units.obligation_text: The requirement to test at maximum chloride input level is waived unless the stack test is conducted for HCl. The requirement to test at maximum mercury input level is waived unless the stack test is conducted for mercury. The requirement to test at maximum TSM input level is waived unless the stack test is conducted for TSM.
units.action_summary: Testing at maximum input levels for chloride, mercury, and TSM is waived except when the stack test is specifically for HCl, mercury, or TSM respectively.

units.obligation_text: If a performance test shows emissions exceeded the emission limit or 75 percent of the emission limit (as specified in Tables 1 and 2 or 11 through 15 to this subpart) for a pollutant, you must conduct annual performance tests for that pollutant until all performance tests over a consecutive 2-year period meet the required level (at or below 75 percent of the emission limit, as specified in Tables 1 and 2 or 11 through 15 to this subpart).
units.action_summary: If a test shows exceedance, conduct annual tests for that pollutant until two consecutive years of tests meet the required level.

units.obligation_text: If you demonstrate compliance with the mercury, HCl, or TSM based on fuel analysis, you must conduct a monthly fuel analysis according to § 63.7521 for each type of fuel burned that is subject to an emission limit in Tables 1, 2, or 11 through 15 to this subpart.
units.actor: owner or operator (you) using fuel analysis
units.action_summary: Conduct monthly fuel analyses for each fuel type subject to emission limits when compliance is by fuel analysis.

units.obligation_text: You may comply with this monthly requirement by completing the fuel analysis any time within the calendar month as long as the analysis is separated from the previous analysis by at least 14 calendar days.
units.actor: owner or operator (you) conducting monthly fuel analysis
units.action_summary: Monthly fuel analyses may be done anytime during the calendar month provided each is at least 14 days apart.

units.obligation_text: If you burn a new type of fuel, you must conduct a fuel analysis before burning the new type of fuel in your boiler or process heater.
units.action_summary: Perform fuel analysis before burning any new fuel type.

units.obligation_text: You must still meet all applicable continuous compliance requirements in § 63.7540.
units.action_summary: Maintain compliance with continuous compliance requirements per §63.7540 even when using fuel analysis.

units.obligation_text: If each of 12 consecutive monthly fuel analyses demonstrates 75 percent or less of the compliance level, you may decrease the fuel analysis frequency to quarterly for that fuel.
units.action_summary: After 12 consecutive monthly analyses ≤75% of compliance level, you may reduce sampling frequency to quarterly for that fuel.

units.obligation_text: If any quarterly sample exceeds 75 percent of the compliance level or you begin burning a new type of fuel, you must return to monthly monitoring for that fuel, until 12 months of fuel analyses are again less than 75 percent of the compliance level.
units.action_summary: Return to monthly fuel analysis if a quarterly sample exceeds 75% or if a new fuel type is used, until 12 months of results are <75%.

units.obligation_text: If sampling is conducted on 1 day per month, samples should be no less than 14 days apart, but if multiple samples are taken per month, the 14-day restriction does not apply.
units.action_summary: Single monthly sampling events should be spaced at least 14 days apart; multiple samples per month are exempt from the 14-day spacing.

units.obligation_text: For affected sources (as defined in § 63.7490) that have not operated since the previous compliance demonstration and more than 1 year has passed since the previous compliance demonstration, you must complete the subsequent compliance demonstration, if subject to the emission limits in Tables 1, 2, or 11 through 15 to this subpart, no later than 180 days after the re-start of the affected source and according to the applicable provisions in § 63.7(a)(2) as cited in Table 10 to this subpart.
units.actor: owner or operator (you) of affected sources restarting after >1 year
units.action_summary: If the source hasn't operated for over a year, complete subsequent compliance demonstration within 180 days after restart, per cited provisions.

units.obligation_text: You must complete a subsequent tune-up by following the procedures described in § 63.7540(a)(10)(i) through (vi) and the schedule described in § 63.7540(a)(13) for units that are not operating at the time of their scheduled tune-up.
units.action_summary: Complete the subsequent tune-up per §63.7540 procedures and schedule, including provisions for units not operating at scheduled tune-up time.

units.obligation_text: If you operate a CO CEMS that meets the Performance Specifications outlined in § 63.7525(a)(3) of this subpart to demonstrate compliance with the applicable alternative CO CEMS emission standard listed in Tables 1, 2, or 11 through 15 to this subpart, you are not required to conduct CO performance tests and are not subject to the oxygen concentration operating limit requirement specified in § 63.7510(a).
units.actor: owner or operator (you) operating a compliant CO CEMS
units.action_summary: Operating a compliant CO CEMS exempts you from CO performance tests and the oxygen concentration operating limit in §63.7510(a).

units.obligation_text: You must conduct a minimum of three separate test runs for each performance test required in this section, as specified in § 63.7(e)(3). Each test run must comply with the minimum applicable sampling times or volumes specified in Tables 1 and 2 or 11 through 15 to this subpart.
units.action_summary: For each required performance test, run at least three separate test runs and meet the minimum sampling times/volumes specified in the referenced tables.

units.obligation_text: For solid and liquid fuels, you must conduct fuel analyses for chloride and mercury according to the procedures in paragraphs (b) through (e) of this section and Table 6 to this subpart, as applicable.
units.actor: owner or operator (you) burning solid or liquid fuels
units.action_summary: Conduct chloride and mercury fuel analyses for solid and liquid fuels per the procedures and Table 6.

units.obligation_text: For solid fuels and liquid fuels, you must also conduct fuel analyses for TSM if you are opting to comply with the TSM alternative standard.
units.actor: owner or operator (you) burning solid or liquid fuels opting for TSM alternative
units.action_summary: If using the TSM alternative, conduct TSM fuel analyses for solid and liquid fuels.

units.obligation_text: For gas 2 (other) fuels, you must conduct fuel analyses for mercury according to the procedures in paragraphs (b) through (e) of this section and Table 6 to this subpart, as applicable.
units.actor: owner or operator (you) burning gas 2 fuels
units.action_summary: Conduct mercury fuel analyses for gas 2 fuels per procedures and Table 6.

units.obligation_text: For gaseous fuels, you may not use fuel analyses to comply with the TSM alternative standard or the HCl standard.
units.actor: owner or operator (you) burning gaseous fuels
units.action_summary: Prohibits using fuel analyses for TSM alternative or HCl standards when burning gaseous fuels.

units.obligation_text: For purposes of complying with this section, a fuel gas system that consists of multiple gaseous fuels collected and mixed with each other is considered a single fuel type and sampling and analysis is only required on the combined fuel gas system that will feed the boiler or process heater. Sampling and analysis of the individual gaseous streams prior to combining is not required.
units.actor: owner or operator (you) of combined fuel gas systems
units.action_summary: Treat mixed gaseous fuels as a single fuel type and only sample the combined fuel gas; no sampling of individual streams required.

units.obligation_text: You are not required to conduct fuel analyses for fuels used for only startup, unit shutdown, and transient flame stability purposes.
units.action_summary: No fuel analyses required for fuels used solely for startup, shutdown, or transient flame stability.

units.obligation_text: You are required to conduct fuel analyses only for fuels and units that are subject to emission limits for mercury, HCl, or TSM in Tables 1 and 2 or 11 through 15 to this subpart.
units.action_summary: Conduct fuel analyses only for fuels/units subject to mercury, HCl, or TSM limits in the referenced tables.

units.obligation_text: Gaseous and liquid fuels are exempt from the sampling requirements in paragraphs (c) and (d) of this section.
units.actor: owner or operator (you) burning gaseous or liquid fuels
units.action_summary: Gaseous and liquid fuels need not follow the sampling requirements in paragraphs (c) and (d).

units.obligation_text: Each composite sample will consist of a minimum of three samples collected at approximately equal intervals during the testing period for sampling during performance stack testing.
units.actor: owner or operator (you) conducting composite sampling during stack testing
units.action_summary: Composite samples during performance stack testing must include at least three samples taken at roughly equal intervals.

units.obligation_text: For a group of two or more existing boilers or process heaters in the same subcategory that each vent to a separate stack, you may average PM (or TSM), HCl, or mercury emissions among existing units to demonstrate compliance with the limits in Table 2 or 15 to this subpart as specified in paragraph (b)(1) through (3) of this section, if you satisfy the requirements in paragraphs (c) through (g) of this section.
units.actor: owner or operator (you) of groups of existing boilers/process heaters
units.action_summary: May average PM/TSM/HCl/mercury emissions among multiple existing units venting to separate stacks to meet Table 2 or 15 limits if requirements in (c)-(g) are met.

units.obligation_text: The averaged emissions rate from the existing boilers and process heaters participating in the emissions averaging option must not exceed 90 percent of the limits in Table 2 or 15 to this subpart at all times the affected units are subject to numeric emission limits following the compliance date specified in § 63.7495.
units.actor: owner or operator (you) participating in emissions averaging
units.action_summary: Averaged emission rate under emissions averaging must be ≤90% of the Table 2 or 15 limits at all times after the compliance date.

units.obligation_text: You must use Equation 1a or 1b or 1c of this section to demonstrate that the PM (or TSM), HCl, or mercury emissions from all existing units participating in the emissions averaging option for that pollutant do not exceed the emission limits in Table 2 or 15 to this subpart. Use Equation 1a if you are complying with the emission limits on a heat input basis, use Equation 1b if you are complying with the emission limits on a steam generation (output) basis, and use Equation 1c if you are complying with the emission limits on a electric generation (output) basis.
units.actor: owner or operator (you) participating in emissions averaging
units.action_summary: Demonstrate compliance under emissions averaging using Equation 1a, 1b, or 1c depending on whether limits are on heat input, steam output, or electric output basis.

units.obligation_text: If you are not capable of determining the maximum rated heat input capacity of one or more boilers that generate steam, you may use Equation 2 of this section as an alternative to using Equation 1a of this section to demonstrate that the PM (or TSM), HCl, or mercury emissions from all existing units participating in the emissions averaging option do not exceed the emission limits for that pollutant in Table 2 or 15 to this subpart that are in pounds per million Btu of heat input.
units.actor: owner or operator (you) unable to determine max rated heat input for one or more boilers
units.action_summary: May use Equation 2 instead of Equation 1a to demonstrate compliance when max rated heat input cannot be determined.

units.obligation_text: For a group of two or more existing affected units, each of which vents through a single common stack, you may average PM (or TSM), HCl, or mercury emissions to demonstrate compliance with the limits for that pollutant in Table 2 or 15 to this subpart if you satisfy the requirements in paragraph (i) or (j) of this section.
units.actor: owner or operator (you) of groups venting through common stack
units.action_summary: May average emissions among units venting to a common stack to meet Table 2 or 15 limits if meeting requirements in (i) or (j).

units.obligation_text: Conduct performance tests according to procedures specified in § 63.7520 in the common stack if affected units from other subcategories vent to the common stack. The emission limits that the group must comply with are determined by the use of Equation 6 of this section.
units.actor: owner or operator (you) of units venting to common stack
units.action_summary: If units from other subcategories vent to a common stack, conduct performance tests in the common stack per §63.7520 and determine group limits using Equation 6.

units.obligation_text: If your boiler or process heater is subject to a CO emission limit in Tables 1, 2, or 11 through 15 to this subpart, you must install, operate, and maintain an oxygen analyzer system, as defined in § 63.7575, or install, certify, operate and maintain continuous emission monitoring systems for CO and oxygen (or carbon dioxide (CO2)) according to the procedures in paragraphs (a)(1) through (6) of this section.
units.actor: owner or operator (you) of boilers/process heaters subject to CO limits
units.action_summary: Install, operate, and maintain required oxygen analyzer system or CO and oxygen/CO2 CEMS per procedures if subject to CO limits.

units.obligation_text: To demonstrate compliance with the applicable alternative CO CEMS emission standard listed in Tables 1, 2, or 11 through 15 to this subpart, you must install, certify, operate, and maintain a CO CEMS and an oxygen analyzer according to the applicable procedures under Performance Specification 4, 4A, or 4B at 40 CFR part 60, appendix B; part 75 of this chapter (if an CO2 analyzer is used); the site-specific monitoring plan developed according to § 63.7505(d); and the requirements in § 63.7540(a)(8) and paragraph (a) of this section.
units.actor: owner or operator (you) demonstrating via alternative CO CEMS
units.action_summary: Install, certify, operate, and maintain CO CEMS and oxygen analyzer per specified performance specifications, site plan, and requirements to use the CO CEMS alternative.

units.obligation_text: Any boiler or process heater that has a CO CEMS that is compliant with Performance Specification 4, 4A, or 4B at 40 CFR part 60, appendix B, a site-specific monitoring plan developed according to § 63.7505(d), and the requirements in § 63.7540(a)(8) and paragraph (a) of this section must use the CO CEMS to comply with the applicable alternative CO CEMS emission standard listed in Tables 1, 2, or 11 through 15 to this subpart.
units.actor: owner or operator (you) with compliant CO CEMS
units.action_summary: If your CO CEMS meets the listed compliance criteria, you are required to use it to comply with the alternative CO CEMS emission standard.

units.obligation_text: Any CO CEMS that does not comply with § 63.7525(a) cannot be used to meet any requirement in this subpart to demonstrate compliance with a CO emission limit listed in Tables 1, 2, or 11 through 15 to this subpart.
units.actor: owner or operator (you) with noncompliant CO CEMS
units.action_summary: CO CEMS that do not comply with §63.7525(a) are not permitted to be used to demonstrate compliance with CO limits.
