units.obligation_text: For each unit for which you decide to demonstrate compliance with the mercury or HCl emissions limits in Tables 1 or 2 or 11 through 15 of this subpart by use of a CEMS for mercury or HCl, you must install, certify, maintain, and operate a CEMS measuring emissions discharged to the atmosphere and record the output of the system as specified in paragraphs (l)(1) through (8) of this section. For HCl, this option for an affected unit takes effect on the date a final performance specification for a HCl CEMS is published in the Federal Register or the date of approval of a site-specific monitoring plan.
units.actor: owner or operator (you) electing to use mercury or HCl CEMS
units.action_summary: If using a mercury or HCl CEMS to demonstrate compliance, install, certify, operate, maintain it, and record outputs per specified paragraphs; HCl CEMS option effective upon publication/approval of performance spec or site plan.

units.obligation_text: If your unit is subject to a HCl emission limit in Tables 1, 2, or 11 through 15 of this subpart and you have an acid gas wet scrubber or dry sorbent injection control technology and you elect to use an SO2 CEMS to demonstrate continuous compliance with the HCl emission limit, you must install the monitor at the outlet of the boiler or process heater, downstream of all emission control devices, and you must install, certify, operate, and maintain the CEMS according to either part 60 or part 75 of this chapter.
units.actor: owner or operator (you) with HCl limit and acid gas control technology electing SO2 CEMS
units.action_summary: If electing to use an SO2 CEMS to demonstrate HCl compliance for units with specified controls, install it downstream of controls and install/certify/operate/maintain per part 60 or part 75.

units.obligation_text: Use EPA Method 5 of appendix A to part 60 of this chapter to determine PM emissions. For each performance test, conduct three separate runs under the conditions that exist when the affected source is operating at the highest load or capacity level reasonably expected to occur. Conduct each test run to collect a minimum sample volume specified in Tables 1, 2, or 11 through 15 to this subpart, as applicable, for determining compliance with a new source limit or an existing source limit. Calculate the average of the results from three runs to determine compliance. You need not determine the PM collected in the impingers ("back half") of the Method 5 particulate sampling train to demonstrate compliance with the PM standards of this subpart. This shall not preclude the permitting authority from requiring a determination of the "back half" for other purposes.
units.actor: owner or operator (you) conducting PM performance tests
units.action_summary: Use EPA Method 5, perform three runs at highest expected load collecting minimum sample volumes, average results to determine compliance; determination of 'back half' is not required for compliance but permitting authority may require it.

units.obligation_text: For a particulate wet scrubber, you must establish the minimum pressure drop and liquid flow rate as defined in § 63.7575, as your operating limits during the three-run performance test during which you demonstrate compliance with your applicable limit. If you use a wet scrubber and you conduct separate performance tests for PM and TSM emissions, you must establish one set of minimum scrubber liquid flow rate and pressure drop operating limits. If you conduct multiple performance tests, you must set the minimum liquid flow rate and pressure drop operating limits at the higher of the minimum values established during the performance tests.
units.actor: owner or operator (you) using particulate wet scrubber
units.action_summary: Set minimum pressure drop and liquid flow rate operating limits during performance tests; if multiple tests or multiple pollutants, select appropriate single/higher limits as specified.

units.obligation_text: If you own or operate a unit subject to emission limits in Tables 1 or 2 or 11 through 15 to this subpart, you must meet the work practice standard according to Table 3 of this subpart. During startup and shutdown, you must only follow the work practice standards according to items 5 and 6 of Table 3 of this subpart.
units.actor: owner or operator (you) of units subject to emission limits
units.action_summary: Comply with the work practice standards in Table 3; during startup/shutdown, only follow items 5 and 6 of Table 3.

units.obligation_text: If you elect to comply with the alternative equivalent output-based emission limits, instead of the heat input-based limits listed in Table 2 or 15 to this subpart, and you want to take credit for implementing energy conservation measures identified in an energy assessment, you may demonstrate compliance using efficiency credits according to the procedures in this section.
units.actor: owner or operator (you) electing alternative output-based limits and seeking efficiency credits
units.action_summary: If electing alternative output-based limits, you may use efficiency credits from energy conservation measures to demonstrate compliance per the procedures in this section.

units.obligation_text: You may use this compliance approach for an existing affected boiler for demonstrating initial compliance according to § 63.7522(e) and for demonstrating monthly compliance according to § 63.7522(f). Owners or operators using this compliance approach must establish an emissions benchmark, calculate and document the efficiency credits, develop an Implementation Plan, comply with the general reporting requirements, and apply the efficiency credit according to the procedures in paragraphs (b) through (f) of this section. You cannot use this compliance approach for a new or reconstructed affected boiler.
units.actor: owner or operator (you) of existing affected boilers
units.action_summary: Existing boilers may use the efficiency credit approach for initial and monthly compliance but must establish benchmarks, calculate/document credits, develop an Implementation Plan, comply with reporting, and apply credits per procedures; new/reconstructed boilers cannot use this approach.

units.obligation_text: The emissions rate as calculated using Equation 20 of this section from each existing boiler participating in the efficiency credit option must be in compliance with the limits in Table 2 or 15 to this subpart at all times the affected unit is subject to numeric emission limits, following the compliance date specified in § 63.7495.
units.actor: owner or operator (you) participating in efficiency credit option
units.action_summary: Adjusted emissions (with efficiency credits) must comply with Table 2 or 15 limits at all times after the compliance date.

units.obligation_text: You must use Equation 20 of this section to demonstrate initial compliance by demonstrating that the emissions from the affected boiler participating in the efficiency credit compliance approach do not exceed the emission limits in Table 2 or 15 to this subpart.
units.actor: owner or operator (you) using efficiency credits
units.action_summary: Use Equation 20 to show initial compliance that emissions (after credits) do not exceed Table 2 or 15 limits.

units.obligation_text: You must demonstrate continuous compliance with each emission limit in Tables 1 and 2 or 11 through 15 to this subpart, the work practice standards in Table 3 to this subpart, and the operating limits in Table 4 to this subpart that applies to you according to the methods specified in Table 8 to this subpart and paragraphs (a)(1) through (19) of this section.
units.action_summary: Continuously demonstrate compliance with applicable emission limits, work practice standards, and operating limits using specified methods and paragraph procedures.

units.obligation_text: To demonstrate compliance with the applicable alternative CO CEMS emission limit listed in Tables 1, 2, or 11 through 15 to this subpart, you must meet the requirements in paragraphs (a)(8)(i) through (iv) of this section.
units.actor: owner or operator (you) demonstrating via alternative CO CEMS
units.action_summary: Meet the specified (a)(8)(i)-(iv) requirements to demonstrate compliance using the alternative CO CEMS standard.

units.obligation_text: Maintain a CO emission level below or at your applicable alternative CO CEMS-based standard in Tables 1 or 2 or 11 through 15 to this subpart at all times the affected unit is subject to numeric emission limits.
units.action_summary: Keep CO emissions at or below the applicable CO CEMS-based standard at all times when subject to numeric limits.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator of a boiler or process heater using a PM CPMS or a PM CEMS to meet requirements of this subpart shall install, certify (PM CEMS only), operate, and maintain the PM CPMS or PM CEMS in accordance with your site-specific monitoring plan as required in § 63.7505(d).
units.actor: owner or operator using PM CPMS or PM CEMS
units.action_summary: Install, (certify if PM CEMS), operate, and maintain PM CPMS or PM CEMS per the site-specific monitoring plan.

units.obligation_text: If you choose to comply with the PM filterable emissions limit by using PM CEMS you must install, certify, operate, and maintain a PM CEMS and record the output of the PM CEMS as specified in paragraphs (a)(19)(i) through (vii) of this section. The compliance limit will be expressed as a 30-day rolling average of the numerical emissions limit value applicable for your unit in Tables 1 or 2 or 11 through 15 of this subpart.
units.actor: owner or operator (you) choosing PM CEMS for PM filterable emissions
units.action_summary: If using PM CEMS for compliance, install/certify/operate/maintain and record outputs per specified paragraphs; compliance expressed as 30-day rolling average.

units.obligation_text: You must report each instance in which you did not meet each emission limit and operating limit in Tables 1 through 4 or 11 through 15 to this subpart that apply to you. These instances are deviations from the emission limits or operating limits, respectively, in this subpart. These deviations must be reported according to the requirements in § 63.7550.
units.action_summary: Report all deviations where emission or operating limits in the referenced tables were not met, per §63.7550 reporting requirements.

units.obligation_text: A summary of the maximum CO emission levels recorded during the performance test to show that you have met any applicable emission standard in Tables 1, 2, or 11 through 15 to this subpart, if you are not using a CO CEMS to demonstrate compliance.
units.action_summary: Submit a summary of maximum CO emission levels from the performance test to demonstrate compliance when not using a CO CEMS.

units.obligation_text: For each boiler or process heater subject to an emission limit in Tables 1, 2, or 11 through 15 to this subpart, you must also keep the applicable records in paragraphs (d)(1) through (11) of this section.
units.action_summary: Retain the specified records for each boiler/process heater subject to emission limits in the referenced tables.

units.obligation_text: If, consistent with § 63.7515(b), you choose to stack test less frequently than annually, you must keep a record that documents that your emissions in the previous stack test(s) were less than 75 percent of the applicable emission limit (or, in specific instances noted in Tables 1 and 2 or 11 through 15 to this subpart, less than the applicable emission limit), and document that there was no change in source operations including fuel composition and operation of air pollution control equipment that would cause emissions of the relevant pollutant to increase within the past year.
units.actor: owner or operator (you) opting for less frequent stack testing
units.action_summary: If testing less frequently than annually, keep records showing prior test emissions were <75% (or as specified) and that operations haven't changed in a way that could increase emissions in the past year.

title: Protection of the Stratospheric Ozone: Motor Vehicle Air Conditioning System Servicing

units.obligation_text: You can obtain the material from the sources listed below.
units.action_summary: May obtain incorporated materials from the listed sources.

units.obligation_text: You may inspect a copy of the approved material at U.S. EPA’s Air and Radiation Docket; EPA West Building, Room 3334, 1301 Constitution Ave. NW, Washington, DC, phone: 202–566–1742, or at the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA).
units.action_summary: Permits inspection of approved incorporated material at EPA docket or NARA.

units.obligation_text: Properly using means using equipment in conformity with the regulations set forth in this subpart, including but not limited to the prohibitions and required practices set forth in § 82.34, and the recommended service procedures and practices for the containment of refrigerant set forth in § 82.36(a) and appendices A, B, C, D, E, F to this subpart, as applicable. In addition, this term includes operating the equipment in accordance with the manufacturer’s guide to operation and maintenance and using the equipment only for the controlled substance for which the machine is designed.
units.action_summary: Defines 'properly using' to require conformity with subpart regulations, specified prohibitions/required practices, recommended procedures, manufacturer's instructions, and use only for the designed refrigerant.

units.obligation_text: operating the equipment in accordance with the manufacturer’s guide to operation and maintenance
units.action_summary: Operate equipment according to the manufacturer's operation and maintenance guide.

units.obligation_text: using the equipment only for the controlled substance for which the machine is designed
units.action_summary: Use the equipment only with the specific controlled substance it was designed for.

units.obligation_text: For equipment that extracts and recycles refrigerant, properly using also means to recycle refrigerant before it is returned to a motor vehicle air conditioner or MVAC-like appliance, including to the motor vehicle air conditioner or MVAC-like appliance from which the refrigerant was extracted.
units.actor: operators of equipment that extracts and recycles refrigerant
units.action_summary: Recycle refrigerant before returning it to any MVAC or MVAC-like appliance, including the source appliance.

units.obligation_text: For equipment that only recovers refrigerant, properly using includes the requirement to recycle the refrigerant on-site or send the refrigerant off-site for reclamation.
units.actor: operators of equipment that only recovers refrigerant
units.action_summary: Either recycle recovered refrigerant on-site or send it off-site for reclamation.

units.obligation_text: Equipment that recovers but does not recycle refrigerants other than CFC–12, HFC–134a, and HFO–1234yf must meet the standards set forth in Appendix F of this subpart (Recover-Only Equipment that Extracts a Single, Specific Refrigerant Other Than CFC–12, HFC–134a, or HFO–1234yf).
units.actor: equipment that recovers but does not recycle refrigerants other than CFC–12, HFC–134a, and HFO–1234yf
units.action_summary: Such recover-only equipment must comply with the standards in Appendix F.

units.obligation_text: The equipment must be able to extract from a mobile air conditioning system the refrigerant other than CFC–12, HFC–134a, or HFO–1234yf to which the equipment is dedicated.
units.actor: equipment (recover-only units dedicated to a refrigerant)
units.action_summary: Equipment must be capable of extracting the specific non-CFC–12/HFC–134a/HFO–1234yf refrigerant it is dedicated to from MVAC systems.

units.obligation_text: Equipment that recovers and recycles HFO–1234yf refrigerant from MVACs and recharges MVAC systems with HFO–1234yf refrigerant must meet the standards set forth in SAE J2843, Recovery Equipment for Contaminated R–134a or R–1234yf Refrigerant from Mobile Air Conditioning Systems, (incorporated by reference, see § 82.31).
units.actor: equipment that recovers and recycles HFO–1234yf and recharges MVAC systems with HFO–1234yf
units.action_summary: Such equipment must meet the SAE J2843 standard.

units.obligation_text: Equipment that recovers but does not recycle contaminated HFC–134a and/or HFO–1234yf refrigerant from MVACs must meet the standards set forth in SAE J2851, Recovery Equipment for Contaminated R–134a or R–1234yf Refrigerant from Mobile Air Conditioning Systems, (incorporated by reference, see § 82.31).
units.actor: equipment that recovers but does not recycle contaminated HFC–134a and/or HFO–1234yf refrigerant from MVACs
units.action_summary: Such recover-only equipment for contaminated HFC–134a and/or HFO–1234yf must meet SAE J2851.

units.obligation_text: Equipment that recovers, recycles, and recharges both HFO–1234yf and R–134a from MVACs must meet the standards set forth in SAE J3030, Automotive Refrigerant Recovery/Recycling/Recharging Equipment Intended for Use with Both R–1234yf and R–134a, (incorporated by reference, see § 82.31).
units.actor: equipment that recovers, recycles, and recharges both HFO–1234yf and R–134a from MVACs
units.action_summary: Equipment handling both refrigerants must meet SAE J3030.

units.obligation_text: Any independent standards testing organization may apply for approval by the Administrator to certify equipment as meeting the standards in § 82.36(a) and appendices A, B, C, D, E, F to this subpart, as applicable.
units.action_summary: Independent testing organizations are permitted to apply for EPA approval to certify equipment to the listed standards.

units.obligation_text: The application shall be sent to: MVACs Recycling Program Manager, Stratospheric Protection Division (6205T), U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, 1200 Pennsylvania Ave. NW, Washington, DC 20460.
units.actor: applicant (the independent standards testing organization submitting an application)
units.action_summary: Requires applicants to send their application to the specified EPA address.

title: Additional Air Quality Designations for the 2015 Ozone National Ambient Air Quality Standards: Notice of Action Denying Petition for Reconsideration of Uinta Basin, Utah Designation; Notice of Action Denying Petition for Reconsideration

units.obligation_text: Section 307(b)(1) of the CAA ... provides, in part, that petitions for review must be filed in the Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit:
units.action_summary: Petitions for review must be filed in the U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit (subject to the conditions in subparts (i) and (ii)).

units.obligation_text: (i) When the agency action consists of "nationally applicable regulations promulgated, or final actions taken, by the Administrator,"
units.action_summary: If the agency action is a nationally applicable regulation or final action by the Administrator, petitions for review are to be filed in the D.C. Circuit.

units.obligation_text: (ii) when such action is locally or regionally applicable, if "such action is based on a determination of nationwide scope or effect and if in taking such action the Administrator finds and publishes that such action is based on such a determination."
units.action_summary: If the action is locally or regionally applicable but is based on a determination of nationwide scope or effect (and the Administrator so finds and publishes), petitions must be filed in the D.C. Circuit.

units.obligation_text: Thus, pursuant to CAA section 307(b), any petition for review of the final letter denying the petition for reconsideration from Patel Industrial Park must be filed in the Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit on or before June 23, 2020.
units.actor: any petitioner for review (Patel Industrial Park)
units.action_summary: Any petition for review of the EPA's denial must be filed in the D.C. Circuit by June 23, 2020.

units.section: SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: I. Where can I get copies of this document and other related information?
units.obligation_text: No hand deliveries will be accepted.
units.actor: members of the public submitting documents to the EPA Docket Center
units.action_summary: Hand-delivered submissions to the EPA Docket Center are not accepted during the temporary suspension.

units.obligation_text: The comment period for the proposed rule (85 FR 10516) is extended to 5 p.m., eastern daylight time, on June 23, 2020.
units.action_summary: The deadline to submit comments on the proposed rule is extended to 5:00 PM EDT on June 23, 2020.

units.obligation_text: You may submit comments as outlined in the February 24, 2020 proposed rule (85 FR 10516).
units.action_summary: Commenters are permitted to submit comments using the methods outlined in the February 24, 2020 proposed rule.

units.obligation_text: Please choose only one method listed.
units.action_summary: Commenters must submit via only one of the listed submission methods.

units.section: SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION (CMS) - Inspection of Public Comments
units.obligation_text: All comments received before the close of the comment period shall be made available for viewing by the public.
units.action_summary: CMS must make all timely comments available for public viewing.

units.section: SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION (CMS) - Inspection of Public Comments
units.obligation_text: including any personally identifiable or confidential business information that is included in a comment.
units.action_summary: The public posting of comments will include any personally identifiable information or confidential business information contained in comments.

units.section: SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION (CMS) - Inspection of Public Comments
units.obligation_text: We will post all comments received before the close of the comment period on the following website as soon as possible after they have been received: http://www.regulations.gov.
units.action_summary: CMS will post timely comments to Regulations.gov as soon as possible after receipt.

units.section: SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION (CMS) - Inspection of Public Comments
units.obligation_text: Follow the search instructions on that website to view public comments.
units.action_summary: Users must follow the website's search instructions to view posted comments.

units.obligation_text: The Administrator of the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), Seema Verma, having reviewed and approved this document, authorizes Evell J. Barco Holland, who is the Federal Register Liaison, to electronically sign this document for purposes of publication in the Federal Register.
units.action_summary: Evell J. Barco Holland is authorized to electronically sign this document for publication purposes.

title: Standards of Performance for New Residential Wood Heaters, New Residential Hydronic Heaters, and Forced-Air Furnaces

units.obligation_text: Unless exempted under § 60.530(b) or electing to use the cord wood alternative means of compliance option in paragraph (c) of the section, each affected wood heater manufactured or sold at retail for use in the United States on or after May 15, 2020, must not discharge into the atmosphere any gases that contain particulate matter in excess of a weighted average of 2.0 g/hr (0.0044 lb/hr).
units.actor: each affected wood heater manufactured or sold at retail for use in the United States on or after May 15, 2020
units.action_summary: Prohibits affected wood heaters manufactured or sold at retail on or after May 15, 2020 from emitting particulate matter in excess of a weighted average of 2.0 g/hr.

units.obligation_text: Unless exempted under § 60.530(b)
units.actor: affected wood heaters (or entities subject to § 60.530(b))
units.action_summary: Provides an exception from the § 60.532(b) emission prohibition for units exempted under § 60.530(b).

units.obligation_text: electing to use the cord wood alternative means of compliance option in paragraph (c) of the section
units.action_summary: Allows electing the cord wood alternative means of compliance in paragraph (c) as an alternative to the § 60.532(b) standard.

units.obligation_text: However, an affected wood heater manufactured or imported on or before May 15, 2020, and certified as of May 15, 2020, to meet the 2015 particulate matter emission limit in paragraph (a) of this section may be sold at retail on or before November 30, 2020.
units.actor: an affected wood heater manufactured or imported on or before May 15, 2020, and certified as of May 15, 2020 to meet the 2015 PM emission limit
units.action_summary: Permits retail sale of certain wood heaters manufactured/imported on or before May 15, 2020 and certified to the 2015 PM limit until November 30, 2020.

units.obligation_text: Compliance for all heaters must be determined by the test methods and procedures in § 60.534.
units.actor: all heaters (or parties responsible for demonstrating compliance)
units.action_summary: Requires that compliance determinations be made using the test methods and procedures specified in § 60.534.

units.obligation_text: For a model line that was previously certified as meeting the 1990 Phase II emission standards under the 1988 new source performance standards (NSPS), in effect prior to May 15, 2015, at an emission level equal to or less than the 2015 emission standards in § 60.532(a), the model line is deemed to have a certificate of compliance for the 2015 emission standards in § 60.532(a), which is valid until the effective date for the 2020 standards in § 60.532(b) (i.e., until May 15, 2020).
units.actor: a model line previously certified as meeting the 1990 Phase II emission standards as described
units.action_summary: Declares that qualifying model lines are deemed to hold a certificate of compliance for the 2015 emission standards, valid until May 15, 2020.

units.obligation_text: However, a model line, manufactured or imported on or before May 15, 2020, with a certificate of compliance for the 2015 emission standards that was in effect as of May 15, 2020, may be sold at retail on or before November 30, 2020.
units.actor: a model line manufactured or imported on or before May 15, 2020 with a certificate of compliance for the 2015 emission standards in effect as of May 15, 2020
units.action_summary: Permits retail sale of qualifying model lines until November 30, 2020 even if their certificate validity is described as ending May 15, 2020.

title: Fuels Regulatory Streamlining

units.obligation_text: For each calendar year (January 1 through December 31) commencing after the date prescribed for any fuel in subpart D of this part, fuel manufacturers must submit to the Administrator a report for each registered fuel showing the range of concentration of each additive reported under § 79.11(a) and the volume of such fuel produced in the year.
units.action_summary: Submit an annual report for each registered fuel showing additive concentration ranges and volume produced.

units.obligation_text: Reports must be submitted by March 31 for the preceding year, or part thereof, on forms supplied by the Administrator.
units.action_summary: Submit the annual report by March 31 on EPA-provided forms.

units.obligation_text: If the date prescribed for a particular additive in subpart D of this part, or the later registration of an additive is between October 1 and December 31, no report will be required for the period to the end of that year.
units.action_summary: No report is required for the remainder of the year if registration occurs between Oct 1 and Dec 31.

units.obligation_text: Assurances that any change in information submitted pursuant to: (1) Paragraphs (a), (b), (c), (d), and (j) of this section will be provided to the Administrator in writing within 30 days of such change; and (2) Paragraph (e) of this section as provided in § 79.5(b).
units.action_summary: Provide assurances that changes to specified submitted information will be reported to the Administrator within 30 days (and per §79.5(b) for paragraph (e)).

units.obligation_text: Any change in information submitted pursuant to paragraphs (a), (b), (c), (d), and (j) of this section will be provided to the Administrator in writing within 30 days of such change.
units.action_summary: Notify the Administrator in writing within 30 days of changes to information submitted under paragraphs (a)-(d) and (j).

units.obligation_text: Any change in information submitted pursuant to paragraph (e) of this section as provided in § 79.5(b).
units.action_summary: Provide changes to information submitted under paragraph (e) as specified in §79.5(b).

units.obligation_text: Assurances that the additive manufacturer will not represent, directly or indirectly, in any notice, circular, letter, or other written communication or any written, oral, or pictorial notice or other announcement in any publication or by radio or television, that registration of the additive constitutes endorsement, certification, or approval by any agency of the United States, except as specified in paragraph (g)(2) of this section.
units.action_summary: Do not represent that additive registration constitutes U.S. government endorsement, except as allowed in paragraph (g)(2).

units.obligation_text: In the case of an additive that has its purpose-in-use identified as a deposit control additive for use in gasoline pursuant to the requirements of paragraph (d) of this section, the additive manufacturer may publicly represent that the additive meets the EPA’s gasoline deposit control requirements, provided that the additive manufacturer is in compliance with the requirements of 40 CFR 1090.240.
units.action_summary: If the additive is a gasoline deposit control additive and complies with 40 CFR 1090.240, the manufacturer may state it meets EPA gasoline deposit control requirements.

units.obligation_text: If the purpose-in-use of the additive identified pursuant to the requirements of paragraph (d) of this section is a deposit control additive for use in gasoline, the manufacturer must submit the following in addition to the other information specified in this section:
units.action_summary: Manufacturers of gasoline deposit control additives must submit additional specified information as part of registration.

units.obligation_text: The lowest additive concentration (LAC) that is compliant with the gasoline deposit control requirements of 40 CFR 1090.240.
units.action_summary: Submit the lowest additive concentration (LAC) that meets 40 CFR 1090.240.

units.obligation_text: The deposit control test method in 40 CFR 1090.1395 that the additive is compliant with.
units.action_summary: Submit the deposit control test method (per 40 CFR 1090.1395) the additive complies with.

units.obligation_text: A complete listing of the additive’s components and the weight or volume percent (as applicable) of each component.
units.action_summary: Provide a complete list of additive components with weight or volume percent of each.

units.obligation_text: When possible, standard chemical nomenclature must be used or the chemical structure of the component must be given. Polymeric components may be reported as the product of other chemical reactants, provided that the supporting data specified in paragraph (j)(3) of this section is also reported.
units.action_summary: Use standard chemical names or structures for components; polymeric components may be reported as reactant products if supporting data is provided.

units.obligation_text: Each detergent-active component of the package must be classified into one of the following designations: (A) Polyalkyl amine. (B) Polyether amine. (C) Polyalkylsuccinimide. (D) Polyalkylaminophenol. (E) Detergent-active petroleum-based carrier oil. (F) Detergent-active synthetic carrier oil. (G) Other detergent-active component (identify category, if feasible).
units.action_summary: Classify each detergent-active component into one of the specified categories (A–G).

units.obligation_text: Composition variability constraints and related rules regarding what may or may not be included in a detergent additive reported in a single additive registration, and related registration/disqualification rules.
units.action_summary: Sets constraints on composition variability under a single registration, when separate registration is required, and EPA's authority to disqualify additives.

units.obligation_text: The composition of a detergent additive reported in a single additive registration may not include detergent-active components that differ in identity from those contained in the detergent additive package at the time of deposit control testing.
units.action_summary: Under a single registration, detergent-active components cannot differ in identity from those present during deposit control testing.

units.obligation_text: The composition of a detergent additive reported in a single additive registration may not include a range of concentrations for any detergent-active component such that, if the component were present in the detergent additive package at the lower bound of the reported range, the deposit control effectiveness of the additive package would be reduced as compared with the level of effectiveness demonstrated pursuant to the requirements of 40 CFR 1090.240.
units.action_summary: Cannot report concentration ranges that would allow the additive at the lower bound to be less effective than demonstrated in deposit control testing.

units.obligation_text: Subject to the foregoing constraint, a gasoline detergent additive sold under a particular additive registration may contain a higher concentration of the detergent-active component(s) than the concentration(s) of such component(s) reported in the registration for the additive.
units.action_summary: Permitted to sell additive with higher detergent-active concentrations than reported, so long as constraints above are met.

units.obligation_text: The identity or concentration of non-detergent-active components of the detergent additive package may vary under a single registration provided that such variability does not reduce the deposit control effectiveness of the additive package as compared with the level of effectiveness demonstrated pursuant to the requirements of 40 CFR 1090.240.
units.action_summary: Non-detergent-active components may vary under one registration if such variability does not reduce deposit control effectiveness.

units.obligation_text: Unless the additive manufacturer provides EPA with data to substantiate that a carrier oil does not act to enhance the detergent additive’s ability to control deposits, any carrier oil contained in the detergent additive, whether petroleum-based or synthetic, must be treated as a detergent-active component in accordance with the requirements in paragraph (j)(3)(ii) of this section.
units.action_summary: Treat carrier oils as detergent-active components unless manufacturer provides data to EPA proving otherwise.

units.obligation_text: Except as provided in paragraph (j)(3)(iii)(E) of this section, detergent additive packages that do not satisfy the requirements in paragraphs (j)(3)(iii)(A) through (C) must be separately registered.
units.action_summary: Additive packages not meeting the composition variability requirements must be registered separately.

units.obligation_text: EPA may disqualify an additive for use in satisfying the requirements of this subpart if EPA determines that the variability included within a given detergent additive registration may reduce the deposit control effectiveness of the detergent package such that it may invalidate the lowest additive concentration reported in accordance with the requirements of paragraph (j)(1) of this section and 40 CFR 1090.240.
units.action_summary: EPA may disqualify an additive if variability could reduce effectiveness and invalidate the reported LAC.

units.obligation_text: A change in minimum concentration requirements resulting from a modification of detergent additive composition does not require a new detergent additive registration or a change in existing registration if the modification is affected by a detergent blender pursuant to the requirements of 40 CFR 1090.1240.
units.action_summary: Changes in minimum concentration from modifications by a detergent blender per 1090.1240 do not require a new or changed registration.

units.obligation_text: For detergent-active polymers and detergent-active carrier oils that are reported as the product of other chemical reactants: identification and manufacturer acceptance criteria, documentation maintenance, and submission requirements.
units.action_summary: Provide identification of reactant materials and acceptance criteria; maintain documentation and submit it to EPA upon request.

units.obligation_text: Identification of the reactant materials and the manufacturer’s acceptance criteria for determining that these materials are suitable for use in synthesizing detergent components. The manufacturer must maintain documentation, and submit it to EPA upon request, demonstrating that the acceptance criteria reported to EPA are the same criteria which the manufacturer specifies to the suppliers of the reactant materials.
units.action_summary: Identify reactant materials and acceptance criteria; keep documentation and submit to EPA on request proving criteria are those given to suppliers.

units.obligation_text: A Gel Permeation Chromatograph (GPC), providing the molecular weight distribution of the polymer or detergent-active carrier oil components and the concentration of each chromatographic peak representing more than one percent of the total mass. For these results to be acceptable, the GPC test procedure must include equipment calibration with a polystyrene standard or other readily attainable and generally accepted calibration standard. The identity of the calibration standard must be provided, together with the GPC characterization of the standard.
units.action_summary: Submit GPC data showing molecular weight distribution and peak concentrations; include calibration standard identity and its characterization.

units.obligation_text: For non-detergent-active carrier oils, the following parameters must be provided.
units.action_summary: Provide specified physical and compositional parameters for non-detergent-active carrier oils.

units.obligation_text: T10, T50, and T90 distillation points, and end boiling point, measured according to applicable test procedures cited in 40 CFR 1090.1350.
units.action_summary: Provide T10, T50, T90, and end boiling point measured per 40 CFR 1090.1350.

units.obligation_text: API gravity and viscosity.
units.action_summary: Provide API gravity and viscosity for non-detergent-active carrier oils.

units.obligation_text: Concentration of oxygen, sulfur, and nitrogen, if greater than or equal to 0.5 percent (by weight) of the carrier oil.
units.action_summary: Provide concentrations of oxygen, sulfur, and nitrogen if ≥0.5% by weight.

units.obligation_text: Description of an FTIR-based method appropriate for identifying the detergent additive package and its detergent-active components (polymers, carrier oils, and others) both qualitatively and quantitatively, together with the actual infrared spectra of the detergent additive package and each detergent-active component obtained by this test method.
units.action_summary: Provide description of an FTIR method and the actual infrared spectra for the additive package and each detergent-active component.

units.obligation_text: The FTIR infrared spectra submitted in connection with the registration of a detergent additive package must reflect the results of a test conducted on a sample of the additive containing the detergent-active component(s) at a concentration no lower than the concentration(s) (or the lower bound of a range of concentration) reported in the registration pursuant to paragraph (j)(1) of this section.
units.action_summary: Ensure FTIR spectra are from a sample with detergent-active component concentrations at or above the reported (or lower-bound) registration values.

units.obligation_text: Specific physical parameters must be identified which the manufacturer considers adequate and appropriate, in combination with other information in this section, for identifying the detergent additive package and monitoring its production quality control.
units.action_summary: Identify physical parameters adequate for product identification and quality control monitoring.

units.obligation_text: Such parameters must include (but need not be limited to) viscosity, density, and basic nitrogen content, unless the additive manufacturer specifically requests, and EPA approves, the substitution of other parameter(s) which the manufacturer considers to be more appropriate for a particular additive package.
units.action_summary: Include viscosity, density, and basic nitrogen as parameters unless EPA approves a manufacturer-requested substitution.

units.obligation_text: The request must be made in writing and must include an explanation of how the requested physical parameter(s) are helpful as indicator(s) of detergent production quality control.
units.action_summary: If requesting substitution of parameters, submit a written request including an explanation of usefulness for quality control.

units.obligation_text: EPA will respond to such requests in writing; the additional parameters are not approved until the manufacturer receives EPA’s written approval.
units.action_summary: EPA will respond in writing and must give written approval before substituted parameters are approved.

units.obligation_text: The manufacturer must identify a standardized measurement method, consistent with the chemical and physical nature of the detergent product, which will be used to measure each parameter. The documented ASTM repeatability for the method must also be cited. The manufacturer’s target value for each parameter in the additive, and the expected range of production values for each parameter, must be specified.
units.action_summary: Specify standardized measurement methods, cite ASTM repeatability, and provide target and expected production ranges for each parameter.

units.obligation_text: The expected range of variability must differ from the target value by an amount no greater than five times the standard repeatability of the test procedure, or by no more than 10 percent of the target value, whichever is less. However, in the case of nitrogen analysis or other procedures for measuring concentrations of specific chemical compounds or elements, when the target value is less than 10 parts per million, a range of variability up to 50 percent of the target value will be considered acceptable.
units.action_summary: Limit expected variability to specified bounds relative to test repeatability or target value, with specific exception for very low target values.

units.obligation_text: If a manufacturer wishes to rely on measurement methods or production variability ranges which do not conform to the above limitations, then the manufacturer must receive prior written approval from EPA. A request for such allowance must be made in writing. It must fully justify the adequacy of the test procedure, explain why a broader range of variability is required, and provide evidence that the production detergent will perform adequately throughout the requested range of variability pursuant to the requirements of 40 CFR 1090.1395.
units.action_summary: Obtain prior written EPA approval for measurement methods or variability ranges that deviate from specified limits; requests must justify and provide evidence.

units.obligation_text: Registration may be terminated by the Administrator if the additive manufacturer requests such termination in writing.
units.action_summary: The Administrator may terminate registration upon a manufacturer's written request.

units.obligation_text: Registration for an additive for an additive that has its purpose-in-use identified as a deposit control additive for use in gasoline pursuant to the requirements of § 79.21(d) may be terminated by the Administrator if the EPA determines that the detergent additive is not compliant with the gasoline deposit control requirements of 40 CFR 1090.240.
units.action_summary: EPA may terminate registration for gasoline deposit control additives found not compliant with 40 CFR 1090.240.

units.obligation_text: Fuel manufacturers must submit the reports specified in 40 CFR part 1090, subpart J.
units.action_summary: Submit the reports required by 40 CFR part 1090, subpart J.

units.obligation_text: Fuel manufacturers must submit the reports specified in 40 CFR part 1090, subpart J.
units.action_summary: Submit the reports required by 40 CFR part 1090, subpart J (for motor vehicle diesel).

units.obligation_text: Nothing in this part is intended to preempt the ability of state or local governments to control or prohibit any fuel or fuel additive for use in motor vehicles and motor vehicle engines which is not explicitly regulated by this part.
units.action_summary: States/local governments retain authority to control or prohibit fuels/additives not explicitly regulated by this part.

units.obligation_text: Lawful use of any of the substances or any combination of these substances requires that they be 'substantially similar' under section 211(f)(1) of the Clean Air Act, or be permitted under a waiver granted by the Administrator under the authority of section 211(f)(4) of the Clean Air Act.
units.action_summary: To lawfully use oxygenates, they must be substantially similar under section 211(f)(1) or permitted under an Administrator waiver under section 211(f)(4).

units.obligation_text: Except as provided in paragraphs (b)(2) through (b)(5) and (b)(8) of this section, parties whose non-export renewable volume obligations are solely related to either the importation of products listed in § 80.1407(c) or § 80.1407(e) or to the addition of blendstocks into a volume of finished gasoline, finished diesel fuel, or BOB, can only separate RINs from volumes of renewable fuel if the number of gallon-RINs separated in a calendar year is less than or equal to a limit set as follows:
units.actor: parties whose non-export renewable volume obligations are solely related to specified importation or blending activities
units.action_summary: Such parties may separate RINs from renewable fuel volumes only if the number of gallon-RINs separated in a year does not exceed a specified limit.

units.obligation_text: Any obligated party described in § 80.1406, and any exporter of renewable fuel described in § 80.1430, must provide EPA with the information specified for registration under 40 CFR 1090.805, if such information has not already been provided under the provisions of this part.
units.actor: obligated parties described in §80.1406; exporters described in §80.1430
units.action_summary: Provide EPA with registration information specified in 40 CFR 1090.805 if not already provided.

units.obligation_text: Any RIN-generating foreign or domestic producer of renewable fuel, any foreign renewable fuel producer that sells renewable fuel for RIN generation by a United States importer, or any foreign ethanol producer that produces ethanol used in renewable fuel for which RINs are generated by a United States importer, must provide EPA the information specified under 40 CFR 1090.805 if such information has not already been provided under the provisions of this part...
units.actor: RIN-generating producers (foreign or domestic) and certain foreign producers
units.action_summary: Provide EPA with the information specified under 40 CFR 1090.805 if not already provided.

units.obligation_text: ...and must receive EPA-issued company and facility identification numbers prior to the generation of any RINs for their fuel or for fuel made with their ethanol.
units.actor: RIN-generating producers and specified foreign producers
units.action_summary: Obtain EPA-issued company and facility identification numbers before generating any RINs.

units.obligation_text: Importers of renewable fuel must provide EPA the information specified under 40 CFR 1090.805, if such information has not already been provided under the provisions of this part and must receive an EPA-issued company identification number prior to generating or owning RINs.
units.action_summary: Provide EPA the 1090.805 information if not provided and obtain an EPA company ID before generating or owning RINs.

units.obligation_text: The representative sample must be selected in accordance with the sample size guidelines set forth at 40 CFR 1090.1805.
units.actor: the party selecting the representative sample (e.g., auditor/obligated party)
units.action_summary: Select representative samples according to the sample size guidelines in 40 CFR 1090.1805.

units.obligation_text: Any party who owns RINs, intends to own RINs, or intends to allow another party to separate RINs as per § 80.1440, but who is not covered by paragraph (a), (b), or (c) of this section, must provide EPA the information specified under 40 CFR 1090.805, if such information has not already been provided under the provisions of this part and must receive an EPA-issued company identification number prior to owning any RINs.
units.actor: any party who owns or intends to own RINs or intends to allow separation and is not covered by (a)-(c)
units.action_summary: Provide EPA 1090.805 information if not already provided and obtain an EPA company ID before owning RINs.

units.obligation_text: Planned and conducted by an independent surveyor that meets the requirements in 40 CFR 1090.55.
units.action_summary: Attest engagements (or specified activities) must be planned and conducted by an independent surveyor meeting 40 CFR 1090.55 requirements.

units.obligation_text: The requirements regarding annual attest engagements in 40 CFR 1090.1800 also apply to any attest engagement procedures required under this subpart M.
units.actor: persons/entities required to perform attest engagements under subpart M
units.action_summary: Annual attest engagement requirements in 40 CFR 1090.1800 also govern attest engagement procedures under subpart M.

units.obligation_text: For obligated parties, compare the volumes of products listed in § 80.1407(c) and (e) reported to EPA in the report required under § 80.1451(a)(1) with the volumes, excluding any renewable fuel volumes, contained in the inventory reconciliation analysis under 40 CFR 1090.1810(b) and the volume of non-renewable diesel produced or imported.
units.action_summary: Compare reported product volumes with inventory reconciliation and non-renewable diesel production/import volumes.

units.obligation_text: Select sample batches in accordance with the guidelines in 40 CFR 1090.1805 from each separate category of renewable fuel exported and identified in § 80.1451(a); obtain invoices, bills of lading and other documentation for the representative samples; state whether any of these documents refer to the exported fuel as advanced biofuel or cellulosic biofuel; and report as a finding whether or not the exporter calculated an advanced biofuel or cellulosic biofuel RVO for these fuels pursuant to § 80.1430(b)(1) or § 80.1430(b)(3).
units.action_summary: Select representative exported fuel sample batches per 1090.1805, obtain shipping/documentation, indicate if documents label fuels as advanced/cellulosic, and report whether exporter calculated advanced/cellulosic RVOs.

units.obligation_text: Select sample batches in accordance with the guidelines in 40 CFR 1090.1805 from each separate category of renewable fuel exported and identified in § 80.1451(a).
units.action_summary: Select sample batches per 1090.1805 from each category of exported renewable fuel identified in §80.1451(a).

units.obligation_text: Obtain invoices, bills of lading and other documentation for the representative samples.
units.action_summary: Gather invoices, bills of lading, and other documentation for representative samples.

units.obligation_text: State whether any of these documents refer to the exported fuel as advanced biofuel or cellulosic biofuel.
units.action_summary: Indicate in findings if documents label exported fuel as advanced or cellulosic biofuel.

units.obligation_text: Report as a finding whether or not the exporter calculated an advanced biofuel or cellulosic biofuel RVO for these fuels pursuant to § 80.1430(b)(1) or § 80.1430(b)(3).
units.action_summary: Report whether the exporter calculated advanced or cellulosic biofuel RVOs per cited provisions.

units.obligation_text: Obtain and read copies of a representative sample, selected in accordance with the guidelines in 40 CFR 1090.1805, of each RIN transaction type (RINs purchased, RINs sold, RINs retired, RINs separated, RINs reinstated) included in the RIN transaction reports required under § 80.1451(a)(2) for the compliance year.
units.action_summary: Obtain and review representative samples of each RIN transaction type from RIN transaction reports for the compliance year.

units.obligation_text: Obtain product transfer documents for a representative sample, selected in accordance with the guidelines in 40 CFR 1090.1805, of renewable fuel batches produced or imported during the year being reviewed; verify that the product transfer documents contain the applicable information required under § 80.1453; verify the accuracy of the information contained in the product transfer documents; report as a finding any product transfer document that does not contain the applicable information required under § 80.1453.
units.action_summary: Obtain representative product transfer documents, verify they contain required information and are accurate, and report any deficiencies.

units.obligation_text: Obtain product transfer documents for a representative sample...
units.action_summary: Obtain representative product transfer documents per 1090.1805.

units.obligation_text: Verify that the product transfer documents contain the applicable information required under § 80.1453.
units.action_summary: Confirm product transfer documents include information required by §80.1453.

units.obligation_text: Verify the accuracy of the information contained in the product transfer documents.
units.action_summary: Check accuracy of information in product transfer documents.

units.obligation_text: Report as a finding any product transfer document that does not contain the applicable information required under § 80.1453.
units.action_summary: Report any product transfer documents missing required information.

units.obligation_text: Obtain documentation, as required under § 80.1451(b), (d), and (e) associated with feedstock purchases for a representative sample, selected in accordance with the guidelines in 40 CFR 1090.1805, of renewable fuel batches produced or imported during the year being reviewed.
units.action_summary: Obtain feedstock purchase documentation for representative sample batches as required under §80.1451(b),(d),(e).

units.obligation_text: Obtain and read copies of a representative sample, selected in accordance with the guidelines in 40 CFR 1090.1805, of each transaction type (RINs purchased, RINs sold, RINs retired, RINs separated, RINs reinstated) included in the RIN transaction reports required under § 80.1451(b)(2) for the compliance year.
units.action_summary: Obtain and review representative samples of each RIN transaction type from the RIN transaction reports required under §80.1451(b)(2).

units.obligation_text: Obtain and read copies of a representative sample, selected in accordance with the guidelines in 40 CFR 1090.1805, of each RIN transaction type (RINs purchased, RINs sold, RINs retired, RINs separated, RINs reinstated) included in the RIN transaction reports required under § 80.1451(c)(1) for the compliance year.
units.action_summary: Obtain and read representative RIN transaction samples from RIN transaction reports required under §80.1451(c)(1).

units.obligation_text: Be independent under the criteria specified in 40 CFR 1090.55;
units.action_summary: Independence required per criteria in 40 CFR 1090.55.

units.obligation_text: Select a sample from the list of vessels identified in paragraph (m)(2) of this section used to transport RFS–FRRF, in accordance with the guidelines in 40 CFR 1090.1805, and for each vessel selected perform all the following:
units.action_summary: Select vessel samples per 1090.1805 and perform required procedures for each vessel transporting RFS–FRRF.

units.obligation_text: Select a sample from the list of vessels identified in paragraph (m)(2) of this section used to transport RFS–FRRF, in accordance with the guidelines in 40 CFR 1090.1805, and for each vessel selected perform the following:
units.action_summary: Select vessel samples per 1090.1805 and perform specified procedures for each selected vessel.

units.obligation_text: Select a sample from this listing in accordance with the guidelines in 40 CFR 1090.1805, and obtain a commercial document of general circulation that lists vessel arrivals and departures, and that includes the port and date of departure and the ports and dates where the renewable fuel was offloaded for the selected vessels.
units.action_summary: Select vessel samples per guidelines and obtain commercial documents listing arrivals/departures with ports and dates of offloading.

units.obligation_text: Be licensed as a Certified Public Accountant in the United States and a citizen of the United States, or be approved in advance by EPA based on a demonstration of ability to perform the procedures required in 40 CFR 1090.1800, § 80.1464, and this paragraph (m);
units.action_summary: Attest auditor must be a US-licensed CPA and US citizen, or obtain EPA pre-approval based on demonstrated ability.

units.obligation_text: Sign a commitment that contains the provisions specified in paragraph (f) of this section with regard to activities and documents relevant to compliance with the requirements of 40 CFR 1090.1800, § 80.1464, and this paragraph (m).
units.action_summary: Sign a commitment including the provisions in paragraph (f) covering activities and documents relevant to compliance with cited requirements.

units.obligation_text: The attest auditor must be licensed as a Certified Public Accountant in the United States and a citizen of the United States, or be approved in advance by EPA based on a demonstration of ability to perform the procedures required in 40 CFR 1090.1800 and § 80.1464.
units.action_summary: Attest auditor must be a US-licensed CPA and US citizen or obtain EPA approval based on demonstrated ability to perform required procedures.

units.obligation_text: The attest auditor must sign a commitment that contains the provisions specified in paragraph (c) of this section with regard to activities and documents relevant to compliance with the requirements of 40 CFR 1090.1800 and § 80.1464.
units.action_summary: Attest auditor must sign a commitment including provisions in paragraph (c) related to compliance activities and documents.

units.obligation_text: Independent third-party auditors may use a representative sample of batches of renewable fuel in accordance with the procedures described in 40 CFR 1090.1805 for all components of this paragraph (c) except for paragraphs (c)(1)(ii), (c)(1)(iii), (c)(2)(ii), (c)(3)(vi), (c)(4)(ii), and (c)(4)(iii) of this section.
units.action_summary: Independent third-party auditors are permitted to use representative sampling per 1090.1805 for specified components of paragraph (c), with listed exceptions.

units.obligation_text: Gasoline-fueled vehicles must have a refueling inlet that allows insertion of the refueling nozzle specified in 40 CFR 1090.1550(a), and does not allow insertion of a nozzle with an outside diameter at or above 24 mm.
units.actor: gasoline-fueled vehicles (vehicle manufacturers/operators responsible for design)
units.action_summary: Vehicles must have a refueling inlet compatible with the refueling nozzle in 40 CFR 1090.1550(a) and that excludes nozzles ≥ 24 mm OD.

units.obligation_text: Gasoline-fueled vehicles must have a refueling inlet that allows insertion of the refueling nozzle specified in 40 CFR 1090.1550(a), and does not allow insertion of a nozzle with an outside diameter at or above 24 mm.
units.actor: gasoline-fueled vehicles (vehicle manufacturers/operators responsible for design)
units.action_summary: Gasoline-fueled heavy-duty vehicles must have a refueling inlet that allows the specified nozzle and prevents insertion of nozzles with OD ≥ 24 mm.

title: Hearing: Fuels Regulatory Streamlining
Control of Air Pollution From Airplanes and Airplane Engines: Greenhouse Gas Emission Standards and Test Procedures

units.obligation_text: To enforce any edition other than that specified in this section, the Environmental Protection Agency must publish a document in the Federal Register
units.action_summary: EPA must publish a Federal Register document to enforce any other edition

units.obligation_text: the material must be available to the public
units.actor: Environmental Protection Agency (material provided under this part)
units.action_summary: The referenced material must be made available to the public

units.obligation_text: the airplane may not exceed the Greenhouse Gas (GHG) standards of this part when certification under title 14 is sought
units.actor: the airplane (when certification under title 14 is sought)
units.action_summary: An airplane seeking title 14 certification may not exceed the GHG standards in this part

units.obligation_text: An airplane that incorporates modifications that change the fuel efficiency metric value of a prior version of airplane may not exceed the GHG standards of this part when certification under 14 CFR is sought
units.actor: modified airplane (when certification under 14 CFR is sought)
units.action_summary: A modified airplane that changes the fuel efficiency metric may not exceed the part's GHG standards when seeking certification

units.obligation_text: A modified airplane may not exceed the metric value limit of the prior version under § 1030.30
units.action_summary: A modified airplane cannot exceed the prior version's metric value limit under §1030.30

units.obligation_text: The requirements of this part do not apply to:
units.actor: this part (requirements) / airplanes meeting listed criteria
units.action_summary: Specifies categories of airplanes to which the part's requirements do not apply

units.obligation_text: Subsonic jet airplanes having a MTOM at or below 5,700 kg
units.actor: subsonic jet airplanes with MTOM ≤ 5,700 kg
units.action_summary: These airplanes are exempt from the part's requirements

units.obligation_text: Propeller-driven airplanes having a MTOM at or below 8,618 kg
units.action_summary: These airplanes are exempt from the part's requirements

units.obligation_text: Amphibious airplanes
units.action_summary: Amphibious airplanes are exempt from the part's requirements

units.obligation_text: Airplanes initially designed, or modified and used, for specialized operations. These airplane designs may include characteristics or configurations necessary to conduct specialized operations that the EPA and the FAA have determined may cause a significant increase in the fuel efficiency metric value
units.actor: airplanes designed or modified for specialized operations
units.action_summary: Airplanes for specialized operations determined by EPA and FAA to potentially increase metric value are exempt

units.obligation_text: Airplanes designed with a reference geometric factor of zero
units.action_summary: Airplanes with RGF of zero are exempt from the part's requirements

units.obligation_text: Airplanes designed for, or modified and used for, firefighting
units.actor: airplanes designed or used for firefighting
units.action_summary: Firefighting airplanes are exempt from the part's requirements

units.obligation_text: No State or political subdivision of a State may adopt or attempt to enforce any airplane or aircraft engine standard with respect to emissions unless the standard is identical to a standard that applies to airplanes under this part
units.actor: State or political subdivision of a State
units.action_summary: States may not adopt or enforce airplane/engine emission standards unless identical to this part's standards

units.obligation_text: unless the standard is identical to a standard that applies to airplanes under this part
units.actor: State or political subdivision of a State
units.action_summary: Exception permitting state standards only if identical to the part's standards

units.obligation_text: Each person seeking relief from compliance with this part at the time of certification must submit an application for exemption to the FAA in accordance with the regulations of 14 CFR parts 11 and 38
units.actor: person seeking relief from compliance (at time of certification)
units.action_summary: Applicants seeking exemption must submit an exemption application to the FAA per 14 CFR parts 11 and 38

units.obligation_text: The FAA will consult with the EPA on each exemption application request before the FAA takes action
units.action_summary: FAA must consult EPA on each exemption application before taking action

units.obligation_text: For each airplane subject to this part, including an airplane subject to the change criteria of § 1030.35, a fuel efficiency metric value must be calculated, using the following equation, rounded to three decimal places
units.actor: manufacturer/applicant for each airplane subject to this part
units.action_summary: A fuel efficiency metric value must be calculated for each subject airplane, rounded to three decimals

units.obligation_text: For each airplane subject to this part the SAR of an airplane must be determined by either—
units.action_summary: SAR must be determined for each airplane by one of the specified methods

units.obligation_text: Direct flight test measurements
units.action_summary: SAR may be determined by direct flight test measurements

units.obligation_text: Using a performance model
units.action_summary: SAR may be determined using a performance model approved and validated as specified

units.obligation_text: validated by actual SAR flight test data
units.action_summary: A performance model used to determine SAR must be validated by actual SAR flight test data

units.obligation_text: approved by the FAA before any SAR calculations are made
units.action_summary: The performance model must be approved by the FAA before SAR calculations are made

units.obligation_text: For each airplane model, establish a 1/SAR value at each of the following reference airplane masses
units.action_summary: For each airplane model, establish 1/SAR values at specified reference masses

units.obligation_text: High gross mass: 92 percent maximum takeoff mass (MTOM)
units.action_summary: Establish 1/SAR at high gross mass equal to 92% of MTOM

units.obligation_text: Low gross mass: (0.45 * MTOM) + (0.63 * (MTOM^0.924))
units.action_summary: Establish 1/SAR at low gross mass using the specified formula

units.obligation_text: Mid gross mass: Simple arithmetic average of high gross mass and low gross mass
units.action_summary: Establish 1/SAR at mid gross mass as the average of high and low gross mass

units.obligation_text: Calculate the average of the three 1/SAR values described in paragraph (b) of this section to calculate the fuel efficiency metric value in § 1030.20
units.action_summary: Calculate the average of the three 1/SAR values to compute the fuel efficiency metric

units.obligation_text: Do not include auxiliary power units in any 1/SAR calculation
units.action_summary: Auxiliary power units must be excluded from all 1/SAR calculations

units.obligation_text: All determinations under this section must be made according to the procedures applicable to SAR in Paragraphs 2.5 and 2.6 of Annex 16, Volume III and Appendix 1 of Annex 16, Volume III
units.action_summary: All SAR determinations must follow the referenced ICAO Annex 16 procedures

units.obligation_text: For each airplane subject to this part, determine the airplane’s nondimensional reference geometric factor (RGF) for the fuselage size of each airplane model, calculated as follows
units.action_summary: Determine the nondimensional RGF for each airplane model per the following procedures

units.obligation_text: For an airplane with a single deck, determine the area ... bounded by the maximum width of the fuselage outer mold line projected to a flat plane ... except for the crew cockpit zone
units.action_summary: For single-deck airplanes, determine the fuselage projected area as specified

units.obligation_text: For an airplane with more than one deck, determine the sum of the areas ...
units.action_summary: For multi-deck airplanes, determine summed projected areas per the listed rules

units.obligation_text: The maximum width of the fuselage outer mold line, projected ... by the forward and aft pressure bulkheads except for any crew cockpit zone
units.action_summary: Determine the projected maximum width for the primary deck as specified

units.action_summary: For specified airplanes between 1/1/2023 and 1/1/2028, any modification increasing the metric by >1.5% requires demonstrating compliance with §1030.30

units.obligation_text: Manufacturers of airplanes subject to § 1030.1 must submit an annual report as specified in this section
units.action_summary: Manufacturers must submit an annual production report as specified

units.obligation_text: You must submit the report for each calendar year in which you produce any airplanes that are subject to GHG emission standards under this part
units.action_summary: Manufacturers must submit the report for each calendar year they produce subject airplanes

units.obligation_text: The report is due by the following February 28
units.action_summary: The annual report must be submitted by February 28 following the reporting year

units.obligation_text: Include exempted airplanes in your report
units.action_summary: Manufacturers must include exempted airplanes in the report

units.obligation_text: Send the report to the Designated EPA Program Officer
units.action_summary: Manufacturers must send the report to the Designated EPA Program Officer

units.obligation_text: In the report, identify your corporate name as listed on the airplane type certificate and the year for which you are reporting
units.action_summary: Report must identify the corporate name as on the type certificate and the reporting year

units.action_summary: Provide the corporate name as listed on each engine type certificate

units.obligation_text: The complete name for each of engine model

units.obligation_text: The corporate name as listed on the propeller type certificate
units.action_summary: Provide the corporate name from the propeller type certificate

units.obligation_text: The complete name for each propeller model
units.action_summary: Provide the complete name for each propeller model

units.obligation_text: Fuel efficiency metric value and the calculated GHG emission standard
units.action_summary: Report the fuel efficiency metric value and the calculated GHG emission standard

units.obligation_text: For airplanes exempted under § 1030.10, identify the approval date for the exemption and the number of exempt airplanes

units.obligation_text: Where information provided for the previous year remains valid and complete, you may report your production volumes and state that there are no changes, without resubmitting the other information specified in this section
units.action_summary: If prior-year information remains valid, manufacturers may simply report volumes and state no changes without resubmitting other details

units.obligation_text: You must keep a copy of any reports or other information you submit to us for at least three years
units.action_summary: Keep copies of submitted reports/information for at least three years

units.obligation_text: If you use the same emissions data or other information to support a new certification, the three-year period restarts with each year that you continue to rely on the information

units.obligation_text: Store these records in any format and on any media, as long as you can promptly send us organized, written records in English if we ask for them
units.action_summary: Records may be stored in any format/media provided you can promptly send organized, written records in English upon request

units.obligation_text: as long as you can promptly send us organized, written records in English if we ask for them

units.obligation_text: We may review them at any time
units.action_summary: EPA may review the records at any time
