title: Mercury and Air Toxics Standards for Power Plants Electronic Reporting Revisions

units.obligation_text: To demonstrate initial compliance using either a CMS that measures HAP concentrations directly (i.e., an Hg, HCl, or HF CEMS, or a sorbent trap monitoring system) or an SO2 or PM CEMS, the initial performance test shall consist of 30- or, if applicable for Hg, 90-boiler operating days.
units.action_summary: Initial performance test must consist of 30 boiler operating days (or 90 for Hg where applicable).

units.obligation_text: If you choose to use performance testing to demonstrate initial compliance with the applicable emissions limits in Tables 1 and 2 to this subpart for your EGUs, you must conduct the tests according to § 63.10007 and Table 5 to this subpart.
units.action_summary: If using performance testing for initial compliance, conduct tests according to §63.10007 and Table 5.

units.obligation_text: Instead, the stack gas flow rate and moisture content can be determined from data that are collected during the EPA test Method 5, 5D, 6, 26A, or 29 test (e.g., pitot tube (delta P) readings, moisture collected in the impingers, etc.).
units.action_summary: You may determine stack gas flow rate and moisture content from data collected during the specified EPA test methods instead of separate Method 2 or 4 determinations.

units.obligation_text: For the purposes of the initial compliance demonstration, you may use test data and results from a performance test conducted prior to the date on which compliance is required as specified in § 63.9984, provided that the following conditions are fully met:
units.action_summary: You may use prior performance test data for initial compliance demonstration if specified conditions are met.

units.obligation_text: You must calculate the weighted average emissions rate for the group in accordance with the procedures in this paragraph (a)(2) using the data from all units in the group including any that operate fewer than 30 (or 90) of the preceding 30 (or 90) group boiler operating days.
units.action_summary: Calculate weighted average emissions rate for the emissions averaging group using data from all units, including those that operated fewer than the averaging-period days.

units.obligation_text: You must use all the data collected during all boiler operating hours in assessing the compliance with your operating limit except:
units.action_summary: Use all data collected during boiler operating hours to assess compliance, except for listed exclusions.

units.obligation_text: Any data recorded during periods of monitoring system malfunctions or repairs associated with monitoring system malfunctions.
units.action_summary: Data recorded during monitoring system malfunctions or related repairs are excluded from compliance assessment.

units.obligation_text: You must report any monitoring system malfunctions as deviations in your compliance reports under § 63.10031(c) or (g) (as applicable);
units.action_summary: Report monitoring system malfunctions as deviations in the specified compliance reports.

units.obligation_text: Any data recorded during periods when the monitoring system is out-of-control (as specified in your site-specific monitoring plan), repairs associated with periods when the monitoring system is out of control, or required monitoring system quality assurance or quality control activities conducted during out-of-control periods.
units.action_summary: Data recorded during out-of-control periods, associated repairs, or QA/QC activities during out-of-control periods are excluded from compliance assessment.

units.obligation_text: You must report any such periods as deviations in your compliance reports under § 63.10031(c) or (g) (as applicable);
units.action_summary: Report out-of-control periods as deviations in the specified compliance reports.

units.obligation_text: Any data recorded during required monitoring system quality assurance or quality control activities that temporarily interrupt the measurement of output data from the PM CPMS;
units.action_summary: Data recorded during QA/QC activities that temporarily interrupt PM CPMS measurements are excluded from compliance assessment.

units.obligation_text: Any data recorded during periods of startup or shutdown.
units.action_summary: Data recorded during startup or shutdown are excluded from compliance assessment.

units.obligation_text: You must record and report the results of PM CPMS system performance audits, in accordance with § 63.10031(k).
units.action_summary: Record and report PM CPMS performance audit results per §63.10031(k).

units.obligation_text: You must also record and make available upon request the dates and duration of periods from when the PM CPMS is out of control until completion of the corrective actions necessary to return the PM CPMS to operation consistent with your site-specific monitoring plan.
units.action_summary: Record and make available, on request, dates and durations of PM CPMS out-of-control periods until corrective actions complete.

units.obligation_text: If you choose to comply with the PM filterable emissions limit in lieu of metal HAP limits, you may choose to install, certify, operate, and maintain a PM CEMS and record and report the output of the PM CEMS as specified in paragraphs (i)(1) through (8) of this section.
units.action_summary: If opting to meet PM limit instead of metal HAP limits, you may install and use a PM CEMS and must follow the specified requirements (i)(1)-(8).

units.obligation_text: Compliance with the applicable PM emissions limit in Table 1 or 2 to this subpart is determined on a 30-boiler operating day rolling average basis.
units.action_summary: Compliance with PM emissions limits is determined based on a 30-boiler operating day rolling average.

units.obligation_text: You must install and certify your PM CEMS according to section 4 of appendix C to this subpart.
units.action_summary: Install and certify PM CEMS per section 4 of appendix C.

units.obligation_text: You must operate, maintain, and quality-assure the data from your PM CEMS according to section 5 of appendix C to this subpart.
units.action_summary: Operate, maintain, and QA the PM CEMS data following section 5 of appendix C.

units.obligation_text: You must reduce the data from your PM CEMS to hourly averages in accordance with section 6.1 of appendix C to this subpart.
units.action_summary: Reduce PM CEMS data to hourly averages per section 6.1 of appendix C.

units.obligation_text: You must collect data using the PM CEMS at all times the process unit is operating except for periods of monitoring system malfunctions, out-of-control periods, repairs associated with monitoring system malfunctions or out-of-control periods, and required monitoring system quality assurance, quality control, or maintenance activities.
units.action_summary: Collect PM CEMS data whenever the process unit operates, except for specified excluded periods.

units.obligation_text: You must use all the data collected during all boiler operating hours in assessing the compliance with your emissions limit except:
units.action_summary: Use all PM CEMS data from boiler operating hours to assess compliance, except for listed exclusions.

units.obligation_text: Any data recorded during periods of monitoring system malfunctions and repairs associated with monitoring system malfunctions.
units.action_summary: Data during monitoring system malfunctions and associated repairs are excluded from compliance assessment.

units.obligation_text: You must report any monitoring system malfunctions as deviations in your compliance reports under § 63.10031(c) or (g) (as applicable);
units.action_summary: Report monitoring system malfunctions as deviations in the specified compliance reports.

units.obligation_text: Any data recorded during periods when the monitoring system is out-of-control (as specified in appendix C to this subpart), repairs associated with periods when the monitoring system is out of control, or required monitoring system quality assurance or quality control activities conducted during out-of-control periods. You must report any such periods as deviations in your compliance reports under § 63.10031(c) or (g) (as applicable);
units.action_summary: Exclude data from out-of-control periods and report such periods as deviations in the specified compliance reports.

units.obligation_text: Any data recorded during required monitoring system quality assurance, quality control, or maintenance activities that temporarily interrupt the measurement of emissions (e.g., calibrations, certain audits, routine probe maintenance);
units.action_summary: Exclude data collected during QA/QC or maintenance activities that temporarily interrupt emissions measurement.

units.obligation_text: Any data recorded during periods of startup or shutdown.
units.action_summary: Exclude data recorded during startup or shutdown from compliance assessment.

units.obligation_text: You must keep records and report data from your PM CEMS in accordance with section 7 of appendix C to this subpart.
units.action_summary: Keep records and report PM CEMS data per section 7 of appendix C.

units.obligation_text: You must record and make available upon request the dates and duration of periods when the PM CEMS is out-of-control to completion of the corrective actions necessary to return the PM CEMS to operation consistent with your site-specific monitoring plan.
units.action_summary: Record and make available, upon request, dates and durations of PM CEMS out-of-control periods until corrective actions are complete.

units.obligation_text: You must calculate each 30-boiler operating day rolling average PM emission rate in units of the applicable emissions limit in Table 1 or 2 to this subpart, in accordance with section 6.2.4 of appendix C to this subpart.
units.action_summary: Calculate each 30-boiler operating day rolling average PM emission rate per section 6.2.4 of appendix C in units of the applicable limit.

units.obligation_text: You must collect data using the HAP metals CEMS at all times the process unit is operating and at the intervals specified in paragraph (a) of this section, except for periods of monitoring system malfunctions, out-of-control periods, repairs associated with monitoring system malfunctions or out-of-control periods, and required monitoring system quality assurance, quality control, or maintenance activities.
units.action_summary: Collect HAP metals CEMS data whenever the unit operates, except for specified excluded periods.

units.obligation_text: You must use all the data collected during all boiler operating hours in assessing the compliance with your emission limit except:
units.action_summary: Use all HAP metals CEMS data from boiler operating hours to assess compliance, except for listed exclusions.

units.obligation_text: Any data collected during periods of monitoring system malfunctions and repairs associated with monitoring system malfunctions. You must report any monitoring system malfunctions as deviations in your compliance reports under § 63.10031(c) or (g) (as applicable);
units.action_summary: Exclude data from monitoring system malfunctions and associated repairs; report such malfunctions as deviations in specified reports.

units.obligation_text: Any data collected during periods when the monitoring system is out of control as specified in your site-specific monitoring plan, repairs associated with periods when the monitoring system is out of control, or required monitoring system quality assurance or quality control activities conducted during out-of-control periods. You must report any out of control periods as deviations in your compliance reports under § 63.10031(c) or (g) (as applicable);
units.action_summary: Exclude data from out-of-control periods and associated repairs and QA/QC activities; report such out-of-control periods as deviations.

units.obligation_text: Any data recorded during required monitoring system quality assurance or quality control activities that temporarily interrupt the measurement of emissions (e.g., calibrations, certain audits, routine probe maintenance);
units.action_summary: Exclude data recorded during QA/QC activities that temporarily interrupt emissions measurement.

units.obligation_text: Any data recorded during periods of startup or shutdown.
units.action_summary: Exclude data recorded during startup or shutdown from compliance assessment.

units.obligation_text: You must record and report the results of HAP metals CEMS system performance audits, in accordance with § 63.10031(k).
units.action_summary: Record and report HAP metals CEMS performance audit results per §63.10031(k).

units.obligation_text: You must also record and make available upon request the dates and duration of periods when the HAP metals CEMS is out of control to completion of the corrective actions necessary to return the HAP metals CEMS to operation consistent with your site-specific performance evaluation and quality control program plan.
units.action_summary: Record and make available upon request dates and durations of HAP metals CEMS out-of-control periods until corrective actions complete.

units.obligation_text: You must submit a Notification of Compliance Status in accordance with § 63.10031(f)(4) or (h), as applicable, containing the results of the initial compliance demonstration, as specified in § 63.10030(e).
units.action_summary: Submit a Notification of Compliance Status containing initial compliance demonstration results per the cited provisions.

units.obligation_text: You must report the emissions data recorded during startup and shutdown.
units.action_summary: Report emissions data recorded during startup and shutdown events.

units.obligation_text: If you are relying on paragraph (2) of the definition of "startup" in § 63.10042, then for startup and shutdown incidents that occur on or prior to December 31, 2023, you must also report the applicable supplementary information in § 63.10031(c)(5) in the semiannual compliance report.
units.action_summary: If relying on the alternative startup definition, for incidents on or before Dec 31, 2023, also report supplementary startup/shutdown information in the semiannual compliance report.

units.obligation_text: For startup and shutdown incidents that occur on or after January 1, 2024, you must provide the applicable information in §§ 63.10031(c)(5)(ii) and 63.10020(e) quarterly, in PDF files, in accordance with § 63.10031(i).
units.action_summary: For incidents on or after Jan 1, 2024, provide the referenced startup/shutdown information quarterly in PDF files as specified.

units.obligation_text: Prior to January 1, 2024, report the tune-up date electronically, in a PDF file, in your semiannual compliance report, as specified in § 63.10031(f)(4) and (6) and, if requested by the Administrator, in hard copy, as specified in § 63.10031(f)(5).
units.action_summary: Before Jan 1, 2024, report tune-up date electronically in semiannual compliance report (PDF) and in hard copy if requested by Administrator.

units.obligation_text: On and after January 1, 2024, report the tune-up date electronically in your quarterly compliance report, in accordance with § 63.10031(g) and section 10.2 of appendix E to this subpart.
units.action_summary: On or after Jan 1, 2024, report tune-up date electronically in quarterly compliance report per §63.10031(g) and appendix E.

units.obligation_text: The tune-up report date is the date when tune-up requirements in paragraphs (e)(6) and (7) of this section are completed.
units.action_summary: Defines the tune-up report date as the date when tune-up requirements are completed.

units.obligation_text: You must submit the applicable reports and notifications required under § 63.10031(a) through (k) to the Administrator electronically, using EPA's Emissions Collection and Monitoring Plan System (ECMPS) Client Tool.
units.action_summary: Submit applicable reports and notifications electronically to the Administrator using the ECMPS Client Tool.

units.obligation_text: If the final date of any time period (or any deadline) for any of these submissions falls on a weekend or a Federal holiday, the time period shall be extended to the next business day.
units.action_summary: Deadlines that fall on weekends or federal holidays are extended to the next business day.

units.obligation_text: If the EPA Host System supporting the ECMPS Client Tool is offline and unavailable for submission of reports for any part of a day when a report would otherwise be due, the deadline for reporting is automatically extended until the first business day on which the system becomes available following the outage.
units.action_summary: If ECMPS is offline, the reporting deadline is automatically extended until the first business day the system is available.

units.obligation_text: Use of the ECMPS Client Tool to submit a report or notification required under this subpart satisfies any requirement under subpart A of this part to submit that same report or notification (or the information contained in it) to the appropriate EPA Regional Office or State agency whose delegation request has been approved.
units.action_summary: Submitting a report via ECMPS satisfies related submission requirements under subpart A to approved EPA regional/state agencies.

units.obligation_text: If you are relying on paragraph (2) of the definition of 'startup' in § 63.10042, you must provide reports concerning activities and periods of startup and shutdown that occur on or prior to January 1, 2024, in accordance with § 63.10031(c)(5), in your semiannual compliance report.
units.action_summary: If relying on the alternative startup definition, for incidents on or before Jan 1, 2024, include the referenced startup/shutdown reports in the semiannual compliance report.

units.obligation_text: For startup and shutdown incidents that occur on and after January 1, 2024, you must provide the applicable information referenced in §§ 63.10031(c)(5)(ii) and 63.10020(e) quarterly, in PDF files, in accordance with § 63.10031(i).
units.action_summary: For incidents on or after Jan 1, 2024, provide the referenced startup/shutdown information quarterly in PDF format per §63.10031(i).

units.obligation_text: The Notification of Compliance Status report must contain all of the information specified in paragraphs (e)(1) through (8) of this section that applies to your initial compliance strategy.
units.action_summary: Notification of Compliance Status must include all applicable information listed in (e)(1)-(8) relevant to your initial compliance strategy.

units.obligation_text: For each of your existing EGUs, identification of each emissions limit specified in Table 2 to this subpart with which you plan to comply initially.
units.action_summary: Identify, for each existing EGU, which emissions limit in Table 2 you plan to comply with initially in the initial notification.

units.obligation_text: If, at some future date, you wish to switch from the limit specified in your initial notification of compliance status, you must follow the procedures and meet the conditions of paragraphs (e)(7)(iii)(A) through (C) of this section.
units.action_summary: To switch emission limits after initial notification, follow specified procedures and meet stated conditions in (e)(7)(iii)(A)-(C).

units.obligation_text: Your request includes performance stack test results or valid CMS data, obtained within 45 days prior to the date of your submission, demonstrating that each EGU or EGU emissions averaging group is in compliance with both the mass per heat input limit and the mass per gross output limit;
units.action_summary: A request to switch emission limits must include performance stack test results or valid CMS data, obtained within 45 days prior, demonstrating compliance with both mass per heat input and mass per gross output limits.

units.obligation_text: You must submit each report in this section that applies to you.
units.action_summary: Submit each applicable report listed in §63.10031.

units.obligation_text: If you are required to (or elect to) monitor Hg emissions continuously, you must meet the electronic reporting requirements of appendix A to this subpart.
units.action_summary: If monitoring Hg continuously, meet the electronic reporting requirements of appendix A.

units.obligation_text: If you elect to monitor HCl and/or HF emissions continuously, you must meet the electronic reporting requirements of appendix B to this subpart.
units.action_summary: If electing continuous HCl/HF monitoring, meet electronic reporting requirements of appendix B.

units.obligation_text: Notwithstanding the requirement in this paragraph (a)(2), if you opt to certify your HCl monitor according to Performance Specification 18 in appendix B to part 60 of this chapter and to use Procedure 6 in appendix F to part 60 of this chapter for on-going QA of the monitor, then, on and prior to December 31, 2023, report only hourly HCl emissions data and the results of daily calibration drift tests and RATAs performed on or prior to that date; keep records of all of the other required certification and QA tests and report them, starting in 2024.
units.action_summary: If you certify HCl monitor per specified methods: on or before Dec 31, 2023 report only hourly HCl data and results of daily calibration drift tests and RATAs performed on or before that date; keep other QA/certification records and report them starting in 2024.

units.obligation_text: If you elect to monitor filterable PM emissions continuously, you must meet the electronic reporting requirements of appendix C to this subpart. Electronic reporting of hourly PM emissions data shall begin with the later of: The first operating hour on or after January 1, 2024; or the first operating hour after completion of the initial PM CEMS correlation test.
units.action_summary: If electing continuous filterable PM monitoring, meet electronic reporting of appendix C; electronic reporting of hourly PM emissions begins at the later of Jan 1, 2024 or after initial PM CEMS correlation test completion.

units.obligation_text: If you elect to demonstrate continuous compliance using a PM CPMS, you must meet the electronic reporting requirements of appendix D to this subpart. Electronic reporting of the hourly PM CPMS output shall begin with the later of: The first operating hour on or after January 1, 2024; or the first operating hour after completion of the initial performance stack test that establishes the operating limit for the PM CPMS.
units.action_summary: If using a PM CPMS for compliance, meet appendix D electronic reporting; electronic reporting begins at the later of Jan 1, 2024 or after the initial performance stack test establishing the PM CPMS operating limit.

units.obligation_text: If you elect to monitor SO2 emission rate continuously as a surrogate for HCl, you must use the ECMPS Client Tool to submit the following information to EPA ...
units.action_summary: If monitoring SO2 continuously as HCl surrogate, use ECMPS to submit required monitoring plan info, certification/QA test results, and quarterly electronic emissions reports with specified contents.

units.obligation_text: Monitoring plan information for the SO2 CEMS and for any additional monitoring systems that are required to convert SO2 concentrations to units of the emission standard, in accordance with §§ 75.62 and 75.64(a)(4) of this chapter;
units.action_summary: Submit monitoring plan information for SO2 CEMS and any additional monitors required to convert concentrations to standard units per cited provisions.

units.obligation_text: Certification, recertification, quality-assurance, and diagnostic test results for the SO2 CEMS and for any additional monitoring systems that are required to convert SO2 concentrations to units of the emission standard, in accordance with § 75.64(a)(5) of this chapter;
units.action_summary: Submit certification, recertification, QA, and diagnostic test results for SO2 CEMS and additional monitors per §75.64(a)(5).

units.obligation_text: Quarterly electronic emissions reports. You must submit an electronic quarterly report within 30 days after the end of each calendar quarter, starting with a report for the calendar quarter in which the initial 30 boiler operating day performance test begins.
units.action_summary: Submit electronic quarterly emissions reports within 30 days after each quarter, starting with the quarter when initial 30-boiler operating day performance test begins.

units.obligation_text: The applicable operating data specified in § 75.57(b) of this chapter;
units.action_summary: Include the operating data specified in §75.57(b) in the quarterly electronic report.

units.obligation_text: An hourly data stream for the unadjusted SO2 concentration (in ppm, rounded to one decimal place), and separate unadjusted hourly data streams for the other parameters needed to convert the SO2 concentrations to units of the standard.
units.action_summary: Include hourly data streams for unadjusted SO2 concentration and separate unadjusted hourly streams for other parameters needed for conversion to units of the standard.

units.obligation_text: An hourly SO2 emission rate data stream, in units of the standard (i.e., lb/MMBtu or lb/MWh, as applicable), calculated according to § 63.10007(e) and (f)(1), rounded to the same precision as the emission standard (i.e., with one leading non-zero digit and one decimal place), expressed in scientific notation.
units.action_summary: Include an hourly SO2 emission rate data stream in the units of the standard, calculated per specified methods and rounded appropriately.

units.obligation_text: The results of all required daily quality-assurance tests of the SO2 monitor and the additional monitors used to convert SO2 concentration to units of the standard, as specified in appendix B to part 75 of this chapter;
units.action_summary: Include results of all required daily QA tests of SO2 monitor and additional monitors used for conversions.

units.obligation_text: A compliance certification, which includes a statement, based on reasonable inquiry of those persons with primary responsibility for ensuring that all SO2 emissions from the affected EGUs under this subpart have been correctly and fully monitored, by a responsible official with that official’s name, title, and signature, certifying that, to the best of his or her knowledge, the report is true, accurate, and complete. You must submit such a compliance certification statement in support of each quarterly report.
units.actor: you (owner or operator/affected source); responsible official
units.action_summary: Include a signed compliance certification by a responsible official stating the quarterly report is true, accurate, and complete.

units.obligation_text: You must submit semiannual compliance reports according to the requirements in paragraphs (b)(1) through (5) of this section.
units.action_summary: Submit semiannual compliance reports as required by the subsection.

units.obligation_text: The first compliance report must cover the period beginning on the compliance date that is specified for your affected source in § 63.9984 ... and ending on June 30 or December 31, whichever date is the first date that occurs at least 180 days after the compliance date ...
units.action_summary: First compliance report must cover the period from the compliance date to the first June 30 or Dec 31 at least 180 days after compliance date.

units.obligation_text: The first compliance report must be submitted electronically no later than July 31 or January 31, whichever date is the first date following the end of the first calendar half after the compliance date ...
units.action_summary: Submit the first compliance report electronically by the first July 31 or Jan 31 following the end of the first calendar half after the compliance date.

units.obligation_text: Each subsequent compliance report must be submitted electronically no later than July 31 or January 31, whichever date is the first date following the end of the semiannual reporting period.
units.action_summary: Submit each subsequent semiannual compliance report electronically by July 31 or January 31 following the end of the semiannual period.

units.obligation_text: The final semiannual compliance report shall cover the reporting period from July 1, 2023 through December 31, 2023. Quarterly compliance reports shall be submitted thereafter, in accordance with paragraph (g) of this section, starting with a report covering the first calendar quarter of 2024.
units.action_summary: Final semiannual report covers July 1–Dec 31, 2023; thereafter submit quarterly compliance reports per paragraph (g) starting first quarter 2024.

units.obligation_text: The semiannual compliance report must contain the information required in paragraphs (c)(1) through (10) of this section.
units.action_summary: Semiannual compliance reports must include the information specified in (c)(1)-(10).

units.obligation_text: If you had any process or control equipment malfunction(s) during the reporting period, you must include the number, duration, and a brief description for each type of malfunction which occurred during the semiannual reporting period which caused or may have caused any applicable emission limitation to be exceeded.
units.action_summary: If malfunctions occurred during the reporting period, include number, duration, and brief description of each that caused or may have caused exceedances in the semiannual report.

units.obligation_text: For EGUs whose owners or operators rely on a CMS to comply with an emissions or operating limit, the semiannual compliance reports described in paragraph (c) of this section must include the excess emissions and monitor downtime summary report described in § 63.10(e)(3)(vi). However, starting with the first calendar quarter of 2024, reporting of the information under § 63.10(e)(3)(vi) (and under paragraph (e)(3)(v), if the applicable excess emissions and/or monitor downtime threshold is exceeded) is discontinued for all CMS, and you must, instead, include in the quarterly compliance reports described in paragraph (g) of this section the applicable data elements in section 13 of appendix E to this subpart for any 'deviation' ... If there were no deviations, you must include a statement to that effect in the quarterly compliance report.
units.actor: you (owner or operator/affected source); EGUs owners/operators
units.action_summary: Before 2024 include excess emissions and monitor downtime summary in semiannual reports; starting Q1 2024 discontinue that reporting and instead include section 13 appendix E data elements for any deviations in quarterly reports; if none, include a statement that there were no deviations.

units.obligation_text: Each affected source that has obtained a title V operating permit pursuant to part 70 or 71 of this chapter must report all deviations as defined in this subpart in the semiannual monitoring report required by 40 CFR 70.6(a)(3)(iii)(A) or 71.6(a)(3)(iii)(A).
units.actor: each affected source with a title V permit
units.action_summary: Affected sources with title V permits must report all deviations in the required semiannual monitoring report under the cited CFR provisions.

units.obligation_text: For each performance stack test completed prior to January 1, 2024 ... you must submit a PDF test report in accordance with paragraph (f)(6) of this section, no later than 60 days after the date on which the testing is completed. For each test completed on or after January 1, 2024, in accordance with § 63.10031(g), submit the applicable reference method information in sections 17 through 31 of appendix E to this subpart along with the quarterly compliance report for the calendar quarter in which the test was completed.
units.action_summary: Submit PDF test reports for performance stack tests completed before Jan 1, 2024 within 60 days; for tests on/after Jan 1, 2024 submit appendix E reference method information with the quarterly report.

units.obligation_text: For each relative accuracy test audit (RATA) of an Hg, HCl, HF, or SO2 monitoring system completed prior to January 1, 2024, and for each PM CEMS correlation test, each relative response audit (RRA) and each response correlation audit (RCA) of a PM CEMS completed prior to that date, you must submit a PDF test report in accordance with paragraph (f)(6) of this section, no later than 60 days after the date on which the test is completed. For each SO2 or Hg RATA completed on or after January 1, 2024, you must submit the applicable reference method information in sections 17 through 31 of appendix E to this subpart prior to or concurrent with the relevant quarterly emissions report. For HCl or HF RATAs, and for correlation tests, RRAs, and RCAs of PM CEMS that are completed on or after January 1, 2024, submit the appendix E reference method information together with the summarized electronic test results, in accordance with section 11.4 of appendix B to this subpart or section 7.2.4 of appendix C to this part, as applicable.
units.action_summary: Submit PDF RATA/RRA/RCA/correlation test reports completed prior to Jan 1, 2024 within 60 days; for tests on/after Jan 1, 2024 submit the applicable appendix E/reference method information per the specified timing and methods.

units.obligation_text: If, for a particular EGU or a group of EGUs serving a common stack, you have elected to demonstrate compliance using a PM CEMS, an approved HAP metals CEMS, or a PM CPMS, you must submit quarterly PDF reports in accordance with paragraph (f)(6) of this section, which include all of the 30- boiler operating day rolling average emission rates derived from the CEMS data or the 30-boiler operating day rolling average responses derived from the PM CPMS data (as applicable). The quarterly reports are due within 60 days after the reporting periods ending on March 31st, June 30th, September 30th, and December 31st. Submission of these quarterly reports in PDF files shall end with the report that covers the fourth calendar quarter of 2023. Beginning with the first calendar quarter of 2024, the compliance averages shall no longer be reported separately, but shall be incorporated into the quarterly compliance reports described in paragraph (g) of this section. In addition to the compliance averages for PM CEMS, PM CPMS, and/or HAP metals CEMS, the quarterly compliance reports described in paragraph (g) of this section must also include the 30- (or, if applicable 90-) boiler operating day rolling average emission rates for Hg, HCl, HF, and/or SO2, if you have elected to (or are required to) continuously monitor these pollutants. Further, if your EGU or common stack is in an averaging plan, your quarterly compliance reports must identify all of the EGUs or common stacks in the plan and must include all of the 30- (or90-) group boiler operating day rolling weighted average emission rates (WAERs) for the averaging group.
units.action_summary: If demonstrating compliance using PM CEMS/HAP metals CEMS/PM CPMS, submit quarterly PDF reports including 30-boiler rolling averages within 60 days of quarter end through Q4 2023; thereafter incorporate averages into quarterly reports per paragraph (g), and include required rolling averages for monitored pollutants and WAERs for averaging groups.

units.obligation_text: You must submit semiannual compliance reports as required under paragraphs (b) through (d) of this section, ending with a report covering the semiannual period from July 1 through December 31, 2023, and Notifications of Compliance Status as required under § 63.10030(e), as PDF files. Quarterly compliance reports shall be submitted in XML format thereafter, in accordance with paragraph (g) of this section, starting with a report covering the first calendar quarter of 2024.
units.action_summary: Submit semiannual compliance reports and Notifications of Compliance Status as PDF files through Dec 31, 2023; starting Q1 2024 submit quarterly compliance reports in XML per paragraph (g).

units.obligation_text: All reports and notifications described in paragraphs (f) introductory text and (f)(1), (2), and (4) of this section shall be submitted to the EPA in the specified format and at the specified frequency, using the ECMPS Client Tool. Each PDF version of a stack test report, CEMS RATA report, PM CEMS correlation test report, RRA report, and RCA report must include sufficient information to assess compliance and to demonstrate that the reference method testing was done properly.
units.action_summary: Submit all specified reports to EPA using the ECMPS Client Tool in required format/frequency; each PDF test report must include sufficient information to assess compliance and show proper testing.

units.obligation_text: An indication of the type of PDF report or notification being submitted;
units.action_summary: Enter an indication of the type of PDF report or notification being submitted into ECMPS at the time of submission.

units.obligation_text: The date the performance test was completed (if applicable) and the test number (if applicable);
units.action_summary: Enter the performance test completion date and test number into ECMPS with the PDF submission, if applicable.

units.obligation_text: Starting with a report for the first calendar quarter of 2024, you must use the ECMPS Client Tool to submit quarterly electronic compliance reports. Each quarterly compliance report shall include the applicable data elements in sections 2 through 13 of appendix E to this subpart. For each stack test summarized in the compliance report, you must also submit the applicable reference method information in sections 17 through 31 of appendix E to this subpart. The compliance reports and associated appendix E information must be submitted no later than 60 days after the end of each calendar quarter.
units.action_summary: Beginning Q1 2024, use ECMPS to submit quarterly electronic compliance reports including specified appendix E data elements and reference method info for stack tests, within 60 days after each quarter's end.

units.obligation_text: On and after January 1, 2024, initial Notifications of Compliance Status (if any) shall be submitted in accordance with § 63.9(h)(2)(ii), as PDF files, using the ECMPS Client Tool. The applicable data elements in paragraphs (f)(6)(i) through (xii) of this section must be entered into ECMPS with each Notification.
units.action_summary: On/after Jan 1, 2024 submit initial Notifications of Compliance Status as PDF files via ECMPS and enter the specified data elements into ECMPS with each notification.

units.obligation_text: If you have elected to use paragraph (2) of the definition of "startup" in § 63.10042, then, for startup and shutdown incidents that occur on or prior to December 31, 2023, you must include the information in § 63.10031(c)(5) in the semiannual compliance report, in a PDF file. If you have elected to use paragraph (2) of the definition of "startup" in § 63.10042, then, for startup and shutdown event(s) that occur on or after January 1, 2024, you must use the ECMPS Client Tool to submit the information in §§ 63.10031(c)(5) and 63.10020(e) along with each quarterly compliance report, in a PDF file, starting with a report for the first calendar quarter of 2024. The applicable data elements in paragraphs (f)(6)(i) through (xii) of this section must be entered into ECMPS with each startup and shutdown report.
units.action_summary: If electing the alternative startup definition, include specified startup/shutdown info in semiannual PDF reports for incidents on/ before Dec 31, 2023; for incidents on/after Jan 1, 2024 submit the info via ECMPS with each quarterly report and enter the specified data elements.

units.obligation_text: If you elect to use a certified PM CEMS to monitor PM emissions continuously to demonstrate compliance with this subpart and have begun recording valid data from the PM CEMS prior to [DATE 60 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF THE FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], you must use the ECMPS Client Tool to submit a detailed report of your PS 11 correlation test (see appendix B to part 60 of this chapter) in a PDF file no later than 60 days after that date. For a correlation test completed on or after [DATE 60 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF THE FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], but prior to January 1, 2024, you must submit the PDF report no later than 60 days after the date on which the test is completed. For a correlation test completed on or after January 1, 2024, you must submit the PDF report according to section 7.2.4 of appendix C to this subpart. The applicable data elements in paragraphs (f)(6)(i) through (xii) of this section must be entered into ECMPS with the PDF report.
units.action_summary: If using a certified PM CEMS and recording data prior to the specified date, submit PS 11 correlation test report via ECMPS PDF within 60 days of that date; for correlation tests on/after the specified date but before Jan 1, 2024 submit PDF within 60 days after test completion; for tests on/after Jan 1, 2024 submit per appendix C section 7.2.4; enter specified ECMPS data elements with each PDF.

units.obligation_text: If you elect to demonstrate compliance using a PM CPMS or an approved HAP metals CEMS, you must submit quarterly reports of your QA/QC activities (e.g., calibration checks, performance audits), in a PDF file, beginning with a report for the first quarter of 2024, if the PM CPMS or HAP metals CEMS is used for the compliance demonstration in that quarter. Otherwise, submit a report for the first calendar quarter in which the PM CPMS or HAP metals CEMS is used to demonstrate compliance. These reports are due no later than 60 days after the end of each calendar quarter. The applicable data elements in paragraphs (f)(6)(i) through (xii) of this section must be entered into ECMPS with the PDF report.
units.action_summary: If using PM CPMS or HAP metals CEMS for compliance, submit quarterly PDF QA/QC activity reports beginning Q1 2024 (or the first quarter used for compliance), due within 60 days after quarter end, and enter specified ECMPS data elements with each PDF.

units.obligation_text: You must keep records according to paragraphs (a)(1) and (2) of this section. If you are required to (or elect to) continuously monitor Hg and/or HCl and/or HF and/or PM emissions, or if you elect to use a PM CPMS, you must keep the records required under appendix A and/or appendix B and/or appendix C and/or appendix D to this subpart. If you elect to conduct periodic (e.g., quarterly or annual) performance stack tests, then, for each test completed on or after January 1, 2024, you must keep records of the applicable data elements under § 63.7(g). You must also keep records of all data elements and other information in appendix E to this subpart that apply to your compliance strategy.
units.action_summary: Keep records as specified: follow (a)(1)-(2), keep appendix-specific records for continuous monitoring or PM CPMS, keep §63.7(g) data elements for tests on/after Jan 1, 2024, and keep applicable appendix E data elements for your compliance strategy.

units.obligation_text: In accordance with § 63.10(b)(2)(xiv), a copy of each notification or report that you submit to comply with this subpart. You must also keep records of all supporting documentation for the initial Notifications of Compliance Status, semiannual compliance reports, or quarterly compliance reports that you submit.
units.action_summary: Keep copies of each notification or report submitted to comply with the subpart and all supporting documentation for initial Notifications of Compliance Status, semiannual, and quarterly compliance reports.

title: Control of Air Pollution from New Motor Vehicles: Heavy-Duty Engine Standards
Protection of Stratospheric Ozone: Listing of Substitutes Under the Significant New Alternatives Policy Program

units.section: Appendix W to Subpart G of Part 82 (Retail food refrigeration--medium-temperature standalone units)
units.obligation_text: Acceptable only for use in new medium-temperature stand-alone units where reasonable efforts have been made to ascertain that other alternatives are not technically feasible due to the inability to meet ADA requirements.
units.actor: users/installers/specifiers of retail food refrigeration equipment
units.action_summary: These listed refrigerants are permitted only for new medium-temperature standalone units and only when reasonable efforts show other alternatives are not technically feasible because of ADA requirements.

units.section: Appendix W to Subpart G of Part 82 (Retail food refrigeration--medium-temperature standalone units)
units.obligation_text: Users are required to document and retain the results of their technical investigation of alternatives for the purpose of demonstrating compliance.
units.action_summary: Users must document and keep records of their investigation showing other alternatives are not technically feasible.

units.section: Appendix W to Subpart G of Part 82 (I. Residential and light commercial air conditioning and heat pumps (new only))
units.obligation_text: These refrigerants may be used only in new equipment specifically designed and clearly identified for the refrigerants (i.e., none of these substitutes may be used as a conversion or "retrofit" refrigerant for existing equipment designed for other refrigerants).
units.actor: manufacturers, installers, and users of air conditioning equipment
units.action_summary: Permits use of listed refrigerants only in new equipment designed and labeled for them; prohibits use as retrofit refrigerants.

units.section: Appendix W to Subpart G of Part 82 (I. Residential and light commercial air conditioning and heat pumps (new only))
units.obligation_text: Applicable OSHA requirements at 29 CFR part 1910 must be followed, including those at 29 CFR 1910.94 (ventilation) and 1910.106 (flammable and combustible liquids), 1910.110 (storage and handling of liquefied petroleum gases), and 1910.1000 (toxic and hazardous substances).
units.actor: employers, technicians, manufacturers, and other persons responsible for manufacture, storage, and servicing
units.action_summary: OSHA regulations cited must be complied with when using these refrigerants.

units.section: Appendix W to Subpart G of Part 82 (I. Residential and light commercial air conditioning and heat pumps (new only))
units.obligation_text: Proper ventilation should be maintained at all times during the manufacture and storage of equipment containing hydrocarbon refrigerants.
units.action_summary: Maintain proper ventilation during manufacture and storage of equipment with hydrocarbon refrigerants.

units.section: Appendix W to Subpart G of Part 82 (I. Residential and light commercial air conditioning and heat pumps (new only))
units.obligation_text: If refrigerant levels in the air surrounding the equipment rise above one-fourth of the lower flammability limit, the space should be evacuated and reentry should occur only after the space has been properly ventilated.
units.action_summary: Evacuate and ventilate spaces if refrigerant concentration exceeds one-fourth of the lower flammability limit before reentry.

units.section: Appendix W to Subpart G of Part 82 (I. Residential and light commercial air conditioning and heat pumps (new only))
units.obligation_text: The charge size for the equipment must not exceed the maximum refrigerant mass determined according to UL 60335-2-40 for the room size where the air conditioner is used.
units.action_summary: Limit refrigerant charge to the UL-specified maximum mass for the room size.

units.section: Appendix W to Subpart G of Part 82 (I. Residential and light commercial air conditioning and heat pumps (new only))
units.obligation_text: The following markings must be attached at the locations provided and must be permanent: (a) On the outside of the air conditioning equipment: "WARNING--Risk of Fire. Flammable Refrigerant Used. To Be Repaired Only By Trained Service Personnel. Do Not Puncture Refrigerant Tubing." (b) On the outside of the air conditioning equipment: "WARNING--Risk of Fire. Dispose of Properly In Accordance With Federal Or Local Regulations. Flammable Refrigerant Used." (c) On the inside of the air conditioning equipment near the compressor: "WARNING--Risk of Fire. Flammable Refrigerant Used. Consult Repair Manual/Owner's Guide Before Attempting To Service This Product. All Safety Precautions Must be Followed." (d) For any equipment pre-charged at the factory, on the equipment packaging "WARNING--Risk of Fire due to Flammable Refrigerant Used. Follow Handling Instructions Carefully in Compliance with National Regulations" (e) On the indoor unit near the nameplate: markings for minimum installation height and minimum room area as specified.
units.action_summary: Equip and package equipment with permanent warning markings in specified locations and with specified content/format.

units.section: Appendix W to Subpart G of Part 82 (I. Residential and light commercial air conditioning and heat pumps (new only))
units.obligation_text: All of these markings must be in letters no less than 6.4 mm (1/4 inch) high.
units.action_summary: Markings required on equipment must use letters at least 6.4 mm high.

units.section: Appendix W to Subpart G of Part 82 (I. Residential and light commercial air conditioning and heat pumps (new only))
units.obligation_text: The equipment must have red Pantone Matching System (PMS) #185 or RAL 3020 marked pipes, hoses, or other devices through which the refrigerant passes, to indicate the use of a flammable refrigerant. This color must be applied at all service ports and other parts of the system where service puncturing or other actions creating an opening from the refrigerant circuit to the atmosphere might be expected and must extend a minimum of one (1) inch (25mm) in both directions from such locations and must be replaced if removed.
units.action_summary: Mark refrigerant-carrying components with specified red color at service points and maintain that marking.

units.section: Appendix W to Subpart G of Part 82 (I. Residential and light commercial air conditioning and heat pumps (new only))
units.obligation_text: Technicians and equipment manufacturers should wear appropriate personal protective equipment, including chemical goggles and protective gloves, when handling flammable refrigerants.
units.action_summary: Wear suitable PPE (goggles, gloves) when handling flammable refrigerants.

units.section: Appendix W to Subpart G of Part 82 (I. Residential and light commercial air conditioning and heat pumps (new only))
units.obligation_text: A class B dry powder type fire extinguisher should be kept nearby.
units.actor: facility operators, technicians, and owners of equipment
units.action_summary: Keep a class B dry powder fire extinguisher near equipment.

units.section: Appendix W to Subpart G of Part 82 (I. Residential and light commercial air conditioning and heat pumps (new only))
units.obligation_text: Technicians should only use spark-proof tools when working on air conditioning equipment with flammable refrigerants.
units.action_summary: Use only spark-proof tools when servicing equipment containing flammable refrigerants.

units.section: Appendix W to Subpart G of Part 82 (I. Residential and light commercial air conditioning and heat pumps (new only))
units.obligation_text: Any recovery equipment used should be designed for flammable refrigerants. Any refrigerant releases should be in a well-ventilated area, such as outside of a building.
units.action_summary: Use recovery equipment designed for flammable refrigerants and vent releases to well-ventilated areas.

units.section: Appendix W to Subpart G of Part 82 (I. Residential and light commercial air conditioning and heat pumps (new only))
units.obligation_text: Only technicians specifically trained in handling flammable refrigerants should service refrigeration equipment containing this refrigerant.
units.action_summary: Require specific training for technicians servicing equipment with flammable refrigerants.

units.section: Appendix W to Subpart G of Part 82 (I. Residential and light commercial air conditioning and heat pumps (new only))
units.obligation_text: Room occupants should evacuate the space immediately following the accidental release of this refrigerant.
units.action_summary: Evacuate immediately after accidental refrigerant release.

units.section: Appendix W to Subpart G of Part 82 (I. Residential and light commercial air conditioning and heat pumps (new only))
units.obligation_text: Technicians should gain an understanding of minimizing the risk of fire and the steps to use flammable refrigerants safely.
units.action_summary: Technicians must be knowledgeable about fire risk minimization and safe use procedures for flammable refrigerants.

units.section: Appendix W to Subpart G of Part 82 (I. Residential and light commercial air conditioning and heat pumps (new only))
units.obligation_text: If refrigerant levels in the air surrounding the equipment rise above one-fourth of the lower flammability limit, the space should be evacuated and reentry should occur only after the space has been properly ventilated.
units.action_summary: Evacuate and ventilate if refrigerant concentration exceeds a quarter of the lower flammability limit.

units.section: Appendix W to Subpart G of Part 82 (I. Residential and light commercial air conditioning and heat pumps (new only))
units.obligation_text: Department of Transportation requirements for transport of flammable gases must be followed.
units.action_summary: Follow DOT hazardous materials transport requirements for flammable gases.

title: Increasing Consistency and Transparency in Considering Benefits and Costs in the Clean Air Act Rulemaking Process

units.obligation_text: the Agency must develop BCAs of significant CAA regulations in accordance with best available scientific information and best practices from the economic, engineering, physical, and biological sciences, including the following practices.
units.action_summary: EPA must prepare Benefit-Cost Analyses (BCAs) for significant Clean Air Act regulations following best available science and best practices.

units.obligation_text: In preparing the BCA, the Agency must include: (i) A statement of need; (ii) An examination of regulatory options; and (iii) To the extent feasible, an assessment of all benefits and costs of these regulatory options relative to the baseline scenario.
units.action_summary: EPA must include a statement of need, examine regulatory options, and, to the extent feasible, assess all benefits and costs relative to baseline in the BCA.

units.obligation_text: In preparing the BCA, the Agency must include a statement of need that provides: A clear description of the problem being addressed, the reasons for and significance of any failure of by private markets or public institutions causing this problem, and the compelling need for federal government intervention in the market to correct the problem.
units.action_summary: EPA must include a statement of need describing the problem, market/institutional failures, and why federal intervention is necessary.

units.obligation_text: In preparing the BCA the Agency must analyze the benefits and costs of regulatory options, as well as the benefits and costs of other notable deviations from the proposed for which the Agency is soliciting comment or the finalized option. Where there is a continuum of options (such as options that vary in stringency), the Agency must analyze at least three regulatory options (as provided in section XX(a)(3)(i)) and explain why these were selected.
units.action_summary: EPA must analyze benefits and costs of regulatory options and notable deviations; when options form a continuum, EPA must analyze at least three options and justify their selection.

units.obligation_text: If fewer than three options are analyzed, or if there is a continuum of options and the options analyzed do not include at least one more stringent and one less stringent option than the proposed or finalized option, then the Agency must explain why it is not appropriate to analyze more options.
units.action_summary: If EPA analyzes fewer than three options or omits more/less stringent alternatives, it must explain why additional options are not appropriate.

units.obligation_text: In preparing the BCA, the Agency must use a baseline that appropriately considers relevant factors and relies on transparent and reasonable assumptions. The factors for which the Agency must account in the baseline include, but are not limited to, the following: (i) Exogenous changes in the economy ...; (ii) Regulations promulgated by the Agency or other government entities; and (iii) The degree of compliance by regulated entities with other regulations. In rulemaking actions where the Agency determines it is appropriate to consider more than one baseline ..., the Agency must provide a reasoned explanation for the baselines used and must identify the key uncertainties in the forecast(s).
units.action_summary: EPA must use an appropriate, transparent baseline accounting for relevant factors (economic changes, other regulations, compliance) and, if using multiple baselines, explain choices and key uncertainties.

units.obligation_text: In preparing the BCA, the Agency must rely on the use of a framework that is appropriate for the characteristics of the regulation being evaluated and must provide an explanation for the approach adopted.
units.action_summary: EPA must use an appropriate analytical framework for the regulation and explain why that approach was chosen.

units.obligation_text: The Agency must consider how costs and benefits may be affected by consumer and producer behavior in the baseline and potential behavioral changes from the policy scenarios.
units.action_summary: EPA must account for consumer and producer behavior effects in baseline and policy scenarios when assessing costs and benefits.

units.obligation_text: During the estimation of benefits, the Agency must link regulatory requirements to the value that individuals place on the change in benefit endpoints that can be meaningfully attributed to those requirements. The Agency must select benefit endpoints that the scientific evidence indicates there is: (i) A clear causal or likely causal relationship between pollutant exposure and effect, and subsequently; and (ii) An anticipated change in that effect in response to changes in environmental quality or exposures expected as a result of the regulation under analysis. The Agency must quantify effects for endpoints which scientific evidence is robust enough to support such quantification.
units.action_summary: EPA must link requirements to individual valuations of attributable benefit endpoints, choose endpoints with causal/anticipatable changes, and quantify effects when evidence supports it.

units.obligation_text: The Agency must, to the extent supported by scientific literature as well as practicable in a given rulemaking: (i) Quantify all benefits; (ii) Monetize all the benefits by following well-defined economic principles using well-established economic methods; and (iii) Qualitatively characterize benefits that cannot be quantified or monetized.
units.action_summary: To the extent supported and practicable, EPA must quantify and monetize benefits using established methods, and qualitatively characterize non-quantifiable benefits.

units.obligation_text: When selecting and quantifying health endpoints in a BCA, the Agency must: (i) Explain the basis for significant judgments, assumptions, data, models, and inferences used or relied upon in the assessment or decision; (ii) Describe the sources, extent and magnitude of significant uncertainties associated with the assessment; (iii) When selecting concentration-response relationships from the scientific literature, the Agency must select from studies where each selected study meets the criteria in paragraphs (b)(8)(iii)(A) through (C) of this section. ... (iv) When multiple studies satisfy these criteria the Agency must characterize multiple concentration-response functions, and, if appropriate, combine them ...; (v) The Agency must base decisions about the choice of the number of alternative concentration-response functions quantified for each endpoint on the extent to which it is technically feasible ...; (vi) The Agency must select and clearly identify concentration-response functions with the strongest scientific evidence, as well as evidence necessary to demonstrate the sensitivity ...; (vii) Once the Agency has identified the concentration-response functions to be used for quantifying the selected health endpoints, the Agency must characterize, in a BCA or related technical support document: (A) ... (G) ...; (viii) When feasible, the Agency must use a probability distribution of risk when determining expected benefits. When it is infeasible to estimate a distribution, the Agency must use measures of the central tendency of risk. Upper-bound risk estimates must not be used unless they are presented in conjunction with lower bound and central tendency estimates.
units.action_summary: EPA must explain judgments and uncertainties, select concentration-response studies meeting specified criteria, characterize multiple functions when appropriate, justify number chosen, identify strongest evidence, document variability/assumptions/confounders/geographic differences, and use probability distributions of risk when feasible (avoiding sole upper-bound estimates).

units.obligation_text: The study was externally and independently peer-reviewed consistent with Federal guidance; The pollutant analyzed in the study matches the pollutant of interest in the regulation; Concentration-response functions must be parameterized from scientifically robust studies; When an epidemiological study is used further criteria include that the study must assess the influence of confounders, that the study location must be appropriately matched to the analysis, and that the study population characteristics must be sufficiently similar to those of the analysis.
units.action_summary: EPA must select concentration-response studies that are externally peer-reviewed, pollutant-matched, scientifically robust, and (for epidemiology) assess confounders and be appropriately matched to the analysis population and location.

units.obligation_text: The Agency must identify uncertainties underlying the estimation of both benefits and costs and, to the extent feasible, quantitatively analyze those that are most influential; and must present benefits and cost estimates in ways that convey their uncertainty. The Agency must provide a reasoned explanation for the scope and specific quantitative or qualitative methods chosen to analyze uncertainties.
units.action_summary: EPA must identify and, where feasible, quantitatively analyze major uncertainties in benefit and cost estimation and present estimates to convey uncertainty along with reasons for chosen methods.

units.obligation_text: To the extent feasible, the Agency must use quantitative methods to analyze uncertainties that have the largest potential effect ... The Agency must characterize, preferably quantitatively, sources of uncertainty in the assessment of costs, changes in air quality, assessment of likely changes in health and welfare endpoints, and the valuation of those changes. Where data are sufficient to do so, the Agency must consider sources of uncertainty both independently and jointly. To the extent feasible, the Agency must also consider, and transparently acknowledge, the extent to which qualitatively-assessed costs or benefits are characterized by uncertainty. Where probability distributions for relevant input assumptions are available, characterize significant sources of uncertainty ... the Agency must characterize how the probability distributions ... would impact the resulting distribution of benefit and cost estimates. Except as provided in this paragraph, the Agency must provide expected-value estimates of benefits and costs as well as distributions about each of the estimates. In cases where estimates based on expected values are not feasible, the Agency must present a plausible range of benefits and costs.
units.action_summary: EPA must use quantitative methods for major uncertainties when feasible, characterize uncertainties in costs/air quality/health/valuation (independently and jointly when possible), acknowledge qualitative uncertainty, use input distributions to assess impact on benefit/cost distributions, and provide expected-value estimates or plausible ranges.

units.obligation_text: In presenting the results of the BCA the Agency must include the following elements: (i) The Agency must present the overall results of the BCA (benefits, costs, and net benefits of each regulatory option evaluated in the BCA) in a manner designed to be objective, comprehensive, reproducible to the extent reasonably possible, and easily understood by the public. (ii) The Agency must describe how the benefits and costs were estimated in the BCA, including the assumptions made for the analysis. The Agency must describe the models, data, and assumptions used to estimate benefits and costs, and the evaluation and selection process for these analytical decisions. The Agency must provide an explanation of procedures used to select among input parameters to the benefit and cost models, and any methods used to quantify risk and to model fate and transport of pollutants. (iii) Consistent with the best available scientific information, the Agency must discuss non-monetized and non-quantified benefits and costs of the action. The Agency must present available evidence on non-monetized and non-quantified benefits and costs, including explanations as to why they are not being monetized or quantified and discussions of what the potential impact of those benefits and costs might be on the overall results of the BCA. (iv) The Agency must assess the sources of uncertainty that are likely to have a substantial effect on the results of the BCA and present the results of this assessment. The Agency must identify any data and models used to analyze uncertainty in the BCA, and the quality of the available data shall be discussed.
units.action_summary: EPA must present BCA results objectively and accessibly; describe estimation methods, models, data, assumptions and selection procedures; discuss non-monetized/non-quantified benefits/costs and their potential impacts; and assess and present major sources of uncertainty and data/model quality.

units.obligation_text: To the extent permitted by law, the Agency must ensure that all information (including data and models) used in the development of the BCA is publicly available. If the data and models are proprietary, the Agency must make available, to the extent permitted by law, the underlying inputs and assumptions used, equations, and methodologies used by EPA, while continuing to provide appropriate protection for information claimed as confidential business information (CBI), personally identifiable information (PII), and other privileged, non-exempt information.
units.action_summary: Where permitted by law, EPA must make BCA data and models publicly available, and for proprietary items provide underlying inputs, assumptions, equations, and methods as allowed while protecting CBI, PII and privileged information.

units.obligation_text: The Agency must provide a reasoned explanation for any departures from best practices in the BCA, including a discussion of the likely effect of the departures on the results of the BCA.
units.action_summary: If EPA departs from best practices in a BCA, it must explain the departure and discuss likely effects on BCA results.

units.obligation_text: The provisions of this subpart apply to benefit-cost analyses (BCA) prepared for all future significant regulations under the Clean Air Act (CAA). Except where explicitly stated otherwise, the provisions of this subpart do not apply to any other type of agency action, including individual party adjudications, enforcement activities, or permit proceedings.
units.actor: the provisions of this subpart / the Agency
units.action_summary: These provisions apply to BCAs for future significant CAA regulations and, unless stated otherwise, do not apply to other agency actions like adjudications, enforcement, or permits.

units.obligation_text: The Agency must provide, in addition to the reporting of the overall results of the BCA as specified in Sec. _._(a)(11)(i), a summary in the preamble of the overall BCA results, including total costs, benefits, and net benefits.
units.action_summary: EPA must include in the preamble a summary of overall BCA results (total costs, benefits, and net benefits) in addition to other reporting.

units.obligation_text: The Agency must provide an additional presentation in the preamble of the public health and welfare benefits that pertain to the specific objective (or objectives, as the case may be) of the CAA provision or provisions under which the rule is promulgated.
units.action_summary: EPA must include in the preamble an additional presentation of public health and welfare benefits tied to the specific objectives of the CAA provisions relevant to the rule.

units.obligation_text: This presentation must list the benefit categories arising from the environmental improvement that is targeted by the relevant statutory provision and report the monetized value to society of these benefits.
units.action_summary: EPA must list benefit categories targeted by the statutory provision and report their monetized societal values in the preamble presentation.

units.obligation_text: If these benefit categories cannot be monetized, the Agency must report the quantified estimates of these benefits to the extent possible and provide a qualitative characterization if they cannot be quantified.
units.action_summary: If monetization is not possible, EPA must report quantified estimates when possible and otherwise provide qualitative descriptions of benefits.

units.obligation_text: When the CAA provision or provisions under which the rule is promulgated contemplate the consideration of specific costs, the Agency must provide a transparent presentation of how those specific costs relate to total costs, to the extent possible.
units.action_summary: When relevant CAA provisions call for considering specific costs, EPA must transparently show how those specific costs relate to total costs, as far as possible.

units.obligation_text: The presentations specified in paragraphs (a), (b), and (c) of this section must be placed in the same section in the preamble of the regulation.
units.action_summary: EPA must place the presentations required by paragraphs (a), (b), and (c) together in the same preamble section of the regulation.

units.obligation_text: A State listed in paragraph (b)(2)(i) of this section may adopt and include in a SIP revision, and the Administrator will approve, regulations replacing specified provisions of subpart BBBBB of part 97 of this chapter for the State’s sources, and not substantively replacing any other provisions, as follows:
units.action_summary: A State may adopt abbreviated SIP revisions replacing specified provisions of subpart BBBBB, and the Administrator will approve such regulations.

units.obligation_text: Year of the control period for which CSAPR NOX Ozone Season Group 1 allowances are allocated or auctioned — Deadline for submission of allocations or auction results to the Administrator: 2023 and 2024 — June 1 of the fourth year before the year of the control period; 2025 and any year thereafter — June 1 of the third year before the year of the control period.
units.actor: A State (submitting allocations or auction results)
units.action_summary: States must submit allocations or auction results for Group 1 allowances to the Administrator by the specified June 1 deadlines for the listed control-period years.

units.obligation_text: Following promulgation of an approval by the Administrator of such a SIP revision, the provisions of the SIP revision will apply to sources in the State with regard to emissions occurring in the control period that begins May 1 immediately after promulgation of such approval, or such later control period as may be adopted by the State in its regulations and approved by the Administrator in the SIP revision, and in each subsequent control period, except as provided in paragraph (b)(15) of this section.
units.actor: Sources in the State; the SIP revision
units.action_summary: After Administrator approval, the SIP revision's provisions apply to sources in the State for emissions in the specified control period and subsequent control periods, unless paragraph (b)(15) applies.

units.obligation_text: A State listed in paragraph (b)(2)(iii) or (iv) of this section may adopt and include in a SIP revision, and the Administrator will approve, regulations replacing specified provisions of subpart EEEEE of part 97 of this chapter for the State’s sources, and not substantively replacing any other provisions, as follows:
units.action_summary: A State may adopt abbreviated SIP revisions replacing specified provisions of subpart EEEEE, and the Administrator will approve those revisions.

units.obligation_text: The State may adopt, as applicability provisions replacing the provisions in § 97.804(a) and (b) of this chapter with regard to the State, provisions substantively identical to those provisions, except that applicability is expanded to include all other units (beyond any units to which applicability could be expanded under paragraph (b)(8)(i) of this section) that would have been subject to any emissions trading program regulations approved as a SIP revision for the State under § 51.121 of this chapter;
units.action_summary: The State may adopt applicability provisions substantively identical to § 97.804(a) and (b) but expanded to include additional units that would have been subject under a SIP revision.

units.obligation_text: Year of the control period for which CSAPR NOX Ozone Season Group 2 allowances are allocated or auctioned — Deadline for submission of allocations or auction results to the Administrator: 2025 and any year thereafter — June 1 of the third year before the year of the control period.
units.actor: A State (submitting allocations or auction results)
units.action_summary: States must submit allocations or auction results for Group 2 allowances to the Administrator by the specified June 1 deadlines for the listed control-period years.

units.obligation_text: Full SIP revisions adopting State CSAPR NOX Ozone Season Group 2 Trading Programs. A State listed in paragraph (b)(2)(iii) or (iv) of this section may adopt and include in a SIP revision, and the Administrator will approve, regulations replacing specified provisions of subpart EEEEE of part 97 of this chapter for the State’s sources, and not substantively replacing any other provisions, as follows:
units.action_summary: A State may adopt full SIP revisions adopting Group 2 trading program provisions and the Administrator will approve such SIP revisions.

units.obligation_text: May adopt, as applicability provisions replacing the provisions in § 97.804(a) and (b) of this chapter with regard to the State, provisions substantively identical to those provisions, except that applicability is expanded to include all other units (beyond any units to which applicability could be expanded under paragraph (b)(9)(i) of this section) that would have been subject to any emissions trading program regulations approved as a SIP revision for the State under § 51.121 of this chapter;
units.action_summary: The State may adopt applicability provisions identical to § 97.804(a) and (b) but expanded to include additional units.

units.obligation_text: A State listed in paragraph (b)(2)(i) or (iii) of this section may adopt and include in a SIP revision, and the Administrator will approve, as correcting the deficiency in the SIP that is the basis for the CSAPR Federal Implementation Plan set forth in paragraphs (b)(1), (b)(2)(i), and (b)(3) and (4) of this section or paragraphs (b)(1), (b)(2)(iii), and (b)(7) and (8) of this section, as applicable, with regard to sources in the State (but not sources in any Indian country within the borders of the State), regulations that are substantively identical to the provisions of the CSAPR NOX Ozone Season Group 3 Trading Program set forth in §§ 97.1002 through 97.1035 of this chapter, subject to the following requirements and exceptions:
units.action_summary: A State may adopt SIP revisions adopting Group 3 trading program provisions (as corrective SIP revisions) and the Administrator will approve them, subject to specified requirements and exceptions.

units.obligation_text: The provisions of paragraphs (b)(13)(i) through (viii) of this section apply to any such SIP revision;
units.action_summary: Any SIP revision under this paragraph must comply with paragraphs (b)(13)(i) through (viii).

units.obligation_text: Following promulgation of an approval by the Administrator of such a SIP revision, the provisions of the SIP revision will apply to sources in the State with regard to emissions occurring in the control period that begins May 1 immediately after promulgation of such approval, or such later control period as may be adopted by the State in its regulations and approved by the Administrator in the SIP revision, and in each subsequent control period, except as provided in paragraph (b)(15) of this section.
units.actor: Sources in the State; the SIP revision
units.action_summary: After Administrator approval, the Group 3 SIP revision's provisions apply to sources in the State for emissions in the specified and subsequent control periods, subject to paragraph (b)(15).

units.obligation_text: A State listed in paragraph (b)(2)(v) of this section may adopt and include in a SIP revision, and the Administrator will approve, as CSAPR NOX Ozone Season Group 3 allowance allocation provisions replacing the provisions in § 97.1011(a) of this chapter with regard to the State and the control period in 2022, a list of CSAPR NOX Ozone Season Group 3 units and the amount of CSAPR NOX Ozone Season Group 3 allowances allocated to each unit on such list, provided that the list of units and allocations meets the following requirements:
units.action_summary: A State may adopt SIP revisions replacing § 97.1011(a) for 2022 by submitting a list of units and allocations, and the Administrator will approve such provisions if the list meets specified requirements.

units.obligation_text: All of the units on the list must be units that are in the State and commenced commercial operation before January 1, 2019;
units.action_summary: The list of units must include only in-state units that began commercial operation before Jan 1, 2019.

units.obligation_text: The total amount of CSAPR NOX Ozone Season Group 3 allowance allocations on the list must not exceed the amount, under § 97.1010(a) of this chapter for the State and the control period in 2022, of the CSAPR NOX Ozone Season Group 3 trading budget minus the sum of the new unit set-aside and Indian country new unit set-aside;
