units.action_summary: The total allocations on the list must not exceed the specified portion of the Group 3 trading budget for 2022 (budget minus set-asides).

units.obligation_text: The list must be submitted electronically in a format specified by the Administrator;
units.action_summary: The State must submit the list electronically in a format the Administrator specifies.

units.obligation_text: The SIP revision must not provide for any change in the units and allocations on the list after approval of the SIP revision by the Administrator and must not provide for any change in any allocation determined and recorded by the Administrator under subpart GGGGG of part 97 of this chapter;
units.action_summary: The SIP revision may not allow any changes to the units or allocations after Administrator approval and may not change allocations recorded by the Administrator.

units.obligation_text: By [DATE 60 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF THE FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER], the State must notify the Administrator electronically in a format specified by the Administrator of the State’s intent to submit to the Administrator a complete SIP revision meeting the requirements of paragraphs (b)(11)(i) through (iv) of this section by [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF THE FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER];
units.action_summary: By the first specified date, the State must electronically notify the Administrator of its intent to submit a complete SIP revision meeting the (b)(11)(i)-(iv) requirements by the second specified date.

units.obligation_text: The State must submit to the Administrator a complete SIP revision described in paragraph (b)(11)(v)(A) of this section by [DATE 180 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF THE FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER].
units.action_summary: The State must submit the complete SIP revision by the specified 180‑day date.

units.obligation_text: A State listed in paragraph (b)(2)(v) of this section may adopt and include in a SIP revision, and the Administrator will approve, regulations replacing specified provisions of subpart GGGGG of part 97 of this chapter for the State’s sources, and not substantively replacing any other provisions, as follows:
units.action_summary: A State may adopt abbreviated SIP revisions replacing specified provisions of subpart GGGGG, and the Administrator will approve those revisions.

units.obligation_text: The State may adopt, as applicability provisions replacing the provisions in § 97.1004(a)(1) and (2) of this chapter with regard to the State, provisions substantively identical to those provisions, except that the words 'more than 25 MWe' are replaced, wherever such words appear, by words specifying a uniform lower limit on the amount of megawatts that is not greater than the amount specified by the words 'more than 25 MWe' and is not less than the amount specified by the words '15 MWe or more';
units.action_summary: The State may adopt applicability provisions like § 97.1004(a)(1) and (2) but may set a uniform lower MW limit between 15 MWe and 25 MWe.

units.obligation_text: The State may adopt, as applicability provisions replacing the provisions in § 97.1004(a) and (b) of this chapter with regard to the State, provisions substantively identical to those provisions, except that applicability is expanded to include all other units (beyond any units to which applicability could be expanded under paragraph (b)(12)(i) of this section) that would have been subject to any emissions trading program regulations approved as a SIP revision for the State under § 51.121 of this chapter;
units.action_summary: The State may adopt applicability provisions identical to § 97.1004(a) and (b) but expanded to include additional units that would have been subject under an approved SIP revision.

units.obligation_text: Requires the State or the permitting authority to allocate and, if applicable, auction a total amount of CSAPR NOX Ozone Season Group 3 allowances for any such control period not exceeding the amount, under §§ 97.1010(a) and 97.1021 of this chapter for the State and such control period, of the CSAPR NOX Ozone Season Group 3 trading budget minus the sum of the Indian country new unit set-aside and the amount of any CSAPR NOX Ozone Season Group 3 allowances already allocated and recorded by the Administrator, plus, if the State adopts regulations expanding applicability to additional units pursuant to paragraph (b)(12)(ii) of this section, an additional amount of CSAPR NOX Ozone Season Group 3 allowances not exceeding the lesser of the two calculations specified in (1) and (2).
units.actor: The State or the permitting authority
units.action_summary: The State or permitting authority must allocate/auction no more than the specified total amount of Group 3 allowances for a control period, with a possible additional amount if applicability is expanded, subject to two alternative calculation limits.

units.obligation_text: The additional amount may not exceed the highest of the sum, for all additional units in the State to which applicability is expanded pursuant to paragraph (b)(12)(ii) of this section, of the NOX emissions reported in accordance with part 75 of this chapter for the ozone season in the year before the year of the submission deadline for the SIP revision and the corresponding sums for each of the two immediately preceding ozone seasons, subject to exclusion of emissions on days without at least one quality-assured monitor operating hour.
units.actor: The State or the permitting authority (calculating additional amount)
units.action_summary: If applicability is expanded, the additional amount of allowances allocated may not exceed the highest of seasonal sums of NOX emissions for additional units, excluding days lacking quality-assured monitoring hours.

units.obligation_text: Or the additional amount may not exceed the portion of the emissions budget under the State’s emissions trading program regulations approved as a SIP revision under § 51.121 of this chapter that is attributable to the units to which applicability is expanded pursuant to paragraph (b)(12)(ii) of this section;
units.actor: The State or the permitting authority (calculating additional amount)
units.action_summary: Alternatively, the additional amount of allowances may not exceed the portion of the State emissions trading program budget attributable to the units added by expanding applicability.

units.obligation_text: Requires that the State or the permitting authority submit such allocations or the results of such auctions for such control period (except allocations or results of auctions to such units of CSAPR NOX Ozone Season Group 3 allowances remaining in a set-aside after completion of the allocations or auctions for which the set-aside was created) to the Administrator no later than the dates in Table 7 to this paragraph (b)(12)(iii)(B). Table 7 deadlines: 2023 — June 1, 2022; 2024 — June 1, 2022; 2025 — June 1, 2023; 2026 — June 1, 2023; 2027 and any year thereafter — June 1 of the third year before the year of the control period.
units.actor: The State or the permitting authority
units.action_summary: The State or permitting authority must submit allocations or auction results to the Administrator by the Table 7 deadlines for the listed control-period years.
units.modal_raw: Requires (submit no later than specified dates)

units.obligation_text: Requires that the State or the permitting authority submit such allocations or the results of such auctions (except allocations or results of auctions to such units of CSAPR NOX Ozone Season Group 3 allowances remaining in a set-aside after completion of the allocations or auctions for which the set-aside was created) to the Administrator by April 1 of the year following the year of such control period;
units.actor: The State or the permitting authority
units.action_summary: The State or permitting authority must submit allocations or auction results (for units covered by §§ 97.1011(b)(1) and 97.1012(a)) to the Administrator by April 1 after the control period year.

units.obligation_text: Does not provide for any change, after the submission deadlines in paragraphs (b)(12)(iii)(B) and (C) of this section, in the allocations submitted to the Administrator by such deadlines and does not provide for any change in any allocation determined and recorded by the Administrator under subpart GGGGG of part 97 of this chapter, § 97.526(c) of this chapter, or § 97.826(c) of this chapter;
units.action_summary: The SIP revision may not provide for any changes to allocations after the submission deadlines and may not change allocations determined and recorded by the Administrator.

units.obligation_text: Provided that the State must submit a complete SIP revision meeting the requirements of paragraph (b)(12)(i), (ii), or (iii) of this section by December 1 of the year before the year of the deadlines for submission of allocations or auction results under paragraphs (b)(12)(iii)(B) and (C) of this section applicable to the first control period for which the State wants to replace the applicability provisions, make allocations, or hold an auction under paragraph (b)(12)(i), (ii), or (iii) of this section.
units.action_summary: The State must submit a complete SIP revision meeting the (b)(12) requirements by December 1 of the year before the year of the applicable submission deadlines for the first control period the State intends to replace applicability, allocate, or hold an auction.

units.obligation_text: A State listed in paragraph (b)(2)(v) of this section may adopt and include in a SIP revision, and the Administrator will approve, as correcting the deficiency in the SIP that is the basis for the CSAPR Federal Implementation Plan set forth in paragraphs (b)(1), (b)(2)(v), and (b)(11) and (12) of this section with regard to sources in the State (but not sources in any Indian country within the borders of the State), regulations that are substantively identical to the provisions of the CSAPR NOX Ozone Season Group 3 Trading Program set forth in §§ 97.1002 through 97.1035 of this chapter, except that the SIP revision:
units.action_summary: A State may adopt and submit a full SIP revision adopting Group 3 trading program provisions as corrective SIP revisions, and the Administrator will approve them, subject to specified exceptions and requirements.

units.obligation_text: May adopt, as applicability provisions replacing the provisions in § 97.1004(a)(1) and (2) of this chapter with regard to the State, provisions substantively identical to those provisions, except that the words 'more than 25 MWe' are replaced, wherever such words appear, by words specifying a uniform lower limit on the amount of megawatts that is not greater than the amount specified by the words 'more than 25 MWe' and is not less than the amount specified by the words '15 MWe or more';
units.action_summary: The State may adopt applicability provisions replacing 'more than 25 MWe' with a uniform lower MW limit between 15 and 25 MWe.

units.obligation_text: May adopt, as applicability provisions replacing the provisions in § 97.1004(a) and (b) of this chapter with regard to the State, provisions substantively identical to those provisions, except that applicability is expanded to include all other units (beyond any units to which applicability could be expanded under paragraph (b)(13)(i) of this section) that would have been subject to any emissions trading program regulations approved as a SIP revision for the State under § 51.121 of this chapter;
units.action_summary: The State may adopt applicability provisions identical to § 97.1004(a) and (b) but expanded to include additional units.

units.obligation_text: May adopt, as CSAPR NOX Ozone Season Group 3 allowance allocation provisions replacing the provisions in §§ 97.1011(a) and (b)(1) and 97.1012(a) of this chapter with regard to the State and the control period in 2023 or any subsequent year, any methodology under which the State or the permitting authority allocates or auctions CSAPR NOX Ozone Season Group 3 allowances and that—(A) Requires the State or the permitting authority to allocate and, if applicable, auction a total amount ... not exceeding ... plus, if the State adopts regulations expanding applicability ... an additional amount ... not exceeding the lesser of: (1) ... or (2) ...
units.actor: The State or the permitting authority
units.action_summary: The State may adopt allocation/auction methodologies for Group 3 allowances for 2023 and later, but such methodologies must limit total allocations to the specified amounts, with additional allowance caps if applicability is expanded, using one of two calculation methods.

units.obligation_text: Requires that the State or the permitting authority submit such allocations or the results of such auctions for such control period (except allocations or results of auctions to such units of CSAPR NOX Ozone Season Group 3 allowances remaining in a set-aside after completion of the allocations or auctions for which the set-aside was created) to the Administrator no later than the dates in Table 8 to this paragraph (b)(13)(iii)(B). Table 8 deadlines: 2023 — June 1, 2022; 2024 — June 1, 2022; 2025 — June 1, 2023; 2026 — June 1, 2023; 2027 and any year thereafter — June 1 of the third year before the year of the control period.
units.actor: The State or the permitting authority
units.action_summary: The State or permitting authority must submit allocations or auction results to the Administrator by the Table 8 deadlines for the listed control-period years.
units.modal_raw: Requires (submit no later than specified dates)

units.obligation_text: Requires that the State or the permitting authority submit such allocations or the results of such auctions ... to the Administrator by April 1 of the year following the year of such control period;
units.actor: The State or the permitting authority
units.action_summary: The State or permitting authority must submit allocations or auction results to the Administrator by April 1 following the control period year for units covered by §§ 97.1011(b)(1) and 97.1012(a).

units.obligation_text: Does not provide for any change, after the submission deadlines in paragraphs (b)(13)(iii)(B) and (C) of this section, in the allocations submitted to the Administrator by such deadlines and does not provide for any change in any allocation determined and recorded by the Administrator under subpart GGGGG of part 97 of this chapter,
units.action_summary: The SIP revision may not allow changes to allocations after the submission deadlines and may not change allocations determined and recorded by the Administrator.

title: National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) Electronic Reporting Rule: Phase 2 Extension

units.obligation_text: As of December 21, 2023 or an EPA-approved alternative date (see 40 CFR 127.24(e) or (f)), all certifications submitted in compliance with paragraphs (b)(15)(i)(A) and (B) of this section must be submitted electronically by the owner or operator to the Director or initial recipient, as defined in 40 CFR 127.2(b), in compliance with this section and 40 CFR part 3 (including, in all cases, subpart D to part 3), § 122.22, and 40 CFR part 127.
units.action_summary: Certifications required under the cited paragraphs must be submitted electronically to the Director or initial recipient, in compliance with specified parts.

units.obligation_text: Prior to this date, and independent of 40 CFR part 127, owners or operators may be required to report electronically if specified by a particular permit or if required to do so by state law.
units.action_summary: Before the electronic reporting deadline, owners/operators may nonetheless be required to report electronically under permit or state law.

units.obligation_text: Submit the signed certification to the NPDES permitting authority once every five years.
units.action_summary: Submit a signed certification to the NPDES permitting authority every five years.

units.obligation_text: As of December 21, 2023 or an EPA-approved alternative date (see 40 CFR 127.24(e) or (f)), all certifications submitted in compliance with this section must be submitted electronically by the owner or operator to the Director or initial recipient, as defined in 40 CFR 127.2(b), in compliance with this section and 40 CFR part 3 (including, in all cases, subpart D to part 3), § 122.22, and 40 CFR part 127.
units.action_summary: Certifications required by this section must be submitted electronically to the Director or initial recipient as of the deadline.

units.obligation_text: Prior to this date, and independent of 40 CFR part 127, owners or operators may be required to report electronically if specified by a particular permit or if required to do so by state law.
units.action_summary: Before the electronic reporting deadline, owners/operators may be required to report electronically under permit or state law.

units.obligation_text: Except as provided in paragraphs (b)(2)(v) and (vi) of this section, dischargers (or treatment works treating domestic sewage) seeking coverage under a general permit shall submit to the Director a notice of intent to be covered by the general permit.
units.actor: dischargers (or treatment works treating domestic sewage)
units.action_summary: Dischargers seeking general permit coverage must submit a notice of intent to the Director, except as provided elsewhere.

units.obligation_text: A discharger (or treatment works treating domestic sewage) who fails to submit a notice of intent in accordance with the terms of the permit is not authorized to discharge, (or in the case of sludge disposal permit, to engage in a sludge use or disposal practice), under the terms of the general permit unless the general permit, in accordance with paragraph (b)(2)(v), contains a provision that a notice of intent is not required or the Director notifies a discharger (or treatment works treating domestic sewage) that it is covered by a general permit in accordance with paragraph (b)(2)(vi).
units.actor: discharger (or treatment works treating domestic sewage)
units.action_summary: A discharger who fails to submit the required notice of intent is not authorized to discharge under the general permit, unless exceptions apply.

units.obligation_text: As of December 21, 2023 or an EPA-approved alternative date (see 40 CFR 127.24(e) or (f)), all notices of intent submitted in compliance with this section must be submitted electronically by the discharger (or treatment works treating domestic sewage) to the Director or initial recipient, as defined in 40 CFR 127.2(b), in compliance with this section and 40 CFR part 3 (including, in all cases, subpart D to part 3), § 122.22, and 40 CFR part 127.
units.actor: discharger (or treatment works treating domestic sewage)
units.action_summary: Notices of intent required by this section must be submitted electronically to the Director or initial recipient as of the deadline.

units.obligation_text: Prior to this date, and independent of 40 CFR part 127, discharger (or treatment works treating domestic sewage) may be required to report electronically if specified by a particular permit or if required to do so by state law.
units.actor: discharger (or treatment works treating domestic sewage)
units.action_summary: Before the electronic reporting deadline, dischargers may be required to report electronically under permit or state law.

units.obligation_text: Unless the permittee is relying on another entity to satisfy its NPDES permit obligations under § 122.35(a), the permittee must submit annual reports to the NPDES permitting authority for its first permit term.
units.action_summary: Permittee must submit annual reports to the NPDES permitting authority during its first permit term unless another entity is relied upon.

units.obligation_text: For subsequent permit terms, the permittee must submit reports in year two and four unless the NPDES permitting authority requires more frequent reports.
units.action_summary: During subsequent permit terms, the permittee must submit reports in years two and four, unless the authority requires more frequent reports.

units.obligation_text: As of December 21, 2023 or an EPA-approved alternative date (see 40 CFR 127.24(e) or (f)), all reports submitted in compliance with this section must be submitted electronically by the owner, operator, or the duly authorized representative of the small MS4 to the NPDES permitting authority or initial recipient, as defined in 40 CFR 127.2(b), in compliance with this section and 40 CFR part 3 (including, in all cases, subpart D to part 3), § 122.22, and 40 CFR part 127.
units.actor: owner, operator, or the duly authorized representative of the small MS4
units.action_summary: Reports required by this section must be submitted electronically to the NPDES permitting authority or initial recipient as of the deadline.

units.obligation_text: Prior to this date, and independent of 40 CFR part 127, the owner, operator, or the duly authorized representative of the small MS4 may be required to report electronically if specified by a particular permit or if required to do so by state law.
units.actor: owner, operator, or the duly authorized representative of the small MS4
units.action_summary: Before the deadline, reporting electronically may be required by permit or state law.

units.obligation_text: The report must include:
units.action_summary: Required reports must include specified elements (listed following in the regulatory text).

units.obligation_text: The permittee shall report any noncompliance which may endanger health or the environment.
units.action_summary: Permittee must report any noncompliance that could endanger health or the environment.

units.obligation_text: Any information shall be provided orally within 24 hours from the time the permittee becomes aware of the circumstances.
units.action_summary: Provide oral notice within 24 hours of becoming aware of the noncompliance.

units.obligation_text: A report shall also be provided within 5 days of the time the permittee becomes aware of the circumstances.
units.action_summary: Provide a written report within 5 days of becoming aware of the noncompliance.

units.obligation_text: The report shall contain a description of the noncompliance and its cause; the period of noncompliance, including exact dates and times, and if the noncompliance has not been corrected, the anticipated time it is expected to continue; and steps taken or planned to reduce, eliminate, and prevent reoccurrence of the noncompliance.
units.action_summary: The report must include a description of the noncompliance, duration with dates/times, anticipated duration if ongoing, and corrective/preventative steps.

units.obligation_text: For noncompliance events related to combined sewer overflows, sanitary sewer overflows, or bypass events, these reports must include the data described above (with the exception of time of discovery) as well as the type of event (combined sewer overflows, sanitary sewer overflows, or bypass events), type of sewer overflow structure (e.g., manhole, combine sewer overflow outfall), discharge volumes untreated by the treatment works treating domestic sewage, types of human health and environmental impacts of the sewer overflow event, and whether the noncompliance was related to wet weather.
units.action_summary: Reports for CSO/SSO/bypass events must include the general report data (except time of discovery) plus event type, structure type, untreated discharge volumes, health and environmental impacts, and relation to wet weather.

units.obligation_text: As of December 21, 2023 or an EPA-approved alternative date (see 40 CFR 127.24(e) or (f)), all reports related to combined sewer overflows, sanitary sewer overflows, or bypass events submitted in compliance with this section must be submitted electronically by the permittee to the Director or initial recipient, as defined in 40 CFR 127.2(b), in compliance with this section and 40 CFR part 3 (including, in all cases, subpart D to part 3), § 122.22, and 40 CFR part 127.
units.action_summary: CSO/SSO/bypass event reports required by this section must be submitted electronically to the Director or initial recipient as of the deadline.

units.obligation_text: Prior to this date, and independent of 40 CFR part 127, permittees may be required to electronically submit reports related to combined sewer overflows, sanitary sewer overflows, or bypass events under this section by a particular permit or if required to do so by state law.
units.action_summary: Before the electronic reporting deadline, permittees may be required by permit or state law to submit CSO/SSO/bypass reports electronically.

units.obligation_text: The Director may also require permittees to electronically submit reports not related to combined sewer overflows, sanitary sewer overflows, or bypass events under this section.
units.action_summary: Director has authority to require electronic submission of other reports under this section.

units.obligation_text: The permittee shall report all instances of noncompliance not reported under paragraphs (l)(4), (5), and (6) of this section, at the time monitoring reports are submitted.
units.action_summary: Permittee must report instances of noncompliance not already reported under other paragraphs when submitting monitoring reports.

units.obligation_text: The reports shall contain the information listed in paragraph (l)(6).
units.action_summary: These reports must include the information required in paragraph (l)(6).

units.obligation_text: For noncompliance events related to combined sewer overflows, sanitary sewer overflows, or bypass events, these reports shall contain the information described in paragraph (l)(6) and the applicable required data in appendix A to 40 CFR part 127.
units.action_summary: Reports for CSO/SSO/bypass events must include paragraph (l)(6) information and applicable data elements in appendix A to part 127.

units.obligation_text: As of December 21, 2023 or an EPA-approved alternative date (see 40 CFR 127.24(e) or (f)), all reports related to combined sewer overflows, sanitary sewer overflows, or bypass events submitted in compliance with this section must be submitted electronically by the permittee to the Director or initial recipient, as defined in 40 CFR 127.2(b), in compliance with this section and 40 CFR part 3 (including, in all cases, subpart D to part 3), § 122.22, and 40 CFR part 127.
units.action_summary: CSO/SSO/bypass reports required under this paragraph must be submitted electronically to the Director/initial recipient as of the deadline.

units.obligation_text: Prior to this date, and independent of 40 CFR part 127, permittees may be required to electronically submit reports related to combined sewer overflows, sanitary sewer overflows, or bypass events under this section by a particular permit or if required to do so by state law.
units.action_summary: Before the deadline, permittees may need to submit CSO/SSO/bypass reports electronically if required by permit or state law.

units.obligation_text: If the permittee knows in advance of the need for a bypass, it shall submit prior notice, if possible, at least ten days before the date of the bypass.
units.action_summary: When anticipating a bypass, the permittee must provide prior notice at least 10 days before the bypass date, if possible.

units.obligation_text: As of December 21, 2023 or an EPA-approved alternative date (see 40 CFR 127.24(e) or (f)), all notices submitted in compliance with this section must be submitted electronically by the permittee to the Director or initial recipient, as defined in 40 CFR 127.2(b), in compliance with this section and 40 CFR part 3 (including, in all cases, subpart D to part 3), § 122.22, and 40 CFR part 127.
units.action_summary: Notices required under this bypass notice provision must be submitted electronically to the Director/initial recipient as of the deadline.

units.obligation_text: Prior to this date, and independent of 40 CFR part 127, permittees may be required to report electronically if specified by a particular permit or if required to do so by state law.
units.action_summary: Before the deadline, permittees may need to submit bypass notices electronically if required by permit or state law.

units.obligation_text: The permittee shall submit notice of an unanticipated bypass as required in paragraph (l)(6) of this section (24-hour notice).
units.action_summary: For an unanticipated bypass, the permittee must submit notice as required in paragraph (l)(6), i.e., within 24 hours.

units.obligation_text: As of December 21, 2023 or an EPA-approved alternative date (see 40 CFR 127.24(e) or (f)), all notices submitted in compliance with this section must be submitted electronically by the permittee to the Director or initial recipient, as defined in 40 CFR 127.2(b), in compliance with this section and 40 CFR part 3 (including, in all cases, subpart D to part 3), § 122.22, and 40 CFR part 127.
units.action_summary: Notices required for unanticipated bypasses must be submitted electronically to the Director or initial recipient as of the deadline.

units.obligation_text: Prior to this date, and independent of 40 CFR part 127, permittees may be required to report electronically if specified by a particular permit or if required to do so by state law.
units.action_summary: Before the deadline, permittees may be required to report electronically if specified by permit or state law.

units.obligation_text: The operator of a large or medium municipal separate storm sewer system or a municipal separate storm sewer that has been designated by the Director under § 122.26(a)(1)(v) must submit an annual report by the anniversary of the date of the issuance of the permit for such system.
units.actor: the operator of a large or medium MS4 (or designated MS4)
units.action_summary: Operators of specified MS4s must submit an annual report by the permit issuance anniversary.

units.obligation_text: As of December 21, 2023 or an EPA-approved alternative date (see 40 CFR 127.24(e) or (f)), all reports submitted in compliance with this section must be submitted electronically by the owner, operator, or the duly authorized representative of the MS4 to the Director or initial recipient, as defined in 40 CFR 127.2(b), in compliance with this section and 40 CFR part 3 (including, in all cases, subpart D to part 3), § 122.22, and 40 CFR part 127.
units.actor: owner, operator, or the duly authorized representative of the MS4
units.action_summary: MS4 reports required by this section must be submitted electronically to the Director/initial recipient as of the deadline.

units.obligation_text: Prior to this date, and independent of 40 CFR part 127, the owner, operator, or the duly authorized representative of the MS4 may be required to report electronically if specified by a particular permit or if required to do so by state law.
units.actor: owner, operator, or the duly authorized representative of the MS4
units.action_summary: Before the deadline, MS4 owners/operators may be required to report electronically if specified by permit or state law.

units.obligation_text: The report shall include:
units.action_summary: Required MS4 annual reports must include specified content (listed following in the regulatory text).

units.obligation_text: The permittee must submit an annual report to the Director.
units.action_summary: CAFO permittees must submit an annual report to the Director.

units.obligation_text: As of December 21, 2023 or an EPA-approved alternative date (see 40 CFR 127.24(e) or (f)), all annual reports submitted in compliance with this section must be submitted electronically by the permittee to the Director or initial recipient, as defined in 40 CFR 127.2(b), in compliance with this section and 40 CFR part 3 (including, in all cases, subpart D to part 3), § 122.22, and 40 CFR part 127.
units.action_summary: CAFO annual reports required by this section must be submitted electronically to the Director/initial recipient as of the deadline.

units.obligation_text: The annual report must include:
units.action_summary: CAFO annual reports must include specified content (listed following in the regulatory text).

units.obligation_text: Permittees that wish to terminate their permit must submit a Notice of Termination (NOT) to their permitting authority.
units.action_summary: Permittees desiring permit termination must submit a Notice of Termination to the permitting authority.

units.obligation_text: If requesting expedited permit termination procedures, a permittee must certify in the NOT that it is not subject to any pending State or Federal enforcement actions including citizen suits brought under State or Federal law.
units.action_summary: To request expedited termination, the permittee must certify in the NOT that it is not subject to pending state or federal enforcement actions, including citizen suits.

units.obligation_text: As of December 21, 2023 or an EPA-approved alternative date (see 40 CFR 127.24(e) or (f)), all NOTs submitted by general permit covered facilities in compliance with this section must be submitted electronically by the permittee to the Director or initial recipient, as defined in 40 CFR 127.2(b), in compliance with this section and 40 CFR part 3 (including, in all cases, subpart D), § 122.22, and 40 CFR part 127.
units.action_summary: NOTs from general permit covered facilities must be submitted electronically to the Director/initial recipient as of the deadline.

units.obligation_text: Prior to this date, and independent of 40 CFR part 127, the permittee may be required to report electronically if specified by a particular permit or if required to do so by state law.
units.action_summary: Before the deadline, permittees may need to submit NOTs electronically if required by permit or state law.

units.obligation_text: As of December 21, 2022, EPA must prepare public (quarterly and annual) reports as set forth here from information that is required to be submitted by NPDES-regulated facilities and the State Director.
units.action_summary: EPA is required to prepare public quarterly and annual reports from specified NPDES-submitted information starting December 21, 2022.

units.obligation_text: States, tribes, and territories that have received authorization from EPA to implement the NPDES program must electronically transfer these data, listed in § 127.21(a), to EPA within 40 days of the completed activity or within 40 days of the receipt of a report from an NPDES permittee, facility, or entity subject to this part [see § 127.1(a)].
units.actor: states, tribes, and territories authorized to implement the NPDES program
units.action_summary: Authorized states/tribes/territories must electronically transfer specified NPDES data to EPA within 40 days of activity completion or receipt of a permittee report.

units.obligation_text: EPA may set an alternative compliance deadline for data sharing for one or more facilities, general permit reports, program reports, and related data elements (see 40 CFR 127.24) provided this alternative compliance date does not extend beyond December 21, 2026.
units.action_summary: EPA has the authority to set alternative data-sharing deadlines, subject to an outer limit of December 21, 2026.

units.obligation_text: A state, tribe, or territory that is designated by EPA as the initial recipient [see §§ 127.2(b) and 127.27] for an NPDES data group [as defined in § 127.2(c)] may submit a request to EPA to establish an alternative compliance deadline for electronic reporting of one or more general permit reports, program reports, and related data elements (see Table 2 to appendix A).
units.actor: state, tribe, or territory designated by EPA as the initial recipient
units.action_summary: Designated initial recipient may submit a request to EPA for an alternative electronic reporting compliance deadline for specified reports and data elements.

units.obligation_text: A State may request to establish an alternative compliance deadline for up to three years beyond the currently-applicable date but not beyond December 21, 2026.
units.action_summary: State may request an alternative compliance deadline of up to three years beyond the current date, not extending past Dec 21, 2026.

units.obligation_text: It is the duty of the authorized NPDES program to re-apply for a new alternative compliance deadline.
units.action_summary: Authorized NPDES program must re-apply when seeking a new alternative compliance deadline.

units.obligation_text: The alternative compliance deadline request shall: Be submitted to EPA by the Director, as defined in 40 CFR 122.2;
units.action_summary: The Director must submit the alternative compliance deadline request to EPA.

units.obligation_text: The alternative compliance deadline request shall: Identify each general permit, program report, and related data elements covered by the request and the corresponding alternative compliance deadline(s);
units.action_summary: The request must identify each general permit, program report, and related data elements covered and their proposed alternative deadlines.

units.obligation_text: The alternative compliance deadline request shall: Identify each facility covered by the request and the corresponding alternative compliance deadline(s) (Note: This only applies if the request covers some but not all facilities subject to the general permit or program report requirement);
units.action_summary: If the request covers some but not all facilities, it must identify each covered facility and its alternative compliance deadline.

units.obligation_text: The alternative compliance deadline request shall: Be submitted at least 120 days prior to the applicable compliance deadline in Table 1 to 40 CFR 127.16 or an alternative compliance deadline previously approved by EPA;
units.action_summary: The request must be submitted at least 120 days before the applicable compliance deadline or previously approved alternative.

units.obligation_text: The alternative compliance deadline request shall: Provide a rationale for the delay and enough details (e.g., tasks, milestones, roles and responsibilities, necessary resources) to clearly describe how the program will successfully implement electronic reporting for general permit, program report, and related data elements covered by the request.
units.action_summary: The request must include a rationale and sufficient detail (tasks, milestones, responsibilities, resources) explaining how electronic reporting will be implemented.

units.obligation_text: EPA will review each alternative compliance deadline request to see if it provides enough detail to accurately assess if the state has a reasonable plan to deploy electronic reporting by the requested alternative compliance deadline.
units.action_summary: EPA will review requests to determine if they contain sufficient detail to assess the state's plan for implementing electronic reporting by the requested deadline.

units.obligation_text: EPA will return alternative compliance deadline requests with insufficient detail back to the Director within 30 days of receipt and provide recommendations.
units.action_summary: If a request lacks sufficient detail, EPA will return it to the Director within 30 days and provide recommendations.

units.obligation_text: EPA will approve or deny each complete alternative compliance deadline request within 120 days of receipt.
units.action_summary: EPA will approve or deny complete requests within 120 days of receipt.

units.obligation_text: EPA will provide notice to the authorized NPDES program of EPA’s approval or denial.
units.action_summary: EPA will notify the authorized NPDES program of approval or denial of requests.

units.obligation_text: The authorized NPDES program may re-apply if the initial request is denied by EPA.
units.action_summary: If EPA denies the request, the authorized NPDES program may submit another request.

units.obligation_text: EPA will update its website after it approves a request to clearly identify the approved alternative compliance deadlines for each facility, general permit report, program report, and related data elements by authorized NPDES program.
units.action_summary: After approval, EPA will update its website to identify approved alternative compliance deadlines by program/facility/report/data element.

units.obligation_text: EPA will also post each alternative compliance deadline request and the corresponding Agency approval or denial notice after each determination.
units.action_summary: EPA will post each request and the corresponding approval or denial notice on its website after making a determination.

units.obligation_text: EPA will provide updated information at: https://www.epa.gov/compliance/npdes-ereporting.
units.action_summary: EPA will provide updated information on its specified web page.

units.obligation_text: EPA may, as it deems appropriate, establish an alternative compliance deadline for electronic reporting and data sharing for one or more facilities, general permit reports, program reports, and related data elements (see Table 2 to appendix A) in one or more states.
units.action_summary: EPA has authority to establish alternative compliance deadlines for electronic reporting/data sharing for one or more entities in one or more states.

units.obligation_text: EPA may establish an alternative compliance deadline up to three years beyond the currently applicable date, but in no event beyond December 21, 2026.
units.action_summary: EPA may extend compliance deadlines by up to three years, but not beyond Dec 21, 2026.

units.obligation_text: Separately, EPA will provide notice to the one or more authorized NPDES program covered by each alternative compliance deadline.
units.action_summary: When EPA establishes an alternative deadline, it will notify the affected authorized NPDES program(s).

units.obligation_text: This notice will include a rationale for the delay and enough details (e.g., tasks, milestones, roles and responsibilities, necessary resources) to clearly describe how it will successfully implement electronic reporting for general permit, program report, and related data elements covered by the extension.
units.action_summary: EPA's notice of an alternative deadline will include a rationale and detailed implementation information.

units.obligation_text: EPA will update its website to clearly identify the alternative compliance deadlines for each facility, general permit report, program report, and related data elements by authorized NPDES program.
units.action_summary: EPA will post the alternative compliance deadlines on its website by program/facility/report/data element.

units.obligation_text: Within 5 days of the time the permittee becomes aware of the sewer overflow event (health or environment endangerment).
units.action_summary: Permittee must report sewer overflow events that endanger health or the environment within 5 days of awareness.

units.obligation_text: At least 10-days before the date of the anticipated bypass.
units.action_summary: Permittee must provide notice at least 10 days before an anticipated bypass.

units.obligation_text: Within 5-days of the time the permittee becomes aware of the unanticipated bypass.
units.action_summary: Permittee must report unanticipated bypasses within 5 days of becoming aware.

units.section: Appendix A to part 127, Table 2 (Basic Permit Information)
units.obligation_text: Permit Component: This field is only required when the permit includes one or more NPDES subprograms. This data element is also required for unpermitted facilities when the authorized NPDES programs is required to share facility, inspection, violation, or enforcement action data regarding these facilities with EPA’s national NPDES data system.
units.action_summary: Authorized NPDES programs must populate the Permit Component field when permits include subprograms and in certain circumstances for unpermitted facilities when sharing data with EPA.

units.section: Appendix A to part 127, Table 2 (Basic Permit Information)
units.obligation_text: Applicable Effluent Limitations Guidelines: This data element will identify the one or more applicable effluent limitations guidelines and new source performance standards for the facility ... This data element can be updated by the Control Authority for SIUs and CIUs through submission of the Pretreatment Program Reports [40 CFR 403.12(i)].
units.actor: authorized NPDES programs; Control Authority for SIUs and CIUs
units.action_summary: The data element identifying applicable ELGs/NSPS is required and can be updated by the Control Authority via Pretreatment Program Reports.

units.section: Appendix A to part 127, Table 2 (Basic Permit Information)
units.obligation_text: NAICS Code: The one or more six-digit NAICS codes/descriptions ... This field is required to be shared with the U.S. EPA when authorized NPDES programs approve NPDES permit coverage after June 12, 2021.
units.action_summary: When approving NPDES permit coverage after June 12, 2021, authorized programs must share the facility NAICS code(s) with EPA.

units.section: Appendix A to part 127, Table 2 (Basic Permit Information)
units.obligation_text: NAICS Code Primary Indicator: This data element will identify the primary economic activity, NAICS code, of the facility. This data element is required for electronic data transfer between state and EPA systems. This field is required to be shared with the U.S. EPA when authorized NPDES programs approve NPDES permit coverage after June 12, 2021.
units.action_summary: Authorized NPDES programs must share the NAICS primary indicator with EPA when approving permit coverage after June 12, 2021; required for electronic transfer.

units.section: Appendix A to part 127, Table 2 (Permitted Feature Information)
units.obligation_text: Waterbody Name for Permitted Feature: The name of the waterbody that is or will likely receive the discharge from each permitted feature. Authorized NPDES programs can also use this data element to identify the name of the source water for other intake structures that are permitted features.
units.action_summary: Authorized programs may use this data element to identify receiving waterbody or source water for intake structures.

title: Hazardous and Solid Waste Management System: Disposal of CCR; A Holistic Aproach to Closure Part B: Alternate Demonstration for Unlined Surface Impoundments; Implementation of Closure

units.obligation_text: An owner or operator of a CCR surface impoundment constructed without a composite liner or alternate composite liner as defined in § 257.70(b) or (c), may submit an Alternate Liner Demonstration to the Administrator or the Participating State Director to demonstrate that the design of the current liner system or the naturally occurring media present performs equivalent to a composite liner as defined in § 257.70(b).
units.action_summary: Owner/operator may submit an Alternate Liner Demonstration to EPA or Participating State Director to show liner equivalence.

units.obligation_text: To be granted, the owner or operator must demonstrate, with a reasonable degree of certainty, that based on the construction of the unit and surrounding site conditions, operation of the surface impoundment will not result in groundwater concentrations above the relevant groundwater protection standard at the unit boundary.
units.action_summary: Owner/operator must demonstrate, with reasonable certainty, that unit operation will not cause groundwater concentrations to exceed standards at the unit boundary.

units.obligation_text: Prior to the submission of the alternate liner demonstration, the facility must submit an alternate liner demonstration application documenting the unit’s eligibility to submit a demonstration.
units.action_summary: Facility must first submit an application documenting eligibility before submitting the alternate liner demonstration.

units.obligation_text: The application and demonstration must be submitted to the Administrator or the Participating State Director no later than the relevant deadline in paragraph (d)(2) of this section.
units.action_summary: Application and demonstration must be submitted to EPA or Participating State Director by the deadlines in paragraph (d)(2).

units.obligation_text: The Administrator or the Participating State Director will act on the submissions in accordance with the procedures in paragraph (d)(2) of this section.
units.actor: the Administrator or the Participating State Director
units.action_summary: Administrator or Participating State Director will act on submissions according to procedures in paragraph (d)(2).

units.obligation_text: To obtain approval under this paragraph, the owner or operator of the CCR surface impoundment must submit the following:
units.action_summary: Owner/operator must submit specified items to obtain approval under paragraph (d).

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator of the CCR surface impoundment must submit a letter to the Administrator or the Participating State Director, announcing their intention to submit a demonstration under this paragraph.
units.action_summary: Owner/operator must submit a letter to EPA or Participating State Director announcing intent to submit a demonstration.

units.obligation_text: The application must include the location of the facility and identify the specific CCR surface impoundment for which the demonstration will be made.
units.action_summary: Application must identify facility location and the specific impoundment for the demonstration.

units.obligation_text: The written demonstration must include information proving all of the following:
units.action_summary: The written demonstration must contain specified evidentiary information (see sub-items A–D).

units.obligation_text: The unit is in full compliance with this subpart except for § 257.71 (a)(1)(ii) and (iii),
units.action_summary: Demonstrate the unit is in full compliance with the subpart except specified provisions.

units.obligation_text: That the existing network of monitoring wells is sufficient to capture any releases, based on direction of flow, well location, screening depth and other relevant factors, including well construction logs and a sufficient number of diagrams to depict depth to groundwater, the potentiometric surface, and the anticipated direction(s) of groundwater flow across the site (multiple diagrams may be necessary if the direction of flow is affected by seasonal, tidal or other influences);
units.action_summary: Demonstrate monitoring well network is sufficient to capture releases and provide supporting logs and diagrams.

units.obligation_text: That there is no indication from groundwater monitoring data that the unit has or will adversely affect groundwater (i.e., no statistically significant increases (SSI) of Appendix IV to this part constituents above relevant GWPS), including documentation of the most recent statistical tests conducted and the rationale for the methods used in these comparisons,
units.action_summary: Demonstrate monitoring data show no adverse groundwater impacts and include statistical test documentation and rationale.

units.obligation_text: That the unit meets the location restrictions under §§ 257.60 through 257.64.
units.action_summary: Demonstrate the unit meets location restrictions in §§ 257.60–257.64.

units.obligation_text: The completed alternate liner demonstration package must be certified by a professional engineer.
units.action_summary: The completed demonstration package must have professional engineer certification.

units.obligation_text: The package must present evidence to demonstrate, with a reasonable degree of certainty, that based on the construction of the unit and surrounding site conditions, operation of the surface impoundment will not result in groundwater concentrations above the relevant groundwater protection standard at the unit boundary.
units.action_summary: Package must include evidence showing operation will not lead to groundwater concentrations above protection standards.

units.obligation_text: For each line of evidence, as well as any other data and assumptions incorporated into the determination, the facility must include documentation on how the data were collected and why these data and assumptions are believed to adequately reflect potential contaminant transport at and around that specific impoundment.
units.action_summary: Facility must document data collection methods and justify assumptions for each line of evidence.

units.obligation_text: The alternate liner demonstration at a minimum must contain all of the following lines of evidence:
units.action_summary: Demonstration must include specified minimum lines of evidence (see A and B).

units.obligation_text: Characterization of site hydrogeology. A characterization of the site-specific hydrogeology that surrounds the surface impoundment that defines the variability of the soil around the impoundment. The characterization must include all of the following:
units.action_summary: Provide a site-specific hydrogeologic characterization defining soil variability and including specified elements (1–5).

units.obligation_text: Measurements of the hydraulic conductivity in the uppermost aquifer measured from existing monitoring wells and discussion of the methods used to obtain these measurements.
units.action_summary: Include measurements of hydraulic conductivity from monitoring wells and explain the methods used.

units.obligation_text: Subsurface samples collected to characterize site hydrogeology must be located around the perimeter of the impoundment at a spatial resolution sufficient to ensure that any regions of substantially higher conductivity have been identified;
units.action_summary: Collect subsurface samples around the impoundment perimeter at sufficient resolution to identify higher-conductivity regions.

units.obligation_text: Conceptual site models with cross-sectional depictions of site stratigraphy that include the relative location of the impoundment (with depth of ponded water noted), monitoring wells (with screening depths noted), and all other subsurface samples used in the development of the models;
units.action_summary: Provide conceptual site models with cross-sections showing impoundment, ponded water depth, monitoring wells with screening depths, and subsurface samples.

units.obligation_text: A narrative description of site geological history;
units.action_summary: Provide a narrative description of the site's geological history.

units.obligation_text: All of the data used in the conceptual site model summarized into easily readable graphs or tables.
units.action_summary: Summarize all conceptual model data into readable graphs or tables.

units.obligation_text: Potential for infiltration. This report must evaluate the potential for infiltration through any liners and underlying soils that control release and transport of leachate by either in-situ sampling, or by conducting an analysis of the soil-based liner and underlying soil of the unit through laboratory testing.
units.action_summary: Report must evaluate infiltration potential through liners/soils via in-situ sampling or laboratory testing.

units.obligation_text: Deadlines for Submission. The owner or operator must submit the application under paragraph (d)(1)(A) of this section to EPA or the Participating State Director for approval no later than April 2, 2020.
units.action_summary: Owner/operator must submit the initial application to EPA or Participating State Director by April 2, 2020.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator must submit the demonstration required under paragraph (d)(1)(B) of this section to EPA for approval no later than one year after the deadline for the initial application.
units.action_summary: Owner/operator must submit the demonstration to EPA within one year after the initial application deadline.

units.obligation_text: If the owner or operator cannot meet this second deadline due to analytical limitations, the owner or operator must submit a request for an extension no later than 90 days prior to the deadline for submission of the demonstration that includes a summary of the data that have been analyzed for the samples responsible for the delay and an alternate timeline for completion that has been certified by the laboratory.
units.action_summary: If unable to meet the demonstration deadline due to analytical limits, owner/operator must submit an extension request at least 90 days before the deadline including required summary and certified alternate timeline.

units.obligation_text: Application Review. EPA or the Participating State Director will evaluate the application and may request additional information as necessary to complete its review.
units.actor: EPA or the Participating State Director
units.action_summary: EPA/Participating State Director will evaluate the application and may request additional information to complete review.

units.obligation_text: Submission of a complete application will toll the facility’s deadline to cease receipt of waste into that unit until issuance of a final decision on the unit’s eligibility.
units.action_summary: If facility submits a complete application, its deadline to stop receiving waste into the unit is tolled until final decision.

units.obligation_text: Incomplete submissions will not toll the facility’s deadline.
units.action_summary: Incomplete submissions do not toll the facility's deadline to cease waste receipt.

units.obligation_text: Within sixty days of receiving a complete application, EPA or the Participating State Director will notify the owner or operator of its determination on the eligibility of their surface impoundment.
units.actor: EPA or the Participating State Director
units.action_summary: Agency will notify owner/operator of eligibility determination within 60 days of receiving a complete application.

units.obligation_text: Demonstration Review. EPA or the Participating State Director will evaluate the demonstration package and may request additional information as necessary to complete its review.
units.actor: EPA or the Participating State Director
units.action_summary: Agency will evaluate demonstration package and may request additional information.

units.obligation_text: Submission of a complete demonstration package will toll the facility’s deadline to cease receipt of waste into that unit until issuance of a final decision under paragraph (d)(2)(v) of this section.
units.action_summary: A complete demonstration package submission tolls the facility's deadline to cease receipt of waste until final decision under paragraph (d)(2)(v).

units.obligation_text: Incomplete submissions will not toll the facility’s deadline.
units.action_summary: Incomplete demonstration submissions do not toll the deadline to cease receipt of waste.

units.obligation_text: EPA or the Participating State Director will publish a proposed decision on the alternate liner demonstration package on EPA’s or the Participating State Director’s website for a 30-day comment period.
units.actor: EPA or the Participating State Director
units.action_summary: Agency will publish a proposed decision on its website for a 30-day comment period.

units.obligation_text: After consideration of the comments, EPA or the Participating State Director will issue its decision on the alternate liner demonstration package within 4 months of receiving a complete alternate liner demonstration package.
units.actor: EPA or the Participating State Director
units.action_summary: Agency will issue its decision on the demonstration package within 4 months after receiving a complete package, after considering comments.

units.obligation_text: If no substantive comments are received, the proposed decision will become effective 5 days from the close of the comment period.
units.action_summary: If no substantive comments, proposed decision becomes effective 5 days after comment period closes.

units.obligation_text: If EPA or the Participating State Director determines that the unit is not eligible under paragraph (d)(1)(i) of this section, the owner or operator must cease receipt of waste and initiate closure within six months of the denial or by the deadline in § 257.101(a), whichever is later.
units.action_summary: If unit found ineligible, owner/operator must stop receiving waste and initiate closure within six months of denial or by § 257.101(a) deadline, whichever is later.

units.obligation_text: If EPA or the Participating State Director determines that the unit’s alternate liner does not meet the standard for approval in paragraph (d) of this section, the owner or operator must cease receipt of waste and initiate closure within six months of the denial.
units.action_summary: If alternate liner fails to meet approval standard, owner/operator must cease receipt of waste and initiate closure within six months of denial.

units.obligation_text: If a facility needs to obtain alternate capacity, they may do so in accordance with the procedures in § 257.103.
units.action_summary: Facility may obtain alternate capacity following procedures in § 257.103.

units.obligation_text: If at any time assessment monitoring pursuant to § 257.95 is triggered for the unit, the facility must conduct intra-well analyses on each well as part of subsequent groundwater monitoring reports to identify any trends of increasing concentrations.
units.action_summary: If assessment monitoring is triggered, facility must perform intra-well analyses on each well in subsequent monitoring reports to identify trends.

units.obligation_text: If there is evidence that the unit may exceed the groundwater protection standard for any constituent within the operational life of the unit, EPA or the Participating State Director will reevaluate the authorization, and may revoke it if source control measures cannot be put in place while the unit continues to operate.
units.actor: EPA or the Participating State Director
units.action_summary: If evidence suggests potential exceedance, agency will reevaluate authorization and may revoke it if source control cannot be implemented.

units.obligation_text: The onus remains on the facility at all times to demonstrate that the unit meets the conditions for authorization under this section.
units.action_summary: Facility bears the ongoing burden to demonstrate the unit meets authorization conditions.

units.obligation_text: If at any point, any condition for qualification under this section has not been met, EPA or the Participating State Director can without further notice or process deny or revoke the owner or operator’s authorization under paragraph (d)(2)(vii).
units.actor: EPA or the Participating State Director
units.action_summary: If qualification conditions are unmet, agency may deny or revoke authorization without further notice or process.

units.obligation_text: Closure by removal of CCR. An owner or operator closing a CCR unit by removal of CCR must follow the procedures specified in either paragraph (c)(1) or (c)(2) of this section.
units.action_summary: Owner/operator who closes a CCR unit by removal must follow the procedures in (c)(1) or (c)(2).

units.obligation_text: Complete all removal and decontamination activities during the active life of the CCR unit. Within the timeframes specified in paragraph (f) of this section the owner or operator must do all of the following:
units.action_summary: Owner/operator must complete all removal and decontamination during active life within timeframes in paragraph (f) and do specified tasks.

units.obligation_text: Complete removal and decontamination of all areas affected by releases from the CCR unit;
units.action_summary: Complete removal and decontamination of all areas affected by CCR releases.

units.obligation_text: Document that constituent concentrations throughout the CCR unit and any areas affected by releases from the CCR unit have been removed and groundwater monitoring concentrations do not exceed the groundwater protection standards established pursuant to § 257.95(h) for constituents listed in appendix IV to this part;
units.action_summary: Document that constituents have been removed and that groundwater monitoring concentrations do not exceed GWPS for Appendix IV constituents.

units.obligation_text: Obtain the completion of closure certification or approval required by paragraph (f)(3) of this section.
units.action_summary: Obtain closure certification or approval as required by paragraph (f)(3).

units.obligation_text: Complete removal and decontamination activities during the active life and post-closure care period of the CCR unit. The owner or operator may close the CCR unit by completing all removal and decontamination activities, except for groundwater corrective action, during the active life of the CCR unit and by completing groundwater corrective action during the post-closure care period pursuant to the following procedures:
units.action_summary: Owner/operator may elect to close by completing removal during active life and completing groundwater corrective action during post-closure per listed procedures.

units.obligation_text: Within the timeframes specified in paragraph (f) of this section, complete all removal and decontamination activities except for groundwater corrective action;
units.action_summary: Within paragraph (f) timeframes, complete all removal and decontamination except groundwater corrective action.

units.obligation_text: Within the timeframes specified in paragraph (f) of this section, begin implementation of the remedy selected under § 257.97 such that all components of the remedy are in place and operating as intended;
units.action_summary: Begin implementing the remedy selected under § 257.97 within paragraph (f) timeframes so all components are in place and operating.

units.obligation_text: Complete groundwater corrective action as a post-closure care requirement as specified in § 257.104(g);
units.action_summary: Complete groundwater corrective action as required in § 257.104(g) during post-closure care.

units.obligation_text: Amend the written closure plan required by paragraph (b) of this section and the written post-closure care plan required by § 257.104(d), if necessary;
units.action_summary: Amend closure and post-closure care plans as necessary.

units.obligation_text: Within the timeframes specified in paragraph (f) of this section, obtain the completion of closure certification or approval required by paragraph (f)(3) of this section;
units.action_summary: Obtain closure certification or approval within paragraph (f) timeframes as required by paragraph (f)(3).

units.obligation_text: Within the timeframes specified in paragraph (f) of this section, record the notation on the deed to the property required by paragraph (i) of this section.
units.action_summary: Record the deed notation required by paragraph (i) within the paragraph (f) timeframes.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator may select an alternative final cover system design, provided the alternative final cover system is designed and constructed to meet the criteria in paragraphs (d)(3)(ii)(A) through (C) of this section.
units.action_summary: Owner/operator may choose an alternative final cover design if it meets specified criteria in (d)(3)(ii)(A)–(C).

units.obligation_text: The design of the final cover system must be included in the written closure plan required by paragraph (b) of this section.
units.action_summary: Include final cover system design in the written closure plan.

units.obligation_text: Notwithstanding the prohibition on further placement in § 257.101, CCR may be used in a CCR unit provided the written closure plan is approved by the Administrator or a Participating State Director.
units.actor: the owner or operator (use of CCR)
units.action_summary: CCR may be placed during closure if the written closure plan is approved by EPA or Participating State Director despite § 257.101 prohibition.

units.obligation_text: The approved closure plan must demonstrate that the use of CCR during closure would pose no reasonable risk of adverse effects during the closure and post-closure care periods by showing that the placed CCR will remain contained (i.e., isolated) in the unit closed in accordance with the closure performance standards under § 257.102(d) so as to limit contact of the CCR in the unit with water and to prevent releases to the environment, including releases through surface transport by precipitation runoff, releases to soil and groundwater, wind-blown dust, and catastrophic unit failures. The following analyses and documentation must be included in the written closure plan:
units.action_summary: Approved closure plan must demonstrate no reasonable risk of adverse effects from CCR placement and include specified analyses and documentation (see A–F).

units.obligation_text: The volume of CCR that would be placed during closure would not exceed the volume of borrow material that otherwise would be used to achieve the subgrade elevations necessary to support the final cover system;
units.action_summary: Demonstrate CCR volume placed will not exceed volume of borrow material otherwise required.

units.obligation_text: The time needed to complete closure of the unit when using CCR would not exceed the time needed to close with soil or borrow material;
units.action_summary: Demonstrate time to close using CCR does not exceed time to close with soil/borrow material.

units.obligation_text: The CCR unit meets the requirements of § 257.64;
units.action_summary: Demonstrate the CCR unit satisfies § 257.64 requirements.

units.obligation_text: The CCR unit is and will remain in compliance with the closure performance standards and requirements specified in § 257.102, even after the further placement of CCR;
units.action_summary: Demonstrate the unit will remain in compliance with § 257.102 after additional CCR placement.

units.obligation_text: In addition to the requirements specified in § 257.102(d)(3), the design and construction of the final cover system must ensure the final cover system is no more permeable than the CCR placed in the unit as part of closure;
units.action_summary: Ensure final cover system design and construction are no more permeable than CCR placed during closure.

units.obligation_text: If the owner or operator of the unit has determined that any constituent listed in appendix IV to this part has been detected at a statistically significant level exceeding a groundwater detection standard defined under § 257.95(h), the additional placement of CCR will not adversely affect compliance with the corrective action remedy requirements under § 257.97(b).
units.action_summary: If Appendix IV constituent exceeds detection standard, demonstrate additional CCR placement will not adversely affect compliance with corrective action requirements under § 257.97(b).

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator must submit the closure plan for the unit that includes the demonstrations specified in paragraph (d)(4)(i) of this section to the Administrator or Participating State Director for review and approval in advance of the anticipated date of CCR use.
units.action_summary: Submit closure plan (including required demonstrations) to EPA or Participating State Director for review and approval before anticipated CCR use.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator must not make use of the exemption under this paragraph (d) until EPA or the Participating State Director has approved the closure plan.
units.action_summary: Owner/operator may not use the CCR-use exemption until EPA or Participating State Director approves the closure plan.

units.obligation_text: The approving authority should notify the owner or operator of approval or intent to disapprove the use of CCR in closure within 3 months after receipt of the initial closure plan or within 2 months after receipt of any supplemental information submitted.
units.actor: the approving authority (Administrator or Participating State Director)
units.action_summary: Approving authority should notify owner/operator of approval or intent to disapprove within 3 months of initial plan receipt or 2 months after supplemental info.

units.obligation_text: Except as provided by paragraph (g)(2) of this section, no later than two weeks from the date the owner or operator initiates closure of a CCR unit, the owner or operator must prepare a notification of intent to close a CCR unit.
units.action_summary: Within two weeks of initiating closure, owner/operator must prepare a notification of intent to close.

units.obligation_text: The notification must include the date that closure of the CCR unit was initiated;
units.action_summary: Notification must state the date closure was initiated.

units.obligation_text: The notification must also include the certification by a qualified professional engineer or the approval from the Participating State Director or the approval from EPA where EPA is the permitting authority for the design of the final cover system as required by § 257.102(d)(3)(iii), if applicable.
units.action_summary: Notification must include professional engineer certification or Participating State Director/EPA approval for final cover design, if applicable.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator has completed the notification when it has been placed in the facility’s operating record as required by § 257.105(i)(7).
units.action_summary: Notification is considered completed when placed in the facility's operating record per § 257.105(i)(7).

units.obligation_text: If the owner or operator previously completed a notification of intent to close a CCR unit prior to the effective date of a rule finalizing this proposal that does not contain the date that closure of the unit was initiated, and if the owner or operator has not yet completed closure of the CCR unit by completing the completion of closure notification in accordance with paragraph (h) of this section, then no later than two months following the effective date of a rule finalizing this proposal, the owner or operator must prepare and place in the facility’s operating record an updated notification of intent to close that includes the of date on which the owner or operator commenced closure of the unit.
units.action_summary: If prior notification omitted initiation date and closure not complete, owner/operator must prepare and place updated notification in operating record within two months after the rule's effective date including the initiation date.

units.obligation_text: An owner or operator that closes a CCR unit in accordance with paragraph (c)(1) of this section is not subject to the requirements of paragraphs (i)(1) through (3) of this section.
units.action_summary: If closure follows paragraph (c)(1), owner/operator is exempt from requirements of paragraphs (i)(1)–(3).

units.obligation_text: Owners and operators of any CCR landfill, CCR surface impoundment, or any lateral expansion of a CCR unit that is closed in accordance with paragraph (c) or (d) of this section must complete the notices and progress reports specified in paragraphs (l)(1) and (2) of this section.
units.action_summary: Owners/operators of CCR units closed per (c) or (d) must complete specified notices and annual progress reports.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator must prepare annual closure progress reports summarizing the progress of closure implementation.
units.action_summary: Owner/operator must prepare annual closure progress reports summarizing closure progress.

units.obligation_text: Discussion on which stage of closure the unit is currently undergoing;
units.action_summary: Report must discuss which stage of closure the unit is undergoing.

units.obligation_text: Discussion of the closure schedule;
units.action_summary: Report must include discussion of the closure schedule.

units.obligation_text: Discussion of any problems that were experienced.
units.action_summary: Report must include discussion of any problems experienced during closure.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator of a CCR unit must prepare the initial closure progress report no later than the first January 31 following the effective date of a rule finalizing this proposal or the first January 31 following the year that closure activities for the unit were commenced, whichever date is later.
units.action_summary: Prepare initial closure progress report by the first January 31 after the rule's effective date or after commencement of closure activities, whichever is later.

units.obligation_text: An annual closure progress report must be completed for the unit until closure of the unit is completed in accordance with paragraphs (f) and (h) of this section.
units.action_summary: Complete annual closure progress reports each year until closure is completed per paragraphs (f) and (h).

units.obligation_text: An owner or operator of a CCR unit that elects to close a CCR unit by removing CCR as provided by § 257.102(c)(1) is not subject to the post-closure care criteria under this section.
units.action_summary: If owner/operator elects closure by removal under §257.102(c)(1), they are exempt from post-closure care criteria under this section.

units.obligation_text: Except as provided by paragraph (c)(2) and (c)(3) of this section, the owner or operator of the CCR unit must conduct post-closure care for 30 years.
units.action_summary: Owner/operator must conduct post-closure care for 30 years unless paragraphs (c)(2) or (c)(3) provide otherwise.

units.obligation_text: An owner or operator closing a unit pursuant to § 257.102(c)(2) must conduct post-closure care pursuant to paragraph (g) of this section.
units.action_summary: If closing under §257.102(c)(2), owner/operator must conduct post-closure care consistent with paragraph (g).

units.obligation_text: For a CCR unit closing pursuant to § 257.102(c)(2), the owner or operator must complete groundwater corrective action by demonstrating that any areas affected by releases from the CCR unit do not exceed the groundwater protection standards established pursuant to § 257.95(h) for constituents listed in appendix IV to this part.
units.action_summary: Complete groundwater corrective action by demonstrating affected areas do not exceed GWPS for Appendix IV constituents.

units.obligation_text: Removal of a deed notation. The owner or operator of a CCR unit closed pursuant to §§ 257.102(c)(2) and 257.104 may remove the notation from the deed specified in § 257.102(i) upon:
units.action_summary: Owner/operator may remove the deed notation specified in §257.102(i) if specified conditions are met.

units.obligation_text: Completion of groundwater corrective action demonstrating that any areas affected by releases from the CCR unit do not exceed the groundwater protection standards established pursuant to § 257.95(h) for constituents listed in appendix IV to this part;
units.action_summary: One condition for removing the deed notation is completing groundwater corrective action demonstrating no exceedances of GWPS for Appendix IV constituents.

units.obligation_text: Completion of the notification of completion of post-closure care period required by paragraph (e) of this section.
