units.obligation_text: 9,999 units
units.action_summary: Alternative threshold: 9,999 units

units.obligation_text: Cold temperature CO emissions measured and calculated in accordance with subpart C shall not exceed: (A) For gasoline-fueled light-duty trucks with a loaded vehicle weight of 3,750 lbs. and less, 12.0 grams per vehicle mile. (B) For gasoline-fueled light-duty trucks with a loaded vehicle weight greater than 3,750 lbs., 15.0 grams per vehicle mile.
units.action_summary: Cold-temperature CO limits for light-duty trucks: ≤12.0 g/mi for loaded weight ≤3,750 lbs; ≤15.0 g/mi for loaded weight >3,750 lbs (measured per subpart C).

units.obligation_text: For gasoline-fueled light-duty trucks with a loaded vehicle weight of 3,750 lbs. and less, 12.0 grams per vehicle mile.
units.action_summary: Limit CO emissions to 12.0 g/vehicle-mile for trucks ≤3,750 lbs loaded weight.

units.obligation_text: For gasoline-fueled light-duty trucks with a loaded vehicle weight greater than 3,750 lbs., 15.0 grams per vehicle mile.
units.action_summary: Limit CO emissions to 15.0 g/vehicle-mile for trucks >3,750 lbs loaded weight.

units.obligation_text: The standards in paragraph (h)(1)(i) of this section apply at both low and high altitude.
units.action_summary: The truck CO standards apply at both low and high altitude.

units.obligation_text: A manufacturer may elect, by entire engine families, to exempt vehicles from the standard in paragraph (h)(1) of this section.
units.action_summary: Manufacturer may elect, by engine family, to exempt vehicles from the §86.093-9(h)(1) standards.

units.obligation_text: The total number of vehicles exempted from the standards in paragraph (h)(1) and in § 86.093-8 (j)(1) shall not exceed the greater of:
units.action_summary: Total exemptions from §86.093-9(h)(1) and §86.093-8(j)(1) are limited to the greater of specified thresholds.

units.obligation_text: 60% of the manufacturers combined production of light-duty vehicles and light-duty trucks with a gross vehicle weight rating of less than 6,001 lbs.
units.action_summary: One threshold: 60% of combined production (GVWR < 6,001 lbs.)

units.obligation_text: 9,999 units
units.action_summary: Alternative threshold: 9,999 units

units.obligation_text: For cold temperature CO exhaust emission compliance for each engine family, the Administrator will select for testing the vehicle expected to emit the highest emissions from the vehicles selected in accordance with § 86.093-24 (b)(1)(i), (ii), (iii), and (iv) of this section.
units.action_summary: Administrator will select, for each engine family, the vehicle expected to have highest cold-CO emissions for testing.

units.obligation_text: This vehicle shall be tested by the manufacturer in accordance with the test procedures in subpart C or with alternative procedures requested by the manufacturer and approved in advance by the Administrator.
units.action_summary: Manufacturer must test the selected vehicle using subpart C procedures or alternative procedures requested by manufacturer and pre-approved by Administrator.

units.obligation_text: If applicable, a statement that the vehicle is exempt from cold temperature carbon monoxide standards.
units.action_summary: When applicable, the vehicle's labeling must include a statement that the vehicle is exempt from cold-temperature CO standards.

units.obligation_text: If applicable, a statement that the vehicle is exempt from cold temperature carbon monoxide standards.
units.action_summary: When applicable, label must include a statement that the vehicle is exempt from cold-temperature CO standards (specified in another paragraph of the labeling section).

units.obligation_text: For gasoline-fueled light-duty vehicles, cold temperature carbon monoxide exhaust emissions shall not exceed 10.0 grams per vehicle mile as measured and calculated under the provisions set forth in subpart C; this standard applies at both low and high altitude.
units.action_summary: 1994-model gasoline light-duty vehicles must meet cold CO limit ≤10.0 g/vehicle-mile measured per subpart C, applicable at low and high altitude.

units.obligation_text: A manufacturer may elect, by entire engine families, to exempt vehicles from the standard in paragraph (j)(1) of this section.
units.action_summary: Manufacturer may elect by engine family to exempt vehicles from the §86.094-8(j)(1) standard.

units.obligation_text: The total number of vehicles exempted from the standards in paragraph (j)(1) and in § 86.094-9(h)(1) shall not exceed the greater of:
units.action_summary: Total exemptions from §86.094-8(j)(1) and §86.094-9(h)(1) are limited to the greater of specified thresholds.

units.obligation_text: 20% of the manufacturers combined production of light-duty vehicles and light-duty trucks with a gross vehicle weight rating of less than 6001 lbs.
units.action_summary: One threshold: 20% of combined production (GVWR < 6001 lbs.) for exemptions.

units.obligation_text: 9,999 units.
units.action_summary: Alternative threshold: 9,999 units for exemptions.

units.obligation_text: Vehicles with a gross vehicle weight rating greater than 6,000 lbs. are exempt from the standards in paragraph (j)(1) of this section.
units.action_summary: Vehicles with GVWR >6,000 lbs are exempt from the §86.094-8(j)(1) cold CO standards.

units.obligation_text: Cold temperature CO emissions measured and calculated in accordance with subpart C shall not exceed: (A) For gasoline-fueled light-duty trucks with a loaded vehicle weight of 3,750 lbs. and less, 12.0 grams per vehicle mile. (B) For gasoline-fueled light-duty trucks with a loaded vehicle weight greater than 3,750 lbs., 15.0 grams per vehicle mile.
units.action_summary: 1994-model truck CO limits per loaded weight: ≤12.0 g/mi for ≤3,750 lbs; ≤15.0 g/mi for >3,750 lbs, measured per subpart C.

units.obligation_text: The standards in paragraph (h)(1)(i) of this section apply at both low and high altitude.
units.action_summary: 1994 truck CO standards apply at both low and high altitude.

units.obligation_text: A manufacturer may elect, by entire engine families, to exempt vehicles from the standard in paragraph (h)(1) of this section.
units.action_summary: Manufacturer may elect by engine family to exempt vehicles from §86.094-9(h)(1).

units.obligation_text: Vehicles with a gross vehicle weight rating greater than 6,000 lbs are exempt from the standards in paragraph (h)(1) of this section.
units.action_summary: Vehicles with GVWR >6,000 lbs are exempt from §86.094-9(h)(1) truck CO standards.

units.obligation_text: For gasoline-fueled light-duty vehicles, cold temperature carbon monoxide exhaust emissions shall not exceed 10.0 grams per vehicle mile as measured and calculated under the provisions set forth in subpart C; this standard applies at both low and high altitude.
units.action_summary: For 1995+ models, gasoline light-duty vehicles must meet cold CO ≤10.0 g/vehicle-mile per subpart C at low and high altitude.

units.obligation_text: Cold temperature CO emissions measured and calculated in accordance with subpart C shall not exceed: (A) For gasoline-fueled light-duty trucks with a loaded vehicle weight of 3,750 lbs. and less, 12.0 grams per vehicle mile. (B) For gasoline-fueled light-duty trucks with a loaded vehicle weight greater than 3,750 lbs. 15.0 grams per vehicle mile.
units.action_summary: For 1995+ models, truck CO limits per loaded weight: ≤12.0 g/mi for ≤3,750 lbs; ≤15.0 g/mi for >3,750 lbs.

units.obligation_text: The provisions of this subpart are applicable to 1993 and later model year new gasoline-fueled light-duty vehicles and light-duty trucks at a nominal test temperature of 20 °F.
units.action_summary: Subpart C applies to 1993+ gasoline-fueled LDVs and LDTs for nominal 20°F tests.

units.obligation_text: Provisions of this subpart apply to 20 °F temperature tests performed by both the Administrator, and motor vehicle manufacturers for tests required under subpart A of 40 CFR part 86.
units.action_summary: Both the Administrator and manufacturers must follow subpart C provisions when performing 20°F tests required under subpart A.

units.obligation_text: The dynamometer shall have a power absorption unit for simulation of road load power and flywheels or other means of simulating the inertia weight as specified in § 86.229.
units.action_summary: Dynamometer must include a power absorption unit and means to simulate inertia weight per §86.229.

units.obligation_text: The dynamometer shall have a roll or shaft revolution counter or other means for determination of distance driven.
units.action_summary: Dynamometer must have a roll/shaft revolution counter or equivalent to determine distance driven.

units.obligation_text: The provisions of § 86.118 apply to this subpart.
units.action_summary: Requirements of §86.118 are applicable to this subpart (i.e., must be followed).

units.obligation_text: The provisions of § 86.119 apply to this subpart.
units.action_summary: Requirements of §86.119 apply to this subpart and must be followed.

units.obligation_text: Dynamometers with other roll specifications may be used if the total simulated road load horsepower can be shown to be equivalent, and if approved in advance by the Administrator.
units.action_summary: Alternative dynamometers allowed if equivalence can be demonstrated and Administrator approves in advance.

units.obligation_text: The provisions of §186.111 apply to this subpart except that measurement of NOx is optional.
units.action_summary: NOx measurement is optional for this subpart; otherwise §186.111 provisions apply.

units.obligation_text: The test fuel used shall be representative of regular-grade winter time commercial unleaded fuel without oxygenates. The Administrator will specify the range of acceptable fuel properties for each model year prior to certification.
units.action_summary: Test fuel must represent regular winter-grade unleaded fuel without oxygenates; Administrator will specify acceptable fuel property ranges by model year before certification.

units.obligation_text: The provisions of § 86.129 apply to this subpart, except that dynamometer settings shall not be increased to simulate the effects of air conditioning.
units.action_summary: Dynamometer settings must not be increased to simulate air conditioning effects.

units.obligation_text: Ambient temperature levels encountered by the test vehicle shall average 20 °F±5 °F and shall not be less than 10 °F nor more than 30 °F.
units.action_summary: Ambient temperatures during testing must average 20°F±5°F and stay between 10°F and 30°F.

units.obligation_text: In addition, the temperature may not exceed 25 °F or fall below 15 °F for more than three consecutive minutes.
units.action_summary: Ambient temperature must not exceed 25°F or fall below 15°F for more than 3 consecutive minutes during testing.

units.obligation_text: The ambient temperature reported shall be a simple average of the test cell temperatures measured at constant intervals no more than one minute apart.
units.action_summary: Reported ambient temperature must be the simple average of test cell temperatures measured at intervals ≤1 minute.

units.obligation_text: The test cell temperatures monitored during testing must be measured at the intake of the fixed speed cooling fan (§ 86.235(b)).
units.action_summary: Test cell temperatures must be measured at the intake of the fixed-speed cooling fan.

units.obligation_text: The vehicle shall be approximately level during all phases of the test sequence to prevent abnormal fuel distribution.
units.action_summary: Vehicle must be approximately level throughout testing.

units.obligation_text: The fuel tank(s) shall be filled to approximately the prescribed "tank fuel volume" with the specified test fuel § 86.213. If the existing fuel in the fuel tank(s) does not meet the specifications contained in § 86.213, the existing fuel must be drained prior to the fuel fill. The test fuel shall be at a temperature less than or equal to 60 °F. For the above operations the evaporative emission control system shall neither be abnormally purged nor abnormally loaded.
units.action_summary: Fill fuel tanks to prescribed volume with specified test fuel; drain nonconforming existing fuel; test fuel temp ≤60°F; do not abnormally purge or load evaporative emission control system during these operations.

units.obligation_text: The drive wheel tires shall be inflated up to a gauge pressure of 45 psi for a vehicle stabilized at ambient temperatures corresponding to the standard FTP temperatures of 68 °F to 86 °F. Alternatively, the drive wheel tires may be inflated to a gauge pressure of 40 psi if the vehicle has stabilized at ambient temperatures corresponding to the cold CO test temperature of 20 °F. The drive wheel tire pressures shall be reported with the test results.
units.action_summary: Inflate drive wheel tires to 45 psi for vehicles stabilized at 68–86°F, or to 40 psi if stabilized at ~20°F; report tire pressures with test results.

units.obligation_text: The fuel in the vehicle shall be stabilized at 20 °F±10 °F prior to the start of the driving cycle.
units.action_summary: Vehicle fuel must be stabilized at 20°F±10°F before starting driving cycle.

units.obligation_text: The Vehicle shall be placed, either by being driven or pushed, on a dynamometer and operated through one Urban Dynamometer Driving Schedule test procedure; see § 86.115 and appendix I. A test vehicle may not be used to set dynamometer horsepower.
units.action_summary: Vehicle must be placed on dynamometer and run through one UDDS test; the test vehicle cannot be used to set dynamometer horsepower.

units.obligation_text: Before the driving cycle may begin, the test cell temperature shall be 20 °F±3 °F, as measured at the intake of the fixed speed cooling fan.
units.action_summary: Test cell temperature must be 20°F±3°F measured at the cooling fan intake before starting driving cycle.

units.obligation_text: During operation of the vehicle through the driving cycle, ambient temperature levels encountered by the test vehicle shall average 20 °F±5 °F and shall not be less than 10 °F nor more than 30 °F. The ambient temperature reported shall be a simple average of the test cell temperatures measured at constant intervals no more than one minute apart. In addition, the temperature may not exceed 25 °F or fall below 15 °F for more than three consecutive minutes. The test cell temperatures monitored during testing must be measured at the intake of the fixed speed cooling fan (§ 86.235(b)).
units.action_summary: During driving cycle, ambient temps must average 20°F±5°F within 10–30°F, reported as simple average measured ≤1-minute intervals; cannot exceed 25°F or fall below 15°F for >3 consecutive minutes; measurements at cooling fan intake.

units.obligation_text: During operation of the vehicle through the driving schedule, the heater and defroster may be used at any temperature and fan settings.
units.action_summary: Heater and defroster may be used at any temperature and fan settings during the driving schedule.

units.obligation_text: For those unusual circumstances where additional preconditioning is desired by the manufacturer, such preconditioning may be allowed with the advance approval of the Administrator.
units.action_summary: Manufacturer may perform additional preconditioning if they obtain advance approval from the Administrator.

units.obligation_text: The Administrator may also choose to conduct additional preconditioning. The additional preconditioning shall consist of one or more driving cycles of the UDDS, as described in paragraph (a)(4) of this section.
units.action_summary: Administrator may conduct additional preconditioning, which must consist of one or more UDDS driving cycles.

units.obligation_text: Within five minutes of completion of preconditioning, the vehicle shall be shut off. During this five minute period, the vehicle shall not experience ambient temperatures less than 10 °F nor more than 30 °F.
units.action_summary: Vehicle must be shut off within 5 minutes after preconditioning; during that period ambient temps must stay between 10°F and 30°F.

units.obligation_text: If the vehicle is stabilized at 20 °F in a separate area and is moved through a warm area to the test cell, the vehicle must be restabilized in the test cell for at least six times the period the vehicle is exposed to warmer temperatures. The ambient temperature (dry bulb) during this period shall average 20 °F±5 °F and shall not be less than 10 °F nor more than 30 °F. In addition, the temperature may not exceed 25 °F or fall below 15 °F for more than three consecutive minutes. The maximum time for moving a vehicle through a warm area shall be 10 minutes.
units.action_summary: When moved through warm area, vehicle must be restabilized in test cell for ≥6× exposure time; test cell ambient must average 20°F±5°F within 10–30°F; cannot exceed 25°F or fall below 15°F for >3 minutes; moving through warm area cannot exceed 10 minutes.

units.obligation_text: The vehicle shall be stored for not less than 12 hours not for more than 36 hours prior to the cold start exhaust test. The ambient temperature (dry bulb) during this period shall be maintained at an average temperature of 20 °F±5 °F during each hour of this period and shall not be less than 10 °F nor more than 30 °F. In addition, the temperature may not exceed 25 °F or fall below 15 °F for more than three consecutive minutes.
units.action_summary: Vehicle must be soaked 12–36 hours before cold start test; soak ambient must average 20°F±5°F per hour and remain within 10–30°F; cannot exceed 25°F or drop below 15°F for >3 minutes.

units.obligation_text: The vehicle shall be stored for no more than 36 hours prior to the cold start exhaust test. The vehicle shall not be stored at ambient temperatures which exceed 86 °F during this period.
units.action_summary: Storage before cold start must be ≤36 hours and storage ambient temperature must not exceed 86°F.

units.obligation_text: Vehicle cooling may be accomplished by either force-cooling or force-warming the vehicle to the test temperature. If cooling is augmented by fans, the fans shall be placed in a vertical position for maximum drive train and engine cooling, not primarily oil pan cooling. Fans shall not be placed under the vehicle.
units.action_summary: Cooling may use force-cooling or force-warming; if fans used, they must be vertical (not under vehicle) to maximize drivetrain/engine cooling, not oil pan cooling.

units.obligation_text: The ambient temperature need only be stringently controlled after the vehicle has been cooled to 20 °F±3 °F as determined by a representative bulk oil temperature. If two or more diverse locations in the oil are monitored, they must all meet the temperature requirements.
units.action_summary: Strict ambient control required only after vehicle cooled to 20°F±3°F per bulk oil measurement; if monitoring multiple oil locations, all must meet the temp requirement.

units.obligation_text: The vehicle must be stored for at least one hour after it has been cooled to 20 °F±3 °F prior to the cold start exhaust test.
units.action_summary: After cooling to 20°F±3°F, vehicle must be stored at that temperature for ≥1 hour before cold start test.

units.obligation_text: During dynamometer operation, a fixed speed cooling fan shall be positioned so as to direct cooling air to the vehicle in an appropriate manner with the engine compartment cover open. In the case of vehicles with front engine compartments, the fan shall be squarely positioned within 12 inches (30.5 centimeters) of the vehicle. ... The fan capacity shall normally not exceed 5,300 cfm (2.50 cubic meters per second). If, however, the manufacturer showed (as provided in § 86.135(b)) that additional cooling is necessary, the fan capacity may be increased or additional fans used if approved in advance by the Administrator.
units.action_summary: Cooling fan must be positioned to direct air appropriately (front-engined vehicles: within 12 inches); fan capacity normally ≤5,300 cfm, but may be increased/extra fans used if manufacturer shows need and Administrator approves.
units.modal_raw: shall; shall; shall not exceed; may be increased

units.obligation_text: The vehicle speed as measured from the coupled dynamometer rolls shall be used.
units.action_summary: Vehicle speed must be measured from coupled dynamometer rolls and that measurement must be used.

units.obligation_text: As long as an emission sample is not taken, practice runs over the prescribed driving schedule may be performed at test point for the purpose of finding the minimum throttle action to maintain the proper speed-time relationship or to permit sampling system adjustment.
units.action_summary: Practice runs are permitted when not sampling, to set minimum throttle or adjust sampling system.

units.obligation_text: Humidity should be set low enough to prevent condensation on the dynamometer rolls.
units.action_summary: Recommended: set humidity low enough to avoid condensation on dynamometer rolls.

units.obligation_text: The dynamometer shall be warmed as recommended by the dynamometer manufacturer, and using procedures or control methods that assure stability of the residual frictional horsepower.
units.action_summary: Dynamometer must be warmed per manufacturer recommendations and by methods ensuring stable residual frictional horsepower.

units.obligation_text: The time between dynamometer warming and the start of the emissions test shall be no longer than 10 minutes if the dynamometer bearings are not independently heated. If the dynamometer bearings are independently heated, the emissions test shall begin no longer than 20 minutes after dynamometer warming.
units.action_summary: After dynamometer warming, start emissions test within 10 minutes (20 minutes if bearings independently heated).

units.obligation_text: If the dynamometer horsepower must be adjusted manually, it shall be set within one hour prior to the exhaust emissions test phase. The test vehicle shall not be used to make the adjustment. Dynamometers using automatic control of preselectable power settings may be set anytime prior to the beginning of the emissions test.
units.action_summary: Manual dynamometer horsepower adjustments must be done within 1 hour before test; test vehicle cannot be used to make adjustment; automatic-control dynamometers may be set any time prior.

units.obligation_text: Before the driving cycle may begin, the test cell temperature shall be 20 °F ± 3 °F, as measured at the intake of the fixed speed cooling fan.
units.action_summary: Test cell temperature must be 20°F±3°F at cooling fan intake before driving cycle begins.

units.obligation_text: During operation of the vehicle through the driving schedule, the heater and defroster may be used at any temperature and fan setting.
units.action_summary: Heater and defroster are permitted at any temperature/fan setting during the driving schedule.

units.obligation_text: The driving distance, as measured by counting the number of dynamometer roll or shaft revolutions, shall be determined for the transient cold start, stabilized cold start, and transient hot start phases of the test. The revolutions shall be measured on the same roll or shaft used for measuring the vehicle's speed.
units.action_summary: Driving distance must be determined by counting roll/shaft revolutions for test phases; revolutions measured on the same roll/shaft as speed measurement.
units.modal_raw: shall be determined; shall be measured

units.obligation_text: Four-wheel drive vehicles will be tested in a two-wheel drive mode of operation. Full time four-wheel drive vehicles will have one set of drive wheels temporarily disengaged by the vehicle manufacturer. Four-wheel drive vehicles which can be manually shifted to a two-wheel drive mode will be tested in the normal on-highway two-wheel drive mode of operation.
units.action_summary: 4WD vehicles are tested in two-wheel-drive mode: full-time 4WD have one drive set disengaged by manufacturer; manually-shiftable 4WD tested in normal on-highway 2WD mode.
units.modal_raw: will be tested; will have; will be tested

units.obligation_text: The prescribed test procedures are contained in subpart B and/or subpart C of this part 80. For purposes of Selective Enforcement Audit testing, the manufacturer shall not perform any of the test procedures in subpart B of this part relating to evaporative emission testing, except as specified in paragraph (a)(2) of this section.
units.action_summary: For Selective Enforcement Audit testing, manufacturers must not perform subpart B evaporative emission test procedures except as specified elsewhere.

units.obligation_text: The Administrator may, on the basis of a written application by a manufacturer, prescribe test procedures other than those in subpart B and/or subpart C of this part for any motor vehicle which he determines is not susceptible to satisfactory testing using the procedures in subpart B and/or subpart C of this part.
units.action_summary: Administrator may prescribe alternate test procedures for vehicles not susceptible to satisfactory testing using subpart B/C upon written application by manufacturer.

units.obligation_text: The manufacturer may measure the temperature of the test fuel at other than the approximate mid-volume of the fuel tank, as specified in paragraph (a) of § 86.231, and may drain the test fuel from other than the lowest point of the fuel tank as specified in paragraph (b) of § 86.231, provided an equivalent method is used. Equivalency documentation shall be maintained by the manufacturer and shall be made available to the Administrator upon request.
units.action_summary: Manufacturer may measure/test fuel temp or drain from different points if equivalent method used; manufacturer must maintain equivalency documentation and provide it upon Administrator request.

units.obligation_text: In performing exhaust sample analysis under § 86.240, the manufacturer shall exercise care to prevent moisture from condensing in the sample collection bags.
units.action_summary: Manufacturer must take care to prevent moisture condensation in sample collection bags during exhaust sample analysis.

units.obligation_text: The manufacturer need not comply with § 86.242 since the records required therein are provided under other provisions of subpart G of this part.
units.action_summary: Manufacturer is not required to comply with §86.242 for recordkeeping when records are provided under other subpart G provisions.

units.obligation_text: The manufacturer shall inspect the fuel system to ensure the absence of any leaks of liquid or vapor to the atmosphere by applying a pressure of 14.5+0.5 inches of water to the fuel system allowing the pressure to stabilize and isolating the fuel system from the pressure source. Following isolation of the fuel system, pressure must not drop more than 2.0 inches of water in five minutes. If required, the manufacturer shall perform corrective action in accordance with paragraph § 86.608(d) and report this action in accordance with paragraph § 86.609(d).
units.action_summary: Manufacturer must inspect fuel system for leaks using specified pressure test; pressure drop must be ≤2.0 inches in 5 minutes; if needed, perform corrective action per §86.608(d) and report per §86.609(d).
units.modal_raw: shall; must not; shall perform; shall report

units.obligation_text: When performing this pressure check, the manufacturer shall exercise care to neither purge nor load the evaporative emission control system.
units.action_summary: During the pressure check, manufacturer must avoid purging or loading the evaporative emission control system.

units.obligation_text: The manufacturer shall not modify the test vehicle's evaporative emission control system by component addition, deletion or substitution, except if approved in advance by the Administrator to comply with paragraph (a)(3)(i) of this section.
units.action_summary: Manufacturer must not modify the evaporative emission control system except with prior Administrator approval to meet specified exceptions.

units.obligation_text: For light-duty trucks, the prescribed test procedure is the Federal Test Procedure and described in subparts B, P, and/or C of this part. The manufacturer shall not perform the evaporative emission test procedure contained in subpart B.

units.obligation_text: The manufacturer may measure the temperature of the test fuel at other than the approximate mid-volume of the fuel tank as specified in paragraph (a) of § 86.231 and may drain the test fuel from other than the lowest point of the fuel tank as specified in paragraph (b) of § 86.231 provided an equivalent method is used. Equivalency documentation shall be maintained by the manufacturer and shall be made available to the Administrator upon request.
units.action_summary: Manufacturer may use alternate fuel temperature/drain points if using equivalent method, but must maintain equivalency documentation and provide on request.

units.obligation_text: In performing exhaust sample analysis under § 86.240, the manufacturer shall exercise care to prevent moisture from condensing in the sample collection bags.
units.action_summary: Manufacturer must prevent moisture condensation in sample bags during exhaust sample analysis.

units.obligation_text: The manufacturer need not comply with § 86.242 since the records required therein are provided under other provisions of subpart K of this part.
units.action_summary: Manufacturer is not required to comply with §86.242 for recordkeeping when provided under other subpart K provisions.

units.obligation_text: The manufacturer shall inspect the fuel system to ensure the absence of any leaks of liquid or vapor to the atmosphere by applying a pressure of 14.5+0.5 inches of water in the fuel system allowing the pressure to stabilize and isolating the fuel system from the pressure sources. Following isolation of the fuel system, pressure must not drop more than 2.0 inches of water in 5 minutes. If required, the manufacturer shall perform corrective action in accordance with paragraph § 86.608(d) and report this action in accordance with paragraph § 86.609(d).

units.obligation_text: The final deteriorated test results for each heavy-duty engine or light-duty truck tested according to subpart B, C, D, N, or P of this part are calculated by multiplying the final test results by the appropriate deterioration factor derived from the certification process for the engine family-control system combination and model year for the selected configuration to which the test engine or vehicle belongs. If the deterioration factor computed during the certification process is less than one that deterioration factor will be assumed to be one.

title: Acid Rain Program: Permits, Allowance System, Continuous Emissions Monitoring, and Excess Emissions [A-90-38-III-A-1]

units.obligation_text: Certain requirements set forth in this part and 40 CFR parts 73-78, as noted herein, shall be applicable to the permitting of affected sources during Phase II of the Acid Rain program under State and local operating permit programs approved pursuant to 40 CFR part 70, or under permitting by EPA pursuant to 40 CFR part 71 in the absence of an approved State permit program under 40 CFR part 70.

units.obligation_text: The terms used in this part shall have the meaning given in the Act as interpreted by this part and 40 CFR parts 73-78, and in this section, as follows:
units.actor: readers/users of this part (including permitting authorities, owners, operators, and designated representatives)
units.action_summary: Terms in this part are to be interpreted as defined by the Act, this part, and parts 73-78.

units.obligation_text: Section 502(a) of the Act, which provides in part that it shall be unlawful for any person to violate any requirement of a permit issued under this title, or to operate an affected source (as provided in title IV of the Act) except in compliance with a permit.

units.obligation_text: The term Acid Rain permit application shall include the proposed compliance plan for each affected unit, which plan shall be deemed incorporated into the Acid Rain permit application by reference by operation of law.

units.obligation_text: Emissions means the quantity of an air pollutant emitted from an affected unit, as measured, recorded, and reported to the Administrator or a State by the designated representative and determined by the Administrator, in accordance with the emissions monitoring requirements of 40 CFR part 75.
units.action_summary: Designated representatives are required to measure, record, and report emissions to the Administrator or State in accordance with part 75.

units.obligation_text: Compliance certification means a submission that is required by this part or 40 CFR parts 73-78, to report an affected source or an affected unit's compliance or non-compliance with a provision of the Acid Rain program to the Administrator or permitting authority, as appropriate, and that is signed and verified by the designated representative in accordance with subparts B and K of this part and 40 CFR parts 73-78.
units.action_summary: Designated representatives are required to sign and verify compliance certification submissions reporting compliance or noncompliance under the Acid Rain program, per subparts B and K and parts 73-78.

units.obligation_text: Allowance transfer deadline means midnight of January 30 or, if January 30 is not a business day, midnight of the first business day thereafter, which is the last day on which allowances may be submitted for recordation in an affected unit's compliance subaccount for the purposes of meeting sulfur dioxide emissions limitation requirements for the previous calendar year.
units.actor: holders of allowances (person(s) submitting allowances for recordation)

units.obligation_text: Whenever the term responsible official is used in 40 CFR part 70 or 71 or in a State operating permit program approved pursuant to title V of the Act and 40 CFR part 70, it shall be deemed to refer to the designated representative as defined herein so far as Acid Rain program actions, standards, requirements, or prohibitions are concerned.
units.actor: regulatory readers and implementers (including permitting authorities, State programs, and EPA)

title: Acid Rain Program: Announcement of Open Meeting on Acid Rain Program Forms; Proposed Rule; Forms Workshop

units.obligation_text: Meeting participants should focus their comments on form quality, including identification of inconsistencies between the forms and requirements in the proposed 'core' rules, redundancies, and ambiguities in terminology or instructions.

units.obligation_text: EPA urges members of the public to review the forms in advance of the meeting, and to submit completed forms (using real or hypothetical information), with their written comments, to the appropriate EPA Air Dockets.

units.obligation_text: Public comments regarding the substantive provisions of the Acid Rain 'core' rules are beyond the scope of the forms meeting and should be made separately at the public hearings or submitted to the appropriate EPA Air Dockets announced in the Federal Register notice of the 'core' rules package on December 3, 1991.
units.action_summary: Comments on substantive provisions must be submitted separately at the public hearings or to the appropriate EPA Air Dockets.

units.obligation_text: Anyone wishing to present Oral comments ... must register not later than January 3, 1991, by calling Gayle Kline at (703) 671-0400.
units.actor: anyone wishing to present oral comments (prospective presenters)

units.obligation_text: Only limited seating will be available for persons who have not pre-registered.
units.action_summary: Attendees who have not pre-registered will have only limited seating available.

units.obligation_text: Seats will be provided on a first-come, first-served basis.
units.action_summary: Available seats for non-preregistered attendees are allocated on a first-come, first-served basis.

units.obligation_text: Oral presentations will be limited to 10 minutes, and will be followed by a roundtable discussion.
units.action_summary: Oral presenters are limited to 10 minutes each; presentations will be followed by a roundtable discussion.

units.obligation_text: On the earlier of the following dates, a unit exempt under this section shall lose its exemption and become an affected unit under the Acid Rain Program and parts 70 and 71 of this chapter: (A) The date on which the designated representative submits an Acid Rain permit application under paragraph (d)(2) of this section; or (B) The date on which the designated representative is required under paragraph (d)(2) of this section to submit an Acid Rain permit application.
units.action_summary: The unit loses its exemption and becomes an affected unit on the earlier of when the designated representative submits, or is required to submit, the Acid Rain permit application described in paragraph (d)(2).

units.obligation_text: Notwithstanding § 72.30 (b) and (c), the designated representative for a unit that loses its exemption under this section shall submit a complete Acid Rain permit application on the later of January 1, 1998 or 60 days after the date on which the unit is no longer exempt.
units.action_summary: If the unit loses its exemption, the designated representative must submit a complete Acid Rain permit application by the later of Jan 1, 1998 or within 60 days after loss of exemption.

units.obligation_text: For the purpose of applying monitoring requirements under part 75 of this chapter, a unit that loses its exemption under this section shall be treated as a new unit that commenced commercial operation on the date on which the unit resumes operation.
units.action_summary: A unit that loses its exemption is treated as a new unit for part 75 monitoring requirements, with commercial operation commencement on the date it resumes operation.

units.obligation_text: The designated representative (authorized in accordance with subpart B of this part) of a unit under paragraph (a) of this section may submit to the permitting authority otherwise responsible for administering a Phase II Acid Rain permit for the unit a complete petition for an exemption for the unit from certain requirements of the Acid Rain Program. If the Administrator is not the permitting authority, a copy of the petition shall be submitted to the Administrator.
units.action_summary: The designated representative may submit a complete petition for an industrial-unit exemption to the permitting authority; if the Administrator is not the permitting authority, a copy of the petition must be submitted to the Administrator.

units.obligation_text: A complete petition shall include the following elements in a format prescribed by the Administrator:
units.action_summary: A complete petition must include the enumerated elements and be in a format prescribed by the Administrator.

units.obligation_text: Identification of the unit;
units.action_summary: The petition must identify the unit.

units.obligation_text: A statement that the unit is not a cogeneration unit;
units.action_summary: The petition must state that the unit is not a cogeneration unit.

units.obligation_text: A list of the current owners and operators of the unit and any other owners and operators of the unit, starting on the date of the signing of the interconnection agreement under paragraph (a)(2) of this section, and a statement that, starting on that date, there has been no owner or operator of the unit, subsidiary or affiliate or parent company of an owner or operator of the unit, or combination thereof whose principal business is the sale, transmission, or distribution of electricity or that is a public utility under the jurisdiction of a State or local utility regulatory authority;
units.action_summary: The petition must list current and historical owners/operators since the interconnection agreement date and state that none have a principal business of selling/transmitting/distributing electricity or are a regulated public utility.

units.obligation_text: A summary of the terms of the interconnection agreement and any related power purchase agreement under paragraph (a)(2) of this section, including the date on which the agreement was signed, the amount of electricity that may be required to be produced for sale by the generator served by the unit, and the provisions for expiration or termination of the agreement;
units.action_summary: The petition must include a summary of the interconnection and power purchase agreement terms, date signed, required electricity amounts, and expiration/termination provisions.

units.obligation_text: A copy of the interconnection agreement and any related power purchase agreement under paragraph (a)(2) of this section;
units.action_summary: The petition must include copies of the interconnection and related power purchase agreements.

units.obligation_text: The nameplate capacity of each generator served by the unit;
units.action_summary: The petition must state the nameplate capacity of each generator served by the unit.

units.obligation_text: For each year starting in 1985, the actual annual electrical output of each generator served by the unit, the total amount of electricity produced for sales to any customer by each generator, and the total amount of electricity produced and sold as required by the interconnection agreement and any related power purchase agreement under paragraph (a)(2) of this section;
units.action_summary: The petition must include annual data (since 1985) on each generator's output, sales to customers, and amounts sold as required by agreements.

units.obligation_text: A statement that the generator or generators served by the unit actually produced electricity for sale only for incidental electricity sales (in accordance with paragraph (a)(4) of this section) required under the interconnection agreement and any related power purchase agreement under paragraph (a)(2) of this section;
units.action_summary: The petition must state that the generator(s) produced electricity for sale only as incidental sales as required by the interconnection/purchase agreements.

units.obligation_text: The special provisions of paragraph (d) of this section.
units.action_summary: The petition must include the special provisions specified in paragraph (d).

units.obligation_text: For any unit meeting the requirements of paragraphs (a) and (b) of this section, the permitting authority shall issue an exemption from the requirements of the Acid Rain Program, except for the provisions of this section, §§ 72.2 through 72.6 and §§ 72.10 through 72.13.
units.action_summary: The permitting authority must issue an industrial-unit exemption for units meeting the criteria, except for specified provisions.

units.obligation_text: If a petition for exemption is submitted for a unit but the designated representative fails to demonstrate that the requirements of paragraph (a) are met, the permitting authority shall deny an exemption under this section.
units.action_summary: If the petitioner fails to show paragraph (a) requirements are met, the permitting authority must deny the exemption.

units.obligation_text: In issuing or denying an exemption under paragraph (c)(1) of this section, the permitting authority shall treat the petition for exemption as a permit application and apply the procedures used for issuing or denying draft, proposed (if the Administrator is not the permitting authority otherwise responsible for administering a Phase II Acid Rain permit for the unit), and final Acid Rain permits.
units.action_summary: When issuing or denying an exemption, the permitting authority must treat the petition like a permit application and use the applicable procedures for draft, proposed, and final permits.

units.obligation_text: An exemption issued under paragraph (c)(1)(i) of this section shall become effective on January 1 of the first full year the unit meets the requirements of paragraph (a) of this section.
units.action_summary: An issued exemption becomes effective on January 1 of the first full year the unit meets paragraph (a) requirements.

units.obligation_text: An exemption issued under paragraph (c)(1)(i) of this section shall be effective until the date on which the unit loses the exemption under paragraph (d)(4) of this section.
units.action_summary: The exemption remains effective until the unit loses it as specified in paragraph (d)(4).

units.obligation_text: The owners and operators and, to the extent applicable, the designated representative of a unit exempt under this section shall comply with the requirements of the Acid Rain Program concerning all periods for which the exemption is not in effect, even if such requirements arise, or must be complied with, after the exemption takes effect.
units.actor: owners and operators and, to the extent applicable, the designated representative
units.action_summary: Owners/operators and designated representative must comply with Acid Rain requirements for periods when the exemption is not in effect, including requirements arising after exemption starts.

units.obligation_text: For any period for which a unit is exempt under this section, the unit is not an affected unit under the Acid Rain Program and parts 70 and 71 of this chapter and is not eligible to be an opt-in source under part 74 of this chapter. As an unaffected unit, the unit shall continue to be subject to any other applicable requirements under parts 70 and 71 of this chapter.
units.action_summary: While exempt, the unit is not an affected unit or eligible opt-in source, but it remains subject to other applicable parts 70 and 71 requirements.
units.modal_raw: shall continue to be subject to

units.obligation_text: For a period of 5 years from the date the records are created, the owners and operators of a unit exempt under this section shall retain at the source that includes the unit records demonstrating that the requirements of paragraph (a) of this section are met. The 5-year period for keeping records may be extended for cause, at any time prior to the end of the period, in writing by the Administrator or the permitting authority. Such records shall include the following information: (i) A copy of the interconnection agreement and any related power purchase agreement under paragraph (a)(2) of this section; (ii) The nameplate capacity of each generator served by the unit; and (iii) For each year starting in 1985, the actual annual electrical output of each generator served by the unit, the total amount of electricity produced for sales to any customer by each generator, and the total amount of electricity produced and sold as required by the interconnection agreement and any related power purchase agreement under paragraph (a)(2) of this section.
units.actor: owners and operators; Administrator or permitting authority (extension)
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must retain specified records for five years at the source proving paragraph (a) compliance; the Administrator or permitting authority may extend that period for cause; the records must include the interconnection and purchase agreements, generator nameplate capacities, and historical annual output and sales data.
units.modal_raw: shall retain; may be extended; shall include

units.obligation_text: On the earliest of the following dates, a unit exempt under this section shall lose its exemption and become an affected unit under the Acid Rain Program and parts 70 and 71 of this chapter: (A) The first date on which there is an owner or operator of the unit, subsidiary or affiliate or parent company of an owner or operator of the unit, or combination thereof, whose principal business is the sale, transmission, or distribution of electricity or that is a public utility under the jurisdiction of a State or local utility regulatory authority.
units.action_summary: The unit loses its exemption if there becomes an owner/operator (or related entity) whose principal business is selling/transmitting/distributing electricity or is a regulated public utility.

units.obligation_text: (B) If any generator served by the unit actually produces any electricity for sale other than for sale to the person specified as the purchaser in the interconnection agreement or any related power purchase agreement under paragraph (a)(2) of this section, then the day after the date on which such electricity is sold.
units.action_summary: If a generator sells electricity to anyone other than the purchaser specified in the interconnection agreement, the unit loses its exemption the day after such sale.

units.obligation_text: (C) If any generator served by the unit actually produces any electricity for sale to the person specified as the purchaser ... where such sale is not required under that interconnection agreement ... or will result in total sales for a calendar year exceeding 10 percent of the nameplate capacity of that generator times 8,760 hours per year, then the day after the date on which such sale is made.
units.action_summary: If a generator sells to the purchaser when not required under the agreement or such sales cause annual sales to exceed 10% of nameplate capacity×8760, the unit loses its exemption the day after the sale.

units.obligation_text: (D) If any generator served by the unit actually produces any electricity for sale to the person specified as the purchaser ... where such sale results in total sales for a calendar year exceeding 10 percent of the actual electric output of the generator for that year, then January 1 of the year after such year.
units.action_summary: If sales to the specified purchaser exceed 10% of the generator's actual annual output, the unit loses its exemption effective Jan 1 of the following year.

units.obligation_text: (E) If the interconnection agreement or related power purchase agreement under paragraph (a)(2) of this section expires or is terminated and any generator served by the unit actually produces any electricity for sale, then the day after the date on which such electricity is sold.
units.action_summary: If the agreements expire/terminate and a generator sells electricity, the unit loses its exemption the day after such sale.

units.obligation_text: Notwithstanding § 72.30 (b) and (c), the designated representative for a unit that loses its exemption under this section shall submit a complete Acid Rain permit application on the later of January 1, 1998 or 60 days after the date on which the unit is no longer exempted.
units.action_summary: When the unit loses its exemption, the designated representative must submit a complete Acid Rain permit application by the later of Jan 1, 1998 or within 60 days after loss of exemption.

units.obligation_text: For the purpose of applying monitoring requirements under part 75 of this chapter, a unit that loses its exemption under this section shall be treated as a new unit that commenced commercial operation on the date on which the unit is no longer exempted.
units.action_summary: A unit losing its exemption will be treated as a new unit for part 75 monitoring, with commencement on the date it is no longer exempted.

title: Control of Air Pollution From New Motor Vehicles and New Motor Vehicle Engines; Regulations Requiring On-Board Diagnostic Systems on 1994 and Later Model Year Light-Duty Vehicles and Light-Duty Trucks

units.obligation_text: manufacturers to install on all new LDVs and LDTs diagnostic systems capable of:
units.actor: manufacturers of new LDVs and LDTs
units.action_summary: Install on-board diagnostic systems on all new light-duty vehicles and light-duty trucks

units.obligation_text: Accurately identifying for the vehicle's useful life emission-related system deterioration or malfunction, including, at a minimum, the catalytic converter and oxygen (O2) sensor, which could cause or result in failure of the vehicles to comply with emission standards;
units.action_summary: OBD systems must be able to detect emission-related deterioration or malfunctions (at least catalyst and O2 sensor) that could cause failures to meet emission standards

units.obligation_text: Alerting the vehicle's owner or operator to the likely need for emission-related components or systems maintenance or repair;
units.action_summary: OBD systems must alert owners/operators when maintenance or repair is likely needed for emission-related components

units.obligation_text: Storing and retrieving fault codes specified by the Administrator;
units.action_summary: OBD systems must store and allow retrieval of fault codes as specified by EPA

units.obligation_text: Providing access to stored information in a manner specified by the Administrator.
units.action_summary: OBD systems must provide access to stored diagnostic information in the manner EPA specifies

units.obligation_text: Today's proposed regulation would require all 1994 and subsequent model year LDVs and LDTs to incorporate on board diagnostic systems.
units.actor: manufacturers (of vehicles sold for 1994 and later model years)
units.action_summary: All 1994+ model year light-duty vehicles and trucks must incorporate OBD systems

units.obligation_text: The OBD system would monitor emission-related components for malfunctions or excessive deterioration that would cause the vehicle's emissions to exceed a specified emission threshold during its useful life.
units.action_summary: OBD systems must monitor emission-related components for malfunctions or deterioration that could cause emissions to exceed thresholds

units.obligation_text: When the system detects a malfunction, it would illuminate a malfunction indicator light on the dashboard and store codes identifying the malfunction in the on board computer.
units.action_summary: Upon detecting a malfunction, the OBD system must light the MIL and store diagnostic codes in the onboard computer

units.obligation_text: manufacturers would also be required to supply to any person, in a timely manner, repair information sufficient to facilitate accurate repair of emission-related components.
units.action_summary: Manufacturers must provide timely repair information to any person sufficient for accurate repair of emission-related components

units.obligation_text: As required by the Act, the OBD system must monitor catalyst and oxygen sensor performance.
units.action_summary: OBD systems must monitor catalyst and O2 sensor performance

units.obligation_text: the proposed rule requires each vehicle's OBD system to detect significant engine misfire.
units.action_summary: OBD systems must detect significant engine misfire

units.obligation_text: for vehicles equipped with sequential fuel injection, EPA proposes that fuel to the misfiring cylinder be shut off during the period misfiring occurs.
units.actor: manufacturers (of vehicles with sequential fuel injection) / OBD systems
units.action_summary: For sequential fuel-injected vehicles, fuel to a misfiring cylinder should be shut off while misfiring occurs

units.obligation_text: the proposed rule would require the OBD system to monitor for electrical disconnect any emission-related component or system which directly or indirectly sends information to or receives information from the vehicle's computer.
units.action_summary: OBD systems must monitor for electrical disconnect of any emission-related component or system that interfaces with the vehicle computer

units.obligation_text: OBD systems conform to both uniform industry standards adopted through SAE and ISO standards and be accessible with the use of a standard hand-held diagnostic tool.
units.action_summary: OBD systems must conform to SAE and ISO standards and be accessible via a standard handheld diagnostic tool

units.obligation_text: the proposed rule requires the following information be provided over the standard link, if the information is available to the on-board computer: calculated load value, diagnostic trouble codes, engine coolant temperature, fuel control system status, fuel trim, fuel pressure, ignition timing advance, intake air temperature, manifold air pressure, air flow rate from the mass air flow meter, engine RPM, throttle position sensor output value, secondary air status, and vehicle speed.
units.action_summary: If available, specified diagnostic and engine operating data must be provided over the standardized data link

units.obligation_text: The capability to perform bi-directional diagnostic control specifications shall be available on demand through the serial port on the standardized data link connector.
units.action_summary: OBD systems must provide bi-directional diagnostic control capability via the standard data link serial port on demand

units.obligation_text: this proposed rule requires at least one frame of information providing engine operating conditions at the time of malfunction.
units.action_summary: OBD systems must record at least one 'freeze-frame' of engine operating conditions when a malfunction occurs

units.obligation_text: EPA is proposing that manufacturers be required to protect the on-board computer from tampering.
units.action_summary: Manufacturers must protect/on-board computers against tampering

units.obligation_text: Write-protect features are required for flash memory systems.
units.action_summary: Flash-memory-based OBD systems must include write-protect features

units.obligation_text: Today's proposal also requires manufacturers to use a single dashboard MIL to indicate all emission-related problems the manufacturer may choose to monitor.
units.action_summary: Manufacturers must use a single malfunction indicator light (MIL) for all emission-related problems they monitor

units.obligation_text: Manufacturers would continue to be allowed to install warning lights intended to alert the driver to safety problems or problems related to engine operation which could result in immediate damage such as low oil pressure or over temperature conditions.
units.action_summary: Manufacturers may still install separate warning lights for safety/engine-damage conditions

units.obligation_text: To discourage tampering, the MIL would also be required to illuminate when the vehicle's ignition is in the 'key-on' position each time the vehicle is started.
units.action_summary: MIL must light during key-on each time vehicle is started to facilitate inspection

units.obligation_text: The MIL would go off after the engine is started unless a malfunction has been detected.
units.action_summary: MIL should extinguish after engine start unless a malfunction is present

units.obligation_text: A readiness code would be required when the diagnostic system has completed all checks and determined that all monitored systems are functioning properly.
units.action_summary: OBD systems must provide a readiness code indicating that all monitored systems have passed their checks

units.obligation_text: Aftermarket parts must be fully compatible with the OBD system.
units.action_summary: Aftermarket parts must not interfere with OBD system operation and must be compatible

units.obligation_text: Installation of aftermarket parts which prevent the OBD system from performing its proper function would be considered tampering.
units.action_summary: Installing aftermarket parts that disable OBD functionality will be treated as tampering

units.obligation_text: EPA proposes requiring all components monitored by the OBD system to be fully evaluated at least once every trip.
units.action_summary: All components monitored by OBD must be evaluated at least once per trip
units.modal_raw: proposes requiring ... to be fully evaluated

units.obligation_text: One CVS-72 driving cycle would qualify as a trip.
units.action_summary: Defines that one CVS-72 driving cycle counts as a trip for the evaluation frequency requirement

units.obligation_text: Manufacturers may determine a need to monitor emission-related components more frequently.
units.action_summary: Manufacturers are permitted to implement more frequent monitoring if needed

units.obligation_text: As soon as the OBD system is able to reliably detect deterioration or a malfunction that could cause an emission increase above the threshold level, the MIL should illuminate to signal, at the earliest opportunity, the need for repair.
units.action_summary: MIL should light promptly when OBD detects a qualifying deterioration or malfunction

units.obligation_text: EPA is proposing to require that the MIL remain illuminated during all periods of engine operation until the trouble codes stored in the on board computer are cleared by a service technician or after repeated re-evaluation fails to detect a reoccurrence of the problem.
units.action_summary: MIL must stay lit during all engine operation until codes are cleared by a technician or until repeat evaluations show the problem no longer occurs

units.obligation_text: Manufacturers may extinguish the MIL if no reoccurrence of the problem is detected, subject to repeat driving operation criteria.
units.action_summary: Manufacturers are permitted to design systems that extinguish the MIL when the fault does not reoccur, provided repeat-driving verification criteria are met

units.obligation_text: EPA proposes that manufacturers not be allowed to adopt OBD systems which extinguish the MIL in less than three subsequent sequential driving cycles which repeat the driving conditions under which the malfunction originally was detected.
units.action_summary: Manufacturers shall not design OBD systems that extinguish the MIL in fewer than three sequential driving cycles repeating the original malfunction conditions

units.obligation_text: Specifically, before extinguishing the MIL, the vehicle must be operated over two subsequent driving schedules which are simultaneously within ten (10) percent of the speed and load conditions which existed when the malfunction was first determined.
units.actor: vehicle operator / manufacturers (to require this verification)
units.action_summary: To qualify for extinguishing the MIL (for misfire/fuel system), the vehicle must be driven over two subsequent drives within ±10% of the original speed and load conditions

units.obligation_text: A manufacturer is required to recall and fix a class of vehicles if a substantial number of those vehicles are found to violate the requirements of section 202 of the Act.
units.action_summary: Manufacturers must recall and repair vehicle classes if many are found violating section 202 requirements
units.modal_raw: is required to recall and fix

units.obligation_text: this section of the amended Clean Air Act requires manufacturers to make available to interested persons all necessary emission-related maintenance and repair information, including information needed to make use of the OBD system.
units.action_summary: Manufacturers must make emission-related maintenance and repair information (including OBD use) available to interested persons

title: Control of Air Pollution From New Motor Vehicles and New Motor Vehicle Engines; Regulations Requiring On-Board Diagnostic Systems on 1994 and Later Model Year Light-Duty Vehicles and Light-Duty Trucks; Extension of Comment Period

units.obligation_text: This notice announces an extension of the public comment period for EPA's proposed regulation for On-Board Diagnostics (OBD) as published in the Federal Register on September 24, 1991 (56 FR 48272).
units.action_summary: EPA extends the public comment period for its proposed OBD regulation.

units.obligation_text: This extension will apply only for comments relevant to proposed § 86.094-38 paragraph (g) on "Maintenance instructions."
units.action_summary: The extension is limited to comments relevant to proposed §86.094-38(g) (Maintenance instructions).

units.obligation_text: The comment period for comments pursuant to proposed § 86.094-38(g) will remain open until January 10,1992.
units.action_summary: Comments on proposed §86.094-38(g) may be submitted until January 10, 1992.

units.obligation_text: The closing of the formal comment period for comments associated with any other aspects of the proposal will remain December 9,1991.
units.action_summary: The comment period for all other aspects of the proposal closes on December 9, 1991.

units.obligation_text: Any comments received after that date, except those concerning § 86.094-38(g), will be considered to the extent possible.
units.action_summary: EPA may consider late comments received after December 9, 1991, but will only do so to the extent possible and excluding late comments concerning §86.094-38(g).

title: Control of Air Pollution From New Motor Vehicles and New Motor Vehicle Engines; Regulations Requiring On-Board Diagnostic Systems on 1994 and Later Model Year Light-Duty Vehicles and Light-Duty Trucks; Reopening of Comment Period

units.obligation_text: Standard No. 209, Seat belt assemblies, specifies that emergency locking retractors [ELR] shall be tested by running the retractor through 50,000 cycles, with at least 10,000 lockups during those cycles.
units.actor: manufacturers/testers of emergency locking retractors subject to Standard No. 209
units.action_summary: ELR devices must undergo a 50,000-cycle test that includes at least 10,000 lockups.

units.obligation_text: Standard No. 209 also specifies that automatic locking retractors (ALR) shall be tested by running the retractor through 10,000 cycles.
units.actor: manufacturers/testers of automatic locking retractors subject to Standard No. 209
units.action_summary: ALR devices must undergo a 10,000-cycle test.

title: Control of Air Pollution From New Motor Vehicles and New Motor Vehicle Engines; Regulations Requiring On-Board Diagnostic Systems on 1994 and Later Model Year Light-Duty Vehicles and Light-Duty Trucks; Notice of Public Workshop and Reopening of Comment Period

units.obligation_text: The docket in this proceeding shall be reopened for thirty days following the workshop for comments pertaining to issues discussed at the workshop.
units.action_summary: EPA will reopen the docket for 30 days after the workshop to accept comments on issues discussed at the workshop.

units.obligation_text: Persons interested in making presentations at the workshop are requested to notify the Agency contact person listed below at least five days prior to the workshop so that a final agenda can be prepared.
units.action_summary: Those who wish to present at the workshop should notify the Agency contact at least five days before the workshop.

units.obligation_text: Interested parties may submit written comments pertaining to the issues addressed at the public workshop on or before July 31.
units.action_summary: Interested parties are permitted to submit written comments on workshop issues by July 31.

units.obligation_text: Written comments must be sent in duplicate to: EPA Air Docket LE-131, Attention: Docket No. __, U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, room M-1500, 401 M Street SW., Washington, DC 20460, (202) 382-7548.
units.action_summary: Submit written comments in duplicate to the specified EPA Air Docket address and attention line.

units.obligation_text: This docket is located at the above address on the first floor of Waterside Mall and is open for public inspection weekdays from 8:30 to 12 noon and from 1:30 p.m. to 3:30 p.m.
units.action_summary: The docket is available for public inspection on weekdays during specified hours.

units.obligation_text: As provided in 40 CFR part 2, a reasonable fee may be charged by EPA for copying services.
units.action_summary: EPA is permitted to charge a reasonable fee for copying services under 40 CFR part 2.

units.obligation_text: A court reporter will be present at the workshop to make a written transcript of the proceedings and a copy will be placed in the docket following the workshop.
units.action_summary: A court reporter will create a written transcript of the workshop proceedings and a copy will be placed in the docket afterward.

title: Control of Air Pollution From New Motor Vehicles and New Motor Vehicle Engines; Regulations Requiring On-Board Diagnostic Systems on 1994 and Later Model Year Light-Duty Vehicles and Light-Duty Trucks; Notice of Public Workshop and Reopening of Comment Period

units.obligation_text: The docket in this proceeding shall be reopened for thirty days following the workshop for the filing of written comments pertaining to issues discussed at the workshop.
units.action_summary: EPA will reopen the docket for 30 days after the workshop to accept written comments on workshop issues.

units.obligation_text: Persons interested in making presentations at the workshop should notify the Agency contact person listed below at least five days prior to the workshop so that a final agenda can be prepared.
units.action_summary: Presenters must notify the agency contact at least five days before the workshop.

units.obligation_text: Persons who want to make presentations are asked to come prepared to address each issue separately and bring with them 50 copies of their presentations.
units.actor: persons who want to make presentations
units.action_summary: Presenters should be prepared to address each issue separately and bring 50 copies of their presentation.

units.obligation_text: Individual presentations on any one issue will be limited to ten minutes.
units.action_summary: Each individual presentation is limited to ten minutes.

units.obligation_text: Interested parties may submit written comments pertaining to the issues addressed at the public workshop on or before August 13, 1993.
units.action_summary: Commenters may submit written comments on workshop issues by August 13, 1993.

units.obligation_text: Written comments must be sent in duplicate to: EPA Air Docket LE-131. Attention: Docket No. A-90-35. Environmental Protection Agency, room M-1500, 401 M Street SW., Washington, DC 20460.
units.action_summary: Commenters are required to send two copies of written comments to the specified EPA air docket address.

units.obligation_text: As provided in 40 CFR part 2, a reasonable fee may be charged by EPA for copying services.
units.action_summary: EPA is permitted to charge a reasonable copying fee under 40 CFR part 2.

units.obligation_text: Vehicle manufacturers would be required to provide initial service, repair, diagnostic and parts information to the NTIS within thirty days of providing it to their franchised dealerships or other persons engaged in the repair, diagnosing, or servicing of motor vehicles or motor vehicle engines.
units.action_summary: Manufacturers must submit initial service/repair/diagnostic/parts information to NTIS within 30 days after providing it to dealerships or similar parties.

units.obligation_text: Service, repair, diagnostic and parts information issued to dealerships during any subsequent thirty day period would be sent to the NTIS at the end of each such thirty day period.
units.action_summary: Manufacturers must batch and send any service/repair/diagnostic/parts information issued during each 30-day period to NTIS at the period's end.

units.obligation_text: Each vehicle manufacturer would be required to provide one copy of all information required under the regulations to the NTIS.
units.action_summary: Manufacturers must provide one copy of all required information to NTIS.

units.obligation_text: Each manufacturer would be required to provide the information to the NTIS free of charge pursuant to a copyright release or other agreement.
units.action_summary: Manufacturers must supply the information to NTIS at no charge, via a copyright release or agreement.

units.obligation_text: Vehicle manufacturers could receive royalties for subsequent distribution of the information by the NTIS based on prearranged agreements.
units.action_summary: Manufacturers are permitted to receive royalties from NTIS distributions under prearranged agreements.

units.obligation_text: Although EPA would require submission of information to the NTIS, vehicle manufacturers would not be precluded from providing service information through any other distribution mechanism.
units.action_summary: Manufacturers must submit to NTIS but are allowed to distribute service information by other means as well.

units.obligation_text: In accordance with section 202(m)(5), vehicle manufacturers are required to provide the same information to the aftermarket as they provide to their dealerships.
units.action_summary: Manufacturers must give aftermarket access to the same information provided to dealerships.

units.obligation_text: EPA proposes that if vehicle manufacturers 'deeply tag' the electronic service information provided to their dealerships ... they will be required to provide the same 'deeply tagged' information to the aftermarket.
units.action_summary: If manufacturers provide more granular ('deeply tagged') electronic service data to dealers, they must provide that same detailed data to the aftermarket.

units.obligation_text: Beginning in model year 1996 vehicle manufacturers would be required to use the service information format being developed by SAE (J2008) (subject to adoption/alternatives described).
units.action_summary: Manufacturers would have to use SAE J2008 electronic service information format starting in model year 1996 unless EPA adopts another format.

units.obligation_text: EPA may propose to adopt its own format that vehicle manufacturers would be required to follow if J2008 is not adopted by mid-1994 or does not meet EPA's needs.
units.action_summary: If SAE J2008 is not suitable or timely, EPA may require manufacturers to follow an EPA-developed electronic format.

units.obligation_text: EPA proposes to require that vehicle manufacturers offer their enhanced diagnostic equipment for sale to the aftermarket.
units.action_summary: EPA proposes that manufacturers must offer their enhanced diagnostic equipment for sale to aftermarket technicians.

units.obligation_text: EPA proposes that manufacturers' enhanced diagnostic equipment must be made available to the aftermarket at the same price at which it is sold to authorized dealerships.
units.action_summary: Manufacturers would have to sell enhanced diagnostic equipment to the aftermarket at the same price as to dealerships.

units.obligation_text: EPA proposes to give vehicle manufacturers a one-year lead time to prepare for aftermarket sales of enhanced equipment.
units.action_summary: EPA would provide manufacturers one year to prepare before requiring aftermarket sales of enhanced equipment.

units.obligation_text: EPA also proposes that vehicle manufacturers should have the option of providing service, repair and diagnostic information through an EDI or similar system.
units.action_summary: Manufacturers may choose to provide service/repair/diagnostic information via EDI or similar systems.

units.obligation_text: If EPA determines that a substantial number of I/M failures are occurring due to systems, components, or parts other than those described here, the extent of emission-related service information will be expanded in a subsequent rulemaking to include such items.
units.action_summary: EPA will expand the required emission-related service information via future rulemaking if I/M program failures show other items cause emissions failures.

units.obligation_text: All meetings are open to the public without advance registration.
units.action_summary: The public may attend all committee meetings without advance registration.

title: Control of Air Pollution From New Motor Vehicles and New Motor Vehicle Engines: Regulations Requiring On-Board Diagnostic (OBD) Systems -- Acceptance of Revised California OBD II Requirements; Notice of Proposed Rulemaking [A-90-35-VI-A-01]

units.obligation_text: Demonstration of compliance with California OBD II requirements (Title 13 California Code section 1968.1), as modified pursuant to California Mail Out #95-03 (January 19,1995), shall satisfy the requirements of this section through the 1998 model year
units.actor: Demonstration of compliance with California OBD II requirements (or entities demonstrating such compliance)
units.action_summary: Showing compliance with the specified California OBD II requirements will satisfy the federal §86.094-17 requirements through the 1998 model year.

units.obligation_text: compliance with Title 13 California Code section 1968.1(d), pertaining to tampering protection, is not required to satisfy the requirements of this section
units.actor: persons complying with California OBD II requirements (or entities demonstrating such compliance)
units.action_summary: Compliance with the California tampering-protection provision (Title 13 §1968.1(d)) is not required to meet the federal §86.094-17 requirements.

units.obligation_text: The base flood elevations and modified base flood elevations are the basis for the floodplain management measures that the community is required either to adopt or to show evidence of being already in effect in order to qualify or remain qualified for participation in the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP)
units.action_summary: Communities must either adopt the specified floodplain management measures or demonstrate they already have equivalent measures to qualify or remain qualified for the NFIP.

units.obligation_text: adopt the base flood elevations and modified base flood elevations as the basis for floodplain management measures
units.action_summary: One alternative requirement: the community must adopt the specified floodplain management measures based on the proposed elevations.

units.obligation_text: show evidence of being already in effect [the floodplain management measures] in order to qualify or remain qualified for participation in the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP)
units.action_summary: Alternative: the community must demonstrate that required floodplain management measures are already in effect to qualify or remain in the NFIP.

units.obligation_text: The community may at any time enact stricter requirements of its own, or pursuant to policies established by other Federal, State, or regional entities
units.action_summary: Communities are permitted to adopt floodplain management requirements that are stricter than the proposed minimums.

title: Vehicle Inspection and Maintenance Requirements for State Implementation Plans
Vehicle Inspection and Maintenance Requirements for State Implementation Plans; Notice of Availability of Regulatory Text, Location of Public Hearing Site and Correction of Proposed Rulemaking

units.obligation_text: Inspection/maintenance (I/M) programs are required in both ozone and carbon monoxide (CO) nonattainment areas, depending upon population and nonattainment classification or design value.
units.action_summary: Areas designated nonattainment for ozone or CO must have I/M programs depending on population and classification.

units.obligation_text: States or areas within an ozone transport region shall implement enhanced I/M programs in any metropolitan statistical area (MSA), or portion of an MSA, within the state or area with a 1990 population of 100,000 or more as defined by the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) regardless of the area's attainment classification.
units.actor: States or areas within an ozone transport region
