units.action_summary: Implement enhanced I/M programs in MSAs (or portions) in ozone transport regions with 1990 population ≥ 100,000.

units.obligation_text: Apart from those areas described in paragraph (a)(1) of this section, any area designated as serious or worse ozone nonattainment, or as moderate or serious CO nonattainment with a design value greater than 12.7 ppm, and having a 1980 Census-defined urbanized area population of 200,000 or more, shall implement enhanced I/M in the 1990 Census-defined urbanized area.
units.actor: areas designated as serious or worse ozone nonattainment, or moderate/serious CO nonattainment with design value >12.7 ppm and 1980 urbanized population ≥200,000
units.action_summary: Implement enhanced I/M in the 1990 urbanized area for such designated areas meeting the population/design-value criteria.

units.obligation_text: Any area designated as marginal ozone nonattainment or moderate CO nonattainment with a design value of 12.7 ppm or less shall continue operating I/M programs that were part of an approved State Implementation Plan (SIP) as of November 15, 1990 and shall update those programs as necessary to meet the basic I/M program requirements of this regulation.
units.actor: areas designated as marginal ozone nonattainment or moderate CO nonattainment (design value ≤ 12.7 ppm)
units.action_summary: Continue operating previously SIP-approved I/M programs and update them as needed to meet basic I/M requirements.

units.obligation_text: Any such area required by the Clean Air Act, as in effect prior to November 15, 1990, to have an I/M program shall also implement a basic I/M program.
units.actor: areas required by the Clean Air Act to have an I/M program
units.action_summary: Implement a basic I/M program if previously required by the Clean Air Act.

units.obligation_text: Any area designated as moderate ozone nonattainment shall implement basic I/M in any 1990 Census-defined urbanized area in the nonattainment area.
units.actor: areas designated as moderate ozone nonattainment
units.action_summary: Implement basic I/M in 1990 urbanized areas within the moderate ozone nonattainment area.

units.obligation_text: Any area outside an ozone transport region designated as serious or worse ozone nonattainment, or moderate or serious CO nonattainment with a design value greater than 12.7 ppm, and having a 1990 Census-defined urbanized area population of less than 200,000 shall implement basic I/M in the 1990 Census-defined urbanized area.
units.actor: areas outside ozone transport regions meeting the designation and population/design-value criteria
units.action_summary: Implement basic I/M in the 1990 urbanized area for such areas with population <200,000.

units.obligation_text: If the boundaries of a moderate ozone nonattainment area are changed pursuant to § 107(d)(4)(A) of the Clean Air Act, such that the area includes additional urbanized areas, then a basic I/M program shall be implemented in the newly included 1990 Census-defined urbanized areas.
units.action_summary: Implement basic I/M in newly included 1990 urbanized areas when boundaries change to include them.

units.obligation_text: If the boundaries of a serious or worse ozone nonattainment area or of a moderate or serious CO nonattainment area with a design value greater than 12.7 ppm are changed any time after enactment pursuant to § 107(d)(4)(A) such that the area includes additional urbanized areas, then an enhanced I/M program shall be implemented in the newly included 1990 Census-defined urbanized areas, if the 1980 Census-defined urban area population is 200,000 or more.
units.action_summary: Implement enhanced I/M in newly included 1990 urbanized areas when boundaries change and 1980 urban area population ≥200,000.

units.obligation_text: If a marginal ozone nonattainment area is reclassified to moderate, a basic I/M program shall be implemented in the 1990 Census-defined urbanized area(s) in the nonattainment area.
units.action_summary: Upon reclassification from marginal to moderate, implement a basic I/M in the 1990 urbanized area(s).

units.obligation_text: If the area is reclassified to serious or worse, an enhanced I/M program shall be implemented in the 1990 Census-defined urbanized area, if the 1980 Census-defined urban area population is 200,000 or more. If less than 200,000, a basic I/M program shall be implemented in the 1990 Census-defined urbanized area(s) in the nonattainment area.
units.action_summary: On reclassification to serious or worse, implement enhanced I/M if 1980 urban area population ≥200,000; otherwise implement basic I/M.

units.obligation_text: If a moderate ozone or CO nonattainment area is reclassified to serious or worse, an enhanced I/M program shall be implemented in the 1990 Census-defined urbanized area, if the 1980 Census-defined urban area population is 200,000 or more. If less than 200,000, a basic I/M program shall be implemented in the 1990 Census-defined urbanized area(s) in the nonattainment area.
units.action_summary: Upon reclassification from moderate to serious or worse, implement enhanced I/M if 1980 urban population ≥200,000; otherwise implement basic I/M.

units.obligation_text: In an ozone transport region, the program shall entirely cover all counties within subject MSAs or subject portions of MSAs, as defined by OMB in 1980, except largely rural counties having a population density of less than 200 persons per square mile based on the 1990 Census can be excluded.
units.action_summary: Programs in ozone transport regions must cover all counties in subject MSAs, but may exclude largely rural counties with density <200 persons/sq mile (1990 Census).
units.modal_raw: shall entirely cover; can be excluded

units.obligation_text: Outside of ozone transport regions, programs shall nominally cover at least the entire urbanized area, based on the 1990 census. Exclusion of some urban population is allowed as long as an equal number of non-urban residents of the MSA containing the subject urbanized area are included to compensate for the exclusion.
units.action_summary: Programs outside ozone transport regions must nominally cover entire 1990 urbanized area; some urban exclusions allowed if compensated by including equal non-urban residents.

units.obligation_text: Emission reduction benefits from expanding coverage beyond the minimum required urban area boundaries can be applied toward the reasonable further progress requirements and can be used for offsets, provided the covered vehicles are operated in the nonattainment area, but not toward the enhanced I/M performance standard requirement.
units.action_summary: Benefits from expanded coverage may be credited toward RFP requirements and offsets if vehicles operate in the nonattainment area, but not toward meeting the enhanced I/M performance standard.
units.modal_raw: can be applied; can be used; not toward

units.obligation_text: In multi-state urbanized areas outside of ozone transport regions, I/M is required in those states in the subject multi-state area that have an urban area population of 50,000 or more, as defined by the Bureau of Census in 1980.
units.action_summary: States with portions of a multi-state urbanized area having population ≥50,000 must implement I/M.

units.obligation_text: In a multi-state urbanized area with a population of 200,000 or more that is required under paragraph (a) of this section to implement enhanced I/M, any state with a portion of the urbanized area having a population of 50,000 or more shall implement an enhanced program.
units.actor: states with portion population ≥50,000 in multi-state urbanized areas ≥200,000
units.action_summary: States with portions of large multi-state urbanized areas must implement enhanced I/M if portion population ≥50,000.

units.obligation_text: The SIP shall describe the applicable areas in detail and shall include the legal authority necessary to establish program boundaries.
units.action_summary: SIP must detail applicable areas and include legal authority to set program boundaries.

units.obligation_text: Enhanced I/M programs shall be designed and implemented to meet or exceed a minimum performance standard, which is expressed as emission levels in area-wide average grams per mile (gpm), achieved from highway mobile sources as a result of the program.
units.action_summary: Design and implement enhanced I/M to meet or exceed specified area-wide gpm emission performance standards.
units.modal_raw: shall be designed and implemented to meet or exceed

units.obligation_text: The performance standard shall be established using the following model I/M program inputs and local characteristics, such as vehicle mix and local fuel controls, except as provided in paragraph (e) of this section.
units.action_summary: Establish performance standard using specified model I/M inputs and local characteristics (with exceptions in paragraph (e)).

units.obligation_text: Network Type. Centralized testing.
units.action_summary: Model program assumes centralized testing network type.

units.obligation_text: Start Date. For areas with existing I/M programs, 1983. For areas newly subject, 1994.
units.action_summary: Model program start dates: existing programs 1983; newly subject areas 1994.

units.obligation_text: Test Frequency. Annual testing.
units.action_summary: Model program assumes annual testing frequency.

units.obligation_text: Model Year Coverage. Testing of 1988 and later vehicles.
units.action_summary: Model program covers 1988 and later vehicles.

units.obligation_text: Vehicle Type Coverage. Light duty vehicles, and light duty trucks, rated up to 8,500 pounds Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR).
units.action_summary: Model program covers light-duty vehicles and light-duty trucks up to 8,500 lb GVWR.

units.obligation_text: Exhaust Emission Test Type. Transient mass-emission testing on 1986 and later model year vehicles using the IM240 driving cycle, two-speed testing (as described in appendix B of this subpart) of 1981-1985 vehicles, and idle testing (as described in appendix B of this subpart) of pre-1981 vehicles is assumed.
units.action_summary: Model program assumes specific exhaust emission tests: IM240 for 1986+, two-speed for 1981-1985, idle for pre-1981.

units.obligation_text: Emission standards for various model years and vehicle classes (i)-(vi) specifying gpm levels for HC/NMHC, CO, and NOx as listed in the regulation.
units.action_summary: Model program specifies emission standards (grams per mile or percentages/ppm for various model years and vehicle classes).
units.modal_raw: shall be established (as part of model inputs)

units.obligation_text: Emission standards for 1981-1985 model year vehicles of 1.2% CO, and 220 ppm HC for the idle, two-speed tests and loaded steady-state tests; and maximum exhaust dilution measured as no less than 6% CO plus carbon dioxide (CO2) on vehicles subject to a steady-state test.
units.action_summary: Specify test-specific emission limits for 1981-1985 vehicles and maximum exhaust dilution measurement criteria.
units.modal_raw: shall be established (as part of model inputs)

units.obligation_text: Emission Control Device Inspections. Visual inspection of the catalyst and fuel inlet restrictor on all 1984 and later model year vehicles.
units.action_summary: Include visual inspections of catalyst and fuel inlet restrictor for 1984+ vehicles.
units.modal_raw: shall (as model input) require visual inspection

units.obligation_text: Evaporative System Function Checks. Evaporative system integrity (pressure) test on 1983 and later model year vehicles and an evaporative system transient purge test on 1986 and later model year vehicles.
units.action_summary: Include evaporative system integrity tests for 1983+ and transient purge tests for 1986+ vehicles.

units.obligation_text: Stringency. A 20% emission test failure rate among pre-1981 model year vehicles. Waiver Rate. A 1% waiver rate, as a percentage of failed vehicles. Compliance Rate. A 98% compliance rate.
units.action_summary: Model program assumes specific failure, waiver, and compliance rates: 20% failure (pre-1981), 1% waiver, 98% compliance.

units.obligation_text: Evaluation Date. Enhanced I/M programs shall be shown to obtain the same or lower emission levels as the model program by 2000 for ozone nonattainment areas and 2001 for CO nonattainment areas, and for severe and extreme ozone nonattainment areas, on each applicable milestone and attainment deadline, thereafter.
units.action_summary: Demonstrate equivalence to model program by 2000 (ozone) or 2001 (CO) and meet milestone deadlines thereafter.

units.obligation_text: The performance standard shall include on-road testing of at least 0.5% of the subject vehicle population as a supplement to the periodic inspection required in paragraph (a) of this section.
units.action_summary: Include on-road testing covering at least 0.5% of subject vehicle population as supplement to periodic inspections.

units.obligation_text: The performance standard includes testing of the vehicle's on-board diagnostics system for vehicles certified to comply with requirements for such capability; however, regulations governing the design of OBD systems are not yet final.
units.action_summary: Include testing of OBD systems for vehicles certified to have OBD capability (subject to future OBD design regulations).

units.obligation_text: Equivalency of the emission levels which will be achieved by the I/M program design in the SIP to those of the model program described in this section shall be demonstrated using the most current version of EPA's mobile source emission model or an alternative approved by the Administrator using EPA guidance to aid in the estimation of input parameters.
units.action_summary: Demonstrate equivalency to model program using the most current EPA mobile source emission model or Administrator-approved alternative with EPA guidance.

units.obligation_text: If the Administrator finds ... that NOx emission reductions are not beneficial in a given ozone nonattainment area, then NOx emission reductions are not required of the enhanced I/M program.
units.action_summary: If Administrator determines NOx reductions not beneficial, enhanced I/M programs are not required to reduce NOx in that area.

units.obligation_text: In the case of El Paso, Texas, providing that its SIP has been approved as meeting the reasonable further progress requirements of the Act and that the Administrator has not determined that a milestone has been missed, the model program inputs shall be as in paragraph (a) of this section, except that the transient and purge tests shall be assumed for 1990 and later model year vehicles two-speed testing on 1981-1989 model year vehicles, idle testing on 1968-1980 model year vehicles and pressure testing on 1971 and later vehicles.
units.action_summary: For El Paso, model inputs differ as specified, provided SIP approvals and milestone status conditions are met.

units.obligation_text: Basic I/M programs shall be designed and implemented to meet or exceed a minimum performance standard, which is expressed as emission levels achieved from highway mobile sources as a result of the program.
units.action_summary: Design and implement basic I/M to meet or exceed specified emission performance standards.
units.modal_raw: shall be designed and implemented to meet or exceed

units.obligation_text: Model inputs for the basic I/M program: Network Type. Centralized testing. Start Date. 1983. Test Frequency. Annual testing. Model Year Coverage. Testing of 1968 and later model year vehicles. Vehicle Type Coverage. Light duty vehicles.
units.action_summary: Basic I/M model inputs specify centralized testing, 1983 start, annual testing, coverage of 1968+ model years and light duty vehicles.

units.obligation_text: Emission Standards. No weaker than specified in 40 CFR part 85, subpart W.
units.action_summary: Basic I/M emission standards must be at least as stringent as those in 40 CFR part 85, subpart W.

units.obligation_text: Emission Control Device Inspections. None. Stringency. A 20% emission test failure rate among pre-1981 model year vehicles. Waiver Rate. A 0% waiver rate. Compliance Rate. A100% compliance rate.
units.action_summary: Basic model specifies no emission control device inspections, 20% failure among pre-1981 vehicles, 0% waiver rate, and 100% compliance rate.

units.obligation_text: Evaluation Date. Basic I/M programs shall be shown to obtain the same or lower emission levels as the model inputs by 1997 for ozone nonattainment areas and 1996 for CO nonattainment areas; and for serious or worse ozone nonattainment areas, on each applicable milestone and attainment deadline, thereafter.
units.action_summary: Demonstrate equivalence to model inputs by 1997 (ozone) or 1996 (CO) and meet milestone deadlines thereafter.

units.obligation_text: The performance standard includes testing of the vehicle's on-board diagnostics system for vehicles certified to comply with requirements for such capability; however, regulations governing the design of OBD systems are not yet final.
units.action_summary: Include OBD testing for vehicles certified to have OBD capability (subject to future OBD regulations).

units.obligation_text: Equivalency of emission levels which will be achieved by the I/M program design in the SIP to those of the model program described in this section shall be demonstrated using the most current version of the EPA mobile source emission model and EPA guidance on the estimation of input parameters.
units.action_summary: Demonstrate equivalency to the basic model using the current EPA emission model and guidance.

units.obligation_text: Areas required to implement basic I/M programs shall meet the performance standard for the pollutants which cause them to be subject to basic requirements. Areas subject as a result of ozone nonattainment shall meet the standard for VOCs.
units.actor: areas required to implement basic I/M
units.action_summary: Meet performance standards for the pollutants that trigger basic I/M requirements (ozone-driven areas must meet VOC standard).

units.obligation_text: Enhanced I/M programs shall be operated in a centralized test-only format unless the state can demonstrate that a decentralized test-and-repair program would be equally effective in achieving the enhanced I/M performance standard.
units.action_summary: Operate enhanced I/M in centralized test-only format unless state demonstrates decentralized test-and-repair is equally effective.

units.obligation_text: Basic I/M programs can be either centralized or decentralized at the state's discretion, but a decentralized program shall be demonstrated to achieve the same emission reduction as the program described in § 51.352 of this subpart.
units.action_summary: Basic programs may be centralized or decentralized; if decentralized, must demonstrate equivalent emission reductions to §51.352 program.

units.obligation_text: A network consisting of stations that perform official I/M testing and in which owners and employees of those stations, or companies owning those stations, are contractually or legally barred from engaging in motor vehicle repair or service, motor vehicle parts sales, and motor vehicle sale and leasing, either directly or indirectly, and are barred from referring vehicle owners to particular providers of motor vehicle repair services (except as provided in § 51.369(b)(1) of this subpart) shall be considered equivalent to a centralized, test-only system.
units.action_summary: Networks meeting the described contractual/legal bar conditions are to be treated as equivalent to centralized test-only systems.

units.obligation_text: Enhanced I/M areas may choose to implement a decentralized, test-and-repair network on a trial basis and shall be granted provisional equivalency if the state submits a plan meeting the requirements of this paragraph.
units.action_summary: States may implement test-and-repair on trial and will receive provisional equivalency if they submit a compliant plan.

units.obligation_text: The SIP include a commitment to submit to EPA an assessment of the program based on the evaluation testing required in paragraph (d) of this section, that determines whether the program is meeting the performance standard. The commitment schedule shall provide sufficient time for EPA to make an equivalency determination and, if necessary, for the state to implement the back-up program required in paragraph (b)(3) of this section.
units.action_summary: SIP must commit to submit program assessment per paragraph (d) and include a schedule allowing EPA equivalency determination and, if needed, implementation of the back-up program.

units.obligation_text: The SIP shall include a plan to implement a back-up program consisting of a centralized, test-only network with transient emission testing, or equivalent. The plan shall include legal authority signed by the Governor and certified by the Attorney General, fully adopted regulations, and any other components needed to implement the back-up program.
units.action_summary: SIP must include a back-up plan for a centralized test-only program, including Governor-signed legal authority, AG certification, adopted regulations, and other implementation components.

units.obligation_text: Implementation of the back-up program shall be automatic unless the Administrator makes a finding in the Federal Register that the test-and-repair system will meet the performance standard by November 15, 1999, or can do so with program design changes that are normal I/M input parameters to the EPA emission factor model, or that accelerate the retirement of older, high emitting vehicles. The back-up program shall be implemented no later than January 1999 in an annual program, or January 1998 in a biennial program.
units.action_summary: Back-up program automatically implemented unless Administrator finds test-and-repair will meet standard by specified date; if required, back-up must be implemented by Jan 1999 (annual) or Jan 1998 (biennial).
units.modal_raw: shall be automatic; shall be implemented no later than

units.obligation_text: For the purposes of satisfying the requirements of § 182(b)(1)(A)(i) and § 182(c)(2) of the Clean Air Act, relating to Reasonable Further Progress requirements, the credit claimed for a test-and-repair program shall be in accordance with paragraph (c) of this section. Credit for the effectiveness of the back-up program may be claimed beginning with scheduled implementation. Credit adjustments may occur at any time based on the results of the program evaluation required in paragraph (d) of this section.
units.action_summary: Credits for test-and-repair must follow paragraph (c); back-up program credit may be claimed when implemented; credits may be adjusted based on program evaluation.
units.modal_raw: shall be; may be claimed; may occur

units.obligation_text: Credits for test-and-repair networks ... are assumed to be 50% less than those for a test-only network for the tailpipe emission test, purge test, evaporative system integrity test, catalyst check, and gas cap check; and 75% less for the evaporative canister checks, PCV check, and air system checks.
units.action_summary: Default credit reductions: test-and-repair networks receive 50% less credit for certain tests and 75% less for others compared to test-only networks.

units.obligation_text: Smaller reductions in credits for the various test protocols may be claimed if a state can demonstrate to the satisfaction of the Administrator that based on past performance with the specific test-type and inspection standards employed, its test-and-repair system will exceed these levels. At a minimum, such a demonstration shall include: (i) Surveys that assess the effectiveness of repairs performed on vehicles that failed the tailpipe emission test and evaporative system tests; (ii) In programs including tampering checks, measurement of actual tampering rates, their change over time, and the change attributable to finding and fixing such tampering as opposed to deterrence effects; and (iii) The results of undercover surveys of inspector effectiveness as it relates to identifying vehicles that need repair.
units.action_summary: States may claim smaller credit reductions if they demonstrate greater effectiveness to Administrator satisfaction; demonstrations must include specified surveys, tampering measurements, and undercover inspector effectiveness results.

units.obligation_text: In the case of hybrid systems including both test-only and test-and-repair facilities, full credit shall apply to the portion of the fleet initially tested and subsequently retested at a test-only facility meeting the requirements of paragraph (a) of this section, and to the portion of the fleet initially tested and failed at a test-and-repair facility but subsequently passing a retest at a test-only facility meeting those same requirements. The credit loss assumptions described in paragraph (c) of this section shall apply to the portion of the fleet initially tested at a test-only facility and subsequently retested at a test-and-repair facility, to the portion of the fleet initially passed at a test-and-repair facility, and to the portion initially failed at a test-only facility and retested at a test-and-repair facility.
units.action_summary: Hybrid system crediting rules: full credit for portions retested/passing at test-only facilities; credit loss assumptions apply to other specified portions.

units.obligation_text: Areas operating test-and-repair networks or hybrid networks may, in the future, claim greater effectiveness than described in paragraph (c)(1) of this section if a demonstration of greater effectiveness is made to the satisfaction of the Administrator using the program evaluation protocol described in paragraph (d) of this section.
units.action_summary: States may claim greater effectiveness (and thus greater credits) if they demonstrate it using the program evaluation protocol to Administrator satisfaction.

units.obligation_text: I/M programs shall include an ongoing evaluation to qualify the emission reduction benefits of the program, and to determine if the program is meeting the requirements of the Clean Air Act and this regulation.
units.action_summary: Include ongoing program evaluation to quantify emission reductions and determine compliance with the Clean Air Act and regulation.

units.obligation_text: The state shall report the results of the program evaluation on a biennial basis, starting two years after the initial start date of mandatory testing as required in § 51.373 of this subpart, in addition to that required in paragraph (b) of this section (for enhanced test-and-repair programs).
units.action_summary: Report program evaluation results biennially beginning two years after mandatory testing starts, and as otherwise required.

units.obligation_text: The evaluation shall be used to establish actual emission reductions achieved for the purposes of satisfying the requirements of § 182(g)(1) and § 182(g)(2) of the Clean Air Act, relating to Reductions in Emissions and Compliance Demonstration.
units.action_summary: Use the evaluation to establish actual emission reductions for satisfying specified Clean Air Act requirements.

units.obligation_text: The evaluation program shall consist, at a minimum, of those items described in paragraph (c)(1) of this section and mass emission test data using the procedure specified in § 51.357(a)(11) of this subpart, or any other procedure approved as equivalent, and evaporative system checks for model years subject to those procedures. The test data shall be obtained from a representative, random sample, taken annually at the time of initial inspection (before repair), of at least 0.1 percent of the vehicles subject to inspection in a given year which shall receive a state administered or monitored IM240 mass emission test or equivalent, as specified in this paragraph, at the time the initial test is due.
units.action_summary: Evaluation must include specified items, mass emission test data per §51.357(a)(11), evaporative checks, and annually sample at least 0.1% of vehicles for IM240 or equivalent at initial inspection.

units.obligation_text: If the comparison shows that the emission factor target specified in § 51.351 or § 51.352, as applicable, has not been achieved, then the state is required to take corrective action. Corrective action shall include whatever measures necessary to achieve the target, in accordance with paragraph (b)(3) of this section.
units.action_summary: If targets not met, state must take corrective actions (including measures per paragraph (b)(3)) to achieve emission factor targets.

units.obligation_text: The SIP shall include a detailed description of the network to be employed, the required legal authority, and, in the case of areas making claims under paragraph (c) of this section, the required demonstration.
units.action_summary: SIP must describe the testing network, legal authority, and demonstrations for claims under paragraph (c).

units.obligation_text: The SIP shall include a description of the evaluation schedule and protocol, the sampling methodology, the data collection and analysis system, the resources and personnel for evaluation, and related details of the evaluation program, and the legal authority enabling the evaluation program.
units.action_summary: SIP must include evaluation schedule/protocol, sampling methods, data systems, resources/personnel, and legal authority for evaluation.

units.obligation_text: The SIP for enhanced I/M areas that are implementing a test-and-repair network shall also address all of the requirements of paragraph (b) of this section. The SIP shall demonstrate that there is adequate time to complete the evaluation, to submit the data to EPA for review, to allow EPA to take formal action, and to implement the back-up program to meet the performance standard by the November 15, 1999 deadline.
units.action_summary: SIP for enhanced test-and-repair areas must meet paragraph (b) requirements and show timelines adequate to complete evaluation, submit data, allow EPA action, and implement back-up program by Nov 15, 1999.

units.obligation_text: The program shall maintain the administrative resources necessary to perform all of the program functions including quality assurance, data analysis and reporting, and the holding of hearings and adjudication of cases.
units.action_summary: Maintain necessary administrative resources for program functions including QA, data, hearings, and adjudications.

units.obligation_text: A portion of the test fee or a separately assessed per vehicle fee shall be collected, placed in a dedicated fund and retained, to be used to finance program oversight, management, and capital expenditures.
units.action_summary: Collect fees and deposit them in a dedicated fund to finance program oversight, management, and capital expenditures.
units.modal_raw: shall be collected; shall be placed; shall be retained

units.obligation_text: Alternatives to this approach shall be acceptable if the state can demonstrate that adequate funding of the program can be maintained in some other fashion.
units.action_summary: Alternative funding approaches may be accepted if the state demonstrates adequate funding can be maintained otherwise.

units.obligation_text: Reliance on future uncommitted annual or biennial appropriations from the state or local General Fund is not acceptable.
units.action_summary: Programs may not rely on future uncommitted state/local General Fund appropriations for funding.

units.obligation_text: The program shall employ sufficient personnel to effectively carry out the duties related to the program, including administrative audits, inspector audits, data analysis, program oversight, program evaluation, public education and assistance, and enforcement against stations and inspectors as well as against motorists who are out of compliance with program regulations and requirements.
units.action_summary: Employ sufficient personnel to perform audits, analysis, oversight, evaluation, education, assistance, and enforcement duties.

units.obligation_text: The program shall possess equipment necessary to achieve the objectives of the program and meet program requirements, including a steady supply of vehicles for covert auditing, test equipment and facilities for program evaluation, and computers capable of data processing, analysis, and reporting.
units.action_summary: Possess necessary equipment (covert audit vehicles, test equipment/facilities, computers) to meet program objectives and requirements.

units.obligation_text: Equipment or equivalent services may be contractor supplied or owned by the state or local authority.
units.action_summary: Programs may use contractor-supplied equipment or state/local owned equipment or services.

units.obligation_text: The SIP shall include a detailed budget plan which describes the source of funds for personnel, program administration, program enforcement, purchase of necessary equipment (such as vehicles for undercover audits), and any other requirements discussed throughout, for the period prior to the next biennial self-evaluation required in § 51.366 of this subpart.
units.action_summary: SIP must include detailed budget plan describing funding sources for program needs through next biennial self-evaluation.

units.obligation_text: The SIP shall include a detailed description of personnel resources. The plan shall include the number of personnel dedicated to overt and covert auditing, data analysis, program administration, enforcement, and other necessary functions and the training attendant to each function.
units.action_summary: SIP must detail personnel resources, numbers for each function, and associated training.

units.obligation_text: The performance standards for I/M programs assume an annual test frequency; other schedules may be approved if the required emission reductions are achieved.
units.action_summary: Default assumption is annual testing; other test schedules can be approved if they achieve required emission reductions.

units.obligation_text: The SIP shall describe the test schedule in detail, including test year selection scheme if testing is other than annual.
units.action_summary: SIP must provide detailed test schedule and selection scheme if not annual.

units.obligation_text: The SIP shall include the legal authority necessary to implement and enforce the test frequency requirement and explain how the test frequency will be integrated with the enforcement process.
units.action_summary: SIP must include legal authority for implementing/enforcing test frequency and explain integration with enforcement.

units.obligation_text: The performance standard for enhanced I/M programs assumes coverage of all 1988 and later model year light duty vehicles and light duty trucks up to 8,500 pounds GVWR. The standard for basic I/M programs does not include light duty trucks. Other levels of coverage may be approved if the necessary emission reductions are achieved.
units.action_summary: Enhanced programs assume coverage of 1988+ light-duty vehicles and trucks up to 8,500 lb; basic programs exclude light-duty trucks; alternate coverage may be approved if emission reductions achieved.

units.obligation_text: All vehicles of a covered model year and vehicle type shall be tested according to the applicable test schedule, including leased vehicles whose registration or titling is in the name of an equity owner other than the lessee or user.
units.actor: owners/operators of covered vehicles / program enforcement
units.action_summary: All vehicles in covered model years/types (including certain leased vehicles) must be tested per schedule.

units.obligation_text: All subject fleet vehicles shall be inspected. Fleets may be officially inspected outside of the normal I/M program test facilities, if such alternatives are approved by the program administration, but shall be subject to the same test requirements using the same quality control standards as non-fleet vehicles.
units.action_summary: All fleet vehicles must be inspected; alternative inspection locations may be used if approved but must meet same test and QC standards as non-fleet vehicles.
units.modal_raw: shall be inspected; may be inspected (if approved); shall be subject

units.obligation_text: Subject vehicles which are registered in the program area but are primarily operated in another I/M area shall be tested, either in the area of primary operation, if the program in that area is willing to test the vehicle and provide compliance documentation, or in the area of registration. Alternate schedules may be established to permit convenient testing of these vehicles.
units.action_summary: Vehicles registered in the program area but mainly operated elsewhere must be tested either where primarily operated or where registered; alternate schedules may be used for convenience.
units.modal_raw: shall be tested; may be established

units.obligation_text: Vehicles which are operated on Federal installations located within an I/M program area shall be tested, regardless of whether the vehicles are registered in the state or local I/M area. The installation shall use one of the following methods to establish proof of compliance: (i) Presentation of a valid certificate of compliance from the I/M program. (ii) Presentation of proof of vehicle registration within the geographic area covered by the I/M program, except for any program whose enforcement is not through registration denial. (iii) Another method approved by the state I/M program administrator.
units.actor: vehicles on Federal installations / installation authority
units.action_summary: Vehicles on Federal installations in an I/M area must be tested; installations must establish proof of compliance via a valid certificate, proof of registration, or another state-approved method.

units.obligation_text: Special exemptions may be permitted for certain subject vehicles provided a demonstration is made that the performance standard will be met.
units.action_summary: Programs may permit special exemptions for certain vehicles only if demonstration shows performance standard will still be met.

units.obligation_text: The SIP shall include a detailed description of the number and types of vehicles to be covered by the program, and a plan for how those vehicles are to be identified, including vehicles that are routinely operated in the area but may not be registered in the area.
units.action_summary: SIP must describe which vehicles will be covered and how they will be identified, including routinely operated but not registered vehicles.

units.obligation_text: The SIP shall include a description of any special exemptions which will be granted by the program, and an estimate of the percentage and number of subject vehicles which will be impacted. Such exemptions shall be accounted for in the emission reduction analysis.

units.action_summary: Use the listed production multipliers for model years 2017–2025 when applying production multipliers.

units.obligation_text: Multiplier-based credits for model years 2022 through 2025 may not exceed credit caps, as follows:
units.action_summary: Multiplier-based credits for 2022–2025 are limited by specified credit caps.

units.obligation_text: Calculate a nominal annual credit cap in Mg using the following equation, rounded to the nearest whole number: [equation].
units.action_summary: Compute the nominal annual credit cap in Mg using the specified equation and rounding rule.

units.obligation_text: Calculate an annual g/mile equivalent value for the multiplier-based credits using the following equation, rounded to the nearest 0.1 g/mile: [equation].
units.action_summary: Compute the annual g/mile equivalent value for multiplier-based credits using the specified equation and rounding rule.

units.obligation_text: Calculate a cumulative g/mile equivalent value for the multiplier-based credits in 2022 through 2025 by adding the annual g/mile equivalent values calculated under paragraph (c)(3)(ii) of this section.
units.action_summary: Add annual g/mile equivalent values for 2022–2025 to obtain a cumulative g/mile equivalent value.

units.obligation_text: The cumulative g/mile equivalent value may not exceed 10.0 in any year.
units.action_summary: The cumulative g/mile equivalent value for multiplier-based credits cannot exceed 10.0 in any year.

units.obligation_text: The annual credit report must include for every model year from 2022 through 2025, as applicable, the calculated values for the nominal annual credit cap in Mg and the cumulative g/mile equivalent value.
units.action_summary: Include the nominal annual credit cap (Mg) and the cumulative g/mile equivalent value for each applicable model year in the annual credit report.

units.obligation_text: The maximum allowable decrease in the manufacturer’s combined passenger automobile and light truck fleet average CO2 emissions attributable to use of the default credit values in paragraph (b)(1) of this section is 10 g/mi through model year 2022, and 15 g/mi for model years 2023 and later...
units.action_summary: Set the maximum allowable fleet-average CO2 decrease from default credit values to 10 g/mi through 2022 and 15 g/mi for 2023 and later.

units.obligation_text: Manufacturers may use 15 g/mi in model years 2020 through 2022 if they meet the definitions in paragraphs (b)(4)(v)(B), (vi)(B), and (x)(B) of this section.
units.action_summary: Manufacturers may use a 15 g/mi default-credit reduction in 2020–2022 if they meet specified definitions.

units.obligation_text: Determine the gram per mile decrease for the combined passenger automobile and light truck fleet using the following formula: [formula].
units.action_summary: Calculate the combined fleet gram-per-mile decrease using the specified formula.

units.obligation_text: If the value determined in paragraph (b)(2)(i) of this section is greater than 10 or 15 grams per mile (as applicable), the total credits, in Megagrams, that may be accrued by a manufacturer using the default gram per mile values in paragraph (b)(1) of this section shall be determined using the following formula: [formula].
units.action_summary: If the calculated fleet decrease exceeds the applicable limit, determine the maximum megagram credits that may be accrued using the specified formula.

units.obligation_text: If the value determined in paragraph (b)(2)(i) of this section is not greater than 10 or 15 grams per mile (as applicable), then the credits that may be accrued by a manufacturer using the default gram per mile values in paragraph (b)(1) of this section do not exceed the allowable limit, and total credits may be determined for each category of vehicles according to paragraph (f) of this section.
units.action_summary: If the fleet decrease does not exceed the applicable limit, manufacturers may determine credits by category according to paragraph (f).

units.obligation_text: If the value determined in paragraph (b)(2)(i) of this section is greater than 10 or 15 grams per mile (as applicable), then the combined passenger automobile and light truck credits, in Megagrams, that may be accrued using the calculations in paragraph (f) of this section must not exceed the value determined in paragraph (b)(2)(ii) of this section.
units.action_summary: If the fleet decrease exceeds the applicable limit, the combined credits determined under paragraph (f) cannot exceed the value calculated under (b)(2)(ii).

units.obligation_text: This limitation should generally be done by reducing the amount of credits attributable to the vehicle category that caused the limit to be exceeded such that the total value does not exceed the value determined in paragraph (b)(2)(ii) of this section.
units.action_summary: Generally reduce credits from the vehicle category that caused the limit to be exceeded to ensure the total does not exceed the allowed cap.

units.obligation_text: Through model year 2019, and optionally for model years 2020–2022, active transmission warm-up means a system that uses waste heat from the vehicle to quickly warm the transmission fluid to an operating temperature range using a heat exchanger...
units.action_summary: For eligibility/definition purposes, manufacturers may treat systems described as 'active transmission warm-up' through 2019 (and optionally 2020–2022) as meeting the definition.

units.obligation_text: Starting in model year 2023, and optionally for model years 2020–2022, active transmission warm-up means a system that uses waste heat from the vehicle’s exhaust to warm the transmission fluid to an operating temperature range using a dedicated heat exchanger. Active transmission warm-up may also include coolant systems that capture heat from a liquid-cooled exhaust manifold if the system is segregated from the coolant loop in the engine block.
units.action_summary: From 2023 (and optionally 2020–2022) the definition of active transmission warm-up includes exhaust-waste-heat systems and may include segregated coolant systems for eligibility.

units.obligation_text: Through model year 2019, and optionally for model years 2020–2022, active engine warm-up means a system that uses waste heat from the vehicle to warm up targeted parts of the engine so that it reduces engine friction losses and enables closed-loop fuel control more quickly.
units.action_summary: Systems meeting this definition qualify as 'active engine warm-up' through 2019 (and optionally 2020–2022) for purposes of credits/definitions.

units.obligation_text: Starting in model year 2023, and optionally for model years 2020–2022, active engine warm-up means a system that uses waste heat from the vehicle’s exhaust to warm up targeted parts of the engine... Active engine warm-up may also include coolant systems that capture heat from a liquid-cooled exhaust manifold if the system is segregated from the coolant loop in the engine block.
units.action_summary: From 2023 (and optionally 2020–2022) the definition of active engine warm-up includes exhaust-waste-heat systems and may include segregated coolant systems.

units.obligation_text: Through model year 2019, and optionally for model years 2020–2022, passive cabin ventilation means ducts, devices, or methods that utilize convective airflow to move heated air from the cabin interior to the exterior of the vehicle.
units.action_summary: Systems meeting this definition qualify as 'passive cabin ventilation' through 2019 (and optionally 2020–2022) for purposes of credits/definitions.

units.obligation_text: Starting in model year 2023, and optionally for model years 2020–2022, passive cabin ventilation means methods that create and maintain convective airflow through the body’s cabin by opening windows or sunroof when the vehicle is parked outside in direct sunlight.
units.action_summary: From 2023 (and optionally 2020–2022) the described methods qualify as 'passive cabin ventilation' for purposes of credits/definitions.

units.obligation_text: A citation to the appropriate previously approved methodology, including the appropriate Federal Register Notice and any subsequent EPA documentation of the Administrator’s decision;
units.actor: applicant/manufacturer (submitting a methodology request or documentation)
units.action_summary: Include a citation to the previously approved methodology and relevant Federal Register notice and EPA documentation in the submission.

units.obligation_text: Full size pickup trucks that are strong hybrid electric vehicles and that are produced in the 2017 through 2025 model years are eligible for a credit of 20 grams/mile.
units.actor: full size pickup trucks (manufacturers of such trucks)
units.action_summary: Strong-hybrid full-size pickup trucks produced 2017–2025 may receive a 20 g/mi CO2 credit.

units.obligation_text: To receive this credit in a model year, the manufacturer must produce a quantity of strong hybrid electric full size pickup trucks such that the proportion of production of such vehicles, when compared to the manufacturer’s total production of full size pickup trucks, is not less than 10 percent in that model year.
units.action_summary: Manufacturer must produce at least 10% of its full-size pickup production as strong-hybrid models in a model year to receive the credit that year.

units.obligation_text: Full size pickup trucks earning credits under this paragraph (a)(2) may not earn credits based on the production multipliers described in § 86.1866–12(b).
units.actor: full size pickup trucks (manufacturers of such trucks)
units.action_summary: Vehicles earning the strong-hybrid credit cannot also claim production-multiplier credits.

units.obligation_text: Full size pickup trucks that are produced in the 2017 through 2025 model years and that achieve carbon-related exhaust emissions less than or equal to the applicable target value determined in § 86.1818–12(c)(3) multiplied by 0.80 (rounded to the nearest gram/mile) in a model year are eligible for a credit of 20 grams/mile.
units.action_summary: Full-size pickup trucks meeting the ≤0.80×target emissions criterion in 2017–2025 are eligible for a 20 g/mi credit.

units.obligation_text: A pickup truck that qualifies for this credit in a model year may claim this credit for a maximum of four subsequent model years (a total of five consecutive model years) if the carbon-related exhaust emissions of that pickup truck do not increase relative to the emissions in the model year in which the pickup truck first qualified for the credit.
units.action_summary: A qualifying pickup truck may claim the 20 g/mi credit for up to four more model years (five total) provided emissions do not increase from its initial qualifying year.

units.obligation_text: This credit may not be claimed in any model year after 2025.
units.action_summary: The full-size pickup truck 20 g/mi credit cannot be claimed for any model year after 2025.

units.obligation_text: To qualify for this credit in a model year, the manufacturer must produce a quantity of full size pickup trucks that meet the emission requirements of this paragraph (b)(2) such that the proportion of production of such vehicles, when compared to the manufacturer’s total production of full size pickup trucks, is not less than 10 percent in that model year.
units.action_summary: Manufacturer must produce at least 10% of its full-size pickup production meeting the emission requirements to qualify for the credit in a model year.

units.obligation_text: A pickup truck that qualifies for this credit in a model year and is subject to a major redesign in a subsequent model year such that it qualifies for the credit in the model year of the redesign may be allowed to qualify for an additional five years (not to go beyond the 2025 model year) with EPA approval.
units.action_summary: A qualifying pickup truck undergoing a major redesign may be allowed, with EPA approval, to qualify for the credit for an additional five years (subject to not exceeding model year 2025).

units.obligation_text: Use good engineering judgment to determine whether a pickup truck has been subject to a major redesign.
units.action_summary: Apply good engineering judgment to determine whether a pickup truck experienced a major redesign.

units.obligation_text: For natural gas dual fuel model types, for model years 2012 through 2015, the arithmetic average of the following two terms; the result rounded to the nearest gram per mile:
units.action_summary: Calculate the specified arithmetic average for natural gas dual-fuel model types for model years 2012–2015 and round to the nearest g/mi.

units.obligation_text: Model year 2021 and later natural gas dual fuel model types may use a utility factor of 0.5 or the utility factor prescribed in this paragraph (j)(2)(vii).
units.action_summary: Model year 2021+ natural gas dual-fuel model types may use a utility factor of 0.5 or the prescribed utility factor.

title: Renewable Fuel Standard Program: Extension of Compliance and Attest Engagement Reporting Deadlines

units.obligation_text: Annual compliance reports must include all the following information:
units.actor: submitters of annual compliance reports (those preparing and submitting the reports)
units.action_summary: Annual compliance reports must contain the required information described in the rule.

units.obligation_text: Except as specified in paragraph (f)(1)(i)(B) of this section, for obligated parties, annual compliance reports must be submitted by whichever of the following dates is latest:
units.action_summary: Obligated parties must submit annual compliance reports by the latest of the specified dates.

units.obligation_text: March 31 of the subsequent calendar year.
units.action_summary: Submit annual compliance reports by March 31 of the following calendar year.

units.obligation_text: The next quarterly reporting deadline under paragraph (f)(2) of this section that is after the date the subsequent compliance year’s renewable fuel standards become effective in § 80.1405(a).
units.action_summary: Submit by the next quarterly reporting deadline after the subsequent compliance year's RFS standards become effective.

units.obligation_text: The next quarterly reporting deadline under paragraph (f)(2) of this section after the annual compliance reporting deadline for the prior compliance year.
units.action_summary: Submit by the next quarterly reporting deadline following the prior compliance year's reporting deadline.

units.obligation_text: For obligated parties that meet the requirements for a small refinery under § 80.1441(e)(2)(iii), for the 2019 compliance year, annual compliance reports must be submitted no later than the next quarterly reporting deadline under paragraph (f)(2) of this section that is after the date the 2021 renewable fuel standards become effective in § 80.1405(a).
units.actor: obligated parties that meet the requirements for a small refinery under § 80.1441(e)(2)(iii)
units.action_summary: Small refineries must submit 2019 annual compliance reports by the next quarterly reporting deadline after the 2021 standards become effective.

units.obligation_text: For the 2020 compliance year, annual compliance reports must be submitted no later than the next quarterly reporting deadline in paragraph (f)(2) of this section after the deadline in paragraph (f)(1)(i)(B)(1) of this section.
units.actor: obligated parties that meet the requirements for a small refinery under § 80.1441(e)(2)(iii)
units.action_summary: Small refineries must submit 2020 annual compliance reports by the next quarterly reporting deadline after the 2019 small refinery deadline.

units.obligation_text: For the 2021 compliance year, annual compliance reports must be submitted no later than the next quarterly reporting deadline in paragraph (f)(2) of this section after the deadline in paragraph (f)(1)(i)(B)(2) of this section.
units.actor: obligated parties that meet the requirements for a small refinery under § 80.1441(e)(2)(iii)
units.action_summary: Small refineries must submit 2021 annual compliance reports by the next quarterly reporting deadline after the 2020 small refinery deadline.

units.obligation_text: For all parties other than obligated parties, annual compliance reports must be submitted by March 31 of the subsequent year.
units.actor: all parties other than obligated parties
units.action_summary: Non-obligated parties must submit annual compliance reports by March 31 of the following year.

units.obligation_text: The annual compliance reporting deadline will be calculated in accordance with paragraph (f)(1)(i) of this section and published on EPA’s website.
units.action_summary: EPA will calculate the annual compliance reporting deadline per paragraph (f)(1)(i) and publish it on its website.

units.obligation_text: Except as specified in paragraph (d)(1)(ii) of this section, for obligated parties, annual attest engagement reports must be submitted to EPA by whichever of the following dates is latest:
units.action_summary: Obligated parties must submit annual attest engagement reports by the latest of the specified dates.

units.obligation_text: June 1 of the subsequent calendar year.
units.action_summary: Submit annual attest engagement reports by June 1 of the following calendar year.

units.obligation_text: The next June 1 annual attest engagement reporting deadline that is at least 60 days after the annual compliance reporting deadline under § 80.1451(f)(1)(i)(A).
units.action_summary: Submit by the next June 1 that is at least 60 days after the annual compliance reporting deadline.

units.obligation_text: For obligated parties that meet the requirements for a small refinery under § 80.1441(e)(2)(iii), for the 2019 compliance year, annual attest engagement reports must be submitted to EPA no later than the next June 1 annual attest engagement reporting deadline that is at least 60 days after the annual compliance reporting deadline under § 80.1451(f)(1)(i)(B)(1).
units.actor: obligated parties that meet the requirements for a small refinery under § 80.1441(e)(2)(iii)
units.action_summary: Small refineries must submit 2019 attest engagement reports by the next June 1 that is at least 60 days after the applicable annual compliance reporting deadline.

units.obligation_text: For obligated parties, for the 2020 compliance year, annual attest engagement reports must be submitted to EPA no later than the next June 1 annual attest engagement reporting deadline that is at least 60 days after the annual compliance reporting deadline under § 80.1451(f)(1)(i)(B)(2).
units.actor: obligated parties (small refineries as referenced in paragraph structure)
units.action_summary: Submit 2020 attest engagement reports by the next June 1 at least 60 days after the 2020 annual compliance reporting deadline.

units.obligation_text: For obligated parties, for the 2021 compliance year, annual attest engagement reports must be submitted to EPA no later than the next June 1 annual attest engagement reporting deadline that is at least 60 days after the annual compliance reporting deadline under § 80.1451(f)(1)(i)(B)(3).
units.actor: obligated parties (small refineries as referenced in paragraph structure)
units.action_summary: Submit 2021 attest engagement reports by the next June 1 at least 60 days after the 2021 annual compliance reporting deadline.

units.obligation_text: All parties other than obligated parties must submit annual attest engagement reports to EPA by June 1 of the subsequent calendar year.
units.actor: all parties other than obligated parties
units.action_summary: Non-obligated parties must submit annual attest engagement reports by June 1 of the following year.

units.obligation_text: The annual attest engagement reporting deadline will be calculated in accordance with paragraph (d)(1) of this section and published on EPA’s website.
units.action_summary: EPA will calculate and publish the annual attest engagement reporting deadline per paragraph (d)(1) on its website.
