title: Alternate Polychlorinated Biphenyls Extraction Methods and Polychlorinated Biphenyls Cleanup and Disposal Regulations

units.obligation_text: Media must not be disturbed, nor may they be diluted (e.g., excavated, placed on a pile, and sampled after such placement) before characterization sampling is conducted.
units.actor: persons conducting characterization sampling / responsible parties
units.action_summary: Do not disturb or dilute media before characterization sampling.

units.obligation_text: The burner will burn the used oil only in a combustion facility identified in paragraph (e)(1) of this section and identify the class of burner they qualify under.
units.action_summary: Burn used oil only in combustion facilities identified in §761.20(e)(1) and identify burner class.

units.obligation_text: Marketers who first claim that the used oil fuel contains no detectable PCBs must include among the records required by 40 CFR 279.72(b) and 279.74(b) and (c), copies of the analysis or other information documenting their claim, and they must include among the records required by 40 CFR 279.74(a) and (c) and 279.75, a copy of each certification notice received or prepared relating to transactions involving PCB-containing used oil.
units.action_summary: Marketers claiming no detectable PCBs must include copies of analyses/documentation and certification notices in specified records.

units.obligation_text: Burners must include among the records required by 40 CFR 279.65 and 279.66, a copy of each certification notice required by paragraph (e)(3)(ii) of this section that they send to a marketer.
units.action_summary: Burners must keep copies of certification notices they send to marketers in the specified records.

units.obligation_text: Any person characterizing PCB contamination in natural gas pipe or natural gas pipeline systems must do so by analyzing organic liquids collected at existing condensate collection points in the pipe or pipeline system.
units.actor: any person characterizing PCB contamination in natural gas pipe or pipeline systems
units.action_summary: Characterization must be done by analyzing organic liquids from existing condensate collection points.

units.obligation_text: Any person characterizing multi-phasic liquids must do so in accordance with § 761.1(b)(4).
units.action_summary: Characterization of multi-phasic liquids must follow §761.1(b)(4).

units.obligation_text: If no liquids are present and they choose, in their discretion, to characterize PCB contamination, the person must use standard wipe samples in accordance with subpart M of this part.
units.actor: any person who chooses to characterize when no liquids are present
units.action_summary: If choosing to characterize without liquids, must use standard wipe samples per subpart M.

units.obligation_text: The EPA Regional Administrator may inform the owner or operator of the site that there is reason to believe that spills, leaks, or other uncontrolled releases or discharges ... constitute ongoing disposal ... and may require the owner or operator to generate data necessary to characterize the risk.
units.action_summary: EPA Regional Administrator may inform and may require owner/operator to generate data to characterize risk.

units.obligation_text: If after reviewing any such data, the EPA Regional Administrator makes a finding, that an unreasonable risk exists, then they may direct the owner or operator of the site to dispose of the PCB remediation waste in accordance with § 761.61 such that an unreasonable risk of injury no longer exists.
units.action_summary: If EPA finds an unreasonable risk, EPA may direct owner/operator to dispose of PCB remediation waste per §761.61.

units.obligation_text: Any person responsible for PCB waste ... must dispose of it in accordance with either of the following:
units.actor: any person responsible for PCB waste
units.action_summary: Persons responsible for PCB waste meeting listed date/concentration conditions must dispose of it according to specified options.

units.obligation_text: As part of this evaluation, the Assistant Administrator will consider the impact of their action on the incentives to construct or expand PCB incinerators.
units.action_summary: Assistant Administrator will consider impacts on incentives to construct/expand PCB incinerators when evaluating actions.

units.obligation_text: Unless otherwise specified in this part, any person conducting the chemical analysis of PCBs shall do so using gas chromatography.
units.actor: any person conducting chemical analysis of PCBs
units.action_summary: Chemical analysis of PCBs must be performed using gas chromatography unless otherwise specified.

units.obligation_text: Any gas chromatographic method that is appropriate for the material being analyzed may be used, including EPA Method 608.3 ... and ASTM D4059–00.
units.actor: any person conducting chemical analysis of PCBs
units.action_summary: Appropriate gas chromatographic methods (including listed methods) may be used for PCB analysis.

units.obligation_text: Representative samples may be taken from either the common containers or the individual electrical equipment to determine the PCB concentration.
units.action_summary: Representative samples for PCB concentration may be taken from common containers or individual electrical equipment.

units.obligation_text: If any PCBs at a concentration of 500 ppm or greater have been added to the container or equipment then the total container contents must be considered as having a PCB concentration of 500 ppm or greater for purposes of complying with the disposal requirements of this subpart.
units.actor: persons subject to the disposal requirements of this subpart
units.action_summary: If ≥500 ppm PCBs have been added, the entire container is considered ≥500 ppm for disposal compliance.

units.obligation_text: For purposes of this paragraph, representative samples of mineral oil dielectric fluid are either samples taken in accordance with ASTM D 923–86 or ASTM D 923–89 ... or samples taken from a container that has been thoroughly mixed ...
units.actor: any person taking representative samples of mineral oil dielectric fluid
units.action_summary: Representative samples of mineral oil dielectric fluid must be taken per ASTM D923–86/D923–89 or from a thoroughly mixed container.

units.obligation_text: Within 30 calendar days of receiving the notification, the EPA Regional Administrator will respond in writing approving of the self-implementing cleanup, disapproving of the self-implementing cleanup, or requiring additional information.
units.action_summary: EPA Regional Administrator will respond in writing within 30 days to the notification on self-implementing cleanup.

units.obligation_text: If the EPA Regional Administrator does not respond within 30 calendar days of receiving the notice, the person submitting the notification may proceed with the cleanup according to the information the person provided to the EPA Regional Administrator.
units.action_summary: If EPA does not respond within 30 days, notifier may proceed with cleanup per their notification.

units.obligation_text: If, upon review of the notification, the EPA Regional Administrator determines that the notification does not contain all of the information required by paragraph (a)(3)(i) of this section ... they may require the submission of additional information.
units.action_summary: EPA may require additional information if notification lacks required information.

units.obligation_text: The cleanup and disposal must comply with all applicable requirements of paragraphs (a)(4) through (9) of this section.
units.actor: person conducting the cleanup and disposal
units.action_summary: Cleanup and disposal must meet all applicable requirements in paragraphs (a)(4) through (9).

units.obligation_text: Once cleanup is underway, the person conducting the cleanup must provide any proposed changes from the notification to the EPA Regional Administrator in writing no less than 14 calendar days prior to the proposed implementation of the change.
units.action_summary: Must provide written notice of proposed changes at least 14 days before implementation.

units.obligation_text: The EPA Regional Administrator will determine in their discretion whether to accept the change, and will respond to the change notification verbally within 7 calendar days and in writing within 14 calendar days of receiving it.
units.action_summary: EPA Regional Administrator will decide whether to accept change and respond verbally within 7 days and in writing within 14 days.

units.obligation_text: If the EPA Regional Administrator does not respond verbally within 7 calendar days and in writing within 14 calendar days of receiving the change notice, the person who submitted it may proceed with the cleanup according to the information in the change notice provided to the EPA Regional Administrator, subject to the submission of additional information if the Regional Administrator determines it is needed ... and in compliance with all applicable requirements of paragraphs (a)(4) through (9)...
units.actor: person who submitted the change notice
units.action_summary: If EPA does not respond in specified timeframes, notifier may proceed with the change, subject to possible later information requests and applicable requirements.

units.obligation_text: The generator must provide written notice, including the quantity to be shipped and highest concentration of PCBs at least 15 days before the first shipment of bulk PCB remediation waste from each cleanup site ... to each off-site facility where the waste is destined for an area not subject to a TSCA PCB Disposal Approval.
units.action_summary: Generator must give written notice with quantity and highest PCB concentration at least 15 days before first shipment to specified off-site facilities.

units.obligation_text: The generator must select applicable method(s) from the following list to extract PCBs and determine the PCB concentration from individual and composite samples of PCB remediation waste: SW–846 Method 3510C, Method 3520C, Method 3535A, Method 3540C, Method 3541, Method 3545A, Method 3546, Method 8082, Method 8082A, Method 8275A, or CWA Method 1668C.
units.action_summary: Generator must select extraction/analysis methods from the listed methods to determine PCB concentration.

units.obligation_text: Modifications to the methods listed in this paragraph or alternative methods not listed may be used if validated under subpart Q of this part or authorized in a § 761.61(c) approval.
units.action_summary: Modified or alternative methods may be used if validated under subpart Q or authorized by §761.61(c) approval.

units.obligation_text: Any person designing and constructing a cap must do so in accordance with § 264.310(a) of this chapter, and ensure that it complies with the permeability, sieve, liquid limit, and plasticity index parameters in § 761.75(b)(1)(ii) through (b)(1)(v).
units.actor: any person designing and constructing a cap
units.action_summary: Caps must be designed and constructed per §264.310(a) and meet specified permeability and material parameters in §761.75.

units.obligation_text: A cap of compacted soil shall have a minimum thickness of 25 cm (10 inches). A concrete or asphalt cap shall have a minimum thickness of 15 cm (6 inches).
units.actor: any person designing and constructing a cap / owner/operator
units.action_summary: Compacted soil caps must be at least 25 cm thick; concrete/asphalt caps must be at least 15 cm thick.

units.obligation_text: A cap must be of sufficient strength to maintain its effectiveness and integrity during the use of the cap surface which is exposed to the environment.
units.actor: owner/operator / person designing and constructing the cap
units.action_summary: Caps must be strong enough to maintain integrity during normal use/exposure.

units.obligation_text: A cap shall not be contaminated at a level ≥1 ppm PCB.
units.actor: owner/operator / person responsible for the cap
units.action_summary: Caps must not have PCB contamination at or above 1 ppm.

units.obligation_text: Repairs shall begin within 72 hours of discovery for any breaches which would impair the integrity of the cap.
units.actor: owner/operator / person responsible for the cap
units.action_summary: Repairs to cap breaches that impair integrity must start within 72 hours of discovery.

units.obligation_text: When a cleanup activity conducted under this section includes the use of a fence or a cap, the owner of the site must maintain the fence or cap, in perpetuity.
units.action_summary: Site owner must maintain fence or cap in perpetuity when used in cleanup.

units.obligation_text: Record, in accordance with State law, a notation on the deed to the property, or on some other instrument which is normally examined during a title search, that will in perpetuity notify any potential purchaser of the property: (1) That the land ... has been used for PCB remediation waste disposal ...; (2) Of the existence of the fence or cap and the requirement to maintain the fence or cap, when applicable; and (3) The applicable cleanup levels left at the site, including inside any fence, and/or under any cap, or in a low occupancy area.
units.action_summary: Owner must record a deed notation (or equivalent instrument) that notifies future purchasers of PCB remediation use, existence/maintenance requirement of fence/cap, and applicable cleanup levels.

units.obligation_text: That the land, or the specific portion thereof identified in the instrument when only a portion is subject to the instrument, has been used for PCB remediation waste disposal and, when applicable, that the area is restricted to use as a low occupancy area as defined in § 761.3;
units.action_summary: The deed notation must state that the land (or portion) was used for PCB remediation waste disposal and any low occupancy area restrictions.

units.obligation_text: Of the existence of the fence or cap and the requirement to maintain the fence or cap, when applicable;
units.action_summary: The deed notation must state existence of fence/cap and requirement to maintain it.

units.obligation_text: The applicable cleanup levels left at the site, including inside any fence, and/or under any cap, or in a low occupancy area.
units.action_summary: The deed notation must state the applicable cleanup levels left at the site and in restricted areas.

units.obligation_text: Submit a certification, signed by the owner, that they have recorded the notation specified in paragraph (a)(8)(i)(A) of this section to the EPA Regional Administrator.
units.action_summary: Owner must submit signed certification to EPA Regional Administrator that the deed notation has been recorded.

units.obligation_text: The owner of a site being cleaned up under this section may remove a fence, cap, or low occupancy designation after conducting additional cleanup activities and achieving cleanup levels, specified in paragraph (a)(4) of this section, which do not require a fence, cap, or low occupancy designation.
units.action_summary: Owner may remove fence/cap/low occupancy designation after additional cleanup achieves required cleanup levels.

units.obligation_text: The owner may remove the notice on the deed no earlier than 30 days after achieving the cleanup levels specified in this section which do not require a fence, cap, or low occupancy designation.
units.action_summary: Owner may remove deed notice no sooner than 30 days after achieving cleanup levels that remove need for restrictions.

units.obligation_text: Any person may clean up and dispose of PCB remediation waste at a site in full compliance with the performance-based cleanup provisions of paragraph (b)(1) of this section and disposal provisions of paragraph (b)(2) of this section.
units.action_summary: Persons may use performance-based cleanup and disposal provisions if they fully comply with them.

units.obligation_text: Alternatively, any person may dispose of PCB remediation waste in accordance with paragraph (b)(2) of this section, but such disposal does not relieve the site owner of cleanup and disposal obligations for any PCBs that remain on-site if the provisions of paragraph (b)(1) of this section are not complied with.
units.action_summary: Persons may dispose under (b)(2), but site owner retains cleanup/disposal obligations for remaining PCBs if (b)(1) provisions are not met.

units.obligation_text: The performance-based cleanup option may not be used to clean up: (1) Surface or ground waters; (2) Sediments in marine and freshwater ecosystems; (3) Sewers or sewage treatment systems; (4) Any private or public drinking water sources or distribution systems; (5) Grazing or agricultural lands; (6) Vegetable gardens; (7) Sites which are adjacent to, contain, or are proposed to be redeveloped to contain: Residential dwellings, hospitals, schools, nursing homes, playgrounds, parks, day care centers, endangered species habitats, estuaries, wetlands, national parks, national wildlife refuges, commercial fisheries, sport fisheries, or surface waters; (8) Sites where the PCB contamination is in the 100-year floodplain.
units.action_summary: Performance-based cleanup option is prohibited for the listed site types and locations.

units.obligation_text: The performance-based cleanup provisions shall not be binding upon cleanups conducted under other authorities, including but not limited to, actions conducted under section 104 or section 106 of CERCLA, or section 3004(u) and (v) or section 3008(h) of RCRA.
units.action_summary: Performance-based cleanup provisions do not bind cleanups carried out under specified other authorities.

units.obligation_text: All on-site PCB remediation waste above the following cleanup levels must be disposed of or decontaminated in accordance with paragraph (b)(2) of this section.
units.actor: persons responsible for on-site PCB remediation waste
units.action_summary: On-site PCB remediation waste exceeding specified cleanup levels must be disposed or decontaminated per (b)(2).

units.obligation_text: The cleanup level for bulk PCB remediation waste and porous surfaces is ≤1 ppm PCBs.
units.action_summary: Threshold: bulk PCB remediation waste and porous surfaces must be cleaned to ≤1 ppm PCBs.

units.obligation_text: The cleanup levels for liquids are the concentrations specified in §§ 761.79(b)(1) and (b)(2).
units.action_summary: Threshold: liquid cleanup levels are specified in §761.79(b)(1) and (b)(2).

units.obligation_text: The cleanup levels for nonporous surfaces are the concentrations specified in § 761.79(b)(3).
units.action_summary: Threshold: nonporous surface cleanup levels are specified in §761.79(b)(3).

units.obligation_text: Verification sampling for bulk PCB remediation waste and porous surfaces must be conducted in accordance with Subpart O. Verification sampling for nonporous surfaces must be conducted in accordance with Subpart P. Verification sampling for liquid PCB remediation waste must be conducted in accordance with § 761.269.
units.action_summary: Verification sampling must follow Subpart O for bulk/porous surfaces, Subpart P for nonporous surfaces, and §761.269 for liquid PCB waste.

units.obligation_text: Recordkeeping is required in accordance with § 761.125(c)(5).
units.action_summary: Must keep records as required by §761.125(c)(5).

units.obligation_text: Within 14 days of sending the final shipment of waste offsite for disposal from a site cleaned up under this paragraph, the person in charge of the cleanup or the owner of the property where the PCB remediation waste was located shall notify, in writing, the EPA Regional Administrator, the Director of the State or Tribal environmental protection agency, and the Director of the county or local environmental protection agency where the cleanup was conducted.
units.actor: person in charge of the cleanup or the owner of the property
units.action_summary: Within 14 days of final shipment, the cleanup lead or owner shall notify EPA Regional Administrator and state/tribal/local directors in writing.

units.obligation_text: The notification shall include: (A) Site identification information ...; (B) Disposal facility and shipment information ...; (C) A summary of all applicable components of the records in § 761.125(c)(5); and (D) A certification using the language in § 761.3.
units.actor: person in charge of the cleanup or the owner of the property
units.action_summary: Required notification must include site ID/contact, disposal/shipment info, record summaries, and a certification per §761.3.

units.obligation_text: Any person disposing of liquid PCB remediation waste under this subsection shall do so according to § 761.60(a) or (e), or decontaminate it in accordance with § 761.79.
units.actor: any person disposing of liquid PCB remediation waste under this subsection
units.action_summary: Liquid PCB remediation waste must be disposed per §761.60(a) or (e) or decontaminated per §761.79.

units.obligation_text: Any person disposing of non-liquid PCB remediation waste under this subsection shall do so by one of the following methods: (A) Dispose of it in a high temperature incinerator approved under § 761.70(b), an alternate disposal method approved under § 761.60(e), a chemical waste landfill approved under § 761.75, a facility with a coordinated approval issued under § 761.77, or a hazardous waste landfill permitted by EPA under section 3005 of RCRA, or by a state authorized under section 3006 of RCRA. (B) Decontaminate it in accordance with § 761.79.
units.actor: any person disposing of non-liquid PCB remediation waste under this subsection
units.action_summary: Non-liquid PCB remediation waste must be disposed by one of listed facility/method options or be decontaminated per §761.79.

units.obligation_text: Any person may manage or dispose of material containing <50 ppm PCBs that has been dredged or excavated from waters of the United States: (A) In accordance with a permit issued under section 404 of the Clean Water Act ...; (B) In accordance with a permit issued by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers under section 103 of the Marine Protection, Research, and Sanctuaries Act ...
units.action_summary: Persons may manage/dispose dredged/excavated material <50 ppm PCBs under specified permits (CWA section 404 or MPRSA section 103).

units.obligation_text: Any person wishing to sample, extract, analyze, cleanup, or dispose of PCB remediation waste in a manner other than prescribed in paragraphs (a) or (b) of this section ... must apply in writing to the Regional Administrator in the Region where the ... site is located, ... or to the Director, Office of Resource Conservation and Recovery, for ... more than one EPA Region.
units.actor: any person wishing to conduct activities other than prescribed
units.action_summary: Persons must apply in writing to Regional Administrator or Director to conduct sampling/extraction/analysis/cleanup/disposal in a manner other than prescribed.

units.obligation_text: Each application must include information described in the notification required by paragraph (a)(3) of this section. EPA may request other information that it believes necessary to evaluate the application.
units.action_summary: Applications must include specified notification information; EPA may request additional information as needed.

units.obligation_text: No person may conduct cleanup activities under this paragraph prior to obtaining written approval by EPA.
units.action_summary: Persons are prohibited from conducting such cleanup activities before obtaining written EPA approval.

units.obligation_text: Any person wishing to sample, extract, analyze, or dispose of PCB bulk product waste in a manner other than prescribed in paragraphs (a) or (b) of this section ... must apply in writing to the Regional Administrator ... or to the Director, Office of Resource Conservation and Recovery ...
units.actor: any person wishing to conduct activities other than prescribed
units.action_summary: Persons must apply in writing to the appropriate EPA official to handle PCB bulk product waste in a manner other than prescribed.

units.obligation_text: Each application must contain information indicating that, based on technical, environmental, or waste-specific characteristics or considerations, the proposed sampling, extraction, analysis, disposal, or storage methods or locations will not pose an unreasonable risk or injury to health or the environment. EPA may request other information that it believes necessary to evaluate the application.
units.action_summary: Applications must show proposed methods/locations will not pose unreasonable risk; EPA may request additional information.

units.obligation_text: No person may conduct sampling, extraction, analysis, disposal, or storage activities under this paragraph prior to obtaining written approval by EPA.
units.action_summary: Persons are prohibited from conducting these activities without prior written EPA approval.

units.obligation_text: Bulk product waste described in paragraph (b)(1) of this section may be disposed of as daily landfill cover as long as the daily cover remains in the landfill and is not released or dispersed by wind or other action.
units.actor: any person disposing of bulk product waste
units.action_summary: Bulk product waste may be used as daily landfill cover provided it remains in landfill and is not dispersed.

units.obligation_text: The waste is placed in a pile or non-leaking, covered container designed and operated to control dispersal of the waste by wind, where necessary, by means other than wetting.
units.action_summary: Waste for storage must be placed in a pile or non-leaking covered container designed to control wind dispersal by means other than wetting.

units.obligation_text: The storage site must have: (A) A liner or container that is designed, constructed, and installed to prevent any migration of wastes off or through the liner or container into the adjacent subsurface soil, ground water or surface water at any time during the active life ... The liner or container must be: (1) Constructed of materials that have appropriate chemical properties and sufficient strength and thickness ...; (2) Placed upon a foundation or base capable of providing support ...; (3) In the case of liners, installed to cover all surrounding earth likely to be in contact with the waste.
units.action_summary: Storage sites must have liners/containers that prevent migration and must meet construction, foundation, and installation requirements.

units.obligation_text: A cover that meets the requirements of paragraph (c)(9)(iii)(A) of this section, is installed to cover all of the stored waste likely to be in contact with precipitation, and is secured so as not to be functionally disabled by winds expected under normal seasonal meteorological conditions at the storage site.
units.action_summary: Storage sites must have covers meeting liner requirements, covering waste susceptible to precipitation and secured against expected winds.

units.obligation_text: A commercial storer of PCB waste shall establish financial assurance for closure of each PCB storage facility that they own or operate.
units.action_summary: Commercial storers must establish financial assurance for closure of each PCB storage facility they own or operate.

units.obligation_text: In establishing financial assurance for closure, the commercial storer of PCB waste may choose from the following financial assurance mechanisms or any combination of mechanisms:
units.action_summary: Commercial storer may choose one or more of the listed financial assurance mechanisms to satisfy closure assurance.

units.obligation_text: The submission of a trust agreement with the wording specified in § 264.151(a)(1) of this chapter ... shall be deemed to be in compliance with the requirement to submit a trust agreement under this subpart except when the Regional Administrator specifies modifications for the purposes of implementation under TSCA.
units.action_summary: Submitting a trust agreement with specified wording will be deemed compliant with the trust agreement requirement unless the Regional Administrator specifies modifications.

units.obligation_text: The use of the surety bonds, surety bond instruments, and standby trust agreements specified in §§ 264.143(b) and 264.151(b) of this chapter, with any modifications specified by the Regional Administrator, shall be deemed to be in compliance with this subpart.
units.actor: users of surety bonds and standby trust agreements
units.action_summary: Use of specified surety bonds/instruments/standby trusts (with any Regional Administrator modifications) will be deemed compliant with this subpart.

units.obligation_text: The submission and use of the surety bond instrument specified at § 264.151(c) of this chapter and the standby trust specified at § 264.143(c)(3) of this chapter, with any modifications specified by the Regional Administrator, shall be deemed to be in compliance with the requirements under this subpart relating to the use of surety bonds and standby trust funds.
units.actor: submitters/users of surety bond instrument and standby trust
units.action_summary: Submitting/using the specified surety bond instrument and standby trust (with any Regional Administrator modifications) will be deemed compliant.

ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION AGENCY

40 CFR Part 761

[EPA-HQ-OLEM-2021-0556; FRL-7122-04-OLEM]

Alternate PCB Extraction Methods and Amendments to PCB Cleanup 
and Disposal Regulations; Extension of Comment Period

AGENCY: Environmental Protection Agency (EPA).

ACTION: Notice of proposed rulemaking; extension of comment period.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------

SUMMARY: The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is extending the 
comment period for the proposed rule entitled ``Alternate PCB 
Extraction Methods and Amendments to PCB Cleanup and Disposal 
Regulations.'' EPA published the proposed rule in the Federal Register 
on October 22, 2021, and the public comment period was scheduled to end 
on December 21, 2021. However, EPA has received at least one request 
for additional time to develop and submit comments on the proposal. In 
response to the request for additional time, EPA is extending the 
comment period for an additional 30 days, through January 20, 2022.

DATES: Comments must be received on or before January 20, 2022.

ADDRESSES: You may send comments, identified by Docket ID No. EPA-HQ-
OLEM-2021-0556, by any of the following methods:
    
 Federal eRulemaking Portal: 
https://www.regulations.gov
 
(our preferred method). Follow the online instructions for submitting 
comments. Do not submit electronically any information you consider to 
be Confidential Business Information or other information whose 
disclosure is restricted by statute.
    
 Mail: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, EPA Docket 
Center, OLEM Docket, Mail Code 28221T, 1200 Pennsylvania Avenue NW, 
Washington, DC 20460.
    
 Hand Delivery or Courier (by scheduled appointment only): 
EPA Docket Center, WJC West Building, Room 3334, 1301 Constitution 
Avenue NW, Washington, DC 20004. The Docket Center's hours of 
operations are 8:30 a.m.-4:30 p.m., Monday-Friday (except Federal 
Holidays).
    Instructions: All submissions received must include the Docket ID 
No. for this rulemaking. Comments received may be posted without change 
to 
https://www.regulations.gov/
, including any personal information 
provided. For detailed instructions on sending comments and additional 
information on the rulemaking process, see the ``Public Participation'' 
heading of the SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION section of this document. Out 
of an abundance of caution for members of the public and our staff, the 
EPA Docket Center and Reading Room are open to the public by 
appointment only to reduce the risk of transmitting COVID-19. Our 
Docket Center staff also continues to provide remote customer service 
via email, phone, and webform. Hand deliveries and couriers may be 
received by scheduled appointment only. For further information on EPA 
Docket Center services and the current status, please visit us online 
at 
https://www.epa.gov/dockets
.

FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT: For further information on this 
document, contact Jennifer McLeod, Program Implementation and 
Information Division, Office of Resource Conservation and Recovery, 
(202) 566-0384; email address: 
[email protected]
.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:

I. Summary

    On October 22, 2021 (86 FR 58730), EPA published in the Federal 
Register a proposal to expand the available options for extraction and 
determinative methods used to characterize and verify the cleanup of 
polychlorinated biphenyl (PCB) waste under the federal Toxic Substances 
Control Act (TSCA) regulations (also referred to as the PCB 
regulations). These proposed changes are expected to greatly reduce the 
amount of solvent used in PCB extraction processes, thereby conserving 
resources and reducing waste. In addition, the proposed changes are 
expected to result in quicker, more efficient, and less costly 
cleanups, due to greater flexibility in the cleanup and disposal of PCB 
waste, while still being equally protective of human health and the 
environment. The proposal also included several other amendments to the 
PCB regulations, such as: The amendment of performance-based disposal 
option for PCB remediation waste; the removal of the provision allowing 
PCB bulk product waste to be disposed as roadbed material; the addition 
of more flexible provisions for cleanup and disposal of waste generated 
by spills that occur during emergency situations (e.g., hurricanes or 
floods); the harmonization of the general disposal requirements for PCB 
remediation waste; and other amendments to improve the implementation 
of the regulations, clarify ambiguity and correct technical errors.
    The comment period for the proposed rule was scheduled to end on 
December 21, 2021. Since publication, EPA has received at least one 
request to extend that comment period to allow for additional time to 
develop comments on the proposed rule. After considering this request 
for additional time, EPA has decided to extend the comment period for 
an additional 30 days, through January 20, 2022.

II. Public Participation

    Submit your comments, identified by Docket ID No. EPA-HQ-OLEM-2021-
0556, at 
https://www.regulations.gov
 (our preferred method), or the 
other methods identified in the ADDRESSES section. Once submitted, 
comments cannot be edited or removed from the docket. The EPA may 
publish any comment received to its public docket. Do not submit to 
EPA's docket at 
https://www.regulations.gov
 any information you 
consider to be Confidential Business Information (CBI) or other 
information whose disclosure is restricted by statute. Multimedia 
submissions (audio, video, etc.) must be accompanied by a written 
comment. The written comment is considered the official comment and 
should include discussion of all points you wish to make. The EPA will 
generally not consider comments or comment contents located outside of 
the primary submission (i.e., on the web, cloud, or other file sharing 
system). For additional submission methods, the full EPA public comment 
policy, information about CBI or multimedia submissions, and general 
guidance on making effective comments, please visit 
https://www.epa.gov/dockets/commenting-epa-dockets
.
    Due to public health concerns related to COVID-19, the EPA Docket 
Center and Reading Room are open to the public by appointment only. Our 
Docket Center staff also continues to provide remote customer service 
via email, phone, and webform. Hand deliveries or couriers will be 
received by scheduled appointment only. For further information and 
updates on EPA Docket Center services, please visit us online at 

https://www.epa.gov/dockets
.
    The EPA continues to carefully and continuously monitor information 
from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), local area 
health departments, and our Federal partners so that we can respond 
rapidly as conditions change regarding COVID-19.

title: Pesticide Product Performance Data Requirements for Products Claiming Efficacy Against Certain Invertebrate Pests

units.obligation_text: Each applicant must ensure through testing that their product is efficacious when used in accordance with label directions and commonly accepted pest control practices.
units.action_summary: Ensure product efficacy through testing per label directions and accepted pest control practices

units.obligation_text: The Agency may require, as specified herein and on a case-by-case basis, submission of product performance data for any pesticide product registered or proposed for registration or amendment.
units.action_summary: EPA may require submission of product performance data on a case-by-case basis

units.obligation_text: All product performance testing is performed using the end-use product.
units.action_summary: Use the end-use product for all product performance testing

units.obligation_text: All product performance testing must report the species tested.
units.action_summary: Report the species used in all product performance testing

units.obligation_text: All products are to be tested to support the claim(s) made on the labeling of the pesticide product.
units.action_summary: Test products to support labeling claims

units.obligation_text: To determine the specific product performance data required to support the registration of each pesticide product, the applicant must refer to the applicable sections of this subpart.
units.action_summary: Refer to applicable sections of Subpart R to determine required product performance data

units.obligation_text: Each product that bears a claim subject to this subpart, must be supported by submission of product performance data, as listed in this subpart.
units.action_summary: Support any claim subject to this subpart with submission of product performance data

units.obligation_text: This product performance data must be submitted with any application for registration or amended registration.
units.action_summary: Submit product performance data with any registration or amendment application

units.obligation_text: For the pest-specific claims listed in this subpart, data must be for the species specified to support the claim.
units.action_summary: Provide data specific to the species identified for the pest-specific claim

units.obligation_text: The claim stated on the pesticide product labeling (such as knockdown, control, mortality, or repellency) determines the performance standard that must be met.
units.action_summary: Meet the performance standard dictated by the product labeling claim

units.obligation_text: In the absence of specific pest/labeling claims/performance standards specified in §§ 158.1708 through 158.1799, the performance standards of paragraphs (b) and (c) of this section apply.
units.action_summary: Default to performance standards in paragraphs (b) and (c) when no specific standards are provided elsewhere

units.obligation_text: For skin-applied insect repellent labeling claims, the performance standard must be greater than or equal to 2-hours complete protection time.
units.action_summary: Achieve a performance standard of at least 2 hours complete protection time for skin-applied insect repellents

units.obligation_text: Any testing required under this part which involves any human subjects must comply with all applicable requirements under 40 CFR part 26.
units.action_summary: Comply with 40 CFR part 26 for any testing involving human subjects

units.obligation_text: Protocols for such testing must be submitted to EPA for review prior to study initiation.
units.action_summary: Submit protocols involving human-subjects testing to EPA for review before starting the study

units.obligation_text: Those protocols determined by EPA to involve intentional exposure of human subjects also require review by EPA’s Human Studies Review Board (HSRB)) prior to study initiation.
units.action_summary: Protocols involving intentional human exposure require HSRB review before initiation

units.obligation_text: If you are uncertain about the applicability of the 40 CFR part 26 requirements to this 40 CFR part 158 testing requirement or uncertain about the nature of your planned testing (such as, for example, whether the testing would involve intentional exposure of human subjects or whether the testing would be an observational study), you should contact the Agency prior to initiating the testing.
units.action_summary: Contact EPA prior to initiating testing if uncertain about applicability of 40 CFR part 26 or nature of planned testing

units.obligation_text: Unless otherwise specified in §§ 158.1710 through 158.1786, for pesticides other than skin-applied insect repellents, the performance standard for a product performance claim against a pest must be greater than or equal to 90 percent, except for non-wearable spatial repellents where the performance standard is greater than or equal to 75 percent.
units.actor: applicants/registrants (products making claims other than skin-applied repellents)
units.action_summary: Achieve ≥90% performance standard for most product claims; ≥75% for non-wearable spatial repellents

units.obligation_text: In instances where there is a conflict between one of the Harmonized Test Guidelines and the provisions of this subpart, this subpart will control.
units.action_summary: When conflicting, provisions of Subpart R control over Harmonized Test Guidelines

units.obligation_text: Data requirements may, on a case-by-case basis, be adjusted by EPA in response to requests for novel technologies or products that have unusual physical, chemical, or biological properties or atypical use patterns which would make a particular data requirement, or data performance standard, inappropriate.
units.action_summary: EPA may adjust data requirements case-by-case for novel or atypical products

units.obligation_text: Requests for such data requirement modifications must be submitted the same manner as waiver requests submitted under 40 CFR 158.45.
units.action_summary: Submit requests for data requirement modifications in the same manner as 40 CFR 158.45 waiver requests

units.obligation_text: EPA will respond in writing to those requests.
units.action_summary: EPA will provide a written response to requests for data requirement modifications

units.obligation_text: The Agency may modify data requirements it finds are inappropriate for the pesticide in question,
units.action_summary: EPA may modify data requirements deemed inappropriate for a given pesticide

units.obligation_text: The Agency will ensure that sufficient data are available to make the determinations required by the applicable statutory standards.
units.action_summary: EPA must ensure sufficient data are available to meet statutory determinations

units.obligation_text: If an application for registration or amended registration requests a labeling claim for effectiveness against an invasive invertebrate species, then on a case-by-case basis, EPA may require submission of product performance data and establish performance standards for those data to support those claims for effectiveness.
units.action_summary: EPA may require product performance data and set standards for invasive species claims on a case-by-case basis

units.obligation_text: Applications for registration or amended registration requests for a labeling claim for the emerald ash borer, Agrilus planipennis, or Asian longhorned beetle, Anoplophora glabripennis, must be accompanied by product performance data to support those claims for effectiveness.
units.action_summary: Include product performance data to support claims for emerald ash borer or Asian longhorned beetle

units.obligation_text: If an application for registration or amended registration requests a labeling claim specific to a disease vector (such as repels mosquitoes that may carry West Nile virus), then submission of testing conducted with the species specific to the disease vector claim and subject to specific performance standards is required even if the test species is not specifically required in §§ 158.1712 through 158.1786.
units.action_summary: Submit testing using the species specific to the disease vector claim, meeting applicable standards

units.obligation_text: If an application for registration or amended registration requests a labeling claim specific to a structural or wood-destroying pest not identified in §§ 158.1782 through 158.1786, EPA may require submission of product performance data, with testing on that specific pest and subject to specific performance standards, to support those claims for effectiveness.
units.action_summary: EPA may require product performance data with testing on the specific structural or wood-destroying pest not listed elsewhere

units.obligation_text: The tables and test notes in this section apply to dust, human itch or scabies, and dog follicle mites. The claim stated on the pesticide product labeling determines the required test species. The required test species for a specific type of mite claim appear in paragraph (b) of this section and the required performance standards appear in paragraph (c) of this section.
units.action_summary: Labeling claim determines required test species and associated performance standards for mite claims

units.obligation_text: Dog follicle mite (Demodex canis).
units.action_summary: Test on Demodex canis for dog follicle mite claims

units.obligation_text: Testing on one of the following species is required: American house dust mite (Dermatophagoides farinae) OR European house dust mite (Dermatophagoides pteronyssinus).
units.action_summary: Test on one of the specified dust mite species to support a dust mite claim

units.obligation_text: Human itch mite (Sarcoptes scabiei).
units.action_summary: Test on Sarcoptes scabiei for human itch or scabies mite claims

units.obligation_text: For the dog follicle mite, a performance standard of 100 percent is required.
units.actor: applicants/registrants (products making dog follicle mite claims)
units.action_summary: Meet a 100% performance standard for dog follicle mite claims

units.obligation_text: For the human itch or scabies mite, a performance standard of 100 percent is required.
units.actor: applicants/registrants (products making human itch/scabies mite claims)
units.action_summary: Meet a 100% performance standard for human itch or scabies mite claims

units.obligation_text: If the pesticide product labeling makes a claim against chiggers, then testing is required using the following test species: Chigger (Trombicula alfreddugesi).
units.action_summary: Test on Trombicula alfreddugesi to support a chigger claim

units.obligation_text: The table and test notes in this section apply to hard ticks (including cattle ticks) and soft ticks. The claim stated on the pesticide product labeling determines the required test species. ... For a claim against any specific species of 'ticks' that individual species and all the listed representative species for 'ticks' must be tested, but not the representative species for cattle ticks or soft ticks.
units.action_summary: Labeling claim determines required test species; specific species plus listed representative tick species must be tested as specified

units.obligation_text: Testing on a total of three hard tick species is required: Blacklegged tick (Ixodes scapularis) AND Lone star tick (Amblyomma americanum) AND one of the following three species: American dog tick (Dermacentor variabilis) OR Brown dog tick (Rhipicephalus sanguineus) OR Rocky Mountain wood tick (Dermacentor andersoni).
units.action_summary: Test on specified three hard tick species (two fixed species plus one selected from three alternatives)

units.obligation_text: Testing on one of the following species is required: Southern cattle tick (Rhipicephalus microplus) OR Cattle fever tick (Rhipicephalus annulatus).
units.action_summary: Test on one of the specified cattle tick species for cattle tick claims

units.obligation_text: Soft tick (Ornithodoros hermsi).
units.action_summary: Test on Ornithodoros hermsi for soft tick claims

units.obligation_text: For products applied to dogs, testing is required on three species: Blacklegged tick (Ixodes scapularis), American dog tick (Dermacentor variabilis), and Brown dog tick (Rhipicephalus sanguineus).
units.action_summary: For canine products, test on the three specified tick species

units.obligation_text: For products applied to cats, testing is required on three species: Blacklegged tick (Ixodes scapularis), Lone star tick (Amblyomma americanum), and American dog tick (Dermacentor variabilis).
units.action_summary: For feline products, test on the three specified tick species

units.obligation_text: If the pesticide product labeling makes a claim against scorpions, then testing is required using the following test species: Striped bark scorpion (Centruroides vittatus).
units.action_summary: Test on Centruroides vittatus for scorpion claims

units.obligation_text: The table in this section applies to spiders. The product labeling claim determines the required test species.
units.action_summary: Labeling claim determines required spider test species as specified in the table

units.obligation_text: Testing on two species is required: Brown recluse spider (Loxosceles reclusa) AND one of the following species is required: Northern black widow spider (Latrodectus variolus) OR Southern black widow spider (Latrodectus mactans) OR Western black widow spider (Latrodectus hesperus).
units.action_summary: For spider pest group claims, test on L. reclusa and one of the specified black widow species

units.obligation_text: Testing on one of the following species is required: Northern black widow spider (Latrodectus variolus) OR Southern black widow spider (Latrodectus mactans) OR Western black widow spider (Latrodectus hesperus).
units.action_summary: For black widow sub-group claims, test on one of the specified black widow species

units.obligation_text: Brown recluse spider (Loxosceles reclusa).
units.action_summary: Test on Loxosceles reclusa for a brown recluse spider claim

units.obligation_text: Brown widow spider (Latrodectus geometricus).
units.action_summary: Test on Latrodectus geometricus for a brown widow spider claim

units.obligation_text: Northern black widow spider (Latrodectus variolus); Southern black widow spider (Latrodectus mactans); Western black widow spider (Latrodectus hesperus).
units.action_summary: Test on the specified black widow species for pest-specific claims

units.obligation_text: The table in this section applies to centipedes. The product labeling claim determines the required test species. The required test species for a labeling claim appears in paragraph (b) of the section.
units.action_summary: Labeling claim determines required centipede test species per the table

units.obligation_text: Testing on one of the following species is required: House centipede (Scutigera coleoptrata) OR Florida blue centipede (Hemiscolopendra marginata) OR Scolopendra sp.
units.action_summary: Test on one of the specified centipede species for centipede claims

units.obligation_text: The table in this section applies to human lice. The product labeling claim determines the required test species. The required test species for a labeling claim appears in paragraph (b) of this section. The required performance standards appear in paragraph (c) of this section.
units.action_summary: Labeling claim determines required lice test species and performance standards

units.obligation_text: Testing on one of the following species is required: Head louse (Pediculus humanus capitis) OR Body louse (Pediculus humanus humanus).
units.action_summary: Test on head or body louse species for lice claims

units.obligation_text: For labeling claims against lice, a performance standard of 100 percent is required.
units.action_summary: Achieve a 100% performance standard for lice labeling claims

units.obligation_text: The table in this section applies to fleas. The product labeling claim determines the required test species. The required test species for a labeling claim appears in paragraph (b) of this section.
units.action_summary: Labeling claim determines required flea test species per the table

units.obligation_text: Testing on the following species is required: Cat flea (Ctenocephalides felis).
units.action_summary: Test on Ctenocephalides felis for flea pest group claims

units.obligation_text: Pest-specific testing required for cat flea (Ctenocephalides felis); chigoe flea (Tunga penetrans); dog flea (Ctenocephalides canis); hen flea (Ceratophyllus gallinae); human flea (Pulex irritans); oriental rat flea (Xenopsylla cheopis).
units.action_summary: Test on the specified flea species for respective pest-specific claims

units.obligation_text: The table in this section applies to cockroaches. The product labeling claim determines the required test species. The required test species for a labeling claim appears in paragraph (b) of this section.
units.action_summary: Labeling claim determines required cockroach test species

units.obligation_text: Testing on two species is required: American cockroach (Periplaneta americana) AND German cockroach (Blattella germanica).
units.action_summary: For cockroach pest group claims, test on American and German cockroaches

units.obligation_text: Testing on the listed species is required for pest-specific claims: American cockroach; Australian cockroach; Brown cockroach; Brownbanded cockroach; German cockroach; Oriental cockroach; Smokybrown cockroach; Turkestan cockroach.
units.action_summary: Test on the specified species for corresponding pest-specific cockroach claims

units.obligation_text: The table in this section applies to keds, screwworms, and bot flies. The product labeling claim determines the required test species. The required test species for labeling claims appear in paragraph (b) of this section.
units.action_summary: Labeling claim determines required test species for keds, screwworms, and bot flies

units.obligation_text: Testing is required on one of the following species: Horse bot fly (Gasterophilus intestinalis) OR Throat bot fly (Gasterophilus nasalis) OR Nose bot fly (Gasterophilus haemorrhoidalis).
units.action_summary: Test on one of the specified bot fly species for bot fly claims

units.obligation_text: Human bot fly (Dermatobia hominis).
units.action_summary: Test on Dermatobia hominis for human bot fly claims

units.obligation_text: Testing is required on the following species: Sheep ked (Melophagus ovinus).
units.action_summary: Test on Melophagus ovinus for ked claims

units.obligation_text: Testing is required on one of the following species: Screwworm (Cochliomyia hominivorax) OR Secondary screwworm (Cochliomyia macellaria).
units.action_summary: Test on one of the specified screwworm species for screwworm claims

units.obligation_text: The table in this section applies to filth flies. The product labeling claim determines the required test species. The required test species for a labeling claim against filth flies or specific species of filth flies appear in paragraph (b) of this section.
units.action_summary: Labeling claim determines required filth fly test species

units.obligation_text: Testing on two species is required: House fly (Musca domestica) AND one of the following species is required: Flesh fly (Sarcophaga sp., Wohlfahrtia sp., and other genera of flesh flies) OR Blow fly (Phaenicia sp., Calliphora sp., and other genera of blow flies).
units.action_summary: For filth fly group claims, test on house fly and one flesh fly or blow fly species

units.obligation_text: Testing on the listed species is required for pest-specific filth fly claims: Blow fly; Cluster fly; Face fly; Flesh fly; House fly; Little house fly.
units.action_summary: Test on the specified filth fly species for corresponding pest-specific claims

units.obligation_text: The tables and test notes in this section apply to mosquitoes. The required test species for a labeling claim against mosquitoes appears in paragraph (b) of this section. For a claim against any specific species of mosquito, that individual species and all the required test genera must be tested.
units.action_summary: Labeling claim determines mosquito test species; specific-species claims require testing that species and required genera

units.obligation_text: Testing in three genera (Culex, Aedes, and Anopheles) of mosquitoes is required: one of the specified Culex species AND one of the specified Aedes species AND one of the specified Anopheles species.
units.action_summary: Test in Culex, Aedes, and Anopheles genera by selecting one species from each list to support mosquito claims

units.obligation_text: The tables in this section apply to biting flies, which includes biting midges and black flies. The product labeling claim determines the required test species.
units.action_summary: Labeling claim determines required biting fly test species

units.obligation_text: Testing is required on three species: Stable fly (Stomoxys calcitrans) AND one of the large biting fly species (Black horse fly (Tabanus atratus) OR Deer fly (Chrysops sp.) OR Striped horse fly (Tabanus lineola)) AND one of the small biting fly species (Biting midge (Culicoides sp.) OR Black fly (Simulium sp. or Prosimulium sp.) OR Black gnat (Leptoconops sp.)).
units.action_summary: For biting fly group claims, test on stable fly plus one large biting fly and one small biting fly from specified choices

units.obligation_text: Testing is required on two species: Stable fly (Stomoxys calcitrans) AND one of the following species: Black horse fly (Tabanus atratus) OR Deer fly (Chrysops sp.) OR Striped horse fly (Tabanus lineola).
units.action_summary: For large biting fly subgroup claims, test on stable fly and one large biting fly species

units.obligation_text: Testing is required on one of the following species: Biting midge (Culicoides sp.) OR Black fly (Simulium sp. OR Prosimulium sp.) OR Black gnat (Leptoconops sp.).
units.action_summary: For small biting fly subgroup claims, test on one of the specified small biting fly species

units.obligation_text: Testing on the listed species is required for pest-specific biting fly claims: Biting midges (Culicoides sp.); Black flies (Simulium sp. or Prosimulium sp.); Black gnats (Leptoconops sp.); Deer flies (Chrysops sp.); Greenhead (Tabanus nigrovittatus); Horn fly (Haematobia irritans); Horse flies (Tabanidae as specified); Sand flies (Lutzomyia sp. OR Phlebotomus sp.); Stable fly (Stomoxys calcitrans).
units.action_summary: Test on the specified biting fly species for corresponding pest-specific claims

units.obligation_text: The table in this section applies to bed bugs. The product labeling claim determines the required test species. The required test species for a labeling claim appears in paragraph (b) of this section.
units.action_summary: Labeling claim determines required bed bug test species

units.obligation_text: Common bed bug (Cimex lectularius).
units.action_summary: Test on Cimex lectularius for bed bug claims

units.obligation_text: The table in this section applies to Conenose bugs and Kissing bugs. The product labeling claim determines the required test species. The required test species for a labeling claim appears in paragraph (b) of this section.
units.action_summary: Labeling claim determines required test species for conenose and kissing bugs

units.obligation_text: Conenose bug (Triatoma sanguisuga).
units.action_summary: Test on Triatoma sanguisuga for conenose bug claims

units.obligation_text: Kissing bug (Triatoma protracta).
units.action_summary: Test on Triatoma protracta for kissing bug claims

units.obligation_text: The table in this section applies to ants (excluding carpenter ants). The product labeling claim determines the required test species. The required test species for labeling claims appear in paragraph (b) of this section.
units.action_summary: Labeling claim determines required ant test species (excluding carpenter ants)

units.obligation_text: Testing is required on the following two species: Pharaoh ant (Monomorium pharaonis) AND Red imported fire ant (Solenopsis invicta).
units.action_summary: For ant pest group claims, test on pharaoh ant and red imported fire ant

units.section: § 158.1776(b) - Pest Sub-Group Claim (Fire and Harvester / Fire ants)
units.obligation_text: Testing is required on the following species: Red imported fire ant (Solenopsis invicta).
units.action_summary: Test on red imported fire ant for fire and harvester/firing ant subgroup claims

units.obligation_text: Testing on the listed species is required for pest-specific ant claims (European fire ant; Harvester ant; Pharaoh ant; Red imported fire ant; Southern fire ant; Tropical fire ant; Black imported fire ant).
units.action_summary: Test on the specified ant species for respective pest-specific claims

units.obligation_text: For colony claims, testing must be done specific to the species listed. For colony claims against the red and/or black imported fire ants, testing may be done on, S. invicta, S. richteri, or their hybrid.
units.action_summary: Colony claims require species-specific testing; for red/black imported fire ants, testing may be on S. invicta, S. richteri, or hybrid

units.obligation_text: For bait products or claims involving outdoor use, the group and sub-group claims in paragraph (b) of this section are for direct kill and residual surface application claims against foraging ants only (excluding colony claims). For bait products or claims involving outdoor use, testing must be specific to the species listed.
units.action_summary: For bait/outdoor use claims, testing must be species-specific and the group/sub-group claims apply only to foraging ant direct kill/residual surface claims

units.obligation_text: The table in this section applies to bees, wasps, yellowjackets, and hornets. The labeling claim determines the required test species. The required test species for labeling claims appear in paragraph (b) of this section.
units.action_summary: Labeling claim determines required test species for bees, wasps, yellowjackets, and hornets

units.section: § 158.1780(b) - Pest Group Claims (Bees, Wasps, Yellowjackets, and Hornets)
units.obligation_text: Testing on three species is required: Two Yellowjacket species (one Vespula sp. AND the Bald-faced hornet (Dolichovespula maculata)) AND one Paper wasp (Polistes sp.).
units.action_summary: For group claims against bees/wasps/yellowjackets/hornets, test on two yellowjacket species (one Vespula and Dolichovespula maculata) and one Polistes species

units.obligation_text: Testing on the listed species is required for pest-specific claims: Bald-faced hornet (Dolichovespula maculata); Mud dauber wasp (Sphecidae sp.); Paper wasp (Polistes sp.); Yellowjacket (Vespula sp.).
units.action_summary: Test on the specified bee/wasp species for corresponding pest-specific claims

units.obligation_text: For colony claims, except Vespula spp., testing must be specific to the species listed. Acceptable data for any Vespula species may support a yellowjacket colony claim for ground nesting Vespula species; however, species-specific claims need to be supported by data from testing of the specific species. Colony claims against Vespula spp. have a performance standard of 100%.
units.action_summary: Colony claims require species-specific testing except Vespula spp. where acceptable data from any Vespula may support ground-nesting claims; Vespula colony claims require 100% performance

units.obligation_text: The table in this section applies to carpenter ants. The product labeling claim determines the required test species. The required test species for labeling claims appear in paragraph (b) of this section. The required performance standards appear in paragraph (c) of this section.
units.action_summary: Labeling claim determines required test species and performance standards for carpenter ant claims

units.obligation_text: Testing on one of the following carpenter ant species is required: Black carpenter ant (Camponotus pennsylvanicus) OR Florida carpenter ant (Camponotus floridanus) OR Western carpenter ant (Camponotus modoc).
units.action_summary: Test on one of the specified carpenter ant species for carpenter ant claims

units.obligation_text: Bait Treatment — 95% prevention of damage to wood for ≥3 years.
units.action_summary: For bait treatments claiming carpenter ant protection, demonstrate 95% prevention of wood damage for at least 3 years

units.obligation_text: Non-Structural: Wood Preservative Treatment — 100% prevention of damage to wood for ≥2 years.
units.action_summary: For non-structural wood preservative treatments, demonstrate 100% prevention of wood damage for at least 2 years

units.obligation_text: Structural Protection — 95% prevention of damage to wood ≥5 years.
units.action_summary: For structural protection claims, demonstrate 95% prevention of wood damage for at least 5 years

title: Withdrawal of Proposed Rules; Discontinuing Three Rulemaking Efforts Listed in the Semiannual Regulatory Agenda

units.obligation_text: For obligated parties that meet the requirements for a small refinery under § 80.1441(e)(2)(iii), for the 2019 compliance year, reports required under this section must be submitted to the EPA no later than June 1, 2022.
units.actor: obligated parties that meet the requirements for a small refinery under § 80.1441(e)(2)(iii)
units.action_summary: Submit reports required under this section for the 2019 compliance year to EPA by June 1, 2022.

units.obligation_text: For obligated parties, for the 2020 compliance year, reports required under this section must be submitted no later than June 1, 2022.
units.action_summary: Submit reports required under this section for the 2020 compliance year by June 1, 2022.

units.obligation_text: For RIN-generating renewable fuel producers, RIN-generating importers of renewable fuel, and other parties owning RINs, for the 2020 compliance year, reports required under this section shall be submitted to the EPA no later than June 1, 2022.
units.actor: RIN-generating renewable fuel producers, RIN-generating importers of renewable fuel, and other parties owning RINs
units.action_summary: Submit reports required under this section for the 2020 compliance year to EPA by June 1, 2022.

title: Toxic Substances Control Act Reporting and Recordkeeping Requirements for Perfluoroalkyl and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances

units.obligation_text: This part specifies reporting and recordkeeping procedures for manufacturers (including importers) of certain per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (hereafter referred to as PFAS) under section 8(a)(7) of the Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA).
units.action_summary: Follow the reporting and recordkeeping procedures established in this part under TSCA section 8(a)(7) for PFAS.

units.obligation_text: The requirements of this part apply to all chemical substances and mixtures that are PFAS, consistent with the definition of PFAS at § 705.3.
units.actor: Persons subject to this part (e.g., manufacturers, importers, processors of PFAS)
units.action_summary: All PFAS chemical substances and mixtures are covered by the requirements in this part.

units.obligation_text: Persons who must report.
units.action_summary: Certain persons are required to submit reports under this part.

units.obligation_text: Recordkeeping requirements.
units.actor: Persons subject to this part (e.g., manufacturers and importers of PFAS)
units.action_summary: Maintain records as required by this part.

units.obligation_text: Imported chemical substances are never site-limited.
units.action_summary: Imported chemical substances cannot be classified as site-limited.

units.obligation_text: Intended for use by children means the chemical substance or mixture is used in or on a product that is specifically intended for use by children age 14 or younger. A chemical substance or mixture is intended for use by children when the submitter answers "yes" to at least one of the following questions for the product into which the submitter’s chemical substance or mixture is incorporated:
units.action_summary: A submitter must answer the listed questions; if any is answered 'yes', the substance/mixture is classified as intended for use by children (age 14 or younger).

units.obligation_text: Is the product commonly recognized (i.e., by a reasonable person) as being intended for children age 14 or younger?
units.action_summary: If the product is commonly recognized as intended for children 14 or younger, the submitter must indicate 'yes' and the chemical is considered intended for use by children.

units.obligation_text: Does the manufacturer of the product state through product labeling or other written materials that the product is intended for or will be used by children age 14 or younger?
units.action_summary: If product labeling or written materials state the product is intended for children 14 or younger, the submitter must indicate 'yes' and the chemical is considered intended for use by children.

units.obligation_text: Is the advertising, promotion, or marketing of the product aimed at children age 14 or younger?
units.action_summary: If advertising, promotion, or marketing is aimed at children 14 or younger, the submitter must indicate 'yes' and the chemical is considered intended for use by children.

TSCA Section 8(a)(7) Reporting and Recordkeeping Requirements for 
Perfluoroalkyl and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances; Extension of Comment 
Period

AGENCY: Environmental Protection Agency (EPA).

ACTION: Proposed rule; extension of comment period.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------

SUMMARY: EPA issued a proposed rule in the Federal Register of June 28, 
2021, concerning reporting and recordkeeping requirements for Per- and 
Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS) under the Toxic Substances Control 
Act (TSCA). This document extends the comment period for 31 days, from 
August 27, 2021 to September 27, 2021. An extension of the comment 
period was requested by some stakeholders to allow interested parties

units.obligation_text: Do not submit information that you consider to be CBI or otherwise protected through https://www.regulations.gov or email.

units.obligation_text: EPA will accept comments on the proposal to partially delete this site for thirty (30) days after publication of this document in the Federal Register.
units.action_summary: EPA will accept public comments on the proposed partial deletion for 30 days following publication.

units.obligation_text: In accordance with 40 CFR 300.425(e), sites may be deleted from the NPL where no further response is appropriate.
units.action_summary: EPA may delete NPL sites when no further response is appropriate under 40 CFR 300.425(e).

units.obligation_text: Responsible parties or other persons have implemented all appropriate response actions required;
units.action_summary: Deletion criterion: responsible parties/persons have implemented all required appropriate response actions.

units.obligation_text: All appropriate Fund-financed response under CERCLA has been implemented, and no further response action by responsible parties is appropriate;
units.action_summary: Deletion criterion: all appropriate Fund-financed CERCLA responses have been implemented and no further response by responsible parties is appropriate.

units.obligation_text: The remedial investigation has shown that the release poses no significant threat to public health or the environment and, therefore, the taking of remedial measures is not appropriate.
units.action_summary: Deletion criterion: the remedial investigation demonstrates no significant threat, so remedial measures are not appropriate.

units.obligation_text: Pursuant to CERCLA section 121(c) and the NCP, EPA conducts five-year reviews to ensure the continued protectiveness of remedial actions where hazardous substances, pollutants, or contaminants remain at a site above levels that allow for unlimited use and unrestricted exposure.
units.action_summary: EPA must conduct five-year reviews at sites where contamination remains above levels allowing unrestricted use/exposure to ensure remedy protectiveness.

units.obligation_text: The following procedures apply to the deletion or partial deletion of the sites in this proposed rule:
units.action_summary: Introductory statement: the listed procedures govern deletion/partial deletion of sites in this rule.

units.obligation_text: (1) EPA consulted with the respective state before developing this Notice of Intent for deletion.
units.action_summary: EPA consulted with the relevant state prior to developing the Notice of Intent for deletion.

units.obligation_text: (2) EPA has provided the state 30 working days for review of this proposed action prior to publication of it today.
units.action_summary: EPA provided the state 30 working days to review the proposed deletion prior to publication.

units.obligation_text: (3) In accordance with the criteria discussed above, EPA has determined that no further response is appropriate.
units.action_summary: EPA has determined, per the stated criteria, that no further response is appropriate for the site/portion proposed for deletion.

units.obligation_text: (4) The state, through their designated state agency, has concurred with the proposed deletion action.
units.action_summary: The state's designated agency has concurred with the proposed deletion.

units.obligation_text: (5) Concurrently, with the publication of this Notice of Intent for deletion in the Federal Register, a notice is being published in a major local newspaper of general circulation near the site.
units.action_summary: A local newspaper notice is being published at the same time as the Federal Register Notice of Intent.

units.obligation_text: (6) The EPA placed copies of documents supporting the proposed deletion in the deletion docket, made these items available for public inspection, and copying at the Regional Records Center identified above.
units.action_summary: EPA placed supporting documents in the deletion docket and made them available for public inspection and copying at the Regional Records Center.

units.obligation_text: If comments are received within the 30-day comment period on this document, EPA will evaluate and respond accordingly to the comments before making a final decision to delete or partially delete the site.
units.action_summary: If timely comments are received, EPA will evaluate and respond to them prior to issuing a final deletion decision.

units.obligation_text: If necessary, EPA will prepare a Responsiveness Summary to address any significant public comments received.
units.action_summary: EPA will prepare a Responsiveness Summary addressing significant public comments if necessary.

units.obligation_text: After the public comment period, if EPA determines it is still appropriate to delete or partially delete the site, the EPA will publish a final Notice of Deletion or Partial Deletion in the Federal Register.
units.action_summary: Following the comment period, if deletion is still appropriate, EPA will publish a final Notice of Deletion or Partial Deletion in the Federal Register.

units.obligation_text: EPA may initiate further action to ensure continued protectiveness at a deleted site if new information becomes available that indicates it is appropriate.
units.action_summary: EPA may take additional remedial actions at a deleted site if new information indicates such action is appropriate.

units.obligation_text: Whenever there is a significant release from a site deleted from the NPL, the deleted site may be restored to the NPL without application of the hazard ranking system.
units.action_summary: If a significant release occurs from a deleted site, EPA may restore the site to the NPL without using the hazard ranking system.
