title: Tribal Implementation Plan: Northern Cheyenne Tribe

units.obligation_text: Subject to paragraph (b) of this section, hearings will be conducted by Copyright Royalty Judges sitting en banc.
units.action_summary: Hearings must be conducted by Copyright Royalty Judges sitting en banc.

units.obligation_text: Hearings will be conducted in person at the Library of Congress or an alternative location, or virtually, at the Judges’ discretion.
units.action_summary: Hearings must be held in person at the Library of Congress or an alternative location, or virtually, as determined by the Judges.

units.obligation_text: For a tribe to receive EPA approval of a TIP, the tribe must, among other things, obtain a determination from the EPA that the tribe is eligible for TAS for purposes of the TIP and submit to the EPA a TIP that satisfies requirements of the Act and relevant regulations that apply to the plan elements and functions the tribe seeks to carry out.
units.action_summary: A tribe must obtain an EPA TAS determination and submit a TIP that meets the Act's and applicable regulations' requirements to receive EPA approval.

units.obligation_text: The memorandum of agreement shall include a process by which the tribe will provide potential investigative leads to the EPA and/or other appropriate federal agencies in an appropriate and timely manner.
units.actor: the memorandum of agreement (parties to the MOA)
units.action_summary: The MOA must include a process for the tribe to provide potential investigative leads to EPA or other federal agencies in a timely manner.

units.section: IV. Tribal Implementation Plan Requirements (criminal enforcement assignment)
units.obligation_text: Where implementation of the TIP requires criminal enforcement authority, and to the extent a tribe is precluded from asserting such authority, the federal government will exercise primary criminal enforcement responsibility.
units.action_summary: If a tribe cannot exercise criminal enforcement authority, the federal government will assume primary criminal enforcement responsibility.

units.obligation_text: The proposed TIP establishes a general prohibition on open burning on the Reservation (see NCCAA Section 5.1), unless otherwise exempted under NCCAA Section 5.2 or is permitted under NCCAA Section 5.7.
units.action_summary: Open burning on the Reservation is generally prohibited except as exempted or permitted.

units.obligation_text: Open burning for cultural, traditional, or spiritual purposes or open burning activity that is less than four feet in diameter and less than three feet in height (is exempted).
units.action_summary: Open burning for cultural/traditional/spiritual purposes or small fires under specified dimensions are exempt from the general prohibition.

units.obligation_text: The Tribe reserves the right to issue burn bans, per NCCAA Section 5.6.
units.action_summary: The Tribe may issue burn bans on the Reservation.

units.obligation_text: The Tribe ... prohibits the burning of listed materials in NCCAA Section 5.4 (unless authorized for training fires).
units.action_summary: Burning of listed materials is prohibited, except when authorized for training fires.

units.obligation_text: Burning of listed materials is prohibited unless authorized for training fires.
units.action_summary: An exception allows burning listed materials if specifically authorized for training fires.

units.obligation_text: Permits are required for open burning activity on the Reservation that is four or more feet in diameter or three or more feet in height (unless exempted under NCCAA Section 5.2) prior to commencing open burning activities.
units.action_summary: A permit must be obtained before commencing open burning activities that meet or exceed the specified size thresholds.

units.obligation_text: Permits may be issued only if the Air Quality Administrator determines, in consultation with the appropriate Bureau of Indian Affairs, Northern Cheyenne Agency personnel, that the proposed open burning activity will not cause an adverse impact on Reservation air quality or otherwise endanger public health or welfare on the Reservation.
units.action_summary: The Air Quality Administrator may issue a permit only after determining, with BIA consultation, that the burn will not adversely affect air quality or public health/welfare.

units.obligation_text: Permits are also required to contain certain minimum permit conditions, including setback requirements, equipment and supply requirements, wind speed limitations, and extinguishment conditions.
units.action_summary: Permits must include specified minimum conditions such as setbacks, equipment/supplies, wind limits, and extinguishment requirements.

units.obligation_text: Violations of any applicable permit terms or conditions are considered violations of the NCCAA.
units.action_summary: Breaching permit terms constitutes a violation of the tribal Clean Air Act.

units.section: NCCAA Section 5.7 (notification to Air Quality Administrator)
units.obligation_text: For all permitted open burning activities, the permittee must notify the Air Quality Administrator at least two working days prior to commencing an open burning activity.
units.action_summary: Permittee must notify the Air Quality Administrator at least two working days before starting permitted open burning.

units.obligation_text: For all permitted open burning activities, the permittee must notify Northern Cheyenne Fire Protection not less than one hour prior to commencing the open burning activity (during regular business hours).
units.action_summary: Permittee must notify Northern Cheyenne Fire Protection at least one hour before starting permitted open burning (during regular business hours).

units.obligation_text: No person shall commence or continue an open burning activity within the Reservation that is determined by the Director of the Tribe’s DEPNR, in consultation with the Air Quality Administrator, to cause or contribute to an exceedance of any Northern Cheyenne Ambient Air Quality Standard.
units.action_summary: Persons must not start or continue burns that the DEPNR Director (with AQ Administrator consultation) determines will cause or contribute to air quality standard exceedances.

units.obligation_text: Under the TIP, the Tribe’s Air Quality Administrator can issue compliance orders for TIP violations.
units.action_summary: The Air Quality Administrator is authorized to issue compliance orders for violations.

units.obligation_text: A compliance order can include civil penalties up to $5,000 per day for each violation and an assessment of costs incurred by DEPNR.
units.action_summary: Compliance orders may impose civil penalties up to $5,000 per day per violation and recover DEPNR costs.

units.obligation_text: The Air Quality Administrator can file an action in Northern Cheyenne Tribal Court pursuant to the Northern Cheyenne Rules of Civil Procedure to enforce a penalty order or to seek preliminary injunctive relief against any person who is suspected to have violated the TIP or a compliance order.
units.action_summary: The Administrator may file civil actions in Tribal Court to enforce penalties or obtain injunctive relief for suspected violations.

units.obligation_text: Alleged violators can challenge compliance orders by petitioning the DEPNR Director for administrative review within 30 days of receiving the order.
units.action_summary: Alleged violators may petition the DEPNR Director for administrative review of compliance orders within 30 days.

units.obligation_text: The Director shall promptly review petitions for administrative review and issue a written decision that upholds, vacates, or modifies the order.
units.action_summary: The Director must promptly review petitions and issue a written decision to uphold, vacate, or modify the order.

units.obligation_text: Alleged violators can challenge a decision by the Director by filing an action in Northern Cheyenne Tribal Court pursuant to the Northern Cheyenne Rules of Civil Procedure.
units.action_summary: Alleged violators may file an action in Tribal Court to challenge the Director's decision.

units.obligation_text: The Tribal Court shall uphold any decision by the Director unless it is arbitrary and capricious or contrary to law.
units.action_summary: The Tribal Court must uphold the Director's decision unless it is arbitrary, capricious, or contrary to law.

units.obligation_text: The Tribe did not submit, and EPA is not proposing to approve, any criminal enforcement authority under the TIP. Accordingly, the EPA is responsible for pursuing any criminal enforcement action for violations of the Act or implementing regulations that occur in Indian country.
units.action_summary: EPA is responsible for pursuing criminal enforcement actions in Indian country for violations of the Act when the Tribe has not submitted criminal enforcement authority.

units.obligation_text: Under the terms of this MOA, the Tribe would refer alleged criminal violations of the Act that exceed the Tribe’s criminal authority to EPA Region 8 if the EPA approves the Tribe for CAA criminal enforcement authorities in the future.

units.obligation_text: Such nonconformity results or will result in the vehicle owner having to bear any penalty or other sanction (including the denial of the right to use the vehicle) under local, State or Federal law, then the manufacturer shall remedy the nonconformity at no cost to the owner;
units.action_summary: If a nonconformity causes the owner to bear penalties or sanctions, the manufacturer must remedy the nonconformity at no cost to the owner.

units.obligation_text: except that, if the vehicle has been in operation for more than 24 months or 24,000 miles, the manufacturer shall be required to remedy only those nonconformities resulting from the failure of any of the specified major emission control components listed in 42 U.S.C. 7541(i)(2) or components which have been designated by the Administrator to be specified major emission control components until the vehicle has been in operation for 8 years or 80,000 miles.

units.obligation_text: In no case may a manufacturer deny an emission warranty claim on the basis of—

units.obligation_text: A claim under any emission warranty required by 42 U.S.C. 7541(a) or (b) may be submitted by bringing a vehicle to:
units.action_summary: A vehicle owner may submit an emission warranty claim by bringing the vehicle to specified locations or facilities.

units.obligation_text: To the extent required by any Federal or State law, whether statutory or common law, a vehicle manufacturer shall be required to provide a means for non-franchised repair facilities to perform emission warranty repairs.
units.action_summary: If federal or state law requires it, the manufacturer must provide a means for non-franchised repair facilities to perform emission warranty repairs.

units.obligation_text: The manufacturer of each vehicle to which the warranty is applicable shall establish procedures as to the manner in which a claim under the emission warranty is to be processed.
units.action_summary: Manufacturers must establish procedures for processing emission warranty claims.

units.obligation_text: Require that if the facility at which the vehicle is initially presented for repair is unable for any reason to honor the particular claim, then, unless this requirement is waived in writing by the vehicle owner, the repair facility shall forward the claim to an individual or office authorized to make emission warranty determinations for the manufacturer.
units.action_summary: Manufacturer procedures must require that if the initial repair facility cannot honor the claim, the facility must forward the claim to an authorized individual/office unless the owner waives the requirement in writing.

units.obligation_text: The vehicle manufacturer shall incur all costs associated with a determination that an emission warranty claim is valid.
units.action_summary: If an emission warranty claim is determined valid, the manufacturer must pay all associated costs.

units.obligation_text: The manufacturer’s obligation under the emission warranties provided under 42 U.S.C. 7541(a) and (b) shall be to make all adjustments, repairs or replacements necessary to assure that the vehicle complies with applicable emission standards of the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, that it will continue to comply for the remainder of its useful life (if proper maintenance and operation are continued), and that it will operate in a safe manner. The manufacturer shall bear all costs incurred as a result of the above obligation, except that after the first 24 months or 24,000 miles (whichever first occurs) the manufacturer shall be responsible only for:
units.action_summary: Manufacturer must perform adjustments, repairs, or replacements necessary to ensure EPA emission compliance and safety for useful life and bear all associated costs, subject to specified post-24-month limitations.

units.obligation_text: The adjustment, repair or replacement of any of the specified major emission control components listed in 42 U.S.C. 7541(i)(2) or components which have been designated by the administrator to be specified major emission control components until the vehicle has been in operation for 8 years or 80,000 miles;
units.action_summary: After 24 months/24,000 miles, the manufacturer remains responsible only for specified major emission control components until 8 years or 80,000 miles.

units.obligation_text: All other components which must be adjusted, repaired or replaced to enable a component adjusted, repaired, or replaced under paragraph (a)(1) of this section to perform properly.
units.action_summary: Manufacturer is responsible for repairing or replacing other components needed to enable covered major emission control components to function properly.

units.obligation_text: Manufacturers shall be liable for the total cost of the remedy for any vehicle validly presented for repair under an emission warranty to any authorized service facility authorized by the vehicle manufacturer. State or local limitations as to the extent of the penalty or sanction imposed upon an owner of a failed vehicle shall have no bearing on this liability.
units.action_summary: Manufacturers are liable for the total cost of remedies for vehicles validly presented for repair under an emission warranty; state/local limitations do not affect this liability.

units.obligation_text: A manufacturer shall furnish with each new motor vehicle, a full explanation of the emission warranties required by 42 U.S.C. 7541(a) and (b), including at a minimum the following information:
units.action_summary: Manufacturer must include a full explanation of emission warranties with each new vehicle.

units.obligation_text: An explanation that an owner may obtain further information concerning the emission warranties or that an owner may report violations of the terms of the Emission warranties provided under 42 U.S.C. 7541(a) and (b) by contacting the Director, Compliance Division, Environmental Protection Agency, 2000 Traverwood Dr, Ann Arbor, MI 48105 (Attention: Warranty) or email to: complianceinfo@epa.gov.
units.action_summary: The warranty explanation must state that the owner may obtain more information or report violations by contacting the EPA Compliance Division.

units.obligation_text: The following acts are prohibited and may subject a manufacturer to a civil penalty as described in paragraph (d) of this section:

units.action_summary: Manufacturers are prohibited from failing or refusing to comply with emission warranty terms and conditions for applicable vehicles.

units.obligation_text: To provide directly or indirectly in any communication to the ultimate purchaser or any subsequent purchaser that emission warranty coverage is conditioned upon the use of any name brand component, or system or upon service (other than a component or service provided without charge under the terms of the purchase agreement), unless the communication is made pursuant to a written waiver by the Office Director.
units.action_summary: Manufacturers are prohibited from conditioning warranty coverage on the use of particular brand-name components or services in communications to purchasers, unless the Office Director has granted a written waiver.

title: Renewable Fuel Standard Program: Standardsfor 2023-2025 and Other Changes

units.obligation_text: Each and every material processed in an agricultural digester must have an adjusted cellulosic content of at least 75%.

units.action_summary: Materials processed in an agricultural digester must have at least 75% adjusted cellulosic content.

units.obligation_text: Digestate must only contain the leftovers that were unable to be completely converted to biogas in an anaerobic digestor that is part of an EPA-accepted registration under § 80.1450.

units.action_summary: Digestate from an EPA-registered anaerobic digester may contain only leftover material not converted to biogas.

units.obligation_text: Actual peak capacity means 105% of the maximum annual volume of renewable fuels produced from a specific renewable fuel production facility on a calendar year basis. (1) For facilities that commenced construction prior to December 19, 2007, the actual peak capacity is based on the last five calendar years prior to 2008, unless no such production exists, in which case actual peak capacity is based on any calendar year after startup during the first three years of operation. (2) For facilities that commenced construction after December 19, 2007 and before January 1, 2010, that are fired with natural gas, biomass, or a combination thereof, the actual peak capacity is based on any calendar year after startup during the first three years of operation. (3) For all other facilities not included above, the actual peak capacity is based on the last five calendar years prior to the year in which the owner or operator registers the facility under the provisions of § 80.1450, unless no such production exists, in which case actual peak capacity is based on any calendar year after startup during the first three years of operation.
units.actor: owner or operator of the renewable fuel production facility (for purposes of determining actual peak capacity)
units.action_summary: Defines how actual peak capacity is to be calculated, with different time-base rules depending on construction date and fuel sources.

units.obligation_text: For facilities that commenced construction prior to December 19, 2007, the actual peak capacity is based on the last five calendar years prior to 2008, unless no such production exists, in which case actual peak capacity is based on any calendar year after startup during the first three years of operation.
units.actor: owner or operator of facilities that commenced construction prior to December 19, 2007
units.action_summary: For pre-December 19, 2007 facilities, actual peak capacity is calculated from the last five calendar years prior to 2008, or if none, from any calendar year within first three years after startup.

units.obligation_text: For facilities that commenced construction after December 19, 2007 and before January 1, 2010, that are fired with natural gas, biomass, or a combination thereof, the actual peak capacity is based on any calendar year after startup during the first three years of operation.
units.actor: owner or operator of facilities commenced after December 19, 2007 and before January 1, 2010 fired with natural gas, biomass, or a combination
units.action_summary: For these facilities, actual peak capacity is determined from any calendar year after startup within the first three years of operation.

units.obligation_text: For all other facilities not included above, the actual peak capacity is based on the last five calendar years prior to the year in which the owner or operator registers the facility under the provisions of § 80.1450, unless no such production exists, in which case actual peak capacity is based on any calendar year after startup during the first three years of operation.
units.actor: owner or operator of other renewable fuel production facilities (for purposes of registration under § 80.1450)
units.action_summary: For other facilities, actual peak capacity is calculated from the last five calendar years prior to the registration year, or if none, from any calendar year within first three years after startup.

units.obligation_text: For flow meters, automated measurement must occur at least once every 6 seconds.

units.action_summary: Flow meters must record automated measurements at least every 6 seconds.

units.obligation_text: For all other meters, automated measurement must occur at least once every 2 seconds.
units.actor: the party operating other meters / responsible for automated measurement
units.action_summary: All other meters must record automated measurements at least every 2 seconds.

units.actor: registered independent third-party auditor (verifying RINs during the interim period)

title: Adoption and Submittal of State Plans for Designated Facilities: Implementing Regulations under Clean Air Act

units.obligation_text: The submission of such plan shall be made in electronic format according with § 60.23a(a)(3) or as specified in an applicable emission guideline.
units.action_summary: State plan submissions must be made in electronic format per §60.23a(a)(3) or as specified in an applicable emission guideline.

units.obligation_text: State plan submission to the EPA be via the use of SPeCS or through an analogous electronic reporting tool provided by the EPA for the submission of any plan required by this subpart.
units.action_summary: States must submit state plans to EPA using SPeCS or an EPA-provided analogous electronic reporting tool.

units.obligation_text: States are not to transmit confidential business information (CBI) through SPeCS.
units.action_summary: States must not transmit confidential business information (CBI) through SPeCS.

units.section: 40 CFR part 60, subpart Ba (proposed; see section III.A.1)
units.obligation_text: The EPA is proposing 15 months for state plan submissions after publication of a final emission guideline (EG).
units.action_summary: States must submit state plans within 15 months after publication of a final EG (proposed).

units.section: 40 CFR part 60, subpart Ba (proposed; see section III.A.2)
units.obligation_text: The EPA proposes to streamline the timeframe for the EPA's determination of completeness on a state plan submission from six months to 60 days from receipt of the state plan submission.
units.action_summary: EPA will determine completeness of a state plan submission within 60 days of receipt (proposed).

units.section: 40 CFR part 60, subpart Ba (proposed; see section III.A.3)
units.obligation_text: The EPA is proposing 12 months for the EPA to take final action on a state plan after a submission is found to be complete.
units.action_summary: EPA must take final action on a complete state plan within 12 months (proposed).

units.section: 40 CFR part 60, subpart Ba (proposed; see section III.A.4)
units.obligation_text: The EPA is proposing 12 months for the EPA to promulgate a Federal plan either after the state plan deadline, if a state has failed to submit a complete plan, or after the EPA's disapproval of a state plan submission.
units.action_summary: EPA must promulgate a Federal plan within 12 months after the state plan deadline if a state fails to submit, or within 12 months after EPA disapproves a state plan (proposed).

units.section: 40 CFR part 60, subpart Ba (proposed; see section III.A.5)
units.obligation_text: The EPA is proposing to require that state plans include increments of progress if the plan requires final compliance with standards of performance later than 16 months after the plan submission deadline.
units.action_summary: If a state plan allows final compliance later than 16 months after the plan submission deadline, the plan must include increments of progress.

units.section: 40 CFR part 60, subpart Ba (proposed; see section III.C)
units.obligation_text: The EPA is proposing to require that states, as part of the state plan development or revision process or if invoking RULOF provisions, undertake outreach and meaningful engagement with a broad range of pertinent stakeholders.
units.action_summary: States must undertake outreach and meaningful engagement with pertinent stakeholders during plan development or revision or when invoking RULOF.

units.obligation_text: A plan submittal must include supporting material demonstrating the state's legal authority to implement and enforce each component of its plan, including the standards of performance.
units.action_summary: State plan submissions must include supporting materials showing the state's legal authority to implement and enforce each plan component.

units.obligation_text: Subpart Ba allows for standards of performance and other state plan requirements to be established as part of state permits and administrative orders, which are then incorporated into the state plan.
units.action_summary: States may establish standards of performance and plan requirements via state permits or administrative orders incorporated into the state plan.

units.obligation_text: If a state does choose to use permits or administrative orders to establish standards of performance, it needs to demonstrate that it has the legal authority to do so.
units.action_summary: If states use permits or administrative orders to establish standards, they must demonstrate they have the legal authority to do so.

units.obligation_text: Each emission guideline may include specific provisions in addition to or that supersede requirements of this subpart.
units.actor: Emission guideline authors / EPA (when promulgating EGs)
units.action_summary: An emission guideline may include provisions that add to or supersede subpart requirements.

units.obligation_text: A State plan may establish a program to allow owners or operators of municipal waste combustor plants to engage in trading of nitrogen oxides emission credits.
units.action_summary: State plans may establish trading programs allowing owners/operators to trade NOx emission credits.

units.obligation_text: The provision permits each state to adopt measures that allow its sources to meet their emission limits in the aggregate, when the EPA determines, in any particular emission guideline, that it is appropriate to do so.
units.actor: States (subject to EPA approval in EGs)
units.action_summary: States are permitted to adopt measures (including trading or averaging) allowing aggregate compliance where EPA finds it appropriate for a particular emission guideline.

units.obligation_text: Manufacturers subject to this part shall construe the following terms in ISO 13485 (incorporated by reference, see § 820.7) as follows:
units.action_summary: Contrue specified ISO 13485 terms as set out in this section

units.obligation_text: Organization shall have the meaning of ‘‘manufacturers’’ as defined in this part.
units.action_summary: Treat 'Organization' as meaning 'manufacturers' under this part

units.obligation_text: Safety and performance shall have the meaning of ‘‘safety and effectiveness’’ for the purposes of this part.
units.action_summary: Treat 'safety and performance' as meaning 'safety and effectiveness' under this part

units.obligation_text: The phrase ‘‘safety and performance’’ does not relieve a manufacturer from any obligation to implement controls or other measures that provide reasonable assurance of safety and effectiveness.
units.action_summary: Manufacturers remain obligated to implement controls or other measures to assure safety and effectiveness

units.obligation_text: Validation of processes shall have the meaning of ‘‘process validation’’ as defined in this part.
units.action_summary: Treat 'Validation of processes' as meaning 'process validation' under this part

units.obligation_text: In addition to the requirements of Clause 4.2.5 in ISO 13485 (incorporated by reference, see § 820.7), Control of Records, the manufacturer must obtain the signature for each individual who approved or re-approved the record, and the date of such approval, on that record and include the below information in certain records as follows:

units.obligation_text: In addition to Clause 8.2.2 in ISO 13485, Complaint Handling, the manufacturer must record the following information, at a minimum, for complaints that must be reported to FDA under part 803 of this chapter, complaints that a manufacturer determines must be investigated, and complaints that the manufacturer investigated regardless of those requirements:

units.obligation_text: Any corrective action taken; and

units.obligation_text: Any reply to the complainant.
units.action_summary: Record any reply provided to the complainant

units.obligation_text: In adhering to Clause 7.5.4 in ISO 13485, Servicing Activities, the manufacturer must record the following information, at a minimum, for servicing activities:

units.action_summary: Record the name of the device serviced

units.obligation_text: Any unique device identifier (UDI) or universal product code (UPC), and any other device identification(s);
units.action_summary: Record the device UDI/UPC or other identifiers for serviced devices

units.obligation_text: The date of service;
units.action_summary: Record the service date

units.action_summary: Record the identity of individual(s) who performed the service

units.obligation_text: The service performed; and
units.action_summary: Record the service that was performed on the device

units.obligation_text: Any test and inspection data.
units.action_summary: Record any test and inspection data related to servicing

units.obligation_text: In addition to the requirements of Clauses 7.5.1, 7.5.8, and 7.5.9 in ISO 13485, the UDI must be recorded for each medical device or batch of medical devices.
units.action_summary: Record the UDI for each medical device or batch

units.obligation_text: Records deemed confidential by the manufacturer may be marked to aid FDA in determining whether information may be disclosed under the public information regulation in part 20 of this chapter.
units.action_summary: May mark records deemed confidential to assist FDA in disclosure determinations

units.obligation_text: In addition to the requirements of Clause 7.5.1 of ISO 13485 (incorporated by reference, see § 820.7), Control of production and service provision, each manufacturer must establish and maintain procedures that provide a detailed description of the activities to ensure the integrity, inspection, storage, and operations for labeling and packaging, during the customary conditions of processing, storage, handling, distribution, and where appropriate, use of the device.

units.obligation_text: The correct unique device identifier (UDI) or universal product code (UPC), or any other device identification(s);
units.action_summary: Ensure correct UDI/UPC or other device identification is present on labeling and packaging

units.obligation_text: Expiration date;
units.action_summary: Ensure expiration date is present and accurate on labeling/packaging

units.obligation_text: Storage instructions;
units.action_summary: Ensure storage instructions are present and accurate on labeling/packaging

units.obligation_text: Handling instructions; and
units.action_summary: Ensure handling instructions are present and accurate on labeling/packaging

units.obligation_text: Any additional processing instructions.
units.action_summary: Ensure any additional processing instructions are present and accurate on labeling/packaging

units.obligation_text: The manufacturer must ensure labeling and packaging operations have been established and maintained to prevent errors, including, but not limited to, inspection of the labeling and packaging immediately before use to assure that all devices have correct labeling and packaging, as specified in the medical device file.

units.obligation_text: inspection of the labeling and packaging immediately before use to assure that all devices have correct labeling and packaging, as specified in the medical device file.

title: Automobile and Light-Duty Truck Surface Coating Operations; Standards of Performance [A-79-05-III-A-1]

units.obligation_text: The provisions of this subpart apply to the following affected facilities in an automobile or light-duty truck surface coating line: each prime coat operation, each guide coat operation, and each topcoat operation.
units.actor: each prime coat operation, each guide coat operation, and each topcoat operation
units.action_summary: This subpart applies to prime coat, guide coat, and topcoat operations on automobile/light-duty truck surface coating lines.

units.obligation_text: The provisions of this subpart apply to any affected facility identified in paragraph (a) of this section that begins construction or modification after (date of publication in the Federal Register).
units.actor: any affected facility identified in paragraph (a) that begins construction or modification after (date of publication)
units.action_summary: Facilities identified in §60.390(a) that begin construction or modification after the listed date are subject to this subpart.

units.obligation_text: After the performance test required by § 60.8 has been completed, no owner or operator subject to the provisions of this subpart shall discharge or cause of the discharge into the atmosphere of VOC emissions which exceed the following limits:
units.actor: owner or operator subject to the provisions of this subpart
units.action_summary: Prohibits owners/operators from emitting VOCs into the atmosphere above specified limits after the required performance test.

units.obligation_text: 0.10 kilogram of VOC (measured as mass of carbon) per liter of applied coating solids from each prime coat operation.
units.actor: owner or operator subject to the provisions of this subpart (each prime coat operation)
units.action_summary: VOC emissions from each prime coat operation must not exceed 0.10 kg carbon per liter of applied coating solids.

units.obligation_text: 0.84 kilogram of VOC (measured as mass of carbon) per liter of applied coating solids from each guide coat operation.
units.actor: owner or operator subject to the provisions of this subpart (each guide coat operation)
units.action_summary: VOC emissions from each guide coat operation must not exceed 0.84 kg carbon per liter of applied coating solids.

units.obligation_text: 0.84 kilogram of VOC (measured as mass of carbon) per liter of applied coating solids from each topcoat operation.
units.actor: owner or operator subject to the provisions of this subpart (each topcoat operation)
units.action_summary: VOC emissions from each topcoat operation must not exceed 0.84 kg carbon per liter of applied coating solids.

units.obligation_text: Any owner or operator subject to the provisions of this subpart shall-
units.actor: owner or operator subject to the provisions of this subpart
units.action_summary: Introduction to monitoring obligations that follow (installation, calculation, and determination requirements).

units.obligation_text: Install, calibrate, operate, and maintain a monitoring device which records the combustion temperature of any effluent gases which are emitted from any surface coating operation and which are incinerated to comply with § 60.392. The manufacturer must certify that the monitoring device is accurate to within ±2°C (±3.6°F).
units.actor: owner or operator (first sentence); the manufacturer (second sentence)
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must install, calibrate, operate, and maintain a temperature-recording monitoring device for incinerated effluents; manufacturers must certify the device accuracy to ±2°C.

units.obligation_text: Determine the weighted average VOC content of the coating materials used in any EDP prime coat operation whenever a change occurs in the composition of any of these coating materials. The owner or operator shall compute the weighted average by the following equation: [equation and definitions].
units.actor: owner or operator of EDP prime coat operations
units.action_summary: When coating composition changes, owners/operators must compute the weighted average VOC content of materials added to an EDP prime coat system using the specified equation and parameters.

units.obligation_text: Determine the average VOC content of the coating materials in any surface coating operation which uses spray application whenever a change occurs in the composition of any of these coating materials. The owner or operator shall determine and record the arithmetic average of the VOC content of all coating materials in a coating operation which uses more than one coating material.
units.actor: owner or operator of spray application surface coating operations
units.action_summary: When composition changes, owners/operators of spray-applied operations must determine and record the arithmetic average VOC content of all coating materials used.

units.obligation_text: Any owner or operator subject to the provisions of this subpart shall report for each calendar quarter all measurement results as follows:
units.actor: owner or operator subject to the provisions of this subpart
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must quarterly report measurement results as detailed in the following subparagraphs.

units.obligation_text: Where compliance with § 60.392 is achieved without the use of add-on control devices, any month during which the weighted average VOC content of the makeup materials used in any prime coat operation employing EDP exceeds the most recent value which demonstrated compliance with § 60.392(a) by the performance test required in § 60.8.
units.actor: owner or operator of prime coat operations employing EDP (where compliance is without add-on controls)
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must report any month where the weighted average VOC content in EDP prime coat makeup exceeds the value that demonstrated compliance.

units.obligation_text: Where compliance with § 60.392 is achieved without the use of add-on control devices, any month during which the VOC content of the coating materials used in any surface coating operation employing spray application exceeds the most recent value which demonstrated compliance with § 60.392 by the performance test required in § 60.8.
units.actor: owner or operator of surface coating operations employing spray application (where compliance is without add-on controls)
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must report any month where VOC content of spray-applied coating materials exceeds the value that demonstrated compliance.

units.obligation_text: Where compliance with § 60.392 is achieved by the use of incineration, all periods in excess of 5 minutes during which the temperature in any incinerator used to control the emission from a surface coating operation remains below the most recent level which demonstrated compliance with § 60.392 by the performance tests required in § 60.8. The report required under § 60.7(c) shall identify each such occurrence and its duration.
units.actor: owner or operator of surface coating operations using incineration
units.action_summary: Owners/operators using incineration must report each occurrence exceeding 5 minutes where incinerator temperature falls below the level that demonstrated compliance, and identify each occurrence and its duration.

units.obligation_text: The reporting requirements in this regulation will automatically expire five years from the date of promulgation unless EPA takes affirmative action to extend them.
units.actor: EPA (for extension); reporting requirements (as subject to expiration)
units.action_summary: Quarterly reporting obligations will expire five years after promulgation unless EPA affirmatively extends them.
units.modal_raw: will automatically expire / unless EPA takes affirmative action

units.obligation_text: The reference methods in Appendix A to this part, except as provided for in § 60.8(b), shall be used to determine compliance with § 60.392 as follows:
units.action_summary: Reference methods in Appendix A must be used (except as noted) to determine compliance with the VOC standards.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator shall use Reference Method 24 (Candidate 1 or Candidate 2) to measure the VOC content of every coating or makeup material used in each surface coating operation of an automobile or light-duty truck surface coating line. The coating sample shall be a 1 liter sample taken at a point where the sample will be representative of the coating material as applied to the vehicle surface. The 1 liter sample shall be divided into three aliquots for triplicate determinations by Method 24 (Candidate 1 or Candidate 2).
units.actor: owner or operator; (sampling) owner or operator
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must use Method 24 to measure VOC content of every coating/makeup material, collect a representative 1-liter sample, and split it into three aliquots for triplicate determinations.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator shall compute the arithmetic average VOC content of all coating materials used in each surface coating operation that uses spray application.
units.actor: owner or operator of spray application operations
units.action_summary: Compute and record the arithmetic average VOC content of all coatings used in spray-applied operations.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator shall use the calculation procedures given in § 60.393(a)(2) to compute the weighted average VOC content of all makeup materials added to an EDP tank during a selected one month period for each prime coat operation that uses EDP.
units.actor: owner or operator of EDP prime coat operations
units.action_summary: Use the §60.393(a)(2) calculation to compute the weighted average VOC content of makeup streams added to an EDP tank for a selected one-month period.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator shall determine the VOC emissions by the equation: E = C / TE (where E = VOC emissions, C = average VOC content, TE = transfer efficiency).
units.action_summary: Determine VOC emissions using the specified equation relating emissions, average VOC content, and transfer efficiency.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator shall select the appropriate transfer efficiency from the following table for each surface coating operation. If the owner or operator can justify to the Administrator's satisfaction that other values for transfer efficiencies are appropriate, the Administrator will approve their use on a case-by-case basis. Where more than one application method is used on an individual surface coating operation, the owner or operator shall perform an analysis to determine the relative volume of solids coating materials applied by each method. The owner or operator shall use these relative volumes of solids to compute a weighted average transfer efficiency for the operation. The Administrator will review and approve this analysis on a case-by-case basis.
units.action_summary: Select transfer efficiency from table for each operation; if multiple methods are used, perform analysis of relative volumes and compute weighted average transfer efficiency; Administrator may approve alternative efficiencies and will review/approve analyses case-by-case.

units.obligation_text: If the owner or operator can justify to the Administrator's satisfaction that other values for transfer efficiencies are appropriate, the Administrator will approve their use on a case-by-case basis.
units.action_summary: Administrator may approve alternative transfer efficiency values on a case-by-case basis if justified.

units.obligation_text: For each surface coating operation which cannot achieve compliance with § 60.392 without the use of add-on control devices, the owner or operator shall use the following procedures to determine that the emission reduction efficiency of the control device(s) is sufficient to achieve compliance with § 60.392:
units.actor: owner or operator of surface coating operations that cannot comply without add-on control devices
units.action_summary: Owners/operators who rely on add-on controls must follow the specified procedures to demonstrate control device emission reduction efficiency is sufficient to meet VOC limits.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator shall compute the emission reduction efficiency required for each surface coating operation by the following equation: ER = (E - EL) / E (where ER = required emission reduction efficiency, E = VOC emissions, EL = numerical VOC emission limit in § 60.392).
units.action_summary: Calculate the required emission reduction efficiency (ER) using the specified equation comparing current emissions to the standard.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator shall determine the emission reduction efficiency achieved by the control device(s) on each applicable surface coating operation as follows:
units.action_summary: Introduction to the procedures (Method 25/2 testing, sampling, and calculations) to determine achieved emission reduction efficiency.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator shall use Reference Method 25 to determine the VOC concentration in the effluent gas before and after the emission control device for each stack that is equipped with an emission control device. The owner or operator shall use Reference Method 2 to determine the volumetric flowrate of the effluent gas before and after the emission control device on each stack. The Administrator will approve testing of representative stacks, on a case-by-case basis, if the owner or operator can show to the Administrator's satisfaction that testing of representative stacks yields results comparable to those that would be obtained by testing all stacks.
units.action_summary: Use Method 25 to measure VOC concentrations and Method 2 to measure flow rates before and after control devices for each stack; Administrator may approve testing representative stacks case-by-case if justified.

units.obligation_text: For Method 25, the sampling time for each run shall be at least 60 minutes and the minimum sample volume shall be at least 0.003 dscm (0.106 dscf) except that shorter sampling times or smaller volumes, when necessitated by process variables or other factors, may be approved by the Administrator.
units.action_summary: Method 25 sampling runs must be at least 60 minutes and 0.003 dscm minimum volume; Administrator may approve shorter times or smaller volumes if justified.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator shall determine the efficiency of each emission control device by the following equation: EFF = (CB x VOLB) - (CA x VOLA) x 10 / (CB x VOLB), where CB = concentration before device, CA = concentration after device, VOLB = volumetric flow before, VOLA = volumetric flow after. If an emission control device controls the emissions from more than one stack, the owner or operator shall measure CB and VOLB at a location between the manifold that receives all the exhausts from the applicable surface coating operation and the control device. If a manifold is not used, the product CB x VOLB shall be replaced by the sum of the individual products for each stack on the applicable surface coating operation controlled by this device.
units.action_summary: Calculate each control device's efficiency using the specified equation and, if device controls multiple stacks, measure concentrations and flows at the manifold or sum individual stack products as specified.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator shall determine the fraction of the total VOC discharged from an applicable surface coating operation which enters each emission control device on that operation by the following equation: Fj = (CBi x VOLBi) / (Σ (CBk x VOLBk) ), and shall use the procedures contained in clause (ii) of this subparagraph for any emission control device that controls the emissions from more than one stack.
units.action_summary: Determine fraction of total VOC entering each control device using the specified equation and use the sampling procedures in (ii) when device controls emissions from multiple stacks.

units.obligation_text: The owner or operator shall determine the emission reduction efficiency achieved by the control device(s) on the applicable surface coating operation using the equation: EA = Σ (Fi x EFFi) where EA = emission reduction efficiency achieved, EFFi = emission reduction efficiency of each control device, and mn = number of control devices.
units.action_summary: Compute achieved emission reduction efficiency for the operation as the weighted sum of each device's efficiency times the fraction of VOC entering it.

units.obligation_text: If EA is greater than or equal to ER, the applicable surface coating operation will be in compliance with § 60.392.
units.actor: applicable surface coating operation / owner or operator
units.action_summary: An operation is in compliance if achieved emission reduction efficiency (EA) is ≥ required emission reduction efficiency (ER).
