units.action_summary: Permanent label must resist open weather exposure without significant loss of visibility or legibility.

units.obligation_text: The permanent label must be displayed on a background of contrasting color;
units.actor: persons selling, distributing, offering for sale, or importing containers
units.action_summary: Permanent label must have a contrasting background color.

units.obligation_text: If a container of a regulated substances is contained within a box or other overpack, the exterior packaging must contain legible and visible information in at least 20-point font of what regulated substance is contained within.
units.actor: persons selling, distributing, offering for sale, or importing containers
units.action_summary: If container is overpacked, exterior packaging must state the contained regulated substance in at least 20-point font.

units.obligation_text: Removing or tampering with this permanent label is prohibited.
units.action_summary: Prohibits removal or tampering with the permanent label on regulated substance containers.

units.obligation_text: No person other than the importer of record may repackage or relabel regulated substances that were initially unlabeled or mislabeled.
units.actor: No person other than the importer of record
units.action_summary: Prohibits anyone other than the importer of record from repackaging or relabeling initially unlabeled or mislabeled regulated substances.

units.obligation_text: In order to repackage the regulated substances, the importer must either: Expend consumption allowances equal to the amount of allowances that would be required if each cylinder were full of HFC-23;
units.action_summary: To repackage, importer may expend consumption allowances equal to the full-cylinder HFC-23 equivalent.

units.obligation_text: In order to repackage the regulated substances, the importer must either: Verify the contents with independent laboratory testing results and affix a correct label on the container that matches the lab-verified test results before the date of importation of the container.
units.action_summary: To repackage, importer may alternatively verify contents via independent lab testing and affix a correct label matching results before importation.

units.obligation_text: No person producing, importing, reclaiming, recycling for fire suppression, or repackaging regulated substances may sell or distribute, or offer for sale or distribution, regulated substances without first testing a representative sample of the regulated substances that they are producing, importing, reclaiming, recycling for fire suppression, or repackaging to verify that the composition of the regulated substance(s) matches the container labeling using the sampling and testing methodology prescribed in 40 CFR part 82, subpart F appendix A for regulated substances offered for sale and distribution as refrigerants and using the following testing method for regulated substances offered for non-refrigerant uses:
units.actor: persons producing, importing, reclaiming, recycling for fire suppression, or repackaging regulated substances
units.action_summary: Those actors may not sell or distribute regulated substances without first testing a representative sample to verify composition matches labeling using specified sampling and testing methods.

units.obligation_text: Use the sampling and testing methodology prescribed in 40 CFR part 82, subpart F appendix A for refrigerants and specified parts of AHRI/Appendix C or EPA Method 18 for non-refrigerant substances as set forth in Table 1 to paragraph (d)(3)(i).
units.actor: persons producing, importing, reclaiming, recycling for fire suppression, or repackaging regulated substances
units.action_summary: Testing must follow prescribed methodologies (appendix A to 40 CFR part 82 subpart F, AHRI procedures, or EPA Method 18) depending on the regulated substance and use.

units.obligation_text: No person may sell or distribute, or offer for sale or distribution, regulated substances as a refrigerant that do not meet the specifications in appendix A to 40 CFR part 82, subpart F—Specifications for Refrigerants that are applicable to that regulated substance or mixture containing regulated substance(s). For persons who are producing, importing, reclaiming, recycling for fire suppression, or repackaging regulated substances, the applicable specifications must be verified using the sampling and testing methodology prescribed in appendix A to 40 CFR part 82, subpart F.
units.actor: No person (and specifically producers, importers, reclaimers, recyclers for fire suppression, repackagers)
units.action_summary: Prohibits selling or distributing substances as refrigerants unless they meet appendix A specifications; producers/importers/reclaimers/repackagers must verify specifications using appendix A sampling/testing methods.

units.obligation_text: Starting with the allocation of 2024 calendar years allowances, the relevant Agency official will issue, through a separate notification, calendar year production allowances to entities that produced a regulated substance in 2021 or 2022, or both 2021 and 2022.
units.action_summary: EPA official will issue calendar-year production allowances by separate notification to entities that produced regulated substances in 2021 or 2022.

units.obligation_text: Take the average of the three highest annual exchange value-weighted production amounts that each eligible entity reported to the Agency for calendar years 2011 through 2019;
units.action_summary: Agency must calculate each eligible entity's average of its three highest exchange value-weighted annual production amounts from 2011–2019.

units.obligation_text: Sum every entity’s average values determined in paragraph (b)(1) of this section and determine each entity’s percentage of that total;
units.action_summary: Agency must sum the averages and determine each entity's percentage share of the total.

units.obligation_text: Determine the amount of general pool production allowances by subtracting the quantity of application-specific allowances for that year as determined in accordance with § 84.13 from the production cap in § 84.7(b)(3);
units.action_summary: Agency must calculate the general pool production allowances by subtracting application-specific allowances from the production cap.

units.obligation_text: Determine individual entities’ production allowance quantities by multiplying each entity’s percentage determined in (b)(2) of this section by the amount of general pool allowances determined in (b)(3) of this section.
units.action_summary: Agency must allocate production allowances to each entity by multiplying its percentage share by the general pool amount.

units.obligation_text: Starting with the allocation of 2024 calendar years allowances the relevant Agency official will issue, through a separate notification, calendar year consumption allowances.
units.action_summary: EPA official will issue calendar-year consumption allowances by separate notification starting with 2024 allocations.

units.obligation_text: For new market entrants that were allocated allowances pursuant to § 84.15(e)(3), take the allowances allocated for calendar year 2023 and divide that value by the proportion of calendar year 2023 consumption allowances received by general pool allowance holders pursuant to paragraph (a) of this section relative to their high three average calculated pursuant to paragraph (a)(2) of this section;
units.action_summary: Agency must calculate new market entrant allocation by adjusting 2023 allocations relative to general pool proportions and high-three averages.

units.obligation_text: For entities that produced or imported a regulated substance in 2021 or 2022, or both 2021 and 2022, and have not been allocated allowances pursuant to § 84.15(e)(3), the relevant Agency official will calculate and issue allowances to a single entity if multiple importers are related through shared corporate or common ownership. The relevant Agency official will take the average of the three highest annual exchange value-weighted consumption amounts, which for entities related through shared corporate or common ownership or control would be aggregated and averaged at the corporate or common ownership level, that each eligible entity reported to the Agency for calendar years 2011 through 2019;
units.action_summary: Agency will aggregate related importers by corporate/common ownership and calculate averages of their three highest exchange value-weighted consumption amounts for allocation.

units.obligation_text: If an entity has a value calculated under (b)(1) of this section and (b)(2) of this section, take the single higher value;
units.action_summary: Agency must use the higher of the values calculated under (b)(1) and (b)(2) for allocation purposes.

units.obligation_text: Sum every entity’s values as determined in (b)(1), (2), and (3) of this section and determine each entity’s percentage of that total;
units.action_summary: Agency must sum calculated values across entities and determine each entity's percentage share.

units.obligation_text: Determine the amount of general pool consumption allowances by subtracting the quantity of application-specific allowances for that year as determined in accordance with § 84.13 from the consumption cap in § 84.7(b)(3);
units.action_summary: Agency must calculate the general pool consumption allowances by subtracting application-specific allowances from the consumption cap.

units.obligation_text: Determine individual entities’ consumption allowance quantities by multiplying each entity’s percentage determined in (b)(3) of this section by the amount of general pool allowances determined in (b)(4) of this section.
units.action_summary: Agency must allocate consumption allowances to entities by multiplying each entity's percentage share by the general pool amount.

units.obligation_text: As part of the availability of additional consumption allowances, applicants must provide the following information and documentation:
units.actor: applicant / entity requesting additional consumption allowances
units.action_summary: Applicants for additional consumption allowances must include specified documentation and information.

units.obligation_text: A copy of the bill of lading and the invoice indicating the net quantity (in kilograms) of regulated substances shipped and documenting the sale of the regulated substances to the purchaser;
units.actor: applicant / entity requesting additional consumption allowances
units.action_summary: Applicants must include bill of lading and invoice showing net quantities and sale documentation.

units.obligation_text: The Harmonized Tariff Schedule codes of the regulated substances exported;
units.actor: applicant / entity requesting additional consumption allowances
units.action_summary: Applicants must provide HTS codes for the exported regulated substances.

units.obligation_text: Internal Transaction Numbers for all shipments;
units.actor: applicant / entity requesting additional consumption allowances
units.action_summary: Applicants must provide internal transaction numbers for shipments.

units.obligation_text: Conveyance names;
units.actor: applicant / entity requesting additional consumption allowances
units.action_summary: Applicants must provide names of conveyances used in shipments.

units.obligation_text: International Maritime Organization number of the marine vessel(s) carrying the export, if applicable;
units.actor: applicant / entity requesting additional consumption allowances
units.action_summary: Applicants must provide IMO numbers for marine vessels carrying exports where applicable.

units.obligation_text: Container numbers.
units.actor: applicant / entity requesting additional consumption allowances
units.action_summary: Applicants must provide container numbers for the shipments.

units.obligation_text: An entity does not need to follow the procedures in this paragraph to expend allowances possessed by another entity that is majority owned by it, it majority owns, related to it through majority ownership, or commonly owned with it.
units.actor: an entity (in relation to majority- or commonly-owned entities)
units.action_summary: Entities may expend allowances possessed by related majority- or commonly-owned entities without following the paragraph's procedures.

units.obligation_text: If at the time of submitting the petition the importer does not know this information, and the importer receives a non-objection notice for the individual shipment in the petition, the importer is required to notify the relevant Agency official of this information prior to the date of importation of the individual shipment into the United States;
units.action_summary: If unspecified at petition time and a non-objection notice is received, importer must notify the Agency official of port/vessel/expected date info before importation.

units.obligation_text: The quantity (in kilograms) of production of each regulated substance used in processes resulting in their transformation by the producer; for any regulated substance that is used in processes resulting in their transformation at a facility that differs from the facility of production, but both facilities are owned by the producer, the name, quantity (in kilograms), and recipient facility of each regulated substance; and the quantity (in kilograms) intended for transformation by a second party;
units.action_summary: Producers must report kilograms of production used for transformation, plus details for transfers between producer-owned facilities and quantities intended for transformation by others.

units.obligation_text: The quantity (in kilograms) of production of each regulated substance used in processes resulting in their destruction by the producer; for any regulated substance that is used in processes resulting in their destruction at a facility that differs from the facility of production, but both facilities are owned by the producer, the name, quantity (in kilograms), and recipient facility of each regulated substance; and the quantity (in kilograms) intended for destruction by a second party;
units.action_summary: Producers must report kilograms used for destruction, plus details for transfers between producer-owned facilities and quantities intended for destruction by others.

units.obligation_text: The quantity (in kilograms) of production of each regulated substance used as a process agent by the producer; for any regulated substance that is used as a process agent at a facility that differs from the facility of production, but both facilities are owned by the producer, the name, quantity (in kilograms), and recipient facility of each regulated substance; and the quantity (in kilograms) intended for use as a process agent by a second party;
units.action_summary: Producers must report kilograms used as process agents, with facility transfer details and quantities intended for use by others.

units.obligation_text: A list of the entities conferring application-specific allowances from whom orders were placed, and the quantity (in kilograms) of specific regulated substances produced for those listed applications;
units.action_summary: Report must include entities conferring application-specific allowances and kilograms of substances produced for those applications.

units.obligation_text: Daily dated records required to be maintained pursuant to paragraph (b)(4)(xiv) of this section of the quantity of allowances expended for the production of regulated substances for all dates falling within the reported quarter and a certification that such allowances were expended on the specified date;
units.action_summary: Producers must maintain daily dated records for allowances expended for production during the reported quarter and certify they were expended on those dates.

units.obligation_text: For the fourth quarter report only, the quantity of each regulated substance held in inventory on December 31.
units.action_summary: Fourth-quarter report must include inventory quantity of each regulated substance on December 31.

units.obligation_text: Within 45 days after the end of the fourth quarter, each producer of a regulated substance must provide to the relevant Agency official a report of emissions on a regulated substance production line and emissions unit basis for each facility that produces regulated substances.
units.actor: each producer of a regulated substance
units.action_summary: Producers must provide an emissions report to the Agency within 45 days after year-end for each production line and emission unit at each facility.

units.obligation_text: Quantity (in pounds) of each of the following emitted in the prior calendar year on a regulated substance production line basis: hazardous air pollutants initially identified in section 112 of the CAA...; regulated substances listed in Appendix A to 40 CFR part 84; and ozone-depleting substances listed in appendix F of 40 CFR part 82, subpart A;
units.action_summary: Annual emissions report must include pounds emitted per production line for specified hazardous air pollutants, listed regulated substances, and ozone-depleting substances.

units.obligation_text: Quantity (in pounds) of each such substance listed in paragraph (b)(3)(i) of this section emitted in the prior calendar year on an emission unit basis from each regulated substance production line.
units.action_summary: Annual emissions report must include pounds emitted per emission unit from each production line for the listed substances.

units.obligation_text: Dated records of batch tests of regulated substances packaged for sale or distribution, including instrument calibration, sample testing data files, and results summaries of both sample test results and quality control test results that are in a form suitable and readily available for review;
units.action_summary: Producers must keep dated batch test records (including calibration and data files) for regulated substances packaged for sale or distribution, in a format suitable for review.

units.obligation_text: On any day allowances are expended for the production of regulated substances, record, on that same day, the date, quantity, and type of allowances expended.
units.action_summary: Producers must record the date, quantity, and type of allowances expended on the same day allowances are expended for production.

units.obligation_text: Daily dated records required to be maintained pursuant to (2)(xvii) of this paragraph of the quantity of allowances expended for the import of regulated substances for all dates falling within the reported quarter and a certification that such allowances were expended on the specified date.
units.action_summary: Importers must maintain daily dated records of allowances expended for imports during the reported quarter and certify those expenditures occurred on specified dates.

units.obligation_text: On any day allowances are expended for the import of regulated substances, record on that same day, the date, quantity, and type of allowances expended.
units.actor: importer of record (or importer expending allowances)
units.action_summary: Importers must record date, quantity, and type of allowances expended for imports on the same day they are expended.

units.obligation_text: The importer of record, or their authorized agent, must include the following no later than 14 days if arriving by marine vessel or 5 days for non-marine vessel prior to the date of importation, via a U.S. Customs and Border Protection-authorized electronic data interchange system, such as the Automated Broker Interface:
units.actor: importer of record or their authorized agent
units.action_summary: Importers must submit specified pre-import information via an authorized EDI system within prescribed timeframes before importation.

units.obligation_text: Cargo Description;
units.actor: importer of record or their authorized agent
units.action_summary: Pre-import submission must include cargo description.

units.obligation_text: Net weight, or if importing a heel when the precise quantity is unknown or has not been measured, the number equivalent to net weight if the volume of the container was 10 percent full;
units.actor: importer of record or their authorized agent
units.action_summary: Pre-import submission must include net weight or the heel-equivalent number when precise quantity is unknown (10% volume assumption).

units.obligation_text: Container number(s), as applicable;
units.actor: importer of record or their authorized agent
units.action_summary: Pre-import submission must include container numbers, if applicable.

units.obligation_text: Vessel name, for maritime shipments;
units.actor: importer of record or their authorized agent
units.action_summary: Pre-import submission for maritime shipments must include the vessel name.

units.obligation_text: International Maritime Organization number, for maritime shipments;
units.actor: importer of record or their authorized agent
units.action_summary: Pre-import submission for maritime shipments must include the vessel's IMO number.

units.obligation_text: Gross Weight, or if importing a heel when the precise quantity is unknown or has not been measured, the number equivalent to gross weight if the volume of the container was 10 percent full;
units.actor: importer of record or their authorized agent
units.action_summary: Pre-import submission must include gross weight or heel-equivalent gross weight (10% container volume) if precise quantity unknown.

units.obligation_text: Weight Unit of Measure;
units.actor: importer of record or their authorized agent
units.action_summary: Pre-import submission must include the unit of measure for weight.

units.obligation_text: Port of Entry;
units.actor: importer of record or their authorized agent
units.action_summary: Pre-import submission must include the port of entry.

units.obligation_text: Scheduled Entry Date;
units.actor: importer of record or their authorized agent
units.action_summary: Pre-import submission must include the scheduled entry date.

units.obligation_text: Harmonized Tariff Schedule (HTS) code;
units.actor: importer of record or their authorized agent
units.action_summary: Pre-import submission must include the HTS code for the imported substance.

units.obligation_text: Harmonized Tariff Schedule (HTS) Description;
units.actor: importer of record or their authorized agent
units.action_summary: Pre-import submission must include the HTS description.

units.obligation_text: Origin Country;
units.actor: importer of record or their authorized agent
units.action_summary: Pre-import submission must include the country of origin.

units.obligation_text: Importer Name and Importer Number;
units.actor: importer of record or their authorized agent
units.action_summary: Pre-import submission must include importer name and importer number.

units.obligation_text: Consignee Entity Name;
units.actor: importer of record or their authorized agent
units.action_summary: Pre-import submission must include the consignee entity name.

units.obligation_text: CAS Number(s) of the regulated substance(s) imported and, for regulated substances that are in a mixture, either the ASHRAE numerical designation of the refrigerant or the percentage of the mixture containing each regulated substance;
units.actor: importer of record or their authorized agent
units.action_summary: Pre-import submission must include CAS numbers and for mixtures either ASHRAE designation or percentages of each regulated substance.

units.obligation_text: If importing regulated substances for transformation or destruction, a copy of the non-objection notice issued consistent with § 84.25;
units.actor: importer of record or their authorized agent
units.action_summary: If import is for transformation or destruction, pre-import submission must include the non-objection notice pursuant to §84.25.

units.obligation_text: If importing regulated substances as a transhipment, a copy of the confirmation documenting the importer reported the transhipment consistent with paragraph (c)(3)(i) of this section;
units.actor: importer of record or their authorized agent
units.action_summary: If importing as a transhipment, include confirmation that the transhipment was reported consistent with paragraph (c)(3)(i).

units.obligation_text: A certificate of analysis.
units.actor: importer of record or their authorized agent
units.action_summary: Pre-import submission must include a certificate of analysis.

units.obligation_text: Any entity that falls under any of the following criteria must submit the information outlined in paragraph (c)(9)(ii) of this section: (A) That anticipates being the importer of record for a shipment of regulated substances must, by November 15 of the prior calendar year; or (B) That is not issued allowances by EPA, but receives transferred or conferred allowances must, within 15 calendar days of receiving a non-objection notice for conferral of application-specific allowances pursuant to § 84.13(h) or for inter-company transfer of consumption allowances pursuant to § 84.19(a).
units.actor: entities anticipating being importer of record or receiving transferred/conferred allowances
units.action_summary: Specified entities must submit the information in (c)(9)(ii) by Nov 15 (if anticipating being importer of record) or within 15 days of receiving certain notices if not issued allowances by EPA.

units.obligation_text: Names of all subsidiaries,
units.action_summary: Entities must submit names of all subsidiaries.

units.obligation_text: Entities commonly owned or majority owned by the same person or persons,
units.action_summary: Entities must submit names of entities commonly or majority owned by the same person(s).

units.obligation_text: Alternative names under which the entity does business,
units.action_summary: Entities must submit any alternative business names.

units.obligation_text: Importer of record numbers, and
units.action_summary: Entities must submit importer of record numbers.

units.obligation_text: If providing information under (b)(9)(i)(A), (B), or (C) of this section: the relationship between the allowance holder and each subsidiary and each entity commonly owned or majority owned by the same person or persons, including alternative names under which each listed entity does business; if applicable, the identity of owners and their respective percentage of ownership; and the quantity and type of allowances to be expended in the calendar year by each affiliated entity, identified by name and importer of record number(s).
units.action_summary: Entities providing prior info must also submit relationships to subsidiaries/affiliates, owner identities and percentages if applicable, and the quantity/type of allowances each affiliated entity will expend in the calendar year.

units.obligation_text: If changes occur to the information previously provided to the Agency, such changes must be transmitted to the Agency at least 21 days prior to expenditure of allowances pursuant to § 84.5(b)(1)(i).
units.actor: entities that previously provided importer information
units.action_summary: Entities must transmit updates to previously submitted information at least 21 days before expending allowances under §84.5(b)(1)(i).

units.obligation_text: Each person meeting the definition of importer for a particular regulated substance import transaction is jointly and severally liable for a violation of paragraph (c)(1) of this section, unless they can demonstrate that the importer of record fulfilled the requirements in paragraph (c)(1) of this section.
units.actor: each person meeting the definition of importer
units.action_summary: Importers are jointly and severally liable for violations of §84.31(c)(1) unless they can show the importer of record met the paragraph's requirements.

units.obligation_text: Each person meeting the definition of importer for a particular regulated substance import transaction is jointly and severally liable for a violation of paragraph (c)(7) of this section, unless they can demonstrate that the importer of record or the importer of record’s authorized agent fulfilled the requirements of paragraph (c)(7) of this section.
units.actor: each person meeting the definition of importer
units.action_summary: Importers are jointly and severally liable for violations of the pre-import reporting requirements in §84.31(c)(7) unless they can show the importer of record or authorized agent complied.

units.obligation_text: Reclaimers must maintain records, by batch, of the results of the analysis conducted to verify that reclaimed regulated substance meets the necessary specifications in appendix A to 40 CFR part 82, subpart F (based on AHRI Standard 700–2016), including instrument calibration, sample testing data files, and results summaries of both sample test results and quality control test results that are in a form suitable and readily available for review. Such records must be maintained for five years.
units.action_summary: Reclaimers must keep batch-by-batch analyses (including calibration and data) verifying reclaimed substances meet appendix A specs; records must be kept for five years.

units.obligation_text: Recyclers must maintain records of the names and addresses of persons sending them material for recycling and the quantity of the material (the combined mass of regulated substance and contaminants) by regulated substance sent to them for recycling. Such records must be maintained on a transactional basis for five years.
units.action_summary: Recyclers must keep transactional records (names, addresses, and quantities by regulated substance) for five years.

units.obligation_text: Recyclers must maintain dated records of batch tests of regulated substances packaged for sale or distribution, including instrument calibration, sample testing data files, and results summaries of both sample test results and quality control test results that are in a form suitable and readily available for review.
units.action_summary: Recyclers must keep dated batch test records (calibration, data files, summaries) for substances packaged for sale or distribution.

units.obligation_text: Repackagers must maintain dated records of batch tests of regulated substances packaged for sale or distribution, including instrument calibration, sample testing data files, and results summaries of both sample test results and quality control test results that are in a form suitable and readily available for review.
units.action_summary: Repackagers must keep dated batch test records (including calibration and data) for substances they package for sale or distribution.

Pesticides; Proposal To Add Chitosan to the List of Active 
Ingredients Permitted in Exempted Minimum Risk Pesticide Products; 
Notice of Data Availability on Chitosan and Chitosan Salts

AGENCY: Environmental Protection Agency (EPA).

ACTION: Notification of data availability.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------

SUMMARY: The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is announcing the 
availability of and soliciting comment on data related to the aquatic 
toxicity of chitosan salts. The EPA seeks public comment on these data.

DATES: Comments must be received on or before June 6, 2022.

ADDRESSES: Submit your comments, identified by docket identification 
(ID) number EPA-HQ-OPP-2006-0766, through the Federal eRulemaking 
Portal at 
https://www.regulations.gov
. Follow the online instructions 
for submitting comments. Do not submit electronically any information 
you consider to be Confidential Business Information (CBI) or other 
information whose disclosure is restricted by statute. Additional 
instructions on commenting or visiting the docket, along with more 
information about dockets generally, is available at 
https://www.epa.gov/dockets
.
    Due to the public health concerns related to COVID-19. The EPA 
Docket Center (EPA/DC) and Reading Room is open to visitors by 
appointment only. The staff continues to provide remote customer 
service via email, phone, and webform. For the latest status 
information on EPA/DC services and docket access, visit 
https://www.epa.gov/dockets
.

FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT: Charles Smith, Director, Biopesticides 
and Pollution Prevention Division (7511P), Office of Pesticide 
Programs, Environmental Protection Agency, 1200 Pennsylvania Ave. NW, 
Washington, DC 20460-0001; main telephone number: (703) 305-7090; email 
address: 
[email protected]
.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:

I. General Information

    The EPA is making two aquatic toxicity reports, submitted by Tidal 
Vision Products, LLC, available for public comment. The EPA seeks input 
from stakeholders on how these reports may be used to inform the 
Agency's assessment of the aquatic toxicity of chitosan and its salts.
    On November 2, 2020, the EPA published ``Pesticides; Proposal to 
Add Chitosan to the List of Active Ingredients Permitted in Exempted 
Minimum Risk Pesticide Product,'' 85 FR 69307 (FRL-10009-24). The 
proposed rule addressed the subject matter of a 2018 petition by Tidal 
Vision Products LLC that requested that the substance commonly known as 
chitosan (also known by its chemical name poly-D-glucosamine) (CAS Reg. 
No. 9012-76-4) be added to the list of active ingredients allowed in 
exempted minimum risk pesticide products under 40 CFR 152.25(f)(1).
    Public comments on the proposed rule discussed these salts. The EPA 
notes that chitosan may form as a salt (e.g., acetate, lactate, 
hydrochloride, and salicylate) when it is solubilized in acids for end 
use product formulation and subsequently applied in the environment. 
The new information submitted by Tidal Vision pertains to these salts.
    As authorized by the Federal Insecticide, Fungicide, and 
Rodenticide Act (FIFRA) section 25(b), the EPA has exempted from the 
requirement of registration certain pesticide products if they are 
composed of specified

[[Page 27060]]

ingredients (recognized active and inert substances which are listed in 
the regulations) and labeled according to the EPA's regulations in 40 
CFR 152.25(f). The EPA created the exemption for minimum risk 
pesticides to eliminate the need for the Agency to expend significant 
resources to regulate products that were deemed to be of minimum risk 
to human health and the environment. Prior to submission of these 
aquatic toxicity reports, the EPA received a petition from Tidal Vision 
Products, LLC, requesting that the substance commonly known as chitosan 
(also known by its chemical name poly-D-glucosamine) (CAS Reg. No. 
9012-76-4) be added to the list of active ingredients allowed in 
exempted minimum risk pesticide products under 40 CFR 152.25(f)(1). 
This matter was the subject of a proposed regulation (85 FR 69307) 
(FRL-10009-24).
    The EPA is considering the information submitted by Tidal Vision in 
its decision regarding whether to finalize the proposal to add chitosan 
to the list of permitted active ingredients, and if so, whether and how 
to address chitosan salts in the exemption.

II. References

    The following is a listing of the documents that are specifically 
referenced in this document. For assistance in locating these other 
documents, please consult the person listed under FOR FURTHER 
INFORMATION CONTACT.

    1. Tidal Vision USA. (2019). Aquatic Toxicology Report by 
Eurofins Environmental Testing Test America. Lab I.D. No. B4345. 
Report Date: June 17, 2019. EPA Master Record Identification (MRID) 
51861901.
    2. Tidal Vision USA. (2019). Aquatic Toxicology Report by 
Eurofins Environmental Testing Test America. Lab I.D. No. B4421. 
Report Date: August 28, 2019. EPA Master Record Identification 
(MRID) 51861902.

Confidential Business Information Claims under the Toxic Substances Control Act

units.obligation_text: Disclosures of information claimed as confidential under TSCA section 14(d)(4), (5), and (6) may be made in accordance with the provisions of the Act, § 2.306 and any applicable EPA guidance required by section 14(c)(4)(B) of the Act.
units.action_summary: EPA may disclose certain TSCA-confidential information under specified statutory and regulatory provisions and guidance.

units.obligation_text: The official purpose for which the information is needed must be in connection with the agency’s duties under any law for protection of health or the environment or for specific law enforcement purposes;
units.action_summary: The purpose for requesting disclosed TSCA-confidential information must relate to health/environment protection duties or law enforcement.

units.obligation_text: EPA notifies the other agency that the information was acquired under authority of the Act and that any knowing disclosure of the information may subject the officers and employees of the other agency to the penalties in section 14(h) of the Act (15 U.S.C. 2613(h)).
units.action_summary: EPA must notify the other agency that the information was acquired under TSCA authority and warn about potential penalties for knowing disclosure.

units.obligation_text: The 10 business day period for notification specified in § 2.209(b)(2) is instead 15 business days.
units.action_summary: The notification period referenced is 15 business days instead of 10 business days.

units.obligation_text: The timeline for notification in § 2.209(d) is replaced by the timeline for notification in 15 U.S.C. 2613(g)(2)(B).
units.action_summary: The notification timeline in §2.209(d) is replaced by the statutory timeline at 15 U.S.C. 2613(g)(2)(B).

units.obligation_text: Under section 14(d)(7) of the Act (15 U.S.C. 2613(d)(7)), any information to which this section applies may be disclosed by EPA when the information is relevant in a proceeding under the Act, notwithstanding the fact that the information otherwise might be entitled to confidential treatment under this subpart.
units.action_summary: EPA may disclose TSCA-confidential information if it is relevant to a proceeding under the Act.

units.obligation_text: However, any such disclosure shall be made in a manner that preserves the confidentiality of the information to the extent practicable without impairing the proceeding.
units.action_summary: When EPA discloses TSCA-confidential information in a proceeding, it must preserve confidentiality as much as practicable.

units.obligation_text: Disclosure of information to which this section applies because of its relevance in a proceeding shall be made only in accordance with this paragraph (e).
units.action_summary: Disclosures in proceedings must follow the procedures set out in paragraph (e).

units.obligation_text: The provisions of § 2.301(g)(2) through (4) apply to disclosures under this paragraph (e).
units.action_summary: The referenced provisions of §2.301(g)(2)-(4) also govern disclosures under paragraph (e).

units.obligation_text: Under section 14(d)(2) of the Act (15 U.S.C. 2613(d)(2)), any information to which this section applies may be disclosed by EPA to a contractor or subcontractor of the United States that is necessary for the satisfactory performance of their work in connection with the Act, notwithstanding the fact that the information otherwise might be entitled to confidential treatment under this subpart.
units.action_summary: EPA may disclose TSCA-confidential information to contractors/subcontractors when necessary for satisfactory contract performance.

units.obligation_text: To a contractor or subcontractor with EPA, if the EPA program office managing the contract first determines in writing that such disclosure is necessary for the satisfactory performance by the contractor or subcontractor of the contract or subcontract;
units.actor: EPA program office managing the contract
units.action_summary: The EPA program office must determine in writing that disclosure to an EPA contractor/subcontractor is necessary before disclosing confidential information.

units.obligation_text: To a contractor or subcontractor with an agency other than EPA, if the EPA program office which provides the information to that agency, contractor, or subcontractor first determines in writing, in consultation with the General Counsel, that such disclosure is necessary for the satisfactory performance by the contractor or subcontractor of the contract or subcontract.
units.actor: EPA program office (in consultation with General Counsel)
units.action_summary: For disclosure to a contractor of another agency, the EPA program office must determine in writing (with General Counsel consultation) that disclosure is necessary.

units.obligation_text: The provisions of § 2.301(h)(2)(ii) through (iv) apply to disclosures under this paragraph (f).
units.action_summary: The referenced provisions of §2.301(h)(2)(ii)-(iv) govern disclosures to contractors under paragraph (f).

units.obligation_text: At the time any information is furnished to a contractor or subcontractor under this paragraph (f), the EPA office furnishing the information to the contractor or subcontractor shall notify the contractor or subcontractor that the information was acquired under authority of the Act and that any knowing disclosure of the information may subject the contractor or subcontractor and its employees to the penalties in section 14(d) of the Act (15 U.S.C. 2613(d)).
units.action_summary: When furnishing TSCA-confidential information to a contractor, the EPA office must notify them it was acquired under TSCA and warn of penalties for knowing disclosure.

units.obligation_text: Under section 14(d)(3) of the Act (15 U.S.C 2613(d)(3)), any information to which this section applies may be disclosed by EPA when disclosure is necessary to protect health or the environment against an unreasonable risk of injury to health or the environment, without consideration of costs, or other non-risk factors, including an unreasonable risk to a potentially exposed or susceptible subpopulation as relevant by EPA under conditions of use.
units.action_summary: EPA may disclose TSCA-confidential information when necessary to protect health or the environment from unreasonable risk, regardless of cost.

units.obligation_text: However, any disclosure shall be made in a manner that preserves the confidentiality of the information to the extent not inconsistent with protecting health or the environment against the unreasonable risk of injury.
units.action_summary: EPA must preserve confidentiality as much as possible when disclosing information to protect health/environment.

units.obligation_text: Disclosure of information to which this section applies because of the need to protect health or the environment against an unreasonable risk of injury shall be made only in accordance with this paragraph (g).
units.action_summary: Disclosures to protect against unreasonable risk must follow paragraph (g)'s procedures.

units.obligation_text: If any EPA office determines that there is an unreasonable risk of injury to health or the environment and that to protect health or the environment against the unreasonable risk of injury it is necessary to disclose information to which this section applies that otherwise might be entitled to confidential treatment under this subpart, the EPA office shall notify the EPA Legal Office in writing of the nature of the unreasonable risk of injury, the extent of the disclosure proposed, how the proposed disclosure will serve to protect health or the environment against the unreasonable risk of injury, and the proposed date of disclosure.
units.action_summary: If an EPA office determines disclosure is necessary to address an unreasonable risk, it must notify the EPA Legal Office in writing including details about risk, proposed disclosure, and date.

units.obligation_text: Such notification shall be made as soon as practicable after discovery of the unreasonable risk of injury.
units.action_summary: The EPA office must notify the EPA Legal Office as soon as practicable after discovering the unreasonable risk.

units.obligation_text: If the EPA office determines that the risk of injury is so imminent that it is impracticable to furnish written notification to the EPA Legal Office, the EPA office shall notify the EPA Legal Office orally.
units.action_summary: If written notification is impracticable due to imminent risk, the EPA office must notify the EPA Legal Office orally.

units.obligation_text: Upon receipt of notification under paragraph (g)(2) of this section, the EPA Legal Office shall make a determination in writing whether disclosure of information to which this section applies that otherwise might be entitled to confidential treatment is necessary to protect health or the environment against an unreasonable risk of injury.
units.action_summary: The EPA Legal Office must make a written determination whether disclosure is necessary to protect health/environment.

units.obligation_text: The EPA Legal Office shall also determine the extent of disclosure necessary to protect against the unreasonable risk of injury as well as when the disclosure must be made to protect against the unreasonable risk of injury.
units.action_summary: The EPA Legal Office must determine how much information to disclose and the timing needed to protect against the risk.

units.obligation_text: If the EPA Legal Office determines that disclosure of information to which this section applies that otherwise might be entitled to confidential treatment is necessary to protect health or the environment against an unreasonable risk of injury, the EPA Legal Office shall furnish notice to each affected business of the contemplated disclosure and of the Legal Office’s determination.
units.action_summary: If disclosure is deemed necessary, the EPA Legal Office must notify each affected business about the contemplated disclosure and its determination.

units.obligation_text: Such notice shall be made in writing, via either electronic notice as described in 40 CFR 703.5(h) or by certified mail, return receipt requested, at least 15 business days before the disclosure is to be made.
units.action_summary: The EPA Legal Office must provide written notice (electronic or certified mail) at least 15 business days before disclosure.

units.obligation_text: The notice shall state the date upon which disclosure will be made.
units.action_summary: The notice to affected businesses must state the disclosure date.

units.obligation_text: However, if the EPA Legal Office determines that disclosure of the information is necessary to protect against an imminent and substantial harm to health or the environment, no prior notification is necessary.
units.action_summary: If imminent and substantial harm is present, EPA Legal Office need not provide prior notice to affected businesses.

units.obligation_text: Claims of confidentiality must be made in accordance with the procedures described in 40 CFR part 703.
units.action_summary: Confidentiality claims must follow the procedures in 40 CFR part 703.

units.obligation_text: Any person who submits information under TSCA or these implementing regulations may assert a business confidentiality claim to information included in such submission.
units.action_summary: Submitters may assert a business confidentiality claim for information in TSCA submissions.

units.obligation_text: Such claim must be made concurrent with submission of the information.
units.action_summary: Confidentiality claims must accompany the submission (be made concurrently).

units.obligation_text: If no such claim accompanies the submission, EPA will not recognize a confidentiality claim, and the information in or referred to in that submission may be made available to the public (e.g., by publication of specific chemical name and CASRN on the public portion of the TSCA Inventory) without further notice.
units.action_summary: If a confidentiality claim is not made with the submission, EPA will not recognize it and may make the information public without further notice.

units.obligation_text: A person asserting a confidentiality claim must submit a statement that the person has: (1) Taken reasonable measures to protect the confidentiality of the information; (2) Determined that the information is not required to be disclosed or otherwise made available to the public under any other Federal law; (3) A reasonable basis to conclude that disclosure of the information is likely to cause substantial harm to the competitive position of the person; and (4) A reasonable basis to believe that the information is not readily discoverable through reverse engineering.
units.action_summary: Submitters must provide a supporting statement certifying they took measures to protect confidentiality, that no other law requires disclosure, that disclosure would likely cause substantial competitive harm, and that the information is not readily discoverable by reverse engineering.

units.obligation_text: The person must also certify that these four statements and any information required to substantiate the confidentiality claim in accordance with paragraph (b) of this section are true and correct.
units.action_summary: Submitter must certify that the supporting statements and substantiation information are true and correct.

units.obligation_text: Confidentiality claims must be substantiated at the time of submission to EPA, unless exempt under paragraph (b)(5) of this section.
units.action_summary: Submitters must substantiate confidentiality claims at submission time unless an exemption applies.

units.obligation_text: In the case of information collected by EPA or on behalf of EPA in person at the site of a TSCA inspection under section 11 of the Act, the affected company must assert its confidentiality claim(s) in writing at the time the information is collected, and then must provide substantiation of its confidentiality claims and the supporting statement and certification described in paragraph (a) of this section within ten working days after the inspection ends.
units.action_summary: For onsite TSCA inspections, the company must assert claims in writing at collection time and provide substantiation and certification within 10 working days after the inspection ends.

units.obligation_text: Information in substantiations may be claimed as confidential. Such claims must be accompanied by the certification described in paragraph (a) of this section, but need not be themselves substantiated.
units.action_summary: Information included in substantiations may be claimed confidential but must include the paragraph (a) certification; the substantiation information itself need not be further substantiated.

units.obligation_text: Unless otherwise specified elsewhere in 40 CFR 700 et seq, answers to the following questions must be provided for each confidentiality claim in a TSCA submission:
units.action_summary: Submitters must answer specified substantiation questions for each confidentiality claim.

units.obligation_text: Please specifically explain what harm to the competitive position of your business would be likely to result from the release of the information claimed as confidential ... explain how disclosure of each type of information would be likely to cause substantial harm to the competitive position of your business.
units.action_summary: Submitters must explain how disclosure would likely cause substantial competitive harm for each type of confidential information claimed.

units.obligation_text: Has your business taken precautions to protect the confidentiality of the disclosed information? If yes, please explain and identify the specific measures ... If the same or similar information was previously reported to EPA as non-confidential ... please explain the circumstances ...
units.action_summary: Submitters must describe precautions taken to protect confidentiality and explain any prior non-confidential disclosures.

units.obligation_text: Is any of the information claimed as confidential required to be publicly disclosed under any other Federal law? If yes, please explain.
units.action_summary: Submitters must state whether the information is required to be public under other Federal law and explain if so.

units.obligation_text: Does any of the information claimed as confidential otherwise appear in any public documents ... If yes, please explain why the information should be treated as confidential.
units.action_summary: Submitters must identify if claimed information appears in public documents and explain why it should nonetheless be confidential.

units.obligation_text: Does any of the information claimed as confidential appear in one or more patents or patent applications? If yes, please provide the associated patent number or patent application number ... and explain why the information should be treated as confidential.
units.action_summary: Submitters must identify related patents/patent applications and explain why the information therein should still be confidential.

units.obligation_text: Is the claim of confidentiality intended to last less than 10 years (see TSCA section 14(e)(1)(B))? If yes, please indicate the number of years (between 1 and 10 years) or the specific date after which the claim is withdrawn.
units.action_summary: Submitters must state if the confidentiality claim is intended to last less than 10 years and specify duration or withdrawal date if so.

units.obligation_text: Has EPA, another Federal agency, or court made any confidentiality determination regarding information associated with this chemical substance? If yes, please provide the circumstances associated with the prior determination, whether the information was found to be entitled to confidential treatment, the entity that made the decision, and the date of the determination.
units.action_summary: Submitters must disclose any prior confidentiality determinations by EPA, other agencies, or courts and provide details.

units.obligation_text: Additional substantiation questions for chemical identity-related claims only. ... answers to the following questions must be provided for each chemical identity-related confidentiality claim in a TSCA submission:
units.action_summary: Submitters must answer additional substantiation questions for chemical identity-related confidentiality claims.

units.obligation_text: Is this chemical substance publicly known ... to be in U.S. commerce? If yes, please explain why the specific chemical identity should still be afforded confidential status ... If no, please complete the certification statement: I certify that on the date referenced I searched the internet for the chemical substance identity ... I did not find a reference to this chemical substance and have no knowledge of public information that would indicate that the chemical is being manufactured or imported by anyone for a commercial purpose in the United States. [provide date].
units.action_summary: Submitters must state whether the chemical is publicly known in U.S. commerce and either explain why confidentiality still applies or provide a specified certification if not publicly known.

units.obligation_text: Does this specific chemical substance leave the site of manufacture (including import) in any form, e.g., as a product, effluent, emission? If yes, please explain what measures have been taken to guard against the discovery of its identity.
units.action_summary: Submitters must state whether the chemical leaves the site and, if so, explain measures taken to prevent discovery of its identity.

units.obligation_text: If the chemical substance leaves the site in a form that is available to the public or your competitors, can the chemical identity be readily discovered by analysis of the substance ... Please explain why or why not.
units.action_summary: Submitters must explain whether the chemical identity could be discovered by analysis if the substance leaves the site and why or why not.

units.obligation_text: Would disclosure of the specific chemical identity release confidential process information? If yes, please explain.
units.action_summary: Submitters must state whether disclosure of the chemical identity would reveal confidential process information and explain if so.

units.obligation_text: Exemptions from the substantiation requirement. Information described in paragraphs (b)(5)(i) and (b)(5)(ii) of this section is exempt from the requirement to substantiate the claim at the time of submission. EPA may identify on a reporting form certain information as exempt from substantiation. Additional assertions of exemption from substantiation may be asserted by the submitter.
units.action_summary: Certain categories of information are exempt from substantiation at submission; EPA may identify exempt items and submitters may assert additional exemptions.

units.obligation_text: Each such assertion must include a detailed explanation for why the information falls within the claimed exemption. If the explanation is missing or inadequate, and the claim is not otherwise substantiated, EPA will place a hold on the submission, as described in paragraph (d) of this section.
units.action_summary: Submitters asserting an exemption must provide detailed explanations; if missing or inadequate, EPA will place a hold on the submission.

units.obligation_text: The following information types are exempt from the substantiation requirement at the time of information submission: (A) Specific information describing the processes used in manufacture or processing of a chemical substance, mixture, or article; (B) Marketing and sales information; (C) Information identifying a supplier or customer; (D) Details of the full composition of a mixture and the respective percentages of constituents; (E) Specific information regarding the use, function, or application of a chemical substance or mixture in a process, mixture, or article; and (F) Specific production or import volumes.
units.action_summary: Specified types of information are exempt from the substantiation requirement at submission.

units.obligation_text: A confidentiality claim for specific identity of a chemical substance, where the submission is made prior to the date on which the chemical substance whose identity is claimed as confidential is first offered for commercial distribution, is exempt from the requirement to substantiate confidentiality claims at the time of submission.
units.action_summary: If a claim for specific chemical identity is submitted before the chemical is first offered for commercial distribution, substantiation at submission time is exempted.

units.obligation_text: This exemption applies where the submitter lacks information to reasonably conclude that the chemical substance has been offered for commercial distribution, where both: (1) The chemical substance is not on the TSCA Inventory, and (2) The substance is otherwise not publicly known to have been offered for commercial distribution.
units.action_summary: The pre-market substantiation exemption applies when the substance is not on the TSCA Inventory and not publicly known to have been commercially distributed.

units.obligation_text: All TSCA submissions and their accompanying attachments that include a confidentiality claim must be accompanied, at the time of submission, by a public version of the submission and any attachments, with all information that is claimed as confidential removed.
units.action_summary: Submitters must provide a public version of the submission (with confidential info removed) at the time of submission.

units.obligation_text: In the case of documents collected by EPA or on behalf of EPA in person at the site of a TSCA inspection under section 11 of the Act, the affected company must provide such public copies at the same time as it provides substantiation of its confidentiality claims in accordance with paragraph (b)(1) of this section, within ten working days after the inspection ends.
units.action_summary: For inspection-collected documents, the company must provide public copies when it provides substantiation, within 10 working days after inspection ends.

units.obligation_text: Only information that is claimed as confidential may be redacted or removed.
units.action_summary: Submitters may redact/remove only information that is claimed confidential; non-claimed information must remain.

units.obligation_text: Generally, a public copy that removes all or substantially all of the information would not meet the requirements of this paragraph (c) of this section and the submission may be temporarily put on hold as deficient.
units.action_summary: EPA may place a submission on hold as deficient if the public copy removes all or substantially all information.

units.obligation_text: Where the applicable reporting form or electronic reporting tool contains a checkbox or other means of designating with specificity what information is claimed as confidential, no further action by the submitter is required to satisfy this requirement.
units.action_summary: If the reporting tool allows precise designation (e.g., checkbox), submitter need not take further action to produce a public copy.

units.obligation_text: For all other information claimed as confidential, including but not limited to information in attachments and in substantiations required under paragraph (b) of this section, the submitter must prepare and attach a public copy.
units.action_summary: Submitters must prepare and attach public copies for claimed confidential information not designated via reporting tool.

units.obligation_text: EPA may hold as deficient submissions with public or sanitized copies that are entirely blank or that are substantially reduced in length as compared to the CBI version.
units.action_summary: EPA may deem submissions deficient and hold them if public copies are blank or substantially shorter than the confidential version.

units.obligation_text: Each confidentiality claim for specific chemical identity must be accompanied by a structurally descriptive generic name for that substance. This generic name must be consistent with guidance on the determination of structurally descriptive generic names developed in accordance with TSCA section 14(c)(4)(A) and 15 U.S.C. 2613(c)(1)(C)(ii).
units.action_summary: Submitters must provide a structurally descriptive generic name consistent with guidance when claiming chemical identity as confidential.

units.obligation_text: At a minimum, the generic name must either: (i) Be identical to the generic name for the same substance included on the non-confidential portion of the TSCA Inventory (if the substance is listed on the TSCA Inventory),
units.action_summary: If the substance is listed on the TSCA Inventory, the generic name must match the Inventory's non-confidential generic name.

units.obligation_text: For substances that are not listed on the TSCA Inventory, mask only the confidential portions of the specific chemical name. ... if the submitter of a proposed generic name wishes to mask more than one such element, the submission must include an explanation of why masking only one element is insufficient to protect the confidential chemical identity.
units.action_summary: For non-listed substances, the generic name should mask only confidential portions; if masking more, submitter must explain why one mask is insufficient.

units.obligation_text: Notwithstanding paragraph (d)(1) of this section, EPA may conclude that a generic name provided with the submission and listed on the current non-confidential version of the TSCA Inventory does not comply with 15 U.S.C. 2613(c)(1)(C). In such cases, EPA will notify the submitting company and proceed as described in paragraph (c)(4) of this section.
units.action_summary: EPA may determine a proposed generic name is noncompliant and will notify the submitter and proceed as specified.

units.obligation_text: A generic name that meets the requirements of section 14(c)(1)(C) of the Act prior to the date on which the chemical substance is first offered for commercial distribution for the purposes of a pre-market submission may not be sufficient for the purposes of subsequent listing on the TSCA Inventory ... In such cases, EPA will notify the submitting company and proceed as described in § 720.102(f) or § 725.190(f).
units.action_summary: A prior generic name may later be insufficient for Inventory listing; in such cases EPA will notify the submitter and follow the referenced procedures.

units.obligation_text: If EPA concludes that the proposed generic name does not comply with 15 U.S.C. 2613(c)(1)(C), EPA will notify the submitter, and provide 10 business days for the submitter to provide a revised generic name.
units.action_summary: If EPA finds the generic name noncompliant, it will notify the submitter and give 10 business days for a revised generic name.

units.obligation_text: If EPA concludes that the revised generic name is still not acceptable, EPA will hold the submission for an additional period of up to 10 business days, and proceed as set out in paragraph (e) of this section.
units.action_summary: If a revised generic name is still unacceptable, EPA will hold the submission for up to 10 business days and proceed under paragraph (e).

units.obligation_text: A confidentiality claim under TSCA is deficient if it meets one or more of the following criteria: (i) The confidentiality claim is not accompanied by the supporting statement and certification required by paragraph (a) of this section; (ii) The confidentiality claim is not accompanied by the substantiation required by paragraph (b) of this section ...; (iii) The confidentiality claim is not accompanied by a public copy that meets the requirements of paragraph (c) of this section; (iv) The confidentiality claim is for a specific chemical identity and is not accompanied by a generic name that meets the requirements of paragraph (d) of this section.
units.action_summary: A confidentiality claim is defined as deficient if it lacks required supporting statement, substantiation, compliant public copy, or required generic name.

units.obligation_text: A submission that is identified as deficient under paragraph (e)(1) of this section will be held for a period of up to 10 business days, and the submitter will be notified via CDX as described in paragraph (h) of this section.
units.action_summary: EPA will hold deficient submissions for up to 10 business days and notify the submitter via CDX.

units.obligation_text: During the hold, which commences on the day the CDX notice is sent, any applicable review period for the underlying submission will be suspended until either the deficiency is corrected or the 10 business days elapse without such correction. If the deficiency is not remedied during the suspension, EPA will proceed with review of the submission and may deny the CBI claim(s).
units.action_summary: During the hold EPA will suspend review until deficiency is fixed or 10 business days pass; if not remedied, EPA will resume review and may deny the CBI claim.

units.obligation_text: Except in the case of information subpoenaed under TSCA section 11(c) or materials collected or requested by EPA as part of an inspection under TSCA section 11(a), TSCA submissions bearing confidentiality claims must be submitted via CDX.
units.action_summary: Submitters must submit TSCA confidentiality-claim-bearing submissions via CDX, except for subpoenaed or certain inspection materials.

units.obligation_text: You must use CISS to complete and submit TSCA submissions via CDX.
units.action_summary: Submitters must use CISS to prepare and submit TSCA submissions through CDX.

units.obligation_text: Submitters of health and safety studies or information from such studies must provide such data in templated form, using an appropriate OECD harmonized template, if such template is available for the data type.
units.actor: submitters of health and safety studies
units.action_summary: Submitters must use appropriate OECD harmonized templates to report health and safety study data when available.

units.obligation_text: Submission of templated data is not a substitute for submitting a full study report where a specific TSCA rule or order requires submission of the full study report (e.g., § 720.50(a), or according to the terms of a specific order under TSCA section 5(e)).
units.action_summary: Templated data cannot replace a full study report when a TSCA rule or order requires the full report.

units.obligation_text: To facilitate ongoing or future communication concerning TSCA submissions, current contact information for all of the individuals associated with a particular TSCA submission must be maintained.
units.action_summary: Submitters/companies must maintain current contact information for all individuals associated with a TSCA submission.

units.obligation_text: Contact information for all the individuals associated with a particular TSCA submission must be updated by amending the submission via CDX, except that submissions that are either no longer accessible to the submitting company or that were not submitted via CDX ... updated company contact must be provided via CDX using the appropriate EPA-provided electronic reporting application in CISS.
units.action_summary: Submitters must update contact information by amending the submission via CDX; if submission not accessible or not submitted via CDX, update via CDX using CISS application.

units.obligation_text: In circumstances where ownership of the company or unit of a company has changed ... a notice of transfer of ownership must be directed to EPA via CDX.
units.action_summary: When company ownership changes, a notice of transfer must be sent to EPA via CDX.

units.obligation_text: When EPA contacts a TSCA submitter concerning confidentiality claims ... EPA may provide notices and other correspondence to the submitter via CDX, using the contact information provided in the most recent version of the submission, or using the contact information provided in a more recent notice of transfer of ownership relating to that submission.
units.action_summary: EPA may send notices about confidentiality claims via CDX using the latest contact information on file.

units.obligation_text: EPA will publish on its website, or other appropriate platform, a list of TSCA submissions with confidentiality claims that are approaching the end of the ten-year period of protection described in TSCA section 14(e). TSCA submissions will be added to this list at least 60 days prior to the end of the ten-year period of protection, along with instructions for reasserting and substantiating expiring claims.
units.action_summary: EPA will publish a list of submissions with expiring confidentiality claims at least 60 days before the 10-year protection period ends and provide instructions for reassertion.

units.obligation_text: When a confidentiality claim is being reviewed pursuant to TSCA section 14(f), EPA will provide, when necessary, notice of such review and an opportunity to substantiate or resubstantiate the affected confidentiality claim to the submitter using the contact information for the authorized official or technical contact provided in the most recent version of the submission or in a more recent notice of transfer of ownership relating to that submission.
units.action_summary: During TSCA section 14(f) reviews, EPA will, when necessary, notify submitters and provide an opportunity to (re)substantiate claims using the authorized contact information.

units.obligation_text: Where the submission with the relevant CBI claim was not originally made via CDX, EPA will send the notice via courier or US Mail to the company address provided in the most recent TSCA submission made by that company, or via other means that allows verification of the fact and date of receipt.
units.action_summary: If a submission was not originally made via CDX, EPA will send notices by courier, US Mail, or other verifiable means to the company's address on record.

units.obligation_text: The notice will provide instructions for substantiating claims that were exempt from substantiation when the confidentiality claim was asserted or for which the submitter was otherwise not required to provide substantiation at the time of initial submission, and for updating or re-substantiating as necessary any claims that were previously substantiated.
units.action_summary: The notice will instruct recipients how to substantiate exempt claims or to update/resubstantiate previously substantiated claims.

units.obligation_text: TSCA confidentiality claims may be voluntarily withdrawn by the submitter at any time.
units.action_summary: Submitters may voluntarily withdraw TSCA confidentiality claims at any time.

units.obligation_text: Confidentiality claims in TSCA submissions that were originally made via electronic submission may be withdrawn by reopening the submission in CDX, removing confidentiality markings (e.g., confidential checkmarks or bracketing), revising sanitized attachments or copies as appropriate, and then resubmitting the submission.
units.action_summary: Submitters can withdraw electronic confidentiality claims by reopening the CDX submission, removing confidentiality markings, revising public copies, and resubmitting.

units.obligation_text: For submissions that were not originally made via CDX, or that are no longer accessible to the submitting company via CDX, confidentiality claims may also be withdrawn via CDX using the 'TSCA Communications' application or successor system. The withdrawal correspondence must indicate the case or document number (or other applicable document identifier or document identifying details) from which CBI claims are being withdrawn, identify the submitting company, and include a list or description of the information for which CBI claims are being withdrawn, including page numbers where relevant. Current contact information for the person withdrawing the claim must also be provided, in the event EPA needs clarification concerning which claim or claims are being withdrawn.
units.action_summary: For non-CDX-original or inaccessible submissions, submitters may withdraw claims via CDX TSCA Communications and must include identifying details, company identity, description/list of information withdrawn, and current contact info.

units.obligation_text: Beginning two years after the effective date of the FIP, no owner or operator shall emit SO2 from Boilerhouse 2 in excess of the following limits:
