units.action_summary: If Airbus mod 157517 was embodied in production and no old-P/N FCDs are installed at the AD effective date, the airplane is compliant with (g)(1) and (g)(3).

units.obligation_text: An airplane on which Airbus modification 157519 or modification 157521 has been embodied in production is compliant with the requirements of paragraph (g)(2) of this AD.
units.action_summary: If Airbus mod 157519 or 157521 was embodied in production, the airplane is compliant with (g)(2).

units.obligation_text: As of the effective date of this AD, do not install on any airplane an FCD part number identified as 'Old P/N' in table 1 to paragraphs (g), (h), (i), and (k) of this AD.
units.action_summary: From the AD effective date, installation of any listed old P/N FCD on any airplane is prohibited.

units.obligation_text: Installation on an airplane of right-hand and left-hand FCD, having a part number approved after the effective date of this AD, is equal to compliance with the requirements of paragraphs (g)(1) and (g)(3) of this AD for that airplane only, provided the conditions specified in paragraphs (l)(1) and (l)(2) of this AD are met.
units.action_summary: Installing FCDs with post-effective-date approved part numbers counts as compliance with (g)(1) and (g)(3) for that airplane if the listed conditions are met.

units.obligation_text: The part number must be approved by the Manager, International Branch, ANM-116, Transport Airplane Directorate, FAA; or EASA, or approved under Airbus's EASA DOA.
units.actor: approval authorities (Manager, EASA, or Airbus's EASA DOA)
units.action_summary: The part number requires approval by the FAA Manager, EASA, or under Airbus's EASA DOA to meet the condition in (l).

units.obligation_text: The FCD installation must be accomplished in accordance with airplane modification instructions approved by the Manager, International Branch, ANM-116, Transport Airplane Directorate, FAA; or EASA; or approved under Airbus's EASA DOA.
units.action_summary: FCD installation must follow modification instructions approved by the FAA Manager, EASA, or under Airbus's EASA DOA.

units.obligation_text: This paragraph provides credit for actions required by paragraph (g) of this AD, if those actions were performed before the effective date of this AD using Airbus Service Bulletin A320-71-1068, dated December 18, 2015.
units.action_summary: Operators who performed the specified actions before the AD effective date using the earlier service bulletin receive credit for paragraph (g).

units.obligation_text: The Manager, International Branch, ANM-116, Transport Airplane Directorate, FAA, has the authority to approve AMOCs for this AD, if requested using the procedures found in 14 CFR 39.19.
units.action_summary: The Manager may approve alternative methods of compliance for this AD when requested per 14 CFR 39.19.

units.obligation_text: In accordance with 14 CFR 39.19, send your request to your principal inspector or local Flight Standards District Office, as appropriate.
units.action_summary: Requesters must send AMOC requests to their principal inspector or local FSDO as appropriate per 14 CFR 39.19.

units.obligation_text: If sending information directly to the International Branch, send it to ATTN: Sanjay Ralhan, Aerospace Engineer, International Branch, ANM-116, Transport Airplane Directorate, FAA; ... Information may be emailed to: 9-ANM-116-AMOC-REQUESTS@faa.gov.
units.actor: persons sending AMOC information to International Branch
units.action_summary: If sending AMOC information directly to the International Branch, send it to the specified contact or email address.

units.obligation_text: Before using any approved AMOC, notify your appropriate principal inspector, or lacking a principal inspector, the manager of the local flight standards district office/certificate holding district office.
units.action_summary: Operators must notify their principal inspector or local FSDO manager before using an approved AMOC.

units.obligation_text: The AMOC approval letter must specifically reference this AD.
units.actor: FAA Manager or approving authority issuing the AMOC approval letter
units.action_summary: Any AMOC approval letter must expressly reference this AD.

units.obligation_text: For any requirement in this AD to obtain corrective actions from a manufacturer, the action must be accomplished using a method approved by the Manager, International Branch, ANM-116, Transport Airplane Directorate, FAA; or the EASA; or Airbus's EASA DOA.
units.action_summary: Corrective actions required by this AD must be accomplished using a method approved by the FAA Manager, EASA, or under Airbus's EASA DOA.

units.obligation_text: If approved by the DOA, the approval must include the DOA-authorized signature.
units.action_summary: If the DOA approves the corrective-action method, that approval must include the DOA-authorized signature.

title: Airworthiness Directives: The Boeing Company Airplanes

units.obligation_text: We must receive comments by November 28, 2016.
units.action_summary: The FAA must receive comments by November 28, 2016.

units.obligation_text: This AD applies to the Boeing Company Model 737-600, -700, -700C, -800, -900, and -900ER series airplanes, certificated in any category, as identified in Boeing Service Bulletin 737-25-1707, dated September 24, 2015.
units.actor: the listed Boeing Model 737 airplanes / their operators and owners
units.action_summary: The AD is applicable to the specified Boeing 737 models as identified in the referenced service bulletin.

units.obligation_text: Comply with this AD within the compliance times specified, unless already done.
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must comply with the AD within the specified compliance times unless already compliant.

units.obligation_text: Within 60 months after the effective date of this AD: Do the applicable actions required in paragraphs (g)(1) and (g)(2) of this AD, in accordance with the Accomplishment Instructions of Boeing Service Bulletin 737-25-1707, dated September 24, 2015.
units.actor: owners/operators/maintenance personnel of the affected airplanes
units.action_summary: Within 60 months, operators must perform the actions in (g)(1) and (g)(2) following the referenced service bulletin.

units.obligation_text: For all airplanes: Remove the existing lanyard and install new lanyard assemblies in the PSUs.
units.actor: owners/operators/maintenance personnel of all affected airplanes
units.action_summary: Remove existing lanyards and install new lanyard assemblies in passenger service units on all affected airplanes.

units.obligation_text: For Group 2 airplanes, as identified in Boeing Service Bulletin 737-25-1707, dated September 24, 2015: Remove the existing lanyard and install new lanyard assemblies in the life vest panels.
units.action_summary: For Group 2 airplanes, remove existing lanyards and install new lanyard assemblies in life vest panels.

units.obligation_text: The Manager, Seattle Aircraft Certification Office (ACO), FAA, has the authority to approve AMOCs for this AD, if requested using the procedures found in 14 CFR 39.19.
units.action_summary: The Manager, Seattle ACO, may approve alternative methods of compliance (AMOCs) for this AD when requested per 14 CFR 39.19.

units.obligation_text: In accordance with 14 CFR 39.19, send your request to your principal inspector or local Flight Standards District Office, as appropriate.
units.action_summary: Requesters must send AMOC requests to their principal inspector or local Flight Standards District Office per 14 CFR 39.19.

units.obligation_text: If sending information directly to the manager of the ACO, send it to the attention of the person identified in paragraph (i)(1) of this AD.
units.actor: requesters sending information directly to the manager of the ACO
units.action_summary: If sending AMOC information directly to the ACO manager, requesters must address it to the person identified in paragraph (i)(1).

units.obligation_text: Information may be emailed to: 9-ANM-Seattle-ACO-AMOC-Requests@faa.gov.
units.actor: requesters seeking to submit AMOC requests
units.action_summary: Requesters are permitted to email AMOC request information to the specified FAA email address.

units.obligation_text: Before using any approved AMOC, notify your appropriate principal inspector, or lacking a principal inspector, the manager of the local flight standards district office/certificate holding district office.
units.action_summary: Operators must notify their principal inspector (or local FSDO/CHDO manager if none) before using an approved AMOC.

units.obligation_text: An AMOC that provides an acceptable level of safety may be used for any repair, modification, or alteration required by this AD if it is approved by the Boeing Commercial Airplanes Organization Designation Authorization (ODA) that has been authorized by the Manager, Seattle ACO, to make those findings.
units.action_summary: Operators may use an AMOC for required repairs/modifications/alterations if approved by the authorized Boeing ODA.

units.obligation_text: To be approved, the repair method, modification deviation, or alteration deviation must meet the certification basis of the airplane, and the approval must specifically refer to this AD.
units.actor: approving authority (Boeing ODA or other approver)
units.action_summary: Any repair/modification/alteration method seeking approval must meet the airplane's certification basis and the approval must specifically reference this AD.

units.obligation_text: For service information that contains steps that are labeled as Required for Compliance (RC), the provisions of paragraphs (h)(4)(i) and (h)(4)(ii) of this AD apply.
units.action_summary: If service information contains RC-labeled steps, the rules in (h)(4)(i) and (h)(4)(ii) govern compliance.

units.obligation_text: The steps labeled as RC, including substeps under an RC step and any figures identified in an RC step, must be done to comply with the AD.
units.action_summary: RC-labeled steps (and substeps/figures) in the service information are mandatory to comply with the AD.

units.obligation_text: If a step or substep is labeled 'RC Exempt,' then the RC requirement is removed from that step or substep.
units.actor: owners/operators/maintainers and those applying service information
units.action_summary: Steps labeled 'RC Exempt' are not subject to the RC mandatory requirement.

units.obligation_text: An AMOC is required for any deviations to RC steps, including substeps and identified figures.
units.actor: owners/operators/maintainers requesting deviations to RC steps
units.action_summary: Approval via an AMOC is required before deviating from RC-labeled steps, substeps, or figures.

units.obligation_text: Steps not labeled as RC may be deviated from using accepted methods in accordance with the operator's maintenance or inspection program without obtaining approval of an AMOC, provided the RC steps, including substeps and identified figures, can still be done as specified, and the airplane can be put back in an airworthy condition.
units.action_summary: Non-RC steps may be deviated from under accepted methods in the operator's maintenance/inspection program without AMOC approval, as long as RC steps remain achievable and the airplane can be returned to an airworthy condition.

title: Airworthiness Directives: Zodiac Aero Evacuation Systems

units.obligation_text: We must receive comments by January 3, 2017.
units.action_summary: The FAA must receive comments by January 3, 2017 (deadline for submitting comments).

units.obligation_text: Comply with this AD within the compliance times specified, unless already done.
units.action_summary: Affected persons must comply with the AD within the specified compliance times unless already accomplished.

units.obligation_text: Within 30 days after the effective date of this AD: Do an inspection to determine the part number and lot number of the fusible plugs installed in the emergency evacuation equipment (including all inflation valves, reservoir and valve assemblies, and evacuation slides, slides/rafts and liferafts).
units.actor: owners/operators of affected airplanes or persons responsible for maintenance
units.action_summary: Within 30 days after the AD's effective date, inspect evacuation equipment to determine fusible plug part and lot numbers.

units.obligation_text: A review of airplane maintenance records is acceptable to make this determination if the part number and lot number of the fusible plugs can be conclusively determined from that review.
units.actor: owners/operators of affected airplanes or persons responsible for maintenance
units.action_summary: Owners/operators may use maintenance records to determine fusible plug part and lot numbers if they conclusively show the information.

units.obligation_text: If any fusible plug has part number (P/N) B13984-3, stamped with Lot PA-21 or PA-22: Before further flight, replace the fusible plug with a new part.
units.actor: owners/operators of affected airplanes or persons responsible for maintenance
units.action_summary: If inspection finds a fusible plug with P/N B13984-3 and Lot PA-21 or PA-22, it must be replaced with a new part before further flight.

units.obligation_text: If any fusible plug having P/N B13984-3, stamped with Lot PA-21 or PA-22, is identified during the inspection required by paragraph (g) of this AD: At the time specified in paragraph (h)(1) or (h)(2) of this AD, report the finding to Air Cruisers, Attention Kelly Schmidt, 1747 State Route 34, Wall Township, NJ 07727-3935; fax: 732-681-9163; email: aircruisers@zodiacaerospace.com. Include the quantity of fusible plugs scrapped and the name of the company or service center.
units.actor: owners/operators or persons performing the inspection
units.action_summary: If an affected fusible plug is found during the required inspection, report the finding to Air Cruisers with specified information at the times specified in (h)(1) or (h)(2).

units.obligation_text: If any affected fusible plug was identified on or after the effective date of this AD: Submit the report within 30 days after the part number identification.
units.actor: owners/operators or persons performing the inspection
units.action_summary: When an affected fusible plug is identified on/after the AD effective date, submit the report within 30 days after identifying the part number.

units.obligation_text: If any affected fusible plug was identified before the effective date of this AD: Submit the report within 30 days after the effective date of this AD.
units.actor: owners/operators or persons performing the inspection
units.action_summary: When an affected fusible plug was identified before the AD effective date, submit the report within 30 days after the AD becomes effective.

units.obligation_text: As of the effective date of this AD, no person may install on any airplane any fusible plug having P/N B13984-3, stamped with Lot PA-21 or PA-22.
units.action_summary: From the AD effective date, installing fusible plugs with P/N B13984-3 stamped Lot PA-21 or PA-22 on any airplane is prohibited.

units.obligation_text: A federal agency may not conduct or sponsor, and a person is not required to respond to, nor shall a person be subject to a penalty for failure to comply with a collection of information subject to the requirements of the Paperwork Reduction Act unless that collection of information displays a current valid OMB Control Number.
units.action_summary: Agencies may not conduct/sponsor, and persons are not required to respond to, an information collection under the PRA without a valid OMB Control Number; persons shall not be penalized for failing to comply absent a valid OMB number.
units.modal_raw: may not / is not required / shall not

units.obligation_text: All responses to this collection of information are mandatory.
units.action_summary: Responses to this specific information collection are mandatory (when the collection displays the valid OMB Control Number).

units.obligation_text: Comments concerning the accuracy of this burden and suggestions for reducing the burden should be directed to the FAA at: 800 Independence Ave. SW., Washington, DC 20591, Attn: Information Collection Clearance Officer, AES-200.
units.action_summary: Comments on the burden estimate and suggestions to reduce it should be sent to the FAA Information Collection Clearance Officer at the specified address.

units.obligation_text: The Manager, New York Aircraft Certification Office (ACO), ANE-170, FAA, has the authority to approve AMOCs for this AD, if requested using the procedures found in 14 CFR 39.19.
units.action_summary: The New York ACO Manager is authorized to approve alternative methods of compliance for this AD if requested per 14 CFR 39.19.

units.obligation_text: In accordance with 14 CFR 39.19, send your request to your principal inspector or local Flight Standards District Office, as appropriate.
units.action_summary: Requesters must send AMOC requests to their principal inspector or local FSDO per 14 CFR 39.19.

units.obligation_text: If sending information directly to the ACO, send it to ATTN: Program Manager, Continuing Operational Safety, FAA, New York ACO, 1600 Stewart Avenue, Suite 410, Westbury, NY 11590; telephone: 516-228-7300; fax: 516-794-5531.
units.action_summary: If sending AMOC requests directly to the ACO, requesters must send them to the specified Program Manager at the given address and contact details.

units.obligation_text: Before using any approved AMOC, notify your appropriate principal inspector, or lacking a principal inspector, the manager of the local flight standards district office/certificate holding district office.
units.actor: users of approved AMOCs (operators/persons using the AMOC)
units.action_summary: Prior to using an approved AMOC, the operator must notify the appropriate principal inspector or, if none, the manager of the local FSDO/CHDO.

title: Airworthiness Directives: The Boeing Company Airplanes

units.obligation_text: We must receive comments by June 19, 2017.
units.action_summary: The FAA must receive public comments by June 19, 2017.

units.obligation_text: Installation of Supplemental Type Certificate (STC) ST01518SE ... does not affect the ability to accomplish the actions required by this AD. Therefore, for airplanes on which STC ST01518SE is installed, a "change in product" alternative method of compliance (AMOC) approval request is not necessary to comply with the requirements of 14 CFR 39.17.
units.actor: operators/owners of airplanes on which STC ST01518SE is installed
units.action_summary: Operators of airplanes with STC ST01518SE need not request a 'change in product' AMOC to comply with 14 CFR 39.17.

units.obligation_text: Comply with this AD within the compliance times specified, unless already done.
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must comply with the AD within the specified compliance times unless already done.

units.obligation_text: Do the applicable inspections required by paragraphs (g)(1), (g)(2), and (g)(3) of this AD.
units.action_summary: Operators must perform the inspections required by paragraphs (g)(1), (g)(2), and (g)(3).

units.obligation_text: For all airplanes: Within the compliance time specified in paragraph (h) of this AD, do the Zone 1 inspection specified in paragraph (g)(1)(i) or (g)(1)(ii) of this AD. Repeat the applicable Part 1 or Part 2 inspection thereafter at the applicable times specified in table 1 of paragraph 1.E., "Compliance," of Boeing Special Attention Service Bulletin 757–53–0097, Revision 3, dated December 2, 2016.
units.action_summary: Perform the Zone 1 inspection (either method (i) or (ii)) within the compliance time in paragraph (h) and repeat per the service bulletin's table.

units.obligation_text: Accomplishing the preventative modification specified in paragraph (k)(1) of this AD or the replacement specified in paragraph (k)(2) of this AD terminates the inspections required by this paragraph.
units.actor: owners/operators who accomplish the preventative modification or replacement
units.action_summary: If the listed preventative modification or replacement is done, the Zone 1 inspections required by (g)(1) are terminated.

units.obligation_text: Do an external sliding probe eddy current (EC) inspection for cracking of the crown skin panel in the applicable Zone 1 areas specified in, and in accordance with, Part 1 of the Accomplishment Instructions of Boeing Special Attention Service Bulletin 757–53–0097, Revision 3, dated December 2, 2016.
units.action_summary: Perform an external sliding probe EC inspection of the Zone 1 areas per Part 1 of the Boeing service bulletin.

units.obligation_text: Do an external spot-probe-medium-frequency EC inspection for cracking of the crown skin panel in the applicable Zone 1 areas specified in, and in accordance with, Part 2 of the Accomplishment Instructions of Boeing Special Attention Service Bulletin 757–53–0097, Revision 3, dated December 2, 2016.
units.action_summary: Perform an external spot-probe medium-frequency EC inspection of the Zone 1 areas per Part 2 of the Boeing service bulletin.

units.obligation_text: For airplanes on which any crack is found during any inspection required by paragraph (g)(1) of this AD; or any repair is installed that covers any portion of the Zone 1 inspection area specified in Boeing Special Attention Service Bulletin 757–53–0097, Revision 3, dated December 2, 2016; or the optional Zone 1 preventative modification specified in paragraph (k)(1) of this AD is installed: At the applicable time specified in table 2 of paragraph 1.E., "Compliance," of Boeing Special Attention Service Bulletin 757–53–0097, Revision 3, dated December 2, 2016, except as required by paragraph (l)(1) of this AD: Do the Zone 2 inspection specified in paragraph (g)(2)(i) or (g)(2)(ii) of this AD. Repeat the applicable Part 4 or Part 5 inspection thereafter at the applicable times specified in table 2 ...
units.actor: owners/operators of affected airplanes meeting the stated conditions
units.action_summary: If a crack is found or certain repairs/modifications are present, perform the Zone 2 inspection at the times specified in table 2 and repeat per the service bulletin.

units.obligation_text: Do an external sliding probe EC inspection for cracking of the crown skin panel in the applicable Zone 2 areas specified in, and in accordance with, Part 4 of the Accomplishment Instructions of Boeing Special Attention Service Bulletin 757–53–0097, Revision 3, dated December 2, 2016.
units.action_summary: Perform an external sliding probe EC inspection of the Zone 2 areas per Part 4 of the Boeing service bulletin.

units.obligation_text: Do an external spot-probe-medium-frequency EC inspection for cracking of the crown skin panel in the applicable Zone 2 areas specified in, and in accordance with, Part 5 of the Accomplishment Instructions of Boeing Special Attention Service Bulletin 757–53–0097, Revision 3, dated December 2, 2016.
units.action_summary: Perform an external spot-probe medium-frequency EC inspection of the Zone 2 areas per Part 5 of the Boeing service bulletin.

units.obligation_text: Accomplishing the replacement specified in paragraph (k)(2) of this AD terminates the inspections required by this paragraph.
units.action_summary: Replacing the specified crown skin panel terminates the Zone 2 inspections required by (g)(2).

units.obligation_text: For airplanes on which any crack is found during any inspection required by paragraph (g)(1) of this AD; or any repair is installed that covers any portion of the Zone 1 inspection area ... or the optional Zone 1 preventative modification specified in paragraph (k)(1) of this AD is installed: At the applicable time specified in table 3 ... except as required by paragraph (l)(1) of this AD, do the Zone 3 inspection specified in paragraph (g)(3)(i) or (g)(3)(ii) of this AD. Repeat the applicable Part 6 or Part 7 inspection thereafter at the applicable times specified in table 3 ...
units.actor: owners/operators of affected airplanes meeting the stated conditions
units.action_summary: If a crack is found or certain repairs/modifications are present, perform the Zone 3 inspection at the times specified in table 3 and repeat per the service bulletin.

units.obligation_text: Do an external sliding probe EC inspection for cracking of the crown skin panel in the applicable Zone 3 areas specified in, and in accordance with, Part 6 of the Accomplishment Instructions of Boeing Special Attention Service Bulletin 757–53–0097, Revision 3, dated December 2, 2016.
units.action_summary: Perform an external sliding probe EC inspection of the Zone 3 areas per Part 6 of the Boeing service bulletin.

units.obligation_text: Do an external spot-probe-medium-frequency EC inspection for cracking of the crown skin panel in the applicable Zone 3 areas, specified in, and in accordance with, Part 7 of the Accomplishment Instructions of Boeing Special Attention Service Bulletin 757–53–0097, Revision 3, dated December 2, 2016.
units.action_summary: Perform an external spot-probe medium-frequency EC inspection of the Zone 3 areas per Part 7 of the Boeing service bulletin.

units.obligation_text: Accomplishing the replacement specified in paragraph (k)(2) of this AD terminates the inspections required by this paragraph.
units.action_summary: Replacing the specified crown skin panel terminates the Zone 3 inspections required by (g)(3).

units.obligation_text: Within the applicable compliance times specified in paragraphs (h)(1), (h)(2), (h)(3), and (h)(4) of this AD, whichever occurs latest: Do the initial inspection required by paragraph (g)(1) of this AD.
units.action_summary: Perform the initial Zone 1 inspection required by (g)(1) within the latest applicable compliance time specified in (h)(1)-(4).

units.obligation_text: For all airplanes: Before the accumulation of 15,000 total flight cycles.
units.action_summary: Initial Zone 1 inspection must be done before the airplane accumulates 15,000 total flight cycles (one of the timing thresholds).

units.obligation_text: For airplanes on which an external sliding probe EC inspection for Zone 1 ... has been done as of the effective date of this AD: Within 620 flight cycles after accomplishing the most recent external sliding probe EC inspection for Zone 1.
units.actor: owners/operators of airplanes previously inspected with external sliding probe EC
units.action_summary: If a sliding probe EC inspection has already been done, the initial inspection must occur within 620 flight cycles after the most recent such inspection.

units.obligation_text: For airplanes on which an external spot-probe-medium-frequency EC inspection for Zone 1 ... has been done as of the effective date of this AD: Within 200 flight cycles after accomplishing the most recent external spot-probe-medium-frequency EC inspection for Zone 1.
units.actor: owners/operators of airplanes previously inspected with spot-probe medium-frequency EC
units.action_summary: If a spot-probe medium-frequency EC inspection has already been done, the initial inspection must occur within 200 flight cycles after the most recent such inspection.

units.obligation_text: For all airplanes: Within 200 flight cycles or 90 days after the effective date of this AD, whichever occurs first.
units.action_summary: Alternatively, initial inspection must be performed within 200 flight cycles or 90 days after the AD's effective date, whichever is earlier.

units.obligation_text: For airplanes on which a preventive modification has been installed as specified in Part 3 of the Accomplishment Instructions of Boeing Special Attention Service Bulletin 757–53–0097, Revision 3, dated December 2, 2016: At the applicable time specified in table 4 ... do eddy current and detailed inspections for cracking of the applicable areas of the fuselage skin of the doublers, triplers, and fillers of the preventive modification, in accordance with the Accomplishment Instructions ... Repeat the inspection thereafter at the applicable times specified in table 4 ...
units.actor: owners/operators of airplanes with the preventive modification installed
units.action_summary: If the preventive modification is installed, perform and then repeat eddy current and detailed inspections of the specified areas at the service bulletin's table 4 intervals.

units.obligation_text: If any cracking is found during any inspection required by paragraph (g)(1), (g)(2), (g)(3), or (i) of this AD, repair before further flight using a method approved in accordance with the procedures specified in paragraph (n) of this AD. Doing the repair ends the repetitive inspections for the repaired area only.
units.action_summary: If cracking is found during required inspections, repair it before further flight using an approved method; this ends repetitive inspections for that area.

units.obligation_text: Accomplishing the preventative modification, including doing high frequency EC open-hole inspections for cracking in the existing fastener holes, in accordance with Part 3 ... terminates the inspections required by paragraph (g)(1) of this AD, provided the preventative modification is done before further flight after accomplishing an inspection required by paragraph (g)(1) of this AD.
units.action_summary: Performing the specified preventative modification (and associated inspections) terminates the Zone 1 inspections required by (g)(1), if done before further flight after a (g)(1) inspection.

units.obligation_text: If any cracking is found during any high frequency EC open-hole inspection, before further flight, repair using a method approved in accordance with the procedures specified in paragraph (n) of this AD.
units.action_summary: If cracking is found during high-frequency EC open-hole inspections, repair before further flight using an approved method.

units.obligation_text: Replacing the crown skin panel between station (STA) 297 and STA 439, and stringers S–4L and S–4R, in accordance with the Accomplishment Instructions ... or using a method approved in accordance with the procedures specified in paragraph (n) of this AD, terminates the inspections required by paragraphs (g)(1), (g)(2), and (g)(3) of this AD.
units.action_summary: Replacing the specified crown skin panel (per instructions or approved method) terminates the Zone 1, Zone 2, and Zone 3 inspections required by (g)(1)-(3).

units.obligation_text: Where Boeing Special Attention Service Bulletin 757–53–0097, Revision 3 ... specifies a compliance time "after the Revision 2 date of this service bulletin," or "after the Revision 3 date of this service bulletin," this AD requires compliance within the specified compliance time after the effective date of this AD.
units.action_summary: When the service bulletin references compliance times after its revision dates, the AD requires compliance within those times measured from the AD's effective date.

units.obligation_text: Where Boeing Special Attention Service Bulletin 757–53–0097, Revision 3 ... specifies to contact Boeing for repair instructions: Before further flight, repair using a method approved in accordance with the procedures specified in paragraph (n) of this AD.
units.action_summary: If the service bulletin says to contact Boeing for repair instructions, the operator must instead repair before further flight using an FAA/ACO-approved method per paragraph (n).

units.obligation_text: This paragraph provides credit for Zone 1 inspections required by paragraph (g)(1) of this AD, if those actions were performed before the effective date of this AD using Boeing Special Attention Service Bulletin 757–53–0097, dated November 22, 2010 ... Revision 1 ... or Revision 2 ...
units.action_summary: Previously performed Zone 1 inspections done using listed earlier service bulletin versions are credited toward the (g)(1) inspection requirement.

units.obligation_text: The Manager, Los Angeles Aircraft Certification Office (ACO), FAA, has the authority to approve AMOCs for this AD, if requested using the procedures found in 14 CFR 39.19.
units.action_summary: The ACO Manager may approve alternative methods of compliance (AMOCs) for this AD when requested pursuant to 14 CFR 39.19.

units.obligation_text: In accordance with 14 CFR 39.19, send your request to your principal inspector or local Flight Standards District Office, as appropriate. If sending information directly to the manager of the ACO, send it to the attention of the person identified in paragraph (o)(1) of this AD.
units.action_summary: Requests for AMOCs must be sent to the principal inspector or local FSDO; if sent directly to the ACO manager, send to the person identified in paragraph (o)(1).

units.obligation_text: Information may be emailed to: 9-ANM-LAACO-AMOC-Requests@faa.gov.
units.action_summary: AMOC request information may be emailed to the specified FAA email address.

units.obligation_text: Before using any approved AMOC, notify your appropriate principal inspector, or lacking a principal inspector, the manager of the local flight standards district office/certificate holding district office.
units.actor: owners/operators who will use an approved AMOC
units.action_summary: Before using an approved AMOC, notify the appropriate principal inspector or, if none, the manager of the local FSDO/CHDO.

units.obligation_text: An AMOC that provides an acceptable level of safety may be used for any repair, modification, or alteration required by this AD if it is approved by the Boeing Commercial Airplanes Organization Designation Authorization (ODA) that has been authorized by the Manager, Los Angeles ACO, to make those findings.
units.action_summary: AMOCs approved by the authorized Boeing ODA may be used for required repairs/modifications/alterations.
units.modal_raw: may be used (if approved by Boeing ODA)

units.obligation_text: To be approved, the repair method, modification deviation, or alteration deviation must meet the certification basis of the airplane, and the approval must specifically refer to this AD.
units.action_summary: Any AMOC approved by Boeing ODA must meet the airplane's certification basis and specifically reference this AD.

units.obligation_text: AMOCs approved for AD 2011–01–15 are approved as AMOCs for the corresponding provisions of paragraph (g) of this AD; except, as of the effective date of this AD, AMOCs that extend the initial compliance times specified in AD 2011–01–15 are no longer approved for the compliance time extension and the compliance times required by this AD must be complied with.
units.action_summary: AMOCs previously approved for AD 2011–01–15 are accepted for corresponding paragraph (g) provisions, but any AMOC that extended initial compliance times in AD 2011–01–15 is no longer valid for that extension; compliance must follow this AD's times.
units.modal_raw: are approved / are no longer approved / must be complied with

units.obligation_text: The steps labeled as RC, including substeps under an RC step and any figures identified in an RC step, must be done to comply with the AD. An AMOC is required for any deviations to RC steps, including substeps and identified figures.
units.action_summary: All steps labeled RC in service information must be performed to comply with the AD; any deviation from RC steps requires an AMOC.

units.obligation_text: Steps not labeled as RC may be deviated from using accepted methods in accordance with the operator’s maintenance or inspection program without obtaining approval of an AMOC, provided the RC steps, including substeps and identified figures, can still be done as specified, and the airplane can be put back in an airworthy condition.
units.action_summary: Non-RC steps may be deviated from per the operator's program without AMOC approval provided RC steps remain achievable and the airplane can be returned to an airworthy condition.

title: Airworthiness Directives: The Boeing Company Airplanes

units.obligation_text: We must receive comments by October 5, 2017.
units.action_summary: Comments must be submitted and received by October 5, 2017.

units.obligation_text: This AD applies to The Boeing Company Model 777–200, 777–200LR, 777–300, 777–300ER, and 777F series airplanes, certificated in any category, excluding line numbers 1165 and subsequent.
units.actor: owners/operators of the specified Boeing Model 777 airplanes
units.action_summary: The AD is applicable to the listed Boeing 777 models, excluding line 1165 and subsequent.

units.obligation_text: Comply with this AD within the compliance times specified, unless already done.
units.action_summary: Operators must comply with the AD within the specified compliance times unless already complied.

units.obligation_text: Within 24 months after the effective date of this AD: Do an inspection to determine the part numbers (P/N) of the motor-operated valve (MOV) actuators of the fuel shutoff valves for the left and right engines, in accordance with the Accomplishment Instructions of Boeing Service Bulletin 777–28A0034, Revision 3, dated September 25, 2015.
units.action_summary: Within 24 months, inspect the MOV actuator P/Ns for the left and right engine fuel shutoff valves per the referenced Boeing service bulletin.

units.obligation_text: A review of airplane maintenance records is acceptable in lieu of this inspection if the part number can be conclusively determined from that review.
units.action_summary: Maintenance-record review may be used instead of physical inspection if it conclusively determines the MOV actuator P/N.

units.obligation_text: If any MOV actuator not having P/N MA30A1017 (Boeing P/N S343T003–76), is found, do the actions in paragraphs (g)(1) or (g)(2) of this AD, as applicable.
units.action_summary: If an MOV actuator other than P/N MA30A1017 is found, the operator must follow either paragraph (g)(1) or (g)(2) as applicable.

units.obligation_text: For airplanes having airplane information management system (AIMS) 1 installed: Within 24 months after the effective date of this AD, install new engine fuel spar MOV actuators having part number (P/N) MA30A1017, in accordance with the Accomplishment Instructions of Boeing Service Bulletin 777–28A0034, Revision 3, dated September 25, 2015.
units.actor: owners/operators of airplanes with AIMS-1 installed
units.action_summary: Within 24 months, install MOV actuators P/N MA30A1017 per the referenced Boeing service bulletin on AIMS-1 airplanes.

units.obligation_text: For airplanes having AIMS–2, Blockpoint Version 16 or earlier, installed: Within 24 months after the effective date of this AD, do the actions specified in paragraph (g)(2)(i) or (g)(2)(ii) of this AD.
units.actor: owners/operators of airplanes with AIMS-2 BlockPoint v16 or earlier
units.action_summary: Operators of airplanes with AIMS-2 BP v16 or earlier must, within 24 months, perform either action (g)(2)(i) or (g)(2)(ii).

units.obligation_text: Install new engine fuel spar MOV actuators having P/N MA30A1017, in accordance with the Accomplishment Instructions of Boeing Service Bulletin 777–28A0034, Revision 3, dated September 25, 2015.
units.action_summary: Install MOV actuators P/N MA30A1017 per the referenced Boeing service bulletin.

units.obligation_text: Install AIMS–2, Blockpoint Version 17A or later-approved version, in accordance with the Accomplishment Instructions of Boeing Service Bulletin 777–31–0218, dated September 8, 2016.
units.action_summary: Install AIMS–2 Blockpoint Version 17A (or later-approved version) per the referenced Boeing service bulletin as an alternative compliance action.

units.obligation_text: Later-approved versions of the software are only those Boeing software versions that are approved as a replacement for AIMS–2, Blockpoint Version 17A, and approved as part of the type design by the FAA after issuance of Boeing Service Bulletin 777–31–0218, dated September 8, 2016.
units.action_summary: Defines which software versions qualify as later-approved: those FAA-approved as replacements and incorporated into the type design after issuance of the referenced service bulletin.

units.obligation_text: Within 24 months after the effective date of this AD, and after accomplishing the actions required by paragraph (g) of this AD on all airplanes in an operator’s fleet, as applicable, revise the maintenance or inspection program, as applicable, to add Airworthiness Limitation (AWL) 28–AWL–MOVA by incorporating the information specified in figure 1 to paragraph (h) of this AD into the Airworthiness Limitations Section of the Instructions for Continued Airworthiness.
units.action_summary: Within 24 months and after completing paragraph (g) across the fleet, operators must revise their maintenance/inspection program to add AWL 28–AWL–MOVA by incorporating figure 1 into the Airworthiness Limitations Section.

units.obligation_text: after accomplishing the actions required by paragraph (g) of this AD on all airplanes in an operator’s fleet, as applicable
units.action_summary: Revision of the maintenance/inspection program must be done after completing paragraph (g) actions on all airplanes in the operator's fleet.

units.obligation_text: Installation of MOV actuator part number (P/N) MA30A1001 (Boeing P/N S343T003–66) and P/N MA20A2027 (Boeing P/N S343T003–56) is prohibited at the following positions:
units.action_summary: Installation of MOV actuators P/N MA30A1001 and P/N MA20A2027 at specified positions is prohibited.

units.obligation_text: Left engine fuel shutoff spar valve position.
units.action_summary: Specifies that the prohibition applies to the left engine fuel shutoff spar valve position.

units.obligation_text: Right engine fuel shutoff spar valve position.
units.action_summary: Specifies that the prohibition applies to the right engine fuel shutoff spar valve position.

units.obligation_text: Accomplishment of the actions required by paragraphs (g) and (h) of this AD terminates all requirements of AD 2015–19–01.
units.action_summary: If paragraphs (g) and (h) are accomplished, this AD terminates all requirements of AD 2015–19–01.

units.obligation_text: This paragraph provides credit for actions specified in paragraph (g)(2)(ii) of this AD, if AIMS–2 Blockpoint Version 17 or 17.1 was installed before the effective date of this AD either in production or using Boeing Special Attention Service Bulletin 777–31–0227, dated November 7, 2014; or Revision 1, dated August 12, 2015.
units.action_summary: Operators who installed AIMS-2 Blockpoint Version 17 or 17.1 before the effective date (in production or via the specified service bulletin) receive credit for paragraph (g)(2)(ii) actions.

units.obligation_text: The Manager, Seattle ACO Branch, FAA, has the authority to approve AMOCs for this AD, if requested using the procedures found in 14 CFR 39.19.
units.action_summary: The Manager of the Seattle ACO Branch is authorized to approve alternative methods of compliance (AMOCs) for this AD when requested per 14 CFR 39.19.

units.obligation_text: In accordance with 14 CFR 39.19, send your request to your principal inspector or local Flight Standards District Office, as appropriate. If sending information directly to the manager of the certification office, send it to the attention of the person identified in paragraph (l)(1) of this AD. Information may be emailed to: 9-ANM-Seattle-ACO-AMOC-Requests@faa.gov.
units.action_summary: AMOC requests must be submitted per 14 CFR 39.19 to the principal inspector or local FSDO, or sent to the certification office manager as specified; requests may be emailed to the provided address.

units.obligation_text: Before using any approved AMOC, notify your appropriate principal inspector, or lacking a principal inspector, the manager of the local flight standards district office/certificate holding district office.
units.action_summary: Operators must notify their principal inspector (or local FSDO manager if no principal inspector) before using any approved AMOC.

units.obligation_text: An AMOC that provides an acceptable level of safety may be used for any repair, modification, or alteration required by this AD if it is approved by the Boeing Commercial Airplanes Organization Designation Authorization (ODA) that has been authorized by the Manager, Seattle ACO Branch, to make those findings.
units.action_summary: Operators may use an AMOC for required repairs/modifications if it has been approved by the Boeing ODA authorized by the Seattle ACO Manager.

units.obligation_text: To be approved, the repair method, modification deviation, or alteration deviation must meet the certification basis of the airplane, and the approval must specifically refer to this AD.
units.actor: Boeing ODA / applicants seeking AMOC approval
units.action_summary: To obtain approval, the proposed repair/modification must meet the airplane's certification basis and the approval must explicitly reference this AD.

units.obligation_text: The steps labeled as RC, including substeps under an RC step and any figures identified in an RC step, must be done to comply with the AD. An AMOC is required for any deviations to RC steps, including substeps and identified figures.
units.action_summary: All steps labeled 'Required for Compliance' (RC), including their substeps and figures, must be performed; any deviation requires an AMOC.

units.obligation_text: Steps not labeled as RC may be deviated from using accepted methods in accordance with the operator’s maintenance or inspection program without obtaining approval of an AMOC, provided the RC steps, including substeps and identified figures, can still be done as specified, and the airplane can be put back in an airworthy condition.
units.action_summary: Non-RC steps may be deviated from using accepted methods per the operator's maintenance program without AMOC approval, provided RC steps remain executable and the airplane can be returned to an airworthy condition.

title: Airworthiness Directives: The Boeing Company Airplanes

units.obligation_text: We must receive comments by December 26, 2017.
units.action_summary: FAA must receive comments by Dec 26, 2017.

units.obligation_text: Comply with this AD within the compliance times specified, unless already done.
units.actor: Owners/operators of the affected airplanes (persons subject to this AD)
units.action_summary: Operators must comply with the AD within the specified compliance times unless already complied.

units.obligation_text: Prior to reaching the compliance times specified in paragraph (i)(1)(i), (i)(2)(i), (j)(1)(i), or (j)(2)(i) of this AD, as applicable, or within 12 months after the effective date of this AD, whichever occurs later: Incorporate a revision into the maintenance or inspection program, as applicable, that provides no less than the required damage tolerance rating (DTR) for each SSI listed in the applicable service information specified in paragraph (h)(1) or (h)(2) of this AD.
units.actor: Operators/holders of the maintenance or inspection program for affected airplanes
units.action_summary: Before specified times or within 12 months after effective date (whichever is later), incorporate a revision into the maintenance/inspection program providing at least the required DTR for each SSI listed in the referenced Boeing service documents.

units.obligation_text: The revision to the maintenance or inspection program must include, and must be implemented in accordance with, the procedures in Section 5.0, "Damage Tolerance Rating (DTR) System Application," and Section 6.0, "SSI Discrepancy Reporting" of Boeing Document D6–35022, "Supplemental Structural Inspection Document for Model 747 Airplanes," Revision H, dated September 2013; and Boeing Document D6–35022–1, "747–400 LCF Supplemental Structural Inspection Document—Appendix A," dated November 2015; as applicable.
units.action_summary: The program revision must include and be implemented according to Sections 5.0 and 6.0 of the specified Boeing documents (as applicable).

units.obligation_text: Accomplishing the revision required by this paragraph terminates the actions required by paragraphs (f), (g), and (h) of AD 2004–07–22 R1.
units.actor: Operators/holders of the maintenance or inspection program
units.action_summary: If the required revision is incorporated, it terminates the listed actions in the earlier AD.

units.obligation_text: For all airplanes except Model 747–400 LCF airplanes: SSIs listed in Boeing Document D6–35022, "Supplemental Structural Inspection Document for Model 747 Airplanes," Revision H, dated September 2013.
units.actor: Operators/maintenance program managers for all airplanes except 747-400 LCF
units.action_summary: For non-LCF airplanes, incorporate SSIs listed in Boeing D6–35022 Rev H into the maintenance/inspection program.
units.modal_raw: must (as part of incorporation in paragraph (h))

units.obligation_text: For Model 747–400 LCF airplanes: SSIs listed in Boeing Document D6–35022, "Supplemental Structural Inspection Document for Model 747 Airplanes," Revision H, dated September 2013; and SSIs listed in Boeing Document D6–35022–1, "747–400 LCF Supplemental Structural Inspection Document—Appendix A," dated November 2015.
units.actor: Operators/maintenance program managers for Model 747-400 LCF airplanes
units.action_summary: For 747-400 LCF airplanes, incorporate SSIs listed in both Boeing D6–35022 Rev H and D6–35022–1 into the maintenance/inspection program.
units.modal_raw: must (as part of incorporation in paragraph (h))

units.obligation_text: For SSIs listed in both Boeing Document D6–35022–1, "747–400 LCF Supplemental Structural Inspection Document—Appendix A," dated November 2015; and Boeing Document D6–35022, "Supplemental Structural Inspection Document for Model 747 Airplanes," Revision H, dated September 2013: Incorporate the SSIs listed in Boeing Document D6–35022–1, "747–400 LCF Supplemental Structural Inspection Document—Appendix A," dated November 2015.
units.actor: Operators/maintenance program managers for Model 747-400 LCF airplanes
units.action_summary: If an SSI appears in both documents, incorporate the SSI listing from D6–35022–1 (the LCF appendix) into the program (it takes precedence).

units.obligation_text: Within 10,000 flight cycles after the replacement of the part with a new part.
units.action_summary: Alternatively, inspect within 10,000 flight cycles after replacing the part with a new part.

units.obligation_text: Prior to the accumulation of 20,000 total flight cycles.

units.obligation_text: Within 1,000 flight cycles measured from 12 months after the effective date of this AD.

units.obligation_text: Comply with this AD within the compliance times specified, unless already done.

units.obligation_text: Remove EEC software standards earlier than SCN 5B/I and install EEC software eligible for installation as follows:

units.action_summary: Remove older EEC software (earlier than SCN 5B/I) and install eligible EEC software.

units.obligation_text: For engines with serial numbers listed in Figure 1, remove the software at next shop visit, or prior to December 2018, whichever occurs first.

units.obligation_text: For engines with serial numbers not listed in Figure 1, remove the software at next shop visit, or prior to July 2024, whichever occurs first.

units.obligation_text: After the effective date of this AD, do not install any software standard earlier than SCN 5B/I into any EEC.
units.action_summary: Prohibits installation of EEC software standards earlier than SCN 5B/I after the AD's effective date.

units.obligation_text: You may email your request to: ANE–AD–AMOC@faa.gov.
units.action_summary: Permits requesters to submit their AMOC request via the specified email address.

units.obligation_text: We must receive comments by February 17, 2017.
units.action_summary: FAA must receive comments by Feb 17, 2017.

units.obligation_text: Comply with this AD within the compliance times specified, unless already done.
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must comply with this AD within the specified compliance times unless already done.

units.obligation_text: At the applicable times specified in tables 1 through 6 of paragraph 1.E., "Compliance," of Boeing Alert Service Bulletin 777–53A0081, dated September 8, 2016: Do detailed inspections for any crack of the left and right side underwing longerons; or do detailed inspections, and high frequency eddy current (HFEC) or ultrasonic inspections, as applicable, for any crack of the left and right side underwing longerons; and do all applicable related investigative and corrective actions; in accordance with the Accomplishment Instructions of ASB 777–53A0081, Revision 0, except as required by paragraph (i)(2) of this AD.
units.action_summary: Perform required inspections (detailed and as applicable HFEC/ultrasonic) of left and right underwing longerons and perform related investigative and corrective actions per the ASB.

units.obligation_text: Do detailed inspections for any crack of the left and right side underwing longerons; or do detailed inspections, and high frequency eddy current (HFEC) or ultrasonic inspections, as applicable, for any crack of the left and right side underwing longerons.
units.action_summary: Either perform detailed inspections alone or perform detailed plus HFEC/ultrasonic inspections (as applicable) for cracks in left and right underwing longerons.

units.obligation_text: Do all applicable related investigative and corrective actions before further flight.
units.action_summary: Any required investigative and corrective actions must be completed before further flight.

units.obligation_text: Repeat the inspections thereafter at the times specified in tables 1 through 6 of paragraph 1.E., "Compliance," of ASB 777–53A0081, Revision 0, as applicable.
units.action_summary: After the initial inspections, repeat inspections at the intervals specified in tables 1–6 of the ASB.

units.obligation_text: Replacing an underwing longeron, including doing all applicable related investigative and corrective actions, in accordance with the Accomplishment Instructions of ASB 777–53A0081, Revision 0, except as required by paragraph (i)(2) of this AD, terminates the repetitive inspections required by this paragraph for that longeron only.
units.action_summary: Replacement of an underwing longeron (with applicable investigative/corrective actions per the ASB) ends the repetitive inspection requirement for that longeron only.

units.section: (h) Repetitive Post-Replacement Inspections and Corrective Actions
units.obligation_text: For airplanes on which any longeron replacement has been done as specified in ASB 777–53A0081, Revision 0: At the applicable times specified in tables 7 through 14 of paragraph 1.E., "Compliance," of ASB 777–53A0081, Revision 0, do detailed inspections of all replaced longerons for any crack, or do detailed inspections and ultrasonic inspections of all replaced longerons for any crack, and do all applicable corrective actions; in accordance with the Accomplishment Instructions of ASB 777–53A0081, Revision 0, except as required by paragraph (i)(2) of this AD.
units.action_summary: For airplanes with replaced longerons, perform required inspections of replaced longerons and corrective actions per the ASB at the times in tables 7–14.

units.section: (h) Repetitive Post-Replacement Inspections and Corrective Actions
units.obligation_text: Do detailed inspections of all replaced longerons for any crack, or do detailed inspections and ultrasonic inspections of all replaced longerons for any crack.
units.action_summary: Either perform detailed inspections alone or perform detailed plus ultrasonic inspections (as applicable) for cracks in all replaced longerons.

units.section: (h) Repetitive Post-Replacement Inspections and Corrective Actions
units.obligation_text: Do all applicable corrective actions before further flight.
units.action_summary: Required corrective actions on replaced longerons must be completed before further flight.

units.section: (h) Repetitive Post-Replacement Inspections and Corrective Actions
units.obligation_text: Repeat the inspections thereafter at intervals not to exceed the applicable time specified in tables 7 through 14 of paragraph 1.E., "Compliance," of ASB 777–53A0081, Revision 0.
units.action_summary: After initial post-replacement inspections, repeat inspections at intervals not exceeding those in tables 7–14 of the ASB.

units.obligation_text: Where ASB 777–53A0081, Revision 0, specifies a compliance time "after the issue date of this service bulletin," this AD requires compliance within the specified compliance time after the effective date of this AD.
units.action_summary: When the ASB gives compliance times referenced to the service bulletin issue date, compliance must instead be within that time after the AD's effective date.

units.obligation_text: Where ASB 777–53A0081, Revision 0, specifies to contact Boeing for appropriate action: Before further flight, repair using a method approved in accordance with the procedures specified in paragraph (j) of this AD.
units.action_summary: If the ASB instructs to contact Boeing, the airplane must be repaired before further flight using a method approved per paragraph (j).

units.obligation_text: The Manager, Seattle Aircraft Certification Office (ACO), FAA, has the authority to approve AMOCs for this AD, if requested using the procedures found in 14 CFR 39.19.
units.actor: Manager, Seattle Aircraft Certification Office (ACO), FAA
units.action_summary: The Seattle ACO Manager may approve AMOCs for this AD when requests follow 14 CFR 39.19 procedures.

units.obligation_text: In accordance with 14 CFR 39.19, send your request to your principal inspector or local Flight Standards District Office, as appropriate.
units.action_summary: AMOC requesters must send requests to their principal inspector or local FSDO per 14 CFR 39.19.

units.obligation_text: If sending information directly to the manager of the ACO, send it to the attention of the person identified in paragraph (k)(1) of this AD.
units.action_summary: If sending AMOC information directly to the ACO manager, it must be addressed to the person identified in paragraph (k)(1).

units.obligation_text: Information may be emailed to: 9-ANM-Seattle-ACO-AMOC-Requests@faa.gov.
units.action_summary: AMOC requesters may email information to the specified FAA address.

units.obligation_text: Before using any approved AMOC, notify your appropriate principal inspector, or lacking a principal inspector, the manager of the local flight standards district office/certificate holding district office.
units.action_summary: Prior to using an approved AMOC, operators must notify their principal inspector or the local FSDO/CHDO manager if no principal inspector exists.

units.obligation_text: An AMOC that provides an acceptable level of safety may be used for any repair, modification, or alteration required by this AD if it is approved by the Boeing Commercial Airplanes Organization Designation Authorization (ODA) that has been authorized by the Manager, Seattle ACO, to make those findings.
units.actor: owners/operators of the affected airplanes / maintainers using AMOCs
units.action_summary: An AMOC approved by the authorized Boeing ODA may be used for repairs/modifications/alterations required by this AD.

units.obligation_text: To be approved, the repair method, modification deviation, or alteration deviation must meet the certification basis of the airplane, and the approval must specifically refer to this AD.
units.action_summary: For an AMOC approval, the repair/modification/alteration must meet the airplane's certification basis and explicitly reference this AD.

units.obligation_text: The steps labeled as RC, including substeps under an RC step and any figures identified in an RC step, must be done to comply with the AD.
units.action_summary: All steps labeled RC in the service information (including substeps and figures) must be performed to comply with the AD.

units.obligation_text: If a step or sub-step is labeled "RC Exempt," then the RC requirement is removed from that step or sub-step.
units.action_summary: Steps labeled 'RC Exempt' are not subject to the RC requirement.

units.obligation_text: An AMOC is required for any deviations to RC steps, including substeps and identified figures.
units.action_summary: Any deviation from RC steps (including substeps/figures) requires approval via an AMOC.

units.obligation_text: Steps not labeled as RC may be deviated from using accepted methods in accordance with the operator’s maintenance or inspection program without obtaining approval of an AMOC, provided the RC steps, including substeps and identified figures, can still be done as specified, and the airplane can be put back in an airworthy condition.
units.action_summary: Non-RC steps may be deviated from using accepted methods under the operator's programs without AMOC approval, so long as RC steps remain executable and the airplane can be returned to an airworthy condition.

units.obligation_text: We must receive comments by April 24, 2017.

units.obligation_text: Comply with this AD within the compliance times specified, unless already done. Within 12 months after the effective date of this AD:
units.action_summary: Comply with the requirements of this AD within the specified compliance times (initial compliance within 12 months).

units.obligation_text: Inspect the affected engines to determine if the compressor front stator case is marked with "RP031" adjacent to the part number. If the case is marked with "RP031," no further action required. If the case is not marked with "RP031," follow the remaining steps in paragraph (f) of this AD.
units.action_summary: Inspect engines for 'RP031' marking; if marked, no further action; if not, proceed with remaining steps.

units.obligation_text: Perform an initial pull force check of stage 1, stage 2, and stage 3 of the compressor VSV actuation system.
units.action_summary: Perform initial pull force checks on stages 1–3 of the VSV actuation system.

units.obligation_text: If any stage requires more than 100 lbs force to move the actuation ring, ream the VSV bores and apply anti-corrosion coating to stage 1, 2, and 3, prior to further flight.
units.action_summary: If pull force >100 lbs on any stage, ream VSV bores and apply anti-corrosion coating to stages 1–3 before next flight.

units.obligation_text: If any stage requires more than 75 lbs and less than or equal to 100 lbs force to move the actuation ring, repeat the inspection within 3 months since last inspection.
units.action_summary: If pull force >75 lbs and ≤100 lbs on any stage, repeat the inspection within 3 months of the last inspection.

units.obligation_text: If all stages require 75 lbs force or less to move the actuation rings, repeat the inspection within 12 months since last inspection.
units.action_summary: If all stages require ≤75 lbs, repeat the inspection within 12 months of the last inspection.

units.obligation_text: Thereafter, continue to perform repetitive pull force checks of stage 1, 2, and 3 of the compressor VSV actuation system and disposition as specified in paragraphs (2)(i) through (2)(iii) of this AD.
units.action_summary: Continue to perform repetitive pull force checks and follow the dispositions in (f)(2)(i)–(iii).

units.obligation_text: Reaming the VSV bores and applying anti-corrosion coating, as specified in paragraph (f)(2)(i) of this AD, is terminating action to the repetitive inspections required by paragraph (f)(3) of this AD.
units.action_summary: Reaming VSV bores and applying anti-corrosion coating (per (f)(2)(i)) terminates the repetitive inspection requirement of (f)(3).

units.obligation_text: For airplanes identified in paragraph (c)(1) of this AD: Within 8 years after the effective date of this AD, do an inspection to determine the part numbers of the MOV actuators of the fuel shutoff valves for the left and right engines, in accordance with the Accomplishment Instructions of Boeing Service Bulletin 737–28–1314, dated November 17, 2014.

units.action_summary: If P/N MA20A1001–1 is found, the SB 757-28-0138 instructions for replacing certain part numbers may be used to replace that part number.

units.obligation_text: For airplanes identified in paragraph (c)(3) of this AD, if, during the inspection required by paragraph (g)(2) of this AD, any MOV actuator of the fuel shutoff valves for the left and right engines, or of the APU fuel shutoff valve having P/N MA20A2027 or P/N MA30A1001 (Boeing P/N S343T003–56 or P/N S343T003–66) is found: Within 8 years after the effective date of this AD, replace each affected MOV actuator with an MOV actuator having P/N MA30A1017 (Boeing P/N S343T003–76), in accordance with the Accomplishment Instructions of SB 767–28–0115 R1.

units.obligation_text: The Manager, Seattle Aircraft Certification Office (ACO), FAA, has the authority to approve AMOCs for this AD, if requested using the procedures found in 14 CFR 39.19.

units.obligation_text: In accordance with 14 CFR 39.19, send your request to your principal inspector or local Flight Standards District Office, as appropriate.

units.obligation_text: An AMOC that provides an acceptable level of safety may be used for any repair, modification, or alteration required by this AD if it is approved by the Boeing Commercial Airplanes Organization Designation Authorization (ODA) that has been authorized by the Manager, Seattle ACO, to make those findings.
units.action_summary: An AMOC approved by an authorized Boeing ODA may be used to satisfy repair/modification/alteration requirements of this AD.

units.obligation_text: To be approved, the repair method, modification deviation, or alteration deviation must meet the certification basis of the airplane, and the approval must specifically refer to this AD.
units.action_summary: Any AMOC/repair/modification used must meet the airplane's certification basis and the approval must specifically reference this AD.

units.obligation_text: The steps labeled as RC, including substeps under an RC step and any figures identified in an RC step, must be done to comply with the AD.
units.action_summary: Any procedure steps labeled 'Required for Compliance (RC)' must be performed to comply with the AD.

units.obligation_text: An AMOC is required for any deviations to RC steps, including substeps and identified figures.
units.action_summary: Any deviation from RC-labeled steps requires approval of an AMOC.

units.obligation_text: Steps not labeled as RC may be deviated from using accepted methods in accordance with the operator’s maintenance or inspection program without obtaining approval of an AMOC, provided the RC steps, including substeps and identified figures, can still be done as specified, and the airplane can be put back in an airworthy condition.
units.action_summary: Non-RC steps may be deviated from using accepted methods under the operator's program without AMOC approval, if RC steps remain achievable and the airplane can be returned to an airworthy condition.

title: Airworthiness Directives: The Enstrom Helicopter Corporation

units.obligation_text: We must receive comments by May 1, 2017.
units.action_summary: FAA must receive comments by May 1, 2017.

units.obligation_text: You are responsible for performing each action required by this AD within the specified compliance time unless it has already been accomplished prior to that time.
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must perform each action required by the AD within the specified compliance time unless already done.

units.obligation_text: Before further flight, remove from service any spindle P/N 28–14282–11 or 28–14282–13 that has 1,500 or more hours time-in-service (TIS).
units.action_summary: Remove from service any listed spindle with 1,500 or more hours TIS before next flight.

units.obligation_text: If the hours TIS of a spindle is unknown, use the TIS of the helicopter.
units.action_summary: If spindle TIS is unknown, use the helicopter's TIS to determine compliance.

units.obligation_text: Thereafter, remove from service any spindle P/N 28–14282–11 or 28–14282–13 before accumulating 1,500 hours TIS.
units.action_summary: Remove listed spindles before they reach 1,500 hours TIS.

units.obligation_text: For each spindle with 500 or more hours TIS:
units.action_summary: Condition applying subsequent inspection and related requirements to spindles with 500 or more hours TIS.

units.obligation_text: Using the hours TIS of the helicopter if the hours TIS of the spindle is unknown.
units.action_summary: If spindle hours are unknown, use helicopter hours to determine the 500-hour threshold.

units.obligation_text: Before further flight, unless already done within the last 500 hours TIS, conduct a magnetic particle inspection (MPI) of the spindle for a crack, paying particular attention to the threaded portion of the spindle.
units.action_summary: Perform an MPI for cracks before next flight unless an MPI was done within the last 500 hours.

units.obligation_text: The MPI of the spindle must be conducted by a Level II or Level III inspector qualified in the MPI in the Aeronautics Sector according to the EN4179 or NAS410 standard or equivalent.
units.actor: Level II or Level III MPI inspector / owner/operator (to ensure qualification)
units.action_summary: MPI must be performed by a Level II or III inspector qualified to EN4179 or NAS410 (or equivalent).

units.obligation_text: If there is a crack in the spindle, replace it with an airworthy spindle before further flight.
units.action_summary: Replace any cracked spindle with an airworthy spindle before next flight.

units.obligation_text: Thereafter at intervals not to exceed 500 hours TIS, repeat the MPI specified in paragraph (f)(2)(i) of this AD.
units.action_summary: Repeat the MPI at intervals not to exceed 500 hours TIS.

units.obligation_text: The Manager, Chicago Aircraft Certification Office, FAA, may approve AMOCs for this AD.
units.actor: Manager, Chicago Aircraft Certification Office, FAA
units.action_summary: Manager may approve alternative methods of compliance (AMOCs) for this AD.

units.action_summary: Submit AMOC proposals to the named FAA contact at the provided address/phone/email.

units.obligation_text: For operations conducted under a 14 CFR part 119 operating certificate or under 14 CFR part 91, subpart K, we suggest that you notify your principal inspector, or lacking a principal inspector, the manager of the local flight standards district office or certificate holding district office before operating any aircraft complying with this AD through an AMOC.
units.actor: Operators conducting operations under 14 CFR part 119 or part 91, subpart K
units.action_summary: Operators are suggested to notify their principal inspector or local FSDO manager before operating an aircraft under this AD using an AMOC.

units.actor: Holders of previously approved AMOCs / operators
units.action_summary: Previously approved AMOCs under AD 2015–08–51 are approved for corresponding requirements of this AD.
