Do the actions at the applicable times specified in paragraph 1.E., "Compliance," of Boeing Alert Service 757–53A0108, dated November 14, 2016, except as provided by paragraph (h)(2) of this AD.
units.actor: owners/operators of affected airplanes (except those in paragraph (g)(2))
units.action_summary: Perform all RC-designated actions in Boeing Alert Service Bulletin 757–53A0108 at the specified compliance times, except as modified by (h)(1)/(h)(2).

units.obligation_text: For airplanes on which blended or scimitar blended winglets are installed in accordance with Supplemental Type Certificate ST01518SE: Do all applicable actions identified as "RC" (required for compliance) in, and in accordance with, the Accomplishment Instructions of APB Alert Service Bulletin AP757–53–001, Revision 1, dated June 21, 2017; and Boeing Alert Service Bulletin 757–53A0108, dated November 14, 2016; except as provided by paragraph (h)(1) of this AD. Do the actions at the applicable times specified in paragraph 1.E., "Compliance," of Aviation Partners Boeing (APB) Alert Service Bulletin AP757–53–001, Revision 1, dated June 21, 2017, except as provided by paragraph (h)(2) of this AD.
units.actor: owners/operators of airplanes with blended or scimitar blended winglets installed per ST01518SE
units.action_summary: For winglet-equipped airplanes, perform all RC-designated actions in APB Alert Service Bulletin AP757–53–001 Rev 1 and Boeing Alert Service Bulletin 757–53A0108 at the specified times, except as provided by (h)(1)/(h)(2).

units.obligation_text: Where Boeing Alert Service Bulletin 757–53A0108, dated November 14, 2016, specifies contacting Boeing for instructions, and specifies that action as RC: This AD requires using a method approved in accordance with the procedures specified in paragraph (i) of this AD.
units.action_summary: If the service bulletin says to contact Boeing for an RC action, use a method approved under paragraph (i) instead of contacting Boeing directly.

units.obligation_text: Where Boeing Alert Service Bulletin 757–53A0108, dated November 14, 2016, and APB Alert Service Bulletin AP757–53–001, Revision 1, dated June 21, 2017, use the phrase "after the original issue of this service bulletin" for determining compliance, this AD requires compliance within the specified compliance time after the effective date of this AD.
units.action_summary: When the service bulletins refer to compliance relative to their original issue, treat the compliance time as measured from this AD's effective date.

units.obligation_text: The Manager, Los Angeles Aircraft Certification Office (ACO), FAA, has the authority to approve AMOCs for this AD, if requested using the procedures found in 14 CFR 39.19. In accordance with 14 CFR 39.19, send your request to your principal inspector or local Flight Standards District Office, as appropriate. If sending information directly to the manager of the ACO, send it to the attention of the person identified in paragraph (j)(1) of this AD. Information may be emailed to 9-ANM-LAACO-AMOC-Requests@faa.gov.
units.actor: Manager, Los Angeles ACO; and requesters of AMOCs
units.action_summary: The Manager, Los Angeles ACO may approve AMOCs if requested per 14 CFR 39.19; requests must be sent via the principal inspector or local FSDO or to the specified contact/email.

units.obligation_text: Before using any approved AMOC, notify your appropriate principal inspector, or lacking a principal inspector, the manager of the local flight standards district office/certificate holding district office.
units.actor: owners/operators who will use an approved AMOC
units.action_summary: Notify the appropriate principal inspector or local FSDO/CHDO manager before using an approved AMOC.

units.obligation_text: An AMOC that provides an acceptable level of safety may be used for any repair, modification, or alteration required by this AD if it is approved by the Boeing Commercial Airplanes Organization Designation Authorization (ODA) that has been authorized by the Manager, Los Angeles ACO, to make those findings. To be approved, the repair method, modification deviation, or alteration deviation must meet the certification basis of the airplane, and the approval must specifically refer to this AD.
units.actor: owners/operators/maintainers (subject to approval by Boeing Commercial Airplanes ODA authorized by Manager, Los Angeles ACO)
units.action_summary: Use an AMOC-approved repair/modification/alteration if approved by the authorized Boeing ODA and if it meets the airplane's certification basis and specifically references this AD.

units.obligation_text: Except as required by paragraph (h)(1) of this AD: For service information that contains steps that are labeled as RC, the provisions of paragraphs (i)(4)(i) and (i)(4)(ii) of this AD apply.
units.action_summary: For RC-labeled steps in service information, follow the rules set out in paragraphs (i)(4)(i) and (i)(4)(ii).

units.obligation_text: The steps labeled as RC, including substeps under an RC step and any figures identified in an RC step, must be done to comply with the AD. If a step or substep is labeled "RC Exempt," then the RC requirement is removed from that step or substep. An AMOC is required for any deviations to RC steps, including substeps and identified figures.
units.action_summary: Complete all RC-labeled steps (and substeps/figures) to comply; 'RC Exempt' removes the RC requirement; deviations from RC steps require an AMOC.

units.obligation_text: Steps not labeled as RC may be deviated from using accepted methods in accordance with the operator’s maintenance or inspection program without obtaining approval of an AMOC, provided the RC steps, including substeps and identified figures, can still be done as specified, and the airplane can be put back in an airworthy condition.
units.action_summary: Non-RC steps may be changed per the operator's maintenance/inspection program without AMOC approval, as long as RC steps remain doable and the airplane can be returned to an airworthy condition.

title: Airworthiness Directives: The Boeing Company Airplanes

units.obligation_text: The FAA must receive comments on this AD action by September 29, 2017.
units.action_summary: Receive comments on this AD by September 29, 2017.

units.obligation_text: Comply with this AD within the compliance times specified, unless already done.
units.action_summary: Comply with all requirements of this AD within the specified compliance times unless already accomplished.

units.obligation_text: At the latest of the times specified in paragraphs (g)(1), (g)(2), and (g)(3) of this AD, accomplish electrical power deactivation on the airplane, in accordance with step 2) in "DESIRED ACTION" of Boeing Multi Operator Message MOM–MOM–15–0248–01B, dated April 19, 2015; or Boeing Multi Operator Message MOM–MOM–15–0248–01B(R1), dated April 20, 2015.
units.actor: Owners/operators/maintenance personnel of the affected airplanes
units.action_summary: Accomplish electrical power deactivation on the airplane at the latest of the times specified in (g)(1)–(g)(3), following the referenced Boeing Multi Operator Message.

units.obligation_text: Within 120 days after the last electrical power deactivation in accordance with step 2) in "DESIRED ACTION" of Boeing Multi Operator Message MOM–MOM–15–0248–01B, dated April 19, 2015; or Boeing Multi Operator Message MOM–MOM–15–0248–01B(R1), dated April 20, 2015.
units.actor: Owners/operators/maintenance personnel of the affected airplanes
units.action_summary: Accomplish the electrical power deactivation within 120 days after the last deactivation performed per the referenced MOM.

units.obligation_text: Within 120 days after the date of issuance of the original certificate of airworthiness or the date of issuance of the original export certificate of airworthiness.
units.actor: Owners/operators/maintenance personnel of the affected airplanes
units.action_summary: Accomplish the electrical power deactivation within 120 days after issuance of the original (export) certificate of airworthiness.

units.obligation_text: Within 7 days after May 1, 2015 (the effective date of AD 2015–09–07).
units.actor: Owners/operators/maintenance personnel of the affected airplanes
units.action_summary: Accomplish the electrical power deactivation within 7 days after May 1, 2015.

units.obligation_text: Repeat the electrical power deactivation thereafter at intervals not to exceed 120 days until the software installation required by paragraph (h) of this AD is done.
units.actor: Owners/operators/maintenance personnel of the affected airplanes
units.action_summary: Repeat the electrical power deactivation every 120 days or less until the software installation required by paragraph (h) is completed.

units.obligation_text: The main and auxiliary power unit (APU) batteries do not need to be disconnected when performing the electrical power deactivation.
units.actor: Owners/operators/maintenance personnel of the affected airplanes
units.action_summary: APU and main batteries may remain connected when performing the electrical power deactivation; disconnection is not required.

units.obligation_text: Within 12 months after the effective date of this AD: Install new operational program software (OPS) into each of the six GCUs, do a software check, and do all applicable corrective actions, in accordance with the Accomplishment Instructions of Boeing Service Bulletin B787–81205–SB240063–00, Issue 002, dated June 7, 2016.
units.actor: Owners/operators/maintenance personnel of the affected airplanes
units.action_summary: Within 12 months, install new OPS into each of the six GCUs, perform software checks, and do all applicable corrective actions per the referenced Boeing Service Bulletin.

units.obligation_text: Do all applicable corrective actions before further flight.
units.actor: Owners/operators/maintenance personnel of the affected airplanes
units.action_summary: Complete all required corrective actions before the airplane is returned to service (before further flight).

units.obligation_text: Accomplishment of the actions required by this paragraph on all six GCUs on an airplane terminates the requirements of paragraph (g) of this AD for that airplane.
units.action_summary: Completing the software installation and associated actions on all six GCUs removes the need to continue the paragraph (g) electrical power deactivation requirements for that airplane.

units.obligation_text: For Group 1 airplanes as identified in Boeing Service Bulletin B787–81205–SB240063–00, Issue 002, dated June 7, 2016: Prior to or concurrently with accomplishing the actions required by paragraph (h) of this AD, do the actions specified in paragraph (i)(1)(i) and (i)(1)(ii) of this AD.
units.action_summary: Before or at the same time as performing the paragraph (h) actions, do the specified actions in (i)(1)(i) and (i)(1)(ii) for Group 1 airplanes.

units.obligation_text: Install new fuel quantity management program software and do a software check, in accordance with the Accomplishment Instructions of Boeing Service Bulletin B787–81205–SB280018–00, Issue 001, dated April 17, 2014.
units.action_summary: Install the new fuel quantity management program software and perform the software check per the referenced Boeing Service Bulletin.

units.obligation_text: If any software check fails, before further flight, do corrective actions, repeat the check, and do applicable corrective actions until the software passes the check.
units.action_summary: If the software check fails, perform corrective actions and repeat checks until the software passes; do corrective actions before further flight.

units.obligation_text: Install new common interface control document 9.3 software and do software checks, in accordance with the Accomplishment Instructions of Boeing Service Bulletin B787–81205–SB420006–00, Issue 003, dated October 15, 2015.
units.action_summary: Install the new common interface control document 9.3 software and perform the software checks per the referenced Boeing Service Bulletin.

units.obligation_text: If any software check fails, before further flight, do corrective actions, repeat the check, and do applicable corrective actions until the software passes the check.
units.action_summary: If the software check fails, perform corrective actions and repeat checks until the software passes; do corrective actions before further flight.

units.obligation_text: For Group 2 airplanes as identified in Boeing Service Bulletin B787–81205–SB240063–00, Issue 002, dated June 7, 2016: Prior to or concurrently with accomplishing the actions required by paragraph (h) of this AD, install new common interface control document 9.3 software and do software checks, in accordance with the Accomplishment Instructions of Boeing Service Bulletin B787–81205–SB420006–00, Issue 003, dated October 15, 2015.
units.action_summary: Before or at the same time as performing the paragraph (h) actions, install the common interface control document 9.3 software and perform software checks per the referenced Boeing Service Bulletin for Group 2 airplanes.

units.obligation_text: If any software check fails, before further flight, do corrective actions, repeat the check, and do applicable corrective actions until the software passes the check.
units.action_summary: If the software check fails, perform corrective actions and repeat checks until the software passes; do corrective actions before further flight.

units.obligation_text: For Group 1 and Group 3 airplanes as identified in Boeing Service Bulletin B787–81205–SB240063–00, Issue 001, dated December 22, 2015: This paragraph provides credit for the actions specified in paragraph (h) of this AD, if those actions were performed before the effective date of this AD using Boeing Service Bulletin B787–81205–SB240063–00, Issue 001, dated December 22, 2015.
units.actor: Owners/operators of Group 1 and Group 3 airplanes
units.action_summary: Prior actions performed using the specified Boeing Service Bulletin before the effective date are credited as satisfying paragraph (h) for Group 1 and Group 3 airplanes.

units.obligation_text: For Group 2 airplanes as identified in Boeing Service Bulletin B787–81205–SB240063–00, Issue 001, dated December 22, 2015: This paragraph provides credit for the actions specified in paragraph (h) of this AD, if those actions were performed before the effective date of this AD using Boeing Service Bulletin B787–81205–SB240063–00, Issue 001, dated December 22, 2015, and provided the actions specified in Boeing Service Bulletin B787–81205–SB420006–00, Issue 003, dated October 15, 2015, are done within 12 months after the effective date of this AD.
units.action_summary: Prior actions using the specified Service Bulletin before the effective date may be credited for paragraph (h) for Group 2 airplanes, provided additional actions in the other referenced Service Bulletin are done within 12 months after the effective date.

units.obligation_text: Provided the actions specified in Boeing Service Bulletin B787–81205–SB420006–00, Issue 003, dated October 15, 2015, are done within 12 months after the effective date of this AD.
units.action_summary: The credit in (j)(2) is conditional on performing the actions in the specified Service Bulletin within 12 months after the AD's effective date.

units.obligation_text: The Manager, Seattle ACO Branch, FAA, has the authority to approve AMOCs for this AD, if requested using the procedures found in 14 CFR 39.19.
units.action_summary: The Manager, Seattle ACO Branch, is authorized to approve alternative methods of compliance (AMOCs) for this AD when requested per 14 CFR 39.19.

units.obligation_text: In accordance with 14 CFR 39.19, send your request to your principal inspector or local Flight Standards District Office, as appropriate.
units.action_summary: Submit AMOC requests to your principal inspector or local Flight Standards District Office per 14 CFR 39.19.

units.obligation_text: If sending information directly to the manager of the certification office, send it to the attention of the person identified in paragraph (l)(1) of this AD.
units.actor: Persons sending AMOC information directly to the manager
units.action_summary: When sending information directly to the certification office manager, address it to the person identified in paragraph (l)(1).

units.obligation_text: Information may be emailed to: 9-ANM-Seattle-ACO-AMOC-Requests@faa.gov.
units.action_summary: AMOC request information may be emailed to the specified FAA email address.

units.obligation_text: Before using any approved AMOC, notify your appropriate principal inspector, or lacking a principal inspector, the manager of the local flight standards district office/certificate holding district office.
units.action_summary: Notify your principal inspector or the local flight standards district office/CHDO manager before using an approved AMOC.

units.obligation_text: An AMOC that provides an acceptable level of safety may be used for any repair, modification, or alteration required by this AD if it is approved by the Boeing Commercial Airplanes Organization Designation Authorization (ODA) that has been authorized by the Manager, Seattle ACO Branch, to make those findings.
units.action_summary: An approved AMOC may be used to accomplish repairs/modifications/alterations required by this AD if approved by the authorized Boeing ODA.

units.obligation_text: To be approved, the repair method, modification deviation, or alteration deviation must meet the certification basis of the airplane, and the approval must specifically refer to this AD.
units.actor: Boeing Commercial Airplanes Organization Designation Authorization (ODA) / approvers
units.action_summary: For an AMOC to be approved by the Boeing ODA, the repair/modification/alteration must meet the airplane's certification basis and the approval must specifically reference this AD.

units.obligation_text: AMOCs approved previously for AD 2015–09–07 are approved as AMOCs for the corresponding provisions of paragraph (g) of this AD.
units.action_summary: AMOCs previously approved for AD 2015–09–07 are acceptable for the corresponding provisions of paragraph (g) of this AD.

units.obligation_text: The steps labeled as RC, including substeps under an RC step and any figures identified in an RC step, must be done to comply with the AD.
units.action_summary: All steps labeled 'Required for Compliance' (RC) must be performed to comply with the AD.

units.obligation_text: If a step or substep is labeled "RC Exempt," then the RC requirement is removed from that step or substep.
units.action_summary: Steps labeled 'RC Exempt' are not subject to the RC requirement.

units.obligation_text: An AMOC is required for any deviations to RC steps, including substeps and identified figures.
units.actor: Persons proposing deviations to RC steps (requesters)
units.action_summary: Deviations from RC steps, substeps, or identified figures require approval via an AMOC.

units.obligation_text: Steps not labeled as RC may be deviated from using accepted methods in accordance with the operator’s maintenance or inspection program without obtaining approval of an AMOC, provided the RC steps, including substeps and identified figures, can still be done as specified, and the airplane can be put back in an airworthy condition.
units.action_summary: Non-RC steps may be deviated from using accepted operator maintenance/inspection program methods without an AMOC, provided RC steps remain achievable and the airplane can be returned to an airworthy condition.

units.obligation_text: Provided the RC steps, including substeps and identified figures, can still be done as specified, and the airplane can be put back in an airworthy condition.
units.action_summary: The permission to deviate from non-RC steps applies only if RC steps can still be performed as specified and the airplane can be restored to airworthy condition.

title: Airworthiness Directives: The Boeing Company Airplanes

units.obligation_text: We must receive comments by October 10, 2017.
units.action_summary: FAA must receive public comments by October 10, 2017.

units.obligation_text: This AD applies to The Boeing Company Model 787–8 airplanes, certificated in any category, as identified in Boeing Alert Service Bulletin B787–81205–SB570030–00, Issue 001, dated March 17, 2017, and line numbers 10, 13, 15, 16, 17, 18, and 19.
units.actor: The Boeing Company Model 787–8 airplanes and their owners/operators
units.action_summary: Specifies which Boeing Model 787–8 airplanes are subject to the AD.

units.obligation_text: Comply with this AD within the compliance times specified, unless already done.
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must comply with the AD within the specified compliance times unless actions already completed.

units.obligation_text: For airplanes identified in ASB B787–81205–SB570030–00, Issue 001: Except as specified in paragraph (k)(1) of this AD, at the applicable time specified in paragraph 5., 'Compliance,' of ASB B787–81205–SB570030–00, Issue 001: Do an ultrasonic inspection for any disbond on the left side and right side upper wing stringers; and do all applicable corrective actions; in accordance with the Accomplishment Instructions of ASB B787–81205–SB570030–00, Issue 001, except as specified in paragraph (k)(2) of this AD. Do all applicable corrective actions before further flight. Repeat the inspection of the upper wing stringers thereafter at the applicable intervals specified in paragraph 5., 'Compliance,' of ASB B787–81205–SB570030–00, Issue 001 until the actions required by paragraph (j) of this AD are done.
units.actor: Owners/operators of airplanes identified in ASB B787–81205–SB570030–00, Issue 001
units.action_summary: Perform ultrasonic inspections for disbond on upper wing stringers, perform corrective actions per the ASB, do corrective actions before further flight, and repeat inspections at specified intervals until required modification is done.

units.obligation_text: Do an ultrasonic inspection for any disbond on the left side and right side upper wing stringers.
units.actor: Owners/operators of airplanes identified in ASB B787–81205–SB570030–00, Issue 001
units.action_summary: Perform ultrasonic inspection of left and right upper wing stringers for disbond.

units.obligation_text: Do all applicable corrective actions in accordance with the Accomplishment Instructions of ASB B787–81205–SB570030–00, Issue 001, except as specified in paragraph (k)(2) of this AD.
units.actor: Owners/operators of airplanes identified in ASB B787–81205–SB570030–00, Issue 001
units.action_summary: Carry out all required corrective actions following the ASB's Accomplishment Instructions (with exceptions in paragraph (k)(2)).

units.obligation_text: Do all applicable corrective actions before further flight.
units.actor: Owners/operators of airplanes identified in ASB B787–81205–SB570030–00, Issue 001
units.action_summary: Corrective actions identified by inspection must be completed before the airplane's next flight.

units.obligation_text: Repeat the inspection of the upper wing stringers thereafter at the applicable intervals specified in paragraph 5., 'Compliance,' of ASB B787–81205–SB570030–00, Issue 001 until the actions required by paragraph (j) of this AD are done.
units.actor: Owners/operators of airplanes identified in ASB B787–81205–SB570030–00, Issue 001
units.action_summary: Repeat the ultrasonic inspections at ASB-specified intervals until required modification in paragraph (j) is completed.

units.obligation_text: Prior to or concurrently with accomplishing the actions required by paragraph (g) of this AD, revise the inspection or maintenance program, as applicable, to incorporate Airworthiness Limitation (AWL) 57–AWL–13, 'Inspection Requirements for In-Tank Fasteners and Edge Seal near Disbond Arrestment (DBA) Fastener Installations of Lightning Zone 2,' of Boeing 787 Special Compliance Items/Airworthiness Limitations, D011Z009–03–04, dated February 2017.
units.actor: Owners/operators of airplanes identified in ASB B787–81205–SB570030–00, Issue 001
units.action_summary: Revise the inspection/maintenance program to incorporate AWL 57–AWL–13 prior to or when performing paragraph (g) actions.

units.obligation_text: The initial compliance time for accomplishing the tasks specified in AWL 57–AWL–13 is within 24,000 flight cycles or 12 years, whichever occurs first, after accomplishing the actions specified in ASB B787–81205–SB570030–00, Issue 001.
units.action_summary: Sets the initial compliance threshold for AWL tasks: within 24,000 flight cycles or 12 years after completing the ASB actions.

units.obligation_text: For airplanes having line numbers 10, 13, and 15 through 19 inclusive: Within 60 days after the effective date of this AD, revise the inspection or maintenance program, as applicable, to incorporate AWL 57–AWL–13, 'Inspection Requirements for In-Tank Fasteners and Edge Seal near Disbond Arrestment (DBA) Fastener Installations of Lightning Zone 2,' of Boeing 787 Special Compliance Items/Airworthiness Limitations, D011Z009–03–04, dated February 2017.
units.actor: Owners/operators of airplanes having line numbers 10, 13, and 15 through 19 inclusive
units.action_summary: These specific-line-number airplanes must revise their inspection/maintenance program to include AWL 57–AWL–13 within 60 days after AD effective date.

units.obligation_text: The initial compliance time for accomplishing the tasks specified in AWL 57–AWL–13 is prior to the accumulation of 24,000 total flight cycles or within 12 years after the date of issuance of the original airworthiness certificate or date of issuance of the original export certificate of airworthiness, whichever occurs first.
units.actor: Owners/operators of airplanes having line numbers 10, 13, and 15 through 19 inclusive
units.action_summary: Sets the initial compliance threshold for AWL tasks for the specified-line-number airplanes.

units.obligation_text: After the action required by paragraph (h) of this AD has been done, no alternative actions (e.g., inspections) or intervals may be used unless the actions or intervals are approved as an AMOC in accordance with the procedures specified in paragraph (l) of this AD.
units.action_summary: Prohibits using alternative actions or intervals after paragraph (h) unless approved as an AMOC per paragraph (l).

units.obligation_text: For airplanes identified in ASB B787–81205–SB570030–00, Issue 001, that have not done 'PART 3: PREVENTIVE MODIFICATION' of the Accomplishment Instructions of ASB B787–81205–SB570030–00, Issue 001, at all of the unrepaired areas of the upper wing stringers: At the applicable time specified in paragraph 5., 'Compliance,' of ASB B787–81205–SB570030–00, Issue 001, do the actions specified in paragraphs (j)(1) and (j)(2) of this AD, in accordance with the Accomplishment Instructions of ASB B787–81205–SB570030–00, Issue 001, except as specified in paragraph (k)(2) of this AD. Doing the actions required by this paragraph terminates the repetitive inspections required by paragraph (g) of this AD.
units.actor: Owners/operators of airplanes identified in ASB B787–81205–SB570030–00, Issue 001
units.action_summary: If the preventive modification hasn't been done, perform specified inspection and modification actions at the ASB-specified time; completion terminates the repetitive inspections of paragraph (g).

units.obligation_text: Do an ultrasonic inspection for any disbond on the left side and right side upper wing stringers, and do all applicable corrective actions.
units.actor: Owners/operators of airplanes identified in ASB B787–81205–SB570030–00, Issue 001 that have not done 'PART 3: PREVENTIVE MODIFICATION'
units.action_summary: Perform ultrasonic inspection of upper wing stringers and carry out any required corrective actions.

units.obligation_text: Do all applicable corrective actions before further flight.
units.actor: Owners/operators of airplanes identified in ASB B787–81205–SB570030–00, Issue 001 that have not done 'PART 3: PREVENTIVE MODIFICATION'
units.action_summary: Corrective actions found during the j(1) inspection must be completed before the airplane's next flight.

units.obligation_text: Do the preventative modification in accordance with 'PART 3: PREVENTIVE MODIFICATION' of the Accomplishment Instructions of ASB B787–81205–SB570030–00, Issue 001.
units.actor: Owners/operators of airplanes identified in ASB B787–81205–SB570030–00, Issue 001 that have not done 'PART 3: PREVENTIVE MODIFICATION'
units.action_summary: Perform the preventative modification as described in PART 3 of the ASB Accomplishment Instructions.

units.obligation_text: Doing the actions required by this paragraph terminates the repetitive inspections required by paragraph (g) of this AD.
units.action_summary: Completion of the paragraph (j) actions ends the requirement to perform the repetitive inspections of paragraph (g).

units.obligation_text: Where paragraph 5., 'Compliance,' of ASB B787–81205–SB570030–00, Issue 001, specifies a compliance time 'after the Issue 001 date of this service bulletin,' this AD requires compliance within the specified compliance time after the effective date of this AD.
units.actor: Owners/operators required to follow ASB compliance times
units.action_summary: Replaces ASB references to compliance time 'after Issue 001 date' with compliance time 'after the effective date of this AD.'

units.obligation_text: Although ASB B787–81205–SB570030–00, Issue 001, specifies to contact Boeing for repair instructions, and specifies that action as 'RC' (Required for Compliance), this AD requires repair before further flight using a method approved in accordance with the procedures specified in paragraph (l) of this AD.
units.action_summary: Repairs indicated as RC in the ASB must be done before further flight using a method approved per paragraph (l) (AMOC procedure).

units.obligation_text: The Manager, Seattle ACO Branch, FAA, has the authority to approve AMOCs for this AD, if requested using the procedures found in 14 CFR 39.19.
units.action_summary: Manager, Seattle ACO Branch is authorized to approve alternative methods of compliance (AMOCs) for this AD following 14 CFR 39.19 procedures.

units.obligation_text: In accordance with 14 CFR 39.19, send your request to your principal inspector or local Flight Standards District Office, as appropriate. If sending information directly to the manager of the certification office, send it to the attention of the person identified in paragraph (m)(1) of this AD. Information may be emailed to: 9-ANM-Seattle-ACO-AMOC-Requests@faa.gov.
units.actor: Requesters of AMOC approval (owners/operators, repair stations, etc.)
units.action_summary: Requests for AMOC approval must be submitted per 14 CFR 39.19 to the principal inspector or local FSDO, or to the manager as specified; email provided for submissions.

units.obligation_text: Before using any approved AMOC, notify your appropriate principal inspector, or lacking a principal inspector, the manager of the local flight standards district office/certificate holding district office.
units.actor: Owners/operators intending to use an approved AMOC
units.action_summary: Operators must notify their principal inspector (or local FSDO manager if no principal inspector) before using an approved AMOC.

units.obligation_text: An AMOC that provides an acceptable level of safety may be used for any repair, modification, or alteration required by this AD if it is approved by the Boeing Commercial Airplanes Organization Designation Authorization (ODA) that has been authorized by the Manager, Seattle ACO Branch, to make those findings.
units.action_summary: Operators may use an AMOC approved by the authorized Boeing ODA to satisfy repair/modification/alteration requirements of this AD, provided approval exists.

units.obligation_text: To be approved, the repair method, modification deviation, or alteration deviation must meet the certification basis of the airplane.
units.actor: Boeing Commercial Airplanes ODA (approving entity) / requesters
units.action_summary: Any AMOC repair/modification deviation must meet the airplane's certification basis to be approved.

units.obligation_text: The approval must specifically refer to this AD.
units.action_summary: AMOC approvals must explicitly reference this AD.

title: Use of Automatic Dependent Surveillance-Broadcast (ADS-B) Out in Support of Reduced Vertical Separation Minimum (RVSM) Operations

units.obligation_text: To issue an RVSM authorization under this section, the Administrator must find that the operator’s aircraft have been approved in accordance with Section 2 of this appendix and the operator complies with this section.
units.action_summary: Before issuing RVSM authorization the Administrator must find aircraft approved per Section 2 and that the operator complies with this section.

units.obligation_text: Except as specified in Section 9 of this appendix, an applicant seeking authorization to operate within RVSM airspace must apply in a form and manner prescribed by the Administrator.

units.obligation_text: The application must include the following:
units.action_summary: The application for RVSM authorization must include the specified information (items listed in the regulation).

units.obligation_text: In a manner prescribed by the Administrator, an operator seeking authorization under this section must provide evidence that:
units.action_summary: An operator must provide, per the Administrator's prescription, evidence required for authorization.

units.obligation_text: Each pilot has knowledge of RVSM requirements, policies, and procedures sufficient for the conduct of operations in RVSM airspace.
units.actor: each pilot (evidence provided by the operator)
units.action_summary: Operators must provide evidence that each pilot knows RVSM requirements, policies, and procedures sufficient to operate in RVSM airspace.

units.obligation_text: The operator is authorized by the Administrator to perform such operations in accordance with Section 3 or Section 9 of this appendix, as applicable.
units.action_summary: The operator may perform RVSM operations only with Administrator authorization in accordance with Section 3 or Section 9, as applicable.

units.obligation_text: The aircraft— (i) Has been approved and complies with Section 2 of this appendix; or (ii) Complies with Section 9 of this appendix.
units.action_summary: An aircraft must either be approved per Section 2 or comply with Section 9 to conduct RVSM operations.

units.obligation_text: Each pilot has knowledge of RVSM requirements, policies, and procedures sufficient for the conduct of operations in RVSM airspace.
units.action_summary: Each pilot must have sufficient knowledge of RVSM requirements, policies, and procedures to conduct operations in RVSM airspace.

units.obligation_text: The Administrator may authorize an aircraft operator to deviate from the requirements of § 91.180 or § 91.706 for a specific flight in RVSM airspace if—
units.action_summary: The Administrator may permit an operator to deviate from § 91.180 or § 91.706 for a specific RVSM flight under stated conditions.

units.obligation_text: At the time of filing the flight plan for that flight, ATC determines that the aircraft may be provided appropriate separation and that the flight will not interfere with, or impose a burden on, RVSM operations.
units.action_summary: ATC must determine at flight-plan filing that appropriate separation can be provided and that the flight will not interfere with RVSM operations; this is a condition for Administrator authorization to deviate.

units.action_summary: The Administrator may prohibit or restrict an operator's RVSM operations if the operator is noncompliant or unable to comply with this appendix or subpart H.

units.obligation_text: the Administrator determines that the operator is not complying, or is unable to comply, with this appendix or subpart H of this part.

units.action_summary: RVSM may be applied within all ICAO Flight Information Regions.

units.action_summary: An operator may conduct RVSM flights provided the conditions listed in Section 9 are met.

units.obligation_text: Two operational independent altitude measurement systems.
units.action_summary: The aircraft must be equipped with two independent operational altitude measurement systems.

units.obligation_text: At least one automatic altitude control system that controls the aircraft altitude—
units.action_summary: The aircraft must have at least one automatic altitude control system that controls altitude within specified tolerances.

units.obligation_text: Within a tolerance band of ±65 feet about an acquired altitude when the aircraft is operated in straight and level flight under nonturbulent, nongust conditions;
units.action_summary: The automatic altitude control system must control altitude within ±65 feet in straight-and-level, nonturbulent, nongust conditions.

units.obligation_text: Within a tolerance band of ±130 feet under nonturbulent, nongust conditions for aircraft for which application for type certification occurred on or before April 9, 1997 that are equipped with an automatic altitude control system with flight management/ performance system inputs.
units.actor: the aircraft/automatic altitude control system (older type-certified aircraft)
units.action_summary: For aircraft with type certification application on or before April 9, 1997 with FMS/performance inputs, the automatic altitude control system must control altitude within ±130 feet in nonturbulent, nongust conditions.

units.obligation_text: An altitude alert system that signals an alert when the altitude displayed to the flight crew deviates from the selected altitude by more than—
units.action_summary: The aircraft must have an altitude alert system that signals alerts when displayed altitude deviates from the selected altitude beyond specified thresholds.

units.obligation_text: ±300 feet for aircraft for which application for type certification was made on or before April 9, 1997;
units.actor: the aircraft/altitude alert system (older type-certified aircraft)
units.action_summary: For aircraft with type certification application on or before April 9, 1997, the altitude alert system must signal when deviation exceeds ±300 feet.

units.obligation_text: ±200 feet for aircraft for which application for type certification is made after April 9, 1997.
units.actor: the aircraft/altitude alert system (later type-certified aircraft)
units.action_summary: For aircraft with type certification application after April 9, 1997, the altitude alert system must signal when deviation exceeds ±200 feet.

units.obligation_text: A TCAS II that meets TSO C–119b (Version 7.0), or a later version, if equipped with TCAS II, unless otherwise authorized by the Administrator.
units.action_summary: If equipped with TCAS II, the aircraft must have TCAS II meeting TSO C-119b (v7.0) or later, unless the Administrator authorizes otherwise.

units.obligation_text: unless otherwise authorized by the Administrator.
units.action_summary: The Administrator may authorize an exception to the TCAS II equipment requirement.

units.obligation_text: Unless authorized by ATC or the foreign country where the aircraft is operated, an ADS–B Out system that meets the equipment performance requirements of § 91.227 of this part.
units.action_summary: The aircraft must have an ADS-B Out system meeting § 91.227 performance requirements unless ATC or the foreign country authorizes otherwise.

units.obligation_text: Unless authorized by ATC or the foreign country where the aircraft is operated,
units.action_summary: ATC or the foreign country may authorize an aircraft to operate without the ADS-B Out system otherwise required.

units.obligation_text: The aircraft must have its height-keeping performance monitored in a form and manner acceptable to the Administrator.
units.action_summary: The aircraft's height-keeping performance must be monitored in a form and manner acceptable to the Administrator.

units.obligation_text: The altimetry system error (ASE) of the aircraft does not exceed 200 feet when operating in RVSM airspace.
units.action_summary: The aircraft's altimetry system error must be 200 feet or less when operating in RVSM airspace.

title: Airworthiness Directives: Piper Aircraft, Inc. Airplanes

units.obligation_text: We must receive comments by December 22, 2017.

units.obligation_text: Comply with this AD within the compliance times specified, unless already done.
units.actor: the owner/operator of the affected airplanes (persons subject to this AD)
units.action_summary: Affected persons must comply with the AD within the specified compliance times unless already done.

units.obligation_text: Within the next 100 hours time-in-service (TIS) after the effective date of this AD or within the next 12 months after the effective date of this AD, whichever occurs first, inspect the lower wing skin near the main wing spar on both wings for the presence of an inspection access panel using Part I of the Instructions section of Piper Aircraft, Inc. Service Bulletin (SB) No. 1304, dated August 23, 2017.
units.actor: the owner/operator of the affected airplanes
units.action_summary: Within the specified timeframe, inspect the lower wing skin near the main wing spars on both wings for inspection access panels using the specified Piper SB instructions.

units.obligation_text: If it is determined that no inspection access panels are present during the inspection required in paragraph (g) of this AD, within the next 100 hours TIS after the effective date of this AD or within the next 12 months after the effective date of this AD, whichever occurs first install inspection access panels on the lower skin of the left wing and the right wing using Piper SB No. 1304, dated August 23, 2017.
units.actor: the owner/operator of the affected airplanes
units.action_summary: If no access panels are present, within the specified timeframe install inspection access panels on both wings using the specified Piper SB.

units.obligation_text: Within the next 100 hours TIS after the effective date of this AD or within the next 12 months after the effective date of this AD, whichever occurs first, inspect the left and the right main wing spar for any evidence of corrosion using Part I of the Instructions section of Piper SB No. 1304, dated August 23, 2017.
units.actor: the owner/operator of the affected airplanes
units.action_summary: Within the specified timeframe, inspect both main wing spars for any evidence of corrosion using the specified Piper SB instructions.

units.obligation_text: Before further flight after the inspection required in paragraph (i) of this AD, if evidence of corrosion is found, take all necessary corrective actions to remove the corrosion using Part I of the Instructions section of Piper SB No. 1304, dated August 23, 2017, and/or make all necessary repairs using Part II of the Instructions section of Piper SB No. 1304, dated August 23, 2017.
units.actor: the owner/operator of the affected airplanes
units.action_summary: If corrosion is found in the inspection, take all necessary corrective actions and repairs using the specified Piper SB before further flight.

units.obligation_text: For service information that contains steps that are labeled as Required for Compliance (RC), the provisions of paragraphs (g) through (j) of this AD apply.

units.action_summary: If service information contains RC steps, the requirements of paragraphs (g) through (j) apply.

units.obligation_text: The steps labeled as RC, including substeps under an RC step and any figures identified in an RC step, must be done to comply with the AD.

title: Recognition of Pilot in Command Experience in the Military and in Air Carrier Operations

units.obligation_text: 250 hours of flight time in an airplane as a pilot in command, or as second in command performing the duties of pilot in command while under the supervision of a pilot in command, or any combination thereof, subject to the following:
units.actor: an applicant for an airplane category rating
units.action_summary: Have 250 hours of flight time in an airplane as PIC, or as SIC performing PIC duties under supervision, or any combination.

units.obligation_text: (i)(A) 100 hours of cross-country flight time.
units.actor: an applicant for an airplane category rating
units.action_summary: Include at least 100 hours of cross-country flight time within the required flight time.

units.obligation_text: (i)(B) 25 hours of night flight time.
units.actor: an applicant for an airplane category rating
units.action_summary: Include at least 25 hours of night flight time within the required flight time.

units.obligation_text: Except for a person who has been removed from flying status for lack of proficiency or because of a disciplinary action involving aircraft operations, a U.S. military pilot or former U.S. military pilot who meets the requirements of § 61.73(b)(1), or a military pilot in the Armed Forces of a foreign contracting State to the Convention on International Civil Aviation who meets the requirements of § 61.73(c)(1), may credit flight time in a powered-lift aircraft operated in horizontal flight toward the flight time requirement.
units.actor: a U.S. military pilot or former U.S. military pilot meeting § 61.73(b)(1), or a military pilot in the Armed Forces of a foreign contracting State meeting § 61.73(c)(1)
units.action_summary: May credit flight time in a powered-lift aircraft operated in horizontal flight toward the flight time requirement, except as provided.

units.obligation_text: Except for a person who has been removed from flying status for lack of proficiency or because of a disciplinary action involving aircraft operations
units.actor: a person removed from flying status for lack of proficiency or because of a disciplinary action involving aircraft operations
units.action_summary: Is not permitted to credit powered-lift flight time toward the flight time requirement.

units.obligation_text: (a)(3) If serving as pilot in command in part 121 operations, has 1,000 hours as second in command in operations under this part, pilot in command in operations under § 91.1053(a)(2)(i) of this chapter, pilot in command in operations under § 135.243(a)(1) of this chapter, or any combination thereof.
units.actor: a pilot serving as pilot in command in part 121 operations
units.action_summary: Have 1,000 hours of specified flight time (SIC in operations under this part, PIC under §91.1053(a)(2)(i), PIC under §135.243(a)(1), or any combination) to serve as PIC in part 121 operations.

units.obligation_text: 1,000 hours as second in command in operations under this part
units.actor: a pilot serving as pilot in command in part 121 operations
units.action_summary: Credit 1,000 hours as second in command in operations under part 121 toward the requirement.

units.obligation_text: pilot in command in operations under § 91.1053(a)(2)(i) of this chapter
units.actor: a pilot serving as pilot in command in part 121 operations
units.action_summary: Credit PIC time in operations under §91.1053(a)(2)(i) toward the 1,000-hour requirement.

units.obligation_text: pilot in command in operations under § 135.243(a)(1) of this chapter
units.actor: a pilot serving as pilot in command in part 121 operations
units.action_summary: Credit PIC time in operations under §135.243(a)(1) toward the 1,000-hour requirement.

units.obligation_text: For those pilots who were employed as pilot in command in part 121 operations on July 31, 2013, compliance with the requirements of this paragraph (a)(3) is not required.
units.actor: pilots who were employed as pilot in command in part 121 operations on July 31, 2013
units.action_summary: Are exempt from complying with the paragraph (a)(3) flight-hour requirements.

units.obligation_text: (c) For the purpose of satisfying the flight hour requirement in paragraph (a)(3) of this section, a pilot may credit 500 hours of military flight time provided the flight time was obtained—
units.action_summary: May credit up to 500 hours of military flight time toward the paragraph (a)(3) flight-hour requirement, subject to conditions.

units.obligation_text: (1) As pilot in command in a multiengine, turbine-powered, fixed-wing airplane or powered-lift aircraft, or any combination thereof;
units.action_summary: The credited military flight time must have been obtained as PIC in a multiengine, turbine-powered, fixed-wing airplane or powered-lift aircraft (or combination).

units.obligation_text: (2) In an operation requiring more than one pilot.
units.action_summary: The credited military flight time must have been obtained in operations requiring more than one pilot.

units.obligation_text: (d) For the purpose of satisfying the flight hour requirement in paragraph (a)(3) of this section, a pilot may credit flight time obtained as pilot in command in operations under this part prior to July 31, 2013.
units.action_summary: May credit PIC flight time in operations under this part obtained prior to July 31, 2013 toward the paragraph (a)(3) requirement.

title: Airworthiness Directives: American Champion Aircraft Corp.

units.obligation_text: The FAA must receive comments on this AD action by February 26, 2018.
units.action_summary: FAA must receive comments on the AD by Feb 26, 2018.

units.obligation_text: Comply with this AD within the compliance times specified, unless already done.
units.action_summary: Affected owners/operators must comply with the AD within the specified times unless already done.

units.obligation_text: As of April 12, 2017 (the effective date retained from AD 2017–07–10), the airplane is restricted to non-aerobatic flight until the actions required in paragraphs (g)(2) through (3) of this AD are done.
units.action_summary: Affected airplanes may only be operated in non-aerobatic flight until required actions in (g)(2)-(3) are completed.

units.obligation_text: Before further flight after April 12, 2017 (the effective date retained from AD 2017–07–10), fabricate a placard using at least 1/8 inch letters with the words "AEROBATIC FLIGHT PROHIBITED" on it and install the placard on the instrument panel within the pilot’s clear view.
units.actor: owner/operator or person responsible for the aircraft
units.action_summary: Fabricate and install a placard reading 'AEROBATIC FLIGHT PROHIBITED' on the instrument panel before further flight after April 12, 2017.

units.obligation_text: This action may be performed by the owner/operator (pilot) holding at least a private pilot certificate
units.actor: owner/operator (pilot) holding at least a private pilot certificate
units.action_summary: Permits the owner/operator (pilot) with at least a private pilot certificate to perform the placard fabrication/installation.

units.obligation_text: and must be entered into the aircraft records showing compliance with this AD in accordance with 14 CFR 43.9 (a)(1)–(4) and 14 CFR 91.417(a)(2)(v).
units.action_summary: The placard installation action must be recorded in the aircraft records per specified CFR provisions.

units.obligation_text: The record must be maintained as required by 14 CFR 91.417, 121.380, or 135.439.
units.action_summary: Aircraft records of compliance must be maintained as required by the cited CFR provisions.

units.obligation_text: Within the next 10 hours time-in-service (TIS) after April 12, 2017 (the effective date retained from AD 2017–07–10), inspect the aileron hinge rib and support for cracks or other damage following American Champion Aircraft Corporation Service Letter (SL) 442, dated February 16, 2017, or American Champion Aircraft Corp. Service Letter (SL) 442, Revision A, dated August 18, 2017 (ACAC SL No. 442).
units.action_summary: Within 10 hours TIS after April 12, 2017, inspect the aileron hinge rib and support for cracks/damage using ACAC SL No. 442 procedures.

units.obligation_text: If no cracks or other damage is found during the initial inspection required in paragraph (h)(1) of this AD, the placard prohibiting aerobatic flight required in paragraph (g)(2) of this AD can be removed.
units.action_summary: If the initial inspection finds no damage, the 'AEROBATIC FLIGHT PROHIBITED' placard may be removed.

units.obligation_text: Within 100 hours TIS from the initial inspection required in paragraph (h)(1) of this AD or within 10 hours TIS after the effective date of this AD, whichever occurs later, and repetitively thereafter at intervals not the exceed 100 hours TIS, inspect the aileron hinge rib and support for cracks or other damage following ACAC SL No. 442.
units.action_summary: Perform recurring inspections of the aileron hinge rib/support within specified time thresholds and at intervals not to exceed 100 hours TIS, following ACAC SL No. 442.

units.obligation_text: If cracks or other damage is found during any inspection required in paragraph (h)(1) or (3) of this AD, before further flight, replace any retained parts or structure that are cracked or damaged, and install the aileron hinge reinforcement kit following American Champion Aircraft Corp. Service Letter 444, dated August 18, 2017 (ACAC SL No. 444).
units.action_summary: If inspections find cracks/damage, before further flight replace cracked/damaged parts and install the aileron hinge reinforcement kit per ACAC SL No. 444.

units.obligation_text: Within 400 hours after the initial inspection required in paragraph (h)(1) of this AD, if not already done as required in paragraph (h)(4) of this AD, install the aileron hinge reinforcement kit following the procedures in ACAC SL No. 444.
units.action_summary: Install the aileron hinge reinforcement kit within 400 hours after the initial inspection if not already installed per (h)(4).

units.obligation_text: After installation of the aileron hinge reinforcement kit required in paragraph (h)(4) or (5) of this AD, as applicable, insert page 4–1 of the Airworthiness Limitations section and page 5–9 of the Time and Maintenance Checks section, both dated October 3, 2017, from the American Champion Aircraft Corporation SM–601 8KCAB Service Manual, Reissue B, dated October 3, 2017, into the maintenance program (service manual).
units.action_summary: After installing the reinforcement kit, insert specified pages into the maintenance program/service manual.

units.obligation_text: Installing the aileron hinge reinforcement kit as required in paragraph (h)(4) or (h)(5) of this AD and the insertion of page 4–1 of the Airworthiness Limitations section and page 5–9 of the Time and Maintenance Checks section, both dated October 3, 2017, of the American Champion Aircraft Corporation SM–601 8KCAB Service Manual, Reissue B, dated October 3, 2017, into the maintenance program (service manual), as required in paragraph (h)(6) of this AD is terminating action to this AD. The revised Airworthiness Limitations section includes a 100-hour/annual inspection requirement for the aileron hinge supports.
units.action_summary: Installing the kit and inserting the specified manual pages terminates the AD's requirements; the revised limitations include recurring inspection requirements.

units.obligation_text: Although ACAC SL No. 442 and ACAC SL No. 444 specify submitting certain information to the manufacturer, this AD does not require that action.
units.action_summary: The AD does not require submission of information to the manufacturer despite the service letters requesting it.

units.obligation_text: No aerobatic flight permitted with a special flight permit.
units.actor: holders of a special flight permit/operators
units.action_summary: Aerobatic flight is prohibited when operating under a special flight permit.

units.obligation_text: The Manager, Chicago ACO Branch, FAA, has the authority to approve AMOCs for this AD, if requested using the procedures found in 14 CFR 39.19.
units.action_summary: The Manager of the Chicago ACO Branch may approve alternative methods of compliance for this AD following 14 CFR 39.19 procedures.

units.obligation_text: In accordance with 14 CFR 39.19, send your request to your principal inspector or local Flight Standards District Office, as appropriate.
units.action_summary: Persons requesting an AMOC must send their request to their principal inspector or local FSDO per 14 CFR 39.19.

units.obligation_text: If sending information directly to the manager of the ACO, send it to the attention of the person identified in paragraph (l) of this AD.
units.actor: persons sending AMOC information directly to the manager
units.action_summary: If sending AMOC information directly to the ACO manager, the sender must address it to the person identified in paragraph (l).

units.obligation_text: Before using any approved AMOC, notify your appropriate principal inspector, or lacking a principal inspector, the manager of the local flight standards district office/certificate holding district office.
units.action_summary: Before using an approved AMOC, notify the appropriate principal inspector or, if none, the manager of the local FSDO/CHDO.

units.obligation_text: If, during any inspection or records review required by paragraph (g) of this AD, any ISS OPS part number COL40–0010–0100 or COL46–0007–0100 is found: Within 12 months after the effective date of this AD, do all applicable actions identified as "RC" (required for compliance) in, and in accordance with, the Accomplishment Instructions of Boeing Alert Service Bulletin B787–81205–SB340036–00, Issue 001, dated June 30, 2017.
units.action_summary: If the specified software part numbers are found, operators must, within 12 months, perform all applicable RC actions in the specified Boeing Alert Service Bulletin.

units.obligation_text: For Group 1 airplanes identified in Boeing Alert Service Bulletin B787–81205–SB340036–00, Issue 001, dated June 30, 2017: Prior to accomplishment of the actions required by paragraph (h) of this AD, install new software for the ISS OPS and the displays and crew alerting (DCA) database, in accordance with the Accomplishment Instructions of Boeing Service Bulletin B787–81205–SB340005–00, Issue 002, dated April 27, 2016.
units.action_summary: Before doing the paragraph (h) actions, Group 1 operators must install new ISS OPS software and the DCA database per the Boeing Service Bulletin.

units.obligation_text: As of the effective date of this AD, no person may install ISS OPS part number COL40–0010–0100 or COL46–0007–0100 on any airplane, except in accomplishment of the actions required by paragraph (i) of this AD.
units.action_summary: Installing the specified ISS OPS part numbers is prohibited except when performing the paragraph (i) installation actions.

units.obligation_text: Except in accomplishment of the actions required by paragraph (i) of this AD.
units.action_summary: Installation of the specified software is permitted when done as part of the paragraph (i) required actions.

units.obligation_text: This paragraph provides credit for the actions specified in paragraph (i) of this AD, if those actions were performed before the effective date of this AD using Boeing Service Bulletin B787–81205–SB340005–00, Issue 001, dated December 11, 2015.
units.action_summary: Operators who performed the paragraph (i) actions before the AD effective date using the earlier Boeing Service Bulletin are credited for those actions.

units.actor: The Manager, Seattle ACO Branch, FAA

units.obligation_text: If sending information directly to the manager of the certification office, send it to the attention of the person identified in paragraph (m)(1) of this AD.

units.action_summary: AMOC requests may be emailed to the specified FAA email address.

units.obligation_text: To be approved, the repair method, modification deviation, or alteration deviation must meet the certification basis of the airplane,

units.action_summary: If service information contains RC-labeled steps, the following RC-specific provisions apply.

units.obligation_text: The steps labeled as RC, including substeps under an RC step and any figures identified in an RC step, must be done to comply with the AD.
units.action_summary: RC-labeled steps (and their substeps/figures) are mandatory to comply with the AD.

units.obligation_text: If a step or substep is labeled "RC Exempt," then the RC requirement is removed from that step or substep.
units.action_summary: A step labeled 'RC Exempt' is not subject to the RC requirement.

units.obligation_text: An AMOC is required for any deviations to RC steps, including substeps and identified figures.

units.action_summary: Deviations from RC steps require approval via an AMOC.

units.obligation_text: Provided the RC steps, including substeps and identified figures, can still be done as specified,

units.obligation_text: and the airplane can be put back in an airworthy condition.
units.action_summary: Deviation from non-RC steps is allowed only if the airplane can be returned to an airworthy condition.

units.obligation_text: Before further flight, repair in accordance with Part 2 of the Accomplishment Instructions of Aviation Partners Boeing Service Bulletin AP767–57–013, Revision 1, dated April 11, 2017.

units.obligation_text: At the applicable time specified in paragraph 1.E., "Compliance," of Aviation Partners Boeing Service Bulletin AP767–57–013, Revision 1, dated April 11, 2017, do an HFEC inspection for cracking, in accordance with Part 3 of the Accomplishment Instructions of Aviation Partners Boeing Service Bulletin AP767–57–013, Revision 1, dated April 11, 2017; and repeat the inspection thereafter at the applicable times specified in paragraph 1.E., "Compliance," of Aviation Partners Boeing Service Bulletin AP767–57–013, Revision 1, dated April 11, 2017.

units.obligation_text: Except as required by paragraph (l) of this AD, at the applicable time specified in Table 1, Table 2, Table 4, or Table 5, of paragraph 1.E., "Compliance," of BSASB 737–32–1448, R2, do an inspection to determine if any of the MLG trunnion pin assembly part numbers identified in paragraph 2.C.3., "Parts Modified and Reidentified," of BSASB 737–32–1448, R2, are installed.
units.action_summary: Perform an inspection at the applicable time to determine whether specified MLG trunnion pin assembly part numbers are installed.

units.action_summary: Operators may use maintenance records instead of a physical inspection if the records conclusively show the part numbers.

units.obligation_text: Except as required by paragraph (l) of this AD.
units.action_summary: The inspection requirement is subject to the exception described in paragraph (l).

units.section: (h) Repetitive Lubrication of MLG Trunnion Pin Assemblies
units.obligation_text: Except as required by paragraph (l) of this AD, at the applicable time specified in Table 1, Table 2, Table 4, or Table 5, of paragraph 1.E., "Compliance," of BSASB 737–32–1448, R2, lubricate the applicable forward and aft trunnion pin assemblies of the right and left MLGs, in accordance with Work Package 1 of the Accomplishment Instructions of BSASB 737–32–1448, R2. Repeat the lubrication thereafter at intervals not to exceed those specified in Table 1, Table 2, Table 4, or Table 5, of paragraph 1.E., "Compliance," of BSASB 737–32–1448, R2. Accomplishment of the actions specified in paragraph (j) of this AD terminates the repetitive lubrication required by this paragraph.
units.action_summary: Lubricate the specified trunnion pin assemblies at the applicable time and repeat lubrication at intervals not exceeding the specified intervals; completion of paragraph (j) actions terminates this repetitive lubrication requirement.

units.obligation_text: Repeat the lubrication thereafter at intervals not to exceed those specified in Table 1, Table 2, Table 4, or Table 5, of paragraph 1.E., "Compliance," of BSASB 737–32–1448, R2.
units.action_summary: After initial lubrication, repeat lubrication at intervals that do not exceed the specified tables.

units.obligation_text: Accomplishment of the actions specified in paragraph (j) of this AD terminates the repetitive lubrication required by this paragraph.
units.action_summary: If the modification actions in paragraph (j) are accomplished, the repetitive lubrication requirement ends.

units.section: (i) Repetitive Inspections, Corrective Actions, and Lubrication
units.obligation_text: Except as required by paragraph (l) of this AD, at the applicable time specified in Table 1, Table 2, Table 4, or Table 5, of paragraph 1.E., "Compliance," of BSASB 737–32–1448, R2, do a general visual inspection of the left and right MLGs at the forward and aft trunnion pin locations and the visible surfaces of the forward and aft trunnion pin assemblies for discrepancies including signs of corrosion or chrome plating damage, and lubricate the forward and aft trunnion pin assemblies as applicable, in accordance with Work Package 2 of the Accomplishment Instructions of BSASB 737–32–1448, R2. Repeat the general visual inspection thereafter at intervals not to exceed those specified in paragraph 1.E., "Compliance," of BSASB 737–32–1448, R2.
units.action_summary: Perform general visual inspections and applicable lubrication at the specified times and repeat inspections at intervals not exceeding those specified.

units.obligation_text: Repeat the general visual inspection thereafter at intervals not to exceed those specified in paragraph 1.E., "Compliance," of BSASB 737–32–1448, R2.
units.action_summary: Repeat the inspections at intervals not exceeding those specified in the referenced compliance table.

units.obligation_text: If any discrepancy is found during any inspection required by this paragraph, before further flight, do all applicable related investigative and corrective actions in accordance with Work Package 2 of the Accomplishment Instructions of BSASB 737–32–1448, R2.
units.action_summary: If discrepancies are found during inspection, perform all required investigative and corrective actions before further flight in accordance with the service instructions.

units.obligation_text: Accomplishment of the actions required by paragraph (j) of this AD terminates the repetitive inspections required by this paragraph.
units.action_summary: Completing the modification in paragraph (j) ends the repetitive inspection requirement.

units.section: (j) Modification of MLG Trunnion Pin Assemblies
units.obligation_text: Except as required by paragraph (l) of this AD, at the time specified in Table 1, Table 2, Table 4, or Table 5, as applicable, of paragraph 1.E., "Compliance," of BSASB 737–32–1448, R2, modify the left and right MLG trunnion pin assemblies, including all applicable related investigative and corrective actions, in accordance with Work Package 3 of the Accomplishment Instructions of BSASB 737–32–1448, R2.
units.action_summary: Modify left and right MLG trunnion pin assemblies at the specified time in accordance with Work Package 3, including related investigative and corrective actions.

units.obligation_text: All applicable related investigative and corrective actions must be done at the time specified in paragraph 1.E., "Compliance," of BSASB 737–32–1448, R2.
units.action_summary: Investigative and corrective actions related to the modification must be completed at the specified compliance time.

units.obligation_text: Accomplishment of the actions in Work Package 3 of the Accomplishment Instructions of BSASB 737–32–1448, R2 terminates the repetitive lubrication required by paragraph (h) of this AD and the repetitive inspections required by paragraph (i) of this AD.
units.action_summary: Completing Work Package 3 ends the repetitive lubrication and inspection requirements from paragraphs (h) and (i).

units.section: (k) Replacement of MLG Forward Trunnion Pin Housing Assembly, Seal, and Retainer
units.obligation_text: Except as required by paragraph (l) of this AD, at the time specified in Table 3 or Table 6, as applicable, of paragraph 1.E., "Compliance," of BSASB 737–32–1448, R2, replace the seal, retainer, and support ring assembly with a new seal and retainer configuration; install the forward trunnion pin assembly into the housing assembly; and lubricate the forward and aft trunnion pin assemblies for the left and right MLGs; in accordance with Work Package 4 of the Accomplishment Instructions of BSASB 737–32–1448, R2.
units.action_summary: At the specified time, replace the seal/retainer/support ring with the new configuration, install the forward trunnion pin assembly, and lubricate the forward and aft trunnion pin assemblies per Work Package 4.

units.obligation_text: Where paragraph 1.E., "Compliance," of BSASB 737–32–1448, R2 specifies a compliance time "after the Revision 2 date of this service bulletin," this AD requires compliance within the specified compliance time after the effective date of this AD.
units.action_summary: When a service bulletin specifies compliance 'after the Revision 2 date', the AD instead requires compliance within that time period measured from the AD's effective date.

units.obligation_text: As of the effective date of this AD, no person may install a MLG or MLG trunnion pin assembly on any airplane identified in paragraphs (c)(1) through (c)(7) of this AD unless the actions required by paragraphs (j) or (k), as applicable, of this AD have been accomplished on the MLG or MLG trunnion pin assembly.
units.action_summary: From the AD effective date, no person may install an MLG or trunnion pin assembly on affected airplanes unless the modification or replacement actions in paragraphs (j) or (k) have been completed on that assembly.

units.obligation_text: Provided the RC steps, including substeps and identified figures, can still be done as specified

units.obligation_text: Provided ... the airplane can be put back in an airworthy condition.

title: Airworthiness Directives: General Electric Company Turbofan Engines

units.obligation_text: For calculation purposes, it should be assumed the mass of an occupant is at least 86 kilograms (190 pounds).
units.action_summary: Use an occupant mass of at least 86 kg (190 lb) for calculations.

units.section: b. Seats, Safety Belts, and Harnesses Factor of Safety
units.obligation_text: For each seat, safety belt, and harness, its attachment to the structure must be shown, by analysis, tests, or both, to be able to withstand the inertia forces prescribed in paragraph (c) of these special conditions multiplied by a fitting factor of 1.33.
units.action_summary: Demonstrate (by analysis, tests, or both) that each attachment can withstand the paragraph (c) inertia forces times 1.33.

units.obligation_text: The balloon—although it may be damaged under emergency landing conditions—must be designed to give each occupant every reasonable chance of avoiding serious injury in a crash landing—when seat belts provided for in the design are properly used—and the occupant is subject to the following ultimate inertia forces acting relative to the surrounding structure as well as independently of each other.
units.action_summary: Design the balloon to give occupants a reasonable chance of avoiding serious injury under emergency landing conditions and to account for specified inertia forces.

units.obligation_text: Forward 6g
units.action_summary: Account for a forward inertia force of 6g.

units.obligation_text: Sideways 6g
units.action_summary: Account for a sideways inertia force of 6g.

units.obligation_text: Downward 6g
units.action_summary: Account for a downward inertia force of 6g.

units.obligation_text: Each seat and its supporting structure must be designed for an occupant mass in accordance paragraph (a) of these special conditions and for the maximum load factors corresponding to the specified flight and ground load conditions, including the emergency landing conditions prescribed in paragraph (c) of these special conditions.
units.action_summary: Design each seat and its support for the specified occupant mass and load factors, including emergency landing conditions.

units.obligation_text: Each seat or berth shall be fitted with an individual approved seat belt or harness.
units.action_summary: Fit every seat or berth with an individual approved seat belt or harness.

units.obligation_text: Seat belts installed on the balloon must not fail under flight or ground load conditions or emergency landing conditions in accordance with paragraph (c) of these special conditions, taking into account the geometrical arrangement of the belt attachment and the seat.
units.action_summary: Ensure seat belts do not fail under specified flight, ground, or emergency landing load conditions, considering geometry of attachment and seat.

title: Yaw Maneuver Conditions-Rudder Reversals

units.obligation_text: For airplanes with a powered rudder control surface or surfaces, the airplane must be designed to withstand the ultimate loads that result from the yaw maneuver conditions specified in paragraphs (a) through (e) of this section at speeds from VMC or the highest airspeed for which it is possible to achieve maximum rudder deflection at zero sideslip, whichever is greater, up to VC/MC.
units.action_summary: Be designed to withstand ultimate loads from the yaw maneuver conditions (a)-(e) over the specified speed range.

units.obligation_text: The applicant must evaluate these conditions with the landing gear retracted and speed brakes (and spoilers when used as speed brakes) retracted.
units.action_summary: Evaluate the yaw maneuver conditions with landing gear and speed brakes/spoilers retracted.

units.obligation_text: In computing the loads on the airplane, the applicant may assume yawing velocity to be zero.
units.action_summary: May assume yawing velocity is zero when computing loads.

units.obligation_text: The applicant must assume a pilot force of 200 pounds when evaluating each of these conditions:
units.action_summary: Assume a 200-pound pilot force when evaluating each of the listed yaw maneuver conditions.

units.obligation_text: With the airplane in unaccelerated flight at zero yaw, the flight deck rudder control is displaced as specified in § 25.351(a) and (b).
units.actor: the applicant (when performing the required evaluations)
units.action_summary: Set the flight deck rudder control displacement as specified in § 25.351(a) and (b) for unaccelerated, zero-yaw flight when evaluating loads.

units.obligation_text: With the airplane yawed to the overswing sideslip angle, the flight deck rudder control is suddenly displaced in the opposite direction.
units.actor: the applicant (when performing the required evaluations)
units.action_summary: Evaluate a sudden opposite rudder displacement when the airplane is yawed to the overswing sideslip angle.

units.obligation_text: With the airplane yawed to the opposite overswing sideslip angle, the flight deck rudder control is suddenly displaced in the opposite direction.
units.actor: the applicant (when performing the required evaluations)
units.action_summary: Evaluate a sudden opposite rudder displacement when the airplane is yawed to the opposite overswing sideslip angle.

units.obligation_text: With the airplane yawed to the subsequent overswing sideslip angle, the flight deck rudder control is suddenly displaced in the opposite direction.
units.actor: the applicant (when performing the required evaluations)
units.action_summary: Evaluate a sudden opposite rudder displacement when the airplane is yawed to the subsequent overswing sideslip angle.

units.obligation_text: With the airplane yawed to the opposite overswing sideslip angle, the flight deck rudder control is suddenly returned to neutral.
units.actor: the applicant (when performing the required evaluations)
units.action_summary: Evaluate sudden return of the flight deck rudder control to neutral when the airplane is yawed to the opposite overswing sideslip angle.

units.obligation_text: at speeds from VMC or the highest airspeed for which it is possible to achieve maximum rudder deflection at zero sideslip, whichever is greater, up to VC/MC.
units.actor: the airplane (design requirement applies over this speed range)
units.action_summary: Specifies the speed range (from VMC or the highest airspeed for max rudder deflection at zero sideslip, whichever is greater, up to VC/MC) over which the airplane must withstand the loads.

units.action_summary: Perform an initial TAI inspection of the 1st stage LPC blades after the AD's effective date as specified in subparagraphs.

units.obligation_text: For 1st stage LPC blades that have accumulated fewer than 6,500 cycles since new (CSN), perform a TAI inspection the next time the engine is separated at the M-flange, or prior to the 1st stage LPC blade accumulating 7,000 CSN, whichever occurs first.
units.action_summary: If a blade has <6,500 CSN, inspect at the next M-flange separation or before it reaches 7,000 CSN, whichever is earlier.

units.obligation_text: For 1st stage LPC blades that have accumulated 6,500 or more CSN, or if the cycles since the blade was new cannot be determined, or if the cycles since the blade was last TAI inspected cannot be determined, perform a TAI inspection within 500 flight cycles or 180 days from the effective date of this AD, whichever occurs first.
units.action_summary: If a blade has ≥6,500 CSN or cycle information is unknown, inspect within 500 flight cycles or within 180 days of the AD effective date, whichever comes first.

units.obligation_text: Thereafter, perform a TAI inspection of 1st stage LPC blades every time the engine is separated at the M-flange and the blades have accumulated 1,000 or more flight cycles since the last TAI inspection, not to exceed 6,500 flight cycles since the last TAI inspection.
units.action_summary: Perform recurrent TAI inspections at each M-flange separation when blades have ≥1,000 cycles since last TAI, and ensure no interval exceeds 6,500 cycles since last TAI.

units.obligation_text: If any 1st stage LPC blade fails the inspection required by paragraph (g)(1) or (2) of this AD, remove the blade from service and replace with a part eligible for installation before further flight.
units.action_summary: If a blade fails inspection, it must be removed from service and replaced with an eligible part before the aircraft's next flight.

units.obligation_text: The TAI inspection and disposition required for compliance with this AD must be accomplished by a method approved by the FAA.
units.action_summary: TAI inspections and any disposition decisions must be done using a method that the FAA has approved.

units.obligation_text: You may take credit for the initial TAI inspection required by paragraph (g)(1) of this AD if you performed the TAI inspection before the effective date of this AD using PW ASB PW4G–112–A72–268, Revision No. 6, dated August 5, 2014.
units.action_summary: Operators may claim credit for the initial TAI inspection if it was performed before the AD effective date using the specified PW ASB Revision No. 6.

units.obligation_text: Do not install any 1st stage LPC blade that has accumulated 1,000 or more flight cycles into any engine unless it has passed the inspection required by paragraph (g)(1) of this AD.
units.action_summary: Blades with 1,000 or more flight cycles may not be installed into any engine unless they have passed the required inspection.

units.obligation_text: unless it has passed the inspection required by paragraph (g)(1) of this AD.
