units.obligation_text: If a main wing spar has been replaced with a new (zero hour TIS) main wing spar, count the number of 100-hour inspections from the time of installation of the new main wing spar.
units.action_summary: If the spar was replaced with a new (zero-hour) spar, count 100-hour inspections starting from its installation.

units.obligation_text: If either main wing spar has been replaced with a serviceable main wing spar (more than zero hours TIS) or the airplane maintenance records are missing or incomplete, the factored service hours cannot be determined. Perform the eddy current inspection as specified in paragraph (h) of this AD.
units.action_summary: If serviceable (used) spar replacement or missing/incomplete records prevent determining factored service hours, perform the eddy current inspection in paragraph (h).

units.obligation_text: Before further flight after completing the action in paragraph (g)(1) of this AD, calculate the factored service hours for each main wing spar using the following formula: (N × 100) + [T-(N × 100)]/17 = Factored Service Hours, where N is the number of 100-hour inspections and T is the total hours TIS of the airplane.
units.action_summary: Before further flight after completing paragraph (g)(1), calculate factored service hours for each main wing spar using the specified formula.

units.obligation_text: (N × 100) + [T-(N × 100)]/17 = Factored Service Hours, where N is the number of 100-hour inspections and T is the total hours TIS of the airplane.
units.action_summary: Specification of the formula to calculate factored service hours.

units.obligation_text: Thereafter, after each annual inspection and 100-hour TIS inspection, recalculate the factored service hours for each main wing spar until the main wing spar has accumulated 5,000 or more factored service hours.

units.obligation_text: Within the compliance time specified in paragraph (h)(1) or (2) of this AD, eddy current inspect the inner surface of each bolt hole on the lower main wing spar cap for cracks by using the procedure in appendix 1 of this AD.
units.actor: owners/operators, maintenance personnel, or certified inspectors
units.action_summary: Perform eddy current inspection of each lower main wing spar cap bolt hole inner surface for cracks using Appendix 1 procedure within the specified compliance time.

units.obligation_text: Within 100 hours TIS after complying with paragraph (g) of this AD or within 100 hours TIS after a main wing spar accumulates 5,000 factored service hours, whichever occurs later;
units.action_summary: Timing condition for required eddy current inspection: within 100 hours TIS after completing paragraph (g) or after a spar accumulates 5,000 factored service hours, whichever is later.

units.obligation_text: For airplanes with an unknown number of factored service hours on a main wing spar, within the next 100 hours TIS after the effective date of this AD or within 60 days after the effective date of this AD, whichever occurs later.
units.action_summary: Timing condition for required eddy current inspection for airplanes with unknown factored service hours: within 100 hours TIS or within 60 days after AD effective date, whichever occurs later.

units.obligation_text: If a crack is found during an inspection required in paragraph (h) of this AD, before further flight, replace the main wing spar with a new (zero hours TIS) main wing spar or with a main wing spar that has been inspected as specified in appendix 1 of this AD and no cracks were found.
units.action_summary: If inspection finds a crack, before further flight replace the main wing spar either with a new zero-hour spar or with an inspected spar that has no cracks.

units.obligation_text: Replace the main wing spar with a new (zero hours TIS) main wing spar.
units.action_summary: One permissible replacement option: install a new (zero-hour) main wing spar.

units.obligation_text: Replace the main wing spar with a main wing spar that has been inspected as specified in appendix 1 of this AD and no cracks were found.
units.action_summary: Alternative replacement: install a main wing spar that has been inspected per Appendix 1 and found free of cracks.

units.obligation_text: Within 30 days after completing an inspection required in paragraph (h) of this AD, using Appendix 2, "Inspection Results Form," of this AD, report the inspection results to the FAA at the Atlanta ACO Branch. Submit the report to the FAA using the contact information found in appendix 2 of this AD.
units.actor: owners/operators or inspectors who completed the inspection
units.action_summary: Within 30 days after inspection, report results to FAA Atlanta ACO Branch using Appendix 2 form and contact information in Appendix 2.

units.obligation_text: Using Appendix 2, "Inspection Results Form," of this AD, report the inspection results to the FAA at the Atlanta ACO Branch. Submit the report to the FAA using the contact information found in appendix 2 of this AD.
units.action_summary: Specify that reporting must be done using Appendix 2 form and contact information provided in Appendix 2.

units.obligation_text: A special flight permit may only be issued to operate the airplane to a location where the inspection requirement of paragraph (h) of this AD can be performed.
units.action_summary: Special flight permits may be issued only to fly the airplane to a location where the required inspection can be performed.

units.obligation_text: This AD prohibits a special flight permit if the inspection reveals a crack in a main wing spar.
units.actor: FAA (issuance of special flight permits) / owners/operators
units.action_summary: If an inspection reveals a crack in a main wing spar, issuance of a special flight permit is prohibited.

units.action_summary: Federal agencies are prohibited from conducting or sponsoring information collections subject to the PRA unless a currently valid OMB Control Number is displayed.

units.obligation_text: Equipment used must provide impedance plane diagrams.
units.action_summary: Inspection equipment must provide impedance plane diagrams.

units.obligation_text: Probes may be either absolute or differential coil configurations.
units.action_summary: Inspection probes may be absolute or differential coil types (permission/specification).

units.obligation_text: For manual bolt hole probing: use probe collars at an increment of every 1/64 inch to ensure the uniform depth of rotation and to aid in reducing lift-off effects.
units.actor: inspectors performing manual bolt hole probing
units.action_summary: When doing manual bolt-hole probing, use probe collars at 1/64 inch increments to ensure uniform depth and reduce lift-off.

units.obligation_text: Automated scanning systems may be used.
units.action_summary: Automated scanning systems are permitted for the inspection procedure.

units.obligation_text: Bolt hole probes must match as closely as possible, but not exceed, the bolt hole diameter. Split core probes may be expanded to a maximum of 0.050 inch beyond the probe's nominal diameter (in accordance with on the probe manufacturer's instructions). The fill factor must be 80 percent minimum.
units.action_summary: Bolt hole probes should match but not exceed hole diameter; split core probes may be expanded up to 0.050 inch per manufacturer's instructions; fill factor must be at least 80%.

units.obligation_text: A right angle (90 degree) surface probe may be used for further detail indication, if needed.
units.action_summary: A 90-degree surface probe may be used for additional detail indications if needed.

units.obligation_text: Other equipment meeting the requirements in A1 may be used.
units.action_summary: Other equipment that meets A.1 requirements is permitted for use.

units.obligation_text: Use a reference standard of the same conductivity 2024 T-3 within +/-15% IACS. It must have electrical discharge machining (EDM) notches for simulating defects as calibration references.
units.action_summary: Use a 2024 T-3 reference standard within ±15% conductivity; it must include EDM notches for calibration.

units.obligation_text: The surface finish must be 63 RHR or better.
units.action_summary: Reference standard surface finish must be 63 RHR or better.

units.obligation_text: The reference standard must have a corner notch size of 0.030 x 0.030 inch (screen set at minimum of three divisions vertical with a phase signal of between 45 and 120 degrees separation from the horizontal liftoff).
units.action_summary: Reference standard must have specified corner notch size and screen/phase settings for calibration.

units.obligation_text: Use a frequency between 100 and 500kHz.
units.action_summary: Eddy current equipment frequency must be between 100 and 500 kHz.

units.obligation_text: The calibration must be checked in the beginning and end and every 30 minutes of inspections.
units.action_summary: Check calibration at the start and end of inspections and every 30 minutes during inspections.

units.obligation_text: Personnel doing the eddy current inspection must have NAS 410 Level II or Level III certification.
units.action_summary: Inspectors must hold NAS 410 Level II or Level III certification.

units.obligation_text: For each wing inspected: (1) Two (2) wing to spar attach bolts; (2) Two (2) wing to spar attach nuts; (3) Two (2) wing to spar attach washers; (4) Cleaning cloth; (5) Isopropyl alcohol or mineral spirits.
units.action_summary: For each wing inspected, these materials/parts are required to perform the inspection and reinstallation.

units.obligation_text: Locate the two (2) lower outboard main spar attach bolts, as shown in Figure 1 of Appendix 1, installed on the lower cap of the main spar, on the forward and aft sides of the spar web.
units.action_summary: Locate the two lower outboard main spar attach bolts on the lower cap of the main spar (forward and aft sides) before inspection.

units.obligation_text: Clean the inspection surfaces using a cloth dampened with isopropyl alcohol or mineral spirits.
units.action_summary: Clean inspection surfaces with cloth dampened in isopropyl alcohol or mineral spirits before inspection.

units.obligation_text: Use eddy current surface and bolt hole examinations to detect surface and shallow subsurface cracking and discontinuities on the left and right lower outboard spar bolt holes. Use SAE ARP4402, "Eddy Current Inspection of Open Fastener Holes in Aluminum Aircraft Structure," or another FAA-approved eddy current inspection method to do these inspections.
units.action_summary: Perform eddy current surface and bolt hole examinations to detect cracks using SAE ARP4402 or another FAA-approved eddy current method.

units.obligation_text: A crack or crack-like indication with an amplitude equal to or greater than 50 percent of the reference level signal must be rejected and documented.
units.action_summary: If an indication amplitude is ≥50% of reference signal, the spar must be rejected and the finding documented.

units.obligation_text: Email completed form to: 9-ASO-ATLCOS-Reporting@faa.gov Or mail to: Federal Aviation Administration Atlanta ACO Branch, AIR-7 AI 1701 Columbia Avenue College Park, GA 30337

units.action_summary: Submit the completed inspection results form by email to the specified email address or mail to the Atlanta ACO Branch address.

units.action_summary: When submitting the form, include Docket No. FAA-2018-1046 in the email or mail subject line.

units.obligation_text: Include photos if applicable
units.actor: persons submitting the inspection results form
units.action_summary: Reporters may include photos with the inspection results if applicable.

title: Airworthiness Directives: Bell Helicopter Textron Inc. Helicopters

units.obligation_text: You are responsible for performing each action required by this AD within the specified compliance time unless it has already been accomplished prior to that time.
units.action_summary: Perform each action required by this AD within the specified compliance times unless already done.

units.obligation_text: Within 25 hours time-in-service or 30 days, whichever occurs first:
units.action_summary: Time threshold: within 25 hours TIS or 30 days, perform the specified inspection/removal actions in (f)(1)(i) and (ii).

units.obligation_text: Remove the T/R hub and blade assembly from the helicopter and remove the T/R blade from the hub. Remove the paint from the spar area on both sides of the T/R blade by following the Accomplishment Instructions, paragraphs 3. through 5., of the following Bell Alert Service Bulletins, all Revision A, and all dated December 8, 2009: Alert Service Bulletin (ASB) No. 205–09–102 for the Model 205A and 205A–1 helicopters; ASB No. 205B–09–54 for the Model 205B helicopters; ASB No. 212–09–134 for the Model 212 helicopters; ASB No. 412CF–09–38 for the Model 412CF helicopters; and ASB No. 412–09–136 for the Model 412 and 412EP helicopters.
units.action_summary: Remove the tail rotor hub/blade assembly and T/R blade; remove paint from spar areas following specified Bell ASBs.

units.obligation_text: Using a 3-power or higher magnifying glass, visually inspect both sides of the T/R blade for any corrosion or pitting in the spar inspection areas as depicted in Figure 1 of the ASB for your model helicopter.
units.action_summary: Visually inspect both sides of the T/R blade spar inspection areas using a 3x or higher magnifying glass for corrosion or pitting.

units.obligation_text: Before further flight:
units.action_summary: Condition: before the next flight, perform one of the required actions in (f)(2)(i)-(iv) depending on inspection results.

units.obligation_text: If you find any corrosion or pitting that is 0.003 inch deep or less, either replace the T/R blade with an airworthy T/R blade or repair the T/R blade.
units.action_summary: If corrosion/pitting ≤ 0.003 inch, either replace the T/R blade with an airworthy blade or repair the blade.

units.obligation_text: If you find any corrosion or pitting that is greater than 0.003 inch deep, replace the T/R blade with an airworthy T/R blade.
units.action_summary: If corrosion/pitting > 0.003 inch, replace the T/R blade with an airworthy blade before further flight.

units.obligation_text: If any parent material is removed during the sanding operation required by paragraph (f)(1)(i) of this AD, either replace the T/R blade with an airworthy T/R blade, or repair the T/R blade if the parent material removed is within the maximum repair damage limits.
units.action_summary: If parent material is removed during sanding, replace the T/R blade or repair it if the removed material is within allowable repair limits.

units.obligation_text: If there is no corrosion or pitting and no damage greater than 0.003 inch deep, refinish the inspection areas and reinstall each T/R blade onto the T/R hub, install the T/R assembly on the helicopter and track and balance the T/R in accordance with the Accomplishment Instructions, paragraphs 8. through 10., of the ASB for your model helicopter.
units.action_summary: If no corrosion/pitting and no damage > 0.003 inch, refinish inspection areas, reinstall blades and T/R assembly, and track and balance per ASB instructions.

units.obligation_text: Actions accomplished before the effective date of this AD in accordance with the procedures specified in AD 2011–12–08 are acceptable for compliance with the corresponding actions specified in paragraph (f) of this AD.
units.action_summary: Previously accomplished actions done per AD 2011–12–08 count as compliance with the corresponding actions in paragraph (f).

units.action_summary: The Manager may approve alternative methods of compliance (AMOCs) for this AD.

units.action_summary: AMOC proposals must be sent to Daniel Moore at the provided postal address, telephone, or email.

title: High Elevation Airport Operations

units.obligation_text: Except as provided in paragraph (c) of this section, pressurized cabins and compartments to be occupied must be equipped to provide a cabin pressure altitude of not more than 8,000 feet under normal operating conditions.
units.actor: pressurized cabins and compartments to be occupied
units.action_summary: Cabins/compartments must be equipped to keep cabin pressure altitude at or below 8,000 feet in normal operations.

units.obligation_text: Warning indication at the pilot or flight engineer station to indicate when the safe or preset pressure differential and cabin pressure altitude limits are exceeded.
units.actor: warning indication at the pilot or flight engineer station (warning system)
units.action_summary: A warning indication must be provided at the pilot/flight engineer station to show when pressure differential or cabin pressure altitude limits are exceeded.

units.obligation_text: Appropriate warning markings on the cabin pressure differential indicator meet the warning requirement for pressure differential limits
units.actor: appropriate warning markings on the cabin pressure differential indicator
units.action_summary: Markings on the pressure differential indicator qualify as the required warning for pressure differential limits if they meet the stated condition.

units.obligation_text: an alert meets the warning requirement for cabin pressure altitude limits, if it warns the flightcrew when the cabin pressure altitude exceeds 10,000 feet, except as provided in paragraph (d) of this section.
units.action_summary: An alert satisfies the cabin pressure altitude warning requirement if it warns the flightcrew when cabin altitude exceeds 10,000 feet (subject to paragraph (d) exception).

units.obligation_text: When operating into or out of airports with elevations at or above 8,000 feet, the cabin pressure in pressurized cabins and occupied compartments may be equal to or less than the airport elevation provided:
units.actor: the cabin pressure in pressurized cabins and occupied compartments
units.action_summary: When operating to/from airports ≥8,000 ft elevation, cabin pressure may be set equal to or below the airport elevation (subject to conditions).

units.obligation_text: The airplane is being operated at or below 25,000 feet;
units.action_summary: The airplane must be operating at or below 25,000 feet (condition for the permission in paragraph (c)).

units.obligation_text: The cabin pressurization system is designed to minimize the time in flight that passenger cabin occupants may be exposed to cabin pressure altitudes exceeding 8,000 feet.
units.action_summary: Cabin pressurization system must be designed to minimize occupants' time exposed to cabin altitudes above 8,000 ft (condition for the permission in paragraph (c)).

units.obligation_text: When operating into or out of airports with elevations exceeding 8,000 feet and the airplane is at or below 25,000 feet, the cabin altitude warning alert may be provided at 15,000 feet, or 2,000 feet above the elevation, whichever is greater, provided that:
units.action_summary: When operating to/from airports >8,000 ft and airplane ≤25,000 ft, the cabin altitude warning may be set to 15,000 ft or 2,000 ft above airport elevation (whichever greater), subject to conditions.

units.obligation_text: An alert is provided to clearly indicate to the flightcrew that the cabin high altitude warning has shifted above 10,000 feet;
units.action_summary: An alert must clearly show the flightcrew that the cabin high-altitude warning threshold has been shifted above 10,000 ft.

units.obligation_text: If the cabin altitude warning alert is shifted above 10,000 feet automatically, an alert is provided to notify the flightcrew to take action should the automatic shift function fail;
units.action_summary: If the warning threshold shifts automatically above 10,000 ft, an alert must notify the flightcrew to take action if the automatic shift function fails.

units.obligation_text: Either an alerting system is installed to notify the flightcrew members on flight deck duty when to don oxygen in accordance with the applicable operating regulations; or flight procedures acceptable to the FAA administrator are provided in the airplane flight manual that require the pilot flying to don oxygen when the high altitude cabin warning has shifted above 10,000 feet and require other flightcrew members on flight deck duty to monitor the cabin pressure to utilize oxygen in accordance with the applicable operating regulations.
units.action_summary: Either install an alerting system to tell flightcrew when to don oxygen, or provide FAA-acceptable AFM procedures requiring donning and monitoring of oxygen when the high-altitude warning is shifted above 10,000 ft.

units.obligation_text: There must be an oxygen dispensing unit connected to oxygen supply terminals immediately available to each occupant wherever seated,
units.action_summary: An oxygen dispensing unit connected to oxygen supply must be immediately available to each occupant at every seat.

units.obligation_text: and at least two oxygen-dispensing units connected to oxygen terminals in each lavatory.
units.action_summary: Each lavatory must have at least two oxygen-dispensing units connected to oxygen terminals.

units.obligation_text: The total number of dispensing units and outlets in the cabin must exceed the number of seats by at least 10 percent.
units.action_summary: Total dispensing units and outlets in the cabin must be at least 10% greater than the number of seats.

units.obligation_text: The extra units must be as uniformly distributed throughout the cabin as practicable.
units.action_summary: Extra oxygen units must be distributed as uniformly as practicable throughout the cabin.

units.obligation_text: Except as provided in paragraph (c)(5) of this section, if certification for operation above 30,000 feet is requested, the dispensing units providing the required oxygen flow must be automatically presented to the occupants before the cabin pressure altitude exceeds 15,000 feet.
units.action_summary: If certification for operation above 30,000 ft is requested, oxygen dispensing units that provide required flow must present automatically to occupants before cabin altitude exceeds 15,000 ft (unless paragraph (c)(5) applies).

units.obligation_text: The crewmembers must be provided with a manual means of making the dispensing units immediately available in the event of failure of the automatic system.
units.action_summary: Crewmembers must be provided a manual way to make dispensing units immediately available if the automatic system fails.

units.obligation_text: When operating into or out of airports with elevations at or above 8,000 feet, the dispensing units providing the required oxygen flow may be automatically presented to the occupants at 15,000 feet or within 2,000 feet of the airport elevation, whichever is higher, provided the airplane is being operated at altitudes at or below 25,000 feet.
units.action_summary: When operating to/from airports ≥8,000 ft and airplane ≤25,000 ft, oxygen dispensing units may be presented automatically at 15,000 ft or within 2,000 ft of airport elevation (whichever is higher) as an alternative to the §25.1447(c)(1) requirement.

units.action_summary: Notify the applicant in writing of insufficient information or issues and tell them what is needed to complete the application.

units.obligation_text: If the FAA cannot review an accepted application because of lack of information or for any other reason, the FAA will toll the review period until the FAA receives the information it needs or the applicant resolves the issue.
units.action_summary: FAA will toll (pause) the review period until required information is received or issues are resolved.

units.obligation_text: Unless applying under incremental review and determination in accordance with § 450.33 of this chapter, if the FAA does not make a decision within 120 days of receiving an accepted license application or within 90 days of receiving an accepted permit application, the FAA informs the applicant, in writing, of any outstanding information needed to complete the review, or of any issues that would affect the decision.
units.action_summary: If FAA misses specified decision deadlines, it must inform the applicant in writing of outstanding information or issues affecting the decision.

units.obligation_text: If the FAA has denied an application in its entirety, the applicant may either—
units.action_summary: Applicant may take one of two options after an entire denial of the application.

units.obligation_text: Attempt to correct any deficiencies identified and ask the FAA to reconsider the revised application. The FAA has 60 days or the number of days remaining in the review period, whichever is greater, within which to reconsider the decision;
units.action_summary: Applicant may correct deficiencies and request FAA reconsideration; FAA must reconsider within 60 days or the remaining review period, whichever is greater.

units.obligation_text: Request a hearing in accordance with part 406 of this chapter, for the purpose of showing why the application should not be denied.
units.action_summary: Applicant may request a hearing under part 406 to contest the denial.

units.obligation_text: An applicant whose application is denied after reconsideration under paragraph (b)(1) of this section may request a hearing in accordance with paragraph (b)(2) of this section.
units.action_summary: If denied after reconsideration, applicant may request a hearing as described in paragraph (b)(2).

units.obligation_text: A safety element approval may be issued independent of a license, and it does not confer any authority to conduct activities for which a license is required under this chapter.
units.actor: the FAA (may issue); the holder (no authority conferred)
units.action_summary: FAA may issue safety element approvals independently, but such approval does not authorize activities that require a license.

units.obligation_text: A safety element approval does not relieve its holder of the duty to comply with all applicable requirements of law or regulation that may apply to the holder’s activities.
units.actor: the holder of a safety element approval
units.action_summary: Holder must comply with all applicable legal and regulatory requirements despite having a safety element approval.

units.obligation_text: Any person eligible under this part may apply to become the holder of a safety element approval.
units.action_summary: Eligible persons may apply for a safety element approval.

units.obligation_text: You may be eligible for a safety element approval if you are—
units.action_summary: Specifies categories of persons who may be eligible for a safety element approval.

units.obligation_text: A designer, manufacturer, or operator of a launch or reentry vehicle or component thereof;
units.action_summary: Designers, manufacturers, or operators may be eligible for safety element approval.

units.obligation_text: The designer or developer of a safety system or process;
units.actor: designer or developer of a safety system or process
units.action_summary: Designers or developers of safety systems/processes may be eligible.

units.obligation_text: Personnel who perform safety critical functions in conducting a licensed launch or reentry.
units.action_summary: Personnel performing safety-critical functions may be eligible for safety element approval.

units.obligation_text: A safety element approval applicant must have sufficient knowledge and expertise to show that the design and operation of the safety element for which safety element approval is sought qualify for a safety element approval.
units.action_summary: Applicant must demonstrate sufficient knowledge and expertise to qualify for safety element approval.

units.obligation_text: Only the safety elements defined under this part are eligible for a safety element approval.
units.action_summary: Eligibility for safety element approval is limited to safety elements defined in this part.

units.obligation_text: The applicant must consult with the FAA before submitting an application.
units.action_summary: Consult with the FAA prior to submitting an application.

units.obligation_text: The applicant must consult with the FAA before submitting an application.
units.action_summary: Applicant must consult with FAA before submission (pre-application consultation).

units.obligation_text: An applicant may submit an application for a safety element approval in one of two ways: (a) Separate from a vehicle operator license application in accordance with § 414.13; or (b) Concurrent with a vehicle operator license application in accordance with § 414.15.
units.action_summary: Applicant may submit a safety element approval application either separately or concurrently with a vehicle operator license application.

units.obligation_text: An applicant must make an application in writing and in English. The applicant must file the application with the Federal Aviation Administration either by paper, by use of physical electronic storage, or by email in the following manner:
units.action_summary: Applications must be in writing (English) and filed with FAA by specified submission methods.

units.obligation_text: For an application submitted on paper, an applicant must send two copies of the application to the Federal Aviation Administration, Associate Administrator for Commercial Space Transportation, Room 331, 800 Independence Avenue SW, Washington, DC 20591. Attention: Application Review.
units.action_summary: If submitting on paper, send two copies to the FAA address provided.

units.obligation_text: For an application submitted by use of physical electronic storage, the applicant must either mail the application to the address specified in paragraph (a)(1) of this section or hand-deliver the application to an authorized FAA representative. The application and the physical electronic storage containing the application must also satisfy all of the following criteria:
units.action_summary: If submitting via physical electronic storage, mail or hand-deliver it to FAA and satisfy the criteria specified.

units.obligation_text: The application must include a cover letter that is printed on paper and signed by the person who signed the application or by an authorized representative of the applicant;
units.action_summary: Include a paper cover letter signed by the signer of the application or an authorized representative.

units.obligation_text: The cover letter must identify each document that is included on the physical electronic storage;
units.action_summary: Cover letter must list each document included on the physical electronic storage.

units.obligation_text: The physical electronic storage must be in a format such that its contents cannot be altered.
units.action_summary: Provide physical electronic storage in a non-alterable format.

units.obligation_text: For an application submitted by email, an applicant must send the application as an email attachment, or as a link to a secure server, to ASTApplications@faa.gov. The application and the email to which the application is attached must also satisfy the following criteria:
units.action_summary: If submitting by email, send application as attachment or secure link to ASTApplications@faa.gov and meet the listed criteria.

units.obligation_text: The email to which the application is attached must be sent from an email address controlled by the person who signed the application or by an authorized representative of the applicant;
units.action_summary: Send the application email from an address controlled by the signer or authorized representative.

units.obligation_text: The email must identify each document that is included as an attachment or that is stored on a secure server;
units.action_summary: Identify each attached or server-stored document in the email.

units.obligation_text: The electronic files must be date-stamped and have version control documentation.
units.action_summary: Ensure electronic files are date-stamped and include version control documentation when emailed.

units.obligation_text: The application must identify the following basic information:
units.action_summary: Application must include specified basic identifying information.

units.obligation_text: Name and address of the applicant.
units.action_summary: Provide applicant's name and address.

units.obligation_text: Name, address, and telephone number of any person to whom inquiries and correspondence should be directed.
units.action_summary: Provide contact information for inquiries and correspondence.

units.obligation_text: Safety element as defined under this part for which the applicant seeks a safety element approval.
units.action_summary: Identify which safety element the applicant seeks approval for.

units.obligation_text: The application must contain the following technical information:
units.action_summary: Application must include specified technical information.

units.obligation_text: A Statement of Conformance letter, describing the specific criteria the applicant used to show the adequacy of the safety element for which a safety element approval is sought, and showing how the safety element complies with the specific criteria.
units.action_summary: Include a Statement of Conformance describing criteria used and showing compliance.

units.obligation_text: The specific operating limits for which the safety element approval is sought.
units.action_summary: Provide the specific operating limits for which approval is sought.

units.obligation_text: The following as applicable:
units.action_summary: Provide the following items as applicable to demonstrate safe performance.

units.obligation_text: Information and analyses required under this chapter that may be applicable to demonstrating safe performance of the safety element for which the safety element approval is sought.
units.action_summary: Provide relevant information and analyses required under this chapter for demonstrating safe performance.

units.obligation_text: Engineering design and analyses that show the adequacy of the proposed safety element for its intended use, such that the use in a licensed launch or reentry will not jeopardize public health or safety or the safety of property.
units.action_summary: Provide engineering design and analyses demonstrating adequacy and safety for intended use.

units.obligation_text: Relevant manufacturing processes.
units.action_summary: Provide information on relevant manufacturing processes as applicable.

units.obligation_text: Test and evaluation procedures.
units.action_summary: Provide test and evaluation procedures as applicable.

units.obligation_text: Test results.
units.action_summary: Provide applicable test results.

units.obligation_text: Maintenance procedures.
units.action_summary: Provide maintenance procedures as applicable.

units.obligation_text: Personnel qualifications and training procedures.
units.action_summary: Provide personnel qualifications and training procedures if applicable.

units.obligation_text: The application must be legibly signed, dated, and certified as true, complete, and accurate by one of the following:
units.action_summary: Application must be signed, dated, and certified as true, complete, and accurate by an authorized signer.

units.obligation_text: For a corporation, an officer or other individual authorized to act for the corporation in licensing or safety element approval matters.
units.action_summary: Corporate applications must be signed by an officer or authorized individual.

units.obligation_text: For a partnership or a sole proprietorship, a general partner or proprietor, respectively.
units.action_summary: Partnership or sole proprietor applications must be signed by the general partner or proprietor.

units.obligation_text: For a joint venture, association, or other entity, an officer or other individual duly authorized to act for the joint venture, association, or other entity in licensing matters.
units.actor: joint ventures, associations, or other entities
units.action_summary: Joint venture or similar entity applications must be signed by an authorized officer or individual.

units.obligation_text: Failure to comply with any of the requirements set forth in this section is sufficient basis for denial of a safety element approval application.
units.action_summary: Noncompliance with section requirements can result in denial of the safety element approval application.

units.obligation_text: An applicant for a vehicle operator license may also identify one or more sections of its application for which it seeks to obtain a safety element approval concurrently with a license. An applicant applying for a safety element approval concurrently with a license must—
units.actor: the applicant for a vehicle operator license
units.action_summary: An applicant applying concurrently must meet the following requirements.

units.obligation_text: Meet the applicable requirements of part 450 of this chapter;
units.action_summary: Meet applicable part 450 requirements when applying concurrently.

units.obligation_text: Provide the information required in § 414.13(b)(3) and (c)(2) and (3);
units.action_summary: Provide the specified information from §414.13 when applying concurrently.

units.obligation_text: Specify the sections of the license application that support its application for a safety element approval.
units.action_summary: Identify which sections of the license application support the safety element approval request.

units.obligation_text: The scope of the safety element approval will be limited to what the application supports.
units.action_summary: Safety element approval scope is limited to what the application demonstrates/supports.

units.obligation_text: To ensure confidentiality of data or information in the application, the applicant must—
units.action_summary: Applicant must take specified steps to request confidentiality for application data.

units.obligation_text: Send a written request with the application that trade secrets or proprietary commercial or financial data be treated as confidential, and include in the request the specific time frame confidential treatment is required.
units.action_summary: Send a written confidentiality request with the application, including the requested time frame for confidential treatment.

units.obligation_text: Mark data or information that require confidentiality with an identifying legend, such as "Proprietary Information," "Proprietary Commercial Information," "Trade Secret," or "Confidential Treatment Requested." Where this marking proves impracticable, attach a cover sheet that contains the identifying legend to the data or information for which confidential treatment is sought.
units.action_summary: Mark confidential data with an identifying legend or attach a cover sheet when marking is impracticable.

units.obligation_text: If the applicant requests confidential treatment for previously submitted data or information, the FAA will honor that request to the extent practicable in case of any prior distribution of the data or information. Data or information for which confidential treatment is requested or data or information that qualifies for exemption under 5 U.S.C. 552(b)(4) will not be disclosed to the public unless the Associate Administrator determines that withholding the
units.action_summary: FAA will honor confidentiality requests for previously submitted data when practicable; such data will not be disclosed to the public unless the Associate Administrator determines otherwise.

title: Airworthiness Directives: The Boeing Company Airplanes

units.obligation_text: The FAA must receive comments on this AD action by August 23, 2019.
units.action_summary: Comments on the AD must be received by the FAA by August 23, 2019.

units.obligation_text: Comply with this AD within the compliance times specified, unless already done.
units.action_summary: Operators must comply with the AD within the specified compliance times unless the actions have already been done.

units.obligation_text: Except as specified in paragraph (h) of this AD: Within 36 months after the effective date of this AD or at the applicable times specified in paragraph 1.E., 'Compliance,' of Boeing Alert Service Bulletin 727–34A0247, dated January 2, 2019; Boeing Alert Service Bulletin 757–34A0611, Revision 1, dated March 22, 2019; or Boeing Alert Service Bulletin 767–34A0828, dated December 6, 2018; as applicable, whichever occurs first, do all applicable actions identified as 'RC' (required for compliance) in, and in accordance with, the Accomplishment Instructions of [the identified Boeing Alert Service Bulletins]; as applicable.
units.actor: Owners/operators of the affected airplanes (or maintenance providers)
units.action_summary: Within specified times, operators must perform all actions labeled 'RC' in the listed Boeing Alert Service Bulletins in accordance with their Accomplishment Instructions.

units.obligation_text: Within 36 months after the effective date of this AD or at the applicable times specified in paragraph 1.E., 'Compliance,' of [the listed Boeing Alert Service Bulletins]; as applicable, whichever occurs first, ...
units.action_summary: The required RC actions must be performed within 36 months after the AD effective date or at the applicable times in the identified service bulletins, whichever occurs first.

units.obligation_text: All replacements of the affected AOA sensors must be done before further flight.
units.action_summary: Any replacement of affected AOA sensors must be accomplished prior to the next flight.

units.obligation_text: Where Boeing Alert Service Bulletin [identified] uses the phrase 'the original issue date of this service bulletin,' this AD requires using 'the effective date of this AD.'
units.actor: Persons determining compliance with this AD (operators/maintainers)
units.action_summary: When service bulletins refer to 'original issue date,' use the AD's effective date for compliance purposes.

units.obligation_text: The Manager, Los Angeles ACO Branch, FAA, has the authority to approve AMOCs for this AD, if requested using the procedures found in 14 CFR 39.19.
units.actor: Manager, Los Angeles ACO Branch, FAA
units.action_summary: The Los Angeles ACO Branch Manager may approve Alternative Methods of Compliance (AMOCs) for this AD using procedures in 14 CFR 39.19.

units.obligation_text: In accordance with 14 CFR 39.19, send your request to your principal inspector or local Flight Standards District Office, as appropriate.
units.action_summary: AMOC requests must be sent to the requester's principal inspector or local FSDO per 14 CFR 39.19.

units.obligation_text: If sending information directly to the manager of the certification office, send it to the attention of the person identified in paragraph (j)(1) of this AD.
units.actor: Requester sending information directly to the manager
units.action_summary: If sending AMOC information directly to the certification office manager, address it to the person named in paragraph (j)(1).

units.obligation_text: Information may be emailed to: 9-ANM-LAACO-AMOC-Requests@faa.gov.
units.action_summary: AMOC request information may be sent via the provided email address.

units.obligation_text: Before using any approved AMOC, notify your appropriate principal inspector, or lacking a principal inspector, the manager of the local flight standards district office/certificate holding district office.
units.action_summary: Before using an approved AMOC, operators must notify their principal inspector or, if none, the local FSDO/CHDO manager.

units.obligation_text: An AMOC that provides an acceptable level of safety may be used for any repair, modification, or alteration required by this AD if it is approved by The Boeing Company Organization Designation Authorization (ODA) that has been authorized by the Manager, Los Angeles ACO Branch, FAA, to make those findings.
units.actor: Owners/operators (to use AMOC) and Boeing ODA (to approve)
units.action_summary: Operators may use an AMOC for AD-required repairs/modifications/alterations if approved by the authorized Boeing ODA.

units.obligation_text: To be approved, the repair method, modification deviation, or alteration deviation must meet the certification basis of the airplane, and the approval must specifically refer to this AD.
units.actor: AMOC applicant and approving authority (Boeing ODA/FAA)
units.action_summary: For approval, the proposed repair/modification/alteration must meet the airplane's certification basis and the approval must explicitly refer to this AD.

units.obligation_text: The steps labeled as RC, including substeps under an RC step and any figures identified in an RC step, must be done to comply with the AD.
units.action_summary: All actions labeled 'RC' in the service information (including substeps and referenced figures) are mandatory for AD compliance.

units.obligation_text: If a step or substep is labeled 'RC Exempt,' then the RC requirement is removed from that step or substep.
units.actor: Owners/operators/maintenance personnel interpreting the service information
units.action_summary: Steps labeled 'RC Exempt' are not subject to the RC requirement.

units.obligation_text: An AMOC is required for any deviations to RC steps, including substeps and identified figures.
units.action_summary: Any deviation from RC steps (including substeps and figures) requires approval via an AMOC.

units.obligation_text: Steps not labeled as RC may be deviated from using accepted methods in accordance with the operator's maintenance or inspection program without obtaining approval of an AMOC, provided the RC steps, including substeps and identified figures, can still be done as specified, and the airplane can be put back in an airworthy condition.
units.action_summary: Non-RC steps may be altered using accepted methods under the operator's program without AMOC approval, if RC steps remain accomplishable and the airplane can be returned to airworthy condition.

units.obligation_text: Provided the RC steps, including substeps and identified figures, can still be done as specified, and the airplane can be put back in an airworthy condition.
units.action_summary: The permission to deviate non-RC steps applies only if RC steps remain accomplishable and the airplane can be restored to airworthy condition.

units.obligation_text: We must receive comments by July 1, 2019.

units.obligation_text: Comply with this AD within the compliance times specified, unless already done.

units.obligation_text: Except as specified in paragraph (h) of this AD: Comply with all required actions and compliance times specified in, and in accordance with, EASA AD 2018–0276R1, dated January 11, 2019; corrected January 15, 2019 ("EASA AD 2018–0276R1").

units.actor: Manager, International Section, Transport Standards Branch, FAA

units.obligation_text: unless already done.

units.obligation_text: Within 24 months after the effective date of this AD, do a general visual inspection for discrepancies of fairing panel 194E, wheel well panel 193D, and support structure, and do all applicable related investigative and corrective actions, in accordance with Part 1 and Part 2 of the Accomplishment Instructions of Boeing Service Bulletin 737–53–1307, dated January 12, 2012.

units.action_summary: Within 24 months, perform a general visual inspection of fairing panel 194E, wheel well panel 193D, and support structure and perform related investigative and corrective actions per Boeing Service Bulletin Parts 1 and 2.

units.obligation_text: All applicable related investigative and corrective actions must be done before further flight.

units.obligation_text: Repeat the inspection thereafter at intervals not to exceed 1,000 flight cycles.

units.obligation_text: If the initial inspection required by paragraph (g)(1) shows that fairing panel 194E, wheel well panel 193D, and the support structure have the number and type of attachments specified in the post-reworked configuration of Boeing Service Bulletin 737–53–1307, dated January 12, 2012, then the repetitive inspections required by paragraph (g)(1) of this AD are terminated.
units.actor: owners and operators of airplanes having line numbers 3533 and subsequent with an original airworthiness certificate or an original export certificate of airworthiness dated on or before the effective date of this AD

units.obligation_text: Within 72 months after the effective date of this AD, do the actions required by paragraph (h)(1) or (h)(2) of this AD, as applicable.

units.action_summary: Within 72 months, accomplish either the rework in (h)(1) or the verification in (h)(2) as applicable.

units.obligation_text: Rework fairing panel 194E, wheel well panel 193D, and the support structure, including accomplishment of all applicable related investigative actions and repair, in accordance with Part 3 of the Accomplishment Instructions of Boeing Service Bulletin 737–53–1307, dated January 12, 2012.
units.action_summary: Perform rework of the panels and support structure and perform investigative actions and repairs per Part 3 of the Boeing Service Bulletin.

units.obligation_text: All applicable related investigative actions and repairs must be done before further flight.
units.action_summary: Complete all investigations and repairs from the rework before the airplane is next flown.

units.obligation_text: Verify that fairing panel 194E, wheel well panel 193D, and the support structure have the number and type of attachments specified in the post-reworked configuration of Boeing Service Bulletin 737–53–1307, dated January 12, 2012.
units.action_summary: Verify that the panels and support structure have the specified number and type of attachments for the post-reworked configuration.

units.obligation_text: As of the effective date of this AD, no person may install a fairing panel 194E on any airplane identified in paragraph (c) of this AD, unless fairing panel 194E, wheel well panel 193D, and the support structure have the number and type of attachments specified in the post-reworked configuration of Boeing Service Bulletin 737–53–1307, dated January 12, 2012.
units.action_summary: Prohibits installation of fairing panel 194E on affected airplanes unless the attachments match the post-reworked configuration.

units.obligation_text: installation allowed only if fairing panel 194E, wheel well panel 193D, and the support structure have the number and type of attachments specified in the post-reworked configuration of Boeing Service Bulletin 737–53–1307, dated January 12, 2012.

title: Airworthiness Directives: Rolls-Royce plc Turbofan Engines

units.obligation_text: The FAA must receive comments on this AD action by August 8, 2019.
units.action_summary: FAA must receive public comments on the AD by August 8, 2019.

units.obligation_text: Comply with this AD within the compliance times specified, unless already done.
units.action_summary: Operators must comply with the AD within the specified compliance times unless already complied.

units.obligation_text: Within 7,500 engine flight hours (FHs) since new, or since the last inspection, or within 150 flight cycles (FCs) after the January 5, 2017 (the effective date of AD 2016–24–08), whichever occurs later, inspect the engine upper bifurcation fairing for cracks or missing material.
units.actor: operators/maintenance personnel of the affected engines
units.action_summary: Perform an initial inspection of the upper bifurcation fairing within the specified FH/FC threshold.

units.obligation_text: Use paragraph (g)(3) of this AD to perform the inspection.
units.actor: operators/maintenance personnel of the affected engines
units.action_summary: The inspection required by paragraph (g)(1) must be performed following the procedures in paragraph (g)(3).

units.obligation_text: Repeat the inspection required by paragraph (g)(1) of this AD within every 7,500 engine FHs since last inspection.
units.actor: operators/maintenance personnel of the affected engines
units.action_summary: Perform the inspection repeatedly at intervals of every 7,500 engine flight hours since the last inspection.

units.obligation_text: Inspect the engine upper bifurcation fairing as follows.
units.actor: operators/maintenance personnel of the affected engines
units.action_summary: Conduct inspection of the upper bifurcation fairing according to the detailed steps that follow.

units.obligation_text: Visually inspect upper bifurcation fairing seal face 22, seal support 23, and Zone A for any cracks or material loss on the right side.
units.action_summary: Perform a visual inspection of specified fairing areas on the right side for cracks or material loss.

units.obligation_text: If fairing seal face 22 is found to have released material, repair or replace the fairing before further flight.
units.action_summary: If material release is found on seal face 22, repair or replace the fairing prior to next flight.

units.obligation_text: If there is a single crack found on fairing seal face 22, shorter than 6 mm, repair or replace the fairing within 100 engine FCs, or at the next shop visit, whichever occurs sooner.
units.action_summary: If a single crack <6 mm is found on seal face 22, repair or replace within 100 engine flight cycles or at the next shop visit, whichever is sooner.

units.obligation_text: If there is a single crack, longer than 6 mm, found on fairing seal face 22, repair or replace the fairing within 15 engine FCs or at the next shop visit, whichever occurs sooner.
units.action_summary: If a single crack >6 mm is found on seal face 22, repair or replace within 15 engine flight cycles or at the next shop visit, whichever is sooner.

units.obligation_text: If there are two or more cracks found on fairing seal face 22, replace the fairing within 15 engine FCs or at next shop visit, whichever occurs sooner.
units.action_summary: If two or more cracks are found on seal face 22, replace the fairing within 15 engine flight cycles or at the next shop visit, whichever is sooner.

units.obligation_text: If there is any cracking or material loss found on seal support 23, replace the fairing within 15 engine FCs or at next shop visit, whichever occurs sooner.
units.action_summary: If any cracking or material loss is found on seal support 23, replace the fairing within 15 engine flight cycles or at the next shop visit.

units.obligation_text: If the visual inspection required by paragraph (g)(3)(i) of this AD does not detect any cracks, fluorescent penetrant inspect Zone A.
units.action_summary: If visual inspection finds no cracks, perform a fluorescent penetrant inspection of Zone A.

units.obligation_text: If a crack shorter than 6 mm is detected, repair or replace the fairing within 100 engine FCs, or at the next shop visit, whichever occurs sooner.
units.action_summary: If fluorescent penetrant inspection detects a crack <6 mm, repair or replace within 100 engine flight cycles or at next shop visit, whichever is sooner.

units.obligation_text: If a crack longer than 6 mm is detected, repair or replace the fairing within 15 engine FCs or at the next shop visit, whichever occurs sooner.
units.action_summary: If fluorescent penetrant inspection detects a crack >6 mm, repair or replace within 15 engine flight cycles or at next shop visit, whichever is sooner.

units.obligation_text: At the next engine shop visit after the effective date of this AD, modify the upper bifurcation fairing assembly in accordance with the Accomplishment Instructions, paragraph 3., of RR Service Bulletin (SB) RB.211–72–J803, Revision 1, dated July 13, 2018, or Original Issue, dated December 7, 2017.
units.action_summary: Modify the upper bifurcation fairing assembly at the next engine shop visit following the AD effective date per the specified service bulletin instructions.

units.obligation_text: Installation of a modified upper bifurcation fairing assembly is terminating action to the inspections required by paragraphs (g)(1) through (g)(3) of this AD.
units.action_summary: Installing the modified fairing terminates the inspection requirements of paragraphs (g)(1)–(g)(3).

units.obligation_text: After the effective date of this AD do not install an upper bifurcation fairing assembly, part number FK25470, onto any engine.
units.actor: any person installing or maintaining engines (installers/operators/maintenance personnel)
units.action_summary: Prohibits installing upper bifurcation fairing assembly part number FK25470 on any engine after the AD's effective date.

title: Special Flight Authorizations for Supersonic Aircraft

units.obligation_text: For all civil aircraft, any operation that exceeds Mach 1 may be conducted only in accordance with a special flight authorization issued to an operator under the requirements of this section.
units.action_summary: Operations exceeding Mach 1 are permitted only with a special flight authorization issued under this section.
units.modal_raw: may (only in accordance with a special flight authorization)

units.obligation_text: Application for a special flight authorization to exceed Mach 1 must be made to the FAA Office of Environment and Energy for consideration by the Administrator.
units.action_summary: Applicants must submit an application to the FAA Office of Environment and Energy for consideration by the Administrator.

units.obligation_text: Each application must include:
units.action_summary: Applications are required to include the information listed in the following items.

units.obligation_text: The name of the operator;
units.action_summary: Application must include the operator's name.

units.obligation_text: The number and model(s) of the aircraft to be operated;
units.action_summary: Application must include aircraft number and models.

units.obligation_text: The number of proposed flights;
units.action_summary: Application must state number of proposed flights.

units.obligation_text: The date range during which the flights would be conducted;
units.action_summary: Application must provide the date range for flights.

units.obligation_text: The time of day the flights would be conducted.
units.action_summary: Application must specify the time of day for the flights.

units.obligation_text: Proposed night operations may require further justification for their necessity;
units.actor: FAA (may require) / applicants proposing night operations
units.action_summary: Proposed night operations may be required by the FAA to include additional justification of necessity.

units.obligation_text: A description of the flight area requested by the applicant, including any environmental analysis required under paragraph (c) of this section;
units.action_summary: Application must include a description of the flight area and any required environmental analysis under paragraph (c).

units.obligation_text: All conditions and limitations on the flights that will ensure that no measurable sonic boom overpressure will reach the surface outside of the proposed flight area;
units.action_summary: Application must include all conditions and limitations that ensure no measurable sonic boom overpressure reaches surface outside the proposed area.

units.obligation_text: The reason(s) that operation at a speed greater than Mach 1 is necessary.
units.action_summary: Application must explain why operation above Mach 1 is necessary.

units.obligation_text: A special flight authorization to exceed Mach 1 may be granted only for operations that are intended to:
units.action_summary: The FAA may grant authorizations to exceed Mach 1 only for specified intended purposes.

units.obligation_text: Show compliance with airworthiness requirements;
units.action_summary: Authorization may be granted for operations intended to show compliance with airworthiness requirements.

units.obligation_text: Determine the sonic boom characteristics of an aircraft;
units.action_summary: Authorization may be granted for operations intended to determine sonic boom characteristics.

units.obligation_text: Establish a means of reducing or eliminating the effects of sonic boom, including flight profiles and special features of an aircraft;
units.action_summary: Authorization may be granted for operations intended to establish methods to reduce or eliminate sonic boom effects.

units.obligation_text: Demonstrate the conditions and limitations under which speeds in excess of Mach 1 will not cause a measurable sonic boom overpressure to reach the surface;
units.action_summary: Authorization may be granted for operations intended to demonstrate conditions/limitations under which supersonic flight will not cause measurable sonic boom at the surface.

units.obligation_text: Measure the noise characteristics of an aircraft to demonstrate compliance with noise requirements imposed under this chapter, or to determine the limits for operation in accordance with § 91.817(b) of this part.
units.action_summary: Authorization may be granted for operations intended to measure noise characteristics to show compliance or determine operational limits.

units.obligation_text: For any purpose listed in paragraph (a)(8) of this section, each applicant must indicate why its intended operation cannot be safely or properly accomplished over the ocean at a distance ensuring that no sonic boom overpressure reaches any land surface in the United States.
units.action_summary: Applicants must explain why the operation cannot be done over the ocean far enough offshore to prevent sonic boom overpressure on U.S. land.

units.obligation_text: An applicant may apply for an authorization to conduct flights outside a test area under certain conditions and limitations upon a conservative showing that:
units.action_summary: Applicants may seek authorization to conduct flights outside a test area only if they make a conservative showing satisfying the listed conditions.

units.obligation_text: Flights within a test area have been conducted in accordance with an authorization granted under paragraph (a)(8)(iv) of this section;
units.action_summary: Applicant must show that flights within a test area have been conducted under an authorization per (a)(8)(iv).

units.obligation_text: The results of the flight tests demonstrate that a speed in excess of Mach 1 does not cause a measurable sonic boom overpressure to reach the surface;
units.action_summary: Applicant must show test results demonstrating supersonic speeds do not cause measurable sonic boom overpressure at the surface.

units.obligation_text: The conditions and limitations determined by that test represent all foreseeable operating conditions and are effective on all flights conducted under an authorization.
units.action_summary: Applicant must show that test-determined conditions/limitations cover all foreseeable operating conditions and are effective on all authorized flights.

units.obligation_text: No special flight authorization will be granted if the Administrator finds that such action is necessary to protect or enhance the environment.
units.action_summary: The Administrator will not grant an authorization if granting would be incompatible with protecting or enhancing the environment.
units.modal_raw: will not be granted (if Administrator finds necessary)

units.obligation_text: The Administrator is required to determine whether the issuance of an authorization for a particular flight area is a 'major Federal action significantly affecting the quality of the human environment' pursuant to the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969 (NEPA), and related Executive Orders and guidance.
units.action_summary: The Administrator must determine whether issuing the authorization constitutes a major Federal action under NEPA.

units.obligation_text: Accordingly, each applicant must provide information that sufficiently describes the environmental impact of any flight in excess of Mach 1, including the effect of a sonic boom reaching the surface in the proposed flight area, as a means to inform a determination by the Administrator.
units.action_summary: Applicants must supply information describing environmental impacts of supersonic flights to inform the Administrator's NEPA determination.

units.obligation_text: An Environmental Impact Statement prepared for the proposed flight area for the purpose of this application;
units.action_summary: Applicants may provide an Environmental Impact Statement prepared for the proposed flight area for this application.

units.obligation_text: An Environmental Impact Statement previously prepared for the proposed flight area, when the FAA has reviewed it and determined the continued adequacy, accuracy, validity and timeliness of the findings it contains;
units.action_summary: Applicants may submit a previously prepared EIS if the FAA reviews and finds it still adequate, accurate, valid, and timely.
units.modal_raw: may take the form of (when FAA has reviewed and determined adequate)

units.obligation_text: Another statement or finding of environmental impact for the proposed flight area, such as an Environmental Assessment, when the FAA has reviewed it and finds that such material is sufficient for the Administrator to make the required determinations for the proposed flight area.
units.action_summary: Applicants may provide another environmental statement or assessment if the FAA reviews and deems it sufficient for the Administrator's determinations.
units.modal_raw: may take the form of (when FAA has reviewed and finds sufficient)

units.obligation_text: An authorization to operate a civil aircraft in excess of Mach 1 may be issued only after an applicant has submitted the information described in this section and the Administrator has taken the required action regarding the environmental findings described in paragraph (c) of this section.
units.action_summary: The FAA may issue an authorization to exceed Mach 1 only after the applicant submits required information and the Administrator completes required environmental actions.

units.obligation_text: After an applicant has submitted the information described in this section (condition to issuance).
units.action_summary: Issuance requires that the applicant has submitted the information described in the section.

units.obligation_text: And the Administrator has taken the required action regarding the environmental findings described in paragraph (c) of this section (condition to issuance).
units.action_summary: Issuance requires that the Administrator has taken the required environmental actions described in paragraph (c).

units.obligation_text: An authorization to exceed Mach 1 will be granted for the time the Administrator determines necessary to conduct the flights for the described purposes.
units.action_summary: Authorization duration is the time the Administrator determines necessary to conduct the described flights.

units.obligation_text: An authorization to exceed Mach 1 is effective until it expires or is surrendered.
units.action_summary: An authorization remains effective until it either expires or is surrendered by the holder.

units.obligation_text: An authorization to exceed Mach 1 may be terminated, suspended or amended by the Administrator at any time the Administrator finds that such action is necessary to protect the environment.
units.action_summary: The Administrator may terminate, suspend, or amend an authorization whenever the Administrator finds such action necessary to protect the environment.

units.obligation_text: The holder of an authorization to exceed Mach 1 may request reconsideration of a termination, amendment or suspension issued under paragraph (e)(3) of this section within 30 days of notice of the action.
units.action_summary: The holder may request reconsideration of administrative termination, amendment, or suspension within 30 days of notice.

units.obligation_text: Failure to request reconsideration and provide information why the Administrator’s action is not appropriate will result in permanent termination of the authorization.
units.action_summary: If the holder fails to request reconsideration and provide information, the authorization will be permanently terminated.

units.action_summary: At the next engine shop visit, remove the affected HPT inner stationary seal and replace it with an approved non-listed seal or an eligible repaired seal.

units.obligation_text: After removing the affected HPT inner stationary seal required by paragraph (g)(1), inspect the removed HPT inner stationary seal for honeycomb separation, as defined in the Accomplishment Instructions, paragraph 3.C.(1), in CFM SB CFM56–5B S/B 72–0952, dated April 23, 2019, or in CFM SB CFM56–7B S/B 72–1054, dated April 23, 2019.

units.obligation_text: If honeycomb separation is found during the inspection required by paragraph (g)(2) of this AD, before further flight:
units.action_summary: Conditional requirement: if inspection finds honeycomb separation, before further flight certain corrective actions must be performed.

units.obligation_text: Remove the rotating air HPT front seal from service and replace with a part eligible for installation.
units.action_summary: Remove and replace the rotating air HPT front seal with an eligible part before further flight if honeycomb separation is found.

units.obligation_text: Inspect the HPT rotor blade internal cavities for honeycomb metal debris per the Accomplishment Instructions, paragraph 3.C.(1)(a)(4), of CFM SB CFM56–5B S/B 72–0952, dated April 23, 2019, or CFM SB CFM56–7B S/B 72–1054, dated April 23, 2019.
units.action_summary: Inspect HPT rotor blade internal cavities for honeycomb metal debris per the referenced service bulletin instructions.

units.obligation_text: If honeycomb metal debris is found, remove the HPT rotor blade from service and replace with a part eligible for installation.
units.action_summary: If debris is found during inspection, remove and replace the HPT rotor blade with an eligible part.

units.obligation_text: Remove the No. 3 ball bearing from service and replace with a part eligible for installation.
units.action_summary: Remove and replace the No. 3 ball bearing with an eligible part before further flight if honeycomb separation is found.

units.obligation_text: If flight deck temperature is excessively hot and could cause incapacitation: (procedural steps follow).

Set the trim air switch to OFF.

units.obligation_text: If outlet air stays excessively hot after one minute: Pack Control Selectors (Both) ........................ STBY-N

units.actor: owner/operator (pilot) holding at least a private pilot certificate

units.obligation_text: Open the oil cooler/baggage compartment door on the right hand side of the helicopter to gain access to the interior of the tail boom.
units.action_summary: Open the specified compartment door to access the tail boom interior.

units.obligation_text: Remove paint and stray sealant and clean the eight attachment fittings (four on the tail boom side and four on the fuselage side). Remove paint and stray sealant and clean the four cap angles, forward of the fuselage fittings, for at least 12 inches from the end of the fittings. Remove paint and stray sealant and clean the four longerons, aft of the tail boom fittings, for at least 12 inches from the end of the fittings.
units.action_summary: Remove paint/stray sealant and clean eight attachment fittings, four cap angles (12 inches forward), and four longerons (12 inches aft).

units.obligation_text: It is only necessary to remove the topcoat. Primer may be left in place and edge and fillet sealant may be left in place.
units.action_summary: You may leave primer and edge/fillet sealant in place; only the topcoat needs removal.

units.obligation_text: If any primer or edge or fillet sealant is removed, before further flight, reapply the removed primer and sealant.
units.action_summary: If primer or edge/fillet sealant is removed during cleaning, reapply it before the next flight.

units.obligation_text: With an additional person pushing on the tail boom at the third vertical rivet line aft of the trailing edge of the elevator with both hands and gradually applying and relieving pressure using body weight a minimum of three times in each of the following directions: Inboard pushing from the left; inboard pushing from the right; and upward pushing from the bottom; and using a bright light and borescope, inspect each of the four tail boom attachment structures for cracks, bond separation, and loose rivets. On the fuselage side, inspect the fittings and the cap angles running forward from the fittings, paying particular attention to the fitting sections near the rivets closest to the attachment bolts and the cap angle rivets next to the fittings. On the tail boom side, inspect the fittings and the longerons running aft from the fittings, paying particular attention to the fitting sections near the rivets closest to the attachment bolts. Without pushing on the tail boom, and using a bright light and borescope, inspect each of the four tail boom attachment structures for scratches, nicks, gouges, tears, corrosion, buckling, and distortion, and for loose, missing, and smoking rivets.
units.action_summary: Perform the specified push and non-push inspections using a bright light and borescope, examining fittings, cap angles, longerons, and rivets for listed defects.

units.obligation_text: If there are any scratches, nicks, gouges, tears, or corrosion within allowable limits, before further flight, repair the affected components.
units.action_summary: Repair scratched/nicked/gouged/teared/corroded components that are within allowable limits before next flight.

units.section: (g)(2)(iii) (remove if exceed limits or severe defects)
units.obligation_text: If there are any scratches, nicks, gouges, tears, or corrosion that exceed allowable limits, or any cracks, buckling or distortion, or loose, missing, or smoking rivets, before further flight, remove the affected components from service.
units.action_summary: Remove from service any components with defects exceeding allowable limits or with cracks, buckling, distortion, or loose/missing/smoking rivets before further flight.

units.obligation_text: If there is any bond separation, before further flight, re-bond the affected components.
units.action_summary: If bond separation is found, re-bond the affected components before the helicopter's next flight.

units.obligation_text: It is not required to push on the tail boom on helicopters with 39-inch extended landing gear installed per STC SR01742NY while checking for cracks, bond separation, and loose rivets.
units.actor: maintenance personnel / owner/operator of helicopters with the specified STC
units.action_summary: Do not have to perform the pushing portion of the inspection on helicopters with the specified 39-inch extended landing gear STC.

units.obligation_text: Inspect each of the four tail boom attachment bolts for exposed threads. If there is less than one full thread or more than three threads exposed, before further flight, remove the bolt and self-locking nut from service and replace with a new bolt and new self-locking nut.
units.action_summary: Inspect bolt threads; if exposed threads are less than one or more than three, remove and replace the bolt and self-locking nut before flight.

units.obligation_text: Inspect each of the four tail boom attachment bolts for movement by either applying the required installation torque in the tightening direction only, or by inspecting for torque stripe misalignment if present and attempting to rotate the bolt by hand. If a bolt is under-torqued, a torque stripe is misaligned, or a bolt moves, before further flight, remove the bolt and self-locking nut from service and replace with a new bolt and new self-locking nut.
units.action_summary: Check bolt movement by torquing in the tightening direction or checking torque stripe and attempting rotation; if under-torqued/misaligned/moves, remove and replace bolt and nut before flight.

units.obligation_text: After the first flight following any bolt replacement as required by paragraph (g)(iv) or (v) of this AD, retighten any replaced bolt by applying torque in the tightening direction only and then apply a torque stripe on the bolt head.
units.action_summary: After the first post-replacement flight, retorque replaced bolt in tightening direction only and apply a torque stripe.

units.obligation_text: At intervals not to exceed 25 hours TIS, perform the actions required by paragraph (g)(2)(i) through (vi) of this AD, except you are only required to perform the actions on the upper left hand tail boom attachment structure and bolt.
units.actor: owners/operators / maintenance personnel of the affected helicopters
units.action_summary: Every ≤25 hours TIS, perform the (g)(2)(i)–(vi) actions but only on the upper left tail boom attachment structure and bolt.

units.obligation_text: At intervals not to exceed 100 hours TIS, perform the actions required by paragraph (g)(2)(i) through (vi) of this AD at all four tail boom attachment locations.
units.actor: owners/operators / maintenance personnel of the affected helicopters
units.action_summary: Every ≤100 hours TIS, perform the (g)(2)(i)–(vi) actions at all four tail boom attachment locations.

units.obligation_text: Within 110 hours time-in-service, remove the sealing compound and inspect each screw on the RH and LH rear attachment fitting by identifying the number of threads "F" that extend beyond the nut as shown in Detail "B" of Figure 2 of Airbus Helicopter Alert Service Bulletin No. AS332–53.02.04, Revision 0, dated November 21, 2018 (ASB AS332–53.02.04).
