units.obligation_text: If there are 2 or less threads on each of the four screws; or there are 3 or more threads on any screw with a thread height "H" less than 5 mm (0.196 in), before further flight, apply a sealing compound on the nuts, and convex and concave washers.
units.action_summary: If thread count/height condition met, apply sealing compound to nuts and washers before further flight.

units.obligation_text: If there are 3 or more threads on any screw with a thread height "H" of 5 mm (0.196 in) or more, before further flight, do the following, and for more than one screw, do one at a time while working in a cross pattern: Remove from service the nut; and remove the screw from the helicopter and measure the length "L" of the screw as shown in Detail "D" of Figure 2 of ASB AS332–53.02.04.
units.action_summary: If thread count/height condition met, remove the nut and screw and measure screw length L (do screws one-at-a-time in cross pattern).

units.obligation_text: If any washers are bent or corroded, before further flight, remove from service the washers.
units.action_summary: If washers are bent or corroded, remove them from service before further flight.

units.obligation_text: If the length "L" measurement is less than or equal to 59.3 mm (2.334 in) for each screw removed as required by paragraph (e)(2) of this AD, visually inspect the screw for corrosion and cracks.
units.action_summary: If measured length L ≤ 59.3 mm, visually inspect the screw for corrosion and cracks.

units.obligation_text: For each screw with corrosion or a crack, before further flight, replace the screw with an airworthy screw.
units.action_summary: If inspection finds corrosion or cracks, replace the screw with an airworthy screw before further flight.

units.obligation_text: For any screw with no corrosion or cracks, before further flight, re-install the screw and washers. Install a new nut and apply sealant.
units.action_summary: If screw has no corrosion/cracks, re-install screw and washers, install new nut, and apply sealant before further flight.
units.modal_raw: before further flight, re-install / install / apply (conditional)

units.obligation_text: If the length "L" measurement is greater than 59.3 mm (2.334 in) for any screw removed as required by paragraph (e)(2) of this AD, before further flight, replace the rear attachment fitting that the screw was removed from and its set of four screws, washers, and nuts, and apply sealant as shown in Figures 2 and 3 of ASB AS332–53.02.04.
units.action_summary: If screw length L > 59.3 mm, replace the rear attachment fitting and its set of four screws, washers, and nuts, and apply sealant before further flight.

units.obligation_text: Within the next 100 hours time-in-service (TIS) after the effective date of this AD or within the next 12 months after the effective date of this AD, whichever occurs first, and thereafter at intervals not to exceed 7 years, inspect ...

units.obligation_text: Gain visual access to the inspection area by complying with either paragraph (g)(1)(i), (ii), (iii), or (iv) of this AD.

title: Airworthiness Directives: Piper Aircraft, Inc. Airplanes

units.obligation_text: This AD applies to Piper Aircraft, Inc. (Piper) airplanes, certificated in any category, with a model and serial number shown in table 1 to paragraph (c) of this AD, and that meet at least one of the criteria in paragraphs (c)(1), (2), or (3) of this AD.
units.actor: owners/operators of the specified Piper airplanes
units.action_summary: Specifies which Piper airplanes are subject to the AD (those listed and meeting at least one criterion).

units.obligation_text: Has accumulated 5,000 or more hours time-in-service (TIS);
units.action_summary: One applicability criterion is airplanes with 5,000 or more hours TIS.

units.obligation_text: Has had either main wing spar replaced with a serviceable main wing spar (more than zero hours TIS);
units.action_summary: One applicability criterion is airplanes that had a main wing spar replaced with a serviceable spar (non-zero TIS).

units.obligation_text: Has missing and/or incomplete maintenance records.
units.action_summary: One applicability criterion is airplanes with missing or incomplete maintenance records.

units.obligation_text: An owner/operator with at least a private pilot certificate may do the aircraft maintenance records review to determine the applicability as specified in paragraph (c) of this AD.
units.actor: owner/operator holding at least a private pilot certificate
units.action_summary: Owners/operators who hold at least a private pilot certificate are permitted to perform the maintenance records review to determine applicability.

units.obligation_text: Comply with this AD within the compliance times specified, unless already done.
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must comply with the AD within the specified compliance times unless the actions have already been done.

units.section: (h) Review Airplane Maintenance Records and Calculate Factored Service Hours
units.obligation_text: Review Airplane Maintenance Records and Calculate Factored Service Hours for Each Main Wing Spar.
units.action_summary: Requires review of maintenance records and calculation of factored service hours for each main wing spar.

units.obligation_text: Within 30 days after the effective date of this AD, review the airplane maintenance records and determine the number of 100-hour inspections completed on the airplane since new and any record of wing spar replacement(s).
units.action_summary: Within 30 days of the AD's effective date, review maintenance records to determine the count of 100-hour inspections and any wing spar replacements.

units.obligation_text: For purposes of this review, count any inspection conducted to comply with the 100-hour requirement of 14 CFR 91.409(b) ... If the purpose of an inspection was to comply with § 91.409(b), then it must be counted.
units.action_summary: When reviewing, inspections done to comply with §91.409(b) must be counted as 100-hour inspections.

units.obligation_text: If a main wing spar has been replaced with a new (zero hours TIS) main wing spar, count the number of 100-hour inspections from the time of installation of the new main wing spar.
units.action_summary: If spar replaced with new zero-hour spar, start counting 100-hour inspections from installation time.

units.obligation_text: If a main wing spar has been replaced with a serviceable main wing spar (more than zero hours TIS) or the airplane maintenance records are missing or incomplete, the wing history cannot be determined. Perform the eddy current inspection as specified in paragraph (i) of this AD.
units.action_summary: If spar replaced with serviceable (non-zero) or records are missing/incomplete, perform the eddy current inspection per paragraph (i).

units.obligation_text: The actions required by paragraph (h)(1) of this AD may be performed by the owner/operator (pilot) holding at least a private pilot certificate ...
units.actor: owner/operator (pilot) with at least a private pilot certificate
units.action_summary: Owner/operator with at least private pilot certificate is permitted to perform the actions required by paragraph (h)(1).

units.obligation_text: and must be entered into the aircraft records showing compliance with this AD in accordance with 14 CFR 43.9(a)(1) through (4), and 14 CFR 91.417(a)(2)(v).
units.action_summary: The actions performed must be recorded in the aircraft records in accordance with the cited CFR provisions.

units.obligation_text: The record must be maintained as required by 14 CFR 91.417, 121.380, or 135.439.
units.action_summary: The aircraft records must be maintained as required by the cited CFR sections.

units.obligation_text: Before further flight after completing the action in paragraph (h)(1) of this AD, calculate the factored service hours for each main wing spar using the formula in figure 1 to paragraph (h)(2) of this AD. Thereafter, after each annual inspection and 100-hour inspection, recalculate/update the factored service hours for each main wing spar until the main wing spar has accumulated 5,000 or more factored service hours.
units.action_summary: Calculate factored service hours before further flight after the records review, and recalculate after each annual and 100-hour inspection until 5,000 factored hours reached.

units.obligation_text: Within the compliance time specified in either paragraph (i)(1) or (2) of this AD, as applicable, eddy current inspect the inner surface of the two lower outboard bolt holes on the lower main wing spar cap for cracks using steps 1 through 3 in the Instructions of Piper Aircraft, Inc. Service Bulletin No. 1345, dated March 27, 2020.
units.action_summary: Conduct eddy current inspection of the specified bolt holes for cracks using steps 1-3 of Piper SB No. 1345 within the applicable compliance time.

units.obligation_text: Although Piper SB No. 1345 specifies NAS 410 Level II or Level III certification to perform the inspection, this AD allows Level II or Level III qualification standards for inspection personnel using any inspector criteria approved by the FAA.
units.action_summary: The AD permits use of Level II or Level III qualification standards using any FAA-approved inspector criteria (not limited to NAS 410 wording).

units.obligation_text: Within 100 hours TIS after complying with paragraph (h) of this AD or within 100 hours TIS after a main wing spar accumulates 5,000 factored service hours, whichever occurs later;
units.action_summary: For applicable airplanes, perform the inspection within 100 hours TIS after completing paragraph (h) or after a spar reaches 5,000 factored hours, whichever is later.

units.obligation_text: For airplanes with an unknown number of factored service hours on a main wing spar, within the next 100 hours TIS after the effective date of this AD or within 60 days after the effective date of this AD, whichever occurs later.
units.action_summary: If factored service hours are unknown, perform inspection within 100 hours TIS or 60 days after the AD effective date, whichever is later.

units.obligation_text: If a crack is found during an inspection required by paragraph (i) of this AD, before further flight, replace the main wing spar with a new (zero hours TIS) main wing spar.
units.action_summary: If inspection reveals a crack, the main wing spar must be replaced with a new (zero-hour) spar before further flight.

units.obligation_text: Before further flight after completing the actions required by paragraph (i) or (j) of this AD, install new bolts by following step 6 of Piper Aircraft, Inc. Service Bulletin No. 1345, dated March 27, 2020.
units.action_summary: After completing the inspection or spar replacement, install new bolts per step 6 of Piper SB No. 1345 before further flight.

units.obligation_text: Within 30 days after completing an inspection required by paragraph (i) of this AD, using Appendix 1, “Inspection Results Form,” of this AD, report the inspection results to the FAA at the Atlanta ACO Branch and to Piper.
units.action_summary: Within 30 days after the inspection, report the inspection results using the form to the FAA Atlanta ACO Branch and to Piper.

units.obligation_text: A special flight permit may only be issued to operate the airplane to a location where the inspection requirement of paragraph (i) of this AD can be performed.
units.action_summary: Special flight permits are permitted only to ferry the airplane to a location where the required inspection can be performed.

units.obligation_text: This AD prohibits a special flight permit if the inspection reveals a crack in a main wing spar.
units.action_summary: If an inspection reveals a crack, issuing a special flight permit is prohibited.

units.obligation_text: The FAA must receive comments on this AD action by December 21, 2020.
units.action_summary: Receive comments on this AD by December 21, 2020.

units.obligation_text: Comply with this AD within the compliance times specified, unless already done.
units.actor: owners/operators of affected airplanes (those subject to this AD)
units.action_summary: Comply with all requirements of this AD within the specified compliance times, unless already accomplished.

units.obligation_text: Within 24 months after May 20, 2013 (the effective date of AD 2013–07–09); Do a general visual inspection to determine if the serial number of the crew oxygen mask stowage box unit is identified in the Appendix of Intertechnique Service Bulletin MXP1/4–35–175, Revision 2, dated May 10, 2011, in accordance with the Accomplishment Instructions of Boeing Alert Service Bulletin 737–35A1121, Revision 1, dated November 7, 2011; Boeing Alert Service Bulletin 747–35A2126, Revision 1, dated September 29, 2011; or Boeing Alert Service Bulletin 767–35A0057, Revision 1, dated November 17, 2011; as applicable.
units.action_summary: Within 24 months after May 20, 2013, perform a general visual inspection to determine whether the crew oxygen mask stowage box unit serial number is listed in the specified Appendix, following the referenced Boeing service bulletin instructions.

units.obligation_text: A review of airplane maintenance records is acceptable in lieu of this inspection if the serial number of the crew oxygen mask stowage box unit can be conclusively determined from that review.
units.action_summary: You may use maintenance records instead of performing the visual inspection if the serial number can be conclusively determined from those records.

units.obligation_text: If any crew oxygen mask stowage box unit has a serial number identified in table 1 of the Appendix of Intertechnique Service Bulletin MXP1/4–35–175, Revision 2, dated May 10, 2011: Before further flight, replace the crew oxygen mask stowage box unit with a new or serviceable unit in accordance with the Accomplishment Instructions of Boeing Alert Service Bulletin 737–35A1121, Revision 1, dated November 7, 2011; Boeing Alert Service Bulletin 747–35A2126, Revision 1, dated September 29, 2011; or Boeing Alert Service Bulletin 767–35A0057, Revision 1, dated November 17, 2011; as applicable.
units.action_summary: If inspection finds a unit with a table 1 serial number, replace that stowage box unit with a new or serviceable unit before the next flight, following the referenced service bulletin instructions.

units.obligation_text: If any crew oxygen mask stowage box unit has a serial number identified in table 2 of the Appendix of Intertechnique Service Bulletin MXP1/4–35–175, Revision 2, dated May 10, 2011: Before further flight, add the letter "I" to the end of the serial number (identified as "SER") on the identification label, in accordance with the Accomplishment Instructions of Intertechnique Service Bulletin MXP1/4–35–175, Revision 2, dated May 10, 2011; and reinstall in accordance with the Accomplishment Instructions of Boeing Alert Service Bulletin 737–35A1121, Revision 1, dated November 7, 2011; Boeing Alert Service Bulletin 747–35A2126, Revision 1, dated September 29, 2011; or Boeing Alert Service Bulletin 767–35A0057, Revision 1, dated November 17, 2011; as applicable.
units.action_summary: If inspection finds a unit with a table 2 serial number, mark the serial number by adding 'I' and reinstall the unit before further flight, following the referenced instructions.

units.obligation_text: If no crew oxygen mask stowage box unit has a serial number identified in the Appendix of Intertechnique Service Bulletin MXP1/4–35–175, Revision 2, dated May 10, 2011: Unless a records review was done to determine the serial number, before further flight, reinstall the crew oxygen mask stowage box unit, in accordance with the Accomplishment Instructions of Boeing Alert Service Bulletin 737–35A1121, Revision 1, dated November 7, 2011; Boeing Alert Service Bulletin 747–35A2126, Revision 1, dated September 29, 2011; or Boeing Alert Service Bulletin 767–35A0057, Revision 1, dated November 17, 2011; as applicable.
units.action_summary: If no unit's serial number is in the Appendix, then before further flight reinstall the stowage box unit per the referenced Boeing instructions, unless a records review already determined the serial number.

units.obligation_text: Unless a records review was done to determine the serial number, before further flight, reinstall the crew oxygen mask stowage box unit.
units.action_summary: If a records review already determined the serial number, the before-flight reinstall requirement does not apply.

units.obligation_text: For airplanes identified in paragraph (g) of this AD: As of May 20, 2013 (the effective date of AD 2013–07–09), no person may install a crew oxygen mask stowage box unit with a serial number listed in the Appendix of Intertechnique Service Bulletin MXP1/4–35–175, Revision 2, dated May 10, 2011, on any airplane.
units.action_summary: As of May 20, 2013, no person may install any crew oxygen mask stowage box unit whose serial number is listed in the Appendix on any airplane identified in paragraph (g).

units.obligation_text: For airplanes other than those identified in paragraph (g) of this AD: Within 24 months after the effective date of this AD, do a general visual inspection to determine if the serial number of the crew oxygen mask stowage box unit is identified in the Appendix of Intertechnique Service Bulletin MXP1/4–35–175, Revision 2, dated May 10, 2011.
units.actor: owners/operators/maintainers of affected airplanes (other than those in paragraph (g))
units.action_summary: Within 24 months after this AD's effective date, perform a general visual inspection to determine whether the stowage box unit serial number is listed in the specified Appendix.

units.obligation_text: A review of airplane maintenance records is acceptable in lieu of this inspection if the serial number of the crew oxygen mask stowage box unit can be conclusively determined from that review.
units.actor: owners/operators/maintainers of affected airplanes (other than those in paragraph (g))
units.action_summary: You may use maintenance records instead of performing the visual inspection if the serial number can be conclusively determined from those records.

units.obligation_text: If any crew oxygen mask stowage box unit has a serial number identified in table 1 of the Appendix of Intertechnique Service Bulletin MXP1/4–35–175, Revision 2, dated May 10, 2011: Before further flight, replace the crew oxygen mask stowage box unit with a new or serviceable unit.
units.actor: owners/operators/maintainers of affected airplanes (other than those in paragraph (g))
units.action_summary: If inspection finds a unit with a table 1 serial number, replace that unit with a new or serviceable unit before the next flight.

units.obligation_text: If any crew oxygen mask stowage box unit’s serial number is unreadable or undetermined, but the manufacturing date can conclusively be determined to be outside the range of July 12, 2007, through November 20, 2007, inclusive, the crew oxygen mask stowage box unit does not need to be replaced.
units.actor: owners/operators/maintainers of affected airplanes (other than those in paragraph (g))
units.action_summary: If the serial number is unreadable but the manufacturing date is conclusively outside the specified range, replacement is not required.

units.obligation_text: If any crew oxygen mask stowage box unit has a serial number identified in table 2 of the Appendix of Intertechnique Service Bulletin MXP1/4–35–175, Revision 2, dated May 10, 2011: Before further flight, add the letter "I" to the end of the serial number (identified as "SER") on the identification label, in accordance with the Accomplishment Instructions of Intertechnique Service Bulletin MXP1/4–35–175, Revision 2, dated May 10, 2011; and reinstall the crew oxygen mask stowage box unit.
units.actor: owners/operators/maintainers of affected airplanes (other than those in paragraph (g))
units.action_summary: If inspection finds a unit with a table 2 serial number, add 'I' to the serial number and reinstall the unit before further flight, following the specified instructions.

units.obligation_text: For airplanes other than those identified in paragraph (g) of this AD: As of the effective date of this AD, no person may install a crew oxygen mask stowage box unit with a serial number identified in table 1 of the Appendix of Intertechnique Service Bulletin MXP1/4–35–175, Revision 2, dated May 10, 2011, on any airplane.
units.action_summary: As of this AD's effective date, nobody may install a stowage box unit with a table 1 serial number on any airplane (other than those in paragraph (g)).

units.obligation_text: For airplanes other than those identified in paragraph (g) of this AD: As of the effective date of this AD, no person may install a crew oxygen mask stowage box unit with a serial number identified in table 2 of the Appendix of Intertechnique Service Bulletin MXP1/4–35–175, Revision 2, dated May 10, 2011, on any airplane, unless that crew oxygen mask stowage box unit has been modified as required by paragraph (i)(2) of this AD.
units.action_summary: As of this AD's effective date, nobody may install a stowage box unit with a table 2 serial number on any airplane unless that unit has been modified per paragraph (i)(2).

units.obligation_text: Installation of a crew oxygen mask stowage box unit with a serial number identified in table 2 is permitted only if that unit has been modified as required by paragraph (i)(2) of this AD.
units.action_summary: The prohibition in (j)(2) does not apply if the unit has been modified per paragraph (i)(2); installation is allowed only in that case.

units.obligation_text: For an affected engine with a combustion outer liner shell that on the effective date of this AD has accumulated 17,500 flight hours (FHs) or greater time since new (TSN), or time since repair (TSR), perform an initial borescope inspection (BSI) or visual inspection of the combustion outer liner shell within 500 engine flight hours (FHs) after the effective date of this AD.
units.action_summary: If engine's outer liner shell has ≥17,500 FHs TSN or TSR on effective date, perform an initial BSI or visual inspection within 500 engine FHs after the AD effective date.

units.obligation_text: For GE CF34–8C engines, inspect using the Accomplishment Instructions, paragraphs 3.A.(4) and 3.A.(5), of GE Alert Service Bulletin (ASB) CF34–8C–AL S/B 72–A0335, dated June 27, 2019.
units.action_summary: Use specified paragraphs of GE ASB CF34–8C–AL S/B 72–A0335 to perform the inspection on CF34–8C engines.

units.obligation_text: For GE CF34–8E engines, inspect using the Accomplishment Instructions, paragraphs 3.A.(4) and 3.A.(5), of GE ASB CF34–8E–AL S/B 72–A0221, dated June 27, 2019.
units.action_summary: Use specified paragraphs of GE ASB CF34–8E–AL S/B 72–A0221 to perform the inspection on CF34–8E engines.

units.obligation_text: For an affected engine with a combustion outer liner shell that on the effective date of this AD has accumulated 17,499 FHs or fewer TSN or TSR, within 500 engine FHs after the combustion outer liner shell has accumulated 17,500 FHs TSN or TSR, perform an initial BSI or visual inspection on the combustion outer liner shell.
units.action_summary: If shell has ≤17,499 FHs on effective date, perform initial BSI or visual inspection within 500 engine FHs after it accumulates 17,500 FHs TSN or TSR.

units.obligation_text: For GE CF34–8C engines, inspect using the Accomplishment Instructions, paragraphs 3.A.(4) and 3.A.(5), of GE ASB CF34–8C–AL S/B 72–A0335, dated June 27, 2019.
units.action_summary: Use specified paragraphs of GE ASB CF34–8C–AL S/B 72–A0335 to perform the inspection for CF34–8C engines when they reach 17,500 FHs.

units.obligation_text: For GE CF34–8E engines, inspect using accomplishment instructions 3.A.(4) and 3.A.(5) of GE ASB CF34–8E–AL S/B 72–A0221, dated June 27, 2019.
units.action_summary: Use specified paragraphs of GE ASB CF34–8E–AL S/B 72–A0221 to perform the inspection for CF34–8E engines when they reach 17,500 FHs.

units.obligation_text: For an affected engine with a combustion outer liner shell for which it is not possible to determine the TSN or TSR, use the engine FHs since new to determine when to perform the BSI or visual inspection.
units.action_summary: If TSN/TSR cannot be determined, use engine flight hours since new to decide when to perform the required inspection.

units.obligation_text: After the effective date of this AD, and after the initial inspection required by paragraph (g)(1) or (2) of this AD, re-inspect the combustion outer liner shell using inspection criteria as follows:
units.action_summary: After the initial inspection, owners/operators must perform repeat inspections using the specified inspection criteria.

units.obligation_text: For GE CF34–8C engines, use Table 1 of GE ASB CF34–8C–AL S/B 72–A0335, dated June 27, 2019.
units.action_summary: Use Table 1 of the referenced GE ASB CF34–8C to determine inspection criteria for re-inspection of CF34–8C engines.

units.obligation_text: For GE CF34–8E engines, use Table 1 of GE ASB CF34–8E–AL S/B 72–A0221, dated June 27, 2019.
units.action_summary: Use Table 1 of the referenced GE ASB CF34–8E to determine inspection criteria for re-inspection of CF34–8E engines.

units.obligation_text: After the effective date of this AD, do not install a combustion outer liner shell with greater than 17,500 FHs TSN or TSR without first inspecting it in accordance with paragraph (g)(1) of this AD.
units.actor: persons installing combustion outer liner shells (owners/operators/maintenance personnel)
units.action_summary: It is prohibited to install a combustion outer liner shell with >17,500 FHs TSN/TSR unless it has first been inspected per paragraph (g)(1).

units.obligation_text: First inspecting it in accordance with paragraph (g)(1) of this AD (as a condition to installation).

units.action_summary: Within 12 months, perform either the actions in (g)(1) or (g)(2).

units.obligation_text: Determine airplane exposure to runway deicing fluids containing potassium formate or potassium acetate by reviewing airport data on the types of components in the deicing fluid used at airports that support airplane operations.
units.actor: Owners/operators of affected airplanes (or their designee)
units.action_summary: Determine whether the airplane has been exposed to deicing fluids containing potassium formate or potassium acetate by reviewing airport deicing-fluid component data.

units.obligation_text: If the airplane has not been exposed: Repeat the requirements specified in paragraph (g)(1) of this AD thereafter at intervals not to exceed 24 months.
units.action_summary: If not exposed, repeat the exposure-determination every 24 months at most.

units.obligation_text: If the airplane has been exposed: Within 90 days after that determination is made, do the inspection required by paragraph (g)(2) of this AD.
units.action_summary: If exposed, perform the inspection required in (g)(2) within 90 days of determining exposure.

units.obligation_text: Repeat the inspection thereafter at intervals not to exceed 24 months.
units.action_summary: After the initial inspection for exposed airplanes, repeat that inspection every 24 months at most.

units.obligation_text: Do a detailed inspection of the electrical connectors, including the contacts and backshells of the line replaceable unit (LRU) in the wheel well of the MLG, for corrosion in accordance with the Accomplishment Instructions of Boeing Alert Service Bulletin 737–24A1148, Revision 1, dated July 10, 2003. Perform applicable corrective actions at the applicable times, as specified in paragraphs (g)(2)(i) through (iii) of this AD, in accordance with the Accomplishment Instructions of Boeing Alert Service Bulletin 737–24A1148, Revision 1, dated July 10, 2003. Repeat the inspection thereafter at intervals not to exceed 24 months.
units.action_summary: Perform a detailed inspection of specified MLG wheel well electrical connectors for corrosion per the Boeing service bulletin, do required corrective actions as specified, and repeat the inspection every 24 months at most.

units.obligation_text: If the total backshell surface area corrosion is 10 percent or less, clean the backshell(s) before further flight.
units.action_summary: If backshell corrosion is ≤10%, clean the backshell(s) before the airplane's next flight.

units.obligation_text: If the total backshell surface area corrosion is greater than 10 percent but less than 20 percent, replace the connectors and backshells within 30 days after the detailed inspection.
units.action_summary: If backshell corrosion is >10% and <20%, replace connectors and backshells within 30 days after the inspection.

units.obligation_text: If the total backshell surface area corrosion is 20 percent or more, replace the connectors and backshells before further flight.
units.action_summary: If backshell corrosion is ≥20%, replace connectors and backshells before the airplane's next flight.

units.obligation_text: Unless that part has a circled letter "G" stamped ... indicating that the cargo fire extinguisher halon bottle has been tested and refilled.

units.obligation_text: For AWL No. 28–AWL–24, 'Spar Valve Motor Operated Valve (MOV) Actuator-Lightning and Fault Current Protection Electrical Bond:' Within 72 months after accomplishment of the actions specified in Boeing Service Bulletin 737–28A1207, or within 72 months after the most recent inspection was performed as specified in AWL No. 28–AWL–24, whichever is later.

units.action_summary: For L/N 1–1754, perform the specified service bulletin actions within 120 months.

units.obligation_text: For airplanes having L/N 1755 and subsequent, within 120 months after the date of issuance of the original airworthiness certificate or the original export certificate of airworthiness, or within 48 months after the effective date of this AD, whichever is later.
units.actor: Owners/operators of airplanes L/N 1755 and subsequent
units.action_summary: For L/N 1755 and subsequent, comply within 120 months of certification or within 48 months after the AD effective date, whichever is later.

units.obligation_text: For AWL No. 28–AWL–35, 'Fuel Quantity Indicating System (FQIS)—Center Fuel Tank In-Tank Component and Wire Harness Protection Features—Separation from Center Tank Internal Structure:' For airplanes that have incorporated Boeing Service Bulletin 737–28–1356, within 120 months after accomplishment of the actions specified in Boeing Service Bulletin 737–28–1356, or within 120 months after the most recent inspection was performed as specified in AWL No. 28–AWL–35, whichever is later.
units.action_summary: Perform AWL No. 28–AWL–35 actions within 120 months after the service bulletin or the most recent inspection, whichever is later, for airplanes that have incorporated the service bulletin.

units.obligation_text: For AWL No. 28–AWL–37, 'Fuel Quantity Indicating System (FQIS)—Built in Test Equipment (BITE) Test:' For airplane L/Ns 6987 and 7000 and subsequent, within 750 flight hours since the date the most recent BITE test was accomplished as specified in AWL No. 28–AWL–37, or within 750 flight hours after the effective date of this AD, whichever is later.

units.action_summary: For specified line numbers, perform the BITE test within 750 flight hours since the most recent BITE test or within 750 flight hours after the AD effective date, whichever is later.

units.obligation_text: For AWL No. 47–AWL–04, 'Nitrogen Generation System-Thermal Switch:' Within 22,500 flight hours after the date of issuance of the original airworthiness certificate or the original export certificate of airworthiness, within 22,500 flight hours after accomplishment of the actions specified in Boeing Service Bulletin 737–47–1003, or within 22,500 flight hours after the most recent inspection was performed as specified in AWL No. 47–AWL–04, whichever is latest.
units.action_summary: Perform AWL No. 47–AWL–04 actions within 22,500 flight hours after certification, service bulletin actions, or the most recent inspection, whichever is latest.

units.obligation_text: For AWL No. 47–AWL–06, 'Nitrogen Generation System (NGS)-Cross Vent Check Valve:' Within 13,000 flight hours after the date of issuance of the original airworthiness certificate or the original export certificate of airworthiness, within 13,000 flight hours after accomplishment of the actions specified in Boeing Service Bulletin 737–47–1003, or within 13,000 flight hours after the most recent inspection was performed as specified in AWL No. 47–AWL–06, whichever is latest.
units.action_summary: Perform AWL No. 47–AWL–06 actions within 13,000 flight hours after certification, service bulletin actions, or the most recent inspection, whichever is latest.

units.obligation_text: For AWL No. 47–AWL–07, 'Nitrogen Generation System (NGS)-Nitrogen Enriched Air (NEA) Distribution Ducting Integrity:' Within 6,500 flight hours after the date of issuance of the original airworthiness certificate or the original export certificate of airworthiness, within 6,500 flight hours after accomplishment of the actions specified in Boeing Service Bulletin 737–47–1003, or within 6,500 flight hours after the most recent inspection was performed as specified in AWL No. 47–AWL–07, whichever is latest.
units.action_summary: Perform AWL No. 47–AWL–07 actions within 6,500 flight hours after certification, service bulletin actions, or the most recent inspection, whichever is latest.

units.obligation_text: For AWL No. 47–AWL–09, 'Nitrogen Generation System—Oxygen Sensor:' Within 18,000 flight hours after the date of issuance of the original airworthiness certificate or the original export certificate of airworthiness, or within 18,000 flight hours after the most recent replacement was performed as specified in AWL No. 47–AWL–09, or within 12 months after the effective date of this AD, whichever is latest.
units.action_summary: Replace or perform AWL No. 47–AWL–09 actions within the specified flight-hour or time thresholds, whichever is latest.

units.obligation_text: For AWL No. 28–AWL–101, 'Engine Fuel Suction Feed Operational Test:' Within 7,500 flight hours or 36 months, whichever occurs first, after the date of issuance of the original airworthiness certificate or the original export certificate of airworthiness; or within 7,500 flight hours or 36 months, whichever occurs first, after the most recent inspection was performed as specified in AWL No. 28–AWL–101; whichever is later.
units.action_summary: Perform AWL No. 28–AWL–101 operational test within 7,500 flight hours or 36 months (whichever is first) after certification or after the most recent inspection, whichever is later.

units.obligation_text: The FAA must receive comments by June 15, 2020.

units.obligation_text: Comply with this AD within the compliance times specified, unless already done.
units.actor: Operators/owners/maintenance organizations subject to this AD
units.action_summary: Affected parties must comply with the AD within the specified compliance times unless already completed.

units.section: (h) Identification of Affected Cylinder and Valve Assemblies
units.obligation_text: Within 60 days after the effective date of this AD, inspect the oxygen valve assemblies, and oxygen cylinder and valve assemblies, to determine if the serial number of the valve, cylinder, and entire assembly, is listed in Appendix 1, 'Affected Shipments,' of the applicable service information identified in paragraph(s) (h)(1) through (3) of this AD.
units.action_summary: Within 60 days of the AD effective date, inspect assemblies or review records to determine if serial numbers match Appendix 1.

units.section: (h) Identification of Affected Cylinder and Valve Assemblies (alternative)
units.obligation_text: A review of airplane maintenance records is acceptable in lieu of this inspection if the serial numbers can be conclusively determined from that review.
units.action_summary: Allowed to use maintenance record review instead of physical inspection if serial numbers can be conclusively determined.

units.section: (i) Inspection of the Gap, Parts Marking Actions, and Replacement
units.obligation_text: If, during any inspection or records review required by paragraph (h) of this AD, any oxygen valve assembly, valve or cylinder of an oxygen cylinder and valve assembly, or oxygen cylinder and valve assembly having an affected serial number is found: Before further flight, do a detailed inspection for correct spacing of the gap between the bottom of the packing retainer and top of the valve body, in accordance with paragraph 3.C. of the Accomplishment Instructions of the applicable service information identified in paragraphs (h)(1) through (3) of this AD.
units.action_summary: If an assembly with an affected serial number is found, perform a detailed gap-spacing inspection before further flight per the referenced service instructions.

units.obligation_text: If the gap is found to be acceptable, before further flight, do the parts marking actions in accordance with paragraph 3.D.(1) of the Accomplishment Instructions of the applicable service information identified in paragraph(s) (h)(1) through (3) of this AD.
units.action_summary: If the gap is acceptable, perform the specified parts marking actions before further flight per the service instructions.

units.obligation_text: If the gap is found to be unacceptable, as defined in the applicable service information identified in paragraphs (h)(1) through (3) of this AD, before further flight, remove the affected assembly, in accordance with paragraphs 3.D.(2) or 3.D.(3), as applicable, of the Accomplishment Instructions of the applicable service information identified in paragraphs (h)(1) through (3) of this AD;
units.action_summary: If the gap is unacceptable, remove the affected assembly before further flight following the referenced service procedures.

units.obligation_text: and replace with a serviceable assembly.
units.action_summary: After removal for unacceptable gap, replace the assembly with a serviceable assembly before further flight.

units.obligation_text: Report the results of the inspection required by paragraph (i) of this AD within the applicable time specified in paragraph (j)(1)(i) or (ii) of this AD. Report the results in accordance with paragraph 3.D.(1)(a), of the Accomplishment instructions of the applicable service information identified in paragraphs (h)(1) through (3) of this AD.
units.actor: Operators/maintenance personnel who performed the inspection
units.action_summary: Report inspection results per the referenced accomplishment instructions within the applicable timeframe.

units.obligation_text: If the inspection was done on or after the effective date of this AD: Submit the report within 30 days after the inspection.
units.actor: Operators/maintenance personnel who performed the inspection
units.action_summary: If inspection occurs on/after AD effective date, submit report within 30 days after inspection.

units.obligation_text: If the inspection was done before the effective date of this AD: Submit the report within 30 days after the effective date of this AD.
units.actor: Operators/maintenance personnel who performed the inspection
units.action_summary: If inspection occurred before the AD effective date, submit report within 30 days after the AD effective date.

units.obligation_text: If, during an inspection required by paragraph (i) of this AD, any gap is found to be unacceptable, within the applicable time specified in paragraph (j)(2)(i) or (ii) of this AD, return the assembly to the manufacturer in accordance with paragraph 3.D.(2) or 3.D.(3), as applicable, of the Accomplishment Instructions of the applicable service information identified in paragraphs (h)(1) through (3) of this AD.
units.action_summary: If an unacceptable gap is found, return the assembly to the manufacturer within the applicable time and per referenced instructions.

units.obligation_text: If the inspection was done on or after the effective date of this AD: Return the assembly within 30 days after the inspection.
units.action_summary: If inspection on/after effective date finds unacceptable gap, return assembly within 30 days after inspection.

units.obligation_text: If the inspection was done before the effective date of this AD: Return the assembly within 30 days after the effective date of this AD.
units.action_summary: If inspection before effective date found unacceptable gap, return assembly within 30 days after the AD effective date.

units.action_summary: Prohibits installation of affected assemblies on any airplane unless paragraph (i) requirements have been completed on that assembly.

units.obligation_text: This paragraph provides credit for the actions specified in paragraphs (h) or (i) of this AD, if those actions were performed before the effective date of this AD using the service information specified in paragraphs (l)(1) through (5) of this AD.

units.obligation_text: This AD applies to all Pratt & Whitney (PW) PW2037, PW2037M, PW2040, and F117–PW–100 model turbofan engines.
units.actor: owners and operators of Pratt & Whitney PW2037, PW2037M, PW2040, and F117–PW–100 model turbofan engines
units.action_summary: The AD's requirements are applicable to those specified engines.

units.obligation_text: Comply with this AD within the compliance times specified, unless already done.
units.actor: owners and operators of affected engines
units.action_summary: Comply with the AD within the specified compliance times unless the action has already been accomplished.

units.obligation_text: For PW PW2037, PW2037M, and PW2040 model turbofan engines with an HPT 2nd-stage air seal assembly, part number (P/N) 1A8209 or 1A8209–001, installed, and with any of the following: An engine with serial number 716301 to 716600, inclusive; 717901 to 717999, inclusive; 718000; 726501 to 727132, inclusive; or 727135 to 727143, inclusive; or an engine that has operated with electronic engine control model number EEC104–1 since the last HPT overhaul: [perform Borescope Inspection as required in paragraphs (g)(1)(i)-(iii)].
units.actor: owners and operators of the specified PW2037, PW2037M, and PW2040 engines meeting the part number/serial/EEC criteria
units.action_summary: For specified engines with P/N 1A8209 or 1A8209–001 and listed serials or EEC104–1 usage, perform borescope inspections of the HPT 2nd-stage air seal assembly as required by subparagraphs (i)-(iii).

units.obligation_text: Within 2,500 flight cycles (FCs) since the last HPT 2nd stage air seal assembly installation or 500 FCs after the effective date of this AD, whichever occurs later, perform an initial BSI of the HPT 2nd-stage air seal assembly using the Accomplishment Instructions, paragraph 6, of PW Service Bulletin (SB) PW2000 72–773, dated March 11, 2020.
units.actor: owners and operators of the specified PW2037, PW2037M, and PW2040 engines (as described in § 39.13(g)(1))
units.action_summary: Perform an initial borescope inspection within 2,500 FCs since installation or within 500 FCs after the AD effective date (whichever is later) using the specified service bulletin instructions.

units.obligation_text: Thereafter, perform the BSI required by paragraph (g)(1)(i) of this AD within every 500 FCs since performance of the last BSI.
units.actor: owners and operators of the specified PW2037, PW2037M, and PW2040 engines (as described in § 39.13(g)(1))
units.action_summary: After the initial BSI, repeat the borescope inspection every 500 flight cycles.

units.obligation_text: If, during any BSI required by paragraphs (g)(1)(i) or (ii) of this AD, a cracked seal is found, before further flight, remove the HPT 2nd-stage air seal assembly from the engine and perform additional inspections of the HPT 2nd-stage air seal assembly using paragraph (g)(2) of this AD.
units.actor: owners and operators of the specified PW2037, PW2037M, and PW2040 engines (as described in § 39.13(g)(1))
units.action_summary: If a cracked seal is found during any required BSI, remove the HPT 2nd-stage air seal assembly before further flight and perform additional inspections per paragraph (g)(2).

units.obligation_text: For PW PW2037, PW2037M, PW2040, and F117–PW–100 model turbofan engines, after the effective date of this AD, at every piece part opportunity of the HPT 1st-stage disk, HPT 2nd-stage disk, or the HPT 2nd-stage air seal assembly: [perform actions in paragraphs (g)(2)(i)-(iii)].
units.actor: owners and operators of PW PW2037, PW2037M, PW2040, and F117–PW–100 engines
units.action_summary: At every piece-part opportunity for specified HPT components after the AD effective date, perform the inspections and related actions required in paragraphs (g)(2)(i)-(iii).

units.obligation_text: Perform a visual inspection of the HPT 2nd-stage air seal assembly, strip the knife edge coating from the HPT 2nd-stage air seal assembly, and then perform an FPI of the HPT 2nd-stage air seal assembly.
units.actor: owners and operators performing work at every piece-part opportunity
units.action_summary: At each piece-part opportunity, visually inspect the HPT 2nd-stage air seal, remove the knife-edge coating, and perform a fluorescent penetrant inspection.

units.obligation_text: If a crack is found in the HPT 2nd-stage air seal assembly during the visual inspection or FPI required by paragraph (g)(2)(i) of this AD, before further flight, remove the HPT 2nd-stage air seal assembly from service and replace it with a part eligible for installation.
units.action_summary: If an inspection reveals a crack, remove the HPT 2nd-stage air seal assembly before further flight and replace it with a part eligible for installation.

units.obligation_text: If a through-crack is found in the forward edge or aft edge of the HPT 2nd-stage air seal assembly during the visual inspection or FPI required by paragraph (g)(2)(i) of this AD, before further flight, remove the HPT 2nd-stage air seal assembly, mating HPT 1st-stage disk, and HPT 2nd-stage hub from service, and replace the parts with parts eligible for installation.
units.action_summary: If a through-crack is found at the forward or aft edge, remove the air seal assembly and the mating HPT 1st-stage disk and HPT 2nd-stage hub before further flight and replace them with eligible parts.

units.obligation_text: In order to return the mating HPT 1st-stage disk and HPT 2nd-stage hub to service, the inspections of the HPT 2nd-stage air seal assembly cannot reveal a through-crack.
units.action_summary: You may not return the mating HPT 1st-stage disk and HPT 2nd-stage hub to service if inspections of the HPT 2nd-stage air seal assembly reveal a through-crack.

units.obligation_text: Replacement of HPT 2nd-Stage Air Seal Assembly: [see paragraphs (g)(3)(i) and (ii)].
units.actor: owners and operators of affected engines
units.action_summary: Replace the P/N 1A8209 or 1A8209–001 HPT 2nd-stage air seal assembly with a part eligible for installation as required in the following subparagraphs.

units.obligation_text: For PW PW2037, PW2037M, and PW2040 model turbofan engines, at the next engine shop visit after the effective date of this AD, remove the HPT 2nd-stage air seal assembly, P/N 1A8209 or 1A8209–001, and replace it with a part eligible for installation.
units.actor: owners and operators of PW PW2037, PW2037M, and PW2040 engines
units.action_summary: At the next engine shop visit after the AD effective date, remove P/N 1A8209 or 1A8209–001 and replace it with a part eligible for installation.

units.obligation_text: For PW F117–PW–100 model turbofan engines, at the next piece part opportunity after the effective date of this AD, remove the HPT 2nd-stage air seal assembly, P/N 1A8209 or 1A8209–001, and replace it with a part eligible for installation.
units.actor: owners and operators of PW F117–PW–100 engines
units.action_summary: At the next piece-part opportunity after the AD effective date, remove P/N 1A8209 or 1A8209–001 and replace it with a part eligible for installation.

units.obligation_text: Removal of the HPT 2nd-stage air seal assembly, P/N 1A8209 or 1A8209–001, and its replacement with a part eligible for installation as required by paragraph (g)(3) of this AD is a terminating action for the repetitive BSI requirements in paragraph (g)(1)(ii) of this AD.
units.actor: owners and operators of affected engines
units.action_summary: Replacing the P/N 1A8209 or 1A8209–001 air seal assembly with an eligible part as required in (g)(3) terminates the repetitive borescope inspection requirement of (g)(1)(ii).

units.obligation_text: The Manager, ECO Branch, FAA, has the authority to approve AMOCs for this AD, if requested using the procedures found in 14 CFR 39.19.
units.action_summary: The Manager may approve alternative methods of compliance (AMOCs) for this AD if requested under the referenced procedures.

units.obligation_text: In accordance with 14 CFR 39.19, send your request to your principal inspector or local Flight Standards District Office, as appropriate.
units.action_summary: Send AMOC requests to your principal inspector or local Flight Standards District Office per 14 CFR 39.19.

units.obligation_text: If sending information directly to the manager of the certification office, send it to the attention of the person identified in paragraph (k)(1) of this AD.

units.action_summary: If sending information directly to the certification office manager, address it to the person identified in paragraph (k)(1).

units.obligation_text: You may email your request to: ANE-AD-AMOC@faa.gov.
units.action_summary: Requesters may submit AMOC requests via the specified email address.

units.obligation_text: Before using any approved AMOC, notify your appropriate principal inspector, or lacking a principal inspector, the manager of the local flight standards district office/certificate holding district office.
units.actor: owners and operators intending to use an approved AMOC
units.action_summary: Before using an approved AMOC, notify your principal inspector or, if none, the manager of the local FSDO/CHDO.

title: Airworthiness Directives: Textron Aviation Inc. Airplanes

units.obligation_text: The FAA must receive comments by June 29, 2020.
units.action_summary: Submit comments so the FAA receives them by June 29, 2020.

units.obligation_text: Comply with this AD within the compliance times specified, unless already done.
units.actor: Owners/operators of the affected airplanes (persons subject to this AD)
units.action_summary: Comply with all requirements of this AD within the specified compliance times unless already accomplished.

units.obligation_text: Within the next 100 hours time-in-service (TIS) after the effective date of this AD or within the next 12 months after the effective date of this AD, whichever occurs later, and thereafter every 500 hours TIS or 5 years, whichever occurs first, visually inspect each stabilizer hinge bracket, tailcone reinforcement angle, corner reinforcement, stabilizer hinge reinforcement channel, stabilizer hinge assembly, stabilizer aft spar reinforcement, and the lower half of the stabilizer aft spar from station (STA) 16 on the left side to STA 16 on the right side for corrosion and cracks; remove any corrosion; and replace any part with a crack by following the Accomplishment Instructions, paragraphs 9 through 11 and 13, of Textron Aviation Single Engine Mandatory Service Letter SEL–55–01, dated December 7, 2017.
units.actor: Owners/operators/maintenance personnel of the affected airplanes
units.action_summary: Perform the required visual inspections of the listed stabilizer/tailcone structure within the initial compliance time and at specified recurring intervals; remove corrosion and replace cracked parts following the specified service instructions.

units.obligation_text: Within the next 100 hours time-in-service (TIS) after the effective date of this AD or within the next 12 months after the effective date of this AD, whichever occurs later ... visually inspect ...
units.actor: Owners/operators/maintenance personnel of the affected airplanes
units.action_summary: Initial inspection must be done within 100 hours TIS or 12 months after the AD's effective date, whichever occurs later.

units.obligation_text: and thereafter every 500 hours TIS or 5 years, whichever occurs first, visually inspect ...
units.actor: Owners/operators/maintenance personnel of the affected airplanes
units.action_summary: Perform recurring inspections every 500 hours TIS or every 5 years, whichever occurs first.

units.obligation_text: Visually inspect each stabilizer hinge bracket, tailcone reinforcement angle, corner reinforcement, stabilizer hinge reinforcement channel, stabilizer hinge assembly, stabilizer aft spar reinforcement, and the lower half of the stabilizer aft spar from station (STA) 16 on the left side to STA 16 on the right side for corrosion and cracks;
units.actor: Owners/operators/maintenance personnel of the affected airplanes
units.action_summary: Inspect the listed stabilizer and tailcone components for corrosion and cracks.

units.obligation_text: remove any corrosion;
units.actor: Owners/operators/maintenance personnel of the affected airplanes
units.action_summary: Remove any corrosion found during inspections.

units.obligation_text: replace any part with a crack by following the Accomplishment Instructions, paragraphs 9 through 11 and 13, of Textron Aviation Single Engine Mandatory Service Letter SEL–55–01, dated December 7, 2017.
units.actor: Owners/operators/maintenance personnel of the affected airplanes
units.action_summary: Replace any cracked part and do so following the specified paragraphs of the referenced service letter.

units.obligation_text: Also inspect for loose rivets and sheared rivets.
units.actor: Owners/operators/maintenance personnel of the affected airplanes
units.action_summary: Inspect for loose and sheared rivets as part of the inspection.

units.obligation_text: If there is a loose or sheared rivet, before further flight, replace the rivet.
units.actor: Owners/operators/maintenance personnel of the affected airplanes
units.action_summary: If a loose or sheared rivet is found, replace it before the airplane next flies.

units.obligation_text: Actions accomplished before the effective date of this AD within the previous 5 years or 500 hours TIS, whichever was the most recent, in accordance with the procedures specified in the documents listed in paragraphs (h)(i) through (viii) of this AD as applicable to your airplane are considered acceptable for compliance with the corresponding actions in paragraph (g) of this AD.
units.actor: Owners/operators who performed the listed actions prior to the effective date
units.action_summary: Earlier actions meeting the listed criteria may be credited as compliance with the corresponding paragraph (g) actions.

units.obligation_text: The time between any inspection for which credit is allowed by this paragraph and the next inspection accomplished in accordance with paragraph (g) of this AD must not exceed 500 hours TIS or 5 years, whichever occurs first.
units.action_summary: The interval between a credited inspection and the next required inspection may not exceed 500 hours TIS or 5 years.

title: Airworthiness Directives: General Electric Company Turbofan Engines

units.obligation_text: The FAA must receive comments on this AD action by July 23, 2020.
units.action_summary: Receive comments on this AD action by July 23, 2020.

units.obligation_text: This AD applies to General Electric Company (GE) CF6–80A, CF6–80A1, CF6–80A2, CF6–80A3, CF6–80C2A1, CF6–80C2A2, CF6–80C2A3, CF6–80C2A5, CF6–80C2A5F, CF6–80C2A8, CF6–80C2B1, CF6–80C2B1F, CF6–80C2B2, CF6–80C2B2F, CF6–80C2B4, CF6–80C2B4F, CF6–80C2B5F, CF6–80C2B6, CF6–80C2B6F, CF6–80C2B6FA, CF6–80C2B7F, CF6–80C2D1F, CF6–80C2L1F, and CF6–80C2K1F model turbofan engines with high-pressure turbine (HPT) disks with serial numbers listed in Tables 1 and 2 of Appendix A in GE CF6–80C2 Service Bulletin (SB) 72–1562 R04, dated May 29, 2019; and Table 1 of Appendix A in GE CF6–80A SB 72–0869 R02, dated May 29, 2019.
units.actor: This AD / owners/operators of specified engines
units.action_summary: Specifies which GE CF6 model turbofan engines (by model and HPT disk serial number lists in specified service bulletins) are covered by this AD.

units.obligation_text: Comply with this AD within the compliance times specified, unless already done.
units.actor: Owners/operators of affected engines (persons subject to this AD)

units.obligation_text: After the effective date of this AD, perform an ultrasonic inspection for cracks in HPT stage 1 and 2 disks on the CF6–80C2 turbofan engine at each piece-part exposure using the Accomplishment Instructions, paragraph 3.A.(2), in GE CF6–80C2 SB 72–1562 R04, dated May 29, 2019.
units.actor: Owners/operators/maintenance personnel of affected CF6–80C2 engines
units.action_summary: Perform ultrasonic inspection for cracks in HPT stage 1 and 2 disks at each piece-part exposure using specified service bulletin instructions.

units.obligation_text: After the effective date of this AD, perform an ultrasonic inspection for cracks in HPT stage 2 disks on the CF6–80A turbofan engine at each piece-part exposure using the Accomplishment Instructions, paragraph 3.A.(2), in GE CF6–80A SB 72–0869 R02, dated May 29, 2019.
units.actor: Owners/operators/maintenance personnel of affected CF6–80A engines
units.action_summary: Perform ultrasonic inspection for cracks in HPT stage 2 disks at each piece-part exposure using specified service bulletin instructions.

units.obligation_text: If any disk fails the inspection required by paragraphs (g)(1) and (2) of this AD, replace the disk before further flight.
units.action_summary: Replace any disk that fails the required inspection before further flight.

units.obligation_text: The reporting requirements specified in the Accomplishment Instructions, paragraphs 3.A.(2)(c) and 3.A.(2)(f), of CF6–80C2 SB 72–1562 R04, dated May 29, 2019, are not required by this AD.
units.actor: Owners/operators/other persons subject to the AD (with respect to those reporting requirements)
units.action_summary: Specifies that certain reporting requirements in the referenced service bulletin are not required by this AD.

title: Airworthiness Directives: The Boeing Company Airplanes

units.obligation_text: The FAA must receive comments on this AD action by August 31, 2020.
units.action_summary: Receive comments on this AD by August 31, 2020.

units.obligation_text: Comply with this AD within the compliance times specified, unless already done.
units.action_summary: Comply with the AD within the specified compliance times unless already accomplished.

units.obligation_text: Within 14 days after February 22, 2019 (the effective date of AD 2019–02–03), revise the existing maintenance or inspection program, as applicable, to add airworthiness limitation 28–AWL–FIRE, by incorporating the information specified in figure 1 to paragraph (g) of this AD into the Airworthiness Limitations Section of the Instructions for Continued Airworthiness.
units.action_summary: Revise the maintenance/inspection program within 14 days after Feb 22, 2019 to add AWL 28–AWL–FIRE by incorporating figure 1 into the Airworthiness Limitations Section.

units.obligation_text: The initial compliance time for accomplishing the actions specified in figure 1 to paragraph (g) of this AD is within 45 days after February 22, 2019.
units.action_summary: Initial compliance time for the actions in figure 1 is within 45 days after Feb 22, 2019.

units.obligation_text: Except as required by paragraph (k) of this AD: After accomplishment of the existing maintenance or inspection program revision required by paragraph (g) of this AD, no alternative actions (e.g., inspections) or intervals may be used unless the actions or intervals are approved as an alternative method of compliance (AMOC) in accordance with the procedures specified in paragraph (o) of this AD.
units.action_summary: After accomplishing the program revision required by paragraph (g), operators may not use alternative actions or intervals unless approved as an AMOC per paragraph (o), except as required by paragraph (k).

units.obligation_text: Alternative actions or intervals may be used if the actions or intervals are approved as an alternative method of compliance (AMOC) in accordance with the procedures specified in paragraph (o) of this AD.
units.action_summary: Alternative actions/intervals are permitted only if approved as an AMOC according to paragraph (o).

units.obligation_text: For the airplanes identified in Boeing Requirements Bulletin B787–81205–SB260008–00 RB, Issue 001, dated March 10, 2020: At the applicable times specified in the "Compliance" paragraph of Boeing Requirements Bulletin B787–81205–SB260008–00 RB, Issue 001, dated March 10, 2020, except as specified by paragraph (j) of this AD, do all applicable actions identified in, and in accordance with, the Accomplishment Instructions of Boeing Requirements Bulletin B787–81205–SB260008–00 RB, Issue 001, dated March 10, 2020.
units.action_summary: Perform all applicable actions in the Boeing Requirements Bulletin at the times specified, in accordance with the Accomplishment Instructions, except as provided in paragraph (j).

units.obligation_text: At the applicable times specified in the "Compliance" paragraph of Boeing Requirements Bulletin B787–81205–SB260008–00 RB, Issue 001, dated March 10, 2020, ... do all applicable actions identified in, and in accordance with, the Accomplishment Instructions of Boeing Requirements Bulletin B787–81205–SB260008–00 RB, Issue 001, dated March 10, 2020.
units.action_summary: Perform the bulletin's actions at the applicable times specified in its Compliance paragraph.

units.obligation_text: Except as specified by paragraph (j) of this AD, do all applicable actions identified in, and in accordance with, the Accomplishment Instructions of Boeing Requirements Bulletin ...
units.action_summary: The required actions in the Boeing Requirements Bulletin must be done unless paragraph (j) provides an exception.

units.obligation_text: Where Boeing Requirements Bulletin B787–81205–SB260008–00 RB, Issue 001, dated March 10, 2020, uses the phrase "the issue 001 date of Requirements Bulletin B787–81205–SB260008–00 RB," this AD requires using "the effective date of this AD."
units.actor: owners/operators of affected airplanes (when following the Requirements Bulletin as required by this AD)
units.action_summary: When the Requirements Bulletin refers to its issue date phrase, use the effective date of this AD instead.

units.obligation_text: Prior to or concurrently with the actions specified in paragraph (i) of this AD, or within 30 days after the effective date of the AD, whichever occurs later: Revise the existing maintenance or inspection program, as applicable, by incorporating the information specified in figure 2 to paragraph (k) of this AD into the Airworthiness Limitations Section of the Instructions for Continued Airworthiness.
units.action_summary: Revise the maintenance/inspection program by incorporating figure 2 into the Airworthiness Limitations Section prior to/concurrently with paragraph (i) actions or within 30 days after the effective date, whichever is later.

units.obligation_text: Prior to or concurrently with the actions specified in paragraph (i) of this AD, or within 30 days after the effective date of the AD, whichever occurs later:
units.action_summary: Timing requirement for when to revise the maintenance/inspection program (prior to/concurrently with paragraph (i) actions or within 30 days after the AD effective date, whichever is later).

units.obligation_text: It is acceptable to change the limitation number from 28–AWL–FIRE to 26–AWL–FIRE, provided the rest of the information in figure 2 to paragraph (k) of this AD remains unchanged.
units.action_summary: Operators may change the limitation number from 28–AWL–FIRE to 26–AWL–FIRE provided the rest of the figure 2 information remains unchanged.

units.obligation_text: The initial compliance time for accomplishing the actions specified in figure 2 to paragraph (k) of this AD is within 30 days after accomplishing the last 28–AWL–FIRE or 26–AWL–FIRE task, as applicable.
units.action_summary: Initial compliance time for figure 2 actions is within 30 days after completing the last specified AWL task.

units.obligation_text: Accomplishing the revision required by this paragraph terminates the actions required by paragraph (g) of this AD.
units.action_summary: Completing the revision required by paragraph (k) ends the obligations imposed by paragraph (g).

units.obligation_text: After accomplishment of the existing maintenance or inspection program revision required by paragraph (k) of this AD, no alternative actions (e.g., inspections) or intervals may be used unless the actions or intervals are approved as an AMOC in accordance with the procedures specified in paragraph (o) of this AD.
units.action_summary: After the paragraph (k) program revision is accomplished, operators may not use alternative actions or intervals unless approved as an AMOC per paragraph (o).

units.obligation_text: Alternative actions or intervals may be used if the actions or intervals are approved as an AMOC in accordance with the procedures specified in paragraph (o) of this AD.
units.action_summary: Alternative actions/intervals are permitted only if approved as an AMOC according to paragraph (o).

units.obligation_text: Accomplishment of the actions required by paragraph (i) of this AD on all affected airplanes in an operator’s fleet terminates the requirements of paragraph (k) of this AD.
units.action_summary: If an operator accomplishes paragraph (i) actions on all affected airplanes in the fleet, the requirements of paragraph (k) are terminated.

units.obligation_text: As of the effective date of this AD, no person may install on any airplane any engine fire control panel having part number (P/N) 412600–001, or any engine fire shutoff switch having P/N 417000–101 or P/N 417000–102.
units.action_summary: Prohibits installation, as of the AD effective date, of specified engine fire control panel and engine fire shutoff switch part numbers on any airplane.
