units.action_summary: For an AMOC to be approved, the repair/modification/alteration deviation must meet the airplane's certification basis and the approval must explicitly reference this AD.

title: Airworthiness Directives: General Electric Company Turbofan Engines

units.obligation_text: The FAA must receive comments on this SNPRM November 9, 2020.
units.actor: commenters / the public (to submit comments to FAA)
units.action_summary: Submit comments to the FAA by November 9, 2020.

units.obligation_text: You are responsible for performing each action required by this AD within the specified compliance time unless it has already been accomplished prior to that time.
units.action_summary: Perform each action required by this AD within the specified compliance times unless already done.

units.obligation_text: Within 6 months, inspect the buckle handle for a crack.
units.action_summary: Inspect the buckle handle for cracks within 6 months.

units.obligation_text: If the buckle handle is cracked, before further flight, remove the buckle as depicted in Figure 5 and by following the Procedures, paragraph 9, of SB 25–1111432, and replace it with an airworthy buckle.
units.action_summary: If inspection finds a crack, remove and replace the cracked buckle before next flight according to the service bulletin.

units.obligation_text: You are not required to return the removed buckle to Pacific Scientific.
units.action_summary: You may remove and replace the buckle without returning the removed part to Pacific Scientific.

units.obligation_text: Within 12 months, measure the thickness of the buckle handle vane as depicted in Figure 3 of SB 25–1111432.
units.action_summary: Measure the buckle handle vane thickness within 12 months.

units.obligation_text: If the handle vane thickness is 0.125 inch or greater, before further flight, remove the buckle from service and replace it with an airworthy buckle.
units.action_summary: If thickness ≥ 0.125 inch, remove and replace the buckle before next flight.

units.obligation_text: As of the effective date of this AD, do not install a buckle or a restraint system with a buckle, P/N 1111430 or 1111475, all dash numbers, with a handle vane thickness of 0.125 inch or greater on any airplane or helicopter.
units.action_summary: Do not install specified buckles with handle vane thickness ≥ 0.125 inch on any aircraft.

units.obligation_text: The Manager, International Validation Branch, FAA, may approve AMOCs for this AD.
units.actor: The Manager, International Validation Branch, FAA
units.action_summary: The Manager may approve alternative methods of compliance for this AD.

units.obligation_text: Send your proposal to: Kristi Bradley, Aviation Safety Engineer, International Validation Branch, General Aviation and Rotorcraft Unit, FAA, 10101 Hillwood Pkwy., Fort Worth, TX 76177; telephone 817–222–5110; email kristin.bradley@faa.gov.
units.action_summary: Send AMOC proposals to the named FAA contact.

units.obligation_text: For operations conducted under a 14 CFR part 119 operating certificate or under 14 CFR part 91, subpart K, the FAA suggests that you notify your principal inspector, or lacking a principal inspector, the manager of the local flight standards district office or certificate holding district office, before operating any aircraft complying with this AD through an AMOC.
units.actor: you (operators conducting operations under part 119 or part 91, subpart K)
units.action_summary: Notify your principal inspector or local FSDO manager before operating an aircraft under this AD using an approved AMOC.

units.obligation_text: The FAA must receive comments by November 9, 2020.
units.actor: commenters / the public (to submit comments to FAA)
units.action_summary: Submit comments to the FAA by November 9, 2020.

units.obligation_text: Comply with this AD within the compliance times specified, unless already done.
units.action_summary: Comply with all requirements of this AD within the specified times unless already accomplished.

units.obligation_text: For all affected GEnx–1B and GEnx–2B model turbofan engines, before exceeding the compliance time in Table 1 to paragraph (g)(1) of this AD, perform a borescope inspection (BSI) or eddy current inspection (ECI) of the stage 6, stage 7, and stage 8 webs, web transitions, and bore faces of the stages 6–10 compressor rotor spool in accordance with the Accomplishment Instructions, paragraph 3, of SB 72–0472 (for GEnx–1B models) or the Accomplishment Instructions, paragraph 3, of SB 72–0415 (for GEnx–2B models).
units.action_summary: Perform BSI or ECI of stage 6, 7, and 8 webs, transitions, and bore faces before the applicable compliance time per Table 1 and service bulletin instructions.

units.obligation_text: For GEnx–1B model turbofan engines, except those identified in paragraph 4, APPENDIX—A, Table 3 of SB 72–0472, if the engines have previously undergone inspections of the aft web of stage 6, stage 7, and stage 8 of the stages 6–10 compressor rotor spool using both GE GEnx–1B SB 72–0448 R00, dated July 29, 2019, and GE GEnx–1B SB 72–0460 R00, dated October 30, 2019, regardless of the CSN accumulated on the stages 6–10 compressor rotor spool, perform the inspection required by paragraph (g)(1) of this AD no later than the next engine shop visit after the effective date of this AD.
units.actor: you (operators/maintainers of GEnx–1B engines meeting the criteria)
units.action_summary: If prior inspections were performed using the two specified SBs, perform the required inspection by the next engine shop visit after the AD's effective date.

units.obligation_text: For GEnx–2B model turbofan engines, except those identified in paragraph 4., APPENDIX—A, Table 3 of SB 72–0415, if the engines have previously undergone inspections of the aft web of stage 6, stage 7, and stage 8 of the stages 6–10 compressor rotor spool using both GE GEnx–2B SB 72–0385 R02, dated July 29, 2019, and GE GEnx–2B SB 72–0398 R00, dated October 30, 2019, regardless of the CSN accumulated on the stages 6–10 compressor rotor spool, perform the inspection required by paragraph (g)(1) of this AD no later than the next engine shop visit after the effective date of this AD.
units.actor: you (operators/maintainers of GEnx–2B engines meeting the criteria)
units.action_summary: If prior inspections were performed using the two specified SBs, perform the required inspection by the next engine shop visit after the AD's effective date.

units.obligation_text: For all affected GEnx–1B and GEnx–2B model turbofan engines, during the inspections required by paragraph (g)(1) of this AD, if a rejectable indication is found, before further flight, remove the stages 6–10 compressor rotor spool from service and replace it with a part eligible for installation.
units.action_summary: If the inspection finds a rejectable indication, remove the stages 6–10 rotor spool and replace it with an eligible part before further flight.

units.section: § 39.13, GE GEnx AD, Table 1 to paragraph (g)(1) - threshold A
units.obligation_text: If Cycles Since New (CSN) accumulated on the stages 6-10 compressor rotor spool is less than 6,500 CSN: Next engine shop visit or before the stages 6-10 compressor rotor spool accumulates 6,500 CSN, whichever occurs first after the effective date of this AD.
units.action_summary: For spools with <6,500 CSN, perform the inspection by the next engine shop visit or before it reaches 6,500 CSN, whichever is first.

units.section: § 39.13, GE GEnx AD, Table 1 to paragraph (g)(1) - threshold B
units.obligation_text: If CSN on the stages 6-10 compressor rotor spool is 6,500 CSN or greater: Before further flight.
units.action_summary: For spools with ≥6,500 CSN, perform the inspection before further flight.

units.obligation_text: For affected GEnx–1B model turbofan engines, you may take credit for the BSI or ECI required by paragraph (g)(1) of this AD, if the stages 6–10 compressor rotor spool webs, web transitions, and bore faces previously received an ECI using Subtask 72–31–45–160–002 of TASK 72–31–45–200–807 in GE GEnx–1B Engine Manual 05–21–00, Life Limits 001 Mandatory Inspections, Rev. 31 dated, January 31, 2020, or earlier, and no rejectable indications were found.
units.action_summary: You may take credit for previously performed ECI inspections meeting the specified criteria and with no rejectable indications.

units.obligation_text: For affected GEnx–2B model turbofan engines, you may take credit for the BSI or ECI required by paragraph (g)(1) of this AD, if the stages 6–10 compressor rotor spool webs, web transitions, and bore faces previously received an ECI using Subtask 72–31–45–160–002 of TASK 72–31–45–200–801 in GE GEnx–2B Engine Manual 05–21–00, Life Limits 001 Mandatory Inspections, Rev. 24 dated, January 31, 2020, or earlier, and no rejectable indications were found.
units.action_summary: You may take credit for previously performed ECI inspections meeting the specified criteria and with no rejectable indications.

units.obligation_text: For affected GEnx–1B and GEnx–2B model turbofan engines, you may take credit for the BSI or ECI required by paragraph (g)(1) of this AD, if you performed these inspections using GE GEnx–1B Service Bulletin (SB) 72–0472 R00, dated April 24, 2020, or GE GEnx–2B SB 72–0415 R00, dated April 24, 2020, respectively, and no rejectable indications were found.
units.action_summary: You may take credit for previously performed inspections using the specified service bulletin revisions if no rejectable indications were found.

units.obligation_text: The Manager, ECO Branch, FAA, has the authority to approve AMOCs for this AD, if requested using the procedures found in 14 CFR 39.19.
units.action_summary: The Manager may approve alternative methods of compliance for this AD when requested per 14 CFR 39.19.

units.obligation_text: In accordance with 14 CFR 39.19, send your request to your principal inspector or local Flight Standards District Office, as appropriate. If sending information directly to the manager of the certification office, send it to the attention of the person identified in paragraph (k)(1) of this AD. You may email your request to: ANE-AD-AMOC@faa.gov.
units.action_summary: Submit AMOC requests per 14 CFR 39.19 to your principal inspector or local FSDO, or directly to the certification office manager as specified; email option provided.

units.obligation_text: Before using any approved AMOC, notify your appropriate principal inspector, or lacking a principal inspector, the manager of the local flight standards district office/ certificate holding district office.
units.actor: you (operators who will use an approved AMOC)
units.action_summary: Notify your principal inspector or local FSDO manager before using any approved AMOC.

title: Special Conditions: magniX USA, Inc., magni250 and magni500 Model Engines

units.obligation_text: The applicant must also comply with the certification procedures set forth in 14 CFR part 21.
units.action_summary: Comply with certification procedures in 14 CFR part 21.

units.obligation_text: Unless otherwise noted in these special conditions, the design must comply with the airworthiness standards for aircraft engines set forth in 14 CFR part 33, except those airworthiness standards specifically and explicitly applicable only to reciprocating and turbine aircraft engines.
units.action_summary: Design must comply with applicable airworthiness standards in 14 CFR part 33, except those only for reciprocating and turbine engines.

units.obligation_text: In addition to § 33.7(a), the design must comply with the following:
units.action_summary: Design must meet additional requirements beyond § 33.7(a).

units.obligation_text: Ratings and operating limitations must be established and included in the type certificate data sheet based on:
units.action_summary: Establish and include ratings and operating limits in the type certificate data sheet.

units.obligation_text: (a)(1) Power, torque, speed, and time for: Rated maximum continuous power;
units.action_summary: Establish power/torque/speed/time for rated maximum continuous power.

units.obligation_text: (a)(2) Power, torque, speed, and time for: Rated maximum temporary power and associated time limit.
units.action_summary: Establish power/torque/speed/time and time limit for rated maximum temporary power.

units.obligation_text: (b) The duty cycle and the rating at that duty cycle.
units.action_summary: Establish duty cycle(s) and associated rating(s).

units.obligation_text: The manufacturer must declare the duty cycle or cycles in the engine certificate data sheet.
units.action_summary: Declare duty cycle(s) in the engine certificate data sheet.

units.obligation_text: The engine design must comply with 14 CFR 33.15.
units.action_summary: Comply with 14 CFR 33.15 materials requirements.

units.obligation_text: The engine design must comply with 14 CFR 33.17.
units.action_summary: Comply with 14 CFR 33.17 fire protection requirements.

units.obligation_text: High-voltage electrical wiring interconnect systems must be protected against arc-faults.
units.actor: high-voltage electrical wiring interconnect systems / the applicant
units.action_summary: Protect high-voltage wiring interconnects against arc-faults.

units.obligation_text: Any non-protected electrical wiring interconnects must be analyzed to show that arc-faults do not cause a hazardous engine effect.
units.action_summary: Analyze non-protected wiring to show arc-faults won't cause hazardous engine effects.

units.obligation_text: The engine design and construction must minimize the development of an unsafe condition of the engine between maintenance intervals, overhaul periods, or mandatory actions described in the applicable Instructions for Continued Airworthiness (ICA).
units.actor: the engine design and construction / the applicant
units.action_summary: Design and construct engine to minimize unsafe conditions between maintenance/overhaul/ICA actions.

units.obligation_text: The engine design and construction must comply with 14 CFR 33.21.
units.action_summary: Comply with 14 CFR 33.21 cooling requirements.

units.obligation_text: If cooling is required to satisfy the safety analysis as described in special condition no. 17, the cooling system monitoring features and usage must be documented in the engine installation manual.
units.action_summary: Document cooling system monitoring features and usage in the installation manual if cooling is required per safety analysis.

units.obligation_text: The engine mounting attachments and related engine structure must comply with 14 CFR 33.23.
units.actor: the engine mounting attachments and related engine structure / the applicant
units.action_summary: Comply with 14 CFR 33.23 for engine mounting and related structure.

units.obligation_text: The engine must comply with 14 CFR 33.25.
units.action_summary: Comply with 14 CFR 33.25 accessory attachment requirements.

units.obligation_text: A rotor overspeed must not result in a burst, rotor growth, or damage that results in a hazardous engine effect, as defined in special condition no. 17(d)(2).
units.action_summary: Rotor overspeed must not cause burst, growth, or damage that leads to hazardous engine effects.

units.obligation_text: Compliance with this paragraph must be shown by test, validated analysis, or a combination of both.
units.action_summary: Show compliance with overspeed requirements by test, validated analysis, or both.

units.obligation_text: Applicable assumed speeds must be declared and justified.
units.action_summary: Declare and justify any assumed speeds used in overspeed compliance showing.

units.obligation_text: Rotors must possess sufficient strength with a margin to burst above certified operating conditions and above failure conditions leading to rotor overspeed.
units.action_summary: Ensure rotors have sufficient strength and margin to burst above certified and failure-induced overspeed conditions.

units.obligation_text: The margin to burst must be shown by tests, validated analysis, or a combination of both.
units.action_summary: Demonstrate margin to burst through tests, validated analysis, or both.

units.obligation_text: The engine must not exceed the speed operational limitations that could affect rotor structural integrity.
units.action_summary: Engine must not exceed speed limits that could affect rotor structural integrity.

units.obligation_text: The engine control system must ensure the engine does not experience any unacceptable operating characteristics or exceed any of its operating limitations.
units.actor: the engine control system / the applicant
units.action_summary: Ensure engine control system prevents unacceptable operating characteristics and limit exceedances.

units.obligation_text: The software and complex electronic hardware, including programmable logic devices, must be designed and developed using a structured and systematic approach that provides a level of assurance for the logic commensurate with the hazard associated with the failure or malfunction of the systems in which the devices are located.
units.action_summary: Design and develop software and complex electronic hardware with a structured approach providing assurance commensurate with associated hazards.

units.obligation_text: The software and complex electronic hardware ... must be substantiated by a verification methodology acceptable to the Administrator.
units.action_summary: Substantiate software and complex electronic hardware using a verification methodology acceptable to the Administrator.

units.obligation_text: All functional aspects of the control system must be substantiated by tests, analysis, or a combination thereof, to show that the engine control system performs the intended functions throughout the declared operational envelope.
units.action_summary: Substantiate all control system functions by test/analysis to show they perform throughout the declared envelope.

units.obligation_text: Environmental limits that cannot be adequately substantiated by endurance demonstrations, validated analysis, or a combination thereof, must be demonstrated by the system and component tests in special condition no. 27.
units.action_summary: Demonstrate environmental limits not substantiated by endurance/analysis via system and component tests (special condition 27).

units.obligation_text: The engine control system must have a maximum rate of Loss of Power Control (LOPC) that is suitable for the intended application.
units.actor: the engine control system / the applicant
units.action_summary: Ensure engine control system's LOPC rate is suitable for intended use.

units.obligation_text: When in the full-up configuration, [the engine control system must] be single-fault tolerant, as determined by the Administrator, for electrical, electrically detectable, and electronic failures involving LOPC events.
units.actor: the engine control system / the applicant
units.action_summary: In full-up configuration, ensure single-fault tolerance for specified failures involving LOPC, as determined by the Administrator.

units.obligation_text: The engine control system must not have any single failure that result in hazardous engine effects.
units.actor: the engine control system / the applicant
units.action_summary: Prevent any single failure that would result in hazardous engine effects.

units.obligation_text: The engine control system must not have any likely failure or malfunction that lead to local events in the intended aircraft installation.
units.actor: the engine control system / the applicant
units.action_summary: Avoid likely failures/malfunctions that cause local events in intended aircraft installation.

units.obligation_text: This assessment must identify faults or failures that affect normal operation, together with the predicted frequency of occurrence of these faults or failures.
units.actor: the system safety assessment / the applicant
units.action_summary: Identify faults/failures affecting normal operation and predict their frequency in the system safety assessment.

units.obligation_text: The design and function of the engine control devices and systems, together with engine instruments, operating instructions and maintenance instructions, must ensure that engine operating limitations will not be exceeded in-service.
units.actor: the design and function of engine control devices and systems / the applicant
units.action_summary: Ensure design, instruments, and instructions prevent in-service exceedance of engine operating limits.

units.obligation_text: Any single failure leading to loss, interruption, or corruption of aircraft-supplied data ... must not result in a hazardous engine effect, as defined in special condition no. 17(d)(2), for any engine installed on the aircraft;
units.action_summary: Such single failures of aircraft-supplied data must not produce hazardous engine effects.

units.obligation_text: Any single failure leading to loss, interruption, or corruption of aircraft-supplied data ... must be able to be detected and accommodated by the control system.
units.action_summary: Detect and accommodate single failures of aircraft-supplied data by the control system.

units.obligation_text: The engine control system must be designed such that the loss, malfunction, or interruption of the control system electrical power source will not result in a hazardous engine effect, the unacceptable transmission of erroneous data, or continued engine operation in the absence of the control function.
units.actor: the engine control system / the applicant
units.action_summary: Design control system so loss/malfunction/interruption of its electrical power won't cause hazardous effects, erroneous data transmission, or continued operation without control.

units.obligation_text: The applicant must comply with 14 CFR 33.29(a), (e), (f), and (g).
units.action_summary: Comply with specified provisions of 14 CFR 33.29.

units.obligation_text: As part of the system safety assessment of special condition no. 10(g), the applicant must assess the possibility and subsequent effect of incorrect fit of instruments, sensors, or connectors.
units.action_summary: Assess risks and effects of incorrect fit of instruments/sensors/connectors within the system safety assessment.

units.obligation_text: Where practicable, the applicant must take design precautions to prevent incorrect configuration of the system.
units.action_summary: Take design precautions, where practicable, to prevent incorrect system configuration.

units.obligation_text: A mechanical, thermal, and electrical stress analysis must show there is a sufficient design margin to prevent unacceptable operating characteristics.
units.action_summary: Show via stress analysis that design margin prevents unacceptable operating characteristics.

units.obligation_text: Maximum stresses in the engine must be determined by tests, validated analysis, or a combination thereof, and must be shown not to exceed minimum material properties.
units.action_summary: Determine maximum stresses and show they do not exceed minimum material properties using tests/analysis.

units.obligation_text: The applicant must show by a safety analysis or means acceptable to the Administrator, whether rotating or moving components, bearings, shafts, static parts, and non-redundant mount components should be classified, designed, manufactured, and managed throughout their service life as critical or life-limited parts.
units.action_summary: Determine via safety analysis whether specified components should be classified and managed as critical or life-limited parts.

units.obligation_text: The applicant must establish the integrity of each critical part or life-limited part by providing the following three plans to the Administrator for approval:
units.action_summary: Provide three approved plans to establish integrity of critical or life-limited parts.

units.obligation_text: (1) An engineering plan that establishes and maintains that the combination of loads, material properties, environmental influences, and operating conditions ... are sufficiently well-known and predictable by validated analysis, test, or service experience.
units.action_summary: Provide an engineering plan showing loads, materials, environment, and conditions are well-known and predictable by validated methods.

units.obligation_text: The engineering plan must ensure each critical part or life-limited part is withdrawn from service at an approved life before hazardous engine effects can occur.
units.action_summary: Ensure parts are withdrawn at an approved life before hazardous engine effects occur.

units.obligation_text: The engineering plan must establish activities to be executed both pre- and post-certification.
units.action_summary: Establish pre- and post-certification activities in the engineering plan.

units.obligation_text: magniX must perform appropriate damage tolerance assessments to address the potential for failure from material, manufacturing, and service-induced anomalies within the approved life of the part.
units.action_summary: magniX must perform damage tolerance assessments for potential failures during approved part life.

units.obligation_text: The approved life must be published in the mandatory ICA.
units.action_summary: Publish the approved part life in the mandatory Instructions for Continued Airworthiness (ICA).

units.obligation_text: (2) A manufacturing plan that identifies the specific manufacturing definition (drawings, procedures, specifications, etc.) necessary to consistently produce critical or life-limited parts with the attributes required by the engineering plan.
units.action_summary: Provide a manufacturing plan identifying definitions and processes to produce parts meeting engineering plan attributes.

units.obligation_text: (3) A service management plan that defines in-service processes for maintenance and repair of critical or life-limited parts that maintain attributes consistent with those required by the engineering plan.
units.action_summary: Provide a service management plan defining maintenance/repair processes preserving engineering-plan attributes.

units.obligation_text: These processes must become part of the mandatory ICA.
units.action_summary: Include the defined service processes in the mandatory ICA.

units.obligation_text: The lubrication system must be designed and constructed to function properly between scheduled maintenance intervals in all flight attitudes and atmospheric conditions in which the engine is expected to operate.
units.action_summary: Design lubrication system to function properly between maintenance intervals in all expected attitudes and conditions.

units.obligation_text: The lubrication system must be designed to prevent contamination of the engine bearings by particle debris.
units.action_summary: Design lubrication system to prevent particle debris contamination of bearings.

units.obligation_text: The applicant must demonstrate by test, validated analysis, or a combination thereof, the unique lubrication attributes and functional capability of (a) and (b).
units.action_summary: Demonstrate lubrication attributes/capabilities of (a) and (b) via test/validated analysis or both.

units.obligation_text: The design and construction of the engine must enable an increase from the minimum power setting to the highest-rated power without detrimental engine effects.
units.actor: the design and construction of the engine / the applicant
units.action_summary: Enable power increase from minimum setting to highest-rated power without harmful effects.

units.obligation_text: The design and construction of the engine must enable an increase from the minimum obtainable power while in-flight and while on the ground to the highest-rated power within a time interval for safe operation of the aircraft.
units.actor: the design and construction of the engine / the applicant
units.action_summary: Enable power increase from minimum obtainable power (in-flight and on ground) to highest-rated within a safe time interval.

units.obligation_text: If the design allows any of the engine main rotating systems to continue to rotate after the engine is shut down while in-flight, this continued rotation must not result in any hazardous engine effects, as specified in special condition no. 17(d)(2).
units.action_summary: Continued in-flight rotation after shutdown must not cause hazardous engine effects.

units.obligation_text: The applicant must comply with § 33.75(a)(1), (a)(2), and (a)(3) using the failure definitions in special condition no. 17(d).
units.action_summary: Comply with specified subsections of § 33.75 using the special condition failure definitions.

units.obligation_text: If the failure of such elements is likely to result in hazardous engine effects, then the applicant may show compliance by reliance on the prescribed integrity requirements of § 33.15, special condition no. 9, or special condition no. 13, as determined by analysis.
units.action_summary: If failures likely cause hazardous effects, the applicant may demonstrate compliance by relying on prescribed integrity requirements as determined by analysis.

units.obligation_text: The failure of such elements and associated prescribed integrity requirements must be stated in the safety analysis.
units.action_summary: State such failures and associated integrity requirements in the safety analysis.

units.obligation_text: The applicant must comply with 14 CFR 33.75(d) and (e) using the failure definitions in special condition no. 17(d) of this special condition.
units.action_summary: Comply with § 33.75(d) and (e) using the special condition failure definitions.

units.obligation_text: Ingestion from likely sources (foreign objects, birds, ice, rain, hail) must not result in unacceptable power loss, or in hazardous engine effects as defined by special condition no. 17(d)(2).
units.action_summary: Design to ensure ingestion from likely sources does not cause unacceptable power loss or hazardous engine effects.

units.obligation_text: If the design of the engine relies on features, attachments, or systems that may be supplied by the installer for the prevention of unacceptable power loss or hazardous engine effects following potential ingestion, then the features, attachments, or systems must be documented in the engine installation manual.
units.action_summary: Document installer-supplied features/attachments/systems in the engine installation manual if design relies on them to prevent ingestion effects.

units.obligation_text: Each liquid system used for lubrication or cooling of engine components must be designed and constructed to function properly in all flight attitudes and atmospheric conditions in which the engine is expected to operate.
units.action_summary: Design liquid systems for lubrication/cooling to function properly in all expected attitudes and conditions.

units.obligation_text: If a liquid system used for lubrication or cooling of engine components is not self-contained, the interfaces to that system must be defined in the engine installation manual.
units.action_summary: Define interfaces for non-self-contained liquid systems in the engine installation manual.

units.obligation_text: The engine must be designed and constructed to function throughout its normal operating range of rotor speeds and engine output power, including defined exceedances, without inducing excessive stress in any of the engine parts because of vibration and without imparting excessive vibration forces to the aircraft structure.
units.actor: the engine design and construction / the applicant
units.action_summary: Design engine to operate across its range without causing excessive vibration-induced stress or transferring excessive vibration to the aircraft.

units.obligation_text: Each proposed engine design must undergo a vibration survey to establish that the vibration characteristics of those components that may be subject to induced vibration are acceptable throughout the declared flight envelope and engine operating range for the specific installation configuration.
units.action_summary: Conduct a vibration survey to establish acceptable vibration characteristics for components subject to induced vibration.

units.obligation_text: This survey must be shown by test, validated analysis, or a combination thereof.
units.action_summary: Demonstrate the vibration survey results via test, validated analysis, or both.

units.obligation_text: When approval is sought for a transient maximum engine overtorque, the applicant must demonstrate by tests, validated analysis, or a combination thereof, that the engine is capable of continued operation after operating at the maximum engine overtorque condition without maintenance action.
units.action_summary: If seeking approval for transient overtorque, demonstrate engine can continue operating afterward without maintenance, via tests/analysis.

units.obligation_text: Each engine must be subjected to calibration tests to establish its power characteristics and the conditions both before and after the endurance and durability demonstrations specified in special conditions nos. 23 and 26.
units.action_summary: Subject each engine to calibration tests before and after endurance and durability demonstrations to establish power characteristics.

units.obligation_text: The applicant must subject the engine to an endurance demonstration acceptable to the Administrator to demonstrate the limit capabilities of the engine.
units.action_summary: Subject the engine to an Administrator-acceptable endurance demonstration to show its limit capabilities.

units.obligation_text: The engine design must demonstrate its capability to endure operation at its temperature limits plus an acceptable margin.
units.action_summary: Demonstrate engine can endure operation at temperature limits plus margin.

units.obligation_text: The applicant must quantify and justify the margin at each rated condition to the Administrator.
units.action_summary: Quantify and justify temperature margin for each rated condition to the Administrator.

units.obligation_text: The demonstration must be repeated for all declared duty cycles and associated ratings.
units.action_summary: Repeat the temperature-limit demonstration for all declared duty cycles and ratings.

units.obligation_text: The engine design must demonstrate safe operating characteristics, including but not limited to, power cycling, acceleration, and overspeeding, throughout its declared flight envelope and operating range.
units.action_summary: Demonstrate safe operating characteristics across the declared envelope and operating range, including power cycling, acceleration, and overspeeding.

units.obligation_text: The declared engine operational characteristics must account for installation loads and effects.
units.action_summary: Account for installation loads and effects in declared engine operational characteristics.

units.obligation_text: The engine must be subjected to a durability demonstration to show that each part of the engine has been designed and constructed to minimize the development of any unsafe condition of the system between overhaul periods, or between engine replacement intervals if overhaul is not defined.
units.action_summary: Subject engine to a durability demonstration proving parts minimize unsafe-condition development between overhauls or replacements.

units.obligation_text: This test must simulate the conditions in which the engine is expected to operate in-service, including typical start-stop cycles.
units.action_summary: Durability test must simulate expected in-service conditions, including start-stop cycles.

units.obligation_text: The applicant must show that systems and components will perform their intended functions in all declared environmental and operating conditions.
units.action_summary: Show systems and components perform intended functions in all declared environmental and operating conditions.

units.obligation_text: If shaft rotation is prevented by a means to lock the rotor(s), the engine must demonstrate reliable rotor locking performance and that no hazardous effects will occur.
units.action_summary: If rotor locking prevents shaft rotation, demonstrate reliable locking and absence of hazardous effects.

units.obligation_text: The applicant must comply with either (a) or (b) as follows:
units.action_summary: Comply with either the teardown evaluation or the non-teardown evaluation provisions.

units.obligation_text: After the endurance and durability demonstrations have been completed, the engine must be completely disassembled.
units.action_summary: Completely disassemble the engine after endurance and durability demonstrations.

units.obligation_text: Each engine component must be within service limits and eligible for continued operation in accordance with the information submitted for showing compliance with § 33.4, Instructions for Continued Airworthiness.
units.action_summary: Ensure each engine component is within service limits and eligible for continued operation per § 33.4 documentation.

units.obligation_text: Each engine component having an adjustment setting and a functioning characteristic that can be established independent of installation on or in the engine must retain each setting and functioning characteristic within the limits that were established and recorded at the beginning of the endurance and durability demonstrations.
units.action_summary: Ensure components with independent adjustment/settings retain those settings/characteristics within initial established limits after demonstrations.

units.obligation_text: If a teardown is not performed for all engine components, then the life limits for these components must be established based on the endurance and durability demonstrations.
units.action_summary: If no teardown, establish life limits for components based on endurance and durability demonstrations.

units.obligation_text: The engine must provide containment features that protect against likely hazards from rotating components as follows—
units.action_summary: Provide containment features to protect against hazards from rotating components.

units.obligation_text: The design of the case surrounding rotating components must provide for the containment of the rotating components in the event of failure unless the applicant shows that the rotor has a margin to burst that would justify no need for containment features.
units.action_summary: Case design must provide containment in failure events unless applicant shows sufficient margin to burst negating containment need.

units.obligation_text: If the margin to burst shows the case must have containment features in the event of failure, the case must provide for the containment of the failed rotating components.
units.action_summary: If margin to burst indicates containment is required, the case must contain failed rotating components.

units.obligation_text: The applicant must define by test, validated analysis, or combination thereof, and document in the installation manual the energy level, trajectory, and size of any fragments released from damage caused by the main rotor failure that pass forward or aft of the surrounding case.
units.action_summary: Define and document fragment energy, trajectory, and size of fragments that pass beyond the surrounding case after main rotor failure, using test/analysis.

units.obligation_text: The applicant must conduct functional demonstrations including feathering, negative torque, negative thrust, and reverse thrust operations, as applicable, with a representative propeller.
units.action_summary: Conduct functional demonstrations (feathering, negative torque/thrust, reverse thrust) with representative propeller as applicable.

units.obligation_text: These demonstrations may be conducted as part of the endurance and durability demonstrations.
units.action_summary: Permitted to conduct functional demonstrations as part of endurance/durability demonstrations.

units.obligation_text: Maintenance of the engine may be made during the tests in accordance with the service and maintenance instructions contained in the proposed ICA.
units.action_summary: Engine maintenance may be performed during tests per service/maintenance instructions in proposed ICA.

units.obligation_text: The applicant must subject the engine or its parts to maintenance and additional tests that the Administrator finds necessary if— (1) The frequency of the service is excessive; (2) The number of stops due to engine malfunction is excessive; (3) Major repairs are needed; or (4) Replacement of a part is found necessary during the tests or as the result of findings from the teardown inspection.
units.action_summary: If certain adverse conditions (listed) occur, subject engine/parts to maintenance and additional tests as the Administrator finds necessary.

units.obligation_text: Upon completion of all demonstrations and testing specified in these special conditions, the engine and its components must be Within serviceable limits;
units.action_summary: After all demonstrations/testing, ensure engine and components are within serviceable limits.

units.obligation_text: Upon completion of all demonstrations and testing specified in these special conditions, the engine and its components must be Safe for continued operation;
units.action_summary: After all demonstrations/testing, ensure engine and components are safe for continued operation.

units.obligation_text: Upon completion of all demonstrations and testing specified in these special conditions, the engine and its components must be Capable of operating at declared ratings while remaining within limits.
units.action_summary: After all demonstrations/testing, ensure engine and components can operate at declared ratings while staying within limits.

units.obligation_text: If the inside of the LH fuel supply hose has any twisting, before further flight, remove the LH fuel supply hose from service and install an airworthy LH fuel supply hose by following the Accomplishment Instructions, paragraph 3.B.3.b of ASB EC225–71A019.

units.action_summary: The software version installed must not be 3.13 or any earlier version (i.e., must be newer than 3.13).
