title: Airworthiness Directives: The Boeing Company Airplanes

units.obligation_text: The Federal Register, issued under the authority of the Administrative Committee, is officially maintained online and is available on at least one Government Publishing Office website.
units.actor: the Administrative Committee of the Federal Register / the Federal Register (maintainers)
units.action_summary: Maintain the Federal Register online and make it available on at least one Government Publishing Office website.

units.obligation_text: Requests for subscriptions to the Federal Register may be made as follows:
units.action_summary: Requesters may make subscription requests using the methods listed in the following paragraphs.

units.obligation_text: Requests from a Member of Congress or any other office of the United States for a specific issue or a subscription may be submitted via a Government Publishing Office website or by email to an email address provided on that website.
units.actor: Members of Congress or any other office of the United States
units.action_summary: May submit requests for a specific issue or a subscription via a GPO website or by email to the address on that site.

units.obligation_text: Official subscription requests: (i) May be made in the current year for that year or for the upcoming year,
units.action_summary: Official subscriptions may be requested for the current year or the upcoming year.

units.obligation_text: Official subscription requests: (ii) Will expire at the end of each calendar year,
units.action_summary: Official subscription requests expire at the end of each calendar year.

units.obligation_text: Official subscription requests: (iii) Will not automatically continue into a new calendar year.
units.action_summary: Subscriptions will not automatically renew or continue into a new calendar year.

units.obligation_text: Notifications regarding procedures for requesting official copies of specific issues or print subscriptions are available:
units.action_summary: Notifications about procedures for requesting official copies or print subscriptions are available at the specified locations.

units.obligation_text: Notifications ... are available: (1) On a Government Publishing Office website dedicated to official subscriptions,
units.action_summary: Notifications are available on a GPO website dedicated to official subscriptions.

units.obligation_text: Notifications ... are available: (2) On www.federalregister.gov, and
units.action_summary: Notifications are available on www.federalregister.gov.

units.obligation_text: Notifications ... are available: (3) In the front matter of the Federal Register, which is the text that precedes the main text of the daily issue of the Federal Register.
units.action_summary: Notifications are available in the front matter of the Federal Register daily issue.

units.obligation_text: The FAA must receive comments by February 12, 2021.
units.action_summary: Comments on the proposed AD must be received by the FAA by February 12, 2021.

units.obligation_text: This AD applies to The Boeing Company Model 757–200, –200CB, and –300 series airplanes, certificated in any category, as identified in Boeing Special Attention Requirements Bulletin 757–25–0315 RB, Revision 1, dated May 20, 2020, and airplane having variable number NB451.
units.actor: owners/operators of the specified Boeing Model 757 series airplanes
units.action_summary: The AD's requirements and limitations apply to the listed Boeing Model 757 series airplanes (including NB451).

units.obligation_text: Comply with this AD within the compliance times specified, unless already done.
units.action_summary: Affected parties must comply with the AD within the specified compliance times unless the actions have already been done.

units.obligation_text: Except as specified by paragraph (h) of this AD: At the applicable times specified in the 'Compliance' paragraph of Boeing Special Attention Requirements Bulletin 757–25–0315 RB, Revision 1, dated May 20, 2020, do all applicable actions identified in, and in accordance with, the Accomplishment Instructions of Boeing Special Attention Requirements Bulletin 757–25–0315 RB, Revision 1, dated May 20, 2020.
units.action_summary: Perform all applicable actions identified in the Accomplishment Instructions of the referenced Boeing Requirements Bulletin at the applicable times, except as specified in paragraph (h).

units.obligation_text: Where Boeing Special Attention Requirements Bulletin 757–25–0315 RB, Revision 1, dated May 20, 2020, uses the phrase 'the Revision 1 date of Requirements Bulletin 757–25–0315 RB,' this AD requires using 'the effective date of this AD.'
units.actor: persons performing the actions required by this AD
units.action_summary: When the bulletin references its revision date, use this AD's effective date instead.

units.obligation_text: For airplane variable number NB451, do the applicable actions for Group 4 identified in, and in accordance with, the Accomplishment Instructions of Boeing Special Attention Requirements Bulletin 757–25–0315 RB, Revision 1, dated May 20, 2020.
units.actor: owners/operators of airplane variable number NB451
units.action_summary: For airplane NB451, perform the Group 4 actions in the Accomplishment Instructions of the referenced Boeing Requirements Bulletin.

units.obligation_text: As of the applicable time specified in paragraph (i)(1) or (2) of this AD, no person may install on any airplane any PSU, life vest panel, or video panel without an updated lanyard assembly installed.
units.action_summary: Prohibits installation of PSUs, life vest panels, or video panels on any airplane unless they have an updated lanyard assembly installed, as of the applicable time.

units.obligation_text: For airplanes that have PSUs, life vest panels, or video panels without the updated lanyard assemblies installed as of the effective date of this AD: After modification of the airplane as required by paragraph (g) of this AD.
units.actor: owners/operators of airplanes that, as of the effective date, have PSUs, life vest panels, or video panels without updated lanyard assemblies
units.action_summary: For airplanes lacking updated lanyards as of the effective date, the installation prohibition applies after the airplane has been modified as required by paragraph (g).

units.obligation_text: For airplanes that do not have PSUs, life vest panels, or video panels without the updated lanyard assemblies installed as of the effective date of this AD: As of the effective date of this AD.
units.actor: owners/operators of airplanes that do not have PSUs, life vest panels, or video panels lacking updated lanyards as of the effective date (i.e., airplanes already equipped with updated lanyards)
units.action_summary: For airplanes already equipped with updated lanyards, the installation prohibition (installing without an updated lanyard) is effective as of the AD effective date.

units.obligation_text: The Manager, Seattle ACO Branch, FAA, has the authority to approve AMOCs for this AD, if requested using the procedures found in 14 CFR 39.19.
units.action_summary: The Manager may approve alternative methods of compliance (AMOCs) for this AD if requested in accordance with 14 CFR 39.19.

units.obligation_text: In accordance with 14 CFR 39.19, send your request to your principal inspector or local Flight Standards District Office, as appropriate.
units.action_summary: Requests for AMOC approval must be sent to the requester's principal inspector or local Flight Standards District Office per 14 CFR 39.19.

units.obligation_text: If sending information directly to the manager of the certification office, send it to the attention of the person identified in paragraph (k)(1) of this AD.
units.actor: persons sending AMOC information directly to the certification office manager
units.action_summary: If submitting AMOC information directly to the certification office manager, it must be addressed to the person identified in paragraph (k)(1).

units.obligation_text: Information may be emailed to: 9-ANM-Seattle-ACO-AMOC-Requests@faa.gov.
units.action_summary: AMOC requests/information may be submitted via the specified email address.

units.obligation_text: Before using any approved AMOC, notify your appropriate principal inspector, or lacking a principal inspector, the manager of the local flight standards district office/certificate holding district office.
units.action_summary: Notify your principal inspector (or, if none, the manager of the local FSDO/CHDO) before using any approved AMOC.

units.obligation_text: An AMOC that provides an acceptable level of safety may be used for any repair, modification, or alteration required by this AD if it is approved by The Boeing Company Organization Designation Authorization (ODA) that has been authorized by the Manager, Seattle ACO Branch, FAA, to make those findings.
units.action_summary: An approved AMOC may be used for required repairs/modifications/alterations if approved by an authorized Boeing ODA.

units.obligation_text: To be approved, the repair method, modification deviation, or alteration deviation must meet the certification basis of the airplane, and the approval must specifically refer to this AD.
units.actor: the approving authority (e.g., Boeing ODA or Manager-authorized entity)
units.action_summary: For an AMOC to be approved, the repair/modification/alteration must meet the airplane's certification basis and the approval must explicitly reference this AD.

title: Airworthiness Criteria: Amazon Logistics, Inc. MK27

units.obligation_text: The applicant must define and submit to the FAA a concept of operations (CONOPS) proposal describing the Unmanned Aircraft System (UAS) operation in the National Airspace System for which certification is requested.
units.action_summary: Applicant must define and submit a CONOPS describing the UAS operation for which certification is requested.

units.obligation_text: The CONOPS proposal must include, at a minimum, a description of the intended type of operations.
units.action_summary: Include description of the intended type of operations in the CONOPS.

units.obligation_text: The CONOPS proposal must include, at a minimum, a description of unmanned aircraft (UA) specifications.
units.action_summary: Include UA specifications in the CONOPS.

units.obligation_text: The CONOPS proposal must include, at a minimum, a description of meteorological conditions.
units.action_summary: Include meteorological conditions in the CONOPS.

units.obligation_text: The CONOPS proposal must include, at a minimum, a description of operators, pilots, and personnel responsibilities.
units.action_summary: Include personnel responsibilities in the CONOPS.

units.obligation_text: The CONOPS proposal must include, at a minimum, a description of control station and support equipment.
units.action_summary: Include control station and support equipment description in the CONOPS.

units.obligation_text: The CONOPS proposal must include, at a minimum, a description of command, control, and communication functions.
units.action_summary: Include command, control, and communication functions in the CONOPS.

units.obligation_text: The CONOPS proposal must include, at a minimum, a description of operational parameters, such as population density, geographic operating boundaries, airspace classes, launch and recovery area, congestion of proposed operating area, communications with air traffic control, line of sight, and aircraft separation.
units.action_summary: Include operational parameters (population density, boundaries, airspace, launch/recovery areas, ATC communications, line of sight, separation) in the CONOPS.

units.obligation_text: The control station must be designed to provide the pilot with all information required for continued safe flight and operation.
units.actor: the control station (as designed by the applicant)
units.action_summary: Design the control station to provide the pilot with all information required for safe flight and operation.

units.obligation_text: This information includes, at a minimum, alerts, such as an alert following the loss of the command and control (C2) link and function.
units.actor: the control station (as designed by the applicant)
units.action_summary: Provide alerts, including alerts for loss of C2 link, to the pilot.

units.obligation_text: This information includes, at a minimum, the status of all critical parameters for all energy storage systems.
units.actor: the control station (as designed by the applicant)
units.action_summary: Provide status of critical parameters for energy storage systems to the pilot.

units.obligation_text: This information includes, at a minimum, the status of all critical parameters for all propulsion systems.
units.actor: the control station (as designed by the applicant)
units.action_summary: Provide status of critical propulsion parameters to the pilot.

units.obligation_text: This information includes, at a minimum, flight and navigation information as appropriate, such as airspeed, heading, altitude, and location.
units.actor: the control station (as designed by the applicant)
units.action_summary: Provide flight and navigation information (airspeed, heading, altitude, location) to the pilot.

units.obligation_text: This information includes, at a minimum, C2 link signal strength, quality, or status.
units.actor: the control station (as designed by the applicant)
units.action_summary: Provide C2 link signal strength/quality/status information to the pilot.

units.obligation_text: To minimize the existence of errors, the applicant must:
units.action_summary: Applicant must take measures to minimize software errors.

units.obligation_text: Verify by test all software that may impact the safe operation of the UAS;
units.action_summary: Verify by test any software that may affect safe operation.

units.obligation_text: Utilize a configuration management system that tracks, controls, and preserves changes made to software throughout the entire life cycle;
units.action_summary: Use a configuration management system to track and control software changes during the life cycle.

units.obligation_text: Implement a problem reporting system that captures and records defects and modifications to the software.
units.action_summary: Implement a problem reporting system to record software defects and modifications.

units.obligation_text: UAS equipment, systems, and networks, addressed separately and in relation to other systems, must be protected from intentional unauthorized electronic interactions that may result in an adverse effect on the security or airworthiness of the UAS. Protection must be ensured by showing that the security risks have been identified, assessed, and mitigated as necessary.
units.actor: the applicant / UAS equipment, systems, and networks (as designed)
units.action_summary: Protect UAS equipment, systems, and networks against intentional unauthorized electronic interactions by identifying, assessing, and mitigating security risks.

units.obligation_text: When required by paragraph (a) of this section, procedures and instructions to ensure security protections are maintained must be included in the Instructions for Continued Airworthiness (ICA).
units.action_summary: Include procedures and instructions in the ICA to ensure security protections are maintained when required.

units.obligation_text: The UAS must be designed so that, in the event of a loss of the C2 link, the UA will automatically and immediately execute a safe predetermined flight, loiter, landing, or termination.
units.actor: the UAS (as designed by the applicant)
units.action_summary: Design the UAS to automatically and immediately execute a safe predetermined action (flight, loiter, landing, or termination) upon loss of C2 link.

units.obligation_text: The applicant must establish the predetermined action in the event of a loss of the C2 link and include it in the UAS Flight Manual.
units.action_summary: Establish the predetermined action for loss of C2 link and include it in the UAS Flight Manual.

units.obligation_text: The UAS Flight Manual must include the minimum performance requirements for the C2 data link defining when the C2 link is degraded to a level where remote active control of the UA is no longer ensured.
units.actor: the applicant (in the UAS Flight Manual)
units.action_summary: Include minimum C2 data link performance requirements in the UAS Flight Manual that define when remote control is no longer ensured.

units.obligation_text: Takeoff when the C2 link is degraded below the minimum link performance requirements must be prevented by design or prohibited by an operating limitation in the UAS Flight Manual.
units.action_summary: Prevent takeoff when the C2 link is below minimum performance by design or prohibit it via an operating limitation in the Flight Manual.

units.obligation_text: Except as provided in paragraph (b) of this section, the UAS must have design characteristics that will protect the UAS from loss of flight or loss of control due to lightning.
units.actor: the UAS (as designed by the applicant)
units.action_summary: Design characteristics must protect the UAS from loss of flight or control due to lightning, unless paragraph (b) applies.

units.obligation_text: If the UAS has not been shown to protect against lightning, the UAS Flight Manual must include an operating limitation to prohibit flight into weather conditions conducive to lightning activity.
units.actor: the applicant (via the UAS Flight Manual)
units.action_summary: If lightning protection is not shown, include an operating limitation in the Flight Manual prohibiting flight into lightning-conducive weather.

units.obligation_text: Except as provided in paragraph (c) of this section, the UAS must have design characteristics that will allow the UAS to operate within the adverse weather conditions specified in the CONOPS without loss of flight or loss of control.
units.actor: the UAS (as designed by the applicant)
units.action_summary: Design the UAS to operate in CONOPS-specified adverse weather (rain, snow, icing) without loss of flight or control, unless (c) applies.

units.obligation_text: For adverse weather conditions for which the UAS is not approved to operate, the applicant must develop operating limitations to prohibit flight into known adverse weather conditions and either:
units.action_summary: If the UAS is not approved for certain adverse weather, the applicant must develop operating limitations to prohibit flight into known adverse weather and take one of two listed actions.

units.obligation_text: Develop operating limitations to prevent inadvertent flight into adverse weather conditions;
units.action_summary: Develop operating limitations that prevent inadvertent entry into adverse weather conditions.

units.obligation_text: Provide a means to detect any adverse weather conditions for which the UAS is not certificated to operate and show the UAS’s ability to avoid or exit those conditions.
units.action_summary: Provide means to detect unapproved adverse weather and demonstrate the UAS can avoid or exit such conditions.

units.obligation_text: If the type design includes critical parts, the applicant must establish a critical parts list.
units.action_summary: If critical parts exist in the type design, establish a critical parts list.

units.obligation_text: The applicant must develop and define mandatory maintenance instructions or life limits, or a combination of both, to prevent failures of critical parts.
units.action_summary: Develop mandatory maintenance instructions or life limits (or both) to prevent critical part failures.

units.obligation_text: Each of these mandatory actions must be included in the Airworthiness Limitations Section of the ICA.
units.action_summary: Include the mandatory maintenance actions/life limits for critical parts in the Airworthiness Limitations Section of the ICA.

units.obligation_text: The applicant must provide a UAS Flight Manual with each UAS.
units.action_summary: Provide a UAS Flight Manual with each UAS produced.

units.obligation_text: The UAS Flight Manual must contain UAS operating limitations.
units.action_summary: Include operating limitations in the UAS Flight Manual.

units.obligation_text: The UAS Flight Manual must contain UAS normal and emergency operating procedures.
units.action_summary: Include normal and emergency operating procedures in the UAS Flight Manual.

units.obligation_text: The UAS Flight Manual must contain performance information.
units.action_summary: Include performance information in the UAS Flight Manual.

units.obligation_text: The UAS Flight Manual must contain loading information.
units.action_summary: Include loading information in the UAS Flight Manual.

units.obligation_text: The UAS Flight Manual must contain other information that is necessary for safe operation because of design, operating, or handling characteristics.
units.action_summary: Include any other information necessary for safe operation related to design, operation, or handling in the Flight Manual.

units.obligation_text: Those portions of the UAS Flight Manual containing the information specified in paragraphs (a)(1) through (4) of this section must be approved by the FAA.
units.action_summary: Obtain FAA approval for the portions of the Flight Manual containing operating limitations, procedures, performance, and loading information.

units.obligation_text: The applicant must prepare ICA for the UAS in accordance with Appendix A to Part 23, as appropriate, that are acceptable to the FAA.
units.action_summary: Prepare Instructions for Continued Airworthiness (ICA) in accordance with Appendix A to Part 23 that are acceptable to the FAA.

units.obligation_text: The ICA may be incomplete at type certification if a program exists to ensure their completion prior to delivery of the first UAS or issuance of a standard airworthiness certificate, whichever occurs later.
units.action_summary: ICA may be incomplete at type certification only if a program ensures completion before delivery of the first UAS or issuance of a standard airworthiness certificate.

units.obligation_text: The UAS must be designed to be durable and reliable commensurate to the maximum population density specified in the operating limitations.
units.actor: the UAS (as designed by the applicant)
units.action_summary: Design the UAS to be durable and reliable appropriate to the maximum population density in the operating limitations.

units.obligation_text: The durability and reliability must be demonstrated by flight test in accordance with the requirements of this section and completed with no failures that result in a loss of flight, loss of control, loss of containment, or emergency landing outside the operator’s recovery area.
units.action_summary: Demonstrate durability and reliability by flight test with no failures causing loss of flight, control, containment, or emergency landing outside recovery area.

units.obligation_text: Once a UAS has begun testing to show compliance with this section, all flights for that UA must be included in the flight test report.
units.action_summary: Include all flights for that UA in the flight test report once testing begins.

units.obligation_text: Tests must include an evaluation of the entire flight envelope across all phases of operation and must address, at a minimum, the following:
units.action_summary: Tests must evaluate entire flight envelope across all phases and address specified conditions.

units.obligation_text: Tests must address, at a minimum, flight distances.
units.action_summary: Include flight distances in test evaluations.

units.obligation_text: Tests must address, at a minimum, flight durations.
units.action_summary: Include flight durations in test evaluations.

units.obligation_text: Tests must address, at a minimum, route complexity.
units.action_summary: Include route complexity in test evaluations.

units.obligation_text: Tests must address, at a minimum, weight.
units.action_summary: Include weight conditions in test evaluations.

units.obligation_text: Tests must address, at a minimum, center of gravity.
units.action_summary: Include center of gravity conditions in test evaluations.

units.obligation_text: Tests must address, at a minimum, density altitude.
units.action_summary: Include density altitude in test evaluations.

units.obligation_text: Tests must address, at a minimum, outside air temperature.
units.action_summary: Include outside air temperature in test evaluations.

units.obligation_text: Tests must address, at a minimum, airspeed.
units.action_summary: Include airspeed in test evaluations.

units.obligation_text: Tests must address, at a minimum, wind.
units.action_summary: Include wind conditions in test evaluations.

units.obligation_text: Tests must address, at a minimum, weather.
units.action_summary: Include weather conditions in test evaluations.

units.obligation_text: Tests must address, at a minimum, operation at night, if requested.
units.action_summary: Include nighttime operation testing if requested.

units.obligation_text: Tests must address, at a minimum, energy storage system capacity.
units.action_summary: Include energy storage system capacity in test evaluations.

units.obligation_text: Tests must address, at a minimum, aircraft to pilot ratio.
units.action_summary: Include aircraft-to-pilot ratio in test evaluations.

units.obligation_text: Tests must include the most adverse combinations of the conditions and configurations in paragraph (b) of this section.
units.action_summary: Include the most adverse combinations of the specified conditions and configurations in testing.

units.obligation_text: Tests must show a distribution of the different flight profiles and routes representative of the type of operations identified in the CONOPS.
units.action_summary: Demonstrate a distribution of flight profiles and routes representative of the CONOPS operations in testing.

units.obligation_text: Tests must be conducted in conditions consistent with the expected environmental conditions identified in the CONOPS, including electromagnetic interference (EMI) and High Intensity Radiated Fields (HIRF).
units.action_summary: Conduct tests in conditions consistent with expected CONOPS environmental conditions, including EMI and HIRF.

units.obligation_text: Tests must not require exceptional piloting skill or alertness.
units.action_summary: Design tests so they do not require exceptional piloting skill or alertness.

units.obligation_text: Any UAS used for testing must be subject to the same worst-case ground handling, shipping, and transportation loads as those allowed in service.
units.actor: any UAS used for testing / the applicant
units.action_summary: Subject test UAS to the same worst-case ground handling, shipping, and transportation loads as in service.

units.obligation_text: Any UAS used for testing must be maintained and operated in accordance with the ICA and UAS Flight Manual.
units.actor: any UAS used for testing / the applicant
units.action_summary: Maintain and operate any test UAS according to the ICA and UAS Flight Manual.

units.obligation_text: No maintenance beyond the intervals established in the ICA will be allowed to show compliance with this section.
units.action_summary: Prohibit maintenance beyond ICA-established intervals to demonstrate compliance.

units.obligation_text: If cargo operations or external-load operations are requested, tests must show, throughout the flight envelope and with the cargo or external-load at the most critical combinations of weight and center of gravity, that—
units.action_summary: If cargo or external-load operations are requested, tests must demonstrate specified conditions throughout the flight envelope with critical weight and CG combinations.

units.obligation_text: If cargo operations or external-load operations are requested, tests must show that the UA is safely controllable and maneuverable.
units.action_summary: Demonstrate that the UA remains safely controllable and maneuverable with cargo/external loads at critical combinations.

units.obligation_text: If cargo operations or external-load operations are requested, tests must show that the cargo or external-load are retainable and transportable.
units.action_summary: Demonstrate that cargo or external-loads are retainable and transportable under critical conditions.

units.obligation_text: The UAS must be designed such that a probable failure will not result in a loss of containment or control of the UA.
units.actor: the UAS (as designed by the applicant)
units.action_summary: Design the UAS so that probable failures do not cause loss of containment or control.

units.obligation_text: This must be demonstrated by test.
units.action_summary: Demonstrate by test that probable failures will not result in loss of containment or control.

units.obligation_text: Probable failures related to the following equipment, at a minimum, must be addressed.
units.action_summary: Address probable failures for the listed equipment at minimum.

units.obligation_text: Probable failures related to propulsion systems must be addressed.
units.action_summary: Address probable failures of propulsion systems.

units.obligation_text: Probable failures related to the C2 link must be addressed.
units.action_summary: Address probable failures of the C2 link.

units.obligation_text: Probable failures related to Global Positioning System (GPS) must be addressed.
units.action_summary: Address probable failures of GPS.

units.obligation_text: Probable failures related to critical flight control components with a single point of failure must be addressed.
units.action_summary: Address probable failures of single-point-of-failure flight control components.

units.obligation_text: Probable failures related to the control station must be addressed.
units.action_summary: Address probable failures of the control station.

units.obligation_text: Probable failures related to any other equipment identified by the applicant must be addressed.
units.action_summary: Address probable failures of any other equipment identified by the applicant.

units.obligation_text: Any UAS used for testing must be operated in accordance with the UAS Flight Manual.
units.actor: any UAS used for testing / the applicant
units.action_summary: Operate any UAS used for testing in accordance with the UAS Flight Manual.

units.obligation_text: Each test must occur at the critical phase and mode of flight, and at the highest aircraft-to-pilot ratio.
units.action_summary: Conduct each test at the critical flight phase/mode and at the highest aircraft-to-pilot ratio.

units.obligation_text: All of the following required UAS capabilities and functions must be demonstrated by test:
units.actor: the applicant / the UAS (to be demonstrated)
units.action_summary: Demonstrate by test the listed required UAS capabilities and functions.

units.obligation_text: Capability to regain command and control of the UA after the C2 link has been lost.
units.action_summary: Demonstrate the UAS can regain command and control after C2 link loss.

units.obligation_text: Capability of the electrical system to power all UA systems and payloads.
units.action_summary: Demonstrate electrical system can power all systems and payloads.

units.obligation_text: Ability for the pilot to safely discontinue the flight.
units.action_summary: Demonstrate pilot can safely discontinue flight.

units.obligation_text: Ability for the pilot to dynamically re-route the UA.
units.action_summary: Demonstrate pilot can dynamically re-route the UA.

units.obligation_text: Ability to safely abort a takeoff.
units.action_summary: Demonstrate ability to safely abort a takeoff.

units.obligation_text: Ability to safely abort a landing and initiate a go-around.
units.action_summary: Demonstrate ability to safely abort a landing and go-around.

units.obligation_text: The following UAS capabilities and functions, if requested for approval, must be demonstrated by test:
units.action_summary: If requested for approval, demonstrate the listed additional capabilities by test.

units.obligation_text: Continued flight after degradation of the propulsion system.
units.action_summary: If requested, demonstrate continued flight capability after propulsion degradation.

units.obligation_text: Geo-fencing that contains the UA within a designated area, in all operating conditions.
units.action_summary: If requested, demonstrate geo-fencing that contains the UA within a designated area in all operating conditions.

units.obligation_text: Positive transfer of the UA between control stations that ensures only one control station can control the UA at a time.
units.action_summary: If requested, demonstrate positive transfer between control stations ensuring only one station controls the UA at a time.

units.obligation_text: Capability to release an external cargo load to prevent loss of control of the UA.
units.action_summary: If requested, demonstrate the capability to release external cargo to prevent loss of control.

units.obligation_text: Capability to detect and avoid other aircraft and obstacles.
units.action_summary: If requested, demonstrate detect-and-avoid capability for other aircraft and obstacles.

units.obligation_text: The UAS must be designed to safeguard against inadvertent discontinuation of the flight and inadvertent release of cargo or external-load.
units.actor: the UAS (as designed by the applicant)
units.action_summary: Design the UAS to prevent inadvertent discontinuation of flight and inadvertent cargo/external-load release.

units.obligation_text: The structure of the UA must be shown to be able to withstand the repeated loads expected during its service life without failure.
units.action_summary: Show the UA structure can withstand expected repeated loads throughout service life without failure.

units.obligation_text: A life limit for the airframe must be established, demonstrated by test, and included in the ICA.
units.action_summary: Establish an airframe life limit, demonstrate it by test, and include it in the ICA.

units.obligation_text: The performance, maneuverability, stability, and control of the UA within the flight envelope described in the UAS Flight Manual must be demonstrated at a minimum of 5% over maximum gross weight with no loss of control or loss of flight.
units.actor: the applicant / the UAS (to be demonstrated)
units.action_summary: Demonstrate performance, maneuverability, stability, and control at least 5% over max gross weight without loss of control or flight.

title: Airworthiness Directives: Goodrich Externally-Mounted Hoist Assemblies

units.obligation_text: The FAA must receive comments by January 25, 2021.
units.action_summary: Receive public comments by January 25, 2021.

units.obligation_text: You are responsible for performing each action required by this AD within the specified compliance time unless it has already been accomplished prior to that time.
units.action_summary: Perform each action required by this AD within the specified compliance times unless already done.

units.obligation_text: For a hoist without the number "4" as the first digit of its serial number (S/N), before further flight:
units.action_summary: For hoists whose S/N does not begin with '4', comply with the required replacement actions before further flight (per monitoring method).

units.obligation_text: For hoists that use operating hours to monitor hoist operation, within 12 months after the effective date of this AD or before the hoist accumulates 55 hoist operating hours, whichever occurs first, replace the hoist.
units.action_summary: Replace hoists monitored by operating hours within 12 months or before 55 hoist operating hours, whichever comes first.

units.obligation_text: For hoists that use hoist cycles (cycles) to monitor hoist operation, within 12 months after the effective date of this AD or before the hoist accumulates 1,200 cycles, whichever occurs first, replace the hoist.
units.action_summary: Replace hoists monitored by cycles within 12 months or before 1,200 cycles, whichever comes first.

units.obligation_text: For hoists that use hoist lifts (lifts) to monitor hoist operation, within 12 months after the effective date of this AD or before the hoist accumulates 1,600 lifts, whichever occurs first, replace the hoist.
units.action_summary: Replace hoists monitored by lifts within 12 months or before 1,600 lifts, whichever comes first.

units.obligation_text: For all hoists identified in the introductory text of paragraph (a) of this AD, before further flight, install placards and revise the existing Rotorcraft Flight Manual (RFM) for your helicopter by inserting a copy of this AD or by making pen-and-ink changes in Section 2, Limitations, of the RFM Supplement for the hoist as follows:
units.action_summary: Before further flight, install required placards and revise the RFM Section 2 Limitations by inserting this AD or pen-and-ink changes.

units.obligation_text: For 500 pound (lb) rated hoists, install a placard with the information in Figure 1 to paragraph (e)(2)(i) of this AD in full view of the hoist operator and add the information in Figure 1 to paragraph (e)(2)(i) of this AD to the existing RFM for your helicopter.
units.action_summary: For 500 lb hoists, install the Figure 1 placard in full view of the hoist operator and add Figure 1 info to the RFM.

units.obligation_text: For 600 lb rated hoists, install a placard with the information in Figure 2 to paragraph (e)(2)(ii) of this AD in full view of the hoist operator and add the information in Figure 2 to paragraph (e)(2)(ii) of this AD to the existing RFM for your helicopter.
units.action_summary: For 600 lb hoists, install the Figure 2 placard in full view of the hoist operator and add Figure 2 info to the RFM.

units.obligation_text: For 500 and 600 lb rated hoists, install a placard with the information in Figure 3 to paragraph (e)(2)(iii) of this AD in full view of the pilot and add the information in Figure 3 to paragraph (e)(2)(iii) of this AD to the existing RFM for your helicopter.
units.action_summary: For 500 and 600 lb hoists, install the Figure 3 placard in full view of the pilot and add Figure 3 info to the RFM.

units.obligation_text: For 500 and 600 lb rated hoists, install a placard with the information in Figure 4 to paragraph (e)(2)(iv) of this AD in full view of the pilot and add the information in Figure 4 to paragraph (e)(2)(iv) of this AD to the existing RFM for your helicopter.
units.action_summary: For 500 and 600 lb hoists, install the Figure 4 placard in full view of the pilot and add Figure 4 info to the RFM.

units.obligation_text: For all hoists identified in the introductory text of paragraph (a) of this AD, as of the effective date of this AD, if a partial peel out occurs, deactivate or remove the hoist from service before further flight.
units.action_summary: If a partial peel out (20 inches or more reels off in one overload clutch slip incident) occurs, deactivate or remove the hoist from service before further flight.

units.obligation_text: For all hoists identified in the introductory text of paragraph (a) of this AD, within 30 days after the effective date of this AD, review the helicopter’s hoist slip load test records.
units.action_summary: Within 30 days of the effective date, review the helicopter's hoist slip load test records.

units.obligation_text: If the cable was load-tested at more than 1,500 lbs or at an unknown weight during one or more cable pulls, replace the cable with an airworthy cable before the next hoist operation.
units.action_summary: If records show cable was load-tested >1,500 lbs or unknown weight, replace the cable with an airworthy cable before next hoist operation.

units.obligation_text: For all hoists identified in the introductory text of paragraph (a) of this AD, within 30 days after the effective date of this AD, and thereafter at intervals not to exceed 6 months, 400 lifts, or 300 cycles, whichever occurs first:
units.action_summary: Within 30 days and then at intervals not to exceed 6 months, 400 lifts, or 300 cycles, perform the specified inspections and tests.

units.obligation_text: Visually inspect the first 18 inches (45 cm) of the cable from the hook assembly for broken wires and necked down sections.
units.action_summary: Visually inspect first 18 inches of cable from hook for broken wires and necked down sections at the specified intervals.

units.obligation_text: If there is a broken wire or necked down section, replace the cable with an airworthy cable before further flight.
units.action_summary: If inspection finds broken wire or necked down section, replace cable with an airworthy cable before further flight.

units.obligation_text: Within the first 18 inches (45 cm) of the cable from the hook assembly, measure the diameter of the cable at the most necked down area.
units.action_summary: Measure cable diameter at the most necked-down area within first 18 inches of the cable.

units.obligation_text: If the diameter measurement is less than 0.185 inch (4.7 mm), replace the cable with an airworthy cable before further flight.
units.action_summary: If measured diameter is <0.185 inch (4.7 mm), replace the cable with an airworthy cable before further flight.

units.obligation_text: Using load check tool P/N 49900–889–104, perform a cable conditioning and a hoist slip load test by following the Accomplishment Instructions, paragraphs 3.C.(1) through 3.C.(3)(g) of ASB 44301–10–18 Rev 6.
units.action_summary: Using specified load check tool, perform cable conditioning and hoist slip load test per ASB instructions.

units.obligation_text: If the average of the five test values is less than the limit shown in Table 2 for 600 lb rated hoists or Table 3 for 500 lb rated hoists of ASB 44301–10–18 Rev 6, remove the hoist from service before further flight.
units.action_summary: If average of five load test values is below the specified table limit, remove the hoist from service before further flight.

units.obligation_text: Visually inspect the first 30 feet (10 meters) of the cable from the hook assembly for broken wires, necked down sections, kinks, bird-caging, flattened areas, abrasion, and gouging.
units.action_summary: Visually inspect first 30 feet of cable from hook for a list of defects at the specified intervals.

units.obligation_text: If there is a broken wire, necked down section, kink, or any bird-caging; or if there is a flattened area, any abrasion, or a gouge that exceeds allowable limits, replace the cable with an airworthy cable before further flight.
units.action_summary: If specified defects are found exceeding allowable limits, replace the cable with an airworthy cable before further flight.

units.obligation_text: Repeat the actions specified in paragraphs (e)(5)(i) and (ii) of this AD.
units.action_summary: Repeat the inspections in (e)(5)(i) (visual) and (e)(5)(ii) (diameter measurement) at the specified intervals.

units.obligation_text: If there is a broken wire or necked down section or the cable diameter measurement is less than 0.185 inch (4.7 mm), replace the cable with an airworthy cable before further flight.
units.action_summary: If after repeating inspections a broken wire, necked down section, or diameter <0.185 inch is found, replace the cable before further flight.

units.obligation_text: Within 30 days after accomplishing the hoist slip load test, report the information requested in Appendix 1 to this AD by email to ASB.SIS-CA@utas.utc.com; or mail to Goodrich, Collins Aerospace; 2727 E. Imperial Hwy., Brea, CA 92821.
units.action_summary: Within 30 days after completing the hoist slip load test, report the requested information by email or mail to Goodrich at the specified addresses.

units.obligation_text: Provide the following information by email to ASB.SIS-CA@utas.utc.com; or mail to Goodrich, Collins Aerospace; 2727 E. Imperial Hwy., Brea, CA 92821. [Helicopter Owner/Operator Name; Email Address; Telephone Number; Helicopter Model and Serial Number; Hoist Part Number; Hoist Serial Number; Time since Last Hoist Overhaul (months); Hoist Operating Hours; Hoist Cycles; Hoist Lifts; Date and Location Test was Accomplished; Point of Contact for Additional Information; Air Temperature; Gearbox Lubricant; Hoist Slip Load Test Value 1-5; Hoist Slip Load Test Averaged Test Value; Any notes or comments:]
units.action_summary: Provide the specified information fields in the Appendix to Goodrich by email or mail as the hoist slip load test report.

units.obligation_text: As of the effective date of this AD, do not install as a replacement part or as an original installation an externally-mounted hoist with a P/N identified in the introductory text of paragraph (a) of this AD unless it has an improved overload clutch assembly with the number "4" as the first digit of the S/N.
units.action_summary: Do not install affected externally-mounted hoists as replacement or original installation unless the hoist has an improved overload clutch assembly with S/N starting with '4'.

units.obligation_text: Unless it has an improved overload clutch assembly with the number "4" as the first digit of the S/N.
units.action_summary: Installation is permitted if the hoist has the improved overload clutch assembly with S/N starting with '4'.

units.obligation_text: A federal agency may not conduct or sponsor ... a collection of information subject to the requirements of the Paperwork Reduction Act unless that collection of information displays a currently valid OMB Control Number.
units.action_summary: Federal agencies are prohibited from conducting or sponsoring a PRA-covered information collection unless it displays a valid OMB Control Number.

units.obligation_text: A person is not required to respond to a collection of information subject to the requirements of the Paperwork Reduction Act unless that collection of information displays a currently valid OMB Control Number.
units.action_summary: Persons are not required to respond to PRA-covered collections unless the collection displays a valid OMB Control Number.

units.obligation_text: Nor shall a person be subject to a penalty for failure to comply with a collection of information subject to the requirements of the Paperwork Reduction Act unless that collection of information displays a currently valid OMB Control Number.
units.action_summary: Persons shall not be penalized for failure to comply with a PRA-covered collection unless it displays a valid OMB Control Number.

units.obligation_text: All responses to this collection of information are mandatory.
units.action_summary: Responses to the specified collection of information are mandatory (subject to the PRA/OMB requirements described).

units.obligation_text: Send comments regarding this burden estimate or any other aspect of this collection of information, including suggestions for reducing this burden to: Information Collection Clearance Officer, Federal Aviation Administration, 10101 Hillwood Parkway, Fort Worth, TX 76177–1524.
units.action_summary: Send comments about the burden estimate or the collection to the Information Collection Clearance Officer at the specified address.

units.obligation_text: The Manager, International Validation Branch, FAA, may approve AMOCs for this AD.
units.actor: The Manager, International Validation Branch, FAA
units.action_summary: The Manager has authority to approve alternative methods of compliance (AMOCs) for this AD.

units.obligation_text: Send your proposal to: Kristi Bradley, Aerospace Engineer, General Aviation & Rotorcraft Section, International Validation Branch, FAA, 10101 Hillwood Pkwy., Fort Worth, TX 76177; telephone 817–222–5110; email kristin.bradley@faa.gov.
units.action_summary: Submit AMOC proposals to the specified FAA contact (Kristi Bradley) via the provided address/telephone/email.
units.modal_raw: Send (is required to for AMOC proposals)

units.obligation_text: For operations conducted under a 14 CFR part 119 operating certificate or under 14 CFR part 91, subpart K, the FAA suggests that you notify your principal inspector, or lacking a principal inspector, the manager of the local flight standards district office or certificate holding district office before operating any aircraft complying with this AD through an AMOC.
units.actor: You (operators conducting operations under part 119 or part 91, subpart K)
units.action_summary: It is suggested that operators notify their principal inspector or local FSDO/CHDO manager before operating any aircraft under this AD using an AMOC.

title: Safety Management System for Certificated Airports

units.obligation_text: The FAA must receive comments on this airworthiness directive (AD) by October 8, 2021.
units.action_summary: Receive comments on this AD by October 8, 2021.

units.obligation_text: This AD applies to all General Electric Company (GE) CF34–10E2A1, CF34–10E5, CF34–10E5A1, CF34–10E6, CF34–10E6A1, CF34–10E7, and CF34–10E7–B model turbofan engines with a stationary oil seal, part number (P/N) B1316–00453 or P/N B1316–01274, installed at the No.1 forward bearing, that has used high thermal stability (HTS) oil or high performance capability (HPC) oil for 56 or more flight hours (FHs) during the life of the stationary oil seal.
units.action_summary: Specifies the engines and seals to which this AD applies (scope of applicability).

units.obligation_text: Comply with this AD within the compliance times specified, unless already done.
units.actor: those subject to this AD (owners/operators/maintenance personnel)
units.action_summary: Must comply with the AD within the specified compliance times unless already complied with.

units.obligation_text: Within the compliance time specified in paragraph (g)(1)(i) or (ii) of this AD, as applicable, perform an initial visual inspection of the strainer assembly screen for Teflon material.
units.action_summary: Perform an initial visual inspection of the strainer assembly screen for Teflon within the applicable compliance time.

units.obligation_text: For an affected stationary oil seal having fewer than 2,250 flight hours (FHs) since new on the effective date of this AD, perform the initial inspection of the strainer assembly screen at the next engine shop visit after accumulating 2,250 FHs since new, but no later than 2,350 FHs since new.
units.action_summary: If seal has <2,250 FHs on effective date, inspect at next shop visit after reaching 2,250 FHs but no later than 2,350 FHs since new.

units.obligation_text: For an affected stationary oil seal having 2,250 or more FHs since new on the effective date of this AD, perform the initial inspection of the strainer assembly screen within 100 FHs after the effective date of this AD.
units.action_summary: If seal has ≥2,250 FHs on effective date, perform initial inspection within 100 flight hours after the effective date.

units.obligation_text: Thereafter, within the following compliance times, repeat the visual inspection of the strainer assembly screen required by paragraph (g)(1) of this AD:
units.action_summary: After the initial inspection, repeat the visual inspection at the intervals specified below.

units.obligation_text: For an affected stationary oil seal having 2,250 to 7,000 FHs since new at the time of the last inspection, repeat the visual inspection every 750 FHs.
units.action_summary: If seal has 2,250–7,000 FHs at last inspection, repeat inspection every 750 flight hours.

units.obligation_text: For an affected stationary oil seal having 7,001 to 10,000 FHs since new at the time of the last inspection, repeat the visual inspection every 375 FHs.
units.action_summary: If seal has 7,001–10,000 FHs at last inspection, repeat inspection every 375 flight hours.

units.obligation_text: For an affected stationary oil seal having more than 10,000 FHs since new at the time of the last inspection, repeat the visual inspection every 100 FHs.
units.action_summary: If seal has >10,000 FHs at last inspection, repeat inspection every 100 flight hours.

units.obligation_text: If, based on the inspections required by paragraph (g)(1) or (2) of this AD, Teflon material is found in the strainer assembly screen, before further flight, remove the stationary oil seal at the No. 1 forward bearing from service and replace it with a part eligible for installation.
units.action_summary: If Teflon material is found, remove the stationary oil seal from service and replace it with an eligible part before further flight.
units.modal_raw: remove and replace (must, before further flight)

units.obligation_text: Before an affected stationary oil seal accumulates 10,000 FHs since new or within 500 FHs after the effective date of this AD, whichever occurs later, remove the stationary oil seal at the No. 1 forward bearing from service and replace it with a part eligible for installation.
units.action_summary: Remove and replace the stationary oil seal before it reaches 10,000 FHs since new or within 500 FHs after the AD effective date, whichever is later.

units.obligation_text: Removal of the stationary oil seal, P/N B1316–00453 or P/N B1316–01274, installed at the No. 1 forward bearing, and replacement with a part eligible for installation, constitutes terminating action for the initial and repetitive inspections required by paragraphs (g)(1) and (2) of this AD.
units.action_summary: Removing and replacing the specified stationary oil seal ends the obligation to perform the inspections in paragraphs (g)(1) and (g)(2).

units.obligation_text: Special flight permits, as described in 14 CFR 21.197 and 21.199, are subject to the requirements of paragraph (j)(1) of this AD.
units.action_summary: Special flight permits must comply with the requirements in paragraph (j)(1) of this AD.

units.obligation_text: Operators who are prohibited from further flight due to Teflon material found in the strainer assembly screen may perform a non-revenue ferry flight, consisting of no more than five cycles, to a location where the engine can be removed from service if operators perform the actions in Appendix—A, paragraph 4.A., GE CF34–10E Service Bulletin (SB) 72–0365 R04, dated April 27, 2021 and the engine still meets the criteria in paragraph 4.A. for flying an additional five cycles.
units.actor: operators prohibited from further flight due to Teflon material
units.action_summary: Permits such operators to perform a non-revenue ferry flight of up to five cycles to a location for engine removal if they perform specified service bulletin actions and the engine meets the criteria for five additional cycles.

units.obligation_text: This ferry flight must be performed with only essential flight crew, without passengers, and involve non-ETOPS operations.
units.action_summary: The ferry flight is required to have only essential flight crew, carry no passengers, and be conducted as non-ETOPS operations.

units.obligation_text: This ferry flight must be performed ... without passengers.
units.action_summary: Prohibits carrying passengers on the permitted ferry flight.

units.obligation_text: This ferry flight must ... involve non-ETOPS operations.
units.action_summary: Requires the ferry flight to be conducted as non-ETOPS operations.

units.obligation_text: The Manager, ECO Branch, FAA, has the authority to approve AMOCs for this AD, if requested using the procedures found in 14 CFR 39.19.
units.action_summary: Manager may approve alternative methods of compliance (AMOCs) for this AD if requests use the procedures in 14 CFR 39.19.

units.obligation_text: In accordance with 14 CFR 39.19, send your request to your principal inspector or local Flight Standards District Office, as appropriate.
units.action_summary: Requests for AMOCs must be sent to the requester's principal inspector or local FSDO as appropriate.

units.obligation_text: If sending information directly to the manager of the certification office, send it to the attention of the person identified in Related Information.
units.actor: persons sending information directly to the certification office manager
units.action_summary: If sending AMOC information directly to the certification office manager, address it to the person named in Related Information.

units.obligation_text: You may email your request to ANE-AD-AMOC@faa.gov.
units.action_summary: Permits requesters to email their AMOC requests to the specified FAA email address.

units.obligation_text: Before using any approved AMOC, notify your appropriate principal inspector, or lacking a principal inspector, the manager of the local flight standards district office/certificate holding district office.
units.action_summary: Before using an approved AMOC, notify the appropriate principal inspector or, if none, the manager of the local FSDO/CHDO.

title: Airworthiness Directives: CFM International, S.A. Turbofan Engines

units.obligation_text: The FAA must receive comments on this airworthiness directive (AD) by May 7, 2021.
units.action_summary: FAA must receive comments on this AD by May 7, 2021.

units.obligation_text: Comply with this AD within the compliance times specified, unless already done.
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must comply with this AD within the specified compliance times unless already done.

units.obligation_text: For all affected CFM CFM56–5B and CFM56–7B model turbofan engines:
units.action_summary: Owners/operators of affected CFM56–5B and CFM56–7B engines must follow the removal and replacement actions specified in paragraphs (g)(1)(i)–(iii).

units.obligation_text: If, on July 5, 2019 (the effective date of AD 2019–12–05), the rotating air HPT front seal has 7,000 cycles or greater since being reconfigured, remove the part from service within 50 cycles after July 5, 2019 (the effective date of AD 2019–12–05), or before further flight, whichever occurs later, and replace with a part eligible for installation.
units.action_summary: If the seal had ≥7,000 cycles since reconfiguration on July 5, 2019, remove it within 50 cycles after July 5, 2019 or before further flight (whichever is later) and replace with an eligible part.

units.obligation_text: If, on July 5, 2019 (the effective date of AD 2019–12–05), the rotating air HPT front seal has between 6,001 and 6,999 cycles, inclusive, since being reconfigured, remove the part from service within 500 cycles after July 5, 2019 (the effective date of AD 2019–12–05), but not to exceed 7,050 cycles since being reconfigured, or before further flight, whichever occurs later, and replace with a part eligible for installation.
units.action_summary: If the seal had 6,001–6,999 cycles since reconfiguration on July 5, 2019, remove it within 500 cycles after July 5, 2019 (but before 7,050 total cycles) or before further flight (whichever is later) and replace with an eligible part.

units.obligation_text: For all remaining CFM56–5B and CFM56–7B model turbofan engines, remove the rotating air HPT front seal from service before accumulating 6,500 cycles since being reconfigured, or within 50 cycles after the effective date of this AD, whichever occurs later.
units.action_summary: For remaining affected CFM56–5B and –7B engines, remove the seal before it reaches 6,500 cycles since reconfiguration or within 50 cycles after this AD's effective date, whichever is later.

units.obligation_text: For all affected CFM CFM56–5C model turbofan engines:
units.action_summary: Owners/operators of affected CFM56–5C engines must follow the removal and replacement actions specified in paragraphs (g)(2)(i)–(iii).

units.obligation_text: If, on July 5, 2019 (the effective date of AD 2019–12–05), the rotating air HPT front seal has 4,250 cycles or greater since being reconfigured, remove the part from service within 25 cycles after July 5, 2019 (the effective date of AD 2019–12–05), within 1,500 cycles since the last fluorescent penetrant inspection (FPI) of the rotating air HPT front seal, or before further flight after the effective date of this AD, whichever occurs later, and replace with a part eligible for installation.
units.action_summary: If the seal had ≥4,250 cycles since reconfiguration on July 5, 2019, remove it within 25 cycles after July 5, 2019, within 1,500 cycles since last FPI, or before further flight after this AD's effective date (whichever is later) and replace with an eligible part.

units.obligation_text: If, on July 5, 2019 (the effective date of AD 2019–12–05), the rotating air HPT front seal has between 3,751 and 4,249 cycles, inclusive, since being reconfigured, remove the part from service within 250 cycles after July 5, 2019 (the effective date of AD 2019–12–05), before accumulating 4,275 cycles since being reconfigured, within 1,500 cycles since the last FPI of the rotating air HPT front seal, or before further flight after the effective date of this AD, whichever occurs later, and replace with a part eligible for installation.
units.action_summary: If the seal had 3,751–4,249 cycles since reconfiguration on July 5, 2019, remove it within 250 cycles after July 5, 2019 (and before 4,275 total cycles), within 1,500 cycles since last FPI, or before further flight after this AD's effective date (whichever is later) and replace with an eligible part.

units.obligation_text: For all remaining CFM CFM56–5C model turbofan engines, remove the rotating air HPT front seal from service before accumulating 4,000 cycles since being reconfigured, or within 50 cycles after the effective date of this AD, whichever occurs later.
units.action_summary: For remaining affected CFM56–5C engines, remove the seal before it reaches 4,000 cycles since reconfiguration or within 50 cycles after this AD's effective date, whichever is later.

units.obligation_text: For CFM56–5B or CFM56–7B model turbofan engines with an affected rotating air HPT front seal that has been operated in a CFM56–5C model turbofan engine since being reconfigured, remove the rotating air HPT front seal from service using the cycle limits in paragraph (g)(2) of this AD.
units.action_summary: If a seal originally for a CFM56–5B/–7B has been operated in a CFM56–5C since reconfiguration, remove it according to the cycle limits specified in paragraph (g)(2).

units.obligation_text: After the effective date of this AD, do not assemble any rotating air HPT front seal with greater than 0 cycles since new, having a S/N listed in paragraph (c) of this AD onto a HPT disk unless it is the same S/N HPT disk on which it has previously been assembled.
units.action_summary: Prohibits assembling listed rotating air HPT front seals (with >0 cycles since new) onto an HPT disk unless it's the same serial-numbered HPT disk previously used.

units.obligation_text: unless it is the same S/N HPT disk on which it has previously been assembled.
units.action_summary: Exception permitting assembly only if the rotating air HPT front seal is installed on the same serial-numbered HPT disk on which it was previously assembled.

units.obligation_text: The Manager, ECO Branch, FAA, has the authority to approve AMOCs for this AD, if requested using the procedures found in 14 CFR 39.19.
units.action_summary: Manager of ECO Branch may approve alternative methods of compliance (AMOCs) for this AD if requested using 14 CFR 39.19 procedures.

units.obligation_text: In accordance with 14 CFR 39.19, send your request to your principal inspector or local Flight Standards District Office, as appropriate.
units.action_summary: AMOC requesters must send their request to their principal inspector or local FSDO as appropriate, following 14 CFR 39.19.

units.obligation_text: If sending information directly to the manager of the certification office, send it to the attention of the person identified in Related Information.
units.action_summary: If sending AMOC information directly to the certification office manager, direct it to the person named in Related Information.

units.obligation_text: You may email your request to: ANE-AD-AMOC@faa.gov.
units.action_summary: Requesters are permitted to email AMOC requests to the specified email address.

units.obligation_text: Before using any approved AMOC, notify your appropriate principal inspector, or lacking a principal inspector, the manager of the local flight standards district office/certificate holding district office.
units.action_summary: Before using an approved AMOC, notify the appropriate principal inspector or, if none, the manager of the local FSDO/CHDO.

title: Amendment and Establishment of Restricted Areas: Clear, AK

units.obligation_text: R–2206A Clear, AK [Amended]
units.action_summary: Establish restricted area R-2206A

units.obligation_text: Boundaries. Beginning at lat. 64°19′44″ N, long. 149°15′42″ W; to lat. 64°19′44″ N, long. 149°10′18″ W; thence south, 100 feet west of and parallel to the Alaska Railroad to lat. 64°16′17″ N, long. 149°10′14″ W; to lat. 64°16′17″ N, long. 149°15′42″ W; to the point of beginning.
units.action_summary: Define the lateral boundaries of R-2206A by listed coordinates and paths

units.obligation_text: Designated Altitudes. Surface to 8,800 feet MSL.
units.action_summary: Set vertical limits for R-2206A from the surface to 8,800 feet MSL

units.obligation_text: For T/R blade P/Ns 3G6410A00131 and 4G6410A00131, within 5 hours time-in-service (TIS) after May 3, 2012 (the effective date of AD 2011–18–52), establish a life limit of 600 hours TIS or 1,500 takeoff and landing cycles (cycles), whichever occurs first, on the affected T/R blades and update the helicopter’s historical records.
units.action_summary: Within 5 hours TIS after May 3, 2012, set and record a life limit of 600 hours TIS or 1,500 cycles for the specified T/R blades.

units.obligation_text: If a T/R blade’s total number of cycles is unknown, determine the T/R blade cycles by multiplying the T/R blade’s hours TIS by 4.
units.action_summary: If cycles are unknown, calculate cycles as hours TIS multiplied by 4.

units.obligation_text: For T/R blade P/Ns 3G6410A00131 and 4G6410A00131, thereafter following paragraph (g)(1) of this AD, remove any T/R blade from service before accumulating 600 total hours TIS or 1,500 total cycles, whichever occurs first.
units.action_summary: After establishing the life limit, remove the specified T/R blades from service before they reach 600 hours TIS or 1,500 cycles.

units.obligation_text: For T/R blade P/Ns 3G6410A00132, 3G6410A00133, 4G6410A00132, and 4G6410A00133, within 5 hours TIS after the effective date of this AD, determine the total number of cycles.
units.action_summary: Within 5 hours TIS after the AD effective date, determine the total number of cycles for the listed T/R blade part numbers.

units.obligation_text: If a T/R blade’s total number of cycles is unknown, determine the T/R blade cycles by multiplying the blade’s hours TIS by 4.
units.action_summary: If cycles are unknown for these blades, compute cycles as hours TIS × 4.

units.obligation_text: Before further flight, remove any T/R blade from service that has accumulated or exceeded its life limit as follows. Thereafter, remove any T/R blade from service before accumulating its life limit as follows:
units.action_summary: Remove from service any blade that has reached or exceeded its life limit before the next flight, and thereafter ensure removal before blades reach their life limits.

units.obligation_text: T/R blade P/Ns 3G6410A00132 and 4G6410A00132: 1,200 total hours TIS or 3,200 total cycles, whichever occurs first.
units.action_summary: These blades must be removed before they reach 1,200 hours TIS or 3,200 cycles.

units.obligation_text: T/R blade P/N 3G6410A00133: 40,000 total cycles.
units.action_summary: This blade must be removed before it reaches 40,000 total cycles.

units.obligation_text: T/R blade P/N 4G6410A00133: 4,033 total hours TIS or 40,000 cycles, whichever occurs first.
units.action_summary: This blade must be removed before it reaches 4,033 hours TIS or 40,000 cycles.

units.obligation_text: For T/R blade P/Ns 3G6410A00131 and P/N 4G6410A00131, within 25 hours TIS after the effective date of this AD, and thereafter at intervals not to exceed 25 hours TIS, visually inspect the T/R blade for a crack and damage that exceeds allowable limits.
units.action_summary: Inspect the specified blades within 25 hours TIS and then every ≤25 hours TIS for cracks or excessive damage.

units.obligation_text: If there is a crack or damage that exceeds allowable limits, before further flight, remove the T/R blade from service.
units.action_summary: If inspection finds a crack or excessive damage, remove the blade from service before the next flight.

units.obligation_text: As of the effective date of this AD, do not install on any helicopter any T/R blade P/N 3G6410A00131 or P/N 4G6410A00131, unless the actions required by paragraphs (g)(1), (2), and (4) of this AD have been accomplished.
units.action_summary: Prohibits installation of the specified blades unless the actions in (g)(1), (2), and (4) have been completed.

units.obligation_text: The FAA must receive comments on this airworthiness directive (AD) by January 3, 2022.
units.action_summary: Receive comments on this AD by January 3, 2022.

units.obligation_text: Comply with this AD within the compliance times specified, unless already done.
units.action_summary: Comply with all requirements of this AD within the specified compliance times, unless already completed.

units.obligation_text: Except as specified by paragraph (h) of this AD: At the applicable times specified in the "Compliance" paragraph of Boeing Special Attention Requirements Bulletin 757–25–0315 RB, Revision 2, dated March 17, 2021, do all applicable actions identified in, and in accordance with, the Accomplishment Instructions of Boeing Special Attention Requirements Bulletin 757–25–0315 RB, Revision 2, dated March 17, 2021.
units.action_summary: At the times specified in the referenced Boeing Requirements Bulletin, perform all applicable actions in the Bulletin's Accomplishment Instructions, except as specified in paragraph (h).

units.actor: Owners/operators following the Boeing Requirements Bulletin

units.obligation_text: The lanyard installation specified in paragraph (g) of this AD is not required on Model 757–200 airplanes modified per VT Mobile Aerospace Engineering (VT MAE) supplemental type certificates (STCs) ST03952AT and ST04242AT.
units.actor: Operators of Model 757–200 airplanes modified per VT MAE STCs ST03952AT and ST04242AT

units.obligation_text: For airplanes identified in Boeing Special Attention Requirements Bulletin 757–25–0315 RB, Revision 1, dated May 20, 2020: This paragraph provides credit for the actions specified in paragraph (g) of this AD, if those actions were performed before the effective date of this AD using Boeing Special Attention Requirements Bulletin 757–25–0315 RB, Revision 1, dated May 20, 2020.
units.action_summary: Grants credit for actions done before the effective date using Revision 1 of the Requirements Bulletin, counting those actions as compliance with paragraph (g).

units.obligation_text: As of the applicable time specified in paragraph (j)(1) or (2) of this AD, no person may install on any airplane any PSU, life vest panel, or video panel without an updated lanyard assembly installed.
units.action_summary: Prohibits installing any PSU, life vest panel, or video panel on any airplane unless it has an updated lanyard assembly, as of the applicable time specified.

units.obligation_text: For airplanes that have PSUs, life vest panels, or video panels without the updated lanyard assemblies installed as of the effective date of this AD: After modification of the airplane as required by paragraph (g) of this AD.
units.actor: Owners/operators of airplanes that, as of the effective date, have PSUs/life vest panels/video panels without updated lanyards
units.action_summary: Specifies the timing: for airplanes already having affected panels without updated lanyards at the effective date, the installation prohibition of paragraph (j) applies after the airplane has been modified as required by paragraph (g).

units.obligation_text: For airplanes that do not have PSUs, life vest panels, or video panels without the updated lanyard assemblies installed as of the effective date of this AD: As of the effective date of this AD.
units.actor: Owners/operators of airplanes that, as of the effective date, do not have affected panels without updated lanyards
units.action_summary: Specifies the timing: for airplanes that do not have affected panels without updated lanyards as of the effective date, the installation prohibition of paragraph (j) applies beginning on the effective date.
