title: Airworthiness Directives: Goodrich Externally-Mounted Hoist Assemblies

units.obligation_text: The FAA must receive comments on this airworthiness directive (AD) action by November 1, 2021.
units.action_summary: FAA must receive comments on this AD by Nov 1, 2021.

units.obligation_text: This AD applies to helicopters, certificated in any category, with an externally mounted Goodrich hoist assembly (hoist) with a part number (P/N) or base P/N listed under the Hoist Family column in Table 1 of Goodrich Alert Service Bulletin No. 44301–10–18, Revision 6, dated October 10, 2016 (ASB 44301–10–18 Rev 6), installed.
units.actor: helicopters certificated in any category / their owners/operators
units.action_summary: Specifies the helicopters/hoists to which the AD applies (scope).

units.obligation_text: Comply with this AD within the compliance times specified, unless already done.
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must comply with the AD within the specified times unless previously accomplished.

units.obligation_text: For a hoist without the number "4" as the first digit of its serial number (S/N):
units.actor: owners/operators of hoists without '4' as first S/N digit
units.action_summary: Condition limiting the following required replacement actions to hoists whose serial number does not begin with '4'.

units.obligation_text: For hoists that use operating hours to monitor hoist operation, within 12 months after the effective date of this AD or before the hoist accumulates 55 total hoist operating hours, whichever occurs first, replace the hoist.
units.actor: owners/operators of hoists that monitor by operating hours
units.action_summary: Replace hoists monitored by operating hours within 12 months or before 55 total hoist operating hours, whichever occurs first.

units.obligation_text: For purposes of this AD, hoist operating hours are counted anytime the hoist motor is operating.
units.actor: owners/operators (definition applies to counting operating hours)
units.action_summary: Specifies how to count hoist operating hours (any time the hoist motor is operating).

units.obligation_text: For hoists that use hoist cycles (cycles) to monitor hoist operation, within 12 months after the effective date of this AD or before the hoist accumulates 1,200 total cycles, whichever occurs first, replace the hoist.
units.actor: owners/operators of hoists that monitor by cycles
units.action_summary: Replace hoists monitored by cycles within 12 months or before 1,200 total cycles, whichever occurs first.

units.obligation_text: For purposes of this AD, a cycle is counted anytime the cable is extended and then retracted a minimum of 16 feet (5 meters) during flight or on the ground, with or without a load.
units.action_summary: Defines a hoist cycle for counting purposes (extend and retract a minimum of 16 feet).

units.obligation_text: For hoists that use hoist lifts (lifts) to monitor hoist operation, within 12 months after the effective date of this AD or before the hoist accumulates 1,600 total lifts, whichever occurs first, replace the hoist.
units.actor: owners/operators of hoists that monitor by lifts
units.action_summary: Replace hoists monitored by lifts within 12 months or before 1,600 total lifts, whichever occurs first.

units.obligation_text: For purposes of this AD, a lift is counted anytime the cable is unreeled or recovered or both with a load attached to the hook, regardless of the length of the cable that is deployed or recovered. An unreeling or recovery of the cable with no load on the hook is not a lift. If a load is applied for half an operation (i.e. unreeling or recovery), it must be counted as one lift.
units.action_summary: Defines a hoist lift for counting purposes and clarifies what counts as a lift.

units.obligation_text: For all hoists identified in the introductory text of paragraph (c) of this AD, before further flight, install placards and revise the existing Rotorcraft Flight Manual (RFM) for your helicopter by inserting a copy of this AD or by making pen-and-ink changes in Section 2, Limitations, of the RFM Supplement for the hoist as follows:
units.action_summary: Before further flight, install specified placards and revise the RFM (Section 2, Limitations) by inserting this AD or making pen-and-ink changes.

units.obligation_text: For 500 pound (lb) rated hoists, install a placard with the information in Figure 1 to paragraph (g)(2)(i) of this AD in full view of the hoist operator and add the information in Figure 1 to paragraph (g)(2)(i) of this AD to the existing RFM for your helicopter.
units.actor: owners/operators of helicopters with 500 lb rated hoists
units.action_summary: Install the Figure 1 placard in view of the hoist operator and add Figure 1 information to the RFM for 500 lb rated hoists.

units.obligation_text: For 600 lb rated hoists, install a placard with the information in Figure 2 to paragraph (g)(2)(ii) of this AD in full view of the hoist operator and add the information in Figure 2 to paragraph (g)(2)(ii) of this AD to the existing RFM for your helicopter.
units.actor: owners/operators of helicopters with 600 lb rated hoists
units.action_summary: Install the Figure 2 placard in view of the hoist operator and add Figure 2 information to the RFM for 600 lb rated hoists.

units.obligation_text: For 500 and 600 lb rated hoists, install a placard with the information in Figure 3 to paragraph (g)(2)(iii) of this AD in full view of the pilot and add the information in Figure 3 to paragraph (g)(2)(iii) of this AD to the existing RFM for your helicopter.
units.actor: owners/operators of helicopters with 500 and 600 lb rated hoists
units.action_summary: Install the Figure 3 placard in view of the pilot and add Figure 3 information to the RFM for 500 and 600 lb hoists.

units.obligation_text: For 500 and 600 lb rated hoists, install a placard with the information in Figure 4 to paragraph (g)(2)(iv) of this AD in full view of the pilot and add the information in Figure 4 to paragraph (g)(2)(iv) of this AD to the existing RFM for your helicopter.
units.actor: owners/operators of helicopters with 500 and 600 lb rated hoists
units.action_summary: Install the Figure 4 placard in view of the pilot and add Figure 4 information to the RFM for 500 and 600 lb hoists.

units.obligation_text: For all hoists identified in the introductory text of paragraph (c) of this AD, as of the effective date of this AD, if a partial peel out occurs, deactivate or remove the hoist from service before further flight.
units.action_summary: If a partial peel out occurs, deactivate or remove the hoist from service before further flight.

units.obligation_text: For purposes of this AD, a partial peel out occurs when 20 inches (0.5 meter) or more of the hoist cable reels off of the hoist cable drum in one overload clutch slip incident.
units.actor: owners/operators (definition applies to identifying a partial peel out)
units.action_summary: Defines what constitutes a partial peel out (20 inches or more of cable reels off in one overload clutch slip).

units.obligation_text: For all hoists identified in the introductory text of paragraph (c) of this AD, within 30 days after the effective date of this AD, review the helicopter’s hoist slip load test records.
units.action_summary: Within 30 days of the AD's effective date, review the hoist slip load test records.

units.obligation_text: If the cable was load-tested at more than 1,500 lbs or at an unknown weight during one or more cable pulls, replace the cable with an airworthy cable before the next hoist operation.
units.actor: owners/operators whose records show >1,500 lbs or unknown test weight
units.action_summary: If prior tests were >1,500 lbs or unknown weight, replace the cable with an airworthy cable before next hoist operation.

units.obligation_text: For all hoists identified in the introductory text of paragraph (c) of this AD, within 30 days after the effective date of this AD, unless already done within the last 6 calendar months, and thereafter at intervals not to exceed 6 months, 400 lifts, or 300 cycles, whichever occurs first:
units.action_summary: Require inspections and tests within 30 days unless done within last 6 months, and thereafter at intervals not exceeding 6 months, 400 lifts, or 300 cycles (whichever occurs first).

units.obligation_text: Visually inspect the first 18 inches (45 cm) of the cable from the hook assembly for broken wires and necked down sections.
units.action_summary: Visually inspect first 18 inches of cable from hook for broken wires and necked down sections at required intervals.

units.obligation_text: If there is a broken wire or necked down section, replace the cable with an airworthy cable before further flight.
units.actor: owners/operators who find broken wire or necked down section
units.action_summary: If inspection finds broken wire or necked down section, replace cable before further flight.

units.obligation_text: Within the first 18 inches (45 cm) of the cable from the hook assembly, measure the diameter of the cable at the most necked down area.
units.action_summary: Measure cable diameter at most necked down area within first 18 inches of cable during inspection intervals.

units.obligation_text: If the diameter measurement is less than 0.185 inch (4.7 mm), replace the cable with an airworthy cable before further flight.
units.actor: owners/operators who find cable diameter < 0.185 inch
units.action_summary: If measured diameter is less than 0.185 inch, replace cable before further flight.

units.obligation_text: Using load check tool P/N 49900–889–103 or 49900–889–104, perform a cable conditioning and a hoist slip load test by following the Accomplishment Instructions, paragraphs 3.C.(1) through 3.C.(3)(g) of ASB 44301–10–18 Rev 6.
units.action_summary: Perform cable conditioning and hoist slip load test using specified tools and ASB procedures.

units.obligation_text: If the average of the five test values is less than the limit shown in Table 2 for 600 lb rated hoists or Table 3 for 500 lb rated hoists of ASB 44301–10–18 Rev 6, remove the hoist from service before further flight.
units.action_summary: If average of five test values is below the specified limit, remove the hoist from service before further flight.

units.obligation_text: Visually inspect the first 30 feet (10 meters) of the cable from the hook assembly for broken wires, necked down sections, kinks, bird-caging, flattened areas, abrasion, and gouging. It is permissible for the cable to have a slight curve immediately after performing the hoist slip load test.
units.action_summary: Visually inspect first 30 feet of cable for specified defects; slight curve after test is permissible.

units.obligation_text: If there is a broken wire, necked down section, kink, or any bird-caging; or if there is a flattened area, any abrasion, or a gouge that exceeds allowable limits, replace the cable with an airworthy cable before further flight.
units.actor: owners/operators who find defects exceeding allowable limits
units.action_summary: If inspection finds defects exceeding allowable limits, replace cable before further flight.

units.obligation_text: Repeat the actions specified in paragraphs (g)(5)(i) and (ii) of this AD.
units.action_summary: Repeat the inspections and diameter measurement actions described in (g)(5)(i) and (g)(5)(ii) at the required intervals.

units.obligation_text: If there is a broken wire or necked down section or the cable diameter measurement is less than 0.185 inch (4.7 mm), replace the cable with an airworthy cable before further flight.
units.action_summary: On repeating inspections, if broken wire, necked down section, or diameter <0.185 inch, replace cable before further flight.

units.obligation_text: Within 30 days after accomplishing the hoist slip load test, report the information requested in Appendix 1 to this AD by email to ASB.SIS-CA@utas.utc.com; or mail to Goodrich, Collins Aerospace; 2727 E Imperial Hwy., Brea, CA 92821.
units.actor: owners/operators who accomplish the hoist slip load test
units.action_summary: Within 30 days after the load test, report specified information in Appendix 1 by email or mail to Goodrich/Collins Aerospace.

units.obligation_text: Provide the following information by email to ASB.SIS-CA@utas.utc.com; or mail to Goodrich, Collins Aerospace; 2727 E Imperial Hwy., Brea, CA 92821: Helicopter Owner/Operator Name; Email Address; Telephone Number; Helicopter Model and Serial Number; Hoist Part Number; Hoist Serial Number; Time since Last Hoist Overhaul (months); Hoist Operating Hours; Hoist Cycles; Hoist Lifts; Date and Location Test was Accomplished; Point of Contact for Additional Information; Air Temperature; Gearbox Lubricant; Hoist Slip Load Test Value 1-5; Hoist Slip Load Test Averaged Test Value; Any notes or comments.
units.actor: owners/operators who must report the test
units.action_summary: Specify the data fields that must be reported to Goodrich as part of the hoist slip load test report.

units.obligation_text: As of the effective date of this AD, do not install as a replacement part or as an original installation an externally-mounted hoist with a P/N identified in the introductory text of paragraph (c) of this AD unless it has an improved overload clutch assembly with the number "4" as the first digit of the S/N.
units.action_summary: Prohibits installing affected externally-mounted hoists unless they have an improved overload clutch assembly whose serial number begins with '4'.

units.obligation_text: The Manager, International Validation Branch, FAA, has the authority to approve AMOCs for this AD, if requested using the procedures found in 14 CFR 39.19.
units.action_summary: Grants the Manager authority to approve alternative methods of compliance (AMOCs) for this AD, when requested per 14 CFR 39.19 procedures.

units.obligation_text: In accordance with 14 CFR 39.19, send your request to your principal inspector or local Flight Standards District Office, as appropriate.
units.action_summary: AMOC requests must be sent to the principal inspector or local FSDO per 14 CFR 39.19.

units.obligation_text: If sending information directly to the manager of the International Validation Branch, send it to the attention of the person identified in paragraph (i)(1) of this AD.
units.actor: requesters who send AMOC info directly to the manager
units.action_summary: If sending AMOC information directly to the manager, address it to the person identified in paragraph (i)(1).

units.obligation_text: Information may be emailed to: 9-AVS-AIR-730-AMOC@faa.gov.
units.action_summary: Allows AMOC requests/information to be emailed to the specified FAA address.

units.obligation_text: Before using any approved AMOC, notify your appropriate principal inspector, or lacking a principal inspector, the manager of the local flight standards district office/certificate holding district office.
units.action_summary: Before using an approved AMOC, notify the appropriate principal inspector or, if none, the manager of the local FSDO/CHDO.

title: Airworthiness Directives: TheBoeing Company Airplanes

units.obligation_text: The FAA must receive comments on this airworthiness directive (AD) by March 8, 2021.
units.action_summary: FAA must receive comments on the AD by March 8, 2021.

units.obligation_text: Comply with this AD within the compliance times specified, unless already done.
units.action_summary: Operators must comply with the AD within the specified compliance times unless already done.

units.obligation_text: Before the affected HPT stage 1 disk exceeds 2,840 flight cycles (FCs) since new, or within 60 days after the effective date of this AD, whichever occurs later, but not to exceed 8 years after the effective date of this AD if using FCs, remove the affected HPT stage 1 disk from service and replace with a part eligible for installation.
units.action_summary: Remove affected HPT stage 1 disk and replace it with a part eligible for installation within the specified flight-cycle/time limits.

units.obligation_text: Before the affected HPT stage 1 disk exceeds 2,840 flight cycles (FCs) since new, ... remove the affected HPT stage 1 disk from service and replace with a part eligible for installation.
units.action_summary: Time threshold: action must be done before disk exceeds 2,840 flight cycles since new.

units.section: Rolls-Royce AD (g) Required Actions — alternative time
units.obligation_text: Within 60 days after the effective date of this AD, whichever occurs later, ... remove the affected HPT stage 1 disk from service and replace with a part eligible for installation.
units.action_summary: Alternative time: action must be done within 60 days after the AD's effective date if that is later than the flight-cycle threshold.

units.obligation_text: But not to exceed 8 years after the effective date of this AD if using FCs, remove the affected HPT stage 1 disk from service and replace with a part eligible for installation.
units.action_summary: Limit: if using flight cycles to determine compliance, removal/replacement must not exceed 8 years after the AD's effective date.

units.obligation_text: After the effective date of this AD, do not install any affected HPT stage 1 disk onto any engine.
units.action_summary: Prohibits installation of any affected HPT stage 1 disk on any engine after the AD's effective date.

units.obligation_text: The Manager, ECO Branch, FAA, has the authority to approve AMOCs for this AD, if requested using the procedures found in 14 CFR 39.19.
units.action_summary: Manager, ECO Branch, may approve alternative methods of compliance for this AD if requested per procedures.

units.obligation_text: In accordance with 14 CFR 39.19, send your request to your principal inspector or local Flight Standards District Office, as appropriate.

units.obligation_text: If sending information directly to the manager of the certification office, send it to the attention of the person identified in Related Information.
units.actor: Person sending information directly to the manager
units.action_summary: If sending AMOC information directly to the certification office manager, direct it to the person identified in Related Information.

units.obligation_text: You may email your request to: ANE-AD-AMOC@faa.gov.
units.action_summary: Requesters are permitted to email AMOC requests to the specified FAA email address.

units.section: Rolls-Royce AD (j)(2) AMOCs — notification before use
units.obligation_text: Before using any approved AMOC, notify your appropriate principal inspector, or lacking a principal inspector, the manager of the local flight standards district office/certificate holding district office.
units.action_summary: Operators must notify their principal inspector (or the manager of the local FSDO/CHDO if no principal inspector) before using an approved AMOC.

units.obligation_text: The FAA must receive comments on this airworthiness directive (AD) action by March 8, 2021.
units.action_summary: FAA must receive comments on this AD action by March 8, 2021.

units.obligation_text: Comply with this AD within the compliance times specified, unless already done.
units.action_summary: Operators must comply with the AD within the specified compliance times unless already done.

units.section: Boeing AD (g) Determination of Modification Status
units.obligation_text: Within 27 months after the date of issuance of the original airworthiness certificate or original export certificate of airworthiness, or within 27 months after the effective date of this AD, whichever occurs later, determine whether the captain’s and first officer’s rudder pedal cover and shroud assemblies have been modified as specified in Boeing Alert Requirements Bulletin 737–27A1313 RB, Revision 1, dated June 24, 2020, or 737–27A1314 RB, Revision 1, dated June 24, 2020, as applicable, or by production equivalent.
units.action_summary: Within 27 months (or later as specified) operators must determine whether the captain's and FO's rudder pedal cover and shroud assemblies have been modified as specified in the referenced bulletins or by production equivalent.

units.section: Boeing AD (g) Determination — records review acceptable
units.obligation_text: A review of airplane maintenance records is acceptable for this requirement if the modification status can be conclusively determined from that review.
units.action_summary: Operators are permitted to determine modification status by reviewing maintenance records if that review conclusively shows the modification status.

units.obligation_text: For airplanes that have not been modified as determined by paragraph (g) of this AD: At the applicable times specified in the 'Compliance' paragraph of Boeing Alert Requirements Bulletin 737–27A1313 RB, Revision 1, dated June 24, 2020, or Boeing Alert Requirements Bulletin 737–27A1314 RB, Revision 1, dated June 24, 2020, as applicable, except as specified by paragraph (i) of this AD, do all applicable actions identified in, and in accordance with, the Accomplishment Instructions of Boeing Alert Requirements Bulletin 737–27A1313 RB, Revision 1, dated June 24, 2020, or Boeing Alert Requirements Bulletin 737–27A1314 RB, Revision 1, dated June 24, 2020, as applicable.
units.action_summary: Operators of airplanes not modified per paragraph (g) must, at the specified times, perform all applicable actions in the Accomplishment Instructions of the referenced Boeing Alert Requirements Bulletins.

units.section: Boeing AD (i) Exception to Service Information Specifications
units.obligation_text: Where Boeing Alert Requirements Bulletin 737–27A1313 RB, Revision 1, dated June 24, 2020, and Boeing Alert Requirements Bulletin 737–27A1314 RB, Revision 1, dated June 24, 2020, use the phrase 'the original issue date of' each Requirements Bulletin for compliance, this AD requires using the effective date of this AD.
units.actor: Owners/operators of affected airplanes (for compliance calculations)
units.action_summary: When the Requirements Bulletins reference 'the original issue date' for compliance, operators must instead use this AD's effective date.

units.section: Boeing AD (j) Credit for Previous Actions
units.obligation_text: This paragraph provides credit for the actions specified in paragraph (h) of this AD, if those actions were performed before the effective date of this AD using Boeing Alert Requirements Bulletin 737–27A1313 RB, dated March 18, 2020, or Boeing Alert Requirements Bulletin 737–27A1314 RB, dated March 18, 2020.
units.action_summary: Operators that performed the specified actions before the AD effective date using the earlier bulletins are credited (i.e., do not need to repeat those actions).

units.section: Boeing AD (k)(1) Parts Installation Limitation (post-effective certificates)
units.obligation_text: For airplanes with an original airworthiness certificate or original export certificate of airworthiness issued after the effective date of this AD: As of the effective date of this AD, no person may install a captain’s or first officer’s rudder pedal cover or shroud assembly on any airplane, unless the cover or shroud assembly has been modified in accordance with the requirements of paragraph (h) of this AD.
units.action_summary: Prohibits installation of captain's or FO's rudder pedal cover or shroud assemblies on any airplane as of the AD effective date unless the part has been modified per paragraph (h).

units.section: Boeing AD (k)(1) Parts Installation Limitation — exception
units.obligation_text: Unless the cover or shroud assembly has been modified in accordance with the requirements of paragraph (h) of this AD.
units.action_summary: Exception to the installation prohibition: installation is allowed only if the cover or shroud assembly has been modified per paragraph (h).

units.section: Boeing AD (k)(2) Parts Installation Limitation (pre-effective certificates)
units.obligation_text: For airplanes with an original airworthiness certificate or original export certificate of airworthiness issued prior to the effective date of this AD: After the modification required by paragraph (h) of this AD has been done, no person may install a captain’s or first officer’s rudder pedal cover or shroud assembly on any airplane, unless the cover or shroud assembly has been modified in accordance with the requirements of paragraph (h) of this AD.
units.action_summary: For airplanes certificated before the AD effective date, after the required modification has been done, installation of cover or shroud assemblies is prohibited unless the part has been modified per paragraph (h).

units.section: Boeing AD (k)(2) Parts Installation Limitation — reinstallation allowance
units.obligation_text: Reinstallation of a rudder pedal cover or shroud assembly that has not been modified in accordance with paragraph (h) of this AD but has been removed for other maintenance is allowed.
units.action_summary: Allows reinstallation of unmodified cover or shroud assemblies if they were removed for other maintenance (i.e., temporary reinstallation permitted).

units.obligation_text: The Manager, Seattle ACO Branch, FAA, has the authority to approve AMOCs for this AD, if requested using the procedures found in 14 CFR 39.19.
units.action_summary: Manager, Seattle ACO Branch may approve AMOCs for this AD if requested per 14 CFR 39.19.

units.obligation_text: In accordance with 14 CFR 39.19, send your request to your principal inspector or local Flight Standards District Office, as appropriate.
units.action_summary: Requesters must send AMOC requests to their principal inspector or local FSDO per 14 CFR 39.19.

units.obligation_text: If sending information directly to the manager of the certification office, send it to the attention of the person identified in paragraph (m)(1) of this AD.
units.actor: Person sending information directly to the manager
units.action_summary: If submitting AMOC information directly to the certification office manager, direct it to the person identified in paragraph (m)(1).

units.obligation_text: Information may be emailed to: 9-ANM-Seattle-ACO-AMOC-Requests@faa.gov.
units.action_summary: Requesters are permitted to email AMOC information to the specified Seattle ACO email address.

units.section: Boeing AD (l)(2) AMOCs — notification before use
units.obligation_text: Before using any approved AMOC, notify your appropriate principal inspector, or lacking a principal inspector, the manager of the local flight standards district office/certificate holding district office.
units.action_summary: Operators must notify their principal inspector (or local FSDO/CHDO manager if none) before using any approved AMOC.

units.section: Boeing AD (l)(3) AMOCs — use if approved by Boeing ODA
units.obligation_text: An AMOC that provides an acceptable level of safety may be used for any repair, modification, or alteration required by this AD if it is approved by The Boeing Company Organization Designation Authorization (ODA) that has been authorized by the Manager, Seattle ACO Branch, FAA, to make those findings.
units.actor: Owners/operators and The Boeing Company ODA
units.action_summary: Amendments/repairs/modifications required by the AD may be performed using an AMOC that provides acceptable safety if approved by Boeing ODA authorized by the Manager, Seattle ACO.

units.section: Boeing AD (l)(3) AMOCs — condition: ODA approval
units.obligation_text: If it is approved by The Boeing Company Organization Designation Authorization (ODA) that has been authorized by the Manager, Seattle ACO Branch, FAA, to make those findings.
units.action_summary: Condition: the AMOC must be approved by the Boeing ODA authorized by the Manager, Seattle ACO Branch.

units.section: Boeing AD (l)(3) AMOCs — condition: meet certification basis
units.obligation_text: To be approved, the repair method, modification deviation, or alteration deviation must meet the certification basis of the airplane,
units.actor: Applicants seeking AMOC approval / repair method providers
units.action_summary: Condition: the repair/modification deviation must meet the airplane's certification basis to be approved as an AMOC.

units.section: Boeing AD (l)(3) AMOCs — condition: approval reference
units.obligation_text: and the approval must specifically refer to this AD.
units.action_summary: Condition: any AMOC approval must specifically reference this AD.

units.section: Boeing AD (l)(4) AMOCs — previous approvals not accepted
units.obligation_text: AMOCs approved previously for AD 2017–14–13 are not approved as AMOCs for the corresponding provisions of this AD.
units.actor: AMOCs previously approved for AD 2017-14-13 / operators
units.action_summary: AMOCs previously approved for AD 2017-14-13 cannot be used as AMOCs for the corresponding provisions of this AD.

units.obligation_text: The steps labeled as RC, including substeps under an RC step and any figures identified in an RC step, must be done to comply with the AD.
units.action_summary: All steps labeled RC (and their substeps/figures) are mandatory to comply with the AD.

units.section: Boeing AD (l)(5)(i) RC steps — RC Exempt
units.obligation_text: If a step or substep is labeled 'RC Exempt,' then the RC requirement is removed from that step or substep.
units.action_summary: If a step/substep is labeled 'RC Exempt', the RC requirement no longer applies to that step/substep.

units.section: Boeing AD (l)(5)(i) RC steps — deviations require AMOC
units.obligation_text: An AMOC is required for any deviations to RC steps, including substeps and identified figures.
units.action_summary: Any deviation from RC-labeled steps (including their substeps/figures) requires approval via an AMOC.

units.section: Boeing AD (l)(5)(ii) Non-RC steps — permissible deviations
units.obligation_text: Steps not labeled as RC may be deviated from using accepted methods in accordance with the operator’s maintenance or inspection program without obtaining approval of an AMOC, provided the RC steps, including substeps and identified figures, can still be done as specified, and the airplane can be put back in an airworthy condition.
units.action_summary: Operators may deviate from non-RC steps using accepted methods without AMOC approval, as long as RC steps remain achievable and the airplane is returned to an airworthy condition.

units.section: Boeing AD (l)(5)(ii) Non-RC steps — condition: RC steps remain
units.obligation_text: Provided the RC steps, including substeps and identified figures, can still be done as specified,
units.action_summary: Condition: RC steps (including substeps/figures) must still be able to be performed as specified when deviating from non-RC steps.

units.section: Boeing AD (l)(5)(ii) Non-RC steps — condition: airplane airworthy
units.obligation_text: and the airplane can be put back in an airworthy condition.
units.action_summary: Condition: after deviation from non-RC steps, the airplane must be returned to an airworthy condition.

title: Airworthiness Directives: The Boeing Company Airplanes

units.actor: Owners/operators and maintenance personnel of affected airplanes

units.obligation_text: The Manager, Seattle ACO Branch, FAA, has the authority to approve AMOCs for this AD, if requested using the procedures found in 14 CFR 39.19.

units.obligation_text: In accordance with 14 CFR 39.19, send your request to your principal inspector or responsible Flight Standards Office, as appropriate.

units.obligation_text: If sending information directly to the manager of the certification office, send it to the attention of the person identified in paragraph (j)(1) of this AD.

units.obligation_text: Information may be emailed to: 9-ANM-Seattle-ACO-AMOC-Requests@faa.gov.

units.obligation_text: Before using any approved AMOC, notify your appropriate principal inspector, or lacking a principal inspector, the manager of the responsible Flight Standards Office.

units.obligation_text: An AMOC that provides an acceptable level of safety may be used for any repair, modification, or alteration required by this AD if it is approved by The Boeing Company Organization Designation Authorization (ODA) that has been authorized by the Manager, Seattle ACO Branch, FAA, to make those findings.

units.obligation_text: To be approved, the repair method, modification deviation, or alteration deviation must meet the certification basis of the airplane, and the approval must specifically refer to this AD.
units.actor: The Boeing Company Organization Designation Authorization (ODA) or approving authority
units.action_summary: Approved AMOC repair/modification/alteration methods must meet the airplane's certification basis and the approval must specifically reference this AD.

title: Airworthiness Directives: General Electric Company Turbofan Engines

units.obligation_text: The FAA must receive comments on this airworthiness directive (AD) by April 8, 2021.
units.action_summary: FAA must receive comments on the AD by April 8, 2021.

units.obligation_text: This AD applies to all General Electric Company (GE) CF6–80A, CF6–80A1, CF6–80A2, CF6–80A3, CF6–80C2A1, CF6–80C2A2, CF6–80C2A3, CF6–80C2A5, CF6–80C2A5F, CF6–80C2A8, CF6–80C2B1, CF6–80C2B1F, CF6–80C2B1F1, CF6–80C2B1F2, CF6–80C2B2, CF6–80C2B2F, CF6–80C2B3F, CF6–80C2B4, CF6–80C2B4F, CF6–80C2B5F, CF6–80C2B6, CF6–80C2B6F, CF6–80C2B6FA, CF6–80C2B7F, CF6–80C2B8F, CF6–80C2D1F, CF6–80C2K1F and CF6–80C2L1F model turbofan engines.
units.actor: owners/operators of the listed GE CF6–80 model turbofan engines (i.e., subjects of the AD)
units.action_summary: Identifies which GE CF6–80 model turbofan engines are subject to this AD.

units.obligation_text: Comply with this AD within the compliance times specified, unless already done.
units.action_summary: Required to comply with the AD within the specified compliance times unless already accomplished.

units.obligation_text: After the effective date of this AD, at every piece-part exposure of the HPT rotor stage 1 disk, HPT rotor stage 2 disk, or the HPT thermal shield, perform a visual inspection and a fluorescent penetrant inspection (FPI) of the HPT thermal shield.
units.action_summary: At every piece-part exposure of specified HPT components, perform a visual inspection and an FPI of the HPT thermal shield.

units.obligation_text: During any inspection required by paragraph (g)(1) of this AD, if a crack extending through either the forward or aft flange of the HPT thermal shield is detected, remove the HPT thermal shield, the HPT rotor stage 1 disk, and the HPT rotor stage 2 disk from service.
units.action_summary: If an inspection finds a crack through the forward or aft flange of the HPT thermal shield, remove the thermal shield and the stage 1 and stage 2 HPT rotor disks from service.

units.obligation_text: Do not install onto any engine an HPT rotor stage 1 disk or HPT rotor stage 2 disk that was removed from service due to the requirements of paragraph (g)(2) of this AD.
units.action_summary: Prohibits installing any HPT rotor stage 1 or stage 2 disk that was removed from service under paragraph (g)(2).

units.obligation_text: The Manager, ECO Branch, FAA, has the authority to approve AMOCs for this AD, if requested using the procedures found in 14 CFR 39.19.

units.obligation_text: You may email your request to: ANE-AD-AMOC@faa.gov.
units.action_summary: Permits requesters to email AMOC requests to the specified email address.

units.actor: users of approved AMOCs (owners/operators/persons implementing the AMOC)
units.action_summary: Requires notification to the appropriate principal inspector or local FSDO/CHDO manager before using an approved AMOC.

title: Airworthiness Directives: The Boeing Company Airplanes

units.obligation_text: The FAA must receive comments on this airworthiness directive (AD) action by April 12, 2021.
units.action_summary: Receive comments on the AD by April 12, 2021.

units.obligation_text: This AD applies to The Boeing Company Model 767–200, –300, –300F, and –400ER series airplanes, certificated in any category, having line numbers (L/N) 1 through 1200 inclusive.
units.actor: The Boeing Company Model 767–200, –300, –300F, and –400ER series airplanes (and their owners/operators)
units.action_summary: Identifies which Boeing 767 airplanes are subject to this AD.

units.obligation_text: Comply with this AD within the compliance times specified, unless already done.
units.action_summary: Require compliance with the AD within the specified times unless the actions have already been done.

units.obligation_text: Within 60 days after the effective date of this AD, revise the existing maintenance or inspection program, as applicable, to incorporate the information in Section A, including Subsections A.1, A.2, A.3, A.4, and A.5, of Boeing 767–200/300/300F/400ER Special Compliance Items/Airworthiness Limitations, D622T001–9–04, revision January 2020; except as provided by paragraph (h) of this AD.
units.actor: Owners/operators of affected airplanes (persons responsible for the maintenance or inspection program)
units.action_summary: Revise the existing maintenance/inspection program within 60 days to incorporate the listed Boeing AWL information, except as provided in paragraph (h).

units.obligation_text: For AWL No. 28–AWL–01, 'External Wires Over Auxiliary (Center) Fuel Tank': Within 144 months after the most recent inspection was performed as specified in AWL No. 28 AWL 01, or within 12 months after the effective date of this AD if no initial inspection has been performed or the last inspection date is unknown.
units.action_summary: Perform the AWL No. 28–AWL–01 inspection within 144 months after the last inspection, or within 12 months after the AD effective date if no prior inspection or date unknown.

units.obligation_text: For AWL No. 28–AWL–05, 'Lightning Protection—Hydraulic Line Fuel Tank Penetration Bonding Path': Within 25,000 flight hours or 72 months, whichever occurs first, since the most recent inspection was performed as specified in AWL No. 28–AWL–05, or within 30 days after the effective date of this AD if no initial inspection has been performed or the last inspection date is unknown.
units.action_summary: Perform the AWL No. 28–AWL–05 inspection within 25,000 flight hours or 72 months since the last inspection, or within 30 days after the AD effective date if no prior inspection or date unknown.

units.obligation_text: For AWL No. 28–AWL–18, 'Fuel Quantity Indicating System (FQIS)—Out of Tank Wiring Lightning Shield to Ground Termination': Within 144 months after the most recent inspection was performed as specified in AWL No. 28–AWL–18, or within 12 months after the effective date of this AD if no initial inspection has been performed or the last inspection date is unknown.
units.action_summary: Perform the AWL No. 28–AWL–18 inspection within 144 months after the last inspection, or within 12 months after the AD effective date if no prior inspection or date unknown.

units.obligation_text: For AWL No. 28–AWL–20, 'Auxiliary (Center) Tank Override Fuel Pumps Auto Shutoff Circuit': Within 12 months after the most recent inspection was performed as specified in AWL No. 28–AWL–20; or within 12 months after accomplishment of the actions specified in Boeing Service Bulletin 767–28A0083, or Boeing Service Bulletin 767–28A0084, as applicable; whichever is later. If no initial inspection was performed or the last inspection date is unknown, then within 30 days after the effective date of this AD.
units.action_summary: Perform the AWL No. 28–AWL–20 inspection within 12 months after the last inspection or within 12 months after specified Boeing service bulletin actions (whichever is later), or within 30 days after the AD effective date if no prior inspection or date unknown.

units.obligation_text: For AWL No. 28–AWL–21, 'AC and DC Fuel Pump Fault Current Bonding Jumper Installation': Within 72 months after the most recent inspection was performed as specified in AWL No. 28–AWL–21, or within 6 months after the effective date of this AD if no initial inspection has been performed or the last inspection date is unknown.
units.action_summary: Perform the AWL No. 28–AWL–21 inspection within 72 months after the last inspection, or within 6 months after the AD effective date if no prior inspection or date unknown.

units.obligation_text: For AWL No. 28–AWL–27, 'Over-Current and Arcing Protection Electrical Design Features Operation—AC Fuel Pump Ground Fault Interrupter (GFI)': Within 12 months after the most recent inspection was performed as specified in AWL No. 28–AWL–27, or within 12 months after accomplishment of the actions specified in Boeing Service Bulletin 767–28A0085, whichever is later. If no initial inspection was performed or the last inspection date is unknown, then within 30 days after the effective date of this AD.
units.action_summary: Perform the AWL No. 28–AWL–27 inspection within 12 months after the last inspection or within 12 months after specified Boeing service bulletin actions (whichever is later), or within 30 days after the AD effective date if no prior inspection or date unknown.

units.obligation_text: For AWL No. 28–AWL–28, 'Auxiliary (Center) Tank Override/Jettison Fuel Pump Failed On Protection System': Within 12 months after the most recent inspection was performed as specified in AWL No. 28–AWL–28, or within 12 months after accomplishment of the actions specified in Boeing Service Bulletin 767–28A0085, whichever is later. If no initial inspection was performed or the last inspection date is unknown, then within 30 days after the effective date of this AD.
units.action_summary: Perform AWL No. 28–AWL–28 inspection within specified 12-month intervals relative to last inspection or service bulletin actions, or within 30 days after the AD effective date if no prior inspection or date unknown.

units.obligation_text: For AWL No. 28–AWL–35, 'Cushion Clamps and Teflon Sleeving Installed on Out-of-Tank Wire Bundles Installed on Brackets that are Mounted Directly on the Fuel Tanks': Within 144 months after the most recent inspection was performed as specified in AWL No. 28–AWL–35 or within 144 months after accomplishment of the actions specified in Boeing Service Bulletin 767–57A0102, whichever is later. If no initial inspection was performed or the last inspection date is unknown, then within 12 months after the effective date of this AD.
units.action_summary: Perform AWL No. 28–AWL–35 inspection within 144 months after last inspection or 144 months after specified Boeing service bulletin actions (whichever is later), or within 12 months after AD effective date if no prior inspection or date unknown.

units.obligation_text: For AWL No. 28–AWL–37, 'FQIS BITE Test (Auxiliary (Center) Tank Circuit Test)': For Model 767–300F airplanes L/N 1094 and subsequent, within 750 flight hours after the most recent inspection was performed as specified in AWL No. 28–AWL–37, or within 30 days after the effective date of this AD if no initial inspection has been performed or the last inspection date is unknown.
units.actor: Owners/operators of affected Model 767–300F airplanes (L/N 1094 and subsequent)
units.action_summary: Perform the AWL No. 28–AWL–37 FQIS BITE test within 750 flight hours after the last inspection, or within 30 days after AD effective date if no prior inspection or date unknown (for applicable airplanes).

units.obligation_text: For AWL No. 28–AWL–38, 'Fuel Level Sensing System (FLSS) Dry Capacitance Test': For Model 767–300F airplanes L/N 1096 and subsequent, within 750 flight hours after the most recent inspection was performed as specified in AWL No. 28–AWL–38, or within 30 days after the effective date of this AD if no initial inspection has been performed or the last inspection date is unknown.
units.actor: Owners/operators of affected Model 767–300F airplanes (L/N 1096 and subsequent)
units.action_summary: Perform AWL No. 28–AWL–38 FLSS dry capacitance test within 750 flight hours after last inspection, or within 30 days after AD effective date if no prior inspection or date unknown (for applicable airplanes).

units.obligation_text: For AWL No. 28–AWL–101, 'Engine Fuel Suction Feed Operational Test': Within 7,500 flight hours or 36 months, whichever occurs first since the most recent inspection was performed as specified in AWL No. 28–AWL–101, or within 30 days after the effective date of this AD if no initial inspection has been performed or the last inspection date is unknown.
units.action_summary: Perform AWL No. 28–AWL–101 operational test within 7,500 flight hours or 36 months since last inspection, or within 30 days after AD effective date if no prior inspection or date unknown.

units.obligation_text: For AWL No. 28–AWL–102, 'Fuel Quantity Indicating System (FQIS)—Low Fuel and Fuel Config Indication Test': Within 750 flight hours after the most recent inspection was performed as specified in AWL No. 28–AWL–102; or within 750 flight hours after accomplishment of the actions specified in Boeing Service Bulletin 767–31–0295 or Boeing Service Bulletin 767–31–0302, as applicable; whichever is later. If no initial inspection was performed or the last inspection date is unknown, then within 30 days after the effective date of this AD.
units.action_summary: Perform AWL No. 28–AWL–102 test within 750 flight hours after last inspection or within 750 flight hours after specified Boeing service bulletin actions (whichever is later), or within 30 days after AD effective date if no prior inspection or date unknown.

units.obligation_text: For AWL No. 47–AWL–04, 'Nitrogen Generation System (NGS)—Nitrogen-Enriched Air (NEA) Distribution Ducting': For L/N 993 and subsequent and all airplanes that have incorporated Boeing Service Bulletin 767–47–0001, within the applicable interval specified in AWL No. 47–AWL–04 since the most recent inspection was performed as specified in AWL No. 47–AWL–04. If no initial inspection was performed or the last inspection date is unknown, then within 4 months after the effective date of this AD.
units.actor: Owners/operators of affected airplanes (L/N 993 and subsequent and airplanes with Boeing SB 767–47–0001 incorporated)
units.action_summary: Perform AWL No. 47–AWL–04 inspection within the AWL-specified interval since last inspection, or within 4 months after AD effective date if no prior inspection or date unknown (for applicable airplanes).

units.obligation_text: For AWL No. 47–AWL–05, 'Nitrogen Generation System (NGS)—Cross Vent Check Valve': For L/N 993 and subsequent and all airplanes that have incorporated Boeing Service Bulletin 767–47–0001, within the applicable interval specified in AWL No. 47–AWL–05 since the most recent inspection was performed as specified in AWL No. 47–AWL–05. If no initial inspection was performed or the last inspection date is unknown, then within 4 months after the effective date of this AD.
units.actor: Owners/operators of affected airplanes (L/N 993 and subsequent and airplanes with Boeing SB 767–47–0001 incorporated)
units.action_summary: Perform AWL No. 47–AWL–05 inspection within the AWL-specified interval since last inspection, or within 4 months after AD effective date if no prior inspection or date unknown (for applicable airplanes).

units.obligation_text: As an option, when accomplishing the actions required by paragraph (g) of this AD, the changes specified in paragraphs (h)(1) and (2) of this AD are acceptable.
units.actor: Owners/operators/persons accomplishing the actions required by paragraph (g)
units.action_summary: Permits use of the changes specified in (h)(1) and (h)(2) as an optional alternative when accomplishing paragraph (g) actions.

units.obligation_text: Where AWL No. 28–AWL–09 identifies wire types BMS 13–48, BMS 13–58, and BMS 13–60, the following acceptable wire types and cables can be added to AWL No. 28–AWL–09: MIL–W–22759/16, SAE AS22759/16 (formerly M22759/16), MIL–W–22759/32, SAE AS22759/32 (formerly M22759/32), MIL–W–22759/34, SAE AS22759/34 (formerly M22759/34), MIL–W–22759/41, SAE AS22759/41 (formerly M22759/41), MIL–W–22759/86, SAE AS22759/86 (formerly M22759/86), MIL–W–22759/87, SAE AS22759/87 (formerly M22759/87), MIL–W–22759/92, and SAE AS22759/92 (formerly M22759/92); and MIL–C–27500 and NEMA WC 27500 cables that are constructed from these military or SAE specification wire types, as applicable.
units.action_summary: Permits adding the listed military/SAE wire types and specified cables to AWL No. 28–AWL–09 as acceptable alternatives.

units.obligation_text: Where AWL No. 28–AWL–09 identifies TFE–2X Standard wall for wire sleeving, the following sleeving materials are acceptable: Roundit 2000NX and Varglas Type HO, HP, or HM, Grade A.
units.action_summary: Permits using Roundit 2000NX or Varglas Type HO/HP/HM Grade A sleeving as acceptable alternatives to TFE–2X Standard wall sleeving specified in AWL No. 28–AWL–09.

units.obligation_text: After the existing maintenance or inspection program has been revised as required by paragraph (g) of this AD, no alternative actions (e.g., inspections), intervals, or CDCCLs may be used unless the actions, intervals, and CDCCLs are approved as an alternative method of compliance (AMOC) in accordance with the procedures specified in paragraph (k) of this AD.
units.action_summary: Prohibits using alternative actions, intervals, or CDCCLs after revising the maintenance/inspection program unless they are approved as an AMOC per paragraph (k).

units.obligation_text: Accomplishment of the revision required by paragraph (g) of this AD terminates the requirements specified in paragraphs (j)(1) through (7) of this AD for that airplane:
units.actor: Owners/operators of the airplane that accomplish the revision required by paragraph (g)
units.action_summary: States that completing the paragraph (g) revision terminates the listed prior AD revision requirements for that airplane.

units.obligation_text: The revision required by paragraphs (g) and (h) of AD 2008–11–01 R1.
units.action_summary: Identifies that the specified revision in AD 2008–11–01 R1 is terminated for the airplane upon accomplishing paragraph (g) revision.

units.obligation_text: The revision required by paragraph (h) of AD 2010–06–10.
units.action_summary: Identifies that the specified revision in AD 2010–06–10 is terminated for the airplane upon accomplishing paragraph (g) revision.

units.obligation_text: The revision required by paragraph (k) of AD 2011–25–05.
units.action_summary: Identifies that the specified revision in AD 2011–25–05 is terminated for the airplane upon accomplishing paragraph (g) revision.

units.obligation_text: The revision required by paragraph (n) of AD 2013–25–02.
units.action_summary: Identifies that the specified revision in AD 2013–25–02 is terminated for the airplane upon accomplishing paragraph (g) revision.

units.obligation_text: The revision required by paragraph (g) of AD 2014–08–09.
units.action_summary: Identifies that the specified revision in AD 2014–08–09 is terminated for the airplane upon accomplishing paragraph (g) revision.

title: Airworthiness Directives: General Electric Company Turbofan Engines

units.obligation_text: The FAA must receive comments on this airworthiness directive (AD) by April 12, 2021.
units.action_summary: Receive comments on this AD by April 12, 2021.

units.obligation_text: This AD applies to General Electric Company (GE) GEnx–2B67, GEnx–2B67/P, and GEnx–2B67B model turbofan engines with lower fuel manifold, part number (P/N) 2619M58G01, installed.
units.action_summary: Defines which GE GEnx–2B model engines with P/N 2619M58G01 are covered by the AD.

units.obligation_text: Comply with this AD within the compliance times specified, unless already done.
units.action_summary: Must comply with the AD within the specified compliance times unless actions already completed.

units.obligation_text: Within the compliance time specified in Table 1 to paragraph (g)(1) of this AD, perform either an ultrasonic inspection (USI), an on-wing spot fluorescent penetrant inspection (FPI), or an in-shop FPI of the lower fuel manifold, P/N 2619M58G01, in accordance with paragraph (g)(1)(i), (ii), or (iii) of this AD, as applicable.
units.actor: Operators/maintenance personnel of the affected engines
units.action_summary: Within the applicable compliance time, perform one of three specified inspections of the lower fuel manifold per the AD's procedures.

units.obligation_text: Less than 1,700 CSN — After the lower fuel manifold has accumulated 1,700 CSN, but before it exceeds 2,200 CSN.
units.actor: Operators/maintenance personnel of the affected engines
units.action_summary: If the lower fuel manifold has less than 1,700 CSN, the inspection must be done after it reaches 1,700 CSN and before it exceeds 2,200 CSN.

units.obligation_text: 1,700 CSN or more — Within 500 engine flight cycles (FCs) after the effective date of this AD.
units.actor: Operators/maintenance personnel of the affected engines
units.action_summary: If the lower fuel manifold has 1,700 CSN or more, the inspection must be done within 500 engine flight cycles after the AD's effective date.

units.obligation_text: Perform a USI of the lower fuel manifold at the locations adjacent to the five support block pads to detect cracks in accordance with paragraph 4. Appendix—A of GEnx–2B Service Bulletin (SB) 73–0089 R01, dated January 11, 2021.
units.action_summary: Perform an ultrasonic inspection at locations adjacent to the five support block pads per the specified service bulletin.

units.obligation_text: Perform an on-wing spot FPI of the lower fuel manifold at the five brazed block joints to detect cracks. Guidance on performing the spot FPI can be found in paragraph 3.B.(6)(a) of GEnx–2B SB 73–0089 R01, dated January 11, 2021.
units.action_summary: Perform an on-wing spot fluorescent penetrant inspection at the five brazed block joints per the service bulletin guidance.

units.obligation_text: Perform an in-shop FPI of the lower fuel manifold at the five brazed block joints to detect cracks. Guidance on performing the FPI can be found in paragraph 3.C.(4) of GEnx–2B SB 73–0089 R01, dated January 11, 2021.
units.action_summary: Perform an in-shop fluorescent penetrant inspection at the five brazed block joints per the service bulletin guidance.

units.obligation_text: If a crack or rejectable indication is found during the USI, on-wing spot FPI, or in-shop FPI required by paragraphs (g)(1)(i), (ii), and (iii) of this AD, before further flight, remove the lower fuel manifold from service and replace it with a part eligible for installation.
units.action_summary: If a crack or rejectable indication is found during the required inspections, remove the lower fuel manifold from service and replace it with a part eligible for installation before further flight.

units.obligation_text: For the purpose of this AD, a part eligible for installation is:
units.action_summary: Defines what constitutes a part eligible for installation under this AD.

units.obligation_text: Any serviceable lower fuel manifold, P/N 2619M58G01, with less than 1,700 CSN,
units.action_summary: A serviceable lower fuel manifold P/N 2619M58G01 with less than 1,700 CSN is eligible for installation.

units.obligation_text: Any lower fuel manifold, P/N 2619M58G01, with 1,700 CSN or more that has been inspected in accordance with paragraph (g)(1)(i), (ii), or (iii) of this AD and a crack or rejectable indication was not found,
units.action_summary: A lower fuel manifold P/N 2619M58G01 with 1,700 CSN or more that has been inspected per (g)(1) and found free of cracks/indications is eligible for installation.

units.obligation_text: Any approved lower fuel manifold with a part number other than P/N 2619M58G01.
units.action_summary: Any approved lower fuel manifold having a different part number is eligible for installation.

units.obligation_text: The reporting requirements specified in paragraph 4. Appendix—A of GE GEnx–2B SB 73–0089 R01, dated January 11, 2021, are not required by this AD.
units.actor: Operators/persons subject to the service bulletin
units.action_summary: Reporting requirements in the referenced service bulletin are not required by this AD.

units.obligation_text: The Manager, ECO Branch, FAA, has the authority to approve AMOCs for this AD, if requested using the procedures found in 14 CFR 39.19.
units.action_summary: Manager may approve alternative methods of compliance (AMOCs) for this AD when requested per 14 CFR 39.19.

units.obligation_text: In accordance with 14 CFR 39.19, send your request to your principal inspector or local Flight Standards District Office, as appropriate. If sending information directly to the manager of the certification office, send it to the attention of the person identified in Related Information. You may email your request to: ANE-AD-AMOC@faa.gov.
units.action_summary: Requesters must send AMOC requests to their principal inspector or local FSDO (or to the certification office manager attention as identified); requesters may email requests to the specified address.

units.obligation_text: Before using any approved AMOC, notify your appropriate principal inspector, or lacking a principal inspector, the manager of the local flight standards district office/certificate holding district office.
units.action_summary: Prior to using an approved AMOC, the user must notify their principal inspector or, if none, the manager of the local FSDO/CHDO.

title: Airworthiness Directives: The Boeing Company Airplanes

units.obligation_text: The FAA must receive comments on this airworthiness directive (AD) action by May 10, 2021.
units.action_summary: FAA must receive comments on this AD by May 10, 2021.

units.obligation_text: This AD applies to The Boeing Company Model 777–200, –200LR, –300, –300ER, and 777F series airplanes having line numbers (L/Ns) 1 through 1609 inclusive, certificated in any category.
units.actor: The listed Boeing 777 airplanes (and their operators/owners)
units.action_summary: Specifies which Boeing 777 airplanes are subject to this AD.

units.obligation_text: Comply with this AD within the compliance times specified, unless already done.
units.actor: Operators/owners of affected airplanes (those subject to this AD)
units.action_summary: Affected parties must comply with the AD within the specified compliance times unless actions already completed.

units.obligation_text: Within 60 days after the effective date of this AD, revise the existing maintenance or inspection program, as applicable, to incorporate the information in Section D, 'Airworthiness Limitations—Systems,' including Subsections D.1, D.2, and D.3, of Section 9, Airworthiness Limitations (AWLs) and Certification Maintenance Requirements (CMRs), of Boeing 777–200/200LR/300/300ER/777F Maintenance Planning Data (MPD) Document, D622W001–9, dated November 2019; except as provided by paragraph (h) of this AD.
units.action_summary: Within 60 days of the AD's effective date, revise the maintenance/inspection program to incorporate specified AWLs/CMRs per the Boeing MPD document, subject to paragraph (h).

units.obligation_text: For AWL 28–AWL–01, 'External Wires Over Center Fuel Tank': Within 16,000 flight cycles or 3,000 days, whichever occurs first after the date of issuance of the original airworthiness certificate or the date of issuance of the original export certificate of airworthiness; or within 16,000 flight cycles or 3,000 days, whichever occurs first after the most recent inspection was performed as specified in 28–AWL–01; whichever occurs later.
units.action_summary: Initial compliance time for AWL 28–AWL–01 is the later of specified 16,000 flight cycles/3,000 days timelines.

units.obligation_text: For AWL 28–AWL–03, 'Fuel Quantity Indicating System (FQIS)—Out of Tank Wiring Lightning Shield to Ground Termination': Within 16,000 flight cycles or 3,000 days, whichever occurs first after the date of issuance of the original airworthiness certificate or the date of issuance of the original export certificate of airworthiness; or within 16,000 flight cycles or 3,000 days, whichever occurs first after the most recent inspection was performed as specified in 28–AWL–03; whichever occurs later.
units.action_summary: Initial compliance time for AWL 28–AWL–03 is the later of specified 16,000 flight cycles/3,000 days timelines.

units.obligation_text: For AWL 28–AWL–18, 'Over-Current and Arcing Protection Electrical Design Features Operation—AC Fuel Pump GFI and GFP': Within 375 days after the date of issuance of the original airworthiness certificate or the date of issuance of the original export certificate of airworthiness; or within 375 days after accomplishment of the actions specified in Boeing Service Bulletin 777–28A0037; or within 375 days after accomplishment of the actions specified in Boeing Service Bulletin 777–28A0038; or within 375 days after the most recent inspection was performed as specified in 28–AWL–18; whichever occurs latest.
units.action_summary: Initial compliance time for AWL 28–AWL–18 is the latest of specified 375-day timelines or after specified service bulletin actions or most recent inspection.

units.obligation_text: For AWL 28–AWL–21, 'External Wires Over Auxiliary Fuel Tank (Cell)': Within 16,000 flight cycles or 3,000 days, whichever occurs first after the date of issuance of the original airworthiness certificate or date of issuance of the original export certificate of airworthiness; or within 16,000 flight cycles or 3,000 days, whichever occurs first after the most recent inspection was performed as specified in 28–AWL–21; or within 365 days after the effective date of this AD; whichever occurs latest.
units.action_summary: Initial compliance time for AWL 28–AWL–21 is the latest of specified 16,000 flight cycles/3,000 days timelines, most recent inspection, or within 365 days after AD effective date.

units.obligation_text: For AWL 28–AWL–26, 'Auxiliary Fuel Tank (Cell) AC Fuel Pump Uncommanded ON/Automatic Shutoff Circuit': Within 375 days after the date of issuance of the original airworthiness certificate or the date of issuance of the original export certificate of airworthiness; or within 375 days after the most recent inspection was performed as specified in 28–AWL–26; or within 30 days after the effective date of this AD; whichever occurs latest.
units.action_summary: Initial compliance time for AWL 28–AWL–26 is the latest of specified 375-day timelines or within 30 days after AD effective date.

units.obligation_text: For AWL 28–AWL–32, 'Cushion Clamps and Teflon Sleeving Installed on Out-of-Tank Wire Bundles Installed on Brackets that are Mounted Directly on the Fuel Tanks': For airplanes having L/N 1 through 503 inclusive, within 3,750 days after accomplishment of the actions specified in Boeing Service Bulletins 777–57A0050, or within 60 months after the effective date of this AD, whichever occurs later. For airplanes having L/N 504 and subsequent, within 3,750 days after the date of issuance of the original airworthiness certificate or the date of issuance of the original export certificate of airworthiness; or within 60 months after the effective date of this AD; whichever occurs later.
units.action_summary: Initial compliance time for AWL 28–AWL–32 varies by line number: specific multi-year/flight-day thresholds as stated.

units.obligation_text: For AWL 28–AWL–101, 'Engine Fuel Suction Feed Operational Test': Within 7,500 flight hours after the date of issuance of the original airworthiness certificate or the date of issuance of the original export certificate of airworthiness; or within 7,500 flight hours after the most recent inspection was performed as specified in AWL No. 28–AWL–101; whichever occurs later.
units.action_summary: Initial compliance time for AWL 28–AWL–101 is the later of specified 7,500 flight hours timelines.

units.obligation_text: For AWL 47–AWL–04, 'NGS—Thermal Switch': Within 108,000 flight hours after the date of issuance of the original airworthiness certificate or the date of issuance of the original export certificate of airworthiness; or within 108,000 flight hours after accomplishment of the actions specified in Boeing Service Bulletin 777–47–0002; or within 108,000 flight hours after the most recent inspection was performed as specified in 47–AWL–04; whichever occurs latest.
units.action_summary: Initial compliance time for AWL 47–AWL–04 is the latest of specified 108,000 flight hour timelines or after specified service bulletin actions or most recent inspection.

units.obligation_text: For 47–AWL–05, 'NGS—Cross Vent Check Valve': Within 10,682 flight hours after the date of issuance of the original airworthiness certificate or the date of issuance of the original export certificate of airworthiness; or within 10,682 flight hours after accomplishment of the actions specified in Boeing Service Bulletin 777–47–0002; or within 10,682 flight hours after the most recent inspection was performed as specified in 47–AWL–05; whichever occurs latest.
units.action_summary: Initial compliance time for AWL 47–AWL–05 is the latest of specified 10,682 flight hour timelines or after specified service bulletin actions or most recent inspection.

units.obligation_text: For AWL 47–AWL–06, 'NGS—NEA Distribution Ducting Integrity': Within 10,682 flight hours after the date of issuance of the original airworthiness certificate or the date of issuance of the original export certificate of airworthiness; or within 10,682 flight hours after accomplishment of the actions specified in Boeing Service Bulletin 777–47–0002; or within 10,682 flight hours after the most recent inspection was performed as specified in 47–AWL–06; whichever occurs latest.
units.action_summary: Initial compliance time for AWL 47–AWL–06 is the latest of specified 10,682 flight hour timelines or after specified service bulletin actions or most recent inspection.

units.section: (h) Additional Acceptable Wire Types and Sleeving
units.obligation_text: As an option, when accomplishing the actions required by paragraph (g) of this AD, the changes specified in paragraphs (h)(1) and (2) of this AD are acceptable.
units.actor: Operators/maintenance personnel accomplishing actions required by paragraph (g)
units.action_summary: Provides optional acceptable changes (alternatives) when completing paragraph (g) actions.

units.obligation_text: Where AWL No. 28–AWL–11 identifies wire types BMS 13–48, BMS 13–58, and BMS 13–60, the following wire types are acceptable: MIL–W–22759/16, SAE AS22759/16 (M22759/16), MIL–W–22759/32, SAE AS22759/32 (M22759/32), MIL–W–22759/34, SAE AS22759/34 (M22759/34), MIL–W–22759/41, SAE AS22759/41 (M22759/41), MIL–W–22759/86, SAE AS22759/86 (M22759/86), MIL–W–22759/87, SAE AS22759/87 (M22759/87), MIL–W–22759/92, and SAE AS22759/92 (M22759/92); and MIL–C–27500 and NEMA WC 27500 cables constructed from these military or SAE specification wire types, as applicable.
units.action_summary: Specifies acceptable alternative wire types that may be used where AWL 28–AWL–11 lists certain BMS wire types.

units.obligation_text: Where AWL No. 28–AWL–11 identifies TFE–2X Standard wall (manufactured as specified in MIL–I–23053) for wire sleeving, the following sleeving materials are acceptable: Roundit 2000NX and Varglas Type HO, HP, or HM.
units.action_summary: Specifies acceptable alternative sleeving materials that may be used where AWL 28–AWL–11 lists TFE–2X standard wall sleeving.

units.section: (i) No Alternative Actions, Intervals, or CDCCLs
units.obligation_text: After the existing maintenance or inspection program has been revised as required by paragraph (g) of this AD, no alternative actions (e.g., inspections), intervals, or CDCCLs may be used unless the actions, intervals, and CDCCLs are approved as an alternative method of compliance (AMOC) in accordance with the procedures specified in paragraph (k) of this AD.
units.action_summary: Prohibits use of alternative actions, intervals, or CDCCLs after the program revision unless approved as an AMOC under paragraph (k).

units.obligation_text: Unless the actions, intervals, and CDCCLs are approved as an alternative method of compliance (AMOC) in accordance with the procedures specified in paragraph (k) of this AD.
units.action_summary: Exception to the prohibition in (i): alternatives are permitted if approved as an AMOC per paragraph (k).

units.obligation_text: Accomplishment of the revision required by paragraph (g) of this AD terminates the requirements specified in paragraphs (j)(1) and (2) of this AD for that airplane.
units.actor: Operators/owners of affected airplanes (performing the revision)
units.action_summary: If the paragraph (g) revision is accomplished, it terminates certain requirements of prior ADs for that airplane.

units.obligation_text: All requirements of AD 2008–11–13 for Model 777–200, –200LR, –300, and –300ER series airplanes only.
units.actor: Operators/owners of the specified Model 777 series airplanes
units.action_summary: Specifies that accomplishment of the paragraph (g) revision terminates all requirements of AD 2008–11–13 for the listed models.

units.obligation_text: All requirements of AD 2014–09–09.
units.action_summary: Specifies that accomplishment of the paragraph (g) revision terminates all requirements of AD 2014–09–09 for that airplane.

units.obligation_text: The Manager, Seattle ACO Branch, FAA, has the authority to approve AMOCs for this AD, if requested using the procedures found in 14 CFR 39.19.
units.actor: The Manager, Seattle ACO Branch, FAA
units.action_summary: Designates the Manager as the authority to approve alternative methods of compliance (AMOCs) for this AD when requested per 14 CFR 39.19.

units.obligation_text: In accordance with 14 CFR 39.19, send your request to your principal inspector or responsible Flight Standards Office, as appropriate.
units.action_summary: Requests for AMOCs must be sent to the requester's principal inspector or responsible Flight Standards Office per 14 CFR 39.19.

units.obligation_text: If sending information directly to the manager of the certification office, send it to the attention of the person identified in paragraph (l)(1) of this AD.
units.actor: Persons sending information directly to the manager of the certification office
units.action_summary: If information is sent directly to the certification office manager, it must be addressed to the person identified in paragraph (l)(1).

units.obligation_text: Information may be emailed to: 9-ANM-Seattle-ACO-AMOC-Requests@faa.gov.
units.action_summary: Requesters are permitted to email AMOC requests to the specified email address.

units.obligation_text: Before using any approved AMOC, notify your appropriate principal inspector, or lacking a principal inspector, the manager of the responsible Flight Standards Office.
units.actor: Persons intending to use an approved AMOC (operators/maintenance personnel)
units.action_summary: Operators must notify their principal inspector (or the Flight Standards Office manager if no principal inspector) before using any approved AMOC.

units.obligation_text: An AMOC that provides an acceptable level of safety may be used for any repair, modification, or alteration required by this AD if it is approved by The Boeing Company Organization Designation Authorization (ODA) that has been authorized by the Manager, Seattle ACO Branch, FAA, to make those findings.
units.action_summary: AMOCs approved by the authorized Boeing ODA may be used for required repairs/modifications/alterations if they provide an acceptable level of safety.

units.obligation_text: To be approved, the repair method, modification deviation, or alteration deviation must meet the certification basis of the airplane, and the approval must specifically refer to this AD.
units.actor: Approving authority (Boeing ODA or other approver)
units.action_summary: Approvals of repair/modification/alteration deviations must meet the airplane's certification basis and explicitly reference this AD.

title: Airworthiness Directives: Various Restricted Category Helicopters

units.obligation_text: The FAA must receive comments on this airworthiness directive (AD) by May 10, 2021.
units.action_summary: Receive comments on the AD by May 10, 2021.

units.obligation_text: Comply with this AD within the compliance times specified, unless already done.
units.action_summary: Comply with all requirements of this AD within the specified compliance times unless already accomplished.

units.obligation_text: Before further flight after the effective date of this AD, determine the total hours time-in-service (TIS) of the main driveshaft.
units.action_summary: Determine the total time-in-service hours of the main driveshaft before the next flight after the AD effective date.

units.obligation_text: If the main driveshaft has accumulated less than 5,000 total hours TIS, before exceeding 5,000 total hours TIS, remove the main driveshaft from service.
units.action_summary: If driveshaft has <5,000 hours, remove it from service before it exceeds 5,000 hours.

units.obligation_text: If the main driveshaft has accumulated 5,000 or more total hours TIS, before further flight, remove the main driveshaft from service.
units.action_summary: If driveshaft has 5,000 hours or more, remove it from service before the next flight.

units.obligation_text: Thereafter following paragraph (g)(1) of this AD, remove the main driveshaft from service before accumulating 5,000 total hours TIS.
units.action_summary: After the initial actions in (g)(1), ensure the driveshaft is removed from service before it accumulates 5,000 total hours (recurring limit).

units.obligation_text: Within 25 hours TIS after the effective date of this AD, remove main driveshaft P/N SKCP2180–1, SKCP2281–1, SKCP2281–1R, or SKCP2281–103 by following 6–24.3 Removal—Main Driveshaft P/N SKCP2281–103, of Headquarters, Department of the Army, Aviation Unit and Intermediate Maintenance Instructions Army Model UH–1H/V/EH–1H/X Helicopters, Technical Manual TM 55–1520–210–23–1, Change No. 42, dated April 14, 2003 (TM 55–1520–210–23–1) and:
units.action_summary: Within 25 hours TIS after the AD effective date, remove the listed main driveshaft P/Ns following the specified technical manual procedure.

units.obligation_text: Inspect for any broken, loose, or missing hardware.
units.action_summary: Inspect the removed driveshaft for broken, loose, or missing hardware.

units.obligation_text: If there is broken or loose hardware, before further flight, remove the driveshaft from service.
units.action_summary: If inspection finds broken or loose hardware, remove the driveshaft from service before further flight.

units.obligation_text: If there is missing hardware, before further flight, replace the driveshaft.
units.action_summary: If inspection finds missing hardware, replace the driveshaft before further flight.

units.obligation_text: Visually inspect each flex frame and mount bolt torque stripe (red or yellow) for movement.
units.action_summary: Visually inspect flex frame and mount bolt torque stripes for any movement.

units.obligation_text: If there is any torque stripe movement, before further flight, replace the driveshaft.
units.action_summary: If torque stripe movement is detected, replace the driveshaft before further flight.

units.obligation_text: Visually inspect each joint for fretting corrosion, which may be indicated by red metallic particles.
units.action_summary: Visually inspect each driveshaft joint for signs of fretting corrosion.

units.obligation_text: If there is any grease, oil, or dirt covering a joint, clean the area and visually inspect again.
units.action_summary: If a joint is covered with grease, oil, or dirt, clean it and re-inspect.

units.obligation_text: If there is any fretting corrosion, before further flight, replace the driveshaft.
units.action_summary: If fretting corrosion is found, replace the driveshaft before further flight.

units.obligation_text: Inspect the main driveshaft for mechanical damage, corrosion, an edge dent, and nick as shown in Figure 1 to paragraph (g)(3)(iv) of this AD.
units.action_summary: Inspect the driveshaft for mechanical damage, corrosion, edge dents, and nicks per Figure 1.

units.obligation_text: If there is a scratch, wear, corrosion, pitting, an edge dent, or a nick within allowable limits, before further flight, repair the main driveshaft in accordance with FAA-approved procedures.
units.action_summary: If damage is within allowable limits, repair the driveshaft per FAA-approved procedures before further flight.

units.obligation_text: If there is a crack, or a scratch, wear, corrosion, pitting, an edge dent, or a nick that exceeds allowable limits, before further flight, replace the driveshaft.
units.action_summary: If damage exceeds allowable limits (including cracks), replace the driveshaft before further flight.

units.obligation_text: Before installing the main driveshaft following paragraph (g)(3) of this AD, and with the engine adapter installed in the end of the engine output shaft, inspect the alignment of the main driveshaft installation between the transmission input drive quill coupling and the engine output shaft adapter by following 6–24. Alignment—Main Driveshaft, paragraphs c. through g., of TM 55–1520–210–23–1.
units.action_summary: Before installing the driveshaft (with engine adapter installed), inspect alignment between transmission quill coupling and engine output shaft adapter per TM paragraphs c–g.

units.obligation_text: If there is misalignment, before further flight, adjust the alignment by following 6–24. Alignment—Main Driveshaft, paragraphs h. through j., of TM 55–1520–210–23–1.
units.action_summary: If misalignment is detected, adjust alignment per TM paragraphs h–j before further flight.

units.obligation_text: Within 300 hours TIS after the effective date of this AD, and thereafter within intervals not to exceed 300 hours TIS, with the main driveshaft installed, accomplish the actions in paragraphs (g)(3)(i) through (iv) of this AD.
units.action_summary: Within 300 hours after the AD effective date and recurrently at intervals not exceeding 300 hours, perform the inspections/actions in paragraphs (g)(3)(i)–(iv) with the driveshaft installed.

units.obligation_text: As an optional terminating action for the requirements of this AD, you may install KAflex main driveshaft P/N SKCP3303–1.
units.action_summary: You may install KAflex main driveshaft P/N SKCP3303–1 as an optional terminating action to the AD requirements.

units.obligation_text: The Manager, DSCO Branch, FAA, has the authority to approve AMOCs for this AD, if requested using the procedures found in 14 CFR 39.19.
units.action_summary: The Manager, DSCO Branch, FAA may approve alternative methods of compliance (AMOCs) for this AD when requested per 14 CFR 39.19.

units.obligation_text: In accordance with 14 CFR 39.19, send your request to your principal inspector or local Flight Standards District Office, as appropriate.
units.action_summary: Send AMOC requests to your principal inspector or local Flight Standards District Office per 14 CFR 39.19.

units.obligation_text: If sending information directly to the manager of the certification office, send it to the attention of the person identified in Related Information.
units.actor: persons sending AMOC information directly to the manager
units.action_summary: When sending AMOC information directly to the certification office manager, address it to the person named in Related Information.
