units.obligation_text: This AD applies to CFM International, S.A. CFM56–3 and CFM56–7B model turbofan engines equipped with an accessory gearbox (AGB) assembly with the following part numbers (P/Ns):
units.actor: CFM56–3 and CFM56–7B model turbofan engines and their owners/operators
units.action_summary: Identifies which engines (and thus which owners/operators) are subject to the AD.

units.actor: CFM56–3, CFM56–3B, CFM56–3C engines (owners/operators of engines with these AGB P/Ns)
units.action_summary: Specifies the AGB part numbers on CFM56–3 series engines that make them subject to this AD.

units.actor: CFM56–7B series engines (owners/operators of engines with these AGB P/Ns)
units.action_summary: Specifies the AGB part numbers on many CFM56–7B variants that make them subject to this AD.

units.obligation_text: For CFM56–7B27A, CFM56–7B27A/3, or CFM56–7B27AE model turbofan engines, AGB P/N: 340–188–601–0, 340–188–603–0, or 340–188–605–0, installed.
units.actor: CFM56–7B27A series engines (owners/operators of engines with these AGB P/Ns)
units.action_summary: Specifies the AGB part numbers on certain CFM56–7B27A series engines that make them subject to this AD.

units.obligation_text: Comply with this AD within the compliance times specified, unless already done.
units.action_summary: Requires affected operators to comply with the AD within the specified compliance times unless the actions have already been done.

units.obligation_text: (g) Required Actions
units.actor: owners/operators and maintenance personnel of affected engines/aircraft
units.action_summary: Requires either performing an independent inspection after AGB handcranking pad cover reinstallation or inserting that inspection into the maintenance program prior to future removals.

units.obligation_text: After the effective date of this AD, after any maintenance that involves removal and re-installation of the AGB handcranking pad cover, perform an independent inspection to verify re-installation of the AGB handcranking pad cover;
units.actor: maintenance personnel/owners/operators performing maintenance involving removal and re-installation of the AGB handcranking pad cover
units.action_summary: After maintenance that removes and reinstalls the AGB handcranking pad cover, perform an independent inspection to verify it was reinstalled correctly.

units.obligation_text: Prior to the next removal of the AGB handcranking pad cover from the engine, insert the independent inspection required by paragraph (g)(1) of this AD as a required inspection item in the existing approved continuous airworthiness maintenance program for the aircraft.
units.action_summary: Before the next time the cover is removed, add the independent inspection from (g)(1) as a required inspection item to the approved continuous airworthiness maintenance program.

units.obligation_text: As a mandatory terminating action to the requirements of paragraph (g) of this AD:
units.action_summary: Describes mandatory terminating actions (replacement of affected AGBs) that, once done, terminate the inspection requirements of paragraph (g).

units.obligation_text: For affected CFM56–3, CFM56–3B, and CFM56–3C model turbofan engines, at the next engine shop visit, or before December 31, 2026, whichever occurs first after the effective date of this AD, replace the affected AGB with a part eligible for installation.
units.actor: owners/operators/maintenance providers of affected CFM56–3 series engines
units.action_summary: Replace the affected AGB with a part eligible for installation at the next engine shop visit or by 12/31/2026, whichever is earlier.

units.obligation_text: For affected CFM56–7B model turbofan engines, except for CFM56–7B27A, CFM56–7B27A/3 and CFM56–7B27AE model turbofan engines, at the next engine shop visit, or before December 31, 2024, whichever occurs first after the effective date of this AD, replace the affected AGB with a part eligible for installation.
units.actor: owners/operators/maintenance providers of affected CFM56–7B series engines (except listed exceptions)
units.action_summary: Replace the affected AGB with a part eligible for installation at the next engine shop visit or by 12/31/2024, whichever is earlier (with specified model exceptions).

units.obligation_text: For the purpose of this AD, an 'engine shop visit' is the induction of an engine into the shop for maintenance involving the separation of pairs of major mating engine case flanges, except for the following situations, which do not constitute an engine shop visit:
units.actor: definition applicable to owners/operators and maintenance providers
units.action_summary: Defines 'engine shop visit' for purposes of the AD and notes exceptions that do not count as engine shop visits.

units.obligation_text: Separation of engine flanges solely for the purposes of transportation of the engine without subsequent maintenance.
units.actor: owners/operators/maintenance providers (in determining whether an engine shop visit has occurred)
units.action_summary: Separating engine flanges only for transportation without maintenance does not count as an engine shop visit.

units.obligation_text: Separation of engine flanges solely for the purpose of replacing the fan or propulsor without subsequent maintenance.
units.actor: owners/operators/maintenance providers (in determining whether an engine shop visit has occurred)
units.action_summary: Separating engine flanges only to replace the fan or propulsor without subsequent maintenance does not count as an engine shop visit.

units.obligation_text: For the purpose of this AD, for affected CFM56–3, CFM56–3B, and CFM56–3C model turbofan engines, a part eligible for installation is:
units.actor: owners/operators/maintenance providers of affected CFM56–3 series engines
units.action_summary: Defines what constitutes a 'part eligible for installation' for CFM56–3 series engines.

units.actor: owners/operators/maintenance providers of affected CFM56–3 series engines
units.action_summary: An AGB having any part number other than the listed ones is considered eligible for installation.

units.obligation_text: An affected AGB that has been reworked and reidentified to a part number eligible for installation using CFM International Service Bulletin (SB) CFM56–3 SB 72–1129, Revision 7, dated May 5, 2020.
units.actor: owners/operators/maintenance providers of affected CFM56–3 series engines
units.action_summary: An affected AGB that has been reworked and reidentified per the specified CFM56–3 service bulletin is eligible for installation.

units.obligation_text: For the purpose of this AD, for affected CFM56–7B model turbofan engines, except for CFM56–7B27A, CFM56–7B27A/3 and CFM56–7B27AE model turbofan engines, a part eligible for installation is:
units.actor: owners/operators/maintenance providers of affected CFM56–7B series engines
units.action_summary: Defines what constitutes a 'part eligible for installation' for specified CFM56–7B series engines.

units.obligation_text: An AGB with a part number other than 340–046–503–0, 340–046–504–0, or 340–046–505–0,
units.actor: owners/operators/maintenance providers of affected CFM56–7B series engines
units.action_summary: An AGB having any part number other than the listed ones is considered eligible for installation for the affected CFM56–7B engines.

units.obligation_text: An affected AGB that has been reworked and reidentified to a part number eligible for installation using, as applicable, CFM International SB CFM56–7B SB 72–0879, Revision 6, dated March 1, 2018, or CFM International SB CFM56–7B SB 72–0564 Revision 8, dated May 6, 2020.
units.actor: owners/operators/maintenance providers of affected CFM56–7B series engines
units.action_summary: An affected AGB reworked and reidentified per the specified CFM56–7B service bulletins is eligible for installation.

title: Airworthiness Directives: The Boeing Company Airplanes

units.obligation_text: Where Boeing Alert Requirements Bulletin 757–57A0074 RB, dated June 11, 2020, specifies contacting Boeing for repair instructions: This AD requires doing the repair before further flight using a method approved in accordance with the procedures specified in paragraph (i) of this AD.

title: Airworthiness Directives: General Electric Company Turbofan Engines

units.obligation_text: The FAA must receive comments on this airworthiness directive (AD) by June 1, 2021.
units.action_summary: FAA must receive comments on the AD by June 1, 2021.

units.obligation_text: Comply with this AD within the compliance times specified, unless already done.
units.action_summary: Affected owners/operators must comply with the AD within the specified compliance times unless already done.

units.obligation_text: For all affected GEnx–1B model turbofan engines, within 120 days of the effective date of this AD, revise the operator’s existing FAA-approved minimum equipment list (MEL) by incorporating into the MEL the dispatch restriction specified in Figure 1 to paragraph (g)(1) of this AD, as a required operation or maintenance procedure.
units.action_summary: Operators of affected GEnx–1B engines must revise their FAA‑approved MEL within 120 days to include the dispatch restriction in Figure 1.

units.obligation_text: Specific alternative MEL wording to accomplish the actions specified in Figure 1 can be approved by the operator’s principal operations or maintenance inspector.
units.actor: the operator’s principal operations or maintenance inspector
units.action_summary: The principal operations or maintenance inspector may approve alternative MEL wording to accomplish the Figure 1 actions.

units.obligation_text: For all affected GEnx–2B model turbofan engines, within 120 days of the effective date of this AD, revise the operator’s existing FAA-approved MEL by incorporating into the MEL the dispatch restriction specified in Figure 2 to paragraph (g)(2) of this AD, as a required operation or maintenance procedure.
units.action_summary: Operators of affected GEnx–2B engines must revise their FAA‑approved MEL within 120 days to include the dispatch restriction in Figure 2.

units.obligation_text: Specific alternative MEL wording to accomplish the actions specified in Figure 2 can be approved by the operator’s principal operations or maintenance inspector.
units.actor: the operator’s principal operations or maintenance inspector
units.action_summary: The principal operations or maintenance inspector may approve alternative MEL wording to accomplish the Figure 2 actions.

units.obligation_text: Dispatch of an airplane is prohibited if the engine indicating and crew alerting system (EICAS) displays the status message "ENG EEC C 1 X" (where "X" is engine position: "L" or "R") and any of the following conditions exist:
units.action_summary: Operators/dispatchers are prohibited from dispatching the airplane if EICAS shows the specified 'ENG EEC C 1 X' message and any listed conditions exist.

units.obligation_text: None of the maintenance messages in the Central Maintenance Computing Function (CMCF) correlate with "ENG EEC C 1 X" status message;
units.action_summary: If no maintenance messages in the CMCF correlate with the EICAS 'ENG EEC C 1 X' message, that condition triggers the dispatch prohibition.

units.obligation_text: The following maintenance message fault codes combination exists in the CMCF for either channel A or B (where "X" is engine position: "1" or "2").
units.action_summary: If the specified combination of maintenance fault codes exists in the CMCF for either channel A or B, that condition triggers the dispatch prohibition.

units.section: Figure 1 to Paragraph (g)(1) ii — Fault Combination detail
units.obligation_text: {TLA out of range fault} {76-1953X (CH-A)} AND {73-3204X OR 73-3121X OR 73-1205X OR 73-1122X (FMV/FSV disagree fault OR FMV/FSV out of range fault on the same channel as TLA out of range fault) {76-2953X (CH-B)} AND {73-3204X OR 73-3121X OR 73-2205X OR 73-2122X}.
units.action_summary: Specifies the exact maintenance message fault code combinations in the CMCF that, if present, satisfy the condition triggering the dispatch prohibition.

units.obligation_text: For all affected engines, before the EEC reaches 11,000 cycles since new, replace the EEC MN4 microprocessor using an approved overhaul procedure.
units.action_summary: Owners/operators must replace the EEC MN4 microprocessor before it reaches 11,000 cycles since new, using an approved overhaul procedure.

units.obligation_text: Thereafter, replace the EEC MN4 microprocessor before accumulating 11,000 cycles since the last replacement.
units.action_summary: After initial replacement, the EEC MN4 microprocessor must be replaced again before it reaches 11,000 cycles since the last replacement (recurring replacement interval).

units.obligation_text: After the effective date of this AD, do not install onto any engine an EEC with a main channel board that was subject to more than three replacements of the EEC MN4 microprocessor.
units.actor: persons installing engines / maintenance personnel / operators
units.action_summary: Prohibits installing an EEC onto any engine if its main channel board has had more than three MN4 microprocessor replacements, after the AD effective date.

units.obligation_text: The Manager, ECO Branch, FAA, has the authority to approve AMOCs for this AD, if requested using the procedures found in 14 CFR 39.19.
units.action_summary: The Manager may approve alternative methods of compliance (AMOCs) for this AD when requested per 14 CFR 39.19.

units.obligation_text: if requested using the procedures found in 14 CFR 39.19
units.action_summary: Specifies that AMOC approval authority applies when a request is made using the procedures in 14 CFR 39.19.

units.obligation_text: In accordance with 14 CFR 39.19, send your request to your principal inspector or local Flight Standards District Office, as appropriate.
units.action_summary: Requestors must send AMOC requests to their principal inspector or local Flight Standards District Office per 14 CFR 39.19.

units.obligation_text: If sending information directly to the manager of the certification office, send it to the attention of the person identified in Related Information.
units.actor: requestor (person sending information directly to the manager)
units.action_summary: If sending AMOC information directly to the certification office manager, requestors must address it to the person identified in Related Information.

units.obligation_text: Information may be emailed to: ANE-AD-AMOC@faa.gov.
units.action_summary: Requestors are permitted to email AMOC information to the specified FAA email address.

units.obligation_text: Before using any approved AMOC, notify your appropriate principal inspector, or lacking a principal inspector, the manager of the local flight standards district office/certificate holding district office.
units.action_summary: Before using an approved AMOC, owners/operators must notify their principal inspector or the manager of the local FSDO/CHDO if no principal inspector exists.

units.obligation_text: Dispatch of an airplane is prohibited if the engine indicating and crew alerting system (EICAS) displays the status message "ENG X EEC Cl" (where "X" is engine position: "1," "2," "3," or "4") and any of the following conditions exist:
units.action_summary: Operators/dispatchers are prohibited from dispatching the airplane if EICAS shows the specified 'ENG X EEC Cl' message and any listed conditions exist (per Figure 2).

units.obligation_text: None of the maintenance messages in the Central Maintenance Computer (CMC) correlate with "ENG X EEC Cl" status message;
units.action_summary: If no maintenance messages in the CMC correlate with the EICAS 'ENG X EEC Cl' message, that condition triggers the dispatch prohibition for GEnx‑2B engines.

units.obligation_text: The following maintenance message fault codes combination exists in the CMC for either channel A or B (where "X" is engine position: "1," "2," "3," or "4").
units.action_summary: If the specified combination of maintenance fault codes exists in the CMC for either channel A or B, that condition triggers the dispatch prohibition for GEnx‑2B engines.

units.section: Figure 2 to Paragraph (g)(2) ii — Fault Combination detail
units.obligation_text: {TLA out of range fault} {78X13 (CH-A)} AND {7X132 OR 7X144 OR 7X130 OR 7X145} AND {FMV/FSV disagree fault OR FMV/FSV out of range fault on the same channel as TLA out of range fault} {78X14 (CH-B)} AND {7X132 OR 7X144 OR 7X133 OR 7X146}.
units.action_summary: Specifies the exact maintenance message fault code combinations in the CMC that, if present, satisfy the condition triggering the dispatch prohibition for GEnx‑2B engines.

title: Airworthiness Directives: The Boeing Company Airplanes

units.obligation_text: For AWL No. 28–AWL–03, "Fuel Quantity Indicating System (FQIS)—Out Tank Wiring Lightning Shield to Ground Termination": Within 120 months after the most recent inspection was performed as specified in AWL No. 28–AWL–03.

units.obligation_text: For AWL No. 28–AWL–14, "Main and Center Wing Tank Fueling Shutoff Valve Body and Actuator—Fault Current Bond": Within 120 months after the most recent inspection was performed as specified in AWL No. 28–AWL–14.

units.obligation_text: For AWL No. 28–AWL–21, "Over-Current and Arcing Protection Electrical Design Features Operation—Boost Pump Ground Fault Interrupter (GFI)": Within 12 months after accomplishment of the actions specified in Boeing Service Bulletin 757–28A0078 or Boeing Service Bulletin 757–28A0079, as applicable; or within 12 months after the most recent inspection was performed as specified in AWL No. 28–AWL–21; whichever occurs later.
units.action_summary: Initial compliance for AWL 28–AWL–21 must be done within 12 months after specified service bulletin actions or 12 months after the most recent specified inspection, whichever is later.

units.obligation_text: For AWL No. 28–AWL–25, "Motor Operated Valve (MOV) Actuator—Lightning and Fault Current Protection Electrical Bond": Within 72 months after accomplishment of the actions specified in Boeing Service Bulletin 757–28A0088, or within 72 months after the most recent inspection was performed as specified in AWL No. 28–AWL–25, whichever occurs later.

units.obligation_text: For AWL No. 28–AWL–26, "Center Tank Fuel Boost Pump Power Failed On Protection System": Within 12 months after accomplishment of the actions specified in Boeing Service Bulletin 757–28A0105, or within 12 months after the most recent inspection was performed as specified in AWL No. 28–AWL–26, whichever occurs later.

units.obligation_text: For AWL No. 28–AWL–30, "AC Fuel Pump Fault Current Bonding Jumper Installation, Main and Center Tank": Within 24 months after the effective date of this AD, or within 72 months after the most recent inspection was performed as specified in AWL No. 28–AWL–30, whichever occurs later.

units.obligation_text: For AWL No. 28–AWL–33, "Full Cushion Clamps and Teflon Sleeving Installed on Out-of-Tank Wire Bundles Installed on Brackets that are Mounted Directly on the Fuel Tanks": Within 24 months after the effective date of this AD; or within 144 months after accomplishment of the actions specified in Boeing Service Bulletin 757–57A0064 (Part 2 through Part 10 of the Work Instructions); or within 144 months since the most recent inspection was performed as specified in AWL No. 28–AWL–33; whichever occurs later.

units.obligation_text: For AWL No. 47–AWL–04, "NGS—NEA Distribution Ducting": Within 17,300 flight hours after accomplishment of the actions specified in Boeing Service Bulletin 757–47–0001 or Boeing Service Bulletin757–47–0005, as applicable; or within 17,300 flight hours after the most recent inspection was performed as specified in AWL No. 47–AWL–04; whichever occurs later.
units.action_summary: Initial compliance for AWL 47–AWL–04 must be done within 17,300 flight hours after specified service bulletin actions or 17,300 flight hours after the most recent specified inspection, whichever is later.

units.obligation_text: For AWL No. 47–AWL–05, "NGS—Cross Vent Check Valve": Within 17,300 flight hours after accomplishment of the actions specified in Boeing Service Bulletin 757–47–0001 or Boeing Service Bulletin 757–47–0005, as applicable; or within 17,300 flight hours after the most recent inspection was performed as specified in AWL No. 47–AWL–05; whichever occurs later.
units.action_summary: Initial compliance for AWL 47–AWL–05 must be done within 17,300 flight hours after specified service bulletin actions or 17,300 flight hours after the most recent specified inspection, whichever is later.

units.obligation_text: For AWL No. 47–AWL–07, "NGS—Thermal Switch": Within 48,000 flight hours after accomplishment of the actions specified in Boeing Service Bulletin 757–47–0001 or Boeing Service Bulletin 757–47–0005, as applicable; or within 48,000 flight hours after the most recent inspection was performed as specified in AWL No. 47–AWL–07; whichever occurs later.

units.obligation_text: As an option, when accomplishing the actions required by paragraph (g) of this AD, the alternatives specified in paragraphs (h)(1) and (2) of this AD are acceptable.

units.obligation_text: Where AWL No. 28–AWL–05 identifies wire types BMS 13–48, BMS 13–58, and BMS 13–60, the following wire types are acceptable: MIL–W–22759/16, SAE AS22759/16 (M22759/16), MIL–W–22759/32, SAE AS22759/32 (M22759/32), MIL–W–22759/34, SAE AS22759/34 (M22759/34), MIL–W–22759/41, SAE AS22759/41 (M22759/41), MIL–W–22759/86, SAE AS22759/86 (M22759/86), MIL–W–22759/87, SAE AS22759/87 (M22759/87), MIL–W–22759/92, and SAE AS22759/92 (M22759/92); and MIL–C–27500 and NEMA WC 27500 cables constructed from these military or SAE specification wire types, as applicable.

units.obligation_text: Where AWL No. 28–AWL–05 identifies TFE–2X Standard wall for wire sleeving, the following sleeving materials are acceptable: Roundit 2000NX and Varglas Type HO, HP, or HM.

title: Airworthiness Directives: General Electric Company Turbofan Engines

units.obligation_text: The FAA must receive comments on this airworthiness directive (AD) by June 21, 2021.
units.action_summary: Comments on the AD must be received by the FAA by June 21, 2021.

units.obligation_text: This AD applies to General Electric Company (GE) GE90–110B1 and GE90–115B model turbofan engines.
units.actor: owners and operators of GE90–110B1 and GE90–115B turbofan engines
units.action_summary: The AD is applicable to the specified GE90 engine models.

units.obligation_text: Comply with this AD within the compliance times specified, unless already done.
units.actor: owners and operators of the affected engines
units.action_summary: Affected owners/operators must comply with the AD within the specified compliance times unless already complied.

units.obligation_text: Within the following compliance times after the effective date of this AD, replace the full authority digital engine control (FADEC) integrated circuit (MN4) microprocessor using an approved overhaul procedure:
units.actor: owners and operators of the affected engines / maintenance providers
units.action_summary: Replace the FADEC MN4 microprocessor within the specified compliance times using an approved overhaul procedure.

units.obligation_text: For a FADEC MN4 microprocessor with 10,500 or more cycles since new (CSN), replace the FADEC MN4 microprocessor before accumulating 500 additional cycles on the FADEC MN4 microprocessor.
units.actor: owners and operators of engines with FADEC MN4 microprocessors
units.action_summary: If MN4 has 10,500 or more CSN, replace it before 500 more cycles are accumulated.

units.obligation_text: For a FADEC MN4 microprocessor with 5,000 CSN or more, but fewer than 10,500 CSN, replace the FADEC MN4 microprocessor at the next FADEC component shop visit or before accumulating 11,000 CSN on the FADEC MN4 microprocessor, whichever occurs first.
units.actor: owners and operators of engines with FADEC MN4 microprocessors
units.action_summary: If MN4 has between 5,000 and 10,499 CSN, replace it at the next component shop visit or before reaching 11,000 CSN, whichever comes first.

units.obligation_text: Thereafter, repeat the replacement of the FADEC MN4 microprocessor at the first FADEC component shop visit after accumulating 5,000 CSN since the last replacement but before accumulating 11,000 CSN since the last replacement.
units.actor: owners and operators of the affected engines / maintenance providers
units.action_summary: After initial replacement, repeat replacement at first shop visit after 5,000 CSN but before 11,000 CSN since last replacement.

units.obligation_text: After the effective date of this AD, do not install onto any engine any FADEC with a main channel board that was subject to more than three replacements of the FADEC MN4 microprocessor.
units.actor: persons installing FADEC onto engines (maintenance personnel/repair organizations)
units.action_summary: Prohibits installing a FADEC whose main channel board has had more than three MN4 microprocessor replacements.

units.obligation_text: For the purpose of this AD, an 'approved overhaul procedure' is one of the following:
units.actor: maintenance personnel / repair facilities (definition applies to them)
units.action_summary: Defines what constitutes an 'approved overhaul procedure' for purposes of the AD.

units.obligation_text: Replacement of the FADEC MN4 microprocessor using FADEC International-approved maintenance procedures;
units.action_summary: Permits replacement using FADEC International-approved maintenance procedures as an approved overhaul procedure.

units.obligation_text: Replacement of the FADEC MN4 microprocessor using the Accomplishment Instructions, paragraph 3.A., of GE GE90–100 Service Bulletin 73–0118, Revision 01, dated April 27, 2021.
units.action_summary: Permits replacement using the specified GE service bulletin instructions as an approved overhaul procedure.

units.obligation_text: For the purpose of this AD, a 'FADEC component shop visit' is the induction of the FADEC into a repair facility to perform internal maintenance on the FADEC.
units.action_summary: Defines 'FADEC component shop visit' as induction of the FADEC into a repair facility for internal maintenance.

units.obligation_text: The Manager, ECO Branch, FAA, has the authority to approve AMOCs for this AD, if requested using the procedures found in 14 CFR 39.19.
units.action_summary: Grants the Manager authority to approve alternative methods of compliance for this AD when requested per 14 CFR 39.19.

units.action_summary: AMOC requesters must send their request to their principal inspector or local FSDO per 14 CFR 39.19.

units.obligation_text: If sending information directly to the manager of the certification office, send it to the attention of the person identified in Related Information. You may email your request to: ANE-AD-AMOC@faa.gov.
units.action_summary: Specifies how to send AMOC requests directly to the manager and provides an email address; allows emailing requests to ANE-AD-AMOC@faa.gov.

units.obligation_text: Before using any approved AMOC, notify your appropriate principal inspector, or lacking a principal inspector, the manager of the local flight standards district office/certificate holding district office.
units.actor: owners and operators (users of an approved AMOC)
units.action_summary: Before using an approved AMOC, the owner/operator must notify the appropriate principal inspector or, if none, the manager of the local FSDO/CHDO.

units.action_summary: Comments on the SNPRM must be received by the FAA by June 21, 2021.

units.obligation_text: Except as specified by paragraph (h) of this AD: At the applicable times specified in the "Compliance" paragraph of Boeing Alert Requirements Bulletin B787–81205–SB320045–00 RB, Issue 001, dated November 9, 2020, do all applicable actions identified in, and in accordance with, the Accomplishment Instructions of Boeing Alert Requirements Bulletin B787–81205–SB320045–00 RB, Issue 001, dated November 9, 2020.

units.action_summary: If you perform an action identified as terminating in the requirements bulletin according to its Accomplishment Instructions, that action will terminate the applicable required actions of this AD.

units.obligation_text: Where Boeing Alert Requirements Bulletin B787–81205–SB320045–00 RB, Issue 001, dated November 9, 2020, uses the phrase "the Issue 001 date of Requirements Bulletin B787–81205–SB320045–00 RB," this AD requires using "the effective date of this AD."

units.obligation_text: Where Boeing Alert Requirements Bulletin B787–81205–SB320045–00 RB, Issue 001, dated November 9, 2020, specifies contacting Boeing for repair instructions: This AD requires doing the repair using a method approved in accordance with the procedures specified in paragraph (l) of this AD.

units.obligation_text: Where the action for "CONDITION 2" in Table 7 of the "Compliance" paragraph of Boeing Alert Requirements Bulletin B787–81205–SB320045–00 RB, Issue 001, dated November 9, 2020, specifies "Do a detailed FPI inspection of the inner cylinder lug bore for heat and friction damage," for this AD, the action is "Do a detailed and FPI inspection on the inner cylinder lug bore for heat and friction damage."
units.action_summary: For CONDITION 2, the AD requires performing a detailed and fluorescent penetrant inspection (FPI) of the inner cylinder lug bore for heat and friction damage.

units.obligation_text: Revising the existing maintenance or inspection program, as applicable, to incorporate the information in CMR item number 32–CMR–01 of Section G, "Certification Maintenance Requirement Task," of Boeing 787 Certification Maintenance Requirements (CMRs), D011Z009–03–03, dated June 2020, terminates the repetitive lubrications required by paragraph (g) of this AD.
units.action_summary: If you revise the maintenance/inspection program to incorporate the specified CMR item, that revision terminates the repetitive lubrication requirements of paragraph (g).

units.obligation_text: After the existing maintenance or inspection program has been revised as required by paragraph (i) of this AD, no alternative actions (e.g., inspections) and intervals may be used unless the actions and intervals are approved as an alternative method of compliance (AMOC) in accordance with the procedures specified in paragraph (l) of this AD.
units.action_summary: Once the maintenance/inspection program is revised per paragraph (i), you may not use alternative actions or intervals unless they are approved as an AMOC per paragraph (l).

units.obligation_text: At the applicable time specified in paragraph (k)(1) or (2) of this AD, do not install an aluminum-nickel-bronze inner cylinder bushing on a MLG inner cylinder on any airplane.
units.action_summary: Do not install an aluminum-nickel-bronze inner cylinder bushing on any main landing gear inner cylinder at the times specified in (k)(1) or (k)(2).

units.obligation_text: For airplanes with aluminum-nickel-bronze inner cylinder bushings installed on a MLG inner cylinder as of the effective date of this AD: After the bushing has been replaced with a copper-nickel-tin inner cylinder bushing.
units.actor: owners/operators/maintenance technicians of airplanes that had aluminum-nickel-bronze bushings as of the effective date
units.action_summary: For airplanes that had aluminum-nickel-bronze bushings on the effective date, the prohibition in (k) applies after the bushing has been replaced with a copper-nickel-tin bushing (timing condition).

units.obligation_text: For airplanes with copper-nickel-tin inner cylinder bushings installed on a MLG inner cylinder as of the effective date of this AD: As of the effective date of this AD.
units.actor: owners/operators/maintenance technicians of airplanes with copper-nickel-tin bushings as of the effective date
units.action_summary: For airplanes that already have copper-nickel-tin bushings on the effective date, the prohibition in (k) applies immediately as of the AD's effective date.

title: Airworthiness Directives: Pratt and Whitney Division Turbofan Engines

units.obligation_text: The FAA must receive comments on this airworthiness directive (AD) action by January 27, 2022.
units.action_summary: Submit comments so the FAA receives them by January 27, 2022.

units.obligation_text: Comply with this AD within the compliance times specified, unless already done.
units.actor: owners/operators of engines to which this AD applies
units.action_summary: Comply with all requirements of this AD within the specified compliance times unless already accomplished.

units.obligation_text: For 1st-stage LPC blades that have accumulated any number of cycles since new (CSN) greater than zero, before further flight after the effective date of this AD, perform a flow path and a mid span ultrasonic testing (UT) inspection of the 1st-stage LPC blades in accordance with the Accomplishment Instructions, Part A—Initial Inspection of All LPC Fan Blades Prior to Their Return to Service, paragraph 1.A. through C., of Pratt & Whitney Alert Service Bulletin (ASB) PW4G–112–A72–361, dated October 15, 2021 (PW4G–112–A72–361).
units.action_summary: Before next flight, perform a flow path and mid-span ultrasonic inspection of 1st-stage LPC blades with CSN > 0 per the referenced service bulletin.

units.obligation_text: New fan blades that have zero CSN do not need to undergo the initial 1st-stage LPC blade flow path and mid span UT inspection required by paragraph (g)(1)(i) of this AD
units.actor: owners/operators of new fan blades (zero CSN)
units.action_summary: New fan blades with zero cycles are exempt from the initial flow path and mid-span UT inspection required by (g)(1)(i).

units.obligation_text: New fan blades that have zero CSN ... but must undergo the repetitive inspections of paragraph (g)(2) of this AD.
units.actor: owners/operators of new fan blades (zero CSN)
units.action_summary: Even if exempt from the initial inspection, new fan blades must undergo the repetitive inspections required in (g)(2).

units.obligation_text: Within the following compliance times after the effective date of this AD, perform a thermal acoustic image (TAI) inspection of the 1st-stage LPC blades for cracks using a method approved by the FAA:
units.action_summary: Perform TAI inspections of 1st-stage LPC blades within the compliance times specified, using an FAA-approved method.

units.obligation_text: For 1st-stage LPC blades with 1,000 CSN or more, with no prior TAI inspection, inspect before further flight.
units.action_summary: If blades have ≥1,000 CSN and no prior TAI, perform a TAI inspection before the next flight.

units.obligation_text: For 1st-stage LPC blades with 1,000 flight cycles (FCs) or more since the last TAI inspection, inspect before further flight.
units.action_summary: If blades have ≥1,000 FCs since the last TAI, perform a TAI inspection before the next flight.

units.obligation_text: For 1st-stage LPC blades with fewer than 1,000 CSN, with no prior TAI inspection, inspect before accumulating 1,000 CSN.
units.action_summary: If blades have <1,000 CSN and no prior TAI, perform a TAI inspection before they reach 1,000 CSN.

units.obligation_text: For 1st-stage LPC blades with fewer than 1,000 FCs since the last TAI inspection, inspect before accumulating 1,000 FCs since the last TAI inspection.
units.action_summary: If blades have <1,000 FCs since the last TAI, perform a TAI inspection before they reach 1,000 FCs since that inspection.

units.obligation_text: Before exceeding 275 FCs since the last flow path UT inspection, and thereafter at intervals not exceeding 275 FCs since the last flow path UT inspection, perform a flow path UT inspection of the 1st-stage LPC blades in accordance with the Accomplishment Instructions, Part B—Repetitive Inspection of All LPC Fan Blades After Their Return to Service, paragraph 1.A., of PW4G–112–A72–361.
units.action_summary: Perform flow path UT inspections before exceeding 275 FCs since the last such inspection and repeat at intervals not exceeding 275 FCs.

units.obligation_text: Before exceeding 550 FCs since the last mid span UT inspection, and thereafter at intervals not exceeding 550 FCs since the last mid span UT inspection, perform a mid span UT inspection of the 1st-stage LPC blades in accordance with the Accomplishment Instructions, Part B—Repetitive Inspection of All LPC Fan Blades After Their Return to Service, paragraphs 1.B. and C., of PW4G–112–A72–361.
units.action_summary: Perform mid-span UT inspections before exceeding 550 FCs since the last mid-span UT and repeat at intervals not exceeding 550 FCs.

units.obligation_text: Before exceeding 1,000 FCs since the last TAI inspection, and thereafter at intervals not exceeding 1,000 FCs since the last TAI inspection, perform repetitive TAI inspections of the 1st-stage LPC blades using a method approved by the FAA.
units.action_summary: Perform TAI inspections before exceeding 1,000 FCs since the last TAI and repeat at intervals not exceeding 1,000 FCs using an FAA-approved method.

units.obligation_text: If any 1st-stage LPC blade fails any inspection required by paragraphs (g)(1) or (2) of this AD, before further flight, remove the 1st-stage LPC blade from service and replace with a part eligible for installation.
units.action_summary: If a blade fails any required inspection, remove it from service and replace it with an eligible part before next flight.

units.obligation_text: Special flight permits, as described in 14 CFR 21.197 and 21.199, are not permitted except for airplanes on which the actions specified in paragraphs (h)(1) and (2) of this AD have been done.
units.action_summary: Special flight permits are prohibited unless the actions in (h)(1) and (h)(2) have been accomplished.

units.obligation_text: A flow path UT inspection of the 1st-stage LPC blades for cracking has been done as specified in the Accomplishment Instructions, Part A—Initial Inspection of All LPC Fan Blades Prior to their Return to Service, paragraph 1.A., of PW4G–112–A72–361, and the 1st-stage LPC blades have been found serviceable.
units.action_summary: To qualify for a special flight permit, perform the specified flow path UT inspection and ensure blades are found serviceable.

units.obligation_text: A functional check of the left and right hydraulic pump shutoff valves to ensure they close in response to the fire handle input and all applicable corrective actions (i.e., repair) within 10 days prior to flight.
units.action_summary: To qualify for a special flight permit, perform the hydraulic pump shutoff valve functional check and any required corrective actions within 10 days before flight.

units.obligation_text: This paragraph provides credit for the actions specified in paragraphs (g)(1) and (h)(1) of this AD, if those actions were performed before the effective date of this AD using the service information specified in paragraphs (i)(1), (2), or (3) of this AD.
units.action_summary: Operators who previously performed the specified actions using the listed service information receive credit for those actions.

units.action_summary: Prior flow path UT inspections performed per paragraph 2 of Special Instruction No. 85F21 qualify for credit.

units.obligation_text: Paragraph 1.a) through c) of the Accomplishment Instructions of Pratt & Whitney Special Instruction No. 130F–21, dated July 1, 2021, for a flow path and a mid span UT inspection.
units.action_summary: Prior flow path and mid-span UT inspections performed per paragraph 1.a–c of Special Instruction No. 130F–21 qualify for credit.

units.obligation_text: Paragraph 2.a) through c) of the Accomplishment Instructions of Pratt & Whitney Special Instruction No. 130F–21, Revision A, dated July 28, 2021, for a flow path and a mid span UT inspection.
units.action_summary: Prior flow path and mid-span UT inspections performed per paragraph 2.a–c of Special Instruction No. 130F–21 Revision A qualify for credit.

units.action_summary: The Manager of the ECO Branch may approve alternative methods of compliance for this AD if requested per 14 CFR 39.19.

title: Medical Certification Standards for Commercial Balloon Operations

units.obligation_text: A private pilot may act as pilot in command or serve as a required flightcrew member of an aircraft without holding a medical certificate issued under part 67 of this chapter provided the pilot holds a valid U.S. driver’s license, meets the requirements of § 61.23(c)(3), and complies with this section and all of the following conditions and limitations:
units.action_summary: Permitted to act as pilot in command or required flightcrew member without a part 67 medical certificate if the pilot holds a valid U.S. driver's license, meets §61.23(c)(3), and complies with this section's conditions and limitations.

units.obligation_text: Complete the medical education course set forth in § 68.3 of this chapter during the 24 calendar months before acting as pilot in command or serving as a required flightcrew member in an operation conducted under § 61.113(i) and retain a certification of course completion in accordance with § 68.3(b)(1) of this chapter;
units.actor: the individual seeking to act as pilot in command or serve as a required flightcrew member
units.action_summary: Must complete the §68.3 medical education course within the 24 months before acting under §61.113(i) and retain the course completion certification.

units.obligation_text: Receive a comprehensive medical examination from a State-licensed physician during the 48 months before acting as pilot in command or serving as a required flightcrew member of an operation conducted under § 61.113(i) and that medical examination is conducted in accordance with the requirements in part 68 of this chapter;
units.actor: the individual seeking to act as pilot in command or serve as a required flightcrew member
units.action_summary: Must receive a comprehensive medical exam from a State-licensed physician within 48 months before acting under §61.113(i), conducted in accordance with part 68 requirements.

units.obligation_text: If the individual has been diagnosed with any medical condition that may impact the ability of the individual to fly, be under the care and treatment of a State-licensed physician when acting as pilot in command or serving as a required flightcrew member of an operation conducted under § 61.113(i).
units.actor: the individual seeking to act as pilot in command or serve as a required flightcrew member
units.action_summary: If diagnosed with any medical condition that may affect fitness to fly, the individual must be under the care and treatment of a State-licensed physician when acting under §61.113(i).

units.obligation_text: The medical education course required to act as pilot in command or serve as a required flightcrew member in an operation under § 61.113(i) of this chapter must—
units.action_summary: The medical education course required for acting under §61.113(i) must meet specified requirements (content/standards) set forth by the regulation.

units.obligation_text: Upon successful completion of the medical education course, the following items must be electronically provided to the individual seeking to act as pilot in command or serve as a required flightcrew member under the conditions and limitations of § 61.113(i) of this chapter and transmitted to the FAA—
units.actor: the entity responsible for course completion (course provider)
units.action_summary: Upon course completion, specified items must be electronically provided to the individual and transmitted to the FAA.

units.obligation_text: An individual who has met the qualifications to operate an aircraft under § 61.113(i) of this chapter and is seeking to act as a pilot in command or serve as a required flightcrew member under that section must have completed the process for obtaining an Authorization for Special Issuance of a Medical Certificate for each of the following:
units.actor: an individual who has met the qualifications to operate under §61.113(i) and is seeking to act as pilot in command or required flightcrew member
units.action_summary: Such an individual must have completed the Special Issuance Authorization process for a medical certificate as specified.

units.obligation_text: This AD applies to the following Bell Textron Inc. helicopters certificated in any category, with a tailboom left hand fin spar cap (spar cap) part number 212–030–447–117 installed.
units.actor: Bell Textron Inc. helicopters with spar cap P/N 212–030–447–117
units.action_summary: Identifies which helicopters are subject to this AD.

units.obligation_text: Comply with this AD within the compliance times specified, unless already done.
units.action_summary: Comply with all requirements of this AD within the specified compliance times unless already accomplished.

units.obligation_text: Within 100 hours time-in-service (TIS) after the effective date of this AD, and thereafter at intervals not to exceed 100 hours TIS:
units.action_summary: Perform the following inspections within 100 hours TIS after the AD effective date and repeat at intervals not to exceed 100 hours TIS.

units.obligation_text: Using a 10x or higher power magnifying glass and a flashlight, inspect both flanges of the spar cap between fin station (F.S.) 50 and F.S. 71 for any crack, loose rivet, and other damage such as a scratch, dent, spalling, or corrosion, as depicted in Figure 1 of Bell Alert Service Bulletin (ASB) 205–20–116, ASB 205B–20–69, ASB 210–20–13, ASB 212–20–162, ASB 412–20–180, or ASB 412CF–20–67, each dated April 15, 2020, as applicable to your helicopter.
units.actor: Owners/operators/maintenance personnel of the affected helicopters
units.action_summary: Inspect both spar cap flanges between F.S. 50 and F.S. 71 with 10x or greater magnification and a flashlight for cracks, loose rivets, or other damage, per the referenced ASB.

units.obligation_text: If either spar cap flange is cracked, has a loose rivet, or has other damage, remove the spar cap from service before further flight.
units.action_summary: If inspection finds cracking, loose rivets, or damage on a spar cap flange, remove that spar cap from service before the next flight.

units.obligation_text: Inspect the exterior of the fin skin in the area that contacts the spar cap for any crack, loose rivets, and distortion.
units.actor: Owners/operators/maintenance personnel of the affected helicopters
units.action_summary: Inspect the exterior fin skin where it contacts the spar cap for cracks, loose rivets, or distortion.

units.obligation_text: If there is any crack, loose rivet, or distortion in the fin skin in the area that contacts the spar cap, remove the spar cap from service before further flight.
units.action_summary: If fin skin inspection reveals cracking, loose rivets, or distortion where it contacts the spar cap, remove the spar cap from service before flight.

units.obligation_text: The FAA amends § 39.13 by: a. Removing Airworthiness Directive 2020–23–05, Amendment 39–21321 (85 FR 73604, November 19, 2020); and b. Adding the following new airworthiness directive:
units.action_summary: Remove AD 2020–23–05 and add the new airworthiness directive to § 39.13.

units.obligation_text: Comply with this AD within the compliance times specified, unless already done.
units.action_summary: Comply with this AD within the specified compliance times unless already accomplished.

units.obligation_text: Before further flight, review Appendix 4.A. of Airbus Helicopters Emergency Alert Service Bulletin No. 05A051, Revision 2, dated February 26, 2019 (EASB 05A051) to determine the date of manufacture of the swashplate.
units.action_summary: Before further flight, review Appendix 4.A. of EASB 05A051 to determine swashplate manufacture date.

units.obligation_text: If the swashplate has accumulated 12 or more years since the date of manufacture, remove from service the swashplate.
units.action_summary: Remove the swashplate from service if it is 12 or more years old.

units.obligation_text: If the swashplate has accumulated less than 12 years since the date of manufacture, create a component history card or equivalent record indicating a life limit of 12 years since the date of manufacture.
units.action_summary: Create a component history card or equivalent record showing a 12-year life limit for the swashplate.

units.obligation_text: Thereafter, continue to record the life limit of the swashplate on its component history card or equivalent record and remove from service any swashplate before accumulating 12 years since the date of manufacture.
units.action_summary: Continue to record the swashplate life limit and remove any swashplate before it reaches 12 years since manufacture.

units.obligation_text: For each swashplate that has accumulated less than 7 years since the date of manufacture, within 15 hours time-in-service (TIS) or 7 days, whichever occurs first after the effective date of this AD, and thereafter at intervals not to exceed 15 hours TIS or 7 days, whichever occurs first, until the swashplate accumulates 7 years since the date of manufacture, visually inspect each yoke for a crack, paying particular attention to the areas shown in Details B, C, and D of Figure 1 of EASB 05A05.
units.action_summary: For swashplates <7 years old, perform initial and recurring visual inspections of each yoke at specified intervals until 7 years old.

units.obligation_text: If no cracks are visually detected, before further flight, perform a dye penetrant inspection of the yoke for a crack.
units.action_summary: If no crack is seen visually, perform a dye penetrant inspection before further flight.

units.obligation_text: If there is a crack on a yoke, before further flight, remove from service the swashplate.
units.action_summary: If a yoke crack is found, remove the swashplate from service before further flight.

units.obligation_text: For each swashplate that has accumulated 7 or more years, but less than 12 years, since the date of manufacture, within 100 hours TIS:
units.action_summary: For swashplates aged 7 to <12 years, perform the specified actions within 100 hours TIS.

units.obligation_text: Remove the grease from areas (E), (F), (G), (H), (J), and (K) of each yoke as shown in Details B, C, and D of Figure 1 of EASB 05A051. Using a plastic spatula, strip areas (E), (F), (G), (H), (J), and (K) of each yoke as shown in Details B, C, and D of Figure 1 of EASB 05A051.
units.action_summary: Within 100 hours TIS, remove grease from specified yoke areas and strip those areas using a plastic spatula.

units.obligation_text: Do not use a metal tool to strip any area of a yoke.
units.action_summary: Prohibited to use metal tools when stripping any area of a yoke.

units.obligation_text: Inspect areas (E), (F), (G), (H), (J) and (K) of each yoke as shown in Details B, C, and D of Figure 1 of EASB 05A051 for corrosion, pitting, and loss of material.
units.action_summary: Inspect the specified yoke areas for corrosion, pitting, and material loss.

units.obligation_text: If there is any corrosion less than 0.0078 in. (0.2 mm), before further flight, remove the corrosion and apply varnish (Vernelec 43022 or equivalent) to the surface of areas (E), (F), (G), (H), (J) and (K).
units.action_summary: If corrosion is <0.0078 in., remove corrosion and apply specified varnish before further flight.

units.obligation_text: If there is any pitting or loss of material of less than 0.0078 in. (0.2 mm), before further flight, remove the damage by sanding with sandpaper 200/400 or 330.
units.action_summary: If pitting/loss <0.0078 in., remove damage by sanding with specified sandpaper before further flight.

units.obligation_text: If there is any corrosion, pitting, or loss of material of 0.0078 in. (0.2 mm) or greater, before further flight, remove from service the swashplate.
units.action_summary: If corrosion/pitting/loss ≥0.0078 in., remove the swashplate from service before further flight.

units.obligation_text: Visually inspect each yoke for a crack, paying particular attention to the areas shown in Details B, C, and D of Figure 1 of EASB 05A051.
units.action_summary: Visually inspect each yoke for cracks, focusing on specified areas.

units.obligation_text: If there are no cracks, before further flight, perform a dye penetrant inspection of the yoke for a crack.
units.action_summary: If no cracks are found visually, perform a dye penetrant inspection before further flight.

units.obligation_text: If there is a crack on a yoke, before further flight, remove from service the swashplate.
units.action_summary: If a crack is found, remove the swashplate from service before further flight.

units.obligation_text: If you performed the actions in paragraph (g)(4) of this AD before the effective date of this AD using Airbus Helicopters Emergency Alert Service Bulletin No. 05A051, Revision 1, dated November 16, 2017, you have met the requirements of paragraph (g)(4) of this AD.
units.action_summary: Credit is granted if actions of paragraph (g)(4) were performed previously per Revision 1 of the service bulletin.

units.obligation_text: The Manager, International Validation Branch, FAA, has the authority to approve AMOCs for this AD, if requested using the procedures found in 14 CFR 39.19.
units.actor: The Manager, International Validation Branch, FAA
units.action_summary: The Manager may approve alternative methods of compliance (AMOCs) for this AD following 14 CFR 39.19 procedures.

units.obligation_text: In accordance with 14 CFR 39.19, send your request to your principal inspector or local Flight Standards District Office, as appropriate.
units.action_summary: Send AMOC requests to your principal inspector or local FSDO per 14 CFR 39.19.

units.obligation_text: If sending information directly to the manager of the International Validation Branch, send it to the attention of the person identified in paragraph (j)(1) of this AD.
units.action_summary: If sending AMOC information directly to the manager, address it to the person in paragraph (j)(1).

units.obligation_text: Information may be emailed to: 9-AVS-AIR-730-AMOC@faa.gov.
units.action_summary: AMOC information may be submitted via the specified email address.

units.obligation_text: Before using any approved AMOC, notify your appropriate principal inspector, or lacking a principal inspector, the manager of the local flight standards district office/ certificate holding district office.
units.action_summary: Notify the appropriate principal inspector or local FSDO/CHDO manager before using an approved AMOC.

units.obligation_text: The FAA must receive comments on this airworthiness directive (AD) by May 5, 2022.
units.action_summary: Receive comments on the AD by May 5, 2022.

units.obligation_text: Comply with this AD within the compliance times specified, unless already done.
units.action_summary: Comply with all requirements of this AD within the specified compliance times unless already accomplished.

units.obligation_text: For Group 1 engines with an affected HPT rotor stage 1 blade installed: Borescope Inspection (BSI) of HPT rotor stage 1 blades and HPT stator stage 1 nozzle set is required.
units.actor: Operators of Group 1 engines with an affected HPT rotor stage 1 blade installed
units.action_summary: Require borescope inspections of HPT rotor stage 1 blades and HPT stator stage 1 nozzle set for Group 1 engines with affected blades.

units.obligation_text: Within 100 flight cycles (FCs) after accumulating 800 MENA takeoffs on the HPT rotor stage 1 blade, before the HPT rotor stage 1 blade accumulates 1,750 cycles since new (CSN), or within 100 FCs after the effective date of this AD, whichever occurs later, perform an initial BSI of the HPT rotor stage 1 blades and HPT stator stage 1 nozzle set in accordance with the Accomplishment Instructions, paragraphs 5.E.(1)(c) and 5.E.(1)(d), of CFM Service Bulletin LEAP–1A–72–00–0461–01A–930A–D, Issue 002–00, dated December 21, 2021 (the SB).
units.actor: Operators of Group 1 engines with an affected HPT rotor stage 1 blade installed
units.action_summary: Perform an initial borescope inspection within the specified flight cycle/time thresholds per the referenced service bulletin.

units.obligation_text: Thereafter, at intervals not to exceed 150 FCs since the last BSI, perform a repetitive BSI of the HPT rotor stage 1 blades and HPT stator stage 1 nozzle set in accordance with the Accomplishment Instructions, paragraphs 5.E.(1)(c) and 5.E.(1)(d), of the SB.
units.actor: Operators of Group 1 engines with an affected HPT rotor stage 1 blade installed
units.action_summary: Perform repetitive borescope inspections every 150 flight cycles or less per the referenced service bulletin.

units.obligation_text: For Group 2 engines with an affected HPT rotor stage 1 blade installed: Borescope Inspection (BSI) of HPT rotor stage 1 blades and HPT stator stage 1 nozzle set is required.
units.actor: Operators of Group 2 engines with an affected HPT rotor stage 1 blade installed
units.action_summary: Require borescope inspections of HPT rotor stage 1 blades and HPT stator stage 1 nozzle set for Group 2 engines with affected blades.

units.obligation_text: Within 100 FCs after accumulating 800 MENA takeoffs on the HPT rotor stage 1 blade, before the HPT rotor stage 1 blade accumulates 2,600 CSN, or within 100 FCs after the effective date of this AD, whichever occurs later, perform an initial BSI of the HPT rotor stage 1 blades and HPT stator stage 1 nozzle set in accordance with the Accomplishment Instructions, paragraphs 5.E.(1)(c) and 5.E.(1)(d), of the SB.
units.actor: Operators of Group 2 engines with an affected HPT rotor stage 1 blade installed
units.action_summary: Perform an initial borescope inspection within the specified flight cycle/time thresholds per the referenced service bulletin.

units.obligation_text: Thereafter, at intervals not to exceed 300 FCs since the last BSI, perform a repetitive BSI of the HPT rotor stage 1 blades and HPT stator stage 1 nozzle set in accordance with the Accomplishment Instructions, paragraphs 5.E.(1)(c) and 5.E.(1)(d), of the SB.
units.actor: Operators of Group 2 engines with an affected HPT rotor stage 1 blade installed
units.action_summary: Perform repetitive borescope inspections every 300 flight cycles or less per the referenced service bulletin.

units.obligation_text: Based on the results of the BSI required by paragraph (g)(1) or (2) of this AD, as applicable, either re-inspect or replace the HPT rotor stage 1 blades or HPT stator stage 1 nozzle set using the criteria, compliance times, and procedures referenced in the Accomplishment Instructions, paragraph 5.E.(1)(f), of the SB.
units.action_summary: Depending on inspection results, re-inspect or replace the affected blades or nozzle set following criteria and times in the referenced service bulletin.

units.obligation_text: Based on the BSI results disposition required by paragraph (g)(3) of this AD, if re-inspection or replacement of the HPT rotor stage 1 blades or HPT stator stage 1 nozzle set is required within 50 FCs based on the criteria, compliance times, and procedures referenced in the Accomplishment Instructions, paragraph 5.E.(1)(f), of the SB, then perform the actions required in paragraph (g)(4)(ii) of this AD.
units.action_summary: If re-inspection or replacement is required within 50 FCs based on prior results, then perform the sister-engine actions specified in (g)(4)(ii).

units.obligation_text: Within 5 FCs after performing the inspection required by paragraph (g)(1) or (2) of this AD, as applicable, either inspect or replace the HPT rotor stage 1 blades or HPT stator stage 1 nozzle set on the sister engine using the procedures and compliance times in the Accomplishment Instructions, paragraph, 5.E.(1)(g), of the SB.
units.actor: Operators/maintenance personnel of the sister engine (other engine on same airplane)
units.action_summary: Within 5 flight cycles after the inspection of the affected engine, inspect or replace the sister engine's blades or nozzle set per the service bulletin procedures and timing.

units.obligation_text: Where the SB specifies to remove the engine, this AD requires replacement of the HPT rotor stage 1 blades or HPT stator stage 1 nozzle set, as applicable.
units.action_summary: If the service bulletin directs engine removal, the AD mandates replacement of the affected parts rather than just removal.

units.obligation_text: If, during any inspection required by paragraph (g)(1), (2), (3), or (4) of this AD, as applicable, any HPT unserviceable finding is found on an engine as identified in the Accomplishment Instructions, paragraph 5.E.(1)(f) of the SB, within 30 days of performing the inspection, report the HPT unserviceable finding to CFM in accordance with the Accomplishment Instructions, paragraph 5.E.(1)(f)1, of the SB.
units.actor: Operators/maintenance personnel who find HPT unserviceable findings during required inspections
units.action_summary: Report any HPT unserviceable findings identified during required inspections to CFM within 30 days in accordance with the referenced service bulletin.

units.obligation_text: Within 2,000 flight hours since the last functional test of the cabin altitude pressure switches.
units.action_summary: One timing option: perform the functional test within 2,000 flight hours since the last test.

units.obligation_text: Prior to the accumulation of 2,000 total flight hours on the airplane.
units.action_summary: One timing option: perform the functional test before the airplane accumulates 2,000 total flight hours.

units.obligation_text: Within 90 days after the effective date of this AD.
units.action_summary: One timing option: perform the functional test within 90 days after this AD becomes effective.

units.obligation_text: Repeat the functional test thereafter at intervals not to exceed 2,000 flight hours.
units.action_summary: Conduct repeat functional tests at intervals no longer than 2,000 flight hours.

units.obligation_text: If, during any functional test, any cabin altitude pressure switch fails to activate at an altitude of between 9,000 and 11,000 feet, replace the switch before further flight.
units.action_summary: If a switch fails to activate between 9,000 and 11,000 ft during test, replace that switch prior to the next flight.

title: Installation and Operation of Flightdeck Installed Physical Secondary Barriers on Transport Category Airplanes

units.obligation_text: An installed physical secondary barrier (IPSB) must be installed to resist intrusion into the flightdeck whenever the flightdeck door is opened.
units.action_summary: Install an IPSB that resists intrusion into the flightdeck whenever the flightdeck door is opened.

units.obligation_text: In addition, when deployed, the IPSB must:
units.action_summary: When deployed, the IPSB must meet the following performance requirements.

units.obligation_text: Resist a 250 pound (1,113 Newtons) static load in the direction of the passenger cabin applied at the most critical locations on the IPSB;
units.action_summary: Resist a 250-pound static load toward the passenger cabin at the most critical locations.

units.obligation_text: Resist a 600 pound (2,669 Newtons) static load in the direction of the flightdeck applied at the most critical locations on the IPSB;
units.action_summary: Resist a 600-pound static load toward the flightdeck at the most critical locations.

units.obligation_text: Delay a person attempting to access the flightdeck by at least the time required for a crewmember to open and reclose the flightdeck door, but no less than 5 seconds;
units.action_summary: Delay a person attempting to access the flightdeck by at least the time for a crewmember to open and reclose the flightdeck door, minimum 5 seconds.

units.obligation_text: Prevent a person from reaching through and touching the flight deck door;
units.action_summary: Prevent a person from reaching through and touching the flight deck door when deployed.

units.obligation_text: Allow for necessary crewmember activities.
units.action_summary: Allow necessary crewmember activities while deployed.

units.obligation_text: For airplanes required by paragraph (f) of this section to have a door between the passenger and pilot or crew rest compartments, and for transport category airplanes that have a door installed between the pilot compartment and any other occupied compartment, that were manufactured after [DATE TWO YEARS AFTER THE EFFECTIVE DATE OF THE FINAL RULE], an installed physical secondary barrier (IPSB) that provides line-of-sight visibility between the flightdeck door and the cabin, and meets the requirements of § 25.795(a)(4) in effect on [EFFECTIVE DATE OF THE FINAL RULE].
units.actor: transport category airplanes manufactured after [DATE TWO YEARS AFTER THE EFFECTIVE DATE OF THE FINAL RULE] (and their manufacturers/owners/operators)
units.action_summary: Such airplanes must have an IPSB providing line-of-sight visibility between the flightdeck door and cabin and meeting §25.795(a)(4) requirements as of the effective date.

units.obligation_text: AD 2021–23–17 requires amending the existing aircraft flight manual (AFM) by inserting abnormal propeller vibration instructions, visual inspection and non-destructive test (NDT) inspection of the propeller hub and, depending on the results of the inspections, replacement of the propeller hub with a part eligible for installation.
units.actor: owners/operators of aircraft with affected Hoffmann HO–V 72 propellers
units.action_summary: Amend the AFM to include abnormal propeller vibration instructions; perform visual and NDT inspections of the propeller hub; replace the hub if inspection results require.

units.obligation_text: This proposed AD would also require a maintenance records review and, depending on the results of the maintenance records review, tightening of each propeller blade retention nut to specific torque values.
units.action_summary: Require a maintenance records review and, if indicated by the review, tighten each propeller blade retention nut to specified torque values.

units.obligation_text: Depending on the results of the maintenance records review, tightening of each propeller blade retention nut to specific torque values.
units.action_summary: If maintenance records indicate, tighten each propeller blade retention nut to specified torque values.

units.obligation_text: Depending on the results of the maintenance records review, this proposed AD would require physically inspecting the propeller blade for shake.
units.action_summary: If indicated by the maintenance records review, perform a physical inspection of each propeller blade for shake.

units.obligation_text: If any axial play is detected during the performance of the inspection, this proposed AD would require the removal of the propeller from service.
units.action_summary: If axial play is detected during inspection, remove the propeller from service.

units.obligation_text: If any axial play is detected during the performance of the inspection, this proposed AD would require ... the performance of an NDT inspection of the propeller hub.
units.action_summary: If axial play is detected during inspection, perform an NDT inspection of the propeller hub.
