units.obligation_text: The FAA must receive comments on this airworthiness directive (AD) by November 4, 2022.
units.action_summary: Receive comments on this AD by November 4, 2022.

units.obligation_text: Comply with this AD within the compliance times specified, unless already done.
units.action_summary: Comply with all requirements of this AD within the specified compliance times unless already done.

units.obligation_text: Within 50 hours TIS after the effective date of this AD, review the aircraft maintenance records to determine the number of hours TIS accumulated on each v-band coupling.
units.action_summary: Review maintenance records within 50 hours TIS after the AD effective date to determine hours on each v-band coupling.

units.obligation_text: Within the compliance times specified in paragraph (i)(1)(i) or (ii) or (i)(2) of this AD, remove the v-band coupling from service and install a new v-band coupling. Apply correct torque as necessary to the v-band coupling nut.
units.action_summary: Remove the v-band coupling and install a new one within the specified compliance times and apply correct torque to the nut.

units.obligation_text: If the v-band coupling has accumulated less than 500 hours TIS: Initially remove the v-band coupling from service before it accumulates 500 hours TIS or within 50 hours TIS after the effective date of this AD, whichever occurs later. Thereafter, remove the v-band coupling from service before it accumulates 500 hours TIS.
units.action_summary: If coupling has <500 hours TIS, remove it before 500 hours (or within 50 hours after effective date if later) and thereafter remove before 500 hours.

units.obligation_text: If the v-band coupling has accumulated 500 or more hours TIS or if the hours TIS of the v-band coupling cannot be determined: Initially remove the v-band coupling from service within 50 hours TIS after the effective date of this AD. Thereafter, remove the v-band coupling from service before it accumulates 500 hours TIS.
units.action_summary: If coupling has ≥500 hours or hours unknown, initially remove within 50 hours after effective date and thereafter before 500 hours.

units.obligation_text: As an alternative to initially removing the v-band coupling from service as required by paragraph (i)(1) of this AD, you may perform the inspections required by paragraphs (j)(1) through (7) or (k) of this AD.
units.action_summary: May perform specified inspections (paragraphs j or k) instead of initially removing the v-band coupling from service as required by paragraph (i)(1).

units.obligation_text: Do the initial inspections at the time the v-band coupling would have been removed from service and thereafter at intervals not to exceed 6 months or 100 hours TIS, whichever occurs first, for a period not to exceed 2 years after the effective date of this AD.
units.action_summary: If using inspections instead of removal, perform initial inspection at the removal time and repeat every 6 months or 100 hours TIS (whichever first) for up to 2 years after effective date.

units.obligation_text: If the v-band coupling fails to meet any inspection criteria in paragraphs (j)(1) through (7) or (k) of this AD, it must be removed from service before further flight.
units.action_summary: If any inspection criteria are failed, remove the v-band coupling from service before further flight.

units.obligation_text: At the next annual inspection after the effective date of this AD or within the next 12 months after the effective date of this AD, whichever occurs first, and repetitively thereafter at intervals not to exceed 12 months, visually inspect the v-band coupling as required by paragraphs (j)(1) through (7) of this AD.
units.action_summary: At next annual inspection or within 12 months and thereafter every 12 months, visually inspect the v-band coupling as specified in j(1)–(7).

units.obligation_text: Inspect the v-band coupling and area around the v-band coupling for exhaust stains, sooting, and discoloration. If any of those conditions are found, remove the coupling and, instead of the inspections in paragraphs (j)(2) through (7) of this AD, do the inspections in paragraph (k) of this AD.
units.action_summary: Inspect for exhaust stains/sooting/discoloration; if found, remove coupling and perform inspections in paragraph k instead of j(2)–(7).

units.obligation_text: Inspect the v-band coupling outer band for cracks, paying particular attention to the spot weld areas. If there is a crack, before further flight, remove the v-band coupling from service and install a new v-band coupling.
units.action_summary: Inspect outer band for cracks; if crack found, remove and install new coupling before further flight.

units.obligation_text: Inspect the v-band coupling for looseness and for separation of the outer band from the v-retainer segments at all spot welds. If there is any looseness or separation of the outer band from any retainer segment, before further flight, remove the v-band coupling from service and install a new v-band coupling.
units.action_summary: Inspect for looseness or separation; if any, remove and install new coupling before further flight.

units.obligation_text: Inspect the v-band coupling outer band for cupping, bowing, and crowning as depicted in figure 1 to paragraph (k)(1)(iii) of this AD. If there is any cupping, bowing, or crowning, before further flight, remove the coupling and, instead of the inspections in paragraphs (j)(5) through (7) of this AD, do the inspections in paragraph (k) of this AD.
units.action_summary: Inspect outer band for cupping/bowing/crowning; if found, remove coupling and perform paragraph k inspections instead of j(5)–(7) before further flight.

units.obligation_text: Inspect the area of the v-band coupling, including the outer band, opposite the t-bolt for damage and distortion. If there is any damage or distortion, before further flight, remove the v-band coupling from service and install a new v-band coupling.
units.action_summary: Inspect area opposite t-bolt for damage/distortion; if any, remove and install new coupling before further flight.

units.obligation_text: Using a mirror, inspect the v-band coupling to determine whether there is a space between the two v-retainer coupling segments next to the t-bolt. If there is no space between the two v-retainer coupling segments next to the t-bolt, before further flight, remove the v-band coupling from service and install a new v-band coupling.
units.action_summary: Using a mirror, inspect for space between v-retainer segments next to t-bolt; if no space, remove and install new coupling before further flight.

units.obligation_text: Determine whether the v-band coupling nut is properly torqued and apply correct torque as necessary.
units.action_summary: Check nut torque and apply correct torque if necessary.

units.obligation_text: Removing the v-band coupling from service and installing a new v-band coupling does not terminate the requirement to do these repetitive inspections.
units.action_summary: Even if the coupling is removed and replaced, the repetitive inspection requirement continues.

units.obligation_text: Remove the v-band coupling and do the inspections in paragraphs (k)(1) and (2) of this AD if required by paragraph (j)(1) or (4) of this AD or as an alternative to the inspections required by paragraph (j) of this AD.
units.action_summary: If required by j(1) or j(4), or as an alternative to paragraph j, remove the coupling and perform inspections in k(1) and k(2).

units.obligation_text: Using crocus cloth and mineral spirits or Stoddard solvent, clean the outer band of the v-band coupling. Pay particular attention to the spot weld areas on the v-band coupling.
units.action_summary: Clean the outer band with crocus cloth and specified solvents, focusing on spot weld areas.

units.obligation_text: If there is corrosion that cannot be removed by cleaning or if there is pitting, before further flight, remove the v-band coupling from service and install a new v-band coupling.
units.action_summary: If corrosion cannot be removed or there is pitting, remove and replace the v-band coupling before further flight.

units.obligation_text: Using a 10X magnifying glass, visually inspect the outer band for cracks, paying particular attention to the spot weld areas. If there is a crack, before further flight, remove the v-band coupling from service and install a new v-band coupling.
units.action_summary: Use 10X magnifier to inspect outer band for cracks; if crack found, remove and install new coupling before further flight.

units.obligation_text: Visually inspect the flatness of the outer band using a straight edge. Lay the straight edge across the width of the outer band as depicted in figure 1 to paragraph (k)(1)(iii) of this AD. If the gap between the outer band and the straight edge exceeds 0.062 inch, before further flight, remove the v-band coupling from service and install a new v-band coupling.
units.action_summary: Inspect flatness with straight edge; if gap >0.062 inch, remove and replace coupling before further flight.

units.obligation_text: With the t-bolt in the 12 o'clock position, visually inspect the attachment of the outer band to the v-retainer coupling segments for gaps between the outer band and the v-retainer coupling segments from the 1 o'clock through 11 o'clock positions. If there are any gaps between the outer band and the v-retainer coupling segments, before further flight, remove the v-band coupling from service and install a new v-band coupling.
units.action_summary: With t-bolt at 12 o'clock, inspect for gaps between outer band and retainer segments; if any gaps, remove and replace coupling before further flight.

units.obligation_text: Visually inspect the bend radii of the v-retainer coupling segments, throughout the length of the segment, as depicted in figure 1 to paragraph (k)(1)(iii) of this AD, for cracks. If there are any cracks, before further flight, remove the v-band coupling from service and install a new v-band coupling.
units.action_summary: Inspect bend radii for cracks; if any, remove and install new coupling before further flight.

units.obligation_text: Visually inspect the outer band opposite the t-bolt for damage (distortion, creases, bulging, or cracks) caused by excessive spreading of the coupling during installation or removal. If there is any damage, before further flight, remove the v-band coupling from service and install a new v-band coupling.
units.action_summary: Inspect outer band opposite t-bolt for damage from spreading; if any, remove and install new coupling before further flight.

units.obligation_text: If the v-band coupling passes all of the inspections in paragraphs (k)(1)(i) through (vi) of this AD, it may be re-installed.
units.action_summary: If coupling passes all k(1) inspections, it may be re-installed.

units.obligation_text: Apply correct torque as necessary to the v-band coupling nut.
units.action_summary: When reinstalling, apply correct torque to the v-band coupling nut as necessary.

units.obligation_text: Inspect the v-band coupling to determine whether there is space between the two v-retainer coupling segments next to the t-bolt.
units.action_summary: Inspect for space between v-retainer segments next to t-bolt prior to reinstalling.

units.obligation_text: If there is no space between the two v-retainer coupling segments next to the t-bolt, before further flight, remove the v-band coupling from service and install a new v-band coupling.
units.action_summary: If no space exists between segments next to t-bolt, remove and replace coupling before further flight.

units.obligation_text: From the effective date of this AD until two years after the effective date of this AD, do not install a v-band coupling that has accumulated more than zero hours TIS on any turbocharged airplane, helicopter, or engine, unless it has passed all inspections required by paragraph (j) or (k) of this AD.
units.action_summary: Do not install any used v-band coupling (>0 hours TIS) until it has passed inspections required by j or k during the two-year period after the AD effective date.

units.obligation_text: As of two years after the effective date of this AD, do not install a v-band coupling that has accumulated more than zero and less than 500 hours TIS on any turbocharged airplane, helicopter, or engine, unless it has passed all inspections required by paragraph (j) or (k) of this AD.
units.action_summary: Beginning two years after effective date, do not install any used coupling with >0 and <500 hours TIS unless it has passed inspections in j or k.

units.obligation_text: As of two years after the effective date of this AD, do not install a v-band coupling that has accumulated 500 or more hours TIS on any turbocharged airplane, helicopter, or engine.
units.action_summary: Beginning two years after effective date, do not install any coupling that has 500 or more hours TIS.

title: Policy Regarding Processing Land Use Changes on Federally Acquired or Federally Conveyed Airport Land

units.obligation_text: The FAA will follow this policy guidance and FAA Order 5190.6, Airport Compliance Manual.
units.action_summary: FAA must follow this policy guidance and FAA Order 5190.6.

units.obligation_text: When FAA lacks approval authority over a particular change in land use or sale of land, all of the airport sponsor’s federal statutory and grant assurance obligations remain in full force and effect, including over its remaining airport property.
units.action_summary: Airport sponsors must continue to comply with federal statutory and grant-assurance obligations even when FAA lacks approval authority.

units.obligation_text: Airport sponsors remain obligated under the Grant Assurances, FAA’s Policies and Procedures Concerning the Use of Airport Revenue (Revenue Use Policy), and FAA’s Policy Regarding Rates and Charges.
units.action_summary: Airport sponsors must comply with Grant Assurances and specified FAA policies.

units.obligation_text: The sale or lease of the land must be accomplished per the FAA’s Appraisal Standards for the Sale and Disposal of Federally Obligated Airport Property (Compliance Guidance Letter 2018–3).
units.action_summary: Sponsors must complete sale or lease transactions in accordance with FAA appraisal standards.

units.obligation_text: The land must be sold or leased at fair market value and the funds must be used in accordance with the FAA’s Revenue Use Policy.
units.action_summary: Sponsors must sell/lease land at fair market value and use proceeds according to FAA Revenue Use Policy.

units.obligation_text: The sponsor should retain sufficient authority over the disposed land to prevent uses that conflict with its federal obligations and related requirements or create conditions resulting in violations of the assurances.
units.action_summary: Sponsors should retain authority over disposed land to prevent conflicting uses and violations of obligations.

units.obligation_text: To retain this authority, sponsors should consider using subordination clauses, reservations, covenants, or other restrictions in a deed or other instrument to protect the public’s right to fly over the land, prohibit obstructions to air navigation or interference with the flight of aircraft, or assure compatible land use.
units.action_summary: Sponsors should consider using legal restrictions in deeds to protect aeronautical interests and prevent conflicting uses.

units.obligation_text: The deed or other instrument containing the restrictions should be recorded in local land records.
units.action_summary: Sponsors should record deeds or instruments with restrictions in local land records.

units.obligation_text: The FAA may verify compliance with these requirements through a financial compliance review, review of supporting documentation, land use inspection, the enforcement of grant assurances, or other enforcement mechanisms.
units.action_summary: FAA is permitted to verify sponsor compliance through audits, inspections, documentation review, enforcement of assurances, or other mechanisms.

units.obligation_text: The sponsor also has the responsibility to comply with all federal, state, and local environmental laws and regulations.
units.action_summary: Sponsors are required to comply with applicable environmental laws and regulations.

units.obligation_text: The approval or consent should run concurrent with the lease term.
units.action_summary: Approval or consent letters should be concurrent with the lease term.

units.obligation_text: The FAA will review the sponsor’s proposal in its entirety without individually examining components of the proposal as aeronautical or non-aeronautical.
units.action_summary: FAA will evaluate land-use proposals as a whole rather than separating components into aeronautical vs non-aeronautical.

units.obligation_text: A letter of approval or consent is required for a non-aeronautical use or mixed use and the approval or consent will remain in effect only for duration of the lease term.
units.action_summary: Non-aeronautical or mixed uses require an FAA approval/consent letter, which remains in effect only for the lease duration.

units.obligation_text: The determination of whether the non-aeronautical use is significant will be based on the primary use of the project.
units.action_summary: FAA will determine significance of a non-aeronautical use based on the project's primary use.

units.obligation_text: FAA will only release federal obligations when the airport sponsor proposes the sale or conveyance of federally acquired or federally conveyed airport land that meets FAA release requirements.
units.action_summary: FAA will release federal obligations only when the sponsor's proposed sale/conveyance meets FAA release requirements.

units.obligation_text: FAA letters of approval or consent and releases will be documented on the Exhibit A in accordance with ARP SOP 3.00—FAA Review of Exhibit ‘A’ Airport Property Inventory Maps.
units.action_summary: FAA must document approval/consent letters and releases on Exhibit A per ARP SOP 3.00.

units.obligation_text: FAA Order 5190.6, Airport Compliance Manual, will be updated to reflect this policy guidance.
units.action_summary: FAA will update Order 5190.6 to reflect this policy.

units.obligation_text: FAA must approve or consent to all non-aeronautical and mixed uses of federally acquired and federally conveyed land.
units.action_summary: FAA is required to approve or consent to any non-aeronautical or mixed use on federally acquired/conveyed land.

units.obligation_text: If the FAA determines that the proposed use serves an aeronautical use or airport purpose as defined above, then FAA approval or consent is not required.
units.action_summary: When FAA determines proposed use is aeronautical or airport purpose, approval/consent is not required.

units.obligation_text: The sponsor’s request needs to include the following:
units.action_summary: Sponsors must include specified items in a land-use change request.

units.obligation_text: documentation on how the land was acquired (i.e., federal conveyance documents, Federal grant agreements, Exhibit A, etc.);
units.action_summary: Sponsor must provide documentation of how the land was acquired.

units.obligation_text: current and future aeronautical demand of the airport and the land;
units.action_summary: Sponsor must provide current and projected aeronautical demand for the airport and land.

units.obligation_text: proposed non-aeronautical use, including the length of the lease.
units.action_summary: Sponsor must include the proposed non-aeronautical use and lease length in the request.

units.obligation_text: The residential use of airport property is incompatible with the needs of civil aviation, is prohibited by FAA policy, and is also contrary to Federal obligations.
units.action_summary: Residential use of airport property is prohibited by FAA policy and federal obligations.

units.obligation_text: The proposal must benefit the airport and its functions in support of aeronautical uses and not adversely affect the value of the Federal investment in the airport and its facilities.
units.action_summary: Proposals must benefit the airport's aeronautical functions and not harm federal investment value.

units.obligation_text: The use should be compatible with the airport’s current or future aeronautical use or demand.
units.action_summary: Uses should be compatible with current or future aeronautical needs or demand.

units.obligation_text: FAA approval shall not be granted if the FAA determines that an aeronautical demand for the land is likely to exist within the period of the proposed use, or it compromises the safety and operation of the airport.
units.action_summary: FAA must not grant approval when foreseeable aeronautical demand exists during the proposed use period or safety/operation would be compromised.

units.obligation_text: FAA consent to or approval of a non-aeronautical use should only extend for duration of the lease term.
units.action_summary: FAA consent/approval should be limited to the lease term duration.

units.obligation_text: FAA consent to or approval of a non-aeronautical use must provide that the land will be returned to aeronautical use at the end of the term.
units.action_summary: FAA consent/approval must require that land revert to aeronautical use at lease end.

units.obligation_text: Upon completion of the review, the FAA will either issue a letter of approval or letter of consent for the non-aeronautical use or mixed-use, or deny the request.
units.action_summary: After review, FAA will issue an approval/consent letter or deny the land-use request.

units.obligation_text: The letter of approval or letter of consent must document the FAA’s approval of a non-aeronautical land use on federally acquired or federally conveyed airport land.
units.action_summary: FAA's approval/consent letter must document the approval of non-aeronautical land use on federally acquired/conveyed land.

units.obligation_text: This letter will outline the conditions of the approval or consent and include a requirement that the land must be available for aeronautical use at the end of the approval or consent period.
units.action_summary: The approval/consent letter must state conditions and require that the land be available for aeronautical use at the end of the approval/consent period.

units.obligation_text: The requirement for NEPA should be coordinated with FAA Environmental Protection Specialists.
units.action_summary: NEPA requirements should be coordinated with FAA Environmental Protection Specialists.

units.obligation_text: All land use changes should be shown on the Exhibit A in accordance with ARP SOP 3.00—FAA Review of Exhibit ‘A’ Airport Property Inventory Maps. This includes depicting in a table format the type of use for a facility, (e.g.: aeronautical, non-aeronautical, mixed-use), and the approval and expiration dates.
units.action_summary: All land use changes should be depicted on Exhibit A per ARP SOP 3.00, including type of use and approval/expiration dates.

title: Update to Air Carrier Definitions

units.obligation_text: Passenger-carrying flights in airplanes, powered-lift, or rotorcraft for the benefit of a charitable, nonprofit, or community event identified in paragraph (c) of this section are not subject to the certification requirements of part 119 or the drug and alcohol testing requirements in part 120 of this chapter, provided the following conditions are satisfied and the limitations in paragraphs (c) and (d) of this section are not exceeded:
units.action_summary: Such flights are excepted from part 119 certification and part 120 drug and alcohol testing requirements if specified conditions are met and limitations in (c) and (d) are not exceeded.

units.obligation_text: The flight is conducted from a public airport that is adequate for the aircraft used, or from another location the FAA approves for the operation;
units.action_summary: The flight must be conducted from an adequate public airport or from an FAA-approved alternate location.

units.obligation_text: The aircraft has a maximum of 30 seats, excluding each crewmember seat, and a maximum payload capacity of 7,500 pounds;
units.action_summary: The aircraft must not exceed 30 passenger seats (excluding crew seats) and must have a payload capacity no greater than 7,500 pounds to qualify.

units.obligation_text: Each aircraft holds a standard airworthiness certificate, is airworthy, and is operated in compliance with the applicable requirements of subpart E of this part;
units.action_summary: Each aircraft must have a standard airworthiness certificate, be airworthy, and be operated in compliance with subpart E requirements.

units.obligation_text: Reimbursement of the operator of the aircraft is limited to that portion of the passenger payment for the flight that does not exceed the pro rata cost of owning, operating, and maintaining the aircraft for that flight, which may include fuel, oil, airport expenditures, and rental fees;
units.action_summary: Reimbursement to the operator is limited to the pro rata costs of owning/operating/maintaining the aircraft for that flight (e.g., fuel, oil, airport costs, rental).

units.obligation_text: Any authorized deviation and exemption that applies to the person conducting operations under this subpart;
units.action_summary: Management specifications must include any authorized deviation and exemption that applies to the person conducting operations under this subpart.

units.obligation_text: The FAA may consider the following factors in determining whether a flight is a commercial air tour:
units.action_summary: The FAA is permitted to consider listed factors when determining whether a flight qualifies as a commercial air tour.

units.obligation_text: Except for operations when common carriage is not involved conducted with any airplane or powered-lift having a passenger-seat configuration of 20 seats or more, excluding any required crewmember seat, or a payload capacity of 6,000 pounds or more, this part does not apply to—
units.action_summary: Lists categories of operations to which part 119 does not apply (exceptions to applicability).

units.obligation_text: Nonstop Commercial Air Tours that occur in an airplane, powered-lift, or rotorcraft having a standard airworthiness certificate and passenger-seat configuration of 30 seats or fewer and a maximum payload capacity of 7,500 pounds or less that begin and end at the same airport, and are conducted within a 25-statute mile radius of that airport, in compliance with the Letter of Authorization issued under § 91.147 of this chapter.
units.action_summary: Nonstop commercial air tours meeting these criteria are excluded from part 119 (provided they comply with LOA requirements).

units.obligation_text: Powered-lift or rotorcraft operations in construction or repair work (but this exception does apply to transportation to and from the site of operations);
units.actor: operators conducting powered-lift or rotorcraft operations for construction/repair work
units.action_summary: Powered-lift or rotorcraft operations for construction or repair are excepted from part 119; exception also covers transportation to/from the site.

units.obligation_text: Sightseeing flights conducted in hot air balloons or gliders;
units.actor: operators of sightseeing flights in hot air balloons or gliders
units.action_summary: Sightseeing flights in hot air balloons or gliders are excluded from the applicability of part 119.

units.obligation_text: Powered-lift or rotorcraft flights conducted within a 25 statute mile radius of the airport of takeoff if—
units.action_summary: Powered-lift or rotorcraft flights within a 25-statute-mile radius are excepted from part 119 provided specified conditions are met.

units.obligation_text: Not more than two passengers are carried in the aircraft in addition to the required flightcrew;
units.action_summary: These excepted flights may carry no more than two passengers in addition to required flightcrew.

units.obligation_text: The aircraft used is certificated in the standard category and complies with the 100-hour inspection requirements of part 91 of this chapter;
units.action_summary: The aircraft must be standard-category certificated and comply with part 91 100-hour inspection requirements to qualify for the exception.

units.obligation_text: Cargo is not carried in or on the aircraft;
units.action_summary: Carrying cargo is prohibited on these excepted flights.

units.obligation_text: A person not authorized to conduct direct air carrier operations, but authorized by the Administrator to conduct operations as a U.S. commercial operator, will be issued an Operating Certificate.
units.action_summary: The Administrator will issue an Operating Certificate to a person authorized to conduct operations as a U.S. commercial operator but not authorized as a direct air carrier.

units.obligation_text: A person not authorized to conduct direct air carrier operations, but authorized by the Administrator to conduct operations when common carriage is not involved as an operator of any U.S.-registered civil airplane or powered-lift with a seat configuration of 20 or more passengers, or a maximum payload capacity of 6,000 pounds or more, will be issued an Operating Certificate.
units.action_summary: The Administrator will issue an Operating Certificate to a person authorized to conduct operations when common carriage is not involved for aircraft with 20+ seats or payload capacity >= 6,000 pounds.

units.obligation_text: Each person who conducts airplane or powered-lift operations as a commercial operator engaged in intrastate common carriage of persons or property for compensation or hire in air commerce, or as a direct air carrier, shall comply with the certification and operations specifications requirements in subpart C of this part, and shall conduct its:
units.actor: each person who conducts such operations
units.action_summary: Such persons must comply with certification and operations specifications requirements in subpart C and conduct their operations accordingly.

units.obligation_text: Each person who conducts operations when common carriage is not involved with any airplane or powered-lift having a passenger-seat configuration of 20 seats or more, excluding each crewmember seat, or a payload capacity of 6,000 pounds or more, must, unless deviation authority is issued—
units.actor: each person who conducts such operations
units.action_summary: Persons conducting such non-common carriage operations must comply with specified requirements unless deviation authority is issued.

units.obligation_text: Conduct its operations in accordance with the requirements of part 125 of this chapter;
units.actor: each person who conducts such operations
units.action_summary: These operators must conduct operations in accordance with part 125 requirements.

units.obligation_text: Each person who conducts noncommon carriage (except as provided in § 91.501(b) of this chapter) or private carriage operations for compensation or hire with any airplane or powered-lift having a passenger-seat configuration of less than 20 seats, excluding each crewmember seat, and a payload capacity of less than 6,000 pounds, must—
units.actor: each person who conducts such operations
units.action_summary: Operators conducting these noncommon carriage or private carriage operations for compensation must comply with the listed requirements.

units.obligation_text: Any authorized deviation or exemption from any requirement of this chapter that applies to the certificate holder.
units.action_summary: Operations specifications must include any authorized deviation or exemption that applies to the certificate holder.
units.modal_raw: must (implicit in context of contents of operations specifications)

units.obligation_text: Any authorized deviation or exemption from any requirement of this chapter that applies to the certificate holder.
units.action_summary: Operations specifications must include any authorized deviation or exemption applicable to the certificate holder (paragraph b).

units.obligation_text: Any authorized deviation or exemption from any requirement of this chapter that applies to the certificate holder.
units.action_summary: Operations specifications must include any authorized deviation or exemption applicable to the certificate holder (paragraph c).

units.action_summary: Certificate holders conducting operations under part 121 must have specified management personnel.

units.action_summary: Certificate holder must have a Chief Pilot for each category of aircraft it uses as listed in §61.5(b)(1).

units.obligation_text: The number and type of aircraft used; and
units.action_summary: Certificate holder must specify the number and type of aircraft used (as part of management/operations information).

units.obligation_text: Director of Operations. To serve as Director of Operations under § 119.65(a), a person must hold an airline transport pilot certificate and—
units.actor: a person serving as Director of Operations
units.action_summary: A person serving as Director of Operations must hold an airline transport pilot certificate and meet the following experience requirements.

units.obligation_text: If the certificate holder uses large aircraft, at least 3 years of supervisory or managerial experience within the last 6 years in large aircraft, in a position that exercised operational control over any operations conducted under parts 121 or 135 of this chapter.
units.actor: person serving as Director of Operations
units.action_summary: If large aircraft are used, the Director of Operations must have at least 3 years of relevant supervisory/managerial experience within the last 6 years involving operational control under parts 121 or 135.

In the case of a person becoming Director of Operations for the first time, he or she must have accumulated this experience as pilot in command within the past 6 years.

units.action_summary: If using large aircraft, the Director must have 3 years PIC experience under parts 121 or 135 in at least one category used; first-time Directors must have obtained this experience within the past 6 years.
units.modal_raw: must (if certificate holder uses large aircraft; for first-time appointees within past 6 years)

units.obligation_text: If the certificate holder uses only small aircraft in its operations, the experience required in paragraphs (a)(1) and (2) of this section may be obtained in either large or small aircraft.
units.actor: person serving as Director of Operations
units.action_summary: If the certificate holder uses only small aircraft, the experience required in (a)(1) and (a)(2) may be obtained in either large or small aircraft (alternative means to satisfy experience requirement).

units.obligation_text: Chief Pilot. To serve as Chief Pilot under § 119.65(a), a person must:
units.actor: a person serving as Chief Pilot
units.action_summary: A person serving as Chief Pilot must meet the following qualification requirements.

units.obligation_text: Hold an airline transport pilot certificate with appropriate ratings in the category of aircraft that the certificate holder uses in its operations under part 121 and over which the Chief Pilot exercises responsibility; and
units.action_summary: Chief Pilot must hold an airline transport pilot certificate with appropriate ratings for the aircraft category used by the certificate holder.

units.obligation_text: Have at least 3 years of experience as pilot in command in the same category of aircraft that the certificate holder uses, as listed in § 61.5(b). The experience as pilot in command described in this paragraph (b)(2) must: (i) Have occurred within the past 6 years, in the case of a person becoming a Chief Pilot for the first time. (ii) Have occurred in large aircraft operated under parts 121 or 135 of this chapter. If the certificate holder uses only small aircraft in its operation, this experience may be obtained in either large or small aircraft. (iii) Be in the same category of aircraft over which the Chief Pilot exercises responsibility.
units.action_summary: Chief Pilot must have at least 3 years PIC experience in the same category of aircraft; for first-time Chief Pilots the experience must be within past 6 years; experience generally must be in large aircraft under parts 121 or 135 unless certificate holder uses only small aircraft; experience must be in the same category the Chief Pilot will oversee.

units.obligation_text: Have occurred within the past 6 years, in the case of a person becoming a Chief Pilot for the first time.
units.actor: person becoming a Chief Pilot for the first time
units.action_summary: First-time Chief Pilots must have the required PIC experience within the past 6 years.

units.obligation_text: Have occurred in large aircraft operated under parts 121 or 135 of this chapter. If the certificate holder uses only small aircraft in its operation, this experience may be obtained in either large or small aircraft.
units.action_summary: PIC experience should occur in large aircraft under parts 121 or 135; if the certificate holder uses only small aircraft, the experience may be in large or small aircraft.

units.obligation_text: Be in the same category of aircraft over which the Chief Pilot exercises responsibility.
units.action_summary: Experience must be in the same category of aircraft that the Chief Pilot will be responsible for.

units.obligation_text: Director of Maintenance. To serve as Director of Maintenance under § 119.65(a), a person must:
units.actor: a person serving as Director of Maintenance
units.action_summary: A person serving as Director of Maintenance must meet the following qualifications.

units.obligation_text: Hold a mechanic certificate with airframe and powerplant ratings;
units.actor: person serving as Director of Maintenance
units.action_summary: Director of Maintenance must hold a mechanic certificate with both airframe and powerplant ratings.

units.obligation_text: Have 1 year of experience in a position responsible for returning aircraft to service;
units.actor: person serving as Director of Maintenance
units.action_summary: Director of Maintenance must have one year of experience in a role responsible for returning aircraft to service.

units.obligation_text: Have at least 1 year of experience in a supervisory capacity under either paragraph (c)(4)(i) or (ii) of this section maintaining the same category and class of aircraft as the certificate holder uses;
units.actor: person serving as Director of Maintenance
units.action_summary: Director of Maintenance must have at least one year of supervisory experience maintaining the same category/class of aircraft as the certificate holder uses (as described in c(4)(i) or (ii)).

units.obligation_text: Have 3 years of experience within the past 6 years in one or a combination of the following—
units.actor: person serving as Director of Maintenance
units.action_summary: Director of Maintenance must have three years of specified experience within the past six years, in one or a combination of the following options.

units.obligation_text: Maintaining large aircraft with 10 or more passenger seats, including, at the time of appointment as Director of Maintenance, experience in maintaining the same category and class of aircraft as the certificate holder uses;
units.actor: person serving as Director of Maintenance
units.action_summary: One option to meet the three-year requirement is experience maintaining large aircraft (10+ passenger seats), including experience maintaining the same category/class as the certificate holder uses.

units.obligation_text: Repairing aircraft in a certificated airframe repair station that is rated to maintain aircraft in the same category and class of aircraft as the certificate holder uses.
units.actor: person serving as Director of Maintenance
units.action_summary: Alternatively, the three-year experience may be obtained by repairing aircraft in a certificated airframe repair station rated to maintain the same category/class as the certificate holder uses.

units.obligation_text: Chief Inspector. To serve as Chief Inspector under § 119.65(a), a person must:
units.actor: a person serving as Chief Inspector
units.action_summary: A person serving as Chief Inspector must meet the qualifications listed below.

units.obligation_text: Hold a mechanic certificate with both airframe and powerplant ratings, and have held these ratings for at least 3 years;
units.action_summary: Chief Inspector must hold A&P mechanic certificate and have held those ratings for at least three years.

units.obligation_text: Have at least 3 years of maintenance experience on different types of large aircraft with 10 or more passenger seats with an air carrier or certificated repair station, 1 year of which must have been as maintenance inspector;
units.action_summary: Chief Inspector must have at least three years maintenance experience on different large aircraft types (10+ seats) with one year as a maintenance inspector.

units.obligation_text: Have at least 1 year of experience in a supervisory capacity maintaining the same category and class of aircraft as the certificate holder uses.
units.action_summary: Chief Inspector must have at least one year of supervisory experience maintaining the same category/class of aircraft as the certificate holder uses.

units.obligation_text: A certificate holder may request a deviation to employ a person who does not meet the appropriate airman experience, managerial experience, or supervisory experience requirements of this section if the Manager of the Air Transportation Division or the Manager of the Aircraft Maintenance Division, as appropriate, finds that the person has comparable experience and can effectively perform the functions associated with the position in accordance with the requirements of this chapter and the procedures outlined in the certificate holder’s manual.
units.action_summary: Certificate holders may request a deviation to employ a person who lacks specified experience if the appropriate Manager finds the person has comparable experience and can perform the required functions.

units.obligation_text: Deviations under this paragraph may be granted after consideration of the size and scope of the operation and the qualifications of the intended personnel.
units.actor: the FAA / Manager of the Air Transportation Division or Manager of the Aircraft Maintenance Division
units.action_summary: FAA managers may grant requested deviations after considering operation size/scope and intended personnel qualifications.

units.obligation_text: The Administrator may, at any time, terminate any grant of deviation authority issued under this paragraph (e).
units.action_summary: The Administrator has authority to terminate any deviation grant at any time.

units.obligation_text: Each person operating an aircraft in operations under this part shall—
units.action_summary: Persons operating aircraft subject to part 125 must follow the rules and obligations set forth in this part.

units.obligation_text: When any requirement of this subpart is more stringent than any other requirement of this chapter, the person operating the commercial air tour must comply with the requirement in this subpart.
units.actor: the person operating the commercial air tour
units.action_summary: If a subpart requirement is more stringent than other chapter requirements, the operator must comply with the subpart's requirement.

units.obligation_text: Operators subject to this subpart who have Letters of Authorization may use the procedures described in § 119.51 of this chapter to amend or have the FAA reconsider those Letters of Authorization.
units.actor: operators subject to this subpart who have Letters of Authorization
units.action_summary: Such operators are permitted to use §119.51 procedures to amend or request FAA reconsideration of their Letters of Authorization.

units.obligation_text: Any operator subject to this subpart who meets the criteria of § 136.71 must comply with the additional requirements and restrictions in subpart D of this part.
units.actor: any operator subject to this subpart meeting §136.71 criteria
units.action_summary: Operators meeting §136.71 criteria are required to comply with the additional requirements/restrictions in subpart D.

units.obligation_text: (b) * * * (1) The aircraft is equipped with floats; (2) The airplane is within power-off gliding distance to the shoreline for the duration of the time that the flight is over water; or (3) The aircraft is a multiengine that can be operated with the critical engine inoperative at a weight that will allow it to climb, at least 50 feet a minute, at an altitude of 1,000 feet above the surface, as provided in the approved aircraft flight manual for that aircraft.
units.action_summary: These are the stated conditions (exceptions) under which the life preserver requirement over water does not apply.

units.obligation_text: The aircraft is equipped with floats;
units.action_summary: If the aircraft is equipped with floats, it meets one condition for exception from life preserver requirements.

units.obligation_text: The airplane is within power-off gliding distance to the shoreline for the duration of the time that the flight is over water;
units.action_summary: If the airplane remains within power-off gliding distance to shore for the duration over water, it meets an exception condition.

units.obligation_text: The aircraft is a multiengine that can be operated with the critical engine inoperative at a weight that will allow it to climb, at least 50 feet a minute, at an altitude of 1,000 feet above the surface, as provided in the approved aircraft flight manual for that aircraft.
units.action_summary: If a multiengine aircraft can meet the prescribed single-engine climb performance at the specified weight/altitude per the AFM, it meets an exception condition from life preserver requirements.

units.obligation_text: A rotorcraft used in commercial air tours over water beyond the shoreline must be equipped with fixed floats or an inflatable flotation system adequate to accomplish a safe emergency ditching, if—
units.actor: operator/aircraft used in commercial air tours over water beyond the shoreline
units.action_summary: Rotorcraft operating over water beyond the shoreline must be equipped with fixed floats or an adequate inflatable flotation system when specified conditions apply.

units.obligation_text: It is a single-engine rotorcraft; or
units.action_summary: If the rotorcraft is single-engine and operates over water beyond the shoreline, it must have floats or an inflatable flotation system.

units.obligation_text: It is a multi-engine rotorcraft that cannot be operated with the critical engine inoperative at a weight that will allow it to climb, at least 50 feet a minute, at an altitude of 1,000 feet above the surface, as provided in the approved aircraft flight manual for that aircraft.
units.action_summary: If a multi-engine rotorcraft cannot meet required single-engine climb performance at specified conditions, it must be equipped with floats or an inflatable flotation system when operating over water beyond the shoreline.

units.obligation_text: Each rotorcraft that is required to be equipped with an inflatable flotation system under this section must have: (1) The activation switch for the flotation system on one of the primary flight controls; and (2) The flotation system armed when the rotorcraft is over water beyond the shoreline and is flying at a speed that does not exceed the maximum speed prescribed in the approved aircraft flight manual for flying with the flotation system armed.
units.action_summary: Rotorcraft required to have inflatable flotation systems must have the activation switch on a primary flight control and must have the system armed when over water beyond the shoreline at appropriate speed.

units.obligation_text: The activation switch for the flotation system on one of the primary flight controls;
units.action_summary: Required flotation systems must have their activation switch located on one of the primary flight controls.

units.obligation_text: The flotation system armed when the rotorcraft is over water beyond the shoreline and is flying at a speed that does not exceed the maximum speed prescribed in the approved aircraft flight manual for flying with the flotation system armed.
units.action_summary: The flotation system must be armed when the rotorcraft is over water beyond the shoreline and flying at or below the AFM-prescribed maximum speed for armed flotation.

units.obligation_text: Neither fixed floats nor an inflatable flotation system is required for a rotorcraft under this section when that rotorcraft is: (1) Over water only during the takeoff or landing portion of the flight; or (2) Operated within power-off gliding distance to the shoreline for the duration of the flight and each occupant is wearing a life preserver from before takeoff until the aircraft is no longer over water.
units.action_summary: Exceptions to flotation equipment requirements exist when the rotorcraft is only over water during takeoff/landing, or when operated within gliding distance with all occupants wearing life preservers.

units.obligation_text: Over water only during the takeoff or landing portion of the flight; or
units.action_summary: If rotorcraft are over water only during takeoff or landing, flotation equipment is not required under this section.

units.obligation_text: Operated within power-off gliding distance to the shoreline for the duration of the flight and each occupant is wearing a life preserver from before takeoff until the aircraft is no longer over water.
units.action_summary: If operated within power-off gliding distance to shore for entire flight and all occupants wear life preservers from before takeoff until no longer over water, flotation equipment is not required.

units.obligation_text: Each operator that uses a rotorcraft must complete a performance plan before each commercial air tour or flight operated under §§ 91.146 or 91.147 of this chapter. The pilot in command must review for accuracy and comply with the performance plan on the day the flight occurs. The performance plan must be based on information in the approved aircraft flight manual for that aircraft taking into consideration the maximum density altitude for which the operation is planned, in order to determine:
units.actor: each operator that uses a rotorcraft; pilot in command
units.action_summary: Operators must complete a performance plan before each applicable flight; the PIC must review and comply with it on the day of flight; the plan must be based on AFM information and maximum density altitude considerations.

units.obligation_text: The pilot in command must review for accuracy and comply with the performance plan on the day the flight occurs.
units.action_summary: The PIC is required to review the performance plan for accuracy and comply with it on the flight day.

units.obligation_text: (1) Maximum gross weight and center of gravity (CG) limitations for hovering in ground effect; (2) Maximum gross weight and CG limitations for hovering out of ground effect; and (3) Maximum combination of weight, altitude, and temperature for which height/velocity information in the approved aircraft flight manual is valid.
units.action_summary: The performance plan must determine maximum gross weight and CG limits for hovering in/out of ground effect and the maximum weight/altitude/temperature combination for which AFM height/velocity data is valid.

units.obligation_text: Except for the approach to and transition from a hover for the purpose of takeoff and landing, or during takeoff and landing, the pilot in command must make a reasonable plan to operate the rotorcraft outside of the caution/warning/avoid area of the limiting height/velocity diagram.
units.action_summary: PIC must plan to operate the rotorcraft outside the caution/warning/avoid areas of the height/velocity diagram, except during approach/transition for takeoff/landing or during takeoff/landing.

units.obligation_text: Except for the approach to and transition from a hover for the purpose of takeoff and landing, during takeoff and landing, or when necessary for safety of flight, the pilot in command must operate the rotorcraft in compliance with the plan described in paragraph (b) of this section.
units.action_summary: PIC must operate the rotorcraft in compliance with the plan made under paragraph (b), except during approach/transition for takeoff/landing, during takeoff/landing, or when necessary for safety.

units.obligation_text: Operations conducted under part 121 of this chapter in airplanes with a passenger seating configuration of more than 30 seats or a payload capacity of more than 7,500 pounds.
units.action_summary: This subpart does not apply to part 121 operations in airplanes with >30 seats or >7,500 lb payload capacity.

units.obligation_text: Flights conducted in gliders or hot air balloons.
units.actor: operators conducting flights in gliders or hot air balloons
units.action_summary: This subpart does not apply to flights conducted in gliders or hot air balloons.

units.obligation_text: No person may conduct an air tour in Hawaii in a rotorcraft beyond the shore of any island, regardless of whether the rotorcraft is within gliding distance of the shore, unless: (1) The rotorcraft is amphibious or is equipped with floats adequate to accomplish a safe emergency ditching and approved flotation gear is easily accessible for each occupant; or (2) Each person on board the rotorcraft is wearing approved flotation gear.
units.actor: any person conducting an air tour in Hawaii in a rotorcraft
units.action_summary: Prohibits conducting air tours in rotorcraft beyond an island shore unless the rotorcraft has approved floats/amphibious capability with accessible flotation gear or each person aboard is wearing approved flotation gear.

units.obligation_text: The rotorcraft is amphibious or is equipped with floats adequate to accomplish a safe emergency ditching and approved flotation gear is easily accessible for each occupant;
units.action_summary: One allowed condition to operate beyond shore is that the rotorcraft is amphibious or has adequate floats and approved flotation gear accessible to each occupant.

units.obligation_text: Each person on board the rotorcraft is wearing approved flotation gear.
units.action_summary: Alternatively, operation beyond shore is permitted if every person on board is wearing approved flotation gear.

units.obligation_text: Performance plan. Each operator must complete a performance plan that meets the requirements of this paragraph (b) before each air tour flight conducted in a rotorcraft.
units.actor: each operator conducting rotorcraft air tours
units.action_summary: Operators must complete a specified performance plan before each rotorcraft air tour flight.

units.obligation_text: The performance plan must be based on information from the current approved aircraft flight manual for that aircraft, considering the maximum density altitude for which the operation is planned to determine the following: (i) Maximum gross weight and center of gravity (CG) limitations for hovering in ground effect; (ii) Maximum gross weight and CG limitations for hovering out of ground effect; and (iii) Maximum combination of weight, altitude, and temperature for which height-velocity information from the performance data is valid.
units.action_summary: Performance plans must be based on current AFM data and consider max density altitude to determine specified gross weight/CG and weight/altitude/temperature limits.

units.obligation_text: The pilot in command (PIC) must comply with the performance plan.
units.action_summary: The PIC is required to comply with the performance plan for each air tour flight.

units.obligation_text: Operating limitations. Except for approach to and transition from a hover, and except for the purpose of takeoff and landing, the PIC of a rotorcraft may only operate such aircraft at a combination of height and forward speed (including hover) that would permit a safe landing in event of engine power loss, in accordance with the height-speed envelope for that rotorcraft under current weight and aircraft altitude.
units.action_summary: Except during certain phases, the PIC may only operate at a height/speed combination that allows a safe landing in the event of engine failure per the rotorcraft's height-speed envelope.

units.obligation_text: Minimum flight altitudes. Except when necessary for takeoff and landing, or operating in compliance with an air traffic control clearance, or as otherwise authorized by the Administrator, no person may conduct an air tour in Hawaii: (1) Below an altitude of 1,500 feet above the surface over all areas of the State of Hawaii; (2) Closer than 1,500 feet to any person or property; or (3) Below any altitude prescribed by federal statute or regulation.
units.actor: any person conducting an air tour in Hawaii
units.action_summary: Prohibits conducting air tours below specified altitudes or closer than specified distances unless necessary for takeoff/landing, ATC clearance compliance, or otherwise authorized by the Administrator.

units.obligation_text: Below an altitude of 1,500 feet above the surface over all areas of the State of Hawaii;
units.actor: any person conducting an air tour in Hawaii
units.action_summary: Air tours may not be conducted below 1,500 feet above the surface over Hawaii except as authorized.

units.obligation_text: Closer than 1,500 feet to any person or property;
units.actor: any person conducting an air tour in Hawaii
units.action_summary: Air tours may not be conducted closer than 1,500 feet to any person or property except as authorized.

units.obligation_text: Below any altitude prescribed by federal statute or regulation.
units.actor: any person conducting an air tour in Hawaii
units.action_summary: Air tours may not be conducted below any altitude set by federal statute or regulation, except as authorized.

units.obligation_text: Passenger briefing. Before takeoff, each PIC of an air tour flight of Hawaii with a flight segment beyond the ocean shore of any island shall ensure that each passenger has been briefed on the following, in addition to requirements set forth in §§ 91.107, 121.571, or 135.117 of this chapter:
units.action_summary: Before takeoff of specified Hawaii air tour flights, the PIC must ensure each passenger has been briefed on additional safety topics in addition to other regulatory briefing requirements.

units.obligation_text: Water ditching procedures;
units.action_summary: PIC must ensure passengers are briefed on water ditching procedures.

units.obligation_text: Use of required flotation equipment; and
units.action_summary: PIC must ensure passengers are briefed on how to use required flotation equipment.

units.obligation_text: Emergency egress from the aircraft in event of a water landing.
units.action_summary: PIC must ensure passengers are briefed on emergency egress procedures in the event of a water landing.

title: Airworthiness Directives: Viking Air Limited (Type Certificate Previously Held by Bombardier Inc. and de Havilland Inc.) Airplanes

units.obligation_text: The FAA amends § 39.13 by: a. Removing Airworthiness Directive 64–09–03, Amendment 718 (29 FR 5390, April 22, 1964);
units.action_summary: FAA will remove AD 64-09-03 from § 39.13.

units.obligation_text: The FAA amends § 39.13 by: b. Adding the following new airworthiness directive: Viking Air Limited ... Docket No. FAA–2022–0190; Project Identifier 2019–CE–048–AD.
units.action_summary: FAA will add a new airworthiness directive for the specified Viking Air Limited airplanes to § 39.13.

units.obligation_text: The FAA must receive comments on this airworthiness directive (AD) by June 9, 2023.
units.action_summary: FAA must receive comments on the AD by the specified date.

units.obligation_text: This AD replaces AD 64–09–03, Amendment 718 (29 FR 5390, April 22, 1964).
units.action_summary: The new AD supersedes and replaces the prior AD 64-09-03.

units.obligation_text: This AD applies to Viking Air Limited (type certificate previously held by Bombardier Inc. and de Havilland, Inc.) Model DHC–2 Mk. I, DHC–2 Mk. II, and DHC–2 Mk. III airplanes, all serial numbers, certificated in any category.
units.actor: Owners/operators of Viking Air Limited Model DHC-2 Mk I/II/III airplanes
units.action_summary: Specifies which airplanes are subject to the AD.

units.obligation_text: Comply with this AD within the compliance times specified, unless already done.
units.action_summary: Operators must perform the AD-required actions within specified compliance times unless already completed.

units.obligation_text: Within 90 days after the effective date of this AD, incorporate into the existing maintenance records required by 14 CFR 91.417(a)(2) or 135.439(a)(2), as applicable for your airplane, the actions and associated thresholds and intervals, including life limits, specified in Parts 2 and 3 of Viking DHC–2 Beaver Supplemental Inspection and Corrosion Control Manual, PSM 1–2–5, Revision 1, dated January 10, 2019 (Viking PSM 1–2–5, Revision 1).
units.action_summary: Incorporate specified inspection and corrosion-control actions and thresholds into required maintenance records within 90 days of the AD's effective date.

units.obligation_text: Do each initial task within 6 months after the effective date of this AD or at the threshold for each applicable task specified in Part 3 of Viking Product Support Manual PSM 1–2–5, Revision 1, whichever occurs later.
units.action_summary: Perform each initial inspection/maintenance task within 6 months or at the specified threshold, whichever is later.

units.obligation_text: Where Viking PSM 1–2–5, Revision 1, specifies contacting Viking for instructions on forward and rear fin attachment bolt replacement, inspection, and installation, and for a disposition regarding attachment bolts, this AD requires contacting the FAA, Transport Canada, or Viking’s Transport Canada Design Organization Approval (DOA).
units.action_summary: If the PSM directs contacting Viking for bolt instructions/dispositions, the AD requires contacting FAA, Transport Canada, or Viking's DOA instead.

units.obligation_text: If approved by the DOA, the approval must include the DOA-authorized signature.
units.actor: Viking’s Transport Canada Design Organization Approval (DOA)
units.action_summary: Any DOA approval must include the DOA-authorized signature.

units.obligation_text: After the action required by paragraph (g)(1) of this AD has been done, no alternative actions and associated thresholds and intervals, including life limits, are allowed unless they are approved as specified in paragraph (i) of this AD.
units.action_summary: Prohibits use of alternative actions/thresholds/intervals after compliance, unless approved per paragraph (i).

units.obligation_text: For inspections done after the effective date of this AD, report to Viking any Level 2 or Level 3 corrosion, as specified in Viking PSM 1–2–5, Revision 1, at the times specified in and in accordance with part 3, paragraph 5, of Viking PSM 1–2–5, Revision 1.
units.actor: Inspectors / owners/operators of the affected airplanes
units.action_summary: Report any Level 2 or Level 3 corrosion found during inspections after the AD effective date to Viking in accordance with the PSM schedule/procedures.

units.obligation_text: For inspections done before the effective date of this AD, within 30 days after the effective date of this AD report to Viking any Level 2 or Level 3 corrosion, as specified in Viking PSM 1–2–5, Revision 1, in accordance with part 3, paragraph 5, of Viking PSM 1–2–5, Revision 1.
units.actor: Inspectors / owners/operators of the affected airplanes
units.action_summary: If inspections were done before the AD effective date, report any Level 2 or Level 3 corrosion to Viking within 30 days after the AD becomes effective.

units.obligation_text: The Manager, New York ACO Branch, FAA, has the authority to approve AMOCs for this AD, if requested using the procedures found in § 39.19.
units.actor: The Manager, New York ACO Branch, FAA
units.action_summary: The New York ACO Branch Manager may approve requests for alternative methods of compliance for this AD when requested per § 39.19.
units.modal_raw: has the authority to approve (may approve)

units.obligation_text: In accordance with § 39.19, send your request to your principal inspector or local Flight Standards District Office, as appropriate.
units.action_summary: AMOC requests must be sent to the principal inspector or local FSDO per § 39.19.

units.obligation_text: If sending information directly to the manager of the New York ACO Branch, mail it to ATTN: Program Manager, Continuing Operational Safety, at the address identified in paragraph (j)(2) of this AD or email to: 9-avs-nyaco-cos@faa.gov.
units.action_summary: If sending AMOC information directly to the New York ACO Branch manager, submit it by mail to the specified address or by email to the specified address.

units.obligation_text: If mailing information, also submit information by email.
units.action_summary: When mailing AMOC information, the requester must also submit the information by email.

units.obligation_text: Before using any approved AMOC, notify your appropriate principal inspector, or lacking a principal inspector, the manager of the local flight standards district office/certificate holding district office.
units.actor: Owners/operators who will use an approved AMOC
units.action_summary: Prior to using an approved AMOC, operators must notify their principal inspector or the manager of the local FSDO/CHDO if no principal inspector exists.

units.obligation_text: An AMOC that provides an acceptable level of safety may be used for any repair, modification, or alteration required by this AD if it is approved specifically for this AD by the Manager, New York ACO Branch, FAA.
units.action_summary: Operators may use an AMOC for AD-required repairs/modifications if the AMOC is specifically approved for this AD by the New York ACO Branch Manager.

units.obligation_text: The Director of the Federal Register approved the incorporation by reference (IBR) of the service information listed in this paragraph under 5 U.S.C. 552(a) and 1 CFR part 51.
units.actor: The Director of the Federal Register
units.action_summary: The Director of the Federal Register approved incorporation by reference of the listed service information under the cited statutes/regulations.

units.obligation_text: You must use this service information as applicable to do the actions required by this AD, unless the AD specifies otherwise.
units.action_summary: Operators must use the incorporated service information to perform AD-required actions unless the AD provides an exception.

units.obligation_text: For service information identified in this AD, contact Viking Air Limited Technical Support, 1959 De Havilland Way, Sidney, British Columbia, Canada, V8L 5V5; phone: (800) 663–8444; fax: (250) 656–0673; email: technical.support@vikingair.com; website: vikingair.com/support/service-bulletins.
units.action_summary: Provide contact details for obtaining the service information identified in the AD.

units.obligation_text: You may view this service information at the FAA, Airworthiness Products Section, Operational Safety Branch, 901 Locust, Kansas City, MO 64106. For information on the availability of this material at the FAA, call (817) 222–5110.
units.action_summary: The service information can be viewed at the FAA office; contact via phone for availability information.

units.obligation_text: You may view this service information that is incorporated by reference at the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA). For information on the availability of this material at NARA, email: fr.inspection@nara.gov, or go to: www.archives.gov/federal-register/cfr/ibr-locations.html.
units.action_summary: The incorporated service information is available for viewing at NARA; contact NARA or visit the provided URL for availability details.

title: Airworthiness Directives; Transport and Commuter Category Airplanes

units.obligation_text: The FAA must receive comments on this airworthiness directive (AD) action by February 10, 2023.
units.action_summary: Submit comments on the AD to the FAA by February 10, 2023.

units.obligation_text: This AD applies to all transport and commuter category airplanes equipped with a radio (also known as radar) altimeter.
units.actor: owners/operators of transport and commuter category airplanes equipped with a radio altimeter
units.action_summary: Identifies the airplanes and operators that are subject to the requirements of this AD.

units.obligation_text: Comply with this AD within the compliance times specified, unless already done.
units.action_summary: Comply with all AD requirements within the specified compliance times unless already accomplished.

units.section: (h) Airplane/Aircraft Flight Manual (AFM) Revision for All Airplanes
units.obligation_text: Before further flight: Revise the Limitations Section of the existing AFM by incorporating the limitations specified in figure 2 to paragraph (h) of this AD.
