title:
Proposed Rules on Food Labeling: Revision of the Nutrition and
Supplement Facts Labels and Serving Sizes of Foods That Can Reasonably Be Consumed at One-Eating Occasion; Dual-Column Labeling; Updating, Modifying, and Establishing Certain Reference Amounts Customarily Consumed; Serving Size for Breath Mints; and Technical Amendments; Public Meeting
April 10 2006 Federal Register for Medical Gas Containers and Closures_ Current Good Manufacturing Practice Requirements(1)

units.obligation_text: Medical gas containers and closures must meet the following requirements:
units.action_summary: Medical gas containers and closures must comply with the listed labeling, color, outlet connection, reuse, and identification requirements.

units.obligation_text: The label must identify the fraction of the gas it represents in the medical gas held in the container by the combination or mixture.
units.action_summary: Labels must state the fraction/portion of each gas present in a combination or mixture.

units.obligation_text: The standard name must be printed on the label in one of the following ways:
units.actor: the standard name on the label
units.action_summary: The gas's standard name must be printed on the label using one of the specified presentation methods.

units.obligation_text: Using lettering that appears in the standard color designated for the gas in paragraph (e)(5) of this section and that is printed against a white background.
units.actor: the labeler/manufacturer (as to how the standard name is printed)
units.action_summary: The standard name may be printed in the gas's standard color against a white background (permitted presentation alternative).

units.obligation_text: Using lettering that appears in white against a background that is painted in the standard color for the gas as designated in paragraph (e)(5) of this section.
units.actor: the labeler/manufacturer (as to how the standard name is printed)
units.action_summary: The standard name may be printed in white lettering on a background painted in the gas's standard color (permitted presentation alternative).

units.obligation_text: The lettering for the name of the gas on the label must be at least 2 3/4 inches high.
units.actor: the lettering for the name of the gas (on the label)
units.action_summary: Gas name lettering must be at least 2 3/4 inches high.

units.obligation_text: The name of the gas must be printed continuously around the label and be capable of being read around the entire container.
units.actor: the name of the gas (on the label)
units.action_summary: The gas name must be printed continuously around the label so it can be read around the whole container.

units.obligation_text: The label must be on the sidewall of the container, as close to the top of the container as possible but below the top weld seam.
units.action_summary: Labels must be placed on the sidewall near the top, but below the top weld seam.

units.obligation_text: The label must be affixed to the container so that it cannot be easily detached or worn, and in a manner that does not interfere with other labeling.
units.action_summary: Labels must be affixed so they are not easily detached or worn and must not interfere with other labeling.

units.obligation_text: If the shoulder portion of a portable cryogenic medical gas container is colored, the color used must be that designated in paragraph (e)(5) of this section for the gas held within the container.
units.actor: portable cryogenic medical gas containers (if shoulder is colored)
units.action_summary: If the shoulder is colored, it must use the color designated for the gas in paragraph (e)(5).

units.obligation_text: Containers or high-pressure cylinders used at any time to hold a liquid or compressed industrial gas may not be subsequently used to hold any type of liquid or compressed medical gas.
units.actor: containers or high-pressure cylinders used at any time to hold a liquid or compressed industrial gas
units.action_summary: Such containers/cylinders previously used for industrial gases are prohibited from being subsequently used to hold medical gases.

units.obligation_text: Was converted to use for holding a liquid or compressed medical gas in accordance with standard industry practice before [effective date of final regulation];
units.actor: a cryogenic container or high-pressure cylinder that was once used to hold an industrial gas
units.action_summary: Exception to the prohibition if container was converted to medical gas use per standard industry practice before the effective date.

units.obligation_text: Is used solely to hold a liquid or compressed medical gas on and after [effective date of final regulation] and is in compliance with all other applicable requirements.
units.actor: a cryogenic container or high-pressure cylinder that was once used to hold an industrial gas
units.action_summary: Exception to the prohibition if, on and after the effective date, the container is used only for medical gas and complies with all other requirements.

units.obligation_text: Portable cryogenic medical gas containers that are not manufactured with permanent gas use outlet connections (e.g., those that have been silver-brazed) must have gas-specific use outlet connections that are attached to the valve body so that they cannot be readily removed or replaced (without making the valve inoperable and preventing the containers' use) except by the manufacturer.
units.actor: portable cryogenic medical gas containers not manufactured with permanent gas use outlet connections
units.action_summary: Portable cryogenic containers without permanent outlet connections must have gas-specific outlet connections attached to the valve body so they cannot be readily removed or replaced (except by the manufacturer).

units.obligation_text: Except by the manufacturer.
units.action_summary: Only the manufacturer may remove or replace the gas-specific use outlet connections without making the valve inoperable.

units.obligation_text: Each portable cryogenic medical gas container must be conspicuously marked with a 360° wraparound label identifying its contents.
units.actor: each portable cryogenic medical gas container
units.action_summary: Portable cryogenic containers must have a conspicuous 360° wraparound label identifying contents.

units.obligation_text: High-pressure medical gas cylinders must be identified with FDA-designated standard colors according to the following:
units.action_summary: High-pressure cylinders must be identified using FDA-designated standard colors as specified in the following subitems.

units.obligation_text: Non-aluminum high-pressure medical gas cylinders must be colored in whole in the standard color designated in paragraph (e)(5) of this section for the gas contained in the cylinder.
units.action_summary: Non-aluminum cylinders must be entirely colored in the gas's standard color designated in paragraph (e)(5).

units.obligation_text: Aluminum high-pressure medical gas cylinders must be colored on the shoulder portion of the cylinder in the standard color designated in paragraph (e)(5) of this section for the gas contained in the cylinder.
units.action_summary: Aluminum cylinders must be colored on the shoulder in the standard color for the gas.

units.obligation_text: The materials used for coloring must be reasonably resistant to fading, durable when exposed to atmospheric conditions, and not readily soluble in water after they have been applied and properly dried or cured.
units.actor: the materials used for coloring (and those who apply them)
units.action_summary: Coloring materials must resist fading, be durable in atmosphere, and not be readily water soluble after proper application and curing.

units.obligation_text: High-pressure medical gas cylinders containing a blend or combination of medical gases must be colored with the standard colors of each component gas, as designated in paragraph (e)(5) of this section.
units.actor: high-pressure medical gas cylinders containing a blend or combination of medical gases
units.action_summary: Blended gas cylinders must be colored with the standard colors of each component gas.

units.obligation_text: Each such color must be visible when viewed from the top of the cylinder.
units.actor: the colors applied to blended gas cylinders
units.action_summary: Each component color must be visible from the top of the cylinder.

units.obligation_text: Each such color must appear in rough proportion to the component [gas].
units.actor: the colors applied to blended gas cylinders
units.action_summary: Colors must be applied in rough proportion to the relative amounts of each component gas.

units.obligation_text: The standard names and colors required to identify medical gases under paragraph (e)(4) of this section are:
units.actor: the standard names and colors used to identify medical gases
units.action_summary: Specifies the required standard names and corresponding standard colors for medical gases.

units.obligation_text: Medical Air — Yellow
units.action_summary: Medical Air must be identified by the color Yellow.

units.obligation_text: Medical Carbon Dioxide — Gray
units.action_summary: Medical Carbon Dioxide must be identified by the color Gray.

units.obligation_text: Medical Helium — Brown
units.action_summary: Medical Helium must be identified by the color Brown.

units.obligation_text: Medical Nitrogen — Black
units.action_summary: Medical Nitrogen must be identified by the color Black.

units.obligation_text: Medical Nitrous Oxide — Blue
units.action_summary: Medical Nitrous Oxide must be identified by the color Blue.

units.obligation_text: Medical Oxygen — Green
units.action_summary: Medical Oxygen must be identified by the color Green.

units.obligation_text: Mixture or Blend of Medical Gases — Standard colors for each component
units.actor: mixtures or blends of medical gases (and their labeling)
units.action_summary: Mixtures must be identified using the standard colors for each component gas.

units.obligation_text: Labeling reconciliation is also waived for 360° wraparound labels on portable cryogenic medical gas containers.
units.actor: persons required to perform labeling reconciliation (for portable cryogenic containers)
units.action_summary: The requirement to perform labeling reconciliation is waived for 360° wraparound labels on portable cryogenic medical gas containers.

units.obligation_text: An applicant has 30 days after the date on which he or she submits a request for relief under § 421.150 to provide us with the evidence required under § 421.151(b)(1) through (3).
units.action_summary: Provide the evidence required under §421.151(b)(1)-(3) within 30 days of submitting a request for relief.

units.obligation_text: An applicant may ask us for more time to submit evidence under paragraph (a) of this section.
units.action_summary: May request an extension of time to submit required evidence.

units.obligation_text: The request for an extension of time must be in writing
units.action_summary: The extension request must be submitted in writing.

units.obligation_text: The request for an extension of time must ... give the reasons why the applicant cannot give us the required evidence within the 30-day period.
units.action_summary: The extension request must explain why the applicant cannot provide the required evidence within 30 days.

units.obligation_text: If the applicant shows us that he or she had good cause for missing the deadline, we will extend the 30-day period.
units.action_summary: The agency will extend the 30-day period if the applicant demonstrates good cause for missing the deadline.

units.obligation_text: To determine whether good cause exists, we use the standards explained in § 404.911 of this chapter.
units.action_summary: Use the standards in §404.911 to determine whether good cause exists for missing the deadline.

units.obligation_text: If the applicant does not submit the evidence required under § 421.151 within the 30-day period provided under paragraph (a) of this section, or within the extended period provided under paragraph (b) of this section, we will dismiss the request for relief.
units.action_summary: If the applicant fails to submit required evidence within the 30-day or extended period, the agency will dismiss the request for relief.

units.obligation_text: An applicant who requests relief under § 421.150 must prove that he or she is not likely to act in a manner dangerous to public safety and that granting relief from the prohibitions imposed by 18 U.S.C. 922(d)(4) and (g)(4) will not be contrary to the public interest.
units.action_summary: Prove unlikelihood of dangerous conduct and that granting relief would not harm the public interest.

units.obligation_text: We may grant an applicant’s request for relief if the applicant establishes, to our satisfaction, that the circumstances regarding the disability, and the applicant’s record and reputation, are such that the applicant will not be likely to act in a manner dangerous to public safety, and that the granting of the relief would not be contrary to the public interest.
units.action_summary: Agency may grant relief if applicant establishes to agency's satisfaction that relief won't pose a public safety risk and won't be contrary to public interest.

units.obligation_text: the applicant establishes, to our satisfaction, that the circumstances regarding the disability, and the applicant’s record and reputation, are such that the applicant will not be likely to act in a manner dangerous to public safety, and that the granting of the relief would not be contrary to the public interest.
units.action_summary: Applicant must establish to the agency's satisfaction facts about disability, record, and reputation showing low risk to public safety and that relief would not harm public interest.

units.obligation_text: We will not grant an applicant’s request for relief if the applicant is prohibited from possessing firearms by the law of the State in which the applicant resides.
units.action_summary: The agency will not grant relief if state law prohibits the applicant from possessing firearms.

units.obligation_text: After the applicant submits the evidence required under § 421.151 and any other evidence he or she wants us to consider, we will review the evidence, which will include any evidence from our records that we determine is appropriate.
units.action_summary: The agency will review submitted evidence (including appropriate records) after the applicant files it.

units.obligation_text: A decision maker who was not involved in making the finding that the applicant’s benefit payments be made through a representative payee will review the evidence and act on the request for relief.
units.actor: a decision maker not involved in the representative payee finding
units.action_summary: A different decision maker will review the evidence and act on the request for relief.

units.obligation_text: We will notify the applicant in writing of our action regarding the request for relief.
units.action_summary: Notify the applicant in writing of the agency's action on the request for relief.

units.obligation_text: If we deny an applicant’s request for relief, we will send the applicant a written notice that explains the reasons for our action.
units.action_summary: If the request is denied, send a written notice explaining the reasons.

units.obligation_text: We will also inform the applicant that if he or she is dissatisfied with our action, he or she has 60 days from the date he or she receives the notice of our action to file a petition seeking judicial review in Federal district court.
units.action_summary: Inform denied applicants of the 60-day period to file a petition for judicial review in Federal district court.

units.obligation_text: If we grant an applicant’s request for relief, we will send the applicant a written notice that explains the reasons for our action.
units.action_summary: If the request is granted, send a written notice explaining the reasons.

units.obligation_text: We will inform the applicant that we will notify the Attorney General, or his or her delegate, that the individual’s record should be removed from the NICS database.
units.action_summary: Inform the applicant that the agency will notify the Attorney General to remove the individual's record from the NICS database.

units.obligation_text: We will also notify the applicant that he or she is no longer prohibited under 18 U.S.C. 922(g)(4) from purchasing, possessing, receiving, shipping, or transporting firearms or ammunition based on the prohibition that we granted the applicant relief from.
units.action_summary: Notify the applicant that they are no longer prohibited under 18 U.S.C. 922(g)(4) with respect to firearms/ammunition based on the grant of relief.

units.obligation_text: We will notify the Attorney General, or his or her delegate, that the applicant’s record should be removed from the NICS database after we grant the applicant’s request for relief.
units.action_summary: Notify the Attorney General (or delegate) to remove the applicant's record from the NICS database after granting relief.

units.obligation_text: The NIAA requires us to process each application for relief not later than 365 days after the date we receive it.
units.action_summary: Process each application for relief within 365 days of receipt, as required by the NIAA.

units.obligation_text: If we fail to resolve an application for relief within that period for any reason, including a lack of appropriated funds, we will be deemed to have denied the relief request without cause.
units.action_summary: If the agency fails to resolve an application within 365 days, the application is deemed denied without cause.

units.obligation_text: In accordance with the NIAA, judicial review of any petition brought under this paragraph shall be de novo.
units.action_summary: Judicial review of petitions under this paragraph must be de novo.

units.obligation_text: Judicial review of our action denying an applicant’s request for review is available according to the standards contained in 18 U.S.C. 925(c).
units.action_summary: Judicial review of a denial is available under the standards in 18 U.S.C. 925(c).

units.obligation_text: At the applicable time specified in Airbus Service Bulletin A300–54–0081, dated August 11, 1993: Modify the pylons, in accordance with Airbus Service Bulletin 300–54–0081, dated August 11, 1993.

units.obligation_text: Thereafter, repeat the HFEC inspection specified in paragraph (h) of this AD at the applicable interval specified in Airbus Service Bulletin A300–54–0075, Revision 04, dated May 26, 2015,
units.action_summary: After modification, repeat the HFEC inspection at the interval specified in the service bulletin.

units.obligation_text: and repair any crack before further flight using a method approved by the Manager, International Branch, ANM–116, Transport Airplane Directorate, FAA; or the European Aviation Safety Agency (EASA); or Airbus’s EASA Design Organization Approval (DOA).
units.actor: owners/operators of the affected airplanes (or repair provider)
units.action_summary: Repair any crack before further flight using a repair method approved by the FAA Manager, EASA, or Airbus's EASA DOA.

units.obligation_text: If any crack is confirmed during the inspection required by paragraph (h) of this AD, repair before further flight using a method approved by the Manager, International Branch, ANM–116, Transport Airplane Directorate, FAA; or EASA; or Airbus’s EASA DOA.
units.actor: owners/operators of the affected airplanes (or repair provider)
units.action_summary: If an HFEC inspection confirms a crack, repair it before further flight using a method approved by the FAA Manager, EASA, or Airbus's EASA DOA.

title: Submission of Food and Drug Administration Import Data in the Automated Commercial Environment

units.obligation_text: When filing an entry in ACE, the ACE filer shall submit the following information for food as applicable, and drugs, biological products, HCT/Ps, medical devices, radiation-emitting electronic products, cosmetics, and tobacco products.
units.action_summary: Submit the required information elements in ACE when filing an import entry for FDA-regulated articles.

units.obligation_text: Product identifying information for the article that is being imported or offered for import. This consists of:
units.action_summary: Submit product identifying information for the imported article consisting of specified elements.

units.obligation_text: FDA Country of Production, which is, the country where the article was last manufactured, processed, or grown (including harvested, or collected and readied for shipment to the United States).
units.action_summary: Submit the FDA Country of Production (country where last manufactured/processed/grown).

units.obligation_text: The FDA Country of Production for an article that has undergone any manufacturing or processing is the country where that activity occurred provided that the manufacturing or processing had more than a minor, negligible, or insignificant effect on the article.
units.action_summary: If the article underwent meaningful manufacturing/processing, report the country where that occurred as the FDA Country of Production.

units.obligation_text: The Complete FDA Product Code, which must agree with the invoice description of the product.
units.action_summary: Submit the Complete FDA Product Code that matches the invoice description.

units.obligation_text: FDA Value which is the total value of the article(s) in an import entry or import line, rounded off to the nearest dollar, which must match the invoice value of those article(s).
units.action_summary: Submit the FDA Value (total value rounded to nearest dollar) matching the invoice.

units.obligation_text: FDA Quantity which is the quantity of the article(s) in an import line delineated by packaging level, including the type of package from the largest packaging unit to the smallest packaging unit; the quantity of each packaging unit; and the volume and/or weight of each of the smallest of the packaging units.
units.action_summary: Submit FDA Quantity detailing packaging levels, quantities of each unit, and volume/weight of smallest units.

units.obligation_text: Entity Identification Information, (1) Name, telephone, and email address of any one of the persons related to the importation of the product which may include the manufacturer, shipper, importer of record, or Deliver to Party. (2) Telephone and email address of the importer of record.
units.action_summary: Submit entity identification information including contact details for a person related to importation and the importer's telephone and email.

units.obligation_text: Name, telephone, and email address of any one of the persons related to the importation of the product which may include the manufacturer, shipper, importer of record, or Deliver to Party.
units.action_summary: Provide name, telephone, and email of one person related to the importation (e.g., manufacturer, shipper, importer of record).

units.obligation_text: Telephone and email address of the importer of record.
units.action_summary: Provide the telephone and email address of the importer of record.

units.obligation_text: The information specified in § 1.72(a)(3) must be submitted in ACE at the time of filing entry for food.
units.action_summary: Submit the FDA Value (§1.72(a)(3)) in ACE at the time of filing entry for food.

units.obligation_text: The information specified in § 1.72 must be submitted in ACE at the time of filing entry for food that is a food contact substance.
units.action_summary: Submit all §1.72 information in ACE at entry filing for food contact substances.

units.obligation_text: For an article of food that is a low-acid canned food, the ACE filer must submit at the time of filing entry the Food Canning Establishment Number and the Submission Identifier, and can dimensions or volume.
units.action_summary: Submit Food Canning Establishment Number, Submission Identifier, and can dimensions/volume for low-acid canned foods at entry filing.

units.obligation_text: For an article of food that is an acidified food, the ACE filer must submit at the time of filing entry the Food Canning Establishment Number and the Submission Identifier, and can dimensions or volume.
units.action_summary: Submit Food Canning Establishment Number, Submission Identifier, and can dimensions/volume for acidified foods at entry filing.

units.obligation_text: In addition to the data required to be submitted in § 1.72, an ACE filer must submit the following information at the time of filing entry for drugs, including biological products, intended for human use that are regulated by the FDA Center for Drug Evaluation and Research.
units.action_summary: Submit additional specified information in ACE at entry filing for human drugs and related biological products.

units.obligation_text: For a drug intended for human use, the Drug Registration Number and the Drug Listing Number.
units.action_summary: Submit Drug Registration Number and Drug Listing Number for human drugs.

units.obligation_text: For the purposes of this section, the Drug Registration Number that must be submitted in ACE is the unique facility identifier of the foreign establishment where the human drug was manufactured, prepared, propagated, compounded or processed before being imported or offered for import into the United States. The unique facility identifier is the identifier submitted by a registrant in accordance with the system specified under section 510(b) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act. For the purposes of this section, the Drug Listing Number is the National Drug Code number of the human drug article being imported or offered for import.
units.action_summary: Definition/specification of what constitutes the Drug Registration Number (unique facility identifier) and Drug Listing Number (NDC).

units.obligation_text: For a drug intended for human use that is the subject of an approved application under section 505(b) or 505(j) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, the number of the new drug application or abbreviated new drug application.
units.action_summary: If the drug is subject to an approved NDA or ANDA, submit the application number in ACE at entry filing.

units.obligation_text: For a drug intended for human use that is the subject of an investigational new drug application under section 505(i) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, the number of the investigational new drug application.
units.action_summary: If the drug is subject to an IND, submit the IND number at entry filing.

units.obligation_text: In addition to the data required to be submitted in § 1.72, an ACE filer must submit the following information at the time of filing entry for animal drugs:
units.action_summary: Submit additional specified information in ACE at entry filing for animal drugs.

units.obligation_text: For a drug intended for animal use, the Drug Registration Number and the Drug Listing Number ... the Drug Registration Number that must be submitted in ACE is the Unique Facility Identifier of the foreign establishment where the animal drug was manufactured ... For the purposes of this section, the Drug Listing Number is the National Drug Code number of the animal drug article being imported or offered for import.
units.action_summary: Submit Drug Registration Number (Unique Facility Identifier) and Drug Listing Number (NDC) for animal drugs.

units.obligation_text: For a drug intended for animal use that is the subject of an approved application under section 512 of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, the number of the new animal drug application or abbreviated new animal drug application. For a drug intended for animal use that is the subject of a conditionally approved application under section 571 of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, the application number for the conditionally approved new animal drug.
units.action_summary: If the animal drug is the subject of an approved or conditionally approved application, submit the applicable application number.

units.obligation_text: For a drug intended for use in animals that is the subject of an Index listing under section 572 of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, the Minor Species Index File number of the new animal drug on the Index of Legally Marketed Unapproved New Animal Drugs for Minor Species.
units.action_summary: If the animal drug is listed on the Minor Species Index, submit the Index File number.

units.obligation_text: For a drug intended for animal use that is the subject of an investigational new animal drug or generic investigational new animal drug application under part 511 of this chapter, the number of the investigational new animal drug or generic investigational new animal drug file.
units.action_summary: If subject to an investigational new animal drug application, submit the application/file number.

units.obligation_text: In addition to the data required to be submitted in § 1.72, an ACE filer must submit the following information at the time of filing entry for medical devices regulated by the FDA Center for Devices and Radiological Health.
units.action_summary: Submit additional specified information in ACE at entry filing for medical devices regulated by CDRH.

units.obligation_text: For a medical device, the Registration Number for Foreign Manufacturers, Foreign Exporters, and/or Domestic Manufacturers, and the Device Listing Number, required under section 510 of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act and part 807 of this chapter.
units.action_summary: Submit Registration Number(s) and Device Listing Number for the medical device as required under section 510 and part 807.

units.obligation_text: For an investigational medical device that has an investigational device exemption granted under section 520(g) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, the Investigational Device Exemption Number.
units.action_summary: If device has an IDE, submit the Investigational Device Exemption Number.

units.obligation_text: For an investigational medical device being imported or offered for import for use in a nonsignificant risk or exempt study, "NSR" to be entered in the Affirmation of Compliance for the "investigational device exemption" that identifies the device as being used in a nonsignificant risk or exempt study.
units.action_summary: If investigational device is for a nonsignificant risk or exempt study, enter 'NSR' in the Affirmation of Compliance.

units.obligation_text: For a medical device that has one, the Premarket Number. This is the Premarket Approval Number ... the Product Development Protocol Number ... the De Novo number ... the Premarket Notification Number ... or the Humanitarian Device Exemption Number ...
units.action_summary: If applicable, submit the appropriate Premarket Number (PMA, PDP, De Novo, 510(k), or HDE number) for the device.

units.obligation_text: If applicable for a medical device, an affirmation identifying that the article being imported or offered for import is a component that requires further processing or inclusion into a finished medical device.
units.action_summary: If the article is a component requiring further processing or inclusion into a finished device, submit an affirmation identifying it as such.

units.obligation_text: For electrode lead wires and patient cables intended for use with a medical device, an Affirmation of Compliance with the applicable performance standard under § 898.12 of this chapter.
units.action_summary: Submit an Affirmation of Compliance with the performance standard (§898.12) for electrode lead wires and patient cables.

units.obligation_text: For impact resistant lenses in eyeglasses and sunglasses, an Affirmation of Compliance with the applicable requirements of § 801.410 of this chapter.
units.action_summary: Submit an Affirmation of Compliance with §801.410 for impact resistant lenses in eyeglasses and sunglasses.

units.obligation_text: If applicable for a medical device, an Affirmation of Compliance that the article imported or offered for import is a convenience kit or part of a convenience kit.
units.action_summary: If the article is a convenience kit or part of one, submit an Affirmation of Compliance stating so.

units.obligation_text: For a combination product consisting of at least one medical device and one drug intended for human use that is the subject of an investigational new drug application under section 505(i) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, where the FDA Center for Devices and Radiological Health has been designated by FDA as the center with primary jurisdiction for the premarket review and regulation of the combination product, the number of the investigational new drug application.
units.action_summary: If combination product is subject to an IND and CDRH is primary jurisdiction, submit the IND number.

units.obligation_text: In addition to the data required to be submitted in § 1.72, an ACE filer must submit all of the declarations required in Form FDA 2877 electronically in ACE at the time of filing entry for products subject to the standards under parts 1020–1050 of this chapter.
units.action_summary: Submit electronically in ACE all declarations from Form FDA 2877 at entry filing for radiation-emitting electronic products subject to parts 1020–1050.

units.obligation_text: In addition to the data required to be submitted in § 1.72, an ACE filer must submit the following information at the time of entry for biological products, HCT/Ps, and related drugs and medical devices regulated by the FDA Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research.
units.action_summary: Submit additional specified information in ACE at entry filing for biological products, HCT/Ps, and related drugs/devices regulated by CBER.

units.obligation_text: Product name which identifies the article being imported or offered for import by the name commonly associated with that article including the established name, trade name, brand name, proper name, or product description if the article does not have an established name, trade name, brand name or proper name.
units.action_summary: Submit a product name identifying the article (established/trade/brand/proper name or product description).

units.obligation_text: For an HCT/P regulated solely under section 361 ... manufactured by an establishment that is required to be registered under part 1271 of this chapter, the HCT/P Registration Number;
units.action_summary: If HCT/P is regulated solely under section 361 and manufactured by a registered establishment, submit the HCT/P Registration Number.

units.obligation_text: For an HCT/P regulated solely under section 361 ... an affirmation of compliance with the applicable requirements of part 1271 of this chapter.
units.action_summary: If HCT/P is regulated solely under section 361, submit an affirmation of compliance with part 1271 requirements.

units.obligation_text: For a biological product that is the subject of an approved biologics license application under section 351 of the Public Health Service Act, the Submission Tracking Number of the biologics license application and/or the Biologics License Number.
units.action_summary: If product is subject to an approved BLA, submit the Submission Tracking Number and/or Biologics License Number.

units.obligation_text: For a drug intended for human use, the Drug Registration Number and the Drug Listing Number ... the Drug Registration Number that must be submitted in ACE is the unique facility identifier ... the Drug Listing Number is the National Drug Code number of the human drug article being imported or offered for import.
units.action_summary: For human-use drugs among biologicals, submit Drug Registration Number (unique facility identifier) and Drug Listing Number (NDC).

units.obligation_text: For a drug intended for human use that is the subject of an approved application under section 505(b) or 505(j) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, the number of the new drug application or the abbreviated new drug application.
units.action_summary: If drug is subject to an approved NDA or ANDA, submit the application number.

units.obligation_text: For a drug intended for human use that is the subject of an investigational new drug application under section 505(i) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, the number of the investigational new drug application.
units.action_summary: If drug is subject to an IND, submit the IND number.

units.obligation_text: For a medical device subject to the registration and listing procedures contained in part 807 of this chapter, the Registration Number for Foreign Manufacturers, Foreign Exporters, and/or Domestic Manufacturers, and the Device Listing Number, required under section 510 of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act and part 807 of this chapter.
units.action_summary: For medical devices among these articles, submit Registration Number(s) and Device Listing Number as required under section 510 and part 807.

units.obligation_text: For an investigational medical device that has an investigational device exemption granted under section 520(g) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, the Investigational Device Exemption Number. For an investigational medical device being imported or offered for import for use in a nonsignificant risk or exempt study, an Affirmation of Compliance that identifies the device as being used in such a study.
units.action_summary: If device has an IDE, submit the IDE number; if for NSR/exempt study, submit an Affirmation of Compliance identifying such use.

units.obligation_text: For a medical device that has one, the premarket number. This is the premarket approval number ... the Product Development Protocol Number ... the De Novo number ... the Premarket Notification Number ... or the Humanitarian Device Exemption Number ...
units.action_summary: If applicable, submit the appropriate medical device premarket number (PMA, PDP, De Novo, 510(k), or HDE).

units.obligation_text: If applicable for a medical device, an affirmation identifying that the article being imported or offered for import is a component that requires further processing or inclusion into a finished medical device.
units.action_summary: If the article is a medical device component requiring further processing, submit an affirmation identifying it as such.

units.obligation_text: In addition to the data required to be submitted in § 1.72, an ACE filer must submit the following information at the time of filing entry in ACE.
units.action_summary: Submit additional specified information in ACE at entry filing for entries that include tobacco products.

units.obligation_text: Brand name of the article that is a tobacco product being imported or offered for import.
units.action_summary: Submit the brand name of the tobacco product being imported or offered for import.

units.obligation_text: Name and address of the ACE filer for any entry that includes an article that is a tobacco product.
units.action_summary: Provide the name and address of the ACE filer for entries including tobacco products.

units.obligation_text: An ACE filer must submit the data specified in § 1.72 at the time of filing entry in ACE.
units.action_summary: Submit the §1.72 data in ACE at the time of filing entry for cosmetics.

units.obligation_text: When a sample of an article offered for import has been requested by the district director, FDA shall provide to the owner or consignee prompt notice of delivery of, or intention to deliver, such sample.
units.action_summary: Provide prompt notice to the owner or consignee of delivery or intent to deliver a sample when requested by the district director.

units.obligation_text: Upon receipt of the notice, the owner or consignee shall hold such article ... until further notice from the district director or U.S. Customs and Border Protection of the results of examination of the sample.
units.action_summary: Upon receiving notice, hold the article until further notice of sample examination results.

units.obligation_text: Upon receipt of the notice, the owner or consignee shall ... not distribute it until further notice from the district director or U.S. Customs and Border Protection of the results of examination of the sample.
units.action_summary: Do not distribute the article upon receipt of the notice until further notice of sample examination results.

units.obligation_text: If it appears that the article may be subject to refusal of admission, or that the article is a drug that may be subject to destruction under section 801(a) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, the district director shall give the owner or consignee a written or electronic notice to that effect, stating the reasons therefor.
units.action_summary: Give the owner or consignee a written or electronic notice stating reasons if the article may be refused admission or may be subject to destruction.

units.obligation_text: If the article is a drug that may be subject to destruction under section 801(a) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, the district director may give the owner or consignee a single written or electronic notice that provides the notice on refusal of admission and the notice on destruction of an article described in paragraph (a) of this section.
units.action_summary: May provide a single written/electronic notice combining refusal of admission and destruction notices for drugs that may be destroyed under section 801(a).

units.obligation_text: Except as provided in paragraphs (c) and (d) of this section, when an HCT/P is offered for import, the importer of record must notify, either before or at the time of importation, the director of the district of the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) having jurisdiction over the port of entry ... and must provide sufficient information, including information submitted in the Automated Commercial Environment (ACE) system or any other Electronic Data Interchange system authorized by the United States Customs and Border Protection Agency as required in part 1, subpart D of this chapter, for FDA to make an admissibility decision.
units.action_summary: Notify the FDA district director before or at importation and provide sufficient information (including ACE-submitted data) for FDA to make an admissibility decision for imported HCT/Ps, except as provided in paragraphs (c) and (d).

title: New Animal Drugs for Use in Animal Feed; Category Definitions

units.obligation_text: Category I—These drugs require no withdrawal period at the lowest use level in each major species for which they are approved or are approved for use only in minor species.
units.action_summary: Category I drugs must have no withdrawal period at the lowest use level in each approved major species, or are approved only for use in minor species.

units.obligation_text: Category II—These drugs require a withdrawal period at the lowest use level for at least one major species for which they are approved, or are regulated on a ‘‘no-residue’’ basis or with a zero tolerance because of carcinogenic concern regardless of whether a withdrawal period is required in any species.
units.action_summary: Category II drugs must have a withdrawal period at the lowest use level for at least one approved major species, or be regulated on a no-residue/zero-tolerance basis due to carcinogenic concern, regardless of withdrawal periods elsewhere.

units.obligation_text: require a withdrawal period at the lowest use level for at least one major species for which they are approved
units.action_summary: A withdrawal period at the lowest use level is required for at least one major species for which the drug is approved.

units.obligation_text: are regulated on a ‘‘no-residue’’ basis or with a zero tolerance because of carcinogenic concern
units.action_summary: Alternatively, such drugs are regulated on a no-residue basis or subject to zero tolerance due to carcinogenic concern.

units.obligation_text: regardless of whether a withdrawal period is required in any species
units.action_summary: The no-residue/zero-tolerance regulation applies irrespective of whether any species has a withdrawal period.

title: List of Bulk Drug Substances That Can Be Used To Compound Drug Products in Accordance With Section 503A of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act

units.obligation_text: The following bulk drug substances can be used in compounding under section 503A(b)(1)(A)(i)(III) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act.
units.action_summary: Permits the use of the listed bulk drug substances in compounding under section 503A(b)(1)(A)(i)(III).

units.obligation_text: Brilliant Blue G, also known as Coomassie Brilliant Blue G–250.
units.action_summary: Permits use of Brilliant Blue G in compounding under § 216.23(a).

units.obligation_text: Cantharidin (for topical use only).
units.action_summary: Permits use of cantharidin in compounding but only for topical use.

units.obligation_text: Diphenylcyclopropenone (for topical use only).
units.action_summary: Permits use of diphenylcyclopropenone in compounding but only for topical use.

units.obligation_text: N-acetyl-D-glucosamine (for topical use only).
units.action_summary: Permits use of N-acetyl-D-glucosamine in compounding but only for topical use.

units.obligation_text: Squaric acid dibutyl ester (for topical use only).
units.action_summary: Permits use of squaric acid dibutyl ester in compounding but only for topical use.

units.obligation_text: Thymol iodide (for topical use only).
units.action_summary: Permits use of thymol iodide in compounding but only for topical use.

units.obligation_text: After balancing the criteria set forth in paragraph (c) of this section, FDA has determined that the following bulk drug substances will not be included on the list of substances that can be used in compounding set forth in paragraph (a) of this section:
units.action_summary: FDA has determined that the listed substances will not be placed on the § 216.23(a) list of substances that can be used in compounding.

units.obligation_text: Oxitriptan.
units.action_summary: Specifies that oxitriptan will not be included on the § 216.23(a) compounding list.

units.obligation_text: Piracetam.
units.action_summary: Specifies that piracetam will not be included on the § 216.23(a) compounding list.

units.obligation_text: Silver Protein Mild.
units.action_summary: Specifies that silver protein mild will not be included on the § 216.23(a) compounding list.

units.obligation_text: Tranilast.
units.action_summary: Specifies that tranilast will not be included on the § 216.23(a) compounding list.

units.obligation_text: FDA will use the following criteria in evaluating substances considered for inclusion on the list set forth in paragraph (a) of this section:
units.action_summary: Requires FDA to apply the listed criteria when evaluating substances for inclusion on the § 216.23(a) list.

units.obligation_text: The physical and chemical characterization of the substance;
units.action_summary: FDA must consider the physical and chemical characterization of the substance when evaluating it for inclusion.

units.obligation_text: Any safety issues raised by the use of the substance in compounded drug products;
units.action_summary: FDA must consider any safety issues associated with use of the substance in compounded products.

units.obligation_text: The available evidence of the effectiveness or lack of effectiveness of a drug product compounded with the substance, if any such evidence exists; and
units.action_summary: FDA must consider available evidence regarding effectiveness of compounded products containing the substance.

units.obligation_text: Historical use of the substance in compounded drug products, including information about the medical condition(s) the substance has been used to treat and any references in peer-reviewed medical literature.
units.action_summary: FDA must consider historical use of the substance in compounding, medical conditions treated, and peer-reviewed references.

units.obligation_text: Any person who represents that a compounded drug made with a bulk drug substance that appears on this list is FDA approved, or otherwise endorsed by FDA generally or for a particular indication, will cause the drug to be misbranded under section 502(a) and/or 502(bb) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act.
units.action_summary: If a person represents that a compounded drug made with a listed bulk drug substance is FDA-approved or FDA-endorsed, that representation will render the drug misbranded under sections 502(a) and/or 502(bb).

title: Lowfat and Skim Milk Products, Lowfat and Nonfat Yogurt Products, Lowfat Cottage Cheese: Proposed Revocation of Standards of Identity; Food Labeling, Nutrient Content Claims for Fat, Fatty Acids and Cholesterol Content of Food

units.obligation_text: (b) "Zar content claims." (1) The terms "fat free," "free of fat," "no fat," "zero fat," "without fat," "negligible source of fat," or "dietarily insignificant source of fat" or, in the case of milk products, "skim" may be used on the label or in labeling of foods, provided that:

units.obligation_text: FDA shall consider the use of an investigational device under a treatment IDE if:
units.action_summary: FDA must consider allowing use of an investigational device under a treatment IDE when the following criteria are met

units.obligation_text: The device is intended to treat or diagnose a serious or immediately life-threatening disease or condition;
units.actor: the device (as to its intended use)
units.action_summary: The device must be intended to treat or diagnose a serious or immediately life‑threatening condition (criterion for consideration)

units.obligation_text: The use has been shown to result in or may be expected to result in dietary concentrations at or below 0.5 parts per billion, corresponding to dietary exposure levels at or below 1.5 micrograms/person/day.

units.obligation_text: Data that will enable the Food and Drug Administration to estimate the daily dietary concentration resulting from the proposed use of the substance. These data should be either in the form of:

units.obligation_text: Validated migration data obtained under worst-case (time/temperature) intended use conditions utilizing appropriate food-simulating solvents;
units.action_summary: One acceptable form of data is validated migration data from worst-case intended use conditions.

units.obligation_text: Levels of the substances used in the manufacture of the food-contact article;
units.action_summary: Another acceptable form of data is the levels of the substances used in manufacture of the food-contact article.

units.obligation_text: Residual levels of the substances present in the food-contact article. units.obligation_text: Under section 409(i) of the FD&C Act, we shall by regulation prescribe the procedure by which regulations under the foregoing provisions of this section may be amended or repealed, and such procedure shall conform to the procedure provided in this section for the promulgation of such regulations.
units.action_summary: FDA must prescribe by regulation the procedure for amending or repealing regulations under section 409, and that procedure must conform to the statute's promulgation procedure.

units.obligation_text: Our regulations specific to administrative actions for food additives provide that the Commissioner of Food and Drugs, on his own initiative or on the petition of any interested person, under 21 CFR part 10, may propose the issuance of a regulation amending or repealing a regulation pertaining to a food additive or granting or repealing an exception for such additive (§ 171.130(a)).
units.actor: The Commissioner of Food and Drugs
units.action_summary: The Commissioner may propose issuing regulations that amend or repeal food additive regulations or grant/repeal exceptions, on his own initiative or on petition.

units.obligation_text: These regulations further provide that any such petition shall include an assertion of facts, supported by data, showing that new information exists with respect to the food additive or that new uses have been developed or old uses abandoned, that new data are available as to toxicity of the chemical, or that experience with the existing regulation or exemption may justify its amendment or appeal (§ 171.130(b)).
units.action_summary: A petition must include an assertion of facts supported by data showing new information, new/abandoned uses, new toxicity data, or experience justifying amendment or appeal.

units.obligation_text: New data must be furnished in the form specified in 21 CFR 171.1 and 171.100 for submitting petitions (id.).
units.action_summary: New data submitted with petitions must be provided in the form specified by 21 CFR 171.1 and 171.100.

units.obligation_text: Under these regulations, a petitioner may propose that we amend a food additive regulation if the petitioner can demonstrate that there are "old uses abandoned" for the relevant food additive (id.).
units.action_summary: A petitioner may propose amendment of a food additive regulation if they demonstrate that old uses have been abandoned.

units.obligation_text: Such abandonment must be complete for any intended uses in the U.S. market.
units.action_summary: Demonstrated abandonment must be complete with respect to any intended uses in the U.S. market.

units.obligation_text: If a FAP seeks an amendment to a food additive regulation based on the abandonment of certain uses of the food additive, such uses must be adequately defined so that both the scope of the abandonment and any amendment to the food additive regulation are clear.
units.action_summary: If seeking amendment based on abandonment of certain uses, the petitioner must adequately define those uses so the scope and any regulatory amendment are clear.

units.obligation_text: Any comments indicating that the specified uses of one or more of the 26 substances have not been abandoned should specify the ortho-phthalate(s) (or substances identified in the petition as ortho-phthalates).
units.action_summary: Commenters asserting that specified uses have not been abandoned should identify the specific ortho-phthalates involved.

units.obligation_text: We also recommend including information about the use, any relevant regulation(s) authorizing the use, and a description of the product that contains the substance(s).
