units.action_summary: If a master file is not referenced within 5 years, FDA will return it to the submitter.

units.obligation_text: The applicant shall periodically update its pending application with new safety and effectiveness information learned about the device from ongoing or completed studies that may reasonably affect an evaluation of the safety or effectiveness of the device or that may reasonably affect the statement of contraindications, warnings, precautions, and adverse reactions in the draft labeling.
units.action_summary: Periodically update the pending application with new safety and effectiveness information from studies that may affect safety/effectiveness evaluations or draft labeling.

units.obligation_text: The update report shall be consistent with the data reporting provisions of the protocol.
units.action_summary: Ensure update reports comply with the protocol's data reporting provisions.

units.obligation_text: The applicant shall submit any update report in electronic format and shall include in the report the number assigned by FDA to the PMA.
units.action_summary: Submit update reports electronically and include the FDA-assigned PMA number.

units.obligation_text: These updates are considered to be amendments to the PMA.
units.action_summary: Updates to a pending PMA are treated as amendments to the PMA.

units.obligation_text: The time frame for review of a PMA will not be extended due to the submission of an update report unless the update is a major amendment under § 814.37(c)(1).
units.action_summary: FDA will not extend PMA review time due to update reports unless the update qualifies as a major amendment under §814.37(c)(1).

units.obligation_text: If a color additive subject to section 721 of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act is used in or on the device and has not previously been listed for such use, then, in lieu of submitting a color additive petition under part 71 of this chapter, at the option of the applicant, the information required to be submitted under part 71 may be submitted as part of the PMA.
units.action_summary: If an unlisted color additive is used, the applicant may submit the required color additive information within the PMA instead of making a separate petition under part 71.

units.obligation_text: When submitted as part of the PMA, the information shall be submitted in electronic format.
units.action_summary: When color additive information is included in the PMA, submit that information in electronic format.

units.obligation_text: A PMA for a device that contains a color additive that is subject to section 721 of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act will not be approved until the color additive is listed for use in or on the device.
units.action_summary: FDA will not approve a PMA for a device containing a section 721 color additive until that color additive is listed for use on the device.

units.obligation_text: For devices regulated by the Center for Devices and Radiological Health, send it to the current address displayed on the website http://www.fda.gov/cdrhsubmissionaddress.
units.action_summary: Send PMA submissions for CDRH-regulated devices to the current CDRH submission address on FDA's website.

units.obligation_text: For devices regulated by the Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research, send it to the current address displayed on the website https://www.fda.gov/AboutFDA/CentersOffices/OfficeofMedicalProductsandTobacco/CBER/ucm385240.htm.
units.action_summary: Send PMA submissions for CBER-regulated devices to the current CBER address on FDA's website.

units.obligation_text: All procedures and actions that apply to an application under § 814.20 also apply to PMA supplements except that the information required in a supplement is limited to that needed to support the change.
units.action_summary: All procedures/actions applicable to a PMA also apply to PMA supplements, but supplements need only include information necessary to support the change.

units.obligation_text: A summary under § 814.20(b)(3) is required for only a supplement submitted for new indications for use of the device, significant changes in the performance or design specifications, circuits, components, ingredients, principles of operation, or physical layout of the device, or when otherwise required by FDA.
units.action_summary: A §814.20(b)(3) summary is required only for supplements involving new indications, significant changes in device performance/design, or when FDA requires it.

units.obligation_text: The applicant shall submit a PMA supplement in electronic format and shall include information relevant to the proposed changes in the device.
units.action_summary: Submit PMA supplements electronically and include information relevant to the proposed changes.

units.obligation_text: A PMA supplement shall include a separate section that identifies each change for which approval is being requested and explains the reason for each such change.
units.action_summary: Include a separate section in the supplement that identifies each requested change and explains the reason for each change.

units.obligation_text: The applicant shall submit additional information, if requested by FDA, in electronic format.
units.action_summary: If FDA requests additional information, the applicant must submit it electronically.

units.obligation_text: All original HDEs, amendments and supplements, as well as any correspondence relating to an HDE, must be provided in electronic format. These materials must be sent or delivered to one of the following:
units.action_summary: Provide original HDEs, amendments, supplements, and related correspondence in electronic format and send/deliver them to one of the specified addresses.

units.obligation_text: For devices regulated by the Center for Devices and Radiological Health, send it to the current address found on the website https://www.fda.gov/cdrhsubmissionaddress.
units.action_summary: Send HDE submissions for CDRH-regulated devices to the current CDRH address on FDA's website.

units.obligation_text: For devices regulated by the Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research, send it to the current address displayed on the website https://www.fda.gov/AboutFDA/CentersOffices/OfficeofMedicalProductsandTobacco/CBER/ucm385240.htm.
units.action_summary: Send HDE submissions for CBER-regulated devices to the current CBER address on FDA's website.

title: Public Information

units.obligation_text: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) will make the fullest possible disclosure of records to the public, consistent with the rights of individuals to privacy, the property rights of persons in trade secrets and confidential commercial or financial information, and the need for the Agency to promote frank internal policy deliberations and to pursue its regulatory activities without disruption.
units.action_summary: FDA must make the fullest possible disclosure of records to the public, consistent with privacy, trade secret, and deliberative process considerations.

units.obligation_text: Except where specifically exempt pursuant to the provisions of this part, all FDA records shall be made available for public disclosure.
units.action_summary: All non-exempt FDA records must be made available for public disclosure unless specifically exempted.

units.obligation_text: FDA will make discretionary disclosures of records or information exempt from disclosure under the provisions of this part whenever disclosure would not foreseeably harm an interest protected by an exemption pursuant to this part.
units.action_summary: FDA must disclose exempt records at its discretion when disclosure would not foreseeably harm an interest protected by an exemption.

units.obligation_text: This provision does not require disclosure of information that is prohibited from disclosure by law.
units.action_summary: The rule does not obligate disclosure of information that is legally prohibited from disclosure.

units.obligation_text: In accordance with the FOIA Improvement Act of 2016 (Pub. L. 114–185), FDA will establish procedures for identifying records of general interest or use to the public that are appropriate for public disclosure, and for posting and indexing such records in a publicly accessible electronic format.
units.action_summary: FDA must set up procedures to identify, post, and index records of general public interest in a publicly accessible electronic format.

units.obligation_text: Except as provided in paragraph (e) of this section, all nonexempt records shall be made available for public disclosure upon request regardless of whether any justification or need for such records have been shown.
units.action_summary: FDA must provide all nonexempt records upon request, without requiring the requester to show justification or need, except as otherwise provided.

units.obligation_text: The exemption(s) under which the information has been deleted shall be noted at the site of the deletion.
units.action_summary: When information is deleted from a record, the specific exemption(s) applied must be noted at the location of the deletion.

units.obligation_text: Response letters shall contain contact information for the FOIA Public Liaison and the Office of Government Information Services as required by the FOIA Improvement Act of 2016 (Pub. L. 114–185).
units.action_summary: Response letters must include contact information for the FOIA Public Liaison and the Office of Government Information Services.

units.obligation_text: All requests for Food and Drug Administration records shall be made in writing by mailing or delivering the request to the Freedom of Information Staff at the address on the Agency’s website at https://www.fda.gov or by faxing it to the fax number listed on the Agency’s website at https://www.fda.gov, or by submission through the Agency’s online FOIA submission portal at https://www.fda.gov.
units.action_summary: Requesters must submit FOIA requests in writing via mail, delivery, fax, or the Agency's online FOIA portal at the addresses/numbers provided on FDA's website.

units.obligation_text: All requests must contain the postal address and telephone number of the requester and the name of the person responsible for payment of any fees that may be charged.
units.action_summary: Requesters are required to include their postal address, telephone number, and the name of the person responsible for fee payment in FOIA requests.

units.obligation_text: The Agency may provide for an extension of up to 10 working days by providing written notice to the requester setting out the reasons for the extension and the date by which a determination is expected to be sent.
units.action_summary: FDA may extend time limits up to 10 working days if it provides written notice stating reasons and a new expected determination date.

units.obligation_text: In the written notice, the Agency will inform the requester of the right to contact the Freedom of Information Act Public Liaison and to seek dispute resolution services from the Office of Government Information Services.
units.action_summary: When extending, FDA must inform the requester of their right to contact the FOIA Public Liaison and to seek dispute resolution from OGIS in the written notice.

units.obligation_text: The Agency may contact the requester for clarification about the request or regarding fee assessment.
units.action_summary: FDA may contact requesters for clarifications or fee discussions.

units.obligation_text: The Agency may toll the 20-day period as follows:
units.action_summary: FDA may pause (toll) the 20-day FOIA response period under the following specified conditions.

units.obligation_text: One time while it is awaiting a response from the requester regarding clarification that it has reasonably requested from the requester;
units.action_summary: FDA may toll the 20-day period one time while awaiting a reasonable clarification response from the requester.

units.obligation_text: One or more times while the Agency is awaiting a response from the requester regarding fee assessment.
units.action_summary: FDA may toll the 20-day period one or more times while awaiting the requester's response about fee assessment.

units.obligation_text: If any record is denied, the letter shall state the right of the person requesting such records to appeal any adverse determination to the Deputy Agency Chief Freedom of Information Act Officer, Department of Health and Human Services, in accordance with the provisions of 45 CFR 5.62.
units.action_summary: Denial letters must inform requesters of their right to appeal adverse determinations to the Deputy Agency Chief FOIA Officer (HHS) under 45 CFR 5.62.

units.obligation_text: If a court determines that exceptional circumstances exist, as defined by the Freedom of Information Act, the Agency’s failure to comply with a time limit shall be excused for the length of time provided by the court order.
units.action_summary: If a court finds exceptional circumstances, FDA's failure to meet a time limit is excused for the period ordered by the court.

units.obligation_text: The Director, Division of Freedom of Information, (or Delegatee) will determine whether to grant a request for expedited processing within 10 days of receipt by the Division of Freedom of Information of all information required to make a decision.
units.actor: Director, Division of Freedom of Information (or Delegatee)
units.action_summary: The Director (or delegate) must decide whether to grant expedited processing within 10 days of receiving all required information.

units.obligation_text: If the request is for a commercial use, the Food and Drug Administration will charge for the costs of search, review, and duplication.
units.action_summary: For commercial-use requests, FDA must charge for search, review, and duplication costs.

units.obligation_text: The Agency shall not assess search fees if the Agency fails to comply with any time limit, as described in § 20.41, if no unusual or exceptional circumstances apply to the processing of the request.
units.action_summary: FDA must not charge search fees if it misses the statutory time limits, unless unusual or exceptional circumstances apply.

units.obligation_text: If unusual circumstances, as outlined in § 20.41, apply and more than 5,000 pages are necessary to respond to the request, the Food and Drug Administration may charge search fees if timely written notice has been made to the requester and the Agency has discussed with the requester via written mail, electronic mail, or telephone (or made not less than three good-faith attempts to do so) how the requester could effectively limit the scope of the request.
units.action_summary: If unusual circumstances and >5,000 pages are needed, FDA may charge search fees, but only after timely written notice and discussion (or three good-faith attempts) about narrowing the request.

units.obligation_text: Timely written notice has been made to the requester.
units.action_summary: FDA must provide timely written notice to the requester as a condition to charging search fees under unusual circumstances.

units.obligation_text: The Agency has discussed with the requester via written mail, electronic mail, or telephone (or made not less than three good-faith attempts to do so) how the requester could effectively limit the scope of the request.
units.action_summary: FDA must discuss (or make at least three good-faith attempts) with the requester how to limit the request before charging search fees under unusual circumstances.

units.obligation_text: If the request is from an educational institution or a noncommercial scientific institution ... and the request is not for a commercial use, the Food and Drug Administration will charge only for the duplication of documents.
units.action_summary: For qualifying educational, scientific, or news media requesters (non-commercial), FDA will charge only duplication costs.

units.obligation_text: Also, the Food and Drug Administration will not charge the copying costs for the first 100 pages of duplication (or its cost equivalent of other media).
units.action_summary: FDA will waive copying charges for the first 100 pages (or equivalent) for qualifying non-commercial requesters.

units.obligation_text: The Agency shall not assess duplication fees if the Agency fails to comply with any time limit, as described in § 20.41, if no unusual or exceptional circumstances apply to the processing of the request.
units.action_summary: FDA must not charge duplication fees if it fails to meet time limits, absent unusual or exceptional circumstances.

units.obligation_text: If unusual circumstances, as outlined in § 20.41, apply and more than 5,000 pages are necessary to respond to the request, the Food and Drug Administration may charge duplication fees if timely written notice has been made to the requester and the Agency has discussed with the requester ... how the requester could effectively limit the scope of the request.
units.action_summary: Under unusual circumstances requiring >5,000 pages, FDA may charge duplication fees after timely notice and discussion (or three attempts) about narrowing the request.

units.obligation_text: If the request is not the kind described in paragraph (a)(1) or (2) of this section, then the Food and Drug Administration will charge only for the search and the duplication.
units.action_summary: For other requests, FDA will charge only for search and duplication.

units.obligation_text: Also, the Food and Drug Administration will not charge for the first 2 hours of search time or for the copying costs of the first 100 pages of duplication (or the cost equivalent of other media).
units.action_summary: FDA will waive charges for the first 2 hours of search and first 100 pages of copying for these other requesters.

units.obligation_text: The Agency shall not assess search fees if the Agency fails to comply with any time limit, as described in § 20.41, if no unusual or exceptional circumstances apply to the processing of the request.
units.action_summary: FDA must not assess search fees if it fails to meet time limits, unless unusual or exceptional circumstances apply.

units.obligation_text: If unusual circumstances, as outlined in § 20.41, apply and more than 5,000 pages are necessary to respond to the request, the Food and Drug Administration may charge search fees if timely written notice has been made to the requester and the Agency has discussed with the requester ... how the requester could effectively limit the scope of the request.
units.action_summary: Under unusual circumstances requiring >5,000 pages, FDA may charge search fees after timely notice and discussion (or three good-faith attempts) to limit the request.

units.obligation_text: Requesters may contact Agency Freedom of Information Act staff or the Freedom of Information Act Public Liaison to assist in reformulating a request to meet their needs at lower cost.
units.action_summary: Requesters are permitted to contact FOIA staff or the FOIA Public Liaison for help reformulating requests to reduce cost.

units.obligation_text: When the search or review is performed by employees at grade GS–1 through GS–8 (or equivalent), an hourly rate based on the salary of a GS–5, step 7, employee; when done by a GS–9 through GS–14 (or equivalent), an hourly rate based on the salary of a GS–12, step 4, employee; and when done by a GS–15 or above (or equivalent), an hourly rate based on the salary of a GS–15, step 7, employee.
units.action_summary: Search/review performed by employees will be charged at specified hourly rates corresponding to GS grade bands.

units.obligation_text: In each case, the hourly rate will be computed by taking the current hourly rate for the specified grade and step in the General Schedule Locality Pay Table for the Locality of Washington-Baltimore-Northern Virginia, DC–MD–VA–WV–PA, adding 16 percent of that rate to cover benefits, and rounding to the nearest whole dollar.
units.action_summary: Hourly rates are computed from specified GS salary steps, plus 16% for benefits, rounded to the nearest dollar.

units.obligation_text: When a search involves employees at more than one of these levels, the Food and Drug Administration will charge the rate appropriate for each.
units.action_summary: If multiple employee grade levels are involved, FDA will charge each at the appropriate rate.

units.obligation_text: Charges for the time spent by the operator to search the computer, database or network, including development of any specialized programming required to perform the search, at the rate given in paragraph (c)(1) of this section plus the cost of any materials.
units.action_summary: Charges for electronic searches (including operator time and specialized programming) are billed at the rates in paragraph (c)(1) plus material costs.

units.obligation_text: A denial of a request for records, in whole or in part, shall be signed by the Director, Division of Freedom of Information, or other official who has been delegated the authority to release or withhold records.
units.actor: Director, Division of Freedom of Information or delegated official
units.action_summary: Denials (in whole or part) must be signed by the Director or an authorized delegate.

units.obligation_text: A letter denying a request for records, in whole or in part, shall state the reasons for the denial and shall state that an appeal may be transmitted to the Deputy Agency Chief Freedom of Information Act Officer, Department of Health and Human Services, within 90 calendar days from the date of the adverse determination, in accordance with 45 CFR 5.61.
units.action_summary: Denial letters must state the reasons for denial and inform requesters of the right to appeal to the Deputy Agency Chief FOIA Officer within 90 days under 45 CFR 5.61.

units.obligation_text: The Agency will also make a reasonable effort to include in the letter an estimate of the volume of the records denied, unless providing such an estimate would harm an interest protected by an exemption under the Freedom of Information Act.
units.action_summary: FDA should reasonably attempt to include an estimate of the volume of denied records in denial letters, unless doing so would harm an exempted interest.

units.obligation_text: This estimate will ordinarily be provided in terms of the approximate number of pages or some other reasonable measure.
units.action_summary: The estimate of denied records should normally be expressed as number of pages or another reasonable measure.

units.obligation_text: This estimate will not be provided if the volume of records denied is otherwise indicated through deletions on records disclosed in part.
units.action_summary: FDA need not provide the estimate when the volume is already indicated by deletions on partially disclosed records.

units.obligation_text: The letter will also include contact information for the Freedom of Information Act Public Liaison and the Office of Government Information Services.
units.action_summary: Denial letters must include contact information for the FOIA Public Liaison and OGIS.

units.obligation_text: The submitter has 10 working days from the date of the notice to object to disclosure of any part of the records and to state all bases for its objections.
units.action_summary: The submitter has a 10-working-day deadline to object to disclosure and state all bases for objections.

units.obligation_text: Division of Freedom of Information may extend this period as appropriate and necessary.
units.action_summary: The Division may extend the 10-working-day period when appropriate and necessary.

units.obligation_text: Inter-agency or intra-agency memoranda or letters that would not be available by law to a party other than an Agency in litigation with the Food and Drug Administration may be withheld from public disclosure except that factual information that is reasonably segregable in accordance with the rule established in § 20.22 is available for public disclosure.
units.action_summary: Inter- or intra-agency memoranda not legally available to outside parties may be withheld, but reasonably segregable factual information must be disclosed.

units.obligation_text: The deliberative process privilege shall not apply to records created 25 years or more before the date on which the records were requested.
units.action_summary: The deliberative process privilege cannot be applied to records created 25 or more years before the request date.

units.obligation_text: The Commissioner may, in his or her discretion, disclose part or all of any Food and Drug Administration (FDA) record that is otherwise exempt from disclosure pursuant to subpart D of this part.
units.actor: Commissioner of Food and Drugs (or designee)
units.action_summary: The Commissioner is permitted to disclose exempt FDA records at his/her discretion.

units.obligation_text: As set forth in § 20.20(b) FDA shall make discretionary disclosures of records or information exempt from disclosure under the provisions of this part whenever disclosure would not foreseeably harm an interest protected by an exemption pursuant to this part.
units.action_summary: FDA must make discretionary disclosures of exempt information whenever disclosure would not foreseeably harm an interest protected by an exemption.

units.obligation_text: Specifically, FDA shall exercise its discretion to disclose such records whenever it determines that such disclosure is in the public interest, will promote the objectives of the Freedom of Information Act and the Agency, and is consistent with the rights of individuals to privacy, the property rights of persons in trade secrets, and the need for the Agency to promote frank internal policy deliberations and to pursue its regulatory activities without disruption.
units.action_summary: FDA must disclose exempt records when doing so serves the public interest, FOIA objectives, and is consistent with privacy, trade secret rights, and agency deliberative needs.

units.obligation_text: Any Food and Drug Administration (FDA) record otherwise exempt from public disclosure may be disclosed to other Federal government departments and agencies, except that trade secrets and confidential commercial or financial information prohibited from disclosure by [specified statutes] may be released only as provided by those sections.
units.action_summary: FDA may disclose exempt records to other federal departments/agencies, but trade secrets/confidential info governed by specified statutes may be released only as those statutes permit.

units.obligation_text: Any disclosure under this section shall be pursuant to a written agreement that the record shall not be further disclosed by the other department or Agency except with the written permission of the FDA.
units.actor: FDA and the other department or Agency
units.action_summary: Any disclosure to another federal department/agency must be made under a written agreement preventing further disclosure except with FDA's written permission.

units.obligation_text: The record shall not be further disclosed by the other department or Agency except with the written permission of the FDA.
units.actor: Other department or Agency receiving the record
units.action_summary: The receiving department/agency must not further disclose the record unless FDA gives written permission.

units.obligation_text: Data and information otherwise exempt from public disclosure may be revealed in Food and Drug Administration (FDA) administrative proceedings ... or court proceedings, where data or information are relevant.
units.action_summary: Exempt information may be revealed in FDA administrative or court proceedings when relevant.

units.obligation_text: The FDA will take appropriate measures, or request that appropriate measures be taken, to reduce disclosure to the minimum necessary under the circumstances.
units.action_summary: FDA must take or request measures to limit disclosure to the minimum necessary in proceedings.

units.obligation_text: The Commissioner of Food and Drugs, or any other officer or employee of the Food and Drug Administration whom the Commissioner may designate to act on his or her behalf for the purpose, may authorize the disclosure of confidential commercial information submitted to the Food and Drug Administration, or incorporated into Agency-prepared records, to State and local government officials as part of cooperative law enforcement or regulatory efforts, provided that:
units.action_summary: The Commissioner (or designee) may authorize disclosure of confidential commercial information to State/local officials for cooperative law enforcement or regulatory efforts, subject to conditions.

units.obligation_text: The State or local government agency has provided both a written statement establishing its authority to protect confidential commercial information from public disclosure and a written commitment not to disclose any such information provided without the written permission of the sponsor or written confirmation by the Food and Drug Administration that the information no longer has confidential status;
units.action_summary: The State/local agency must provide a written statement of authority to protect confidential info and a written commitment not to disclose it without sponsor permission or FDA confirmation.

units.obligation_text: Disclosure would be in the interest of public health by reason of the State or local government’s possessing information concerning the safety, effectiveness, or quality of a product or information concerning an investigation, or by reason of the State or local government being able to exercise its regulatory authority more expeditiously than the Food and Drug Administration;
units.action_summary: Disclosure is authorized if it would serve public health because the State/local government has pertinent information or can act more quickly to exercise regulatory authority.

units.obligation_text: Subject to all the foregoing conditions, a visiting State or local government scientist may have access to trade secret information, entitled to protection under section 301(j) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, in those cases where such disclosures would be a necessary part of the joint review or training.
units.actor: Visiting State or local government scientist
units.action_summary: A visiting State/local scientist may access trade secret information when necessary for joint review or training, subject to preceding conditions.

units.obligation_text: The review is in the interest of public health.
units.action_summary: The joint review must be in the interest of public health as a condition for visitor access to trade secrets.

units.obligation_text: The Food and Drug Administration retains physical control over the information.
units.action_summary: FDA must retain physical control over the information as a condition for visitor access.

units.obligation_text: The Food and Drug Administration requires the visiting State or local government scientist to sign a written commitment to protect the confidentiality of the information.
units.action_summary: FDA requires the visiting scientist to sign a written commitment to protect confidentiality.

units.obligation_text: The visiting State or local government scientist provides a written assurance that he or she has no financial interest in the regulated industry of the type that would preclude participation in the review of the matter if the individual were subject to the conflict of interest rules applicable to the Food and Drug Administration advisory committee members under § 14.80(b)(1) of this chapter.
units.actor: Visiting State or local government scientist
units.action_summary: The visiting scientist must provide a written assurance of no disqualifying financial interest as specified.

units.obligation_text: Except as provided under paragraph (d)(1)(ii)(C) of this section, this provision does not authorize the disclosure to State and local government officials of trade secret information concerning manufacturing methods and processes prohibited from disclosure by section 301(j) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, unless pursuant to an express written authorization provided by the submitter of the information.
units.action_summary: The rule does not authorize disclosure of manufacturing-method trade secrets to State/local officials, except with the submitter's express written authorization (or as provided in (d)(1)(ii)(C)).

units.obligation_text: Unless pursuant to an express written authorization provided by the submitter of the information.
units.action_summary: Disclosure of certain manufacturing trade secrets to State/local officials is permitted only if the submitter provides express written authorization.

units.obligation_text: The Commissioner of Food and Drugs, or any other officer or employee of the Food and Drug Administration whom the Commissioner may designate to act on his or her behalf for the purpose, may authorize the disclosure to, or receipt from, an official of a State or local government agency of nonpublic, predecisional documents concerning the Food and Drug Administration’s or the other government agency’s regulations or other regulatory requirements, or other nonpublic information relevant to either agency’s activities, as part of efforts to improve Federal-State and/or Federal-local uniformity, cooperative regulatory activities, or implementation of Federal-State and/or Federal-local agreements, provided that:
units.action_summary: The Commissioner may authorize exchanges of nonpublic predecisional documents with State/local officials to improve regulatory uniformity or cooperation, subject to conditions.

units.obligation_text: The State or local government agency has the authority to protect such nonpublic documents from public disclosure and will not disclose any such documents provided without the written confirmation by the Food and Drug Administration that the documents no longer have nonpublic status;
units.action_summary: The State/local agency must have authority to protect nonpublic documents and must not disclose them without FDA's written confirmation that they are no longer nonpublic.

units.obligation_text: The Commissioner or his or her designee makes the determination that the exchange is reasonably necessary to improve Federal-State and/or Federal-local uniformity, cooperative regulatory activities, or implementation of Federal-State and/or Federal-local agreements.
units.action_summary: The Commissioner/designee must determine that the exchange is reasonably necessary to improve Federal-State/local uniformity or cooperative regulatory activities.

units.obligation_text: For such officials, the statement and commitment required by paragraph (e)(1)(i) of this section shall be provided by both the organization and the individual.
units.action_summary: Both the organization and the individual must provide the authority statement and non-disclosure commitment described in paragraph (e)(1)(i).

units.obligation_text: The Commissioner of Food and Drugs, or any other officer or employee of the Food and Drug Administration whom the Commissioner may designate to act on his or her behalf for the purpose, may authorize the disclosure to, or receipt from, an official of a foreign government agency of nonpublic, predecisional documents concerning the Food and Drug Administration’s or the other government agency’s regulations or other regulatory requirements, or other nonpublic information relevant to either agency’s activities, as part of cooperative efforts to facilitate global harmonization of regulatory requirements, cooperative regulatory activities, or implementation of international agreements, provided that:
units.action_summary: The Commissioner may authorize exchanges of nonpublic predecisional documents with foreign government officials for global harmonization or cooperative regulatory activities, subject to conditions.

units.obligation_text: The foreign government agency has the authority to protect such nonpublic documents from public disclosure and will not disclose any such documents provided without the written confirmation by the Food and Drug Administration that the documents no longer have nonpublic status;
units.action_summary: The foreign government agency must have authority to protect nonpublic documents and must not disclose them without FDA written confirmation.

units.obligation_text: The Commissioner or his or her designee makes the determination that the exchange is reasonably necessary to facilitate global harmonization of regulatory requirements, cooperative regulatory activities, or implementation of international agreements.
units.action_summary: The Commissioner/designee must determine that the exchange is reasonably necessary to facilitate global harmonization, cooperation, or implementation of international agreements.

units.obligation_text: Any exchange under this section of nonpublic documents does not invoke the rule established in § 20.21 that such records shall be made available to all members of the public.
units.action_summary: Exchanging nonpublic documents under this section does not require making those records available to the public under § 20.21.

units.obligation_text: Both public reading rooms are open from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m., Monday through Friday, excluding legal public holidays.
units.actor: Freedom of Information Staff and Dockets Management Staff Public Reading Rooms / FDA (operating reading rooms)
units.action_summary: The public reading rooms must be open to the public from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m., Monday–Friday, excluding legal public holidays.

units.obligation_text: If, after receiving all of the data that are necessary to make a determination about whether the identity of an ingredient is a trade secret, FDA tentatively decides to deny the request, the Agency will inform the person requesting trade secrecy of its tentative determination in writing.
units.action_summary: If FDA tentatively denies a trade secret claim after receiving necessary data, FDA must notify the requester in writing of the tentative denial.

units.obligation_text: FDA will set forth the grounds upon which it relied in making this tentative determination.
units.action_summary: FDA must state the grounds supporting its tentative denial determination.

units.obligation_text: The petitioner may submit, within 60 days from the date of receipt of the written notice of the tentative denial, additional relevant information and arguments and request that the Agency reconsider its decision in light of both the additional material and the information that it originally submitted.
units.action_summary: The petitioner is permitted to submit additional information and request reconsideration within 60 days of receiving the tentative denial notice.

units.obligation_text: If suit is brought within 30 calendar days after such a determination, FDA will not disclose the records involved or require that the disputed ingredient or ingredients be disclosed in labeling until the matter is finally determined in the courts.
units.action_summary: If the affected party sues within 30 days of a final determination that an ingredient is not a trade secret, FDA must not disclose the records or require ingredient disclosure in labeling until final court determination.

units.obligation_text: If suit is not brought within 30 calendar days after a final determination that an ingredient is not a trade secret within the meaning of § 20.61 of this chapter, the records involved will be available for public disclosure in accordance with part 20 of this chapter.
units.action_summary: If no suit is filed within 30 days of a final determination that an ingredient is not a trade secret, the records will be made available to the public under part 20.

title: Institutional Review Board Waiver or Alteration of Informed Consent for Minimal Risk Clinical Investigations

units.obligation_text: Except as provided in §§ 50.22, 50.23, and 50.24, no investigator may involve a human being as a subject in research covered by these regulations unless the investigator has obtained the legally effective informed consent of the subject or the subject’s legally authorized representative.
units.action_summary: Investigators are prohibited from involving human subjects in covered research unless legally effective informed consent is obtained from the subject or the subject's legally authorized representative.

units.obligation_text: the investigator has obtained the legally effective informed consent of the subject or the subject’s legally authorized representative.
units.action_summary: Investigator must obtain legally effective informed consent from the subject or the subject's legally authorized representative.

units.obligation_text: The IRB responsible for the review, approval, and continuing review of the clinical investigation described in this section may approve an informed consent procedure that does not include or that alters some or all of the elements of informed consent set forth in § 50.25(a) and (b), or that waives the requirement to obtain informed consent, provided the IRB finds and documents the following:
units.actor: the IRB responsible for the review, approval, and continuing review of the clinical investigation described in this section
units.action_summary: The IRB may approve an altered or waived informed consent procedure for the described clinical investigation if it finds and documents the specified conditions.

units.obligation_text: The clinical investigation involves no more than minimal risk to the subjects;
units.action_summary: IRB must find and document that the clinical investigation involves no more than minimal risk to subjects.

units.obligation_text: The waiver or alteration will not adversely affect the rights and welfare of the subjects;
units.action_summary: IRB must find and document that the waiver or alteration will not adversely affect subjects' rights and welfare.

units.obligation_text: The clinical investigation could not practicably be carried out without the waiver or alteration;
units.action_summary: IRB must find and document that the clinical investigation could not practicably be carried out without the waiver or alteration.

units.obligation_text: Whenever appropriate, the subjects will be provided with additional pertinent information after participation.
units.action_summary: IRB must find and document that, when appropriate, subjects will be provided additional pertinent information after participation.

units.obligation_text: An investigator is responsible for ensuring that an investigation is conducted according to the signed investigator statement, the investigational plan, and applicable regulations;
units.action_summary: Investigator must ensure the investigation is conducted according to the signed investigator statement, investigational plan, and applicable regulations.

units.obligation_text: for protecting the rights, safety, and welfare of subjects under the investigator’s care;
units.action_summary: Investigator must protect the rights, safety, and welfare of subjects under their care.

units.obligation_text: and for the control of drugs under investigation.
units.action_summary: Investigator must maintain control of drugs under investigation.

units.obligation_text: An investigator shall obtain the informed consent of each human subject to whom the drug is administered, in accordance with part 50 of this chapter.
units.action_summary: Investigator must obtain informed consent from each human subject administered the drug, in accordance with part 50.

units.obligation_text: Ensures that each investigator participating in an investigation of the device obtains from each subject under the investigator’s care, informed consent in accordance with part 50 of this chapter.
units.action_summary: Sponsor must ensure each investigator obtains informed consent from each subject under the investigator's care, in accordance with part 50.

units.obligation_text: A person who applies for the knowledge test for an airline transport pilot certificate with an airplane category multiengine class rating must present a graduation certificate from an authorized training provider under part 121, 135, 141, or 142 of this chapter certifying the applicant has completed the following training in a course approved by the Administrator.
units.actor: a person who applies for the knowledge test (applicant)
units.action_summary: Present a graduation certificate from an authorized training provider certifying completion of the required training in a course approved by the Administrator.

units.obligation_text: Except for a person who has been removed from flying status for lack of proficiency or because of a disciplinary action involving aircraft operations, a U.S. military pilot or former U.S. military pilot may apply for an airline transport pilot certificate with an airplane category multiengine class rating or an airline transport pilot certificate concurrently with a multiengine airplane type rating with a minimum of 750 hours of total time as a pilot if the pilot presents:
units.actor: a U.S. military pilot or former U.S. military pilot
units.action_summary: May apply for an ATP certificate with multiengine class/type rating with at least 750 hours if the pilot presents the required documentation.

units.obligation_text: A person may apply for an airline transport pilot certificate with an airplane category multiengine class rating or an airline transport pilot certificate concurrently with a multiengine airplane type rating with a minimum of 1,000 hours of total time as a pilot if the person:
units.action_summary: May apply for an ATP certificate with multiengine class/type rating with at least 1,000 hours if the person meets the specified conditions.

units.obligation_text: A person may apply for an airline transport pilot certificate with an airplane category multiengine class rating or an airline transport pilot certificate concurrently with a multiengine airplane type rating with a minimum of 1,250 hours of total time as a pilot if the person:
units.action_summary: May apply for an ATP certificate with multiengine class/type rating with at least 1,250 hours if the person meets the specified conditions.

units.obligation_text: A graduate of an institution of higher education who completes fewer than 60 semester credit hours but at least 30 credit hours and otherwise satisfies the requirements of paragraph (b) may apply for airline transport pilot certificate with an airplane category multiengine class rating or an airline transport pilot certificate concurrently with a multiengine airplane type rating with a minimum of 1,250 hours of total time as a pilot.
units.actor: a graduate of an institution of higher education who completes fewer than 60 but at least 30 semester credit hours and otherwise satisfies paragraph (b)
units.action_summary: May apply for an ATP certificate with multiengine class/type rating with at least 1,250 hours if the graduate meets the credit and paragraph (b) requirements.

units.obligation_text: Successfully complete the airline transport pilot certification training program specified in § 61.156;
units.actor: a person seeking the additional aircraft category or class rating (applicant)
units.action_summary: Complete the airline transport pilot certification training program specified in §61.156.

units.obligation_text: A person applying to add a multiengine class rating, or a multiengine class rating concurrently with a multiengine airplane type rating, to an airline transport pilot certificate with an airplane category single engine class rating must—
units.actor: a person applying to add a multiengine class rating (applicant)
units.action_summary: Must satisfy the listed requirements to add a multiengine class rating (or concurrently a multiengine airplane type rating) to an ATP certificate that has a single-engine class rating.

units.obligation_text: Pass a required knowledge test on the aeronautical knowledge areas of § 61.155(c), as applicable to multiengine airplanes;
units.actor: a person applying to add a multiengine class rating (applicant)
units.action_summary: Pass the required knowledge test covering the aeronautical knowledge areas of §61.155(c) relevant to multiengine airplanes.

title: Medical Devices: Classification of Accessories Distinct from Other Devices; Proposed List of Accessories Suitable for Class I; Request for Comments

units.obligation_text: Subject to the exceptions identified in § 820.30(a)(2) for specific devices and those automated with computer software, design controls under § 820.30 do not generally apply to a class I device.
units.actor: class I devices / manufacturers of class I devices
units.action_summary: Design controls in § 820.30 generally do not apply to class I devices.

units.obligation_text: The classification of each accessory will be based on the risks of the accessory when used as intended and the level of regulatory controls necessary to provide a reasonable assurance of safety and effectiveness of the accessory, notwithstanding the classification of any other device with which such accessory is intended to be used (see section 513(f)(6)(A) of the FD&C Act).
units.action_summary: FDA will base classification of each accessory on its risks and the regulatory controls needed to assure safety and effectiveness.

units.obligation_text: In general, we considered an accessory to be eligible for classification into class I distinct from another device if the accessory: (1) Is not for use in supporting or sustaining human life, or of substantial importance in preventing impairment to human health; (2) does not represent a potential unreasonable risk of illness or injury; and (3) general controls alone would be sufficient to provide a reasonable assurance of safety and effectiveness of the accessory.
units.action_summary: An accessory is eligible for distinct class I classification only if it meets the listed criteria regarding life-support, risk, and sufficiency of general controls.
units.modal_raw: is considered to be eligible if

units.obligation_text: (1) Is not for use in supporting or sustaining human life, or of substantial importance in preventing impairment to human health.
units.action_summary: To be eligible, the accessory must not be for use in supporting/sustaining human life or of substantial importance in preventing impairment to health.

units.obligation_text: (2) does not represent a potential unreasonable risk of illness or injury.
units.action_summary: To be eligible, the accessory must not present a potential unreasonable risk of illness or injury.

units.obligation_text: (3) general controls alone would be sufficient to provide a reasonable assurance of safety and effectiveness of the accessory.
units.action_summary: To be eligible, general controls alone must be sufficient to assure the accessory's safety and effectiveness.

units.obligation_text: By regulation, design controls apply to class I devices only if the devices are automated with computer software or are listed under § 820.30(a)(2)(ii).
units.action_summary: Design controls for class I devices apply only when the device is automated with software or listed under § 820.30(a)(2)(ii).

units.obligation_text: If an accessory is not automated with computer software but would require design controls to provide reasonable assurance of safety and effectiveness, we did not consider it eligible for classification through the final action based on this document.
units.action_summary: Accessories that are not automated but would nonetheless require design controls are not eligible for classification via this final action.

units.obligation_text: You may wish to propose additional accessories as suitable for distinct classification into class I using the factors described above where the accessories are otherwise eligible for classification under section 513(f)(6)(D)(i) of the FD&C Act.
units.action_summary: Commenters are permitted to propose additional accessories for distinct class I classification using the listed factors.

units.obligation_text: Should you wish to propose additional accessories, your comment should briefly explain why you think general controls alone will provide reasonable assurance of safety and effectiveness.
units.action_summary: If proposing additional accessories, the commenter should briefly explain why general controls alone are sufficient.

units.obligation_text: Should you disagree with any of the proposed accessories for class I, your comments should briefly explain why additional regulatory controls, such as premarket review through a 510(k) submission or premarket approval (PMA), are necessary to provide reasonable assurance of safety and effectiveness.
units.action_summary: If disagreeing with proposed accessories, commenters should explain why additional regulatory controls (e.g., 510(k), PMA) are necessary.

units.section: III. Policy Clarification for Classification of Certain Accessories Used in Orthopedic Surgery; § 888.4540
units.obligation_text: Orthopedic manual surgical instruments are classified in § 888.4540 ... These devices are class I, subject to general controls, and exempt from premarket notification procedures, subject to the limitations of exemptions in 21 CFR 888.9.
units.actor: orthopedic manual surgical instruments / their manufacturers
units.action_summary: Orthopedic manual surgical instruments in § 888.4540 are class I, must comply with general controls, and are exempt from premarket notification procedures subject to exemption limits.
units.modal_raw: are; are subject to; exempt from

units.section: III. Policy Clarification for Classification of Certain Accessories Used in Orthopedic Surgery
units.obligation_text: Instruments that are 'device-specific,' or designed for use with a specific parent device/system and thus are accessories, have historically been reviewed in the same premarket submission as the parent device.
units.action_summary: Device-specific orthopedic instruments have historically been reviewed together with the parent device in a single premarket submission.

units.section: III. Policy Clarification for Classification of Certain Accessories Used in Orthopedic Surgery
units.obligation_text: For example, certain device-specific instruments are accessories and require precise technical specifications or design characteristics to function as intended to support, supplement or augment the parent device...
units.action_summary: Device-specific instruments must have precise technical specifications or design characteristics to function properly with the parent device.

units.section: III. Policy Clarification for Classification of Certain Accessories Used in Orthopedic Surgery
units.obligation_text: Class I orthopedic manual surgical instruments do not require such controls.
units.actor: class I orthopedic manual surgical instruments / manufacturers
units.action_summary: Class I orthopedic manual surgical instruments are not required to have the design controls discussed for device-specific accessories.

units.section: III. Policy Clarification for Classification of Certain Accessories Used in Orthopedic Surgery
units.obligation_text: It is often necessary for orthopedic instruments to be described in a premarket submission (e.g., 510(k), PMA) to evaluate that the parent device functions as intended.
units.action_summary: Manufacturers often need to describe orthopedic instruments in premarket submissions to allow evaluation of the parent device's intended function.

units.section: III. Policy Clarification for Classification of Certain Accessories Used in Orthopedic Surgery
units.obligation_text: Such orthopedic instruments may be appropriately classified in an existing class I regulation (§ 888.4540) if they do not meet the definition of a device-specific orthopedic accessory above and their risk profile and necessary regulatory controls are commensurate with that of orthopedic manual surgical instruments.
units.action_summary: Orthopedic instruments that are not device-specific and whose risks and controls align with manual instruments may be classified under § 888.4540.

units.section: III. Policy Clarification for Classification of Certain Accessories Used in Orthopedic Surgery
units.obligation_text: If they do meet the definition of a device-specific orthopedic accessory above, then such orthopedic accessories may still be eligible for classification under section 513(f)(6)(D)(ii) of the FD&C Act.
units.action_summary: Device-specific orthopedic accessories may be eligible for classification under section 513(f)(6)(D)(ii) if they meet the definition.

units.section: IV. Proposed List of Accessories That May Be Suitable for Distinct Classification Into Class I
units.obligation_text: We are proposing the following accessories ... as suitable for distinct classification into class I.
units.action_summary: FDA proposes that the listed accessories are suitable for distinct classification into class I.

units.section: IV. Proposed List of Accessories That May Be Suitable for Distinct Classification Into Class I
units.obligation_text: When we publish the final list of accessories based on this list and the factors in section II, we will consider those accessories classified into class I, distinct from other devices, through such action.
units.action_summary: Upon publishing the final list, FDA will classify the listed accessories into class I, distinct from other devices.

units.section: IV. Proposed List of Accessories That May Be Suitable for Distinct Classification Into Class I
units.obligation_text: We would place each of these accessories in 21 CFR part 876, 878, or 886, as appropriate.
units.action_summary: FDA would assign each accessory to the appropriate part of 21 CFR (876, 878, or 886).

units.section: IV. Proposed List of Accessories That May Be Suitable for Distinct Classification Into Class I; 21 CFR part 807
units.obligation_text: Each of these accessories would be class I, exempt from the premarket notification procedures in 21 CFR part 807, subject to the applicable limitations of exemption (i.e., 21 CFR 876.9, 878.9, or 886.9).
units.action_summary: The listed accessories would be classified as class I and exempt from premarket notification procedures, subject to exemption limitations.

units.section: IV. Proposed List of Accessories That May Be Suitable for Distinct Classification Into Class I
units.obligation_text: We intend to make conforming changes to existing classification regulations as appropriate.
units.action_summary: FDA intends to update existing classification regulations to conform with these changes.

units.action_summary: Comments submitted by October 16, 2018 will be accepted.

units.action_summary: Commenters may submit comments via the eRulemaking portal or by mail.

units.obligation_text: All submissions received must include the agency name and docket number or RIN for this Federal Register document.
units.action_summary: All submitted comments must include the agency name and docket number or RIN.

units.actor: Department of Defense / agency processing submissions
units.action_summary: The agency will make public submissions available online as received, including personal identifiers.
