units.action_summary: If implemented, beneficiaries enrolled in ECHO would be permitted to receive up to 16 hours of respite care per month regardless of other ECHO benefits.

title:
Nonclinical Laboratory Studies Proposed Regulations for Good Laboratory
Practice Regulations

units.obligation_text: Each person engaged in or responsible for supervising the conduct of a nonclinical laboratory study have the education, training, and experience, or combination thereof, to perform the assigned functions.
units.actor: each person engaged in or responsible for supervising the conduct of a nonclinical laboratory study
units.action_summary: Those engaged in or supervising nonclinical laboratory studies must possess appropriate education, training, and/or experience to perform their assigned functions.

units.obligation_text: The testing facility to maintain a curriculum vitae and job description for each person engaged in or responsible for supervising the conduct of a nonclinical laboratory study.
units.action_summary: Testing facilities must keep a CV and job description for each person engaged in or supervising nonclinical studies.

units.obligation_text: A sufficient number of personnel is to be available to ensure timely and proper performance of activities specified by the protocol.
units.action_summary: Testing facilities must have enough personnel to perform protocol activities timely and properly.

units.obligation_text: Personnel to practice good sanitation and health habits, wear clothing appropriate for the duties they perform, and change such clothing as often as necessary.
units.action_summary: Personnel must maintain sanitation and health habits and wear and change appropriate clothing as necessary.

units.obligation_text: Each nonclinical laboratory study shall have a study director who is a scientist or other professional person of appropriate education, training, and experience or combination thereof and who is responsible for the overall conduct of the study.
units.action_summary: Every nonclinical study must have a qualified study director responsible for overall conduct.

units.obligation_text: The study director is responsible for assuring that the approved protocol is followed; test substances are characterized; test systems are appropriate for the study; personnel involved in the study clearly understand their functions and are qualified to perform them; data are accurately and promptly verified and recorded; health hazards to the test system which appear during the study are recognized and removed; good laboratory practices are followed; the studies are conducted in a manner that is safe for laboratory personnel; and the required data have been transmitted to the archives for storage.
units.action_summary: The study director must ensure protocol adherence, substance characterization, appropriate test systems, qualified personnel, accurate/ prompt data verification and recording, recognition/removal of health hazards, GLP compliance, safety, and archive transmission of required data.

units.obligation_text: Establishment of a quality assurance unit within the testing facility that is charged with the responsibility for assuring that the facilities, equipment, personnel, methods, practices, procedures, records, and controls are designed and function in conformance with good laboratory practice regulations and the protocols for individual nonclinical laboratory studies.
units.action_summary: Testing facilities must establish a quality assurance unit responsible for assuring that facilities, equipment, personnel, methods, procedures, records, and controls conform with GLP and study protocols.

units.obligation_text: The quality assurance unit would be required to inspect periodically each phase of a study and to document the inspection.
units.action_summary: The QA unit must perform periodic inspections of each study phase and document those inspections.

units.obligation_text: Written reports giving the status of each study, the problems noted, and the actions taken to resolve the problems would be required to be submitted to management periodically.
units.action_summary: The QA unit must periodically submit written status reports to management detailing problems and corrective actions.

units.obligation_text: For any study lasting more than 6 months, the quality assurance unit is required to perform an in-depth evaluation of the study to detect, at an early stage, errors in recording data, and unusual patterns of events, lack of conformity to the protocol, and deviations from good laboratory practice and standard operating procedures.
units.action_summary: For studies over six months, the QA unit must perform an in-depth evaluation to detect early errors, unusual patterns, protocol nonconformity, and GLP/SOP deviations.

units.obligation_text: A master schedule sheet of all studies conducted at a testing facility must be maintained showing the current status of each study.
units.action_summary: Testing facilities must maintain a master schedule of all studies showing each study's current status.

units.obligation_text: All records required to be maintained by the quality assurance unit are to be made available for inspection to authorized FDA employees.
units.action_summary: Records the QA unit maintains must be made available for inspection by authorized FDA employees.

units.obligation_text: Provides for the availability of a scientist or other professional to respond to requests from technicians or less experienced personnel for assistance or consultation.
units.action_summary: Testing facilities must ensure a qualified scientist or professional is available to provide assistance or consultation to technicians or less experienced personnel.

units.obligation_text: The proposed regulations require separate areas for the (1) receipt and quarantine of animals, (2) housing and care of animals, (3) storage of feed, bedding, supplies, and equipment, (4) receipt, storage, and mixing of the test substance, (5) laboratory testing operations, (6) cleaning, sterilizing, and maintaining of laboratory equipment, (7) specimen and data storage, and (8) administration and personnel.
units.action_summary: Testing facilities must provide separate areas for animal quarantine, housing, storage, test substance handling, lab operations, equipment maintenance, specimen/data storage, and administration.

units.obligation_text: Environmental control of animal rooms or areas be in compliance with the Animal Welfare Act of 1970 as set forth in 9 CFR Part 3; where specifications regarding housing of certain species are not set forth by that act, the recommendations contained in HEW Publication No. (NIH) 74-23 are to be used.
units.action_summary: Animal room environmental controls must comply with the Animal Welfare Act; where the Act is silent, NIH Guide recommendations must be used.
units.modal_raw: be in compliance / are to be used

units.obligation_text: Separate areas are to be provided for (1) effective isolation of animals either known or suspected of being diseased, or of being disease carriers, from animals that are in good health and (2) for isolation of studies being done with test substances known to be infectious to both man and animals to protect personnel and to prevent cross-infection.
units.action_summary: Testing facilities must provide separate isolation areas for diseased/suspect animals and for studies involving infectious substances to protect personnel and prevent cross-infection.

units.obligation_text: Animals be separated by species when necessary, e.g., to protect against interspecies transmission of infectious diseases.
units.action_summary: Testing facilities must separate animals by species when necessary to prevent interspecies disease transmission.

units.obligation_text: Storage areas for feed and bedding be separated from areas housing the test systems and that the storage area be protected against infestation or contamination.
units.action_summary: Feed and bedding storage must be separate from test system housing and protected against infestation or contamination.

units.obligation_text: To prevent contamination or mixups of test and control substances there shall be separate or defined areas for: (1) the receipt and storage of the test and control substances, (2) mixing of those substances with a carrier, and (3) the storage of the test and/or control substance mixtures; storage areas ... are to be separated from test system housing areas and are to be adequate to maintain the identity, strength, quality, purity, and stability of the substances and mixtures.
units.action_summary: Testing facilities must have separate/defined areas for receipt, storage, mixing, and storage of mixtures of test/control substances, separated from housing and adequate to maintain identity, strength, quality, purity, and stability.

units.obligation_text: Require specialized areas for performing activities such as aseptic surgery, intensive care, necropsy, histology and radiography, and special areas for the use of radioactive and biohazardous materials, volatile agents, and hazardous aerosols to protect personnel and test systems from unnecessary radiation exposure, contamination, or infection.
units.action_summary: Testing facilities must provide specialized areas for certain procedures and separate areas for radioactive/biohazardous/volatile/hazardous aerosol work to protect personnel and test systems.

units.obligation_text: Requires space, limited to access by authorized personnel only, for the storage and retrieval of all raw data and specimens.
units.action_summary: Testing facilities must provide secure space (authorized access only) for storage and retrieval of raw data and specimens.

units.obligation_text: Requires space in the testing facility for administrative, supervisory, and directional functions; space for washing and toilet facilities is also required.
units.action_summary: Testing facilities must provide space for administration/supervision and for washing/toilet facilities.

units.obligation_text: Sets forth requirements for the design, and describes the required cleaning, maintenance, and calibration of the equipment in a testing facility; specifies the records of such activities which are required to be kept; written standard operating procedures are required assigning responsibility for cleaning, maintaining, inspecting, and testing equipment; periodic calibration of automatic, mechanical, and electronic equipment is required.
units.actor: testing facility / personnel responsible for equipment
units.action_summary: Testing facilities must design equipment properly, implement cleaning/maintenance/calibration, keep records, have SOPs assigning responsibilities, and perform periodic calibrations.

units.obligation_text: Requires written standard operating procedures setting forth in detail the methods for performing the various laboratory operations; such written standard operating procedures shall include methods for all sampling, testing, or other laboratory control mechanisms as well as for preparing and maintaining any records and reports required by these regulations.
units.action_summary: Testing facilities must have detailed written SOPs for lab operations, sampling, testing, control mechanisms, and records/reports preparation and maintenance.

units.obligation_text: Deviations from these operating procedures for a given study must be properly authorized by the study director.
units.action_summary: Any deviations from SOPs for a study must be authorized by the study director.

units.obligation_text: Significant changes to the testing facility's standard operating procedures must be authorized by management.
units.action_summary: Management must authorize significant changes to facility SOPs.

units.obligation_text: Describes procedures for handling reagents and solutions to assure their proper and reliable use.
units.action_summary: Facilities must follow specified procedures for handling reagents and solutions to ensure proper and reliable use.

units.obligation_text: Sets forth the requirements for the care and handling of animals used as the test systems in a nonclinical laboratory study; requirements regarding housing, feeding, and handling are to be consistent with existing standards.
units.action_summary: Testing facilities must meet specified animal care and handling requirements consistent with existing standards for housing, feeding, and handling.

units.obligation_text: All newly received animals must be placed in quarantine until their health status has been evaluated in accordance with acceptable veterinary medical practice.
units.action_summary: Newly received animals must be quarantined until evaluated per veterinary practice.

units.obligation_text: Sets forth requirements for the unique individual identification of animals either in accordance with the Animal Welfare Act, or for species not required to be so identified by that act, identification by a number that identifies the shipment or purchase order number on receipt of the animal; a unique permanently attached identification number ... would be required for animals that are moved from one cage to another during a study or if such animals are used in laboratory procedures that require manipulations and observations over extended periods of time.
units.action_summary: Animals must have unique identification per Animal Welfare Act or shipment/purchase number; permanent ID is required if animals are moved between cages or used in long-term procedures.

units.obligation_text: Animals should not be moved to a new location or placed under different environmental conditions during a study without written permission from the study director.
units.action_summary: Animals must not be moved or have environmental conditions changed during a study without the study director's written permission.

units.obligation_text: Sets forth requirements for the periodic analyses of the feed and drinking water used for animals to ensure that known interfering contaminants are not present at a level above predetermined specifications.
units.action_summary: Testing facilities must periodically analyze animal feed and water to ensure contaminants do not exceed preset specifications.

units.obligation_text: Sets forth the procedures to be followed regarding the identification and testing of test and control substances.
units.actor: testing facility / study director / laboratory personnel
units.action_summary: Testing facilities must follow specified procedures for identification and testing of test and control substances.

units.obligation_text: Describes requirements for the handling of these substances in general, and for the handling of carcinogenic substances.
units.action_summary: Facilities must follow specified handling requirements for test/control substances, including special requirements for carcinogens.

units.obligation_text: The uniformity and concentration of the substances in the diet mix must be determined before the start of the study; random samples of each batch of the test or control substance mixture should be analyzed periodically during the course of the study to ensure that the proper mixing and formulation procedures are being used.
units.action_summary: Determine diet mix uniformity and concentration before study start and periodically analyze random batch samples during the study to ensure correct mixing/formulation.

units.obligation_text: Each nonclinical laboratory study have a written protocol that clearly indicates the objectives and procedures for the conduct of the study and sets forth the minimum information to be contained in such a protocol; changes or revisions to an approved protocol are to be documented, dated, and signed by the study director.
units.action_summary: Each study must have a written protocol with objectives/procedures and minimum required information; any changes must be documented, dated, and signed by the study director.

units.obligation_text: Test systems shall be monitored in conformity with the protocol; moribund animals should either be sacrificed or placed in isolation and observed carefully at least twice daily; if an animal is found dead outside normal working hours and a qualified person is not available to perform necropsy, then the carcass should be immediately preserved at 2°–8° C and necropsied on the next day; qualified personnel should be available to monitor and necropsy moribund and/or dead animals on weekends or holidays.
units.actor: testing facility / study personnel / qualified personnel
units.action_summary: Monitor test systems per protocol; manage moribund animals per protocol (sacrifice or isolate and observe twice daily); preserve carcasses if necropsy cannot be performed immediately; ensure qualified personnel are available, including weekends/holidays.

units.obligation_text: Sets forth the manner in which specimens are to be identified.
units.action_summary: Specimens must be identified in the specified manner to minimize misassignment.

units.obligation_text: Records of post-mortem observations be available to a pathologist when examining a specimen histopathologically.
units.action_summary: Post-mortem observation records must be available to the pathologist examining specimens histopathologically.

units.obligation_text: All data generated during the conduct of a nonclinical laboratory study, except those that are generated as direct computer input, are to be recorded directly, promptly, and accurately in ink in bound books with prenumbered pages or on worksheets that are to be bound during or at the conclusion of the study; all data entries are to be dated on the day of entry and signed, or identified in the case of direct computer input, by the person generating the data; any changes in an entry are to be made in such a manner so as not to obscure the original entry, the reason for such change must be indicated, and the change shall be dated and signed, or identified in the case of direct computer input, by the person making the change.
units.action_summary: Record non-computer data promptly and accurately in ink in bound, prenumbered records or bound worksheets; date and sign entries; make changes without obscuring originals, indicate reasons, and date/sign the changes.
units.modal_raw: are to be / are to be dated / are to be made

units.obligation_text: All recorded data be reviewed, signed, and dated by a person, other than the person entering the data, responsible for the performance and evaluation of the activity from which the data were derived to assure adherence to procedures.
units.actor: a person other than the data enterer (responsible for performance/evaluation)
units.action_summary: Recorded data must be reviewed, signed, and dated by someone other than the data entry person who is responsible for the activity, to ensure procedures were followed.

units.obligation_text: Sets forth information that must be included in a final nonclinical laboratory study report; the final report would have to be signed and dated by the study director and each segment signed and dated by the responsible scientist or other professional person.
units.actor: study director / responsible scientists and other professional persons
units.action_summary: Final study reports must include specified information and be signed/dated by the study director, with each segment signed/dated by the responsible scientist or professional.

units.obligation_text: Corrections or additions to a final report be in the form of an amendment by the study director clearly identifying that part of the report that is being added to or corrected and the reasons for the correction or addition; the amendment is to be signed by the person responsible for the correction or addition and dated.
units.actor: study director / person responsible for correction or addition
units.action_summary: Corrections/additions to final reports must be submitted as amendments by the study director identifying the change and reasons; the responsible person must sign and date the amendment.
units.modal_raw: be in the form / is to be signed

title: Nonclinical Laboratory Studies, Proposed Regulations for Good Laboratory Practice; Correction

units.obligation_text: The identity, strength, quality, and purity of each batch of a test or control substance shall be determined and documented by the testing facility before the initiation of the study, unless this determination with verifying documentation has been done by the sponsor.
units.action_summary: The testing facility must determine and document identity, strength, quality, and purity of each batch of a test or control substance before the study starts.

units.obligation_text: unless this determination with verifying documentation has been done by the sponsor.
units.action_summary: If the sponsor has already determined and documented the batch identity/strength/quality/purity with verifying documentation, the testing facility need not repeat it.

units.obligation_text: The charter participant for whom a new participant is substituted shall receive a full refund of all monies paid to the charter operator with respect to the charter.
units.action_summary: When a participant is substituted, the operator must fully refund all monies that participant paid for the charter.

units.obligation_text: with respect to non-European charters, the charter operator may reserve the right to retain an administrative fee of not more than $25 for effecting the substitution.
units.action_summary: For non-European charters, the operator is permitted to keep up to $25 as an administrative fee when arranging a substitute.

title: Nonclinical Laboratory Studies; Amendment of Good Laboratory Practice Regulations

units.obligation_text: For studies of more than 4 weeks' duration, a reserve sample of each test or control article-carrier mixture shall be taken and retained for the period of time provided by § 58.195.
units.action_summary: For studies longer than 4 weeks, take and retain a reserve sample of each test/control article-carrier mixture for the time specified in §58.195.

units.obligation_text: These samples are to be retained even if the batches are prepared daily.
units.action_summary: Retain reserve samples even when mixture batches are prepared daily.

units.obligation_text: But only sufficient sample need be retained to permit meaningful reanalysis of the test or control article.
units.action_summary: Retain only enough sample to permit meaningful reanalysis.

units.obligation_text: The samples must be retained either for the periods of time specified in § 58.195 or for the useful life of the sample (dependent on the stability or the quality of the sample), whichever is shorter.
units.action_summary: Keep samples for the period in §58.195 or for the sample's useful life, whichever is shorter.

units.obligation_text: Storage conditions should be those that minimize the deterioration of sample quality, but exhaustive study to determine those conditions that maximize stability is not required.
units.action_summary: Use storage conditions that minimize sample deterioration; exhaustive studies to maximize stability are not required.

units.obligation_text: Exhaustive study to determine those conditions that maximize stability is not required.
units.action_summary: There is no obligation to perform exhaustive studies to determine optimal stability conditions.

units.obligation_text: Section 58.107(d) requires that study records contain an inventory of test article disposition that demonstrates test article accountability for the study.
units.action_summary: Study records must include an inventory showing disposition and accountability of the test article for the study.

units.obligation_text: Such records must show the initial quantity of test article used to prepare the mixture and must show also the quantity of test article remaining after each mixture has been prepared.
units.action_summary: Records must document the initial amount of test article used and the amount remaining after each mixture is prepared.

units.obligation_text: Section 58.35(b)(3) requires the quality assurance unit to inspect the operations and records described in items 1 through 7 above.
units.action_summary: The QA unit must inspect the listed operations and records.

units.obligation_text: By amending § 58.113 by deleting and reserving paragraph (b).
units.action_summary: Delete and reserve paragraph (b) of §58.113 (proposed amendment to remove reserve-sample requirement).

units.obligation_text: By amending § 58.195 by deleting from paragraph (c) the phrase "samples of test or control article carrier mixtures."
units.action_summary: Delete the phrase "samples of test or control article carrier mixtures" from §58.195(c).

units.obligation_text: Interested persons may, on or before February 4, 1980, submit to the Hearing Clerk (HFA-305), Food and Drug Administration, Rm. 4-65, 5600 Fishers Lane, Rockville, MD 20857, written comments regarding this proposal.
units.actor: interested persons / members of the public
units.action_summary: Permits interested persons to submit written comments on the proposal by February 4, 1980.

units.obligation_text: Four copies of any comments are to be submitted.
units.action_summary: Commenters must submit four copies of comments (unless exception applies).

units.obligation_text: Individuals may submit one copy.
units.action_summary: Individual commenters are permitted to submit only one copy of comments instead of four.

units.obligation_text: Comments are to be identified with the Hearing Clerk docket number found in brackets in the heading of this document.
units.action_summary: Comments must include the Hearing Clerk docket number to identify the submission.

units.obligation_text: Received comments may be seen in the above office between 9 a.m. and 4 p.m., Monday through Friday.
units.action_summary: Submitted comments will be available for public inspection at the specified office and times.

title: Mammography Quality Standards Act

units.obligation_text: If a facility has failed to become accredited after three consecutive attempts, an accreditation body shall not accept an application for accreditation from the facility for a period of 1 year from the date of the most recent accreditation failure.
units.action_summary: Accreditation bodies must not accept accreditation applications from a facility for 1 year after three consecutive accreditation failures.

units.obligation_text: If a facility’s certificate was revoked on the basis of an act described in 42 U.S.C. 263b(i)(1), as implemented by § 900.14(a), no person who owned or operated that facility at the time the act occurred may own or operate a mammography facility within 2 years of the date of revocation.
units.actor: no person who owned or operated that facility at the time the act occurred
units.action_summary: Persons who owned or operated a facility at the time of a disqualifying act cannot own or operate a mammography facility for 2 years after certificate revocation.

units.obligation_text: Facilities shall maintain records of training and experience relevant to their qualification under MQSA for personnel who work or have worked at the facility as interpreting physicians, radiologic technologists, or medical physicists.
units.action_summary: Facilities must keep MQSA-relevant training and experience records for interpreting physicians, radiologic technologists, and medical physicists who work or have worked there.

units.obligation_text: These records must be available for review by the MQSA inspectors.
units.action_summary: Facilities must make personnel records available for MQSA inspector review.

units.obligation_text: Records of personnel no longer employed by the facility must be maintained at least until the next annual inspection has been completed and FDA has determined that the facility is in compliance with the MQSA personnel requirements.
units.action_summary: Facilities must keep former employees' records until the next annual inspection is completed and FDA determines personnel compliance.

units.obligation_text: The facility shall provide copies of these personnel records to current or former interpreting physicians, radiologic technologists, and medical physicists upon their reasonable request.
units.action_summary: Facilities must provide copies of personnel records to current or former relevant staff upon reasonable request.

units.obligation_text: Before a facility closes or ceases to provide mammography services, it must make arrangements for access by personnel to their MQSA personnel records.
units.action_summary: Before closing or stopping services, facilities must arrange for personnel access to their MQSA records.

units.obligation_text: This access may be provided by the permanent transfer of these records to the personnel or the transfer of the records to a facility or other entity that will provide access to these records.
units.action_summary: Facilities may provide access by permanently transferring records to personnel or to another entity that will provide access.

units.obligation_text: All digital accessory components shall be approved or cleared by FDA, (A) Specifically for mammography or, (B) For a use that could include mammography and have the same equipment specifications as those approved or cleared by FDA specifically for mammography.
units.actor: Digital accessory components / manufacturers of such components
units.action_summary: Digital accessory components must be FDA-approved or cleared either specifically for mammography or for a use that could include mammography with equivalent specifications.

units.obligation_text: (A) Specifically for mammography
units.action_summary: One acceptable approval is FDA clearance specifically for mammography.

units.obligation_text: (B) For a use that could include mammography and have the same equipment specifications as those approved or cleared by FDA specifically for mammography.
units.action_summary: Alternatively, approval for a use that could include mammography with identical equipment specifications is acceptable.

units.obligation_text: A mammography unit that is converted from one mammographic modality to another is considered a new unit at the facility under this part and must, prior to clinical use, undergo a mammography equipment evaluation demonstrating compliance with applicable requirements.
units.actor: The facility / the converted mammography unit
units.action_summary: When a unit is converted to a different mammographic modality it is treated as new and must undergo an equipment evaluation showing compliance before clinical use.

units.obligation_text: The facility must also follow its accreditation body’s procedures for applying for accreditation of that unit.
units.action_summary: Facilities must follow their accreditation body's procedures to apply for accreditation of the converted unit.

units.obligation_text: For facilities using screen-film units, the facility shall use x-ray film for mammography that has been designated by the film manufacturer as appropriate for mammography.
units.action_summary: Screen-film facilities must use x-ray film designated by the manufacturer as appropriate for mammography.

units.obligation_text: For facilities using hardcopy prints of digital images for transfer, retention, or final interpretation purposes, the facility shall use a type of film designated by the film manufacturer as appropriate for these purposes and compatible with the printer being used.
units.actor: Facilities using hardcopy prints of digital images
units.action_summary: Facilities using hardcopy prints must use film designated appropriate by manufacturer and compatible with the printer.

units.obligation_text: Systems with image receptor modalities other than screen-film shall demonstrate compliance with quality standards by successful results of quality assurance testing as specified under paragraph (e)(6) of this section.
units.actor: Systems with image receptor modalities other than screen-film / facilities using them
units.action_summary: Non-screen-film image receptor systems must demonstrate compliance via successful QA testing as specified in paragraph (e)(6).

units.obligation_text: Each facility shall prepare a written report of the results of each mammographic examination performed under its certificate. The mammographic examination presented for interpretation must be in the original mammographic modality in which it was performed, and must not consist of digital images produced through copying or digitizing hardcopy original images. The mammography report shall include the following information:
units.action_summary: Facilities must prepare a written report for each mammogram, present original-modality exams for interpretation (no copies/digitizations), and include specified information in the report.

units.obligation_text: The name of the patient and an additional patient identifier;
units.action_summary: The mammography report must include the patient's name and an additional identifier.

units.obligation_text: Date of examination, facility name, and location. At a minimum, the location shall include the city, State, ZIP code, and telephone number of the facility;
units.action_summary: Reports must include date, facility name, and detailed location information (city, State, ZIP, telephone).

units.obligation_text: The name of the interpreting physician who interpreted the mammogram;
units.action_summary: Reports must include the name of the interpreting physician.

units.obligation_text: Overall final assessment of findings, classified in one of the following categories: (A) "Negative:" ... (B) "Benign." ... (C) "Probably Benign:" ... (D) "Suspicious:" ... (E) "Highly suggestive of malignancy:" ... (F) "Known Biopsy Proven Malignancy." ... and (G) "Post-Procedure Mammograms for Marker Placement."
units.action_summary: The report must state an overall final assessment categorized into one of the listed categories (A–G).

units.obligation_text: "Negative:" Nothing to comment upon (if the interpreting physician is aware of clinical findings or symptoms, despite the negative assessment, these shall be explained);
units.action_summary: One allowed final assessment category is 'Negative', with explanation of any clinical findings known to the interpreting physician.

units.obligation_text: "Benign." Also, a normal result, with benign findings present, but no evidence of malignancy (if the interpreting physician is aware of clinical findings or symptoms, despite the benign assessment, these shall be explained);
units.action_summary: One allowed category is 'Benign'; interpreting physician should explain any clinical findings if aware.

units.obligation_text: "Probably Benign:" Finding(s) has a high probability of being benign;
units.action_summary: One allowed category is 'Probably Benign'.

units.obligation_text: "Suspicious:" Finding(s) without all the characteristic morphology of breast cancer but indicating a definite probability of being malignant;
units.action_summary: One allowed category is 'Suspicious'.

units.obligation_text: "Highly suggestive of malignancy:" Finding(s) has a high probability of being malignant;
units.action_summary: One allowed category is 'Highly suggestive of malignancy'.

units.obligation_text: "Known Biopsy Proven Malignancy." Reserved for known malignancies being mammographically evaluated for definitive therapy;
units.action_summary: One allowed category is 'Known Biopsy Proven Malignancy'.

units.obligation_text: "Post-Procedure Mammograms for Marker Placement." Reserved for a post-procedure mammogram used to confirm the deployment and position of a breast tissue marker.
units.action_summary: One allowed category is 'Post-Procedure Mammograms for Marker Placement'.

units.obligation_text: In cases where no final assessment category can be assigned due to incomplete work-up, one of the following classifications shall be assigned as an assessment and reasons why no assessment can be made shall be stated by the interpreting physician.
units.action_summary: When a final assessment cannot be assigned because of incomplete work-up, the interpreting physician must assign one of the 'Incomplete' classifications and state reasons.
units.modal_raw: shall be assigned / shall be stated

units.obligation_text: "Incomplete: Need additional imaging evaluation." Reserved for examinations where additional imaging needs to be performed before an assessment category ... can be given;
units.action_summary: One 'Incomplete' classification is 'Need additional imaging evaluation' when more imaging is required before final assessment.

units.obligation_text: "Incomplete: Need prior mammograms for comparison." Reserved for examinations where comparison with prior mammograms should be performed before an assessment category ... can be given.
units.action_summary: One 'Incomplete' classification is 'Need prior mammograms for comparison' when prior images are needed.

units.obligation_text: If this assessment category is used, a follow up report with an assessment category identified in paragraph (c)(1)(iv)(A) through (E) of this section must be issued within 30 calendar days of the initial report whether or not comparison views can be obtained.
units.action_summary: If 'Incomplete: Need prior mammograms for comparison' is used, a follow-up report with a definitive assessment must be issued within 30 calendar days of the initial report.

units.obligation_text: Overall assessment of breast density, classified in one of the following categories: (A) "The breasts are almost entirely fatty." (B) "There are scattered areas of fibroglandular density." (C) "The breasts are heterogeneously dense, which may obscure small masses." (D) "The breasts are extremely dense, which lowers the sensitivity of mammography."
units.action_summary: Reports must include an overall breast density assessment categorized into one of four specified categories.

units.obligation_text: "The breasts are almost entirely fatty."
units.action_summary: Density category: breasts almost entirely fatty.

units.obligation_text: "There are scattered areas of fibroglandular density."
units.action_summary: Density category: scattered fibroglandular density.

units.obligation_text: "The breasts are heterogeneously dense, which may obscure small masses."
units.action_summary: Density category: heterogeneously dense, which may obscure small masses.

units.obligation_text: "The breasts are extremely dense, which lowers the sensitivity of mammography."
units.action_summary: Density category: extremely dense, lowering mammography sensitivity.

units.obligation_text: Recommendations made to the healthcare provider about what additional actions, if any, should be taken. All clinical questions raised by the referring healthcare provider shall be addressed in the report to the extent possible, even if the assessment is negative or benign.
units.action_summary: Reports must include recommendations for additional actions and address clinical questions from the referring provider to the extent possible, even when assessments are negative or benign.

units.obligation_text: Each facility shall provide each patient a summary of the mammography report written in lay terms within 30 calendar days of the mammographic examination which shall, at a minimum, include the name of the patient, the name, address, and telephone number of the facility performing the mammographic examination and an assessment of breast density as described in paragraph (c)(1)(vi) of this section.
units.action_summary: Facilities must give patients a lay-language summary of the mammography report within 30 days that includes patient name, facility contact info, and breast density assessment.

units.obligation_text: The summary shall, at a minimum, include the name of the patient, the name, address, and telephone number of the facility performing the mammographic examination and an assessment of breast density as described in paragraph (c)(1)(vi) of this section.
units.action_summary: The lay summary must minimally include patient name, facility contact info, and breast density assessment.

units.obligation_text: If the assessment of the mammography report is "Suspicious" or "Highly suggestive of malignancy," the facility shall provide the patient a summary of the mammography report written in lay language within 7 calendar days of the final interpretation of the mammograms but in no case later than 21 calendar days from the date of the mammographic examination.
units.action_summary: If the assessment is 'Suspicious' or 'Highly suggestive of malignancy,' facilities must provide a lay summary to the patient within 7 days of final interpretation and no later than 21 days from exam date.

units.obligation_text: Patients who do not name a healthcare provider to receive the mammography report shall be sent the report described in paragraph (c)(1) of this section within 30 days, in addition to the written notification of results in lay terms.
units.action_summary: If a patient doesn't name a healthcare provider, the facility must send the full report to the patient within 30 days, in addition to the lay summary.

units.obligation_text: Each facility that accepts patients who do not have a healthcare provider shall maintain a system for referring such patients to a healthcare provider when mammographically or clinically indicated.
units.actor: Each facility that accepts patients who do not have a healthcare provider
units.action_summary: Facilities accepting patients without a healthcare provider must maintain a referral system when indicated.

units.obligation_text: If the mammography report identifies the patient’s breast density as "The breasts are almost entirely fatty" or "There are scattered areas of fibroglandular density," the lay summary shall include "Some patients have high breast tissue density (more glands than fat in the breasts), which makes it harder to find breast cancer on a mammogram. Your breast tissue density is low, not high. Follow the recommendations in this letter, and talk to your healthcare provider about breast density, risks for breast cancer, and your individual situation."
units.action_summary: If density is 'almost entirely fatty' or 'scattered areas', the lay summary must include specified text indicating the patient's density is low and advising to follow recommendations and discuss with their provider.

units.obligation_text: If the mammography report identifies the breast density as "The breasts are heterogeneously dense, which may obscure small masses" or "The breasts are extremely dense, which lowers the sensitivity of mammography," the lay summary shall include "Some patients have high breast tissue density (more glands than fat in the breasts), which makes it harder to find breast cancer on a mammogram. Your breast tissue density is high. Some patients with high breast density may need other imaging tests in addition to mammograms. Follow the recommendations in this letter, and talk to your healthcare provider about high breast density and how it relates to breast cancer risk, and your individual situation."
units.action_summary: If density is heterogeneously dense or extremely dense, the lay summary must include specific text advising the patient that their density is high and suggesting further discussion/testing as appropriate.

units.obligation_text: If the assessment is "Suspicious" or "Highly suggestive of malignancy," the facility shall provide a written report of the mammographic examination, including the items listed in paragraph (c)(1) of this section, to the referring healthcare provider, or if the referring healthcare provider is unavailable, to a responsible designee of the referring healthcare provider within 7 calendar days of the final interpretation of the mammograms but in no case later than 14 calendar days from the date of the mammographic examination.
units.action_summary: For 'Suspicious' or 'Highly suggestive' assessments, facilities must send the full written report to the referring provider (or their designee) within 7 days of final interpretation and no later than 14 days from the exam date.

units.obligation_text: Recordkeeping. Each facility that performs mammograms:
units.action_summary: Facilities performing mammograms have multiple recordkeeping obligations detailed in subparagraphs (i)-(v).

units.obligation_text: Shall (except as provided in paragraph (c)(4)(ii) of this section) maintain the mammograms and mammography reports in a permanent medical record of the patient for a period of not less than 5 years, or not less than 10 years if no additional mammograms of the patient are performed at the facility, or a longer period if mandated by State or local law.
units.action_summary: Facilities must keep mammograms and reports in patients' permanent medical records for at least 5 years (or 10 years if no additional mammograms are performed there), or longer if state/local law requires.

units.obligation_text: Facilities shall implement policies and procedures to minimize the possibility of loss of these records.
units.action_summary: Facilities must have policies and procedures to minimize the risk of losing mammographic records.

units.obligation_text: The mammograms must be retained in retrievable form in the mammographic modality in which they were produced. They cannot be produced by copying or digitizing hardcopy originals.
units.action_summary: Mammograms must be retained in retrievable form in their original modality and cannot be copies or digitized hardcopy originals.

units.obligation_text: Shall upon request by, or on behalf of, the patient, permanently or temporarily transfer the original mammograms and copies of the patient’s reports to a medical institution, a physician or healthcare provider of the patient, or to the patient directly during the time specified in paragraph (c)(4)(i) of this section. Transfer of the mammograms and mammography reports must take place within 15 calendar days of the facility receiving such request.
units.action_summary: Upon patient (or authorized) request, facilities must transfer original mammograms and reports to a designated recipient within 15 calendar days.

units.obligation_text: The transferred mammograms must be in the mammographic modality in which they were produced, and cannot be produced by copying or digitizing hardcopy originals.
units.action_summary: Transferred mammograms must be in the original modality and cannot be copies or digitized versions.

units.obligation_text: For digital mammograms or digital breast tomosynthesis, if the examination is being transferred for final interpretation purposes, the facility must be able to provide the recipient with original digital images electronically;
units.action_summary: If transferring digital exams for final interpretation, facilities must provide the recipient with original digital images electronically.

units.obligation_text: Shall upon request by, or on behalf of, the patient, provide copies of mammograms and copies of mammogram reports to a medical institution, a physician or healthcare provider of the patient, or to the patient directly during the time specified in paragraph (c)(4)(i) of this section. Release of the copies must take place within 15 calendar days of the facility receiving such request;
units.action_summary: Facilities must provide copies of mammograms and reports upon patient (or authorized) request within 15 calendar days.

units.obligation_text: Any fee charged to the patients for providing the services in paragraphs (c)(4)(ii) or (c)(4)(iii) of this section shall not exceed the documented costs associated with this service;
units.action_summary: Any fee charged for transferring or copying mammograms/reports must not exceed documented costs for the service.

units.obligation_text: Before a facility closes or ceases to provide mammography services, it must make arrangements for access by patients and healthcare providers to their mammographic records. This access may be provided by the permanent transfer of mammographic records to the patient or her healthcare provider or the transfer of the mammographic records to a facility or other entity that will provide access to patients and healthcare providers for the time periods specified in paragraph (c)(4)(i) of this section.
units.action_summary: Before closing or ceasing services, facilities must arrange for patient and provider access to mammographic records, e.g., by permanent transfer to patients/providers or to another entity that will provide access.

units.obligation_text: The facility must notify its accreditation body and certification agency in writing of the arrangements it has made
units.action_summary: Facilities must notify their accreditation body and certification agency in writing about arrangements made for record access when closing or ceasing services.

units.obligation_text: and must make reasonable efforts to notify all affected patients.
units.action_summary: Facilities must make reasonable efforts to notify all affected patients of the record access arrangements.

units.obligation_text: Each facility shall establish a system to collect and review outcome data for all mammographic examinations performed, including follow up on the disposition of all positive mammograms and correlation of pathology results with the interpreting physician’s mammography report.
units.action_summary: Facilities must set up a system to collect and review outcome data for all mammograms, including follow-up on positives and correlating pathology with mammography reports.

units.obligation_text: Positive predictive value—percent of patients with positive mammograms who are diagnosed with breast cancer within 1 year of the date of the mammographic examination.
units.action_summary: Facilities must determine the positive predictive value metric as part of outcome data analysis.

units.obligation_text: Cancer detection rate—of the patients initially examined with screening mammograms who receive an assessment of "Incomplete: Need additional imaging evaluation," "Suspicious," or "Highly suggestive of malignancy" on the screening mammogram or on a subsequent diagnostic mammogram, the number of patients who are diagnosed with breast cancer within 1 year of the date of the initial screening mammogram, expressed arithmetically as a ratio per 1,000 patients.
units.action_summary: Facilities must calculate the cancer detection rate per 1,000 screened patients as specified.

units.obligation_text: Recall rate—percentage of screening mammograms given an assessment of "Incomplete: Need additional imaging evaluation."
units.action_summary: Facilities must compute the recall rate (percentage of screenings assessed as 'Incomplete: Need additional imaging evaluation').

units.obligation_text: If FDA or the State certification agency believes that mammographic quality at a facility has been compromised and may present a significant risk to human health, the facility shall provide clinical images and other relevant information, as specified by FDA or the State certification agency, for review by the accreditation body or the State certification agency.
units.action_summary: If FDA or State believes quality is compromised and may present significant risk, the facility must provide clinical images and relevant information for review.

units.obligation_text: FDA or the State certification agency may require such a facility to notify all patients who received mammograms at the facility or those patients who are determined to be at risk due to the quality of their mammography, and their referring physicians or healthcare providers, of the deficiencies and resulting potential harm, appropriate remedial measures, and such other relevant information as FDA or the State certification agency may require.
units.actor: FDA or the State certification agency
units.action_summary: FDA/State may require a facility to notify affected patients and referring providers about deficiencies, potential harm, remedial measures, and other required information.

units.obligation_text: Such notification shall occur within a timeframe and in a manner specified by FDA or the State certification agency.
units.actor: The facility (if required to notify) or notifying authority as applicable
units.action_summary: Required notifications must occur within the timeframe and manner specified by FDA or the State certification agency.

units.obligation_text: If the facility is unable or unwilling to perform such notification, FDA or the State certification agency may notify patients and their referring physicians or other healthcare providers individually or through the mass media.
units.actor: FDA or the State certification agency
units.action_summary: If the facility cannot or will not notify patients, FDA/State may notify the patients and referring providers individually or via mass media.

units.obligation_text: Except as provided in paragraph (b) of this section, FDA may suspend or revoke a certificate if FDA finds, after providing the owner or operator of the facility with notice and opportunity for a hearing in accordance with part 16 of this chapter, that the facility, owner, operator, or any employee of the facility:
units.action_summary: FDA has the authority to suspend or revoke a facility's certificate after notice and opportunity for hearing if specified findings exist.

units.obligation_text: Has failed to comply with reasonable requests of FDA, the State certification agency, or the accreditation body for records, information, reports, or materials, including clinical images for an additional mammography review under § 900.12(j), that FDA or the State certification agency believes are necessary to determine the continued eligibility of the facility for a certificate or continued compliance with the standards of § 900.12;
units.actor: The facility, owner, operator, or any employee of the facility
units.action_summary: Failure to comply with reasonable records/information requests for determining eligibility/compliance is a ground for suspension or revocation.

units.obligation_text: Has violated or aided and abetted in the violation of any provision of or regulation promulgated pursuant to 42 U.S.C. 263b;
units.actor: The facility, owner, operator, or any employee of the facility
units.action_summary: Violating or aiding violations of provisions or regulations under 42 U.S.C. 263b is a ground for suspension or revocation.

units.obligation_text: Has failed to comply with prior sanctions imposed by FDA or the State certification agency under 42 U.S.C. 263b(h), including a directed plan of correction or a patient and referring physician notification;
units.actor: The facility, owner, operator, or any employee of the facility
units.action_summary: Failing to comply with prior sanctions (e.g., plan of correction or required notifications) is a ground for revocation or suspension.

units.obligation_text: Has failed to comply with reasonable requests of current or former facility personnel for records of their training or experience relevant to their qualification under MQSA, in violation of § 900.12(a)(4).

title:
Content and Format of Substantial Equivalence Reports; Food and Drug
Administration Actions on Substantial Equivalence Reports

units.obligation_text: An applicant may submit a SE Report intended to demonstrate that a new tobacco product is substantially equivalent to a predicate tobacco product.
units.action_summary: Applicant is permitted to submit an SE Report to demonstrate substantial equivalence.

units.obligation_text: The applicant must submit the SE Report at least 90 calendar days prior to the date the applicant intends to introduce or deliver for introduction a new tobacco product into interstate commerce for commercial distribution.
units.action_summary: Applicant must submit the SE Report at least 90 days before intended commercial introduction.

units.obligation_text: The applicant cannot begin commercial distribution of the new tobacco product until FDA has provided the applicant an order stating that the Agency has determined that the new tobacco product is substantially equivalent to a predicate tobacco product, unless the new tobacco product has received authorization to be marketed through another premarket pathway.
units.action_summary: Applicant is prohibited from starting commercial distribution until FDA issues an SE order (unless another premarket authorization exists).

units.obligation_text: Unless the new tobacco product has received authorization to be marketed through another premarket pathway.
units.action_summary: Exception allowing commercial distribution if product has another premarket authorization.

units.obligation_text: The SE Report must provide information uniquely identifying the new tobacco product and the predicate tobacco product, and compare the new tobacco product to either a grandfathered tobacco product or a tobacco product that FDA previously found to be substantially equivalent. The SE Report must provide sufficient information as described in this section to enable FDA to determine whether the new tobacco product is substantially equivalent to a tobacco product that was commercially marketed in the United States as of February 15, 2007.
units.action_summary: The SE Report must identify and compare the new and predicate products and include enough information for FDA to determine substantial equivalence.

units.obligation_text: If FDA cites deficiencies and requests information to support a statement in the SE Report, the applicant must provide that information for review to continue
units.action_summary: Applicant must provide requested information if FDA cites deficiencies to allow review to continue.

units.obligation_text: or FDA may issue an order under § 1107.48.
units.action_summary: If applicant does not provide requested information, FDA may issue an order under §1107.48.

units.obligation_text: FDA will refuse to accept an SE Report if it does not comply with this section.
units.action_summary: FDA will not accept SE Reports that do not comply with the section's requirements.

units.obligation_text: The SE Report must contain the following information:
units.action_summary: SE Report is required to include a specified list of information items.

units.obligation_text: General information (as described in paragraph (c) of this section).
units.action_summary: Applicant must include general information as described in paragraph (c).

units.obligation_text: Summary (as described in paragraph (d) of this section).
units.action_summary: Applicant must include the summary described in paragraph (d).

units.obligation_text: New tobacco product description (as described in paragraph (e) of this section).
units.action_summary: Applicant must provide the new product description per paragraph (e).

units.obligation_text: Predicate tobacco product description (as described in paragraph (f) of this section), including a statement that the predicate tobacco product has not been removed from the market at the initiative of FDA and has not been determined by judicial order to be adulterated or misbranded, and the submission tracking number of the SE order finding the predicate product SE, or the submission tracking number of, or information to support, a grandfathered determination of the predicate tobacco product;
units.action_summary: Applicant must describe the predicate product and include statements and STN(s) showing its status (SE order or grandfathered determination).

units.obligation_text: Comparison information (as described in paragraph (g) of this section);
units.action_summary: Applicant must provide comparison information between new and predicate products per paragraph (g).

units.obligation_text: Comparative testing information (as described in paragraph (h) of this section);
units.action_summary: Applicant must include comparative testing information as required in paragraph (h).

units.obligation_text: Statement of compliance with applicable tobacco product standards (as described in paragraph (i) of this section);
units.action_summary: Applicant must include a statement of compliance with applicable tobacco product standards per paragraph (i).

units.obligation_text: Health information summary or statement that such information will be made available upon request (as described in paragraph (j) of this section);
units.action_summary: Applicant must include either a health information summary or a statement that the information will be made available on request.

units.obligation_text: Compliance with 21 CFR part 25 (as described in paragraph (k) of this section); and
units.action_summary: Applicant must include information demonstrating compliance with 21 CFR part 25 as described.

units.obligation_text: Certification statement (as described in paragraph (l) of this section).
units.action_summary: Applicant must include the required certification statement per paragraph (l).

units.obligation_text: The date the SE Report is submitted;
units.action_summary: Include the date of SE Report submission.

units.obligation_text: Type of submission (e.g., the SE Report or amendment to a report);
units.action_summary: State the type of submission (initial SE Report or amendment).

units.obligation_text: FDA STN if previously assigned;
units.action_summary: Provide the FDA submission tracking number if previously assigned.

units.obligation_text: Any other relevant FDA STN, such as a request for grandfathered determination or SE Report previously found substantially equivalent (if applicable), and cross-references to meetings with FDA regarding the new tobacco product;
units.action_summary: Include other relevant FDA STNs and references to meetings with FDA about the product.

units.obligation_text: Applicant name, address, and contact information;
units.action_summary: Provide applicant's name, address, and contact information.

units.obligation_text: Authorized representative or U.S. agent (for a foreign applicant), including the name, address, and contact information;
units.action_summary: Provide authorized representative or U.S. agent contact details if applicable.

units.obligation_text: For both the new and predicate tobacco products, the following information to uniquely identify the products:
units.action_summary: Include identifying information for both new and predicate products.

units.obligation_text: Manufacturer;
units.action_summary: Provide the manufacturer's name for each product.

units.obligation_text: Product name, including the brand and sub brand (or other commercial name used in commercial distribution);
units.action_summary: Provide the product name, brand and sub-brand used in commerce.

units.obligation_text: Product category, product subcategory, and product properties (if the product does not have a listed product property, e.g., ventilation or characterizing flavor, the report must state 'none' for that property) as provided in the following table:
units.action_summary: Provide product category/subcategory and product properties; state 'none' for any non-applicable listed property.

units.obligation_text: Provide product properties as specified in the table (e.g., package type, product quantity, length, diameter, ventilation, characterizing flavors, and additional properties) appropriate to the product category and subcategory.
units.action_summary: Populate the specified product properties table with applicable attributes for the product category/subcategory.

units.obligation_text: The applicant must submit the SE Report using the form(s) that FDA provides.
units.action_summary: Applicant must use FDA-provided form(s) to submit the SE Report.

units.obligation_text: The SE Report must contain a comprehensive index and table of contents, be well-organized and legible, and be written in English.
units.action_summary: SE Report must have an index and table of contents, be organized, legible, and in English.

units.obligation_text: As described in § 1107.62, the applicant must submit the SE Report and all information supporting the SE Report in an electronic format that FDA can process, read, review, and archive, unless FDA has provided a waiver.
units.action_summary: Applicant must submit the SE Report and supporting information electronically in a format FDA can handle, unless FDA waives this requirement.

units.obligation_text: Unless FDA has provided a waiver.
units.action_summary: Exception: FDA may provide a waiver to the electronic submission requirement.

units.obligation_text: The SE Report must include a summary at the beginning of the SE Report that includes the following:
units.action_summary: Applicant must include an introductory summary containing specified elements.

units.obligation_text: A concise description of the characteristics of the new tobacco product;
units.action_summary: Include a concise description of the new product's characteristics in the summary.

units.obligation_text: A statement as to whether the applicant believes the new tobacco product has the same characteristics as the predicate tobacco product or has different characteristics but does not raise different questions of public health;
units.action_summary: State whether the applicant believes the new product is the same as the predicate or differs without raising different public health questions.

units.obligation_text: A concise description of the similarities and differences between the new tobacco product and the predicate tobacco product with respect to their characteristics (materials, ingredients, design, composition, heating source, or other features).
units.action_summary: Provide a concise description of similarities and differences in characteristics between the new and predicate products.

units.obligation_text: The applicant must identify one new tobacco product in the SE Report for comparison to one predicate tobacco product. The SE Report must describe the new tobacco product in sufficient detail to enable FDA to evaluate its characteristics. This part of the SE Report must include:
units.action_summary: Applicant must identify one new product (compared to one predicate) and describe it in sufficient detail; the report must include specified elements.

units.obligation_text: A narrative description of the new tobacco product and detailed drawings or schematics of the new tobacco product, including its container closure system, illustrating all components or parts of the product. For a portioned tobacco product, the SE Report must also include a diagram illustrating all components or parts of the individual unit of use;
units.action_summary: Provide a narrative description and detailed drawings/schematics of the new product and its components; include a unit diagram for portioned products.

units.obligation_text: A description and the function of each component or part of the new tobacco product, and an explanation of how each component or part is integrated into the design of the new tobacco product;
units.action_summary: Describe each component/part, its function, and how it is integrated into the product design.

units.obligation_text: A concise overview of the process used to manufacture the new tobacco product, including the fermentation process, where applicable, with information on the type and quantity of the microbial inoculum and/or fermentation solutions.
units.action_summary: Provide a concise overview of the manufacturing process, including fermentation details where applicable.

units.obligation_text: If the manufacturing process for the new tobacco product does not affect the characteristics of the new tobacco product beyond what is described elsewhere in the SE Report, an applicant must state that to satisfy this provision.
units.action_summary: If manufacturing process does not affect characteristics beyond what's described, applicant must state that fact.

units.obligation_text: The applicant must identify a predicate tobacco product that is either a grandfathered tobacco product or a tobacco product that FDA previously found to be substantially equivalent.
units.action_summary: Applicant must identify a predicate product that is grandfathered or previously found substantially equivalent by FDA.

units.action_summary: Commenters must submit comments (either electronically or in writing) by July 17, 2019.
