title: Revocation of the Test for Mycoplasma

units.obligation_text: This rule revokes the 610.30 Test for Mycoplasma
units.action_summary: FDA is revoking the 21 CFR 610.30 mycoplasma test requirement.

units.obligation_text: The 610.30 Test for Mycoplasma requires manufacturers to test for mycoplasma during manufacture of live and inactivated vaccines produced from in vitro living cell cultures
units.action_summary: Manufacturers must test for mycoplasma during manufacture of specified vaccines under the 610.30 test.

units.obligation_text: The regulation outlines a specific testing method that manufacturers must follow
units.action_summary: Manufacturers are required to follow the specific testing method set out in the regulation.

units.obligation_text: These procedures require a minimum of 28 days to complete
units.action_summary: The specified testing procedures take at least 28 days to complete.

units.obligation_text: If the results of testing reveal no evidence of contamination, vaccine manufacturers can distribute the vaccine
units.action_summary: Manufacturers are permitted to distribute vaccine when testing shows no contamination.

units.obligation_text: a vaccine producer must obtain FDA approval for modifications to mycoplasma testing in accordance with 21 CFR 601.12(b) or (c) and meeting the requirements of 21 CFR 610.9
units.action_summary: Manufacturers must obtain FDA approval to modify mycoplasma testing, complying with 21 CFR 601.12(b) or (c) and 21 CFR 610.9.

units.obligation_text: All manufacturers would also continue to submit supplements for FDA approval in order to change mycoplasma testing procedures
units.action_summary: Manufacturers must submit supplements to FDA for approval to change mycoplasma testing procedures.

units.obligation_text: Because FDA must approve all supplemental changes to a vaccine licensing agreement regardless of whether 21 CFR 610.30 is in place
units.action_summary: FDA is required to approve supplemental changes to vaccine licensing agreements.

units.obligation_text: Eliminating this regulation allows manufacturers of live virus vaccines and inactivated virus vaccines produced from in vitro living cell cultures the flexibility to determine the most appropriate and effective mycoplasma testing methods
units.action_summary: Manufacturers are permitted to choose appropriate mycoplasma testing methods after elimination of the regulation.

units.obligation_text: manufacturers may choose to conduct testing in-house or contract the testing to an external laboratory
units.action_summary: Manufacturers are permitted to perform testing themselves or hire external laboratories.

title: Medical Devices; Ear, Nose, and Throat Devices; Establishing Over-the- Counter Hearing Aids

units.obligation_text: Air-conduction hearing aids that satisfy the requirements in paragraphs (c) through (f) of this section are considered "available" over the counter as section 520(q)(1)(A)(v) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act uses the term.
units.action_summary: If an air-conduction hearing aid meets paragraphs (c)-(f), it is classified as available over the counter under section 520(q)(1)(A)(v).

units.obligation_text: Air-conduction hearing aids that do not meet the definition in section 520(q) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act and do not satisfy the following requirements are prescription hearing aids.
units.action_summary: If an air-conduction hearing aid does not meet section 520(q) or the specified requirements, it is a prescription hearing aid.

units.obligation_text: A hearing aid shall not be "used" merely because a prospective user wore it as part of a bona fide hearing aid evaluation to determine whether to select that particular hearing aid for that prospective user.
units.action_summary: Do not classify a hearing aid as 'used' just because a prospective user wore it during a bona fide evaluation.

units.obligation_text: An OTC hearing aid shall bear all of the following in the labeling.
units.action_summary: OTC hearing aids must include specified labeling content.

units.obligation_text: The outside package of an OTC hearing aid shall bear all of the following:
units.actor: outside package of an OTC hearing aid (manufacturer/distributor)
units.action_summary: Require specific items to appear on the outside package.

units.obligation_text: WARNING: If you are younger than 18, do not use this. You should go to a doctor because your condition needs specialized evaluation and management. Over-the-counter hearing aids are only for users who are age 18 or older.
units.action_summary: Prohibits use by persons under 18 and advises they should see a doctor.

units.obligation_text: Important Information: You can seek assistance from a hearing healthcare professional. If you try this device and continue to struggle with or remain concerned about your hearing, you should seek a consultation with a hearing healthcare professional.
units.action_summary: Permits seeking assistance from a hearing professional and recommends consultation if problems persist.

units.obligation_text: If the OTC hearing aid is used or rebuilt, the outside package shall declare that fact.
units.actor: outside package of an OTC hearing aid (manufacturer/distributor)
units.action_summary: Packages must indicate if the device is used or rebuilt.

units.obligation_text: The manufacturer or distributor of an OTC hearing aid shall include a user instructional brochure inside the package and shall make an electronic version available for download without site or customer registration and without requiring purchase of any product or service.
units.action_summary: Manufacturers/distributors must provide a printed user brochure in the package and an electronic downloadable version freely accessible.

units.obligation_text: The following warnings, which shall appear in the following order and prior to any content except the cover page:
units.action_summary: Specific warnings must be placed in the brochure in a prescribed order before other content.

units.obligation_text: Prior to purchasing this device, you should promptly consult with a licensed physician, preferably an ear specialist, if you have any of the following: [list of conditions].
units.action_summary: Consumers are advised to promptly consult a licensed physician before purchase if they have listed 'red flag' conditions.

units.obligation_text: This information and other labeling, including the user instructional brochure, are available on the internet at: [weblink]. You may also call [telephone number] to request a paper copy of this information and other labeling.
units.action_summary: Consumers may access labeling online and may call to request a paper copy.

units.obligation_text: Any additional warnings the manufacturer may include prior to the caution and notices to users in paragraph (c)(2)(iii) of this section.
units.action_summary: Manufacturers are permitted to include additional warnings prior to other cautions/notices.

units.obligation_text: The following caution and notices for users, which shall appear prior to any content except the cover page and the warnings under paragraphs (c)(2)(i) and (ii) of this section:
units.action_summary: Cautions and notices listed must appear in the brochure in a specified position relative to other content.

units.obligation_text: WARNING: If you are younger than 18, do not use this. You should go to a doctor because your condition needs specialized evaluation and management.
units.action_summary: Prohibits use by persons under 18 and recommends medical evaluation for persons under 18.

units.obligation_text: WARNING: Conditions that Require Medical Care Prior to purchasing this device, you should promptly consult with a licensed physician, preferably an ear specialist, if you have any of the following: [list of conditions].
units.action_summary: Advises consumers to promptly consult a physician before purchase if specific conditions are present.

units.obligation_text: WARNING: This hearing aid should not cause pain when inserting it. Remove this device from your ear if it causes pain or discomfort when inserting or placing it. To try again, make sure to follow the instructions. If you feel pain or discomfort again, contact the manufacturer. You may also report this to FDA as an adverse event according to the instructions that appear later.
units.action_summary: Advises users to remove device if it causes pain, to follow instructions, contact manufacturer for recurrent pain, and permits reporting to FDA.

units.obligation_text: Caution: This is not hearing protection. You should remove this device if you experience overly loud sounds, either of short or long duration. You should use appropriate hearing protection in loud environments. As a general rule, if you would use ear plugs in a loud environment, you should remove this device and use ear plugs in that environment.
units.action_summary: Warns device is not hearing protection and recommends removing it and using hearing protection in loud environments.

units.obligation_text: Caution: The sound output should not be uncomfortable or painful. You should turn down the volume or remove the device if the sound output is uncomfortably loud or painful.
units.action_summary: Advises users to reduce volume or remove device if sound is uncomfortably loud or painful.

units.obligation_text: Note: If you remain concerned, consult a professional. If you try this device and continue to struggle with or remain concerned about your hearing, you should consult with a hearing healthcare professional.
units.action_summary: Advises consumers to consult a professional if concerns persist.

units.obligation_text: Note: Expectations about what a hearing aid can do ...
units.action_summary: Provides informational expectations (no direct obligation).

units.obligation_text: An illustration(s) of the OTC hearing aid that indicates operating controls, user adjustments, and the battery compartment.
units.action_summary: Brochure must include illustrations showing controls, adjustments, and battery compartment.
units.modal_raw: shall (implied by listing under required brochure content)

units.obligation_text: Information on the function of all controls intended for user adjustment.
units.action_summary: Brochure must describe functions of all user-adjustable controls.

units.obligation_text: A description of any accessory that accompanies the OTC hearing aid, including but not limited to wax guards and accessories for use with a computer, television, or telephone.
units.action_summary: Brochure must describe accompanying accessories.

units.obligation_text: Instructions for sizing or inserting the eartip of the OTC hearing aid to prevent insertion past the bony-cartilaginous junction of the external auditory canal and damage to the tympanic membrane.
units.action_summary: Brochure must include instructions to prevent deep insertion and tympanic membrane damage.

units.obligation_text: The tools, tests, or software that allow the user to control the OTC hearing aid, including self-select, self-fit, and self-check the performance of the OTC hearing aid, and customize it to the user’s hearing needs, including information about properly fitting eartips.
units.action_summary: Brochure must describe tools/tests/software that let users control and customize the device, including fitting eartips.

units.obligation_text: Use of the OTC hearing aid with any accompanying accessories.
units.action_summary: Brochure must include instructions for use with accessories.

units.obligation_text: Maintenance and care of the OTC hearing aid, including the procedure to follow in washing the earmold, when replacing tubing on those hearing aids that use tubing, and in storing the hearing aid when it will not be used for an extended period of time.
units.action_summary: Brochure must include maintenance and care procedures.

units.obligation_text: If the battery is replaceable or rechargeable, how to replace or recharge the battery, including a generic designation of replacement batteries.
units.action_summary: Brochure must explain replacing/recharging batteries and identify replacement batteries.

units.obligation_text: Expected battery life.
units.action_summary: Brochure must state expected battery life.

units.obligation_text: Any other information necessary for adequate directions for use as defined in § 801.5.
units.action_summary: Brochure must include any additional information necessary for adequate directions for use.

units.obligation_text: Identification of any known physiological side effects associated with the use of the OTC hearing aid that may warrant consultation with a physician, including if applicable, skin irritation and accelerated accumulation of cerumen (ear wax).
units.action_summary: Brochure must identify known physiological side effects that could warrant medical consultation.

units.obligation_text: The technical specifications required by paragraph (c)(4) of this section.
units.action_summary: Brochure must include the specified technical specifications listed in paragraph (c)(4).

units.obligation_text: A description of commonly occurring, avoidable events that could adversely affect or damage the OTC hearing aid, including but not limited to ear wax buildup, drops, immersion in water, or exposure to excessive heat.
units.action_summary: Brochure must describe common avoidable events that could damage the device.

units.obligation_text: If the hearing aid incorporates wireless technology in its programming or use, appropriate warnings, instructions, and information relating to electromagnetic compatibility and wireless technology and human exposure to non-ionizing radiation.
units.action_summary: If device has wireless tech, brochure must include warnings/instructions about electromagnetic compatibility and exposure.

units.obligation_text: If the manufacturer provides a repair service or licenses or certifies third-party repair services, information on how and where to obtain repair service, including at least one specific address where the user can go or send the OTC hearing aid to obtain such repair service.
units.action_summary: If repair services are provided or authorized, brochure must give information on obtaining repair service including a specific address.

units.obligation_text: If clinical or non-clinical studies were conducted by or for the manufacturer to support the performance of the OTC hearing aid, a summary of all such studies.
units.action_summary: If studies were conducted, the manufacturer must include a summary in the brochure.

units.obligation_text: The labeling on an OTC hearing aid itself shall bear all of the following clearly and permanently, except as provided in paragraph (c)(3)(iii) of this section:
units.action_summary: Require specific markings on the device itself, permanently and clearly.

units.obligation_text: The serial number.
units.action_summary: Device must bear a serial number.

units.obligation_text: If the battery is removable, a "+" symbol to indicate the positive terminal for battery insertion unless the battery’s physical design prevents inserting the battery in the reversed position.
units.action_summary: If battery removable, device must bear '+' symbol for positive terminal unless design prevents reversed insertion.

units.obligation_text: If the OTC hearing aid is used or rebuilt, the manufacturer shall physically attach a removable tag to the hearing aid declaring that fact.
units.action_summary: Manufacturers must attach a removable tag to used or rebuilt devices declaring that status.

units.obligation_text: All of the following technical specifications shall appear in the user instructional brochure that accompanies the device. You may additionally include it on the outside package.
units.action_summary: Brochure must contain listed technical specs; manufacturer may also include them on the outside package.

units.obligation_text: The maximum output limit value (OSPL90); The full-on gain value; The total harmonic distortion value; The self-generated noise value; The latency value; The upper and lower cutoff frequencies for bandwidth.
units.action_summary: Brochure must list specified technical metrics (OSPL90, gain, THD, self-noise, latency, cutoff frequencies).

units.obligation_text: The output limit for an OTC hearing aid shall be the device maximum acoustic output sound pressure level (SPL) in a 2-cubic centimeter (cm3) coupler when the device input is a 90 dB SPL pure-tone, and the gain/volume control is full on. An OTC hearing aid shall not exceed the following limits:
units.action_summary: Defines how output limit is measured and states that devices must not exceed specified output limits.

units.obligation_text: An OTC hearing aid shall not exceed an output limit of 115 dB SPL at any frequency except as provided in paragraph (d)(2) of this section.
units.action_summary: Device maximum output must not exceed 115 dB SPL at any frequency, subject to exceptions.

units.obligation_text: An OTC hearing aid that includes input-controlled compression and a user-adjustable volume control shall not exceed an output limit of 120 dB SPL at any frequency.
units.actor: OTC hearing aid with input-controlled compression and user-adjustable volume control
units.action_summary: Devices with input-controlled compression and user volume control must not exceed 120 dB SPL output.

units.obligation_text: An OTC hearing aid shall perform within all of the following electroacoustic limits.
units.action_summary: Device must meet the specified electroacoustic performance limits.

units.obligation_text: The total harmonic distortion plus noise shall not exceed 5 percent for output levels within one of the following sets of levels, depending on the test method:
units.action_summary: Total harmonic distortion plus noise must not exceed 5% at specified output levels.

units.obligation_text: You must measure the total harmonic distortion using a 500-Hz input tone with an analyzer that has a bandwidth at least as wide as the frequency limits of the OTC hearing aid.
units.action_summary: Measurement of total harmonic distortion must use a 500-Hz input tone and an analyzer with sufficient bandwidth.

units.obligation_text: You must measure the output distortion at the OTC hearing aid’s maximum volume and the input sound level to the OTC hearing aid adjusted to produce the required outputs.
units.action_summary: Output distortion must be measured at maximum volume with input adjusted to required outputs.

units.obligation_text: Self-generated noise shall not exceed 32 dB SPL. You must disable any methods that artificially lower the apparent noise floor for the measurement.
units.action_summary: Self-noise must be ≤32 dB SPL and methods that artificially lower noise floor (e.g., auto-muting) must be disabled during measurement.

units.obligation_text: Latency shall not exceed 15 ms. You must measure the latency with a method that is accurate and repeatable to within 1.5 ms.
units.action_summary: Latency must be ≤15 ms and measured with a method accurate and repeatable to within 1.5 ms.

units.obligation_text: The lower cutoff frequency shall extend to 250 Hz or below, and the upper cutoff frequency shall extend to 5 kHz or greater. You must measure the frequency response bandwidth as specified in the Method for clause 4.1 in ANSI/CTA–2051:2017.
units.action_summary: Device bandwidth must meet cutoff frequency limits and be measured per ANSI/CTA–2051:2017 clause 4.1.

units.obligation_text: No single peak in the one-third-octave frequency response shall exceed 12 dB relative to the average levels of the one-third-octave bands, two-thirds octave above and below the peak. You must measure the frequency response smoothness using values for a diffuse field and the corrected one-third-octave frequency insertion response as specified in the Method for clause 4.1 in ANSI/CTA–2051:2017.
units.action_summary: Limit on response peaks (≤12 dB) and measurement method specified per ANSI/CTA–2051:2017.

units.obligation_text: An OTC hearing aid must conform to all of the following design requirements.
units.action_summary: Device must meet listed design requirements.

units.obligation_text: The design of an OTC hearing aid shall limit the insertion of the eartip to the bony-cartilaginous junction of the external auditory canal and no deeper.
units.action_summary: Device must be designed to prevent eartip insertion beyond the bony-cartilaginous junction.

units.obligation_text: The material for the eartip of an OTC hearing aid shall be atraumatic.
units.action_summary: Eartip material must be atraumatic.

units.obligation_text: The OTC hearing aid shall be designed to enable consumers to readily achieve a safe, customized, acoustically favorable, and comfortable physical fit in the ear canal and/or external ear.
units.action_summary: Device must be designed to allow consumers to obtain a safe, customized, and comfortable fit.

units.obligation_text: The OTC hearing aid shall, through tools, tests, or software, permit a lay user to control the device and customize it to the user’s hearing needs.
units.action_summary: Device must include tools/tests/software enabling lay users to control and customize it.

units.obligation_text: The sale of an OTC hearing aid to or for a person younger than 18 years of age is prohibited.
units.action_summary: It is prohibited to sell OTC hearing aids to persons under 18.

units.obligation_text: No State or local government shall establish or continue in effect any law, regulation, order, or other requirement specifically related to hearing products that would restrict or interfere with the servicing, marketing, sale, dispensing, use, customer support, or distribution of OTC hearing aids through in-person transactions, by mail, or online, that is different from, in addition to, or otherwise not identical to, the regulations issued under section 709(b) of the FDA Reauthorization Act of 2017, including any State or local requirement for the supervision, prescription, or other order, involvement, or intervention of a licensed person for consumers to access OTC hearing aids.
units.action_summary: States and localities are preempted from imposing requirements on OTC hearing aids that differ from federal regulations, including requirements for licensed-person supervision.

units.obligation_text: The servicing, marketing, sale, dispensing, customer support, or distribution of OTC hearing aids ... shall not cause, require, or otherwise obligate a person providing such services to obtain specialized licensing, certification, or any other State or local sanction unless such requirement is generally applicable to the sale of any product or to all places of business regardless of whether they sell OTC hearing aids.
units.actor: State or local government / licensing authorities
units.action_summary: States/localities cannot require specialized licensing/certification for persons providing OTC hearing-aid services unless the requirement is generally applicable.

units.obligation_text: A licensed person may service, market, sell, dispense, provide customer support for, or distribute OTC hearing aids.
units.action_summary: Licensed professionals are permitted to provide services for OTC hearing aids.

units.obligation_text: A person shall not incur specialized obligations by representing as a servicer, marketer, seller, dispenser, customer support representative, or distributor (or an equivalent description) of OTC hearing aids.
units.action_summary: Representing oneself as a servicer/marketer/seller/etc. of OTC hearing aids does not create specialized obligations.

units.obligation_text: The standard required in this section is incorporated by reference into this section with the approval of the Director of the Federal Register under 5 U.S.C. 552(a) and 1 CFR part 51.
units.actor: Director of the Federal Register / regulatory framework
units.action_summary: Specifies incorporation by reference of ANSI/CTA–2051 standard into the regulation.

units.obligation_text: Any hearing aid that does not satisfy the requirements of § 800.30 of this chapter shall be a prescription device.
units.action_summary: Hearing aids not meeting §800.30 requirements are classified as prescription devices.

units.obligation_text: A prescription hearing aid shall bear all of the following labeling.
units.action_summary: Prescription hearing aids must include specified labeling content.

units.obligation_text: The outside package of a prescription hearing aid shall bear all of the following:
units.actor: outside package of a prescription hearing aid (manufacturer/distributor)
units.action_summary: Require specific items to appear on the outside package of prescription hearing aids.

units.obligation_text: If the prescription hearing aid is used or rebuilt, the outside package shall declare that fact. A sticker under and visible through the outer wrapper will suffice to declare such fact.
units.action_summary: Used or rebuilt prescription devices must be declared on the outside package; a visible sticker suffices.

units.obligation_text: The manufacturer or distributor of a prescription hearing aid shall include a user instructional brochure inside the package and shall make an electronic version available for download without site or customer registration and without requiring purchase of any product or service.
units.action_summary: Manufacturers/distributors of prescription hearing aids must include a brochure and make an electronic version freely available.

units.obligation_text: WARNING - Medical evaluation for people younger than 18: The use of a hearing aid in people younger than 18 years old without a medical evaluation may worsen impairment or disability. A prospective hearing aid user who is younger than 18 should have a recent medical evaluation from a licensed physician, preferably an ear specialist. Prior to purchase, a physician should determine that the person is a candidate for the use of a hearing aid.
units.action_summary: Advises that users under 18 should get a recent medical evaluation and physician should determine candidacy prior to purchase.

units.obligation_text: WARNING: Conditions that Require Medical Care Prior to purchasing this device, you should promptly consult with a licensed physician, preferably an ear specialist, if you have any of the following: [list of conditions].
units.action_summary: Advises consumers to promptly consult a physician before purchase if listed conditions are present.

units.obligation_text: Note: Ask about trial-rental or purchase-option programs. If you are unsure about your ability to adapt to using a hearing aid, you should ask about the availability of a trial-rental or purchase-option program.
units.action_summary: Recommends consumers ask about trial-rental or purchase-option programs if unsure about adapting to a hearing aid.

units.obligation_text: WARNING to Hearing Aid Dispensers: You should advise a prospective hearing aid user to consult promptly with a licensed physician, preferably an ear specialist, before dispensing a hearing aid if you determine through inquiry, actual observation, or review of any other available information concerning the prospective user, that the prospective user has any of the following: [list of conditions].
units.action_summary: Dispensers should advise prospective users with listed conditions to consult a physician before dispensing.

units.obligation_text: WARNING to Hearing Aid Dispensers, Outputs in excess of 132 dB SPL: You should exercise special care in selecting and fitting a hearing aid with a maximum output that exceeds 132 dB SPL because it may impair the remaining hearing of the hearing aid user.
units.action_summary: Dispensers should exercise special care when selecting/fitting devices with outputs >132 dB SPL.

units.obligation_text: Note: Tell FDA about injuries, malfunctions, or other adverse events. To report an adverse event, you should submit the information to FDA as soon as possible after the event.
units.action_summary: Advises users to report adverse events to FDA as soon as possible; instructs where/how to report.

units.obligation_text: The following caution and notices for users, which shall appear prior to any content, except the cover page and the warnings under paragraph (c)(2)(i) of this section:
units.action_summary: Cautions and notices must appear prior to other content in the brochure as specified.

units.obligation_text: Caution: This is not hearing protection. You should remove this device if you experience overly loud sounds, either of short or long duration. You should use appropriate hearing protection in loud environments.
units.action_summary: Advises users that device is not hearing protection and recommends removing device and using hearing protection in loud environments.

units.obligation_text: Caution: The sound output should not be uncomfortable or painful. You should turn down the volume or remove the device if the sound output is uncomfortably loud or painful.
units.action_summary: Advises users to reduce volume or remove device if sound is uncomfortably loud or painful.

units.obligation_text: To report an adverse event, you should submit the information to FDA as soon as possible after the event. Instructions for reporting are available at https://www.fda.gov/Safety/MedWatch, or call 1-800-FDA-1088.
units.action_summary: Advises users to report adverse events promptly and provides reporting instructions.

units.obligation_text: An illustration(s) of the prescription hearing aid that indicates operating controls, user adjustments, and the battery compartment; Information on the function of all controls intended for user adjustment; A description of any accessory that accompanies the prescription hearing aid.
units.action_summary: Brochure must include illustrations, control function information, and accessory descriptions for prescription devices.

units.obligation_text: Specific instructions for Use of the prescription hearing aid with any accompanying accessories; Maintenance and care of the prescription hearing aid, including the procedure to follow in washing the earmold, when replacing tubing on those hearing aids that use tubing, and in storing.
units.action_summary: Brochure must include instructions for accessory use and maintenance/care procedures.

units.section: § 801.422(c)(2)(v)(E) (Note about hearing loss in people younger than 18)
units.obligation_text: A person who is younger than 18 years old with hearing loss should have a medical evaluation by a licensed physician, preferably an ear specialist, before the purchase of a hearing aid.
units.action_summary: Recommends medical evaluation by a licensed physician for persons under 18 before purchasing a hearing aid.

title: Medical Devices; Immunology and Microbiology Devices; Classification of Human Leukocyte, Neutrophil and Platelet Antigen and Antibody Tests

units.obligation_text: HLA, HPA, and HNA typing devices must comply with the following special controls:
units.actor: manufacturers/sponsors of HLA, HPA, and HNA typing devices
units.action_summary: Devices are required to comply with specified special controls for Class II classification.

units.obligation_text: Premarket submissions must include detailed documentation of the following:
units.actor: the sponsor/applicant submitting the premarket submission
units.action_summary: Premarket submissions are required to include detailed documentation covering specified studies and materials.

units.obligation_text: Device accuracy study using well-characterized samples representing as many targets as possible.
units.action_summary: Include an accuracy study using well-characterized samples that represent as many targets as possible.

units.obligation_text: Precision studies to evaluate possible sources of variation that may affect test results.
units.action_summary: Include precision studies to assess sources of variation affecting test results.

units.obligation_text: Comparison studies to evaluate the device’s performance compared to a predicate.
units.action_summary: Provide comparison studies evaluating performance against a predicate device.

units.obligation_text: Specific information that addresses or mitigates risks associated with false positive antibody reactivity, e.g., reactivity with denatured/cryptic epitopes, if applicable.
units.action_summary: Provide information addressing or mitigating risks of false positive antibody reactivity (e.g., denatured/cryptic epitopes) if applicable.

units.obligation_text: Description of how the assay cutoff was established and validated as well as supporting data.
units.action_summary: Describe how assay cutoff was established and validated and provide supporting data.

units.obligation_text: Documentation for device software, including, but not limited to, software requirement specifications, software design specifications, e.g., algorithms, alarms, and device limitations; hazard analysis, traceability matrix, verification and validation testing, unresolved anomalies, hardware and software specifications; electromagnetic compatibility and wireless testing.
units.action_summary: Provide comprehensive software documentation (requirements, design, hazard analysis, V&V testing, EMC/wireless testing, etc.).

units.obligation_text: Design specifications that are in place to prevent incorrect reactivity assignment or multiplex assays in which large numbers of probes and/or primers are handled during manufacturing process.
units.action_summary: Include design specifications that prevent incorrect reactivity assignment, especially for multiplex assays with many probes/primers during manufacturing.

units.obligation_text: Description of a plan on how to ensure the performance characteristics of the device remain unchanged over time when new HLA alleles are identified and/or reactivity assignments are changed from the assignments at the time the device was evaluated.
units.action_summary: Provide a plan to ensure device performance remains unchanged over time as new HLA alleles are identified or reactivity assignments change.

units.obligation_text: The device labeling must include:
units.action_summary: Device labeling is required to contain specified statements.

units.obligation_text: A limitation statement that reads, "The results should not be used as the sole basis for making a clinical decision."
units.action_summary: Labeling must include a limitation stating results should not be the sole basis for clinical decisions.

units.obligation_text: A warning that reads "The device has not been cleared or approved for use as a companion diagnostic."
units.action_summary: Labeling must include a warning that the device has not been cleared or approved for use as a companion diagnostic.

title: Menu Labeling: Supplemental Guidance for Industry (Edition 2); Draft Guidance for Industry; Availability

units.obligation_text: Submit either electronic or written comments on the draft guidance by February 12, 2024 to ensure that we consider your comment on the draft guidance before we begin work on the final version of the guidance.
units.action_summary: Commenters must submit electronic or written comments on the draft guidance by February 12, 2024 for FDA to consider them before finalizing the guidance.

units.obligation_text: Submit electronic comments in the following way: Federal eRulemaking Portal: https://www.regulations.gov. Follow the instructions for submitting comments.
units.action_summary: Commenters using the Federal eRulemaking Portal must follow the portal's instructions when submitting electronic comments.

units.obligation_text: Comments submitted electronically, including attachments, to https://www.regulations.gov will be posted to the docket unchanged.
units.action_summary: FDA will post electronic comments and attachments to the docket unchanged.

units.obligation_text: Because your comment will be made public, you are solely responsible for ensuring that your comment does not include any confidential information that you or a third party may not wish to be posted, such as medical information, your or anyone else's Social Security number, or confidential business information, such as a manufacturing process.
units.action_summary: Commenters must ensure their publicly submitted comments do not contain confidential personal or business information they do not want posted.

units.obligation_text: If you want to submit a comment with confidential information that you do not wish to be made available to the public, submit the comment as a written/paper submission and in the manner detailed (see "Written/Paper Submissions" and "Instructions").
units.action_summary: Commenters who want confidential handling must submit their comments as written/paper submissions following the specified instructions.

units.obligation_text: Submit written/paper submissions as follows: Mail/Hand Delivery/Courier (for written/paper submissions): Dockets Management Staff (HFA-305), Food and Drug Administration, 5630 Fishers Lane, Rm. 1061, Rockville, MD 20852.
units.action_summary: Written/paper submissions (including confidential ones) must be submitted to the Dockets Management Staff at the specified address.

units.obligation_text: For written/paper comments submitted to the Dockets Management Staff, FDA will post your comment, as well as any attachments, except for information submitted, marked and identified, as confidential, if submitted as detailed in "Instructions."
units.action_summary: FDA will post written/paper comments and attachments to the docket, except information properly marked and submitted as confidential.

units.obligation_text: All submissions received must include the Docket No. FDA-2011-F-0172 for "Menu Labeling: Supplemental Guidance for Industry."
units.action_summary: Submitters are required to include the docket number FDA-2011-F-0172 with all submissions.

units.obligation_text: Received comments will be placed in the docket and, except for those submitted as "Confidential Submissions," publicly viewable at https://www.regulations.gov or at the Dockets Management Staff between 9 a.m. and 4 p.m., Monday through Friday, 240-402-7500.
units.action_summary: FDA will place received comments in the docket and make them publicly viewable unless they are properly submitted as confidential.

units.obligation_text: You may submit comments on any guidance at any time (see 21 CFR 10.115(g)(5)).
units.action_summary: Commenters are permitted to submit comments on any guidance at any time.

units.obligation_text: Submit written requests for single copies of the draft guidance to the Office of Nutrition and Food Labeling, Center for Food Safety and Applied Nutrition, Food and Drug Administration, 5001 Campus Dr., College Park, MD 20740. Send two self-addressed adhesive labels to assist that office in processing your request.
units.action_summary: Requesters must submit written requests for single copies of the draft guidance to the specified office and send two self-addressed adhesive labels.

units.obligation_text: Confidential Submissions--To submit a comment with confidential information that you do not wish to be made publicly available, submit your comments only as a written/paper submission. You should submit two copies total.
units.action_summary: To ensure confidentiality, commenters must submit confidential comments as written/paper submissions and are advised to provide two copies.

units.obligation_text: One copy will include the information you claim to be confidential with a heading or cover note that states "THIS DOCUMENT CONTAINS CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION." The second copy, which will have the claimed confidential information redacted/blacked out, will be available for public viewing and posted on https://www.regulations.gov. Submit both copies to the Dockets Management Staff.
units.action_summary: Submitters of confidential information must provide one unredacted copy labeled as confidential and one redacted copy for public viewing, and submit both to the Dockets Management Staff.

units.obligation_text: If you do not wish your name and contact information to be made publicly available, you can provide this information on the cover sheet and not in the body of your comments and you must identify this information as "confidential."
units.action_summary: Commenters may place contact information only on the cover sheet and must label it as confidential to avoid public disclosure.

units.obligation_text: Any information marked as "confidential" will not be disclosed except in accordance with 21 CFR 10.20 and other applicable disclosure law.
units.action_summary: FDA will not disclose information marked confidential except as allowed by applicable disclosure laws.

units.obligation_text: We will review this copy, including the claimed confidential information, in our consideration of comments.
units.action_summary: FDA will review the unredacted confidential copy when considering comments.

units.obligation_text: Section 3506(c)(2)(A) of the PRA requires Federal Agencies to publish a 60-day notice in the Federal Register for each proposed collection of information before submitting the collection to OMB for approval. To comply with this requirement, we will publish a 60-day notice of the proposed collection of information in a future issue of the Federal Register.
units.action_summary: FDA will publish a 60-day Federal Register notice for the proposed collection of information to comply with the PRA before submitting it to OMB.

title: FEMA’s Hazard Mitigation Assistance and Planning Regulations

units.obligation_text: Administer and provide oversight to all FEMA-related hazard mitigation programs and grants, including:
units.action_summary: FEMA must administer and oversee all FEMA-related hazard mitigation programs and grants.

units.obligation_text: Issue program implementation procedures, as necessary, which will include information on availability of funding;
units.action_summary: FEMA will issue program implementation procedures including funding availability information as needed.

units.obligation_text: Award all grants to the recipient after evaluating subaward applications for eligibility and ensuring compliance with applicable Federal laws, giving priority to such properties, or to the subset of such properties, as the Administrator may determine are in the best interest of the NFIF;
units.action_summary: FEMA will award grants to recipients after eligibility review and compliance checks, prioritizing properties as determined by the Administrator.

units.obligation_text: Provide technical assistance and training to State, local and Indian Tribal governments regarding the mitigation and grants management process;
units.action_summary: FEMA will provide technical assistance and training on mitigation and grant management to States, localities, and Tribes.

units.obligation_text: Review and approve State, Indian Tribal, and local mitigation plans in accordance with part 201 of this chapter;
units.action_summary: FEMA will review and approve mitigation plans under part 201.

units.obligation_text: Comply with applicable Federal statutory, regulatory, and Executive Order requirements related to environmental and historic preservation compliance, including reviewing and supplementing, if necessary, the environmental analyses conducted by the State and subrecipient in accordance with applicable laws, regulations, and agency policy;
units.action_summary: FEMA will comply with environmental and historic preservation requirements and may review/supplement state/subrecipient analyses.

units.obligation_text: Monitor implementation of awards through quarterly reports;
units.action_summary: FEMA will monitor award implementation via quarterly reports.

units.obligation_text: Review all closeout documentation for compliance and sending the recipient a request for additional supporting documentation, if needed.
units.action_summary: FEMA will review closeout docs and request more support if necessary.

units.obligation_text: The recipient must have working knowledge of NFIP goals, requirements, and processes and ensure that the program is coordinated with other mitigation activities.
units.action_summary: Recipients must understand NFIP goals and coordinate the program with other mitigation activities.

units.obligation_text: Have a FEMA approved Mitigation Plan in accordance with part 201 of this chapter;
units.action_summary: Recipients must have a FEMA-approved mitigation plan under part 201.

units.obligation_text: Provide technical assistance and training to communities on mitigation planning, mitigation project activities, developing subaward applications, and implementing approved subawards;
units.action_summary: Recipients will provide technical assistance and training to communities on mitigation planning and subawards.

units.obligation_text: Prioritize and recommend subaward applications to be approved by FEMA, based on the applicable mitigation plan(s), other evaluation criteria, and the eligibility criteria described in § 77.6;
units.action_summary: Recipients will prioritize and recommend subaward applications to FEMA based on plans and criteria.

units.obligation_text: Award FEMA-approved subawards;
units.action_summary: Recipients will award subawards that FEMA approves.

units.obligation_text: Monitor and evaluate the progress of the mitigation activity in accordance with the approved original scope of work and budget through quarterly reports;
units.action_summary: Recipients will monitor project progress per scope and budget via quarterly reports.

units.obligation_text: Closeout the subaward in accordance with 2 CFR 200.343 and 200.344, and applicable FEMA guidance;
units.action_summary: Recipients must closeout subawards per federal closeout rules and FEMA guidance.

units.obligation_text: Comply with program requirements under this part, grant management requirements identified under 2 CFR parts 200 and 3002, the grant agreement articles, and other applicable Federal, State, Tribal and local laws and regulations.
units.action_summary: Recipients must comply with program and grant management requirements and applicable laws.

units.obligation_text: Complete and submit subaward applications to the recipient for FMA planning and project subawards;
units.action_summary: Subrecipients must complete and submit subaward applications to the recipient.

units.obligation_text: Implement all approved subawards;
units.action_summary: Subrecipients must implement approved subawards.

units.obligation_text: Monitor and evaluate the progress of the mitigation activity in accordance with the approved original scope of work and budget through quarterly reports;
units.action_summary: Subrecipients must monitor and report project progress via quarterly reports.

units.obligation_text: Comply with program requirements under this part, grant management requirements identified under 2 CFR parts 200 and 3002, the grant agreement articles, and other applicable Federal, State, Tribal and local laws and regulations;
units.action_summary: Subrecipients must comply with program and grant requirements and laws.

units.obligation_text: Closeout the subaward in accordance with 2 CFR 200.343 and 200.344, and applicable FEMA guidance.
units.action_summary: Subrecipients must close out subawards per federal closeout rules and FEMA guidance.

units.obligation_text: For the amount made available for the FMA program, the Administrator will allocate the available funds based upon criteria established for each application period.
units.action_summary: The Administrator will allocate FMA funds according to established criteria for each application period.

units.obligation_text: The criteria may include the number of NFIP policies, severe repetitive loss structures, repetitive loss structures, and any other factors the Administrator determines are in the best interest of the NFIF.
units.action_summary: The Administrator may consider specified factors when allocating funds.

units.obligation_text: The amount of FMA funds used may not exceed $50,000 for any mitigation plan of a State or $25,000 for any mitigation plan of a community.
units.action_summary: FMA funds used for mitigation plans are limited to $50,000 for States and $25,000 for communities.

units.obligation_text: For each severe repetitive loss structure, FEMA may contribute either: (i) Up to 100 percent of all eligible costs if the activities are technically feasible and cost effective;
units.action_summary: FEMA may pay up to 100% of eligible costs for severe repetitive loss structures if technically feasible and cost-effective.

units.obligation_text: (ii) Up to the amount of the expected savings to the NFIP for acquisition or relocation activities;
units.action_summary: FEMA may contribute up to the expected NFIP savings amount for acquisition or relocation for severe repetitive loss structures.

units.obligation_text: For repetitive loss structures, FEMA may contribute up to 90 percent of the eligible costs;
units.action_summary: FEMA may pay up to 90% of eligible costs for repetitive loss structures.

units.obligation_text: For all other mitigation activities, FEMA may contribute up to 75 percent of all eligible costs.
units.action_summary: FEMA may cover up to 75% of eligible costs for other mitigation activities.

units.obligation_text: For projects that contain a combination of severe repetitive loss, repetitive loss, and/or other insured structures, the cost share will be calculated as appropriate for each type of structure submitted in the project subapplication.
units.action_summary: Cost share for mixed projects will be calculated appropriately for each structure type.

units.obligation_text: Any FMA application or subapplication that does not receive a Federal award within 5 years of the application/subapplication submission date is considered to be denied, and any funding amounts allocated for such applications/subapplications will be made available for other FMA awards and subawards.
units.action_summary: Applications not awarded within 5 years are considered denied and their funds reallocated.

units.obligation_text: Applicants will be notified of the availability of funding for the FMA program pursuant to 2 CFR 200.202 and 200.203.
units.action_summary: FEMA will notify applicants about FMA funding availability per 2 CFR requirements.

units.obligation_text: The applicant is responsible for soliciting applications from eligible communities, or subapplicants, and for reviewing and prioritizing applications prior to forwarding them to FEMA for review and award.
units.action_summary: Applicants must solicit, review, and prioritize subapplications before sending to FEMA.

units.obligation_text: Communities or other subapplicants who choose to apply must develop subapplications within the timeframes and requirements established by FEMA and must submit subapplications to the applicant.
units.action_summary: Subapplicants must develop and submit subapplications within FEMA-established timeframes and requirements.

units.obligation_text: States, Indian Tribal governments, and communities must be participating in the NFIP and may not be suspended or withdrawn under the program.
units.actor: States, Indian Tribal governments, and communities
units.action_summary: States, Tribes, and communities must participate in the NFIP and cannot be suspended or withdrawn.

units.obligation_text: For projects that impact individual structures ... an NFIP policy for the structure must be in effect prior to the opening of the application period and be maintained for the life of the structure.
units.action_summary: Structures impacted by projects must have an NFIP policy in effect before application opening and maintained for the structure's life.

units.obligation_text: States must have a FEMA-approved mitigation plan meeting the requirements of § 201.4 of this chapter ... The FEMA-approved mitigation plan is required at the time of application and award.
units.action_summary: States must have a FEMA-approved mitigation plan at application and award time meeting §201.4 requirements.

units.obligation_text: Indian Tribal governments must have a FEMA-approved mitigation plan meeting the requirements of § 201.7 of this chapter ... The FEMA-approved mitigation plan is required at the time of application and award.
units.action_summary: Indian Tribal governments must have a FEMA-approved mitigation plan at application and award time meeting §201.7 requirements.

units.obligation_text: To be eligible for FMA project grants, subapplicants must have an approved mitigation plan in accordance with part 201 of this chapter ... The FEMA-approved mitigation plan is required at the time of application and award.
units.action_summary: Subapplicants must have an approved mitigation plan under part 201 at application and award time to be eligible.

units.obligation_text: FMA planning grants may be used to develop or update State, Indian Tribal and/or local mitigation plans ...
units.action_summary: FMA planning grants may be used to develop or update mitigation plans meeting part 201 criteria.

units.obligation_text: Projects funded under the FMA program are limited to activities that reduce flood damages to properties insured under the NFIP.
units.action_summary: FMA-funded projects must reduce flood damage to NFIP-insured properties.

units.obligation_text: Applications involving any activities for which implementation has already been initiated or completed are not eligible for funding, and will not be considered.
units.action_summary: Activities started or completed before award are ineligible and won't be considered.

units.obligation_text: Acquisition of real property from property owners, and demolition or relocation of buildings and/or structures to areas outside of the floodplain to convert the property to open space use in perpetuity, in accordance with part 80 of this subchapter;
units.action_summary: Acquisition and conversion of property to open space outside the floodplain is an eligible activity.

units.obligation_text: Elevation of existing structures to at least base flood levels or higher, if required by FEMA or if required by any State or local ordinance, and in accordance with criteria established by the Administrator;
units.action_summary: Elevation of structures to base flood levels or higher (as required) is eligible.

units.obligation_text: Floodproofing of existing non-residential structures in accordance with the requirements of the NFIP or higher standards if required by FEMA or if required by any State or local ordinance, and in accordance with criteria established by the Administrator;
units.action_summary: Floodproofing of qualifying non-residential structures per NFIP or higher standards is eligible.

units.obligation_text: Floodproofing of historic structures as defined in § 59.1 of this subchapter;
units.action_summary: Floodproofing historic structures (per §59.1) is eligible.

units.obligation_text: Demolition and rebuilding of properties to at least base flood levels or higher, if required by FEMA or if required by any State or local ordinance, and in accordance with criteria established by the Administrator;
units.action_summary: Demolition and rebuilding to required flood elevations is eligible.

units.obligation_text: Localized flood risk reduction projects that lessen the frequency or severity of flooding and decrease predicted flood damages, and that do not duplicate the flood prevention activities of other Federal agencies. Non-localized flood risk reduction projects such as dikes, levees, floodwalls, seawalls, groins, jetties, dams and large-scale waterway channelization projects are not eligible;
units.action_summary: Localized flood risk reduction projects are eligible; large-scale/non-localized projects listed are ineligible.

units.obligation_text: Elevation, relocation, or floodproofing of utilities;
units.action_summary: Elevation, relocation, or floodproofing of utilities is eligible.

units.obligation_text: Other mitigation activities not described or identified in (c)(2)(i) through (vii) of this section that are described in the State, Tribal or local mitigation plan.
units.action_summary: Other mitigation activities described in approved mitigation plans may be eligible.

units.obligation_text: If a recipient applied for and was awarded at least $1 million in the prior fiscal year, that recipient may be eligible to receive a technical assistance grant for up to $50,000.
units.action_summary: Recipients awarded $1M+ prior year may be eligible for up to $50,000 in technical assistance grants.

units.obligation_text: In addition to being an eligible project type, mitigation grant projects must also:
units.action_summary: Mitigation grant projects must meet additional minimum criteria listed.

units.obligation_text: Be in conformance with State, Tribal and/or local mitigation plans approved under part 201 of this chapter for the jurisdiction where the project is located;
units.action_summary: Projects must conform to approved mitigation plans for the jurisdiction.

units.obligation_text: Be in conformance with applicable environmental and historic preservation laws, regulations, and agency policy, including parts 9 and 60 of this chapter, and other applicable Federal, State, Tribal, and local laws and regulations;
units.action_summary: Projects must comply with environmental and historic preservation laws and policies.

units.obligation_text: Be technically feasible and cost-effective; or, eliminate future payments from the NFIF for severe repetitive loss structures through an acquisition or relocation activity;
units.action_summary: Projects must be technically feasible and cost-effective, or eliminate future NFIF payments via acquisition/relocation for severe repetitive loss structures.

units.obligation_text: Solve a problem independently, or constitute a functional portion of a long-term solution where there is assurance that the project as a whole will be completed. This assurance will include documentation identifying the remaining funds necessary to complete the project, and the timeframe for completing the project;
units.action_summary: Projects must solve a problem independently or be part of a long-term solution with documented assurance of completion including funds and timeline.

units.obligation_text: Consider long-term changes to the areas and entities it protects, and have manageable future maintenance and modification requirements. The subrecipient is responsible for the continued maintenance needed to preserve the hazard mitigation benefits of these measures;
units.action_summary: Projects must account for long-term changes and be maintainable; subrecipients are responsible for ongoing maintenance.

units.obligation_text: Not duplicate benefits available from another source for the same purpose or assistance that another Federal agency or program has more primary authority to provide.
units.action_summary: Projects must not duplicate benefits available from other sources or more primary Federal programs.

units.obligation_text: Recipients are eligible to receive management costs consisting of a maximum of 10 percent of the planning and project activities awarded to the recipient, each fiscal year under FMA. These costs must be included in the application to FEMA.
units.action_summary: Recipients may receive management costs up to 10% and must include those costs in the FEMA application.

units.obligation_text: Subapplicants may include a maximum of 5 percent of the total funds requested for their subapplication for management costs to support the implementation of their planning or project activity. These costs must be included in the subapplication to the recipient.
units.action_summary: Subapplicants may include up to 5% for management costs and must include them in the subapplication.

units.obligation_text: Indirect costs of administering the FMA program are eligible as part of the 10 percent management costs for the recipient or the 5 percent management costs of the subrecipient, but in no case do they make the recipient eligible for additional management costs that exceed the caps identified in paragraph (a)(1) of this section. units.obligation_text: FEMA may fund eligible pre-award costs related to developing the application or subapplication at its discretion and as funds are available. units.obligation_text: At the time of closeout, FEMA will recapture any funds provided to a State or a community under this part if the applicant has not provided the appropriate matching funds, the approved project has not been completed within the timeframes specified in the grant agreement, or the completed project does not meet the criteria specified in this part.

Requests for reconsideration must be made in writing to FEMA within 60 calendar days after receipt of a notice of the action, and in accordance with submission procedures set out in guidance. FEMA will notify the requester of the disposition of the request for reconsideration. If the decision is to grant the request for reconsideration, FEMA will take appropriate implementing action.
units.action_summary: Requesters must file reconsideration requests in writing within 60 days; FEMA will reconsider, notify the requester, and take implementing action if granted.

units.obligation_text: FEMA may fund eligible pre-award project costs at its discretion and as funds are available. Recipients and subrecipients may be reimbursed for eligible pre-award costs for activities directly related to the development of the project proposal. These costs can only be incurred during the open application period of the respective grant program. Costs associated with implementation of the project but incurred prior to grant award are not eligible. Therefore, activities where implementation is initiated or completed prior to award are not eligible and will not be reimbursed.
units.action_summary: FEMA may fund eligible pre-award project costs; recipients/subrecipients may be reimbursed for pre-award costs incurred during the open application period; implementation costs before award are ineligible.
units.modal_raw: may; may be; can only; are not eligible; will not

units.obligation_text: Grant funds may not duplicate benefits received by or available to applicants, subapplicants and other project participants from insurance, other assistance programs, legal awards, or any other source to address the same purpose. Such individual or entity must notify the subapplicant and FEMA of all benefits that it receives, anticipates, or has available from other sources for the same purpose. FEMA will reduce the subaward by the amounts available for the same purpose from another source.
units.action_summary: Grant funds must not duplicate other benefits; individuals/entities must notify subapplicant and FEMA of other benefits; FEMA will reduce subawards by amounts available from other sources.

units.obligation_text: Eligible acquisition projects are those where the property owner participates voluntarily, and the recipient/subrecipient will not use its eminent domain authority to acquire the property for the open space purposes should negotiations fail.
units.action_summary: Property owner participation must be voluntary; recipients/subrecipients will not use eminent domain to acquire property for open space if negotiations fail.

units.obligation_text: The deed restriction language, which must be consistent with the FEMA model deed restriction that the local government will record with the property deeds. Any variation from the model deed restriction language can only be made with prior approval from FEMA’s Office of Chief Counsel;
units.actor: Local government/Subrecipient; FEMA Office of Chief Counsel
units.action_summary: Deed restrictions must match FEMA model deed restriction and be recorded by local government; variations require prior approval from FEMA Office of Chief Counsel.

units.obligation_text: The subrecipient must take steps to ensure it does not acquire or include in the project properties contaminated with hazardous materials by seeking information from property owners and from other sources on the use and presence of contaminants affecting the property from owners of properties that are or were industrial or commercial, or adjacent to such. A contaminated property must be certified clean prior to participation. This excludes permitted disposal of incidental demolition and household hazardous wastes. FEMA mitigation grant funds may not be used for clean up or remediation of contaminated properties.
units.action_summary: Subrecipients must avoid acquiring contaminated properties by seeking contamination info; contaminated properties must be certified clean before participation; FEMA funds may not be used for cleanup/remediation.

units.obligation_text: The subrecipient will obtain a title insurance policy demonstrating that fee title conveys to the subrecipient for each property to ensure that it acquires only a property with clear title. The property interest generally must transfer by a general warranty deed. Any incompatible easements or other encumbrances to the property must be extinguished before acquisition.
units.action_summary: Subrecipients must obtain title insurance and ensure fee title transfers by general warranty deed; incompatible easements/encumbrances must be extinguished before acquisition.

units.obligation_text: A property owner who did not own the property at the time of the relevant event, or who is not a National of the United States or qualified alien, is not eligible for a purchase offer based on pre-event market value of the property. Subrecipients who offer pre-event market value to the property owner must have already obtained certification during the application process that the property owner is either a National of the United States or a qualified alien.
units.action_summary: Property owners who didn't own at relevant event or are not nationals/qualified aliens are ineligible for pre-event market value offers; subrecipients must have certified the owner's status if offering pre-event value.

units.obligation_text: Certain tenants who must relocate as a result of the project are entitled to relocation benefits under the Uniform Relocation Assistance and Real Property Acquisition Act ... in accordance with 49 CFR part 24.
units.action_summary: Tenants forced to relocate are entitled to relocation benefits per URA and 49 CFR part 24.

units.obligation_text: If a purchase offer for a residential property is less than the cost of the homeowner-occupant to purchase a comparable replacement dwelling outside the hazard-prone area in the same community, subrecipients for mitigation grant programs may make such a payment available in accordance with criteria determined by the Administrator.
units.action_summary: Subrecipients may provide additional payment when purchase offers are insufficient to purchase comparable replacement housing, per Administrator criteria.

units.obligation_text: The subrecipient must inform each property owner, in writing, of what it considers to be the market value of the property, the method of valuation and basis for the purchase offer, and the final offer amount. The offer will also clearly state that the property owner’s participation in the project is voluntary.
units.action_summary: Subrecipients must notify property owners in writing of valuation, basis, final offer amount, and that participation is voluntary.

units.obligation_text: Existing incompatible facilities must be removed by demolition or by relocation outside of the hazard area within 90 days of settlement of the property transaction. The FEMA Regional Administrator may grant an exception to this deadline only for a particular property based upon written justification if extenuating circumstances exist, but will specify a final date for removal.
units.action_summary: Incompatible facilities must be removed within 90 days of settlement; the Regional Administrator may grant exceptions in writing and will set a final removal date.

units.obligation_text: The subrecipient, upon settlement of the property transaction, must record with the deed of the subject property notice of applicable land use restrictions and related procedures described in this part, consistent with FEMA model deed restriction language.
units.action_summary: Upon settlement, subrecipients must record deed notices of applicable land use restrictions consistent with FEMA model language.

units.obligation_text: The property must be dedicated and maintained in perpetuity as open space for the conservation of natural floodplain functions.
units.action_summary: Property must be dedicated and maintained forever as open space to conserve floodplain functions.

units.obligation_text: Any improvements on the property must be in accordance with proper floodplain management policies and practices. Structures built on the property according to paragraph (a)(2) of this section must be floodproofed or elevated to at least the base flood level plus 1 foot of freeboard, or greater, if required by FEMA, or if required by any State or local ordinance, and in accordance with criteria established by the Administrator.
units.action_summary: Improvements must follow floodplain management policies; structures must be floodproofed or elevated to specified levels per FEMA/ordinance and Administrator criteria.

units.obligation_text: After acquiring the property interest, the subrecipient, including successors in interest, will convey any interest in the property only if the Regional Administrator, through the State, gives prior written approval of the transferee in accordance with this paragraph.
units.action_summary: Subrecipients may convey property interests only with prior written approval of the transferee by the Regional Administrator through the State.

units.obligation_text: The request by the subrecipient, through the State, to the Regional Administrator must include a signed statement from the proposed transferee that it acknowledges and agrees to be bound by the terms of this section, and documentation of its status as a qualified conservation organization if applicable.
units.action_summary: Subrecipients' requests must include a signed transferee statement agreeing to terms and documentation of conservation status if applicable.

units.obligation_text: The subrecipient may convey a property interest only to a public entity or to a qualified conservation organization. However, the subrecipient may convey an easement or lease to a private individual or entity for purposes compatible with the uses described in paragraph (a) of this section, with the prior approval of the Regional Administrator, and so long as the conveyance does not include authority to control and enforce the terms and conditions of this section.
units.action_summary: Subrecipients may convey property only to public entities or qualified conservation organizations; easements/leases to private parties allowed with prior Regional Administrator approval and without enforcement authority.

units.obligation_text: If title to the property is transferred to a public entity other than one with a conservation mission, it must be conveyed subject to a conservation easement that must be recorded with the deed and must incorporate all terms and conditions set forth in this section, including the easement holder’s responsibility to enforce the easement.
units.action_summary: If transferred to a non-conservation public entity, the transfer must include a recorded conservation easement incorporating all terms and enforcement responsibilities.

units.obligation_text: Conveyance of any property interest must reference and incorporate the original deed restrictions providing notice of the conditions in this section and must incorporate a provision for the property interest to revert to the subrecipient or recipient in the event that the transferee ceases to exist or loses its eligible status under this section.
units.action_summary: All conveyances must include and reference original deed restrictions and a reversion provision if transferee ceases/exits eligible status.

units.obligation_text: FEMA, its representatives and assigns, including the recipient will have the right to enter upon the property, at reasonable times and with reasonable notice, for the purpose of inspecting the property to ensure compliance with the terms of this part, the property conveyance and of the grant award.
units.actor: FEMA, its representatives and assigns, including the recipient
units.action_summary: FEMA, its reps, and the recipient have the right to inspect the property with reasonable notice to ensure compliance.

units.obligation_text: Every 3 years the subrecipient (in coordination with any current successor in interest) through the recipient, must submit to the FEMA Regional Administrator a report certifying that the subrecipient has inspected the property within the month preceding the report,
units.action_summary: Every three years, subrecipients must submit a certification to the FEMA Regional Administrator that the property was inspected within the prior month.

title: Revisions to Publication Requirements for Community Eligibility Status Information Under the National Flood Insurance Program

units.obligation_text: If, subsequently, copies of adequate flood plain management regulations are not received by the Administrator, no later than 30 days before the expiration of the original six month period the Federal Insurance Administrator shall provide written notice to the community and to the state and assure publication of the community’s loss of eligibility for the sale of flood insurance on the internet or by another comparable method, such suspension to become effective upon the expiration of the six month period.
units.action_summary: If required regulations are not received, the Federal Insurance Administrator must provide written notice to the community and state and ensure publication of the community's loss of eligibility; the suspension becomes effective at the six-month expiration.

units.obligation_text: If, subsequently, copies of adequate flood plain management regulations are not received by the Administrator
units.action_summary: Condition triggering the obligation when required regulations are not received by the Administrator.

units.obligation_text: no later than 30 days before the expiration of the original six month period the Federal Insurance Administrator shall provide written notice to the community and to the state

units.obligation_text: no later than 30 days before the expiration of the original six month period the Federal Insurance Administrator shall ... assure publication of the community’s loss of eligibility for the sale of flood insurance on the internet or by another comparable method
units.action_summary: Ensure publication of the community's loss of eligibility on the internet or by a comparable method no later than 30 days before expiration.

units.action_summary: When a community is to be suspended, the Federal Insurance Administrator must inform the community, providing 30 days prior written notice and informing upon publication of the loss of eligibility online or by a comparable method.

units.action_summary: When a community is to be suspended, the Federal Insurance Administrator must inform the community with 30 days prior written notice and upon publication of the loss of eligibility online or by a comparable method.

units.action_summary: When a certified copy of final legislative action is received, the Federal Insurance Administrator must withdraw the community from the Program and publish its loss of eligibility online or by a comparable method.
