units.action_summary: Publish the community's loss of eligibility on the internet or by a comparable method.

units.obligation_text: FEMA will maintain a list of communities eligible for the sale of flood insurance pursuant to the National Flood Insurance Program (42 U.S.C. 4001–4128).
units.action_summary: FEMA is to maintain a list of communities eligible for NFIP flood insurance.

units.obligation_text: This list will be published and maintained on the internet or through another comparable method.
units.action_summary: Publish and maintain the eligible-communities list on the internet or by a comparable method.

title: National Environmental Policy Act Compliance

units.obligation_text: This part applies to all organizational elements of the Forest Service.
units.actor: all organizational elements of the Forest Service
units.action_summary: The part is applicable to every organizational element of the Forest Service.

units.obligation_text: Consistent with 40 CFR 1500.3, no trivial violation of this part shall give rise to any independent cause of action.
units.action_summary: Trivial violations will not create an independent cause of action.

units.obligation_text: This part supplements and does not lessen the applicability of the CEQ regulations, and is to be used in conjunction with the CEQ regulations and USDA regulations at 7 CFR part 1b.
units.actor: users of this part / Forest Service
units.action_summary: This part must be used together with CEQ and USDA regulations and does not reduce their applicability.

units.obligation_text: As required by 42 U.S.C. 4321 et seq., a Forest Service proposal is subject to the NEPA requirements when all of the following apply:
units.action_summary: A Forest Service proposal must comply with NEPA when the listed criteria are met.

units.obligation_text: The Forest Service has a goal and is actively preparing to make a decision on one or more alternative means of accomplishing that goal and the effects can be meaningfully evaluated (see 40 CFR 1508.23);
units.action_summary: Condition: the agency has a goal and is preparing to decide among alternatives with effects that can be meaningfully evaluated.

units.obligation_text: The proposed action is subject to Forest Service control and responsibility (see 40 CFR 1508.18);
units.action_summary: Condition: the action must be under Forest Service control and responsibility.

units.obligation_text: The proposed action would cause effects on the natural and physical environment and the relationship of people with that environment (see 40 CFR 1508.14);
units.action_summary: Condition: the action would have environmental effects.

units.obligation_text: The proposed action is not statutorily exempt from the requirements of section 102(2)(C) of the NEPA (42 U.S.C. 4332(2)(C)).
units.action_summary: Condition: the action must not be statutorily exempt from NEPA section 102(2)(C).

units.obligation_text: When the responsible official determines that an emergency exists that makes it necessary to take urgently needed actions before preparing a NEPA analysis and any required documentation in accordance with the provisions in §§ 220.5, 220.6, and 220.7 of this part, then the following provisions apply.
units.action_summary: If the responsible official determines an emergency exists requiring urgent action before NEPA analysis, the emergency provisions in this section apply.

units.obligation_text: The responsible official may take actions necessary to control the immediate impacts of the emergency and are urgently needed to mitigate harm to life, property, or important natural or cultural resources.
units.action_summary: The responsible official is permitted to take urgent actions to control immediate emergency impacts to protect life, property, or resources.

units.obligation_text: When taking such actions, the responsible official shall take into account the probable environmental consequences of the emergency action and mitigate foreseeable adverse environmental effects to the extent practicable.
units.action_summary: When taking emergency actions, the responsible official must consider environmental consequences and mitigate foreseeable adverse effects as practicable.

units.obligation_text: If the responsible official proposes emergency actions other than those actions described in paragraph (b)(1) of this section, and such actions are not likely to have significant environmental impacts, the responsible official shall document that determination in an EA and FONSI prepared in accord with these regulations.
units.action_summary: If non-(b)(1) emergency actions are not likely to have significant impacts, the responsible official must document that finding in an EA and FONSI.

units.obligation_text: If the responsible official finds that the nature and scope of proposed emergency actions are such that they must be undertaken prior to preparing any NEPA analysis and documentation associated with a CE or an EA and FONSI, the responsible official shall consult with the Washington Office about alternative arrangements for NEPA compliance.
units.action_summary: If emergency actions must proceed before NEPA analysis, the responsible official must consult with the Washington Office about alternative NEPA arrangements.

units.obligation_text: The Chief or Associate Chief of the Forest Service may grant emergency alternative arrangements under NEPA for environmental assessments, findings of no significant impact and categorical exclusions (FSM 1950.41a).
units.actor: The Chief or Associate Chief of the Forest Service
units.action_summary: The Chief or Associate Chief may authorize alternative NEPA arrangements for emergencies.

units.obligation_text: Consultation with the Washington Office shall be coordinated through the appropriate regional office.
units.action_summary: Consultations with the Washington Office must be coordinated through the appropriate regional office.

units.obligation_text: If the responsible official proposes emergency actions other than those actions described in paragraph (b)(1) of this section and such actions are likely to have significant environmental impacts, then the responsible official shall consult with CEQ, through the appropriate regional office and the Washington Office, about alternative arrangements in accordance with CEQ regulations at 40 CFR 1506.11 as soon as possible.
units.action_summary: If emergency actions are likely to have significant impacts, the responsible official must promptly consult with CEQ (through regional and Washington offices) about alternative arrangements.

units.obligation_text: For each Forest Service proposal (§ 220.4(a)), the responsible official shall coordinate and integrate NEPA review and relevant environmental documents with agency decisionmaking by:
units.action_summary: The responsible official must integrate NEPA review and relevant environmental documents into agency decisionmaking for each proposal.

units.obligation_text: Leading the proposal development and environmental analysis process, to ensure a focused approach;
units.action_summary: Lead development of the proposal and environmental analysis to keep the process focused.

units.obligation_text: Completing the environmental document review before making a decision on the proposal;
units.action_summary: Complete review of environmental documents prior to deciding on the proposal.

units.obligation_text: Considering environmental documents, public and other agency comments (if any) on those documents, and agency responses to those comments;
units.action_summary: Take into account environmental documents and public/agency comments and responses.

units.obligation_text: Including environmental documents, comments, and responses in the administrative record;
units.action_summary: Include environmental documents, comments, and responses in the administrative record.

units.obligation_text: Considering the alternatives analyzed in environmental document(s) before rendering a decision on the proposal;
units.action_summary: Consider analyzed alternatives prior to making a decision.

units.obligation_text: Making a decision encompassed within the range of alternatives analyzed in the environmental documents.
units.action_summary: Ensure decisions fall within the range of analyzed alternatives.

units.obligation_text: Minimum requirements for scoping and public notice are listed below, except where specified by applicable statutes or regulations (for example, 36 CFR part 218). Additional public involvement is at the discretion of the local responsible official.
units.action_summary: Local responsible official may decide on additional public involvement beyond minimum requirements.

units.obligation_text: The Forest Service will publish to the Schedule of Proposed Actions (SOPA) all proposed actions that will be documented with a decision memo, environmental assessment, or environmental impact statement.
units.action_summary: Publish all proposed actions that will be documented in decision memos, EAs, or EISs to the SOPA.

units.obligation_text: The local responsible official shall ensure the SOPA is updated
units.action_summary: Ensure the SOPA is kept current.

units.obligation_text: The local responsible official shall notify the public of the availability of the SOPA.
units.action_summary: Notify the public that the SOPA is available.

units.obligation_text: Scoping is required for all Forest Service environmental impact statements (40 CFR 1501.7).
units.action_summary: Scoping must be performed for all Forest Service EISs.

units.obligation_text: Cumulative effects analysis shall be carried out in accordance with 40 CFR 1508.7 and in accordance with "The Council on Environmental Quality Guidance Memorandum on Consideration of Past Actions in Cumulative Effects Analysis" dated June 24, 2005.
units.action_summary: Carry out cumulative effects analysis consistent with 40 CFR 1508.7 and CEQ guidance.

units.obligation_text: With respect to past actions, during the public involvement process and subsequent preparation of the analysis, the agency must determine what information regarding past actions is useful and relevant to the required analysis of cumulative effects.
units.action_summary: Determine which information on past actions is relevant and useful for cumulative effects analysis.

units.obligation_text: To the extent practicable, the responsible official shall segregate any information that has been classified pursuant to Executive order or statute.
units.action_summary: Segregate classified information from analysis documents where practicable.

units.obligation_text: The responsible official shall maintain the confidentiality of such information in a manner required for the information involved.
units.action_summary: Maintain confidentiality of classified information according to requirements.

units.obligation_text: Such information may not be included in any publicly disclosed documents.
units.action_summary: Classified information must not appear in publicly disclosed documents.

units.obligation_text: If such material cannot be reasonably segregated, or if segregation would leave essentially meaningless material, the responsible official must withhold the entire analysis document from the public; however, the responsible official shall otherwise prepare the analysis documentation in accord with applicable regulations.
units.action_summary: If classified material cannot be segregated, withhold the entire analysis from the public and otherwise prepare documentation per regulations.

units.obligation_text: Material may be incorporated by reference into any environmental or decision document.
units.action_summary: Materials can be incorporated by reference into environmental or decision documents.

units.obligation_text: This material must be reasonably available to the public and its contents briefly described in the environmental or decision document.
units.action_summary: Ensure incorporated-by-reference material is reasonably available to the public and briefly described in documents.

units.obligation_text: The responsible official shall make policies or staff available to advise potential applicants of studies or other information foreseeably required for acceptance of their applications.
units.action_summary: Provide policies or staff to advise prospective applicants about required studies/information.

units.obligation_text: Upon acceptance of an application as provided by 36 CFR 251.54(g) the responsible official shall initiate the NEPA process.
units.action_summary: Start the NEPA process once an application is accepted per 36 CFR 251.54(g).

units.obligation_text: In making this determination, the responsible official shall evaluate:
units.action_summary: The responsible official must evaluate whether prior NEPA analysis suffices for a new action.

units.obligation_text: Is the new proposed action essentially similar to a previously analyzed proposed action or alternative analyzed in detail in previous NEPA analysis?
units.action_summary: Evaluate whether the new action is essentially similar to a previously analyzed action.

units.obligation_text: Is the range of alternatives previously analyzed adequate under present circumstances?
units.action_summary: Evaluate adequacy of previously analyzed alternatives under current circumstances.

units.obligation_text: Is there any significant new information or circumstances relevant to environmental concerns that would substantially change the analysis in the existing NEPA document(s)?
units.action_summary: Assess whether new information or circumstances would substantially change previous NEPA analysis.

units.obligation_text: Are the direct, indirect, and cumulative effects that would result from implementation of the new proposed action similar (both quantitatively and qualitatively) to those analyzed in the existing NEPA document(s)?
units.action_summary: Compare projected effects of the new action with those analyzed in existing NEPA documents.

units.obligation_text: A DNA for a new proposed action shall be included in the project record for the new proposed project or activity.
units.action_summary: Include Determination of NEPA Adequacy (DNA) in the project record for the new project/activity.

units.obligation_text: New project and activity decisions made in reliance on a DNA shall be subject to all applicable notice, comment, and administrative review processes.
units.action_summary: Decisions relying on a DNA must undergo applicable notice, comment, and administrative review processes.

units.obligation_text: The proposed action and any alternatives to the proposed action may include adaptive management.
units.actor: the proposed action and any alternatives
units.action_summary: Adaptive management may be included in proposed actions and alternatives.

units.obligation_text: An adaptive management proposal or alternative must clearly identify the adjustment(s) that may be made when monitoring during project implementation indicates that the action is not having its intended effect, or is causing unintended and undesirable effects.
units.actor: an adaptive management proposal or alternative
units.action_summary: Adaptive management proposals must identify possible adjustments triggered by monitoring findings.

units.obligation_text: The NEPA analysis must disclose not only the effect of the proposed action or alternative but also the effect of the adjustment.
units.action_summary: NEPA analyses must disclose effects of both the action and any adaptive adjustments.

units.obligation_text: Such proposal or alternative must also describe the monitoring that would take place to inform the responsible official during implementation whether the action is having its intended effect.
units.actor: the adaptive management proposal or alternative
units.action_summary: The proposal must describe monitoring that will inform responsible official about action effectiveness.

units.obligation_text: The proposed action and any alternatives may include condition-based management.
units.actor: the proposed action and any alternatives
units.action_summary: Condition-based management may be included in proposed actions and alternatives.

units.obligation_text: A condition-based management alternative must clearly identify the management actions that will be undertaken, and any design elements that will be implemented, when a certain set or range of conditions are present.
units.action_summary: Condition-based alternatives must specify actions and design elements tied to triggering conditions.

units.obligation_text: The NEPA analysis must disclose the effects of all condition-based actions, taking into account design elements that limit such actions.
units.action_summary: NEPA analyses must disclose effects of condition-based actions, considering limiting design elements.

units.obligation_text: Such proposal or alternative must also describe the process by which conditions will be validated prior to implementation.
units.action_summary: Describe process to validate triggering conditions before implementation.

units.obligation_text: The responsible official shall prepare supplements to either draft or final environmental impact statements (40 CFR 1502.9(c) or environmental assessments if:
units.action_summary: Prepare supplemental EISs or EAs under specified conditions.

units.obligation_text: The agency makes substantial changes in the proposed action that are relevant to environmental concerns;
units.action_summary: Prepare a supplement if the agency makes substantial, environmentally relevant changes to the proposed action.

units.obligation_text: There are significant new circumstances or information relevant to environmental concerns and bearing on the proposed action or its impacts and there remains Federal action to occur.
units.action_summary: Prepare a supplement if significant new circumstances or information arise and federal action remains.

units.obligation_text: The responsible official may prepare a supplemental information report to document the review of potentially significant new circumstances or information.
units.action_summary: The responsible official may prepare a supplemental information report to document review of new circumstances/information.

units.obligation_text: If a supplemental information report is prepared, it shall be included in the project record.
units.action_summary: If prepared, include the supplemental information report in the project record.

units.obligation_text: A proposed action may be categorically excluded from analysis and documentation in an EA or EIS when there are no extraordinary circumstances related to the proposed action, and the proposed action is within one or more of the categories listed at 7 CFR part 1b.3 or 36 CFR 220.5(d) or (e).
units.action_summary: Proposed actions meeting criteria and lacking extraordinary circumstances may be categorically excluded from EA/EIS analysis/documentation.

units.obligation_text: Resource conditions that should be considered in determining whether extraordinary circumstances related to a proposed action warrant analysis and documentation in an EA or an EIS are:
units.action_summary: Identify resource conditions to consider when determining if extraordinary circumstances require EA/EIS.

units.obligation_text: Federally listed threatened or endangered species or designated critical habitat and species proposed for Federal listing or proposed critical habitat;
units.action_summary: Consider presence of listed or proposed threatened/endangered species or critical habitat when evaluating extraordinary circumstances.

units.obligation_text: Flood plains, wetlands, or municipal watersheds;
units.action_summary: Consider floodplains, wetlands, and municipal watersheds when evaluating extraordinary circumstances.

units.obligation_text: Congressionally designated areas, such as wilderness, wilderness study areas, potential wilderness areas, wild and scenic rivers, or national recreation areas;
units.action_summary: Consider congressionally designated areas in extraordinary-circumstance determinations.

units.obligation_text: Roadless areas designated under 36 CFR part 294;
units.action_summary: Consider roadless areas under 36 CFR part 294 in extraordinary-circumstance evaluations.

units.obligation_text: Research natural areas;
units.action_summary: Consider research natural areas when determining extraordinary circumstances.

units.obligation_text: American Indian and Alaska Native religious or cultural sites;
units.action_summary: Consider American Indian and Alaska Native religious or cultural sites in the evaluation.

units.obligation_text: Archaeological sites, or historic properties or areas.
units.action_summary: Consider archaeological sites and historic properties in determining extraordinary circumstances.

units.obligation_text: Extraordinary circumstances exist when there is a cause-and-effect relationship between a proposed action and listed resource conditions and the responsible official determines that there is a likelihood of substantial adverse effects.
units.action_summary: Responsible official must determine extraordinary circumstances exist if a proposed action likely causes substantial adverse effects on listed resource conditions.

units.obligation_text: The responsible official may consider whether long-term beneficial effects outweigh short-term adverse effects in making this determination.
units.action_summary: Responsible official is permitted to weigh long-term benefits against short-term adverse effects when determining extraordinary circumstances.

units.obligation_text: In addition to public notice in the SOPA, as required at 220.4(d), the responsible official may choose to conduct additional public engagement activities to involve key stakeholders and interested parties.
units.action_summary: Responsible official may conduct additional public engagement beyond SOPA notice to involve stakeholders.

units.obligation_text: This additional involvement shall be conducted commensurate with the nature of the decision to be made.
units.action_summary: Any additional public involvement must be proportionate to the decision's nature.

units.obligation_text: A supporting record and a decision memo are not required, but at the discretion of the responsible official, may be prepared for the following categories:
units.action_summary: Project/case file and decision memo are not required for listed categories, but the responsible official may prepare them at discretion.

units.obligation_text: The applicant or holder must be in compliance with all the terms and conditions of the existing or expired special use authorization.
units.action_summary: Applicants or holders must comply with all terms and conditions of the prior special use authorization to qualify for clerical replacement issuance.

units.obligation_text: A supporting record is required and the decision to proceed must be documented in a decision memo for the categories of action in paragraph (e)(1) through (28) of this section.
units.action_summary: For the listed categories, prepare a supporting record and document the decision to proceed in a decision memo.

units.obligation_text: Post-fire rehabilitation activities, not to exceed 4,200 acres (such as tree planting, fence replacement, habitat restoration, heritage site restoration, repair of roads and trails, and repair of damage to minor facilities such as campgrounds), to repair or improve lands unlikely to recover to a management approved condition from wildland fire damage, or to repair or replace minor facilities damaged by fire. Such activities:
units.action_summary: Post-fire rehabilitation activities are authorized subject to the following constraints.

units.obligation_text: Shall be conducted consistent with Agency and Departmental procedures and applicable land and resource management plans;
units.actor: those post-fire rehabilitation activities / responsible official
units.action_summary: Post-fire rehabilitation activities must conform to Agency/Department procedures and applicable plans.

units.obligation_text: Shall not include the use of herbicides or pesticides or the construction of new permanent roads or other new permanent infrastructure;
units.actor: those post-fire rehabilitation activities / responsible official
units.action_summary: Post-fire rehabilitation activities are prohibited from using herbicides/pesticides or building new permanent roads/infrastructure.

units.obligation_text: Shall be completed within 3 years following a wildland fire.
units.actor: those post-fire rehabilitation activities / responsible official
units.action_summary: Post-fire rehabilitation activities must be finished within three years after the fire.

units.obligation_text: Harvest of live trees not to exceed 70 acres, requiring no more than 1/2 mile of temporary road construction. Do not use this category for even-aged regeneration harvest or vegetation type conversion.
units.action_summary: Harvest of live trees is limited to 70 acres and up to 1/2 mile of temporary road; cannot be used for even-aged regeneration or type conversion.

units.obligation_text: Removal of individual trees for sawlogs, specialty products, or fuelwood,
units.action_summary: Example actions allowed under the category include removal of individual trees for sawlogs, specialty products, or fuelwood.

units.obligation_text: Commercial thinning of overstocked stands to achieve the desired stocking level to increase health and vigor.
units.action_summary: Commercial thinning to improve stand health is an example of allowed activity under this category.

units.obligation_text: Salvage of dead and/or dying trees not to exceed 250 acres, requiring no more than 1/2 mile of temporary road construction.
units.action_summary: Salvage harvests are limited to 250 acres and up to 1/2 mile of temporary road construction.

units.obligation_text: Harvest of a portion of a stand damaged by a wind or ice event and construction of a short temporary road to access the damaged trees,
units.action_summary: Example allowed salvage activity: harvest damaged stand portion and build short temporary access road.

units.obligation_text: Harvest of fire-damaged trees.
units.action_summary: Example allowed salvage activity: harvest fire-damaged trees.

units.obligation_text: Commercial and non-commercial sanitation harvest of trees to control insects or disease not to exceed 250 acres, requiring no more than 1/2 mile of temporary road construction, including removal of infested/infected trees and adjacent live uninfested/uninfected trees as determined necessary to control the spread of insects or disease.
units.action_summary: Sanitation harvests for insect/disease control limited to 250 acres and up to 1/2 mile temporary road; may include adjacent tree removal as necessary.

units.obligation_text: Plan amendments developed in accordance with 36 CFR part 219 et seq. that provide broad guidance and information for project and activity decisionmaking in a NFS unit. Proposals for actions that approve projects and activities, or that command anyone to refrain from undertaking projects and activities, or that grant, withhold or modify contracts, permits or other formal legal instruments, are outside the scope of this category and shall be considered separately under Forest Service NEPA procedures.
units.actor: proposals that approve or command or grant/withhold/modify legal instruments / Forest Service
units.action_summary: Plan amendments providing broad guidance are within this category, but proposals that approve/compel/alter legal rights or instruments are excluded and must be considered separately under NEPA procedures.
units.modal_raw: are outside the scope ... and shall be considered separately

units.obligation_text: Approval of a Surface Use Plan of Operations for oil and natural gas exploration and initial development activities, associated with or adjacent to a new oil and/or gas field or area, so long as the approval will not authorize activities in excess of any of the following:
units.action_summary: Approve Surface Use Plans only if they do not authorize activities beyond specified thresholds.

units.obligation_text: One mile of new road construction;
units.action_summary: Threshold: approval must not authorize more than one mile of new road construction.

units.obligation_text: One mile of road reconstruction;
units.action_summary: Threshold: approval must not authorize more than one mile of road reconstruction.

units.obligation_text: Three miles of individual or co-located pipelines and/or utilities disturbance; or
units.action_summary: Threshold: approval must not authorize more than three miles of pipeline/utility disturbance.

units.obligation_text: Four drill sites.
units.action_summary: Threshold: approval must not authorize more than four drill sites.

title: Modernization of Swine Slaughter Inspection

units.obligation_text: The establishment must conduct market hog sorting activities before the animals are presented for ante-mortem inspection.
units.action_summary: Conduct market hog sorting before ante-mortem inspection.

units.obligation_text: Market hogs exhibiting signs of moribundity, central nervous system disorders, or pyrexia must be disposed of according to paragraph (c) of this section.
units.action_summary: Dispose of market hogs with specified signs according to § 309.19(c).

units.obligation_text: The establishment must develop, implement, and maintain written procedures to ensure that market hogs exhibiting signs of moribundity, central nervous system disorders, or pyrexia do not enter the official establishment to be slaughtered.
units.action_summary: Create and maintain written procedures preventing sick market hogs from entering for slaughter.

units.obligation_text: The establishment must incorporate these procedures into its HACCP plan, or sanitation SOP, or other prerequisite program.
units.action_summary: Incorporate the written procedures into HACCP, sanitation SOP, or other prerequisite program.

units.obligation_text: The establishment must identify carcasses of livestock that establishment employees have sorted and removed from slaughter or that FSIS inspectors have condemned on ante-mortem inspection with a unique tag, tattoo, or similar device.
units.action_summary: Identify sorted or condemned carcasses with a unique tag, tattoo, or similar device.

units.obligation_text: The establishment must immediately denature all major portions of the carcass on-site and dispose of the carcass according to 9 CFR part 314.3.
units.action_summary: Immediately denature major carcass portions on-site and dispose per 9 CFR part 314.3.

units.obligation_text: The establishment must maintain records to document the number of animals disposed of per day because they were removed from slaughter by establishment sorters before ante-mortem inspection by FSIS inspectors.
units.action_summary: Maintain daily records documenting animals disposed of by sorters prior to ante-mortem inspection.

units.obligation_text: These records are subject to review and evaluation by FSIS personnel.
units.action_summary: FSIS personnel may review and evaluate the records.

units.obligation_text: The establishment must immediately notify FSIS inspectors if the establishment has reason to believe that market hogs may have a notifiable animal disease.
units.action_summary: Immediately notify FSIS inspectors if there is reason to believe market hogs may have a notifiable disease.

units.obligation_text: The NSIS may be used for market hogs if the official establishment requests to use it and meets or agrees to meet the requirements in 9 CFR 309.19 and 9 CFR 310.26.
units.action_summary: Establishments may use NSIS for market hogs if they request it and meet the cited requirements.

units.obligation_text: The Administrator may permit establishments that slaughter classes of swine other than market hogs to use NSIS under a waiver from the provisions of the regulations as provided by 9 CFR 303.1(h).
units.action_summary: Administrator may permit non-market-hog swine establishments to use NSIS under a waiver per 9 CFR 303.1(h).

units.obligation_text: The Administrator also may permit establishments that slaughter market hogs and other classes of swine to slaughter market hogs under NSIS and slaughter other classes of swine under traditional inspection.
units.action_summary: Administrator may allow establishments to use NSIS for market hogs and traditional inspection for other swine classes.

units.obligation_text: Traditional inspection shall be used for swine when NSIS is not used.
units.action_summary: When NSIS is not used, establishments must use traditional inspection for swine.

units.obligation_text: Although not required in a one- or two-inspector slaughter configuration, except in certain cases as determined by the inspection service, if a mirror is used, it must comply with the requirements of § 307.2(m)(6).
units.action_summary: If a mirror is used in one- or two-inspector configurations, it must comply with § 307.2(m)(6).

units.obligation_text: Official swine slaughter establishments must develop, implement, and maintain written procedures to prevent contamination of carcasses and parts by enteric pathogens, fecal, ingesta, and milk contamination throughout the entire slaughter and dressing operation.
units.action_summary: Develop, implement, and maintain written procedures to prevent contamination throughout slaughter and dressing.

units.obligation_text: Establishments must incorporate these procedures into their HACCP plans, or sanitation SOPs, or other prerequisite programs.
units.action_summary: Incorporate contamination-prevention procedures into HACCP, sanitation SOPs, or other prerequisite programs.

units.obligation_text: These procedures must include sampling and analysis for microbial organisms in accordance with the sampling location and frequency requirements in paragraphs (c)(1) and (2) of this section to monitor their ability to maintain process control.
units.action_summary: Include sampling and analysis for microbial organisms per specified locations and frequencies to monitor process control.

units.obligation_text: Official swine slaughter establishments, except for very small establishments or very low volume establishments, must collect and analyze samples for microbial organisms at the pre-evisceration and post-chill points in the process.
units.actor: official swine slaughter establishments (except very small or very low volume)
units.action_summary: Collect and analyze microbial samples at pre-evisceration and post-chill points (except very small/very low volume establishments).

units.obligation_text: Very small establishments and very low volume establishments must collect and analyze samples for microbial organisms at the post-chill point in the process.
units.actor: very small establishments and very low volume establishments
units.action_summary: Very small/very low volume establishments must sample and analyze microbial organisms at post-chill point.

units.obligation_text: All swine establishments must sponge or excise tissue from the ham, belly, or jowl areas.
units.action_summary: Sponge or excise tissue from ham, belly, or jowl areas for sampling.

units.obligation_text: An establishment may substitute alternative sampling locations if: (A) The establishment has support to demonstrate the alternative sampling locations are able to provide a definite improvement in monitoring process control than at pre-evisceration and post-chill; and (B) FSIS does not determine, and notify the establishment in writing, that the alternative sampling locations are inadequate to verify the effectiveness of the establishment’s process controls for enteric pathogens.
units.action_summary: Establishments may use alternative sampling locations if they demonstrate improvement and FSIS does not disapprove in writing.

units.obligation_text: The establishment has support to demonstrate the alternative sampling locations are able to provide a definite improvement in monitoring process control than at pre-evisceration and post-chill.
units.action_summary: Establishment must have supporting evidence showing alternative locations improve monitoring.

units.obligation_text: FSIS does not determine, and notify the establishment in writing, that the alternative sampling locations are inadequate to verify the effectiveness of the establishment’s process controls for enteric pathogens.
units.action_summary: FSIS must not notify the establishment in writing that the alternative sampling locations are inadequate (i.e., FSIS must not disapprove).

units.obligation_text: Establishments, except for very small and very low volume establishments as defined in paragraphs (c)(1)(i) and (ii) of this section, must collect and analyze samples at a frequency proportional to the establishment’s volume of production at the following rates.
units.actor: establishments (except very small and very low volume)
units.action_summary: Establishments must collect and analyze samples at frequencies proportional to production volume as specified.

units.obligation_text: Establishments, except for very small and very low volume establishments as defined in paragraphs (c)(1)(i) and (ii) of this section, must collect and analyze samples at a frequency of once per 1,000 carcasses, but a minimum of once during each week of operation.
units.actor: establishments (except very small and very low volume)
units.action_summary: Sample frequency: once per 1,000 carcasses, minimum once per week.

units.obligation_text: Very small and very low volume establishments as defined in paragraph (c)(1)(i) and (ii) of this section must collect and analyze samples at least once during each week of operation starting June 1 of every year.
units.actor: very small and very low volume establishments
units.action_summary: Very small/very low volume establishments must sample at least once per week starting June 1 each year.

units.obligation_text: If, after consecutively collecting 13 weekly samples, very small and very low volume establishments can demonstrate that they are effectively maintaining process control, they may modify their sampling plans.
units.actor: very small and very low volume establishments
units.action_summary: After 13 consecutive weekly samples demonstrating control, very small/very low establishments may modify sampling plans.

units.obligation_text: An establishment may substitute an alternative frequency if: (A) The alternative is an integral part of the establishment’s verification procedures for its HACCP plan; and (B) FSIS does not determine, and notify the establishment in writing, that the alternative frequency is inadequate to verify the effectiveness of the establishment’s process controls for enteric pathogens.
units.action_summary: Establishments may use an alternative sampling frequency if it's part of HACCP verification and FSIS does not disapprove in writing.

units.obligation_text: The alternative is an integral part of the establishment’s verification procedures for its HACCP plan.
units.action_summary: Alternative frequency must be integral to the establishment's HACCP verification procedures.

units.obligation_text: FSIS does not determine, and notify the establishment in writing, that the alternative frequency is inadequate to verify the effectiveness of the establishment’s process controls for enteric pathogens.
units.action_summary: FSIS must not notify the establishment in writing that the alternative frequency is inadequate (i.e., FSIS must not disapprove).

units.obligation_text: Establishments must sample at a frequency that is adequate to monitor their ability to maintain process control for enteric pathogens.
units.action_summary: Sample at a frequency adequate to monitor process control for enteric pathogens.

units.obligation_text: Establishments must maintain accurate records of all test results and retain these records as provided in paragraph (e) of this section.
units.action_summary: Keep accurate test-result records and retain them as required in paragraph (e).

units.obligation_text: Official swine slaughter establishments must develop, implement, and maintain written procedures to prevent contamination of the pre-operational environment by enteric pathogens.
units.action_summary: Develop, implement, and maintain written procedures to prevent enteric pathogen contamination in pre-operational environment.

units.obligation_text: Establishments must incorporate these procedures into their HACCP plans, sanitation SOPs, or other prerequisite programs.
units.action_summary: Incorporate pre-operational contamination procedures into HACCP, sanitation SOPs, or other prerequisite programs.

units.obligation_text: These procedures must include sampling and analysis of food contact surfaces in the pre-operational environment for microbial organisms to ensure that the surfaces are sanitary and free of enteric pathogens and that water used to clean food contact surfaces is free of enteric pathogens.
units.action_summary: Include sampling and analysis of food contact surfaces and cleaning water to ensure sanitation and absence of enteric pathogens.

units.obligation_text: The sampling frequency must be adequate to monitor the establishment’s ability to maintain sanitary conditions in the pre-operational environment.
units.action_summary: Use a sampling frequency adequate to monitor sanitary conditions in the pre-operational environment.

units.obligation_text: Establishments must maintain accurate records of all test results and retain these records as provided in paragraph (e) of this section.
units.action_summary: Maintain accurate test-result records and retain them per paragraph (e).

units.obligation_text: Official swine slaughter establishments must maintain daily records sufficient to document the implementation and monitoring of the procedures required under paragraphs (c), (d) and (e) of this section.
units.action_summary: Maintain daily records documenting implementation and monitoring of procedures in (c), (d), and (e).

units.obligation_text: Records required by this section may be maintained on computers if the establishment implements appropriate controls to ensure the integrity of the electronic data.
units.action_summary: Records may be kept electronically if appropriate controls ensure data integrity.

units.obligation_text: Records required by this section must be maintained for at least one year and must be accessible to FSIS.
units.action_summary: Keep required records for at least one year and make them accessible to FSIS.

units.obligation_text: The establishment must comply with the facilities requirements in 9 CFR part 307.
units.action_summary: Comply with facilities requirements in 9 CFR part 307.

units.obligation_text: If the establishment has less than three inspection stations, the establishment must provide a mirror at the carcass inspection station in accordance with 9 CFR 307.2(m)(6).
units.action_summary: Provide a mirror at the carcass inspection station if fewer than three inspection stations, per § 307.2(m)(6).

units.obligation_text: The establishment must conduct carcass sorting activities and identify any condemnable conditions or defects before carcasses are presented to online inspectors.
units.action_summary: Conduct carcass sorting and identify condemnable conditions before presenting carcasses to online inspectors.

units.obligation_text: The establishment must develop, implement, and maintain written procedures to ensure that market hog carcasses contaminated with septicemia, toxemia, pyemia, or cysticercosis are properly removed before the point of post-mortem inspection of carcasses.
units.action_summary: Create and maintain written procedures to remove carcasses contaminated with specified conditions before post-mortem inspection.

units.obligation_text: The establishment must incorporate these procedures into its HACCP plan, or sanitation SOP, or other prerequisite program.
units.action_summary: Incorporate the carcass-removal procedures into HACCP, sanitation SOP, or other prerequisite program.

units.obligation_text: These procedures must cover establishment sorting activities required under this section.
units.action_summary: Ensure the procedures address the sorting activities required by this section.

units.obligation_text: The line speed limits in 9 CFR 310.1 do not apply to the establishment, provided that they are able to maintain effective process control and prevent contamination of carcasses and parts by fecal material and enteric pathogens.
units.action_summary: Line speed limits in § 310.1 do not apply if establishment maintains effective process control and prevents contamination.

units.obligation_text: Establishments operating under NSIS must reduce their line speed as directed by the Inspector-in-Charge (IIC).
units.action_summary: Reduce line speed when directed by the Inspector-in-Charge.

units.obligation_text: The IIC is authorized to direct an establishment to operate at a reduced line speed when in their judgment a carcass-by-carcass inspection cannot be adequately performed within the time available due to the manner in which the carcasses are presented to the online inspector, the health conditions of a particular herd, or factors that may indicate a loss of process control.
units.action_summary: IIC may direct reduced line speed when carcass-by-carcass inspection cannot be adequately performed or loss of process control is indicated.

units.obligation_text: The establishment must maintain records to document that the products resulting from its slaughter operation meet the definition of ready-to-cook pork product in 9 CFR 301.2.
units.action_summary: Maintain records documenting that products meet the 'ready-to-cook' definition in § 301.2.

units.obligation_text: These records are subject to review and evaluation by FSIS personnel.
units.action_summary: FSIS personnel may review and evaluate the ready-to-cook product records.

units.obligation_text: The establishment must maintain records to document the number of animals disposed of per day by plant sorters or condemned per day by FSIS inspectors upon post-mortem inspection.
units.action_summary: Maintain records documenting daily numbers of animals disposed by plant sorters or condemned by FSIS upon post-mortem inspection.

units.obligation_text: These records are subject to review and evaluation by FSIS personnel.
units.action_summary: FSIS personnel may review and evaluate the animal disposition/condemnation records.

units.obligation_text: Each establishment that participates in the New Swine Slaughter Inspection System (NSIS) must submit on an annual basis an attestation to the management member of the local FSIS circuit safety committee stating that it maintains a program to monitor and document any work-related conditions of establishment workers, and that the program includes the following elements:
units.action_summary: Annually submit an attestation to the local FSIS circuit safety committee management member confirming maintenance of a worker-condition monitoring and documentation program that includes specified elements.

units.obligation_text: Policies to encourage early reporting of symptoms of injuries and illnesses, and assurance that it has no policies or programs in place that would discourage the reporting of injuries and illnesses.
units.action_summary: Program must include policies encouraging early reporting of injuries/illnesses and no policies that discourage reporting.

units.obligation_text: Notification to employees of the nature and early symptoms of occupational illnesses and injuries, in a manner and language that workers can understand, including by posting in a conspicuous place or places where notices to employees are customarily posted, a copy of the FSIS/OSHA poster encouraging reporting and describing reportable signs and symptoms.
units.action_summary: Notify employees of occupational illness/injury symptoms in understandable language and post FSIS/OSHA poster in conspicuous places.

units.obligation_text: Monitoring, on a regular and routine basis, injury and illness logs, as well as nurse or medical office logs, workers’ compensation data, and any other injury or illness information available.
units.action_summary: Regularly and routinely monitor injury and illness logs, medical logs, workers' compensation data, and other available injury/illness information.

title: Elimination of the Requirement That Livestock Carcasses Be Marked U.S. Inspected and Passed at the Time of Inspection Within a Slaughter Establishment for Carcasses To Be Further Processed Within the Same Establishment

units.obligation_text: Each carcass that has been inspected and passed in an official establishment must be marked at the time of inspection with the official inspection legend containing the number of the official establishment, if the carcass is to be shipped into commerce from the establishment without further processing.
units.action_summary: Mark inspected and passed carcasses at the time of inspection with the official inspection legend (including establishment number) if the carcass will be shipped into commerce without further processing.

units.obligation_text: A passed and inspected carcass that is to be further processed in the slaughtering establishment need not be marked with the official inspection legend at the time of inspection, provided the establishment develops and implements, as part of a HACCP plan, Sanitation SOPs, or other prerequisite program, procedures to ensure that:
units.action_summary: A passed and inspected carcass to be further processed in the slaughtering establishment is not required to be marked at inspection time, if the establishment develops and implements appropriate procedures as part of HACCP/Sanitation SOPs or other prerequisite programs.

units.obligation_text: Unmarked carcasses are further processed only in the slaughtering establishment;
units.action_summary: Ensure that unmarked carcasses are processed only within the slaughtering establishment.

units.obligation_text: Unmarked carcasses that, for any reason, are not further processed in the establishment do not leave the establishment unmarked;
units.action_summary: Ensure unmarked carcasses that are not further processed do not leave the establishment while unmarked.

units.obligation_text: Unmarked and retained carcasses or parts remain under FSIS control until the establishment makes any corrections that are necessary to render the carcass or part eligible to bear the mark of inspection.
units.action_summary: Unmarked and retained carcasses or parts must remain under FSIS control until the establishment makes necessary corrections to render them eligible for the inspection mark.

units.obligation_text: the establishment makes any corrections that are necessary to render the carcass or part eligible to bear the mark of inspection.
units.action_summary: Make any corrections necessary to render the carcass or part eligible to bear the mark of inspection.

units.obligation_text: By March 1, 2016, FSIS required foreign countries to submit written documentation identifying a list of establishments that had been exporting and would continue exporting Siluriformes fish to the United States.
units.action_summary: Submit written documentation listing establishments that had been exporting and would continue exporting Siluriformes fish to the U.S. by March 1, 2016.

units.obligation_text: By March 1, 2016, FSIS required foreign countries to submit written documentation to demonstrate that they had laws or other legal measures in place that provide authority to regulate the growing and processing of fish for human food, and to assure compliance with FDA’s good manufacturing practices, Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Point (HACCP) requirements, sanitation control procedures, and other regulatory requirements in 21 CFR part 123, Fish and Fishery Products.
units.action_summary: Provide documentation showing legal authority and measures to regulate fish production and compliance with FDA GMPs, HACCP, sanitation, and 21 CFR part 123 requirements by March 1, 2016.

units.obligation_text: Foreign countries that wished to continue exporting after September 1, 2017, were required to submit documentation substantiating the equivalence of their Siluriformes fish inspection system to that of the United States.
units.actor: foreign countries wishing to continue exporting after September 1, 2017
units.action_summary: Submit documentation substantiating that their inspection system is equivalent to the U.S. system in order to continue exporting after September 1, 2017.

units.obligation_text: Foreign countries that submitted complete equivalence documentation by September 1, 2017, were permitted to continue exporting Siluriformes fish until such time that FSIS determines if their Siluriformes fish inspection systems are equivalent to the U.S. system.
units.actor: foreign countries that submitted complete equivalence documentation by September 1, 2017
units.action_summary: Allowed to continue exporting Siluriformes fish pending FSIS determination of equivalence if complete equivalence documentation was submitted by Sept. 1, 2017.

units.obligation_text: Under the regulations, foreign countries must be listed in the CFR as eligible to export Siluriformes fish to the United States.
units.action_summary: Be listed in the CFR to be eligible to export Siluriformes fish to the United States.

units.obligation_text: Once listed, the eligible country is required to certify that establishments meet the requirements to export Siluriformes fish to the United States and to ensure that products from these establishments are safe, wholesome, and not misbranded.
units.action_summary: Certify that establishments meet export requirements and ensure their products are safe, wholesome, and not misbranded.

units.obligation_text: Foreign countries wanting to export Siluriformes fish to the United States are required to provide information to FSIS certifying that their inspection system provides standards equivalent to those of the United States, and that the legal authority for the system and their implementing regulations are equivalent to those of the United States.
units.actor: foreign countries wanting to export Siluriformes fish
units.action_summary: Provide FSIS with certification/information that their inspection system standards and legal authority are equivalent to U.S. standards.

units.obligation_text: The frequency and documentation of the monitoring of the sanitation operations must replicate the frequency and monitoring in the written sanitation procedures.
units.action_summary: Ensure the frequency and documentation of sanitation monitoring match the written sanitation procedures.

units.obligation_text: Should this rule become final, the government of Vietnam must certify to FSIS those establishments that wish to export Siluriformes fish to the United States and that operate in accordance with requirements equivalent to that of the United States (9 CFR 557.2(a)).
units.action_summary: Certify to FSIS which establishments wish to export and operate in accordance with U.S.-equivalent requirements if rule becomes final.

units.obligation_text: Siluriformes fish imported into the United States must be from foreign countries that maintain an inspection system that ensures compliance with requirements equivalent to all the inspection, sanitary, quality, species verification, and residue standards, and all other provisions of the FMIA.
units.actor: imported Siluriformes fish / exporting foreign countries (condition of import)
units.action_summary: Imports must originate from countries that maintain inspection systems equivalent to U.S. inspection, sanitary, quality, species verification, and residue standards and other FMIA provisions.

units.obligation_text: Siluriformes fish exported from Vietnam will continue to be subject to re-inspection at U.S. points-of-entry for, but not limited to, transportation damage, product and container defects, labeling, proper certification, general condition, and accurate count.
units.actor: Siluriformes fish exported from Vietnam / FSIS inspectors
units.action_summary: Imported Siluriformes fish from Vietnam are subject to re-inspection at U.S. entry points for listed checks (damage, defects, labeling, certification, condition, count).

units.obligation_text: If imported product fails FSIS testing, the product is refused entry and the designated competent authority of the foreign government’s inspection system is notified and further shipments of product from the foreign establishment are placed under either an increased or intensified level of sampling.
units.actor: FSIS (and the designated competent authority is notified)
units.action_summary: When imported product fails FSIS testing, it is refused entry; the foreign competent authority is notified; further shipments from that establishment are placed under increased or intensified sampling.
units.modal_raw: is refused entry / are notified / are placed under

units.obligation_text: Products that pass re-inspection will be stamped with the official mark of inspection and allowed to enter U.S. commerce.
units.action_summary: Products passing re-inspection will be stamped with the official inspection mark and allowed to enter U.S. commerce.
units.modal_raw: will be stamped / allowed to enter

units.obligation_text: If they do not meet U.S. requirements, they will be refused entry and within 45 days must be exported to the country of origin, destroyed, or converted to animal food (subject to approval of FDA), depending on the violation.
units.actor: imported products / responsible parties (importer/consignee) and FSIS (refuse entry)
units.action_summary: Products not meeting U.S. requirements will be refused entry and, within 45 days, must be exported to origin, destroyed, or converted to animal food (with FDA approval as applicable).
units.modal_raw: will be refused entry / must be exported/destroyed/converted

units.obligation_text: Within 45 days must be exported to the country of origin.
units.action_summary: Refused product must be exported to the country of origin within 45 days.

units.obligation_text: Within 45 days must be destroyed.
units.action_summary: Refused product must be destroyed within 45 days.

units.obligation_text: Within 45 days must be converted to animal food (subject to approval of FDA).
units.actor: importer/owner of the refused product / FDA for approval
units.action_summary: Refused product must be converted to animal food within 45 days, subject to FDA approval when applicable.

units.obligation_text: Section 557.2 is amended by adding "Socialist Republic of Vietnam" in alphabetical order to the list of countries in paragraph (b)(1).
units.action_summary: Add 'Socialist Republic of Vietnam' to the list of countries in 9 CFR 557.2(b)(1).

title: Eligibility of the Socialist Republic of Vietnam to Export Siluriformes Fish and Fish Products to the United States

title: Endangered and Threatened Species: Endangered Species Status for the Texas Hornshell

units.obligation_text: We request comments or information from other concerned governmental agencies, Native American tribes, the scientific community, industry, or any other interested parties concerning this proposed rule.
units.actor: governmental agencies, Native American tribes, scientific community, industry, and other interested parties
units.action_summary: The Service requests submission of comments or information from interested parties about the proposed listing rule.

units.obligation_text: (1) The Texas hornshell’s biology, range, and population trends, including: (a) Biological or ecological requirements of the species, including habitat requirements for feeding and spawning; (b) Genetics and taxonomy; (c) Historical and current range, including distribution patterns; (d) Historical and current population levels, and current and projected trends; and (e) Past and ongoing conservation measures for the species, its habitat, or both.
units.action_summary: Provide information on the species' biology, genetics, range, population trends, and conservation measures.

units.obligation_text: (2) Factors that may affect the continued existence of the species, which may include habitat modification or destruction, overutilization, disease, predation, the inadequacy of existing regulatory mechanisms, or other natural or manmade factors.
units.action_summary: Provide information on factors that could threaten the species' continued existence.

units.obligation_text: (3) Biological, commercial trade, or other relevant data concerning any threats (or lack thereof) to this species and existing regulations that may be addressing those threats.
units.action_summary: Submit data on threats to the species and relevant regulations addressing those threats.

units.obligation_text: (4) Additional information concerning the historical and current status, range, distribution, and population size of this species, including the locations of any additional populations of this species, particularly in Mexico.
units.action_summary: Provide any additional distribution, status, and population information, especially locations of populations in Mexico.

units.obligation_text: (5) Information related to climate change within the range of the Texas hornshell and how it may affect the species’ habitat.
units.action_summary: Provide information on climate change impacts within the species' range and effects on habitat.

units.obligation_text: (6) The reasons why areas should or should not be designated as critical habitat as provided by section 4 of the Act (16 U.S.C. 1531 et seq.)
units.action_summary: Provide reasons for or against designating areas as critical habitat under the Act.

units.obligation_text: (7) Specific information on: (a) The amount and distribution of habitat for the Texas hornshell; (b) What areas, that are currently occupied and that contain the physical and biological features essential to the conservation of the Texas hornshell, should be included in a critical habitat designation and why; (c) Special management considerations or protection that may be needed for the essential features in potential critical habitat areas, including managing for the potential effects of climate change; and (d) What areas not occupied at the time of listing are essential for the conservation of the species and why.
units.action_summary: Provide detailed information on habitat amount/distribution, areas to include in critical habitat, needed management/protections, and essential unoccupied areas.

units.action_summary: Permits glaucous-winged gull egg gathering in Yakutat during May 15–June 30.

units.obligation_text: Closure: July 1–August 31.
units.action_summary: Prohibits gull egg gathering in Yakutat during July 1–August 31.

units.obligation_text: Upon finding that continuation of these subsistence regulations would pose an imminent threat to the conservation of threatened Steller’s eiders (Polysticta stelleri), the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service Alaska Regional Director, in consultation with the Co-management Council, will immediately under § 92.21 take action as is necessary to prevent further take.
units.actor: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service Alaska Regional Director, in consultation with the Co-management Council
units.action_summary: Requires the Regional Director, upon finding an imminent threat to Steller’s eiders, to immediately take necessary actions under § 92.21 to prevent further take.

units.obligation_text: Regulation changes implemented could range from a temporary closure of duck hunting in a small geographic area to large-scale regional or Statewide long-term closures of all subsistence migratory bird hunting.
units.actor: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service Alaska Regional Director (implementing regulations)
units.action_summary: Authorizes a range of regulatory changes the Regional Director may implement, from small temporary closures to large-scale long-term closures.

units.obligation_text: These closures or temporary suspensions will remain in effect until the Regional Director, in consultation with the Co-management Council, determines that the potential for additional Steller’s eiders to be taken no longer exists.
units.actor: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service Alaska Regional Director, in consultation with the Co-management Council
units.action_summary: States that closures/suspensions stay in effect until the Regional Director determines the risk to Steller’s eiders no longer exists.
