title: Endangered and Threatened Species: Listing Species and Designating Critical Habitat

units.obligation_text: The Secretary shall make any determination required by paragraphs (c), (d), and (e) of this section solely on the basis of the best available scientific and commercial information regarding a species’ status.
units.action_summary: Make determinations under paragraphs (c), (d), and (e) based solely on the best available scientific and commercial information about the species' status.

units.obligation_text: A species shall be listed or reclassified if the Secretary determines, on the basis of the best scientific and commercial data available after conducting a review of the species’ status, that the species meets the definition of an endangered species or a threatened species because of any one or a combination of the following factors:
units.action_summary: List or reclassify a species when, after review and based on the best available data, the species meets the definition of endangered or threatened due to one or more listed factors.

units.obligation_text: The present or threatened destruction, modification, or curtailment of its habitat or range;
units.action_summary: Condition: habitat/range destruction or modification as a factor for listing/reclassification.

units.obligation_text: Overutilization for commercial, recreational, scientific, or educational purposes;
units.action_summary: Condition: overutilization as a factor for listing/reclassification.

units.obligation_text: Disease or predation;
units.action_summary: Condition: disease or predation as a factor for listing/reclassification.

units.obligation_text: The inadequacy of existing regulatory mechanisms; or
units.action_summary: Condition: inadequate existing regulatory mechanisms as a factor for listing/reclassification.

units.obligation_text: Other natural or manmade factors affecting its continued existence.
units.action_summary: Condition: other natural or manmade factors as a factor for listing/reclassification.

units.obligation_text: In determining whether a species is a threatened species, the Services must analyze whether the species is likely to become an endangered species within the foreseeable future.
units.action_summary: Analyze whether the species is likely to become endangered within the foreseeable future when assessing threatened status.

units.obligation_text: The Services will describe the foreseeable future on a case-by-case basis, using the best available data and taking into account considerations such as the species’ life-history characteristics, threat-projection timeframes, and environmental variability.
units.action_summary: Describe the 'foreseeable future' case-by-case using best available data and considering life-history, threat timeframes, and environmental variability.

units.obligation_text: The Services need not identify the foreseeable future in terms of a specific period of time, but may instead explain the extent to which they can reasonably determine that both the future threats and the species’ responses to those threats are probable.
units.action_summary: Not required to set a specific time period for the foreseeable future; may explain the extent to which future threats and species responses are probable.

units.obligation_text: The Secretary will delist a species if the Secretary finds that, after conducting a status review based on the best scientific and commercial data available:
units.action_summary: Delist a species when, after a status review based on the best available data, one of the specified conditions is met.

units.obligation_text: The species is extinct;
units.action_summary: Condition under which the Secretary will delist: species is extinct.

units.obligation_text: The species does not meet the definition of an endangered species or a threatened species.
units.action_summary: Condition under which the Secretary will delist: species no longer meets statutory definition of endangered or threatened.

units.obligation_text: In making such a determination, the Secretary shall consider the same factors and apply the same standards set forth in paragraph (c) of this section regarding listing and reclassification;
units.action_summary: When determining that a species does not meet the definitions, consider and apply the same factors and standards in paragraph (c) used for listing and reclassification.

units.obligation_text: The listed entity does not meet the statutory definition of a species.
units.action_summary: Condition under which the Secretary will delist: the listed entity is not a species as defined by statute.

units.obligation_text: The fact that a species ... is protected by the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species ... or a similar international agreement ... may constitute evidence that the species is endangered or threatened.
units.action_summary: The Secretary may treat protection under CITES or similar agreements, or foreign/state identification of need, as evidence that a species is endangered or threatened.

units.obligation_text: The Secretary shall give consideration to any species protected under such an international agreement, or by any State or foreign nation, to determine whether the species is endangered or threatened.
units.action_summary: Give consideration to species protected under international agreements or by State/foreign agencies when deciding if species is endangered or threatened.

units.obligation_text: The Secretary shall take into account, in making determinations under paragraphs (c) or (e) of this section, those efforts, if any, being made by any State or foreign nation, or any political subdivision of a State or foreign nation, to protect such species, whether by predator control, protection of habitat and food supply, or other conservation practices, within any area under its jurisdiction, or on the high seas.
units.action_summary: Consider conservation efforts by States, foreign nations, or their political subdivisions (e.g., predator control, habitat protection) when making listing or delisting determinations under (c) or (e).

units.obligation_text: The Secretary may, but is not required to, determine that a designation would not be prudent in the following circumstances:
units.action_summary: Permitted (not required) to determine that designating critical habitat would not be prudent under listed circumstances.
units.modal_raw: may, but is not required to

units.obligation_text: The species is threatened by taking or other human activity and identification of critical habitat can be expected to increase the degree of such threat to the species;
units.action_summary: Circumstance in which designation may be determined not prudent: identifying critical habitat would likely increase threats from taking or human activity.

units.obligation_text: The present or threatened destruction, modification, or curtailment of a species’ habitat or range is not a threat to the species, or threats to the species’ habitat stem solely from causes that cannot be addressed through management actions resulting from consultations under section 7(a)(2) of the Act;
units.action_summary: Circumstance in which designation may be determined not prudent: habitat threats are not a threat to species, or habitat threats stem only from causes not addressable by section 7(a)(2) consultations.

units.obligation_text: Areas within the jurisdiction of the United States provide no more than negligible conservation value, if any, for a species occurring primarily outside the jurisdiction of the United States;
units.action_summary: Circumstance in which designation may be determined not prudent: U.S. areas have negligible conservation value for species mainly outside U.S.

units.obligation_text: No areas meet the definition of critical habitat;
units.action_summary: Circumstance in which designation may be determined not prudent: no areas qualify as critical habitat.

units.obligation_text: After analyzing the best scientific data available, the Secretary otherwise determines that designation of critical habitat would not be prudent.
units.action_summary: Circumstance in which designation may be determined not prudent: after analysis of best scientific data, the Secretary otherwise determines designation is not prudent.

units.obligation_text: The Secretary will designate as critical habitat, at a scale determined by the Secretary to be appropriate, specific areas outside the geographical area occupied by the species only upon a determination that such areas are essential for the conservation of the species.
units.action_summary: Designate unoccupied areas as critical habitat only if determined essential for the species' conservation, at an appropriate scale determined by the Secretary.

units.obligation_text: When designating critical habitat, the Secretary will first evaluate areas occupied by the species.
units.action_summary: First evaluate areas occupied by the species when designating critical habitat.

units.obligation_text: The Secretary will only consider unoccupied areas to be essential where a critical habitat designation limited to geographical areas occupied would be inadequate to ensure the conservation of the species or would result in less efficient conservation for the species.
units.action_summary: Consider unoccupied areas essential only if designating only occupied areas would be inadequate or less efficient for conservation.

units.obligation_text: In addition, for an unoccupied area to be considered essential, the Secretary must determine that there is a reasonable likelihood that the area will contribute to the conservation of the species.
units.action_summary: Must determine a reasonable likelihood that an unoccupied area will contribute to conservation before considering it essential.

title: Endangered and Threatened Species: Interagency Cooperation

units.obligation_text: A written request to initiate formal consultation shall be submitted to the Director and shall include:
units.action_summary: Submit a written request to initiate formal consultation to the Director and include required information.

units.obligation_text: A description of the proposed action, including any measures intended to avoid, minimize, or offset effects of the action. Consistent with the nature and scope of the proposed action, the description shall provide sufficient detail to assess the effects of the action on listed species and critical habitat, including:
units.action_summary: Provide a detailed description of the proposed action and measures to avoid/minimize/offset effects sufficient to assess effects on listed species and critical habitat.

units.obligation_text: (A) The purpose of the action;
units.action_summary: Include the purpose of the proposed action in the description.

units.obligation_text: (B) The duration and timing of the action;
units.action_summary: Include the duration and timing of the proposed action.

units.obligation_text: (C) The location of the action;
units.action_summary: Include the location of the proposed action.

units.obligation_text: (D) The specific components of the action and how they will be carried out;
units.action_summary: Describe the specific components of the action and how they will be implemented.

units.obligation_text: (E) Maps, drawings, blueprints, or similar schematics of the action; and
units.action_summary: Provide maps, drawings, blueprints, or similar schematics of the action.

units.obligation_text: (F) Any other available information related to the nature and scope of the proposed action relevant to its effects on listed species or designated critical habitat.
units.action_summary: Include any other available information relevant to the nature and scope of the action and its effects on listed species or critical habitat.

units.obligation_text: A map or description of all areas to be affected directly or indirectly by the Federal action, and not merely the immediate area involved in the action (i.e., the action area as defined at § 402.02).
units.action_summary: Provide a map or description of all areas directly or indirectly affected by the Federal action (the action area).

units.obligation_text: Information obtained by or in the possession of the Federal agency and any applicant on the listed species and designated critical habitat in the action area (as required by paragraph (c)(1)(ii) of this section), including available information such as the presence, abundance, density, or periodic occurrence of listed species and the condition and location of species’ habitat, including any critical habitat.
units.actor: The Federal agency and any applicant
units.action_summary: Provide information in the agency's or applicant's possession on listed species and designated critical habitat in the action area, including presence, abundance, habitat condition/location, etc.

units.obligation_text: A description of the effects of the action and an analysis of any cumulative effects.
units.action_summary: Describe the effects of the proposed action and analyze any cumulative effects.

units.obligation_text: A summary of any relevant information provided by the applicant, if available.
units.action_summary: Include a summary of any relevant information provided by the applicant, if such information is available.

units.obligation_text: Any other relevant available information on the effects of the proposed action on listed species or designated critical habitat, including any relevant reports such as environmental impact statements and environmental assessments.
units.action_summary: Provide any other relevant available information on effects of the proposed action, including reports like EISs and EAs.

units.obligation_text: A Federal agency may submit existing documents prepared for the proposed action such as NEPA analyses or other reports in substitution for the initiation package outlined in this paragraph (c).
units.action_summary: Federal agencies may substitute existing documents (e.g., NEPA analyses) for the initiation package.

units.obligation_text: However, any such substitution shall be accompanied by a written summary specifying the location of the information that satisfies the elements above in the submitted document(s).
units.action_summary: If substituting existing documents, provide a written summary specifying where the required initiation-package elements are located in those documents.

units.obligation_text: Formal consultation shall not be initiated by the Federal agency until any required biological assessment has been completed and submitted to the Director in accordance with § 402.12.
units.action_summary: Do not initiate formal consultation until a required biological assessment has been completed and submitted to the Director per § 402.12.

units.obligation_text: Any request for formal consultation may encompass, subject to the approval of the Director, a number of similar individual actions within a given geographical area, a programmatic consultation, or a segment of a comprehensive plan.
units.action_summary: A request for formal consultation may encompass multiple similar individual actions, a programmatic consultation, or a plan segment, subject to Director approval.
units.modal_raw: may (subject to the approval of the Director)

units.obligation_text: This provision does not relieve the Federal agency of the requirements for considering the effects of the action or actions as a whole.
units.action_summary: Federal agencies remain required to consider the effects of the action(s) as a whole despite grouping actions in a request.

units.obligation_text: Evaluate the current status and environmental baseline of the listed species or critical habitat.
units.action_summary: Assess the current status and environmental baseline of the listed species or critical habitat when formulating an opinion.

units.obligation_text: Add the effects of the action and cumulative effects to the environmental baseline and in light of the status of the species and critical habitat, formulate the Service’s opinion as to whether the action is likely to jeopardize the continued existence of listed species or result in the destruction or adverse modification of critical habitat.
units.action_summary: Incorporate effects of the action and cumulative effects into the environmental baseline and formulate an opinion on jeopardy or adverse modification.

units.obligation_text: In formulating its biological opinion, any reasonable and prudent alternatives, and any reasonable and prudent measures, the Service will use the best scientific and commercial data available and will give appropriate consideration to any beneficial actions as proposed or taken by the Federal agency or applicant, including any actions taken prior to the initiation of consultation.
units.action_summary: Use the best available scientific and commercial data and give appropriate consideration to beneficial actions proposed or taken by the Federal agency or applicant when formulating opinions and measures.

units.obligation_text: The biological opinion shall include:
units.actor: The Service (author of the biological opinion)
units.action_summary: The biological opinion must contain specified elements.

units.obligation_text: A summary of the information on which the opinion is based;
units.action_summary: Include a summary of the information underlying the biological opinion.

units.obligation_text: A detailed discussion of the effects of the action on listed species or critical habitat;
units.action_summary: Provide a detailed discussion of how the action affects listed species or critical habitat.

units.obligation_text: The Service’s opinion on whether the action is: (A) Likely to jeopardize the continued existence of a listed species or result in the destruction or adverse modification of critical habitat (a "jeopardy" biological opinion); or (B) Not likely to jeopardize the continued existence of a listed species or result in the destruction or adverse modification of critical habitat (a "no jeopardy" biological opinion).
units.action_summary: State the Service's opinion on whether the action is likely to jeopardize listed species or adversely modify critical habitat, or is not likely to do so.

units.obligation_text: (A) Likely to jeopardize the continued existence of a listed species or result in the destruction or adverse modification of critical habitat (a "jeopardy" biological opinion);
units.action_summary: When applicable, the opinion may conclude the action is likely to jeopardize species or adversely modify critical habitat (jeopardy opinion).

units.obligation_text: (B) Not likely to jeopardize the continued existence of a listed species or result in the destruction or adverse modification of critical habitat (a "no jeopardy" biological opinion).
units.action_summary: When applicable, the opinion may conclude the action is not likely to jeopardize species or adversely modify critical habitat (no jeopardy opinion).

units.obligation_text: A "jeopardy" biological opinion shall include reasonable and prudent alternatives, if any.
units.action_summary: A jeopardy biological opinion must include any reasonable and prudent alternatives, if they exist.

units.obligation_text: If the Service is unable to develop such alternatives, the Service will indicate that to the best of its knowledge there are no reasonable and prudent alternatives.
units.action_summary: If the Service cannot develop reasonable and prudent alternatives, it must indicate that none exist to the best of its knowledge.

units.obligation_text: The Service may adopt all or part of: (i) A Federal agency’s initiation package; or (ii) The Service’s analysis required to issue a permit under section 10(a) of the Act in its biological opinion.
units.action_summary: The Service may adopt all or part of a Federal agency's initiation package or the Service's section 10(a) permit analysis into its biological opinion.

units.obligation_text: (i) A Federal agency’s initiation package;
units.action_summary: The Service may adopt a Federal agency's initiation package into its biological opinion.

units.obligation_text: (ii) The Service’s analysis required to issue a permit under section 10(a) of the Act in its biological opinion.
units.action_summary: The Service may adopt its own section 10(a) permit analysis into its biological opinion.

units.obligation_text: A Federal agency and the Service may agree to follow an optional collaborative process that would further the ability of the Service to adopt the information and analysis provided by the Federal agency during consultation in the development of the Service’s biological opinion to improve efficiency in the consultation process and reduce duplicative efforts.
units.actor: The Federal agency and the Service
units.action_summary: The Federal agency and the Service may agree to use an optional collaborative process to facilitate adoption of agency-provided information and improve consultation efficiency.

units.obligation_text: The Federal agency and the Service shall consider the nature, size, and scope of the action or its anticipated effects on listed species or critical habitat, and other relevant factors to determine whether an action or a class of actions is appropriate for this process.
units.actor: The Federal agency and the Service
units.action_summary: Both parties must consider the action's nature, size, scope, anticipated effects, and other factors to determine appropriateness for the collaborative process.

units.obligation_text: The Federal agency and the Service may develop coordination procedures that would facilitate adoption.
units.actor: The Federal agency and the Service
units.action_summary: The Federal agency and the Service may create coordination procedures to facilitate adoption of information.

units.obligation_text: Expedited consultation is an optional formal consultation process that a Federal agency and the Service may enter into upon mutual agreement.
units.actor: The Federal agency and the Service
units.action_summary: Federal agencies and the Service may, by mutual agreement, enter into an optional expedited consultation process.

units.obligation_text: To determine whether an action or a class of actions is appropriate for this type of consultation, the Federal agency and the Service shall consider the nature, size, and scope of the action or its anticipated effects on listed species or critical habitat and other relevant factors.
units.actor: The Federal agency and the Service
units.action_summary: Both parties must consider the action's characteristics and anticipated effects and other relevant factors to decide appropriateness for expedited consultation.

units.obligation_text: Upon agreement to use this expedited consultation process, the Federal agency and the Service shall establish the expedited timelines for the completion of this consultation process.
units.actor: The Federal agency and the Service
units.action_summary: If they agree to use expedited consultation, the Federal agency and the Service must set expedited timelines for completing consultation.

units.obligation_text: To request initiation of expedited consultation, the Federal agency shall provide all the information required to initiate consultation under paragraph (c) of this section.
units.action_summary: To request expedited consultation, the Federal agency must provide all information required under paragraph (c) for initiating consultation.

units.obligation_text: To maximize efficiency and ensure that it develops the appropriate level of information, the Federal agency is encouraged to develop its initiation package in coordination with the Service.
units.action_summary: Federal agencies are encouraged (but not required) to develop initiation packages in coordination with the Service to maximize efficiency and completeness.

units.obligation_text: Service responsibilities: In addition to the Service’s responsibilities under the provisions of this section, the Service will:
units.action_summary: The Service has additional responsibilities in the expedited consultation process, described below.

units.obligation_text: (i) Provide relevant species information to the Federal agency and guidance to assist the Federal agency in completing its effects analysis in the initiation package; and
units.action_summary: Provide relevant species information and guidance to help the Federal agency complete its effects analysis in the initiation package.

units.obligation_text: (ii) Conclude the consultation and issue a biological opinion within the agreed-upon timeframes.
units.action_summary: Conclude the expedited consultation and issue a biological opinion within the timeframes agreed upon with the Federal agency.

units.obligation_text: Reinitiation of consultation is required and shall be requested by the Federal agency or by the Service, where discretionary Federal involvement or control over the action has been retained or is authorized by law and:
units.actor: The Federal agency or the Service
units.action_summary: Where discretionary Federal involvement or control is retained or authorized by law, reinitiation of consultation is required and must be requested by the Federal agency or the Service.
units.modal_raw: is required to / shall be requested

units.obligation_text: An agency shall not be required to reinitiate consultation after the approval of a land management plan prepared pursuant to 43 U.S.C. 1712 or 16 U.S.C. 1604 upon listing of a new species or designation of new critical habitat, provided that any authorized actions that may affect the newly listed species or designated critical habitat will be addressed through a separate action-specific consultation.
units.action_summary: An agency is not required to reinitiate consultation after approval of a land management plan upon listing of a new species or designation of critical habitat, provided authorized actions that may affect the species/habitat are addressed through separate action-specific consultation.

units.obligation_text: Provided that any authorized actions that may affect the newly listed species or designated critical habitat will be addressed through a separate action-specific consultation.
units.action_summary: Condition: authorized actions that may affect newly listed species or designated critical habitat must be addressed through separate action-specific consultation.

title: Migratory Bird Hunting: Proposed Frameworks for Migratory Bird Hunting Regulations

units.obligation_text: Shooting and Hawking (taking by falconry) Hours: Unless otherwise specified, from one-half hour before sunrise to sunset daily.
units.action_summary: Hunters may take migratory game birds only between one-half hour before sunrise and sunset daily unless otherwise specified.

units.obligation_text: Possession Limits: Unless otherwise specified, possession limits are three times the daily bag limit.
units.action_summary: A hunter's possession limit is three times the daily bag limit unless specified otherwise.

units.obligation_text: These Federally authorized, State-issued permits are issued to individuals, and only the individual whose name and address appears on the permit at the time of issuance is authorized to take migratory birds at levels specified in the permit, in accordance with provisions of both Federal and State regulations governing the hunting season.
units.action_summary: Only the named individual on a Federally authorized, State-issued permit is authorized to take migratory birds at levels specified by the permit.

units.obligation_text: The permit must be carried by the permittee when exercising its provisions and must be presented to any law enforcement officer upon request.
units.action_summary: Permit holders must carry their permit while using it and present it to law enforcement upon request.

units.obligation_text: The permit is not transferrable or assignable to another individual, and may not be sold, bartered, traded, or otherwise provided to another person.
units.action_summary: Permits cannot be transferred, assigned, sold, bartered, traded, or otherwise provided to another person.

units.obligation_text: If the permit is altered or defaced in any way, the permit becomes invalid.
units.action_summary: Altering or defacing a permit invalidates it.

units.obligation_text: In the Atlantic Flyway States of Connecticut, Delaware, Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, New Jersey, North Carolina, and Pennsylvania, where Sunday hunting is prohibited Statewide by State law, all Sundays are closed to the take of all migratory game birds.
units.action_summary: In specified Atlantic Flyway States where Sunday hunting is prohibited by State law, taking migratory game birds on Sundays is prohibited.

units.obligation_text: Special Youth Waterfowl Hunting Days: States may select 2 days per duck-hunting zone, designated as 'Youth Waterfowl Hunting Days,' in addition to their regular duck seasons.
units.action_summary: States are permitted to select two youth waterfowl hunting days per duck-hunting zone in addition to regular duck seasons.

units.obligation_text: The days must be held outside any regular duck season on weekends, holidays, or other non-school days when youth hunters would have the maximum opportunity to participate.
units.action_summary: Selected youth hunting days must occur outside regular duck seasons and on days that maximize youth participation (weekends, holidays, or non-school days).

units.obligation_text: The days may be held up to 14 days before or after any regular duck-season frameworks or within any split of a regular duck season, or within any other open season on migratory birds.
units.action_summary: States may schedule youth hunting days up to 14 days before or after regular duck seasons, within splits, or within other open migratory bird seasons.

units.obligation_text: Daily Bag Limits: The daily bag limits may include ducks, geese, tundra swans, mergansers, coots, moorhens, and gallinules and would be the same as those allowed in the regular season.
units.action_summary: Daily bag limits on youth days may include the same species as the regular season and must be the same as regular season limits.

units.obligation_text: Shooting Hours: One-half hour before sunrise to sunset.
units.action_summary: On youth hunting days, shooting hours are from one-half hour before sunrise to sunset.

units.obligation_text: Participation Restrictions: States may use their established definition of age for youth hunters.
units.action_summary: States may define the age of youth hunters using their established age definitions.

units.obligation_text: However, youth hunters may not be over the age of 17.
units.action_summary: Youth hunters participating on youth days cannot be older than 17.

units.obligation_text: In addition, an adult at least 18 years of age must accompany the youth hunter into the field.
units.action_summary: A supervising adult of at least 18 must accompany each youth hunter into the field.

units.obligation_text: This adult may not duck hunt but may participate in other seasons that are open on the special youth day.
units.action_summary: The accompanying adult is prohibited from duck hunting on the youth day but may participate in other open seasons on that day.

units.obligation_text: Youth hunters 16 years of age and older must possess a Federal Migratory Bird Hunting and Conservation Stamp (also known as Federal Duck Stamp).
units.action_summary: Youth hunters aged 16 or older must have a Federal Migratory Bird Hunting and Conservation Stamp.

units.obligation_text: Tundra swans may only be taken by participants possessing applicable tundra swan permits.
units.action_summary: Only participants with the applicable tundra swan permits may take tundra swans.

units.obligation_text: Special September Teal Season: Between September 1 and September 30, an open season on all species of teal may be selected by the following States in areas delineated by State regulations: [lists of States].
units.action_summary: Specified States may select an open season on all teal species between Sept 1 and Sept 30 in areas defined by State regulations.

units.obligation_text: Hunting Seasons and Daily Bag Limits: Not to exceed 16 consecutive hunting days in the Atlantic, Mississippi, and Central Flyways. The daily bag limit is 6 teal.
units.action_summary: Teal seasons in specified flyways may be up to 16 consecutive days, and the daily bag limit for teal is 6.

units.obligation_text: Shooting Hours Atlantic Flyway: One-half hour before sunrise to sunset, except in South Carolina, where the hours are from sunrise to sunset.
units.actor: hunters in Atlantic Flyway (and South Carolina exception)
units.action_summary: Default shooting hours are one-half hour before sunrise to sunset; South Carolina is an exception where shooting hours are sunrise to sunset.

units.obligation_text: Special September Duck Seasons: In lieu of a special September teal season, Florida, Kentucky, and Tennessee may select a 5-consecutive-day teal/wood duck season in September.
units.action_summary: Florida, Kentucky, and Tennessee may choose a 5-day combined teal/wood duck season instead of a teal-only season.

units.obligation_text: The daily bag limit may not exceed 6 teal and wood ducks in the aggregate, of which no more than 2 may be wood ducks.
units.action_summary: During the 5-day teal/wood duck season the aggregate daily bag cannot exceed 6, with no more than 2 wood ducks.

units.obligation_text: Iowa may hold up to 5 days of its regular duck hunting season in September. The September season segment may commence no earlier than the Saturday nearest September 20 (September 22). The daily bag and possession limits will be the same as those in effect during the remainder of the regular duck season. The remainder of the regular duck season may not begin before October 10.
units.action_summary: Iowa may schedule up to 5 days of regular duck season in September starting no earlier than the Saturday nearest Sept 20; daily bag/possession limits remain the same; the rest of the season may not start before Oct 10.

units.obligation_text: Waterfowl Atlantic Flyway Outside Dates: Between the Saturday nearest September 24 (September 22) and the last Sunday in January (January 27).
units.action_summary: Waterfowl seasons in the Atlantic Flyway may be selected with outside dates between the referenced Saturday and the last Sunday in January.

units.obligation_text: Hunting Seasons and Duck Limits: 60 days. The daily bag limit is 6 ducks, including no more than 4 mallards (no more than 2 of which can be females), 2 black ducks, 2 pintails, 1 mottled duck, 1 fulvous whistling duck, 3 wood ducks, 2 redheads, 2 scaup, 2 canvasbacks, 4 scoters, 4 eiders, and 4 long-tailed ducks.
units.action_summary: Atlantic Flyway duck seasons are 60 days with a 6-duck daily bag limit and specified species-specific sublimits.

units.obligation_text: Closures: The season on harlequin ducks is closed.
units.action_summary: Hunting harlequin ducks is prohibited (season closed).

units.obligation_text: Merganser Limits: The daily bag limit of mergansers is 5, only 2 of which may be hooded mergansers. In States that include mergansers in the duck bag limit, the daily limit is the same as the duck bag limit, only 2 of which may be hooded mergansers.
units.action_summary: Daily merganser bag is 5 with maximum of 2 hooded mergansers; if mergansers counted within duck bag, the same duck-bag rules apply with same hooded- merganser limit.

units.obligation_text: Special Sea Duck Seasons: [Listed States] may select a Special Sea Duck Season in designated Special Sea Duck Areas.
units.action_summary: Specified States may select Special Sea Duck Seasons in designated special sea duck areas.

units.obligation_text: If a Special Sea Duck Season is selected, scoters, eiders, and long-tailed ducks may be taken in the designated Special Sea Duck Area(s) only during the Special Sea Duck Season dates; scoters, eiders, and long-tailed ducks may be taken outside of Special Sea Duck Area(s) during the regular duck season, in accordance with the frameworks for ducks, mergansers, and coots specified above.
units.action_summary: If a state selects a Special Sea Duck Season, the listed sea ducks may be taken in designated areas only during those season dates, while outside those areas they are taken during the regular duck season under regular frameworks.

units.obligation_text: Special Sea Duck Areas: ... provided that any such areas have been described, delineated, and designated as special sea duck hunting areas under the hunting regulations adopted by the respective States.
units.action_summary: States must describe, delineate, and designate any Special Sea Duck Areas in their hunting regulations before applying special sea duck seasons there.

units.obligation_text: Areas open to the hunting of Canada geese must be described, delineated, and designated as such in each State’s hunting regulations.
units.action_summary: States must describe, delineate, and designate areas open to Canada goose hunting in their hunting regulations.

units.obligation_text: Shooting Hours: One-half hour before sunrise to sunset, except that during any special early Canada goose season, shooting hours may extend to one-half hour after sunset if all other waterfowl seasons are closed in the specific applicable area.
units.action_summary: Normal shooting hours are one-half hour before sunrise to sunset; during special early Canada goose seasons, hours may be extended to one-half hour after sunset if other waterfowl seasons are closed in that area.

units.obligation_text: White-fronted Geese and Brant: [States listed] may select a season for white-fronted geese not to exceed 74 days with 3 geese daily, or 88 days with 2 geese daily, or 107 days with 1 goose daily between September 1 and February 15; ... States may select a season for brant not to exceed 70 days with 2 brant daily, or 107 days with 1 brant daily ... alternately, States may include brant in an aggregate goose bag limit with either Canada geese, white-fronted geese, or dark geese.
units.action_summary: Specified States may select among various season lengths and daily bag limits for white-fronted geese and brant or include brant in aggregate goose bag limits as described.

units.obligation_text: Light Geese: States may select a 107-day season between October 1 and March 10, with a 25-bird daily bag limit and no possession limit. States may split their seasons into three segments.
units.action_summary: States may set light goose seasons up to 107 days with a 25-bird daily bag and no possession limit, and may split the season into three segments.

units.obligation_text: In Oregon and Washington permit zones, the hunting season is closed on dusky Canada geese. ... Hunting of geese will only be by hunters possessing a State-issued permit authorizing them to do so.
units.actor: hunters in Oregon and Washington permit zones
units.action_summary: In Oregon and Washington permit zones, dusky Canada geese hunting is closed, and goose hunting generally requires a State-issued permit.

units.obligation_text: Swans: Permits will be issued by the State and will authorize each permittee to take no more than 1 swan per season with each permit. Nevada may issue up to 2 permits per hunter. Montana and Utah may issue only 1 permit per hunter. Each State’s season may open no earlier than the Saturday nearest October 1 (September 29).
units.action_summary: State-issued swan permits authorize no more than one swan per permit per season, with specified per-hunter permit limits by State and earliest opening dates for seasons.

units.obligation_text: Montana: No more than 500 permits may be issued. The season must end no later than December 1. The State must implement a harvest-monitoring program to measure the species composition of the swan harvest and should use appropriate measures to maximize hunter compliance in reporting bill measurement and color information.
units.action_summary: Montana may issue up to 500 swan permits, must end the season by Dec 1, must implement a harvest-monitoring program, and should use measures to maximize hunter compliance in reporting required swan data.

units.obligation_text: Utah: No more than 2,000 permits may be issued. During the swan season, no more than 10 trumpeter swans may be taken. The season must end no later than the second Sunday in December (December 9) or upon attainment of 10 trumpeter swans in the harvest, whichever occurs earliest. The Utah season remains subject to the terms of the Memorandum of Agreement ... regarding harvest monitoring, season closure procedures, and education requirements to minimize the take of trumpeter swans during the swan season.
units.action_summary: Utah may issue up to 2,000 permits, limits trumpeter swan take to 10, must end season by Dec 9 or upon attainment of 10 trumpeters, and must follow MOA terms on monitoring, closures, and education.

units.obligation_text: Nevada: No more than 650 permits may be issued. During the swan season, no more than 5 trumpeter swans may be taken. The season must end no later than the Sunday following January 1 (January 6) or upon attainment of 5 trumpeter swans in the harvest, whichever occurs earliest.
units.action_summary: Nevada may issue up to 650 permits, limits trumpeter swan take to 5, and must end the season by Jan 6 or upon attainment of 5 trumpeters.

units.obligation_text: In addition, the States of Utah and Nevada must implement a harvest-monitoring program to measure the species composition of the swan harvest. The harvest-monitoring program must require that all harvested swans or their species-determinant parts be examined by either State or Federal biologists for the purpose of species classification.
units.action_summary: Utah and Nevada must implement harvest-monitoring programs requiring examination of harvested swans or their species-determinant parts by biologists to classify species.

units.obligation_text: The States should use appropriate measures to maximize hunter compliance in providing bagged swans for examination.
units.actor: States of Montana, Nevada, and Utah
units.action_summary: States are encouraged to use measures to maximize hunter compliance in providing harvested swans for examination.

units.obligation_text: Further, the States of Montana, Nevada, and Utah must achieve at least an 80-percent hunter compliance rate, or subsequent permits will be reduced by 10 percent.
units.actor: States of Montana, Nevada, and Utah
units.action_summary: Montana, Nevada, and Utah must achieve at least 80% hunter compliance in monitoring; failing which their subsequent permits will be reduced by 10%.

units.obligation_text: All three States must provide to the Service by June 30, 2019, a report detailing harvest, hunter participation, reporting compliance, and monitoring of swan populations in the designated hunt areas.
units.actor: States of Montana, Nevada, and Utah
units.action_summary: Montana, Nevada, and Utah must submit a report to the Service by June 30, 2019, detailing harvest, participation, reporting compliance, and monitoring of swan populations.

units.obligation_text: Tundra Swans: Permits will be issued by the States that authorize the take of no more than 1 tundra swan per permit. A second permit may be issued to hunters from unused permits remaining after the first drawing. The States must obtain harvest and hunter participation data.
units.action_summary: States will issue tundra swan permits authorizing one swan per permit; second permits may be issued from unused permits; States must collect harvest and hunter participation data.

units.obligation_text: In the Atlantic Flyway — The season may be 90 days, between October 1 and January 31. In North Carolina, no more than 6,250 permits may be issued. In Virginia, no more than 750 permits may be issued.
units.action_summary: Atlantic Flyway tundra swan seasons may be up to 90 days; North Carolina may issue up to 6,250 permits; Virginia up to 750 permits.

units.obligation_text: In the Central Flyway — The season may be 107 days, between the Saturday nearest October 1 (September 29) and January 31. In the Central Flyway portion of Montana, no more than 625 permits may be issued. In North Dakota, no more than 2,500 permits may be issued. In South Dakota, no more than 1,875 permits may be issued.
units.actor: States (Central Flyway, Montana, North Dakota, South Dakota)
units.action_summary: Central Flyway tundra swan seasons may be up to 107 days with listed permit caps for Montana (625), North Dakota (2,500), and South Dakota (1,875).

units.obligation_text: Registrants may conduct resident Canada goose nest and egg destruction activities at any time of year.
units.action_summary: Registrants are permitted to destroy resident Canada goose nests and eggs at any time of year.

units.actor: Homeowners’ associations and local governments or their agents
units.action_summary: Homeowners' associations and local governments (or their agents) must comply with all applicable State and local laws and regulations when destroying nests and eggs.

units.obligation_text: Authorized agricultural producers and their employees and agents may conduct management and control activities, involving the take of resident Canada geese, under this section between May 1 and August 31.
units.actor: Authorized agricultural producers and their employees and agents
units.action_summary: Authorized agricultural producers and their employees and agents may conduct management and control activities involving take between May 1 and August 31.

units.actor: Authorized agricultural producers and their employees and agents
units.action_summary: Destruction of resident Canada goose nests and eggs is permitted at any time of year (exception to date-limited management activities).

units.obligation_text: Authorized State and Tribal wildlife agencies and their employees and agents may conduct management and control activities, involving the take of resident Canada geese, under this section between April 1 and August 31.
units.actor: Authorized State and Tribal wildlife agencies and their employees and agents
units.action_summary: Authorized State and Tribal wildlife agencies and their employees and agents may conduct management and control activities involving take between April 1 and August 31.

units.action_summary: Destruction of resident Canada goose nests and eggs is permitted at any time of year (exception to date-limited management activities).

units.actor: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, in cooperation with the States

units.action_summary: The draft post-delisting monitoring plan calls for population monitoring every 5 years for a 20-year period.

title: Endangered and Threatened Species: Endangered Status for the Island Marble Butterfly and Designation of Critical Habitat

units.obligation_text: Within the critical habitat area on San Juan Island, Washington, the physical or biological features essential to the conservation of the island marble butterfly consist of:
units.action_summary: Defines the physical and biological features that constitute critical habitat for the island marble butterfly.

units.obligation_text: Open, primarily treeless areas with short-statured forb- and grass-dominated vegetation that include diverse topographic features such as ridgelines, hills, and bluffs for patrolling, dispersal corridors between habitat patches, and some south-facing terrain. Areas must be large enough to allow for the development of patchy-population dynamics, allowing for multiple small populations to establish within the area.
units.action_summary: Areas must be large enough and have specified topographic and vegetation characteristics to allow patchy-population dynamics and multiple small populations to establish.

units.obligation_text: Low- to medium-density larval host plants for egg-laying and larval development, with both flower buds and blooms on them between the months of May through July. Larval host plants may be any of the following: Brassica rapa, Sisymbrium altissimum, or Lepidium virginicum.
units.action_summary: Larval host plants included in critical habitat should be low- to medium-density, have buds and blooms May–July, and may be any of the listed species.

units.obligation_text: Adult nectar resources in flower and short-statured, white-flowering plants in bloom used for mate-finding, which may include, but are not limited to Abronia latifolia (yellow sand verbena), Achillea millefolium (yarrow), Amsinckia menziesii (small-flowered fiddleneck), Cakile edentula (American sea rocket), Cerastium arvense (field chickweed), Erodium cicutarium (common stork’s bill), Geranium molle (dovefoot geranium), Hypochaeris radicata (hairy cat’s ear), Lomatium utriculatum (common lomatium), Lupinus littoralis (seashore lupine), Myosotis discolor (common forget-me-not), Ranunculus californicus (California buttercup), Rubus ursinus (trailing blackberry), Taraxacum officinale (dandelion), Toxicoscordion venenosum (death camas, formerly known as Zigadenus venenosus), and Triteleia grandiflora (Howell’s Brodiaea, formerly Brodiaea howellii).
units.action_summary: Adult nectar resources in bloom that are used for mate-finding may include the listed plant species (but are not limited to them).

units.obligation_text: Areas of undisturbed vegetation surrounding larval host plants sufficient to provide secure sites for diapause and pupation. The vegetation surrounding larval host plants must be left standing for a sufficient period of time for the island marble butterfly to complete its life cycle.
units.actor: The vegetation surrounding larval host plants
units.action_summary: Vegetation around larval host plants must remain undisturbed and be left standing long enough for diapause, pupation, and completion of the butterfly's life cycle.

units.obligation_text: Critical habitat does not include manmade structures (such as buildings, aqueducts, runways, roads, and other paved areas) and the land on which they are located existing within the legal boundaries on the effective date of this rule.
units.action_summary: Manmade structures and the land they occupy as of the rule's effective date are excluded from critical habitat.

title: Endangered and Threatened Species: Designation of Critical Habitat for Sonoyta Mud Turtle

units.obligation_text: Section 4(b)(2) of the Act states that the Secretary of the Interior shall designate and make revisions to critical habitat on the basis of the best available scientific data after taking into consideration the economic impact, the impact on national security, and any other relevant impact of specifying any particular area as critical habitat.
units.action_summary: Designate and revise critical habitat based on best scientific data and consideration of economic, national security, and other relevant impacts.

units.obligation_text: The Secretary may exclude an area from critical habitat if he determines that the benefits of such exclusion outweigh the benefits of specifying such area as part of the critical habitat, unless he determines, based on the best scientific data available, that the failure to designate such area as critical habitat will result in the extinction of the species.
units.action_summary: May exclude areas from critical habitat when benefits of exclusion outweigh benefits of designation, unless exclusion would result in extinction.

units.obligation_text: Designations and revisions of critical habitat can only be completed by issuing a rule.
units.actor: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service / Secretary
units.action_summary: Must issue a rule to complete designations or revisions of critical habitat.

units.obligation_text: Under the Act, any species that is determined to be endangered or threatened requires critical habitat to be designated, to the maximum extent prudent and determinable.
units.action_summary: When a species is listed as endangered or threatened, critical habitat must be designated to the maximum extent prudent and determinable.

units.obligation_text: Critical habitat receives protection under section 7 of the Act through the requirement that Federal agencies ensure, in consultation with the Service, that any action they authorize, fund, or carry out is not likely to result in the destruction or adverse modification of critical habitat.
units.action_summary: Federal agencies must ensure, in consultation with the Service, that actions they authorize, fund, or carry out are not likely to destroy or adversely modify critical habitat.

units.obligation_text: The designation of critical habitat does not allow the government or public to access private lands.
units.action_summary: Government and public are not allowed to access private lands solely because of a critical habitat designation.

units.obligation_text: Such designation does not require implementation of restoration, recovery, or enhancement measures by non-Federal landowners.
units.action_summary: Non-Federal landowners are not required to implement restoration, recovery, or enhancement measures due to critical habitat designation.

units.obligation_text: Where a landowner requests Federal agency funding or authorization for an action that may affect a listed species or critical habitat, the consultation requirements of section 7(a)(2) of the Act would apply.
units.action_summary: If a landowner requests federal funding or authorization for an action that may affect listed species or critical habitat, the federal agency must follow section 7(a)(2) consultation requirements.

units.obligation_text: Even in the event of a destruction or adverse modification finding, the obligation of the Federal action agency and the landowner is not to restore or recover the species, but to implement reasonable and prudent alternatives to avoid destruction or adverse modification of critical habitat.
units.actor: Federal action agency and the landowner
units.action_summary: If destruction/adverse modification is found, the agency and landowner must implement reasonable and prudent alternatives rather than restore or recover the species.

units.obligation_text: The obligation ... is not to restore or recover the species
units.actor: Federal action agency and the landowner
units.action_summary: Agency and landowner are not required to restore or recover the species after a destruction/adverse modification finding.

units.obligation_text: The obligation ... is to implement reasonable and prudent alternatives to avoid destruction or adverse modification of critical habitat.
units.actor: Federal action agency and the landowner
units.action_summary: Agency and landowner must implement reasonable and prudent alternatives to avoid destruction or adverse modification.

units.obligation_text: We will accept comments on the proposed rule or draft economic analysis that are received or postmarked on or before February 4, 2019.
units.actor: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (the agency) / commenters
units.action_summary: Agency will accept comments received or postmarked by February 4, 2019.

units.obligation_text: Comments submitted electronically using the Federal eRulemaking Portal (see ADDRESSES, below) must be received by 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time on the closing date.
units.action_summary: Electronic comments must be received by 11:59 p.m. ET on the closing date.

units.obligation_text: We must receive requests for public hearings, in writing, at the address shown in FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT by January 22, 2019.
units.action_summary: Requests for public hearings must be received in writing by January 22, 2019.

units.obligation_text: You may submit comments on the proposed rule or draft economic analysis by one of the following methods:
units.action_summary: Public commenters are permitted to submit comments by the listed methods.

units.obligation_text: (1) Electronically: Go to the Federal eRulemaking Portal ... You may submit a comment by clicking on "Comment Now!"
units.action_summary: Commenters may submit comments electronically via regulations.gov by using 'Comment Now!'.

units.obligation_text: (2) By hard copy: Submit by U.S. mail or hand-delivery to: Public Comments Processing, Attn: FWS–R2–ES–2017–0014, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, MS: BPHC, 5275 Leesburg Pike, Falls Church, VA 22041–3803.
units.action_summary: Commenters may submit comments by U.S. mail or hand-delivery to the specified address.

units.obligation_text: We request that you send comments only by the methods described above.
units.action_summary: The agency requests commenters use only the described submission methods.

units.obligation_text: We will post all comments on http://www.regulations.gov.
units.actor: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (the agency)
units.action_summary: Agency will post all comments to regulations.gov.

units.obligation_text: For comments submitted via hard copy, we will post your entire comment—including your personal identifying information—on http://www.regulations.gov.
units.actor: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (the agency)
units.action_summary: Agency will post entire hard-copy comments, including personal identifying information, to regulations.gov.

units.obligation_text: You may request at the top of your document that we withhold personal information such as your street address, phone number, or email address from public review; however, we cannot guarantee that we will be able to do so.
units.action_summary: Commenters may request that certain personal information be withheld from public review (subject to the agency's ability to do so).

units.obligation_text: Comments and materials we receive, as well as supporting documentation we used in preparing this proposed rule, will be available for public inspection on http://www.regulations.gov, or by appointment, during normal business hours, at the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Arizona Ecological Services Field Office.
units.actor: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (the agency)
units.action_summary: Agency will make received comments and supporting documentation available for public inspection online or by appointment.

units.obligation_text: We request comments or information from other concerned government agencies, the scientific community, industry, or any other interested party concerning this proposed rule.
units.actor: concerned government agencies, the scientific community, industry, and other interested parties
units.action_summary: Agency requests that these stakeholders submit comments or information concerning the proposed rule.

units.obligation_text: (1) The reasons why we should or should not designate habitat as "critical habitat" under section 4 of the Act (16 U.S.C. 1531 et seq.) including whether there are threats to the subspecies from human activity, the degree of which can be expected to increase due to the designation, and whether that increase in threat outweighs the benefit of designation such that the designation of critical habitat may not be prudent.
units.action_summary: Provide reasons for or against designating habitat as critical habitat, including whether threats from human activity would increase and outweigh benefits.

units.obligation_text: (2) Specific information on:
units.action_summary: Provide specific pieces of information listed in subparts (a)–(e).

units.obligation_text: (a) The amount and distribution of Sonoyta mud turtle habitat;
units.action_summary: Provide information about the amount and distribution of habitat for the Sonoyta mud turtle.

units.obligation_text: (b) What areas, occupied at the time of listing and that contain the physical or biological features essential to the conservation of the subspecies, should be included in the designation and why;
units.action_summary: Identify occupied areas with essential features that should be included in the designation and explain why.

units.obligation_text: (c) Special management considerations or protection that may be needed in critical habitat areas we are proposing, including managing for the potential effects of climate change;
units.action_summary: Provide information on special management or protections needed in proposed critical habitat, including climate adaptation.

units.obligation_text: (d) What areas not occupied at the time of listing are essential for the conservation of the subspecies and why;
units.action_summary: Identify unoccupied areas that are essential for conservation and explain why.

units.obligation_text: (e) Current habitat information within the Rio Sonoyta watershed and whether any potential habitat areas there may be essential to the conservation of the Sonoyta mud turtle.
units.action_summary: Provide current habitat information for the Rio Sonoyta watershed and whether those areas are essential.

units.obligation_text: (3) Land use designations and current or planned activities in the subject areas and their possible impacts on proposed critical habitat.
units.action_summary: Provide information on land use designations and activities and their potential impacts on proposed critical habitat.

units.obligation_text: (4) Information on the projected and reasonably likely impacts of climate change on the Sonoyta mud turtle and proposed critical habitat.
units.action_summary: Provide projected and reasonably likely impacts of climate change on the species and proposed habitat.

units.obligation_text: (5) Any probable economic, national security, or other relevant impacts of designating any area that may be included in the final designation, and the benefits of including or excluding areas that may be impacted.
units.action_summary: Provide information on probable economic, national security, or other impacts and benefits of including or excluding areas.

units.obligation_text: (6) Information on the extent to which the description of probable economic impacts in the draft economic analysis is a reasonable estimate of the likely economic impacts of the designation.
units.action_summary: Comment on whether the draft economic analysis reasonably estimates likely economic impacts.

units.obligation_text: (7) Whether any specific areas we are proposing for critical habitat designation should be considered for exclusion under section 4(b)(2) of the Act, and whether the benefits of potentially excluding any specific area outweigh the benefits of including that area under section 4(b)(2) of the Act.
units.action_summary: Identify proposed areas that should be considered for exclusion under section 4(b)(2) and whether exclusion benefits outweigh inclusion benefits.

units.obligation_text: (8) The likelihood of adverse social reactions to the designation of critical habitat, as discussed in the draft economic analysis, and how the consequences of such reactions, if likely to occur, would relate to the conservation and regulatory benefits of the proposed critical habitat designation.
units.action_summary: Provide information on likely adverse social reactions and how their consequences relate to conservation and regulatory benefits.

units.obligation_text: (9) Whether we could improve or modify our approach to designating critical habitat in any way to provide for greater public participation and understanding, or to better accommodate public concerns and comments.
units.action_summary: Suggest improvements or modifications to the agency's approach to designation to increase public participation and address concerns.

title: Endangered and Threatened Species: Louisiana Pinesnake; Section 4(d) Rule

units.obligation_text: Except as noted in paragraph (i)(3) of this section, all prohibitions and provisions of §§ 17.31 and 17.32 apply to the Louisiana pinesnake.
units.actor: persons subject to §§ 17.31 and 17.32 (the public/persons taking actions affecting the species)
units.action_summary: All prohibitions and provisions in §§ 17.31 and 17.32 govern activities affecting the Louisiana pinesnake, except as provided in paragraph (i)(3).

units.obligation_text: Incidental take of the Louisiana pinesnake will not be considered a violation of section 9 of the Act if the take results from any of the following activities:
units.actor: any person whose actions result in incidental take of the Louisiana pinesnake
units.action_summary: Incidental take is exempted from violation of section 9 when it results from listed activities.

units.obligation_text: Forestry activities, including tree thinning, harvest (including clearcutting), planting and replanting pines, as well as other silviculture practices, that maintain lands in forest land use and that result in the establishment and maintenance of open canopy conditions through time across the landscape.
units.actor: persons conducting forestry or silviculture activities
units.action_summary: Forestry and silviculture activities that maintain forest land use and open canopy are exempted as sources of incidental take outside known EOHAs.

units.obligation_text: Prescribed burning, including all firebreak establishment and maintenance actions, as well as actions taken to control wildfires.
units.actor: persons conducting prescribed burning or wildfire control actions
units.action_summary: Prescribed burning and related fire management actions outside known EOHAs are exempted as sources of incidental take.

units.obligation_text: Herbicide application that is generally targeted for invasive plant species control and midstory and understory woody vegetation control, but also for site preparation when applied in a manner that minimizes long-term impact to noninvasive herbaceous vegetation.
units.action_summary: Herbicide applications aimed at invasive species control, midstory/understory control, or site preparation (with minimal long-term impact) outside known EOHAs are exempted as sources of incidental take.

units.obligation_text: All exempted herbicide applications must be conducted in a manner consistent with Federal and applicable State laws, including Environmental Protection Agency label restrictions and herbicide application guidelines as prescribed by herbicide manufacturers.
units.action_summary: Exempt herbicide applications must comply with federal and state laws, EPA label restrictions, and manufacturer guidelines.

units.obligation_text: Within any known EOHAs on lands with suitable or preferable soils that are forested, undeveloped, or non-farmed (i.e., not cultivated on an annual basis) and adjacent to forested lands, activities described in paragraphs (i)(3)(i)(A) through (C) of this section provided that:
units.actor: persons conducting activities described in (i)(3)(i)(A)–(C) within known EOHAs on specified lands
units.action_summary: The exemptions for forestry, prescribed burning, and herbicide applications also apply within certain EOHAs on suitable soils only if conditions in (ii)(A) and (ii)(B) are met.

units.obligation_text: Activities do not cause subsurface disturbance, including, but not limited to, wind-rowing, stumping, disking (except during firebreak creation or maintenance), root-raking, drum chopping, below-ground shearing, and bedding.
units.actor: activities/persons conducting the activities described in (i)(3)(i)(A)–(C) within the specified EOHAs
units.action_summary: Within specified EOHAs, the exempted activities must not cause subsurface disturbance such as wind-rowing, stumping, disking (except for firebreak work), root-raking, drum chopping, below-ground shearing, or bedding.

units.obligation_text: In highly degraded areas with no herbaceous vegetation, subsurface disturbance will be limited to that less than 4 inches in depth.
units.actor: persons conducting activities in highly degraded areas with no herbaceous vegetation
units.action_summary: In highly degraded, vegetation-free areas, any allowed subsurface disturbance is limited to less than 4 inches depth.

units.obligation_text: Activities do not inhibit the persistence of suitable Louisiana pinesnake and Baird’s pocket gopher habitat.
units.actor: persons conducting the activities described in (i)(3)(i)(A)–(C) within the specified EOHAs
units.action_summary: Within the specified EOHAs, activities are allowed only if they do not prevent the continued existence of suitable habitat for the Louisiana pinesnake and Baird's pocket gopher.

title: Endangered and Threatened Species: Atlantic Pigtoe; Critical Habitat Designation

units.obligation_text: Except as noted in paragraph (a)(2) of this section, all prohibitions and provisions of §§ 17.31 and 17.32 apply to the Atlantic pigtoe.
units.actor: persons subject to §§ 17.31 and 17.32 (the regulated public)
units.action_summary: The prohibitions and provisions in §§ 17.31 and 17.32 apply to the Atlantic pigtoe.

units.obligation_text: Incidental take of the Atlantic pigtoe will not be considered a violation of the Act if the take results from any of the following activities:
units.actor: persons who incidentally take Atlantic pigtoe
units.action_summary: Incidental take is not a violation if it results from the listed activities.
units.modal_raw: will not be considered a violation

units.obligation_text: Species restoration efforts by State wildlife agencies, including collection of broodstock, tissue collection for genetic analysis, captive propagation, and subsequent stocking into currently occupied and unoccupied areas within the historical range of the species.
units.action_summary: Incidental take resulting from state species restoration efforts (broodstock collection, tissue sampling, captive propagation, stocking) is not a violation.
units.modal_raw: will not be considered a violation if the take results from

units.obligation_text: Channel restoration projects that create natural, physically stable, ecologically functioning streams (or stream and wetland systems) that are reconnected with their groundwater aquifers. These projects can be accomplished using a variety of methods, but the desired outcome is a natural channel with low shear stress (force of water moving against the channel); bank heights that enable reconnection to the floodplain; a reconnection of surface and groundwater systems, resulting in perennial flows in the channel; riffles and pools comprised of existing soil, rock, and wood instead of large imported materials; low compaction of soils within adjacent riparian areas; and inclusion of riparian wetlands.
units.actor: those conducting channel restoration projects (project proponents/implementers)
units.action_summary: Incidental take from channel restoration projects that produce natural, stable, ecologically functioning streams (with described characteristics) is not a violation.
units.modal_raw: will not be considered a violation if the take results from

units.obligation_text: Bank stabilization projects that use bioengineering methods to replace pre-existing, bare, eroding stream banks with vegetated, stable stream banks, thereby reducing bank erosion and instream sedimentation and improving habitat conditions for the species. Following these bioengineering methods, stream banks may be stabilized using live stakes (live, vegetative cuttings inserted or tamped into the ground in a manner that allows the stake to take root and grow), live fascines (live branch cuttings, usually willows, bound together into long, cigar shaped bundles), or brush layering (cuttings or branches of easily rooted tree species layered between successive lifts of soil fill).
units.actor: those conducting bank stabilization projects (project implementers)
units.action_summary: Incidental take resulting from bank stabilization projects that use specified bioengineering methods is not a violation.
units.modal_raw: will not be considered a violation if the take results from

units.obligation_text: These methods would not include the sole use of quarried rock (rip-rap) or the use of rock baskets or gabion structures.
units.actor: those conducting bank stabilization projects (project implementers)
units.action_summary: Sole use of quarried rock (rip-rap), rock baskets, or gabion structures is excluded from the allowed bioengineering methods.

units.obligation_text: Silviculture practices and forest management activities that:
units.action_summary: Incidental take resulting from silviculture and forest management activities is not a violation if they meet the following subconditions.
units.modal_raw: will not be considered a violation if the take results from

units.obligation_text: Implement highest-standard best management practices, particularly for Streamside Management Zones, stream crossings, and forest roads;
units.action_summary: Practitioners must implement highest-standard best management practices for certain forestry features as a condition of the exception.

units.obligation_text: Comply with forest practice guidelines related to water quality standards, or comply with Sustainable Forestry Initiative/Forest Stewardship Council/American Tree Farm System certification standards for both forest management and responsible fiber sourcing.
units.action_summary: Practitioners must comply with water-quality-related forest practice guidelines or recognized certification standards as a condition of the exception.

units.obligation_text: The coordinates or plot points or both on which each map is based are available to the public at http://www.regulations.gov under Docket No. FWS–R4–ES–2018–0046 and at the field office responsible for this designation.
units.action_summary: The public may access the coordinates/plot points for the critical habitat maps at Regulations.gov and at the responsible field office.
