units.action_summary: The public may obtain field office location information by contacting Service regional offices (addresses listed at 50 CFR 2.2).

title: Endangered and Threatened Species: Eastern Black Rail; 12-Month Petition Finding

units.obligation_text: Prohibitions. The following activities are prohibited:
units.action_summary: General prohibition header: the following listed activities are prohibited.

units.obligation_text: Purposeful take of an eastern black rail, including capture, handling, or other activities.
units.action_summary: Prohibits purposeful take (capture, handling, etc.) of eastern black rails.

units.obligation_text: Prescribed burn activities that result in the incidental take of eastern black rails when the activity occurs:
units.action_summary: Prohibits prescribed burns that result in incidental take of eastern black rails in specified circumstances.

units.obligation_text: During the nesting, brooding, or post-breeding flightless molt period;
units.action_summary: Prescribed burns during nesting, brooding, or post-breeding flightless molt that result in incidental take are prohibited.

units.obligation_text: Outside of the nesting, brooding, or post-breeding flightless molt period, unless best management practices that minimize effects of the prescribed burn on the eastern black rail are employed.
units.action_summary: Prescribed burns outside the sensitive periods that result in incidental take are prohibited unless best management practices (BMPs) minimizing effects are employed.

units.obligation_text: Examples of best management practices include employing slow burn fires;
units.action_summary: Using slow burn fires is an example of a BMP that can allow prescribed burns to avoid prohibition.

units.obligation_text: limiting the block of land burned to ensure suitable dense cover habitat remains for the eastern black rail;
units.action_summary: Limiting the burned area to retain suitable dense cover is an example BMP to minimize effects.

units.obligation_text: employing patch or refugia techniques to allow for eastern black rails to survive or escape fire;
units.action_summary: Using patch or refugia techniques is an example BMP that can reduce impacts to eastern black rails.

units.obligation_text: avoiding the use of ring fires or perimeter fires.
units.action_summary: Avoiding ring or perimeter fires is an example BMP to minimize effects on eastern black rails.

units.obligation_text: Mowing, haying, and mechanical treatment activities in emergent wetlands that result in the incidental take of eastern black rails when the activity occurs during the nesting, brooding, or post-breeding flightless molt period, except in accordance with paragraph (f)(2)(iii) of this section.
units.actor: persons conducting mowing, haying, or mechanical treatments
units.action_summary: Prohibits mowing/haying/mechanical treatments in emergent wetlands causing incidental take during sensitive periods, except as allowed under §17.41(f)(2)(iii).

units.obligation_text: Grazing activities on public lands that result in the incidental take of eastern black rails when the activity:
units.actor: persons conducting grazing activities on public lands
units.action_summary: Prohibits grazing on public lands that results in incidental take of eastern black rails under specified conditions.

units.obligation_text: Occurs during the nesting, brooding, or post-breeding flightless molt period;
units.actor: persons conducting grazing activities on public lands
units.action_summary: Grazing that occurs during nesting, brooding, or post-breeding flightless molt and results in incidental take is prohibited.

units.obligation_text: Involves intensive or high-density grazing that occurs on suitable occupied eastern black rail habitat;
units.actor: persons conducting grazing activities on public lands
units.action_summary: Intensive or high-density grazing on suitable occupied habitat that results in incidental take is prohibited.

units.obligation_text: Does not support the maintenance of appropriate dense vegetation cover for the eastern black rail.
units.actor: persons conducting grazing activities on public lands
units.action_summary: Grazing that fails to maintain appropriate dense vegetation cover, resulting in incidental take, is prohibited.

units.obligation_text: Possession and other acts with unlawfully taken eastern black rails. It is unlawful to possess, sell, deliver, carry, transport, or ship, by any means whatsoever, any eastern black rail that was taken in violation of section 9(a)(1)(B) and 9(a)(1)(C) of the Act or State laws.
units.action_summary: Prohibits possession, sale, transport, or shipment of eastern black rails unlawfully taken in violation of the Act or State laws.

units.obligation_text: Import and export of the eastern black rail.
units.action_summary: Prohibits import and export of eastern black rails.

units.obligation_text: Delivery, receipt, carry for transport, or shipment in interstate or foreign commerce, by any means whatsoever, and in the course of a commercial activity, of any eastern black rail.
units.action_summary: Prohibits interstate or foreign delivery, receipt, transport, or shipment of eastern black rails in commerce or as a commercial activity.

units.obligation_text: Sale or offer for sale in interstate or foreign commerce of any eastern black rail.
units.action_summary: Prohibits sale or offer for sale of eastern black rails in interstate or foreign commerce.

units.obligation_text: Exceptions from prohibitions.
units.actor: persons and entities subject to these rules
units.action_summary: Header indicating exceptions to the prohibitions listed in paragraph (f)(1).

units.obligation_text: All of the provisions of § 17.32 apply to the eastern black rail.
units.action_summary: Permits or governs actions under the provisions of §17.32 as they apply to the eastern black rail (i.e., §17.32's permit provisions apply).

units.obligation_text: Any employee or agent of the Service, of the National Marine Fisheries Service, or of a State conservation agency that is operating a conservation program for the eastern black rail pursuant to the terms of a cooperative agreement with the Service in accordance with section 6(c) of the Act, who is designated by his agency for such purposes, may, when acting in the course of his official duties, take eastern black rails.
units.actor: designated employees or agents of the Service, NMFS, or State conservation agencies operating an approved conservation program
units.action_summary: Designated employees/agents acting in official duties may take eastern black rails as part of approved conservation programs.

units.obligation_text: Mowing or mechanical treatment activities in emergent wetlands that: (A) Occur during the nesting, brooding, or post-breeding flightless molt period; and (B) Are maintenance requirements to ensure safety and operational needs for existing infrastructure.
units.actor: persons performing mowing or mechanical treatments
units.action_summary: Permits mowing or mechanical treatments during sensitive periods if they are maintenance actions required for safety/operations for existing infrastructure.

units.obligation_text: Occur during the nesting, brooding, or post-breeding flightless molt period;
units.actor: persons performing mowing or mechanical treatments
units.action_summary: Condition (A): to qualify for the exception, the activity must occur during nesting, brooding, or post-breeding flightless molt period.

units.obligation_text: Are maintenance requirements to ensure safety and operational needs for existing infrastructure.
units.actor: persons performing mowing or mechanical treatments
units.action_summary: Condition (B): to qualify for the exception, activities must be maintenance needs for safety/operations of existing infrastructure.

units.obligation_text: Existing infrastructure may include existing fire breaks,
units.action_summary: Provides example that existing fire breaks are infrastructure qualifying maintenance exception.

units.obligation_text: roads,
units.action_summary: Provides example that roads are infrastructure qualifying maintenance exception.

units.obligation_text: transmission corridor rights-of-way,
units.action_summary: Provides example that transmission corridor rights-of-way qualify as existing infrastructure for the exception.

units.obligation_text: and fence lines.
units.action_summary: Provides example that fence lines qualify as existing infrastructure for the exception.

units.action_summary: Incidental take is excepted from section 9 prohibitions when it results from specified activities.
units.modal_raw: will not be considered a violation of section 9 of the Act

units.obligation_text: Species restoration efforts by State wildlife agencies, including collection of broodstock, tissue collection for genetic analysis, captive propagation, and subsequent stocking into currently occupied and unoccupied areas within the historical range of the species.

units.obligation_text: Channel restoration projects that create natural, physically stable, ecologically functioning streams (or stream and wetland systems) that are reconnected with their groundwater aquifers.

units.action_summary: Incidental take during channel restoration projects that create natural, stable, functioning streams reconnected to groundwater is not a violation.

units.obligation_text: Bank heights that enable reconnection to the floodplain.

units.obligation_text: Streambank stabilization projects that utilize bioengineering methods to replace pre-existing, bare, eroding stream banks with vegetated, stable stream banks, thereby reducing bank erosion and instream sedimentation and improving habitat conditions for the species.

units.actor: project implementers conducting streambank stabilization projects
units.action_summary: Prohibits stabilizing stream banks solely with quarried rock, rock baskets, or gabion structures.

units.obligation_text: Silviculture practices and forest management activities that:
units.action_summary: Incidental take resulting from silviculture and forest management activities meeting specified criteria is not a violation.
units.modal_raw: will not be considered a violation of section 9 of the Act

units.obligation_text: Implement highest-standard best management practices, particularly for Streamside Management Zones, stream crossings, and forest roads;
units.action_summary: Practices must implement highest-standard best management practices, especially for stream-adjacent zones, crossings, and roads, to qualify for the exception.

units.obligation_text: Comply with forest practice guidelines related to water quality standards,
units.action_summary: Practices must comply with forest practice guidelines related to water quality standards to qualify for the exception.

units.obligation_text: or comply with Sustainable Forestry Initiative/Forest Stewardship Council/American Tree Farm System certification standards for both forest management and responsible fiber sourcing.
units.action_summary: As an alternative, practices may comply with specified certification standards (SFI, FSC, ATFS) for forest management and responsible fiber sourcing to qualify for the exception.

units.obligation_text: Transportation projects that provide for fish passage at stream crossings;
units.action_summary: Incidental take during transportation projects that provide fish passage at stream crossings is not a violation.
units.modal_raw: will not be considered a violation of section 9 of the Act

units.obligation_text: Projects carried out in the species’ range under the Working Lands for Wildlife program of the Natural Resources Conservation Service, U.S. Department of Agriculture.
units.actor: projects carried out under the Working Lands for Wildlife program (NRCS/USDA)
units.action_summary: Incidental take during projects under the NRCS Working Lands for Wildlife program is not a violation.
units.modal_raw: will not be considered a violation of section 9 of the Act

title: Endangered and Threatened Species: Designation of Critical Habitat for the Candy Darter

units.obligation_text: Within these areas, the physical or biological features essential to the conservation of the candy darter consist of the following components:
units.actor: critical habitat for the candy darter (the designation)
units.action_summary: The critical habitat designation must consist of the listed physical or biological features.

units.obligation_text: Ratios or densities of nonnative species that allow for maintaining populations of candy darters.
units.actor: critical habitat for the candy darter (the designation)
units.action_summary: Maintain ratios or densities of nonnative species that allow candy darter populations to be maintained.

units.obligation_text: Blend of unembedded gravel and cobble that allows for normal breeding, feeding, and sheltering behavior.
units.actor: critical habitat for the candy darter (the designation)
units.action_summary: Include unembedded gravel and cobble substrate suitable for breeding, feeding, and sheltering.

units.obligation_text: Adequate water quality characterized by seasonally moderated temperatures and physical and chemical parameters (e.g., pH, dissolved oxygen levels, turbidity) that support normal behavior, growth, and viability of all life stages of the candy darter.
units.actor: critical habitat for the candy darter (the designation)
units.action_summary: Provide water quality with appropriate temperature and chemical/physical parameters to support all life stages.

units.obligation_text: Abundant, diverse benthic macroinvertebrate community (e.g., mayfly nymphs, midge larvae, caddisfly larvae) that allows for normal feeding behavior.
units.actor: critical habitat for the candy darter (the designation)
units.action_summary: Provide an abundant, diverse benthic macroinvertebrate community to support feeding.

units.obligation_text: Sufficient water quantity and velocities that support normal behavior, growth, and viability of all life stages of the candy darter.
units.actor: critical habitat for the candy darter (the designation)
units.action_summary: Maintain adequate water quantity and flow velocities to support the species' life stages.

units.obligation_text: Critical habitat does not include manmade structures (such as buildings, aqueducts, runways, roads, and other paved areas) and the land on which they are located existing within the legal boundaries on the effective date of this rule.
units.action_summary: Exclude existing manmade structures and the land they occupy from the critical habitat designation.

units.obligation_text: The coordinates or plot points or both on which each map is based are available to the public at https://www.fws.gov/northeast/candydarter/, at http://www.regulations.gov at Docket No. FWS–R5–ES–2018–0050, and at the field office responsible for this designation.
units.action_summary: The public may access the coordinates/plot points for each map at the listed websites and the responsible field office.

units.obligation_text: You may obtain field office location information by contacting one of the Service regional offices, the addresses of which are listed at 50 CFR 2.2.
units.action_summary: The public may obtain field office location information by contacting a Service regional office (addresses in 50 CFR 2.2).

title: Subsistence Management Regulations for Public Lands in Alaska-Cook Inlet Area Regulations

units.obligation_text: Unless restricted by regulations in this section, or unless restricted under the terms of a subsistence fishing permit, you may take fish at any time in the Cook Inlet Area.
units.actor: you (fishers in the Cook Inlet Area)
units.action_summary: Fishers may take fish at any time in the Cook Inlet Area unless restricted by other regulations or permit terms.

units.obligation_text: If you take rainbow or steelhead trout incidentally in subsistence net fisheries, you may retain them for subsistence purposes, unless otherwise prohibited or provided for in this section.
units.action_summary: Incidental rainbow or steelhead trout taken in subsistence net fisheries may be retained for subsistence unless other rules prohibit it.

units.obligation_text: With jigging gear through the ice or rod-and-reel gear in open waters, there is an annual limit of two rainbow or steelhead trout 20 inches or longer, taken from Kenai Peninsula fresh waters.
units.actor: you (fishers using jigging or rod-and-reel gear)
units.action_summary: Annual limit of two rainbow or steelhead trout 20 inches or longer when using jigging or rod-and-reel in Kenai Peninsula fresh waters.

units.obligation_text: Under the authority of a Federal subsistence fishing permit, you may take only salmon, trout, Dolly Varden, and other char.
units.action_summary: Permit holders are allowed to take only salmon, trout, Dolly Varden, and other char.

units.obligation_text: All fish taken under the authority of a Federal subsistence fishing permit must be marked and recorded prior to leaving the fishing site.
units.action_summary: Fish taken under a federal permit must be marked and recorded before leaving the fishing site.

units.obligation_text: The fishing site includes the particular Federal public waters and/or adjacent shoreline from which the fish were harvested.
units.action_summary: Defines 'fishing site' as the federal waters and adjacent shoreline where fish were taken.

units.obligation_text: Marking means removing the dorsal fin.
units.action_summary: Specifies that marking a fish entails removing its dorsal fin.

units.obligation_text: You may not take grayling or burbot for subsistence purposes.
units.action_summary: Taking grayling or burbot for subsistence is prohibited.

units.obligation_text: You may take smelt with dip nets in fresh water only from April 1 through June 15.
units.action_summary: Smelt may be taken with dip nets in fresh water only between April 1 and June 15.

units.obligation_text: There are no harvest or possession limits for smelt.
units.action_summary: No harvest or possession limits apply to smelt.

units.obligation_text: You may take whitefish in the Tyone River drainage using gillnets.
units.action_summary: Whitefish may be taken with gillnets in the Tyone River drainage.

units.obligation_text: You may take fish by gear listed in this section unless restricted by other regulations in this section or under the terms of a Federal subsistence fishing permit (as may be modified by regulations in this section).
units.action_summary: Fishers may use listed gear unless restricted by other regulations or permit terms.

units.obligation_text: Seasons, harvest and possession limits, and methods and means for take are the same as for the taking of those species under Alaska sport fishing regulations (5 AAC 56 and 5 AAC 57) unless modified herein or by issuance of a Federal special action.
units.action_summary: Seasons, limits, and methods match Alaska sport fishing regulations unless modified here or by Federal special action.

units.obligation_text: Harvest limits may not be accumulated.
units.action_summary: Harvest limits cannot be combined over time (not accumulable).

units.obligation_text: Each household may harvest its annual salmon limits in one or more days.
units.action_summary: Households may take their annual salmon limits across one or multiple days.

units.obligation_text: All salmon harvested as part of a household annual limit must be reported to the Federal in-season manager within 72 hours of leaving the fishing site.
units.action_summary: Households must report all salmon taken under their annual limit to the Federal in-season manager within 72 hours after leaving the fishing site.

units.obligation_text: For Ninilchik residents, the household annual limits for Chinook salmon in the Kasilof River and for late-run Chinook salmon in the Kenai River are combined.
units.action_summary: Ninilchik households have combined annual limits for Chinook across the Kasilof and Kenai (late-run) rivers.

units.obligation_text: Household annual limits for salmon in Kasilof River fisheries are as follows:
units.action_summary: Introduces household annual limit thresholds for Kasilof River salmon species.

units.obligation_text: Sockeye: 25 allowed for each permit holder; additional 5 fish allowed for each household member.
units.action_summary: Sockeye household limit: 25 per permit holder plus 5 per household member.

units.obligation_text: Chinook: 10 allowed for each permit holder; additional 2 fish allowed for each household member.
units.action_summary: Chinook household limit: 10 per permit holder plus 2 per household member.

units.obligation_text: Coho: 10 allowed for each permit holder; additional 2 fish allowed for each household member.
units.action_summary: Coho household limit: 10 per permit holder plus 2 per household member.

units.obligation_text: Pink: 10 allowed for each permit holder; additional 2 fish allowed for each household member.
units.action_summary: Pink household limit: 10 per permit holder plus 2 per household member.

units.obligation_text: Residents of Ninilchik may take sockeye, Chinook, coho, and pink salmon through a dip net or rod and reel fishery on the upper mainstem of the Kasilof River from a Federal regulatory marker on the river below the outlet of Tustumena Lake downstream to a marker on the river approximately 2.8 miles below the Tustumena Lake boat ramp.
units.action_summary: Ninilchik residents may take listed salmon species by dip net or rod and reel at the specified stretch of the upper Kasilof River.

units.obligation_text: Residents using rod-and-reel gear may fish with up to two baited single or treble hooks.
units.action_summary: Rod-and-reel users are allowed up to two baited single or treble hooks.

units.obligation_text: Harvest seasons are as follows: Sockeye and Chinook June 16–August 15; Coho and Pink June 16–October 31; Rainbow and steelhead trout April 1–August 15. The Federal in-season manager will close the take of rainbow and steelhead trout after 200 have been harvested.
units.actor: you (fishers) and Federal in-season manager (for closure)
units.action_summary: Specifies seasons for species in the Kasilof dip net/rod and reel fishery and directs the Federal in-season manager to close rainbow/steelhead take after 200 harvested.

units.obligation_text: Residents of Ninilchik may harvest sockeye, Chinook, coho, and pink salmon through a fish wheel fishery in the Federal public waters of the upper mainstem of the Kasilof River.
units.action_summary: Ninilchik residents may harvest listed salmon species using a fish wheel in the specified Kasilof River waters.

units.obligation_text: Residents of Ninilchik may retain other species incidentally caught in the Kasilof River fish wheel except for rainbow or steelhead trout, which must be released and returned unharmed to the water.
units.action_summary: Incidental species may be retained except rainbow/steelhead which must be released unharmed.

units.obligation_text: Only one fish wheel may be operated on the Kasilof River.
units.action_summary: A single fish wheel only is allowed to operate on the Kasilof River.

units.obligation_text: The fish wheel must: Have a live box, be monitored when fishing, be stopped from fishing when it is not being monitored or used, and be installed and operated in compliance with any regulations and restrictions for its use within the Kenai National Wildlife Refuge.
units.action_summary: Fish wheel must include a live box, be monitored when fishing, not fish when unattended, and comply with Kenai NWR regulations.

units.obligation_text: One registration permit will be available and will be awarded by the Federal in-season fishery manager, in consultation with the Kenai National Wildlife Refuge manager, based on the merits of the operational plan.
units.actor: Federal in-season fishery manager (in consultation with Kenai NWR manager)
units.action_summary: Federal manager (with Kenai NWR manager) will award one registration permit based on operational plan merits.

units.obligation_text: The registration permit will be issued to an organization that, as the fish wheel owner, will be responsible for its construction, installation, operation, use, and removal in consultation with the Federal fishery manager.
units.action_summary: Permit issued to an organization that must be responsible for construction, installation, operation, use, and removal of the fish wheel in consultation with Federal fishery manager.

units.obligation_text: The owner may not rent or lease the fish wheel for personal gain.
units.action_summary: Owner is prohibited from renting or leasing the fish wheel for personal gain.

units.obligation_text: Prior to the season: Provide a written operational plan to the Federal fishery manager including a description of how fishing time and fish will be offered and distributed among households and residents of Ninilchik.
units.action_summary: Organization must submit a written operational plan before the season describing allocation and distribution among households/residents.

units.obligation_text: During the season: Mark the fish wheel with a wood, metal, or plastic plate that is at least 12 inches high by 12 inches wide, permanently affixed, and plainly visible and that contains the following information in letters and numerals at least 1 inch high: Registration permit number; organization’s name and address; and primary contact person name and telephone number.
units.action_summary: During the season, the fish wheel must be marked with a permanent 12x12 inch plate showing permit number, organization name/address, and a contact name/phone in 1-inch characters.

units.obligation_text: After the season: Provide written documentation of required evaluation information to the Federal fishery manager including, but not limited to, persons or households operating the gear, hours of operation, and number of each species caught and retained or released.
units.action_summary: Owner must provide post-season written evaluation data including operators, hours, and catch/retention/release counts by species.

units.obligation_text: People operating the fish wheel must have in possession a valid Federal subsistence fishing permit and remain onsite to monitor the fish wheel and remove all fish at least every hour.
units.action_summary: Operators must have a valid federal permit, remain onsite, monitor the fish wheel, and remove fish at least hourly.

units.obligation_text: Any person operating the fish wheel who is not the owner must attach to the fish wheel an additional wood, metal, or plastic plate that is at least 12 inches high by 12 inches wide, is plainly visible, and contains the person’s fishing permit number, name, and address in letters and numerals at least 1 inch high.
units.actor: person operating the fish wheel who is not the owner
units.action_summary: Non-owner operators must attach a 12x12 inch plate on the fish wheel with their permit number, name, and address in 1-inch characters.

units.obligation_text: The organization owning the fish wheel may operate the fish wheel for subsistence purposes on behalf of residents of Ninilchik by requesting a subsistence fishing permit that identifies a person who will be responsible for operating the fish wheel;
units.action_summary: Owner may operate the fish wheel on behalf of Ninilchik residents if a permit is requested that identifies a responsible operator.

units.obligation_text: The organization owning the fish wheel may operate the fish wheel for subsistence purposes on behalf of residents of Ninilchik by requesting a subsistence fishing permit that includes provisions for recording daily catches, the household to whom the catch was given, and other information determined to be necessary for effective resource management by the Federal fishery manager.
units.action_summary: Owner may operate on behalf of residents if the permit includes required recording provisions for daily catches and distribution to households as determined necessary by the Federal manager.

units.obligation_text: Fishing is allowed from June 16 through October 31 on the Kasilof River unless closed or otherwise restricted by Federal special action.
units.actor: you (fishers) and Federal in-season manager (who may close)
units.action_summary: Fishing is permitted June 16–Oct 31 on the Kasilof River unless closed or restricted by Federal special action.

units.obligation_text: Residents of Ninilchik may harvest sockeye, Chinook, coho, and pink salmon through an experimental community gillnet fishery in the Federal public waters of the upper mainstem of the Kasilof River from a Federal regulatory marker on the river below the outlet of Tustumena Lake downstream to the Tustumena Lake boat launch June 16 through August 15.
units.action_summary: Ninilchik residents may harvest listed salmon via experimental community gillnet in specified Kasilof River waters June 16–Aug 15.

units.obligation_text: The experimental community gillnet fishery will expire July 13, 2020.
units.action_summary: The experimental gillnet fishery has an expiration date of July 13, 2020.

units.obligation_text: Only one community gillnet may be operated on the Kasilof River. The gillnet may not be over 10 fathoms in length and may not obstruct more than half of the river width with stationary fishing gear. In addition, subsistence stationary gillnet gear may not be set within 200 feet of other subsistence stationary gear.
units.action_summary: Only one community gillnet allowed; it must be ≤10 fathoms, not obstruct >half the river width, and stationary gillnet gear cannot be set within 200 feet of other stationary gear.

units.obligation_text: Prior to the season: Provide a written operational plan to the Federal fishery manager including a description of fishing method, mesh size requirements, fishing time and location, and how fish will be offered and distributed among households and residents of Ninilchik.
units.action_summary: Prior to the season the organization must submit an operational plan describing method, mesh size, times/locations, and allocation/distribution among households/residents.

units.obligation_text: After the season: Provide written documentation of required evaluation information to the Federal fishery manager including, but not limited to, persons or households operating the gear, hours of operation, and number of each species caught and retained or released.
units.action_summary: After the season the organization must submit post-season evaluation data including operators, hours, and catch/retention/release numbers.

units.obligation_text: The experimental community gillnet is subject to compliance with applicable Kenai National Wildlife Refuge regulations and restrictions. It is the obligation of the gillnet owner to be familiar with such regulations and restrictions.
units.action_summary: The gillnet must comply with Kenai NWR rules, and the owner must be familiar with those regulations.
units.modal_raw: is subject to / is the obligation

units.obligation_text: The organization owning the gillnet may operate the net for subsistence purposes on behalf of residents of Ninilchik by requesting a subsistence fishing permit that identifies a person who will be responsible for fishing the gillnet and includes provisions for recording daily catches, the household to whom the catch was given, and other information determined to be necessary for effective resource management by the Federal fishery manager.
units.action_summary: Owner may operate the gillnet on behalf of residents if permit identifies responsible person and includes required catch-record provisions.

units.obligation_text: Residents of Ninilchik may retain other species incidentally caught in the Kasilof River experimental community gillnet fishery. The gillnet fishery will be closed when the retention of rainbow or steelhead trout has been restricted under Federal subsistence regulations.
units.actor: Residents of Ninilchik; Federal managers (for closure)
units.action_summary: Residents may retain incidental species; the fishery will close when retention of rainbow or steelhead trout is restricted by federal subsistence rules.

units.obligation_text: Residents of Ninilchik may also take coho and pink salmon through a rod and reel fishery in Tustumena Lake. Fishing is allowed with up to two baited single or treble hooks.
units.action_summary: Ninilchik residents may take coho and pink in Tustumena Lake by rod and reel using up to two baited hooks.

units.obligation_text: Seasons, areas, harvest and possession limits, and methods and means for take are the same as for the taking of these species under Alaska sport fishing regulations (5 AAC 56), except for the following harvest and possession limits: Coho 16 inches and longer 4 per day and 4 in possession; Pink 16 inches and longer 6 per day and 6 in possession.
units.action_summary: Tustumena Lake rod and reel follows Alaska sport fishing regs except coho and pink have specified size and daily/possession limits.

units.obligation_text: Resident fish species including lake trout, rainbow or steelhead trout, and Dolly Varden or Arctic char may be harvested by rod and reel in Federally managed waters of the Kasilof River drainage the entire year as follows:
units.action_summary: Resident species may be harvested year-round by rod and reel in Federally managed Kasilof drainage waters subject to listed specifications and limits.

units.obligation_text: Lake trout: Fish 20 inches and longer 4 per day and 4 in possession; Fish less than 20 inches in length 15 per day and 15 in possession.
units.action_summary: Lake trout daily and possession limits vary by size: 20+ inches = 4; <20 inches = 15.

units.section: § ll.27(e)(10)(ii)(E) - Dolly Varden and Arctic char thresholds
units.obligation_text: Dolly Varden and Arctic char: In flowing waters 4 per day and 4 in possession; In lakes and ponds 10 per day and 10 in possession.
units.action_summary: Dolly Varden/Arctic char limits: 4/day in flowing waters; 10/day in lakes/ponds.

units.section: § ll.27(e)(10)(ii)(E) - Rainbow or steelhead trout thresholds
units.obligation_text: Rainbow or steelhead trout: In flowing waters 2 per day and 2 in possession; In lakes and ponds 5 per day and 5 in possession.
units.action_summary: Rainbow/steelhead limits: 2/day in flowing waters; 5/day in lakes/ponds.

units.obligation_text: You may fish in Tustumena Lake with a gillnet under the ice, or with jigging gear used through the ice. The gillnet may not be longer than 10 fathoms.
units.action_summary: Permitted fishing methods under ice include gillnet (≤10 fathoms) and jigging gear.

units.obligation_text: Harvest limits are as follows: Jigging gear through the ice: Household annual limit of 30 fish in any combination of lake trout, rainbow trout, and Dolly Varden or Arctic char. Gillnet under the ice: Total annual harvest quota of 200 lake trout, 200 rainbow trout, and 500 Dolly Varden or Arctic char. The Federal in-season manager will issue a closure for this fishery once any of these quotas has been met.
units.action_summary: Specifies jigging household annual limit (30 total) and gillnet annual quotas (200 lake trout, 200 rainbow, 500 Dolly Varden/Arctic char) and directs manager to close fishery when quotas met.

units.obligation_text: You may harvest fish under the ice only in Tustumena Lake. Gillnets are not allowed within a 1/4-mile radius of the mouth of any tributary to Tustumena Lake, or the outlet of Tustumena Lake.
units.action_summary: Under-ice harvest is limited to Tustumena Lake; gillnets prohibited within 1/4 mile of tributary mouths or the outlet.

units.obligation_text: A permit is required. The permit will be issued by the Federal in-season manager or designated representative and will be valid for the winter season unless the season is closed by special action.
units.action_summary: A permit from the Federal in-season manager is required for the winter under-ice fishery and is valid for the winter season unless closed by special action.
units.modal_raw: is required / will be issued / will be valid

units.obligation_text: The permittee must report the following information: The number of each species caught; the number of each species retained; the length, depth (number of meshes deep), and mesh size of gillnet fished; the fishing site; and the total hours fished.
units.action_summary: Permittee must report species caught/retained counts, gillnet dimensions, fishing site, and total hours fished.

units.obligation_text: The gillnet must be checked at least once in every 48-hour period.
units.action_summary: Gillnet must be checked at least once every 48 hours.

units.obligation_text: For unattended gear, the permittee’s name and address must be plainly and legibly inscribed on a stake at one end of the gillnet.
units.action_summary: For unattended gear, permittee must place their name and address legibly on a stake at one end of the gillnet.

units.obligation_text: Incidentally caught fish may be retained and must be recorded on the permit before transporting fish from the fishing site.
units.action_summary: Incidental catches may be retained but must be recorded on the permit before transporting from the fishing site.

units.obligation_text: Failure to return the completed harvest permit by May 31 may result in issuance of a violation notice and/or denial of a future subsistence permit.
units.action_summary: If permittees fail to return completed harvest permit by May 31, they may receive a violation notice or be denied future permits.

units.obligation_text: Household annual limits for salmon in Kenai River fisheries are as follows:
units.action_summary: Introduces household annual limit thresholds for Kenai River salmon species.

units.obligation_text: Sockeye: 25 allowed for each permit holder; additional 5 fish allowed for each household member. Chum salmon that are retained are to be included within the annual limit for sockeye salmon.
units.action_summary: Sockeye household limit: 25 per permit holder plus 5 per household member; retained chum salmon count toward sockeye annual limit.

units.obligation_text: Chinook—Early-run (July 1 through July 15): 2 allowed for each permit holder; additional 1 fish allowed for each household member for the Kenai River community gillnet fishery described under paragraph (e)(10)(iii)(B) of this section.
units.actor: permit holders / households (for Kenai River community gillnet fishery)
units.action_summary: Early-run Chinook household limit: 2 per permit holder plus 1 per household member (applicable to Kenai River community gillnet fishery).

units.obligation_text: Chinook—Late-run (July 16 through August 31): 10 allowed for each permit holder; additional 2 fish allowed for each household member.
units.action_summary: Late-run Chinook household limit: 10 per permit holder plus 2 per household member.

units.obligation_text: Coho: 20 allowed for each permit holder; additional 5 fish allowed for each household member.
units.action_summary: Coho household limit: 20 per permit holder plus 5 per household member.

units.obligation_text: Pink: 15 allowed for each permit holder; additional 5 fish allowed for each household member.
units.action_summary: Pink household limit: 15 per permit holder plus 5 per household member.

units.obligation_text: You may take only sockeye salmon through a dip net or rod and reel fishery at one specified site on the Russian River. For the Russian River fishing site, incidentally caught fish may be retained for subsistence uses, except for early- and late-run Chinook salmon, coho salmon, rainbow trout, and Dolly Varden, which must be released.
units.action_summary: Only sockeye may be targeted at the Russian River site; incidental fish may be retained except specified species that must be released.

units.obligation_text: At the Russian River Falls site, dip netting is allowed from a Federal regulatory marker near the upstream end of the fish ladder at Russian River Falls downstream to a Federal regulatory marker approximately 600 yards below Russian River Falls. Residents using rod and reel gear at this fishery site may not fish with bait at any time.
units.actor: residents using dip net or rod and reel at Russian River Falls site
units.action_summary: Dip netting allowed within specified markers; rod and reel users at this site are prohibited from using bait.

units.obligation_text: For both Kenai River fishing sites below Skilak Lake, incidentally caught fish may be retained for subsistence uses, except for early-run Chinook salmon (unless otherwise provided for in this section), rainbow trout 18 inches or longer, and Dolly Varden 18 inches or longer, which must be released.
units.actor: you (fishers at Kenai River sites below Skilak Lake)
units.action_summary: Incidentally caught fish at these Kenai River sites may be retained except early-run Chinook (unless provided), rainbow trout ≥18 inches, and Dolly Varden ≥18 inches which must be released.

units.obligation_text: At the Kenai River Moose Range Meadows site, dip netting is allowed only from a boat from a Federal regulatory marker on the Kenai River at about river mile 29 downstream approximately 2.5 miles to another marker on the Kenai River at about river mile 26.5. Residents using rod and reel gear at this fishery site may fish from boats or from shore with up to two baited single or treble hooks June 15 through August 31.
units.actor: residents using dip net or rod and reel at Moose Range Meadows site
units.action_summary: Dip netting allowed by boat between specified markers; rod and reel users may fish from boat/shore with up to two baited hooks June 15–Aug 31.

units.obligation_text: At the Kenai river mile 48 site, dip netting is allowed while either standing in the river or from a boat, from Federal regulatory markers on both sides of the Kenai River at about river mile 48 downstream approximately 2.5 miles to a marker on the Kenai River at about river mile 45.5. Residents using rod and reel gear at this fishery site may fish from boats or from shore with up to two baited single or treble hooks June 15 through August 31.
units.actor: residents at Kenai river mile 48 site
units.action_summary: Dip netting allowed in specified stretch from shore or boat; rod and reel users may use up to two baited hooks June 15–Aug 31.

units.obligation_text: Residents of Ninilchik may harvest sockeye, Chinook, coho, and pink salmon in the Moose Range Meadows area of the Federal public waters of the Kenai River with a single gillnet to be managed and operated by the Ninilchik Traditional Council.
units.actor: Residents of Ninilchik; Ninilchik Traditional Council (manager/operator)
units.action_summary: Ninilchik residents may harvest listed salmon in Moose Range Meadows using a single gillnet managed by the Ninilchik Traditional Council.

units.obligation_text: Salmon taken in this fishery will be included as household annual limits of participating households.
units.action_summary: Salmon taken in this community gillnet fishery count toward participating households' annual limits.

units.obligation_text: Early-run Chinook salmon less than 46 inches in length or greater than 55 inches in length (July 1–15): Fish may be retained if the most current preseason forecast from the State of Alaska Department of Fish and Game projects the in-river run to be within or above the optimal escapement goal range for early-run Chinook salmon; otherwise, live fish must be released. Fishery will close until July 16 once 50 early-run Chinook salmon have been retained or released.
units.actor: participants; Federal/State managers (for forecasts and closure)
units.action_summary: Early-run Chinook may be retained only if state preseason forecast predicts adequate escapement; otherwise live fish must be released. Fishery will close until July 16 once 50 early-run Chinook have been retained or released.

units.obligation_text: Late-run Chinook salmon (July 16–August 15): Fishery will close prior to August 15 if 200 late-run Chinook salmon have been retained or released prior to that date. Fishery will reopen September 10–30 for species available at that time.
units.action_summary: Fishery closes before Aug 15 if 200 late-run Chinook retained/released; reopens Sept 10–30 for available species.

units.section: § ll.27(e)(10)(iii)(B)(2)(ii) - Incidentally caught rainbow and Dolly Varden
units.obligation_text: Incidentally caught rainbow trout and Dolly Varden: All live fish must be released. Fish that die in net may be retained. Fishery will close for the season once 100 rainbow trout or 150 Dolly Varden have been released or retained.
units.action_summary: Live incidentally caught rainbow trout and Dolly Varden must be released; dead fish may be retained. Fishery closes for season after 100 rainbow trout or 150 Dolly Varden have been released or retained.

units.obligation_text: Chinook salmon less than 20 inches in length may be retained and do not count towards retained or released totals.
units.action_summary: Chinook under 20 inches may be retained and are exempt from retained/released total counts.

units.obligation_text: Other incidentally caught species may be retained; however, all incidental fish mortalities, except for Chinook salmon less than 20 inches in length, count towards released or retained totals specified in this section.
units.action_summary: Other incidental species may be kept, but incidental fish mortalities (except Chinook <20") count toward released/retained totals.

units.obligation_text: Only one community gillnet may be operated on the Kenai River. The gillnet may not: Be over 10 fathoms in length to take salmon; be larger than 5.25-inch mesh; and obstruct more than half of the river width with stationary fishing gear.
units.action_summary: Only one community gillnet allowed; it must be ≤10 fathoms, ≤5.25-inch mesh, and not obstruct >half the river width.

units.obligation_text: Subsistence stationary gillnet gear may not be set within 200 feet of other subsistence stationary gear.
units.action_summary: Stationary gillnet gear cannot be set within 200 feet of other stationary gear.

units.obligation_text: One registration permit will be available and will be issued by the Federal in-season manager, in consultation with the Kenai National Wildlife Refuge manager, to the Ninilchik Traditional Council. As the community gillnet owner, the Ninilchik Traditional Council will be responsible for its use and removal in consultation with the Federal in-season manager. As part of the permit, the Ninilchik Traditional Council must provide post-season written documentation of required evaluation information to the Federal in-season manager including, but not limited to: persons or households operating the gear; hours of operation; and number of each species caught and retained or released.
units.actor: Federal in-season manager; Ninilchik Traditional Council
units.action_summary: Federal manager will issue one registration permit to the Ninilchik Traditional Council, which will be responsible for the gillnet and must provide post-season evaluation documentation including operators, hours, and catch numbers.
units.modal_raw: will be issued / will be responsible / must provide

units.obligation_text: The Ninilchik Traditional Council may operate the net for subsistence purposes on behalf of residents of Ninilchik by requesting a subsistence fishing permit that: (i) Identifies a person who will be responsible for fishing the gillnet; and (ii) Includes provisions for recording daily catches, the household to whom the catch was given, and other information determined to be necessary for effective resource management by the Federal in-season manager.
units.action_summary: The Council may operate the net on residents' behalf if it requests a permit identifying a responsible person and including required catch-recording provisions.

units.obligation_text: For Federally managed waters of the Kenai River and its tributaries, you may take sockeye, Chinook, coho, pink, and chum salmon through a separate rod and reel fishery in the Kenai River drainage.
units.actor: you (fishers in Federally managed Kenai River waters)
units.action_summary: Fishers may take listed salmon species via separate rod and reel fishery in Federally managed Kenai River waters.

units.obligation_text: In the Kenai River below Skilak Lake, fishing is allowed with up to two baited single or treble hooks June 15 through August 31.
units.actor: you (fishers in Kenai River below Skilak Lake)
units.action_summary: In Kenai River below Skilak Lake, fishing allowed with up to two baited hooks June 15–Aug 31.

units.obligation_text: Annual harvest limits for any combination of early- and late-run Chinook salmon are four for each permit holder.
units.action_summary: Annual combined early- and late-run Chinook harvest limit is 4 per permit holder.

units.obligation_text: Incidentally caught fish, other than salmon, are subject to regulations found in paragraph (e)(10)(iii)(D) of this section.
units.action_summary: Non-salmon incidental catches are governed by the rules in paragraph (e)(10)(iii)(D).

units.obligation_text: For Federally managed waters of the Kenai River and its tributaries below Skilak Lake outlet at river mile 50, you may take resident fish species including lake trout, rainbow trout, and Dolly Varden or Arctic char with jigging gear through the ice or rod and reel gear in open waters. Seasons, areas, harvest and possession limits, and methods and means for take are the same as for the taking of these resident species under State of Alaska fishing regulations (5 AAC 56, 5 AAC 57, and 5 AAC 77.540), except for the following harvest and possession limits: (various size/limit specifications).
units.action_summary: In lower Kenai River waters below Skilak Lake, resident species may be taken by jigging through ice or rod and reel, generally following State regs except for specified limits.

units.section: § ll.27(e)(10)(iii)(D)(1) - Lower Kenai lake trout limits
units.obligation_text: Lake trout: 20 inches or longer 4 per day and 4 in possession; Less than 20 inches 15 per day and 15 in possession.
units.action_summary: Lower Kenai lake trout limits: ≥20" = 4/day; <20" = 15/day.

units.section: § ll.27(e)(10)(iii)(D)(1) - Lower Kenai Dolly Varden/Arctic char limits
units.obligation_text: Dolly Varden or Arctic char: In flowing waters for fish less than 18 inches, 1 per day and 1 in possession; In lakes and ponds 2 per day and 2 in possession, of which only one may be 20 inches or longer, may be harvested daily.
units.action_summary: Lower Kenai Dolly Varden/Arctic char limits: flowing waters <18" = 1/day; lakes/ponds 2/day with at most one ≥20".

units.obligation_text: Rainbow or steelhead trout: In flowing waters for fish less than 18 inches in length, 1 per day and 1 in possession; In lakes and ponds 2 per day and 2 in possession, of which only one fish 20 inches or longer may be harvested daily.
units.action_summary: Lower Kenai rainbow/steelhead limits: flowing waters <18" = 1/day; lakes/ponds 2/day with only one ≥20".

units.obligation_text: For Federally managed waters of the upper Kenai River and its tributaries above Skilak Lake outlet at river mile 50, you may take resident fish species including lake trout, rainbow trout, and Dolly Varden or Arctic char with jigging gear through the ice or rod and reel gear in open waters. Seasons, areas, harvest and possession limits, and methods and means for take are the same as for the taking of these resident species under Alaska fishing regulations (5 AAC 56, 5 AAC 57, 5 AAC 77.540), except for the following harvest and possession limits: (various size/limit specifications including special rules for Hidden Lake and different length thresholds).
units.action_summary: Upper Kenai River waters above Skilak Lake allow taking resident species by jigging or rod and reel, with State regs applying except for specified additional limits and variations (e.g., Hidden Lake).

units.section: § ll.27(e)(10)(iii)(D)(2) - Upper Kenai lake trout limits
units.obligation_text: Lake trout: 20 inches or longer 4 per day and 4 in possession; Less than 20 inches 15 per day and 15 in possession; From Hidden Lake 2 per day and 2 in possession regardless of length.
units.action_summary: Upper Kenai lake trout limits: ≥20" = 4/day; <20" = 15/day; Hidden Lake = 2/day regardless of length.

units.section: § ll.27(e)(10)(iii)(D)(2) - Upper Kenai Dolly Varden/Arctic char limits
units.obligation_text: Dolly Varden or Arctic char: In flowing waters for fish less than 16 inches in length, 1 per day and 1 in possession; In lakes and ponds 2 per day and 2 in possession, of which only one fish 20 inches or longer may be harvested daily.
units.action_summary: Upper Kenai Dolly Varden/Arctic char limits: flowing waters <16" = 1/day; lakes/ponds 2/day with at most one ≥20".

units.obligation_text: Rainbow or steelhead trout: In flowing waters for fish less than 16 inches in length, 1 per day and 1 in possession; In lakes and ponds 2 per day and 2 in possession, of which only one fish 20 inches or longer may be harvested daily.
units.action_summary: Upper Kenai rainbow/steelhead limits: flowing waters <16" = 1/day; lakes/ponds 2/day with only one ≥20".

title: Endangered and Threatened Species: Threatened Species Status for Coastal Distinct Population Segment of the Pacific Marten

units.obligation_text: Except as noted in paragraph (a)(2) of this section, all prohibitions and provisions of section 9(a)(1) of the Act apply to the coastal marten.
units.actor: persons subject to the Act / the public
units.action_summary: The prohibitions and provisions of section 9(a)(1) of the Endangered Species Act apply to the coastal Pacific marten (i.e., take prohibitions cover this DPS).

units.obligation_text: Incidental take of the coastal marten will not be considered a violation of the Act if the take results from any of the following activities:
units.actor: persons whose incidental take results from the listed activities
units.action_summary: Incidental take is excepted from being a violation of the Act when it results from specified activities.
units.modal_raw: will not be considered a violation

units.obligation_text: Forestry management activities for the purposes of reducing the risk or severity of wildfire, such as fuels reduction projects, fire breaks, and wildfire firefighting activities.
units.actor: persons conducting the described forestry management activities
units.action_summary: Incidental take resulting from wildfire-risk-reduction forestry activities (e.g., fuels reduction, fire breaks, firefighting) is not considered a violation.
units.modal_raw: will not be considered a violation (if incidental take results from these activities)

units.obligation_text: Forestry management activities included in a State-approved plan or agreement for lands covered by a Natural Communities Conservation Plan, Habitat Management Agreement, or Safe Harbor Agreement that addresses coastal marten as a covered species and is approved by the California Department of Fish and Wildlife under the authority of the California Endangered Species Act.
units.actor: persons conducting forestry management activities under the described State-approved plans or agreements
units.action_summary: Incidental take resulting from forestry activities carried out under specified State-approved conservation plans/agreements that cover coastal marten and are approved by the California Department of Fish and Wildlife is not considered a violation.
units.modal_raw: will not be considered a violation (if incidental take results from these activities)

units.obligation_text: Forestry management activities consistent with the conservation needs of the coastal marten. These include activities consistent with formal approved conservation plans or strategies, such as Federal or State plans and documents that include coastal marten conservation prescriptions or compliance, and for which the Service has determined that meeting such plans or strategies, or portions thereof, would be consistent with this rule.
units.actor: persons conducting forestry management activities consistent with coastal marten conservation plans or strategies
units.action_summary: Incidental take from forestry activities that are consistent with formal approved conservation plans/strategies for the coastal marten is not a violation, provided additional Service-determined consistency conditions are met.
units.modal_raw: will not be considered a violation (if incidental take results from these activities and conditions are met)

units.obligation_text: for which the Service has determined that meeting such plans or strategies, or portions thereof, would be consistent with this rule.
units.actor: the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service
units.action_summary: The Service must determine that implementing (or meeting) the referenced plans or strategies, or portions of them, would be consistent with this rule for the exception to apply.

title: Endangered and Threatened Species: Reclassifying the American Burying Beetle from Endangered to Threatened on the Federal List

units.obligation_text: Take of the American burying beetle, except that take that is incidental to otherwise lawful activity (incidental take) is only prohibited when the take occurs on suitable American burying beetle habitat:
units.action_summary: Prohibits take of the American burying beetle; incidental take is only prohibited when it occurs on suitable American burying beetle habitat in specified areas.

units.obligation_text: In the New England and Northern Plains Analysis Areas where the incidental take results from soil disturbance;
units.action_summary: Incidental take that results from soil disturbance in the New England and Northern Plains Analysis Areas is prohibited.

units.obligation_text: In the Southern Plains Analysis Areas where the incidental take occurs on defined conservation lands, except where incidental take is in compliance with a Service-approved conservation plan.
units.action_summary: Incidental take on defined conservation lands in the Southern Plains Analysis Areas is prohibited unless it is in compliance with a Service-approved conservation plan.

units.obligation_text: except where incidental take is in compliance with a Service-approved conservation plan.
units.action_summary: Exception allowing incidental take on defined conservation lands in the Southern Plains Analysis Areas if the incidental take is in compliance with a Service-approved conservation plan.

units.obligation_text: Possession and other acts with unlawfully taken American burying beetles.
units.action_summary: Prohibits possession and other acts involving unlawfully taken American burying beetles.

units.obligation_text: It is unlawful to possess, sell, deliver, carry, transport, or ship, by any means whatsoever, any American burying beetle that was taken in violation of paragraph (c)(1)(i) of this section or State law.
units.action_summary: Prohibits possessing, selling, delivering, carrying, transporting, or shipping any American burying beetle taken in violation of federal or state law.

units.obligation_text: Notwithstanding paragraph (c)(1)(ii)(A) of this section, Federal and State law enforcement officers may possess, deliver, carry, transport, or ship any American burying beetle taken in violation of the Act as necessary in performing their official duties.
units.actor: Federal and State law enforcement officers
units.action_summary: Permits Federal and State law enforcement officers to possess, deliver, carry, transport, or ship unlawfully taken American burying beetles as necessary to perform official duties.

units.obligation_text: Import and export of the American burying beetle.
units.action_summary: Prohibits import and export of the American burying beetle.

units.obligation_text: It is unlawful to deliver, receive, carry, transport, or ship in interstate or foreign commerce, by any means whatsoever, and in the course of a commercial activity, the American burying beetle.
units.action_summary: Prohibits delivering, receiving, carrying, transporting, or shipping the American burying beetle in interstate or foreign commerce in the course of commercial activity.

units.obligation_text: It is unlawful to sell or to offer for sale in interstate or foreign commerce any American burying beetle.
units.action_summary: Prohibits selling or offering for sale the American burying beetle in interstate or foreign commerce.

units.obligation_text: Any employee or agent of the Service or of a State conservation agency that is operating a conservation program pursuant to the terms of a cooperative agreement with the Service in accordance with section 6(c) of the Act, who is designated by his agency for such purposes, may, when acting in the course of his official duties, take American burying beetles, provided that, for State conservation agencies, the American burying beetle is covered by an approved cooperative agreement to carry out conservation programs.
units.actor: designated employees or agents of the Service or of a State conservation agency
units.action_summary: Permits designated Service or State conservation agency employees or agents to take American burying beetles in the course of official duties, with an additional requirement for State agencies regarding cooperative agreements.

units.obligation_text: for State conservation agencies, the American burying beetle is covered by an approved cooperative agreement to carry out conservation programs.
units.action_summary: Condition: State conservation agency personnel may take beetles only if the beetle is covered by an approved cooperative agreement to carry out conservation programs.

units.obligation_text: Federal or State government agencies may incidentally take American burying beetles when conducting wildlife management activities in the Northern Plains Analysis Areas.
units.action_summary: Permits Federal or State government agencies to incidentally take American burying beetles during wildlife management activities in the Northern Plains Analysis Areas.

units.obligation_text: Incidental take of American burying beetles resulting from ranching and grazing activities is allowed.
units.actor: persons conducting ranching and grazing activities
units.action_summary: Allows incidental take of American burying beetles resulting from ranching and grazing activities.

units.obligation_text: Incidental take of the Neuse River waterdog will not be considered a violation of the Act if the take results from any of the following activities:
units.actor: persons whose actions result in incidental take

units.modal_raw: will not be considered a violation

units.obligation_text: Species restoration efforts by State wildlife agencies, including collection of broodstock, tissue collection for genetic analysis, captive propagation, and subsequent stocking into currently occupied and unoccupied areas within the historical range of the species.
units.action_summary: Incidental take resulting from species restoration efforts by State wildlife agencies (including broodstock collection, tissue collection, captive propagation, and stocking) will not be considered a violation.
units.modal_raw: will not be considered a violation

units.obligation_text: Channel restoration projects that create natural, physically stable, ecologically functioning streams (or stream and wetland systems) that are reconnected with their groundwater aquifers. These projects can be accomplished using a variety of methods, but the desired outcome is a natural channel with low shear stress (force of water moving against the channel); bank heights that enable reconnection to the floodplain; a reconnection of surface and groundwater systems, resulting in perennial flows in the channel; riffles and pools composed of existing soil, rock, and wood instead of large imported materials; low compaction of soils within adjacent riparian areas; and inclusion of riparian wetlands. Second- to third-order, headwater streams reconstructed in this way would offer suitable habitats for the Neuse River waterdog and contain stable channel features, such as pools, glides, runs, and riffles, which could be used by the species for spawning, rearing, growth, feeding, migration, and other normal behaviors.
units.action_summary: Incidental take resulting from channel restoration projects that produce specified natural, stable, ecologically functioning stream conditions will not be considered a violation.
units.modal_raw: will not be considered a violation

units.obligation_text: Bank stabilization projects that use bioengineering methods to replace pre-existing, bare, eroding stream banks with vegetated, stable stream banks, thereby reducing bank erosion and instream sedimentation and improving habitat conditions for the species. Following these bioengineering methods, stream banks may be stabilized using live stakes (live, vegetative cuttings inserted or tamped into the ground in a manner that allows the stake to take root and grow), live fascines (live branch cuttings, usually willows, bound together into long, cigar-shaped bundles), or brush layering (cuttings or branches of easily rooted tree species layered between successive lifts of soil fill).
units.action_summary: Incidental take resulting from bank stabilization projects that use specified bioengineering methods will not be considered a violation.
units.modal_raw: will not be considered a violation

units.obligation_text: These methods would not include the sole use of quarried rock (rip-rap) or the use of rock baskets or gabion structures.
units.action_summary: Prohibits relying solely on quarried rock (rip-rap), rock baskets, or gabion structures for bank stabilization under the allowed bioengineering methods.

units.obligation_text: Silviculture practices and forest management activities that: (A) Implement highest standard best management practices, particularly for Streamside Management Zones, stream crossings, and forest roads; and (B) Comply with forest practice guidelines related to water quality standards, or comply with Sustainable Forestry Initiative/Forest Stewardship Council/American Tree Farm System certification standards for both forest management and responsible fiber sourcing.

units.action_summary: Incidental take resulting from silviculture and forest management activities will not be considered a violation if they meet the stated BMP and compliance/certification conditions.

units.action_summary: Must implement highest standard best management practices, especially for streamside zones, crossings, and forest roads.

units.obligation_text: Comply with forest practice guidelines related to water quality standards, or comply with Sustainable Forestry Initiative/Forest Stewardship Council/American Tree Farm System certification standards for both forest management and responsible fiber sourcing.
units.action_summary: Must comply with forest practice guidelines related to water quality, or comply with specified certification standards for forest management and responsible fiber sourcing.

title: Endangered and Threatened Species: Regulations for Designating Critical Habitat

units.obligation_text: At the time of publication of a proposed rule to designate critical habitat, the Secretary will make available for public comment the draft economic analysis of the designation.
units.action_summary: Publish the draft economic analysis for public comment at time of the proposed critical habitat designation.

units.obligation_text: The draft economic analysis will be summarized in the Federal Register notice of the proposed designation of critical habitat.
units.action_summary: Summarize the draft economic analysis in the Federal Register notice for the proposed designation.

units.obligation_text: The Secretary will also identify any national security or other relevant impacts that the Secretary determines are contained in a particular area of proposed designation.
units.action_summary: Identify national security or other relevant impacts in particular areas of the proposed designation.

units.obligation_text: Based on the best information available regarding economic, national security, and other relevant impacts, the proposed designation of critical habitat will identify the areas that the Secretary has reason to consider for exclusion and explain why.
units.action_summary: Identify and explain areas the Secretary has reason to consider for exclusion in the proposed designation.

units.obligation_text: The Secretary will consider impacts at a scale that the Secretary determines to be appropriate and will compare the impacts with and without the designation.
units.action_summary: Consider impacts at an appropriate scale and compare impacts with and without the designation.

units.obligation_text: Impacts may be qualitatively or quantitatively described.
units.action_summary: Impacts may be described either qualitatively or quantitatively.

units.obligation_text: Prior to finalizing the designation of critical habitat, the Secretary will consider the probable economic, national security, and other relevant impacts of the designation upon proposed or ongoing activities.
units.action_summary: Before finalizing designation, consider probable economic, national security, and other relevant impacts on proposed or ongoing activities.

units.obligation_text: Subject to paragraph (c)(2) of this section, the Secretary has discretion as to whether to conduct an exclusion analysis under 16 U.S.C. 1533(b)(2).
units.action_summary: The Secretary may choose whether to conduct an exclusion analysis under the cited statute, subject to paragraph (c)(2).

units.obligation_text: The Secretary will conduct an exclusion analysis when:
units.action_summary: Conduct an exclusion analysis in the circumstances specified in following subparagraphs.

units.obligation_text: The proponent of excluding a particular area (including but not limited to permittees, lessees or others with a permit, lease or contract on federally managed lands) has presented credible information regarding the existence of a meaningful economic or other relevant impact supporting a benefit of exclusion for that particular area;
units.actor: the proponent of excluding a particular area
units.action_summary: Condition: an exclusion analysis will be conducted if a proponent presents credible information of meaningful impacts supporting exclusion.

units.obligation_text: The Secretary otherwise decides to exercise discretion to evaluate any particular area for possible exclusion.
units.action_summary: Condition: an exclusion analysis will be conducted if the Secretary decides to exercise discretion to evaluate an area for exclusion.

units.obligation_text: When the Secretary conducts a discretionary exclusion analysis pursuant to paragraph (c) of this section, the Secretary shall weigh the benefits of including or excluding particular areas in the designation of critical habitat, according to the following principles:
units.action_summary: When conducting a discretionary exclusion analysis, weigh the benefits of including or excluding areas according to listed principles.

units.obligation_text: When analyzing the benefits of including or excluding any particular area based on impacts identified by experts in, or by sources with firsthand knowledge of, areas that are outside the scope of the Service’s expertise, the Secretary will assign weight to those benefits consistent with the expert or firsthand information, unless the Secretary has knowledge or material evidence that rebuts that information.
units.action_summary: Assign weight to benefits identified by outside experts or firsthand sources consistent with that information, unless rebutted by evidence.

units.obligation_text: Nonbiological impacts identified by federally recognized Indian Tribes, consistent with all applicable Executive and Secretarial orders;
units.actor: federally recognized Indian Tribes (as sources identifying impacts)
units.action_summary: Example of impacts outside Service expertise: nonbiological impacts identified by Tribes.

units.obligation_text: Nonbiological impacts identified by State or local governments;
units.actor: State or local governments (as sources identifying impacts)
units.action_summary: Example of impacts outside Service expertise: nonbiological impacts identified by State or local governments.

units.obligation_text: Impacts based on national security or homeland security implications identified by the Department of Defense, Department of Homeland Security, or any other Federal agency responsible for national security or homeland security;
units.actor: Department of Defense, Department of Homeland Security, or other Federal national security agencies (as sources identifying impacts)
units.action_summary: Example of impacts outside Service expertise: national/homeland security impacts identified by national security agencies.

units.obligation_text: Nonbiological impacts identified by a permittee, lessee, or contractor applicant for a permit, lease, or contract on Federal lands.
units.actor: permittee, lessee, or contractor applicants (as sources identifying impacts)
units.action_summary: Example of impacts outside Service expertise: nonbiological impacts identified by permittees/lessees/contractor applicants on Federal lands.

units.obligation_text: When analyzing the benefit of including or excluding any particular area based on economic impacts or other relevant impacts described in paragraph (b) of this section, the Secretary will weigh such impacts relative to the conservation value of that particular area. For benefits of inclusion or exclusion based on impacts that fall within the scope of the Service’s expertise, the Secretary will assign weight to those benefits in light of the Service’s expertise.
units.action_summary: Weigh economic or other relevant impacts relative to the area's conservation value and assign weight to impacts within the Service's expertise accordingly.

units.obligation_text: When analyzing the benefits of including or excluding particular areas covered by conservation plans, agreements, or partnerships that have been authorized by a permit under section 10 of the Act, the Secretary will consider the following factors:
units.action_summary: Consider specified factors when evaluating areas covered by section 10-authorized conservation plans/agreements.

units.obligation_text: Whether the permittee is properly implementing the conservation plan or agreement;
units.action_summary: Consider whether the permittee is properly implementing the conservation plan/agreement.

units.obligation_text: Whether the species for which critical habitat is being designated is a covered species in the conservation plan or agreement;
units.action_summary: Consider whether the species is included as a covered species in the plan/agreement.

units.obligation_text: Whether the conservation plan or agreement specifically addresses the habitat of the species for which critical habitat is being designated and meets the conservation needs of the species in the planning area.
units.action_summary: Consider whether the plan specifically addresses the species' habitat and meets its conservation needs in the planning area.

units.obligation_text: When analyzing the benefits of including or excluding particular areas covered by conservation plans, agreements, or partnerships that have not been authorized by a permit under section 10 of the Act, factors that the Secretary may consider include, but are not limited to:
units.action_summary: The Secretary may consider the following factors when evaluating areas covered by non-permitted conservation plans/agreements.

units.obligation_text: The degree to which the record of the plan, or information provided by proponents of an exclusion, supports a conclusion that a critical habitat designation would impair the realization of the benefits expected from the plan, agreement, or partnership.
units.action_summary: Consider whether the plan record or proponents' information indicates designation would impair expected benefits.

units.obligation_text: The extent of public participation in the development of the conservation plan.
units.action_summary: Consider the extent of public participation in plan development.

units.obligation_text: The degree to which agency review and required determinations (e.g., State regulatory requirements) have been completed, as necessary and appropriate.
units.action_summary: Consider extent to which agency review and required determinations have been completed.

units.obligation_text: Whether National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA; 42 U.S.C. 4321 et seq.) reviews or similar reviews occurred, and the nature of any such reviews.
units.action_summary: Consider whether NEPA or similar reviews occurred and their nature.

units.obligation_text: The demonstrated implementation and success of the chosen mechanism.
units.action_summary: Consider the demonstrated implementation and success of the mechanism.

units.obligation_text: The degree to which the plan or agreement provides for the conservation of the physical or biological features that are essential to the conservation of the species.
units.action_summary: Consider whether the plan provides for conservation of essential physical or biological features for the species.

units.obligation_text: Whether there is a reasonable expectation that the conservation management strategies and actions contained in a management plan or agreement will be implemented.
units.action_summary: Consider whether there is a reasonable expectation that the plan's management strategies and actions will be implemented.

units.obligation_text: Whether the plan or agreement contains a monitoring program and adaptive management to ensure that the conservation measures are effective and can be modified in the future in response to new information.
units.action_summary: Consider whether the plan includes monitoring and adaptive management to ensure and adjust conservation effectiveness.

units.obligation_text: If the Secretary conducts an exclusion analysis under paragraph (c) of this section, and if the Secretary determines that the benefits of excluding a particular area from critical habitat outweigh the benefits of specifying that area as part of the critical habitat, then the Secretary shall exclude that area,
units.action_summary: If, after an exclusion analysis, benefits of exclusion outweigh inclusion, the Secretary must exclude that area.

units.obligation_text: unless the Secretary determines, based on the best scientific and commercial data available, that the failure to designate that area as critical habitat will result in the extinction of the species concerned.
units.action_summary: Exception: do not exclude the area if failure to designate it would result in species extinction, based on best available scientific and commercial data.
