title: Migratory Bird Hunting: Proposed 2023-24 Frameworks for Migratory Bird Hunting Regulations

units.obligation_text: States may select seasons for hunting migratory game birds between the dates of September 1, 2023, and March 10, 2024.
units.action_summary: States are permitted to select hunting seasons within the specified date range.

units.obligation_text: Season lengths are the maximum number of days hunting may occur within the outside dates for hunting seasons.
units.action_summary: Season lengths set the maximum number of hunting days that may occur within outside dates.

units.obligation_text: The sum of the hunting days for all season segments may not exceed the season lengths allowed.
units.action_summary: Total days across all season segments cannot exceed the allowed season length.

units.obligation_text: Unless otherwise specified, States may select hunting seasons by zones.
units.action_summary: States are permitted to select hunting seasons configured by zones unless otherwise specified.

units.obligation_text: Zones for duck seasons (and associated youth and veterans–active military waterfowl hunting days, gallinule seasons, and snipe seasons) and dove seasons may be selected only in years we declare such changes can be made and according to federally established guidelines for duck and dove zones and split seasons.
units.action_summary: States may select zone-based seasons for listed categories only in years the Service allows and following federal guidelines.

units.section: I. General (Area, Zone, and Unit Descriptions)
units.obligation_text: Areas open to hunting must be described, delineated, and designated as such in each State’s hunting regulations.
units.action_summary: States are required to describe, delineate, and designate areas open to hunting in their hunting regulations.

units.section: I. General (Area, Zone, and Unit Descriptions)
units.obligation_text: Except for early teal seasons, these areas must also be published in the Federal Register as a Federal migratory bird hunting frameworks final rule.
units.action_summary: Except for early teal seasons, areas open to hunting must be published in the Federal Register as a frameworks final rule.

units.obligation_text: Unless otherwise specified, from one-half hour before sunrise to sunset daily.
units.action_summary: By default, hunting (including hawking) is permitted from half an hour before sunrise until sunset each day unless specified otherwise.

units.obligation_text: Unless otherwise specified, possession limits are three times the daily bag limits.
units.action_summary: By default, hunters' possession limits equal three times the daily bag limit unless otherwise specified.

units.obligation_text: For some species of migratory birds, the Service authorizes the use of permits to regulate harvest or monitor their take by hunters, or both.
units.actor: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (the Service)
units.action_summary: The Service may authorize the use of permits for certain species to regulate or monitor harvest.

units.obligation_text: The Service determines the amount of harvest that may be taken during hunting seasons during its formal regulations-setting process.
units.actor: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (the Service)
units.action_summary: The Service sets the authorized amount of harvest during its regulatory process.

units.obligation_text: The States then issue permits to hunters at levels predicted to result in the amount of take authorized by the Service.
units.action_summary: States are to issue individual permits set at levels expected to produce the Service-authorized take.

units.obligation_text: Although issued by States, the permits would not be valid unless the Service approved such take in its regulations.
units.action_summary: State-issued permits are invalid unless the Service has approved the authorized take in its regulations.

units.obligation_text: Only the individual whose name and address appears on the permit at the time of issuance is authorized to take migratory birds at levels specified in the permit, in accordance with provisions of both Federal and State regulations governing the hunting season.
units.action_summary: Only the named individual on a permit may take migratory birds under that permit's terms.

units.obligation_text: The permit must be carried by the permittee when exercising its provisions and must be presented to any law enforcement officer upon request.
units.action_summary: Permit holders are required to carry the permit while using it and present it to law enforcement upon request.

units.obligation_text: The permit is not transferrable or assignable to another individual, and may not be sold, bartered, traded, or otherwise provided to another person.
units.action_summary: Permit holders are prohibited from transferring, assigning, selling, bartering, trading, or otherwise providing the permit to another person.

units.obligation_text: If the permit is altered or defaced in any way, the permit becomes invalid.
units.action_summary: Altering or defacing a permit causes it to become invalid.

units.obligation_text: In the Atlantic Flyway States ... where Sunday hunting of migratory birds is prohibited statewide by State law or regulation, all Sundays are closed to the take of all migratory game birds.
units.actor: Hunters in specified Atlantic Flyway States
units.action_summary: In listed states where state law/regulation prohibits Sunday hunting, taking migratory game birds on Sundays is prohibited.

units.section: II.A (Special Youth and Veterans–Active Military Personnel Waterfowl Hunting Days)
units.obligation_text: States may select 2 days per duck-hunting zone, designated as 'Youth Waterfowl Hunting Days,' and 2 days per duck-hunting zone, designated as 'Veterans and Active Military Personnel Waterfowl Hunting Days,' in addition to their regular duck seasons.
units.action_summary: States are permitted to select two youth days and two veterans/active-duty days per duck-hunting zone in addition to regular seasons.

units.obligation_text: The days may be held concurrently or may be nonconsecutive.
units.action_summary: States may schedule the special days concurrently or nonconsecutively.

units.obligation_text: The Youth Waterfowl Hunting Days must be held outside any regular duck season on weekends, holidays, or other non-school days when youth hunters would have the maximum opportunity to participate.
units.action_summary: Youth days must occur outside regular duck seasons and on weekends/holidays/non-school days to maximize youth participation.

units.obligation_text: Both sets of days may be held up to 14 days before or after any regular duck-season frameworks or within any split of a regular duck season, or within any other open season on migratory birds.
units.action_summary: The special youth and veterans days may be scheduled up to 14 days before or after regular duck seasons or within splits or other open seasons.

units.obligation_text: The daily bag limits may include ducks, geese, swans, mergansers, coots, and gallinules.
units.action_summary: Daily bag limits for the special days may include listed species groups.

units.obligation_text: Bag limits are the same as those allowed in the regular season except in States that implement a hybrid season for scaup (i.e., different bag limits during different portions of the season), in which case the bag limit will be 2 scaup per day.
units.action_summary: Special-day bag limits generally match regular seasons; if a State has a hybrid scaup season, the daily limit is 2 scaup on these days.

units.obligation_text: Flyway species and area restrictions would remain in effect.
units.action_summary: Existing flyway species and area restrictions continue to apply during special days.

units.obligation_text: States may use their established definition of age for youth hunters.
units.action_summary: States may apply their own age definitions for youth hunters.

units.obligation_text: Youth hunters must be under the age of 18.
units.action_summary: Youth hunters are required to be under 18 years old.

units.obligation_text: An adult at least 18 years of age must accompany the youth hunter into the field.
units.action_summary: A supervising adult 18+ must accompany the youth hunter in the field.

units.obligation_text: This adult may not duck hunt.
units.action_summary: The adult accompanying the youth is prohibited from duck hunting during the youth day.

units.obligation_text: This adult ... may participate in other seasons that are open on the special youth day.
units.action_summary: The adult may participate in other concurrently open seasons (but not duck hunt).

units.obligation_text: Swans may be taken only by participants possessing applicable swan permits.
units.action_summary: Taking swans is permitted only for participants who possess the required swan permits.

units.obligation_text: Veterans (as defined in section 101 of title 38, United States Code) and members of the Armed Forces on active duty ... may participate.
units.action_summary: Qualified veterans and active-duty military are permitted to participate in the special waterfowl days.

units.obligation_text: Swans may be taken only by participants possessing applicable swan permits.
units.action_summary: Veterans and active-duty participants may take swans only if they have applicable swan permits.

units.obligation_text: States in designated Areas may select special early teal seasons with the following specifications (Areas listed).
units.action_summary: States in specified areas are permitted to establish a special early teal season per the framework.

units.obligation_text: Outside Dates: September 1–30.
units.action_summary: The outside dates for special early teal seasons are September 1–30.

units.obligation_text: Season Lengths: 16 days.
units.action_summary: Special early teal season lengths are limited to 16 days.

units.obligation_text: Daily Bag Limits: 6 teal.
units.action_summary: Daily bag limit for the special early teal season is six teal.

units.obligation_text: Shooting Hours: One-half hour before sunrise to sunset, except in [listed States] where the hours are from sunrise to sunset.
units.action_summary: Default shooting hours apply, but certain states have shooting hours from sunrise to sunset.

units.obligation_text: In lieu of a special early teal season, a 5-consecutive-day teal–wood duck season may be selected in September.
units.action_summary: States may choose a 5-day teal–wood duck season instead of the special early teal season.

units.obligation_text: The daily bag limit may not exceed 6 teal and wood ducks in the aggregate, of which no more than 2 may be wood ducks.
units.action_summary: The combined daily bag for teal and wood ducks is limited to six total, with at most two wood ducks.

units.obligation_text: A 4-consecutive-day teal-only season may be selected in September either immediately before or immediately after the 5-day teal–wood duck season. The daily bag limit is 6 teal.
units.action_summary: States may select an adjacent 4-day teal-only season with a daily bag limit of six teal.

units.section: II.D.1.a (Atlantic Flyway Duck, Merganser, and Coot Seasons)
units.obligation_text: Outside Dates: Saturday nearest September 24 (September 23)–January 31.
units.action_summary: The outside dates for Atlantic Flyway duck, merganser, and coot seasons are from the Saturday nearest Sept 24 to Jan 31.

units.obligation_text: Season Lengths and Daily Bag Limits: 60 days. The daily bag limit is 6 ducks, including no more than 2 mallards (no more than 1 of which can be female), 2 black ducks, 1 pintail, 1 mottled duck, 1 fulvous whistling duck, 3 wood ducks, 2 redheads, 2 canvasbacks, and 4 sea ducks (including specified limits).
units.action_summary: Atlantic Flyway duck season length is 60 days with a 6-duck daily bag limit and specified species-specific sublimits.

units.obligation_text: The season for scaup may be split into 2 segments, with one segment consisting of 40 consecutive days with a 1-scaup daily bag limit, and the second segment consisting of 20 consecutive days with a 2-scaup daily bag limit.
units.action_summary: Scaup season can be split into a 40-day segment with 1 scaup/day and a 20-day segment with 2 scaup/day.

units.obligation_text: The daily bag limit of mergansers is 5. In States that include mergansers in the duck bag limit, the daily limit is the same as the duck bag limit.
units.action_summary: Merganser daily bag limit is five, but in states where mergansers are counted under the duck limit, the merganser limit equals the duck bag limit.

units.obligation_text: The daily bag limit of coots is 15.
units.action_summary: Daily bag limit for coots is set at 15.

units.obligation_text: There is no open season on the harlequin duck.
units.action_summary: Hunting of harlequin ducks is prohibited (no open season).

units.obligation_text: Delaware, Florida, Georgia, Rhode Island, South Carolina, and West Virginia may split their seasons into 3 segments. Other specified States may select seasons in multiple zones and split seasons as enumerated.
units.action_summary: Listed states are permitted to split seasons into multiple segments and select by zones as specified.

units.obligation_text: Connecticut, Maryland, North Carolina, and Virginia must conduct an evaluation of the impacts of zones and splits on hunter dynamics (e.g., hunter numbers, satisfaction) and harvest during the 2021–25 seasons.
units.action_summary: These states are required to evaluate how zones and split seasons affect hunter dynamics and harvest during 2021–25.

units.obligation_text: A craft under power may be used to shoot and retrieve dead or crippled birds in the Sea Duck Area in the Atlantic Flyway.
units.action_summary: Use of powered craft to shoot/retrieve dead or crippled birds is permitted in designated Sea Duck Areas under the conditions described.

units.section: II.D.1.b (Special Early Canada and Cackling Goose Seasons)
units.obligation_text: Special early Canada and cackling goose seasons may be held with outside dates and season lengths specified by area, and daily bag limits of 15 geese in the aggregate.
units.action_summary: States may hold special early Canada/cackling goose seasons with specified dates and an aggregate bag limit (15 geese in the aggregate).

units.obligation_text: Shooting hours may extend to one-half hour after sunset if all other waterfowl seasons are closed in the specific applicable area.
units.action_summary: During special early goose seasons, shooting hours can extend to 30 minutes after sunset if all other waterfowl seasons are closed in that area.

units.obligation_text: Hunting is by permit only.
units.actor: Hunters in specified Pacific Flyway areas
units.action_summary: Swan hunting in the designated Pacific Flyway areas is allowed only with a permit.

units.obligation_text: Permits will be issued by the State.
units.action_summary: State agencies will issue the required swan hunting permits.

units.obligation_text: The total number of permits issued may not exceed 50 in Idaho, 500 in Montana, 650 in Nevada, and 2,750 in Utah.
units.action_summary: Limits are placed on the number of swan permits each listed State may issue.

units.obligation_text: Permits will authorize the take of no more than 1 swan per permit.
units.action_summary: Each swan permit authorizes taking at most one swan.

units.obligation_text: Only 1 permit may be issued per hunter in Montana and Utah; 2 permits may be issued per hunter in Nevada.
units.action_summary: Per-hunter permit issuance limits differ by State: one per hunter in MT and UT; two per hunter in NV.

units.obligation_text: The swan season in the respective State must end upon attainment of the following reported harvest of trumpeter swans: 20 in Utah and 10 in Nevada.
units.action_summary: Swan seasons in UT and NV must end once the reported harvest quota for trumpeter swans is reached (20 UT, 10 NV).

units.obligation_text: Each State must evaluate hunter participation, species-specific swan harvest, and hunter compliance in providing either species-determinant parts ... or bill measurements ... of harvested swans for species identification.
units.action_summary: States are required to monitor hunter participation, species-specific harvest, and compliance in providing identification material/measurements for harvested swans.

units.obligation_text: Each State should use appropriate measures to maximize hunter compliance with the State’s program for swan harvest reporting.
units.action_summary: States are advised to use measures aimed at maximizing hunter compliance with swan harvest reporting programs.

units.obligation_text: Each State must achieve a hunter compliance of at least 80 percent in providing species-determinant parts or bill measurements of harvested swans for species identification, or subsequent permits will be reduced by 10 percent.
units.action_summary: States are required to achieve at least 80% hunter compliance in swan reporting or face a 10% reduction in subsequent permits.

units.section: II.D.4.b.iii (Pacific Flyway - Brant Seasons Special Provisions)
units.obligation_text: In Oregon and California, the brant season must end no later than December 15.
units.action_summary: Oregon and California are required to end brant seasons by December 15 at the latest.

units.obligation_text: The seasons, limits, and shooting hours should be the same between New York’s Lake Champlain Zone and Vermont’s Lake Champlain Zone, and between Vermont’s Connecticut River Zone and New Hampshire’s Inland Zone.
units.action_summary: These adjacent/matching zones are advised to have consistent seasons, limits, and shooting hours.

title: Migratory Bird Hunting; Migratory Game Bird Hunting Regulations on Certain Federal Indian Reservations and Ceded Lands

units.obligation_text: Tribes may independently (separate from the State or States in which the reservation is located) establish special migratory game bird hunting regulations.
units.action_summary: Tribes are permitted to independently establish special migratory game bird hunting regulations separate from the State(s).

units.obligation_text: Migratory birds may be taken if the take is consistent with the regulations in this section and applicable Tribal hunting regulations.
units.actor: Hunters (Tribal and nontribal persons taking migratory birds)
units.action_summary: Taking migratory birds is permitted provided the taking complies with this section's regulations and applicable Tribal hunting regulations.

units.obligation_text: Special Tribal migratory game bird hunting regulations may be established by Tribes that have reserved hunting rights on Federal Indian reservations (including off-reservation trust lands) and ceded lands.
units.action_summary: Tribes with reserved hunting rights are permitted to establish special migratory game bird hunting regulations on specified lands.

units.obligation_text: These regulations also may be applied to the establishment of migratory game bird hunting regulations for nontribal members on all lands within the reservations where Tribes have full wildlife-management authority over such hunting, or where the Tribes and affected States otherwise have reached agreement over hunting by nontribal members on non-Indian lands within the reservation.
units.action_summary: Tribes/authorities may apply these special regulations to establish hunting rules for nontribal members on certain reservation lands or where agreement with States exists.

units.obligation_text: Special Tribal migratory game bird hunting regulations must be consistent with the annual March 11 to August 31 closed season mandated by the 1916 Convention ... and with these provisions:
units.actor: Tribes (when establishing special Tribal migratory game bird hunting regulations)
units.action_summary: Any special Tribal migratory game bird hunting regulations are required to be consistent with the March 11–August 31 closed season and the listed provisions.

units.obligation_text: Tribes may establish on-reservation hunting regulations, for both Tribal and nontribal members, with hunting seasons that may differ from those in the State(s) in which the reservations are located.
units.action_summary: Tribes are permitted to set on-reservation hunting regulations for Tribal and nontribal members that can differ from State seasons.

units.obligation_text: Opening and closing dates, season length, and daily bag and possession limits for nontribal members on the reservations must be within the annual frameworks for migratory bird hunting seasons established by the Service,
units.actor: Tribes (when establishing regulations for nontribal members)
units.action_summary: When setting regulations for nontribal members, Tribes must ensure opening/closing dates, season length, and bag/possession limits fall within the Service's annual frameworks.

units.obligation_text: all Federal hunting regulations in this part also apply to nontribal hunters.
units.action_summary: Nontribal hunters on reservations are subject to all Federal hunting regulations in this part.

units.obligation_text: Tribes may choose to set the same opening and closing dates, season length, and daily bag and possession limits for hunting by Tribal members and nontribal members on their reservations,
units.action_summary: Tribes may opt to set identical season dates, season length, and bag/possession limits for both Tribal and nontribal hunters on their reservations.

units.obligation_text: or, in accordance with the provisions in paragraph (c)(1)(ii) of this section, Tribes may choose to establish regulations for Tribal members only.
units.action_summary: Tribes may opt to establish hunting regulations that apply only to Tribal members (permitted alternative under paragraph (c)(1)(ii)).

units.obligation_text: Tribes may establish on-reservation hunting regulations by Tribal members only, with hunting seasons that may be outside of annual frameworks for season dates, season length, and daily bag and possession limits.
units.action_summary: Tribes are permitted to establish on-reservation hunting regulations that apply only to Tribal members and may set seasons outside the Service's annual frameworks.

units.obligation_text: All Federal hunting regulations in this part apply.
units.actor: Tribal members (when hunting under Tribal-only regulations)
units.action_summary: Even under Tribal-only regulations, Tribal members remain subject to all Federal hunting regulations in this part.

units.obligation_text: For a short-term experimental hunt, a Tribe and the Service may formally agree on allowed methods of take, notwithstanding the regulations in § 20.21.
units.action_summary: For short-term experimental hunts, a Tribe and the Service may jointly agree to allowed methods of take that override § 20.21.

units.obligation_text: The Service will make public any such formal agreement.
units.action_summary: The Service is required to publish any formal agreement with a Tribe regarding allowed methods of take for short-term experimental hunts.

units.obligation_text: Tribes may establish off-reservation hunting regulations by Tribal members on ceded lands, with hunting seasons that may be outside of annual frameworks for season dates, season length, and daily bag and possession limits.
units.action_summary: Tribes are permitted to set off-reservation hunting regulations for Tribal members on ceded lands, potentially outside annual frameworks.

units.obligation_text: Tribes that have special migratory game bird hunting regulations for Tribal members on ceded lands must send a copy of the Tribal regulations to officials in the affected State(s) prior to the season opening.
units.actor: Tribes that have special migratory game bird hunting regulations for Tribal members on ceded lands
units.action_summary: Such Tribes are required to provide the affected State(s) with a copy of their Tribal regulations before the season opens.

title: Endangered and Threatened Species: Establishment of a Nonessential Experimental Population of the Gray Wolf in Colorado

units.obligation_text: These wolves will be managed in accordance with the provisions of this rule in the boundaries of the NEP area within the State of Colorado or any Tribal reservation found in the State that has a wolf management plan
units.action_summary: The experimental wolves must be managed according to this rule within the NEP boundaries and Tribal reservations with wolf plans.

units.obligation_text: the State of Colorado or any Tribe within the State that has a wolf management plan consistent with this rule can request the Service to assume the lead authority for wolf management under this rule
units.actor: the State of Colorado or any Tribe within the State
units.action_summary: States or Tribes with a consistent wolf management plan may request the Service to take lead authority for wolf management under this rule.

units.obligation_text: All wolves found in the wild within the boundary of the Colorado NEP area are considered nonessential experimental animals
units.actor: wolves in the wild within the Colorado NEP area (classification applied by the Service)
units.action_summary: Wolves within Colorado NEP boundaries are designated nonessential experimental animals.

units.obligation_text: Any wolf that is outside the Colorado NEP area, with the exception of wolves in the States of Idaho, Minnesota, Montana, Wyoming, and portions of the States of Oregon, Washington, and Utah, is considered endangered
units.actor: any wolf outside the Colorado NEP area
units.action_summary: Wolves outside the Colorado NEP area (except specified states/portions) are classified as endangered.

units.obligation_text: Any wolf originating from the Colorado NEP area and dispersing beyond its borders may be managed by the wolf management regulations established for that area or may be returned to the Colorado NEP area
units.actor: the Service or relevant management authority
units.action_summary: Wolves dispersing out of Colorado NEP may either be managed according to destination rules or returned to the NEP.
units.modal_raw: may be managed / may be returned

units.obligation_text: Take of gray wolves in the experimental population is allowed without a permit only in these specific circumstances: opportunistic harassment; intentional harassment; take in defense of human life; take to protect human safety; take by designated agents to remove problem wolves; incidental take; take under any previously authorized permits issued by the Service; take per authorizations for employees of designated agents; take for research purposes; and take to protect livestock animals and dogs
units.actor: any person / designated agents / employees as specified
units.action_summary: Unpermitted take is only allowed in the listed specific circumstances; other take requires permit or is prohibited.

units.obligation_text: Anyone may conduct opportunistic harassment of any gray wolf in a non-injurious manner at any time
units.action_summary: Any person is permitted to non-injuriously harass wolves opportunistically at any time.

units.obligation_text: Opportunistic harassment must be reported to the Service or a designated agent within 7 days as set forth in paragraph (a)(6) of this section
units.action_summary: Opportunistic harassment incidents must be reported within 7 days to the Service or a designated agent.

units.obligation_text: After we or a designated agent have confirmed wolf activity on private land, on a public land grazing allotment, or on a Tribal reservation, we or the designated agent may issue written take authorization valid for not longer than 1 year, with appropriate conditions, to any landowner or public land permittee to intentionally harass wolves
units.action_summary: The Service/designated agent may issue up-to-1-year written authorizations to landowners/permittees to intentionally harass wolves after confirmed activity.

units.obligation_text: The harassment must occur in the area and under the conditions as specifically identified in the written take authorization
units.actor: any landowner or public land permittee conducting intentional harassment
units.action_summary: Authorized intentional harassment must follow the area and conditions specified in the written authorization.

units.obligation_text: Intentional harassment must be reported to the Service or a designated agent(s) within 7 days as set forth in paragraph (a)(6) of this section
units.actor: anyone conducting intentional harassment under authorization
units.action_summary: Intentional harassment authorized under this provision must be reported within 7 days.

units.obligation_text: Landowners may take wolves on their private land in the following two additional circumstances
units.action_summary: Landowners have additional permissions to take wolves on private land under specified circumstances.

units.obligation_text: Consistent with State or Tribal requirements, any landowner may take a gray wolf in the act of attacking livestock or dogs on their private land, provided that there is no evidence of intentional baiting, feeding, or deliberate attractants of wolves
units.action_summary: Landowners may take a wolf actively attacking livestock or dogs on private land if no intentional attractants are present and consistent with State/Tribal rules.

units.obligation_text: To preserve physical evidence that the livestock or dogs were recently attacked by a wolf or wolves, the carcass and surrounding area must not be disturbed
units.actor: landowner or person taking the wolf
units.action_summary: The carcass and surrounding area must be left undisturbed to preserve evidence of wolf attack.

units.obligation_text: The Service or designated agent must be able to confirm that the livestock or dogs were wounded, harassed, molested, or killed by wolves
units.action_summary: The Service/designated agent must confirm wolf-caused harm to livestock or dogs for the landowner's take to be validated.

units.obligation_text: The Service or designated agent may issue a 'shoot-on-sight' written take authorization of limited duration (45 days or fewer) to a landowner or their employees to take up to a specified number of wolves on their private land if: (1) The landowner has had at least one depredation by wolves on livestock confirmed within the last 30 days; (2) the Service/designated agent has determined that problem wolves routinely occur and present a significant risk to livestock; and (3) the Service/designated agent has authorized lethal removal of wolves from those same private lands
units.action_summary: The Service/designated agent may issue limited-duration shoot-on-sight authorizations to landowners if specified depredation and problem-wolf conditions are met and lethal removal is authorized.

units.obligation_text: These authorizations may be terminated at any time once threats have been resolved or minimized
units.action_summary: Shoot-on-sight authorizations can be ended at any time when threats are resolved or minimized.

units.obligation_text: Consistent with State or Tribal requirements, any livestock producer and public land permittee who is legally using public land under a valid Federal land-use permit may take a gray wolf in the act of attacking livestock or dogs on the person's allotment or other area authorized for the person's use without prior written authorization
units.actor: livestock producers and public land permittees legally using public land
units.action_summary: Authorized public land users may take wolves attacking livestock or dogs on their allotted areas without prior written authorization, subject to State/Tribal requirements.

units.obligation_text: The Service or designated agent must be able to confirm that the livestock or dog were wounded, harassed, molested, or killed by a wolf or wolves
units.action_summary: Confirmation by the Service/designated agent of wolf-caused harm is required for public-land take to be validated.

units.obligation_text: The carcass of any wolf taken and the area surrounding it should not be disturbed to preserve physical evidence that the take was conducted according to this rule
units.action_summary: Persons taking wolves should leave the carcass and surrounding area undisturbed to preserve evidence.

units.obligation_text: Any person legally present on public land may immediately take a wolf that is in the act of attacking the individual's stock animal or dog, provided conditions described in paragraph (a)(5)(iii)(A) of this section for private land are met
units.actor: any person legally present on public land
units.action_summary: Legally present persons on public land may immediately take wolves attacking their stock/dog if private-land conditions are satisfied.

units.obligation_text: Any take or method of take on public land must be consistent with the laws and regulations on those public lands
units.actor: any person taking or using a method of take on public land
units.action_summary: All takes and methods on public lands must comply with applicable public-land laws and regulations.

units.obligation_text: The Service or our designated agent may issue a 'shoot-on-sight' written take authorization of limited duration (45 days or fewer) to a public land grazing permittee to take up to a specified number of wolves on that permittee's active livestock grazing allotment if: (1) The grazing allotment has had at least one depredation by wolves on livestock confirmed within the last 30 days; (2) the Service or our designated agent has determined that problem wolves routinely occur on that allotment and present a significant risk to health and safety of livestock; and (3) the Service or our designated agent has authorized lethal removal of wolves from that same allotment
units.action_summary: The Service/designated agent may issue limited-duration shoot-on-sight authorizations to public land grazing permittees if specified depredation/problem-wolf conditions and lethal removal authorization are met.

units.obligation_text: These authorizations may be terminated at any time once threats have been resolved or minimized; Any take or method of take on public land must be consistent with the rules and regulations on those public lands
units.actor: the Service or designated agent; any person taking on public land
units.action_summary: Shoot-on-sight authorizations can be terminated when threats abate; take on public land must comply with public-land rules.

units.obligation_text: The Service or our designated agent may carry out harassment, nonlethal control measures, relocation, placement in captivity, or lethal control of problem wolves
units.action_summary: Agency personnel may use various control measures, including lethal means, on problem wolves.

units.obligation_text: The Service or our designated agent will consider: (A) Evidence of wounded livestock, dogs, or other domestic animals... (B) The likelihood that additional wolf-caused losses... (C) Any evidence of unusual attractants...; and (D) Evidence that animal husbandry practices recommended in approved allotment plans and annual operating plans were followed
units.action_summary: When deciding agency actions for problem wolves, the Service/designated agent will consider specified evidence and circumstances.

units.obligation_text: Any person may take a gray wolf in defense of the individual's life or the life of another person
units.action_summary: Persons may take a wolf to defend human life.

units.obligation_text: The taking of a wolf without an immediate and direct threat to human life may be referred to the appropriate authorities for prosecution
units.action_summary: If a wolf is taken absent an immediate/direct human-life threat, the act may be referred for prosecution.

units.obligation_text: The Service or our designated agent may promptly remove any wolf that we or our designated agent determines to be a threat to human life or safety
units.action_summary: The Service/designated agent may promptly remove wolves deemed threats to human life or safety.

units.obligation_text: Take of a gray wolf is allowed if the take is accidental and/or incidental to an otherwise lawful activity and if reasonable due care was practiced to avoid such take and such take is reported within 24 hours as set forth at paragraph (a)(6) of this section
units.action_summary: Accidental/incidental takes are allowed if due care was used and the incident is reported within 24 hours.

units.obligation_text: We may refer incidental take that does not meet these provisions to the appropriate authorities for prosecution
units.action_summary: Incidental takes not meeting the criteria may be referred for prosecution.

units.obligation_text: Shooters have the responsibility to identify their target before shooting
units.action_summary: Shooters must identify targets before shooting to avoid unlawful takes.

units.obligation_text: Any person with a valid permit issued by the Service under 50 CFR 17.32, or our designated agent, may take wolves in the wild, pursuant to terms of the permit
units.action_summary: Persons holding valid Service (or designated agent) permits may take wolves according to permit terms.

units.obligation_text: When acting in the course of official duties, any employee of the Service or a designated agent may take a wolf when necessary in regard to the release, tracking, monitoring, recapture, and management of the NEP or to: (A) Aid or euthanize a sick, injured, or orphaned wolf and transfer it to a licensed veterinarian for care; (B) Dispose of a dead specimen; (C) Salvage a dead specimen that may be used for scientific study; (D) Aid in law enforcement investigations involving wolves; or (E) Remove wolves with abnormal physical or behavioral characteristics
units.actor: employees of the Service or designated agents
units.action_summary: Agency employees may take wolves as necessary for NEP activities and listed purposes (A–E) during official duties.

units.obligation_text: Such take must be reported to the Service as set forth in paragraph (a)(6) of this section, and specimens are to be retained or disposed of only in accordance with directions from the Service
units.actor: employees of the Service or designated agents
units.action_summary: Agency employee takes must be reported per reporting rules and specimens handled as directed by the Service.

units.obligation_text: Permits are available and required, except as otherwise allowed by this rule, for scientific purposes, enhancement of propagation or survival, educational purposes, or other purposes consistent with the Act (50 CFR 17.32)
units.actor: persons seeking to take wolves for research/scientific/educational/enhancement purposes
units.action_summary: Permits are required for research, propagation, education, or other Act-consistent purposes unless otherwise allowed by this rule.

units.obligation_text: Except as otherwise specified in this rule or in an authorization, any take of a gray wolf must be reported to the Service or our designated agent as follows: Lethal take must be reported within 24 hours, and opportunistic or intentional harassment must be reported within 7 days
units.actor: any person who takes a gray wolf
units.action_summary: All takes must be reported: lethal takes within 24 hours; opportunistic or intentional harassment within 7 days, unless otherwise specified.

units.obligation_text: Report any take of wolves, including opportunistic harassment or intentional harassment, to U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Colorado Ecological Services Field Office Supervisor ... or a Service-designated agent of another Federal, State, or Tribal agency
units.actor: any person who takes or harasses wolves
units.action_summary: Takes and harassment must be reported to the specified Service office or a designated agent.

units.obligation_text: Unless otherwise specified in this paragraph (a) any wolf or wolf part taken legally must be turned over to the Service, which will determine the disposition of any live or dead wolves
units.actor: any person who legally takes a wolf or wolf part
units.action_summary: Legally taken wolves or wolf parts must be turned over to the Service for disposition.

units.obligation_text: Take of any gray wolf in the NEP is prohibited, except as provided in paragraphs (a)(5) and (8) of this section
units.action_summary: Taking wolves in the NEP is generally prohibited except where expressly allowed by (a)(5) and (8).

units.obligation_text: No person shall possess, sell, deliver, carry, transport, ship, import, or export by any means whatsoever, any wolf or part thereof from the experimental population taken in violation of the regulations in this paragraph (a) or in violation of applicable State or Tribal fish and wildlife laws or regulations or the Act
units.action_summary: Possessing, selling, transporting, or moving wolves or parts taken in violation of this rule or applicable laws is prohibited.

units.obligation_text: It is unlawful for any person to attempt to commit, solicit another to commit, or cause to be committed any offense defined in this paragraph (a)
units.action_summary: Attempting, soliciting, or causing offenses defined in this paragraph is unlawful.

units.obligation_text: Gray wolves in the NEP area will be monitored by radio telemetry or other standard wolf population monitoring techniques as appropriate
units.actor: the Service or designated monitoring entities
units.action_summary: Wolves in the NEP will be monitored using telemetry or other standard techniques.

units.obligation_text: Any animal that is sick, injured, or otherwise in need of special care may be captured by authorized personnel of the Service or our designated agent and given appropriate care
units.actor: authorized personnel of the Service or designated agent
units.action_summary: Authorized personnel may capture and provide care to sick, injured, or needy wolves.

units.obligation_text: Such an animal will be released back into its respective area as soon as possible, unless physical or behavioral problems make it necessary to return the animal to captivity or euthanize it
units.actor: authorized personnel of the Service or designated agent
units.action_summary: Captured animals should be released promptly unless health/behavior require captivity or euthanasia.
units.modal_raw: will be released / necessary to return

units.obligation_text: If a gray wolf is taken into captivity for care or is euthanized, it must be reported to the Service within 24 hours or as soon as reasonably appropriate
units.actor: authorized personnel or person taking a wolf into captivity/euthanizing
units.action_summary: Captivity or euthanasia of a wolf must be reported to the Service within 24 hours or as soon as reasonably appropriate.

units.obligation_text: To evaluate progress toward achieving State downlisting and delisting criteria, the Service will summarize this information in an annual report by CPW, submitted by June 30 of each year, that describes wolf conservation and management activities that occurred in Colorado each calendar or biological year
units.action_summary: The Service will compile and CPW will submit an annual report by June 30 describing wolf conservation and management activities.

units.obligation_text: The Service will evaluate Colorado's wolf reintroduction and management program in a summary report each year that wolf reintroductions occur in the State and for a minimum of 5 years after reintroductions are complete
units.action_summary: The Service will annually evaluate Colorado's reintroduction program during reintroductions and for at least 5 years thereafter.

units.obligation_text: If the Service determines that modifications to reintroduction protocols and wolf monitoring and management activities are needed, the Service will coordinate closely with the State to ensure progress toward achieving recovery goals while concurrently minimizing wolf-related conflicts in Colorado
units.action_summary: The Service must coordinate with the State to modify protocols or management if needed to meet recovery goals while minimizing conflicts.

units.obligation_text: The State of Colorado or any Tribe within the State, subject to the terms of this rule, may request an MOA from the Service to take over lead management responsibility and authority to implement this rule by managing the nonessential experimental gray wolves in the State or on that Tribal reservation, and implement all parts of their State or Tribal plan that are consistent with this rule, provided that the State or Tribe has a wolf management plan approved by the Service
units.actor: the State of Colorado or any Tribe within the State
units.action_summary: States or Tribes with an approved wolf management plan may request an MOA to assume lead management under this rule.

units.obligation_text: The State or Tribal request for wolf management under an MOA must demonstrate: (A) that authority and management capability reside in the State or Tribe; (B) that the State or Tribe has an acceptable conservation program including requisite authority and capacity; (C) exactly what parts of the State or Tribal plan the State or Tribe intends to implement; and (D) that the State or Tribal management progress will be reported to the Service on at least an annual basis
units.actor: the State or Tribe requesting an MOA
units.action_summary: MOA requests must demonstrate authority/capability, an acceptable conservation program, specified plan parts to implement, and annual reporting commitments.

units.obligation_text: The Service will approve such a request upon a finding that the applicable criteria are met and that approval is not likely to jeopardize the continued existence of the gray wolf in the NEP
units.action_summary: The Service will approve MOA requests only if criteria are met and approval is unlikely to jeopardize the wolf's continued existence in the NEP.

units.obligation_text: If the Service approves the request, the Service will enter into an MOA with the State of Colorado or appropriate Tribal representative
units.action_summary: Upon approval, the Service will enter into an MOA with the State or Tribal representative.

units.obligation_text: The MOA may not provide for any form of management inconsistent with the protection provided to the species under this rule, without further opportunity for appropriate public comment and review and amendment of this rule
units.action_summary: An MOA cannot authorize management inconsistent with this rule's protections without further public comment and rule amendment.

units.obligation_text: The MOA cannot vest the State of Colorado or any Tribe within the State with any authority over matters concerning section 4 of the Act (determining whether a species warrants listing)
units.action_summary: An MOA cannot grant State or Tribe authority over section 4 listing determinations.

units.obligation_text: In the absence of a Tribal wolf management plan or cooperative agreement, the MOA cannot vest the State of Colorado with the authority to issue written authorizations for wolf take on reservations. The Service will retain the authority to issue these written authorizations until a Tribal wolf management plan is developed
units.action_summary: Without a Tribal plan/agreement, the State cannot be given authority to authorize take on reservations; the Service retains that authority until a Tribal plan exists.

units.obligation_text: The MOA for State or Tribal wolf management must provide for joint law enforcement responsibilities to ensure that the Service also has the authority to enforce the State or Tribal management program prohibitions on take
units.action_summary: MOAs must include joint law enforcement responsibilities ensuring the Service can enforce prohibitions on take under the State/Tribal program.

units.obligation_text: The MOA may not authorize wolf take beyond that stated in the rule but may be more restrictive
units.action_summary: An MOA cannot permit take beyond the rule's allowances but may impose stricter restrictions.

units.obligation_text: The authority for the MOA will be the Act, the Fish and Wildlife Act of 1956 ..., and the Fish and Wildlife Coordination Act ..., and any applicable treaty
units.actor: the Service and MOA parties (authority citation)
units.action_summary: The MOA authority is established under specified federal statutes and applicable treaties.

units.obligation_text: In order for the MOA to remain in effect, the Service must find, on an annual basis, that the management under the MOA is not jeopardizing the continued existence of the gray wolf in the NEP
units.action_summary: The Service must annually determine that MOA management is not jeopardizing the gray wolf's continued existence for the MOA to remain in effect.

units.obligation_text: The Service or State or Tribe may terminate the MOA upon 90 days' notice if: (A) Management under the MOA is likely to jeopardize the continued existence of the gray wolf in the NEP; (B) The State or Tribe has failed materially to comply with this rule, the MOA, or any relevant provision of the State or Tribal wolf management plan; (C) The Service determines that biological circumstances indicate that delisting the species is warranted; or (D) The States or Tribes determine that they no longer want the wolf management authority vested in them by the Service in the MOA
units.actor: the Service or State or Tribe
units.action_summary: The Service, State, or Tribe can terminate an MOA with 90 days' notice for specified causes including jeopardy, material noncompliance, delisting, or desire to relinquish authority.

units.obligation_text: When one or more of the for cause standards provided in paragraph (b)(2) of this section applies to a Treasury-certified surety, ICE may, in its discretion, initiate the process to notify the surety that it will decline future bonds.

units.obligation_text: This written determination constitutes final agency action.

units.obligation_text: Consistent with section 10(c) of the Administrative Procedure Act, 5 U.S.C. 704, the AAO's decision on appeal of a breach determination constitutes final agency action.

units.obligation_text: Dismissal of an appeal is effective upon the date of the AAO decision.

units.obligation_text: Only the granting of a motion to reopen or reconsider makes the decision no longer final.

units.action_summary: The surety or its agent is required to raise all issues and present all supporting facts in its AAO appeal.

units.obligation_text: A Treasury-certified surety's or its agent's failure to timely raise any claim, defense, or argument before the AAO in support of reversal or remand of a breach decision waives and forfeits that claim, defense, or argument.
units.action_summary: If the surety or agent does not timely raise a claim, defense, or argument before the AAO, that claim/defense/argument is waived and forfeited.

units.obligation_text: If a Treasury-certified surety or its bonding agent does not timely file an appeal with the AAO upon receipt of a breach notice, a claim in favor of ICE is created on the bond breach determination, and ICE may seek to collect the amount due on the breached bond.

units.action_summary: Person who violates 49 U.S.C. 32911(a) must pay a civil penalty up to $41,484 for each violation.

units.obligation_text: A separate violation occurs for each day the violation continues.
units.action_summary: Each day a violation continues is counted as a separate violation for penalty purposes.

units.obligation_text: Except as provided in 49 U.S.C. 32912(c), a manufacturer that violates a standard prescribed for a model year under 49 U.S.C. 32902 is liable to the United States Government for a civil penalty of $5.50 multiplied by each .1 of a mile a gallon by which the applicable average fuel economy standard under that section exceeds the average fuel economy—
units.actor: A manufacturer that violates a standard prescribed for a model year under 49 U.S.C. 32902
units.action_summary: Manufacturer violating a model-year fuel economy standard must pay a civil penalty equal to $5.50 per 0.1 mpg by which the standard exceeds the manufacturer's average fuel economy, subject to calculation rules and statutory exceptions.

units.obligation_text: Except as provided in 49 U.S.C. 32912(c)
units.actor: A manufacturer that violates a standard prescribed for a model year under 49 U.S.C. 32902
units.action_summary: The liability in paragraph (h)(2) is subject to the exceptions provided in 49 U.S.C. 32912(c).

units.obligation_text: Calculated under 49 U.S.C. 32904(a)(1)(A) or (B) for automobiles to which the standard applies manufactured by the manufacturer during the model year;
units.actor: The manufacturer (for purposes of the penalty calculation)
units.action_summary: The manufacturer's average fuel economy used in the penalty calculation is determined under 49 U.S.C. 32904(a)(1)(A) or (B) for applicable automobiles manufactured in the model year.

units.obligation_text: Multiplied by the number of those automobiles;
units.action_summary: The per-0.1-mpg penalty amount is multiplied by the number of applicable automobiles manufactured by the manufacturer in the model year.

units.obligation_text: Reduced by the credits available to the manufacturer under 49 U.S.C. 32903 for the model year.
units.action_summary: The calculated penalty is reduced by any credits available under 49 U.S.C. 32903 for the model year.

title: Make Inoperative Exemptions: Vehicle Modifications To Accommodate People With Disabilities

units.obligation_text: A rental company that modifies a motor vehicle temporarily in order to rent a covered rental vehicle to a person with a disability to operate, or ride as a passenger in, the motor vehicle is exempted from the "make inoperative" prohibition in 49 U.S.C. 30122 to the extent that those modifications make inoperative any part of a device or element of design installed on or in the motor vehicle in compliance with the Federal motor vehicle safety standards or portions thereof specified in paragraph (d) of this section.
units.action_summary: Rental companies are exempted from the statutory 'make inoperative' prohibition to the extent their temporary modifications make inoperative parts installed in compliance with the FMVSS provisions specified in paragraph (d).

units.obligation_text: Modifications that would make inoperative devices or elements of design installed in compliance with any other Federal motor vehicle safety standards, or portions thereof, are not covered by this exemption.
units.action_summary: Modifications that make inoperative devices installed to comply with any FMVSS other than those specified in paragraph (d) are not exempted.

units.obligation_text: The exemption described in paragraph (a) extends only for the period during which the covered rental vehicle is rented to a person with a disability and a reasonable period before and after the rental agreement in order to perform and reverse the modification described in paragraph (d) of this section.
units.action_summary: The exemption applies only during the rental to a person with a disability and for a reasonable time before and after to install and remove the modification.

units.obligation_text: Any rental company that temporarily modifies a motor vehicle to enable a person with a disability to operate, or ride as a passenger in, the motor vehicle in such a manner as to make inoperative any part of a device or element of design installed on or in the motor vehicle in compliance with a Federal motor vehicle safety standard or portion thereof specified in paragraph (d) of this section must affix to the motor vehicle a label of the type and in the manner described in paragraph (e) of this section and must provide and retain a document of the type and in the manner described in paragraph (f) of this section.
units.action_summary: When a rental company temporarily modifies a vehicle in a way that makes inoperative parts installed to meet the FMVSS provisions in paragraph (d), it must affix a label as described in (e) and provide and retain a document as described in (f).

units.obligation_text: 49 CFR 571.208, in the case of the disablement of a knee bolster air bag to allow the installation of hand controls.
units.action_summary: Specifies that 49 CFR 571.208 is the FMVSS provision covered when the knee bolster air bag is disabled to permit installation of hand controls.

units.obligation_text: The label required by paragraph (c) of this section shall:
units.action_summary: Introduces the mandatory specifications for the label that rental companies must affix under paragraph (c).

units.obligation_text: Be affixed within the passenger compartment of the vehicle.
units.action_summary: Label must be placed inside the vehicle passenger compartment.

units.obligation_text: Be affixed in a location visible to the driver in a manner that does not obstruct the driver’s view while operating the vehicle.
units.action_summary: Label must be visible to the driver and must not obstruct the driver's view.

units.obligation_text: Contain the statement "WARNING—To accommodate installation of hand controls, this rental vehicle has had its knee bolster air bags temporarily disabled,"
units.action_summary: Label must include the specified warning statement about temporarily disabled knee bolster air bags.

units.obligation_text: Be removed when the modifications described in paragraph (d) are reversed.
units.action_summary: Label must be removed when the underlying modifications are undone.

units.obligation_text: The document required by paragraph (c) of this section shall:
units.action_summary: Introduces the mandatory specifications for the document that rental companies must provide and retain under paragraph (c).

units.obligation_text: Be provided in original or photocopied paper form, or in electronic form to the renter of the covered rental vehicle at the time of execution of the rental agreement;
units.action_summary: Document must be given to the renter at the time the rental agreement is executed, in paper or electronic form.

units.obligation_text: Contain the name and physical address of the rental company making the modifications;
units.action_summary: Document must include the name and physical address of the rental company that made the modifications.

units.obligation_text: Be kept in original or photocopied paper form, or retained electronically, by the rental company for a period of not less than five years after the conclusion of the rental agreement for which the modification is made;
units.action_summary: Rental company must retain the document for at least five years after the rental agreement ends.

units.obligation_text: Be clearly identifiable as to the vehicle that has been modified;
units.action_summary: Document must clearly identify which vehicle was modified.

units.obligation_text: Identify the devices or elements of design installed on or in a motor vehicle in compliance with a Federal motor vehicle safety standard made inoperative by the rental company.
units.action_summary: Document must identify which FMVSS devices or design elements were made inoperative by the rental company.

title: Standard Reference Test Tire

units.obligation_text: For vehicles with a GVWR greater than 10,000 pounds, road tests (excluding stability and control during braking tests) are conducted on a 12-foot-wide, level roadway, having a peak friction coefficient of 1.02 when measured using an ASTM F2493–19 (incorporated by reference, see § 571.5), standard reference test tire, in accordance with ASTM E1337–19 (incorporated by reference, see § 571.5), at a speed of 40 mph, without water delivery.
units.actor: test administrators/parties conducting the road tests
units.action_summary: Road tests for vehicles over 10,000 lb GVWR must be conducted on a 12-foot-wide, level roadway with PFC 1.02 measured with ASTM F2493–19 tire at 40 mph, without water delivery, per ASTM E1337–19.

units.obligation_text: Burnish stops are conducted on any surface.
units.action_summary: Burnish stops must be performed and may be conducted on any surface.

units.obligation_text: The parking brake test surface is clean, dry, smooth, Portland cement concrete.
units.actor: test administrators/parties setting up the parking brake test
units.action_summary: The parking brake test surface must be clean, dry, smooth Portland cement concrete.

units.obligation_text: For vehicles with a GVWR greater than 10,000 pounds, stability and control during braking tests are conducted on a 500-foot-radius curved roadway with a wet level surface having a peak friction coefficient of 0.55 when measured on a straight or curved section of the curved roadway using an ASTM F2493–19 standard reference tire, in accordance with ASTM E1337–19 at a speed of 40 mph, with water delivery.
units.actor: test administrators/parties conducting stability and control tests
units.action_summary: Stability and control braking tests for vehicles over 10,000 lb GVWR must be conducted on a 500-foot-radius wet curved roadway with PFC 0.55 measured with ASTM F2493–19 tire at 40 mph with water delivery per ASTM E1337–19.

units.obligation_text: Stop the vehicle from 60 mph on a surface with a peak friction coefficient of 1.02 with the vehicle loaded as follows:
units.actor: test administrators/persons performing the stop test (vehicle being tested)
units.action_summary: During the test, the vehicle must be stopped from 60 mph on a surface with PFC 1.02 with specified vehicle loading.

units.obligation_text: Using a full-treadle brake application for the duration of the stop, stop the vehicle from 30 mph or 75 percent of the maximum drive-through speed, whichever is less, on a 500-foot radius curved roadway with a wet level surface having a peak friction coefficient of 0.55 when measured on a straight or curved section of the curved roadway using an ASTM F2493–19 (incorporated by reference, see § 571.5) standard reference tire, in accordance with ASTM E1337–19 (incorporated by reference, see § 571.5), at a speed of 40 mph, with water delivery.
units.actor: test administrators/persons performing the stop test (vehicle being tested)
units.action_summary: Using full-treadle brake application, the vehicle must be stopped from 30 mph (or 75% of max drive-through speed) on a 500-ft radius wet curve with PFC 0.55 measured using ASTM F2493–19 tire per ASTM E1337–19 at 40 mph with water delivery.

units.obligation_text: When stopped six times for each combination of weight and speed specified in S5.3.1.1, except for a loaded truck tractor with an unbraked control trailer, on a road surface having a PFC of 1.02, with a single failure in the service brake system of a part designed to contain compressed air or brake fluid (except failure of a common valve, manifold, brake fluid housing, or brake chamber housing), the vehicle shall stop at least once in not more than the distance specified in Column 5 of Table II, measured from the point at which movement of the service brake control begins, except that a truck-tractor tested at its unloaded vehicle weight plus up to 1,500 pounds shall stop at least once in not more than the distance specified in Column 6 of Table II.
units.actor: the vehicle (during the emergency brake system performance test) / test administrators conducting the test
units.action_summary: Under the specified single-failure emergency condition and test regimen, the vehicle must stop at least once within the distances given in Table II Column 5 (or Column 6 for certain truck-tractors).

units.obligation_text: The stop shall be made without any part of the vehicle leaving the roadway,
units.action_summary: The required stop must be completed without any portion of the vehicle leaving the roadway.

units.obligation_text: with unlimited wheel lockup permitted at any speed.
units.action_summary: Wheel lockup is allowed without limit at any speed during the stop.

units.obligation_text: Unless otherwise specified, stopping tests are conducted on a 12-foot wide level, straight roadway having a peak friction coefficient of 1.02.
units.action_summary: Stopping tests must be conducted on a 12-foot-wide level straight roadway with PFC 1.02 unless otherwise specified.

units.obligation_text: For road tests in S5.3, the vehicle is aligned in the center of the roadway at the beginning of a stop.
units.action_summary: At the start of a stop in S5.3 tests, the vehicle must be aligned in the center of the roadway.

units.obligation_text: Peak friction coefficient is measured using an ASTM F2493–19 standard reference test tire (see ASTM F2493–19 (incorporated by reference, see § 571.5)) in accordance with ASTM E1337–19 (incorporated by reference, see § 571.5), at a speed of 40 mph, without water delivery for the surface with PFC of 1.02, and with water delivery for the surface with PFC of 0.55.
units.actor: test administrators/parties measuring peak friction coefficient
units.action_summary: PFC must be measured with ASTM F2493–19 tire per ASTM E1337–19 at 40 mph: without water for surfaces targeted PFC 1.02 and with water for PFC 0.55.

units.obligation_text: Stopping distance requirements are as specified in Table II (Column 5 and Column 6 referenced in S5.7.1).
units.action_summary: The maximum allowable stopping distances for the emergency stop requirement are set by the values in Table II (columns referenced by S5.7.1).

units.obligation_text: High friction surface. A high friction surface is used for all dynamic brake tests excluding the ABS tests where a low-friction surface is specified.
units.actor: test administrators/parties conducting dynamic brake tests
units.action_summary: High-friction surfaces must be used for all dynamic brake tests except where ABS-tests require a low-friction surface.

units.obligation_text: The high-friction surface test area is a clean, dry and level surface, with a gradient of ≤1 percent.
units.actor: test administrators/parties preparing the test area
units.action_summary: The high-friction test area must be clean, dry, level, and have gradient ≤1%.

units.obligation_text: The high-friction surface has a peak braking coefficient (PBC) of 1.02.
units.actor: test administrators/parties providing the test surface
units.action_summary: The high-friction surface must have a PBC of 1.02.

units.obligation_text: Low-friction surface. A low-friction surface is used for ABS tests where a low-friction surface is specified.
units.action_summary: Low-friction surfaces must be used for ABS tests where specified.

units.obligation_text: The low-friction surface test area is a clean and level surface, which may be wet or dry, with a gradient of ≤1 percent.
units.actor: test administrators/parties preparing the test area
units.action_summary: The low-friction test area must be clean and level, may be wet or dry, and have gradient ≤1%.

units.obligation_text: The low-friction surface has a PBC of ≤0.50.
units.actor: test administrators/parties providing the test surface
units.action_summary: The low-friction surface must have a PBC of ≤0.50.

units.obligation_text: Measurement of PBC. The PBC is measured using the ASTM F2493–19 standard reference test tire, in accordance with ASTM E1337–19, at a speed of 64 km/h (both publications incorporated by reference; see § 571.5).
units.action_summary: PBC measurement must be performed using the ASTM F2493–19 tire per ASTM E1337–19 at 64 km/h.

units.obligation_text: Test surfaces. A low friction surface immediately followed by a high friction surface with a PBC ≥0.90.
units.actor: test administrators/parties setting up the test surfaces
units.action_summary: The test sequence must use a low-friction surface immediately followed by a high-friction surface having PBC ≥0.90.

units.obligation_text: The road test surface must produce a peak friction coefficient (PFC) of 1.02 when measured using an ASTM F2493–19 (incorporated by reference, see § 571.5) standard reference test tire, in accordance with ASTM E1337–19 (incorporated by reference, see § 571.5) at a speed of 64.4 km/h (40 mph), without water delivery.
units.actor: test administrators/parties providing the road test surface
units.action_summary: Road test surface must produce PFC 1.02 measured with ASTM F2493–19 tire per ASTM E1337–19 at 64.4 km/h (40 mph) without water delivery.

units.obligation_text: Unless otherwise specified, the road test surface produces a peak friction coefficient (PFC) of 1.02 when measured using an ASTM F2493–19 (incorporated by reference, see § 571.5) standard reference test tire, in accordance with ASTM E1337–19 (incorporated by reference, see § 571.5), at a speed of 64.4 km/h (40 mph), without water delivery.
units.actor: test administrators/parties providing the road test surface
units.action_summary: Unless stated otherwise, road test surfaces must produce PFC 1.02 measured with ASTM F2493–19 tire per ASTM E1337–19 at 64.4 km/h (40 mph) without water delivery.

units.obligation_text: Test surface: PFC of at least 1.02.
units.actor: test administrators/parties providing the test surface
units.action_summary: The test surface must have a peak friction coefficient of at least 1.02 for the test in S7.4.3.

units.obligation_text: Test surface: PFC of 1.02.
units.actor: test administrators/parties providing the test surface
units.action_summary: The test surface must have a PFC of 1.02 for the S7.5.2 test.

units.obligation_text: Test surface: PFC of 1.02.
units.actor: test administrators/parties providing the test surface
units.action_summary: The test surface must have a PFC of 1.02 for the S7.6.2 test.

units.obligation_text: Test surface: PFC of 1.02.
units.actor: test administrators/parties providing the test surface
units.action_summary: The test surface must have a PFC of 1.02 for the S7.7.3 test.

units.obligation_text: Test surface: PFC of 1.02.
units.actor: test administrators/parties providing the test surface
units.action_summary: The test surface must have a PFC of 1.02 for the S7.8.2 test.

units.obligation_text: Test surface: PFC of 1.02.
units.actor: test administrators/parties providing the test surface
units.action_summary: The test surface must have a PFC of 1.02 for the S7.9.2 test.

units.obligation_text: Test surface: PFC of 1.02.
units.actor: test administrators/parties providing the test surface
units.action_summary: The test surface must have a PFC of 1.02 for the S7.10.3 test.

units.obligation_text: Test surface: PFC of 1.02.
units.actor: test administrators/parties providing the test surface
units.action_summary: The test surface must have a PFC of 1.02 for the S7.11.3 test.

units.obligation_text: The road test surface produces a peak friction coefficient (PFC) of 1.02 when measured using an ASTM F2493–19 standard reference test tire, in accordance with ASTM E1337–19, at a speed of 64.4 km/h (40 mph), without water delivery (both documents incorporated by reference; see § 571.5).
units.actor: test administrators/parties providing the road test surface
units.action_summary: The road test surface must produce a PFC of 1.02 measured with ASTM F2493–19 tire per ASTM E1337–19 at 64.4 km/h (40 mph) without water delivery.

units.obligation_text: Snow tire means a tire that attains a traction index equal to or greater than 112, compared to the ASTM F2493–19 (incorporated by reference, see § 571.5) Standard Reference Test Tire when using the snow traction test on the medium pack snow surface as described in ASTM F1805–20 (incorporated by reference, see § 571.5), and that is marked with an Alpine Symbol specified in S5.5(i) on at least one sidewall.
units.action_summary: To qualify as a 'snow tire' a tire must achieve a traction index ≥112 versus the ASTM F2493–19 reference tire on the medium pack snow test (ASTM F1805–20) and be marked with the Alpine Symbol on at least one sidewall.

units.obligation_text: Pavement friction. Unless otherwise specified, the road test surface produces a peak friction coefficient (PFC) of 1.02 when measured using a standard reference test tire that meets the specifications of ASTM F2493–19, in accordance with ASTM E1337–19, at a speed of 64.4 km/h (40.0 mph), without water delivery (both incorporated by reference; see § 571.5).
units.actor: test administrators/parties providing the road test surface
units.action_summary: Unless otherwise specified, road test surfaces must produce PFC 1.02 measured with a standard reference test tire meeting ASTM F2493–19 per ASTM E1337–19 at 64.4 km/h (40 mph) without water delivery.

units.obligation_text: Drive the convoy on the test roadway for 16 circuits (approximately 6,400 miles).
units.actor: test administrators/operators conducting the convoy test
units.action_summary: The convoy must be driven for 16 circuits (~6,400 miles) on the test roadway.

units.obligation_text: After every circuit (approximately 400 miles), rotate each vehicle’s tires by moving each front tire to the same side of the rear axle and each rear tire to the opposite side of the front axle. Visually inspect each tire for treadwear anomalies.
units.action_summary: After each ~400-mile circuit, rotate tires in the specified pattern and visually inspect tires for treadwear anomalies.

units.obligation_text: After every second circuit (approximately 800 miles), rotate the vehicles in the convoy by moving the last vehicle to the lead position.
units.action_summary: After every ~800-mile (2-circuit) interval, move the last vehicle to the lead position in the convoy.

units.obligation_text: Do not rotate driver positions within the convoy.
units.action_summary: Rotating driver positions within the convoy is prohibited.

units.obligation_text: In four-car convoys, vehicle one shall become vehicle two, vehicle two shall become vehicle three, vehicle three shall become vehicle four, and vehicle four shall become vehicle one.
units.action_summary: For four-car convoys, the vehicles must be rotated forward in sequence as specified.

units.obligation_text: After every second circuit (approximately 800 miles), if necessary, adjust wheel alignment to the midpoint of the vehicle manufacturer’s specification,
units.action_summary: If necessary after every ~800 miles, wheel alignment must be adjusted to the manufacturer's midpoint specification.

units.obligation_text: unless adjustment to the midpoint is not recommended by the manufacturer; in that case, adjust the alignment to the manufacturer’s recommended setting.
units.action_summary: If the manufacturer does not recommend midpoint alignment, adjust to the manufacturer's recommended alignment instead (exception to the midpoint requirement).

units.obligation_text: In all cases, the setting is within the tolerance specified by the manufacturer of the alignment machine.
units.action_summary: Regardless of chosen alignment setting, it must be within the alignment machine manufacturer's specified tolerance.

units.obligation_text: After every second circuit (approximately 800 miles), if determining the projected mileage by the 9-point method set forth in paragraph (e)(2)(ix)(A)(1) of this section, measure the average tread depth of each tire following the procedure set forth in paragraph (e)(2)(vi) of this section.
units.action_summary: If using the 9-point method, after every ~800 miles measure average tread depth per the procedure in paragraph (e)(2)(vi).

units.obligation_text: After every fourth circuit (approximately 1,600 miles), move the complete set of four tires to the following vehicle. Move the tires on the last vehicle to the lead vehicle. In moving the tires, rotate them as set forth in paragraph (e)(2)(viii)(A) of this section.
units.action_summary: After every ~1,600 miles, move each vehicle's full set of four tires to the next vehicle (last to lead) and rotate tires according to paragraph (e)(2)(viii)(A).

units.obligation_text: The course monitoring tires used in a test convoy must be no more than one-year-old at the commencement of the test
units.actor: test administrators/operators (those selecting/using course monitoring tires)
units.action_summary: Course monitoring tires must be no more than one year old at the start of the test.

units.obligation_text: and must be used within four months after removal from storage.
units.actor: test administrators/operators (those selecting/using course monitoring tires)
units.action_summary: Course monitoring tires removed from storage must be used within four months.

units.obligation_text: Round off the percentage to the nearest lower 20-point increment.
units.actor: test administrators/NHTSA personnel computing the grade
units.action_summary: When computing the NHTSA nominal treadwear grade percentage, round it down to the nearest lower 20-point increment.

title: Civil Penalties

units.obligation_text: Except as provided in 49 U.S.C. 32912(c), beginning with model year 2019, a manufacturer that violates a standard prescribed for a model year under 49 U.S.C. 32902 is liable to the United States Government for a civil penalty of $14, plus any adjustments for inflation that occurred or may occur (for model years before model year 2019, the civil penalty is $5.50), multiplied by each .1 of a mile a gallon by which the applicable average fuel economy standard under that section exceeds the average fuel economy—
units.actor: a manufacturer that violates a standard prescribed for a model year under 49 U.S.C. 32902
units.action_summary: Manufacturer is liable to the U.S. Government for a civil penalty calculated per 0.1 mpg by which the standard exceeds the manufacturer's average fuel economy, using the specified dollar amount and adjustments.

units.obligation_text: Except as provided in 49 U.S.C. 32912(c),
units.actor: a manufacturer that violates a standard prescribed for a model year under 49 U.S.C. 32902
units.action_summary: The liability in this paragraph does not apply where 49 U.S.C. 32912(c) provides otherwise.

units.obligation_text: beginning with model year 2019,
units.actor: a manufacturer that violates a standard prescribed for a model year under 49 U.S.C. 32902
units.action_summary: The $14 (plus inflation adjustments) penalty amount applies starting with model year 2019.

units.obligation_text: (for model years before model year 2019, the civil penalty is $5.50)
units.actor: a manufacturer that violates a standard prescribed for a model year under 49 U.S.C. 32902
units.action_summary: For model years before 2019, the civil penalty amount is $5.50 (per 0.1 mpg as otherwise specified).

units.obligation_text: Calculated under 49 U.S.C. 32904(a)(1)(A) or (B) for automobiles to which the standard applies produced by the manufacturer during the model year;
units.actor: the manufacturer (for purposes of determining the average fuel economy used in the penalty calculation)
units.action_summary: The manufacturer's average fuel economy used in the penalty calculation must be calculated under 49 U.S.C. 32904(a)(1)(A) or (B) for applicable automobiles produced during the model year.

units.obligation_text: Multiplied by the number of those automobiles;
units.actor: the manufacturer (as to whose produced automobiles the calculation applies)
units.action_summary: The per-0.1 mpg penalty amount is multiplied by the number of applicable automobiles produced by the manufacturer.

units.obligation_text: Reduced by the credits available to the manufacturer under 49 U.S.C. 32903 for the model year.
