units.actor: the manufacturer (and the assessing authority calculating the penalty)
units.action_summary: The calculated penalty amount must be reduced by any credits available to the manufacturer under 49 U.S.C. 32903 for that model year.

title: Corporate Average Fuel Economy Standards for Model Years 2024-2026 Passenger Cars and Light Trucks

units.obligation_text: This part applies to manufacturers of passenger automobiles.
units.action_summary: The part's provisions are applicable to manufacturers of passenger automobiles.

units.obligation_text: Except as provided in paragraph (f) of this section, each manufacturer of passenger automobiles shall comply with the fleet average fuel economy standards in Table 1 to this paragraph (a), expressed in miles per gallon, in the model year specified as applicable:
units.action_summary: Manufacturers must meet the fleet average fuel economy standards shown in Table 1 for the applicable model year.

units.obligation_text: For model year 2011, a manufacturer’s passenger automobile fleet shall comply with the fleet average fuel economy level calculated for that model year according to Figure 1 to this paragraph (b) and the appropriate values in Table 2 to this paragraph (b).
units.action_summary: Manufacturers must comply with the fleet average fuel economy level calculated using Figure 1 and Table 2 for MY 2011.

units.obligation_text: For model years 2012–2026, a manufacturer’s passenger automobile fleet shall comply with the fleet average fuel economy level calculated for that model year according to Figure 2 to this paragraph (c) and the appropriate values in Table 3 to this paragraph (c).
units.action_summary: Manufacturers must comply with fleet average fuel economy levels calculated using Figure 2 and Table 3 for MYs 2012–2026.

units.obligation_text: In addition to the requirements of paragraphs (b) and (c) of this section, each manufacturer shall also meet the minimum fleet standard for domestically manufactured passenger automobiles expressed in Table 4 to this paragraph (d):
units.action_summary: Manufacturers must also meet the domestically manufactured passenger automobile minimum fleet standard shown in Table 4.

units.obligation_text: The following manufacturers shall comply with the standards indicated in paragraphs (e)(1) through (15) of this section for the specified model years:
units.actor: the manufacturers listed in paragraphs (e)(1) through (e)(15)
units.action_summary: Named manufacturers must comply with the specific standards provided for them in subparagraphs (e)(1)-(15).

units.obligation_text: The fleet average fuel economy performance of all passenger automobiles that are manufactured by a manufacturer in a model year shall be determined in accordance with procedures established by the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) under 49 U.S.C. 32904 and set forth in 40 CFR part 600.
units.actor: the determination of fleet average fuel economy performance (for manufacturers)
units.action_summary: Fleet average fuel economy must be determined according to EPA procedures in 40 CFR part 600.

units.obligation_text: For model years 2017 and later, a manufacturer is eligible to increase the fuel economy performance of passenger cars in accordance with procedures established by the EPA set forth in 40 CFR part 600, subpart F, including any adjustments to fuel economy the EPA allows, such as for fuel consumption improvements related to air conditioning efficiency and off-cycle technologies.
units.actor: a manufacturer (for model years 2017 and later)
units.action_summary: Manufacturers may increase fleet fuel economy using EPA procedures and allowed adjustments (e.g., AC efficiency, off-cycle tech) for MY 2017 and later.

units.obligation_text: Manufacturers must provide reporting on these technologies as specified in 49 CFR 537.7 by the required deadlines.
units.action_summary: Manufacturers are required to report on technologies (e.g., AC efficiency, off-cycle) as specified in 49 CFR 537.7 by deadlines.

units.obligation_text: A manufacturer that seeks to increase its fleet average fuel economy performance through the use of technologies that improve the efficiency of air conditioning systems must follow the requirements in 40 CFR 86.1868–12.
units.actor: A manufacturer that seeks to increase fleet average fuel economy via AC efficiency technologies
units.action_summary: Manufacturers using AC-efficiency technologies must follow 40 CFR 86.1868–12 requirements.

units.obligation_text: Fuel consumption improvement values resulting from the use of those air conditioning systems must be determined in accordance with 40 CFR 600.510–12(c)(3)(i).
units.actor: Manufacturers (or entities determining fuel consumption improvement values)
units.action_summary: Fuel consumption improvements from AC technologies must be determined per 40 CFR 600.510–12(c)(3)(i).

units.obligation_text: A manufacturer that seeks to increase its fleet average fuel economy performance through the use of off-cycle technologies must follow the requirements in 40 CFR 86.1869–12.
units.actor: A manufacturer that seeks to increase fleet average fuel economy via off-cycle technologies
units.action_summary: Manufacturers using off-cycle technologies must follow 40 CFR 86.1869–12 requirements.

units.obligation_text: A manufacturer is eligible to gain fuel consumption improvements for predefined off-cycle technologies in accordance with 40 CFR 86.1869–12(b) or for technologies tested using the EPA’s 5-cycle methodology in accordance with 40 CFR 86.1869–12(c).
units.action_summary: Manufacturers may obtain fuel consumption improvements for predefined off-cycle technologies per 40 CFR 86.1869–12(b) or via EPA 5-cycle testing per 40 CFR 86.1869–12(c).

units.obligation_text: The fuel consumption improvement is determined in accordance with 40 CFR 600.510–12(c)(3)(ii).
units.action_summary: Fuel consumption improvements from off-cycle technologies must be determined per 40 CFR 600.510–12(c)(3)(ii).

units.obligation_text: A manufacturer is eligible to increase its fuel economy performance through use of an off-cycle technology requiring an application request made to the EPA in accordance with 40 CFR 86.1869–12(d).
units.action_summary: Manufacturers may increase fuel economy using off-cycle technologies that require an EPA application under 40 CFR 86.1869–12(d).

units.obligation_text: Eligibility under the corporate average fuel economy (CAFE) program requires compliance with paragraphs (b)(3)(i)(A) through (C) of this section.
units.actor: A manufacturer seeking CAFE eligibility for alternative-method off-cycle credits
units.action_summary: To be eligible under CAFE for this alternative methodology, manufacturers must comply with subparagraphs (A)–(C).

units.obligation_text: Paragraphs (b)(3)(i)(A), (B), and (D) of this section apply starting in model year 2024.
units.actor: manufacturers and agencies (with respect to applicability)
units.action_summary: Subparagraphs (A), (B), and (D) begin to apply starting in MY 2024.

units.obligation_text: A manufacturer seeking to increase its fuel economy performance using the alternative methodology for an off-cycle technology, if prior to the applicable model year, must submit to EPA a detailed analytical plan and be approved (i.e., for its planned test procedure and model types for demonstration) in accordance with 40 CFR 86.1869–12(d).
units.actor: A manufacturer seeking to use the alternative methodology
units.action_summary: Manufacturers must submit and obtain EPA approval of a detailed analytical plan per 40 CFR 86.1869–12(d) before the model year.

units.obligation_text: A manufacturer seeking to increase its fuel economy performance using the alternative methodology for an off-cycle technology must also submit an official credit application to EPA and obtain approval in accordance with 40 CFR 86.1869–12(e) prior to September of the given model year.
units.actor: A manufacturer seeking alternative-method off-cycle credits
units.action_summary: Manufacturers must submit an official credit application to EPA and obtain approval under 40 CFR 86.1869–12(e) before September of the model year.

units.obligation_text: Manufacturer’s plans, applications, and requests approved by the EPA must be made in consultation with the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA). To expedite NHTSA’s consultation with the EPA, a manufacturer must concurrently submit its application to NHTSA if the manufacturer is seeking off-cycle fuel economy improvement values under the CAFE program for those technologies.
units.action_summary: Manufacturers must ensure EPA-approved plans/applications are made in consultation with NHTSA and must concurrently submit applications to NHTSA when seeking CAFE off-cycle values.

units.obligation_text: A manufacturer may request an extension from NHTSA for more time to obtain an EPA approval.
units.action_summary: Manufacturers are permitted to request an extension from NHTSA to obtain EPA approval.

units.obligation_text: Manufacturers should submit their requests 30 days before the deadlines in paragraphs (b)(3)(i)(A) through (C) of this section. Requests should be submitted to NHTSA’s Director of the Office of Vehicle Safety Compliance at cafe@dot.gov.
units.action_summary: Manufacturers are advised to submit extension requests 30 days before deadlines to NHTSA's Director at cafe@dot.gov.

units.obligation_text: NHTSA will provide its views on the suitability of using the off-cycle technology to adjust the fuel economy performance to the EPA.
units.action_summary: NHTSA is to provide views to EPA regarding suitability of off-cycle technologies for fuel economy adjustments.

units.obligation_text: NHTSA’s evaluation and review will consider: (A) Whether the technology has a direct impact upon improving fuel economy performance; (B) Whether the technology is related to crash-avoidance technologies, safety critical systems or systems affecting safety-critical functions, or technologies designed for the purpose of reducing the frequency of vehicle crashes; (C) Information from any assessments conducted by the EPA related to the application, the technology and/or related technologies; and (D) Any other relevant factors.
units.action_summary: NHTSA must consider specified factors (impact on fuel economy, relation to safety technologies, EPA assessments, and other relevant factors) when evaluating off-cycle technology suitability.

units.obligation_text: Technologies found to be defective, or identified as a part of NHTSA’s safety defects program, and technologies that are not performing as intended, will have the values of approved off-cycle credits removed from the manufacturer’s credit balance or adjusted if the manufacturers can remedy the defective technology.
units.action_summary: If technologies are defective or not performing, approved off-cycle credit values will be removed or adjusted; adjustments possible if manufacturer remedies defect.

units.obligation_text: NHTSA will consult with the manufacturer to determine the amount of the adjustment.
units.action_summary: NHTSA must consult with the manufacturer to determine how much to adjust removed/changed credit values.

units.obligation_text: Approval granted for innovative and off-cycle technology credits under NHTSA’s fuel efficiency program does not affect or relieve the obligation to comply with the Vehicle Safety Act (49 U.S.C. Chapter 301), including the 'make inoperative' prohibition (49 U.S.C. 30122), and all applicable Federal motor vehicle safety standards issued thereunder (FMVSSs) (49 CFR part 571).
units.action_summary: Receiving off-cycle/innovative technology credit approval does not exempt manufacturers from complying with the Vehicle Safety Act and FMVSSs.

units.obligation_text: In order to generate off-cycle or innovative technology credits manufacturers must state— (1) That each vehicle equipped with the technology for which they are seeking credits will comply with all applicable FMVSS(s);
units.action_summary: Manufacturers seeking off-cycle/innovative credits must state that each vehicle with the technology will comply with all applicable FMVSSs.

units.obligation_text: In order to generate off-cycle or innovative technology credits manufacturers must state— (2) Whether or not the technology has a fail-safe provision. If no fail-safe provision exists, the manufacturer must explain why not and whether a failure of the innovative technology would affect the safety of the vehicle.
units.action_summary: Manufacturers must state whether the technology has a fail-safe; if not, explain why and whether its failure would affect vehicle safety.

units.obligation_text: This part applies to manufacturers of light trucks.
units.action_summary: The part's provisions are applicable to manufacturers of light trucks.

units.obligation_text: Each manufacturer of light trucks shall comply with the following fleet average fuel economy standards, expressed in miles per gallon, in the model year specified as applicable:
units.action_summary: Manufacturers must meet the fleet average fuel economy standards set forth for light trucks in the applicable model year.

units.obligation_text: For model year 1979, each manufacturer may: (i) Combine its 2- and 4-wheel drive light trucks and comply with the average fuel economy standard in paragraph (a) of this section for 2-wheel drive light trucks; or (ii) Comply separately with the two standards specified in paragraph (a) of this section.
units.action_summary: For MY 1979 manufacturers may either combine 2- and 4-wheel drive trucks and comply with the 2-wheel standard or comply separately with both standards.

units.obligation_text: For model year 1979, the standard specified in paragraph (a) of this section for 4-wheel drive light trucks applies only to 4-wheel drive general utility vehicles. All other 4-wheel drive light trucks in that model year shall be included in the 2-wheel drive category for compliance purposes.
units.action_summary: In MY 1979, only general utility 4-wheel drive vehicles are subject to the 4-wheel standard; other 4-wheel drive light trucks must be counted in the 2-wheel category.

units.obligation_text: For model years 1980 and 1981, manufacturers of limited product line light trucks may: (1) Comply with the separate standard for limited product line light trucks; or (2) Comply with the other standards specified in paragraph (a) of this section, as applicable.
units.actor: manufacturers of limited product line light trucks (for MYs 1980 and 1981)
units.action_summary: For MYs 1980–81 limited product line manufacturers may either follow the separate limited product line standard or comply with the other applicable standards.

units.obligation_text: For model years 1982–91, each manufacture may: (1) Combine its 2- and 4-wheel drive light trucks (segregating captive import and other light trucks) and comply with the combined average fuel economy standard specified in paragraph (a) of this section; or (2) Comply separately with the 2-wheel drive standards and the 4-wheel drive standards (segregating captive import and other light trucks) specified in paragraph (a) of this section.
units.action_summary: For MYs 1982–91 manufacturers may either combine 2- and 4-wheel drive trucks (with segregation) and comply with the combined standard, or comply separately with the two standards.

units.obligation_text: For model year 1992, each manufacturer shall comply with the average fuel economy standard specified in paragraph (a) of this section (segregating captive import and other light trucks).
units.action_summary: For MY 1992 manufacturers must comply with the average fuel economy standard in paragraph (a), segregating captive imports and other trucks.

units.obligation_text: For each model year 1996 and thereafter, each manufacturer shall combine its captive imports with its other light trucks and comply with the fleet average fuel economy standard in paragraph (a) of this section.
units.action_summary: From MY 1996 onward, manufacturers must combine captive imports with other light trucks for compliance with the fleet standard in paragraph (a).

units.obligation_text: For model years 2008–2010, at a manufacturer’s option, a manufacturer’s light truck fleet may comply with the fuel economy standard calculated for each model year according to Figure 1 to paragraph (a) of this section and the appropriate values in Table 5 to paragraph (a) of this section, with said option being irrevocably chosen for that model year and reported as specified in § 537.8 of this chapter.
units.action_summary: For MYs 2008–2010 manufacturers may opt to comply using Figure 1/Table 5; the option is irrevocable for that model year and must be reported as specified in §537.8.

units.obligation_text: said option being irrevocably chosen for that model year and reported as specified in § 537.8 of this chapter.
units.action_summary: If manufacturer chooses the Figure 1/Table 5 option for a model year, that choice is irrevocable for that model year and must be reported per §537.8.

units.obligation_text: For model year 2011, a manufacturer’s light truck fleet shall comply with the fleet average fuel economy standard calculated for that model year according to Figure 1 to paragraph (a) of this section and the appropriate values in Table 5 to paragraph (a) of this section.
units.action_summary: For MY 2011 manufacturers must comply with fleet average fuel economy standard calculated using Figure 1 and Table 5.

units.obligation_text: For model years 2012–2016, a manufacturer’s light truck fleet shall comply with the fleet average fuel economy standard calculated for that model year according to Figures 2 and 3 to paragraph (a) of this section and the appropriate values in Table 6 to paragraph (a) of this section.
units.action_summary: For MYs 2012–2016 manufacturers must comply with fleet average fuel economy calculated via Figures 2 and 3 and Table 6.

units.obligation_text: For model years 2017–2025, a manufacturer’s light truck fleet shall comply with the fleet average fuel economy standard calculated for that model year according to Figures 2 and 4 to paragraph (a) of this section and the appropriate values in Table 7 to paragraph (a) of this section.
units.action_summary: For MYs 2017–2025 manufacturers must comply with fleet average fuel economy calculated via Figures 2 and 4 and Table 7.

units.obligation_text: Any reference to a class of light trucks manufactured by a manufacturer shall be deemed to include all light trucks in that class manufactured by persons who control, are controlled by, or are under common control with, such manufacturer;
units.actor: any reference to a class of light trucks (for purposes of compliance/accounting)
units.action_summary: References to a class of light trucks include trucks manufactured by entities under common control with the manufacturer.

units.obligation_text: Any reference to a class of light trucks manufactured by a manufacturer shall be deemed to include only light trucks which qualify as non-passenger vehicles in accordance with 49 CFR 523.5 based upon the production measurements of the vehicles as sold to dealerships;
units.actor: any reference to a class of light trucks (for purposes of compliance/accounting)
units.action_summary: References to a class include only light trucks that qualify as non-passenger vehicles per 49 CFR 523.5 based on production measurements as sold to dealerships.

units.obligation_text: Any reference to a class of light trucks manufactured by a manufacturer shall be deemed to exclude all light trucks in that class manufactured (within the meaning of paragraph (a)(1) of this section) during a model year by such manufacturer which are exported prior to the expiration of 30 days following the end of such model year.
units.actor: any reference to a class of light trucks (for purposes of compliance/accounting)
units.action_summary: References exclude light trucks that are exported within 30 days after the model year ends.

units.obligation_text: The fleet average fuel economy performance of all light trucks that are manufactured by a manufacturer in a model year shall be determined in accordance with procedures established by the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) under 49 U.S.C. 32904 and set forth in 40 CFR part 600.
units.actor: the determination of fleet average fuel economy performance (for manufacturers)
units.action_summary: Fleet average fuel economy for light trucks must be determined following EPA procedures in 40 CFR part 600.

units.obligation_text: For model years 2017 and later, a manufacturer is eligible to increase the fuel economy performance of light trucks in accordance with procedures established by the EPA set forth in 40 CFR part 600, subpart F, including any adjustments to fuel economy the EPA allows, such as for fuel consumption improvements related to air conditioning efficiency, off-cycle technologies, and hybridization and other performance-based technologies for full-size pickup trucks that meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 86.1803.
units.actor: a manufacturer (for model years 2017 and later)
units.action_summary: For MY 2017+, manufacturers may increase light-truck fuel economy using EPA procedures and allowed adjustments (AC efficiency, off-cycle, hybridization for full-size pickups meeting 40 CFR 86.1803).

units.obligation_text: Manufacturers must provide reporting on these technologies as specified in 49 CFR 537.7 by the required deadlines.
units.action_summary: Manufacturers are required to report on these technologies per 49 CFR 537.7 by specified deadlines.

units.obligation_text: A manufacturer that seeks to increase its fleet average fuel economy performance through the use of technologies that improve the efficiency of air conditioning systems must follow the requirements in 40 CFR 86.1868–12.
units.action_summary: Manufacturers using AC-efficiency technologies for light trucks must follow 40 CFR 86.1868–12.

units.obligation_text: Fuel consumption improvement values resulting from the use of those air conditioning systems must be determined in accordance with 40 CFR 600.510–12(c)(3)(i).
units.actor: Manufacturers (or entities determining fuel consumption improvement values)
units.action_summary: Fuel consumption improvements from AC technologies for light trucks must be determined per 40 CFR 600.510–12(c)(3)(i).

units.obligation_text: The eligibility of a manufacturer to increase its fuel economy using hybridized and other performance-based technologies for full-size pickup trucks must follow 40 CFR 86.1870–12 and the fuel consumption improvement of these full-size pickup truck technologies must be determined in accordance with 40 CFR 600.510–12(c)(3)(iii).
units.actor: A manufacturer (seeking incentives for advanced full-size pickups)
units.action_summary: Manufacturers seeking hybridization/performance-based incentives for full-size pickups must follow 40 CFR 86.1870–12 and determine improvements per 40 CFR 600.510–12(c)(3)(iii).

title: Proposed Rule to Implement a Federal Limited Entry Permit in the California/Oregon Large-Mesh Drift Gillnet Fishery

units.obligation_text: A commercial fishing vessel of the United States must be registered for use under a general HMS permit that authorizes the use of specific gear, and a recreational charter vessel must be registered for use under a HMS permit if that vessel is used:
units.actor: a commercial fishing vessel of the United States; a recreational charter vessel
units.action_summary: Vessels must be registered under an appropriate HMS permit to use specified gear or to engage in the listed activities.

units.obligation_text: To fish for HMS in the U.S. EEZ off the States of California, Oregon, and Washington;
units.action_summary: If used to fish for HMS in the specified EEZ off CA, OR, WA, the vessel must be registered under an HMS permit.

units.obligation_text: To land or transship HMS shoreward of the outer boundary of the U.S. EEZ off the States of California, Oregon, and Washington.
units.action_summary: If used to land or transship HMS shoreward of the EEZ boundary off CA, OR, WA, the vessel must be registered under an HMS permit.

units.obligation_text: Only a person eligible to own a documented vessel under the terms of 46 U.S.C. 12102(a) may be issued or may hold (by ownership or otherwise) a general HMS permit.
units.actor: persons seeking issuance or holding of a general HMS permit
units.action_summary: Only persons eligible under 46 U.S.C. 12102(a) are permitted to be issued or hold a general HMS permit.

units.obligation_text: Following publication of the final rule implementing the FMP, NMFS will issue general HMS permits to the owners of those vessels on a list of vessels obtained from owners previously applying for a permit under the authority of the High Seas Fishing Compliance Act, the Tuna Conventions Act of 1950, the Marine Mammal Protection Act, and the Fishery Management Plan for Pelagic Fisheries of the Western Pacific Region, or whose vessels are listed on the vessel register of the Inter-American Tropical Tuna Commission.
units.action_summary: After final rule publication, NMFS will issue general HMS permits to vessel owners identified from specified lists/registries.

units.obligation_text: An owner of a vessel subject to these requirements who has not received a permit under this section from NMFS and who wants to engage in the fisheries must apply to the SFD for the required permit in accordance with the following:
units.action_summary: Owners without a permit who wish to fish must apply to the Sustainable Fisheries Division (SFD) for the required permit according to the listed procedures.

units.obligation_text: A West Coast Region Federal Fisheries application form may be obtained from the SFD or downloaded from the West Coast Region home page ... to apply for a permit under this section. A completed application is one that contains all the necessary information and signatures required.
units.action_summary: Applicants may obtain or download the application form; an application is complete only if it contains all necessary information and signatures.

units.obligation_text: A minimum of 15 days should be allowed for processing a permit application. If an incomplete or improperly completed application is filed, the applicant will be sent a notice of deficiency. If the applicant fails to correct the deficiency within 30 days following the date of notification, the application will be considered abandoned.
units.action_summary: NMFS should allow at least 15 days for processing. NMFS will send a notice of deficiency for incomplete applications, and if the applicant doesn't correct deficiencies within 30 days the application is considered abandoned.

units.obligation_text: A permit will be issued by the SFD. If an application is denied, the SFD will indicate the reasons for denial.
units.action_summary: SFD will issue permits; if denying an application, SFD will state the reasons for denial.

units.obligation_text: Any applicant for an initial permit may appeal the initial issuance decision to the Regional Administrator. To be considered by the Regional Administrator, such appeal must be in writing and state the reasons for the appeal, and must be submitted within 30 days of the action by the Regional Administrator. The appellant may request an informal hearing on the appeal.
units.action_summary: Applicants may appeal initial issuance decisions to the Regional Administrator; appeals must be in writing, state reasons, and be submitted within 30 days; appellant may request an informal hearing.

units.obligation_text: Upon receipt of an appeal authorized by this section, the Regional Administrator will notify the permit applicant, or permit holder as appropriate, and will request such additional information and in such form as will allow action upon the appeal.
units.action_summary: Regional Administrator will notify the applicant/permit holder and may request additional information to act on the appeal.

units.obligation_text: Upon receipt of sufficient information, the Regional Administrator will decide the appeal in accordance with the permit provisions set forth in this section ... The Regional Administrator will notify all interested persons of the decision, and the reasons for the decision, in writing, normally within 30 days of the receipt of sufficient information, unless additional time is needed for a hearing.
units.action_summary: Once sufficient information is received, the Regional Administrator will decide appeals per permit provisions and notify interested persons in writing, normally within 30 days.

units.obligation_text: If a hearing is requested, or if the Regional Administrator determines that one is appropriate, the Regional Administrator may grant an informal hearing before a hearing officer ... after first giving notice of the time, place, and subject matter of the hearing to the applicant. The appellant, and, at the discretion of the hearing officer, other interested persons, may appear personally or be represented by counsel at the hearing and submit information and present arguments as determined appropriate by the hearing officer. Within 30 days of the last day of the hearing, the hearing officer shall recommend in writing a decision to the Regional Administrator.
units.actor: Regional Administrator; appellant; hearing officer; other interested persons
units.action_summary: Regional Administrator may grant an informal hearing after giving notice; appellants and others may appear or be represented and present information; hearing officer must recommend a written decision within 30 days after the hearing.

units.obligation_text: The Regional Administrator may adopt the hearing officer’s recommended decision, in whole or in part, or may reject or modify it. In any event, the Regional Administrator will notify interested persons of the decision, and the reason(s) therefore, in writing, within 30 days of receipt of the hearing officer’s recommended decision. The Regional Administrator’s decision will constitute the final administrative action by NMFS on the matter.
units.action_summary: Regional Administrator may adopt/reject/modify the hearing officer's recommendation and must notify interested persons in writing within 30 days; that decision is final administrative action by NMFS.

units.obligation_text: Any time limit prescribed in this section may be extended for a period not to exceed 30 days by the Regional Administrator for good cause, either upon his or her own motion or upon written request from the appellant stating the reason(s) therefore.
units.action_summary: Regional Administrator may extend any prescribed time limit up to 30 days for good cause, on motion or written request.

units.obligation_text: General HMS permits issued under this subpart will remain valid until the first date of renewal, and permits may be subsequently renewed for 2-year terms.
units.action_summary: Permits remain valid until first renewal date and may be renewed for subsequent 2-year terms.

units.obligation_text: An application for a permit, or renewal of an existing permit under this section will include a fee for each vessel. The fee amount required will be calculated in accordance with the NOAA Finance Handbook and specified on the application form.
units.action_summary: Permit and renewal applications must include a per-vessel fee; fee amount will be calculated per NOAA Finance Handbook and shown on the application.

units.obligation_text: Individuals who target, retain, transship, or land fish captured with a large-mesh DGN must possess a valid Federal limited entry DGN permit. Federal limited entry DGN permits are issued to an individual, and a vessel must be specified on the permit.
units.actor: individuals fishing with large-mesh DGN; permit issuer
units.action_summary: Persons engaging in those activities must have a valid Federal limited entry DGN permit, which is issued to an individual and must specify a vessel.

units.obligation_text: Upon publication of NMFS’ final rule to establish the Federal limited entry DGN permit, all State of California limited entry DGN permit holders are eligible to obtain a Federal limited entry DGN permit.
units.actor: State of California limited entry DGN permit holders
units.action_summary: California state limited entry DGN permit holders are eligible to obtain Federal limited entry DGN permits upon final rule publication.

units.obligation_text: If a 2017–2018 California state DGN permit renewal application is not received by the California Department of Fish and Wildlife or postmarked by March 31, 2018, the permit holder is not eligible to receive a 2018–2019 Federal limited entry DGN permit.
units.action_summary: Permit holders who do not submit or postmark the 2017–2018 renewal by March 31, 2018, are ineligible to receive the 2018–2019 Federal DGN permit.

units.obligation_text: An individual applying for issuance, renewal, transfer, or assignment of a Federal limited entry DGN permit must prove that they meet the qualification requirements by submitting the following documentation, as applicable: A certified copy of the assigned vessel’s documentation as a fishing vessel of the United States ... a copy of a current State of California limited entry DGN permit ... a copy of a written contract reserving or conveying limited entry rights ... and other relevant, credible evidence that the applicant may wish to submit or that the SFD may request or require.
units.actor: individual applying for issuance, renewal, transfer, or assignment
units.action_summary: Applicants must prove qualification by submitting applicable documentation (vessel documentation, state permit, contracts, and other evidence as requested or required by SFD).

units.obligation_text: other relevant, credible evidence that the applicant may wish to submit or that the SFD may request or require.
units.action_summary: SFD may request or require additional evidence; applicants may submit additional relevant evidence.

units.obligation_text: Any processing fee will be determined by the service costs needed to process a permit request. ... A fee may not exceed such costs and is specified with each application form. The appropriate fee must accompany each application.
units.action_summary: Processing fees will be determined by actual service costs and specified on the application; fees may not exceed such costs; applicants must include the appropriate fee with each application.

units.obligation_text: The SFD will make initial decisions regarding issuing, renewing, transferring, and assigning limited entry permits.
units.action_summary: SFD is responsible for making initial decisions on issuing, renewing, transferring, and assigning limited entry permits.

units.obligation_text: Adverse decisions shall be in writing and shall state the reasons for the adverse decision.
units.action_summary: Any adverse decision by SFD must be provided in writing and state the reasons for the decision.

units.obligation_text: The SFD may decline to act on an application for issuing, renewing, transferring, or assigning a limited entry permit and will notify the applicant, if the permit sanction provisions of the Magnuson-Stevens Act at 16 U.S.C. 1858(a) and implementing regulations at 15 CFR part 904, subpart D, apply.
units.action_summary: SFD may decline to act on an application under specified sanction provisions and will notify the applicant if it declines.

units.obligation_text: Federal limited entry DGN permits will be issued by the SFD. If an application is denied, the SFD will indicate the reasons for denial. A DGN permit will be issued to an individual and assigned to a specific vessel. A permit holder may assign the permit to another vessel once per permit year (April 1 to March 31).
units.action_summary: SFD will issue DGN permits to individuals assigned to a specific vessel and will state reasons if denying an application; permit holders may assign their permit to another vessel once per permit year.

units.obligation_text: Any applicant for an initial permit may appeal the initial issuance decision to the Regional Administrator. Appeals will be made and processed following procedures as described at paragraph (b)(3)(iv) of this section.
units.action_summary: Applicants for initial DGN permits may appeal issuance decisions to the Regional Administrator following the appeal procedures in paragraph (b)(3)(iv).

units.obligation_text: Federal limited entry DGN permits may be transferred to another individual only if the current permit holder has held the Federal DGN permit for a minimum of three consecutive years (counted April 1 to March 31 of the following year).
units.action_summary: Permits may be transferred only after the current holder has held the Federal DGN permit for at least three consecutive years.

units.obligation_text: At the time of the establishment of the Federal limited entry DGN permit system, the length of time an individual has held a State of California limited entry DGN permit carries over (e.g., if an individual has held a California DGN permit for two years, they are eligible to transfer the Federal DGN permit after holding the Federal DGN permit for one year).
units.actor: state permit holders transitioning to Federal system
units.action_summary: Time held under a California state DGN permit counts toward the Federal three-year transfer eligibility requirement.

units.obligation_text: The permit holder suffers from a serious illness or permanent disability that prevents the permit holder from earning a livelihood from commercial fishing.
units.action_summary: Serious illness or permanent disability that prevents earning a livelihood is an exception to the transfer time limitation.

units.obligation_text: If a deceased permit holder’s estate or heirs submit a transfer request within six months of the permit holder’s death.
units.actor: estate or heirs of deceased permit holder
units.action_summary: Transfer limitation may be excepted if the deceased permit holder's estate or heirs submit a transfer request within six months of death.

units.obligation_text: Upon dissolution of marriage if the permit is held as community property.
units.actor: permit holder(s) upon dissolution of marriage
units.action_summary: Dissolution of marriage where permit is community property is an exception to the transfer time limitation.

units.obligation_text: The SFD will send notices to renew limited entry permits to the most recent address of the permit holder on file.
units.action_summary: SFD will send renewal notices to the permit holder's most recent address on file.

units.obligation_text: The permit owner is responsible for renewing a limited entry permit.
units.action_summary: Permit owners are responsible for renewing their permits.

units.obligation_text: The deadline for receipt or postmark of a Federal DGN permit renewal application is April 30 of the permit year ... Federal DGN permits must be renewed yearly.
units.action_summary: Renewal applications must be received or postmarked by April 30 each permit year; permits must be renewed annually.

units.obligation_text: A DGN permit that is allowed to expire will not be renewed unless the permit owner requests reissuance by July 31 ... and NMFS determines that failure to renew was proximately caused by illness, injury, or death of the permit owner. If the permit expires, it will be forfeited and NMFS will not reissue the permit to anyone.
units.action_summary: Expired permits won't be renewed unless the owner requests reissuance by July 31 and NMFS finds proximate cause (illness/injury/death); expired permits will be forfeited and NMFS will not reissue them.
units.modal_raw: will not; must request; will be forfeited

units.obligation_text: Except as provided in paragraphs (ii) through (v), the DGN permit holder must be on-board the vessel and in possession of a valid Federal limited entry DGN permit when engaged in DGN fishing activity.
units.action_summary: Permit holder must be physically on-board the vessel and have the permit in their possession during DGN fishing, except as specified in (ii)-(v).

units.obligation_text: A permit holder may designate another individual to fish under their permit for up to 15 days per fishing year (April 1 to March 31 of the following year); the substitute must comply with all other Federal permitting requirements. A permit holder shall notify NMFS of a substitution at least 24 hours prior to the commencement of the trip.
units.action_summary: Permit holders may designate a substitute to fish under the permit for up to 15 days per year; the substitute must comply with all federal permitting requirements; permit holder must notify NMFS at least 24 hours before the trip.

units.obligation_text: If the person who owns a Federal DGN permit is prevented from being on-board a fishing vessel because the person died, is ill, or is injured, NMFS may allow an exemption to the owner on-board requirement for more than 15 days. The person requesting the exemption must send a letter to NMFS requesting an exemption from the owner on-board requirements, with appropriate evidence as described at paragraph (f)(10)(iv) or (v) of this section. All exemptions for death, injury, or illness will be evaluated by NMFS and a decision will be made in writing to the permit owner ... within 60 calendar days of receipt of the original exemption request.
units.action_summary: NMFS may grant exemptions to owner-on-board requirement for >15 days for death/illness/injury; the requester must submit a letter with evidence per (iv)/(v); NMFS will evaluate and provide a written decision within 60 days of receipt.

units.obligation_text: Evidence of death of the permit owner shall be provided to NMFS in the form of a copy of a death certificate. In the interim before the estate is settled ... the estate of the deceased permit owner may send a letter to NMFS with a copy of the death certificate, requesting an exemption from the owner-on-board requirements. An exemption due to death of the permit owner will be effective only until such time that the estate ... has registered the deceased permit owner’s permit to a beneficiary, transferred the permit to another owner, or three years after the date of death as proven by a death certificate, whichever is earliest. An exemption from the owner-on-board requirement will be conveyed in a letter from NMFS to the estate of the permit owner and is required to be on the vessel during DGN fishing operations.
units.actor: estate of deceased permit owner; NMFS
units.action_summary: Death must be evidenced by a death certificate to NMFS; the estate may request an exemption with the certificate; such exemption lasts until estate registers/transfers permit or three years after death (whichever earliest); NMFS will convey the exemption in writing, and that letter must be on the vessel during operations.
units.modal_raw: shall; may; will; is required to

units.obligation_text: Evidence of illness or injury that prevents the permit owner from participating in the fishery shall be provided to NMFS in the form of a letter from a certified medical practitioner. This letter must detail the relevant medical conditions of the permit owner and how those conditions prevent the permit owner from being on-board a fishing vessel during DGN fishing. An exemption due to injury or illness will be effective only for the fishing year of the request for exemption. In order to extend a medical exemption for a succeeding year, the permit owner must submit a new request and provide documentation from a certified medical practitioner detailing why the permit owner is still unable to be on-board a fishing vessel. An exemption from the owner-on-board requirement will be conveyed in a letter from NMFS to the permit owner and is required to be on the vessel during DGN fishing operations.
units.actor: permit owner; certified medical practitioner; NMFS
units.action_summary: Illness/injury must be evidenced by a medical practitioner's letter detailing conditions and impact; such exemptions apply only for the fishing year and to extend require a new request with documentation; NMFS will convey exemption in writing and that letter must be on the vessel during operations.

title: Fisheries off West Coast States: Highly Migratory Fisheries; Amendment 5 to the Highly Migratory Species Fishery Management Plan; California Drift Gillnet Fishery; Implementation of a Federal Limited Entry Drift Gillnet Permit

units.obligation_text: Comments on Amendment 5 must be received by November 14, 2017.
units.action_summary: Public comments on Amendment 5 must be submitted by November 14, 2017.

units.obligation_text: Comments must be submitted by one of the above methods to ensure they are received, documented, and considered by NMFS.
units.action_summary: Comments must be submitted via the specified methods (e.g., regulations.gov or mail) so NMFS will receive and consider them.

units.obligation_text: Do not submit confidential business information, or otherwise sensitive or protected information.
units.action_summary: Commenters are prohibited from submitting confidential business information or other sensitive/protected information through the public comment channels.

units.obligation_text: NMFS will accept anonymous comments (enter "N/A" in the required fields if you wish to remain anonymous).
units.action_summary: NMFS permits commenters to submit comments anonymously by entering 'N/A' in required fields.

units.obligation_text: All comments received are a part of the public record and will generally be posted for public viewing on www.regulations.gov without change.
units.action_summary: NMFS will include all received comments in the public record and generally post them on regulations.gov unchanged.

units.obligation_text: In order to participate in the DGN fishery, current participants must possess a State of California LE DGN permit, a California commercial fishing license, a California general gill/trammel net permit, and a California swordfish permit.
units.actor: current participants in the DGN fishery
units.action_summary: To participate in the DGN fishery, fishers must hold four specified California permits/licenses.

units.obligation_text: The vessel that the participant fishes from must have a federal Pacific Highly Migratory Species (HMS) permit with a DGN gear endorsement.
units.action_summary: The fishing vessel must hold a federal Pacific HMS permit with a DGN gear endorsement.

units.obligation_text: Possession of a current and up-to-date State of California LE DGN permit is the only permit required to initially obtain a federal LE DGN permit.
units.actor: applicants for a federal LE DGN permit
units.action_summary: To initially obtain a federal LE DGN permit, an applicant must possess a current California LE DGN permit (no other permit required for initial issuance).

units.obligation_text: After the LE DGN permit transitions from the State of California to federal management, each participant will need to hold all the same permits and licenses, except that the federal LE DGN permit will take place of the State of California LE DGN permit.
units.action_summary: Once the permit program transitions, participants must continue to hold the same permits/licenses, with the federal LE DGN permit replacing the State LE DGN permit.

units.obligation_text: NMFS would adopt current California requirements regarding the assignment of a permit (i.e., issued to an individual and assigned to a specific vessel), the transfer of permits between permittees..., and an annual renewal cycle.
units.action_summary: NMFS intends to adopt California's permit assignment, transfer, and annual renewal rules into the federal program.

units.obligation_text: A permit must be held for three years before it is eligible to be transferred.
units.action_summary: Permit holders must hold a permit for at least three years before transferring it.

units.obligation_text: Permit assignment: issued to an individual and assigned to a specific vessel.
units.action_summary: Permits are to be issued to individuals and assigned to a specific vessel.

units.obligation_text: Upon the date of publication of the final rule to implement Amendment 5, all 70 state-eligible permit holders would be eligible to receive a federal DGN permit if they have renewed their state DGN permit by March 31, 2018.
units.action_summary: State-eligible permit holders will be eligible to receive a federal DGN permit provided they renewed their state permit by March 31, 2018.

units.obligation_text: Permit holders who fail to renew their state DGN permit by March 31, 2018, will not be eligible for a federal DGN permit.
units.action_summary: Failure to renew by March 31, 2018 makes a permit holder ineligible for a federal DGN permit.

units.obligation_text: If a state LE DGN permit is transferred after publication of the proposed rule to implement Amendment 5, the transferee, but not the transferor, would be eligible to receive a federal LE DGN permit upon publication of the final rule.
units.action_summary: If a state permit is transferred after the proposed rule publication, the transferee (not the transferor) is eligible to receive a federal LE DGN permit when the final rule publishes.
units.modal_raw: would be eligible / would not be

units.obligation_text: Federal LE DGN permits would be issued annually for the fishing year starting April 1 and ending March 31 of the following year.
units.action_summary: NMFS will issue federal LE DGN permits annually for the April 1–March 31 fishing year.

units.obligation_text: Permits would expire on March 31 of each year.
units.action_summary: Federal LE DGN permits expire annually on March 31.

units.obligation_text: After initial issuance (expected in 2018), the permit renewal deadline would be April 30 of the fishing year.
units.action_summary: Following initial issuance, permit renewals are due by April 30 of the fishing year.

units.obligation_text: A completed DGN permit renewal form must be received by NMFS no later than close-of-business April 30.
units.action_summary: Permit owners must ensure NMFS receives a completed DGN renewal form by close-of-business April 30.

units.obligation_text: Any renewal form received after that date would result in the permanent expiration of the Federal DGN permit.
units.action_summary: If NMFS receives a renewal form after April 30, the permit will permanently expire.

units.obligation_text: A permit owner who fails to submit a renewal by the deadline may submit a renewal form to NMFS with a written statement that the failure to renew the permit by the deadline was proximately caused by the permit owner's illness or injury.
units.action_summary: A permit owner who missed the renewal deadline due to illness or injury may submit a late renewal with a written explanatory statement.

units.obligation_text: When a permit owner has died, the owner's estate or other personal representative may submit a statement explaining that the permit owner's death has prevented a timely renewal.
units.action_summary: If the permit owner died, the estate or representative may submit a statement that death prevented timely renewal.

units.obligation_text: The permit holder, or in the case of a deceased permit owner, the estate or other personal representative, will need to provide written proof of illness, injury or death.
units.actor: permit holder / estate or personal representative
units.action_summary: A late-renewal requester must provide written proof of illness, injury, or death to support the late renewal justification.

units.obligation_text: NMFS will not consider any such renewal request made after July 31.
units.action_summary: NMFS will not consider late renewal requests received after July 31.

units.obligation_text: If the permit expires, it would permanently expire and NMFS would not reissue the permit.
units.action_summary: Permits that expire will be permanently expired and NMFS will not reissue them.
units.modal_raw: would permanently expire / would not reissue

units.obligation_text: A permittee would need to hold a federal LE DGN permit for three or more years before it would be eligible to be transferred.
units.action_summary: Permit holders must hold a federal LE DGN permit for at least three years before transferring it.

units.obligation_text: This vesting period would extend across both state and federal permit programs (i.e., if a permit holder held a state LE DGN permit for two years and a federal LE DGN permit for one year, the permit may be transferred).
units.action_summary: The three-year holding requirement counts combined years across state and federal permits; transfers are permitted once the combined three years are met.

title: Fisheries Off West Coast States: Highly Migratory Fisheries; California Drift Gillnet Fishery; Implementation of a Federal Limited Entry Drift Gillnet Permit

units.obligation_text: A commercial fishing vessel of the United States must be registered for use under a general HMS permit that authorizes the use of specific gear, and a recreational charter vessel must be registered for use under a HMS permit if that vessel is used: (i) To fish for HMS in the U.S. EEZ off the States of California, Oregon, and Washington; or (ii) To land or transship HMS shoreward of the outer boundary of the U.S. EEZ off the States of California, Oregon, and Washington.
units.actor: commercial fishing vessel owners/operators; recreational charter vessel owners/operators
units.action_summary: Vessels (commercial and recreational charter) used to fish for, land, or transship HMS in the specified West Coast areas must be registered under an appropriate general HMS permit.

units.obligation_text: Only a person eligible to own a documented vessel under the terms of 46 U.S.C. 12102(a) may be issued or may hold (by ownership or otherwise) a general HMS permit.
units.actor: person eligible to own a documented vessel under 46 U.S.C. 12102(a)
units.action_summary: Only persons meeting the cited eligibility to own a documented vessel may be issued or hold a general HMS permit.

units.obligation_text: Following publication of the final rule implementing the FMP, NMFS will issue general HMS permits to the owners of those vessels on a list of vessels obtained from owners previously applying for a permit under the authority of the High Seas Fishing Compliance Act, the Tuna Conventions Act of 1950, the Marine Mammal Protection Act, and the Fishery Management Plan for Pelagic Fisheries of the Western Pacific Region, or whose vessels are listed on the vessel register of the Inter-American Tropical Tuna Commission.
units.action_summary: After the final rule, NMFS will issue general HMS permits to listed vessel owners from specified sources/lists.

units.obligation_text: A West Coast Region Federal Fisheries application form may be obtained from the SFD or downloaded from the West Coast Region home page ... to apply for a permit under this section.
units.action_summary: Applicants may obtain or download the West Coast Region Federal Fisheries application form from SFD or the region's homepage.

units.obligation_text: A minimum of 15 days should be allowed for processing a permit application.
units.action_summary: Permit processors should allow at least 15 days to process a permit application.

units.obligation_text: If an incomplete or improperly completed application is filed, the applicant will be sent a notice of deficiency.
units.action_summary: SFD will send a notice of deficiency to applicants who file incomplete or improperly completed applications.

units.obligation_text: If the applicant fails to correct the deficiency within 30 days following the date of notification, the application will be considered abandoned.
units.action_summary: If applicants do not correct deficiencies within 30 days of notice, SFD will consider the application abandoned.

units.obligation_text: A permit will be issued by the SFD.
units.action_summary: SFD will issue permits when appropriate.

units.obligation_text: If an application is denied, the SFD will indicate the reasons for denial.
units.action_summary: SFD must provide reasons in writing when denying an application.

units.obligation_text: Any applicant for an initial permit may appeal the initial issuance decision to the Regional Administrator.
units.action_summary: Applicants may appeal initial permit issuance decisions to the Regional Administrator.

units.obligation_text: To be considered by the Regional Administrator, such appeal must be in writing and state the reasons for the appeal, and must be submitted within 30 days of the action by the Regional Administrator.
units.action_summary: To be considered, appeals must be written, state reasons, and be submitted within 30 days of the Regional Administrator's action.

units.obligation_text: The appellant may request an informal hearing on the appeal.
units.action_summary: Appellants may request an informal hearing on their appeal.

units.obligation_text: Upon receipt of an appeal authorized by this section, the Regional Administrator will notify the permit applicant, or permit holder as appropriate, and will request such additional information and in such form as will allow action upon the appeal.
units.action_summary: The Regional Administrator will notify affected parties and may request additional information needed to act on the appeal.

units.obligation_text: Upon receipt of sufficient information, the Regional Administrator will decide the appeal ... and will notify all interested persons of the decision, and the reasons for the decision, in writing, normally within 30 days of the receipt of sufficient information, unless additional time is needed for a hearing.
units.action_summary: Regional Administrator will decide appeals after sufficient information and notify interested persons in writing of the decision and reasons, normally within 30 days.

units.obligation_text: The Regional Administrator may grant an informal hearing before a hearing officer designated for that purpose after first giving notice of the time, place, and subject matter of the hearing to the applicant.
units.action_summary: Regional Administrator may grant an informal hearing but must first give notice of its time, place, and subject matter to the applicant.

units.obligation_text: The appellant, and, at the discretion of the hearing officer, other interested persons, may appear personally or be represented by counsel at the hearing and submit information and present arguments as determined appropriate by the hearing officer.
units.action_summary: Appellants and possibly other interested persons may appear or be represented and submit information and arguments at hearings as allowed by the hearing officer.

units.obligation_text: Within 30 days of the last day of the hearing, the hearing officer shall recommend in writing a decision to the Regional Administrator.
units.action_summary: Hearing officer must provide a written recommended decision to the Regional Administrator within 30 days after the hearing ends.

units.obligation_text: The Regional Administrator may adopt the hearing officer's recommended decision, in whole or in part, or may reject or modify it. In any event, the Regional Administrator will notify interested persons of the decision, and the reason(s) therefore, in writing, within 30 days of receipt of the hearing officer's recommended decision. The Regional Administrator's decision will constitute the final administrative action by NMFS on the matter.
units.action_summary: Regional Administrator may adopt, modify, or reject the hearing officer's recommendation, but must notify interested persons in writing within 30 days and that decision is final administrative action.

units.obligation_text: Any time limit prescribed in this section may be extended for a period not to exceed 30 days by the Regional Administrator for good cause, either upon his or her own motion or upon written request from the appellant stating the reason(s) therefore.
units.action_summary: Regional Administrator may extend prescribed time limits up to 30 days for good cause, on own motion or upon written appellant request.

units.obligation_text: General HMS permits issued under this subpart will remain valid until the first date of renewal, and permits may be subsequently renewed for 2-year terms.
units.action_summary: Permits remain valid until first renewal and may be renewed thereafter for two-year terms.

units.obligation_text: An application for a permit, or renewal of an existing permit under this section will include a fee for each vessel.
units.action_summary: Permit applications and renewals must include a fee for each vessel.

units.obligation_text: The fee amount required will be calculated in accordance with the NOAA Finance Handbook and specified on the application form.
units.action_summary: NOAA/NMFS will calculate required fee amounts per NOAA Finance Handbook and specify them on the application form.

units.obligation_text: Individuals who target, retain, transship, or land fish captured with a large-mesh DGN must possess a valid Federal limited entry DGN permit.
units.action_summary: Persons engaging in DGN fishing activities with large-mesh gear must have a valid Federal limited entry DGN permit.

units.obligation_text: Federal limited entry DGN permits are issued to an individual, and a vessel must be specified on the permit.
units.action_summary: DGN permits are issued to individuals and must list a specific vessel on the permit.

units.obligation_text: Upon publication of NMFS' final rule to establish the Federal limited entry DGN permit, all State of California limited entry DGN permit holders are eligible to obtain a Federal limited entry DGN permit.
units.actor: State of California limited entry DGN permit holders
units.action_summary: California state limited entry DGN permit holders are eligible to obtain the Federal limited entry DGN permit upon final rule publication.

units.obligation_text: If a 2017-2018 California state DGN permit renewal application is not received by the California Department of Fish and Wildlife or postmarked by March 31, 2018, the permit holder is not eligible to receive a 2018-2019 Federal limited entry DGN permit.
units.action_summary: Failure to renew or have renewal postmarked by March 31, 2018, makes the holder ineligible for the 2018-2019 Federal DGN permit.

units.obligation_text: An individual applying for issuance, renewal, transfer, or assignment of a Federal limited entry DGN permit must prove that they meet the qualification requirements by submitting the following documentation, as applicable: A certified copy of the assigned vessel's documentation ...; a copy of a current State of California limited entry DGN permit ...; a copy of a written contract reserving or conveying limited entry rights ...; and other relevant, credible evidence that the applicant may wish to submit or that the SFD may request or require.
units.action_summary: Applicants for issuance, renewal, transfer, or assignment must prove qualifications by submitting specified documentation and any other requested evidence.

units.obligation_text: A certified copy of the assigned vessel's documentation as a fishing vessel of the United States (U.S. Coast Guard or state) is the best evidence of vessel identification.
units.action_summary: Applicants should provide a certified copy of the vessel's U.S. documentation as primary evidence of vessel identification.

units.obligation_text: A copy of a current State of California limited entry DGN permit is the best evidence of initial qualification for a Federal limited entry DGN permit.
units.action_summary: Applicants should provide a copy of their current California limited entry DGN permit as best evidence of initial qualification.

units.obligation_text: A copy of a written contract reserving or conveying limited entry rights is the best evidence of reserved or acquired rights.
units.action_summary: Applicants should provide a written contract as best evidence of reserved or acquired limited entry rights.

units.obligation_text: Any processing fee will be determined by the service costs needed to process a permit request.
units.action_summary: Processing fees, if any, will be set based on administrative service costs to process a permit request.

units.obligation_text: A fee may not exceed such costs and is specified with each application form.
units.action_summary: Processing fees cannot exceed the actual administrative costs and will be specified on application forms.

units.obligation_text: The appropriate fee must accompany each application.
units.action_summary: Applicants must include the required fee with each permit application.

units.obligation_text: The SFD will make initial decisions regarding issuing, renewing, transferring, and assigning limited entry permits.
units.action_summary: SFD is responsible for making initial decisions on issuance, renewal, transfer, and assignment of limited entry permits.

units.obligation_text: Adverse decisions shall be in writing and shall state the reasons for the adverse decision.
units.action_summary: If SFD issues an adverse decision, it must be in writing and must state the reasons.

units.obligation_text: The SFD may decline to act on an application for issuing, renewing, transferring, or assigning a limited entry permit and will notify the applicant, if the permit sanction provisions of the Magnuson-Stevens Act ... apply.
units.action_summary: SFD may decline to act on applications when sanction provisions apply and will notify the applicant if it does so.

units.obligation_text: Federal limited entry DGN permits will be issued by the SFD. If an application is denied, the SFD will indicate the reasons for denial.
units.action_summary: SFD will issue Federal DGN permits and must state reasons when denying applications.

units.obligation_text: A DGN permit will be issued to an individual and assigned to a specific vessel.
units.action_summary: DGN permits are issued to individuals and are assigned to a specified vessel.

units.obligation_text: A permit holder may assign the permit to another vessel once per permit year (April 1 to March 31).
units.action_summary: Permit holders are permitted to assign their permit to a different vessel one time per permit year.

units.obligation_text: Any applicant for an initial permit may appeal the initial issuance decision to the Regional Administrator. Appeals will be made and processed following procedures as described at paragraph (b)(3)(iv) of this section.
units.action_summary: Initial permit applicants may appeal issuance decisions to the Regional Administrator following the established appeal procedures.

units.obligation_text: Federal limited entry DGN permits may be transferred to another individual only if the current permit holder has held the Federal DGN permit for a minimum of three consecutive years (counted April 1 to March 31 of the following year).
units.action_summary: Permits can be transferred to another individual only after the current holder has possessed the Federal DGN permit for at least three consecutive years.

units.obligation_text: At the time of the establishment of the Federal limited entry DGN permit system, the length of time an individual has held a State of California limited entry DGN permit carries over ...
units.action_summary: Previously held years of a California state DGN permit count toward the Federal permit transfer eligibility period.

units.obligation_text: Exceptions to this limitation on permit transfer may be made if the permit holder suffers from a serious illness or permanent disability that prevents the permit holder from earning a livelihood from commercial fishing.
units.action_summary: SFD/NMFS may allow transfer exceptions if the permit holder has a serious illness or permanent disability preventing fishing livelihood.

units.obligation_text: Exceptions to this limitation on permit transfer may be made if a deceased permit holder's estate or heirs submit a transfer request within six months of the permit holder's death.
units.action_summary: Transfer exceptions may be granted if the deceased holder's estate or heirs request transfer within six months of death.

units.obligation_text: Exceptions to this limitation on permit transfer may be made upon dissolution of marriage if the permit is held as community property.
units.action_summary: An exception to transfer limitations may be made upon dissolution of marriage when the permit is community property.

units.obligation_text: The SFD will send notices to renew limited entry permits to the most recent address of the permit holder on file.
units.action_summary: SFD will mail renewal notices to the permit holder's most recent address on file.

units.obligation_text: The permit owner is responsible for renewing a limited entry permit.
units.action_summary: Permit owners are responsible for renewing their limited entry permits.

units.obligation_text: The deadline for receipt or postmark of a Federal DGN permit renewal application is April 30 of the permit year ... Federal DGN permits must be renewed yearly.
units.action_summary: Renewal applications must be received or postmarked by April 30 and permits must be renewed annually.

units.obligation_text: A DGN permit that is allowed to expire will not be renewed unless the permit owner requests reissuance by July 31 ... and NMFS determines that failure to renew was proximately caused by illness, injury, or death of the permit owner.
units.action_summary: Expired permits won't be renewed except if the owner requests reissuance by July 31 and NMFS finds failure to renew was due to illness, injury, or death.

units.obligation_text: If the permit expires, it will be forfeited and NMFS will not reissue the permit to anyone.
units.action_summary: Expired permits are forfeited and NMFS will not reissue them.

units.obligation_text: Except as provided in paragraphs (ii) through (v), the DGN permit holder must be on-board the vessel and in possession of a valid Federal limited entry DGN permit when engaged in DGN fishing activity.
units.action_summary: Permit holders must be on-board and have the permit in their possession during DGN fishing, except as otherwise provided.

units.obligation_text: A permit holder may designate another individual to fish under their permit for up to 15 days per fishing year (April 1 to March 31 of the following year); the substitute must comply with all other Federal permitting requirements.
units.action_summary: Permit holders may designate a substitute fisher for up to 15 days per year; the substitute must comply with all federal permitting requirements.

units.obligation_text: A permit holder shall notify NMFS of a substitution at least 24 hours prior to the commencement of the trip.
units.action_summary: Permit holders must notify NMFS at least 24 hours before a trip when designating a substitute to fish under their permit.

units.obligation_text: If the person who owns a Federal DGN permit is prevented from being on-board ... NMFS may allow an exemption to the owner on-board requirement for more than 15 days.
units.action_summary: NMFS may grant exemptions to the owner-on-board requirement for periods longer than 15 days when the owner is prevented from being on-board due to death, illness, or injury.

units.obligation_text: The person requesting the exemption must send a letter to NMFS requesting an exemption from the owner on-board requirements, with appropriate evidence as described at paragraph (f)(10)(iv) or (v) of this section.
units.actor: person requesting the exemption (permit owner or estate/heirs)
units.action_summary: To obtain an owner-on-board exemption, the requester must send a letter to NMFS with appropriate supporting evidence.

units.obligation_text: All exemptions for death, injury, or illness will be evaluated by NMFS and a decision will be made in writing to the permit owner ... within 60 calendar days of receipt of the original exemption request.
units.action_summary: NMFS will evaluate exemption requests for death, injury, or illness and must issue a written decision within 60 days of receipt.

units.obligation_text: Evidence of death of the permit owner shall be provided to NMFS in the form of a copy of a death certificate.
units.actor: estate of the deceased permit owner or other requester
units.action_summary: Requesters must provide a death certificate as evidence when requesting an exemption based on the permit owner's death.

units.obligation_text: An exemption due to death of the permit owner will be effective only until such time that the estate of the deceased permit owner has registered the deceased permit owner's permit to a beneficiary, transferred the permit to another owner, or three years after the date of death as proven by a death certificate, whichever is earliest.
units.action_summary: Death-based exemptions last only until the estate registers/transfers the permit or three years after death, whichever comes first.

units.obligation_text: An exemption from the owner-on-board requirement will be conveyed in a letter from NMFS to the estate of the permit owner and is required to be on the vessel during DGN fishing operations.
units.action_summary: NMFS will issue exemption letters to estates/owners, and the exemption letter must be carried on the vessel during DGN operations.

units.obligation_text: Evidence of illness or injury that prevents the permit owner from participating in the fishery shall be provided to NMFS in the form of a letter from a certified medical practitioner.
units.action_summary: Requesters must provide a medical practitioner's letter documenting illness or injury when requesting an exemption.

units.obligation_text: This letter must detail the relevant medical conditions of the permit owner and how those conditions prevent the permit owner from being on-board a fishing vessel during DGN fishing.
units.actor: certified medical practitioner (preparing letter) / permit owner (submitting)
units.action_summary: Medical letters must describe the medical conditions and explain why the permit owner cannot be on-board during DGN fishing.

units.obligation_text: An exemption due to injury or illness will be effective only for the fishing year of the request for exemption. In order to extend a medical exemption for a succeeding year, the permit owner must submit a new request and provide documentation from a certified medical practitioner detailing why the permit owner is still unable to be on-board a fishing vessel.
units.actor: permit owner; certified medical practitioner; NMFS (granting)
units.action_summary: Medical exemptions apply only for the fishing year; to extend, owners must reapply with updated medical documentation for further consideration by NMFS.

units.obligation_text: An exemption from the owner-on-board requirement will be conveyed in a letter from NMFS to the permit owner and is required to be on the vessel during DGN fishing operations.
units.action_summary: NMFS will issue exemption letters to permit owners for illness/injury-based exemptions, and the exemption letter must be carried on the vessel during DGN operations.
