title: Revising the Beryllium Standard for General Industry

units.obligation_text: The employer must use engineering and work practice controls to reduce and maintain employee airborne exposure to beryllium to or below the PEL and STEL, unless the employer can demonstrate that such controls are not feasible. Wherever the employer demonstrates that it is not feasible to reduce airborne exposure to or below the PELs with engineering and work practice controls, the employer must implement and maintain engineering and work practice controls to reduce airborne exposure to the lowest levels feasible and supplement these controls using respiratory protection in accordance with paragraph (g) of this standard.
units.action_summary: Use engineering and work practice controls to reduce and maintain employee airborne beryllium exposure at or below the PEL and STEL, or if not feasible, reduce exposures to the lowest feasible levels and supplement with respiratory protection per paragraph (g).

units.obligation_text: For each operation in a beryllium work area that releases airborne beryllium, the employer must ensure that at least one of the following is in place to reduce airborne exposure:
units.action_summary: Ensure at least one listed control is in place for each operation that releases airborne beryllium.

units.obligation_text: (A) Material and/or process substitution;
units.action_summary: Use material or process substitution to reduce airborne beryllium exposure.

units.obligation_text: (B) Isolation, such as ventilated partial or full enclosures;
units.action_summary: Use isolation (e.g., ventilated enclosures) to reduce airborne exposure.

units.obligation_text: (C) Local exhaust ventilation, such as at the points of operation, material handling, and transfer; or
units.action_summary: Use local exhaust ventilation at points of operation, handling, and transfer to reduce exposures.

units.obligation_text: (D) Process control, such as wet methods and automation.
units.action_summary: Use process controls (e.g., wet methods, automation) to reduce airborne beryllium exposure.

units.obligation_text: An employer is exempt from using the controls listed in paragraph (f)(2)(ii) of this standard to the extent that:
units.action_summary: Provides exemptions from the controls in (f)(2)(ii) under specified conditions.

units.obligation_text: (A) The employer can establish that such controls are not feasible; or
units.action_summary: Employer may be exempt if it can establish that the listed controls are not feasible.

units.obligation_text: (B) The employer can demonstrate that airborne exposure is below the action level, using no fewer than two representative personal breathing zone samples taken at least 7 days apart, for each affected operation.
units.action_summary: Employer may be exempt if it demonstrates exposures are below the action level using at least two representative personal breathing zone samples taken ≥7 days apart per operation.

units.obligation_text: The employer must ensure that beryllium is not removed from beryllium-contaminated personal protective clothing and equipment by blowing, shaking, or any other means that disperses beryllium into the air.
units.action_summary: Employer must prevent removal of beryllium from contaminated PPE/equipment by blowing, shaking, or any method that disperses beryllium into the air.

units.obligation_text: Beryllium-contaminated surfaces in eating and drinking areas are as free as practicable of beryllium;
units.action_summary: Ensure eating and drinking area surfaces are as free as practicable of beryllium contamination.

units.obligation_text: No employees enter any eating or drinking area with beryllium-contaminated personal protective clothing or equipment unless, prior to entry, surface beryllium has been removed from the clothing or equipment by methods that do not disperse beryllium into the air or onto an employee’s body;
units.action_summary: Employees are prohibited from entering eating/drinking areas wearing beryllium-contaminated PPE/equipment unless surface beryllium was removed beforehand by methods that do not disperse beryllium into the air or onto a person's body.

units.obligation_text: unless, prior to entry, surface beryllium has been removed from the clothing or equipment by methods that do not disperse beryllium into the air or onto an employee’s body;
units.action_summary: Exception allowing entry only if surface beryllium has been removed beforehand by non-dispersive methods.

units.obligation_text: The employer must maintain all surfaces in beryllium work areas and regulated areas as free as practicable of beryllium and in accordance with the written exposure control plan required under paragraph (f)(1) and the cleaning methods required under paragraph (j)(2) of this standard;
units.action_summary: Maintain surfaces in beryllium work and regulated areas as free as practicable of beryllium, following the written exposure control plan and required cleaning methods.

units.obligation_text: The employer must ensure that surfaces in beryllium work areas and regulated areas are cleaned by HEPA-filtered vacuuming or other methods that minimize the likelihood and level of airborne exposure.
units.action_summary: Ensure surfaces are cleaned by HEPA-filtered vacuuming or other methods that minimize airborne exposure.

units.obligation_text: The employer must not allow dry sweeping or brushing for cleaning surfaces in beryllium work areas or regulated areas unless HEPA-filtered vacuuming or other methods that minimize the likelihood and level of airborne exposure are not safe or effective.

units.obligation_text: For materials that contain beryllium in concentrations of 0.1 percent by weight or more or are contaminated with beryllium, the employer must ensure that:
units.action_summary: For materials containing or contaminated with ≥0.1% beryllium, ensure specified disposal and recycling requirements are met.

units.obligation_text: (i) Materials designated for disposal are disposed of in sealed, impermeable enclosures, such as bags or containers, that are labeled in accordance with paragraph (m)(3) of this standard;
units.action_summary: Ensure materials for disposal are placed in sealed, impermeable, labeled enclosures.

units.obligation_text: (ii) Materials designated for recycling are cleaned to be as free as practicable of surface beryllium contamination and labeled in accordance with paragraph (m)(3) of this standard, or place in sealed, impermeable enclosures, such as bags or containers, that are labeled in accordance with paragraph (m)(3) of this standard.
units.action_summary: Ensure materials for recycling are either cleaned to be as free as practicable of surface beryllium and labeled, or placed in sealed, impermeable labeled enclosures.

units.section: Definition of CBD diagnostic center (§ 1910 (b) proposed)
units.obligation_text: A CBD diagnostic center must have a pulmonologist or pulmonary specialist on staff and on-site facilities to perform a clinical evaluation for the presence of CBD; must have capacity to perform pulmonary function testing, bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL), and transbronchial biopsy; must have capacity to transfer BAL samples to a laboratory for appropriate diagnostic testing within 24 hours; and the pulmonologist or pulmonary specialist must be able to interpret the biopsy pathology and the BAL diagnostic test results
units.action_summary: To qualify as a CBD diagnostic center, the facility must have specified specialist staffing, testing capabilities, sample transfer capacity within 24 hours, and specialist interpretation ability.

units.obligation_text: An employee is 'confirmed positive' if the person tested has had two abnormal BeLPT test results, an abnormal and a borderline test result, or three borderline test results obtained within the 30 day follow-up test period required after a first abnormal or borderline BeLPT test result, or the result of a more reliable and accurate test indicating beryllium sensitization
units.action_summary: Confirmed positive is defined by specific combinations of BeLPT results obtained within a 30-day follow-up period or by a more reliable test.

units.obligation_text: An employee must be offered a follow-up BeLPT within 30 days if the initial test result is anything other than normal, unless the employee has been confirmed positive
units.action_summary: If an initial BeLPT is abnormal or borderline, the employee must be offered follow-up testing within 30 days unless already confirmed positive.

units.obligation_text: Handling beryllium materials in non-particulate solid form that are free from visible dust containing beryllium in concentrations ≥ 0.1 percent by weight is not considered dermal contact with beryllium under the standard
units.action_summary: Contact with non-particulate solid beryllium materials free of visible dust ≥0.1% is excluded from the definition of dermal contact.

units.obligation_text: Dermal contact with beryllium is skin exposure to soluble beryllium compounds, beryllium solutions, or visible dust, fumes, or mists containing beryllium in concentrations ≥ 0.1 percent by weight
units.action_summary: The definition of dermal contact covers skin exposure to specified beryllium-containing forms including visible particulates at ≥0.1% concentration.

units.obligation_text: The employer must use engineering and work practice controls to reduce and maintain employee airborne exposure to beryllium to or below the TWA PEL and STEL, unless the employer can demonstrate that such controls are not feasible.
units.action_summary: Use engineering and work practice controls to keep employee beryllium exposure at or below the TWA PEL and STEL, unless infeasible.

units.obligation_text: Wherever the employer demonstrates that it is not feasible to reduce airborne exposure to or below the PELs with engineering and work practice controls, the employer must implement and maintain engineering and work practice controls to reduce airborne exposure to the lowest levels feasible and supplement these controls by using respiratory protection in accordance with paragraph (g) of this standard.
units.action_summary: If controls cannot get exposures to PELs, implement and maintain the lowest feasible controls and supplement with respiratory protection per paragraph (g).

units.obligation_text: The employer must use engineering and work practice controls to reduce and maintain employee airborne exposure to beryllium to or below the TWA PEL and STEL, unless the employer can demonstrate that such controls are not feasible.

units.obligation_text: Wherever the employer demonstrates that it is not feasible to reduce airborne exposure to or below the PELs with engineering and work practice controls, the employer must implement and maintain engineering and work practice controls to reduce airborne exposure to the lowest levels feasible and supplement these controls by using respiratory protection in accordance with paragraph (g) of this standard.
units.action_summary: If controls cannot get exposures to PELs, implement and maintain the lowest feasible controls and supplement with respiratory protection per paragraph (g).

units.obligation_text: Where airborne exposure exceeds, or can reasonably be expected to exceed, the TWA PEL or STEL, the employer must provide at no cost, and ensure that each employee uses, appropriate personal protective clothing and equipment in accordance with the written exposure control plan required under paragraph (f)(1) of this standard and OSHA’s Personal Protective Equipment standards for shipyards (subpart I of this part):
units.action_summary: Provide, at no cost, appropriate PPE and ensure employee use when exposures exceed or can be expected to exceed limits, per the exposure control plan and PPE standards.

units.obligation_text: The employer must ensure that each employee removes all personal protective clothing and equipment required by this standard at the end of the work shift or at the completion of all tasks involving beryllium, whichever comes first.
units.action_summary: Ensure employees remove required PPE at shift end or after tasks involving beryllium.

units.obligation_text: The employer must ensure that personal protective clothing and equipment required by this standard is not removed in a manner that disperses beryllium into the air.
units.action_summary: Ensure PPE is not removed in ways that disperse beryllium airborne.

units.obligation_text: The employer must ensure that beryllium is not removed from personal protective clothing and equipment required by this standard by blowing, shaking or any other means that disperses beryllium into the air.
units.action_summary: Prevent removal of beryllium from PPE by blowing, shaking, or other dispersal methods.

units.obligation_text: When cleaning dust resulting from operations that cause, or can reasonably be expected to cause, airborne exposure above the TWA PEL or STEL, the employer must ensure the use of methods that minimize the likelihood and level of airborne exposure.
units.action_summary: Ensure use of cleaning methods that minimize airborne exposure when cleaning dust from operations that cause or may cause exposures above limits.

units.obligation_text: The employer must not allow dry sweeping or brushing for cleaning up dust resulting from operations that cause, or can reasonably be expected to cause, airborne exposure above the TWA PEL or STEL unless methods that minimize the likelihood and level of airborne exposure are not safe or effective.
units.action_summary: Prohibit dry sweeping or brushing to clean dust from operations that cause/may cause exposures above limits, unless safer/effective methods are not available.

units.obligation_text: Exception: dry sweeping or brushing is allowed when methods that minimize the likelihood and level of airborne exposure are not safe or effective.
units.action_summary: Exception allowing dry sweeping/brushing if minimizing methods are unsafe or ineffective.

units.obligation_text: The employer must not allow the use of compressed air for cleaning where the use of compressed air causes, or can reasonably be expected to cause, airborne exposure above the TWA PEL or STEL.
units.action_summary: Prohibit use of compressed air for cleaning where it causes or may cause airborne exposures above limits.

units.obligation_text: Where employees use dry sweeping, brushing, or compressed air to clean, the employer must provide, and ensure that each employee uses, respiratory protection and personal protective clothing and equipment in accordance with paragraphs (g) and (h) of this standard.
units.action_summary: Provide and ensure use of respiratory protection and PPE when employees use dry sweeping, brushing, or compressed air to clean.

units.obligation_text: The employer must ensure that cleaning equipment is handled and maintained in a manner that minimizes the likelihood and level of airborne exposure and the re-entrainment of airborne beryllium in the workplace.
units.action_summary: Handle and maintain cleaning equipment to minimize airborne exposure and prevent re-entrainment of beryllium.

units.obligation_text: The employer must provide an evaluation at no cost to the employee at a CBD diagnostic center that is mutually agreed upon by the employer and the employee.
units.action_summary: Provide, at no cost, an evaluation at a mutually agreed CBD diagnostic center.

units.obligation_text: The employer must also provide, at no cost to the employee and within a reasonable time after the initial consultation with the CBD diagnostic center, any of the following tests if deemed appropriate by the examining physician at the CBD diagnostic center: pulmonary function testing (as outlined by the American Thoracic Society criteria), bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL), and transbronchial biopsy.
units.action_summary: Provide, at no cost and within a reasonable time after consultation, pulmonary function testing, BAL, and transbronchial biopsy if deemed appropriate by the CBD physician.

units.obligation_text: Employers must include beryllium in the hazard communication program established to comply with the HCS.

units.obligation_text: Employers must ensure that each employee has access to labels on containers of beryllium and to safety data sheets, and is trained in accordance with the requirements of the HCS (29 CFR 1910.1200) and paragraph (m)(3) of this standard.

title: Procedures To Adjust Customs COBRA User Fees To Reflect Inflation

units.obligation_text: CBP will determine annually whether an adjustment to the fees and limitations is necessary and a notice specifying the amount of the fees and limitations will be published in the Federal Register annually for each fiscal year at least 30 days prior to the effective date of the new fees and limitations.
units.action_summary: CBP must annually determine whether fee adjustments are necessary and publish a notice in the Federal Register at least 30 days before the effective date of any new fees and limitations.

units.obligation_text: The fees and the limitations will also be maintained for the public’s convenience on the CBP Web site at www.cbp.gov.
units.action_summary: CBP must maintain the fees and limitations on its public website.

units.obligation_text: If a customs user has pre-paid or met the calendar year limit prior to the effective date of the new fees and limitations, no additional fees will be required for that calendar year.
units.action_summary: If a customs user prepaid or met the calendar limit before a fee change, no additional fees may be required for that calendar year.

units.obligation_text: If the customs user has not pre-paid or met the calendar year limit prior to the effective date of the new fees and limitations, the customs user will be subject to the adjusted limitation or prepayment amount.
units.action_summary: Customs users who have not prepaid or met the limit before the effective date must comply with the adjusted fee limitation or prepayment amount.

units.obligation_text: Upon arrival at a CBP port of entry, the driver or other person in charge of a commercial truck must tender the fees to CBP unless they have been prepaid as provided for in paragraph (c)(3) of this section.
units.actor: the driver or other person in charge of a commercial truck
units.action_summary: On arrival at a CBP port, the truck driver/person in charge must pay the applicable fees to CBP unless those fees were prepaid under paragraph (c)(3).

units.obligation_text: unless they have been prepaid as provided for in paragraph (c)(3) of this section.
units.actor: the driver or other person in charge of a commercial truck
units.action_summary: Exception: drivers/persons in charge need not tender fees on arrival if the fees were prepaid per paragraph (c)(3).

units.obligation_text: The fees will not apply to any commercial truck which, at the time of arrival, is being transported by any vessel other than a ferry.
units.action_summary: CBP will not apply the commercial truck arrival fees to trucks arriving while being transported by a vessel other than a ferry.

units.obligation_text: No CBP fee will be collected under paragraph (c)(1) of this section for the arrival of a commercial truck during any calendar year once a prepayment of $100, as adjusted by the terms of paragraph (k) of this section, has been made and a transponder has been affixed to the vehicle windshield as provided in paragraph (c)(3) of this section.
units.action_summary: CBP will not collect the CBP commercial truck arrival fee for a calendar year once a $100 prepayment has been made and a transponder affixed as required.

units.obligation_text: Subject to paragraphs (g)(1)(ii) and (g)(3) of this section, a fee of $5.50, as adjusted by the terms of paragraph (k) of this section, must be collected and remitted to CBP for services provided in connection with the arrival of each passenger aboard a commercial vessel or commercial aircraft from a place outside the United States except:
units.actor: responsible collecting parties (e.g., carriers, operators) / entities required to collect and remit fees
units.action_summary: A $5.50 (adjustable) fee must be collected and remitted to CBP for each passenger arriving by commercial vessel or aircraft from outside the U.S., subject to specified exceptions.

units.obligation_text: When the journey of the arriving passenger originates in a territory or possession of the United States;
units.actor: passenger / fee collectors (as exception to collection)
units.action_summary: Exception to the $5.50 fee when the passenger's journey originates in a U.S. territory or possession.

units.obligation_text: When the journey of the arriving passenger originates in the United States and was not limited to the territories and possessions of the United States.
units.actor: passenger / fee collectors (as exception to collection)
units.action_summary: Exception to the $5.50 fee when the passenger's journey originates in the United States and was not limited to U.S. territories and possessions.

units.obligation_text: Subject to paragraph (g)(3) of this section, a fee of $1.93, as adjusted by the terms of paragraph (k) of this section, must be collected and remitted to CBP for services provided in connection with the arrival of each passenger aboard a commercial vessel whose journey originated in a territory or possession of the United States or whose journey originated in the United States and was limited to the territories and possessions of the United States.
units.actor: responsible collecting parties (e.g., carriers, operators) / entities required to collect and remit fees
units.action_summary: A $1.93 (adjustable) fee must be collected and remitted to CBP for each passenger arriving by commercial vessel from U.S. territories/possessions or on journeys limited to those areas.

units.obligation_text: Customs brokers are subject to an annual user fee of $138, as adjusted by the terms of paragraph (k) of this section, for each district permit and for a national permit held by an individual, partnership, association, or corporation.
units.action_summary: Customs brokers must pay an annual user fee (adjustable amount) for each district or national permit they hold.

units.obligation_text: The annual user fee for each district permit must be submitted to the port through which the broker was granted the permit.
units.action_summary: Brokers must submit the district permit annual fee to the port that granted the permit.

units.obligation_text: The annual user fee for a national permit must be submitted to the port through which the broker’s license is delivered.
units.action_summary: Brokers must submit the national permit annual fee to the port through which their license was delivered.

units.obligation_text: CBP will determine annually whether an adjustment to the fees and limitations is necessary and a notice specifying the amount of the fees and limitations, as adjusted, will be published in the Federal Register annually for each fiscal year at least 30 days prior to the effective date of the new fees and limitations.
units.action_summary: CBP must annually decide whether fees need adjustment and publish the adjusted amounts in the Federal Register at least 30 days before their effective date.

units.obligation_text: CBP will determine the adjustments, if any, by making the following calculations:
units.action_summary: CBP must compute adjustments using the specified calculation steps.

units.obligation_text: Calculate the arithmetic average of the Consumer Price Index—All Urban Consumers, U.S. All items, 1982–84 = 100 (CPI–U) for the current year based on the most recent June–May period. This figure is referred to as (A).
units.action_summary: Compute the arithmetic average CPI–U for the current year (June–May) and call it (A).

units.obligation_text: Use the figure 236.009 which is the arithmetic average of the CPI–U for FY 2014. This figure is referred to as (B).
units.action_summary: Use 236.009 as the FY 2014 arithmetic average CPI–U (B).

units.obligation_text: State the arithmetic average of CPI–U for the comparison year which will be either (B) if the fees have never been adjusted in accordance with this paragraph (k), or the arithmetic average of the CPI–U for the last year in which fees were adjusted in accordance with this paragraph (k) as set forth in the Federal Register notice that last adjusted the fee. This figure is referred to as (C).
units.action_summary: Determine and identify the comparison-year CPI–U average (C) as either B (if never adjusted) or the last adjusted year's CPI average per the Federal Register notice.

units.obligation_text: Calculate the difference between the arithmetic averages of the CPI–U of the comparison year (C) and the current year (A). This difference is referred to as (D). (D) = (A)¥(C).
units.action_summary: Compute D = A − C, the difference between current and comparison year CPI averages.

units.obligation_text: Round the difference (D) to the nearest whole number. This figure is referred to as (E).
units.action_summary: Round D to the nearest whole number to obtain E.

units.obligation_text: Calculate the percentage change in the arithmetic averages of the CPI–U of the comparison year (C) and the current year (A) which is referred to as (F). (F) = ((E)÷(C)) × 100%.
units.action_summary: Compute F = (E ÷ C) × 100%, the percentage change between comparison and current year CPI averages.

units.obligation_text: If (F) is one percent or more, proceed to the next step (viii). If (F) is less than one percent, no adjustment will be made.
units.action_summary: If F ≥ 1% then proceed to step (viii); if F < 1% then do not adjust fees (no adjustment will be made).

units.obligation_text: Calculate the difference in the arithmetic average of the CPI–U between the current year (the most recent June through May period) and the base year (FY 2014). This difference is referred to as (G). (G) = (A)¥(B).
units.action_summary: Compute G = A − B, the difference between current year and FY2014 CPI averages.

units.obligation_text: Calculate the percentage change in the CPI–U from the base year to the current year. This figure is referred to as (H). (H) = ((G)÷(B)) × 100%.
units.action_summary: Compute H = (G ÷ B) × 100%, the percent change from base year to current year CPI.

units.obligation_text: Increase the fees and limitations that are subject to the rules of this paragraph by (H), calculating fees and limitations to the second decimal.
units.action_summary: Adjust fees and limitations upward by H percent, rounding to the second decimal.

units.obligation_text: CBP will determine annually whether an adjustment to the fees and limitations is necessary and a notice specifying the amount of the fees and limitations will be published in the Federal Register annually for each fiscal year at least 30 days prior to the effective date of the new fees and limitations. The fees and the limitations will also be maintained for the public’s convenience on the CBP Web site at www.cbp.gov.
units.action_summary: CBP must annually determine adjustments to merchandise processing fees and publish notice at least 30 days before changes; maintain amounts on its website.

units.obligation_text: Each carrier or operator using an express consignment carrier facility or a centralized hub facility must pay to CBP a fee in the amount of $1.00, as adjusted in accordance with the terms of paragraph (k) of § 24.22 of this chapter, per individual air waybill or individual bill of lading for the processing of airway bills for shipments arriving in the United States.
units.actor: each carrier or operator using an express consignment carrier facility or a centralized hub facility
units.action_summary: Carriers/operators using specified facilities must pay an adjustable $1.00 fee per individual air waybill or bill of lading for shipments arriving in the U.S.

units.obligation_text: In addition, if merchandise is formally entered and valued at $2,500 or less, the importer of record must pay to CBP the ad valorem fee specified in paragraph (b)(1) of this section, if applicable.
units.action_summary: If merchandise is formally entered and valued at $2,500 or less, the importer of record must pay the specified ad valorem fee to CBP, if applicable.

units.obligation_text: Payment must be made to CBP on a quarterly basis and must cover the individual fees for all subject transactions that occurred during a calendar quarter.
units.actor: each carrier or operator required to pay the facility fee
units.action_summary: Quarterly payments to CBP are required and must cover all applicable transaction fees for the quarter.

units.obligation_text: Subject to the provisions of paragraph (b)(1)(i)(A) and (b)(4) of this section relating to the express consignment carrier facility or centralized hub facility fee, the fee per individual air waybill or bill of lading charged under paragraph (b)(1)(i)(A) of this section must not exceed $1, as adjusted in accordance with the terms of paragraph (k) of § 24.22 of this chapter, and must not be less than $0.35, as adjusted by paragraph (k) of § 24.22 of this chapter.
units.actor: the fee-charging parties (carriers/operators) and CBP (with respect to fee limits)
units.action_summary: The per-waybill fee must be no more than $1.00 and no less than $0.35 (adjustable), subject to specified provisions.
units.modal_raw: must not exceed / must not be less than

units.obligation_text: the fee per individual air waybill or bill of lading charged under paragraph (b)(1)(i)(A) of this section must not exceed $1, as adjusted in accordance with the terms of paragraph (k) of § 24.22 of this chapter.
units.action_summary: The fee per individual waybill/bill of lading must not exceed $1.00 (adjustable).

units.obligation_text: the fee per individual air waybill or bill of lading charged under paragraph (b)(1)(i)(A) of this section must not be less than $0.35, as adjusted by paragraph (k) of § 24.22 of this chapter.
units.action_summary: The fee per individual waybill/bill of lading must be at least $0.35 (adjustable).

units.obligation_text: The quarterly payment must conform to the requirements of § 24.1, must be submitted electronically via Fedwire or pay.gov, or mailed to Customs and Border Protection, Revenue Division/Attention: Reimbursables, 6650 Telecom Drive, Suite 100, Indianapolis, Indiana 46278, and must be received by CBP no later than the last day of the month that follows the close of the calendar quarter to which the payment relates.
units.actor: each carrier or operator required to make the quarterly payment
units.action_summary: Quarterly payments must meet §24.1 requirements, be submitted electronically or by mail to the specified address, and be received by the deadline (last day of the month following the quarter).

units.obligation_text: The following information must be included with the quarterly payment:
units.actor: each carrier or operator making the quarterly payment
units.action_summary: Carriers/operators must include specified information with the quarterly payment.

units.obligation_text: The identity of the calendar quarter to which the payment relates;
units.actor: each carrier or operator making the quarterly payment
units.action_summary: Include the identity of the calendar quarter covered by the payment.

units.obligation_text: The identity of the facility for which the payment is made and the port code that applies to that location and, if the payment covers multiple facilities, the identity of each facility and its port code and the portion of the payment that pertains to each port code;
units.actor: each carrier or operator making the quarterly payment
units.action_summary: Include facility identity, port code, and allocation of payment among multiple facilities, if applicable.

units.obligation_text: The total number of individual air waybills and individual bills of lading covered by the payment, and a breakdown of that total for each facility covered by the payment according to the number covered by formal entry procedures, the number covered by informal entry procedures specified in §§ 128.24(e) and 143.23(j) of this chapter, and the number covered by other informal entry procedures.
units.actor: each carrier or operator making the quarterly payment
units.action_summary: Provide the total number of individual waybills/bills covered and a breakdown by entry procedure type for each facility.

units.obligation_text: In the case of an overpayment, the carrier or operator may request a refund by writing to Customs and Border Protection, Revenue Division/Attention: Reimbursables, 6650 Telecom Drive, Suite 100, Indianapolis, Indiana 46278.
units.actor: the carrier or operator (in the case of an overpayment)
units.action_summary: Carriers/operators may request a refund for overpayments by writing to the specified CBP address.

units.obligation_text: The refund request must specify the grounds for the refund and must be received by CBP within one year of the date the fee for which the refund is sought was paid to CBP;
units.actor: the carrier or operator requesting a refund
units.action_summary: Refund requests must state the grounds and be received by CBP within one year of the fee payment date.

units.obligation_text: In the case of an underpayment, interest will accrue on the amount not paid from the date payment was initially due to the date that payment to CBP is made.
units.actor: the carrier or operator (with respect to amounts owed)
units.action_summary: Interest accrues on underpayments from the original due date until payment is made to CBP.

units.obligation_text: The underpayment or failure of a carrier or operator using an express consignment carrier facility or a centralized hub facility to pay all applicable fees owed to CBP pursuant to paragraph (b)(4) of this section may result in the assessment of penalties under 19 U.S.C. 1592, liquidated damages, and any other action authorized by law.
units.action_summary: CBP or enforcement authorities may assess penalties, liquidated damages, or take other authorized actions if carriers/operators underpay or fail to pay applicable fees.

title: Modernization of the Customs Brokers Regulations

units.obligation_text: A national permit issued to a broker under § 111.19 will constitute sufficient permit authority for the broker to conduct customs business within the customs territory of the United States as defined in § 101.1 of this chapter.
units.action_summary: A national permit serves as sufficient authority for a broker to conduct customs business throughout U.S. customs territory.

units.obligation_text: Customs business must be conducted within the customs territory of the United States as defined in § 101.1 of this chapter.
units.action_summary: Customs business must be conducted within the U.S. customs territory.

units.obligation_text: A licensed customs broker, or partnership, association, or corporation, conducting customs business under a national permit must designate a knowledgeable point of contact to be available to CBP during and outside of normal operating hours to respond to customs business issues.
units.actor: licensed customs broker, partnership, association, or corporation conducting business under a national permit
units.action_summary: Designate a knowledgeable point of contact available to CBP during and outside normal hours.

units.obligation_text: The licensed customs broker, or partnership, association, or corporation, must maintain accurate and current point of contact information in a CBP-authorized electronic data interchange (EDI) system.
units.actor: licensed customs broker, partnership, association, or corporation conducting business under a national permit
units.action_summary: Keep accurate and current point-of-contact information in a CBP-authorized EDI system.

units.obligation_text: If a CBP-authorized EDI system is not available, then the information must be provided in writing to the director of the designated Center.
units.actor: licensed customs broker, partnership, association, or corporation conducting business under a national permit
units.action_summary: If no CBP-authorized EDI is available, provide point-of-contact information in writing to the designated Center director.

units.obligation_text: An application for a broker’s license must be timely submitted to the director of the Center identified by CBP after the applicant attains a passing grade on the examination.
units.action_summary: Submit the application for a broker's license in a timely manner to the Center director after passing the exam.

units.obligation_text: The application must be executed on CBP Form 3124.
units.action_summary: Execute the application using CBP Form 3124.

units.obligation_text: The application must be accompanied by the application fee prescribed in § 111.96(a) and one copy of the appropriate attachment required by the application form (Articles of Agreement or an affidavit signed by all partners, Articles of Agreement of the association, or the Articles of Incorporation).
units.action_summary: Include the prescribed application fee and required attachment with the application.

units.obligation_text: If the applicant proposes to operate under a trade or fictitious name in one or more States, evidence of the applicant’s authority to use the name in each of those States must accompany the application.
units.action_summary: Provide evidence of authority to use any trade or fictitious name in each State where it will be used.

units.obligation_text: An application for an individual license must be submitted within the 3-year period after the applicant took and passed the examination referred to in § 111.11(a)(4) and § 111.13.
units.action_summary: Submit an individual license application within three years after passing the exam.

units.obligation_text: The Center director may require an individual applicant to provide a copy of the notification that the applicant passed the examination (see § 111.13(e)) and will require the applicant to submit fingerprints at the time of the interview.
units.action_summary: The Center director may request proof of passing the exam and will require the applicant to submit fingerprints at the interview.

units.obligation_text: The Center director may reject an application as improperly filed if the application is incomplete or, if on its face, the application demonstrates that one or more of the basic requirements set forth in § 111.11 has not been met at the time of filing; in either case the application and fee will be returned to the filer without further action.
units.action_summary: The Center director may reject incomplete or noncompliant applications and the application and fee will be returned to the filer.

units.obligation_text: The director of the designated Center will forward the application and supporting documentation to the appropriate Executive Director Office of Trade.
units.action_summary: Forward the application and supporting documents to the appropriate Executive Director, Office of Trade.

units.obligation_text: The Center director will also submit his or her recommendation for action on the application.
units.action_summary: Submit a recommendation for action on the application.

units.obligation_text: The appropriate Executive Director, Office of Trade, may require further inquiry if additional facts are deemed necessary to evaluate the application.
units.actor: appropriate Executive Director, Office of Trade
units.action_summary: May order further inquiry when additional facts are needed to evaluate an application.

units.obligation_text: The appropriate Executive Director, Office of Trade, may also require the applicant (or in the case of a partnership, association, or corporation, one or more of its members or officers) to appear in person or by another approved method before the appropriate Executive Director, Office of Trade, or his or her representatives for the purpose of undergoing further written or oral inquiry.
units.actor: appropriate Executive Director, Office of Trade / applicant
units.action_summary: The Executive Director may require the applicant or certain representatives to appear for further inquiry.

units.obligation_text: If the appropriate Executive Director, Office of Trade, finds that the applicant is qualified and has paid all applicable fees prescribed in § 111.96(a), the Executive Assistant Commissioner will issue a license.
units.action_summary: Issue a license when the Executive Director finds the applicant qualified and fees paid.

units.obligation_text: The license will be forwarded to the director of the designated Center, who will deliver it to the licensee.
units.action_summary: Deliver the issued license to the licensee after forwarding from headquarters.

units.obligation_text: If the appropriate Executive Director, Office of Trade, determines that the application for a license should be denied for any reason, notice of denial will be given by him or her to the applicant and to the director of the designated Center.
units.actor: appropriate Executive Director, Office of Trade
units.action_summary: Give notice of denial to the applicant and the designated Center director when the Executive Director determines denial is appropriate.

units.obligation_text: The notice of denial will state the reasons why the license was not issued.
units.actor: appropriate Executive Director, Office of Trade
units.action_summary: State reasons for denial in the notice provided to the applicant.

units.obligation_text: Upon the denial of an application for a license, the applicant may file with the appropriate Executive Director, Office of Trade, in writing, additional information or arguments in support of the application and may request to appear in person, by telephone, or by other acceptable means of communication.
units.action_summary: Applicant may submit additional information or request to appear to the Executive Director after denial.

units.obligation_text: This filing and request must be received by the appropriate Executive Director, Office of Trade within sixty (60) calendar days of the denial.
units.action_summary: The additional filing and appearance request must be received within 60 calendar days of denial.

units.obligation_text: Upon the decision of the appropriate Executive Director, Office of Trade, affirming the denial of an application for a license, the applicant may file with the Executive Assistant Commissioner, in writing, a request for any additional review that the Executive Assistant Commissioner, deems appropriate.
units.action_summary: Applicant may request additional review by the Executive Assistant Commissioner after an affirmation of denial.

units.obligation_text: This request must be received by the Executive Assistant Commissioner within sixty (60) calendar days of the affirmation by the appropriate Executive Director, Office of Trade, of the denial of the application for a license.
units.action_summary: The request for additional review must be received within 60 calendar days of the Executive Director's affirmation.

units.obligation_text: Upon a decision of the Executive Assistant Commissioner affirming the denial of an application for a license, the applicant may appeal the decision to the Court of International Trade, provided that the appeal action is commenced within sixty (60) calendar days after the date of entry of the Executive Assistant Commissioner’s decision.
units.action_summary: Applicant may appeal to the Court of International Trade within 60 calendar days after the Executive Assistant Commissioner's decision.

units.obligation_text: A national permit is required for the purpose of transacting customs business throughout the customs territory of the United States as defined in § 101.1 of this chapter.
units.action_summary: A national permit is required to transact customs business throughout U.S. customs territory.

units.obligation_text: An applicant who obtains a passing grade on the examination for an individual broker’s license may apply for a national permit.
units.actor: applicant who passed the broker exam
units.action_summary: After passing the broker exam, an applicant may apply for a national permit.

units.obligation_text: The applicant will exercise responsible supervision and control (as described in § 111.28 of this part) over the activities conducted under that national permit.
units.actor: the applicant who holds the national permit (individual broker)
units.action_summary: The national permit holder must exercise responsible supervision and control over activities under the permit.

units.obligation_text: An application for a national permit under this paragraph must be in the form of a letter or CBP-approved electronic submission to the director of the designated Center. The application must set forth or attach the following:
units.action_summary: Submit national permit application as a letter or CBP-approved electronic submission to the designated Center director and include specified information/attachments.

units.obligation_text: The applicant’s broker license number and date of issuance if available;
units.action_summary: Provide broker license number and date of issuance, if available, in the national permit application.

units.obligation_text: If the applicant is applying for a national permit on behalf of a partnership, association, or corporation: The name of the partnership, association, or corporation and the title held by the applicant within the partnership, association, or corporation;
units.actor: applicant applying on behalf of partnership/association/corporation
units.action_summary: Provide entity name and applicant's title within the entity when applying on behalf of a partnership, association, or corporation.

units.obligation_text: If the applicant is applying for a national permit on behalf of a partnership, association, or corporation: A copy of the documentation issued by a State, or local government that establishes the legal status and reserves the business name of the partnership, association, or corporation;
units.actor: applicant applying on behalf of partnership/association/corporation
units.action_summary: Attach state or local documentation establishing legal status and reserved business name when applying on behalf of an entity.

units.obligation_text: The address, telephone number, and email address of the office designated by the applicant as the office of record as defined in § 111.1. The office will be noted in the national permit when issued;
units.action_summary: Provide contact information for the office designated as the office of record; it will be noted on the permit.

units.obligation_text: The name, telephone number, and email address of the point of contact described in § 111.3(b) to be available to CBP to respond to issues related to the transaction of customs business;
units.action_summary: Provide point-of-contact name and contact information for responding to customs business issues.

units.obligation_text: If the applicant is applying for a national permit on behalf of a partnership, association, or corporation: The name, broker license number, office address, telephone number, and email address of each individual broker employed by the partnership, association, or corporation;
units.actor: applicant applying on behalf of partnership/association/corporation
units.action_summary: List each employed individual broker's name, license number, office address, phone, and email.

units.obligation_text: A list of all employees together with the specific employee information prescribed in § 111.28 for each employee;
units.action_summary: Provide a list of all employees with the employee information required under § 111.28.

units.obligation_text: A supervision plan describing how responsible supervision and control will be exercised over the customs business conducted under the national permit, including compliance with § 111.28;
units.action_summary: Attach a supervision plan explaining how responsible supervision and control will be exercised, including compliance with § 111.28.

units.obligation_text: The location where records will be retained (see § 111.23);
units.action_summary: Indicate the location where records will be retained.

units.obligation_text: The name, telephone number, and email address of the knowledgeable employee responsible for broker-wide records maintenance and financial recordkeeping requirements (see § 111.21(d)); and
units.action_summary: Provide contact information for the employee responsible for records maintenance and financial recordkeeping.

units.obligation_text: A receipt or other evidence showing that the fees specified in § 111.96(b) and (c) have been paid in accordance with paragraph (b) of this section.
units.action_summary: Provide evidence that the required national permit fees have been paid.

units.obligation_text: The director of the designated Center who receives the application will review to determine whether the applicant meets the requirements of paragraphs (a) and (b) of this section.
units.action_summary: Review national permit applications to determine whether the applicant meets the section's requirements.

units.obligation_text: If the director of the designated Center is of the opinion that the national permit should not be issued, he or she will submit his or her written reasons for that opinion to the appropriate Executive Director, Office of Trade, CBP Headquarters, for appropriate instructions on whether to grant or deny the national permit.
units.action_summary: If recommending denial, submit written reasons to the appropriate Executive Director for instructions on granting or denying the permit.

units.obligation_text: The appropriate Executive Director, Office of Trade, CBP Headquarters, will notify the applicant if his or her application is denied.
units.actor: appropriate Executive Director, Office of Trade
units.action_summary: Notify the applicant if the national permit application is denied.

units.obligation_text: CBP will issue a national permit to an applicant who meets the requirements of paragraphs (a) and (b) of this section.
units.action_summary: Issue a national permit to applicants who satisfy the section's requirements.

units.obligation_text: CBP will maintain and make available to the public an alphabetical list of permitted brokers.
units.action_summary: Maintain and publicly provide an alphabetical list of permitted brokers.

units.obligation_text: Upon the denial of an application for a national permit under this section, the applicant may file with the Executive Assistant Commissioner, in writing, additional information or arguments in support of the denied application and may request to appear in person, by telephone, or by other acceptable means of communication.
units.action_summary: Applicant may submit additional information and request to appear to the Executive Assistant Commissioner after national permit denial.

units.obligation_text: This filing and request must be received by the Executive Assistant Commissioner within sixty (60) calendar days of the denial.
units.action_summary: The additional filing and appearance request must be received within 60 calendar days of denial.

units.obligation_text: Upon a decision of the Executive Assistant Commissioner affirming the denial of an application for a national permit under this section, the applicant may appeal the decision to the Court of International Trade, provided that the appeal action is commenced within sixty (60) calendar days after the date of entry of the decision by the Executive Assistant Commissioner.
units.action_summary: Applicant may appeal to the Court of International Trade within 60 calendar days after the Executive Assistant Commissioner's decision.

units.obligation_text: The individual broker who qualifies for the national permit will exercise responsible supervision and control (as described in § 111.28 of this part) over the activities conducted under that national permit.
units.actor: individual broker qualifying the national permit
units.action_summary: Exercise responsible supervision and control over activities conducted under the national permit.

units.obligation_text: Each broker must provide notification to the broker’s designated Center of any known breach of electronic or physical records relating to the broker’s customs business. Notification to CBP must be provided within 72 hours of the discovery of the breach with a list of all compromised importer identification numbers (see 19 CFR 24.5).
units.action_summary: Notify the designated Center and CBP within 72 hours of discovering any breach of electronic or physical records, including a list of compromised importer IDs.

units.obligation_text: Each broker must designate a knowledgeable employee as the party responsible for brokerage-wide recordkeeping requirements.
units.action_summary: Designate an employee responsible for brokerage-wide recordkeeping requirements.

units.obligation_text: Each broker must maintain accurate and current point of contact information in a CBP-authorized electronic data interchange (EDI) system. If a CBP-authorized EDI system is not available, then the information must be provided in writing to the director of the designated Center.
units.action_summary: Maintain accurate point-of-contact info in CBP-authorized EDI, or provide it in writing to the Center director if EDI is unavailable.

units.obligation_text: A licensed customs broker must maintain the records referred to in this part, including any records stored in electronic formats, within the customs territory of the United States and in accordance with the provisions of this part and part 163 of this chapter.
units.action_summary: Keep required records within U.S. customs territory and in accordance with this part and part 163, including electronic records.

units.obligation_text: The records referred to in this part and pertaining to the business of the clients serviced by the broker are to be considered confidential, and the broker must not disclose their contents or any information connected with the records to any persons other than those clients, their surety on a particular entry, and representatives of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), or other duly accredited officers or agents of the United States, except on subpoena or court order by a court of competent jurisdiction, or when authorized in writing by the client.
units.action_summary: Keep client-related records confidential and do not disclose their contents except to specified parties or under specified legal authorization or client authorization.

units.obligation_text: Except on subpoena or court order by a court of competent jurisdiction, or when authorized in writing by the client.
units.action_summary: Disclosure is permitted on subpoena/court order or when client authorizes in writing.

units.obligation_text: This confidentiality provision does not apply to information that properly is available from a source open to the public.
units.action_summary: The confidentiality rule does not bar disclosure of information already publicly available.

units.obligation_text: During the period of retention, the broker must maintain the records referred to in this part in such a manner that they may readily be examined.
units.action_summary: Keep records in a manner that allows them to be readily examined during the retention period.

units.obligation_text: Records required to be maintained under the provisions of this part must be made available upon reasonable notice for inspection, copying, reproduction or other official use by representatives of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) within the prescribed period of retention or within any longer period of time during which they remain in the possession of the broker.
units.action_summary: Make records available upon reasonable notice for inspection, copying, or other official use by DHS within retention periods.

units.obligation_text: Upon request by DHS to examine records, the designated recordkeeping contact (see § 111.21(d)), must make all records available to DHS within thirty (30) calendar days, or such longer time as specified by DHS, at the location specified by DHS.
units.action_summary: Provide all requested records to DHS within 30 calendar days (or longer if specified) at the DHS-specified location.

units.obligation_text: Records subject to the requirements of part 163 of this chapter must be made available to DHS in accordance with the provisions of that part.
units.action_summary: Make records subject to part 163 available to DHS according to part 163's provisions.

units.obligation_text: Every individual broker operating as a sole proprietor, every licensed member of a partnership that is a broker, and every licensed officer of an association or corporation that is a broker must exercise responsible supervision and control (see § 111.1) over the transaction of the customs business of the sole proprietorship, partnership, association, or corporation.
units.actor: individual brokers, licensed members, and licensed officers as specified
units.action_summary: Exercise responsible supervision and control over the custom business of the entity.

units.obligation_text: A sole proprietorship, partnership, association, or corporation must employ a sufficient number of licensed brokers relative to the job complexity, similarity of subordinate tasks, physical proximity of subordinates, abilities and skills of employees, and abilities and skills of the managers.
units.actor: sole proprietorship, partnership, association, or corporation broker
units.action_summary: Employ a sufficient number of licensed brokers relative to operational factors to ensure supervision and control.

units.obligation_text: Each national permit holder must submit to the director of the designated Center, a list of the names of persons currently employed by the broker. The list of employees must be submitted prior to issuance of a national permit under § 111.19 and before the broker begins to transact customs business.
units.action_summary: Submit a list of current employees to the designated Center director prior to permit issuance and before transacting customs business.

units.obligation_text: For each employee, the broker must provide the name, social security number, date and place of birth, date of hire, and current home address.
units.action_summary: Provide specified personal and employment information for each employee.

units.obligation_text: After the initial submission, an updated list must be submitted to a CBP-authorized electronic data interchange (EDI) system if any of the information required by this paragraph changes. If a CBP-authorized EDI system is not available, then the information must be provided in writing to the director of the designated Center. The update must be submitted within thirty (30) calendar days of the change.
units.action_summary: Submit updated employee information to CBP-authorized EDI within 30 days of change, or in writing to the Center director if EDI is unavailable.

units.obligation_text: Within thirty (30) calendar days of the start of employment of a new employee(s), the broker must submit a list of new employee(s) with the information required under paragraph (b)(1) of this section to a CBP-authorized EDI system.
units.action_summary: Within 30 days of a new employee's start, submit the new employee list with required information to CBP-authorized EDI (or in writing if EDI unavailable).

units.obligation_text: Within thirty (30) calendar days after the termination of employment of an employee, the broker must submit a list of terminated employee(s) to a CBP-authorized EDI system.
units.action_summary: Submit a list of terminated employees within 30 days of termination to CBP-authorized EDI (or in writing if EDI unavailable).

units.obligation_text: Notwithstanding a broker’s responsibility for providing the information required in paragraph (b) of this section, in the absence of culpability by the broker, CBP will not hold the broker responsible for the accuracy of any information that is provided to the broker by the employee.
units.action_summary: CBP will not hold the broker responsible for the accuracy of employee-provided information absent broker culpability.

units.obligation_text: If the ownership of a broker changes and ownership shares in the broker are not publicly traded, the broker must immediately provide written notice of that fact to the appropriate Executive Director, Office of Trade, and must send a copy of the written notice to the director of the designated Center.
units.action_summary: Immediately give written notice of ownership changes (when shares are not publicly traded) to the appropriate Executive Director and send a copy to the Center director.

units.obligation_text: When a change in ownership results in the addition of a new principal to the organization, and whether or not ownership shares in the broker are publicly traded, CBP reserves the right to conduct a background investigation on the new principal.
units.action_summary: CBP may conduct a background investigation on any new principal added after a change in ownership.

units.obligation_text: The director of the designated Center will notify the broker if CBP objects to the new principal, and the broker will be given a reasonable period of time to remedy the situation.
units.actor: director of the designated Center / CBP
units.action_summary: If CBP objects to a new principal, the Center director will notify the broker and the broker will be given a reasonable period to remedy the issue.

units.obligation_text: If the background investigation uncovers information which would have been the basis for a denial of an application for a broker’s license and the principal’s interest in the broker is not terminated to the satisfaction of the director of the designated Center, suspension or revocation proceedings may be initiated under subpart D of this part.
units.action_summary: CBP may initiate suspension or revocation proceedings if a new principal's background would have warranted license denial and the principal's interest is not terminated satisfactorily.

units.obligation_text: A broker is responsible for providing CBP with the broker’s current addresses, which include the broker’s office of record address as defined in § 111.1 and, if the broker is not actively engaged in transacting business as a broker, the broker’s non-business address.
units.action_summary: Provide CBP with current addresses, including office of record and non-business address if not actively transacting business.

units.obligation_text: If a broker does not receive mail at the broker’s office of record or non-business address, the broker must also provide CBP with a valid address at which he or she receives mail.
units.action_summary: Provide CBP with a valid mailing address if mail is not received at the office of record or non-business address.

units.obligation_text: When address information changes, or the broker is no longer actively engaged in transacting business as a broker, he or she must update his or her address information within ten (10) calendar days through a CBP-authorized electronic data interchange (EDI) system.
units.action_summary: Update address information within 10 calendar days via CBP-authorized EDI when address changes or broker ceases active engagement.

units.obligation_text: If a CBP-authorized EDI system is not available, then address updates must be provided in writing within ten (10) calendar days to the director of the designated Center.
units.action_summary: If no EDI is available, provide address updates in writing to the Center director within 10 calendar days.

units.obligation_text: A partnership, association, or corporation broker must update within ten (10) calendar days in writing to the director of the designated Center any of the following: (1) The date on which a licensed member or officer ceases to be the qualifying member or officer for purposes of § 111.11(b) or (c)(2), and the name of the licensed member or officer who will succeed as the license qualifier; (2) The date on which a licensed employee ceases to be the national permit qualifier for purposes of § 111.19(a), and the name of the licensed employee who will succeed as the national permit qualifier; and (3) Any change in the Articles of Agreement, Charter, Articles of Association, or Articles of Incorporation relating to the transaction of customs business, or any other change in the legal nature of the organization.
units.action_summary: Notify the designated Center director in writing within 10 days of changes to qualifying members/officers, national permit qualifiers, or changes in corporate articles/legal nature.

units.obligation_text: A broker who changes his or her name, or who proposes to operate under a trade or fictitious name in one or more States and is authorized by State law to do so, must submit to the appropriate Executive Director, Office of Trade, at the Headquarters of U.S. Customs and Border Protection, evidence of his or her authority to use that name.
units.actor: broker who changes or proposes to use a trade/fictitious name
units.action_summary: Submit evidence of authority to use a changed or trade/fictitious name to the appropriate Executive Director.

units.obligation_text: Each broker must file a triennial status report with CBP on February 1 of each third year after 1985. The report must be filed through the CBP-authorized EDI system and accompanied by payment or valid proof of payment of the triennial status report fee prescribed in § 111.96(d). If a CBP-authorized EDI system is not available, the triennial status report must be filed with the director of the designated Center.
units.action_summary: File a triennial status report every third year on Feb 1 via CBP-authorized EDI with payment/proof, or file with the Center director if EDI unavailable.
units.modal_raw: must file / must be filed / must be accompanied

units.obligation_text: Each individual broker must state in the report required under paragraph (d)(1) of this section whether he or she is actively engaged in transacting business as a broker. If he or she is so actively engaged, the broker must also: (A) State the name under which, and the address at which, the broker’s business is conducted if he or she is a sole proprietor;
units.action_summary: If actively engaged and a sole proprietor, state the business name and address in the triennial report.

units.obligation_text: (B) State the name and address of his or her employer if he or she is employed by another broker, unless his or her employer is a partnership, association or corporation broker for which he or she is a qualifying member or officer for purposes of § 111.11(b) or (c)(2);
units.action_summary: If employed by another broker (and not a qualifying member/officer), provide the employer's name and address in the triennial report.

units.obligation_text: (C) State whether or not he or she still meets the applicable requirements of § 111.11 and § 111.19 of this part and has not engaged in any conduct that could constitute grounds for suspension or revocation under § 111.53 of this part.
units.action_summary: State whether the broker continues to meet required qualifications and has not engaged in conduct that could lead to suspension or revocation.

units.obligation_text: An individual broker not actively engaged in transacting business as a broker must provide CBP with the broker’s current mailing address, and state whether or not he or she still meets the applicable requirements of § 111.11 and § 111.19 of this part and has not engaged in any conduct that could constitute grounds for suspension or revocation under § 111.53 of this part.
units.action_summary: Provide current mailing address and state whether still meets requirements and has not engaged in disqualifying conduct.

units.obligation_text: Each partnership, association, or corporation broker must state in the report required under paragraph (d)(1) of this section the name under which its business as a broker is being transacted, the broker’s office of record (see § 111.1), the name and address of each licensed member of the partnership or licensed officer of the association or corporation, including the license qualifier under § 111.11(b) or (c)(2) and the name of the licensed employee who is the national permit qualifier under § 111.19(a), and whether the partnership, association, or corporation is actively engaged in transacting business as a broker. The report must be signed by a licensed member or officer.
units.action_summary: Include specified entity and personnel information in the triennial report and have it signed by a licensed member or officer.

units.obligation_text: A partnership, association, or corporation broker must state whether or not the partnership, association, or corporation broker still meets the applicable requirements of § 111.11 and § 111.19 of this part and has not engaged in any conduct that could constitute grounds for suspension or revocation under § 111.53 of this part.
units.action_summary: State whether the entity continues to meet required qualifications and has not engaged in disqualifying conduct.

units.obligation_text: A broker must not file or procure or assist in the filing of any claim, or of any document, affidavit, or other papers, known by such broker to be false.
units.action_summary: Do not file or assist filing claims or documents known to be false.

units.obligation_text: A broker must not give, or solicit or procure the giving of, any information or testimony that the broker knew or should have known was false or misleading in any matter pending before the Department of Homeland Security or to any representative of the Department of Homeland Security.
units.action_summary: Do not give, solicit, or procure false or misleading information or testimony in matters before DHS or its representatives.

units.obligation_text: A broker also must document and report to CBP when the broker separates from or cancels representation of a client as a result of determining the client is intentionally attempting to use the broker to defraud or otherwise commit any criminal act against the U.S. Government.
units.action_summary: Document and report to CBP when terminating or canceling representation because the client is attempting fraud or criminal acts against the U.S. Government.

units.obligation_text: The broker must obtain a customs power of attorney directly fro
units.action_summary: Obtain a customs power of attorney directly (text truncated in source).

title: International Entrepreneurs

units.obligation_text: Application for Entrepreneur Parole (Form I-941). For filing an application for parole for entrepreneurs: $1,200.
units.action_summary: A filing fee of $1,200 is required for an Application for Entrepreneur Parole (Form I-941).

units.obligation_text: An alien seeking an initial grant of parole as an entrepreneur of a start-up entity must file an Application for Entrepreneur Parole (Form I-941, or successor form) with USCIS, with the required fees (including biometric services fees), and supporting documentary evidence in accordance with this section and the form instructions, demonstrating eligibility as provided in paragraph (b)(2) of this section.
units.actor: alien seeking initial grant of parole
units.action_summary: Applicants must file Form I-941 (with required fees and supporting evidence) to seek initial entrepreneur parole.

units.obligation_text: An alien may be considered for parole under this section if the alien demonstrates that a grant of parole will provide a significant public benefit to the United States based on his or her role as an entrepreneur of a start-up entity.
units.action_summary: An applicant may be considered for parole if they demonstrate that their presence provides a significant public benefit as an entrepreneur.

units.obligation_text: Demonstrating that the alien is an entrepreneur as defined in paragraph (a)(1) of this section and that his or her entity is a start-up entity as defined in paragraph (a)(2) of this section;
units.action_summary: Applicant must demonstrate they meet the definitions of entrepreneur and that the entity is a start-up entity as defined.

units.obligation_text: Received, within 365 days immediately preceding the filing of an application for initial parole, a qualified investment amount of at least $345,000 from one or more qualified investors;
units.action_summary: One qualifying criterion is that the start-up received at least $345,000 in qualified investments within 365 days before filing.

units.obligation_text: Received, within 365 days immediately preceding the filing of an application for initial parole, an amount of at least $100,000 through one or more qualified government awards or grants.
units.action_summary: Alternative qualifying criterion: the start-up received at least $100,000 in qualified government awards/grants within 365 days before filing.

units.obligation_text: An alien who satisfies the criteria in paragraph (b)(2)(ii)(A) of this section and partially meets one or both of the criteria in paragraph (b)(2)(ii)(B) of this section may alternatively meet the standard described in paragraph (b)(2)(i) of this section by providing other reliable and compelling evidence of the start-up entity's substantial potential for rapid growth and job creation.
units.action_summary: Applicants who partially meet investment/grant criteria may instead provide other reliable and compelling evidence of the start-up's potential.

units.obligation_text: To request such parole, an entrepreneur parolee must timely file the Application for Entrepreneur Parole (Form I-941, or successor form) with USCIS, with the required fees (including biometric services fees), and supporting documentation in accordance with the form instructions, demonstrating eligibility as provided in paragraph (c)(2) of this section.
units.action_summary: To request re-parole, parolees must timely file Form I-941 with required fees and supporting documentation.

units.obligation_text: An alien may be considered for re-parole under this section if the alien demonstrates that a grant of parole will continue to provide a significant public benefit to the United States based on his or her role as an entrepreneur of a start-up entity.
units.action_summary: An entrepreneur may be considered for re-parole if they show continued significant public benefit.

units.obligation_text: Demonstrating that the alien continues to be an entrepreneur as defined in paragraph (a)(1) of this section and that his or her entity continues to be a start-up entity as defined in paragraph (a)(2) of this section;
units.action_summary: Applicant must show continued status as an entrepreneur and that the entity remains a start-up entity.

units.obligation_text: Received at least $500,000 in qualifying investments, qualified government grants or awards, or a combination of such funding, during the initial parole period;
units.action_summary: One re-parole criterion is that the start-up received at least $500,000 in qualifying funding during the initial parole period.

units.obligation_text: Created at least 10 qualified jobs with the start-up entity during the initial parole period;
units.action_summary: Alternative re-parole criterion: the start-up created at least 10 qualified jobs during the initial parole period.

units.obligation_text: Reached at least $500,000 in annual revenue and averaged 20 percent in annual revenue growth during the initial parole period.
units.action_summary: Alternative re-parole criterion: the start-up reached $500,000 annual revenue and averaged 20% annual revenue growth during the initial parole period.

units.obligation_text: An alien who satisfies the criteria in paragraph (c)(2)(ii)(A) of this section and partially meets one or more of the criteria in paragraph (c)(2)(ii)(B) may alternatively meet the standard described in paragraph (c)(2)(i) of this section by providing other reliable and compelling evidence of the start-up entity's substantial potential for rapid growth and job creation.
units.action_summary: Applicants who partially meet re-parole criteria may alternatively provide other reliable and compelling evidence of the start-up's potential.

units.obligation_text: DHS may grant parole under this section in its sole discretion on a case-by-case basis if the Department determines, based on the totality of the evidence, that an applicant's presence in the United States will provide a significant public benefit and that he or she otherwise merits a favorable exercise of discretion.
units.action_summary: DHS has discretionary authority to grant parole on a case-by-case basis if it finds significant public benefit and favorable discretion.

units.obligation_text: DHS may grant an initial period of parole based on the start-up entity listed in the request for parole for a period of up to 2 years from the date the request is approved by USCIS. Approval by USCIS of such a request must be obtained before the alien may appear at a port of entry to be granted parole, in lieu of admission.
units.action_summary: DHS may grant initial parole for up to 2 years; USCIS approval must be obtained before the alien may appear at a port of entry to be granted parole.

units.obligation_text: DHS may re-parole an entrepreneur for one additional period of up to 3 years from the date of the expiration of the initial parole period. If the entrepreneur is in the United States at the time that USCIS approves the request for re-parole, such approval shall be considered a grant of re-parole. If the alien is outside the United States at the time that USCIS approves the request for re-parole, the alien must appear at a port of entry to be granted parole, in lieu of admission.
units.action_summary: DHS may re-parole for up to 3 years; if approval occurs outside the U.S., the alien must appear at a port of entry to be granted parole.

units.obligation_text: There is no appeal from a denial of parole under this section. USCIS will not consider a motion to reopen or reconsider a denial of parole under this section. On its own motion, USCIS may reopen or reconsider a decision to deny the Application for Entrepreneur Parole (Form I-941, or successor form), in accordance with 8 CFR 103.5(a)(5).
units.action_summary: Denials of parole are not appealable and USCIS will not consider motions to reopen or reconsider denials, though USCIS may on its own reopen or reconsider in accordance with 8 CFR 103.5(a)(5).

units.obligation_text: An alien seeking parole or re-parole under this section will be required to pay the biometric services fee as prescribed by 8 CFR 103.7(b)(1)(i)(C). An alien seeking an initial grant of parole will be required to submit biometric information. An alien seeking re-parole may be required to submit biometric information.
units.action_summary: Parole applicants must pay the biometric services fee; initial applicants must submit biometrics; re-parole applicants may be required to submit biometrics.
units.modal_raw: will be required / may be required

units.obligation_text: No more than three entrepreneurs may be granted parole under this section based on the same start-up entity.
