An alien shall not receive more than one initial grant of entrepreneur parole or more than one additional grant of entrepreneur re-parole based on the same start-up entity, for a maximum period of parole of five years.
units.action_summary: Limit: maximum three entrepreneurs per start-up may be granted parole; an alien may not receive more than one initial and one re-parole based on the same start-up (max five years).

units.obligation_text: An entrepreneur who is paroled into the United States pursuant to this section is authorized for employment with the start-up entity incident to the conditions of his or her parole.
units.action_summary: A parolee entrepreneur is authorized to be employed by the start-up entity consistent with parole conditions.

units.obligation_text: The entrepreneur's spouse and children who are seeking parole as derivatives of such entrepreneur must individually file an Application for Travel Document (Form I-131). Such application must also include evidence that the derivative has a qualifying relationship to the entrepreneur and otherwise merits a grant of parole in the exercise of discretion. A biometric services fee is required to be filed with the application. Such spouse or child will be required to appear for collection of biometrics in accordance with the form instructions or upon request.
units.actor: spouse and children seeking derivative parole
units.action_summary: Derivative spouse/children must file Form I-131 with evidence and pay the biometric fee, and must appear for biometric collection as instructed or upon request.
units.modal_raw: must / is required / will be required

units.obligation_text: The spouse and children of an entrepreneur granted parole under this section may be granted parole under this section for no longer than the period of parole granted to such entrepreneur.
units.actor: spouse and children of entrepreneur parolee
units.action_summary: Derivative family members may be granted parole only up to the length of the entrepreneur's parole period.

units.obligation_text: To request employment authorization, an eligible spouse paroled into the United States must file an Application for Employment Authorization (Form I-765, or successor form), in accordance with 8 CFR 274a.13 and form instructions. An Application for Employment Authorization must be accompanied by documentary evidence establishing eligibility, including evidence of the spousal relationship.
units.actor: eligible spouse paroled into the United States
units.action_summary: Eligible paroled spouses must file Form I-765 (with supporting documentary evidence) to request employment authorization.

units.obligation_text: Notwithstanding 8 CFR 274a.12(c)(11), a child of the entrepreneur parolee may not be authorized for and may not accept employment on the basis of parole under this section.
units.action_summary: Children of entrepreneur parolees are prohibited from being authorized for or accepting employment based on parole under this section.

units.obligation_text: As a condition of parole under this section, a parolee must maintain household income that is greater than 400 percent of the federal poverty line for his or her household size as defined by the Department of Health and Human Services. USCIS may impose other such reasonable conditions in its sole discretion with respect to any alien approved for parole under this section, and it may request verification of the parolee's compliance with any such condition at any time.
units.action_summary: Parolees must maintain household income >400% of the federal poverty line; USCIS may impose other conditions and verify compliance.

units.obligation_text: An alien granted parole under this section must immediately report any material change(s) to USCIS. If the entrepreneur will continue to be employed by the start-up entity and maintains at least a 10 percent ownership interest in the start-up entity, the entrepreneur must submit a new Application for Entrepreneur Parole (Form I-941, or successor form) with filing fee (not including any biometrics fees) and supporting documentary evidence to notify USCIS of the material change(s). The entrepreneur parolee must immediately notify USCIS in writing if he or she will no longer be employed by the start-up entity or ceases to possess at least a 10 percent ownership stake in the start-up entity.
units.action_summary: Parolees must immediately report material changes to USCIS; if continuing employment and ≥10% ownership, must submit new Form I-941 with filing fee and evidence; must notify USCIS in writing if they stop employment or fall below 10% ownership.

units.obligation_text: DHS may, in its discretion, terminate parole granted under this section at any time and without prior notice or opportunity to respond if it determines that the alien's continued parole in the United States no longer provides a significant public benefit. Alternatively DHS may, in its discretion, provide the alien notice and an opportunity to respond prior to terminating the alien's parole under this section.
units.action_summary: DHS may terminate parole at any time without notice if it finds the parole no longer provides significant public benefit, or DHS may give notice and an opportunity to respond.

units.obligation_text: Parole granted under this section will be automatically terminated without notice at the expiration of the time for which parole was authorized, unless the alien timely files a non-frivolous application for re-parole.
units.action_summary: Parole automatically ends at authorized expiration unless the alien timely files a non-frivolous re-parole application.
units.modal_raw: will be automatically terminated / unless ... files

units.obligation_text: Parole granted under this section may be automatically terminated when USCIS receives written notice from the entrepreneur parolee that he or she will no longer be employed by the start-up entity or ceases to possess at least a 10 percent ownership stake in the start-up entity in accordance with paragraph (j) of this section.
units.action_summary: Parole may be automatically terminated when USCIS receives written notice from the parolee that they will no longer be employed or no longer have ≥10% ownership.

units.obligation_text: Additionally, parole of the spouse or child of the entrepreneur will be automatically terminated without notice if the parole of the entrepreneur has been terminated.
units.actor: spouse or child of entrepreneur parolee
units.action_summary: Derivative parole terminates automatically without notice if the entrepreneur's parole is terminated.

units.obligation_text: USCIS may terminate on notice or provide the entrepreneur or his or her spouse or children, as applicable, written notice of its intent to terminate parole if USCIS believes that: (i) The facts or information contained in the request for parole were not true and accurate; (ii) The alien failed to timely file or otherwise comply with the material change reporting requirements in this section; (iii) The entrepreneur parolee is no longer employed in a central and active role by the start-up entity or ceases to possess at least a 10 percent ownership stake in the start-up entity; (iv) The alien otherwise violated the terms and conditions of parole; or (v) Parole was erroneously granted.
units.action_summary: USCIS may issue notice to terminate parole if it believes any listed grounds (false information, failure to report material changes, loss of central role or ≥10% ownership, violation of terms, or erroneous grant) exist.

units.obligation_text: A notice of intent to terminate issued under this paragraph should generally identify the grounds for termination of the parole and provide a period of up to 30 days for the alien's written rebuttal. The alien may submit additional evidence in support of his or her rebuttal, when applicable, and USCIS will consider all relevant evidence presented in deciding whether to terminate the alien's parole. Failure to timely respond to a notice of intent to terminate will result in termination of the parole. When a charging document is served on the alien, the charging document will constitute written notice of termination of parole (if parole has not already been terminated), unless otherwise specified. Any further immigration and removal actions will be conducted in accordance with the Act and this chapter. The decision to terminate parole may not be appealed. USCIS will not consider a motion to reopen or reconsider a decision to terminate parole under this section. On its own motion, USCIS may reopen or reconsider a decision to terminate.
units.action_summary: Notice of intent to terminate should identify grounds and generally allow up to 30 days for rebuttal; failure to respond results in termination; charging documents may constitute notice; termination decisions are not appealable and USCIS will not consider motions to reopen or reconsider those decisions, though USCIS may on its own reopen or reconsider.

units.obligation_text: The investment and revenue amounts in this section will be automatically adjusted every 3 years by the Consumer Price Index and posted on the USCIS Web site at www.uscis.gov. Investment and revenue amounts adjusted under this paragraph will apply to all applications filed on or after the beginning of the fiscal year for which the adjustment is made.
units.action_summary: Investment and revenue thresholds will be automatically adjusted every 3 years by CPI and posted on USCIS website; adjusted amounts apply to applications filed on or after the fiscal year start for the adjustment.

units.obligation_text: An entrepreneur who has timely filed a non-frivolous application requesting re-parole with respect to the same start-up entity in accordance with 8 CFR 212.19 prior to the expiration of his or her parole, but whose authorized parole period expires during the pendency of such application, is authorized to continue employment with the same start-up entity for a period not to exceed 240 days beginning on the date of expiration of parole. Such authorization shall be subject to any conditions and limitations on such expired parole. If DHS adjudicates the application prior to the expiration of this 240-day period and denies the application for re-parole, the employment authorization under this paragraph shall automatically terminate upon notification to the alien of the denial decision.
units.action_summary: If a timely non-frivolous re-parole application is pending when parole expires, the entrepreneur is authorized to continue employment with the same start-up for up to 240 days; that authorization is subject to prior parole conditions and will terminate automatically if DHS denies the re-parole and notifies the alien.

title: EB–5 Immigrant Investor Program Modernization

units.obligation_text: An EB–5 immigrant petition to classify an alien under section 203(b)(5) of the Act must be properly filed in accordance with the form instructions, with the appropriate fee(s), initial evidence, and any other supporting documentation.
units.action_summary: File the EB-5 immigrant petition properly, following form instructions and including required fees, initial evidence, and supporting documentation.

units.obligation_text: An alien may file a petition for classification as an investor on his or her own behalf.
units.action_summary: An alien is permitted to file an investor petition on his or her own behalf.

units.obligation_text: A priority date is not transferable to another alien.
units.action_summary: Prohibits transferring a petition's priority date to a different alien.

units.obligation_text: The priority date of an approved petition shall not be conferred to a subsequently filed petition if the alien was lawfully admitted to the United States for conditional residence under section 203(b)(5) of the Act based upon that approved petition or if at any time USCIS revokes the approval of the petition based on: (1) Fraud, or a willful misrepresentation of a material fact by the petitioner; or (2) A determination by USCIS that the petition approval was based on a material error.
units.action_summary: USCIS will not confer an approved petition's priority date to a later petition when the alien obtained conditional residence from the approved petition or if the petition is revoked for fraud, willful misrepresentation, or material error.

units.obligation_text: Unless otherwise specified, for EB–5 immigrant petitions filed on or after [INSERT EFFECTIVE DATE OF FINAL RULE], the amount of capital necessary to make a qualifying investment in the United States is one million eight hundred thousand United States dollars ($1,800,000).
units.action_summary: Establishes the standard minimum qualifying investment amount as $1,800,000 for applicable petitions.

units.obligation_text: Beginning on October 1, [INSERT YEAR FIVE YEARS AFTER EFFECTIVE DATE OF FINAL RULE], and every five years thereafter, this amount will automatically adjust for petitions filed on or after each adjustment’s effective date, based on the cumulative annual percentage change in the unadjusted All Items Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI–U) for the U.S. City Average reported by the Bureau of Labor Statistics for the previous five years.
units.actor: the qualifying investment amount / DHS (administrative adjustment)
units.action_summary: The standard investment amount will be periodically automatically adjusted every five years based on the cumulative CPI-U change for the prior five years.

units.obligation_text: The qualifying investment amount will be rounded down to the nearest hundred thousand.
units.action_summary: When adjustments are made, the investment amount is rounded down to the nearest $100,000.

units.obligation_text: DHS may update this figure by publication of a technical amendment in the Federal Register.
units.action_summary: DHS is permitted to update the investment amount via a technical amendment in the Federal Register.

units.obligation_text: Unless otherwise specified, for EB–5 immigrant petitions filed on or after [INSERT EFFECTIVE DATE OF FINAL RULE], the amount of capital necessary to make a qualifying investment in a targeted employment area in the United States is one million three hundred and fifty thousand United States dollars ($1,350,000).
units.actor: the investor (in a targeted employment area)
units.action_summary: Establishes the targeted employment area (TEA) minimum qualifying investment amount as $1,350,000 for applicable petitions.

units.obligation_text: Beginning on October 1, [INSERT DATE YEAR FIVE YEARS AFTER EFFECTIVE DATE OF FINAL RULE], and every five years thereafter, this amount will automatically adjust for petitions filed on or after each adjustment’s effective date, to be equal to 75 percent of the standard minimum investment amount described in paragraph (f)(1) of this section.
units.actor: the qualifying TEA investment amount / DHS adjustment process
units.action_summary: The TEA investment amount will automatically adjust every five years to equal 75% of the standard minimum investment amount.

units.obligation_text: DHS may update this figure by publication of a technical amendment in the Federal Register.
units.action_summary: DHS may update the TEA investment amount by technical amendment in the Federal Register.

units.obligation_text: Unless otherwise specified, for EB–5 immigrant petitions filed on or after [INSERT EFFECTIVE DATE OF FINAL RULE], the amount of capital necessary to make a qualifying investment in a high employment area in the United States is one million eight hundred thousand United States dollars ($1,800,000).
units.actor: the investor (in a high employment area)
units.action_summary: Establishes the high employment area minimum qualifying investment amount as $1,800,000 for applicable petitions.

units.obligation_text: Beginning on October 1, [INSERT DATE YEAR FIVE YEARS AFTER EFFECTIVE DATE OF FINAL RULE], and every five years thereafter, this amount will automatically adjust for petitions filed on or after each adjustment’s effective date, based on the cumulative annual percentage change in the unadjusted All Items Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI–U) for the U.S. City Average reported by the Bureau of Labor Statistics for the previous five years.
units.actor: the qualifying investment amount / DHS adjustment process
units.action_summary: The high employment area investment amount will automatically adjust every five years based on the cumulative CPI-U change over the prior five years.

units.obligation_text: The qualifying investment amount will be rounded down to the nearest hundred thousand.
units.action_summary: When adjustments are made for the high employment area amount, it will be rounded down to the nearest $100,000.

units.obligation_text: DHS may update this figure by publication of a technical amendment in the Federal Register.
units.action_summary: DHS may update the high employment area investment amount via a technical amendment.

units.obligation_text: The total number of full-time positions created for qualifying employees shall be allocated solely to those alien investors who have used the establishment of the new commercial enterprise as the basis for a petition.
units.action_summary: Full-time positions must be allocated only to alien investors who based a petition on establishment of the new commercial enterprise.

units.obligation_text: No allocation must be made among persons not seeking classification under section 203(b)(5) of the Act or among non-natural persons, either foreign or domestic.
units.action_summary: Prohibits allocating qualifying positions to persons not seeking EB-5 classification or to non-natural persons.

units.obligation_text: USCIS will recognize any reasonable agreement made among the alien investors in regard to the identification and allocation of such qualifying positions.
units.action_summary: USCIS will accept reasonable agreements among alien investors about how qualifying positions are identified and allocated.

units.obligation_text: USCIS may designate a particular geographic or political subdivision as an area of high unemployment (at least 150 percent of the national average rate).
units.action_summary: USCIS is permitted to designate specific geographic or political subdivisions as high unemployment areas for EB-5 purposes.

units.obligation_text: Such geographic or political subdivision must be composed of the census tract or contiguous census tracts in which the new commercial enterprise is principally doing business,
units.actor: the geographic or political subdivision (designation criteria)
units.action_summary: A subdivision designated as high unemployment must comprise the census tract(s) where the new commercial enterprise principally operates.

units.obligation_text: and may also include any or all census tracts contiguous to such census tract(s).
units.actor: the geographic or political subdivision (designation criteria)
units.action_summary: The designated subdivision may include contiguous census tracts in addition to the principal tract(s).

units.obligation_text: The weighted average of the unemployment rate for the subdivision, based on the labor force employment measure for each census tract, must be at least 150 percent of the national average unemployment rate.
units.actor: the geographic or political subdivision (designation criteria)
units.action_summary: To qualify as high unemployment, the subdivision's weighted average unemployment must be at least 150% of the national average.

units.obligation_text: Evidence of property transferred from abroad for use in the United States enterprise, including U.S. Customs and Border Protection commercial entry documents, bills of lading, and transit insurance policies containing ownership information and sufficient information to identify the property and to indicate the fair market value of such property;
units.action_summary: Petitioner must provide evidence of property transferred from abroad for use in the U.S. enterprise, including customs documents and other items evidencing ownership and value.

units.obligation_text: To show that the petitioner is or will be engaged in the new commercial enterprise, either through the exercise of day-to-day managerial control or through policy formulation, the petition must be accompanied by:
units.action_summary: Petitioner must include supporting evidence showing engagement in the new commercial enterprise (managerial control or policy formulation).

units.obligation_text: Evidence that the petitioner is engaged in policy making activities. For purposes of this section, a petitioner will be considered sufficiently engaged in policy making activities if the petitioner is an equity holder in the new commercial enterprise and the organizational documents of the new commercial enterprise provide the petitioner with certain rights, powers, and duties normally granted to equity holders of the new commercial enterprise’s type of entity in the jurisdiction in which the new commercial enterprise is organized.
units.action_summary: Defines evidence sufficient to show petitioner is engaged in policy making: equity holder status and organizational documents granting typical equity-holder rights.

units.obligation_text: (6) Evidence requirements related to whether the new commercial enterprise is in a rural area or a high unemployment area.
units.action_summary: Petitioner must provide evidence regarding whether the enterprise is located in a rural area or qualifies as a high unemployment area.

units.obligation_text: In the case of a rural area, evidence that the new commercial enterprise is principally doing business within a civil jurisdiction not located within any standard metropolitan statistical area as designated by the Office of Management and Budget, nor within any city or town having a population of 20,000 or more as based on the most recent decennial census of the United States;
units.action_summary: For rural area classification, petitioner must show the enterprise principally does business in a jurisdiction outside MSAs and outside cities/towns of 20,000+ population.

units.obligation_text: In the case of a high unemployment area: Evidence that the metropolitan statistical area, the specific county within a metropolitan statistical area, the county in which a city or town with a population of 20,000 or more is located, or the city or town with a population of 20,000 or more, in which the new commercial enterprise is principally doing business has experienced an average unemployment rate of at least 150 percent of the national average rate;
units.action_summary: To qualify as a high unemployment area, petitioner must provide evidence that the relevant MSA/county/city has an average unemployment rate of at least 150% of the national average.

units.obligation_text: A description of the boundaries of the geographic or political subdivision and the unemployment statistics in the area for which designation is sought as set forth in 8 CFR 204.6(i), and the reliable method or methods by which the unemployment statistics were obtained.
units.action_summary: For high unemployment designation, petitioner must submit boundary descriptions, unemployment statistics per §204.6(i), and reliable methods used to obtain the statistics.

units.obligation_text: The petitioner will be notified of the decision, and, if the petition is denied, of the reasons for the denial.
units.action_summary: USCIS must notify the petitioner of its decision and provide reasons if the petition is denied.

units.obligation_text: The petitioner has the right to appeal the denial to the Administrative Appeals Office in accordance with the provisions of part 103 of this chapter.
units.action_summary: Petitioner is permitted to appeal a denial to the Administrative Appeals Office under part 103.

units.obligation_text: A petition to remove the conditional basis of the permanent resident status of an investor accorded conditional permanent residence pursuant to section 203(b)(5) of the Act must be filed by the investor with the appropriate fee.
units.action_summary: Investor is required to file a petition to remove conditions and include the appropriate fee.

units.obligation_text: The investor must file within the 90-day period preceding the second anniversary of the date on which the investor acquired conditional permanent residence.
units.action_summary: Investor must file the removal petition within the 90-day period before the second anniversary of conditional residence.

units.obligation_text: Before the petition may be considered as properly filed, it must be accompanied by the fee required under 8 CFR 103.7(b)(1), and by documentation as described in paragraph (a)(4) of this section, and it must be properly signed by the investor.
units.action_summary: For the petition to be properly filed, investor must include required fee, specified documentation, and a proper signature.

units.obligation_text: Upon receipt of a properly filed petition, the investor’s conditional permanent resident status shall be extended automatically, if necessary, until such time as USCIS has adjudicated the petition.
units.action_summary: USCIS must automatically extend the investor's conditional status upon receipt of a properly filed petition until adjudication is complete.

units.obligation_text: The investor’s spouse and children may be included in the investor’s petition to remove conditions.
units.action_summary: Spouse and children are permitted to be included on the investor's petition to remove conditions.

units.obligation_text: Where the investor’s spouse and children are not included in the investor’s petition to remove conditions, the spouse and each child must each file his or her own petition to remove the conditions on their permanent resident status, unless the investor is deceased.
units.action_summary: If not included in the investor's petition, each spouse and child must file their own petition to remove conditions, unless the investor is deceased.

units.obligation_text: If the investor is deceased, the spouse and children may file separate petitions or may be included in one petition.
units.action_summary: If the investor is deceased, spouse and children may either file separately or be included together in one petition.

units.obligation_text: A child who reached the age of 21 or who married during the period of conditional permanent residence, or a former spouse who became divorced from the investor during the period of conditional permanent residence, may be included in the investor’s petition or must each file a separate petition.
units.actor: the child or former spouse described
units.action_summary: Such a child or former spouse may be included in the investor's petition or otherwise must file a separate petition.

units.obligation_text: Failure to properly file the petition to remove conditions within the 90-day period immediately preceding the second anniversary of the date on which the investor obtained lawful permanent residence on a conditional basis shall result in the automatic termination of the investor’s permanent resident status and the initiation of removal proceedings.
units.action_summary: If the investor fails to timely file, their permanent resident status will be automatically terminated and removal proceedings initiated.

units.obligation_text: USCIS shall send a written notice of termination and a notice to appear to an investor who fails to timely file a petition for removal of conditions.
units.action_summary: USCIS must send written notice of termination and a notice to appear to investors who fail to timely file.

units.obligation_text: No appeal shall lie from this decision;
units.action_summary: No appeal is permitted from the termination decision.

units.obligation_text: the investor may request a review of the determination during removal proceedings.
units.action_summary: Investor is permitted to request review of the termination determination during removal proceedings.

units.obligation_text: In proceedings, the burden of proof shall rest with the investor to show by a preponderance of the evidence that he or she complied with the requirement to file the petition within the designated period.
units.action_summary: In removal proceedings, the investor has the burden to prove timely filing by a preponderance of the evidence.

units.obligation_text: USCIS may deem the petition to have been filed prior to the second anniversary of the investor’s obtaining conditional permanent resident status and accept and consider a late petition if the investor demonstrates to USCIS’ satisfaction that failure to file a timely petition was for good cause and due to extenuating circumstances.
units.action_summary: USCIS may, upon satisfactory showing of good cause/extenuating circumstances, treat a late petition as timely and accept it.

units.obligation_text: If the late petition is filed prior to jurisdiction vesting with the immigration judge in proceedings and USCIS excuses the late filing and approves the petition, USCIS shall restore the investor’s permanent resident status, remove the conditional basis of such status, and cancel any outstanding notice to appear in accordance with 8 CFR 239.2.
units.action_summary: If USCIS excuses and approves a late petition before IJ jurisdiction, USCIS must restore status, remove conditions, and cancel any outstanding NTA.

units.obligation_text: If the petition is not filed until after jurisdiction vests with the immigration judge, the immigration judge may terminate the matter upon joint motion by the investor and DHS.
units.action_summary: If filed after IJ jurisdiction vests, the IJ may terminate the matter upon a joint motion by the investor and DHS.

units.obligation_text: If an investor dies during the prescribed 2-year period of conditional permanent residence, the spouse and children of the investor will be eligible for removal of conditions if it can be demonstrated that the conditions set forth in paragraph (a)(4) of this section have been met.
units.actor: the spouse and children of the deceased investor
units.action_summary: Spouse and children may be eligible to have conditions removed after investor death if they meet the conditions in paragraph (a)(4).

units.obligation_text: USCIS shall review the petition to remove conditions and the supporting documents to determine whether to waive the interview required by the Act.
units.action_summary: USCIS must review the petition and supporting documents to decide whether an interview may be waived.

units.obligation_text: If satisfied that the requirements set forth in paragraph (c)(1) of this section have been met, USCIS may waive the interview and approve the petition.
units.action_summary: USCIS may waive the interview and approve the petition if requirements in paragraph (c)(1) are met.

units.obligation_text: If not so satisfied, then USCIS may require that an interview of the investor be conducted.
units.action_summary: If USCIS is not satisfied the requirements are met, it may require the investor to appear for an interview.

units.obligation_text: Unless waived, an interview relating to the petition to remove conditions for investors shall be conducted by a USCIS immigration officer at the office that has jurisdiction over either the location of the investor’s commercial enterprise in the United States, the investor’s residence in the United States, or the location of the adjudication of the petition, at the agency’s discretion.
units.action_summary: If not waived, USCIS must conduct the interview at the office with jurisdiction over the enterprise location, the investor's residence, or the adjudication location.

units.obligation_text: If the investor fails to appear for an interview in connection with the petition when requested by USCIS, the investor’s permanent resident status will be automatically terminated as of the second anniversary of the date on which the investor obtained permanent residence.
units.action_summary: If investor fails to appear for a requested interview, their permanent resident status will be automatically terminated as of the second anniversary of conditional residence.

units.obligation_text: The investor will be provided with written notification of the termination and the reasons therefore, and a notice to appear shall be issued placing the investor in removal proceedings.
units.action_summary: USCIS must provide written notice of termination and issue a notice to appear initiating removal proceedings.

units.obligation_text: The investor may seek review of the decision to terminate his or her status in such proceedings,
units.action_summary: Investor is permitted to seek review of termination in removal proceedings.

units.obligation_text: but the burden shall be on the investor to establish by a preponderance of the evidence that he or she complied with the interview requirements.
units.action_summary: In seeking review, the investor has the burden to prove compliance with interview requirements by a preponderance of the evidence.

units.obligation_text: If the investor has failed to appear for a scheduled interview, he or she may submit a written request to USCIS asking that the interview be rescheduled or that the interview be waived.
units.action_summary: Investor who failed to appear may request that USCIS reschedule or waive the interview by submitting a written request.

units.obligation_text: That request should explain his or her failure to appear for the scheduled interview, and if a request for waiver of the interview, the reasons such waiver should be granted.
units.action_summary: The investor's written request for rescheduling or waiver should explain the reasons for failing to appear or for granting a waiver.

units.obligation_text: If USCIS determines that there is good cause for granting the request, the interview may be rescheduled or waived, as appropriate.
units.action_summary: If USCIS finds good cause, it may reschedule or waive the interview.

units.obligation_text: If USCIS waives the interview, USCIS shall restore the investor’s conditional permanent resident status, cancel any outstanding notice to appear in accordance with 8 CFR 239.2, and proceed to adjudicate the investor’s petition.
units.action_summary: If USCIS waives the interview, it must restore conditional status, cancel any outstanding NTA, and adjudicate the petition.

units.obligation_text: If USCIS reschedules that investor’s interview, he or she shall restore the investor’s conditional permanent resident status, and cancel any outstanding notice to appear cause in accordance with 8 CFR 239.2.
units.action_summary: If USCIS reschedules the interview, it must restore the investor's conditional status and cancel any outstanding NTA (text as drafted).

units.obligation_text: If derogatory information is determined regarding any of these issues or it becomes known to the government that the investor obtained his or her investment funds through other than legal means, USCIS shall offer the investor the opportunity to rebut such information.
units.action_summary: If derogatory information or evidence of illegally obtained funds is found, USCIS must offer the investor an opportunity to rebut it.

units.obligation_text: If the investor fails to overcome such derogatory information or evidence that the investment funds were obtained through other than legal means, USCIS may deny the petition, terminate the investor’s permanent resident status, and issue a notice to appear.
units.action_summary: If investor cannot rebut derogatory information or illegal-funds evidence, USCIS may deny the petition, terminate status, and issue an NTA.

units.obligation_text: If derogatory information not relating to any of these issues is determined during the course of the interview, such information shall be forwarded to the investigations unit for appropriate action.
units.action_summary: USCIS must forward other derogatory information found during the interview to the investigations unit for action.

units.obligation_text: If no unresolved derogatory information is determined relating to these issues, the petition shall be approved and the conditional basis of the investor’s permanent resident status removed, regardless of any action taken or contemplated regarding other possible grounds for removal.
units.action_summary: If no unresolved derogatory information exists on relevant issues, USCIS must approve the petition and remove the conditional basis of status.

units.obligation_text: If, after initial review or after the interview, USCIS approves the petition, USCIS will remove the conditional basis of the investor’s permanent resident status as of the second anniversary of the date on which the investor acquired conditional permanent residence.
units.action_summary: Upon approval, USCIS will remove the conditional basis of the investor's permanent resident status as of the second anniversary.

units.obligation_text: USCIS shall provide written notice of the decision to the investor.
units.action_summary: USCIS must provide written notice to the investor of its approval decision.

units.obligation_text: USCIS may request the investor and derivative family members to appear for biometrics at a USCIS facility for processing for a new Permanent Resident Card.
units.action_summary: USCIS may require biometrics appointments for the investor and derivatives to process a new Permanent Resident Card.

units.obligation_text: If, after initial review or after the interview, USCIS denies the petition, USCIS will provide written notice to the investor of the decision and the reason(s) therefore, and shall issue a notice to appear.
units.action_summary: If denied, USCIS must provide written notice explaining the denial and issue an NTA.

units.obligation_text: The investor’s lawful permanent resident status and that of his or her spouse and any children shall be terminated as of the date of USCIS’ written decision.
units.action_summary: Upon denial, the lawful permanent resident status of the investor and eligible derivatives will be terminated as of the date of USCIS's decision.

units.obligation_text: The investor shall also be instructed to surrender any Permanent Resident Card previously issued by USCIS.
units.action_summary: USCIS must instruct the investor to surrender any previously issued Permanent Resident Card.

units.obligation_text: No appeal shall lie from this decision;
units.action_summary: No appeal is allowed from the denial decision.

units.obligation_text: the investor may seek review of the decision in removal proceedings.
units.action_summary: Investor is permitted to seek review of the denial in removal proceedings.

units.obligation_text: In proceedings, the burden shall rest with USCIS to establish by a preponderance of the evidence that the facts and information in the investor’s petition for removal of conditions are not true and that the petition was properly denied.
units.action_summary: In removal proceedings challenging denial, USCIS has the burden to prove by a preponderance of the evidence that the petition's facts are untrue and denial was proper.

title: Registration Requirement for Petitioners Seeking to File H-1B Petitions on Behalf of Aliens Subject to the Numerical Limitations

units.obligation_text: A petition filed under section 101(a)(15)(H) of the Act may not be filed earlier than 6 months before the date of actual need for the beneficiary’s services or training.
units.action_summary: A petition cannot be filed earlier than 6 months before the beneficiary's actual need date.

units.obligation_text: Except as provided in paragraph (h)(8)(iv) of this section, before a petitioner can file an H–1B cap-subject petition for a beneficiary ... the petitioner must register to file a petition on behalf of an alien beneficiary electronically through the USCIS website (www.uscis.gov).
units.action_summary: Before filing an H-1B cap-subject petition, the petitioner must register electronically through USCIS for that beneficiary (unless paragraph (h)(8)(iv) applies).

units.obligation_text: To be eligible to file a petition for a beneficiary who may be counted against the H–1B regular cap or the H–1B advanced degree exemption for a particular fiscal year, a registration must be properly submitted in accordance with 8 CFR 103.2(a)(1), paragraph (h)(8)(iii) of this section, and the form instructions.
units.action_summary: Registrations must be properly submitted in accordance with 8 CFR 103.2(a)(1), paragraph (h)(8)(iii), and form instructions to be eligible to file.

units.obligation_text: A petitioner may file an H–1B cap-subject petition on behalf of a registered beneficiary only after the petitioner’s registration for that beneficiary has been selected for that fiscal year.
units.action_summary: Petitioners may file for a registered beneficiary only after that beneficiary's registration has been selected.

units.obligation_text: A petitioner must electronically submit a separate registration to file a petition for each beneficiary it seeks to register, and each beneficiary must be named.
units.action_summary: Petitioners must submit a separate electronic registration for each beneficiary and must name each beneficiary.

units.obligation_text: each beneficiary must be named.
units.action_summary: Every registration must include the named beneficiary.

units.obligation_text: A petitioner may only submit one registration per beneficiary in any fiscal year.
units.action_summary: Petitioners are limited to one registration per beneficiary per fiscal year.

units.obligation_text: If a petitioner submits more than one registration per beneficiary in the same fiscal year, all registrations filed by that petitioner relating to that beneficiary for that fiscal year will be considered invalid.
units.action_summary: If multiple registrations are submitted for the same beneficiary by the same petitioner in one fiscal year, USCIS will consider all such registrations invalid.

units.obligation_text: The annual initial registration period will last a minimum of 14 calendar days and will start at least 14 calendar days before the earliest date on which H–1B cap-subject petitions may be filed for a particular fiscal year, consistent with paragraph (h)(2)(i)(I) of this section.
units.action_summary: The initial registration period must last at least 14 days and start at least 14 days before the earliest filing date.

units.obligation_text: USCIS will announce the start and end dates of the initial registration period on the USCIS website at www.uscis.gov for each fiscal year.
units.action_summary: USCIS will publish the registration period start and end dates on its website each fiscal year.

units.obligation_text: A petitioner may submit a registration during the initial registration period only if the requested start date for the beneficiary is the first business day for the applicable fiscal year.
units.action_summary: During the initial registration period, petitioners may submit a registration only when the requested start date is the first business day of the fiscal year.

units.obligation_text: If USCIS keeps the registration period open beyond the initial registration period, or determines that it is necessary to re-open the registration period, a petitioner may submit a registration with a requested start date after the first business day for the applicable fiscal year, as long as the date of registration is no more than 6 months before the requested start date.
units.action_summary: If USCIS extends or reopens registration, petitioners may request start dates after the first business day provided the registration date is within 6 months before the requested start date.

units.obligation_text: In determining whether there are enough registrations to meet the H–1B regular cap, USCIS will consider all properly submitted registrations relating to beneficiaries that may be counted under section 214(g)(1)(A) of the Act, including those that may also be counted under section 214(g)(5)(C) of the Act.
units.action_summary: USCIS will consider all properly submitted registrations that may be counted toward the regular cap (including those overlapping the advanced degree exemption) when determining if the regular cap is met.

units.obligation_text: At the end of the annual initial registration period, if USCIS determines that it has received fewer registrations than needed to meet the H–1B regular cap, USCIS will notify all petitioners that have properly registered that their registrations have been selected.
units.action_summary: If registrations are fewer than needed, USCIS will notify all properly registered petitioners that their registrations are selected.

units.obligation_text: USCIS will keep the registration period open beyond the initial registration period, until it determines that it has received a sufficient number of registrations to meet the H–1B regular cap.
units.action_summary: USCIS will keep registration open past the initial period until enough registrations are received to meet the regular cap.

units.obligation_text: Once USCIS has received a sufficient number of registrations to meet the H–1B regular cap, USCIS will no longer accept registrations for petitions subject to the H–1B regular cap under section 214(g)(1)(A).
units.action_summary: When enough registrations are received, USCIS will stop accepting further registrations subject to the regular cap.

units.obligation_text: USCIS will monitor the number of registrations received and will notify the public of the date that USCIS has received the necessary number of registrations (the "final registration date").
units.action_summary: USCIS will track registrations and publish the date it received the necessary number (the final registration date).

units.obligation_text: When necessary to ensure the fair and orderly allocation of numbers under Section 214(g)(1)(A) of the Act, USCIS may randomly select the remaining number of registrations deemed necessary to meet the H–1B regular cap from among the registrations received on the final registration date. This random selection will be made via computer-generated selection.
units.action_summary: If needed for fairness, USCIS may randomly select registrations received on the final registration date using a computer-generated selection process.

units.obligation_text: At the end of the initial registration period, if USCIS determines that it has received more than sufficient registrations to meet the H–1B regular cap, USCIS will no longer accept registrations under section 214(g)(1)(A) of the Act and will notify the public of the final registration date.
units.action_summary: If registrations exceed the cap during the initial period, USCIS will stop accepting registrations and announce the final registration date.

units.obligation_text: USCIS will randomly select from among the registrations properly submitted during the initial registration period the number of registrations deemed necessary to meet the H–1B regular cap. This random selection will be made via computer-generated selection.
units.action_summary: USCIS will use a computer-generated random selection among registrations submitted during the initial period to choose the number needed to meet the cap.

units.obligation_text: After USCIS has determined it will no longer accept registrations under section 214(g)(1)(A) of the Act, USCIS will determine whether there is a sufficient number of remaining registrations to meet the H–1B advanced degree exemption.
units.action_summary: Once regular-cap registrations are closed, USCIS will assess whether remaining registrations suffice to meet the advanced degree exemption.

units.obligation_text: If USCIS determines that it has received fewer registrations than needed to meet the H–1B advanced degree exemption numerical limitation, USCIS will notify all petitioners that have properly registered that their registrations have been selected.
units.action_summary: If remaining registrations are fewer than needed for the advanced degree exemption, USCIS will notify properly registered petitioners that their registrations are selected.

units.obligation_text: USCIS will continue to accept registrations to file petitions that may be counted toward the H–1B advanced degree exemption numerical limitation ... until USCIS determines that it has received enough registrations to meet the H–1B advanced degree exemption numerical limitation.
units.action_summary: USCIS will keep accepting registrations that may count toward the advanced degree exemption until enough are received.

units.obligation_text: USCIS will monitor the number of registrations received and will notify the public of the date that USCIS has received the necessary number of registrations (the "final registration date").
units.action_summary: USCIS will track registrations and announce the final registration date for the advanced degree exemption when the necessary number is received.

units.obligation_text: When necessary to ensure the fair and orderly allocation of numbers under Section 214(g)(1)(A) of the Act, USCIS may randomly select the remaining number of registrations deemed necessary to meet the H–1B advanced degree exemption numerical limitation from among the registrations properly submitted on the final registration date. This random selection will be made via computer-generated selection.
units.action_summary: USCIS may randomly select registrations submitted on the final registration date for the advanced degree exemption using computer-generated selection.

units.obligation_text: If USCIS determines that it has received more than enough registrations to meet the H–1B advanced degree exemption numerical limitation, USCIS will no longer accept registrations that may be counted under section 214(g)(5)(C) of the Act and will notify the public of the final registration date.
units.action_summary: If registrations exceed the advanced degree exemption, USCIS will stop accepting registrations that may be counted under the exemption and will announce the final registration date.

units.obligation_text: USCIS will randomly select the number of registrations needed to meet the H–1B advanced degree exemption numerical limitation from among the remaining registrations that may be counted against the advanced degree exemption numerical limitation. This random selection will be made via computer-generated selection.
units.action_summary: USCIS will use a computer-generated random selection among remaining registrations that may count for the advanced degree exemption to choose the needed number.

units.obligation_text: Unselected registrations will remain on reserve for the applicable fiscal year.
units.action_summary: Registrations not selected initially will be kept on reserve for that fiscal year.

units.obligation_text: If USCIS determines that it needs to increase the number of registrations projected to meet the H–1B regular cap or advanced degree exemption allocation, and select additional registrations, USCIS will select from among the registrations that are on reserve a sufficient number to meet the H–1B regular cap or advanced degree exemption numerical limitation, as applicable.
units.action_summary: If more registrations are needed to meet allocations, USCIS will select additional registrations from the reserve to meet the numerical limits.

units.obligation_text: If all of the registrations on reserve are selected and there are still fewer registrations than needed to meet the H–1B regular cap or advanced degree exemption numerical limitation, as applicable, USCIS may reopen the applicable registration period until USCIS determines that it has received a sufficient number of registrations projected as needed to meet the H–1B regular cap or advanced degree exemption numerical limitation.
units.action_summary: If reserve registrations are exhausted and more are needed, USCIS may reopen the registration period until enough registrations are received.

units.obligation_text: USCIS will monitor the number of registrations received and will notify the public of the date that USCIS has received the necessary number of registrations (the new "final registration date").
units.action_summary: USCIS will continuously monitor registrations and announce the new final registration date when enough are received.

units.obligation_text: When necessary to ensure the fair and orderly allocation of numbers, USCIS may randomly select the remaining number of registrations deemed necessary to meet the H–1B regular cap or advanced degree exemption numerical limitation from among the registrations properly submitted on the final registration date.
units.action_summary: USCIS may use a random selection among registrations submitted on the final registration date to allocate remaining numbers.

units.obligation_text: If the registration period will be re-opened, USCIS will announce the start of the re-opened registration period on the USCIS website at www.uscis.gov.
units.action_summary: USCIS will announce the start date of any reopened registration period on its website.

units.obligation_text: Petitioners will receive electronic notification that USCIS has accepted a registration for processing.
units.action_summary: USCIS will send petitioners electronic confirmation when a registration is accepted for processing.

units.obligation_text: USCIS will notify all petitioners with selected registrations that the petitioner is eligible to file an H–1B cap-subject petition on behalf of the beneficiary named in the notice within the filing period indicated on the notice.
units.action_summary: USCIS will notify petitioners whose registrations are selected that they are eligible to file for the named beneficiary within the specified filing period.

units.obligation_text: the petitioner is eligible to file an H–1B cap-subject petition on behalf of the beneficiary named in the notice within the filing period indicated on the notice.
units.action_summary: A petitioner whose registration is selected may file an H-1B cap-subject petition for the named beneficiary during the filing period indicated on the notice.

units.obligation_text: In addition to any other applicable requirements, a petitioner may file an H–1B petition for a beneficiary that may be counted under section 214(g)(1)(A) or section 214(g)(5)(C) of the Act only if the petitioner’s registration to file a petition on behalf of the beneficiary named in the petition was selected beforehand by USCIS and only within the filing period indicated on the notice.
units.action_summary: Petitioners may file an H-1B petition only if the beneficiary's registration was previously selected by USCIS and only during the filing period indicated.

units.obligation_text: the petitioner’s registration to file a petition on behalf of the beneficiary named in the petition was selected beforehand by USCIS
units.action_summary: A condition for filing is that the petitioner's registration for the beneficiary was selected in advance.

units.obligation_text: only within the filing period indicated on the notice
units.action_summary: Filing is permitted only during the filing period shown on the selection notice.

units.obligation_text: A petitioner may not substitute the beneficiary named in the original registration or transfer the registration to another petitioner.
units.action_summary: Petitioners are prohibited from substituting the named beneficiary or transferring the registration to another petitioner.

units.obligation_text: If a petitioner files an H–1B cap-subject petition based on a registration that was not selected beforehand by USCIS, or based on a registration for a different beneficiary than the beneficiary named in the petition, the H–1B cap-subject petition will be denied or rejected.
units.action_summary: USCIS will deny or reject H-1B cap-subject petitions filed based on an unselected registration or a registration for a different beneficiary.

units.obligation_text: An H–1B cap-subject petition must be properly filed within the filing period indicated on the relevant selection notice.
units.action_summary: Petitioners must properly file the H-1B cap-subject petition within the filing period shown on the selection notice.

units.obligation_text: The filing period for filing the H–1B cap-subject petition will be at least 60 days.
units.action_summary: The filing period will be no less than 60 days.

units.obligation_text: If petitioners do not meet these requirements, USCIS will deny or reject the H–1B cap-subject petition.
units.action_summary: USCIS will deny or reject petitions that do not meet the filing requirements.

units.obligation_text: When calculating the number of registrations needed to meet the H–1B regular cap and the H–1B advanced degree exemption numerical limitation for a given fiscal year, USCIS will take into account historical data related to approvals, denials, revocations, and other relevant factors.
units.action_summary: USCIS will consider historical approvals, denials, revocations, and other factors when computing the number of registrations needed.

units.obligation_text: If necessary, USCIS may increase those numbers throughout the fiscal year.
units.action_summary: USCIS may increase the projected numbers throughout the fiscal year if needed.

units.obligation_text: USCIS may suspend the H–1B registration requirement, in its discretion, if it determines that the registration process is inoperable for any reason.
units.action_summary: USCIS has discretion to suspend the H-1B registration requirement if the registration process is inoperable.

units.obligation_text: If USCIS suspends the registration requirement, USCIS will make an announcement of the suspension on its website (http://www.uscis.gov) along with the opening date of the applicable H–1B cap-subject petition-filing period.
units.action_summary: If USCIS suspends registration, it will announce the suspension and the opening date of the petition-filing period on its website.

units.obligation_text: In any year in which USCIS suspends the H–1B registration process for cap-subject petitions, USCIS will allow for the submission of H–1B petitions notwithstanding paragraph (h)(8)(iii) of this section and conduct a cap-subject selection process based on the petitions that are received.
units.action_summary: If registration is suspended, USCIS will accept H-1B petitions and conduct a selection process based on received petitions.

units.obligation_text: USCIS will deny petitions indicating that they are exempt from the H–1B regular cap and the H–1B advanced degree exemption if USCIS determines that they are subject to either the H–1B regular cap or H–1B advanced degree exemption, unless the petition can still be counted under the H–1B regular cap or advanced degree exemption at the time of determination.
units.action_summary: USCIS will deny petitions labeled as exempt if it later determines they are subject to the cap, unless they still qualify at the time of determination.

units.obligation_text: If a petition is denied under this paragraph (h)(8)(iv)(B), USCIS will not return or refund filing fees.
units.action_summary: USCIS will not return or refund filing fees for petitions denied under this suspended-registration provision.

units.obligation_text: In determining whether there are enough H–1B cap-subject petitions to meet the H–1B regular cap, USCIS will consider all petitions properly submitted in accordance with 8 CFR 103.2 relating to beneficiaries that may be counted under section 214(g)(1)(A) of the Act, including those that may also be counted under section 214(g)(5)(C) of the Act.
units.action_summary: When registration is suspended, USCIS will consider all properly submitted petitions that may be counted toward the regular cap (including those overlapping the advanced degree exemption) to determine if the cap is met.

units.obligation_text: When calculating the number of petitions needed to meet the H–1B regular cap USCIS will take into account historical data related to approvals, denials, revocations, and other relevant factors.
units.action_summary: USCIS will use historical data and other relevant factors to calculate the number of petitions needed to meet the regular cap when the registration process is suspended.

units.obligation_text: USCIS will monitor the number of petitions received and will announce on its website the date that it receives the number of petitions projected as needed to meet the H–1B regular cap (the "final receipt date").
units.action_summary: USCIS will track petition receipts and announce the final receipt date on its website when it receives the projected number of petitions needed for the regular cap.

units.obligation_text: When necessary to ensure the fair and orderly allocation of numbers under the H–1B regular cap, USCIS may randomly select via computer-generated selection the remaining number of petitions deemed necessary to meet the H–1B regular cap from among the petitions properly submitted on the final receipt date.
units.action_summary: If needed, USCIS may use a computer-generated random selection among petitions submitted on the final receipt date to allocate the remaining regular cap numbers.

units.obligation_text: If the final receipt date is any of the first five business days on which petitions subject to the H–1B regular cap may be received (i.e., if the cap is reached on any one of the first five business days that filings can be made), USCIS will randomly select from among all the petitions properly submitted during the first five business days the number of petitions deemed necessary to meet the H–1B regular cap.
units.action_summary: If the cap is reached on one of the first five business days, USCIS will randomly select needed petitions from all petitions properly submitted during those first five business days.

units.obligation_text: After any random selection under this paragraph (h)(8)(iv)(B)(1), petitions that are subject to the H–1B regular cap and that do not qualify for the H–1B advanced degree exemption will be rejected if they are not randomly selected or were received after the final receipt date.
units.action_summary: USCIS will reject petitions subject to the regular cap (and not qualifying for the advanced degree exemption) if they were not selected in the random draw or were received after the final receipt date.

units.obligation_text: After USCIS has received a sufficient number of petitions to meet the H–1B regular cap and, as applicable, completed the random selection process of petitions for the H–1B regular cap, USCIS will determine whether there is a sufficient number of remaining petitions to meet the H–1B advanced degree exemption numerical limitation.
units.action_summary: Once the regular cap process is complete, USCIS will assess whether remaining petitions suffice to meet the advanced degree exemption.

units.obligation_text: When calculating the number of petitions needed to meet the H–1B advanced degree exemption numerical limitation USCIS will take into account historical data related to approvals, denials, revocations, and other relevant factors.
units.action_summary: USCIS will use historical data and other factors to calculate the number of petitions needed for the advanced degree exemption under a suspended-registration process.

units.obligation_text: USCIS will monitor the number of petitions received and will announce on its website the date that it receives the number of petitions projected as needed to meet the H–1B advanced degree exemption numerical limitation (the "final receipt date").
units.action_summary: USCIS will track petitions and publish the final receipt date for the advanced degree exemption on its website when the projected number is received.

units.obligation_text: When necessary to ensure the fair and orderly allocation of numbers under the H–1B advanced degree exemption, USCIS may randomly select via computer-generated selection the remaining number of petitions deemed necessary to meet the H–1B advanced degree exemption numerical limitation from among the petitions properly submitted on the final receipt date.
units.action_summary: USCIS may randomly select petitions submitted on the final receipt date for the advanced degree exemption using a computer-generated process when needed.

units.obligation_text: If the final receipt date is any of the first five business days on which petitions subject to the H–1B advanced degree exemption may be received (i.e., if the numerical limitation is reached on any one of the first five business days that filings can be made), USCIS will randomly select from among all the petitions properly submitted during the first five business days the number of petitions deemed necessary to meet the H–1B advanced degree exemption numerical limitation.
units.action_summary: If the advanced degree exemption limit is reached on one of the first five business days, USCIS will randomly select needed petitions from all properly submitted during those five days.

units.obligation_text: After any random selection under this paragraph (h)(8)(iv)(B)(2), petitions that are not randomly selected or that were received after the final receipt date will be rejected.
units.action_summary: USCIS will reject petitions not selected in the random draw or received after the final receipt date for the advanced degree exemption.

units.obligation_text: When calculating the numerical limitations under section 214(g)(1)(B) and 214(g)(10) of the Act for a given fiscal year, USCIS will make numbers available to petitions in the order in which the petitions are filed.
units.action_summary: For H-2B numerical limits, USCIS will allocate numbers to petitions in filing order.

units.obligation_text: USCIS will make projections of the number of petitions necessary to achieve the numerical limit of approvals, taking into account historical data related to approvals, denials, revocations, and other relevant factors.
units.action_summary: USCIS will project how many petitions are needed to reach the numerical limits, using historical and other relevant data.

units.obligation_text: USCIS will monitor the number of petitions (including the number of beneficiaries requested when necessary) received and will notify the public of the date that USCIS has received the necessary number of petitions (the "final receipt date").
units.action_summary: USCIS will track petition receipts (and beneficiaries when needed) and announce the final receipt date once the necessary number is received.

units.obligation_text: When necessary to ensure the fair and orderly allocation of numbers subject to the numerical limitations in 214(g)(1)(B) and 214(g)(10) of the Act, USCIS may randomly select from among the petitions received on the final receipt date the remaining number of petitions deemed necessary to generate the numerical limit of approvals. This random selection will be made via computer-generated selection.
units.action_summary: If needed to fairly allocate H-2B numbers, USCIS may randomly select petitions received on the final receipt date using computer-generated selection.

units.obligation_text: Petitions subject to a numerical limitation not randomly selected or that were received after the final receipt date will be rejected.
units.action_summary: USCIS will reject petitions subject to numerical limits that are not selected or that arrive after the final receipt date.

units.obligation_text: Petitions indicating that they are exempt from the numerical limitation but that are determined by USCIS after the final receipt date to be subject to the numerical limit will be denied and filing fees will not be returned or refunded.
units.action_summary: If a petition claims exemption but is later found subject to the numerical limit after the final receipt date, USCIS will deny it and will not refund filing fees.
units.modal_raw: will be denied; will not be returned or refunded

units.obligation_text: If the final receipt date is any of the first five business days on which petitions subject to the applicable numerical limit may be received (i.e., if the numerical limit is reached on any one of the first five business days that filings can be made), USCIS will randomly apply all of the numbers among the petitions received on any of those five business days.
units.action_summary: If the numerical limit is reached on one of the first five business days, USCIS will distribute numbers by random selection among petitions received during those first five days.

units.obligation_text: USCIS will consider all the evidence submitted and any other evidence independently required to assist in adjudication.
units.action_summary: USCIS will review all submitted and any other independently required evidence to assist adjudication.

units.obligation_text: USCIS will notify the petitioner of the approval of the petition on a Notice of Action.
units.action_summary: USCIS will send the petitioner a Notice of Action when a petition is approved.

units.obligation_text: The approval notice will include the beneficiary’s (or beneficiaries’) name(s) and classification and the petition’s period of validity.
units.action_summary: The approval notice must state the beneficiary's name(s), classification, and the petition's validity period.

units.obligation_text: A petition for more than one beneficiary and/or multiple services may be approved in whole or in part.
units.action_summary: USCIS may approve petitions covering multiple beneficiaries or services either fully or partially.

title: Removal of International Entrepreneur Parole Program

units.actor: an employer (or person verifying identity and employment authorization)
units.action_summary: Accept a foreign passport together with Form I-94/I-94A bearing the same name and a valid endorsement as evidence of identity and employment authorization, provided the endorsement is unexpired and the employment is not in conflict with the endorsement or its restrictions.

units.obligation_text: The following classes of nonimmigrant aliens are authorized to be employed in the United States by the specific employer and subject to the restrictions described in the section(s) of this chapter indicated as a condition of their admission in, or subsequent change to, such classification.

units.obligation_text: An alien paroled into the United States temporarily for urgent humanitarian reasons or significant public benefit pursuant to section 212(d)(5) of the Act.

units.action_summary: Specifies that aliens paroled under section 212(d)(5) for urgent humanitarian reasons or significant public benefit are included among classes authorized to accept employment.

title: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services Fee Schedule and Changes to Certain Other Immigration Benefit Request Requirements

units.obligation_text: Filing fees generally are non-refundable regardless of if the benefit request is approved or denied, or how much time the adjudication requires.
units.action_summary: Applicants/payors are not entitled to refunds of filing fees in general.

units.obligation_text: Except as otherwise provided in this chapter I, fees must be paid when the benefit request is filed.
units.action_summary: Applicants/payors must submit required fees at the time of filing the benefit request.

units.obligation_text: Submitted with the correct fee(s).
units.action_summary: Benefit requests must be submitted with the correct fee(s).

units.obligation_text: If a check or other financial instrument used to pay a fee is returned as unpayable because of insufficient funds, USCIS will resubmit the payment to the remitter institution one time.
units.action_summary: USCIS will attempt to redeposit a returned payment once if returned for insufficient funds.

units.obligation_text: If the instrument used to pay a fee is returned as unpayable a second time, the filing may be rejected.
units.action_summary: USCIS may reject the filing if the payment instrument is returned unpaid a second time.

units.obligation_text: Financial instruments returned as unpayable for a reason other than insufficient funds will not be redeposited.
units.action_summary: USCIS will not redeposit payments returned for reasons other than insufficient funds.

units.obligation_text: If a check or other financial instrument used to pay a fee is dated more than one year before the request is received, the payment and request may be rejected.
units.action_summary: USCIS may reject the payment and the benefit request if payment instrument is over one year old.

units.obligation_text: USCIS will send secure identification documents, such as a Permanent Resident Card or Employment Authorization Document, only to the applicant or self-petitioner unless the applicant or self-petitioner specifically consents to having his or her secure identification document sent to a designated agent, their attorney or accredited representative or record, as specified on the form instructions.
units.action_summary: USCIS will deliver secure ID documents only to the applicant/self-petitioner unless that person consents to alternate designated recipients.

units.obligation_text: The designated agent, or attorney or accredited representative, will be required to provide identification and sign for receipt of the secure document.
units.action_summary: Designated agents or representatives must provide ID and sign when receiving secure documents on behalf of an applicant.

units.obligation_text: USCIS may accept DOJ fees.
units.action_summary: USCIS is permitted to accept fees payable to the Department of Justice under certain conditions.

units.obligation_text: Except as provided in 8 CFR 1003.8, or as the Attorney General otherwise may provide by regulation, any fee relating to any EOIR proceeding may be paid to USCIS.
units.action_summary: Payers may pay EOIR-related fees to USCIS except as otherwise provided.

units.obligation_text: Payment of a fee under this section does not constitute filing of the document with the Board or with the immigration court.
units.action_summary: Paying a fee to USCIS for EOIR proceedings does not mean the associated document has been filed with EOIR.

units.obligation_text: DHS will provide the payer with a receipt for a fee and return any documents submitted with the fee relating to any immigration court proceeding.
units.action_summary: DHS/USCIS will give a receipt and return documents submitted with payment for immigration court proceedings.

units.obligation_text: Fees paid to and accepted by DHS relating to any immigration proceeding as provided in 8 CFR 1103.7(a)(3) must include an additional $30 for DHS to collect, store, and use biometric information.
units.action_summary: Payers must add $30 to specified fees to cover DHS biometric collection and storage costs.

units.obligation_text: An immigration judge or the Board may waive any fees prescribed under this chapter for cases under their jurisdiction to the extent provided in 8 CFR 1003.8 and 1003.24.
units.action_summary: Immigration judges or the Board are permitted to waive prescribed fees under specified authorities.

units.obligation_text: USCIS fees will be required as provided in 8 CFR part 106.
units.action_summary: Applicants/payors must pay USCIS fees as laid out in 8 CFR part 106.

units.obligation_text: Remittances to the Board of Immigration Appeals must be made payable to the "United States Department of Justice," in accordance with 8 CFR 1003.8.
units.action_summary: Payments to the Board of Immigration Appeals must be made payable to the U.S. Department of Justice as specified.

units.obligation_text: The fee is due after approval of the application but before use of the DCL.
units.action_summary: Approved DCL participants must pay the DCL system cost fee after approval but before using the lane.

units.obligation_text: DCL System Costs Fee. For use of a Dedicated Commuter Lane (DCL) located at specific U.S. ports-of-entry by an approved participant in a designated vehicle: (i) $80.00, or (ii) $160.00 for a family ...; plus, (iii) $42 for each additional vehicle enrolled.
units.action_summary: Approved participants must pay the applicable DCL fees specified for individuals, families, and additional vehicles.

units.obligation_text: This fee is non-refundable, but may be waived by DHS.
units.action_summary: DCL fees are generally non-refundable; DHS may waive the fee in its discretion.

units.obligation_text: DHS may charge a fee to collect biometric information, to provide biometric collection services, to conduct required national security and criminal history background checks, to verify an individual’s identity, and to store and maintain this biometric information for reuse to support other benefit requests.
units.action_summary: DHS is permitted to impose fees for biometric collection, background checks, identity verification, and biometric storage.

units.obligation_text: If a request for immigration benefits must be submitted with a biometric services fee, 8 CFR part 106 will contain the requirement.
units.action_summary: When a benefit requires a biometric services fee, that requirement will be specified in 8 CFR part 106.

units.obligation_text: When a biometric services fee is required, a benefit request submitted without the correct biometric services fee may be rejected.
units.action_summary: USCIS may reject benefit requests that lack the required biometric services fee.

units.obligation_text: USCIS provides on its website ... the required forms in electronic versions: Genealogy Index Search Request, or Genealogy Records Request.
units.action_summary: USCIS makes required genealogy request forms available electronically on its website.

units.obligation_text: A separate request must be submitted for each individual searched.
units.action_summary: Requestors must file a separate genealogy request for each individual they want searched.

units.obligation_text: All requests for records or index searches must include the individual’s: (i) Full name ..., (ii) Date of birth ..., (iii) Place of birth ...
units.action_summary: Requestors must include specified identifying information (name, date of birth, place of birth) with genealogy requests.

units.obligation_text: To better ensure a successful search, a Genealogical Research Request may include each individual’s: (i) Date of arrival in the United States. (ii) Residence address at time of naturalization. (iii) Names of parents, spouse, and children if applicable and available.
units.action_summary: Requestors may include optional additional information to improve search success.

units.obligation_text: For a Genealogy Records Request, requests for copies of historical records or files must: Identify the record by number or other specific data used by the Genealogy Program Office to retrieve the record as follows: (A) C-Files must be identified by a naturalization certificate number. (B) Forms AR–2 and A-Files numbered below 8 million must be identified by Alien Registration Number. (C) Visa Files must be identified by the Visa File Number. Registry Files must be identified by the Registry File Number (for example, R–12345).
units.action_summary: Requestors must identify records by specific identifiers (certificate numbers, A-file number, visa file number, registry number) when requesting copies.
