units.obligation_text: Documentary evidence must be attached to a Genealogy Records Request or submitted in accordance with the instructions on the Genealogy Records Request form.
units.action_summary: Requestors must attach documentary evidence or follow form instructions when requesting records.

units.obligation_text: Search subjects will be presumed deceased if their birth dates are more than 100 years before the date of the request. In other cases, the subject is presumed to be living until the requestor establishes to the satisfaction of USCIS that the subject is deceased.
units.action_summary: Subjects born over 100 years ago are presumed deceased; otherwise the requestor must prove death to obtain records.

units.obligation_text: Documentary evidence of the subject’s death is required (including but not limited to ...).
units.action_summary: Requestors must supply documentary evidence of death to obtain certain records.

units.obligation_text: Requestors ... may submit a request for index search.
units.action_summary: Requestors are permitted to submit index search requests to determine existence of records.

units.obligation_text: If no record is found, USCIS will notify the requestor accordingly. If records are found, USCIS will give the requestor electronic copies of records stored in digital format for no additional fee.
units.action_summary: USCIS will notify requestors about search results and provide electronic copies of digital records at no extra charge if found.

units.obligation_text: Fees must be submitted with any USCIS benefit request or other request in the amount and subject to the conditions provided in this part and remitted in the manner prescribed in the relevant form instructions, on the USCIS website, or in a Federal Register document.
units.action_summary: Applicants/payors are required to submit fees with benefit requests in the prescribed amount, conditions, and manner.

units.obligation_text: Fees must be remitted from a bank or other institution located in the United States and payable in U.S. currency. The fee must be paid using the method that USCIS prescribes for the request, office, filing method, or filing location, as provided in the form instructions or by individual notice.
units.action_summary: Fees must be paid from a U.S. bank/institution in U.S. currency by the payment methods USCIS prescribes.

units.obligation_text: If a remittance in payment of a fee or any other matter is not honored by the bank or financial institution on which it is drawn: The provisions of 8 CFR 103.2(a)(7)(ii) apply, no receipt will be issued, and if a receipt was issued, it is void and the benefit request loses its receipt date;
units.action_summary: If payment is dishonored, receipt may be voided, no receipt given, and the benefit request loses its receipt date per 8 CFR 103.2(a)(7)(ii).
units.modal_raw: will apply / no receipt will be issued

units.obligation_text: If the benefit request was approved, the approval may be revoked upon notice. If the approved benefit request requires multiple fees, this provision will apply if any fee submitted is not honored. Other fees that were paid for a benefit request that is revoked under this provision will be retained and not refunded. A revocation of an approval because the fee submitted is not honored may be appealed to the USCIS Administrative Appeals Office, in accordance with 8 CFR 103.3 and the applicable form instructions.
units.action_summary: USCIS may revoke approved benefits if payment is dishonored; fees already paid are retained; the revocation may be appealed as provided.
units.modal_raw: may / will be retained / may be appealed

units.obligation_text: Application to Replace Permanent Resident Card, Form I–90. For filing an application for a Permanent Resident Card ...: $415.
units.action_summary: Applicants filing Form I-90 must pay a $415 filing fee.

units.obligation_text: Application for Replacement/ Initial Nonimmigrant Arrival-Departure Document, Form I–102. For filing an application ... to replace one lost, mutilated, or destroyed: $490.
units.action_summary: Applicants filing Form I-102 to replace arrival/departure or crewman permit must pay $490.

units.obligation_text: (i) For nonimmigrant member of in the U.S. armed forces: No fee for initial filing; (ii) For a nonimmigrant member of the NATO armed forces or civil component: No fee for initial filing; (iii) For nonimmigrant member of the Partnership for Peace military program under the Status of Forces Agreement (SOFA): No fee for initial filing.
units.action_summary: Certain nonimmigrant service members (U.S. armed forces, NATO, Partnership for Peace) are exempt from the initial Form I-102 filing fee.

units.obligation_text: Petition or Application for a Nonimmigrant Worker. For filing a petition or application for a nonimmigrant worker: (i) Petition for H–1B ...: $560. (ii) Petition for H–2A ... with 1 to 25 named beneficiaries: $860. (iii) ...
units.action_summary: Petitioners/employers filing various nonimmigrant worker petitions must pay the specified fees for each petition type.

units.obligation_text: For a K–3 spouse ... who is the beneficiary of an immigrant petition filed by a U.S. citizen on a Petition for Alien Relative, Form I–130: No fee.
units.action_summary: K-3 spouses who are beneficiaries of an I-130 filed by a U.S. citizen are exempt from the fee.

units.obligation_text: Petition for Alien Relative, Form I–130. For filing a petition ...: $555.
units.action_summary: Petitioners filing Form I-130 must pay $555.

units.obligation_text: There is no fee for applicants who filed USCIS Form I–485 on or after July 30, 2007, and before [EFFECTIVE DATE OF THE FINAL RULE], and paid the Form I–485 fee, or for applicants for Special Immigrant Status based on an approved Form I–360 as an Afghan or Iraqi Interpreter, or Iraqi National employed by or on behalf of the U.S. Government or Afghan National employed by the U.S. Government or the International Security Assistance Forces ("ISAF").
units.action_summary: Certain applicants (I-485 filers in specified dates or specified Special Immigrant Status applicants) are exempt from the I-131 fee.

units.obligation_text: Application for Carrier Documentation, Form I–131A. For filing an application ... to board ... to return to the United States: $1,010.
units.action_summary: Lawful permanent residents applying for carrier documentation must pay $1,010.

units.obligation_text: Supplement A to Form I–485 for persons seeking to adjust status under the provisions of section 245(i) of the Act: A sum of $1,000 must be paid while the applicant’s Application to Register Permanent Residence or Adjust Status is pending, unless payment of the additional sum is not required under section 245(i) of the Act.
units.action_summary: Applicants seeking adjustment under section 245(i) must pay an additional $1,000 while their I-485 is pending, unless not required by law.

units.obligation_text: For filing an application to extend or change nonimmigrant status: $400. (i) For nonimmigrant A, G, and NATO: No fee.
units.action_summary: General I-539 filers must pay $400; certain nonimmigrant A, G, NATO applicants are exempt from the fee.

units.obligation_text: Application for Asylum and for Withholding of Removal, Form I–589. For filing an application for asylum status: $50. There is no fee for applications filed by unaccompanied alien children who are in removal proceedings.
units.action_summary: Asylum applicants must pay $50, but unaccompanied alien children in removal proceedings are exempt from the fee.

units.obligation_text: Petition to Classify Orphan as an Immediate Relative, Form I–600. (i) There is no fee for the first Form I–600 filed for a child on the basis of an approved ... I–600A ... during the Form I–600A approval or extended approval period. (ii) ... fee is $810 for the second and each subsequent Form I–600 petition submitted. (iii) If more than one Form I–600 is filed during the Form I–600A approval period on behalf of beneficiary birth siblings, no additional fee is required.
units.action_summary: First I-600 filed during I-600A approval is fee-exempt; subsequent filings are $810 except filings for birth siblings are exempt.

units.obligation_text: Request for Action on Approved Form I–600A/I–600, Form I–600A/I–600 Supplement 3. This filing fee is not charged if ... filed in order to obtain a first extension ... or to obtain a first time change of non-Hague Adoption Convention country during the Form I–600A approval period. ... Second or subsequent extensions ... are permitted with Form I–600A/I–600 Supplement 3 with the filing fee: $405.
units.action_summary: Certain first-time extensions or country changes are fee-exempt; second/subsequent extensions or specified requests require a $405 fee.
units.modal_raw: is not charged / are permitted / with the filing fee

units.obligation_text: Application for Waiver of Ground of Inadmissibility, Form I–601. For filing an application for waiver of grounds of inadmissibility: $985.
units.action_summary: Applicants for an I-601 waiver must pay $985.

units.obligation_text: Application for Provisional Unlawful Presence Waiver, Form I–601A. For filing an application for provisional unlawful presence waiver: $960.
units.action_summary: Applicants for the provisional unlawful presence waiver must pay $960.

units.obligation_text: Petition to Remove Conditions on Residence, Form I–751. For filing a petition to remove the conditions on residence based on marriage: $760.
units.action_summary: Filers of Form I-751 must pay $760.

units.obligation_text: Application for Employment Authorization, Form I–765: $490.
units.action_summary: Applicants for employment authorization generally must pay $490.

units.obligation_text: There is no initial fee for: (i) An applicant who filed USCIS Form I–485 on or after July 30, 2007, and before [EFFECTIVE DATE ...], and paid the Form I–485 fee; (ii) Refugees and aliens paroled as refugee; (iii) Victims of Severe Forms of Trafficking (T–1); (iv) Nonimmigrant Victim of Criminal Activity (U–1); (v) Dependents of certain government and international organizations or NATO personnel; (vi) N–8 and N–9 nonimmigrants; (vi) VAWA Self-Petitioners; (vii) Applicants for Special Immigrant Status ...; and (viii) Aliens granted asylee status (AS1, AS6).
units.action_summary: Specified categories of applicants are exempt from the initial I-765 filing fee.

units.obligation_text: Petition to Classify Convention Adoptee as an Immediate Relative, Form I–800. (i) There is no fee for the first Form I–800 filed ... during the Form I–800A approval period. (ii) Except ... if more than one Form I–800 is filed ... the fee is $810 for the second and each subsequent Form I–800 petition submitted. (iii) If more than one Form I–800 is filed ... on behalf of beneficiary birth siblings, no additional fee is required.
units.action_summary: First Form I-800 during I-800A approval is fee-exempt; subsequent filings are $810, except filings for birth siblings are exempt.

units.obligation_text: Request for Action on Approved Application for Determination of Suitability to Adopt a Child from a Convention Country, Form I–800A, Supplement 3. ... Second or subsequent extensions of the Form I–800A approval, second or subsequent changes of Hague Adoption Convention country, requests for a new approval notice based on a significant change and updated home study, and requests for a duplicate approval notice are permitted with the filing of a Form I–800A, Supplement 3 and the required filing fee: $405.
units.action_summary: Certain requests (second/subsequent extensions, changes, new approval notices, duplicate notices) require filing Supplement 3 with a $405 fee.

units.obligation_text: Application for Family Unity Benefits, Form I–817. For filing an application for voluntary departure under the Family Unity Program: $590.
units.action_summary: Applicants for Family Unity Program voluntary departure must pay $590.

units.obligation_text: Application for Temporary Protected Status, Form I–821. (i) For first time applicants: $50 or the maximum permitted by section 244(c)(1)(B) of the Act. (ii) There is no fee for re-registration. (iii) A TPS applicant or re-registrant must pay $30 for biometric services unless exempted in the applicable form instructions.
units.action_summary: First-time TPS applicants must pay $50 (or statutory max); re-registrants pay no fee; TPS applicants/re-registrants must pay $30 biometric fee unless exempted.

units.obligation_text: Consideration of Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals, Form I–821D. (i) For first time requestors: $0. (ii) The fee for renewal is $275.
units.action_summary: First-time DACA requestors pay no fee; renewal requests require a $275 fee.

units.obligation_text: Request for Premium Processing Service, Form I–907. The Request for Premium Processing Service fee will be as provided in 8 CFR 106.4.
units.action_summary: Premium processing fee amounts and requirements are provided in 8 CFR 106.4 and apply to I-907 filings.

units.obligation_text: Application to File Declaration of Intention, Form N–300. For filing an application for declaration of intention to become a U.S. citizen: $1,320.
units.action_summary: Applicants filing Form N-300 must pay $1,320.

units.obligation_text: Request for a Hearing on a Decision in Naturalization Proceedings ... Form N–336. For filing a request for hearing ...: $1,755. There is no fee for an applicant who has filed an Application for Naturalization under sections 328 or 329 of the Act with respect to military service and whose application has been denied.
units.action_summary: General N-336 filers must pay $1,755; certain military naturalization applicants who were denied and had filed under sections 328 or 329 are exempt.

units.obligation_text: Application for Naturalization, Form N–400. For filing an application for naturalization: $1,170. No fee is charged an applicant who meets the requirements of sections 328 or 329 of the Act with respect to military service.
units.action_summary: Naturalization applicants generally pay $1,170; qualifying military applicants under sections 328 or 329 are exempt.

units.obligation_text: Genealogy Index Search Request, Form G–1041: $240. The fee is due regardless of the search results. Genealogy Records Request, Form G–1041A: $385. USCIS will refund the records request fee when it is unable to locate any file previously identified in response to the index search request.
units.action_summary: Requestors must pay fees for genealogy index and records requests; USCIS will refund the records request fee if it cannot locate the previously identified file.

units.obligation_text: USCIS Immigrant Fee. For DHS domestic processing and issuance of required documents after an immigrant visa is issued by the U.S. Department of State: $200.
units.action_summary: Immigrants subject to DHS domestic processing must pay a $200 USCIS immigrant fee.

units.obligation_text: American Competitiveness and Workforce Improvement Act (ACWIA) fee. For filing certain H–1B petitions ...: $1,500 or $750.
units.action_summary: Employers filing certain H-1B petitions must pay the ACWIA fee in the specified amount.

units.obligation_text: Fraud detection and prevention fee. (i) For filing certain H–1B and L petitions ...: $500. (ii) For filing certain H–2B petitions ...: $150.
units.action_summary: Certain employers filing specified H-1B, L, and H-2B petitions must pay the fraud detection and prevention fee in the stated amounts.

units.obligation_text: Fraud detection and prevention fee for CNMI. For employer petitions in CNMI ...: $50.
units.action_summary: Employers filing petitions in CNMI must pay a $50 fraud detection and prevention fee.

units.obligation_text: CNMI education funding fee. (i) The fee amount must be paid in addition to, and in a separate remittance from, other filing fees; (ii) Every employer who is issued a permit must pay the education funding fee every year; (iii) An employer who is issued a permit with a validity period of longer than 1 year must pay the fee for each year of requested validity at the time the permit is requested;
units.action_summary: Employers must pay the CNMI education funding fee in addition to other fees, annually while permitted, and for each year of multi-year permits at time of request.

units.obligation_text: Beginning in FY 2020, the fee may be adjusted once per year by notice in the Federal Register based on the amount of inflation according to the Consumer Price Index ...
units.action_summary: DHS/USCIS may annually adjust the CNMI education funding fee based on inflation by Federal Register notice starting FY2020.

units.obligation_text: 9–11 Response and Biometric Entry-Exit Fee for H–1B Visa ... $4,000. This fee will apply to petitions filed on or before September 30, 2027. 9–11 Response and Biometric Entry-Exit Fee for L–1 Visa ... $4,500. This fee will apply to petitions filed on ...
units.actor: petitioner/employer filing H-1B or L-1 petitions meeting thresholds
units.action_summary: Certain large employers filing H-1B or L-1 petitions must pay the specified 9-11 response/entry-exit fees when thresholds are met, applicable through specified dates.

title: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services Fee Schedule and Changes to Certain Other Immigration Benefit Request Requirements

units.obligation_text: The comment period for the NPRM published November 14, 2019, at 84 FR 62280, is extended to December 30, 2019.
units.action_summary: Extends the NPRM comment period to December 30, 2019.

units.obligation_text: You may submit comments, identified by DHS Docket No. USCIS-2019-0010, by one of the following methods: Federal eRulemaking Portal; Mail.
units.action_summary: Permits the public to submit comments via the specified methods identified by the docket number.

units.obligation_text: Mail must be postmarked by the comment submission deadline.
units.action_summary: Requires mailed comments to be postmarked by the comment deadline.

units.obligation_text: To ensure proper handling, please reference DHS Docket No. USCIS-2019-0010 in your correspondence.
units.action_summary: Requests commenters include the docket number in mailed correspondence to ensure proper handling.

units.obligation_text: Please note that USCIS cannot accept any comments that are hand delivered or couriered.
units.action_summary: Prohibits submission of comments by hand delivery or courier.

units.obligation_text: USCIS cannot accept mailed comments contained on any form of digital media storage devices, such as CDs/DVDs and USB drives.
units.action_summary: Prohibits mailed comments that are submitted on physical digital media (CDs, DVDs, USB drives).

units.obligation_text: All submissions should include the agency name and DHS Docket No. USCIS-2019-0010 for this rulemaking.
units.action_summary: Requests that all comment submissions include the agency name and docket number.

units.obligation_text: Providing comments is entirely voluntary.
units.action_summary: States that submitting comments is voluntary (not required).

units.obligation_text: Regardless of how you submit your comment, DHS will post all submissions, without change, to the Federal eRulemaking Portal at http://www.regulations.gov and will include any personal information you provide.
units.action_summary: DHS will post all comment submissions to regulations.gov, including any personal information provided.

units.obligation_text: Because the information you submit will be publicly available, you should consider limiting the amount of personal information in your submission.
units.action_summary: Advises commenters to limit personal information because submissions will be public.

units.obligation_text: DHS may withhold information provided in comments from public viewing if it determines that such information is offensive or may affect the privacy of an individual.
units.action_summary: Permits DHS to withhold certain comment information from public view if offensive or privacy-affecting.

units.obligation_text: For additional information, please read the Privacy Act notice available through the link in the footer of http://www.regulations.gov.
units.action_summary: Requests that persons consult the Privacy Act notice on regulations.gov for more information.

units.obligation_text: For access to the docket, go to http://www.regulations.gov and enter this rulemaking's eDocket number: USCIS-2019-0010.
units.action_summary: Instructs the public to access the docket at regulations.gov using the specified eDocket number.

units.section: SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: II. Extension of Comment Period
units.obligation_text: The comment period for the NPRM will end on December 30, 2019, including comments on the forms DHS must submit to OMB for review and approval under the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995, 44 U.S.C. 3501-12.
units.action_summary: Specifies that the NPRM comment period (including comments on PRA-related forms) ends December 30, 2019.

units.section: SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: II. Extension of Comment Period
units.obligation_text: The NPRM contained erroneous references to comments being accepted for 60 days from the publication date of the proposed rule.
units.action_summary: States that prior NPRM references to a 60-day comment period were erroneous.

units.section: SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: III. Supplemental Information Regarding ICE Activities To Be Funded by the IEFA
units.obligation_text: DHS proposes to establish USCIS fees at a level necessary to recover the full amount of this proposed transfer in addition to the costs of operating USCIS.
units.action_summary: Proposes setting USCIS fees to recover the ICE transfer amount plus USCIS operating costs.

units.obligation_text: Moving forward, USCIS will reimburse ICE for costs associated with supporting immigration adjudication and naturalization services.
units.action_summary: USCIS will reimburse ICE for costs that support adjudication and naturalization services.

title: Asylum Application, Interview, and Employment Authorization for Applicants

units.obligation_text: An asylum application must be properly filed in accordance with 8 CFR part 103 and the filing instructions.
units.action_summary: File the asylum application properly according to 8 CFR part 103 and the form instructions.

units.obligation_text: Receipt of a properly filed asylum application will commence the 365-day period after which the applicant may file an application for employment authorization in accordance with § 208.7 and 8 CFR 274a.12 and 274a.13.
units.action_summary: After receipt of a properly filed asylum application and the 365-day period, the applicant may file for employment authorization per cited sections.

units.obligation_text: Upon the request of the alien, and as a matter of discretion, the asylum officer or Immigration Judge with jurisdiction may permit an asylum applicant to amend or supplement the application.
units.actor: the asylum officer or Immigration Judge with jurisdiction
units.action_summary: Discretionarily allow an asylum applicant to amend or supplement the asylum application upon request.

units.obligation_text: Any delay in adjudication or in proceedings caused by a request to amend or supplement the application will be treated as a delay caused by the applicant for purposes of § 208.7 and 8 CFR 274a.12(c)(8).
units.action_summary: Delays caused by amendment/supplement requests are treated as applicant-caused delays for purposes of employment authorization rules.

units.obligation_text: Subject to the restrictions contained in sections 208(d) and 236(a) of the Act, and except as otherwise provided in paragraphs (b) and (c) of this section, an applicant for asylum who is in the United States may apply for employment authorization pursuant to 8 CFR 274a.12(c)(8) and 274a.13(a)(2) of this chapter.
units.action_summary: An asylum applicant in the U.S. may apply for employment authorization under the cited provisions, subject to listed restrictions.

units.obligation_text: The applicant must request employment authorization on the form and in the manner prescribed by USCIS and according to the form instructions, and must submit biometrics at a scheduled biometrics services appointment.
units.action_summary: Submit the employment authorization request using the USCIS-prescribed form and instructions and attend a scheduled biometrics appointment.

units.obligation_text: Employment authorization is not permitted during any period of judicial review of the asylum application, but may be requested if a Federal court remands the case to the Board of Immigration Appeals.
units.action_summary: Employment authorization cannot be granted during judicial review, but the applicant may request authorization if a federal court remands the case to the BIA.

units.obligation_text: USCIS may grant initial employment authorization under 8 CFR 274a.12(c)(8) for a period that USCIS determines is appropriate at its discretion, not to exceed increments of two years.
units.action_summary: USCIS may grant initial employment authorization in its discretion in increments it determines appropriate, up to two-year increments.

units.obligation_text: An applicant for asylum cannot apply for initial employment authorization earlier than 365 calendar days after the date USCIS or the immigration court receives the asylum application in accordance with 8 CFR part 103 or 8 CFR 1003.31, respectively, and the filing instructions on the application.
units.action_summary: Do not file for initial employment authorization until 365 days after USCIS or immigration court receipt of the asylum application.

units.obligation_text: If an asylum application is denied by USCIS before a decision on an initial or renewal application for employment authorization, the application for employment authorization will be denied.
units.action_summary: If USCIS denies the asylum application before deciding on employment authorization, USCIS will deny the employment authorization application.

units.obligation_text: An applicant for asylum is not eligible for employment authorization if:
units.action_summary: Sets general rule that asylum applicants meeting listed conditions are ineligible for employment authorization.

units.obligation_text: The applicant was convicted in the United States or abroad of any aggravated felony as described in section 101(a)(43) of the Act;
units.action_summary: Applicant convicted of an aggravated felony (domestically or abroad) is ineligible for employment authorization.

units.obligation_text: The applicant was convicted in the United States of any felony as defined in 18 U.S.C. 3156(a)(3);
units.action_summary: Applicant convicted in the U.S. of any felony is ineligible for employment authorization.

units.obligation_text: The applicant was convicted of any serious non-political crime outside the United States.
units.action_summary: Applicant convicted of a serious non-political foreign crime is ineligible for employment authorization.

units.obligation_text: USCIS will consider, on a case-by-case basis, whether aliens who have been convicted of any non-political foreign criminal offense, or have unresolved arrests or pending charges for any non-political foreign criminal offenses, warrant a favorable exercise of discretion for a grant of employment authorization;
units.action_summary: USCIS will evaluate whether non-political foreign convictions or unresolved foreign charges merit a discretionary grant of employment authorization.

units.obligation_text: The applicant was convicted in the United States of a public safety offense involving: (1) Domestic violence, domestic assault, or any other domestic or spousal battery-type offense...
units.action_summary: Applicant convicted of listed public safety offenses (domestic violence, child abuse, controlled substances, DUI) is ineligible for employment authorization.

units.obligation_text: Domestic violence, domestic assault, or any other domestic or spousal battery-type offense unless the applicant has been subjected to extreme cruelty, is not and was not the primary perpetrator of the violence in the relationship, and is not otherwise ineligible.
units.action_summary: Domestic violence-type convictions render the applicant ineligible unless the applicant was a victim of extreme cruelty, was not the primary perpetrator, and is not otherwise ineligible (exception).

units.obligation_text: Child abuse, child neglect, or any other offense against a child, regardless of an element of sexual or inappropriate touching.
units.action_summary: Convictions for offenses against a child make the applicant ineligible for employment authorization.

units.obligation_text: Controlled substances, including possession, possession with intent to distribute, or delivery.
units.action_summary: Controlled substance convictions result in ineligibility for employment authorization.

units.obligation_text: Driving or operating a motor vehicle under the influence of alcohol or drugs, regardless of how the arresting, charging, or convicting jurisdiction classifies the offense.
units.action_summary: DUI convictions make the applicant ineligible for employment authorization.

units.obligation_text: If an applicant has unresolved domestic arrests or pending charges, USCIS will decide at its discretion if it will grant the applicant employment authorization, based on the totality of the circumstances.
units.action_summary: USCIS will use discretion to decide on employment authorization when the applicant has unresolved domestic arrests or pending charges.

units.obligation_text: An asylum officer or an Immigration Judge has denied the applicant’s asylum application within the 365-day period or before the adjudication of the initial request for employment authorization;
units.action_summary: If the asylum application was denied within 365 days or before adjudication of the initial employment authorization request, the applicant is ineligible for employment authorization.

units.obligation_text: The applicant filed his or her asylum application beyond the one-year filing deadline, unless and until the asylum officer or Immigration Judge determines that the applicant meets an exception for late filing as provided in section 208(a)(2)(D) of the Act and 8 CFR 208.4 and 1208.4, or unless the applicant was an unaccompanied alien child on the date the asylum application was first filed;
units.action_summary: Applicants who filed beyond the one-year deadline are ineligible unless an exception for late filing is found or the applicant was an unaccompanied alien child.

units.obligation_text: The applicant is an alien who entered or attempted to enter the United States at a place and time other than lawfully through a U.S. port of entry, unless the alien demonstrates that he or she: (1) Presented himself or herself without delay to the Secretary of Homeland Security or his or her delegate; (2) Indicated to the Secretary of Homeland Security or his or her delegate an intention to apply for asylum or expresses a fear of persecution or torture; and (3) Has good cause for the illegal entry or attempted entry, provided such good cause does not include the evasion of U.S. immigration officers, convenience, or for the purpose of circumvention of the orderly processing of asylum seekers at a U.S. port of entry.
units.action_summary: Applicants who entered unlawfully are ineligible unless they meet three conditions demonstrating prompt presentation, intention to seek asylum/fear, and good cause for entry (excluding specified reasons).

units.obligation_text: Presented himself or herself without delay to the Secretary of Homeland Security or his or her delegate;
units.action_summary: Applicant must have presented themselves without delay to DHS or its delegate after unlawful entry to be eligible.

units.obligation_text: Indicated to the Secretary of Homeland Security or his or her delegate an intention to apply for asylum or expresses a fear of persecution or torture;
units.action_summary: Applicant must indicate intent to apply for asylum or express fear of persecution or torture to be eligible after unlawful entry.

units.obligation_text: Has good cause for the illegal entry or attempted entry, provided such good cause does not include the evasion of U.S. immigration officers, convenience, or for the purpose of circumvention of the orderly processing of asylum seekers at a U.S. port of entry.
units.action_summary: Applicant must show good cause for unlawful entry that does not include evasion, convenience, or circumvention to be eligible.

units.obligation_text: Provided such good cause does not include the evasion of U.S. immigration officers, convenience, or for the purpose of circumvention of the orderly processing of asylum seekers at a U.S. port of entry.
units.action_summary: Clarifies that specified reasons (evasion, convenience, circumvention) cannot qualify as good cause for unlawful entry.

units.obligation_text: Paragraphs (a)(1)(iii)(A) through (D) of this section apply to applications that were filed prior to and remain pending on [effective date of final rule].
units.action_summary: Specifies that the listed ineligibility provisions apply to applications filed before and still pending on the rule's effective date.

units.obligation_text: Any delay requested or caused by the applicant on his or her asylum application that is still outstanding or has not been remedied when USCIS adjudicates the application for employment authorization under 8 CFR 274a.12(c)(8) will result in a denial of such application.
units.action_summary: Applicant-caused delays that remain unresolved at adjudication will lead to denial of the employment authorization application.

units.obligation_text: A request to amend or supplement an asylum application that causes a delay in its adjudication or in proceedings as permitted in 8 CFR 208.4(c);
units.action_summary: Requesting amendment/supplement that causes delay is an example of applicant-caused delay that can result in denial.

units.obligation_text: Failure to appear to receive and acknowledge receipt of the decision as specified in 8 CFR 208.9(d);
units.action_summary: Not appearing to receive/acknowledge the decision is an applicant-caused delay example that can lead to denial.

units.obligation_text: A request for extension to submit additional evidence fewer than 14-days prior to the interview date as permitted by 8 CFR 208.9(e);
units.action_summary: Requesting an extension to submit evidence fewer than 14 days before the interview is an example of applicant-caused delay that can result in denial.

units.obligation_text: Failure to appear for an asylum interview, unless excused by USCIS as described in 8 CFR 208.10(b)(1) for the failure to appear;
units.action_summary: Failure to attend the asylum interview (unless excused) is an applicant-caused delay example that can result in denial.

units.obligation_text: Failure to appear for scheduled biometrics collection on the asylum application;
units.action_summary: Not appearing for scheduled biometrics collection is an applicant-caused delay example that can result in denial.

units.obligation_text: A request to reschedule an interview for a later date;
units.action_summary: Requesting to reschedule the interview is an example of applicant-caused delay that can result in denial.

units.obligation_text: A request to transfer a case to a new asylum office or interview location, including when the transfer is based on a new address;
units.action_summary: Requesting case transfer to a new asylum office or interview location is an example of applicant-caused delay that can result in denial.

units.obligation_text: A request to provide additional evidence for an interview;
units.action_summary: Requesting to provide additional evidence for the interview is an example of applicant-caused delay that can result in denial.

units.obligation_text: Failure to provide a competent interpreter at an interview;
units.action_summary: Not providing a competent interpreter for the interview is an example of applicant-caused delay that can result in denial.

units.obligation_text: Failure to comply with any other request needed to determine asylum eligibility.
units.action_summary: Failure to comply with other requests needed to determine asylum eligibility is an applicant-caused delay example that can result in denial.

units.obligation_text: USCIS may renew employment authorization under 8 CFR 274a.12(c)(8) in increments determined by USCIS in its discretion, but not to exceed increments of two years.
units.action_summary: USCIS may renew employment authorization in discretionary increments up to two years.

units.obligation_text: For employment authorization to be renewed under this section, the alien must request employment authorization on the form and in the manner prescribed by USCIS and according to the form instructions.
units.action_summary: To obtain renewal, the alien must submit the renewal request using the USCIS-prescribed form and instructions.

units.obligation_text: USCIS will require that an alien establish that he or she has continued to pursue an asylum application before USCIS, an Immigration Judge, or the Board of Immigration Appeals and that he or she continues to meet the eligibility criteria for employment authorization set forth in 8 CFR 208.7(a).
units.action_summary: For renewal, the alien must show continued pursuit of the asylum application and ongoing eligibility under §208.7(a).

units.obligation_text: For purposes of renewal of employment authorization, pursuit of an asylum application before an Immigration Judge or the Board of Immigration Appeals is established by submitting a copy of the referral notice or Notice to Appear placing the alien in proceedings, any hearing notices issued by the immigration court, evidence of a timely filed appeal if the alien appealed the denial of the asylum application to the Board of Immigration Appeals, or remand order to the Immigration Judge or Board of Immigration Appeals.
units.action_summary: To establish pursuit of proceedings for renewal, the alien must submit referral/Notice to Appear, hearing notices, timely appeal evidence, or remand orders as applicable.

units.obligation_text: Employment authorization granted after the required 365-day waiting period will continue for the remaining period authorized (unless otherwise terminated or revoked) if the asylum officer refers the alien’s asylum application to an immigration judge.
units.action_summary: If the asylum officer refers the application to an Immigration Judge, employment authorization granted after 365 days will continue for the remaining authorized period unless terminated or revoked.

units.obligation_text: The alien may be granted renewals of employment authorization while under such review by the Immigration Judge.
units.action_summary: An alien under Immigration Judge review may receive renewals of employment authorization.

units.obligation_text: If the Immigration Judge denies the alien’s asylum application, any remaining period of employment authorization will continue for the period authorized (unless otherwise terminated or revoked) during the period for filing an appeal with the Board of Immigration Appeals under 8 CFR 1003.38(b) or, if an appeal is timely filed within such period, during the pendency of the appeal with the Board of Immigration Appeals.
units.action_summary: If the IJ denies asylum, remaining employment authorization continues during the period for filing an appeal or, if timely filed, during the appeal's pendency unless terminated or revoked.

units.obligation_text: The alien may be granted renewals of employment authorization during these periods while the appeal is under review by the Board of Immigration Appeals and any remand to the Immigration Judge.
units.action_summary: During BIA appeal review or remand periods, the alien may be granted renewals of employment authorization.

units.obligation_text: The alien’s employment authorization granted pursuant to 8 CFR 274a.12(c)(8) will automatically terminate effective on the date the asylum officer denies the asylum application, thirty days after an Immigration Judge denies the asylum application unless timely appealed to the Board of Immigration Appeals, or the Board of Immigration Appeals affirms or upholds a denial, regardless of whether any automatic extension period pursuant to 8 CFR 274a.13(d)(3) is in place.
units.action_summary: Employment authorization automatically terminates upon specified denial events (asylum officer denial, IJ denial after 30 days unless appealed, or BIA affirmance).

units.obligation_text: The applicant or the applicant’s representative will have an opportunity to make a statement or comment on the evidence presented. The asylum officer may, in his or her discretion, limit the length of such statement or comment and may require its submission in writing.
units.action_summary: After the interview, the applicant may make a statement or comment; the asylum officer may limit its length and may require it in writing.

units.obligation_text: USCIS will inform the applicant that he or she must appear in person to receive and to acknowledge receipt of the decision of the asylum officer and any other accompanying material at a time and place designated by the asylum officer, except as otherwise provided by the asylum officer. An applicant’s failure to appear to receive and acknowledge receipt of the decision will be treated as delay caused by the applicant for purposes of 8 CFR 208.7.
units.action_summary: USCIS will notify the applicant that the applicant must appear in person to receive and acknowledge the asylum decision, and failure to do so is treated as an applicant-caused delay.

units.obligation_text: The applicant must submit any documentary evidence at least 14 calendar days in advance of the interview date.
units.action_summary: Submit documentary evidence at least 14 days before the interview.

units.obligation_text: As a matter of discretion, the asylum officer may consider evidence submitted within the 14-day period prior to the interview date or may grant the applicant a brief extension of time during which the applicant may submit additional evidence. Any such extension will be treated as a delay caused by the applicant for purposes of § 208.7.
units.action_summary: Asylum officer may (discretionarily) consider late evidence or grant a brief extension; such extensions count as applicant-caused delays.

units.obligation_text: The failure to appear for an interview or biometric services appointment may result in:
units.action_summary: Failing to appear for interview or biometrics can lead to specified adverse consequences.

units.obligation_text: Waiver of the right to an interview or adjudication by an asylum officer;
units.action_summary: Failure to appear may waive the right to an asylum officer interview or adjudication.

units.obligation_text: Dismissal of the application for asylum;
units.action_summary: Failure to appear may result in dismissal of the asylum application.

units.obligation_text: Referral of the applicant to the immigration court; or,
units.action_summary: Failure to appear may result in referral to immigration court.

units.obligation_text: Denial of employment authorization.
units.action_summary: Failure to appear may lead to denial of employment authorization.

units.obligation_text: There is no requirement for USCIS to send a notice to an applicant that he or she failed to appear for his or her asylum interview or biometrics services appointment prior to issuing a decision on the application.
units.action_summary: USCIS is not required to notify an applicant of a failure to appear before issuing a decision.

units.obligation_text: Any rescheduling request for the asylum interview that has not yet been fulfilled on the date the application for employment authorization is adjudicated under 8 CFR 274a.12(c)(8) will be treated as an applicant-caused delay for purposes of 8 CFR 208.7.
units.action_summary: Unfulfilled interview rescheduling requests at the time of adjudication are treated as applicant-caused delays.

units.obligation_text: USCIS, in its sole discretion, may excuse the failure to appear for an interview or biometrics services appointment and reschedule the missed appointment as follows:
units.action_summary: USCIS may, in its discretion, excuse failures to appear and reschedule appointments under the conditions specified.

units.obligation_text: Asylum Interview. If the applicant demonstrates that he or she was unable to make the appointment due to exceptional circumstances.
units.action_summary: USCIS may reschedule an asylum interview if the applicant shows inability to attend because of exceptional circumstances.

units.obligation_text: Biometrics services appointment. USCIS may reschedule the biometrics services appointment as provided in 8 CFR part 103.
units.action_summary: USCIS may reschedule biometrics appointments consistent with 8 CFR part 103.

units.obligation_text: An alien who has filed a complete application for asylum or withholding of deportation or removal pursuant to 8 CFR parts 103 and 208, whose application has not been decided, and who is eligible to apply for employment authorization under 8 CFR 208.7 because the 365-day period set forth in that section has expired.
units.actor: an alien who has filed a complete asylum application
units.action_summary: Defines the class of aliens who may seek employment authorization: those with a pending complete asylum application and who have passed the 365-day period.

units.obligation_text: Employment authorization may be granted according to the provisions of 8 CFR 208.7 of this chapter in increments to be determined by USCIS but not to exceed increments of two years.
units.action_summary: USCIS may grant employment authorization under §208.7 in discretionary increments up to two years.

units.obligation_text: Aliens seeking initial or renewed employment authorization under 8 CFR 274a.12(c) must apply on the form designated by USCIS with prescribed fee(s) and in accordance with the form instructions.
units.actor: aliens seeking initial or renewed employment authorization
units.action_summary: Apply for initial or renewed employment authorization using USCIS-designated form, pay fees, and follow form instructions.

units.obligation_text: The approval of applications filed under 8 CFR 274a.12(c) is within the discretion of USCIS.
units.action_summary: USCIS has discretion to approve or deny applications filed under the cited provision.

units.obligation_text: Where economic necessity has been identified as a factor, the alien must provide information regarding his or her assets, income, and expenses.
units.action_summary: If economic necessity is a factor, the alien must submit financial information (assets, income, expenses).

units.obligation_text: An initial employment authorization request for asylum applicants or for renewal or replacement of employment authorization submitted in relation to a pending claim for asylum, in accordance with 8 CFR 208.7 and 8 CFR 274a.12(c)(8), must be filed on the form designated by USCIS in accordance with the form instructions with prescribed fee(s).
units.action_summary: Initial or renewal/replacement employment authorization requests related to a pending asylum claim must be filed on the USCIS-designated form with required fees and instructions.

units.obligation_text: Employment authorization automatically extended pursuant to paragraph (d)(1) of this section will automatically terminate the earlier of up to 180 days after the expiration date of the Employment Authorization Document (Form I–766), or on the date USCIS denies the request for renewal. Employment authorization granted under 8 CFR 274a.12(c)(8) and automatically extended pursuant to paragraph (d)(1) of this section is further subject to the termination provisions of 8 CFR 208.7(b)(2).
units.action_summary: Automatically extended employment authorization will terminate either up to 180 days after EAD expiration or on the date USCIS denies renewal; such authorization is also subject to §208.7(b)(2) termination rules.

title: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services Fee Schedule and Changes to Certain Other Immigration Benefit Request Requirements

units.obligation_text: You must submit comments, identified as DHS Docket No. USCIS–2019–0010, through one of the following methods:
units.action_summary: Submit comments identified with the DHS docket number through one of the listed methods.

units.obligation_text: Federal eRulemaking Portal (preferred): http://www.regulations.gov.
units.action_summary: May submit comments via the Federal eRulemaking Portal.

units.obligation_text: Follow the website instructions for submitting comments.
units.action_summary: Follow the portal's website instructions when submitting comments.

units.obligation_text: Mail: Samantha Deshommes, Chief, Regulatory Coordination Division, Office of Policy and Strategy, U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services, Department of Homeland Security, 20 Massachusetts Avenue NW, Washington, DC 20529–2140.
units.action_summary: May submit comments by mail to the specified address.

units.obligation_text: Mail must be postmarked by the comment submission deadline.
units.action_summary: If submitting comments by mail, the mailed comments must be postmarked by the deadline.

units.obligation_text: To ensure proper handling, please reference DHS Docket No. USCIS–2019–0010 in your correspondence.
units.action_summary: Reference the DHS docket number in correspondence to ensure proper handling.

units.obligation_text: Comments submitted in a manner other than those listed above, including emails or letters sent to DHS or USCIS officials, will not be considered comments on the proposed rule.
units.action_summary: Comments sent by methods other than the listed methods (including emails or direct letters to officials) will not be treated as comments on the proposed rule.

units.obligation_text: Please note that DHS and USCIS cannot accept any comments that are hand delivered or couriered.
units.action_summary: Hand-delivered or couriered comments will not be accepted.

units.obligation_text: USCIS cannot accept mailed comments contained on any form of digital media storage devices, such as CDs/DVDs and USB drives.
units.action_summary: Mailed comments on digital media (CDs, DVDs, USB drives) will not be accepted by USCIS.

units.obligation_text: Written comments and related material must be submitted on or before February 10, 2020.
units.action_summary: Submit written comments and related material by February 10, 2020.

units.obligation_text: All submissions received must include DHS Docket No. USCIS–2019–0010.
units.action_summary: Include the DHS docket number in all submissions.

units.obligation_text: Interested persons are invited to participate in this rulemaking by submitting written data, views, or arguments on all aspects of this rule.
units.action_summary: May participate in the rulemaking by submitting written comments, data, views, or arguments.

units.obligation_text: Comments that will provide the most assistance to DHS will reference a specific portion of the rule, explain the reason for any recommended change, and include data, information, or authority that support such recommended change.
units.action_summary: Comments should reference the rule portion, justify recommended changes, and include supporting data or authority to be most helpful.

units.obligation_text: Providing comments is entirely voluntary.
units.action_summary: Submission of comments is voluntary, not mandatory.

units.obligation_text: Because the information you submit will be publicly available, you should consider limiting the amount of personal information in your submission.
units.action_summary: Advised to limit personal information in submissions because submissions will be publicly available.

units.obligation_text: DHS may withhold information provided in comments from public viewing if it determines that such information is offensive or may affect the privacy of an individual.
units.action_summary: DHS has the authority to withhold comment information from public view if offensive or privacy-affecting.

units.obligation_text: Comments must be received on or before March 9, 2020.
units.action_summary: Submit comments by March 9, 2020.

units.obligation_text: Send comments on this proposal to the U.S. Department of Transportation, Docket Operations, West Building Ground Floor, Room W12–140, 1200 New Jersey Avenue SE, Washington, DC 20590.
units.action_summary: Send comments to the specified DOT Docket Operations address.

units.obligation_text: You must identify FAA Docket No. FAA–2019–0790; Airspace Docket No. 19–ASW–10, at the beginning of your comments.
units.action_summary: Identify the FAA docket and airspace docket numbers at the start of comments.

units.obligation_text: You may also submit comments through the internet at https://www.regulations.gov.
units.action_summary: May submit comments online via regulations.gov.

units.obligation_text: You may review the public docket containing the proposal, any comments received, and any final disposition in person in the Dockets Office between 9:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m., Monday through Friday, except federal holidays.
units.action_summary: May review the public docket in person at the Dockets Office during specified hours.

units.obligation_text: Interested parties are invited to participate in this proposed rulemaking by submitting such written data, views, or arguments, as they may desire.
units.action_summary: May participate by submitting written data, views, or arguments.

units.obligation_text: Comments that provide the factual basis supporting the views and suggestions presented are particularly helpful in developing reasoned regulatory decisions on the proposal.
units.action_summary: Provide factual support for views and suggestions to help in decisionmaking.

units.obligation_text: Communications should identify both docket numbers and be submitted in triplicate to the address listed above.
units.action_summary: Identify both docket numbers and submit communications in triplicate to the listed address.

units.obligation_text: Commenters wishing the FAA to acknowledge receipt of their comments on this notice must submit with those comments a self-addressed, stamped postcard on which the following statement is made: "Comments to Docket No. FAA–2019–0790; Airspace Docket No. 19–ASW–10."
units.action_summary: Submit a self-addressed, stamped postcard with comments containing the specified statement to receive an acknowledgement.

units.obligation_text: An electronic copy of this document may be downloaded through the internet at https://www.regulations.gov.
units.action_summary: May download an electronic copy of the document from regulations.gov.

title: Security Bars and Processing

units.obligation_text: In determining whether there are reasonable grounds for regarding an alien or a class of aliens as a danger to the security of the United States under section 208(b)(2)(A)(iv) of the Act, the Secretary of Homeland Security may consider whether the alien exhibits symptoms consistent with being afflicted with any contagious or infectious disease or has come into contact with such disease, or whether the alien or class of aliens is coming from a country, or a political subdivision or region of that country, or has embarked at a place, where such disease is prevalent or epidemic ...
units.action_summary: Secretary may consider disease symptoms, contacts, or originating place prevalence when determining whether an alien poses a danger to U.S. security.

units.obligation_text: Determined that because the disease is a communicable disease of public health significance ... the physical presence in the United States of aliens who are coming from such country or countries ... would cause a danger to the public health in the United States;
units.actor: Secretary of Homeland Security and the Attorney General (in consultation with the Secretary of Health and Human Services)
units.action_summary: Secretary and Attorney General must jointly determine that presence of aliens from specified places would cause danger to U.S. public health.

units.obligation_text: Designated the foreign country or countries (or one or more political subdivisions or regions thereof) or place or places and the period of time or circumstances under which the Secretary and the Attorney General jointly deem it necessary for the public health that aliens described ... be regarded as a danger to the security of the United States ...
units.actor: Secretary of Homeland Security and the Attorney General (in consultation with the Secretary of Health and Human Services)
units.action_summary: Secretary and Attorney General must jointly designate the countries/regions/periods or circumstances under which aliens from those places are to be regarded as a danger.

units.obligation_text: Except as provided in paragraph (d)(3) of this section, an application for withholding of removal under section 241(b)(3) of the Act or under paragraph (c) of this section shall be denied if the applicant falls within section 241(b)(3)(B) of the Act ...
units.actor: the Department of Homeland Security / adjudicator
units.action_summary: Applications for withholding of removal must be denied if the applicant falls within specified statutory disqualifying provisions.

units.obligation_text: For purposes of section 241(b)(3)(B)(ii) of the Act ... an alien who has been convicted of a particularly serious crime shall be considered to constitute a danger to the community.
units.action_summary: An alien convicted of a particularly serious crime is to be treated as a danger to the community.

units.obligation_text: If the evidence indicates the applicability of one or more of the grounds for denial of withholding enumerated in the Act, the applicant shall have the burden of proving by a preponderance of the evidence that such grounds do not apply.
units.action_summary: Applicant must prove by a preponderance of the evidence that statutory grounds for denial do not apply.

units.obligation_text: In determining whether an alien or a class of aliens can reasonably be regarded as a danger to the security of the United States under section 241(b)(3)(B)(iv) of the Act, the Secretary of Homeland Security may consider whether the alien exhibits symptoms consistent with being afflicted with any contagious or infectious disease ...
units.action_summary: Secretary may consider disease symptoms, contacts, and origins when assessing whether aliens pose a danger to U.S. security for withholding of removal purposes.

units.obligation_text: Determined that because the disease is a communicable disease of public health significance ... the physical presence in the United States of aliens who are coming from such country or countries ... would cause a danger to the public health in the United States;
units.actor: the Secretary and the Attorney General (in consultation with the Secretary of Health and Human Services)
units.action_summary: Secretary and Attorney General must jointly determine that aliens from specified places would pose a danger to U.S. public health for the disease-consideration authority to apply.

units.obligation_text: Designated the foreign country or countries ... and the period of time or circumstances under which the Secretary and the Attorney General jointly deem it necessary for the public health that aliens described ... be regarded as a danger to the security of the United States ...
units.actor: the Secretary and the Attorney General (in consultation with the Secretary of Health and Human Services)
units.action_summary: Secretary and Attorney General must jointly designate the places and periods/circumstances under which aliens shall be regarded as a danger for withholding determinations.

units.obligation_text: Nothing in this section or § 208.17 shall prevent the Department from removing an alien requesting protection to a third country other than a country to which removal is currently withheld or deferred.
units.action_summary: Department may remove an alien requesting protection to a third country (subject to limitations).

units.obligation_text: Nothing in this section or § 208.17 precludes the Department from removing the alien to a third country prior to a determination or adjudication of the alien’s initial request for withholding or deferral of removal if the alien has not established that his or her life or freedom would be threatened ... or that it is more likely than not that he or she would be tortured in that third country.
units.action_summary: Department may remove an alien to a third country before adjudication if the alien has not established threat to life/freedom or likelihood of torture in that third country.

units.obligation_text: Such a removal shall be executed only if the alien was: (i) Advised at the time of requesting withholding or deferral of removal of the possibility of being removed to a third country prior to a determination or adjudication of the same under the conditions set forth in this paragraph (f);
units.action_summary: Department must advise the alien at time of request that the alien could be removed to a third country prior to adjudication under the specified conditions.

units.obligation_text: Such a removal shall be executed only if the alien was: (ii) Provided, but did not accept, an opportunity to withdraw the request for withholding or deferral of removal in order to prevent such removal and, instead, proceed to removal pursuant to section 241(b) of the Act, as appropriate.
units.action_summary: Department must provide the alien an opportunity to withdraw the withholding/deferral request to avoid third-country removal; removal can occur only if the alien was provided but did not accept that opportunity.

units.obligation_text: In the event that any provision in this part is stayed, enjoined, not implemented, or otherwise held invalid, the remaining provisions shall nevertheless be implemented as independent rules and continue in effect.
units.actor: the Department of Homeland Security (implementing authority)
units.action_summary: If any provision is invalidated, the remaining provisions must nonetheless be implemented and remain in effect.

units.obligation_text: The asylum officer shall create a written record of his or her determination, including a summary of the material facts as stated by the applicant, any additional facts relied on by the officer, and the officer’s determination of whether, in light of such facts, the alien has established a credible fear of persecution or torture.
units.action_summary: Asylum officer must create a written record of the credible fear determination with specified contents.

units.obligation_text: An alien will be found to have a credible fear of torture if the alien shows that there is a significant possibility that he or she is eligible for withholding of removal pursuant to § 208.16(c)...
units.action_summary: An alien will be adjudicated to have a credible fear of torture if they show a significant possibility of eligibility for withholding of removal.

units.obligation_text: In determining whether the alien has a credible fear of persecution ... the asylum officer shall consider whether the alien’s case presents novel or unique issues that merit consideration in a full hearing before an immigration judge (IJ).
units.action_summary: Asylum officer must consider whether the case has novel or unique issues warranting a full IJ hearing.

units.obligation_text: If an alien: (A) Is able to establish a credible fear of persecution but appears to be subject to one or more of the mandatory bars ... the Department of Homeland Security shall nonetheless place the alien in proceedings under section 240 of the Act for full consideration of the alien’s claim, if the alien is not a stowaway. If the alien is a stowaway, the Department shall place the alien in proceedings for consideration of the alien’s claim pursuant to § 208.2(c)(3).
units.action_summary: DHS must place aliens who establish credible fear but appear subject to mandatory bars into section 240 proceedings; stowaways are placed pursuant to §208.2(c)(3).

units.obligation_text: If an alien ... would be able to establish a credible fear of persecution but for the fact that he or she is subject to the mandatory bars ... but nevertheless establishes that it is more likely than not that he or she would be tortured ... the Department of Homeland Security may, in the unreviewable discretion of the Secretary, either place the alien in proceedings under section 240 of the Act for full consideration of the alien’s claim, or remove the alien to another country.
units.actor: the Department of Homeland Security (in the unreviewable discretion of the Secretary)
units.action_summary: DHS may either place the alien in section 240 proceedings or remove the alien to another country when alien meets specified torture-likelihood condition.

units.obligation_text: If the Department places the alien in proceedings under section 240 of the Act, then the IJ shall review all issues de novo, including whether the alien has established that it is more likely than not that he or she would be tortured in the prospective country of removal.
units.action_summary: If DHS places the alien in proceedings, the IJ must review all issues de novo including torture risk.

units.obligation_text: If the Department decides to remove the alien to another country, it shall do so in a manner consistent with section 241 of the Act and 8 CFR 241.15, including by not removing the alien to a country where the alien has established that his or her life or freedom would be threatened ... or to a country where the alien has established that he or she would more likely than not be tortured. Further, such a removal shall be executed only if the alien was: (i) Advised ...; and (ii) Provided, but did not accept, an opportunity to withdraw the request ...
units.action_summary: If DHS removes to another country, removal must comply with section 241/8 CFR 241.15 and not send the alien to countries where life/freedom or torture likelihood is established; removal may occur only if alien was advised and given opportunity to withdraw request.

units.obligation_text: Advised at the time of requesting withholding or deferral of removal of the possibility of being removed to a third country prior to a determination or adjudication of the same under the conditions set forth in this paragraph (e)(5)(i);
units.action_summary: Department must advise alien at time of request of the possibility of removal to a third country prior to adjudication under specified conditions.

units.obligation_text: Provided, but did not accept, an opportunity to withdraw the request for withholding or deferral of removal in order to prevent such removal and, instead, proceed to removal pursuant to section 241(b) of the Act, as appropriate.
units.action_summary: Department must provide the alien an opportunity to withdraw the request to prevent removal; removal may occur only if the alien was provided but did not accept that opportunity.

units.obligation_text: If the alien fails to affirmatively establish, during an interview with the asylum officer, that it is more likely than not that he or she would be tortured in the prospective country of removal, then the asylum officer will provide the alien with a written notice of decision that will be subject to IJ review consistent with paragraph (g) of this section.
units.action_summary: Asylum officer will provide a written notice of decision (subject to IJ review) if alien fails to establish torture likelihood during the interview.

units.obligation_text: If the alien is found to be an alien described as ineligible for asylum in § 208.13(c)(4), then the asylum officer shall enter a negative credible fear determination with respect to the alien’s intention to apply for asylum.
units.action_summary: If alien is ineligible under §208.13(c)(4), asylum officer must enter a negative credible fear determination as to asylum application intent.

units.obligation_text: If the alien: (A) Establishes a reasonable fear of persecution or torture ... or (B) Would be able to establish a reasonable fear of torture ... but nevertheless affirmatively establishes that it is more likely than not that he or she would be tortured ... the Department of Homeland Security may, in the unreviewable discretion of the Secretary, either place the alien in proceedings under section 240 ... or remove the alien to another country.
units.actor: the Department of Homeland Security (in the unreviewable discretion of the Secretary)
units.action_summary: DHS may place the alien in section 240 proceedings or remove the alien to another country when the alien establishes reasonable fear or more-likely-than-not torture under specified conditions.

units.obligation_text: If the Department places the alien in proceedings under section 240 of the Act, then the IJ shall review all issues de novo, including whether the alien has established that it is more likely than not that he or she would be tortured in the prospective country of removal.
units.action_summary: If DHS places the alien in proceedings, the IJ must review all issues de novo including the likelihood of torture.

units.obligation_text: If the Department decides to remove the alien to another country, it shall do so in a manner consistent with section 241(b)(2) of the Act and 8 CFR 241.15, including by not removing the alien to a country where the alien has established that his or her life or freedom would be threatened ... or to a country where the alien has established that he or she would more likely than not be tortured. Further, such a removal shall be executed only if the alien was: (i) Advised ...; and (ii) Provided, but did not accept, an opportunity ...
units.action_summary: DHS must carry out third-country removal consistent with statutory/regulatory protections and only after advising the alien and providing an opportunity to withdraw the request.

units.obligation_text: Advised at the time of requesting withholding or deferral of removal of the possibility of being removed to a third country prior to a determination or adjudication of the same under the conditions set forth in this paragraph (e)(5)(iii);
units.action_summary: Department must advise alien at time of requesting withholding/deferral about possibility of third-country removal prior to adjudication under these conditions.

units.obligation_text: Provided, but did not accept, an opportunity to withdraw the request for withholding or deferral of removal in order to prevent such removal and, instead, proceed to removal pursuant to section 241(b) of the Act, as appropriate.
units.action_summary: Department must provide the alien an opportunity to withdraw the withholding/deferral request; removal only if alien was provided but did not accept the opportunity.

units.obligation_text: In determining whether an alien or a class of aliens can reasonably be regarded as a danger to the security of the United States under section 208(b)(2)(A)(iv) of the Act, the Attorney General may consider whether the alien exhibits symptoms consistent with being afflicted with any contagious or infectious disease ...
units.action_summary: Attorney General may consider disease symptoms, contacts, or originating place prevalence when determining whether an alien poses a danger to U.S. security.

units.obligation_text: Determined that because the disease is a communicable disease of public health significance ... the physical presence in the United States of aliens who are coming from such country or countries ... would cause a danger to the public health in the United States;
units.actor: the Attorney General and the Secretary of Homeland Security (in consultation with the Secretary of Health and Human Services)
units.action_summary: Attorney General and Secretary must jointly determine that presence of aliens from specified places would cause danger to U.S. public health.

units.obligation_text: Designated the foreign country or countries ... and the period of time or circumstances under which the Attorney General and the Secretary of Homeland Security jointly deem it necessary for the public health that aliens described ... be regarded as a danger to the security of the United States ...
units.actor: the Attorney General and the Secretary of Homeland Security (in consultation with the Secretary of Health and Human Services)
units.action_summary: Attorney General and Secretary must jointly designate places and periods/circumstances under which aliens are to be regarded as a danger.

units.obligation_text: Except as provided in paragraph (d)(3) of this section, an application for withholding of removal under section 241(b)(3) of the Act or under paragraph (c) of this section shall be denied if the applicant falls within section 241(b)(3)(B) of the Act ...
units.action_summary: Applications for withholding of removal must be denied if the applicant falls within specified statutory disqualifications.

units.obligation_text: If the evidence indicates the applicability of one or more of the grounds for denial of withholding enumerated in the Act, the applicant shall have the burden of proving by a preponderance of the evidence that such grounds do not apply.
units.action_summary: Applicant must prove by a preponderance of the evidence that the statutory grounds for denial do not apply.

units.obligation_text: In determining whether an alien or a class of aliens can reasonably be regarded as a danger to the security of the United States under section 241(b)(3)(B)(iv) of the Act, the Attorney General may consider whether the alien exhibits symptoms consistent with being afflicted with any contagious or infectious disease ...
units.action_summary: Attorney General may consider disease symptoms, contacts, and originating places when assessing danger for withholding of removal.

units.obligation_text: Nothing in this section or § 1208.17 shall prevent the Department of Homeland Security from removing an alien requesting protection to a third country other than a country to which removal is currently withheld or deferred.
units.action_summary: DHS may remove an alien requesting protection to a third country (subject to limitations).

units.obligation_text: Nothing in this section or § 1208.17 precludes the Department of Homeland Security from removing the alien to a third country prior to a determination or adjudication of the alien’s initial request for withholding or deferral of removal if the alien has not established that his or her life or freedom would be threatened on account of a protected ground in that third country and that he or she is not subject to the mandatory bar ... or that it is more likely than not that he or she would be tortured in that third country.
units.action_summary: DHS may remove an alien to a third country before adjudication if the alien hasn't established threats or likely torture in that country.

units.obligation_text: However, such a removal shall be executed only if the alien was: (i) Advised ... of the possibility of being removed to a third country prior to a determination ...; and (ii) Provided, but did not accept, an opportunity to withdraw the request for withholding or deferral of removal ...
units.action_summary: DHS may execute a third-country removal prior to adjudication only if the alien was advised of the possibility and provided an opportunity to withdraw the request (which the alien did not accept).

units.obligation_text: In the event that any provision in this part is stayed, enjoined, not implemented, or otherwise held invalid, the remaining provisions shall nevertheless be implemented as independent rules and continue in effect.
units.actor: the Attorney General or Department of Homeland Security (implementing authority, as applicable)
units.action_summary: If any provision is invalidated, the remaining provisions must still be implemented and remain in effect.

units.obligation_text: If the alien is found to be an alien ineligible for asylum under § 1208.13(c)(4), (6), or (7), then the immigration judge shall find that the alien does not have a credible fear of persecution with respect to the alien’s intention to apply for asylum. The immigration judge’s decision is final and may not be appealed.
units.action_summary: If alien is ineligible under specified provisions, the IJ must find no credible fear of persecution regarding asylum intent; that decision is final and cannot be appealed.

units.obligation_text: If the immigration judge concurs with the determinations of the asylum officer that the alien does not have a credible fear ... then the case shall be returned to the Department of Homeland Security for removal of the alien. The immigration judge’s decision is final and may not be appealed.
units.actor: immigration judge; Department of Homeland Security
units.action_summary: If IJ concurs with asylum officer's negative credible fear determination and lack of torture likelihood, the case must be returned to DHS for removal; IJ decision is final and not appealable.

units.obligation_text: If the immigration judge ... finds that the alien ... has a credible fear of persecution or torture ... the immigration judge shall vacate the order of the asylum officer ... and the Department of Homeland Security may commence removal proceedings under section 240 of the Act, during which time the alien may file an application for asylum or withholding of removal ... or remove the alien to a third country pursuant to 8 CFR 208.30(e)(5). If the Department of Homeland Security commences removal proceedings under section 240 of the Act, the immigration judge presiding in those proceedings shall consider all issues de novo, including whether the alien has established that it is more likely than not that he or she would be tortured in the prospective country of removal.
units.actor: immigration judge; Department of Homeland Security
units.action_summary: If IJ finds credible fear, IJ must vacate asylum officer's order; DHS may commence section 240 removal proceedings (or remove to third country); if DHS commences proceedings, the IJ must consider all issues de novo including torture risk.

title: 30 DAY COMMENTS CLOSE ON 12/2/2020; 60- DAY IC COMMENTS CLOSE ON 1/4/2021; Modification of Registration Requirement for Petitioners Seeking To File Cap- Subject H-1B Petitions

units.obligation_text: before a petitioner is eligible to file an H–1B cap-subject petition ... the prospective petitioner or its attorney or accredited representative must register to file a petition on behalf of an alien beneficiary electronically through the USCIS website (www.uscis.gov).
units.actor: the prospective petitioner or its attorney or accredited representative
units.action_summary: Register electronically on USCIS website before filing an H-1B cap-subject petition.

units.obligation_text: USCIS will rank and select registrations as set forth in paragraphs (h)(8)(iii)(A)(5) and (6) of this section.
units.action_summary: USCIS will rank and select registrations according to the rules in paragraphs (h)(8)(iii)(A)(5) and (6).
