units.obligation_text: For purposes of the ranking and selection process, USCIS will use the highest corresponding Occupational Employment Statistics (OES) wage level that the proffered wage will equal or exceed for the relevant Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) code and area(s) of intended employment.
units.action_summary: Rank registrations using the highest OES wage level that the proffered wage equals or exceeds for the relevant SOC and area.

units.obligation_text: If the proffered wage is lower than the OES wage level I, because it is based on a prevailing wage from another legitimate source (other than OES) or an independent authoritative source, USCIS will rank the registration in the same category as OES wage level I.
units.action_summary: If proffered wage is below OES level I (even if based on another legitimate source), rank it in OES wage level I category.

units.obligation_text: If the H–1B beneficiary will work in multiple locations, or in multiple positions if the registrant is an agent, USCIS will rank and select the registration based on the lowest corresponding OES wage level that the proffered wage will equal or exceed.
units.action_summary: For multiple work locations/positions, rank based on the lowest OES wage level that the proffered wage equals or exceeds.

units.obligation_text: Where there is no current OES prevailing wage information for the proffered position, USCIS will rank and select the registration based on the OES wage level that corresponds to the requirements of the proffered position.
units.action_summary: If no current OES data exists, rank based on the OES wage level matching the position's requirements.

units.obligation_text: If USCIS has received more registrations on the final registration date than necessary to meet the H–1B regular cap under Section 214(g)(1)(A) of the Act, USCIS will rank and select from among all registrations properly submitted on the final registration date on the basis of the highest OES wage level that the proffered wage equals or exceeds for the relevant SOC code and area of intended employment, beginning with OES wage level IV and proceeding in descending order with OES wage levels III, II, and I.
units.action_summary: If more registrations received on final date than needed, rank/select registrations by highest OES wage level descending (IV to I).

units.obligation_text: Where there is no current OES prevailing wage information for the proffered position, USCIS will rank and select petitions based on the appropriate wage level that corresponds to the requirements of the proffered position.
units.action_summary: If no current OES data, rank/select based on the wage level corresponding to the position's requirements.

units.obligation_text: If USCIS receives and ranks more registrations at a particular wage level than the projected number needed to meet the numerical limitation, USCIS will randomly select from all registrations within that particular wage level a sufficient number of registrations needed to reach the numerical limitation.
units.action_summary: If too many registrations at a wage level, randomly select enough to meet the cap.

units.obligation_text: If USCIS has received more than a sufficient number of registrations to meet the H–1B regular cap under Section 214(g)(1)(A) of the Act, USCIS will rank and select from among all registrations properly submitted during the initial registration period on the basis of the highest OES wage level that the proffered wage equals or exceeds for the relevant SOC code and area of intended employment, beginning with OES wage level IV and proceeding in descending order with OES wage levels III, II, and I.
units.action_summary: If initial registration period yields more registrations than needed, rank/select by highest OES wage level descending (IV to I).

units.obligation_text: Where there is no current OES prevailing wage information for the proffered position, USCIS will rank and select petitions based on the appropriate wage level that corresponds to the requirements of the proffered position.
units.action_summary: If no OES data during initial registration, rank/select based on the wage level matching position requirements.

units.obligation_text: If USCIS receives and ranks more registrations at a particular wage level than the projected number needed to meet the numerical limitation, USCIS will randomly select from all registrations within that particular wage level a sufficient number of registrations needed to reach the numerical limitation.
units.action_summary: If too many registrations at a wage level during initial registration, randomly select enough to meet the cap.

units.obligation_text: If on the final registration date, USCIS has received more registrations than necessary to meet the H–1B advanced degree exemption limitation under Section 214(g)(5)(C) of the Act, USCIS will rank and select, from among the registrations properly submitted on the final registration date that may be counted against the advanced degree exemption, the number of registrations necessary to reach the H–1B advanced degree exemption on the basis of the highest OES wage level that the proffered wage equals or exceeds for the relevant SOC code and in the area of intended employment, beginning with OES wage level IV and proceeding in descending order with OES wage levels III, II, and I.
units.action_summary: If more registrations than needed for advanced degree exemption on final date, rank/select those counted against exemption by highest OES wage level descending (IV to I).

units.obligation_text: Where there is no current OES prevailing wage information for the proffered position, USCIS will rank and select petitions based on the appropriate wage level that corresponds to the requirements of the proffered position.
units.action_summary: If no OES data for advanced degree exemption final-date registrations, rank/select based on the wage level matching position requirements.

units.obligation_text: If USCIS receives and ranks more registrations at a particular wage level than the projected number needed to meet the numerical limitation, USCIS will randomly select from all registrations within that particular wage level a sufficient number of registrations necessary to reach the H–1B advanced degree exemption.
units.action_summary: If too many advanced-degree registrations at a wage level, randomly select enough to meet the exemption limit.

units.obligation_text: USCIS will rank and select, from among the remaining registrations properly submitted during the initial registration period that may be counted against the advanced degree exemption numerical limitation, the number of registrations necessary to reach the H–1B advanced degree exemption on the basis of the highest OES wage level that the proffered wage equals or exceeds ... beginning with OES wage level IV and proceeding ...
units.action_summary: From remaining initial-period registrations that count toward the advanced-degree exemption, rank/select by highest OES wage level descending (IV to I).

units.obligation_text: Where there is no current OES prevailing wage information for the proffered position, USCIS will rank and select petitions based on the appropriate wage level that corresponds to the requirements of the proffered position.
units.action_summary: If no OES data for remaining initial-period advanced-degree registrations, rank/select based on wage level matching position requirements.

units.obligation_text: If USCIS receives and ranks more registrations at a particular wage level than the projected number needed to meet the numerical limitation, USCIS will randomly select from all registrations within that particular wage level a sufficient number of registrations necessary to reach the H–1B advanced degree exemption.
units.action_summary: If too many remaining advanced-degree registrations at a wage level, randomly select enough to meet the exemption limit.

units.obligation_text: Unselected registrations will remain on reserve for the applicable fiscal year.
units.action_summary: Keep unselected registrations on reserve for that fiscal year.

units.obligation_text: If USCIS determines that it needs to select additional registrations to receive the number of petitions projected to meet the numerical limitations, USCIS will select from among the registrations that are on reserve a sufficient number to meet the H–1B regular cap or advanced degree exemption numerical limitation, as applicable.
units.action_summary: If additional selections are needed, select sufficient registrations from the reserve to meet numerical limits.

units.obligation_text: If all of the registrations on reserve are selected and there are still fewer registrations than needed to reach the H–1B regular cap or advanced degree exemption numerical limitation, as applicable, USCIS may reopen the applicable registration period until USCIS determines that it has received a sufficient number of registrations projected to meet the H–1B regular cap or advanced degree exemption numerical limitation.
units.action_summary: USCIS may reopen the registration period if reserves are exhausted and more registrations are needed.

units.obligation_text: USCIS will monitor the number of registrations received and will notify the public of the date that USCIS has received the necessary number of registrations (the new "final registration date").
units.action_summary: Monitor registrations and notify public when necessary number received (new final registration date).

units.obligation_text: When selecting additional registrations under this paragraph, USCIS will rank and select properly submitted registrations in accordance with paragraphs (h)(8)(iii)(A)(1), (5), and (6) of this section.
units.action_summary: When selecting additional registrations, rank/select according to paragraphs (h)(8)(iii)(A)(1), (5), and (6).

units.obligation_text: If the registration period will be re-opened, USCIS will announce the start of the re-opened registration period on the USCIS website at www.uscis.gov.
units.action_summary: If registration is reopened, announce the start on USCIS website.

units.obligation_text: In addition to any other applicable requirements, a petitioner may file an H–1B petition for a beneficiary that may be counted under section 214(g)(1)(A) or eligible for exemption under section 214(g)(5)(C) of the Act only if the petition is based on a valid registration submitted by the petitioner, or its designated representative, on behalf of the beneficiary that was selected beforehand by USCIS.
units.action_summary: A petitioner may file an H-1B cap-subject petition only if it is based on a valid registration selected beforehand by USCIS.

units.obligation_text: The petition must be filed within the filing period indicated in the selection notice.
units.action_summary: File the petition within the filing period shown in the selection notice.

units.obligation_text: A petitioner may not substitute the beneficiary named in the original registration or transfer the registration to another petitioner.
units.action_summary: Petitioner cannot substitute a different beneficiary or transfer the registration to another petitioner.

units.obligation_text: If a petitioner files an H–1B cap-subject petition based on a registration that was not selected beforehand by USCIS, based on a registration for a different beneficiary than the beneficiary named in the petition, or based on a registration considered by USCIS to be invalid, the H–1B cap-subject petition will be rejected or denied.
units.action_summary: USCIS will reject or deny petitions based on registrations not selected, for a different beneficiary, or considered invalid.

units.obligation_text: USCIS will consider a registration to be invalid if the registration fee associated with the registration is declined, rejected, or canceled after submission as the registration fee is non-refundable and due at the time the registration is submitted.
units.action_summary: Treat a registration as invalid if its fee is declined, rejected, or canceled after submission; fee is non-refundable and due at submission.

units.obligation_text: the registration fee ... is non-refundable and due at the time the registration is submitted.
units.action_summary: Registration fee must be paid at time of submission and is non-refundable.

units.obligation_text: If USCIS determines that the statement of facts contained on the registration form is inaccurate, fraudulent, misrepresents any material fact, or is not true and correct, USCIS may reject or deny the petition or, if approved, may revoke the approval of a petition that was filed based on that registration.
units.action_summary: USCIS may reject or deny a petition (or revoke an approved petition) if the registration contains inaccurate, fraudulent, or materially misrepresentative facts.

units.obligation_text: USCIS also may deny or revoke approval of a subsequent new or amended petition filed by the petitioner, or a related entity, on behalf of the same beneficiary, if USCIS determines that the filing of the new or amended petition is part of the petitioner’s attempt to unfairly decrease the proffered wage to an amount that would be equivalent to a lower wage level, after listing a higher wage level on the registration to increase the odds of selection.
units.action_summary: USCIS may deny or revoke subsequent new or amended petitions if filed to unfairly decrease the proffered wage after listing a higher wage level to increase selection odds.

units.obligation_text: USCIS will not deny or revoke approval of such an amended or new petition solely on the basis of a different proffered wage if that wage does not correspond to a lower OES wage level than the wage level on which the registration selection was based.
units.action_summary: USCIS will not deny or revoke an amended/new petition solely because the proffered wage differs if it does not correspond to a lower OES wage level.

units.obligation_text: If the final receipt date is any of the first five business days on which petitions subject to the H–1B regular cap may be received, USCIS will select from among all the petitions properly submitted during the first five business days the number of petitions deemed necessary to meet the H–1B regular cap.
units.action_summary: If the cap is met within the first five business days, select necessary petitions from those submitted in that period.

units.obligation_text: If USCIS has received more petitions than necessary to meet the numerical limitation for the H–1B regular cap, USCIS will rank and select the petitions received on the basis of the highest Occupational Employment Statistics (OES) wage level that the proffered wage equals or exceeds for the relevant Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) code in the area of intended employment, beginning with OES wage level IV and proceeding in descending order with OES wage levels III, II, and I.
units.action_summary: When over-subscribed, rank/select petitions by highest OES wage level descending (IV to I).

units.obligation_text: Where there is no current OES prevailing wage information for the proffered position, USCIS will rank and select petitions based on the appropriate wage level that corresponds to the requirements of the proffered position.
units.action_summary: If no current OES data for petitions, rank/select based on wage level matching position requirements.

units.obligation_text: If the wage falls below an OES wage level I, USCIS will rank the petition in the same category as OES wage level I.
units.action_summary: If proffered wage is below OES level I, rank the petition in OES wage level I category.

units.obligation_text: USCIS will rank the petition in the same manner even if, instead of obtaining an OES prevailing wage, a petitioner elects to obtain a prevailing wage using another legitimate source (other than OES) or an independent authoritative source.
units.action_summary: Rank petitions the same way even if petitioner uses a non-OES legitimate prevailing wage source.

units.obligation_text: If USCIS receives and ranks more petitions at a particular wage level than the projected number needed to meet the numerical limitation, USCIS will randomly select from among all eligible petitions within that particular wage level a sufficient number of petitions needed to reach the numerical limitation.
units.action_summary: If too many petitions at a wage level, randomly select sufficient petitions to meet the limit.

units.obligation_text: After USCIS has received a sufficient number of petitions to meet the H–1B regular cap and, as applicable, completed the selection process of petitions for the H–1B regular cap, USCIS will determine whether there is a sufficient number of remaining petitions to meet the H–1B advanced degree exemption numerical limitation.
units.action_summary: After regular cap processing, determine if remaining petitions suffice to meet advanced degree exemption limit.

units.obligation_text: When calculating the number of petitions needed to meet the H–1B advanced degree exemption numerical limitation USCIS will take into account historical data related to approvals, denials, revocations, and other relevant factors.
units.action_summary: Consider historical approvals, denials, revocations, and other factors when calculating number needed for advanced degree exemption.

units.obligation_text: USCIS will monitor the number of petitions received and will announce on its website the date that it receives the number of petitions projected as needed to meet the H–1B advanced degree exemption numerical limitation (the "final receipt date").
units.action_summary: Monitor petitions and announce on website when the projected number for the advanced degree exemption is received (final receipt date).

units.obligation_text: If the final receipt date is any of the first five business days on which petitions subject to the H–1B advanced degree exemption may be received ... USCIS will select from among all the petitions properly submitted during the first five business days the number of petitions deemed necessary to meet the H–1B advanced degree exemption numerical limitation.
units.action_summary: If advanced degree exemption cap is reached within first five business days, select necessary petitions from those submitted in that period.

units.obligation_text: If USCIS has received more petitions than necessary to meet the numerical limitation for the H–1B advanced degree exemption, USCIS will rank and select the petitions received on the basis of the highest Occupational Employment Statistics (OES) wage level that the proffered wage equals or exceeds for the relevant Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) code in the area of intended employment, beginning with OES wage level IV and proceeding with OES wage levels III, II, and I.
units.action_summary: If over-subscribed for the advanced degree exemption, rank/select petitions by highest OES wage level descending (IV to I).

units.obligation_text: Where there is no current OES prevailing wage information for the proffered position, USCIS will rank and select petitions based on the appropriate wage level that corresponds to the requirements of the proffered position.
units.action_summary: If no OES data for advanced degree petitions, rank/select based on wage level matching position requirements.

units.obligation_text: If the proffered wage is below an OES wage level I, USCIS will rank the petition in the same category as OES wage level I.
units.action_summary: If proffered wage is below OES level I for advanced-degree petitions, rank it in OES level I category.

units.obligation_text: USCIS will rank the petition in the same manner even if, instead of obtaining an OES prevailing wage, a petitioner elects to obtain a prevailing wage using another legitimate source (other than OES) or an independent authoritative source.
units.action_summary: Rank advanced-degree petitions the same way even if petitioner uses non-OES legitimate prevailing wage source.

units.obligation_text: If USCIS receives and ranks more petitions at a particular wage level than necessary to meet the numerical limitation for the H–1B advanced degree exemption, USCIS will randomly select from among all eligible petitions within that particular wage level a sufficient number of petitions needed to reach the numerical limitation.
units.action_summary: If too many advanced-degree petitions at a wage level, randomly select enough to meet the exemption limit.

units.obligation_text: The petition may be denied if it is determined that the statements on the registration or petition were inaccurate.
units.action_summary: USCIS may deny a petition if statements on registration or petition are inaccurate.

units.obligation_text: The petition will be denied if it is determined that the statements on the registration or petition were fraudulent or misrepresented a material fact.
units.action_summary: USCIS will deny a petition if statements are fraudulent or materially misrepresent facts.

units.obligation_text: A petition also may be denied if it is not based on a valid registration submitted by the petitioner (or its designated representative), or a successor in interest, for the beneficiary named in the petition.
units.action_summary: USCIS may deny a petition not based on a valid registration submitted for the named beneficiary.

units.obligation_text: A valid registration must represent a legitimate job offer.
units.action_summary: Registrations must represent legitimate job offers.

units.obligation_text: USCIS also may deny a subsequent new or amended petition filed by the petitioner, or a related entity, on behalf of the same beneficiary, if USCIS determines that the filing of the new or amended petition is part of the petitioner’s attempt to unfairly increase the odds of selection during the registration or petition selection process, as applicable, such as by reducing the proffered wage to an amount that would be equivalent to a lower wage level than that indicated on the original petition.
units.action_summary: USCIS may deny a new/amended petition if it concludes the filing was intended to unfairly increase selection odds (e.g., by reducing the proffered wage).

units.obligation_text: USCIS will not deny such an amended or new petition solely on the basis of a different proffered wage if that wage does not correspond to a lower OES wage level than the wage level on which the registration or petition selection, as applicable, was based.
units.action_summary: USCIS will not deny an amended/new petition solely because the proffered wage differs if it does not equate to a lower OES wage level.

units.obligation_text: The statement of facts contained in the petition; the registration, if applicable; or on the temporary labor certification or labor condition application; was not true and correct, inaccurate, fraudulent, or misrepresented a material fact;
units.action_summary: Forms or associated statements that are untrue, inaccurate, fraudulent, or materially misrepresent facts are identified grounds (for action by USCIS).

units.obligation_text: The petitioner, or a related entity, filed a new or amended petition on behalf of the same beneficiary, if USCIS determines that the filing of the new or amended petition is part of the petitioner’s attempt to unfairly increase the odds of selection during the registration or petition selection process, as applicable, such as by reducing the proffered wage to an amount that would be equivalent to a lower wage level than that indicated on the registration, or the original petition if the registration process was suspended.
units.action_summary: Filing new/amended petitions that USCIS determines were meant to unfairly increase selection odds (e.g., reducing proffered wage) is a specified ground for action.

units.obligation_text: USCIS will not revoke approval of such an amended or new petition solely on the basis of a different proffered wage if that wage does not correspond to a lower OES wage level than the wage level on which the registration or petition selection, as applicable, was based;
units.action_summary: USCIS will not revoke approval solely because the proffered wage differs if it does not correspond to a lower OES wage level than the selection basis.

title: Removal of International Entrepreneur Parole Program

units.obligation_text: DHS withdraws the proposed rule published May 29, 2018 at 83 FR 24415 as of May 11, 2021
units.action_summary: DHS withdraws the May 29, 2018 proposed rule (83 FR 24415) effective May 11, 2021.

units.obligation_text: Such applications will continue to be decided consistent with the Secretary's statutory authority to grant parole on a case-by-case basis
units.action_summary: Applications for IE parole will continue to be decided in accordance with the Secretary's statutory parole authority on a case-by-case basis.

units.obligation_text: when it is determined that the applicant will provide a significant public benefit and that the applicant merits a favorable exercise of discretion
units.action_summary: Decisionmakers may grant parole under the Secretary's authority only when the applicant provides a significant public benefit and merits favorable discretion.

units.obligation_text: continuing to administer the IE parole program, in accordance with 8 CFR 212.19
units.action_summary: DHS/USCIS will continue to administer the International Entrepreneur parole program under 8 CFR 212.19.

title: Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals

units.obligation_text: Application for Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals, Form I–821D: $85.
units.action_summary: Pay a $85 filing fee for Form I-821D (DACA application).

units.obligation_text: During this period of forbearance, on the basis of this subpart only, DACA recipients who can demonstrate an economic need may apply to USCIS for employment authorization pursuant to 8 CFR 274a.13 and 274a.12(c)(33).
units.actor: DACA recipients who can demonstrate an economic need
units.action_summary: May apply to USCIS for employment authorization if they demonstrate economic need.

units.obligation_text: USCIS may consider requests for Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals submitted by aliens described in paragraph (b) of this section.
units.action_summary: USCIS may consider DACA requests submitted by aliens meeting the threshold criteria.

units.obligation_text: A pending request for deferred action under this section does not authorize or confer any interim immigration benefits such as employment authorization or advance parole.
units.action_summary: A pending DACA request does not confer interim immigration benefits (e.g., employment authorization, advance parole).

units.obligation_text: Subject to paragraph (c) of this section, the requestor bears the burden of demonstrating by a preponderance of the evidence that he or she meets the threshold criteria described in paragraph (b) of this section.
units.action_summary: The requestor must prove by a preponderance of the evidence that they meet the threshold criteria.

units.obligation_text: Subject to paragraph (c) of this section, a request for deferred action under this section may be granted only if USCIS determines in its sole discretion that the alien meets each of the following threshold criteria and merits a favorable exercise of discretion:
units.action_summary: A DACA grant may be issued only if USCIS determines the alien meets each listed threshold criterion and merits favorable discretion.

units.obligation_text: Came to the United States under the age of 16. The requestor must demonstrate that he or she first resided in the United States before his or her sixteenth birthday.
units.action_summary: Demonstrate that first residence in the U.S. occurred before turning 16.

units.obligation_text: Continuous residence in the United States from June 15, 2007, to the time of filing of the request. The requestor also must demonstrate that he or she has been residing in the United States continuously from June 15, 2007, to the time of filing of the request.
units.action_summary: Demonstrate continuous residence in the U.S. from June 15, 2007 through the filing date.

units.obligation_text: Unauthorized travel outside of the United States on or after August 15, 2012, will interrupt continuous residence, regardless of whether it was otherwise brief, casual, and innocent.
units.action_summary: Unauthorized travel outside the U.S. on or after Aug 15, 2012 breaks continuous residence.

units.obligation_text: The absence was short and reasonably calculated to accomplish the purpose for the absence;
units.action_summary: To be considered brief/innocent, the absence must have been short and reasonably calculated to accomplish its purpose.

units.obligation_text: The absence was not because of a post-June 15, 2007 order of exclusion, deportation, or removal;
units.action_summary: The absence must not have been due to an order of exclusion, deportation, or removal issued after June 15, 2007.

units.obligation_text: The absence was not because of a post-June 15, 2007 order of voluntary departure, or an administrative grant of voluntary departure before the requestor was placed in exclusion, deportation, or removal proceedings;
units.action_summary: The absence must not have been due to a voluntary departure order or administrative grant of voluntary departure issued after June 15, 2007 before proceedings.

units.obligation_text: The purpose of the trip, and the requestor’s actions while outside the United States, were not contrary to law.
units.action_summary: The trip's purpose and the requestor's conduct abroad must not have been contrary to law.

units.obligation_text: Physical presence in the United States. The requestor must demonstrate that he or she was physically present in the United States both on June 15, 2012, and at the time of filing of the request for Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals under this section.
units.action_summary: Show physical presence in the U.S. on June 15, 2012 and at the time of filing.

units.obligation_text: Lack of lawful immigration status. Both on June 15, 2012, and at the time of filing of the request for Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals under this section, the requestor must not have been in a lawful immigration status.
units.action_summary: Must not have been in lawful immigration status on June 15, 2012 and at time of filing.

units.obligation_text: If the requestor was in lawful immigration status at any time before June 15, 2012, or at any time after June 15, 2012, and before the submission date of the request, he or she must submit evidence that that lawful status had expired or otherwise terminated prior to those dates.
units.action_summary: If the requestor was previously in lawful status, must submit evidence showing that status expired/terminated before the relevant dates.

units.obligation_text: Education or veteran status. The requestor must currently be enrolled in school, have graduated or obtained a certificate of completion from high school, have obtained a General Educational Development certificate, or be an honorably discharged veteran of the United States Coast Guard or Armed Forces of the United States.
units.action_summary: Must meet one of the listed education or honorable veteran status conditions.

units.obligation_text: The requestor must currently be enrolled in school.
units.action_summary: Be currently enrolled in school.

units.obligation_text: The requestor must have graduated or obtained a certificate of completion from high school.
units.action_summary: Have graduated or obtained a high school certificate of completion.

units.obligation_text: The requestor must have obtained a General Educational Development certificate.
units.action_summary: Have obtained a GED certificate.

units.obligation_text: The requestor must be an honorably discharged veteran of the United States Coast Guard or Armed Forces of the United States.
units.action_summary: Be an honorably discharged veteran of US Coast Guard or Armed Forces.

units.obligation_text: Criminal history and public safety. The requestor must not have been convicted ... of a felony, a misdemeanor described in this paragraph (b)(6), or three or more other misdemeanors not occurring on the same date and not arising out of the same act, omission, or scheme of misconduct, or otherwise pose a threat to national security or public safety.
units.action_summary: Must not have disqualifying criminal convictions (felony, specified misdemeanors, or three+ other misdemeanors) or otherwise pose a threat to national security/public safety.

units.obligation_text: A single misdemeanor is disqualifying if it is an offense of domestic violence; sexual abuse or exploitation; burglary; unlawful possession or use of a firearm; drug distribution or trafficking; or driving under the influence.
units.action_summary: Certain named misdemeanors (domestic violence, sexual abuse, burglary, firearm offenses, drug distribution, DUI) are disqualifying even as a single misdemeanor.

units.obligation_text: If not an offense listed above, [a single misdemeanor] is one for which the individual was sentenced to time in custody of more than 90 days.
units.action_summary: A non-listed misdemeanor is disqualifying if sentenced to more than 90 days in custody (time actually served).

units.obligation_text: Or otherwise pose a threat to national security or public safety.
units.action_summary: USCIS may find the requestor disqualified if they pose a threat to national security or public safety.

units.obligation_text: Age at time of request. The requestor must have been born on or after June 16, 1981. Additionally, the requestor must be at least 15 years of age at the time of filing his or her request, unless, at the time of his or her request, he or she is in removal proceedings, has a final order of removal, or has a voluntary departure order.
units.action_summary: Must have been born on or after June 16, 1981 and be at least 15 at filing, except in specified circumstances.

units.obligation_text: Exception: if, at the time of his or her request, he or she is in removal proceedings, has a final order of removal, or has a voluntary departure order.
units.action_summary: Applicants under 15 may still apply if they are in removal proceedings, have a final order of removal, or have a voluntary departure order.

units.obligation_text: Deferred action requests submitted under this section are determined on a case-by-case basis. Even if the threshold criteria in paragraph (b) are all found to have been met, USCIS retains the discretion to assess the individual’s circumstances and to determine that any factor specific to that individual makes deferred action inappropriate.
units.action_summary: USCIS may deny DACA requests on discretionary grounds even if threshold criteria are met.

units.obligation_text: A request for Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals must be filed in the manner and on the form designated by USCIS, with the required fee, including any biometrics required by 8 CFR 103.16.
units.action_summary: File the DACA request on the USCIS-designated form, manner, and with required fee and biometrics.

units.obligation_text: A request for Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals may also contain a request for employment authorization filed pursuant to 8 CFR 274a.12(c)(33) and 274a.13.
units.action_summary: May include a concurrent request for employment authorization with the DACA request.

units.obligation_text: If a request for Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals does not include a request for employment authorization, employment authorization may still be requested subsequent to approval for deferred action, but not for a period of time to exceed the grant of deferred action.
units.action_summary: May request employment authorization after approval, but only for a period not exceeding the term of deferred action.

units.obligation_text: All requests for Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals, including any requests made by aliens in removal proceedings before EOIR, must be filed with USCIS.
units.action_summary: All DACA requests must be filed with USCIS (including those by aliens in removal proceedings).

units.obligation_text: USCIS has exclusive jurisdiction to consider requests for Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals.
units.action_summary: Only USCIS may consider DACA requests; it has exclusive jurisdiction.

units.obligation_text: EOIR shall have no jurisdiction to consider requests for Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals or to review USCIS approvals or denials of such requests.
units.action_summary: EOIR may not consider DACA requests or review USCIS decisions on them.

units.obligation_text: A voluntary departure order or a final order of exclusion, deportation, or removal is not a bar to requesting Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals.
units.action_summary: Having a voluntary departure order or final removal order does not bar requesting DACA.

units.obligation_text: An alien who is in removal proceedings may request Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals regardless of whether those proceedings have been administratively closed.
units.action_summary: Aliens in removal proceedings may request DACA even if proceedings are administratively closed.

units.obligation_text: An alien who is in immigration detention may request Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals but may not be approved for Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals unless the alien is released from detention by ICE prior to USCIS’ decision on the Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals request.
units.action_summary: Detained aliens may request DACA, but USCIS may not approve while detained unless ICE releases the alien before USCIS decision.

units.obligation_text: USCIS may request additional evidence from the requestor, including, but not limited to, by notice, interview, or other appearance of the requestor.
units.action_summary: USCIS may request additional evidence via notice, interview, or other appearance.

units.obligation_text: USCIS may deny a request for Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals without prior issuance of a request for evidence or notice of intent to deny.
units.action_summary: USCIS may deny a DACA request without first issuing an RFE or notice of intent to deny.

units.obligation_text: A grant of Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals will be provided for an initial or renewal period of 2 years, subject to DHS’s discretion.
units.action_summary: Grants of DACA will be issued for initial or renewal periods of 2 years, subject to DHS discretion.

units.obligation_text: In considering requests for Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals, USCIS may consult, as it deems appropriate in its discretion and without notice to the requestor, with any other component or office of DHS, including ICE and CBP, any other Federal agency, or any State or local law enforcement agency, in accordance with paragraph (e) of this section.
units.action_summary: USCIS may consult other DHS components, federal agencies, or state/local law enforcement when considering DACA requests.

units.obligation_text: USCIS will notify the requestor and, if applicable, the requestor’s attorney of record or accredited representative of the decision in writing.
units.action_summary: USCIS will provide written notice of its decision to the requestor and counsel/representative if applicable.

units.obligation_text: Denial of a request for Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals does not bar a requestor from applying for any benefit or form of relief under the immigration laws or requesting any other form of prosecutorial discretion, including another request for Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals.
units.action_summary: Denial of DACA does not prevent the requestor from applying for other immigration benefits or submitting another DACA request.

units.obligation_text: If USCIS denies a request for Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals under this section, USCIS will not issue a Notice to Appear or refer a requestor’s case to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement for possible enforcement action based on such denial unless the case involves denial for fraud, a threat to national security, or public safety concerns.
units.action_summary: USCIS will not issue an NTA or refer the case to ICE based solely on DACA denial, except in specified circumstances.

units.obligation_text: Exception: unless the case involves denial for fraud, a threat to national security, or public safety concerns.
units.action_summary: Exceptions permitting NTA issuance/referral include fraud, threats to national security, or public safety concerns.

units.obligation_text: There is no administrative appeal from a denial of a request for Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals.
units.action_summary: No administrative appeal is available from a DACA denial.

units.obligation_text: The alien may not file, pursuant to 8 CFR 103.5 or otherwise, a motion to reopen or reconsider a denial of a request for Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals.
units.action_summary: The alien may not file a motion to reopen or reconsider a DACA denial under 8 CFR 103.5 or otherwise.

units.obligation_text: Discretionary termination. USCIS may terminate a grant of Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals at any time in its discretion with or without issuance of a notice of intent to terminate.
units.action_summary: USCIS may terminate a DACA grant at any time, with or without prior notice.

units.obligation_text: Automatic termination. Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals is terminated automatically without notice upon certain events.
units.action_summary: DACA grants automatically terminate without notice upon specified events (listed in subitems).

units.obligation_text: Filing of a Notice to Appear for removal proceedings with EOIR, unless the Notice to Appear is issued by USCIS solely as part of an asylum case referral to EOIR;
units.actor: filing of a Notice to Appear / grant termination
units.action_summary: Filing of an NTA terminates DACA automatically, except where USCIS issues the NTA solely as part of an asylum referral to EOIR.

units.obligation_text: Departure of the noncitizen from the United States without advance parole.
units.action_summary: Leaving the U.S. without advance parole triggers automatic termination of DACA.

units.obligation_text: Exception: unless the Notice to Appear is issued by USCIS solely as part of an asylum case referral to EOIR.
units.action_summary: An NTA issued by USCIS solely as part of an asylum referral to EOIR does not automatically terminate DACA.

units.obligation_text: Upon termination of a grant of Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals, any grant of employment authorization pursuant to § 274a.12(c)(33) of this chapter will automatically terminate in accordance with § 274a.14(a)(1)(iv) of this chapter.
units.action_summary: Employment authorization issued under §274a.12(c)(33) automatically terminates when DACA is terminated, per §274a.14(a)(1)(iv).

units.obligation_text: Notice of intent to revoke employment authorization is not required pursuant to § 274a.14(a)(2) of this chapter.
units.action_summary: USCIS is not required to issue a notice of intent to revoke employment authorization when it automatically terminates under §274a.14(a)(2).

units.obligation_text: Information contained in a request for Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals related to the requestor will not be used by DHS for the purpose of initiating immigration enforcement proceedings against such requestor, unless DHS is initiating immigration enforcement proceedings against the requestor due to a criminal offense, fraud, a threat to national security, or public safety concerns.
units.action_summary: DHS will not use information in a DACA request to initiate immigration enforcement against the requestor, except for specified exceptions (criminal offense, fraud, national security/public safety threats).

units.obligation_text: Exception: when DHS is initiating immigration enforcement proceedings against the requestor due to a criminal offense, fraud, a threat to national security, or public safety concerns.
units.action_summary: DHS may use DACA request information to initiate enforcement if there is criminal conduct, fraud, or threats to national security/public safety.

units.obligation_text: Information contained in a request for Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals related to the requestor’s family members or guardians will not be used for immigration enforcement purposes against such family members or guardians.
units.action_summary: DHS will not use information in a DACA request to initiate immigration enforcement against the requestor's family members or guardians.

units.obligation_text: Except as provided for in paragraph (c)(33) of this section, an alien who has been granted deferred action, an act of administrative convenience to the government that gives some cases lower priority, if the alien establishes an economic necessity for employment.
units.actor: an alien who has been granted deferred action
units.action_summary: Aliens granted deferred action may be authorized to accept employment if they establish economic necessity (subject to paragraph (c)(33)).

units.obligation_text: An alien who has been granted deferred action pursuant to 8 CFR 236.21 through 236.23, Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals, if the alien establishes an economic necessity for employment.
units.actor: an alien granted Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA)
units.action_summary: A DACA recipient may be authorized to accept employment if they establish economic necessity.

title: Circumvention of Lawful Pathways

units.obligation_text: An alien who ... enters the United States at the southwest land border without documents sufficient for lawful admission ... after traveling through a country other than the alien’s country of citizenship ... that is a party to the 1951 United Nations Convention ... is subject to a rebuttable presumption of ineligibility for asylum unless the alien, or a member of the alien’s family ... with whom the alien is traveling: (i) Was provided appropriate authorization to travel to the United States to seek parole, pursuant to a DHS-approved parole process; (ii) Presented at a port of entry, pursuant to a pre-scheduled time and place, or presented at a port of entry without a pre-scheduled time and place, if the alien demonstrates by a preponderance of the evidence that it was not possible to access or use the DHS scheduling system due to language barrier, illiteracy, significant technical failure, or other ongoing and serious obstacle; or (iii) Sought asylum or other protection in a country through which the noncitizen traveled and received a final decision denying that application.
units.actor: an alien who entered the United States as described
units.action_summary: Such an alien is subject to a rebuttable presumption of ineligibility for asylum unless one of three specified conditions is met.

units.obligation_text: Was provided appropriate authorization to travel to the United States to seek parole, pursuant to a DHS-approved parole process;
units.actor: the alien or a member of the alien's family with whom the alien is traveling
units.action_summary: Authorization to travel to the U.S. to seek parole via a DHS-approved parole process qualifies the alien to avoid the presumption.

units.obligation_text: Presented at a port of entry, pursuant to a pre-scheduled time and place, or presented at a port of entry without a pre-scheduled time and place, if the alien demonstrates by a preponderance of the evidence that it was not possible to access or use the DHS scheduling system due to language barrier, illiteracy, significant technical failure, or other ongoing and serious obstacle;
units.actor: the alien or a member of the alien's family with whom the alien is traveling
units.action_summary: Presenting at a port of entry (either at a pre-scheduled time or without one when the alien demonstrates inability to use DHS scheduling) qualifies to avoid the presumption.

units.obligation_text: Sought asylum or other protection in a country through which the noncitizen traveled and received a final decision denying that application.
units.actor: the alien or a member of the alien's family with whom the alien is traveling
units.action_summary: If the alien sought and received a final denial of asylum/other protection in a transit country, that qualifies to avoid the presumption.

units.obligation_text: The presumption in paragraph (a)(1) of this section can be rebutted if an alien demonstrates by a preponderance of the evidence that exceptionally compelling circumstances exist, including if the alien demonstrates that, at the time of entry, the alien or a member of the alien’s family ... with whom the alien is traveling: (i) Faced an acute medical emergency; (ii) Faced an imminent and extreme threat to life or safety ...; or (iii) Satisfied the definition of 'victim of a severe form of trafficking in persons' provided in § 214.11 of this chapter.
units.action_summary: The presumption may be rebutted if the alien shows by a preponderance of evidence that exceptionally compelling circumstances existed (including listed circumstances).

units.obligation_text: Faced an acute medical emergency;
units.actor: the alien or a member of the alien's family with whom the alien is traveling
units.action_summary: Having faced an acute medical emergency at the time of entry is an example of exceptionally compelling circumstances that may rebut the presumption.

units.obligation_text: Faced an imminent and extreme threat to life or safety, such as an imminent threat of rape, kidnapping, torture, or murder;
units.actor: the alien or a member of the alien's family with whom the alien is traveling
units.action_summary: Facing an imminent and extreme threat to life or safety is an example of exceptionally compelling circumstances that may rebut the presumption.

units.obligation_text: Satisfied the definition of 'victim of a severe form of trafficking in persons' provided in § 214.11 of this chapter.
units.actor: the alien or a member of the alien's family with whom the alien is traveling
units.action_summary: Meeting the trafficking victim definition constitutes an exceptionally compelling circumstance that may rebut the presumption.

units.obligation_text: The presumption in paragraph (a)(1) of this section shall necessarily be rebutted if an alien demonstrates by a preponderance of the evidence any of the circumstances in paragraphs (a)(2)(i) through (iii) of this section.
units.action_summary: If the alien demonstrates any of the listed circumstances, the presumption must be treated as rebutted.

units.obligation_text: Unaccompanied alien children, as defined in 6 U.S.C. 279(g)(2), are not subject to paragraph (a)(1) of this section.
units.action_summary: Unaccompanied alien children are exempt from the presumption of ineligibility in (a)(1).

units.obligation_text: For applications filed by aliens who entered the United States between [EFFECTIVE DATE OF FINAL RULE] and [24 MONTHS AFTER EFFECTIVE DATE OF FINAL RULE], also refer to the provisions on asylum eligibility described in § 208.33.
units.action_summary: Applications by aliens who entered in the specified period are to be considered under the asylum-eligibility provisions in § 208.33.

units.obligation_text: The asylum officer shall first determine whether the alien is covered by the presumption in paragraph (a)(1) of this section and, if so, whether the alien has rebutted the presumption in accordance with paragraph (a)(2) of this section.
units.action_summary: Asylum officers must first determine whether the presumption applies and whether it has been rebutted.

units.obligation_text: If the alien is covered by the presumption in paragraph (a)(1) of this section and fails to rebut the presumption in accordance with paragraph (a)(2) of this section, then the asylum officer shall enter a negative credible fear determination with respect to the alien’s asylum claim and continue to consider the alien’s claim under paragraph (c)(2) of this section.
units.action_summary: If the alien is covered by the presumption and fails to rebut it, the asylum officer must enter a negative credible fear determination and proceed under (c)(2).

units.obligation_text: If the alien is not covered by the presumption in paragraph (a)(1) of this section or has rebutted the presumption in accordance with paragraph (a)(2) of this section, the asylum officer shall follow the procedures in § 208.30.
units.action_summary: If the presumption does not apply or is rebutted, the asylum officer must follow § 208.30 procedures.

units.obligation_text: In cases in which the asylum officer enters a negative credible fear determination under paragraph (c)(1)(i) of this section, the asylum officer will assess whether the alien has established a reasonable possibility of persecution ... or torture, with respect to the prospective country or countries of removal identified pursuant to section 241(b) of the Act.
units.action_summary: When a negative credible fear determination is entered, the asylum officer must assess whether the alien has a reasonable possibility of persecution or torture in the prospective removal country(ies).

units.obligation_text: In cases described in paragraph (c)(2)(i) of this section, if the alien establishes a reasonable possibility of persecution or torture with respect to the identified country of removal, the Department will issue a Form I–862, Notice to Appear.
units.action_summary: If the alien establishes a reasonable possibility of persecution/torture, DHS will issue a Notice to Appear (Form I–862).

units.obligation_text: In removal proceedings, the alien may apply for asylum, withholding of removal under section 241(b)(3) of the Act, withholding of removal under the Convention Against Torture, or any other form of relief or protection for which they are eligible.
units.action_summary: In removal proceedings commenced after issuance of a Notice to Appear, the alien is permitted to apply for asylum/withholding of removal or other relief for which eligible.

units.obligation_text: In cases described in paragraph (c)(2)(i) of this section, if an alien fails to establish a reasonable possibility of persecution or torture with respect to the identified country of removal, the asylum officer will provide the alien with a written notice of decision and inquire whether the alien wishes to have an immigration judge review the negative credible fear determinations.
units.action_summary: If the alien fails to show a reasonable possibility, the asylum officer must provide a written decision and ask if the alien wants IJ review of the negative determination.

units.obligation_text: The alien must indicate whether he or she desires such review on a Record of Negative Fear Finding and Request for Review by Immigration Judge.
units.action_summary: The alien is required to indicate on the specified form whether they want immigration judge review.

units.obligation_text: Only if the alien requests such review by so indicating on the Record of Negative Fear shall the asylum officer serve the alien with a Notice of Referral to Immigration Judge.
units.action_summary: The asylum officer must serve a Notice of Referral to the IJ only if the alien requests review on the Record of Negative Fear.
units.modal_raw: shall (only if the alien requests review)

units.obligation_text: The record of determination, including copies of the Notice of Referral to Immigration Judge, the asylum officer’s notes, the summary of the material facts, and other materials upon which the determination was based shall be provided to the immigration judge with the negative determination.
units.action_summary: The asylum officer/DHS must provide the IJ with the record of determination and related materials when sending a negative determination.

units.obligation_text: Immigration judges will evaluate the case as provided in 8 CFR 1208.33(c).
units.action_summary: Immigration judges are to evaluate the case under the procedures set forth in 8 CFR 1208.33(c).

units.obligation_text: The case shall then proceed as set forth in paragraphs (c)(2)(v)(A) through (C) of this section.
units.action_summary: After referral, the case must proceed according to the procedures in (c)(2)(v)(A)-(C).

units.obligation_text: Where the immigration judge issues a positive credible fear determination under 8 CFR 1208.33(c)(2)(i), the case shall proceed under 8 CFR 1208.30(g)(2)(iv)(B).
units.action_summary: If the IJ issues a positive credible fear finding under the specified provision, the case must proceed under the referenced §208.30(g)(2)(iv)(B) procedures.

units.obligation_text: Where the immigration judge issues a positive credible fear determination under 8 CFR 1208.33(c)(2)(ii), DHS shall issue a Form I–862, Notice to Appear, to commence removal proceedings under section 240 of the Act.
units.action_summary: If the IJ issues a positive credible fear finding under the specified provision, DHS is required to issue a Notice to Appear to start removal proceedings.

units.obligation_text: In removal proceedings, the alien may apply for asylum, withholding of removal under section 241(b)(3) of the Act, withholding of removal under the Convention Against Torture, or any other form of relief or protection for which the alien is eligible.
units.action_summary: Upon commencement of removal proceedings, the alien is permitted to apply for asylum or other forms of relief for which eligible.

units.obligation_text: Where the immigration judge issues a negative credible fear determination, the case shall be returned to DHS for removal of the alien.
units.action_summary: If the IJ issues a negative credible fear finding, the case must be returned to DHS for removal of the alien.

units.obligation_text: No appeal shall lie from the immigration judge’s decision and no request for reconsideration may be submitted to USCIS.
units.action_summary: There is no right of appeal from the IJ's decision and no requests for reconsideration may be submitted to USCIS (subject to the one discretionary exception below).

units.obligation_text: Nevertheless, USCIS may, in its sole discretion, reconsider a negative determination.
units.action_summary: USCIS has discretionary permission to reconsider a negative credible fear determination.

units.obligation_text: For applications filed by aliens who entered the United States between [EFFECTIVE DATE OF FINAL RULE] and [24 MONTHS AFTER EFFECTIVE DATE OF FINAL RULE], also refer to the provisions on asylum eligibility described in § 1208.33.
units.action_summary: Applications by aliens who entered in the specified period are to be considered under the asylum-eligibility provisions in §1208.33.

units.obligation_text: An alien who ... enters the United States at the southwest land border without documents sufficient for lawful admission ... after traveling through a country other than the alien’s country of citizenship ... that is a party to the 1951 United Nations Convention ... is subject to a rebuttable presumption of ineligibility for asylum unless the alien, or a member of the alien’s family ... with whom the alien is traveling: (i) Was provided appropriate authorization to travel to the United States to seek parole, pursuant to a DHS-approved parole process; (ii) Presented at a port of entry, pursuant to a pre-scheduled time and place, or presented at a port of entry, without a pre-scheduled time and place, if the alien demonstrates by a preponderance of the evidence that it was not possible to access or use the DHS scheduling system due to language barrier, illiteracy, significant technical failure, or other ongoing and serious obstacle; or (iii) Sought asylum or other protection in a country through which the noncitizen traveled and received a final decision denying that application.
units.actor: an alien who entered the United States as described
units.action_summary: Such an alien is subject to a rebuttable presumption of ineligibility for asylum unless one of three specified conditions is met (mirrors §208.33).

units.obligation_text: Was provided appropriate authorization to travel to the United States to seek parole, pursuant to a DHS-approved parole process;
units.actor: the alien or a member of the alien's family with whom the alien is traveling
units.action_summary: Authorization to travel to the U.S. to seek parole via a DHS-approved parole process qualifies the alien to avoid the presumption.

units.obligation_text: Presented at a port of entry, pursuant to a pre-scheduled time and place, or presented at a port of entry, without a pre-scheduled time and place, if the alien demonstrates by a preponderance of the evidence that it was not possible to access or use the DHS scheduling system due to language barrier, illiteracy, significant technical failure, or other ongoing and serious obstacle;
units.actor: the alien or a member of the alien's family with whom the alien is traveling
units.action_summary: Presenting at a port of entry (at a pre-scheduled time or without one when unable to use DHS scheduling) qualifies to avoid the presumption.

units.obligation_text: Sought asylum or other protection in a country through which the noncitizen traveled and received a final decision denying that application.
units.actor: the alien or a member of the alien's family with whom the alien is traveling
units.action_summary: A final denial of asylum/other protection in a transit country qualifies to avoid the presumption.

units.obligation_text: The presumption in paragraph (a)(1) of this section can be rebutted if an alien demonstrates by a preponderance of the evidence that exceptionally compelling circumstances exist, including if the alien demonstrates that, at the time of entry, the alien or a member of the alien’s family ... with whom the alien is traveling: (i) Faced an acute medical emergency; (ii) Faced an imminent and extreme threat to life or safety ...; or (iii) Satisfied the definition of 'victim of a severe form of trafficking in persons' provided in 8 CFR 214.11.
units.action_summary: The presumption may be rebutted if the alien shows exceptionally compelling circumstances (including listed circumstances) by a preponderance of the evidence.

units.obligation_text: Faced an acute medical emergency;
units.actor: the alien or a member of the alien's family with whom the alien is traveling
units.action_summary: Facing an acute medical emergency is an example of an exceptionally compelling circumstance to rebut the presumption.

units.obligation_text: Faced an imminent and extreme threat to life or safety, such as an imminent threat of rape, kidnapping, torture, or murder;
units.actor: the alien or a member of the alien's family with whom the alien is traveling
units.action_summary: Facing an imminent and extreme threat to life or safety is an example of an exceptionally compelling circumstance to rebut the presumption.

units.obligation_text: Satisfied the definition of 'victim of a severe form of trafficking in persons' provided in 8 CFR 214.11.
units.actor: the alien or a member of the alien's family with whom the alien is traveling
units.action_summary: Meeting the trafficking victim definition is an example of an exceptionally compelling circumstance to rebut the presumption.

units.obligation_text: The presumption in paragraph (a)(1) of this section shall necessarily be rebutted if an alien demonstrates by a preponderance of the evidence any of the circumstances in paragraphs (a)(2)(i) through (iii) of this section.
units.action_summary: Demonstration of any listed circumstance requires that the presumption be treated as rebutted.

units.obligation_text: Unaccompanied alien children, as defined in 6 U.S.C. 279(g)(2), are not subject to paragraph (a)(1) of this section.
units.action_summary: Unaccompanied alien children are exempt from the presumption in (a)(1).

units.obligation_text: Where an asylum officer has issued a negative credible fear determination pursuant to 8 CFR 208.33(c), and the alien has requested immigration judge review of that credible fear determination, the immigration judge shall evaluate the case de novo, as specified in paragraph (c)(2) of this section. In doing so, the immigration judge shall take into account the credibility of the statements made by the alien in support of the alien’s claim and such other facts as are known to the immigration judge.
units.action_summary: If IJ review is requested of an asylum officer's negative credible fear determination, the IJ must review the case de novo and consider the alien's credibility and other known facts.

units.obligation_text: The immigration judge shall first determine whether the alien is covered by the presumption at 8 CFR 208.33(a)(1) and 1208.33(a)(1) and, if so, whether the alien has rebutted the presumption in accordance with 8 CFR 208.33(a)(2) and 1208.33(a)(2).
units.action_summary: The IJ must first determine whether the presumption applies and whether it has been rebutted, consistent with the referenced provisions.

units.obligation_text: Where the immigration judge determines that the alien is not covered by the presumption, or that the presumption has been rebutted, the immigration judge shall further determine, consistent with § 1208.30, whether the alien has established a significant possibility of eligibility for asylum under section 208 of the Act, withholding of removal under section 241(b)(3) of the Act, or withholding of removal under the Convention Against Torture. Where the immigration judge determines that the alien has established a significant possibility of eligibility for one of those forms of relief or protection, the immigration judge shall issue a positive credible fear finding. Where the immigration judge determines that the alien has not established a significant possibility of eligibility for any of those forms of relief or protection, the immigration judge shall issue a negative credible fear finding.
units.action_summary: If the presumption does not apply or is rebutted, the IJ must determine whether the alien has a significant possibility of eligibility for relief and issue a positive or negative credible fear finding accordingly.

units.obligation_text: Where the immigration judge determines that the alien is covered by the presumption and that the presumption has not been rebutted, the immigration judge shall further determine whether the alien has established a reasonable possibility of persecution ... or torture. Where the immigration judge determines that the alien has established a reasonable possibility of persecution or torture, the immigration judge shall issue a positive credible fear finding. Where the immigration judge determines that the alien has not established a reasonable possibility of persecution or torture, the immigration judge shall issue a negative credible fear finding.
units.action_summary: If the presumption applies and is not rebutted, the IJ must determine whether the alien has a reasonable possibility of persecution or torture and issue a positive or negative credible fear finding accordingly.

units.obligation_text: Following the immigration judge’s determination, the case will proceed as indicated in 8 CFR 208.33(c)(2)(v)(A) through (C).
units.action_summary: After the IJ's determination, the case must proceed according to the procedures set forth in the referenced provisions.

units.obligation_text: Where a principal asylum applicant is eligible for withholding of removal under section 241(b)(3) of the Act or withholding of removal under § 1208.16(c)(2) and would be granted asylum but for the presumption in paragraph (a)(1) of this section, and where an accompanying spouse or child as defined in 208(b)(3)(A) of the Act does not independently qualify for asylum or other protection from removal, the presumption shall be deemed rebutted as an exceptionally compelling circumstance in accordance with 8 CFR 208.33(a)(2) and 1208.33(a)(2).
units.actor: the presumption/application of law by adjudicators
units.action_summary: If the principal applicant would be granted asylum but for the presumption and an accompanying spouse/child does not independently qualify, the presumption is to be deemed rebutted as an exceptionally compelling circumstance.
